_childDocuments_.review: If you're wondering if this game is worth a buy, it is.  Just get it.  It is a lot of fun, and the way you advance through the game is very intriguing as it teaches you some of the ins and outs of being a drug dealer, or at least as best as any videogame currently on the market can.  To begin, Drug Dealer Simulator is unique and the basic fundamental gameplay is enough to draw you in, and keep you playing, without noticing how much time has passed.  And sure--the game requires a certain amount of grind, but that's really part of the fun, because as a simulator for selling drugs, you need to build up a reputation through selling less valuable and addictive drugs to begin, like amphetamines and marijuana.  At first, you might find that you've lost your stash or your money, yet you'll gradually start to understand how everything works, and that's when you'll really start enjoying the game.  As your character progresses, you will have access to drugs such as Esctasy, crystal meth, heroin, and Fentanyl.  Plus, you have the option of mixing drugs and cutting your drugs a certain way at your own work station so as to create your own unique strength and recipe.  Some other activities to partake in include building up your reputation through handing out free samples of certain drugs to people, as well as spray painting your own symbol on the walls throughout different territories.  And then of course, there is always the looming threat of getting caught by the police and having your stash seized.  I haven't gotten too deep into the game yet, but I've found thus far there is enough to do to keep you entertained and coming back for more for quite a while.  I think it's fair to say this game is at least somewhat addictive.  Not as addictive as you know heroin, but maybe at least methamphetamine.  Now for some of the disappointing aspects of Drug Dealer Simulator.  Graphically the game is decent, but really nothing too impressive for 2020.  It almost looks like a game you could find on mobile.  Second, there is too much walking in the game.  The fact you have to always go back to your apartment to make deals, order drugs, and use the work station, before you can sell any drugs to anyone on the street can become somewhat tedious and repetitive.  But maybe that's the reality of being a drug dealer.  The controls are alright.  There is no way to use a controller so moving your character around will invariably result in constantly bumping into people and walls.  While there could be more content to the game, that's not my main problem with it.  In fact, one of my biggest gripes at this point isn't really the lack of content, as I think for a game at this price there is a fair amount, but that there aren't any Steam achievements.  What gives?  I think not having these in the game does a huge disservice to the gamer, because a game like this is designed for Steam achievements.  Additionally, there are so many different things that can happen to you, and several ways to gain status that I kept expecting to gain at least one achievement as I progressed through the game.  Plus, I could only think about how funny some of the achievements would be depicted.  And yet, as of now at least, there are none.  For a game of this nature, that's a let-down.  Hopefully the developers will be adding some very soon, because that would incentivize someone to keep playing.  Additionally, as far as the available content of Drug Dealer Simulator goes, I think the variety and quantity of available drugs to sell in the game is somewhat lacking.  For example, there are so many addictive prescription medications like benzodiazepines, muscle relaxers, sleeping pills, even steroids.  None of these are in the game.  Had they been, there would be much greater depth to the gameplay.  It would be reasonable to expect that certain drugs would be delivered to different settings, each with a different clientele that is interested in those specific drugs.  Imagine going out to the countryside looking to sell some crystal meth; a gym selling steroids; or a college campus selling amphetamines--there are so many possibilities!  Instead though, you just sort of wander around the streets selling drugs to people in areas that aren't at all unique and which look the same.  I also felt certain characters in the game should have personalities that at least would lead one to believe there is a specific drug for which they're craving.  But instead every character just has a generic disposition.  For a game designed to simulate the lives of people who sell drugs, some of these ideas, all of which can be found in the real world, should be in there.  Nevertheless, for $20, this game is worth it.  There's enough to do and it's intriguing enough to keep you playing to the point where having paid that amount is justified.  It's lacking in certain areas, but the positives outweigh the negatives.  And if you ever find this game on sale, it is a must-buy, without any doubt.  The game is a massive amount of fun, and can be hilarious at times as well.  Overall, I'm happy with my purchase, and recommend people on the fence about this one go ahead and get Drug Dealer Simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting and unique sim that didn't quite live up to my expectations.It is very monotonous and pretty grindy. For the most part you are running or sneaking around the map, trying to deliver the goods without being caught by the police. It might be thrilling early on, but after a while it gets a bit stale.After playing for over 230 hours, I'm left with a bitter-sweet mixed feeling. I still give this a thumbs up, because it's not a bad game and I did have my fair share of fun. I just wish there were more depth to it than running around as a delivery boy. So, before you buy this, try the demo! If you like it, then it might actually be worth it. If it's on sale then it definitely is!GOOD- Currently the only good game of its genre ("Weed Shop 3" doesn't count, that's a legal grow/dispensary sim. It's good though, but maybe even more grindy than DDS).- Mix/make your own stuff using functional lab equipment. Just remember that your customers demands a certain level of quality and a bad product can kill them. So be careful what you mix and how much.- You can use the products and observe its effects on your character. Hint: - Recruit dealers and sell larger quantities.- Several buildings are for rent, which you can use as hideouts or set up as a lab and assign crew.- You can buy villas and decorate them, but they are very expensive!- OK, but not great, selection of furniture and decoration for your hideouts/labs/villas.- Good in-game music (it's a shame that you can't buy a stereo/radio for your hideouts).NEUTRAL- No vehicles or guns.- Can't go inside "Two Towers", the party building.BAD- Making money and progression is grindy!- Sneaking around the police, gets boring after a while.- The way the police is patrolling the streets is unrealistic. They will almost always stop and search you if your in their near vicinity.- Police hours between 21:00 and 07:00, which means people are not allowed to be outside. You will be arrested even if you don't carry anything illegal. I get why this was implemented (), but it's kinda dumb. Police doesn't have any issue with everyone else walking around.- City is split up into three regions. Each time you travel to another region you must pass through a police post at the border which means they will stop and search you. There are other secret ways to travel between the regions, like , but it requires frequent lockpicking and after a while just feels like a chore.- Lab UI is not especially user-friendly and makes everything very tedious, even the simplest task as splitting your products for your customers. It's a bit of a learning curve for new players, but not the worst I've seen in games.- City feels dead and lifeless, partly by the fact that there's no traffic but also because there's few NPCs walking around. They also act kinda robotic.- Lockpicking. You have to lockpick the same locks over and over again, since they automatically lock after some time. I really wish there were a lockpicking skill, making it faster and easier to lockpick later in game.- Police chatter (mainly there for you to hear the police coming) goes like this "......, OVER!". Nobody uses the closure phrase "over", that's from way back in stone-age times. It might not sound like a big deal, but after 230h+ it becomes very annoying, especially when they sometimes camp right outside your hideout while you're trying to do some cutting/mixing work.- Map size is fairly small.- Story is a bit short. It's just ends way too early. After the story ends, you haven't exactly finished the game, but you now have to find your own motivation to continue playing. Either it be achievements, the villas or whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I thought I'd spend just 5 minutes with the free sample, and here I am, 30 hours in. Drug Dealer Simulator is surprisingly addictive!You start out as a lowly street dealer, selling to users out of your run down apartment. From there, it's a long way to the top as you build your enterprise and gain respect throughout the city.This isn't a game about running around shooting people, because there's thousands of other games like that. The fun comes from figuring out how to maximize profit while keeping your clients happy, and running from the police!My biggest gripe with this game is the lab controls. Where are the keyboard shortcuts? Having to point and click your way through packaging kilos of drugs gets tedious. Also, there does seem to be a point where the game runs out of content. Also, I can't end this review without mentioning the soundtrack. The ambient hip hop is very well made and really sets the mood for the game.Best of all, thanks to Proton, this game is suitable for Gaming on the Linux Desktop.

The language needs to be way more clear and then maybe the game would be halfway playable but in this state...Im just uninstalling because im getting sick and tired of having to be so closely engaged with developers and analyze someones product just to get decent gameplay out of it and not have to be confused all the time and edit game files and all this nonsense.Ive been gaming long enough to remember when games just came out ready to go. _childDocuments_.review: This game is another reason why I really think Steam needs to add a neutral button to the review. It felt like Thief Sim just in a different setting. There is nothing wrong with this game in terms of glitches, bugs, or gameplay. It's fun and challenging. However, it suffers from the same massive drawback that Thief Sim suffers from and that is that there is zero replayability. This has even less replayability than Thief Sim though. At least in Thief Sim, it will take you a long time to clean out every house. Here is literally the boring grind over and over again. I like that instead of Thief Sim, it's infinite what you can do in this game but it renders it boring after a while. Also only other knock I can give this is the perk system is absolutely awful. The cops will find drugs on you and will spot you even if you have stealth and illusionist maxed out. Only runner and stamina work and are remotely useful. Salesman does nothing in letting you raise your prices. Also one other knock I can give is, this game expects you to know the street names of every drug and so I lost clients and delayed progression accidentally. It never explains that or recipes for things and the spray painting and respects mechanics make absolutely zero sense. So honestly, this game is fun and a good challenge but there are many things you have to work around and it can get boring. I hit recommend because I do enjoy playing this but only get it if it's on sale. 6 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Drug Dealer Simulator gives you the thrill of slinging dope without the real life consequences. While the game is fun, it leaves a lot on the table as far as desired features.Pros:-Wide variety of drugs to sell (although pills and prescription drugs are completely missing from the game)-Player "safe houses" can be furnished-Police chases get your adrenaline pumpingCons:-You can't specialize in dealing one type of drug. You HAVE to sell them all.-Cops tend to patrol the same routes, which can easily be used to avoid them entirely-The checkpoint in the middle of the map is just a frustrating mechanic. For essentially no reason, you have to pay hundreds of dollars each time you want to transport drugs between the 2 sides of the map. You can take the sewers, but you can't bring a backpack, which means you can't carry anything but maybe some cash and a dimebag across at once.-The map itself is small-A lot of pertinent gameplay information, such as how long someone will wait for you to deliver, is missing from the game-There's no multiplayer. The single player version of the game is great, but if I could run a drug smuggling empire with my friends, I'd be more likely to spend longer in the game.For the price, I'd say this game is worth it. If the devs improve the amount of content in the game, this could be one of Steam's best hidden gems.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, it's awesome and there aren't really any other games that do what this one does anywhere near as well as this one.  for the most part.the problem: There isn't enough content to keep you going...   after about 10-15 hours of playing, you'll be at a point where you have everything unlocked (for the most part), and will be making so much cash you can't do anything with it.  because there is only so much stuff to spend your money on.  buy a new small shed in each of the zones, and/or a small apartment. (I think that there are like 15-20 purchasable "properties" which isn't much in the scope of the game, as what you can do with your properties is extremely limited, specifically. you can buy your small apartment or shed, and then buy some of the few furniture items for it.   which essentially are: Cheap bed, couch, chair, table, etc.  Decent bed, couch, chair, table, etc. or Expensive bed, couch chair table etc.          as well as a few things like cabinets for storage, or a "wardrobe" that lets you "change your clothes" (Doesn't actually change how you look as you can't see your playermodel.)  or buy some paintings/decorative plants.other than that for actual functional stuff you can buy, is where the game shines, you can buy various drug mixing/making equipment, ranging from cheap and inefficient ways of doing things like using an electric coffee grinder, a hand mortar and pestle.  all the way up to using high end lab grade equipment, such as: lab grade centrifuges, lab grade precision mixers, Flasks to break down drugs for mixing, to pill pressing machines to make your own pills. and so on.  This aspect of the game is amazing and is done so well, in my opinion no other game does it better.   the dealing itself is fairly fun, while avoiding police patrols, and trying to keep your "suspicion" or "heat" level down, all while trying to deliver the "goods" as fast as you can in order to keep your dealer rating as high as can be. (which in turn lets you charge higher prices for your "goods")the game loop is repetitive, but very fun in itself.   the problem is, the game lacks any real "content" after you get to the point when you're selling to gangs in huge quantity. example,   some of the more expensive properties to buy are only like $4000  and you can make upwards of 20-30K when selling to gangs in bulk...  which means off of a few sales to gangs you can easily make enough cash to essentially be able to buy everything.   and then there isn't much reason to continue selling. This issue essentially is you just get into the "good" part of the game right around the time you unlock gangs,  (the "good" part of the game is when you get access to all of the "merchandise" to sell.  as all of the merchandise in the game is locked behind a level restriction.      so around the same time you finally unlock all the end game stuff, (H, Coke, Fentanyl,) and can start making these crazy mixes with the Fentanyl,  which is when the game really shines as you have to go through numerous steps in your lab to make a super drug.       you unlock the gangs, and that makes it so making your own super drugs is almost irrelevant.  because why should I waste my time making a super drug to sell and make a few thousand dollars over hours of work. when I can just bulk buy coke, or meth, and do a cheap cut, and sell it for 30K?)So all in all, the game is amazing, it just doesn't have enough end game content, or reason to keep you playing.    But the devs don't really care about the game, and barely put any work into updating it.so far they push out a "MAJOR UPDATE" every year or so, and it adds a tiny bit of content. almost like they have one or 2 people working on DDS still, and the rest of the studio is working on other projects.     but Movie Games S.A. and PlayWay S.A. are known to be scummy publishers who release unfinished products, hype them up, and get people to buy them, then run away with the cash. Unfortunately Byterunners ( the games devs) appear to have none, or almost no, active media presence... which means no way to tell how big of a company they are, or if they are a legitimate company. or if they're owned by MovieGames or Playway.I just wish they could put a little bit more focus on this game, or try to force the publiser(s) they partnered with to help put some elbow grease into making this game better.as if they did, I believe this game could be incredibly huge and popular.I wish steam had a "neutral" option instead of having to choose positive or negative review.I'd say buy the game if you think you like the concept of selling drugs in a game.     otherwise wait for a sale, until the devs actually add more content.Maybe try to mess around with procedural generation for maps? or for extra sections of the map that are done with procedural generation, to add replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The date is 09/01/2022. I have changed my review to "no". Do NOT purchase this game. IT IS A MONEY GRAB. The "company" producing this game has endlessly neglected this title and has falsely advertised promises they did not keep. Just look at the comments on their "community" posts and you will understand the general census of how people feel how this developer. This is purely an asset flip, taking premade assets, making false promises and taking as much money as possible then ditching the game completely. These devs wholeheartedly do NOT deserve your hard earned money, please spend it elsewhere and save yourself the disappointment.The good: I'm only 14 hours in but I managed to hit level 15, a goal we all wish to get to for that sweet sweet ganja growing. Anyways, the game is pretty damn solid. Good mechanics, a nice amount of frustrating, just enough to keep you wanting to flip more packs like the real g you are. I can endlessly flip drugs of my choice with nothing forced upon me, the freedom is truly fun. Whipping up some amphetamine and drying your big bags of weed as you grow your empire, what more is there to love? The voice acting is pretty fresh and the accuracy is much enjoyed. It takes some time to get the hang of the best ways to do things, but once you do you're running around constantly with a plan that could change at any given moment. The system of heat works well and I love having to tone it down and not supply anyone but my closest dealers in order to avoid heat but still keep the income rolling in, a thoroughly realistic experience.The bad:The game is however lacking in some areas. The map is fairly confined and in one 8 hour sitting I had unlocked the whole area. There's no use of vehicles or at minimum a peddle bike, meaning you HAVE to run everywhere and so does everyone else. The idea we're locked in by the government with constant unrealistic checkpoints can eventually get quite dull and feels like an excuse to do less work, since we already know how big game worlds can be in 2020. In my opinion, multiplayer in this game would be a breathe of fresh air in many ways, given that there would be a bigger world to accompany it and things like vehicles in order to really feel like I can flex my big cash gains. A server-based multiplayer (where only one player can claim a property, other players can band up or be rivals etc. and everything saves on the server) or co-op mode with saves would be great and really give us some greater goal. I thoroughly enjoy the messaging app, but it seriously needs to work on the phone rather than just the laptop, role-playing as a drug dealer who doesn't really use his phone is a bit... naff. In conclusion, the core mechanics are really sick. There isn't another game quite like it and it can feel fairly addictive at times. This game is essentially what GTA V is missing, but then it's also missing a vast open world like GTA V. Quite a frustrating reality from someone who was so ready to properly slang drugs in the GTA Online world just to be horribly disappointed by Rockstar Games. I just really need a way to flex my money, starting out walking and buying better and better transport as I go along. Being able to visit other cities and not live in a dystopian universe where there are walls surrounding the city and the ability to really experience the high life and get out of the ghetto. So that's it, all this game lacks is a sense of accomplishment and a big open world to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this a neutral review if I could, was thinking of recommending it but after hearing the Dev's responses to their player base I feel like it has to be given a thumbs down. I understand that this game was made by a small indie team, is only $20, and compared to most sim games or games of this style it actually has some nice polish to it and actually has time and energy put into it. However, it has a lot of elements missing to the game that would take it from a fun time to a viral must play game that hopefully they make in DDS2 or give the game to a company with money, a bigger crew, and more time. Good:-Game play is addicting and fun.-Graphics are very acceptable.-Some customization options in both locations and sales/location of sales.Bad or Missing:-Police: One of my major problems with this game is how the police work. The game needs to have a risk and reward system so it is nice that they implemented this with the police. However, they are extremely persistent which gets annoying. Being from a bad neighborhood where almost everyone is messed up on drugs I can say from observation the police don't care about ♥♥♥♥, so for the police to search you at all hours every time they see you always gets old fast. I understand when the lights go down and it is police hours, but during the day when you are just walking around with a small bag I don't feel like you should be harassed by every single cop ever unless you were sprinting or had ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of drugs in a giant bag.-Guns: What drug dealer doesn't have a gun?...I have never bought, sold, or used drugs but everything I have seen or heard is that selling drugs is dangerous. There will be junkies that will hold you up at gunpoint to get stuff for free, would be fun to blow them away if they try it. You have dealers that you give product to, what if they decide not to pay up? You hunt them down and blow them away. Cops trying to shake you down when you clearly have drugs? Blow them the ♥♥♥♥ away and throw the bodies in the river/lake. All this could also be a system where you develop a reputation and no one will try to ♥♥♥♥ with you, including police, because they know you aren't afraid to start lighting ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. So for the Dev's to tell the fan base "If you want guns go play GTA" is not only insulting to the people that gave them money but also A DRUG DEALER WOULD HAVE A GUN. Don't yell at your patrons because you are too lazy or don't have the money to implement things that would make your game better.-Messages: On the phone don't work, would be nice to at least schedule a pickup or money drop off without having to go into a safe house.-Jar Controls: Having to drag each individual bag to each jar is slightly tedious and not being able to put the exact amount of grams you want to take out is odd and tedious as well. Why can't I take a 4g bag of something why do I have to give my client one 1g bag and one 3g bag instead that doesn't make any sense.-New Safe Houses: It would be nice if safe houses had a communal storage system, in the early stages of the game you run through drugs fast and can only buy so much at a time that chances are when you get a new house you won't be able to get or store drugs from there for a very long time so they are kinda useless to you aside from police escapes.-Spending Money: I haven't gotten to this part but I hear what you can spend money on fades fast when you start making real money, you can't go on club/hooker binges, can't buy sick houses and vehicles so there is no real end game goal, and with no guns there isn't even the satisfaction of hoarding tons of cash and daring people to come at your empire. Also no drip or character customization so you can't even walk around like a boss with the swag of a God. Can't pay off the corrupt police force to not ♥♥♥♥ with you (cause lets face it in a run down place like this place the cops would either be non-existent as mentioned before or super corrupt). I'm sure there are some other examples available that I either haven't gotten to yet or don't remember at the time but when it comes down to it is the game fun? Yes, it is the kind of game that you can lose hours to and be like "oh crap is it that late already?". Would I recommend the game? No, I would say wait for the second one that they are working on and watch some reviews/gameplay to see if they fixed everything. The game is good but it could have been SO much more and it is kinda sad to see them be like "we'll just make a second one and get more money that way" instead of fixing up and mastering the version they already made.

_childDocuments_.review: Drug Dealer Simulator - Exploring the Dark Side of the Criminal World[Introduction]"Drug Dealer Simulator" is a simulation game developed by Byterunners Game Studio. In this game, players immerse themselves in the dangerous world of the underground by engaging in drug trade. The game offers a realistic drug business simulation, allowing players to explore the criminal underworld.[Gameplay]"Drug Dealer Simulator" focuses on drug production, distribution, and trade. Players can produce drugs, sell them to customers, make a profit, and expand their operations. However, they must also deal with the police and rival gangs. The gameplay is realistic and requires players to make risky decisions.[Graphics and Sounds]"Drug Dealer Simulator" successfully captures the gritty and dangerous atmosphere of the criminal underworld through its graphics and sounds. Dark streets, drug labs, and character designs immerse players in the criminal world. The sound design enhances the atmosphere with police radio chatter, street noise, and other details, adding to the realism.[Conclusion]"Drug Dealer Simulator" offers an intriguing experience for players interested in exploring the dangers of the criminal world and the complexities of the drug trade. Realistic gameplay, tough decisions, and the intricacies of the criminal underworld make the game appealing. However, please note that the game contains themes and content related to crime, so age restrictions should be considered.Rating: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction:Drug Dealer Simulator is a captivating virtual adventure that takes players on an adrenaline-fueled journey into the gritty underworld of illicit drug trade. Developed by skilled creators, this game offers a unique and immersive experience, blending elements of simulation, strategy, and storytelling. As a player, you will find yourself engrossed in a thrilling world of crime, making crucial decisions and navigating the consequences of your actions. Let's dive into the reasons why Drug Dealer Simulator deserves accolades for its engrossing gameplay, realistic mechanics, and dynamic storytelling.Engaging Gameplay:One of the most outstanding aspects of Drug Dealer Simulator is its deeply engaging gameplay. From the very start, players are tasked with building their drug empire from scratch, making every decision count. Whether it's scouting for the perfect location, managing resources, or negotiating with suppliers, each action has a tangible impact on the game's progression. The mechanics are skillfully designed to keep players invested in their virtual drug-dealing venture, providing a constant sense of achievement and satisfaction as they climb the ranks of the criminal underworld.Realistic Simulation:The game's developers have done an excellent job of creating a realistic drug-dealing simulation. Every aspect, from the buying and selling of drugs to evading the law enforcement, is intricately detailed and well-thought-out. The supply and demand mechanics are dynamic and responsive, making players feel like true entrepreneurs as they adapt their strategies based on market trends. The inclusion of law enforcement elements adds an extra layer of excitement and challenge, making each drug deal feel like a thrilling cat-and-mouse game.Immersive World and Graphics:Drug Dealer Simulator boasts an immersive open-world environment that feels alive and teeming with activity. The streets pulse with an authentic urban atmosphere, and NPCs (non-playable characters) add depth to the surroundings, making it feel like a bustling city with its own ecosystem of crime. The graphics are visually appealing and do justice to the dark and gritty theme of the game. The attention to detail in both the environments and character designs further enhances the overall gaming experience, drawing players deeper into the virtual criminal underworld.Compelling Narrative:Beyond its exceptional gameplay and mechanics, Drug Dealer Simulator weaves a compelling narrative that adds an emotional dimension to the game. Players will encounter various characters and make alliances, creating a sense of attachment to the evolving story. The decisions players make throughout the game significantly impact the storyline, providing an element of unpredictability and replay value. This approach ensures that each playthrough is unique, keeping players engrossed and eager to discover different outcomes.Conclusion:Drug Dealer Simulator on Steam is a masterful creation that successfully combines thrilling gameplay, realistic simulation, and an immersive world, all enveloped within a compelling narrative. Its strategic elements and dynamic mechanics make it a standout title in the simulation genre, while its gripping storytelling keeps players on the edge of their seats throughout their criminal journey. If you're seeking an adrenaline-pumping adventure that challenges your strategic prowess and storytelling abilities, Drug Dealer Simulator is undoubtedly a game worth exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: Drug Dealer Simulator is a criminally underrated game that you should give a try if you like what you read in this review. You start off selling weed and amphetamine to a couple of people, but you slowly make your way up the ranks until you start selling harsher drugs like meth, coke, and fentanyl. As you progress in the game you'll buy new warehouses, equipment, and furniture. All have their uses. For example, you should split your product and move it to different warehouses so if you get raided by the DEA you won't lose everything. DDS isn't your average game, you ALWAYS have to think ahead and keep on your toes to prevent raids, loss of area respect, and the time limit for providing product for gangs later in the game. If everything you just read seems appealing to you, I would 100% recommend trying out this game.

Fun gameplay2. Optional chemistry for drug improvisation 5. Game still developed and updated in long periods of time so there's new content when you don't expect it.-- Pros --1. Small map (They're currently working on expanding it according to dev news 1, 2, 3 and 4)2. Repetitive gameplay (gets boring after around 20h)3. No multiplayer4. No guns5. Unending story (the story doesn't have an ending and you will probably never get to hear your character's voice again after level 30)While this game is fun and has a good amount of content in it, it's still missing a few things, the map isn't the largest, but definitely seems to keep expanding with updates, and the story is pretty short and doesn't have an ending to it. The game feels a little repetitive after a while (around 20h is where you start to feel it) and the gameplay can be challenging if you decide to mess with chemistry (modifying your drugs); otherwise it's pretty easy.I currently love the game, but in my opinion if it had a good story with an ending instead of an unfinished infinite one, I'd really love it. I like the idea of having Keiji and La Ballena to expand to outside the ghetto, but if there were to be the option to grow your own cartel and things that would be awesome. Of course there are limitations. I love the latest additions to the game which both made it more realistic and also gave you a bit more control over your drugs, featuring weed growing and the sewers, the fact that police cars spawn in very specific locations to prevent people from just running around the map when there's no patrol in the best places, and the Sector C update, with the new way to launder money of having your own business to tunnel the money through, but I wish there was some way you could actually do it on your own instead of just dropping the cash you have at drop points and funneling it by yourself. A thing I would also love to see in the game is multiplayer. The ability to play this game with my friends or maybe even have competition will encourage players to use chemistry in order to make their drugs even better, making the game more challenging and also more fun! Another thing I'd like to recommend is Investments! A way to invest into businesses by buying stocks, cryptocurrency value prices, and stuff like that! The last addition I would like to see THE MOST is very easy to implement and will make the game a lot more fun. ADD MORE VOICE OVERS! for example, after you get away from cops (become fugitive) your character says something like "Whoo hoo! That was close, go change your clothes before they find you again, quick!" and a few different dialogs like this which gets selected randomly every time you run away so it won't say the same thing every single time which can become annoying after a bit. The thing I would like the most, is competition. Doesn't have to be real players, but could also be A.I!! Or maybe even see your dealers just run around and deal drugs as well! That would most definitely add life to the game! Maybe NPCs just standing and talking to each other, instead of just walking around. So much things could be added and made so the game would have much more life and would be way more entertaining. Maybe some more DEA presence and a life water and food system would be a pretty cool addition! Everyday life expenses, including subscriptions and gambling would be super awesome![/spoiler]

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead– murdered by my brother-in-law, Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now, and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, he asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded. I... I always thought Hank was a very moral man, and I was particularly vulnerable at the time – something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me in on a ride-along and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin, so I agreed. Hank had a partner, a businessman named Gustavo Fring. Hank sold me into servitude to this man. And when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling-out. Things escalated. Fring was able to arrange – uh, I guess... I guess you call it a "hit" – on Hank, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured. And I wound up paying his medical bills, which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge. Working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring. The bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA. To keep me in line, he took my children. For three months, he kept them. My wife had no idea of my criminal activities, and was horrified to learn what I had done. I was in hell. I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, and in response, he gave me this. [Points to bruise on face.] I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. All I could think to do was to make this video and hope that the world will finally see this man for what he really is.

The last update made the game very dark, can't see a thing at night. Instead of fixing it, the developers explained that WE can download some program to manually fix the brightness issue each time you play the game. Nice huh? TLDR. Buy something else.

_childDocuments_.review: 87 HOURS UPDATE: the game certainly got repetitive, there's no end-game, is unfinished, the teaser showcases game elements that are just not there, the developers don't update it or even fix its bugs and their PR comms are vague attempts to pretend there's some movement (where there's obviously none). This game massively improves when bought half-priced.---Surprisingly addictive and with more depth than I expected. The base mechanics are stealthy fetch quests, a neighbourhood reputation system, drug design and lab (base) building. The map is large, keeps some secrets and allows traversal progression by picking locks, unlocking areas and finding alternative routes. Regarding drugs, how you mix them results on losing clients over time, turning them into addicts or their death. There's also a money laundering system to allow you acquire property (spaces and equipment).The worst thing I've seen so far is difficulty and repetitiveness. While I find it easy on the highest difficulty I also suspect the game is keeping some surprise for later. The next worst thing are the whinny comments from the community (some famous Youtuber played it on his channel and attracted attention). Please, note this is an indie game, the company isn't CDPR and the pricetag is quite affordable (low for the fun I'm having, TBH). I'm hooked to this game and considering starting my own business IRL =)

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fascinating game - yeah it's definitely repetitive, and not for the easily offended but an interesting experience nonetheless, playing as someone who makes profit off other's misery. My only criticism, which is the same to all of the other more immersive "simulator games" - i.e. thief simulator, probably even house flipper, is that there's very little past the mechanical side of the game (i.e. buy drugs, cut drugs, sell drugs, expand. This game does endeavour to add a little bit of attitude with the addition of a narrator and some interesting quirks of characters, but these games would really benefit into playing into a bit of a power fantasy via relationships. You quickly start to make some bank and some reputation but outside of more people wanting your ♥♥♥♥, there's very little in terms of people either "fearing" you or wanting to be part of your crew. I think part of what makes this dark side of life a little more "attractive" is the feeling (albeit very fragile) of power. I'd love for one of these games to really develop that concept, but alas, a good game and you will sink some hours into it.

name: Hell Let Loose
detailed_description: Check Out CONSCRIPT Discord Community About the Game Join the chaos of war and be a part of the most iconic battles of the Eastern and Western Fronts, including Carentan, Omaha Beach, Stalingrad, Kursk and more. Hell Let Loose drops you into the action, where you will have to fight across fields, bridges, forests, towns and more war-torn environments! Lumbering tanks will be dominating the battlefield and crucial supply chains fuelling the frontlines, you are essential to the colossal, combined arms warfare. An Epic Theatre of War Take to the battlefield in this squad-based, 50v50 multiplayer game, and choose one of our 14 roles available within the Command, Infantry, Recon and Armour unit types. Play as an Officer, Spotter, Medic, Tank Commander and more, to experience every aspect of World War II combat. Each role is equipped with different historical weapons, vehicles, and equipment that are intricately detailed, bringing the realism to the brutal and bloody warfare. Unit focussed gameplay is crucial and when done well can command the tide of battle. Hardcore Gameplay The combat takes place across huge, to-scale maps, recreated by utilising aerial and satellite imagery of real battle locations in stunning detail using Unreal Engine 4. These realistic battlefields are divided up into large capture sectors allowing emergent and constantly unique gameplay to evolve between the two forces of fifty players. Work as a team and make continual large scale, tactical decisions as to where to attack or defend. Fight Together - Win Together Hell Let Loose is not about kill to death ratios – teamwork is central to gameplay. Communication is essential. Players work together beneath the leadership of Officers and their Commander to take strategic targets on the battlefield and dominate the opposition. In Hell let loose, it’s always better to tackle things as a team. If you think you can handle the chaos of war, we’ll see you on the frontlines! Unique Meta Game Manage resources and supplies to call in support, bombing runs, new vehicles, strafing runs and to reinforce strong-points or flank enemies. When a sector is captured, it will generate one of three resources for your team, creating a complex game that will influence your team’s march to victory. Strategy is key to success. Key Features: • Fight in epic 50 vs 50 multiplayer battles. • Two distinct gamemodes - Offensive and Warfare • 9 maps with more added frequently - land at Omaha Beach, fight through Carentan and into the frozen forests of Foy before climbing Hill 400. • Never fight the same battle twice - 99 capture point variations per map, means thousands of potential battles. • Play and master one or many of 14 unique roles, including: Officer, Medic, Machinegunner, Commander, Crewman, Sniper and more. • Constantly updated with new maps, weapons, features and fixes. • True to life ballistics and recoil patterns create satisfying, skillful gunplay. • In-game proximity voip, command voip and unit voip. • Brutal combat - friend and foe are dismembered by heavy weapons. • Persistent player progression - show off your experience by unlocking new uniforms, loadouts and other customisation options as you level up each individual role, as well as your player. • Take control of a huge array of WW2 vehicles - including the Tiger, Sherman, Stuart, Puma and more - with additional vehicles still to come • Bombard and wipe the enemy from the field by taking control of heavy weapons - such as anti-tank guns and artillery. • Build defenses on the battlefield to fortify your position. • Use teamwork to smash through the enemy front line and push through to victory. • Play the game as the Commander and lead your team to victory using different abilities as you orchestrate your forces via the tactical map.

_childDocuments_.review: After an initially shaky start, Hell Let Loose really did improve. However, it still has  some ways to go.If you're a fan of Red Orchestra style gameplay, you'll most likely enjoy Hell Let Loose. The gunplay is pretty solid, everything feels solid and punchy. The classes meld pretty well together, although they're only as good as the player playing them. But that's a given with games like this.The 100 player game modes work pretty well. Some lag can occur depending on server health. Other elements, like animation, vehicle controls, and placement of constructable items is very finicky. Voice chat still needs improvement, mostly on the quality end. I'd also recommend different sliders for various sounds, because certain elements like engine sounds can be extremely loud.It's a very promising game, and I recommend you try it.Overall, it's a pretty fun and immersive WW2 shooter experience that has a lot of care put into it. People who like RO/RS will feel right at home here. If HLL continues on this path, it'll be one of the best WW2 shooters I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to share with you my first experiences in this game, they did not disappoint!My first map took me to Hurtgen forest but I spawned in and it was pretty evident we were losing and on the last point. Before the game ended I did manage to get my first and only kill. I was running through the forest, stopped at a tree and surveyed the area. To my left I noticed a German soldier crouched at another tree looking a different direction. I pulled my garand sights up and aimed onto his head....pulled the trigger and ding. That satisfying headshot sound; a sound I'd come to familiarize myself with on my second game.The hurtgen game ended pretty soon after that but not before I could grab a picture of my first prize kill: Sorry buddy, you're just the first in a long line to come! :)The next map was Foy and this would be my first proper full game; and what a game it would be! I was on the German side and instantly when I spawned in I was already happy as my FPS had instantly shot up from the 30-60 range I was getting on hurtgen to the 90+ I was now getting on Foy. (The FPS remained quite well on this map throughout the game, around 70-80ish 95% of the time which is definitely playable) Regardless I got my Kar98 and I started running to the frontline with my squad.Upon reaching the frontlines a small skirmish ensued and I managed to craftily get into a position behind a large hay bale in the middle of a snowy field. I took a couple shots into a smokey haze unsure if I was killing anyone but it didn't matter as two seconds later a bullet pierced my skull. My first death of HLL, unfortunately the lucky person happened to be a medic on my own team some metres back. I forgave him and it was all okay as he came to my rescue a little later.The next area I found myself in was crouch behind a wall next to a little stone cottage watching retreating American forces cross my line of fire in the next field over, I aimed my rifle and starting knocking them down one after one, hearing that beautifully satisfying headshot sound! It was awesome! It wasn't long before I saw what caused the panicked retreat. As planes flew over head, two tiger tanks fiercely charged over the mounds on the edge of the field, crashing onto the next field and into my view in what can only be described as reminiscent of that scene in Saving Private Ryan.A little later into the match was where my rifle prowess really got going. In the middle of the woods cutoff from my squad, enemies all around. I spot one. Aim. Ding. Dead. I crawl to his position and see two more charging towards me danger close! I drop them too and their bodies lay all around me and I'm wriggling around between them getting into better position to kill enemies further in the distance. This is some Enemy at the gates type of ♥♥♥♥. I've never felt more immersed then I did in those moments. Not long after the game ended in a beautiful victory for the Fatherland. I think I fulfilled my role as a rifleman pretty well, getting 21 infantry kills and only dying 4 times :)I really don't know why I hadn't picked this up earlier, its awesome and the next update looks insane! TLDR: This game is so immersive, killed ♥♥♥♥ tons of dudes, had moments that reminded me of movies! Holy ♥♥♥♥ why didn't I play this before?

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review with 96+ hours in with the game since December of 2019.TL:DR- Great community that encourages teamwork. - Very fun to play!- Lot's of FPS purists trying to mold this to be a game like "that other one <they> play".- Early Access = tweaks and bugs.Simply put, Hell Let Loose is one of the best WW2 FPS games to come along in quite some time. I'm really hoping that this game makes it out of Early Access and continues to grow. HLL requires patience, coordination, and the ability to commit to something bigger than your own personal score. If you're looking to polish your FPS #1 Player Trophy, I strongly suggest that you go elsewhere - this is not your game. I can't tell you my K:D ratio, nor do I care. However, in my time playing this game, I have jumped into plenty of squads with people who want to coordinate and win as a team. I've seen some fantastic turn-around games where squads came together to earn a coordinated win. What a great feeling. I have to say, the community in this game is incredible so far. It's quite refreshing. This game is about teamwork. Make no mistake, this game has a frustration factor. The other team can get together as a team and ruin your day by earning a great win (of a point or a game). Sometimes, you'll get picked off and not even know where it came from. There are players who lone wolf and try to pad their own stats, the ever-popular tactic to exploit a wrinkle to maximize kills. Snipers and infantry hiding in hedges is a popular move. This is war, kids, and it's Hell. It's loud, chaotic, and frantic.The game is Early Access... so that means they are still tweaking things. Let's hope it keeps coming along.So, if you want to jump into a game with 100 people waging all out war, communicating, and being productive then support this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Yesterday I saw a homeless man drink straight, undiluted lemon juice. Straight from the bottle. I have been trying to figure out why ever since. What horror does a man need to see in this world to drink lemon juice like that? I was so consumed by this question that it broke me. My mind was no longer my own. Hours passed and my mortal shell of a body could only rock back and forth as my husk of a mind repeated "Why the lemon juice?" Time slipped from my grasp.  My friends and family despaired for my madness. I took to wonder the wilds, naked as the day I was born. Stopping only to growl and slobber at passing small animals who were unfortunate enough to meander across my path. "Why the lemon juice?" I left this world in my distraction and passed into the realm of the fairies. Wicked spirits swam around and through my head, cackling with rotten glee. I'll never know how I came to leave the land of the fairies, truth is that I do not want to know. I cannot remember for a reason I am sure. Next thing I know I am standing over the trembling figure of a friendly old man. A clever ruse old man! I know what you want. You asked me the time. Clearly you are planning a heist. Who else would need to know the time except for someone who was planning a daring heist to steal all the worlds lemons? God alone knows where I got the bottle of lemon juice from, maybe the fairies gave it to me as a parting gift. But I knew what it was for. I had to save the lemons and the bottle of lemon juice was how. Quickly and deftly I waterboarded the kind old man with the lemon juice. Screaming at him to "Leave the lemons alone!" It took five strong men who happened to be in the same car park at the time to restrain me. As the old lemon thief took to run away, doused as he was in lemon juice, I knew that my only hope of catching him was to unlock all of my potential. My hands shaking, I raised the bottle of lemon juice to my own lips. I drank deeply. I drank as an infant quaffs milk. The bitterness of the lemon juice turned my very soul inside-out. Just then time stood still. With euphoric rapture I saw in an instant the events of the last day. I saw it all in perfect detail, all in the tiniest fraction of a fraction of a second. I had not seen a homeless man drink lemon juice at all. For that mans face was my own. It was I all along. The moral of the story is that perhaps time travel is possible.Also Hell Let Loose is pretty fun.

The new Driel map is basically Remagen but improved in ways that make the experience of a bridge map much more enjoyable. El Alamein feels quite unique amongst all the other maps due to its vastly open ranges and rocky cliffs, I like it quite a bit.As for the rest of the non-British side of the game, I think HLL is a great blend of casual-shooter and milsim that you don't often find elsewhere. The game requires good communication between squads if you want to truly contend on the battlefield. I don't have any friends who play HLL but its pretty easy to find fun squads to just kill stuff with and have a great time. _childDocuments_.review: 5500+ hours, and loads of memories. I've made new friends, been a part of amazing player communities, and played in amazing matches. All of this was possible because of the game's , Black Matter Ltd.These devs worked themselves senseless building a rather excellent game. It was different from their original Kickstarter vision, and some of those backers were right to be upset about that. But the Hell Let Loose they did build was an exciting passion project by WW2 enthusiasts. Black Matter eventually sold the intellectual property for this game, to their partner and publisher, Team17. Team17 is NOT an Indie Game group, it's one of the largest publishing companies in the UK. Their goals are driven by profits first, not players or gameplay first. Their employees are paid poorly and suffer from sexual harassment, all while Team17 tries to grift people with schemes like NFTs. (Google these accusations, you won't have to look far to read about them.)Poor business practices aside, Team17 are poor game developers. They neglect their quality control, passing it off to their players to find bugs instead. Meanwhile, they spare no instance into milking their newly acquired franchise for money, by opening merch shops, and marketing their microtransactions.There's no soul left in this game, at least none coming from its owners. The PLAYERS make/made this game special. From the 70 year olds looking to kick ass, to the young adults looking for teamwork and communication. These people who spent their own money and time renting servers, filtering out the trolls/racists, and building custom admin tools. These people who ran competitions, made trailers/content, and who taught players how to play this game at its best.I used to be one of these people; until I recognized that people like me deserved better. The final nail in the coffin for this game was a half-baked trailer of .  It showed us the truth about HLL's future; Team17 wants to milk this game, not uphold its legacy and improve on it.This game isn't an indie game any more, it's a poor attempt to turn an indie game into a microtransaction filled AAA game. It's Team17's attempt to compete with Call of Duty and Battlefield, and that's NOT what this game was supposed to be. It was supposed to be a shooter with teamwork, communication, and a competent developer team that cared about its playerbase. Hell Let Loose used to have all that, but it doesn't now, and that hurts to write.

It's like rising storm, except the maps are way too big for that gameplay without transport vehicles. There's only ever like 1 truck active and it's usually just taking ammo to the one or two tanks that are ever on the map at the same time, or its sitting stuck in a ditch until it respawns.If they can replicate the scale and battle flow of heroes and generals then it'll be in a good spot. Kind of disappointed it isn't even close already. I'm not asking for a big selection of vehicles, or aircraft in early access, just that the game has some sense of combined arms gameplay, I don't care if every single tank or transport vehicle are the same model in early access. It just currently doesn't have the framework for the depth of gameplay like ARMA, and it doesn't have the action of something like battlefield or rising storm.Right now it's just a bunch of running through fields to get to some stale infantry gameplay that isn't solid enough to hold up on its own. The tools to give the game some character are there, the foundation is there, but the framework isn't, and that's what worries me, because a lot of early access games just never quite figure out the specifics of what the game is, and at that point they just start adding meaningless content to a relatively featureless game. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot. The combat feels good, the mechanics have enough depth that I feel alright playing on just five maps. It's a very good mix of arcade and sim. For those coming in from Squad, the game feels a bit more streamlined. If you want to have a similar experience to Squad in terms of team play, it's great to hop into (not that Squad is too complicated, it just feels like more responsibility on the leading side).That being said, a lot of these reviews that are calling it the most cinematic experience and saying things like "I've never seen teamplay like this before" have clearly never played shooters like it, and that's okay! I just need to point out that from a technical point, the game has a long way to go. Something that disappointed me was the lack of good sounds. The weapons have all been reworked, but the new sound engine has not come out yet. As a result, it can be hard to tell where you're getting shot from and there are times where battles don't feel as intense as it should. Any Squad and Post Scriptum player knows how important sound is to immersion.Two smaller things that annoy me are also the lack of server queue and terrible anti-aliasing. Overall though, great game. If you feel like the things I listed bother you, just hold on and wait for the upcoming patches! The devs have been consistently dropping content every other month since launch, and their work ethic is impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, there is no better "realistic" WW 2 shooter on the market today.Hell Let Loose is not a local 4-player game. It has been designed for more players, 100 to be exact. And I would advise you to play on servers that are rather full, or you will have a rather lonely experience. The maps are large and not meant for a few players only.If you are a fan of unrealistic shooters with tiny maps, short rounds and a lot of jumping around... this is not the game for you. Hell Let Loose aims to be a "realistic" simulation of WW II infantry warfare, while still being fun to play. You know what to expect if you have played games like Red Orchestra or Insurgency. Real success only comes to those players that are willing to join a team and cooperate with their teammates. Cover fire, flanking, maybe a bit artillery support or aerial recon or even a tank to support the operation - this works best when coordinated by good officers via chat.The setting is during the last phase of World War II, after the allies have landed in the Normandy and are now pushing towards Germany. You can play either on the US or German side.The game currently is in Early Access, but it already plays like a finished product. I encountered no game breaking bugs while wandering across the various battlefields, but marveled at the fantastic graphic. If you stay away from the mission objectives, you can play this game as a walking simulator as well and discover the beautiful landscape... often damaged from heavy fighting.At the moment there are only 2 vehicles implementewd, a Sherman and a Panther tank, but I hope additional tanks will follow. Also the number of maps is limited, but there is enough to see that you will not get bored soon.Teamkilling is easy in this game, so watch where you shoot! And take cover when under fire, or a bullet will find you very fast!Best looking "realisitic" WW II shooter you can buy atm!Addendum: The game has left Early Access now, and after 10 large updates also added Soviet forces and 2 maps taking place in Russia. Nice!

If you are not willing to talk try to break your shyness or at least keep close to your squad and follow your squad leader.Huge thumbs up for original developer Black Matter for making this game.However saying all that, as a sign of protest to what Team 17 is doing to the game I give a negative review.As they have shown so far they have no idea what made this game a success or who their playerbase is.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is a tough military sim shooter set in WW2 that's impossible not to compare with the likes of Arma, Squad and Post Scriptum. It's thoroughly unforgiving and if you're looking for a old fashioned gaming experience then this might be it.I found it fairly dull and frustrating when playing alone, but when teaming up with a friend in a tank we had an epic time. Him driving and crashing into bushes, me firing the guns at men charging at us through wheat fields. It was glorious. Tanks are a highlight for sure. The turrets turn painfully slowly and you have next to no visibility when battened up inside. Just like the real thing no doubt. The maps do feel a little on the large side and it's one of those games where you can run for miles only to end up getting killed by God knows what and have to start all over again from HQ. However, when you do do well it's thrilling. When you have a well organised squad with a spawn beacon it's even better. Looking forward to seeing how they update and improve this one going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I have logged 2 hours so far on this game. Sure, probably not impressive. But I'm a dad, married and have a needy dog. Logging that many hours is a big deal to me because that means I successfully snuck that many hours of gameplay in. So, if you're someone like me that loves video games but has to sneak away at night after the spouse falls asleep and the kids are down for the count after 13 bed time stories, keep on reading.I bought HLL in lieu of Battlefield 2042. I have logged many years of gameplay on the Battlefield series. But, the reviews came out and I was let down. So, I browsed and browsed for a game to play. I have experience on Squad, liked it, but it wasn't fully drawing me in. Was very complex. A fun game (definitely check it out), but there was so much going on I just couldn't commit. Hell Let Loose is very simliar to squad. So, I'mma break this down as best I can.What I like:o 1 shot 1 kill, for the most part. It's hardcore. Literally. Don't worry about pumping rounds into people's bodies. One shot will do.o Games can last for 1.5 hours, so you get REALLY into it. You have to, just so the game can end.o It is extremely well balanced. It doesn't matter if you are level 3 and the other team is level 132. You all get the same guns. Snipers get scopes. That's it. None of this "oh well in WW2 they had a type of red dot site" garbage that some games do. Nah, fam. That carbine? Iron sites. That STG-44? Iron sites. That LMG? Iron sites, my guy. Which is great, because that means when you die, it wasn't from some garbage or BS. It was a legitimate kill.o The community is fantastic. I was so lost when I joined my first server. Had no clue what was going on. I hopped into the "recon" squad and was the spotter. Told the dude "Hey man. First time playing this. What do I do?" You know what his response was? "Not a problem man! I'll walk you through it." This dude literally explained how this game worked for me in one match. It was fantastic. When you join regular infantry squads, I have had the same experience. "Hey, how do I do nodes? How do I mark things?" The community has been my favorite part. They're all there to have fun, and they hate toxic individuals. Very rarely do I encounter someone who is toxic. And if they're a dee-eye-see-kay, they usually get booted from the game.o Are you a tank guy? You like driving around in track vehicles shooting big rounds? You can do that and not get destroyed by a squad full of rocket launcher dudes. Nah, each squad gets 1 person to have an anti tank launcher. Which means it takes coordination and team work to take down armoured vehicles. Don't worry, to run a tank? You need 3 people. Everyone plays a role in the tank, not just 1 person. You need driver, gunner and tank commander. So, that helps offset the fact that they're giant beasts and gives the guys on the ground a fighting chance.There's a couple others, but overall, this game is exactly what I was looking for. Big maps, great graphics, SO MUCH CHAOS oh man the audio! It's insane. Artillery blowing up everywhere, machine guns ripping over your head to where your screen goes blurry and you got the spins like it's St. Patty's Day and you're in Boston.But overall, it's just the balance of the game. No squad can be overpowering and dominating. No vehicle is overpowering. It's all balanced as it should be, because neither succeed unless everyone works together.So, if you're like me who's a sort-of-casual-player-but-also-wants-to-be-hardcore, get this game. It's a breath of fresh air from Battlefield, the community is great, and it's nice to play a game where everyone is communicating but also, for the most part, treats each other with respect.9/10.It would be a 10/10 but I'm not that great at the game and too prideful to admit that it's actually me who's bad, so I'll blame the game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's rarely a game I'd give a rating within the first week of playing it. But this game, without a doubt, is one of the best gaming experiences in years!If you're used to the vast and huge open grounded maps of Call of Duty I, the atmosphere and versatility of Red Orchestra, and/or early Battlefield games without all the ingame money stripping nonsense, then you're in the right place. This is Call of Duty what it would have become, if the devs kept going the way they initially intendend before the greed took over. It feels a lot like the RO-Mod 'Darkest Hour' without the control shenanigans. If you love Escape from Tarkov, but hate how terribly unbalanced and cheaty the game is, I promise that's nothing you're going to experience in this game.The maps are huge, yet don't feel empty. Tactical realism feels true, yet installs the right tiny bit of arcade to keep the game lots of fun. The atmosphere is tight, yet it has its moments of giving you time to relax and regroup. Teams are (forcibly) well balanced by a decent installment of class limits. The graphics are outstanding, yet the game is extremely performant. This might be the major asset of this game, as in multiplayer a good ping and performance means the difference between win and lose, the difference between joy and frustration, the difference between motivation and dispair.An aspect that shouldn't be under-emphasized is communication. The game, by default, encourages you to use your microphone to communicate. While a lot of games are doing this, I've yet to experience a game that implements the need for tactical communication at such a splendid level. You will communicate. No seriously, even if you're the silent type of guy, you WILL communicate. Everybody does it, and communcation is indeed what you want to use a lot, since all tactics rely on communication. This is a tactical game, not a random arcade shooter. Any amount of communication you give, is the right amount. Any information you'd get from that communcation, is essential to your whole units tactics.I would usually recommend anyone to buy games on Steam for a sale, but in this case I'd love to see you invest the whole price. Give those devs the money, they totally deserve it. If they don't take the wrong way like past games, they will indeed be the future of tactical WW2 gameplay, and might even go so far as to outperform COD and/or RO in that regard.Is there room for improvement? Yes, there always is. From a gameplay point of view, there's virtually nothing I can think of that needs improvement. But what I'd like to see in future is the UK, and maybe even more factions, and of course, coming with that, more maps. Don't get me wrong, for a game of that quality there's already a good amount of map versatility, but more choice is always a good choice, if the maps keep having the same quality.Since I'm a natural modder(creator and user), I would obviously love to see official tools to allow users to make custom maps. I don't necessarily need mods, since the default game is already in an almost perfect state. But if official map tools help to create more quantitys of good maps, then I'm all for it. The devs could even start monthly creator competitions, and try integrating the best maps into the base game.So in essence, do I recommend this game? Yes, I do. Can you trust in this recommendation? Well, I've been playing game since age 8(1983), and I think I qualifie as someone who recognizes a good game if he sees it. I would usually allow critics on any notion, but in this game, all the negative reviews I've red so far are either plain wrong, made by people that don't know what they're talking about, or are not the type of player that enjoy tactical gameplay at this level of realism. Don't blame the devs if you're either incapable of playing intelligent games, or used to couch dwelling console arcadians. The game was never ment to be played by the likes of you!

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review on Steam. Hell Let Loose is the WW2 FPS that I have waited for, for years. Its a very good game, even in its Early Access stage it manages to outshine nearly all of its peers.  I was seriously surprised by how good this is....  Its well optimised unlike its competition (i.e Rising Storm 2: Vietnam, Heroes and Generals), it looks great graphically and the VOIP is spot on. I watched HBO's Band of Brothers years ago and loved the series and this game reminds me of it so much. A truly epic game in the making.. Forget Battlefield 1 or 5. Forget C.O.D WW2.  They are ♥♥♥♥♥ in comparison.  And before anyone accuses me of bias. I own all those games I just mentioned. I can only hope that the developers don't ♥♥♥♥ this game up before full release, as this could be the WW2 FPS king for years to come.EDIT: This review was made in 2019. Its now 2021. The developers have really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the game up.  The latest updates have caused frame rates to drop by 20 FPS on my machine across every map whilst using more resources.  Foliage takes ages to draw in at close distances. And thats IF it draws in at all.. Character movement has been slowed. The game crashes more than I have ever experienced.  The addition of being able to use a controller was pointless. It feels clunky like a generic PS2 game.The game is still piss poorly optimised.  Which is something I expected the dev's to address before adding all the latest content and features. But it's clear they won't do this.  They will just add maps and teams without real testing.  This is proven with the launch of every update, which breaks the game every time.This game had some much promise, to which I got friends to purchase the game.  Now I have been made to look like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot because of this.  I cannot defend the game or its makers any longer.Such a shame, as this game had serious potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great when Black Matter was still running the show and keeping the game true to its roots, rather than another COD or BF copy. Unfortunately, with the advent of Team 17 obtaining Hell Let Loose, it has strayed away from its aim to be a solid and historically inspired WW2 game and is now leaning towards the fantasy of BFV.With Update 14, HLL is no longer the iconic game that carved its niche amongst its loyal fanbase, instead like other developers, selling out and trying to be something its not in hopes of being the "next best thing" following in the footsteps of BF 2042. I don't understand why its so hard for developers to understand, betraying your gamer base is akin to killing your own game, nice and simple.The fact the Brits in the new update start with a P14 instead of a SMLE makes absolutely no sense, and what the hell is up with the uniforms? Stop trying to be BFV or COD, stick to being as accurate as possible, we don't need your inspired ideas, stick to the historic source material, or we'll pull a Henry Cavill in the Witcher with their "inspired bullsh**".Hopefully the ignorant fools at Team 17 can actually read and understand the feedback the community is providing, otherwise they'll just end up killing their own franchise.TLDR* Game started great with BM, got sold to T17 becames BFV high fantasy WW2 BS and is killing off its player base, not worth the purchase.*Update following response from Wombat*While the change in direction and attitude is promising, I remain sceptical and would gladly be proven wrong. It required mass negative feedback on Steam, which is deserved considering the significant decline in product quality (ie patch & trailer), before any meaningful statement was made and was only addressed after an impact on their pocketbook.The fact that the update came and multiple inaccuracies were overlooked, many of which an amateur with a passing interest in WWII and google could correctly inform you about is mind-boggling.The target audience is not your average COD plebeian, despite that being what the higher-ups appear to be targeting to a mild success. We're looking for something more challenging than your run and gun, die, respawn. Up until the update, I have had a great time communicating and working with random players towards an objective, with intermittent roleplaying that livened the game up and added to its charm. Following the update, I heard trash talking, players telling others to shut-up, and numerous incidents of teamkilling, all of which came from new low level players. This ultimately led to a decline in the quality of players, and the game was no longer the one I enjoyed with my friends.Until the game is actually improved, its all words, I hope the devs and T17 actually put into action what they intend to and maintain a semblance of the quality of the game following the IP acquisition from Black Matter.TLDR 2: Use your actions, not words, we've all heard the backpedalling from dev's and PR reps when they mess up, only I've never seen a game I enjoyed do this badly. I'll hold my judgement until the game is actually brought back to the standard I enjoyed prior to T17's acquisition.
