_childDocuments_.review: This game does good and bad things. It seems like it has some "casual" features to it, which appeals more to the console players as this game is also on consoles, but it also tries to be hardcore in some aspects, and this sort of conflict of identity that this game has annoys me. But here are the things I CAN say about this game.The gunplay feels good overall. Enemies usually drop with 1 or 2 shots, only small caliber guns take 3. There is no zoom for aiming for most of the weapons, there is a little bit of zoom when you hold shift, you can do it for about 7 seconds and then you need to wait a little, it makes your aim quite steady. I do like that there is no zoom, this makes the firefights more interesting and not everyone becomes a sniper like in some games. It would be cool if you could rest your weapon on a wall or on a rock to make it more steady (if there was any sway to begind with) but maybe thats asking too much. There seems to be bulletdrop and you have to lead your target. Id say that this is one of those games where the terrain really helps with camouflage, it's quite hard to see enemies prone on a forest. So if you think something is an enemy, shoot it! suppress an area and you might get a kill. Suppression works really well in this game, it disturbs your vision and jolts your aim, so make sure to suppress the enemy when you wanna move. The maps look quite nice on higher settings but i have the settings on low as i only have a GTX 1650, it runs the game from 40 to 70 fps.----------------------------------------------Now to the annoying things, some are major and some are just some comments about the game:1. There is no stamina implemented yet, you can run forever and it wont really affect your aim in any way, so a guy can run run run and turn and shoot you from 150 meters easy, specially if they hold shift. Just the fact that you have perfect aim after a 400 meter sprint is what kind of bothers me. Also, you can fire while strafing without ANY sway to your aim.2. When you die, you FIRST you need to give up, then have to wait 10 seconds and you can't do anything at that time, not even change class, then you need to press space, if you don't then you'll just stay in that screen forever. Then you have to click on where you wanna spawn and wait for the timer on that spawn point, if you don't click spawn soon enough then you'll have to wait another 40 seconds. This happens a lot when you are trying to change class. This is not like other games such as squad, squad does a much better job at this. So the gameplay feels casual but having to wait 1 minute (or more) to spawn and die again shortly is sort of annoying, a smoother procedure to respawn would fix this, so less screens and less buttons between death and respawing.3. The spawnpoints, this is what annoys me the most. So this game requires players to build spawn points for the team or for their own squad. This is where it tries to be a hardcore game with an overall casual gameplay. It happens often where players are defending the forward-most objective and they lose their spawnpoints that get overrun and the point itself, and the only spawnpoint is at base, and most players just wait for someone to create a spawnpoint. So all the team spawns at base and the enemies are already done capturing the next point. Games are usually over when this happens, a lot of players leave the match. A sort of fix to this would to have a gamemode where there is a spawnpoint at the objective BEFORE the objective you are defending / attacking, a more casual approach, sort of like red orchestra 2 or rising storm 2.4. Players do not communicate in this game, its quite rare, and if they do its only your squadmates. This often makes it so the spawnpoint issue happens over and over again and it also feels like you're playing on your own. There is barely any teamwork in this, and this wouldn't be a problem if it weren't for the requirement of it. If you don't coordinate to place spawnpoints then the match is over.5. Medics have barely any use as you don't really have tickets in this game, if you die, whatever. Waiting for a medic could take just as long as respawning. ALSO if you get revived and die instantly, it's 3x slower than just giving up and respawning instantly. Medics still have no use.6. Sadly you cannot zero your gun, I wish I could zero it to 200 or 300 meters when I have to. For instance the m1 carbine has a lot of drop, so zeroing it to 200 would be great for those longer engagements.7. Objectives seem to sometimes zig-zag on the map and this leaves a lot of empty unused space, so what usually happens is that the players run from the south side of the map to the north, from the previous to the next objective, so usually when players capture, they B line for the next objective and leave the previous one unattended, so enemies can usually easily flank since the map is too wide and just go for your abandoned objective while the rest of your team is in battle. This is straight up bad game design, it's a huge map and it's mostly unused and the objectives seem to be always the same. If the main gamemode was to advance evenly throughout the map, like a frontline and capture the most tyles, then the map could be better used.I believe you lose the XP you gained during the match if you don't stick until the end (apparently). So if you wanna level up so you can get better weapons then you have to stick until the end of the match, but maybe i'm wrong.----------------------------------------------I bought this game because i wanted something for a good time, where I don't have to worry like in squad or post scriptum, where i can just have some fun with the game mechanics that i like and this game does a good job overall but the points above annoy me. I wanted something to replace that feeling i had with Day of Defeat where i can just hop on and have some fun without worrying too much, but with modern gameplay, post scriptum followed the same path as squad so it doesn't fit that role. This game tries to have mechanics like in squad but it also tries to be confortable for console players it seems. So do I recommend this game? Yes and no. If some of these annoying things are fixed, those being number 1, 2 and 3 then i would make it a definitive yes.Edit: I'd like to add that there are only 3 servers for south america, two are always full and the last one empty cause players won't join an empty server. So we have to join north american servers which are also full most of the time, so it's another 10 minutes of waiting just so you can suffer in a game.November 2024:Yeah this game is still ♥♥♥♥. A lot of stupid ♥♥♥♥ plague this game and overall i think it's just filled with bad game design and lacks a lot of QoL stuff. I keep coming back hoping its a bit better but the things that annoy me the most are still there and won't ever be changed cause the money is still coming in for them i guess.

It's a bit more relaxed than the most hardcore tactical team based shooters, but the game does not suffer from this as the overall experience and team-play is excellent.The action is intense, and the quiet moments are suspenseful.The models and graphics are impressive, the controls feel fluid and natural (not janky), and the community so far has been great. _childDocuments_.review: I'll begin this review by saying that with 20 hrs into the game now, I finally have a feel of what the game is and how to be successful at it. Hell Let Loose is an excellent platform with loads of potential. As new playable armies are released and new maps come out I can see this being the best WWII FPS sim available to date. The gameplay is fantastic, graphics are spectacular, and the immersive sound is some of the best. There are a handful of drawbacks. Namely, it is an early access title so it feels a little unpolished. Buggy accuracy showed its ugly face even when not in combat, as it seems like on high rate of fire weapons it runs into hit registry failing to account for half of the fired shots. Finding a server is seizure inducing at times, half of the given servers are privately owned and will kick you without a second thought for even the most trivial of things (i.e. not speaking to your squad, not doing exactly as the commander says, even if you're in a squad alone). The other half of the servers are official and are full to breaking point 24/7. One last feature that is odd and jarring coming from other tactical FPS, is the spawn system. It focuses on Outposts placed by squad leads, and garrisons that are team wide. The spawn timers are wave-based, and are different for EACH spawn location.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose lies at an excellent intersection between Battlefield, Squad and Insurgency. It brings the scale of the former, the logistics and teamwork of the middle and immediacy of the latter to impress with its 50 vs 50 WW2 battles that teeter between bombastic chaos and matter-of-fact single shot kills. Having just two modes - a 90 minute Warfare mode with single objective conquest, and the staggered 30 minute Offensive mode where a frontline is gradually and permanently pushed back by attackers -, restricting loadout customisation to two or three presets and no allowance for custom rules might seem overly strict or boring to some, but really it allows the game to enjoy an unusual focus foRr a genre that's by now bogged down in noise and lack of polish. HLL's ambition is to push you into almost a slice of life style of storytelling, where each individual is but a small cog in a grand machine.It does this by dividing teams into neat hierarchies, where equipment and abilities are restricted to roles, themselves restricted to categories: At the top of the pyramid sits the commander, who gets access to the leader voice chat channel to communicate with officers, and who can use map-wide abilities like supply drops, bombing runs, spawn vehicles or issue map marker orders for the team. Beneath the commander are the officers, who are in charge of relaying information between their squad and other officers and the commander, and issuing orders to their squad. An infantry officer's squad who has access to the usual shooter roles: Engineers can build and destroy structures, support can provide construction supplies and ammo, medics can revive and heal teammates, assault gets access to SMGs and more grenades, and so on. Each squad is expected to follow orders from their officer and communicate as a small team of their own. Alternatively to infantry, there are special squad types for recon and armour, with two-man sniper teams and tank crews respectively, each having their own specialised roles and exclusive abilities and gear.Ideally, a match will unfold with the three squad types working together under their officers, who in turn work with other officers and their commander as one great team, shifting between attack, defence and support. The latter is most interesting, because there are cases where some players or even an entire squad will be dedicated to logistics, driving supply trucks back and forth to build defenses in controlled territory. These unofficial roles are just as important as any medic or rifleman, allowing players to fortify points, man artillery, or act as infantry support or repair crews for tanks. Participating in this massive cooperation never fails to be thrilling. I enjoy getting headshots on the frontline or sneaking into an enemy objective and laying mines down, but there's a quiet satisfaction to spending an hour transporting supplies to engineers or building intricate layers of barbed wire and barricades that's just as rewarding. Intellectually engaging with the map, the movement of the team, evaluating risk and reward - these are rare treats that make not shooting a single time the entire match just as fun as doing so a thousand times, and no matter the role, extensive use of the map and compass's grid coordinates, bearings, cardinal directions and distance measurements separates the good players from the best.Agency works differently in HLL compared to most shooters, but it's one of the first pressure points where things can go horribly wrong. A match in Battlefield can be turned around by a single person, even despite the vast scale. All it takes is a great flank and quick reflexes or helicopter pilot to potentially dominate an entire team, but in HLL the opposite is true - most conquests are a meat grinder regardless of your individual experience or skill. In fact the better both teams are, the longer conquest takes. It can thus become frustrating to have your performance tied so intrinsically to the team's. A great squad could theoretically turn the tables, but most of the time you're simply at the mercy of your officer and commander (or lack thereof), and while the highs of teamwork are higher than they otherwise would be, the lows of miscommunication and a lack of team autobalancing are very low indeed. This is offset by the game's intentional deemphasising of player stats, hiding kill/death ratios or victim/nemesis trackers away in a secondary screen, but the act of dying 20 times in a match and losing at the end still stings. Such an issue is however an unavoidable result of the demands of teamwork. When things go well - which they mostly do - HLL shines. Matches tend to ebb and flow over wide frontlines, incorporating the staccato pacing that can at times near the absurd. There are points when you'll have been lying on your stomach for five minutes until a single shot pierces the silence and your enemy a hundred metres away falls dead in a heap, and the rifle's echo fades into silence; there are others when you'll be sprinting out of a trench into a wall of enemies in a vast field scarred by craters and debris, dodging the rain of bullets and competing bombing runs as tanks charge through the cacophony and their thunderous fire sends your head spinning. The magnitude of the action can be truly impressive, and knowing that it's often the result of those 49 coordinating strangers, from infantry riflemen to sniping saboteurs all following the violent vision of a single commander at the helm, is awesome.There are some bugs, imperfections in audio, and poor level design that marr the proceedings, but presentation and controls are generally excellent, giving HLL a sleekness uncharacteristic of multiplayer shooters, and far surpassing Arma 3, Squad, or any other milsims. And realistically, you're going to struggle to find another indie/AA game that looks or sounds as good as this, much less at such an enormous scale. HLL isn't a perfect game by any means, but its relentless focus on teamwork, trimming of fat, and straightforward design make it the best time I've had with a shooter in eons. There isn't much room for one man army heroics in its action, with all facets of its design encouraging and rewarding teamwork instead. With ample space for gameplay styles from solitary sabotage to quiet construction and frontline armoured engagements, there's something for everyone. It's a mature game for players who are tired of the uncontrolled chaos of Battlefield or Call of Duty that makes most matches blend together into an indistinct haze of inconsequential mass slaughter, and enormously thankfully it also eschews their stats pages, storefronts, caricaturesque customisation, battle passes, daily missions and endless notifications and popups that make those competitors become overwhelming assaults on your senses that also demand to be treated like a second job. It still needs some polish, and some new maps and equipment would be welcome, but I've hugely enjoyed my time playing HLL. Cerebral without becoming exclusionary, intense without becoming mind-numbing, I cannot recommend this enough as a minimalistic breath of fresh air.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is an enjoyably rough slow-paced, teamwork oriented, communication driven tactical shooter with dynamic game-play that requires good strategy and the reality, lot's of experience. There's so much to learn about the game and since it's pretty large-scale (50v50, 1:1 maps) most tend to not really grasp the true concept of the game, expecting to to be more akin to Battlefield. This is not Battlefield. It's closer to squad, except WW2 PTSD. The matches are meant to be long, and often are... if you leave mid-match or even at the end of the match before your XP is calculated, all progress is lost as if it didn't happen. Just like any other game, it has it's issues. Physics aren't the best, particularly for the armored vehicles. It can honestly be a little frustrating when a wimpy street light or tree/bush, or really any other small wooden object and bump in the road puts a 30 ton war machine traveling 20km/h at a complete stop or even flips the damn thing like it's paper weight. Infantry game-play for the most part is quite smooth, interactive and certainly requires skill as well as good eye-sight. There is a proximity chat, but you unfortunately (I'm sure there's a valid reason) cannot communicate with the enemy. Graphics, sound effects, visual effects, all are very stunning and I wouldn't expect any less coming from the UE. I will admit that in my opinion this is still the best WW2 shooter out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I have almost 600 hours in this game and I find myself always coming back for more. _childDocuments_.review: This game does not respect your time. Allow me to explain: You know how game designers have ways to make games generally more enjoyable or streamlined for the gamer? Not this game! Your first clue is the fact that you can't skip any of the intro credits. Next? Actually spawning in the game. This game is unique in that it uses several respawn timers to get back in the game. You die? You get a 10 second timer to contemplate respawning, then you get another timer until you actually respawn. The average wait-time can be between 20-90 seconds.  Spawn in the middle of an artillery barrage and die immediately? Too bad. You'll need to wait at least another 30 seconds before you can do anything. Bring a book. You'll need it. Finally, the running. Oooooooh boooy. The maps are massive (thats actually a positive), to get anywhere you need to run (which for some reason, you run like an obese polio victim), or you need to be in a squad with a competent squad leader who can place spawn points. Here's the issue: Squads are set to 6 people (why??) which often means squads are capped, or locked. If you join a game, you're unlikely to get in a squad unless you make one, which means you'll play as a squad lead, or not at all.Oh did I mention there's no base shielding for the starting spawns? The enemy can literally drive up in a tank and blast you away and there's nothing you can do about it. Enjoy that. But on the positive side, tanks are fun and the game is pretty. So. Theres that.

_childDocuments_.review: Shows promise but still a lil ganky. This is still early access keep in mind. Jun/2019Pros:Gives that old BF 1942 feel with a facelift.Firefights are pretty fun. Being stuck in crossfire is crazy.Squad based but can Lone Wolf if you like.Team area chat is hilarious.Community is positive, unlike most FPS's. Cons:Gun fire needs work, as in physics.Gun balance needs work. LMG's feel weak compared to other fps. They can lay down coverfire, but imo could dish out more damage and have tad more accuracy when prone.Be nice to know how one dies.Movement is a bit stiff. Animations etc.All the pros make the game a blast, but the cons can make you a lil disappointed at times.Update: 12/1/2019Same points as before. Only things that has changed is the player base is more focused. 1) Lone Wolf is frown upon. Better use your mic or peeps will be upset. Also "Know your Role" is in effect. So go into your control menu and learn somethang.2) Gun accuracy has improved a lot. Sounds of rounds buzzing by is awesome too.3) Still have no clue what killed ya when downed...4) Battles feel a lot more intense than last I remembered. Rounds, explosions going off everywhere and people yelling why your team is failing LOL.5) There are new maps and they are pretty good. Map overlay has been improved too, more detail.6) Added motion blur, I have a 1080Ti and everytime it went into blur mode the game bogged. Did not look if it could be turned off. But I would turn it off if possible.7) Animations still feel ganky when moving, hoping objects etc. Really hope this gets an overhaul.Over all game is shaping up, still needs work. But shows they are improving it. Battles can be crazy, But the side splitting LOL's seem to have faded with Peeps that are focused on winning. As one would think for a tactical fps. I dont play it much due to the long battles. Work kicks my butt and the long matches is a bit much when I get home.Which brings me to something I forgot to mention when I first made this review, this is not CoD or even BF. These battles take 1hr to 30mins to complete. So if fast pace combat with rounds that are over in 20mins is what you like, this game would not be for you. Think of this as BF's big brother, he means business and does not care for lil rifle charms or stickers for his helmet. Only cares about winning the battle.All and All if you like tactical fps, this game should have a place in your library.See ya on the Battlefield and Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Its unfortunate that I have to not recommend this game. I wish there was a neutral button, but in lack of one I will say no. I've played over 100 hours in squad, and coming to this game from squad is almost the same, but the developers have made some weird game choices. In squad you have tickets, and each life/vehicle is a certain amount of tickets. The more you die, the more tickets you expend, same with the vehicles that are destroyed. This game is a tug of war map, like squad, but instead of tickets all there is is a timer. Now this seems like a small difference, but it really hampers one of the classes in the game, the medic.In Squad when you get revived instead of respawning, you don't loose the ticket. This gives you incentives to wait for a medic or a teammate to come and revive you. Since HLL game doesn't have ticket mechanic, it doesnt matter that you die. So instead the developers have implemented pointless counters. You die, have to hold F to 'let go' for around 5 seconds, and respawn. This sends you to a useless 'Killed in Action' screen that you cant do anything for 10 seconds, not even look at the map, then you have to press space to get out of that and wait for the timer to respawn. Again, unlike Squad where if you wait for a medic to come to revive you, but you end up giving up anyway, your timer to respawn at the map screen counts the time you waited to get revived. HLL does not. The timers always count down, and restart when they hit zero, giving a more 'wave' feeling to the forces. IF your team is implimenting the spawn points like they should be, you should be able to spawn somewhere near the front line, thus making the medic even more useless. In fact, there are few players even playing with the medic now, that it makes it pointless to wait anyway. But the teamplay in HLL is lacking compared to squad to begin with. No squad leader talks or gives directions. Everyone is silent. When you can actually find a good SL its a great game, and you can actually utilize the medic in appropriate ways. But right now, there are very large flaws that aren't getting addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: If only there where a server for Africa!It shows great promise and offers a refreshing take on the historical genre. However, there are a few aspects that could benefit from improvement.First and foremost, the game's strengths lie in its attention to detail and dedication to historical accuracy. The battles feel intense and realistic, making players truly feel like they are in the midst of a warzone. The use of authentic weaponry and vehicles adds to the immersion and overall enjoyment.On the downside, the game currently lacks servers in certain regions, particularly Africa. This limitation restricts the potential player base and can lead to connectivity issues for those in underserved regions. Expanding server coverage to include Africa would not only attract more players but also create a more inclusive and diverse gaming community.While Hell Let Loose utilizes Unreal Engine 4, which enables impressive visuals, the game could still benefit from some graphical polish. A few areas, such as the shooting range, could use a graphics overhaul to enhance the overall visual experience and make it more appealing to players.Another consideration is the game's pricing structure. While a high-quality gaming experience is worth paying for, the current pricing might seem a bit steep, especially when considering the limited server availability. Developers should assess pricing options and ensure that players are getting adequate value for their investment.In conclusion, Hell Let Loose has the potential to become a standout World War II gaming experience, capturing the hearts of both history enthusiasts and fans of immersive gameplay. Addressing the server limitations, improving graphics in specific areas, and reevaluating the pricing model would undoubtedly contribute to the game's success. With continued efforts to refine and expand the game, Hell Let Loose can truly shine and attract a dedicated community, including veteran players from classic Battlefield titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much yes.Hell Let Loose fills the admittedly overfilled niche of 'WWII-themed team-based FPS', but it actually does so in a satisfying manner with an interesting twist.On the generics, the game checks all boxes in regards to graphics, sounds, weapon design, vehicles, immersion ("Eeeeeerika!").The gunplay is solid and satisfying, with the most common weaponry being one-hit-kill rifles (assuming you hit the main body, limb shots are not instantly fatal). There's no real health or injury system beyond 'if you get hit, you are either dead or you start bleeding and are on a timer to bandage'.Vehicle-wise, there's ~3 tanks of differeing weight and a number of support/transport trucks. The most striking feature is that the tanks are very realistic in regards to being utterly cumbersome to maneuver, and highly vulnerable to sneak attacks by AT infantry, whilst bringing unrivalled long-range firepower. Driving tanks is actually an art, in particular due to the layout of some maps.There's currently 3 factions, though the Sovjet Army is only present on a single map, with most maps being US Army vs Germany. There are some nuances and differences in equipment between the factions (i.e. the US fielding 3 differently priced and equipped versions of the Sherman, whilst the Germans have either the cost-efficient Panzer VI or the expensive lumbering beast that is the Tiger), but I wouldn't have noticed any particular instance of balance issues. There's no single class, equipment or rifle that is considered irredeemably OP, at worst people will generally agree that Artillery is frustrating to be on the receiving end of.But the biggest twist and key feature of the game: Logistics. It's no Foxhole,but innately, the maps are vast, with 5 sectors to fight over (in a smart mix of control-point and general frontline mechanics), and it can easily take 15 minutes to traverse the map on foot. And there's no innate spawnpoints except for the HQs on either end of the map.Instead, Squadleaders can drop Outposts for their own squad, or build garrisons to function as more permanent team-wide spawnpoints. Yet setting up garrisons requires supplies, which need you to coordinate with your Support soldiers, the Commander's supply-drop or a logistics player driving about the fatly-loaded Supply Trucks. Regularly, matches are won by the side that places their garrisons better (and dismantles the enemy's ones better), independent of individual player, or even squad-level, skill. (Additionally, supplies can be used by Engineers to set up fortifications, or by one of the AT subclasses to set up AT Cannons, which are as devastating to tanks as they are immobile and easy to take out by Infantry.)A key element of the game is intra-team communication and coordination. And the game does a splendid job providing a 3-layered VOIP (local, squad, command) of pretty solid quality, plus a nuanced system of squad & command separated map markers, giving squad leaders great tools to convey information to each other, whilst not cluttering up the maps of the grunts actually doing the fighting. It's a remarkable abstraction of needless information that improves both gameplay and realistic immersion.Of course "Team coordination in a public game with randos? Impossibru!" is a straightforward concern, and I would be lieing if I hadn't seen matches thrown by the team's utter lack of coordination. But remarkably, most matches have at least a decent level of communication, so on average I'm positively surprised by the community.If the game had any striking drawback, it would be the difficulty curve. Going into the game with no further information, you'll just spend a hours or two getting lost on the map and hear things happening before you randomly die to a sniper. Understanding the flow of the game, based around garrison placement and squad-based movement, isn't conveyed very well if you don't happen to end up with a veteran Squad Leader willing to teach you the basics. The Field Manual can give you a jumpstart, but you should not expect a casual 'dive right in' FPS experience if you pick up this title.Another minor gripe is the functional, but very slow and at times frustrating server browser (the game uses official + dedicated servers, no matchmaking): It takes a good minute to refresh the servers, and most servers use VIP slots & queues which, when combined with the loading times of the maps for non-SSD, means you'll constantly come across 95/100 servers that you cannot actually join. Filtering out 'full' servers does exactly nothing for that same reason. Add in the fact most servers enforce 'must have mic and speak this language' rules (which IS reasonable, given the game's need for coordination), and it can take a minute or five to find a server that fits your language, latency and IS actually joinable.Overall, I can strongly recommend the game for fans of highly-tactical shooters, and also to fans of 'tanks that behave more realistically than highly armored sportscars'. Just make sure to bring enough time and nerve to get past the initial learning hurdle, or join up with a friend who can show you the ropes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT A RUN-N-GUN GAME. It's best described as a strategic FPS, like a more sophisticated version of RS2. Constant communication and initiative are key, and winning a round requires more than solely killing the enemy. Here's some examples of how to lose, and not have fun (as a whole team):- No mic- Inexperienced leadership - Choosing a role for its gun- Zero coordination/cooperation with relevant team members- Defending/attacking everywhere except the objective- Expecting people to always tell you what to do- Not doing what people tell you to do- Not expressing your intentions ("what am I doing, and why am I doing it")- Being Johnny Rambo while totally disregarding everything else.I hope this was helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: Found myself alone in some foreign field, my squad obliterated by enemy ordinance. Somehow, I survived. The Americans had cut us off, I was on the far-left flank seeking refuge behind the only cover available amongst the vast snow-blanket that coated this French countryside, a dead cow. I watched from afar as a Tiger Tank was peppered with anti-tank rockets and grenades, it held its own for a while but eventually succumb to its fate. At least two more squads went down beneath a hail of machine gun fire from enemy elevated positions. I did my part, with my bolt action rifle I dropped two advancing yanks. But it attracted too much attention, scanning the field with my iron sight. I saw it and it saw me, the barrel of a Sherman roared in to life. 10/10 Would walk blindly in to the unknown again.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews, but this game deserves one. This game has gone from collecting dust in my library to being the most satisfying FPS I own. The changes made in the latest update removed all of the issues I had with the clunkiness of the shooter and I can't stop playing it now. Let me be clear, I thought this game was garbage before the update. The infantry movement, and subsequently the combat, was just awful and felt extremely rigid. The update introduced changes that are night and day with the past system and this is the most natural feeling FPS out there. There are a few quirks still, but things move at the perfect pace for a tactical shooter. Not too fast and not too slow.These devs managed to find the perfect balance between arcade and simulation, taking the best aspects from each and blending them together beautifully. Here is how I see it (Arcade --> Simulator):Call of Duty --> Battlefield --> Hell Let Loose --> Post Scriptum / Squad --> ArmaI'm also a sucker for great graphics and this game definitely delivers on that too. I know there are some optimization issues going on right now but my 2080ti has been a true champ and gotten us through these difficult times. The maps on Hell Let Loose are incredibly detailed and well done.If you haven't bought the game yet, give it a chance. It's the best WWII shooter available right now and its only going to improve going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: HLL combines some of the best aspects of Battlefield with hardcore mil-sim like Arma, then drops the player into the WWII warzone for a taste of real combat.  No bullet sponge players here, no overshields.  Like in real warfare, a single well-placed bullet can kill, so strategy and communication are key.  The game features dynamic squad composition, with each role serving a specific purpose, and squad roles ranging from general infantry to armor units to recon.  Within each squad, riflemen, medics, engineers, officers, and other roles will give players a unique focus, whether it be tank hunting, healing wounded teammates, or constructing fortifications to help the rest of the team.  Many new players may be tempted to go lone wolf or strive for an amazing K/D ratio, but this is not the game for that.  Those sorts of exploits are a fast way to get killed over and over by snipers, tanks, or just someone on defense.  This game is all about teamwork, and as such will be a bit slower paced when it comes to advancing down the map and gaining ground.  However, if you can put aside the personal glory notions, the game is crammed full of spontaneous moments of battlefield awesomeness.  There is nothing like being caught up in the middle of a massive firefight over a river crossing, with bullets flying, tanks exploding left and right, AT rockets flying overhead, and the sheer chaos that is present in a real firefight.  It's these moments that make you appreciate what this game is, and the huge sense of achievement in a successful push to an objective, or the commendations of the team commander or squad officer for a job well done.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst aspect to the game is the terrible, terrible optimization... this game runs like crap. You suffer from huge FPS drops in gunfights which are the most important part in a shooter. If you own a very performant system this might not concern you but sometimes people with 3080's need to ask for help in the forums because they cant get high FPS rates.Regarding the gameplay.. .I like some of the aspects of the classes in the game, because you need a little variety in roles to perform well as a squad. What I do not like is the squad leader role. It is super boring, just standard equipment and the ability to build outposts and garrisons. It is not uncommon that a lot of players are waiting for someone to open a squad because no one wants to play as leader and all other squads are full or private.While there is a large community with a lot of full servers, the games are often very one sided. Either you play round after round with a predictable outcome or you try your luck on another server cause there is no team balancing. It's also not possible to create a lobby with your friends and join a server together. The squads are disbanded every round which is very sad because often i wish that i would keep playing together with some other good and communicative players. This also makes it impossible to balance rounds taking squad performances into account.The balancing of weaponry is a bit tricky.. this game tries to be authentic, but that also leads to some imbalance of the factions. For example: the german Tiger tank is often untouchable and oneshots the other tanks or the americans field semi-automatic weapons while the germans have to reload after every shot. The imbalance regarding guns changes somewhat tho when you unlock some loadouts for each role.TL;DR:While i dont mind the authenticy, the performance issues and features regarding squad gameplay need to be adressed in order to recommend this game. As usuall for an EA game it has a lot of potential, but it remains to be seen whether they will be able to use it. Whith some QoL improvements this game should be a blast as long as you dont mind the slow paced gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Every... single... thing... that Team 17 has done for this game is of abysmal quality and has stripped it of its identity to appeal to the mass Call of Duty and Battlefield audience.Update 13.5Removed the previous backdrop for seemingly no reason and replaced the rotating list of the countries' victory songs that played in the main menu with only one generic and poorly looped song.Update 14Oh boy... Half-assedly added the horribly balanced, completely historically inaccurate British faction into the game alongside poorly balanced, giant engagement maps that make it heaven for only a small select of infantry roles, and hell for all the others. Swapped the identifiable, tasteful, and mature logo of the game with a childish, cheap looking logo and title that is more like a mobile game than a mil-sim game that takes itself seriously. Changed the movement speed by 25% to 18 kph, which matches some of the tanks' top speed in the highest gear, and added in new movement mechanics like the dive to appeal to those who were more familiar with the fast-paced, run-and-gun play style of games like Call of Duty and Battlefield. And all the while never change any parts of the game that will be affected by such movement changes, like player inertia, respawn times, vehicle speeds, and time to get to point as the defensive team on Offensive gamemode matches. The British guns have sway, recoil, and iron sights that don't match at all any of the previous weaponry in the game in terms of quality and balance. And so so so much more.Update 15 trailerThis trailer is perhaps the lowest quality trailer I have ever seen in my life. It screams its an animation a 15 year old made in 2 days on his chromebook for a meme. The amount of issues in the trailer is nearly uncountable. Some of the notable things that caught my eye were the improperly modeled M1 Garands, the horribly janky animations, the t-poses, the floating arms, only 1 or 2 guys being animated per scene even when multiple people are being featured in a shot, the voice acting sounding like it was recorded in a bath tub by the animator's uncle Gary, grass covering an entire shot of a soldier throwing a grenade, the repeating grass textures on a completely flat plane, the scenery being composes of like 4 trees, 2 flat houses, an anti-tank gun, and some sandbags, the hilarious up-close face shots, and it goes on and on. I question what the trailer was even for, why did it need to be made? What were they trying to show off? The parachuting from the planes? Well it's been confirmed not even that is coming to the game.The whole point of me bringing up all of this is it shows Team 17's incompetence with this game. If they cannot spare the time or resources to make a simple trailer, then how could we trust Team 17 with this game? Nothing they have added has sparked any sort of confidence within the community, and even those where were on Team 17's defense are abandoning the ship after that trailer.I want to end with this. It was just half a year ago that I started tanking with 2 of my buddies and it honestly became some of the most fun, most memorable moments I have ever had gaming in my life. We got pretty good and were excited to get better. It is an absolute tragedy, that just some months later, the game is on its way into the grave...

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Graphics are crisp and clear, although you should make a few tweaks (make sure your team name tags set to max, test some of the other setting to see what your card can handle best, etc...).  There are videos out there that explain the settings pretty well.  The game is fairly easy to learn, plenty of roles to play for your given play style.  The hacking issues they had in the early days seems to have been addressed  (that are detectable to most at least even though occasionally you wonder how some shots are made lol).  The lack of hacking was huge for me and a determining factor for choosing to purchase it in the first place.  I've only seen two in the past and they were early 2020 (one machine gunner shooting from far away and through things and one speed hacker running X10 speed).  They were nearly immediately detected by the players and kicked not just from the match but banned from the server.  The games admin functions to report misuse works well and the admins are attentive.  I've not seen anything noticeable since then.Each new version seems to be developed with thought, tested well, and have few noticeable issues.  There are a few things not directly related to game play that should be addressed.  For example, the queues indicating there are 95 people in a match and when you try to join the queue is full, recon dweebs that have a friend join a match - or they do with a second account only to lock it and then log off the spotter so they can be sniper heroes, or locking tank groups with only one person, etc...basically the people that don't care about the team or how much they contribute.  Typically they are the ones with the fewest contributing points at the end.  Overall, great game and I would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is an intense and immersive World War II shooter game that offers an exceptional experience for all players. This tactical game is set in a detailed and realistic battlefield where two factions fight for control in different maps.The graphics and sound effects in Hell Let Loose are impressive, adding to the game's overall realism. The game's historical accuracy, realism, and teamwork-based gameplay offer a unique experience that sets it apart from other WW2 shooters.The game offers a range of different classes, each with its strengths and weaknesses, motivating players to find the best tactics to win the game. Players can choose between different roles, including infantry, armor, support, and recon.One criticism leveled at the game is its steep learning curve that may deter casual gamers. However, the game offers useful tutorials and training modes that can help onboard new players.In summary, Hell Let Loose is an authentic and engaging simulation of WW2 warfare that offers a unique, immersive gameplay experience. It's an intense game that aims to immerse players in the typically brutal and often unforgiving nature of war, shooting to kill with every moment feeling like it counts towards winning the war.

_childDocuments_.review: As a new player to Hell Let Loose, I have to say that my experience with this game has been nothing short of amazing. Developed by Black Matter, this World War II first-person shooter game offers an immersive and realistic gaming experience that is both thrilling and satisfying.One of the things I love about Hell Let Loose is the attention to detail. From the sound of gunfire to the movements of the soldiers, everything feels incredibly authentic and realistic. This level of detail makes the game feel like a true representation of the chaos and danger of war, and it's easy to get fully immersed in the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game about a year ago and didn't like it at the time so I refunded it.Since it was on sale this week and I had some leftover funds in my Steam wallet I thought I'd give it another try, since the game just had multiple updates since the last time. At that time my major complaints were based on the overall gameplay and performance of this game.Now, a full year (or more) forward I tried the game again, and while I told myself I will not refund this game AGAIN, it's getting harder and harder. (that's what she said) I am a big fan of Red Orchestra 2/Rising Storm and Rising Storm 2: Vietnam. Those games all appealed very much to me and since both those games are dying out I am craving a similar experience. Hence the reason I (re-)bought Hell Let Loose.Here's a list of some of the things that I generally like about this game;- Somewhere inbetween arcade and mil-sim. It's not as realistic as Squad or Post Scriptum, but also not as arcade as, say, Battlefield (the older ones, not the hot mess that is 2042).- Weapons and vehicles look cool- Graphics look good but are nothing special. But then again; gameplay -> graphics- Movement is slow but also fast. What I mean by this is that the player movement itself is quite slow but the actual animations for reloading, swapping weapons and such is quite fast. Mantling is also very fluent and miles better than what RS2:V uses.Here's a list of some of the things that I generally dislike about this game:- Sounds are still weak as hell. MG42 sounds are a bit better but still sounds.. off. Single shot weapons are even worse.- Sound engine in general is weird. If a teammate shoots his weapon from around 30m away from me, it sounds like its coming from behind me.- The frontline system. While a cool concept, the battle is not really evolving or changing all that much. It's a constant back and forth of moving which usually ends in a bit of a stalemate with both sides trying to move through enemy lines and occasionally pulling it off, but then dying and see their entire move get shattered by the opponent since it's their territory. There is basically no room for flanking.- Hardly any communication. I've been in several servers and I see an occasional chat message but that's about it. Not even the Commander communicates with his team all that often.- The entire UI. What a mess is that. Who even thought of that? The map is barely readable as you can barely see your own position let alone your teammates positions. I get that because of the high player count it's hard to cramp it all in one map but at least point my squadmates to me. Also the entire way the loadout system works is just annoying. The entire screen is just cluttered and I feel like I'm seeing way too much at once. - Respawning. Having to wait half a minute or a minute just to play a game just isn't fun to me. I get that the timer shouldn't be short because of the way the entire game modes are built but if I have to wait a full minute just to spawn on my squadmates I lose interest very fast. What doesn't help either is that you have to stare at a menu at this time without any sound whatsoever.- Practically no VO. There's an occasional grunt from soldiers but there's no VO for capturing something or anything. Now I do get that this isn't a thing in real life either, but at least hearing soldiers speak, shout and such creates an entirely different experience.- No way of telling whether you're doing something useful or not. There's some symbols on the map but again, it's very cluttered.- Dying from random things. I think I got killed by either grenades or bombs or something, I really don't know. In the games defense; I don't know what everything is so identifying what killed me is practically impossible. As I said before, it's really annoying to get killed on my own spawnpoint by 1 enemy soldier that just happened to move into our territory without being seen.I feel like this game could really benefit from another more "arcadish" gamemode like RO2 had. The territories gamemode they designed is certainly not the most perfect but at least people knew what was going on and where they should advance. You die somewhere? Then you get the choice to try the same route or try something different.Also I'd love to see a Pacific theatre for this game. Fighting as Japan vs. Americans just hit different and can spice up a game greatly, especially because there's already other games that do just this theatre (Post Scriptum, Enlisted).I will take a small break from this game as I don't think I've given it a full try yet. If I ever change my mind, fair enough, I will change my review/opinion accordingly.Also keep in mind that this is my opinion and it is from a new-player's point of view. These are the thoughts and experiences that I had while playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is entertaining and by all means a good time to have but the weakness is that those moments are few and far between the more occasional and frequent frustrating moments that populate your game time.      When, and only when, you get competent commanders and squad leaders on BOTH sides is the game enjoyable. The other times the game is frustrating due to multiple reasons that all more or less stem from the lack of team cohesion and leadership.      There are those that will point out that war is very confusing and this would be accurate, and while we can      agree and this is an appropriate informational point. This is a video game and they should be more      entertaining, especially considering the point we are trying to have some semblance of fun.     The role of artillery does do the job historically and mechanically well it does not work in-game. The amount of times all players have complained about artillery, both by friendly fire and enemy, makes the game  stagnate and frustrate the players getting killed over and over.     The role of recon is more often than not to just go to the enemy spawn and outright spawn kill whoever is unlucky enough to try and spawn there including the artillery crew. Making this not fun for either side since one side cannot play the game and the other reduced to baby sitting a specific area and mindlessly clicking those that don't know where they are being shot from.     The terrain as a tank crew is some of the most confusing and frustrating things as trees which would normally stop a tank and make it run over it take a few minutes the tank can just phase through no problem  but the moment a ditch or small hill is under the tracks  the tank loses all speed and momentum. Not to mention how some of the hills just outright stop and make the  tank stuck with no chance of it being stuck. Additionally tank crews are limited to three people severely hampers the crew as far as communication and cohesion, there should be at the very least four to a tank since the squad leader can easily flex as radio operator to ease his job of directing orders easier.All in all either I expect the to either 'fix itself' or at least address the issues that I laid or and the community has voiced their opinions and grieve about to make the game enjoyable for all.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game out of love, I found these heavy issues that signal very big red flags for the game, that need dev addressing. I'm running it with a RTX 2070 and I'm only getting around 45 FPS in MID settings, with one to two stutters every minute and some serious FPS drops. It's slowly getting there, but still the stiffness is just way too much to handle, transitions from running to walking to aiming, missing climbing animations that are important, a lot of prone clipping, among others. There is very little destruction (understandable for a heavy game like this), but traversing terrain with a tank is really, and I mean, REALLY hard given that you can't even pass over a low wooden fence, sometimes not even simple rocks. Tank driving is difficult per se, which I find great, but this makes it annoying instead of challenging. Tank over railway is also super bugged, sometimes you go out flying into the air.If you still want to support the game tolerating this stuff,  Once they fix all of these issues, I can guarantee it'll be the best WW2 shooter out there. I have thousands of hours playing realistic shooters, and somewhow I deeply feel that gameplaywise this software can become possibly the best in terms of a hardcore WW2 simulator given enough time. Devs... it is up to you. MAKE IT HAPPEN. You have my support.

_childDocuments_.review: Credit where credit is due, Team 17 have reverted the speed increase and the game has gone back to its classic feeling, bugs and stuttering still occurs, but a step in the right direction nonetheless.(Leaving the old review in)________________________________________________________________________Don't bother, Team 17 owns it now, ruining what could've been one of the greats. Shame.The reason why I've not recommended this game is because of they way the new developers have handled the game since gaining ownership.Just before Team 17 took over, the game was headed in a truly great direction. Most games that you played contained some great moments, moments that you really crave in a realistic shooter on a grand scale, intertwined with an excellent community driven by teamwork to achieve victory. You could easily have an excellent experience in one game with your friends, or by joining a random squad, something that Squad, Post Scriptum and similar games just don't quite fulfil.The problem with this game now is that they're trying to change the gameplay by joining the other popular FPS games, faster paced.And by that, I mean increased movement speed, crouching, crawling, sprinting, running around corners and rinsing players, whereas before, it was a little slower with a more tactical feeling. It feels closer to a Call of Duty game than an immersive, realistic shooter.Nowadays, you can catch up to a tank by sprinting at it. You're able to attach a mine to it, and it's gone. Before this, the tank was feared, requiring anti tank weapons to take it down. Being part of a tank crew was fairly difficult to begin with, anti tank is deadly and with correct decision making really made it feel like you were on the edge of being very successful and completely failing, the perfect balance.Now? You're terrified of infantry, you can try driving away but more than likely you will explode and be sent to the respawn screen, it is incredibly frustrating to watch this gem of a game reach a point where it has great potential to do more, now the current dev team wants to take all of that progress to make it more popular by making it faster paced for the masses.Please do not buy this game and encourage the direction, the FPS genre NEEDS a game like this to scratch an itch that no other FPS game has right now, and it's a damn shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is a realistic and authentic WWII first person shooter for the thinking person who appreciates historical accuracy. Victory requires patience, teamwork within the various squad roles, and individual marksmanship. The lack of juvenile cosmetics and anachronistic weapon attachments focuses the player on actually being apart of the team, and reward something other than K/D. There are two progression tracks: overall rank and class proficiency, and all squad actions produce XP towards ranking up these tracks. Weapons have realistic range and damage and incoming fire produces a significant suppression effect. Realistic movement and jump speeds mean that bunny hoppers from COD perish in no-man's land like the scum they are. Most importantly, as of this review in late May 2022, there is a thriving community and no lack of full servers. If Battlefield V has left you wanting, try this.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 70 hours in and I feel like I'm still figuring this game out. The developers are also figuring it out. I will say, I hate this game and love it. It's what I wish Call of Duty: United Offensive was 20 years ago, sorry 17 years ago. An immersive world war 2 shooter that feels like a massive battle. And this game delivers there. But it also hurts to play. You'll slowly start to realize that nodes, resources, and garrisons are key to winning the game along with a solid commander, and competent teammates. And sometimes you magically find all of that and get pummeled because the other team captured the middle spawn first. I want this game to be great because it is close to that. It is starting to lean towards Post Scriptum which feels dead in the water with so much to learn and build. People want to run into a battle and shoot. I'm tired of watching youtube videos to figure out what I'm supposed to be doing to win. Wild Bill Jammin' is the only one out there, as far as I know, providing critical feedback to the developers while ♥♥♥♥♥ are out there complaining that people hate change. Change is good when things don't work. Keep it simple and make the basics feel great like Insurgency: Sandstorm has done.

_childDocuments_.review: Both developers, Black Matter and Team17, refuse to fix game breaking bugs and performance issues. While the game has unique highs that are not reached by many other games, it impossible to reach said highs when the game continuously crashes due to poor optimization, quality control, and overall lack of testing. It's a damn shame because I frankly enjoy this game.I still would not recommend. Performance has gotten worse.June 1, 2023: The new developers have removed any notion of transparency in the direction of the game. The game is clearly changing into a game I did not originally purchase. June 9, 2023: I fixed some user end issues that prevent the game from running. Having spent more time with most recent update, previous criticisms still stand around existing glaring issues and direction of game. Current developer team appears to be rushing out content with little to no attention to quality. A true quality of quantity approach. June 12, 2023: After seeing the absolute joke of a trailer for update 15 I am convinced of the direction of Hell Let Loose. It is clear that the acquisition by Team17 was done without consideration for their own abilities, the fanbase, and most of all care for the subject. While I have previously recommended and even bought the game for friends, I can not recommend it.June 22, 2023: After a large community backlash of the Update 15 trailer, Team17 chose to postpone the update and in turn focus on quality and fixing issues introduced as communicated in Dev brief 190. However, as of this morning with the roll out of the Update 14 patch that was intended to address some of the issues introduced in the update, the game is broken further. Server list indicates that the update has killed a lot of servers, which is being corroborated by known community server admins. The brief time I did manage to get into game, there appeared to be new bugs (typing while crouching) introduced while amplifying existing bugs (loadout bug). It is very clear that Team17, Cover6, Expression Games, and whatever other sketchy new studios that have been tasked with handling the Hell Let Loose IP lack the understanding of the community and IP, while also lacking the technical ability to even execute their own vision. June 28, 2023: Vehicle performance has been absolutely trashed by the latest patch. Vehicles now stutter to the point of being unusable. Prior to patch, I only have experienced this level of rubberbanding on the official servers and servers on the other side of the world. Team17's promises of improved quality control and testing are nothing more than empty promises.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is a MILSIM set in WW2 and one of the best ones out there, if you want a cod or battlefield type of game but set in WWII then look elsewhere because this game isn't for you. HLL is a slow game where careful strategy wins the game, this isn't a game where your number of kills matters but where strategic boldness prevails and map control is key.If you want a tactical game, where you have a specific role in your squad, slow-paced, and where communication is a . Then you will find this type of game more enjoyable, you don’t get overwhelmed by an absurd amount of action, you get to use your brain more. How can you capture that objective? Where could the enemies be? Can I set an ambush point or a really strong defence point? Is it viable to flank or push straight to the point? Also the cooperation between squads it’s really fun. This game lets you have all those things, with the fun shooting mechanics.This game has been out since 2019 and the devs have shown love and care for this game updating it and adding new features with Developers Briefings to keep the players up to date for what's to come, this game deserves your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Revised Review after ~100 more hours played:I've just come to realize that Hell Let Loose is a game that I hate that I love. It's painful to play, yes, that's true. And the first 20 hrs may make you feel like there's no point to it all. But as more time is spent, more cosmetics accrued, more skill is gained, it begins to come together and foment itself as a title worth returning to for many hours more. Only read below if you're interested in pure, unfiltered Peruvian copium: =====================================================================================First and foremost it's evident that some care and thought has gone into this game. Unfortunately, despite the craftsmanship the end result is something that many people may not enjoy. Primarily this is because of the sheer monotony of the gameplay. It is a very simple gameplay loop, no matter the skill of your commander. You're going to spending the majority of your time in this game either at the spawn screen or running. Running from spawn-points called "garrisons" is often a lengthy procedure as they are rarely placed down, and often very far from the fighting. The spawn timers are also very lengthy, making it feel like you're doing more waiting than fighting. It is complete luck if you enter a squad with a squad leader that places "outposts" or spawn-points that can be in enemy territory. Most of the deaths you experience will feel cheap, as you are either relentlessly spawn-killed by artillery and infantry or shot from over 200 meters away while you cower behind a hedgerow. Due to the large amount of explosives and long-range weaponry, most fights devolve into hiding behind hedgerows, popping out once in a while to take a shot. After a few bullets you are invariably killed by a grenade, tank, or shot by someone you could not see. The standard American infantry in the game has a large advantage over the German infantry, as the bolt action Kar98k rifle has a vastly inferior fire rate to the M1 Garand, Thompson, or M1A1. It's pretty much whoever shoots first wins, and if the German player misses it usually all over. The sheer length that individual matches can take is extreme, upwards of an hour. Halfway through is usually my breaking point in dealing with the reasons I have already espoused. Of course if you leave early, you get no XP. Vital squad positions are often left unfilled unless a squad leader explicitly tells someone to go a certain class. This can lead to squads without a medic, or MG, or support. The commander role is most often taken by someone that does not fundamentally understand how to use the role, and this results in lackluster gameplay for the entire team. In the end, I would not recommend this game for the reasons I have stated. There needs to be a fundamental change in the core gameplay mechanics for me to consider playing continuously.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR version: Id buy the game again at full price. Few games create a feeling as good as a fierce firefight in a town center, armor catching a ricochet next to you, planes bombing overhead, and gambling on an all in attack to clutch the middle point for a 3-2 victory in the closing minutes of a 90 minute game. Few games create the gut punch feeling of being on the losing side of that scenario.Strategy, communication, and teamwork really shine through here. The game centers around building spawn points for your team, and using them to attack and defend strategic points. The community, from what ive experienced, is probably the best in any FPS game ive played. The game is incredibly deep, despite looking simple on the surface. Find a good server and join their Discord.This is not like COD/Battlefield or any other arcade shooter, so if that is what youre looking for, look elsewhere. This is along the lines of Arma and Squad. Playing the game like Warzone will result in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ experience, and you basically playing a running simulator just to die without ever knowing what killed you.This is an immersive game with realistic "hardcore" gunplay. TTK is extremely fast, with most guns above pistol caliber killing in one shot to the torso within their effective range. Suppression with artillery, tanks, and light machine gun fire is an effective tactic. Smoke cover is a necessary tool. There is bullet penetration, travel time, and drop.Graphics can be clunky at times. Many complain of poor optimization, however I have not personally experienced performance issues. (consistent 100-120fps with a 3060ti and Ryzen 5600X, in 1440p) Bugs are there, but not gamebreaking. Most involve interacting with terrain and objects (bipods, im talking to you).DLC is all mediocre cosmetics, nothing pay to win. No microtransactions, battle pass, loot crates, or in game currency ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is the game that everyone that used to play the OG Battlefield titles had asked for in the era of modern FPS titles. This the premier WW2 hardcore FPS and will provide you with some of the most authentic gaming experience at this time.The difficulty curve is HARD. This game will punish you for any small mistake. You will run for 10 minutes to flank an enemy MG only to picked off by his assault troops watching said flank. You will be shot in the head from a random German solider in the middle of the forests of Foy and wonder where he was. However, this only provides to the rich moments of getting your own headshot and hearing the ping of your bullet hitting an enemy square in the helmet. Hearing your teammates scream for help and the squad leader barking directions to the enemy tank with its barrel and MG fixated right onto your squad's position. HLL will make you feel like you are just another cog in the machine and you will love every second of it.The community is helpful and amazing, while there are some very unruly members of HLL, a majority of people in each server will absolutely help you with any facet of the game. I can't tell you how many times I've stepped into a new role and realize I have no idea what to do, only to find a high level veteran with over 200+ hours in the game telling me step by step how to drive a tank, set up point defenses, or man the artillery. The gameplay is fluid, your shots hit hard, it's realistic. The game feels like you're in the thick of it at any moment. It's hardcore through and through. You don't feel like you're playing an arcade shooter like some WW2 COD titles, you will understand that this is the ultimate hardcore FPS shooter it markets itself to be.The sound design is amazing. MG42s sound like a buzzsaw and echo across a field. The sounds of death are real and surround you. The menu music will change from Soviet marching bands to American WW2 fight songs. The proximity chat allows you to play around even those not in your squad.Long queue times can be a bit of a barrier but the ability to pick a server that you consistently find good players to play with is awesome. If the server starts to depopulate, simply switch into a new one.Overall this is a must get if you enjoyed the old-school battlefield titles and enjoyed the feeling of 50v50 hardcore lobbies. It is simply put, one of the best FPS titles on the market today.9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game held an amazing place in the Milisim genre for a long while. It was right up there with Arma3 and Squad in terms of its gritty, squad-based realisitic gameplay. It was one of the most rewarding games in the genre with memes, solid VOIP-based teamplay, and rewarding gameplay loops. Then some crappy mobile game company called Team17 bought it from its original devs, Black Matter.The game has so rapidly decreased since then, it's almost laughable.The devs have consistently shown a complete disregard for the veteran playerbase and what made this game good: its niche gameplay loop of squad-based, tactical gameplay set in a gritty, realistic WWII setting.Squad communication is nonexistent. Armor is frustrating to play. The British faction is laughably broken with multiple glitches and bugs in both gunplay and armor. The British maps are simply not fun to play, and are a burden to the game as a whole. Team17 has released two updates since their acquisition, and have not addressed these issues at all. They have had virtually no communication with the playerbase, further eroding the already tenuous relationship they had since the acquisition. Instead they've released two lukewarm updates and a trailer that's so laughable it's been ratioed into oblivion on YouTube.Anymore, Team17 is completely devoted to watering down this incredible game into a pale shadow of what it once was: a cheap Battlefield knockoff with a crappy WWII paint slapped on top of it. All in the name of "appealing to a wider audience." The only problem is they're completely alienating their strongly dedicated playerbase in the process.Team17 has shown a complete disregard of what made this game special. They have ignored player feedback. They have radically changed the core gameplay loop from what it once was. And they will have a dead game in a year's time if they don't course correct NOW.Fix your game, T17. Stop making this into a Battlefield knockoff. Listen to your fans. Fix the bugs, don't change core gameplay loop. And maybe, just maybe we'll give this game positive reviews again. Maybe, just maybe we'll come back. Until then, it was nice knowing ya.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it on the free weekend 25th March 2021. (This was a live updated review through the weekend)Where as I generally liked the game's look and feel, i had too many game breaking issues to say I'd recommend it in its current state.1) I could not change my resolution. The item is missing from my options list. Actually, the label is there, but the selections are not there.2) After playing 2 games, I thought I'd quit out, change my fullscreen option to windowed, then fullscreen again, now it NEVER lets me load a map. Therefore my game is now permanently broken. Therefore I wont buy the gameEDIT: I managed to fix this by deleting a hidden file deep in my PC. Follow this support ticket to fix. Gameplay:+ If you have ever played Battlefield. Its EXACTLY the same but MUCH slower and with less polish. ( I also do get vibes of Call of Duty 2 but on a larger scale ). This is not a bad thing and I enjoyed playing the game.+ Guns felt fine, reloading, aiming is fine.+ Playing as a unit commander is fun, especially setting up outposts and garrisons so we could spawn near or in enemy lines. Adds a nice tactic which worked well for us.+ Most players playing the game seem very nice and very low toxicity in the servers (UK)- Running movement is too slow, in actual fact, its not much different from normal movement. - People ALWAYS pick the sniper roles because they are the only weapons with scopes- The lack of weapon options at lower levels is a little off putting for a new player- The lack of "specialist" class with small scopes is off putting for a new player ( I get the realism aspect here and I had to explain to a friend that most soldiers in WW2 didn't have a scope )- Sounds are all over the place in terms of volumes. I couldn't hear my commanders, even with voice turned all the way up. My gun volume is incredibly low. Surely it should deafen me when I shoot?- There is NO option to "TOGGLE" view down sights. I hate holding my mouse button down for sights.- There is no help or explanation on how things work while playing in game via tooltips. As a unit commander, I couldn't build a "garrison" because of "no supplies". What are supplies? Where can I get them from?- Tanks. What in gods name is going on with the tanks.A "heavy" tank is so slow, its slower than the already slow infantry. I've watched a real Tiger in real life, its very quick compared to what is potrayed in this game. I'd recommend the developers take another look at the speed.Heavy tanks are invincible to everything, even other tanks.- After 4 hours of playing. I am bored. Friday night was fun, Saturday night was an absolute bore fest. Almost felt like there were cheaters in every game and/or it just was one of those nights. Nobody spoke to each other and you were literally "running" (see above) for 15 minutes then dying instantly over and over. Got boring, very quickly.Graphics:- The game suffers from an Unreal Engine issue with resolution not scaling correctly with better monitors (Happened with Insurgency Sandstorm too until 1.7). So it looked very pixelated and washed out on my screen. Almost like it was automatically resolution dropping or just defaulting to a low resolution that I couldnt change. This is likely bound the issue that stopped me playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose is a tactical World War II shooter game that stands out from the crowd due to its immersive gameplay and impressive attention to detail. The game is set in realistic battlefields where you and your teammates work together to conquer territories, capture objectives, and ultimately win the game.One of the most striking features of Hell Let Loose is the game's stunning graphics and realistic physics. The textures are highly detailed, and the physics are so well-developed that you can feel the weight and impact of every bullet fired. This makes the gameplay feel incredibly immersive and authentic, which is especially important for a game set in a historical context like World War II.However, it's not just the graphics that make Hell Let Loose stand out. The game has a steep learning curve that can be challenging, but this is what makes it so rewarding to play. It requires strategic thinking, planning, and teamwork in a military sense. Players must communicate with their squad leaders and work together to achieve their objectives. This makes for a deeply engaging and thrilling experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat.One thing that can't be stressed enough is the importance of communication in this game. Squad leaders need to voice and relay their squad's communications in order to achieve success. This means that players who are good at communicating and coordinating with their teammates will have a significant advantage in the game.Overall, Hell Let Loose is an immaculate game that offers a unique and immersive World War II experience. The graphics and physics are astonishing, and the gameplay is challenging but rewarding. If you're looking for an intense, tactical shooter that requires critical thinking and teamwork, then Hell Let Loose is definitely worth checking out.
