_childDocuments_.review: This game is built on broken promises and lies. The "1.0" update is half baked and honestly did more to hurt the game than improve it. The Russians don't even have a light tank and the game is still riddled with bugs and performance issues, but don't worry, the game is "1.0" and finished. It feels like Russian content was just reskinned from the other factions, especially since the armor rework made all respective vehicle classes identical to each other in terms of armor and weapons.The game used to have interesting asymmetrical vehicle gameplay but the armor rework completely threw that all into the trash, despite the devs claiming that they were making the factions more asymmetrical in their dev briefings. It is an absolute joke that the Panther cannot penetrate the Sherman and T34 from the front and that the Tiger can penetrate the Jumbo from the front. The fact that they said they wanted to reduce heavy tank spam is a joke, as heavy tanks are just objectively better than other tanks, leading to heavy tanks dominating the battlefield. The only way to get rid of a heavy tank? Have your commander spawn one for your team. The resource changes (which will be talked about more down below) make it so that you can effectively spawn another heavy tank for one lost, so they will always have a battlefield presence. Not to mention the new engine immobilization's implementation is a joke, you can only destroy the engine if you get a direct rear hit, making it a completely pointless feature, because if you get behind a tank in your tank, the opposing tank is already dead. The game's armor gameplay was it's one saving grace and now its gone. The infantry and armor balance in this game is also horrid. They nerfed the hell out of handheld anti-tank weapons and then locked the anti-tank gun (which was originally unlocked by default) at anti-tank rank 6, which takes a substantial amount of time to unlock. This results in tanks basically becoming unkillable by infantry. During my time playing the 1.0 patch, my friends and I were not killed by infantry in our tank a single time, the only threat to our tank was other enemy tanks. Enemy infantry were helpless as we slaughtered them. This problem is exasperated for the Soviets, who do not have access to any proper handheld anti-tank weapons and can only plink away at tank tracks. During my time playing in German armor with my friends, there was not a single instance where Soviet infantry was able to even take out our tracks.The progression system in this game is horrid. Not only did the devs originally promise in their Kickstarter campaign that nothing would be locked behind progression, but later unlockable loadouts are just objectively better than the base class. Examples include:-The Tank Commander and Crewmen unlocking Repair Tools (which were absurdly buffed, 1 person can repair as fast as 2 people did before the 1.0 patch)-Assault unlocking a loadout with additional grenades without any drawbacks-Support unlocking a kit that allows them to drop both explosive and standard ammo crates in addition to supplies-The German Machine Gunner unlocking the MG42, which is superior ingame to the MG34The infantry unlocks also have a lot of overlap between classes, effectively changing the role of the class to a different oneExamples include:-Assault, Engineer and Anti-tank all having an unlocked loadout giving them the Satchel charge. (This is even more atrocious due to the fact that the Engineer loses it's building capabilities for the Satchel charge, effectively stripping the class of its purpose)-Support gains the ammo boxes that the Rifleman class has, and non-US Rifleman can unlock the explosives ammo box, making these two classes redundant. (Rifleman should have been removed ages ago, Squad sizes are too small for an entire squad to take every infantry role, each being limited to 1 outside of the Rifleman)-Assault and Automatic rifleman effectively unlocking each other's loadouts. (Assault loses smoke grenades for AR and Automatic rifleman gains smoke grenades with SMG)The "unique resource based RTS-inspired meta-game" is bad and has done nothing but hurt this game. Before patch 1.0, all it did was cause teams to completely steamroll the other due to the fact that the losing team did not generate as many resources as the winning team. With the current changes to the resource system, they basically nullified it's existence. Both teams generate so many resources now and I have not been in a single game where my team has run out of any of the three resources. As mentioned above, commanders can now infinitely spawn vehicles due to the insane fuel income that's default now. Every patch they make the node system worse, without fail. The first nail in the coffin was when they made it so that Nodes behind enemy lines would despawn upon losing territory. They've made the nodes even more pointless now after patch 1.0 because you aren't rewarded for building them in the frontline anymore, so everyone would just build them closer to the HQ. Why not just make Node income a part of the base income then, if the enemy team most likely will not destroy them? Better yet, just get rid of the resource/node system entirely and replace it with a more fleshed out logistics system. This game's performance is subpar at best. This game runs worse on my machine than better looking combined arms shooters, such as Battlefield and Squad, and looks worse than them too. This game is horribly optimized even when the Level of Detail at far ranges in this game is pathetic. The far models and textures in this game are low quality and blurry. The worst part is, THERE ARE OBJECTS AT FAR RANGE THAT WILL NOT RENDER. You can see people through objects at long ranges. How is this game out of early access and considered a finished product? There are many times where tanks will be behind cover and be able to shoot at you, but you can't tell if you are hitting them because they are behind invisible cover. How is this acceptable? No other combined arms shooter I have played has had this issue.Finally, this game's most atrocious sin is that it ACTIVELY ENCOURAGES people to spawn camp the enemy HQ. Why? Because the artillery pieces in the game are placed in each team's middle HQ. So in order to get rid of the enemy team's indirect fire support, you have to go into the enemy's HQ and spawn camp it to make sure that no one is able to use the artillery pieces. This would easily be fixed by giving people in HQs spawn protection and making artillery fire a commander call in ability. I've had so many games where enemy armor will spawn camp your HQ and kill infantry and vehicles as they spawn, this is absolutely horrid game design. In fact, in one of the newer maps, Kursk, you can even shoot into the enemy's spawn from halfway across the map because there are no line of sight blockers between the HQ and the middle of the map. This game has a lot of issues and the Devs seem more interested in adding more half-baked content than actually fixing them. They even had the audacity to say the game is out of early access. The Devs are not transparent at all with their community and when asked hard hitting questions about the game, they simply ignore them. They did a Reddit AMA a while ago that was an absolute farce, only responding to people who did not ask about the issues in the game. Don't give these Devs your money and spend it elsewhere. I wish I could refund this game, but sadly, I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: ****************************************************************IN SHORT*********************************************************************Squad leader screams over mic yelling enemy positions while me and another squadmate both worked one artillery gun decimating the enemy with well places artillery strikes. The feeling you get when you let off 5 rounds and hear the ping from the confirmed kills is satisfying in ways my wife could never satisfy me in............. Then 2 other squads jump on the last 2 guns next to you and now all 3 are firing off round after round shaking the entire spawn aiming at a maker halfway across the map and the SL jumps on the radio screaming beautiful while you're nutting all over the hot spent shells........ sorry moving on. Here goes the rest......If my opinion changes I will come back to this review. But over the past 48 or so hours I watched the game go from mixed to at this time of writing is mostly positive and I now see why. The people upset about the game are some of the kickstarter fans which in no way should reflect the game not being GOOD it just wasn't what some of the community wanted. HLL at launch was instantly fun and has a solid core with some rough edges. I love the idea of military sims that focus on team play but they aren't friendly to solo players. HLL gives you the military sim you want and is friendly to solo players who want to team up but if you want a meat grinding rambo blood fest this isn't for you. This game is a lot like RO/RS and Arma. Arma and others alike are amazing games when the stars align because they suffer from too much map and too many places to go and no front line chaos. This game gives you frontline chaos and intense battles while also giving you that rewarding experience you had that one time with the perfect randoms in Arma. To really have fun in this game you need to get a mic and just talk and ask for help. people will help you and you'll be surprised how many people start talking after one person calls an enemy tank out. When you join in look for the best squad and you'll have the best experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game - but make sure you know what you are getting intoI really enjoy Hell Let Loose, when you are playing with friends or a good squad it can be tons of fun here is a condensed reviewPros:1. Atmosphere: This game has one of the best in game atmospheres you will find. Similar to how in RDR2 you will feel like you are in the Wild West, in this game you really do feel like you've been dropped into Saving Private Ryan, Band of Brothers or Enemy at the Gates. It is so incredibly immersive that you will full on panic when an MG42 is fired at you. 10/ 10 for atmosphere2. Audio Design: The folley artistry in this game is excellent, almost every gun feels like they are incredibly powerful, and explosions sound / feel awesome. Sometimes the lower caliber weapons can feel the tiniest bit underwhelming, but I don't think thats really fair because I am comparing an MP40 to an M1 Garand. On the basis of them nailing the Garand ping, 10/10 audio.3. Gameplay: For the most part, the gameplay of HLL is pretty sweet, especially when you are playing with friends or good squadmates. The feeling of communicating with your squad to discuss a strategy to push toward an enemy position, then pulling it off is so much fun. Gunplay is good, putting shots into someone feels realistic and satisfying, in a grounded, brutal way. Weapon recoil for everything is quite high, so pacing shots is a must, and introduces a nice thought process of deciding whether to equip a more powerful gun (say an M1 Garand, chambered in 30-06) or a less powerful gun with lower recoil (M1 Carbine). The only major flaw i can thing of with the gameplay is sometimes you will die seemingly out of nowhere, and when this happens it can be frustrating. Overall gameplay is 8/10Cons:1. Blurriness/ graphics: The actual textures of HLL look pretty good up close actually, not bad at all. The problem is that the game is quite blurry at longer distance (most engagements in the game are past 100m), and the Anti Aliasing (in my opinion anyway) is ♥♥♥♥, which can make it very difficult at longer ranges to identify, yet alone hit targets, which can detract somewhat from the gameplay. There have been numerous times where I've been shooting at someone in the distance "If the game wasn't as blurry / better anti-aliasing, I would have definitely killed them". This is probably the biggest flaw with the actual game by far, as only the Sniper class, which is limited to only 2 - 4 in a match (so like 1 or 2 a side, I can't remember which) has magnified optics. So unless you are very lucky, you are using iron sights, which have no magnification, and only a slight bit when you hold breath (I'm eyeballing it to be maybe 1.25X, maybe 1.5X , either way not much). If they could fix this then honestly I don't think there are really many major flaws with the game. In terms of how much a pain in the @ss this is, 7/10 - pretty bloody annoying.2. Inconsistent teammates: This is why I recommend playing with friends whenever possible, as sometimes you will be matched with great teammates who you'd want to buy a beer for, but other times you will be matched with teammates who are either unhelpful, or do not have mics  / speak your language (I've found that English speakers make up a smaller percentage of the playerbase than many other games, so if you are not multi lingual then you may often be a member of a squad who you are unable to communicate with). Due to how important teamwork is in this game, the quality of your squad will have a massive impact on how much you will enjoy the game. So its just something to keep in mind.Overall, I really enjoy Hell Let Loose, and if you are prepared to put up with some of the issues I have mentioned, then you will have a ton of fun, in what I would say is one of the best WW2 shooters that is on the market right now. Welcome to Hell soldiers "_"7

_childDocuments_.review: I'm old and slow. Shooters aren't for me in this modern world.But this is. This is everything an older FPS player could want and more. It's a gorgeous, atmospheric game with exceptional visuals. You matter - your position, your feedback and your actions are part of a greater scheme of things. You're actually part of a war in this game. If you shoot and land your shot - it's usually a kill. That one kill could have been part of a push that stops and forces the enemy squad into another area.The roles are fantastic and all feel great, none feel OP. There's a good selection and the community (bar some angry commanders) has been great, even on VOIP. You'll catch RP'ing soldiers breathing their last, or maggots singing along as they are in a transport to the front lines and inevitable death. Hunkering down, suffering with your mates - knowing these are your last moments before the enemy descend upon your point...it's glorious. Absolutely glorious. These moments last. Me and my friends are absolutely loving this game. It's like Battlefield without the "wtf happened". Each death is likely your own fault.Negatives: Traversal can be a pain in the backside, Team 17 need to make it easier to climb walls and fences, it's a bit hard at the minute. Also there should be some level of indication of how many bullets you've got left. Too often I've been left with nothing but my pistol when I've not known I've been out of ammo. There should also be an option to force Squad Leaders into only being able to select that role if they have a mic and punishing them for not putting down Outposts/Garrisons. Besides that? Incredible.Get it. Join us in HELL

Players can choose to play as either the Axis or Allies, each with their own unique weapons and vehicles, and engage in tactical warfare across various maps.One drawback of the game is its lack of content, which can be somewhat disappointing for players who enjoy more extended playtime. However, the game's new studio has promised to update the game more frequently, so fans can expect more content to be added in the future.Despite its current content limitations, Hell Let Loose still stands out as an excellent game due to its realistic gameplay, immersive environments, and attention to detail. The game has received positive reviews from gamers and critics alike, who have praised the game's attention to detail and its engaging gameplay.In conclusion, Hell Let Loose is a great game that offers an immersive World War II experience, but it is currently limited in content. _childDocuments_.review: As a more mature gamer (an old bunny) and loving historically accurate wargames this one goes straight to the top of the WWII first person shooters!!! I hate to even call it by that name as that isn’t really what it's about. This is the "game" that some of us have waited 30 years for! Finally, a WWII game that comes about as close to being in real combat as I ever want to be! After the first night of play I was sore from the tension it created, the suspense, the uncertainty of combat! Its a Platoon level game that combines thinking, teamwork, combined arms, into a total experience treat for the senses! WWII was not so much about just killing the enemy as it was about using tactics, firepower, and skill in conjunction with your side other assets like armor, artillery, air power to suppress an enemy force causing him to give up a strategic location of strength or value to your side. Slowly weakening him until he surrendered, moved or died!It’s all here even to the roll of a medic being very important to the success of the mission. The graphics and modeling of game from the map / terrain to the weapons and uniforms is spot on compared to just a few years ago. I have high hopes for this game upon full release and thank / curse the designers for making me return to play a game I never thought would ever exist!

_childDocuments_.review: A very Immersive WW2 Shooter. Given that it is Early Access and came out only a couple weeks ago I'd say this game has a bright future. When you're working with a team the battles can be intense and overwhelming. The maps are relatively large giving one many options in terms of movement and tactics. I've played a lot of Rising Storm 2, and Arma 3. I'd say this game is a good balance between action and realism. It does have some flaws, all of which I believe are currently being addressed. In my opinion here are some things that need improvement: Sound (everyones brought it up, it is a little lacking).Queue: There is currently no Queue option when a Server is full, this is a must.Clipping: I've noticed my rifle hit an invisible wall when I'm looking off the side of cover, like a cement pillar for instance. Machine Guns: Currently the machine guns are a little buggy, deploying them on berms can cause the gun to clip through the ground. Generally, deploying them is clunky. There also needs to be a small zoom feature  like on Rising Storm 2 and with the rifles.Weapons: More deployable weapons like medium and heavy machine guns. I would also prefer a weapon selector for individual classes like in RS2. Like maybe support could have a choice between the Garand and the Carbine.Damage: For the most part it seems okay, but ive been hit twice by a machine gun and survived. It should be one shot one kill unless its a limb shot I supposeStability. The ability to gain a small amount of accuracy by resting your weapon on a wall/fence (among other things)Overall I recommend this game. It is a lot of fun and I keep finding myself wanting to play it more. Hopefully we will see the small bugs addressed and I have a good feeling it will become an even better shooter in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I come from a background of Call of Duty and Battlefield on Xbox and PlayStation and always wanted a better 'mil-sim' experience. Never having enough friends for a proper ArmA or DayZ attempt, Hell Let Loose has come in as a new fave for military FPS games.Between the atmosphere, the natural roleplaying of fulfilling your class's purpose and the fact that you can die infinitely within the 30 minute (per flag in Offensive) or 90 minute (Warfare) timers, there's so much to love. You'll definitely die more here than in any Souls-type, whether by Artillery, Grenades, Tanks, people you can't see, or friendly fire (which... kind of happens weirdly more than you'd think some days), but that's just part of the charm. You become so enveloped in the notion of being a World War II soldier; screaming for a medic as your buddy just lost a foot or having a bombing run evaporate any semblance of safety. The game does a great job of making you go deaf and having fun requesting a squad to defend.Just remember to communicate and ask questions. The community is always willing to help, you just need to be willing to ask... or you may get roasted for being a CoD/BF fanboy.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Battlefield 2 or Project Reality, Hell Let Loose is a First-Person-Shooter wrapped up in a Real-Time-Strategy game that encourages teamwork and active coordination.Beginners can jump in and get started immediately learning as a member of a small unit. Shoot, move, and communicate. As you explore the game mechanics, you can experience all of the multiple infantry and vehicle roles. Self-graduating to the role of Officer and eventually Commander, is where the RTS aspects skyrocket. The most rewarding for me is communicating with, and in some cases convincing, 49 other players to work together with you toward team goals and defeating the equally motivated 50-player adversary team.Public matches are good, but community arranged events with coordinated battles, pre-arranged squads, well scripted tactical, operational, and strategic battle plans, and coordinated mass movements are truly epic.The game developers are incredibly interested in community feedback and participation in the development process. I am really looking forward to seeing where the game continues to progress as it powers through early access.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of negativity from people is coming from the fact that the game isn't what people had hoped for. I understand completely if you're disappointed with how the game turned out especially if you backed the game on Kickstarter.This review is coming from a person who didn't really follow HLL, but I did follow Post Scriptum. PS had unfortunately fell into a slow development hell shortly after release.  It promised content that was not provided at release and is still struggling to reach or maintain said promises. I decided to give HLL a try after seeing lots of beta footage on Youtube. And in my personal opinion it's a good game. It isn't a full on Mil-Sim. It seems to fall somewhere in between.The gunplay feels similar to RO2/RS2 but a bit tighter and arcade-y feeling.Teamplay isn't as in depth as a Mil-Sim, but coordinating with a squad to flank around enemy positions or communicating with other squads to effectively take out a tank is thrilling and fun.Tanks are a lot of fun and with a well coordinated driver/gunner/commander you can be an enormous threat on the battlefield.Game can take 30 minutes to almost 2 HOURS to play. Take this as a positive or negative but personally when the game is a stalemate with lots of push and pull its WAY more enjoyable.Game performance is a pretty big issue at the moment. The minimum specs required to run this game are absurdly high in my personal opinion. Visually the game is good looking but Anti-Aliasing is a bit of an issue at the moment. Even with a decent rig I have issues with frame rates ranging from 90-150fps steady on "Epic" quality settings to less than 45 at times. I'm currently running the game with a mixture of Med/High with relatively stable FPS in the 60-90 range when things get crazy.Some gameplay issues are finicky vaulting, awkward bipod mechanics on sloped surfaces, VOIP breaking from time to time ruining teamplay and coordination, and lack of infantry vehicles (though they are going to be added).The game feels more like a RO2 than a Mil-Sim. And personally I wouldn't mind if it became more tactical with larger maps once more vehicles are added. But as it stands it's fun to play, even though some people are in disagreement with how the game turned out. If you like the Red Orchestra series you'll really like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A Message to the StudioHello Team17 and Cover6, hello community managers and community,Communication is key you say. Then please communicate in precise statements as to what is going to happen in the future, similarly to how you would communicate in the game we all love.I imagine you are swamped with responses to this post and hope you'll read through them just as I hope you've been monitoring the responses to the trailer and U14 on reddit and other social media. Of course I hope you read this as well and can use this feedback better than some of the other responses I'm currently seeing.Let me tell you a little story of how my weekend and monday went. I was visiting my family this weekend and thoroughly enjoying the nice summer weather. Yet I was eager to pick up this great game that you've recently acquired from BM again, once I got back home. When I got back Sunday evening I wasn't able to play since I still had some chores to do. "No worries", I thought, "I'll just hop on tomorrow. I basically have the day off." Monday morning rolls around and I remember "Hey wasn't there supposed to be a trailer for U15 coming out? Let me check that out."-5minutes later-Actually, I don't think I feel like playing Hell Let Loose anymore. This trailer looked so bad. And what was that voiceacting??So this is what I did: I spent all day yesterday solving jigsaw puzzles. It was fun.Okay enough of that, let's get back to business. And I will try being as polite as possible since just swearing about isn't going to help you much. So let's analyse what has happened since U13.5:U13.5 (APR 5):You introduce new background mechanics which should help you fix the loadout and grenade bug. Preem! That's what we want. It would have obviously been better if you fixed those right away but if you require more information I think we can all accept that. The issue with this was that it created server problems and people would have way more connectivity issues than before. Following this, I wrote a review, saying I wouldn't recommend the game right now due to these issues.You adressed the known issues approximately 3 weeks later(APR 21) in a DevBrief(#185). -Okay good, you're not ignoring the players, you're actually listening although it took a while for you to respond.U14 (MAY 25):The long awaited British faction releases. Along with it 2 maps, Driel and El Alamein. Everyone is excited to play and roleplay "the ♥♥♥♥ out of this faction" (sorry for this wording, it seemed appropriate). We open the game to check out the British (for me that was just through the barracks at first) and notice: "Hey none of these guys have a moustache." That was the first disappointment. Then we see: "Hey basically every class only has one(!!!) uniform and there isn't even an option to wear shorts!" That was the second disappointment. Third, we check out the loadouts for all the classes. And what do we take away from that? Historical accuracy seemingly is out the window. The standard rifle is one that frontline troops barely used, etc etc. I honestly don't have too much knowledge on the history of guns, which was used when and so on but even I know that the Thompson should have been in there. Following the disappointments of the barracks came the disappointments of the gameplay. Let's join a match and try to play as the British. My first 5 matches were always on Driel, which overall is not a bad map. Being able to cross the river everywhere definitely opened up some opportunities. But why can I not enter a single house on the map? Is that perhaps due to rushed development (granted you did release U14 earlier than shown on the roadmap)? And why is everyone sitting in bushes? This feels a lot like the Vietnam War (“They’re in the trees!!”). Surely this is just due to the map design.Onto El Alamein. I honestly don’t have anything to say here. I’ve enjoyed El Alamein a lot more than Driel and haven’t really noticed anything off-putting. A big issue with many were the locomotion changes (15% increase running speed) and the armor nerf that came with it (I was able to satchel 5 tanks in a game without too many issues). I believe an increase was a good choice, yet such a dramatic increase is just too much. Increasing the sprint speed by 5-7% would have most likely been enough and more appreciated.Okay sorry let’s get back to the Brits and how they play. First impressions: “Are the guns from the other factions also taking up this much of my view when I ADS? Why can’t I hit anyone even though my aim should be on point? Why am I losing almost every gunfight? The guns are cycling too slow.” As you can see, there’s a bunch wrong. I’m not going to talk about the issues with tanks since I barely ever play armor. In the meantime, Reddit is going crazy, saying HLL is doomed, the update is utter garbage, and we can only hope for improvements. Many veterans have started to leave Hell Let Loose and gone over to Post Scriptum or Squad.I’m wondering what they did in testing and who signed off on the update? Like what happened to QA?You respond a week later(JUN 2) in another DevBrief(#189) addressing certain issues while completely ignoring others such as the historical inaccuracy, just to name one. But you’re giving us a date as to when we can expect fixes to be implemented.-Okay good to know that they’re listening. It still kind of feels like they waited a while to respond.The trailer (JUN 11):WOW! What is this ♥♥♥♥?! How are there so many obvious glitches and visual bugs? Why don’t the assets look like the in-game ones? What is this voiceacting? The speech in the plane scenes sounds like it was the very first version written by some AI. There’s no emotion in the voices and it’s clearly being read off of a script. Why are the paratroopers using red parachutes? Why does the M1 suddenly have an extended mag? What happened to all the foliage? Why does the German soldier running into the trench have to reload his MP40? Did he come unprepared? Who would yell “Keep pushing! I think we got an enemy OP.”?Honestly, I think there’s plenty of material out there both on Youtube and Reddit where this trailer is being ripped apart and all the faults are being shown. I don’t think I need to list them all for you to understand what I’m trying to say.I’m wondering who signed off on that trailer? Like what happened to QA?You respond 2 days later (JUN 13) in “A message to the community”.-Okay good. They’re listening. They see the community is unhappy with what is happening.But what exactly is happening?Well, since you have taken over we followed a simple structure:Update -> Community is voicing their opinion -> Silence -> Community still at it -> DevBrief with empty excusesSo I’m asking, no I’m begging you, for the sake of the future of Hell Let Loose: “PLEASE! Improve your communication within the company. Improve your communication with the community. Listen to what the community has to say. And reinstate your QA department or if that’s too expensive/not possible with your current resources reinstate public testing (the community wants the game to do well and be playable).”Now to finish off, I’ll give you some information on me as a HLL player: I have played since Nightmaps (and I believe Remagen) have been introduced. I currently have about 260 hours of playtime and am around level 118.I imagine you will be experiencing more negative reviews and a small drop in player count following this “Message to the community”.Honestly whoever gave the okay for that trailer to be published must have been blind, deaf, mute and had a multitude of mental shortcomings.This was my “A Message to the Studio”. Thank you for coming to my TED Talk. I hope you could learn something and will improve in the future.Sincerely,A concerned and disappointed player

_childDocuments_.review: I kickstarted this game, on the premise it was going to be a WW2 tactical shooter with an emphasis on communications and teamwork. Unfortunately in my experience, the game misses the mark completely in that regard.While the game has voip, squad structuring etc communication and teamwork Is not something that is exactly needed to be utilized outside of Squad lead and commander roles. The fundamental design of partnering game mechanics completely negate the need to communicate or use teamwork outside of these roles.Due to the no ticket system, lives mean nothing. So medics will rarely attend to the the incapped and just leave you be, since it's much more effective and efficient to just respawn and shift W at objectives repeatedly, thanks to no tickets and no stamina system. Plus, 75% of the time being incapped results in being blown up by friendly or enemy grenades as you wait for a medic. Medic roles are a suggestion, not a requirement.Despite there being VOIP, people don't really communicate. They won't call out where they've been shot from, since they just instantly give up due to the aformentioned issues. People won't talk since everyones lives don't mean a thing, they're chasing the kills, then get killed themselves, respawn, repeat. The game actively entices this gameplay for the average squad member. You're playing in Squad, but everyone is playing for themselves. Squad leads most of the time don't care, just plop down a spawn and then just vaguely guide their squad on where they want to go. That's about the core level of teamwork within a Squad. The game as a whole isn't bad, it's just seems to have lost it's original direction with the rise in popularity and playerbase growth. It's a game that is fun to jump in every so often, have some mindless fun, and then revisit briefly next patch.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can look incredibly scenic at times, like something directly out of Saving Private Ryan or (insert WW2 movie here). Where other games can feel like full blown running simulators, Hell Let Loose does a better job of keeping you engaged in the action; sometimes to it's own detriment by throwing you directly into incoming bullets as soon as you spawn on a poorly placed Outpost. It even has the detachable limbs that we all loved from World At War. The death animations are glorious and feel incredibly dynamic. The reason I have to give this awesome game a thumbs down is because it's still plagued by the same QoL problems that were persistent when I first tried it out years ago. I run a 6900xt and get consistent, sporadic frame rate drops that others have mentioned; I'm talking like ~10FPS at times. I've found no fixes and upon research it appears that the devs have no plans on fixing any QoL problems like this and are more focused on rolling out "content". The physics in this game also feel like something straight out of a 2007 PC game. You /will/ get frustrated by invisible walls stopping you from hopping over things or preventing you from stepping in a certain direction etc.

_childDocuments_.review: In the actual state of the game I cannot suggest anyone to try this game. Many problems would need to be fixed if my decision would come to change. I am playing this for these mere reasons only, im poor and im bored with my other games. _childDocuments_.review: I want to enjoy this game but...it just isn't fun. It's beautiful, but that's about as far as it goes. It feels like it wants to be the spiritual successor, at least in terms of gameplay, to Red Orchestra II, however it lacks any of the immersion that made ROII what it was. The weapons in this aren't responsive; using the Kar98k for example, feels (and sounds but more on that in a moment) like using a nail driver than a rifle. The sounds are subpar, and although there's been constant promises for the devs to overhaul sound files, a year in it hasn't as of this review happened.I understand that people enjoy this game, it just isn't for me and I imagine if you're someone who like me, wants something a bit more immersive and realistic rather than slightly realistic run and gun (another failing, this game falls closer to Rising Storm II than either Red Orchestra), I'd recommend Post-Scriptum. That said, there's nothing per se bad about this game, it just isn't as good as other options. It falls squarely in the middle, leaving me to not recommend the game due to Steam's "either or" rating system. I don't regret at all owning this game, or supporting a small team who gave it a shot. But at 1/3rd the content and quality at the same price as its main competitor, I would recommend waiting for a sale.The positive side of this game however is that there is an active community - although I would, much like PS or any other game that's a bit more on the realism side, say you're better of joining a clan if tactical and team-oriented game play is what you wish. If you just play public games with randoms, I wouldn't expect much communication. However this is also something of a positive if you recognize that this game is a bit more run-gun / jump in play, you can quickly hop in, play a bit without investing an hour or two like PS. The downside to that however, is that the rounds are just as long as in PS (about 50 minutes or so), and this game for whatever reason, has an experience-based cosmetic system where the experience you receive is only tallied *after* a full round is played. This means if you like me, have limited time to play, you'll likely not be unlocking any of these extras anytime soon. I'm curious to see where HLL goes; I enjoy that HLL has touched on battles that aren't so oft-discussed, such as the Battle of the Hurtgen Forest and would enjoy seeing more obscure and less-seen content in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated ReviewFrom the played hours you can tell that I find it one of the better FPS games. It just hits the right spot between realism vs. arcade. The community overall is mature and friendly.The reason for the thumbs down is that the game was released in 2021 and the developers have still not fixed major bugs. UE4 game crashes are still common, suddenly the mouse stops working, in-game VOIP stops working… it was and still is a pretty mess. Plus the data privacy is still weird.Gameplay wise it is good. Could be improved. Quality of live functionalities like joining team as a group in the server browser or at least a functionality to join a selected friend directly from the steam friends menu are entirely missing. Also the amount of new maps is a bit low. If Team17 is struggling to create those, they should open the game for Steam Workshop.Another issue is that it is too unattractive to play as an SL. So, it is a constant struggle to find an (open) squad. The role should be made more rewarding so playing this crucial role does not feel like a punishment. For example, unlocking a less restricted equipment selection when playing as an SL with an open squad that has at least 3 to 4 squad members. Result: More players are incentivised to take the SL role and won’t lock the squads. When there are more squads, suddenly players can select between the different SL. Because the SL want the players to stay in their squad (otherwise no reward) it will incentivise them to actually do SL tasks (placing OP, map markers, using VOIP), else their soldiers will simply jump to another open squad.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a WW2 fps that gives you the experience of being in the thick of battle with your Buddies and gives you the desire to do your part HLL might be for you. You will see death, a lot of it, your death, your squadmates and the enemy’s. This is a game where one bullet is enough to drop you, and it could come from anywhere, it might not even be meant for you but you stepped in front of it. Accept the Death screen in HLL. The coms are excellent, you need a Mic. Comms are however sometimes bugged, it's an old bug among a few that persist. This game to me is not an FPS or a Tactical Sim, it's a Sandbox where 50 people can work together for a singular goal, to win the game through communication and reaction. The Meta of the game is not obvious to a newcomer, but it is important to learn if you plan on sticking around, knowing it will give you the tactical advantage, the ability to out smart, to deny and to kill the enemy. You use the environment to your advantage, you need to move slower to survive. Playing this game solo is not how this game is designed, you will not get the best of HLL this way, communicate and cooperate, then celebrate together at the end, win or lose. Being in the right area at the right moments is the critical aspect of the Meta, kills alone will be important but it won’t matter if the enemy are outsmarting you and taking your territory. You never communicate with the enemy, only with your team, this means the toxicity is uncommon, but there are outliers. If someone says “do something or else” and you don’t and they were right about the “or else” start listening to them. Respect the chain of command, the officers should be communicating on a separate channel consolidating their efforts. Officers giving orders is what HLL is about, if you can’t follow orders or choose not to, you won’t last long in the community. Expect others to follow you if you lead, but get to know the game mechanics so you actually can lead people to success, your troops will love you for it. Do your part for the team, you have a roll, do it. Change rolls if it’s needed or requested. The Graphics are excellent.The Sounds are immersive and tactically informing.The Gunplay is all you could ask for, you grandpa could get kills in this game. It is not a run and gun, camping is incentivised. Play like it's for onelife. The communication is great but has technical issues sometimes, it makes HLL when it works and is used.The community are for the most part very friendly, don’t confuse assertive tactical information or criticism as abuse. If you don’t know something ask.  The game Meta is hard to learn but if leveraged, it’s what gets you the wins, if you don’t know it expect the enemy does and they will steamroll you. Plenty of How to's online.

_childDocuments_.review: What can you say about a game so popular? Other than popularity doesn't mean for much when triple-A companies produce garbage that people purchase en mass. Perhaps that is why others give indie studios a break for making games with questionable playability. Industry standards such as bullet penetration are done away with. It is claimed that the game does indeed include bullet penetration. Certain constructable barricades do include bullet penetration I've heard. As for the rest of the environment, the same cannot be said. I've seen tank shells be blocked by shrubs and bushes. If a tank shell is blocked by bushes, chances for your rifle to penetrate a thin piece of wood is next to nil. As for map size, to many it is seen as a boon for the game. I would agree, if the map size was actually utilized in game. As it stands now, most of the map becomes unused save for the odd squad of ineffective infantry to wander out into aimlessly and without direction. Which brings me to the next issue I've found with the game. As far as front lines as we know them go, the map sizes create scenarios where any supposed front line is easily circumvented because it is next to impossible to maintain a perimeter for attack or defense. Why fight on the line when you can just as easily gain ground by going around it? It makes fighting for areas of contention tedious and I cannot see it getting better unless maybe the player count is increased in order for players to actually take advantage of the map. Lastly I take exception with the gameplay. Gunplay feels much slower than other contemporaries such as Rising Storm 2. Beyond that. Squad compositions are such that if the squad isn't full, and certain roles are not picked, the squad can be very ineffective. For example, a squad leader without a support role assigned will mean the Squad leader is unable to construct much more than temporary outposts. As for building defenses, again certain squad roles are required in order to do so. While I can agree this promotes teamwork and coordination, it simply does not in most public games. Instead the average public match experience will find you barely communicating with others because there is simply too much to coordinate between players. It takes two different players to place down defenses. One to place supplies, another to actually place construction. Perhaps if you played with a group of people who took the game very seriously and actually planned these issues would be remedied. But I think it is too much to expect from most casual players.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really optimistic about this game, based on all the glowing reviews.Maybe I'm too old for these nowadays popular die-respawn-die games, but that's exactly what this game is. There are no tutorials, so you'll have to figure everything out on the fly, which is rough since you are already in the middle of a battle. You'll get shot down by people who you didn't even get a glimpse of, even if a whole bunch of your teammates are around you. You'll then respawn, and the same thing will happen again, then again, then again. If you're lucky, you might be able to spot an enemy in the distance, but you'll be dead a microsecond after.I was also looking forward to the squad based, voice-enabled, tactical aspect that everyone seems to praise. My experience was the opposite. More often than not, you won't be anywhere near your squad members, so it doesn't even matter if they're talking, because that information will rarely be relevant to you. If you're hoping for some kick-ass teamwork, where the squad leader keeps the group together and issues clear commands, calls covering fire for friendlies, and in general helps the unit members not get lost - this is definitely not that game.All in all, I expected much more from this game based on the reviews, but it's just your run of the mill, "who-the-heck-shot-me" respawn simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to purchase a WWII game with depth and realism this is for you. you can play casually or become far more realistic if you so choose. You can just grab a M1 Garand or Kar98k and start firing upon your enemies for some casual PvP fun. Or maybe you've found your new favorite like myself and want to become a apart of something bigger. Setting spawn points, talking to the commander and giving your own squad direction on "secure this street" or "defend this position" you can most certainly do that. The absolutely beautiful thing about Hell Let Loose is you are the one who determines just how immersed, real, casual, stimulative the game is. This is by far one of the best WWII games and massive multiplayer games I've played. With great maps and a learning curve that is just enough to be challenging yet so rewarding. You'll start out not knowing a thing, and hearing over your squad radio "OP on my ping, garry on F3" or "need an engineering for some nodes." This can be a bit overwhelming at first however the community within the game is amazing, everyone is excited to teach you the lingo or show you some great tips and tricks. The gun-play is fantastic, the firing and suppressing mechanics are quite intense, immersive and fun!     1 hour matches fly by with artillery hitting all around you with small arms fire darting over your noggin'! You hear your commander over Officer radio telling you to hold the point for only 2 more minutes until victory and BAM a thompson round to the liver takes you down. But you see a medic running toward you through the smoke. He calls out over proximity chat "you're not dying on me here." and saves you with grenades blowing up the dirt all around you'll feel like he cares about more than just your character, sound off a "I wont let you down", raise up and mow two Americans down with your trusty MP-40 and you'll feel like Hell, is quite literally Letting Loose.If anyone would like a guy to play with or your new to the game and are a bit overwhelmed feel free to add me and throw a comment below! Id be more than ecstatic to play with anyone! (I typically play German Officer or machine-gunner)

_childDocuments_.review: After some time and a change of developer, I have to change my recommendation from a clear "YES!!" to a "no :( ".When I first started playing the game it was all about teamwork, tactics and strategy (if you don't know the difference between tactics and strategy, you should think about whether the game is for you).Then a new developer came on board, the old one takes care of something new.And for whatever reason (yes, because of the dear money...) it was decided to make the game "more accessible". So more arcade-heavy.About 50% of the old community, where some players have invested more than 1000 hours in the game, was alienated, because HLL was not (exclusively) played because of the setting, but because of the orientation. It was more authentic, realistic and challenging than other games.That is now being lost more and more.I'm someone who has a lot of patience when it comes to games and their development, but what I find always a bad sign is when the developer acts AGAINST the wishes of the community just to make a game more mainstream to earn money. I would have rather invested 50 euros in a DLC than see the game go down the drain.If you point out unwanted changes and their impact to the developer, you are comforted with big words ("We understand and we will change it, and we are with you, it will be more authentic again"), but the next patch in which the problem should be addressed (according to the patch notes) only shows that one does not want to deal with the problem and the question of authenticity, or cannot (no idea which is worse).A pity. Clear. Every company wants to make money. That's okay too.But if players buy exactly THIS game, DLCs, BECAUSE of the direction of a game, the community builds up and remains loyal, then it is sad when this path is left because of greed.It feels like you bought a VW that is now slowly becoming a Dacia. Sad.-----------------------------------Original review:A game that doesn't reward kills but rewards overall faction performance?A game that doesn't reward lone wolves but you and your fellow combatants if you work together sensibly and pull together?Without K/D, but with points for just bringing the truck with supplies to the front to build up the defenses?YES! And it's fun.The community is grown and mature, in contrast to kindergartens like Call of Duty and Co.Shooting is a minor thing here. Think, plan, act.Sometimes fail too. But even losing is fun with a good team and an hour and a half of hot battles.Rarely had as much fun as here.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to do this, but I have to. Because I love this game, but it's being run into the ground.TL;DR: DO NOT INVEST YOUR MONEY HERE. The devs don't give a sh*t about the community, and do not care about the quality of their content anymore.Hell Let Loose is supposed to be a real gem in the world of WW2 shooters -- it's cooperative, focusing strongly on communication, and -- as you may notice due to the hours I played it -- I kind'a like it.But it is also buggy. Development has been rough, with every update introducing more and more nasty bugs, balancing- and performance-issues, and major (meta-)game-changes that literally noone asked for. Black Matter made itself a reputation of neither listening to their community, nor having basic quality assurance and testing before releasing their updates.Then the development team changed. They were introduced as experienced developers, and promised to heavily focus on bug-fixes and quality improvements. But what we got was another botched update with bugs and more. Now they released a trailer for the next content update -- and I can't decide whether I want to laugh or cry. It's bad. Really bad. Go watch it, but I can assure you, the game looks and feels way better than the "devotion to duty"-trailer. At least for now, as the update is not released yet.The thought that someone at their studio said "yep, that's good enough, release the trailer!" is just... offending. There is no more hope for any "quality" in the further development, it's just going down...

_childDocuments_.review: Highlights: Hell Let Loose is really a game that excites me and really scares the heck out of me because you never really know whats going on, its nothing like your standard FPS games but rather allows you to compete on huge maps against 50 other guys feeling just as lost as you.What to expect:Honestly I've had alot of fun in this game. if you are going to have fun too you need to know what you're in for- Dying pretty much instantly if you run into open areas thinking you're gonna be fine- Shooting wildly in the direction of shape you beleive to be people hoping to hit something  - Throwing a grenade that insta kills your entire squad because you wiffed the throw- Feeling like a bad ass as you run into battle while explosions rain down from artillery and bullets wizz past you- Spending 15 minutes in a heavy tank driving before you even see any combat - playing as a medic to watch people die as you are healing them or crawling 60m just to save that one guy yelling your nameThe game has a really big focus on comunication so its important that you find a good server to play on where everybody uses mics. if everybody playing has a mic the game is such a joy, requesting support and getting it or asking your camander for a bombing run on a especially troublesome area. there are three main roles; infantry, armour, recon. infantry is the most common and i like to spend most of my time running around dodging the never ending artilary fire. about artilary, its operated by a crew of two and like everything in the game requires some level of talking.  the role that requires the best teams is armour, where you drive a tank, ooooh yeah. I have some funny memories yelling about the enemy tank on the horizon or spraying my machine gun at poor soldiers running around, the tanks can be a bit slow but like everything have a level of complexity without being too complicated so all three roles (driving, gunning, spotting, all of which are vital for a good team) are fun to play.Things I don't like: - most servers have terrible ping - It can be a pretty graphically weak game at times and sometimes just doesnt look the greatest) - often servers have a bit of a wait to get in so its hard to just pick up a game right away- I spend way to much time playing it because matches are long and I love this game a little too much even though i'm trash Value if you're worried about spending your hard earned cash know that at least for me there is a lot of play time in this game, you can try your hand at all the different roles and progress your soldiers to unlock new weapons or devices to blow things up. I have a few hours in this game and I still have not seen alot of the game showing me that there is alot too learn and more fun to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game good? YES!Is this game Worth playing? YES!Is this game worth the price tag now? NOOOOO!This game has potential and I hope the devs will not give up on this little project of theris, but the game right now is a buggy mess. It's lacking alot of content, some maps are just badly designed, the camera and character movement are bad. This game is nor worth playing IMO at this moment... if you can bare the annoying bugs and want to play a tactical game, then sure, go for it, but if you want to play a finished game then just stay away from this one for a while. Probably in about 1 year, the game will be much better than it is right now and it will actually be worth playing...REVIEW UPDATES AS OF 16.JUNE.2020:Ok, they did fix some bugs and changed some things as well. The bug where you get stuck in the air after jumping over a fence or obstacle is still there and it got me killed plenty of times. The in-game voice service still craps out sometimes, vehicles in general are still buggy. All and all these are the bugs I experienced so far...Now with the good parts:They did fix some of the bugs, not all of them but some... so that's a good start.They did add another type of vehicle in game which is a nice addition.The new bullet ballistics are just awesome, right on point most of the time as I mostly play sniper, these new mechanics actually made the game way more fun... I would love if the devs would add a way to set the distance of your scope on the sniper rifle but oh well...The new map is pretty decent, some parts are a little weird, but all in all a pretty well designed map.They did add some customizations to your character which even though I am not to invested in this aspect of the game, they do add a nice touch to the overall experience.All in all I am pretty happy with the new update and I hope they will fix the bugs I mentioned earlier which pretty much all the community wants fixed. Keep up the good work and pls don't dissapoint me now, would be a real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: 3100 hours in the game and not recommending it?This game was the greatest shooter of all times for me. But with the developer switch to Team17, the latest 2 updates literally killed it for me. The game wasn't perfect, many bugs, glitches and issues were (and still are apparent).Hit detection is broken, especially on long range shooting and very close combat. Deploying machine guns on walls/windows is inconsistent, random and seems lack luster. In one building you can deply the MG in a window. The same building on another location on the map doesn't allow you to deploy... Sprinting breath sounds are broken and annoying, never mind the increased sprint speed (+15% to before the patch) that nobody asked for. Now we are all Usain Bolts with no stamina issues and running full speed and stopping on the spot is no problem (well, it is...). This means riflemen are literally obsolete because everybody is bunny jumping, zig-zagging like crazy.Tank gameplay is dumbed down as well and if meant to be as it is, I am wondering what the devs are thinking. Heavy tanks shooting light tanks but get multiple shots bouncing off.... It takes 3 AT rockets in the back of a heavy tank again to destroy it...British faction was added because it can be sold as a content update, but the faction is simply boring and unbalanced. The Lee Enfield should shoot almost as fast as a SVT40/G43, but it's the slowest shooting bolt action rifle. Uniforms are bad and so limited that you can smell the missing ones will be payable DLC.Team17 needs to fall back to the previous update gameplay wise and build up on it. Fix bugs, add new maps to the existing theaters (western and eastern front). We don't need more factions at this stage, we need the existing stuff to work.I am still playing the game and I still believe they can fix the stuff, but the next 2 updates will be decisive as the long-term players and Clans are abandoning it in big numbers.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Let Loose: A Gripping and Authentic WWII ExperienceHell Let Loose thrusts players into the heart of World War II with a level of immersion and authenticity that few games achieve. From the sprawling battlefields to the tactical depth, every aspect of this shooter is crafted to deliver a visceral and unforgettable experience.One of the first things that strikes you about Hell Let Loose is its stunning visual fidelity. The meticulously recreated landscapes of war-torn Europe are both hauntingly beautiful and incredibly realistic. Whether you're trudging through dense forests, storming a bombed-out town, or defending a strategic position under heavy fire, each environment feels alive with history and danger.The gameplay in Hell Let Loose is where it truly shines. Battles are massive, with up to 100 players divided into squads fighting for control of key objectives across expansive maps. Teamwork isn't just encouraged—it's essential. Coordinating with your squadmates, whether you're storming a bunker, providing covering fire as a machine gunner, or directing artillery strikes as a commander, creates an unparalleled sense of camaraderie and achievement.The attention to detail in Hell Let Loose extends to its weaponry and vehicles. Each weapon feels distinct, from the punch of a bolt-action rifle to the thunderous roar of tank cannons. The sound design further enhances the immersion, with explosions echoing across the battlefield and the chatter of soldiers under fire adding to the intensity of combat.The strategic layer of Hell Let Loose adds depth to the gameplay. As a commander, you're tasked with coordinating your team's efforts, calling in reinforcements, and making crucial decisions that can turn the tide of battle. This adds a layer of strategy rarely seen in other shooters, rewarding players who can think tactically as well as shoot accurately.Multiplayer matches are dynamic and unpredictable, with battles evolving organically as players adapt to the changing battlefield conditions. Whether you're playing as infantry, armor crew, or support roles, every action feels impactful and contributes to the larger war effort.Overall, Hell Let Loose is more than just a shooter—it's a testament to the sacrifices and heroism of World War II. With its immersive environments, strategic gameplay, and dedication to historical accuracy, it's a must-play for fans of military history and tactical shooters alike.Score: 9/10 - A gripping WWII experience that raises the bar for authenticity and immersion in online multiplayer shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world that is grossly over-saturated with copycat battle royals and twitchy shooters full of angry teens who spew vulgarity and think T-bagging is a form of legitimate communication, we have few games worth spending our valuable time on. Hell Let Loose is one of those gems worth searching for. It's one of those amazing games that sadly get's overshadowed by the giant AAA titles that are far more popular and well-known.And that's a shame really, because Hell Let Loose in it's current state is a better game than the current titles from any of the big name franchises like COD and Battlefield - both who have completely ♥♥♥♥ the best with their newest releases and have more or less proved that they don't care about releasing completed quality games anymore. It's all about making amazing looking trailers, and raking in that sweet sweet pre-order and cosmetic DLC money before anyone realizes how much of a half-assed dumpster fire your "game" is upon release. Hell Let Loose is a milsim-ish shooter with just enough strategy and variables to turn the tide of the game if a group of players care enough to do so. Playing as a well-coordinated squad that is part of a much larger team is the name of the game here. Battles take place on a large-scale map, armor and supporting assets such as artillery, air strikes, and carpet bombing runs are absolutely terrifying (as they should be) and really sell the feel of an on-going battle. This is no place for losers who care only about their K/D ratio, but instead players are rewarded for observing the battlefield, paying attention to their maps, and using their brains. (Yeah I know - it's crazy, a video-game that requires you to use more than the few brain cells that tell your trigger finger to go click.) There is no brain-dead spray and pray, no sprinting and sliding through buildings, it's a slower, more tactile game, one where timing and careful shots can be the difference between your squad getting wiped out, and taking out a strategic enemy position. I highly recommend this game, I'd happily place it up there right next to Squad and Ready Or Not as some of the best online games out there that focus on teamwork and communication.

_childDocuments_.review: “Hell Let Loose” is a meticulously designed WW2 first-person shooter that offers a refreshing alternative to mainstream titles like Battlefield 5 and Call of Duty. This game is not about flashy stunts or fast-paced action; it’s about strategic teamwork and a willingness to learn. The gameplay is slower, but it keeps you engaged as you devise strategies to outmaneuver your opponents.The game offers a variety of roles, including tank crews, recon squads, artillery squads, commanders, and infantry squads. Success hinges on team coordination and communication. For instance, operating a tank effectively requires a three-person team: a spotter, a driver, and a gunner. This level of realism sets it apart from typical arcade-style WW2 games.Despite being in early access, the developers are highly engaged with the community, regularly holding Q&A sessions and keeping players informed about upcoming updates. They are committed to historical accuracy, which is evident in the game’s sound design and visuals.However, the game is not without its flaws. The Unreal Engine 4, which the game is built on, is resource-intensive, but the developers are making steady progress in optimizing the graphics.In conclusion, I highly recommend “Hell Let Loose”. It combines elements of Squad and Day of Defeat, with the added bonus of tanks and artillery, making it a strong contender for the “Better with Friends” award.====================16/12/2020 - UpdateUnfortunately, the game has taken a downturn recently. The competitive community, of which I am a part, has been negatively affected by changes to the game’s meta. Communities are doing their best to support the game, but without proper recognition and consideration from the developers, these efforts may not be sustainable.====================23/03/2021 - UpdateThe game seems to be losing its way again. The developers appear to be prioritizing profit over player experience, neglecting the competitive scene and introducing features that detract from the gameplay.====================01/05/2021 - UpdateA recent incident involving the community manager failing to attend a charity event organized by the Hell Let Loose community has further strained relations. This incident, along with other issues, has led to a decline in the game’s long-term player base.====================19/07/2022 - UpdateThe game continues to be developed by a team that seems disconnected from its player base. The competitive community, in particular, feels ignored.Please note that this is a subjective review and others may have different experiences and opinions.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually never post comments or recommendations for games, but this is from an emotional perspective after 2450+ hours playing HLL and now I believe is the right time for me to do so. Every individual who plays FPS Shooters online has their own idea's, goals and desires on why the keep playing a certain game and become part of a gaming community for that particular game. HLL has one of the best communities you shall ever come across, the people who play this game come from many different countries and backgrounds who each share one of the most valuable values you can have for a game...passion, wherever it be a keen interest in WW2, ancestral reasons, friendship, social reasons or because HLL gives you one of the most entertaining and exhilarating experiences you have ever come across, HLL shall go down as one of the best WW2 Fps shooters which was ever created. A little backstory...HLL was started as a kickstarter project initially back in 2017/18 as a group of friends who had a keen/passionate interest for WW2 wanted to recreate the authenticity and originality of certain stages of WW2 which would eventually become Black Matter Studios, but to do so, they researched, consulted, strategised and thought through on the best practice on how to design and create a game which would resemble the original battles/geographical layout in the 1940's and demonstrate a sign of sombreness to the men/women who wore military uniforms and who served in certain units on those very battlefields. Black Matter grew and built a solid foundational community with HLL by meticulously keeping the player base engaged and sharing idea's whilst also asking the community what they desired from the game, mistakes where made, yes, but the mistakes which where made was met with reassurance, conviction and deliverables. Near to the end of the Black Matter era of HLL, the HLL community became skeptical as everyone knew something behind the scenes had come to fruition and either 1. A few team members had fallen out. 2.Black Matter was on the verge of selling out and buy out proceedings had begun - Unfortunately we as a close knitted and active community knew Black Matters time had come and they outgrew the game in some sense, especially as the new gaming developer studio Team 17 had materialised an offer of £46m for the IP of HLL. As an outsider and avid player of the game, one of the only games I actually play, in some aspect, I wouldn't blame Black Matter for selling out, but if I from a Black Matter employee perspective could now see how HLL is materialising, I would be feeling disappointed, let down and unjust, especially after all the years of articulate historical research, input and development which made this game one of the best WW2 shooters.   Upon leading to posting my review today, the current state and recent developments/announcements from Team 17 not only have me concerned but the incredible HLL Community as a whole. The past month since the launch of U15 has been very difficult for HLL, which I believe has been one of the worst times for the community since the beginning of the HLL Journey back in June 2019 when it first give us a truly immersive and unique experience on historical accuracy, warfare, tactics, strategy and gameplay. Before I actually get started on the recent developments, I would like to address this directly to the developers/artists/designers/marketing.First of all, I appreciate each and every one of you who spend your time, effort and input into the growth of HLL and as I am aware (coming from a commercial background). you did not have any input on the initial acquisition of HLL, however needless to say, I really do hope due diligence was done on behalf of your senior leadership AT Team 17 before purchasing HLL, essentials such as the following, ensuring the correct resources and assets where in place for the growth of HLL and resolving any underlying in game issues from the previous owners (in this case Black Matter), budgeting (game development, designing), keeping the player base on a high retention rate, community base management, coinciding with historical accuracy using historians and experts in specified chosen fields, factual fact checking, player experience management and ensuring you have the correct tools at your disposal. Needless to say, since the acquisition of HLL, I have only seen fragments of the aforementioned and this internally for you must becoming a nightmare, especially as of this moment right now you are slowly but surely losing one of the best gaming communities/playerbases for a game such as HLL and ultimately for you your investment.  Recent Developments...I really don't know how to express myself with this part...but it is a disaster,  especially after the great job you did with community engagement upon the build up to the release of the most recent update of HLL U14 (The first major update of T17'S tenure) which had some great additions, let's start with the good before the bad...Good - Driel, the layout orientation, terrain and map control is competitive for both sides.El Alamein, has it's inefficiencies but overall a great tanking/mg gunner map and one of the best looking maps currently in the game - certainly facilitates a combination of AT gun firing and using your initiative to flank. Bad - - Weapon loadouts for the Brits needs to have an overhaul, bren should have a bipod, the sights on the Lee Enfield, Lanchester needs to be compensated, especially when you are aiming against an STG44 or MP40. - Should have Valentine/Matilda/M4 tanks for the brits in El Alamein, a sherman firefly never served in El Alamein.- Few latency issues when driving on El Alamein. - Brits or Germans don't have north african campaign orientated uniforms.- Sherman Firefly is not a heavy but more like a medium, especially as the tank hit box system is incorrect. The latest trailer for U15 as I am assure the majority of you you are already aware now from the other recommendations/reviews is a detriment to the people who served, thought and gave their lives fighting against tyranny, a game of HLL's magnitude which has been built on the values of historical accuracy has to showcase the historically correct uniforms, equipment and map layout- Not a third party videography studio or brief which you have just correlated off the top of your head without any real thought. So yes, you have finally come to the conclusion of my somewhat rather emotional recommendation, before u14 I would have hugely recommended the game but things change, people make decisions, actions are delivered and sometimes in life it doesn't always work out, but as an optimistic person I am really hoping the next stages of this game are very different to the ones which I have just been implemented. See you on the battlefield hopefully, over and out....

_childDocuments_.review: Team17's inherent ineptitude and complete lack of a stakeholder engagement strategy is on full display following U14. As a community owner and server provider, I am extremely disappointed with the level of communication we've had through official channels both prior to game updates/patches, and afterwards when we've encountered issues. Communities such as mine form the backbone of the broader Hell Let Loose community. We host 6 servers across three regions ($780 AUD/month), attract and retain new players, promote the game to our broader audience, and contribute to the game's social fabric. To say I am disappointed that I cannot elicit answers from Team17 on the most basic hosting questions is an understatement. The lack of a PTE (or anything outside of developer QA) prior to the latest updates is nonsensical, and it really shows in U14. Other reviews have articulated the myriad of bugs better than I can, but needless to say, the amount and severity of the bugs is unacceptable for an established $70 game made by a large studio. The QA processes need an overhaul, and desperately needs broader community involvement. Invest in your key stakeholders as we have invested in your game. 18/06/23

It is perhaps, the best game of its type. I feel it really has a great community of people who have fun and communicate and learn. 10/10, It is the best game I found during the pandemy.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, this game's maps are to-scale and a single match can take over an hour depending on how much of a defense a team puts up. It's objectively the angriest WWII game ever made. Instead of reviewing the game, I'm just going to list a few experiences I've had in under 10-hours of playtime. I saved the best for last. Queue the war stories. 1. I'm hunkered down as a medic with 8 other folks all creeping towards an objective. Suddenly, artillery falls from the sky and I'm surrounded by the mangled corpses of the comrades I failed to save. Their eviscerated bodies whisper to me. I failed, they say. I whisper back apologetically.But wait: one actually survived and I rush to his aid. I save him and then we both die to another explosion but this time, we go together. That one hurt the least. Next.2. I'm (again) hunkered down but, this time, as a machine gunner way-too-deep in enemy territory. Still, I'm a survivor. I'm all alone after a tank ran over my team. It's gone now and I signal where it's headed. I hear infantry coming towards me. My squad mates can't get to me because I walked across the map by myself. I somehow proceed to frantically clear an entire objective by myself and, almost by cosmic justice, accidentally step on my own grenade. That one really hurt. And, last but not least; here's one from the first match I ever played. 3. In the first game I ever played, I tried to cross a river as an anti-tanker and drowned while another player told me to swim. They said I could do it and I failed. I still don't know if they were being sarcastic. That's actually the first way I died in this game. By drowning, I mean. This one didn't hurt but I still cannot believe that was my first death in an MP-WW2 game.Hell Let Loose, indeed.Edit: this reviewer has since learned how to not drown.
