_childDocuments_.review: It's very raw considering it has been released for 2 years. Devs said they are officially getting out of early access in the next few months while most of the game mechanics either don't work or feel very unfinished.Cons:- Hitboxes for players, tanks and most static objects in the game are all over the place. Unless you are standing 1 meters out of cover your shots are going to land on whatever cover you have right in front of you.- There's almost no controllable ballistics in game. They've recently added projectile drop that is not really noticeable with anything other than tank guns, and even then there's no sight adjustments to control it. Add the hitbox problem to this and you can't shoot anything that is even slightly obstructed by cover.- Balance is still undecided. The fate of a lot of matches are decided by whatever happens in the first 5 minutes of the game. (google truck rush) Losing the first objective in firefight matches leads to a massive snowball.- Logistics suck. You need to constantly put down resource nodes to prevent your team from getting starved to death.  - Infantry mobility is ♥♥♥♥. Your running speed has a constant speed at sprint which is quite low (understandable for a hardcore shooter but...) cars and jeeps are non existent and trucks are very few.- Tanks and trucks drive like jet skis and have this shake glitch all the time. They can go through massive walls (not destructible environment, they just glitch through without even slowing down) yet can get stuck on the smallest object on the ground. There's a gearbox mechanic in place (promised to be improved in the next update) which is the same for all vehicles in-game and consists of revving to 2000 rpm at 1st gear and then switching to the highest gear instantly, and it works regardless of vehicle's speed and inertia. It's so raw one would suspect a programming intern could write it better in a week. Put in short: Tanks in RO2 -a 2010 title with notorious tank combat- feel much better and are programmed much better than this game.- Tank damage mechanics are arcadey as hell, there are health bars and you need 2-3 shots in the back with antitank weapons to kill a tank. Tank crews are impervious to damage inside the tank. There's no modular damage mechanics; unless the enemy tanks is going up in flames it will still function.- Grenades are thrown from somewhere other than your hand and the angle is usually 20 degrees off from where you're aiming.- Don't get me started on gunplay... Guns feel more like 2012 than 2021.- You can't pick up anything off the ground. You can only replenish at 3 ammo nodes that are usually scattered around a 20 km^2 map, or wait for someone to pick the rifleman role that can supply friendlies with ammo. The problem is nobody plays rifleman because if they do the other more crucial roles would be left empty.- Expanding on the issue above: You're constantly switching roles because there are 8 different roles with 24 different loadouts that are constantly needed by the squad, but squads are capped at 6 players each.Pros:- Infantry is mostly 1 shot to kill with rifle calibers so that's done OK for a tactical shooter I guess.- Graphics are beautiful. Some scenes look as good as Kingdom Come.I seriously hate this new trend of 'work in progress' fps games that don't even have the basics done at release. Hell let Loose, Post Scriptum, Squad, all the 1917 games like Verdun-Tannenberg and Insurgency: Sandstorm don't have the level of polish Rising Storm 2 has despite that game being literally abandoned by the developers halfway through development.If you're looking for an FPS that's not arcade ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like COD and BF, either buy Arma 3 or go for RS2 for a milder experience. If you have those 2 don't touch other titles in the market until '83 the game releases.

_childDocuments_.review: You're in an American light tank. It's light, nimble, easy to drive. You'd like to use speed to your advantage. You see a German light tank ahead. You know you can't penetrate its front armor, so you race to get behind it. There's a flimsy wooden stake in front of you and you should be able to drive through it without a problem. You do! You're getting closer to your target now. Victory is within your grasp.You come across another flimsy wooden stake, just the same as before. But this time, when you try to drive through it? You screech to a halt, dead in your tracks. In a panic, you try to reverse, try to recover the situation, get your speed back. But it's too late. You were spotted, shot, and you're dead. That's Hell Let Loose in a nutshell. So much of the game comes close to being good. But its bugs, its inconsistencies, its lack of polish completely ruin the experience, over and over and over again.Let's break it down:MOVEMENT WOESTanks collide with fences and hedges in unpredictable ways. Some fences can be driven through, others can't. Driving a tank is an exercise in frustration.As an infantryman, you'll find yourself unable to vault over low walls, inexplicably. They're the right height, the right shape, you've vaulted over low walls like this before, but, sometimes, you just can't. You'll see a small gap in stone fences, just about man-sized. You figure the developers intended for you to be able to walk or crawl through it. But nope, you can't pass through it. You can't even vault over it. You just died, trying to do that. SOUND SYSTEM ISSUESEven after almost 100 hours in the game, I strain to tell the difference between an MG42 and a Browning LMG, or an American Carbine and a German G43. You won't be able to tell where shots are coming from. A gun fired 100m behind you sounds the same as a gun fired 100m in front of you.Footsteps make (almost) no noise. Someone walking around in the attic above you? You won't hear it. Someone noisily stomping through the grass a few meters away? Nope, no sound. Every soldier is a ninja.RESOURCE MECHANICS: SUICIDE SQUADResources are critical to victory: Manpower, fuel, munitions. The superior strategy is to task a squad to, at the start of the match, spend 10 minutes finding some hidden area of the map to drop resource nodes. On some maps, there's interesting counterplay available, but on most maps, there's not. It's a boring job for a few unlucky players.Supply could be done better. Currently, the ideal Supply Soldier is expected to continually commit suicide, which refreshes his supplies. Not being willing to do this makes you bad at your job.OBJECTIVES: RANDOM DESIGN ISN'T GOOD DESIGNMap objectives are random. You might have a map where capture points lend themselves to fun gameplay. But that might be followed up with a map where it's a 60 minute slog over a swamp with no cover on the edge of the map (Purple Heart Lane, I'm looking at you).This is a poor choice. Developers shouldn't just rely on randomness to design their maps for them. They should've picked a sector progression that's well designed, that lends itself to fun gameplay, and stick with it.A GAME OF SPAWN POINTSKilling the enemy isn't nearly as important as killing Garrisons and Outposts (spawn points). The primary role of squad leaders and supply soldiers revolves around setting up new Garrisons, opening up new fronts in the fight. Sometimes, this kind of gameplay works really well. You and a supply-soldier successfully flank an enemy and reach a great spot to throw down a Garrison, which helps advance the fight. But this lends itself to unfun gameplay: Your team just secured a sector. Congratulations, you've got 120 seconds where the enemy can't take it back (it's "locked"). Your teammate set up a new garrison in the next sector. The ideal thing to do is to have your entire team commit suicide, then respawn at the forward garrison. Does that make any sense?IMMORTAL WALLS, IMMORTAL TREESBuildings, fences, trees, bushes, are all totally immortal. Shells don't leave craters. A house can be camped indefinitely, regardless of how many shells are pumped into it.Tanks are not particularly effective. They're not particularly scary. Effective pushes with tanks are rare, because they can't effectively destroy enemy bunkers and garrisons. They can't open new paths for infantry by, for example, knocking over a wall. Battlefield: Bad Company figured this out a decade ago. Why can't HLL?Furthermore, bullets never penetrate surfaces. A tank can sit behind a hedge (a hedge!), totally immune from high velocity anti-tank rounds. Granted, penetration without a destructible object system might be pretty lame, so I see these two ideas as linked.  DATED IN ALL BUT LOOKSThe game looks fantastic. The Unreal Engine is put to use well. The maps are beautiful, and huge. The game looks just like you're in the war. But the gameplay dated. The poor sound design, poor movement systems, and lack of destructible terrain and penetration feel like a huge step backwards.I had hoped that this would be THE definitive hardcore World War 2 multiplayer shooter. In fact, it's little more than a mediocre Red Orchestra clone set in the Western front.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current iteration, Hell Let Loose (Update 10) is an epic and satisfying multiplayer experience suffering from severe performance issues even on high-end rigs. An otherwise joyful experience is held back by omnipresent framerate issues and latency. Sparsely populated, rural maps run fine; Hell Let Loose takes players from the beaches of Normandy to frozen European forests in several iconic locations. Combat here feels meaningful and tense. A well-coordinated squad can turn the tide of the entire match, and when unhampered by performance issues, Hell Let Loose can be a spectacle. There's nothing quite like storming Omaha Beach as an American or launching an epic German counterattack with dozens of players. The scale (50 vs 50) adds to the immersion, as do the incredible sound effects. Dense urban maps like the recently-added Stalingrad are bogged down by low FPS (on an RTX 2060, I was routinely getting 30fps or below on Stalingrad). Older urban maps suffer from the same issue, which greatly diminishes an otherwise epic large-scale multiplayer experience. Optimization has been a problem for HLL for years. It seems as though the developers are more keen to add additional content than fix the performance on what we have, based on the absence of an optimization patch in the Roadmap. -Iconic WWII weaponry for American, German, and Russian units-Several classes to pick from; class differences (medic, machine gunner, support, etc.) are meaningful and variety is necessary-Some maps look gorgeous -Maps are generally well put together and take players on a tour of Second World War's iconic locals-Combat is tight and satisfying-Mastery of the game's system takes time but is rewarding-Poor performance and poor optimization-Server selection is antiquated, more reminiscent of Battlefield 1942 or Medal of Honor than a modern shooter. Players have to manually select a sever- a task confounded by inaccurate player counts and an obnoxious queue system-Matches can easily take upwards of 1 hour to complete. There isn't a "quick game" mode akin to Team Deathmatch. Thus, HLL is a significant time commitment even to play a single match. Steam's refund system will allow you to accurately judge whether the game runs to your satisfaction. I can't imagine playing this on a 1060 or below. HLL is a hardcore WWII simulation shooter that is outstanding when it works and downright infuriating when it does not.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I love it so much that I'm going to write a review for it, but it will not be a positive one. I'm hoping by some chance, I don't deter anyone from playing the game and capture team17's attention to any capacity at all. Throughout my 100ish hours of gameplay over the past month, I've loved and hated the game. I will talk about why I hated the game. All of these points I experience almost every single day if not every other day:- The game is just not optimized well. Out of the box, with all settings on the lowest setting, 1440p resolution, a GTX 2070/Ryzen 7/32gb of 3000Mhz ram, I got 35-55fps on average. It wasn't until I went on the most intensive optimization mission I've ever been on, changing every single windows setting that had even a remote impact on performance, monitor settings, Nvidia control panel settings, MSI Afterburner, steam launch commands, etc... That I was able to achieve an average of around 60fps (with a 175hz monitor), but the game is still awful and doing the above increases the chances of a crash. There are loads of flickering which is incredibly distracting, textures/objects render as you move and are delayed at times, and there is just more studder than any other AAA or AA fps game I've played ever, and I'd like to think this game falls in those categories given the amount of money that was just spent on it/how much it costs. - The servers are terrible at times. Every single server that I have ever played on suffers from the same issues. The issues are: a studdering that occurs abruptly for a few seconds every few hours or so, which is incredibly frustrating because for a few seconds, your screen is basically jittering and it's not a pleasant experience when you're in combat; every single server that I have been on has disconnected either me or someone in my squad at least once. There are other issues that I'll talk about below that might even be server related issues but they deserve their own complaint paragraph. - Communication is terrible. For my first few games, I had to manually select my input device but after ensuring my default devices in windows were all selected properly, I still had in game comms issues. Sometimes comms won't work at all, meaning V/C/X does not bring up an indicator. Sometimes the indicator will show after pressing the comms key but my voice indicator won't show (despite my squad being able to hear me on discord), and very frequently my comma are cut off which is not pleasant when calling out targets and watching your teammates die. - Textures don't render, especially on carentan. What I mean is, I can see an enemy on my screen, shoot an enemy dead in the face, only to find the bullet has been stopped by a seemingly invisible obstacle. The only way to solve this is to restart the client, which is very frustrating given you have to sit in a several minute long queue. - Bullet deflection on obstacles. What does this mean? I can be taking cover next to a barricade, peaking over it, have a seemingly clear line of fire towards my enemy and have the bullet be deflected by what looks like an "invisible wall." This is likely not an invisible wall, but a collision with the nearing obstacle you are taking cover behind. This is so frustrating because you have to maneuver your way further away from the obstacle you are taking cover behind, leaving you exposed, giving your enemy movement to detect, and most likely killing you. - Spawn killing. One of the things I like about call of duty and even a more similar game like squad is that I don't have to deal with battlefield style spawn and get immediately killediterally dozens of times a day. In the end, it's frustrating and I'd rather be spending time not playing video games at all or playing a very tactical game like squad where I'm barely engaging in any combat at all than sit there, try to spawn somewhere and get immediately killed. It's also one of the least realistic points of the game. Of course this isn't a WWII sim, but the game certainly captures a level of realism and the whole spawn camping problem is very call of duty and battlefield-esque. Now this is tricky to manage, I can't personally think of many solutions to this from a design lens, I'm just listing a major frustration I have with the game. - I'm starting to get bored of the content. To be specific, I am talking about infantry weapons. I've been using the same 4-5 guns/loadouts for over 100 hours of gameplay and I am a little tired of it. There are only two factions (honestly I don't even count the Russians because I rarely get to play as Russia, they need to be included in more maps), and within those factions there are only 2 guns I can really get myself to play often because there aren't many viable guns in most situations. After maxing my favorite classes, I'm now forced to keep using the same gun I've already gotten 1k+ kills with, use a gun I don't like, or play armor/recon, and it's starting to become a turn off.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. There are a few moments that are really something special. However, the devs seem to be focusing new content, such as guns, maps and the Eastern Front for the final release. This sounds good, but the game has a myriad of issues. First are foremost is optimization. The game doesn't run well. To add onto this, it looks amazing at max settings, but looks like hell as you scale the options down. This is because the devs are using basic UE4 assets rather than making them custom. Second, there are massive pacing issues in the game. A full match can be over in 10 minutes if the first point is taken decisively, or it can drag on for an hour on the same point, where the winning the game only involves taking a single point. Ultimately, the objective system is so broken that it forces you to make your own fun. Third, guns are not as fun compared to similar games such as Rising Storm 2 or Insurgency: Sandstorm. In those games, running makes your weapon sway, resting your gun on a window sill stabilizes it, and injuries have different effects based on where they hit. HLL, on the other hand, doesn't have anything outside a suppression system. This lends to a system in which a moving squad is not significantly disadvantaged when attacking an entrenched one. This reduces the need for tactical thinking and clear communication when addressing a house full of enemies, because chances are it will be easier for a dude with a machine gun to run in there and clear everyone out. Also, the addition of the BAR has been a disaster. 1/3 of a team can have heavy full auto weapons, and it completely changes the pacing and kill distribution for the worse.Ultimately, the game could be recommended. However, the the developers really seem to think that More Content=More Fun. There is little attention paid towards actual principles of game design, and if those things aren't addressed by the full release, they probably never will be.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a walking sim at this point. There has been a steady rise in cheaters over the last few months that make this game pretty unbearable. Nothing like walking a mile to get killed by a guy that sees through terrain and buildings. The game also struggles with poor optimization. Even with a 3080 + Ryzen 7 5800x some maps only get between 36-54 fps on max quality and 1440p res. Textures usually don't load at distance (even with a scoped weapon), which makes windmills, churches, and other structures look blurred and hides the vision of windows so people can sit and snipe you without exposing themselves. Grass, shrubs, and other foliage does not appear at distance. So even though you appear to be hidden, you are easily visible to anyone from a distance. Trees in this game look like they are from a pixel game (at distance) due to a weird anti-aliasing bug the developers still haven't fixed since launch. Not to mention all the buggy mechanics with grenades disappearing after being thrown and MG's clipping into the map (and sometimes going invisible) when extending the bipod. The list goes on. With that being said, I think the game is a very fun game - especially when you have a squad that communicates. I do however believe that this game is on the downhill as of now. The dev team seems pretty active with content but until they fix optimization and mechanics (and cheaters), they are putting time/effort in the wrong place (by introducing new maps that have performance issues and crashes annnnnd skins....). Fix the base game, then focus on making more content.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want an authentic WW2 FPS that strives to be as historically accurate as possible, then look no further. HLL is not without its flaws though ie (poor communication, lack of experienced players, poor commanders and SLs) However, the good matches make up for the poor ones. You can also join communities or add players that communicate on steam and fix the communication problem easily. This game gives the same energy that you put in, so use your mic and talk. You will be surprised by how many people don't communicate until you do. If your squad isn't communicating switch squads. And remember, always be polite and respectful. A toxic game is no fun for anyone. If you are a squad lead just put down outposts and communicate with your team. It is simple, and other players will respect you for your effort. If you want to practice being a commander join a lobby that has a low player count (seeding) and practice there. The same strat goes for tanks and other armoured vehicles. Tell people you are new and learning, and that you are open to advice. If someone is toxic to you, then switch squads. Have fun and communicate.

Unfinished animations are in the game, bugs have been in the game for over a year, horrendous stuttering, a lack of investment into correct loadouts and much more.I really hope they actually bother with this game, but at the current moment in time, this game is left unplayed. I'm having much more fun with Squad and Rising Storm 2:Vietnam. If you're thinking about getting this game, I'd come back in a few months and see if the developers are putting in effort again. if not, I'd give it a miss. Make it with minced lamb for a Shepherd’s pie.* several large potatoes* 2 oz cheese* dried herbs (Rosemary & Thyme work well)* salt and pepper* beef stock or vegetable stock ( 1 pint or more)* bisto gravy powder* peas and finely chopped carrots and onion optional* blob butter or margarine1. Brown the mince2. Add the chopped veggies (optional)3. Add salt and pepper and herbs4. Add beef stock, stir and simmer for 15 minutes (thickening towards the end by mixing bisto powder with a little cold water to a runny paste and adding to beef stirring all the time- beef sauce should be quite thick!)5. Meanwhile chop up all the potatoes into small chunks6. Place in salted hot water and bring to the boil until tender and drain.7. Mash with generous (if rations allow) blobs of butter or margarine, add salt and pepper to taste8. Finally add milk so mash is spreadable9. Place mince sauce in a small cooking tray with deep sides or shallow casserole dish10. Pipe or spread mashed potato on top11. _childDocuments_.review: It's like Men of War Assault Squad 2 but in FPS. I dislike FPS games and multiplayer games. Can't get into them. Probably because COD and Battlefield ruined them in my eyes. However, this game, no one tries to play the hero. No one is trying to get the most kills on their team and the least amount of deaths. If you run off on your own, you will die. You can not win single handed. You absolutely have to work with your squad leader, and the squad leaders have to work with the other squad leaders, and all squad leaders have to work with the Commander. If you don't, you will fail and die. I love this teamwork concept. And everyone in chat is working together and when something crazy happens, people laugh. They are legit enjoying themselves. No one cares if they lose or win. It's about teamwork. And it's a blast!There is a level/rank up system but it barely works as I can tell. Nor do I know what it does when I do reach a higher level. I don't care honestly because I want a fair balanced fight. I don't want special treatment. We have an option, work together to survive or die. Either way it's fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game had an amazing potential to be one of the best WW2 tactical shooters but had been ruined by the increasing number of cheaters who exploit the game. Unfortunately most of the private servers share the same fate, simply because admins of such use cheats /cams themselves to their benefit. Putting cheaters aside, gameplay is really fun and having the right people in your squad can make a deciding difference during the match. Both offensive and warfare modes are very well put together and thought through. It's only a shame that points of capture are not randomised. With such beautifully designed maps those points could have been placed anywhere on the map, giving a bit more diversity to the approach and gameplay.  Content of the game is sufficient, although more maps and game modes would be welcome, however I believe it's more important that devs will focus on fixing remaining bugs and work on the optimisation - as the latter one is lacking badly. For game that's been on the market for so long, this is only a a sign of a lazy programming.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Jan. 2023Decided to see if things have improved.  Nope.  If anything the game is worse.  Every round consists of 3/4th of both teams camping and the remaining 1/4th putting in work.  Garbage is the only word that's fitting and it's largely the community's fault, though, the game play itself tends to support this boring grindfest that's become a digital turd.This is now a hard NO.Original Review:An accurate rating is 'Depends'; not a 'Yes' or 'No'.  But since Steam lacks options, I must choose the 'No' only b/c my preferred play-style does not match the game and it's community.  Others with similar preferences should take notice.If you're the milsim / team-coordinated style player:  Hell Let Loose will severely disappoint.  There is little to no coordination/planning, communication or teamwork.  B/c of that, I do not recommend the game.  If you play ARMA, Squad, or similar titles that involve active team work, this game falls very, very short.  HLL is very much an arcade-style shooter.If you're a casual player (i.e. enjoy Call of Duty, Counter Strike, Battlefield series, etc.) then you may enjoy HLL.  The pace is fast and there's not much downtime between fights.  (In other words, you'll spawn, fight, die & repeat often.  If you don't mind that, then it's a plus!)But for me, the game is largely a meat grinder (even though I usually have good score & K/D).  Winning rounds typically involve whichever team can get to the capture points most quickly/efficiently and hold the line while the rest move to the next.  Sadly, most games involve the entire team leaving the capture point as soon as it's won, only to return a few minutes later b/c the enemy team has begun to recapture the very same zone.  The back and forth is annoying to those with a more strategic preference.(To be fair, some responsibility of this falls on the community itself:  it just doesn't have the player base with the same mindset as those found in Squad, ARMA, etc.)With the major cons out of the way, I'll end with some positives:  The game looks alright and the gun-fighting is pretty good.  Hit registration seems decent (better than most games).  There are plenty of servers, although expect to wait in queue on Fridays and weekends.  The community is generally nice and I haven't experienced too many trolls.TL;DR:  If in doubt, purchase on sale.  I continue to play this from time-to-time but only in short doses; anymore than 45 minutes and the repetitious grind gets very old and frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a serious review. At the time of writing this, I have just under five hours of gameplay, so I’m not very experienced, but I can say a few things. The game is good, it’s very fun to play, the guns are great, and pretty much everything else the other reviews say. But this game has traumatized me. I am not joking. I went from riding in a transport vehicle with my squad mates, laughing and singing stupid songs and having a good time, to being pinned behind cover by an lmg, constantly hearing the deafening blasts of artillery, terrified that the next shot won’t miss, and frantically struggling to look after my teammates as medic. I watched my mate run towards me as he was bleeding out, yelling, “I’m out of bandages, I need you doc! I need bandages!” I was only ten meters away from him as I witnessed a stray artillery shell blow him into literal pieces, causing his cries to suddenly stop. I turned around to my other mate behind me, who had seen this, and he stared and said “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!” It was just a split second he stood still, but that was enough time for the enemy to line up a shot. I watched as my second friend got his brains splattered onto the cold trench we were huddled up in. I was fairly new, so I thought I could revive him, but headshots kill a man for good. I must’ve spent at least twenty seconds cradling his headless corpse, frantically trying to bring him back before I realized it was pointless. Not too far away I could hear a friendly on a different squad calling out “Jack! Jack, where the ♥♥♥♥ did you go? I need you!” I was scared and didn’t have any squad members nearby, so I dove into the enemy trench, where I immediately found a foe waiting. Without hesitation, I drew my pistol and shot him in cold blood. It was only after I emptied an entire magazine into his dead body that I realized what was going on. This man was a medic, trying to resurrect an ally, just like I had done so many times before. He died trying to save his friend, his body now slumped over his. I was genuinely traumatized by this event. We won the battle, but I just kept thinking of that short, stressful period of time I spent in that damn trench. This game is immersive, but that isn’t necessarily a good thing. 8/10 please fix spawnkilling

_childDocuments_.review: Poorly optimized, queues up to 15 mins only to get kicked out because if you join the exact moment the server changes map you lose connection.This game doesn't know if it wants to be like battlefield or like squad, the majority of games that i played nobody had a mic and everybody played kind of at random (which happens reaaaally often, like 40-50% of times you join a server); The main issues are:1 spawn points get placed in bad areas leaving you to get spawnkilled for 10 times or you have to run for 10 minutes just to get to the point (this happens in EVERY game with poor communication, which sadly is a lot)2 playing with good graphic settings is a suicide in every map with fog or lots of rain because it nerfs your vision3 random stutters (which i got at the same frequency with high and low graphic settings) in a fps is a big problem4 the fact that i have to level up a class for 10 to 15 hours only to use a non-bolt action rifle with germany and the USSR but not with the US (since they have the M1 Garand) makes certain teams stronger in certain maps, aside for being a pain in the ass(why do i have to put in effort if i can only unlock 2 or 3 weapons at most with each class) doesn't have much sense in a game like this.This is really a shame since the feeling itself is fantastic, i wish other fps had this feeling of immersion and "gun feel" which is usually rare in strategic games like this which usually feel a lot more clunky.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 14 was very lazy, and I hope this isn't what we can expect from HLL's new daddy, Team 17. British forces being released alongside a desert map- Operation Torch theater was a driving talking point about the update. You get one uniform for the Brits, and it's not even a desert uniform.They started going the battlefield route- Using guns/vehicles that saw little/no frontline usage like the Lancaster, that was issued to the Navy, and not even to frontline troops. They gave the base rifle of the faction as something from WW1, the 1914 Lee Enfield. It would be like giving the American faction the Springfield. The Sten SMG, the most produced allied SMG of the war, is barely seen but again, the Lanchester is scattered all throughout the other classes in the game. The lazyiness and lack of research doesn't bode well for the game, and this could be the first turn to something more akin to battlefield or cod if changes aren't made. I want the changes to be made because I've enjoyed the game, and I'm hoping that with some negative reviews we can start seeing those changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. It looks amazing, super immersive, and overall an amazing experience IF you are willing to communicate with your team and have your head slightly wrapped around war strategy. This game is not for COD players who don’t play the objective and only run in guns blazing only to get shot time and time again.There are a couple of problems, however. Some minor problems are that the sounds and animations are quite crappy, as well as the hitboxes. In a trench if it is occupied by other players it is almost IMPOSSIBLE to move around as another player will prevent you from being able to move, and the only way to get around them is to run into the line of fire and likely get shot. Also, there are sometimes instances for me where the frames drop from 50 to 60 down to 5 or even lower, and I always need to leave and rejoin and lose all of my progress. In other words, it is an amazing game, but the devs have some work to do.

_childDocuments_.review: My very first game, I crawled, hid, cowered, and cried to myself. I died 30 times and never once saw an enemy. One of these first matches saw no less than a dozen squad-mates turned to mush with a single tank shell right in front of me as a medic whimpered in a corner, unsure what to do with what was left of them. The game is grotesque, immersive, and one of the best I've ever played. Whether you like to lead the charge or hold the line, whether you prefer to command, fight, or support, this is the game for you. And it's only going to get better.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Let Loose

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for two rounds. Both lasting over an hour. Each time I died; Which was often and usually to someone with a machine gun; I would sit for almost 30 seconds on a respawn screen. Normally, that isn't an issue. But when it comes to how slow you move, you will probably spend most of the game walking into death and not getting anything done. The first match was amazing. I had great teammates and they were willing to teach me how to play support. The second match, however, I was instantly insulted and berated for each and every mistake I made. I should also state that I was playing the game at 1280x1024. Unless your computer can run in on 1920x1200, you won't be able to see anything. I switched to a recon squad later on in the second game to try it and found that I couldn't even see through the scope due to the poor resolution. Once again, I found myself unable to play the game- This time because I literally couldn't see anything I aimed at in a first person shooter.Near the end of the match, I ended up shooting my first enemy after a constant stream of deaths by the hands of teammates and enemies and then got vote-kicked by a poorly made system that I can consistently see other people complaining about.I had fun for the first match and I'm glad I had players who were kind enough to show me the ropes in it- Even if it was one class- but I can see it need a lot of polish until it's gotten it, I will probably refund the game and try something a little less focused on 'hardcore realism' and something a little more focused on being enjoyable and accessible.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Let Loose

_childDocuments_.review: Right now the lack of basic features such as FOV sliders (like, really?), aim sensitivity (if we're gonna be hunting pixels let us be more accurate), leaning (no tactical game shouldn't have leaning) and other features we've come to expect from a 2019 PC-exclusive tactical shooter is what keeps me from rating this a positive. Optimisation is still a thing as well, pop-in of foliage can be ridiculous at times and general audiovisual still needs work to be on par with similar games in the genre.Update 21/7/21: A few of the previous features have finally been added, but the game still leaves very much to be desired. Aside from serious performance and pop-in/rendering issues (and I even upgraded my system since then) they dropped the historically accurate hardcore game they were aiming for and instead started catering to a more casual crowd, this happened around the time they announced they were coming to consoles as well and this unfortunately explains a lot. They are coming to the conclusion of early access, but this game is far from ready to go to full release.

_childDocuments_.review: My 350-hour review was negative, but it has changed. At the time the game (14.8) would never run properly, and nothing seemed to fix it. (crashing, frame drops, etc) After countless hours of researching (and help from a friend (iron(nerd))) we (him) found the fix; for a short time. The problems came back. I took a break from the game to play other games (osrs), and when I came back, after a few updates, everything was fixed/fine.           I have added about 250 hours since those problems happened and I am no longer upset. I swear off the game and turned people away from the game, but I wish I didn't. I've met SO MANY great people in this game! There are a few bad apples, but there are WAY more good people. Some may even say great people, the greatest even. So many high-level players are just itching to help the next noob, truly greatness. So if you just got this game or think about it, try it! Hop into a game READY to learn!          The game isn't perfect and I would change a lot, but who cares? Little things here, little things there. At the end of the day, I'm not here to load into the most realistic WW2 sim, I'm here to make new friends and teach them noobs a thing or two (and get blown up by arty (RECON DO UR JOB))

_childDocuments_.review: Some background first.I played BF1942 on release and every other battlefield game since then, I also played Arma series, Post scriptum (briefly) and squad and TBH quiet a few others. Battlefield started to go to far to the casual test tube shooter what I mean by this is each team are at either end of the tube and you're shooting down a set path think the metro grind (its boring). Arma was to big and bots are no fun.The game looks amazing I am running a RTX 2080TI and and intel I7 8086k everything running on Epic, I have had one instance of bad performance this was due to server lag and rubber banding.The walking isn't as bad as people are suggesting get with some friends or make friends get a support, put down a supplies crate get the squad leader to create a garrison EVERYONE CAN SPAWN HERE!!ProsBody parts are so immersive watching a tank shell hit a hedge row and seeing bits of bodies fly is great coupled with actually walking behind the hedge and seeing that there was probably a squad there and more parts lying on the ground is great.Team work is there if you are willing to look for it.Tank is fun with friends.Gun sounds, sound good although sound directions are in Cons.Scenery looks fantastic details on the floor and trees look great.ConsIt can be a bit hard to see the enemy led down in a hedge row and sometimes it feels like you are glowing bright pink.There will always be campers hiding in weird places.Tanks cant drive through simple objects Fences,small walls, bushes and it can be hard to get to a road.(more practice driving maybe)Tank commander needs more to do.People walk in front or stand behind tank and you cant see them.. squishRandom lagging people.I cant get my head around the bullet directions I cant get my head around hit markers often it appears i am being shot by the other directionTeam killingHow to win or lose needs to be easier to understandMap time should be reduced it can be quiet tiring playing for 2 hours.Some people go to weird places and just don't do enoughCons are longer than the pros but this game is great and I hope they don't ruin it by catering to the BF3 metro crowd, There is so much potential to create a really exciting WW2 shooter here and the devs are pretty much there.I will add more when i think of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A brutal, unforgiving multiplayer experience awaits in Hell Let Loose, but when it all comes together and your team is clicking on all cylinders, it's something unforgettable. You will need to communicate with your team to find success, because when you're all alone, the game will begin to frustrate you, unfortunately, making teamwork not just a recommendation, but a necessity. If you are looking for a run-and-gun shooter or even just a game focused around a kill-death ratio, this isn't the game for you. Hell Let Loose is most certainly a MilSim, though it's a bit less hardcore than it's contemporaries, such as Squad or Post Scriptum. For those hardcore MilSim players, however, you will still find a lot to love here. The sound and graphics, especially the frequent explosions, are sure to immerse any player in the terrifying battlefields of World War II. Massive dust clouds kick up into the sky when artillery shells land, your vision will get so blurry you're nearly blind when you are suppressed by enemy fire, and the near constant cracking sound of rounds being discharged will litter the landscape for the entire game. Other than the Battlefield series, few other games have done such a remarkable job with setting the stage and making the player feel like they are fighting for their lives in a massive warzone.In terms of maps, the developers have done a good job of steadily adding new areas for players to fight in, as well as new weapons and vehicles to go with them. Featuring a mix of famous locations seen in media like Band of Brothers and Enemy at the Gates, Hell Let Loose currently features maps in both the Western and Eastern theaters of Europe, meaning the teams will either be Allies (US) vs. Germany, or Germany vs. The Soviets. Recently, the developers even added night versions of several maps, which changes the dynamics of the battle even more. To further make each match feel a little different from one another, the capture points have semi-randomized locations each match. This, combined with how utterly massive the maps are, makes every battle feel unique and the content feel nearly endless.Being a MilSim, you will, of course, be locked to the weaponry and vehicles of your faction in any given match. This creates the interesting balance that is present in many World War II games, where the Allied forces typically have better infantry (a semi-automatic rifle being standard issue, compared to the German's bolt-action Kar98k) and the Germans have better vehicles (Fear the Tiger tank). If you find yourself playing German infantry and don't want to use a bolt-action rifle, however, you do have options! Whether it's picking one of the other classes, such as Automatic Rifleman or the Machine Gunner, you will have a bevy of different, unique roles to play that each will provide support to the team in different ways. Even if you are not the best shot or if you simply don't enjoy gunplay much, there's still roles for you to play. The Medic is given a paltry supply of ammo but tons of bandages and a method of reviving defeated players while the Engineer is focused around constructing supply nodes and defensive structures, like barbed wire and tank traps.If you're a fan of real-time strategy games, the Commander role in Hell Let Loose offers a unique experience as well. With three resources to spend (generated via the aforementioned supply nodes), command will be able to call in bombing runs, drop supplies from the skies, spawn new tanks, and many more helpful features to go along with the verbal orders that must be delivered to the individual squad leaders in the game. There's nothing quite as satisfying in a team game of this size than to give orders and watch 49 other dots on the map follow those commands and fight their way to victory, all while giving them fire support and the supplies to create forward spawn points.Sometimes, however, things will not go to plan. As it might be expected, getting fifty people to work together in any capacity can be a struggle. Thankfully, however, the community has been nothing but helpful in my experience. In the nearly fifty hours of playing before writing this review, I can count the bad interactions with other friendly players on one hand. The vast majority of players are understanding, they know the game is complex and they went through all the same learning struggles you will if you play this game, but communicate and explain yourself as a newbie and I can almost guarantee you will have people to hold your hand and guide you through the unforgiving and unforgettable game that is Hell Let Loose.Oh, and watch out for artillery.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Let Loose

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent years playing Squad, I have not played Post Scriptum, which is the WWII variant, but considering how similar Hell Let Loose is to Squad, I am going to make a direct comparison, both are great games, so I will simply point out the differences and let you decide which you would prefer.The game engine for Hell Let Loose is a few years younger than in Squad, and it really shows, the lighting effects and terrain detail, all the way to the character and weapons modelling look amazing, however (Just like Squad), the engine seems to lack optimization somewhat and you will find that you need to turn a lot of settings down so that you don't tank your graphics card, I recommend a beast of a gaming machine to even come close to appreciating this game with near fully fleshed out settings, I run a 1080ti, 8700k and have to turn most settings down to low or medium to get about 80fps.Furthermore, there is a bug where your settings reset every time you relaunch the game, so each time you get into the game, you will need to optimize your graphics settings all over again (annoying!)The sound effects in Hell Let Loose are seriously lacking, some of the audio effects are decent enough, such as artillery guns firing and tank explosions, even the M1 Garand has a nice sound to it, but overall the sound effects really lack the punch I feel is required for an immersive war experience, most of the weapons sound flat, like you're firing a paintball gun, grenade explosions, even from a few metres away, sound like firecrackers, and the tank engines sound like someone driving a go kart. The lack of decent audio effects in this game has a huge impact on the immersive experience of the game, it takes away from the awesome graphics on show. This is something that Squad has pulled off really well, when you play Squad, everything from driving a big supply truck to firing a weapon sounds amazing, I froth setting up a 50. cal machine gun in that game, because the audio is LOUD and packs a punch, even firing at nothing is heaps of fun, just because the game makes you truly feel like you are sitting behind pure destruction.This is the big one, this is the number one reason you are all looking at these games, is it not? A lot of us are sick of the selfish gameplay that is displayed, even in games like Call of Duty or Battlefield, where there are team based game modes, most people fight for themselves and only communicate to abuse other players. We want a REAL team experience, we want to be part of something bigger, a team that has worked together to achieve victory over a tough and determined enemy. There are a few important details to this, that I will explain with some detail, so I will break this down even further:At the moment, this is the SOLE reason why I would recommend Hell Let Loose over Squad, originally the community in Squad was fantastic and was much like the community you will experience in Hell Let Loose, the majority of people are friendly towards new players and are more than willing to teach the game to someone that has never stepped foot into a game of this caliber before. Squad seems to have lost this very important feature over time and the community in Squad seems to have been replaced by slightly newer players that contribute less to the teamwork than the predecessors who played the game a couple of years ago. I suppose when you sit a game in Early Access for going on 5 years, adding what feels like very little to the game, your dedicated player base are going to lose interest, this is a subject I will touch on later.This is something that both games need to implement a lot better, and I believe is a good reason as to why Squad has lost the appeal that it once had. While both games do reward players for good teamwork, with providing everyone with a more enjoyable experience, and likely resulting in victory for the better communicating team, it is not punishing enough for players that refuse to partake in this part of the game. This can be incredibly frustrating for players that are playing the game as intended, especially if you're in a position of leadership. As a commander or Squad leader, if you have other squad leaders or squad members that do not communicate and typically run around doing whatever they feel like, it can have a huge impact on the difficulty of you achieving any objectives you may have, making for a frustrating experience and at the end of the day, if that is the kind of game we wanted to play, we could just play something like Battlefield instead.The kick vote system in Hell Let Loose needs a huge overhaul, as it is currently, it does not work, the idea that the opposing team is allowed to vote on whether a player on the opposite side is kicked or not, is ridiculous! If the Germans have a terrible commander who does nothing and does not communicate and they are trying to kick him from the game, but the Allies are allowed to vote, and can clearly see what is happening, of course they are going to down vote that action, as it is going to benefit their chance of victory. What I would like to see implemented in Hell Let Loose, is a kick vote system which gives more power to Commanders and Squad Leaders, +5 for commander, +3 for Squad leaders, that way the players which contribute the most to the team experience can actually have some power over this problem and get rid of the ability to kick vote players on the opposite team, it's ridiculous! Also, it would be nice if you could detail the reason you are kicking said player, so that people can see for themselves and have a more informed opinion as to why they should or shouldn't vote to kick a certain player. I also feel like some sort of system for squad members should be put in place, when I go squad leader and end up with squad members that don't follow orders or communicate, I kick them from the squad, simple as that, I think other squad leaders should take up this method, as it should help to persuade players to use the teamwork and communication that the game asks of them. Some kind of system that adds a mark against a player when a Squad leader boots them from a squad, so as to warn other squad leaders about that player should be implemented, that way, the new Squad leader can prompt that player to play by the rules, or they will be kicked from that squad as well.I feel like Hell Let Loose has taken a page directly out of Squads book with their gameplay modes, the way conquest mode is set up, so that their are multiple objectives, but each team has to capture consecutive objectives to unlock the ability to move on to the next ones, then there's the offensive game mode, which has one team defending objectives, which they can't capture back, and the other side has a certain limit on how long they can assault each objective for.I feel like this is something that Squad pulls off far better than Hell Let Loose, I know the use of a ticket system for counting team loss is quite an old school method for determining the outcome, but the bottom line is that it just WORKS. The idea of victory conditions being determined by a timer in Hell Let Loose often feels like an unfair system at times. (Continued)

detailed_description: MIND CONTROL DELETE is █ first person shooter where time m░ves only w▒en you move. No regen▒rati░g he▀lth bars. No conv▒nie▄tly pla▒ed am▄o dr▄p█▒■ YOU SHOULDN’T BE HERE. YOU HAVE ALREADY WON. BUT THERE IS MORE. The long-awaited third game in the groundbreaking SUPERHOT franchise - MIND CONTROL DELETE gives you more insight into the world of SUPERHOT, more story, more weapons, more enemies, more purpose, more signature gameplay. Time only moves when you do. Keep dancing the slow-motion ballet of destruction for so much longer than ever before. Built on the foundations of smash-hit SUPERHOT and the best-selling SUPERHOT VR , MIND CONTROL DELETE delivers more of SUPERHOT’s signature power fantasy. Amass an arsenal of new skills and new weapons. New enemies pour in from every direction. You are in complete control as you shoot, slice, and explode your way through dozens and dozens of increasingly challenging and varied combat encounters. The closer you get to the core, the more powerful you become. Unlock new skills. Uncover snippets of precious knowledge - of the meaning that you crave so much. You begin to believe. MIND CONTROL DELETE Features: More gameplay. MCD is much bigger and longer than its predecessors. Become immersed in the SUPERHOT universe for increased understanding and extraordinary slow motion combat. More mechanics at your disposal. Experiment with new play styles, new weapons, different character builds and fresh tactics to outsmart and dominate your enemies. More bosses, enemies and characters to control. Test your arsenal of tricks and weapons against increasingly deadlier, smarter foes. More progression and power to accumulate. Amass skills, hacks and special techniques to conquer ever more dangerous enemies. More polish applied over nearly four years of Early Access development. MCD offers a more refined, sharper, flashier experience than any SUPERHOT so far. More story. More lore. More meaning? You shoot and slice. You move forward. You repeat. You repeat. You repeat. It becomes a ritual. It starts to mean something again. You take a moment to consider. You’ve been here before. So many times. Maybe this time it will actually mean something. Everything explodes into action. You hope this time will be different. Is this VR? Will this be VR? MCD is a regular, non-VR title. It’s designed for conventional screens and longer play sessions. If you played and enjoyed SUPERHOT VR, you’ll have a blast playing the original SUPERHOT and MCD as well SUPERHOT: MIND CONTROL DELETE started out life in Early Access. With many thanks to our wonderful players, Kickstarter Backers, and Early Access community, We couldn’t have done this without you, Thank you, SUPERHOT Team

_childDocuments_.review: ! gameplay spoilers !The game brings in some new weapons, moves, and objects, but is all barricaded behind the insanely repetitive "campaign" that keeps cycling between 32 levels, which is not a lot considering you are forced to play each about 10 times or more.Initial game focused on level design and each level was interesting in its own way. You only got one life and there was no need for more. And after completing the game you could play with various modes and endless runs.This game made each level work as endless run, requiring you to kill X dudes to complete it. Each level can start in few different ways, but after killing those 2-3 dudes, the rest is pretty much the same. The concept of lives made the game more arcadey which supports the nature of its repetitiveness. All the hacks, modes, or enemy variations you unlock throughout the game are fun but don't give any better value to overall gameplay and pretty soon become repetitive.Overall, the game has its cool moments (throwing a credit card into dude's skull; boomerang shurikens, disco room), but the moment is gone as soon as you start hitting the same level 5 or more times.

_childDocuments_.review: Mind Control Delete was given to owners of Superhot for free, which is how I got my copy.The introduction of the game is excellent. The random hacks and abilities you get really make the game pop for the first few hours. But the real strength of Superhot and SuperhotVR was in those carefully crafted rooms from stage to stage. Mind Control Delete puts you in a set of rooms that are nearly identical every time. By the third hour you begin to know the layout of just about every stage and it doesn't do much to vary it up or the approaches you can take. Some of the hacks are so hilariously overpowered that you'd be stupid to not pick them. The very end of the game is a terrible slog. _childDocuments_.review: A sequel which should've been a free DLC.The original Superhot is a mix of puzzles, in my opinion a bit creepy story yet enjoyable, wrapped around the most innovative game mechanics I've seen in years (jk, still a nice concept). This made a very good mix despite the short playtime, which landed on my list of favourite games.Mind Control Delete is nothing like the first Superhot. My first impressions were great, new weapons, some minor changes to the core gameplay, what could possibly go wrong..? Well.. You're playing through a randomly generated list of arenas (32 possible maps), length of the list depends on your progress. After spending 2 hours, everything looks and feels repetitive. BECAUSE IT LITERALLY IS. You're playing through 32 random maps over and over, you're given random perks which either are dogsh*t or broken as hell (faster movement versus bullets being frozen when nearby), so you're either gonna do the map list in 5 minutes or 30 minutes, depending on RNG.Story? Well, there is none. You're being told by the game to stop playing it, to be honest I feel like I should've listened to that, and of course, the player doesn't listen. After ~200 arenas, assuming you've finished them without failing, which is impossible, you're being forced by the game to stop playing it by.. making you finish ~20 arenas without perks/modifiers, and then soft-locking itself so you can't no longer play it. Unless you'll wait 2.5 hours IN REAL LIFE, then it lets you play again (also that's the requirement for 100% completion).2.5 hours is too long? What if I told you that on day-one you had to wait 8 hours?TL;DR you're better off playing an Endless mode in the prequel rather than playing Mind Control Delete.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything that made the original game neat is gone with Mind Control Delete. I'm barely an hour in and it already feels repetitive and mundane, like a chore. If you like the idea of playing randomized SUPERHOT levels on repeat over and over, you may enjoy this game; otherwise, I would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the first instalment, I was really disappointed with this title.In summary:Almost all the new elements or modifiers added to the game does not add to the core experience. And the little that was improved, was completely undone by the fact that they turned the game into an RNG roguelite. Gone are the scripted, handcrafted levels. Now you will just be playing the same few rooms over and over. If you die, you need to try the whole set of levels again before advancing to the next set of random levels.They made the core experience unfun and uninspired. I'm honestly quite shocked the devs made these mistakes.Do not buy. Just go play the original again if you still have an itch. More details (spoilers):This part is less of a review, and more feedback to the devs.1. RNG: Going for uninspired RNG roguelite levels instead of more scripted, handcrafted levels that made the first game so inspired was a big mistake. It makes the devs seem lazy.1.1 One thing that made the original so fun is you could pull off these amazing stunts. Now it's too much of a risk. If you mess up, you have to do up to 8 levels all over again. Not fun. Makes experimenting unrewarding.1.2 The game now uses a node system in order to progress. Each node has a random set of levels (8ish). If you die in any of those levels, you need to redo the node. This causes more frustration than a sense of learning to get better due to more than half the time RNG kills you instead of you making a mistake.1.3 Game introduces modifiers ("hacks") given to you between levels in a node. You get a choice of two random hacks out of a pool of unlocked hacks. In theory these should spice up the game and give you more ways to play. But once again RNG messes this up. The modifiers are not balanced to begin with. Adding RNG to the mix makes it feel even more cheesy. Got bad hacks? Now you are forced to take the heal hack each time you get it in order to just stay in the fight. Got the killheal or bulletslowmo hack? Congrats you basically can't die.1.4 The game also adds more "core" hacks. Where in the first game you get hotswap, now you also have katana mode and charge. But charge is just a worse hotswap. I found katana mode quite fun though. You start with a katana and you can recall it like a lightsaber to cut enemies along the way back. I found it more consistent and versatile than hotswap. You always start with a katana, and recall gives you a safety net to have a weapon in your hand at all times to deflect bullets.1.5 Ironically the RNG does not give the game replayability, because you can't really experiment, and the levels are so boring anyway.2. You want to replay anyway? Nope, they put an obnoxious 8 hour lock at the end of the game that you need cheat engine in order to skip. Seriously, who's friggen idea was this? Even if you want to go the story, fourth wall break route, fine, but make it so that the game uses the system time and a person can just adjust their PC clock to get past the time lock. Same point made, with much less frustration.3. A lot of new enemy modifiers and mechanics simply detract from the experience and makes it unfun.3.1 Adding exploding enemies and mines restricting your movement slows the game pace right down. 3.2 Adding unique boss enemies seems like a good idea. But they are invulnerable and very cheesy. You have no counter to them besides avoiding them, and even then, RNG can mess you up. Failed to throw your AR away before the boss hotswaps with you? Well tough luck now you have an invulnerable guy in your face with an AR.3.3 The enemies which can only be killed by hitting a certain body part was actually the only good new enemy modifier. It forces the player to think more about how to approach a situation. Unlike exploding enemeies where it's almost always safer to just avoid them.In the end, I do want more SUPERHOT. But the devs really need to go back and think what made the first game so good, and build on that.

_childDocuments_.review: Having backed Superhot on KIckstarter long ago, the team made backers aware of this game and gave us early previews to play when it was playable. I wasn't convinced on first play that this was going to be worth it, however the released product far exceeded my expectations. Adding a narrative/interactive story layer to Superhot is quite an idea, and it really does work. It's a Roguelite FPS at its core, but the same weird dystopic narrative you're familiar with from franchise prior. Burned through about 4 layers of this before calling it quits, but in that time I'd unlocked all sorts of weird new abilities, I could now make projectiles explode, recall my thrown Katana, all sorts of weird fun variations on the theme. Honestly if you enjoyed Superhot, this is a similar game with greater gameplay depth. Simple as that.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift when it was still in early access and after a few playthroughs of the game during that period, as well as getting the ending and a majority of the achievements at the time of writing this I've decided to give this review.I wish I could give a neutral opinion for reviews as I don;t know how to feel about this game. The game has the same mechanics of time only moving when you move as the previous Superhot but the sort of puzzle like elements of the last game are gone. The way the game works now is you have to complete a series of "Nodes" in order to progress. Each Node has a series of levels where you have to kill X amount of enemies to progress, there's also a health mechanic where you can take up to three hits before dying and having to restart the node from the start. There is around 30 level designs that can appear in the nodes, and the nodes grow longer the further you progress, so eventually the game grows more tedious with a lack of variety. There's also some semblance of enemy variety with enemies who can only be killed by attacking one body part, enemies who's weapons die with them and guys who explode in a hail of bullets when killed, but other then that there's no real variety.There's also three "Cores" that get to change up your playstyle, the hotswitch core, a core that starts you off with a katana and allows you to recall it when thrown and a core that allows you to charge at an enemy and punch them. It is possible to start a node with one of these cores at the cost of only having two hearts for the node. Each core has a boss like character counterpart that can randomly appear in one of the missions. These bosses are a bother to deal with since as far as I can tell there is no real way to kill them.My biggest problem with the game is the lack of story and the ending, if anyone who's still interested in this game doesn't want to know what the ending is, then please skip the spoiler marked section ahead:In the end, I'm not sure how to feel about this game and again I wish there was a way I can give this review a neutral rating. If you still wish to buy this game after reading this go ahead, just be aware of what I have said in this review.Edit made on August 3rd 2020: After gaining 100% completion on this game shortly after writing this review, I have not returned to this game at all. I have heard that the 8 hour wait after completing the game's "story" (if it can be called as such, that is) has been reduced to around 2 to 2.5 hours. While it is an improvement, it's a negligible improvement if at all as all the problems from above still apply with lack of engaging content and entirely changing the game's design from it's predecessor. My stance still stands as of when I initially wrote this review, purchase it if you wish (during a sale is recommended), however don't be surprised to find it is not as great as previous entries.

_childDocuments_.review: First, this is still pretty unique take on FPS games, core mechanic makes the game stand out in today's overcrowded market. Also, like everyone owning the original, I got the game for free which is nice. So the question is - should you buy it?Short answer - no. Long answer - yes, but wait for deep discount. Why is that?Because the game is way more repetitive than original. Levels are too small, enemies spawn in a weird way and though there is a lot more different opponents, I find them more of a annoyance than welcome addition. Basically the gameplay principle is - try until you succeed, and that would have been fine if I hadn't play the same levels 1000 times already. It just kills the fun.So yeah, first 2 hours were a blast, everything after that is getting more and more annoying. Shame really, maybe I come back to it one day, but for now I will focus on something less repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: im definitely a bit conflicted about this one, the game does a great job with the power fantasy vibe with all the new powers, and keeps it exciting by dropping new and more powerful abilities throughout. i really like the lives for a set of levels addition as well vs just never get hit on 1 level. the biggest issue i take with this one though is now that the game embraced roguelike elements the levels are no longer nearly as interesting as the previous game. before the game was a puzzle shooter where dying and learning how to take on the level with frame perfect precision was a feature, now you go through the same handful of levels over and over with none of that great level design from the previous game. Another side effect of this is since you spawn in a random location, and enemies no longer on a fixed pattern sometimes you have an amazing fight with the 4 guys who spawned in front of you and then promptly lose your last life to a shotgun blast from the final enemy who spawned directly behind you, only to have to go through the 6 or 7 levels to get back to the point all over again.if i could give this game a middle of the road i would, but i have had fun with it, the fact it was free probably heavily impacts my opinion here, i would grab it on a sale, if you havent played the first, do that before you consider this one, its definitely the better game in my opinion.EDIT: upon completing this  game i am EXTREMELY disapointed with both the end gameplay and the "ending" itself the devs literally took the end of the game and went "lets finish this by stripping out all the cool new bits, and highlighting all the  worst parts in the new system for about 2 hours of gameplay. and then the "ending" is literally just a 2 hour loading screen. this is vastly inferior to the first game, play that instead, the start of this game is a slightly worse version of the first game, the end is just bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for the first few hours until you realise it's the same arenas on repeat with endlessly spawning enemies until you kill enough in that arena. Instead of carefully constructed unique environments, you go through the game doing levels which consist of a number of arenas (the same limited number of arenas on shuffle). Kill enough enemies and you'll advance to the next arena. Die and you'll get knocked back to the first arena. As you play through the game, you'll unlock different skills such as charging at an enemy and force pull your katana you just threw or found on the floor. You can only use one skill at a time in a single and you choose which one at the start of a level. Skills are kinda nice. They add another dynamic to the game that would be very tedious without them. That being said, I find myself only using the charge skill because it's practically a get out of jail free card. The others I've found so far don't feel anywhere near as potent, but maybe I just haven't played with them enough.Along with these skills, you can unlock buffs. Buffs are additional effects such as piercing bullets, stronger punch, kills reload your gun instantly etc. You start each level with no buffs and you'll get a choice between 2 buffs between every couple of arenas in a level. There are some buffs you'll rarely want because they rarely do anything for you, such as headshots ricochet bullets towards enemies; it sounds good until you realise the bullets ricochet towards an enemy's current position, meaning if they're moving (which they're going 95% of the time) they're not getting hit. Ever. This means in some situations your 2 options are a clear cut choice. Your choice of buffs can also lead to some very potent combos; for example, the "kills reload your guns" and the "more bullets in each gun" buffs can lead to you killing a huge chunk of enemies in short periods of time. I've used it a number of times to get out of situations I should've died in because I've gotten surrounded by too many enemies to deal with otherwise.I'm at 4 hours at the time of this review. Outside of new skills and buffs I've unlocked, I feel like the game has done very little to make things interesting, which it sorely needs to do given it's shuffling arenas based gameplay loop. The biggest change so far has been the introduction of traps which explode bullets when you get near and an enemy which randomly spawns which you cannot kill and will chase you around the arena, forcing you to always be on the move. Both were introduced at the same time. To me, the game had been consistent on it's difficulty up until this point and suddenly spiked because of these new mechanics. This spike, I've found it more frustrating than engaging. I played and finished the first game a few years ago. It was short, but sweet and an experience I'll never forget. The devs gave this game out for free to those who owned the original. I was quite excited for this game, expecting it to be more of the original, but instead we've been given something tedious and uninteresting once you've played enough. It's not a bad game, but it's not good either, especially in comparison to the original. It still have the same basic mechanics as the original but has not even half it's soul. If you just want more of the mechanics, this will be great for you. If you wanted the same puzzle-like shooter experience the original provided, you won't find it here.

_childDocuments_.review: I always had an interest in the original but for some reason never tried it out.  I figured now would be a great time to jump in as I love roguelike experiences when theyre done well and I could imagine this game being an excellent fit for that type of thing.  Nope.  Now, it's certainly possible that I didn't give the game a fair shake.  I had 27 minutes played at the time of my refund request, but I went from the elation of discovering the truly amazing and unique gameplay mechanic, to being completely bored with it within 25 minutes.  The last 2 minutes was spent paused while I cleaned up a bag of almonds I knocked over as I turned away from my computer to go do something else.  I can imagine a scenario where something reveals itself through the course of further gameplay that really spices things up, but I can also imagine a scenario where I subject myself to further boredom unnecessarily while I have many other things I could be doing.  When my mind is wandering 20 minutes into a brand new gaming experience thats generally a sign for me to cut and run.
