_childDocuments_.review: i think this game is really enjoyable but i have many problems with the micro-transactions that plague this game. This comes from someone who has put many hours into the zombie army trilogy and had moved onto zombie army 4. Firstly, the amount of accessible content in terms of weapons and character without purchasing the £90 worth of season passes, is highly limited. This is really sad to me as the zombie army trilogy had a plethora of guns available, all with different characteristics. This game gives you 3 rifles, 3 secondaries and 3 sidearms. This is an abysmal choice of weaponry compared to this game's predecessor which boasted many more.furthermore the weapons you have to purchase all previously stared in the trilogy which makes this ever more infuriating as i would have liked to continue using weapons such as the Lee Enfield but instead i was stuck with 3 other weapons.This is my main gripe as the cosmetics don't bother me personally but putting the majority of weapons behind a paywall is really disheartening. Adding to this the DLC is shoved in your face. You don't get a break with this game, it always nudges you to purchase DLC.Secondly, for those who enjoyed the difficult of the previous game, there is a lack of challenge. I played the whole campaign with 1 other friend on a 4 player setup on hard difficulty. Personally i'm not sure if the enemy count levels with the player count but from what i can tell (as i never hosted) the enemy count was lackluster at times. Only after a difficulty spike later in the game did zombie numbers ramp up to very impressive levels. The enemy hitboxes are larger which does make the kill counts more enjoyable but may be a little disappointing to some. Regardless, at the end of the game the hordes are very fun to cut into but the start can be annoying as your combo never gets very high. - it may be worth noting my friend was incredibly good at the shooting, so for those more casual the numbers may be suitable, you will end up sniping a couple hundred+ towards the end in horde sections.There are a few needless mechanics such as stamina management which is needless but this is only a small gripe.I did in-fact give this game a thumbs up for a reason. When the issues of £90 worth of season passes and weird design choices are ignored. The base game is incredibly fun. The UI is very accessible, the weapons have a fun upgrading system and feel great to play with. I personally went down the route of explosive ammunition for my sniper which made combat very satisfying. There is a perk system that can spice up the game, many of which are superfluous but a few kept me interested in that mechanic. The enemy variety is good, there are mini bosses and a nice variety of enemies. The score system for killing returns, this time way more colourful. Higher killstreaks give you a nice number on the right, changing to ever more vibrant colours the more kills you get. The score multiplies more and more. There is a lot of equipment and special weapon attachments alongside the signature weapons like the preacher return. The campaign took 16 hours to complete, that's with hunting for secrets and collectables, something my friend was very eager to hunt for considering the trilogy was full of them. This is definitely a good campaign time, especially since the perks and weapon choices give more replay-ability. Finally, since this is a sniper elite game, the slowmotion bullet time/camera stuff returns, it adds very much to the gameplay loop. When fighting a horde of zombies, this all culminates to an exhilarating and enjoyable game which i will definitely return too.Overall i did very much enjoy this game as the base content is very high quality and satisfying. I would definitely recommend it as i enjoyed this too much to leave a bad review. It's just a real shame that this game was full of microtransactions, enough to buy this game twice over.

_childDocuments_.review: Interested in the previous chapters? You can find my review of Zombie Army Trilogy .Catching up after the end of ZA3, this installment will see both old faces and new heroes undertake a series of perilous missions to destroy the diabolical Hell Towers that have sprung up around Italy and neighboring countries. Even with Hitler’s demise, the undead are far from defeated. The world is in shambles as a result of the zombie apocalypse, so expect a setting consisting of ruined cities, crumbling bunkers and literal hellscapes. There is somewhat of a step back in the amount of macabre sights, compared to the previous entries.Don’t expect much from the plot of a zombie-killer title. Clichèd characters undertake engaging but narratively-bland endeavors through a simple plot line centered on dark magic and the occult. At no point there will be any shocking revelations or gripping moments; and that’s okay for this kind of game, which has story as the last of priorities.Each level will be divided in generally four chapters, taking place in a different section of a larger map. Once you cross the Safe Room marking the chapter’s end, there’s no going back, but you’ll be able to take eventual special weapons or consumables with you. The layout is mostly linear but rich in secondary areas and explorable zones out off the beaten path - they often house extra supplies, collectibles, upgrade kits or Easter eggs with plentiful references to video-game, pop and cinema culture. Exploration is rewarding, as the attentive player will certainly gain more advantages in terms of equipment and supplies. Each collectible (documents, comics, hands, heroic actions) will not only count towards achievements, but also award extra upgrade kits if all in the same chapter are found, while unlocking useful passive perks if enough are found globally. It’s great to see a game that gives you something in return for the extra effort of collecting such amenities, plenty of devs should take notes!You’ll be equipped with a primary weapon - always a sniper rifle of some kind - alongside a secondary close-range gun like a shotgun or an SMG, and finally a sidearm such as a pistol for dealing with weaker foes. Sniping enemies with precision shots will be the primary activity, since most zombies (but not all) have the head as the primary weak spot, meeting their demise with a single well-placed hit if unprotected. Enemies can also be killed in other body parts, but in that case they have a chance of resurrecting - except for Elites, brutal mini-bosses that need to be prioritized, as they wield heavy weapons and have a truckload of health.Usually maps have environmental dangers you can exploit, like explosive barrels, and crates providing throwables like grenades, mines and even artillery signals for total destruction of the biggest hordes. In addition, traps engineered by the resistance or improvised ones can be found and activated by a well-placed shot, excellent if used correctly to dispatch even the most powerful foes. Your own abilities and weapon mods will play a large part in battle too, with all throwables and consumables having two unlockable mods that significantly alter how they work, while passive perks and special abilities make the difference at higher difficulties.There’s only one real boss fight in the final level, in the shape of a multi-stage confrontation with the Zombie Army’s most lethal weapon. It’s an engaging fight, well-balanced and decently designed, that can be hard but also is fair. Each completed level will award a rating based on points, the higher the rating the more XP will be awarded, on top of optional challenges which also give some additional XP. As you level up, you’ll unlock new mod slots, abilities and consumable mods. While the former cost Upgrade Kits to be enabled, the latter ones are all free. Each weapon can be customized to best suit your needs with sights, expansions, better damage and more, and comes with a specific elemental damage that imbues shots with a different status effect once in a while. Maintaining a combo during levels by not missing shots is essential to get the coveted Gold medals. Horde mode pits you and your eventual allies against endless zombies in slightly reworked maps that open up more each couple of waves. New areas offer fresh healing, upgrades, heavy weapons and traps you’ll need to have a chance against the ever-stronger enemy. Nightmare is a special modifier that turns the zombie spawns up to an insane level - only for the most tryhard masochists, because the game on this level is nearly impossible to beat - by design.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough game to make a review for, if this could be neutral it would be.I recommended this game, ONLY if you get it on sale, this game at full price doesn't have enough content to justify it. Plus the DLC content (I'll get to that) furthers the lack content issue.Overall this game is basically better in every way than the previous Nazi zombie game.The other game was barley a DLC in my opinion but sold as a whole game. I think this game is a great game. The combat, controls, game play, it's all great and I don't have much to say but it's very good, it's fun to play, but I don't see this being fun in single player. This game if definatly a coop game.My issues with game play and difficulty.The game could stand to be more difficult. In a party of 3 on max difficulty there wasn't much challenge. Not enough zombies and far too many ammo crates. I find that there is so many ammo crates I never run out of ammo on anything bar the max difficulty. It could be argued that there isn't enough zombies and that the placement of ammo crates is just perfect IF there we're more zombies.Normal difficulty (with 2 players), there wasn't enough zombies, far too many ammo crates. No challenge whatsoever. Hard difficulty (with 2 players), there was barley more zombies than normal, just as many crates so the challenge was a marginal increase at best. Only in some situations when there is an influx of special's that actually make the game feel like it should.Very hard (with 3 players), there is finally a reasonable amount of zombies but I find the amount of crates of ammo is still a bit too much. No matter how reckless and trigger happy I am if I ever do run out of ammo there's an ammo crate just around the corner. The combo counter.Not much to say here, it just doesn't work. There isn't enough zombies to get large kill streaks so I don't see the point of it. The game has bonuses for getting kill streaks of 50's and 100's and most the time it's a struggle to get a 50 kill streak. There's not enough zombies to make it work.Level design and the drastic change.At first I was so happy with the map design, the game felt sudo open world in all the best ways. The level design was well thought out, fun to explore and large. This was a welcome change from the previous game as the first Nazi Zombie felt really small and linear. About halfway though the game this changed. Suddenly every mission became totally linear, almost no exploration options anywhere. It was a drastic change going from such an open map design to so closed. I was very disappointed when the maps stopped being so open with different areas to go to explore for collectable and pickups. I felt that the second half of the game was designed by an totally different team in terms of map design, this really bothered me. The game went from awesome to eh. Guns.Let's be frank here, this game has the lest amount of guns from all the sniper franchise. In the other games you could at least earn different guns, there was a wide variety of guns to choose from. Here you only get 9 guns. Yeah, 9. 3 snipers, 3 secondary and 3 pistols. I wouldn't take as much issue with this if there wasn't so much DLC content for more guns. The price for the DLC guns are so overpriced it's disgusting.  DLC content is fine but when the base content is actually lacking, loading it with overpriced DLC doesn't sit right with me.Having on 9 base guns and over 15 DLC (that are far too overpriced) just pisses me off. I don't approve of this practice and I think it's greedy and in bad taste. Keep in mind they took an exclusive release with Epic for a year so being this greedy with DLC is even more egregious. DLC is optional but the base game suffers from a lack of content, it feels like a paywall rather than optional DLC.Performance and stability.The performance is good, the game runs smooth and I had no issues with performance.This game had a year exclusive on Epic games, this is fine, what isn't fine is when the game finally comes to Steam it wasn't stable.There was crashing issues for this game until vulkan came out, since that it's been fine but a game being out for a whole year and having random crash issues is unacceptable. If a game takes an exclusive deal with Epic, when it comes to steam it better be bloody stable. I expect a year of being exclusive to be a year of dev work, small fixes and  patches, waiting until it comes to steam to make to actually stable? This isn't what game standards should be for stability.The loud intro.This is seriously just ridiculous, why the hell is the intro to all rebellion games so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loud. Stop it rebellion. I seriously have developed a hate for you over this issue alone. I own 4 of your games, I love the games, the time I have spent with friends enjoying myself but this damn intro, just stop it already.Take from this review what you will. I'm 50/50 on if I recommended this or not.Due to my frustration with the way they did DLC/lack of guns, initial launch instability/ crashes, short game play / overall lack of content just avoid this game. You will miss out on a unique and better take on the first Nazi Zombie game but for the price that unique and better take isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Army Zombie 4 delivers a solid experience for fans of the genre. The diversity of enemies is a highlight, and it will surely appeal to those nostalgic for the zombie mode of the Call of Duty franchise. Moreover, unlike CoD, Army Zombie 4 offers a flawless cooperative experience, allowing you to play with friends without any hitches.However, there are areas that need improvement. The game's sound design can be a bit off-putting and, at times, even irritating. The biggest letdown, though, is the soundtrack. It comes across as repetitive and doesn't vary between different maps, failing to establish an immersive atmosphere.Another point that could be revisited is the enforced use of snipers. Giving players the freedom to choose their weapons for each slot would enrich the gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The fourth installment in the Nazi Zombie Army spin-off series from Sniper Elite.  This game is a culmination of gameplay improvements starting with Nazi Zombie Army Trilogy's overhaul, added quest system, and narrative focus as well as lessons learned from The Strange Brigade.  I really like this game, and while it has some opportunities, in general I think it's a solid co-op zombie shooter that doesn't take itself too seriously, with varied characters, weapons, and powers to utilize.The first thing I need to address before getting into my pros/cons list is about the huge list of DLC for this game.  You'd be surprised how that detail flies right by people looking at the store page and then running to the forums to complain.  These games offer you the choice to buy what you want ( a dollar here, a dollar there), or get the whole lot at a tremendous discount.  For those conscious about spending large amounts of money, the game does routinely go on sale, and season passes can be bought later.  The latter content includes non-essential stuff like cosmetics, charms, and weapon skins, as well as expansions to the campaign, new characters and weapons.  Cosmetic stuff is neither here nor there, but the greater content really adds flavor to the game, and all the campaign stuff is set after the main game's available content, so you can purchase later if you truly enjoy the game.  You don't NEED to buy everything up front, and if you're on the fence about it, you definitely shouldn't.Pros:+  Looks great, runs great.  Seems to run on the same engine as Sniper Elite 4, which I enjoyed, with a bit of Strange Brigade mechanics thrown in for good measure.+  Supports a good variety of playstyles, has different fun game modes, and good campaign missions.+  Replayability, with objectives (main campaign missions net you upgrades for doing optional objectives), as well as means of upgrading certain weapons by using them to say, Shoot X amount of Zombie type Y type mini-objectives.  +  Four player co-op, and you can customize and scale the difficulty accordingly.+  Good dark humor, balancing between NZAT and SB as previously mentioned.+  You fight Nazi Zombies in Europe and Hell.  The main mission has crazy stuff going on, and then the DLC campaign missions go straight into awesome stuff I don't want to spoil.  Just... I love it.Cons:-  A lot of good guns are DLC only.  While you can use the base game guns, upgrade them to max, and have a good time, a lot of flavor is DLC exclusive and this causes some contention among fans.-  One character from NZAT is entirely absent, except as a cosmetic costume for a new character (who has a pretty crap German accent into the bargain).  Some of the DLC characters have weird passives or gimmicks, which makes them less attractive than Karl or Jun (two of the stronger ones in practice).  -  The game score system, like previous titles in the series, rewards combo kills and gratuitous violence over say, precision kills using a rifle like the main game series (Sniper Elite).  Those looking for an experience similar to SE will find Zombie Army scoring to be a bit obtuse, especially when a friend or some rando just hoses down a bunch of zeds with machine guns and throws grenades and gets number one score for the match.-  Some of the DLC weapon upgrade objectives are a bit too grindy.  Until certain missions launched (after the game was released), trying to get medic headshots for the PPK was a chore.  And good luck getting a last chance headshot on a Butcher using the same.  -  A plethora of weird masks, hats, and weapon charms seem a bit out of place, but I'll allow it.Really I'd have to reach for negatives in my review.  The game does what it sets out to do - make a zombie co-op shooter inspired by a bit of WW2 fantasy nonsense, with some stuff George Lucas probably watched as a kid in serials.  I had a good time soloing content, and a good time with friends as well.  And I'm looking forward to more content, or a sequel, when either occurs.

_childDocuments_.review: We have this odd but lovable child named Zombie Army 4: Dead War (ZA4) that surprisingly brings a lot of unique features and gameplay elements to the table. Despite its inspiration, ZA4 certainly manages to become a title of its own by providing a fun, leisure but also challenging and intense experience for newcomers and hardcore players alike.Like its predecessor Zombie Army Trilogy (ZAT), ZA4 is set in an alternative timeline of World War 2; Hitler resurrected his army from the dead using dark artifacts in the hope of turning the tide of the losing war. As one of the few survivors of the living, you must repel the undead, alone or with other comrades, and end the apocalypse once and for all.From traveling throughout Europe in ZAT, the journey now guides you across Italy, with many cities like Rome, Venice, the island of Sardinia, etc and eventually Hell itself. With  (haha get it?) campaigns in the base game, each one features different maps and themes associated, making the whole experience more less repetitive. Passing the narrow streets of Venice, or traversing the haunted forests of Sardinia, although each level in all campaigns is still linear by design, the layouts are more complex, with different paths and levitation.Unlike in ZAT where exploring every corners provides you with little to no worthy rewards, ZA4 makes sure to recognize the players’ time by giving them the tools to even turn the tide of a battle, like heavy machine guns, rocket launchers or the hard-hitting shotgun Preacher; consumables like medkits, traps and throwables. And of course, finding collectibles will also grant you perks that boost your stats in one way or another.With a total of 10 guns in 3 categories, and only 3 sniper rifles are pale in comparison to the arsenal of ZAT. If counting only rifles, then the previous title already gives us 9, with a total of 19 guns. At least, there are more variants of throwable, like the bait grenade that can help you score 20 multi-kills at once, or the divine grenades which are basically throwable medkits, unless you’re playing as a zombie (yes, you can do that in ZA4).Regardless, the limited weaponry still delivers a lot of firepower, more so when combined with mods. Gunplay is solid, paired with a heavy and impactful sound design and smoother animation; all of which conveys a much more modern experience compared to ZAT.With the introduction of mods, guns can be altered to perform much better than they once were. Aiming in first-person via a scope isn't exclusive to the sniper rifles anymore; the assault rifle MP44 can be equipped with a special scope that heals you everytime a critical hit is scored. Or if you prefer to go loud, the Shotgun Mortar is a destructive but pay-to-win tool that shoots grenades which can incinerate and (or) electrocute zombies with mods. Need an automatic gun but with the accuracy of a sniper rifle? The Gewehr 43 is waving at you.All of this progression is particularly noticeable in the late game, and everything can be upgraded with weapon upgrade kits scattered throughout the map, or rewarded from doing certain tasks like saving NPC, fully mastering a weapon, etc.You can’t expect to play a co-op Nazi zombie shooter without the  undead officers with hierarchy. The typical, cannon fodder, mindless husks are unthreatening, unless you get surrounded by them in higher difficulties. Then we have the elite variants like the slow-moving heavy gunners; and his intimidating brother called the butcher rushing to melee at you with a deadly chainsaw, which can be used against him with brutal takedowns. Not only that, we also face the more intelligent generals that can enrage or resurrect the fallen ones unless we put a bullet in their heads.Overall, the undead horde is well designed, and each archetype supports one another like a cohesive and orderly army, at least for the unliving. My only gripe is that the sound cues for some of the specials aren’t distinctive enough, making it harder and rather annoying to identify and prioritize them in a big fight, since the game likes to throw a butt load of zombies all at once in some events.If you’re a Left 4 Dead veteran looking for something new and refreshing, fans of Zombie Army series, or just completely new players to the franchise as a whole, ZA4 is definitely worth picking up, especially in a sale. Just don’t expect anything revolutionary, and enjoy the game, more so with a partner.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 hrs in less than 24 hrs. That's my other way of saying, this game is addictive. I can't believe how it took me this long to play this incredible zombie game. Shoot, and I thought Days Gone, The Evil Within, and Resident Evil, were the BEST third person zombie games out there. This game is its own category. The music, omg the music, is so awesome with a touch of 70's/80's background spooky noises. This game makes you feel you're watching a horror show from back in the day. Each level so far in my 10hrs of gameplay are very very very different. Each level with its own unique objective. Repetitiveness? that is quite unseen in this game. However, by the looks of it, this game can be played on numerous occasions each time being played differently, with a new character, different approach, etc... replayability is HUGE here. Collectibles, one of my favorites things in this game. You can collect from comics, to documents and how can I forget, my most favorite, the spooky zombie hand, which can literally be anywhere lol... there are 4/5 collectibles per level, which gives each level its sense of exploration. This game doesn't have copy/paste environment. Each level is totally different from the previous, giving you a breath of fresh air, each time you beat a level. Zombies, yes we have hundreds on top of hundreds of zombies. Zombies on this game are pretty fun. We even have zombies with weapons, yes, you read that wrong..wait..no you did not. this game has very unique zombies, from suicidal zombies to sniper zombies, you name it, this game has it.  DLC's, oh boy, here we go again, yes, DLC's, this game has plenty and when I say plenty, I mean over 30 DLC's, from season pass, to skins, to weapons cosmetics, etc... this is a deal breaker to some people, but in all honesty, the DLC's are there to whoever wants to buy them, the game doesn't really make you want to buy it. I guess it all depends how you see it. I bought this game on greenmangaming for 10 dollars less, I bought the season pass 2 close to 20 dollars less, and I bought the season pass 3 for full price. So I got a pretty good deal and I ended up getting all the DLC's. Season pass 1 is totally free to everyone (in the past people needed to buy it) which pissed off a lot of people....but hey, not our fault, at the end we all won someway or another. Sniper cam, do you like watching your bullet travel until it explodes your enemy's brain? orrr testicles? well you got it! if you're a fan of Sniper Elite, then you're familiar with the awesome kills from a sniper. Nothing like blowing off zombie heads or watching their baby makers get destroyed for your amusement. I totally recommend this game to anyone that's a huge zombie fan. You wont be disappointed if anything, you will only be disappointed you didn't bought it sooner, which is my case. The gameplay in this game is phenomenal and a well optimize game as well! !BUY IT YOU WUSS!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this off saying that I'm a veteran Sniper Elite/Zombie Army player. I've played SE since V2 and Zombie Army since the first game. I enjoy the challenge of these games and figuring out the bullet simulation in both series. Few games have made sniping so satisfying as Sniper Elite or Zombie Army when you nail that shot because you judged the proper distance and windage. Get a kill camera too? Icing on the cake of a job well done.This game spits on that entirely. This is the first game in the entire series that has decided to make it impossible to remove the bullet indicator. What's that? Well in all these games you have the option to hold your breath which then steadies your aim, increases your zoom level a tad, and in single player would slow time a bit to help you get that shot just right. When you would do this on lower difficulty settings a giant, ugly red diamond marker shows up inside your scope to tell you where to shoot. The bullet indicator is, and has been, one of the most annoying things to me from the entire series as it essentially negates the point of even playing with windage or gravity on and quite honestly feels insulting to the player (my OPINION). Previously that wasn't a problem as you just chose a higher difficulty that would remove it, or in later installments could actively turn it off in settings period. That setting is non-existent in this game. I tried checking forums to see if I was missing something. Everything is from a year ago when this launched on Epic and is the same thing: "Nope. Can't turn it off. Please give us the option, devs." Far as I can tell difficulty settings in this game will not remove it either. I can't say for certain because the highest difficulty (Brutal) setting is not available to you from the start. Hard is and certainly keeps it. I even looked into console commands and couldn't find anything worthwhile. Maybe somebody else out there knows a command for it, but I can't find it myself so ymmv.Now that the indicator rant is done the rest of this game for me just comes down to design choices that I cannot agree with and wouldn't recommend to anybody who enjoyed the previous installments. Everything is designed to try and push you towards the shop to buy guns that would previously have been available by default in the earlier titles, or (mostly, and this part is opinion) gaudy cosmetics for said guns and characters. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sniper rifles don't even have a zoom function until you level up your gun and then spend an upgrade kit to BUY THE FUNCTION OF ZOOMING IN ON YOUR SNIPER RIFLE IN A GAME ABOUT SNIPING. These games have always been fairly hokey as well (particularly the ZAT series), but this one jumps the bloody shark. Everything from the design elements to the way the game is played feels like it was just somebody trying their best (read: piss poor) to copy what they thought made people like Call of Duty's Zombie games. The feeling of previous Zombie Army games is gone. I don't know how to describe that exactly in a quantifiable way, but it is. That you'll just have to take my word for or waste your money and time to see for yourself.The game does add some interesting new things that for some players might be a bonus. One that I liked was being able to pick the reticle I wanted to use on each gun. That's something from the mainline SE series that was added in 3 (if I'm remembering correctly) and a welcome addition. The other additions are cosmetic as well with gun skins, character skins, hats, gun charms, emotes, etc. Basically any little dumb cosmetic thing that you had in other shooters of recent years is here. Yes I realize this game is a year old now as of this review being written.Summed up Pros/Cons (*cough* mostly cons)-This game doesn't feel like Sniper Elite or Zombie Army in a good way at all. Functionally similar features are there from previous titles, but they feel cheap and gimmicky by comparison.-Stuff that used to be part of the regular game by default is now locked behind paywalls (to include staple guns like the M1903 Springfield)-Sniper rifles need some asinine upgrade to even have a functioning zoom level for their scopes+Neat little cosmetics were added for characters and weapons-Most of said cosmetics were locked behind real money paywallsTLDR:I'm long winded on this, and for that I apologize, but this is a series I enjoyed immensely. For now I recommend saving your money and skipping this game. Maybe if the developers retroactively make massive changes it'll be worth it. For the record I got this on sale and even went so far as to get the SuPeR DeLuXe version recommended by another review. It was not, and is not in this current state, worth my time or money (or yours for that matter).

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a third person WWII Left 4 Dead. It is an extremely enjoyable experience, however, I do have my grievances. "Levels" are "chapters" in this game. Each level (set piece) has four of what I'll call "missions". The missions within each chapter can sometimes get monotonous. For example, a mission may just be, "clear this area" or "survive the horde", with some small thing to do, like flip a switch. After which, the safe room door unlocks and you can run in, ending the level. The mission will end and you will start the next mission in the safe room. The set pieces are all unique and memorable, and I love the start menu artwork for each level. It reminds me of 1950s horror movie posters (in the same vein as L4D2's levels).I beat the main campaign (non-DLC) on Medium my first playthrough, and I would say that there were only a few times that I felt like I was going to die. The game provides you with plenty of ammo boxes (which I like), so unless you are completely flippant with your ammo usage, you should always have some kind of weapon (and of course, melee). There are multiple levels of difficulty and, to be honest, I have yet to try Hard or above. With each difficulty, you can separately select the number of enemies spawned, based on how many people you are playing with. For example, if it's just you and you don't want to be overwhelmed, you can select "One Player". If you want a challenge, you can select up to "Four Players". The final option is "Nightmare", essentially fills areas with hordes of zombies, with a few heavies/specials sprinkled into the mix for good measure. These options provide players with in-depth difficulty settings, which I appreciate. Sometimes I want to complete a challenge that requires a lot of kills, but I don't feel like trying too hard. I'll just choose "Easy" as the difficulty, and "Nightmare" for the number of zombies.Each mission has a score counter. You can earn a higher score through kill-chains, basically shooting zombies in succession (within a time frame), or through double kills, etc. Once you reach the safe room, you are awarded XP based on your mission score. The XP system in this game is similar to most, with each level unlocking things like perks or cosmetic items. The level cap is 100, but you can "Prestige" and start again. As of this review, I am a level 60, but from what I've read, nothing resets upon prestige. I have absolutely no clue what the highest prestige is, but I saw a guy on YouTube that was a prestige 5.Aside from the story mode, there is also a horde mode. You select a map and it plays much like Call of Duty's zombie mode, with each wave getting more and more difficult. Once you complete wave 12, you can extract or continue (much like CoD). This mode will also earn you XP which, just like story mode, is based on your mission score. To be fair, most of the horde maps are just extensions of the story mode maps, but I can't fault the developers. If you are a fan of CoD zombies like me, you'll enjoy this mode (and the game as a whole).The one thing about this game I cannot stand is the amount of DLC. Luckily, I was able to purchase this game during the 2023 winter sale, so the base game was only $10, with each season pass being around $18 (season 1 pass is free). The DLC missions aren't bad (I've played two chapters so far) and the season passes do add a lot of content. However, if I had just bought the base game, I would have a very limited selection of weapons. Many of the DLC weapons are fun and unique, so that's a bummer for those who don't have any DLC. I do recommend getting the DLC, but only if it's on sale. For what it's worth, I do enjoy this game and plan on sinking some serious time into it. I also appreciate that Rebellion actually included swastikas in the game. It's always a little lame when WWII games focus on Nazis but all the flags are Iron Crosses or something (I get that the imagery is banned in some countries). I think the Nazi stuff is a little played out, but I like WWII history and the game is fun regardless. I think you should buy this game, but only on sale. I think $50 is a little steep for the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda conflicted over this entry to the series. Lets start with the most notable:- The monetisationquite frankly is disgusting. making us pay for weapons that are a staple of the entire series and included by default in previous entries. It feels like they were locked behind a paywall specifically to make you pay again just to get the same amount of content the previous 3 titles had. The only redeeming quality is that it goes on sale and you can buy each thing individually- The gameplay It's really weird... it took 10 minutes inside a mission to feel something was off, and after 2 hours as of writing this review i was able to pinpoint why. Compared to the last 3 in the series, the over the shoulder camera is noticeably lower down. more of the screen is taken up by your character. kind of annoying when you literally need the peripheral vision to see zombies approaching from all sides.Most importantly however, in all the previous games, when you aimed through your rifle scope, . now though? the scope is merely an overlay on the already awkwardly positioned camera, the bullet actually comes out of your gun. sounds fine, but the ADS camera doesn't adjust to your players position, so when you align a shot, sometimes you'll miss completely because the bullet is being fired from like 2 meters to the left of where the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scope is. I've ruined streaks because of this, it feels like you're no longer actually aiming down the scope and is horrible.Add to that, hit registration is ass. I've seen my bullet trails go straight through zombies without them taking any damage or flinching in the slightest, no hitmarker either. ♥♥♥♥ like that is kind of important in a game based around being a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ marksman surely? Why this got changed, i wish i knew. The original trilogy feels better and is more reliable.- The gameplay I love the new features and progression systems they've added. I never found an issue with previous titles not having these, but i do like feel like i'm getting stronger as i'm able to upgrade my weapons and perks, this is a good addition, albeit not a necessary one.Though i do find it weird how upgrading your stamina, requires you to not use your stamina... weird- Visuallyi mean i've always had a soft spot for nazi zombies, no matter how cliché and overdone it is at this point, especially when it goes full occult/hell. the whole series is great for this. Nice and colourful despite being mostly blacks/reds/greens/yellows. It really sets the atmosphere well.- Audiothe guns have always sounded weird to me, not horrible, but not great. I feel like they need a little more oomf.I wish our characters would shut up a little more often.the soundtrack is also great at matching the atmosphere, couldn't imagine myself listening to it outside the game though, nothing stellar.- The charactersAs i just mentioned, i wish they had less voicelines, or at least the new characters, even Karl to an extent... They suffer from cliché-action-hero-never-shut-up-itis. Pick a character from the original group or the left 4 dead packs instead.- The nameI'm genuinely confused, why'd you guys drop Nazi from the title? There's literally no hiding it in the game, you fight Hitler for christ sake. Come to think of it, you dropped the Sniper Elite part too when you released the previous Trilogy. i guess they're just trying to distinguish each sub-series more?Overall:It's still really fun. i've always enjoyed this series, the 4th entry is no different despite my strong distaste for whatever the ♥♥♥♥ they did to the camera and aiming mechanics. But the dlc situation gets on my nerves, probably too much. The game itself is still enjoyable as is, just make sure you get it on sale, because there's no way in hell, pun intended, that the whole game is worth the roughly £200 total asking price. even the just the base game at £40 is pushing it. It's worth £30 at a stretch, but even then, hold off for a sale for cheaper

_childDocuments_.review: Zombie Army 4 is a game I’ve held off from playing, but always thought was interesting. It gave me this arcade-y, silly vibe, and now that I have, it’s exceeded my a lot of my initial expectations.This game right off the bat feels very polished, and all of its mechanics feel very cohesive. It’s truly a rewarding experience going through each chapter, discovering upgrades, and going through new mechanic and opponents one after another. It feels absolutely amazing shooting heads of an entity that’s both zombie and nazi. It’s a fantastic combo.Each to their own, but the shared kill cam mechanic feels ridiculous. It’s an overglorified moment but it brings friends together.Despite making the basic zombies to walk, the game is nothing is short of terrifying. Especially when the game decides to spawn suicide bomber spawns left and right, and the number of opponents, each with unique gimmicks and mechanics. What strikes me is how they managed to really thin the line between silly and horrifying. This game feels like a weird fever dream of Michael Jackson’s Thriller gone wrong.It’s slightly disappointing that most of the guns are accessible through DLCs. On the other hand, the season one pass is free, and at the very least you have a ♥♥♥♥ ton of content to burn through. This is unlike many of the zombie co-op games we have, with the exception of L4D2. Furthermore, as long as one person has access to the DLC, you should be able to play all of the maps the game has to offer with your squad.The in-game UI is very snappy, and it takes a second to get in and out of a game. I’m at loss for words, but as a programmer, it makes me really happy. I’m sure even non-programmers would describe this experience as delightful.

_childDocuments_.review: This comes highly recommended.  It takes everything that made ZAT fun and does it better.  As far as the DLC goes, the game is completely playable and enjoyable without the DLC.  In fact, the only DLC that could be seen as "must have" would be the maps.  As far as guns go, base game guns are limited and fall into 3 standard categories: high damage/slow, low damage/fast, and mid for both.  The DLC weapons tend to fall within the 3 basic categories above and none are game breaking, pay to win and are comparable to those in the base game.  You will miss nothing by not buying any DLC characters as the abilities they have are available through the free L4D characters.  Character skins are nice but add nothing but cosmetics.  Weapon skins are skippable and who really cares about charms?  Is there a lot of DLC for the game, yes.  Is the DLC needed to enjoy/play the game, no.  Get the base game, maps, maybe a DLC gun or character/skin or two and call it a day.  So to those complaining about the DLC amount/price:  it is not necessary to get it all.  As of Jan. 2022, you can get the base game and 9 map packs on sale for around $62.00 and you will have just about everything concerning game play.  The rest  is just cosmetics or variety.

They've also removed the ability to stomp your way out of trouble, which was kind of ridiculous in ZAT.Slight update: Having played a few more hours, I'd say this is definitely good value without shelling out on any additional DLC. One other thought is that this feels a lot like RE4 in parts (which is a good thing) and is much more geared towards rifle use. _childDocuments_.review: The sad thing is that I really wanted to be able to give this game a positive review. The game itself is great. The combat is smooth and flows well with your character swapping between weapons, using abilities, pickups, and using the environment to face unique challenges on each map. However I only ever played single player, as the online community is non-existent. If you want to play with people, you need friends. And it's really difficult to convince your friends to buy a $60 base game with over $100 of downloadable content (even on sale), especially for a game that they are only likely to play for a month or two. The game itself is perfectly fine. It was well made. The gameplay is smooth. The graphics are great. The classes are balanced. Even the story-line is at least interesting. But the ridiculous amount of DLC the developers have locked behind a paywall is just sad. And this drives away any hope of a flourishing community. Single player mode is great to see the story and experience it once. But there's no replay value without others to play with. This franchise could have been the next Left4Dead. But no. Corporate greed. So I cannot recommend this game, unless and until the developers change their practices. I feel like I am just echoing a very common theme among gamers these days. We are tired of this nonsense.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to add a qualifier to my 'no': steam only allows to either recommend or not recommend a game. There is no in-between option.For me this game would fall into the 'in-between'-area. I would rate it 3 of 5 stars. It is not a bad game  - but it isn't as good as some similar games I have played (Strange Brigade by the same developers is a lot more fun IMO as is L4D2 by Valve). The reason why I decided on a thumbs down instead of a thumbs up is the price: for a 3 of 5 star 'ok but not great' type of game it is overpriced. It cost € 50 for the normal edition and € 60 for the deluxe edition when I  was writing this review. It is just not good enough to warrant that price. However once it drops to maybe 10-12 € things would be different. It would be worth it then.***Here are the details of why the game is just average:- the game story is too deadly serious and overly dramatic. The ease and humor of Strange Brigade is entirely missing. Even L4D2 (although a serious zombie shooter) is more humorous and has some flair of ease compared to this game.- exacerbating the above problem is the game art: the surroundings are always dark and misty. This obviously is an artistic choice of the game developers to make the game look more eerie but it has the effect that the game dampens my mood and I don't want to continue playing. - the game has a leveling system. This makes it harder to just join a group of other players and have fun for half an hour or so without having to worry about relative combat strength of the toons. This is contrary to Strange Brigade and L4D2 where everyone is the same power level and you can just join anyone without having to worry.- game paths in the Zombie Army 4 campaigns are too narrow. You never get an 'open world' feeling because there are always obvious fences/map borders to your left and to yourt right. Now in Strange Brigade and L4d2 you  have game paths you have to follow too BUT these are better hidden and the areas you are in somehow look more open so that your lack of choice as which path to follow is less obvious. That gives those games a more realistic feel and more immersion.- lack of jumping/dodging ability in Zombie Army 4.  It is just not there. Meaning your character is much less agile which lessens the fun of the game considerably. Contrast that with the very cool dodge-jump in Strange Brigade and with the jumping ability in L4D2 and the 'push away enemy' ability there. Those are fun things to have. I am puzzled as to why they left that out of Zombie Army 4.- too many things you have to pay for as dlcThe game already is too pricy for the fun it offers. Now if you want to use this weapon or that skin you have to pay for those too? And it is not just a few things. It is a ton of things. They are trying to grab your money for their own benefit. Understandable? Maybe. Good for you? Definitely not.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, an improvement over the previous iterations in the series.  In short, ZA4 is a melding of Zombie Army, Sniper Elite, and Strange Brigade: NZA tropes + watered-down SE sniping + SB minus chests.Some things have taken steps backwards: unlike SE, it's linear; going prone is gone; many weapon upgrades feels like an afterthought (scopes on machine guns; generic fire / electricity mods; more powerful melee--in a shooter); world interactivity (climbing, hurdling, accessible doors / windows) isn't as prominent.. While some aspects have gotten better: take-down melee system; magic melee weapons; customisation / skins; significant visual (graphics / animation) improvements.As others have mentioned, the product's price point, and "DLC" retail model irk most.  There is no way to buy the "complete" game (*as of writing, a "4th season" is in the offing -- i.e., it's a TBC on the game's final "completeness" / available retail packages) -- with even the "Super Deluxe" package lacking a lot subsequently-released DLC accoutrements.  If one buys the so-called "base game", they won't get access to half of the missions; much less, a lot of the weapons, characters, and/or skins.  That, and the game is far from cheap to begin with; especially considering the title had 12 months to baste at EGS.All in all, the game is a solid step forward in the NZA series, and is certainly fun in co-op (rather repetitive in solo).  Having said that, many of those steps, visuals aside, are baby strides; and it would nice to see these Rebellion TPS games being move in a more open-world direction.  If one can acquire the game's "Super Deluxe" package while it is on a 50%~75% off sale, and they have regular co-op partners to play with, NZA4 is worth it (any loose DLC's can then be selectively / frugally bought, if desired, and without feeling 'as' ripped-off).  However, outside of sales -- especially if with most / all available content* -- the game is egregiously overpriced.  Rating: ★★★★★★★☆☆☆

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa, slow down there, mate! Are those microtransactions giving you a bit of a headache, eh? I hear ya loud and clear! Skins are all well and good, but once they start fencing off weapons behind a paywall, it's like, come on, don't go messing with the essence of the game!But before you toss this game out like yesterday's news, give me a sec to bend your ear. It's actually a hoot to play, especially now that they've chucked in season one with the base game without dipping into your wallet for extra dough. I reckon it's a cracking deal when it's on sale.The core game is a right blast. The interface is dead easy to navigate, the weapons have this cracking upgrade system that's just a joy to mess about with. Personally, I went all in on explosive ammo for my sniper, and let me tell ya, popping off shots with that thing was bloody brilliant. Then there's this perk system that adds a bit of spice to the mix. Sure, some of them are a bit pointless, but a few really kept me hooked.And the baddies? Oh, they've got variety, they do. Mini-bosses, all sorts of nasties to deal with. Plus, the scoring system when you're taking 'em down? It's like a bloody rainbow, mate! The more you kill, the more vibrant it gets. It's proper satisfying.Loads of gear to mess about with, special attachments, and all your favorite signature weapons make a comeback. The campaign? Will take a good 15-20 hours, and that's with poking around for secrets and collectibles. My mate, he's all about that stuff, you know. And with the perks and weapon choices, there's heaps of replay value.And let's not forget the pièce de résistance—slow-motion bullet time. Adds a whole new layer of fun, especially when you're mowing down zombies by the horde.Sure, there are a few bumps in the road – like a gazillion DLCs cluttering up the landscape. But hey, at least season one helps ease the pain. And while the cosmetic add-ons don't ruffle my feathers, locking most of the weapons behind a paywall? Now, that's a head-scratcher.Overall, I gotta say, I had an absolute blast with this game, especially when mucking about with friends. Would I recommend it? Absolutely! It's just a shame it's drowning in microtransactions – enough to buy the game twice over. But hey, nothing's gonna rain on my parade when the core gameplay is this rock solid.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you're looking for a really satisfying zombie shooting gallery.  It feels like someone took Nazi Zombies from the old Call of Duty World at War and made a narrative campaign building from that base.  It very much feels like a spiritual successor to the days when CoD Zombies was good.  I can very easily recommend this game.There is a good selection of weapons, an upgrade system for said weapons, varying difficulty options, very well-designed maps, good zombie variety,  and a great co-op experience with friends.  A very nice package overall.  I was trying to find a game that satisfied my zombie-slaughtering itch for years.  This definitely did it.However, I cannot do this review without talking about the negative: the price.  The price of the base game plus the DLC content that adds new maps and weapons is simply outrageous.  There are far better games out there available for far less money.  It is an obvious rip-off on the pricing, whether the publisher or developer is to blame, I don't know; but it blows hard.If you are willing to pay the over-inflated price to buy this game and you are looking for a great Zombie-killing experience, this is a game to get.  I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside of the obvious (the high price of the game and season passes) it's a great game. If you can get all of the content on sale, it will be very well worth it.Now, let's go over the good things this game has to offer.If things like visuals are important to you, this game holds up still. Areas are very well crafted, character models and their outfits, explosions, gun skins, you name it, they all look pretty solid.There are X-Ray cinematics on kills which are nice to look at, you can also set their frequency and speed which is a nice touch, a little bit of everything for your taste.Sounds and music fit the situations you will find yourself in very well.So, with base game you will get 9 chapters in total (first season pass is free which contains 3 chapters).You will have all sorts of different objectives, refuel the boat, defend certain areas, repair the bridge and so on. There is a lot of variety in what you have to do throughout the missions which makes it a lot more interesting compared to other zombie shooters.Season pass 2 and 3 bring the best maps in my opinion. They are extremely well designed, have new different objectives, more elite enemies, more of the story. Great package overall.They also bring some of the best guns in the game that are also very fun to use. New character skins are looking so good as well.Ragnarok part 1 and 2 will bring you more story and few more cosmetics, it goes very cheap on sale so you can't go wrong with it.You can find public games fairly easily still, so if you plan to play random matches you are not gonna have a hard time getting into the game.If you have friends from different parts of the world that you want to play the game with, don't be alarmed, even on high ping this game still works incredibly well. There is minimal lag even when you go above 250 ping, which is honestly extremely good.One thing i can't stress enough is to not play this game on easier difficulty. Even if you are just getting into the game, my advice is to set difficulty to at least Hard and enemy scaling to 4 players (if you are in full party this will be automatically set to max). This will make the game much more fun and chaotic and your experience will be much better than if you choose easy or normal. Work your way towards Brutal and Nightmare (or both) because that is where this game really shines.I wholeheartedly recommend this game! It's one of the best in the genre and if you get all the content on sale, you will be very pleased with your purchase! Happy slaying!

_childDocuments_.review: Ana and I have purchased Zombie Army 4: Dead War. Its a follow-on to Zombie Army Trilogy. This game offers more difficulty levels and a semi decent campaign. It is plagued by the multiple season passes, and low price in game purchases. What puts this game over the edge is the revived "Horde Mode" in which you see how many waves you can go on a relatively small map. The objective is to get to the beginning of wave 13 and you can escape if you decide to do so. If you decide to hold your ground after wave 12, the waves get increasingly more difficult and complex.There are "zombie officers" that perform different functions.There are zombie "Heavies" which as 'bosses" of different types, like The Butcher who dances at you with a huge buzzsaw looking to take your limbs off, or the Flamer who is not shy about using his oversized flame thrower to knock you down, or anything in its flame spewing path. Add in the Gunner who boasts a HUGE machine gun laying waste to anything he aims at.There is even a "Screamer" who is blind and attacks by hearing . Be aware because it has acute hearing and is deadly.Oh did I mention, there Grenadiers who constantly whip explosive or fire damaging grenades at you.There are pesky zombie Snipers who are pretty accurate, along with their pals who are called Rocket Snipers who propel Bazooka rounds at you feet for splash damage.Not to mention a sicko looking twisted zombie who is tied up in grenades and TNT and has a rather explosive personality.There is a Shadow Demon we simply call death. If he "grabs" you and draws you into the zombie chaotic mess, if his actions don't make you fall down, being surrounded by the zombie horde just might.Oh yeah, then the horde itself ! The "green" zombies that "puke" globs of green goo at you that damage as well as slow your retreat.The rather quick (compared to most "normal") zombie who wields a MP44 and although not purely accurate, can make you curse if it hits you and you have very few hitpoints left.When you're not looking - or paying attention to your feet, along comes the "Creeper" who is a zombie on all fours crawling low to the ground and gnawing away at your precious health. They do not come one at a time, typically if you see one, you can expect to see about a dozen or more headed your way.Then, the parade of semi regular zombies comes about, mixed in with all the above mentioned beast.You are then tasked with trying to figure out what to kill first.Oh, did I mention, that the above list of madness above can come all at once, in a single wave? yeah this is freakin' crazy at times. Ana and I play this on EASY 1 players worth of enemies and as the waves head past 20+, it gets down right chaotic. I don't even want to think what comes on Normal mode, Hard mode or Brutal mode.THIS game is truly a game of Chaos management. Although, the campaign side of the house is a little more forgiving. At least in Campaign mode, you're able to use the best of the best guns you can master. In Horde mode, it's luck of the draw on about 6 different gun drops on the map as you progress along. You will hear me say "YES !" when I get the Mosin-III Sniper, a Thompson-III and the M-1911 pistol, as these are the highest ones you can get. A few games you are forced to run the horde gambit with a mediocre sniper, a SMG not to your liking and a pistol which just might heal your team mates.Fate had something to do with the creation/creativity of Zombie Army 4: Dead War. I feel Fate in my bones every time I start to feel in command of the horde mode only to look up and see three bosses, a massive army of exploding TNT weirdos and snipers trying to keep me busy.Crazy. But, fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)Zombie Army 4: Dead War enthralls with its stunning graphics, immersing players in a post-apocalyptic world filled with eerie atmospheres and hauntingly beautiful decaying environments. From blood-soaked streets to crumbling buildings, the attention to detail is exceptional, complemented by atmospheric lighting that intensifies the horror. Smooth animations and well-executed character design further enhance the visual appeal.Gameplay: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)The gameplay in Zombie Army 4: Dead War is an absolute thrill ride from start to finish. The controls are intuitive, responsive, and easy to grasp, allowing both experienced and novice players to jump right into the action. The vast selection of weapons, including shotguns, snipers, and explosive devices, offers a satisfying arsenal to obliterate hordes of undead enemies. Each mission offers strategic opportunities for varied playstyles, while the cooperative multiplayer truly shines with seamless online connectivity and intense team-based combat.Sound Design: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)The spine-chilling sound design in Zombie Army 4: Dead War is nothing short of phenomenal. From the eerie background ambiance to the haunting groans of zombies, every audio element contributes to the terrifying atmosphere. The visceral sound effects of bullets piercing undead flesh and the thunderous explosions of heavy weaponry add an extra layer of immersion, enhancing both the intensity and satisfaction of each encounter.Storyline and Narrative: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)While not the main focus, Zombie Army 4: Dead War delivers an engaging and intriguing storyline that keeps players invested in the game's world. The narrative unfolds through enthralling cutscenes and well-voiced dialogue, providing context and depth to the zombie-infested journey. Although it may veer into familiar territory at times, the inclusion of supernatural elements and unexpected plot twists inject vitality into the overall narrative experience.Multiplayer Experience: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)Zombie Army 4: Dead War excels in its cooperative multiplayer, designed for intense zombie-slaying sessions with friends or online partners. The seamless matchmaking system ensures quick and hassle-free connections, allowing players to team up and face the unrelenting undead together. The cooperative element fosters camaraderie, encouraging strategic teamwork, resource sharing, and coordinated tactics, all of which intensify the multiplayer enjoyment.Replayability: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)Zombie Army 4: Dead War offers ample replay value, with its various difficulty levels, unlockable weapons, upgrades, and hidden collectibles. Each playthrough presents opportunities to discover additional secrets, try new loadouts, and tackle the campaign with different approaches. Moreover, the thrilling horde mode provides endless waves of zombie chaos, perfect for honing skills and testing endurance.Conclusion:Zombie Army 4: Dead War delivers a captivating co-op zombie experience with its breathtaking graphics, immersive sound design, and highly satisfying gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Zombie Army 4 is a lovely game. Its primary inspiration is Left 4 Dead, with some DOOM and CoD Zombies influences sprinkled within. I have been a big fan of the franchise since the first Nazi Zombie Army and all I can say is that Zombie Army 4 certainly innovates over its predecessors. Some times in ways that I enjoyed (Abilities, Variety in equipment, Customization etc) but other times In ways I really didn't like (A massively overloaded HUD, an actual army of DLC content, way too many particle effects and sounds not fitting the themes of the setting).My biggest gripe with Zombie Army 4 is the atmosphere and aesthetics. The Original trilogy had a much heavier suffocating atmosphere. The gore was much more as well. And so was the occult symbolism. Overall it felt more like a heavy metal cover with the absurd levels of grotesque violence and overwhelming atmosphere on display. Zombie Army 4 doesn't feel quite like that. It feels more cartoonish, like someone tried to make the original trilogy in a platform like Fortnite. The "silliness" of a lot of the DLCs, the taunts and the extreme levels of dialogue that were lacking in the first three games also play a role in ZA 4's loss of identity.The game is GOOD. The shooting feels legit. The zombies are fun to massacre. There is a lot of challenge to be had and a lot of things to collect. On top of that the graphics are amazing. Also the finally fixed the Submachineguns which is lovely. I recommend this game IF on sale, because frankly the asking price for the game itself + all the season passes outside of a sale is outrageous.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi.I'm sharing my Zombie Army 4 Dead War Playthrough at  played with SubnormalHunter.The new mechanics are great and the action was improved on this last game from the Saga.Summary:Zombie Army 4: Dead War is a third-person shooter video game developed and published by Rebellion Developments. Set in an alternate version of World War II, the game follows a group of survivors fighting against hordes of Nazi zombies unleashed by Adolf Hitler's occult rituals.Players take on the role of one of four characters, each with unique abilities and skills, as they traverse various locations across Europe, including cities, forests, and desolate landscapes. The main objective is to eliminate the undead using an arsenal of weapons, traps, and special abilities while completing missions and objectives.The game features both single-player and cooperative modes, allowing up to four players to team up online to battle the zombie horde together. As players progress, they unlock new weapons, upgrades, and character customizations to enhance their chances of survival.Zombie Army 4 incorporates intense action, strategic gameplay, and a blend of horror elements with a dark and atmospheric setting. The game's narrative unfolds through missions and cutscenes, revealing a story of survival, mystery, and the struggle against overwhelming odds in a world overrun by the undead.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this and I'm not disappointed.  It is different than ZAT - they turned it into a lot more of an Arcade-Shooter but improved it in a lot of areas too.  If you played Strange Brigade it is easy to see the marriage between that and ZAT(part 3) in ZA4: Dead War. -Each character has their own strengths and weakness making character builds more varied and a bit more interesting. Plus you can pick perks to tailor to your playstyle.  -Horde mode is more progressive, as it was in Strange Brigade. -New kill combo rewards, heavy weapon category, traps, and limited inventory/supply turn previous tactics into more of a run-n-gun style play (again like SB and ZATpt3).  -Laying prone is a thing of the past but you can still sprint, crouch, and vault. -The game isn't as gritty - following the direction of Part 3 of ZAT - and has a lot more splatter and dry British humor. -There are lots of Easter Eggs and nods to pop-culture abound. -Excellently optimized. Long maps and well detailed. -Several new enemy types. Sure it is a bit steeply priced even after waiting a year for it to come out on Steam, but the game has a lot more to offer than ZAT or SB and with Season Pass 1 & 2 it would seem that the game is doing well and probably won't be steeply discounted for a long while yet. Hope to catch you all in the game!Updated after 80hrs more of play:Some campaign levels feel short towards the later end of the main story but overall there is a good mix of layouts and map diversity. I'm looking forward to replaying them all with a full party of four.I reviewed the Season Passes separately and you can find the reviews on the Season Pass pages. But in short, Season Pass One is a great deal: the maps, weapons, and new characters make it worth getting the Super Deluxe Edition of the game. Season Pass 2, although having also nice maps and great weapon additions, offers little else worth note (ie: some of the bonus cosmetics are nice but mostly bad filler). Season 2 is inferior to the first and should be, in my opinion, reduced in price accordingly. Season Pass 3 was announced in 2020 for 2021. I'm looking forward to it.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is interesting. The gameplay is a much more advanced version of L4D2 and a tps version. It ties in faithfully to the first trilogy. Gameplay is great. The level designs are generally magnificent. It was definitely a great experience. The game constantly flows and even the cinematics are great. The best Sniper Elite game overall. Even though I prefer realistic game design, I loved this game. It's even more enjoyable with friends. You can finish most of the game on your own, but I'm not sure about that in the final chapter of Ragnarok Part 2. Still, it's not impossible. I always played on hard. So what I said is valid for hard. At the same time, the game repeats itself very little. This is another success. The art design is great. The enemy types are very good. It never gets boring. Hit feeling is good. Strategic limb dismemberment is a spectacular feature that reflects both visually and physically. At the same time, the characters have personalities. They all have some degree of character development. This is really awesome. In general, even the side characters and antagonists manage to be interesting when necessary. The dialogues are very well written. Every character has a style. They even have their own passive bonuses. And even the side equipment we use has separate development features. If it were a popular series, it would be as loved as Doom. I'm not joking, I mean it literally. I even think it's better than Doom.There are somethings I don't like it. Some weapons are more powerful than others. So there is a balance difference between weapons. You understand this more clearly later in the game, and unfortunately, you can only upgrade 4 weapons in your first playthrough. It is unnecessary to have missions to unlock the features of some weapons. Unfortunately, the story is left unfinished in Ragnarok part 2. It should definitely continue. The endings of the original Zombie Army Triology and Zombie Army 4 Vanilla were very good. This was quite a disappointment. At the same time, the last episode is very boring and poorly designed. It's like it was rushed. There's a lot of DLC and that means spending a lot of money.My attitude towards the game is generally very positive. The number of players is still sufficient and it has a loyal audience. Playing the game co-op from start to finish is another reason for praise, and they reflected all this adventure in the cinematics. I would love for them to release one last DLC, complete the whole story, and maybe connect it to Zombie Army 6 (if they have such a plan in mind). Happy hunting!My score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game but my recommendation is to not buy this at full price or just buy it on sale cause honestly, when you're playing it alone, it's not worth the full price. Main reason being that it doesn't have bot players. All the missions (except for the first one) are really tough when you're alone EVEN in easy difficulty, zombies swarm the f*ck out of you. And even if you have the sufficient tactics to overcome that, if you get pinned even ONCE by a special zombie you bet that your ass ain't surviving that. On the flip side, game optimization is great, you can literally play this game with a not so strong PC (given you're playing it at the lowest setting) and also, this game is really fun when you have at least one friend to accompany you, controls are  great, aiming is great and the upgrades really do give you decent advantages for survival and offense. Levels are designed well items are placed where it's not too easy or too hard to get them. Enemies are positioned  in places that you're able to take them on when playing with a friend. Though again, still not friendly with solo players.One thing I forgot to mention is the online queuing, yes you could have strangers instead of friends to play with you instead but you don't really get a choice most of the time about what mission you want to play.  Queuing is long for the mission you want to play and if you just picked "Quick Play" instead, you're just going to be dropped (most of the time) at a random game whilst it's still in progress, I know some people are fine with that, but for me, I personally hate it when I don't start at the very beginning of a mission/episode. So to reiterate, for the most part, you won't get the mission you want with multiplayer and you also won't start at the very beginning to experience the mission in its full glory. Not everyone has a friend that's interested in playing this game so for those players, they don't really have that much of a choice but to go play with strangers or go solo.TLDR; Game is fun but it not having any bot players killed this game for me. If you're going for solo or you want to play with strangers, just go get World War Z instead you'll have a much better time in that.Overall Rating: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, let me get that out of the way very quickly. There are changes between this one and the rest of the series that are just baffling, frustrating, or just dumb.The core gameplay is still there, still basically the same. Kind of. You have less weapons to pick from, and can't pick out any kit items when selecting a chapter. In exchange, they've introduced some kind of modern multiplayer FPS setup screen which reeks of the trappings of what all the other games were not. Player skins, stupid trinkets, weapon skin. I don't mind the introduction of abilities, that was a twist I thought would freshen things up a bit.The modern FPS post mission wrap up screen also makes an appearance between each chapter. In the old games, each mission had four or five chapters separated by safe rooms. You'd walk around in the safe room restocking on grenades and deciding whether or not to switch out your weapons from the ones lying on tables or sitting in racks or what not. It all helped the levels flow together seamlessly, giving a sense of unbroken gameplay to each mission. All the care a detail in safe rooms is gone and an offensively ugly competitive FPS screen throws itself in your face the moment you step into the saferoom, demolishing the flow of the level and story entirely.But that brings up the worst thing of all. All the problems I have with the game, including the ones listed here, are mostly subjective and all forgivable. Except, for the DLC. There was no DLC for any of the other games. ZA4 has three ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hundred dollars worth of DLC. Each category of weapons has three non-DLC weapons each, and five or six DLC weapons. Each DLC weapon is a single item of DLC cost 5$. You have to buy each weapon, individually. The game has fifteen missions, six of them are individual DLC. Skins and trinkets, fortunately, can be applied to multiple weapons or come in a pack with the same skin for all the weapons. I don't understand why it was necessary to gouge people with DLC for features in a game where they just don't belong. It's not like this is a cheap game either. ZA4 is a FULL PRICED GAME. It costs 50$, and they're still throwing 300$ of DLC at us. That's Paradox numbers when it comes to DLC. Did it sell poorly on the Epic store and they had to show returns on that exclusivity bribe? I don't want to think renegade are this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ greedy and chalk it up to some obligation to Epic, but you never know. Things change.Go get Zombie Army Trilogy instead. All the weapons are free and it comes bundled with all the missions from Nazi Zombie Army 1 and 2, free of charge. Also a bunch of characters to pick from, and no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really liked the first three in the series, but this one just falls flat. Beyond the obvious, obnoxious, and unending money-grab, it just seems linear and inflexible, and far less engaging in terms of game-play and story than any of the earlier entries. It also comes across as more of a tower-defense game than anything else: follow a pre-set path, kill enemies along the way, survive the incoming horde. Repeat and repeat and repeat. No complaints on voice acting or graphics, and If you can get it on sale and don't have very high expectations, it's fine enough. To expect it to equal or surpass any of the first three, though, is a hope doomed to die in failure...

_childDocuments_.review: So, the game itself is overall fun and well made yet feels like a massive upgrade in terms of combat when compared to Zombie Army Trilogy or even SE4/V2 Remastered. I highly recommend the game-play as it feels but doesn't copy and paste Left 4 Dead nor World War Z. Now onto the bad things. So, the game itself can be fun, yes. But that's still a bit exaggerated when playing online due to the controls feeling unresponsive and overall laggy yet showing me "Green" ping (full signal bars). I saw a LOT of negative reviews before getting this, stating "too much monetisation". Holy f*ck! This game has so much monetisation, it makes Call of Duty, Battlefield and Fortnite look good. So, the game itself is £40 (or on sale right now for £13.59). That's the base game. We still have 87+ separate DLC's which only TWO are free being a Left 4 Dead crossover. £30 for a season pass that includes 3 maps, okay. But THREE season pass' alongside season pass two and three NOT being included in the "Super Deluxe Edition". To add more to this fact, outside the season pass is weapons that were Free and available in Rebellion games prior to this, skins for character, weapons, charms and even emotes (taunts and celebration). On estimate, I like the game but refuse to play it and refunded it due to the monetisation as if I were to get into the game. For me to enjoy it and play all the maps (as most people want to do in games), I would have to spend £90 on Season Pass'. I recently bought God of War for £40 and got 50 hours of play-time out of it on my FIRST play-through. A FULL GAME, BELOW HALF THE PRICE. That's just the THREE pass' as well. I ain't even including some weapon packs, cosmetics etc. Anyhow, it's a massive shame as I love Rebellion as a company, they aren't the biggest of companies but always produce top tier games since Sniper Elite 1. ZA4:DW has ruined their streak for me and hope Sniper Elite 5 that has been announced doesn't get this anti-consumer marketing. Maybe I'm just nostalgic, maybe I just like to complain about things that others don't care about... But to me, if I buy a game, I expect to have hours of fun and not spend MORE on the side content compared to the base game. Bring back GTA IV, CoD MW2, Kane and Lynch 2 and Max Payne 3. For a side note, as much as I did actually have fun playing the game, I just had this grinding in the back of my head every time I went to the menu seeing everything locked. I refunded it and going to tell you the best advice. If you love Rebellion games or are new to Rebellion games. Go play the better games. Sniper Elite's (2-4 are amazing games), Zombie Army Trilogy (lacks level up system but hours of fun nonetheless) or even Strange Brigade (underrated Rebellion game and great CO-OP). TLDR:Unless willing to spend double, even triple the price of the base game on the extra content. Avoid at all costs. Bad marketing and very anti-consumer.
