_childDocuments_.review: I like to go into games as blind as possible. Scorn was such a game where I knew from the first seconds I saw the first trailer that it was a must play for me and have not looked at it again until now when I picked it up. I must confess though that this time because of not taking in any other info I misjudged the game and was at first a bit disappointed. I had just played through the amazing System Shock 1 and 2 again and for some reason I had assumed this would be a "Shock" style game with inspiration from games like System Shock, Bioshock and Prey etc. It might have been these "vending" machines that do things to your body that really had those vibes. But all set in a very different and interesting setting. That is not the case though (The "shock" part that is, the setting is every bit as interesting as one could want and even more) there is no sprawling map to explore or skill trees with different paths to choose from in how you modify and "splice" your body with different abilities as you progress. Instead it is more streamlined linear game that centers around some puzzles and some bare bones combat.After my initial let down as to what I thought the game was going to be and what it actually was I still felt amazed by the game. The setting and environments are just on a whole other level compared to most games. The landscape is like something out of a nightmare or straight out of hell. Sometimes it reminds me of prometheus from Alien, other times the cthulhu myth but most of the time something completely unique. This is actually what makes the game and what makes it such an unique experience. It really feels like stepping into another world that is not just a copy of something else you have seen before. It feels alien and familiar at the same time. If I had to choose one game world where I would not want to end up in personally it would probably be this one. It is truly nightmarish. The puzzles are ok and the combat is quite lackluster (one could even say bad, though I am still glad they have it in there for variety), but the whole package still shines above it all and makes it something I am really glad I played. Some scenes are also completely beautiful, often in a nightmarish way at the same time. I still wished in some ways that it was more of a "shock" game in gameplay with this special setting, that could be truly amazing and something I have a hope that the developers might do if they continue to explore this world in future games. But what the game actually evolves into from start to finish is also something that is more memorable than most other games.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but with several reservations.Surface level: Buy it, but only on sale.Diving deeper, this game is artistically stunning. Its a demented love-child combining H.R. Giger, I Have No Mouth and I Must Scream, and Fire in the Sky, really delving into a niche of Sci-Fi horror not commonly explored. I continued playing the game to the end, not because I enjoyed the game play (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hated it), but just out of simple curiosity.Light spoiler warning.You never find out what your 'protagonists' motivations are or why they are doing what they're doing. I felt very immersed in trying to keep my character alive, even when I had no choice in the matter.I don't recommend this game if you are looking for something casual. At best its artsy and pretentious, at worst its a multi-hour walking simulator. If you appreciate atmosphere and metaphors, this game is a good buy (when on sale).There is the saying, 'the flesh is weak', but not in Scorn.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited six years for it, and it makes me so happy to say that Scorn is a fascinating and stylish adventure/survival horror game. To get it out of the way, the graphics and the art direction in this game are mind boggling. The influence of Giger and Beksinski are on full display, and the haunting atmosphere and grotesque biomechanical environments are as repulsive as they are magnetic. Navigating the spaces here is an incredibly immersive experience, with brilliant sound design, sparse and haunting ambient music, and lighting that leaves everything stark and shrouded in a bleak darkness. It plays like your typical point and click from the first person perspective and is comprised of exploring environments and solving puzzles. While that is the majority of what you're doing, it's punctuated by occasional combat encounters that, while clunky, are suited to the games overall feel. I get the feeling some people were expecting a Doom-esque shooter (which would explain some of the baffling negative reviews), however I think having that level of smooth, efficiently violent capability would've undermined the tension at play here. The narrative here is subtle, and isn't spoon fed to the player. It's ambiguous, with the games ending leaving me awe struck; I'm still thinking about it. I'd equate this game to something like an arthouse film. If slow gameplay and extracting meaning for yourself don't seem like things that you'd enjoy, this may be a skip for you. But if you're open to genuinely unique experiences in games, I can't recommend Scorn enough. It's worth every penny full price despite its length. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: So to start off, I'm someone who's been following this game for years, and while I wasn't a backer, I still watched the development of this. Without going on and on, I do appreciate that the devs of this DID deliver what they advertised, even if it took a while, AND on top of that they were honest during delays and kept people up to date, at least compared to some devs I've seen. I know they offered refunds to backers at points too.Anyway, moving onto the actual game. I know prices are always subjective to a degree, what's worth $40 to me may not be worth it to you. Personally I'm not really missing my $40, and given all the time that went into this, and the obvious amount of effort that went into level and art direction I'd say it's fair. I understand the complaint however that it could have stood to be longer, but still I'd say there's far worse examples of price versus content out there. The actual game I found incredibly enjoyable. Generally it's slow paced, and has a lot of build up which I think works in it's favor. I also think it's strange that so many people are focusing on the combat being bad, and even saying they were misleading when it comes to showing how the combat works and how little of it their actually is. But from my perspective, I never saw this as something to expect outstanding gunplay or shooter action from. At first and foremost, it's a puzzle exploration game, and I get the game has combat so it's fair to criticize it, but personally I found the uses of it very interesting and I never had an issue with it in terms of doing what I needed to. The boss towards the end actually was pretty good, and I can understand why some would have wanted more of that if the game had been longer, I certainly wouldn't have minded more area's with bosses, but I did like how late into the game the boss came in, it made it all the more unnerving when I was all of a sudden like "wait, I have to fight this?!" There are parts that are very "walking simulator"-esque, however I think there's plenty of parts that are more open and give you a chance to either go in circles or really pay attention to where your going. Not to mention as someone who loves puzzle/point and click games, this has some of the coolest puzzles I've seen in a while, and I loved how intricate and interlocked they were with the areas. All in all my biggest complaint is I DID want more, and I'd love if they used these same assets to make a continuation with more lore added. I get that's part of the experience, is the mystery and I actually liked that you weren't told how to do everything, and instead had to adapt to the weird mechanics on your own. But I'd LOVE for this to not be the end of Scorn. I think there's tons of potential here for an elaboration on this world and why it got to this point. I'm not expecting tons of writing at every corner, but just something, ya know? Anyway, a very beautiful experience, and while it wasn't perfect and the road to completion was long and sort of rocky, I'm very glad to have played this and I really look forward to whatever the devs do next.

_childDocuments_.review: (as a start: I did not watch any marketing in the last 2 or more years, so I don't know if that was misleading or not.But I DID watch some non-edited gameplay that was posted in 2020 or so and THAT was very representative of what you get.)SCORN is a bodyhorror puzzle walking-simulator with a few combat sequences that borrow elements of oldschool survival horror. that is the easiest way I can describe it.let's break this down:· "bodyhorror" should be self-explainatory from the screenshots/videos above. on top of the visuals the events in the game are fittingly as disturbing as the visuals.· "puzzle walking-sim" is exactly that. a lot of walking in semi-open levels to solve puzzles that are not too easy and find keys/ways to progress into the next area.· "oldschool survival horror-elements” means that, when you have to face enemies, you should keep in mind your very spare resources. ammo and healing are really rare so  maybe you can hide or run past enemies instead of confronting them? you can't really move fast enough to dodge attacks and combat is cumbersome. imagine old resident evil pace of combat but first person. you are thrown into a really messed up h.r. giger-esque world and need to figure out what to do and where to go. pressing on is the only objective really. and to do that you need to solve some puzzles, find keys and in some parts fight or evade bizzare monstrosities. nothing is explained and you never know what will happen when you interact with something. the entire time you will be wondering what is happening, what it means, where you are going and why... so if confusion and exploration are not your thing in a video-game you won't enjoy this.The game is quite short depending on how you can deal with the puzzles and combat but it has such an amazing vibe that I can't help but recommend it.SCORN is slow; deliberately so, and it is rough. no doubt about it. it is not perfect.BUT it is rich in atmosphere, has amazing sound and visual design and if that is what you are looking for, then you won't be disappointed.my biggest gripe is how you can manouver yourself into really tricky situations without knowing it. this leaves you to choose between nearly impossible sections or having to restart a level. a simple saving system would help solve this issue but might take away from the tense stress of dealing with SCORNs world and inhabitants.if you are unsure: wait for a sale.PROs:+ amazing art design+ disturbing setting / experience+ great sound and (ambient) music+ dense atmosphere+ challenging puzzlesCONs:- short playtime - high pricetag for the length- bad checkpoints and missing save function- (deliberately) clunky combat

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn offers a unique experience that challenges expectations of what defines a great horror game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a combination of great tedium, sparse storytelling, non-existent explanation, but great visuals.A H.R. Giger fan will appreciate the scenery and atmosphere. But won't enjoy everything around it.1: Textures, animations, scenery. Just everything visual is amazing and top notch.2: Music and ambiance is great. It's dark, melancholic and alien.3: The oppressive atmosphere and mood of this game is also a plus.1: Combat.... It's just terrible. It's clunky, tedious and reaaallly wasn't needed. Without combat (I would prefer this). Or a lot more streamlined, it would be much better. But in its current state, it's just a deal breaker.Let me give you some examples:- Hits won't connect all the time. This results in missing your shot while you have them right in your visor. - The gunplay is way too slow. Every gun has a reload/charge time that's just too damn long.- There isn't a lot of space to dodge attacks most of the time because of the environment.2: The overall storytelling isn't good. There is no text in the game that tells you the story, nor it is there to explain certain things to you. Everything is "show don't tell", which can be a great tool to tell a story or explain certain things. But in this game. It is very lacking and nothing is explained to you at all with this.3: The puzzles are a mixed bag for me. They felt very otherworldly, which is a good thing. But since nothing is explained to you, they are also very annoying to do.4: Game is short. Very short. 5 hours tops and you have beaten the game...5: Replay value is also non-existent. Since there is only 1 or 2 very small things that can be done differently, and that's it. But from what i know, this won't affect anything in the game later on.6: The ending felt very anticlimactic and really didn't explain anything.The game is a beautiful disappointment. It looks and sounds amazing, but that is all. Not really worth full price. If you really want to try it out. Buy it at the sale when it's greatly discounted.PS: Even Darkseed 1 and 2 had better "H.R. Giger Darkworld" stories than this game. They where even told and explained a lot better than this game... That says a whole lot to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals of this game are insane and highly enjoyable. I've been excited for this game for about 2 years now and it's been in development for 8. The puzzles were very immersive and in depth and difficult. I found the puzzles very very enjoyable. The lack of tutorial or guidance was actually something I have very much enjoyed as it contributes heavily to the immersion and overall environment of the game. Any quest or task system would ruin the immersion so it was a nice touch to kind of be let to our own devices when it comes to solving the puzzles. The combat however, not so much. The combat needs a complete and total rework. I understand what they were going for, good horror games have difficult combat systems (Ex. Resident Evil). Scorn however just could not nail it on the head. Having enemies with ranged attacks while having a very close up melee weapon directly from the start was not a good move. It becomes very frustrating and monotonous to replay short sections of the game over and over again just to get passed one enemy interaction. The healing mechanic is actually pretty cool in my opinion my only problem with it is that it should be just a hair more forgiving. Again, I enjoy the difficulty as it adds to the immersion but I also feel like  ultimately between the poor combat mechanics and unforgiving health mechanics it makes just about any enemy interaction very frustrating. Ultimately I am enjoying the game so far I just truly believe it needs a bit more work and fine tuning.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eagerly awaiting Scorn ever since it first debuted on Steam Greenlight, but now that I played and finished it, I'm just sad and disappointed. Gorgeously disturbing art and atmosphere can only take a game so far when everything else about it is a janky underdeveloped mess.Years before release, Scorn's developers have been showing off the game's nifty combat system and importance of moral choices on the progression - all of that is gone now. The released game is a clunky linear puzzle game, where you can expect to play such bangers as:* A convoluted sliding tile puzzle.* Guide-a-light-through-a-maze puzzle.* Align asynchronous rotating disks puzzle.* And the all time classic - light up all the nodes puzzle!The fact Scorn wraps such trite exercises into its gorgeous Geiger/Beksiński art style feels utterly insulting.But then "combat" is introduced three chapters in, and it gets so much worse! Your fragile, lumbering, meat-man with slow, imprecise short range attack on a 10 second cool down is suddenly pitted against aggressive fast-projectile-lobbing damage-sponges. And so, you die, and die and die and die some more, each time sitting through a painfully slow death animation and a lengthy load time, then get respawned at the last checkpoint that may often be 15-20 minutes ago, forcing you to redo puzzles, or re-watch long unskippable cutscene animations. Health and ammo recharge stations don't regenerate, so if you used one up, then got mauled or missed a few shots shortly after, you might as well restart the chapter and lose hours of progress, as Scorn has no qualms about soft-locking progression and generally wasting player's time.I am not mentioning the game's story because there isn't one. You just move from one gorgeously grotesque setpiece to another without any real connection, until your meat-man is murdered in a convoluted, completely undeserved way, and the credits roll.Don't bother playing Scorn - it's clunky and boring, with a borderline broken checkpoint system, and no respect for player's time. If, like me, you were allured by the art of HR Geiger and Zdzisław Beksiński - watching a LongPlay on youtube will be a much better experience. Don't waste your money, especially at the current asking price of $40! Holy crap it's not even close to worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Tbh, the graphics is awesome, that was basically the main reason I bought this game on the first place, the atmosphere is stunning, but the gameplay is boring and takes hours just hanging around and clicking on every other obect, because you got to figure out what to do by yourself without any instructions. The game has some puzzles, and beside walking all around the map for several times looking for interactive objects, the puzzles themself are easy to solve. I would recommend this game only for people who mostly like visual part of the game and doesn't bother about the game's plot and enjoys figuring out everthig themself, but I'm personally not this type of people.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game... but it is a walking sim. There is some clunky combat that leaves a lot to be desired. The game is beautiful and intriguing. The puzzles are fun and sometimes infuriating. Sound is a little off - monster sounds don't always match up with where they are. I am using a 7.1 dolby surround headset - updated drivers, blah, blah. I am sure if I progressed further in to he game it might make more sense, but for now I am stuck wandering around and trying to solve the next puzzle.. which isn't all that interesting. I'd wait for it to drop in price.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: When I was an angsty teenager I had prints of Giger and Zdzslaw Beksinski on my walls. I listened to Lustmord's dark ambient soundscapes. Now as an adult I can play a game heavily inspired by Giger/Beksinski and features music by the dark master Lustmord himself. What an insanely fantastic idea huh? I followed this game closely because it resonated so much with the art teenage me enjoyed...The art is fantastic. 3d environments are wild, do yourself a favor and play this on a powerful PC, it simply looks amazing. It also plays like ♥♥♥♥. It is unfun. You get lost a lot because interior environments all look the same after a while, yes the game is trying to be disorienting, but it can be so disorienting it will tire you down and turn you off.When you first visit an area you feel a temporary sense of awe that quickly dissipates to boredom and frustration as you aimlessly wonder around. Enemies are not threatening or scary but cute, dorky and annoying. Animations cannot be skipped, so if you use a lever by mistake, be ready to waste tons of time using it against to undo whatever action you just did.Maybe hostile alien worlds should not be fun - a little voice whispers. Maybe this is an experience and not a "game" game. Yes, and in that case it should cost as much as a movie ticket, or a museum admission price - a loud angry voice would answer back. $40 is too expensive for a ticket to "an experience". I paid 5 euro to visit the legit Giger museum in Switzerland, why am I paying $40 to visit a fan's tribute to Giger through my computer screen? I would highly recommend this if it was $15 or maybe $20But I do think in the end the game would have been better as a guided artistic experience (with lower price and duration). This "strange" lackluster mix of survival/exploration/adventure/walking sim, feels like a dishonest attempt at padding so the game can boast a 5 hour campaign and avoid steam refunds for a short experience or something. In any case, I only hope the developers do not get defensive but learn from this and keep making strange artistic games in the future with improved gameplay and/or exploration mechanics
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The last chapter is the best.  Goriest and funnnest to play.  Wish the whole game was like the last chapter.  I dont really like the combat too much.  Does feel like an engine demo at time.  But the majority of the scene scape is non repatative.  Very non traditional.  But if you dont like old school games you likely wont make it to the last chapter.  You can save they guy in the early part of the game.  I get the feeling they wanted you to be able to make decisions that effect your long play. But That was cut due to having to get the game out and done.  It will leave you wanting more.  But its worth the ride. Just wish there was more.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a boring game period. Aesthetically good and that is pretty much the whole thing. The combat is one of the worst and most frustrating experiences i ever had in a game. Any review that mention instrospective, journey, exploration etc are not true. You walk, solve some basic puzzles the exploration has no meaning as there’s no story. There’s not one single line of dialog or anything to make the world interesting. Some will say is left to interpretation but I’d say is just lazy work for a game that was almost 8 years in development.  I get that people might want to justify the money they invested (this is not worth the money much less the full price) but people are just convicing themselves.  I was hyped for this one from the beginning but now I’m super glad i skipped it and got it through the humble bundle monthly choice. What a disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric masterpiece; Ebb Software has more than delivered in creating something with an unparalleled ambience. It is a game truly carried by its art direction: Every frame is a putrid painting, every sound discomposing, every animation stomach churning; these elements combine and compliment each other to deliver a grotesque world seldom seen in video games. You will find yourself stopping to look around many times during your playthrough not due to any difficult roadblock, but simply due to your own curiosity and awe of the environment's intricate detail which limitlessly envelops you.Ebb Software is a small team however, and although its clear that an incredible amount of effort went into the crafting the game's art and world, the same - unfortunately - cannot be said for its gameplay. The puzzles are painfully average, with nothing particularly to write home about regarding them. The combat is atrocious, with the main culprits being a severe lack of ammunition, and the game's God-awful melee weapon. Whenever you wish to conserve your ammo, using this thing is horrible: Not only does it have a hitbox which demands accuracy, but you can only use it twice before needing to recharge your stamina. This coupled with the fact that trying to use the weapon with insufficient stamina will freeze the stamina regeneration makes it feel incredibly stringent and frustrating to use.Scorn often feels like an interactive art piece more so than a game, and with its demands of the player for patience, discovery, and ability to theorise its mysteries, you certainly won't get the same experience watching a playthrough than you will actually playing it. Your personal enjoyment then will ultmately come down to both your own interest in the game's setting, and whether you feel this interest will carry itself through lackluster gameplay. For me, this answer was a resounding  but this certainly won't be the case for everyone.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "maybe" option for Scorn. I don't HATE the game, but I think it will disappoint some people going in blind. I am going with a SOFT yes to recommend it, but lemme explain a little. At time of writing, I am a little under halfway through the game to my understanding. I will probably update when I complete it. tl;dr, the good/fun parts are the atmosphere, world design, and puzzles. The not so good/fun part is the combat.I'll go over the good first. The atmosphere and world design here is incredible. I think I could best describe it as if HR Giger made a silent, less-grounded version the David Cronenberg film eXistenZ. It's alien, it's disgusting, and I love it. Everything looks wet. The buildings, tools, and weapons look like they're made from flesh and bone. The game throws you into a grotesque hell and leaves you for dead in it. It is absolutely the strongest trait this game has. The other really strong trait, perhaps as a result of this, is the puzzles. Most of my time in the game has been spent with puzzles so far. They aren't unfair, but due to the nature of the game's world, you have to stand back and really figure out what you're even looking at for the first few puzzles. It kinda adds this layer of feeling isolated and utterly lost in this world when you barely can figure out what certain pieces of architecture are at first.Now, the part I'm NOT a fan of: the combat. I have obtained 2 weapons so far. The first is basically a pile-bunker, a close range piston that slams into enemies bodies and in some situations, can instantly kill them. I sadly, cannot figure out how to reliably MAKE it instantly kill an enemy, and I'm becoming convinced it's just random. If you DON'T instantly kill them, it takes between 2-5 hits for most enemies I've encountered so far (usually more like 5). It also has a cooldown time of about 4 seconds after you "fire" it twice. Now, that isn't a HUGE problem right? Correct, if you're only fighting 1 enemy. You can generally jump behind a corner and come back to smack the enemy a couple more times, rinse and repeat if they give you some breathing room. The issue is, every enemy I've met has a ranged attack, and the range seems pretty far. You also don't dodge well which adds to the biggest issue of just taking damage with little or no way to skillfully avoid it in a lot of situations. The other problem is that you ONLY have that close range weapon for the first 2 and a half HOURS of the game. You don't get a gun at all until that deep in. Which is the second weapon I found. The gun is...okay. I really like the design of it, and it's much better then the pile bunker. The issue is, it has VERY limited ammo and the game starts throwing larger groups of enemies at you after you find it. I dunno what other weapons there are yet, but the combat is mostly boring or frustrating so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game despite terrible, terrible combat. This is a truly unique game that could have been a masterpiece just by removing the combat altogether. I almost gave up on it, but thankfully, didn't, as some of the things this game does stay with you for a very long time. There is nothing like Scorn, except the works by H.R. Giger. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start? The world and atmosphere are amazing, the game is graphically beautiful, the puzzles are fun, the combat is painful at best, the game is short, the save system is absolutely horrendous and i lost over an hour of progress by loading a previous save as auto-saves are not access-able. I enjoyed Scorn, but there's a lot that was promised, a lot that is lacking, and i just cant recommend it at this time.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best games I've played. As far as gameplay goes, it starts off as a walking simulator with light puzzle solving elements, then it morphs into a pretty desperate survival horror, the combat is supposed to be clunky, you just need to take your time with it, the best survival horror games need mechanics that fight back against the player in my opinion, and the combat in this game accomplishes that wonderfully.The aesthetics worship Beksinski and Giger with an escalating sense of body horror as the game goes on. You can spend hours in this game just taking in the environments and landscapes and details of the architecture and I implore everyone to play it like that to get the most out of it. That's not even to mention all of the disgusting machinery you can interact with. Some of it is straight out of Cronenberg's Crimes of the Future (2022).An unforgettable experience I'll be replaying soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a deeply atmospheric horror game that immerses you in a biomechanical world inspired by the works of H.R. Giger. The intricate, grotesque environments create an unsettling atmosphere.The game’s forces you to think about dread and curiosity, there are hard puzzles like in Act 3 and Act 4 where you might pull up a guide to figure it out. The game may not be for everyone as it's essentially a walking simulator with horror elements. If your looking for an unsettling experience with puzzle elements the game will take roughly 5-6h to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to review the deeper meaning and the story that can be explained by the environment because that's not what I experienced playing this game. The combat was awful. It's nearly impossible to dodge the attacks from enemies being in such narrow corridors all the time. There's no alluding to the idea that you can get past enemies without fighting them. However, I did like the puzzles. I feel like the game would've been more enjoyable for me if it focused more on being a puzzle game. If you're a creative and imaginative person who likes to think about things they don't understand I think you'll like this game. If you're looking for a more simple, blunt experience I don't think this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: No, hand holding. Greate Giger\Alien like aesthetics and great atmosphere. Decent adventure game. Was worth my time, but I think being a Giger fan has a huge impact on one liking this game or not. That said, this is not a FPS shooter ala Quake or something. This is a exploration game that also happens to have some combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people make dumb excuses to dislike this game. Either you like the art direction and are willing to pay for a 5 hour experience or you don't. That's up for you to decide. I personally got exactly what I was expecting from the trailers when playing. A short game with a little bit of puzzles and shooting, but it's main appeal is the gnarly environment. Not every game needs to be a several hour long experience with room for sequels and DLC and branching paths. This game is a simple and strong experience designed to be played once, if you want that then Scorn is for you. If you see the trailer and think "I don't get why people are interested" then that means you just don't get it and won't like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is an incredible experience that left we with those deep feels that you rarely get from a video game. It takes a while to get into because it throws you into an experience with no explanation about what to do or why. But stick with it - it is more than worth your time and money. The puzzles can be a little hard just because they make you think alot but are rewarding when you complete them. I found the combat to be not too bad - just approach it as if you really need to stay alive at all costs!Art, music, sound and atmosphere are top tier that any horror and biomechanical art fan will enjoy. I've never played a game like this before and you should try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but with the caveat that this game is not for everyone, and it's marred by some flaws that may ruin the experience even for those who are primed to love it. Who I think this game is for: If you like old-fashioned adventure games that are slow, don't explain anything, require you to solve puzzles to progress AND/OR you are a huge fan of H. R. Giger's art, this is the game for you. At least, that's who I am, and I liked this game overall. But even as the person this game was made for, there were things that almost ruined the experience for me (see below).If you don't like slow-paced "walking simulator" games or beating your head against the wall to solve some puzzles, or want a more survival-horror type of experience with jump-scares, you probably shouldn't play this game.As for the issues, they all really all stem from the combat. It's fine for there to be combat in a game like this, but with the way the check-pointing and health system works, it becomes needlessly frustrating. The enemies are pretty good at hurting you if you're not careful, your weapons are quite slow and awkward, and health/ammo recharge stations are scarce. On their own these would be fine, but some truly awful checkpoints makes deaths excessively punishing. On more than one occasion, I lost a lot of progress because a death reset me considerably further back than I would have expected from a modern game. The bad check-pointing and scarce resources causes the combat to get in the way of the adventure and puzzle solving. By far the most frustrating experience I had was when I really think this game is just a patch or two away from having these issues fixed. Throw in some better checkpoints, and make the DOT effects not kill the player. That's it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game in plenty of ways, the art was beautiful and also disgusting which is something I personally appreciated. The mechanics weren't too bad. The reason I stopped playing is the combat, or lack thereof. The options are: fight or run. I don't mind sometimes having to hide instead of fight but when it comes to the enemies that take the most ammo to kill (when you already get little ammo to start with), they are very difficult to run away from and don't disappear into a hole like the rest do. That just feels like a punishment and not like fun, I don't feel like continuing to do that. So, if you don't mind that? By all means, play the game. Maybe wait for a discount first though, just in case.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: No manual save system.  (It saved me at 2 hits left in front of a puzzle with an enemy next to me who shoots me immediately upon reloading)Combat feels painfully slow and clunky, it honestly shouldn't be in the game at all.  Only about 4 enemy types with one "boss" (you fight twice back to back) being extremely slow and boring.It's all just shock horror with its visuals.  Never attempts to actually scare you, just gross you out.Only about 4-5 hours but it feels like an eternity with how slow paced it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely isn't for everyone, but I enjoyed every minute of it. The atmosphere of lingering horror and biomechanical desolation the developers create here is unmatched. There's a few puzzles and a little combat (most of it can be avoided) but both those components feel like they fit well into the world created. Took me four hours to complete, so if you think it's too expensive for that amount of playtime I recommend waiting for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the deluxe edition and reading through the art book was more fun than actually playing the game.First off, the art direction of the game is incredible - if you're interested in Beksinski or H.R. Giger's art you'll be interested in the game. You won't however, actually enjoy anything to do with the gameplay. If you're one of those people who bought it for that reason, literally just watch someone play the game on youtube. The idea of Scorn is really fun - every bit of the gameplay in execution isn't. Even though the art is amazing, it doesn't carry the game - if you took the all the cool art away, there wouldn't be anything special to the game.There's some pretty basic puzzles and shooting (neither are fun, or good by any means). You'll see the same puzzle repeated multiple times throughout the game, and it wasn't even a particularly good or interesting puzzle in the first place. The gameplay itself is too tedious to recommend playing the game just for its art style and nothing else. Honestly, for what the game is, the idea the devs had would have worked better as a pure walking simulator without the shooting or puzzles.I like supporting the devs for making a game as unique as this, but the thing is, with how minimal gameplay is and how short the game is, I wouldn't say the game is worth paying more than $15.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big Alien fan and also a fan of FPS/Horror games as well. I saw footage for this game a year or so back and thought it looked cool. Heard it was out now and decided to pick it up. I had to request a refund after playing. My biggest problem with the game was the fact that I got an out of bounds glitch in Act 3 that pretty much made me fall thru the floor from the big middle platform and I lost like 2 hours of progress after loading the save. I had to reload because I was stuck and I got no death state. I had to redo all the puzzles again and just decided to quit and request a refund because that ruined the whole experience for me. It was already getting frustrating and tedious before that, but that killed my enjoyment. Other than that, I thought the game was interesting as an idea, but just not good in execution.The game looks great. I think that's its best aspect and that alone kept me engaged early on. I thought the atmosphere building with like the music and stuff was good too. Everything else I think was not that great I hate to say because I think the look of the game was so good and I really wanted this game to be good, but I did not enjoy it after a while. I was alright with the lack of handholding at first, but I got tired of not knowing where to go and the relevance of what my most recent action actually just did kind of after an hour. There were times where I did something and there was very little indication as to what it actually did, so I just wandered around trying to figure out what just happened. I thought some of the puzzles were cool, but I did not want to redo them after losing my progress either after a death or after the glitch happened. Just was frustrating. The combat was not great and it felt very difficult to avoid the projectiles/acid spit of the enemies, especially in tight corridors. If you can't go behind a wall fast enough, you will most likely just get hit. I also thought the first weapon was not fun to use at all. I unfortunately didn't get far enough past the 2nd weapon to see what else there was, but I didn't like the combat anyway. It was either you hit them or they hit you. They can hit you during your heal and also during your slow and very hard and weird to cancel reload animation. Not that engaging of combat. You can also just run past the enemies and you are probably fine if you can tank 1 hit. I feel like the game was kind of disappointing. I would definitely give it a second chance if it got something else added to it or some improvements were made, That glitch killed the experience for me completely. It would have been ok if I got one of the death checkpoints instead, but I didn't. The game definitely was great to look at though and a very interesting idea, but could have done many different things better.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: First-person walking with a lot of puzzling & some combat. The latter is seriously discouraged and you're often better off avoiding enemies all together. They serve more to set the mood, than to provide lots of gameplay which is what the puzzles are for. This weird-ass world this game takes place in follows logical rules & order, the puzzles revolve around controlling machinery. You get zilch in terms of tutorials, some basic skills of observation & deduction are enough.That has to count for something, as the presentation is the polar opposite. It's uncanny, it weirds you out and telling more would spoil the latter chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made for people looking to scratch an oldschool gaming itch. The art direction, sound design, and overall atmosphere are fantastic. This game is a labor of love and one of the few in the last 20 years I can remember to actually be worthy of being called a work of art. It is clearly an homage to H.R. Giger and the scifi movies he was involved with.The people tearing this game down probably have the attention span of a mayfly, degraded from constant dopamine overload. If you are not one of those people, I guarantee you will enjoy this game. The lack of handholding, the implied story forcing you to piece things together, and the unsettling feeling you get from the environment make this one of the best gaming experiences I've had since I was a child.Gets a solid 'A' from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Short game that's a lot of fun. It is a nice puzzle game that has great graphics. This game is a little confusing to play for the first time because you are unsure of what to do or where to go, but it only allows you to pretty much go in one direction the entire game. small sections that you run around in and solve the basic puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Alien movies or any of Giger's or similar works you will enjoy this too. It's not a fast paced shooter, or some RPG, it's a grotesque puzzle/exploration game with FPS elements that has you saying "WTF?" a few times throughout its playthrough. It's not holding your hand and it's also not giving you any direct explanation as to why things are the way they are.If this sounds off-putting to you then the game simply isn't meant for you.Otherwise, I am personally enjoying the art, sound and world design a lot. If you have an affinity for these things as well you should enjoy this beautifully grotesque work of art just as much.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game! Dunno how some people finished it in 5 hours or so - I took 9.5 hoursScorn is a game dripping in atmosphere. Stunning visuals - there isn't a game out there with this kind of art style. I took so many screenshots! The great sound design and ambient score really adds to the experience too.The environments are really cool and there are clues throughout the game which hint at what happened to the world of Scorn and its inhabitants. but enough mystery to keep you thinking. Combat is frustrating however, and sometimes atrociously bad - one of the worst I've experienced in memory. The puzzles can be quite tricky too, but not without their own logic. I'm an idiot and could figure them out without a guide. Despite its flaws, Scorn is still a game worth playing if you're into Giger/Beksinski/Alien/weird stuff. Don't expect a conventional horror game!Edit: the game is also really well optimised (i7 6700k, RTX 3070)
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Scorn. Its a slow burn with lots of mystery. If you love games that refuse to hold your hand, leave you plenty questions, beautiful body horror and with an awesome design, I cant recommend this enough. The combat may be simple. but it helps to make you feel like less than nothing, the weak link and under powered. Making victory over your disgusting combatants all that more relieving once they lay limp at your feet. I adore the design of this game. its truly disgusting and made me a little uncomfortable on more than one occasion, and i'm so happy to look back at this sadly short game and know that i wont forget the grossness i saw in there. So...Go ahead. Find your feet. And be reborn.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the somewhat jank gun-play and generally underdeveloped (as i would describe it) combat system,  what this game sets out to achieve I believe it accomplishes. From the stunning visuals to the fantastic atmosphere it creates, both things many people who were eager for the release of this title knew would be notable points of interest. Where I feel this game falls flat is in the lack of replayability and enjoyment in gameplay aside from solving the puzzles. It feels more like an artistic walkthrough more akin to an exhibition moreso than an interactive and immersive world, which would and very well could have worked if there was more embracing of exploration, aside from key required steps to progress through puzzles and the game, after replaying a number of times already I find that once you know your way there is no benefit to being a secret finder, no collectables, no upgrades that could reward you for being thorough and thus make combat easier later (given we had a more fleshed out combat system to begin with) generally no goals in playing other than to beat the game and also no incentive to really explore and gawp at the fantastically artful world the devs put most of their resources into building, in point it's very much so a one off playthrough where if you're not doing some sort of speedrun or arbitrary goal in replaying it, there's not all that much value. Now much is to be appreciated from a design perspective given things such as the strong notions of Heideggerian philosophy, or the beautifully dull desaturated reds and browns of this bio-mechanical world we find ourselves in, much of scorn is crafted to look hostile and unappealing in the most tasteful and intentional of ways and from a graphical standpoint it's perfect in my eyes, the way the world twists and wraps back into itself and the different designs throughout the acts is also highly worthy of praise. And the atmosphere accompanied by a strong soundtrack has me placing this game in a wierdly soft spot in my heart but The flaws are there. Were this game twice, maybe even triple the playtime, had a major revamp to the enemy design, gun/combat experience, filled in the baron areas with things like systems of reward for exploration (exploration being one of the key factors of enjoyment for me at least regarding this game) whether collectables or items, to little tidbits of lore or artworks within the game as a little "ah cool" moment and generally made gameplay and the actual experience of progressing through this world more captivating, i truly believe this would have far surpassed the hype that had been building for over 7 years. All in all i will recommend it as what it does right, it nails, and upon first playthrough it is a genuinely great experience, just somewhat of a letdown given mainly the playtime and lack of reason to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: You were dreaming. Your body lies in the dirt entwined with living tendrils that hold you tight and suck your life juices out of you. Then you wake up. It wasn't a dream!Scorn throws you into an unknown, strange world. The game gives you the privilege of exploring and experiencing a world like no other. There are no explanations. There are no dialogues. No one will take you by the hand to show you around. And that's exactly what makes the game so unique.There are many games that take the player into strange worlds. But unlike Scorn, after a while players realize where they are, what is required of them and what they have to do. Scorn throws you into a world so strange and alien that you won't know where you are, what's required of you, or how to escape this nightmare. All you know is that you have to leave the area you are in. This world is hostile. This world is dangerous and you want to live. So you have to get out of here.Every level is different, looks different, and challenges you with new tasks. The game never gets boring and keeps surprising you with completely unexpected events until the very end. This is euphoric. Again and again, you stare at your monitor in fascination while you think to yourself, 'This can't be true!'. It's absolutely intoxicating.Beside occasional combat with amazing creatures, Scorn's gameplay is mainly puzzles. Sometimes you have to solve puzzles directly on a wall or in a mechanism, but often the whole map is a puzzle on which you have to activate machines, move levers and find upgrades to open doors or move gates. All puzzles are challenging, but at the same time cleverly designed so that you can always solve them. Since all maps are large labyrinths, you often run back and forth trying to solve everything, and occasionally you might feel lost. I was a little frustrated, once in level 4 because I wasn't able to find the last of three mechanisms. But then eventually I found the last one. Scorn is an achievement friendly game. Except for the first two achievements, you will collect all of them automatically. As for the first two, you can only collect one of them during a single game. Therefore, after finishing the game once, you just need to replay the first 15 minutes to collect the missing achievement.Scorn has received overall positive reviews, but some players are annoyed by the fact that the game costs 40 $/Euros but only offers 7 hours play time. I doubt you can complete the game in 7 hours without instructions. It took me 11 hours without guide. Nevertheless, I can understand the criticism. At the same time, Scorn is a very special game, and I can imagine how much work it took the developers to create it. Wait for a sale. Personally, I think $20 is a reasonable price.If there were Oscars for games, Scorn would collect many of them. In my opinion this game is a masterpiece. It’s a work of art. Scorn is like visiting a gallery of absurdities, where you can't help but be amazed. It's scary and brutal, and there's a lot of blood in this game. Scorn is simultaneously cruel and incredibly fascinating. I only played the game at night with headphones because I wanted to enjoy every moment, and I succeeded. I love Scorn. It's a great game! I strongly doubt I will play anything better this year. - breathtaking world- brilliant atmosphere- beautiful graphics- fantastic soundtrack- fantastic sound effects- very innovative - unique (there is nothing like it)- smart- exciting fights- mysterious- surprising - very brutal - if the map is the puzzle it can get a little frustrating
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: WowThis experience was fantastic. One of the coolest art directions I've seen in a game. The slow paced movement and combat fit the aesthetic perfectly. The mystery of the whole thing captivated me and the visuals pulled me right in for one of the greatest short story video game experiences I've ever had. This game is a masterpiece of an artwork.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This IS a walking simulator, but it's one that I thoroughly enjoyed. There's nothing wrong with a game being a walking simulator as long as you are enjoying the walk. That's the key. But this is a world that I understand if many wouldn't enjoy walking around in it. If a dull grey color palette turns you right off, then stay away. Me personally, I thought it was morbidly gorgeous, but then again, I have an H.R. Giger Necronimicon art book sitting on my coffee table. As far as the gameplay goes, the puzzles were nice and challenging, and the combat was fine. Those that complain about the combat don't understand that this was never designed to be a twitch action game. Your weapons are there for you IF YOU HAVE NO OTHER CHOICE. Use them if you're cornered, but your character is not a walking harbinger of death. This isn't Doom. Go slow and avoid confrontation if you can.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I unfortunately cannot recommend this. The artwork is 10/10. The depth of the story and gameplay is possibly some of the most shallow I've ever seen- 3/10. I really wanted to like this game, but it really is just void of playability. -There's no choices that have any impact on the story. -I am convinced that the developers were close to running out of money and cut a bunch of content in order to release it.-It's just a large puzzle game and is so linear that it takes most of the enjoyment out of it. Most Call of Duty games have more depth in gameplay than Scorn (I wish I was joking). Literally all you do is this: move to new area, solve puzzle to get to next area. Repeat for the entire game.-The combat is an afterthought. It's clunky and not intuitive.The artwork is fantastic. But I was hoping for more depth to the storytelling than what we got. The atmosphere is carried solely by the art, but the shallowness of gameplay pulls you out of the atmosphere and you're constantly reminded that you're playing a game. In my experience, if you're playing a great game, you're not thinking about it, you're just immersed in it- same as watching a great movie. Unfortunately, Scorn falls way short of this. It's just not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: If the game intends the player to avoid all the smaller enemies then why have the enemies at all?  And why give us FOUR weapons to fight them? While giving us ZERO methods to avoid them other than backing up? Needing to sprint through the mesmerizing scenery was the opposite of what I wanted to do which is soak in the gorgeous design and atmosphere. The inconsistent hit-detection and environment collision detection made combat simply frustrating. It forces a player to cheese their way through it by kiting enemies in circles or spending minutes waiting for enemies to leave. Completely ruined the whole game for me really.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric, dark, and wet.It's a pretty good first person puzzle game, like Myst but filtered through a body horror lens. No idea why so many people expected it to be an action game, because it isn't, failure of marketing perhaps?Overall the art direction and sound design elevate this game a lot for me, it feels very immersive and disgusting and if you think you might enjoy something slower paced inspired by dark surrealism, give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a disturbing but amazing experience, I have never played something so disgusting and I loved it.But alas, the game has its flaws...The main problem I had is the combat which is really unnecessarily hard for what essentially is an interactive art gallery. I recommend skipping most encounters if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for people who really like first person puzzles. This game is full of pretty gore fleshy atmosphere, It is very beautiful with its design and graphics really similar to Beksinski's style, who is the game's inspiration, It's so nice to see it! _childDocuments_.review: Basically a Walking Simulator. Sure, you get some weapons but shooting feels quite bad so I just walked past enemies unless defeating them was necessary. Looks decent, but hoped for more since I only bought it to get some usage of my graphic card (Game runs great btw). _childDocuments_.review: The world building, art and general level design for this game are at the triple A game level. Yet I felt that when I was finally sinking my teeth into the game it suddenly ended. I understand that to get this level of 3D rendering, sound design and polish requires a vast amount of time (especially since you notice a lack of reused assets compared to other games) but to pay $40 for an experience averaging 5 hours is just not worth it for me. I would have gladly played $60 if it doubled the playtime. Looking at the video footage shown in the steam store, it seems quite a bit of the level design was revamped. Maybe this is where they lost some time. Quite frankly I'm just sad that such a unique experience ended so early. I would have liked to explore the world of Scorn for longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: ORIGINALLY FINISHED THROUGH GAMEPASS AFTER ABOUT 5 HOURS, GIVE OR TAKE.Overall I'd say this is slightly leaning towards a neutral rather than a flat no, but your mileage may vary.Visually, easily in my top 10 of all time. Right up there with the likes of Metro Exodus Enhanced and both Ori games. I cannot praise the visual design and atmosphere enough.The small amount of combat here actually hurts the game and should have just been removed. Enemies can hit you through objects and walls sometimes, the first weapon takes a stupid amount of time to "reload" whilst having a bar thats not very intuitive to look at and even goes away when the weapon isn't held out (which shouldn't be happening when relying on the timing of the "reload"). You're also quite slow and its easy to get stuck on enemies and other objects when trying to run away from their ability to hit you almost every time.With the puzzles I'm mostly neutral. I didn't find the few of them difficult personally and the game is mostly just going to a room to pick up the item needed for the room you were in before which leads you into a room you were in before but from another side now and then opening a door or taking an elevator to the next area to repeat. There's nothing "non-linear" about this game at all.Storywise I was ok with pondering my own interpretations of the themes and metaphors but was aware of the fact the world felt quite empty, but then I learned there is actually a whole narrative and even events that have happened before we arrive that are simply left out of the game. The artbook that comes with the deluxe edition talks about pretty significant events I won't spoil and talks about cut levels that likely would have contained a lot of clues for us to use as building blocks as to what this world is and what happened. Unfortunately the game is so lacking in environmental storytelling that almost nothing of substance is ever communicated to the player. There's just some vague imagery to look at and wonder about to yourself. It makes the overall package feel incomplete.Honestly, I think this game could have been so much more enjoyable if the combat was removed (maybe a chase-like sequence or 2 could have provided a more memorable encounter with these enemies?), the puzzles were more puzzle like (we get a couple but as I said, for the most part its just wondering around and picking up items to open the next door) and if exploration was more of a focus. Let me get lost in completely random rooms that tell their own story or let me explore vast landscapes that hint at a long lost civilisation or something. As it stands the game is just so linear and devoid of the things that make the vague storytelling of the Souls games so great. I really really want the devs to make more with this world though. There is so much potential and I would love to see something in the realm of a sequel or DLC that listens to the common criticisms people have. With this game finally out I imagine there's scope to reuse assets or maybe unused content which could greatly speed up development time. Kudos to the team for finally getting this one out the door after so many years of development and funding issues. I'm excited to see what else they do.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: What a weird thing. The art is fantastic. The sound works wonderfully. Everything else falls flat.I hadn't heard of scorn before it's launch, so I didn't have any previous expectations going in. I saw like 2 minutes of video showcasing the visual style and immediately stopped watching to avoid any spoilers when I realized I wanted to actually play the thing myself. So what I did know going in is that Scorn was a puzzle game with some slow combat. Something like Myst in H.R. Giger-land with some guns for flavor. Scorn is like 1/4 of one of those things. It nails visual and audio presentation. It looks and feels like taking a tour through a Giger landscape. There's the good. Now the bad-ish. It has too few puzzles to be a full on puzzle game. Most of the "puzzling" is which way did I want this elevator to go. There are a few "proper" puzzles, but if you went in expecting something in the vein of an old school puzzle/adventure game, then you'd be disappointed with the number and complexity.  Then it has too little combat to be a full on shooter. You don't see your first enemy until about halfway through if you're moseying through to see the sights. And oh boy is combat clunky. Not because it's slow. Which it is and isn't. It almost made it. The few weapons are melee, revolver equivalent, shotgun equivalent, and grenade launcher. Grenade launcher sounds great, but you only get it at the end and use it to solve "puzzles". Shoot grenade to break the chain to open the door. Like 3 times. Melee has 2 charges and recharges extremely slow. Actually everything does. Which wouldn't be a problem, but they don't feel powerful enough to justify it. If you give me 3 enemies at once, which is a lot for Scorn. And I have to use 4 out of 6 shots to kill 1 of the enemies and then switch to Melee. But melee takes 4 hits to kill the doggos and only has a charge of 2. So you have to dance around dodging acid spits while it recharges, which wouldn't be a problem, BUT you move at like 3/4 of the speed required to dodge. The range on the doggo spit is longer than the visual, so you'll think you're safe, then lose 3 bars of health. The little spitters basically have auto-aim unless you get around a corner, which isn't always available, and chargers Exist.The point being that it feels bad to never finish a fight better off than you started it. I didn't get through a combat encounter once in the entire game without losing a way bigger chunk of health than was comfortable. And the nearest health station for more ampules, might be 30 minutes away. And maybe I'm just bad at it, but then I couldn't avoid it.Whoever said you could avoid combat was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ liar. Here's how enemy AI worked for me. If I get close enough to the spawn point to trigger aggression, they'll follow me a set distance. If I go backwards out of that distance the way I came in, they'll despawn and the cycle repeats when I get close to the trigger again. If I go forwards I die because there's a door in the way and you can't dodge for ♥♥♥♥. Coupled with things just getting spawned behind you half the time for the lolz. I'm looking directly at that hallway that spawns bulls in-front of AND behind-you at the same time, but only AFTER you go down the hallway, which is a dead end to get the health refill down there. Actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.So no matter which side of gameplay you enjoy more, there's not enough substance and too much funk and the two sides DO NOT mesh well together. Scorn would have been a better game if it was all puzzler. It also would have been a better game if it was all shooter with tighter mechanics and better level design for that type of gameplay. It also would have been a better game if they just cut all gameplay elements besides walking through the fantastic landscape their art team made. Nobody wins here.Which funny enough is the moral of the game. Which I think is some Grade-A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The first character doesn't win, so he decides to make sure the second character doesn't win so we all have to go down in this dying hell-scape together. Spend half the game fighting with this parasite, finally get rid of it at the end and then he just swoops back in deus-ex-machina style at the very last second. You get a "♥♥♥♥ you, nobody wins, doesn't that suck" 30 second cutscene and then get kicked back to the menu. It honestly feels unfinished. Like they switched it up and cut so many things over the course of development and whoever had control at the end just made up this cop-out ending at the last minute. With more development and expanding on the theme, it could have worked. But it didn't and I finished the game just kind of disappointed with every aspect except for the parts where I got to just walk around looking at the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The one and probably only reason to recommend this game is the visuals. Anybody into Giger, Beksinski and overall biopunk nightmarish visuals is going to have a blast here. Beyond that, there's not much positive left to say. The puzzles, which are the main mechanic of the game, are just interesting enough to keep the gameplay afloat. But the gun play is where it gets simply insufferable. You'll find yourself idiotically playing ring around the rosie with enemies, to compensate for stealth mechanics that there was apparently no time to implement. Match that with the unforgiving checkpoint system and you've got a match made in hell.TLDR: must have for Alien / Giger fans. Puzzle enthusiasts, consider it. For anybody else, there are probably much better ways to spend their money.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn.A game that I've been waiting and waiting to play for over 6 years. Having come out only last Friday, I've already gotten a handful of play throughs with it.I'll start with how to approach the game. Without spoilers, I'm asking,  that you approach this with the same or similar respect to a foreign painting in an art museum. It's an interactive art piece, allowing one to take a glimpse into a world struggling to take its final breaths.This game was a labor of love, and it's seen in its environments, it's creature design, it's character design, and it's interactable design. It's a game that you'll never experience anywhere else in the market.And what an experience it is.Its isolated wasteland, it's empty halls, the lack of anything else that you can make a connection to, it's a game that really sells and forces you to settle in on pure, utter loneliness. You become lost in its twisting corridors, holding your breath as you meet creatures you could only see in nightmares, half-remembers when you wake, relieved when they're gone.It's a game that's thought-provoking, its designs eye-catching, tickling parts of your brain that you most likely haven't felt in such a way before. It brings the best of H.R. Giger's best works to life, embracing it, and distancing itself far enough away to be a unique, standalone experience. Open your mind, look around you, and appreciate the work and struggle that has gone into bringing this game to life. Bringing this  to life. It's an eclectic nightmare, but one that should be remembered.I highly recommend purchasing the Delux Edition, as not only does it come with the game, but comes with it the art book. The art book is a treat, and I highly recommend reading through the entire thing once you've finished your first play through of the game, as it gives much-needed insight into the world, and lets you know what kind of work was put into it.Play it for yourself, and please, treat it like an interactive art piece.That's all I ask of you.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you have been following this project for years. Try not to listen to the buzz. It's more Beksiński than Giger, most of the time. It's you, alone, discovering mysterious mechanisms and trying to figure out how they work and what they do. Abandon your expectations and wander into this game like a child. Open your mind to the experience. It wants you to be utterly lost, without context nor the language to express what you're seeing.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE SCORN which is more like a crazy art exhibition than a video game, even it got me frustrated sometimes after I try desperately to finish so many annoying tasks in a bleeding health limited condition but end up dead then have to start from the last check point saved 2 hours ago (it really kills the mood) I still love this game.No doubt, the concept's good, the art's good, but I have a unsatisfied feeling like the game should have show more but not bold enough to do it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Although Scorn might have the best visuals I've seen in any video game, the gameplay, puzzles, combat and its mechanics are just not fun at all. On top of that, no ability to manual save? Like c'mon, we'll got real life stuff to do. Most of us can't sit through long sessions when there no real indication on where the checkpoints are. I lost maybe an hour or so or progress, just because of that. I must say though, the game nails the atmospheric horror setting perfectly. It just looks insanely good. It's dark, eerie, unsettling, and surreal. That's pretty much the only thing I loved about the game. Overall, it's pretty disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this thoroughly.  The grotesque atmosphere is a lot of fun to explore, wondering how everything came to be and the purpose of everything around you.  I haven't had many experiences like this, but it does a very good job of leaving you with a lot of wonder about the atmosphere and what's happening throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and checkpoints are frustrating sometimes but if you can put those aside, the game becomes really interesting. Scorn is about strangeness, goriness, depression, loneliness, hopelessness and it doesn't tell you ♥♥♥♥ so the story is driven by your macabre imagination. Even if it's not perfect, you can still see the passion from the team and nothing compares to it. Still a must play for any horror fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game is intensely frustrating and ruins what otherwise would be a decent game. There are also no catch up points in the game, so if you wasted any resources early on you can very very easily soft lock your save. The only option at that point is to restart the entire game and do better. Redoing anything in the game is doubly frustrating due to the painfully long animations as your character interacts with consoles, which would normally add to the cinematic experience, but not so much when you're retreading your steps with 1 HP.Don't waste your time and money, this is one you can probably watch on YouTube.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Went from loving exploring every room, enjoying the soundtracks ambiance, really digging the creativity of puzzle connection to the environments, and just enjoying how the spaces linked together... then combat was introduced. Your intro to it is how the weapon and enemy hitboxes never seem to sync with where you'd expect it hit and has a very long reload period; therefore, once you realize how sparse healing stations are, you'll already be perpetually at the one-hit-and-you're-dead health level for the rest of the game. When killed you don't regain your health but return to the single remaining hitpoint you had when the last checkpoint occurred again and again as you keep dying to the same autotargetting enemy slime or the forced damage cutscenes that keep happening from your parasite. Once you finally get a gun, you think phew i can finally clear some enemies out and enjoy the world again, until you realize how limited the ammo is and how long the animations are to use it.Punch an enemy, run around the corner before it spits at you, wait for it to walk up, punch it around the corner, and then repeat is the strategy if you don't just run past every enemy ignoring combat and the views entirely. Looping them around a control box breaking their line of sight so they can't attack you has been my current way to just get through it.I hope to maybe finish this game, but the combat has changed my love for the playing the game into a tedious chore to see what big set piece is next.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of reviews complaining about how short the game was for such a myst-like puzzle game like this is just ridiculous.No need to speedrun, if you finish, you're pretty much done with the game unless they release expansions.The game is good. If you like games like Myst or just like to enjoy relaxing puzzles, bit of stealth and appreciate the great homage to H.R. Giger, it's pretty solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to others, but certainly not to everyone. If you're looking for a good shooter game, look elsewhere.If you're looking for a game where your choices matter, look elsewhere.But if you're looking for one of the most immersive, hauntingly beautiful biomechanical experiences ever, you're in the right place. The ambience, the enviroment and the sound design fully sucks you in and you're very easily transported to this nightmarish world of flesh and machinery. It grips you and doesn't let go. It's intriguing to the point of being sickening, my only complaint is that unless you have read the artbook you have no idea where you are or what's going on.This is a very linear storytelling of what I can only describe as a journey through hell.The sheer amount of loneliness, alienation and disgust I've felt whilst playing this game is something else.There were moments I just wanted to curl up into a fetal position, no doubt what the protagonist feels like during the entire journey too as well.I'm not big on puzzles myself,  but they seem quite intuitive most of the time (I am jusa very impatient smoothbrain and needed a guide for almost all of them).TLDR: If you're looking for a hauntingly beautiful, disgusting and riveting experience that will make you feel appaled by everything you see, hear and feel, this is the game for you. My only complaint is that it's a bit short for the price it usually has on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to say it! and damn it im going to say it loud! SCORN IS A GOOD GAME!!!Game-play? not many ground breaking mechanics.  7/10Shooting? Forget it!  1/10Puzzles? A little easy sometimes, but keeps you on your toes! 8/10Horror? God yes! the horror is a great mix with a lot of the downtime and mystery. 10/10Scorn is amazing visually, so much to see and soak in. Its more immersive than cyberpunk and it feels older than earth itself. Its an amazing experience if you like Alien, or lovecraft, or your just a nerd about grim bio mechanics like me, this is a game for you!Overall:8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short game, but dense with detail and with a gory mystique that adds to its unmatched atmosphere.  I'll keep my own beliefs out of it, but there is some really deep symbology here.  Stuff about human nature, the pain of life, and the attempts at something more.  The game is a survival-horror shooter with heavy puzzle elements.  There's not a lot of shooting and your guns are slow and take time to aim.  The emphasis is on your fragility.  If you can just relax and enjoy a game for its atmosphere and art, then this is for you.  It's like a visual feast.

_childDocuments_.review: *barely recommended*Often visually striking,  Scorn's biomechanical look would do H. R. Giger proud.  However, this surreal look can grow to feel a little samey at times and the detailed geometry can often camouflage the few interactive objects in the game.Plodding and sometimes dull, Scorn doesn't offer anything in the way of tension and is only superficially horrifying to those squeamish to gore.  Initially the game offers no combat and the level design is weaker than later in the game, making me wonder how many gave up on it before it really starts to get going.Not that my 7+ hours with Scorn ever left second gear.  The slow pace and surprisingly unemotional combat feels almost like a grind.  It was the visuals that kept me going, along with the bizarre story that Scorn barely hints at.  Thankfully, the game ends better than it starts, but since it starts fairly rough…that's hardly high praise.I think horror fans would get something from this game, at least from the visual thrills and squishy environments.  It is relatively easy and the puzzles never stumped this action gamer.  You aren't playing Scorn for riveting gameplay, but the visuals and short runtime make it a memorable experience at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia, Stanley Parable, Portal, Soma, The Talos Principle and many other games which are not your daily mainstream games but have the special power to carry you into another world and make you think about yourself and how you perceive your environment. It's not even about the art alone, rather about creating a dense atmosphere and to take you on a journey.Scorn combines the riddles from Talos Principle with the horror and art of some parts of Alien Isolation (Apollo Core design) and Soma, heavily influenced by H.R Giger and Zdzisław Beksiński and takes you into a world of horror, beauty and the question which defines humanity since the dawn of men,"Who Are We And Where Are We Going?You are given no hints whatsoever and your only job is to observe your environment and become a part of it.This is no shooter, no adventure game, not necessarily a puzzle-game and not even really a horror game, its a "art-game".It was never about the horror itself, more the world, the lore, the story. the atmosphere and all the questions which still havent been entirely answered.And this is what defines this beautiful masterpiece. Your own interpretation matters.The graphics looks so crunchy on 1440p and 4K, so real and rubenesque, I want to touch it. I want to be a part of it and smell the metallic and bloody odor, the rotten and dying organic scent.This is where you just turn off the lights, put on your headphones and dive into another world.13 hours in and no end in sight. I want the full experience. It want it all.To the folks who hate this game, you are entitled to your opinion but you might have been misled by the hype. Sh*t happens but its time to move on. Still, no reason to downvote this game.To the folks who enjoyed and who are still enjoying this game, I salute you and I hope, we'll get some DLCs soon.Thanks @devs for this special treat. Bought this game on GOG but I bought it again on Steam for cheevos and the art book.Now if you excuse me, gotta dive back.Enjoy yourselves.
