_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game for visuals and soundtrack alone, the game looks and feels AMAZING. And when something interesting is happening the game is very enjoyable.The problem is, for the first couple of hours you will be walking around massive beautiful environments looking around in awe. But there is nothing, anywhere. No items, no secrets, no hazards. Puzzles are not very clever and they are very few of them with lots of nothing between. After you find weapons the game picks up and actually starts to feel like something that was shown in old trailers. Weapons are satisfying, resource management is simple but it's there and adds extra tension, enemies are grotesque and disgusting and it feels good to fight them. Combat really offers a nice filler between puzzles and exploration now has a purpose because you can actually find health and ammo around.Because of troubled development the game is basically nothing like what developers have originally planned and it's painfully obvious that these massive environments were a part of something else and they were cut down and slapped together just to have some levels to go through. It's most obvious in the final act which is EXTREMELY disappointing because it again goes back to the same gameplay from the start of the game and all your resources you've collected prior are wasted, because there is nothing to do apart from A SINGLE PUZZLE that takes up the entire final act. The ending is sad and poetic but can't save the game for me overall. What a waste of fantastic visuals and concepts. I recommend the game overall just to support the devs, god knows they need it, but take it with the grain of salt, definitely not the game for everyone.

Giger ruined by some poor game design decisions.I was aware of the controversy around this game so I went in expecting a 'walking simulator', a living 3D art museum. The FPS got so bad in the boss fight that I stopped playing and figured out that I needed to run it in windowed mode on 2nd monitor or fullscreen on the first monitor.I would love the devs to create some DLC or a sequel, as long as they can innovate and not dress up a dull game in alien goo.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a weird game, while I enjoyed the rollercoaster for what it was, I struggle to say Yes, you should play this. The answer rather is "No, unless"Scorn as a game involves two main segments, a slow paced trek through a Gigerian Nightmare, solving puzzles and wondering if the sculpture on the wall is supposed to represent the fear of intercourse or the damaging effect of growing up and realizing your parents really did have sex. The art itself is very nice to look at but just a lot all around, the middle portion of the game particular being where you'll find yourself cross-eyed and forgetting whether the path with the phallic tendril going into the egg was the way you came from or the way you're supposed to go. The puzzles are alright, they're never too much of a head scratcher, and if you're struggling with one you just have to remember you only have to do it two more times. Every puzzle in this game adheres to the rule of 3's. Every. Single. One. Some areas have you spending minutes upon minutes walking back and forth up and down halls to repeat what you've done once and twice now.The second segment of gameplay is combat, to make it short, the combat is not good. There are 3 Schlongs in this world, that you'll fight over and over. They'll despawn or stop attacking if you walk past certain thresholds in the map. The weapons never seem to have enough ammo, which results in encounters approaching tedium as your pistol runs out of spunk and there's always one more Weiner that you'll have to duke it out with the Melee Penetrator that comes with 2 hits and takes 5 seconds to use again after, and no, you cannot use the Penetrator 3 times if you take a week break between goes. There's a healing system that's just flat out not shown to you unless you open up the settings and look at the controls. There's an Organ constantly rearranging your insides that burns one of said heals every time he digs a little deeper. The saving grace of the combat is that it ends, jokes aside, you're only fighting off Todgers for a short 1 and half period of a 4-6 hour game.  Leave it to the Bollocks. Dong.In short, if you can get past the mediocre gameplay and enjoy the art design for what it is, yes buy it but for most people there are 100 games that may not look as good. But you'll feel better after playing.

_childDocuments_.review: The Puzzles:Not sure why people giving negative reviews for the lack of tutorials or guidance through the puzzles. That's kind of the point of the game. Waking up with no idea what we are, where we are or how anything works. Learning only through visual & audio cues and trial & error like a baby would. The Combat:The devs put out an intentional hint in the latest narrated trailer saying "The creatures in this world want nothing more then to be left alone." If you don't approach every encounter like an FPS and monitor enemy walk cycles, they eventually crawl into drain pipes or up walls. I played the game more evasively and I only died twice in the final boss because of negligence. The guns are slow, require lining up shots and pack a mean punch by design, because they're meant to be used defensively. The piston gun is only meant for staggering enemies and opening doors. It saved me so many times when the battle was 2v1 which is inevitable death.The World:One of the most visually and audibly outstanding games I've ever played. I don't think anyone can disagree that the world they've built is a true work of art. Which also baffles me why there are complaints that the game isn't a big open world graphic adventure in the vain of Myst. If you're expecting this level of hand crafted detail in a game of that size, then you have incredibly unrealistic expectations and should probably wait another 5-10+ years of development from a small team. Conclusion:The game is a beautiful nightmare. It takes a different approach to conventional game mechanics and in my opinion succeeds at providing a unique experience. As with anything that's striving to be different, there will be negative feedback from people expecting it to fit the mold of other more popular games but I highly recommend giving this one a try and experiencing it for yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it at this price point, for most people.   If you are an absolute enthusiast for the biomechanical style of H.R. GIger and you don't mind a $40 entry ticket for an art experience, go for it.  The art style of HR Gigier is slavishly copied, almost beyond the point of parody.  HR GIger was an industrial artist prior to his career in the movies, and Ebb Software seems to have lost that thread of his work completely.   All of it is gross, sexy, oozing and sucking... but a lot of it looks non-functional.   Consider the parasite you meet a few hours in:  would that naturally evolve in any environment?   For my taste, the puzzles and chemicals are too simple and not novel.   So the 'gameplay' elements of this 'game' were very under cooked, and definitely not worth my time or money.The entire 'game' is available on YouTube in multiple formats:  You will get the same experience that the game strives to deliver, for free.  At the $10 point, this would have been a fascinating experiment.   At $40, it's almost an insult.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly want to love this game, and in a lot of ways, I do love it. The "game" (and I use this term lightly) captures a 1st person tour of an alien biomechanical body horror heavily inspired by Giger (although I'm more than certain he would frown at some of the more bloody parts), and there are several hauntingly beautiful scenes that you slowly absorb what good art direction can do. It's clearly a labor of love from someone who worships the altar and I am right there with them.Unfortunately, it feels like SCORN sat in the oven for too long. There's a few fixed view puzzles (an annoying slider puzzle, a "rotate the angles until everything is aligned right",  a "push the ball through the maze" puzzle, and a few other puzzles that would make even the worst Playstation-era survival horror game feel embarrassed to exist). They only happen to prevent whatever you would call the plot from moving forward, or you continuing your rather linear voyage forward, and it really takes me out of the game's alien vibe. There's a few poorly done combat encounters most can be avoided by running by, one of which you have to do twice over towards the end and it had me saying "That's it?" The game would be honestly better off keeping the alien mystery going and completely removing any combat.Finally, as you start getting into the last act, the level design starts to show some seams as devices and level gates are the only thing to keep you going forward without thought as to how to integrate them better than the vague plot. "Oh you have to run through the door after hurting your arm, good thing there's lots of those arm hurting things right there. Oh we have to do another weight puzzle again." It really took me out of the gameplay.It's hard to give something that has obviously had so much love poured into it, and something that I aesthetically enjoy a non-recommendation. If there's like a new game+ where there's zero combat and no bad fixed view puzzles, I'd give it a 4/5. As it sits now, to have someone who isn't already a Giger-head, or at least a light appreciator of the crazy swiss surrealist, they will more than likely get quickly bored.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most dichotomous opinions of a game I've had in a really long time.As a *video game*, this is astoundingly cruddy. Inherently sluggish/frustrating combat even by survival horror standards is compounded in seemingly every way the developers tried to imagine - often not enough room to strafe to dodge projectiles, supremely annoying checkpointing, missable weapons before points of no return that the game later expects you to have (yes, I had to reload from an earlier chapter), no manual saving, a couple of instances of bugged enemy behavior that necessitate particularly tedious stealth/chase sequences, not even any degree of enemy variety to look at, and one pair of back-to-back fights against two identical elites one after the other, after which you're very possibly drained of health refills and then are required to repeatedly damage yourself in order to finish the next sequence.The worst part of all of it is that this is such a masterwork of visual design and atmosphere and mood, such a singular piece of interactive art, that it had no need whatsoever of any video game DNA, let alone any so poorly shoveled in as to undignifiedly regurgitate all over itself and nearly spoil the entire experience.If you have a strong appetite for artwork even attempting to approach the likes of Giger or Beksinski, you unfortunately still owe it to yourself to walk the halls and see the sights of Scorn. The long development time shines in every facet of its presentation, and I can just about guarantee you've never seen a game like it, never found yourself surrounded by this particular brand of mesmerizing hellscape. If, however, that in itself does not *acutely* excite you and you still expect to enjoy Scorn as a *video game* in order to feel your money was justifiably spent, I can confidently say you can pass on it.If you are still onboard, I offer just a few pointers in hopes that it will mitigate/eliminate for you the undue misery that in no small part made up my experience:- The two most common enemy types are introduced one right after the other. These two types will almost always slink away into some hole avoiding combat altogether if you keep your distance and avoid them for a moment or two.- Keep your eye out for weird interfaces on walls. Be sure that you have looked around every room in the general area before moving forward. Don't miss weapons.- Make sure weapons are reloaded before using ammo stations.- In actuality the 'hurt yourself' stretch is not as bad as it seems like it's going to be; you don't have to be as infuriated and incredulous at the audacity of even such an idea as I was when I ran into it. You'll probably be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are amazing. The game is very fun and atmospheric. I had a blast playing it. The game also doesn't insult the player by dumbing things down, the puzzles are unique (as in, the same mechanics are only sparsely re-used) and the fights are tough and fair. The story also has an interesting twist that I dind't figure out without a story analyses.The only reason I do not recommend this game is because of its runtime. I got all 12 achievements and have seen everything this game has to offer in 6.3 hours according to steam. And I took my time and also died a fair bit along the way because I got to 1 checkpoint relatively low on health. If you don't mind paying €40 for a very high quality 6.3 hour experience, than I would actually recommend buying this game. And if you compare this to eating dinner somewhere or something, it's well worth the money. But if you compare it to other games of €40, most will entertain you for more than 6.3 hours... but might be less quality entertainment if this is your vibe.In the end, I don't regret my purchase as money isn't as large a factor for me personally so I was very reluctant to give a thumbs down, but when compared to other games, they are probably worth your money more. When this game reaches a prize you think is worth 6 hours of entertainment though, definitely pick it up, it's an experience worth having.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying that I had no hype or particular expectations for this game and had understood that it's not supposed to be an iteration of Doom. I also don't mind paying more for short games as long as they're good, and am generally forgiving of all kinds of problems. I love the art of Giger and Beksinski and cosmic horror in general. I went into Scorn with a very forgiving mindset and tried to love it (and there were quite a few moments that I did love), but by the end of the game I was laughing in disbelief and frustration at how much not a good game Scorn is.For the first two-three hours, Scorn is actually pretty solid. This is almost entirely due to its fantastic and strong art direction and sound design (LUSTMORD worked on the soundtrack). A lot of the scenery is fantastic and invites you to stop and take in the sights and sounds. There is a sense of foreboding and the puzzle-heavy  gameplay is disorienting. The puzzles are mostly all right; they either require some thought and attention to detail, or else are braindead easy. But the problems that will plague the rest of the game appear early on, starting with a "moral choice"--the nature and implications of this choice are impossible to figure out, it is the only such moment in Scorn, and it means nothing. You also repeat certain puzzles or sequences in this stretch of the game, and this also ends up becoming a recurring and abhorrent problem. That key you graft to your left hand? You better get used to that, because you'll repeat it multiple times. Eventually you get some weapons and enemies to fight; the combat is clunky but forgivable. What's disappointing is that this unsettling setting cannot give you anything more creative than a pistol, shotgun and grenade launcher. You can also simply avoid most combat encounters by just walking far away enough, leading to the enemies being despawned. There are only 3 regular enemy types in the game, and beating them requires nothing more than pointing and shooting.Scorn starts falling apart quickly and spectacularly in the final area. By that point it has become clear that the game is just a linear trek from scenery to scenery with increasingly tedious puzzle and combat sections sprinkled on top. The final area has you repeat a number of gameplay sequences multiple times, one of which makes no logical sense whatsoever (the pods and the pregnancy robots). There are no more puzzles at this point, instead we get treated to riveting(!) sequences such as pressing a button, running along a straight line and pressing another button. This section also presents us with three repetitions of the game's sole boss battle. Any discerning player realizes at this point that the game is running out of ideas and is resorting to very transparent padding to last longer. This is also the section where the game tries to pull off particularly shocking imagery, but those made me laugh out loud. That's not a reaction you want in this game.Attempts at padding eventually fail, as they must, and there's an abrupt ending sequence with a very strange conclusion. The problem isn't that Scorn doesn't explain things, it's that the people who are imagining it to be asking deep existentail questions are inhaling copium, and there really is nothing substantial behind it all. This seems to be the case simply because most of the planned content has been cut from the game, as a look through the art book will make clear. In fact, there is a pervasive sense of incompleteness throughout the experience. Scorn is a decayed fragment of something that was shaping up to be potentially majestic.Ultimately, I was left annoyed and drained at repeating unimaginative and effortless combat or progression sections and was amused at some of the storytelling choices made. A bad aftertaste washed over the aesthetic experience Scorn had provided me with its cyclopean landscapes and music, leaving only disappointment. Even with all the time I took to explore without trying to progress, it was done in a little over six hours. Factoring in the huge amounts of padding, it's incredible to think that eight years of work amounted merely to an impressionistic short story. It also feels like the Giger-Beksinski imagery comes from a place of pure artistic talent but is disconnected from the psychological weirdness and darkness that those two had tapped into.There is some good in Scorn, and it's not the worst game ever as some seem to be claiming. Taking the risk to make something like this and not merely following the latest trend is commendable. But there's just too little here, and what is there is mostly tiresome and shallow. The price for it all, not just money but more importantly, time, is too steep.

_childDocuments_.review: Giger/Bekinski art immersive experience. The first puzzle discourages you, but it's solvable and if you pass beyond, the game becomes very dynamic. I truly love the sheer monumental scale of the outdoors, first time in my long gaming life I experience exterior spaces like in this game. Deeeelightful! (...And creepy)
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell this game falls flat on what could have been something truly unique. Its a proper shame it really is because i wanted this game to do so much more.The Good Points:Looks amazingWell animatedBrilliant sound design and art direction.The Bad Points:Combat feels last minute and is flat out awful (should never have been put in)While levels look great they begin to blend together and become almost flat at times.There is absolutely no story at all. (Watched a friend play it all the way and it leads to nothing)Puzzles are not fun at all and often feel like they were made up as they went along.I supported this game way back when it looked like it wouldn't ever be finished.After all this time and early access to its demo i can say the wait wasn't worth it. If the game was nothing but another 1 time walking sim it would have fared much better. The story is "cryptic" which is too often used in games as a lazy means of world building but there's giving the player hints and some idea of whats going on and then there's not doing anything hoping that you fill in the gaps yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to level with you. I recommend this game ONLY IF YOU LIKE PUZZLE GAMES AND WALKING SIMS. I've noticed that there are a LOT of people who walked into this, following it over the development, and expected it to be a much larger standard shooter, or something that is much more along the lines of that genre. Approach this as Interactive Art, and with an interest in such things, and this is the game for you. It's incredibly faithful to H.R. Giger's work, and the influence is prominent and well kept throughout the entire game. If that's your interest, this is honestly worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This is first and foremost an art piece, not an FPS. Don't go into this expecting to blast monsters and having a good time.  This game is meant for you to walk through and enjoy the fantastic digital art, the dark atmosphere, and the few puzzles sprinkled through out.  Keep in mind, this has serious horror, gore, and sexual overtones, so discretion is advised.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Some people aren't understanding this game and attributing it to the game being bad. So far from the truth. A masterclass in surreal environment design, from visual art to audible ambiance. An nightmarish alternate reality, the conceptual styles of Giger and Beksinski, brought to life by the incredible artists at EBB. I applaud this work of art and the team behind it, and would love a sequel or even dlc. Like take my money, I need more.  I also highly recommend tripping through this game with the vorpx VR mod. I've never had a more memorizing, terrifying, and immersive gaming experience. This is it chief.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Will recommend to anyone who loves good visuals and sound in a game.The atmosphere was like no other game I ever played before!Puzzles were quite interesting and fun to figure out and also having to think twice about engaging enemies or finding a way around them.It did feel like it left me wanting more, with only 6 hours spent on playthrough but, now that the ground work has been done I can only hope they do Scorn 2...
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: No.This game certainly is unique. The atmosphere is there. You feel alone, there's not much in terms of music, which is not necessarily a bad thing, but it can feel dull at times.The design is of course outstanding. The game has very cruel moments. And it's mostly up to you to figure out how things work, there are not really tutorials nor is there a map.That being said, the combat is the worst I've seen in a good while. Your first weapon, which you'll use for quite a bit, is a melee only weapon. It takes 5-6 hits to kill the standard enemy and if that wasn't bad enough, the enemy attacks outrange yours. Did I mention that the melee weapon grants you 2 strikes before it needs to refill for what seems like over 5 seconds? So you go in, hit 1-2 times and then run away for 5 seconds before returning and striking again. Hoping you don't lose 1-2 of your precious health bars in the process. It's annoying.Throw a punishing checkpoint system into the mix and you get why nobody likes this games combat. You may face a situation where you throw levers, watch their animations, do a bit of running and take out a total of ~5-6 enemies before you may die and do the whole repetitive thing again.Why?The puzzles are solvable so far, but a bit tedious and the game itself is pretty maze-like. You may end up running around a bit before progressing, without much happening.I don't quite know what to think of this yet, it seems very experimental. If it weren't as frustrating (see above), I may find it ok. But so far, it's a tedious walking simulator with puzzles, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat and (at least so far) no (obvious) story. You run around this semi-dead, empty-feeling biomechanical world not knowing what you are, why you're there, where you are or anything of that sort. You just solve puzzles to continue on your way (to what?).Could've been a better game and especially with the design, it seems like a missed opportunity. At least that's my opinion so far after not quite 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: First off , ok with that now out of the way;This is a great atmospheric game, its pacing is slow to allow you to really look at the world. There is no dialog or text to tell you what to do next, all you know is that you must to get to somewhere. The sound design is really good as well, letting the world feel empty when appropriate and adding just enough on some of the more impactful parts. Entropy at its finest.I liked the puzzles it has, it actually required some thinking to get past. Now combat was a bit janky but that was not the focus of this game and in most cases you could avoid it out right.For those that want a slow burn horror experience and are fine with body mutilation of yourself and others, you will have a great time. But for those that want a DOOM like experience or can't handle body mutilation I would say this is not the game for you.

It has 4 guns you can find and use to kill things with. +Disturbing imagery-Pretty linear-No replayability-Seems to have a lot cut content judging from the trailer, which I assume is meant to appease censors to get an M rating-Weak enemy design
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game and work of art, more so a great work of art. I seriously had to stop every 5 minutes in the game to just look around or focus on something specific for a while, everything just looks and feels like it has been handcrafted with a lot of care and attention to detail put into it. As well as appearances, the atmosphere is great, being eerie, beautiful and disturbing at the same time. This is definitely a one time playthrough kind of game though, as I can't really see any reason to revisit it unless you are tripping balls or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is not your typical horror game. More than scary, it is disturbing. It makes you uneasy. It messes up with the perception you have of what is disgusting and alien to your reality. Makes you question what are you playing, and why are you playing such game. And you play exactly because of that - you want to understand the purpose behind all of this eery, scary, disturbing atmosphere, who are you and what are you doing there. Graphically beautiful, with an amazing immersive and eery ambience. The weapon mechanics are somewhat cluncky, but once you understand them it becomes easy to see that as something that could be improved rather than a negative point from the beginning. The puzzles present are challenging enough, and they will make you question your ability to resolve a problem or to drive you a bit insane if you don't pay attention, but nothing overall impossible.Overall, for a game that is completed in between 5 - 9h, I can definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: As many have already mentioned, art direction carried the game. I laughed several times when I got lost looking at the world, enjoying all the details in the design, not knowing or keeping track where I was going, I've ended up lost several times, a surprising feeling when the game is somewhat linear, even with it's large rooms and overlaying vistas. Aside from puzzle aspects of the games everything else in Scorn seemed lacking. the combat felt odd, the games length is very disappointing and my biggest gripe was the lack of lore/story telling. It's good to leave some questions unanswered but to the point where it's simply frustrating to go along with what's going was a breaking point for me. And what was the ending supposed to mean? Very confusing. This is a deep sale game only.

_childDocuments_.review: honestly at first i thought this game was pretty bad ass the mystery behind everything had my curiosity going crazy.... most of the game is pretty repetitive with annoying ass puzzles that will have you running back and forth throughout each stage.... everything looks the same for the most part and there is no sort of map so this is the only reason it takes time to beat... the boss you have to fight is a level one boss (if that)to any fps chad and how fast i beat this game made me really disappointed in buying for $40.... not worth it at all it is 1/10 of a game.... graphics and creation 10/10 game play/story 1/10.... buy at own risk.

_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know this game existed at all until about three weeks ago. That being said, the art and world design is amazing. The atmosphere is decently dreadful and somber although I'd argue there was a bit more silence throughout the game then what you would hope for.The combat is... not so great. Very tank like, enemies are fairly easy to outsmart and highly predictable. I hate to say this, but I was actually falling asleep 3 hours into the game (visible on my stream), although the ramp up in combat shook me awake a bit later on. I think they did a great justice to the Giger aesthetic, there's also a fair bit of doom/dead space blending, but the price tag is highly unjustified.The description they provided themselves about the game on steam is pretty spot on. They "throw" you straight into this world with no real idea what the hell is going on, who the hell you are, or where in the hell you're supposed to go. I can't recall seeing a single line of text anywhere in-game past the Main Menu.The difficulty curve drops a bit on the puzzles after the first Act but overall they're fairly easy to grasp in concept albeit somewhat tedious at times, I wouldn't call them baby puzzles or anything like that. All in all, I'd argue it's a $25 art piece at most but that still may be too steep of a price tag for people who aren't buying this for some type of artistic experience. This is one of those games that makes me wish I could give star ratings instead of a thumbs up/down but unfortunately, I'm going to have to generalize it as a non-recommendation.edit: i'm voting for this game for outstanding visual style award but my initial review still stands and seeing as there's not really any foundation for them to add on to this game, it will likely be my final take
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The Devs had clearly a vision with this game and delivered.Personally i expected mixed reviews for this,the game is truly like the art its inspired by and Audiences take it likewise.(But that also means in a few years you will see alot of articles and yt vids or whatever is modern then,mentioning what an outstanding game Scorn was, that went against modern mechanics without ignoring them)Cause it truly is.Its one thing to be inspired by something and taking the look of it.But its a whole other level to build logical environments and a story with it.Also the puzzles are pretty intuitive,give yourself time and you notice it while playing.There was put alot of work into this,definitely.Game oozes with Athmosphere,supported by a great Soundtrack.I have to get that physical artbook.Scorn is not your typical Horror game,despite the look.Its also not your typical adventure,and definitely not an ego shooter.It is its own creative beast born from the imagination of Gamers that are also artists.Personally its a kind of game i wanted to play for a really long time.And its probably one of the few im coming back from time to time for the Athmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely so amazing and there was so much love put into every detail. The gameplay was decent, combat was unforgiving, and the story is such a mystery that I'm still trying to process what happened. However, for a game that we have been waiting for since 2016, i only wish that it was longer. My total playtime is currently 4 hours, which feels so short. I'm hoping for a DLC or some addon that makes this game longer, because there is so much more that could come out of this. There are so many questions left unanswered (for me that is) and I want to be immersed more into the world that the Devs have created. I recommend this game for people who love cosmic horror and puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting body horror game. Fully in the H. R. Giger aesthetic. Gameplay is decent with puzzles and some fairly intuitive combat.There was one section where you could get soft-locked if you weren't careful with health and I needed a guide to that. Otherwise everything was able to be figured out.Only downside is it is way way too short for the full price. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: While not bad, it does function no glitches or crashes so its well optimised.It's pretty and leaves much to the imagination, as was in short supply for this games sadly.Shallow puzzles, three enemy types with only two solutions: avoid or shoot.Many say symbolism is its main draw, which is true but done very blandly if not poorly. passive storytelling and its "meh"Final thoughts, a very pretty puddle. i hope they get another chance, it will be very easy to overcome this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Nighthmare fuel to the highest! If you love all things ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, then you'll love the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game.The score is oppressive and makes you feel like you're not welcome. The environment is something else, as everywhere you look, no matter where, is extremly detailed. The games feel best played with an xbox controller rather than a keyboard & mouse.  I love all the horrific amounts of blood and gore all over the place. The bio-mechanical structures are epic. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just vibes and atmosphere. To me there's nothing wrong with that as long as the art direction and visual presentation are on point. In the end despite phenomenal art direction the game has been in development so long the graphics were already looking dated on release which is a shame because of how spectacular it could have looked. The combat mechanics felt a bit inconsistent and sometimes frustrating but nothing too bad because that aspect of the game thankfully doesn't outstay its welcome. Despite what i see a lot of people say in the reviews I enjoyed the puzzles but i can see them being frustrating for someone who doesn't have any experience with puzzle games. Despite the flaws and thanks to the fact that's it's short and sweet i really enjoyed the game overall. It's a good value if you grab it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of puzzle and horror that i have not seen in a game prior. No dialog which creates a different perspective for each player. Not much replay value unless trying to find secrets or alternate puzzle solutions. Very interesting game highly recommend for anyone willing to try an art perspective story being told by developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Very slow, very buggy, very visually impressive, and extraordinarily immature.  Scorn presents itself as a unique, mind-bending horror, but most of its elements are just banal objects with a lump of techno-organic texture slapped on top.  Every interaction you do involves a long, unskippable cutscene, the movement and combat are sluggish and infuriating, and the checkpoint saving is obnoxious and designed to waste the maximum amount of time.  When people complained about the combat, the defense was 'well, it's not really a shooter.'  It is.  It's just a very, very bad one.  Your reward for sitting through hours worth of non-interactive first-person views of your character shoving their hands into alien buttholes and pulling out their own guts is a tour through an art gallery of statues blowing each other.  What an embarrassing pile.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Waited years as a backer for this game and never lost my hope, but unfortunately, I have to say that the final product isn't worth it.To give detail without spoiling it.Solving puzzles felt more like time wasters rather than fun.There are a few major forced plot situations.combat is very unenjoyable, I often found myself backing out of the room waiting for the enemies to despawn, then continuing. The ending literally meant nothing to me because there was no context as to what anything was.Though I don't recommend the game, it's definitely not the worst game out there, but it isn't something I could see myself recommending over other games in the genre.----------------Spoilers-------------------Alright so there are a few things that really frustrated me, like the lack of effort to remove the parasite, the whole setting the embryos into the mechs then fighting (why couldn't you just shoot them in their containers?), the convenience of the machines that would cut off the infection on your arm, I could keep going but I think I've said enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Careful recommendation. Scorn is one of the most beautifully crafted games I've ever played, but the gameplay is just not that fun. It has some interesting puzzles that fit into the world, others are just distracting and out of place. The combat is also not that much fun, the enviroments are very cramped and you get cornered or stuck very easily. Still, the visual design is so impressive that it's worth going through. I finished the game in about 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I've been watching this game for a few years and was really pumped for it's release. Unfortunately it's a bit underwhelming when played. I understood that this was going to be a puzzle/walking sim but this was a slog even for that genre. I'll sum it up like this; there was to much distance between puzzle components which is made worse by the movement speed. The setting and art direction was amazing however it was largely, empty, uninteractive and seemed to be to get a bit repetitive. If you did like this environment i'd recommend Tormentum - Dark Sorrow. Similar art style, a bit more direct narrative, better puzzles and better pacing. It is 2D so it's a bit of a hard caparison in that regard.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Why oh why don't I listen?  So, despite overwhelming evidence that Scorn should just be left alone, I couldn't believe that a game with such amazing visuals wouldn't have something to offer.  Well, it did.  In the first 10 minutes of game-play.  Stunning visuals!  Amazing bio-mechanical antique landscapes reminiscent of a chitin like organic vista.  Enough gore to whet the appetite and then .... well then ... nowhere to go from there.  Most horror games build the visceral experience as you advance.  Each hour played should take you deeper and deeper through the graphics, story, and environment.  Sadly, Scorn has just the one environment.  A few shifts but overall nothing that made me care about what came next.  As to the puzzles...basic meh.  They did little to create any real environment around the characters interactions.  We are not fixing a aging machine or undoing layers of locks to take us to hell...we are simply using mechanical puzzles to let us know that we are progressing from one checkpoint to the next.  Combat felt completely out of place.  Not sure if it was to create tension or just stretch out the game.  To me, it just got in the way.I did completely play through the game.  There were breaking glitches at the end so I had to redo it a few times and fell back on a walkthrough to make sure that I wasn't missing a step.  All the way I kept hoping that there would be something redeeming but alas, I should have listened.  I really hope that this could be inspiration for something larger.  I really don't mind the lack of back-story or allowing the player to create their own explanation but you got to keep the player awake at least.  So ill say it one last time....I should have listened.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: nice game with very good visuals, but why dont i recommend this game then?well very simple you pay 40$, for a game that you can finish within 3 hours and there is not more gameplay then that. i am very sad that i could not finish it within 2 hours because then i could have still refunded the game lol.on serious note wait for sale, if this game is worth 5-10 euro you should buy, for this amount of money i expected a bit more gameplay.

When I restarted a second time, it hadn't saved, being so early on, and there was no way in hell I was going to drag my ass through that same hour long slog of an opening, just to see if it did it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I truly hate to say this.Dont buy Scorn.When I first saw that Game play Trailer 5 years ago, I was watching this game with a close eye. Excited for a new horror game with an H.R. Geiger style. And after many long delays, and what seems like development hell, Scorn has finally released.Ill say The beginning starts us off really strong, Questions behind everything, a world that looks amazing. The artists truly did an amazing job. I stopped many times to look at the environment and it sold that there was more on the plate than there really was.but the game is ungodly short, and that wouldn't be a problem if the game play made up for it, It doesn't. The story is nonsensical and I can describe it as goal-less. right at the end, they introduce a super rad mechanic and use it once then the game ends. I am not kidding the best part of this game is the last 10 minutes, then it ends with no real conclusion which im sure someone will write up to some artsy fartsy reasoning, but it truly feels like We waited 5 years for 30% of a game.If it was longer, if it built upon mechanics, if there was more things in place to tell me what my ultimate goal was, then we'd have a game.This isn't a game, Its a means to an end to deliver on their kick starter promise to release something.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorn is a beautiful crafted game and was truly a blessing to play. The  and unique environments, buildings, and themes were something to behold and will stick with me forever. In fact, I personally don't usually leave reviews recommending or not for games because each person's experience with a game will be different. Not to mention that the story and themes of that story of every game will always speak to each person differently due to their own experiences and view.However, despite this I feel like I need to leave one for Scorn, as this game while being a wonderful and fantasti game it is also a game I cannot with any conscience recommend to another player to buy with their money in this current economic environment, especially when we have so many games that are stealing the stoplight due to their amazing achievement. Don't get me wrong this game is definitely a one of a kind but it is incredibly short, I beat the game start to finish with all the achievements except for one in only 4.2 hours. That means that at full price $40, you are paying $10 for each hour almost. I got it for half off ($20) and still feel like it wasn't worth it despite that really is the only reasonable price for the game.It's because of this that I usually do not buy games from small teams or companies that are not trip A studios. Not to discredit the team that made this game, as they definitely deserve praise for making such an amazing game and I truly believe that an incredible game such as this one could have never been made by a trip A/big studio due to it's mature themes, buildings, "story", and creatures and I am not just talking about the blood and gore; therefore, I commend this team in making this game and would love to recommend it to friends, family, and strangers. However, for the reasons that I will get into besides just the length of this game, I cannot.Starting with the combat, while it is certainly unique and different from most games that does not necessarily mean it's a compliment. In fact at the start of the game I recommend completely avoiding combat at all costs as if anything it will slow you down and annoy you more than anything. The first gun you get in the game in punishing and has a range that is hard and confusing to read much like classic COD Zombies "knifing" before they fixed it later generations. Except in this case in addition to having confusion on the range, if you miss or hit you are forced to go through a short cool-down before you can fire this flesh piston again into the enemy.I am sure this was created with the best of intentions to seemly make tease combat situations where you think about your health and ammo when you get "guns" that require it later, which I will speak on later in this review in their own respective places; however, instead it creates this situations that feel unfair, frustrating, and down right ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Which is why even after I got the ranged weapons throughout the game I avoided combat at every opportunity I could which could even how I manage to beat the game so quickly. My intention was never to "speedrun" this game the issue is that even once you get range weapons the combat is way to punishing.As in they only give you enough ammo to fight every scenario exactly without missing, which combined with dying and the save system (which I will speak on later) makes this game down right rage inducing and there were several times I just simply quit the game as it wasn't worth continuing in the slightest knowing that these same issues were going to be present throughout the entire game. The only reason I would continue was simply to continue to enjoy the amazing scenery and to see where this story would go. That being said, I love discovering each of the "guns" and loved out original and amazing each one was, as well as I was impressed with the "inventory system" and the animation for switching "guns" and for seeing how much ammo and blood (which works as a potion to restore your health) was left.The real issue is that because the ammo is limited that missing a station for health or ammo because it's tucked around a corner is a death sentence and combining this with the games saving and death, downright makes it again too punishing and makes the issue a glaring red-flag that you will be reminded of throughout the game time and time again. Not mention enemies don't drop anything, no ammo or health making your character effectively a masochist and giving the player literally no incentive to participate in combat unless obviously necessary to continue with the story and/or to complete a puzzle. Which quick tip, I found that enemies will leave you alone while you are doing puzzles. I only found this out because of how "nails against a chalkboard" the combat was and this resulted in an endless loop where I would kite/ignore/run-past enemies get to the obvious puzzle->complete it->get out of the animation and lead the enemies out of a corridor->dodge enemies and run to the next section.Which is why I constantly avoided combat; however, that being said the moments outside of combat, even the small sections between combat was downright fantastic! All the puzzles were intuitive to a degree I have not seen in a game before. I am talking about being about to understand what to do without any hints or guides, but still being hard enough that it gives you a fair challenge and some moments of failing only to understand what the game is asking of you and getting it immediately or after a couple more times. Which is honestly an impressive feat and something the devs should be praised for, for sure! This cause and effect with lack of rewards from the combat, limited ammo/health, and puzzle all wouldn't such an issue if death and saving in this game weren't what was holding this game back so much.Death in this game is the kind of torture of having each finger nail painfully and slowly being pulled off each finger which aptly fits into this games theme so maybe that was the point! *jokingly* It is the same in that one the first nail has been ripped off it sucks, but you think to yourself, "At least it's over" only to see them move to the next finger to start the process all over again. This being that there are several story related animations that occur while moving from each section that I will not spoil that happen, which by themselves are incredible and a sight to behold! The problem is that since all saving is all automatic and not controlled by the player at all that once you die sometimes you have to watch these scenes over and over again because you die because you missed a single shot, didn't know what to do, activated a puzzle/story piece too early (this one really only an issue towards the end as most things can't be done out of order as the game wont let you), etc.Which is what ruins what are otherwise some of the coolest *cutscenes*/animations I have seen in a game in such a long time. This also bleeds back into the combat issues I have discussed eariler about missing hidden stations for ammo/health as when the game does auto save (and it does this without telling you) it saves your health and ammo you have left exactly as they are. So if you think you could do a combat encounter or boss battle better after you know what to do, well the game says, "♥♥♥♥ you, git gud scrub." Except unlike a game such as Dark souls it saves seemly at random not always after important animation, events, progression which makes it again super frustrating and has a feeling of being down right unfair. It's such a simple fix too if you are going to do this or have a game feel tense let the players save and load at their own discretion. Could you imagine if it saved your health and how many estus flasks you had before got to the boss door and not being able to refill them until you beat the boss? Being forced to watch the boss cut-scene or animation without being able skip it every single time? There's more but I'll say this free on gamepass

_childDocuments_.review: I love almost everything about this game - art, atmosphere, puzzles, even the combat - all except for 2 points:The first is a bit subjective: Lack of actual LoreI was hoping that there would be some actual story slowly revealed throughout the game. Even vague explanations for what this world was, why it's in it's current state, and what the beings are or what they mean in terms of this world's current state. But there's truly nothing.The second point is much more important: Scorn is VERY shortI feel like I really took my time with this game and I maxed out at about 5 hours to beat the game. And an hour of that was spent dying repeatedly on one particular point near the end of the game. It's a real shame because everything else about this game is absolutely incredible! I even found myself really enjoying the survival horror combat that felt deliberately clunky in a polished way. I would have gladly spend hours upon hours slowly making my way through long dungeons that really emphasized the choices of survival, when to fight and when to run away. But instead the whole path is very linear with only a couple segments letting you actually choose between fighting or fleeing. My only hope is that they used some kind of creation kit in building this game so modders can go wild creating custom stories but based on the level design that seems unlikely.Worth it to get on sale but not full price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to write a good review about that one, and it's also hard to write a bad one. But ultimatively a verdict about a game's quality has to be made if you care to write a review about it, because Steam beggens for one and doesn't allow for neutrality.The visuals and aesthetics in this game are fantastic, no questions asked. So is the whole atmosphere and the disturbing feeling it creates...but that's about it...unfortunately. It simply isn't enough to say "it's just the world it is" and leave the player with no conceptual thought whatsoever, when stripping them 40€ at full prize. That's literally like saying "f you, give me your money because we don't care!". And no, of course I didn't pay full prize. But the fact they ask 40€ from you for 7-8 hours of a visual astonishing Tech-Demo, on a game engine the devs absolutely had no hold on, is outrageous to say the least. If it wasn't for the Unreal Engine, this game wouldn't have gotten anywhere. No wonder it failed at Kickstart.We have an obviously symbiotic culture, be it Human or Alien, that's open to speculation. It doesn't really matter in detail because both lifeform arguments are valid. The symbiont seems to be some kind of Cthulu like Alien resemblance, as showen on one of the final wall images. We also have a machinery made to engineer in favor for the symbiotic civilization, by putting them on a higher level of existance. And we do have some form of Virus or Bacteria corrupting the whole machinery, and as a result, the civilization. There may have been a war, or there may not have been a war. It's just an argument floating around about the game on the internet, because the visuals might give that away. But to be honest I've seen no physical coherent reason in game to actually support the war theory. For it all it could just be a hellish dreamscape fading out of existance, or an ancient civilization's architectics on a planet corrupted by weird gravity and slow decay. In a present or past warfare scenario you'd need to have two active parties commiting, or having commited to a/the war. And none of the lifeforms in this game seem to resample any form of present or past activity at all outside of what has been build. Why does time seem to work on some of the dead bodies, but others are completely unaffected?But where it starts to really collapse into meaningless is when we go into detail about how the whole "idea" was transported to gameplay. Why does an advanced Alien civilization have a "Alien Parasite Removal Machine" for a very specific situation? How was it known to the "Priests" preparing "Choosen Ones" for their journey to a deity world, or whatever the devs trying hard to imagine? It's that one question that doesn't make any sense at all...the other stuff all together? Not cohesive? Sure it is, because I just gave you a general image of what this civilization is about. The problem here however, is much more concerning as you could tell the devs had absolutely no idea what they were doing.The gameplay is terrible, like literally everything of it. It feels like they wrapped all bad gameplay elements you could possibly imagine, and wrap it up into a single game, and just went for it. Clunky controls. Terrible hitboxes. Physical glitches. Outrageously stupid difficulty because of control shenanigans and tedious die-rinse-and-repeat-situations...oh wait...actually there's only one such situation, the moment you have to kill giant Cyborgs to receive the Trinity of Miscarriage. I recon it's a resamblance to the movie Running Man?So you basically have zero replay and gameplay value aside from one-time-annoying puzzles, because once you did them you will always know how to solve them, as there is absolutely no dynamic process to it, removing even more substance from the reason to replay the game. Then you get build up to that one Trinity situation through the whole game, without any serious challenge and fairly hard combat situations, which you can totally avoid by hiding and letting the script engine to its pre-set "monster will submerge in the flesh continuum", only to experience the ultimate unfair rinse-and-repeat cheating at the player situation with control shenanigans, and pre-scripted sequences to kill those Cyborgs in a painful agony of reloading and doing the whole sequence again? Any of you devs ever heard about pacing? Why have the player be mad about one situation, if all the other situation's difficulty is lackluster at best? You trying hard to pull an "Evil Within" or "Alien: Isolation" but didn't know how to?No seriously. I think it's time to get to the point. It's easy to lead and blend people into believing something outside of their comprehension or control is happening, in and outside of the game. Like the devs are a bunch of super skilled artisitical heroes that achieved a new form of art and something never seen before...if you have zero knowledge about past art and all the aesthetics and concepts of the game, well then, yes, you might get the picture we have a Class A game developed by a class A team. But nowadays it's all to common that developers just wrap up already existing ideas and content, slap a new lable on it, and sell it to the masses as something genuinly different and unique. In this case they didn't even care much to hide they've blatantly stolen creative and physical content from so many past sources and ideas.So no. I don't recommend you are paying 40€ for this sadomasochistic copycat agony. Go to Youtube, save the money, and just watch an 8k review. Its visuals serve as a good movie entertainer while you are enjoying a cup of popcorn, but as a game, in the literal sense of "game" which supposed to carry some sort of entertainment or fun...no...just no!

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn's atmosphere and visuals are absolutely amazing.  The time and attention to detail that it took to make an H.R. Giger fever dream into a video game must be staggering.  Playing Scorn is like walking through a masterpiece of dark art.  It is 100% living in a (less sexy) version of Giger's work.  BUT......the "combat" is atrocious and literally the opposite of fun.  I cannot even continue to explore this amazingly crafted universe because getting PWN'ed by undead chicken fetuses and playing the same loop repeatedly gets very old very fast.  The weapons are awesome looking and their design is interesting but they function terribly and the enemies apparently are all expert acid spitting marksmen.  As for the puzzles, meh.  I don't care for puzzle games much so I don't really have an unbiased opinion.  Scorn feels like a mind blowing immersive walk through sprinkled with unnecessarily frustrating game play, and would have been better served to be an actual walk through.  I still give it a thumbs up because it might as well have Giger's signature on it and I am a devout H.R. fan boy

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all, while I would recommend this game, that comes with some caveats; in the game's current state, I would recommend this game only to hardcore fans of HR Giger that can look past some questionable gameplay decisions and the price tag. The game's world is absolutely a love letter to Giger, and everything about the sound, visuals, and atmosphere ring true to the feel of his artwork, you are exploring a piece of his art, through and through. However. The checkpointing and difficulty of the combat makes the game frustrating to play at times, and while the combat is by no means the focus of the game (it did not need to be 'deeper' or 'more involved' like some people have been saying), it is clunky enough that it feels less like a struggle to survive in an alien world, and more like a struggle against the systems of the game.The scarcity of healing and ammunition encourages you to avoid unnecessary combat and evade monsters where you can, the issue therein lies in the fact that a lot of the game is corridors and tight spaces, meaning it is often times difficult to evade monsters without taking a decent amount of damage. This, coupled with the quite frankly sparse autosave checkpoints you have to rely on for saves, means that a run of bad luck can set you back a decent amount of progress, which is a serious blow to your immersion in the world.The puzzles themselves are nothing too difficult, I wouldn't say they're too easy, as I don't think the point of them is to be difficult, the point of them is to add to the world; the puzzles are the main way the player interacts with the world and has an effect on it, and the fact that your character physically uses everything you interact with is key in bringing that immersion together, I honestly think that if the puzzle pieces simply moved on their own as you pressed the button, the game would lose a lot of it's magic.While I haven't finished the game yet myself, I would agree that the pricetag of $40 is steep for what is apparently about 8-9 hours of game, and as such I would say wait for a sale for this one, even if you are a huge fan of Giger's work.While I am not as disappointed by Scorn as others have been, I do think there are some very key issues that need fixing in order to make the game less tedious at points, namely the combat and the sparse checkpoints. It is my hope that with time and patches, the game can be enjoyable for a larger audience, as it is criminal for people to have their experience in this beautiful, grotesque world marred by questionable design. Personally, I was able to push past the bad and deeply enjoy the good, but I completely understand those who got too frustrated and put the game down, and I want everyone who did to get the chance to enjoy it as much as I did at some point in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded this missed opportunityReally great aesthetics, almost perfectly delivers the Giger feels (it misses sexuality), but lacks in terms of gameplay or story. The puzzles are very easy, combat is only hard because of very scarce health items and annoying reasons (ie: you get two shots in your melee gun, then slow reload, while first type of enemy needs 5 hits and attacks every few seconds). The interactions with the environment (buttons, levers, opening of doors) is exceptionally well done visually, but very poor in any kind of logical sense. I mean.... in this technologically advanced place, why does a simple door need like 6 different non related steps to open? It really makes you feel like the whole place didn't had an actual purpose other than to create puzzles for you, which really brakes immersion for me. 2 hours in, I didn't find logs/messages or anything that would let me know anything about the story, where my character came from, why is he here, etc. Things just happen, you are just walking from area to area. Well, only you as a player, because after the first hour you change to a different player character without any explanation. Maybe all of this get's explained later, but I just felt the current price tag doesn't worth this, and based on other review, it's not too long anyway. (4-8 hours)It's a pity, because even in this two hours there were a few very neat parts. Maybe grab it on a sale around 10 bucks, or just watch the gameplay for the feels.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn has an incredible art style, good animations, and well-crafted level design. Visually, it’s a masterpiece. But beyond that, it falls short.The game is very short—I finished it in just 6 hours, even taking my time exploring and admiring the world. There’s also no reason to replay it, as there are no choices, secrets to find, or alternative game modes. There’s no story context either: you don’t know who you are, what you’re doing, or why. The lack of guidance, combined with unexplained controls, made finding my way especially frustrating. The environment is alien, filled with buttons and interactive objects, but the game never makes it clear where to go or what to do next, leaving you to wander aimlessly and hope you're in the right place.Combat is clunky and unrewarding. Ammo and health are scarce, and there’s no stealth option, making fights more of a hassle than fun. I ended up avoiding enemies altogether, either by waiting for them to despawn or simply running past.At 40 Euros, I can't recommend it. For under 15 Euros in a sale, maybe—if you love the art and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: The marketing and reviews I've seen for this game are incredibly disingenuous. I was sold on this by a Rock Paper Shotgun article talking about the "difficult" puzzles and interesting interconnected world. That doesn't exist. This game is completely linear and does not have any difficult puzzles. It can be interesting, definitely, and I don't have as many issues with the combat as some. I can only recommend this if you use Game Pass or buy it at a discount with the expectation that you will get a 5-6 hour walking sim with occasional puzzles and combat.The visual design is beautiful, but there is no story to speak of, the themes are... not as interesting as the developers seem to think they are, the combat and enemy variety are lacking, and the ending was insulting. There are 3 enemy types and a boss, and 4 weapons; however, the first weapon is basically a pneumatic hammer that only fires twice and is used more for opening doors than for actual combat, and you get the fourth weapon for about 15 minutes at the end of the game and never kill anything with it except a single enemy. You read that right, a quarter of this game's arsenal *is never used in actual combat* outside of one very specific instance. The guns sound and feel pretty good, but there's severely limited ammunition and in some sections enemies respawn indefinitely, so you aren't motivated to use them all that often.There's an incredible amount of animation and modeling work on display, but despite the polish I would compare this game to agony or inner chains, and inner chains had more ideas and better combat. I enjoyed the game but it's significantly overpriced and marketed disingenuously.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't write another warning to potential buyers. This is a really beautiful game, with a lot of care and work, and (unsurprisingly) most of it went to create a perfect atmosphere. The game won't give you many definitive answers.Gameplay, specially gunplay, is enough. It is not designed around gameplay, but it's good enough and I think it kind of reinforces that your character isn't made for combat. The puzzles and the interactions with the different machines and objects added to the immersion and added to your interpretation of the enviroment. I recommend deactivating the HUD, as the HUD breaks part of the immersion and it isn't very necessary (Although you can activate it again to check for interactive objects for puzzles or to check your health).The artbook is also very beautiful, and I recommend reading it after finishing the game, as it may help to understand some things better.Overall a great game and I really enjoyed it a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a game at odds with itself, never quite sure what it wants to be. Some people have come to it thinking it's a standard first person shooter: to be clear it is absolutely not. It is both made for a very specific audience and yet tries to please several.Scorn's obvious crown jewel is the visual design. As a huge fan of Giger, Beksinksi and all things body horror Scorn is a florid nightmare of exquisitely designed environments and set pieces, never shying away from the phallic and yonic imagery of its inspirations. I have never seen such gorgeous visuals from a videogame, and it often feels like skulking through sprawling work of art - my F12 key got a hell of a workout. The sickly squelches of flesh and deep rumbles of machinery are all tied together harmoniously with Lustmord's soundscapes. What I'd give for smell-o-vision.The game design's attitude to the player mirrors the world you are trapped in, cold and indifferent as to if you ever make progress. There is no map, waypoints, or tooltips. Puzzles are arcane and obtuse. For a "I wish more of my bones were broken" kind of person I absolutely adore this kind of treatment, but will frustrate many players expecting something more streamlined.After a couple of hours completely entranced by this compelling world I was handed a weapon, and things quite quickly fell apart. Combat in Scorn is clunky, unsatisfying, and far too common. You are given extremely limited ammo but an increasing number of enemies seem to spawn as you make progress. It's not difficult gunplay but it's not fun either, and you have to weigh each encounter up with that or tedious cat and mouse. The game doesn't seem sure if it want to be a Resident Evil or Penumbra, and fails to really deliver on either design philosophy. This encapsulates a majority of the game and completely distracts from what I really want to do in Scorn which is soaking in the atmosphere and savouring the grotesque visuals.In an alternate reality, Scorn drops the biogun stuff, treats enemy encounters like Amnesia, and fully leans in the puzzle and exploration elements, creating something like a body horror Myst or Zork Nemesis. Maybe next time.Steam's binary recommend/don't recommend makes this a hard review to finish. I enjoyed my time with Scorn, and short of a photo mode being added don't see much reason to go back to it. It's clear quite a bit of content was cut with stuff from even recent trailers not making the final version. There is no obvious plot, which is fine but makes the ending particularly unsatisfying. I've waited six years and wanted to love Scorn, and I'll be thinking about it a whole lot, but all-in-all it's a mixed six hour experience for thirty quid. Can't recommend it at that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember saw the inception of SCORN back in about 2014 or so. I remember being sudden captive by just the concept art and the look of the game. It pique my interest very hard on how can someone going to make a game that look literally straight out of the H.R. Geiger himself. Well, After almost a decade later, I get to experience that on my own.SCORN to be put in the most simplest term, Is a walking simulator with puzzles element sprinkle between each layer and top.  You are going to walking around and solving a puzzles on your own.By the direction of the game, It is very intention on leaving a blank check for you to filled in on which puzzles to working on and how each suppose to get you progressing through the game, Which in my opinion. I like it, No hand holding for you. So you have to clench your thinking muscle to figuring out the way forward.Problem is, The puzzles in this game, Whilst not that repetitive in nature, Are still over sometime too complicate and pointlessly dragging on, I admit to just stammering through the puzzles until I got them right and hardly find myself to really enjoying them that much. Taking the "Egg" puzzle for instant, That one got me to quit the game multiple of time before I figured the right way to solving the puzzle.But then again, I understand the core merit of this game. Its an art and everything is just a second thought.If you play SCORN, I can assured that you will feel like having a fever dream beyond anything you ever had up to this point. The whole world is a pure nightmare fuel to look at, Let alone interacting with them and you can see a fine tune on animation for each action you took. The game is a purest art house translate into a video game in a most magnificent way I could even has hoped for.In conclusion. The game is good, A bit too short (5 hours  in my case) but the price felt just right as well. For someone who looking forward this game on all these time. I say this is worth a shot. Especially if you want to feel yourself being squeamish as you are playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game after seing a story explained video and was really interested by the Universe that has a very unique spirit and uncommun artistic vibe. I was so happy to find an estheatic close to the movie "the war of the worlds" and Gigger's Art. Such a deception...Frankly the gameplay with the gun is so broken I would have simply removed it from the game since it does not bring anything. This is the first time I'm playing a game with a gun hitting closer than my arm reach. This is crazy considering that fixing this element should take roughly 5 minute of coding and would make the game so much more enjoyable. Also, the gamedesign elements are not very optimized all the time which also break the fluidity of the "journey". Some puzzles are interesting though, but since the game is not presented as a puzzle game and they are sparsely distributes across the levels, we don't really understand why they are there? Honestly, at some stage, I just thought that their civilization has fallen apart because they implemented such weird mechanism just to open a door... Such a non-optimization may have only result in their loss. There are a few problems with the game even when considering the "Universe" as the main  "concept" of the game. Typically, you can't have such a poor sound design if the goal is to catch the players into your atmosphere. I understand that we are living on a silly and dying world, but even in such a case, musics and soundtracks can be used. You can introduce travelling point of view or cinematic to highlight the landscape or peculiar elements of the decor. Finally, you can put discret texts hidden in the levels (such as drawings on the wall) that would help the players to "get" the story you want to tell. Simply hiding your video game concept behind a creepy cruel and dirty world esthetic is not sufficient to claim 50$. I got it with a 75% discount and this was already too expensive for me and asked a refund.As an example "Agony", that is far to be perfect, was definitely more successful in that sense.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not an easy game to rate.First of all this game has fantastic atmosphere and just looks amazing. In terms of looks alone this game is pure art and the environmental storytelling just adds to it perfectly.But I was about to drop this game in the first half because once combat gets introduced it is honestly just absolutely horendous. I get that it's probably trying to add to the atmosphere that it is not easy "to be you" but for me it was simply frustrating and made me quit the game. Also puzzles just seem absolutely confusing and the very slow pace of the game made it honestly quite boring.I really wanted to like this game because of the incredible art and I couldn't get myself over it to uninstall the game, luckily so. The second half of the game still introduces quite a lot of combat but since you get actual weapons to fight it is bearable and not as frustrating as in the first half of the game. As you start to get used to the world the puzzles almost start making sense too (not really tho). But as stated before the atmosphere and environmental storytelling is just absolutely fantastic, especially nearing the end of the game.In conclusion I can say that the gameplay of the game is not great but I will still give it a thumbs up as the art and atmosphere is something you rarely see in other games. It may be a struggle but at the end it's worth it, atleast in my opinion. I think it's probably best to see this as an "experience" rather than a game.

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting for 6 years, like many others, I was heavily disappointed.Sure there is a lot of good you can talk about. The puzzles were good(in my opinion), the graphics and world was great(though not really if you look at some of them up close), among some other things. With all that said, I cannot recommend it, especially at this price point. Should have been $30 at max, id cap it at $20 personally.The game is very short, took me under 5 hours and I really took my time with it, going slow and looking at everything. I was getting stuttering issues, probably due to the game loading in things when you get to a new area, but at the same time I maintained 150-200 FPS during the stutters.... I at one point just lowered the settings a bit, even though my PC was handling it more than enough like I said, and it seemed to stutter a lot less.If you are buying this for combat, just close the steam page immediately, its definitely not the main focus.If you enjoy walking simulators and occasional puzzles, then you will enjoy this.There were other minor issues I didn't like during my play-through, though I cant really remember.The ending really annoyed me, Really a shame they spent so much time (like 7-8 years!) for 4-5 hours of walking. At least the art direction was on point.Oh yeah, almost forgot. This is by no means a horror game. Id say thriller at most.P.P.S I dont get why people were complaining about ammo, I would argue there was too much ammo available and even though I avoided as many interactions with enemies that I could, I felt like I could of killed them all and would be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something and rather unique.You feel like you understand things, unlock knowledge the more you progress, but until the very end you're at the cusp of getting what the f this is all about, but never really understanding. Otherwordly.Visuals are more than great, sound is just peachy, athmosphere is perfect, music is on point.All that being said: What the ♥♥♥♥ developers? What is going on with this Towerdefense-level of enemy numbers in acts 3 and 4. Combat is a bit clunky, but I'd be more than fine with it. Your character is not really a UFC fighter. But when there's an enemy every 3 meters, with groups of flesh chickens bombarding you while you're getting charged at and melted at the same time; you really start to feel how limited combat (and movement in combat) really is. I guess it's to emphasize the "survive, don't fight" aspect of the game, but it kinda ruined those acts for me.Regardless, if you feel you can like this type of otherwordly cosmic horror blend of strangeness, pick the game up. _childDocuments_.review: If you don't like thinking during a game or simply don't have an appreciation for art in a traditional sense (e.g. paintings, drawings, etc.) then this game is not for you in the least.If you do, however, enjoy an experience that requires some mental exercise and aren't afraid to take things slowly to absorbed the imagery, then this game is for you.For those who are capable of appreciating what this game has to offer, there is one note to be made. For as much as I enjoyed my time playing, I do agree with many that I felt like I finished it just as quickly as I started it. You've been warned.If you're here reading through reviews, DO NOT GO INTO THIS GAME EXPECTING ACTION LIKE A DUNCE. Many negative reviews have complain about the "combat" being bad or not feeling good, when in reality this game doesn't have any combat. This is through and through a very (very)  scenic puzzle game. Again, if you don't like to think while playing a game feel free to engage with the wildlife. But in reality, the creatures in this game are just another puzzle to navigate in the world.Lastly, if you find yourself not knowing what to do, don't be afraid to take a break. Despite what many have said about this game, it is rife with tutorials if you're actually paying attention so you can tell when you're getting them.
