_childDocuments_.review: I've quite literally played this game 10 times (on here and xbox pc gamepass) After waiting about 7 years. I can say it paid off pretty well. The H.R Giger inspired art design is gorgeous, the sound design is eargasmic, puzzles are fun, the combat is done well enough, story is told through visuals and interpreted from there instead of being directly explained, the animation is pretty incredible too. In particular the humanoid you can choose to save at the beginning, each movement of him trying to stand up on his feet felt so intentional and precise. This is coming from someone who tends to enjoy games that are more of an "experience" if you will and so I understand and respect many people's reasons towards disliking the game. There are no upgrades, there isn't exactly any direction towards where to go (although I found navigating the enviorment to be fairly easy) the combat is slow, and I know there's too been complaints over the checkpoints. I've personally never had an issue with the checkpoint system but perhaps they updated it I'm not sure. _childDocuments_.review: It's honestly not much more than an ok horror game. Yes, the art style is great but gameplay really isn't. I feel like the devs didn't really know which genre they want their game to be so thex mixed it all: Part walking sim, part shooter, almost survival horror as the ressources are so scarce, and part puzzle game. The game should have focused on one of those and definitly not on puzzles imo, as those kinda suck in this game. There are often way too complicated and you have no clue what you are supposed to do. This is often an issue in the game, just like almost at the very start of the game you get into a way too big area and there is so much stuff you can interact with but everything looks so weird that you can't tell what something does until you try it out. So you wander in this way too big area, try everything out and try to find out what you are suppoed to do. This is just annoying and boring and almost made me quit the game at that point. How about combat? Well, it takes way too long till you get your first weapon, maybe an hour, which is a weird melee weapon and combat with it sucks hard because it has only 2 charges, after that it has to recharge which takes quite some time. And the most common enemy takes 5 hits from that. So usually what you do is wait around a corner till the enemy comes around, hit it twice quickly as this way it shouldn't have time to hit you, then quickly run away till you are in another cover (enemies almost always have a ranged attack), wait till your weapon recharges and repeat. This is just boring. To make it worse: it takes way too long till you get your first actual gun after that (maybe another hour) and even then ammo is so scarce you often have to still use the melee weapon which is a shame as the guns do feel pretty good to use. A bit disappointing though that there are only 3 guns, basically a pistol, a shotgun and a grenade launcher and you don't get a chance to use the latter in combat like at all except for one (joke) boss fight (which is the only boss) and you just shoot it once with it. Seriously? And then for like the last 45 minutes of the game you loose all your weapons. So maybe just 2-3 hours of the game you have any combat.Oh and don't expect a good story here as it basically doesn't even have one.Also this game is way overpriced with 40 bucks while having a playtime of around 5 hours with no replay value.I would only recommend this with a big discount to huge horror fans but more for the experience and not for the game it is.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are the average tiktok user clinically diagnosed with a 2 second attention span that needs a constant dopamine rush expecting to dolphin dive into every room like it's your generic fps multiplayer game, this game is not for you.If you are expecting to be told a story but play games like dark souls, play that instead.If you don't have time or patience, this game is not for you.This game is moreso designed for a particular kind of folk who don't mind investing to the themes of exploration, strategizing, puzzles, and speculation, if you enjoyed your adventures with games such as Myst, but have also wondered what such a related genre would be like in a more 3D space with movement, this may peak your interest.Scorn developed by Ebb, published by Kepler Interactive, brings you into a completely alien world with themes of wonder and theories, to the right kind of person you will often find yourself exploring all kinds of spaces gazing at while dreadful but gorgeous vistas that make even for great kinds of wallpapers, all kinds of visual astonishment which is a benefit to you should you be the more observant kind of folk.And while the world itself is quite alien and mysterious left for the player to wonder where exactly they are, it also has it's own hostile presence encouraging you to plan ahead before you go to the next room, 'lest you fall for an ambush and meet such an untimely death by abominations of varying kinds, unless you are nimble and know your path well.The game is not very much suited for your generic "battle royale player" as it wants to present itself more with art and pacing, and even the sounds play this into quite a major role, often wondering what exactly did happen on such a world.Having backed the project personally from the highest tier possible through kickstarter, Scorn has provided me with an experience not quite common to a lot of other games, and while the puzzles are initially challenging, once you see the pattern it would never be too long until it's a thing of a past and you head out to discover more terrifying but gorgeous scenery.As other subhumans find alarming distaste to this title with their poor and often low quality standards for video games as they purchase the next "battle pass" and wonder why greedy corporations continue to exploit them and their vulnerabilities, being the "whales" they typically are, I am still proud and happy to at least witness the product that the developers have managed to bring on and forth to present, a gift still brewing through significant time at which several points many thought it would never come to a release.I have, at least by personal experience have enjoyed Scorn, and if you like games that encourage exploration and discovery such as Myst though add with a little form of combat, I am certain you would not mind taking a gander at this alien world, witnessing a completely different and bizarre kind of past civilization.

_childDocuments_.review: This game genuinely unsettles me it in a way unlike other games. I have to take breaks. It has a way of sneaking up on you and dropping you in over your head. It's like the game whispers to your subconscious, conjuring unfamiliar feelings of visceral and cosmic existential dread from the most primal nodes of your being. I haven't encountered many games that can stir the estranged fear and spiritual terror of a bad trip but this one really nailed that. I can only play in short sessions before the fear gets too thick. I see why they called it "scorn". This "game" takes you to a place that you will deeply and completely scorn from the core of your being.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing art direction, bad combat, extremely short for the price. Took a grand total of 5 hours to complete and the only achievement I'm missing at the moment is keeping the little egg baby in the beginning alive instead of killing it. If you have game pass then play it on there or wait for a heavily discounted sale. The gameplay mostly consists of puzzle solving. I would say there is little to no exploration here since every room is related to a puzzle in some way, shape or form. There's nothing to really find beyond the next piece of the puzzle to continue. The combat being bad is forgivable to me since most enemies will just walk to a point where they'll despawn, for the most part. There are a few enemies that have to be killed, but they're few and far between. The biggest disappointment is the lack of environmental storytelling. There's nothing to explain what this society was really like before all the corruption. Only real thing that was ever explained was probably the following:  The society itself might not have been all that nice or benevolent either given the nature of some of these machines and the way they might be piloted or interacted with.These are my thoughts. Buy it if you really don't care about the story and just want an artsy game to play solo or with some friends.TL;DR Not worth the 40 USD for the game, imo. Wait for a sale or get gamepass. Art direction slaps, puzzles are alright, combat sucks. It's an interactive art piece.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is not a game for everyone. It is best enjoyed by people that can get lost in artwork, love to walk down the paths of "what ifs" and are not uncomfortable with unanswered questions.I am the kind of person that gets annoyed with art where the author's main message is "It is what you think it is" because I consider it lazy. I didn't feel annoyed with Scorn in that respect - there are plenty of ideas woven together for the player to grasp on to and play around with .All of that being said, I completely understand why many people are underwhelmed with this game after 5+ years of waiting. It is quite short for a game being sold for 40€ (not to mention whatever amounts were pledged in the kickstarter).As a side note, the game's graphics are so incredibly detailed that I need a new pair of eyes to be able to take it all in :')

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but I found the whole experience annoying. While the visuals are impressive and great to look at, after a while I found that they actually obstruct the gameplay, as they hinder navigation and orientation. It took me 1.5 hours to solve the first act because I couldn't find the wall-nubbin to finish the puzzle and found myself pacing back and forth between corridors. Some of the puzzles require a lot of backtracking, so you better try to remember which blood-soaked tentacle you took a left turn at. Had this been a walking simulator (which for the first act, it really is) I would have been happy; I could have overlooked the bland puzzeling, but then the game introduced enemies and combat, which made the whole experience even worse. What a waste, I don't think I will finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospherically, visually and sound-wise, Scorn really does everything right. A strong stomach would be recommended, because the character goes through a lot in the course of the game that can only be described as sadistic torture in the real world.I had a hard time evaluating the technical aspects of the game, because there are some weaknesses here. For example, it was very often difficult for me to solve the puzzles without help from the Internet. Absolutely nothing is explained to you in the game, you are faced with a puzzle and have to find out what you have to do in the first place. There is also a lack of variety in the number of enemy types in the game. There are only 5 different enemy types (with the final boss) in the whole game (4 of them are similar in appearance and behavior almost like one egg to the other). Finally, some game points are not perfectly set, sometimes you have to completely repeat a few minutes of a level after the death of the character.My conclusion: Unfortunately, Scorn is not enough to win the top title. Nevertheless, especially because of the dense atmosphere, despite some shortcomings, there is also counterplay value after the first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr I paid 45 bucks for a decent artbook.As a game, SCORN is atrocious.The puzzles are simple, relying more on hidden elements than actual logic; it hides things from you, and pretends it's clever for making you run around for no reason until you find the slightly glowier thing that you need to press. Or outright hiding half the interface from you, in one memorable case about halfway through.The combat is even worse: you receive a weapon with infinite ammo early on, however it's incredibly short ranged and slow to recharge. This wouldn't necessarily be a problem, if you didn't get stuck on every 1-inch bump in the environment while trying to doge enemies which are all ranged. This actually gets worse once you find a ranged weapon; it takes a fair while to aim, which again would be bearable, if not for the incredible limitations on ammo, and the fact that it does very little damage over the melee weapon.Then you run into charging enemies which only spawn in areas designed to prevent you from dodging.Which leads us to the next point: once one of these enemies kills you (assuming your save doesn't get bugged and sets you back an entire chapter), you have to replay 10 to 15 minutes just to get a chance at facing them again, until you find a way to get them stuck on the environment. I can only assume this was supposed to build tension by convincing you to run away from danger, however the only result it has in practice is frustration; the devs seem to have convinced themselves that annoying their players and wasting their time qualifies as both challenge and longevity, displaying the same impressive disconnect from reality and logic they show in the footnotes for the artbook.Story-wise... there is very little. You're some variety of worker drone that should be doing something for some eldritch purpose, but end up breaking it and causing something of an apocalypse, but that's about where it ends. The artbook hints at a more coherent story that existed at some point during development, however it seems to have been completely eradicated. Despite the claims of environmental storytelling, footnotes proudly claim that bits have been added without regard to whether they serve a purpose, and that interpretation being left up to the player is a valid form of expression.This is true. It also directly contradicts the purpose of environmental storytelling. If you're leaving it up to the player, you're not telling anything, you're letting the player make up their own mind - it's a copout, and a rather pathetic one that takes the burden entirely off your shoulders but still lets you claim that the philistines just don't get it.Now, to not be entirely negative, as the other reviews have pointed out, the art is indeed gorgeous. No, it's not photorealistic, it's not the highest resolution you'll ever see, glitches abound, but it's the closest you'll ever get to running around a Space Jockey ship, and if that's your jam, I actually recommend buying the deluxe edition, and using cheat engine to make the combat bearable.

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing and just what I was waiting for. The attention to detail and artwork is really awe inspiring and is what drew my interest in the first place. The themes in this game, heavy  H.R Giger inspiration, are really what makes it shine. Well worth the wait. Can't say I don't want more, but that's true with most things that are great.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: BEAUTIFUL SOUND DESIGN, GRAPHICS, MUSIC, ANIMATIONS, very well made puzzles, everything about this game feels extremely cinematic, amazing map and game design, visuals are breath taking cons: it's a short game, combat is like silent hill, choosing your fights wisely and kiting / running a lot from enemies that'll ruin your day, you'll be walking and running a lot, the start is very slow and can confuse you if you're not in a puzzle solving mood, it does get better and harder, there is NO HAND HOLDING, if you're truely getting fustrated at something you can't solve, just google it, not everyone is perfect, not everyone wants to stay fustrated on one puzzle 24/7conclusion: I recommend this game if you're in it for the pros, for some, the cons might strongly out weigh the pros, but if you're into suspense after the boring beginning , and into that silent hill / puzzle solving and mapping mind set with crazy sounds , animations, and visuals, this is for you, the price does kind of out weigh the length of the game though, if they ever add custom map and puzzle support, that would be amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Man do I have some mixed feelings about this game.First off, the game is graphically beautiful. It has an absolutely amazing sound design, and it has a huge amount of visual only lore to unpack, which is phenomenal. the world design is fantastic, piecing together things that may have happened and interpret. However, that is kind of where it ends for me. Right out the gate, the game gives you an illusion of choice. It is the only choice that leads to any sort of different outcome in the game. This gives the impression that throughout the game if you think a little harder, give some thought into what you are doing, it may change the overall tone and story of the game. You're then introduced to how the weapons work in the game, and thus concludes the tutorial. Placing that 'moral' choice in the game in the first place is probably the first turn that something went wrong with development. You then go forth into the game, and utilize the weapons to defeat some skin/meat creatures that spit at you. With having a pretty bad autosave only system, this can lead to you running through long sections of the game repeating all of the things you just did, or waiting for things to move, especially if you had an autosave where you were only one hit away. You continue going downwards into the depths, still killing or avoiding monsters, you finally hit the bottom. No moral choices have been made to this point, and several somewhat large events have occurred to the visual story, leading me at least to believe that there are choices in this game. Is there a different outcome if I ignored the skin monsters? is it possible for me to ride the elevator without making the big friend fella upset? Unfortunately, no. There are no further choices in the game.  I cannot honestly recommend this game unless it was $15 or less. Unfortunately, the genuinely poor combat, bad save system, illusions of something more grandiose, cannot express enough that this game just isn't where it should have been. Especially with budgets saved on things like voice acting, the shortfalls of this game to me are too numerous to recommend it in good faith.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a shame that I didn’t like this game as much as I wanted to. Five years of waiting and this is where we get off. Starting with some positives, the atmosphere is beautifully sickening. The H. R. Giver inspiration is very clear, and I get flashbacks of the original Alien movie and Darkseed as I walk through the derelict structures of this world. And the puzzles are a decent brain tickler, though I will admit they’re a bit more obtuse than most would like; prepare to be stuck on the very first puzzle for a while if you suck at sliding puzzles.However, what made me give up on this game was the combat. Yes, I know this game isn’t trying to be the next Doom Eternal or Ultrakill, but there is a bit too much fighting uncooked chicken monsters to make the experience feel worth it. You deal pitiful damage while the monsters can smack a fair bit of health off of you with ease, and some seem to be better at leading their shots than you’d think. Couple that with very rare health refill points and the fact you don’t get a ranged weapon until at least an hour or so in, and you have an unenjoyable mess. Again, I know combat is not the focus of this game, and I’m glad we have a game like this where you can fight back instead of being forced to run away and hide, but still… I’ll probably give this game another chance eventually, but not while it costs $40. If you’re curious about this game, I suggest waiting for it to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a fever dream, in all the best ways. It is not like any other game I've ever played. It's more like a visual novel than anything else. I could have torn through it in probably half the time, but I spent an inordinate amount of playtime just exploring and admiring the environment and the soundtrack.The gorgeous graphics that are straight out of Giger's wildest imaginings. Every level is a different flavor of fresh nightmare hellscape. No procedural rendering here. Throbbing, oozing, pulsating, disturbing and revolting- this has it all. The final level was strangely beautiful, in an utterly alien way. It was terrifying without cheap jump scares and overdramatic gore. There is gore, but it's more flavor than anything else. Storywise, I can't say too much without serious spoilers, but it is engaging and leaves you wondering. The ending was much more moving than something I would have expected from this genre of game. The puzzles are challenging without causing spontaneous rage-quitting. Explore everything thoroughly, take your time, and you'll get most of them with little trouble. And there's always walk-throughs. Combat is avoidable with a few exceptions, and it's more about learning the patterns and behaviors of enemies than shooting everything that moves. Most of the time, running away and hiding in a convenient corner solves your issue.If you're looking for a DOOM clone, or a hack n'slash gore fest, this isn't it. A lot of folks have panned this as a glorified walking simulator. Which it is- a walking simulator through one of the most compelling alien nightmares I've seen in a long time. It's contemplative, disturbing, and leaves you wondering what the hell you've just played.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more like Yume Nikki and MYST than it is DOOM. I'm seeing a lot of complaints about "mundanity" but i found the pacing to be just right. If you like unveiling intensely detailed and well-planned environments, you'll eat this right up. The combat is another point that many have complained about. Yes you can avoid enemies, yes it's super basic, but In my opinion, Scorn's combat couldn't be anything other than this—these are its defining traits. It still hits the survival horror sweet spot of resource scarcity, risk management and presentational impact. The feedback sounds and effects especially are great.On the topic of price—if you think $36USD is too much for a game of this quality just because it isn't x hours long, you can go f yourself.Scorn is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is more of an art piece than a game.  The first person puzzle game mechanics are mostly there to pace the exploration of the intense, brooding, biomechanical environment that has been crafted.Scorn is definitely a horror game, if you don't have a high threshold for blood and guts, buy something else.There are no missions, or quests, not a word of dialog or a scrap of writing about the place, no plot to speak of, only your desire to explore this mysterious, disturbing and bleak world being the only motivation. I always wanted to see what was around the next bend, behind the next door, what amazing vista would rise out of the fog.There is a small amount of combat and most of that is optional.  Which is good because the gun play is weak.  This is not a first person shooter in the vein of half-life, more like a stalker simulator.   This is my new headcannon : Scorn is set on a combine world and we're playing as the local equivalent of a stalker.The graphics are great, I can tell a lot of work want into making this game, there is a not a flat surface to be found. I have a nasty feeling it will look dated very quickly.   The ambient music adds to the mood without distracting from it and the sound effects emphasise the icky biological nature of the setting.  I recommended Scorn, but maybe wait for a sale, unless your a big fan of Geiger's art.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzles this is the game for you. I refunded it after about an hour and found out shortly after that it was the right choice for me as the game takes a little over 2 hours to fully complete and there is already a complete run on youtube so I could see the ending. _childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous nightmare. Undeniable Giger and Beksińki influences, which I very much appretiated, as a big fan of both. I’ve seen people ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the game, but noone could give an actual good enough reason, only that Scorn is boring. And it might be, if what you’re looking for is another Doom clone with lots of action in expense of world building and immersion. I like Doom, but every single one of the games in the franchise is mad overrated and I’ll hardly ever play any of them again. Scorn on the other hand offers a detailed, beautiful world that sucks you in and doesn’t let go until you reach the very end. I know this, because I’ve finished the game twice now. First time when I was visiting my friend and we went through it in one go, playing for about 6-7 hours because it’s just that good. And then I came home and bought the game for myself, because I wanted to replay it after some time. After the second playthrough, I can confidently say that this is my favorite game I’ve ever played and one of the most underrated/overhated titles out there. Haven’t seen the marketing for it, but from all the crybabies who go to various playthroughs on yt crying how boring the game is, I assume they expected another action-packed AAA title.If you’re a fan of Giger and Beksińki and can appretiate a great atmospheric puzzle game, this is a title you should not miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Well ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this game nightmare fuel. Actually for me it was gorgeous alien world. I found myself taking the time to admire all the artwork via the game. The puzzles weren't hard by any stretch but this is something different in the gaming world. I'm super picky and more so go for survival games such as subnautica but those are few and far between but once in a while something like this shows up and blows my mind. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most gory and beautiful games I´ve played.The ambient in this game is simply breathtaking and stunning.Everytime you progress through a puzzle feels awesome and walking through this "living" world does not get boring. But be aware, that this is not a shooter or a fast paced game. You progress slowly and enemies can become frustrating. Most of the time you are low on ammo and health so be careful.I did not encounter any gamebreaking bugs and overall the gameplay and the performance feels polished.The last enemy you encounter will become very frustrating if you don´t get the fight.Overall, this was a great experience.If you are not sure about the game, wait for a discount, since the price is too high in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A game like no other. A game where all the puzzles make sense and the end result is inexplicable on so many levels. A visceral experience. The art direction and attention to detail are top-notch. I love a game which doesn't hold your hand, and this one is up there, as you have to figure out everything on your own. No spoken dialogue, no prompts. I see people who are trashing the combat. Yeah, it's no Call of Duty, sorry guys. Your character is slow to aim and slow to reload. Ammo and health are sparse. Still, the combat is serviceable, in my opinion. After all, it's not the main focus of this game.Is the game perfect? Probably not. But it is worthwhile? Yes. At the very least, it got me to write a review, something which can't be said for most of the games I play. The pacing suffers a little bit at times, but it is a short game, so it's not a huge issue. There is no map or any mechanism which shows you where to go and what to do. In the age of objective markers, Witcher Senses and Ubisoft towers, this can be considered a bad thing. You may get lost sometimes. You will be unsure how to progress sometimes. If you welcome this kind of challenge, then this game is for you.tl;dr: I recommend Scorn, if your cup of tea is a unique game with lots of gore and disturbing imagery. It's rather short and slow-paced, but worth your attention. If you're interested, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I will always strongly recommend games that are a visual feast that get unneeded negative reviews for being "short" or not being much for game play because some how people though it was going to be more?! To name a few Silt, Papertura, and a current one Stray. Where its clear what you are getting by the videos you see. Hell even a game like stray where some parts overstay there welcome at least its controls nice, feels nice, and things felt fare.  But for Scorn I don't understand the good reviews and I can't give this a good review on visuals alone because I don't and everything but the visuals feels horrible.But I can't I just can't recommend this game. The Combat: The combat is so sluggish, slow, infuriating, just down right bad and feels bad. I either tried avoiding everything or dying because without spoilers though they thought it was fun to throw a Charger. spitter, and crawler all in the same room. Oh did I mention if the enemy shoots they have god like tracking so YOU WILL GET HIT EVERY TIME!!! Oh you get a gun? Well unless you STAND STILL which if you played this game is not an option in combat and the reticle takes forever to get small for precise aiming. Oh and you think getting a gun will make fights easier? Enjoy the 12 shots you will waste on the next 2 enemies you run into. Then you have to go back to using the THRUSTMASTER 5000 that can only attack 2 times and then has a 5 second cool down. You want to juke the enemies? Not gonna happen your taking a hit. Oh don't worry if the enemies take off 1 or 2 bars per hit you can heal right? Yeah enjoy the 4 heals and hope you never get hit again or you are doing that over again! Again the trailers make the combat look somewhat decent or good but let me say its way way worse and feels worse then it looks. Oh I almost forgot! Say the enemy needs one JUST one more shot to kill but you nee to reload. ENJOY RELOADING EVERY SHOT THAT YOU CAN"T CANCEL!!!! You have to sit there and watch your dude slllllowly put each bullet slowing you to a walk meaning you will take damage...........GOD THIS COMBAT IS THE WORST I HAVE EVER PLAYED!The puzzles: ♥♥♥♥.....they all over stay their  welcome like the VERY FIRST one takes an unseeded amount of effort and should have been a warning sign. Later in the game you have  a 3 part puzzle where you rotate they cylinders shaped in like a diamond formation. The typical move this one and it rotates that one so you have to sync them up so when you finally rotate them all its syncs, easy enough right? WELL the last one I just about wanted to quite until I BY MISTAKE selected the TOP cylinder. Want to know how? Well on all the others I moves around selecting left and right like no problem. Then they introduced the top one I can move left.....right....up cant move up I guess I have to move that one by moving others.....NOPE i had to keep selecting left or right till the TOP was highlighted. But I can't even explain that there was even an extra bit of that where you are sitting there saying WELL I did the puzzle why is it not complete?! It's still hard to explain how boring and unneeded these puzzles are to pad out the game. None felt good to complete, they just like the combat all feel bad and I feel bad even after completing them.The Visuals: What can't I say about them? They are a masterpiece and I can't imagine the time and effort put into making them. If you are a fan of body horror or HR Giger you will love everything you look at. BUT THIS DOESN'T make up for a game that feels bad in every other way!Like I said most visually beautiful games though "lacking" still feel good to play. This game at every moment does NOT feel good to play and feel like a chore. Watch someone play it and save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn, at its core, is a challenging game. Not necessarily in terms of puzzle complexity or combat difficulty, but challenging as in its presentation and its unforgiving world. The entire game is bleak and, honestly, self-destructive. It doesn't feel like Scorn is trying to win you over with flashy combat and satisfying gunplay, in fact it feels as if it is actively trying to deter people who aren't a good fit for its style, content, and narrative.This is all part of the appeal. Scorn is brutal and honest, matter-of-fact in its uncaring presentation of an alien nightmare. There are no one-liners, no tacky dialogue, and no comedic relief. The things Scorn asks you to do will most certainly make you feel like you shouldn't be doing them, but manhandles you into doing them anyway. It contains some of the most grotesque imagery I can ever recall seeing in a video game but does so in a way that doesn't feel over the top, on the contrary it feels grounded in the bizarre and grimy setting.While Scorn won't appeal to all, if you appreciate video games as an art and don't mind the first half of the game being relatively slow-paced compared to the second, this game will not disappoint. The atmosphere is entirely unique and the setting is unrivaled in beauty and disgust.While I think the game is great as-is, I think if Scorn were to have a VR release as close to the original intent as possible, it would be a truly groundbreaking piece of content, however perhaps too intense for most people to complete due to imagery and oppressive atmosphere. Also, if anyone involved with making a new Quake game is reading this, please get these guys to help you. Almost every environment here would fit right in with Quake's universe and I couldn't stop seeing parallels the whole time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous... and creepy. Everything is perfect from a design standpoint. There is less than 8 hours of content however and a very inconclusive ending. IMHO this game we waited so long for wasn't, and probably never will be finished.If it were longer perhaps i could recommend, but as it stands it simply isn't worth the investment. Huge bummer since i waited years for this one :(
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, beautiful, disturbing, scary...Scorn was worth the wait. Most of the time you spend walking and solving puzzles, but this is art imo, so i personally don't mind. Game takes you through nightmarish, yet beautiful landscapes and biotechnological alien environments. Accompanied by eerie ambient music and amazing sound/scene transitions, this game takes you straight into H.R. Giger's dreams. Awesome tribute to one of greatest artists of all times, may he rests in peace.Having limited ammo and health cells kinda made me hide and try to evade hostile bioforms as much as possible, rather than shoot everything that moves, which imo adds even more into scary atmosphere the game already provides. One thing i found as a con was, that their pathing was kinda easy to predict, but sometimes also found myself ambushed out of nowhere... Can't remember one jumpscare throughout the entire playthrough, which i appreciate a lot. It takes a lot to scare someone without such cheap tricks, and i think this game has all of it. I just wish there was more of this.I recommend to everyone, who likes Aliens/Prometheus franchise, body horror, Lovecraftian themes, gore, mixed with beautiful graphics and music and amazing visionary design.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true work of art. The foley artists and the artistic artists really went all out here.The only thing I don't like is not being able to have separate sound options. It would be nice to have music at lower volume to not take away from the atmosphere. This and some other games like Soma, Callisto Protocol, and Amnesia should IMO be mandatory study for horror visuals and study atmosphere settings.The game does make you wonder. Are you the same person throughout? Just another random soul coming awake and trying to find their way?My interpretation is something whatever happened and it is clearly a post-apocalyptic setting. You are some equivalent of a troubleshooting tool that is turned on to see one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hell of a damn ♥♥♥♥ show.Only real valid complaint with the game is the awful combat. Enemies need at least a third of their health removed. Otherwise game is pretty nice visual experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such a beautiful passion project of the team behind it to pay homage to artist H.R. Giger. I have been excited for it since it was first announced back in 2014 following Giger's passing.The game has no dialogue or text, and the story is entirely ambiguous to the point even the achievements have no names, really builds on the aspect of personal interpretation when it comes to story telling. Horrifically gory and brutal, this game is a true work of art that requires a strong stomach to progress through, and a decent IQ for it's puzzles due to the ambiguity of their nature.If you have problems with controversial topics revolving around infantile loss, deformations, torture, ect. I would suggest not playing this, but if you are strong willed, please play it, it is a disgusting work of beauty.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a visually stunning game that draws inspiration from the works of H.R. Giger. The bio-mechanical graphics are beautiful and the game's setting and mood effectively immerse the player in its world. The soundscape also fits the tone of the game nicely. However, the game's mostly corridor-based gameplay limits the player's ability to explore the surrounding landscape, which could be improved in the next installment.One thing that could have been improved is the sound-effect design. The lack of footsteps for the main character takes away from the immersion of the game.Additionally, the game's potential for mature content, particularly sexual symbolism, was not fully realized, which i find, was a missed opportunity.Finally, the enemies in the game are generally uninteresting and lacking in detail. They look like off-white bags filled with something, and while some are placed in the level, they often spawn only after certain actions, which makes them predictable and boring. The "flesh infested" parts of the game look generic and could have been more stylized to fit in with the game's overall aesthetic.Overall i had fun exploring the world. I would recommend it to everyone that is interested in H.R.Giger and bio-mechanical designs. If you are like me, you would stand still from time to time and just stare at the graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

Giger is besides "the guy that designed the xenomorphs from Alien", or ever watched any Cronenberg movie.Moreover, criticizing the game length after 10+ years of paying 50 to 70 bucks for Call of Duty campaigns that are arguably shorter than Scorn it's absolutely disingenuous.Won't even comment about those complaining about the pace of the gameplay, as they obviously did not even bother reading the game description before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I got what I wanted from Scorn, and I am happy with it.I wanted to be immersed in biotech horror with a Geiger-esque visual theme, and I got it.  Lots of it.  I wanted weird alien (not the movie, just inhuman) experiences, and I got much more of them than I expected.  The story is wordless and hard to figure out and totally alien, but there clearly is one.  The farther you go along the more things start making sense, if an inhuman sense.  I enjoy that theme-based guessing game.  I was pleasantly surprised that it's vastly more a puzzle game than a shooter.  It was long enough for me to enjoy what it gave without getting boring.  I thought the multiple lives twist was cute.Things a player might not like:  It is not a shooter.  I think a lot of people were expecting one.  If you want combat, look elsewhere.  You are a clumsy combatant with limited ammo and life like an old-fashioned survival game.  Most of the time you're better off killing what you can't avoid, retreating, and letting everything that came running to an alarm crawl back into its hole.Scorn is not long.  It took me about 10 hours.  There are no explanations of anything, so it's possible to get lost and not know what to do next.  That happened to me once, but the game is much more linear than it looks, so only once.  The puzzles are usually not difficult.  There's always something you need to do, so it's not a walking sim, but this is definitely a game more about the experience than overcoming a challenge.  Ironically, the final boss is kind of annoying, but nowhere near invincible.Whether this game is good or bad depends on what you want.  I got vast amounts of "Wow, this is messed up" scenery and events, many I would never have predicted.  That's what I wanted when I saw the trailers, I got it, and I am happy with the game.My only personal disappointment is the ending, and I'll trade thirty seconds of "Aw, come on!" for the several minutes of "Woah, so THIS is what happened" that precedes it, even without the whole game's pleasing weirdness.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people s*ing on the game because of its combat system and length. _childDocuments_.review: There is nothing of any artistic value here. This is weird, overly phallic torture porn. The best part is the end - not because there is a good ending or anything, but because it is over.A combination of an absolutely awful checkpoint system and no manual save function make it nearly impossible to play this game in any interval that you actually want, because you definitely don't want to have to do any of this ♥♥♥♥ over. On top of that it takes forever to get through some completely unnecessary animations, many of which you already have to endure repeatedly. The minimal amount of combat that is in the game is absolutely abysmal. I was not even entirely sure that the first weapon I found was a weapon at all, because it is also a key. The inventory system is atrocious, having to open up and manually switch weapons takes forever and you cannot move while doing so. Hopefully you have the right weapon out for whatever enemy is coming up, because again you certainly don't want to die and have to do any of this ♥♥♥♥ over again. Who knows when you hit the last checkpoint. The puzzles range from being so easy that you wonder why they even bothered to being mind-numbingly infuriating. Do yourself a favor and just look up the solutions to the final ones so you can get this experience over with as fast as possible.Scorn sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Wait for a $10 sale.Atmosphere, graphics, ambiance, music - all of these are stellar. Unfortunately, the designers thought that adding frustration mechanics (combat, health, death) into this would improve it. They do not.The combat is difficult and your weapons are slow. Your ammo is limited. Your health is limited. The enemies are way too strong and it is really easy to die. And when you die, you respawn somewhere, not sure where, and you have to figure out where you are and where you are going since everything in this game is impossible to navigate a second time. You don't respawn with full health either. Prepare yourself for infinite loops of being one hit from dying, dying, and then respawning one hit from dying.Generally these sort of frustration mechanics are reserved for action games and Dark Souls. This is not the game for these mechanics. I don't want to learn how to be a combat master in Scorn. I want to be creeped out and experience the atmosphere. Pretty much ruined for me after I realized I needed to memorize enemy spawns and snipe them with headshots.Edit - Just finished the game, that final boss battle was everything I said above that I hated all wrapped up into one giant wipefest. But the ending was cool. Still wait for $10.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique (WTF) experience with a blend of Darkseed & Beksiński artstyle astonishing me constantly, questioning what I am actually doing in this game, let alone who or what I am. Gameplay consists mostly walking around and observing the environment, with mechanical puzzles slowly drawing from the depths. An out of this world 1st person shooter starts to emerge, but (luckily) never fully surfaces, as Scorn's strength is its disturbing landscape, of which you are more observer than participant. A small criticism I must add, for a game that focuses so much on visuals, it would have been much more immersive if the 'weapon' you are holding could be lowered.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be up front. This game won't be for everyone. If you want to play a game set in a bleak future inspired by the works of Giger and Beksinski AND you want to solve puzzles without any kind of help AND you want to fight strange flesh creatures with barely effective weapons then you should turn your eye to this game when it goes on sale.As a full price game Scorn falls short in a lot of areas. The combat isn't the most engaging and the puzzles aren't the most complex. The game is short. You can easily complete it in around 4 hours if you don't spend any time sight seeing. Where this game succeeds though is in its atmosphere, sound design, art direction, and pacing. Despite the short run time of the game it is paced incredible well. At no point did I ever feel bored or like I was engaging in repetitive tasks. Every time I felt like an area was wearing out its welcome the game shifted environments. The sound evokes a feeling of uneasiness and desolation that truly makes you feel alone in this strange world. The art direction aids in this feeling by painting everything in muted organic tones. All of this together makes the game feel incredibly atmospheric in an unsettling way.I'll admit that you have to be in a certain mood, appreciate a certain aesthetic, and like certain games to be into this one though. I just happen to tick all those boxes so I was destined to like this game. During the last hour or so I thought out loud, "I don't know if I can recommend this. If I look at this game outside of my own perspective it really doesn't offer a whole lot.". So I struggled with myself, when I'm done will I recommend this or not? The answer is that I give a very begrudging and conditional recommendation that hinges on a great many factors.I recommend this game if you're a fan of gory body horror, don't mind walking, like solving tasks with no instruction, don't mind fiddling with clunky combat, atmospheric ambient music, and a feeling of desolation. I don't recommend this game if you don't check every one of those boxes. Simply put there isn't much here and trying to sell this game for $40 is outrageous. If you're thinking you want this try the Xbox Game Pass or wait for a sale for this game to be around $5 or $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is less a game and more an interactive walking experience through nightmarish and alien vistas that offer no explanation to the player. While the game is gorgeous to look at, and even frightening in some aspects, I wouldn't say the game is scary. For half of the game you are walking around solving puzzles, and then in the second half it's more of the same, but you also have to fight monsters sometimes.Nothing is ever explained and it's left up to the player to try and come up with some backstory for what they are seeing. There apparently is a story, but you'd have to read the graphic novel, which should never be the case. A game should be able to stand on its own. While some may say that's artistic license, I say that it's lazy storytelling. The game feels like it was created as a school project that someone else liked and demanded a game be made out of it. And it feels like that. The locale and art design came first, and a story and "game play" very much came second. The game is also very short, consisting of just two sections. The game ends where you'd think the end of Act 1 might be in a regular game. No explanation for what just happened is given. No thanks for playing. No satisfaction for whatever it is you just accomplished. Or didn't? Scorn, while visually impressive and intriguing, fails to live up to its own promise. There are no vast areas to explore. No winding paths that take you off the beaten path and into strange new areas. You follow a very linear path throughout the game, and then it's over before you know it. If you're into that sort of thing, go ahead and get it, but if you're looking for a game, then look elsewhere, because you won't find that here.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: An experience like walking through the art book of H.R. Giger. Some people here have said it was not worth the price or long wait bu I beg to differ. While It does often feel like more of an experience and less of a game in the traditional sense, with mechanics serving to break up bouts of walking then being abandoned or replace, The feeling of this world is unlike anything else I've played. I truly felt like an explorer discovering some alien civilization and combing through its decaying remains. The sights, sounds, and remaining denizens of this strange landscape and complex truly feel brought to life with a great attention to detail.To me, this is what a game has the power to do. Take a world or concept and bring it to life in a way you can interact with and speculate upon without having things spelled out or espoused to you like in a movie or novel. So While Scorn doesn't have the tightest gameplay loop or the most addictive mechanics, it is dripping with atmosphere and chock full of incredible insights into a place that very well could be real in some twisted alternate reality. I recommend giving it a go before judging it based on other's critiques.

_childDocuments_.review: This is nuts. I think this is clearly not for everyone... I saw it as a kind of modern first-person transposition of the weird, outlandish late 80s/early 90s point-and-click adventure games taking place in utterly alien and bizarre worlds. But there's also a slight "shooter" (TERM USED VERY LOOSELY) side to it.Beyond that, it's... as you'd expect from this description above... a lot of running around, trying to avoid enemies, and occasionally solving puzzles. I'm not gonna lie, a significant portion of it was more frustrating than interesting. Especially when you get effectively stuck with one hit point but you've got to make a lot more progress towards the next invisible checkpoint. I saw that lots of people describe the combat as "clunky" and janky... but it's not as bad as I thought it'd end up being after taking a short peek at other players' opinions. It's not great... but also not that bad...?There's a ton of interesting environmental and visual storytelling taking place, especially in the last chapter. The last half-hour of the game is insane and had me pick my jaw up from the floor. The world and its story just have me yearning for more. I would love to see the developers have another go at it.Now, do I think it's worth the launch price of 40€?I backed the game on Kickstarter several years ago, so I got to experience it for a mere 13€. I feel like I got WAY more than my money's worth. But I can see how Scorn would be a hard sell to some people at the full price. If you really love H.R. Giger, bizarre alien worlds, absolutely gorgeous 3D artwork, and don't mind the game being a bit more frustrating than it should... I think you should go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? Yes and No. This game is not for everyone, at times you can get lost and feel like you have been going around in circles but it has a very unique touch to it. This game is clearly an artistic one, this is not an average game, so if you don't like to have a different game in your lap don't play it. If you like the feeling of being at the game's mercy and the feeling of helplessness then this game is for you. It has a way of telling its story visually exclusively, making you feel like the protagonist. The overall story is nice but can be overshadowed by slight disappointments in the gameplay. For instance how you can miss an upgrade pretty early and be forced to replay a section to get it. Overall a great game but not for everyone, it can leave the player yearning for more and even a feeling of emptiness when you finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is both a visually disturbing and visually challenging game that really brings something different to the table. It doesn't hold your hand in any way or offer much of an explanation as to why the main character in the game finds him-/herself  is. Your own imagination has to fill out the blanks here, which perhaps makes it even more disturbing.Clearly an homage to H. R. Giger's night terror inspired drawings from the 70s, the game, as i see it, lingers on the border between computer game entertainment and art, drawing on strengths from both sides. I also recognise some of the themes in Giger's art, such as birth, death, mechanics, corruption and fear of the different. Often i find myself just looking at the screen trying to take in the details of what i see and then making up my mind about what it is I'm actually seeing. This is one of the great strengths of the game. The environment isn't created just as a backdrop, but it takes on a life of it's own, challenging the player to explore and create possible explanations as to what the function of i.e a corridor is.  It's hard for me to put a verdict on Scorn, since it is so different in so many ways. All i can say is this: Scorn isn't for everyone, but if you're interested in nightmarish landscapes, interesting architecture or just looking for a very different and artsy experience (because an experience is absolutely what it is), i think you should try Scorn out. It makes you wonder, it makes you feel and it makes you imagine things, which are very important facets of computer games, and unfortunately we don't get to see that so often anymore. At least not from most of the triple-A title companies.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10Scorn is the best interactive art exhibition of HR Giger I've found, and a contender for Beksinski, too. On those grounds alone the game is worth its admission. This is more Amnesia: a Machine for Pigs, than it is Doom. It is more Dark Souls than it is Dead Space. Fans of walking simulators and the Skedar in Perfect Dark 64 will love this game.  I only wish the game had the scope of its initial teasers-- all of the Heidegger stuff, the open world and non-linearity, the emotive and expressive protagonist character are all gone, essentially. The PC save point system seems to be broken. I was frequently lost, and seem to have taken nearly 3x as long to complete the game as most players. More time to look around and take it in.

_childDocuments_.review: In short it's exactly what I expected it to be. It's a puzzle game that draws you in and makes you uncomfortable, the closest to a Giger-esque experience as you can get, like taking a stroll inside his necronomicon, approaching all the subjects he would and more. It's dark, immersive, gruesome all while at the same time addictive to keep going back for more. I'm not one for replaying games but I am curious to see what things I have missed. The only major con is the combat, the game could've done very well without it as it's not a "fun" elements, it's just frustrating, it's the wrong kind of challenging. Honestly I would've rather have harder puzzles. Which brings me to a second "downside" but maybe not quite. It definitely could've been longer. There seems to have been some locked doors that amounted to nothing right in the very beginning that I would've very much liked to explore. DLC's would be a hard thing to request but if I could request for something from the devs and from the game would've been more to wander in. Overall, if you're a fan of the Giger aesthetic, the dark and the macabre, this is definitely a buy for all of what was mentioned, a walking "simulator" of something unsettling.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an exceptionally unique experience. I´vent suffered that much in some parts of a game since back in 2005 with Doom 3.For those who are complaining that the game is too short, I have to say that they have missed something very important and , probably, the key of the game: It´s not just one guy´s story.In the other hand, back in the time we could see some different trailers with scenes that does, t occur during this part of the game.I don´t know if I´m wrong , but maybe the studio finally decided to release the game as its first version: In two parts.If that´s not the case, anyways the experience was worth. The uncomfortableness, the lack of more movement freedom and the agony of feeling that you can die in every moment, are some of the pillars of the game experience, not a mistake in its playability.If you are looking for fast moves, blasting thousands of enemies and also  have a military arsenal of weapons, go for a classic RPG or shooter.Scorn is not that kind of game. _childDocuments_.review: A-If you love Alien (H.R. Geiger) or Lovecraft stories, I think you will enjoy this simply because of the art, sound, and ominous environment.  While the game sits mostly in the walking sim with lite adventure elements and there is some combat, the game is mostly about exploration (mostly linear) and learning the story visually.The progression of getting new tools is interesting because nothing is explained you just have to figure it out.  I liked the variety of weapons and they do get better but the main melee weapon was so satisfying to us; main complaint for it was I could never tell when it was charged and ready.  The combat is pretty clunky but if you practice you can get good at dodging and fighting.  The reloading on the other hand made me die very often; you should definitely be able to cancel such a long  animation.I am one of the ones that was very satisfied with the ending as it fits the theme extremely well and has many over/under tones.  I would've loved for this to be longer to maybe experience two more generations but maybe for other games.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write review often, so here's my take on this, since I see its getting controversial in the review section:This game   hold your hand, it does not show you any hints on solving puzzles and that is the overall vibe and theme of the game. Its like that by design, like good old games back in the day, its interesting to see the world crafted masterfully by Ebb and get immersed in it. No map, no markers, no objective, and yet it has as kind of continuity that shows you the path logically to the next area.A lot of reviewers are saying its boring or its a walking sim, this for sure is a niche game and you will probably like it because its basically as it is in the trailers, your meant to be methodical and slow in your actions because The game is very simple in its gameplay as you are mainly walking and observing the world, interacting with various objects to try and complete the puzzle. There is combat in the game, not a lot of it, it adds a sense of dread to the game, as the puzzles themselves probably wouldn't be enough for this experience, think of it as Alien Isolation but you kinda have to fight back as most of the enemies will stop you from progressing or interacting with the puzzle.A LOT of reviewers sh!t on the game because it's doing something new and unique, don't let this stop you from trying out this very immersive experience.Is the game worth full price? Tricky question, I would pay the price as I am a fan of these types of games, I got it at a -10% sale at launch and I think thats an okay price to pay for this. It took me around 5.6 hours to complete the game in one sitting start to finish. Don't want to say too much, because the whole game is worth experiencing yourself, don't watch youtube or twitch for this one, do it all yourself and trust me you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a walking sim and should be judged as such. In Scorn you will explore, solve puzzles and fight enemies. The exploration is, for me, what this game is all about and it is what took me the longest. I was fascinated by this world that is both inert and yet continues to live outside of time. The environments are extremely detailed, each element feels unique and tells its own story. To progress, you will also have to solve puzzles. Sometimes they will be quite well integrated and give information about the game world, sometimes they will seem clumsily added and remind you that you are playing a video game. There will also be combat, which I think is the least successful part of the game. The weapons are few and far between and fairly standard but their design is like the rest of the game, original. The feeling is excellent, you can feel their power. The enemies are not very varied, some are not very resistant but attack at a distance and others are the opposite. The problem is the cohabitation of the combat system in this game, which is a walking sim. All actions take time because there are animations, which is problematic when you have several enemies to deal with. If you have to reload, or change your weapon, it will take time, your character will slow down and it's guaranteed death.As it stands, the game is not perfect but can still be fixed. It will remain quite short but I recommend it for its singular beauty and its atmosphere as disturbing as it is fascinating.
