_childDocuments_.review: Usually don't write reviews but I felt like it deserved one after there are so many negative reviews based on false expectations that aren't even the developers fault. For some dumbfounding reason, there are a lot of people that thought this was gonna be a more action focused game (sometimes even close to DOOM) because the developers dared to show off a weapon in their trailers and giving it bad reviews because of it.This game is NOT a first person shooter. Nor is it a survival horror or "scary" horror game. It's an atmospheric -what some would call- "walking simulator" with puzzles and very light survival horror-like combat. It's exactly what it always tried and advertised itself to be.If you don't like those things that's fine but that doesn't mean it's a bad game and deserves a negative review solely because you can't read or because you can't handle playing a game that doesn't stimulate you every 2 seconds with combat like a CoD campaign.That being said, if you're just slightly interested in those types of games and looking for an incredibly atmospheric trip into an amazingly crafted hellish Giger-inspired (mixed with good amounts of body horror) world with stunning visuals and sound design, that is unlike anything else, this game is worth checking out. Though be aware that this game is only around 5 hours average in playtime without much replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a nightmarish and grotesque gem. It's dark, violent, cruel and constantly disturbing. But it's also a beautiful work of art, a technical prowess and an artistic marvel.A unique experience, and despite its shortcomings (lots of cut content, short length), i highly recommend it. But not to the faint of heart...
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is freaking beautiful in a gore filled twisted way. The design of the environment seems like it's out of a Aliens movie. The story is basically a perfect example of the human experience and it's quite thought provoking. The game play doesn't favor combat, instead it favors patience and observation so you can pick up on the behaviors of the creatures that can attack you, avoiding combat and sneaking behind enemies is a viable strategy. I played through the game 2 times, one cautiously taking my time and one killing everything I could. The puzzles are good except for 2 that i don't bother memorizing and just spam until i get them solved.  Overall this won't get close to AAA game in scope or length, but it is well polished (no crashes or glitches) and unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: What in the Lovecraftian hell did I just play? Holy smokes. The overall design provides little instruction or in-game training as to what to do next, but somehow, that doesn't matter. As abstract as the concepts to progression are, they still make sense (albeit after a touch of struggle here and there). That, in and of itself, is quite the feat. The blood, guts, and gore are gross as I've ever seen -- KUDOS! This developer really had an aesthetic they were going for here, and they flipping nailed it. The sound design and soundtrack really complement that aesthetic as well. I look forward to checking out other offerings from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely beautiful. I never thought I'd see a silent film version of a game before. But this game just blew me away. The art style is gorgeous. The atmosphere is dark and horrifying. There's this endless feeling of hopelessness. As if the world is long dead and you were just born from the remains of it. The symbolism is amazing as well. Very subtle at first but becomes more obvious right at the end. But the major themes of child-birth, sex, and other forms of conception are always shown throughout the game. It had me constantly wondering what was wrong with this world. What happened? What caused all of this to happen? What was it like before? There's millions of questions going through my head the entire time and none of them are answered. And I love it for that. While I'd usually find it lazy. I find it done extremely tastefully. No explanation is given ever. And rarely do I see a piece of media that give you nothing. And continues giving nothing the entire way through. It allows people to have purely their own interpretation. PLAY THIS GAME. PLEASE
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it on sale, it was way to short, about 5 hours. This length is fine for some games, but those games have replayability which this has none of. no collectibles, extra modes, challenges. Nothing you do in the game impacts the ending, which is fine but for such a short game multiple endings would have been nice. Combat is clunky like a lot of horror games, which is a plus. Graphics are fantastic, but honestly its a game that you watch someone play once and thats it. There not really a reason to play it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of crazy to think that I backed Scorn five whole years ago. The project at that point was already two years deep in development, and the financing of the community as well as further funding by Microsoft gave this game a face lift which allowed it to stand the test of time, which many games fail to survive after such long and arduous development times.The developers said years ago that they wanted to develop the game in radio silence and offer minimal material to market the game in order to manage hype and allow people to delve into the final result for what it was, rather than as the product of self-maintained expectations. I believe that when approached from that angle, Scorn is a great, if stilted experience with some flaws inherent to the game it wants to be and others which are unbecoming of this genre.On the positive site, Scorn is a positively beautiful game to look at; seven years of development gave the developers ample time to create some genuinely inspired visuals, intensely detailed and uncompromisingly graphic when it needs to be. As far as exploration heavy games go, Scorn manages to present an atmosphere and a world which I found truly mesmerizing from start to finish. Interestingly, the early game footage looked quite different, and because of the lack of material present between 2017 and 2022, it's hard to tell whether those changes are the result of graphical enhancements, an overhaul of the art direction, or merely an intended refining of the art to grow closer to the initial vision. The 2017 version, which can be seen on the KS campaign and in the alpha demo, was drier, more sterile, and much sharper; this 2022 version is softer, glistening, humid with repulsive detail.Scorn sells itself purely on the visuals. The puzzles, although not necessarily unique, offer novelty in the confusion of the space which surrounds them and rarely had me genuinely stuck, and are primarily here to give the player a more involved vehicle to navigate a world which is in of itself fascinating. Where the game in my opinion shines is that the universe it creates and the progression of the story, for lack of a conventional narrative, can be appreciated equally for its metaphorical musings as for its raw, chaotic, matter-of-fact presentation.On the negative side, Scorn's combat feels unnecessary in great parts, often forced onto the player in a way which is unsatisfying, and in the scant few occasions where one must absolutely engage with it, the mechanics leave to be desired. It's not uncommon at all for horror games to have "deliberately bad" combat, although the term can be misleading; the issue with Scorn is not so much that the fights feel like they were made bad on purpose and more that the overall feel of the combat is simply off. It wants to be slow, and it is slow, but not in a way that feels methodical or calculated. It simply feels sluggish and unresponsive. There's obviously a desire to bring the game closer to the likes of survival horrors with scarce resources and punishing damage, but it is in my opinion the part which falls farthest from its intention.The subject of the game's length is likely going to be a hot topic. At 40 dollars, the game's five to six hours of play time at a leisurely pace can be hard to justify. Having backed the game years ago for half of that amount, it's definitely less of a concern; for the price of a xbox game pass subscription, it's a steal. I think anyone who's in love with this sort of aesthetic should buy the game at this amount anyhow and appreciate the fact that games take a long time to make and cannot always be put out in a handful of years through sheer crunch of an increasingly weak workforce.I would not recommend Scorn to anyone who's looking for a shooter, an action game, or generally a game with decent combat. I would recommend it for people who are in for the exploration, the visuals, and the trip of it all. It definitely could use some QOL additions in potential updates, in a similar vein to how SOMA later included modes to remove its enemies. The combat could be fixed, but an easier solution would be for the devs to simply add an option to trivialize it, as its inclusion is already trivial to the purpose of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a highly atmospheric puzzle horror game that took almost 9 years to develop. After waiting several years, I can say that it met my expectations. It is definitely not for everybody, but it is still a very impressive project that deserves every ounce of recognition it is getting. If you go into it with the right expectations, it will not disappoint.Pros:-Environment speaks for itself.-Sound design is incredible.-Soundtrack is just perfect. Not too much, not too little.-Graphics are fantastic.-Puzzles are fun and creative.-Animations are very polished and realistic.-UI and gameplay are very simple and minimal, which is perfect for this type of game.-Highly immersive.-Littered with scary and disturbing moments.-Impressively optimized. It is not a game that will fry your PC.-Very artistic visually and story-wise.Cons:-There are some current glitches that can be game-breaking. I experienced one that prevented me from proceeding through Act V, which forced me to redo 45 minutes of a level I just did. From what I have heard, this is not the only issue.-Ending is a bit disappointing. It's not bad, but it did not leave me satisfied.-It is overpriced. If you take your time in observing the environment, you will get around 6 hours of gameplay. For $40, that isn't great.Many people complain that the game is disappointing because it did not live up to their expectations. It is not a first person shooter. It is a puzzle walking simulator with some combat. The goal of the game is not to be like COD set in Giger's nightmare. The goal of the game is to immerse the player as much as possible into its world, and it achieves this. The developers put a lot of care and love into making it as realistic as possible so that the players can enjoy the environment and piece together the story.Another thing people complain about is the storytelling. This game has no dialogue or writing, as it is heavily reliant on its environment. People who complete the game in 3 hours simply did not take the time to see what happened to the world, so they finished it confused and disappointed. If you pause to walk around and see the world the developers want you to see, you will be able to discover the story more and more. Lastly, people complain about the combat. Scorn has 4 varieties of weapons: a melee weapon, pistol, shotgun, and grenade launcher. What Scorn does differently, however, is it keeps the combat simple. You are not going to find upgrades to any of the weapons, and there are no iron sights. This is because you shouldn't rely on weapons entirely to get out of situations. In the situation where you absolutely, shooting is still smooth and very manageable. I think the devs were, again, going for realism here.Overall, Scorn is a game that is unlike anything I have seen or played. On the surface level, it is simple and easy to play through. On a story level, it is complicated and unique. If you are considering buying it, wait for a sale. Once you get it, set your expectations right. Scorn is not a shooter; it is a puzzle walking simulator. It will not serve you the story on a silver platter, either. The developers carefully crafted the world for the player to explore and discover its past, not breeze through. If you appreciate the love and thought put into this game and play it for the purpose of experiencing the world rather than completing it, you will enjoy it much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game all the way up its dramatic end and then reading through several of the other reviews of this game, I think it is safe to say that we all have pretty much the same opinion about it. The game was obviously made more in favor of the 'visual aspects' than the game play itself, and I am not explicitly referring the combat aspects so many others have complained about.I'll start with the good things first. ------Throughout the game there are a nice variety of unique and interesting puzzles the player must traverse in order to move the story forward. Most of the puzzles themselves are very clever and force you to stop and think about their answers, Excellent brain fodder for people who enjoy a slight challenge... without being stuck for hours.Alongside the puzzles there are the visuals, the main selling point of the game. These are, to say the least... phenomenal. The atmosphere driven story telling was what got me to purchase this game alone- despite the many complaints and warnings about game play. While I believe that the price of $40 is a bit much for a game this short (especially for its pretty limited desire of replay-ability), it is definitely a worthy purchase for those who enjoy digging deep into environmental clues and world driven storytelling to find a deeper meaning behind what is being directly presented.Now with the bad stuff. ------Since I've seen a large majority of comments complain about the combat aspect, I will try to look at it from a different perspective so I am not repeating the same thing others have said countless times over and over.The main issue with the combat in this game according to others is that it is 'clunky' or 'unfair' on several occasions, exclaiming that enemies tend to swarm you in specific acts in ways that are impossible to avoid or fight against. While I certainly found this to be true at the beginning, I began to quickly realize that there was another option. To easily get through the combat sections of this game without taking unneeded damage and dying many agonizing times: All you have to do is wait.Eventually the enemies will despawn without ever attacking you and there will pretty much be no need for combat at all once you get used to movement patterns.This was an intentional storytelling/game play device the developers were trying to push that was grossly overlooked by a majority of the people that left negative reviews. Once I began to use this method the game lost most of its irritating behavior regarding combat.This did not however, fix the really big issue I have with this game, the one that overshadows almost everything else: The respawn mechanic.The game autosaves without alerting the player in any way, at very annoying and inconvenient places. If you are unfortunate enough to be low on health and reach one of these autosaves with only one hit left, you are pretty much just out of luck in specific areas. You will be swarmed and overwhelmed before even being able to move.I got stuck at an autosave after completing a puzzle for about 20 minutes thanks to this.On a similar note, some autosaves require you to sit through small cutscenes over and over again each time you respawn, which after a while becomes irritating in of itself. This is an issue I am much more willing to overlook however.There are several issues regarding one of the only real 'fights' this game contains, but it is impossible to go over these without spoiling, so I will not mention them in great detail here.Just try not sit on low health at any given time, as it will actually soft lock you at this point if you cannot meet specific health requirements once defeating the segment. You will have to start the section over again. The same can be said about ammo usage here, you are not allowed to miss.The last negative thing to talk about is the utter lack of instruction the game gives you. While I realize this is a choice that was specifically made to help fit the theme, it caused me to spend a good 50% of the time in game running around in circles after completing a part of a puzzle, as there is zero indication of where to go afterwards to get to the next part. Sometimes the game requires you to majorly backtrack, while other parts require you to explore entirely new areas (some of which you may not have even seen being opened to begin with). This problem could be easily fixed by making interactables or newly opened paths much easier to discern. This is the only time where I believe the incredible visuals actually hurt the game, because they make progression a bit... too hard to spot.--------With all this being said:While this game definitely needs work, and is obviously not for everyone- I believe that if you give it a chance it can still be enjoyable. If you go into it knowing that it has some issues and are patient enough to sit through them, then the great storytelling, ambiance, and puzzles will out-weigh the bad. I'd still recommend this game despite its flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and I ABSOLUTELY LOVE IT. I though it was a Doom-like fps with horror, from the trailer, but actually it is super slow paces environment driven puzzle game with some shooting in it. To me it kinda short, took 3~4 hours on playthrough if didn't stucked on puzzles, but I'm still ok with that considering they put alot of heart and effort into crafting the unique environment and scenery, and its a well polished game too. It still cheaper than most other triple A games if compare the game length with them. What will you gonna expect in here? Its a H.R.Giger theme environment horror with tough puzzles in it. No narration, no monologue, no jumpscares, no reading notes. Its not flawless, I still got some problem with it, - Its 60 fps locked, I didn't suffer any framedrop but most likely happen to other general audience. - Why not entirely remove UI? Most of the time UI was non-exist but I can see all resources while looking down the body, why then show everything again on UI while holding gun? From the trailer I though I have to manually open the gun to check ammunition by that. - Not gore enough as for modern gaming, if gore is one of the selling point, hope they can push the limit further.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: If Scorn had been a solid walking simulator, I'd have liked it. But it's too linear for that, and doesn't use the environment to tell a story until the final act.If Scorn had been a solid survival horror FPS, I'd have liked it. But it's too poorly tuned and doesn't mix together different monster types and different placements to create varied encounters.If Scorn had been a solid puzzle game, I'd have liked it. Riven-but-gross! But the puzzles often aren't well integrated into the environment. There's a sliding block puzzle on level 1. C'mon!This game looks great but it's *so* onerous to play. According to the credits: one game designer and no specialist level designers, on a team of 50. Poor dude, imagine trying to advocate for design when the art team is like the whole company!
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn started off good, and fell off, over and over again.The fights are sluggish, the character clunky, the level design badly done (Not the aesthetic and feel of the environments).Frustrating, disappointing for me and not worth at all the 44$. Good job on the sound design and rare music, the game is very disgusting and have horrific elements to it. If you want an experience that is off putting, gore and have the money to do it? Go for it, if you are looking for a scary game? Pass, it's not scary and I am easily scared.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The story of a child hoping to be born. A prodigal son's hopeless attempt to ascend the entropic cycle of death, decay, and rebirth. A world in its final stages, whose architecture is anatomical. Scorn is a sadistic, and deeply disturbing existential nightmare that I was incredibly immersed in the entire way through. It gives you a lot to think about, without telling you anything. My only complaint is its really short length. I savored every gruesome detail of this game, and the imagery will stick with me for some time like a parasite. Artistically and thematically sublime. I loved its approach to story-telling, really felt like a breath of fresh air. Or I guess, a breath of pungent, fetid air.Don't be confused, this is not a shooter. It's an arthouse exploration game that's more like moving through a living version of a H.R. Giger or Zdzislaw Beksinski artwork with light gameplay. If that sounds interesting to you, then you'd definitely like Scorn.EDIT: The artbook goes into the lore in greater detail. It doesn't explain everything (the game speaks for itself), but it does shed light on some things. Worth checking it out after playing through.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A great narrative that doesn't rely on narration. This really takes your Imagination to unconquered realms. One can only guess what the beings in this universe have gone through and how they see their world and live their lifes. Fascinating and exciting. The Art department of this game was on something else than standard human nutrition and the sound design is also great. You can really hear that the machinery is made from something else than metal. Everything looks, sounds and feels outerworldly. A piece of art to walk through. If Giger's and Beksiński's minds melted into a big blob and took over the universe, this is what would become of it. A peace of Art.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: You play someone named after the title.An atmospheric light shooter, puzzle walking simulator with gorgeous scenery and unapologetically Geiger-esque gore.I don't recommend this game heavily, since it is not for a lot of people and really only a few folks will enjoy it, but it definitely was something new and different.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the bad and even the good reviews scared me off from buying the game, but the dev for Dusk said something about it on twitter so I thought I'd give it a go, and omg I'm glad I did.Let's get one thing clear, it's a horror game. Closer to SOMA than any other game I can think of. It's not a shooter. I don't know why people expected Doom because the trailers never hinted at anything like it. Atmosphere and sound design is amazing, and the biomechanical designs are genius and so well executed. Cannot recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: h1] The best walking sim...[/h1]The main thing you need to keep in mind about Scorn is that is first and foremost and artistic walking sim with combat thrown in to mix things up. To start its a nice atheistic mix of Beksinski and Giger a very gross and uneasy world lighting sound effects are insanely well done - to such an extent that any frame of your playthrough could be a promo screen shot. Another thing that i really liked was that there was zero yellow paint handholding just properly designed levels with enemy placement acting as a guide, I only got stuck once but not to such an extent that i had to look at a guide (which really says a lot for a puzzle-ish game in the modern era). With that being said the biggest rough patch this game has is it combat. Which really feels like it was either not fully implemented or rushed, there's plenty of ammo sure but there are also plenty of " bro c'mon! " moments.Either way its a nice unique game, would i ever touch it again? Maybe. I would like to see a sequel / part 2  for sure .
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I truly wish I could refund this game, a 6 hour play time is rarely worth $40, and this is not one of those times. I never really followed the development, and bought the game because of the interesting world it attempts to build rather than the gun play, so the FPS part of the game is not a letdown for me. I actually rather enjoyed the FPS aspect, even though it only lasted about 30 collective minutes.My issue with the game is the setting and your actions lead you to believe there's this grand story you can unfold and you can find out what happened in the past, only for it to actually just be a large metaphor which honestly isn't even that thought-provoking. I feel as if none of what you explore, encounter, and alter matters because instead of being explainable and contributing to world building, it just exists to further the metaphor that the devs want to illustrate. It's a shame, because the world is beautiful (and grotesque) and has so many stories to tell, but you get the story where your effort explains nothing and effectively means nothing, and neither does your $40, all because the game is designed to "send a message", or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but beautifully and meticulously crafted experience.I seem to have gotten a bit more play time out of my first time through than most, with my Steam game time sitting around 8 hours. Maybe I'm just not that good. There's a fair bit of time that was just me re-playing parts of the game due to a combination of deaths and sparse checkpoints, and an unfortunate bug(?) where I lost my progress when I loaded a previous save to re-play part of an earlier level, expecting that my current progress would be saved. Much of this re-played time was spent on elevators or watching various machinery do the same things I saw them do the last time. I got a bit frustrated but I didn't mind too much because everything in the game was so intricately detailed and clearly painstakingly created to immerse me in the experience.I haven't been this completely enveloped by a gaming experience in years. Maybe developers are getting lazy. Maybe I'm getting old. This was a breath of fresh air either way.If you're buying this as a game, wait for a sale. The dollar to hour ratio is just not there, though I do see this as a game I will spend some more time exploring in the short term, and re-playing periodically in the long term. It's mostly just a walking simulator, with some shooter and puzzle elements. The puzzles are challenging enough to incentivize you to explore your surroundings but not enough to tout as a main attraction, and the shooter elements add some suspense to the experience and keep you engaged but again, not enough to list it as a selling point. It felt a bit clunky to begin with, but I ended up feeling that the combat fit the game very nicely and I quite enjoyed the various mechanics they worked in throughout.I view buying this game more as supporting an artist whose work I appreciate. Does saying that in a Steam review make me sound a bit pretentious? Probably. This game is beautiful, in a sort of hellish, Giger-esque nightmare trip kind of way. You can tell that the devs really love this game and had a very specific vision they were working to create. Despite the critiques I have been seeing this game receive, I believe they were fairly successful in realizing that vision. In the 8 hours I spent in this game I felt things that I have never felt playing a game before, and I value that more than a big number in my time played counter. I hope to see more from this game, but I am satisfied with the experience I've had to this point.One hell of a journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a negative review.. But a video on YouTube changed my mind since i couldn't understand the meaning behind the story, and the explanation was quite interesting.However, the gameplay is still pretty boring, slow and short. I wouldn't recommend people to buy this game on full price, on sale it could be fine.The graphics are amazing, I really love the unique design, its something you don't usually see in other horror games.I guess you need to keep an open mind and theorize this game while playing it, which is something i didn't do and it ruined the experience. Overall the game isn't that bad :)
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game to come out since it was first announced several years ago. I had almost forgotten about it until it magically popped up out of nowhere with a release date. The original trailers for this game showed it as more of a biopunk fps vs the atmospheric puzzle game it really is. Still it is worth the play. It is incredibly unique and there isn’t anything like it. The visuals and atmosphere are wild. The negative reviews are from people who do not appreciate slow pace atmospheric gameplay. It reminds me of older style puzzle games and if you are an older player you will appreciate this game more than the ADHD kiddos do.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know really what just happened in this game especially the ending. If your looking for a game with good gameplay then you can look else where, if your looking for a game that's more of an experience then Scorn is a very unique one at that. I do recommend Scorn but its definitely not for most people and play it with headphones on.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I would not describe this game as fun to play or even enjoyable. However, it is absolutely compelling, beautiful, disturbing, grotesque, confusing, challenging, at times frustrating (though not too much), and awe-inspiring. I took 14 hours to beat the game because 1. I'm a dummy at puzzles and kept getting lost, and 2. The environments were so beautiful I often found myself just staring at things.It's a survival horror puzzler, so don't expect to run in guns blazing. You'll have to be patient, pay close attention to your surroundings, and use your intuition for the puzzles.Also, the ending is quite possibly one of the more bizarre things I've witnessed in my life, so kudos to Ebb Devs for that. Loved the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I had mixed feelings about the game as I was playing through it, but ultimately I would recommend the game IF you like slow-burn game play and the art-style. I wouldn't call this so much a game as it is a walkable art piece.PROS:-The art direction and world environment is simply incredible. It feels nightmarish, dreadful, and truly alien. Just exploring it is satisfying to me personally. There really isn't any other game out there like it.-Gore and body horror and very well done, feels truly gruesome and otherworldly. -Music and sound design add to the atmosphere the visuals create.-Without a HUD, the game feels very immersive .-Animations are well-done and fluid, everything feels alive around you because it mostly is.-Puzzles are somewhat challenging at times but rewarding.CONS:-The combat system is one of the worst I've ever used, and the game might have been better off without it and instead focused entirely on the puzzles.-Some areas may require replay as you learn what to do because the game does not tell you ANYTHING. You must figure out where to go and what to do on your own. I wouldn't entirely call this a con as it adds to the feeling of being in a completely alien world, but it can be frustrating.-Game feels too short and could have used more content. I would have loved to have at least some more story and explanation of the world you're in. -Ending feels abrupt and leaves it entirely to interpretation.All-in-all, I really enjoyed exploring the game and I hope more games are made with this kind of art-style and tone, except with deeper story and more compelling combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: If you purchased this hoping to indulge in a Doom - like massacre, ask for a refund.This is mostly an interactive art piece - homage to the works of H.R.Giger, Zdzisław Beksinski and Mariusz Lewandonski.If you want to immerse yourself in a world inspired by the aforementioned gentlemen's sick (and brilliant) art, then look no further.An unsettling mental horror adventure like no other...
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone. The game caters to a very niche audience. If you are expecting a FPS horror game with jumpscares and shooting you will be disappointed. Don't get me wrong, the game has combat, but it is not focused on it. This is not Doom, nor Amnesia, or the next Dead Space, this game is it's own thing. The art direction and sound design, combined with puzzles create this atmosphere with sense of dread that linger throughout the game. It is heavily influenced by Gieger and Bezinsky which drew me in in the first place, and Ebb definitely delivered and more. Being a fan of their work I was eager to jump in.The soundtrack compliments the atmosphere and art direction, and helps tie the world right in. Eerie, dystopian and ambient are the words I would use to describe it.Story is hidden in the world and you will have to rely on yourself to make it out.The game does not hold your hand, there is no tutorial, and I love it. You wake up in this brutal world and you have to rely on yourself and the world clues for solutions and answers.  You have to explore and think, which, lo and behold, requires walking and thinking, but it did not feel, at least for me, like a walking simulator because it kept me on the edge of my seat, eager to find out if I have the right solution, and I was just soaking in the scenery and art direction. As far as I've perceived there are multiple solutions to some of the puzzles so it will require multiple playthroughs if you want to get all the achievements.I've heard people say "This is just like Stray, if you take the cat out, what are you left with?", but that is the point, it is the same as saying "If you take combat out of CoD, what are you left with?" you would be playing as a war victim and I know you would't enjoy that. You can't remove the main thing and expect the game to be something that it isn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and grotesque little game. I highly recommend it if you're a fan of H.R. Giger. The combat however is rather obnoxious/poor so if you're looking for a fun shooter, you're looking at the wrong game. It's also very short, taking me only about five hours to finish it, even spending a lot of time exploring and admiring the environments.

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game since development and was very excited for what seemed to be a unique indie horror title and I normally don't post reviews about games like at all, but this one no. Just no. It masquerades itself as a very interesting indie horror title with puzzle solving and grotesque but exotic scenery. What it delivers is limited scenery (often feels repetitive), limited game mechanics (combat is a joke and the puzzles are so easy a monkey could solve them blindfolded), and ONLY 5 hours of total game time with an ending that feels half baked (devs stated at least 8-10 originally). Do not buy this game for anything above 10$. I'm currently processing a refund hoping the steam gods will hear my plea and grant me mercy for my horrible purchasing decision. If I'm forced to sit with this piece of #### in my library, please avenge me and either don't buy the game or wait for a huge sale. Rip off those devs like they ripped off us.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Reality vs. (hyped) expectations!I haven't finished the game yet, but i like it so far and i feel like i need to write something about it.Scorn might not be a perfect game, but it's a great game for a certain type of player: Those who love puzzle heavy exploration games like Myst, Obduction, The Witness and Quern - Undying Thoughts should have a lot of fun in this one. Scorn is a very slow paced puzzle and exploration game, NOT a shooter, NOT a survival horror game and it does not help you in any way solve the puzzles or find the right place to go. You have to experiment, explore and figure things out for yourself.If all this sounds good to you and you like the setting and the art style: You can buy it. You're most likely not gonna be disappointed. If you expect something like Doom, Resident Evil or jumpscare horror like Outlast or Visage: Scorn definitely is not the game you're looking for!Little update to my review: While i really like the stuff mentioned above: The very clunky combat mechanics and the intransperent save system (game doesn't tell me when or where it saves) leaves a bad after taste. It's not a bad game, especially if you enjoy exploration and the art style without constantly being interupted by endless cut scenes. But combat and save systems definitely need some improvement. It's not even challenging, it's just frustrating because it doesn't give much feedback at all.I still give it a thumbs up because i think the game is still too good to for thumbs down. I wish Steam had an option to give neutral ratings.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I would go into this more as an interactive visual novel or maybe an immersive 3D painting than a game. Its got beautiful art and atmosphere and an interesting world filled with beautiful and grotesque sights, some sometimes-challenging sometimes-not (but usually pretty fun) puzzles. Oh and some monsters that are a pain to fight (and not in a fun or good way). But not much else. There is pretty much zero context clues to what is going on/ who you are/ what happened to the world/ etc. And that isn't explained at the end. The end being rather unimpactful and disappointing on account of the complete lack of story telling or context.That being said its a pretty quick game that truly is beautiful. So if the art and atmosphere are very interesting to you and you enjoy immersing yourself in art give it a shot. If you want to play an interesting video game.... maybe skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The most Twisted, Gorey, and Disgusting body horror game. Combined with an FPS a little bit in there but it fits really well. You never feel safe in this game and always feel so isolated not seeing anyone else except the abhorred mutants created by this. Everything wants to kill you but most of them are bound to flesh piles. The style is very unique and the views you get in this game are literally out of this world. The story is not very clear but that leaves you up to your imagination.DO NOT PLAY IF YOU HAVE A WEAK STOMACHMy issues i had with it are that you can definetly get stuck if you consume too much health and ammo. Also there were mechanics that didn't really get to see a whole lot of action, such as the switching ability. But it is a short game. However if you do want this game and are not good at fps, play on Easy and conserve ammo and health. Puzzles can be very hard, even the first one is. Good luck and bring a puke bag.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game for more than a fiver and that's only if you scale your hours of fun for one money.incredibly short, buffered by "enemies" that you don't have to fight, but if you choose  you'll probably die, just let them wander off."Final boss" added weak points which for the entirety of the game doesn't exist."It is designed around the idea of "being thrown into the world".Thrown into a world that you are almost already assimilated into!"you will explore different interconnected regions in a non-linear fashion." Straight lie this is only one path"Every location contains its own theme (story), puzzles and characters that are integral in creating a cohesive world."every location is the same apart from one, one puzzle per area which aren't hard to figure out on first look over with no other characters at all."Each region is a maze-like structure with various rooms and paths to discover"The option to turn left into a dead and then turn right into the linear path forwards "All the storytelling happens in-game, with no cut-scenes to distract you from the grisly reality of the living, breathing world you’re in."Nothing is ever explained anywhere and everyone is wildly speculating"But keep your eyes open - the game won’t show you any sympathy if you miss something important on your uneasy travels."General gamers wont miss anything "Players will experience better immersion being aware of the character’s body and movement. _childDocuments_.review: First thing I love here is the biomechanic design that was probably inspired by the master of the genre, filled with nuances behind it. The game's design however, stays original with its own artistic touches, it has its own personality and vibe with original lines I never saw before, one true playable art also because of the correct manipulation of graphics and so. The developers style of assembling and programming seems VERY organized, I'd say very precise and clean, almost a science job to be honest. I mostly played it just to be there, relaxing my brain. When there is music it is sinister and done right, but most of the time the real music is "ambient," only shoving darkness into the mind.There is no savegame station, only immediate check-points if you die and chapter points if you load a game. Puzzles shows up, but they're environmental and object orientated. I recommend finding the answers on your own so immersion rewards nicely if you think your way out of it. They're usually not hard, but sequential or replaceable, it requires some exploration and observation. When it comes to the survival horror part, you must manage limited bullets and resources. The controls responds good enough at the pace it proposes - at first. It takes some time for other guns to show up, but eventually powers and enemies comes at the right time. Sadly, an issue undermines this good aspect of it.AI is well animated, but behavior is basic of the basics. The game fails to hit higher notes because of that. You can run, but you can't turn or backstep or strafe any faster, so you're just a pathetic slow puncher that barely moves. Since you can't save game directly, if you screw something up, either forever load to death or roll back an entire episode. So the survival horror slowly derails into a generic corner shooter, after the middle game up. It slowly pushes the game to a limit it can't provide, so fights turns out predictable, clumsy and sorry to say, downright annoying. The action imbalance; you're simply forced to abide as if these encounters were mandatory puzzles. Action becomes an one-way street, failing to rhyme the hidden art with what should be a challenging survival.Can't holster a main weapon, so the beautiful POV is always blocked in part by the gun. To make it worse there is no screenshot mode to fully make use of all that bizarre tapestry. Replay-factor is small, because there is no multiple endings.Developers should start considering this before delivering their games to Steam or any other platform. I grew tired of notifications popping up with every move I did for whatever challenge I unlocked, because some were downright spoiling the game with its challenge names. The only thing you can do right now is to deactivate notifications manually, but Steam is not that smart to provide a checkbox for specific games, while some others you actually want or need it turned on. Gaming platforms are fast-food of gaming, where games like Scorn are treated like a kid's toy.My personal opinion on the matter; horror is at risk of extinction. Real horror for me are Amnesia series, Rebirth I couldn't even finish it, Dead Space 1 and Alien Isolation. Honorable names and other games were just not enough for me. I finally found another game to my personal best list. Scorn is a good horror because direction and art does it just right for those who likes it. It makes no sense, but not to be confused with nonsensical stuff, there is a difference.While puzzles are so intricate and rational, it makes things look reasonable. Your brain starts mapping things. But questions keeps coming, answers not so much and all that collides into one true dance macabre. The design is so good it almost works stand-alone as you ignore any flaws, like the blocky action I mentioned. It is a rare experience to have if you pay attention.Well the problem here, that isn't a problem, is that the design is so fakking fantastic it makes you appreciate the deformities rather than fear it. Not careful enough and you'll end up loving it, and I'll have to welcome you into the goth state of mind we live everyday.Acid trip, nightmare, alien mutations, rotting in hell, its just too pretty. I don't care for the "real" meaning, whatever is just beautiful. Inventory and gadgets are VERY attractive due the level of details that makes you wish you could have these items in the real world. I want these gadgets. I want the weapons, these implants. I want to install these switches in my home. Imagine some doors, a bed or a wardrobe with authentic Scorn design. What a dream that would be.Now, while some games overdo adult things like Agony Unrated did, at the point of ridicule, some games disguises it too much like they're afraid of it. Scorn does that. I thought I should put this as a con but I don't have the courage to complain, I understand why it wasn't done more directly. So there are other ways to sprout things inside the hot humid cave.An erected mechanical pump exploded a white goo inside the cell after penetrating the engine.That's the "closest" the game will get to refer to that, and perhaps a few figures. For such dark art expression, ignoring that thing directly and toward the player is just bad - but at the same time it is a clever way to bypass censorship. See how it limits us? Such designs like those of HR Giger are obviously referring to the lowest spheres of that, very explicitly yet so needed. I don't want to spoil it, so I'd just say like that. Scorn is beautiful, because it is an unnoficial yet closest exploration of that thing in a game - but insufficient without it at best. Sadly, developers are probably forced to keep adult content away, so not to be stopped from selling a game to potential underage that shouldn't be playing it. It would end up in some wanking site instead of rightfully absorbed.Liked this review? There is just one Scorn's background image for Steam profiles that is good, so you can use to represent the genre with pride. Since no other game really got this close, if you're a fan of the style, you need to have it. Sadly, cards are not as dark for my tastes and emojis could have been much better, exposing more of the game's brilliant item trinkets instead of its enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting to give Scorn a play through for a while now. It was recommended to me to wait till it was on sale and the recent summer sales event on steam was just the right price. Scorn is an insane world. Insane to look at and insane to play. It's only saving grace is that there isn't a whole lot of it. I would recommend Scorn, just get it on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: A visual and audio feast! I was genuinely intrigued all the way through. Not understanding much of what's going on is part of the charm.Not sure about all the complaints about the combat. I thought it suited the game perfectly considering all the biomass mixed with tech. Ending was a bit vague. Guess it leaves it to our own interpretation. Still, I don't regret a single minute playing this. Extremely well polished. Attention to detail is incredible. _childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting experience, but a terrible game. The environments are very atmospheric (disgusting), but the game makes no effort to explain anything.You spend all your time exploring, using and fighting sphincters.I think the worst thing about this game is the combat - I can't believe I'm saying this, but the combat makes me wish this were just a walking simulator. Scorn uses a checkpoint system to save your progress, although it isn't clear when the game is being saved. A lot of the game is you exploring before finding yourself in a battle, dying, and then reloading from some random point in the past.I think this game would be better served by either getting rid of the combat altogether, or leaving it in and enabling manual save. I came very close to throwing in the towel just because I was tired of doing the same battle 3-4 times.

_childDocuments_.review: The ambience is perfectly eerie and unsettling all throughoutThe sound design is crispy, unnerving and constantly reminding you that none of this is human or is as far removed from what is known on Earth to be considered alienThe combat is rough and uncertain in the aim department, but that's fine, good even. It's a survival horror game, not a shooter, you're meant to be at a disadvantage all things considered.The music, though absent throughout the first Acts, is subtle, perfectly fitting and at times awe inspiringThe damage taken from hits can feel unfair, but considering the fact that most combat is optional (you can wait out enemies in most situations) and that healing wares restore 2 blocks of HP, it shouldn't be a problem. Unless you're tanking hits, and if you're taking hits in a survival horror game, you should reconsider heavily.The small amount of weapons is fine, limited ammo is fine since you find plenty to carry you throughout the game, same for the healing wares.The design of the environments is gorgeous, engrossing and while at times disorienting, it's easy to find the next place to go to, provided your paying attention.The puzzles are the right amount of difficult, and if you're expecting something like the puzzles out of Silent HIll 1-4, get real; it's a survival horror game set in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ alien planet, and you'll get corresponding puzzles. Just like in Silent HIll puzzles are supposed to clue you in to parts of the story, so do the ones in this game. Most of the time anyway.The issue of game lenght is a sore spot for many people, and I understand as I too was hoping for something longer, and while I'm sure many thought this would be a AAA game, the fact that this came out looking as gorgeous as it does and came out at all (not in Early Access) is something to praise. Could it have been longer? Sure. Should it have been longer? Maybe not. Quit while you're ahead, and all of that.The story, a non verbal narrative told through envrionments, puzzles and the implications of the protagonist's actions and the ultimate conclusion are wonderfully rich and imaginative. Until you reach the end. Seriously, what the ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking. Imagine completely botching the end of your story for the sake of some worthless nihilist cycle ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Why even bother writing it at that point.Everything else is great, but don't play this expecting a 20 hour game. It's certainly a first step in the right direction to revitalize the horror genre and move it beyond its "spooky house of jumpscare horrors" phase it's currently in, and so I give it high praise for that.But seriously, give your stories a proper ending or don't btoher at all.

_childDocuments_.review: A strange and awesome game. Not at all what I was expecting (I avoided all coverage in order to go in fresh), but I still enjoyed it.The main thing to understand is that this is almost purely a puzzle game. It's like HR Geiger and David Cronenberg got together and made Myst. There ARE hostile creatures, and you can technically fight those creatures with the couple weapons you find along the way, but fighting is really inefficient and not very fun. You're much better off hiding until the creatures crawl off and disappear down a hole, or knocking the big ones down with a shot and then running past them. This also isn't really a typical horror game. It's certainly horrifying, in it's way. But there aren't any scares. No chase sequences, or quick-time escapes. Even the enemies are more just weird and sad than scary. The game is more about a pervasive sense of dread and disgust. The puzzles themselves aren't very complicated, in themselves, but they are made trickier by the fact that they all involve bizarre alien machinery that doesn't make any sense at first glance. It's hard to tell which controls and switches will do what, until you fiddle around with them to see what effects they have, and piece together what's missing or out of place. And finally, there are no words in this game, anywhere. Neither written nor spoken. No audio logs, no NPCs to talk to, no diaries left in desk drawers, no lore dumps. It is left to you to interpret what's going on, why it's going on, what led up to it...and what it means when it's over.Needless to say, if you don't have the patience for slightly obtuse puzzle games, you're gonna hate all of that. I personally do happen to enjoy slightly obtuse puzzle games, and I still had moments of impatience or frustration. But they were more than made up for by the awesome atmosphere and visual design. As a crochety old jaded veteran of horror games, I don't often come across one that actually disturbs me or creeps me out. I've seen all the horror tropes done a million times. But this game is something I haven't quite seen before. It's fresh, and weird, and I wasn't sure what to expect. And that's maybe the thing I prize most in a game these days. HIGHLY recommend, if you're in the mood for a fairly slow, brooding experience with gross visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games where, after the first hour or so, it loses its novelty and "wow" factor, so you just end up wanting it to be over. Halfway through the game, I found myself holding the sprint button constantly and getting annoyed with the enemies because the "challenge" comes down to the combat being clunky more so than anything else.The cherry on top was beating the game and having more questions than when I first started. Being ambiguous and left up to interpretation works for some games, but I personally don't think it worked for Scorn.If the game was half what it costs now then I might recommend it. The atmosphere and scenery are definitely interesting and beautiful, but that's all the positive I really have to say.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, Everyone here has already stated "Its art! not just a game!" whatever. im too drunk to care. Heres the real deal. This game. is not fun. The puzzles are mediocre, the combat is boring, and the story is non-existant. yes, the H.R Geiger inspired landscape is there, and yes, finding beautiful art is in the game. BUT, There is barely a sound track, there is no real horror elements to keep you on your toes, and overall, i found myself clawing my own brain out trying to force myself to finish the game. its not long, (4-6 hours) but every wall where i had to fight enemies, or solve a puzzle, i could have been doing other stuff. If you are looking for a game that focuses on its art design, then sure. have fun (or whatever you'd call this), but keep in mind, THIS GAME IS NOT WORTH ITS PRICE TAG. Please get this on sale. you'd be a legit idiot if you buy this game full price. also, like i said, theres barely any music in the game, so dont bother buying the deluxe edition for the sound track. oh yeah. i have to address the "gore" element as well. its not the worst ive seen. you'd see more gore just playing DOOM. theres nothing about this game or "art" that i found amusing. im not saying i cant appreciate the work put into it, but theres no element in the game that captivates me to learn more about the world. again, im drunk, so everything im writing is true TO MY THOUGHTS. if you enjoyed it, then good, im glad, but personally, as someone who was excited for this game, only buy it when its on a sale, and even then, be ready for when you do play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The draw for most is the art style, and it succeeds in what it is going for. Exploring its unsettling creepy environments was fun. The game is primarily exploring and puzzle solving, and for the most part they aren't too obtuse or aggravating. It can be easy to get lost sometimes and maybe a map would've been helpful but I think being lost in the insanity is intentional.The combat, which most will dislike, can be difficult because of how slow the character is when strafing while aiming and reloading. It has very limited ammo and health, but I kind of expect that from a survival horror. It can also be hard to avoid enemies when they shoot stuff at you, since there isn't much cover and you strafe slowly. If possible it is usually better to just run the opposite direction and hope they scamper off or "de-spawn". Luckily the combat isn't overused.My main complaint is how it saves with only using checkpoints that can sometimes set you back annoyingly far. Manual saves would've been nice.The game doesn't outstay its welcome though, with "storytelling" that is vague and told through the environment. It is a unique crazy trip through an unsettling disgusting world.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: It is great game, I was a bit slower with inspecting textures, level design and assets. It is really piece of art.I played using Proton Experimental wit all details maxed. No glitches or crashes experienced. Game was smooth and responsive. Alt+Tab was switching paused game to the menu. Sound was just basic stereo, so tracking enemies without line of sight felt weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda weird. Don't get me wrong, I did enjoy in some kind of form, but i certainly wouldn't recommend it.The only thing Scorn does well is setting the atmosphere. All other aspects of the game are clunky, slow or outright bad.The combat is horrid (yes, it is not a main point of the game, but still...), there are like 4 puzzles in the entire game and the 5 hours of play time are basically a glorified walking simulator without enough content.Don't get me started on the checkpoints. The game saves in the beginning of every act and after that only saves in some passages during it. Having the game crash on you is not fun, but it's even worse if you realize you have to play through the entire act again because the game does not support manually saving.All in all, if you're a fan of the setting, you might enjoy it. But if you want to play a game with actual mechanics, Scorn will not be able to satisfy you.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A game that blends the beautiful with the grotesque, cruel, and horrifying in a way no other piece of media does. The world feels alive but empty at the same time. Ebb absolutely achieved the setting and tone they set out to create from the start, years ago. I agree with the complaints that the game is too short; I wish there were more of it to experience. The puzzles are engaging and feel like part of the world itself for the most part, rather than arbitrary roadblocks, and while the combat is very basic, it also isn't a major part of the game anyway. I've got mixed feelings on the ending as well; they could have given us a lot more.It isn't a perfect game, but it's exactly what I wanted when I saw the announcement trailer back in 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: I became a backer for Scorn on Kickstarter back in 2017, I paid about $17.00 for the full base game. For that price, I feel like I got a lot more than my money's worth for the final product, but this isn't to say that it doesn't have it's issues. Mostly it seems like another case of what we got being a whole lot different than what was expected.For starters, the graphics, art design, sound, animations, everything about the game visually and how it presents itself is top notch. They captured Giger's and Beksiński's style into a full world that I desperately want to explore further. This game is literally a piece of interactive art and it has captured my imagination. I want more!However, where the game suffers most is how they talked about and described it compared to what it actually was. Looking at the game's description on it's stream page, you may get the idea that this is like some kind of survival game set in a large region, having to traverse endless hallways, structures and dead ends to find your way around, like some kind of metroidvania. I was expecting to have to scrounge for limited ammo and supplies, needing to backtrack and explore to find my way through, having to make tough choices on how to handle the living world around me.Instead the game is pretty linear and often forgiving in how you progress, any survival mechanics are of the basic variety, consisting of ammo, health and a few items you pick up to progress. The puzzles overall were not that hard, taking only a bit of experimenting to figure out, none of them or the items needed were optional. Scorn is not a survival game, there is no inventory management, it's not open-ended, the levels aren't "interconnected", your interactions and choices with the world are pre-determined, you don't learn or gain any skills and you don't need different play styles to progress.I don't feel like I can recommend Scorn at it's default price of $40, but I can easily recommend it at the $20-$30 range hands down. I got just a bit over 8 hours out of the game, but that was with me taking my time to explore. You could probably beat it in 6 hours or less if you really wanted to, but I don't reccomend that.HOWEVER, I will say that despite the game not being what they impressed upon us that it would be, the building blocks are there, it could be done. If Ebb Software wanted to add more "chapters" to this story, perhaps following another character in a new location, they could craft something that starts to actually match the description of Scorn, or perhaps they could put some work into giving the community everything they need to make their own maps and campaigns, like the custom stories in Amnesia.I want to see a larger region with far more locations to explore, I want the puzzles and choices we make to actually have multiple solutions, I want to have to traverse endless hallways and make multiple trips across dangerous terrain, I want to feel like I'm actually trying to survive in a dangerous environment that feels alive instead of having a small and finite population.In the end, I love this game and reccomend it, but not at full price. I want to explore it's world and story more, but our ability to do so right now is limited.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Scorn is an unparalleled experience if you go into it with the right expectations, but is exceptional in a very limited manner, and will be frustrating if you are expecting more.Scorn is morbidly, hauntingly beautiful at the same time that it is unrelentingly bleak, disgusting, and merciless in it's depiction of an alien world.I feel that expecting Scorn to be anything more than an interactive museum piece with philosophical overtones is overselling the premise. Everything in the game has been compromised in service of meeting specific stylistic goals - so it's a good thing the visual and audio design is superlative: Scorn has the most cohesive and consistent 'alien world' environment and audio design that I've experienced since Metroid Prime 2.Scorn is more an "experience" than a game. The combat is frequently frustrating and the puzzles are either too obviously mechanically a puzzle dressed in Zdzisław Beksiński clothes (in example, one is just "Rush Hour" but with horrible alien eggs instead of cars) or trial-and-error contextual buttons. Anyone looking for slick, polished game mechanics will be left extremely wanting. But, of course, there's a sensation that even these frustrations are intentional and part of the experience.I loved Scorn. It succeeds mightily at what it attempts, but that narrow goal certainly isn't for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I come here to tell what most have said before: this game should not have combat or it should be designed in a different way. The game has permanent health, limited recovery, far away checkpoints and a combat system based on the fluidity of movement of a walking sim. It's a shame that with such a strong atmosphere somebody managed to ruin the game just by saying "but it can't be oppresive if there's no real tension", without that decision this game would no doubt have extremely positive reviews. Also, the shift into combat-oriented gameplay happens like 30% into the game and it goes from 0 to 100 in the span of like 10 minutes, I don't know what the purpose of that was but it really makes you appreciate how good the game is without combat just to take it away from you.As an extra sidenote, from my 3 hours of gameplay almost one was me fixing an audio issue that the devs have neglected for a least one year from what I've been able to find, it's kind of a rare bug but if you feel like the game is too silent, it's not a feature, it's a bug.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually a very cool and grotesque looking game and I do like how the game doesn't hand hold you so you pretty much have to figure everything out yourself. That said the game does have quite a few issues, especially the way it starts out because you almost immediately get thrown into a big room and have to go find and solve a puzzle which does take a bit so I could see a lot of people just quitting right out of the gate and not bothering so I don't think it was a good way to start the game. It isn't all puzzles though, there's maybe a handful of actual puzzles in the game, the rest is just wandering around finding things, killing things and opening doors so very simple and straight forward, the game is extremely linear so its not hard to figure it out and get through it all.The combat is okay, can be annoying trying to avoid enemy projectiles and it is also annoying having to ready your weapon every time you go to attack. There's like 4 weapons in the game and each one has its uses so yeah they're alright but slow to use so if you're not ready it can be frustrating at times. There's not really many enemies in the game just like 4 and then a boss so its like whatever really, they're alright. The game doesn't have a save option nor does it tell you when it is autosaving so you just have to hope that whenever you stop playing you won't have to redo much the next time you play. I guess the game is meant to be beaten in one sitting or something since it is very short, about 4 hours so very short game unfortunately so I think for the price its definitely not worth it so I would wait for a discount. The game itself runs decently well, was able to consistently stay above 100fps at 1080p on gtx 1080 + i7 7700k. Only issue I think was there were a few framedrops every now and then but since the game doesn't have any loading screens I imagine it was just loading more stuff, would be nice if it could load stuff without lagging but oh well. Didn't really have any glitches or anything and there were no crashes so that's decent.Overall a very strange and interesting game, sadly very short and just not enough to it really. I don't understand too much why the game took so long to come out, feels like it was announced a very long time ago and if this is all its got then it is a bit disappointing. Its not a bad game but its definitely best to wait for sale. 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this will be a big piece to tackle right here.To contextualize, this has been since 2014 that the game has been announced and 2016 that the game had a very proper trailer. I was actually really really hyped. That was one of the games that I was waiting the most for years and years now. And I think it was the same for many people. Thus we waited. And waited. And now, in 2022, they release the game. Finally. And, for a wait that long, I knew I had to lower my expectations, which I did.I must say, I really love the ambiance of this game, a really great mix between Gigger, Beksiński and Barker. And also a bit of Lovecraft here and there. And this was present for many years. In all of the trailers. Did we have this atmosphere and aesthetic in the present game? Yes. Yes we did. And I absolutely adored it. The entirety of the game, I was in awe with what the game showed me. It was really  good. It was creepy and enerving and fascinating and beautiful and there is the fourth act that is so much tense (when you don't know what will happen to you). And, also, the artbook is very generous, which is something really refreshing these past years.... Now, why do I not recommend this game?For many unfortunate reasons. I would have loved to recommend it, really, I had a great time playing it, but... But the game is not worth it... Get yourself a coffee and something to eat for this one. Okay, the gameplay is quite poor. The puzzles are basic and the fights are nor really entertaining, even if they can be tense... and infurating, I'm not gonna lie. There are 4 different enemies and 1 boss that you fight twice (well, the second time, you don't really "fight" it). The boss was okay. The enemies were frustrating but had a cool design. And, I will ask one thing : WHERE IS THE THING YOU SHOULD NOT LOOK AT FROM THE 2017 GAMEPLAY SHOWCASE?! IT WAS A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ INTERESTING IDEA! IT COULD HAVE ADDED DEPTH TO THE GAMPLAY! WHERE ARE THE LIMPING ENEMIES FROM THIS SAME SHOWCASE? IT ADDED TO THE ATMOSPHERE! HERE? THE ENEMIE JUST DIES, NOTHING INTERESTING! WHERE THE ♥♥♥♥ IS IT! WHERE IS THE TENSION! AT ONE MOMENT YOU HAVE A CHOICE AND IT CHANGES NOTHING TOO! AND THAT'S THE ONLY CHOICE YOU MAKE, AT THE BEGINNING OF THE GAME! WHY, GAME, WHY!!! WHY ARE YOU SO POOR YOU'RE LIKE A WALKING SIM WITH SHOOTER ELEMENTS! WE WAITED 8 YEARS FOR THIS GAME!...Sorry, got carried away. The game is very linear. Too linear. I would have loved a game less... like that.  Graphic bugs, popups, heads of the decapitated enemies moving along the body... It's minor (8 years old) but it's there. Alright, I liked how the storytelling was, I like that kind of thing. It wasn't transcendantal so it didn't excuse the poor gamplay but it was still there. I didn't really feel anything with the story, I had no emotional attachment nor distance in any way. And that also has to do with... well, that ending... It is a bit disapointing. It's not really satisfying, I didn't feel like I did anything in this game. It was promising but... at that ending, I was left with but one question: "Is that it?" So that ending is a big letdown. AND, if you want to really understand the world and the story, you HAVE to read the artbook, because FromSoft is like the kindergarden of obscure and vague storytelling next to that, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ novel written in a very comprehensible style. Scorn... is like a poem written in a different language: if you want to understand it, you have to have the translation, unless you're already very familiar with the language. I finished the game (and 100% it) in 7 hours. Because I was bad at one or two part and because I took my time to observe and appreciate the atmosphere. I read that people finished it in 5 hours. That, with all the achievements. Couldn't you put more interesting things in the achievements? Some challenge, perhaps. Now, how much cost that game...? Ah, yes, that's right. ! If you don't preorder it, that is. But, still,  FOR 5 HOURS OF GAME. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥!...Sorry, I got carried away once again. But the price is way too high for what the game actually is. It feels more like a 20 to 30 dollars game . No more. I felt like the dev stole my money, not earned it, even if they worked for it. It's like paying footballers millions of dollars-. But yeah, the price is way too high. If Steam's refund system wasn't as bad, I would have asked for a refund. Unfortunately, I cannot.Thus, I will give you this advice. Don't buy this game. At least not now. Wait for it to be like 20$. Then it will be a bit worth it. Is it a good game? . Is it disappointing? Yes.And, if I would give it a notation:12/20. 3/4 of these points are for the aesthetic and atmosphere alone. And it hurts me to give a notation that low to this game...Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a game to unistall.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a mixed bag.PROS+The game is beautiful in a disgusting way.+The game is disturbing, just like it wants to be.MIDDLE- No dialogue and almost no text. This isn't something that breaks the game, but they didn't compensate for these limits elsewhere. Detailed below.CONS-The visual design for puzzles is terrible. It's hard to distinguish what is an interactable element or not. The worst is an egg puzzle early on that really, really doesn't explain itself. With no text or dialogue, visual design was even more important for a game with puzzles, but it feels like they made this part bad on purpose, to spite the player. The corridors also all look the same and it's very easy to get lost, especially during the puzzle underneath the big guy about 2/3 through.-The storytelling is pretty mixed.-The art-book is essential for understanding plot elements, but the digital version got downgraded after people had purchased it, which is one of the most consumer unfriendly decisions I've heard in a while.-The save-points system is abysmal. Dying can send you way back and you have to go through a lot of nonsense to get back there.-If you get behind on resources, like bullets or healing items, you are behind for the rest of the game. Missing a few shots is enough for this to happen.-There is a lot of audio clutter, especially around the parasite that is on your back. Every hour or so, it screams at you, you look down and the parasite punches your guts. Also, this is unavoidable damage that can kill you, which is a terrible design choice and forced me to restart a chapter because healing is very limited.-The boss fight takes way too long and is very repetitive, which is extra frustrating because of the previously mentioned check points garbage.OVERALLScorn is a game that makes almost every decision against the player. It's a game that wants you to feel as much torment as the character you're playing as and expects you to like it. Scorn is a game that hates that it's a game and wants to watch the world burn.

_childDocuments_.review: Not my cup of tea. It's not a game: you're walking through a semi-labyrinthine environment. You have to discover the rules and purpose of a puzzle, then solve it in the one and only way possible. The graphics and atmosphere save this walking simulator a little, but not enough, and certainly not at full price. Don't waste your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a deliberately crafted and surreal experience unlike any I've previously engaged with, and I enjoyed being given the opportunity to fully interpret my observations in whatever ways it made me feel. The art direction is beautiful, the audio design is impeccable, and the pacing of the puzzles and combat are appropriate for the experience. It made me think about life, existence, creation, pain, relationships, endurance, and the end left me wondering what it meant, if anything at all.

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, the game is short. It only took me about 4 and a half hours to beat. But, despite it's length, I really enjoyed it.The atmosphere is really really unsettling, and it succeeded at making me extremely uncomfortable throughout the game (which is good, since this is a horror game).The idea of exploring a place that is completely alien and beyond your understanding, where the simple act of opening a door requires you to get some kind of grotesque implant grafted to your arm and to stick your other hand into a disgusting meat gauntlet, is not something you see very much in video games in my opinion, and for that reason, this game if very appealing to me.I really wish there was more of this game, and I really hope that ebb decides to make an expansion, sequel, or some other thing set in this universe, because I want to see more of this horrifying world.A lot of people saying this game is bad are philistines IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Short, amazing world, beautiful in a grotesque way. this is an immersive game and you're meant to experience the world. it's downfall seems to be peoples expectations that this is meant to be a fps or more action orientated... it's not. very minor combat that you could probably just run away from and quite a few puzzles to expect.
