_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my experience with Scorn, it was what I was looking for in a H.R Geiger world for a video game. I haven't seen a game this raw in a long time and I'm glad the developers did such a beautiful job capturing the style of Geiger in this unique experience of a game. The atmosphere was stellar and the animations and sound design are pretty damn good. I was often times disgusted and repulsed by what I saw, which was a huge achievement for Ebb Software to pull off.However, this game was not at all worth the massive development time behind it, and totally not worth the $40 price tag set. This game was a birthday gift for me, so I can't say that I regret spending my money on it, because I didn't. And even if I had, I wouldn't say it's so bad it's refund material. It's a really solid puzzle game muddied by things that shouldn't have taken up development time.Scorn's combat is probably some of the worst paced combat I've experienced in quite some time. Enemies attack really fast and at range, which sucks because you have very little ammo and most enemies take an absurd amount of melee hits for a weapon that attacks twice and then goes on cooldown. During your playthrough you are also forced to experience an incredibly shallow boss fight, which is super ill fitting for this games pacing. I wish that they had cut the "combat" from the game and just continued to add more puzzles, more levels, and more storytelling. The games story is remarkably absent and has honestly left me very confused. I feel like they should have kept the morality system that was originally going to be in the game that offered alternative endings, that would have made things a tad bit more clear. What we were left with was also a really short product too, I took about 4 hours to beat it.For Geiger fans, get this bad boy on sale. For people that want some kind of horror shooter, please do yourself a favor and move onto another product. Overall though, I'd still recommend the game for just the unique experience alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle in deciding whether to recommend Scorn. It is a magnificent game full of macabre and grotesque vistas, a beautiful succession of dark and gruesome sights. A piece of art ruined by weak gameplay. Combat is lacklustre and worsened by slow animations and boring enemies. Some will say combat is not the point of the game, well then I believe it should've been removed or further resources dedicated to it. As it is right now, it is frustrating. Even more so during pseudo boss encounters which amounts to you plodding around obstacles while you dodge stuff, sometimes getting hit for no reason. All of this is worsened with the checkpoint system which places checkpoints at arbitrary times and makes you go through useless animations to get back on track. Failure should punish you with having to try again. Not wade through animation after animation to get to the moment where you failed. Enough on combat. You shouldn't play this game for the combat.The puzzles are satisfying enough, sometimes quite obscure in their presentation. There is some allure to it. I never got stuck anywhere or had to google though some took more time to figure out. If you like games with puzzles you've probably seen better. So you shouldn't play this game for the puzzles.The soundscape and music are atmospheric though I think there could've been added effort on giving presence to the player movement. Footsteps are quite weak which kind of makes sense considering the MC is barefoot but there is too little presence as a result. Some soundscapes are better than others but overall there wasn't enough "stuff" in each room's soundscape. You shouldn't play this game for the Sound Design.The story is interesting and a sort of metaphor of birth in a strange world. However the ending felt uninspiring and unsatisfying. You shouldn't play this game for the Story.So why play this game? Because Scorn is truly a magnificent trip through one of a kind environments. It will take a toll on you gameplay wise but I believe it's worth it. If any of those negatives ( basically everything except the artistic vision) are no gos for you then skip it. But if you want to dream, imagine and feel the strangeness of an alien world then by all means do play it.P.S I do not mean to insult anyone on the team in the non artistic departments. Perhaps they put their priorities in the wrong places or didn't have enough time. I'm excited for their next game with more time and resources.

_childDocuments_.review: (2/10) This game reminds me of a tech demo where the just make a map with no real gameplay elements yet.Very cool/gross scenery. I think they thought "puzzles"  meant hide & go seak the next thing to click on or if your lucky one of those race against the clock puzzles.... but without a clock. Overall waste of time and money. 1 point basically for cool scenery. Would have gave it another point or 2 if I wasn't so bored while looking at it. I didn't even finish the last part as I was so bored out of my mind at there wasn't a story or a reason to even care about finishing it. Insane that a game that looks this cool gets a 2/10

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is an absolutely fantastic game and experience, but it is first and foremost a game that is not for everyone.If you were looking for an action shooter or "gameplay" heavy game, this is not for you! And that's okay!Scorn has an exceptional amount of layers to it, mostly revolving the incredible atmosphere and scenery it sets up. The game is living in H.R. Giger's innards and loving every second of it. The way the game plays with the idea of what is "alien" and what is "familiar" to us is fantastic: for example, midway into the game, you get a "security pass," but it's really an odd alien mechanism with glowing lights. Yet, you can immediately recognize it for what purpose it serves. Unlike many horror games where we are easily able to identify what's normal, and what's paranormal, Scorn is a completely bizarre realm where it's impossible to discern between the flesh that was there before, and the flesh that shouldn't be there. If the art is appealing to you, BUY THIS GAME. It's truly lovely. I only had some minor frustrations with the clunkiness of some weapons and a glitch in the last section of the game, but overall this is a wonderful experience as a body horror fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous. If you do buy it I recommend getting the artbook as most of the appeal is the visuals.The puzzles were fun, probably the second best part of the experience. They make you consider your environment and question the function of everything, making the visual elements and creative world design stand out even more.The combat is terrible.First off, not having a HUD for most of the game makes you really appreciate the horrific beauty of your surroundings and there's a notable contrast between that experience and the time when your life bar and ammo meter are visible.Second, the movement isn't great. Trying to strafe around enemies to avoid their attacks or run past them will get you cornered or stuck on terrain, which is basically a death sentence, and you have to avoid most enemies since ammo is so scarce.The hit boxes being kinda vague doesn't really help this issue. Some enemies seem to just stun-lock you when they get close making your health seem kinda meaningless since you just want it to deplete faster so you can retry the section sooner.There were also times when I would complete a puzzle with an enemy chasing me and a tiny bit of health left, causing the checkpoint to start me with an enemy DIRECTLY behind me and only a few seconds to sprint away or suffer another loading screen.Third, shooting things just isn't fun. The animations are very slow, every action feels labored and imprecise. The first weapon you get has a cooldown timer worth two shots, a deceptively long animation that will get you killed if you try to spam it, and an itty-bitty hit box that will miss things sometimes even when you are right up against them.To the developer's credit I think a feeling of helplessness and discomfort was what they were going for, but having to repeat sections again and again because you have no ammo\health left and have to squeeze through a narrow hallway with an enemy in it without getting hit at all to get to the next part is just tedious and not fun, imo.I would like this game a lot more if it had no combat at all, which is really saying something, for me. I think if the focus had been on puzzle solving it would have been better overall. It made me wish that godmode existed, frankly, just so I could look at everything and not worry about the enemies.Bottom line: it's worth experience for the visuals alone, but probably not worth the current price tag. It's also rather short. If it was on sale for 15 or 20 USD I'd say go for it, until then just watch your favorite YouTuber play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful -but utterly meaningless and devoid of any plot. First of: You do not care about the protagonist at all, there's no story what so ever, except that you are some kind of lost soul in a Gigersqe nightmare and the door puzzles are tedious and mind numbing, like running through various mazes and tunnels after different keys to make bizarre machines work and open doors. Once you encounter enemies, you realize how awful your pityfull weapon truly is, how you can't even dodge, run or even jump from them and then tedium really sets in. Sure it's not meant to be a shooter, but even a horror game has to have some kind of hook, an engaging story or just someone you can care for, let alone some basic variation in the action. This is all icing on a cake, made out of sawdust and sand.This was not worth waiting 6 years for!
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The opening of this game is very strong, with intense atmosphere and and a good introduction to how you will be interacting with most puzzle elements. I have my issues with the puzzle mechanics, and how the game feels to play, but those are a small price for the atmosphere you get with this experience. The main glaring problems start when you get your first weapon. Combat in this game is clunky at best, putting you in a position where you realize that avoiding combat is in your best interest. It becomes a game where the most effective way to deal with most monsters is to backtrack, wait ten seconds, and then proceed after they have climbed back into the walls. It is less of a game of stealth, and more of one of getting irritated by the appearance of enemies, rather than fear. As you reach the late game, more and more enemies start being placed in such a way where you are pretty much forced to fight them. Instead of being interesting puzzles of what bullets to use with what, it becomes a cycle of restarting from your last check point because you get mobbed by enemies that crawl out of the walls after you engage with an encounter you think is worth clearing. I am all for high stakes, but when the most basic of monsters take four to five hits from your main tool that only can hit twice at a time before waiting for a long cool down, it feels less like I am not failing from a lack of judgement or strategy and I am just getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the sake of it. If you are a big fan of atmosphere and enjoy walking simulator puzzle games I would still recommend this game, if the price looks steep, you could get about the same enjoyment of atmosphere from watching a play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying this experience so far. The attention to detail in this world is uncommon to see and incredible to experience. The lore is interesting and am enjoying trying to piece together what has happened.There are a couple of frustrating elements like the checkpoint system (between act 3 and 4 there is very few) but think that could be addressed in a patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn left me torn.A beautiful experience, real art was delivered even after so much development hell, and i don't mean just visually, in general. It was genuinely mesmerizing to experience, incredibly immersive.If only it was, ultimately, finished. Because it didn't feel like one, to me. First of all because a couple of times i had whole sections of the level not load in so i couldn't proceed and had to start an entire section of the game from scratch. And second...It really feels cut, cut hard, there feels void during the final act, like there was supposed to be more, much more than we got, and the ending feels like it was supposed to be different, although still the same in vibes.But even then, it's still one of a kind experience, and i'm happy it finally came out. It was a beautifully horrifying experience, and in my eyes - it's all worth it. A must have experience that WILL make you think a bit, but think of what - that's down to your own experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This review is set as positive for one specific reason: I don't want all the hard work of developers to fall into oblivion.I just hope that the game receives enough attention to encourage Ebb Software to continue expanding on what they have built already.I completed the game without encountering any technical or performance issues, which means it was tested thoroughly – a rare situation for the first release of indie studio.But gameplay wise it feels like at some point either developers or their publisher said: "Enough, it's definitely sinking into development hell. Let's put together what we have today, polish it, test it then release it."So if people who made this are not tired to death with what they have done already, and will find energy to expand on their initial ideas, we might eventually get the game Scorn allegedly meant to be.Most enlightening part of the game is, well, the art book. The funny thing is it contradicts itself from the very first lines: as game director states that they meant to build the world as alien to player, as it is for developers, further on the pages we encounter a very clear functional explanation of different parts of the world from developer's point.With current level of in-game details the world falls in an awkward position of being too logical for a fever dream, but not logical enough to be a solid universe.Our main goal is to move forward. As protagonist receives zero motivation to do anything, he (anatomy looks clearly masculine) can either do nothing or try to get somewhere. The puzzles are all centered around getting access to next area. And here comes the semi-logical approach: we clearly have a key with different levels of clearance, but there is no apparent reason for different areas having different security levels. And stations upgrading your key don't seem like they were guarded in any way.Every puzzle seemed straightforward. I never felt, well, puzzled. Combat is criticized enough, I don't think it's wise to repeat it. Just a point about boss fight: we assemble our enemy with our own hands, and the thing we carry to make it whole, its weak point, and what we need to extract – is one and the same. So there is no way of ditching the question "Why did we assemble it and bother fighting it when we could just break the core from the beginning?"So from my point of view current puzzles and combat both feel kind of superfluous. The thought "Are they here just to make the game not a walking simulator?" is everpresent.That's basically it. A tremendous amount of vision and aesthetics, carefully tested and polished product, but it still feels incomplete. Getting "Scorn Reborn" with more murals for interpretation, more coherent world, better combat and carefully arranged puzzles would be the best thing we can hope for.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I would describe Scorn as a first person horror puzzle game with a bit of shooting. First of all a short game. Most of its kind are. Second of all gruesome. And it just gets worse as the game goes on. One design choice that enhances the experience is that there is no explanation of anything and no kind of tutorial. This points is actually what I enjoyed about the puzzles. Though none were complicated, the enjoyment comes from figuring out the order of things on your own. Fiddling about with the parts seeing what they do than figuring out what the goal of it is. And they were forgiving with it all by not having infinite things you can interact with so just by exploring the limited space you're in what you need to do becomes clear. The combat sucks. No ways around that fact. You start with a cattle prod basically and get a couple of other weapons along the way. Combat is just management really, shoot the enemy, dodge as much as you can and don't let health drop too low. And since the main enemies have so much health it's just the slog of witling them down while clumsily trying to get out of the way of  them or their projectiles. The move slowly so there's not much threat. The danger comes when suddenly you're surrounded but at that point you should just run past them since the smaller enemies tend to just despawn. Luckily there's not too much combat. Just enough to annoy me when trying to explore the sections where there are enemies. Now, the real place the game shines is in its art direction, which was itself why I wishlisted it to begin with. Sci fi horror shooters are rare to begin with so I'll take what I can get. But they've put a lot of effort into making the world feel eerie and disturbing. The closest thing I can think of to describe the look is the Engineers ship in Prometheus for the beginning section, but the environment moves and changes through the game so the designs evolve as the game progresses. 7.5/10I would recommend it if you like sci-fi horror games, and don't mind some puzzles and not being handheld.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: A disgusting romp through the sopping wet hallways of an alien mystery. Delightful to get lost in the atmosphere, taking in the obviously standout visuals of gore and rebirth made wholly unnatural, letting your brain try and connect the dots as to 'why?' Not for everyone, you need to like looking at weird ♥♥♥♥ and the weird ♥♥♥♥ is very weird but also rad as hell. Suffers from a lack of enemy variety but I feel the clunky combat suits your poor husk of a protagonist. Raw and kinda forlorn.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn has a misleading description on Steam, and I suspect this caused the majority of negative reviews. I was waiting for this game since its initial trailer, fell in love with the visuals and was not disappointed in the end.Scorn is a short and linerar game created in an outstandingly beautiful environment and soundscape.So beautiful that you don't press shift to run and just turn your head around to catch every detail of this bizarre and alien world. The game doesn't tell you anything, but for me it provided food for my imagination and interpretation of these living organizms and long dead machines.And the game stays true to its style until the end, providing an immersive experience. I would call it an eye candy, but I suspect this metaphor would sound ambiguous in the fleshy setting of Scorn.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, Scorn is harsh. It's oppressive and unyielding. While this may be immediately obvious from the visuals and music, I felt that the gameplay is also deliberately slow and heavy to underline this point. You're not meant to act with much agency in this world; the world has forgotten about you and moved on. You're the foreign body that violently cuts through new forms of life by reactivating the ancient machinery of a failed civilization.In that sense, Scorn managed to make me feel an incredible sense of alienation and unease. It's horror on a very slow burn, more psychological and disturbing than twitchy and frantic. This also means that anyone looking for a more traditional horror (or, god forbid, horror shooter) experience might not like what this game has to offer. To make matters worse, the store page is not doing a good job of managing expectations.I picked this game up completely blind and had a blast. The visuals, combat, and story inform its exploration of existential themes and make them more impactful. Sadly this cannot be said about the puzzles. Most of them feel tacked on and exist separately from the world Scorn is trying to create. Solving small logic puzzles does not heighten existential dread, it instead distracts from it through arbitrary gating of progress. The more simple and direct interactions with the various creatures in the game are what will stay in my mind instead.In the end I'm glad to see this game published, especially in light of most of all the other heartless and unoriginal AAA junk. The game is not perfect, and it might not be for you, but it is part of what keeps open an authentic dialogue about games as an important art form. It made me feel uneasy in a way I had never felt before and nearly a week after finishing Scorn I still regularly catch myself thinking about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like ending, I don't care if there's this artsy, symbolic, or metaphoric meaning to this ending, it sucks ass.  There was no point to the ending.  Granted, the game did a better job of paying tribute to H.R. Giger, but ♥♥♥♥ this game. SOMA and Observer are best examples of better game play than this piece of luxurious garbage. 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn. A game I backed on Kickstarter back at 2017 and one of my most anticipated games ever.Unfortunately I can't recommend this game. All the promised content we were supposed to get is just missing. The game is too short and when you finally get the feeling that the story is about to get unfolded throughout the environmental storytelling, the game just says"Oh, you are actually piecing the story together and starting to get more and more invested in the world?" *SLAP ON THE FACE* "Think again ♥♥♥♥♥ and go ♥♥♥♥ yourself." and just ends. Just a few examples of promised things we didn't get: - World and enemy behavior changing based on our moral/immoral choices. In the whole game there is only one choice and it just dictates which first achievement you get. Nothing else.- Acquiring new skill. What skills? If you mean upgrading our key or getting a healing pod, then those are not skills.- Non-linear story progression. You just have a big area where you are trying to solve big environmental puzzle to get to the next area and do it all over again. - 6-8 hours of gameplay. I finished the game not even in 5 hours. And I got stuck or got lost a few times throughout the game. The game is just too short. To sum it up. The visuals are awesome, the whole soundtrack is chilling, atmosphere is just graspable, the story looked like it could have been really cool, but unfortunately the game as a whole feels more like the intended first part of a game they planned in the beginning. If they plan to release more content I am ok with that but until then it just isn't worth it. Especially for 40 euros.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Through the whole play through, I couldn't shake the feeling that I was playing through a Tool music video.  The whole experience was pretty great, albeit short.The visuals were great, and gory.  The puzzles weren't too intense but was enough to keep me engaged.  Combat really isn't necessary in this game...but it's their.  There are too many mobs that do dumb s%#t, and not a whole lot of stations for ammo and health to make combat worth while to engage in. I really think the developers have created a intriguing world that, hopefully, gets built upon.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is a masterpiece.A masterpiece of art.Unfortunately not really as a "game", like you might expect from seeing pictures and trailers.Scorn even isn't really a game, but more of an experience. And it's good!As a Kickstarter backer, I've been eager to get my hands on Scorn for more than 5 years. I love the Alien franchise, its visuals with its weird and unconventional look.I've played through Scorn, and it felt great for most parts. Until you hit a boss fight. The boss fight is tough and frustrating, as you need to figure out how it works, which is much contrary to what you have experienced in the areas before, where you had to explore mostly, could avoid enemies and just had solve cool puzzles.Then the ending comes pretty quickly, and at first you might feel left empty.And here comes the big but: This is an awesome experience none the less! And in conjunction with the Art book, things start to make sense. So this is mostly a walking simulator, with emphasis on exploring and trying to make sense out of impressions. But the game doesn't give you any confirmation about your conclusions, until you read the Art book.Here you realize how things are connected, what's the reason behind some things (not all of them), and then you'll see the game with different eyes... it will be even more fascinating!Can I recommend this as a game? Probably not.Can I recommend Scorn? Yes, as it's a very unique experience you currently can't find elsewhere.Play it blind first. Then check theories against your own, maybe read the Art book. It will leave a better impression after knowing more (even the Boss fight makes sense then), but you shouldn't know it before playing as it would take much of the fascination.Played on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS Linux with nVidia, VoDs: Works also great on Steam Deck:
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The ugliest game ever made.I think an incredibly important thing of note with this game is each individual element is relatively weak but as a whole it can be an enjoyable experience. Let me break this game down to three elements. - World building and art style: The art style is of course the thing that is driving this game. I think it's relatively strong and the game loves to show it off at every chance it gets. It's kind of one-note but the game is only 5 or so hours so I don't think it overstays its welcome but it may for some. The world however I feel like is extremely lacking. I was drawn in and wanted to explore the world to figure out how it ticks but I couldn't figure out the logic behind this world as I'm not sure there is one. - Puzzles: They're nothing that'll really tax your brain. Some of the puzzles aren't really puzzles and more of just an excuse for the character to walk from this area to another. An aspect of a good puzzle is maximizing the time for a player thinking and testing things out in the puzzle and minimizing time walking around and waiting for animations to play. In that aspect, the game fails at it loves to revel in its art style and animation. - Combat/survival horror: I understand the idea of adding this in to the game. It promotes more exploration for ammo/health and breaks things up. I think a big problem with it is your melee weapon is absolutely horrendous. You can only use it to hit an enemy twice before you run away and wait for it to recharge. It's more aggravating than engaging when you have to repeat the hit an enemy twice and run away a number of times for an encounter. You also can't sprint to cancel a reload or weapon swap animation to dodge an enemy which will leave to some frustrating deaths. I know your character isn't some 1337 mega soldier and that's fine but I would expect him to prioritize his health and safety and sprint to dodge. Mostly the combat is serviceable but does get annoying at times. I would say the puzzle, combat, and world building are poor but they are fine enough tacked onto the art and atmosphere aspect of it. Just need to set your expectations correctly, I'd say it's worth it if you will be fascinated by the weird and disgusting things the artists came up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: How is it possible that this game have mostly positive on steam?I rather play Bad rats than this game again for real.One of the worst puzzle games i've tried so far.Environment and visuals are fantastic, but that's it.Game design otherwise is pretty bad, lame combat mechanics that makes no sense and are frustrating, puzzles are terrible, story...no comments.., the checkpoints and autosave frustrating...Do you want to torture yourself? play this game.Do you want to be happy? do not.

_childDocuments_.review: what a disappointing game, the trailers were setup in a way that portrayed this as the next doom game when in reality its a glorified walking simulator horror game, with basic and short combat, basically 1 boss and is so short i got all the achievements in 5 hours, the visuals, areas and theme had such potential but were let down by its unimaginative combat, basic puzzles, linear level design and relied to heavily on shock factor. not worth the time and or money.

_childDocuments_.review: I opened this game expecting H.R Giger to enter my scrotum and burst me open. What did I get? I got SCORNFUL! I was playing my Scorn while eating my corn... BREAD! And as my dry lips covered in bread pursed around my water bottles top. I SPIT EVERYWHERE! This feels like H.R Giger personally came to my house sat me down at a fancy table FULL of cornbread. Let me eat. Took me to my bed. AND RAILED ME! Could NOT be happier! Too bad this game blows chunks of steaming scorn!

_childDocuments_.review: The design and atmosphere is top tier to me in this game. You truly feel like you've played something on another alien world. I love the feel that everything is perfect to that feeling. That being said, I find the combat and story to be very underwhelming and probably unecesary for combat to even be a thing in this game.I feel a game to contrast this to would be Outlast. The design and world are presented in great form, but it also shows that you don't necessarily need to have weapons to help with the game. The guns are great, but minus the last Act, you don't really need this in the game. Honestly its mixed, but I still recommend it.Does anyone else feel like this game is missing something for its end? _childDocuments_.review: How many years have I had this sitting in my wishlist, waiting for it to arrive. Finally it did. 30 Minutes in and I refunded it. It is simply (sadly) not what I expected. If you were hoping for a survival first person horror game, you may want to skip this.  Disappointing. Was so looking forward to it.The only thing that I enjoyed is the unique art style it offers.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Effectively an interactive piece of art - can understand some people's frustrations in the pricing and the length of the game, but ultimately it is very immersive in an alien world, and a thought provoking environment and plot lineAtmosphere is fantastic, sound design is quality, admittedly the elements that give it an aspect of FPS are a little clunky, the puzzles aren't tricky, and the path is linearI just liked being gross and hanging out in a gross placeP.S. - If ever there were a chance for it to go VR, it would be a disgustingly brilliant experience
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly beautiful game, with an astonishing amount of Giger-style architecture and biomechanical machines from beginning to end. Some light shooter elements, but most fights can be avoided by just getting out of creatures' ways and letting them go about their business. Otherwise it feels like a Myst-style game with free movement and the aforementioned amazing visuals. There is zero in-game text, which is important for such an alien setting, but the environment does a fantastic job of telling a story, and I felt like I had a clear understanding of the setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very mehPros: everything on the visual and sound design is amazing. the atmosphere in this game is unmatched and everything is just coolCons:basically everything else, gun play feels like it doesn't need to exist, the environmental puzzles are extremely straight forward, the one boss fight is really bad, the level design for the first area is good but the other areas are extremely linear so any question of what you should do is answered almost immediately.overall I think its not great, but huge props to the graphic designers and anyone who worked on how the game looked, everything else is kinda a bruh moment
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game. If you enjoy surreal and disgusting environments I would say it's worth picking up. Honestly the game could have done without the combat element at all and it would have been better, it can be pretty frustrating sometimes. Incredible visual story-telling and interesting puzzles. The ending has got me ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up though. It was good, I just wasn't expecting... that.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is, for lack of a better description, not a game in the traditional sense.  It's more like an interactive piece of art masquerading as a game.  I understand it's not for everyone but quite frankly not everyone has an imagination that is equal to interpreting what Scorn has to show us.  Imagination is your best friend when navigating the physical and contextual landscape the world of Scorn presents.  Not only that, but you need a certain amount of imagination to relate with the protagonist(s) that let you see everything Scorn has to offer through their eyes.  I get why some have issues with certain features like the combat mechanics and so on but this isn't a trained soldier type or experienced combatant you're dealing with.  This is quite literally a shambling train-wreck of a creature that has no previous experience or knowledge of where he came from, why he's here, what he's supposed to do, etc.  It's like waking up in the body of a walking corpse with the mind of a baby, to put things in perspective.  Think about that when you make your treacherous way through the obstructed bowels of what remains of a lost civilization and see if it doesn't put things in perspective.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a techno-organic horror/walking simulator/puzzle game. I personally think it's really cool. So far I've really liked the puzzles. They aren't super tough or cryptic and the environments are pretty well made so it's not too hard to find your way around everything. I love the aesthetic so I'm really enjoying just exploring everything.*update* I just beat the game and I really enjoyed it. The game is an artistic masterpiece. That being said, if you don't like the idea of walking around and solving fairly basic puzzles and shooting some basic enemies while doing it, you will probably hate this game. I can really tell that the devs put their absolute heart and soul into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is not the point of this game. It's a mediocre video game, but it's an artistic masterpiece, and I can't fault it for that. The game-play is functional, the game is polished (not a single bug in 7 hours), and the environmental and visual story-telling is top-notch. If you're a fan of macabre horror, you owe it to yourself to immerse yourself in this world for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I hope the people who made this game get the therapy they so desperately need. But really. I do on one hand understand why this game has many bad reviews. At full price I would not recommend this game. its around 5 hours of play time so if you think that price is worth 5 hours its up to you. I personally did not need a guide to to figure out this game but that is not to say it wasnt easy, it requires some amount of backtracking which is tedious. The combat is tedious as well as others have pointed out, I do think this game requires combat to really keep you on your toes but it was not implemented well. Just a couple of enemy types and a weapon system that feels like you arm is tied to your back is not it. But I dont think its a deal breaker, the 'story' and the ambience make up for any shortcomings in that regard, and in 5 hours of playtime it didnt feel like i was constantly fighting. I recommend this game on sale, its a nice or i guess hellish experience for a weekend
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a visually stunning and horrific game. The gameplay and puzzles were pretty good—maybe a little hard to understand at first, but not bad at all. However, the biggest downside, I would say, is the game’s length. I basically beat it the same day I got it, in about 5 hours, even while exploring everything I could.For the price I paid (10€), it’s alright. Definitely not replayable unless you forget the entire storyline.If it’s on sale for 75% off or more, I would say it’s worth giving a shot.I would rate it a .The game time is quite short, but for what it was, it definitely didn’t disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting for 10 years, I can say I thoroughly enjoyed this game. My only gripe is that it is short, like probably too short, but the feeling of anxiety and dread is so intense and omnipotent. So many great ideas and designs come out in such interesting ways. It reminded me of Myst puzzles mixed with Resident Evil resource management all wrapped in an abstract interpretative H.R.Giger inspired package.If you're into any of this then this game is defiantly for you, if you're iffy about any of this then wait for a sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Over the past eight years, I have been able to complete the process of the game. I feel very happy all the way. It is a great art and story. I am very gratified and sorry. I still have a lot to do. But at the same time, it is very unhappy. For a work that has been waiting for 8 years but only one has been castrated, the checkpoint scenes and a large number of biological designs in two or more areas have been abandoned, the war relics of the two Dwarves camps Also, the giant head altar in the propaganda has been "abandoned" without warning. That is a very good design, but you forced to cut off the best expectations at the beginning for the sake of project progress. Now the contempt is like "incomplete", it is not the best state. I want to ask EBB, will you still develop games like "scorn"? Please give me a dlc or something? Please give more, more, more! More scenes and levels, more biological designs, more world settings and supplements, and more images in the concept map become reality, because the current contempt is really too thin!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what I would call, a below average game.Pros:1, Great visual and aesthetic.2. Great sound.Cons:1. There is one particular puzzle that is god awful. I dont know what to call it but its a puzzle where you have to light up 3 or 4 things by rotating them.2. The final part of Act 5, if you dont know what you are doing, you can get softlocked out of progression and you may have to redo the entire Act again.3. Look at my playtime, that is how long it takes for me to beat the game including me afk for dinner and then came back.4. Finally the main reason why I give this game a thumbs down. The combat. Combat in this game sucks really badly. Reloading takes forever, switching to different weapons take forever, you walk really slowly while reloading, one particular type of enemy have a homing projectile and you will have to fight the enemies in very small spaces in most fights. Also, the killing blow animation takes foreverrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr, the animation is way longer than reloading and swapping weapons combine which means, if there are still some enemies around you, YOU ARE F----ED.Here is the thing, if the combat of this game is not so atrocious, I probably would have given this game a thumbs up. I got my moneys worth buying it at 40% but its certainly not worth at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Not often does one come across game that is carried entirely by its setting and atmosphere. The gameplay is... acceptable. It's not boring, but consists of fairly interesting puzzles; and challenging, but simple combat. Nothing new is brought to the table here, especially among other horror games of its ilk, but the gameplay takes second stage, as I believe it merely serves as a vehicle for the player to traverse this perverse labyrinth dreamt up by some of the sickest and most creative minds out there. What starts out as simply a completely alien cave system, slowly begins to uproot into a concordantly horrifying, otherworldly, (and oddly sexual?) labyrinthian hell of ungodly amplitude. You won't find any cutscenes, dialogue, or journal entries here. Just you, a hellish landscape, and a friend who hugs  too tightly.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: I was someone who donated to the kickstarter back in the day. I have beaten the game and I am still glad I backed it. There are positives and negatives.Will say this right off, this is not for people who prefer long games. I beat this in 5 hours, and that alone can be a deal breaker. I also wouldn't recommend it for people who prefer fast pace games, this is a very slow game. There is no tutorial, no nothing. You wake up, and you go. That's it. No dialogue, no words, no maps.You will have to figure out what is going on in the world of Scorn yourself. You are a person? and that is all you get. The environment is how the "story" is told, so each person will probably come up with their own general idea of what is happening/happened.This is a puzzle game. It isn't a FPS horror game. 95% of your time is going to be figuring out these puzzles. The other 5% will be the small amounts of shooting. The shooting mechanics are shallow, there isn't much too it. You will barely have ammo, barely be given enough health. I ended up going through most of the game not shooting anything, which you can do and I found it much better to do it this way. You shoot as a last resort, it isn't something you seek out to do or the main focus. It is like walking through a painting. You could stop at any point in this game and the detail in the environment are fantastic. A lot of love went into this world. There isn't a single detail missed. The architecture in this so grand, large, foreboding. As you no doubt know, this is all heavily HR Giger inspired. If you want to walk through a painting of one of his worlds, this game will do that for you. It is like a love letter to HR Giger and fans of such art. It is gross, gorey, sexual in uncomfortable ways and yet somehow stunning. My biggest issue is, sadly well spoiler-...The ending. I went "oh". And that was it. It has the same vibes as "I have no mouth and I must scream", but I was hoping for more. And with how little we are given story wise, left to our devices, I don't know why we ended up with that ending. I would love for just some crumbs of more information. But at the same time, that might be the point of this game? As some would say, it is quite "arty farty". If there is anymore hidden in this game, I am sure the gamers will find it.All in all, I am glad I played it. Guess my biggest issues in the end, was that there wasn't more.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is an outstanding art piece.  It is worth your time and money.  However, Scorn suffers the difficult fate of having been highly anticipated for many years.  A great deal of hype and expectation was built up around an perceived version of scorn that the developers didn't deliver.  This is the dual result of both unbridled fan anticipation and an  pre-release representation of Scorn by the developers.I won't talk about what Scorn isn't - the negative reviews have taken care of that.  Instead I'll talk about what Scorn : a harrowing, beautiful, atmospheric arthouse experience.    Those who complain about a lack of story are absolutely oblivious to the painstakingly detailed environments, the visualized passage of time, the deep symbology, the guided worldbuilding process.  .  It's meant to be ambiguous and interpretive - but it's absolutely saturated with complexity, content to be reflected on and mulled over for weeks, months after play.  I sincerely believe that if Scorn had released without years of preceding hype and fanfare - simply appearing one day on Steam - it may have gone down in legend as a cult classic.  However, despite how much I loved it, I really considered not recommending this game, because Scorn advertised itself  poorly pre-release and really confused a lot of people.Scorn is an audiovisual marvel, a sumptuous artistic feast.  It is almost totally atmospheric and one dimensional: a brief, single-threaded dive through a complex world that we know nothing about, a world about which we are left to draw our own conclusions.  If this sounds appealing to you, Scorn is a strong 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Mild positive review. It's clear based on audience response that this game is a victim of misleading marketing. It is not, as the trailer suggests, a combat-heavy game. It is also not, as most online posts suggest, a Myst-style adventure game. It would be more accurate to characterize this game as a narrative-light walking simulator. If you are able to stomach gore, viscera, and bio-horror and you like walking simulators, you'll enjoy this. It is quite short (5.1 hours for me for a complete playthrough + a replay of the first chunk of the game to get an achievement) and I think even for people who are fans of the genre waiting for a sale at something more like $10-15 would be the right move.The main reason I'm bothering to write a review is to push back against the notion that I've seen expressed on discussions on Steam and elsewhere that this is a "Myst-like" game. It is not. Myst games employ hub-and-spoke open-world designs. Scorn is a series of six or seven linear levels (once you finish a level, you can't go back). Myst games employ large world-system puzzles: for example, Riven has three major puzzles all of which span the entire game's map. Scorn's puzzles tend to be highly localized, about things you can do on a single screen. Myst tends to have world design that is immediately clear: you can always tell what something is doing. Scorn's mystery is based on the idea that you have no idea what part of the world will be triggered by a switch that you interact with. Myst does not have puzzles take take place on separate 2D screens: Scorn has three such puzzles (a Sokoban style constrained block pusher, a Lights Out-style puzzle built around a rotation mechanic, and a maze puzzle) which form the bulk of the game's puzzles. Myst puts you in a dead world and challenges you to find out what happened to make it that way. Scorn is content to have you walk through a dead world and is not interested in revealing much about how it got that way. Myst is a game where you constantly take notes. You will not take notes for Scorn. Myst is substantially more opaque than Scorn, but also substantially more rewarding as you uncover how things are connected.Many people online have discussed the first section of Scorn, which is said to be "Myst-like" in that you are spawned in a level and not given any direction. This is not Myst-like. The Scorn level is highly linear. You emerge into a complex that contains several rooms, each of which have machines that unload something from a rail track and into a machine. Following the rail track, you find a main hub which features a machine that allows you to adjust the rail track and a machine that grabs something from above to put on the track. Clearly you need to go to the second floor, and indeed when you find an elevator it brings you to a linear second floor that brings you directly to the first major puzzle. This is functional, of course, but if anyone is confused by what's being asked of them it's because they aren't paying attention. Myst, on the other hand, encourages you to explore an open world in a non-linear way and make connections between segments.The other major difference is, of course, the combat. I don't think Scorn's combat is very good. This is different than saying that all combat should be fast and agile. Slow and deliberate combat is good. Scorn has some weird design decisions. The bulk of the game's combat involves needing to dodge enemies or kite them into an open room and strafe, waiting for a chance to strike. But most enemies are spawned in narrow corridors. This, combined with sponginess of enemies, limited ammo, slow reloading, very slow weapon switching, no automatic health regeneration, and widely spaced checkpoints (and no manual saves) means that encountering an enemy rarely feels good. There are also only three enemy types (and a final boss). The final boss fight is interesting, but it's interesting in the way that a first boss fight would be in most games: an offering from the developers about ideas that could develop around the combat system.As with many walking simulators, the game's default walk speed is substantially too slow. The default controller bind for running is LB (L1), which is obnoxious. I assume that walking simulators do this to pad out their runtime, and given the complaints about how short Scorn is for the price, I'd not be surprised if that's the case here. A secondary reason is to make it easier to have players take in the environment. But this is at odds with the art and game design: the environments have low visual contrast and are undifferentiated because of how writhing, pustulant, and organic they are. A lot of the level design actually involves many corridors being familiar and disorienting. There are no items to collect or optional content to encounter, no narrative to unpack. And many dead ends contain enemies which deplete your already limited ammo, so there's a strong incentive to rush through the main pathway. So should we go fast or slow?Finally, I wanted to comment a little bit about "themes". Since Scorn is not a game with a conventional narrative, positive coverage of the game focuses on its apparent themes -- conception, maternity, the relationship between the sexual act and violence, transhumanism, divine punishment, etc. -- but there's a difference between stating a theme and developing one. If your theme is climate change, then just showing a picture of a polar bear on a piece of melting ice is a statement of a theme. It's the thing where you point at the screen and say "I know what that is." Developing a theme means showing how different facets of the theme interact, how the experience of the theme can be at once highly personal and universal. It involves quoting and synthesizing ideas advanced from previous authors. When you develop a theme, it changes how the viewer/player reflects on or thinks about the ideas. Does Scorn develop its themes? Not really.I wrote this review as a critique rather than a buyer's guide because I do think it's somewhere between an interesting failure and a shallow success. The art design really is quite gorgeous. I especially like a section at the end that departs from Giger and gets into Alex Grey territory. The final level, whose mechanics involve mulching fetuses to get blood, is a genuinely gripping bit of body horror. The puzzles, though simple, are well made. Side note: if you see anyone saying the puzzles are hard, you should be highly critical of that claim or you should wonder if they've ever engaged with a puzzle before. Scorn plays to me like a project made by an intelligent but green student who needs the firm hand of a teacher encouraging them to innovate and iterate more. An enthusiastic first draft. I hope if the developers make a new game that they recruit more experienced designers and refocus their study of art and literature around deeper understanding and less on superficial reproduction. Still, a fun diversion.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games I've paid full price for and I do NOT regret it.  This game is a work of art.  If you're the type of person that's always wondered what it was like to walk around an H.R. Giger painting, this is your chance.The environments are absolutely gorgeous.  The music is haunting.  There is no dialog and no hand-holding and I absolutely love it.My opinion on combat - It is definitely frustrating, but I believe that's by design.  I don't think it 'sucks' so much as I just think the developers purposefully designed it that way.  I think people need to be aware that this is NOT a run and gun type of game.  Combat is VERY strategic.  I personally wish they had just left it out.  I felt it detracted from me enjoying the beautiful and marvelously crafted environments by constantly being on the look out for enemies.  I still highly recommend this game and I hope there is more to come from the developer.  It is rather short, but I still think it's worth full price.  Oh, and this game is in NO way similar to Myst.  I don't know who first made that comparison, but it is WAY off base.

_childDocuments_.review: To address the other reviews and comments. Yes, this game is short, some of the puzzles can be a little too obtuse, the ending can be seen as unsatisfying, and the combat is clunky. Despite all of that, this is still one of the most unique horror / surreal puzzle game experiences you will find, and I recommend it if you are at all a fan of horror, surrealism, H.R. Giger, Beksinski art, or just all of those like me. It is a short, but memorable experience that I think will stay with you for some time. There really is not another game out there that quite nails this look like Scorn does. Money well spent in my case, especially if we get as sequel (I can dream). Achievements:   11/12 achievements are story related. The other achievement can be done in a very short 10 minute 2nd play through for an easy 12/12. I appreciated this as I could immerse myself in the game / world and not have to worry about having a guide open. Collectibles / etc would only have detracted from the experience. This is more of an experience than it is a achievement hunter game.

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is an atmospheric bio-horror driven adventure game, inspired by our good friend Giger. It lived up to its hype.I'll get the bad out of the way: It's quite short. Even with a combat softlock and plenty of walking for sightseeing, it took me aroung 5 hours to get to the ending cutscene.Now for the good. This game is a jumpscareless horror title. All the shuddering comes from the world, your interactions with it, the visual and sound design, and the story, if it can be called that. Combat is purposefully made thight and punishing, with your ammo and health being a finite resource, making encounters have a certain impact, and certain enemies could be used as a looming presence.I would argue that it could be removed from the game entirely, fully making this making this title a puzzle walking sim, but enemies crawling out of the environment to halt your progress is a neat way to break the walking and wandering, plus, the enemy designs are just perfectly grotesque. In addition to that, without outright spoiling anything, all I can say is that the enemies are a necessary evil.The game does no shy away from going DEEP into the disgusting and visceral, which is its trademark, really. It does not disappoint, with scenes that make your skin crawl and possibly even your dinner come back to say hi again. Truly makes me question how will there be any media coverage of this game when it comes to let's plays...I have only encountered one bug thorough the entire game which was solved after a save reload. The optimization is fairly neat, and the game runs smooth with vSync.Verdict: A very unique and terrifyingly gross game, which while lived up to its hype, has left players begging for more, and ended right when things started getting awfully interesting. Do NOT sleep on this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Visual Design and Atmosphere:One of Scorn's most remarkable aspects is its visual design, heavily inspired by the works of H.R. Giger. The game's grotesque and surreal art style creates a captivating and haunting environment that immerses players in a world that feels both familiar and uncanny. The attention to detail is exceptional, with organic and biomechanical structures that are simultaneously repulsive and mesmerizing. The meticulous craftsmanship of the visuals, combined with the atmospheric lighting and sound design, contributes to an unrelenting sense of dread and unease throughout the game.Narrative and Storytelling:Scorn's narrative is deeply rooted in psychological horror, unfolding gradually through environmental cues, cryptic symbolism, and subtle narrative fragments. The game embraces ambiguity and leaves much of the story open to interpretation, allowing players to piece together the fragmented narrative as they progress. The lack of explicit exposition adds to the sense of mystery and invites players to delve deeper into the unsettling world of Scorn, questioning their own understanding of the events unfolding before them.Gameplay and Exploration:Scorn offers a non-linear and interconnected world, inviting players to explore its intricately designed environments. The gameplay mechanics encourage thorough exploration, as hidden pathways, secret areas, and interactive elements are scattered throughout the game. Puzzles and environmental challenges are intelligently integrated into the gameplay, requiring players to think critically and employ observation skills to progress. This non-traditional approach to puzzle-solving contributes to the immersive and atmospheric experience, as players are compelled to decipher the twisted logic of the game world.Audio and Sound Design:Scorn's audio design plays a crucial role in creating an immersive and unsettling experience. The game employs ambient soundscapes, eerie musical compositions, and subtle cues to intensify the psychological horror. The atmospheric audio design effectively heightens tension and amplifies the sense of unease, further immersing players in the nightmarish world of Scorn.Conclusion:Scorn is a game that pushes the boundaries of psychological horror, offering a deeply immersive experience for players seeking a cerebral and atmospheric journey. Its intricate visual design, atmospheric storytelling, and challenging gameplay mechanics combine to create a uniquely unsettling experience. While Scorn may not appeal to those seeking fast-paced action or a straightforward narrative, it is a remarkable achievement for players who appreciate atmospheric and psychological depth. Brace yourself for a descent into darkness and embark on a chilling journey through the twisted recesses of the mind with Scorn.

_childDocuments_.review: There really isn't any other game quite like Scorn.It shares a lot of similarities with older point-n-click games, such as no instructions on where to go or what to do. It's atmosphere is unmatched, and genuinely horrifying and disgusting at times. It is NOT an FPS, even though there is technically "combat" and shooting, so don't expect that kind of experience. The combat encounters are more a test of puzzle solving and resource management. This is a  that's a lot more linear than you'd expect. You just gotta pay attention and be able to keep track of locations in your head.Visually, it's stunning.. in the worst way possible. Every single detail is polished to an incredible sheen, and the atmosphere is downright oppressive. Despite you being "alone" for most of the game, the world feels like it's alive, or just sentient around you. You never feel safe, you never feel relief, and it's a crushingly frightening setting to be in. Plus, the sound design is insane. I don't even wanna know how the audio guy made some of these sounds.Story-wise, there isn't much, To say it's vague is an understatement, but the game can tell you a lot if you take the time to soak in the environment. There's no "plot" really, just a concept of what this place used to be. There's no characters, just creatures and entities, if you could call them that. My favorite is the big one, you'll see what I mean if you play it.Now, is it worth full price? Well despite my praise and recommendation, I don't think so. $40 is quite a lot for such a short game. I'm pretty easy to please, because I REALLY value a great atmosphere and a unique experience, so it's a big reason why I enjoyed it. But I'd say most people wouldn't get much out of this, unless you look at the screenshots and videos on the Steam page and go "wow this looks awesome" and you like a subtle and unique gameplay experience. TL;DR - This game is horrifying, disgusting, and downright incomprehensible. I adore it.

You truly felt you were there and the levels were intuitive to be able to figured out without any hints or guidance.Quick breakdown of thoughts, while there are no SPOILERS in here, I will be talking about certain mechanics found in game (as general as I can) which MAY be construed as a spoiler. I don't think they spoil anything, but hey... I knew someone who didn't even watch reveal trailers of new Pokemon so there are different levels of spoilers (hopefully those people don't try and read reviews then):Pros-> While "The Design" is an easy thing to point to about this game, as it's kind of it's selling point, I want to focus more on the game design aspect of this as opposed to the artistic direction (which is obviously great, but you could tell that from the trailer):- The levels: Each area is massive, but takes great care to create visual landmarks so you can easily learn your way around (which is very handy when they end up looping you around). I kept entering new worlds with a daunting "Oh God, I'm going to get so lost" mentality, but after some wandering around I always was able to find my footing (with one MINOR exception where a lever placement looked like a direct copy of the one before it so I legitimately thought I was looped around when I was, in fact, not).- The "puzzles": Each puzzle is based on something you've likely seen before, this DOES kind of make it where the challenge is finding the concept. None of these kept me stumped for longer than a few minutes, you've likely solved WAY harder versions of each puzzle found here in other games. There was one I solved in literal seconds closer to the end of the game because it was so blatantly obvious, but that made me feel kinda like a genius so I don't think it's a bad thing. But if you're an expert puzzle solver than these will be child's play.- The "boss fight": I would say there's really only one "boss" in this game, and I did struggle a little bit to figure out the pattern. However, the designs lend itself very nicely to helping you figure it out as long as you're looking and not blindly wasting your resources.- The story-telling: I spent a LOT of time asking, "why is my character doing that?" and in a dialogue-less story with MINIMAL cut-scenes (don't let the marketing fool you, there are TECHNICALLY cut-scenes in this game, especially between some level transitions) that can be hard to convey. But the way the levels are built where some of what you need to know is told through the architecture around you, the desperation you feel in your character as you're reaching end game, and that final cut scene painted a BEAUTIFUL picture of what was going on. Most of my admiration of the story-telling comes from that last level, the way a whole civilization is explained just through the statues around was jaw-dropping!- The "FACE": Without giving anything too major away, there is a moment in the game that feels like a total "God of War" moment and it's epic and unnerving! If there is one moment that I'll remember from this game, it's that particular portion of the second to last(?) level!Cons:- The combat: The beginning and ending of the game have some truly memorable moments, however the middle section where you get your weapons and it tries to be a Resident Evil type game with bullet resource management just wasn't for me. And it's not because I don't like those types of games, it's because those freaking enemies are bullet sponges with VERY hard to avoid attacks due to your limited movement. I can see that it's supposed to add tenseness to the game and make you feel like the world wants to kill you... But it's just in one section so it just ramped up the pace to kill it in the third act when we're back to a more ambient setting. The combat started as okay (a good amount of enemies are avoidable if you just wait for them to pass), but then there are times when you've got two of the bigger ones and you don't have the mobility to deal with them and just die if you can't kill them RIGHT at spawn. For me it was just a little too frustrating for no reason just to still show off their cool guns that were introduced in the original 2017 Kickstarter, but the game took a different direction but they wanted to keep the pew pew in.- The save system: This was only highlighted to me because I had a power outage during my play-through and I had to start a level over from the beginning. Obviously my power cutting out isn't a fault of the game, but it did make me realize that I NEVER knew when I reached a checkpoint. If I could only play for a limited amount of time, I would have a really hard time knowing when I could safely log out of the game (apart from the middle section, I was never frustrated enough to NOT be able to do it, but who wants to do a puzzle a second time because they didn't reach a checkpoint and didn't know it?)- Achievements 1 & 2! So this is MOSTLY an issue for me because I was a backer and was given a "Prologue" version, which was the first level, a few weeks before the full game release. That version did not have achievements activated, so when I got the full game and started from where I left off... I did not get achievement 1 or 2 (they represent a very minor "choice" you can take). And so I had to replay that first portion TWICE because I didn't get one on my first play-through. Now, you CAN get both by just playing through up to the choice and then reloading your last checkpoint to get the second... But that still required me to do a puzzle portion another time because the checkpoint was before it was solved (it's not hard, just tedious and obnoxious when I'm doing it multiple times in the same sitting)- Not a lot of replayability (which is funny, because this game does like you to have to do the same thing a lot): Apart from that 1&2 achievement, I don't see a lot of reason to come back and play it again. It's certainly worth that first play through because a lot of what makes this game great is the way you're interacting with the world, but beyond that I do not see me wanting to do some of those puzzles again (and I ESPECIALLY don't want to fight those freaking flesh monster things again). This is also exemplified through the occasional time I found myself annoyed at having to do a "mundane" task 2 or 3 times to unlock something before I could move on (this a minor note, it only truly bugged me at the beginning level and the other times were fine enough). But in a game that has such variety in design, puzzles, and mechanics.. The occasional "fetch this thing 3 times" feels out of place and a little short-cutty when they spent all this time on everything else.------------All-in-all I think this game was an incredibly fun time for the Halloween season to give me a nice light horror ambience without revving up the terror factor too much where I have to sleep with the lights on. The difficulty never got too frustrating levels where death was constant, and no puzzles left you wondering what you were supposed to do for too terribly long (which is a an accomplishment in a game with no tutorial or hints). As an original backer, I think that it promised a LITTLE more than it delivered based on the length of the game, but with the sheer variety in each level's architecture and puzzle design I can see where there development time was mostly spent. I think it deserves a play-through for anyone who likes to appreciate the artsy side of video games that want to give an "experience" as opposed to just another "video game".

You will be frustrated by this game, undoubtedly. _childDocuments_.review: This is for the gamers who cry that games these days hold your hand too much. This one just drops you in with a good luck and then it's up to you to figure everything out. You have no map, no markers, no directions, no tutorial, no difficulty slider, no HUD (unless you aim your weapon and even then it's just health and ammo info), and no over-arching goals to work to not even any story to guide you.It's just you in a strange world trying to go... somewhere.  The levels can be confusing, it is often unclear how you need to progress, and the puzzles leave you guessing for the solution. The combat and enemies are annoying in stead of challenging to the point I wish they'd just not bothered with them in the first place. But I wouldn't call this a difficult game, by the end I had so much health and ammo that I could skip recharge stations.That's a lot of complaints so why the thumbs up.As an atmospheric post-apocalyptic, alien inspired, exploration game this is very well done.The environments are hauntingly beautiful, the game has mastered the art of making you feel lost, like a trespasser in a world that has died eons ago. It's an expert at making you feel unwelcome, like you're disturbing something that's been slumbering for ages. What adds to this atmosphere is something that just permeates this entire world and is constantly present, sometimes obvious, often in the background: pain and death. From the body-gore to the torture devices that should maybe actually represent medical machinery and the total disregard for the value of life. One thing is clear: this is not a fun place to be.You feel like your life (and every life around you) is disposable, like whoever built that place had a goal and does not care at all about the suffering the machinery and processes might inflict. The machine must keep running and pain, suffering, and death is a side-effect of such little importance that it is not even acknowledged.It's hard to describe the atmosphere as you wander through this world. But the depressing nature of it all was actually weighing on me to the point that I was honestly glad I'd reached the end.

_childDocuments_.review: To tell you the truth I don't know HR. Giger, never read his work, but the fantastic depiction of the downfall of probably one of the first, long lost and forgotten ancient civilizations, based on the beauty of the horror of sentient organic life, including the portrayal of sex and reproduction with highly advanced technology, the gruesome horrific atmosphere, sounds, and with the fact that how well the implementation of environmental puzzles, and progression work in-game, without the game even slightly holding your hand or giving clues on what to do next, I think Scorn is one of the best psychological indie horror games, that was ever made.And of course, as such, the horrifying and terrorizing conclusion will all so leave you with a little less breath.It needs to be said, that Scorn isn't a shooter, it's a walking simulator with its own gameplay elements, so you shouldn't expect it to be one.The game can be completed in approximately 6 hours, therefore, despite its pros I can't recommend it at its full price.Scorn in my understanding deserves an 8.5 score out of 10, although only on a discounted price.

_childDocuments_.review: The one and only reason I got this game is because of the sickening atmosphere and the extremely grotesque environment, and on that aspect this game did not disappoint. It was disgusting and absolutely brutal to the enemies, the poor random helpless creatures throughout the game, and especially to you. The ♥♥♥♥ that is done to you in just the first two hours of this game made me literally cringe. However, despite how amazingly horrible the atmosphere is, the game play makes it almost unplayable. The puzzles span across huge areas and give you literally no clues as to what the hell you're supposed to be doing. That fact is bad enough in most games, but the world in this game is absolutely alien so you literally have to walk around and interact with each and every single mechanism just to figure out vaguely what it's supposed to do, which means you will be pointlessly walking around just interacting with random objects and accomplishing nothing for a big part of the game. The developers then decided to spice it up by adding combat... giving you weapons that have sluggish fire rates and take a handful of shots to take down a single enemy. The pacing of this game is way too slow and the maps themselves are confusing and have no guide what so ever so that game is literally a combination of choosing random hallways to walk down and hoping you don't run into any enemies just because you don't want to have to deal with the combat.Edit: looked it up and apparently you actually aren't even supposed to engage the enemies. The game is designed where the enemies are tough to kill so you just leave them alone and they will literally just leave and walk away. So I take back the part about the devs adding combat to spice up the already super boring gameSummary: The atmosphere is incredible but the gameplay is so boring I was literally day dreaming while I was playing this game, and the combat is designed to not be used apparently.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely inspiring work that has given me faith in the future of gaming (as someone who has been gaming for more than 40 years and never felt anything really new ever happens these days). I'm 13 hrs in and on the final boss. There are few games that you can just stand and admire the surroundings for as long as you can 'play'. The attention to detail is simply overwhelming. Surreal bio-mechanical flesh labyrinths to get totally lost in.Its so refreshing to play a game that will stress you out, frustrate you, have you wondering if you missed something or is there a bug that is stopping your progression. It's great to be down to absolutely zero 'ammo' and health wondering 'how the hell can I get out of this?'. You die in great games IMHO. Many times. You want to throw the controller and in this the greatest satisfaction is gained when you pin it down. I'm a huge Far Cry fan but lets face it. You never die. Modern games seem to be more about what method you will use to finish a level instead of 'HTF am I going to get out of this?'.I love there are zero instructions, No hand holding and 'arrows' towards the way forward. The puzzles impossible and when you nail them, so obvious.I've been a huge Giger fan for many years and I reckon he would have been overwhelmed how far his works have been utilised in these days.Bravo Devs. I laughed, was sad, tingly, scared, frustrated, sweaty, excited. Everything a brilliant game should have me feeling. Games as unique as this are so rare. Space Invaders. Quake 2. Scorn.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game, but broken due to an extremely bad implemented combat, and save point, system.You'll lose "life" during your first few encounters with dangerous enemies. This can easily leave you with 1 "life point" left, so that every time you run into an enemy you WILL DIE, and the game will end.Restarting will let you start again... way back at some checkpoint that could be half an hour away, and still with that one life point left.Combat is not fun or challenging either. _childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game since 2014; I was in highschool, and now I'm finishing college. Was the wait worth it? Yes. Scorn is a beatufiul artful experience; a puzzle adventure game with little survival horror elements. The game is not perfect; just like every review has pointed out, the combat is straight up bad. Your movement is not precisely fast and the terrain of the game sometimes betrays you. At some ppint you'll want to dodge certain attacks, but an indistinguishable section of terrain won't let you move and straight up die.  There are 4 types of enemies and 1 boss; which is pretty underwhelming.  And that's it, tjat's all the negatives I can point out♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is gorgeous. The developers did H.R Giger and Zszislaw Beksinski the best tribute possilbe. Every section of the map is so impressively detail. At some point you can get lost at the beauty of the architecture. Although at some points I got lost and didn't know where to go, I wasn't mad because I took the time to appreciate every artistic decision they made. This game isn't for everyone. This is an adventure puzzle game with horror aspects. The puzzles themselves are simple yet efective in their symbolism (which make more sense once you reach the last level of the game). For some player, they can get tedious because there is a lot of backtracking. Personally, I didn't bother for this aspect; it was extra time to enjoy the atmosphere and design.I can do nothing but give huge respects to the developers for sticking with their vision. This is a unique game that I'm sure will be talked abaout more in the future. 8 years were worth it after all, and I can't wait to see Ebb Software's next project

_childDocuments_.review: A disgusting and hauntingly beautiful arthouse game that is a masterclass of "show, don't tell" through in media res and the use of brilliant metaphor and allegory. The world and environment design are stunning, and despite the alien world, the user experience and user interface are intuitive and delightful through the clever use of affordances, (e.g. object interactions are obvious), and through immersive animation. The puzzles in this game are novel and fun to solve, and while the game does not hold your hand, it is never frustratingly difficult and teaches you game mechanics one at a time.I would encourage players of this game to play this game with a sense of curiosity, interrogate the existence of the world around you, and take your time observing the environment because it's immersive as hell; there is a lot to be seen and felt. Some parts of the game may feel a bit clunky to some, but it never felt incorrect to me given the world.All that said, despite an appearance that may suggest otherwise, the game is relatively linear without a lot of backtracking, and it's only four to five hours of gameplay, so it doesn't have much replay value.If you like the work of H.R. Giger, e.g. Alien, body horror, or this game otherwise sounds like your jam, get this on sale and give it a play. You won't regret it.
