_childDocuments_.review: great game and everyone who hates it has bad tasteEDIT: But seriously though, with how many popular games these days end up as these big open world explorations that boast about how long it takes to play, or have the most complicated gameplay imaginable, or convoluted storytelling and lore, it's almost refreshing to have something a bit more simple or short in length. That being said, there are of course aspects of the game that I think could potentially be improved upon, but I don't think they necessarily detract from the overall quality in a significant way. Things don't always need to have the smoothest combat or else do away with it entirely, and in this case I feel as if the game's current combat is more thematically appropriate than the alternative; you are a newborn wandering around in the desiccated remains of society and trying to fend off wild animals with technology you don't understand, not Doomguy on his trillionth year anniversary of killing demons.The game is also, as many people have pointed out, very linear with no option to explore or do other stuff. And again, I have to refer back to other games such as the Portal games or the original God of War. Games don't really need to be open world or have hidden collectibles or sidequests, and some games really don't need it. Would it be enjoyable to have more places to explore and do more things in Scorn? I'm sure that it absolutely would, but that doesn't seem to be the story that the devs were trying to tell here, nor do I think that Scorn specifically needs it in order for the experience to be good or enjoyable. With regards to the puzzle aspect of the game, I think the difficulty and quality of the puzzles present ingame really is subjective and varies from person to person. But that aside, I do have to wonder how many of the people complaining about the puzzle aspect or the lack of combat have also played and enjoyed the Portal games, which are both hugely popular and in my opinion more similar to Scorn than Doom or Resident Evil, and don't really have combat in the traditional sense. Personally, I enjoyed the puzzles in Scorn because while they did take me a bit of time to navigate, they weren't so difficult that I had to resort to looking up solutions. But again, not everyone enjoys puzzles, or are good at solving puzzles.And finally, the perceived lack of explicit storytelling, the lack of dialogue, and the complete absence of any text that you might find in other games. I think that this is something that could also vary from person to person in terms of how good it is or how successful it was in this instance. Environmental storytelling is it's own method of getting information across, but a lot of times you end up with a Bethesda situation where the only environmental storytelling we get consists of a skeleton with knife in its chest and a note next to it that says "ahhhh no the raiders are coming i hope they don't kill me". There's always ways in which games can and should improve upon things such as environmental storytelling, but I do think it's very telling when someone would rather eschew it altogether and refuse to actually stop and think about what something could mean. I think that there is great value in storytelling methods that are vague and are more up to interpretation than anything else, and that's what the case is with Scorn. The game doesn't tell you anything, and you kind of have to try and figure it out yourself based on what you see ingame, and even reading the information given in the digital artbook doesn't completely elucidate what's going on. As simple as it is, and while it might not be for everyone, it remains a very unique game that has quite a lot of potential that can be built off of in the future, and I believe that criticism of it would be more constructive if it focused on what the game actually is rather than what it isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun times. Positive vibes. Brilliant atmosphere, masterfully done narration that doesn't use any text but conveys a clear artistic statement. I don't remember being so emotionally hurt by a game since Silent Hill 2. It can get a bit tedious at some point but in light of the finale this tedium seems like a deliberate move rather than inability to produce lots of different environments. I can't understand people complaining about the lack of story. The idea that is even stated in the game description is that you are thrown into an unknown and hostile world. There is absolutely no need in some lengthy explanation of how this civilization came to be. It is irrelevant to the narrative and would even subtract from it. While some of the puzzles do seem out of place they are an integral part of the overall feeling that you are being subjected to a painful ordeal. The game is short by the modern standards but it's not like the longer the game the better. The authors produced a concise and complete statement. It doesn't have anything to do with development time. If you think that any book that took 'x' years to write must be 'y' pages long then yes, But that is not how art works. It's not "style over substance". There is plenty of substance, it's just that it's not spoon-fed to you.So please don't listen to massive complaints in the reviews. If you are capable of symbolic thinking, are not allergic to puzzles and don't expect this game to be a survival action like Resident Evil chances are you will be pleasantly surprised. For me it's the most aesthetically pleasing and meaningful game of the last several years.

It's another to just leave all explanation, and guidance out to artificially lengthen the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: In regards to all the negative reviews, I am convinced that humanity is never satisfied with anything, and will always find something to complain about. Reviews are subjective, and as such, so is mine, but here it is anyways:Scorn is a disgustingly beautiful first-person survival horror game. With heavy emphasis on atmosphere and graphics, there simply is nothing out there that comes close to replicating what Scorn has to offer. Every nook, corner, hallway, room, is meticulously crafted, leaving no empty or copy-pasted spaces. To possess the ability to bring about a world inspired by the works of H.R. Giger is truly a talent, kudos to the modeling team, I am sure you never slept. The lighting and sound design are also superb, I was so engrossed into this world I wanted to take my time to soak in everything, trying to figure out more about the character, his people, and the world they live in. The game features some unique puzzles that while aren't too difficult, will make you sweat a decent amount (reference the key lock thing, if you know you know). The combat is not the focus of the game, therefore it is not going to hold up to something like Destiny 2 or DOOM in terms of shooters or combat oriented games. Rather I liken the combat to that of Silent Hill, it is an option, you have limited amount of ammunition, and it is up to you whether or not you decide to pick a fight, or run from it, all the while creating an anxious atmosphere that plays into the game cohesively. My only complaint is that this felt like an appetizer for what Ebb Software could do, even getting lost, getting deaded, and putting my fingers into strange holes, I clocked almost 9 hours. The ending only made me want more, perhaps there will be sequel/prequel episode 2, though the ending might say otherwise. I should also say I played this with an Xbox Controller, so maybe the experience would be different with keyboard and mouse, that is up to you.I personally recommend this game if you like the Alien movies and dig all the weird biomechanical stuff, and you want something short to play. It was an experience like no other, truly. Great job Ebb Software, can't wait to see what you bring to the table next!

_childDocuments_.review: this game isn't anything like advertised and definitely is not worth $40, all atmospheric choices (ie: enemies, weapons, looting, the lack of dialogue or narrative) all negatively impact gameplay in some way, the ending was beyond disappointing and gave me no feelings other than that I wanted my money back, the save points were by far the worst, I fought the worst boss ever conceived (poorly implemented, gimmicky pattern and design that doesn't match any of the other enemies in the game) I blew myself up with the weapon the fight gives you and was reset to before the fight had even started. That being said I loved the design and art style of the game as well as the feel of loneliness the game creates, however atmosphere is not worth a game I never want to touch again, sorry devs :(

_childDocuments_.review: If Steam allowed you to leave mixed/middle thumb reviews, I would give Scorn that rating. I'm giving it a thumbs down but it's not a bad game, it just leaves a lot more to be desired.The art direction, atmosphere, and sound design are top notch. The Giger/Beksinski influences are clearly present in the art direction, and it is grotesquely beautiful and unnerving. This is Scorn's greatest strength. The atmosphere felt very dense, unnerving, and surreal, which made for an immersive experience. However, the game play is sorely lacking.As much as I enjoyed being in the mind boggling world of Scorn, I really didn't enjoy playing it that much.Most of the time you're going to be walking around a few levels and solving puzzles. Occasionally, you'll break into combat against some wandering monsters, but the combat is REALLY not great. It's not fully fleshed out and it ends up feeling really clunky. I was hoping to get some elements of survival horror, but the game never fully leans into that, and instead, focuses more on walking and solving puzzles. I didn't mind the puzzles that much because most of them are fairly straightforward, however, I do wish that they were more creative and engaging. On top of that, progression isn't clear and the game doesn't tell you where you're supposed to go. I didn't mind this design, but some may find this frustrating.The game is about 4 to 5 hours long, and asking people to pay $40 dollars is way too much.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a disappointment, it's all style no substance. Visually yes it is incredible. But I'd love to find out more about the wold, it's entities and locations. The combat is terrible. And yes I know this game is not meant to be a shooter, but it feels very wooden when it comes to movement, and I am going to be really mean here and say this: The puzzles are there to "bloat" the game and make you play past 2 hours so you can't get a refund. I had much higher expectations for a game that was in development for this long. Only get this at a really massive discount, and only if you're a fan of H.R. Giger.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: So, as we all probably knew up front, this game is a bit of an oddball and definitely not for everyone. Yes, it is indeed relatively expensive if you only look at the length of the game and yes, it is long overdue, but to be quite honest, for me it was totally worth the wait. Admittedly, I never backed it up before, so I never felt like my money was lost. At times I even forgot about the game. That arguably made it easier to enjoy, perhaps.But now that I've finished the game, I would totally recommend it. At least to people who are not afraid of the themes and the really, really, really explicit gore. Because, this game is just a work of art. The whole uncanny feeling it fosters, the sound design with those really crispy, crackly sounds, the way the puzzles fit in the world, everything is so well-designed, so elaborate and crafted with so much love for detail, it is just awesome to look around and absorb it all. Some games just manage to make it all just 'fit', and this is one of them.Every single world has a distinctive feel to it, each having their own type of horrors to experience. However, to me it never felt as if the creators wanted to shock or just put some gore in for the sake of gore, it all adds to the story, it is simply just part of the world you are moving through. It does not make it easier to stomach it all, but it does make you realize that, well, this is your world now and you'll just have to muscle (literally) through.So, to conclude, it was an awesome experience. Fun fact: One level made me long for spare ribs ... somehow ... For some small spoilerish hints, read below.Spoilery hints:People were complaining about clunky combat. I wouldn't call it that, but it's definitely slow, even though every shot and melee hit is impactful, I think the intention was to avoid combat and only engage enemies when really needed. Makes it a lot easier and more exciting if you're being chased. And, ammo is kinda sparse, so avoiding combat avoids running out of ammo, simply put.For me, puzzles were really do-able, perhaps due to my twisted mind. Look for obvious solutions. Look for lighting effects. Puzzles were never overly complicated. You just need some patience and some thinking of "hey, in which hole could I put this thingy?".Lastly, the last level involves some level demolition in certain areas, which to me felt a little bit 'weird' and random, but that's the only time I thought that it didn't make complete sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Scorn

_childDocuments_.review: Visually Scorn is a masterpiece. It feels like a mixture between Alien and Event Horizon or just straight out of one of Zdzisław Beksiński’s nightmares. This extents to all parts of the game including weapon design, reload animation and health pickups.The puzzles are also visually stunning and unsettling but thanks to their otherworldly nature also very convoluted especially when the game expects you to solve multi-level puzzles without any hints or you even knowing what the end goal is supposed to be. Now you can still solve most of them by just running around trying different buttons until something progresses, but they are way more frustrating than they need to be.The game also offers combat which is by far its weakest point. Your weapons are extremely slow to use, ammo is pretty much non-existent, and enemies take way too many hits to kill.  In addition figuring out what objects block enemy procetiles boils down to just guessing as there seems to be no real logic behind it. Especially in act 3 puzzle and combat flaws become obvious, bringing the game to a crawl.Lastly there is absolutely no lore or any explanation for who and where you are or what is going on which is kind of disappointing since the environments are quite interesting and I would have hoped for more information about any of it. Although you can probably argue that this is intented.All that negative feedback aside if you can get the game for a discount to just experience the art style and the visuals it’s still probably worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Would not recommend this game, it looks cool, and if like me you like H.R Giger then there is certainly a lot of that, unfortunately that is all there really is, take away the aesthetics and all there is a somewhat mediocre at best, frustrating at worst game. The puzzles are dull or just irritating, combat is frustrating and while most of the time you can avoid foes or just flee you can get cornered by some foes, and there's a mandatory boss fight at the end that you have to take down in a specific way and was a chore to fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly, highly recommended -- for some people.If you find the screen shots intriguing, buy it, even at full price.   If you don't like the first hour, refund it.  It's the most horribly beautiful game I have ever played.  The level designs are wonderful, shamelessly cribbed from the graphic art of H. R. Giger and Zdzisław Beksiński.  Excellent sound work, too. If you aren't interested in the art style and mood, skip it.  The gameplay is adequate, the puzzles are decent but not groundbreaking.  Don't buy the game for those alone.  80% of my enjoyment of this game was staring awestruck at the world they built.Be prepared for body horror.  Lots of body horror.  And some ethical horror.  No way you come out of this game proud of yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is my 4th(?) attempt to write a review for Scorn. I wanted to do so in the same way i usually do, i wanted to do a shorter version, i wanted to do a funny crackpot version with phrases like "let's cut open big monster milkers to open an elevator" thrown around. So let's try this instead:You won't find a Giger style and atmosphere done better anywhere else.It is well-polished and well-paced, lacks any game breaking or obvious bugs, and is generally a pleasant game to be in. Minus the Giger stuff, of course. The environments could probably rival Doom Eternal's scenery, design of various devices and weapons is great, though, it hardly extends to the enemies. And devs honestly tried to put enough thought and effort into non-focal parts of the game. It is no Doom, but using guns is fun. There's no stealth, so you don't need to worry about bullchit detection range, don't need to crouch or stare at a locker door for half the playtime, and stamina is infinite.It has a lot of body horror and visceral imagery, but it is hardly a horror game.It has guns and resource management, but it is no survival-horror or a shooter.It has puzzles, but few of them hard enough to be a problem.So Scorn lands somewhere in the limbo of walking simulators, missing the usual parts of exploring stuff through dialogues and documents, while having weird appendages of a horror shooter, protruding from odd places. If you want something concrete from one of these genres, look for something else. If you don't mind chimeras, you can try it out.It is short enough to keep the style fresh, but it IS short enough to make a 40$ price tag questionable. + a lot of what was advertised about the game went under a knife, meaning most of the stuff you'll see in old trailers and screenshots isn't even there.

_childDocuments_.review: This review was written at launch and might not reflect the current stage of the game.In many instances, Scorn is very similar to the 2012 film Prometheus: both use “biomechanical” art style created by H.R. Giger, lead artist of the 1979 movie Alien; the two have similar music style and a similar pacing and vibe to storytelling; and they both stirred some controversy for the somewhat misleading marketing: Scorn was marketed as first person shooter, but it essentially is a walking simulator with some shooting; while Prometheus emphasized on the connection with Alien, throughout the movie you only see the iconic xenomorph for less than a minute. Audiences have polarized opinions to them too: some think it (the game or the movie) is absolute boredom while some think it is a work of genius. It is important to set your expectation straight so you don’t blindly jump into what you might not like.Despite the controversy, people universally praise the game’s stunning visuals and art style. Aside from “biomechanical” style, the game took inspiration from Polish artist Zdzisław Beksiński, whose works are best described as “Lovecraftian style”. Lots of twisted body parts, cut-off limbs, exposed flesh and blood, give a bizarre, living-being feeling to environment design. Color psychology is also in effect to convey emotion and feeling, as different sessions use distinct colors for certain vibes. In short, light and shadow, brightness and darkness, color and contrast, line and shape are all meticulously crafted for the mixture of simplicity from machinery and grotesqueness from flesh: it looks beautiful and evil at the same time, and playing this game is like walking in concept art.Music only briefly appears on certain occasions, but it is very on point and precisely conveys the feeling at that moment. The only flaw is the lack of spatial audio, causing some confusion during combat.Scorn is pretty hands-off in terms of guidance with minimalist UI elements. You wake up in a pile of flesh and no one tells you what to do or where to go, and you are on your own finding a way to proceed, which is very immersive because it is what would happen if the scenario was real. No guidance sounds harsh, but it is actually not bad, since Scorn accommodates it with organized and relatively simple, mostly linear map design. There is no messy way crossing and paths are either where you should proceed, or short dead ends that offer resource replenishment. The game has a few non-linear areas that require minimal backtracking, but I don’t think players would stumble too long because the map structure is not easy to get lost in as long as you have a sense of direction.Based on the gameplay, the game is divided into three parts (which all have corresponding color themes): walking and puzzle sessions, combat sessions, late game boss fight and puzzle sessions, taking me a little over 6 hours to finish.The starting puzzle is actually the hardest one, but as long as you realize it is a multi-stage puzzle, it is not so bad, and the rest are all mechanical puzzles and environmental puzzles. There is no universal logic to the solution, but they are very intuitive and easy anyway, except for the wheel puzzle in mid game (I don’t understand how I solved it but I just did). Puzzle session has nothing innovative or captivating, but it is good enough to fill up content.Combat is much more interesting by comparison. Scorn is not the traditional kind of shooter where you just blast every enemy to kingdom come, combat is actually puzzle solving in disguise, similar to Superhot. As the game plays like survival horror, you get a very limited amount of ammo and healing. Hence you have to find an optimal way to make each bullet count and not get hurt, which involves choosing the right kind of weapon, doing the right movement in combat and catching the right timing to attack, and these change when you face different enemy types.Combat is innovative, and the survival horror aspect is very pressing, as I basically used up my ammo right when I found a supple point, which is good. Perhaps the game tries to create tension from sluggish control like old Resident Evil, moving, aiming, reloading and swapping weapons are all slow despite shooting itself feeling good and powerful. But correspondingly, enemies are slow too, so they actually make a decent combat experience.The only exception is when you only get the starting weapon, which is a hammer-like melee-ish weapon that deals short-range damage and has a long cooldown. At that point in the game, players lack combat skills and experience. With slow movement and aiming, and a hard-to-use weapon, this session feels very bad. It can argue that the bad experience is to force players to realize you are not just shooting but to find a way to solve a puzzle  It is an interesting approach to teach mechanics, but I don’t think it is smart to purposely make the game feel bad. Fortunately, this session only lasts 20-30 minutes and it gets much better after you get the second weapon.In real life, we often can’t see the whole picture and have to puzzle out an event with a few clues we have, which is the spirit of environmental storytelling and how Scorn handles its story in an immersive way - you go places, see stuff, experience things, and you interpret the story on your own. Many games use this method: Little Nightmare, Haydee, Elden Ring and Dark Souls (but these two have dialogues and written descriptions) etc., but Scorn is a more obscure one as it is full of symbolism and mysticism.  yet the charm of an open story is everyone can interpret on their own, which is why I like its story and think this method is brilliant, though it does require players to have good observation and imagination.I quite enjoy Scorn for what it is: stunning art, innovative combat, interesting storytelling, except the starting weapon session is a little rough. But seeing the mixed reception, I don’t think it is for everyone even without the misleading information. I hope this review can help you to think it through.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare case where I don't regret buying this game without checking its user score.Wow this game is something else. Both technical and creative sides of it are excellent. I enjoyed A LOT being in the world of Scorn and experiencing its horrors.Pros:+ Level design+ Visuals+ Sound design+ 0 bugs+ No jumpscares+ Totally brutalCons:- Just 3 different types of enemies. Gameplay gets a bit repetitive but not too much, the game itself is pretty short.- 60% puzzles 20% stealth 20% shooting- In some levels/puzzles it's unclear what is expected from you. I had to play with a help of walkthrough, but overall levels are designed well and you're locked in a very limited area with very limited number of choices.Scorn is a unique experience and pure art. It's rare to play something like that nowadays. Unfortunately, gaming community doesn't seem to appreciate it much.85/100

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about a Benadryl addict and his daily commute through post-Brexit Birmingham. Your job is to go around sticking your hands in as many random organisms and machine parts as you possibly can, just to see what happens!But on a serious note, this game creates an amazing atmosphere with its superb sound design, extraordinary creatures, and beautifully created environments. I can’t say I found myself scared at any point in time, and it could get quite confusing trying to figure out how to backtrack to specific areas, but there was a good sense of progression overall. You could usually figure out where to go or what to do, just not always simultaneously.The devs leave you to find out pretty much all of the mechanics by yourself, which in this case isn’t necessarily a good strategy. It took me four back-to-back deaths and a quick Google search to find out that the plumbus-looking thing was an estus flask, and that was one of the earlier discoveries I made (About halfway through the game).The main issue of this game is the combat, which for the most part isn’t fun or innovative in any way. Many of the enemies hit for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of damage, and scripted events can also deplete your health significantly. Enemies are hard to handle in groups, which is often how you’ll encounter them, and ranged enemies in particular can be quite the hassle when accompanied by friends. Dying greets you with an extremely long animation, followed by an equally long loading screen, and usually a checkpoint just far enough away to be inconvenient and mildly infuriating. I understand that it’s the kinda game where combat is meant to be a last resort, but given the claustrophobic map design and prevalence of ranged attacks, you end up having to fight more often than you probably should. There is also a distinct lack of health pickups, many of the branching paths often leading to dead ends or ammo pickups, which usually just restock the ammo you spent to get there, leaving your health at a net loss.On a technical note, there are some very mild performance issues on the higher graphical settings, and I did have monsters clip through the world from time to time (Although I’m not necessarily complaining about that part), but it was otherwise bug-free.I can’t say it’s exactly what I was expecting to get after watching the original teaser back in 2016, but it’s definitely what I needed after bingeing the Ripley saga and craving more of that Gigeresque goodness. For the price I paid, I do wish it was a little longer (Keeping in mind that I got it 35% off). Free DLC is always a possibility, but given that it took roughly 8 years to craft this 5 hour experience, I don’t see it happening anytime soon, let alone for free.

_childDocuments_.review: Immersive walking-sim that is the embodiment of Giger's work. Stunning presentation with rich environmental storytelling and a few clever puzzles. Slow pace plus very annoying enemy encounters will make this a hard sell for a lot of people, especially giving the play time that averages around 4 hours... That being said, I've had a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I want so badly for there to be more to experience in this game. It's one of the most fascinating games I've ever played and it introduces you to far too little and ends far too soon. The Art/Lore book goes on to show how much of this world that ended up being cut. Two whole new areas and seemingly dozens of different "husks".I wish they wouldn't have started over in 2020 and speed developed the game in around two years. This universe deserves to be fleshed out.That's what I'm left with when I think of this game, how much it is one of a kind, how much it has stuck with me after finishing it and how much I wish there were more to it. I respect if this was their vision, but I can't help but feel like they wish they could've included more as well. Worth it on sale, but for most, probably will leave you feeling disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually impressive and very unsettling, but feels hollow and devoid of content.With extremely basic puzzles and no story (not even a Dark Souls style "A world was here before" story emerges through context), the abrupt ending at what feels like the half-way point is just insulting. It took me 4 hours to complete the game, and I looked in every nook. The start of the game feels way more complex and developed than the latter portions, leading to a clear image of the game development. A real shame as the imagery and sound design feel like the base for a potentially fantastic project.Do not purchase for anything more than 90% discount.

Amazing unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good thing first. The Style and Atmosphere is Amazing, if you are a Fan of Giger like art that is. And if all you want is too walk through a Giger painting, go fo it.As a game however.... i cannot believe that this has been in Development for so long (nearly 8 years) and this is the end result.For what you are getting it is astounding that this has been in development for ages, a bunch of indie Developers could have done 10 times as much content with that amount of time, if maybe not nail the art Style like this. The lack of content and "story" is a slap in the face and a kick to the nuts to be honest, especially for the price.It is really sad because I was personally very hyped for this and though i was Visually well entertained it was way to short. Maybe if some content gets added later down the line I will change my judgment but for now I sadly cannot recommend to buy it for the full price.Just one more thing as i have seen it mentioned a lot here in the reviews, I think the Puzzels are neither to easy or to hard, they are pretty normal for games Like this, if Compared to Amnesia, Soma and alike. The Combat feels a bit weird at times, although i managed to only die once at a Certain Special enemy and that was it. I found it, if not unnecessary, just a bit weird.I would recommend to wait for a sale and pick it up for 10 - 15 Bucks. Sorry....TL:DR Wonderful Artwork, Bad Game.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a game that was created with the talents of a world class artist, a world class sound designer, and a world class writer, and an AWFUL game designer. the game play is simply completely terrible. level design is confusing and its easy to get lost, movement, gun play, and enemy encounters are terribly designed or completely bare bones, and there is zero repeatability. I still think its worth it to an extent because the art direction and sound design are simply that good, but be warned that if you go in expecting anything fun out of the game play you will be very disappointed. simply put, if you took away the aesthetics and atmosphere of scorn, you would be left with absolutely nothing of value. I very much hope that the concept for this game can one day be remade into a new game that's actually fun to play considering how there is nothing else that looks like scorn out there on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game. Tired of shooters with generic stories and gameplay. This is not a shooter and certainly not generic. DO NOT run through this game. Take your time to examine the rooms, the objects, the mix of bio and mechanical functions and try to figure out what happened and what is going on. Each room and corridor tells a story if you'll take the time to absorb it all.It's heavily atmospheric with strange machines and a distinct lack of sameness. It's sad and beautiful at the same time. Something terrible happened here and that was a long, long time ago. Probably many thousands of years. I've not played a game in a long time that has captivated me like this one. I think about it during the day and night pondering the purpose of this machine and that corpse. It's that engrossing.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR H.R Giger meets walking sim - horror game, wait for a sale and don't expect the gripping game play experience that was promised.Long version : This game is a beautiful visual experience, however what little game play exists is shallow and at times tedious. For everything else it’s a H.R Giger style Disney ride. You're thrown into a world of wonder and mystery with no explanation as to why and only your thoughts to fill the void. There is a story to be told here but the story told is lacking to say the least. The world grips you with its stunning visuals but falls short of anything meaningful or thrilling.It teases you with moral ambiguity but gives you no choice on how to proceed except for “do the scripted thing”. The game desperately needs a driving motivator for the character you play and fails to provide even a simple “you must escape or else”. Combat is simple in nature right up until a boss fight which breaks immersion quickly if you don’t completely understand how to beat it on the first try. The game's description straight up lies to you, it’s not open world, there are cutscenes which pull you out of your body and I can tell you for certain that whoever wrote it could make watching paint dry sound interesting. I unfortunately can’t recommend this game due to the steep price. There’s nothing wrong with a nice looking, walking sim horror game but it’s simply not worth the asking price at launch for the 4 hours of game play that is here, and I took my time wanting to take in the sights. Wait for a good sale and then maybe play it. Better yet watch your favorite streamer or YouTuber play it and forgo the awkward combat all together.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good game.I'm several hours into this thing and I have to say it's more frustrating than anything. The puzzles aren't intellectual, they're stumble around until things work out sort of thing. They're a very few clues to tell you what order you have to do things. The visual aesthetic is fun, but the monotone colors and unrelenting textures means you can miss a lot very easily because nothing stands out. I've missed an important tunnel several times just because it's a small hole off to the right and I just didn't see it.The puzzles give you vague clues of what you're supposed to do, but on the whole it's mostly just trying everything until something works.Combat is useless. The enemies are pretty dodgy as well. I've had them disappear, and then reappear behind me when there was no way they could have been there.The most frustrating thing for me though is as I'm going through the game I'm wondering what the point is. Who are these idiot aliens who have designed even the most simple systems to be complex puzzles that they have to solve. It's no wonder they don't seem to be doing very well. I also don't understand what my purpose is in this game, although I'm certain it's an escape with my life sort of thing. It's just not very obvious.Kind of entertaining for the design, grossness and neat alien landscape, but that's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Along with many others, I cannot recommend this game with the current price tag of $40. Even the current discount to $35.99 is not enough.Although the game's atmosphere, animation quality, and visual fidelity are top-notch and capture the essence of H.R. Giger's artistry, the game's length runs about my play time of 4 hours, give or take an hour if you stumble on certain puzzles, or if your deep-grooved brain comprehends them right away. To be fair, the puzzles are excellent and have just the right amount of difficulty to give you that great dopamine dump of achievement when you solve them. The gun-play is fine, and you seem to get just enough ammo to get through segments with many enemies. Even the sound of the guns are fantastic, beefy, and pack a punch. At the end of this game, I wanted more. Not much more, but a nice 8-12 hour trek would have been worth my money. Many people will tell you to open your mind to the possibility of games that are "quality" and not quantity, but a game sold at $40 should at least hit that 8 hour mark, and I think a lower price would also lower player expectation to understand that this is a short game. On a secondary note, there is some real meat here for a long-form game, but it sounds like the devs cut a lot of content and wanted to get it out there. Sometimes, it's better to make sure the game stays in the oven for longer, instead of producing an okay carrot cake. Some people like carrot cake, but if you're like me, you don't want to spend $40 on one.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro: 1.Looks awesome, a great soundtrack and sound design.Cons: 1."...non-linear fashion..." ??? this game is as linear as it can get.2."...acquire different skill sets..."   like what? In the end, you as unskilled  as in the beginning (no level up or any other equvivalent system).3."... open-ended world..." see 1st.4. "All the storytelling happens in-game..." means: just look at guts and bones around you (and there are a lot of short cut-scenes).5. "Different play styles will be needed to advance." means: we will force you to play as we please and you can not run past or spare enemies.6. "Environmental storytelling", more like environmental guessing of a non-existent story. I'm in love with games that do not shove their lore in your face (my favorite example is Dark Souls), but at this point, it is just a pure absence of any comprehensible story.7. The ending was much worse than I expected (at that moment my expectations has been low already).8. The combat system is utterly terrible: slow, monotonous, repetitive, unavoidable, and there is a lot of it. It is really noticeable that it never was meant to be in the game.9. Really SHORT. I played really slow, to see every detail and appreciate the visuals, and still finished it in 6 hours. Realistically you can do it in 3 or fewer hours.10. Considering everything above, the price is laughable. Wait until -50% at least.God, I'm sorry for those unfortunate souls who waited for 5 years for THIS.Conclusion:1. It is an ATMOSPHERIC game. Not a shooter, not storytelling, and not a challenging puzzle game. The visuals and sounds are mesmerizing... but that is all. I do believe such Cons are caused by miscommunication between devs and the public. If to see the most common description by devs, it is a "... game set in a nightmarish universe of odd forms and somber tapestry..." which is completely true. But all the other stuff was thrown in without a thought.2. If you enjoy Ginger and Beksiński, you will love it.3. This game is a mere shadow of what it could have been gameplay and story-wise.4. If devs and new content/choises/endings/locations/actuall story/anything, it might get better.I do want to love this game. But considering all its problems, I can barely like it. What a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style reminds me of Aliens mixed in with eXistenZ. It is a game brimming with atmosphere and immersion, but there is very little to no story line. You  travel from one place to another without knowing where you are going or for what reason. This exploratory element can be exciting, but not knowing the whole game just begs the player to ask when is this going to end? For the lack of direction, I cannot recommend it unless you are solely drawn to this kind of art-style.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I liked the game setting, and story. Wish it was longer and would purchase the sequel/DLC if it ever comes.Pros: Great setting and environmental storytelling, which is the bread and butter of this game. There is a lot to take in at all times, from minute details in architecture to grand landscapes of biomechanical structures, to grotesque enemies. The puzzles take a minute to figure out mechanics, but are relatively simple once you figure out how they work. Cons: There is no dialogue either spoken or text, and as such it is often difficult to ascertain one's next steps. Absent mindedly missing a corridor can lead to backtracking and wandering around looking for something new to interact with.  Thankfully cutscenes are pretty obvious about what happened and what to do next, and the environments are interesting enough that a short jaunt off of the rails is still enjoyable as there are always small details and environments to enjoy. The combat can feel clunky, mostly due to having to aim before one can take a shot. This creates a delay between deciding to fight and acting that feels frustrating. However, the best choice in many cases is to avoid fights. Once you've seen the one or two execution animations, it feels like a waste of ammo. That said, this game could do without combat in general. The enemies add challenge and are scary, but not being able to retaliate would have made for much more tense scenarios imo.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has atmosphere to spare, but isn't terribly long. playing at a normal pace i was able to finish in around 5 hours. this isn't really a problem outside of price, which is subject to change the longer the game is out, and pacing-wise the game never really overstays its welcome.It IS a survival horror game, however light. A good tip that I wish I knew earlier is that a large portion of the enemies in your way are actually unaware of you at first and are busy heading to rest somewhere, so if you give them space you can save a decent amount of ammunition, only fighting the more aggressive ones.This game was in development for nearly 10 years but there is clearly still a lot of cut content, I hope that with the money it has raised so far, the devs might make something more fleshed-out (pardon the pun) and fully-realised. If the artbook is anything to go by, they clearly have a few more ideas left in them.

_childDocuments_.review: The question that always comes to mind with very specific games is: What are we? What is the human body and mind? How did it actually came to be? Questions that only bring despair and the inevitable feeling of being small and insignificant compared to the bigger picture, few games have had that theme and actually portrayed in a playable and long lasting way for me, games I’ve played like the Nier Saga, Parasite Eve, Dragon’s Dogma, and now, Scorn, some of the elements in those games being tightly knotted in sweet cosmic horror.As you have probably realized by now, I’m a big fan of feeling like a worthless speckle of dust in the universe, Lovecraft horror/Eldritch games are one of my most painful pleasures, there are not a lot of games that can encapsulate the feeling of being someone or something else and knowing from the beginning that you will fail or at least that it’s going to cost you everything you have, if you have anything else but your insignificant life given in-game to begin with, but you still do it, you still play the game, why? For me feeling that cosmic horror drain in my brain is the best, getting my life questioned into the ground until I finally finish the game, only to realize that the base of the experience of being questioned in the first place is you being alive, playing a game made by someone else’s ideas, dreams and terrors, for me the human experience is best when reminded of how fragile and insignificant it is in a universal way.In the end, you are still sitting there, living, breathing, experiencing, being reborn in the idea that none of what you saw would have any meaning if your life wasn't worth everything to begin with, if that is not a good enough reason to buy this game I don't know what is.The puzzles sucked though.

But I dunno, I'm not even halfway thru the game yet, I just got tired of getting spat on by the tamarind-shaped and chicken thing creatures, having only the tool gun to defend myself (which takes FOREVER to recharge) so I stopped for a while lol. Might change my review later when I finish the game.edit: Finished the game. Ok I feel kinda guilty. I think this game doesn't deserve the thumbs down. I can see a lot of work and effort were put into it. The sound design and visuals are GREAT❤️, very eye pleasing for enjoyers of grotesque art like me. The downside for me is that the game is too short for the price. I don't mind the lack of combat, stealth mode, or whatever people are complaining about, it's just the length (and price maybe?) that bothers me lol. If only I could give a neutral review but there's no option for that so..oh well, taking back my thumbs down and giving my thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: SCORN REVIEW FROM ADVENTURE/PUZZLE GAMER PERSPECTIVEIam an adventure gamer. I never wanted combat from this game, i never really cared for its "monster-chasing" elements, and i did not wanted a walking sim neither - i love hardcore puzzles, coming from Myst type games, Quern, Mysterious Island, Return of the Obrah Dinn. Those are my anchors for this review. The use of my brain is what i expected... so, what i got?*GRAPHICSThe graphical representation of this game is simply perfect, you could even call it an interactive artbook if u wish. The biomechanical, organic type design follow Giger's steps and its working for the worldbuilding very well. Its gross, also melancholic on its own way. *PUZZLESHere we go. I am hugely disappointed what the game offers in the name of "puzzles" or "solvable objects". Almost every single objective in this game is a pixelhunting in a biomechanical labyrinth. We get a huge walkable level every time, they sprayed out 5-6 levers, switches and keys, and u have to find them in the exact order. Thats 80% of Scorn. If u miss a door, or a lever, u can add 1-2 hours to your gameplay easily by walking up and down again, and again, and again.And DON'T BE MISLEADED by walkthroughs that are 2-3 hours long. Yes, they are, if they know exactly, where are these objects on the map. But if you want to finish it alone, you will running around like a madman for hours. So - my main problem... and i will COMPARE this game to titles, yes - lets talk about Quern, the best puzzle game ever made in ma opinion. Every single machine in QUERN is like a little minigame, a sole puzzle - and even part of a bigger puzzle as well. You have to learn how those machines work, their rules, find their parts, move their parts, solve the engines, the machinery and make them to start working. There is nothing more interesting for me in these type of games, than repairing, fixing alien devices and making them work.So how about Scorn?Scorn is an alien world as well, it has alien devices... HOWEVER... i can count maybe 2 or 3 machine that actually were a "puzzle" and even them were way too easy and short. Devs: it you simply hide 32 switches in a huge map - please, don't call it a puzzle. Go play quern, and learn, how puzzles made of. (the pulling wall at the beginning of the game was kind of okayish).STORYSo, if the game lacks puzzles, at least it should have a good story. Which it has not. I mean, yeah, sure, environmental storytelling. I would call it: setting. If you cut out half the game, and you give artbooks to a players to try to invent some story into it, thats just wont work. I can see the metaphoric nature of this game, i can invent 120 different theories about birth, reproduction, a fall of a civilization based on flesh engineering, artifical birth, or anything - which themes are heavily involved in this game - BUT STILL... these are "elements" of the worldbuilding, and i cannot call it a story. COMBATAnd at the end u have something - they try to call combat. I won't. Its terrible, annoying and frustrating. I will be short: every single encounter is terrible in Scorn. The game stinks from combat, it simply doesn't needed a combat system AT ALL. It should have been a nice puzzle - adventure game with alien devices and a good storytelling. Iam sorry, i know so many years went into it's production, and there has to be the most talented graphic designers on the team, becouse the atmosphere and the world is beautifull... ...but at the end of the day, there is a word, that every game should feature, and its called:F U N A video game should and would have FUN. In every genre. The gameplay should be fun, should give u satisfaction. That never happenes here. The puzzles are non existant, or too easy, or simply endless pixelhunting labyrinths. Combat is disaster, story is not a story. Could not recommend it, not for 40 euro. 40 EURO? Man... Which country do you live in? I mean, i thought you are from serbia... Which is similar to Hungary.... you know exactly how insanely unfair and bad this pricing is if we really dive into gameplay. Its better for people to get the artbook then and watch it...

_childDocuments_.review: Scorn is an atmospheric first person horror adventure game set in a nightmarish universe of odd forms and somber tapestry. It is designed around an idea of "being thrown into the world". Isolated and lost inside this dream-like world you will explore different interconnected regions in a non-linear fashion. The unsettling environment is a character itself. Every location contains its own theme (story), puzzles and characters that are integral in creating a cohesive lived in world. Throughout the game you will open up new areas, acquire different skill sets, weapons, various items and try to comprehend the sights presented to you.

name: World War Z
detailed_description: WORLD WAR Z: AFTERMATH Experience 6 new zombie-ravaged missions from around the world and a heart-pounding new perspective with Aftermath’s immersive new First-Person Mode. About the Game World War Z is a heart-pounding co-op third-person shooter for up to 4 players featuring swarms of hundreds of zombies that has now captivated over 20 million players. Based on the Paramount Pictures film, World War Z focuses on fast-paced gameplay while exploring new storylines from around the world. Humanity is on the brink of extinction. From New York to Moscow to Japan and Jerusalem, the undead apocalypse continues to spread. As the end looms, a hardened few band together to defeat the horde and outlive the dead. Battle swarms of hundreds of zombies The Swarm Engine™ seamlessly renders hordes of zombies in incredible firefights. Advanced gore systems offer gruesomely satisfying action. In-game Zombie Hordes behave like real crowds, getting stuck in narrow corridors and climbing on top of each other to reach players on higher levels. Hordes become increasingly more difficult to defeat and behave like single entity bosses as players progress through the game. Coop story-driven campaigns Survive around the world, as unique groups tell their stories of perseverance. Choose Your Class Level up to 8 unique classes – Gunslinger, Hellraiser, Slasher, Medic, Fixer, Exterminator, Dronemaster and the new Vanguard class in WWZ: Aftermath – each with their own unique perks and play styles. Deep Progression Grow stronger – unlock powerful weapon upgrades and level your character class to take on greater challenges. PVPVZ Fight other players for survival – several intense Player vs Player vs Zombies game modes complement the coop campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: Vermintide 2 was my introduction to this type of game.  I have never been a huge fan of zombie games, but this one has me hooked.  The grind to upgrade weapons and classes feels a bit slow, but overall it keeps you with goals to work towards (which I love).  The difficulty settings have a wide range to allow for solo play if you like, but the real fun is found in coop mode with friends.  The AI of NPC allies is really terrible since they jump into your line of fire, taking damage, and they aren't intuitive enough to be useful.  The best thing they do is help you up  when you are overwhelmed.  That aside, if you like Vermintide, or Left for Dead, you will find simliar elements here.
_childDocuments_.name: World War Z

_childDocuments_.review: It's like L4D but with an actual progression system (Classes with specific abilities, weapon levels), it actually gives the game purpose so that you have a reason to repeat campaigns and/or go to higher difficulties. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much brain-dead. Run around, shoot zombies ( A LOT ) and press buttons in rather short campaign maps. That is not to say that the game is not fun. It has it's moments but it is dragged by MANY design choices, to a level of just another average zombie game. To start with, the campaign ranges from cool looking cities to underground facilities and even massive ships. Sadly you never get to explore much, as all of the levels are linear and quite frankly short and forgettable. There is no level destruction aside from scripted areas and you can't even shoot a zombie through a glass. There is a bullet hole in a window.... but the zombie never takes any damage. Really breaks immersion.Game is missing a DODGE functionality, this is especially annoying when trying to avoid special zombies that will home in to player's location. Your only choice is either to listen to audio ques and be ready to shoot or simply running away which is not always working. Player's can use melee which is way stronger than your basic pistol or smg but you are only allowed limited uses. It works a bit like SHOVE action from Left 4 Dead. Creates some space for the player to either run or shoot. First person mode is bad. There is no proper aiming with your weapons and using melee reverts back to third person view... so it break the whole immersion. Why was it even added ? Beats me.Zombies can have broken attack hitboxes so occasionally you will be hit from 2-3 meters away yet no enemies around in immediate vicinity of the player... Everything can look gory up-close but the moment you start blowing things up from anywhere longer than 20 meters away, suddenly there isn't much blood or limbs flying around. Bodies despawn faster than you can shoot them breaking the immersion further. Now I understand they had to do it this way otherwise the performance would tank but it is what it is. Classes are awfully similar to each other with mostly passive bonuses so at the end of the day you will be shooting, blowing up or slashing zombies. Leveling up is grindy especially because of the prestige perks that can only be obtained by reaching max level and resetting your character class to 0. There are weapons in the game available that can offer max stats out of the box. I am not sure whether they are part of Aftermath bundle but it kinda spoils the progression for weapon trees, as there is no point of choosing worse version of assault rifle when you have decked out version for free.Cosmetics are available only through hard earned currency which is gained at snail pace by playing on highest difficulties or completing challenges. Fear not however because most of the cosmetics sucks. Add to that the fact you have TONS of characters that are linked to specific campaigns and you probably won't be caring much... neither did I. Ultimately the game is as average as it can get. I had problems finding players so waiting in the lobby for 15 minutes only to find one person is not unusual. There is no ANTI CHEAT, therefore I recommend playing PvP or PvE campaign with friends only. Game will not let you play online unless you accept the DATA COLLECTION. Which is another aspect that I don't like in modern video games. Extra launchers / accounts and data collection. I think only gamers have so low customer standards or simply are not caring enough to allow such practices to thrive. I do not recommend this game unless you have friends to play it with. A.I bots are awful. Can't handle anything more than normal mode. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Once I figured out how certain things varied from Left4Dead, and then upped the difficulty to at least level 3, the game became a lot more fun. In L4D you can mostly gather in a corner and shove and shoot through a horde until the tank comes.  In WWZ you need to keep your feet moving, but still keep your team in site and protected, or you’ll be quickly overwhelmed.  The stealth possibilities, headshotting a hallway of zombies with silenced weapons, is fun too but rare in matched games where someone is always shotgun happy.Anyway, game is totally entertaining and I’m sad to see the low review scores.  It is a lot like Left4Dead 3 might have been, minus the first person view.  No shoving though, just slicing and chopping which is admittedly more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z Aftermath is the definitive edition of 2019 World War Z, which is adapted from the same name movie. I played the original on Xbox Game Pass in 2020 and noticed some changes in this version, mainly including new content and improved AI. However, there is no life-changing improvement and the game remains mostly the same – if you don’t like it before, this version doesn’t give you any reason to. I still regard it as a repetitive zombie shooter that lacks depth.There is nothing wrong with a simple zombie shooter – we might even need that to ease our brains sometimes, which is why I played it back in 2020. But if you have played lots of games, such as, you have listened to the story of The Witcher, crafted your build and fought the Hollow in Dark Souls, or tasted the level design in Dishonor, then when you go back to mindlessly shooting zombies, you start to feel World War Z lacks the depth that keeps you playing. This is what I feel about this game. Technically, the game has weapon and character class systems for the depth, but in fact, they do so little to diversify the gameplay or make it more strategic or something. I am sure lots of people wouldn’t mind that, but for experienced players who have tasted masterpieces, I don’t think the gameplay will keep them engaging for too long. Mindlessly shooting zombies is easy to get bored.Above all, World War Z is a coop shooter like Left 4 Dead. I played Left 4 Dead 1 and 2, though I don’t feel the hot of Left 4 Dead either, I can tell Left 4 Dead is better than this game in many ways. Per se, in Left 4 Dead, special zombies like tank, charger and witch, are so memorable and iconic, whereas in this game special zombie is just zombie with special customs. Remember in Left 4 Dead every time a random witch is nearby, the background music can give you a spook? In World War Z, they don’t have similar input in sound design, which I don’t really mind, but the level design is so scripted that it eliminates all the element of surprise.  There are in total four types of level: walking – to reach one location from another; escorting someone/something; searching items/keys/switches or setting bombs; guarding locations and eliminating zombie hordes. When you only make four types of levels and recycle them throughout the whole game, it is lazy, boring, predictable and repetitive. It is not a joke to go fully autopilot in this game. Last but not least, AI is so dumb that I actually was mad at the original. It is improved in this version, but still leaves a lot to be desired: they don’t heal you or themselves; they always use the weakest beginning weapons; their character levels are always 0 despite you ungraded yourself to god-tier; three of them do less damage output than you alone; them going to save you is like the slowest thing in the world. In Left 4 Dead, the AIs are gods. Whereas here, their sole function is to save you when you are immobilized. Otherwise, they are completely useless.More about the AI problem: you can probably get by at normal difficulty, but at higher difficulty, you have to pair with real players since AI is so dumb and useless; every time you are in guarding location level, the game is going to be very hectic in a not-very-comfortable way, because AI won’t help you place defense kits and their damage output is not enough to withhold zombie hordes (wherever you don’t shoot at zombies are going to break through). It is not a friendly game for solo player because of the AI.There are still some redeeming qualities about this game, depending on how you judge a game. Shooting is top-notch and the greatest strength of this game – it is accurate, responsive, has comfortable recoil, nice shooting sound and good thrusting feedback. I say the shooting is worth 30 out of 40 USD of the price. Also, the game has good optimization. It runs great on low-end PCs even with hundreds of zombies running around. Graphics are way better than Left 4 Dead 2 if you have to make a comparison. But on the flip side, in first-person mode, movement control has a small but noticeable lag between button input and the character actually moving, causing this mode doesn’t feel as good and responsive as the third person. If you look close into the graphics, textures and models (particularly zombie models) are actually very rough. As a result, the iconic zombie pyramid scene doesn’t look as astonishing as it should be, which is what draws lots of people to buy the game. I personally don’t care much about the two, but they should be noted if they are your concern.In conclusion, I don’t recommend this game. The gameplay lacks depth making it easy to get bored, which you can say is more of a personal preference. However, I don’t feel much love was put into the game – the art design, the level design, the AI, all feel so sloppy, and it doesn’t even have an actual story. The shooting is undeniably good and graphics are half-decent, but I just don’t think they are enough to redeem the bad. You can still buy it if all you really look for is to shoot some zombies, but at least not at its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my low playtime here, I have been playing on and off since it's initial launch as an Epic store exclusive and was excited to finally be able drop it and move back to Steam.The new weapon upgrade system is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful. It wasn't great to begin with but it was infinitely more preferable than what we got now. There is no way to preview any of the new perks so you now have no idea what weapons are worth upgrading or what they even do when they get there.And the new hoard map is a mixed bag. While it's nice we finally have a new survival map that's a little more involved it feels needlessly complicated. There is no clear way to know where the zombies are coming from, or what route they'll take, or what the new traps do or even what areas are in bounds until you play it once, and even then it's confusing and easy to forget when you have dozens of zombies bearing down on you from every single direction.As nice as free updates are this one aint it, chief.So apparently some of my information was entirely wrong, and I feel kind of bad for not doing my due diligence and leaving a review while emotionally compromised. There is a way to see experience for a your current weapon, but it is tucked away and easy to miss if you don't know its there (In the in-game scoreboard at the bottom right). Also, needing to unlock new levels was actually how it worked before and there are others that claim that you can now level up multiple times in one run. Unfortunately, the one game I played to test these new features ended with me being hit with a glitch that did stop my weapon progression, which combined from my long absence from the game led me to believe this was the new system.I apologise for my mistake. However, my stance on the game still stands and anything I haven't struck through I feel is still perfectly valid, along with a few new criticisms, even if they are more minor. Customizing your weapon now feels entirely pointless since it is purely visual. A few guns seem to be nerfed with the removal of the silencer upgrade seemingly chosen arbitrarily, and others buffed for the same reason. Popular long standing weapon grinding spots seem to have also been nerfed in response to the leveling buff. All in all it seems like a mostly solid win but the increased grind makes it hard to recommend to anyone not interested in the grind, or have no one to grind with.

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to Left 4 Dead but with 100x the zombies, 40 upgradeable weapons, 7 campaigns, 8 classes with upgradeable perks, and the ability to switch between 1st and 3rd-person mode. It's a very fun COOP zombie shooter, and the progression system gives you plenty to work toward as you improve your weapons and classes.Optimisation and PC features are great. This runs on Unreal Engine 4, so you should have some idea of what to expect. Graphically it looks great, the controls are fluid and responsive, and you get options for field of view, film grain, etc. There's also AMD FSR for lower-spec PC's, though I haven't tried it myself. On a 2080 Super and i7 6700K, I've had no issues at all holding 144fps on the Ultra settings at 1440p. Smooth as silk and feels great to play.This 'Aftermath' version contains every single piece of content from the 2017 game, including all the weapon DLC's, the Game of the Year content, and the French expansion pack. It also includes 2 new campaigns, several new useful weapons, first-person mode, and a new Horde XL mode with even more zombies.The general gameplay is very much like L4D; 4 survivors in each campaign have to make their way through environments filled with hundreds of zombies, while completing objectives, flipping switches, fetching items or defending against waves of 1000's more zombies. It's a fun COOP experience, and very challenging on the harder difficulties.Each playthrough is randomised, with some areas having branching paths, different objectives, different weapons and gear, and different enemy counts. Sometimes you'll find areas filled with claymores, other times it will be hostile turrets, etc. It's fun not knowing how the mission will play out each time.During wave defence sections, you can pick up defensive items like Auto Turrets, Manual Turrets, Electric Fences and more, and place them in areas to help fend off the hordes. These are also randomized each time, so you might get unlucky and have very few useful defenses sometimes.There's somewhat of a stealth system too, so you need to prioritise suppressed weapons (and upgrading existing weapons with suppressors) so that you don't bring a horde of 200 zombies every time you fire your guns.There are special infected much like L4D; you've got the Bull (charger), Infector (spitter), Creeper (jockey), Bomber (boomer), Rat Swarms, and in October the 'Booster'. If any of these catch a lone player off-guard, it could mean their death.If you're a fan of L4D, I highly recommend checking this out!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hell of an interesting one - I would argue they have a better game and model than B4B and maybe even L4D at this point - gun work feels crisp on PC with M&K, there's crossplay, the level design is pretty fun (something about going country to country is actually super enjoyable) and overall the game feels good whether mowing down zombies one by one or in big packs with a ton of adds and deployable's. In sum, it feels like an actual zombie game - like real zombie game. Ill give it a positive, I think there are some cons, the matchmaking system you can tell is as unpolished as a dog turd, and generally speaking the weapon upgrade system makes little to no sense. It doesn't necessarily explain how you get cosmetic outfits in the early game, and the story (while we know it from the book and movie) feels like it could have been fleshed out so much more. But again, the maps feel good, gunplay feels good, and I may be enjoying this more than B4B which I put plenty of time in an early buyer, and the maximum tier of ultimate, dlc, whatever BS they sold to me - so I recommend this without a shadow of a doubt for anyone looking for co-op, "mow-em-down", zombie slaying gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend buying this unless you have a group of friends that you know want to play it with you already. I like the setting and enjoy the game itself but it's main componant (which is multi-player/co-op) is now pretty close to non existant. It's almost as dead as it's own zombies, in other words. Many of the levels are dependant on having a team to play with. You can really only get so far with the AI meat shields :D Finding a match up, let alone a good one is a few and far between sort of event. Sometimes you'll get lucky and snag one quick. More often than not though you'll be lost at sea wondering just how far from the nearest coast you are.Content wise, for this type of game, it's not really massively expansive. So far there's about 7 episodes with anything from 3-5 chapters each. You also get 8 different classes so if you want to level all of them up there's a fair amount of time you can burn on this game. The problem, really, is replayability. There's very little replay value once you've completed all of the episodes. The classes play different but like I said, it's finding a team that's the trick. co-op or multiplayer team finding can make an other wise one day task take 3-5 days because you'll be waiting to find teams so much. You can also play horde mode and horde mode xl. They're ok but similar to the call of duty survival matches, they can get boring pretty fast.Once you've gone through all of the maps it's pretty much a rinse and repeat cycle. I expected as much when I bought it but god I didn't expect multiplayer to be this dead after only four years old (base game. Two if you count its main dlc; aftermath).Edit: I actually found a slight work around for finding a team. Start from the episode you want and wait about 30-60 seconds. If you don't find a team, in that time frame, for your level then you can subsequently repeat the process on each episode, going backwards through the episodes. You'll find a team more often than not unless the gods of luck really hatin' on you.Find a team somewhere using that method and if you're very lucky they'll eventually get to the episode you're after. Team retention is still a problem though and you'll be hard pressed to find a team that'll stick for more than a full episode. So finding friends you know wanna play is still your best bet. But at least some progression is viable now.Edit: As pointed out by a commentator on my review, I have decided to add general area to my review.I play from the general area of London, England, UK, Northern Europe. This should tell you just how bad it is. Since my region should be one of the most active regions in the entire world. Probably only second to North America and maybe some parts of Southern Europe.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve seen the motion picture, this is a 1-1 recreation of it. 6/10, and please read the book. WWZ rewards skilled players for exploration, and helps beginners when they bunch up. The gameplay loop is fine, rewards map knowledge and quality aim. The game director is fair, it’s unlikely that you’ll be strung out without a medkit for too long, and specials aren’t normally spammed non-stop. The sound design is fair, graphics are fine and technical performance is sound. As of time of writing, the online population is still active, and it’s a coin flip between a chinese dronemaster or a lv999+ save file editor. It’s a game that’s best in small doses, and honestly, that’s a fine thing to be. Look, this game is middle of the road with a decent gimmick, and it’s sometimes fun enough to do just that. However, while this game isn’t bad, there are things wrong with it.  end of story. I feel permanently poor in WWZ. Grinding weekly missions, three daily missions, horde mode and daily challenges for challenge coins is awful. It’s restrictively expensive to levels and upgrades, and the rate of money earned is a pittance of what’s needed to buy the essentials. From my game time of 50+ hours of normal play, I still didn’t have lv5 on all weapons to get suppressors, something which the game doesn’t tell you. I’m nowhere near able to buy all the skills for a class tree, or cough up for unique weapon perks, I’d have grey hair before I get all of those. It’s no wonder that the people in matchmaking tend to use cheat engine to max out their classes, no-one wants to grind Marseille-2 checkpoints for money for thirty hours.   because the solo experience is flatly bad, and trying to beat 4 skulls+ difficulty with anything less than a full team is impossible. Bots are braindead, fall far behind players in kills to a comical degree, melee first and shoot later, have no sense of self-preservation, burn their healing items willy-nilly and refuse to use heavy weapons. They’re dated, useless, and are a genuine detriment to any team playing 3 skulls and above. Any buff for them would be an improvement in my books. At the end of the day, I can see why Epic games would let this game go non-exclusive. It’s fine, and for a middle-priced game, that’s ok.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that scratched the co-op zombie itch.While it is true there is something a little different here compared to Left 4 Dead, I believe that Saber Interactive delivered very well here.The main campaign follows various groups of survivors spread across the world map, each location having 3 or so maps associated with its own plotline. I really enjoyed this, while the characters are not as well developed as say the crew in Left 4 Dead  2, they offer their own personalities and quirks that play out as the levels progress. In contrast the Left 4 Dead characters were present in all of the campaigns and had more time to develop as the game went on.The core gameplay is very good, at first I was worried about the 3rd person view; but it actually is made very well, since the camera pulls back when you are aiming down sights and it feels like first person anyway (similar to Metal Gear Solid 5). The updated version on Steam gave us an option to play entirely in first person mode, though after trying it once I went back to the original designed viewpoint.The zombies feel threatening, and there are a bunch of specials in the mix as well. They are made quite different to Left 4 Dead’s offering, thankfully. The common zombies will blow apart depending on when you shoot them, with a bonus damage when hitting the heads; a crucial part of the higher difficulties. The zombies will sometimes dodge and weave around, making this a difficult task to achieve sometimes; adding to the threat and the immersion of the game.The maps are varied and very different in how they play out. Additional map variety occurs with some maps having routes that change, and the battle crescendo moments have defence hardpoints designed into them. The catch is that some defences will spawn randomly, and some defence crates will randomly spawn as well: these are 50-cal turrets, auto-turrets, car batteries attached to fences for stunning and frying zombies, barbed wire, and mortar launchers. The crates allow the player to choose where to place the defence, given a valid hardpoint that it matches with.As for the normal play, there are a very nice mix of weapons similarly divided into 3 tiers just like Left 4 Dead. Instead here we also got a weapon upgrade system, where each weapon is a slot and as you level up that weapon you can buy different versions which have different mods on them and different statistics. This progress was very fun to unlock and gave a gradual curve to managing the difficulty of the 5-point skull system.On difficulty, going from easy to extreme, the rule changes are consistent and the challenge is very real and insane and extreme; but not impossible. The idea I think is that you get a group of max level (at 30) players with max upgraded weapons and try to complete each map in extreme. This grants you an unlockable which is like a skinned version of the sniper rifle, this model granting bonus stats and special abilities on the weapon.Other weapons have a variety of unlocks as well, by ‘prestiging’ a class twice; you are granted a unique skin for their related default weapon (offering something different gameplay wise). Each prestige level resets your level to 0 for that class; and as you level it up again you are awarded bonus skills not previously accessible. This system gives some replay value and time to really learn a class. Since there are 8 classes in the game, there is a lot to try out and a lot of replayability here. Each class plays quite differently, and I have to say the levelling system and customisation on how you set up each class is very welcomed. Other stuff is the PVP mode, no comment from me since I don't bother with these modes to avoid toxicity. The challenge mode allows you to play the maps again to collect a set of 9 documents per map. When collecting these you unlock bonus chances for more loot/map aids when playing the maps. This is useful for beating the extreme difficulty on the standard campaign. Also the challenge mode has a normal and hard difficulty; and a set of random mutators that mix up the gameplay. In some cases the mutators make the hard challenge mode  even more difficult than the extreme campaign difficulty.A whole bunch of high difficulty modes and challenge modes (with daily and weekly bonus challenges) award you with blue coins. These can be used to unlock character skins and unique weapon skins (which have unique stats).The online play is pretty good, I haven’t had any major issues but I wish there were more controls of your lobby and a few more online player features. A note on the options and performance, pretty good selection to tweak the engine, and the option to switch from DX11 to Vulkan was very welcomed. The game in my opinion look very beautiful; the engine creates a very vivid world to play in. One of the best features in this game are the zombie hordes, which are something special to witness and never gets old.So in summary for me the class system, weapon upgrades, defence kits, and a few other additional features give something moreover than what Left 4 Dead 1 and 2 gave us. And I love that. I hope this game gets more updates and more DLC, because it is a very good co-op survival game.
