_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game.  If you like Left 4 Dead 2 and if you prefer TPS, this is for you.  The swarms are MASSIVE!Pros:- Simple and addicting gameplay- Classes (different gameplay per class)- Graphics and atmosphere with so many story telling details- Guns feel right and many to choose from- Each map has different vibes- Game modes: Solo/Coop Campaign | Horde Mode | PVP (dead mode)- Many characters to choose from- Improved bots for beginners and solo players (*THIS IS NEW UPDATE)- Mutators- FPS (for guns)- Surprise big updates- Nice communityCons:- Bugs - Sudden disconnections- Lobby bug (when someone leaves, player is still "there" hence no one can replace him/her)- Annoying specials (Quick respawning lurkers, Rats, Booster)- FPS (melee shifts to TPS - disorienting) - Lack of communication from devs (we don't know if they are still updating the game or done with it)- Surprise big updates (takes like 2 years)*NOTE TO BUYERS:- Buy World War Z: Aftermath or Deluxe Edition for better experience.- Buy World War Z only if you don't mind having no access to 3 chapters (France, Rome, Kamchatka) and FPS modeOverall:I have been playing this game for 2 years now and it earns my positive review.  With the current update, the game feels fresh for me.  The game is easy to pick and have fun.  I highly recommend this game if you are looking to fight zombie massive swarm with friends or solo.

_childDocuments_.review: I will try to keep it as short as possible;This game took L4D2 formula and tried to implement the aspect of: It is basically what would happen if Left 4 Dead and Killing Floor had a child.World War Z in my opinion is jack of all trades but master of none, the KF gameplay is much more repeatable, clean and satisfying and L4D2 formula cannot be copied. In order to unlock all features and perks you will need 500+ hours because developers made it as grindy as possible in order to stick you to the game as long as possible which is a double edge sword, you either get burned shortly after completing all campaigns (like me) or you grind it out to level 999 (max level) Cross platform co-op is a big No-No since console players cannot see chat and use voice communication nor any sort of communication with PC players, and I honestly suggest just leaving the party when you see console player in it.Introduction of First Person mode made this game in my opinion worth trying, I avoided this game because of its 3rd person Fortnite cartoony look, even with because major bugs in FP mode it is still good and worth trying.Overall this game will give you ~100 hours gameplay for sure, and for its price its absolutely worth it - especially if you have someone to play it with !

_childDocuments_.review: Just buy the DLC there instead for way cheaper. Unless you absolutely must play it on Steam for some reason. In that case have at it. Just be aware that this is just the same game you've had on Epic for years. It's not a sequel, it's not an expansion, it's the same exact dang game. There's absolutely nothing different about it, other than you have to start all over again from level 0 on all your classes and unlock all your fun weapons and such all over again.Some positive reviewers are saying it's ignorance on the part of people who feel scammed by this game, that this is just a re-release on a new platform which happens all the time. Hogwash! Nonsense! The description of the game on Steam is deliberately misleading. It says, "World War Z: Aftermath is the ultimate co-op zombie shooter and  of the  hit World War Z..." This makes it sound like a sequel. It is worded to sound like it's a different game. When you say a thing is the  of an , you're literally saying that that thing has changed over time from the original thing. You're saying the original is still the same, and that this new thing is different. Aftermath is no different from regular plain ol' WWZ. They're the same game on different platforms, that is all.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z  is a zombie survival game, takes place in the context of zombies dominating the world and "Aftermath" is an expansion pack with many notable additions to the co-op shooter. It added two new levels Rome and Kamchatka. Each level continues to be divided into three different chapters like the old episodes, but still has the same task requirements as what you experienced in the original game. Much of it revolves around defending the base and escorting the NPC to the gathering point. The quest design has not improved from before, especially the Rome stage, more or less leaving me a little disappointed because of this.Although the amount of new content is not too massive, this expansion still adds some interesting gameplay updates, making it more challenging and diverse than the original. Notably, the option allows players to switch back and forth between first and third person in the game experience. However, this feature is designed quite  "half-heartedly",  so it still feels a bit 'pretentious'. Specifically, the scope of most weapons becomes useless when experienced in first-person perspective. This is very evident when you let the character sit and shoot, the feeling is no different from the character when standing and shooting when compared to the experience of any FPS game. The game also have some miscellaneous bugs related to the behavior of the zombies. The 'force feedback' feature of the handle also does not convey the feeling of experience well. The most obvious is when performing "bull butt", Vanguard character class players do not feel the ironing power of the electric shield, so it is difficult to know if the attack hit the enemy or not.In overall from my point of view: This is a good game, things i love about the game is the survival horde mode, it can up to 3 hours of playing and the weapon + player class "ability".  BUT compare with the game made by Valve,  .  Personally i  this game due to the game + DLC price, we can still have lots of other better games with better price

_childDocuments_.review: I spend MONTHS looking at this game page, watching reviews, analyzing whether or not this was worth buying... And after purchasing , and immediately refunding it after 3 hours because the game felt like it was made by an indie studio, I then gave  a chance with the refunded money...Just make sure you get Aftermath too, since the 1st person mode is included in there. It's not "perfect" 1st person, seeing that you don't really "aim down sight"... But after a few minutes, you don't notice it anymore because you are too busy enjoying the game. :)Zombies feel incredible, and are VERY satisfying to fight. And the Horde mechanic is SO good, and gives you a "bad a**" feeling while you fight them. Which is important, seeing this was the ONE doubt I had about the game, since I was afraid that the quantity of zombies in the horde mechanic, would decrease the quality of them. THIS IS NOT THE CASE.The solo (offline) experience is decent, and I recommend giving it a go when you first buy the game, since you can enjoy the levels at your own pace. Also, if you join a public game with strangers, you mostly get pushed into a ongoing game, where they have already progressed the level quite a bit. Once you are happy with playing through the story, you can then increase the difficulty, and play with other strangers, for a more fun experience. :)There is also a good progression system, and MANY characters to choose from, which all have a back story cinematic, that you unlock by completing a level with that character.All in all, you will REALLY enjoy this, if you are looking for "the new Left 4 Dead" game. ;) Well worth the "non-sale" 40 euro price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: only worth the purchase on sale. Grinding for weapon upgrades is a slog because the devs introduced new mechanics to slow your progression down. Upgrading a weapon's level costs up to 4 or 5 missions on the highest difficulty worth of coins. Higher tier weapon perks like damage upgrades or +magazine size may require up to 3 complete documents, which can only be found while playing challenges. Most weapon perks are useless or too situational eg missing health to be useful. Weapon perk tree needs a complete overhaul. Plenty of people play on modded save files, so although they are max level, they still play terribly. TLDR Dev's don't know how to address player attrition so they put up lots of barriers to player progression and try to get you addicted to daily quests to promote longevity. Core game still fun but 'perks' and 'bonuses' do nothing but aggravate players. 'Cheaters' are everywhere

I think only half or maybe less of the characters have an alternate look, and every character has a recolour of their default look with maybe a accessory added on or swapped. _childDocuments_.review: Fun combat that involves shooting a lot of zombies in quick succession. The missions are simple and straight forward. You run around and shoot zombies and then hold your position against an army of them while you set up defense, rinse and repeat. There is a little "stealth" involved, but don't expect much, it's mostly not drawing attention to yourself by blowing stuff up or not using silencers. Lots of variety in the maps and the enemies have the usual suspects in variety. The challenge is just right (plenty of difficulties to choose with mutators if you want). Playing alone is not harder, the AI is using aimbot and you really need that. You can choose a class and progression to learn more skills in that class is pretty quick. Lots of weapons to choose and attachments to unlock for them. You can change your appearance but it's very limited. The optimization is just right (not great but good enough if you tweak the settings). The new first person mode is fun, but the game is clearly intended to be played in thirdperson. No mods needed so far to make the game more fun/playable. The game allows you to increase the FOV, customize the HUD, has full controller support etc. Also no unnecessary effects like vignette and filmgrain.The only complaints I have are the occasional performance problems (nothing major though, just some framedrop) and the fact that you can't pause the game when you play offline.

Although special zombies are a bit more challenging.Unfortunately, the UI in this game is a total disaster:Bots are super dumb. Playing solo with 3 bots is very difficult, even on the easiest difficulty. You really need some friends to play with.Weapons customisations seen on the screenshots are cosmetic skins only. Although once levelled up they have some perks. But those are a real end game - don’t expect to have any in the first 50h of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - worth every penny, tons of content to keep you entertained. A good game to jam out to your favorite playlist and just tear through zombies. Good ol fun mindless shooting that can also be serious when you want it to be. Ton of replayability !!Breath of fresh air! Takes me back to the good ol days of Payday 2 in a weird way. This game plays very similar to Left 4 Dead with a few differences. One of the biggest differences and one that keeps the game fresh is the good sized variety of guns to pick up and level up and a good variety of perks with varying skills to grind for and unlock. Each perk has different starting weapons which is nice, so youre not left scrambling over the good weapons when going about the level with your teammates. When things are working well and your team is cooperating, it is an absolute blast, playing now on hard and it can def be a challenge. Seeing the massive swarms hasnt gotten old and is awesome every time it happens. This game isnt reinvinting the wheel, its just a straight up zombie coop shooter with a nice leveling system.With Vulkan disabled I get pretty spotty FPS when huge crowds of zombies are around, I get anywhere from 60-144 on my i9 9900k 2080ti build at 1440p. However with Vulkan enabled on a mix of ultra and high I get over 144 pretty stably, occasionally I will drop to around 120-130 but it shoots right back up. This performance is while having a stream open and watching a podcast.

_childDocuments_.review: I just love this game since I bought it back then in the epic launcher (188 hours playtime there) and instantly bought it again on steam, as it got finally released on steam now.The game in itself is in most aspect a standard zombie coop shooter. Tho at the points that let World War Z stand out of the crowd, it REALLY shines.This mostly mean its hordes, as those hordes are the main focus of the movie and the books. It's just so amazing seeing over 100+ Zombies charging towards you while all you got is "just" a assault rifle / shotgun / sniper and so on. It's also equally awesome to just shred those hordes with all the possible defensiv devices / equipments / weapons you can have.Speaking of that, the weapons are pretty much standard guns you see in most of the current shooter games.Means you got your assault rifles, shotguns, sniper, machine pistols, pistols you get the idea. The equipments however are bound to the current class you are on. So each class has its own equipment which defines them. So you either can have e. g. molotovs, claymores, C4, Stim packs (health boost), ZAP-gun and so on. Most of the classes are pretty unique in their playstyle and function in a team. Only a few are a bit blurry in what they can do or should be used for.Before you fight a incoming horde you have a timer to prepare yourself and fortify your current location. For that you can find defence boxes which can include a stationary machine gun, an electric grid, automatic turrents for example. Basically, if you like shooting lots of zombies and burn / nuke / zap / bomb / shred zombies with either smart placed traps, lots of bullets or a good ol' 50 cal. you might love this game too. It does have some issues, but basically every game has some problems or issues anywhere but what they did amazingly well is to catch the theme and feeling of the World War Z universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent way, way more hours on Epic when they made it free during the pandemic, but decided to switch over out of spite and somewhat support the devs.It's a good game when you just want to jump in with some friends and shoot some zombies. WWZ feels polished and all of the classes feel satisfying to use, often because they feel cohesive and have something unique to bring to the table. The ones I've enjoyed are Medic, Dronemaster, and Vanguard. There's a lot of content to enjoy, and it's easy to get back to once in a while.The third-person perspective by design makes the game a lot more accessible. Plenty of my friends have nausea after playing an FPS game, but WWZ gives us the opportunity to have a nice time. That said, I still highly recommend you remove any camera shakes and motion blur, and to lower your mouse sensitivity.L4D2 world-building, sound design, and overall atmosphere is a class of its own, but WWZ is immersive on its own right. The game is not perfect by any means, but I find it to be good enough as a successor to the former title.I wish this game had first-class support for mods, but I'll take what I can get. The DLCs are good enough for me as only one person has to own it for it to be playable for the entire group. I like knowing there's probably a new episode coming out in a year or two for me to enjoy with friends, first-timers and old dogs alike.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the sort that wants their coffee and grits in single sentences, this game is Left for Dead 2 how it should've been done.  There I said it.Oh, you're still here? Okay then, here we go! Any game can be nit picked down to minute details if you want, this game is no different. Do you really have to throw the switch on both generators nearly at the same time or the breaker will trip? Well if you have a couple portable gas generators hooked up to your home, this logic might be sound. But when you're talking about an industrial sized back up generator system for a hospital, or any industrial sized system for that matter, that's just not how these systems work. But it's an action game, big explosions, lots of bullets and blood and mass slaughter of zombies, who needs a bullet-proof plot? The John Wick theory is strong with this game and I love it.I fully endorse the value in this game, too; whether you bought the base version for $30, Aftermath for a little more, or the Deluxe with the Arizona expansion for the full $60 (especially if you got anyone of those one sale). If you like zombie wave defense, slaughter types of games with just enough plot to make it interesting and slightly believable, that actually animates thousands of zombies onto your screen (and making them all hit-able targets) without lagging your computer to it's grave, this game is worth it.Do yourself and your friends a favor, buy four copies and go kill some zombies ;)

It has maps set in USA, Israel, Vatican City, France, Japan and Russia.Pros:Co-op gameplay: This game is great played with games, it is definitely a team shooter.Variety of locations: The levels take you all across different cities in the globe.Aftermath Expansion: The aftermath DLC adds a new mode and different classes.Extra DLC available: There is the Valley of the Zeke Episode available and various weapon skins available in the Steam store, the Xbox store and the PlayStation store.Cons:Levels are a bit repetitive: Some players might find the missions and level designs a bit repetitive over time.Forgettable Story: The narrative story isn't strong or memorable, which might be a let down for those looking for a decent campaign story.Solo Play: The game can be particularly challenging when played solo as it is designed with solo in mind.Overall World War Z is a fun game, especially with those who enjoy co-op shooters and zombie themed games. The has a few flaws which can be overlooked if you like this type of gameWorld War Z gets 4/5 stars and I recommend buying this game on PC, Xbox or PS5

_childDocuments_.review: I would call this game a spiritual successor to Left 4 Dead. Kind of like what Back4Blood could have been if it were made by people who understand videogame design.You have the typical 4-person squad fighting through a zombie apocalypse. The differences which elevate this game is mainly the sheer amount of enemies present at one time. (I'm sure you've seen this on all of the promo materials.) Left 4 Dead had a limit on 30 zombies at once I believe. In World War Z you will regularly get faced with hundreds of them at once.There are various special enemies that can sometimes unexpectedly flank you or simply get covered by the tide of enemies that approach. They aren't visually disturbing when compared to the typical zombie crowds and each of them has a certain unique feature to them that can occasionally catch you off-guard.As far as the player's side of things go there are (With the aftermath and newest DLC update.) a handful of general items for healing, supply bags and some other collectible items that can help you out on your mission. Each player has a unique class (Unique in terms of class to class, not per session. A session can have 4 copies of a single class no problem though I'd recommend a more rounded approach.) which defines their special ability which gets refilled by collecting supply bags on the map. These are shared for everyone (The singular Supply Bag item refills whichever unique ability your class has. It is not a special class-specific pickup.) so you need to know when to pick up and when to leave it for someone else on the team who might make better use of it.Besides the special ability, each class has their own tree of various upgrades that can notably alter how to best play the class. These upgrades are locked behind one heck of a grind though which is probably the biggest metaphorical anchor this game has attached to it. You get all the regular abilities for the class by reaching level 30 on that specific class which is not a problem. (Following refers to in-game currency, not real life money.) However, you need to buy every single upgrade which you might want to have unlocked. After that's done you can pay more in order to prestige which resets all of your bought upgrades as you start from the very beginning with that specific class but you get a small extra ability unlocked in the skilltree. These red abilities are all always on (you don't pick 1 out of 3 in each column like you would with regular abilities.) and at the time of writing this review the lowest prestige to get all of the red abilities is prestige 9. Which means you would need to grind through each of the 8 classes 9 times. That means (30 x 9) x 8 = 2160 levels needed to (CURRENTLY) max out all classes. (Plus you need to pay to prestige and get skills every single prestige unless you want to be severely undergeared in a match.)Apart from leveling your class you also level your weapons by using the specific weapon which might occasionally be easier said than done when the weapon spawns are pretty random and you have no real say in what weapon you'll find. And with there being quite a good handful of weapons: When you come across a weapon in the game, you are not provided with information about the level of the weapon in any way apart from pausing the game while holding the weapon. So it can really take a while along with the fact that you also need to pay for each weapon level up all the way to level 15 for most weapons. You gain no experience for the weapon until you pay for the level up and any XP you gain while maxed for the weapon is just gone to limbo.I'd say that the amount of grind needed is quite annoying but to be honest, you can just level up each class to level 30 and not prestige. For most classes you won't be missing that much.Either way the grind doesn't outweigh how well the game is made as a whole. Lots of various characters, a good handful of unique classes, a few handfuls of weapons and various campaigns taking place across the planet as the world is doing their best to deal with the endless hordes. It is a very enjoyable game that scratches the itch of zombie genocide quite well. There's a good chance that even after you're done with the game and beaten it, you'll come back every now and then and head over to Quick Play for a bit just to get a good scratch in for the time being before you go play something else - similar to Left 4 Dead.World War Z is most definitely it's own thing and it is made very well and enjoyable. It might be on the costly side but if you manage to ever find a good deal while having a zombie killing itch you certainly ought to grab it and have a good bit of fun. (I believe I got my Steam copy from the Ukraine Humble Bundle while I played previously on Epic.) But I cannot stress this enough: If you aim to play anything difficulty 3 or higher you should know what your place is in the team and also what each teammate should be good at. I've lost games because of players not knowing what their class is doing and just not bringing any proper synergy to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: WWZ was honestly a pleasant surprise in 2019. I had no expectation of the game when it released, but it quickly grabbed my attention and sated the hunger that I desired for another PVE zombie experience. The game in general follows a simple formula of clearing objectives to progress through each act, essentially building on what Left 4 Dead established. Objectives can range from the classic crescendo events, defending a point, collecting supplies, completing puzzles and so on. It sounds simple enough, but there's a lot of enjoyment to be had in the simplicity. Some of my favorite moments are the ones that emphasize proper cooperation and teamwork. For instance on an act in Marseille, one person is required to be on flashlight duty in a pitch black tunnel. Zombies are crowding in from all angles and its their job to properly light and guide everyone through the tunnel. On another act in Russia, you're required to complete puzzles involving switches and generators while making the proper call outs and killing floods of zombies. I find the game to be far more enjoyable when playing on the harder difficulties. This is, again, where proper teamwork is a necessity. One can't just sprint throughout the level and solo their way to each objective because sprinting alerts hordes in the area. Weapons also have to be suppressed. Firing an unsuppressed weapon is a quick way to get everyone overwhelmed. Zombies only take a few hits to down you, so it becomes very tense. Other things, like proper positioning and crouching in front of teammates so they don't shoot you in the back of your head, all come together to make the teamwork aspect of the game shine. The one thing that really sets this game apart from other zombie PVEs, however, is the sheer amount of zombies that are thrown your way. At any point during a level you could be dealing with droves of hundreds of zombies occupying the screen. One memorable point that stands out to me is seeing 1000s of zombies flood an overpass on the Tokyo act as you prepare to defend the area; those 1000s will eventually accumulate in the area and rush your position. Which brings me to performance. The game is very well optimized and runs great on most setups I've seen. When I played the game on my gtx 1080/ i7 8700k on ultra settings and 1080p, the game easily sat at a consistent 144fps. The game far exceeds that on an RTX 3080 currently. There's virtually no fps drops during swarms and the game overall just runs like a charm. Overall, WWZ is a game that surprised me. I didn't expect much of it. I didn't have hype for it. I just went in wanting to play a little zombie PVE game and quench my thirst in the drought of that subgenre. I came out pleasantly surprised and addicted for over a year. The game is well made, it looks nice, it runs nice and delivers, in my opinion, a great, cooperative zombie PVE experience. I would say if anyone is looking for that, I would definitely recommend WWZ.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z is a L4D-like game, with some additions. There are special infected like in L4D, but what is missing is a more feared special infected like the Tank in L4D. The zombies act a lot like the zombies in the movie World War Z, where they form pyramids and climb on each other to get to different places. It's insanely satisfying to just blast away into the horde with heavy weapons when they do this.There is a progression system in this game where you get to choose to play between 8 different classes that are good at different things. You can level up your classes to strengthen yourself and your team by unlocking perks. One class might be good at killing large hordes of zombies, while another is better at building defenses, etc. You can also level up all weapons to unlock attachments, such as silencers, skins and perks for your weapons. Once you have reached the max level of a class, which is lvl 30, you can also take prestige to unlock additional perks for the class.The zombies AI is similar to L4D. They try to flank you, surround you, attack from behind, etc. If you're playing solo, you can choose to have bots on your team or play all by yourself. The behavior of the bots is similar to L4D, which is not always the best. I highly recommend playing with other players to get the best experience. It's not very easy to find players in matchmaking, but you can join the World War Z discord server to find people to play with if you don't already have a bunch of friends to play with.The game has 5 difficulty levels. Easy, Normal, Hard, Insane and Extreme. The game has 4 episodes, with 3-4 chapters in each episode. If you own the DLC, there are 3 more episodes, making a total of 7 episodes. There is also Horde Mode where you have to survive 50 waves of zombies while building defenses etc. Silencers are strongly recommended on harder difficulty levels. It is also very fun and exciting to go stealth.I think the replayability is good. There are Personal, Daily and Weekly challenges that rotate. Personal challenges can be to kill a certain amount of zombies with headshots, kill special infected in certain ways, and more. In Daily and Weekly challenges you replay random chapters with random mutators making the levels harder, where the Weekly is usually harder than the Dailys. Here you can only choose between Normal and Hard though, but it can be hard enough depending on which mutators are active. Higher difficulty give greater reward and xp, whether you play daily/weekly challenges or not. In any case, there are hundreds of hours to put into this game if you want to level up to max and unlock everything.There is also a multiplayer mode where you play against other players in different game modes, while hordes of zombies periodically appear. However, multiplayer is almost completely dead, so finding a single match in matchmaking is very difficult, almost impossible. Eventually I managed to find a couple of games and try it out (always with the same players) and it was pretty fun.There is one thing that is a bit annoying in this game, and that is the inability to jump. You can't jump in this game, but you can climb on things, such as cars and other things. If you then want to descend from the height you are at, you cannot fire or load your weapon while falling from this height to the ground. If you start a reload before you start falling, your reload will be interrupted in mid-air and you will have to reload again when you land.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Buy with Aftermath DLC with or without sale, game is worth its full price. Avoid if going only for base game regardless of sale. Buying with friends recommended, solo buyer looking for multiplayer not ideal unless you're okay with spending some time leveling alone first before heading into multiplayer.IMPORTANT NOTE: If you're going into this game solo hoping for an alive online play, I suggest reconsidering firstly. The "veterans" will outright leave your lobby if they see that you are low level. This is most likely due to horrible practice that shockingly many YouTuber that were World War Z focused, pushed. They all pretty much emphasized on leaving lobbies with lower level players to "not waste time" and personally I've experienced this despite not being completely new to this game. Essentially, if you are solo looking for an online scene, you'd need to play solo with bots first to gain some levels before "veterans" will want to stick around your lobby. At least this game supports full crossplay though, with Epic, Microsoft Windows Store(Game pass), Xbox and PlayStation so you will likely always find players.As a double dipper of this game (owned this on the PS4 back in 2019) and having finally finished all the DLC Aftermath has to offer, I'm confident to say that I can still recommend this game.I'm sure you've heard this comparison before if you've ever looked up "Left 4 Dead 3" but World War Z is pretty much the Left 4 Dead 3 that never was. Its a great zombie shooter that focuses on MASSIVE hordes of zombies. Its even got its own kind of special infected too but they are miles more annoying than L4D1/2's and some are less balanced than others. Great selection of guns too but a meh progression built for it. Who's silly idea was it that you cannot level up your guns if you dont unlock the next level? This wouldnt be a flaw if the game was generous or reasonable with its ingame currency but they pay you in peanuts even in the higher difficulties. Dont even let me start with the challenge coins. The amount given for both currency are pitiful.Overall, I'd say only pick this game up with Aftermath DLC. If you can only go for the base game, I suggest waiting for a sale with the DLC or dont bother because without Aftermath DLC, you would be missing out on a lot of content.The game is pretty much still alive too with weekly and daily challenges along with it still being updated by the developers. As a vanilla player back in 2019, the most notable changes are being able to play whatever character you want regardless of which campaign map you're on, a reworked weapon progression system whereby attachments are just cosmetics now instead of functional and a first person mode (although this is DLC locked) and many more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good, but I'm glad I didn't pay full price for it. The multiplayer is dead, so I'm only reviewing the co-op side of the game.It's basically Vermintide but with guns. You must travel from Point A to Point B while being besieged by swarms of zombies. Literal swarms. Thick, opaque swarms of zombies that rush at you very fast and can kill you very easily. The swarms are done very well and, for some reason, always have a fence or a ledge in their way that they need to climb over, leading to a visually-appealing pyramid of zombies climbing over each other in an attempt to reach your brains. This has a small drawback of individual zombies not looking very impressive, but when you see that swarm pouring over a cliff like an unstoppable waterfall, your money is officially well spent.The characters are... interesting. Unlike Left 4 Dead, you're playing with a separate group of survivors in each campaign, each with their own goal and story. They are, for the most part, surprisingly well fleshed out for this kind of approach, and it leads to a ton of diversity in the cast as you travel around the world. The downside to this is that you only play them in one campaign, so if you particularly liked a certain character, you're not going to see them again until Horde mode.The varied campaigns and characters also means varied locales, though, all of which are pretty well-crafted!The guns feel good, too. Blow the zombies away with the shotgun or pierce through the mob with a sniper rifle, heads will pop, action will be had. It's especially thrilling to see that kill confirm indicator popping constantly as you shoot into a swarm, and yet you don't see the swarm thinning out at all. You run out of ammo... and then an even thiccer swarm comes pouring over the hills. Pull out the bigger gun, things just got serious!It's basically Vermintide but with bad melee. "Action will be had" until the zombies get anywhere near you, at which point you can either run away, or you can flail, take damage, and get shot in the back by your teammates, killing yourself faster than the zombies could ever hope to. Hitting the melee key makes you dash forward if a zombie is close enough (you cannot swing while moving normally like you can in Killing Floor or Vermintide). This ensures that you're close enough to hit them... and also ensures that you're in the middle of a swarm in a game where basic zombies, not just specials, are allowed to . The Slasher class has a whole suite of passive skills to alleviate some of these problems, but good luck trying to melee anything safely if you're not a Slasher.This game is also trying way too hard to be Left 4 Dead when it doesn't need to. Most of the missions feel exactly the same. Travel from Point A to Point B, someone will be there with some stupid excuse for you to "bunker down" and lay some traps, then you defend against the swarm of zombies. It's cool the first time. It's cool the second time. By the end of the campaign, though, you're left wondering why this is the structure of almost every single level in the game. The mechanics seem to lend themselves more towards Payday 2's "hold F"-style missions, and the ones that are in this game are a lot more fun to play. The game shines when you're trying to protect teammates who are trying to complete the objective and the swarm is just unending. When you're sitting around shooting a pyramid, it's good eye-candy, but it gets boring.That said, it would be fine if the special zombies were more threatening. Unlike Left 4 Dead (and every other zombie game I can think of, actually), where the primary threat isn't the basic zombie, but instead the special zombies that can wipe a whole squad and/or have tons of HP, the primary threat in WWZ  the basic zombie. The swarm itself is the most dangerous entity in the game. The specials are underwhelming and terrible. Yes, they can incapacitate you, but they can also be taken out very quickly, and they never get stronger. There is no Tank, there is no Siren, there is no Scrake or Fleshpound, there are no bosses. There are also no ranged grabs, such as the Smoker. Instead, there are mild irritations as you deal with the horde.I can't say that focusing entirely on the swarm was necessarily a bad idea, but again, it lends itself more towards Payday 2-style missions, and this game doesn't like doing those.Fun for a bit, but lacks longevity. It has progression systems—you can level up your classes and weapons—but the basic gameplay loop becomes too repetitive too fast, and there's no mods to save it. Playing different classes also will not likely be enough to keep you around, since they don't differentiate from each other  to warrant replaying the game.It's still very fun for that "bit", though, so I recommend picking this up when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a big gamer. For over a decade i only played left 4 dead on xbox whenever i was board. after branching out to pc and needing a new zombie adventure and being disappointed by some titles (back 4 blood mainly) i found WWZ. I'd describe WWZ as a more complex L4D without being overly strategic. my biggest gripe with B4B was it was way to strategic when all i wanna do is run and shoot. If i wanted to play dungeons and dragons id play that and B4B frankly pissed me off. Fortunately I found WWZ and was surprised a game based on a movie(book first) was exceptionally good. There are a few quirks... Dont run out of an elevator or closing vault doors after just entering. the doors will close without you and wont be able to open them and only see a highlighted indicator of an "interaction" inside the doors you can no longer access. literally have to exit, lose your progress and start that "episode" over. The game is very inconsistent with the equipment it supplies as you prepare for swarms. Time limits on preparing defenses is very annoying when theres more or less defense equipment available making an easy difficulty sometimes feel like a hard difficulty setting. Unless you aspire to reach high levels of "classes" for every class, the game is pretty short and lacks "episodes" for the total gameplay thats available if your goal was to max out all the classes and weapons levels. I play just offline. I dont care for online gameplay and thus playing campaigns, jjust because youve built up levels in classes, doesnt mean that the "computer" players on your team that presumably would be one of those classes, would have a higher level of "class" and skillset. In short, As you get better at playing the game and increase in "classes" your teammates still play like rookies no matter the diificulty. One thing ive never been able to figure out and maybe this is normal for more serious gamers to understand but its wildly frustrating that playing offline campaign (or horde mode) that I cannot pause the game without the game going with me. I also noticed this on several other games as i tried to branch out of L4D such as fallout when I would receive a phone call and hit "start" yet find i was still taking enemy damage. thats ridiculous. I understand for online games but if i need to take a piss i should be able to do so by hitting the "start" button like every game in history before ones mentioned. Back to the positives of the game....Graphics are great and I say that as someone who barely cares about such things. running on a I5-9500 and msi rtx 2070 with 32gb ddr4 ram hitting over 100 fps and barely breaking 55C on GPU and 41C CPU temps. So any pc components newer than 2018 can play this game flawlessly. overall im happy i found this game as L4D was finally getting a little stale even with the workshop customization. If WWZ had a workshop option in Steam this would be a 5+ hours a day on average game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted this game to be better than Back 4 Blood, but it's not.- Horrible gunplay, zero impact from the weapons, even iconic for zombie games chainsaw feels plastic and not fun to use- Pointless gun upgrades (maybe it's more useful on higher levels but God is my witness I'm not gonna grind for them)- Couple dozens of random guns which will only slow down your progress on upgrades- Skill system that confuses you completely (several classes, abilities that you can't even see before leveling up, GRIND again)- Game-breaking bugs (you either play on Vulkan and pray that game doesn't break at the end of the longest level or play on DX11 and enjoy smooth 40 FPS experience with constant stutters)- Dead community, there are around 1k players everyday and good part of them either complete beginners or straight up trolls ruining your game- Strange spawn of items on maps, sometimes you find 0 breach charges, but there are about 10-15 doors for them with good guns behind them. Variety of items also disappointing, even compared with B4BOnly good part for me - map design. Some of the levels are absolutely breathtaking, with waterfalls of zombies, famous landmarks and even environmental storytelling sometimes. But all this beauty of the maps can't hide absolutely horrific core mechanics. My disappointment is indeed immeasurable.If you search for good zombie-shooter with coop to play with friends or strangers - buy B4B. Even though support of B4B is ended, game still provides a lot more fun gameplay and mechanics than WWZ

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend enough! I have about 150 hours on Epic and I never get enough of this game. It is a technical marvel, throwing hundreds of zombies at you while running smoothly and looking great. The weapons are great, all feeling different and useful in their own way. Hard to pick a favorite. The new FPS mode makes in even more immersive and slaying zombies have never felt better. Not to mention the different classes and equipment, most are useful in their own way, had a lot of fun levelling them all up.The only downside of this game is the lack of community made maps and no real endgame. Extreme difficulty is a challenge for anyone, but after reaching max level there is no real continuous progression on levels or weapon improvement. There are quite a few maps, but adding the possibility for players to make maps and sharing them would make this game infinitely replayable!

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've beat the entire Campaign, I'd say this is my favorite zombie game. Definitely better than COD Zombies, Days Gone, and Day Z. World War Z does a lot right but can be a drag at times.Pros+ Good graphics+ Hundreds of zombies populate the map and climb over each other just like in the movie+ Progression, replayability, different weapons, etc.+ 4 player online co-opCons- When you set up a turret or auto turret you can't place it anywhere, you have to place it where they want you to, and sometimes it's mostly facing a wall, and you can barely aim it so that's bad, and turrets are kinda weak too- Lurkers. Lurkers are annoying AF. Around every corner, a lurker is waiting to jump on you and knock you down. When that happens it holds you on the ground and beats you to death (unless a teammate shoots it). Also the game stats call it a lurker yet the voice actors say "creeper" for whatever reason. Also, even if you kill a lurker, it respawns after a couple minutes so when you backtrack it jumps on you again which is annoying AF. And also this game has dismemberment, but it doesn't work on higher level zombies such as lurkers, which is disappointing because I want to dismember lurkers.- AI teammates are kinda useful, but they jump right in front of my bullets all the time. Duck down or something FFS.- Mission objectives are not always clear. A character will say "shoot the zombies off the fence!" but there are like four fences so I don't know which fence they mean. Sometimes I focus on shooting like a hundred zombies, then lose the mission because more zombies were at a different fence.- Some missions you have to protect NPCs. But the NPCs will sometimes just walk right into a crowd of zombies. If they die, you have to restart the entire level (there are no checkpoints).This game is like the movie in that there are huge amounts of zombies and they climb atop each other like ants to scale walls and fences. Other than that, this is not like the movie. In the movie, zombies have black blood and don't bleed much, but in this, they have lots of red blood and there are severed feet all over the ground. There are 7 missions which each take a little over an hour if you don't die or fail an objective, and each mission takes you to another city. Also you pick from a selection of characters. The character options are mid, the game would probably be more popular if the characters were more interesting, but for the most part it's just a group of regular people that are wearing jeans and hats and stuff. Overall the game is pretty solid for a zombie game but it's lacking in some areas. There is an online VS mode too, but I wouldn't bother with PvP in a game like this, PvE is where it's at.

_childDocuments_.review: REAL TALK REVIEWS-------------VISUAL: 3/5Streets are bloody, blood and guts everywhere. This game does a good job giving you a good visual of how it is during the apocalypse. All the models looks nice, with good lighting, and the dark areas not being too dark. UI effects when getting shot or infected is a nice touch.AUDIO: 2/5Sound effects are what you expect it to be. Zombies groaning, bullets firing. You can distinguish the different noises each special zombie makes and sometimes the characters do have some funny one liners. After awhile it does get a little repetitive. Soundtrack is nothing great.CONTROLS: 3/5This game is better played as a third-party camera view. The controls are pretty straight forward and easy to learn. There are times when you accidentally toggle first person view - and that honestly messes up the flow of the game sometimes. MECHANICS: 3/5This game is your basic CO-OP live service game. While you can play this game solo with bots filled in as partners, this game is made for online CO-OP play. I do wish there was local co-op, but unfortunately it does not have it.The game is split into episodes, with each episode containing about 3 levels. Within each level are different tasks the players must complete to advance the level. There are certain sections where players must survive the "horde" attacks. During this time, players are given time to set up some defences before being swarmed by the horde. You work with your teammates to go through the level and survive.After completing (or dying) each level, players earn points that can be used to improve classes and weapons. This system is pretty straight forward. It does have enough perks to provide various builds for each class. Some provide better survival skills, while others give more offensive perks.This game does suffer from lots of bugs, but luckily this game is still being supported by the developers. Frame rate issues, connection issues, ghost zombies, balance issues, grievers, etc. are some problems players face. However, even though there are lots of bugs, the community is still somewhat active. PLOT: 2/5Loosely based off of the book and movie; this game follows a zombie apocalypse with survivors fighting through hordes of zombies. There isn't really a main story line to follow, but each episode does have some back story that's provided in the collectables section. The characters also have a small backstory to them which is nice. FUN FACTOR:  4/5For a live service game, this game is fun. Designed to be played with others over online, the game does provide a solo option to play. However, the computer does not make smart choices and sometimes going at it alone is the better option. Even on higher difficulty! The bots are useful for reviving you when you're down. But other than that, they're basically pylons, or cheap versions of automatic turrets.When playing with friends, the game really shines. Friendly fire give it a fun challenge and some accidental laughs. The horde portions of the game is really fun. Some levels are more challenging than others. The developers have included a "horde" mode where waves and waves of zombies keep coming at you as you earn points to build defences. This game gives off Left for Dead vibes and that's a good thing. It's not exactly the same, but nor should it be. --------VERDICT: 3/5A Zombie killing survival game that resembles similar mechanics from an old OG game - Left for Dead. While not aiming to be its replacement, this game does scratch the itch you're looking for to have a similar type game. In fact, out of many clones we've played, WWZ is the closest modern L4D type game. This alone is worth it to try.When buying, the game is best when ALL add-ons are purchased.--------RTR OVERVIEW--------3/5 - VISUALS2/5 - AUDIO3/5 - CONTROLS3/5 - MECHANICS2/5 - PLOT4/5 - FUN FACTOR---------3/5 - VERDICT--------BUY:         YES (During Sale)ADD-ONS: YES - for best experience.--------

_childDocuments_.review: A 4 player co-op zombie shooter that's quite different than other games of it's kind (looking at you L4D and B4B). While other games put emphasis on non-stop action, WWZA prefers a more tactical, and stealthy approach. You can go in guns blazing, but due to scarce ammo you'll probably die more often than win against the game massive hordes (more on them later). The maps are also a little bit more complex than what's available in similiar titles: usually there are two paths to take through the terrain, with various connections in-between them, which makes map appear more open than linear corridors typical of the genre.Then there are defense stages of the levels - the staple of WWZA gameplay. When you end up in a large open spaces, you will usually have to set up the place to defend against an oncoming horde, using various equipment found around the area: manual, and automatic machinegun nests, mortars, barbed wire and electric fences. Due to the limited time for preparation, and random location of the equipment, you will never be truly ready. Especially since the hordes are enormous, with literally thousands of screaming zombies coming to you. What's really great is that zombies will climb upon eachother to get to you shooting at them from elevated position, that you were 100% sure was safe. Not in this game.Add the typical assortment of special zombies (tanks, exploders, chemical gas ones, and "screamers" which will increase the spawn rate of zombies) and you will have a lot of shooting on your hands. Inbetween the stealth and defense stages you also have to operate various machinery, search for items or defend NPCs. This all makes game more interesting, and adds to the replay value - especially since no playthrough is the same due to the random character of many events.Still, the game is not without faults. The biggest one is probably the way how FPP was designed. Game started as third person shooter, and Aftermath update introduced the first person mode, but it mostly sucks. There's no aim-down sight view, which really affects the game "meta", because many weapons have two branches of upgrades: one focused on accuracy and damage, and other focused on portability. In most cases you would want to go with damage branch, because there's no downside to it. If game would have true sight views, the choice wouldn't be so obvious, since more damage would mean a high-zoom scope with low field of view. And that would make the red-dot equipped "handling branch" version of the same gun an interesting alternative.Also the additional "Horde Mode", which is a tower defense like wave survival, is just not varied enough. As opposed to the defense stages in campaign, here the zombies always attack from the same places, which removes some of the unpredictability of the game. It's still fun, and there's always difference in what special zombies will spawn, but some more diversity would be appreciated (and apparently "Horde XL" mode is planned, although I don't know what's supposed in there).Apart from that, personally I found many of the classes and perks underpowered, but that may be just my playstyle. Otherwise the game is really well made and entertaining - even for solo players, as it's possible to play with bots. It may not win any "game of the year" award, but in it's niche of 4 player co-op zombie shooters it gives an interesting approach to the genre, and stands out among many straight-forward L4D clones. Two thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't fathom the positive reviews of this game. If you want to play a good version of this play L4D2, even as old as it is it is a much better/polished game. WWZ is, in all aspects, extremely mediocre. It's not terrible and not great, just midling. It's buggy as all get out, and has massive grind layered over the top for no good reason.Gameplay:WWZ gameplay is ok. It's a basic zombie shooter cloned from L4D with specials that mimic the specials in L4D and a singular unique mechanic of zombies building on top of each other to climb walls.  The weapons are ok, the maps are ok, the strategies are ok.Placing defensive items is both interesting and frustrating as you can only place them in pre arranged spots and in many cases they face in different directions (your oprions) and you never know what direction the horde will come from so it feels a bit forced, rather than being able to place them anywhere or even reposition them.They don't allow you turn off Friendly fire separate from the difficulty level. In my view this is a mistake made by many games FF should always be a checkbox separate from the difficulty. We want to play at the max difficulty but lag and other things like the bugs (described below) make Friendly Fire idiotic.Bugs:I only play MP with 3 other freinds for a team of 4. None of us can walk up stairs in this game, or over train tracks or over anything else on the ground. You stop as if you hit an invisible wall. Running, or couching and uncrouching your way up the stairs can usually get you up but it happens routinely and I can't fathom why it would not have been fixed by now.Other players also routinely turn invisible. In our playthroughs basically at all times, at least one player can not see one other player. Someone is always invisible to someone until them pick up something (medkit) or interact with something and then they pop back, but interacting can also turn your invisible, so it's a rotation of who can't see who, and sometimes you can't see multiple players. Fairly gamebreaking in a zombie shooter with Friendly Fire that can't be turned off.Grind:This is perhaps the worst part of the game and pushes this review into negative territory. The game introduces XP and leveling of your character and weapons. As you play you gain XP to level your character and XP to level each gun you use (you pick up random guns during the game and don't generally start with the one you may want to use). There are three tiers of weapons. Each time you level a weapon (or your character) you have to pay money to buy the level, even though you just got enough XP to get it. If you don't buy the level of the gun... you STOP gaining further XP until you do buy it. You can not earn enough money to raise 3 guns (one in each weapon tier) and your character. Therefore you are wasting XP, also you can't delay deciding what gun you want to spend money on since you will not be gaining XP for it.To get money you have to play ridiculous challenge maps and modes that are simply not fun and grind out the money you need, but you will also gain levels doing this. There is no way to smoothly play through the campaign and raise even one on gun at each tier never mind trying some of the others. Not worth it at all. Play L4D2 again, or Dying Light, or any other decent zombie game out there.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on 100% completion and 91.2 hours of gameplay.Would I recommend the game? Absolutely. This is hands down the best horde shooter game on the market to date. I really enjoy all aspects of this game and honestly don’t have any complaints.The gameplay is incredibly fun, offering a large range of weapons to use and experiment with—not to mention the various versions of weapons you can unlock. Coupled with the different classes and their skill trees, there’s a ton of variety in gameplay options. While the maps and modes are somewhat limited, which could make them feel repetitive to some players over time, I personally enjoyed every run. The sound design, audio, and graphics are all solid, but the gameplay and mechanics are the real highlights of this game.The story told through the individual campaigns is decent and easy to follow, but I feel it’s overshadowed by the exceptional gameplay. It almost fades into the background as you focus on the action and mechanics, which speaks volumes about how fun the core gameplay is. While that could be seen as a downside, I believe all the elements work together extremely well to create an amazing experience.The base price of the game is, in my opinion, worth it for the quality and content you receive. However, since the game has been out for a while and often goes on sale, I’d recommend waiting for a discount if you can.There are multiplayer/coop-specific achievements required for 100%.Most achievements in this game are fairly straightforward and will come naturally through normal gameplay, though they’ll require a lot of grinding. The only ones to be concerned about are the coop/multiplayer achievements. At the time I went for them, the specific modes required were essentially dead, so we had to create a full group to get them. Just keep that in mind when aiming for 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the best horde game out there.  It has good mechanics, perks, and at this point a bunch of missions to play so you won't get bored.  I still like games like back 4 blood, alien's fireteam elite, space marine 2, left 4 dead, darktide, and vermintide but this game is probably the best all around.  I really enjoy how the weapon upgrades are persistent between playthroughs and they skill up through use.  I also like how many perks you get to select on your build at any given time.  It gives you a lot of freedom to make all the different things synergize.  There are a few builds where you can get infinite equipment items at a fairly short interval.  When used correctly you can have infinite ammo bags with the fixer, molotovs or gas grenades with the exterminator, infinite claymores and grenade launcher shots with the hellraiser, etc.  It just feels really good as you go on and get stronger and stronger.  The slasher with the right melee weapon and build is nigh invincible even when complete overwhelmed which makes a huge difference when holding out for team respawns.  I will warn however, the game doesn't have a tutorial.  In the early stages tips pop up but you absolutely can and will fail missions due to not knowing what you are doing or understanding what is going on.  You still get decent experience and currency even if that happens so its not a total loss.One thing I will mention is that viral samples function like gene-seeds in space marine 2 and give you extra xp and currency upon mission completion.  Unlike gene-seeds, the viral samples can be damaged and cause zombie infections and also break so you gotta play defensively if you have one.Anyway, I love the hordes in this game.  It feels good to blow them up, it feels good to fire grenades at zombie hordes, it feels good to set them on fire, it feels good to put a stationary turret down and just unload into the group.  The swarms here are serious, and the horde xl mode is just wild.  It is interesting to see how easy it feels with a good group with upgraded equipment and a bad group with low level equipment.  The zombies might not even reach you at all with the good group, they'll just all die at range, but a bad group you'll constantly have people incapacitated and tons of zombies slipping through.  Overall, I love the experience, its really fun, the defensive aspect is satisfying and there are missions where you board up the houses or rebuild doors, put down barbed wire or hook electricity up to a fence and then give yourself a bit more time to cluster and blow up zombies.  It just feels good, pretty much universally throughout.  Love the game.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z, is a cooperative third-person shooter inspired by the 2013 film. Players team up to combat massive zombie hordes across various global locations.Pros:- Intense Co-op Gameplay: The game excels in delivering thrilling cooperative experiences, especially when facing overwhelming zombie swarms. - Diverse Locations: Players traverse varied environments, from New York to Tokyo, each offering unique challenges and atmospheric settings. - Class-Based System: The inclusion of distinct classes with upgradeable abilities adds depth and encourages strategic team compositions. Cons:- Repetitive Missions: Some players may find the objectives and mission structures become monotonous over time. - Limited Enemy Variety: While the zombie hordes are impressive, the lack of diverse enemy types can lead to a sense of repetition. - Technical Issues: The game can struggle sometime when there is exceptionally large hordes and cause glitching.In conclusion, "World War Z" offers a thrilling cooperative experience with its intense action and diverse settings, though it faces challenges with mission variety and technical stability.Score: 85 out of 100 zombies in a horde—A solid undead uprising with room for more bite.

_childDocuments_.review: Superb co-op game!Pluses:+ With Aftermath, the game is fair in length. It is well worth price tag even if you can't wait for a sale (IMPORTANT: it is apparently NOT worth it IF you already own the base World War Z tho, I read in other reviews, as this one only adds 2 locations to the previous 5, if so wait for a big sale). + Fantastic gameplay and level design. Doesn't really get old.+ The sheer number of zombies rendered on-screen and the fantastic feeling you get both when mowing them down together with your team, or the panic you get when you're about to be overrun (and your last standing team-mate hopefully heroically saves the day!). Great feel all through.+ The game has a lot of replay value as well thanks to the various classes, difficulty levels, perks and prestige modes. All this means you can find a play style that suits you, and that players can specialize according to their abilities to form a competent team.+ Seems well-optimized. Played mostly on very high settings and frame rate on my 6 yo gaming desktop and it feels great. AND when I sometimes play on my 3 yo mid-range gaming laptop, the performance is sufficient as well, and it honestly looks pretty great even on the lower settings on the laptop, plus I get a stable 60+ fps.+ On a random note, if you enjoy Left 4 Dead, or you liked The Last of Us multiplayer on Playstation and you felt that game lacked a co-op mode, I feel like this game is for you.+ Works well both with mouse and keyboard AND controller. Whatever suits you. Controller settings are so good you can easily compete with mouse players on the scoreboard after some practice.Tiny gripes of mine:- Probably best with friends (as with anything...) although the public matchmaking system is more than sufficient. My only wish with the matchmaking is that you could select several maps and difficulties to search for. As it is currently you need to select either one specific map and difficulty to play on, or there is the quickplay option that matches you to ANY map on your selected difficulty. In this way it is a tiny bit clunky and sometimes you got to wait few minutes for a game if you want to play a particular map on a particular difficulty.- It is obviously designed to be played in third person (which works great for this game!). Third person gives you a bigger FOV and a better feel for your surroundings. But if you are one of those that only plays FPS, you won't be happy as the first person mode feels a bit like a gimmick since you can only aim down sights with the sniper rifle.  You also have to go to the in-game menu to switch between FP and TP, you can't do it with a button press if you are one of those that enjoys that. It is a bit of a shame that they didn't add a FPS mode with ADS, and made it like a separate game mode. I feel like that would add even more replay value (to be fair tho, you already got a lot!).- There are some sections where you 'see through' the level design when you get a few hours in, and can use it to your advantage, and in other scenarios you feel a bit hindered by it. I feel like I don't want to  expand on that since it might spoil the experience a tiny bit, find out for yourself! This is not really a big deal tho as the level design is overall fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: One of my favorite games now on Steam in a convenient package that also includes the latest DLC! By far my favorite zombie game and In my opinion, way more fun than B4B. Highly recommended!The negative reviews are definitely caused by misconceptions that some people had and are not fully deserved. The sentence "the next evolution of the original hit WWZ" might indeed be misleading I guess. To be absolutely clear - World War Z: Aftermath is a DLC for the original game. The difference is that it is now free from being an Epic exclusive and it came to steam as a completely new package. Would you rather see the base game for 20-30 E and the expansion for 20 E on the Steam store? It's just conveniently packed up at a good price. On top of that, there are several free updates coming soon!People complaining that it is a full price game? The expansion is pretty great and has tons of new content, on it's own it's still 20E on Epic to do the upgrade. Basically, if you're getting it on Steam, for the extra 10E you're actually getting the full GOTY edition of the base game (which was worth 40E) + the expansion on top of it. About matchmaking. Can't be sure how it actually is in places like Australia but in Europe the game has been very much alive. Even over the past month I had no issues finding a full party for insane and extreme runs, right now it seems even better with full super easy crossplay capabilities. Lobbies match you automatically with PS, XBOX and Epic and if you just want to play with your buddies from a different platform it's as easy as sharing a code. I'm really struggling to find another game where it's so easy to play in a cross platform party. We even managed to find people to play PvP which has been completely dead for quite some time.In comparison, I tried B4B in the beta and it just felt so stiff... The zombies are just meh and feel really pale in comparison to the swarming hordes in WWZ. The gunplay in B4B felt off as well. I loved L4D back in the days so maybe that's why the addition of the ADS and guns taking half of my screen feels odd. Whenever I shot the zombies in B4B I felt there's fake blood spraying all over the place and that was it. Don't even get me started on how disappointing a pipe bomb explosion was but maybe there was just something wrong with the ragdolls. It just feels so damn good when the horde is rushing and there are body parts and zombie bodies flying all over the place. You can shoot half a zombie's head off or just it's hand.. it looks and feels great and the weapons feel just right. The progression system in feels a lot better too in WWZ. At it's current state, in my opinion WWZ is vastly superior and just simply more fun.About the launcher... EGS is just inconvenient so I was looking forward to the steam release where the social overlay is not utter garbage. I also like to have all my things in one place. I was willing to start the progression from scratch but as a cherry on top the savegames are very easy to transfer from Epic. Hell.. I even just dumped all the EGS WWZ files into my steam folder and could play straight away saving me time on the 30GB download.To sum it all up. WWZ is just a game that I love coming back to and I'm super chuffed to see more content for it. For some reason, hitting a dozen zombies in the head one after another and/or playing a medic and helping out the team just makes me happy :D

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z : By Triple F“World War Z,” developed by Saber Interactive, is a cooperative, third-person shooter inspired by the 2013 film and 2006 novel of the same name. Set in a world overrun by zombies, the game takes players through diverse global locations including New York, Jerusalem, Moscow, and Tokyo, where survivors band together to fight off massive waves of the undead. Though it might initially seem like a straightforward, run-and-gun experience, “World War Z” introduces unique gameplay elements like massive zombie swarms and tactical class-based combat, creating a cooperative experience that’s both challenging and engaging.The game’s core campaign is divided into episodic chapters, each featuring a different group of survivors and storylines set in iconic cities. Each location has a distinct feel, with environments that reflect the culture, architecture, and atmosphere of each setting. While the story is minimal and primarily serves as a setup for the action, it effectively establishes the desperation and scale of the global outbreak. Players are tasked with a variety of objectives in each chapter, ranging from rescuing survivors and holding defensive positions to escaping chaotic situations. Although the narrative is not particularly deep, the sense of urgency and survival that permeates each episode adds tension to the gameplay.One of “World War Z’s” standout features is its “Swarm Engine,” which creates massive waves of zombies that behave like a single, relentless entity. Hundreds of zombies can flood the screen, piling on top of each other to form living walls that can scale buildings, barricades, and any other obstacle in their way. This sheer volume of enemies is both visually impressive and highly challenging, as players must work together to manage these overwhelming hordes. The swarming mechanic sets “World War Z” apart from other zombie shooters, creating a unique sense of dread and requiring players to strategically position themselves, use explosives, and manage their ammunition carefully.Cooperative gameplay is at the heart of “World War Z,” with each player choosing from a selection of six character classes, Gunslinger, Hellraiser, Medic, Fixer, Slasher, and Exterminator. Each with its own strengths, abilities, and gear options. For instance, the Medic can heal teammates and revive downed players faster, while the Hellraiser specializes in explosives and heavy firepower. This class-based system encourages teamwork and strategic planning, as a balanced squad can be the difference between survival and failure. As players progress, they unlock upgrades and perks for each class, allowing them to further specialize and create a personalized loadout that matches their preferred playstyle.The game’s combat is intense and satisfying, with a wide variety of weapons that players can find and upgrade. The arsenal includes standard firearms like assault rifles, shotguns, and sniper rifles, along with special heavy weapons like chainsaws and grenade launchers. Weapon upgrades, such as increased magazine sizes, scopes, or stability improvements, add an RPG-like progression to the experience, giving players a sense of growth as they progress through missions. The zombie AI, while not individually complex, becomes overwhelming in numbers, and players need to be vigilant about resource management to avoid being caught off-guard. The moment-to-moment gunplay is thrilling, especially when holding defensive positions against massive zombie waves.“World War Z” also features a versatile multiplayer mode that adds additional replay-ability to the game. The multiplayer component includes competitive modes like King of the Hill and Team Deathmatch, blending traditional PvP elements with the chaos of zombie swarms. This mix of PvP and PvE introduces unpredictable situations where players can not only fight each other but also have to contend with zombies that appear mid-match, attacking everyone indiscriminately. The unpredictability of these swarms during PvP matches adds a unique dynamic, creating tense moments where alliances are tested and strategies are constantly shifting.Visually, “World War Z” is well-polished, with detailed environments and animations that enhance the immersion. Each city has its own atmosphere, from New York’s gritty urban streets to Tokyo’s clean, structured architecture. The game’s graphics are complemented by excellent sound design, with the terrifying roars of zombie hordes and the constant crackle of gunfire immersing players in the chaos. Audio cues play a crucial role, as players can hear zombies approaching from different directions, and special infected types have distinct sounds that alert players to their presence. This attention to detail in both graphics and audio enhances the game’s horror elements and intensifies the pressure players feel during horde encounters.In conclusion, “World War Z” is a fast-paced, cooperative zombie shooter that succeeds in delivering a high-stakes, adrenaline-fueled experience. While the story may lack depth, the game more than makes up for it with its intense action, unique swarm mechanics, and strategic, class-based gameplay. The combination of massive zombie waves, diverse environments, and the need for teamwork creates a memorable experience for fans of cooperative shooters and the zombie genre. Although it may not reinvent the wheel, “World War Z” executes its premise with skill and polish, making it a solid addition to any action or co-op gamer’s library.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this on ps4 previously so i already know what i'm getting into so let me preface this with prior knowledge at least for a console game. I'd like to focus on what it does well rather the very obvious concerns (rightly so) around P2P and no regional servers. So far i'm basing this review on the PC copy and the ability to engage cross play with any console, yes even Sony came to the party on this one. I would tentatively recommend this game on a few conditions.  If you have a single friend that owns the game i'd recommend it,  the cross play party invites are intuitive and easy to use click on the party invite give the code and bam your in.  I've got someone to play with on ps4 and it runs really well we didn't notice any lag issues so far. I've not played the new DLC yet there are 3 new maps added to Aftermath and at least two new classes. Haven't used the new classes yet can't comment on it. I wouldn't recommend this if you didn't have a friend to play with only with the current small player base, lets face it's an older game that was an Epic exclusive for awhile that really did it an injustice. Is it fun?  Personally yes i have had a lot of a fun with it, it really benefits from keyboard and mouse but the controller is also decent option as well.  The class variety is good and the weapons are satisfying. I'll touch briefly on the regional issues,  I'm in Australia so i know the pang of 100ms pings and higher it is a possibility which is why i refer back to have a friend to play it with, the enjoyment of the game will really hinge on if you can play with someone regularly. It has mixed reviews but i don't think that is a fair assessment of the game itself it has a lot of replay ability not in the realms of L4D but definitely get your moneys worth. Price is always a factor, i don't feel this is a $60 game i would highly encourage people to utilise Is There Any Deal to find a discount, i got it for $40 aus and it feels like a fair price it even came with some extra goodies couple of skins and what not. I'd also just like to touch on people saying there are getting games, i'd like to point out that the people still playing this are likely playing on a higher difficulty and once you get past the easy mode you'll find more games. Overall i'd recommend it but maybe watch a video or find a friend first, and definitely utilise Is There Any Deal to find it for a bargain.

_childDocuments_.review: This may be my favorite out of all of the 4-man co-op style games.  It's got some really good competition of late though. The difficulties, by the way, are scaled so perfectly in my opinion.  As soon as you're proficient, MOVE UP!  the zombies employ different tactics and teach you to be more effective if you pay attention.   This is a really well-crafted game that got unfairly overlooked.   I think it's movie tie-in circumstance probably affected this game negatively because it's one of the exceptions.  there can be frustrations in regards to adding friends sometimes from meeting in game, if you're on crossed platforms, so to speak.  I've met people in this game that it really hurt me to lose because there wasn't any efficient way of contacting them again after you're disconnected or w/e.  That may change or may have already. I played the slasher class almost all the time, until i started playing in the final difficulty extreme or whatever it is.  the slasher is kind of  set up for failure in many ways, no matter what difficulty, but there's a couple really effective perk combinations for this guy that can make it almost unstoppable until you get on extreme.    sadly, the slasher's prestige perks are all 100% useless and it's a total waste of money and time to grind them all out.  the only good perk you get out of prestige as slasher is hitting 1 more enemy before you become fatigued.   everything else is so negligible that you can only perceive them statistically.  i did it on epic games, but i just decided to keep the imaginary money on the steam version.
