_childDocuments_.review: This review is solely from the perspective of singleplayer / offline play because it is likely that others have waxed lyrical over multiplayer.Despite multiple updates since I bought the game, it would seem that the only things the updates provide are class changes which only serve to provide more tedious grinding as well as new weapon skins. No noticeable change in gameplay at all. Most glaringly, I still see the following problems still being perpetuated despite the updates:1. The classes of the AI companions cannot be changed. That is already a problem because SP / offline players should be allowed to change what classes they want for their AI companions for the player to have access to whatever ability a specific class can bring into a mission. Being unable to do so basically makes the player stuck with the same AI character classes.2. If Problem #1 is not bad enough and the AI companions classes are stuck, Problem #2 is that they are also stuck at level 0! How ridiculous it is when (A) not only the game forces the SP / offline players to grind to get to the relevant normal/prestige level so they can get the skill they want but (B) the AI companions are stuck at level 0 and do not use the levels/skills of the classes that you have been forced to grind so tediously to get? What is wrong with that? That means that AI companions are also unable to start with class weapons that the SP / offline players had so tediously grinded to start.What is the difference between a player entering a MP game with their selected class at whatever level they're already at and the SP being able to choose the class/skills for AI companion and them getting to use/have the same level/skills of the class that the SP had so tediously grinded for? None. There is no logical reason whatsoever for making the SP / offline players totally unable to change the AI character skill/class and also making the AI character stuck on level 0.EDIT 1: As further revision to the earlier review, the AI companion classes being stuck as it is is further exacerbated by denying certain class i.e. Medic if you choose to play as a specific character and yet a class which remain constant regardless whatever character you choose i.e. Gunslinger become the example of problem class causing trouble to the single player.For example: In the New York scenario, if you choose to play as Bunko, you have absolutely no Medic class in the group and if you get injured and request for medical assistance, you get none! Even requesting for a med pack gets you silence. See what's the problem here? And yet the AI Gunslinger, for example, continues to create problems by chucking a grenade at the first special zombie it sees or if a Lurker jumps out of hiding or if the number of zombies appears to be more than 5, drawing swarms and then has the sheer dumbness to say "We're too loud!" If you are playing singleplayer, the Medic class is perhaps the most important character especially at insane or extreme difficulty because as mentioned, certain classes like the AI Gunslinger are UTTERLY DUMB and yet there is still no rectification on this by Saber Interactive. Seriously, what kind of nonsense is this? Saber Interactive, this must be rectified. More cosmetics and more gun leveling are actually not needed, they are basically wastes of time but class selection for AI companions/bots and the ability to use skills that the SP had so tediously grinded for IS IMPORTANT. IMPLEMENT IT.3. If the problems #1 and #2 above are not bad enough, then there's the issue with the weapons. This is yet another tedious grinding part of the game but one that a player will most like gladly undertake just to get the option to put on suppressors on most of the weapons. This leads to Problem #3 where they use unsuppressed weapons in the missions regardless of the fact that suppressor option has already been unlocked for said weapons. The stupid thing is that SP / offline players will get companion remarks like 'keep silent' or something to the effect and yet, they are using un-suppressed weapons? And will use them whenever the number of active/running zombies go above 10 or so? What nonsense is that? Zombie waves already appear to trigger on its own from time to time regardless so why make it more difficult for SP / offline players at high or max difficulty level?From a personal perspective, this is just nonsense and makes the SP / offline players grinding to get that suppressor option pointless in relation to AI companions on top of the already nonsensical lack of ability to change their class and being stuck at level 0.All of the above also gives the impression that SP / offline option was added merely as an afterthought and players are basically forced for multiplayer if they want to enjoy (A) actual leveled companions and (B) use of suppressed weapons (other than the pistol) by their companions.Point is, if the developer wants to further milk the product to cater for SP, then don't half-ass it. Otherwise, just make it strictly multiplayer only and I can happily return this to Steam. No refund required.As much as I like the game and I honestly do, unfortunately I have to give this a thumbs down for the problems abovementioned which continue (from personal perspective) to persist for whatever nonsensical reasons that the developer may have.EDIT2: The only reason I continue to play this is just to kill/pass time because I have no other game that I can play in short bursts before returning back to whatever work I am doing. However, if the issues are not rectified, even this game will bore me eventually and when that happens (yes, not if but when), this would be a disincentive to buy any other Saber Interactive products for continuing failure to rectify obvious problems that should have been long since corrected.

_childDocuments_.review: Have played this game on Epic but moved to steam version recently.The game offers a gripping and immersive experience that's sure to delight both fans of the series and newcomers, impressing with its intense cooperative action and strategic depth. Classes, abilities, and weapon upgrades add layers to game play, making teamwork essential, and the revamped melee system is a highlight, offering visceral satisfaction. The game also boasts stunning graphics with detailed environments and realistic character models, while its lighting effects and sound design create an atmosphere that draws players in.While not groundbreaking, the narrative-driven campaigns provide a compelling backdrop to the action, immersing players in a globe-trotting journey to uncover the outbreak's mysteries. The game truly shines in its cooperative multiplayer mode, emphasizing teamwork and replay ability, thanks to the dynamic AI Director that keeps each play through fresh and exciting.Offering diverse characters, satisfying combat, and stunning visuals, it's a must-play for fans and newcomers alike. It delivers adrenaline-pumping action and heart-pounding cooperative play in a post-apocalyptic world. Don't miss the chance to experience the Aftermath for yourself, embrace the chaos and survive the swarm ☠️.

_childDocuments_.review: So, World War Z: Aftermath. A horde-shooter based of a gimmick from a film and adapted it into it's main mechanic. What can be cooler than mowing down a literal wall of flesh hungry rotbags, right? And it has so many different locations, characters, weapons, tactics. It must be a dream come true, isn't it?But after a few matches I have a few very important things to share. WWZ: Aftermath has a potential to be a great game, but right now it's mediocre at best. As someone with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ internet, the whole P2P thing is disastrous if my connection decides to kill itself. But that's a minor complaint and something most players can live with. What I can't forgive is lack of general customization of bots, dull and sometimes stock sounds for weapons and very poor audio work for special infected.Problem No.1 - Bots are dumb as a sack of bricks.Sure, they can be useful, but only in killing. The entire map is just babysitting a bunch of level 0 braindead idiots, who can't even navigate correctly. If they are stuck somewhere, they are teleported to you and potentially can fall through a texture. You also can't customize them, give them different classes and other great stuff. They can't even follow simple commands like "pick this up, refill the turret, hold this position". If this is not true, please let me know how to, because the menu is a god-awful mess. If it is, then what are they even good for? They are useless! How did a 12-year-old game managed to make a good AI and this one didn't? Probably because they didn't think that someone would actually play with bots and threw it in just for show, but those bots are still part of the game and it needs to be done good.Problem No.2 - Weapons sound weak and feel like peashooters.How a weapon sounds and feels impacts overall enjoyment of combat in a game like this. Guns here sound weak and I swear, I heard one or two stock sounds every now and then. This is bad. Bad on so many levels. Just why does .45 ACP pistol sounds like .22 LR? IT'S WEAK. EVERYTHING HERE SOUNDS WEAK.Problem No.3 - Special Infected lack sound design.Left 4 Dead did this one great. Vermintide 2 did this one great. WWZ did it this one poorly.If your game depends on huge hordes of enemies, then for the love of god, do some proper sound and art design for them. WWZ's infected are near impossible to detect in a big crowd. And don't get me started with "but they made sound design for them, can't you hear it?". No. I can't. In amidst all the chaos, I can't hear them. Again, L4D did a good job, Vermintide 2 did a good job, but here it seems incomplete.Problem No.4 - This one is pure nitpicking, but REALLY? We can't place AT LEAST turrets where WE want? We can't pack them up and relocate? Why?Overall, the game is solid in its own right, but it has so many small inconveniences that just pile up and ruin the fun, so I PERSONALLY cannot recommend this to anyone. My time with it was not an enjoyable experience. But I'll hold off a refund and hope for the best - that Saber will improve on it and make this game into another exceptional horde-shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Great 4 person coop fun with mates and solo, though bots can be pretty dumb. Large hordes, zombies are satisfying to shoot, specials are well designed with clear audio cues, directional sounds and fair counterplay just like in L4D2. Maps are varied enough to keep each session fresh, with daily and weekly challenges with unique modifiers to keep the game interesting.Difficulty range is adequate with 5 levels of challenge, from easy to extreme. Harder difficulties will need good team coordination, map/objective knowledge and levelled weapons and classes for maximum advantages against the infected. Keeping silent to avoid unnecessary hordes is a key skill to learn.Gunplay is like L4D2 with no ADS even in first person, but not necessary. Good variety of weapons and classes for different flavours of zombie killing. Almost feels like a spiritual successor to l4d2 with more customization and depth. No versus though.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun but has a few larger issues. I will speak of the issues I take with the game first. The early and late game both feel dissatisfying for different reasons. The early game nothing feels special about until you start unlocking perks for whichever class you are playing which isn't an issue for long but made it harder to initially get my friends into it. As well the difficulties don't feel well balanced where anything below three skulls is absurdly easy and at four skulls and higher felt much harder with certain maps making things harder or easier as well. Before I can explain the issues with the late game I must explain the problems with the AI. The AI simply can't replace actual people. The bots cannot use defenses, gather anything, use higher tier weapons, or level up alongside you. For these reasons you have to play more less on your own o higher difficulties, which is what you must play in the late game.  The late game is simply too much of a grind. On the easier difficulties you don't earn enough credits to prestige classes and level up weapons without a serious grind though I learned of an easier grind for credits and XP.  The issue is that it doesn't give any blue credits which are required for some of the better weapon perks. On the topic of weapon perks to even be granted the option to purchase some weapon perks you must collect documents which can only be gotten 1/3 of a piece at a time on the randomized daily challenges. As I said, a major grind. The hordes and zombies in general are phenomenal to watch run, pile up and break through defenses. It also feels great gunning down those same hordes. Each class does feel unique and fun as you level them up. The campaign is fun to play through the first few times and has enough variety between the episodes to allow each to feel unique despite following the same general formula. I think the game can be fun alone but is much better enjoyed with friends and do recommend it. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing World War Z since launch on Epic store and still play it on Steam Today and just now I'm writting a review?Anyways World War Z the game is based off the Movie which was not well received however i did like both the book and the movie but i viewed the movie as it's own thing. However i will say that this game makes the concept of the movie and makes it work. I will explain more of that later as i separate this review in sections.Gameplay: The gameplay for Wwz is really good, you might think of this as just another horde shooter. However that is not the case. With the various classes and abilities you can use in combination with weapons and teammates. There's a lot of variety in what you can do. Zombies (Zeke) will climb over each other to form a pyramid to get you. The game has a lot of "defense" moments in which you prepare a defence and hold. However this game does them right and it doesn't feel repatative because sometimes you are met with an objective or the general environment is nice to play in. The classes and weapons in this game are all well balanced, no specific class or weapon is particuarly better then the other and it all comes down to playstyle preferense. For example i love playing Gunslinger with the sporting carbine. I have it maxed out to the point that my sporting carbine a tier 2 rifle is better then most of my tier 3 weapons. The overall flow of the game is great and the zombie types are really good from the Bull/Stalker and the annoying Screamer that tends to ruin your Nightmare runs because it screams, bringing in a horde. I only really played the PVP multiplayer once and got completely steamrolled so i don't have much of an opinion. But most people play it for the PVE anyways.Story: The overall story of Wwz is broken up into Episodes and Chapters, each taking place in different locations with different survivors trying to achive a specific goal. I really love this concept because aside from Episode 1 New York in which your on your own until the last chapter where your working with the military. You get that feeling like your fighting a war against the undead. Episode 2 has you getting an orbital laser online to use against the Zeke. Episode 3 has you poisioning the streets of Moscow to clear it out so that one day you can take back the city and with Episode 4 you're evacuating Tokyo and later play as the same crew from Tokyo in Episode 7. But they mention that one day they will return. I do like how story wise the zombies are actively hunting to wipe out humanity and that the virus's soul purpose is to pretty much wipe out humanity. It feels like a genuine war in which they are being hunted rather then the zombies are just mindlessly wondering around looking for their next victim to eat. And in chapter 6 set in Rome you fight to take back the city and you do manage to take it back. And that concept is something i am very interesting in exploring more into. Civilization reclaiming their land from the zombies is definitely something i want them to explore more on. Adding more to that feeling of fighting a war against the undead.Horde mode: I had to give this it's dedicated spot because to me i think I've spent more time on Horde mode then any other. It's the basic consept of defending your position and holding out. But you have a gate that you must protect. If destroyed, you lose. You are given resources that you can use to buy more weapons or defense setups. The hordes will get more and more difficult as each wave comes. You have 2 locations to defend and every 5 waves you will be relocated to the next spot. Note that you can never have both locations be under attack at the same time unless you happen to go over there and trigger a mini horde from making too much noise. But the horde mode is a great way to level up weapons and find good strategies in dealing with large hordes and using defense kits. I normally do like survival modes or horde modes. And sometimes they can get repetative but overall something with WwZ's horde mode just keeps me coming back no matter what. The idea of trying to go better then last time is what really keeps me going on this mode. And when you do break your own record, it's a feel good feeling. There's also Horde XL wich is Horde but with bigger waves in different locations which is a welcomed edition but can get more difficult.Conclusion: World War Z is a great game, taking from the Movie which took nothing from the book. And made it great, the gameplay, maps, characters, story is all good and always has me and my friends coming back to play more of. I hope to see this game thrive and keep going. If you have been curious to picking this game up, It's worth it

_childDocuments_.review: Not just a Left4Dead clone, I think World War Z: Aftermath has a lot of things that set it apart from Left4Dead and similar games.The major one is classes that let you play the way you want and give you a clear role to perform on the team. And within each class there are different skills that you can unlock as you progress in level. Some of the classes are pretty unique as well, such as the Drone Master which gives you a deployable drone that you can customize with your skills.There are way more objective types. Defending points, stealthing, bypassing traps, and escort missions are just some of the different objectives I've seen. It's not just running and gunning the entire time, sometimes you take a break to restock your supplies and setup defensive for a coming horde. Defensive turrets and traps can be placed which make these very dynamic.The zombie hordes are massive. Hundreds of zombies on screen at once. You don't want to get caught out in the open when they bust through the defenses.I originally bought this just to scratch my zombie game itch until Back4Blood came out. But after playing the Back4Blood beta and World War Z for about the same amount of time, I've definitely had more fun with World War Z.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike Back 4 Blood, this game is actually fun.-Weapons are great. Variety, upgrades, the sounds, feedback, camera.-Characters have decent backstory and are not dudebro 12 year old appeal cringe.-Levels are decently varied, though somewhat short and linear.-Defense items and heavy weaponry feels powerful and useful and is nice to use.-Big swarms are pretty cool to take down, special zeds are well made and for lack of a better term 'realistic' which I kinda dig.-And icing on the cake is a bunch of (rather basic) classes to pick from, a switchable first person mode on the fly and crossplay with your friends on console.These things are all excellent. A grounded in reality, fun, engaging horde shooter that has *some* longevity in it's fun combat and upgrade system.It's only big weakness is the amount of maps. They're pretty short, slightly generic and the game needed way more of them. It's like having a big Supra but only being able to drive it in your local parking lot. L4D and KF are endless because of workshop maps and how repeated playthroughs can play out different but this game doesn't have workshop nor many maps or alternate paths, all you can end up doing is play the same identical runs but on a higher difficulty if you care about that. You always go the same exact A to B on repeating a map. Only difference is some objective item placement and only rarely. A dent in an otherwise enjoyable game, but it knocks the value down considerably.One last mention would be that AI bots are only functional on starting difficulty but atrocious and useless on any difficulty above that and will make you uninstall the game in .3 seconds. They are incredibly weak and even fully healed will go down in the first 20 seconds of a battle on higher difficulties, they need a serious buff. So for normal or higher it's with friends only or you're basically carrying the entire AI team on your own. Base difficulty is mostly fine solo, but even there the bots will randomly all perish and have almost no contribution to kills and will just randomly leave you to die from a special zed.If the game would have workshop maps or more maps / paths I would recommend the game for $40,- but with the low replay value because of the linear and small number of maps I set the value on about $15-20,-It'll be pretty fun for a few evenings solo or with friends but most regular players won't get 100 hours or more out of it like other games in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: While it has its issues (these vary depending on who you ask), this fro me is a pretty good online multiplayer experience. Has been my most played game fro at least two years, originally on PlayStation and now on PC. While the multiplayer (PvPvE) is pretty much abandoned the horde mode and multiplayer story levels have enough activity you are never far away from people to group with. Starting out it can be difficult as there are a lot of players who know what needs to be done, where the hidden picks ups are and some are critical of players who don't play by the unwritten rule book of the WWZ class system. You may feel you are always trying to catch up with everyone else.  That's said you will find plenty of 999 level players who are happy to support new players and understand that when you are starting out you may not have realised your unsilenced gun attracts zombies and that's why they keep appearing. They are also 99 player who don't understand that new players wanting to play with other players will have to search for games on a higher difficulty that there character is levelled for.Levels themselves  are semi-random in what pickups etc you come across and this coupled with other players actions in the game makes each level play out slightly differently. Personally I find this a really good game to unwind. There is no seasons pass, no IAP's. There are lots of things in game to unlock and there are some optional skins that can be bought which are visual only and I assume a way for the developer to bring in additional funds for a game that has been out for a while. These are completely optional though and no shoved in your face to buy.  A common want from many of the payers is new levels to be added. More have been added over the years but I view this as a some measure of how good the core game play is. People want more of it. If you want to point and shoot, blow up, hack down hundreds of zombies in a game that can provide a challenge once you ramp up the difficulty you wont be disappointing with WWZA

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you can get this dirt cheap (90% or more discount levels of dirt cheap) AND have friends to play with, avoid.The only thing that stands out (positively) in this game is the novelty of meat tubes for zombies.Too bad the animations on them are absolutely awful, coupled with an overwhelming amount of bugs and out of whack hit boxes that quickly make said novelty tedious and stale rather than cool.- Underneath the shiny little veneer of "good graphics", is an unpolished mess that constantly tanks in quality and gives you no ability to stop its internal control. Flagship PCs will still get massive FPS plummets out of nowhere, be plagued by stuttering and witness every meat tube turn into indistinguishable messes for textures alongside the world around them.- Regional Servers don't exist (NA or bust) & private servers aren't allowed. And the developers answer to this? LAN or bust. - You cannot kick people from a lobby.- You need 3/4 votes to kick people from an active game. Voting is as cumbersome as it is unintuitive, leading to most players not taking the time (or the risk of dying) to kick someone if they even know how to. Nevermind the fact that if you've got ANY bots in your game, the kick will never pass. - Quite the "lovely" community that will make you rethink the "but being able to kick would be abused" stance.- Public Matchmaking is absolutely awful- PVP matchmaking is nonexistant - No pause in single player- Single Player is not Offline; it is Online Only.- You cannot rejoin a game after you've been disconnected.- Zombies will hit you from more than two full character lengths away- I've lost count of how many T-Posed zombies have completely wrecked an entire team- Rat Pack audio does not play far more often than it does. It also has the most bugged out hit boxes out of every single enemy in the entire game, while simultaneously being the most dangerous (will wipe the entire team in less than 60 seconds if activated and not killed immediately; less than 30 seconds if on higher difficulties). - Zombies treating the floor like an ice rink and moving faster because of it is extremely common- The bulk of ones play time will be finding matches and dealing with bugs, rather than actually enjoying the game.- Majority of the available guns are not impactful and they do not feel fun to use, something that does not change even with perks and class swaps. While this isn't extremely apparent on the easier difficulties, Insane/Extreme will have you using the exact same thing every single time because anything else is as much of a hindrance as it is a vastly inferior damage choice.- The chore of having to level every single gun to level 6 just to get the silencer for it exists. Comes with the added bonus of silencers being varying degrees of effective on each weapon (the values of which are not listed and you're expected to figure it out on your own). - The XL Horde modes are poorly designed nightmares- The party A.I is a special kind of stupid that makes bots from late 90s games look like heroes; you'll spend more time fighting with the bot A.I than you will anything else, especially if unfortunate enough to be solo- Every single special infected is a lazy L4D rip off that border on being carbon copies. _childDocuments_.review: World War Z is a four-player, third-person, co-op shooter where you complete objectives while fending off zombie waves. You can play it with other people or play solo. The game emphasizes strong teamwork; if you try to Rambo your way through a level, like I did the first time I playing you will die. You need to stay close to your teammates and watch each other's back. I played the entire game solo and bots always saved me when I was pinned down by a zombie and helped me out of trouble. AI of the bots is good. Aftermath retains all the features from the base game, while adding new elements that further enhance the terrifying experience. The new, first-person perspective is a great addition. It brings you closer to the action. There are two brand new co-op story missions to shoot through, set in the Vatican City and Russia’s snowy Kamchatka peninsula. These follow the theme of World War Z’s epic backdrops that host each separate episode in the interconnected, zeke infested world. Each mission looks distinctly unique and fun to play. Classes are the way in which World War Z offers the player customisation, with numerous skills to unlock as you gain experience. Weapons also work in a similar way, with you upgrading them in numerous ways as you use them in the co-op campaign episodes. Also, in Aftermath the melee system has had an overhaul. Vanguard is the brand new class available in this update, as well as daily missions offering unique rewards which you can find out more about in the brand new message of the day pop up box in the game menu. World War Z: Aftermath is the most substantial, and impressive update yet. New content and improvements to how the game performs means World War Z has never been in better shape. The question is Is Aftermath worth it? It is if you are a fan World War Z and are looking for more content. The new class is a decent addition and can add a new tactical choice when facing the hordes, while both the episodes of Rome and Kamchatka add a couple more hours of content and more variety for when you're grinding for levels and upgrades. World War Z: Aftermath improves on the base game in a number of ways. Despite the new content only adding a few short hours of gameplay, there are more reasons than ever for players to keep coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - the game is very good fun and to anyone who hasn't played it before or doesn't own WWZ, this is a good buy. To elaborate: a slightly different take on L4D's formula that allows the game to cohabit in the genre rather than feeling like a worse knock-off (looking at you B4B...). Highly enjoyable in coop and the masses of zombies getting mowed down by lots of bullets or explosions is incredibly satisfying. There is a lot of gameplay here for those that want it, weapon and skill trees, horde mode, daily challenges etc. Plenty of missions too and difficulty makes a large difference. A caveat to mention: this game IS the older title found on other services like EGS and Gamepass, but with an added 2 mission trees, an FPP mode, updated melee, a new class and some new weapons. In other words, this is functionally a GOTY edition with all the frills (another note - there are a further two DLC that provide weapon skins and a couple of melee weapons that SHOULD have been included in the base price - very cheeky to have them as further DLC). The value proposition on this one will vary depending on how the game was obtained before. I would say for people who own the previous version, the £30 price tag is a bit steep and they should wait for an inevitable sale. Similarly for people who own this on different services and consoles. Personally, I had the chance to play and complete this during a Gamepass trial and knew what I was going into. Overall a surprisingly fun game. New content since the original release, fun gameplay and generally a strong recommend for new people or those who never paid full price. To those that own the game already, I would say this is a "sale" game. Also note that progress can be carried over from EGS quite easily, but Gamepass makes it much more of a nuisance. That, and there are potentially oceanic server issues (in that they dont have any). However, just looking at the game - its a big thumbs up for a simple, fun and undemanding experience that can be challenging in a good way.

_childDocuments_.review: August 2022 edit: Game is developmentally dead. It has a bunch of campaigns which are about 3-4 missions long each, a single Horde survival map, and pvp multiplayer. Multiplayer is absolutely dead, but you can still find people to play with in the campaigns and horde mode relatively easily, as the game is crossplay with Steam, Epic, PS and Xbox. Pick it up on sale, it's a fun time, you'll probably get around 80 hrs of replayability before you never want to look at it again, though. I think the amount of campaigns the game has is fine, but it absolutely needs more horde maps.*** Unironically one of the best co-op zombie games in recent years. Do yourself a favor and pick it up.However, there's lots of cheaters. Being primarily co-op, it's not *that* big of a deal but it's still annoying as there's so many lv 999's that are inexcusably garbage players because they're boosted through cheats. I've yet to see a legitimate high level player, aside from a single 800-something who was beasting his way through an Insane-difficulty level on his own.The cheaters vary from doing nothing out of the ordinary, to increasingly obvious things such as quietly getting their health back, respawning themselves after death, to teleporting out of bounds and aimbotting all the zombies on the map. With the game running on a peer-to-peer matchmaking system, the character files are easily editable and there's no way to report anyone so it's something you just have to either deal with or find a new lobby. It's a prevalent issue, but by-and-large, because of the nature of the game, not one that impacts your game experience 98% of the time. If you've played it, It's comparable to the cheaters in Payday 2 -- a lot of users and a few abusers.Cheaters aside, the game honestly gets an 8/10 from me, as a longtime-fan of the 4 player co-op genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially was put off by this game for a couple of reasons, the first being the fact that the publisher/developer initially made this an Epic Games exclusive, and I don't like to support that, also after watching videos I saw of people getting insta-killed by invincible rats, and the fact the zombies seemed "weightless" and almost too easy to kill.Regarding the Epic/Steam thing, I came to the conclusion that if you don't support the game on the platform of your choice, then you're just giving companies less incentive to put it on that platform. For the invincible rats, it seems to be totally fixed now, I don't think I've even been downed by them once. As for the weightless zombies and being too easy to kill, when you're actually playing versus watching gameplay, it doesn't bug me, and I've realized that in order to have that many zombies attacking you at once, they really need to be somewhat easy to kill or you wouldn't survive a single map. After about 10 hours I can say this game is pretty awesome, and far more enjoyable than Back 4 Blood. I say this as someone who has more hours in L4D2 than any other game, and I've been wanting another a game that scratched that itch. Pros: -The amount of zombies on screen and how many you kill is amazing, I have no idea how they made it run so smoothly. -The game doesn't have any stupid card system and the guns are handled similar to L4D where you don't have to earn money to buy them-Easy game to jump in and play a map and then go about your day. If you're an older, jaded FPS gamer who just likes to play a few minutes here and there, then it's a good buy-Good amount of levels, each one takes you around 20-30 minutes-Characters aren't as annoying as Back 4 Blood-Private and offline game modes-Very gory. Not just the shooting of the zombies, but the environments have a lot of gruesome details you would expect to see in the aftermath of a zombie apocalypse-Nice color palette. Not all washed out and dark. Mostly well lit levels where you can see everything.Cons:-Game was not originally designed for first person, so it feels slightly wonky at first, but you get used to it. -No real ADS (Aim Down Sights), just a slight zoom in-Bots aren't the brightest, but better than Back 4 Blood and similar to L4D's bots at launch. So far I've been able to beat every map I've tried with bots on the easier difficulty levels -Each "campaign" has 3 levels (maybe some have 4), and each one is set in a different location with different characters, so you don't really get attached to any character like you would in L4D. They also don't have the great personality's that L4D characters have-Can't bind certain keys like Delete above the arrow keys (this is a problem with a lot of Unreal games)-"Special infected" are underwhelmingOverall: I'd say pick this up if you are looking for something similar to L4D, especially if you were let down by Back 4 Blood. B4B has a few things that this game doesn't like more continuity between maps and characters, and of course ADS, but I personally just find WWZ to be a more enjoyable game.For the record I only played a few hours of Back 4 Blood, but I think I played enough to get a good idea of the differences between the games.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z is constantly being compared to Left 4 Dead, and no wonder: too many concepts are borrowed from the classic dilogy. And the first races in WWZ give the same feelings that L4D gave at first. However, the gameplay of both games is based on a different philosophy. Left 4 Dead is dedicated to the confrontation of survivors and special infected, and ordinary zombies are there more for the atmosphere. In World War Z, everything is exactly the opposite: players confront the horde, sometimes distracted by special zombies. Key mechanics are built around the horde, and it is the mistakes in the confrontation with it that lead to defeat.Actually, the main thing that is required of the survivors is to productively exterminate hundreds of zombies until they destroy some plot object or pile the whole crowd on your team. And it would be fine if they only reduced their health with their attacks, so no: the horde can really crush the mass, knocking the player who was in its path to the ground. Instantly! I didn't have time to get out of the way, and you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥ — you're lying down and calling your allies for help via voice chat.Yes, these "stars" can be dropped on the heads of zombies. But, in general, the interactivity leaves much to be desiredOf course, they will not be able to lift you right away — you must first destroy the living dead, otherwise the rescuer will immediately find himself side by side on the ground, crushed by the all-destroying horde. Therefore, the key to successful passage is the competent positioning and use of stationary machine guns and mortars.During the defense, you have to distribute responsibilities: one sits behind a heavy weapon, the second helps him with automatic fire, the third fights off small groups of zombies trying to come from the rear, and the fourth mines approaches and simultaneously replenishes ammunition. There is no universal scheme: you always have to adjust to the situation, taking into account the protective devices thrown by the game and the classes available to players.Competent handling of a stationary machine gun is half the success, because you can't get enough ammunition for all zombiesThere are six of them in the game. The shooter throws grenades and increases weapon damage. The bomber scatters mines and C4, and can also use shotguns more effectively. The medic distributes stimulants to allies that temporarily increase health. A technician can carry camouflage grenades (for a while they hide survivors in a cloud of gas from the hungry gazes of zombies), reinforced cartridges and a piercing charge with which you can break into rooms with a good loot. The executioner specializes in melee weapons, and the fighter enhances heavy weapons and burns enemies with Molotov cocktails.Each class has an impressive leveling tree, so the field for experimenting with the composition of the ideal group is quite wide. With a technician and a medic, any four players act much better, although a quartet of some shooters gives a good light. Pumping also depends on how difficult you can play: if in Left 4 Dead the starting conditions for players are unchanged, and success depends solely on direct hands, then in World War Z a group of beginners will not physically master the highest difficulty — there simply will not be enough firepower.Of the three gray abilities in the column, only one can be used at the same time, so it's not worth spending precious currency to buy each skillPumping is simple: when playing for a certain class, the player gets experience, which opens access to new abilities, and the currency for which they need to be bought. It's the same with weapons: they shot enough — the next level of improvement was opened. True, the weapon has only five degrees of pumping, but some barrels have two paths of development. There is always a little less money in your pocket than you need, so you have to save as much as possible.The characters calmly walk through each other. It breaks the atmosphere, but at least the players are not satisfied with traffic jams in narrow corridors!The difficulty increases smoothly (it also has five levels), and that's fine, but most of the players prefer to hang out on the first three. It is difficult to conquer "very difficult" and "crazy" levels without friends, often it is not even possible to recruit players. And going with bots is not an option: not only do they match the strength of the first—level players, they also do not know how to pick up first-aid kits and shoot stationary weapons.Unlike L4D, where all the events take place in America, World War Z — what a book, what a movie, what a game — tells about the fight against a zombie epidemic all over the planet. Here we get to different countries and can admire not only American landscapes. The variety of settings is a significant advantage of the franchise, but the execution in places leaves much to be desired.The subway turned out to be the most reliable from the creators. But the GUM in the game is just a pale shadow of a real buildingFor example, Moscow was frankly screwed up: it looks not like a European city, but like a Soviet mausoleum. Microscopic gray GUM, reinforcement bars on windows in the city center, the same type of faceless cars — if there was such a capital of Russia, it was only in the last century! The plot of this campaign also raises questions: the heroes, under the cheerful commands of a man named Paper and a certain Svetlana, as if descended from the posters of the Red Alert game, should fill the city with nerve gas from a secret bunker under the Kremlin… In general, cranberries in their own juice. To complete the picture, the only thing missing from the four Russians is an alcoholic bear exterminating zombies with a balalaika.It sounds like the ending of a bad joke: "Why did the Russians build a secret underground bunker?.."It's hard to say how much other locations have been misrepresented: New York looks exactly the same as in The Division, and the other levels are quite authentic. Although, perhaps, the residents of Hokkaido and Jerusalem would not say so. But diversity has definitely succeeded, and it's not just about architecture, but also about the tasks of the heroes. In the USA, we fight our way through the city to escape, in Israel — for the activation of satellite weapons, in Japan we help organize the last stage of evacuation. Every time the heroes have to defend an object, defend themselves, look for some keys or supplies, it is logical and brings a pleasant variability to the gameplay.Israel is not petty — the locals exterminate zombies with orbital weapons strikesThe wide geography of the game pushed the developers to a completely logical decision: each campaign involves a separate set of characters. And although this decision is reasonable, three missions are decidedly not enough to reveal the characters. The developers also understand this — apparently, that's why they put videos with the backstories of the participants of each team into the game. Alas, this is still not enough: you don't stick to the heroes, and you don't get into their characters. It is remembered only that Sergius is a former bandit, and now an Orthodox priest and a zombie fighter.A zombie "ram" must either be shot with a shotgun, or thrown with grenades, or beaten in close combat from the backThe situation is quite sad in the camp of special infected: there are few of them, and they are quite weak. The catcher looks like a hunter from L4D on tranquilizers: he can't jump from above, and he blows your health quite lazily. A toxicist in a chemical protection suit is dangerous only after death: if you shoot him not in the head, he begins to emit a poisonous gas that limits visibility and causes damage. A battering ram is just an armored zombified special forces fighter, who can only be shot in the back or through the helmet glass.

The first time you see the hordes your jaw will drop, and the terror of it all, as well as the hype, is great when sharing it with a group of people you know. Just when you thought the devs exaggerated it as far as it can go, they'll make you go "no way...that's craaazy lol" again and again. Standing back to back with your team and seeing that you're outnumbered a gazillion to one is exhilarating.The game is pretty easy on normal difficulty so we played out the story on hard mode, which is also far from the hardest difficulty. If you're looking for a challenge I assure you, this game can get pretty brutal and frustrating. Between grinding your class for perks/weapons in horde mode and the campaign alone, there's a lot of content here already. I haven't touched any of the multiplayer modes. Only hordes for grinding prestige to get all of my perks and story mode have provided me with 69 hours of gameplay. Pretty decent for $40 if you ask me, even better on sale.There's not much in the way of bugs other than one or two enemy specific bugs we've encountered only when the game is on hard mode. Outside of that the game runs great. Some of us had high-end rigs, others with low end laptops with iGPUs. Everyone was able to get a stable, high frame rate experience, while making adjustments to the graphic settings of course. I'm glad the devs plan to release a new horde mode soon. Looking forward to that and extending the time I spend with the game. It's a really fun PvE co-op.

Character skills are a bit better as they offer multiple builds, but even then balance is an issue as some skills are objectivly better. Stealth is really light and all it does is either make the areas inbetween defenses easier or hard, if you use suppressor you won't trigger hordes and vice versa. Defenses are probably where the game really shines, you get a minute or so of time to set up defenses and then have to defend the objective from massive hordes(I'm talking hundreds of them).This is also very lore friendly and canonically right which is a plus. The game seems REALLY short and is on the grindy side if you want to max it out and for that reason I wouldn't pay full price for it, sub 30 and you're golden.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I thought I was done with first-person shooter zombies. This fps does what we always hoped would be done - years ago - with the game genre, adding tangible long-term depth to the experience in the best tradition of deep bank-robbing fps's. Anachronistically, World War Z is faithful to the film yet bereft of the mad mutant million-mile-an-hour scrambling this player has grown to hate. You can actually appreciate creature animation and graphical work in this game. Various minor and major aspects of play set World War Z apart as a fun experience, rather than a straight-forward attempt to kill players. That's refreshing. Excellent dialogue, imaginative environmental design, satisfying gunplay. Many character classes & persistent skills contribute rpg-lite qualities to this title. This cooperative shooter is WORTHY.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME SAVED MY LIFE.I am 28My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to recommend this game, but can't. It's far too grindy, the bots are completely worthless, some classes just aren't worth playing, and the matchmaking is terrible. People constantly go AFK and take up a slot so no one else can join, leaving you (at best) in a 3 man team fighting a horde sized for 4. People also like to friendly fire a lot. Having to play on Hard challenge mode to get challenge coins makes this extremely frustrating, as a lot of the "challenges" make the level essentially unbeatable unless you're playing with 4 high leveled people that are very good at the game.I've gotten fairly far in terms of meta progression, but the barrier to entry on a single match makes me just not care anymore. The length of wait time to get into a match is bad enough, but having to rely on luck to get good teammates just obliterates any chance of me wanting to play anymore. As there's no way to create/search individual lobbies, or stop yourself from matching with a person you know is intentionally friendly firing your whole team, you're subjected to the whims of whatever algorithm this game's search function is running.One positive thing about the game: The horde mode is pretty cool, and there's not usually wait time for it. Unfortunately, I'm not sure you get any points if you leave early. It's a good way to power level upgrades and regular currency, but most of the more desirable upgrades for guns require blue challenge coins, which you'll have to play the regular challenge modes for.If the lobby system were fixed so people could actually host a lobby, kick/ban people from joining their lobbies, and search for a list of lobbies, the game would actually be playable. Unfortunately, I can't recommend it in its current state, and I have no reason to believe it will change.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: (29/12/21) Since I wrote this review, the latest patch from Sabre has added in Oceania servers, and the game play has been improved. I've removed the negative score, and updated the commentary to reflect the current games state.TL:DR: It's fun If you love L4D style games, this is an excellent game. Graphically, the cities, player models and environments look quite good, and give a sense of atmosphere, whether you are prowling the streets of New York, or skulking through a foggy graveyard in Rome.Audio is likewise good, with recognisable sound effects from L4D and Dead Island. Gameplay is smooth, the guns feel 'right', and the zombies are just as nimble as their L4D counterparts, sometimes more so. More than once, a zombie would run at me full speed, hunched over to avoid getting headshotted like the rest of the horde. They also have the same mechanism as L4D, where they will often run behind you to attack, causing you to frequently do a 360 melee spin to clear them off.The maps are quite large, detailed and the loot spawns are random, so it's not guaranteed that the same defences or weapons will be there next time. Ammo resupplies are fairly constant in their spawn areas, but you might find that the gap between them is too large, especially if the Director is happy to see you and sends lots of zombies to come hug and kiss you. For some maps, you may have to melee through the trash mobs, and shoot the hordes.There is a progression system for weapons and perks, based on XP points gained from missions, regardless of whether you were successful or not. You'll find yourself levelling up quite quickly after a few hours, and increasing the addons and magazine capacity of your weapons.There is also several class systems (gunslinger, demo, medic, etc) that you can level up in, making the team loadout much more varied and with a decent allocation of complimentary skills. This, of course, adds in replayability as you might want to main as the team medic or drone specialist on harder levelsOverall the feel is very consistent, and if you've played these games before, it'll be like slipping on a pair of comfortable shoesWould have no hesitation is recommending it to a friend. _childDocuments_.review: This game requires a LOT of polish and quality of life, and it seems to prevent itself from making it very fun for the sake of balance or weird design decisions:- Can't see perk chosen by teammates.- UI requires a LOT of work: -- make the primary weapons / secondary weapons / skills available to choose easily from lobby (not through another menu but through a box you can click which will show your teammates what you got as well).-- perk selection are very confusing: as an exterminator, I want to play with molotov, but if I select both molotov perks and claymore perks, I am automatically equipped with claymores.-- very confusing to know where to choose weapons and skins for the mission. You have a menu to observe all characters, and a menu to select your character for the mission.- It's nice to find unique weapons, but it's not fun to just ditch them out once they are empty. Allow players to play more with unique super weapons.- Explosions / aoe weapons feedbacks are lacking. Every explosions feel very underwhelming.- It's heresy to have aoe weapon only affect a limited amount of enemies. I want my grenade to hit everything in the radius of its explosion, not just "x" enemies based on perk or level.- Coop does not feel very significant. There is not much/enough synergy and you feel more as 4 individual players, rather than a team.- Lacks a good communication wheel (ping item or location / say thanks or taunt / etc available from  button)- No server list to browse. You just press "find a game" and hope for the best.- Sound design of weapon feels bland, it's not very exciting to shoot.In short, it feels too much as a medium arcade title thought for console first, even with the zombies waves system. It could be amazing, if the devs polish it a lot: rework the UI, the feedback of weapons, the coop aspect and give your weapons a lot more personality.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been sinking hours into World War Z, and let me tell you, it’s a blast! If you’re a fan of fast-paced, cooperative zombie shooters, this game delivers in spades. The gameplay is incredibly engaging—whether you’re teaming up with friends or jumping into random squads, the experience is always thrilling.The horde mechanics are a standout feature. Watching hundreds of zombies swarm towards you can be both terrifying and exhilarating. The game does a fantastic job of creating that intense, "hold-the-line" feeling, and the sense of urgency keeps you on your toes.The variety of weapons and classes adds a nice layer of strategy. I appreciate the customization options, allowing you to tailor your loadout and skills to fit your playstyle. Plus, the different character classes each bring something unique to the table, which helps keep the gameplay fresh.Graphically, the game looks good, especially when the action ramps up. The environments are well-designed, though sometimes repetitive, and the zombie models are pretty detailed. There’s a certain charm to the chaos that’s hard to resist.The downside? There are occasional bugs and matchmaking issues, but they’re minor compared to the overall fun. Plus, the game has a solid update schedule, which is reassuring.In summary, World War Z is a fantastic game for anyone who enjoys cooperative zombie action. It’s not perfect, but the adrenaline-pumping gameplay and cooperative fun make it a standout title. If you’re on the fence, give it a shot—you might just find yourself hooked!

_childDocuments_.review: When the game description mentioned that you can only play as certain characters per area in the co-op campaign, but could play as any in multiplayer, I thought that meant in the story mode you have to play as certain characters but in the regular replayable multiplayer missions you get to play whoever you want. Apparently their definition of "multiplayer" is the competitive game mode. The phrase "co-op campaign" here refers to the entire rest of the game.So you don't get to make your own character, massively destroying player customization and individuality, but you also only get to play as specific characters in each sub section of missions; thus you can't even ground yourself in puppeteering a specific premade character you have to switch to a completely new individual every single sub section. In a game that was originally designed to be in third person, which puts huge emphasis on the appearance of the player.There are layers to the baffling amount of incompetence at play here.Besides destroying customization, forcing players into premade characters does save on short term development but it also hampers the creators long term. Because now that they've created all these completely different characters with completely different body types, designing cosmetics to fit all of them is much more difficult. Which results in developers adding dozens of cosmetics into the game, but each character only has access to the few that were made explicitly for them and all the cosmetics made for characters each player doesn't like are now going to waste. Which is blatantly observable in this game too, each character only has a couple of lazily designed alternate cosmetics because the developers shortsightedly did not design them to be compatible with modular cosmetics like an actual customization system would be.But what's truly disturbing is that the developers added so many premade characters into this game that there's now enough faces and body types for them to have made an actual basic customization system out of it. But they didn't, not only did they go out of their way to design all these completely different character models instead of consolidating it all as one customization system but they explicitly prohibit you from playing as most of them in every single mission. So they put the same amount of effort into producing a more restrictive system, then added a completely new form of restriction onto it which devalues the breadth of their own work.What, do you think the lore of this stock copy paste zombie world is so deep and precious that you had to restrict the characters per chapter to preserve the integrity of the story? What's the story? Random humans run around a random environment inexplicably fighting off an impossible amount of scientifically illogical enemies while performing asinine objectives that could of been completed by whoever took the time to set them up before the protagonists got here; meanwhile the protagonists are casually finding weapons of mass destruction littered around the scenery and can survive blatantly devastating wounds with little duress then completely mend those wounds by just opening up a medical kit on the fly likely without any extensive training in actual medical science. I scarcely believe from a story standpoint something so bereft of creativity would be engaging the first time around let alone after players have been through these missions potentially dozens of times, since this is supposed to be replayable.But I think it's more likely that the game is just this way simply because the developers made a very foolish design decision which quite obviously only made things worse for zero ultimate benefit.Absolutely saddening that I was so looking forward to finally playing another third person multiplayer shooter only to find out it has possibly the most restrictive and completely irrational character system I've ever seen in the game. Which is not only a fundamental design problem in general but is exceptionally worse in a game where you're constantly looking at the character you're meant to be controlling. What an entirely unnecessary stroke of absolute folly.If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: So many asterisks to my recommendation.  It's a very fun game, so it does have the most important element down.  It's addicting and has a perk/class system with prestige and what-not, you'll find a lot of incentive to keep playing the co-op (also a daily challenge mode that seems to occasionally glitch and not tell you the accurate challenges, which can be quite annoying since some of these challenge modes can severely handicap certain classes.  Fix that ♥♥♥♥).The xp system for guns is kind of dumb for multiple reasons.  You hardly get any xp for kills from what I've seen, and you also start with a bunch of unique skins that are mostly better than highest unlockable skin.  The credits that you get after each round are mostly useful for perks and prestige mode, and I have found it to run out pretty quickly once you prestige since it's expensive, so I'm not too bummed by it's uselessness for unlocking gun skins.  I find this to mostly be a good modern alternative to Left 4 Dead.  A lot of people seem to hate Back4Blood and think this game is better, and what I will say is that this does have some unique features (the defense kits can be pretty fun to set up even if they are super fixed and therefore make missions far more repetitive than they need to be).  The game feels incomplete, but the devs do seem to still update it so maybe there's more to come, but $40 is asking a lot.  Yes, it's addicting and fun, but there are more in-depth swarm-coop-shooters out there for a lower price (Payday 2 and Deep Rock Galactic being the best examples).  I'd say wait for a sale, I bought it as part of a bundle for 10 bucks (given, this is the only game I've played out of that bundle) and am totally satisfied paying that.  I'd say it's worth no more than 30 dollars which is how much Deep Rock Galactic costs, and if you had to choose between the two I'd say go with Deep Rock Galactic.Still, I can't deny that it satisfies that L4D itch, and I'd much rather play this than that tbh.  The perk system, the different characters per level, the large amount of levels, the fun defense kits, the large amount of guns that actually all have their own usefulness, it really is an unofficial sequel to L4D and it actually greatly expands upon that type of game.  Side Note: This is a much more accurate adaptation of World War Z than the movie was.  You actually get to see how people around the world try to survive the ordeal as opposed to just one guy saving the world.  Keep in mind, the movie wasn't accurate at all.  Like, at all.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z is a third-person mix of Left 4 Dead and Killing Floor 2 with the biggest enemy hordes I've ever seen in a game. This is really impressive, but at some point you get fed up with it and what's left is a zombie shooter like many others - mind you not a bad one, but not one that absolutely must be played. It's the gaming equivalent of a bad horror movie and a big bucket of popcorn, but it could have been more. There’s the glimmer of potential there that raises the question of what would have happened if the game pulled from the book World War Z, and had things like characters and overarching narratives. There’s plenty of space for this game to exist alongside Left 4 Dead, but instead it comes across as a weaker successor.Pros-------- Rushing zombie hordes are awesome- Classes and weapons allow different play styles- Levels and objectives offer significant variety- Characters are interesting and look really good (aside from Russian accents, that alternate between horrible Russian and French, for some reason)- Set pieces have fantastic presentation, and the sheer amount of zombies filling the screen and falling from above is virtually unmatched in any other coop shooter- Weapons look good, especially when upgradedCons-------- What sliver of lore there is in the game isn't very good- The game fails to properly utilize its settings - Coop campaign is way too short- Dialogue, mission narrative, and even music get grating in repeated runs- Developers should have given each class a choice of starting weapons in a single category instead of forcing players to waste a perk slot- Weapon upgrades are virtually useless before level 5, due to their cost- Lack of explanation for game mechanics- Higher difficulties have sudden difficulty spikes due to extra enemies/short timers and no proper way to deal with them

_childDocuments_.review: Short review:World War Z iz a zombie shooter game with FPS logic. There are similarities between the game and the movie. It mainly focuses on cooperation and multiplayer. It has serious amount of challenge if you want. The weapons are diverse and strategy is mandatory. I think it is better than Left 4 Dead 1 and 2 but this comparison is not valid, since this game has horde mode. Overall, could be real fun with friends who know how to play this good.Long review:Ok first of all we should not be comparing this game with Left 4 Dead. That game is also awesome and rich. World war z is mostly about strategy. This game has 2 modes, 1 is just story progression and 1 is for multiplayer. There is also a horde mode to kill swarm of zombies in a strategic way.Story is kind of boring but you can play it offline and easily finish all of it with bots on your side. All of the story requires 4 players and it can be multiplayer or singleplayer with bots. If you go into multiplayer and expect other people to jump in, be aware, the game changes its progression and map a little. It expects you would get human help and increases the difficulty. If you stick to offline mode, the game will help you a little, since the bots are way too stupid :DYou will meet new characters in the campaign mode. Each has some unique characteristics on the outside. They also have customized outfits but you have to unlock them with challenges. This is not cool. Each campaign mission has some sort of story but mostly, it is point to point zombie survival game.The traps are improtant in this game. There are auto turrets, electric traps, proximity greanades. You will use these to stop and efficiently kill zombies of like 100 in numbers. There are also good number of different weapons from the get go in the game. But in the story, you will start with small ones and discover bigger weapons throughout. Also in horde mode, you will have to unlock them with points.BTW, horde mode. This is where the game excels. It is basically area defense war. Zombies swarm in and you have weapons, traps and friends to stop them. There are destructable environmental ebjects like fences to slow them down but you will need to replace them when they are broken. The game will throw waves at you and you will be rewarded with points. You will use them to buy traps, guns, ammo, medkit and etc. Bots will not get points, so you have to work for them too :DIn this game, bots are idiots. They don't know how to use a stationary machine gun or take a medkit to heal themselves. You will need to take care of them. That is why this game really need friends to be played with.I have never actually played multiplayer mode. There are like capture the flag modes or something. I think horde mode is good enough.There are lots of weapons and their upgrades. You will have unlock points to unlock weapon upgrades, as you play horde mode or story mode. Every character can use every gun in the game.There are classes to chose. Every character can chose every class. These classes are like Medic, Gunslinger, Explorer, Slasher ...etc. They have unique abilities and they will be upgraded too, as long as you play in tha class. Again you will spend unlocking points like in guns. These should have been separated i guess. But the same points will be used for guns and classes so be wise.Visuals are good enough i guess. The gam renders literally a hundred zombies on screen with no problemo in my pc, which is I5 966K and GTX 1660 Super OC. I was able to play at 50-70 ms pings online. Not many people are online though. Nevertheless, you may find some people with some patience :)Overall, very good game for its price. You might get bored after around 30 hours or so. But this game doesn't promise huge load of content. This game promises zombies and slaughter and strategy. You can also find serious challange here. I would give it 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE Jan 2023 - Horde Mode XL upgrade:This used to be one of my favorite games. Then they released the Horde XL upgrade and messed up everything. More DLCs with weapon skins, but no new levels. They completely changed the weapon upgrade system from ground up ---3 years after the initial release!--- and deliberately made you lose all of your weapon progress and perks (I had everything maxed out). If I want to max out everything again, I'll have to grind weapon XP and documents all over again. Horde Mode XL is underwhelming before wave 10 or so, but then it starts getting interesting. As for the rest of the game, campaign seems easier in all difficulties since the last few patches, which sucks, because that was pretty much all the game had to offer: the challenge of higher difficulties. The game used to be fun. But if you completely change fundamental things like the weapon system several years down the road and make people lose progress with even not-so-major updates, I can't recommend playing this game in the long term anymore.OG REVIEW Dec 2021 - WWZ Aftermath:This is probably my favorite zombie shooter! (616 hours on Epic)Before WWZ, I played over 300 hours of L4D2. And as much as I like L4D2, I must say that I like WWZ better.When I first came from L4D2 to WWZ, I actually hated WWZ. I was used to the first-person view and the third-person view felt clunky and really hard to aim.But I gave WWZ a chance. Once I got used to the controls and third-person view, the game became real fun.I play mostly co-op campaign, online with randoms, or with friends.In L4D2 all characters have the same skill set, and the only challenge you face is increasing the difficulty and unlocking achievements.On the contrary, in WWZ you can choose 1 of 8classes (gunslinger, hellraiser, slasher, fixer, medic, exterminator, dronemaster, vanguard), each of which has different abilities. When you progress through the game, you level up your class and unlock new skills (perks), and you can also level up your weapons to improve them and unlock more powerful versions of those weapons. In addition, you can choose 1 of 5 levels of difficulty, and you can unlock special weapons if you prestige your classes or finish all missions in the highest difficulty ("extreme").All of this makes the co-op campaign extremely replayable.On top of all this, the game has a pretty decent PvP mode, and the horde mode is quite nice every now and then for some mindless grinding.If you like zombie shooters, give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a fun game. As expected, it is only loosely World War Z (there's a bunch of zombies around the world), but it does follow different characters in different areas with different goals so it does somewhat capture the spirit of the book.  + Difficulty scaling seems to be pretty good, so easy is actually easy and you can choose harder if you want+ Weapon upgrading is a fun mechanic + Class skills are enjoyable to choose, though some are obviously better than others+ Mutators to change things up (though most of these are about making the game harder, it could do with more directly beneficial ones and/or amusing mutators)+ Maps look excellent? The game really likes swarms suddenly running in as you wander about. L4D2 did more of a 'there are a bunch of zombies already waiting in the level', while this has that, most of the enemies you face while walking around are ones which rush in.? The game really likes areas where you have to defend against large swarms. There's at least 2 every mission. Place some defenses, try to defend a specific place which is for some reason attracting zombies (sometimes this makes sense due to a large noise, sometimes you're left questioning as to why hundreds of zombies are rushing this area). This isn't bad, but it does feel overdone. L4D2 did this more often just at the very end of a level.- The game appeared to give some upgraded versions of weapons at the start? I don't know if this is DLC or just things they've added after the game has been out for a time, but they tend to be better than the default ones for that level. This makes so you basically skip a couple levels of a weapon, which is weird.- There's no (notable) modding or custom maps, and you can get through all the maps in ~12 hours (probably shorter if you really try, or longer if you take your time on harder difficulties).- It feels too easy to get most of the weapons? - There's 'blue coins' for accessories which you get from completing challenges, but with how few you get via just playing the game rather than focusing on challenges, you probably won't get any accessories for the characters without essentially playing through the game repeatedly. As well, since the missions have a different set of four characters each time (except for the Japan and last Russia mission, though I don't know if they get the same accessories since they're treated as different characters elsewhere) then you won't be having them a lot of the time.The game is fun, but I'm not certain I'd suggest paying the current $40 for it. It has some issues in polish (though the maps are beautiful, I'm referring to gameplay) and notable issues in how much replayability there is or will be.

_childDocuments_.review: So far been enjoying this a decent bit, a fair amount more than some other recent  jab attempts at the L4D formula  I'd say, such as B4B's beta and Aliens Fireteam Elite.It has some annoying elements such as some special infected having odd balance decisions, like this game's charger can do almost full 180 turns during its charge instead of being committed to one direction and the newly introduced rat swarm is just not fun to deal with but they thankfully toned down the swarm's HP with a recent patch, used to be impossible to kill them even on the 3rd difficulty (Hard) if you didn't have explosive or fire weapons on you.Visually the game looks pretty solid, especially considering the fact it can fit what genuinely seems like thousands of zeds on screen at the same time yet it still keeps running incredibly well during those moments.My average FPS i get is like 100 fps on Ultra setting in 1080p on my Ryzen 3700x and RX 580 8GB which is amazing to see with how many enemies there are and the pretty cool human pyramid physics the zeds get when they start climbing over each other to reach you. However some odd and rare hitching/stuttering can occur but it's rather rare, seems to mostly happen at the start of booting the game up and getting into the first mission.Player base seems somewhat small on Steam currently but the game support cross platform play with Xbox and Playstation so even if player count is somewhat low, there's still the other platforms to play with.The game has a ranking,prestige,perk and progression system, so levels do matter when you wanna do higher difficulties for sure, don't expect to do the 4th or 5th difficulty (highest difficulty) on characters that are super low level. So it's not fully like left 4 dead where it mainly boils down to your and your team's skill, instead XP,perks and weapon attachment will play a factor however it still retains the left 4 dead system of finding guns as you go through out the level. You cannot for an example start out with the most powerful gear from the get go, instead they're split down to multiple tiers,  tier 1 is the starter  loadout gear and then the next tiers are guns you'll find as you go or sometimes be able to start with if a class you're playing as has a perk that allows it to start from the beginning with maybe a tier 2 gun but most of the better things you'll have to find in the levels as you progress.Most complaints you'll see currently are some Aussie folk upset over no official Oceanic servers, granted you can still do P2P to avoid having to use NA/EU official servers when you just wanna play with your other fellow c*nts in down under land. And the other complains are mostly some B4B fanboys copping over the fact their game is not turning out to be a true successor to l4d so now they're going around to other l4d-like/clones games and spamming them with negative reviews and the last group are some tards who don't understand what an expansion is and spent 0 minutes researching Aftermath, so they believed in their heads this was World War Z 2 and not just an Expansion so now they think they got "scammed" but it's just their own stupidity screwing them over.So far i have beaten all the 7 campaigns on Hard, have ventured a bit into Insane difficulty, done some horde mode, fooled around with some mutators you can turn on and did two weekly challengesand have enjoyed it all quite a bit, however it can get frustrating when you often get stuck with bad rando' team mates who seem to often ignore objectives or fail to realize it's time to move , so if you got buddies it's gonna be more enjoyable, sadly i only ever get a chance to play with 1 friend at most, meaning it's either bots or randos who can be bad or good filling the other spaces. Bots have the plus of following your lead almost perfectly and making stealth parts where you can avoid alerting hordes much easier but since they can't use equipment, carry objectives around or use their perks they're often far worse in the swarm holdout parts of a mission.So yeah, i for sure recommend giving this a go if you love 4 player l4d-like co-op games, this is definitely one that does that formula really well.
