_childDocuments_.review: Edit 11/8/2024 - I've been getting less Lost Connections, thanks Sabre. This review will remain unedited though - Too lazy.- Blood. Gore. Violence. Zombies. A horde shooter that literally throws a horde into you to the point where you feel like you're fighting like a hundred enemies on the screen. This is a good game for those who enjoy horde shooters like Left 4 Dead 2, Killing Floor 2, Warhammer: Vermintide 1/2, and this new game that came out called Space Marine 2 definitely made by a different developer.- The cinematic experience of what the movie is probably most-known for can be seen here, which is the zombies stacking on one another forming this tower of human beings to climb to areas, and you have the power to destroy the Horde Stacks.- It is especially satisfying to see enemy ragdolls fly everywhere courtesy of a nearby explosion.- The special infected are a good addition to spice things up a bit so you're not just mindlessly killing the strangely strategic zekes.- I've found another decent Left 4 Dead 2-esque game which is a win in my book.- Weapon variety is satisfactory; even with a bunch of weapons locked because I didn't get the Aftermath, there's still plenty to choose from. Assault Rifles, Sub-machineguns, Shotguns, Rifles, Handguns, even Missile Launchers and Flamethrowers are here.- Class variety is satisfactory as well, every class has it's own strength and weakness, and you're still free to customize the way you play that class via changing your class' perks; also, you're free to bring whatever class you want to bring without party restrictions - Your team can have 4 Medics or 4 Slashers!- Heroes (idfk what they're called) are set for where the game takes place, but you're free to bring your rootin' tootin' 'Murica man to Japan or Russia to chill with the other Japan or Russia Heroes - at the cost of possibly missing out on Japan or Russia Hero banter which is definitely understandable.- The grind is not that bad, I say. It's comfortable to start an unlevelled class on Normal difficulty if you've got the game's common knowledge sorted out (Healing, Defense Events, Abilities, etc). I've been playing for, like, 4 hours and I already have a Level 17 Medic and a Level 4 Fireman (the molotov-throwing person).- That being said, there is a separate grind for both Classes and Weapons. Class experience you get by completing missions, Weapon experience you get by using that weapon more and more. The pain peko is that you're using a single currency for both buying Perks and buying Weapon Levels.- There is no tutorial or prologue whatsoever, so you're just immediately dropped into the main menu for yourself to navigate to your first mission, where you're just immediately dropped into the game for you to figure out.- There is that small tooltip box on the top-right from time to time, but you can't really look at it and read what's on it when you're, I dunno, fighting some entire city's population during a Defense Event?- There is a Weapons Section in the customization interface, but the game doesn't tell you that you can only change your melee weapon. The Primary and Secondary weapons that you find can only be attainable randomly in the middle of the match, or when assigned to your starter kit.- The Weapon Leveling system may force players to go down on the difficulty scale for when they're using weapons they've never used; Since underlevelled weapons will, expectedly, underperform on higher difficulties.- The perks section doesn't really say that you can only equip one perk for every column and you don't have to buy every perk every time your level goes up. Which means people may tend to spend on perks that are not really their playstyle, or perks that deem incredibly situational or otherwise useless.- Most of the Special Infected have confusing health values even if you're shooting them in what I assume their weak spots (a Bull eating an entire magazine even if I'm hitting its' back, a Lurker instantly dying when I shoot it in the foot, an Infector taking 8 shells and still in its' Fight For Your Life phase, is this lag?), which can lead to unfairly-taken damage.- Sometimes the explosive Heavy Weapons tend to just bug out (for me), like a Horde Stack getting a direct hit from an RPG Shell did little effect. There is definitely a high chance that it might just be skill issue.- A Booster can buff standard enemies around them to the point where the standard enemies can pin you down which is a bit dumb. Why couldn't it just have buffed their attack or defense or even both? Why is this standard zombie suddenly capable of pinning down?- A Bomber will run up to you and has a timer before it ultimately explodes, or it will instantly explode if shot or hit with a melee attack. I just wish we had a way to push them away if they're close enough to give breathing room or to knock them down even.- Screamers can spawn from the weirdest of places. Sometimes they're in plain sight for the party's sniper to pick them off easily, other times they're behind enemy spawns or beyond gate objectives so you're just stuck there dealing with horde after horde after horde.- There is no omega supreme digital deluxe edition legendary bossman zombie enemy as far as I know, which is a bit sad. Something like a towering 2-storey enemy to invoke upon players several issues.- For SOME reason, the Peer-to-Peer game hosting isn't the default server-hosting in this game and it relies on Dedicated Servers that you need to pray to whatever gods you need that you'll get lucky and the game will actually start instead of hanging onto "Starting Game" for an entire minute before cutting off your server's life support and giving you that "Lost Connection" while you're still connected to the services. You're not even getting disconnected mid-game, you're getting disconnected PRE-GAME. (From what I can gather uninterestedly, the latest update might have botched the servers or something which is why they're being so cursed)- I've literally had a smooth(ish, thanks randoms) first 2 hours of gameplay only to be ruined by the next few hours waiting to win the Server Roulette. Conspiracy: It's rigged.- If all else fails, you can just have a few of your friends play on a Private Server's exclusive feature, the P2P connection. Or you can host your own game and suffer by playing with bots.- Speaking of the bots, their aim and their ability to use their ability are the only things that are good. Their navigation, their lack of care for Defense Items, and their lack of care for Objectives make some missions unnecessarily long or harder. They feel like unmodded PAYDAY2 bots whose weapons and classes you cannot change.- The AI also never use any of the Heavy Weapons which makes solo Defenses more hectic.- The AI seem to be level 1, but I THINK they at least have non-default perks equipped. Wish we could use our other levelled classes to fill in the ranks instead.- Sometimes when you're pinned by an enemy, they will ssssssslowly walk towards you NOT aiming at you until they practically have their ass on the enemy, to then which they'll turn around and shoot it.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game after the overwhelming elements of Back 4 Blood. This is more simple (in a good way) more comparable to Left 4 Dead series.Gameplay: 7.3/10The gameplay is nothing new, but it is enjoyable. With friends or randoms. The gun play is my favorite part of the gameplay. Guns handle great and the effect the gameplay too, for instance a using a suppressed weapon actually allows you to pick of zombies that haven't noticed you yet and shooting loud will alert nearby zombies of your position. Killing zombies is very satisfying, tearing through zombies with an AR, pistol is good fun and each weapon has a respectable amount of recoil that is not too intrusive. Shotguns though I think could use a little more visible kick, it shows barely any kick when firing.Characters: 5.5/10Each campaign choice has its own unique characters, each one has a video introducing them and who they were before the zombies came. It's average at best, the characters are pretty forgettable as we don't get to spend a lot of time with them as we would in the L4D series. They are not annoying either, when their dialogue is used it feels fair and not overdone in situations.Progression: 7/10The game has numerous class systems from Medic, to gunslinger. With each class offering lots of progression. I enjoy leveling up one class then moving to the next and so on... You can also prestige classes too. Each class has its own perks which each benefiting the team in different ways. I only play PvE so I cannot comment on the state of PvP but I do know they have their own class systems different to PvE.Graphics: 6.5/10The graphics are okay, nothing special and definately something you have seen before. I have nothing to complain about here, it looks like your average mid-gen PS4 game. Animations are pretty good though, very fluid in motion, only ever looks weird when performing the climb animation as it is always the same.Sound: 6/10Again, like graphics, sound is nothing special. The music is forgettable but at least it is not bad. There are sometimes sound ques to approaching hoards but the sound design is not as good as Left 4 Dead 2.Performance: 8/10The performance is great overall for this game. moving around the environment, big explosions, large hordes AND explosions, I have not seen drastic frame drops. I am always getting above 80fps and the lowest will hit early 70s. Performance paired with the slick animations makes the game run and look great almost all the time.Microtransactions: The game offers a few weapon camo/specialty packs to buy but these don't affect anything. All skins and weapon varients (except to few MTX ones) can be earned through gameplay. In fact, all the DLC campaign additions are free. Verdict: 7.4/10This game is worth a buy if you are looking for a game similar to Left 4 Dead series. After trying Back 4 Blood I felt overwhelmed by the tedious card system they introduced, the weapon rarity levels and MTX. I will be playing this game for a while, getting everything unlocked and trying new weapons/classes. I would buy this game full price as I feel it is worth it, but if you can get it on sale you are getting a lot of content at a steal price.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10The year is 2015 and life around the world apparently goes on as normal, people wake up and go to work or study, sometimes travel between countries, among many other things, but no one realizes that without wanting to, a worker in an Asian country accidentally contaminating himself with a type of virus hitherto unknown to humanity, which has a clinical condition that is noting pleasant, invading the victim's nervous system and once it reaches the victim's brain, making it incapable of thinking and extremely aggressive, especially against other people, but nobody detected it. ^^In this way, allowing patient zero of this new disease to return to his home and silently begin transmitting to one, who will transmit to others, who will go to more people and thus spreading around the world, sometimes giving signs of danger, such as sporadic outbreaks cases in several countries of "Rabies" due to its symptoms or people being attacked "for no reason", until the day one year later that the world finally identified that it was a new virus called Solanum, and humanity realized that there is no cure for the already taken by the virus and the only option is to eliminate those infected before they make more victims, but it is very difficult to do that, when they are millions all over the world, attacking anyone they find in real hordes. ^^+ A good zombie game to play either alone with AI-controlled teammates who are capable of defending themselves and the player, and with friends even without having a full team of four.+ A good range of weapons, ranging from fully automatic to semi-automatic, including more exotic ones like ballistae with explosive shells and chainsaws. Along with most of the weapons, we have a system of levels, where we gain experience by eliminating enemies with the weapons and at each level we can buy improvements.+ Interesting stories, with each chapter showing a small story of a group of survivors in a different city in the world, finding their way to survive or helping to eliminate the infected.+ Good work of creation for each city that we have in the game, from the architecture of the buildings, to the arts of the posters in the languages of the country where the story takes place.+ Several and the most diverse references to the World War Z book, either in the form of documents, speeches of the characters or during its introduction videos. Including things that were changed in the movie, but here they were faithful to the book.+ Each story has four character options to choose from, and eight class options, each class with its passive perks, some of which are quite useful.- While the AI is capable of defending itself against the Infected, it also does strange things, such as sometimes not shooting the Infected due to not looking the right way, as well as never picking up healing items or interacting with objectives.- Some special zombies are very annoying because if they are not eliminated soon, like one that, if not killed, can summon more zombies forever, in addition to the fact that at the time of chaos it is easily undetected.- It has a good number of chapters in different cities but, I wouldn't complain a bit, with the release of more chapters in new cities, mainly due to some continents and regions not having a single city among them represented, like South America, Africa, Oceania and Islamic Middle East.- The cities are well represented, from the architecture to the texts, but the attention given to the text was not given to the dubbing, with Japanese, Russian, Italian characters, among many others, always speaking only in English and never in their native language.- The weapons system has a strange thing, because the weapons gain levels as we kill infected with them, but we can only continue evolving after buying an improvement. For example, I take a rifle from level one to two, I will only be able to go from two to three, after buying the level two improvement, and so on for all weapons.- Each chapter has several documents that enrich the player's experience by informing us more about this world, but the vast majority of these need to be collected specifically in challenge mode only, to read them all it is necessary to collect nine files in each part of a total of twenty-three, which is twenty-three times nine, giving a total of two hundred and seven files that have to be collected to unlock all game documents.And so begins the mission of our players, either in groups or playing alongside characters controlled by the AI, advancing through cities infested with people infected and taken over by the virus, while trying to survive or fulfill the mission objectives, some easier and others not so much at all, as I learned by playing each of the chapters. With the most varied types of objectives, connecting something, picking something up and taking it to that place, protecting that place, always objectives that the group needs to work together to survive. ^^Mainly depending on the difficulty level, as the game has five difficulty levels, and the higher not only do the infected have more life, but the group also starts to find less weapons, ammunition and healing items. All vital equipment to eliminate the infected, which not only are in much greater numbers, but are also sensitive to shots made without a silencer, but mainly to eight special types of infected, some that will attack as soon as they see the players, and others that are more stealthy, but all capable of causing damage to distracted players. ^^The graphic part I thought was well done despite having some caveats. As mentioned the setting part of the cities, including using the local language for posters and signs, the different characters for each country, the intro videos for most of the characters that have their own artistic style, but at the same time some things could be better like the special infected having different clothes according to the city. As for the sound, I thought it was well done, with songs that match the theme, especially when combined with the sounds of the infected and the weapons. ^^World War Z: Aftermath was an interesting case for me, I've already watched the movie a few times and I already knew in a summarized way the story of the book and that's why I knew that the two had differences, so I was very pleased to start exploring and seeing them have chosen to be more faithful to the book, just for that reason I would recommend the game, but I also recommend it because I found it a fun and interesting game for those who like zombie games or similar, I admit that some phases made me a little angry, but with patience to try again, you can overcome obstacles and have fun with the AI or other players, so I recommend it. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing World War Z since it first released on EGS a bit over two years ago and have probably racked up close to 100 hours of playtime, and with the two new campaigns included with the Aftermath expansion I'm looking forward to playing a lot more of this game. After being utterly disappointed with Back 4 Blood in nearly every regard, WWZ will continue to be the closest thing to a Left 4 Dead 3 (unless Valve ever wakes up). WWZ sticks to L4D's formula of keeping things simple and arcade-y, but expands on it just enough with a few modern ideas like classes, weapon leveling/upgrades, and cosmetics you can unlock by simply playing the weekly challenges. This is perfect, imo. It doesn't go too far with trying to modernize things. That's something that most of these L4D clone developers don't understand, they try to do too much and it ruins it. L4D1 and 2 were such great games because they were pick-up-and-play, but had just enough depth to keep replayability very high. You won't be fiddling with cards and weapon attachments in the middle of a level, trying to compare stats while zombies are chasing you like in Back 4 Blood. Levels and objectives randomize enough to feel different on multiple playthroughs, something that Aliens: Fireteam Elite failed with. There is no randomized loot, no weapon rarities, and difficulty scales up in a sensible way that doesn't feel broken like in Vermintide. Weapons feel punchy and satisfying, something both Back 4 Blood and Earthfall did terribly.There isn't too much that stands out to me as very poorly done with WWZ. There's bugs here and there, currently the new rat swarm enemies are a bit OP (but the devs have already tweeted that they'll be tweaking them with an update later this week), and the new first person view is a bit meh (it feels like the camera is on some sort of swivel when looking up/down, and weapons are very close to the screen). Nothing game-breaking, nothing that ruins my time with the game.The developers are pretty cool, over the last two years they've done a ton of free updates. I can't think of many games that were still getting updates and DLCs two years post-launch. They've already confirmed there's more to come. Next month we're getting a new special infected type, and in 2022 we're getting an expanded version of the Horde mode, all for free.Anyway, highly recommend checking this out if you're a fan of Left 4 Dead, zombie games, or just co-op games in general. I'd only say to wait on a sale if you're planning on playing solo with bots. You can find matches with randoms near-instantly, though there are a few griefers out there trying their best to ruin things for others on higher difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of zombie games, where I've played Left 4 Dead 1 and 2 with friends in computer shops, Dead Island on both console and PC, Dying Light, Resident Evil, the list goes on. So when WWZ came along, it was a welcome game to play on coop, especially when the pandemic came soon after.Now, I loved the movie, the book, and the game when it came out in 2019, it was awesome. But the recent changes have been so disappointing. It feels like the devs are not even trying, or they had an intern craft up the new weapon progression system. Now, I didn't have difficulty wrapping my head around the changes, but the changes were not carefully planned out.The cosmetic skins of the weapons, that's fine, I don't have much issue with it as the stats and perks of your choice are added to the weapon. What really bothered me was how grindy the whole process was going to be in leveling each weapon, because obviously enough, you can play favorites, but how often does your favorite gun come out? You now have to grind out 15 levels or so for the weapons, which is very tedious and time consuming.The perks are hit or miss, some are really good, and some just plain suck. But the kicker here is that they tied a portion of the perks to the silly document hunting system they introduced some time in 2022 or earlier. Imagine having to play the same level 9 times, along with mutators that might or might not be in your favor. I did this for the "Advanced Combat Weapon" before the update, and while we did achieve a stage with all 9 documents, the achievement was short-lived, because the devs locked the most important part of the perk weapon to collecting every document for an entire episode. Sorry, but not all of us want to search every nook and cranny in a level to find 1 document, and repeat the entire thing again hoping that you'll complete the stage without incident.Looking at the horde XL update, it isn't that big an achievement in all honesty. First off, it's mandatory to own the aftermath DLC to access horde XL - but before the update, you could actually invite friends that only had the base game, from different platforms to join you in the aftermath DLC stages. That was really good, but it does not apply to horde XL. Speaking of these changes, they have yet to address the framerate issues, the lag and freezing on devices that aren't next gen, like the PS5 and what have you. This actually occurs when you're just playing the normal story stages, which totally ruins the gameplay for all of us, especially where the game continues to run and your character just dies by the time the lag or the framerate goes back to normal.The devs could have added more stages (seriously it's called WORLD War Z for a reason) yet we're stuck with New York, Jerusalem, Moscow, Tokyo, Marseille, Rome, and Kamchatka. I'll throw in South Korea because they made it clear that the normal horde mode takes place there. But no other countries have been added yet? After the game has been out this long?And they still haven't added the 3rd row skills for our classes. It's rather obvious that with the space left for it, there should have been a 3rd row of new skills, but the devs have not sorted that out yet.So would I recommend this game to anyone else? No, I'd wait until the devs have sorted out the performance issues of the game at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games you play and wonder how you never heard off. If you're looking for more left 4 dead your not going to do better than this. It's defiantly not as polished but you may find it more fun.  The only games in this category that do it "better" are L4D 2 and vermitide 2. And they could both learn some things from this game.What this game does better:Hordes, if you're favorite part of the l4d series was hordes you'll love this game. This games throws hordes at you that are larger than entire L4d campaigns. You get to set up defenses to fortify yourself and since the weapons in this game are powerful (the starting pistol is more powerful than the assault rifles in l4D) you get the a satisfaction of making a visible dent in the horde.Teamwork, this game encourages you to stay together without the heavy handed tactic of having a special murder you because you were more than five feet away from your team or lost line of sight for 2 seconds. Heck sometimes you're encouraged to explore on your own or strategically split up.World building, the world actually feels alive and dynamics in this game. I'd say this probably due to the use of NPC's having other humans you're interacting with makes it feel like a Zombie apocalypse rather than a zombie post-apocalypse  Progression. This game hits the right balance of progression, where I feel like I could beat any of the levels with a brand new charterer but the the new abilities unlocked are noticeable.difficulty ramp, I've only done the first 4 difficulties but so far it right, both L4D and vermitied suffer from the difficulty jumping from cake walk to RNG-nightmareledges, the are no insta-death ledges that you or bots can accidentally walk off of or randomly be thrown off of.Less BS, losses in this game tend to be not so frustrating, so far both specials and death usually feel like my mistake and not the game deciding the randomly up the difficulty be 3 levels. Melee, it's a viable offensive option, and if you're the melee class you can clear large portions of levels with it. There is only one melee button, and panic smashing it works in many situations, but learning to time and aim strikes makes it much more effective. It's defiantly better than L4D 2, and personally as someone who's played to hardest levels of vermintide 2 and got good at it's melee system I find the melee in this game more fun and rewording. What it does mehBots, they used to play like a party of players doing a bad job of pretending they don't secretly hate you. They have been greatly upgraded, while they are still stupid and will still switch from their shotgun to their pistol while a creeper has you pinned and is beating you to death, they no longer jump in front of your shots to protect zombies. Most of the upgrade have been mechanical, they can pick up items, use special abilities, free them selves from pins ect... They are by no means good but they are good enough to not hamper you on solo runs and are actually better than many of randos out there.What it does worse.Bosses, there are none, while this is better than too many the occasional equivalent of a tank or rat ogre would add to the game. The closet thing is the Juggernaut which sounds exactly like another special, when it charges it's hit you despite you being 2 feet away, it's week spots are it arms and legs but this isn't communicated in any way, and they can show up seconds apart.VS multiplayer, seems like something they were forced to add on. It's all human with human, with npcs zombies that will overrun aeras. It's kinda a fun, it's got some interesting ideas that it doesn't do much with, but there are much better competitive FPS game out there. Also this mode is kinds dead.Polish, it definitely more polished than B4B but not as polished as L4D2, I'd put it around vermitide 2022 levels.What else it does well.Support, this games is continuing to get updates and new content added, there are weekly challenges that so far are interesting and dailies if you enjoy grinding.Weapon variety, it has a wide variety of weapons that play differently, though it doesn't do a good job surfacing that.Carrying, as the member of my group who plays this the most, I found it's easy to tailor my builds in a way that helps my teammate get through what would be difficult and potentially frustrating sections.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:It has weapon upgrades and customization. You can level up your weapon and put skin and perks on it.+ There is a character classes, such as Medic class that excel in healing, Gunslinger that excel at reloading and weapon damage, Hellraiser that specialized in explosives, or a Slasher that excel in melee weapons, etc. You can select perks and play as you wish.+ The number of zombies is really large, which is both challenging and satisfying.+ Various random daily challengesCONS:- It has a random matchmaking system, and sometimes it will take so long to find players to play with us. And honestly, it's better to have a lobby system with a room list where you can search, create, lock, and join the rooms.- This game's save data is saved locally, so people can have 100% game progression by changing their save data. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I'm about 4 to 5 hours into the gameplay, and so far it's been a good time. I got the game on sale, for roughly $25, and I cannot complain about that at all. This game is touted as the "complete edition" of World War Z because it comes with a new first-person mode, revamped melee system, a new class, and 3 or 4 new campaign maps. Really, it's a good package especially for the price.Here's a quick summary of my experience with World War Z so far.PROS+ The inclusion of the new first-person mode is what a lot of players really wanted. Though I still prefer the third-person, I can see how it's appealing to the original players of the game.+ The Swarm Engine is fantastic at handling the insane amount of Z bodies on the screen during hordes. Their attention to detail is great, and it doesn't seem to suffer slowdowns as you would expect.+ The shooting is tight and arcade-y. It's not a serious shooter with realistic mechanics, it's meant to be fun, and every weapon packs a serious punch.+ The classes are fun and varied. I'm running an Exterminator class right now, arguably my favorite class because of shotguns and pure crowd control power. There are something like 8 others to choose from, though, with a lot of unique and cool abilities.+ The graphics are great. The game even has Vulkan rendering instead of DX11 which just feels  much smoother.+ Built-in AMD FSR support is amazing, too. Due to the ongoing Great GPU Shortage of 2020+ I'm still using my RX 580 8GB and man does FSR really help keep things going.+ Cross-platform play is great. It features the ability for Xbox and PS4 players to play with you on PC and does a seamless job doing so.+ Character customization is great. Many characters have some pretty slick threads to put on.+ Gun customization is great, too. You can amp up your weapons with things like suppressors or different attachments for different missions.+ TBC...CONS- No mod support. Big-time game devs don't often do that, so it's not a huge point of contention or anything, but it'd be cool if community-made maps were a part of every game to help keep them alive and thriving just a bit longer than usual.- The AI, at least on the creeper class, is a bit typical. That particular Z will always alert you to his presence way ahead of time and you'll know within 2 seconds which corner he'll be hiding behind. On harder difficulties it doesn't change.- The companion AI repeat a lot of lines, though again it's not a big point of contention or anything as it's easy to just keep going and tune it out. I heard the same voice line when I was loading mortars about 4 times in a 20 second span, though, which was a bit annoying.- Adding onto it, the companion AI are a bit slow to react to being caught by a creeper or bull. They help, but not til you've lost a little more HP than you'd have liked to.- TBC...Overall I really like this game. I've always been a fan of Z shooters and this is no exception. Not all were great, but this is a fun one. Now that Epic's exclusivity is over with on the original, this Aftermath edition has been a welcome addition to my Steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z is now finally on Steam after they cash cowed on Steam, got dried up and came to Steam because it's better but let's not sh*t on the company and how they treated Steam, we're here for the game.I've played a fair amount before it came to Steam, it was the only game I bought on the Trash EGS!Graphics: The graphics are decent and it's very well optimised. There is a nice amount of gore, explosions and special effects, it's all pretty to look at (Keep reading for the "thousands of zombies on screen") but graphically it's not amazing but still pretty nice.Audio: Zombies, guns, foot steps, screams, dashing, it's all here and some good audio queue's to listen too making it nice.Controls: Now fixed because originally the keybinds where tailored to WASD and now it's been fixed. Easy to pick-up and easy to follow.Game-play and everything else after: So let's the "thousands zombies" out the way. The trailer shows a lot of them running, BUT the devs do not state you can fight them, also these encounters of this many zombies are ONLY ever at key points like defending BUT and it's a huge BUT.. If you get 4 players, run away and let the "crowd" over run you.. They do not... It's STILL a handful and NEVER EVER thousands in-front of you to right.. You can even spot this at the beginning, when you see the hord, look closely.. Graphically it's like a video render, it's not the actual zombies, then when they attack the gate on the first level, back away and run to the back staying away and watch how the gate and only some climb over, it's about.. 100 or less, that's it. - This feature is a misleading gimmick which is sad.So the game is a 4 player co-op 3rd person shooter with a lot of the same, get to safe place, get items, repair that and that's it.We smashed the campaign very quickly. It's not a massive skill gap or even a long game time.Each part of the game you HAVE to defend, no matter what, it's the same thing through-out the campaigns, but the item drops will be random to a point, but again it's not a huge difference. It's pretty easy to smash the game with a team all sticking together.Yes, you can upgrade your character which is cool and makes for something to work too, but it never gives you feeling of being stronger.Online PvP is pretty much dead. It takes forever to get a match and if you can, someone quits and it's a one sided match, but PvP again is only fun for a small amount of time.There is a handful of campaigns to run through but they are short plays, nothing that you can drag hours upon hours out off, unless you keep upping the difficulty, but again it's the same stuff each time with no real difference... Unlike Back 4 Blood game.There are lots of annoying things like unable to scroll to change your mouse, you have to press a button.. Which is stupid.The First Person mode they've added to the game, is just not feeling right. You can tell the game is not designed for first person yet this was added because of the B4B incoming. Also when using first person, it's very sway like feeling and then when you melee, it goes instantly third person, so it's very strange and just does not work.If you are bored of the L4D series, then this is a decent step in a different direction for a different point of view.Would I recommend? Yes if it's on sale, full price not worth it. Back 4 Blood has a much more enjoyable replayability style game and a lot more going for it.. WWZ is kinda, yeah it's fun on a run, up the difficulty? Sure, but let's do one run.. That's it...

_childDocuments_.review: World War Z is an absolute blast, a heart-pounding thrill ride that captures the essence of zombie apocalypse chaos like no other game before it. From the moment you step into its beautifully rendered, globally spanning environments, you're thrust into a world teetering on the brink of collapse, where only your wits, your weapons, and your teammates stand between humanity and utter annihilation.The game's crowning achievement is undoubtedly its swarm technology. Never before have I witnessed such an awe-inspiring spectacle in a video game. The sheer number of zombies that can flood the screen at once is mind-boggling. Watching these undead hordes pour over walls, cascade down buildings, and form writhing pyramids of flesh to reach you is both terrifying and exhilarating. It's a technical marvel that truly brings the intensity of the World War Z universe to life.The cooperative gameplay is where this title truly shines. Teaming up with three other players to face the relentless onslaught creates moments of camaraderie and tension that are hard to match. Whether you're frantically rebuilding barricades, watching each other's backs as you're swarmed from all sides, or making a desperate last stand against seemingly impossible odds, the game fosters a sense of teamwork that's both rewarding and addictive.The variety of classes and weapons on offer adds a layer of strategy and replayability that keeps the experience fresh. Each class feels distinct and useful, allowing players to find a role that suits their playstyle. The gunplay is satisfying and impactful, with each weapon feeling appropriately weighty and powerful. There's something undeniably cathartic about mowing down waves of zombies with a well-placed machine gun burst or explosives.Visually, World War Z is a treat. The locations are diverse and atmospheric, ranging from the claustrophobic streets of New York to the eerie calm of Tokyo. The attention to detail in the environment storytelling is commendable, with each level feeling lived-in and authentic to its setting. The zombie designs are appropriately grotesque and varied, adding to the game's overall immersion.The sound design deserves special mention. The cacophony of snarls, screams, and gunfire creates a soundscape that perfectly captures the chaos of a zombie apocalypse. The music ramps up at just the right moments, heightening the tension and driving the action forward.One of the game's strongest points is its commitment to post-launch support. The developers have consistently released new content, including additional episodes, weapons, and game modes. This ongoing support has helped to keep the community engaged and the game feeling fresh long after its initial release.World War Z manages to capture the epic scale of its source material while crafting a unique gaming experience. It's a love letter to zombie enthusiasts and action gamers alike, offering an adrenaline-pumping adventure that's best enjoyed with friends. Whether you're a fan of the movie, the book, or just love mowing down hordes of the undead, World War Z delivers in spades. It's a game that understands what makes zombie fiction compelling and translates that into an interactive format with aplomb.In conclusion, World War Z is more than just a game; it's an experience. It's the closest many of us will ever come to living out our zombie survival fantasies, and it does so with style, intensity, and a whole lot of undead to slay. If you haven't yet had the pleasure of diving into this zombie-infested world, you're missing out on one of the most exciting cooperative shooters of recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: By all means, this isn't a bad game. That being said, this is not a phenomenal game either. Overall, it's very middling. It does some things right, some things mediocre, and some things outright bad. However, the game has garnered a healthy following and I can at least understand why. So let me start with what it does good:-The gunplay is fun, it's very satisfying to shoot most weapons and the feedback is pretty good-the zombie variety, weird thing to list but, it's nice when every zombie isn't a copy of 3 existing models-special zombie designs, I love L4D2 but one thing that was a nitpick of mine was that the special infected just existed, there was really no way to connect them to the infection and how they got that way, however, in WWZ, the zombie designs themselves tell you their lore, for example, it's very obvious the bomber is an infected demolitions expert or the screamer was a worker with a mic still connected, it's very grounded world design-the level variety, not gonna praise it too much but it's a nice change of scenery from fighting zombies in NY to Tokyo to Marseille-the progression feels fluid and like you're actually earning towards better equipment-classes actually add some variety to gameplay-replayability, the game is fairly replayable and you don't feel burnt out playing certain missions again, granted it's not l4d2 replayable, it's still decentand now the Bad:-the game is soulless, the game has absolutely no soul of it's own, while it does do some things right, it just doesn't try to distinguish itself from anything other zombie horder shooter-the characters are awful, they aren't fleshed out and having absolutely nothing interesting about them-the campaign stories are fairly lacking, granted they didn't need a whole lot of narrative to keep things rolling. the writing for some is just outright badLike I said, this isn't a bad game but it isn't a great one either. It's fun but it's not groundbreaking and it's certainly no "left 4 dead killer". A lot of people have been attempting to compare this with the upcoming title Back 4 Blood but let me give a bit of impartial advice, dont compare them, they aren't the same and they aren't comparable. I'll probably get both at the end of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've reviewed a game, so I am going to keep this short and sweet....Pros: Zombies, third-person shooter, simplistic yet challenging, intense horde mechanics, and excellent for those who prefer online play. Cons: Lackluster level progression schemes, on rails, no real customization away from pre-rendered skins, and is most certainly, "Better with friends."My biggest gripe with the game is going to be that they didn't flesh out the levels, but instead created a series of extremely condensed environments where the only time spent there is extended through contrived, "search, activate, fight the horde," loops. I spend most of my time in-game attempting to locate keys and switches in low-light environments, all the while I'm waiting for the next horde to inevitably show up and make my nearly-blind search that much more of a chore. This game is definitely worth it on a sale, it's splendid for what it tried to be, but the contrived game play loop in every condensed section of every map is really killing it for me.

The special Infected semi-mirror Left 4 Dead and they require "teamwork" which wouldn't be a problem except the friendly AI are as useless as porn to a eununch.  They can fire their gun.  Not accurately either (try the Crossbow Fiesta mutator and see how bad they really are).  And that's pretty much all they can do as of the time of this review. _childDocuments_.review: It feels like a confused, soulless version of L4D. There isn't much polish or redeeming qualities in it, and coming from developers that mostly did car/silly games up to this point, it isn't surprising. Click  to see my other Reviews or follow my  for more recommendations.The choice of gameplay for this game is a bit confusing. Melee attacks are designed as something fast-paced, as you can't equip the weapons (like in L4D), but rather you melee attack with a shortcut. Yet, all other actions in the game, like pressing a button, or picking up stuff, ALL take an arbitrary amount of time to do, which implies a slow-paced design.The game is meant to be a co-op experience. That's what it is designed around. Yet the AI is a nightmare. They're entirely useless, don't pick up items, don't correctly swap weapons and come in melee range to get a special infected off your face, instead of shooting it as soon as possible. If you get downed while playing with bots, the game ends instead of letting the bots pick you up. Removing the bots also doesn't make the game any easier. They could've at least lowered spawn-rates. The next worst thing are the players. A lot of them just downloaded maxed out save files and don't know how to actually play the game, and you can't even kick them out of your own lobby. But hey, they let you kick out your own friends that you just invited.I was thrown off by the fact that there is no jumping - or even a dodge button for that matter. So, when facing bombers or spitters that crept up to you, there's no other way around them, even if your reflexes are great. You rely on the game's vault system to get over some obstacles, which often just screws you over as it doesn't register that well. Map accessibility is made limited by the cliche "crate in the stairs" or other silly methods that could easily be jumped over, swam across, climbed on, walked to et cetera.Movement isn't the only weak aspect of this game, however, as gunplay is.. not fun. Shotguns feel more like rifles, molotovs/explosives can only kill a limited amount of zombies per explosion/fire. Why? The core mechanic of the game is tearing up hordes of walking cadavers, yet you lock this potential fun behind a frag that blows up 5 of them. This also makes a lot of the heavy weapons feel like peashooters. It's sad. In the end, your best bet is just using the Slasher class, as it dispatches through a ton of enemies effortlessly by spamming your melee (regardless of the stamina bar).The item placement is also tricky. It relies on some sort of RNG, but since it's pure RNG, you may end up with a ton of equipment charges or defensive kits in areas where you don't need them, only to then run dry where it's most crucial. Speaking of defenses, you may only place them in predetermined locations, which isn't too horrible for stuff like fences, but sucks for turrets. Said turrets also have a horrible range of motion, meaning in some cases you're just a few pixels away from being able to shoot the rest of the horde. Mortars are super delayed, so it relies on you timing your shot beforehand to actually hit something. This is often pointless because hordes are inconsistent, and chances of you timing it right are very low.Loading screens are long, there's no suicide button when you're downed, XP for guns only counts for that specific level. Meaning if you go over the 100XP for a level, the gun won't continue leveling until you buy the next upgrade for it. The atmosphere and zombie layouts aren't great, animations are pretty bad, especially in some cutscenes. There were random disconnects which meant I would get no rewards for completing levels. Finishing levels with modifiers doesn't count towards completion, and this isn't pointed out anywhere. While playing online both my partner and I had issues with invisible zombies that would almost instakill you, and mission objectives like "defend X/Y", for which the timers were broken. We'd either clear all the zombies and it would still fail the mission, or we'd kill a few of them and we'd be in the green immediately.Every time I played this game, it would ruin my night. Finishing it on the highest difficulty was a nightmare and was not one bit fun or challenging. Just unfair. Where did Epic's money go towards? Definitely not the improvement of this game. I don't understand how people can worship WWZ and praise it, when it's mechanically worse than a game that released a decade ago.

_childDocuments_.review: + It's a perfectly serviceable coop zombie game. It plays well and is optimized well. There are flaws and shortcomings but overall it's fun, which is the most important measure of most games IMO+ / - While there's lots of missions to play through featuring characters from across the globe, there's also lots of overlap in mechanics and mission design. They all have almost the same exact pacing from start to finish+ / - The ability to level and customize classes adds some variety and replayability, but most of the traits and equipment one unlocks doesn't feel terribly effective, and collectively doesn't make any one class seem all that different from another or crucial in any given circumstance. Some of the unique class equipment is actually so poorly thought out that trying to figure out how to effectively use it can lead to swift death. Some of the class trees seem incoherent as well, with late-stage upgrades/unlocks going against the overall design of the class given previous unlocks - and not in a way that allows for more specialized builds. It's just all over the place- The AI for team mates is terrible. They won't go for objectives, they rarely use their equipment, they won't heal themselves or others. The game is a really poor experience if one tries to solo it+ Crossplay seems to be implemented well and the community, while seemingly not large, isn't toxic like with some other games in this genre

Here's the steps:1. Open Steam: Launch the Steam application on your Steam Deck. 2. Go to Library: Navigate to your game library. 3. Select the Game: Right-click on the game you want to validate. 4. Open Properties: From the context menu, select "Properties." 5. Local Files Tab: In the Properties window, go to the "Local Files" tab. 6. Verify Integrity: Click on the "Verify Integrity of Game Files" button and let the process completeRestart Steam Deck and should work perfectly!.

I also have a major gripe about this game which got me off the game after my very first Prestige. The game really shine when I could stay in one place and actually  ( most satisfyingly in the first encounter of Jerusalem's second act, "Dead sea stroll" ). However, the game is obviously pushing for the run-and-gun dynamic which work very poorly with the current integration of the enemy system:- Sometimes I and my mates just get jumped out of nowhere, wherever and whenever. - There are many objectives that demand us to do fetch quests and kill scattered enemies around the map and their intended behaviors to work in hordes shows very blatantly when they're alone. Bad animations.. LODs popping everywhere.. It's just a very excruciating and unfun experience.And even the horde mode update that was supposed to scratch that horde shooting itch didn't do it too well. Enemies usually spawn horizontally to our rally and come up at very randomly small numbers in bursts. I and my squadmates usually have to fight eachother to have fun and sometimes end up TKing as we try to get some kills on our feed. The NYC mall and sewer segment as well as Jerusalem's dam encounter in Dead Sea Stroll did it so well while maintaining a great level of challenge for a team of 4, yet no other encounter other than those 3 offers the same fantastic experiences.

When you perform a headshot,the hitmarker is red,indicating instant death for the zombie in your crosshair. The game reacts well to you shooting a zombie.You also can find different weapons as you progress.REPLAYABILITYThe game has tons of replayability,because there are a lot of perks you can unlock and also different types of guns.You can also customise your character,which is also cool.Even though there are only 7 episodes,they have different chapters,and even if you finish them,you can increase the difficulty of the game and get more rewards at the end.SINGLEPLAYERAlthough this game does not have a dedicated singleplayer mode,you can still play with the bots.The bots are not entirely stupid,but i would give them a stupidity rating of 4/10.I have heard about some people having problems with ping,but i myself play on my own only,so i have no problems.However if you have friends to play with who can also buy the game along with you,i highly recommend it.you can also go fully solo without bots,which is extra challenging.I play on my own because i am the alpha male and i do not need anyone else's help.PERFORMANCEI play this on my gaming laptop with a rtx3050ti , and on ultra , i get very good performance, getting around 90-100 fps.If you have a rtx 20 or 30 series card,u can definitely play this on 1440p or even 4k,Even with large hordes,I have not seen any large fps drops,so a great thank you to the devs for optimising the game so well.SHOULD YOU BUY IT?well,it depends on you.I have heard of some people buying this because it is on steam,but i am a new player,so i anyway bought it.If you are new to this game,i definitely recommend it over back 4 blood,and it is also way cheaper.Everything feels good about this game.hence,gigachad recommends this game,and yes.you should buy it.This is an order.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty decent zombie game that offers plenty of challenge on the harder difficulties. The levels have a lot of different objectives to do but most are defending some helpless survivors against an insane amount of zombies. The locations in the levels are really cool by themselves too. Some of the classes in the game have pretty cool perks that set them apart from each other. My favorite being Vanguard which can charge into the horde and not care or draw aggro from the team by blocking hits. Getting the prestige perks requires a lot of grinding though so I dont really care to much about that aspect of the game. I was surprised at all the playable characters and thought it was shame they're not available in every campaign but at least Survival mode gives you that option.
_childDocuments_.name: World War Z

_childDocuments_.review: If you were one of the unfortunate people to have bought Back 4 Blood and are now experiencing what the latest update to that game has done, then i highly recommend you come to this game instead. The class system in this game is a lot more polished and functional than it is in B4B, the difficulties actually feel difficult and the levels are a good length with plenty of things to look at (minus new york which is very boring). There are many characters to play on each campaign in this game, lots of weapons to choose from, smoother melee combat (sometimes). Weapons can be customized with points you earn by playing and using them enough, same with classes. The only downside for this game is really the players. it's to be expected with any game but this game and B4b seem to suffer from the same problem, Low level/new players playing on higher difficulties. you are only as strong as your weakest link in this game and if you see a player on Playstation then you should immediatly find a new match.

World War Z is a thrilling four-player cooperative third-person shooter featuring massive swarms of zombies that recklessly rush their living prey. name: Wattam
detailed_description: Wattam is a game about the joys of friendship and discovery, from the imagination of Keita Takahashi (creator of Katamari Damacy and Noby Noby Boy ) and developer Funomena. Friend Them All In Wattam, more than 100 wacky and carefree characters are waiting to be unlocked and become your friends, from sushi to seashells, and gigantic trees to normal-sized toilets. The Mayor will be your tour guide through this whimsical world, as you dance, chase, climb, stack, float, explode and hold hands through all the fun. A Game for Everyone Play solo or co-op on the same screen with friends (parents and siblings count, too). You can pop in and out of multiplayer mode, so the choice is yours. The adventure takes place through all four seasons - Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter - so there's always plenty to do and discover, whether you're playing with pals or making new friends in Wattam. Go Ahead, Goof Around :-) Wattam is the ultimate goof-around simulation. See what kinds of silly things happen when you push the limits of the game's physics and animations to create crazy and comical results. Solving puzzles, uncovering secrets and playing mini-games has never been weirder or more wonderful. The sheer multitude of friendship combinations and hijinks means there's always fun in store. Keita Takahashi’s Latest Game The legendary creator of Katamari Damacy and Noby Noby Boy makes his long-awaited return to video games with Wattam , a dream-like sandbox adventure that has been in development with Funomena since 2015. In Wattam , Takahashi’s familiar themes of quirky creativity and inventive puzzle-solving combine with a zest for zany friendship interactions. Smiles are guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: Keita Takahashi is one of the most unique and creative game developers working in the industry to this day, and Wattam is the culmination of his many experimental games up to this point, from Noby Noby Boy's open sandbox design, to Woorld's string of toys unlocked through casual play. There's hardly anything else like it out there, providing plenty of joy, purity, and wholesome experiences, all while having a compelling narrative filled with mystery and intrigue.
_childDocuments_.name: Wattam

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game.I love Katamari and was looking forward to Wattam. While the game retains the charm, whimsy, and heart of Katamari, it's just not fun to play. The unplayable cutscene to gameplay ratio feels 1:1, and it's constantly telling you exactly what to do. It takes the same amount of strategy and skill as a walking simulator.If that's what you're looking for, this is cute. But, if you're looking for a puzzle-type game this isn't really it. The graphics are adorable though!
_childDocuments_.name: Wattam

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute treat of a game showing how every little thing matters and how important the people around you are and you should cherish every moment you can. Wattam starts off with a little mayor being lonely and soon off to making new friends and more on the way. The little sandbox you start out in continues to expand as you progress through the 4 seasons. The music once again never fails to amuse me, and the atmosphere gives the katamari damacy series vibes which gives a lot of childhood memories. Each character you unlock feels very unique and adorable to interact with. The story has a lot of meaning towards life and the world itself. The game roughly takes 3-4 hours long to beat but there is after game content if you haven't unlocked all the visitors/achievements just to mess around in the sandbox. Can't believe this adorable but absurd game managed to tear me up in the end truly a fantastic game. Will recommend this game if you are looking for a happy/peaceful time.Thank you Keita Takahashi for your wonderful creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Wattam

_childDocuments_.review: Wattam is an okay puzzle game with truly horrible controls. The characters and story were actually quite charming but the controls really stood in the way of this being an enjoyable experience.Why were the controls terrible? Well, for starters the camera controls (only left and right, no up and down, and the camera only very very very slowly moves in the direction you are moving). KBM: hold right click and drag to change the direction the camera scrolls. The camera doesn't move like the mouse moves, it just moves in that direction at a fixed max speed. Gamepad: Right Trigger and Left Trigger to move camera right and left, respectively.KBM: Left-click to change characters (not that bad). Gamepad: right stick to choose the direction you wish to change characters, God help you if there is more than 1 character nearby in that general direction.Both: Walk into a character to climb them. Have fun climbing everything that dares stand vaguely in your way.Also, unless I missed something early on, by basically the end of the game they introduce the ability to swap characters by a way that doesn't involve hunting from island to island to find them, then get close, then mis-swap (on gamepad) and it's used for the last thirty minutes of the game, probably. That would have been nice to know earlier.The game crashed for me all 3 times I chose to exit the game. Not a huge issue considering it's a very short game, but still annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: I had to have this game for the fact that the person behind it is Keita Takahashi, who created Katamari Damacy, and I have been following the game for years. It's a really really cute game with simple puzzles and lovely ideas; however, it is swamped by really really terrible controls. There are no control scheme options and  you cannot remap them. I am going to have to refund it until the control scheme is better or we can easily remap to more intuitive controls. I tried playing on and off for the past few days, but the controls are taking away my enjoyment of the game.I will definitely plan to revisit at a later date, should this get fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Keita Takahashi is known as an auteur in the video games industry because of his sense of humor, unique style of storytelling, and the whimsical atmosphere he brings to the projects he works on. If you love Katamari Damacy, the gameplay is nothing like that, but you can't play this game without thinking, "Yeah, this is a Keita Takahashi game," because it has a charm to it that's distinct from most other games.I'm not a fan of the toilet-related humor and mechanics, the controls are a little wonky, and Wattam leaves little room for problem solving with quest titles or hints telling you almost exactly what to do.Grievances aired, though, the game is short enough the main story can be completed in one sitting: I took just under three hours to roll the credits and reach the post-game. If you're going into this expecting what it is, which is a cute, fun, story about loneliness, making friends, and forgiveness, with fairly novel mechanics and design, then you're not going to be disappointed. If you go into this wanting a '3D sandbox game' that suggests in its description that it has some fun and interesting physics interactions you can mess around with... it's not *bad,* but I don't think the sandbox element is what this game excels at, personally. Or maybe I'm just not the type of person who finds experimenting with stuff like that fun.All in all, it's a good time! I do think it's worth the original price despite its short main story play time -- there's still a few more hours' worth of stuff I could do in the post-game if I wanted to get more out of it -- but I think it's especially worth it if you're considering it during a sale.(Also, side note: this game's probably pretty good for kids, which is something I think they hint at in the description with mention of playing with siblings or parents. Easy gameplay, simple story and dialog, nothing scary or violent. One of my friends said it was 'like a baby sensory video' when I streamed my playthrough, which I think is reductive, but I do agree that it seems to be aimed at a younger demographic than Katamari Damacy and has pretty engaging audio and visual design.)

_childDocuments_.review: Sooo slooow. Continuous spoon feeding. Disruptive annoyances/cutscenes overshadow any cuteness and happiness the visuals and animations try to establish.+ Cute characters+ Great variance+ Positive/Colorful atmosphere* Playthrough ~3h* Stylistic face is confusing; nose looks like a mouth leading to repeated misreading* Activities are pretty basic; driven by the humorous, cute, and varied characters* Some of the interactions seemed bad to control- Pretty much every activity is introduced, filled, and concluded with cutscenes disrupting gameplay- Character animation, speech bubbles, and subtitles often mismatch due do intertwining states- Character selecting works bad at best (specifically in the 3D world)When you’re already annoyed, control gets taken away yet again, and four characters say and do the same thing one after the other, each for 3 or 4 seconds; I don’t get it what they were going for. It seems pretentious and forceful, with no regard for interactive game design, or any mindfulness on . Maybe others don’t experience it this bad. But to me, through disruption, taking control away, and spoon feeding, it was an annoying experience through and through.I like absurd, colorful, happy worlds, but any setup this had for it with cute charaters, animations and interactions was completely negated with the 80% of the time waiting and getting annoyed. Too bad. A less restrictive, less forceful approach would have made this game a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone in my mid-30s atm, I want to give Wattam a "Maybe" rating. It's a sandboxy game with simple mechanics and sometimes cryptic goals you can do if you want to progress the (weirdly serious) story. I think it's a great game for kids to play around in and work out some simple puzzles, but the controls could use some work.I love games, so I think these kinds of games are especially important to support. For me, this kind of thing is great to experience and understand games as an art medium, creating diverse experiences for all kinds of players that can be fun, silly experimental games instead of only safe franchises. However, my personal experience of Wattam was one of mostly wanting it to be over so I could just be done with it and move on. To that end, all I did was the story bits where it felt like I was doing different versions of the same stuff over and over. Maybe you could break it into many short sessions and that might improve the experience for grown-ass people like me. I felt like I didn't care about anything anyone said because it was so chaotic and random that nothing made sense anyway, but the story got a bit deeper toward the end, and there were some genuinely heartfelt moments. I just felt like things were dragged out a lot by the slow cut scenes and samey gameplay.If you're an adult and you want something lighthearted and playful, or something truly unique in the gaming space, get this if nothing more than to have in your "distinguished gaming connoisseur collection for big brain gamers who know what art is". I would say though, that for 4hrs of game, you may want to wait for a sale from the $30AUD it goes for.

_childDocuments_.review: Calling this game a "sandbox" - it's more like a toybox.  I am not far in, but so far, every single entity barring the floor in this game can:- Be controlled by the player whenever the player wants.- Jump (different gravity for every entity)- Be tethered to two other entities with accompanying physics and some stretch mechanics on the tethers (i.e. you can make them all join hands and smash around together)- Climb other entities and stay fixed on top pf them- Be blown up by the Mayor and go into a "dizzy" mode with unique controls and physics - Be eaten along with another entity to produce new entities - have fun mixing them Some of these entities are so massive that they are basically living chunks of the map.The emphasis is on simply playing around with these features, smashing them together and seeing what happens. There almost always is some kind of satisfying result from doing so.As you play in the sandbox, you are (uninterruptedly) given small objectives to complete which unlock brand new entities, enough of which do completely new things.  Did I mention that it's wonderful? The music and sound effects do a lot of heavy-lifting, giving this cheaply rendered world a lot of character and charm. As an indie developer, I can think of few cult developers I look up to more than this one. Every release from this man is built around gameplay that is fresh, bizarre, simple, sloppy (in a fun way) and completely out of left-field to the rest of the industry. There are a fair few big Japanese auteurs in the industry, but for my money, this guy is the realest one.

_childDocuments_.review: Wattam is the newest game from the mind of Keita Takahashi snd similar to his previous two games of Noby Noby Boy, and Katamari Damacy, it’s hard to describe, bizarre, and unique.Wattam feels mostly like a story where the player has to act out some actions to see the next part.  The actions are usually quite simplistic, but it’s the story that brings out the usual charm of Keita Takahashi.  Everything in Wattam is colorful and friendly, and it often feels like you’re reading a children’s storybook with bright characters that are always helpful and seldom mean.   Even the way Wattam brings up challenges to the character feels similar to the storybooks, such as a telephone base that has lost its telephone receiver, and players are expected to track it down. Much of Wattam involves finding out who is having an issue, and a quick chat that will switch between a subtitled request for help, and a few pictographs when they are appropriate.  Players then take control of their characters, tasked with doing whatever goal the game has planned out.  Most tasks will take only a few minutes at most between the player talking to a character, understanding the goal, and then completing it.   Soon after that, the next task will appear and the cycle repeats.If this sounds like a game for young children, you might be right, but as an adult man with my own teenager, I still found myself falling for the charm of Wattam’s style, characters, and actions.  Every character is bright and colorful and having characters say hi to each other, or even cheering for joy after being blown up by another character and asking for more, puts a smile on my face. Wattam isn’t a very long game, and with the game reaching an end after around three to four hours of content, most players will be left wanting more.  The way the story can draw the player in and make them care about the objects at the heart of Wattam is magical, but yet the story told in Wattam is perhaps the perfect length as the final parts of the game struggle a bit.By the end, players will understand that it’s the journey that matters.  The result of “beating Wattam” rings hollow even as it resolves the story, but that is due to Wattam’s “brilliance” not being in narrative design, but in the childlike innocence it evokes in the players who are drawn to it. Yet it wouldn’t be right to say that Wattam is perfect as it is.  Three hours fly by as players enjoy the game and while many of the tasks from the characters are interesting, many characters are quite useless, even the tree that can eat objects and turn them into fruit, or the toilet that can turn objects into poop feel like they are out of place since the game really doesn’t explore that concept outside of one or two requests. Most characters in the game are there to be looked at and accumulated but have no interactions or purpose in the story, they become another trinket to collect and then quickly move on from. While some players might search for deeper meaning there, the more I played Wattam, the shallower some of the requests become, with the game ending with the original main character being the only one who could do specific tasks, and a strange “Figure out which object we’re thinking of” puzzle being presented as the last task. These tasks sadly don’t make Wattam stronger and leave the player not just wanting more, but wanting a return to the original parts of the game that felt more like a fun celebration of making friends with a purpose behind each appearance and introduction, rather than meaningless guessing puzzles and characters who show up just to be shown off. Ultimately Wattam is a satisfying game.  For ten dollars, it’s not a very expensive game, though, at three hours, players may expect a little more, however coming from the mind of Keita Takahashi, fans probably should expect more experimental and bizarre games rather than narrative or action-filled video games.  Players of Keita Takashi’s previous games of Katamari Damacy, or Noby Noby Boy will find an interesting and unique experience here, but new players may not understand the silly strange style of Wattam.I give Wattam a bizarre but arbitrary 7/10 If you enjoyed this review and want to see more from me, including more in-depth reviews of select games, check out my youtube channel at

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty neat family friendly game, it may not be a long game, but it's really well made game that teaches you about friendship, and family, and why it's important to be together, there a lot of little things to do, with some puzzles, learning what happen in the storyline, and making new friends along the way, and the music sometimes makes you think of Katamari.God I would kill for another Katamari game.

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear, I'm a big fan of Takahashi's other work already, so Wattam has been in my wishlist for some time.I'd gone in mainly spoiler free as far as what the hell this game actually was, and even after playing for 6 hours, I still don't know what it is. The game's layout is very simple, you're basically stuck in a giant cloud cube where you meet a bunch of friends, and do tasks for your friends, which in turn progresses the story, focused on moving through seasons to learn more about what happened to the world.The gameplay is super simple, but still has a nice hook, and by that I mean befriending other things makes you feel good. For example, you need to help an acorn get planted to grow a tree, which signals a change in seasons.Making friends is fun.Holding hands with friends is fun.Meeting new Korean, Russian and Japanese friends is fun.If you are alone, or sad, or like things that look like the Mr. series of books, get this game. I bought it while it was on sale at $10, but I'd gladly pay full price for this game, because it actually made me feel things for how simple and downright bizarre it is. 2020 has sucked, but Wattam has landed and helps by providing that same sort of feeling that Animal Crossing does, the feeling of doing good to help a fren.tl;dr: WELCOME BACK WATTAM.

_childDocuments_.review: is a bizarre game about the end of the world as we know it. But more importantly its about picking up and putting back together the fragmented pieces, and realising the strength in humanity rather than its weaknesses. It's a surprising philosophical piece considering all pointers indicate it was made for an audience of age seven and below. So good job you have me (twenty one year old adult) to shine a spotlight on it. This doesn't fit mosts idea of traditional "game design", its very hands off with the way it explains nearly everything. The puzzles are the main loop and they exist based not on your understanding of the game but your understanding of basic societal principles. Like how an ice cream cone usually has well, ice cream in it. Or a house usually has, people in it. Or a pool sometimes has, floaty toys in it. It is dependent on peoples common associations. Stuff easy enough for anyone to understand, unless you have a debilitating disease that prevents you from seeing shapes correctly. Because that's what this "game" is really, its shapes and colours, all the joys of the world. But this is why it is special, it's an expressive and unique title, unlike anything I've seen before. I've never played a game from Keita Takahashi before but I understand now why he has such a reputation for the truly perplexing and the unorthodox. I recommend  for anyone who wants a few hours of confused faces, happy glee's and the joy of blowing up a lot of people over and over and over again. In my post game endeavours I've stumbled across the fact that this is the most buggy achievement run I've ever had the displeasure of attempting. I have done nearly all the awkward and dull tasks required for near completion, the terribly buggy sushi wheel and the stupidly boring 100 "Kaboom"s and "Poop"s. Only to find out that my snowman has apparently fell off the map, OUTSIDE OF MY CONTROL, and thus rendered my entire save useless as it is a glitch that is seemingly unfixable. So I give a bit of caution to anyone buying this for achievements, . It's one of the most stupid, buggy experiences I've ever had. Everything I said prior stands, its an enjoyable game, but I've docked my rating because of aforementioned glitches. .

_childDocuments_.review: This was a religious experience for my mother and I, and I can say we learned everything and nothing at the same time. Its very funny and an oddly wholesome game, which gave us more joy in the first 30 minutes on our couch than anything HGTV produces. Its absurd presentation, the light toilet humor, and somber quirky and Jazzy soundtrack work hand in hand, to create the ideal game for any bad day. There are a few bumps, some character interactions like stacking can be choppy, I had to wait a bit for it to load initially, and the mouth(?) characters can be annoying, but in comparison to most games with a higher price, it runs relatively smooth. Personally, I could not recommend this g̶a̶m̶e̶  no, experience, any more than I can recommend "Godzilla Minus One", or "Everything Everywhere All At Once", or any Pikmin game, or "Katamari Damacy", or "The Big Lebowski", or any other form of peak fiction. _childDocuments_.review: - As you've likely assessed from the promotional artwork, the visual style of the game is extremely cute- The music is pretty catchy and probably the game's greatest strength. I loved how the music changed when switching between characters. The credits song is also nice and well performed- The rest of the sound design was honestly sort of awful. At any given point all of the babbling and crying gives you the impression of being in a daycare- In a nutshell, you play as a lonely green cube (the Mayor) who is trying to bring everything back into existence after the earth is destroyed- Besides that somewhat grim undertone, the rest of the game is cloyingly cute. It's just not as charming as the creator's other games like Katamari- As the Mayor, you're mostly limited to walking agonizingly slowly, climbing incredibly poorly, holding hands with your friends, and blowing things up with the bomb you keep inconspicuously tucked beneath your fashionable bowler cap- As you bring other characters back, however, you can switch to them instead of the Mayor. A few of them have abilities like eating other characters or turning them into poop. No matter which character you're playing as, however, you will still shamble along at a glacial pace- Some characters have tasks for you to complete when they're introduced. These serve to move along the plot, but they're all very easy and largely tedious- I did kinda like the design choices around zooming in or out to control different characters. Changing the time of day by zooming out and switching to the sun or ferrying around characters to different islands with boats/bowling alleys/tables was a neat idea- I played the entirety of the game on the Steam Deck, so take this list of encountered bugs with a grain of salt:- Two instances of events not triggering, two hard freezes, and crashing every time I closed the game- There's a lot of grinding achievements but no gameplay incentive to complete them- . The music is excellent and the visuals aren't without their appeal, but I was happy to see the credits. It's not a "bad" game. I just wouldn't recommend it unless you're really interested in Keita Takahashi's works and it's deeply discounted
