_childDocuments_.review: DIrector Takahashi Keita's games are always designed to be fun from the ground up, and this game is no different. If you've ever wanted to experience being a colorful book in a toddler's show inside a fever dream, here's your chance. .As you start the game, you play as a lonely green cube named mayor who reunites the creatures on the planet after a cataclysm has destroyed the world. By interacting with anthropomorphized objects such as toilets, bottle caps, trees, and bowling balls, circle dancing to summon creatures, and using objects you find to interact with other objects that were destroyed by the cataclysm, and you learn more about how the world was destroyed, until you reunite your family and the everything that was destroyed..The game is a plot-based adventure about making friends and helping others, and, like every Keita Takahashi game like Katamari Damacy and Noby Noby Boy, is difficult to describe. The game doesn't fit into any genre, and that's the beauty of it. You have to experience it to find out. I can't adequately describe what makes this game so good..How good is this game? No matter how frustrated I got, I never put it down; I never rage quit, I never uninstalled this game from my pc. Controls can be frustrating as you change characters and, unlike Takahashi's other games, they're not intuititive and you may find yourself pressing and holding different buttons to try to figure out what does what. But I got used to my frustrations as I enjoyed seeing all the abstract characters, listening to the music, and doing bizarre things like using the mouth and tree characters to eat characters and poop them out. .As I played this game, I found myself constantly trying out different things. How does the music change as you swap characters, see different environments, or explode your main chracters. I even changed the font from English, as the game features this big bubbly font that sometime fills up the scream and wants to be hugged; I've never played a game where I've actively changed the languages just to see the text. Japanese is so cool, with this big bubbly font that fills the text box. English, I realized, expands words horizontally or vertically just to change the text box. Chinese is kind of boring, as the text is just bold. If you're multilingual, it's worth changing the game to a language you know. .That's how fun this game is to explore; i found myself changeing the freakin' language just to explore the game's mechanics. .You'll have a blast exploring this indie game. There is an issue where the game sometimes crashes right at the ending and some assets don't layer correctly, namely weather such as snow. but no matter how frustrated i was, I found myself enjoing walking around and exploring again and again..tl;dr If you want a game with a distinct points system, kill score, levels, etc. this game won't be for you. This game is made for people who enjoy exploration, and not for some field reports or in-game collectible or pin system, just explore the world and how the game was made. .PC SPECS: 2020 Windows 10 LaptopIntel Core i5-1035G7 quad-core Ice Lake processorIris Plus 940 graphics16gb RAM

_childDocuments_.review: Loved katamari (all of them) but it's heritage isn't enough to carry the game. You can certainly pitch the concept as being abstract. Many abstract games are great. This is not one of them. In this case the "fun" seems to be derived from anthropomorphised objects engaging in mindless drivel. You can expect them to spend an excessive amount of time using prolonged facial expressions to slowly explain how the characters feel about obvious story cues, laugh at confetti-laden explosions, and perform shallow social interactions. Things happen, and you get more things. The lack of meaningful content coupled with characters which universally behave like obnoxious children result in a game which is not engaging. After playing for almost an hour I checked some interviews with Takahashi. it is clear how the game relates to his initial inspiration: wanting to capture the child-like play of his own children. It is equally clear how little the concept progressed beyond that point. As an adult the entire experience comes across as unpleasantly juvenile. You would do better to provide free childcare to your friends and relatives. Maybe that was what Takahashi wanted all along? A full hour of this would be too much. Rather than engaging with my inner-child this makes me want to lock them in a cupboard with some crayons. Are we having fun yet?

_childDocuments_.review: Wattam is beautiful, colourful, and sounds great. What it isn't, is a game, at least not in the adult sense. For an adult, Wattam is little more than a pricey tech demo, because this game is a sandbox--not in the gaming term, but like a literal sandbox for a child. Bright colours, fun interactions, silly noises; this game is everything you would expect from children's TV, and would likely delight any child put before it. For an adult, however... well, picture yourself in a children's sandbox. What do you do? You either leave indignantly or go through the motions of how a child would enjoy themselves, but you feel nothing. That is Wattam. I wanted it to be Katamari 2.0, I wanted it to be an audio-visual joyride, I thought I was the audience for its oddity, but what I got was a children's cardboard book--colourful, shallow, not for me. I want to enjoy it, I do; I paid more than I do for most games, but it's like I've been handed a rattle and I'm supposed to 'get into it'.Whoever had the genius idea to make an achievement requiring multiple specific characters to be specific spots needs to be literally shot. The character select arrow is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious at the best of time, snapping to everything but what you want, even going through the level to do it. Then you have to use the physics balloon to move the characters up onto a platform, which is the worst feeling controls I have felt for anything in any video game. Then you require four sushi characters (10 including the roe) to stand and remain on specific spots, which would be a challenge to get them there in the first place, but every character in this game wanders when you are not specifically controlling them. You move one character onto the correct spot, go through all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to get the second character up there, and the first one is gone, sometimes so far as another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ island, which takes a solid minute to travel between, especially if it's one of the crying eggs. And you can't do them all at once because the balloon is impossible to control, oh and let's not forget the the physics in this game can go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nuts for no reason and shoot you into the sky or fall through the ground. You need to get a stack of six eggs standing on top of one another and the sushi onto an elevated island, without any of them falling off or wandering off, with no way to make them stay still, all white fighting the ♥♥♥♥ controls and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ass camera. These achievements are beyond retarded, literally fighting against the core design of the game. I have never raged at a game like this before, I thought it would be impossible, but I am about to smash my controller because this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ uncontrollable and fighting against everything I am trying to do. ♥♥♥♥ this game and ♥♥♥♥ whoever chose these achievements.Oh and apparently the game crashing at the end of the credits is a common bug, so I had to play through the unskippable ending twice for it to register, and you can't click out because the game pauses. Good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ job, guys.Not only is it miserable to play with offensively grindy or broken achievements, but it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ made too, with multiple characters and accessories locked into infinite falls in my game, or permanently stuck in the void. This is what happens when you base a game entirely around a ♥♥♥♥ physics engine. Attaching two balloons apparently created a feedback loop that sent them both higher than the sun, and took minutes of waiting for them to fall back down. The Mayor has permanently lost his hat, which cannot be returned using the summon hat command, and characters frequently fall over rendering them unusable until the game decides they're no longer a physics object and play their get-up animation. _childDocuments_.review: This is a game that seems to be entirely at odds with itself, it's like trying to watch an episode of Teletubbies where all of the tubbies get caught up in an existential crisis because the tubby custard machine broke down.The gameplay is extremely simple and juvenile, probably on purpose so that anyone can pick the game up and play, even a toddler, you go around, jump, climb, hold hands, make things food, then poop, and explode, but it's at odds with the story which plays out in cutscenes and is extremely wordy with almost pretentious writing for some reason, there are some missions as well that don't just play things out in sign speak, there's an amount of reading required that's far beyond what appears to be the target audience for the game is capable of grasping.I don't really know how else to explain just how bizarre things get in terms of the writing, so I'll present you with one of the last moments of the game, which contains more text than anything else in the entire game put together and has absolutely no impact on what happens in the end (spoilers obviously): Who this game is supposed to be for is a mystery to me, it's far too simplistic for your average or even below average video game player, and has a language and story barrier too high for a toddler, maybe a child and parent playing together in co-op? Who knows, but it certainly didn't hold any of my attention for the amount of time it took to finish it and had me staring at the screen in apathetic bafflement at the end.Damn good music though, dynamic tracks that change depending on location and player character, not quite Katamari tier but it's nice.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game because of its colorful and unique artstyle. The game being very easy helped and the story was alright.  The GoodThe artstyle is very cute.Though the gameplay got pretty repetitive. It was unique in that; things were coming from the sky. Then you needed to go and find something for them. The game does try to change it up here and there, like when you have to use the fan and sword.The music was good.The kid sounds were pretty cute but the crying was a bit annoying.The ui was simple.The game was short.The BadThe controls. You walk too slow. You turn too slow. You have to turn the camera with “left trigger” and “right trigger.” There were many times that I kept trying to turn the camera with the analog stick, and then it switches your character. It was pretty frustrating.One part of the game, you have to climb on top of a tall cake and enter a door. Once I got to the door, I knew I had to press “Y” to enter it, but then my character started climbing the door, and then my character exploded and then made my character start flying around. What you must know, is that in this game, you can make your character explode by pressing “Y” which will send them flying. It is dumb to have that button also be tied to opening doors. I don’t even understand why they didn’t just make it, so that once you walked into the door, it would trigger a transfer to another level event. Anyways, I failed it twice until I finally got in the door.The crashing is a problem. At the very end after the credits, the screen turned black with the loading guy in the bottom right, and then I heard loud music that I’ve never heard before, and then the game crashed. I opened the game again and luckily there was an autosave. I went into it and it allowed me to continue playing the game in a sandbox type of game. But I still wanted to know what happened after the credits. And so, I tried it again by clicking on the sun which was the credits. This time I heard a different loud song and then it crashed again. I do not know why it crashes at the very end of the credits but I’m sure that it will never be fixed.At one part of the game, you have to go find a bunch of things that a person wants. It will be a silhouette of a shape. One of the shapes was an upside-down U-looking shape. It was very frustrating to find out what it was. I eventually had to use a guide.After beating the game, I looked into the steam forums and someone posted a link to a video by "peoplemakegames" talking about the abuse that happened at the studio. I feel bad that it happened during the making of this game, and I don’t understand why it did. Like, why did the katamari creator have to work with that woman? Why was her team needed to work on this game?ConclusionI liked the game. It was easy and cute. A bit too repetitive, which prolonged its game time, but it was okay. I bought it because I’ve been playing serious story games for a while and I really wanted a casual game. This game didn’t end up being the casual game that I wanted because of the times I got frustrated. It seems like only a Mario game can fix my casual game needs. Or maybe I might give that new kangaroo platformer game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10: Wattam is a silly, colorful, family-oriented game from the same creator as Katamari Damacy. Less replayability compared to KD, but artfully crafted and wholesome as an experience.A sad cuboid fellow named Mayor sits alone and weeps. What cataclysm left him alone with only this focusing spotlight as company? Will he ever find a friend? Interacting with the nearby rock reveals that the rock is a friend, animated with arms and legs and everything. You notice the rocks name just in time for it to introduce you to its friend, the boulder. Things progress steadily from there as all manner of objects, both natural and household, are reintroduced as long lost friends returning from the aether. Some chase each other, or hold hands and spin in circles.Then the Mayor grabs his hat. All around him await in suspense until at last, he reveals a present hidden beneath his hat! Exploding, it launches the Mayor and those nearest to him upward in a multicolored plume of laughter and giggling. A good time was had by all, even as they pick themselves up off the ground. Really, Wattam feels like a childrens concept book turned into a playground. Nose walks around and can sniff things. Ruler can stand next to things to measure them. Fan can blow wind at things. Mouth can eat food type characters, then actually poops them out in their appropriate color. Toilet takes things and flushes them away, though why they come out of the Chimney and colored gold I can't quite understand. Seeds can turn into Trees, which can eat most other characters to turn them into things like fruits, food, and seasonal decorations. Meanwhile, larger things like the Bed and Birthday Cake act as platforms to bring characters between the handful of islands. Each island has it's own seasonal theme, but it's also paired with a separate language, resulting in a mixture of 4 different languages in the game: English, Russian, Japanese, and Korean. None of the characters strictly speak in a language, but their names and the comments they make are all based on one of these four languages. It's hard to say it's a way to learn them, as you don't hear the sounds and have to know how to read all of them beforehand to understand it without subtitles. Nonetheless, it grants a sense of multiculturalism to a collection of inanimate objects.  Doing tasks like stacking up as high as a Bowling Pin or retrieving the handset for the Phone progressively unlock more platforms, characters, and backstory. One should be able to reveal everyone over the course of 5-10 hours, including fan favorites like the Prince from Katamari Damacy and even Noby Noby Boy, though the Steam achievements add a little more to do after the endgame.Stylistically, Wattam is bright and childlike, with all these little characters running about, climbing around, and generally goofing off on their own as you switch between them to accomplish tasks. The use of music is very clever, with each character having their own musical instrument track that joins together with others if they join hands and switches depending on which platform or island they're standing on. The combination makes everything feel very lively and playful, and gives each of them a bit of personality as well.Although not cerebral or particularly challenging, Wattam has an uncomplicated purity to it that one can't help but like. Between a straightforward message on family and togetherness and a conceptual playground to interact with, it's a game that is perfect for families with young children and fans of Keita Takahashi's style.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea for this game came from when Keita was playing with his two-year old son, and wondered about what if all toys lived, and connected by themselves? It would be such a fun world to explore and play with! The word “Wattam” itself is actually composed of the Tamil and Japanese words for “making a circle” or “making a loop”. The initial prototype for this game was made by Keita and his friend Vikram, who are from these two cultures respectively, and this new word acknowledges one of the game’s core inspirations: making connections between different types of things.

name: POSTAL 4: No Regerts
detailed_description: The POSTAL Dude is back! Several years have passed since the events that devastated the once proud town remembered as Paradise. The only two to walk away from the cataclysm unscathed, the hapless everyman known as the POSTAL Dude and his loyal companion Champ, drive aimlessly through the scorching deserts of Arizona looking for a new place to call home. After a fortuitous gas station rest stop ends with their car, trailer home, and the rest of their worldly possessions stolen, all the Dude’s seemingly got left to his name is his canine cohort and his bathrobe, and neither of them smells all that great. However, on the horizon, the duo glimpses an unfamiliar and dazzling town that beckons to them. What untold prospects lie within? Fame? Fortune? Maybe a bidet or two? Edensin awaits. POSTAL 4: No Regerts is a satirical and outrageous comedic open world first person shooter and the long-awaited true sequel to what’s been fondly dubbed as 'The Worst Game Ever™', POSTAL 2! (No third game is known to exist.) Key Features Approach your errands in a non-linear fashion within total free roam, open world, sandbox gameplay! Seek out optional side quests for additional rewards! Or ignore all of that and just cause general pandemonium at your own leisure in the town of Edensin! Pick-Yer-Dude ! Choose Jon St. John, industry veteran and legendary voice for Duke Nukem, as the voice of the POSTAL Dude! Or go with returning fan favorites Rick Hunter (P1 & P2), Corey Cruise (PIII), and Zack Ward (The Movie) as alternate voice choices, giving you more POSTAL Dude than ever at your fingertips! Enjoy full freedom in your choice of pacifist vs. aggressive playstyle! Plenty of new tools to support your (mostly) peaceful confrontations, but violence is still always an option too! Brandish an over-the-top arsenal , from the devastating boom of the quadruple-barreled Fournicator to the feathered chaos of the Pigeon Mine! Add that POSTAL twist to your weaponry with potent power-ups such as the classic Cat Silencer, the slow motion-inducing Catnip, and the dual wielding Energy Drink! Supercharge your fists, mighty foot, and urethra with a dose of the testicle-shrinking Vitamin X! Discover unique weapon combos and capabilities ! Combine a feline with a Grenade or the Rocket Launcher for some mobile explosive pussy! Mix a little Catnip with your Hunting Rifle to curve every bullet to its exact mark! Feeling down? Use the Rattler to grapple your way to new heights! Experience a bevy of interactivity as you feed Doggie Treats to strays to gather canine armies to do your dirty work, stock up on inventory (for a price!) at automated Vending Machines, and, for the first time ever in the franchise, use and flush functioning toilets!

_childDocuments_.review: Postal 4 is the true sequel to Postal 2, one of the greatest games I've ever played. I was extremely excited to play this game and waited for the 1.0 release to try it out for myself. After finishing the game, I can say that it's a ton of fun, although it does still need some work (Which RWS is currently doing. With each update I've noticed the game becoming more and more enjoyable for me, so I fully trust RWS to make the game the best it can be).RWS definitely poured their heart and soul into this game, and it shows. There's a ton of stuff to do, all of it fun and hilarious. Although the humor does feel more juvenile than ever (I suppose it would be difficult to do some of the stuff they got away with in Postal 2 today what with cancel culture), it's still fun and the jokes made me laugh more often than not. That's not to say the game lost its offensive, satirical sense of humor. It's still very much in this game.The game's story mirrors Paradise Lost's more so than Postal 2's, considering you're meeting the town's factions throughout the game and doing chores that are a bit more over-the-top than the mundane tasks found in Postal 2. They're still funny and a lot of fun to play for the most part.Gunplay in the game is fantastic. While I agree that they should add more weapons in the future, they still have a solid line-up that feels REALLY good to use, something that I thought was missing in Postal 2.The open world is nice and rewarding to explore, and while I agree that it is currently a bit empty, RWS is (and has been) steadily updating the game over the course of time to make the map feel more populated.There are lots of bugs and crashes to be found in the game, which is my biggest complaint. However, I've noticed that the crashes are getting consistently less frequent with each patch, which is fantastic. Plus, RWS will be sending the game to a port house to not only port the game over to consoles, but also iron out the technical issues in the PC version. Some people have been complaining of poor frame rates, lagginess, and graphical issues, but I've had absolutely no issues with these things. Maybe I just have a really good computer???In conclusion, Postal 4 is an immensely fun experience that truly lives up to the Postal name. Not sure why this one has been so divisive-- I've had nothing but fun with it in my 30-some hours playing it. Although it's certainly not perfect, I'll still give it an excellent score of...9/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Postal Dude and Champ, his devoted dog partner, are back in Postal 4. The two are left abandoned at the side of the road without a place to call home after stopping for gas and failing to lock their car. Their automobile, trailer home, and all of their earthly belongings are all taken. The fictitious Arizona community of Edensin is just over the horizon, so the unusual pair go on a journey there to find work and their stolen goods.You are given a different set of tasks to finish every day, from Monday through Friday, just like in previous games in the series. The majority of these are mundane jobs like encouraging people to sign a petition, changing lightbulbs in the sewer, and acting as a rent to hire prison guard for the day. Some are a little stranger, like one where you must use an improvised catapult to fling disillusioned Americans across the border into Mexico. The one thing that all of these goals have in common is that they aren't enjoyable to work for. In certain circumstances, this is probably deliberate, but why? Postal 4 doesn’t offer a satirical critique of capitalism or anything like that; the game is just designed around dull busywork that proves more effective than any sleeping pills.The weapon selection and AI behavior can lead to very underwhelming experiences. The Postal Dude's collection of pistols, shotguns, and rifles are lacking in credibility minus the revolver as it is the only gratifying weapon since it allows you to quickly take down a number of foes. Due in part to the weak sound design, all of the weapon types lack the punch and sensation of contact you would expect and looking down sights feels excessively awkward and stiff in a way that not many shooters experience. The only weapons other than your typical weaponry are the pigeon mine and boomerang machete. The former lets you slash off limbs with a blade that returns to you, while the latter releases a flock of pigeons that will tear any enemies in their path apart in a storm of feathers. Although the Fornicator sounds bizarre, it's really simply a shotgun with four barrels.Postal 4 has numerous technical problems, especially while navigating the vast world. Even on a powerful PC, the frame rate of this unattractive and dated-looking game struggles to keep up. Additionally, because it frequently crashes on the desktop, quick saving is essential. Several of these crashes are entirely random, but players can easily duplicate some of them. The prm of entering a new area in the open world is one of the more frequent ones. Between these places, there are loading screens, and when you pass through them, the game frequently drops you within a mountain. Reloading a prior checkpoint is the only way to get out, however even this doesn't always function as planned. Players can repeatedly be spawned into a damaged version of the world where the majority of the surroundings had disappeared. In this situation, your only option is to keep reloading until it finally decides to start working.Postal 4: No Regerts lacks humor and mechanics that even somewhat resemble being enjoyable or captivating. The only thing it consistently has are technological problems, which add to the game's long list of other serious flaws.Read full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: The game falls apart during numerous missions in the game. The dam mission on Friday could not be completed without cheats due to the locked doors not opening when two holes were filled, locking me out of achievements for the rest of the save. Multiple areas on the map that look filled in and are accessible are clearly not intended to be seen since they have no terrain and you end up falling through the map. Many missions are unclear in their instructions such as Fix the Race on Thursday; you deposit your weapons, cannot interact with anything on the track so I assume you have to PIT the other four vehicles with only three VERY short laps to get the alternate ending or just fail like I did and get sh!t-talked by Vince. Another similar issue occurred on Wednesday, The Dude never shuts up about intimidating people to get them to sign the petition, but the game never explains (through the absent Krotchy tips or through in game menus) that you can hold down the scroll wheel to hold a gun WHILE ALSO holding the clipboard. On top of all the messy user experience, missions hold no significant impact. You just go through a 20 minute tunnel map, watch a cutscene with whatever faction, then walk back. In Postal 2, you at least had factions that would remember you, but not here. SJWs from Tuesday? Gone. Treasure people from Friday? Gone. Bidet or Gamba people? All gone. Bosses are another issue. There's maybe 5 of them and they're all beaten by chugging an energy drink and smoking some catnip and mowing them down. In Postal 2 and even Postal 3, some bosses took a bit of strategy to beat like with Mad Cow Mike J or that AIDS rhino. Without nicely designed boss arenas or fights you spend most of your time in this game go-karting from mission to mission, shotgunning whatever "boss" then go-karting somewhere on the other side of the map. You might think "okay, well, postal 2 was like that for most of the game" but this is much worse in Postal 4 since there are no shortcuts and the fast travel stations are seemingly placed as far away from future mission areas as possible with some load zones without them at all and there are ZERO map shortcuts in this game. Almost everything else is bugged in some way on top of all of this. Save system? Bugged, sometimes your inventory gets wiped or you have to reload. In a mission with a timer? The time you had left when you died carries over to your reloaded save sometimes and then sometimes I started gaining back a few minutes at a time after a cutscene in that same mission. How about the weapon inventory? Also bugged. The game can't remember which guns you've equipped a cat to or which guns had certain skins applied so have fun reapplying both of those! The game can't even keep track of which costume The Dude is wearing. What about collectibles? Surely that's not - BUGGED! They all respawn after any kind of reload. Dolls, ammo, pickups - all come back every time you reload an area. Absolutely nothing works as intended 100% of the time in this game. Maybe they'll fix most of this in a couple of years but as of right now it's not at all worth 40 dollars and after one playthrough, I'm not at all eager to pick it up ever again.

The one who made this has breached the Geneva convention at least 3 times. 5) When you start a quest, there's no clear instructions on what to do other than a few voice lines. _childDocuments_.review: I deeply love the Postal Series-- having just played Postal II and Brain Damaged, I came into this hoping to find the same quality the other two games had but I was... mixed. Let's break it down.Pros:Delightfully tasteless and really awful in the good way. Same Postal comedy and same Postal vibes.Corey Cruise as a voice! I really love Corey's portrayal of Dude so it made me happy to see him star in a good mainline Postal Game.It looks great. Amazing gunplay second only to BD in my opinion. The best soundtrack imoIt's not Postal III.Drag Dude makes the game a 10/10 period. Cons, and strap in, there are a lot. Prefacing this with I know that it's being actively worked on and these will probably be patched but I will complain anyways:Constant crashing-- I haven't finished the game yet due to this.The constant glitches that are gamebreaking. The amount of times I've clipped through the map is absurd.The world feels empty in a sense despite Edensin being the largest most vibrant town, it feels empty and lonely. Paradise was more alive despite the graphics and small town.It feels like there should be more content if that makes sense. Entire areas with NOTHING that feels like it should have something.I think you should buy the game overall: Postal 4 has a LOT of potential and from what I hear it's very similar to what P2 was like at launch. I'm seeing some good patches come out of RWS and I'm really looking forward to seeing this game get better. Support RWS and buy the game but be wary of the glitches and emptiness of the world. Remember that P2 is only as good as it is because it's had years to get better. There's a lot of potential in P4 for it to be as good if not better than P2, but it feels incomplete.Overall, a fun game, very glitchy but has potential.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT Post Wednesday update. Graphics don't bother me quite as much as they did before, i don't know if they improved it a bit or not. But despite a good chunk of time passing, and a couple big updates. Not much has changed. The Wednesday video is quite misleading. Only the quad shotgun gibs, and only sometimes, and costs a full 4 rounds. Emotes do nothing, no NPC react to them at all. Scooter still slow as hell. I would prefer to see the base move speed be the walk speed, then have a sprint thats close to the speed of the scooter, then have the scooter be even faster. The world still feels lifeless and bland. During my current play through, i have encountered several gaps in the map, as well as a house that's floating a bit above ground. Guns feel underwhelming, buring people alive just see them run a bit and fall down they dont burn. And still the biggest issue for me that makes the game frustrating to play is the long load times when moving from one side of the map to the other, the map is broken up into sections, some require the train to get to others you can just move there, but there are loading borders.Instead of live loading as you approach, it locks the game while it loads the next section, leading to long loading times. Its really something that needs to be addressed. I do still hope the game by the time its done will feel much better, but improvements are slim and far between. I still cannot recommend this game, for anyone who is looking to play now. -----Its hard to say yes or no. But really unless you are a big fan and want to buy now just to help back the game. I suggest holding off. The video looks fun, but the game really for 2019/2020, looks REALLY i mean REALLY out dated. The gunplay is terrible, no iron sights, you can only shoot heads off, no total dismemberment, even with shotguns. The game map doesn't feel good either. It feels cheap, and rushed tbh. I would love to see the game expanded so the map and city looks and feels sensible. And the NPCs to walk properly and go about their daily to some degree, rather then there being a janky road with random buildings dotted about while the people just walk aimlessly through the streets and all over the road. Make it larger, let us use cars or something. Its postal 4, not postal 2, think bigger and more modern. And the gore and violence, its just so tame, there no shock to it, its not satisfying. Turn the dial up past crazy, and go nuts with it. I know its in EA but so much of this feels like its a final map type deal.and the loading screens when moving around the map really don't do it justice.I really want to love this game, but unless postal 4 can go from this boring mediocre mess, to something thats so over the top and push the envelope more on the shock and gore and dark humor then what postal 2 did.And it did so much so that it was banned, then i don't see it going down as anything but a poor attempt, and may even see it go down as what will be seen as a cash grab. _childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of POSTAL, this is a game you'll probably be tickled by regardless of its state. With that being said, there are a laundry list of caveats to the question of whether or not you should purchase this game.All of it having already been said however, I'd like to point some things out.  The game has updated with astounding regularity since release. Maybe not a huge deal, it hasn't been out for very long obviously, but it's better than a lot of trash that gets thrown up in early access. Running With Scissors has a track record of supporting and updating their games for a completely unreasonable amount of time. The original POSTAL (released 1997) feels fairly modern despite its dated looks thanks to years of updates going all the way up to its most recent in 2015, for example. While the game does in fact run like ♥♥♥♥, it seems to run about the same amount of ♥♥♥♥ all the way down. People with i7 8700k 2080Ti rigs are going to get the same issues as people further down the performance spectrum, because it's mostly the engine chugging rather than your resources being eaten up. This is being improved upon on what is quite literally a daily basis, so there's little room to complain from my perspective.All said and done, I still wouldn't recommend that  buy a copy right now, but fans absolutely should hop in and give feedback. The average person might want to wait a few months for the game to be more complete, but the price will likely go up as the game becomes more finished. I think that the choice will be fairly clear for most people with the information that's freely available now, so if the answer is yes you'll likely be satisfied and waiting for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Postal 4 is exactly what you'd expect. It is a masterpiece of mayhem that builds upon its predecessor's legacy. It's a natural progression from Postal 2 in every way: the graphics and sound quality are better (obviously), the world map is bigger, and the game mechanics have been updated for modern players (i.e. iron sights, weapon wheel, reloading, etc). All around the game is basically just an HD version of Postal 2 with more content! What more could you want?! Running With Scissors' mature humor makes a return and it's better than ever! Long time fans will appreciate the many throwbacks and references to the previous games, but there's still plenty of laughs to be had by newcomers as well! The developers should also be commended for going out of their way to make their fans happy! When the community said that they didn't like the new voice actor for Postal Dude, they got another one. When people didn't seem to like that guy either, they changed it again! Finally they got the original voice actor, Rick Hunter to reprise his role as the iconic character, and gave players the option to select whichever voice they liked best! Nobody forced Running With Scissors to do that, but they did it anyway because they care about their fans and they want what's best for the community. This is the kind of behavior we want to support as consumers. The gaming industry needs more developers like this, because right now, the way things are going, companies are just taking advantage of gamers, and that needs to stop. Not trying to be a downer, that's just reality. Anyway, Postal 4 is a great game and it lets you run around an open sandbox wreaking havoc in crazy ways. The sheer amount of destruction in the game is worth the price of admission alone, just make sure you have a strong stomach for the gore! Postal 4 is a fantastic game, so what are you waiting for? Download it and start going postal! If nothing else, this game makes for great stress relief after a rough day! Take out all your anger on the unsuspecting virtual citizens of Edensin and you'll feel much better! Trust me!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it's flawed.But god is it fun. I see a lot of people saying this game is a "cash grab," but there's clearly a lot of love put into this game. It's a game for Postal fans. A simple cash grab would not have gone out of its way to get each voice actor from each of the previous games (AND the movie??) to reprise their roles.The shooting is surprisingly fun too. While Postal 2 is the better game, 4's shooting is up to snuff with a lot of AAA shooters. It's punchy, responsive, and satisfying.The inclusion of a 3rd person camera is great. While I prefer playing in 1st, it's like a glimpse into what Postal 3 could have been.The collectibles are fun, and make exploring the open world that much more interesting. But that does lead into one of my few issues. Some buildings feel totally barren and devoid of life. I'd even be fine with copy-and-pasted assets.My only other major issue is that some of the loading zones are super screwy. Driving a scooter through some of them has you spawn on the other side in the geometry or that side of the map won't even load properly.Minor issues are the Kunny boss: she becomes invincible if you set her on fire. And not everything seems to reset properly when you die and respawn. Enemies will remain aggro'd and bosses health doesn't reset.Like I said, flawed but fun. I love the series and discovered it in 2014 when Dunkey made a video about 2. I regret nothing, especially not buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Postal 4 is basically the sequel to Postal 2, because well nobody can find Postal 3. It's Postal again in its ideal form. Be a nobody.Do things that you would not normally do. Enter people's homes, stores, offices, and find their guns and ammo, bulletproof vests, and perhaps smoke pipes, just like in real small town America.Complete Jobs that offer you well discovered rewards on site. Did I mention, First Person Platforming? Oh yeah the true test of skill. Also It's not Postal without commentary from The Dude you are playing as.However I recommend you to play Postal 2 first as Postal 4 is an incomplete Alpha with some doodad assets not really well hidden for later development. I would also like to mention that the game is not optimized, as it stutters with pretty mild camera movement.  Some things missing right now: A mention that middle mouse (usually the scroll wheel button) button is the holster key, because just holding a shovel imbrues fear in pedestrians that see it. It’s not shown on the well-illustrated control map.Police. The Police Station is empty. Pedestrians not dropping cash, but they still drop guns when they have them. They still use the audio tracks from Postal 2. “One Side”, a phrase I never understood.   There are no stores or interactive vending machines, but the framework is there.Destructible windows that you can access though. It teases me how I can't steal all of those smoke pipes in the window.The story itself is limited to the first day, and it is a pretty long day that would take you nearly 2 hours to do. The story narration though is generous enough to mention that the game itself is more of a demo than a complete game, so depending on where that goes let’s hope we are not paying full price for a demo that may not be completed.

_childDocuments_.review: A proper sequel to Postal 2 (we don't talk about 3). Postal 4 feels like a positive upgrade in almost every way, i even find the game to run more stable than postal 2 did despite its Alpha status (Likely due to age and modern system conflicts). Doesn't mean 4 isn't without its problems atm but again, alpha state.Gameplay mechanics feel solid. Most of the classic weapons make a return and have gotten a much needed facelift both visual and mechanically. Weapons sound and look like they have impact, headshots often drop a target in one hit even with the basic pistol which can be satisfying.NPC and level interaction feels somewhat basic even barren in some areas but update progress has shown this is just part of the building process and more will come.So far my only real complaint is i find the open world a little too big. In postal 2 the world felt like it was making the most of its limited space per zone and packed them tight with goodies, NPCs and lots of jokes. I know the world will continue to be fleshed out over time but there are still segments of the map that seem excessively large. Huge swathes between areas where theres nothing but a empty road with 1 or 2 wandering NPCs.The addition of vehicles (humorously in the form of mobility scooters) makes this less noticeable but its still irksome sometimes.Postal 4 looks and feels like a passion project. RWS has managed to trap what made Postal 2 fun and put it into a modern title and while its still a bit scuffed its not anymore so than it was back in the day. I look forward to more progress and a final release.

_childDocuments_.review: The POSTAL 3 we deserved but never got! if I were completely honest here, I was genuinely not expecting to see a fourth entry in the POSTAL series, especially considering we never got a third entry! but here it is: POSTAL 4. was browsing the store and typed in "postal" just to see what came up, and here it is. POSTAL 4: No Regerts is currently in an early alpha stage, but I'm very amused and interested in what I see. the game runs on Unreal 4, and is mostly like POSTAL 2 in terms of gameplay and plot. you once again play as The POSTAL Dude in his attempt at finding home. you have to check off various errands, and can terrorize people if you feel like it. there's new weapons including an AKM, an Ingram Mac-10, a Quad-Barreled Shotgun, a reloading mechanic (the only other game to do so other than Postal 3, the one that doesn't exist), vehicles, Pigeons (about damn time!), Jon St. John as The POSTAL Dude (that's right, Duke Nukem's voice actor!) and best of all: TOILETS! you can actually use and flush toilets in POSTAL 4! hah! overall, I haven't seen much, but I've seen enough to say it's a must-have for POSTAL fans! have a nice day, I REGERT NOTHING!

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible, unsatisfying, almost to the point of feeling like an asset flip game which lends further credence to this being some kind of cash grab, however time will tell if that is really is true. If you're expecting the quirky, charming, and fun experience Postal 2 had to offer, you'll find very little of that here, from the strange Postal 3 esque plot to Jon Saint John voice acting Postal dude, which I don't know if it's the writing or just the way Jon voice acted the role but he ends up sounding oddly optimistic and very much like a boomer, instead of the cool, edgy, and laid-back demeanor that Rick Hunter had. To start out you get this great menu music and well done opening cutscene which gives you a little hope that the game won't be as bad as it looks from the trailer or screenshots, but on further inspection from the main menu, half of the options are all grey'd out leaving you unable to even change your controls or save your game, which in all fairness are probably going to be properly implemented in the coming days. The plot is, you get your trailer stolen with all your belongings, including your favorite trenchcoat and t-shirt, all because you left your car door unlocked while you were off using some gas station bathroom while in a purple bathrobe for whatever reason (probably to make a big lebowski joke as seen in the promotional art and opening cutscene). because of this you end up stuck in some Arizona gambling town in dire need for some cash, leaving you to beg for work. What makes this so strange is that instead of having you, maybe ask around town if anyone has seen your car, or trailer, or hell even a guy wearing your clothing, you're right away holding up a cardboard sign begging for work in a scene oddly reminiscent of asking people to sign your petition, asking for money for the wedding OR asking people if they've seen your dog, Champ, all things you did in Postal 2 and its expansions.  The gameplay itself is like Postal 2, but more buggy, and unsatisfying. Lighting people on fire with the jerry can will usually have them just standing around until they finally fall over dead, throwing the machete at people will only some of the time unceremoniously turn them into a pile of gibs and spaghetti, and the other time be stuck floating mid air, and being unable to even chop off any limbs, shooting people in the head with the revolver will sometimes leave their brain matter and head giblets floating mid air, all be it sometimes satisfactory, however still disappointingly lacking the ability of execution shots like it did in paradise lost, hitting people with the shovel lacks and weight or real feeling, and just overall feels terrible, every gun needs to reload, stunning people with the stun baton will sometimes not actually work and just have the effects glitch out everywhere, and anytime you walk off the blurry road onto the dirt you'll take damage stepping on tiny little cacti WHILE WEARING ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BOOTS. Everyone is saying "This is fine", "Hey it's all good guys, you're helping fund this new Postal game and get a demo with it until takes off!", "Don't be too critical on it guys, it's only early access they'll fix everything, it's a labor of love!", "Isn't it great that running with Scissors is making games again?" And to that I say, why this? How come after all this time we haven't seen a new IP? We get Postal Redux which was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. We get people floating around rumors that "Running with Scissors has been working on a new IP not postal related" totally unsubstantiated. And then out of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ no where, WE GET THIS! Early Access Postal 2² for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 20 dollars? By god I want to be wrong about this, but this looks like it's going to be on and off updates for a couple of years, probably starting with optimization and bug fixes, and ending with some new areas and story missions until they call it a day once the money pit runs dry. Its this real bad feeling I get, that all the weapon models and animations with the phone game Ul, and reused Postal 2 sound effects,and that stock unreal fan game look and feel of everything is going to stay the same as it ever was, having no major change in artstyle or gameplay overhaul at all as time goes by, and holy ♥♥♥♥, I hope I am wrong about this. I hope in like a years time, this whole review is gonna be dated garbage and I can rewrite the whole thing singing it's praises talking about how wrong I was, but until that day if it ever comes ever comes, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review from positive to negative.While this is a much better sequel to Postal 2 than Postal 3 will ever be, I don't think it's as good as Postal 2 nor will it ever be.This game is still in Early Access so I hope that there will be a lot of changes made to the game, and I'll be very excited for when it officially releases, but for now, I would not recommend this game to anyone who has played Postal 2.To someone who has never played Postal 2, I can see this game being a lot of fun and pretty interesting, but from someone who has finished Postal 2 and it's DLC multiple times, I personally feel like this game tries way too hard to be Postal 2. The same jokes, same voice-lines for NPCs and similar walking animations make this feel more like a port of Postal 2 to the Unity engine than a new game made by the same company. Bugs are also very apparent, but it's an Early Access so it's not that big of a deal for now.Really, my main issue is how this game feels like it's trying so hard to be Postal 2. I didn't come to this game expecting Postal 2. That would be an awful way to judge a game, but it's hard not to compare it to Postal 2 when the two games feel so similar, the only difference really being the graphics, models, and a few new concepts.I'm excited to see where this game goes in the future, but as for right now, I feel like it'd be more worth your money to just buy Postal 2 and the DLC and play that while you wait for this game to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Postal 4: No RegertsGenre: Action/Adventure, FPS, ShooterGraphics: 3/5Music: 4/5Sound: 3/5Strong Suits:☠ Great gun models and sounds☠ Classic Postal chaos☠ Amazingly good cinematics (shockingly good in contrast to the rest)☠ Good power-ups and items with some items returning from old games and some new☠ Large map with lots of freedom of where you goWeak Points:☠ Visual bugs☠ Near constant crashing☠ Bosses not spawning or spawning in the wrong place☠ Unexplainable bugs constantly☠ Some weapon boxes will not return your gear, forcing you to get everything again☠ Some doors will de-spawn or disappear forcing you to be trapped forever☠ Some bugs can make the game unplayable forcing a total restart☠ Most store and house interiors are totally barrenComments: In its current state I cannot recommend this, not even as an early access title.It has really good roots and definite potential but it is in a very poor state currently. If you liked Postal 2, then what this game is supposed/going to be will be good for you, but in its current state, it's nearly unplayable. I couldn't even complete the game due to the door in the mall disappearing after I finished the errand there, even no clip and teleport cheats cannot get me out of the mall.The map is huge and you can go into almost every house and business, which sounds cool till you realize that most of them are totally barren. Just a house asset that is totally empty. The ones that aren't empty are hit or miss if there will be stuff no clipping through walls, or if it will actually look like an interior.Another side note, not a huge deal, but all the gun animations and reloads are great, but when you reload the shotgun, the shells just kinda spawn in your palm. Like I said, not a big deal, just lazy.It honestly makes me pretty sad. I wish that I would have waited because I do believe that this will eventually be a good Postal game, but right now, it's nothing more than a pretty empty romp around that gets annoying and frustrating due to its bugs and lack of stability. My suggestion is to wait till it is more complete, I got this on sale and I am still disappointed.The only way I recommend this is if you are a hardcore Postal fan who wants to support the devs despite progress. With that being said even then I would be wary seeing as they have OK'd another game to be made by another dev team.Overall Score: 1.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Before I dig in, I would like to start by saying that I'm a massive fan of Postal 2. It's the peak of the early 2000s edgy games with tons of gore that got all the parents and idiots like Jack Thompson screeching at the top of their lungs. I'm a proud edgy boi to this day and Postal 2 showed me how to ruffle feathers in the best way possible. I've played it multiple times and enjoy the freedom it offers every single playthrough. So honestly, the fact that Postal 4 is just Postal 2 2 (2022) means that I'm instantly sold.  I've owned this game and followed it's developments since early access and the current product is kind of a mixed bag, I'll get more into that, but the gist of it is, it's not as good as Postal 2, but it's still fun for much the same reasons. I don't regert buying this game in the slightest. Anyway, here we go:Pros:+You can still piss on everything+Graphics are pretty alright, nice blend of fidelity and style. They also managed to really keep the original vibe of Postal 2+The errands are fun and engaging. Over the course of the week, you will partake in a wide variety of activities and you can really tell they tried to do something different this time round. There's also plenty of side activities to engage with in the meantime+Connected to the above, the storytelling and characters are typically Postal and the humour is exactly what you can expect. While some areas are toned down, this game is still proudly offensive and an awesome parody of modern culture. It got quite a few genuine laughs from me. Honestly the absurd story alone makes this game a worthwhile play+There is a great variety of weapons that are modeled and implemented fantastically+The gore isn't as good as P2, but it's still really fun with the ragdolls and fluid physics+Because of the above 2 reasons, P4 is the best game to go on an unstoppable rampage in. Seriously, whenever you are pissed off at the world, it's such a great stress reliever to just go on a murderous rampage in this game+You get a choice of multiple voices for the Dude - from newcomer and legend Jon St. Jon to every man that has portrayed the character in the previous games or even the movie. The return of the man, the myth, the icon Rick Hunter feels truly special+Music is pretty good and they managed to keep the iconic sound effects from the old games+Driving is actually quite serviceable+Emotes are cool and a welcome addition+They've fixed a lot of the bugs and improved the optimization substantially since Early Access. RWS are also continuing development with more improvements and new content, including co-op! So everything here is subject to improvement. I will make sure to update this review as necessaryCons:-They've fixed a lot of bugs and issues, but far from all of them. There's still plenty of glitches that are quite the nuisance. It also drops frames on certain occasions, so optimization needs more work too. And I have a pretty decent PC that runs far more demanding games at ultra settings. This is definitely not a hardware issue-The fact that the map is still split into tiny zones with loading screens in between is honestly just, bad. P2 is like this, but it gets a pass for being a very old game. In P4 however, this type of design feels woefully inadequate, especially given how a ton of open world games have effectively eliminated loading screens after the initial game start for over a decade now.-Some missions are horribly imbalanced and are a pain in the posterior to get through without channeling your inner Billy Mitchell and looking longingly at the list of cheats-The save feature is good to have but has some issues with it. One of the more annoying things is how if you respawn directly after dying, it puts in the location you were but doesn't refill your ammo to what it was, even though enemies will still respawn-NPC programming is quite bad, worse than P2 by far. NPCs often just wander around randomly, don't react adequately to your actions or just glitch into things. There's still plenty of work to do here. Part of what made P2 so great is how the crowds would react to your antics. The same needs to happen here for the experience to be complete-Only 2 driveable vehicles - a mobility scooter and a buggyOverall, I can understand why some people are disappointed from this game, but I also stand by my point that there is a lot to love here. The action is still fun, the humour is still great and it remains an amazing stress reliever to just slaughter some civilians whenever you get up on the wrong side of the bed. Even as it is right now, I still think it's worth playing through. There's just still plenty of issues that stop this game from being truly great. Still I'm holding out hope that it will improve in future. I've seen how much better it is now compared to years ago in beta, so here's to hoping that this trend continues. I'm definitely gonna keep my eyes on it for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a big Postal fan, it was clear I had to give this alpha a quick play to see where Postal 4 is at. I will revisit this review as the updates are pushed through, but I just wanted to compare some of the bits and pieces between this and the ol' favorite (Postal 2). - The first thing that hit me was the level of eye-candy staring back at me from the computer screen. This is already a good-looking game! The level of detail throughout the level is amazing. Everything looks like it has been gently brushed, and I didn't find many textures that didn't appeal to me. Even the animal models were great. I gave the third-person, over-the- shoulder view a try and that worked as expected. The Dude looks as majestic as ever, though lacking his classic trench coat. The weapon models look good too, though I only found half a dozen different weapons in the half hour I played. The NPCs looked fine as well, though that was were I began noticing a few issues.. which leads me on to..- The AI. I understand the NPCs are running to a similar degree to what Postal 2 had, but they seem extra janky in their movements. They would often get stuck when standing up, and I feel their movements are just too rough in nature. Their voices are also a little odd, sometimes switching from different voice tones when conversing with each other. This is an area that I suppose will need addressing in the near future.- I do appreciate the similarities between Postal 2 in terms of sound. I recognised the same sound effects for certain actions, such as kicking things and collecting items. And the sounds I found new fit in nicely for the most part. The gunshots had a nice "weight" to their acoustics, as did the usage of items. What I didn't really care for was the screams and reactions of NPCs. They seemed a little watered down and unenthusiastic. But that's just something else to be worked on.- The on-screen indicators (or UI) look fresh and familiar in a way, which I respect the devs for. Sometimes you just need a fresh lick of paint and light redesign to make things look brand spanking new again. The keys for switching between items have been carried over from Postal 2, making things a little easier for me. (Though one thing that annoyed me was the unzip pants key. It has been changed from R to C which is just odd). I also like the new "map", and additional stats/info tabs. Overall I found this to be a good starting point for an Alpha build. The foundation is there for something decent, and though there is a lot lacking, there is also potential. I understand it is early days, and so I expect many changes to be made in the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: As of January 2023, i would say this game is playable. however, i do wish i could give a middle review, cuz there's a lot to go over (and these are the main ones i could come up with):Pros:-EVERY voice actor for the postal dude is available in this game. from Rick Hunter to Duke St John, and they're each written and voiced for basically everything.-While the humour/writing isn't like the original its clear a lot of effort was put into it.-The world is MUCH more lively and open with so much more to do than the previous titles, like vehicles, missions, and random collectables.-More weapons, and gunplay feels SO much more satisfying in this title.-If you're looking for the next postal, this is it. they didn't take any drastic changes where they didnt need to and improved GREATLY where Postal 2 fell flat.-there's a LOT of cool console cheat commands to mess around with.-you can tell this game is a project of passion. the developers have kept with it for SO long to make it as best as they possibly can. it's a very ambitious project that is slowly coming together and i absolutely respect running with scissors for taking it on even after all the initial launch backlash.Cons:-This game had a VERY rocky start. like, oh man, it was bad. it's taken a few years to get where it is.-even with that said, there are still plenty of bugs and glitches. some harmless and innocuous, some that just RUIN gameplay constantly, others that are rare but essentially softlock you or force you to do a previous autosave.-there are still sections of the game you can easily just walk out of bounds into.-the checkpoint system in this game is VERY infuriating in some of the later missions. why do medkits go away when i die, but enemies come back when my health dosent?-similarly to postal 2, there's a few sections that are just insanely difficult without much balance in terms of how the player has progressed, to a point where i had to whip out the console.-a LOT of the bosses and game mechanics are kind of pointless or boring. one i can get to mind is the beginning of thursday, and if you want the achievement for killing all the enemies, good luck shooting randomly in the air to get their attention so you can find them all.-for some reason trying to turn off the VR weapon skins isn't in menus, and dosent work with the console?-like i said in the pros, the writing and humour is different from 2. it's good in a lot of respects, but i'd say 25% of the time, probably more if Rick didnt steal the show, the humour really falls flat and dosent feel timeless/iconic. -and probably more i haven't touched onAll in all, i love this game A LOT. but my love for it dosen't blind me from that this game is very flawed. but honestly, that's okay. if you're curious to see where the series goes, this is for you. but don't keep your bar too high, at least in the current state. Im absolutely excited to see where the developers go next.

_childDocuments_.review: POSTAL 4 rules. Monday is a bit slow, Tuesday starts to heat things up, and Wednesday you finally realize the slow build-up, actually made thematic sense. The less action-heavy opening allows for a more goofy, fun, and silly atmosphere, that is worth the slower build-up. By the time you are cleaning huge mountains of poo, and fending off P'oed Taco Makers, you know things just got Legend-freaking-dairy! Clearly, someone had a whole ton of dairy and it so did not agree with them.Once you raid the cult of Toilet Paper, battle wittle Twinkleage, and take a trip to a very warm and wet theme park, things get really tight yall!In short, the only thing missing is the lack of rival factions who will label you an enemy and attack you on sight, to my knowledge, that type of thing only happens on Friday when all hell breaks loose and the entire town tries to kill ya!The game does have some crash issues, and some slight bugs and whatnot, but overall runs well and is a freaking epically awesome amazingly great fun good time!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely better then postal 3. The jokes always hit right on the point, the karma system is truly an amazing feature and not something just thrown in mindlessly for extra content. The easter eggs are amazing and even nostalgic from time to time. The karts are truly an amazing addition, one of the main issues I personally had with postal 2 was the long time it would take to get from point a to point b and with the load zones it was very time consuming. But with the karts it makes traversing the map way easier even with the load zones freezing your game from time to time. The weapon arsenal is definitely much bigger and more refined then postal 2s arsenal, each and every weapon has an upside and a downside meaning that every weapon has a use and some weapons perform better in given scenarios then in certain others. The upgrades you can get for your weapons always feel rewarding to use (I personally like using the electric ammo upgrade) and to counteract using upgrades they make them costly and more of a luxury then essential to survive conflict. The "go postal" challenges always feel fun, rewarding and challenging. There are multiple endings meaning your choices about how you do your day to day tasks and what you do during your free time between said tasks is very important, the story actually makes you feel as if you actually have a role in the story instead of it being a "wrong place at the wrong time" story like in postal 2. I am still in my first play through myself so I don't know much about the endings myself. The daily side missions are a great distraction from the story and reward you greatly for completing them. The story even if flawed in places is overall hilarious, whitty, offensive, and completely fits the style of the postal spirit. Overall postal 4 is truly an amazing masterpiece and a truly welcome addition to the postal franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: POSTAL 4: NO REGERTS is definitely an experience I like to get around despite its current state. When you are finished for the day, why not cause havoc? Why not kill everyone like the sadist you are? What else is there to do than go through the story without having chopped one head off?In the day and age of gameplay and visuals, this is a significant upgrade over the mistake POSTAL 3. _childDocuments_.review: Being developed by Running With Scissors means they pass the sniff test automatically. I never played 3 but I did know it stunk up the whole community's nostrils. Fortunately, with literal feces on every bathroom floor, the real sequel to POSTAL 2 is back.I appreciate bringing back Rick Hunter, as well as letting you choose Jon St. John (the "intended" new VA for The Dude) or  Corey Cruise (the POSTAL 3 Dude). Also they reintroduced the nice little stuff like the famous "petition", catnip being a strategic buff, health "pipes" which oh-so-cleverly skirted ESRB rules of old, and the fact you can literally walk into people's houses in the style of traditional RPGs.POSTAL 4 is not so much an sequel on POSTAL 2 as it is a take on POSTAL 2 for the modern age. It was going to be a remake until they got enough creative ideas to just start new. That does not mean any kind of BS pandering or any of the offensiveness being toned down, but just the opposite. It  mean tons of COVID references, political hot takes and pop culture references, and accommodations for the 18 years that's passed, such as the Dude now having a smartphone. You can even see a screen protector on that sucker!Some of the frustrations from POSTAL 2 return, too. These difficulties include: massive amounts of backtracking that stretch from sides of the area to sides of the map, loading zones like the old game (clearly marked), and a few opportunities to really screw yourself and softlock any further progression. There is an area northwest of the Chinese gazebo that if you fall into the canyon you'll be unable to get back up to Edensin.The rampages are not bad, just poorly designed. Most of them are just "kill these [x] people in [y] seconds". It is a mistake that you can start them without having the necessary weapons equipped.The game is technically "1.0", but even the developers know it is not fully cooked, it's just a way to say the game is no longer "Early Access". Hourly crashes (with default UE4 crash reporting, wow!) put a damper on the experience. The game is fairly unoptimized on higher settings, leading you to either reduce your resolution or some of the effects to get it to a more desirable 60fps or greater.Despite these sizeable concerns, which would turn someone who did not like or play 2 into a "not recommend" review, there is still plenty of game to be found here and heart put into the project. And I am looking forward to seeing this game through to the end.tl;dr: Currently 6/10. Worth $19.99, and buy it cheaper if possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Alas, this has come out to my long awaited pleasure. First off, I love Postal 1, 2, and Redux. I played a lot of those games and am a big fan of all of them, though, not sure between Redux or 2 which one's my favorite. I absolutely love this game, it's fun in all ways, though, I have my complaints. 1. The map sizeI get that RWS probably wanted to expand the map and see what they can do with modern hardware since Postal 2 was made in the 2000s. But I think it's to the game's bad side. Postal 2 was easy to move around in. I memeorized all the secrets and where all the crack is. I still have plenty of time to play this, I haven't beat it yet, and I'll write why that is in a later. But the map didn't need to be this big I feel. I think Postal 2's strength is being super compact and being able to work with its small world. This though, I mean, there's so many places to go and driving is sometimes admittedly boring. I'm not a developer so I don't know how things work in how to make a world map, but if it was sized down, though that may be impossible, I feel that would be better. I may be biased though due to my utter love to Postal 2. Another thing I dislike is: 2. Some of the missionsThe VR mission is where I had to take an extended break. It was not my cup of tea, I really disliked it. It could be just me, as I'm not much of a person who likes si-fi type things, but man it drug on to a point where I had to quit. The other mission is when you're in Cunny Land. Shooting the electrical boxes was lame, I felt. Even paying off Cunny and the others still made it feel like a chore. 3. The humorI think humor is subjective, so I don't judge other's likes to jokes, but I didn't like it either. But that's just me. Some of the jokes landed, others didn't, I can live with it. I can tell, though, that RWS enjoyed making them, so that's all that matters. Other than that, what are the good things? Well, everything is good. The gameplay, controls, the story, everything. Sure, do I think it holds a candle to Postal 2? No. But it's still enjoyable. I enjoyed my time playing it and I will play it further, especially when Zack Ward is coming to voice Postal Dude, which is really nice of RWS to not make the voice packs DLC. Thanks for that. Just be weary of the jank. There's a lot of it, but I'm sure it'll be ironed out soon enough. I'll update my review later when I beat the game. But, man, PLEASE make another Postal game like 1, that would be the best.Update:I beat the game and loved every moment of the ending. However, I was going to do a pacifist run, but I didn't really want to. For whatever reason, I don't feel the same way about replaying the game as I do 2 or Redux. I think it's due to it's length. With 2, I was able to beat the game in 56 minutes on a pacifist run. Pacifist is the only way I play Postal 2, but here, it's not as fun as 2. I love this game still, the ending, all the voice actors of the Dude, the guns and story are all fun. It's just navigating is the weakest part of the game. As I said, the map size for Postal 2 was perfect. But in this? I think it's way to big. I also prefer the shorter chores of Postal 2 than the longer missions of 4. The plugging of the dam, the VR mission (which I'm glad they have an alternate route for it now), the tagging of the billboards, and the sewer level were weak points.The other missions are fun, as each day you can explore the world and get an advantage if you really look for items. But, it could just be me with my bias for Postal 2. It's still a good game, still with jank, but I'm sure it's going to be ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally managed to play through this game after purchasing it in 2019. I wanted to get every achievement before writing this review, but the only achievement I haven't gotten is currently impossible to get for a reason I'll discuss below.For starters, if you're looking for a game that is comparable to Postal 2 in terms of replayability, humor, and all the other things that makes Postal 2 great, you won't find it here. Don't get me wrong, I really tried to enjoy this game, but its flaws make it hard to do so. Below are some of my complaints with the game, but keep in mind there is a lot I could talk about here:- Weapons in this game are a mixed bag. One of the biggest changes made compared to Postal 2 is that many guns require you to reload. By itself, this isn't a bad change, but part of what made the guns in Postal 2 so fun to use was that you didn't have to ever reload with most of them, allowing you to keep the mayhem up. Another change is that the ammo capacity of some weapons has been reduced, requiring a purchasable upgrade in order to gain a larger boost in ammo. The point of this change is to make the player use different weapons and not focus on a single one the whole time, but it just feels like an unnecessary constraint on what I want to do, i.e. if I want to use the M16 for my entire playthrough, I should be able to. Even melee weapons aren't safe: the machete now takes 4 or more swings to kill someone, though it can still kill with one throw. However, the changes aren't all negative: the shovel can usually kill someone with a single swing, and the introduction of the rattler weapon was a good choice. The M60 is probably my favorite weapon introduced.- Postal 4's map may be large, but it isn't interesting to explore. While there are many buildings to see and interact with, a lot of them feel repeated and barren, almost as if there were plans to decorate them at some point but no changes were ever made. Most of the time, I found myself just trying to run from one errand to the next as quickly as possible. This problem is somewhat solved by the addition of vehicles like the scooter, but you then become bound to these vehicles if you want anywhere quickly. It doesn't help that many buildings that look interesting to explore aren't explorable.- The humor in this game just isn't funny. Humor is subjective, but I didn't catch myself laughing at almost anything in this game, save for some of the signs you see and messages the scooter can display.- Errands in this game range from engaging and entertaining to sluggish and boring. An example of a good errand is the VR mission on Thursday, which features a Tron-like shootout if you choose to go down the glitched path. Examples of missions that aren't good are the pit boss errand, the graffiti tagging errand, the dam errand, the mexi-cleaner errand, and so on. My point here is that only a handful of errands in this game are actually enjoyable to do, whereas in Postal 2 just about every errand was enjoyable and is still memorable to this day.- NPC behavior is (sometimes) a complete mess. Hostile NPCs will experience short-term memory loss and completely forget about you after unloading 30 rounds into your head. When you enter someone's house, there is a 50/50 chance that they will either completely ignore you or begin to shoot at you. Killing civilians with melee weapons in front of other civilians, including cops, elicits no reaction from the group, even when they watch you murder someone in front of them.- The game is a buggy mess. One of the more annoying bugs, and the one preventing me from getting every achievement at this point, is that some of the Postal challenges just don't work, specifically those dealing with killing people on the scooter and pissing on people. Other bugs that I encountered include clipping through the map when falling off the scooter, getting the scooter stuck in the geometry of the map, being able to see under the map by going to locations a player can easily access, level loading pauses being skipped when riding a vehicle into a level, vehicles disappearing when loading between levels, getting stuck on odd geometry, items spazzing out on the ground or being unreasonably obscured due to map textures, and more. I know that many of these bugs will be fixed over time, but it distracts from the experience you should have when playing the game for the first time.- Postal 4 doesn't run well. I don't have the beefiest system, but I do have a 2080 and am able to run all of the newest games I own at well over 100 FPS on a 2K monitor with settings on high or ultra. Postal 4 seems to be the exception, as even with settings only on high (or medium in some cases), I only seem to get a maximum of 70-80 FPS. Not terrible, but not what I would expect. Perhaps the worst cases for FPS drops occur during cutscenes and gameplay occur at the end of Friday, which for some reason causes me to drop to ~45 FPS. I'm willing to blame this on Unreal Engine being a piece of ♥♥♥♥, but it's worth bringing up to me.There are nice things about this game. The return of Rick Hunter as the voice of the Dude was great to hear, and the option to choose your Dude voice is a nice touch. I can also appreciate the various references to the other games in the series. However, as long as Postal 2 exists, I cannot recommend Postal 4 as it is now. I understand that RWS is currently working on fixing up the console release of the game, so hopefully changes will happen over time that make this a true Postal game.

_childDocuments_.review: At least they admit the game is janky. They obviously care about the game, and making it the best game for the fans that they can. Aside from New Blood, I've never seen this level of involvement with the community.By buying the game now, you're giving people a paycheck so they can keep making a damn good game, and continuing the legacy of Postal 2. It is still so damn fun to start a rampage. Whacking people with a shovel is still fun, with a satisfying clunk. Pissing on people until they vomit is still fun. Someone running away after you came at them with a machete? Well, it's a good thing the machete is a boomerang as well. Right now, it's just the basics, and I wish it was longer. But the consistent updates, and the responses to bug reports, feedback, and suggestions on the forum, show that RWS really cares about making a great game.Time will tell, but if you liked Postal 2 and you want to support a proper new Postal game, share the pain.
