_childDocuments_.review: Postal 4 : No Regerts has the same chaotic fun spirit that Postal 2 had but in it's current state it is indomitably bug ridden. It only gets worse with each day until they become glaring awful issues that actively hinder the fun and chaos that Postal 4 proves it is capable of bringing. In addition the game gets actively weaker over the course in terms of it's comedy,plot and spirit. If you are a Postal 2 fan, this game at times can win you over but the majority of the game at least from Wednesday onward is fighting the game's bugs ruining your enjoyment. There are many concessions and features that make Postal 4 enjoyable, it's arsenal is goofy and feels satisfying to use even if you end up using certain weapons almost exclusively. New mechanics for non-violence open up another avenue of raw hilarity. The vehicles are good additions as a mechanic but aren't without flaws i'll get into that later. The voice acting talent of pretty much every Postal Dude is very very very appreciated. I like Corey Cruise's VA of Postal Dude and while Hunter absolutely is the Postal Dude most will remember, he's good in here too. John St John's delivery isn't as great and i feel like he would have been better suited as another character. The pseudo open world nature of the game is at times really fun to just goof around in. At least the first half of the game has a bunch of relatively entertaining tasks for the Postal Dude to deal with, increasing in outlandishness.Unfortunately i gotta talk about the bad. Even all of the good sides above have caveats. The Bug. A looooot of bugs. It gets to the point where they become more numerous and severe over the course of the game. At one point, i ran into a bug that gave me a consistent frame rate in the single digits. I had to reload the game for it to be playable again. Another stripped me of ranged weapons entirely for the rest of the day. Another consistent repeatable bug was one where my map would stop being functional after i had completed the first job for the day. The map frequently refuses to load all of it's assets. I'm not sure if there is a memory leak or something. The narrative while starting out strong gets rather tiresome and while you build up a list of antagonists that grows, you will barely encounter them. In many way Postal 4 feels very safe which is pretty ironic considering the content, it doesn't try to do anything too new and it won't surprise you if you've already played Postal 2. I felt like there could have been a real space for Postal 4 to go really dark in a similar manner to Postal 1 but what chance there was is lost as fast as it comes. Overall i wasn't upset with Postal 4 but it feels like a game that could have been way better. The open world design means you are often just mario karting to your next location and if you bother to explore it's world you will quickly realise how little there really is to explore compared to Postal 2 having entire factions of enemies hidden away. It's also not a very well designed world at that. Postal 2's Paradise was sized appropriately for the amount of space you had to travel to a new zone and there was always at least one landmark to explore inbetween. There is very little of the sort in Postal 4. Yes, there is still some stuff to find but more often than not you are going to be disappointed. However i feel like i can still recommend this one, for all of it's faults when it all comes to ahead the amount of pure unadulterated carnage you can cause is on par with Postal 2 and even then some. If you want that experience then you'll find it here but if you would rather to wait back and sit out what is an incredibly buggy experience then nobody is going to blame you. If it wasn't a fun game then i wouldn't recommend this but it absolutely is.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not that this game needs polish, which it needs a lot of, but it needs a complete overhaul of almost every mission. Some of the arenas are designed really well but what you do for the mission is just boring. Any missions I don't describe left such little impact on me that they might as well not exist. They weren't fun and were only slightly annoying at best. Other than the prison guard mission every Monday job needs to be scrapped entirely. I just beat the game and forgot what you did on Tuesday, outside of the spray painting mission. Wednesday is okay, but the Kunny Island mission is awful. Add some highlighting to the fuse boxes. Thursday was a chore. The VR mission didn't load the secret glitched area for me and the job where you rig a scooter race is awful. The treasure hunting mission on Friday is awful. It has tons of invisible walls that you can see loot behind, it's hard to walk anywhere, and most of the difficulty comes from being unable to see anything. Also the enemies will spawn under the floor and shoot you, but you can't shoot them.The giant open world is the worst part of the game. There is a fast travel system and if it functions (it only worked once for me, in the tutorial for it) it takes you to like 4 spots. 4 spots where you will still need to transition through at least 2 loading screens to get to the closest job. Notice that I said at least because sometimes it's 4. The world is so massive that if you get the fastest vehicle and bee line to your next mission it can sometimes take 5 minutes just to drive there. I used LiveSplit to keep track of the time. If you don't have to money to rent a scooter then you're walking a LONG walk. If you're thinking at least you can loot stuff along the way, then you're wrong. Depending on which part of town you're in most of the buildings will have no items in them. They might have a chicken bucket, which is supposed to be a healing item, but it lacks the shimmer of items so you can't pick it up. Also depending on the way you're going you will just go through tons of empty canyons with long and winding roads. Long and winding roads that make it a pain to drive on, especially since the scooters control worse than the cars in Borderlands.Is the game at least fun to go postal in? I didn't think so but some people do. I like the  weapon variety in Postal 2 and Paradise Lost a lot more than Postal 4. I actually like the weird weapons in Postal 3, like the badger, a lot more than any of the weapons in Postal 4. Even the machine that shot used tissues was more fun to use than most of the exotic weapons in Postal 4. My favorite weapon, the can of Axe with a lighter, was sadly nowhere to be found. Going postal doesn't matter if the weapons aren't fun to use. Sure the SWAT are a lot harder to take down, and will phase through walls/arcade cabinets,  but it's just not fun taking them on.For some reason we don't have a quick switch to our holstered weapon nor do we have key binds to use specific items. We also don't have any UI indicators of how long buffs will last for. Some of the stores still use the horrible Postal 2 store mechanic, despite the vending machines showing they can have a working shop. However, the vending machines are limited on how many things they can sell. Hope you enjoy walking back and forth into store keepers to buy things.I had no real issues with the story itself, outside of the Dude being way too dumb/oblivious, but almost none of the jokes landed for me. John St John does a wonderful job voicing this and I never switched to Rick's voice.I commend RWS for trying to fix this game but it just feels like they're polishing a turd. If you just want an open world to go crazy in while John Wu-ing it up, then I guess I can recommend it?

So why the negative review?I love RWS, but Postal 4 left early access while:-important new features are still being added-on a slower HDD, updates (which, as of writing, are happening weekly) can take longer to patch than redownloading the entire game-on older machines, the game is still too poorly optimized to be played in 1080p60 at the lowest possible graphics settings (to get stable fps on such computers you would have to turn down the resolution scale, which looks terrible and gives me headaches)Honestly, I think the devs were too focused on the 4/20 meme to realize that billing this as a full release was kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥, as most players who barely meet the recommended specs are going to struggle to enjoy this. If I bought the game like this and didn't expect it to change eventually, I'd ask for a refund.Even if your computer ran the other postal games perfectly on max settings, and can generally run recent AAA releases at 60+ fps on medium settings, don't expect to be able to run this at all. At this rate, it will probably be quite a while before the devs finish adding stuff and fulfill their plans send this to a porting house to get everything fully optimized. Until then, buy only if you have a really high-end computer (and even then, from what I hear, the performance can be surprisingly bad).Although it would be inefficient from a development standpoint, the devs really should just suspend all their plans for new features until they've bugfixed/optimized the living hell out of the current game. Everything they add is worthless to the dedicated fans who still can't play, and each day this game is out of early access in its current state is another day of misleading those fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Postal 4: No Regerts is the latest installment in the controversial Postal series, and it still manages to bring the same over-the-top and raunchy comedy style that the previous games were known for. The game's humor is not for everyone, but if you enjoy crude and absurd humor, you will find plenty to enjoy here.One area where Postal 4 really stands out is its visuals. The game looks stunning compared to its predecessors, with detailed environments and character models that are a significant upgrade from the previous games in the series. The improved visuals really help to bring the world of Postal 4 to life and make it feel more immersive.However, the game has a few negatives that are worth mentioning. One of the most significant drawbacks of Postal 4 is its lackluster story. The game's story is thin, and it's really just an excuse to send the player on a series of violent and outrageous missions. This lack of a compelling story can make the game feel repetitive and lacking in substance.Another issue with Postal 4 is the lame cheesy jokes that the game relies on heavily. These jokes are not particularly funny, and they feel dated and out of touch with modern humor. They feel like they were lifted straight out of a comedy from 2003 and have not been updated since.Lastly, Postal 4 has some issues with its keybinding controls. The game's controls feel outdated, and they don't offer the level of customization that many modern games provide. This can make the game feel clunky and frustrating to play, especially if you are used to more modern controls. In conclusion, Postal 4: No Regerts is a game that will appeal to fans of the series who enjoy its crude humor and over-the-top violence. The game's visuals are impressive, but its lackluster story, outdated jokes, and poor keybinding controls hold it back from being a truly great game. If you're a fan of the series, Postal 4 is worth checking out, but if you're new to the series, it's probably best to start with one of the earlier games in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my least favorite game in the series. MAP AND DESIGN:The missions are boring, map is full of bugs. The missions are not very exciting, often having to just run back and forth until a quota is met. The "employers" are constantly nagging you over the radio to do the tasks, even though you are doing the objectives and fighting hordes of enemies. Healing items are almost useless (except the health pipe) because they heal like 3-10 health PER ITEM. Meaning you need to hold tens of food items just to get back to high health. I've played this game on normal, very hard, hestonworld, and postal difficulties. It gets really annoying with the amount of enemies you have to face. Every mission, no matter what the objective is, you will be chased by some psychos with guns, ripping out the fun from the tasks. It's like they tried to make the jobs interesting by adding more enemies. Also, the game makes you feel like you are playing a homeless stinky hobo rather than the POSTAL dude. While the game is somewhat fun and I enjoy the new "going POSTAL" challenges, I would not recommend the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I respect the hell out of RWS. Instead of buckling under the controversy their first game caused, they doubled down and made a sequel so stupidly offensive you'd have to be an idiot to take it seriously. When the sequel to their beloved cult classic turned out to be utter rubbish, they pushed support and DLC for Postal 2 for years to make sure fans didn't have a sour taste in their mouth. And with the most recent entry, they not only brought in huge new voice talent, but every single previous Postal Dude as well, even Zack freaking Ward. It genuinely feels like RWS sees the series as more than just a title they can milk for steady cash. The fans love the series for its tastelessness, and RWS respects the fans enough to keep their communal trash fire burning as long as it can.That said, Postal 4 feels less like hot garbage and just regular garbage. I played this during early access, and I was excited to see the game shape up as development went on. As soon as 1.0 launched however, the load times were simply too much; quite literally for my PC, most times. If the game didn't crash on level transitions, my computer did. Killing things too quickly would make the game lurch almost audibly, and I often fell through or got stuck on level geometry just by walking wrong.Optimization is far from the only issue I had. Gunplay feels incredibly stiff, only really just passing a "usable" mark. Melee just feels wrong. The story is . . . well, Postal. The biggest offender though has to be the open world. It most certainly is very open, with most if not all buildings having some way of entering, but about 80% of the time there's no real reward for searching those buildings unless you REALLY need a couple pistol rounds.Maybe RWS are pulling a big brain commentary, making their most recent game offend gamers by just not being very good. Maybe I'm an idiot expecting anything technically solid when Postal 2 was held together with duct tape and offensive jokes. Maybe RWS will give Postal 4 the love they did Postal 2 and in a few years it'll be damn near perfect. But "maybe" isn't enough for me to recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a game here under all the mess that I love. It can't be overstated how broken this game is. I understand and appreciate that RWS is regularly fixing things, but man is there a lot to fix. A lot of people are saying that the missions and humor are two big things that can't be fixed, though. The argument with the missions is that they're mundane. That Postal 2 would start you doing something simple and then things would get crazy. However, I feel like that's exactly what the missions do in this. The reason people aren't coming away with that impression is probably because of a few things. The AI can be so janky that it makes the combat feel significantly less exciting than it would've been otherwise, so when crap goes down, it still feels as "boring" as the beginning. Also, the missions in general are significantly longer, and so the mundane part is as well. I'm fine with doing more mindless things in games, so it doesn't really bother me. The other reason people have a problem with the missions ties into the other big problem people have with the game, which is the humor. I'm just gonna come out and say it without shame; I like the humor. It's just as lowbrow as the series has ever been and it made me chuckle consistently. I didn't think ALL of it was funny, but that's commonly the case with comedy. It's basically South Park, but not as regularly clever. And just to comment on the political side of it, I know the left thinks it's too much and the right thinks it's not enough, but I think it's just fine where it is. So ultimately, for me, the biggest problem is its towering jank level. I have a high threshold for jank, but this crosses it by a mile. Crashes, really bad performance, softlocks, glitches, design flaws and much immersion breakage. I do have faith that a lot of this stuff will get fixed, though, which is why I'm gonna give a recommendation with a sizable caveat; If you can, wait to play it. At the least, possibly after another couple of major updates. But if you can REALLY wait, maybe let there be about another year of updates. I will say, though, that if you're willing to put up with quite a bit, then you could get it now. Just be warned that you WILL be fighting with it most of the time. In my case, the fight was worth it in the end. It might not be the same for you, but that dice roll is up to your discretion.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - It still feels Way Too Early for Released,But it is showing potential.Where do I start my in-depth look into Postal 4. RWS put this game through Early Access a decision made to acquire public funding for the project and to involve the Postal community in the game's development for the true sequel to Postal 2. Originally this was planned out to be a remake of Postal 2 before ultimately deciding to make a new game entirely which I am so glad they went with. Don't get me wrong, I would absolutely love to see the day we get a Postal 2 Remake and the question of if that's still happening could still be in the air for all I know. They show arrows at the top of the New Game which may suggest that they plan to expand upon this game for the coming future.. Maybe they can still do a Postal 2 Week in the later years if Workshop/SDK does come out too.Story will be considered Hit or Miss. I say it strays away from the familiar dark offensive satire of Postal 2 for more "Reddit"/Internet Humor. Our Dude gets his trailer stolen right outside of Edensin and has to spend another week in Arizona searching for his missing trailer home.. At least Champ is still with him, in cut scene mostly. There does exist two separate endings depending on how you play. Remember, this game is only as violent as you (the player) are. a Nice call back to Postal 2 and sort of expanding on that "Sanity Meter" in that one game which we don't talk of.. Though this time, Story altering cutscenes. Every Day of the Week starts the same with a "Animated?" cutscenes but I think RWS is still working on adding alternate dialogue depending on the path you chose to play. I'd say the story has more questions/theories in spoiler territory but from what I hear from Mayor MikeJ most of the story is B.S.. So I guess just take the story as you would. Still better than Postal 3 I guess.Thing is.. it's still kinda fun to just mess around and do the game at your own leisure like the original Postal 2. Exploration is once again encouraged with how huge Edensin has become,Not kidding this map is sort of MASSIVE but also Empty.. Though that goes without saying that currently most of the building are lifeless if not entirely empty placeholder buildings that they intend to get back to updating eventually. Speaking of how big the map is. Postal Dude can finally use a scooter and theirs Sprinting we can finally feel like were Running with Scissors which I am all for. They did mention more vehicles to be added in the future for this game. Cars and Lambos still exist with the sole-purpose of being exploding props. Though that makes me wonder if the Postal Dude will really be showing his Grand Theft Auto side a little bit. I would like to see a traffic system be properly implemented in the near future. If vehicles are planned then the possibilities of Car Jacking and Carbustion could truly be endless and ridiculous which makes it more fun. Most likely gonna break the game and crash. but it's fun! Having all Four dudes returning has made me appreciate Corey Cruise's performance so much more and props that he's comes back for a official Postal Game this time. Jon St. John is the official Postal Dude for Postal 4 and he gives off a older more calmer Dude than what we've seen from Rick Hunter who we're familiar with his sarcastic sounding tone.For me that fit perfectly well though because this is the same Dude from Postal 2 and Paradise Lost. After all that stuff he dealt with back in Paradise. I imagined he did calm down after finding peace with just Champ,Himself and the Trailer Home. Though I'm not the only one who was rejoiced by the return of Rick Hunter,I felt Rick's felt more like he was winded down from the sarcastic dude from P2 which for returning players may or may not throw-off how they feel about his performance.. But I think he did great like every Dude can. Zack Ward returning into the Postal series was an unexpected but incredible announcement for this game which made me so much more hopeful for the possibilities of Co-op. I hope Multiplayer comes with Four player compatibility so all Four Dudes can go on this Crazy,Cruddy Arizona Adventure.I hope the controller sensitivity settings would be fixed later because it's a little slow for me and I have been using a Switch Pro Controller and Steam Deck to play this game.This game has potential to grow and the devs seem aware it'll be a Long Road ahead before this game even resembles/recaptures a quality to P2 which from what I've seen was the original plan was to make this a remake. Speaking of.. In the New Game options there are arrows, thought I wasn't gonna notice RWS? I do believe they will one day make a road map and consider making the Postal 2 Remake as "A Week in Paradise". Funny because now people can say Postal 2 can be played on Console as I am writing this the game has expanded to the PS4 and PS5 Marketplace. I don't think they'd make Paradise Lost maybe something later down the road for Edensin though? So long as they regularly pump out updates and continue to polish this game and support it. I think this game is worth trying. It's dumb fun but Hey, that what Postal 2 was known for and this one's in HD!

_childDocuments_.review: There are things that are good about this, and there are a lot of things to hate about it.The fact that they've brought back all the voice actors and got a new one (Duke Nukem 'imself) AND the guy from the movie is just awesome!The commitment of the devs to update the game and make it good, is commendable.But.... this is janky, buggy, and overall - the game plays - weird. I heard there's a special thing that happens at the end, depending which Dude you pick, so I really wanna see it.In any case, if you like Postal, or RWS, you - probably could buy this game, as IT IS Postal, however  unpolished and it feels - more like it's still in EA rather than a fully realised game (but this could be credited to many factors, one of which would be financial). Depending on your expectations and - how janky you like it, you'll either have a fun time, or you'll regert ever buying this and quickly refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: POSTAL 4: Riding a very fine line.If you were to tell me we'd get a Postal sequel in 2021, I would've called you high. And if you were to tell me it'd be an early access game running on UE4, I would've called you insane. Postal 2 already ran like crap in 2004 and we just had to recreate history. So when Regerts hit its first sale, I bought it, played it for an hour and then waited. Waited for RWS to either get its act together or collapse like a flan in the cupboard. Lo and behold...It still runs REALLY poorly. But at least it's "finished" in quotes.No Regerts feels weird. It feels weird in how it approaches itself, how it plays, especially how it looks and how weirdly decent RWS has been with updates. Look I will still say it runs like crap and it looks like trash but it's at least getting semi-regular updates so it trumps a lot of "cash grabby sequels". But there's a weird divide in vibes. That same childishly weird humor is there, but there's enough sprinkles of self-referential in-jokes that makes the game flirt with being a nostalgia trip for a game we all liked for opposite reasons. Like I didn't need to re-live the funny petition bit. I like the autism of giving us not one, or two or three but four Dudes to filter from but...There's still underlying problems that undercut both the vibe the game has going for. Frame rates, the utterly weird lighting of the place, crusty textures and a tone that can't tell if it loves the previous games, hates them or wants to be just as good. It's a game that feels like it didn't expect to ever become a thing, and it doesn't have as much of a cohesive idea. Ironically for a game that likes to make fun of not being Postal 3, it has a bit of Postal 3 identity crisis in it. At least it isn't in third person, although I'd take Source Engine over UE4.I like No Regerts. And I like it enough to have concern on where it goes from here. The worst kind of like.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm rating this negatively, but I do want to point out a few positives about the game first. If you played Postal 2, it does have some of the same "charm" (if you can even use that word). The game is genuinely hilarious. It's well written, well voice acted. I've never found another game which features such interesting and different missions.The game features many improvements from Postal 2, for example the UI feels great imo, better /cooler weapons, graphics etc. I actually really want to give this game a neutral review. I don't think it's fair to give a negative after all of the work the devs have done so far, but in the current state of the game I can not recommend it.I bought this when it came out around 2 years ago. It wasn't in a playable state at that time, but I loved Postal 2 so much that I wanted to support the devs. So at the time of buying, the game ran like crap. That issue seems to be fixed - at least for me. My issue is the amount of game breaking bugs there are. The first couple I was like ok ill excuse this since this is beta and they've promised to fix them. But honestly?? That was ages ago. I reinstalled recently to see what's changed. A lot has changed, but when you get to day two prepare to be continuously annoyed. And don't even think about playing Wednesday. Some bugs which are currently annoying the living ♥♥♥♥ out of me include but are not limited to :Inconsistent hit boxes / bullets sometimes hitting and sometimes not depending on how they are feeling. In the theme park, cannot use either roller coaster bc game CTD (and yes I always send crash reports) Random unpredictable crashesNPCs blocking important paths (is this skyrim?) Noise randomly cutting out Some items aren't pick-up able despite having the glowAs it stands, I will probably return in the future to reinstall this game bc I am excited about it and I'll be following its updates , and when the game is improved I will change my review to positive. If you do want to take a chance on the bugs, pick the game up on sale. Maybe in the future it will be worth it's full price. There isnt a lack of content, but a lack of stuff that works.

_childDocuments_.review: I desperately wanted to like this game. I brought Early Access. I kept up with Mike's videos about the game. I helped suggest features and fixes. I pushed this game as far as I possibly could because I REALLY wanted to see a good sequel to Postal 2. But ♥♥♥♥ me, man, this game suffers from so many issues that I and other people absolutely cannot get over. The biggest and most irritating of all the problems for me personally was the guns. In Postal 2, all you had to do to kill people was point and click to unleash a hellstorm of bullets until they dropped. It was simple, effective, and allowed you to stack bodies even before you left the game's very first load zone. Now in the case of Postal 4, imagine for a second if you took a tactical shooter like ARMA and you put shooting mechanics that work like GTA into the mix. It would drastically change the flow of the gameplay, and that's exactly what I feel the problem is with Postal 4's weapons but in reverse: Having to stop, ADS, and work my shots into each and every enemy feels so sluggish and just makes combat an absolute chore. Hell, it'd be way easier to shoot people in real life than it would be to shoot someone in this absolute cluster♥♥♥♥ of a game. Mind you, this wasn't as bad of a problem with guns like the Ingram, the Fournicator, and the M60, but most of the semi-autos didn't feel very good to use because of the drastic change of the pace of combat. Even the melee weapons aren't spared, as they all just feel too same-y and generally just kind of lame to use.And that's far from my only issue with this game. The game is insanely buggy and crashed for me more than a few times. It's also very poorly optimized. Load zones take only about a half century to load anything if they don't just crash my game altogether. The NPCs in this game are sometimes unresponsive, as there's times where I decide to just shoot someone on the street and they just kind of stand there, stare at the body and do nothing, much like people in real life except real-life people will usually stand around recording ♥♥♥♥ happening with their iPhones while screaming "OH MY GOD OH MY GOD OH MY GOD!!!", which is something the borderline vegetative NPCs in this game are beyond incapable of doing. The chores feel really drawn out and not all that entertaining to do, and the map size is way too large so the game winds up turning into a walking simulator, which, when combined with the loading zone issues, was ultimately what turned me away from even trying to finish this dumpster fire. And don't even get me started on the scooter: A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Fisher-Price tricycle could handle better than that thing.I've heard talk that apparently the humor in the game might have been toned down so that RWS could have an easier chance at finding publishers due to obvious reasons, and although I can't say for certain whether or not this is true, I do agree that the humor in this game feels dumbed down to being a bizarre combination of sex jokes, toilet humor, memes, or just outright LOL XD Randumb stuff. There's also lots of bizarre references that don't work, either because they have no punchline (The Pigonea Virus and the Border Wall just sort of... exist. little to nothing is done with them) or because they are so bizarrely specific that unless you're in the know, you won't get it (Vince's Tiger King thing, Civvie, Postal 1 callbacks). Some people might find these elements amusing, but it definitely feels like a far cry from the give-no-♥♥♥♥♥ crude & cynical humor of this game's predecessors. It's almost like they're trying very hard to replicate what they did in Paradise Lost, but they take the ridiculous factor to such a point where it really dumbs down the game into being what is essentially nothing more than your average episode of modern Family Guy. Because being stupid, over-the-top and using poop fart butt jokes is what adults find funny in current year, right?If I had to say there was at least one thing I did like about the game, it was the Going Postal minigame. It was a nice little callback to Postal 97', and would've only been funner to play if the weapons didn't feel so bad to use. I've seen many of this game's loyalists use the counterargument "BUT POSTAL 2 WAS ALWAYS JANKY YOU ANGRY TRIGGERED ZOOMER LOL!!!!" which is a pathetic excuse to deflect criticism of the game because while Postal 2 might've been janky, it was both engaging and entertaining to play. Here, there's just neither. It just feels like a far-from-finished game that RWS shoved out the door, maybe for that epic funny "based" 4/20 release date, but who ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ knows. Overall, Postal 4 feels like a bizarre, almost schizophrenic mishmash of ideas made in a bizarre attempt to recapture the glory of the "Worst Game Ever", but failing miserably due to the many shortcomings of the confused writing and poor gameplay.And if you like this game and completely disagree with me, then good for you. That is absolutely fine. We can all coexist with differing opinions right? With all that said, I'd say if you're looking for a decent $40.00 game, or even just a good Postal game, this one is definitely NOT worth the price tag in its current state. At this point, I can safely say I've utterly lost hope that this game will become a decent product. As if the tumorous writhing mass of performance problems, gameplay problems, and writing problems wasn't bad enough, it seems that apparently a few of the developers have *shockingly* been going around deriding and disregarding the opinions of folks who don't like the game. Must be a tad bit sensitive about their labor of love, I suppose. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a longtime fan of the postal series (Full disclosure for disclosures sake, the developer and I follow each other on Twitter) Its still in a very rough state as its just been released as an alpha build, but this is one of the few devs I've bought Early Access from without a second thought. So if you get into it now, expect the full Jankiness that an alpha has to offer (Empty buildings, lack of optimization, lack of features (No police, saving, etc.) I will say that what is on display is promising. Tone-wise it seems like a return to form for RWS, Postal Dude just trying to make a living in a crazy world, rather than some psychodelic trip that Apocolypse Weekend or Paradise Lost was. Its a bit jarring that Postal Dude is no longer voiced by Rick Hunter, but Jon St John does a damn good job, and I have to say I like his take on an older sounding Dude running around in his bathrobe when he's not riding around in a rascal scooter.  The weapons on display aren't quite anything new but enough to still get that postal experiance. (The boomerang machete that can reduce a crowd of people into nothing but  chicken nuggets in a matter of seconds is there)Something I'd also like to go on a bit of a tangent on is that RWS knows how to load a game with popculture referances without them ever being obnoxious. Theres always been plenty of them in the Postal Series but its entirely possible to miss them all if you don't know where to look, and when you do find them it feels like a neat little detail and they feel like even when referancing real world things, they are still a part of the world itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, but I can't. Not as it is. I'll start with the positive. Game looks pretty good, Unreal was a good engine choice. There's a LOT to do, almost like they took time to add every little thing they came up with, occasionally to its detriment, but mostly to great effect (or as great as you'll get with Postal 4 standards.) The arsenal of weaponry looks great and feels great, that's all I can ask for. Humor is hit or miss but I prefer a swing and a miss to no attempt at all. I think this is where I have to transition into the bad though, the gore is an integral part of the Postal experience, and as it stands, I think Postal 2 has better gore. Not that there wasn't an earnest effort on RWS' part to make good gore, but the bodies lack proper dismemberment, and NPCs keel over in ragdoll after a few bullets to the legs. They did at least add shooting off limbs in a recent update, which is a good start, hopefully indicative of more to come? Then there's the matter of performance. There's no sugar coating it, its terrible. For a game running on Unreal, the only thing unreal about its performance, is how bad it still is 2 years post launch. I was very lenient about it for the couple years it was in EA, even post launch, but updates have come and gone with no significant changes in how well it runs. I play better looking games at 144 frames on my PC, and the Steam Deck runs better looking games at 60-90 fps. Speaking of the Steam Deck, for all my Deck gamers out there, this game's verified rating is a sham. I would say the claim that it "runs well" is just an outright lie. The game struggles to hold even 24 fps, going as low as 10 in some areas with the only fix being to leave that area. Lowering video settings does not help. This barely falls under "playable" let alone verified. Another thing I thought was worth mentioning is the "edge" factor. Original Postals were very edgy, from the original's infamous school level, to the sequel's Muslim representation. Nothing like that is present here. Its very much "safe edgy" that is accepted by the establishment and makes sure to not actually offend anyone. Its disappointing because Postal especially was always known for being offensive to someone, even including them in Postal 2 satirically. Even its namesake is rather provocative.All in all; the game is fun (for PC) for a little while, good time waster, but lacks in many departments. I really meant when I said I want to recommend it, especially since they have multiple dude voices including the amazing Rick Hunter, but its 40 whole stones and if you just want an edgy gorefest timewaster, then Postal 2 is probably the game for you. its often on sale for as low as $2.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is a POSTAL game and that's what makes it great. 7.5/10 on that standard you can tolerate alot of jank... like alot.So, now the shiny 1.0 has been released and is now to face the scrutiny of the general public...Where do we start?In terms of general knowledge for the game I'm deriving from my time with the early access and the current 1.0 build (Mon-Tue), and it's safe to say the game is solid-ish state that it's well justified the 1.0 title (to some extent). Performance and Graphics seems to have been somewhat improved compared to prior builds as things like loading screens don't cause my computer to ♥♥♥♥ the bed and have an CTD. There is an underlying issue with framerates being... wanting for further improvements, but that will supposedly be fixed to be more optimized in future subsequent patches and support down the line. What can be said comfortably is that it runs well depending on personal setups and game settings. (Mine runs an RTX 2060 Super with 16GB of RAM with High Settings framerate being 50s-60s) In terms of gameplay it play rather well things like gunplay compared to prior iterations of series feels good and has a fair amount (but limited) set of customization options such as ammo type, baton type, and optic choice (only between iron or red dot currently). I'd say if you played any FPS in the last few years that's been arcade-y or casual you'd probably be at home. However things like NPC interaction with the player is lacking as for the most part as they function that same as a GTA pedestrian, and while the game is as violent as you play there doesn't seems to be any opposing factions (ie. POSTAL 2 Protesters, Hillbillies, or Gimps) or even retaliation against you for just walking into their home and taking their ♥♥♥♥. Story-Wise this game is the deepest compared to prior game in the series, granted it's now as deep as puddle in a pot-hole but hey that deeper than what POSTAL 1,2, Weekend, and Lost ever had. If your looking for some greater meaning to life or even some ungodly revelation that would change your outlook on things... I'm afraid you are insane if your looking into a POSTAL game of all things to find that answer, as this story quite literally revolves around a dude just looking for his trailer and bouncing from town. Comedy-Wise this game is... abhorrently offensive, crude, and dated. Which is to be expected as this game is riddled with political commentary, meta-humor, and who can forget literal toilet humor. Humor is in the eye of the beholder so I will leave that as "It's aight." Extra Things to remark: - Third-Person Camera is here and though simplistic and janked... it's better than Parcel Service Between 2&4 by a whole mile.- Driving in this game feels okay, it's no racing game but you can't go wrong as you can use any one handed weapon.- The choice between three voice actors is a novel but welcomed choice as you can go Classic 2 or Modern 4. But who can forget Parcel Guy from not 3?All in all this game is pretty good for a 1.0 update/release as it does cover the things that POSTAL has been come to know for. I can't say it's for someone that is looking for simple edge and crass cynical humor, but for POSTAL fans who walk the fine line between Gungho Killer and Pacifistic Bystander it's most certainly a romp worth trying and getting... even if a few pieces like crazy NPC factions and interactions are missing from the game, or a map that has tons of interactive props, or doors that can be opened from both ways. Overall a solid 7.5/10 Score.Can't wait for them to earn that extra shiny .5 score to be a rounded 8/10 with optimizations and additions (if any).

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game back when there was only Monday to play. I've kept track of it as new content has been released and now that the game is finished......oh wait, it isn't finished. Sure there's five days worth of errands, but it's still buggy, load times are way too long, and many areas of the map are filled with empty buildings and rooms. My save games don't work so I have to start from the beginning which I wouldn't have a big issue with doing if it weren't for one big problem.It's boring.Very boring.Many of the errands aren't interesting- clearing out the sewer, three (including one side mission) that involved hosing things down (two fires, and one where you hose down piles of ♥♥♥♥), and just general stuff that honestly I can't remember because there is little of note. There is also little escalation as the days went on. In Postal 2 you would regularly piss off various groups, be it feminists or rednecks, and they would attack you from then on. Plus the police presence would step up as the game went on, reacting to the stuff you've been doing. Here there's zero escalation up until Don't get me wrong there are interesting things in there. The mission at the mall I enjoyed, as well as the one where you have to go install bidets. The voting mission was quite enjoyable too. But they're also joined with missions that had a drawback of some kind. The VR mission, for instance, was simply annoying. It looked like a lot of effort went into it too. Oh well.Plus of course you're going to be spending lots of time going between where the errands are to be carried out, through a mostly uninteresting map that- as already mentioned- isn't finished being filled. Clearly putting collectable dolls throughout the map was far more important. I did the 'find the paintings' errand and boy did that drag a lot, searching through uninteresting houses to find the paintings. I suggest finding a walkthrough that circles which houses have them in it to save time.It also isn't that funny. There is stuff that I found amusing- poking fun at cries of cultural appropriation was pretty good, but what's with all the poop and bidet jokes? Isn't there supposed to be at least some sort of attempt at satire? Postal 2 came in the wake of 9/11 and poked fun at a lot of the stuff that was happening around that time in regards to people's attitudes towards Islam. Couple that with poking fun at animal rights activists, and game violence protesters, and it- while being very low hanging fruit- actually had some sort of substance. Here it's just... gross for the sake of being gross. Which is neither funny nor interesting.*sigh*, I really wanted this to be good but honestly I just didn't find myself having fun while playing it. Maybe in a year when they actually fill out the world it *might* be interesting. It's doubtful though, as not even a large chunk of the main missions are that great. Because of that I just can't recommend people buy it

_childDocuments_.review: NEGATYWY------- Jeśli przyjmiemy, że wersja 1.0 to gra "gotowa" w 100%, to tutaj nadal mamy wersję 0.80 ;) - Tak - twórcy sami przyznali, że gra dostała nalepkę 1.0, ale nie jest jeszcze ukończona, ale muszę przyznać, że i tak jestem niektórymi niedokończonymi rzeczami zaskoczony.- Ilość błędów na chwilę obecną jest dość spora - od banalnej możliwości wyjścia poza mapę, oraz wpadnięcia w teren, do niewłaściwych ekranów ładowania (połowa gry, ja ja nadal mam "poniedziałek").- Parę rzeczy nie zapisuje się podczas gry - od kilku ustawień, po personalizację broni między wczytaniami gry. Gra nie pamięta, jaką amunicję masz załadowaną do strzelby i że na jej końcu w momencie zapisu znajował się kot.- Przedmioty kolekcjonerskie się respawnują po wczytaniu gry, co rozwala cały system zbierania.- Rozwalona ekonomia. Mam wciąż +6000$ i nie mam na co ich wydać. Broń praktycznie zawsze jest pełna.Nie jestem pewien, czy tak to miało funkcjonować.- Dużo budynków jest nadal pustych. Ale widać, że ilość przedmiotów i dekoracja wnętrz jest w tej odsłonie priorytetem.POZYTYWY------- Wyzwania są fajne - jeśli potrzebujesz zachęty, żeby niezobowiązująco siać zniszczenie, to ta jest idealna.- Humor. Specyficzny. Dziwny. Niepoprawny politycznie.- Dużo broni, wiele nowych pomysłów, ale widać też wpływ tego, jak rozwijał się Postal 2.- Dalsze wsparcie i oddanie twórców temu projektowi.Jeśli ludzie narzekają, że łatki są tak częste, że nie ma jak zagrać, bo gra się co chwilę aktualizuje, to chyba dobry znak.- Deweloperzy są niezależni - wydają grę sami.Nie sposób oszacować, jak dużą to ma wartość.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ENGNEGATIVES------- If we assume that version 1.0 is a 100% "finished" game, then here we still have version 0.80 ;) - Yes - the developers themselves admitted that the game got the 1.0 sticker, but it's not finished yet, but I must admit that I'm still surprised by some of the unfinished stuff.- The amount of bugs at the moment is quite large - from the trivial possibility of going outside the map, and falling into the terrain, to incorrect loading screens (halfway through the game, I still have "Monday").- A couple of things don't save while playing - from some settings, to weapon customization between game loads. The game doesn't remember what ammo you have loaded in your shotgun and that there was a cat on the end of it when you saved.- Collectibles respawn after loading the game, which breaks the whole collectibles system.- Broken economy. I still have +$6000 and nothing to spend it on. Weapons are practically always full.I'm not sure if this is how it was supposed to work.- A lot of buildings are still empty. But you can see that the amount of items and interior decoration is a priority in this installment.POSITIVE------- Challenges are fun - if you need an incentive to casually wreak havoc, this one is perfect.- Humor. Specific. Weird. Politically incorrect.- Lots of weapons, lots of new ideas, but you can also see the influence of how Postal 2 evolved.- The continued support and dedication of the developers to this project.If people are complaining that patches are so frequent that there's no way to play because the game updates every so often, that's probably a good sign.- The developers are independent - they release the game themselves.It's impossible to quantify how much value this has.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my opinion on the game being pretty negative, there's a lot here that has so much potential. Combat is fun, and the environment is very fun to explore-- That's basically what Postal is about. However, there's a lot that hinders these things.Having watched this game through development, I figured it would release in an unfinished state. Of course, that ended up being true, so I waited to buy the game. All of the following issues were present in the first hour or-so of playing, and even the obnoxious bugs happen pretty frequently. This game has been out far too long to be in the state it's in.I bought it yesterday, and was immediately met with extremely obnoxious bugs such as:1. The map breaks frequently and will not work until you save and reload.2. Any time you lose your weapons for any reason, the game will still show that you're holding a weapon when you're not, and will not let you continue attacking. Again, reloading your session is required to fix this.3. Falling through the terrain is somewhat commonplace.Of course, there are also some minor issues that aren't exactly complaint-worthy, such as:1. Art direction making it difficult to spot items that can be picked up, even with the sheen lootable items have.2. NPCs standing still and completely ignoring you when you attack them from even a short distance away.3. I think the camera is placed above the actual player "model," making everything feel weirdly small.4. Reflections are often broken; you only see Dude's hand, or nothing at all. Some reflections aren't even really reflections and look extremely off-putting. You can really see the issue with #3 when you do see Dude's model in a reflection.Not only are there numerous bugs (which I'm sure there are plenty more of beyond what I've listed), but there are just inherent problems with the game's design, characters, and plot that will forever prevent this game from living up to its predecessors. These flaws, however, are not bad enough to prevent me from recommending the game... Y'know, when it's in a finished state!  with the price tag it has. Maybe once the game is in a finished state, I could recommend it.I'll likely play the game through once and update with more bugs / issues as I go forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Some useless Background Information:I love you guys for making a new sequel of Postal!! <3 I felt back like I was the little 8-10 year old child again, who just got a cracked version of Postal 2 from a brother's friend, because it was indexed in Germany back in these days. (Of course I bought it when I got older and it was available DRM free on GoG ;) .)______________________________________________________________________________I just love the humoristic and satiric style of this piece of art! Of course i couldn't understand all of it, but atleast the essential parts as a kid and when I played it as a adult again, I just had a blast of laugther and entertainment, which was similar to GTA: Vice City or GTA: San Andreas.IMPORTANT:If you are new to this franchise u have to play Postal 2 at first or atleast wait till the game gets a little bit more stable and has more and better varied content, because otherwise you can't really see why this game has so much potential. Summary:If you are familiar with the franchise just buy it, it has the old quality from Postal II and the same satiric and harsh offensive humour you want and expect, when playing this type of game. _childDocuments_.review: Postal 4 is... okay. Below average for a game of it's age. There's not much of a reason to play it unless you're just a huge Postal fan like myself. I'll likely clock a lot of hours in this game, out of love for the series.If you've never played Postal 2, go buy that instead. It's a solid experience that over shadows this release, and very much holds up to this day. Postal 2's graphics are charming and contribute to a realistic atmosphere, which is impressive for a 2003 release. Postal 2's AI still holds up, and is batting in the same field as major triple A titles like GTA 4/5, the Fallout series, etc etc. Hell, I think Postal 3 outshines this title in many regards.Postal 4 is clearly a mess from the get go. I've counted an insane amount of bugs in the 3 hours I've played so far. NPCs talk to each other through walls, you can trigger objects through walls, the AI seems to lack any form of self preservation, and the achievements do not seem to work at all (maybe a steam bug, but I doubt it.) I'm sure there are way more glitches waiting for me as I complete this game. The humor isn't as clever, nor edgy, as previous titles. They recycled a lot of the assets from previous titles, which isn't out of the norm for RWS, but I feel like that's the one of the few things that makes P4 feel somewhat like a Postal game.I just can't help but feel empty when I play Postal 4. Postal 4 is exceptionally good at making you crave Postal 2. I wanted to love P4, but I feel we would have been better off with another Postal 2 DLC. Please RWS, consider releasing more DLC for Postal 2.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very important to remember what this is - this is not a complete game. Hell, it's barely even a competent experience. It's a launching point, designed to help fund the development of the game in the future. Most people will not be okay with that. If that's you, stop buying early access games.PROS:- Unreal Engine 4, upgraded over the older UE2 used in Postal 2- Engine seems to mostly replicate features in Postal 2 competently, polish is missing and content isn't there, but the framework is there, functioning, and easily able to be built on.- Same devs as Postal 2, so none of that Postal 3 garbage.CONS:- Really isnt much to do. That's to be expected, this is a super mega-early build.- Reused assets from Postal 2, see above line- What is there is glaringly unfinished - multiple holes in the environment, some assets don't load, performance is horrendous given what is being rendered, etc.- No save functionality yet- Minor bugs, visual and gameplay impacting, again the content is super earlyBasically, if you love Postal and want more, and you want to support RWS, go for it, you get it for cheaper and get the experience of telling the devs how broken their ♥♥♥♥ game is and them responding to your emails telling you to drink their piss. What is here is a competent vision of the future - weapons work more or less the same they do in Postal 2. AI works more or less the same they do in Postal 2. Level design, audio, core gameplay loop, it's all here and is a great place to build on to add content and polish up and clean up over time. But it is not a "fun" or "compelling" game by any stretch of the imagination.If you are looking for ANY form of experience involving even a slightly playable game, go away. This isn't for you. That will come with time, and hey, even if it doesn't, i'm just glad I was able to give the devs more money cause I like what they do and want to support that. They could have done a "this does nothing but give us money" DLC for Postal 2 and I would have bought that as well.Looking forward to the future, and even if all you guys do is run off with my money, oh well, at least I was able to give you more money than the cheap sale price I paid for Postal 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Postal 4 is still a highly unfinished and flawed game. The AI has massive problems at times, there are quite a few small grafics glitches here or there and some of the mechanics still don’t work properly or not at all.that’s not to say that Postal 4 is bad or unplayable, far from it. The game is no visual powerhouse but it looks decent. Due to it‘s unrefined technical status it is a pretty demanding game when maxed out, but if you find your sweet spot for the video- and performance settings, it delivers at least solid, stable 30 FPS while still looking good enough. Be prepared for a couple of crashes though, but nothing serious.however, even though it’s a big leap forward again in comparison to that worthless piece of junk that is postal 3, postal 4‘s gameplay is not quite a return to postal 2‘s form yet. the gunplay may be the best in the whole series but on the other hand the missions are quite boring, sometimes very vague and lack creativity. the jokes and satire, which were among postal 2‘s biggest strengths, limit themselves to simple, tame, childish and unfunny toilet humor here for the most part. Last but not least Edensin, the town were postal 4 takes place, feels lively enough, but apart from the main missions and maybe a handful of sidequests there is literally nothing else to do, so you won’t get more than maybe 7 or 8 hours out of this. the fact that this game still lacks a big chunk of content two years after its initial early access release doesn’t help in this regard either: at the time of this review „friday“, (the final chapter of the game) is still missing.If this would be the final state of the game it would be a 3/8 at best. Neither does it have the downright sick, twisted and unsettling premise and shock value of the first postal game, nor does it have the creativity, vast scope and crazy humor of the second plus it is still buggy as fakk. But after Postal 3 turned out to be one of the worst games i‘ve played in years, Postal 4 is a definitive step in the right direction again and if the developers manage to add some more content, iron out the bugs and realize Postal 4‘s full potential, it could actually be a pretty good game. At the moment though, It‘s current price tag (30 Euros) is way overpriced. If you consider buying Postal 4, wait until the last chapter is released and instead get Postal 2 first, which is a completely finished, truly great game for half the money.EDIT AFTER "FRIDAY" UPDATE:So after finishing the game little more than a month after the release of the "Friday" Update, unfortunately things didn't go that well with the latest content update:I got the impression that instead of being noticably improved, the technical condition of the game seemed to have gotten severly worse. While running with at least somewhat stable 30 fps on nearly maxed out settings before, the game now constantly dipped below 30 fps, often even into single digits, with severe stuttering. I experienced significantly more crashes, too, especially during the endgame. I don't know if it caused some problems that I used my old savegames from the end of Thursday, to continue where i left off, instead of playing through the whole game from the beginning again, but wether this was the case or not, Postal 4 definitely went downhill on the technical side with the Friday Update, at least on my system.Another problem that still persists is the atrocious AI. It is still a butchered mess and makes the enemies just randomly run around like headless chickens, only occasionally stopping to shoot at you, or just plain doing nothing at all. Even though the weapons themselves are decent and fun to use, gunfights are still annoying and not fun at all due to the erratic and super-stupid AI.The three final Friday missions are as boring and uninspired as anything else we've seen so far during Monday to Thursday and the mission design strongly feels like the devs just wanted to finally get this over with. All three missions are basically the same fetch quest: Just go there, get whatever you are supposed to get and shoot everybody (or everything) who stands in your way. The lackluster missions make the final chapter feel really drawn out. After that the game even makes you fight four bosses and you have to cross the whole town again to get to each boss encounter. To make matters worse, the final boss fight seems to be severly glitched and it screwed up three of my Autosaves. I actually had to fight the final boss two times, because after the first time the severe grafics glitches in the broken autosaves made it impossible for me to complete the game. Furthermore I noticed some more small flaws that for some reason slipped by the first time I played Postal 4, for example the characters not moving their lips while talking in the cutscenes, or the lacking variety of enemy skins during the missions.Literally the only improvement I noticed was that the game now finally has a proper way to put a marker on your map screen and the mini-map finally guiding you there like a navi. If I remember correctly, you always had to open the map screen every few metres to see how to navigate to your current objective before, while now you can finally just mark your destination on the map and follow the dotted line on the mini map. But this "improvement" might have been already present in prior releases and i just forgot about it, but oh well.I really hoped that there would be a significant improvement of the whole game with the "Friday Update", which now has "finished" the game in a sense that it now has a completed story, but unfortunately it still lacks a lot of polish. The game still has much potential to be realized and I really hope that it will happen. With its outlandish premise and oddly likable protagonist there are many things to like about Postal 4 and it makes it something really different within the shooter genre. But sadly, even with a complete story now, Postal 4 is far from finished and there is still a lot of work to do. As it is, the game is almost ruined by its poor technical state and it is not worth the 30 bucks they currently want for it at all, so I'd still take Postal 2 over this any day. I wouldn't write Postal 4 off just now, but I'd seriously recommend to wait for a 50% discount, at least as long as the game is not properly patched up.__________________________________________________________________________POSTAL 4: NO REGERTSGenre: First-Person-Shooter / Open-World-SandboxRelease: Q4 2019     ( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I'm a big postal fan, I own and have played all of the games, including Postal 3. I'll also say that one of the things I find most fun to do in my free time is playing scuffed game jam games made by people in a week. Still, while being a big fan of laughing at ♥♥♥♥, having a broken sense of humor, and being able to feel something related to happiness even throughout my playthroughs of Postal 3, this game is at it's core an unfunny, infantile, horrid, disgusting badly programmed game, and to this day that only game I bough, or even got for free, that was unable to get me a quick laugh, even with all the care and no lick of expectation.  The movement and gun play is slightly better than Postal 2's, not to say that's an achievement, as no one plays Postal for it's gameplay, but the weapons do feel better to use, most have improved animations and their power ups are interesting. The dollar store Duke Nukem dub sounds very bad, Corey Cruise does a fine replacement of Rick Hunter and they should have just recurred to him when Rick was unavailable, but you can't complain about having the choice of which of the 3 dudes you like best.  I was unable to finish this game in any of the chances I gave it, not only due to the bad performance and minutes long load times, but due to it feeling more like a chore than a pastime. I specifically despise the little tasks scattered around the map, and I don't think the rampages are fun either.  This game can only be compared to Postal 2, as it's a rough recreation of that made by skull mask wearing morbidly obese 12 year olds. Postal 3 could also be compared as it was awful in every way this is, but due to being different in terms of gameplay to both, it still was a more refreshing experience in the similar nonsense world of Postal.  The humor is insufferable, there is no dark humor at all, no minorities are oppressed, there is no subtle racism, the highly relevant social justice warriors in present times are just very lightly attacked, there is no reference to cancel culture, no opposition to anything, no one is offended and the awful reviews the game received, while proudly displayed to imitate Postal 2, make no sense without this offensive factor this game doesn't have. With all the good taken out, what remains is poop fart funny jokes, and a lot of these. Actually, mostly these. This game has a creepy addiction to feces, and toilets, and toilets filled with feces. There is also that Krotchy clit clone, the Postal Dude is wearing a pink robe. Oh! and what about that wheel menu which lets you do the super wacky funny twerk animation and stare at it, wow!!! All this contributes to the third grade humor feel this game has.   The Postal Dude is also a shadow of what he once was, in fact, nothing of him remains in this game. Taking place after the events of Paradise Lost, it is no surprise that after  he would be happier, but this jolly wacky man does not conform to his past apparitions, and after playing him in the past games, it's not so funny seeing the same twisted edgelord picking up a marker and writing in a cardboard sheet that he would suck ♥♥♥♥ for money, this is by the way the first that we see of him, and it never gets old as it never was funny to begin with.  The atmosphere and general vibe of Postal 2 is a fat part of what makes it great, and this game has a completely different one, it's in contrast to it's ancestor not creepy, macabre, and edgy, which relates to the first game and gives good contrast to be in the mind of the same twisted psychopath that is the Postal Dude, but now with the task not to murder, but to do mundane, simple tasks which turn into minority induced madness or chaos caused by the Dude's bad luck, and all that while giving the player the choice to be either a devilish murderer or a pacifist (this choice is also present in this game, but with all this added dialogue and cutscenes it no longer feels the same, because the Dude acts, as previously stated, just as a goofy middle aged poor victim of society). While you walk through the cities of this game you hear no weird ambiance like the first two games, you don't question anything as it's all just gaily riding a mobility scooter (hilarious) through a grey empty city, only to sometimes stumble open the few interesting interiors in the obligatory missions. There is nothing worthwhile to explore outside the main story line that I could find, while in Postal 2 you had lots of areas you didn't even need to go through in the entirety of the game, as well as the entirety of Tora Bora.    Seeing the game updates go by gives me certain hope for the sequel that this one day might be playable, and who could say, maybe nearly as fun as the second game if only the sandbox aspect, putting the story aside, is taken into consideration. However, I get no itch to try the game and see the newly added improvements, as the core is and always will be the same. I couldn't say everything I hate about this game in the wall of text, and I'm sure there are many other things to hate in the other half of this game I couldn't bare playing.  I will probably only give this another choice when the steam workshop update comes out, as without it's hideous story and potty humor, given that they improve performance, it would serve as a decent stable base with an updated engine for community modding. Otherwise, no matter how much they polish the game from now on, the main story will remain pitiful, the map uninteresting, and the art style ugly. The Postal Dude also became a twitter trans pride progressive furry libertarian reddit-user icon, which is not all this game's fault, but sucks nonetheless.I regret everything.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly fun throwback to the early 2000's. It embraces it's wacky, crude, and outrageous humor with unapologetic delight. Not for those who are easily offended, or lack a sense of humor, this game takes the franchise back to Postal 2, with a brand new city and shiny new graphics. And just like Postal 2, how violent The Dude is rests solely in the hands of the player. You can choose to be a pacifist, or be a homicidal maniac. While it is sad that Rick Hunter retired from voicing The Dude, Jon St. John (famous for voicing Duke Nukem) does a fantastic job taking over the role. As of the writing of this review, the game is still in "Early Access" and thus still under development. This means that there are still some bugs, and areas of unfinished game. However, the devs are constantly working to update and improve the game, with lots of new content and bug fixes. If the term "Early Access" makes you hesitant, then wait until the game is finished. However, if you need a new Postal fix (and one the helps further push the bad taste of Postal 3 out of your mouth) then I highly recommend getting Postal 4. I've enjoyed my time with it thus far, and look forward to seeing the final product.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- Get Postal 2 + Apocalypse Weekend and wait a few more years.I've been playing it off and on for the last three years of development (GOG), watching it grow and morph into the kind of game Postal fans have been wanting in a sequel. Underneath all the jank, bugs, crashes, performance issues, lack of polish and questionable design decisions is a good game, but not a great one. The challenges are extremely lame, the world is hollow and the majority of the missions don't have the same ramp up of stakes and insanity like they used to. Some do, don't get me wrong, but there's far too many underwhelming tasks with so little pay off it beggars belief. That escalation into insanity is, at it's core, one of the key elements of Postal 2. The inter-connective gameplay elements is there, but the world isn't as exciting to use it against like before. Going Postal is fun, but it never feels like the citizenry are as crazy, or often crazier, than the player playing the protagonist.It has a lot of potential to surpass as a sequel, it's just not there yet. Postal 2 remains one of the greatest video games to ever exist that a lot of people can't understand because they shy away from the ugliness of it. The sandbox you get to play in is as deranged as the player can and often is encouraged to be. It has high replay value, it has grit and flagrant commentary of the time period its set in, a nasty world full of nasty people, extremely creative, and clever re-use of connecting game mechanics. Postal 4: No Regerts is aspiring to be the next step, and while it's stumbling in the right direction, it has ways to go.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR it's an okay game that doesn't live up to it's predecessor, with lots of technical issues.This review will make many comparisons to postal 4's predecessor postal 2 (don't ask about postal 3.) And i will be refraining from mentioning the frequent glitches, long load times and some general jankiness as it is an alpha or beta or whatever.The main thing you'll notice about postal 4 compared to postal 2, is the increase in graphical fidelity. I say fidelity not quality in this instance because it leads to multiple gameplay related issues. Doors that you can interact with are not easy to differentiate form doors you can't, and weapons and items are much harder to differentiate from the surrounding environment, due to the fact that they are seemingly given the same amount of graphical detail. This could probably be remedied by increasing the time of the sheen flash or decreasing the interval at which the sheen triggers.postal 4 has slightly bigger open world areas! But much like real life, most of it is taken up by parking lots, inaccessible areas, and empty space. To help mitigate the long travel times the developers have added mobility scooters dotted around the map. these have around 2 times the speed of the postal dude(who can sprint now B.T.W.), but I'd rather just have a closer together open world. Now this isn't the  of issues, but the problem for some bewildering reason also persists in interior levels. There are lots of large empty pointless rooms and hallways which, even with the minimap I still manage to get lost in. In around 1 out of every 3 rooms there are a few health/ammo and/or armor pickups, and there are enemies in most of them, but everything just feels so pointlessly large, empty, and surface level.The weapons and combat in the game have also been given a modern™ touch, with reloading and sprinting now prominent mechanics. Most of the weapons from postal 2 have been added, which work mostly the same. Some new weapons have also been added, i like these new additions, but also have some comments.The revolver: very nice! although I think that it should still be able to target people who you look away from.The Rattler:   It's a good weapon, headshots instakill most enemies, but does not pull enemies to you unless they die making it just like a short range machete(which has been nerfed pretty hard B.T.W.)Squirt Gun: shoots fire, piss or water(apparently, i have not found the water jug.)the game makes frequent use of cutscenes and comic like videos. The game's humor seems even more immature/gross than previous, making frequent use of feces, and innuendos in main questline missions. it also seems shorter than postal 2, although that might just be because the experience is somewhat forgettable. Seems to be lacking almost any actual satire.it's lacking secrets and fun secret areas right now, but that's probably due to the fact that it's in betaand fun secrets are a secondary. there are a few, but a far cry from the original.EDIT: I forgot to mention the U.I.! It sucks! weapon selection uses a clunky and inefficient radial menu, and there's no way to see all your weapons at once! I do like the way you can select modes/ammo types for weapons though, i just wish there was a better way to do it.Edit 2: I have even more to say! I like the new voice actor, but again have a few comments. The postal 2 voice actor delivered almost all of his lines with an underlying tone of anger/disgust, with exceptions for throwing the machete, killing someone, or using explosives. I did not feel this present in my time with this game. You can really hear the difference in the way he asks people to sign his petition. Postal II's dude has a sense of "just sign my petition already you moron" even when asking for the first time, and even though the dialogue is seemingly more neutral. Postal 4 has more of just a bland delivery I think, only getting an angry/annoyed tone when he has to ask multiple times. I think this might be what the deves were going for though, as he seems more neutrally stupid in the cutscenes that he is in, not just motivated by anger or annoyance. Which i think is even more justified in this game as his ♥♥♥♥ is actively stolen, as opposed to just having to do chores. This creates a stark divide between the cutscene postal dude and the actions that postal dude takes during gameplay. (I am also against cutscenes in general though, as I do not feel that they do a good job of utilizing the medium that they are contained in.)overall, not too good in it's current state, wait for the full game to release, and i'll update my review on request. Unless you want to support the development of the game, I don't recommend it. lacking the "edge"pretty generic 4/10 (5 is an average game 10 is a perfect game.(there are no 10s))if you disagree with any points i have made please leave them in the comments, which i have conveniently enabled. I am interested in hearing other opinions on this topic.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: 3 years laterAfter the poor Early Access release and reception, here's what happening.RWS started throwing a bunch of content updates that nobody ever asked for. Meanwhile, people started getting increasingly more vocal about the blatantly obvious lack of graphical optimization and polish. This resulted in several dozen arguments, and most of them ended with the person voicing the games' future getting banned on the Hub, because Zeron couldn't get off his high-horse, no matter how constructive the feedback was.Simply put, if your opinion does not line up with the devs' narrative, you'll be either shamed into silence or banned, citing, "yOu dIDn'T pOSt yOUr sYStEm sPEcs, tHuS wE cAN't hELp", despite them being fully aware that the game runs like garbage for the past 3 years, with marginal improvements that simply can't be felt, even on present day hardware. In other words, I and other people was treated as if we were trolling, but problem is - since they  the fact that the game has optimization issues (even if not word-for-word) - this makes the devs come off as hypocritical as well.They will try really hard to convince you that the game running @ 60-70 fps in 2023 is decent, despite the game being a complete technical mess even 3 years post-EA launch. Everyone who didn't agree with them, was subsequently banned for refusing to support this laughable excuse of a game even symbolically. Any and all traces of their past contribution are simply removed to erase the memory of them in the P4 Hub. They really tried rubbing in that I was comparing apples to oranges, but in practicality, it was another form of their silence-shaming rhetoric.I bought the game at day 1, because it was dirt-cheap, but if I bought it today even on a Postal 2-style 90% discount, I would still feel robbed. Why? Because the game is a trainwreck that pales in comparison in almost every single way to Postal 2, its' expansions and more importantly, the workshop content. The game looks like potato and should run as such, and in essence is trying to leech off of Postal 2's decades of work and fame.Yet I can run many last of the last two generation games on max settings at 120 fps at worst. Dare I say it, even Postal 3 is better than this game in certain aspects (and that game has also gotten community trearment the past few years).Thus, given the issues highlighted above,Do NOT buy P4 at full price. Or at all until it gets an adequate tier of polish.You're better off supporting the company with Postal 2 purchases, but know that your money will go towards a product that is still a mess 3 years later and may never get actually finished to an enjoyable degree.Oh and yeah - everything I posted here will probably be marked as hyperbole.
