_childDocuments_.review: This game is bad. REALLY bad. After Postal 2 which was amazing, these games have been atrocious and unplayable. This game crashes. It's buggy. There's Lamborghinis and vehicles everywhere, but you're stuck driving boring motorized carts. I don't mind running around and exploring, but people are silent and there's really nothing to do except find random Krotchy dolls on the floor. There's food trucks and businesses that are empty and you can't interact with anything. The map is way bigger but there's not enough ways to get around so you're walking forever looking at a mountain and dirt for 10 minutes. The cinematics are cheap motion graphics and don't use in-game graphics. The story isn't about the Postal dude's day, but rather these lame characters with bad voice acting that you don't care about and annoy you all the time when you're trying to progress in missions.In Postal 2 you used to be able to break into houses and take guns, ammo and health with hopes that no one would see you. You could shoot your way into a bank vault and steal tons of cash with secret exits to avoid cops. Businesses had people behind the counter asking if you needed assistance. There was lots to explore. You used to go into a hospital that was full of NPCs that talked and you could piss into a machine that'd heal you up. If you go into a hospital in this game however, it's empty and baron with no interactivity or people of any kind. Just random chicken and pizza laying around in a quiet room. When your day was done in Postal 2, it would teleport you home. Not in this game. You have to drive a cart for 10 mins to get to a fast travel station. Then you have to walk another 10 minutes after you fast travel to finish your day. My game jumped from Monday to Wednesday. Where's Tuesday? In P2, the missions were silly and the tasks were simple but fun since the game threw funny curve balls at you. You even observed Gary Coleman going mad with a deagle shooting cops at a mall book signing! It was so good! What happened? This game lost all of it's everything. And the loading screens! GAH, the loading screens!! They're everywhere and they take ages to load. GTA has a map the size of Los Angeles and it doesn't have loading screens and that came out in 2013! What were they thinking?!This game feels dead a very incomplete. Feels like they spent all the time making the faces look good and tinkering graphics. Where's the game?! This game just officially launched but it still feels like it's in an alpha state. I don't think this game will ever get close to it's older brother that came out in 2003. Big oofs on this one. Do your research online and look at the ratings. They're all right. I wanted to believe that this would be good after they had time to tinker with it after it first released in 2019. After 3 years, it's still stinks worse than the moldiest Krotchy you can imagine. After 5 hours, it's time to delete and run through Postal 2 again so I can remember when these games were good.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been "playing" this since like janky alpha 0.1 or 0.2 and this release version hardly feels improved over those early versions. Before I was willing to forgive it because it was "janky alpha" but it's been literally years at this point and now it's being sold as a "finished" product I guess so it's time to give my unsolicited impression of it.I've been a fan of Postal 2 ever since release and I'd rank it among my all time favorite games. I don't play it as often as I used to (countless hours and days spent playing the old CD version) but I did complete a full playthrough of Postal 2 plus A Week In Paradise last year and as I've gotten older it's interesting to see what has aged well and what hasn't (a surprising amount has) and to see how Postal 4 is shaping up in comparison.So I'll just get into it.Postal 4 runs so bad I would be embarrassed if this were my "finished" product, and after as much time as it has had in development, and for as empty and static the world is, in conjunction with the 2003-esque loading zones that the world is broken into, this lack of performance optimization is unacceptable. It's not even a matter of low frame rates but that it also varies wildly with no rhyme or reason. It'll bob up and down from 20fps to 120fps in the same area, sometimes even in the same scene! Even in those rare moments where my frame rate is 60 or more it doesn't feel smooth, there's a consistent micro stutter in addition to the fluctuating, low frame rate. This has been the biggest hurdle to me playing this game for any period of time longer than 20 minutes. Putting the awful performance aside, exploring the world itself has been disappointing. This is being made with I think Unreal Engine 4 and yet everything is static and fixed in place like it's Unreal Engine 2 still. So much of the environment is just static dressing with no interaction it actively detracts from the experience. Go drop a grenade in a random living room and marvel at how not a single thing gets thrown around or breaks. See that empty bucket, or basketball sitting on the ground? Run into it and it'll stop you in your tracks because it is an immovable object. For as many NPCs as there are meandering around in some areas, everything is empty and lifeless. Many buildings and dwellings are empty, as most NPCs are meandering in the streets and the NPCs (and the Postal Dude) look like dolls, which fits with the static dollhouse-like world they inhabit, I guess.The humor and writing is dire. I'm not saying Postal 2 is some ironic masterpiece, it definitely has some ♥♥♥♥ in it that has aged horribly, but it felt earnest in it's attempts. I think as time went on and Postal 2 developed this reputation of being "the worst game ever"  the way people began to engage with it started to change. The early 2000's parody's of various groups became satire and the point of it became to punch at various groups for the sake of punching rather than just laughing at some ridiculous ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The clownish parts became emphasized and the more "sinister" tones of the setting became absorbed into this. Postal 4 feels like a fan-game that's focused on one part of a two part recipe. The Postal Dude is now the sometimes violent straight man in a wacky world instead of the disgruntled psycho in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, absurd world. P2 Postal Dude is your weirdo loner cousin nobody really talks to at the family gatherings and P4 Postal Dude is your loser divorced uncle. Sure, you don't want to be around either of them, but it's different flavors of repulsiveness. I don't want to say Postal 4 is the flanderized version of Postal but it's toeing that line. It's like the devs are writing a sequel to a greatest hits album. Postal 2 was a lot of regular, mundane situations suddenly spinning out of control with the introduction of some outside variable and there's a build up over the course of the game in the absurdness. As far as I can tell there's nothing like "Go cash your paycheck at the bank" with an actual line you can wait in to do so until bank robbers break in. In Postal 4 it's just clown ♥♥♥♥ from the get go. The game feels unfocused . The updates are seemingly random collections of whatever the devs have thought up that month in addition to bugfixes with no improvements to performance ever. The environments feel unfinished, half the cutscenes are animated ingame while the other half (including the opening cinematic to the game!) are literally just moving pictures. The gameplay loop feels lackluster and mediocre. I could not give less of a ♥♥♥♥ about collectible dolls, chasing after stray dogs... I mean the missions are as boring as watching paint dry. I don't know if they get any more interesting or better in the latter half of the game because as I've already mentioned the awful performance has made it unbearable to actually play this game in addition to it's other shortcomings. They added in multiple versions of the Postal Dude's voice acting to choose from, which is cool no doubt but the fact that something like that was just added in this late in development while there is so much other, much more important work that needs to be done kinda paints a picture to me where maybe there isn't some grand plan in place and the devs are instead winging it and going with whatever sounds cool at the moment. I mean, ffs, they literally just released a 20gb "content update" today that added... a sledgehammer and rubber mallet... a help section in the menu.... dogs can randomly pee... cops confiscate your stuff upon arrest... hate groups like in Postal 2... more bugfixes... no performance optimizations.... police helicopters.... Why is this update 20gb? And this is supposed to be some big content update? Why hasn't the opening cutscene been updated with an actual cutscene yet? What is even going on at RWS?Do the devs plan on just updating this game forever? For as much updating as this game gets it still feels lackluster compared to Postal 2, not just technically or gameplay wise, but in just the sheer amount of content available to the player to engage with. I assume at some point they'll have to stop working on Postal 4. What state will the game be in then? This still feels like a janky alpha and it honestly kinda makes me mad a little that they're selling this as a finished product. This isn't even a "he-he this is a so bad on purpose it's good" type situation, Postal 4 is just straight up mediocre. I had more but I've been writing this so long it's getting hard keeping it straight. tl;dr: Buy and play Postal 2 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Postal 2, but this just doesn't hit the mark at all. I get that this game is made by an indie studio on a low budget but releasing 1.0 of this game now is a joke. This is primarily because of bugs and terrible performance issues. Whilst I believe there's a very good game under here it is obvious that there has been little done to fix obvious performance issues. It is terribly optimised, running on a high end rig I rarely get higher than 60FPS in all areas of the game, and when settings are changed no difference is made to performance. This is a fundamentally bad looking game and therefore it doesn't deserve such a hit on performance. I get that the issues are probably CPU bound but still, does this game really do enough to bring my 8700K to its knees? I would argue not. After playing just over an hour of the game it now refuses to launch and crashes on the splash screen. This is supposed to be a completed game, and the fact it is out of early access means it is promoted as one. I get that the devs are going to continue updating the game but I cannot at all recommend it in its current state, unless to support the developers. It is wrong to pull this game out of early access. Even when it comes to its content I would argue that Postal 4 lacks personality, the map is too big for what the devs are trying to do and there is so much empty space. Whilst the missions are packed with personality, the majority of the environments are stock textures and objects obviously bought from asset packs. There are whole trailer parks that are empty of all content and personality. Some buildings have shining white rooms where there are no objects or shadows. The AI is embarrassingly bad, they won't complain if you break into their houses and their aim is absolutely ridiculous. Enemies will wipe you out in this game with hitscan guns. None of these issues appeared in Postal 2, a 19 year old game. The game's NPCs are a similar affair when it comes to creativity, most non plot related NPCs have voice lines lifted from Postal 2, without any re recording or remastering and stands out like a sore thumb in contrast with the rest of the voice work. Yes, postal 2 is buggy but this is just ridiculous, I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A boring, buggy, mediocre at best game with barely a fraction of the edge, vulgarity, player freedom, and general fun factor of Postal 2. Any fun to be had with this game lasts about five minutes before it gets dull, due in part to the game having a open world with practically nothing to do other then kill NPCs and do missions, and the player doesn't have much incentive to explore said open world because it's not jam-packed with weapons and items that serve as rewards for exploration, which was a big part of what made Postal 2 fun. The player is often forced to play the game a certain way instead being free to play how they want like Postal 2. One such is example is Postal 4's the scooter racing mission, where the player is forced to participate in the race, and is permitted to use weapons to take out NPC racers. The comedy did get a few laughs out of me, but it lacks the shock humor, dark humor, and much of the satirical aspect of Postal 2, and relies too much on sex jokes and pop culture references. At times, it feels like it wasn't even made by the same developers as Postal 2, but rather, it was made by a different developer that was asked to make a Postal game by a publisher, which is ironically what basically happened with Postal 3, a game that RWS and much of the fan-base has actively disowned. To close, don't buy Postal 4. If you want to support the developers, buy Postal 2, or Postal Redux, or Postal: Brain Damaged, or buy the merchandise on their website, but don't Postal 4.TL:DR This game is a worse version of Postal 2. _childDocuments_.review: Very recently and for no real reason I decided to play the game Postal 2, had a good time with that. when I completed Postal 2, Apocalypse weekend, and Paradise Lost I was thoroughly satisfied with all of them. I appreciated those games for the unique experience they provided. A few days later I began browsing steam and saw Postal 4, after reading a few reviews I came to the conclusion that despite the bugs and overall janky-ness I was warned about I'd give it a shot anyway.   In the beginning of the game everything was going ok. It ran well enough and there was still much to explore. After a while I came to the realization that the world created for this installment Is nowhere near what paradise was in postal 2. Despite attempts at humor ingrained in much of the world building everything is bland. There's rarely more than meets the eye anywhere, Granted I've yet to go through the game with a fine toothed comb but after 10 hours you'd think I'd have found something right? In Postal 2 it didn't take more than a quarter hour for me to find myself invading the home of the middle eastern convenience store clerk and fighting off his army of wives. But in Postal 4 a casual playthrough won't grant you those moments of absurdity, I'm not even sure they're in the game at this point.   The combat in this game is boring at best and infuriating at worst. I can't really provide specific examples without spoiling parts but I'll give you bullet points which you should take as warnings.* The Dam* Doors* Dogpiles* Psychic ability to locate the player   The combat is made more boring by the fact that in 90% of cases it seems that the only destructible body part is the head, In postal 2 I thought it was interesting that with a bladed weapon you could remove whichever part of the body you aimed for, In 4 I may have cut off 3 hands total compared to more heads than I can count. on that note I remember that in 2 when NPCs where injured to the point of staying on the ground but still being alive, they'd show clear signs of pain and have voicelines to match. In 4 if you were to remove a limb the NPC is dead immediately. This may seem like a particularly dark note but I think showing that suffering inflicted by the player is one of the most important aspects in not only believability, but also because it gives the player a reason to reflect on their actions. In a game with no consequences I found that specific feature to be shocking, It made me feel dirty, and wrong. Its important to have things like that.   Something else I Noticed here is that there were very few parts of the game, outside of the missions that i felt like I had enough ammo to actually "Go Postal". I didn't really have the desire to do that but I thought it was interesting enough to add. In addition to limited ammo pickups there also seems to be fewer health or body armor items scattered around the map than in Postal 2. This of course makes the late game slightly more difficult.   If you are hoping for an experience similar to postal 2, honestly this is probably the closest your going to get. In many ways it seems like steps were taken in the wrong direction. That being said, I think if I went into this game without the expectations I set based on Postal 2 I would have enjoyed it much more. In its current state I wouldn't recommend you play this. There are still a lot of bugs, crashes, and other things that need to be ironed out first. Other than that it feels like a lot less love was put into the open world than I'd expect, Last time I found Osama hiding in a hidden sewer complex because i was interested in poking around. This time they force you to fast travel on Monday and hide one specific part of the map behind invisible barriers. seriously if I don't get to see whats behind that little iron bar door in the opening in the rock wall SOMEBODY is going to receive a strongly worded letter.

_childDocuments_.review: - DudePostal has never been a pretty series, although it was always simple to understand and deeply tied to the mundane. Postal 4 has divorced from this and gone on a drinking spree; Not at any point are your objectives easy to understand, nor are you provoked to act out and be creative with your arsenal. Your character behaves like a complete pushover both mechanically and in the narrative, from start to finish, regardless of how many people you decapitate; it is painfully boring as result.Fundamentally, this game is actually awful and not in the expected way. Even beyond what's tolerable for jank in this series, Postal 4 does not feel like a Postal game. It feels like an extremely (and I mean extremely) dumbed down version of . To help you understand what this means, here's a quick rundown of each main game in the series:In case you haven't noticed, Postal 4 wanted to be the odd one from the bunch. And it managed to, it's not very good.It's borderline unplayable; glitches are a common sight, soft locks are omnipresent, performance is deplorable. Crashes are almost as exciting as the actual game and happen quite often.The map is bigger, but now there are extremely long paths to traverse with nothing in them; I have not personally found a way to traverse them fast enough in my 10 hours of play. There are no actual vehicles you can drive, only speed capped mobility scooters with different colors. I expected there'd be some sort of drug that helped, but no. Somehow, there are still load zones exactly like those from 2003 in Postal 2 - just in case you think you're going too fast.You have random "minigame" points around the map that challenge you to "kill 10 people with a shotgun" or run a miniscooter course. Collectibles. Again, this is a painful amount of effort that just makes the game look like a bootleg  .The inventory has grown larger with numerous redundant items like 3 different types of Junk food or Spray cans and Mops that you can carry. Navigating it by the end of the week is painful. Using items like health pipes takes like a 4 second hold down press which is very bothersome.As mentioned earlier, the presence of effective non-lethal weaponry and ammo is basically a discouragement from doing the one thing the game had to do; provoke you to go postal. Normally I'm all for choice, but between having a Postal game where not going mad is encouraged I'd much rather just go play a more sane game.As of currently, there are only 3 difficulty settings compared to the dozens of difficulties in Postal 2, and none of them are equivalent to the POSTAL difficulty which would give every pedestrian a gun and instant aggro towards you. So, replayability is sorely limited.There was an obsession by the team with detailed art assets and interior design, resulting in highly decorated stores and houses. But, there are usually no people or things to buy or even interact with. This involves things like entering a Porcelain store and finding out you're not able to break a single vase.Of course, this needs not mean the game will be pretty! The game is super fugly. Even if you find the place to pick a different set of clothes, your character will still wear their purple bathrobe in every cutscene and quite frankly it's an eye sore.Audio is highly reused and remixed from Postal 2, including pedestrian voice lines, screams and sound effects. Map Muzak is somehow worse by having a filter on top. The poor NPC interaction is highly reused and might as well be the same code.I do not know how they messed up the violence but they did it. You hit someone with the broad side of a shovel and their neck is cut clean. Gore, which was the best candidate for improvement, is plain cartoony rather than cathartic and excessive. Pedestrians can tank hits from bladed weapons which feels absolutely terrible.Postal 4 underdelivers at every front. It fails to be a graphical upgrade, it fails to be a gameplay upgrade, it fails to be a Postal upgrade. All it truly upgraded was the models of feces, and it seems like they were real proud of this one - at least one whole errand day is dedicated to toilets and fecal matter.If you think Postal 4 sounds interesting for its violence and open world, check one of the following instead:- - -

_childDocuments_.review: Before anyone reads this, it's my opinion and you allowed to disagree with my opinion.I'm a huge fan of postal 2, and i'm really dissapointed with this one. The cutscenes look alright, but that's as much positives that I can say. I Feel like a huge part of what made Postal 2 so good has been lost here. It really felt like janky and unpolished experience, I really had to force myself to continue and beat this one, it wasn't a fun experience. I don't understand why they decided to bring this game out of Early Access, when it was supposed to still be there, the game has more bugs than Cyberpunk 2077 on release. I imagine this was a corporate move to make sure it's """finished""" before Brain Damaged Spin-off came out? (which btw, is like 100% better game than this). Where do i even begin?There's jank everywhere, and i mean jank you can't ignore. Game breaking stuff. bugs that felt was obvious and should have been caught in testing that wasn't before. Everytime they push out an update, they fix one bug but then 2 more bugs appear that breaks the game or disrupts the experience in one way or another , some of these bugs that i encountered really makes me believe there is very little effort or none QA testing being done to this game before update is being pushed, like certain sequences breaking, preventing you from advancing the game. I had so many instances where the game threw a random ass bug at me, that prevented me from completing a game (for example, catch dogs and cat mission in day 1, Dogs refused to follow me and just ate their snacks from miles away, or getting stuck in the mall on day 5 after defeating boss with no way out). Now, this was fine during Early Access , but it's something you just can't no longer ignore when they took Early Access Tag off, let me make this clear, THIS GAME IS STILL IN EARLY ACCESS. It's baffeling they decided to take EA off but left unfinished textures everywhere in the game! Go into a random house in the game, you will see speaker models, monitor models, bunch of models that has default Unreal engine untextured textures applied (most notable is Kunny island, half of the main stage models are unfinished/untextured) It's seriously feels like you playing Very early beta of a game , when they claim it's not. I know bugs are expected, even in full releases, but the unfinished models are really something that can't be excused in 1.0 release of the game.But let's ignore that a bit, let's ignore all the jank and clearly unfinished nature of the game. There's other serious problems with the game that I think are just simply unfixable. Let's start with graphics. They are just AWFUL. Yes I know people complain about peformance, i run relatively high rig, so I can't really complain about it, what i can complain is how ugly and just unappealing graphics looks, i have everything on ultra and the game, graphically, again looks like something out of Early beta/alpha stage, specially when it comes to Geometry and overall feel of the game. Npcs models are awful, The hair/grass rendered specially is a huge eyesore. This creates my biggest problem with this one. It does not have a charm that postal 2 had. It lacks identity and cosistency that postal 2 had that this one does not. The town itself is extremely boring. They added collectibles in terms of dolls, but the problem is the map itself sucks ass. There's a couple of semi interesting locations in the game but exploration is extremely gimped in this game. There's very little in terms of clever secrets to discover, very little in terms of unique buildings to see. In postal 2, every building was different, had different loot in it, while postal 4 has a little bit of that, i say it missed the mark. Specially when it comes to living quarters, most of it is one building Copy pasted with same interiors, it's even worse once you realise that again, there's a lot of unfinished models and textures that they filled these buildings with. The map is really not worth exploring. At first, i was doing all collectibles but i quickly gave up because just how bad that problem is. It really makes exploring less satisfying that it did in postal 2.  More problems include- Guns/melee weapons feel very unsatisfying to use. Specially melee weapons. I would say they are more gimped than postal 2-This might be taste thing, but most of humour in this game is non existent or felt extremely flat. There we're one or two funny moments (like when you have to spray over the tags and the cutscene with 2 gang members play out, just to get run over by SJW protestor , i laughed at that not gonna lie), but aside from few instances, most of the humour really felt flat and just plainly not funny. P2 had such memorable characters and funny moments . it felt like they really played it safe in this one- Overall tasks felt boring and uneventful, the only exception i can think off was in day 2.My biggest issue is that it lacks an charm and atmosphere that P2 had. I think they just should had stick with older UE engine and made it in same style as P2. Honestly, i think they shot themselfs in the foot by going with newer engine, because it really ruined atmosphere that the game was trying to have, and i would argue that P2 just looks better than P4Overall, i would say get Brain Damaged instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of POSTAL 2. Easily one of the greatest pieces of satire I've played in my life. But I just can't recommend POSTAL 4 in good faith.I can appreciate and see the effort, and Jon St. John's awesome performance prevents me from hating the whole experience.But something just feels missing.2's combat already required the player to take it rather slow for the most part, especially on harder difficulties where 2 hostile NPCs alone could quickly drain your health, but 4 just amps that up to 11. The new wanted system where you can have a horde of cops attacking you (basically like a 5 star in GTA) makes engaging in combat completely pointless with how slow the guns themselves are. Even running away requires you to be extremely lucky, since just like P2, hostile NPCs barely miss their shots. What doesn't help is that the wanted meter doesn't go away when you respawn after death, so you die, load your last save and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of cops immediately starting firing hot lead into you. Tl;dr I definitely don't recommend the game to be played on any objectively hard difficulty.The open world doesn't do itself any favors either. I don't mind a bigger world, especially when traditional open-world mechanics like vehicles and quick travel stations are there to make travelling more convenient, but it just feels... empty? The usual stuff from POSTAL 2 like every house being explorable and sometimes containing useful items are there, but the much more flat lighting compared to 2 and the houses basically being large neighborhoods that have the exact same house structure makes exploration a chore. The game fails to make the open-world intriguing and fun to explore.And going back to the 'flat lighting' thing, the game's ugliness and jank just doesn't feel intentional this time. POSTAL 4 is very much janky like 2 was and the early access versions wore that on their sleeves, but the jank just doesn't feel like it should be there this time around. You have janky physics and vehicle controls, over-the-top ragdolls, an experimental third-person mode that leaves a lot to be desired, (it's clearly not intended to be used outside of vehicles) and pre-rendered cutscenes that make an 11 year old's SFM animation feel like a high-production music video made in Blender, yet they're thrown right next to the Postal Dude's smooth reloading animations, realistic animations of burning NPCs trying to put themselves out and decent Unreal 4 lighting.Tl;dr the game can't make up its mind as to whether it wants to take the piss again with the jank, or just abandon it.The comedy and shock humor were what I was hyped the most on. It was POSTAL 2's selling point after all. But RWS just made it a mishmash of taking ideas from 2 again and mildly over-the-top, yet unfunny depictions of current social issues like SJWs and that wall Trump tried making. The idea of literally slingshotting Mexican immigrants over the wall and SJW "hispers" getting mad at the Dude for vandalizing billboards sounds hysterical, but it just falls so flat on its face. I wish I could explain it, but I'm mainly confused as to how they managed to make it feel this unfunny and uninteresting. And it's not like taking ideas from P2 is a bad idea in a vacuum. The game thankfully doesn't do it that much to begin with and when it does (with the petition mission for example) it does it pretty well. This version of the petition mission (mainly being able to hold the NPCs at gunpoint so they sign the petition) was one of the rare instances of the game getting a genuine laughter out of me. But other than that, this game just feels so so flat as a whole.I really wish I could point at one specific aspect of POSTAL 4 and say "that's the problem!" But I can't. The game just does so many things worse than POSTAL 2 and really missed the mark as the first true sequel to such a timeless classic. I'm definitely glad that they turned a full-on POSTAL 2 remake project into this instead, but like I said at the beginning: I cannot recommend POSTAL 4. If you'd still like to give it a shot, just lower your expectations from 2 and you might still have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Old: Although it is quite janky in its alpha stages, this is a proper sequel to POSTAL 2. Best to send feedback to anything majorly game-breaking for better results, that'd be my advice.New updated one: This game just keeps getting better with each fresh update, whether be a major update with a new day of the week, new weapons, new scooters (whether be cosmetic designs, tank-like armoured ones) new features and whatnot, or minor updates that are just casual bug fixes. Nonetheless, it is hard to believe that this game became early access over a year ago and it has grown to be a much proper sequel as we hoped for. As of this moment (10th of December 2020 as I type this) Tuesday has been added with new everything and it is great to play the new errands, explore new areas, use new weapons, and so forth. But that's not all. The mad lads 1-Up'd themselves. In the absence of sawn-off double-barreled shotgun from Postal 2, we instead have now a QUADRUPLE-barreled shotgun here in Postal 4, known as the Fournicator! If the crazy weapons from Postal 2 is what got ya into the Postal series, then the Fournicator quad-barrel shotgun is what will get you into Postal 4 alone.Tuesday, a new-and-improved scooter, the Fornicator shotgun. These are the top 3 features that are making Postal 4 into the true proper sequel that Postal 2 deserves. The RWS devs deserve high praise for being real cool dudes. I await Wednesday with great anticipation, but do not worry on rushing Wednesday out the door, take as much time as needed.

_childDocuments_.review: While many might argue that Postal 4 is just a worse copy of Postal 2 - which... yes, to some extent it is - I kindly have to disagree with the notion that the game in itself is downright awful.Perhaps it's the fact that I have the ability to be entertained by any moving set of polygons and pixels, or that I'm already a huge fan of the franchise to begin with, but Postal 4 is actually... pretty fun, once you look past its flaws.Framerate issues aside, (which might be the case due to my below average PC setup, anyway) the game did make me laugh quite a few times, and I also had a bit of fun just by exploring the map. Although it all still felt... a little unfinished in many places, that's one of the things I respect RWS for: their commitment to keep on updating the game and improving it as time goes on. Afterall, that's the same thing they did with Postal 2 throughout the years.Overall, Postal 4 isn't a game I'd recommend to newcomers of the series, but to anyone who isn't looking for an overly polished product to be entertained by. _childDocuments_.review: The state this game is in  is horrendous. FPS counter going below 20 on lowest settings. Constant crashes. Items disappearing from your inventory. There are multiple places in the game, where you can get your save file completely broken and be unable to progress. 3 Years of active development and the game has stability of a tech demo.Even if they clench their asses and actually fix all the technical problems the game is still bad on the design level. Large open world with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in it. Houses are copy-pasted and have nothing in them. 10 minutes of walking in straight path between objectives is what you'll be doing between every mission. Postal 2 from 2003 is more technologically impressive than UE4 game from 2022 (Postal 4 doesn't even have working mirrors). Dirty and harsh aesthetic of previous games is replaced with something that looks like stock assets pack bought for 25$. Inconsistent art style, especially when it comes to NPCs. Any step forward this game takes, it does a 3 meter long backflip and lands on its face. At times I cannot even believe it was developed by the same people as Postal 2 and Paradise Lost.And a bit of a fun fact: As of now, there's a bug in the game that makes it crash A LOT, softlocking most players, since they cannot load any location they're not in. Developer said they won't fix it until a week from now.

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote my last review out of anger and disappointment. Having greatly enjoyed Postal 2, I had in my mind a sort of modern rebirth for the Postal series with No Regerts, and in fairness maybe my expectations were too high. I wasn't recommending it, but now I am.Here it is, the game is objectively unfinished. The world is littered with things that could have been. Things you might have interacted with. People you could have spoken to. Ultimately though, it's a constant reminder that the game isn't what you want it to be. That said, if you enjoy Postal as a franchise, give it a go. Probably better if you pick it up on sale. And if you're new to Postal, go in expecting a lot of issues. One of the main problems I had was the saves would not load. Every save crashed. You need to validate the game files after updates to solve this - who knew. Found that hint after checking the message boards.There is a ton of Postal humour here. I love their attention to details. The packaging for all of the food. So much makes me smile. I just wish there was more polish on the big stuff, like having clear dialogue with shop keepers, knowing what you are going to spend, and what you'll buy, instead of silence and a prompt to provide money...One huge tip for your first play through, explore. A lot. Look in the nooks. Stock up. Sell goods to vendors for money. A bigger bag and a stock of fast food can go a long way.Come on RWS, nail Postal 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the early access on Day 1 and swore off of playing more until it's full release because it was so janky, glitchy, and clearly unfinished. I really hate to say that still by 1.0.7 it is still janky, glitchy, and unfinished. It is stupidly easy to get out of bounds, level transitions take forever and sometimes warp me to the wrong place, some errands are glitched (i am currently stuck because an errand I've completed twice never got marked on the errand list as done), the performance is extremely spotty (especially for how bad the graphics look sometimes), many locations are empty(/unfinished), texture pop-in is basically standard, game-breaking glitches are as easy to discover as intended mechanics, and the game crashes or softlocks me basically hourly. The elements are there. There are many weapons and mechanics to toy around with, and some of the errands are highlights. The juvenile sense of humor is here, and having 4 voices to choose from is such a fun feature for any long time fans, but it is nearly impossible to enjoy all of that when the game's fundamental aspects are still so broken. I know RWS is a small passionate team but there is no good reason to say this game is "1.0" ready. There is still a lot of stuff that needs fixed.To anyone considering buying, have you played Postal 2 and it's expansions, Apocalypse Weekend and Paradise Lost? Have you played Postal: Brain Damaged? If not, those are all way more worth your time than this at the moment. I sincerely hope that I can update my review to a positive one soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Does this try to be Postal 2?Yes.Does it succeed?Not entirely.Yes, you can cause mayhem and it looks better than ever, yet somehow there is a disconnect. It just does not 'feel' the same as Postal 2In Postal 2 I could suspend my disbelief and pretend these are actual people I am torturing (too dark?), yet in 4 they are empty NPCs and nothing else. Don't get me wrong, it is still fun to cut their legs off, there is just a distinct Postal 2 feel that is not present.Personally the biggest problem I have is with the daily tasks. Postal 2 had fairly normal errands like, get milk, return a library book, go vote, etc. firmly grounded in reality. The game does everything it can to prevent your day of errands running smoothly by introducing out of the ordinary situations.  I like this. Postal 4 seems to go out of its way to be out of the ordinary forcing you to find the ordinary amongst the crazy. To me, this is the wrong way round.I don't like this. Overall it's a fun game with a lot of the wackiness you had in Postal 2 and will still recommend it to any Postal fan.It is still EA, so let's hope it improves.FYII have had no major bugs apart from missing content and walls you can walk through. _childDocuments_.review: First of i want to say this game is very beta in its current stage.I found some random bikes laying around the city and as a homeless guy i was hoping i could steal one to get around the town a little faster but just found that it was just a static object just for decor. I was also surprised to find out that not one person tried to beat me up for peeing on them all they did was either puke, die, or run away. Acid pee i guess. As a guy growing up in Florida i know if i did that i would get my azz kicked or get shot or at least some one would call the cops and have me arrested. okay and i went to the circle j store and was hoping to rob the place so i could make some extra money but nope. The cashier just runs away when i point the gun at him and then i find out the cash register doesn't even open. Dissapointing. I couldn't even take any food or goods to restore my health. I did at least later find a health kit on the wall. You cant punch people when you have your hands equipped, really? I did notice allot of stray pitbulls free roaming the city and am surprised none of them wanted to bite me. I know i play as a smelly homeless guy but dam i must smell really bad for the dogs to not even growl at me. Kicking the dogs does absolutely nothing. My foot goes through the dog and kicks the dirt. I also did notice that the sidewalk leading to the tall building at the bottom of the map had an invisible wall. Not sure if you unlock it later in the game but i was curious only because the postal dude made a comment saying "some one must be compensating for something".  You cant steal cars and some of the car windows are checkered? Cant see into them? I also feel as if the interact button should also be a talk button to make comments to the citizens sort of the way you can in GTA V. I noticed there was an arcade in the city so it would be nice for some of them to be usable as a mini-game using the in-game money. You cant run in the game which sucks. An animation should be added when using the vending machines and you could use the in game money for those power drinks like the Akimbo power machine. I did like how you could find special weapons in the houses. I am surprised i didn't get shot for breaking into people's houses but they did try to fight me. It would be funny to walk in on someone taking a really loud dump and use the feces as a weapon sort of like in duke nukem. If a mini map was added that would be nice so that i don't have to keep pausing to look at the map to see where i am going. Using a controller in the pause menu doesn't really work that well so i find myself switching back to keyboard and mouse frequently which is annoying. Why doesn't drinking that kimbo power drink refill my bladder? Finding beer or wine in peoples houses would be a nice touch to unlock some sort of drunken rage mode. It was weird finding an empty store with a random NPC walking around in it. I am assuming the map isn't finished yet? it was the building across from the job agency. The dogs seem to only attack me on the scooter? The police department was empty so i guess that is still in development. Maybe that could be another potential Job? You should really add the ability to use the iron sights on the guns because you currently cant. A couple of prisoners were shooting at me through the walls... prisoners are pretty wimpy because a spanish guy calling me a mory-con was punching me and it did not hurt me at all like i was invincible or something. There really needs to be and objectives list during jobs because it isn't very clear where to go or what to do in the prison job. My game session ended with a random crash to desktop. Otherwise this is a pretty good game! keep going! I hope that a split-screen co-op mode will be added in the future maybe as a co-worker?

_childDocuments_.review: Several years have passed since the events that devastated the once proud town remembered as Paradise. The only two to walk away from the cataclysm unscathed, the hapless everyman known as the POSTAL Dude and his loyal companion Champ, drive aimlessly through the scorching deserts of Arizona looking for a new place to call home. After a fortuitous gas station rest stop ends with their car, trailer home, and the rest of their worldly possessions stolen, all the Dude’s seemingly got left to his name is his canine cohort and his bathrobe, and neither of them smells all that great. However, on the horizon, the duo glimpses an unfamiliar and dazzling town that beckons to them. What untold prospects lie within? Fame? Fortune? Maybe a bidet or two? Edensin awaits. POSTAL 4: No Regerts is a satirical and outrageous comedic open world first person shooter and the long-awaited true sequel to what’s been fondly dubbed as "The Worst Game Ever™", POSTAL 2! (No third game is known to exist.)

name: Code of Princess EX
detailed_description: Code of Princess EX brings a unique combination of hack-and-slash, beat-‘em-up action and role-playing depth to the table! Fans of both genres are sure to be captivated by this epic adventure of intense multi-plane fantasy combat, with a roster of over 50 playable characters, all of whom can be upgraded with new abilities and equipment. The game’s Campaign mode supports local two-player co-op, and there are also options for both competitive and cooperative online play. The story within Code of Princess EX follows Princess Solange of DeLuxia as she fights to restore order in a world where monsters are trying to overtake the human race. Armed with the legendary sword DeLuxcalibur, Solange assembles a team of talented fighters to join her quest. Together, they embark on an epic journey where they will confront the monster uprising and try to discover it’s secret origins. Features: -Action-packed “hack-and-slash” gameplay featuring customizable RPG elements. -Players can freely move between three different planes of action during combat, with some projectile attacks able to travel between planes. -Over 50 different characters are playable throughout multiple game modes, including Campaign, Free Play and Bonus Quests. -Players can level up and equip their favorite characters with weapons and accessories that modify their stats in six different categories. -Cooperative and competitive local/online multiplayer modes include leaderboards and let players tracked their coveted “Princess Points” -Created by former members of the original Guardian Heroes development team. -Characters and worlds created by legendary Capcom artist Kinu Nishimura, with art contributions from Street Fighter artist Bengus.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah I loved guardian heroes. I love this style of game...But the difficulty is handled SOOOOO POORLY I cannot play it past where I'm at without grinding so long that I can just juggle this boss to death with lasers. Since engaging most bosses in melee combat in this game seems to spell certain death after a certain point.Enemies get so fast, so aggressive, you NEVER have time to do anything other than play keep away, juggle them forever or use your 3 limit breaks while using a weapon that gives super armor.The boss I'm at right now PERMANENTLY LIMIT BREAKS at like 40% health and is uninteruptable and constantly jumps right on top of you and stunlocks you.How is that fun at all? What am I supposed to do about this other than never let him touch the floor so he cant limit break or limit break back and burst him? I dont even want to know how much grind it would take to even do that because using full mana bar on a full damage build isnt doing any substantial damage as is. I tried kiting him but he's MUCH faster than you. I tried blocking but he just kicks your ♥♥♥♥ in. Good luck outrunning him because he's faster than you, can instantly change lanes to catch you, jumps across the entire map to you if you get any distance.There's about 3 different points I've progressed to that are equally awful. On extra quests the 2 missions I have left to beat are starting surrounded by 6 iron golems that use ranged machine gun attacks to instantly stunlock you from the get go.The other one is just another boss with the same super armor crap and 2 skeletons that respawn no matter how many times you kill them. I got him to 400 hp, he perma limit breaks and I cannot hit him because he interrupts EVERYTHING i do nearly instantly. You cannot even get light hits off. I was that close to just scrapping with him, but I couldnt even get 3 melee hits off on him. Instant jumping to you.Faster attacks with less windup.You cannot hit him to get a combo off and kill him. This games difficulty curve is absurd. I was having so much fun with this game, noticing enemies were getting faster and it was fine, until they got FASTER than me and you cannot play around it.Dont even get me started on the fact that 3 bees will spell your doom if you get hit a single time because you get shocked to death from ranged attacks the spam endlessly. I got stun locked by it once. I got timed out another time while blocking because there was no break in their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lightning ball spam from across the map. They can do it while flying too. Some characters cannot hit them while flying. You could use shock immunity to help that issue but the actual hit still interupts you and I dont think that would stop 3 of them from locking you in place to death.I really like this game, I love the playstyle. But for the love of god dont make a game where you just get dog piled to death by 20 enemies that are faster than you with long chain stun attacks from across the map or bosses that you cannot interrupt from the second HALF of their health bar while they're ALSO faster than you and can whoop you in about 2-3 combos while you nibble their health bar down.

_childDocuments_.review: In this new game, the bosses have infinite burst: for example, Schwarz (If I'm not mistaken) become now a walking tank in the middle of the fight with infinite super armor. In the original game the bosses were agressive, but now you have no way to stun him. It's just bad. The original Code of Princess wasn't really hard, or at least that's how I recall it. Now it seems the only way to win against certain bosses is to grind, and for Schwarz to use Solange with the weapon that gives no knockback on burst and to spam the attack button. Which is bad.I think that Code of Princess was a decent game, something akin to a 6/10. Ok. Maybe more a 5/10. But we all have our guilty pleasures. I knew what to expect and I didn't have any high expectations about it. So I wasn't (too much) surprised when I saw that the port of the original game was rather lazy. It lacked a lot of basic options. Code of Princess Ex was the chance to make amends. Alas, this game is just more of the same. For example, it's impossible to change the resolution or changing the button configuration will also affect which button you have to press in the menu.Luckily, it's not a very expansive buy. But if you possess the original game, I don't really believe it's necessary to buy it again. After all, it's a rather lazy port, with just the minimum amount of options avaible, in order to make it functionnal (and with maybe some very angry bosses). That's all. So if you really want to play a mediocre beat them up, I would advise to buy the first game. It's graphically less polished, or less beautiful (and this Ex version is not really a looker either to be honest) but, and I know what you' re going to read will be subjective, I liked the first more.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is just as fun as I remember, the combat systems haven't changed. The game would have done well, if not better, if the actual 3d models were utilized instead of sprites, imo, but regardless: Now it's all in HD, with a loading time of less then 5 seconds and smooth 60 frames (GTX 1060). I've been having a lot of fun with this beat-em-up port. But: With that said, there are some glaring criticisms.-Artifacts from the original port are still there, and still outstanding. The pixelation being the most obvious, especially in the cutscenes.-The voices and sound effects also seem to have noticeable compression as well; Thankfully, this does not apply to the soundtrack.-The game does not seem to have (good) mouse/keyboard, or remapping support. Perhaps I'm being hasty, but I noticed no guide to the controls in regards to the keyboard as well.-Perhaps it's just me, but the songs don't loop, leaving one track to play to the end, and dead silence for the rest of the time spent in an instance, even in the menus. - No English voice-overs? The original game possessed this, and I combed the settings, but found nothing related to it.Granted, there's still more for me to explore. Despite all these shortcomings, I'm still enjoying myself greatly.EDIT: The changes made to the burst system hurt the gameplay somewhat, and the fixed stat up system also is a bit of a turn-off. Still recommended, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never seen a game miss the point as much as Code of Princess. The guys behind Guardian Heroes made it. it has Guardian Heroes DNA down to its core. Most of the crazy RPG/fighting hybrid design decisions are there complete with spellcasters blanketing the field in overpowered ridiculous friendly fire spell explosions, but in every other way the game feels like an early access title made by amateurs. Worse still, Streets of Fury EX completely humiliates it at doing the exact same style of beat-em-up.I have never had enemies break out of an uppercut->air combo move and go into neutral air attacks against me on the way down before this game.The only chain you get in this game is X-X-X and then you can cancel into a special move, but only about half of your special moves do anything useful. Some uppercuts don't even finish before the enemy flies out of reach so you can jump and go into an air combo. Ali has a whistle that resets enemy states but NOTHING in this game comes fast enough to make this an interesting mechanic. The first main character boss spends so much time in air that you spend half the fight chasing each other because you're both so slow and incapable of doing anything with your conflicting movesets. And then he bursts, where he gets permanent hyper armor and defense and you have NOTHING that can counter that.The stats only serve to make what should be a short, replayable game into a one-and-done affair, which is stupid when you have almost a dozen main characters to play and every single enemy and several NPCs as playable joke characters. The whole system doesn't serve the game at all except that apparently since it's a fantasy game you MUST have an RPG system because it's a convention.You don't even have to understand Japanese to see that the localization is very liberal with deviations from the Japanese script. The dub from the 3DS port is gone, you have the Japp voice track here, but the original text from the localization is kept and it never matches. Clearly they weren't writing high art to begin with but the additions get a little annoying.Also the music doesn't loop. It just cuts out mid level. The original game was amateur hour ♥♥♥♥ but this is DOUBLY embarrassing.Code of Princess is one of the most disappointing works I have ever played, a complete waste of the considerable talent that went into it and this remake does almost nothing meaningful to improve the game outside of giving us the original Japanese voices. They botched twice in a row. If you really want Guardian Heroes back go play Streets of Fury EX and stay far away from this hunk of trash.

_childDocuments_.review: I have read most of the reviews about the game before the purchase and I must say after trying it out, Im totally flabbergasted by how harsh and untrue the complaints were. Yes, there are significant changes (not all good) from the previous release but overall it is STILL a bloody decent game for its time. I have played my fair share of bad games my entire life but this aint it and I often wonder if those people who condemned this game even come from the same planet I live in while I load the game up and think about what combos Im able to pull off that session. Yes, they remove the stat allocation system, which reduced the customization of your characters greatly but it isnt all that bad. You can still change some stats with your gear/equipment. I know it takes away the fun from creating funny or crazy characters with ridiculous stats but think of it as rebalancing the game for the better. And yes, they removed the crazy unlimited Bursting system too BUT again, like Ive said, think of it as a rebalancing for the game because some characters can go really crazy with the old Burst system and I dont think anybody would enjoy being on the receiving end of those combos (unless it is the boss, so yeah sure). Now you are limited to a fixed number and I think overall it makes you plan your approach to the stage more carefully so you dont go wild the moment you enter like the old days (which is also fun but lets move on) and having tougher bosses mean that you cant just spam attacks carelessly and mindlessly now (which is good). In fact, I like beat-em-ups with tougher (or a lil cheesy/unfair) bosses, because it is so much more satisfying when you finally beat them flawlessly after getting your butt handed to you the first time and spending time to get it right after that. Im sure nobody wouldve liked Dark Souls if it was easy, right? But seriously, lets just admit that we tend to just mash the attack buttons without any repercussions in the past because as long as you connect with something, you can always burst cancel into anything you want. Its all comes down to who hit who first so you just keep throwing attacks out. Now that burst is limited, you will finally sit down and play the game the way it was meant to be played ie mastering and utilizing the attack negating and crushing system where you can negate incoming attacks with attacks of your own cancelling each other out or beating the opponent with it. This deepens gameplay significantly IMHO.  Graphically, yes it is NOT perfect but still overall it is a big improvement from the previous. Also, the game plays really smooth now, so what is there to complain? Is graphics really more important than gameplay? Also, I see no problems with the controller setup. Are people actually trying?Next is "the lack of English voice dubbing." Id be very honest and biased here, Ive always preferred the original voices in Japanese videogames because they sound in character and the characters in THIS game are designed to be VERY colorful aesthetically both visually and orally. Many of the humor just do NOT translate well into English. Heck do most people even understand the humor of it all? The skimpy (boobalicious) and naive airhead princess tasked with saving the world, accompanied by the flat-chested anego/robber ringleader (who actually did not want to take part in anything), the suspicious yet nonchalant undead Lady "Zozo" (who is actually a loli), the bratty Allegro who always claim to be a sage etc etc I doubt even the translators knew what they were translating because they did not get to play or experience the game characters prior to their assignment so its not hard to see why some Japanese grunts are badly translated into weird long sentences that mysteriously appear out of nowhere. Doh.    That aside. I only have one gripe with the game, they didnt make the maps bigger as a bonus. Maybe that is expecting too much but one can wish cant one? Also, the non-existant online community is a real shame, all thanks to the bad reviews it totally didnt deserved. This game does NOT suck. Period. You should get it when it is on discount because it is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a year late, but before anything I just want to say, "I called it." Back in 2019, about a year before this game was released on PC I predicted they were going to double dip the fanbase and try to resell us the same game to us. Scumbag move after selling lackluster port in the first place. So Code of Princess EX, how is it difference from 2016 and is it worth the extra money?Well let's just say the first thing that comes to mind just by looking at EX. Compared to the original 2016 version, EX is gorgeous, but that may not be saying much because 2016 looked like garbage. Stretched out graphics, pixlated sprites, that terrible DS two screen mechanic with all the empty space. 2016 Princess was a disgusting garbage pile to look at. Thankfully EX fixed this. The sprites look good, the backgrounds look good, the FMVs look good. They did everything I wanted them to do with the EX version and made the game look less like barf. Sadly they went and did other things no one else asked them to do to the game.I think the biggest complaint you'll read about is the changes to the game balance and difficulty. Sadly, I haven't played enough of EX to notice the difficulty spike yet, but I have noticed they nerfed the Burst mechanic, limiting it to three uses per stage for a short duration rather than being linked to your MP gauge, and it would seem they completely removed the Bonus Points to Stats earned on level up. With that alone I can say the game WILL be harder since you don't get the extra Bonus Points to distribute to your stats. Considering how difficult some of the later bosses can be in the 2016 version I feel like this was a frustrating change for many people. Granted, I admit I was one of those people who complained about the "Block - Burst" play style needed to defeat bosses in the later half of the game, but that doesn't mean I wanted them to buff the bosses and nerf the player. I just wanted them to adjust the AI so or such so the combat wasn't so monotonous. So is it worth it? Going back and forth between the two games EX just looks so nice and sexy in comparison to the potato that was 2016. If you're a fan I'd say EX is worth buying, just because the game  is visually superior and I do want to show support for a future game. _childDocuments_.review: Stupid character designs, but the combat is pretty great.  This is a substantially more interesting take on brawlers than many other games on the market.  COPEX plays similarly to a fighting game or, for the old-school crowd, like Guardian Heroes for the Saturn.  Special attacks are command based, though simplified, and you can string attacks together to combo and juggle your opponents.  Learning the ins-and-outs of your favorite character will unlock their full potential, and allow you to take on harder difficulties.  There's also an RPG element to the game, giving you the option to strengthen your character in various ways in case the encounters become too difficult.If you'd ever wanted to try and get the hang of fighting game inputs, you could do worse than this game.  It's at least got some standard inputs to get you used to quarter-rolls, but learning to chain combos is where you'll get the most mileage.  TLDR: If you can get over the awful character designs and tropey writing, COPEX stands out as a robust yet easy to pick-up brawler/fighting game hybrid.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're planning on buying this game because you liked Guardian Heroes, know that you're not going to have the same experience. While everything looks nice enough, the game has some issues. Stages are fairly short and the story is linear.  You don't allocate skill points in this version of the game, it levels up your character automatically based on their class. Though, to be fair, your reserve characters share a portion of the XP you gained from clearing stages which is really nice. They'll need it because some enemies really tank damage and are an absolute chore to fight. Some constantly block or preemptively strike at you. Other enemies like to hover around the edge of the screen and spam projectiles at you, in some cases stun-locking you. And if you don't grind XP by replaying stages again and again before continuing too far into the story, you WILL eventually reach boss characters who will absolutely shut your adventure down until you do.But gameplay issues aside, the presentation gets even sloppier. The game's music, of all things, doesn't loop. The music just cuts out after it plays once, leaving you with grunts and attack sounds for the next three minutes or so. Another thing that annoys me more than it should, is that character's spoken language is Japanese while the text is English. I know for a fact it has been "westernized" in places and only makes me wonder how characters were originally meant to act. And there's plenty of characters in this game, unlike the 5 from Guardian Heroes. I confess I do really like the design of several of the cast, but sometimes less is more.But the biggest issue is that the game just doesn't feel fun to play. You're going to spam the same attacks the entire time. You're going to unlock so many useless trinkets and weapons and only switch items a few times. And you're going to do it all by yourself because the game doesn't utilize remote play. Hell, the multiplayer function doesn't even seem to work at all... or maybe it does and it's just that no one wants to touch this game. I bet it's the latter.

name: Those Who Remain
detailed_description: WISHLIST MEOW! 😻 About the Game Those Who Remain places you in an up-close, psychological horror story set in the sleepy town of Dormont – a town in a spiralling split from the fabric of reality, warped by darkness and the deeds of the Citizens who reside. Confront the uncomfortable horrors reflected by the darkness and survive the night of Dormont as Edward is confronted with a test of his sanity, morality and the shadows of evil that lurks below. Darkness Has Eyes Navigate the encroaching darkness and manipulate light sources to clear paths through the mysteries of Dormont. To survive, you’ll need to stay in the light by any means. Worlds Torn Apart Explore two interconnected dimensions as you move between Dormont and a strange alternate reality to solve thought-provoking puzzles and unlock the mysteries held within the dark. Conscience of Choice Choose to condemn or reprieve the lost souls of Dormont and their cursed trove of secrets, as you make tough morale decisions that will determine the fate of Edward, through multiple different endings. Savour your Sanity Discover an up-close psychological thriller wrapped in a deeply human story which explores family, loss, mistakes and how real people can be haunted by more than just demons in the dark. Unique Atmospheric Horror Immerse yourself in a story-driven adventure inspired by classic supernatural film and TV series that presents a deeply atmospheric alternative horror experience. STORY As the lights go out, the embers of darkness are stoked in the sleepy town of Dormont. Whispers of disappearances carry through the town as a burgeoning, uneasy and irrational fear begins to spread and darkness comes to be an unwelcome reflection to Those Who Remain. Some mistakes should never happen, not when your life is complete – and yet they do. Edward had the good life, a beautiful wife and the perfect little girl, yet finds himself several whiskeys down and driving through the night of Dormont to end his secret affair - in a bid to fix his mistakes. As Edward pulls into the Golden Oak Motel, he is unaware just how much this night will change his life… The horrors and darkness that thrive in the corner of every eye are torn loose…

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain could be best described as a collection of everything that is wrong with the horror genre these days, a yet another take on the most common style of modern horror game - a walking simulator with minor puzzles, chase sequences, predictable narrative that tackles some dark themes and in this particular case also completely lacking in good scares or any sort of horror atmosphere.While the game has some interesting ideas, they aren't used to their full potential and quickly get buried under the static and repetitive nature of the gameplay loop: Avoid the darkness, search lockers/drawers/etc. for documents or a key/item you need to progress, solve a puzzle, escape or hide from a creature, do a narrative decision and repeat.It took me roughly 4 to 4.5 hours to complete the game and during that time, there were 3 things in particular that bothered me quite a bit: Lack of immersion, inconsistency and the lack of proper horror atmosphere.Immersion suffers from how limited your actions as a player are: You can walk, run, interact with objects and throw things. If a monster is searching for you and you are supposed to hide from it, rather than sneaking around and crouching behind objects you simply walk around and make sure the monster doesnt face you - it seemingly doesn't even matter if you run right behind them. If a puzzle could be solved in a logical manner, an area could be accessed if only you could do *insert some completely logical action here* or some object would be perfect as a mobile light source, you can be damn sure you don't get a chance to do anything that deviates from the one way that the developers intended the player to progress with.Inconsistency, the game hammers in the point that the darkness is death, it is to be avoided... But the game is incredibly inconsistent in applying that rule: Some dark areas seem safe to walk around, while sometimes you step only tiny bit inside a darker area and immediately get shanked - only to restart from a checkpoint a few minutes ago, leaving you to repeat puzzles or picking up the same items/documents again further hampering any attempts at keeping the player immersed.Finally the horror atmosphere or rather, the lack of it. You quickly discover that outside of the hide/chase sequences everything is static, darkness exists in some areas until you flip a switch and the area becomes safe to enter. There is no fear of the unknown, no unexpected threats to be scared of - instead it all is just kinda... safe and dull.Perhaps I am being too harsh, but in my opinion Those Who Remain is yet another unremarkable and dull addition to the genre and its gameplay loop has been executed far better by other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Edward is a man with a good life; a beautiful wife, a smart daughter, and a nice home. Yet despite all of his good fortunes, he finds himself at the bottom of a whiskey bottle night after night, on top of having a secret affair. When his lover, Diane, texts him from a motel in the quiet town of Dormont, he summons the courage to visit her and break off their lust-fueled relationship for good. However, when he arrives at the location, Diane is nowhere to be found. Instead, Edward finds himself on a journey to piece together the death of a young girl, solve the disappearance of the entire town, and figure out exactly where his life went wrong, in Those Who Remain.Don't let the Steam store tags fool you, there is no survival horror here. What this game really is, is a psychological horror walking simulator that does well at masking its key and note finding with clever puzzles and ensnaring atmosphere. It helps that the campaign is straight-forward most of the time, unlike a lot of indie horror games of a similar nature that force well-hidden item hunting on its unsuspecting players. Be prepared to dive between dimensions to solve many of the enigmas here, as reality shifts and the past keeps trying to inject itself into the present; another key element that keeps the time-worn core gameplay from becoming stale. There are also a few chase and stealth segments with one-hit kill enemies, but you'll be pressed to have a difficult time maneuvering the mostly deaf and blind AI.If you've been into horror games for at least the last two decades or have invested a lot of time in back catalogue, Those Who Remain is not going to offer up anything new for you. It takes ideas from a plethora of other titles and stuffs them all haphazardly into its own agenda; grotesque physical manifestations of guilt (Silent Hill), shadow people that are afraid of light (Alan Wake), a final moment that was basically pulled from Paranormal Activity: Lost Souls. It's all here, and there's not a drop of actual originality to be found. As harsh as that may sound, the developers were able to blend all of these inspirations together into a well-crafted story and decent horror-based walking simulator. Remember, it's not about reinventing the wheel, it's what you do with it that counts.Although you can tell that Those Who Remain was made in Unity thanks to the stagnant style of the menus and loading screens, the game functions well at a consistent 60 FPS at 1080p, using a GTX 1080/i7-6700k combo. Though it is a title that thinks gamma is equal to brightness, which is a shame. The game is so incredibly dark that it's difficult to enjoy the visuals at all, and all the gamma does is add an awful white hue to everything. Another thing that brings this release down are the aforementioned stealth sections; every time the campaign builds up a good momentum, the developers slowed it down again with a tedious slow-paced area. More notably, a section closer to the end where it's necessary to carry six very spaced out lion statues one-by-one to a platform while avoiding a large enemy, and being unable to run the entire time due to the items being too heavy.Despite its low points, Those Who Remain has enough high points to be both exciting and engaging. The atmosphere is gripping, though the developers would benefit from adding a brightness slider. The story does end up diving off in a totally different direction than what it seems to begin as, but it all ends up combining together into a well-developed tale. If you take your time and explore everything, you'll land yourself at around 5-6 hours of play time, with an additional 2-3 hours required for a second run through for the second ending. All in all, a potential 9-10 hour adventure for $22 CAD isn't a bad haul at all. If you're into paranormal ghost tales with a psychological twist and don't mind ideas that have been rehashed quite a few times over, check this one out.The Horror Network  |  Click for Gore

_childDocuments_.review: (TWR) is a first-person horror adventure set in the present times. Players impersonate Edward, an american man that suddenly finds himself engaged in the terrible events happening in the city of Dormont. Streets are deserted, the city in shambles, while dark figures with glowing eyes are ever-present in any shadow - with murderous intent. In these terrifying circumstances, you'll have to find your way through a Dormont scorched by chaos, while also facing Edward's own past and (quite literal) demons.🟩 🟥 The good points about TWR are not many at all. Some scenes in several parts of Edward's adventure have some pathos in them and are actually pretty good, quite spectacular. A pity these moments are just a very small part of what is largely a dull experience. The other good points is about the light effects, which are overall well done and not only crank up the atmosphere in most sections, but also integrate in the gameplay mechanics well.Now onto the more consistent bad parts of it. First and most importantly, for being a horror game it really doesn't incite fear or anxiety in the least. The reasons for this are to be found in how poorly various aspects of gameplay and graphics have been designed, the combination of these factors annihilates immersion most of the time. The story is nothing special and very early on gives you the elements to understand the whole picture, and even if you don't the events are B-movie tier horror tropes without any uniqueness or pathos to them.The voice acting doesn't help either, as the main character sounds like an automaton completely devoid of any emotion, and the other few sentient characters aren't much better either. It really kills the mood to see Edward react flatly, without emotion to situations that would scare the hell out of anyone. Graphics are only saved in part by the quality lighting, but models are inconsistent in quality as are textures: they used asset packs of different quality and make to create the game, and it shows. Puzzles and stealth sections are both very mediocre and either simplistic or tedious, they really feel like a chore and again do not make any tension. 🎮 Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Puzzles, Stealth and Chase Sequences. Is always done on foot, you can sprint for an unlimited time as well if needed, but you cannot crouch or perform any other movement. It is possible to grab many objects and throw them around, this is sometimes useful to find items such as keys or documents, but is done mostly to give more interaction to the environment. While exploring many areas will be blocked off by the Ghosts, which will instantly murder you if you get too close. There is no indicator of how close you can get and that goes often to luck. By using buttons and light switches you can progressively free areas of ghosts and explore them. Portals give you the ability to shift to another dimension, where ghosts are absent and really reminds of the "upside-down" from . In this dimension you may sometimes find a previously blocked way open, and swapping between the two realities is fundamental to progress.Are frequent and the most common type is a series of items to find in order to access a blocked off area. There sometimes are hints to the position of these objects in the current location, while some other times you will be left wandering on your own, which can be frustrating since keys can be very small and locations quite large. Other puzzle types include logic-based trials, platforming sections, and little investigative puzzles too. The problem is, they are all quite simple and dull with barely any challenge, or in some instances obscure solutions. Sections are all about staying out of sight of various creatures, that unlike Ghosts will move around. Most of these sections are a dull affair as well because there really is no sense of tension or dread, the monster you escape from is well visible at all times, slow, doesn't react to sound, and you can eventually lose it if you run for enough time. Some other stealth sections, one in particular involving lion statues, are extremely badly designed, in that particular one the monster could spot you from beyond your sight distance, and that would mean a certain death. Are your run of the mill "escape from the screaming monster" type of effort without any particular flair or spectacle to them. Usually they are brief, annoying, and don't really put you in any startled mood. Unremarkable, again.  None. Bad. in 1440p, 85hz there is a 75% memory use on a RTX2080Ti on average.  No problems to report.  No major bugs to report. None.Those Who Remain is a bad horror game that fails in the most critical points of this genre, delivering an unremarkable, dull and clichè experience that is simply not worth playing.
