_childDocuments_.review: I love me a scary game, and this one definitely spooked me. But I am struggling  with some serious issues that make it not fun to play.The game focuses on staying in the light, and entering some dark areas will instantly kill you. But this game has no method of indicating if you are lit or not, and doesn't indicate well which dark places are safe to enter and which will kill you instantly. This makes the game feel really unfair. The level design forces you to almost constantly run into a dark place and you have no idea if you will die or not. This kept putting me in a "♥♥♥♥ it" mood which really ruins the point of scary games. All around this game has serious issues with player direction. It's either beating you over the head with obvious instructions or leaving you in the dark (pun intended) to wander around hoping you're doing the right thing. At one point a character says "follow me!" and then vanishes  leaving the player to wander until they find them and then once you find them, they blink away again. As shown in the games description, you travel between two realms. Changing things in one will effect things in the other but there is no way of knowing what changes will actually effect the other side. I ran in a loop between the two sides multiple times because there are no established rules about what changes carry over, and I needed to turn on a lamp somewhere in a house full of lamps. In contrast, one level you walk into a small study room with paintings all over the walls with no apparent exit. When you click on a flashing note on the table, it might as well say "click on a painting to progress". It's like they are drowning you in the deep end only to pull you up and say "stop drowning!" before shoving you back under.There are also a lot of smaller issues that don't break the game, and are expected from low budgets and small indie studios:     Awful voice acting     Graphical detail inconsistencies (some things look great, others look terrible)    Questionable level design    Terrible character animations     A plot that is a little hard to follow (but I haven't finished it yet so maybe it will straighten out)    Strange character designI really wanted to like this game. But I don't think it wanted me to like it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a horror game with a troubled past protagonist.This is a game with physics puzzles and platforming without a jump button.This is a game where decisions matter but all of those decision are binary markers and slight alterations to the ending. It's a game where "darkness" means pitch black and light barely propagates anywhere else making it difficult to see anything much less navigate around the chair that fell over in your path. This is a game with death and running from unkillable monsters where punishment for failure is a reload at a checkpoint too far back and often forcing you to rewatch the same cutscene and hear the same dialogue again and again.Would I recommend this? No.Would I say it's a bad game? No, not really. But - everything you'll see here you've seen elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this on my wishlist for so long, and completed it tonight. Completing it inspired me to write a review, and I never write reviews. This isn't a good thing.I'm a sucker for a spooky game with a strong story, and this game didn't give me much of either. The story, while overdone, would have resonated more with me if not for the INCREDIBLY tedious puzzles. And some I can't even call puzzles. I was just a dog told to find a bone, and then another bone, and then another- and if I didn't put the bones in proper order (which was rarely clear) nothing would be happen, and I'd be stuck. I don't require spoonfeeding when it comes to puzzles in games, but a little direction would have been nice.And then the baddies. Mother. Mother is a character reminiscent of Resident Evil with none of the fun. You can't run, really. You definitely can't fight back. You're just gonna get one-hitted back to the beginning of the "chapter" and have to re-do 30 minutes of tedious puzzles to HOPEFULLY not get smacked again.And all of this, with my chat trying to help me along (as I live-streamed this), the frustration, re-do's, only to get the worst ending of 3. I spent 8 hours on this game, I won't spend another 8 to try to get a better ending. I'm sad.

_childDocuments_.review: I would've marked this review as neutral, but there's no such option. I can't actually recommend  but at the same time it's not a bad game. is a psychological thriller with rather weak narrative part, while gameplay is more focused on "progression through locations via finding keys to locked doors etc.", from what you could expect puzzle-ish gameplay, but unfortunately on practice it's closer to pixelhunting in Point'n'Clicks (you're checking every damn drawer for a key here instead). Add (mostly) clunky "avoid that monster"/"run from that monster" sequences and that's all gameplay in this game.To sum up, there're some good things in this game too:+ Simple but somewhat interesting story. There're 3 endings and several rather interesting decisions during the game, but it would be too boring to replay whole game to get those.+ A decent work with light and darkness along with a couple of good ideas created spooky atmosphere in some moments.+ A couple of actually good gameplay moments.+- Good optimization and technical aspects, though visuals are rather bad/outdated. Sound/music/voiceovers were nice.- Plenty of horrible gameplay mechanics/decisions to extend playtime. You're often either running around same locations over and over again to find a "correct" pixel to interact with or solving obscure "puzzles". Add some misleading main character comments to the mix and you get a perfect combination for a frustration.All in all,  is a mediocre and totally skippable psychological horror/thriller game. I can't say that it's bad, but it was boring too often. Imagine a decent B-movie horror that was forcedly extended from 1,5 to 4 hours and you'll get a good idea about this game. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "kinda recommend" because this game gave me mixed vibes. It was fun, but at the same time, I hated it. Coupled with things being dark af, and you've got a game that is just plain brutal. Oh wait, there's more, you cannot crouch. I enjoyed it, though it was painfulPROS : Excellent graphics, a Nvidia 1060 can handle this game excellentlyThere is a lot of detail and interactivityThe locations make sense and are thoroughly interestingNeutral :Voice acting was sometimes good, sometimes medicoreThe hand monster thing is weird and not my forteThe souls or whatever can be a bit annoying You get stuck on props, and you cannot jumpYou cannot jumpCONS :Extremely frustrating. The puzzles sometimes don't make sense, and other times you don't realize you're goal is to solve a puzzleYOU CANNOT CROUCHThere are sections where I had to rely on either A.) _childDocuments_.review: INITIAL REVIEWSo after playing an hour of the I can say that it's super creepy, unsettling and has a fantastic atmosphere. Which is exactly what you want from a horror gameThe graphics are great, high textures, fantastic lighting. Definitely has it's own art style Animations are good. The only thing that feels a bit off is the sprinting as it looks like the guy is taking small steps. A good thing is that you do seem to have unlimited stamina, which is a nice bonusSounds are creepy and add to the overall atmosphereVoice acting is great but nothing to write home aboutThe puzzles so far aren't challenging, but you will have to explore the area to be able to solve themThe only thing I don't like is that you can't crouch behind object, which means you'll be more easily noticed. But that's very small gripe.So I'd definitely recommend the game if your looking to get creeped out and be put on edge___________________________________________________________FULL REVIEWSo after finishing the full game i'm going to have to retract some of my initial review as it's not 100% accurate to the full gameIt's a definitely a good game but lacks in certain areas.It does start out super creepy and unsettling, but eventually looses the creepiness as they use the same way to creep you out throughout the whole game. I got use to it after awhile. Although the atmosphere definitely makes up for that, as it's got lots of weird supernatural ♥♥♥♥ going on with objects moving and the buildings changing. I'd say this is the games strong point. You also go into a somewhat mirror reality, which has floating objects and a different  gradient over the game to tell you it's a different reality (Not sure that's the best way to describe it but that's the best I could come up with). some of these sections are great while others aren't as good. The games strong suit as I mentions above is where supernatural stuff is going on (if that's even the correct way to describe it) with objects floating. Closing one door opening other and being in a completely different area or having a building change layout on you. These are the games strong suit. Not the best description but I hope you get the pictureThe puzzles don't seem to get much harder although they do get some what repetitive in a sense that I think I picked up like 10 or so keys throughout the whole game to unlock doors. There was even one point where the game turned into a platformer, which felt very out of place. They say it's a psychological horror but for some odd reason they decide to throw in chase scenes, which is straight out of survival horror and personally doesn't fit in psychological horror, which relies on mental, emotional, and psychological states to frighten, disturb, or unsettle its audience. I wouldn't mind it if they didn't feel like Btech versions of Outlast/Amnesia. The running animation isn't very good, which I mentioned in my initial review and the death animation aren't very good either. There's was a lot of potential here, it just falls flat in certain areas with being repetitive and having lackluster chase scenes, but does have some great moments with the weird supernatural stuff going on, which I really enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I've been waited for Those Who Remain to be out.Well the wait was over and I found myself in Eddy's shoes quickly after launch.After playing the game...I find it difficult to recommend...Here is why.In summary it is not a bad game.Level design is wonderful.Graphics are mostly beautiful and there are great light games that add to the feel.The sound is good and voice acting is doing the job.but that's about it...The game play is simple and superficial (you can't jump, you can't crouch).It is a short game...about 6 hours with a lunch break.The game mostly consist on go through corridors, turn the light switch, look at the lockers, find a note...run from monster and again...There are some good tension and scares out there in the game, but they are just few and there is a build up missing here.I couldn't find myself connecting to the characters or immersing myself with the plot as it is not that clear sometimes and not really connect.There are few endings to the game, but I found myself unable to play it again to get them all.my verdict is 5/10 - could have been a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain was a hard one to judge for a Steam review, because of the polar opposite characteristics when it comes to the game's quality. Those are the hardest to give just a yay or nay on, because quite frankly it's all about ignoring the negatives to see the positives of the game's experience. And let's be clear: Those Who Remain nails a creepy atmosphere for a horror game: a game that puts you on edge and makes you wonder what's around the corner. The story, while being similar to tropes before it, does intrigue you enough to want to see what happens next. The game does reward you with exploring to get a little more information about the people you have to make choices on.The gameplay however is where the game falters, which can lead you down frustrating paths of dead ends and not knowing what to do. UI elements are so precise at how you open them that you can easily miss the one cabinet you need to open, and the inconsistency of being able to open things can make you think that it's not even an option. It introduces a new mechanic that it doesn't use for a while, and the game then starts to get samey very quickly. Those Who Remain may have been able to get over this if the presentation was a bit better, but several elements will take you out of the experience rather quickly as the game descends into uncanny value.The achilles heel for Those Who Remain however is one undeniable truth: it's inconsistent rule set. Where you can be grabbed in the dark by the baddy by not turning on a light......a floor above. See, the problem with something even as simple as that, where it may not be on the main path of how to get through the level: is it makes the user question EVERYTHING about the game, and that leads to unfortunate backtracking, and to frustration. Where the game puts you in a new situation that you really don't know if you can now break a rule that was established before. This is why the game ultimately ends up getting the nay from me: the above atmosphere ends up being broken due to the repetition and the uncanny nature of what you're experiencing, to the point where the frustration overloads and makes you want to stop. If you can really overshadow everything for just atmosphere alone: Those Who Remain does deserve your time. Otherwise, it's a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Did I enjoy playing Those Who Remain? Yes. Would I recommend it? Meh. I enjoyed it enough to play through it, but like others mentioned, the storyline is lackluster and the horror element isn't too intense. The game just didn't quite captivate me to feel for the characters, which is something I revere most in any game. I was fond of the game's theme of isolating myself to illuminated zones and avoiding the dark at all costs. The puzzles were enjoyable, as they didn't inflict unnecessary stress or push me to glance over a walk-through guide. I also appreciated how the devs kept things fresh throughout the game; the effort was there and admired. All-in-all Those Who Remain is not the greatest horror game to hit the market, but it's certainly not a candidate for the bargain bin. If you're one for mediocre horror thrills, smooth lighting, simple (yet relaxing) puzzles and generic ghost stories, this game is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: What a joke.In my one hour gameplay, all I did was searching key objects without any lead. Those essentials can be hidden at any corner: a key hidden in a unimpressive drawer that you need to fully open a already half-opened gate; a fuse fully covered underneath a random box; a hotel key under the doormat in near darkness and player was given 0 hint, 0 lead at all.The graphic is not effective, a weird place like a huge glass window at a Motel. Many large spaces are unfilled, and the light does not feel right. The story is dropping pieces, one time I am at a motel, then a deserted house, and suddenly I am at a mystery place with a door that leads to a gas station, where the player needs to go back in time through an extremely bright door. Running back to the past just to interact with those cannot be interact "now" is plain and boring, a waste of time - actually, the whole searching part is a waste of time with no story base, just "Follow the light". Speaking of the ghosts, I do not see any horror because they are dull and just remain silent and still like ordinary trees.Then bugs. I picked up a book twice, both times it sank into the table on different sides, not to mention the lighter is automatically turned on once picked, with no indicator showing gas consumption. I went out in the darkness, only to see it turn off suddenly when I am surrounded by ghosts. A quick game over, then starting over a long while ago. I CANNOT recommend this game even for a sale price.If you are into horror games, save your money and time and go for some quality games like "In Sound Mind" instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game and would recommend it, if you look for a story focused horror game.The game is linear and not too long but has a pretty nice story and atmosphere.It offers 3 different endings depending on the choices you make during the plot.The game took inspiration from several horror games and mixed it together in my opinion in a good way. Some parts remembered me a bit of Layers of Fear and Alan Wake.Mainly you will have to explore / find specific objects, solve puzzles and hide / escape.There are some more intense / scary moments and also some more quite story and exploration focused parts.From a technical point of view there is not much to complain about. Some of the character models could use some more polish but since they are anyway not used to often and the environment textures / lightning etc. look nice it's really not a big deal.Another thing worth to mention for the german speaking people is that the game offers a very nice german voice over. The main protagonist is spoken by a professional german voice actor I already know from other games / movies. That's not that common for a game from such a small team so I think that's really worth to mention.Also I had a technical issue with the game and contacted the support.Not only did I get immediately reply, but they tried everything they could to find the issue and help.I was already in touch with support from many other developers but this one was definately one of if not the best experiences i had in this regard.So even tough the game is a bit short I think it's definately worth the money and I can only recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Short but enjoyable 5 Hour walking sim where you explore a small town with some trippy visuals at points but disappointing ending. Grab it for 5-8$ CND at most. I enjoyed with time in "Those Who Remain"... but there is a few things that you should know.The ending is abrupt and makes everything pointless imo (there are 3 but they all end up just as abrupt and pointless) so this is definitely a "journey is more important than destination" type of games. Also, the story can be confusing but its actually rather simple once you piece it together. It tries to make a point about morality being ambiguous or something but most "decisions" you make (which will determine your short 5 second ending) in the game are rather binary and I never felt like I needed time to reflect on my choices cause of big philosophical conundrum. The game is very clearly trying to pay tribute to horror classics such as Silent Hill, you explore a small town that has an alternate nightmare reality composed of people`s regrets, but unlike that game, the nightmare that haunts the main character is the misshapen body of a woman with headlight for a head and a pole going through them.. so no subtle at all, you will most likely understand why that is the first time you see them. You are also chased by a crying woman at some points, and a troll?? However your main and worst enemy is the dark..literally (which is an obvious reference to Alan Wake), stepping into any darkness is an instant kill and this game has low gamma by default, so if you are playing the game and you are looking at a wall and all you see is a black square, definitely raise the gamma asap. Unlike other so called "Walking Sims" (cause c`mon this game is not really horror), the game actually lets you sprint... fast and without any annoying stamina bars, which I really appreciated, because making you walk like a snail to pad you game is BS. But this can be a double edge sword, cause as I mentioned.. a single step into the dark is an instant kill and when you are jogging fast around an area, sometimes you will accidentally step into the dark. Another thing you constantly gotta keep doing, is very slowly enter a room and carefully look for a light switch, because if you take one step too far... you guess it, instant kill, and for some reason sometimes the checkpoints can be a few minutes back (one time I had to repeat a 15 minute sequence cause of a single mistep).As for puzzles, there is a few but most are very easy to figure out, which I also appreciated.. cause im so tired of horror games that have the most obscure puzzles that waste hours of my time. The only time that I was annoyed, was when the game wasn't very clear of what my objective was, but if you go to every room and click on everything you can click, you will most likely figure it out.So basically, what you are getting is a game where you teleport around a series of small town locations, sometimes being chased, sometimes things get trippy, sometimes you go to an alternate version of the town where everything is the same except blue and it has moon physics, connected by a meh storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: An unremarkable and periodically irritating experience that is content to be safe and predictable. The "protective light" paradigm has been implemented far better in many other games, the lighting here isn't even impressive or artful and most of the environments look ugly. Nothing remotely frightening happens and this also has some of the worst chase sequences ever, painfully quotidian. I swear to God if I play one more horror game where I have to flee from a banshee - I'm giving it a zero. There is an awful narrative structure which involves you reading several notes in an area to inform your decision regarding a character's fate, and the moment before you make your choice an NPC regurgitates the exact same information you just read 5 minutes ago. Why? Do the developers really have that little confidence in their players?Those who remain to complete this game are rewarded with emptiness.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who saw this game advertised on imgur a few years ago, i was really interested by the concept of a "jumpscare free" horror game, not because i hate jump scares, but because i prefer psycological horror. I did stream this game and got several viewers who said they enjoyed watching the play through.... heres some things i have to say:The game is buggy, there were several times an item would glitch into another item and fly across the room i was in or something.The game is lacking in the graphic quality department, i dont personally have an issue with this, but i know some people do so im pointing it out in my review.Every now and then you have to look for something in a game and it seems impossible to find. so a little context here, this game i streamed over a session of 3 streams. at the end of night one and night two i stopped playing the game because i could not find items the game wanted me to find... night one was because of a bug and night two is because it was a tiny item in a massive area.you will most likely die, not because youre bad at the game, but because the monsters will catch you out, there are several spots in this game where you get cornered and just have to accept your fate.some of the things in the game seem to exist just because they look cool, not because they make any logical sense in the story, for example... the hall of arms in the images for the store pages exists for only a few minutes in the game and doesnt really do anything except be creepy, like its cool... but it was a big build up for not much going on at that point in the game.this game did a very good job of giving me chills from time to time, the room you are in will change or something and you wont expect it to and it works well.the ending feels rushed, not bad.... it just happens very quick and left me with a "welp, thats it i guess" kind of feeling. (small spoiler that wont ruin your gameplay) the choices you make in the game affect how the game ends, i may be more pleased with the ending if i replay the game and make other choices, however the choices seem................. poorly thought out and arent explained very well... the effects they cause arent explained in any way, youre just given a choice. kinda imagine if little sisters in Bioshock were never explained to you... what happens when you decide what happens to them, it makes a greater overall impact on the game than people realize.I did very much enjoy this game, i just think it could use a little more work... im glad it got released though instead of never launching at all. there are so many indie games that just dont make it to market, so im glad i got to experience this and i look forward to more games like this from the developer. i think they had a great idea and i would like to see more like it!

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain (TWR) is a first-person horror adventure that tries to be scary, serious, and mature, but ends up being mostly annoying and just plain awful. It features a fairly interesting (albeit disappointingly generic) story, easy puzzles, terrible chase and stealth scenes, and a catastrophically bad checkpoint-based save system that forces you to replay already solved parts multiple times, before the game kills you again without warning, and you have to repeat the same boring stuff for yet another time. The story was good enough to make me want to see the end, but the gameplay was very poor, in fact it may very well be the worst out of any of the three-digit number of horror games that I have completed over the past 35 years.Those are strong words, and I actually wish I were exaggerating because that would mean that the game was better, but sadly I'm not. I actually deleted my first attempt at a review because it used even stronger words, and I wanted to let a few days pass, hoping that I might see some redeeming features in this game after the initial disappointment wore off. Well, several days have passed, and my assessment unfortunately hasn't changed. So here's a list of the many, many things that make this game a failure in my opinion, written with calm sadness a few days after completing it.(Please note: Due to a character limit, I can only fit two-thirds of my review here. If you're interested, you can read the full thing here:  )(continued at  )

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, you can only do one of two things. You either have a horror game based on darkness where you can hardly see anything, or you have a horror game about looking for and through a ton of stuff. If you've ever had to look for something in real life, like, say, your keys or your wallet, in the dark, in a cluttered room, and you have no idea where they could be, that is what this game feel like. It's not that it's impossible, or even hard; it's that I can just think to myself, do I want to spend five, or god forbid, ten minutes of my life looking for some mcguffin to open the next of a hundred metaphorical doors? Especially when there are plenty of better, more entertaining horror games on offer? The answer is no. A puzzle is one thing, something that you can logically think through with all of the pieces there to put together. Having to scrounge around in the dark for a jigsaw piece is something else, something that I have a far and away lower patience for. Maybe the game is good, maybe it gets better later on, but if this is the kind of gameplay I have to slog though, I'd rather just watch a let's play of someone who already knows what to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but it's mediocre during it's best moments and obnoxious during its worst moments. Unfortunately, the bad moments are far more frequent than the former. The game is very janky. I frequently encountered issues with event triggers, enemy AI, and clipping through walls. Even if you can look past that, you are left with a low quality puzzle game with very, very light horror elements. Don't expect this game to provide any scares. If the plot were good, maybe the game would be salvageable, but it's just a collection of tired horror tropes. You can easily guess the entire plot within the first hour or so. The event at the core of the events is unoriginal and really tame for a horror game like this. If judgement is going to be a theme of your game, make sure the event you are judging people for has real weight to it. This game completely failed at that aspect, which removes all the weight from the choices in the game. I got this in a bundle for dirt cheap, but even so it really isn't worth the time it takes to play it. It had some interesting ideas and I kept hoping a plot or gameplay twist would help salvage it, but it never did.

_childDocuments_.review: Awful.Gameplay is going through a series of set pieces (levels) looking for items. Lots of opening of cabinet drawers. Sounds exciting, right? Then you get to judge people to death or forgiveness according to ludicrously superficial stakes. This guy did something really bad ... but he was going through some tough stuff himself. Wow, really makes you think, right? So deep.I'm not sure which is worse, the writing or the voice acting, but both excelled at draining me of all delight. Also, I hope you like jump scares. You don't? Of course not, nobody does and it's the cheapest and most annoying way to do "horror". It's this game's only trick. Oh wait, there are also instant-death chase scenes. Not scary, just frustrating, and another fan favorite. Not.It's also a technical mess. Something is way off with the contrast, making the bright lights just unbearably bright. Half of the time you can't see anything. The camera is wonky as hell and will produce stuttering no matter how powerful your rig. And the physics are right out of Goat Simulator.Skip this, please. It is really really bad. I like to support indie devs, but in this case I think they are mocking us. Not only do I want my money back, but I want an apology, too.And don't trust most of these positive reviews. They smell inauthentic and paid. Steam has a rat problem!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a massive load. I've had it on my wishlist for ages and it was a MASSIVE letdown.First and foremost, the mechanics suck.It is a game where the core gameplay revolves around staying in the light. While this sounds cool initially, really it just means flicking on lightswitches to make entire rooms "safe" with no pressure of them becoming unsafe again.It is VERY hard to tell what is considered light and what is considered dark. There are areas of black shadow you can stroll through safely, and there are areas of slight dimness where you instantly die. An exception annoyance is that many rooms are "dark" and unsafe, but you are allowed (and intended) to walk a few steps in, look to the side and flick on the lightswitch. Other rooms will kill you instantly for attempting that. Deaths set you back to the start of the area so any death like this means running back around to collect all the usable items.The entire game is completely linear; walk to A, pick up B, walk to C, use B on D, repeat. There's no room for creativity or problem solving. Many "puzzles" were very simply laid out, others seemed to just be guesswork, an element that came up in many monster scenes which hinged on "choose which of these 20 doors is unlocked" far more times than was welcome.Pet peeve, I LOATHE games like this where you collect things or search for clues when they put in 500,000 drawers and lockers to open and search when only about 1-2 have things in them across the whole game. Obviously they cut down work by reusing assets, because I've never seen so many excuses to have locker rooms in a game just so they could fill the space with a copy pasted empty locker.The story was ABYSMAL. Going by "the good ending" that I got, the opening scene was completely unrelated to the story and just a weak excuse for why the character is where they are. The rest of the events are completely unrelated to the character. You find many characters related to those events and judge them by either "forgiving" or "condemning" them. Roughly 3 of these characters had the exact same actions, motives and outcomes, none of them were unique at all. There was no challenge to doing any of the options, it was literally just "click A or B to choose what your ending will be later." When the ending came for me it wasn't even really a scene, just "GOOD JOB."Monster encounters were awful. You can sprint around, dance right behind them, whatever, as long as they aren't looking right at you you're safe, and they basically just walk in a straight line down hallways. The game is overly reliant on jumpscares made through forced camera changes and things just appearing instantly with a loud noise, because there's no real tension in the atmopshere.Character animations and models were poor at best. Voice acting was bland. The main character was monotone and boring, and a character meant to be creepy and evil just talked like some guy having a casual chat.Really wish I had've listened to the reviews on this one and never bought it, or at least finished it fast enough for a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I was looking forward to this game for awhile now, but was severely disappointed with the gameplay, dialogue, story, and horror aspect of the game. Super dull, and not scary. ALSO THIS IS THE FIRST REVIEW I'VE EVER WRITTEN IN MY 7+ YEARS ON STEAM, THAT'S HOW DISAPPOINTED I WAS. (Also, my friend also bought this game with me and I couldn't bear through it so I just watched him finish it so I can just refund this game).The game plays like a bad MMO where you run back and forth the same area fetching items. An example per se, *find a screwdriver* *oh its in the house i bet* *get screwdriver to open door* *ahh now i need a ladder, bet its in the house* *got the ladder* *now i need a flashlight, bet its in the house* - imagine that all game but the character even says all this dialogue. The "Monsters" or "Ghosts" are also not scary, they're tossed around the game like H-Mags in a weebs house, after the first 10 minutes of the game you've probably seen hundreds of these NON MOVING enemies that just very tediously block your path. 100% loses all scare appeal and potential super early in. The character dialogues are super dull, its like reading / hearing a bad middle-school theater classes 1st semester submission. No emotion either, feels like I'm listening to a google translate web browser.  It also has many of the same aspects as Alan Wake, which isn't a bad thing, BUT it was just so poorly executed. It's as if they were huge fans of that franchise and wanted to create a game to commemorate the series but instead made a game so horrible that Alan Wake seems way better than it should now. And Alan isn't even amazing to begin with. This game takes everything that was wrong with Alan Wake being in the horror genre AND AMPLIFIED THAT BY 9000 AND THEN ADDED IN BAD GAMEPLAY AND STORY TO BOOT.Don't waste your time, you'll have a more genuine and scary experience shopping at walmart without a mask.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice horror game that addresses the relationship between light and dark.There's a subtle message in the game about this: there are dark things in the light, vice-versa.It has a very strong environment, which becomes extremely unnerving sometimes. The town has a very classical look, which makes it hard to establish in the timeline. Sometimes it looks like we're in the 50's, some others it looks more modern. I'm guessing this is intentional.There's no combat, so I'd recommend this to the slower examiner explorer kind of player.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the money. Not a bad experience per say, but really wasn't able to grip me. The atmosphere ends up being a swing and a miss. This is due to several factors. Attention to detail is inconsistent. This might sound nit picky but having rain when you can see an open sky with starts above you bothers me. And that's really not something you can chalk up to "Its just trying to mess with you man". The puzzles I had come across were insultingly easy, the game play consists of opening drawers to find keys, with nothing to make that specific lame mechanic interesting. It did not do a whole lot outside of the little bit of story it had to keep me playing in the first hour and a half. The first moral choice was mildly interesting, but it really didn't feel like it had enough meat on its bones. The cat and mouse sequences, for lack of better way to describe them, don't feel like a threat what so ever due to your insane run speed and lack luster death animation. And the music does a lot to hamper this game, but not because its bad in particular. The beginning of the game could just benefit greatly from a good dose of silence.There are good moments I came across that seem like they could redeem the game if I continued playing. I just don't think its worth it for the extra couple of slightly unsettling scenes 2 hours later in the game. The light concept is cool at first thought, but for the the portion I played it didn't seem like anything truly interesting was done with it. Though a lot of what I've said should be taken with some perspective. I play a lot of horror games, and this game had some relatively high expectations. For someone that isn't much of a veteran in the genre,  this game could possibly be moderately entertaining in terms of scare value and story . At the end of the day I purchased this game for a good horror experience, and I feel like it didn't deliver for the expectations I had.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a good 7/10. The creepiness is fantastic in the beginning, but once you get the hang of how the game works it really does die off. _childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain is a game that I thought I wanted for a long time, until I played it. The graphics are mostly mediocre, sometimes they look a little better, the sounds are pathetic along with terrible voice acting. The puzzles aren't fun, there isn't any balance. They are either blatantly obvious or obscure nothing in-between. Everything feels stiff and sluggish, like walking through molasses. The controls are unresponsive and sluggish. I got to the point where I would just let the character die, he's very unlikable and I didn't care. I decided that I really despise "stay in the light games" after this. Thankful that I got this in a cheap bundle and didn't pay much for it. Not recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 5 hours in the game and I don't know how much longer it'll take to finish it.  One thing I do know is that I will continue to play because the story is interesting and I want to see the ending. I love how the light is used to create the atmosphere and although I'm usually not a big fan of bloom, the effect has been used brilliantly in this game.  The soundscape and ambient noises are excellent as well, and a lot of the tense atmosphere is created with it. Looking around with the (xbox) controller is much too slow by default, but you can easily adjust this in the settings. The writing could be a bit better and the animation of the NPCs is the weakest part of the game. Nevertheless,  if you love horror/exploration/adventure with little or no action, but with focus on the narrative in an eerie atmosphere (instead of cheap jump scares), then you might love this game too.

_childDocuments_.review: "Those Who Remain" is a 5 hour game that is about 5 hours too long.Incompetently designed from start to finish with gameplay mostly consisting of walking into a room, turning on a light, picking up notes that avoid subtlety or nuance like it's the plague, and then being confused for 3 minutes trying to figure out wtf the game wants you to do. The enemy design is laughable at best and pitiful at worst without a single moment of tension existing at any point during the experience. And whoever allowed those "Stealth" sections to see the light of day should be tried for a federal offense. How the ♥♥♥♥ are you gonna have a stealth section where you A. Can't crouch B. Can't out run/out maneuver the monster, and C. are stuck in a tiny a$$ room with it, searching random drawers for dumb notes that are required to progress.The storyline is immediately apparent from the first 20 seconds and the voice actor sounds like the devs woke him up at 4am, kicked him in the chest a few times, handed him a mic and yelled "READ IT QUIETER DAMMIT!!" everytime he tried to show emotion. The game also spells out its themes and ideas like you're the slowest chimpanzee who's still working through pre-k for the 20th year in a row.It's a combination of copy and pasted ideas from better games and movies, without a single original idea in sight. Silent Hill, Observer, Amnesia, The Shining, Stranger Things, Repulsion (though I doubt the devs have even seen that movie with how embarrassing their "homage" was) nothing is safe from this game's shameless copy and pasting. It also looks like pure a$$, and these devs need a quick lesson in Unity's post processing because apparently it's too hard for these jugheads to figure out. You know the color grading is awful when the fire looks grey.Even the music is really annoying and they probably would have been better suited to just let ol' Kevin Macleod do the honors. Seriously, nothing escapes the mindnumbingly awful brush that these unimaginative paste eaters smear over every inch of the experience. How Wired Productions picked this up to publish is beyond me.It was kinda funny how bad it was at first, but that feeling wore off after about 30 minutes. Then after 3 hours of the same repetitive nonsense, I looked up how much more there was, and decided to call it when I saw there was still over 2 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hours left. I looked up the rest of the story/ending (which was exactly as terrible as I predicted) and went to bed, never to touch this travesty of a video game again. If steam had a rating scale, I would give it a 0.5/10. Because the game turns on when I hit play, so I guess half a point for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly can't recommend the game. There are too many grievances with not enough good stuff to offset them. The game is obviously cribbing hard off of Silent Hill, but with none of the symbolism, imagery, or thought put into it like that series.Graphics range from pretty alright to mediocre. The voice acting is mediocre. The mechanics, such as they are, are often poorly defined. The puzzles range from very easy to being pure grade A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (such as hiding an item on top of a palette mover that you have to click to lower so that you see the item on top of boxes... how exactly was I supposed to know that was there, developers?).The game is massively frustrating where "cut scenes" will sometimes drag on far too long after they've completed, are unskippable even if it's the ninth time you've seen it, and checkpoints are often few and far between requiring you to go through whole sections over and over again.One of the worst parts is how little credit the developers give the player - you find little documents scattered around that paint a picture of the sort of person the people you are judging are... but they're entirely meaningless, as right before you have to make the judgement, you'll get documents that blatantly spell out what is going on, assuming that everyone playing is too stupid to figure it out themselves.It had a strong start, I was very intrigued, but the rest of the game was often slow, annoying, frustrating, and just not a fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A greatly atmospheric game with an emphasis on single player story driven content. You play Edward, a man who seemingly has nothing to live for. Driving to a seedy motel to meet with a woman he's having an affair with, things start to drastically go downhill as someone steals his car. Reminiscent of Alan Wake with the 'stay out of the darkness' type gameplay, you'll explore the town of Dormont by solving puzzles in the police station, the post office, the sawmill, firestation and other locations. There are sections where you have to avoid a monster, and the puzzles are balanced in a way that may make you scratch your head for a moment before logic dictates what you need to do to progress.Pros:  - Great atmosphere  - Immersive story with moral choices that actually make you stop and think  - Puzzles are well balanced and will make you think  - Genuinely eerie encounters Cons: - Insta-death segments are not fun. Trial and error with a few sections - Segments where you are fetch questing breaks the immersive atmosphere.  - Could be more checkpoints littered in segments. After inadvertently stepping into the 'dark' and being chopped up by the spectres, it was draining to go ALL the way back to the start of the section. - Stealth sections are a little clunky and outdatedOverall, I'd recommend this game to people who want to experience a genuine horror/eerie adventure in the vein of BioShock or Alan Wake. The town of Dormont seemed well established and I'd like to find out more about the residents that live there. Game will probably last you about 4-5 hours, dependant on logic skills and how fast it takes you to find certain key items.   You can check out Inside Your Screen's playthrough here:

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could have enjoyed the game. The atmosphere is really cool, the creature designs are pretty unique and..... that's all positives I can give. The story is mildly interesting, the "moral" choices are bland and the ending changes on whether you make good or bad choices, whose goodness and badness is very arbitrary. Letting a serial killer with a fully loaded gun, who has no intention of stopping serial killing, leave unharmed is apparently a morally good choice.The "puzzles" are similarly inane. Look for a random key under a random box, inch into a room to check if there is a light switch, randomly try valves to find the correct ones, click a lamp that you thought was just set dressing, open the third drawer from the left to find a key etc. You get the picture.The checkpoints are insultingly spaced. You complete the entire section, die to bs and have to do the last 5 minutes again, including listening to dialogue breaks where you can't move.That really is the crux of my issues. The game does not respect your time. I would not recommend this game even if it was free, nevermind for 20 Bucks.I do hope the dev team learned a lot from this project as they had a lot of cool ideas,  especially when it comes to creature and environment design.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about loss, about how it affects our lives and everyone else around us.The environment is haunting and beautiful, with a washed down tone that evokes feelings of despair and loneliness.The game itself works more like like a scary investigation than hardcore horror. There's no split second button mashing to escape something or hiding in closets or anything like that. There are monsters and chase sequences, but these feel like they belong to the world, not to the gameplay itself. Your purpose is to investigate and find out what happened. They're there to stop you.Had a lot of fun with it. Felt like a light smooth horror experience.

If you die, you're going back to the beginning of the level to redo your puzzles.- Ugly environments- Bad voice actingThose reasons aren't why I'm reviewing this. The absolute worst part of this jank game are the  you will encounter. They are very frequent and surprisingly unpredictable. You will be doing a puzzle in an adequately lit room and have to go down some stairs only to be surprised by a giant white light. It's even worse when you walk through the door, which fills yours entire screen with white light.You  get a headacheYou  go blindFor your own safety,  play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was very disappointed by this game. Its a pretty standard horror puzzle game with a few slight variations. The gameplay is similar to so many other indie horror out there. You wander around buildings trying to find keys and solve"puzzles". Some of the ideas with using light can be cool, and the guys in the darkness are creepy for the first 1-2 levels then don't matter. A lot of the problem is the gameplay. Most of the time your just walking around aimlessly looking for a hidden key or random item to interact with. There are levels with 40 lockers and 8 different rooms and you have to open every drawer to find 1 thing. Then randomly you will have to know after going downstairs to go 2 floors upstairs to read a piece of paper on a desk. A lot of the sequences have no direct and seem like random things you need to do in a specific order for no reason. Sometimes it involves moving a box you didnt know youi could or interacting with an object that isn't lit up to interact with compared to other objects. Without consulting a walkthrough intermittently it would be hard to know what to do throughout. The story isn't very interesting, the ability to make decisions on peoples fate can be interesting but its a binary good/bad and most of it seems pretty obvious what decision to make based on what the game says. The main monster looks dumb and has some bad erratic pathing, but there are a few good scares in the game. Overall the game is pretty boring, and the puzzle solving seems just designed for you to do it without cause or interaction with the story. 5.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: First of graphics and atmosphere are good, however control scheme and overall flow of the game kills any enjoyment for me. controls are simplistic and sometimes don't work correctly. And the parts where there is an active monster present don't feel scary when you can't even crouch or look behind a corner. it just feels off. The idea of going through a town with ghost people watching you is cool and all, but all the places you visit feel like they exist only on their own. you have no sense that it all fits together as a town. for me that ruined my immersion and believability of the game. besides that the horror elements most of the time don't work that well. and although the shadow people are cool and gave me a chill their presence wasn't scary at all 10 minutes after their first introduction. Then you have the active monster that walks around and kills you if he sees you. But as far as i know he does not react to sound only to seeing you. making it very easy and not scary to get around him and run away. overall cool looking game, not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty good game, i enjoyed it over all.the story is pretty interesting, However, it was pretty predictable.one of the chase scenes was pretty terrible and quite frustrating.There are quite a few things that could be fixed and changed.Namely fixing a few of the levels so as to not let you fall OFF of the map and into the endless void if you wander too far forcing a quite out and reload. a death barrier under the entire map would fix this.There are quite a few objects and walls that have ZERO collision.i managed to break the lighting in a few of the levels. The game was acting like there were lights but it was pitch black. This glitch also lets you bypass flickering lights with the ghosts that kill you.A couple of the puzzles had ZERO clues on how to solve them, nothing in game at all. i had to resort to googling to figure them out which really breaks immersion and ruins the flow of the game. It's also frustrating. There were a few times when an event was supposed to trigger but it simply didn't. Forcing me to wonder around for 30 plus minutes til it decided to trigger randomly.A Journal to log all the audio clues and text files you find in game. It would make solving a certain set of puzzles easier and help keep track of any missed collectibles/papers.this is less a review and more a list of stuff for the Devs to take a look at.

_childDocuments_.review: I find "Those who remain" both undercooked and incredibly successful. It feels unfinished but powerful, always finding the perfect balance between sadness, tension and pure horror.If you blended Frictional Game's "SOMA" with a John Carpenter movie like "Prince of darkness","The fog" or "Village of the damned" you would probably get something like "Those who remain", a creepy, suspenseful game that gets under your skin. This walking sim / horror puzzle game succeeds thanks to its outstanding sound design, which transforms the game's creatures, jumpscares and scenarios into something truly terrifying.  It's been ages since I experienced an atmosphere as compelling and frightening as "Those who remain"'s one. The game itself is pretty much searching for clues and objects and running and hiding from monsters. Its simplicity is far from maddening, quite the opposite, I find it definitely rewarding in here. Your mind doesn't need to wander very far to solve its puzzles. On the contrary, you are forced to face moral dilemmas, creepy sounds, bad memories and scary voices with all your heart. It's been a while since I experienced this kind of tension.At the same time, "those who remain""really needs some polish as a game. For a game focused in "light" and detail, some areas are incredibly dark and low resolution so it is almost impossible to find anything. You cannot see a thing, and I mean it in a very literal way. Besides, the game crashed and i've fallen out of scenarios several times, mostly in the post office and the supermarket areas. But for every bug or unpolished aspect, there are several good ideas that make it worth it. Almost seven hours in and I'm still being surprised and having a blast. To my mind, more ambitious (and obviously more "indie") than Outlast II or Amnesia:Rebirth, and more satisfying, despite its formal shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the nice trailer & cool font design on the store page, it's mediocre at best. That & the artwork tries to sell it as some 80s-retro-synthwave-type of thing that is in fashion right now, but there is very little, if any, of that in the actual game.Some nice ideas, environmental puzzles & visual style mixed with a lot of frankly horrible character models, tired cliche's, sadly overused assets (HQ Residential House, again...) & some incredibly frustrating clunky controls at times (like how close can I get to an enemy in the darkness in order to reach within throwing distance to some boxes that is blocking light that I need to shine, or to press a button, and how do I know when a button switches OFF the light in the room in which I'm standing, or TURNS ON the light in the next room?).Admittedly I like some of the light work & the concept of going into a different dimension to alter things in the real world in order to progress. The gameplay is also varied, & the voice acting, puzzles & stealth sections are okay. But the writing is terrible. The script & dialogue... Oh dear. And unfortunately that, along with some really hit & miss enemy encounters, stealth & chase sections & embarrassing “moral choices”, brings one out of it quite a lot.I usually have huge issues being “bad” in games, even if it's by accident I tend to linger on it for days. But in this game, basically everyone is an a-hole who deserves the worst karma. I honestly don't even know how people stomach to get the “good” ending for any other reason than for the achievements sake. The thing about forgiveness is that it sounds great, but in some cases you're not doing someone a favor by forgiving them. For some, being caught and made accountable for something is the best thing that ever happened to them, and put them on the right path in life. Forgiveness (or looking the other way because you feel sorry for someone, as is often the attempted strategy in this game I feel) is occasionally irresponsible & down right mean. Of course in game terms putting blame where it belongs usually means murdering the one at fault, and that is of course a smidge exaggerated... Plus it doesn't make you any better, of course. So sure, the karma system kinda works, I guess. But it does have a somewhat strange aftertaste.

_childDocuments_.review: it's amazing that it took me 8+ hours to finish the game once. maybe some of i was eating or something. but i was mostly playing during that time.since the game is possible to finish around 3 hours if you have a general idea of what you are doing.STORYI enjoyed the disturbing atmosphere in this,as well as the story telling. it truly got exciting though when it is revealed you get to judge characters. sending them to hell or heaven presumably.which inspired me to keep going to see what other have done and decide their fate!these choices however effect the ending.minor spoiler. good,bad and nightmare. 2 are obvious and the 3rd should be clear how to get after getting the last of those.having said that. other than backing up saves and reloading...you will need to replay the entire game to get everything...which...for me is not an exciting idea...GAMEPLAYA "walking simulator" as some call them. though there are objects you can pick up and throw. mostly for fun.most of the puzzles in game are pretty strait forward. some require you to pay attention to your surroundings, read notes,or find symbols. also figure out what to do between dimensions (there is a alternate world that looks similar to the main one)dying was personally THE MOST ANNOYING aspect of the experience.the 2 main causes of this are shadow people and special creatures that chase you.the chasing things are the more annoying ones. you instantly die if they get you. but what bothers me is the checkpoints. they put them too far back pretty often. instead of right before a chase. you have to get to the chase. which sometimes means going through cut scenes again or other delays making it more tedious...even more so when as mentioned prior. in some cases lighting scripts broke...better placed checkpoints would have been nice.OVERALLThere were some frustrating moments in this. but for the most part i enjoyed the experience and would recommended it to those into these kind of games.GLITCHSthere were a few times this game has issues with its lighting script (sawmill, and annicas house)where the lights would not be working properly. in 1 case. they would be on. even though it looked like it was  another i died and lights would be off for some reason.in my case,the half of the sawmill that was closer to the entrance was effected.and at annicas house after a death her mothers room was.this would be bad under normal circumstances. but in a game where lighting is a matter of life or death.this was unacceptable!restarting the game did fix some of these (did not test all)there was a minor glitch in annicas house, where i got a copy of a key i already used. thankfully it somehow left my inventory on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: Running down the corridor with furniture obstacles, that you need to remove in seconds, escaping monster - what could be "better"? Only absence of checkpoint before this run and 6 doors to guess for correct one in the end of the run - and in case of mistake you must start all over.Game seemed to be walking simulator with relaxing gameplay occationly having short stealth parts... and suddenly you are stressed with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "run, GUESS, stuck, dead, repeat" (emphasis on GUESS, you cant figure out correct path in seconds). So game suggests to you replay this damn run several times in order to memorize correct actions sequence until finally succeed. I'll remind you, that checkpoint, for God only know reason why, is NOT BEFORE RUN, but about 1-2 min before. It seems not much, but it is absolutely enough to be extremely annoying.The biggest problem is contrast between this idiotic part and the rest of the game. It looks like... chocolate cake with pork steak in the center. You bought cake, enjoy it and suddenly taste meat... Nice? Do you want to smash this cake in cook's face? Me too.I hate "frightened rabbit" gameplay. And game decieves you pretending not to have one for several hours, when it is too late to refund. It is just fraut.Given above I made conclusion that some of the devs are not quite sane. _childDocuments_.review: Well, it definitely isn't bad.I know, not the greatest way to start positive review, so let me unpack good stuf:storyline, for what I played - is pretty good. Nothing revolutionary, but what it does, it does well.Graphics are also pretty good.Locations are interesting.Finally the mechanics of not being able to walk into the dark, and always being cautious where there's a single source of light - are pretty good.The big bad: it is all unutilized. The execution doesn't really work it out to its full potential, at all. Somehow, it feels janky even if it isn't really janky, but.... I don't know... I can't put my finger on it.Its worth the money I paid for it, for sure, but after about 15 minutes short of 2 hours, and realizing I'm about 1/3 of the game in or so - I kind of had enough.Don't get me wrong - I wasn't timing my playthrough and looking to refund. I am not refunding. My playthrough just ended naturally because I stopped having fun.So, its uninstall and into the Archive group, which I know not to bother with again.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain - conceptually interesting, but terribly implemented in every aspect psychological horror.Script is simple, cliched, moral choices are way too unambiguous, there are no shades between good and evil: being good is always to forgive everyone no matter what they did (oh, they suffered so much themselves, poor things, let us feel sorry for them), otherwise you are revenge-obsessed moral monster (you won't get the good ending). Horror-part of Those Who Remain is mediocre. Only a few locations are able to provide a thick atmosphere of complete unsafety, bad nightmare. The screamers don't work at all. The ghosts with shining blue eyes look scary, but they are obvious threat: they're not frightening as much as if they were appearing less often, all of a sudden. They seem mostly decorative, like a fence or a wall, outlining the brim of an available area.Graphics are decent enough for a low-budget indie, gameplay-wise the game is a walking sim with quite awkward controls, the game design sometimes leaves much to be desired. Moveable objects are senselessly placed throughout levels, they are just garbage, that gets in the way. Tasks, requiring you to light the darkness to safely get through, are tedious: you move in constant gloom with no flashlight or other directional light source (yes, the concept is clear, but it is too inconvenient, even frustrating to navigate around locations, even so small ones; the flashlight could be added with lack of ability to scare monsters away).I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: is an atmospheric horror game that seems to fall short of what it could have been due to frustrating puzzles and a general lack of direction for the player. The game starts off with an intro where the protagonist/adulterer finally grew a conscience, decided to do the right thing and break things off with his mistress, Diana, as he is heading over to the motel outside the sleepy town of Dormant to meet her. Without spilling any spoilers, you'll quickly realize that this little guilty conscience bit isn't the main thing about the story when the game then introduces its actual main plot - . I guess it's safe to say that things took a turn for the worse. For an atmospheric game, Those Who Remain has some really nice graphics and sounds to match. There aren't any "jump scares" per se, but there's a time when a basketball was suddenly dropped in front of me that had startled me for a bit. This is an oddly random event, to be honest, and it doesn't even seem to be tied into the game (as in using the ball to solve a puzzle or something) or the story in any way. The story is pretty okay so far and the atmosphere is brilliant, but what I really didn't like about the game is its frustrating puzzles... well, not all of them are actual puzzles - many of them involve searching in every random drawer and underneath every random cardboard box in search of keys. Besides maybe the  part, there is no logic as to why certain items are "hidden" the way they were. To me, most of the puzzles here just feel like busywork... something to impede the storytelling whenever I'm starting to be interested in the story.If you couldn't find something, the game doesn't have a hint system unlike your typical hidden object games and you're just stuck there. However, I actually like the alternate dimension part of the gameplay where you'll solve a puzzle on "the other side" and reap your reward (an open door for instance) in the original dimension. It's not exactly a unique concept for someone who has played her fair share of HOGs and adventure-puzzle games though. So, TLDR?+ Nice stories so far but it sounds rather typical as far as horror stories go+ Some interesting game design choices (using shadowy people as invisible walls to stop you from going places you shouldn't be) and settings (different locations you can explore)+ The developer is very helpful - The game kept crashing during start-up back when the game was first released, so I sent them the crash logs, and they really put in the effort to get the issue/s fixed.+ Okay voice acting and sound. Love the visuals here too. They aren't high-end or anything but they look great enough.* Some unrealistic physics. Throwing a bottle of wine against the wall and it doesn't smash into pieces, for instance. Oddly enough the unrealistic physics - items floating in midair that can be pushed around by running into them - in the alternate dimension is quite fun to play around with though.* Checkpoints are poorly placed. I've had to replay several puzzles from the beginning and that is annoying.- Puzzles that frustrate, especially when there's a big bad baddie stalking after you, and there will be plenty of times when you're just standing around, after scouring every corner of the place, not really sure what you should do. The objectives indicator isn't particularly helpful too.- Quest items like keys are sometimes hidden in the most random of places; like underneath some random cardboard box.- Personally, I find the game rather boring after a while mainly because I had absolutely no idea what to do next and I got bored exploring the same few rooms again and again, looking for stuff that I missed - I didn't find it, unfortunately.- I'm not sure if the game is worth the cost. It's really just not that great. Maybe get it at a discount if you're still interested.- Lots of "Gotcha"-style deaths here, which I'm not a fan of. (Spoiler)Like many of the players here, I'm more inclined towards a slightly below average rating for Those Who Remain. It may have an interesting story to tell but the game has been marred, at least for me, by tedious and frustrating puzzles that could have been made less frustrating and tedious with a little bit more direction, as well as some annoying game design choices. So, yeah, get it during a sale if you really want to play the game but I wouldn't recommend buying the game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got every indie horror game cliche imaginable- the protagonist narrates every single one of his actions, there's a monster with a spotlight to show its vision, the gameplay consists entirely of wandering through area after area moving items from one room to the other to solve a "puzzle," etc. From what I hear, they even used quite a few free unity assets. However, it has a nice Twin Peaks-esque aesthetic going for it, the voice acting is sometimes questionable but overall not bad for a low-budget indie game, and the story is an interesting psychological study on morality and how we as humans are "quick to judge, slow to self-correct." Also, your actions actually effect which ending you get, which is more than can be said for a lot of games out there. With a better budget and a slightly bigger team, I think this game had the potential to be as good as something Frictional Games would put out. It's a flawed but overall enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have an intense fear of the dark, and the entire game focuses on staying in the light and avoiding the darkness - this made for a pretty terrifying experience for me (which is what I was hoping for).  The story was interesting and kept my attention right until the end, and the enemy creatures were sufficiently creepy.As many other reviews point out, the game can be frustrating at times, as there is no manual save, and the checkpoints are few and far between.  Dying and having to restart an area can sometimes mean replaying large portions of the game.  The only cutscene you can skip is the one at the very beginning of the game, but you must sit through every cutscene from that point on.  Each cutscene holds you there for a bit after it ends, which I know aggravated a lot of players and is cause for a lot of the negative reviews. The real issue with this comes into play when you're trying to get 100% achievements and have to complete multiple playthroughs - that time adds up!  These issues are not dealbreakers for me though; it didn't ruin the game, it was just mildly annoying.The environment and sound design work well together to create an eerie atmosphere.  There are paranormal elements, foul play, demonic forces, and an internal struggle with guilt for the protagonist.  Some of the puzzles felt more like trial and error, though it's possible I was just missing the clues on how to solve them. You'll also find various fun little Easter eggs - nods to iconic horror games and films, memes, and photos of the devs and other notable people (playtesters, friends, etc.).  A lot of love went into this game!I also have had nothing but positive interactions with Camel 101 and Wired Productions.  The devs are very active on their forums, they reply quickly to emails, and they are some of the nicest people I've ever met.  It's very clear to me they are all passionate about what they do, and a lot of work went into the creation of this game.  I'm impressed with how much they've done with such a small team, and I am excited to see them grow and release more games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain is such a roller coasting of amazing and semi lack luster features, but overall it balances out to be a solid experience! Is it the scariest game I've played? Not at all, is it the most engaging? No, but it has enough really big pluses to be considered a solid horror game, despite my technical issues with this game (more on that) Pros- The lighting and fog in this game is beautiful. There's many moments in the game where it's definitely flexing on other games with the great shadows cast and whatnot. - The sound design is solid. Directional audio spoops are good, no shrilly high pitched noises, decent music, and solid voice acting. The voice acting won't blow you away or anything, but it's really good all things considered. - The story for this game is basic enough for me to understand (which is great) and has just enough twists to subvert your expectations. - One of the core mechanics of the game is to have a moral dilemma and you decide what to do from there. These seem pretty straight forward at first and become more difficult as the game goes on, which is a welcome nuance compared to a normal game's obvious "If you pick this, you're a bad person" option. Cons- The mouse doesn't always lock even in fullscreen. I have two monitors, I had to constantly switch between fullscreen, windowed, click around for the mouse to actually lock onto the game and stop dragging off to the other monitor and click off of it. Super annoying. - A basic mechanic of the game is that enemies are present in the dark. There were times I'd turn on a light, the enemies would disappear, but no light turned on. I have trust issues with horror games and it took me a minute to do a trust fall and wander into the dark room. - There's a couple of moments in the game that after a weird camera zoom cutscene the frame rate just TANKS every minute or so until you finish the area. It was really obnoxious, but it was just for a couple of areas. Ultimately, I really like this game. There's moments where it's not so scary, but then there's other moments that really got me just because the game was so chill. Think of this more like a thriller story with horror moments/elements and you'll have a much better time. This game is for someone who likes the indie horror gem and less for someone looking for the next Outlast.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the game directly from Wired Productions so that I could get the comic book with it.  The comic was pretty short but it was a good setup for what was to come. I did enjoy the big behemoth creatures in the other world but for the main two things who you will see throughout the game they were not scary at all.  I think the pitchfork darkness guys could have been even more creative in more advanced lighting puzzles.  That would have made the game a bit more challenging and fun in those areas.  From a story standpoint, I think too much was given way too early too soon.  If you find all the letters and read them you'll know what I'm talking about.  The length was pretty decent as I clocked a little over 6 hours.  Maybe Camel 101 can knock it out of the park the next time around.  :)

_childDocuments_.review: Having known Camel101 for quite a few years, off the back of their previous major title Syndrome, I admit I am slightly more invested in Those Who Remain than many of these reviews might be. However, any personal friendships never get in the way of my honesty and this piece will be fair.TWR is basically a gothic chiller - a supernatural mystery - it would be innaccurate to call it horror. A lot of these reviews are playing it as a horror, and reviewing it as such, but the reality is it's a deeply interactive story about life, death and the morality in between.You're Edward, a man who appears to be at a low rung, and is ready to make a big decision in his life when things go strange, and he finds himself in a surreality questioning what's real and what isn't.TWR is significantly a departure from Syndrome - there's no sci fi ship here nor Alien Isolation vibe - this is old school supernatural.Is it good? Well that depends on what you want from your indie games (albeit Camel worked under a publisher for this one) - if you want varied gameplay and fast-paced action, this is the wrong place - the game is limited - there's an interact button and that's really about all there is. But it's really just a story with choices to be made.There are notable issues - many of which were addressed with the recent update, and of course many users have rightly complained about the moral choices causing a bad ending and giving no scope to see alternative paths without replaying the whole thing. And overall when yours truly played through, it was certainly rough in places - but then these releases always are. But I enjoyed it - bottom line, it was a good story, with pretty good voice acting, a good atmosphere and some nice environments. That it wasn't terribly 'playable' in terms of having different things to do is up to the player if they hold that against it.Personally, it's a recommended. It's got enough about it to entertain you for about 6 hours, more if you fancy a full replay for different outcomes.PS the moral choices, in places, are very good - they make you look inside yourself and see what you'd choose, and not just your character.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes I really wish you could give games a mixed result but Im gonna stick with positive cause overall this game has:- Lovely soundtrack (really the music is very well selected and some scenes still stick with me)- Good sounddesign- Great atmosphere- Good voice acting- a story- amazing level designThe cons are present of course:- chase sequences (I get it, the feel of panic is something that keeps the player on their feet but at the same time...CHASE SEQUENCES!!)- the horrible character models (compared to the surroundinds, the characters mouth and face movements are just bad)- sometimes the riddles/tasks are so confusing and dont give you any clue, what or where you're supposed to look- kinda repetetive "find key to open door" gameplay It doesnt need cheap jumpscares and relies mostly on the build up athmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: Nightmare journey through a backwater US town.It's a sad emotional story with puzzles and moral decisions that branch in several different endings.Great environments and audio effects, highly immersive. _childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest by saying that at first was underwhelmed and not taking the game seriously.Regardless I managed to be invested and remain engaged with the story and gameplay, because it simply managed to keep itself entertaining.The constant danger of having to stay in the light was a good mechanic to keep you alert on each level, the puzzles were surprisingly creative and the story even if predictable for the most part, it was a good way to drive your main character through the game.However there were some instances where I had fun for the wrong reasons, either from anti-climatic animations, pacing and transitions that would throw you off. But even with this and the amount of resources one could get from an Unity Engine, they managed to make visually pleasing levels and jarring surreal scenarios.What surprised me as well were the 'choice-making' situations that showed up throughout the game, forcing you to consider your morals and even after reaching a conclusion, you would find yourself relieved or regretting this one after learning the bigger picture the more progress you made.Overall this game has a fair amount of flaws but it delivered and didn't become stale nor boring.Worth playing but not fully taken seriously from a personal perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to recognize the influence of several titles in here, in a good way. I understand why they call it a psychological thriller, as this is not a heavy-horror game. Maybe light horror.It's unsettling and creepy, but there's no heavy gore or violence. It still keeps you on your toes, though. That's probably the difference between horror and thriller.There's a lot of exploration to do, lore discovery and puzzle situations, some easier than others.The environments and audio really draw you in. There are also other characters, which is cool. In this kind of game, the player usually feels like the last man on earth.Should be about halfway through, enjoying it very much.

_childDocuments_.review: A scary puzzle adventure game that deals with loss and choices.It's obviously inspired by a few bigger games, but it doesn't disappoint, as it doesn't try to go to AAA space, instead focusing on a couple of simple but very interesting mechanics.The game really shines with its environments, completely sucking you into the game.There's a lot of exploration and object finding, and when things start to appear to be under control, some sort of nasty monster appears.
