_childDocuments_.review: This could be called 'Lights Out: The game'. Hard to stop thinking about the movie while playing.It's not survival horror like the movie though, it's a narrative driven story with lots of puzzles and decisions / judgments to make.The eyes in the dark will keep you uncomfortable all the time, while struggling to find the safety of light.Puzzles could be just a bit harder imo, but I guess that's a matter of perspective. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game and now that I've played through it, I'm a bit disappointed. This game feels like it tried for The Evil Within vibes but missed the mark by a lot. I'm sorry but I can't recommend this game at it's price because of these reasons: Pros:- The story is decent. It's pretty cliche but, without spoilers, the game branches into something a bit deeper than what your character thinks they're experiencing and it's a welcome change.- The game has really good lighting.Cons:- Clunky menu UI. The cursor snapping to the menu elements after selections makes navigation annoying. - The dropping objects if something so much as breathe on it. It made moving things during intense moments painful. - Weird and un-inspired puzzle design. The puzzles weren't hard but you have to play hardcore hide and seek a lot and it's a major drag. Of my 6-hr playthrough, almost 3 hours were easily spent searching around for the necessary items to progress because they were in extremely obscure places.- The world/dimension swapping mechanic that happens at some parts. It was irritating right out of the gate and I disliked every time it appeared. Made navigating environments a headache and it wasn't friendly on the eyes as looking at it gave me an actual headache.- The constant environment jumping with no real cohesion. I know a story was supposed to be there and it was an okay one but every place you visit felt disconnected like it was just thrown together in different scenes. Didn't help that I recognized immediately some of the places because they're assets.- The dialogue/information UI when interacting with objects. You have to wait a couple seconds after interacting with a note or item before you can close the screen, which slows the pace of the game unnecessarily and sometimes can lead to you being killed or spotted in some areas. Not as bad but still led to some awkward moments.- One of the major decisions is kinda screwed up. A bit of a spoiler but having the choice to condemn a child to hell because of the consequences of their trauma and immaturity made me, and others watching on stream, uncomfortable.- Enemies, Aside from 2 of the game's threats, the other ones didn't really make any sense for being in the game other than variety.I would give this game a 4-5/10. If you really want to play, I would recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a hardcore horror game. I would call it a light horror, if that's even a thing. _childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain is an interesting, atmospheric horror game. story progression is linear, but can result in three different endings that are achieved with set choices that are clearly presented as such.the story itself is fine. the concept of it is very interesting, as it centres on grappling with grief, guilt, and justice - but sometimes the execution is a bit rough around the edges. and i was admittedly a little disappointed in how clearcut the endings did away with the theme, after hearing so much about how things aren't just black and white the whole game. mercy good, judgement evil seems like a lacklustre conclusion to come to.the gameplay is neat. i really like the concept of having to stick to these islands of light and having to navigate from safe zone to safe zone. the different locations/settings all have a couple of different game mechanics added to the game's standard "walk around, turn on lights, find notes" approach, which helped in keeping my attention. none of the puzzles are spectacularly difficult, but i actually found this to be quite a relief. no need to look up a walkthrough for any of them and risk spoiling the fun. sometimes it was a bit difficult to figure out what to do next, but nothing that a bit of walking around couldn't fix for me.all in all, i liked Those Who Remain. it was a unique approach to horror i hadn't encountered before and i had a good time with it. plus, i'll be adding the main theme to my regular playlist for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but its also not particularly great. A simple narrative with some fairly low-effort tropes, but it's very pretty. Most of the "puzzles" were pretty clear on their solutions so there wasn't much frustration to progress. My only real complaint game mechanic related is how clunky the physics were, making the poltergeist chase sequence incredibly frustrating as you try to keep moving weirdly floaty and heavy chairs out of the way.I'm not sure I'd call this horror or a thriller, it's much more a standard walking simulator than anything else. The fact that the "good" ending is tied to  I have some... misgivings with the moral narrative, although if you squint we're actually dealing with blue-and-orange morality and the narrative explains that position through the two bad endings in a way that it makes sense even if I don't agree with it.Fantastic visual design (even if your left hand is kinda weird the whole game), some neat set pieces, even if it is on the formulaic side of things. If you prefer narrative/fridge horror this may be your speed but I hesitate truly suggesting it beyond the binary metric. A definite "maybe" more than a yes or no.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: There's a nostalgic look in everything that works really well, from the posters to the radios and the cars. Even though the action is taking place in the present day, that makes the it much more interesting. All that's missing is a Stranger Things-themed soundtrack. Speaking of which, there are some elements from Stranger Things here.The gameplay is fairly simple, but that's what's to be expected of a puzzle game. Story is nice, shows us the ugliness of people. There are 3 possible outcomes, but you have to play the game 3 times to see all of them, so I'll probably see the other 2 somewhere in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the headline says, stays in the light. That's the focus throughout the game almost as soon as the adventure starts. Staying in the light is not new in horror games, since almost all horror takes place in the dark, but it's interesting to see how this idea turns into gameplay. Turn on a light here, point a spotlight to the road, fix another light there. Has a lot of puzzles, but most of them are easy, nothing that will get you stuck for long. The other reality is very, very cool. I wish we could have explored more of it.Very tense if you get into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain was suggested to me by a good friend of mine, I know what most are you thinking and no he isn’t a bad friend for recommending the game to me in fact he knows I enjoy horror games like this. I will say that I am enjoying it for the most part, but it is not without a few faults though. I am going to break down this review into parts.They are not the worst thing in the world and they certainly are not the best, but for two to three guys creating video games in a self-funded dev team, they are top notch for indie teams. Unity is not the worst engine to develop in and it can make some pretty good games, layers of fear 1 comes to mind, when manipulated right. The creepy shadowpeople looking at you from the dark shadows as you navigate in the light is some of the best design, I have seen from a game to keep you in a ‘level’.Now granted I am only about 2 hours into the game so I cannot really say much to the story of the game, but so far it is interesting finding papers and articles about Dormont and the strange disappearances throughout. There is almost a point where it feels like you have good shadow people and bad shadow people. I will not dive more into that and let you explore that on your own, but it is a complex web of characters the more you dive into it and with that I won’t spoil the fun at allIf you are not a fan of trying to solve puzzles to continue moving forward in a horror game, then back away from this game. This game does require solving some puzzle aspects to get from point a to point b and so on. The game does it in an interesting way that I will tip my hat, if I wore hats, to the dev team on because some puzzles if not most require traveling between two dimensions and/or avoiding the big bad who stalks, or as I have dubbed ‘big mamma’ and will refer to this big bad as that name.Some of them are easy to get and some our downright frustration, looking at you second home where chained door is. It is nice that the devs want you to stop and think through what needs to be done and take in the scenery so to speak, but doing countless puzzle after puzzle after puzzle can frustrate a player to the point of just giving up for a while, or in my case giving up for a while and writing a review.The puzzles where I have had to avoid big mama have been the only thing so far to get my heart really racing, again I enjoy my horror games so it is rare to find one that can truly spook me to the point where I don’t ant to play it. These puzzles make you think on the fly or huddle in the back corner scared and trying to think it through while big mama and her lamp face looks for you. There were times I was sure my cover was blown because her light was in my eyes, but since I guess we have no crouch ability she has to see you fully to eat you or notice you, would have liked to crouch still around a car or something.The music and sound mixing are good for such a small team. The music picks up as you approach the darkness area where all you can see are these glowing blue eyes looking into your soul in a very judgey way. Did I mention that they do not blink at all and only slightly move their heads? No, well they do and that is creepy. The music also picks up when big mama sees you and starts running at you to eat your face off, not the most welcoming mother in the world. Some of the sounds are a bit off, like in the diner there is a swinging door for a kitchen like area that just does not sound right. It sounds almost really heavy to me, but I have never worked in a restaurant that has used the old-style swing door, so I might be wrong on the sound of it.Overall, for such a small team they did a great job with what they had to work with.Of course, I have already mentioned the two monster types that I have seen so far one being the hoard of shadowfolk who stand in the darkness looking at you mocking you from their dark distance. I believe I already said that this was a smart move on the devs to force you to stay on a ‘level’ and not wonder off on your own adventure. The shadowfolk won’t let you as darkness is their friend and light is their enemy. We get told this pretty early on in the game before we meet them and trust me, they don’t do a thing unless you waddle up to them for a handshake.I can not say the same thing about big mama. You meet her maybe an hour in or sooner depending on how much time you take to explore the lightened areas or how long it takes to solve puzzles. Big mama can move, and she can stalk you. I would liken her to the monster from _Observer, for anyone who has played that game you know what I mean. It’s a happy mix of a layers of fear with an observer, you know if they were to have a child this game would be it. The nice thing is that you can just run into the light and big mama will almost reset in her spot and continue to walk around scanning for you while you huddle into the corner trying to figure out what to do next.I like that we get these two types as the shadowfolk let you thin at your own pace where big mama makes you think fast or just out stalk her till the eureka moment happens, but when it does and you can get away from her for even just a moment, it is the best feeling ever.Anyone who caught the live stream got a taste of a few nods to the horror genre be it book, movie or other game. There was a silent hill bunny nod, a huge Christine reference, a nod to Friday the 13th (maybe), a repulsion reference (gathered by a screenshot on the store page), and a silent hill room 302 reference. That is what I have found so far and to be fair, I may have missed a few. What I love is that they are subtle enough to work within the story that they are trying to tell without derailing from the narrative. Another thing I enjoy is so far, I have had time to admire the nod without feeling forced to quickly run to the next part unlike layers of fear 2.The nods are great for any horror fan a like and maybe all of us can band together and teach each other about new horror through the Easter Eggs in this game.lOverall, it isn’t a bad game and the dev team has done a great job making it and being transparent on the delays to the proper channels, which is a lot for a small indie team to do. They did it brilliantly, unlike another development company who will not be mentioned…. But trust me I am not happy with them.If you enjoy the type of horror game that makes you stop, think and read things around you, then you will enjoy this game as you have to pick things up to learn what is going on. In fact, a puzzle may depend on if you are reading and paying attention to what is around you. This isn’t like your survival horror, well it can sometimes be that way when you are facing down big mama and her lightbulb head, but it is more so the feeling of dread trying to stay in the light while danger stares you in the face. The only weapon you get is the light which I feel makes you feel better connected to the story than if you were handed a gun and were told to mow down the shadowfolk till none remain. I think this will play out in the narrative of the story as to why you are not handed a weapon, well and the fact you were preparing to end an affair not be tossed into this whirlwind of an adventure.If puzzles and stealth are a hard pass for you, you might not enjoy this game to the fullest and you might pull your hair out of your head and toss the digital copy out of the digital window to collect dust on the digital floor. No one can fault you for it, but if you are willing to give it a shot, you might come out the other end of dormant satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: The calmness of the main character even exceeds the level of the calmness of Ethan Winter."Hmm, looks like someone banged my wife. I wonder who that is?""Hmm, there are scary-eyed shadows carrying axes, tomahawks, and grenade launchers. I wonder why they are holding that?""Hmm, there are dead bodies lying on the floor."Needless to say that if you want to try to turn off a light to see what that does, you might die instantly. Kind of like a jump scare. Also controls are very primitive, which could be expected from an indie game. However, there are many wardrobes, drawers etc. in the game and game forces you to open all of them in order to not miss anything. There are almost no graphic settings, and you can't adjust the brightness mid-game. I started the game with the recommended brightness level, and everything is way too dark for me to see. At one point, I was stuck and couldn't find what to do. So I decided to look it up from youtube. Apparently, there is a cabinet in one of the rooms with a key in it. However, in my game, that cabinet was in the dark and it was impossible to see.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviewers get frustrated with the game based on the premise of an intense HORROR Gore journey. Well, i really enjoyed the game atmosphere and overall ambience. It is mainly ambiental and less horror with a sinusoidal characteristic, pushing you gently into it. Despite an overall narrative cliché, i dont think that its structure is cliché at all. We have to realize that lots of people´s zone of confort is to play more of the same. Sure, there are a lot of other "indie" (whats does this mean nowadays, anyway?) super solid polished games with the usual nervous violins, loud breaths, broken music boxes, quasi humanest skeletons, super complex mechanics, frame rate for the boys, etc but, again, nevertheless, almost non experimental. Some games dont leave you the same way after you played them, they are leaps of any form, for sure, and this is not the case with Those Who Remain, but it is for sure an interesting approach from this guys. From the photogrammetry, to the lightning, to the sounds, its not a vulgar game.  I had a lot of fun specially with the transitions to the platforms level and the church underground puzzle based on the player´s memory and distance calculation. Frustrating, random, fun. Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: I was actually really looking forward to finally playing Those Who Remain. Unfortunately my expectations FAR exceeded what the game had to offer. The lackluster story is reminiscent of something inspired by Silent Hill but fails miserably to even dip it's toe in the depths that SH reached in terms of story telling, character building and psychological horror. If you're a huge fan of Vanishing of Ethan Carter there is definitely something here for you. You'll be familiar with the gameplay loop and goal of the game. Just don't expect to get within eye shot of the same emotional investment in the characters. TWR leaves the main character a complete mystery outside one event from his past and there are NO supporting characters outside of extremely repetitive interactions with a psuedo antagonist. The puzzles are BEYOND tedious. Some of them I would even go so far as to say are unsolvable without a dedicated hour of scouring and ripping apart every single inch of 20 rooms in some cases. Maybe one or two of the puzzles were good enough for me to give a nod to but the rest are just infuriating time wasters. There is no combat whatsoever so expect to do nothing but run and hide from monsters. Luckily all their AI is extremely dumb or easy to avoid. I could go on about the good and bad of the game's graphics, lack of consumable or interactable items or the fact you won't meet but one of the characters relevant to the story but it would be a waste of both our time. I did open ALOT of lockers though. Probably somewhere in the neighborhood of 200 or more of them. It seemed like every area had at least 20-50 of them..
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not without its merits, the voice acting is overall very good, the graphics are often moody as hell with its heavy use of darkness and volumetric fog.The writing and gameplay however leaves a lot to be desired.The interactability of the world goes from you-can-interact-with-every-item to everything is static, back and forth. You can go from one room where chairs can be moved to a second room where the chairs are apparently glued to the floor.Everything that can kill you does so instantly if you touch it. This is especially frustrated when like my previous point it can be very inconsistent. Take as an example, you will die if going into pitch black darkness, but for some rooms you have to nudge inside so you can click the light switch on the wall, while in other rooms doing the same is insta-death.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is garbage.It feels really tedious and just a chore to get through.Puzzles are not intuitive. No hand-holding for such obscure solutions.Running down the corridor with furniture obstacles, that you need to remove in seconds, escaping monster - what could be "better"? Only absence of checkpoint before this run and 6 doors to guess for correct one in the end of the run - and in case of mistake you must start all over.This is one of the worst games I have ever played in my entire life.I'm sitting here trying to think of a single good thing about this game.The game looks bad. It's like everything is cast in plastic or play-doh.The movement is very janky. You run way too fast (although if that helps you finish this awful game faster then maybe that's good), and the movement itself is just very stiff and sharp. Ruins immersion.The story/writing is awful. Just a flat, unengaging story that expects you to care.The voice acting is mediocre at best, and genuinely bad at certain parts. I guess the horrible writing is to blame for this, partially.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: + Good use of atmosphere- Tedious gameplay- Abysmal puzzle design- Generic storyline- Inconsistent graphicsIt seems, at least these days, that horror games are either good, or terrible, with little in-between. For every Yomawari and Pathologic, we get disasters like The Blackout Club and Dollhouse. So the question remains, where does Those Who Remain fall on that scale?To put it simply, Those Who Remain is not a good horror game, not even an average horror game. It exemplifies everything that is wrong with the genre, including the tedious gameplay, tacked-on chase scenes, forced stealth sequences, and the shoddy puzzle design. And for a story-driven game, the writing here isn’t really that good. It’s got its moments, but the overall experience is one of mediocrity. It at least does something right with regards to its atmosphere, but that unfortunately does not save the game.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: THREE TIMES THIS GAME HARD CRASHED MY COMPUTER SO BAD I NEEDED TO RESTART PC. I HAVE A GTX 1070, AMD RYZEN 7, AS ROCK X470 TAICHI MOTHERBOARD. NO WAY THIS GAME SHOULD HAVE CRASHED MY PC WHEN I'VE PLAYED MORE RESOURCE INTENSE GAMES ON THIS THING. TAKE THIS AS A WARNING IF YOU GET THIS GAME. Game is boring and very mediocre. Like a 4/10. I'm a chicken when it comes to playing spooky things myself and I wasn't even scared at this game really. Only reactions were reflex yells to being chased or an object being flung at my face.Story makes no sense, you start by going to a motel to find your dead wife or something, then you end up passing judgement on these random adults for being idle in the death of a random 13 year old girl who you're supposed to just suddenly care about because small child I guess. Judgements aren't even hard, the endings are probably based on whether you forgive everyone even though the few judgements I did get to do before the game crashed my computer so hard the CPU fan went into ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ overdrive, were real boring and also the people did kinda suck ball but you have to forgive everyone because cliche 'be the better person' when these adults were actively trying to cover up a murder and two kids actively killed that girl we're supposed to randomly care about, like bruh. Graphics looked okayish, Edward (or whatever his name is, he's incredibly forgettable even when you're actively playing as him) has weird sausage hands but it's kind of expected of this type of like unity/unreal 'muh horror' game. Other 'humans' look pretty terrifying in that plastic unity asset way but the flashlight monster is pretty cool. The shadow people that stand in the dark are like, okayish. Spooky at first but they get boring and I had more fun throwing object at them than being afraid of them. The spider creatures are pretty good but I'm not whether that's because I'm scared of spiders. Devs tried to copy sequences and ideas from other games and media (Stranger Things upside down and PT's corridors) but fails to realise why these things work in their prospective media and how to use them in any sort of impactful way. Music was kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ too, when everything's on a crescendo, that kind of just becomes normal and you don't care anymore. I only had fun playing this because I spent what playtime I did manage to get before the game started crashing was spent running around at full speed like an idiot and rinsing the whole experience with a friend on discord. A refund is in the process and I'm gonna be real pissed if I can't get one because I physically cannot play this game without my computer sounding like it's about to take off to space or if it's going to nuke my entire house.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy horror survival adventure puzzle solving games but this one is non of it. It's not scary, monsters are cheesy, has no real plot behind it, no real puzzle solving, primitive graphics, and its performance is real bad (unity engine). I did not expect much from a game that costed me $1 but even with low expectations I was able to sustain only one hour of its "gameplay" and then happily uninstalled it.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Did a first run through on this game, for the time it took as well as price...you cannot beat this game.  The Story was amazing, as well as playthrough.  While streaming this game people also loved it and got involved as well.  I Highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys horror as well as puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me take my brown pants out of my closet again.... Gonna have to do laundry..... Those who remain is a story about a small village and a murdered girl. I loved how to game is taking you down the path to find out what happened and the thing you do through out the game. I got a lot of Alan Wake vibes in the game and the mother is creepy af. Voice acting is one of the best i have encountered in such small titles. Def a recomendation 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Lacks polish.The voice acting is fine but everything else feels... off for some reason.I mean the trailer looks very interesting and well made but I feel like it's not representative of the end product at all. You see in the 19 minutes I played before asking for a refund I was making a face, a "something is not right" face, and not because it's supposed to be scary, which it wasn't. And believe me if you're making that kind of face right at the beginning of a game, something is terribly wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Not the traditional horror experience like the sorts of Outlast or Resident Evil.If you're looking for something similar, this might not be your cup of tea.What this is is a truly immersing trip through the dark.The game certainly has its issues, as all games do, but it is definitely a solid one.There's a mix of exploration, running, weird environments, different dimensions and strange demons.And you get to decide who lives and who dies.Really cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Those who Remain has many gameplay related issues, but it has enough positive parts that justify two engaging playthroughs. This game does its job as a psychological horror title, and has the potential to affect its audience. Considering its 20$ price tag, this game is recommended to all fans of horror genrecheck my full review at:
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game but very slow start which could easily turn people off from playing, the premise itself is quite good but ultimately falls short, the psychological elements are not strong enough to hold the story together. The game graphics and atmosphere are quite impressive but there are better horror psychological games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad at all. Has a good story that keeps you interested until the end. It's not entirely original, but has a few surprises that make it stand on its own.The other world is especially interesting, but unfortunately it's not that explored. Could be something to dive into in more detail in a future game.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Uninspired plot, bland "puzzles" that come down to "find the thing, likely in a drawer" and spam clicking every interactable object until something changes arbitrarily, a protagonist so wooden you could sell him for lumber, and scares that are below standard for this sort of game. The only saving grace is the atmosphere of the game, but even that seems like it was just copied from better games. Despite the constant music hinting at a frightful or dangerous environment, there's no urgency or fear to be had here. Just a walking point-and-click adventure that can't manage to have any adventure to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: The typical haunting story with a few twists. Instead of being trapped inside a house, the characters are trapped in a village. Of course there's a mystery that needs to be unravelled and the player will have some tips and indirect help from other characters. The gameplay is straightforward. Like others in the genre, you have to search for clues and key objects to be able to progress. Each level is a closed section in itself, which means there's no way to go back to previous scenes. The way the world is built is especially nice, with the shadows and the dark alleys and corners creating a sense of constant dread.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Edward was a guy with a good life. Nowadays his life isn't that good anymore and he finds himself in the middle of a haunted down where the sun seems to be gone. This is the starting point. Then you'll get to investigate the death of a child, some bad stuff that happened on that down and ultimately decide on the fate of some people.The story and atmosphere are highly immersive. Great game for a rainy night.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not very good. it's 5/10 or a 6/10. It's not particularly frightening and the levels are mostly small sections of a town's buildings. You'll be doing backtracking with keys, etc... I found the puzzles unappealing as well. The character models are quite bad and it really doesn't look good. It's an incredibly overpriced game. If you're really driven to play it, wait until it's on a steep sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A psychological horror game with some investigative gameplay. It's dark (not only figuratively) as the story takes place in a small village where it's always night. Naturally there are some weird things going on, some evil people and curses, and you have to discover what and why. Story is decent and some moments are truly tense. The creatures in the dark are really cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly pretty cool game for a 4-5h game play. The Atmospehere was amazing, the story telling was fantastic and the puzzle were too hard but not too easy either. I enjoyed my time with this one and I would definitely recommend it. even tho I would advice you to get it on sale since i don't think it's worth 20 dollars for it. I got it for 5 euros on sale and tbh i wouldn't had if it was more than that. But i don't regret buying it
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A simple but deep psychological horror / walking sim that does a lot with few resources. Intertwined plots, mysteries and dark secrets. A broken protagonist who's not looking for answers but ends up getting them. A cursed town where the day doesn't rise. Aside from a frustrating puzzle where you have to place statues in a certain place while a monster hunts for you, it's a solid experience that tells a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so good i underestimated at first  before buying it. im glad i got it! i highly recommend if u really like horror spooky scary games definitely got my moneys worth also supports controller puzzles arent that hard to figure out barely have to look it up good game to stream definitely ya moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Not great.Initially, the mystery is interesting enough, but then the game tips its hand very quickly, thinking it's being cryptic, cool and mysterious, when it's actually being embarrassingly loud and obvious, like a drunk person flirting. She's sat there at the bar,  smoking a cigarette, giving you a the look, saying "do you wanna know my name?" and hiccupping. It's Claire. You heard her slur it at the last bloke.Gameplay is servicable but not fun or interesting, just find the object you need to advance the story. You won't have any trouble figuring out how to progress since you only really hold one object at a time, don't have to combine them, anything like that. You'll need to get into a garage and find garage key labelled "garage key". Sometimes you have to avoid a monster's gaze. That's it.If, like me, you enjoy things set at night then you might enjoy this but the initial atmosphere is all this has going for it, really.I love spooky motels, petrol stations, farms and diners, but the game burns through those, in that order, very quickly and I have no motivation to play the rest of the game knowing it's not going to be entirely that tbh.Game seems determined to sing the old favourites of the horror genre with absolutely nothing new to bring to them.*Inhale* Demons, cults, follower type enemy with an inanimate object for a head, dead daughter, sad protagonist, unappealing woman with her breastices out going boogy woogy woo in your face Tralalala.Tells a lot about the studio that they thing Skeeter Davis' The End of the World is an interesting song to pick for a horror trailer.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a simple investigative gameplay that becomes really special because of the oppressive and dark atmosphere that reminds so much of Silent Hill. You have to find clues, objects or find out something in other to progress from one area to other, as the character is being led to learn about something. Can't say more because of spoilers, but it works nicely. The villain is really cool and sarcastic. Would love to see him explored with more depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A good and simple horrorish game with an amazing atmosphere. The graphics and sound work perfectly in tandem, making the whole thing feel like a horror flick. There are some weird creatures and places, most of them explained, others will leave you guessing. Simple puzzles, short dialogs, very tense. It's neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Intriguing game. Linear, with the narrative guiding the players along a creepy journey, while unraveling a mystery and solving a series of puzzles and simple challenges. But then it forces you to make moral choices at some points, and you know that things are going to end badly. And they did, for me.I also have to mention the environment, which by itself is enough to send shivers down your spine.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I have no words for the disappoint I felt with playing this game. In addition to many puzzles having no apparent reason to them, I have to say that getting the "bad ending" without making all bad choices is just...meh. Secondly, you can't replay chapters and would have to play the entire game again. With an ending that left more questions than answers...such as why Eddy snapped in the bad ending? I honestly don't foresee myself wasting the time. The story was lackluster. There were too many awkward lag-out transitions. No genuine character growth. Not to mention the annoying flashing lights that makes your eyes want to bleed. Save yourself the time and just watch a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Silent-hilly kind of game, where reality and dreamworld blend together and horrible creatures come out of it. While the gameplay is fairly simple and slow-paced, the strong narrative and emotional ride is definitely the strong point.Everything is very surreal with some nods here and there to other well known stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle game / walking adventure where the protagonist finds himself in a small town surrounded by darkness.It's a very atmospheric game with a good deep story, but it also has some flaws. It misses a more dynamic saving system and some kind of proximity warning before you get stabbed.It's entertaining though, and the story keeps you going. Worth a play-through.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to another reviewer, I really thought that I would enjoy this game -- until I played it.  I finished largely out of disbelief and curiosity of a modern game being so bad so uniformly.The first scene is super klunky, but I chalked that up to "learning the game."  Sadly tho it never got better.  I don't like writing negative reviews if I haven't experienced something in a complete form, so I did finish the game.  It does not redeem itself.  I ran into a few bugs, which given the gameplay honestly don't set you back very far -- but that's in large part because the gameplay is quite underdeveloped and static - the "zombies" (or, whatever) essentially force your path both inside and outside; and in cases where they don't, your path is mandated by doors which lock and unlock for no reason other than "it's time to do so," and hallways which appear and then are gone for the very same reason.  One or two things might kill you once or twice on each level; and then once you learn that there's not much more than the monotony of repeating things up until that point and doing "the other thing" to progress until you get whacked again.The visuals, graphics, and gameplay are all pretty bad.  After the first two or three times that you're ... devoured? ... by "the mom" or "the karen" it becomes laughable.  When cornered, I found myself just letting my character die and restarting the level / puzzle rather than put in much effort to save myself.  The flipping between the two worlds is kind of a near concept that has been done before -- unfortunately in this case it is done poorly but that's mainly because the gameplay in general is done poorly.The alternate endings aren't different enough to warrant any replay.  The puzzles are all the same, very static, the only differentiator in a replay is if you save someone or not.This might entertain you if you're 12; but it's certainly no Phantasmagoria (which actually had better graphics, storyline, voice acting, gameplay, and even inventory back in 1995).
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A rough and at times frustrating horror gem.If anyone today can find a game that doesn’t have glitches, issues and all-around, frustrating features or lack of features by all means, let me know. Yes that’s right they don’t exist. That said yes, this game can be rough around the edges, has its glitches and can be frustrating at times. I played this game on stream a few times, and what I can honestly say is above all I thoroughly enjoyed myself. The story was interesting, and the ending caught me off guard. Not an Uber surprise just was expecting something a bit different. Was nice to know there were multiple changes that could be made to get a different ending but do not expect a completely different experience. The ending is essentially the last two or three minutes of the game. essentially you will get a different narrative. That said, I did enjoy this title. I love the indie feel horror genre. I bought this game early when it came out and paid full price. I don't regret my purchase. Yes we all love a sale but I didn't mind spending $20 on this. As you can see I played it for over 19 hours and really did enjoy myself. I’d give it a 6.5 out of 10. The minor glitches, rare crashes, and occasionally confusing puzzle System are the only reason I did not rate this higher.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I know it's not completely original, but the premise of this game had potential. And although it had some of its moments, unfortunately it turned out to be a tedious, frustrating and annoying experience overall.This is a game that constantly disappoints. You play, make some progress, find items, unlock puzzles and then you die. Usually you will have to start the level all over and all your progress turns out to be wasted time. Yes you will have to do it all over again, because checkpoints in this game are very rare to cross. So when you die the game becomes super repetitive and you have to literally force yourself to play. That's one huge problem I had with the game, but the second on is that the game is "cleverly" structured all the way so that you'll die often.These are the two main reasons that made me super annoyed with this game, and are resons enough to not  reccomend this game to anyone, but a masochist. It reminds me of a similarly frustrating, tedious and annoying + right down infuriating horror game I played called Home Sweet Home. In conclusion what can I say? I reccomend you avoid both of these games.Edit: I manage to persist and finish this game. I still regret it, just seeign the screenshots make me cringe. It was a really bad game, IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game’s atmosphere and supernatural elements, which kept me on edge and intrigued. The game had some really creative and surprising moments where the environment changed and objects moved. I appreciated the variety of puzzles and challenges, even though some of them were a bit familiar. The chase scenes and the platforming section added some excitement and tension to the game, which I thought was a nice contrast to the psychological horror. The game had a lot of potential and delivered in many aspects.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Definatly didn't live up to the expectations. I followed this game way before it's release and expected immersion, high-quality graphics and attention to detail. The game had none of those. Just an interesting premise and a cool concept that had a lot of potential in theory, but lacked fullfilling that potential in reality. It would need much improvement in level design and implementation of various mechanics to become fun and feel like you are always competing with the monster. Unfortunatly, due to games like Amnesia, SOMA and even Resident Evil to some degree we have a higher standard of what should be made in games and as a developer you should think about the standards games before yours have set. All in all, I could complete the game if the story was told in a bland way cause it stil has you hooked to know more about the workd and what happened, but I just can't forgive the gameplay that tales all the fun from it. That being said, if you don't mind the things I listed, you should definatly give it a go. It does have something unique to offer and I do sincerely believe it will interest some players.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Nice psychological horror game with a decent length. Not too short, not too long, feels just right.Has a great setting and atmosphere, with some simple puzzles that don't require too much headbanging, which is good.There are a couple scenes that can get a bit frustrating, like a chase sequence where all the furniture is moving in front of the camera. After dying the 3rd time, stops being tense and starts being annoying. Other than that, it's an enjoyable game with a nice story.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Psychological horror game with a nice tragic story. No gore or "in your face" stuff, it slowly builds tension like a thriller. Some chases get a bit scarier, but it doesn't go too hard on the horror part.There are some (easy) puzzles along the way, moral choices to be taken and the usual notes and stuff to read. Most of them aren't necessary to read, but you'll probably miss a lot from the story if you skip them.Perfect for horror lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Although it looks quite nice for the most part, Those Who Remain is unfortunately one of the most tedious games I've played.It may look like a horror game but there is basically no horror atmosphere to be found. The "puzzles" range from tedious to frustrating, and rarely do they have anything to do with the themes of the game. There are way too many occasions where the only way to progress is to walk up and down the same hallway until a new path appears. There are too many occasions where the only way to progress is to recheck every room of the area you're in as a new portal has appeared after an unannounced criteria has been met. The story is not strong enough to keep you engaged. Checkpoints are too far apart and there is no manual saving so if you get toward the end of a "puzzle" and then get caught in one of the far too numerous chase sequences, you have to do the whole area from the start.On the positive side, the voice acting was good and I do not recall any bugs during my time. There just isn't enough here to recommend playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: It's entertaining and scary, without going too hard on the jumpscares. It focuses instead on intense and suspenseful gameplay, which works a lot better than close-up screams imo.Strong focus on the narrative with a really nice story, although you should keep notes about who's who. There are a lot of secondary characters and it's hard to keep track of who did what.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A trip to Anytown USA, where everything is not what it seems. And i mean this figuratively and literally speaking, as the two realities show what lies beneath some interesting objects.There are certain obvious messages from the developers, and I see what they did here. There's always a duality in the game that's most present in the light versus the dark, and this works great in gameplay terms. Stay in the light, hide from the dark.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: It's an interesting game with a few cliches that are put to good use: the story seems bland at first, but it slowly evolves into something much deeper. Without spoiling, there's a lot more than an angry ghost trying to kill everyone just because. But where it truly shines is with the light vs dark mechanic. The stress of staying in a lighted area keeps you alert and constantly waiting for something to jump you, and sometimes it does.This is not a AAA game, but it's intense and fun, and that's all that matters.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the best atmospheres I've seen. It's ominous and intense, serving as the layer for everything that happens throughout the story.It has some nice puzzles - not too easy, not too hard, and it involves a good amount of investigating and searching around for clues or special items.There's an alternate dimension with strange creepy stuff going on, but I can't say more without spoiling.The story is really good, it's all about morals without trying to tell what's good and what's right. It's up to the player to decide.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: This game was extremely frustrating at a couple points, but after taking a break and returning (or looking up a walkthrough) I got through it. The graphics are good, it's a super creepy atmosphere, I loved it. Story was awesome. I'll probably ply again to get the achievements I missed. Only thing I'm confused about - I spared EVERYONE except the guy in the cop car, I lit his ass on fire. Still, somehow, I got the bad ending. Oh well, like I said, I will play again. Definitely recommend for anyone that enjoys creepy/horror atmospheres.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this, but the save system is on the the worst I have seen in decades. The really badly made stealth parts just add frustration. If the dev would have just stuck to the light/darkness puzzles instead of adding all the bloat, it might have been decent enough.Also shame on the publisher for the bad quality control and the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: The voice actor for your character in this makes me wish he would have ignored his phone and pulled the trigger. His delivery is so blasé and lethargic that he sounds like he just woke up from a deep sleep. He doesn't even comment on the creatures around him until he's seen them many, many times, and when he finally does he just goes straight into wondering how he can get around them using the same tired, mildly interested second thought/musing tone as he gives for everything else. It makes the rare moment that he does actually express surprise at something sound desultory and forced. Ugh!Boring protagonist = boring experience, couldn't deal with more than an hour of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. The environment is very well done, it's very effective into quickly bringing the player into the action. There's no boring or long explanation, it starts and things start happening quickly but fluidly.Some animations are a bit janky, but nothing that can be considered immersion breaker.I like that it doesn't have in-your-face jumpscares, as these can get annoying very quickly. It has a good story and some decision moments which bring more depth to the story. Of course it also has some of the usual tropes, but it uses them wisely.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Had this game on my WL for quite some time and finally got around to play it, It was more of an indie game than i expected when i first saw it and it had some ugly spots but surprisingly it was actually overall enjoyable!The biggest issues for me was crappy animations and some of the characters looked really bad but it did not bother me that much.The different endings pretty much required me to play through the game the same way 99% of the time with just some change of choices and they ended up not being anything great anyways.8.2hours of gameplay and i paid like 3-4 euros for it? Can't complain!
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I am pretty sure that I am not this far in the game but it is fun to play and sometimes I really needed some minutes to figure out what I need to do. And tbh I needed help in the first house xD Some jumpscared but okay I am really easy to scare so not sure if this means anything to other ppl out there :P I like it ! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A town with a curse, a man with a trouble past.Starts like so many other stories, but it quickly spirals into an intense trip between real life and a distorted reality. The atmosphere is king. The details are everywhere, from the beautiful eerie shadows to the chirps and the howls in the woods.You might guess what's really going on about halfway through the game, but you'll probably be wrong. I know I was. No combat, not that many jumpscares, some evasion and chase sequences.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: A town where the sun doesn't rise, and where dark faceless figures appear in every lightless corner.This alone would be a great setting, but it gets even more crazier as things unfold.It's very psychological, in a sense that there's a reason for everything that's happening, instead of just a random collage of visions and headaches that we're so used to see in so many horror games.Deciding about other character's fates is cool. I like that no one is evil per se, and again there's a reason for every action taken by the characters.Remember to look at every evidence before deciding someone's fate. The more you look at it, the harder will be to decide.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: It's creepy and unsettling, it is atmospheric and is exactly what you want from a horror game. Good graphics, fantastic lighting in a style of its own. Sounds are creepy and add to the overall atmosphere. The puzzles are not overly challenging, but you will have to explore the area to be able to solve them.The game gives about 4-5 hours, dependant on logic skills and how fast it takes you to find certain key items. I would definitely recommend the game if your looking to get creeped out and be put on edge and want to experience a genuine horror/eerie adventure in the vein of BioShock or Alan Wake.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I actually think this game is great, the only thing that's missing is:-it could have a more well developed stealth aspect, in Those Who Remain you can't crouch so you can't hide from monsters as easily.-it could also have save slots so that players can more easily alter their endings.-it could have more options for unfolding paths like with "Dry Drowning" and some others.Overall, this game is kind of scary and is challenging but not maddeningly frustrating. I can see why some thought it was too easy but you probably won't feel this way if you don't play a lot of video games. It could be a little cheaper in the future and I think if they make some of the changes that I and other players are recommending then a sequel would be worthwhile.The only other issue I had is that my computer has had trouble processing it (it freezes in random spots), which could be due to a bug, but not necessarily. I'm running windows 10 with an i7 skylake processor and a 1060 GTX graphics card which i believe is a little overpowered for a game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sad game. I mean sad in a good way, because the story really touched me. There will never be too many games that talk about bullying.The environments and the city are really immersive and believable, pulling you into this modern day nightmare.The game itself is a puzzle adventure. There are no zombies, cannibals or split second decisions here. There are monsters, but they can be easily evaded most of the times.And there's a familiar place to Stranger Things fans. Easily my favorite parts of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't rate this game as horror, but more like a mysterious emotional adventure.It's certainly different, with a pacing that will make explorer-like players feel at home. The action starts right at the beginning, with the rules being set out at that moment when a voice says «Stay in the light» over the phone. That's the most important thing you'll need to remember.Moral choices are not obvious and offer replayability. There are a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in that town, but some of them might not be that bad. Took me a while to decide, which is good. The game is different, and that's good.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrative-exploration game with a pinch of horror.Focused on puzzles and decisions, it'll have you visiting locations on a cursed town where it's always night, with creepy guys with knives standing everywhere where it's dark.Alan Wake obviously comes into mind, and it was obviously an inspiration for this.The gameplay is simple but intuitive, although a crouch button would be welcome.Overall environments are top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: I would call this a hybrid puzzle adventure with a horror/horrorish story.The game is quite different from the usual walking simulators.I guess I'm about half through at the moment, and I've enjoyed very much what I've seen so far.The puzzles aren't difficult, but they do require some analyzing and exploring.What will definitely draw you in is the environment and the story. That and all the stranger things *wink*
_childDocuments_.name: Those Who Remain

_childDocuments_.review: Not to bad a game for the price, very average story about death and judgment. It does have it's issues, like i hate the saving system (you can't manually save, everything is automatic so beware that you may have to run through the same motions again if you die). Some of the puzzles can be annoyingly nuanced as well, one in particular where the missing item you need is literally sitting behind a random box on a shelf. The horror elements are very rinse and repeat, you will not see a wide variety of enemies, but instead reoccurences of the same enemies you've already encountered.If you like walking simulators and horror i think this is a decent game for it's price. The winning aspects of this game for me was the variety of environments they put you in from an abandoned post office and diner to a hospital. The game also really encourages you to follow the very simple story as you will make judgements of the people within the story and decide their fate. I really loved that aspect of it, though for me some decisions were very hard as the game doesn't account for nuiance. Some people deserved less punishment than others, and the game doesn't account for that. Everything is morally binary in the game, he either did good or bad and you must pick one extreme or the other. But life isn't that simple.Again, i recommend this for the walking sim and horror fan that has a spare $20. But for everyone else i really don't recommend it. IF you're looking to get into these types of games i recommend something like Layers Of Fear instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Those Who Remain was the kind of title i didn't expect much from... but i did turn out a wonderful surprise! name: Wasteland 3
detailed_description: Feature List The End Has Just Begun A party-based roleplaying game with the series’ signature focus on story reactivity and strategic combat in a post-apocalyptic world. A Core RPG Experience Features a deep and engaging story, utilizing a dynamic dialogue system with full English voiceover, allowing players to choose their role, and immersing fans of the series and newcomers alike. Survive the Blistering Cold Set in the savage lands of frozen Colorado, where survival is difficult and a happy outcome is never guaranteed. Players will face difficult moral choices and make sacrifices that will change the game world. Deep and Reactive Tactical Gameplay Player vehicles, environmental dangers and a revamped, more fluid action system lay the foundation for tactical, yet explosive turn-based combat. Assemble your Squad A detailed character creation system with dozens of skills, perks, and quirks allow for deep customization of your squad of up to six Rangers, geared to your playstyle. Take in the Scenery A significant graphical upgrade, character animations, and first-person conversations bring Colorado and its sensational landscapes to life and elevate the series to new heights. Bring a Friend Play single player or with a friend in story-driven co-op. Choices open (or close off) mission opportunities, areas to explore, story arcs, and more. About the Game In Wasteland 3 you take command of a squad of Desert Rangers, lawmen and women in a post-nuclear world, trying to rebuild society from the ashes. More than a century after the bombs fell, you’re fighting a losing battle to keep your beloved Arizona alive. Then the self-proclaimed Patriarch of Colorado radios, promising aid if you'll do a job he can only entrust to an outsider—rescue his land from the ambitions of his three bloodthirsty children. You’re dispatched on a desperate quest from the scorching deserts to the snowy mountains to start from scratch, building a new base, finding a snow-worthy vehicle, training new recruits, and fighting your way through hostile frozen wastes. All the while, you'll have to decide who to trust in this land torn apart by corruption, intrigue, warring factions, crazed cultists, cutthroat gangs, and bitter sibling rivalries. Build a reputation for yourself by making decisions that will profoundly impact Colorado, its inhabitants and the story you experience. Will you be Colorado’s savior or its worst nightmare? Wasteland 3 is a squad-based RPG from inXile entertainment, featuring challenging tactical turn-based combat and a deep, reactive story full of twists, turns, and brutal ethical decisions that will keep you hooked whether you’re a Wasteland veteran or new to the series. Create a squad of up to six Rangers and customize them with perks and abilities geared to your playstyle. You even get your own battle truck, which you can upgrade into a hardened war beast, bristling with weapons, to help mow down your enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Some rebalancing to make things interesting didn't save it from failure.Story is more of the same, with choices that at most goes three-ways and no option is a "happy ending". If that turned you off on 2, no changes here. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but I expected some refresh on that.Mechanics wise, skills became rebalanced, to the point where "skill mules" (characters that get lots of maxed skills but can't really fight as well) are dead. Each character will max up to 3 or 4 skills, realistically 3 (good use of skill books guarantee 4). The quirk that increases skill points give you enough for one more max, at the cost of making that character die on a sneeze (specially on higher difficulty). Can't quite say it's a bad thing. The difference between the highest difficulty (Supreme Jerk) and the second one (Ranger) is that the same level of preparation means retrying a battle 3 or 4 times due to one-crit kills on your party (I swear enemy crti rate feels like 70%) plus 3 times more rounds and resources used on SJ, and you wiping out the enemy on two turns with no one downed on Ranger. They could left the high damage on SJ if that meant enemies not being bullet sponges, but the mix of both is just frustrating. In the end, SJ victory strategy is to spam animal companions (that are as tanky as the enemies) and mechanical consumables, or abuse some mechanics in ways that feel like exploits.Bugs wise, didn't had problem in the first 10 hours or so of gameplay, only for things to get out of hand. Quests breaking all the time, triggers breaking and activating every time, reloading a save to find an enemy rising from the dead.Lots of these bugs feel like they came to be because of the change into multiplayer (or at least, the change in engine, which again might've be pushed for because of the multiplayer). Having the game broken like that because some development hours were dedicated to make a handful of moments where multiplayer make a difference is beyond me. Wasteland 2 and 3 are great single player games in their own rights, but forcing a multiplayer onto the same formula with the smallest of tweaks just doesn't work. Would've been better to make a standalone action game with focus on multiplayer (something like Remnant/Diablo-like with Wasteland skill system) than break Wasteland 3 for the sake of it.Sountrack is still very good tho.Don't regret buying, cause I loved Wasteland 2 and wanted more, but was it frustrating. If they at least do a lot of bug hunting, I won't care about the SJ balance and change this to a positive (keeping nearly the same text, the problem with multiplayer design simply doesn't "go away"). If you loved Wasteland 2 and wants more, than it's worth a try. Othewise, wait about a year to see if things get better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an awful lot of potential but it falls short in pretty much every area, lots of things feel like they are only half finished.  -Characters generally feel rushed: there's a substantial lack of dialogue and exploration vs Wasteland 2.  This is relevant because at launch Wasteland 2 was only £35, Wasteland 3 is £55 so I expect to play a larger, higher quality game.  You aren't going to get that at the moment.-Bugs: just so many, nothing game breaking per se, some e.g. npc animal characters vanishing, sections of story are skipped (second playthrough they were present but others were not - I kept the same choices to make sure), really bad ui interface, when battle starts I lost count the number of times the screen would just move to the corner of the map when it was my turn, characters getting stuck in cover, sometimes my turn would just skip for no reason whatsoever.-The illusion of choice, this game makes a big deal on reputation having a huge effect for the player, it doesn't.  You have rep with certain factions, and then individuals have their own allegiances towards you.  I found the latter was only affected by 3-4 main missions, and the 20+ optional quests I undertook had absolutely no effect what so ever.  There is supposed to be this feel of building something from nothing but you're just left feeling underwhelmed.  The reputations are supposed to affect the ending but even those fall short.  They don't do much besides getting you a few free items and a discount when buying for your squad.-Poor item & squad management: inventory management is just awful, having a storage box would be helpful, not sure why no one thought to include it, perhaps on the transport used.  You also can't respec your points but you can delete the custom character and redistribute the points that way, less the xp you gained in that level, as well as any skill books you've read.  Frustrating.  Attributes per character are also badly designed, a couple of areas aren't worth investing in because they give nothing back, whilst others are ridiculously over powered. -More clarity on missions: what I mean by this is that some missions are on a timer and some are not, and whilst it is often fairly obvious which ones are, it would be helpful to know just how much time you have.  It feels like the game punishes you if you want to do chunk of story first and then the optional stuff later.-The final 1/3 of the game just drops off: it's like they ran out of time and just finished with what they had.-Online Co-op:  It's broken, doesn't work.  Needs to be patched asap.-The ending: I won't put any spoilers in but in my play-through the end summary contradicted itself which boils down to poor story telling.  It also felt rushed and poorly told, from the choices I made I had this build up for a large showdown and it was over in 2 minutes, I already have that with gf, I don't want it in the games I play too.I want to like the game, I do like it, but I can't recommend it as it is.  Not unless they make some big changes.  It's a game that has some genuinely decent moments of voice acting and story/character development, and it looks good too.  However, all of these areas are hampered by a plethora of bugs and the feeling that everything you encounter feels unfinished, rushed or poorly designed.  And it's £55.  Buy Wasteland 2, it's much better. Or go play Fallout 2 and use the unofficial mods.

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding well rounded RPG, I'd highlight:- A dynamic, engaging and fun well-balanced turn based combat.- Multi-layered and ever branching decisions with true impact in many key plot events.- Immersive and fitting soundtrack- Humorous at times, not taking itself too seriouslyIf I had to put out some cons from my point of view:- Writing incurs in some stereotypes thus falling flat at times- There were not many secret areas to explore- Its last dlc for me was less interwoven with the story if you compare it with the first one, it felt less interesting.I'd rate it a strong 8,5 out of ten, I feel it could have had more secret/hidden areas to explore and the last dlc could have had more repercussions in the story as the first one really had, but it's engaging and it doesn't overstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this on 4th of July. Let me tell you, this is the most American game I've ever played. No other game has captured how messed up and how amazing we are as a society. This was an extremely ambitious goal - to take a look in the mirror, and the developers have pulled it off. Far better than Fallout 3, 4 and even New Vegas.Arizona Rangers are in trouble and they need supplies, so they dispatched a convoy to a potential ally in Colorado, who promised to deliver those supplies in exchange for establishing law and order in his land. Very quickly you find yourself inside a total political clusterf... of fragile alliances, moral compromises, back stabbing and opportunities to back stab.There is no clear path through this game. There is no perfect ending. There is no way to make it through without making some tough choices and turning your back on something or someone. Just pick your battles and pick your allies. No one is coming out perfectly clean.Build your squad wisely. I found that having narrow specialists, who have expertise in a specific topic, was much better than having a squad of average generalists. My permanent party was divided into long range (sniper/HMG) team and a close range (assault/shotgun) team. Each member had a secondary specialty (mechanics, electronics, trash talking, etc). I relied on companions to provide medical and modding. But my Rangers were the primary strike force.Put in the effort to do the reconnaissance before the fight. Separate the squad and let your sniper occupy the most favorable position first. Then position the assault team. I typically started the fight with either the sniper or the rocket launcher, taking out small groups if possible.In conclusion, this game is incredible. This is how you do an Americana-Western, manifest destiny in post apocalypse. A separate word must be said about the music. The soundtrack to the boss fights could not have been picked better.On this fine Fourth of July this game gets my seal of approval.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's good. If you like CRPGs for their story and characters, you will probably like this. This is one of the few games that does a decent job of depicting morality as a shade of grey instead of black and white, and I appreciate that.However, it's worth noting that certain parts of the game are buggy as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ for no reason. Sometimes the UI breaks and you can't use any abilities until a character makes a basic attack. One of my characters entirely lost the ability to use a "strike attack" (a core component of a high charisma build) half way through a play through. I could not find any way to fix it. I was still able to complete a playthrough on the normal difficulty, but it is incredibly disappointing given the funding behind the game. Like seriously, the basic UI elements should work. This isn't really acceptable. There are $10 indie games with more polish.A less major bug, but still bug, was that I released a certain character from jail, only for him to show up back in jail in the closing moments of the game. Again, not a gamebreaker, but really disappointing to see.Also, the soundtrack ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SLAPS. Or rather, parts of it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SLAP. Other parts are completely forgettable, or even kinda bad. It is really sad to see such inconsistency here. The bangers only come out during boss fights, and each boss fight has it's own music. Most were great, some where mediocre, one was just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad. If the entire game had a soundtrack on par with the first two boss fights I would have recommended it for the soundtrack alone. Unfortunately, that is definitely not the case.tl;drA 9/10 CRPG that gets downgraded to a 6/10 because of constant bugs that break up the gameplay, and a soundtrack that could have blown my mind, but instead gave me blue balls halfway through the game. Play it and enjoy it in spite of its flaws, but DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE.EditOriginally, I recommended this game because despite it's blatant flaws it was an enjoyable experience.I retract that statement.After completing the game, I decided to browse the spoilers section on the wiki to see what I missed. Do you know what I missed? Entire cut storylines that are listed on the wiki, because they are in the game files, but aren't actually in the game because they were cut to be sold back as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DLC. Go right ahead and ♥♥♥♥ off with that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I already had a sneaking suspicion that the game was less fleshed out than Wasteland 2, and this is just confirmation of that.For a game that is very satirical of capitalism, they pulled a pretty classic capitalist move on this one.I wanted to love this. I wanted to appreciate it despite it being a buggy mess.♥♥♥♥. Right. Off. with this ♥♥♥♥. This is exactly the kind of garbage we need less of in the gaming industry.Buy this on ♥♥♥ so the devs don't get your money. They don't deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: So far 20 hours in and I'm having a blast with this game. Rpg elements are solid. Story is entertaining supplemented by great side missions. Dont be fooled by the term "side" they like main missions which builds your world. World is immersive and there is a feeling of a journey that you undertake both literally and figuratively.As time passes you get attached to your characters be it custom characters or premade. You find your self role playing in your head as your character contenplating on choices and their possible future consequences. It is immersive very much. Im playing with a friend in COOP but  i feel this games warrats a single player campaign as well. Even though I'm the dominat voice in the campaign there are some compromises between us in terms of choices. That being said COOP is hella fun.  To share the stroy and the experience with another is great. Especially in this game. The build diversity is just right. Not too much so you miss out on some of the game elements and not too little that every character is the same. Our skills complement each other meing having the custom tank that puches people and another custom medic with him having sniper/tech npcs. We get the best of both worlds and you fell like a squad of different individuals. That being said I still think people should play this 1 more time in singleplayer. Basicly you should experience both coop and single if you can.Now for combat. I'm gonna be hyporitical here say I hate turn based combat. That being said I have 200 ish hours on XCOM2 I know I know. Anyways with that out of the way the combat feels solid. It has depth and it keeps you on your toes. Overall 9/10 so far. I might update if my feelings chance but If I didnt update then take the full review as it is. Also I'm deducting 1 point because I'm playing this after I played "Cyberbug2077" so I might be a bit biased because the 2077 I played, besides the story was a trashfire and frankly a bad rpg by desing.

_childDocuments_.review: After having just finished my first playthrough I can say that this is a hard game. It's not hard in the traditional sense, but the decisions I had to make were sometimes extremely difficult. Rarely did I ever feel like there was a "right" choice or a "good" choice. Very little in Wasteland 3 is as clear as black or white, everything felt like varying degrees of gray and that's exactly why I love this game.As far as mechanics are concerned, everything plays out as it should (though misclicks can happen, so be careful with your cursor). The typical half-cover/full-cover mechanic is at play; the percentage-to-hit; all pretty standard turn-based strategy RPG stuff. But it is done well.Visually the game looks good, nothing to write home about.All-in-all I feel like the story is the star of the show here. A large part is due to the fact that it feels like you're helping to write it as you go. The choices you make along the way really do make this out to be a unique experience. I don't feel good about the ending that I got. Not because it wasn't "good" but because I kind of wonder now if the unforeseen outcomes were avoidable and if the repercussions I earned were worth the actions I took. I feel torn about the decisions I had to make. This game will stick in my head for quite a while and I wouldn't have it any other way. Also...Poultron is best boi.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I had a good time - you can feel someone was actually trying to design fun gameplay mechanics (somewhat improved fallouts).Some skills are useless (don't level up Survival).It gets very easy in mid game (I played Ranger difficulty, as I read jerk one is just enemies dod more dmg and have tons of hp), which is bad IMO - you don't have a purpose of trying to set statuses on enemies (burning, bleeding, slowed, poisoned etc.) as every fight last 2-3 turns.Character design is on point, important NPCs are actually interesting, not generated.Overall story is good, but I didn't like it - the fact that you are not doing anything "big" like saving the world from hostile AI, but rather scouting for food supplies is meh.I recommend playing this game at least till Denver (+airport) - best quest/location/characters/voice acting, itself worth purchasing. After that you may finish or not, doesn't matter.In general, it feels like inXile did first 1/3 of the game with caution and were trying to make it interesting and fun, and then they had to finish the rest - a lot of blank spots in the map, locations becomes more generic, gameplay too (go, kill, loot, return, repeat). Feels like main devs got fired or had no money for more content. TBH, it is common for many games nowadays (see all isometrics from Obsidian),

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this is like ordering a prime steak at restaurant and then the waiter sneezes on it,Most of the issues fall under party management, the major one being that if you remove a character from the party and then immediately re-add them, not only  do they lose their pet permanently, but they can't get another one -permanently- (and some parts REQUIRE you to remove party members).My main issue with the game play is that the enemy relies on suicide bombers that can one-shot you by running farther than any gun can shoot in one turn.Actually, by the end your entire party will be wiped out in one turn if you don't get initiative. This would be perfectly reasonable if triggering dialogs didn't automatically give initiative to the enemy. You die, you reload, you shoot them from a distance. The enemy AI is dumb as rocks but they "fixed" it by giving them 5x the number of hit points as your party. This of, coarse, requires the player to rely on exploits to win. So the combat isn't really tactical in any way, it's just who can cheat the best.I do really like the story and just about everything else in this game. Pity that it was ruined by bugs and short cuts.

_childDocuments_.review: Taking the best things from some excellent games, This has the RPG choices, dialogue and immersion of Pillars of Eternity 2, The fun feel of the early fallout games, and the smooth streamlined balanced combat of X-Com 2.
