_childDocuments_.review: A fun well polished C-RPG with excellent combat, good progression and engaging roleplay. Brought crashing down by forced parody and careless catastrophic immersion breaking issues.The game is very new player friendly, but benefits from the higher difficulties. Well polished with few bugs, an intuitive UI and decent graphics. The visual storytelling rewarding the observant player with stories, loot and options. Set in a well thought out postapocalyptic Colorado. The setting has a great sense of living history through compelling characters, living their own stories. I will admit more than one felt like a character I could just as easily be playing, or their legacy. There are many interesting roleplaying choices, with unclear morality, and uncertain outcomes. Occasionally suffering through the predictable negative consequences of good choices is great. The game brilliantly emphasizes choice through gameplay, and does so throughout the story. Rarely are all the options in the open and the hidden options generally feel fair. The game will recognize your choices in unexpected ways, giving the feeling of a living responsive world. The only thing I really miss are mechanics around the base and vehicle for gas and food. So why isnt this game absolutely great? Well for starters the combat gets a bit repetitive over time, there are far too few enemies and random encounter maps. The progression isnt really balanced for the lower difficulties either. The hard choices in skillup go away, and the entire consumable and equipment progression system becomes obsolete, as you dont need to learn it. These are minor issues however. There are great moments in Wasteland 3, but if you will enjoy it depends on how much parody and immersion breaking you can stand. For me the parody is was not too bad most of the time, but  the density is a bit high and more minor areas with sane people would really help. Wisely, most of the parody stuff is walled off in separate areas. I just wish someone told the random encounter designer. The careless immersion breaking is much worse. The toaster repair skill rarely comes into play, but you see it every time you open the levelup menu. A simple option to rename it to hoverdrone repair in the options would fix this and no graphics and very little text would need to be fixed. Its like the weird wasteland feat, but always on. The refugee living quarters is a good early example of bad quest design, and repeatedly breaks immersion for me. In story you have a base and you find some refugees living there, if you let them stay, for the rest of the game your troops will complain about the base being overcrowded every time you visit, which is often. The problem is that the base also has a gigantic trophy room, twenty times larger than the entire living quarters. This room remains empty until you fill it with a museum intendent and then it is a museum. So every time I pass by I get the complaint about there not being enough room, while standing next to the gigantic utterly useless vanity room. There is no option to give it to them, which would have been an interesting choice of player vanity versus roleplay. But no, the curator just wont give it up, and even shooting her does nothing. Simple dialogue changes about there being multiple barrack buildings outside your base where they live, and them needing the base power and water waste and food instead of space would fix this, while keeping the conflict intact. As a ranger with delusions of policing you have a prison. This leads to another terrible immersion breaking example. You find a potentially murderous robot who after you paralyze them you must chose to kill, or set free. There is no choice to forcibly take them to prison, even a hard one of subduing them without killing after he resists. There is also no hacking option, or anything like that. Its a trivially weak criminal you want to arrest, but somehow it can force you to either kill them or let them go entirely free. If these things dont sound too bad, you may very likely enjoy the roleplaying. If you dont like roleplaying but really like xcom tactical fights and wished there was more you could do to change how your soldiers progress and or have a bad sense of humor, you may really like the gameplay. Wasteland 3 is tantalizingly close to great, and I really sympathize with about half the writers. I had fun with it, but its a mixed bag.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed WL2. it was my first RPG of this genre. but i tried DOS 1 and DOS 2 after it. I just finished WL3 and it bleaks a lot compared to DOS. - characters, including main ones, are having no story whatsoever. only villains somewhat do, but very low detail. - all fights are exactly the same. it get serously boring- the game forces you to spend 75% of its time in battle. yet battle system is primitive. all you really can advance is chance to hit per weapon type- tactics in all the battles is the same exactly- char development strategy and party composition is also very primitive. you can develop each member specialized in one, maximum 2 weapon types. the specialization gives you a better chance to hit and a small damage boost. second and third skill for each member would be 2 more skills in discovery/exploraiton/lockpicking tree. your party covers them all in the endgame. you don't need to have a choice of strategy at all. no variability, no need to get one skilltree over another. - yet the gave makes you chose attributes/skills/perks. a process very time consuming and low-yelding as you already know what needs to be boosted as you don't need to chose- advancing skill tree gives perks, perks in most skill trees are useless. yes some are very useful (automatic weapons)- status effects never change tide of battle in your favor and useless- gear usually gives at most + 1 to an attribute/skill/perk which makes very little difference. - ambush is necessary but ill executed. it's either you ambush and start a battle first or not. placing chars is boring and time consuming and could be automated- the most real difference for your party strength comes from your armor ratingit's all dull, not well thought and generally boring

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, because I had a lot of fun while playing, but in the end I feel disappointed. I would recommend to buy it only if you are interested mostly in RPG and story-telling aspects but not so if you are here for turn-based tactics.First PROs:- The non-linear storytelling is one of the best I have ever seen in games. There are non-trivial choices everywhere and different options to pass the same quests.- RPG system is really good, lots of attributes, skills, perks, and most of them matter. Also less important skills cost less skill points, which makes total sense. Good variety of weapons and instruments as well.Then CONs:- NPC AI is terrible. It is just unbelievably bad for a year 2020. All enemies behave in the same way, and they either zerg-rush to your location or just sit there and shoot. AOE effects are totaly ignored, any NPC will mindlessly run into fire including your pet animals. Enemies never use ambush but always get trapped into yours. Many smaller games has better AI, for instance Mutant Year Zero.- I expected a lot of fights with robots, at least not less then I had in W2, but they are practically not existing. Robots were like 5% of enemies in my playthrough, and most of them were either weak or easily stunned.- And there were 0 (ZERO) vehicles or synth enemies, even though they are listed as possible enemies in weapons stats. Particularly vehicles are a huge wasted opportunity. They are a nice addition to the game, but your own vehicle is OP and I have never seen any other vehicle on the road.- Shops' inventories are leveled in a weird way, which is very limiting. You can't see better items and so you buy some trash, then instantly better items appear and you regret it. But you can't sell it back as they propose you just a few bucks in return. Even leveling Barter doesn't help much.- Covers system is weird, even slight height gives enormous advantage and covers are practically ignored for shots from above, even when characters are standing behind a wall. Enemies are not using it purposely (because of dumb AI) and this doesn't make a game any harder, it rather feels like cheating in some areas.- I expected some epic and challenging fights in the end, but it was the opposite - short and easy. They have added "epicness" by simple adding more dumb AI-controlled fighters on both sides to watch. Really? I couldn't believe my eyes. - There is a communism propaganda in this game. When you are making a game about choices you are not supposed to take sides. But not here. Everything related to communism and Soviet Union is smart, positive and friendly, not a single joke about this topic, unlike any other. But it wasn't enough and they included cosmetics item with a Soviet Union-emblem. Seriously? You wouldn't do it for Nazi symbolic, would you? But for Soviets which also killed millions of people this is suddenly ok?I am not even mentioning bugs, slow loading times etc... Technical issues can be fixed or worked around. But bad design choices and dumb AI will remain.I would give it 6/10 just for the looks and storytelling. For combat only it would be 3/10. And I would recommend to buy this game only on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this out kind of negative. I do not like top-down games. I prefer first-person POV but that's just my preference. It is this prejudice that has stopped me from experiencing the earlier fallout games. Quite frankly, I hate myself for it. This is an absolute masterpiece and as you can see I have barely begun the game. This game has revolutionized my perspective on top-down games and I plan to go back a play the beginning fall out games because of it (only good thing about buying fallout 76 is that you get the older games for free). Wasteland 3 has truly showed me what RPG really is and how much fun it can be to play the role of multiple characters. It's almost like reading a wonderful book series but you get to see it play out visually and make the decisions of key characters. I cannot recommend this game more if you're looking for a great RPG, awesome storytellers, GOOD WRITING, good voice actors, and overall laid back experience where you can have a few beers and play a game without sweating the whole time.PS. unlimited inventory storage (FU Fallout 76)

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for the aesthetics and while I want to call it a "squad based Fallout game" I think that takes away from its unique charm. The game is challenging but not overwhelming on most difficulties, the squad based combat feels satisfying with plenty of customization options that rewards diverse parties, and a constant stream of successful battles and meaningful upgrades that reward exploration and tactics. The world itself is dark but hopeful, and can make you laugh with its humor before showing you something depressing or giving you a change that can effect your fame.If you enjoy tactical RPG's, Fallout style games, or a more agressive XCOM style game then this will satisy and is worth it for its price with a very low barrier of entry.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Wasteland 2, and about 40 hours into this sequel, I've found I just don't want to play it anymore, and for one reason only. The way combat plays out isn't fun due to design decisions the devs have made regarding combat. Armor is useless, it's too easy for your own characters to get killed with one or two shots, requiring you to carry a pharmacy's worth of medical supplies with you.A search on Google on the topic related to this issue shows that it's a common complaint, and most answers on how to deal with this are the same. This demonstrates that the combat system pigeon-holes players into just a handful of strategies in order to succeed, and that's a poor game design decision.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option. It's really pretty to look at but all the game play mechanics lack depth and feel like dumbed-down. It's great game for new players of the genre, but for veterans the flaws are big.UI is absolutely horrible. Exapmle: there is no limit on how much you can carry, but then there is no option for you to short your weapons based on type, value ec. It's designed to be used by gamepad. Mods will fix that.Interaction with party members is non existed and dialocue with NPCs quite simplistic. Your party is so big that you can have every skill maxed by one of the members (dialogue, lockpicking, hacking and so on) making skill checks pointless. Fighting is kind of fun and entertaining  nice to look at but isn't very tactical or deep. Arenas are all basically the same with couple of exploding barrels and stones for cover.The open word doesn't really add anything to the experience, radiation levels make sure you don't go wrong places too early.Overall i think that the game should have been more linear action experience and just drop the open world RPG - aspect when it's so shallow that it doesn't add to the experience in any way.And then there are bugs. _childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 could as well be the "real" Fallout 3If we skip all the first person Fallout games and look at the original Fallout 1-2, Wasteland 3 could be named Fallout 3 and I wouldnt complain. Ok, it lacks Vaultboy and vaults, but the overall mood, weird humor, brutal violence, VATS shots, turn based combat, multiple endings, good/bad choices for quests etc. are close to what original Fallouts had.  While Wasteland 3 is not as vast and free as Fallout 2 was, this is still the closest thing to it we have seen since those in my opinion. Bad things are similar too; Wasteland 3 is full of small bugs, a few game breaking bugs (easy to avoid though due game saving automaticly to many slots), weirdish balance game design choices, poorish skill balance between good skills and bad skills, and poor late game balance. Call me weird, but some of those are part of the charm (not the bugs obviously), as due to many design/balance things this feels more like an old school rpg where its fun to be overpowerful and fun to do things your way, unlike in most modern rpgs where you get boring +2% perks at level up and character building is straight forward progression with no jumps.Battles are quite varied, as you dont need to face same enemies more than a few fights each, there is variety in gang styles even though their AI and tactics are pretty much the same. At world map you have plenty of more repetitive ambush fights, but those you can skip with survival skill if you want. Enemies on the hardest difficulty level are a bit of bullet sponges, but if you utilize your perks and weaponry as intended, they go down fast as VATS to the eyes in Fallout 1, so this feels like those in that aspect too. Enemy has 5x more dmg than your weapons base dmg seems, but you still one shot them all the time, go figure, but to me that feels rewarding. And the weapons, oh the weapons... full of weird weapons and full of gun porn too, you can play your favourite sniper with 0.50 anti-material rifle, your huge guy with super sledge hammer, your shotgun hobo clearing the room with automatic shotgun, your nerd guy freezing everyone with frozen ferret launcher and finishing the battle with a tactical nuke, BOOM. Actually you can play all of those, since thanks to the 6 team members you get to enjoy all the crazy and sweet weapons the game gives to you. For an isometric cRPG, the graphics are very good. Combat is full of breaking objects, gory high quality animations, and nice visual effects. And man, the music is great! They went REALLY creative with the country/gospel songs coming out of nowhere, burning bandits with a flamethrowers and while gospel chorus sings at the background has very unique atmosphere and feels awesome! Marvellous creative choices, and the sounds are great quality too! Other music is also quality work from the composer of Fallout 1-2 so you feel at home for the ambient too. I also love how everything is voice acted, as its fun just to listen to what people talk to each other in cities. Dont rush, let yourself be immersed in the world and conversations, there is plenty of fun stuff happening everywhere if you pay attention to it. There isnt nearly as much neverending conversations as in Pillars of Eternity, Tyranny, etc, but there is plenty of dialogue that happens next to you if you want to listen to it.Storywise Wasteland 3 might be disappointing to some due its simplicity, but I think it nailed the feeling of a "mission" perfectly. There are some twists in the story but nothing that made you feel that the twists are there just for the twists sake. Its a cowboy story set in the future, where you in the end decide where to pull the trigger. Doesnt need to be full of twists, simple stuff like this works perfectly for this setting and feels natural to the world. Even if you spend only a few minutes with some characters, you learn to respect them. Conversation skill trees are a bit lacking, but still used in every location of the game at least a bit.Even with the faults of balancing, bugs and some odd gameplay design choices, I am very happy with the game. Personally, while I also liked Wasteland 2, Wasteland 3 was much more immersive, more fun and more Fallout to me.  Most likely my GOtY.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I expose technical issues and rant because I care.I backed the game on fig years ago, really liked Wasteland 2 despite its clunkiness and lack of polish (Don't know if they addressed that in the director's cut version) and I'm very sad to say that I can't really recommend this one. I wish there was a rating between recommend and not recommend on Steam but at the end of the day I had to choose and the balance was a little bit more towards the "not".So what exactly happened here? Bug, mostly. The game has a lot of them, so much in fact that it prevented me to really appreciate the game.- Companions: the game rewards you for some choices with non-playable companions that will go along with you on your journey. Problem is: They're bugged as hell, same with the animal companions. They just vanish, like that. I lost 3 companions like this, one moment they're here, the next, poof!- The ui is atrocious, some inventory filters are not working properly, like for cyber mods or utility items.- When you equip an item that gives you +1 in a stat it's not displayed in the stats but when you equip an item that gives you +1 in a skill, it's displayed as if you actually have acquired that point and make the next upgrade cost MORE. There are requirements for some perks and you can actually learn them even if you don't actually have enough points, I never did that by fear of a bug if I remove an item that gives me +1.- There is no dialogue recap. The new ui makes the whole thing more cinematic but in a heavy-text RPG like this, I'd like to be able to see what a character said, especially when they talk outside of dialogue and the bubbles are bugging.- Speaking of dialogue, I encountered some HEAVY framerate drop for some reasons and it sometimes make you click twice on a dialogue thinking the game hasn't registered your click but it did, it was just lagging. This situation makes you loose the line of the character since there is no dialogue recap.- Since we're talking performance, I don't know if it's because Unity is on it's last legs but damn. Freezes at the start of encounters, when it's your companion's turn, huge framerate drop sometimes. I have a 2080 Super so it's really frustrating to see these issues, I can't begin the imagine how it must run on someone with a lesser GPU.- The IA is dumb. Your freaking cat will run in the fire if he can spend less AP reaching it's target and pathing is not working very well. You'll often see some of your rangers trigger a fight or a mine when they follow your leader because they sometimes stop at random places.- The whole choices system is borked. So I had some weird things happening, like some NPCs mentioning some stuff I didn't do, or sometimes worse, the OPPOSITE of what I did do. At the end some NPC asked me meet me in a farm that I saved early on. When the dialogue began the NPC started screaming at me and saying I was an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for not saving that farm. The farmers were standing next to me, alive and well. One quest I didn't know was time sensitive was resolved for me. When I got back to the location, it was empty with corpses everywhere. No explanation was ever given.- As per usual with games like Xcom, you will often miss even with 90% chance to hit. I once missed 3/5 revolver shots with a 95% chance.- And finally the worst offender: THE LOADING SCREENS. My god, kill me please. "Quick"load takes between 30 seconds and 1 full minute. I once got up from my desk, peed, topped up my water bottle in the kitchen and got back to see that it was still not resolved. In a modern RPG like that where you save and load a lot it's practically a sin to not optimize that. In the first city, you sometimes have 6 loading screens back to back when you have to turn a quest in and get back to HQ. I would safely say that the loading took between 1 and 2 hours out of my total playtime.And there are others... However now I would like to talk about what I personally didn't like and wasn't technical.I really enjoyed the first 2/3 of the game but the last third was so weak that it prompted me to write this review. I was so let down by the end of the game, I was expecting more, way more, in terms of content and depth. The main quest is resolved extremely quickly and the options I was given were extremely underwhelming. The wolrd map looks big at first but there is no explorations and barely 15 locales to visit, some of them being a single house.In that same last stretch of the game your characters are so empowered that you just stomp on everything that comes in your way. I killed the Golden Scorpitron in one turn. I also killed the final boss and its whole entourage in the first turn, they couldn't even act. It felt like the endgame wasn't properly playtested, if I judge by the underwhelming choices and player empowerment.I remember that in Wasteland 2, the final battle was epic and every choice you made during the game determined if you had some people helping you, here it VERY basic, only your companions will or will not come with you and that's pretty much it.Speaking of the companions, I liked Lucia alright but HATED each of the other, besides maybe the last 2 you can have. Lucia had her own quest that was resolved by the end of the game, idk about the others but they have NO depth, at all. They witness some stuff during the whole game and by the end, like, NOTHING they experienced made them think of changing their mind, it's lazy.Graphics are meh, at best. The hair look glossy and weird.Finally I think it's fair to take a step back and compare it to the competition. Divinity: Original Sin 2 was an indie game I also backed, on Kickstarter and I mean, look at it. You should strive to achieve that level of polish, content and depth and even if the last part of Divinity was kinda buggy at the release (due to too many variables in terms of the choices you could make), it was patched within a week. Where are the patch for the bugs?It took me less than 40 hours to clear the game, and I'm a completionist, I look in every nooks and crannies and talk to every NPC. I spent double that time on Divinity, the game was ALWAYS challenging (Boi that final boss) and I felt rewarded. The writing was also extremely well done and player's agency was paramount.I love you inXile, I never spent that much time writing a review and it's because I genuinely care. I backed every single one of your games and will continue to do so because I want to support you and the kind of games you make but damn you guys need wake the ♥♥♥♥ up, do the work and do it good. You HAVE to crush Divinity: Original Sin 2, it must be your sole objective if you want to make another Tactical. Upgrade your engine, Unity's done and dusted, have some proper QA, don't dumb down the experience, add more exploration, more locations, more player agenda... If Larian did it, so can you.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... what a fantastic game! I'm definitely going to do at least two more playthroughs to discover what other choices I could have made and how they will affect the people of both Arizona and Colorado. I have played a few CRPGs in my time;, Divinity: Original Sin II, Fallout 1, Wasteland 2, and a few others, but NEVER has a game made me laugh so much. Never has a game made me think so hard about my decisions to the point that I'm constantly writing pros and cons to every decision on a piece of paper to weigh up what I believe is right. Never have I been so interested in the ending, actually SEEING that all of the decisions I made had an actual impact. I love this game so much, and it has earned a place in my heart. I recommend this game to EVERYONE, whether it's your first time playing a CRPG, or you're looking for a new CRPG to sink your teeth into. My first playthough went for about 40 hours, and I'm assuming the other playthroughs that I want to do will take roughly the same amount of time. I cannot recommend this game enough; although I highly suggest you play wasteland 2 first, and at least watch a recap video about the other wasteland games.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this upon completing my first play-through of the game. All in all, I have mixed feelings. The combat is good, but does not evolve as the game progresses. Given that combat is what you will spend most of your time doing, it begins to grow stale about a third of the way into the game. If there was more variation in the enemy types, and I had to adapt my party and strategy to fit the situation, it would go a long way in keeping the combat fresh.Combat is not the only draw. The story attempts to be rich and intricate, with many decisions for the player to make which will affect their play-through one way or the other. Sadly, Wasteland 3 does not quite pull this off. I was initially intrigued by characters such as the Patriarch and his three children. However, as time went on, there was no real depth to their personalities or motivations. I have seen each of these characters a million times before, just dressed up different with different names. Stereotypes can be used to great effect, but here it feels like they were used where there should have been sustenance. The choices the player is forced to make also feel shallow and limited at times. Many times an obvious solution to an approach was completely absent from the player's options, and this is very frustrating.For example: It wasn't all bad, but it wasn't all that great either. The atmosphere and tone make up for the games shortcomings to an extent. The music is great, and used very well at times throughout the story. Solid 6/10. Decent core gameplay, a story that you'll at least want to finish, and a nice coat of paint to make it look pretty. But if you are anything like me, you probably won't be picking it up for a second play-through. For a game that is built around impactful player choices and having multiple outcomes, having low replayability is a damn shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of layers to it that allow it to shine out against the status quo in the RPG realm.The plot is unique and silly with just enough realism to make you wonder if this could happen in real life.The voice acting is well done and each character with a dialog set stands out and has emotional depth.The customization of your party members and vehicles is well thought out and decisions, while seemingly subtle, can absolutely be felt.The fighting is engaging and challenging with lots of dialog options that open up and are able to be explored depending on how your party members perks and abilities are tuned.The open world is quite large, and at ~40 hours in, i have yet to even complete 1/3 of it.This game, to me, feels like a mash up between the depth of the plot and level design of divinity original sin 2, the combat of xcom 2, with a universe similar to something from the fallout series.9/10Highly recommend, and am anxiously looking forward to another play through to experience the perks and dialog options i neglected this run.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, howdy there, stranger! Name's Wyatt Earp, and I've got a tale to share 'bout the Wasteland 3 game. Now, I may not have experienced a post-apocalyptic world myself, but I've seen my fair share of lawless towns and dangerous outlaws. So, let's dive into this review, shall we?In Wasteland 3, you find yourself in the frozen wastelands of Colorado, a land ravaged by nuclear war. Now, I've dealt with my fair share of lawlessness, but this here game takes it to a whole new level. You'll be leadin' a group of Desert Rangers, tryin' to restore order in this chaotic landscape. It's a fight for survival, where every decision you make can have far-reaching consequences.The gameplay in Wasteland 3 is what you'd call a tactical RPG, partner. You'll be explorin' the frozen wilderness, takin' on quests, and engagin' in turn-based combat. The combat is where things get real interestin'. You gotta use cover, plan your moves carefully, and make strategic choices to come out on top. It's all about usin' your noggin' and thinkin' ahead, just like I used to do when facin' outlaws on the dusty streets of Tombstone.Now, let me tell ya 'bout the world of Wasteland 3. It's a gritty, unforgivin' place filled with desperate folks and dangerous factions. The visuals paint a vivid picture of this post-apocalyptic landscape, with its icy tundras and ruined cities. The attention to detail is somethin' to behold, partner, and it really helps immerse you in this lawless world.One thing that stands out 'bout Wasteland 3 is the story. Now, I've always been a sucker for a good tale, and this game delivers. It's got complex characters, moral dilemmas, and twists and turns that'll keep you on the edge of your seat. You'll be makin' tough choices that can affect the fate of the wasteland and its inhabitants. It's just like bein' in the middle of a high-stakes showdown, where every move counts.I reckon I gotta mention that Wasteland 3 ain't for the faint of heart. It's a challenging game, partner, and you'll be facin' some tough enemies and makin' difficult decisions along the way. You gotta be ready to deal with the consequences of your actions, and sometimes that means sacrificin' for the greater good.One thing I admire 'bout Wasteland 3 is the attention to detail and player choice. You can customize your Desert Rangers, upgrade your gear, and even make alliances with different factions. It gives you a real sense of agency and allows you to tackle the wasteland in your own way. The developers have really gone the extra mile to make sure you have plenty of options and freedom to shape your own story.Now, like any good tale, Wasteland 3 does have its fair share of flaws. Some folks have reported technical issues and occasional bugs. But, just like me takin' down outlaws in Tombstone, the developers have been workin' hard to address those issues and provide updates to improve the game.So, if you're lookin' for a gritty, immersive post-apocalyptic adventure, Wasteland 3 might just be your ticket. It's got tactical gameplay, a compelling story, and enough player choice to keep you comin' back for more. So saddle up, partner, and get ready to face the challenges of the wasteland head-on. Remember, in the lawless land of Wasteland 3, it's up to you to bring justice and restore order. Ride on!

_childDocuments_.review: So I recommend the game for the right crowd. If you were a die hard Wasteland 2 fan this one is NOT done in the same light. So hear me out and let me walk you through why this game broke my heart.Like so many I waited for Wasteland 3 with baited breath. It was to be THE game I had been waiting for with a great leader (Brian Fargo) behind it I hoped it would be everything wasteland 2 was and more. I got the game like so many other fans and played it for some time. I was intrigued but I kept waiting to be sucked in... so that all I wanted to do is play the game through and play it again or try different choices. I never got sucked in.... I found myself FORCING myself to play it, because I wanted it so badly to be the true Wasteland 3 in my mind.The reason that wasteland 2 sucked me in so greatly was the choices or illusion of choices in some situations that were real world choices in a way. Sometimes there is no right choice and you just have to decide what side of the line you want to fall on. You never had any weird carni Cities or thought that it was too cartoony or unrealistic. Everything that happened in wasteland 2 was at least in the possible realm. The darkness, the Grit, and the Characters, although at times over the top, could still suck you in.Wasteland 3 took the borderline walked by Wasteland 2 and a blew it away. Half of the weapons, armor, and mode of transportation seem to be a little too far fetched, cheesy, or just annoyingly cartoony. The stories and quests are alright, but the characters usually feel a little hollow. You almost never feel like you're doing extra right or extra wrong by anyone. The immersion is also sometimes broken by puzzles that don't make any sense or have to be looked up on google. It just does not have the same GRIT that the original fallouts or wasteland 2 had. This game was made with children in mind and probably rightfully so, though, it is and was disappointing to me to deviate from the realism of past games. Ultimately this game is for a lot of people, but I myself cannot feel it the way I did with Wasteland 2. The gritty reality and darkness are there at times for sure... but are put off by the cartoony props and somewhat hollow characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Great follow up in a series!  So far the choices you make can have huge impacts, the skills and stats you choose are hard choices, and the story and characters feel more memorable this time around.  For an RPG these are the things that make a good game great.  There are a few issues (quality of life) that I hope get settled out in patching, for example mods need to be able to be removed (scraping a weapon or piece of armor should have a chance based on mod skill for each mod applied to return to the inventory)....top down scroll out needs to be adjusted just a bit to allow for a larger view of the battlefield (minor gripe but just a bit more would be a huge tactical help, not being able to see stats on hit percentage because its out of view range is a pita especially for snipers), useful junk items need to be noted in white not grey, and equipable utility items need their own tab in the UI.Performance issues are still a problem on high end machines but again hopefully this will get worked out in patching (my personal gripe is left shift lag/stutter).All in so far and having a blast.  Thanks inXile for making a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Stopped playing when I got the kumbaya achievement. Other than that, it's decent. It copies a lot of Fallout's homework; not in a way that's new and feels like an extension of the Fallout universe. They just copied a bunch of the same ideas and re-used them. There are some cool original ideas but not enough to make it great. It reads like New Vegas with the Wild Wasteland perk. I didn't really care about the characters besides the two self-inserts I made. I found myself grinding through it just for the serotonin hit and to see how the story wraps up. The mechanics are pretty good and the AI makes the game challenging enough. There's a few glitches here and there and a couple of times I had to reload a save. Other than that, the friendly fire off option makes the game very annoying; hit (not kill) an ally and now you're regarded as an enemy. It's a 5/10. Good distraction but don't expect New Vegas 2.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Right now, since there are no "NEUTRAL" reviews on Steam, IN IT'S CURRENT STATE, its a no from me. If the bugs get ironed out, its a pretty good game. If it gets fixed, I'll likely change to a recommend.Got 2 copies as a Fig Backer to play with my brother. My single player experience (POSSIBLE MINOR SPOILERS):GOOD:--Love that the choices REALLY matter and there are a LOT of them in this game.--Many different ways to approach a situation and your reputation affects interactions. Your reputation MAY be good enough to talk yourself out of fights! Many opportunities for KISS ASS and HARD ASS and other Squad builds (Nerd stuff, Mechanics, etc.) to be useful throughout the game.--The fire modes have grown on me. Some weapons have their own perks which add a fire mode. Other fire modes are available via perks you can obtain in the perk tree. The Precision Strike you get once your strike meter is full is very powerful and can change a fight (can malfunction a robot with aimed shot or fire a huge burst to take out multiple hostiles).--You can build a new squad member at any time that will start at your current level. Messed up a squad member build? That's okay, just create a new one.--I like the PREPARE and AMBUSH abilities. PREPARE lets you save up to 2 AP for next turn. The AMBUSH ability allows your squad members to trade in some AP to fire on an enemy that enters their range during hostile turns.--I love the Animal Whisperer skill and animal companions. I like the variety of animals you can bring along with your squad.--Shift key to highlight stuff you can interact with. This takes away having to pixel hunt for obscured boxes and containers. When you get old and can't see as well you appreciate stuff like this.--I like that I only have to loot one body at the end of combat and I can easily cycle through and grab the loot from all the other lootable bodies in the area.--A high Luck attribute will occasionally result in more loot, and even free actions. Sometimes you'll get a free attack or a free movement from a lucky action.--I like the variety and usefulness of Utilities (+5% XP, +2 PER, +1 Weapon/Armor modding, etc.)--A lot of stuff that can be used for cover can also be shot and destroyed.--Humor can be a bit over-the-top, but I've chortled quite a few times.NOT SURE:--Can only charm a single animal per squad member with Animal Whisperer. You CAN get other special animal followers that don't count as the single. While disappointed, I can see why they limited it (more would be OP and they can start to get in the way during combat).--Enemies have a circular view area, which means even if you're trying to sneak past behind them, you can still be "seen" after a brief time.BAD/BUGS:--Cant team crouch. You have to manually go through all of your squad and crouch them 1 by 1, and it costs 2 AP to crouch in combat. You also cant move crouched as far as I know. You can't "change stances" (AKA crouch or stand up) while in cover, either. Save a game right before a fight with all your squad members crouched and ready to go? When combat locks up and you have to load the save, you have to re-crouch everybody.--Combat can lock up, causing you to have to reload a previous save (for me, twice per play session usually but sometimes twice for the same fight).--Attributes, Skills, Combat Buffs/Debuffs (and probably other stuff) need more tool tips.--Lost character progression.--Very laggy Dialogue Tree and later in the game the inventory gets laggy too.--Creating a Bookworm Squad Member with 1 STR creates a situation where your Squad Member is losing 3 CON (total hit points) every level up and will be erased like Marty McFly in B2TF.--Load screens are too long. 30+ seconds to load into different zones, over 1.5 minutes to load a game on SSD. From another review: "while we wait, let us read the lore books we've collected."--Squad portraits don't stay in order.--When you have more than 6 Ranger recruits in the select character screen, the "Companions" section gets pushed off-screen, hiding their portraits, and making it very unintuitive to add them back into your squad (you have to use the keyboard). Need a scroll bar here.--Saves don't have specific names so can be easily overwritten. There is only 1 autosave by default, and later on the game autosaves right after a game changing decision, making you have to revert to a manual save (2 hours earlier for me) if you wanted to try different options. I recommend turning on timed saves as well as taking advantage of quicksaves (and of course saving often!)--FPS drops, sometimes so bad you have to reload.--Squad Members shooting through walls/floors/ceilings.--Radiation difficult to detect in some areas and no warning (other than your squad health draining) going from radiation level 2 to 3 for instance.--Combat messages briefly appear above your acting Squad Member's head and are easy to miss (like "Out of Range")--When getting shot at, the camera doesn't always auto focus on who is shooting you.--At least three bugged missions I can think of (but hey, one is an unlimited money glitch so more of a feature).--Character models and other things (switches) not loading properly leading to invisible characters you can interact with (or fight with, as it happens in combat sometimes too).--The game can become unresponsive when trying to move 2 Squad Members separately and interact with someone.--Explosive Barrels not actually exploding when shot (this seems to be related to being too far away from the barrel when sniping it, as if you get closer, they'll actually explode).--Cybernetic Implants are a good idea, but they take up your Utility Slot instead of giving you another slot dedicated to them so when you have the ability to finally use them, it feels more like a trade-off rather than an augmentation.--No Inventory filter for Utilities. Gotta scroll through your hundreds of items and the Utilities aren't even grouped together entirely in the inventory, they are scattered throughout.--When you open a door to a closed room, fog of war usually obscures what is in the room until you physically walk a squad member into the room.--Cannot have multiple types of the same animal in a Squad with multiple Animal Whisperers.--Don't try to loot two containers at once.--Some traps can't be disarmed.--Various graphic glitches like missing texture or dialogue bubbles that are blank or don't disappear.--Can't remove and reuse weapon mods.--Some equipped weapons will display inflated damage numbers (by 300% in some cases) until re-equipped. Not even sure how long it has been that way or if it was affecting my game.--If you misclick the filter categories in a vendor encounter on the World Map, it'll kick you out of the encounter to the radio and you can't get back to the random encounter at that time. I only mention this since I've done it so many times.--You can't pause the game which may or may not affect time sensitive quests. You can be detected and attacked in the menu (escape key) or in your inventory.--There is no way to have Special companions/followers that you get from Missions follow a different squad member. If you dump that Squad Member later, you lose the follower too (as far as I know).--Get radio signals with "coordinates to follow" yet I have no clue who from or what it opened up on the map (if anything).--Gaining access to certain parts of the Rangers HQ requires you to do something pretty awful.--I'm out of room....It feels like I'm fighting against the game more than the Wasteland sometimes. I don't even want to try multiplayer until it gets fixed (and my brother doesn't either).If you're a developer of this game, thank you for your time and effort! Polish it up and I'll be happy to change this to a recommend! Edited for clarity/additions and I cut a lot. Thank you for reading and thank you for the comments and awards! Have a great day and be kind to others.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far (29 hours in). Playing on Hard. I write a paragraph below on my one big design issue but I love the game and don't want that to get lost. Just thinking at length about what bugs me. Pros:X-Com style combatDeep RPG character mechanicsGreat voice acting and writingNicely cracked worldviewCons:Small technical glitches (I haven't hit anything game breaking that a reload or alternate option didn't solve)Companion characters don't do as much commentary as I thought they wouldBiggest Issue:The high level of synergy developed with the main team over time makes it very hard to slot in a new character. You will be dramatically less efficient and they don't appear to bring that much to the table anyway so hard to justify switching. For example, Scotchmo has small arms plus lockpicking. I already have max lockpicking on my tank. To add him, I will lose survival/weapon modding or sneaky ♥♥♥♥/kiss ass/armor modding from my other companions. That means I not only need to switch him in and max the skills he has, I also need to switch out the tank and give the new ranger the skills I am losing. Too much hassle for a handful of voice lines that might come up at some point in the future. Maybe I don't know what i'm missing but it is hard to see the value. Maybe later when everyone has lots of points and skills, this will be an easier switch to make.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few times where I do not understand why a game has such good reviews on steam. Wasteland 3 is competently made, but other than that is incredibly bland, both in the gameplay and writing department. Writing: Wasteland 3 tries so incredibly hard to hit that sweet spot between funny and serious that the Fallout games are known for. I understand humor is subjective, but this game made me cringe more than it made me laugh, and this undercuts the more serious parts. In general I find the world building to be all over the place and unfocused to a point where I can barely remember anything from the 14 hours I have played.Gameplay: Unlike the writing, this is less subjective. The balancing is completely screwed. It took no effort at all to build a team of experts that allowed me to pass around 90% of all skill checks I encountered. In general, the extremely easy gameplay sucks out any complexity the RPG system could have. The combat is serviceable, but mechanically incredibly underwhelming, especially compared to other RPGs out there. However, this might make it a good RPG for newcomers. Quick Disclamer: There are a couple difficulty options in game, that might make this better for some, but I have found them to only make a small difference.I sadly cannot recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Great to see that original line of post apocalyptic games keeps keeping on!Wasteland 3 has expanded its gameplay while keeping awesomeness of Wasteland 2. Mechanically it has solid and fun combat with multiple builds and combinations to try . Travelling on global map is even more fun with colorful armored truck.Atmosphere of Colorado is incredible with really great soundtrack, weird characters, and plenty of choices. Plot of this story is definitely a strong part of this game. Despite of all weirdness of characters here, their actions are logical and make sense in this world. Choices that i had to make were real ones and had many pros and cons. Art is comical, colorful and grim at the same time.All together it allows to play real RPG with specific character and story in mind. Could it be better? Yes, but what we have here is already better then 99.9% of RPGs on Steam. Some passages could have been more detailed, and plot lines could have more branching. There are bugs, but i have not seen anything game breaking.I really hope that InXile will keep building on this story further. I had to wait for a long time since Wasteland 2 and then since announcement on kickstarter, and then since demo. But it is here now, and it is a great RPG!

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is a good RPG/Strategy game with good writing and dialog options a good Soundtrack and good graphics. The Combat is very bloody and sometimes very hard as well especially when you encounter Scorpitrons together with lots of other robots. This game feels more like Fallout and is also better than Wasteland 2 which was also a lot of fun. The songs are also very good that play on the radio when you drive around on the worldmap or on certain missions/locations. The missions are good and fun some were annoying but there could be more missions and more places to visit. There is not much you can visit and the random encounters can be quite annoying. I love to fight Scorpitrons they are quite rare but there is a lot of stuff to loot when you encounter one of them on the worldmap.The Characters are also cool and I love Major Tomcat the animals help a lot during combat and have a good amount of health and can do a lot of damage as well. The humor is also very good and the character voices but some characters were hard to understand because they were talking in an annoying way not a very big problem because I'm playing with subtitles. I also appreciate that your squad can't really die you can always resurrect them and fix them up (it is a game over when all your squad members get downed) and you can learn abilities that are also very helpful. The combat feels better than in Wasteland 2 and there is a lot of cover you can take or destroy.The game however still has a lot of bugs from infinite loadingscreens to weird character bugs were you can't open crates or even heal teammates. The enemies also shoot through walls or throw healing darts through walls which can be quite annoying. I also don't like the shared inventory when you play co-op would be better if each player has their own inventory and also can loot what the other player already looted. The game doesn't pause when you press ESC which is quite annoying. Also some weird vehicle bugs too nothing that annoying but still weird. Would love some more places to visit and more missions I'm still not done with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, but wanted to put my 2 cents in on this game. I "like" rpgs, but I don't LOVE them. I have Pillars of Eternity and Divinity Original Sin, but didn't finish either of them. This game is one I can see myself finishing. It's a great combo of RPG with Fallout kinda vibes. I really like the post-apocalyptic vibe. I strongly recommend making your own custom characters. I started with one of the pre-set groups and then restarted with 2 custom chars. I'm really enjoying this game so far. I like the characters, the sense of humor and the tough choices. If you like RPG type games and especially post-apocalyptic games, I'd give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: A superb opening, decent middle, and good finish.Wasteland 3 opens with an abundance of choice. It was only now, after having beaten the game and looking up several aspects online, that I realized that I had let my very first playable companion die within an hour of starting the game not because she was doomed to that fate, but simply because I didn't have the proper skills to save her. What would be flavor text in other games leads to tangible separate paths in Wasteland 3, and your companions host a litany of possible reactions based on your decision making and the gradual ideology you start to form during your trek across Colorado. Unfortunately, those reactions in and of themselves *are* little more than flavor text, for the most part, and are sparse in their volume. There were so many times where I was certain at least one of my party members would chime in on specific events as they unfolded in front of our eyes, yet they remained silent 95% of the time. Their silence in the overworld belies good character arcs for the quests principally concerning each companion first and foremost, yet that focus swings in and out on a whim as you go along the main story, and never result in what I would call well-defined characters in your party. That isn't to say that they aren't memorable in moments, or that the world at large isn't either. Wasteland 3 carries moments of absolute brilliance, often accompanied by its phenomenal soundtrack, yet those separate instances never coalesce into a singular whole. Plot threads that are excellent in their execution are forgotten altogether after their quest wraps, characters that you'd love to see more of will never move from their rooted spot in the ground, and the narrative as a whole ultimately fails to pack much of a punch. Even so, that doesn't change the fact that those individual moments of stellar quality are stellar all the same, and I would say well worth the entrance fee on their own. It's just a shame Wasteland 3 never truly realizes the potential that shone so brightly in its opening.

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving Wasteland 3 the thumbs up with a caveat - they need to fix their bugs first. As of 04.11., there are still numerous bugs that need attention, some really game-breaking - ergo you cannot progress forward in your main quest line and either have to look for solutions online or restart the entire game. However, the rest of the game is very enjoyable, both fun and punishing, and it's hard to say no to a game that kept me glued to the laptop until 7-8 in the morning, itching to play it more and more.The GOOD:1. The STORY: in a very dark post-apocalyptic setting, where everything goes, and the law is non-existent, you lead 2 surviving rangers in a land torn by war, plunder, pillage, and struggle for power. Your decisions will shape the outcome of everything. It is amazing just how much you can influence everything - easily 50% of the locations are tied to various outcomes which you will examine at the end of the game in a very creative story summary.2. The COMBAT: the AI will make you rage over and over, be it at its own stupidity, or at their crazy way to do everything possible to incapacitate at least a few of your rangers a turn while your guys miss everything XCOM style. While I am sure that there are many hardcore Wasteland 3 gamers, saving before a fight is the best way to avoid losing tons of progress, as the combat is tough as nails. But when you win a tough fight... nothing compares to this feeling of accomplishment.3. The interactions: combat isn't everything. You are given plenty of options to avoid it through speech interactions. This allows you to roleplay a bit and tailor the experience to your own playstyle, which is always welcome in an RPG of this type.4. The locations are diverse and interesting, often offering multiple ways of advancement and approach to the end goal.5. The music will be down to personal preference, but even as a foreigner, I quite enjoyed the country style songs. It gives a real post-apocalyptic wild west style to it.The BAD:1. BUGS, BUGS, BUGS. One bug is so bad, that it locks you in combat somehow (even though you obviously are not), preventing you from entering the next zone in Aspen. This very much breaks the main story line, making the game impossible to win. While I am sure that the developers are working on the issues, the game definitely needed more play-testing, as I slowly started to get tired of seeing dark rooms (even though I have a ranger who can scout it), modifications going on the wrong weapon when having two equipped, etc. Keeping multiple hard saves and quicksaving is an absolute must unless you want to lose hours and hours of progress at the time.2. The COMBAT: one of the more irritating issues with it is the 4-directional movement. While I eventually got used to it, people who played XCOM and similar games will find it exceptionally annoying, forcing you to spend 1 AP if moving N, S, E, W and 2 points if moving NE, SE, NW, SW. I suppose taking step to the side is different to taking an angular step of 45 degrees in any direction. In a game where action points are everything, this is not a fun experience when you are facing an overwhelming force and every shot and AP counts. I'd add the AI stupidity on certain occasions to it, but with the combat as tough as it is, I never cared all too much.Conclusion:Wasteland 3 is a very solid 7/10 experience for anyone who enjoys the franchise, or a good mixture of RPG/Turn based combat XCOM style. The story is solid, the decisions you make are extremely impactful, and there is no easy way around it. Be with a wink and a smile, or a smoking barrel of a gun, you need to move forward and shape the state of the land as you envision it, or as intended by the developers. With each play-through ranging from 30-40 hours, the game is an easy buy at 25% or more off. At full price, I would still stay away from it for a month or so, until they fix all the glaring issues with it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Could use alot more development time". The game launch was the biggest disaster I have seen in a game. (And I play Battlefield) It did not even run on most systems. The devs had to crunch for two weeks after release making patches, just to make it run and then ran like crap! One year later a great mountain of issues remain. The game is playable in singel player, but very buggy.  Save alot and keep multple saves, because of bugs like game crashes, your characters getting stuck, missions just bugging out completely.  There are alot of numbers in this game, they do no really seem to represent anything, equipment with worse stats are often better. Enemies with much bigger number the you are easy at normal difficulty but lower sometimes may be almost undefeatable. Just ignore all numbers and go for it if you play.The atmosphere is great in the game! But leave your brain out of the story! Most of the story arches and motivations make no sense what so ever if you think about them. There are alot of stories but they seems to been slapped in there with haste, written without care or understanding of storytelling. Think of a fan-fic written by a 12 year old.It can be very addictive but alot of players will not finish out of frustration. Can't recomend you buy it at full price €60. Current value at most €20.

_childDocuments_.review: 31 Hours in and still only scratched the surface, I've had a lot of fun.Good XCOM style combat, with RPG party management and a really remarkable story that adjusts to all your decisions in surprising ways.It's actually kind of impressive how much is in the game, considering the size of the studio developing it, this does show sometimes though in the form of bugs, jank and general roughness in some parts of the game, even after all the patches.My biggest gripes are the performance and roughness of the game, it feels like it needs a lot more polishing. And the weirdly serious, then wacky dialogue, it's like playing New Vegas on Wild Wasteland X10, great if you are into that, but the zanieness can get a bit over the top sometimes.Overall though, a great purchase, I would reccomend even warts and all for a fun, Fallout XCOM hybrid.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on the original back in the day and enjoyed Wasteland 2, but I've got issues with this one.Right off the bat you can only customize 2 characters. This is just too limiting considering the history of these games.I also have a problem with the amount of profanity in the game. You want to sprinkle some throughout the game to add emphasis here and there? Fine, that's called flavor. But when you are bombarded with it in the tutorial and it is even in the character creation area, that's just too much. When it is everywhere it becomes too common. I get it, you want to shock people and beat Cyberpunk 2077 to the punch, but if you are going away from what has worked so well in the past then you should at least add a filter.Lastly, something about the graphics is off. The extra flair just doesn't fit the old engine. I know that keeping the engine saves cost and effort but maybe the graphics shouldn't have been so extravagant if you weren't going to upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how, but the developers made a game that runs slow on GTX 2080 laptop, that's really impressive for a game with mediocre graphics and small levels. Each time it loads between locations I remember those times when I played fallout 2 on Pentium 166MMX machine: waiting, just waiting.But bigger issue with the game is: BUGS. Still haven't fixed the Fishlips bug though it's widely reported, and the bug with characters getting negative stats after switching them (a lot of people complained about that on reddit). And it's not only technical bugs, for example in Old Survivalist Bunker if you choose to avoid guards you will still trigger dialog "what's up with all that shooting" and later new shift of guards will come in saying that "someone wiped out the last shift".That's not just bad QA work, that's some plot holes. I'm not sure how the game at this stage got to production. It's a promising game for people who love old school fallout style rpg, but it definitely not worth $60. Don't buy it now, buy it later when (hopefully) all bugs are fixed and price is more adequate. To compare, Fallout 4 and Dead Red Redemption 2 costs the same but it's way ahead of Wasteland 3 in terms of graphics (at the moment of release),  gameplay options, size of levels and overall amount of objects/npcs you can use and interact with.

_childDocuments_.review: Having never played any of the other games in the series, I saw some gameplay and was quite intrigued.I like playing Divinity: Original Sin 2 on occasion, and while it is fun, sometimes the fantasy aspects of it just aren't my cup of tea.This game feels very much like that game, which is great, but takes out all the fantasy and replaces it with guns and steel and robots. And it's a blast. The combat is straight forward, but really fun so far. While it does play on a grid, it seems to have a bit more flexibility than an X-Com type game. It reminds me more of Gears Tactics, which I really enjoyed playing.All in all, I would definitely recommend this game if you enjoy Top Down RPGs like Divinity, or want more story and choice than the usual turn-based combat style game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Simply a fantastic game, and I'm not even a huge fan of isometric turn-based strategy titles. The story is outstanding: lots of humor, intrigue, choices, and ways to alter outcomes based on leveled up skills. The turn based combat is outstanding: I've found that you can build a variety of different characters that specialize in different fields, and those skills are frequently put to use during combat, and not during combat.  So you never build a character that feels weak, or seldom used. Very much appreciate this.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: I played about half of Wasteland 2 years ago and didn't really get into it that much, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that Wasteland 3 is a much better incarnation of the series and one that I was actually keen to complete.Wasteland 3 is a very good game with a great storyline punctuated by some genuinely difficult moral dilemmas with which you are forced to wrestle. I honestly found myself frequently weighing up the pros and cons of my decisions and agonizing over which path felt the most righteous to me, as few things in the game are totally black and white. Its rare when a game is able to achieve this, so bravo to the devs for that. The characters and voice acting are also superb - really top notch - and practically all of it was voiced. It made me actually care about the people I was dealing with. The jokes all hit their mark, as did the poignant moments.In terms of criticisms, I would say that the power balancing was off by quite some way. I started the game barely being able to scratch most bullet-sponge enemies until about a third of the way through when I found some high end weaponry and suddenly I was one-shotting everyone I came across right up to the end. Also, while the map was big it was also largely empty, which felt a little pointless because there really aren't that many random encounters that occur while you're travelling around it.Overall though, a great story thats extremely well acted, with some tough, meaningful decisions to be made and some very enjoyable gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, no doubt. It has amazing dialogs, great voice acting and immersive gameplay as compared to its previous versions. * The character building system is more concise now. (although it has a few downfalls as well)* The environment is lively. Going into towns or settlements makes you feel like they're "alive".* There is no longer a typewriter that will constantly keep typing every time you walk somewhere ! Instead, you can just highlight the area you're in (press the Z key) and you can find interactable/clickable objects or areas for lore.* When you're fighting in encounters, the weapon animations and sounds are much better than WL2. The same goes for the music. Some fights have special music which really fits the scene.* There are 2 additional slots for armor now, helmet & legs. You can also modify your armor with different mods.* The quest logs system is organized in a better manner and is easier to understand than WL2. It also has a level system, that tells you if you're under (or over) level for a particular quest.* Buying/selling weapons is easier, since your inventory is combined by default and characters don't have individual inventories.* Minor spoiler ahead: * Minor spoiler ahead: * There's also a reputation mechanism now, from where you can track the Ranger's reputation as well as their reputation with various factions. Its an interesting mechanic and is often used in many conversations throughout the game. It also influences many encounters.Unfortunately, the current state of this game is the reason why I am not recommending this game. It has TOO many bugs, which I will highlight separately.* The biggest gripe that I have about this game is the , so here's a sub-section for it:-^ Unlike WL2, the accuracy for all characters is hard capped at 95%. So, even if you invest points to increase your accuracy, whether through Attributes or Skills, it will never go beyond 95%. That means you ALWAYS have a 5% chance to miss. That doesn't sound too bad...except when it feels like you miss MUCH more than 95%. 95% means 9.5 times out of 10. On average, I would miss 3-4 shots out of 10 shots. That's ridiculous. Also yes, I have played a lot of XCOM games and that is what it reminded me of.^ To compensate for the lack of accuracy, a player is actually supposed to invest points in the Intelligence attribute, which increases their crit. chance. That was never clearly explained. ^ Another huge change from WL2 is that now you can choose which character to shoot first, regardless of initiative. This was a very stupid change IMO and it took some getting used to. ^ Following that, you no longer have that bar in the top-center of the screen that showed you whose turn it was next. Because of that, you can't plan ahead accordingly and you have to shoot whoever your character can shoot, instead of particularly aiming for one enemy because their turn was next.^  This was a huge change from WL2 and it honestly annoyed me a lot. I was always uncertain of investing mods in my weapons, knowing either I might get a better weapon later on or might not get a better mod. (or both)^ Unlike WL2 DC, Precision strikes are no longer available immediately. Instead, you have to build up for it by shooting enemies and killing them. That's not a big dislike, but I just didn't like the fact that they changed this up. I liked having it for all my characters and using it wisely.* The loot pool was very...strange. For eg: for ammo boxes, you could either loot 3 flamethrower fuel (which is very cheap) or you could loot 9-17 5.56 ammo & 4-8 energy cells (which is obviously more expensive combined). Naturally, I was rarely save-scumming, but I could notice these things and it confused me a lot.* Heavy story spoilers ahead: ^ So, you can have pets as friendly characters to give you a small bonus & fight alongside you, same as WL2. However, there were a lot of encounters when my pet was , and the game decided not to include it in the encounter. I can understand if there might have been specific encounters where animals/robots weren't allowed, but I noticed that some pets would be active and some wouldn't. There was no logic behind it, it was just...random. ^ Combat animations would randomly get glitched. For eg: if my character is in cover and I move him up, he would stay in the crouched animation and he would just...slide over. The animation of him getting up, running and then going in cover, wasn't there. Why ? Go figure.* When you're travelling in the world map, if you enter a new area, the name of the area comes up in all caps. and then slowly fades out. However, it doesn't always fade away and it gets permanently etched on the screen until you save-quit. * Minor spoiler ahead: * Minor spoiler ahead: * There is no limit on inventory. You literally have infinite inventory and none of your characters can be encumbered. I both like & dislike that, but for role-playing purposes, its obviously not logical.* The Toaster Repair skill is useless. You just get tokens and lore books out of it now and they no longer have mission critical items. * Exploring the World Map with your car/truck is very refreshing, yet I wish I had the option of changing out my vehicle. That huge monstrosity is certainly far from looking like a Ranger's vehicle, but sadly, you never get the option of changing the vehicle itself.* I might be stupid on this one, but strangely enough, the "Weird Science" had actually nothing to do with..Computers but "Nerd Stuff" was all to do with computers. I don't know, maybe its my perspective. They could have labelled them in a better manner.* Speaking of which, the Weird Science skill is..weird and next to useless. Its only used for a few armor and a few weapons. Outside of that, it has no use.This took me more than an hour to type, but if it helps out anyone in buying or not buying this game, I'll appreciate it. Thanks for reading. Also, I had to shorten the review because there's a character limit.

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't take itself as serious as the Fallout franchise - You can't go 5 minutes without a pun or very contrived sit-com. Fine so far.The control and combat are straight from a 1990s "we can't sell this crap" reject pile. Some random stupidities: Usually combat start with a little dialogue, unless you shoot on sight. That means your team is in the open, getting creamed by enemies that take the first turn. Once combat has started, you can be lucky if you don't walk instead of shoot, shoot instead of use skill and so on.The story and characters are the usual post apocalyptic over the top fare. At best it makes you feel smart for getting some pop culture reference from 1990. At worst it's just bad writingSince it's just a halfbaked "not early access, honest!" game that trickle feeds you content as DLC I am putting it on hold until it is actually done. Sometime 2022 I guess. I got the game assuming I am buying a finished product since there was no DLC announcements, no season pass etc and WL2 was a one off prodeuct as well. Turns out we only got the barebones version now.

_childDocuments_.review: A gigantic step up from Wasteland 2, I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of WRPGs and want to play a game with multiple game world altering choices, the ability to create up to 4 of your own party members out of a 6 member party, and a wide variety of different builds around either explosives, guns, melee weapons, or just plain wacky future gadgets! The quest design is immaculate and gives you a huge manner of expression as to how you want your rangers to be perceived in the world, whether as ruthless justicars or hope for the downtrodden, or even ruthless, cold-blooded killers out for personal gain. Definitely one of my favorite RPGs in recent years, and I look forward to jumping back in to try for a different ending!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, a bit of context: After the first instalment (1980s), two more instalments were planned but never saw the light of day. In this way, Wasteland ended up serving as the basis for the development of Fallout. Today Fallout has taken a different path and thanks to crowfunding the missing parts of the trilogy have been released.What stands out most about Wasteland 3 is its commitment to making decisions matter, meaning that it's possible to either screw up miserably or get a great reward at the most unexpected moment.The combat is tactical and turn-based, and is not the most remarkable part of the game, but it strives to offer, like the story, interesting choices and several possibilities for the player to explore.Is it classic? Yes, it is.Is it subtle? Not at all.Are there better in the genre? There might be.Is it recommendable to play it? Without a doubt.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Wasteland 2 and this is more of the same, but a little bit better in every aspect.  It's not revolutionary, it's just fun to play.   Combat is fun, exploring is fun, there are lots of little jokes thrown in - "Flab the Inhaler" ~ "Vlad the Impaler", the Joker in the casino brothel, etc.   I don't play Co-op so can't speak to that but I can't wait to find another 30 minutes throughout the day to go explore the wasteland before real life intrudes.  When you're old like me, you don't have time to waste on games that aren't fun and this game is quickly becoming one of my favorites.

However, I don’t regret playing it, because underneath the mound of issues lays buried a pretty good cRPG which will most likely come to shine with a Director’s Cut.Pros:+ Great progression system+ Improved writing that’s mixing seriousness and humor+ The combat system has its moments+ Fantastic soundtrack+ Fully voice acted+ Replay valueCons:– Consolized camera and UI– Flawed initiative system– Dated graphics– Poor performance and nerve wrecking loading times– Price tag– Bugs, bugs, bugs…Read the full review at:

broken animations, kodiak moves half buried in the ground on world map, vehicle movement animations bug out and just slides on the ground without any apparent movement- stuck in chat while game still runs in background, this is poor game design, if you are sneaking try to avoid detection and get stuck in chat that you cannot escape, happen in multiple places, very poor implementation of sneak/stealth- declared % chance is a nonsense, tested it on several mechanics, 95% hit chance is around 77% (231 hits from 300 shots), 10 luck double money chance on money chest declared is 5% real chance is 2% (2 from 100 tries), it was probably implemented by the same guy as in wasteland 2 who has no idea what % is- you can't snipe enemy before you get detected in some cases are dialog locked so you have 0 choice but to get to them end engage in dialog before you can kill them - sniper attack from sneak triggers dialog, what brainless moron coded that into the game- bugged random swap primary and secondary weapon, randomly weapons not reloaded outside of combat so i have to reload them manually- bugged inconsistency while traveling on world map, randomly hides your mini-map, unable to interact with locations or events - was downed by poison after it was cleared - weapon dealers with no weapons, not even weapon mods- inconsistent team orders and movement, i specify a guy with gold digging perk to loot diggable and random not selected char start digging instead, few times team member just ignores move command and i have to move him through several shorter movements while all other team members did move without issue- random swaps of primary and secondary weapons, few times i swapped to secondary weapon and suddenly game also swap them on other team member too,  i don't mean it change to secondary weapon it swapped the position of primary with secondary weapon- bugged skills and skill benefits, animal whisperer lvl 10 pet max health randomly changes between 11k 8.5k 6.4k 5.6k 4.6k similar wild changes in pet damage too- loot bug, after combat unable to loot corpse, prompt to loot is visible but unable to loot it just stand at the corpse- your clone/pet health bar bugs out too, after combat you can't see it at all, you have to reload to see it properly again - bugged out mechanics, 100% fire resist but you still can get full damage from fire and burning- bugged out heavy turret captures, missing all the time, not a single hit from multiple shots in several turns- try to heal injured team mate it states "invalid target" but when you move first and then try to heal it works - try to disarm the trap, poor pathing make the character run trough the trap then try to disarm it- factions are poorly implemented without any specific long term goals or strategy. and these are the bugs and issues i have encountered multiple times during a single play trough.
