_childDocuments_.review: I find the notion of Americana, especially the period of rapid development of that vast geography after WWI, quite fascinating. The pain and suffering this exploitation brought, and how it led to unprecedented levels of economic superiority and its massive impact on art, architecture and generational psychology is undeniably a nerdish subject, but not a boring one. If one wants to understand the human condition better, what better time there is than one filled with struggle, conflict and progress. Nevertheless, the culture and psyche of people who built this colossal hegemonic power is quite an underdeveloped subject in gaming when compared to other artistic mediums. Wasteland 3 is an exception. It is a love letter to Americana, unlike so many proponents of it, Brian Fargo and his team knows that love of Americana can exist without romanticizing it. They know that their mistress’ eyes are nothing like the sun and yet, their love is rare. Wasteland 3 doesn’t engage in masturbatory nostalgia, alluding back to a cultural greatness that never existed, but faithfully portrays people hardened and brutalized by immeasurable hardships. Traditionalist falsification of the common American of this period, deeply religious, stilted, and enduring has no place here. Most people you will meet in this game are people no civilized person by today’s standards will want to associate with. But in this world the spectrum of morality is so far distorted by common acts of cruelty, out of necessity or reaction, even a tyrant will start to look reasonable. This is what Americana is, and crossing it with a post-apocalyptic setting makes it shine.While the subject matter is depressingly oppressive, the brilliant humour of inXile, dark and even bitter at times, is in a delicate balance with it. I assume the fans of  Baldur’s Gate 3 will be delighted to know that you can ♥♥♥♥ a goat or participate in a terribly written erotic show, and the fans of The Witcher 3 will laugh at pettiness and inefficiency of human cruelty. What really lightens this sombre setting though, is the fact that the whole purpose of our agency in the game is not a mere return to status-quo. Unlike the usual CRPG conceptualization, history in reality is not an inertial happenstance that jumps through certain periods like a warp drive. It is a wheel made to turn and in Wasteland 3 there are stronger forces for progress or regress than there are for returning to status quo. Allowing the player to have agency in creating change whichever path you take, introduces a semblance of hope to the cold, snow-laden Colorado.Agency, in typical CRPG fashion, comes in the form of pure, unadulterated violence. What distinguishes Wasteland 3 from others is the fluidity of violence that it almost feels like a tactics game when in combat. UI and UX is a level above from any other CRPG I’ve played and combat animations are visceral and responsive. Skills of various builds in your party of six are all designed with consideration how they can complement each other well. Rushing the cluster of enemies with your shotgun wielding Ranger, draining their HP pools, finishing the job with your sniper that gets extra action whenever they finish off an enemy never gets old. Once the dust settles and you’re dutifully looting the battlefield, an inventory tab opens that shows all lootable objects in one tab, and individual boxes and corpses in other tabs. This simple addition immensely reduces the time you spend with busy work, and lets you focus on more important matters, like dancing on the grave of your annihilated enemies. What’s disappointing is, agency in Wasteland 3 rarely comes in the form of environmental puzzles or dialogue. As an example, there is a newspaper in the town that publishes slanderous headlines about our actions throughout the game. I wanted to visit their offices and have a chat with their chief editor to convince or coerce him to support the Ranger takeover I was planning to accomplish as all coups need to manufacture consent to be successful. This is simply not an option because almost all the quests are designed around combat, even though some outcomes can be influenced by non-combat skill checks.Of course, it would be unfair to expect a crowdfunded game to be the ultimate CRPG experience. But while playing Wasteland 3, all I could think was I wanted more of this heartless and treacherous world. I wanted more pre-defined companions, I wanted more side quests, I wanted more easter eggs, I wanted a larger city, I wanted more NPCs, I wanted more choices. I created my character with the background “disciple of the metal” expecting it to have at least some bearing to gameplay other than its 15% fire damage bonus. As in, short guitar solo every time I land a crit hit or meeting other disciples of my tribe. Most importantly I wanted more of that hauntingly beautiful soundtrack that reimagines classic, biblical and patriotic hymns of Americana in the context of this post-apocalyptic universe. As of writing this review I’m still listening to the soundtrack album and I desperately crave more of it. Despite my desire for more, Wasteland 3 is obviously a finished article. This is of course a personal preference but I’d rather play a game that leaves me wanting more, than one that overstays its welcome.I usually write in-depth reviews within a week of completing a game, while its memory is still fresh in my mind. If it passes that threshold, there is almost no chance I’ll write a review. Wasteland 3 is an exception. It has been more than a month and I keep thinking to myself, what a great game and homage to Americana it was. As far as I can see, it flew under the radar mostly due to bugs at launch, but my experience was almost flawless other than FPS drops here and there, which were solved by loading a save. If you want a unique CRPG with a soul, it doesn’t get any better than this.Love letter/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some minor bugs that aren't bad enough to prevent playing. Aesthetically it looks good. Having finished it the main con for me was the generation of reputation (and managing it) that has a effect on the end game as well as the game itself seeming like it should have been longer. It may be cynical to say but it feels like that got to a point where "this pandemic has forced us to put this game out right now or the money people will be mad". Supposedly it has 35 levels for characters and none of mine made it to level 30. My final battle of the game (on normal) lasted a grand total of 3 rounds with none of my characters taking over half damage and only 2 of them taking any damage at all.I like the game, could be more. I love the IP and hope to see a bigger, longer game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game that I'd highly recommend to fans of CRPGs.  This was my first time playing a game from this franchise, and Wasteland 3 has a load zaniness and charm that I did not expect.  It really feels like there's a lot of heart put into this game, and there are so many silly details sprinkled all over the place that make the game's world feel alive.The amount of hand-crafted combat scenarios, with creative gimmicks and level designs, greatly surprised and impressed me; as well as the degree to which investing in dialogue skills let you affect the outcome of certain scenarios.  There are some repetitive combat encounters which can be initially annoying, but can be skipped once you are at a high-enough level in certain skills.  I was also surprised at the bespoke animations that the devs made when speaking with important NPCs in certain scenes.  That was a level of presentation I was not expecting, and really made those scenes feel much more immersive.  If you have a friend who's interested, playing the game in co-op is a lot of fun, too!Wasteland 3 may not be the best in terms of graphics, or gameplay; but it does well enough in those categories; and with its larger-than-life characters and worldbuilding, and tons of enjoyable voiceacting, the whole is definitely greater than the sum of its parts.

_childDocuments_.review: From my perspective, they took away all the elements of Wasteland 2 that I disliked, kept all the elements I did like, and increased the production value by a large amount. The combat is great, the story is great, the music (sparse though it is) is great (when it's present). They simplified some of the systems, but in a good way - for example, instead of having a separate medicine and surgery skill, they are combined as First aid. They took out the ridiculously annoying "separate inventories for separate character" nonsense, which is fantastic.It IS a bit buggy. Some quests are VERY buggy. And you can tell they ran out of time on the bug testing, because the beginning areas and quests are largely bug free, but as you get further and further on, more and more bugs start popping up. There's one side-quest I had to completely abandon since, on completing it, the game just.... froze up. No matter what I did, when I got to the end, it just didn't progress (The Quest is called Elf on the Shelf). A couple of time the enemy AI just froze up and refused to move. But it's a hell of a lot less buggy than Wasteland 2 (Or the Bethesda fallout games for that matter!). If you like games like Divinity or Balder's Gate, or Fallout - you'll like this, almost guaranteed. It IS buggy though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. It looks like X-Com in terms of combat and plays like a core RPG (think: Pillars of Eternity/Tyrant or Divinity: Original Sin II which it actually stole some ideas from) and does both excellently.Firstly, the combat: In truth, I never like X-Com 2's style of combat, from it's dice rolling hit/miss system to its line of sight system which often seemed to work in unexpected ways. Wasteland 3 does it right. Single-fire pistols require a small amount of AP allowing gun slingers to move and fire multiple shots on the same turn. Automatic weapons fire multiple times so even a 30% hit chance with 10 bullets is still decent odds. The combat in general feels rewarding and smart with many strategic variations and serious consequences for bad decisions. It can feel unfair and punishing at times, and yet doable.Characters are not locked into a specific class, you allocate skill points into different weapon types or combat skills. Any character can wield any weapon, but will face a penalty if they don't have, for example, enough "Big Gun" skill points. This makes the strategies one can derive from a pool of characters very wide as they can progress in very different ways than what the designers intended. Combat skills can tie into social and exploration, too. For example, "Toaster repair" (a surprisingly useful skill) can grant a perk boosting fire damage which a "Big Guns" character will benefit from since they can use flame throwers.That was combat, now for story and writing: The main NPC protagonist or villain (depending on how you play) is a man calling himself "the Patriarch" who wields a giant hammer with an American flag wrapped around the shaft and an iron fist for the head. He literally rules with an iron fist! I knew pretty early on I'd like the writing and the voice overs a great, too. There is a lot of room for moral ambiguity where the player has to either decide what they think is the most politically convenient solution to a problem, or morally correct. In many ways, I feel that the tensions between politics and ethics are at the heart of Wasteland 3's themes and how you resolve this tension will guide you through the experience. There are numerous people and factions with interlocked relations to each other and nuanced decisions to make. Many of the people you meet will have ideas worth thinking about, life philosophies, religious doctrine, and a lot of referential humor.This game has my highest recommendation, but I want to list a few of my complaints at the end. Loading screens are too long and too frequent. There appears to be a memory leak and after long sessions of play, the game can go from max graphical settings at 144pfs to just a handful in short order. There are some bugs and they're generally not game breaking, but... well, you should be quicksaving often, anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is essentially 'original generation' Fallout tweaked for the 21st century: an isometric turn-based party-based RPG set in a post-apocalyptic hellscape. That said, be wary of the fact that this game currently has a fair number of bugs and performance issues on all platforms. _childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is a good game but nowhere near the awesomeness of Wasteland 2. The story, the role-playing, the characters, the combat system, everything is decent but dumbed down. The result feels like they replaced some of Wasteland's depth, nuance, and humor with more gore. Lots and lots of gore.The Good:- The story is still entertaining and the setting is different.- All key storylines offer you multiple outcomes that effect the end game drastically and give you very different campaign outcomes.- After the patches the combat system has decent balance for different types of characters and weapons. You can make very different skill combos viable.- Non-combat skills matter a great deal, too. There's a lot of dialogue, hacking, lock-picking, etc. in both quests and combat.- The world is darker and bloodier than in splatters. Good if you're into that sort of a thing, bad if you're not. Wasteland 2 was sunshine and rainbows compared to Wasteland 3.The Bad:- The combat system is a lot more simplified than in Wasteland 2. It makes combat less interesting and varied. They reduced what was one of the best turn-based combat systems since Fallout to something resembling 'X-COM Lite'.- There's a lot more more focus on "good" and "bad" outcomes instead of different outcomes. This makes the choices given to the player less interesting.- The devs decided that some seemingly sensible decisions have horrible outcomes even when the Rangers could easily intervene to prevent those outcomes. This makes the consequences of your choices seem arbitrary and inconsistent, making the choices and the story itself less interesting.- The effects of many of your choices ultimately boil down to a few lines of text at the end. It would have been nicer if more of the effects had been shown during the gameplay.The Ugly:- The game is still incredibly buggy even after all the updates. Some quests don't work, some combat mechanics are broken, and the game has serious performance issues.- FPS drops to near zero are constant even on a 2080 Ti (fixed by changing graphics settings to low and back to high, so it's definitely a bug).

_childDocuments_.review: So, it's been a while since Wasteland 2, the hype is real but...is it though?Wasteland 3 is a great Turn Base RPG. The story is compelling enough to keep you going, some characters are really interesting and the gameply is great.  Let's make this a quick pros and cons lists:PROS:- Great gameplay- Good Story- Most dialogues are funny to hear- Some really great characters with personality- Good Cutscenes(too few on my opinion)- Good variety of weapons, armors, modsCONS:- No gritty and rough environment like previous game. Even if this is a snowy land it seems like a great fairytale- Combat is not that punishing as previous games. It's hard at the beginning but the difficulty curve softens as you progress a little into the game. - Some minor bugs like doors never opening and you go through them. - Major FPS drops on some terrains/effects- Character creator could be much better- The main character face texture could be better, even if it is a custom face.

_childDocuments_.review: When all the good parts of a game are weighed down by the shortcomings.Been going in circles wether or not to recommend this game. My love for the genre and wish to support further projects tell me to recommend it. But my disappointment has eventually won out, and my thumb has to point down.After all the wait, having skipped all tests of the game and production updates to be completely in the dark about the story. I still wanted the max experience so I tweaked everything to the max difficulty wise from the get go. And after a couple of wipes I understood most mechanics. And then it all went south, once you understand the mechanics and start using your people. You don't even have to be imaginative to outplay the AI even at the maximum difficulty settings. The enemy will not move even if your giant vehicle is moving towards them at ramming speed, they will sit there and be run over in packs. Their vehicle in turn will do no such thing. There is no flanking, surrounding, serious outnumbering. Mechanics do not include the ability to go prone to present a smaller target. There is no fear of loosing any of your men because they can't be killed even on max difficulty.So the fear of traps, mines etc is just a matter of convenience. Run a man trough it all to set it off, follow and heal him. Rinse and repeatIt entirely feels as every setting and choice is a matter of how "convenient" will you want to play trough this game.Even dialogue has been dumbed down to show you which options you are not eligible to use because you haven't the skill for it. So you can just refrain from using skill points till you need them. And if that is not enough. Drive back home to camp, replace a team member, level up the new one to have the skill for the challenge. Be it dialogue, mines, traps. Same same.I must have restarted 3-4 times learning the game. And about 5 times did I start over between levels 12-22. Because it felt like my team was too high level for the challenges they faced. In my final and only completion of the game I tried skipping any random encounter to avoid xp. I skipped out on several non story missions. And I was only allowed to load / save the game when I was going to and from the computer. Any wipe was to be punished by starting the game over.I encountered 2 fights that were not needed for game completion, but were actually immensely punishing and forced an initial retreat. And the final end combat was a complete and utter letdown. You can litterally finish it mostly being out of the enemy lines of fire.And trough all of my time playing this game, the camera controls, load times, ui, keybinds were just a pain in the.... And rebinding keys was only partly an option due to conflicts with some hard binds/numeric keyboard. It honestly felt as if the game had gotten stuck somewhere in between pc, consoles and possibly low end performance machinery.Story, it felt like all choices boiled down to the same, story line with little to no gameplay differences. But the game does have a story and I am sure others might be liking it.After this disaster I spent the past 2 weeks playing fallout, fallout 2 and fallout tactics. All of these significantly more challenging, punishing and annoying AI wise. The ancient ai from these games won't just let you sit in cover and wear them down. They will fall back, run away, pull you out from cover or into more enemies. If I didn't already know these story lines I would say these games outperform Wasteland 3 by a fair margin. Of course not on the graphics part.I am so sorry, I wish I could have written a positive review to support a wasteland 4 and the genre

_childDocuments_.review: Middling recommendation. Not a recommendation for CRPGs, only if you really like Fallout 1/2, or this type of combat system.Maybe good for coop and more goofy tone that entails.Story/World:Main storyline/quests are really solid, but side quests are very mixed bag.Game tries really hard to make you feel bad for not being 100% 'pro-democracy peace and love' in the literal post-apocalypse with murder-clowns and cannibals all over the place.Game also thinks it is some sort of revelation to tell you that the warlord known as the Patriarch that sits on an 'Iron Throne' of missiles is maybe not the nicest guy ever.Game world is too 'gamey' and instance-based. Lot of sidequests and encounters almost feel like a tableaux with how brief they are.Too many pop culture references imo, if you like FO2 for that you'll enjoy it here.Weird amount of product placement. Food items include Snickers, Chips Ahoy, Big League Chew, etc. Kind of works as this setting is a lot closer to real life, but still weird to see and other things are clearly parodies (Eterni-tarts for Twinkies).Game systems:Economy is surprisingly well balanced. Never felt like I had infinite money or crafting materials, even by the very end.Normal/Wastelander difficulty is too easy if you have any experience in tactical RPGs(Divinity, XCom, etc.) despite what the tooltip says. I was 1-turning most encounters by mid-game.I like the way the weapon progression system is set up, however item drops are too infrequent for it to work really well. Often times I'd skip 3 or 4 tiers of a certain weapon before I got an upgrade for it because of how rare and RNG item drops are.I dislike how armour progression is setup as some of the best passives on armour pieces are on very early game items, with no late game equivalents. (Merc headgear for 2% crit, Trooper/Scout headgear for hitchance.) This made it feel pointless for most of the game, and I finished the game with my sniper still using the very first helmet they picked up for the crit chance. This might not have felt as bad had I been playing on a harder difficulty necessitating more armour, but the loss of bonuses with no equal would still feel bad.The CLASSIC attribute system isn't very good imo. Every character build pretty much normalizes into roughly the same. (Every character wants max Coordination for AP, every character probably wants INT for crit and skillpoints, SPD is pretty worthless on everything but melee.)Getting attribute points per level is an interesting idea, but takes away from the uniqueness of different builds.The perks are way too all over the place. Some are really good and useful while many are borderline useless.The pet/follower system is terrible. Either give control of pets to the player or have them be completely passive. Having your pets suicide charge into the enemy every encounter is mind-numbingly annoying. If I had been playing on a harder diffculty this probably would have made me quit or respec without pets entirely. This also ruins most chances to set up ambushes as enemies will just attack your suicidal pet rather than pushing to attack your team.The mod system is terrible and discourages you from experimenting with your loadouts entirely. Mods being 1-time use is a terrible mechanic in a game this unforgiving with item drops and crafting supplies.I played with and highly recommend everyone to use the 'Better Equipment Mods' mod. It allows you to take mods off and reuse them, thus letting you actually experiment with your guns. Even with this mod I only felt like I had everything I could possibly want by the late game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it really doesn't feel like an upgrade from Wasteland 2. The game is fine, but really doesn't meet today's standards for RPG's like it. I'm just saying that there is so little customization that it may as well just not have any at all and give you pre-made characters with unique dialogue and personalities. _childDocuments_.review: Things looked promising with Wasteland 3, they really did. It had a decent background, Fallout 3 meets Fallout 4, with a touch of X-COM thrown in (hell, you can spot these devs like X-COM cause they even colour the half-turn spaces blue and the full-turn spaces orange just like X-COM does). The writing isn't half bad from what I saw of it, and the animation isn't too shabby either, no.But it's lacking a lot of the heart, and the soul, that X-COM had as a tactical shooter. The enemies are senseless, from what I can tell. The health-bars are gradients, which makes killing enemies harder to plan. What X-COM did was like 4-dimensional chess, and what Wasteland 3 has done has tried to improve upon something that isn't really broken to begin with.I always say that you can tell a good game from a great game by putting it on its hardest difficulty, and seeing where it takes you. Is the game so hard you can't beat it because you can't beat yourself? Or is it so hard because the computer has been given too many advantages? In Wasteland 3, it feels like you don't put out enough damage to really make a difference - and this is perfectly encapsulated by your squad. You pick a couple of randoms to come join your random misfit of a crew, and they just add more meat to the equation. And they go down so quickly, in fact, everybody does, that by comparison, it's a game of meat, not strategy. How much meat, where meat is placed, is meat thick enough to punish other meat. Meat. Meat.I get the feeling that this is going to be another one of those mile wide, inch deep games. A bit like Battletech. In X-COM, you had this sense of desperation. Every move, every choice, mattered. In Battletech, you had this gloriously inspired story, stakes, even if it was a rip off of Frank Herber's DUNE. Instead, Wasteland 3 punishes you either way. Save the convoy of traders, at the expense of letting everyone get murdered over at the Dursleys or whatever's house. Or save the Rangers at the Dursleys, and the convoy dies; hey, in real life, you can't have your cake and eat it, too,  I get that...And then, as I'm playing, I hear a knock at the door and it's this guy in a mask I've never seen before. Looks fraught. Tells me his wife has just hit a cat, and it's dead. I ask him what colour it is, and I already know the answer, somehow. And I go out and see my beloved cat, Tigger. And he's gone, I'm grateful that the people who hit him by accident, they came outside and apologised. And for Tig Tig, it was quick, he was long gone before I ever got there, and I hope he wasn't scared but I know he would've been. And I buried him deep. Afterwards, I come back in a daze, I need to just. Not be me for 24 hours; game will help. And Wasteland 3 is still kind of running in the background, so I play to distract myself. I'm in the Kodiak, this snow-plough tank that's got a turning circle like Jupiter's orbit, and somehow, in the middle of this snowstorm hellscape post-apocalyptic nightmare, there are bucks and does littered across the landscape. Just trying to meek out an existence, you know? Imagine these lives, cats, dogs, foxes, you can befriend in game, but the deer - no. They sort of linger in the middle of the road and the snowplough doesn't really have a horn, and the bucks aren't scared at all. So I try to skirt around the first buck to get to the next objective, and that goes down pretty well. Then I come up to another buck, and I'm trying to find a horn button to no avail. Move outta the way. I don't want to hit you. And I think I do my best at avoiding the buck, but I don't, and it explodes spectacularly, and with all the bravado I think the devs must've been going for, you know? Gory, bloody, gooey mess. Splattered in every direction. Downright visceral. Meant to be kind of tragic funny. And I can't help but think of my cat just now, he didn't look like that - he was solid, he was heavy, his fur was coming a little bit undone because he'd just died and that's what bodies do. He looked like he was asleep but not asleep. And not that I wanted this buck to look that way, but that I couldn't avoid hitting the buck, and when I tried, it exploded, even though I was going less that 5 kilometres an hour. It sort of hit me: Why have the devs put this in here? What purpose does it serve? In a Wasteland, we're fighting to survive to protect... what? Ourselves? From the next raid, the next rationing? In a game where I can befriend that doggo I just ran up to, why does the buck instantly explode? Why is the buck on the road nibbling at snow in a snowstorm? Who coded that algorithm, that if/therefore function: if truck = hit, hit = true, true = explode?So, this game gave me one of those existential crises you get from time to time where you just stop to think and realise and wake up from the kind of game that you're playing that's always set in America, America, America for some reason, that it's not really a good enough game to keep going on playing. The buck was the last straw, because I just don't feel like I can embody the sensibilities of the characters I want to roleplay in this game, none of these characters I've tried to build myself. I don't feel like the squad has a good sense of camaraderie. And I don't think the devs understand the natural environment after a nuclear catastrophe, and just how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ we are afterwards. Life is already pretty precious, but in a wasteland? Every. Life. Matters.So... This one goes out to you, Tig Tig, you beautiful bastard, you. I'd trade this game for tummy rubs any day of the week. I'll miss you, buddy. Rest easy, now.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is one of the best RPGs in recent memory. The level of player choice and world reactivity is phenomenal, the story and characters are layered and nuanced, and it has one of the most unique depictions of a post-apocalyptic America in any video game. And the music is absolutely BANGIN! By the end, I was left with a question that plagued me for days: did I make the right decision?
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Charmingly irreverent & fun to play! Reminds me of other tactical games like X-COM or Fallout, but with deeper roleplaying mechanics and a story with more meaningful choices & consequences. Several of the pre-generated characters have interesting builds; but if you want to really get the most from Wasteland 3, then take advantage of the deep customization options & role-play the hell out of it! I've spent a significant amount of time just playing with the character creation system, and I'm often surprised at how many different archetypes & pop culture icons that I can re-create in this game. If you're feeling particularly hardcore, try out the Friendly Fire & Permadeath optional modes!
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Good game that could be much, much better.What's good?Combat's good. Combat's juicy. Lot's of guns and armors, you get vehicle that can run over your enemies, bunch of nice skills, few different gangs that require bit different approach, new status effects (burn them! Freeze them! Poison ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!), animal companions that are more than just cannon fodder, load of ♥♥♥♥ to craft (although game could give you more info about stuff you're doing) and fights that require bit more than just pulling the trigger. What's bad?Well, not exactly bad, but the story is meh. Like, the idea is great: swap sands of Arizona for snowy Colorado, let Rangers fight for their survival - should they accept the help of Patriarch even though there's more to him than meets the eye (if three bonkers children are any indication)? Who to ally with, who to save, who to damn to slow and painful death? Sounds great... if only script could actually deliver. Problem is, the game can't really decide, if wants to be serious and somber or wacky. Gangs massacring the refugees, slaves turned into meat puppets, thousands sent to be turned into human sacrifices, tought political reality of postapocalyptic world, blurred line between saviours and tyrants... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, LOOK AT THAT CHICKEN TRANSFORMERS! AND ROBOT OF R.REAGAN THAT SHOOT LASERS AND IS WORSHIPPED BY CRAZY LADIES DRESSED AS HIS WIFE! AND COMMUNIST ROBOTS - DID I MENTIONED COMMUNIST ROBBOTS?What's worse, game makes such a big deal of Buchanan's children (especially Liberty, who is portrayed at least like she's Genghis Khan incarnate) but when you decide that words might be stronger than bullets everything is resolved by - like - one dialogue line, lleaving you completely flabbergasted. I know that shooting everything was default option, but come one - let me actually feel like it was a great feat!Nonetheless enjoyed the game, although if I was to chose the game to replay, probably would go with W2.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Wasteland 2, you're likely going to love this too. It's basically the same thing but with extra bells and whistles.Having finished my first playthrough at 44 hours, I can safely say that I liked and highly recommend this game, though I probably have to suggest waiting a bit before getting it. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who bounced off Wasteland 2, I found Wasteland 3 to be one of the best - if not the best - post-apocalyptic RPGs since Fallout: New Vegas. The tone, humor, and worldbuilding of Wasteland 3 is closer to the classic Fallout games and stands starkly against the recent Bethesda offerings. I won't say that it redeems the genre, but it absolutely demonstrates how to do it in a way that's more interesting than Fallout's recent offerings.Overall, the game is made up of a lot of things that work well enough. The story is fine and opens strongly. The characters are fine, although this is not a game where you should expect much depth or much in the way of cool character moments. There's a neat amount of reactivity in the game world, enough that I'd be interested in seeing how things go if I were to make different choices in another playthrough. Two elements stand out as being the more remarkable part of the games. The first of these is, of course, the absolutely incredible soundtrack. It's up there with Disco Elysium as being perfectly suited to the atmosphere and themes of the game. The other element I liked were the moments-of-interest that were conveyed through a first-person camera, which I don't recall seeing in a game like this before. I wish there were more of them. All in all, Wasteland 3 is a solid post-apocalyptic RPG.However, there were two things that I found as particularly weak.The first of these was the combat. By the time I was rounding up the second Buchanan child, it'd become a bit of a slog. It starts off as a good X-Com-esque formula but, like most turn-based games, eventually reaches a point where you just kind of want to get it over and done with. Either because the combat has stopped posing a threat to your well-equipped team, or just because you've 'solved' the combat system.The second of these was the main plotline. Specifically, the form it takes after Denver. It all feels a bit rushed and incomplete. This is felt especially keenly on the main conflict between your mission to assist the Patriarch and a well-meaning band of guerrilla revolutionaries. While I can see what the writers were going for, and I think it's quite interesting how they handled the Patriarch's character and wider regime, it ultimately was not an interesting series of choices. You don't get enough of an opportunity to engage with the revolutionary leader, her motivations, beliefs, plans, and hypocrisy.  Because of this, it means that the revolutionaries don't just come off as idealistic and well-meaning but flat out stupid. If I'm able to poke holes in their 'strategy' the moment I meet then, then I think my character should be allowed to do the same. It's a cool idea for a plot and I like the concepts and ideas they were dealing with, it just wasn't very interesting to engage with.Despite that, I enjoyed my time with Wasteland 3 and do not regret the purchase at full price. Honestly, it's worth a play just for the soundtrack alone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has spectacular story telling! I was fully immersed the entire time and really felt the impact of each decision I made! I loved the numerous opportunities to think through each decision as though it were real life, because things would actually play out as I would expect them to in a real life situation! The Character creation was fun and getting to see my custom team work through each situation was consistently engaging. This game has plenty of serious moments and situations but it has plenty of clever comic relief to keep me laughing and wanting more! This game lived up to the hype built by Wasteland 2 Director's Cut and if they decide to make a wasteland 4 I'm already determined to buy it as well! Great job!

_childDocuments_.review: Looks good but doesn't zoom far enough out. Great music and full voice acting but some valley girlish sounding deliveries were cringey. Dialogue choices and writing were generally good but the characters and stories were not enthralling, feminism was jarringly pervasive throughout, and the pace was sporadic. Character development seemed unique at first but by midgame choices amounted to either right or wrong. Crafting seemed like it was interesting at first but ultimately proved impactless. Itemization was awkward, there was tons of cool stuff but most of it went unused. Combat missed the mark... it was too easy to kill, die, heal, and revive which left tactics and victories feeling cheap and hollow. For such a polished feeling game its a shame it just wasn't interesting, not terrible just not very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up Wasteland 3 as I'm a big fan of fallout and xcom and have really wanted something new from both franchises for a while. I'm just over 30 hours in and I've enjoyed every hour! A few notes though:- Game has bugs. It's not littered with them but there's a few lingering issues that can sometimes ruin the experience. The main bug for me being that sometimes during the enemy turn phase, the game just hangs. No enemies move, nothing happens and you'll be sat there for a good 5-10 minutes before the game realises it actually needs to end the turn. Really annoying, can sometimes be fixed by a quickload (although you can't save during combat, so hopefully the game saved before you entered combat!).- Once you modify things like armor or guns, you can't modify them again. Once a mod is put into an item, it can't be removed. This seems to have been done to allow for a perk to be introduced by levelling up weapon modding; but field stripping doesn't give you the mods back. I found this out the hard way because the game doesn't explain this.- Along with the previous point, there's no respec for perks and abilities. You have to seriously commit to a certain playstyle with your different characters. Once you get more skill points you are able to put them in new categories but this seriously inhibits your ability to rethink how you play and personally I feel it harms the enjoyability of an open world rpg.Other than that, the story is really good. The writing is on par with the seriousness of xcom and the lighter, comedic side of fallout. The gunplay is tactful and really fun to play around with. It feels like your actions have a serious weight in the world, with different npcs making comments about recent events and actions you've taken can show a real difference in how the world responds. A very good game, one that I think any xcom or fallout fan would really enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun at the start but major issues will start to crop up the further you get in. Played through with a friend on Supreme Jerk. Weapon balance is a joke. Half the weapon skill trees are completely underwhelming end game while others completely dominate. Explosives do not scale at all so your frag grenades will still be doing a paltry 60 damage when enemies have over 3000 health. Animal handling is extremely good but slows down combat a ton as the animal AI slowly walks up to the enemy and takes each swipe at the enemy slowly. Combat balance is also a joke. You will have on average 200 HP on PCs end game while enemies will usually have about 3000. Enemies will also easily one shot you every turn. Picking up 2 downed allies every turn wasn't that fun for me. Fights with many allied NPCs will take upwards of an hour because of how slow the combat can get in large battles. If you even sneeze on the NPCs they will easily turn on you which brings up my next point. Doing a single crime in a faction will permanently aggro them for the rest of the game. Those factions that say they love you? Don't even think of talking to them again, it's kill on sight after you steal or murder someone for the rest of your playthrough. Music and voice acting are a big plus but the really stellar tracks only show up in the beginning. After you get past mid-game you get repetitive long versions of America, America. The world map is mostly just a lot of empty space with a points of interest. It's pretty boring to traverse and the random combats are not implemented very well. Overall, I'd give give this game a 6/10. The weaknesses make for a very flawed experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: The Fallout sequel Fallout fans deserved. The writing is good, the choices feel meaningful, and the characters are wonderfully absurd. Combat remains tough-but-manageable through most of the game, and resource management strikes that balance between too scarce to be fun and too plentiful to be meaningful.  All in all, a very fun reminder that 2020 could have been a lot worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is great. Gameplay wise its a mix of the classic isometric RPG from the heydey of the genre and Xcom2  style turn-based combat. Combine that with a rich, choice driven story set in a fallout-esque universe (given that the original Wasteland inspired Fallout this is a given) you have a recipe for an amazing post-apocalyptic winter hellscape romp.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: 10+  hours of gameplay so far on PC.I'm enjoying it but don't feel for me that it is as good as gaming review sites have indicated. It's good but not great and I don't know if I'll end up finishing it. The writing is a little too cutesy/juvenile (in a way that tries too hard to be clever) and I'm surprised by how many sites are praising that given that it's woefully inferior to say Disco Elysium, the graphics are uneven (the landscape and vehicles look great when you're exploring in the kodiak but the characters look bland, and half the time you can't see their faces). The gameplay seems very much like WL2, which isn't a bad thing but so far it doesn't show much innovation - it's less fussy and that's nice. If I had to rate it with a number, it's a 7/10, maybe an 8/10 if the gameplay possibilities deep the longer you play. If it doesn't, then 80 hours is way too long. And there's nothing pioneering about the game at this point.It's basically WL2 with some streamlining/optimization, better voice acting, and somewhat improved graphics.Overall, can't recommend it at full price. Unless you loved WL2, wait for the price to drop. I do recommend buying it when it's $40 or less.It reminds me a bit of Obsidian's lackluster Outer Worlds, as far as a nostalgia approach to games sounding good in theory but the reality is a game that ends up feeling a little stale and basic compared to current games like it, but with a full AAA price tag that doesn't feel worth it. Both OW and WL3 should IMO have been priced below $40.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: So here is the problem with the game.There is nothing plot wise that will hook you onto the story. Unlike Wasteland 2, Wasteland 3 tells you who you are going to fight and everything about your enemies from the start. Are they interesting groups? Sure, nothing wrong with the enemies and NPCs they all add to the story. Though that's not the issue, the combat is great, the characters don't feel shallow, the new "talking heads" make the world more immersive.Yet once you beat the game you'll be wondering "is that it?" Because you are told everything from the start it leaves you with nothing in the main story that will surprise you. No tension, no flair, just hey go kill or don't there three rebellious kids once you level up some. And that's it for the main story.I have to say i'm very disappointed, show don't tell. The game devs told everything up front and it was a bad idea. Let the players explore and get to know the world through their interactions; not by the default of information dumps through dialogue.Maybe it's just me, but I like exploring worlds not just playing them.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: You see the three and a half hours of playtime? There were like five bugs, some of them reoccurring, that made the game unplayable. I couldn't rotate my camera, couldn't interact with npcs, coop partner couldn't interact with npcs, ridiculous clipping... oh, god. In only three and a half hours.I can't believe I paid 60$ for this game. Pulled the gun after a 1.10 patch was supposed to fix some of the bugs. That was a mistake.To all potential buyers and my friends interested in this game, WAIT. WAIT. WAIT. Wait until perhaps 2 more patches come out AND the All Reviews turn "Very Positive" because most of the negative reviews bringing it down are because of the bugs, and I guarantee you will come across some bugs. If I went through this game and encountered 5 bugs in 3.5 hours of playtime, that's a telling sign that this is an objectively bad, unpolished game riddled with bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best role playing games of the last few years. _childDocuments_.review: BLUF: A Game made for the Pandemic (e.g., "trapped" inside with hours to blow while looking out your window wondering... how the Fudge did we come to this?) If you enjoy Political intrigue, complex narrative, sociopathic antagonists, sophisticated "protagonists", radioactive clouds, monstrous creatures, basic and complex weaponry, technologies, intelligent war machines, et cetera  then you are going to love Wasteland 3.Gameplay: XCOM like tactical placement and shooting. Fully voiced NPCs. Close-up interactions. True decision making with benefits and consequences. Plenty of options for weaponry and modifications. Survival Tips: (a) Save your games often (F5 is your friend); (b) Never treat an engagement lightly which means scroll down to see all your verbal response options; (c) Write your Team's skill on a 'notepad' to ensure you do not overlap (i.e., a multitude of skills is needed to avoid frustration in this hellish Wasteland); (d) You are going to require medicine, ammunition, patience, and stamina in getting through this game (i.e., I have restarted several times because I am not imbued with patience); (e) Do not build an average characters - focus your dynamic duo's build into 2 categories: close combat and ranged combatant (initially) - see YouTube recommendation on character builds - ammunition is expensive and the mindless and astute NPC antagonist shall either charge for toe-to-toe combat or remain annoyingly out of range while picking off your characters; and (f) Arrange your Team to take advantage of cover all the time - If you want to survive and not restart the encounter - look for cover (either partial or full), check the angle by which the enemy can fire, move your Team into position by using your mouse pointer to determine the best location. When getting ready to take a shot, look to see if it can potentially be blocked, and then put steel or laser on target. Minor annoyances: Infrequently the camera jumps to an area where nothing is - if this happens double-click on a squad mate. The camera will position itself centered on your troop.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, it's a tactical role-playing game. When combat starts, it's turn-based, and the combat offers a lot of flexibility in how you can defeat enemies. Outside of combat, on the area maps, it's "real-time." The overview map has encounters that area based on movement.You have a 6-character party, each with stats, skills and perks you get to upgrade as you level-up. Note that you're limited to 4 player made characters and should take on at least 2 pre-made characters. You really do want the pre-made characters for the enjoyable interactions. I wouldn't call it an open-world. You have the overview map which you navigate with a vehicle and then you have the area maps. You have freedom to move around, sure, but there's a lot of map loading and this is the most tedious part of the game, moving around staring at load screens.Summary: It an awesome game, but not without flaws.- Pacing. You're rarely bored or left wondering what to do.- Story. The writing is entertaining and fresh and the world is rich. Also, great voice acting makes it shine.- Great tactics game! The interface makes the trade-offs of your combat decisions explicit.- Damn good music.- Excellent writing.- Choices matter.- Too many bugs.- Game mechanics still in flux as of 09/03/2021- Game should be labelled as "early access," but isn't; seems deceptive/disingenuous.It's a good game, but I'd wait a while until after it gets a game of the year edition. Maybe all the bugs will be fixed by then, the game mechanics wills settle and you'll get a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played plenty of Top Down Turn-based RPG's over the years, and although this game was actually a bit short compared to some, it was still fun to play. I had not played the original Wasteland in many years, and never did try out Wasteland 2, but there is definitely some polish to this game. Such as it is almost entirely voiced, from the narration to most NPC's. There was a ton of story related text to read in the form of letters, notes, books, and other tid bits that you find as loot, to add more depth to what is going on in both the main story as well as all the side story content (those parts are not voiced). I also loved character progression, even though it is a bit uneven. What I mean by that is that each character you control has it's own XP bars, so the levels of each member of your party (in single player) may level unevenly. That being said, the game does try to keep characters you've placed on the back burner (aka left at your HQ Base) somewhat caught up with your party's levels, so that they don't fall behind. This game is very Skill based, as in you will have a much more fulfilling and fun play-through if you try to keep regular (as in non-weapon related) skills covered across your team. Sure, there are multiple ways sometimes to accomplish goals and side-goals, but you will experience more content if you have all the skills covered and you invest in them. More so on your first few play-throughs, if you want to experience as much as possible. It's not a necessity, but more of a recommendation. Also, as a warning, this game is intended for adult players, as not only is there lots of profanity, but many many dark (or even very dark) themes, situations, and choices that are presented in this game, that some folks might find a bit disturbing. There is also quite a bit of dark humor, scattered through out the game. As to game play, it was fun and easy to get the hang of. There were a few times when some quests were time-gated, without actually telling you they were. They might have subtley hinted perhaps that time was of the essence, but at no point was it pointed out that failing to accomplish them in a timely manner would lead to story related consequences. That brings up another point, as there are consequences to some decisions, good or bad I prefer not to spoil it, but just be aware. As to my earlier comment about the length of the game being a bit short. The game play is quest/mission based as well as requires a bit of exploration of the main map to open up some content. So there are things to help keep you busy, but I still felt as though the amount of over all content was o.k., but not as lengthy as some other story rich RPG's I've played over the last few years. All in all, it's not a bad game, and I did enjoy my play through... I might play another run through it, making different decisions, but also be aware, that there are a tiny few moments where the game can prematurely punish you by ending the game early (based off a game play and/or story decision), so I highly recommend you save game often, just in case you don't like the outcome of a choice you are about to make (fyi - you can not save game while in the middle of story text/NPC conversations). Last thing I wanted to comment on, was the fact that some Companions and some gear doesn't come along till your almost at the end-game, which is a bit odd. Giving you new companions to optionally join your team so late in the game felt a bit wasteful. Same with getting high end gear almost near the end of the over all content, shortly before the game is over and the credits are rolling, also felt rather wasteful. As you either have very little time to play with them, or feel like it would be a waste of time to customize them only for the game to end not too long afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5 out of 10 - Good, but has flawsGood - Music is great, although the twangy version of Green Acres theme song is a odd to say the least.If you like X-com style games/RPG it's mostly there.  Good choice mechanics for the most part to branch the story a bit.Pretty customizable charcters, although the thumbnails only match if you make them look that way to begin with.  The stats are very fluid though allowing for a lot of builds.Good dialogue/ambient music fits.Enjoyable, with a fair enough replay value.Bad - pets are nigh worthless.  They definitly add combat value but have very animal brains, as in they will rush headlong in situations that are fairly terrible.  They also like to block you off sometimes.  IMO more hassle than value.  The cyborg chicken quest is a very poor reward in the end.  Funny yes, useful no.Loading screens - good lord, who wrote how to load transitions.  I feel like I'm back in the 90s with the load times.Shotguns/Snipers are far more valuable that other weapons with the exception of the mini gun.  Wierd science is hit and miss.  Assault/Melee are not nearly as powerful, although brawling late game can pack a punch (pun intended).Both LIberty and The Patriarch fights were phoned in.  After all that run up, it just lost all the momentum and ended with a whimper, not a bang.Pet management is atrocious, not just the control but who has what and losing the special pets (tom and so forth).Toaster repair is meh at best.Overall I'd still say it's a worthwhile game. _childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical going into Wasteland 3, because Wasteland 2 left a rather poor aftertaste. It was terribly drawn-out, the plot was barebones, and the balance was non-existent. Well, they did improve upon all that. Combat is still lacking – if you don't get the first turn, chances are, you're dead. If you do, however, it's over for your enemies. But I've completed the game on the Supreme Jerk difficulty, and I got tired of combats only on the very last location. One major improvement over W2 is that there's much fewer fights, but they are more meaningful. There are only a few instances where you mow down nameless mooks. Also, the combat itself is more enjoyable, with mechanics like flanking, cover destruction, special attacks and, of course, Strikes – ultimate attacks that cause serious damage, but must be "charged up" by landing normal hits. It opens up a bunch of possibilities when it comes to character building. And there's even more when you take into account weapon modding: for example, you can make fire minigun with +20 dmg per bullet, which will turn usually so-so heavy weapon specialist into a murder machine. So, as I said, it's fun.But the thing I enjoyed most was the story. Surprising, I know, but inXile really did it. Every choice you make leads to a number of consequences, both short- and long-term. For example, would you save a convoy with high-tech weapons from a raid or a homestead being slaughtered to draw your team out? Whatever decision you make, rest assured it will come back to you at the endgame. And if you tiptoe just right (hint: don't always do as you're told, no matter which side you're on) - you'll get a really satisfying conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite RPG across all genres that uses the isometric perspectiveGeneral advice:1. Play on a difficulty level higher than the preset...don't pick beginner or normal otherwise you won't be challenged and combat wont actually be tactical.2. When building out players Skills, dont spread yourself too thin, You've got 6 rangers and about 13 different skills so you only need 2 or maybe 3 per character...otherwise you wont be able to max out all 13 abilities because there aren't enough points to allocate.Pros:-Great story line where you truly feel like your decisions are changing the trajectory of the game.-Some of the less desirable/more tedious aspects of traditional RPGs have simplified to speed up game play (I.e. You don't need to have your best speechcraft person be the one who engages dialogue to use their bonuses + after combat, looting one dead body gives you access to all other dead body inventories in the area + looted containers can no longer be inspected after they are empty so you don't duplicate searches etc)-Lots of different combat tactics you can use depending on how you build out your character-Great Soundtrack! Some songs even play  over critical battle sequences and gives a very special feel.-Excellent Post Apoc ambiance, feel, and motifs.-Using the vehicle in combat and to navigate the map is fun-A thought provoking ending.-Navigating quests and maps is very intuitiveCons:-Bugs - one that prevented me from completing a nominal quest that wasn't critical to the storyline, loss of sound when navigating the world map, and an instances where backtracking and reloading was necessary.-Although you can customize outfits, the sprites are not that well differentiated from eachother-The Cluster Bomb mortar attachment for the vehicle is way OP and, towards the end of the game, boss battles involving the vehicle (on "Hard" difficulty) are way too easy if you use it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fantastic. The character creation, customisation, graphics, combat, general gameplay, story. It all feels really really solid. The performance is fantastic too. My rig is a tad outdated but I'm still getting 60fps easily.The only gripe I've got is it's clearly been streamlined for consoles and inXile shouldn't have done that. This game inspired the Fallout games and helped develop and entire sub-genre. Games like this always benefit from being complex.There is, however, a downside. The multiplayer aspect is borked. I've seen people jump in games and get kicked at every loading screen, quests not progression and today I even saw that it wasn't possible to jump into a co-op game with my best friend. The co-op could've been incredible but, for now, it's downright bad.EDIT 1/9/2020So after my first playthrough which took 40 hours I'm ready to give more thoughts.Pros;-- The story; whilst the whole "power struggle" story has been overdone, it's actually told really well here with the addition of choices that aren't as black and white as in other games.-- The combat; setting up your sniper to take out 5 enemies in 1 turns, having your gunner pelt an area with lead or simply opening up with a massive attack to take down a really meaty boy. The combat felt consistently good.-- The environments;  from old world bunkers to train stations, energy plants and cities. The areas themselves are fairly varied.-- Character creation and customisation; from character builds to cosmetics. It ticked a lot of boxes for me.-- Pacing; early on you'll only fight a handful of mobs at once but later on the game escalates to throwing literally 40 mutants at you at once. The game gives you time to learn about enemies, fight with them and gear up before throwing too much at you.-- The characters; From an old dude who loves nothing except booze, a flamboyant marshall and even a sheep you can put your naughty-parts into. There's a solid cast of characters. Some of which I got fairly attached to.Cons;-- The length; 40 hours isn't what I was expecting. It feels like there's a decent amount of side-content but the story itself is rather short. I would've loved a helluva lot more content with more deep questing.-- Post-game; there is nothing post-game. No new game plus which is saddening. My biggest problem here is that, by the end of the game, you'll have a squad that're literal death-dealers but there's nothing to really test yourself out against. No amazing bosses, end-game quests. This hurts in terms of playability.-- Streamlined; instead  of skills for specific weapons and skills, a lot of it has been condensed. It wholeheartedly reminds of me what happened to the Fallout games where they started as CRPG's but ended up becoming RPG-lites. I've no doubt this was because of the console release and I don't approve because it's taken so much of what the previous games instilled.-- Bugs; I've not personally come across too many although I have heard of a lot of people having problems with bugs. Firstly;  co-op for me just flat-out doesn't work. There's been times when I've gone to save and it's instead loaded me into an older save, times when the game itself crashes and a fair few visual bugs including missing textures.All in all I wanted this to be my GOTY. I genuinely believe the Devs have messed up. The lack of quality is fairly apparent, the streamlining has put a LOT of people off the game and, in terms of content, it feels a tad empty. _childDocuments_.review: In my mind, a successful CRPG is a game that engages the player in a decision making process that they have to justify to themselves. It is not so much the ability to pick good or evil that intrigues me, but the process of justifying what you consider to be "good" or "evil", and how each individual player may come to a different conclusion about the events of the plot. If your game is able to affect players to the point where they feel that it is necessary to justify the choices they made to people outside of the game, then you've created a truly engaging experience worthy of being held up as great CRPG.  fits into this category. Following the disastrous events of the previous games' ending, the Arizona Rangers are struggling to survive. A call comes in from The Patriarch, a powerful and influential dictator working out of Colorado, and he offers them a choice: bring back his three traitorous children, and in return he will send supplies to help the Rangers back on their feet. The plot is nominally about tracking down the Patriarch's children, but it soon branches out into a complex story about the nature of compromising one's own morals and the struggle for self-preservation. The Rangers pride themselves on fighting tyranny, but to survive they become state-sanctioned police for a foreign power. In doing so they run the risk of compromising their values to survive, and this issue is exacerbated when Patriarch is slowly revealed to be less of a benevolent force than he claims to be. Colorado is shaped by individuals abandoning their morality in pursuit of power, and the Patriarch is no different... but is he really worse than the sadistic gangs that stalk the wastes? Even then, many innocent people are waiting for those supplies back home in Arizona, and there's no guarantee that they'll survive without the Patriarchs help. This "power/ethics" dilemma creates an interesting backbone that informs every decision you make throughout Colorado and drives the story forward in interesting ways.Such heavy themes run the risk of burning out the player, but  manages to keep things relatively light throughout most of the journey thanks to the absolutely oddball nature of its world and cast. You can't go half an hour without running into some sideshow reject, or a gang of murderous cannibal clowns who speak Spanish, or an artificial intelligence based off of Ronald Reagan. That's not even getting into the weaponry- you have more mundane offerings like assault rifles, revolvers, submachine guns, rocket launchers and sharpened bits of rebar, contrasted against guns that shoot frozen ferrets, shrink rays, miniguns, electrified sledgehammers, The Gun From , and this isn't a tenth of the really wacky tools you can find in the wasteland. Your skills are also suitably unique, with traditional CRPG staples like Lockpicking, Melee Weapons and Automatic Weaponry mixed in with Animal Whispering, "Sneaky ♥♥♥♥", Toaster Repair, and "Hard Ass/Kiss Ass" (your Intimidation and Coercion analogues). All of these skills come into play in surprisingly effective ways too, ala - a high First Aid can help you identify that the Patriarch has the early stages of Cerebral Palsy via nerve damage when you first meet him, which can dramatically colour your interactions with him from then on. Colorado is a wonderfully weird place that never loses its edge and stands tall amongst some of the most well-realised worlds in modern gaming. Speaking of modern gaming,  launched as a bit of a disaster. The game was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, to put it bluntly, with broken quests, rampant bugs, missing animations and a general lack of polish on the technical side of things. The game is still rather buggy six months after release, even after numerous patches. Seeing my allies slide along the floor to the next point of cover I've directed them to is a common occurrence, though I thankfully never met any huge gamebreaking glitches. If this sort of stuff really bothers you, then i'd wait for at least another few months before giving this a shot.Outside of technical issues, the game does have some minor hiccups. The gameplay generally works fine, but isn't much to write home about. There's room for lots of potential and the game always makes combat information, like percent chances to hit and enemy health very clear, but there's little in the way of unique mechanics. The game also constantly rewards you for making smart decisions and creating a team of balanced Rangers, with frequent ways to undermine your enemies via skill checks in conversation. Entire encounters, right up the final boss, can be skipped or made easier by bringing certain skills, and the direction of quests can be radically altered by who's been killed and what skills you have on offer. These constant rewards and reactivity feel meaningful, and the game continually sets up interesting scenarios to talk and fight through.The games biggest issue is economic balance. Ammo and supplies are expensive, and your main source of income is killing enemies. Since world traversal is gated off by radiation that can only be bypassed through buying upgrades for your kitted out snowplow, I highly recommend that you buy nothing but healing items, deployables, and vehicle upgrades. The game has an adaptive loot system that will reward you with successively better weapons, more supplies and unique weapons the more you level up, meaning shops are for emergencies and getting a leg-up in the early game. Other inconveniences include the awkward control scheme, aggressive level scaling for quests, and a final act that shows the signs of development deadlines. The final mission is very reactive to your choices however, and the game has many different endings. Presentation is similarly a mixed bag.  is far from the ugliest games I've played, but it certainly does not look like it came out in 2020. Textures are mediocre, some of the more aggressive particle effects are an eyesore, and the modelling ranges from "acceptable" to "terrible". Thankfully, the environmental design is consistently impressive. Locales like The Warrens, a mall parking garage buried under years of snow, or Aspen's "Little Hell", a ski resort turned to a gory menagerie are among some of the most memorable. Alongside these interesting locales are the great cast of characters, each one brought to life with solid writing and great delivery. The score is also absolutely wonderful- while the ambient and battle tracks are alright, the game uses tons of remixed licensed music at key moments to excellent effect. You get insane-on-paper-amazing-in-practice covers like a country-folk version of the  theme song, or a sinister and malicious performance of . It should not work, but it absolutely does, and the perfect placement of these songs adds to the games already memorable world.I think the best praise I can give to  is that the broad critical summary I've given to it can be applied to some of the greatest CRPGs of all time, both in strengths and weaknesses. It creates a fascinating world with memorable characters, fills it with meaningful and creative quests, and then gives you complete control in completing your objective,. You can abandon the main quest to join the villains, become your own villain, side with or against the numerous fleshed out factions, and ultimately decide the fate of Colorado in major and minor ways. Even with the games raw technical side, I still think  is worth playing, especially in contrast to the first and second game to which this is an unbelievable improvement. If you thought CRPGs were dead, if you want a narrative you have real control over, or if you just want something that oozes passion and charm from every orifice, please play

_childDocuments_.review: Try and take Divinity 2 Original Sin. Now put it in a post apocalyptic setting. That's Wasteland 3 in a nutshell. Wasteland 3 is the 3rd in the Wasteland Strategy RPG series where to take control of a Team of Arizona Rangers, Named Team November, in a Post Apocalyptic Snowy Wasteland. The State known as Colorado. First lemme get the cons outta the way. The Multiplayer is Iffy. Occasionally you may drop connections and the sync may screw up once or twice. Input to attack on some enemies may be iffy sometimes and you may end up attacking something else or an empty space. And some animations may glitch out. Sometimes hilariously (Bro WHERE ARE YOU AIMING AND HOW DID YOU EVEN HIT THEM!?) or badly. (Freezing in place for a period of time before acting or even nothing happening at all and wasting turns.) And occasionally hitreg issues. (My Sniper Kept hitting a wall he was hiding behind no matter how good of a shot he had.)With all those out of the way, This game is awesome! The Story is beautifully made and it's got that Fallout brand of world where there are mostly serious yet cool stuff but also some pretty wacky stuff to help balance it out. The companions you recruit are all unique in their own way and are pretty well acted. The Music is pretty good. (Blood Of The Lamb, the first piece of music you hear during the first part of the game is my all time favorite) Gameplay is solid. It plays much like Divinity 2 where you have to think about where to go, what to do, what weapons to fire or what items or abilities to use, etc. Character creation is pretty extensive and no two playthroughs will be the exact same. It can go horribly wrong or amazingly right especially on higher difficulties. Yes there are multiple difficulties. Friendly Fire is Optional (THANK YOU!) as well as Perma-Death. So you can play as casual or as hardcore as you wish. The Graphics are stunning, from the ambient surroundings to occasional Cutscenes of characters up close and personal talking directly to the camera. Every inch of this game is lovingly crafted and the Character Models are beautiful. There isn't a single character in this game (NPC, Ally or Enemy) that doesn't have a voice and each character is voiced by a wonderful cast of actors. (Gabriela Carrillo, Erica Cain, Lucas Schuneman, Antonia Flynn, Jay Preston, Harrison Bacon, etc) The In your Face Cutscenes are especially good as they look like they used actual actors in mocap suits to capture their movements. It's that good. Overall, Yes. Buy this game. This is a must have for any Strategy RPG lovers like myself.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game, it has many good elements - but in the  summary, I have to lower the thumb.Too many weird design choices (you need a Nexus mod to allow uninstalling weapon and armor mods).Unclear game mechanics (debuffs on enemies have no description - you to get the same debuff yourself to be able to learn its effects, unclear stats progression, etc.)Weird and unclear morality and loyalty effects - some of which come into effect in the end game, only but never surface anytime before.Uneven availability of different types of weapons and armor.Some individual weapons are very overpowered while the rest is normal - and those are also unevenly distributed.No fast-travelCombat becomes very repetitive after you figure out the details of the game mechanics.The list goes on and on...Many of these annoyances would have less impact with a second play-through - but the game is BY FAR not interesting enough to warrant a second round.I did not finish the game after the end-game restrictions and effects became clear to me - I simply lost interest, even though I was nearly at the end of the story. _childDocuments_.review: I recently had the chance to play Wasteland 3 and I must say, it was a great experience. The game is a post-apocalyptic RPG set in a frozen wasteland and the player takes on the role of a team of Desert Rangers tasked with saving Colorado.The graphics of the game are fantastic and the attention to detail is remarkable. The environment is richly designed with different terrains and a variety of enemies, ranging from mutants to robots. The game also features real-time combat, which makes the battles intense and action-packed. The controls are smooth and easy to learn, allowing for seamless gameplay.One of the things I loved about the game is the depth of the character customization. The player can choose from a variety of skills, weapons and attributes to make their characters unique. The dialogues are also well written and the decisions made by the player have real consequences that affect the game's outcome.Another aspect of the game that I appreciated is the sense of humor. Despite being set in a dark and dystopian world, the game has its fair share of lighthearted moments that add a touch of levity to the otherwise heavy atmosphere.One thing I noticed, however, is that the game can be quite challenging, especially for new players. The difficulty level is set high, which requires careful planning and strategy to progress. It is not uncommon to fail a mission or die in combat, but that just adds to the overall excitement of the game.Overall, I highly recommend Wasteland 3 to any computer player looking for an immersive RPG experience. The game has great graphics, engaging gameplay and a compelling story that will keep you hooked for hours on end.

_childDocuments_.review: There's something wrong with this game. Actually, there are many things wrong with this game. And what really shines about the game - the stories, characters, item scarcity (post apocalyptic realism), and choices-with-actual-consequences - are completely bulldozed by some poor design and gameplay decisions. The Combat: is horrible. The worst part of the game. You will spend half of every encounter - at a minimum - sending your medic around to rez multiple characters, multiple times. The AI has absolutely no sense of self-preservation and will kill you at any cost. Defensive postures like crouching or taking full cover, are almost entirely useless; you should expect to get hit behind full cover always and often. Hoping to set up your team in formation to assault a position? Sorry! Most entrances to battlefields are bottlenecks. If there's a cutscene involved, you CANNOT sneak past a certain point without triggering a quicktime event. Maps and Travel: there is no fast travel in this game. Need to get from one side of the local map to the other? Well, you need to find where you're going - on maps almost entirely devoid of information about the area - close the map, and click to where you want to go, waiting for your team to make the journey. Are you inside an area that's inside of another area? You have to walk back out, to walk back out. All manually. You can't even click on an area of the popup map you want to travel to, you have to actually click on the mesh itself. When traveling the Colorado worldmap, you cannot fast travel anywhere either. No simulated encounters, so time speed mechanism. In what Universe are these [lack of] features well-received?Inventory and Status: some of my team were poisioned after combat. So, instead of assigning an item to my doc and having him go through one by one to remove the status, I clicked on each team member so they could take an antidote manually. Only, the inventory screen gives no indication about the negative status effects on your team members so I had no idea who I needed to heal! Buying and selling items is equally tedious. There's no shopping cart, so you're buying items by clicking on them and specifying the quantity you want one at a time. Frankly, it is nonsense that any game wouldn't have a viable, easy to use inventory system in the day and age of e-commerce. Crafting: some crafted items are components of other, more advanced crafted items. Well if I have a recipie, can I just craft the advanced component and have the crafting system just charge me the difference for the components I need, but just haven't crafted yet? NO! You need to have everything crafted individually. Honestly, what absolute trash is this?Bugs: with REGULARITY - and I mean multiple times in combat, every combat - I was unable to click on or use buttons for an active character. Couldn't use their special ability, couldn't use "Overwatch" or whatever WL3's equivalent is, couldn't move, couldn't use a special ability, couldn't reload etc. Mutliple times. Per combat. Sometimes the fix of cycling through character portraits would free up the character. Other times not. Horribly frustrating. The more I write, the more I am reminded of how many awful design decisions were made for this game, and about how the fun grew ever more sparse as my hour count increased. I stuck with it for the story and the characters, and left after I realized I wasn't enjoying myself. At all. 3/10 - Do Not Buy

Even if an enemy npc is 3-4 levels below yours, they can AP-run twice as much, they can shoot through walls, 9/10 shots crit and one tap you.You, the player, can't do any of the above. Every battle is a constant frustration, not a challenge. Afterwards, spend all your money and crafting materials to prepare for the next unfair fight, leaving you constantly broke. Items, crafting materials, weapons, ammo, armor all cost absurdly much and getting cash is extremely hard. Missions don't reward much so, yeah, constantly broke. I'm not an expert in such games but this game pissed me off so I had to uninstall.Nice music and level design. Nothing more.
