_childDocuments_.review: Short version:This is one of those games where you can tell the devs ACTUALLY cared about making this game. Any fan of Wasteland, Jagged Alliance, X-com, or any similar games, will very likely enjoy this.Long version:Okay, I'm not too far in to the game, but man am I having fun. The dialog/interactions are interesting and, quite often, hilarious. I have never laughed this much playing a game. The characters and dialog get a big thumbs up.The combat is instinctive and enjoyable. I, personally, started on normal and may up the difficulty for myself, as I find myself a little unchallenged having played a few games of the genre. That said, I feel like the game does a great job of scaling the difficulty. Someone who hasn't played this type of game before would likely be fine on normal and find it challenging but enjoyable.The overall story itself is making me actually pay attention and stay engaged. I remember characters, interactions, and conversations in a way that I normally wouldn't in this type of game. I can't wait to see where it's heading and I feel like I'm actually doing something in the world.Another selling point is the character creation. You start off with the choice of using several different pre-made duos, or you can create 2 characters of your own. You can also create more characters for your party later down the line, which allows you to really play how you want. And that's great given the many different options the game gives you as you progress.If you asked me to pick a negative point about this game... I honestly wouldn't know what to say. Which is probably a first ever for me, as I am usually pretty cynical.The game is currently on sale, and is a STEAL at 11.37 CAD. Regular price is also worth it in my opinion. I suggest you pick up this game, sit back, and get ready for a very enjoyable night/day of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: So time has passed, improvements have been made and it is about time I adjust my previous review, which was negative.If you never played Wasteland before: It basically is Fallout 1&2, but with a team. This includes the sometimes weird humor as well.Pro:- Intuitive skill system both allowing and requiring specialisation of your team members.- Interesting quests and storytelling, spiced with twisted Fallout-style humor.- You get to meet old acquintances.- Sex with robots (and potentially goats).Con:-  The game now includes a crafting system that allows you to craft ammo, grenades, weapons, stimpaks, and lets you upgrade mods you find along the way, depending on the various skills of your teammates. The higher the skill, the more sophisticated the stuff you can craft becomes. This was lacking in the release version and I am glad it is available now.-  This has been resolved long ago already, loading times are pretty ok now and we did not encounter another wipe of our progress.-  Did also not occur again or at least not to a notable extent.-  Yeah, no. See above ;)- Both enemies and you can shoot directly through walls, rendering the X-Com-like cover system sometimes useless.  Cancel that and go and get this game if you like tactical shooter RPGs with a pinch of twisted humor. As I said, go and grab this game. I still have to take a look at the DLCs that are out, but the base game is fun and entertaining. Since your decisions affect the outcome and the end credits of the game as well the replay value is also rather high. g2g and replay!
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended it shines through its role-playing elements and branching choices that'll influence the gameplay and story.i was skeptical at first as i was never a fan of post apocalyptic setting, but this game changed my view for its rpg factors alone even outshines other big, popular tabletop crpg games i know
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Games later in a series can go either better as the improve upon the success of the previous ones or they can become worse as the developers lost their inspiration and just go for the money. Happily, this is one of the few examples of the  former. I liked Wasteland 2 very much, but this just takes it to a higher plane. Everything is better: the story, the characters, the voice acting, the crazies, playability, the map, combat, UI, etc. The one thing I wish they kept was fast travel on the world map, but the distances are small enough that your heavy vehicle can get anywhere in a minute or two real time. There are several possible endings, depending on decisions made throughout the game. That gives it more replayability. 92/100

_childDocuments_.review: If CyberPunk 2077 never got delayed, then I wouldn't have made the mistake of buying this at full price so early.Not experiencing the bugs that some are having, but the few I do get are the kind where a dialog interaction or cut scene doesn't want to end and hand control of back to the player, requiring a hard crash of the client. My son who normally likes a heavy dose of that kind of humor, has already reached the point where even he finds some of the names and character lines to be annoying.On the plus side, I really do enjoy having the type of control it gives. _childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is a wonderfully written and impressively vast Fallout-like XCOM strategy shooter only held back by the bugs that go unfixed even today. With the game turning 3 years old, it's disappointing that regular bug encounters still plague the game - but the core game is so strong it's easy to turn a blind eye. List of bugs I've encountered in 2023 (Many bugs are unfixable and you must reload an old save and figure out how to work around them to progress):- Frozen Ferret Launcher never hits and causes combat to be stuck in infinite loop. This makes this weapon completely unusable- Any type of dart/launcher weapon/item takes 20-30 seconds for the game to decide how to resolve before resuming combat if not stalling indefinitely.- Killing ghouls out of combat never triggers combat state making you stuck in an open world instance. You must reload an old save to get out.- Doorways in combat frequently cause characters to get stuck or cannot shoot through them. Once had my team split after combat was over and had to reload to fix the bug.I've learned to live with the bugs and enjoy the game immensely. The humor ranges from comical to make your weird uncle blush. I would say I recommend this game to anyone that's a fan of turn based strategy and post-apocalypse settings but only if you have a strong tolerance for bugs and restarting a combat that you've practically already won or losing progress to recover a bugged state.Without bugs this game is an easy 9/10.Taking bugs into consideration 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit scared to purchase this based on some bad reviews, but when it went on sale I took the plunge and I'm glad I did.  I had very few problems with the game running smoothly on my PC.  I became addicted to the game from the first 10 minutes in and that's always my personal "test" as to whether a game is going to be worth playing or not.  The story was great for the most part.  I do have a few complaints... ended the game and there was still quite a few places on the map I hadn't been to, and once you end the game you cannot go back to those places with your squad without reloading a previous save (that I know of anyway).  Radiation so bad to get to those areas and I couldn't find an upgrade to the vehicle that would allow me to get to them.  And, I don't think the game is a candidate to "replay" any time soon because I really don't see how the choices I made would change very much of the story if I made different choices the second time around.  All in all, a great game that gave me around 50 hours of play and I felt like I got really great value from my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: After 116 hours of play and many updates later i feel this game is up to where it should be, there are still bugs but not game breaking. However the issue with this game is all the bugs left over and a lot of missing polish. There is no seperate save for the multiplayer VS single player so you will over write your singleplayer or multiplayer campaign if not payng attention. _childDocuments_.review: There are no words to describe my frustration and disappointment in inXile Entertainment. Having patiently waited for the game since its announcement, and with such a price tag, one might have high expectations. So, imagine my chagrin, when I faced a game-breaking bug some 45h+ in. Two major characters will leave your party for "killing civilians" after a regular fight....with enemies...who attacked *you*. Trying to report the bug was of no use, for the company has been aware of it for over a year. "Fixing it as soon as we can" my arse. Requesting a refund was not possible either, since the bug appeared 15 days after the purchase, which is like an item breaking a day after its warranty expires. Do. Not. Buy! Save your money. This is all very sad and frustrating, since the game would be excellent, if only it worked.

The genre might not be fantasy, but I wouldn't hesitate to award points for writing. In my 3 decades of gaming I don't remember being this frustrated with lack of "happy resolutions" for the stories you can find in this post apocalyptic world. Everybody's an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in their own way, either by happy sycophant tendencies, unadulterated rage, flawed ideals, boundless greed, you name it.With that said, I'm hoping to see more games like this to see improvements in writing. _childDocuments_.review: Game is amazing so far. I played through Wasteland 2 (Director's Cut) and enjoyed it. It has its issues, but was overall a fun experience. This game is so far superior to it in every way. I love that they re-did the skills system to make it less cluttered and more intuitive. I see that some complain that it has been "watered down", but I disagree as there are still plenty of options to customize your characters as you see fit. Between skills, attributes, perks, armor/weapon mods, utilities, etc., there are so many options to specialize each member of your party. The combat is vastly improved and flows way better than the previous entry which really felt cumbersome and boring at times.I am not far into the game yet as I am still pretty much in the opening act and setting up my base and collecting various roles, but I am loving what I'm seeing so far. The graphics, voice acting, presentation are all great. I am having a blast during combat and the story is intriguing.Now, if you were NOT a fan of Wasteland 2 or this genre in general, then this game will not do much to convert you. However, if you're looking for a fun, deep, and tactical RPG story driven experience, then you will love this game. Support this developer who is one of the few that still makes ambitious games like this in the genre and give this game a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 6.5-7/10As far as CRPGs, Wasteland 3 can be seen as a competent spiritual successor to classic Fallout games, however don't come into Wasteland 3 and expecting it to be something like Divinity OS or Fallout NV. It's a much shorter game, and not as in-depth as a full length CRPG, but for what it is worth, it was enjoyable. Story: 7/10The game started on a strong premise, with a very interesting intro and really helped fan eased into the story of the game and of the universe. The opening cinematic is gorgeous, and the first few character introduction animation absolutely blown my mind away. Unfortunately, the plot runs out of steam halfway through the game. The biggest problems with the writing is that all characters are too... agreeable. Everyone is right in their own way, and the final choice in the game doesn't feel significant at all. It's mainly because the two main characters that you will have to side with at the end of the game - and by that I mean the very end, you can just not choose as far as the final quest - is really not that compelling or charismatic. You have the Patriarch who ruled with an Iron fist, and his counterpart whom I won't name who wanted to overthrow him. The problem is the usurper didn't really present a compelling argument against him other than "the current one is kinda bad", and didn't offer a good solution. Furthermore, factions do not really interact with each other. There is no ideology clash, there is no class conflicts, there is no real gang wars. Even something such as human vs AI is teased for a bit then left at that. Everyone is kinda just mind their own business and live in secular harmony. The reputation system is kinda worthless. There isn't a real penalty for going against a faction other than mild inconvenience. Side quests are OK on its own. Nothing outstanding or revolutionary, but they are really few and far in between and not very memorable. I would guess the entire game has around 25-30 quests in total. One good point are the party members, they make occasional comments and remarks when it's appropriate, which adds a bit to their characters. Gameplay: 7/10As far as CRPG go, the gameplay is simple. It's fun enough, but like the story you will get a strong feel that it should have been expanded on more. Combat is straight forward, and fights are serviceable, with not too many RNG. There aren't many memorable fights however. The high damage that you take makes you want to start most fights by hitting first then wipe out most of the goons before they even get a turn, making it feels a bit samey. There are very few active perks or weapon skills, so don't expect a lot of creativity. In terms of skill check, since you get 6 members there isn't really a problem most of the time. Leveling the last few points is a pain so hold on to those skill books. Exploration is a bit bland. The world map bad with low visibility, plus 90% of places you visit feel like mini-dungeons instead of a settlement. There are exactly 2 "towns" in the game, around 10 other locations of interest and no place that will make you go *damn this is cool*. Music: 5/10Other than maybe 3 pieces, the music are forgettable. Exploration music is generic and so are most combat tracks. You will have better enjoyment playing Far Cry 5 OST in the background since it fits the theme better. Blood of the Lamb for the intro is pretty good, but the choir music for the final fight is just straight up boring. Graphic: 7/10:Good, nothing great. Everything is white and grey and there aren't many interesting locations to see in the first place. Combat effects are good.Overall, Wasteland 3 is by no mean a bad RPG, but I'm mildly disappointed from the strong beginning. Certainly the game feel like a passion project, a love letter to the genre but severely constrained by budget. I'd still recommend it if you want a short adventure, plus it's really a good bargain on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Decent story with many choices. Fun XCOM-style combat. A good choice if you want a simple and modern Fallout-style CRPG. Juggling skill proficiencies and armor/weapon mods on your party was probably the most tedious part.Companions are ok, not super memorable or deep, although I found myself sticking to the first two that you meet, since I didn't want to go through the hassle of respeccing party members to have a well-rounded team. To be fair, the game does offer reasonably priced respecs, so changing up the party doesn't seem like a huge ordeal.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland brand true to its core - interesting story, strong characters, perfect replay-ability and non-black'n'white decisions. I have enjoyed all these RPG aspects represented. Well...occasionally the humor is kind of overboard and it partially kills the immersion but this was just a minor flaw. Overall a thoroughly enjoyable piece!
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a positive experience marred by simplistic binary decision making.  When compared against other RPG's, the choices you have feel extremely 2 dimensional.  For major decisions you can either chose A or B.  When you see the designated "combat arena" it is time for combat.  Very important characters and situations have their own special cut scenes.The story is better than most, the combat works well, and for the most part this is a good B game.  I am wishing for a bit more freedom and inspiration.  By no means a 'game of the year' kind of game, but I do not regret playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Been looking forward to this game ever since backing it on fig 3 years ago, and I was positively surprised it lived up to my hype. Took me about 60-70 hours (with reading all the lore-stuff and convos) to complete the campaign on hard difficulty and I had a blast (quite literally, with all the things I blew up with my rocket launcher guy). The story is great, some choices were really tough, the music is excellent, and if you're a fan of turn-based tactics and the fallout-ish post-apocalyptic setting, then you can't do anything wrong with this game. Apparently though, there's a lot of bugs in this game. I have played the campaign in single player for roughly 2-3 weeks directly after release and never encountered a major problem, except for the long loading times. Most of the bugs seem to be in co-op, however, and are being worked out consistently.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Wasteland 2 it seems a little bit shorter. I played the game shortly after release so minor bugs were here and there, but I was pleasently supprised by the high technical quality state of the game since these days is more common to release unfinished product. Loved the soundtrack, songs and atmosphere of the game. Storywise it's great, but I missed some bigger misteries in the main plotline which was pretty staightforward from the start and most of twist were easy predictable. Concerning gameplay I was disappointed how the weapon mods worked. Getting melee mods from fireguns was a big letdown and step back from the system in Wasteland 2. Overall Wasteland 3 is a very good game. Simpler story without much branching and mystery is a hurdle which is letting it down from being a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a fan of turn combat games but I do like RPGs a lot. I played DOS 2 and I was told this game was very similar gameplay wise and it really is. Some people say this is what Fallout 3 would have been had Bethesda not bought the IP. The graphics are great, the world is detailed, the music is fantastic, the combat mechanics are good, the story and the dialogs are ok, the quests are fun and with a lot of memorable characters.The things I didn't like: It's too short (for me), the bugs (not many nasty ones in my case but I did find some annoying ones) and  not enough item variety.Definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from Wasteland 2, it disappoints... I bought the Digital Deluxe version for 70,= EURO, thinking these guys know how to build a good lasting game.It mostly disappoints in game play duration and story. I just finished my first run trough in 55 hours. The previous game took me around 100 hours to finish and add to that another 130 hours of replay value.The story is to short its also to straight forward, to flat, doesn't feel like there are unexpected consequences in the late game. You kind of already know the consequences during the decision making. Its all to easy. I miss a certain depth and layering to the story, it doesn't grab me as much as Wasteland 2 did. And finally add to that the bugs that need to be ironed out.For me it doesn't feel the game is worth 70,= Euro's, I would wait for it to be on sale for 30,= Euro's max.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, but a bit buggy. Especially the UI.There have been many times where characters simply didn't perform an action, despite having the AP to do so and no debuffs that would prevent that action. Happened a lot after reviving a character.[Spoilerfree] Near the end there is a certain area that ALWAYS caused a CTD when I moved my camera to look at it. I figured out that it's just that specific area and only if you look at it in combat state, so I found a work-around. I had my sniper eliminate the only enemy in that CTD area from Stealth and then avoided moving my camera there for the rest of the combat.7/10, but only because of the frequency of the bugs. If the bugs didn't occur multiple times literally every game session, the game would be an easy 9 or 10 out of 10. They aren't gamebreaking (except for the last one described above but that one occurred only once) so it's not the end of the world.Like I said, really nice game with a lot of replayability and a neat story.Also the music is great and fits the thematic perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it. Quite unbalanced. It is missing so much basic stuff RPG players are used to. In short can not compare to Divinity: Original Sin II in any way. I really cant see how this game got so high ratings. I played 22h on normal level and it does not require any strategy at all. Combat is easy and predictable you dont need to think it through before combat, just go, you can not loose. I remember Baldur's Gate where I played some battles over and over again until I make proper strategy. In wasteland you just go, no need to quick save at all lol. Interface is ok but sometimes buggy. Camera focus is extremely annoying and there are no options to tune it. Sometimes it is very hard to distinguish characters in the combat because all looks very messy. There is so much more I dont like with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Game. 8/10The good:Combat and Gameplay is fun. Plenty of ways you can go about building your units. Choices makes sense. Investing in a specific skill feels rewarding. Story is decent, characters are likeable. World is immersive. There is plenty of drip.The bad:The fact that the game is balanced around having a team. I like playing as one character, and from the start you are stuck with two. Personal preference. Bugs. There are a few but the most annoying one is the one where a turn freezes, be it enemy or ally. It is incredibly frustrating in the middle of a long drawn out fight that a random character just stops doing anything and holds up the entire game, forcing you to reload and do everything again. The stealth system, idk its just ass and underwhelming for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original Fallouts & Baldurs gate's.However these days for some reason I get bored of the stories half way through most story based games.For some reason not this one, I'm still going strong and can easily see myself playing this one through again to try another route.Add to that the Combat is really fun and the Character building mechanics are some of the best I've seen in a long time.A Great game by todays standards & 10/10 for Nostalgia Gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: I'd take the negative reviews with a grain of salt. Most were made on day one, and almost all of the complaints were fixed. One review gave it a thumbs down because it's "not their cup of tea". It's fine if the game isn't to your tastes, but that's not thumbs up or down worthy, and that's not the point of the thumb system. I was ranting there, but the game is running 85% smooth, the soundtrack is amazing, and the characters are memorable. I'd get it on sale when it's up or wait for definitive/director's cut that will most likely be out next year. It's a good game and you won't regret your patience with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The devs went through a lot of trouble to paint the Rangers as the good guys. The player's Rangers are, for the most part, the White of a black and white world, even though it is really all shades of grey. However, the devs also force the player to help slavers, no choice, no alternative, and then punishes the players if they chose the high road. This is a very scumbag kind of thing for the devs to do, especially after establishing that the Rangers Should be able to get into the entire base no problem AND take out the slavers.  The Devs set it up the be both ways, and then are too lazy, or malicious, to do it right. I cannot refund and I can honestly say that anyone with a conscious should not like this decision, this IS a $15, to $20 dollar game made by devs still stuck in the 1980s. The bugs (and lack of a forum thread to report bugs, and the terrible combat issues), overpricing (the game just comes off feeling lazy, lacking the potential it could have had, as I mentioned this is a game for the 1990s), and lack of utility (such as no control over animal companions, no way to effectively check status effects) only makes this worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall score: 9/10 - Evaluation: Sure buyGreatness: absorbing story; graphic details; deep characters; dialogues and lore; SoundtrackStandard: strategy elements; RPG elements: inventory mgmt; battle mechanics; lootingBelow par: InnovationMy notes: I became a fan of Wasteland 2 and was eager to play the next installment. The devs didn't disappoint me. After 90 hours on my first playthrough I can say this is the best Isometric tactical/strategy squad building game I've played since Jagged Alliance: Back in Action. The story, the choices, the irony, the humor and the depth of most NPCs all sum up to make this game a great experience. Although there's nothing particularly innovative here, it's a well crafted old school kinda game and you can feel the love the devs dedicated to it. Take your time and enjoy the ride. I sure did.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 4/10.Pros:- Decent turn-based, tactical system- Non-trivial resource management- Towards the end of the game it becomes somewhat more interesting in terms of possible choices of action.- Decent graphicsCould be better:- Companions - not that many of them, pretty much locked in terms of what ending they support. Except for comments in various situation there is no real interaction.Just wrong:- There is plethora of small technical issues A.K.A  features that really get on nerves. I.e. opening up anything but map (why on earth it's map ?) does not stop time. If your character is bleeding it will keep happening until you actually use the proper item. It also means that enemy might spot you at that time etc.    Numerous NPCs start banter as soon as they are visible. Which can be annoying considering the fact that many of them have just one conversation played on repeat.   Weapons have different ranges of effective fire. Not indicated anywhere, you can only guess that by hovering over movable fields to see successful strike odds against enemies in range from given cell.   And numerous others.- Difficulty - enemy with 16 pts of armor means that some 1/3 of weapon types just can't really hurt him. You having 25 points of armor means nothing - many enemies will easily get past it. On that note though - anyone can significantly decrease enemy's armor provided they stacked up successful attacks. Plus energy weapon might do that, though energy cells are fairly expensive and it's not a feasible strategy. Makes you wonder why there couldn't be some normal way of decreasing it. Scaling difficulty by inflating enemy's hp and armor is also cheap.- Your options in most of the situations are really limited and it's hard to say why. Well - you probably can guess why, but that's not what you should be facing. No similar options (i.e. favouring some faction but with different outcomes), no creative solutions (i.e. I wish I could convince kid with inflated ego to be mu puppet, but that's just not happening). Then again - frequently it's just about on what terms you are going to enter the fight.- Story is shallow. Interactions are shallow. There is hardly any deception, content writers couldn't be bothered.- Maps are claustrophobic. Another "largest town" of all in all perhaps 25 buildings, residential area of Hundred Families included.- Tactics are somewhat crippled by the fact that half of the usables don't make much difference and that virtually any table is out of the sudden as good a cover as a crate or road blocker making denial tactics just useless. Somewhat better with skills, but they also are mostly useless. Also no factors of height visibility etc.- Short. I mean - nothing has been really done well and on the top of that there is little content.All in all - it's just not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a 94 year old widower who's wife joined the heavenly choir a long time ago and these days one of the only joys I get is from gaming. However, I'm not sure I can say I got much joy from this game. It reminded me of the days when my wife, Ethel, was alive. "Walk here and perform this boring task" she used to say, then "now you've done that, go over there and perform another seemingly pointless and uninteresting task". Much like the game, these tasks were often interspersed with fights, which livened up my day a little but I knew that when they were over I'd be back to doing some task that I had very little interest in and was more of a chore than anything else. Much like Ethel, I gave this game a really good go and tried to like it's finer points of which there were few, but like her it became boring and unappealing. And, also much like Ethel, it'll now end up buried in my Library

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is an extremely decent CRPG.+Great build diversity and difficulty scaling. +Each major quest has a few different ways to complete them. +Large variety of weapons +Many interesting, often funny NPC's.+Huge crafting list of consumables, plus weapon & armor mods.+Lots of secrets and wacky content. +Not overly long. -Main story is just okay. -Overland travel, overland events, and the survival skill could have been fleshed out more.-I had a frequent issue during combat where I would click on one character and another would be selected.-"Radio chatter" can get annoyingly repetitive-No major way to filter/search through long crafting list.-Interactable objects would sometimes glitch and become unusable. A restart was needed.+-Almost too many non-player companions towards the end of the game. Each combat turn ends up taking quite a while. And you're not even making inputs for the last half of each turn.The DLC was worthwhile for me, too. Decent side stories and a few new mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Wasteland 3 is a good game. This game presents more agency than any other I've played in a long while. Completing some quests will lock you out of completion of others. The choices you make can easily leave you feeling hollow, as there sometimes is no good choice to make. That's a noteworthy design choice, and one that should be lauded.The logic some NPCs use does not always stack up (I'm looking at you Angela). Although you can't really call them out, thankfully some NPCs will. Its also a bit strange that for all the agency you are given the game will sometimes assume you take particular actions, like radioing people to tell them you're going to kill their boss, rather than going about it quietly. The principle detraction from the game is that it didn't feel like Wasteland. Most of the levels were relatively short, and the level of weird was curtailed compared to earlier games in part because the majority of the antagonists were human. Only the Gippers felt truly inspired in terms of novel Wasteland crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: What Wasteland 3 lacks in graphics it makes up for in spades with its Gameplay, Lore, Storytelling, and Voice Acting. Don't just glance at Wasteland 3 and say "Meh the graphics are bad the game must be bad" or "This RPG isn't even first person how can this even be fun?"Overview:When was the last time a game moved you to make personal emotional decisions that affected not only your group but the perception of you and your group among various factions? You don't need to play this game long to start seeing these questions pop up. Your decisions in Wasteland 3 MATTER, that dude in a cutscene who is totally about to get murdered but you have a chance to change the outcome.. that matters, whether you or another group kills them, that matters, how long the character lives or if they die early, that matters. You know that drunk you see bumbling around in a dumpster who no one would miss if you murdered them and took their loot, killing them matters.Gameplay:Gameplay in Wasteland 3 boils down to 3 main points Turn based strategy, Decision Making, and Recruiting members to your squad.Every decision you make in Wasteland 3 no matter how insignificant you may find it will matter at some point in the game and this goes further than just good decision, neutral decision, bad decision. Due to how many potential outcomes there are, each playthrough will be different (unless you decide to make the same choices) Among the five other people I know who played this game the same time I did, we all made different decisions in the beginning stages of the game and already have vastly different gameplay options available to us.Your squad will be composed of characters you recruit or find in your travels. Recruited members can be chosen from a list of pre-made characters or you can create your own. Character creation is robust you can choose the characters background which applies different traits to them, apply attributes to various stat blocks to affect how they act in and out of combat, apply skill points to further specialize what type of character they will be in your squad, and also chose to give them a quirk which are trade-offs. For example one quirk is called "Sadomasochist" this quirk allows your character to deal more damage but they also receive more damage, among the quirks are other interesting choices such as "When a party member dies, gain more actions on your turn for the next 2 turns +damage bonus, Once the two turns are over reduce your actions for the following 4 turns". The skill system is extremely vast and will allow you to build a team of very different individuals who's varying skills will allow you access to extra content throughout the game, thus building a well-rounded team of members who specialize in different avenues is extremely rewarding.Combat:Combat in Wasteland 3 is turn-based and feels very much like XCOM without prema-death. There's a cover system, a watchdog action, defense, and hold action. Watchdog allows your character to fire at someone if they cross your line-of-sight, defense gives you additional defense stats equal to how many actions you didn't take, and hold action will allow you to carry over additional actions on your next turn. Melee is hilarious and awesome definitely recruit a melee character when you gain access to do so.Voice Acting:I want to say the game is about 95% voice acted, there are some scenes where it isn't and you will have to read but I've run into that perhaps twice during the 10 hours I played the game. Also the voice actors are really good, I'm unable to tell how many different VA's they used because every character just sounds that much different.This game is 100% worth the $60 price tag, it really does have the feel of the original fallout series (CRPG) to it. If you enjoy CRPG's or have a steam gift card laying around or money on your steam account and are able to get it for less than $60 you won't regret spending a dime.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just beat Wasteland 3 after a 25 hour long journey through Colorado. A lot of folks on my friends list have asked me how it is, and how it compares to Wasteland 2, and I've decided that it's very good, better than Wasteland 2, but that there was certainly room for improvement.That being said, 25 hours for a first play through is quite good, and there seem to be a fair few endings, branching paths, and shifts in narrative that would make for interesting replayability.Let's start off with the things I wasn't such a big fan of.Weapon balancing, scaling and the lack of real variety. There seem to be maybe four or five tiers to each different weapon - Pistols start out as pea-shooters, as everything else does (though of course hitpoints scale with weapon damage as well), and as you progress through the game you find each incremental stage upward. The problem with this is that there aren't any real 'unique' weapons - There are cosmetic differences between them, like the Prototype Patriarch Hammer being on par with the Engine Block Hammer but in a different flavor. I don't know what I would've liked to have seen be different there - On hit effects making a difference? Better unique weapons? In any case, a lot of the joy in finding cool loot was largely absent in Wasteland 3; The most exciting things I could find were higher ranking weapon mods, and even those were nothing to write home about.Factions - Why does it feel like there are only two shifts for the Hundred Families? Why do the Hundred Families not impact the ending? Why are half of the factions in the game present just in Colorado Springs, and that's just three of them? These are questions for the developers, largely, but I can't help but to feel that the game, particularly the southern portion of the map, were extremely barren in regard to groups, factions, encounters, etc.Ranger Headquarters. I hauled my ass to Colorado, got blown to ♥♥♥♥ on an ice lake, got made the CO of a mission with one other surviving ranger, ended up with a base, and you're telling me it's just "Okay, find yourself a grease monkey, an armorer, a doctor and a cook. Also, maybe a scientist and a museum curator". There are opportunities to collect a few more people here in there, like a robot doctor, or some extra folks for the garage, but by and large there are no real changes. Why is there not a Command and Control bunker at the AFB? WtfContent - I feel like I was always waiting for the LA section of Wasteland 3, to be dropped into the southern half of the map and have a whole other 22+hr shindig in front of me. Instead, after you get Radiation Resistance 3 on your Kodiak, it's barren wasteland city and Scorpitron hunting for you before you go to meet the power top that is the Patriarch's daughter. Speaking of, where is the involvement with the Patriarchs kids? You go scoop Vic and Val and they just sit in your jail? Daddy Dearest doesn't even come to slap them around? And there are no words about what happened with Liberty?With all that being said, I still recommend the game. It's still better than Wasteland 2. It looks better. It's more enjoyable to play. It might have some performance issues, and there might be missing content, and there might be some reactivity and quest issues, but I still prefer it over going to Ag Center and listening to Highpool berate me over the radio for an hour because I couldn't be two places at once.I hope that additional content comes out for Wasteland 3 - At the time of reviewing, the game is positively rated, it's in the top 100 concurrent players on Steam list, and it seems to be selling more copies still. It's very good. It could be better. But it's still very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm probably about 2/3 the way through the game. I really want to like it. I like a lot about it, from the mechanics, leveling, loot, etc. That said, at a story level, I dread the choices presented, and it makes me hesitate to keep playing.The good:Visuals: Enjoyable, a lot of unique stuff, cool weapons from the realistic to the fantastic, some interesting armors. Cool scenery. Fun to watch a menagerie of animals kill the bad guys.Combat: A little repetitive at times, but that's possibly my fault for being very meticulous.Writing (not counting the story): Good, sometimes quite funny, and the voice work is pretty solid as well.Sound: In general, pretty good. Sometimes I hate that certain songs will get stuck in my head, but I especially love the remakes of classics in new ways (some remind me of Natural Born Killers).The Bad:Choices: Reading other reviews, and tips and the occasional help on a quest (or a bug), I see over and over again that you get punished for doing the right thing. That's annoying. I understand that sometimes right is going to be harder, but every damn time you want to do what is probably the 'rightest' thing, it sucks. Then, more than once, you're presented with options that both suck.As a future game dev and a writer, I get that we can't have infinite choices, but sometimes, you're just shoved into something that me and my squad wouldn't be in, and I feel like the devs were just a little to laser focused on the idea that the apocalypse will suck and everyone will suck, and sucks to suck. I'm not asking for cupcakes and rainbows, but I think a little more towards small/slow/long term benefits for doing the right thing, or even having the option to do the right thing, would have been cool.All of that not to mention that 'the right thing' isn't always a clear choice, but I'm not a fan of the lesser of two evils.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to this game after playing so many countless hours of fallout. I learned that inXile were the original creators and i thought it was a pretty raw end of the deal they got with the whole franchise so i gave this a chance, i love everything about the worlds and experiences they themselves created in the early games. Quite honestly, I haven't played a squad/turn based since i was a kid and had completely no interest in them whatsoever being a simracer/fps kind of gamer, but something about wasteland's world and history intrigued me to the point of going on out on a limb and spending money on something i didn't even know i would absolutely fall in love with! Hands down this game is an excellent buy with a great story that holds up pretty well no matter what your play style is, gameplay itself is legit, good fun there are many different ways to build your characters and the weapons they use and i enjoyed every second all 73.4 hours of it before completing the game. My only criticism-and i say this ever so lightly because a large majority of the time the options you want are there, would be to include more dialogue/quest options but there are plenty that will satisfy 99% of anybody else. Truthfully i would recommend this game to anybody, and I do. Thanks inXile for persevering and staying true to yourselves you've made something that will forever leave it's mark in gaming history and in my heart. I will be playing 1 and 2 next :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me 40 hours to complete this includes I would say 95% of side quests. It was amazing. Feels like playing Fallout 1 and 2 again. _childDocuments_.review: 8/10About ~75hrs of playtime out of the game,  $40 is worth it, but I wouldn't pay more.Pros-Music was amazing, great job-Very immersive, I was solidly caught up in the story & it is most definitely a "Just one more turn" game.-Very funny, good dialogue to boot.-Good story, as you would expect from a Wasteland title.Cons-I'd say almost no replayability.  Once you go through it once you've got a pretty solid idea of how the story would play out if you made any other decisions than what you made in the first run.  Very linear.  The fact that I got 30/62 achievements in just a single play through bolsters my point.-Generally bug free as an AAA title, but a couple more than it should have had.-The inability to 'set' your order and make it stick is obnoxious.  It doesn't matter what you do, after every load/new zone you enter you need to put your crew in the order you want them.  And then they don't actually even walk in formation in that order.  I know similar engines are capable of this, should have been done.Issues with game design (warning spoilers)-The combat felt pretty stale about 2/3-3/4 through the game.-On normal difficulty I resolved almost every combat in the entire game in 2-3 rounds.  The final two boss fights I completed in 2 & 3 rounds respectively.  This made at least 1/3-1/2 of the perks completely worthless.-You could anticipate virtually every combat and then position for a surprise round, making initiative a nearly worthless ability.-Healing was insanely powerful.  3AP to 100% heal yourself?  Any team member can revive any other team member with no skill needed and no device needing to be equipped to do so?  Healing darts that can reach 50% of the battlefield for 50% heal?  It just didn't matter if a team member went down, if that happened I'd just finish the battle that round anyway and they'd insta heal.-Survival was WAY too powerful as a skill.  I skipped all but 3 ambush battles on the map the entire game.  No repercussions, no story line involved, extremely minor loot you'd miss out on, didn't even need to get it past level 6-7 iirc.  No need to do it to even level up your characters!  Unless I guess if you wanted for some reason to skip all the side quests?  But why even do that to do lesser content for the same result?-I didn't even realize Pvt. Wesson was one of my recruitable team members until the last few scenes of the game.  There are dozens of "Pvt.'s" wandering around your base that have 0 part in the story at all, should have given her another name so it was more clear you could recruit her.-I felt like there should have been a lot more NPC's available people to recruit as team members if you require 2 of them to be a part of your team.  That part of the game felt like it failed a bit compared to Wasteland 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, not a successor to Fallout - since Wasteland came first - but picking up where Fallout left off as a tactical RPG, Wasteland 3 doesn't tread new waters, but navigates the old ones well. Players can create up to 4 custom Rangers with a number of skills ranging from weapon specialisation to wild animal taming, to first aid to lock picking, to bartering and leadership. With the ability to add to companions from the campaign to your squad, the max squad size is 6, allowing for a wide coverage of skills across the whole team.Combat plays out in a style similar to the XCOM or Divinity: Original Sin games, where each unit has a pool of Action Points to use on everything one can do on a turn. Moving, using items, using skills, attacking, or interacting with switches in combat all cost AP, and once all the team's AP reaches 0, the turn is handed over the the enemies and any AI-controlled allies that may be present. Perks and weapon-based abilities offer a little flexibility in encounters, with some clocking in as more helpful than others depending on the kinds of enemies being encountered.As for narrative, Wasteland 3 doesn't take itself too seriously. Alongside the main plot of political intrigue, bizarre wasteland encounters are going on all over the place. Each encounter can be solved a number of ways that rely on a variety of skills, the skills Kiss Ass and Hard Ass being the chief negotiation and intimidation skills respectively. Most any NPC that matters can be worked over with one or both of these skills. But failing to talk your way out of these encounters hardly feels dissatisfying, as it almost always results in combat - which is fun.The graphics are basic but not terrible, but the music is where the game shines. Western acoustic renditions of songs such as "Everybody Have Fun Tonight" by Wang Chung play in a lineup alongside patriotic gospel singing for much of the game's soundtrack, playing over key story moments or intense encounters while people shoot the heck out of each other. It's always a treat.Edit: I've since learned that multiplayer in this is not good lol. Well, that's a shame, but even without that it's still a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was reluctant to buy this game given all the feedback about bugs and crashing, but happy to report that I've had almost no issues. There have been a few very minor graphical glitches with zero impact on gameplay, a perk/skill that doesn't seem to be working with my sniper, and that's about it. Not sure if it's just my machine or the first patch was that effective but I've had no crashes and load times aren't that bad. Really, really fun. I'm about 25 hours in (That 125-hour figure isn't accurate as I frequently leave the game running and forget to pause) so my characters are really starting to build up some skills and abilities. I've got a brawler who just destroys people; a change-up from my normal play style and extremely entertaining using him to mash enemies into a gory pulp. Am also enjoying the switch to Colorado after the previous desert setting. So given my experience, I'd give this top high marks as a worthy successor to Wasteland 2, which I played twice -- a huge rarity for me.

_childDocuments_.review: When I played Xbox and didn't have a PC many moons ago, I purchased the Xbox Game Pass, which was fantastic. One day I was bored, and began looking for games to play on the large library that XGP has to offer, and thus I landed upon the masterpiece that was Wasteland 2. I wasn't sure at first, but after finishing the game twice I knew that it was my favourite game of all time. The tactical combat, the funny encounters, and just about everything you did or didn't do had an effect on the world. When I heard Wasteland 3 was coming out as well, I was beyond excited. While I was too late to become a Fig backer, I waited patiently for Wasteland 3 to come out. Then the release date came, and then it was delayed. Finally, after what I can imagine was a lot of polishing, they released Wasteland 3.This game surprised me from the start, as I had very high expectations and hopes for this game. I was slightly worried that inXile would simplify it too much, or screw it up in some way. But thankfully, the game is spectacular so far. I'm having more fun with Wasteland 3 than I ever did with 2, and that's saying a lot. A couple issues have emerged, such as the long loading times, (I have an Nvme drive, it should not take 15 seconds to load a small area lol) but everything so far is great. Combat was improved upon greatly, the vehicles were implemented well, and leveling feels much more rewarding now, but not too much. Overall, great job inXile, thank you very much.

_childDocuments_.review: A WASTELAND 3 REVIEW                                                              By: Mentally a Challenged Kutaku Writer''This is my Wasteland 3 experience: I’ve found that playing on the lowest difficulty counterbalances all confusion, to a degree. I certainly never grasped why I could only shoot once per turn but my enemies could shoot two or three times. Turning things down to Rookie made fights a manageable, if still punishing, experience. In one frustrating encounter, a group of pigs strapped with dynamite kept running into my team, killing two or three party members at a time. At every turn, I found myself sorely missing the overwatch feature from Gears Tactics and XCOM. Wasteland’s complex world wasn’t made for a rookie like me—in fact, I still don’t fully understand how all these systems work. It all contributes to the unmistakable feeling that Wasteland 3 is a creature of the past.  You might find it all enough to keep you going through an 80- to 100-hour adventure. In series tradition, there are many, many endings, based on the various choices you make from tip to tail. As a newcomer, it’s a longshot that I’ll see even one of them.''

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge wasteland fan and have gotten hundreds of hours out of both 1 and 2. 3, while great (so far) story and combat mechanics and overall content, I have to say there are a few bugs in here that need to be addressed. This is after about 70 true hours (currently showing 104.8) of gameplay and multiple starts to try and dink around with the choices, anyway I digress the bugs that I've noticed weren't game breaking (in my experience) but were/are definitely frustrating to say the least. The list that follows is what I've noticed so far:- Random items upon looting will not transfer to inventory and subsequently be lost to the void.- Failed selection clicks - trying to select a character (with mouse to clarify) will sometimes not register the click thus not selecting the character (this had lead to a few unintentional injuries lol).- Various skills and abilities will not allow you to click on them for use, even if conditions are met (this is GENERALLY corrected by selecting another character and re-selecting the previous character)So far other than that I'm loving the game. _childDocuments_.review: The tactical components of Wasteland 2 have been removed and replaced with a grind system to win-or-lose battles through lateral progression.  Battles are decided before they start.  Either you play enough side missions before-hand to crush the curve--or you simply save scum your way to an unsatisfying finish line.   Immersion breaking shortcuts like bullet sponging on hard difficulty levels, and team based initiative, replace the tactical decision making of WL2.   Gone are the days where you balanced speed with forcefulness, in a team that was weighted evenly to deal with a multitude of challenges.  In post-acquired-developer Wasteland 3, you simply get out the cookie cutter, throw down the turrets, ready the rocket launchers.  Most weapons are obsolete by the time you find them.  Most skills are obsolete, since backtracking with absurd specialists in place of your front-liners is the expected play style.  Overall, it's a game rife with artificial content and lacking in strategy, immersion, character depth and storytelling.  It's not the third chapter in the Wasteland saga--it's the first one that came *after* the one that was worth playing\ through.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to pure gameplay, the game is great:* Combat feels good and rewarding, if you're a fan of tactical turn-based combat you'll be right at home* Dialogue is great, a bit more mature than fallout 1/2 and uses a lot of recent pop culture references* Character progression is good but can sometimes be confusing especially if you're a first-time player* Quests are very diverse and most can be finished in more than one way* Choices made affect how certain factions react towards you and how events will play out, meaning there's a lot of new things to be discovered during a second playthrough* NPCs have their own personality and can make a very strong impression on you, to the point where you want to help them because you like them rather than because helping them may give you a better reward* Exploring the "overworld" or even new locations is a joy and feels very rewardingNow for the bad part, nothing gameplay related but it's mostly technical issues:* Poor optimization: I have a Ryzen 3900X and a Radeon 5700XT and with this system I should blow the game out of the water even at max settings but it is not the case, with everything on ultra I hit 75 fps (which is fine) however GPU usage sits at around 20-30% all the time and my CPU usage sits at around the same, this means that the game is not using all resources available to it, I tried reducing graphical settings to the lowest but it doesn't change anything, I barely hit the 80 fps...* FPS drops and stutters when highlighting interactable items (pressing shift), it pisses me off because it's such a core mechanic,* Dialogue can be clunky and sometimes it even freezes for a while (I've read that for other people it outright causes crashes, although the game hasn't crashed once for me)* Very very very long load times between areas... even with an NVMe SSD* Bad UI / UX / Tutorial: UI feels clunky in general.Some things like using a medpack with your character with highest first aid skill on another is so cumbersome, you must add it to the first character's quickslot via the inventory menu, exit said menu then click on the medpack in the quickslot and then on the character that needs a heal, why is this not doable through the inventory directly?Clicking on interactable items (say lockpick a door) then realizing you did it with the wrong character, you change character and then hover over the interactable item again and the cursor doesnt change from "pointer" to "interact" or takes a long time.Some of the mechanics are not well explained, I had to find through a reddit post how to check status effects (through an 'i' icon on the top right corner).The combat action bar is not very clear / ergonomic, you don't easily know if you're in normal attack mode or in ability / precision strike mode (the UI doesn't give you feedback), not to mention that if you want to cancel an action it's very weird, the amount of times I've moved my troops by mistake trying to cancel an action is far too great.* Last bad point but also the least important: the graphics are not the best, but most of the time it doesn't matter because of the isometric view, however it is noticeable during cutscenes / cinematics / animated dialogueTL;DR: Gameplay is great but the game needs some serious polish, the technical aspect gets really annoying after a while

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, the game can be enjoyable and even rather good for long stretches of time. However, there are some things that annoy me:- The bugs (wait for tons of patches)- Not using my awesome Wasteland 2 ending- Too short/small in scope (where did all that dev time go? Certainly not in QualityControl or content)- The main choice/conflict isn't interesting- People say the small choices really matter. I didn't get that impression.- The combat isn't all that good in my opinion. The maps and encounters/fights are really tiny.- The main base feels boring to me.- The writing, humor and atmosphere could have been better. The game just taught me early on not to care about anything. It's so superficial and small and didn't provoke any emotional reactions.- The companions (not rangers) aren't interesting. Seldom has a game managed to make me care so little.- Why can't I re-skill my team?- It seems to me that you have to do terrible things in order to get good stuff in the game (for example to support slavery. Why didn't they drop the code, when I killed the slavers?) Why should I support cannibals later on?Buy it on a sale after most bugs are gone and you'll have an okay time. Be aware that this is a very subjective opinion. I just expected much more and I must say that I liked the previous game better.
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've been excited to play a game, and even longer since a game left me so enthralled that I had a physiological need to finish it--sleep, food, responsibilities, etc... all ceased to matter. There was only Wasteland 3.My husband wasn't home for the first 8 hours that I was playing, so I would continuously send him screenshots of things that both confused and amused me. His typical responses were a 50/50 split of "lol" and "wtf".I've never played a game that has made me laugh this hard, nor have many had this degree of emotional impact. For me, the bugs and crashes that I encountered were forgivable, because I felt that I was given a story-rich, interesting environment, with memorable characters and tough decisions to make throughout. I never once felt that the game suffered from the bland kill and fetch missions that plague most RPGs. I enjoyed it so much that I have wanted to replay it since  completing my first play through. I genuinely wish that I could express how thankful I am to the developers that they've given me another game to love.

_childDocuments_.review: Killed Santa Claus and busted up his drug lab.10/10But more seriously, there's some bugs (some big, some small, co-op notably bugged), load times are consitently 15-30 seconds on an NVEe SSD, the odd CTD (2x in 30 hours) and massive frame rate drops despite an Ryzen 3700 series, 32GB RAM, and an NVidia 1080. inXile did promise fixes and it's all hands on deck there, and I believe they'll make good on those fixes as they did for Wasteland 2. Behind all that, there's an amazing turn based combat system, and with a strong choice and consequence system. One of the better RPGs of any kind is there right now, and will be a fan favourite RPG for a long time to come when all the optimization is done.** Edit **Majority of bug fixes and loading fixed. Definitely worth picking up now if you have any interest in cRPGs. Looking forward to DLC if that's on the horizon.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun playing it. It had its ups and downs. When I got the most frustrated with the game (combat mostly) and said that I wouldn't play it again, I was right back at it hours later thinking that maybe if I do this and that different I would get the result I wanted. The story was cool. The side missions were mostly grey areas with where you had hard decisions to make. I tried for a self centered, money hungry, bad but not good either type of a character. The combat was kind of a disappointment to me. I played it on Ranger difficulty which was one below the hardest. I will say that weapons / armor and stats for your character compared to the enemies were very underwhelming. I felt like during the majority of combat encounters one of characters was going to die no matter my approach. The enemies will one shot most of your crew whether you have decent armor or not. I felt more like a necromancer at the end of every combat turn than a ranger. I quick loaded in this game more than any other. While with some fights changing my strategy and approach did seemed to work, I do feel that not every fight, especially those near the end, a simple change in approach was going to allow you to do better. Some fights just required that you get lucky.  I think it deserves a one time play through. I would recommend the normal difficulty at first, no matter if you are new or a returning player. I just feel like the first time shouldnt be so frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has inherited the great cover and fighting system of the second one and without going to much into details, it has obviously been refined here and there, which gives a great feel to the game. The weapons are powerful and the animations as well as the combat areas are coherent.The story sometimes seems a bit too boring to me, because the game has the typical "kill this guy", "go there and find out whats going on" missions etc. I dont like to be an Errand Boy tbh. They are not bad in general, but nothing special. This is just my opinion and can change as the game progresses.The opponents often shoot/heal through walls, which is a bit annoying every now and then, but the AI is doing well.Overall a good game up to this time. I like the freedom you have and the Combat Mechanics. The Story is ok.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Fallout 1 & 2, I would definitely recommend this game. If you're looking of a CRPG with Xcom/tactics sort of combat, search no further. The story is pretty strong, the combat can be very satisfying, and has a pretty banging soundtrack. Does a great job at building the universe. It even has some Suikoden sort of base building, allowing you to recruit people to join your base to unlock unique buffs, equipment, and content.Overall an actual overlooked gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Working on my third playthrough on Supreme Jerk (this time with an all melee squad), I'm noticing a drop in overall difficulty right around level  10-13 or so.  Mechanics, smoke grenades, 1 AP food buffs combined with rally really allows the squad to push through anything fairly easy.  I was looking for the moment the game would get WAY more difficult and become a struggle halfway through, much like the synth cattle thieves encounter in wasteland 2 on Surpeme Jerk difficulty, but didn't really find it.Despite the relative ease of the highest difficulty, the game is engaging and you can find success with almost any squad type (even on Supreme Jerk mode) and the game choices allow multiple rewarding endings I wont spoil here.  Next up is 4 big guns characters and NO mechanics, followed by an all pistol; group.  The two supreme jerk run throughs so far have been:1. One each of Sniper, Big Guns, Small Armsd and Auto, with Pistol NPC and Shotgun NPC (1 mechanic)2. All Auto Weapons (3 AR and 1 SMG), Shotgun NPC and Snip[er NPC (2 mechanics)3. (Current) - All Melee - No npcs yet, but going to try to keep it to melee only (1 Mechanic)4. (Next) - All Big Guns (No mechanics)5. (Then) - All pistols (2-4 mechanics)

I hate it when in a game like this (looking at you X-COM!) takes away the camera controls while im holding the mouse. _childDocuments_.review: 24 hours in game and I'm going to finish it. It's a great game but in its current unpolished state I can not recommend it.Pros: Good character customization. Many ways to build your characters. Diverse equipment. Interesting world AND story. You are constantly being pelted with moral questions that don't necessarily have a correct answer. Voice acting is very good.Cons: This game cost 60 bucks and has the polish of a 20 dollar game.The indicator for action points in a fight is mildly bugged. Action point estimates don't update between switching weapons unless you try different actions first. The loading times are terrible. Random bugs where quests will start over or you receive the beginning dialog again. Feels like the devs didn't playtest parts of the game, otherwise they would have realized they have to spend twenty minutes running and sitting through loading screens to leave a dungeon with more than one area.My biggest complaint is that there is just a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ menu. Like, why can't I view a stats page about my character? I can't see how much damage they do, what their resistances are, or even what exactly these skills do. Does melee damage count toward brawling damage?? I don't know because the game doesn't explain ♥♥♥♥. Also no area to see interesting stats like how many sawpups or los payasos I've killed. Lack of interesting stats or even detailed attributes about the character makes the player characters feel pretty replaceable/meaningless. Game is just missing a huge amount of polish that was present in the games it borrowed heavily from (XCOM and Divinity Original Sin)EDIT: I just wasted 45 minutes in a very long fight only for it to bug out near the end. I revived a unit with my last AP in the turn. The character revived, but I couldn't switch to them. I couldn't use the end turn button. This character had 3 AP but I couldn't use their action points. I tried using the escape menu, inventory, etc. Nothing triggered it. THEN, the inventory bugged out. Equipping items to this bugged character began to disappear items. The ultimate kicker was that I couldn't even close my inventory screen by the end. I could only quit the game with alt+f4.How embarrassing to release a game in this state.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty disappointed overall for this game.  I'm just entering Denver and my squad is about level 11.  Things that suck:  Overall the game has zero polish.  It's a real kick in the nuts if you're used to quality titles like Divinity 1 or 2.  Stats don't have tooltips to explain them (what does perception do?).  Using the mouse is clunky, if you use the shrink grenade - good luck trying to click on an enemy if it is on the same square as literally anything else.  The voice acting is horrendous, I'm pretty sure they just skipped using actors and asked for volunteers from the dev crew.  The overall story and writing is really boring and predictable.  Some powerful male king figure sends you on a mission, but then things get mysterious as he turns out to be not who he says he is and...blah blah...ok, i'm not 12, give me something new.  The combat messages appear and disappear before you can read them.If you get shot from an enemy there is a 50/50 chance you either won't see who shot you or who got shot, because the camera isn't pointing at both actors, so you kinda have to guess.If you're in your car/tank thing you can't really see if you're near radiation until it is too late, and then you have a squad with 24% less hp then 2 seconds ago. It's like a game that had some juvenile ideas, was hobbled together with a lot of obvious time and money saving corners cut, and kind of crapped out this pretty lame experience.  I saw a robotic statue of a US president melt a robot and kinda lost interest completely.  Like...we get it, you think Americans are idiots and we worship ourselves and violence.  Social commentary is ok, but the way it's presented in this game is just overdone, and quite honestly if I were a red state person I'd probably be a little offended by their obvious and relentless mockery.The lore books I have no interest in reading.  There are too many ammo types, like I don't want to keep track of 10+ ammo types and constantly sell 100's of useless weapons.  Targeting is clunky and often broken.  The UI is hard to understand, and never really explained.  Why have quickslots if you can just go to the inventory and drag the item into the quickslot DURING combat with no ap penalty?  Just give us 5 quickslots.  It's that kind of dev-blind player experience that really has me thinking twice about playing this game anymore.  Then you have stupid AI.  Where in Divinity you have a party of 4 and none of them will walk over say...fire on the ground.  In this game you have a party of 6 + 3 animals and they all die because you forgot to unselect them all and they stupidly run right through the fire, or ice spray or whatever...so it's another reload...Got a grenade?  Watch it get thrown in a stupid nonsensical arc up through the ceiling and then back down through it a second time, only to do a nonsensical amount of damage.   Using a sniper rifle?  Watch yourself shoot the 2 foot high barrier in front of you like a moron.  Got 10 strength and a cool fist weapon?  Watch yourself hit like a wet noodle and realize unarmed is broken.  Use a molotov cocktail?  Hope you don't have animals as they fearlessly run right through the burning flames and scream every turn as they burn.  Also, it's almost impossible to tell where the fire ends and a safe square begins, so you kind have to guess.Ultimately, these are all tiny issues, but combined they lead to a play experience that I just can't recommend.  The game needs a lot more polish.  It wasn't ready for release.  It was game-breaking bug free...maybe...but not polished and ready to be enjoyed.  It's in a state where an intelligent gamer is going to spend as much time moaning and groaning as leveling up...which is another tedious experience.  I'm only level 11, and that means I've leveled up 3 separate stats tabs, 11 times each, for 6 characters...that's 180 tabs of clicking a square to choose a perk or a single strength stat.  That isn't fun.  That feels like a job working for a business in the 80's when Microsoft excel was just released for the first time.  No thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very meh.It has a lot of going for it. The graphics look good, there is music, and a lot of voiced dialog (the acting can be very amusingly bad, but still). The tactical combat is also solid. There is not enough variety from fight to fight, but the core is good, and I would rank it above average for RPGs.But whenever I saw the graphics, or enjoyed the music, my thoughts were always: this is such a waste. Because the game itself is just bland. The blandness starts from the get-go. The story begins as you, a ranger (good guys) is sent to work as a mercenary for some country leader, so he gives you supplies. You are already the hero, the sole survivor, the mercenary, and also you are just following orders (of dead people), and the game didn't even start.Then there is the world building. Maybe I played too many apocalyptic games, but it really striked me as odd as nothing in the wasteland felt new in any way. How is the wasteland different than any other world you could have made? The only answer seems to be: the crazy people. Not that other games don't have crazy people, but it's that the crazy people in this game are crazy in different ways than crazy people in other games. I know I am being a little unfair because so many RPGs tend to do this, but at some point it needs to be said that just adding more new flavors of crazy to your world is the most boring kind of world-building possible. Crazy psychos are crazy psychos, and having them dress differently doesn't make the world more diverse or more interesting.The game's steam page is heavily misleading at describing the game as having a dark atmosphere. "post apocalyptic", "desperate quest", "losing fight". In practice, this game is best described as "goofy". Among themselves, wasteland's fans love the series for its goofiness, so why would you market the game as anything else? Personally, I found that occasional mass graves of recently murdered children often come in the way of  enjoying the 20-th toaster joke. Humor is subjective, after all.The RPG elements are... I don't know. You have 6 character to upgrade so you basically just need to make sure each skill is developed for 1 character so your team ends up with pretty much all the skills. It's very shallow, and very annoying, because despite being mostly trivial, you still need to upgrade skills for every one of the six characters every time they rank up, and whenever you are done ranking up and try to move screen, you get a pop-up that asks you if you are sure that you want to rank up this way. There are 6 characters, 3 pages to edit, a lot of ranks, and the game still give me this pop-up every single time I move screen. So scr@# everything else I said up until now, this is the real reason I am giving it the game thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: First, ignore all the rose-tinted review from the fanboys. I will give you impartial one from someone who is fresh to this series. This game deserves a neutral and maybe a thumb-up later if they manage to patch the so many game-breaking bugs and serious balance issues down the line. As it is, it is not really worth the price. maybe 20-30% lower would do. We have good thing here but it is lacking in many areas. Gameplay is the biggest gripe for me, as it also should be since this is a turn-based combat heavy game. Think about this as Divinity Original sin 1 but half the combat depth and un-ignorable balancing issues. Why? Let me go point by point. They seem trivial alone but when combined, you get a very accumulative annoying experience.Class/gameplay diversity is terrible: Why? You have combat stage that is mostly empty space with very little cover. This means to fight effectively, you need to shoot far and precisely, i.e. the game shoehorns you into running snipers or somewhat acceptable assault rifles. You can get away with pistol on lower difficulty but most likely, you will die before you even get into position. Enemies hit hard even on easy. Game demands preparation when it will only take a few turns before enemies start piling up on you and by the time you are ready to fight, you are wiped. So you either have to make everyone sharpshooter or have a dedicated doc with tons of med packs running around reviving (boring). Melee is useless. Unless you body block or is the only one in wide proximity surrounded by enemies, they will go after the weakest ones in your team. I mean, they will beeline to them to kill them and purposefully ignore your tank. So why even give us a tank build? There is also serious issue with stat building. Every class and spec needs to max out Coordination, i.e. forced. If you play melee, you need strength and speed. If you play gun, you need luck and awareness. If you play utility, you need intelligence and maybe leadership. Wanna play turret/engineer? Too bad every deployment costs an arm or a leg. The game does not favor hybrid and force your builds to be very one-dimensional. If you dabble, you will suck because your stat will suck and you won't have access to high level active skills that are acquired through leveling these professions. These are just the more high level examples. The game LOOKS like it has ♥♥♥♥ ton of customisations but it doesn't if you don't want to wipe the floor every turn. Compared to games like Pillars 2 or DoS2 when it comes to balancing diversity with viability, this game is terrible at it. Like I mentioned earlier, this also extends to how the level design is made to favor only certain playstyles. Level design is bland and uninspiring:Continuing on previous point, it seems the only mechanic around the battlefields boil down to a few thing: shoot this, cover here, shoot this barrel for some extra explosion. and that's about it. maybe you will land stun once or twice as CC in an encounter but that's as far as combat depth go, i.e. extremely bland. It's NOT BAD but it's not something like DoS2 or Pillars2. This game fails at the classic combat design. It favors dps creep and make tactical thinking saved for some position meaningless. In DoS2, you can manipulate the battlefield for some fantabulous battle strategy. You can't expect that here. SO. MANY. GAME-BREAKING BUGS:At some point, it will crash or freeze, or get stuck, etc. get used to it if you don't want to wait for patchesThose are some major gripes. Story is a bit short but if you play blind and try to do everything, it will be long enough. Companions are..... there but don't expect Bioware level. Game oversells on the moral choices and consequences. They are there but again somewhere inbetween Bioware and Bethesda kind of meaningful. I will give a thumb up because I think there is potential here and a lot of things can be tweaked and improved if they put effort. We'll see.
