_childDocuments_.review: A decent game, but doesn't really grab you or stick with you. Kind of like a mindless science fiction novel. Its distracting and at times mildly entertaining. There is some humor, but parts of it seem like they tried too hard to be quirky and funny. The factions and voice acting is a bit over the top in its stereotypes and often pretty cringeworthy. Companions are fairly shallow characters, yet to have a full team you have to include two of them. While there is choice that affects the ending, and while those choices attempted to create a morally gray area that made you think, I didn't find them to be that compelling. Other games have done it far better. The gameplay is decent. X-COM style turn-based combat. Plenty of weapons and approaches to choose from. Super easy to create new builds to fit your style as you can just create new characters for your merry band, which I really liked. It was a variant of the "buy the potion to reset stats" thing which I appreciated because it could really be done at any time. No real fetch quests which is probably my favorite thing about it. While there are "side quests" they are minimal, contribute to the story, and are evenly distributed. I felt this was well-balanced and considering the load times, too many unnecessary side or fetch quests would probably doom this game. The load times complained of are not a joke. You really feel this in a few quests - I am thinking of one in particular which involves going into a building (load screen), doing maybe 20 minutes of combat, leaving the building (load screen), walking to a character and then having to return to the building (load screen) to finish the quest and then having to leave (load screen) as there is nothing else to do there. Load time is easily a real minute that feels like 5. I give it a thumbs up because I was interested enough to finish a playthrough. But, many of the negative reviews are legitimate.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm walking away very satisfied with the time I spent with Wasteland 3. I can see the flaws which have impacted some players (weird engine bugs and some issues with the combat that I'll mention), but truth be told there aren't many games like this. What made Wasteland 3 special were how the storytelling and core conflict challenged personal morality in grounded situations which ask: what would you do?The setting and factions of the game were very unique among post-apocalyptic media, and deserve a shout out. New Vegas may have popularized the term "nuclear winter," but Wasteland 3's Colorado really accentuates what that would be like to live under. Post-apocalyptic settlements built on top of pre-war structures partially buried under a perpetual snowstorm felt like my team were unearthing the ruins of an era forever lost. Colorado's overworld map was also gorgeous, and I doubt travelling between instances would have been as interesting had I not been driving around in the squad's Kodiak tank beforehand. (That tank has a variety of horns to blare while driving around btw, with my favorite being a random callback to an '80s TV show  .)Speaking of New Vegas, the factions of Colorado were as varied and fully realized as those present in Fallout's Mojave. The sadistic God-Fishers whose natural spirituality was grotesquely tied towards human sacrifice and the Reagan-worshipping Gippers were just a few unique cults who rose out of the ashes of Wasteland's apocalypse. I can't overstate just how  it was to explore the faction conflicts. I really loved that part of this experience.But Wasteland 3 wasn't perfect, even a few years after its release. I can only hope that inXile drops Unity for their next title, as the engine really struggled to meet the team's vision in my opinion. Graphical effects and the loading breaks between rather small instanced locations are areas I thought really showed the limits of using Unity as an engine. I'll preface with the usual "I'm no game designer" caveat, but the cinematic flourishes that the team used were so sparse that I can only assume they were the most difficult to work in. Think first-person Fallout-esque dialogue sequences and cinematic combat encounters, which were great inclusions I wish Wasteland 3 had more of. I also had to reload some combat encounters when enemy turns would stall, which was a bug I'd encountered in other Unity cRPG's like Wasteland 2, Pathfinder: Kingmaker, and Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous. These combined problems were annoying, but not deal-breakers for my experience. Unity simply can't handle the talent and vision inXile has moved to, it's as simple as that.Overall, Wasteland 3 was a huge step up from Wasteland 2 in just about every way. Some complexity was sacrificed to streamline the experience from the previous title, and I missed having a combat log in the corner while playing this game. But I was hooked to Wasteland 3 from the get-go and couldn't wait to see how things played out. I couldn't say the same for Wasteland 2, which didn't have nearly the level of writing this game had. I strongly recommend at least the base game for Wasteland 3: it gave me an experience I hadn't had since playing New Vegas for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, but it has way too many bugs for being out for 2 years or more. Game-breaking bugs that prevent you from being able to play it. Bugs that, after combat, I can't control any character anymore and can't even initiate combat to see if that fixes it, as the enemies place me in the combat state but don't actually do anything and get stuck in their turn. This bug also requires you to completely relaunch the game in order to fix it, as the game gets stuck reloading a save if you try to fix it that way. Plenty of smaller bugs too. Characters during combat getting stuck behind doors that are open and being unable to walk through them until you open them again (despite the door being open). Characters losing AP randomly, or teleporting to different places when ordering them to move. Weird audio bugs where the audio cuts out randomly, though this tends to happen mostly during the introductory sequence.But even beyond those bugs, the game has some frustrating rng elements that seem unfair. Playing on the hardest difficulty, I understand that the AI is going to get a bunch of random, unfair bonuses and buffs. They have way more health, do way more damage, etc. What I don't expect or enjoy is when, out of 10 attacks that have roughly 90% hit chance (up to 95%), 6 of those attacks whiff. I don't expect or enjoy that happening much more often than it statistically should. The challenge of the hardest difficulty is fun. It's fun to build a balanced team of specialists that can take advantage of situations and get through skill checks. It's not fun to run into rng that seems like it's lying to you. I have only played the hardest difficulty, so I don't know if this is something exclusive to the hardest difficulty, but I have found that the Evasion stat often feels completely worthless. Lucia Wesson sitting behind a waist-high cover with base 43% Evasion buffed by a Defend turn end with 7 AP (which equates to 7*5%=35% bonus Evasion) still ends up getting hit multiple times and dying instantly through her cover. This seems to happen even when an enemy has had its accuracy debuffed through Demoralize, Engulfed, or Crippled. This makes Lucia Wesson, a character that is meant to be agile and get interesting angles on enemies with a high Evasion rate feel like a liability. I will reiterate that this could be due to the difficulty level I play at, but I can't say for sure.I like this game a lot. It's really interesting with deep rpg mechanics. The story and characters are great. Your choices have weight, and impact the relationships you have with other factions and the overall way people view you (the Rangers). I love the way the combat works, and take the difficulty in stride. Going from barely getting through fights to being able to reasonably handle them feels good. But dealing with bugs that unfairly make the game much harder (by cheating me of AP) or simply make it unplayable ruins all of that. I forgot up until just now, but the game also seems to (still) have a memory leak issue, where after you've played for a certain amount of time the game is liable to randomly tank fps down to the single-digits. I say "still" because apparently this has been an issue with the game since 2020, and in my experience has not been fixed. It's a crying shame, because I was looking forward to getting all the DLCs and playing through them even despite their poor reviews. I don't know if I'm even going to attempt finishing the base game at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I've nearly completed my first play through on the 2nd most difficult setting (I like a challenge and I am a "min/maxer completionist.").  My favorite PC game genres and games include RPGs and tactical turn-bused strategy... so Baldur's Gate, XCOM, Into the Breach, Dragonage, Witcher, Skyrim, Fallout (setting matters less to me than the game mechanics).  I played Wasteland 30 years ago and really enjoyed Wasteland 2 a few years ago.Wasteland 3:  PUNCHLINE:  This is an excellent game that I really enjoy.  Wonderful combination of XCOM/Divinity combat mechanics with tons of humor, throwbacks, and easter eggs and a plethora of opportunities to creatively package up different ranger profiles with different weapons, armor, and kit to build a party that can handle everything (usually).LIKE MOST:  Story, setting, characters, game play fundamentals.DISLIKE:Buginess -- I played mostly pre-patch v1.4 which fixed a lot of the most irritating bugs for me, but those bugs were really irritating (disappearing pets especially)... there were times when I didn't even know if I was experiencing bugs or if I had just made some fundamentally flawed assumption about how things should work.  There is also a bit too much wonkiness as it relates to targeting in combat and which enemies you can hit and where they can effectively hit you (especially across different vertical levels of a battlefield).My only other main beef is with the sequencing of acquiring high-end gear.  Some of the most fun weapons and armor that one can obtain shows up literally immediately before the end-game.  I get that you don't want level 27 stuff to show up in the first chapter of a story and make newb parties overpowered.  However, having the high-end stuff available so that a player has enough time and battles to enjoy it is pretty darn important and this was a big disappointment for me.  I have two suits of armor that are unambiguously the best in the game that I will likely only use in 3% of my end-to-end playthrough battles.  If this was Skyrim, that's okay because its open world... I can always invent ways to use that gear (mods, DLC's, etc.) but given there is no open world element of Wasteland 3, it is a disappointing limitation of this design.

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying the game, but as I progressed I was noticing that the game wasnt taking itself serious. At the end of the first mission I recruited an NPC cat that wears a ranger hat. Later a chicken, and a goat. At the mid late to late game game I recruited a golden toaster that shoots what I think are fireballs, a disco ball that shoots, and some strange Golem creature that speaks like a child... It was pretty stupid. From what I gathered lore wise, Desert Rangers are supposed to be severe bad asses like Clint Eastwood but with bigger guns, however, the selection of starting rangers didn't give that impression at all. The impression you will get is that the starting two characters are just some hitchhikers you picked up on your way to Colorado. They also dont have anything meaningful to say that adds to their personalty like some of the recruits you will encounter throughout the story.From the selection of recruits that you encounter, only one fits the Ranger persona. A former Colorado deputy. You will also encounter an engineer who makes as a good soldier perhaps but not a friggen Ranger. A little girl with a huge Mexican hat that is supposed to be like a desperado I think? A shotgun wielding hillbilly drunkard that doesnt belong, an evil psychopath  warband leader that should be shot on site, a goody two-shoes green mutant female ranger (She hulk without the muscles), an evil fist fighting cyborg former warlord, and a raider cannibal. Thats your selection and none of them can be taken seriously as Ranger material. You dont have to recruit any of them and infact you can kill all of them from first meeting them or on the battlefield, but you NEED at least half of them to make it through the game or you will die.There is no Game+ mode where you can continue with your endgame characters for a new and higher difficulty play through. Huge mistake on the developers part as it takes away fro the replay value tremendously. Weapon selection is pretty good, nice variety even though some of them retain that unwelcome cartoony feature to them like a rifle with a kitchen microwave attached to the end of it, or a "shrink gun" that does exactly what it sounds like. The armor does what armor is supposed to do, but the designs are bland and uninspiring. A big swing and a miss is the weapon and armor mods. The biggest complaint is that you cant unattach these mods. Once your use them that's it you cant get it back to use on better armors/weapons you come across. Some of these mods you will only come across once or twice in the game as well. Most of the late game mods come with such a severe penalty to stats that you will be left wondering if you are better off using the mid or early game mods. This has the consequence of leaving you wondering if you wasted valuable skill points in the weapon or armor modding skill tree.Combat gameplay is good. I like how it mimics the XCOM franchise as this is exactly what I was looking for and the reason I bought this game. What I wasn't looking for was all the goofyness. Where are all the real Rangers at? The tactical elite warriors I was expecting to play as. The rangers that know they will win the battle and not make weak comments like "We made it?!" after a simple battle. I can tell that a lot of effort was made to make this a great game, but it misses the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: (CW: Very mild spoilers)This game definitely gets the thumbs up, but I would recommend waiting a few months or a year to play it. The game is still riddled with bugs, none of which halted my progress, but there were quests that couldn't be completed, companions that simply despawned, never to be seen again, and so many reasons to spam quicksave in case the game decided to softlock or pathing caused one of your team members to run into the trap instead of disarming it when you clicked on it, among other things.The story is alright, but I found that most of the companions weren't compelling - do I want cannibals or otherwise despicable people joining my party? No, but I guess that's a personal preference. And, trying not to spoil anything, but the companion's choices at the end of the game seemed completely arbitrary and unpredictable given how they behaved right up until the end.The other thing this game needs is a *lot* of quality of life improvements. Inventory management is a nightmare, and the sorting could really use improvement. Weapon stripping takes *forever*. Load times are really, really bad. Items that boost skills cause skills to cost more to level up, so you have to take off your items before you bump your skills, which is just tedious. Companions block player-controlled characters, so if your characters randomly position themselves around your characters before a fight starts, your melee character is stuck doing literally nothing waiting for your companions turn to come up (seriously, you need to be able to run through your companions). The map was also simply too big for how much content it contained, and a lot of time is spent tediously running around. Also the game really felt like it lacked end-game weapon upgrades for most characters - endgame armor was cool (and looked great), but most of my weapons peaked like 2/3 through the game. Maybe this is to prepare for DLC or something, who knows.Difficulty scaling seems mostly well done, playing on the Hard difficulty I had to continue to strategize to win even towards the end when I had optimized my characters, though no fights were particularly difficult. What was extremely disappointing was how easy the final fight was - it was seriously one of the easiest fights in the entire game and a total let-down. I figured that my choices earlier to armor the patriarch's troops would come back to bite me, but nope, the patriarch has like 4 guards you can just run over with your truck.My final complaint was the music. My god was the music bad. Maybe if hollow, low-fi, gospel and children's music is your thing you'll enjoy it, but I certainly did not.All that said, I did really enjoy this game. It presented a good challenge, and offered plenty to explore and tough decisions to make. Very worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: The Wasteland series carries a heavy legacy. The original Wasteland is one of the great classics of PC gaming, having pioneered the nuclear post-apocalyptic setting and heavily inspired the Fallout series. The first sequel, released during the Kickstarter fueled cRPG renaissance, was also a respectable game. The promise of a return to Wasteland's world and the hope of an even better installment certainly had me interested from the get-go. Still, I somehow managed to wait a good 2 year before playing this game. I really don't know how I manage to always be this late. Well, better late than never as they say. Let's see if this second sequel does justice to the name it bears.The plot picks up shortly after the end of the previous game. The Arizona Rangers are still licking their wounds following their showdown with Cochise and his synth army. The unforgiving wasteland does not offer much respite. Food and resources are low and a tough winter is approaching. Desperate, the Ranger command cuts a deal with the powerful potentate of Colorado, a figure known as the Patriarch. In return for the Rangers capturing his wayward children, the Patriarch offers Arizona regular convoys of aid. Team November is assigned to see the mission through. Another chapter in the Rangers' chronicle is about to begin. Should November fail, it could be their last.The setting of the game is strong. The snowy expanses of Colorado are a refreshing take on the wasteland. An endless snowstorm seems to be raging over the irradiated ranges of the Rockies and makes them feel even more desolate and inhospitable than the hottest desert of the west. There are numerous factions to be found in the various locations that dot the map, many interesting characters to interact with and, unsurprisingly, various madmaxesque gangs roaming the land to fight. All of them quite interesting. Perhaps a bit too tongue-in-cheek sometimes, but interesting. From a gang of crazy clowns convinced the world is a joke, to brutal crazies that cut people to pieces and fly them on kites, to... well, Santa Claus.There isn't too much focus on the main plot. It has enough meat to make it memorable, which is more than I can say for the plot of the previous game, but it clearly plays second fiddle to the setting. I am fine with that. I am also very appreciative of how gray the world is. Unlike previous games there is no evil AI that needs to be stopped in order to save the world. Just groups of people representing different shades of gray, with a pinch of black. Maybe the Patriarch is a despot, but he also provides stability and the Rangers need his help to survive. Maybe the rogue Rangers calling for his overthrow have a point, but their moral absolutism and shortsightedness may cause a lot more suffering than it spares. November has few easy choices ahead of them.The presentation of the game is another highlight. The cold wasteland aesthetic that defines the setting enhances all visual aspects of the game. Their clothes and armour, as well as the tank the Rangers use to travel, are all quite striking. The interface icons, starring a retro robot, deserve some special mention for their consistency and humour. The sound and voice acting is also generally on point. Still, there is one final element here that stands above the rest. Music. The soundtrack is simply put phenomenal and greatly adds to the atmosphere. The game contains interesting performances of many great songs. From actual American folk classics to songs that should have been American folk classics. It was always a pleasure when one of those started playing.So, is the game perfect? Not quite. Unfortunately, there are some pretty serious flaws too. For starters there is the bugs. One of the benefits of often playing games a few years after their release is that I get to avoid the early unpatched versions. Wasteland 3 has had 2 years and 2 DLCs, yet still is anything but bug-free. I encountered plenty. From purely cosmetic ones like my tank turning into a question mark on the map, to more serious ones like my UI disappearing and not letting me play or even quit, to my Rangers starting to drift funnily on the screen. Thankfully they were fairly rare. The most serious of them didn't occur more than once or twice throughout my run. But still, it's been 2 years. Come on.Either way, my strongest complaint concerns combat balance. Early on, combat is engaging and fun, but as the game progresses it becomes apparent there is something not quite right. First, armour is practically useless. You got a power armour? Oh well, the mook with the plasma rifle will cut through it as if it was your old pajamas anyway. Add in to that the relative fragility of the Rangers and the game basically becomes a race. Lose the initiative and you are toast. It doesn't help that all late enemies are damage sponges with hitpoints in the thousands. A number of pretty unfair fights near the end feel particularly grating. To be fair, the combat system is still fine for the most part, but balancing and the endgame totally needed more work.In the end, do I recommend Wasteland 3? For fans of the genre the answer is categorically yes. The setting and atmosphere alone would be enough to make this a worthwhile experience. The fact that it also plays reasonably well, for the most part, is the semi-delicious cherry on top. I consider it a clear improvement over the previous iteration and I am curious to see where inXile can take the series to next. Of course, now that they've been gulped down by Microsoft maybe they won't take it anywhere. But I do hope we'll see more and I am patient enough to wait.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single farther to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just, watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. loaded into the game, made my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. loved it as it was the best time had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories

_childDocuments_.review: Please note this is purely for the base game with no dlc's. (the dlc's are far worse)W3 is an post-apocalyptic  game that doesnt take itself very seriously. So very few games bother with it and I dont know why. +500 points- Skill points checks (fixed requirements for skill checks) instead of the ol' RNG skill checks. +200 points- Different perk system. +50 pointsCons:- Bugs. Bugs. More bugs!! Would you like to know more? -999 points- Goofy things that break immersion. -300 points- Sometimes the dialogue is so stupid you want to bathe your eyes in boiling oil. -100 points- Devs was obsessed with cramming as many references into the game (and not subtle) as possible, breaking immersion. -100 points- Unrealised potential. -0 points. -999 my own soul pointsAll in all the game can be played on discount and if you can stand the tide of bugs, but even though I somehow managed to finish the game I dont want to recommend this buggy mess.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.69/10 : Very pleasant experience :D-----------------------------------------------So one day, DOS2, XCOM, and fallout decided to have a threesome, and thus this game was born!This game is like a salad. There's a THING for everyone, which is really nice!We got the DOS2 exploration system We got the grid style turn-based combat from XCOM (and covers)We got the "post-apocalyptic America" Vibes from fallout (and the point system/skill checks)and of course, freakin Dungeons and Dragons reference!----------------------------------------------------------------------Is this game nice? oh yes it is! Worth the price? sure sure!However, having played DOS2 before, I can't help but be kinda biased. You see I prefer games that have nice soundtrack/music, and don't get me wrong, this game's OST IS really NICE. There's just one nitpick:IT DIDN'T PLAY OFTEN ENOUGH. It mostly only plays on boss fights and or certain moments, as compared to DOS2 which is music ALL the time. Most of the time the music (I kinda feel like) dim and or lacking, like it's too silent. I get that it's supposed to be post-apocalyptic, therefore being ambient, but somehow, I kinda don't like it (it's kind of a subjective matter) which is why I don't give this game full score.That nitpick aside, this game is just awesome. I'm having fun and I will definitely try to 100% it if possible. What it lacks from DOS2 music, kinda made up by the good writing/story. I definitely recommend anyone to try this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game. It's a well-made, humorous game with good voice acting. I bought it on sale, but I think it's worth the full price. It was worth it even for those 5 hours that I played.I had doubts about turn-based combat because I thought it's the cheap cop-out way to program if you can't program good AI. It might be true, but the turn-based combat surprisingly doesn't really distract from the game. It's more of an... adventure game I guess? Or a party-based adventure-RPG game? It's not meant to be played like Diablo, it's more exploratory. But there are plenty of little funny details, jokes, funny stereotypes that are well-executed and cause a smile.I'd say, why not? Costs the same as a couple of burgers or whatever, but you get to enjoy it for a number of hours, probably 20+ hours if you wanted to.

_childDocuments_.review: This is realy a hard one. Because on one hand, Wasteland 3 isn`t a bad RPG. Actually it basicly has what it takes to be a good one. But for whatever reason a design decision was made to make this more interesting for the Diablo player who is looking for that quick dopamin fix of finding cool new loot in a container, then for an actual roleplaying fan who is looking for immersion. Therefor loot got randomized. People dont have on them what seconds ago they used to try and kill you. Oh, and because all that cool new loot you randomly can get needs ever increasing numbers in damage, of course the enemies need ever increasing numbers of hitpoints to counter that. So it doesn`t take long and you meet people who have 3 times as much HP as even your maxed out tank has, killing immersion even more. Want an example. My maxed out tank currently has around 300HP at around level 10. I guess he will be maxed out at around 500-600 I guess. My normal chars have around 80-120 HP now and probably around 120-250 when maxed. One of the nscs I just met had over 12k. Thats 12 0 0 0. So you wanna tell me that a normal person can have 10 times the hitpoints as my whole party AND the tank we are driving around in? That`s just a load of crap.And I`m not complaining about the game being hard, because it isn`t because as said the weapons just rapidly scale in damage. I complain that someone decided to market a game from a series that was one of the first PC RPGs to the wrong crowd. Basicly every container in the game becomes a lootbox. If you wanna find a game that makes this better, play Colony Ship for example. There everyone you meet is build using the same ruleset. So when you meet someone, they do the same damage as you, they take the same damage as you and they have the same equipment (for example consumables) then you and will use them, forcing you to use them aswell if you dont already have an edge over them because your crew is consisting mainly of combat veterans. If there will ever be a Wasteland 4 (and I hope there will be one) then hopefully the devs remember to create an immersive RPG first, a tactical game second and a numberinflating lootbox game not at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland is the 1980's style post-apocalypse to Fallout's 1950's retro-future aesthetic. It also built as a party based RPG instead of classic Fallout's Lone Survivor plus AI (Artificial Imbecile) controlled teammates. Overall a great game. Combat is fun, there are a lot of ways to build and kit out your party, with a lot of absurd weapons and gear to give you stuff to play with beyond the "does +5 energy damage" or "gives 3% poison resist when under 25% health" nonsense that a lot of modern RPGs fall into. Character creation system is not as inflexible as it may at first appear, just specialize each of your mains in 4 skills each max, use all the different weapon classes,  remember to find and use the skill books to buy the last most expensive skill levels, and know that points in intelligence are never a waste. Story is also good, with lots of shades of grey around the various factions, making it much less obvious how to always "do the right thing". It is a little crashy, so apply "save" liberally.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Wasteland 2 in almost every area. Beat the game on supreme jerk, seems like the game was balanced with that in mind, nothing really seemed damage spongy, if you know what you're doing you can end most engagements within 2 turns if you get the drop on your targets. Otherwise it's a lot of your team getting wiped out. Story is good, spoilers aside I actually like that it can end exactly like you'd expect. Buchanan is a man of his word, if nothing else. All of that said, the UI is the buggiest feature of the game, I ignored the issues and didn't have any actual crashes or quest breaking or game-breaking bugs. To people unsure I'd say wait about a year for all the kinks to get worked out. If you liked 2 you'll probably like this more.Solid 8/10, would play again, Morningstar is best carfu.

_childDocuments_.review: What should be the sucessor of post apocalyptic RGP W2 turned out into an arcade RPG.If you, like me, felt in love with W2 then this game is NOT for you. Lets get into some features:*weightless items. As you read, bullets, weapons, ammo, consumables, and so on no longer represent  addition to be very inmmersion breking, this leads to a much more simplistic gameplay: Aim>shoot>win>end combat>loot repeat. Tactical thinking is completely absent now. You no longer need to think how many "mags" will your rifleman carry, how many medkits or other items because now you can carry all the animals in Noah Ark*2 and you will not feel the weight.*no permadeath. At least at the beggining of the game (dont know now a days) rangers no longer have permadeath. In the same way as in the previous point, we mentioned that this breaks the immesion, it should be noted that the role of "doctor" is now useless. Any ranger, by magic, can lift a partner, develop medical skills? For what? even a wolf could lift you up*Kodiac (the vehicle). I assume that many of us looked foward with this feature. The kodiac is a vehicle devoid of emotions. It has a turret with infinite ammunition and is almost indestructible. It does not generate the affective attachment, which, for example, the Highwayman of the F2 had. It is an element that tips the balance at your side in many battles, a seventh companionI could go on but I prefer to focus on the most important points. Im looking foward for Inxile to develop a HARDCORE MODE where all this points are addresed properly, otherwhise, I would advice for future buyers, if you are looking for a hobby while your girlfriend is taking a bath, go for W3

_childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is a great successor to Wasteland 2, which itself was a great successor to Fallout 1 and 2.  This is what the Fallout series should have become, and I'm glad to see Brian Fargo continuing the series that inspired Fallout in the first place!However, given how long they spent developing it, and that it was in backer beta testing for a long time, the game is surprisingly buggy (which itself is a callback to the Fallout games).  Doors that were open will be closed when you go back to them, but the game will still treat them as open (i.e. you can walk through them, but can't re-open them).  Some traps don't have the right disarm UI with them. The pause function, which would be quite useful (even the menu doesn't pause the game), was removed, but the keybind option is still there. Some of the achievements don't work according to their descriptions. So far, I've found no game-breakers, but most of these bugs should have been really obvious in any testing!Despite the bugs, though, this is a great RPG!
_childDocuments_.name: Wasteland 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of the few gems that let's you actually control the story. For example, you can try to kill a main character the first time you meet them without asking questions, but it's a matter of if you live through the encounter. (Meeting the Patriarch outside  of future Ranger HQ for example).The game hands you all the mechanics for managing your fame and reputation and let's you go wild. I didn't notice any problems with the game not pointing me in the right direction during my playthrough.Combat is fun and fairly well balanced, melee seems to be lacking but that could be due to me not gearing my characters for some good ole' CQC.Leveling is handled very well, with the game explaining to you in full what each perk, skill, and trait does as you level upGenuinely just all around fun, kept me up way later than it should of far too many times.Only two really bad things I picked up on, The soundtrack being utterly wasted and the game seemingly unable to get a handle on how much comedy is too much comedy. Starting with the soundtrack, only some combats trigger something besides the usual lackluster combat music, when these few combats occur, that one battle feels much more significant than any of the others around it. This comes at a cost of most combats being just a fairly enjoyable battle of you using your squad to survive or shred against the enemy depending on the difficulty you chose. It feels like a huge waste, having some really good songs but keeping them constrained to important battles, especially when the default music is so incredibly weak in comparison, it's genuinely like comparing a city apartment to a mansion. (Big spoilers)> . Second is how much trouble the game has taking it seriously, I'm fine with everyone game having a joke here and there to give you a chuckle, like running into a goat in a brothel with a bucket and a note reading '10$', or (Spoilers)> . But it takes it and runs waaay further than it should some times, the goat cannon you can get for the truck being a perfect example, it's a fairly solid weapon, but it shoots an actually goat. It's hard to get into the "We must complete our mission or our home is screwed and doomed to fail" vibe when you're firing goats at your enemy in a gorilla costume while your character is smaller than the weapon they're holding. You can avoid all of this sure, but they are just examples for a general theme the game has.This game is less and less stable the longer you play it. It's not bad enough to warrant being called bad as a few bugs here and there aren't world ending, but the game will soft lock combat or crash once you get near the end of the game.I realize now the bad section is a lot longer than the good, don't get me wrong I love this game, I just feel strongly about the two major flaws and I feel they constantly degrade the rest of the experience by being what feels easy fixes if the devs would let people mod the game. Thanks for reading and uhhh drink water and consume nutrients thanks

_childDocuments_.review: Brian Fargo did it again - an excellent tactical CRPG, the real Fallout 3, but with a big influence from Fallout Tactics (I guess someone could not like that part).The game took a core gameplay of Wasteland 2, improved it's RPG system a lot, added some more variety from Torment: Tides of Numenera and excellent musical numbers from Bard's Tale IV and the result is an excellent game on all levels - atmosphere, gameplay, roleplay, everything is top-notch.Sadly, while overall the game feels great, it's also kinda flawed, and those flaws are also coming from the previous games by inXile - Unity here is pretty clumsy, poorly optimized and resulting visuals are quite mediocre. Loading time are quite depressing (NVME doesn't help at all). The loot system is plagued by useless junk items - there are like 100 types of different junk items, and almost all of them are completely useless and are just for sale. The game interface, at least by PC standards, is an unusable garbage, made for console peasants (probably would be fine if you want to play it with a gamepad).The thing is - inXile is making a great games, with very strong narratives, dubious moral choices and pretty strong core gameplay and RPG systems. The issue is that those guys aren't too good at techincal stuff. And if you would find peace with all those relatively small flaws, you would get yourself about 50 hours of excellent game (I've just went to a second walkthrough, but the initial one took about 50h).

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Buggy and release price is expensive but I got 63 hours from my run through, which works out to less than $1 per hour of solid entertainment. If you know you like the genre, this will probably scratch an itch - though the ending may leave you cold.(Played on PC with i7, 16 GB RAM, GeForce 2080 RTX)Pros:- satisfying combat system, mostly (could have done with more variation in tactical scenarios) - looks purdy (on high default settings)- lots of voice acting- meaningful story decisions- silly, gonzo but on-the-mark humour - fun!Cons:- long loading screens between map areas and annoying map design sometimes requiring 2-3 loading screens to traverse areas  - more bugs than an entomology convention (though mostly minor)- inventory system needs work - colour palette seems buggy during character customisation - combat maps and camera can get messy EDIT: Just finished the game... distinct sense of 'meh'. Have to say that the journey was far better than the destination as the ending was lacklustre both in terms of a final combat encounter (literally completed in two turns, zero adrenaline) and the paltry story wrap-up. I can see that there are probably lots of alternative endings but it didn't leave me wanting to replay the game to discover them. I would still recommend this game but I'd have to suggest waiting for a later date when the bugs are all patched out. Would have graded it 8/10 during play, dropping to 7/10 after completing. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very buggy at the moment. Not surprised really. I am a little disappointed that I didn't wait. Currently, the game feels like it needs another solid six months of polish. Also, the loading screens are way, way too long--not sure if they can fix this issue though.Sample of some bugs I've encountered so far:Bugs aside, the game controls somewhat poorly. It feels janky--and sometimes controlling characters can be problematic. There is no way to toggle a slower movement speed, and I don't believe there is a key to "stop" squad members. Consequently, I've triggered more traps than I would have liked to . The jank is most obvious when characters are "taking cover." They don't actually hug the object they're hiding behind, and any time they use a "end turn" action they will move away from the cover and then slam back up to the cover. No idea why devs decided to do this. It would look and feel so much better if the icon just popped up over the ranger head while they were hunkered down instead of the wonky, disjointed movements they currently perform. I'm enjoying the story and quests so far. It's not the best story I've ever seen, but I have a weakness for post-apocalyptic settings. Leaving this review as a negative for now. I might switch later if we see some improvements to combat and overall polish--especially bug removal.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this is a proper top-down Fallout 3 we never got. The game feels like a mix of Fallout 1/2 and Jagged Alliance 2 (you have a team of different rangers), and this is just great. Maybe that's because I didn't have high hopes for the game after Wasteland 2 (that I didn't finish), but Wasteland 3 is a really solid RPG on its own and totally manages to deal with that post-apocalyptic turn-based RPG itch we all have from time to time.The writing, the characters, the locations, the missions – everything is as good as it can be in an RPG. The world is interesting to explore, the main quests offer at least two ways to solve them, and generally the game is totally worth the second playthrough since there's a lot of situations that could resolve differently based on your previous actions. So in terms of actual role-playing, this is definitely a plus.Combat and balancing might be on a weak side (I was playing on ranger, i.e. hard, and the fights were rather trivial, especially in the second half of the game). Maybe that's because I was building a balanced party (by the end I had a specialist in almost every skill), but maybe that's just a balancing issue. On the other hand, the game punishes for mistakes, and enemies can easily one shot even rangers wearing the toughest armor, so I wouldn't say the game is a walk in a park. No, you still have to level up your skills and hunt for better gear, it's just that battles didn't feel like I was barely making it (unlike Divinity Original Sin, for instance). Moreover, som of the battles are a tad repetitive, though it's obvious the developers tried to create as many unique encounters as possible even within each location.If the combat and balancing are arguably weak, the pathfinding and optimization are plain bad. Sometimes the game dropped to 10-20 fps with 100% GPU load (on 3080Ti!@1440p), and stayed that way until loading a new location or a save game, so there's definitely a memory leak here and there. And pathfinding is just horrible: characters often go into traps and mines and set them off instead of disarming. Thankfully, this happens only during exploration (which is real time), and you have much better control over your rangers in combat which is turn based.But other than that, I think the game is near perfect for Fallout fans. And, best of all, it ends just when you are about to get bored with it (at least that's the case for me: the game ended exactly when I was becoming tired of it). All in all, I totatlly recommend it. Definitely one of the best classic party RPGs in the recent years.P.S. It's in the Humble Choice until January 3rd, and that's why I got it in the first place. Thanks Humble!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 60 hours and doing every side quest i could find, ive beaten Wasteland 3. The story was pretty good and i felt like my decisions actually made a impact. The game felt a little unfinished and buggy though. Almost always when i selected a character to move in combat, they wouldn't walk to the way-point normally, but instead would kinda t-pose with no walking animation. This occurred a lot and looked really lame. The AI for enemies during combat was atrocious as well. When it was a enemies turn, they would take almost 10 seconds sometimes to attack, and during a fight with a ton of enemies you can see how this could get annoying. The enemy health scaling on normal mode was pretty weird as well, with some low-class enemies having around a thousand health sometimes at character lvl25. On the good side, i always had plenty of interesting weapons and armor to find, and there were a lot of Easter eggs hidden which made exploring fun. If you like games like fallout and divinity then i would recommend this game to you, although i wouldn't buy this game at full price until they patch all the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about as bugged as everyone describes it. But I still really loved playing it. It's an excellent co-op RPG. It's definitely unique. I was very satisfied with the choices and the dilemmas in the game- we often had to stop and discuss what we wanted to do and why. And that's awesome. In the world of Fallout 3, 4, and Skyrim, this level of story telling and quest variability is so rare. This was definitely on the New Vegas level for me, for the most part.Like I mentioned before, it is buggy in multiplayer. We had to restart several times. But we never lost a save or anything. Just be sure you know where the quicksave button is. Lol. Sometimes we'd play and have zero issues, sometimes we had to restart several times a session. Either way, we never really got set back too far and it wasn't that big of a deal to us. The story was interesting enough to keep us going to the very end. I love this game. Without the bugs, it'd be a 10/10 easy. But even with the bugs, 8.5-9/10 would still be a valid score, in my opinion. This is fun to play with a friend and it would be just as good to play alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most sophisticated and deep RPG I ever played. The story was engaging. The decissions that you make change the ending dramatically, the dialogues of the NPC pop them to life. You can of course skip this all and go striaght for combat. To me this game is a mix between Fallout series and XCom Series. Absolutely fantastic. I never played Wasteland 2 , or the Original. But the story is sufficiently well written in a way that you don't need to know what happened to follow. The game is full of little easter eggs with references to shows like Star Trek and Arrested Development. Even if veiled and quite hidden (such as the name of a character, or a certain description of an object). The game is well designed in the sense that you can make it work any way you want, although you have to work around it. You can choose to RP the most difficult encounters and it's probably the game with the most replayability that I ever seen. I have only completed it twice and despite I "only" played 130 hours , I can't wait to start all over again with a higher difficulty setting. The game allows this level of choice of how casual or how hard you want it to be. I absolutely love this game and I can't recommend enough for anyone to play it. 9/10. The reason I don't give this a full 10 is because sadly it has quite a few glitches, most of them are solved keeping frequent saves and reloading, or loading from previous points. That's the only thing I disliked, but I didn't mind it that much nor prevented me from having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with and enjoy the Wasteland franchise this game is a must play. _childDocuments_.review: Wasteland 3 is a fully competent, if somewhat uneven, tactical RPG. If you're on the fence about tactical, turn based games, I worry this one won't hold your interest. The tactical combat system implemented here has good roots, but isn't always fully engaging in the moment. It usually isn't difficult to win the fight directly in front of you, but you have to be aware what resources you've used so that you're ready for the next fight. The fights when you are asked to balance immediate gain with long term loss of firepower are where the game really comes alive. Unfortunately, those moments grow less common as you get further into the endgame and begin amassing an abundance of consumables and cash. For a game set in a Borderlands style, apocalyptic future, the ending is surprisingly mature. The problem is that the game doesn't fully embrace its somber side. The skeleton of this story is an excellent western style tragedy, but the presentation is marred with numerous, embarrassingly flat comedic moments.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is special. Maybe in very weird ways and sometimes underwhelming at things it absolutely shouldnt be. But this game has absolutely captured something very special in its narrative. You can just scroll through reviews and see people go absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ over which ending is the correct one or 'good' one. People are so mad, excruciated that no matter what, sacrafices have to be made. You can't save everyone. You can't satisfy everyone. But will you hold onto the reason you came to Colorado? When you see everything thats going on here. The truth behind the little piece of civilization, that is heaven compared to the world ridden with cannibals, psychopaths, slavers and monsters. Would act out of love if it results in suffering? Would you act out of hate to satify justice? The baseline question was never who is right or wrong in Colorado. It is how do you percieve it? Who do you prioritize? And can you really fault anyone for doing what they think is right? Want to get really frustrated at hard decisions, with satisfying, gory combat? Want to enjoy one of the best OSTs of the modern era, while wondering if you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and wasted 1000 of innocents lives to get your way? Can you endure a little jank and the slight suspicion the last 15% of the game needed a month or two more in the oven? If yes then this is one of the most fun gaming experience you will have. I adore this game. I hate that it just so so narrowly missed on the opportunity to be considered a modern classic. But my god this game is filled with love and detail. Ambitious, brave, genius at moments. I can only recommend trying it. Because even if it is not your cup of tea. If it turns out it is, you will have a game thats gonna have you thinking for days.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 50.1 hours into the game now, just finished it in the Ranger (hard) difficulty. It is one of the most punishing and rewarding experiences I have ever had in games.Compared to Wasteland 2 this one could be considered smaller in map size and quests BUT, it isn't; every single NPC has a voice and some of them can even talk to you face to face. The immersive aspects of this game are crazy.They excluded some useless skills that its predecessor had (for example: lockpicking X safecracking, surgeon X first aid, assault rifles X smgs, etc) and combined it, now if you pick lockpicking you will also be able to crack safes, and so on an so forth. This is a .  choices  matter. The combat feels insanely fluid. In Wasteland 2 it was kind of clunky, but this time they nailed it. A single fight can and will have infinite outcomes depending on how you position your party or in which kind of characters you have builded up.Afterall it really is an upgrade compared to Wasteland 2, and I llove that game.In these 50 hours I have encountered 2 bugs: For some reason my ending screen froze, but I was promptly helped by one of the devs, who helped me fixing it (he also said that it will be fixed for good in the next patch) (It was fixed!). The other bug was more recurrent, when sometimes when a moving NPC would slide (like skateboarding) to the desired location.As said before, your choices will punish you later on, and many times the later income of your choices will disappoint you, but like real life, you do some stuff thinking you are doing good just to discover you committed mass muder. But for me, this is a pro, not really a con. We are playing a  for godsake. I don't regret a single second refunding Cyberpunk 77 and picking this game up. It was a hell of an experience and now I am going to fight my way through Supreme Jerk difficulty (hardest) and getting all achvs like I did for W2.Ps.: Oh, and  Reagan.Pps.:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious. You'll say things out loud that have no business being said, just to make sense of what you're seeing. A few examples of things I've said in a discord chat whilst playing this game:"I just fired a rocket into a crowd of refugees." - To which the reply was "Based.""My parrot just told someone that they're the worst ♥♥♥♥ their mother ever took, and then killed them.""Ronald Reagan just wiped my squad.""One of my Rangers is now a male pornstar."Now, all that silliness aside, this game has probably the best story in a game I've ever played. The voice acting does not let that story down in any way at all. Every character is voiced brilliantly, and basically all of them are unique, or appear so. Only downside for the voice work I'd say is a fair number of repeated lines. The music is sensational, I don't know what else to say.The gameplay is similar to games such as XCOM, with an action points driven turn based combat system that people familiar with it would recognise and pick up very quickly. If you like that kind of system, you'll probably like this game, as it does it well, not brilliantly, but well.Character customization is fairly in-depth, but not overwhelming by any stretch of the imagination. Just faces, hair, hair colour, armour, hats, voice, etc. Nothing massive in the visual regard, but in terms of what the characters in your squad can actually do, there's a lot. Your characters skills, perks, and attributes are of vital importance to your squads effectiveness.Look, I don't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do reviews, I can't do one that does this game justice, just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ buy it and play it, on Ranger difficulty, you ♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of these types of games, Wasteland 3 is a must have. I started playing it and I was already hooked in an instance. It is easy to understand and get into gameplaywise and storywise that you do not need to play the previous games. The world feels cool, the atmosphere is nice, it flows super well, but again you need to be a fan of this style of game or it might not do it for you. The cons about the game I would say is that early game choices are very simple by if you save one person the other one dies and vise-versa, the game tries to show you that you can't save everyone and no choice is black or white because the later choices get a lot more complex and have much bigger repercussions, however I do wish and think they could have shown that  in a better way. Additionally certain quests will trigger even if you don't do them because they are time sensitive even if they don't tell you. It makes sense when two parties ask you to save them and you can only save one, but for example to keep it as spoiler free as possible, I was in the middle of a side quest that wasn't time sensitive and a NPC contact me to help them with something shady and I declined, their response was that they will wait for me if I change my mind so I continued finishing the quest I was on and then decided to go to the area where I had other quest and thought to stop by where that person asked me to go, maybe I can convince them or stop them from doing what they planned and when I got there, it was already too late, they killed everyone there, before I entered the area I still had the quest to go there to meet with them and talk which disappeared once I entered. It was strange I tried reloading a much earlier save I didn't overwrite and got to the same point and I stopped the quest I was doing at the time, went to the area and everyone was alive and I could talk to that NPC and stop them from what they were doing and then I could continue the quest I originally was in the middle of, its not with a lot of things that this happens but there are some. Anyways if that doesn't discourage you get this game. There are a lot of funny NPCs and potential companions, the team building is great, there are so many options to mix and match abilities

_childDocuments_.review: The vast majority of the Co-Op bugs have been corrected. This includes infinite loading screen, lost saves, deleted progression, inventory items disappearing, etc.I firmly believe the game shouldn't have been released in the state it was, but InExile reacted swiftly to patch these issues and resolve them accordingly. Thus, I give the game a thumbs up. Its a great game.At the time of writing, you cannot enter a new area with a co-op partner without being stuck at the load screen indefinitely. The only workaround is to; Exit the session, load the session in single player, enter the area you want to go to, save the game in the new area, exit the session, re-host a new session in co-op and load into the new area with your friend.Another downfall is the optimization. The game is poorly optimized. When you select items, characters, or selectable crates there is significant stuttering and frame drops. This is noted by many major reviewers. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece from start to finish in my opinion. I just finished my 2nd playthrough of this game (first was on game pass when it released) and I finally bought it because I enjoyed it so much. For those new with Wasteland, you play as the Desert Rangers. In Wasteland 3, you are on a mission from Arizona (play Wasteland 2 to find out) when things go not as planned and you're thrusted into a Colorado on the fringe of multiple factions vying for control. What makes this game a masterpiece is the writing with all the great characters, locations, factions, and choices for the player to explore. In typical Wasteland fashion, you get to create your main squad of characters and build them to fit their needs. For example, I love to create my friends and then experiment with different class builds. My main character was a brawler who ended up snowballing into Mike Tyson by the end of the game. After that, the player explores to find companions who have stories connected in the world which are great to share the game with and will gladly share their opinions on your choices. Throughout the whole game you'll meet some really cool characters that tie into different storylines. The thing that sets this franchise apart from others in the genre in my opinion is the fact that your choices DO matter. I've played through the game multiple times just because of this reason. I got different endings. Once the new DLC comes out, I will be playing this game again to do everything I didn't do once again. The gameplay is also great! I love all the different weapons, ways to build a character, armor, and the new crafting system which added a lot of cool stuff to the game. You are able to find blueprints to craft new stuff yourself which encouraged me to do a lot of exploring to find anything I could craft. All the different factions also have their own playstyle, which adds tremendous amounts of depth to the game because every section of the game is nothing like the last. I cannot tell you to play this game enough if you're on the fence. It's one of my favorite RPG's (along with Wasteland 2) and I hope this franchise continues like this because I am a sucker for the innovative gameplay and interesting stories!

_childDocuments_.review: My friend and me are huge fans of open world coop rpgs such as Divinity Original Sin 2 and when we first heard of Wasteland 3 and that it would have a coop mode we were very excited. The Online reviews all seemed to be very promising and were praising the game so we bought it. But it looks like none of those testers got to test out the Coop mode which is just almost unplayable. I dont know whether these issues apply in Singleplayer but im just gonna list some of them. The loading times are huge and for an open world game it is far too much divided into different sectors, and you have to look at a boring loading screen for at least 3-4 minutes each time you go to another sector which happens often.The conversation handling with two players is just random and sometimes simply doesnt work. In some conversations you can listen to what your partner says and in some other conversations you have two seperate conversations with the same npc at the same time which is just confusing as hell because you never know which of your answers count.But my biggest complaint are the bugs in the coop mode. They range from small inconveniences (like interrupted voice acting and a speechbubble which does not want to go away) to huge gamebreaking bugs (Game breaks in a conversation so noone can answer, the hud just disappears, action points disappearing so noone can act, and we already had three times where just all of our active and completed quests got deleted so we have to either do it all again or we have to take a save game from over half an hour ago which leads to even more boring loading screens)The game in itself may be a good one with many cool and funny ideas like the toaster repair skill line but they marketed it also as a good coop game so i will rate that experience with it. And it is just frustrating and almost unplayable especially for a non early acsess and full prize game. Hope there will be a patch soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! The combat system is what you'd expect, similar to Wasteland 2, Shadowrun, etc. The characters are fun, and add flair to the campaign. The setting is well done, and the different factions are neat. Character creation is rewarding, and a bit more condensed than Wasteland 2.  The story is alright, but if you're somebody who strives for the best ending, you NEED to look up how to get it. If you try to make all the best choices, you will not get the best ending, and there's nothing you can do to change that. It was super fun up until I realized that. That aside though, I definitely recommend it, especially if it's on sale. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This was the first Wasteland game I've played but I've greatly enjoyed my experience with it so far! _childDocuments_.review: I am completely whelmed by Wasteland 3. The writing and story is okay, it can't seem to decide what tone it wants. It jumps between committing war crimes to haha quirky wacky quickly, and the juxtaposition is jarring. Some of the missions were decently involved with multiple ways to accomplish the end goal, but 90% of the time there is one way to get a task done, and if you don't have the skills in your party ready, too bad, you just fail.  One example is when you are rescuing a couple of hostages that are standing on explosive traps that must have pressure on them or they explode. The literal only way to keep both of them alive is to have a certain level in mechanics on one of your characters, otherwise one of them has to die. This kind of fake choice is in damn near every quest, and it's incredibly annoying.The game is short as hell and buggy too.About once an hour I had to reload my game to get one of my characters to be unglitched. I also did the main storyline and over half of the side missions according to the wiki in 20 hours. . Finally, the turn based combat just flat out sucks. There is only one good strategy for every engagement that turns every combat encounter into a snoozefest, which you can easily find online. Melee character builds are way too weak for way too long, and all turning up the difficulty does is make the enemies bullet sponges. No different AI, no different enemy group comps based on the difficulty, no scarcity of resources at higher difficulties with the same health to make you think about every engagement, just plain old health increases. TLDR, Wasteland 3 manages to take Fallout and XCOM and combine it to create the most mediocre RPG you've ever played. If you pay over $15 for this you are a fool. Just play any of the Fallout games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather unimpressed.I waited a long time to buy the game because I read a lot about bugs. It's been out for over a year now, so I thought I'd give it a try.I like CRPGs. I liked Wasteland 2. I'm a big player of games like Divinity: Original Sin, Pillars of Eternity, Baldurs Gate, etc.This is like, 2/10 so far. Don't look at the hour count on my profile, I get up and walk away a lot. I could probably get where I am at writing this review in an hour or so.It's between XCOM and D:OS. The combat is XCOM, with some Divinity mixed in. And it does neither well. Not impressed so far.Thoroughly average and mediocre. Find a truck in the wasteland? It's got one health pack in it. Maybe, just maybe, my expert mechanic could fix it up or strip it for parts? Nope.Maybe an area with walking bombs? Maybe, my expert computer hacker and drone specialist can take control of them? Nope, that ability can't be used outside of combat, and they have initiative, so they just walk up and blow apart my whole team.It's just.... not very good. Want a good CRPG? Play Divinity or Pillars. Or go back and play Wasteland 2. This isn't very good.

_childDocuments_.review: In Wasteland 3 you take command of a squad of Desert Rangers, lawmen and women in a post-nuclear world, trying to rebuild society from the ashes. More than a century after the bombs fell, you’re fighting a losing battle to keep your beloved Arizona alive. Then the self-proclaimed Patriarch of Colorado radios, promising aid if you'll do a job he can only entrust to an outsider—rescue his land from the ambitions of his three bloodthirsty children. You’re dispatched on a desperate quest from the scorching deserts to the snowy mountains to start from scratch, building a new base, finding a snow-worthy vehicle, training new recruits, and fighting your way through hostile frozen wastes. All the while, you'll have to decide who to trust in this land torn apart by corruption, intrigue, warring factions, crazed cultists, cutthroat gangs, and bitter sibling rivalries. Build a reputation for yourself by making decisions that will profoundly impact Colorado, its inhabitants and the story you experience. Will you be Colorado’s savior or its worst nightmare? Wasteland 3 is a squad-based RPG from inXile entertainment, featuring challenging tactical turn-based combat and a deep, reactive story full of twists, turns, and brutal ethical decisions that will keep you hooked whether you’re a Wasteland veteran or new to the series. Create a squad of up to six Rangers and customize them with perks and abilities geared to your playstyle. You even get your own battle truck, which you can upgrade into a hardened war beast, bristling with weapons, to help mow down your enemies.

name: Mundaun
detailed_description: Mundaun is a lovingly hand-penciled horror tale set in a dark, secluded valley of The Alps. Explore various areas full of secrets to discover, survive hostile encounters, drive vehicles, fill your inventory, and solve a variety of handcrafted puzzles. Key Features Experience a unique hand-penciled aesthetic, and immerse yourself in an alpine world where reality and myth intertwine. Explore varied and open levels from green meadows to snowy peaks. Beware of the creatures roaming the landscape. Robust inventory system to keep you focused on collecting and uncovering the story’s secrets. The game’s fear resistance factor creates a “cause and effect” for the player within the game. The stronger the fear, the more slowly you move. Solve puzzles that are integrated into the game world as you make your way up the mountain. Interact with eccentric inhabitants who have their own obscure spoken language.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes it only takes one picture to see that the game will be - at the very least - interesting. I saw the first picture of  on an indie website something like two years ago,  and after that was patiently waiting for release. I was expecting another tiny 2-3-hour horror game - only this time with actual style and atmosphere.What I didn't expect was was ten hours of high production values all across the board.I'm definitely replaying it a few years down the line. You rarely see such quality from small teams of independent developers. It's the kind of game indie studios don't usually make leaning more towards procedural experiences. is hand-tailored in each and every way.PSWatched Dreyer's  lately (a very visually impressive movie), and saw a few images as well as aesthetic choices I'd already encountered in this game. I doubt it's a coincidence.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write reviews for the games I played, but after finishing this game, it kinda feel wrong for me to not spare a few minutes to share my thoughts and denying the very slight possibility that it may help out the studio responsible for this amazing game.After completing both Resident Evil Village and Mundaun in that order, I was trying to figure out why did I find Mundaun to be a much more satisfying experience than Resident Evil Village. After some head-scratching, this is what I manage to articulate so far:Though Resident Evil Village is epic in its own right, it can be a bit overly bombastic for my taste with its super-human villains' shenanigans and breakneck pacing.  Characters seem to come and go far too fast before I can fully understand their relevance and motivations. And when the ending came, the confusion I felt kinda erodes the initial investment I had with the characters and their goals. Mundaun, on the other hand, just feels a lot more grounded, with characters packing motivations that are grounded, relatable and easy to understand. And when the story finally comes to a satisfying conclusion at the end, I feel like I actually understood the story and why the characters acted the way they did. I guess this factor is what made this game more memorable to me.With its well-told story, unique art-style, solid soundtrack and a surprising amount of gameplay variety, it seems like the developers really care about their game and would have had invested a tremendous amount of effort and care in making it. Hope this game sells well. Looking forward to the studio's next project! A sequel perhaps.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't beaten the game yet, but I feel the need to leave a review — in a lot of senses because this is how you can help a good game to get noticed by more people on Steam these days.I won't say anything new about how the game looks — just look at the screenhots, they're gorgeous. It doesn't feel like a classic indie way of cutting corners with a simple art style, it's a completelly unique and painstakingly  created visual language.At first you as a player can think that it's a narrative based walking simulator of sorts (I made some small walking simulator games myself so I can throw a little shade on the genre), but it's actually a solid adventure game with survival horror elements. And the narrative focus is here — it's just backed with game mechanics, and it's perfect.I adore the choice to record the voice lines in Romansh language, native to Switzerland. It's a language spoken by very few people, comparatively, and this game will forever be a monument to that language. The whole game in general is a great monument to the folklore of the Alps, a real work of art, a bridge between generations, it is truly an important videogame.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Mundaun, a small village in the Swiss Alps where you play as a man named Curdin who has come to lay his grandfather to rest. There was an unfortunate accident involving a barn fire, and when Curdin arrives on his grandfather's land it doesn't take long to realize that things are amiss. The village priest says that his grandfather was buried in the cemetery, but you've seen with your own eyes that the body still resides in the barn; trapped in the ashen remains and charred lumber. A mysterious man appears to Curdin and burns his hand and despite now having physical proof that something is awry, no one wants to talk about what exactly is going on. It's up to you to explore these Alps, and figure out exactly what dark secrets your veteran grandfather has been hiding all of these years.Mundaun has a unique black-and-white(ish) aesthetic that's authentically hand-drawn with heavy, almost oppressive, thick-leaded pencils; there's a great mini-documentary on YouTube that follows the developers on their trip to Switzerland and shows where they got inspiration for their textures, building structures, and environment design, as well as how they transitioned the paper drawings to in-game textures and character models. MWM Interactive and Hidden Fields put in a great deal of time and effort to produce something that's accurate to the life of pre-modern Switzerland, and their hard work shows superbly in the outstanding atmosphere and crude beauty of Mundaun's visuals. To miss it, you would have to deliberately ignore the loving craftsmanship that went into every detail of this title's visuals. At this time, there is no other video game with this type of hand-drawn imagery.The flowing mist and fog that overcomes parts of the Alps makes the location feel otherworldly at times; peering down into what would be a network of villages, only to be met with marshmallow-like clouds conveys the feeling of floating in another dimension. At times this fog overtakes portions of the map that you explore, and it allows the developers to gently force a guided linearity to the story; something that's necessary due to just how large the six-area map truly is. Although the gameplay is linear, it never makes you feel like you're 'on-rails'... there is always a good chunk of land open to scouting to your hearts content. Taking the time to survey the landscape, not only for the spectacular views, pays off with tangible items such as bullets, matches, and stat upgrades, as well as some extra additions to the plot through notes and optional encounters.It has been said before, but it's worth repeating; the atmosphere in Mundaun is simply incredible. The days are well lit, but cloudy. Sometimes there's rain, sometimes there's snow. The nights are usually clear, with star-filled skies and a bright full moon, though sometimes there are lingering snow clouds. Although this is a horror game, the nights feel especially calm and peaceful, and you can almost feel yourself breathing in the crisp, cold, fresh mountain air; of course, that is until the monsters show up... but that doesn't happen all the time. The developers were even able to add in some wind effects here and there, and there's sections with a rushing flow of water coming in from a waterfall. I'd usually gripe about how there's no soundtrack in a horror game but much like Dark Souls, Mundaun just doesn't need it; the footsteps of your character and ambience from the natural environment works outstandingly well to immerse you.Rarely is a game perfect, so of course Mundaun has its own shortcomings. Most importantly, the combat is dreadfully clunky. Hitting an enemy requires players to press and hold a button for a seriously lengthy amount of time before being able to actually execute the hit; this extends to all weapons but it only makes sense for aiming the rifle, and using the pipe to thwart bees and beekeepers is the worst offender. The cumbersome mechanics become increasingly frustrating and you're better off avoiding combat all together if possible, but that brings us to the second major annoyance; enemies can hit you without even aiming at you. This issue is predominant with the Haymen, who shoot hay at you and can do so from an ungodly range. If you're on the right, and they're pointing left, their hay attack will still make contact with you.Ultimately, the monster encounters in this game just do not add anything to the overall experience. In fact, they detract quite substantially from it. Added to the underwhelming combat system is a 'fear' mechanic that doesn't make much sense, in that you'll be 'afraid' and move slower even when you cannot see an enemy, and doesn't seem to get much better even when it's fully upgraded. As a side note, you can max out fear resistance, health, and combat by finding items, but only the health upgrade truly seems to matter in the long run since it lets you take a couple more hits.Despite its pitfalls, Mundaun remains a labour of love that's worthy of every word of praise it receives. Visually, the game is a breath of fresh air in a genre that has started wearing its redundancy like a favourite cozy sweater. Although much of the aesthetic leaves you feeling calm, there's still a certain unsettling ambience and overarching weirdness that you can't quite shake, and for good reason. The story is like a good book that you just can't bring yourself to put down, and you'll have a hard time not seeing it through to the end in one sitting. There are five endings that you can obtain, and each one requires a new playthrough; though whether the 4-6 hours to do multiple runs is worth it is ultimately up to the individual. If you're looking for a new experience that you're guaranteed to have not come across before, no matter how many horror games you've played, then this is the game for you.The Horror Network  |  Click for Gore
