_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game easily. The caveats: You know what you're in for mechanically - it's an exploration-based walking simulator with some survival horror elements. I had a very good time with the exploration (more on that below), but I agree with the other reviewers' complaints about the enemy encounters. I will say in their (the encounters') defense, they do an admirable job of breaking up the pace of the game - if they were removed entirely, the game would be worse for it. Unfortunately, the game saves its 2 most fun mechanics (  ) for the third act. Only a couple of the characters had charm, and I was expecting the game to capitalize more on the potential of at least one of them, BUT they don't outstay their welcome since the game mostly treats them as a delivery mechanism for its excellent set-pieces. The meat of it: the game kept genuinely surprising me. Several of the set-pieces made my jaw drop, and there were some smaller curves in the road that kept me on my toes. The atmosphere is incredible. I was also surprised by how foregrounded the religious aesthetics were and how seriously the game took them - they never felt cheap (which is especially rare in the horror or horror-adjacent space), and at the game's best moments they imbued it with some real awe. I had a great time exploring the environment - the game is very clever in peppering enough items, keys, mapping points and stat upgrades to pull you, almost without your realizing it, through the world, sometimes rewarding you with letters/bits of world-building, sometimes setting up environmental mechanics which will pay off in a satisfying way later on, at one point even , and all the time building that nice round sense of place that only an exploration-based game can give you.With that I feel quite confident recommending this game. It's a compelling, atmospheric European art piece, and that is a very unique promise for a game to deliver on. I'm excited to see what the studio does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Just washed my hands of this game minutes ago.  It's hard to tell whether I would've liked this game without the two bugs that killed progress for me, so let's see where we end up:Pros:--Voice acting (though it's in the game's specific language, the subtitles are still good and you get some tone from the voice lines).--Looks nice, and the hand drawn aspect is a neat change from the usual FPS horror without going over the cartoony edge.--Story seems neat - I did get far enough to see what looks like all the unknowns pieced together in the third act (except maybe "sled girl," of whose involvement I'm still uncertain).--You can sneak/run from most monsters, it seems, and I sure had to. I only had one situation where I had to improvise vehicular weaponry because it seemed I had to sit around at an objective point and let multiple of them kill me to death whilst armed with a pitchfork - more on that below.Bad:--Pitchforks with the resilience of a branch.  The above-mentioned instance had me with one pitchfork with two of its tines already broken off and nothing else to defend myself with but a truck that would be unavailable if I began the event - this after one, maybe two encounters with the starting enemy, including one instance where I got a stealth attack on them.  Attacking with them feels awkward as well.--I get the impression there's a way to make use of matches to fight these guys but I never did figure out how exactly. Running them over with the truck repeatedly seemed to be simpler.--I found myself wondering how to get to A to B often in the middle and later portion of the game.--I kept receiving rifle ammo but no rifle, to the point I thought I'd missed something when I was dumped unceremoniously into a situation with lots of enemies who could hurt me just by looking at me (the above situation).  I FOUND the rifle much later, and then proceeded to be unable to use it to kill things five steps from me, which is how I found out I could at least run from most things.--BUGS:I had one bug make it impossible for me to progress in the bunker because the toy lift's key was neither in existence nor was it already in place after I'd used it in my last session, which should've left things open for me to proceed when I loaded, but said path was closed off to me with the key no longer in game (reloading from an older save fixed this, after an hour of trying to play games with a mirror thinking maybe it was a puzzle then giving up and looking for a walkthrough).The other, final and game-killing bug came for me in what was undoubtedly the third act, after it seems like all there is left is go back to X, burn the thing, confront this one and that other one and maybe save this third one.  After going all the way up the mountain, doing shenanigans in the devil's house or whatever it was, coming back out, getting lost all over the way back down to where I could spawn the muvel (truck) like it told me to do so I could go back down the mountain to do the confrontation/saving... the truck would not go forward.To be honest, the truck went forward at centimeters a time. You couldn't even tell if you were looking forward, but if you looked out the side and picked a landmark and checked where it was related to the frame of the truck you were sitting in, you'd see scenery very, very, VERY slowly creeping past.  Weirdly, backing up went a little faster (not much, but easily noticeable compared to trying to go foward).A truck respawn by the exit tunnel (I wasn't allowed to just walk out - needed the truck) planted the truck facing dead forward into it. One spawn I got into the truck it wouldn't go forward but it suddenly had a grand ol' time speeding backwards until it crashed.  I looked up this bug and found mention of it in a reddit post from THREE YEARS AGO.  The one person with anything significant to say about it basically said "I put on a podcast and held forward for 30 minutes and then the truck was normal after the scene transition."  I spawned the truck again, and decided to try u-turning and reversing into the tunnel. It was slow going, but I made it to the tunnel - at which point, the truck sped forward away from the tunnel.  And that's when I quit.I'd ask for a refund if it weren't already 8 hours into the playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: First hour impressions & gameplay - I am just over an hour into Mundaun but it had won me over after only a few minutes. Mundaun has a quiet, dark & brooding atmosphere that seeps into every detail of it's hand drawn world, playing this reminds me of films such as The Witch, The Lighthouse & Saint Maud, less about jump scares & set pieces and more about getting under your skin & leaving you unsettled.There is so much to praise here that I'm not quite sure where to start; gorgeous visuals, a slow burn mystery to unravel, a world that begs to be explored, side quests that add to the world and experience, beautifully voiced characters & some awesome gameplay systems and mechanics (the upgrade system is particularly cool and gives players a reason to explore the world).The best gaming purchase I've made so far this year, can't wait to see how it all plays out!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a strange game. I certainly respect it but not sure I like it. The art style is wonderful and they do some impressive, creative things with it too. Music is very atmospheric.What doesn't work for me at all is combat. Feels like it doesn't even belong here and was added at the last minute. So obtuse and janky with the enemies that are not scary but just annoying. What's worse, the main character, NPCs and the overall story don't even acknowledge these enemies exist. Ugh, I just really disliked the combat here.Still, I can't bring myself to give this a thumbs up. It's a unique thing, clearly a passion project. And the overall folksy vibe is really amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal and utterly unique first-person horror game about navigating supernatural phenomena inspired by real folklore of the towns of the Swiss Alps. The developer took every opportunity to pour as much love as possible into this game, which shines through its simple yet haunting hand-drawn pencil texturing and its wonderful voice acting in Romansh, a regional language of Switzerland spoken by fewer than 100,000 people. Every step of the story makes its mark upon your soul, and once your finished you will be left simultaneously sated yet hungry for more games like this one. No other games have quite the impact that Mundaun does, one would be doing themselves a disservice to miss out on an opportunity to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Love the atmosphere and surreal feel of this game. I loved exploring the area and finding everything. To be honest, this is the first horror game I've actually played because I'm a bit of a scaredy cat...and I was able to play it, so I guess it's not *too* scary. Still has some jump-y moments, and it feels tense throughout. I also love the hand drawn art style (that's what made me want to play it) the puzzles, and the story. The ending I got (one of several, as I understand) managed to surprise me!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about Mundaun felt oppressive, the greyscale imagery disturbing but also having a certain beauty to it. I just had to explore every corner while navigating the various puzzles and monsters. Even the simple things—making coffee—held my attention and reminded me that optional activities can feel the most satisfying. One thing’s for sure, it embraced its cultural roots, with voice acting in Romansh, Switzerland’s fourth national language—this did wonders for immersion. Unfortunately, I absolutely detested the fear mechanic that affected movement when near an enemy as it negatively impacted stealth and the already janky combat.One of the more noteworthy indie horror titles out there, but it was definitely rough around the edges, especially in relation to its enemies and the gameplay surrounding them.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Rejoice one and all, for Mundaun is about to enter your life and it is good, very good. To explain why it's so good. I must first talk about a different game: Call of Cthulhu Dark Corners of the Earth which I'll be calling DCOTE from here on. DCOTE features an incredible opening. You play as an investigator sent to the small fishing town of Innsmouth to investigate spooky goings-on. You spend the game's first 2-3 hours doing just that, investigating and solving puzzles and whatnot. The game spends this time setting up its ominous atmosphere and getting you invested in its story. Then all hell breaks loose, featuring one of the most terrifying gameplay sequences ever, in which you desperately try to escape from a spooky inn as you are chased by the town's monstrous inhabitants. Then comes the epic climax where you blast your way out of Innsmouth, finally getting back at all the weirdos who have been creeping you out for the entire game. It is glorious and tragically unique. But then the game keeps going. And going. It suddenly changes into a full blown FPS, one of the most difficult ones ever, and it quickly becomes apparent that the expertly paced game you just played was really just the exceptional first third of a generic and infuriating FPS.Mundaun is like if the first third of DCOTE was the entire game. I'm not sure if the developer was inspired by DCOTE, and Mundaun is by no means a ripoff of it, but it's a thought that didn't leave my head for the entire game. You play as Curdin, a young man who has gotten word that his Grandfather died in a barn fire high in the alpine town of Mundaun. When Curdin arrives it becomes clear that something is up with the town and its inhabitants. I'll stop there since Mundaun has one of the most well presented and absorbing video game stories in a long time, and I'd hate to spoil it. It's not that it's full of CRAZY twists or anything, it's just best experienced in-game.The gameplay is split into two halves: exploration and combat/stealth. If you were to put the two parts on a scale, it would be weighted heavily in favor of exploration, and that's just fine. The world is engrossing and steeped in regional folklore. It feels like there is another mystery or magical discovery around every corner and most of the time there is. There are puzzles to solve and they're pretty easy which may be a downside for some, but for me it meant that frustration over difficult puzzles never got in the way of the story. Also, while they are easy they're creative and fun. The combat is also rudimentary, and is probably the game's weakest aspect. The game features two weapons, a pitchfork which breaks after multiple uses and must be frequently replaced, and a rifle which you pick up about 60% of the way through the game. There is little feedback when hitting an enemy with the pitchfork which often led me to wonder whether or not I was doing damage. The rifle doesn't suffer from this problem as it usually knocks an enemy down with one shot and has a soul-shakingly loud sound effect, but it still feels floaty and has no recoil, which means it doesn't feel great to use. That being said the combat exists to complement the exploration, a little splash of tense action to disrupt the eerie serenity, so as long as it's at least passable (which it is) it will only make the game better (which it does).So there you go, that's Mundaun. I haven't even touched on the oddly satisfying coffee brewing system which nearly every review I've read has, so if you want to hear more about that go read one of those (or just play the game). I give this one a strong recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review by saying that this has been the top 3 games I've played in 2022. I first heard about this gem from Ragnarox's video on it. Thankfully, he reviews games in a way that leaves the story intact. The setting of a European horror story in the rural mountains had me instantly set in.The Setting: You're a young man heading to his grandfather's mountain house for the holidays. Things turn worse on the mountaintop after finding his barn on fire and meeting with a mysterious stranger. Soon, you're thrust into a setting that resembles a blend of Hatchet, Silent Hill, and the Great War. It is a unique experience I haven't had with another game.The Story: As stated, you're trying to find out what has happened to your grandfather and the more profound secret the townspeople keep. The pacing is lovely, and no character or place overstays its welcome. The antagonist of the story is intriguing and thoughtful. They genuinely feel like they're from another world. I even laughed when you get a surprising companion for a stretch of your journey.Game Mechanics: You have the two core mechanics in the game: puzzles and combat. Combat is meant to feel unreliable. It's a horror game. I would have preferred ditching it entirely for more puzzle-style handling of the enemies (therein). A little extra doesn't hurt. The puzzles were never too demanding and made excellent use of the environment and setting of the game.Pace: Like I stated earlier, the game is paced beautifully. I was never bored, and nothing overstayed its welcome. The ending feels faster, and I couldn't appreciate the setting as much as the other game sections.In conclusion, this has been the biggest surprise for 2022 and is one of my favorite indie games. I'm excited to see what these developers develop in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a masterpiece.The Gameplay exceeds all expectations, it's content-rich, well-rounded and satisfying as hell.The Story is on another level, it's incredible, it's the most unique and well-crafted narrative I've ever seen.It subverts all expectations and keeps you engaged, it'll have you scrambling to find out what happens next.The Graphics are wonderfully unique and the amount of visual story-telling and subtext is mind-blowing.I'd give this game 10/10 without a second of hesitation, it truly is a lovingly-handcrafted masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun has a familiar format as a story-driven horror game, but it is presented in top-tier fashion. The art is hand drawn and the game is fully (and excellently) voiced in an obscure dialect of the Alps. Every character, including the villain and even a certain animal, is quirky and memorable. Lengthwise, it felt like a full authentic folktale and it didn't overstay its welcome. I streamed my playthrough for a few friends so we could share the experience, and I recommend doing the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on sale because of a random video I saw on youtube praising it.Turns out this was actually some of my best spent money on this platform. The game scratches that itch that Penumbra Overture had, of a semi-survival horror that has combat but strongly disencourages it.You should really give it a try. Story is kinda wild, but the creative gameplay and immersion make this an amazing indie horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Setting this game in the swiss canton of the Grisons and voicing its charactars in Romansh works brilliantly in two ways: Firstly, it serves to make a language and culture that is as little-known as it is interesting more visible. Secondly, it creates a wonderful dichotomy between the foreign and the familiar, between the homey and the unsettling. At least, except for maybe like sixty thousand people from Switzerland. All this works really well in a world painstakingly hand-textured by pencil, creating a dream-like, surreal immersion. And I am happy to report that it rests on a healthy foundation of solid level design, memorable characters, and an interesting mystery to uncover. Sound design and music is also top notch. My only gripes are with the enemy creatures, who don't really scare or intimidate you, but more often rip you out of the immersion with predictable and easily exploitable behaviour.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool little game! It's more unsettling/creepy than outright terrifying, like exploring an old European folktale.As other reviewers have mentioned, the gameplay isn't too complex. It's mostly exploration and puzzle solving, but there is some stealth (or combat if you feel like fighting the monsters). There is also a difficulty setting, so you could set it to Easy in case you prefer to just enjoy the story without worrying about a lot of enemies, but honestly the normal setting isn't too bad. I avoided most enemies since the main character can outrun them for the most part..it didn't work every time though haha. What I loved the most though is the story and the atmosphere, and the hand-drawn textures give the game a really unique look and just adds to the creepiness. If you're looking for a story-rich short adventure experience, I'd definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: solid game! if i have anything to criticize it's that the combat feels largely unnecessary until one sequence towards the climax. the enemies leave a lot to be desired and melee combat is extremely unresponsive.that said, combat is a really small part of the experience of Mundaun, and everything else is pretty great. the visuals are unique and beautiful, the atmosphere is palpable, and the tone is fantastic. love this kind of folk horror. at 6 - 7 hours, it's a well-paced, worthwhile experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I avoid games with any sort of combat mechanic. So it shows how much I loved this game that I overcame my fear and nerves to play it. Although there was a moment that I found to be particularly challenging for me, I wanted to get to the end of it so I could know what would happen next.It is an absolute 10/10 for me. The artistic choices are great, the voice acting is amazing and the story is superb. There isn't a single thing that i would change in this game, even the (light) combat of it. I don't want to say anything else in order not to spoil anyone else's experience, but really, it's worth playing it.I'm really grateful the creator took their time to create this game, so I could experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and unique. The ambience, the slow rhythm, the naturally of the difficulty, etc, makes you dive in this world and identifiy with the protagonist and his actions. This immersion also is valid for the horror, that is, sometimes, in small details. The sound design/soundtrack  (AMAZING) is very responsible to guiding your look to theses "small pieces of horror", like "hey bro, something is wrong, look around". I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: There's nothing else quite like Mundaun.Not much needs to be said about the art design... it's gorgeous and I found myself looking closely at in-game textures thinking "damn, I can't believe someone drew all this in pencil!!"The vibe of the game is great also, you're given moments to explore without the threat of enemies during some sections, as well as the opportunity to make a nice cup of virtual coffee! There's a kind of slow burn horror that Mundaun builds up perfectly, using the quiet backdrop of a small valley to create an eerie, unsettling atmosphere. Folk horror has never been better!The puzzles were enjoyable and satisfying. Combat was a little awkward at times but I think stealth is definitely the way to go. Or if you're lazy like me, just run over your enemies with Grandpa's truck ;)I'd highly recommend Mundaun, I have no doubt it will remain very near the top of my list of favourite games for this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: So you need to have patience to enjoy it, and you're probably going to have to check a guide in a few places because Mundaun is *not* great at communicating where you need to go next, but this is like a slower, walking-sim-ier Betrayer and it rules.Calling it folk horror feels like it kind of misses what Mundaun is. It's so specific to its environment that I'd call it alpine horror instead.You very slowly roam the mountains, Have Experiences, and solve puzzles in a cumbersome, low-fi sort of way.It reminds me a lot of Amnesia, but it's given waaay more room to breathe. Walking is slow, environments are big, combat is very stiff, and interactions all have long, slow animations on them.It's to Mundaun's credit that this builds atmosphere more than it frustrates, and if you want a fast-paced version of this same thing you should try Northern Journey instead.Ultimately, I'd recommend this at full price if you like art, gorgeous and slow-paced settings, and extremely indie horror. If you're on the fence, maybe wait for a sale, but I'd instabuy this at 70% off or higher.Edit: Lol, softlocked. "Get away from Florina." "Make me." On constant loop with no way to interact. Also this is an autosaver, and I saved in my house, so apparently I've locked myself out of the good ending AND locked myself into this glitched state. The correct answer was "look out the window at the bridge back in the painter's house." Other ways of looking at the bridge don't work, and I can't get back to the painter's house from where I am. This is still a *really* good game, even if you run into this weird issue and have to youtube the ending, but it's a shame my final impression is a little scuffed.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a short, 4-6 hour indie horror game about a man named Curdin who returns to his childhood home, the eponymous village of Mundaun, in the alps after having received news of his grandfather falling into some trouble. The entire premise of the game revolves around you wandering through the mountains seeking a way to lift a peculiar curse from your grandfather, trapped inside of his burned down barn under mysterious circumstances. It is a story about evil, of choice, and mystery. The gameplay involves puzzle solving with some light survival and exploration elements. There are monsters that wander about, and you can either avoid them or take them down with melee or ranged combat. The variety of weapons and monsters is not that vast, which makes encounters pretty predictable, but the game is short enough where this doesn't prove to be very problematic. The areas are open and unlock slowly as you progress the game. There are vehicles in this game, which handle surprisingly well. The game looks nice for a Unity title, and has a very distinct visual style which enhances the rustic, horror feel the game is going for. Mundaun could, perhaps, be described as a very barebones, distant cousin version of Resident Evil 7/8. This is not meant to be an insult, but a compliment. Mundaun is eerie, atmospheric, and mysterious. It doesn't take itself so seriously that ridiculous plot elements stick out as being absurd, nor does it take itself so lightly that serious things feel out of place. It is well balanced in this regard. Mundaun is not a ground breaking title, but it is a solid horror game. The music is soft and doesn't impose itself when it shouldn't, the story is actually far more interesting that one might first think, and can end in three different ways depending on the choices you make. I enjoyed this game, despite how short it was, and would recommend it to anyone who likes horror, and indie games. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is, obviously, a lovingly hand-drawn horror experience. The amount of work going in to the visuals is immediately apparent from any screenshots or videos you've probably already seen. This style (and workflow) is so unique, I put together a video analyzing the techniques used to create it: So, instead of dwelling on the visuals - which are already covered in that video, plus the hundreds of other reviews - I'll speak on other aspects of the game.Despite being firmly rooted in horror, and having a handful of spooky moments, I often felt like I was playing an adventure/puzzle game of old. Something along the lines of Myst or Obduction. Much of the game involves carefully exploring environments, collecting items, and solving puzzles to progress on to the next area. The "levels" are somewhat open-world, giving the player a bit of freedom to explore at their leisure. But there is always one linear path forward that you must eventually come to. The exploration was always a driving factor, finding new scenic sites and curiosities along the mountainside kept me constantly inching forward. The story and characters were also pretty well done. Although I was able to figure out where the story was headed very early on, I still enjoyed the ride, and came in to a few unexpected events along the way.The puzzles worked well for me, a little easy at times, but nothing I lingered on for too long. The enemies were generally not threatening - mainly just to be avoided. I tried stealth and combat for a little bit, but both felt like a waste of time when you can run away from threats or give them a wide berth. You do get  at one point, which added a bit to the combat, but I still think the game would've been fine without it.The horror themes paired well with the story, even if they may not be as overstated as most games. I wouldn't say I ever felt scared, but I don't think horror games have to limit themselves to scaring the player in the first place. Resident Evil 4 is a great horror game, but it definitely isn't scary. But I digress. There was a jump-scare or two, but the majority of the game has more of a "quiet horror" ambiance. Nothing outright spooky, just some creepy themes.Overall I'd recommend Mundaun. It's got a great world, story, and of course some excellent hand-drawn visuals. Despite the more "gamey" elements feeling a bit understated, I had fun with it. I'd gladly play more work by the developer in the future, so here's to hoping we see that!P.S. The Swiss countryside is quite beautiful, and Mundaun just gets me itching to go back again. Maybe it'll inspire you to visit too. I don't think you'd regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is more like a dark fairy tale than a horror game. The grayscale aesthetic and hand drawn textures gives it a very unique look that I've never seen before. Exploring the alpine setting is easily my favorite part. Reminds me of when I visited the Swiss alps and traveled to the Jungfraujoch. Being high up above the clouds was really impressive visually.The game is a bit clunky and unintuitive in some areas. The combat is the worst offender with enemies slowing you down when they spot you and being able to attack you from long range. The game wants you to use stealth in some locations but I found it easier just to charge through. There are some puzzles but nothing too complicated.The story was very unique to me; like it was based on an old folktale form the alpine region of Europe. There are a few unhelpful NPCs to interact with and voice acting is ok but nothing special. The goat is the best character. 🐐I would recommend this game for its uniqueness. I don't suspect I'll ever play another game quite like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem...and a goat or three. The unique art style, the story...what I probably appreciated the most is that it relied on Swiss folklore. It doesn't try to hard to be scary, and it evokes emotions rather than force them out of you. I got it as a birthday gift, and I loved every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "recommended, but..." kind of review. The tl;dr; is that visually and tonally, it's great, but the experience, for me, was mired by irritating and poorly conveyed mechanics.I'll start with the good and say that the story and atmosphere are great and very unique. The art is fantastic, though sometimes it makes it difficult to visually parse the scene because of the gray-scale nature of things. The animations are probably the weakest aspect of the art, as they look very amateurish when contrasted with the high quality hand-drawn art.My biggest gripe is with the monster/encounter design. The mechanics of the fear system aren't ever meaningfully conveyed, and you will die to monsters that you literally cannot see (and that cannot even see you!)  Sometimes you will be pitted against multiple monsters in very narrow corridors and the only way to progress is to die a bunch of times until you figure out the "right" way to progress. These types of encounters, to me, don't really add any sort of fear or tension and are purely just a tiresome roadblock between me and story progression.The only time I got actually "stuck" and had to look up a guide was when I had to talk to Allegria, the goat head, through the inventory screen. Nothing that I saw meaningfully hints that you have to do this, so I wandered around for 20 minutes trying everything *but* what I was actually supposed to do before I caved and just looked it up.Overall, though, the art and story is fantastic, which is what everyone is here for anyways. If you can look past some of the wonky mechanics, you'll have a good time.Also, I love the Muvel.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a moody, idiosyncratic game that in terms of its look and feel is like nothing else. Set in one of the most beautiful regions of Switzerland, it does the opposite of satisfying the player's touristic urges: Heidi this certainly ain't. Instead you become engaged in a fight for your survival and your soul in what could be called survival folk horror. The game has some bugs and it is janky (in particular the combat), but it is supremely atmospheric and pretty unique - where else would you have an opportunity to hear Rumansh, the fourth national language in Switzerland, in a video game?What I did dislike a fair bit, though, is the "screw you" ending I got, also because to my mind it negates the story of the game. If you can do everything right and then the antagonist still wins pretty much by snapping his finger, it doesn't feel like a sting in the tale so much as it feels somewhat cheap. By all means, give us an "It's all over... or is it?" ending, but don't just show the player that everything they did was pretty much pointless.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of horror and thus, I normally give horror games a wide berth. However, as this game has such a unique and beautiful graphics style and as it is a Swiss game, I brought myself to give it a try and didn't regret it once. The setting in the Swiss alps is well chosen and the Rhaeto-Romance adds the whole thing another mysterious layer. The story is really good and could come straight out an old tale book containing rural mysteries. And except for the two little jump scares, the horror level was completely managable even for me as a non-horror fan.So I can definitely recommend this game, also to non-horror fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The kinda game you sink right into. I absolutely loved it.There's something meditative about it. You don't feel rushed, or like you're plodding around aimlessly. You can pretty much explore this Swiss village at your leisure. Soaking in the wee cultural touches you've never seen before. Picking up clues to what's happening here and there.Such a unique look with all hand drawn textures, and that off-white colour palette. Everybody speaking beautiful Romansh. Unsettling imagery paced just right. Man, this would have absolutely been my 2021 GOTY if I'd played it at release.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: An exquisite game with a singular art style. Not many games have pulled such a unique feel and yet remained so consistent in all of their mechanics, story and UI elements. This is a work of Art, and the artist has put every bit of themselves into this game. A faithful feel for the swiss alps. I'm glad I played this. I hurt no enemies, so barely engaged with combat and as a result never died. For those wondering whether you can play this game without combat, you can. And I'd say it's not a lesser experience playing that way. Might even be a better experience, given the narrative and how helpless our character is in front of such weird creatures.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The Devil's in the Details.Mundaun is an interesting horror game from the very start. The creators have spent considerable effort literally drawing this world to life. As a result, the game looks like an old sketch book come to life. This certainly gives the world a lovely, unique look to it, but at the same time, leaves everything feeling off in some fashion. You feel unwelcome and out of place in the world, and far more so when the unusual starts happening. Yes, there are enemies, and you will have to confront them, with stealth, cleverness and maybe even violence. And yet, somehow, despite their presence, it is still you that feels out of place. That somehow, this is how things work on this mountain, and you're the one intruding.And while I feel uncomfortable, unwelcome and totally out of place, I never really quite feel the terror and fear of other horror games. And here, I think it's a good thing. There's very little direct fear. You won't scream or panic, you won't end up flailing wildly trying to fight or escape. This game is one that is frighting in the whole chain of events. Rarely, will you point at a scene and say, "This part scared me so bad." Indeed, this isn't a game you can look at part by part, but as one you need to view in its entirety. Playing through it, I can certainly say that, outside of bumbling face first into a monster (and that's more me being hasty than anything) I never really felt scared, but I certainly felt dread as things progressed. Things were happening that felt so horribly out of my control, I found myself wishing that getting back on the bus and leaving was an option.Mundaun is not a game for those who want to be hunted by monsters, run from killers and come face to face with supernatural horrors. There are enemies, and you can face them with violence, but that's not what Mundaun is about. Mundaun is a game you'll feel uncomfortable playing through, and much of the time you won't really know why.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Eerie and unnerving, "Mundaun" offers beautiful landscapes and memorable characters. Its puzzles are pretty good so far, even if the fighting system can be a bit clunky. Its retro style makes it look like a lost classic. And now that our screens are packed with new folk horror films, it was about time to see a proper game in this style. This game, and by extension this studio, show a lot of promise. It's a yes.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Not great, but is interesting enough that it was difficult to give it a Not Recommended. The art and music give a really cool and spooky atmosphere, and the story is all right. Give it a shot on sale, or watch a playthrough from someone who really enjoyed it. The rest of the review is pretty focused on negatives. This was a "play once and uninstall" for me, even though there are more achievements and multiple endings to obtain.I think the root of the problems I had with this game is that it was overhyped, which is unfortunate since I wouldn't have heard of it otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know that I can give this game enough praise. Fantastic story and fantastic art direction. The horror is very eerie and the developers nailed it with the story and pacing. The hand drawn world is a great medium and i felt the horror elements were complimented by the art. The Story itself is a *deal with the devil* affair that has a great ending and provides the players with a compelling choice. It did not take too long to finish. This is a gem of a game and i can't wait to see what Hidden Fields does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The game has artistic values and a nice story but some mechanics (especially enemies)* are a bit tedious. Definitely something different that is worth a play if you like basic walking simulators. I would not say it's a horror game (it's not scary) but the story is pretty dark and dramatic, with a very gloomy atmosphere.*honestly without enemies could have / would have even been better
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I've only managed to spend a few minutes so far but I can already tell I'm going to love this. The aesthetics are reminiscent of a real-time Yuri Norstein short and the sound design instills a sense of unease without veering into cliche. Will update with further impressions as I get further, but so far it's seeming like a future cult classic gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: En el nombre del Padre, this is a really fantastic horror game. There’s some confusion about the visuals being “hand pencilled” - the displacement/texture maps are done by hand, then those are placed over the models in-game. It’s not Paper Mario. It looks excellent; both purposeful and haphazard. You frequently hallucinate monsters and faces in the streaks of charcoal, and it keeps the atmosphere moody and oppressive throughout. It’s mostly a run-hide-puzzle style horror game, but the high variety of gameplay sections and environments make it hard to pin down a genre outside of “exploration,” which Mundaun is very good at. Several different endings, a pretty generous amount of save files, and a point-of-no-return warning give it a nice little replay value without being annoying about it. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute labor of love and a truly unique gaming experience. Whether you love horror games with excellent storytelling or just looking for the next unique thing in the indie scene, Mundaun will give you plenty to love. As can be seen at a glance, the visuals are incredibly striking and serve as a wonderful backdrop for this northern European folk tale. Even more impressive - and far less touted - is the sound design, pacing, tone, and the intricate details scattered throughout the world. Everything feels cohesive and alive and could only have been created by people with a strong creative vision and an intimate familiarity with the source content. There are some very strange portions of the game - some very 'what am I looking at right now' type moments - that are absolutely spectacular to witness. You'll know them when you see them and they will fill you with awe.Finally, the game is not perfect by any means, as there are areas that could be improved, but don't let minor annoyances prevent you from appreciating the overall gestalt of this experience. There is so much to love throughout the journey which will make it easy to overlook an out of place texture or AI inconsistency. This is the perfect example of a game's whole being much greater than the sum of its parts. Also, I experienced 0 bugs in 10 hours of game play - pretty impressive for the small team size. Go get the game!I'm jealous you get to experience it for the first time! Let it wash over you and good luck with the bees!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Easily a favorite! The charm, the story.. It's all just so good. Is it possible to get nostalgic for a game you've never played before? Because that's how it feels from the moment you start Mundaun. A wonderful gaming experience that I think about so often even after months of finishing this game. Thank you for this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by making one thing clear: while Mundaun is indeed story-focused it is also a game through-and-through and anyone dismissing it as a "walking simulator" is a fool who did not have the attention span longer than half an hour. With that out of the way I can say that Mundaun is an incredibly well-crafted experience that forms a cohesive whole and outright drips atmosphere and charm, complete with a gameplay system that empowers those elements. If you are looking an interesting, unique game that is deeply-rooted in culture that is (most-likely) foreign to you, but is still an interactive piece of media - this is a hard recommend from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is worth it for its atmospheric setting and style, as well as its captivating and well-paced story. If the style you see in the trailer or screenshots intrigues you, and light combat and puzzle elements are not a dealbreaker, this one is worth trying.The story feels like it could be authentic folklore or heavily inspired by it. I don’t know whether it is or not, but it felt like it was, and that made the experience of playing Mundaun unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very, very suprised by this game! I went into it thinking it would be an okay time, but not anything unique when it comes to Indie horror games, but boy was I wrong!This game is really good! There are a ton of mechanics in the game, including, shooting, sneaking, sneak attack, driving, exploring, upgrading and so on! And everything is set in a beautifully handcrafted world! You can really tell that the developer of this game has a deep passion for the project!Mundaun is not just "another one of those indie horror games". It's a truly special one! Grab it! Grab it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: this game has such a charming and unique art style. The mechanics are pretty simple but like the art style, very charming (making coffee is incredibly relaxing). Most of the puzzles are pretty straightforward (still engaging though!). I think the use of Romansh for voice acting was an amazing choice for immersion. So if you like horror but prefer an unsettling game instead of a terrifying one, i recommend Mundaun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: An evocatively surreal masterpiece that tells a story about the sins of the fathers, lifelong debt that spread its claw to torment generations, and a lesson in solving that debt by making amend to the past. Intoxically creative and ferocious in the way it delivered its narrative, theme and message, Mundaun didn't pull no punch with storytelling manifested by wonderful magical realism. This is easily one of the greatest horror games and horror story in video games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend purchasing Mundaun and playing through it - whilst also going in as blind as humanly possible - the artstyle/visuals of Mundaun are striking, haunting and incredibly well put together, everything comes packaged neatly in a well-written, acted and presented story, the atmosphere is tranquil and eerie, the scenery serene and dangerous, definitely worth a buy for anyone who wants a genuinely good horror game. Hope to see more from the studio in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little indie game. It will probably meet the fancy of players who have enjoyed games such as The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, as the gameplay is pretty straightforward, and it's mainly focused on story-telling and exploration. I think it's pretty successful at what it wants to achieve. The story, while simple, has several creative touches, a distinctive (often rather dark and sometimes even disturbing) atmosphere, and some fairly memorable characters. As far as I'm concerned, the small issues here and there didn't really detract from the overall enjoyment of the game. If you like story-driven games that deal with folklore and mysteries, I'd definitely recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game as soon as it came out, and sadly I dropped it immediately after the first haymen appeared. It just wasn't the right time, but I knew that eventually I would come around to give it another go. There's something about the folksy nightmarish tale that kept me orbiting around it, and now I finally pushed through and finished it.Rambling aside, this is one of my favourite indie horror games. The hand-penciled textures and homogeneous colours might be a turn-off for some people, but I think both landscape and narrative benefit from this artistic choice. The more mundane activities, like brewing coffee or loading a truck full of hay, are also pretty entertaining and endearing among the horrors that lurk ahead. Also, I cannot go by without mentioning how safe and calm I felt whenever I reached any of the houses that our character gets to sleep in throughout the game. It really excels at contrasting with the mysterious dangers that you're faced with in each area.Lastly, I was impressed that the dialogues were entirely in Romansh. I never heard that language in my life, so it was a nice addition to an already culture-packed game. I fully recommend it to anyone looking for a slightly different first person horror experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Now I don't really enjoy survival horror mechanics, and folk horror really gives me the creeps - so this is game should seem like something I'd probably ignore.  So why didn't I?  Mainly as it looked so beautiful and atmospheric, and the few people I know who had played it LOVED it.So I finally sat down to take my beautiful but creepy stroll through this quiet Swiss valley.  I reached the end, took a deep breath during the credits, went away and mulled over the game in my mind for a couple of hours, came back and started all over again.  The journal can be irritating on occasion to flick through, but it's design and usefulness make it an overall positive.Btw game is excellent for those who love horror, but dislike jumpscares.  There is only one big jumpscare (and yes even though I knew it was coming I think I jumped even more the second time around).Also, but perhaps most importantly, you can pet goats!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This review isn't all that put together, just wanted to get my thoughts down. A really good game with a couple of bugs.Really enjoyed how much it leaned into Nordic culture and let the environments speak for themselves. And the fact everything is textured by pencil really gave it a heightened eeriness, too. Things felt haunted, full of presence when nothing is there. It's incredibly atmospheric, and I loved just exploring everywhere and getting rewarded for it. Interesting storyline, too. Very idiosyncratic in how it chose to unfold itself.I played a large portion of it on the Steam Deck. It's a good game to curl up in bed to, but it really eats the battery (1080x800, 30fps, low graphics for about 2 hours).I would recommend playing this with patience -- make sure you have time for it to draw you in and soak in the sights.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Highly recommended! If you're already intrigued by the art style and enjoy moody slow-burns, chances are you'll love this.This was quite an experience! I don't want to speak at length as I think that the less you know going in the more you'll get out of the game. That being said, don't go into this expecting abject horror. This is more of a surreal, moody slow burn of a game with great atmosphere and surprisingly solid world-building (through environments, objects, and the language spoken especially). As for the art style, I don't think you need me to tell you how singularly unique it is. It's used to great effect throughout and adds a ton of depth that wouldn't have otherwise been possible. I will also recommend that you don't get too caught up in achievements your first time through--there ARE multiple endings so if that's your jam you'll already be needing to play through a few times anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding Visual Style Award 2021!Update: Oct 18 2022I made a joke-y review right around the Steam awards season and before I finished the game. Mundaun is an incredible game that deserves a bit of explanation.Mostly when I talk to others who have played this game, we come to the conclusion that it's "an adventure game with horror in it" and that horror is typically a deep sense of dread. That dread is well written in to the story of the game, in which I feared for the town, the people and myself while uncovering the mysteries within Mundaun. I could always feel like worse and worse things would happen in this world, and that there could not be a resolution.The art style is the immediate selling point of this game, although everything else about it is fantastic. I thought the black-and-white / sepia tones would be boring or ugly to look at for hours, but it is both unique and has been beautifully used throughout lands. There is a distinction between regions you enter and the skybox is typically always visible and gorgeous.Beyond the artistic choice, what gives this game outstanding visual style is how that the way the player is drawn to environmental scripted moments. There are things that happen throughout the game that you could miss if you weren't watching, and I almost did, but there is a particular way these moments pop out of the background, or the players focus gets pulled to them. I don't know how to explain it, but when these moments happen it is startling and mesmerising!Mechanically, the game is a simple adventure, with an appropriate amount of verbs and interactions the player can make. It leans minimally on a survival-horror genre, with limited supplies to use against enemies, but doesn't rely entirely on them. I ended up exploring as much as I could, not because of collecting but because I was craving more storytelling.This game is also really fun! I enjoyed driving around, meeting new people and walking around the world. I'm not big into adventure game puzzles as I can find them either too easy and boring or too difficult and frustrating. Mundaun found a happy-medium, where every next objective was explained when necessary. If I found something I could interact with and didn't understand, I would eventually be told how I could use it when needed. I didn't end up backtracking a lot to figure out if I forgot or missed something, it wasn't much and did not feel like a chore, as the vehicle is fun, the land is nice to look at, and the creepiness of some environments is pleasant to pass through.Mundaun is a wonderful game, and after beating it, wanted to revisit for another possible ending - or just to be in this world again, find the secrets I may have missed and be amazed by the visual moments I may have forgotten about. I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: After 8 Hours I've completed Mundaun and it was an awesome experience. I really love horror game and investigation, and this is what this game is all about. There's also a bit of exploration as you have to investigate through small open area, but you'll never be lost, the level design is perfect, the game design very clever, and if you'r ok with the graphics, it feels really nice and oppresive. There's some nive Lovecraftian vibe in Mundaun story, and also know there's multiple endings.The only small flaw is about aiming interactions, it's not always obvious with which object you will interact if two of them are very close (for example the doors of the oven), but that's really it. Everything else is so cool, interresting story and characters, some stealth mecanisms too, as I said : I reaaaally loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a game that stands out thanks to its arty style and setting. The game is set in a secluded town in the Swiss alps, with all of the characters voiced in a local dialect. In combination with the pencil-drawn art style, the developers at Hidden Fields have created a game that is both visually and thematically engaging, unique in its setting and depiction of Swiss culture. The setting does keep things interesting, pulling, I assume, from local folklore to present a story that while familiar still manages to feel fresh. It’s not the most original story in terms of plot, but there were always aspects that felt novel and kept me engaged. My only two criticisms come from the gameplay aspect. I found some of the puzzles to be a bit obtuse and often referenced a walkthrough as I played. My biggest was with combat, which I felt to be underwhelming and stealth an inconsistent alternative. Neither truly felt like good options when facing enemies, especially since most enemies have ranged attacks that slow your movement. The game doesn’t make it clear what direction you’ve been spotted from, and enemies could often spot you from far away, which made me give up on getting the achievements for not hurting any enemies and not dying (at least for now). As a whole I still found Mundaun to be an engrossing and unique experience. It was cool to see a slice of Swiss culture, and despite my issues with combat and some obtuse puzzles, I found myself quite enamoured with the game by the end of my playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games I've played this year, and one of the best and most unique horror games I've ever played. The game has a really awesome atmosphere that persists throughout, and although its story isn't the most unique, the way it is told and the way it mixes in moments of beauty and peace with the unsettling horror is an experience more than worth the price. This flow of game play, between walking simulator, life simulation, and tense horror is perfectly balanced, and ensures that the game feels legitimately fun to move forward in throughout it's 6-ish hour run time.. Even more credit can be given in how well it handles larger moments, giving them a cinematic quality while not feeling like it puts you on rails. Multiple times throughout I would throw myself behind cover with only a second to spare before death, or jump into my truck and frantically turn the key as enemies advanced on me. It does an incredible job guiding you towards these small moments, while allowing you player agency throughout. Mundaun isn't perfect, as most of the enemies, besides a few near the end, are clunky and occasionally frustrating to deal with, and the multiple endings might leave you feeling unsatisfied if you make a pretty logical decision near the game's end. Despite these, this game is one of the best I've played all year, and is an incredible and entirely worthwhile experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A really neat folk-horror game that takes it's priority toward ever-building dread over spooks for reactions.I do have a minor gripe with the gameplay mainly in how your character can slow to a complete crawl if close to an enemy making it harder to run away while attempting a no-death/no hurting enemies run. (And this is with most of the coffee which I assume is to build resistance to that? I may be wrong however.)The game does suffer from the Unity stutter (Running at high framerate but feels like the frame-pacing is off)But those are minor complaints to what's here. I am purposefully not writing any story details because I do believe it should be experienced knowing the least about it.The art-style speaks for itself and I cannot imagine how time-consuming scanning in all the pencil-drawings to textures was.The game has a focus on exploration and depending on what paths you take, you may need to backtrack more than others. I personally did not mind this at all, but I know some of my friends who don't like that sort of thing. Take it slow, explore every nook and cranny as you get to new areas and you'll be fine :)Amazing work that all those who participated in making it should be proud and I'm really looking forward to whatever these developers make in the future!A solid recommend from me for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little survival horror game. Very atmospheric, gave me vibes of folk horror and German Expressionism. Exploration is often rewarded with tangible benefits. Most enemies can indeed be killed, though you will need to expend resources in order to do so, which helps enable the rewarding side of exploration.This is the kind of horror game I wish that Frictional Games and Bloober Team would make. Being able to actually fight back, while also having that privilege require exploration in order to execute, is something that too many horror games forget is important. If all you're doing is running and hiding, eventually the unease gives way to dull annoyance as you do the same thing over and over.If you can also fight back, but only have so many resources with which to do so, you feel the creeping dread of resource scarcity, and you'll find yourself having to decide whether to run and hide, sneak past, or expend precious resources to fight your problems. Mundaun offers this amidst a sea of mechanically-minimalist haunted house rides that adhere to the erroneous belief that being truly defenceless enhances the experience.Also, you get to pet the goats in this game. Which in itself is a major bonus that more horror games should have.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

Not even gonna talk about the art style since everyone and their mom already is but just know it's super stylized and really sets a mood. Music is fantastic, puzzles are simple but still require a bit of using the ol noggin to get through. Game also has several endings that you don't need to do anything crazy to get to see. All in all, fantastic lil game that really paid off for all the effort put in. Fully recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning little gem of a game. The artstyle is what sells it - I'm glad people have realized there's so much more potential for style in games aside from "trying to be photorealistic" or "cartoon". The story is interesting, the game *oozes* a thick creepy atmosphere not dissimilar from Silent Hill; the soundscape is great. My only gripe is that the combat is really janky and most of the time the enemies feel more of a nuisance than a threat, but it's a very small flaw in an almost perfect game. Play it. We don't get games as good as this very often.

_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying, I believe it's absolutely CRUCIAL you play through this game more than once. With that out of the way, I love this game. I spent so much of my first play through trying to figure out mechanics and how to interact with my inventory that it was hard for me to really appreciate all of the things that make Mundaun great.First of all, atmospherically, the game really excels. You get dropped into Mundaun and it's so easy to get engrossed by your surroundings. The story is great and the cast of characters are wide ranging. This game sucked me in immediately, and these 15 hours (so far) have flown by. Planning to do at least 1 more playthrough. One thing I want to make clear as well, if you're looking for a "horror" game, this isn't the one for you. Is it tense? Yes, but in moments. It doesn't constantly have you on the edge of your seat or anything.Highly recommend! Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is so criminally underrated, it's a damn shame. This is beautiful folklore horror experience that you're not gonna find anywhere else and I mean that. The unique setting, art direction, and culture are enough to set it apart from other more typical horror titles still copying Amnesia and Slender. Mundaun is a nice blend of puzzles, combat, stealth, exploration, and even RPG progression. These elements are rather simple in their design, but that's fine by me. It's a short, cinematic experience that never compromises on its vision. Don't get it twisted. This is NOT a walking sim. There is gameplay. There are enemies. You can die, and there are even multiple endings. It just puts its presentation and narrative first and foremost and it executes this perfectly. The narrative is simple enough, but is nonetheless compelling and uplifted by its folklore influence. It's an emotional story about family and generational sin. The whole reason you're here is to save your grandfather's soul. The voice acting is quite good, especially for the Old Man. He has that sinister tone down perfectly. I found all of the characters memorable to the point where I was getting attached to them. The goats are unironically my favorite characters. They're true friends to the end. The sound design is excellent. The music sets a very creepy tone and adds to the tension while the environmental ambiance creates atmosphere. However, the show stopper here is the art style. This is genuinely one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. Neverending Nightmares had a pencil sketch style as well, but was 2D and not very atmospheric. This game is full 3D with textures that truly look hand drawn. So many moments that looked straight out of a sketchbook. This feels like an interactive nightmare with its dreamlike design. I don't have many complaints. I do think the game could have benefited from better stealth mechanics since enemies can detect you easily from far away and they all attack from range. That said, they're pretty easy to just run away from and hide. Also, you can fight back against them anyway and when you finally get the rifle, it is a glorious moment. Despite there being weapons, they gave never stops being creepy and at times, genuinely scare. There's at least one jumpscare that scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. Well timed and well earned. Mundaun deserves far more attention. We need more unique horror titles like this. There's just too many samey indie horror games out there solely designed for streamers and youtubers to fake scream at. I look forward to whatever this small team creates next.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I can't type enough good things about this game. 1: it has a coherent story2: it has good game mechanics3: it's engaging and you really want to learn the mysterybad: really only 2 quibbles, the "good ending" is not intuitive and I disagree with the rationale, what I thought was the proper ending wasn't.there are some minor bugs and glitches none of which affect or break the game.How one person did this is beyond me, my highest recommendation.

My only gripes are the interact detection can be frustratingly finicky at times (especially while searching for key items) and the way the endings work is kinda of not great.Otherwise a solid 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a captivating first person psychological horror game, with a distinct presentation and immediately gripping story. The game design provided me with one too many frustrations, sadly, and so I ended up quitting and cannot recommend. However, if you're a fan of this genre, there's enough here to warrant giving it a go.You play as Curdin, a man visiting Mundaun following the death of his grandfather, who lived there. Mundaun is a sparse, severely isolated, rural community in the Alps, haunted both metaphorically and literally by a number of events that have taken place there. It's the perfect setting for the chills which follow, and the game beautifully constructs a number of very creepy set-pieces instead of relying on cheap jumpscares.The graphical style is incredible. Everything is rendered in a sepia monochrome, which reflects the folk-tale vibe. This also heightens the tension as lines can be easily misinterpreted as you explore. The soundscape is subtle but also effective, capturing the whistling and rustling of the environment and never letting you feel unwatched.All of these positives really drove me to push on despite some very frustrating design choices. Early on in the game, I encountered two doors, both locked, with no keys to open either, and no indication whatsoever where I might find those keys. 20 minutes of exploring the area produced... nothing... It eventually turned out that I needed to be standing in the right spot and looking at the right rock to trigger a cutscene which permits the game to continue. Any other game, I would have quit at that point, but I decided to continue. Sadly, I encountered similar problems on three further occasions. I realised I was just walking and looking at random, in the hopes of accidentally doing the action which progresses the story.If your familiarity with the genre gives you more patience or intuition with these kinds of problems, then there is enough here to recommend this game. However, I can't recommend based on my experiences, which ended up being characterised by frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really special. The atmosphere and pacing of the story was incredibly well done and you can tell the devs really put a lot of care into it. The music and visuals are both stunning and the gameplay combines the best of survival horror and satisfying exploration and adventure mechanics. Definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The game creates expectation of a certain kind of story-telling, a certain kind of atmosphere, and slowly replaces it with simple scares used to fill in the space between fetching random objects for strangers. Plenty of time is spent on creating an interesting sense of place, but the characters are far from interesting. The game's art-style, to me, implied there would be striking imagery and mounting dread. Instead there were more and more moments of allegedly brutal things suddenly happening that bore no consequence and had no effect on the narrative. I laughed at some of the final scares. The ending let me down, as more things happened, and i felt less and less impact until a sudden gotcha had me rolling my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly very different from my usual 1st person shooter games (far cry, battlefield  etc.) now appreciate a whole new genre, found this game very arty, clever graphics that soon seem very suited to the mood of the events unfolding. basically loved it and did find some scenes made the hair on my neck stand up!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, beautiful game! I completed it in 16 hours in one sitting! I loved the variety of endings, and that you can go back to previous saves to easily complete all the endings!I'm a huge walking simulator fan. I hate that term, but I'm talking about the type of games like Firewatch, Dear Esther, and The Vanishing of Ethan Carter. I have little tolerance for ones where there are enemies, but if the story and overall game is worth it to me, I'll tough it out up to a point. This game is an example of where I almost quit due to the fighting/enemy avoidance, even on easy. However, I'm very glad I stuck with it because it was totally worth it!Another awesome thing about this game is the full controller support! I started it out with keyboard and mouse but found it very hard to steer vehicles, so mid game I switched to my PS4 controller (which worked much better!) and was pleasantly surprised to see tutorials pop up again showing me which buttons to use for journal, inventory, run, crouch, etc. I thought that was a nice touch!The only negative I can think of is the jump. It's more of a little hop, really. I'd ask why it's even there, except it did get me over a sticky threshold of one building.Other than that, overall, very awesome game! The hand-drawn pencil graphics give it a creepy look, the story keeps the right tension, and there's even two or three jump scares for good measure! I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Very difficult to get into.The setting, aesthetic, mood, set-pieces, and characters are strong points. The story might be good, and the gameplay got good eventually. But I'm sure you can tell that this game is good just by watching the trailer.That said, it makes itself difficult to get into for the following reasons:- While it does NOT have a real time system, it doesn't tell you that at first.- The puzzles usually don't make it clear whether you have all the tools you need, or if you need to progress the story first.- The first enemy encounter is a bit too rough if you don't make the coffee as soon as you can, so keep that in mind. HOWEVER, this may trick you into systematically exploring every section of the map like it's your second job. Don't do that. Set the difficulty to easy and be done with it.Overall, I would recommend but be prepared for the game to throw you some curve-balls, like giving you a fair few rifle upgrades before even giving you a rifle.EDIT: Ending was pretty dull. It uses the Endingtron 5000 with a good and bad ending (a tired trope in my view), and there was no emotion to the climax. I would just barely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: With its distinctive hand-drawn visual style, slow pacing, intriguing story, minimalist UI and immersive sound design, I'm recommending this game wholeheartedly to everyone with an interest in first-person exploration games. The 'horror' part stems more from atmospheric worldbuilding and the feeling of helplessness (even slowing the player's movement when in a dangerous situation or near an enemy, much like you would experience during a nightmare) than from any actual threats. Enemies are easy to kill and even easier to avoid when following the game's many show-and-tell tutorial mechanics, but both combat and stealth parts play a minor role throughout the game.Dialogue with the many quirky NPCs and the protagonist’s inner monologue take center-stage, both featuring the language of Rhaeto-Romanic, spoken only in a small part of the canton of Grisons. The folklore-fueled story is compelling and even warrants more than one playthrough as there are multiple endings depending on a few choices the player is presented with. A playthrough will take you anywhere from four to nine hours and the semi-open layout of the three rather large areas suits both purists and completionists alike. Explorers are going to be rewarded with items and/or locations needed to get some of the game's achievements.Do yourself a favor: Take a hike in the Swiss mountains, treat yourself to a mysterious village above the sea of fog and take in the beautifully recreated alpine scenery before
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is pretty solid case of style and substance managing to drown out some honestly pretty stale gameplay. Its a good length for what you're getting, but sluggish controls and barely functioning enemies keep the game from being truly great and not just memorable. Pros: - The aged sepia tone look and feel paired with the old swiss mountain village is great.  This game aesthetically made me think about Haneke's "The White Ribbon"- In addition to the first point, the hand drawn art style is stellar and helps really fit the game. All of these visual elements also helped soften the "horror" of the game and make it feel more unique and special than just run of the mill horror. - I loved the story and the few characters given (the goats are GOAT tbh)- Stopping to look at things sometimes triggers sounds and camera movements that made exploring feel deeper than it actually wasCons:- Movement sucks. Its stiff and varies between slow and slower depending on your terrain. This was an 8 hour playthrough for me and I'm confident it would have been closer to 6 if the walking speed were suited to something a little more on par with modern games. - Combat is boring, but you can skip it for the most part- Load times annoyed me a bit. Didn't think about it until the end, but there was a part in the final act that is somewhat challenging (due to the movement and combat issues) and caused me to die a few times and the reloads were enough that I got kind of annoyed. There are more pros and cons but these are things that really standout to me, and while the pros definitely outweigh the cons, there is disappointment in knowing how this could have been such a great indie and not just a really good one. Light to strong 7 on this one. Props for making something different.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A really pleasant experience overall. Short but sweet. It's horror elements are minor if that's something that puts you off but still has a tense atmosphere that kept me hooked for the full time I played through it. I should mention it does have one jumpscare that nearly killed me because I absolutely wasn't expecting it.It has a distinct visual style that makes everything look as though it was a pencil drawing which really unique and despite looking very stylized it does a good job of immersing you in the world. This is helped by a surprisingly strong soundtrack with songs that really emphasize each of the key moments in the story. It also has some pretty solid sound design which I greatly enjoyed.I definitely recommend this one for anyone looking for a short little singleplayer experience that has a fun mix of horror, exploration and some occasional simple puzzles. The branching paths towards the end of the game weren't the best choice in my opinion as they might leave you with an ambiguous ending or lack of closure as it did in my case. That said, it was an enjoyable story overall and it didn't completely detract from the full package.
