_childDocuments_.review: The horror is at times quite vivid when the game is in its storytelling mode, but the gameplay is never suitably tense and is, in my opinion, always slower and less eventful than it should be. But, then again, had things been faster paced (in a horror/tension kind of way) and more eventful, the stealth, action, and combat would likely just drag this game down even further than it already does. What is for certain is that the art is, usually, pretty wonderful and I appreciate the Swiss setting and culture as intriguing and unique to horror videogames. I just wish the game was more tightly designed around its horror gameplay rather than the art and plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a rather wild mix of concepts and mechanics with a unique swiss alps horror story.As other negative reviews have pointed out, the enemies basically ruin this game (for me) since they serve no purpose other then being annoying roadblocks that slow down progress. What starts as a really unique walking-simulator soon becomes overloaded with a few too many mechanics. Enemies, cars/driving, sanity system, health upgrades, fetch quests. The game would be better off if it did focus on fewer mechanics, especially the exploration, storytelling and puzzles in my opinion, unfortunately the puzzles are also a bit lacking and in 2.5 hours I encountered only a single one.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A proper atmospheric horror game that brings one of the most unique styles and some of the best storytelling to the genre. The hand-drawn charcoal textures and the faded palate create an unsettling feeling that you're being watched at all moments, with a score that will send a chill through your bones to the tips of your hair. It envelopes you in the rich folklore of the Swiss Alps and pokes at a child-like fear of monsters in the closet. Mundaun is a game that forces you to confront horrors while curating your curiosity to the point of self destruction.Now that we have the pretentious ♥♥♥♥ out of the way, this game is amazing! Its truly unique, I can't even think of another game to compare it to. The mechanics are easy to get into, and the overall flow of the narrative feels organic and engaging. Whip out your wallets peeps, its $20. For this quality, its a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A delightly devilish tour de force of slightly spooky shenanigans.  While not self soilingly scary, certainly there are unsettling things that'll keep grandma up at night!  (Aka, watering the goat).The atmosphere, and charm, are both charming, and atmospherical. If you have an older monitor, that doesn't properly display all of todays modern color schemes, you'll be alright with this purchase, as it uses shades of one color.  Gunplay is horrible, the main character acts as if the gun is a pencil in which they are learning to draw the perfect circle, instead of using it as an instrument of death.  The wicker men can burn in hell...Go play Rotgut.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The Overwhelmingly Positive reviews are completely earned.This game is excellent and completely unique to the entire genre of psychological horror gaming. It's art style is used to great effect, as if horror film noir is a thing.It doesn't beat the player over the head with obvious hints, and allows you to explore and figure things out in an intuitive way.The narrative is VERY well done and it has a definite story to tell, and does so in a unique way with a great antagonist.Genuinely creepy and mysterious, but without major cliche's found in other games.PS- I have never been to Switzerland, and now I don't want to.  ;)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little walking simulator, with a nice pencil colored art style. While it's hard for me to classify it completely as "horror" there was definitely one moment which gave me a startle. I'd say it's got a pretty nice ambiance, taking place in the Swiss mountains. Though, the story often verges into a bit of absurdist surrealism, which makes the tone a bit unusual at times.The game is short too. You can easily finish this in a day.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is clearly a result of very hard work from an indie studio, and it provides a unique aesthetic experience with everything (everything?) drawn by hand. It does a very good job of setting the right atmosphere for a "rural horror" story (the use of Romanche was great in that regard), which happens to be coherent.However, it also does many things poorly:1. Faces and hands are hideous: they are not even creepy, just cartoonish.2. Movements (or controls) are horrendous. Jumping, running, and crawling are unintuitive. Driving a vehicle is absolute madness. Pointing and shooting feel extremely clunky, so combat is a mess.3. It is usually unclear where exactly the game wants you go to, and how to get there. 4. For some reason you get automatic zooming in when standing still and facing a wall. This is ridiculous.5. It is buggy as hell. The worst bug is that if you pause the game (or go alt + tab) when there are dialogs onscreen, or even get anything resembling a pop-up from your computer (I got an Nvidia notification), you get stuck and have to reload the game. Also, at least one achievement seems to be locked somehow.6. The saving system is very inconvenient, especially if you want all achievements.7. It felt tedious all the way, except near the end. Puzzles are simple once you know how to solve them; otherwise, they are a nightmare. There were many instances where I got stuck so badly that I had to look up the answer in a guide.I believe there is a gem hidden beneath all that dirt, but I cannot recommend this game in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game, but I just can't.To its credit, it's an absorbing horror yarn with a little light combat to spice things up. It has a unique aesthetic, an interesting cultural spin, some clever mechanics, and it's about the right length. It also doesn't try too hard to be scary.Unfortunately, it is also fatally flawed.On a couple of occasions, you can get yourself into a state where you have literally no idea what to do next. Worse, on those occasions, the game's diary/notebook tells you to do something that your character explicitly refuses to do.Resorting to Google is never fun, but I could have forgiven those hiccups if not for the fact that I can't complete the game. I got to a certain point quite near the end, and I am stuck. I can't do anything but repeat the same two lines of dialogue. I can't move, use my inventory or any other items - it's game over. Reloading from an earlier save leads to the same result, so all the build up and interest and excitement has soured.

_childDocuments_.review: I like a lot of things about Mundaun. Unease permeates most of the journey, only fading away at times when the pastoral beauty simply becomes overwhelming through picturesque views of the mountainside parish. The Swiss folk horror storytelling mixed with good ol' creepy Catholicism and light touches of antique tech gives the game such distinct character, blurring the familiar with the unfamiliar to heighten the feeling of things being a bit off-kilter. There's a quiet confidence to the slow pacing that I admire. The game lets you explore open environments at your own leisure without worrying about you triggering progress to hit the next plot beat. Curiosity is rewarded with scraps of worldbuilding, items to help you on your quest, or arresting vistas of the mystic alps. It never feels like a waste of time to get off the beaten path. When you  on the critical path, you find yourself somnambulating through hazy daydreams of hay demons and paper vessels slicing sea and sky, ponderously navigating chiaroscuro nightmares of talking severed goat heads and dark figures casting ominous shadows, and spiraling into vignetted memories of foregone duty and pacts undone in claustrophobic tunnels and caverns as you stare into pictures that stir the past. Oh, and you do simple horror adventure game puzzles like play musical notes on hooked carcasses so that a key oozes out of a hanged man's mouth. You drive a hay baling truck sometimes. You can tune its radio to any of the stations that play different flavors of traditional church music, operatic ballads, and local talk radio in Romansh, then leave it playing as you wander off. You can also turn on the headlights to serve as a beacon at night. But you can't leave the engine running. You have to turn the key every time you get in to start moving your beloved Muvel. It can go surprisingly fast, but its handling cannot handle any surface outside clearly marked roads at a speed any faster than a crawl. You have to drive it deliberately, somewhat like a normal person in a normal world would, or you risk careening off winding tracks and barreling down steep slopes. It can feel a .That deliberateness and silliness extend to the rest of the mechanics, in a way that's charming and effective at times and immersion-breaking at others. When I had to make coffee by filling a pan with water by the fountain a stone's throw away from grandpa's house, returning home to put it on top of a stove, pouring coffee beans into the water-filled pan, placing a log in a compartment and lighting it on fire, waiting to let the coffee boil, then using a cup to collect the coffee, I found the process to be a soothing little ritual. When I had to weakly poke at lumbering enemies with a pitchfork that broke off one prong with every hit, rendering it useless after three strikes, resulting in two consecutive game over screens for me, I found myself cursing at the intrusion of combat and hard failure states once more. Never have I so quickly turned down the difficulty setting of a video game to easy. The explicitly game-y stat upgrades and on-screen text like saying you did "bonus damage" for a successful sneak attack feel so out of place and took me out of the reverie whenever I had to contend with them. They're jarring compromises to facilitate survival horror elements that don't add anything to the experience. I don't need the game to be a straight-up, conflict-free, linear walking sim, but the puzzle-solving and exploration were totally enough to keep me engaged on a mechanical level. The tension in the narrative and presentation was all the tension i needed.While I can't say I was emotionally engrossed in the story and that it was fairly easy to grok the broad strokes, the odd imagery in its set sequences and the small tricks it pulls made for a captivating time. I wanted to see what weird thing it would show me next, and I was satisfied with the ending that fit the genre. Aside from a couple of minor complaints about the mechanics, I enjoyed Mundaun, with the pencil-drawn visual style, the unsettling mood, and the strange sights as the obvious highlights.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember how Mundaun ended up on my wishlist, but I'm so glad I saw it there and bought it.The visual style does not serve to necessarily overwhelm with oppressive and dreary atmosphere. There is a lot of elements which can be considered silly, but non of them feel out of place. You build snowmen to distract enemies, race in sledges and blow smoke from a pipe to fend of aggressive bees, but all these elements show confidence in how much can rest of the game unnerve. Moments of idyll relaxation mix with the uncanny and surreal in such a way that at no point did I felt like what the game is making me feel was unintentional. For a horror game, the fact that it can evoke a feeling of serine calmness may go underappreciated, but I find it incredibly that it never detracts from the creepiness. Said creepiness is also derived largely from the art direction, which can be subtly disturbing in how subjective certain patterns and shapes can appear. I saw faces in wooden walls that I'm still not sure were put there on purpose. The way the Old Man morphs, shifts and twitches would probably look cheesy if there were more details in the models, but with every texture being drawn on paper with a real pencil, scanned and put in the game, there is enough vagueness that imagination can conjure a much more memorable and believable vision of this world that photo realist attempts would. Sound and voice acting also helps with getting immersed into this dreamlike experience and music never distracts but always enhances moments when it's used.The strongest element of this game however is not the presentation, but it's story and gameplay, which I can compare to Kona with no survival elements and simplified investigation angle. It consists mainly of exploring several mid-sized open environments and solving different puzzles or avoiding occasional enemy encounters. Said encounters may not be fantastic on their own, but they do add some stakes and intensity to the story as a whole. Complete lack of any danger in the game would perhaps make it a little too tame, so presence of even the most basic stealth and combat is welcome (and yes, there is some basic combat, you even get a gun later on). Existence of the enemies is also an excuse for putting items which increase your max health or shooting skills around the map. So exploration of all the numerous hidden and optional locations is rewarded with some practical benefits, on top of uncovering some story and lore elements which help to puzzles the whole story.  Speaking of story - it is simply amazing. I can't remember the last time I was this intrigued by not only what this whole thing is about, but also about that happens next. There are multiple ending and which one you get depends on a few actions, all of which you make in the last 30 minutes or so. Weirdly however, what decisions to make towards the end, is not really informed by everything you've seen before, not directly anyway. To get the 'good' ending, you not only have to do something that seems to not align with rest of the story, it goes 180 degrees in the opposite direction. This is in line the the whole plot being a sort of 'trick', but it can result in consequences feeling unearned at first. After some considerations and analyses I think that thematically it works and said 'trick' is clever enough to be 'fair', but feeling 'tricked' by an ending is rarely a positive in any context. The best thing about the story however is the slow discovery and unraveling of the compelling mystery at it's core. The slower pace of the story goes along perfectly with the pace of exploration and gameplay in general, as wall as the horror elements. And I say 'elements' because this isn't much of a horror game. Based on the art style you may think that it's going for a feeling of relentless terror present in every frame, but as I wrote above, it's full of silly and frolic elements, some of which can be considered creepy in an off kilter, macabre kind of way (talking goat head or walking straw men), but some of which are deliberately there to be fun and to entertain the player (man from the bunker for example is clearly a comic relief character, as is the soldier stock in the snow). The tone is not meant to be monochromatic, it has clear elements for a horror but that doesn't mean that driving volka into enemies is not meant to make you laugh. It may not be an objective flaw, but I can see how some might find the lightness of this game disappointing. For me, all the elements together help create a unique and special kind of experience, I've never had with any other video game I can think of. It's addicting, fun, creepy, beautiful, intriguing and truly one of a kind. I'm looking forward to anything this dev makes next.

_childDocuments_.review: Art, atmosphere, and sound design? Top notch.Game play? Not so much. There were plenty of times where I’d want to walk to some area. Only for the character to stop and say “I’ll check that later.” Where I realized this was an incredibly linear game. Once I hit a story beat, then I was able to walk to the given area. Even though the only thing blocking my way was an invisible wall. I also found gameplay to be rather barren. More of a walking simulator with some puzzles. Occasionally doing other stuff.Oh and the inventory system isn’t robust at all. If you’re expecting Re 4 levels of item management. Think again, like any horror game I was an utter kleptomaniac. Hoarding all items only using them as needed. Braving any off beaten paths to find more stuff. Not once did I ever run the risk of filling up the inventory. It’s just a glorified menu. _childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is not a very good game, it's not bad, but it's just very plain.The visuals are okay, the "hand drawn" part of it is in name only, Only the textures are hand drawn, everything else is a typical low poly model and it rarely sells the feeling of the game being hand drawn. Maybe the dev tried it and it didn't work, but looking at mountains with stretched pencil textures is just not right.Audio is fine.Game design wise, it's very much your typical fetch quest adventure game. You are following literal instructions with "story" dripping in the background (most of which you can piece together very early on). There are  bugs and lack of polish and way you interact with objects is infuriating.The game feels like an idea of "a lovingly hand-penciled horror tale" put to life, except why is this a game? _childDocuments_.review: You'd think indie games would have freedom not to do what is done in regular dumb commercial games. And sure, this game has remarkable hand-drawn visuals and the daring choice to publish in an obscure European language -- I did not even know Romansh existed before I played this game. But  has everything a regular dumb commercial game has, including:- stupid pointless open world- stupid pointless combat - stupid pointless enemies who are there just to annoy you and make you waste your time- stupid pointless jumpscares- stupid pointless upgrades- stupid pointless objective list- stupid pointless choices- stupid pointless multiple endingsThe first, like, 20 minutes of the game are great. It graciously hooks you on the disturbing atmosphere of the village (almost) without recurring to any of the elements I listed above. But the moment the first enemies appeared and I noticed I would be annoyed by playing hide and seek with haystacks, I almost lost interest. I mean, you can't even have fun fighting the enemies like in . This game gave employs that ridiculous system from  where your weapon breaks after three hits and then you are forced to run.Hell, it has been more than 10 years that walking simulators have become a thing. And what indie developer have learned? Why regress to stupid pointless mechanics and design choices? I still firmly believe that video games are a medium that has something worthwhile to offer. The problem is not in the medium. The problem is in the stupid audience who wants stupid pointless things

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is an interesting game carried primarily by its art style and atmosphere. The hand drawn but still 3D style of the game ensures it will be a memorable experience and really helps it create a fantastic atmosphere. The developers love of the game's setting is clear as well. The feeling of being in the mountains is captured well and small touches like a chair lift that rattles at the appropriate time over pylons adds a lot to the game. The story of the game is decent though it won't stick with me for too long. The biggest issue with the game is the enemies and combat. It's never clear whether is really focused on stealth, combat, or another approach however none of these ideas are satisfying or even fully functional. Still, I'd recommend grabbing this game on a sale just to experience what makes it unique because those aspects are genuinely worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a celebration of the unusual, perfectly combining just the right quantities of mystery, intrigue and fear to concoct a cocktail that is unlike anything you've ever tried before. None of its ingredients, nor the emotions they evoke upon the player, are overpowering to the extent that they dilute the others, and rarely have I played a game where I am regularly unable to predict - even guess - what will happen next.The game mostly involves exploring one of the three decent-sized areas of the map, using NPC conversations, environmental storytelling, and occasional combat to help you complete each objective in your journal that, in turn, helps to clarify the fateful actions your grandpa took decades ago in the war that eventually led to his mysterious demise.The visual aesthetic of the game is as unusual as it is captivating, and it doesn't change from the opening bus ride until you reach one of the five endings. This charcoal drawing effect may take some getting used to at first, but you soon realise that it's absolutely perfect, as it gives the player the constant feeling that they're not quite in reality, heightening their sense of unease, and adding an extra angle to the occasionally-injected moments of horror that the game loves to throw at you from time to time. The endings themselves are perhaps the only criticism I have for this work of art, for the simple reason that including the "multiple endings based on your decisions throughout the game" trope felt unnecessary and superfluous. It doesn't go over the top with it - five possible endings based on two or three decisions during gameplay - but the ending that I, along with most other people, got, would have been perfectly fitting by itself.Some may also criticise the game's combat mechanics, aiming and "firing" your weapons feeling cumbersome and unintuitive. However, I didn't mind that approach, as it reinforced upon me the notion that I'm just an ordinary guy trying to figure out what on Earth is going on around here. Furthermore, with combat only being a minor element of the game (indeed it can be avoided altogether as demonstrated by the pacifist Steam achievement), this minor gripe holds little traction.Don't let either of these minor points put you off though, as the art style, audio, exploration, continuous mild unease, creative gameplay elements and well-written story are more than enough to make Mundaun a worthy purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The sketch book art style absolutely makes Mundaun. Beyond it being visually unique, it feels essential to building the creepy atmosphere found here. The narrative is a weird take on atoning for the crimes of the past. For the most part I enjoyed it, but the game doesn’t quite stick the landing. If you want a game that wouldn’t feel too out place from an A24 film, Mundaun feels like a great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Came here from an old RagnarRox video.Delightful little game. Really suits fans of folk horror with its interesting designs and the balance between the whimsy of walking around the beautiful mountain air and the dread and horror lingering under it is struck well. Incredible art design and I very much enjoyed my time in Switzerland.The main criticism is a lot of goals and puzzles are not well telegraphed and can be infuriating when something super minor with no indication at all, is a major part of a puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game might be the perfect version of a walking sim. It's got a great story, it oozes atmosphere, and there's actual gameplay both in the form of combat/stealth as well as good puzzles. In addition to this the game has fairly large areas to explore but it guides the player quite well towards forward progression. This is done in obvious ways through lines of dialogue and on screen tips and also in more subtle ways like placing an excess of spare keys and visual contrast in the areas of the game to help navigate. The game also has many convivence features like good checkpoints, faster travel mechanisms (along with workarounds in case you leave your vehicle behind or get stuck). Even the fact that the game tracks every save as a separate file is great for exploring the multiple endings!On the negative side I've only got a few critiques. I felt that the story's pacing got a bit stagnant towards the end of the 2nd act in to the 3rd, though it was never bad it just got a bit of a slog where it has you running back and forth across large areas. I also found the bee segment to be more frustrating than clever or immersive. While I immediately knew how to combat this enemy I died several times due to the janky item usage in the game. It would have ruined the immersion but some sort of visual indicator for your cooldown would have been so nice. Aside from that one segment the combat is well tuned, it's doable to fight enemies but clearly not the best option, especially if you're playing on hard mode where one pitchfork is likely to only last long enough to take out one enemy. The driving mechanics were fun albeit comically janky, which did take me out of the more serious tone the rest of the game is going for but it's overall a net positive.Very much worth checking out if you're looking for a heavily story driven game that's a nice slow burn.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: is a very unique first-person horror puzzle / mystery game with a very interesting story and a beautiful, hand-drawn look. It features great voice acting spoken in Romansh (with subtitles of course), a relatively uncommon language spoken in parts of Switzerland, where the game takes place.The gameplay was slightly confusing at first,  But I got used to it quickly.I had one small issue, where if I tabbed out of the game, I couldn't figure out how to unpause with my keyboard. I solved this by turning on a controller and pressing B.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Bizarre and evocative folk horror game. The main draw here is the hand-drawn art, which seems to be entirely textured in charcoal and pencil for a completely unique aesthetic. This helps all the horror feel more abstracted, and more visceral for being less representational. The game is not very long, and I think it's at its weakest when it tries to be a survival horror game (I recommend playing on easy so you can just run from enemies). But the atmosphere and music is top-notch, and as a horror experience I think it's very worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I was lukewarm with this game at first, it felt like a good game but i still wasn't sure if would actually enjoy it. But at around the 80 minute mark the game, in my opinion, gets A LOT better. And i have to say that i really enjoyed my experience. I played for a total of 6 hours before beating the game and i would definitely recommend it. The enemies are kind of janky to begin with but in the later chapter you get a rifle AND there is a new kind of enemy which is just so much fun to play against. I also really liked the story too, which is another thing that i was unsure i'd like when i first played. But i do like the variety that this game has considering the story elements get even better as well.TLDR: Good game. Underrated. Should get.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn by the combination of beautiful art style and horror game. The aesthetic of it is truly astonishing and somehow adds a layer of mysterious strange vibe to the game. But as lots of comments said, the control is beyond difficult when it comes to fighting the enemies. I tried both controller  and keyboard, and they both gave me pretty hard time. Eventually, I was forced to hide from enemies most of the time instead of fighting them. The puzzles are adequately designed and the hint on journal will keep you in line. It is easy to get lost especially during night time. I got very puzzled about the ending I got  but still willing to revisit the game some other time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A game with incredible atmosphere and a very unique art style. The story is engaging and surreal, and the setting is equal parts tranquil and sinister. The gameplay is simple, basically just picking items up and using them at the appropriate time, but the simplicity doesn't harm the experience. To me, it was part of the charm.I found that Mundaun really shines in the quiet moments. The moments spent making coffee or closing shutters are just as effective as the big set piece events. Sometimes it has an almost cosy feel, interrupted by all the spooky stuff going on. I really loved the folk horror vibes.My only complaint is with the combat, if you can call it that, which is extremely clunky and best avoided. Luckily you aren't forced into it and can choose to sneak around.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous game with an innovative visual style, an incredible sense of atmosphere, some lovely and very effective sound design, and an intriguing story that never gives too much away. This game is really nice. I do have some itty-bitty issues though. There are some issues with interactions as mentioned above, you can relatively easily lock yourself somewhere or fall out of the map if you mash interact too hard. This is especially true in scripted sequences. It's also a little finicky interacting with your backpack items, and I personally wish a few more common use items had hotkeys like the lantern. And a really basic issue, I wish there was an option for a reticle. There's a lot of ambiguity in which thing you're interacting with, especially on items with multiple moving parts like the stoves, and a simple low opacity dot would fix these issues completely.All that aside, I think this is a really worthwhile experience, give it a shot. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a game developed by Hidden Fields and published by Annapurna InteractiveThe game offers some nice graphics and a really beautiful aesthetic, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with it being incredibly short and not offering much in terms of gameplay and more of a short, touching story. For me personally, it didn't bug me at all but if you're expecting a really deep, intricate game with some clever gameplay mechanics and such, Mundaun isn't the game for you.Mundaun overall, however, is a short, beautiful game to play, it is a good interactive horror adventure game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a breath of fresh air. The puzzles in the game were even more intriguing because of the artwork medium, and I appreciate that- it was beautiful to play. The story was so bizarre and quite fun to discover throughout the game. I had a ton of fun driving around, and exploration is encouraged, which is a bonus for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good.  Great art direction and a legitimate understanding of creepy and unsettling visuals, sound, and setting make this a very good indie horror title.  The story is not overly complicated but it is told well.  Exploration is fun and the segments of map instead one large open world was the correct decision for this game.  Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a weird game, but in a good way.A fantastically atmospheric horror-esque adventure game viewed through the lens of hand-drawn Swedish countrysides - Mundaun is a unique 'walking-simulator' with combat, stealth, and multiple endings. Take your time, bask in the beauty, meet the townsfolk, ask the severed goat head for directions.I've seen some say the game's length (6-ish hours) is a negative, but I disagree - Mundaun presents its story quickly and wraps it up before the mechanics can start to get stale. Perfect for a few comfy nights of spooky survival in the Alps.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning and soothing to play. I wouldn't call this game a horror game besides the single jumpscare that happens. It's mostly just a walking simulator through beautiful environments and grabbing item to item to get to the next location. Which I was totally fine doing as I really enjoyed the overall vibe and uniqueness the game had, Mundaun is a breath of fresh air.Some big complaints I have is that the tacked on different endings seems kinda stupid and didn't really do anything for the story other than make it feel unsatisfying. Also, even though you get upgrades to your movement speed, you still move way to slow through most of the game. A lot of the padding simply comes from walking which can be painful at points. The movement speed should have been 15 to 20% faster, which would have cut the game time a lot and made it more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Accidentally stumbled upon this gem. Great storytelling and an amazing art + atmosphere combination. Some puzzles were hard to figure out, but that's the charm of it. You do not get any pointers that show you the way in which you have to go to complete tasks and progress, but you do get a journal that tells you what your task is - the rest is up to you to figure out.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, wish there were more stuff like this out there. The visuals and atmosphere are a really unique mix of creeping you out while also making you admire the views. The story is pretty interesting, partly due to them really driving home local culture from the bit less used setting. You can tell the devs really put their heart into this.And it's not just another typical walking simulator either, there's some combat and different tools to use against enemies even though the game isn't really about the fighting. If you try to find and collect everything it's a nice challenge.Negatives are somewhat regular bugs like if you alt-tab often you can lock yourself out from menus. Saves are pretty regular so it's nothing you can't deal with
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10, what this game does well, it does really well. The art is beautiful especially with the mountain scenery. The world feels full of life but devoid at the same time, and exploring is very fun. The story is great although 1 of the 4 (theres 4 i think) endings is just a "what just happened" moment. It isn't really horror so much as being semi linear exploration with everything being unsettling.The combat sucks easily the worst combat I've ever seen, it just feels slapped in, it's incredibly hard and half the time impossible.Buy it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy but not scary.Original in all the aspects where originality matters.Does not require a walkthrough.Easy to digest folklore horror story.Good script. Likeable characters. Slightly annoying, but avoidable enemies (I played on easy and I don't regret it).Deserves to be mentioned alongside titles like Layers of Fear.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: my first steam game reviewi adored it !! devoured it !!! folklore FTWit got all the mythology you could ever neednature as a source of endless inspirationand how wonderful michel ziegler (the creator/game designer) paid respect to the material by writing the dialogue in romanshi love you, you are so sweet and kind, thank you for your generosity and genius for creating this beautiful experience leaving a review as apparently It really helps the game a lot
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A real gem of atmospheric horror. The unique art style combined with fascinating lore and narrative really lets you suspend your disbelief and get completely absorbed in the world in a way that very few games can manage. A must-play for anyone who enjoys a slow-burn approach to horror along with some surreal elements and rewarding exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 can't think of a single bad thing to say. If you are even remotely interested in this game your should play it. Will it be your favorite game? Maybe not, but it is just really good.It was well written the game play was functional and aided in telling that story. Many story driven games ignore fun for emotions, but this game managed to do both.The art is excellent, the hand drawn textures really help keep the tone. Where so many games end up looking the same and distracting the player, this game stands out. The music is excellent, Both the diegetic radio tracks, and the original score.The voice acting is surprisingly good for a game of this scale. The Old Man would not have had nearly as much impact with bad or no voice.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Played on PS5. I don’t write reviews. But this game is so astoundingly unique, and mesmerizing tonally, it truly is in a class all to itself. The mystery and pacing is executed masterfully resulting in a transcendent horror experience. The art style is strikingly original and weird as hell in the best way. Beyond that, the distinct setting and folklore of the region are on full display here, enlightening players who may not be familiar beforehand. It’s just hands down one of the best indie horror games I’ve played, and I truly can’t recommend it highly enough. Cheers
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a wonderful horror game, and I would highly recommend it. The hand-drawn artwork lent to a sense of being lost in time, being trapped in a world outside of our own. This feeling was compounded through the exclusive use of Romansh in all dialogue, giving the game a voyeuristic notion, as I felt an outsider looking in at all that was occurring. Mundaun is an excellent example of slow-burn horror and it begs you to take your time as you explore it, with an absence of markers or way-points encouraging you to seek out its secrets. Whilst the game consists of a lot of walking, each area has unique objectives and distinct styles that keep the game feeling fresh. Combat is a welcome addition, and the difficulty with you dispatch enemies fits perfectly into the games narrative. The story kept me gripped throughout and I spent much of my time in the game trying to find every note and picture to piece together the wider aspects of the narrative. Mundaun is an easy recommendation for me and is unfortunately an underappreciated hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The handdrawn textures and sepia look add a lot to the wonderfully eery and weird feeling of the game. It's a very fresh setting for a horror story with a lot of things to do, puzzles, some fighting if you like and a lot to explore. I really enjoyed the calmness of the horror, the storytelling and the design and different ways of fighting the enemies.I'm also from the alps and could piece together some tales, others felt new and peculiar.Definitely worth a look, especially if you have played a lot of horror and are looking for something fresh.And if you like calm horror games who don't only rely on jump scares and gore.Also, you can pet the goat. 10/10I really really loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Initially got this because of the unique art style, but was genuinely surprised with the game's broad design. Mundaun covers a whole lot of ground, but it is stubbornly immersive, with all of its varied mechanics having just enough depth to pull you into its world. From a horror perspective it's less  terrifying and more surreal, focusing on the strange and disconcerting. It employs a lot of neat tricks to unnerve you. Look closely at any picture in the game and you'll understand what I mean.Mundaun has become my gold standard for horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: this game was everything that  i have ever wanted and is the reason that i play video games to begin with. at some point in my lifetime i have started to watch alot of horror movies especially ones that are filled with folklore and give you anxiety/dread. thankfully i was able to actually live through that this time as a playable character instead of a passive movie watcher. that being said, the game has its minor flaws. movement is slow unless you turn of vsync, and the car driving can be a bit awkwardbut those are minor issues. the main flaw is probably the combat. i actually really liked setting the hay people on fire as well as poking them with the sharp melee weapon (haystick), but than you get to the point of the game where you get a rifle and thats when i didnt like it as much. the gun is pretty shaky and sometimes even when i am aiming point blank at an enemy the bullet will go through, its still the most powerful game in the weapon though and overall after a while you get used to it and you know how to use it better. again these are all very MINOR flaws. the actual experience of being transported to another world is the most valuable aspect of this game that i emjoyed the most and i am definitely picking up whatever the developers are making next if its horror based!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The town of Mundaun is very small, with only ten or so residents. It's main exports are honey, hay, and livestock produce. Should one choose to visit Mundaun, despite being about as remote as you can get without being an uncontacted tribe, there are a few sights that might be worth seeing. The local chapel is of immaculate construction, with beautiful illustrations upon the walls. There are spectacular views of the countryside, including many perches overlooking the valley, the lake, and the nearby peaks. Near the summit of the mountain, there are some decent ski and sled slopes, though nothing that any hobbyist hasn't seen before.Overall, I enjoyed my time in Mundaun, but travelers accustomed to more accessible or comfortable locales may want to carefully consider whether or not they'd want to visit.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. My first playthrough lasted for 9,5 hours. I've only completed one, of what I think might be three, endings. I failed my mission in playing the game as thorough as possible so I will be replaying the game in some time. The narrative, graphics, story telling, score, and overall story is very entertaining and immersive. It's hard to stop, once you've first gotten into playing. The narrative can sometimes get slightly corny, and some of the game mechanics and physics were wonky. Still, the game holds quite good replay value, and is well worth the price, especially for half price. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding, if not for the art style alone. Personally, I'm really drawn (no pun intended) to games with distinctive art styles, so I had to give Mundaun a try with its immediately eye-catching black and white, hand-drawn art.While the art style is probably the highlight of the game, I have to say that the story is also very engaging. Mundaun is a horror, walking simulator/survival horror type of game where you're not overly in danger of dying, but you're also not mindlessly walking. Unlike more "traditional" walking simulators like What Remains of Edith Finch or Dear Esther, you can die in Mundaun. However, the game is more lenient in terms of inventory management and saving compared to traditional survival horror games like Resident Evil. This makes Mundaun a more atmospheric, narrative horror game that rides the line between something like Soma and Amnesia: The Dark Descent.The fact that the game is set in a remote Swiss city and the characters speak in Romansh helps with immersion into this strange world and story. I really liked the voice acting, sound design, and music; all of it was really good.I guess that's mostly what will be the deciding factor for most people on whether they want to play the game or not. The gameplay itself is nothing extraordinary; it's good, but it's not outstanding compared to the other elements of the game. As with most first-person games, you'll be doing a lot of walking, have a chance to drive, and need to solve some puzzles. I think the key to a good puzzle is feeling a satisfying "ah ha!" moment when you realize the solution. However, Mundaun's puzzles rarely provide that, with most puzzles either having the solution given to you (like the puzzle to cross the bridge near the end) or not being very puzzling in the first place (like the puzzle with the meat slabs). The combat isn't very deep or sophisticated, so it isn't very satisfying either. The stealth mechanics are very bare bones, to the point that it's kind of misleading to call it stealth compared to other games with actual stealth mechanics. Lastly, the exploration isn't entirely unsatisfying, but it's also not very productive, with most of the exploration's rewards being lore notes and some items that might help if you want to get 100% achievements.The game itself can be completed fairly quickly (although you might have to play it at least twice if you want to get 100% achievements). So overall, I'd recommend this game to anyone who's into narrative-horror games with distinctive art styles, but with the understanding that the game's mechanics might not be as memorable as the art and the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Such a lovingly crafted experience, its unlike any other game I played in recent memory. While Mundaun's gameplay may leave some to be desired, its atmosphere and artstyle are top notch. If I had to put Mundaun into a genre, I would say its a folk horror game, however its pretty light on horror, I experienced only one jump scare. Its more strange than scary, its dripping with atmosphere and the use of Romansh language makes it feel even more "alien".What's most unique about Mundaun however is its artstyle. You might not notice it at first glance, just by looking at Steam page screenshots, but every texture used in game is literally hand-penciled. It makes for a very unusual look, that pulls you into its world even more. Sheer attention to detail and variety of said textures is insane for a game with such low-fi graphics. Visuals of Mundaun alone make it worth playing, but they are also accompanied by an interesting story and "colorful" cast of oddball characters. Throughout your journey you'll be talking to goats, making deals with the Devil and hanging painters. Its a Faustian story through and through, that while not super original, kept me interested all the way to the end. There are multiple endings to this story, so you better be careful with your decisions near the final act of the game.Mundaun's gameplay consists mostly of exploring, solving puzzles, hiding from enemies (or fighting them) and most importantly... driving the Muvel. I'll not spoil all the surprise gameplay mechanics you'll encounter, but they are quite varied for such a small game. Enemy encounters are unfortunately the weakest part of gameplay. I avoided any combat and either hid or ran from enemies, neither of which was especially fun, but still better than fighting them. Enemies detection range is quite big and all of them can attack and slow you down from the distance, which gets a bit annoying when you just want to avoid them and keep exploring.It took me almost 6 hours to finish Mundaun and while there isn't much of a replay value here, I'd say it was worth every penny. Its a very unique experience, that will live in my head rent free for a long time. Mundaun is a small piece of art, that should be played by everyone who is even remotely into "walking sims", atmospheric horrors or simply likes its artstyle. There may never be another game that mixes genres and uses artstyle like Mundaun, so do yourself a favor and give this one a shot. Just... do it for the Muvel.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the best world building and atmosphere I've seen in any game. This said, I feel that the story in some ways was a little poorly constructed. Gameplay wise, it mostly kept its suspense, though there were some moments that a repeated, irritating enemy would detract from this.Overall, I would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent stylized, atmospheric horror / puzzle game. Really reminiscent of older horror games.Just a warning, the first time you meet enemies is by far the worst. Please do not quit if you run into this section and think the whole game will be like that, as it really isn't. I assume they realized the probably added too many enemies there and toned it down later.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure exactly what this game was for awhile, other than it being generally folk horror and that all the textures were hand-drawn with pencil, subsequently meaning the game is in black and white.Almost immediately, it impressed me with an intro where you ascend into the mountains on a bus to your hometown village so high up that you are looking down on the clouds, following a strange letter from the old priest. And then some strange, disturbing events occur almost immediately that drew me in and didn't let me go until I saw credits.The visuals here are more than just drawn with pencils, though that never stops being a striking element. The ideas on display here, and the way everything is presented, from the framing to the way some parts move, feels precise, comparably to a Wes Anderson movie but much darker than anything in his filmography.The soundwork supports those visuals, bringing them from interesting to being alive. There are pictures on the walls in this game, and when you look at them, the camera slowly zooms in and a whole new ambient soundscape takes over, as if you are experiencing a real memory. There was something soothing about these pieces of the game for me, and I have to praise the decision to put these in the game.The story isn't exactly revelatory, but the other elements of the game elevate it. There is also an interesting thing near the end that I don't know if I love, but it IS clever if I'm understanding it correctly.Anyway, this is a great game and more people should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, unique, lively game. I truly enjoyed my time in Mundaun. The people, the language, the folklore. Everything feels lived and drawn from real life. It is sweet and quirky, funny when it needs to be, tense. The pacing and variety experience as you journey over the quaint part of the alps is immaculate.Fantastic sound design and soundtrack.Movement feels appropriately weighty, though sometimes it stretches into feeling clunky. I managed to break the game once.Definitely recommend this game. If you like folk stories, good stories, horror stories, cottagecore, mountains, finding warmth in cold beauty, goats, sleds, creatures beyond understanding.... or if you don't, check out Mundaun for the love of god.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of things Mundaun does amazingly well: hand-drawn art, atmosphere, music, sound design, exploration. In terms of horror storytelling, this is absolute master class. The characters are engaging, the plot is simple yet fascinating, and the horror stuff is pleasently creepy. There's also cultural richness to it because of its very specific setting and attention to detail. I can say without hesitation that I've never played anything like Mundaun, and I never will. Until I replay it that is - which I intend to do at some point. There are multiple endings and they actually are interesting enough to warrant multiple playthroughs. One drawback that stops me from immediately submerging myself in the world of Mundaun are its enemy encounters. Most are just terrible: the stealth is simplistic, boring and frustrating at times. It gets a bit more tolerable once you venture further into the mountains and encounter new enemy types. The further up, the easier things become, and the less stealth you'll have to do. That said, even with this seemingly fatal flaw, I'd say Mundaun is a great work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: sates my hunger for more first-person adventure games rly nicely, before even all the obvious aesthetic draw. feels authentically folkloric and fableistic in its narrative structure, somehow up to and including the multiple endings, which all feel like plausible outcomes to a story mutated by oral tradition...makes me think a lot ab how much i love horror's central Thing of making u realize the world is More Then What U Thought It Was, ab grappling w/ the impossible, ab questioning the bedrock of "normal" reality, whats shaped it, whats going on behind the curtain. maybe not an all-timer but a rly nice little bundle of basically everything i could want from this type of thing...except perhaps pronounced emotional connection, but perhaps thats the price paid sometimes for the somewhat Distancing effect of fables. whats meant 2 provoke u is not any traditional narrative Thing, but the story residing in yr internal world later, ready for u to remember it the next time u see a big spooky stack of hay
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this! Mundaun is a survival-horror game. The artstyle is both interesting and used well within the gameplay for "hiding in plain sight" moments. The level design and oddly specific inventory management, especially the first area, got me invested and immersed right away in its mountain-goat-farmer setting. The story is compelling, and while it isn't the most original idea, it sticks to its "folktale horror" in a way that makes sense narratively.My two major criticisms both come from the enemy design, especially the first encounter. The game does an exceedingly poor job at both describing what enemies do, and what tools you have to deal with them. This led to 3 total deaths before I cleared encounter 1, each time having no idea what was killing me and from which direction. They aren't overpowered, once you know how they work you can run through the game pretty easily... but man, that first encounter probably leads most players to struggle with future encounters as well. My second criticism is, the maps have so many narrow corridors, the enemies probably shouldn't follow you so far once you run away. It feels like a very tedious slow process to wait for the enemy to walk all the way down to where it saw you (with a VERY far vision range) and then walk all the way back past where you wanted to go. If the map had more branching paths or even obstacles to stop attacks this design could work, but enemy attacks are always ranged, and very often pierce obstacles.I still recommend the game, but during that first encounter:1) There is a second enemy hiding on a ledge above the first one's walk path2) If either of them sees you, you should hide in the hay barn, you cannot 1 v 2 ever3) Their damage happens at range, on a timer, by them looking at you. Although the game mentions "fear," the level of darkness and your characters' vision of them do not matter at all.4) If you isolate one, the pitchfork will kill it in a few hits, but then break or be too damaged to kill 2. Use matches on hay-traps sparingly, I scrounged like crazy and had just enough for all 6 coffees and 3 match-kills5) Sometimes enemies will just see you even if you're crouch-walking far behind them, if this happens just run away, the slow they apply will most likely kill you before you can run all the way to them and kill them.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I was amazed by Mundaun. The style and designs are truly unique and gorgeous. The story is not complicated but has a great twist and interesting characters, making the game impressive. The Romansh language selection was brilliant and created a fantastic atmosphere. I had difficulties driving the car but hadn't had any other problems. It's worth playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a quirky exploration/horror-lite game with an interesting story. The Romanish is really nice to listen to. The art and animation style is fitting. The enemy encounters can be kind of annoying but can be tuned in the settings. I only had a couple of glitches that made me reload a save. My only advice to players would be to consider the end game choices carefully!3.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Took me a bit of time to get into, but really enjoyed it once I did. Fantastic folk horror vibe and fun stealth elements that remind me of Forbidden Siren. The art style is unique and really works well. Great, immersive story and some genuinely terrifying bits. Using inventory can be a bit clunky, but I soon got used to it. Highly recommend this fantastic game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable horror game with lots of personality. The visuals are unique and striking, especially when the environment distorts or there is an illusion which happens quite a bit. A few collectibles offer incentives for exploring the map and adding depth to the game's plot.Most of what I found scary in the game was well planned jump scares as well as the audio in certain situations or environments, definitely recommend playing with headphones or on nice speakers if you have either. I finished Mundaun in 14 hours but I am the kind of person to explore as much as possible trying to find everything I can and look at all the details and find collectibles, I bet it could be done in 7 or 8 hours if that's not your style.It also has multiple endings, 5 is what I have read but correct me if I'm wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Being Swiss myself, I felt obligated to support and play Mundaun.The overall experience was interesting, but it certainly wasn't without flaws. First of all, the atmosphere is there. This is, without a doubt, a good depiction of rustic Switzerland. However, the game isn't scary. If anything, it will feel foreign, which could lead to being disturbing.If you're looking to delve into some of Switzerland's landscapes, habits and beliefs, I can recommend Mundaun. Just remember that it won't be anything too in-depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Pencil based mediums always take a special place with me because I personally found it the only tool I could actually illustrate with. I don't play a lot of horror games these days, but I'll try to set time aside for games that like to dwell on the atmosphere like Mundaun.The representation of this niche Swiss language (dialect?) also lends itself to a novel experience on top of the art style.. All the voice acting sounds like a flute to me, constantly bouncing between the melodies of this language.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a great first-person folk horror game that mechanically plays something like a combination of the newer Resident Evil games and a walking simulator. The game seems poorly optimised but then, it was made by a small team and performance rarely pulled me out of the experience. The distinctive pencil-textured visual style, neat set pieces (very Silent Hill in places) and soundtrack/sound design are stellar and I heartily recommend this to fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just full of atmosphere.  The hand drawn graphics are great, and the lack of color helps add to the mood of the game.  The general aesthetic of the world, and even the story somewhat, gave me a Seventh Seal vibe.  There is enough mystery and intrigue in the narrative to keep you tied in for the whole length of the game.  The voice acting in Romansh is one of the highlights of the game for me; it really puts you in that rural Swiss alpine setting.  Some of the enemies and things you experience in the game are based off of Swiss folklore, and a few of the areas in game are recreations of real world locations.  All this just further adds to the immersion.  This game definitely feels like a passion project.  The only negatives I really have with the game, are that some of the enemy encounters are more annoying than scary, and some puzzle solutions were a bit obtuse.  This is a definite buy if you're interested in folk horror or well crafted indie games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: As a Swiss guy who grew up in the Alps, I enjoyed taking a stroll inside Mundaun beautiful environment, and searching for little touches and sounds bringing back memories.Usually not a fan of horror game, but it's very mild in this one. It felt of bit like Outer Wilds, but in Switzerland and with goats.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun has surprised me, there is no other way to put it. The horror subgenre has become saturated this last couple of years, to the point it has become increasingly difficult to find games that stand out and also deliver on its promise. Mundaun has managed to do exactly that for me, the ideas, the pacing, the different mechanics, everything feels fresh. Even those aspects that are borrowed from other games or not entirely new are used in a way that stands out. Don't miss out on this one, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and fascinating game. Hand drawn and completely unique looking, with an inter-connected map letting you go between the different areas (incl. shortcuts to unlock) if you want to go back to a previous area. Various different items which you can collect which improve your gameplay, from consumables which improve your stats to items which make the world easier to travel through.It's flagged as a horror game but it's psychological horror, not actual horror so it's not scary, just deals with dark topics.There are five endings which aren't hugely different, but different and interesting enough to bother with. The game without doing the alternate endings with completionist took about 9-10 hours. There is stealth and combat but you can do as much or as little of both as you want. In fact, there is an achievement for full pacifist.Completely bug free, no crashes, no graphical issues, steady 60 fps, and all the mechanics worked. Refreshing in a time when almost every game is released incomplete or buggy.On the down side, I have two issues. 1) The game is probably longer than it should be and drags a bit in the middle. 2) The story is very old fashioned and lacking. There's not much there but the ending does make up for it a bit, with there being a cool twist in some of the endings. You can drop manual saves so can do all of the endings without doing extra playthroughs.Overall, I really enjoyed it, even if it did drag on a bit. The environments are very unusual looking and interesting, with a large open map and lots of secrets to find and explore. The mechanics are interesting and I can't emphasise how good the environments are, really being an upside to the game. Could have used a more interesting or more deep story, but still very much worth playing. It was better than I expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Complicated feelings about this game.(very minor spoilers)For what should've been an average at best game, to me it gives off a strange feeling of intimacy. To give an example at the beginning you get introduced to your grandfathers house. Like any other game it is the place to save the game, organise inventory and all that stuff. But it does not feel like a safehouse. It truly gives the feeling of home and safety. In no other game when leaving the safehouse for the last time have I naturally turned off the lights, cleaned up the silverware, closed the windows and locked the door before departing. Its not like the game tells you to do that. It just feels right.Id recommend it just for that experience. The artstyle is also unique, characters feel human and the story aint half bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun may well be the best horror game I played, it is really phenomenal. It is so successfull in creating a sense of place, you really get the impression of arriving at a secluded region, where old customs are still practiced and folkloristic horrors can roam freely at night. This starts at the choice of the spoken language Romansh, that even to swiss people will not sound overly familiar, as it is not very common. This underlines that feeling of crossing a threshold into a world, where the passing of time and what goes on outside of its boundaries doesn't really matter. And then of course there is the lovingly hand drawn pencil art style, that just oozes a bizarre and eerie atmosphere.  Main developer Michel Ziegler claimed the main influences for Mundaun had been Jeremias Gotthelfs novella The Black Spider - and yes, this feels very much like reading an old horror tale from the 19th century in spirit, even if there are modern elements in it also. The other influence he mentions is The Shining, and obviously, the sense of isolation and seclusion is very tangible here. And then there is of course the rich swiss folklore, I would advise to play this game as blindly as possible, just hop into it like the protagonist Curin does and let the events unfold. It is a very unique experience. And while some gameplay elements felt a little rough, it didn't distract from the massive enjoyment I got from this. Truly a gem of a game. And it is nice to see an original approach to a genre, that is so oversaturated with references to slasher flicks or to the works of H.P. Lovecraft - even though I would really love to see more really good ones of the latter.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I think horror games are starting to devolve, something like Mundaun comes along and rekindles my hope that there's still people out there who are willing to step away from P.T clones and 1.5 hour long vhs/ps1 style horror 'experiences' in order to create a truly unique and original idea.The hand drawn style lends itself well to the sheer bizarre and confusing landscape that shifts and distorts, mixing together surrealism and folklore horror to create a perfect blend of uneasiness. Whether it's talking to characters or looking at your self in the mirror, there's always a sense of "is this real?".Despite the combat feeling unnecessary and at times annoying, the journey was well worth it for me. I hope we can see more games express this level of creativity when it comes to horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: yeah its alright. nice stylized graphics but I found the sepia/grey scale kind of wore on me. I kept expecting for color to creep in but from what I can recall, it never did. There are a few bugs, specifically in regards to the vehicle you get, but they can be fixed by closing and reopening the application. I wish that there were more areas accessible by the truck, because it forces you to walk in many areas, and when you are trying to retread areas you have already been through to find what you need to progress it can become a bit tiring. The standout element to me was the journal, which functions as kind of a quest log and stores most of the notes and hints that you find. you manually interact with the pages and it feels like a real book. I recommend it if you like quaint, story driven horror games with very little action and a narrow scope.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique experience. Don't get into this title expecting jumpscares or your classic horror tropes, Mundaun focuses more on exploration, atmosphere and delving into old folktales and bizarre situations all the time.It might not be for everyone (especially those who crave action) but if you're a fan of eerie settings and strange npc's while exploring creepy settings, houses and such, go for it. I guarantee you won't find another game like this on the market.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best horror games I've played in years, right up there with the most recent Resident Evils. It's got an excellent aesthetic that works even better in gameplay than it does in the promotional materials. The story effortlessly strikes a balance between the surreal and the comprehensible, and feels familiar in a traditional folk story way. Exploration feels very satisfying: free and open-ended without being overwhelming, reminiscent of Half Life 2. There are also several mechanics in place to keep you immersed and identifying with the character you're inhabiting (my favorite mechanic being the coffee preparation). Excellent game, easy recommendation for anyone who enjoys exploration-based horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unique, beautiful, and finished. If there are any bugs, I did not experience any. I got frustrated constantly with this game due to the way the game is played. This frustration lead to rewarding sensations of achievement. This game is for horror fans that want a singularly unique artistic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Received the key from Michael Ziegler , full disclosure, much obliged.I would love to say that Mundaun is a great psychological horror game but there are some reasons holding it back form being a great experience.One thing is for sure, I will never forget this game because it is unique, beautiful hand drawn images of a small village somewhere in Swiss Alps and great sound design will live long in my memory. It was a big risk and a strange decision to choose this setup for a horror game but in the end I think it worked well.Mundaun relies heavily on eerie atmosphere and that was a good choice because if you expected a survival horror game you will find this game has almost none of survival features.It is a kind of game where you  can take a time and smell the flowers without any fear of being killed :)So great graphics,great sound design and unique setting are the strong points of this game and in the middle of this review I will recommend this game if you like slow paced atmospheric horror games.Now the stuff that wan't so great. The story was building towards something...well at least I thought so for 2/3 of the game but as the story was unraveling I felt more and more disengaged and in the end the it felt unsatisfying, to sum it up it fell flat. I was really disappointed because I was engaged in this mystery for a major part of my play time and it is a shame that this intriguing story ended on such a low note.I will not  write in depth about combat and puzzles because they are there just to add some extra contend, standard stuff.I may be in minority but the game did not run smoothly. Stuttering, screen tearing and glitches really did not help. I tried to fix this but couldn't find a way. There was one bug where I could not interact with objects and other minor annoyances.I think it is safe to say that making a game such as this in Unity engine wasn't a good choice.All in all a very good atmospheric horror game with an unsatisfying story. It has flaws but it is a unique experience and it will live in my memory for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky and fun horror experience that is honestly perfect for those more interested in a scary story and themes than constant spooks and loud noises. The art style is genuinely incredible, and the game can be deeply unsettling with it, or sometimes even darkly comedic to great effect. It's not perfect, though. Driving can feel very strange and enemy encounters are a little awkward but neither of these take away from the game but rather add to the charm. Mundaun is an easy sell for anyone looking for an extremely unique game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a virtual vacation to the Swiss alps with some local folklore inspired horror elements added in. I really wouldn't call this a horror game though, overall it has a very homey atmosphere contrasted by a few charming characters (except for one). The gameplay is slow paced, you can take your time while transporting hay, making coffee, listening to the radio or just exploring the expansive mountainous region. The story is fairly straightforward but does its job to keep the pace. Mundaun is one of those games that you keep thinking about way after you finish them because of their unique atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend Mundaun albeit with lingering, hard-to-pin-down reservations.There's a lot to digest here in roughly 5-7 hours. A lot of strange. Some fear (). Some deaths. Light survival mechanics. Stats and stat boosts. Stealth. Fighting. Inventory management. Exploration. Intrigue. Reduced color palette. Hand-drawn looking textures. Low-ish polys. Vehicles. Murder! Mystery!  Beautiful music (although a bit sparse/"off" in a couple situations). Swiss Romansh voiceovers with captions. Just... a lot.After completing the game, I feel satisfied but wishing there was more - even after that long list. Perhaps what is frustrating me is I  what I would change. Mundaun is fine as-is. Stands on its own, stands perhaps a bit higher than, say, Amnesia (which is a fair comparison, I'd say) in terms of accomplishing what it feels the creators set out to do. This is a more open, more tale-focused Amnesia with some mechanics added.Perhaps if a few things were tweaked here, a few things were polished there, I'd feel .Or perhaps... perhaps Mundaun is what it is and there's nothing you can change.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Modern mainstream videogames are a wasteland of imagination, so I appreciate it when, every now and then, a game like this one comes along - a game, that feels fresh and inspired and reminds me, that the medium actually still has something new to offer.This game was pretty much a perfect experience for me. The length was just right: not so short, that it felt like I paid for only a partial experience but not so long, that it outstayed its welcome for even a second.It's a game with no jumpscares, but a lot of atmosphere. It's rich in local color and lore, the sound design is amazing (looking at the various pictures hanging on walls literally draw you in), there are some truly gorgeous sights and the visual style is slightly stylized and therefore leaves certain things to the imagination, which can make things more unsettling.The plot is fantastical, but not completely detached from reality - it really worked for me, because it reminded me of some dark fairy tales that I read as a child. The game was also really fun to play. It has puzzles, combat and even some exploration elements. In fact, the game has content for more than one play-through, considering that there are multiple endings and collectibles and it's one of those titles I can definitely see myself play again in the future.I loved this game and I highly recommend it to anyone, who craves for something more than mass-produced slop but that is still well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Hand drawn style, setting and music gave it creepy feeling and it was done well. I don't like when jump scares define horror game and here that's not the case. You will immediately get dragged into folk horror story by visiting Mundaun due to death in the family. I loved almost everything this game provided, there are so many  todetails discovered that I don't understand why more games aren't like this (like staring at pictures). This is the first time I heard someone speak Romansh and its great. Would recommend it to anyone interested in folk horror, lovely scenery and great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game, throughout the playthrough you can feel the passion that went into this. From the hand drawn artstyle, well designed folk-lore enemies, and the full voice over in the language spoken by approx 30,000 in the region of the game's setting. Definitely worth the experience and the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny pencil drawn story about lie, faith, relations and it's consequences. Interesting storytelling, a bit too consice as for me, but it might be just how it's meant to be by devs. Very unusual graphics and style, nice level design. Well-paced, good balanced adventure-like gameplay with stealth hide and-seek mechanics. Not just a "walking sim", one have to run and make decisions quickly here. As it seems, several endings presents. Can't say for sure, I finished a game only once by now. A bit of rpg elements, you can upgrage some stats of your character. Also, player can use several types of transport here. Horror-like mystical suspence presents here. I can call Mundaun one of the typical indie horror adventure game, perharps, one of the strongest of it's type. Definitely recommend this little gem for anyone who like story-driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a game where you can tell the developers had something special they wanted to make. The horror is phenomenal, with much of it delivered through great atmosphere and a general sense of unease emanating from the environment. Fantastic use of shadows and visual framing. And of course the artstyle is awesome, with a  sketchbook look achieved via creative texture work. Well worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is the type of horror I like: chilling, unsettling, and brave enough to let your own mind scare you, instead of forcing scares to happen. Mundaun is not gorey, it has no jumpscares. Instead, it plays as a stripped down, survival horror-esque title. The town of Mundaun is a simple village, high in the mountains. While it might have been a regional attraction at some point, it is now almost a ghost town. And, of course, strange things are happening. You've returned to learn the circumstances involving your grandfather's death, and then things escalate. Mundaun's greatest strength is it's monochromatic palette, stylized to make everything look hand drawn. It adds such a natural sense of unease, and it allows the player to fill in the blanks where detail might been, creating almost ironically a greater immersion to the setting. It's soundtrack is perfect, creating loud crescendos when appropriate and, masterfully, disappearing to make you feel even more alone.Playing Mundaun is...fine. It's mechanics are simple, but it keeps the player engaged. The stripped down approach to HUD, stats, story is such a strong artistic choice, but it does feel like it backfires at times. Once I felt like I "figured out" Mundaun, I lost a lot of tension. Dealing with threats is easy, thanks to the openness of the map. And I never felt at risk of running out of any resources. Mundaun uses it's gameplay as a vehicle to progress you through it's story, instead. What's available here is intriguing, and tightly told. The story, for the most part, stays within the scope of what it can handle. Unfortunately, I felt the logic of it fell apart slightly near the end, but nothing so bad as to sour my taste with it.
