Additionally, there are a few standout set-pieces of narrative that really draw you in.In short, Mundaun is worth your time. It's a remarkable and original entry in the indie horror scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5The atmosphere and general tone of the game is really great even outside of the novel art style. I loved the music and despite some minor issues with the gameplay (combat especially), it's short enough that it didn't end up being too big of a deal. I'm excited to see what the developer's next project will be. I did run into a bug/unintentional sequence break towards the end of the game by accidentally getting around a boundary that was meant to force me to pick up an item, but luckily the game autosaves throughout and allows you to reload an earlier save through the pause menu so I didn't have to restart or anything. I think the story told here is really thought provoking and while I wish there was a little more meat to the gameplay and maybe another pass/more options in combat, though I really liked the way it handles the rifle specifically. I'm very glad that I saw the game through to the end. The one option I wish was in the game would be one to remove the filter over the camera or something, as it becomes a little too overbearing in a few scenes. Overall, I think this is worth playing, especially if you're into more artsy folk horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.More a bleak and creepy game than a straight up horror, although there are a couple of moments where I did jump a bit, but the real draw here is the aesthetics help build an extraordinary atmosphere throughout.  Coupled with a unique and intriguing plot, and fascinating and horrific enemies, it ends up with a winning combination.  And the game has a great knack for delivering on what can only be described as cinematic moment.I'm an absolute fiend for all things folkloreish and this delivers in spades, and for the cheap price of entry it still took me at least 5 hours to complete with minimal padding.Can't recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty cool. As someone who doesn't often enjoy horror games, I had a good time with this one.Pros:- Awesome art style- Amazing atmosphere (nighttime felt truly terrifying, while daytime gave an eerie false sense of security)- Pretty cool story/twist- Some cool hidden secrets to discover- Decent size world with a good amount of exploring to do- Good length if looking for a shorter game (took me about 5 1/2 hours)Cons:- Awful combat system, don't even try with it. For real. You don't have to fight in this game, don't do it.- Not many NPC's / enemies- Puzzles were kinda boring and uninteractive- Pretty clunky; movement is slow and feels artificial, the vehicle is very hard to operate, using tools/weapons is a choreOverall, if you're looking for a horror/adventure game with a great narrative and interesting story, Mundaun is definitely for you. If you're looking for a horror game with great mechanics, puzzles, and is incredibly well polished, Mundaun is not for you.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Great little gem of a horror game. Love the visuals and atmosphere, and the music is fantastic. Doesn't rely on jump scares too often, but when they do happen, they're very effective. The only complaint I have is that it's a little too short. It took less than 10 hours to complete, but there are multiple endings, so I will be playing it through a few more times.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: It's creepy, haunting, very unsettling, and the atmosphere is unlike anything I've played before. If you've ever stared into an old painting that made you feel uneasy, this game captures that ambiance. The talent, voice acting, and passion that went into making this game is rare. It comes highly recommended to anyone who wants a special horror tale.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly pure genius. Aside from the obvious merits of its visual style, it manages to do so many things right: backtracking and fetch-quests are always made fun with the help of new mechanisms (sleds, lifts, truck driving, etc). There are so many moments when an object that just seemed like direction suddenly comes to serve a purpose in some sinister and esoteric way... its remarkable how the game manages to skate so perfectly on the edge of enjoyable playground and atmospheric dread. In a time when we seem to have gotten used to and accepted 1 note horror games, this game is an absolute feast, and well worth the price. Can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the art style, stayed for the game play and story.Mundaun is a nice little survival game similar to other walking sim horror games.  It's full of cool folklore and the cozy feel of the Swiss alps.  The less you know going in the better, but if you enjoy spooky walking sims with some combat sprinkled you will most likely have a good time with this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent atmosphere and art direction. Shares a place with Pathologic in the "smart" sub-category of first-person horror games. It benefits from doing a lot, but not attempting too much in terms of storytelling. The story creates mystery and depth without being confusing or overly-wordy. I am excited for future work from this developer. Extra points for being the only Romansh-language media I've encountered. As others have said, it's more of a slow-burn type of horror. But there was one part (which I will avoid spoiling) that made me wake up my family because I screamed so loud.The minor complaints from mainstream critics that have sunk this game's Metacritic score into the yellow are churlish and I advise ignoring them. The game being "too dark" (as in literally too dark for the player to navigate) at some points was not really a significant thing. Here we are about nine months after its release, it's one of the year's most unique games and it's only 10 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Didnt enjoyed the graphic look of the game but the story really got me in. It was perfectly balanced what types about spookenes and having a chill hike, only thing that really pissed me was the endings. But i recommend this game for everyone who likes to get into deep story game where fighting or jumpscaring is at lowest and main thing is story. Still enjoyed thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: the graphic style may be weird at first, but it turns out the designer made excellent use of it - particularly the later bits are absolutely gorgeous. Also, the story is great, very 30s German expressionist cinema. I did keep pressing the wrong buttons until the end though, so, the controls are a bit odd -but not unplayable, just a bit odd. I highly recommend this
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a 3-D point-and-click adventure, without the bad logic of one. It's a nice, short game, and I wish it was a bit longer; however, this also means nothing in the game overstays its welcome. As the game progresses it keeps changing the scenery and enemies, keeping them fresh. It has philosophical ideas floating around and some introspective moments. I do like the art style and the story.I don't know if the devs are planning on making more games, but I'm here for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is how you do horror.There is ONE jump scare in the whole game (to be fair, an extremely good one that got me good), but the game manages to stay consistently unsettling and unnerving throughout its whole duration. It's also spoken in an extremely beautiful language that you don't get to hear often, which is a plus.The only issues I found are that sometimes it's hard to see objects to pick up because they blend in the environments (but this is due to the amazing graphical style, so it can easily be forgiven) and a slight input lag when played on a TV with HDMI cable and a wireless controller.10/10 would burn weird strawmen again.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: the Dark Descent in the Alps! Nothing less!Almost made by a single man this game is a work of art and a masterpiece.The black & white drawings & textures deeply immerse yourself in the universe.The music is also top tier.The puzzles are not really complicated but the background is sooooo nice that you quickly forget about this.The use of the Swiss folklore is really refreshing.And David Szymanski as beta tester seals the deal.Congrats & thank you for such a nice game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Cultural horror at its finest. If you're here it's because of this game's art-style. You'd think there's only so much you can do with monotone pencil sketched textures but the game looks amazing in so many places.A little synopsis of the story, I'm marking it as spoilers because it's best if you experience it on your own . You decipher this mystery through the game and the pacing never feels too slow or too fast.The voice acting is great and it is not in English thank God. It gives you a deeper sense of immersion and I wished more games based in non English speaking regions did this. This game is a hidden gem, I'm surprised not a lot of people are talking about it. If you're a fan of horror games you should definitely play Mundaun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is an incredible experience. The hand-drawn visuals are impressive and fit perfectly with the setting. They also do a great job contributing to the game's unsettling atmosphere (which is a huge feat, as the game is set in a cozy farming village in the Swiss Alps.)Fun Fact: The dialogue is all spoken in Romansh, a regional Romance Language in the Swiss alps, and the 4th National Language of Switzerland.The game comes highly recommended, and it will make you want to drink coffee out of a pan in a comfy Alpine shack.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: a bit too long for what it tries to be. and a bit too slow. i lost the interest for what this game had to offer.pros:-uses combat and dramatic moments sparsely making them more meaningful-plot meshes well the mystical and delusional. one moment you in mundaun another in a memory, its very good storytelling that keeps you guessing till you discover what hapenned.-coffee and food as mechanic, those are pretty nice. also has a weird skill system that gives you meaning-great use of  enemy design that transcends plot points perfectly into them-not all combat can be won.- clues and journal is so well implemented making a very good diegetic implementation.-great simple art direction. showing we dont need AAA graphics to tell a good story.cons:-game feels slow, like too slow. near the end the game starts dragging itself down. also some item interactions arent really easy to udnerstand specially that you have to "consume" clues from the inventory and then they will unlock the usage of them. shouldve been automatic for all of them because for most clues they do that, but weirdly one specifically dont. werid.-i just tried avoiding encounters because of how slow they felt. not because i was afraid or anything. they just were too punishing for my experience in a whole. not frustating because you could always escape but more like annoying.-movement could ve been accelerated near the end because of how reliant on backtracking it is in the near of the end. mountain scene is bad but interesting.-open world implementation is weird. maps arent even that good. coulved all been a single map but ok i guess. Also it might have gotten better incentives for exploration if there was more of npcs in the world even if they werent intrisically tied to the narrative.northern journey feels like a weird souvenir from a village that is a tourist spot between the alps and the eastern serbian. this one feels like an author movie that lost its message in the end by being weird and not editing some stuff that makes a bit sense but dragged itself for a bit too long.10/10 we need more games like this. great journey even if you didnt finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the movies "Ritual", "Midsommar", and "The Wicker Man"?Do you enjoy David Lynch's vibes?Are you tired of cheesy and/or pop vanilla games?Then this unique niche masterpiece is def for you.But beware, closer to the end you'll feel the same as when you're about to finish a good book."You know you've read a good book when you turn the last page and feel a little as if you have lost a friend." ~Paul Sweeney
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric survival horror game with elements of walking simulator.  Beautifully hand drawn.  Great length.  Oftentimes I get bored of survival horror and this length of about 5 hours was perfect!  Very unique in its appearance and story (which are both great).  Only real downside is that the controls and maneuvering can be a bit clunky, but that's expected with an indie game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little indie game. It has a creepy, weird atmosphere and takes place in a very immersive world. The story is strange, but I was totally invested in it up until the end. As far as I can tell, this is also the first game to be entirely in the Swiss Romansh language (not Swedish, like I've seen some suggest), which is itself pretty cool. My only criticism is that some of the puzzles were a little bit underwhelming, but considering the strange story and overall feel of the game, I was able to look past those flaws. It won't be for everybody, but it was definitely for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I played in Force 3D on my system....and it felt like I tripped and fell face first into someones sketchbook, telling a story- and depicting a time. The daunting solitude was only ever interrupted by the warm, but questionable friendship in my baaackpack. The weight in my heart upon completion suggests I could've fared better, but this was MY fate. What a BRILLIANT work of art this was..... like one of a mad painter. I hope to return to Mundaun someday...but feel I may be left hanging....                                                        ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~In all seriousness; this was one of my FAV slow burn horror games. SO original and themed, I felt DRAWN into it's world (;p) Never too rough not to figure, but challenging at times - Mundaun takes you somewhere else. lil' bit O combat, and too - puzzles, it never slows the story enough to lose interest. If you're a self proclaimed fan of anything I've said before - do NOT hesitate, PLAY......and I'll see you inside the caves in the Mountain.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I'll (try to) make it short: Mundaun was, at least for me, exceptionally good! The art style might not be everybody's cup of tea, but if you're into classic and well told horror storys without a lot of blood, gore, jumpscares and enemies around every corner, you should definitely give this a try. I expected a slighly above average little indie horror game with 2 or 3 hours of gameplay, but i got one of the best interactive horror stories i know, with (i'm a slow player) more than 10 hours of very fun and diverse gameplay. Even if you're fast you should at least expect 5 or 6 hours, maybe more.What i liked about Mundaun:- The art style is low poly and all the textures are drawn by hand. It's needs a little time to get used to it, but i still loved it. Very unique looking game.- The romansh voice acting works quite well and creates a very unique atmosphere- The game might not graphically too details, but it is very detailed in terms of level design. There's stuff to find everywhere- It's not too big and not too small- I really liked the characters and story. Very classic horror stuff! If this wasn't a game but a book or movie, i'd definitely read/watch it.What i didn't like:- equipping and unequipping items from the inventory screen could be a little more intuitive. But once i learned the controls it was okay.- One or two little bugs, but nothing serious.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: It's tense, the design is really effective and unique, and the environmental storytelling is fantastic.  It's really well paced; the tone and atmosphere remain unsettling for the entire story. I still found myself huddling in the corner of an old decaying house out of legitimate fear in the last area a few times instead of getting over it after the opening stages like a lot of other horror games.The exploration/less tense sections are also just as engaging.  I don't want to comment on the story or anything, but the game is just good.  Great style, design, tone, atmosphere, storytelling.  Horror fans and anyone who enjoys a mystery will probably love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The story and voice acting is so good while I was playing through Mundaun I thought about it at work and where the story was going to go. Couldn't wait to get back to it. It's not the scariest game ever, it's more scary in a twin peaks kinda way that is really bizarre and gets under your skin. The plot will keep you eager to keep going. If you're a horror fan you will definitely enjoy this. It's a little on the short side (I finished in 12 hours without all achievements) but you buy this for the unique artistic and gripping experience not the length. Worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: You get what you think you will get. But better. It's not just artsy horror game. It's a story about the past and how some decisions will haunt you and generations after you. It keeps you tense to the very last moment (wchich may be a lilttle different for you :D). I loved every minute of it. At first i was sceptical 16 euro for some indie horror. Now im mad at myself that i haven't bought it earlier. Stronk 10/10  for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The best part of Mundaun for me is the journal you keep. It’s got this tactile sense to it. Flipping through it exposes what you’ve experienced thus far. Maps of the areas. Environmental details. Illustrations of people you meet. Feelings you’re dealing with. Puzzles. Some cover the whole page, some not. Others are written on pieces of paper tucked in between other pages. None of them in any logical order, just hastily scribbled down. The whole thing just feels so good to browse through. And it really showcases one of Mundaun unique selling points: a lot of what you see in the game is textured with penciled drawings. It’s actually a very important part of the overall game aesthetic, not just a visual quirk. Because Mundaun is a game about memories, nostalgia and folklore, which is the type of storytelling that often blurs the lines between fact and fiction. Like scribbles, they capture the gist of it -- but still leave a lot to the imagination. And that’s a great space for a horror game to be in, especially one like this, full of ambiguity and romantics. There’s not that much to talk about in terms of mechanics here, other than that there’s a surprising amount of stuff to do, and a surprising level of openness to it as well. But the fact still remains that the sum of what I’ve been through in Mundaun, is a lot broader of an expression than just game play. There’s a sense of place and time. It feels culturally significant, and personal, in a way. It’s , which is a quality that seems to be hard to come by these days.Recommended, if you enjoy hiking through a weird, twisted European countryside.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while i stumble upon a game that amazes me. Mundaun was quite an experience. Atmosphere and graphics were really pleasing to the eye and the story was captivating. Some of the puzzles were a bit confusing, but that didn't spoil the game. It has its scary moments and when they happen its big. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: i would recommend this to anyone who wants a more pensive horror experience!! also yes you can pet the goatsi'm writing this from the standpoint of someone who's trying to enjoy a game and understand its design.i liked the pacing of the story very much.controls felt clunky at first. after a little getting used to them, I think they fit well with the overall atmosphere of the world. i liked the sound design and art style. i felt a heavy sense of dread all the time, which is great for this kind of horror.i'm bad at directions, so i was a little worried about how open some of the areas were. thanks to the journal, the layout of the areas, and the distinct design of key landmarks, i never felt frustrated or completely lost/stuck! it seems hard to make things distinguishable with an art style that can get messy/scribbly, so i appreciate that i could always tell what i was looking at.kind of wish big goat man got a little more glory. i'm kind of sad that i only had 1 good encounter with him.i ran into some bugs along the way, but nothing that a game restart didn't fix.overall i felt like the game designers put a lot of good thought into this entire experience. to me, the music/sound, art, and game mechanics all contributed to the horror atmosphere. maybe i will play again and find other endings :)
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A must-play for fans of the horror genre. Much like Silent Hill 2, the main attractions are the story and atmosphere. Rather than rely on jump scares, Mundaun creates a sense of dread as thick as the fog separating the mountain peaks from the civilized world below. The sepia tones and Romansh language may be off-putting at first, but stick with it and you'll find that these bold choices by developer Hidden Fields enhance the game tremendously. The hand-drawn textures are wonderfully charming, the pacing is perfect, the sound design is spectacular, and the goats... well, let's not even go there.If you enjoy games such as Silent Hill, Outlast, Amnesia and/or Soma then you owe it to yourself to play Mundaun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The game is slightly clunky, but brimming with atmosphere. Through the story it continue to surprise with new gameplay elements, and even moral choices. The world might be static, but it's gorgeus and has a real sense of place. The rough, hand penciled textures fits the dark Swiss fairytale well. Romanche is also a fascinating language, and speakers of Latin-influenced languages should recognize words here and there. The music underbuilds the atmosphere and the voice actors do a solid job.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, unique and atmospheric. If I had to pick one favourite aspect, it would be the weapon handling. Pitchforks and the rifle feel as clumsy as they would in real life, making it all the more satisfying when you actually successfully kill something.Other gameplay mechanics follow the same idea. I never thought I'd be so thrilled and feel so accomplished about making a cup of coffee in a videogame.Unfortunately, some animations look really janky, which breaks the immersion quite a bit. (which is the only negative thing that comes to mind)
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I don't post reviews for games because I'm a rather private person, however with Mundaun I absolutely have to make an exception. I can't say I have any critique since I'm not good at giving constructive criticism, so this will mostly be a shower of praise :"DI don't know if I'm particularly biased because horror is my favorite genre, especially folk horror, but Mundaun is truly a gem. The art style is wonderful, the story is good and captivating yet not too confusing and feels very much like a traditional folk tale, and the gameplay is fun and doesn't feel too much like a chore. Granted, you can change the difficulty for your own needs-- things in the line of liking challenges or just wanting to focus on the art and story. As somebody that plays games more casually and focuses more on the latter of the two, normal difficulty was perfect for me. Getting the achievements and finding easter eggs was fun too, and considering there are a few challenging achievements and multiple endings I'd say the replay value is one of good quality! The length of the game was also perfect, not dragging things on for too long but also not too short to the point where players would feel unsatisfied (well, at least imo). Exploration of the environment was wonderful, and the puzzles add an extra touch to everything! Even though some people may not be big fans of the puzzles considering I've seen some critique of it, personally I found them really solid. Again, not too hard, but not too easy. There was only one puzzle I truly didn't get, and that's probably because having some musical knowledge would have helped in that case (and I have zero to none). I suppose a summary of my review would be: If you like folk horror (or just horror in general), an enticing story, a gloomy artstyle, an amazing soundtrack, interesting characters (+ enemies) and options to explore and do many things in the dark and secluded valley of the alps, then this game is for you. For it's price point, it's definitely one of my favorite horror games of the year and hopefully will stay that way for a while. Can't wait to see what comes next by Hidden Fields!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: for brief background, Mundaun is a folk horror game set in the Alps, with all dialogue being spoken in Romansh, where you try to find out what happened to your grandfather.obviously Mundaun has a unique (and excellent) art style, but the sound design and the world building deserve mention as well as they also help elevate the entirety of the gameplay. having played through the game multiple times, i appreciate the options afforded to the player regarding playstyle and approach. the game can be very nerve-racking, especially if you are trying to remain undetected and are playing as a pacifist. i appreciate the game making a point to be scary by way of making the player feel week and overwhelmed, and not necessitating numerous cheap jump scares.it was very exciting to be able to play this game after watching its development for many years. if you are into "art" games and horror, most likely you will enjoy this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A work of genius. Compelling story, fantastically unique graphics, mesmerising soundtrack.  It's eerie, mystical, and at times plain surreal. I absolutely recommend this to people who like quirky indie adventure games.  Roughly 8 to 11 hours long, with a few endings (you decide at the end, so no need to replay huge sections of the game).
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is one of the best "small-town with a dark secret" type of horror games. The best part to me was the atmosphere and light exploration in the swiss mountain village. The game does a fantastic job balancing both the mundane feeling of the quiet mountain with explosions of weirdness and occult at key points. A particular high-point to me was the decision to have all dialogue in a very rare language particular to this actual area in switzerland. It really adds to the immersion and help to make the mountain community feel like a real place with history.Note here that unlike a lot of modern horror experiences, Mundaun is not a straightforward walking simulator. There are light puzzles, exploration, navigation and even some combat to engage in. None of these systems are particularly deep, but the game has very good pacing and sticks the landing perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is the kind of game that makes you skeptical in the beginning about play it or not and you end up loving it. It has a unique art style which i loved and amazing voice acting. The plot and the gameplay works really nice together and you never feel bored or repetitive. I recommend for anyone that likes unique art styles and don't care for fancy graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem of an indie-game. The gameplay mechanics are pretty standard, but the aesthetics, the presentation and the mood are unique. The story is interesting and scary without many jumpscares. Worth playing if ou like games with an similar intense atmosphere like pathologic and the silent hill games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a brilliant and surreal survival horror game. One of the best I've played to date in fact. This game really manifests that eerie folk feel in many ways; goats, pitchforks, wicker, evil spirits--the whole shabang.I just wish there was more replay value though, after 1 playthrough I feel like the twists and mystery kinda lose their value. It's still a brilliant game, but I haven't been itching to pick it up again since completing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a terrific game which has somehow managed to slip under the radar of many. Set in the isolated valley of Mundaun in the Swiss Alps, the game is beautifully hand drawn, literally. Every texture in the game was pencil drawn and shaded then mapped over the world and its objects. The game has the player investigate the mysterious death of your grandfather and the circumstances surrounding his death. As you trek through the valley, strange occurrences begin to pop up. As your journey brings you to the submit of the mountain, the truth of the Mundaun's history is revealed. Inspired by Swiss folklore, the world if rich with flavor and love. From the Rumantsch language, to collecting hay with the movel, the game is tied to its real world counterpart. Lastly, the game is full of details. In the distance, someone is always watching you. In the world, imagery is used to further emphasize the influence of the devil on Mundaun. In conclusion, Mundaun is truly a gem and well worth playing. This game deserves every ounce of praise and I would recommend it anyone who enjoys atmospheric walking-sim games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a a gorgeous game.  The visuals, the music, the imagination, the whole atmosphere of it. And so Swiss! makes me think of Jung, Lovecraft and of course the Alps!  The pencil drawings are absolutely beautiful.  It gives the game an enchanting uncanny atmosphere. The gameplay is varied too,  it's not just a walking sim.   A mix of point and click, FPS, some basic driving,  I'd say it's point and click/adventure game with an FPS perspective.  It's scary too, but not what I expected.  It's much  more than just a horror game. There's beauty and goodness here, as well as horror -  and not all goats are satanic! Huge recommendation if you like indie games, horror or artistic endeavours.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't know how and where to begin, let's start that this is the best game I played in a while.The story at first is really intriguing and later when you start to realise what's going on is when you really get into it. The game is a hand drawn and created with passion and love. I only had one single and very rare bug and after speaking with the dev via twitter he fixed it the same day...yes...just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: even if you are not a big fan of the genre, i'd say give it a try. Mundaun strike a perfect balance between a relaxed experience and enough mechanical complexity to accomodate all type of players, offers stunnings visuals and beautiful strange dream sequences. it's a game made with passion and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Fabulous game. It doesn't innovate much from a mechanical perspective -- basically, if you're a fan of post-Amnesia horror titles, you're going to know what to expect. It has a sanity mechanic, coupled with some fairly cool brambles that cover your body and slow you down. It has some light combat mechanics, kind of like the first Penumbra game, but they are mostly awkward, meaning that you're going to spend most of your time sneaking away from monsters. None of this is particularly groundbreaking, but it's extremely competent. The main innovation, in my opinion, is the hand-drawn pencil graphics, which is a stroke of brilliance and unquestionably carries the game. When layered on top of the relatively clumsy models and animations, it makes the game feel like something directly out of a nightmare. You're not going to get a bunch of jump scares, but the game oozes with dread from the opening act.Sad to see this is not getting more love. It's probably the best Amnesia-like I've played in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is beautiful not only in its handwritten art style but in its story and gameplay. The story is fascinating, and the fact that the game is not dubbed and plays in its original language Romansh, which is native to the alps, amplifies the whole mood of the game. The game is both creepy yet beautiful and a massive recommendation on my part!PS. Give the goats a pat :)
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and I have to say I enjoyed it. If I had to rate it I would probably give it about a 8/10. The game itself has more of a creepy factor to it. There was a couple moments that were truly scary and got to me. If you purchase keep in mind it is a puzzle game with some traveling from point A to B. For a few things it took quite a bit of traveling til I realize I did something wrong and had to go about it differently.  The art is great and I think the fear just comes from the atmosphere that the game gives off.  Also there are a few chances to make a choice on what you do which leads to multiple endings which is pretty cool and makes you want to  play the game again to see what else can happen! This was my first review I ever left so thanks for reading!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever by chance stumbled into watching an obscure european movie that is truly unique and interesting. Not the greatest thing you've ever seen but you're glad that you experienced it?I really like the focus on the local folklore for the horror, making it almost alien in culture with the language adding to it (Romansch is really similar to Portuguese though!). Fear of the Unknown and all that
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: So I saw this game being advertised on Facebook and thought it looked cool, nothing more... Boy was I wrong. I decided to finally give it a shot, and I was blown away! Beautiful art desgin, great mechanics and an incredible compelling story (with many possible endings). I could totally see this being made into a film one day. Bottom line... if you like horror and folktales GET THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet and dripping with atmosphere and style. If your looking for something to scare the pants out of you then this game is not for you. It has like 2-3 jumpscares and couple more scripted scenes that might give you goosebumps but you ll most likely spend your time walking around with your pitchfork in hand for the majority of this game. If your looking for a game that might keep you interested throughout its entire length with its story and world then while tickling you here and there with spooky moments and creepy atmosphere then this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The creepy atmosphere alone makes this game a must play. This little alptraum of an adventure have you investige some strange things in a seemingly cozy little community.Gameplay is simple, explore, pick up items make some coffe, drive around gather hay. All in a days work! The artstyle is short of amazing. And the use of Romansh is a nice touch. The attention to detail to the little things as the water fountains and the houses makes it really feel like "home" so to speak. It looks very authentic in that way.The story hooks you pretty much instantly and you wan't to know what all the creepy things happening is all about as soon as they starat happening. Give it a go for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while, a truly marvellous experience comes along that just enraptures you and makes you wish you could experience it all over again completely blind. Mundaun is one of those experiences.I love everything about this game, the hand-drawn assets, the beautiful vistas, the fantastic atmosphere, the story that kept keeping me engaged, the subdued but effective music and the simple but very pleasant gameplay.I wholeheartedly recommend this game; at full price, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMENDEDhighly immersive world that favours quality over quantity+ amazing sound design+ game mechanics integrated into setting in meaningful, interesting ways+ very clever level design+ original setting+ engaging, well-paced story+ perfect length (~7h30 for me)+ incredible attention to detail! the environment is not huge, but is very rich, and rewards paying close attention- as with many narrative-driven games, you are sometimes "forced" to take the path that advances the story(- encountered one minor bug + clunkiness from time to time, including stutter, but it didn't really affect my experience)
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A delightfully unnerving folklore-driven adventure thriller. The art style is obviously stupendous, and really helps sell the creepy disjointed subjects of Mundaun. The animations are similarly alarming, keeping you on guard for every interaction. Cool puzzle/world design and well handled UI and management. I wish combat was more satisfying if even it had to be there at all. Not a fan personally of being paralyzed more the closer an enemy gets to you. Otherwise, an excellent one-shot spooky experience perfect to scratch the Resident Evil itch you may be having.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Mundaun, and I'm not sure how exactly to structure my thoughts about it, so I'm gonna go for the tried and true method of pros and cons :)+ Visuals are very unique+ Story is very engaging, never missed a beat+ Sound design is incredible, really drew me into the setting+ Enemy variety is really solid, always felt challenging too+ Enemy balance is very good, encourages being sneaky but also gives weapons as a last ditch option+ Goofy animations on one particular character who I won't spoil that really gives them a personality+ Overall really good balance of goofy and horror+ Also theres a CAR and its REALLY FUN+ Mostly didn't hold my hand, and allowed me to figure out game mechanics on my own (I actually missed the opportunity to grab the very first weapon, meaning I went through a portion of the game barehanded+ goats- Minor gripe, but the black and white color scheme can sometimes make it difficult to sense depth in very dark areas- I was left stuck on one part of the game for over an hour, and the correct way to progress felt really obscure and was sort of disappointing- Some of the dialogue felt really flat while the captions had exclamation marks on the end of the sentences. This could be down to translation but it felt worth mentioning- Enemy AI feels really bare-bones, all of them have one particular pattern to them that makes it really easy to avoid encounters once you know how to schmoove- Ultrawide implementation was a bit janky, inventory would sometimes not work and I would have to crouch to fix itOverall, I had a really good time with Mundaun, I would recommend it to any fan of horror or folk tales, and I think the unique setting makes it feel special. 9/10, would goat again
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game for what it is. The art style is awesome. The story is satisfyingly dark, even if you make the "good" decisions. Puzzles are challenging, but not so much that you'll likely be stuck forever. It's not super scary either. Only one real jump-scare, and the rest is just a somewhat creepy vibe. Overall, if you're okay with a 5 hour experience for the price, and are looking for a unique horror experience, pick this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Art style is similar to The Long Dark, but sepia toned and obviously horror. One thing to note though is that the entire game is hand-drawn or at least appears hand-drawn. While you might not think that would be scary, you'd be surprised. This game is great at instilling the fear of dread and panic. Usually not that into walking simulator type games, but this one has such a creepy/believable-yet-fantastic atmosphere and story that it kept me hooked. Multiple endings, lite combat/stealth, puzzles, lite upgrade-able stats. Set in the Swiss Alps in the 40's (?i think?), that takes its nods from European fables and The Shining. It's not without it's hiccups, but they are relatively few; (note: there was one area that I got frustrated with but that's because the mechanics aren't explained THAT well, but I got it after awhile.) All-in-all I'd give it a 8.5/10 for what it is: a cool indie horror game. Definitely check it out.TL;DR - Indie Horror set in the alps that is one part European fable, one part The Shining.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. While black and white, the charcoal drawn visuals are great. In terms of being a horror game, Mundaun wasn't particularly scary, just had horror elements. With that said, the environment and world were wonderful. If anyone is into stylized games that have strong artistic merits, I would heartily suggest.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very neat experience! Genuinely pretty spooky at times, and an interesting story that baffles at times in a positive way! Exploring the environment is great because the art style is unique, and there are little items and interesting places hidden throughout. There is combat in the game, but as the other reviews will say as well, it is quite clunky. It can be fun at times to use the weapons, but mainly, you'll be sneaking around or avoiding enemies, there are more fights in the later half of the game though. It's a slow burn type of game, but it truly picks up a lot in the second half! There are also puzzles to solve throughout, and they are definitely not challenging, but still very clever. This is a solid horror game, and if you were curios at all by looking at it, you should totally pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Wholesome and Genuine are words that I think sum up Mundaun. A great example of what "art" games should strive for. A true masterpeice in both setting and story. I hazard to say anything else as this game should be experienced personally. An amazing game, that sheds some light on a very distinct culture.P.s. It would be cool if steam allowed Rumantsch to be a selectable language.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: (Steam says I've played for two hours but start-to-finish with a lot of the optional and side content it's been like 5/6h)Mundaun is a strikingly beautiful survival horror set in the swiss alps, where the best way to deal with the supernatural horrors around is to make yourself a nice cup of coffee and chill a bit in a beautiful cabin. The story goes to some unexpected and surreal places, which is a perfect fit for the tone of the writing and the atmosphere of the town, making everything feel like a dark fairytale in the vein of german expressionist films. All in all, a great find that I'll be sure to replay. Very recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game that starts out a bit weird and clunky, but you quickly learn to love the innovative art style, the atmosphere (which weirdly allows both for uneasy and comforting situations), interesting characters and the well-told story. Combat is quite inelegant but can and should be avoided anyway. Take your time and enjoy this!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I think authenticity was the main thing that attracted me to his game. The setting, the engaging gameplay, the folk horror aspect, the hand drawn aesthetic, all of it seems to be something the makers of it have thoroughly thought through. I believe that the creator, Michel Ziegler, had a very clear vision of what he wanted to do and how to do it. It has a specific captivating quality, where the situations and environments that the player’s character is placed into not only speak about the story contained within the game, but also about the bigger picture: the clash of modernity and Christianity with pagan folklore, the trauma of war. All of it is conveyed through magical realism and fairytale-like storytelling. I love how various strange occurrences are met with a humorous lack of concern, as if as soon as you step into the area of Mundaun, anything goes. It is refreshing, given how often the protagonists in modern horror games like to announce to the player what is that they are going through and do so in the most dramatic way possible. Although the characters are heavily stylized, they still retain a certain sense of realism due to their authenticity. And by authenticity, I mean that it feels like all of the details presented in this game come from the real life experiences of its creators. Another thing that is definitely worth mentioning is the amazing sound design. The way the camera slowly zooms into the pictures you are observing and then the faint sounds portraying the story of the picture begin to appear. The music is really beautiful and haunting, one sequence particularly comes to mind, during a set piece that occurs at night, near a mountain lake. It gave me the feeling of wonder, when you don’t want to rush, but rather to slow down, take in the surroundings and explore. It also invites one to learn more about this particular region of Switzerland itself, its history, the Romansh language. Overall, a very pleasant surprise: dark yet fun, engaging and educational.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: The hand-drawn textures lend an unreal amount of atmosphere to this game. The setting is unique and the voice acting is really well done. This is a creeeeepy folk-horror game that relies less on jump scares and more on creating and eerie mood. Highly recommended if you're a horror fan (or a linguist)
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: You don't get a (horror) game that takes elements from folklore from the alps a lot. As a child I was in the alps a lot since my grandparents used to live there. Playing this game brought back memories from my childhood, which really touched me. I like the art style and atmosphere of this game. It's gripping for the whole 5-6 hours it took me to complete it. It definitely is a gem of 2021 and everybody who likes horror/narrative games should pick it up and play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun for me is a clear 9/10 - it is nearly perfect some bugs and one puzzle aside, I will go into that later.This review is written nearly spoiler free, so you can read it and go into the experience as blind as if you'd just have seen the trailer.If you ever wanted to visit the Alps, Mundaun is the experience, which is both culturally and visually appropriate. The oppressive and thick atmosphere of the region excellently lends itself as a setting for a horror experience and Mundaun is a hidden gem in this genre.Before I will talk about the cultural aspect, let me quickly run over the common review aspects:The game has excellent immersion, there is no element in it which will pull you out of the experience. If you are used to maps and blinking markers there is a chance that you might get lost, but the valley of Mundaun is a place you want to get lost and explore anyways and the areas are small enough and provide enough landmarks, that you can find your way even without a UI you are used from open world games.Another element which adds greatly to the immersion is the local language used by the inhabitants of the valley and that every element you use in the gameplay is tied into the gamedesign and worldbuilding. The game never asks you of any videogamey tasks and uses it's mechanics with a focus on player experience and not padding in terms of overall playtime for the player.And Mundaun is not a short game, it still provides you with about 6-10 hours of quality gameplay which is really a lot more than I expect for that price.In the playtime you will experience quiet periods of exploration, story sequences and some more intense horror passages, all perfectly paced, that it never gets boring. The progression always will throw new things at you and when you think you saw all, a new area opens up or a new mechanic is introduced which keeps you engaged.Culturally Mundaun is the only videogame experience I know of which paints a believable and realistic picture of the Alp region. All of the architecture, all of the dangerous mountain paths, all of the plantlife and small details are highly accurate. Some elements of fantasy, are so well woven into the world, that you don't even know if it's made up or real in some sense (e.g. the encased bed in the first house and the device which protects you from evil spirits). All monsters you will encounter also are deeply rooted in the folklore of the mountain region and the story is an interpretation of the folklore woven into a new and exciting (fairy)tale perfectly blending in with other local legends.There is nothing in the game which is not fitting for the setting, and I don't remember when I felt last time so immersed in a piece of software. I think I was a kid and didn't really question much in games. But Mundaun deeply questions itself with what it is presenting and therefore feels real. I even closed the gates behind me after traversing them, which is a custom of the region and to switch off the lights and close the doors of the houses afte rleaving, because they felt real and I am saying that as someone who grew up in that setting. Therefore from an artistic point of view, I only got praise for it and if you don't know the region and you like to experience a different culture, with this game you definitely will!If you love horror games and you like to experience new settings Mundaun  is an experience you should not miss out on.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------About the bad things (spoiler do not read if you want to go into it totally blind):There is one passage in the later game with a puzzle in which you have to unlock a bridge, which seems to have not been playtested enough and is quite frustrating and there is more than one design issue with this passage.First of all you will encounter the first part of the puzzle before you will encounter the puzzle and there is one bugs connected with interacting with the contraption which might prevent you from opening the game, or cost you a lot of time.Secondly you will get a journal page, which you can look at in your inventory, but you have to read in order to trigge rthe puzzle. It took me about 1 hour to figure out that I have to interact with the page in the backpack with "E" before the puzzle really kicks in. If you don't do it, the levers don't snap into the exact position and even if you try to solve it like that you'll ge tfrustrated, because the character only tells you "I have no clue what I am doing" and the white message on top of the right screen which says "there are items to use" seems like a leftover bug from some other activity - because you as player figured out what to do, but the game needs you to read the page, but you already got all information visually, especially since earlier in the game you had to interact with pieces in the inventory.Once you figured this out, you still have to solve the puzzle exactly from the top of the mountain to the bototm, not in any order to complete the quest.All of those things would be half as bad, if the whole leveldesign would not require you to take the skilift every time you want to go up the mountain, which ttakes you a couple of minutes. It was highly frustrating, because I took tht lift like 5 times before thinking it was a bug, reading the steam comments, firing up youtube and watching a playthrough to find out i have to read the page, which then changes the levers and then you need to interact with it.Solutions:-don't make the contraptions interactible until you got the page in your journal. And let the character say "This looks Fragile, i better get some instructions before I touch it" or something like this.And once you ge tthe page, the message in the top right should say, you need to read the page in your inventory.FIguring out the puzzle then would imo be ok.Other bugs and curiosities:After taking the first tunnel of the game with the muvel: if you jump out of the muvel and go by foot back to the tunnel entrance you'll see the the side towards the mountain peak is missing texture. Also if you go by foot into the tunnel, the whole screen turns black and it's nearly impossible to find out again (wasted a couple of minutes there)If you summon the Muvel through the posters, in some locations it will land in weird positions. I had it 45° standing, lying on the side, standing on it's windscreen side, or just bugging halfway through the world mesh. Some polish is necessary there. The place where you mostly can encounter this, is the poster next to the snow barricade which you have to blast away with the bunker cannon.There are a couple of little houses in which flurina seems to play. Sometimes there are drawings or toys inside. If you crouch and move in and you stand inside those little house and let go of the crouching button you clip through the roof of this little hut, which just is super weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most immersive, eerie first-person horror games I've played. Utterly unique setting and aesthetic, with the bonus of drawing from a real region, real languages, and real folklore.In terms of gameplay, it's a (somewhat) linear affair using tried-and-true first person mechanics. It's a small, concentrated, finely-crafted time that doesn't outstay its welcome, where each and every planted plot point lands with a great payoff. In terms of similar games, it gives me the eerie exploration vibes of STALKER with a hint of the charm, unique feeling, and experimental attitude of a fantastic HL2 mod circa 2012 (and this is meant in the best possible way!).If you're like me and you absolutely adore expressive, unique, and well-crafted games, pick this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Buy and play this!It's the slowburn period horror game the medium has needed for a while now. You'll see it in film (The Witch, A Field in England) but not as much in games: letting you soak in the atmosphere and dread, punctuated with stand-out surreal bits.It feels like a Thief campaign a bit as well, a really weird Thief conversion. Rewind back to when you had *no idea* how to kill the haunts in the cathedral and had to sneak around them, a nervous wreck. And there are also cool puzzles like you might've stumbled upon in a 90's slideshow adventure game: you are all of the sudden trapped on the island in Myst. That's a lot of comparisons (too much) to other things for a game that's so fresh. One of the mindblowing things is how meta it is. You've heard the whole game is made of drawings, right? It's clever your character is an artist and throws doodles and found documents/errata in their journal. But it goes further, early on you are afflicted with a curse- your hand gets burned...or does it turn to wood? I took it like you are now cursed with Charcoal, the actual drawing medium itself. Just like your grandpa and his barn, the rot in this world is a simple texture, when an artist angrily scrawls darkness onto paper.Spoilers ahead.   That's the coolest thing ever.Genius game...There are some satisfying collectibles as well! er, if you liked Obra Dinn, play it! If you like horror or even immersive sim, play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: this is a really nice surprise. i wasnt really sure what to expect, except that i like old school adventures and a bit of horror/mystery. i was also very pleased that this isnt really an adventure game, it feels more like resident evil actually.  this one is very atmospheric, it encouraged me to research a bit of swiss lore, gameplay is fun. its cool to explore the mysterious locations. the world is surprisingly interactive. getting some gabriel knight 3 / lost crown series vibes here. very nice so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it (6.1 hours).A neat little game that takes a lot from the creator's culture of rural Switzerland. Feels like playing an underrated 70s folk horror movie (think The Wicker Man). Gameplay doesn't do anything new, but there's a lot of heart and soul here. Worth the money and I'm looking forward to what the studio does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up the game because I was immediately drawn to the hand-pencil textures, and the rural isolated theme, and let me tell you the game didn't disappoint me at all.Mundaun borrows some inspiration from games like the long dark, there are several houses in the village in which you can take refuge, leave supplies there and upgrade yourself with coffee. The story is really captivating. When you come back to the village where you grew up, the priest of Mundaun sends you a letter informing you of the death of your grandfather. Once you arrive you see the hut of your grandfather turned to ashes, something tells you this was not an accident. From there you meet a mysterious man that greets you with a firm handshake that will leave a mark on you.  I have to add the fantastic use of portraits in this game. The FOV gets shallower and you start listening to the sounds of the painting almost as if you are reliving the occurances of the painting.My favorite part without a doubt was the exploration the game offers. You can backtrack almost at every point ( which is rare for a story driven game ) . The level design is amazing. I was always having that feeling of discovering something new, while having a clear direction of where to go and how to. Many interactions result in the addition of journal pages, which are amazing. These range from: entries with puzzles instructions, drawing of the characters, breakdowns of how the enemies behave and my favorite, hand drawn maps that can aid with navigation.In terms of length the game feels really adequate to me, it's a short story, expect around 4 to 5 hours, it has some replayability potential since there are some important choices you can revisit, but I dunno how big those are since I just finished my first play through.In short if you like horror this is a must have small indie masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Most original indie horror game I've played in recent memory. It's not particularly scary, instead it keeps a creepy things-aren't-quite-right atmosphere for almost 8 hours. Which works in tangent with the snowy mountain vista and the beautiful rare Swiss dialect (think that's correct).Looks like a walking sim, but there's lots of interact with: driving, some combat, making coffee, and much more. It all adds to a convincing game world rather than an art one where you're only a tourist.Sick of jump scares, overly dark levels, killing monsters with super guns. You might enjoy this indie horror more than the rest.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely feels like a passion project. It doesn't try to outright scare you off like Amnesia or Outlast. This game unsettles you as you slowly understand the secluded village in the Alps filled with disturbing things I can't even describe with certainty. You arrive in the village to confirm that your grandfather had been put to rest in the graveyard and ever since leaving the bus I felt I was being watched. The atmosphere felt like someone was always behind me while the story only reinforced that feeling. The Romansh voices for the characters did make the game feel more authentic. If they just spoke English then I would've felt like I was in an Amish town.I bought this on a whim for $15 and it was a solid purchase. I hope to see another game drawn to this degree. Support them because they deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great horror game. This game follows the mechanics of you will fear the unknown and the dread that creeps up on you. There are puzzles you will need to complete for this game and side options to do as well. The visuals of this game are fantastic. The art makes it more creepy and atmospheric with how terrifying a small mountain town can be. It is kinda short but the are multiple endings. All in all, a really fantastic game and I cant wait to see more from this developer. 10 outta 10. A solid horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a very interesting horror game. Heavily based on swiss locations and folklore, the game revolves about the misterious death of the protagonist's grandfather and the attempt to try to clarify what is going on.The aesthetic style, based on penciled textures, works very well with the dark/aerie ambient of the story, and it is one of the main features of Mundaun. It makes you feel like you're inside a dreary surreal story.In general, this a solid horror/adventure game, very immersive with s gripping plot and intriguing characters. Maybe the weakest aspects are related, curiously, to gameplay design like monster encounter or item finding quests, but nevertheless, they do not really have a bad impact on the overall experience.All in all, I considered Mundaund not only one of the best recent horror games, but one of the best games I have played lately.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique first-person horror game with strong puzzle sections and somewhat clunky stealth and action elements. In this case though, the atmosphere is far more important than the gameplay. And oh my God, is the atmosphere fantastic! The story is dark and twisted, but also much more funny and quirky than I expected. The pencil art style is just brilliant. The horror is more on the atmospheric side with some jumpscares in between. It can be janky at times, but it is an unsettling and odd piece of art. If that's your thing, you can't go wrong with Mundaun!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is basically a mild horror exploration game. I was pulled in by its creepy atmosphere and it got me few times with its jump scares. Many elements of Mundaun were executed well except for the controls. Combat was stiff and nearly useless without the rifle. Which could have been intentional for this type of game and walking was incredibly sluggish. On the bright side, driving was comically janky. You'll get a good laugh out of it. Munduan never overstays its welcome and can be beaten in a short 7-9 hours. If you are a fan of horror stories then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun experience overall! The setting and enemies were very cool, and most of the set pieces were interesting. I did feel like the pacing near the end was a bit off; the first 75% was paced nicely with new enemies and characters being introduced but nearing the end, when you get to the last 2 areas, it feels a bit meandering like it needs to wrap stuff up. Some puzzles felt like the dev thought there needed to be an interaction there, 1 or 2 instances where I picked up the solution to a puzzle before getting to it, or the key-item was a couple of steps away. The game could have been a bit more streamlined if those were cut out (giving toilet paper to the person on the toilet for instance).Apart from being able to walk off the map near the lake, having to reset in the maze because a hallway was blocked, and a prompt not appearing, the rest of the game went smooth! The unique visuals, and great music and story made for a fun experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun has a lot going for it: the most apparent thing is it's striking, uniquely hand drawn graphics. The sketchy charcoal look transforms the 3D landscapes into something I've never quite seen before in a game, and adds a somber, melancholy mood as well as an atmosphere of dread. Which is good, because Mundaun is at its heart, a really terrifying game. The folk horror elements are handled extremely well, not just because of the graphics, but also thanks to the mystic folktale-like backstory and the great monster designs. Thankfully, it doesn't shy away from the weirder parts either, and gives us some nice, bizarre moments of talking goats' heads and walking straw men.Sadly, the gameplay isn't as good as it's mood. The pure adventure game/puzzle/exploring bits are great, with some bits of stealth thrown in that are stressful, but fun. The more action-oriented bits, however, are at best tolerable, at worst really awful. The combat sequences feel rather clunky, and the driving parts made me scream in frustration at how shoddy the controls were. That being said: the overall experience of Mundaun is a good one. The mystery and suspense, the great monster design and breathtaking graphic style makes it all worthwhile, even though I think this would have worked better as a more purely adventure/puzzle oriented game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: A solid folklore horror story set in the Swiss Alps, good pacing and writing. The game deserves its place in the indie horror history books just for the fresh setting but it also delivers some unexpected gameplay. You set up camp in your grandfather's house which you then use as a hub. You even get a small truck to explore the village of Mundaun. The map is mostly "open" which means you can always move back and forth between areas. Even right before the final boss you could, in theory, still drive around and take care of some unfinished business, like locked doors or achievements... but the village will be crawling with monsters by then.Mundaun's story escalates over several days, which means you will visit the same locations several times but they will change from day to day. So even though the game has three different areas, I would classify it as "single location" horror, much like The Shining or The Thing. Actually, Mundaun reminds me a lot of Cryostasis.The main plot device is clear right from the start. A black goat, a weird old man with a walking cane... you know right away who the villain is. That's why I'm happy to report that the story still took some unexpected twists and turns. I finished it in two long sittings. Happy Easter?
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I just played through Mundaun and it turned out to be just the unique and detailed experience I was hoping for. The game owes a lot of its dense atmosphere to the chosen style with the hand-drawn textures. In addition, there is a very varied gameplay with many facets. If you want to experience a gloomy fairy tale in the setting of the Alps, which is chosen far too rarely in games, this is the right place!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me feel like a kid, listenning to a horror tale that respected old folks would tell you at night sitting around a firecamp: The graphics are beautiful and unique. The story is humourous, clever and intriguing. Characters are endearing in their own way, and the world is incredibly immersive. A one kind of a piece of art made with care and love
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very good. The story, atmosphere, artwork, and gameplay were all great. The only negative thing I would have to say is that I personally had issues seeing during certain sections due to a filter on the screen that makes the screen look dirty. Other than that this game is fantastic and I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: 4/9/21 Edit: The devs fixed the problem and I was able to complete the game, ran into a few more bugs, but nothing else that stalled out my progress. Honestly, I think the game is absolutely beautiful and it's a work of love, the gameplay itself is nothing groundbreaking, but it was a good game overall and took me approximately 6 hrs to complete. I definitely recommend this game at this time and I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unique if nothing else, for films I could draw comparisons to Midsommar or The Witch but for games this stands pretty much alone and is worth to try just for that. The visual style isn't always the prettiest, the pencil-drawn textures aren't the exciting feature that they were made out to be, but wow can this game look absolutely stunning in certain environments, making these all the more rewarding. The gameplay features some unique twists that you wouldn't expect going into this game for the first time, but ultimately it is the fantastic atmosphere, absolutely beautiful and haunting score and sound design and firm grasp on unsettling imagery and careful tuning of the horror-screws that shine bright in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is a very atmospheric game. The Horror itself is rather subtle, but there is no lack of scary moments like in e.g. Amnesia. Besides the great story and atmosphere, encounters with opponents can sometimes produce dynamic situations, which benefits immersion for this horror game but partially also produce funny moments. By the way, playing time easily ranges from 7 to 10 hours depending on how much you want to soak up the atmosphere. Therefore, it really is a very fair price for the quality offered. An absolute recommendation for horror fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic experience, Mundaun is haunting and mysterious without being filled with cheap scares, engaging story with interesting characters that kept me pushing on to see what would happen. Beat it in one sitting, which I don't often do with games, even on the shorter side. Really enjoyed the visuals and the soundtrack as well, just a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game had potential to be good, but I was wrong...its is phenomenal! Here is a condensed list of the things I was blown away by: the story telling, the atmosphere, the design and how well it works with the setting/story, and the subtle, but very effective scary moments. Take your time with this game, because eventually you'll wish you could experience it again like it was the first time...its that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic folk horror game with a beautiful art style which is used perfectly. Feels like playing a dark fairy tale book. Enemy design was creative and the characters were interesting. I'm looking forward to seeing how some of the other endings play out and what you need to do in order to get others!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is absolutely worth the price, no question. Made with love and care, it feels like an A24 moody horror movieThis game is a mood and a half! It's like if a classic point-and-click game, The Witness, and The VVitch got all blended together. Atmosphere is everything and this game's got it. No obnoxious hand-holding, the game trusts you to explore. I think this game is absolutely worth it's price tag. It's got a killer art style and mood, and while it hasn't lost its "indie" feel for me yet, it feels like a complete game that was made with care. Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of games out there that try so hard to scare the player, only to fail miserably.Mundaun, on the other hand, does not rely on jumpscares or heavy horror scenes and yet it manages to create a perfect atmosphere.Anyone who has ever looked at the mountains in the silence of the night knows how powerful and frightening they can be, and this is exactly the feeling Mundaun gives the player.A wisely-narrated plot and a gameplay which blends exploration and action complete the picture.Mundaun is a horror game which must not be overlooked, a real gem inside the enormous amount of trash we've grown accustomed to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: Mundaun is an interesting horror title, with an old 1920's washed out retro visual style and deliciously strange and surreal horror, which grabs you even before a title screen is shown. The location within the Swiss Alps feels unique and well established, and the macabre mood of unsettling horror is strong. While these are merely first impressions, the game features a clear novelty, an excellent sense of horror and I'm excited to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good so far. The hand drawn look of the game makes it feel really unique. The story is super interesting as well and gives a sense of dark horror without being outright scary. I would really recommend this. I am only about an hour in but if you want to see my first look at it you can check out the link below. You should really play it for yourself first though so as not to spoil anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

_childDocuments_.review: After learning of his grandfathers mysterious death in a fire, the protagonist travels to Mundaun for the first time since childhood. He will soon discover that something old and diabolical is haunting the remaining inhabitants. The quest to find out the meaning behind these sinister events takes the player on an odyssey up Mundaun mountain: From steep meadows across stony fields and to the snow-covered peak. Mundaun is a lovingly hand-pencilled horror tale set in a dark, secluded valley of the alps. Explore various areas full of secrets to discover, survive hostile encounters, drive vehicles, fill your inventory and solve a variety of hand-crafted puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Mundaun

name: Vigil: The Longest Night
detailed_description: Embark on a Shadowy Adventure 'Vigil: The Longest Night' is a side-scrolling action game in the Metroidvania style, inspired by classics like 'Salt and Sanctuary' and 'Castlevania.' It offers broad map exploration, a rich combat mechanism, and a unique storyline with dark narratives. Players will accompany the Vigilant Leila on her journey of trials, protecting the town, combating evil creatures, and gradually uncovering the mysteries of Shimmer's Faith and its hidden schemes. Master the Art of Combat Players can choose from an extensive range of weapons, including swords, axes, daggers, and bows, many featuring their unique attack styles and moves, or even engage in combat unarmed. This varied weaponry, coupled with a combination of distinct arcane abilities and throwable items, provides many combat options beyond basic weaponry. This allows players to choose the most suitable combat style based on their preferences and the unique characteristics of each weapon. Forge Your Path with Custom Gear The game offers a wide array of equipment for players to choose from. Through enchant and Forge systems, players can further craft unique equipment to face the challenges of brutal combat. Unravel Secrets of a Mysterious World Players will start their adventure from Maye town, freely exploring the vast world and dungeons, uncovering secrets related to the story, interacting with distinctive NPCs, and acquiring rare items and equipment. Face the Horrors of the Night Vigil features over a hundred monsters, as well as nearly 20 boss battles, ranging from humanoid bosses to gigantic creatures, providing a thrilling and challenging combat experience.
