Unravel Secrets of a Mysterious World Players will start their adventure from Maye town, freely exploring the vast world and dungeons, uncovering secrets related to the story, interacting with distinctive NPCs, and acquiring rare items and equipment. Face the Horrors of the Night Vigil features over a hundred monsters, as well as nearly 20 boss battles, ranging from humanoid bosses to gigantic creatures, providing a thrilling and challenging combat experience.
short_description: Embark on a journey through the longest night with Leila, a valiant member of the Vigilant Order. Delve into the hidden truths shrouded in eternal darkness, unravel the mystery surrounding Leila's enigmatic sister, and confront the eldritch horrors lurking in a world that has lost the light of day.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't the best metroidvania game - and this leans 100% toward the Castlevania part of that - Bloodstained is definitely better in terms of recent releases. It is enjoyable and worth checking out if you've exhausted other games and need to scratch the itch, but it has quite a few things that hold it back from being truly satisfying. 6/10 alone. Using a 100% complete/annotated "cheat" map to help resolve some of the below, 7.5/10. I would comparatively give Bloodstained 9/10 base or 10/10 if allowing for outside sources for completionists. Bloodstained also includes alternative character modes which aren't my thing, but definitely cool for some.- Story is OK so far, setting is good but standard gothic monster fare. - I mostly like the weapon/armor upgrade system. Upgrade components are a bit rare relative to weapons you may want to upgrade, and discourages experimentation in early-mid game (0-10 hours).- Gold is a bit stingy, and monster drops could be better managed. Mostly minor.- The RPG component is OK, but I wish there was a more generalized "physical attack" tree, along with a dedicated "magic" tree; as is there's 4 weapon-type trees (sword/balanced, axe/heavy, bows/ranged, daggers/light) and a general character tree that covers magic and all stats. Switch weapon types and you can lose up to 20 levels of specialized skills that have zero influence on the other 3 weapon trees.- I wish the individual spells had an upgrade path like weapons because so far it's very underwhelming (a spell you can get during the first 1-2 hours is as good or better than most spells you get in hours 3-8). - Quest tracking could be strongly improved. There are many characters and it's sometimes very obvious what you need to do, while in other cases it may be entirely across the map. Some quests get tons of step updates; others are 2-3 notes that can span multiple areas requiring a new ability to access each area.- Exploration could be improved, especially regarding platforming - it's not very clear when you need to just find a better jump point vs when you need a new ability or to approach it from a completely different point on the map. In contrast obstacles that can only be destroyed/opened from one side (unlocking map shortcuts), or by a certain skill are very well marked. - Fall damage is bad, especially for as much as they encourage pushing boundaries to reach certain platforms for upgrades/weapons. It can also be pretty unforgiving even if you survive fall damage, where certain jumps can require a minute or two to get back to try it again. The decision to not have "10% health damage and instant recovery" is annoying. - Save/teleport could be improved. The points are relatively plentiful but a bit inconsistently spread out. There is a skill to instantly teleport back to the last point interacted with and a consumable item to create a "quick save". The number of fall deaths, or wow, I messed that up, I'd rather restart than spend 4 minutes getting back there is annoying. - "Branch exploration" is pretty inconsistent. Sometimes really exploring an area uncovers a powerful item. Most often it uncovers nothing. - Movement skills need some tweaking. Double jump or air dash lets you easily recover from what would be failed single jumps. Some interim optional skill is needed to allow you to recover from sub-optimal double jump + air dash attempts.Many of the past bullets make necessary to consult one of the external maps (Steam Guides) to figure out how to proceed forward unless you want to spend 30 minutes moving around the map and seeing where you may have missed something, only to discover you need to solve a completely different part of the map. Where to obtain new movement skills, find quest items, move quests forward, find unique items, what is jumpable, or solve hidden quests is far more difficult than it should be without.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Vigil: The Longest Night is alright. And that's just it:  alright. I would give it a neutral review if I could, but Steam only allows the two nuclear options. Vigil is weirdly clunky in a way other Soulslikes and Metroidvanias I've played aren't. Menus and combat feel weirdly stiff when compared to something like Salt and Sanctuary, bosses aren't particularly engaging, controls are frustrating (Dash is on the right D-Pad by default, when, if trying to hold the controller in a way that makes that even remotely comfortable, you'll probably crouch, halting any and all movement), platforming feels finicky and occasionally it takes multiple tries to climb onto a ledge, death brings you back to a save instead of the Owl Statue for a corpse run (Which, is really odd for a Soulslike to break up gameplay like that), etcetera.  All in all, it feels extremely unpolished, which is unfortunate, because the story isn't all bad, the setting is pretty decent, the visuals are alright, and the music is quite good. I'd rather play Salt and Sanctuary, Bloodborne or Hollow Knight instead, but if you've exhausted most of the games like this and want something new, maybe grab this on like 30% sale. You could do worse than play this.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - very good combat varied build possibility, passable plot, oversized map design and not so well executed quest system, somewhat rewarding exploration with a limited item roster (a lot of duplicates dropping from chests). Worth the price for the combat and build variety, but if you are looking for a good story and metroidvania style progression of movement and abilities, you may come out dissapointed.Now let's dissect the above:So the combat and fluidity of it was really nailed down in this game, the enemy roster is varied enough, and their attack patterns are well telegraphed making it very awesome experience to dodge, block, parry and fight in general. There are 4 types of weapons to use, each with a skill tree attached to it, adding some nice looking moves, along with a passive tree that increases genral stats.When it comes to equipment it provides a very varied experience and each part of the equipment is acutally viisble on the character (kudos to that)The story was very vague and not very interesting, it contain several endings, but personally didn't have the strenght to finish up the game with be best ending due to a overbearing amount of quests, frustrating quest menu and an oversized map to go with it (with a very hard to read world map)Now while we're on the map point - this is probably the second weakest point next to the story. The areas are definelty TOO BIG to hold interest and very quickly drains the will to explore. What doesn't help with holding the interest of cheking evey nook and cranny, is the fact that you get a lot of duplicate items, and only a few location have unique items from my experience (most of em are quest related). The next thing is that most areas are open from the start and not require any special abilities to get to, so you are quickly overwhelmed by the crazy amount of exits and area switches, (And the consistency of the legend on the map is horrible)So in conclusion: The combat in this game definetly carried the experience for me, the basic story would've been fine if not for an overbearing amount of quests that quickly fill out your log book making it hard to track anything going on. From the 14 hours I spent most of it was exploration and trying to grasp where to go and what to do next from the quest log. It's definetly a solid buy on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my first time to really play a 2D Bloodstained/Castlevania type game, so I don't have much to compare this game to. Regardless of comparisons,  I have been enjoying the game to say the least.The only complaints I can think of are weird incidents with  taking fall damage (eg, trying to mitigate fall damage by double jumping or using an ability before landing but still taking fall damage. Also one that blew my mind was dropping down to grab a ledge, then taking damage and dying after climbing up from the ledge.) I also feel taking damage in combat is not visually apparent enough and don't notice I've taken damage until I look at my health bar. This might just be me though.Everything else is great though.Combat is really engaging and diverse, and I've only been using one weapon.Graphics and art are splendid.Leveling progression feels smooth as opposed to grindy like a lot of rpgs.Though dying is meaningful and really sucks when unprepared, there are mechanics to ease the losses if you make good judgement.Boss fights feel meh (Though I've only killed the first 3 or so)Edit: I play this game in Chinese, but in response to the other reviews/comments about this game having awkward dialogue - This game was made (in part at least?) by Taiwanese developers, whose native language may not be English.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A game with excellent visual and musical art direction, good exploration, and solid skill trees let down by terrible controls, frustrating questing / good ending gatekeeping, an annoying save system and severe balance issues (no challenge after gear upgraded at mid game).Anyway this game has some really cool stuff about it but the cons really soured my experience overall. If they tightened the controls, balanced it properly for hard mode, used a modern save system, and made the questing less ridiculous, it would've been a classic. _childDocuments_.review: This game is outstanding, but it has one of the worst and most confusing intros I have ever seen. The first hour of the game is basically a prologue introducing you to the bizarre world of The Longest Night - an intricate blend of Slavic myth, Christian theology and Lovecraftian horror by way of Taiwan. Falling heavily in the action-rpg square of the Metroidavania axis, you'll have to talk to villagers to get quests, puzzle out some cryptic clues and make decisions that have huge effects on the story and progression - including making difficult trade offs with no good solutions and where someone will suffer no matter what you do (well placed in an eldritch universe where most people die in horror and misery).An hour long prologue probably seems excessive, but another cool thing about Vigil is that it is proper old school metroidvania length. You're looking at 12 hours plus to finish the game, and well in excess of 24 if you want to 100% it. There are entire areas you won't even know exist if you don't go exploring, and the unique setting and combat make exploration continuously feel worthwhile.The combat follows the Soulsborne variety, and there are items in the game which allow you to tilt it further in the souls or the borne direction - imo the game is meant to be played borne style though, with decisive aggression. This isn't apparent when you first start playing because until you are used to its odd rhythm the combat feels like a slowmo or semi-detached button masher, but the last boss of the prologue basically forces you to learn the combat flow. The enemies vary from forest creatures and bandits through mythical beasts and the undead and on to mutilated flesh experiments, cosmic horrors and even deities. Lastly I want to mention the music, which is beautiful and brilliant at setting the mood of mingled awe and despair befitting a story where even the secret best ending is a nightmare. If you like cosmic horror or massive metroidvanias, Vigil is well worth a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigil: The Longest Night is a game developed by Glass Heart Games and published by Another Indie. It's pretty much a Metroidvania combined with some horror elements. It has a solid story, good combat, nice art, four skill trees and lots and lots of equipment and several sidequests. Good:+Each weapon has a unique style, same goes for the skill tree for that weapon.+Impressive mood and setting, dark and gloomy.+Good replay value due the three endings and different skill trees.+Lot of maps to explore, more than I expected.+Interesting designs for all bosses. Bad:-While the music is good, it tends to get repetitive.-No warning on the three points of no return. While the last one is forgivable because it's right before the last boss/dungeon, the first one comes out of the blue.-Some jumps are very, very precise and annoying. At least it's only for extra content and not plot. -A couple of plot points are abandoned or not given proper closure.Despite the flaws the game is very, very recommended. Bugs have been fixed and the devs have listened to feedback and improved stuff. The visuals are amazing and can help you inspire your tabletop horror campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: Something just felt off about this game. By all accounts I should love it, because I love Dark Souls 1, 2, and 3... and I've played those games, beaten them, and recently got Dark Souls Remastered to experience the first game again. I also love Metroidvanias, such as Hollow Knight, Bloodstained, and the Metroid series itself. But Vigil just didn't feel good to play, as soon as I hit the first boss I was instantly frustrated and annoyed. The clunky movement didn't help with how unfairly precise dodging must be to avoid its attacks, and the fact it can just push you into a corner to combo you down was irritating. The fact the arena for the first boss was so small didn't help me getting backed into a corner. The game, by all accounts, seems awesome and I can see why people love it but it just isn't for me. I need better and more precise control, and more fluid combat, to enjoy this game. It also, quite frankly, feels like it's trying too hard to be Dark Souls with how the movement and dodging feels, but it just doesn't work in 2D dimensional play ( which is fine and great, I LOVE Metroid Dread and other sidescrollers, and it can work in other games ). Grime is a better example of a game far more forgiving and fluid with its movements and combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Vigil is a Victorian Metroidvania that feels as though it drew a great deal of inspiration from bloodborne. With the plethora of updates it's received. The combat is even more fluid and functional. The world is fairly large so there is no shortage of exploration, The abilities you acquire to traverse and even some combat abilities make traversal somewhat of an incredible performance. There are a few build types to play around with that add to the variety. With a surprising amount of depth if you actually want to get deep into it. None of that is required to see completion. That's all a nice addition and function which is always available to you. There are plenty of side quests to keep you busy and the bosses are some of the strongest aspects of the game (a common theme I seem to find in metroidvania/souls-like games). Which isn't necessarily a bad thing. Overall functionality and presentation remain solid and this game seems at best 8/10 and at worst 7/10. Arguably worth it at full price, but I have seen it on sale a few times so if you want to save some money and still get a good game. Hold off for a sale, the game isn't going anywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very much enjoying this game.  The controls feel so nice and tight.  I tend to shy away from most games with a lot of platforming, this game took care of a lot of my frustrations.  Jumping feels precise, the 'pull up on ledge' mechanic works well and there was rarely an area where I jumped forever, missed one jump and then died or had to start all over again.  (My own poor reaction times not withstanding.)Big fan of the art style.  I love how even though it is dark and displays a level of despair and hopelessness, it still has a wide range of colors.  The monsters look appropriately disturbing and fit their areas well.Music is fantastic, moody where appropriate yet also pulse pounding and strong when needed.We've already had a few quality of life improvements showing that feedback is being listened to.Combat feels very satisfying (though an issue some of us have with a dual blades move I hope is addressed).I can't speak to challenge levels first hand as, because I was so eager to see more, my first run has been on easy and while I felt I probably could have handled Normal, I've not tried it yet.  Still, nothing in easy felt like a cake-walk, which I'm glad for.The quest system does not hold your hand.  I love that.  I missed doing something in the earlier part of the game that directly effected the ending I was able to get.  You need to talk to NPCs multiple times on top of not rushing through a few things.  I am not complaining about that in the slightest.  I liked I couldn't go back and fix that since it was my fault for assuming I'd already spoken to someone.  Honestly, I'm looking for the NG+ run I've just started now that I've got a taste of everything, found the weapon types I like, and feel more patient about how to handle things.Overall, I just really enjoy this game and look forward to playing more.

_childDocuments_.review: This...This does put a smile on my face.What a familiar feeling...I've been washed up on a coast with nothing to my name besides the starting gear and a complete lack of understanding to the world around me.Dangers and monsters of all manner, twisted and grotesque. They lunge and bite, snap and gnaw at what sanity I have left. My heart pounds at the sight of them, my mind reels and grows cold with fear at their cries. I feel the earth beneath my quaking boots shake...Something has disturbed that great old tree...As I face the untold masses of monstrosities only born from the most vivid of nightmares made manifest, I feel but one thing.The racing beat of my heart, rising to meet the night with a blazing passion. Radiant like the sun is my desire to shed the blood of these beasts, and so it shall be done.For my mind is broken and my sweat runs cold, but my heart is in my craft and my hands are steady.The night is long, dear vigil...but a Hunter must Hunt...So, good hunting to you.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, it feels good and it has that obvious Bloodborne vibe to it, but who the hell decided that resetting progress on death was a good idea?  It's not. It's a bad idea. It makes me not want to play this game because while it hasn't been super hard just yet, it's also easy to die, like, for instance, if you fall down an elevator shaft. Take my xp earned, gold, w/e, just let me keep my map progress. Very frustrating.Amending my initial review, but leaving the words there because they still apply. I've put 10 hours into this game now, and I've very much fallen for it. Once I established that death means an erasure of all progress, I simply stopped dying. Glibness aside, the game actually isn't very difficult, at least the way I'm going through it. The iframes are very generous, you can get quite powerful pretty fast, and it almost feels like the Vigilant is bullying her way through the game for the most part. And I like that. This game nails atmosphere and tone, and doesn't hold your hand in the way of all Souls likes. It feels quite good, from the platforming to the combat - it's all very tight. I'm impressed with the scope of the game. It seems like it just keeps opening up, and my map at this point is looking remarkably robust. There are some things I wish it did better. I think it could benefit for a more user friendly inventory screen. The way it mashes together consumables and magic spells is not very player-friendly, and honestly it sells the magic system short. There are a lot of spells I'd probably use more if I weren't afraid of accidentally burning a consumable. This might be a hollow fear considering the game is very generous in doling out its consumables, but players have a conserve mindset when it comes to that stuff. It's very obvious what this game is going for. It's the closest thing to a side scrolling Bloodborne that exists. It borders on plagiarism at times, but I've no complaints there. Bloodborne is a masterpiece worthy of mimicry. The game does enough different, obviously in its mechanics, that it doesn't feel derivative. In feel, it reminds me more of Hollow Knight than any other metroidvania that I've played. I'm not entirely sure why that is, but it feels like it has something to do with the world layout. Everything is connected in a satisfying way. The only other thing I can think of is that I wish there were some indication that you were leaving the prologue area because I'd have liked to finish the quests I had there, and the lack of any clear guides in the game meant that I basically stumbled out of it just exploring. Not a huge deal, but something that would have been nice to include.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but I'm a good way through.If you're looking for a difficult game, then this isn't really it.  It can be tough at times, but is way more level.  It's actually a lot like Salt & Sanctuary in that way (I absolutely loved S&S).  I don't think this game has gotten enough visibility, it is an excellent game, and really enjoyable to explore.There are three (technically 5) weapon classes (sword, dagger, axe, bow, and arcane).  By far my favorite is the axe, I always play a slow heavy hitter in these souls-likes :-P.  Within each weapon class there are a number of weapons which are slightly different (and some in each have unique attacks that you input using a movement followed by attack).  This makes exploration fun and rewarding (you never know when you'll find a new weapon or ring/armor).The art is beautiful, and it's almost always easy to determine what's foreground or background (every foreground object has some form of a color marker differentiating it from the background).  The usefulness and ease it makes playing cannot be understated.  The enemies aren't too difficult, and have easily learnable patterns.  The areas are diverse, and each has a unique presentation.The bosses are definitely the highlight with the design and attack patterns (and many have multiple phases).  None so far have been too difficult, but challenging enough to be fun (not too many trivial pushovers).Overall, this is a great game, and if you've played S&S and enjoyed it then it's a must buy.  However, even if you're just looking for a good souls-like or metroidvania, you'll likely have a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: These are my impressions from the first 3 hours:An excellent Metroidvania game, fantastic art style, intriguing world and lore, tight combat and platforming.I am not going to lie when I first saw that the game had souls like elements I was a little put off, I am not one to die over and over again, lose my progress and grind out a win. I gave this game a go anyway as I knew I had the safety of the refund window. I can safely say that even though this game has those souls like elements they have been implemented in a way that makes the game extremely accessible. The combat in games like this is fairly basic but satisfying nonetheless, at times you will be challenged, at time you will feel invincible, the game continues to make you feel good about yourself.My only issue at the minute is that good loot seems to be few and far between, I have downed 3 bosses so far and still using the original sword. Some of the dialogue is misspelled but It is not noticeable enough for me to really mark the game down.If you are a fan of 2d side scrollers, metroidvania games, souls games, do yourself a favour and pick up this gem.Review edit: I have now finished this game so I want to make some additions to this review. The lack of voice acting really does start to get tedious and does break the immersion somewhat, the story ends up being very shallow which is a bit of a disappointment as it had so much potential. The combat becomes a bit too repetitive too, especially when you have levelled your chosen weapon, you can just steamroll through the game. The biggest negative for me is that there is a LOT of missable content, this is unfortunate as I do not feel that the game is good enough to warrant a second playthrough. The quests are also left very ambiguous to try and force you to explore the map, quite often I was lost as I had the quest item but I had no idea where I had to take it. I think if they made a second game and fixed some of the things I and others have mentioned they could have something quite compelling.I am still recommending the game as I do think it is worth a playthrough, just be warned there are quite a few issues with it however.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Vigil as a metroidvania with some Souls-like combat mechanics. But I loved it because of the art style, the atmosphere of the world and the exploration. I felt transported back in time to the dark fir-studded skyline of the original Castlevania games. There are a good number of large interconnected areas, including towns, forests, catacombs, mountains, mines, swamp, etc. The NPCs you meet along the way have only a few lines of dialogue, but they contribute to making the map feel like a real cohesive country. It's certainly not the Witcher 3 but it made me feel a tiny bit like that.The combat relies on dodging, blocking and parrying, with stamina management. However, the stamina is so generous and replenishes so fast that I rarely paid attention to it. There are 4 different weapon types with their own skill tree, plus magic spells, though I only used swords in combat and never found it necessary to switch to a different fighting style. Combat felt satisfying but not challenging most of the time. I beat the majority of the bosses on the first or second try, except a couple of the optional late-game bosses. Still they were all very fun to fight and had memorable designs.Movements and animation felt fluid and responsive, which is important for a metroidvania. But the number of traversal skills you unlock are not very numerous or original. There's a double-jump, and a slide to pass through narrow spaces. A mid-air dash I got very late in the game. Still there are many secrets to discover and collectibles to find such as special weapons, outfits and decorations for your home.Overall a surprisingly satisfying experience at a very good price.

_childDocuments_.review: A rather strange Metroidvania that's greater than the sum of its parts -- it's kinda all over the place in terms of balance and the storytelling/localization is really janky, but the core combat is fun as hell and the world exploration is extremely satisfying.If it doesn't hook you at first, try pushing through until you get past the "prologue" (you'll know it when you reach it). The game didn't "click" for me at first since it feels a bit constrained, but once you get past the intro the entire map opens for you explore in almost any order you want, with most "open" level design I've ever seen in a 'Vania. Seems antithetical to the genre, but it works here, somehow.tl;dr: Definitely worth a play if you don't mind a bit of quirkiness.

_childDocuments_.review: VISUALSThe visuals here are fantastic and somewhat reminiscent of Vanillaware’s painterly style. I was consistently surprised by the number of unique assets and attention to detail in the environments; the foreground, backgrounds and interiors all look great and are suitably atmospheric. Weapons and armour all change the cosmetic appearance of your character. Great job on the visuals.STORYIn terms of story I was really surprised by how effectively the narrative hooked me. While some aspects of the lore are reminiscent of Dark Souls cryptic “piece it together yourself” style of storytelling, the core narrative is relatively straightforward and easy to follow. The NPCs you’ll meet on your journey are surprisingly well characterised, despite no voice acted dialogue, and as you unearth the games mysteries you’ll learn more and more about the relationships in this little village. Without spoiling anything, the story itself has echos of Bloodborne. This can be seen both thematically and, at times, visually (you can even dress your character in such a way that they very much resemble BBs "hoonters”) though it is told in a much different way and definitely carves it own path.GAMEPLAY/MECHANICSAfter playing Vigil’s demo, I was a little worried about how this game would come together. Turns out I shouldn’t have been. Vigil is a fantastic Metroidvania and fans of the genre will recognise inspirations and similarities to some classic titles. Most notably the game pays homage to Ska Studios fantastic 2D Souls-like Salt & Sanctuary (there’s even some cross-over content in the game). Where the two titles differ, in my opinion, is in which sub-genre they skew toward most. S&S aimed to be 2D Dark Souls; it had DkS style sword and board combat, no map, DkS style lore, bonfire style checkpoints and currency lost upon death that could be retrieved if you didn't die before getting to it.Vigil, on the other hand, aims to be a Metroidvania first and foremost. There’s a map that is revealed as you explore more of the world (though it is not terribly useful right now), abilities that allow you to reach previously unreachable areas and when you die you are taken back to your last save and any progress you made is lost. The combat does have a lot in common with S&S (rolls, dodges, blocks, parries etc.). It’s weighty and feels good though the roll sometimes feels like it has excessive i-frames. Like S&S there are plenty of weapons and armour sets to be found and skill trees to upgrade & unlock. Level design is good and the game has fast travel between checkpoints right from the start, so backtracking is no chore at all. The game can be challenging but not oppressively so.One quick tip for anyone picking this up. The game does have a few "points of no return" that can cause you to miss items/quests for the entire playthrough. If, like me, you always do your first run of a game blind you won't care but for players who may find this annoying at least you now know they exist and you can check a guide to identify these points before you hit them. AUDIOWhat’s there is good. Sound effects are fine and although the soundtrack is very good, I feel like it could have done with a few more tracks. One track in particular is straight out of the Castlevania playbook!DEMOGRAPHICThe game can be very gory and sometimes quite disturbing. Should be ok for players 15+ in my opinion.DIFFICULTYAs mentioned, the game can be challenging but nothing a little practice and perseverance can’t overcome from what I’ve seen.BUGSSo far nothing too bad:-The script and item descriptions could use another once over to remove the semi-frequent typos and grammatical errors I’ve come across (some fixes according to last patch notes)-Found a bug where certain arcane items no longer work after a certain point (fixed)-I've been able to jump out of bounds on a few occasions. One time I was able to bypass a section of an area by double jumping toward, then falling down the left edge of the screen at the Graveyard just before Catacombs (fixed)In general the game was mostly fine for me at launch. EDIT: The developers have updated the game with many fixes and additional content in the following months. GRINDIt’s possible to grind up levels relatively quickly in Vigil if needed. I did a bit of early game grind in the first hour to level up the sword skill tree but since then I haven’t really needed to. DURATIONThe game world is sprawling and really opens up after the first "Act". There's countless secret areas to find, many of them hidden in satisfying ways. It gives me a similar feeling that I had playing Hollow Knight in that just when you think you've explored an area completely you find a hidden path that takes you into a completely new area.PRICEThis is a must-play at full price for Metroidvania lovers.I seriously enjoyed this game and hope it does really well. It's probably in my top 5 games of 2020. Congratulations Glass Heart Games on this fantastic title! Overall Rating 9/10!

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly one of the best Metroidvania games I've played in decades.  The gameplay is smooth, and the character progression is balanced enough to prevent you from growing into godhood and rendering the game too easy, but rapid enough to give you that constant sense of advancement that makes you feel like you're accomplishing something.The combat is a homogeneous blend of equipment combinations and player skill, but with more emphasis on the latter.  The result is a gameplay experience that favors quick reflexes and clever tactics over constant grinding for "the best drops," and this does wonders to keep things well-paced and stave off those bouts of boredom inherent in other games that found us constantly killing the same mobs over and over to get "that one sword" we needed to move on.It also features a wide variety of offensive (and defensive) abilities that cater to an equally broad variety of play styles.  If you're the type that likes to get in close, deal lots of damage, then dart away before the enemy can strike—there's a gear set for that.  If you want to storm in, tank a hit, and win the battle by sheer virtue of dishing out far more than you take—there's a gear set for that.  If you'd rather stand back, far back, and plink away slowly at your enemies while they scream and grunt, frustratingly unable to even reach you to counterattack as their hitpoints slowly dwindle away, one arrow at a time—there's a gear set for that, too—and a whole host of things in the in-betweens of all of these.The art is beautiful, some of the best I’ve seen in a sidescroller.  I’ve seen complaints that the animations “lack weight,” but I feel like this complaint is overstated; and, indeed, if present at all, is part of the intended effect.  The developers state that they’re going for a cut-paper effect, and I believe they’ve nailed this very effectively.  If I had to make one complaint about the art, it would be that it’s too good, in some places.  2D/2.5D sidescrollers rely on certain “cartoonish” aspects of their artwork to denote and create focal points in the environment, e.g., platforms and walkable surfaces most notably.  This is the heart of one of my two major complaints:  though they have tried to make these distinctions, the art is so well done and so seamless that sometimes it can be slightly difficult to distinguish between walkable and non-walkable surfaces—and fall damage is very much a thing in this game, though there is a way to mitigate it as you progress.The soundtrack is amazing, and very much brings back a swell of memories of the genre’s ancestors as you play.  I find, however, that there are times when the music will mysteriously stop for long periods of time, usually amid area transitions, and then resume at awkward points.  These strange interruptions in background music can be something of a distraction, considering that they often happen in areas where you are actively in combat.The story is compelling enough to maintain your interest, and drive you to interact with NPCs and complete their questlines without being overbearing and railroading your every movement and action.  The sidequests are interesting and rewarding enough, though be warned, it is not only possible, but also quite easy, to permanently fail many quests, some of them main-plot critical.Which brings me to my second and final major complaint:  there is no tangible barrier to failing many of these fail-able quests.  If you just so happen to progress to certain points without visiting certain areas first, there are NPCs that will literally never appear (to your knowledge), and quests that will simply pop up as “failed” in your notes without any explanation whatsoever.  In order to complete this game to the fullest, it becomes necessary to meticulously explore every new area with microscopic scrutiny—usually multiple times, at least once after every major game event—or risk permanent loss.  This creates a massive speed bump in an otherwise perfectly-paced game.All-in-all, however, if you are a fan of Metroidvanias, specifically SOTN-era Castlevania, then I believe you owe it to yourself to give Vigil: The Longest Night a go.  As always, search for gameplay videos and read more than just one review before you spend the bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game. Some highlights are the graphics and the character models. Something that I really appreciate is the fact that armor pieces do change the character model. This is something that it is not quite common any longer, but I do like it a lot. The story/lore and soundtrack are fantastic and the gameplay is great. I have been playing with a generic controller and so far so good.  I have been playing around 23 hours, and I have been having a blast. I do have some negatives. The minor issue is that some of the items portraits do not display correctly when you are in the menus, but the text remains so you will know with what item are you dealing with. The biggest issue is the map. The map does not display correctly, and it varies, in some areas no map is displayed at all, in some it works, and in some, it does not display correctly. Let say that I am in the Wasted Town, but the map marker shows that I am by the Mine. It is not a game breaker. You can definitely find your way around, but it is a bit frustrating since, to my surprise (a good one), the game is rather big. There is plenty to do, many areas to visit, and some secret ones as well. My suggestion is to use the "Teleport" feature in the save points. Otherwise, you might get lost a few times since the map is not reliable.

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage port for a pretty interesting game.It's a fine game, ugly, but fine.It tries to be Salt & Sanctuary but fails in certain fields. For instance the death mechanic is similar to Castlevania, where it would greatly benefit from Dark Souls mode. The reason behind this is most enemies hit rather hard and it is really easy to get killed. This only makes you not want to explore, as if you'll find something rare, talk to NPCs, complete a quest and die afterwards, you will have to do everything again. The exploration is another issue. There are so many secrets, yet they rarely will reward you with anything useful. Prepare to find useless consumables and piss poor amount of money. Bosses are fine, but are veeeryyy easy, and very easy to counter - the hardest and last I've enountered was the big frog creature. Killed me twice until I relized that Vinegar makes you completely immune to poison for several seconds..Map is fine, but becomes useless due to different areas you can enter via gates which take you to completely different place on a map. Gets confusing really fast.Don't try to understand the story, the game isn't properly translated into English. Everyone just talk nonsense and I don't know if it's intentional or not.The game also has a point of no return and it won't warn you about it. You will propably have some of the map unexplored because of that.Combat mechanics, leveling up, and upgrades are done well, and this is the part where the game shines.The biggest problem is, it's very unstable, to the point of freezing my PC and forcing me to gard reset. It also crashes constantly without any reason.The online solution suggested that my PC isn't powerful enough... My PC that can run CP2077 on ultra with raytracing on cannot run this without issues?I would recommend the game as it is fun to play, but not when it kills my PC.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 3 hours I was thinking to myself that the game feels like a dull overly long tutorial more than anything. Turns out that is because the first half of the game IS a overly long tutorial. Half way through the game is reset and you can start playing the actual game. If you don't know that is coming, like I did, you can easily fail most sidequests when you accidentally pass the point of no return. Which is an ... interesting design decision. Main issue is that the combat in the game is not great. Only one weapon type has parry so don't get too attached to that mechanic. Also enemies can dodge your attacks but they don't telegraph that with good animations but instead a simple DODGE text appears to let you know. Similarly the brood mother, one of the first bosses is awful to fight as her armsweep fills literally the entire screen so you have to dodge the exact second she attacks no matter where you stand. Later bosses have easier patterns but that one is really awful. Since this game is so drawn out I still can't comment on how it will come together at the end or even if. I mean in the tutorial there is a spot that tells you about your magic meter and stats, yet I have not encountered a single magic item (except the thing that lets you warp to save points). Some of the drops of the enemies go under "quest items" in your inventory but I haven't found a fetch quest yet so I don't know if they actually ever used for quests or if I should sell them.This is a game where I feel like opening a wiki every few minutes which I never do on principle (Which also lead me to fail most quests so there is that).All in all this game is a very mixed bag and I can understand why it had an initial bad reception.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly good and fun metroidvania!The controls are super tight and I did not have any "I totally crapped that ledge when I fell to pit" deaths that many recent similar games had. Some combat moves can be little hard to execute using x-box controller but those are minor issues that do not really take away from the game.The combat itself is really good and using many different weapons will affect your tactics. The enemies arent anything to write home about but they can be challenging, especially on higher difficulties.Graphically the game is hit & miss for me. I like how the atmosphere is, but some assets are down right ugly to look at and can sometimes make platforming or finding secrets hard (thats the point I quess) before you realise what is what in the world. It does not ruin the game, and at the end of the game I found myself really enjoying the style and aesthetics the game had going, but I am not just fan of the artstyle itself, but we cant all like apples.Music in this game is amazing! The soundtrack really has that good old castlevania feel to it but still adding its own amazing spin to it. Shame the game does not have spoken dialogue because there is quite a lot to read in the game. And on that note the games biggest issue the game has comes from typos and wonky dialogue.The game is NOT souls-like in the sense that if you die all your stuff will stay there waiting you. Once you die you will have to replay all the stuff you did to the point where you saved the game, so if you clear the map 100% and die at the very end to anything, its back to clearing that map all over again, kinda like in Super Metroid back in the day. So save the game, A LOT!!!And speaking of stuff, there is a lot to discover in this world! It is so much fun to try and find every little hidden secret via platforming on top of trees or going deeper into monster filled cavern and find some kick ass looking gear or new weapon and skill to use. The game really rewards you with exploration and the more skills you get, the more open the world becomes.The game has NG+ that allows you to take along your skills and gear so you can use your favourite weapons to kick the earlier bosses and clear some missions you might have missed or see the other endings the game has to offer, 3 in total.The game did not crash on me once and I had only few minor bugs that did not break the game, but did lock me out of 2 side missions (NPC not appearing or the quest just not finishing) but 99% of the time it was smooth sailing. Highly recommend this to any metroidvania fans who enjoy bloodborne-styled world and killing eldrich monsters.

_childDocuments_.review: **If you have trouble with your PS4 controller, you need to disable Steam native controller support for the game.1. Right-click on game, properties, general (tab), "steam input per game" (change to off).2. In game, settings, controller, change to (ps4 1st row, and usb 2nd row).This game seems very underrated. It has lovely graphics and great soulslike gameplay with various characters with their own personalities and quests which give way to an engaging story.PROSThere is a solid skill tree for various weapons and general abilities. Combat is quite deep with dodging, parrying and backstabs though you have to unlock abilities for some of these functions. You have various weapon types with different abilities and movesets. There are also multiple spells with varied functions and graphics as well as thrown weapons. There are also various armour and ring types and interestingly, there is a poise mechanic.Gameplay is highly dependent on skill. I found it smooth and enjoyable but you NEED to effectively use timing, dodging and backstepping.CONSThere are numerous typos or mediocre translations, even early in the game. This sharply contrasts with the excellent quality of the graphics and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: For a first time indy team, and at the price point, very much worth it. Have finished an entire run through, 100% but with minor bugged quests.Over-all: it's not that original in design, but the art is good, the mechanics decent (with some codas) and the pacing is good. At the moment it's rather easy if you've played a lot of metrovanias and the RPG mechanics are a bit light (although, apparently: +stats come in NG which is an odd choice). The skill trees are decent (although some skills are vastly better than others - looking at Axe/Halberd Earthshaker, will carry you through the entire game) and there's a medium amount of variety to the load outs / weapons. You can grind areas / drops, but it's really not required as most drop rates are generous and just by playing you'll naturally find most items. It has a strong emphasis on platforming, although later abilities (double-jump / dash etc) make this much easier: but there's a generous lee-way for it and very few "pixel perfect" jumps required.All weapons/armors change the character model, which was a nice touch (and missing from Bloodstained) - the enemy variety is good (if a little strange in the pacing: for instance even the last level up to the end has unique enemies you'll only see there) and the bosses range from good to merely ok (some have too heavy RNG on attacks, allowing them to chain stun the player easily).There's some minor quest flag bugs and achievements not firing, but other than that the game is stable & didn't find any code / game mechanics bugs or stuck in geometry, which given the platforming was nice. Devs are active on the forums and seem intent on patching out bugs quickly.Over-all: very good first effort, if you like Metrovanias / 2D aRPGs worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game.Combat is well-designed, there's 4 different weapon-types to choose from, all of which have their own skilltree and play in different ways. You can equip three weapons at the same time and switch between them, so you don't need to equip a new weapon from your inventory every time. There are also items like throwing knifes, bombs and poison needles if you prefer fighting with throwing weapons, as well as arcane items and mana if you want to play as a mage. Overall the combat is pretty balanced, with exceptions of Hand of Shadow, Mechanical Bow and the sword's heavy attack. These let you pretty much ignore any difficulty that is present throughout the game. Upgrading and enchanting your weapons will make the game pretty easy as well.Enemy design is okay, the non-boss enemies fit well into the style of the game and the area they are in. The bosses are pretty cool. Most of them are large mutated creatures that in reality would kill the player character in a single attack, so killing them feels good.Story is good, and is told to the player through character interactions and writings that are found through the game. There are quests you can do too, that will give you weapons/armors/furniture as a reward. Like every Souls-like, there are different endings depending on what actions the player chooses to take, so if you want, you can play through the game multiple times to get all of them, or all in the same playthough by going back to an earlier save file.Soundtrack was great, it fit really well with the artstyle. It made backtracking to get all of the achievements a lot more bearable, and the boss fights were made a lot more epic because of the music.No game-breaking bugs for me, and the game ran smoothly with no problems on a 6 year old gaming laptop. The only bugs I found at all were visual bugs when upgrading or selling equipment.Fun game, I recommend it if you like Metroidvanias, Souls-likes or games that are high quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

Was very slow pace, and couldn't keep me interested. I am either thinking to refund, or keep moving forward. I just don't know. This game might be decent later on, right now it feels like I should just breath through my mouth while trying not to get too invested. I did all the achievements for Salt and Sanctuary, and played through it a few times. I don't think this game can hold a candle to its flame.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: An Eldritch nightmare in Metroidvania form, Vigil: The Longest Night brings brutal combat, and papercraft animation to an elegant, but horrifying world. Vanillaware meets Bloodborne, it offers punishing difficulty and genuine horror to a 2D world, tying the experience together with a lengthy amount of content, and involved, intriguing story with plenty of twists and turns. The difficulty at its core can be adjusted to be more or less forgiving to properly tailor the experience to all who wish to delve further into its madness, and intrigued players should have no issue finding something to love here…...but that’s not all you want to hear is it?Indie Stop Recommendation: GO (Fantastic Atmosphere | Challenging, but fair)(VIDEO HAS A SPOILER WHEN RECALLING STORY ELEMENTS AT 11:40. If you wish to avoid any and all instances of spoilers, skip from 11:40 to 17:39 when watching)
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: - Salt&Sanctuary ref.- Blasphemous map- Bloodborne blood vial- 4 types of weapon but sadly there's no magic :(Sword, Two-handed axe, Bow, Twin daggers- Not much armor sets- You can apply your skill points to increase your attributes instead but the place is quite secret.- You can reset your skills and your attributes- Multiple endings- New game plusThis game is one of the best metroidvania games as it is a combination of multiple games in similar. And also the art-style cutscenes are drawn gorgeously. In this game, you can change a difficulty as you need. If you want to experience dark souls'level, I'll highly recommend HARD. Actually it's not that hard, so don't be disappointed. Unlike Salt&Sanctuary, this game has no magic at all, but there're arcane items which will channel spells instead. At the time of writing this review, the Wiki is quite futile. There're few useful information. Also on Youtube, there're not much helpful walkthroughs. Things you need to do are exploring, doing NPCs'quests and finding secret items by yourself. These're how we enjoy the game. Some say the quests are still buggy, but i beg a differ. All of the quests i got are doable and not buggy at all. I'm certain that i have done all, literally all quests the game has. So if you're looking for a good metroidvania game, i'll highly recommend this game. It's really worth playing with 10 dollars price and also definitely addictive. If you enjoy playing Blasphemous or Salt&Sanctuary, Vigil: The Longest Night is your love.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely fantastic. Only a few hours in, and I'm really feeling at home with the controls and overall mechanics of the games. The bosses look great and the general ambience is pretty cool! Congratulations for a job well done to the team that worked on this. A big shock was when after a certain event I was forced to advance to the "next chapter" so to speak, leaving behind some quests I'd rather have done. If I had any hint I was going to move on, I missed it thoroughly until it was too late. The one other small detail that would help me enjoy the game more would be a bit more SFX to feel like I'm truly walking and moving around the world. Right now it just feels like I'm floating around and not really interacting.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Vigil is a Salt and Sanctuary and Bloodborne inspired metroidvania that caught my eye one day and was pleasantly surprised with what i got. Vigil's graphic style is a mix of Salt and Sanctuary's dirty style, with Bloodborne's disgusting enemy design, most enemies are just plain creepy but add a wolf with spider eyes, and you got some new nightmare fuel. Everything runs smoothly too, in my 17 hours i have encountered 0 issues aside from minor clipping and hit detection issues, nothing long lasting or game breaking.Vigil's combat is essentially, a soulslike, Bloodborne to be exact with its emphasis on dodging rather then blocking. Vigil only has 4 types of weapons, axes, swords, daggers, and bows, but each have a skill tree you can put points into to unlock unique and pretty broken abilities for each weapon class. Unique weapons can have abilities tied to them as well, so there is a large amount to variety in playstyles to suit whatever your into. Another very Bloodborne thing, is the inclusion of magic items, these are separate from your build and are just equipable side pieces of damage or traversal.Vigil's story, quite honestly, is Bloodborne's. Not a carbon copy, but similar events transpire, with a similar emphasis on character side quests. What isnt Bloodborne however, is its crazy amount of side story stuff that require ALOT of digging to find. I wont get into spoilers, but your first playthrough and your 2nd or 3rd playthroughs are going to VERY different near the end assuming to actually attempt to find all the hidden lore dumps.Onto the one and only con i had with Vigil. Minor spoilers but im going to save you a massive headache or potential game quiter. Near the end of the game you need to climb a massive tree, but you need the last movement ability to get up it. This ability is tied to a seemingly side quest where you need to find all the paintings and get awarded an ocarina. This ocarina is brought to an alter where you must defeat the boss and only then do you acquire the ability to air dash. Keep in mind, i bought this game when the reviews were in the 100's, and videos or guides were very limited. This took me ages to find and even then, i ended up watching a guy you fell upon the solution. I dont mind cryptic BS in soulsborne games, but not when i need to actually find them to finish the game.Vigil is a fantastic find in a genre, i don't usually touch or even like very much. So to find one that i thoroughly enjoyed enough for 2 playthroughs, 100% my character, and actively sought out secrets and bosses, shows how good the game is. A must own for both metroidvania and soulsborne fans alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game very much. It's a perfect example of "the sum is greater than its parts", this game is a combination of metroidvania, souls-like, and RPG - neither of the elements are as strong as more pure examples of those genres, but together they form a very good experience. Originally I wasn't a fan of the visuals, which held me off from playing this game for so long, but once you start playing it looks better than the screenshots, it really gives me a Diablo 1 vibe in its mood, which is really nice. The combat starts pretty difficult, as you have access to very little, but as you gain experience and level up you gain skill points that you can invest in 5 skill trees (one for each weapon + 1 passive) and together with better gear and understanding of the combat system that difficulty goes away a lot over the time, you actually get very overpowered towards the end. The story isn't anything special, but I did enjoy playing through Leila's personal story. Do bear in mind, the true ending for this game requires a number of special steps, some of which are VERY missable if you don't know so if that kind of thing interests you do look up the guide at the wiki. I highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the game very long as I just bought it but it is pretty awesome so far. Everyone is comparing it to Salt & Sanctuary and, yes, it totally has that vibe. It's art style is superb, combat is fluid, graceful and spot on. Looking forward to playing this many, many more hours. It's a great Souls-like rogue lite.EDIT: 10 hours in and have to say this game has EASILY become my 2nd favorite rogue lite next to Salt & Sanctuary. I went into this game enjoying it but thinking, for some dumb reason, it was going to be "easier" than S&S. I was wrong. While the standard enemies can surprise you, they're still fodder for gold and experience. However, these bosses are pretty quick and tight. First two were fairly easy but I did notice it got a little harder on the 2nd one. Made it to the 3rd boss and, granted, you need to learn their move set, but he surprised me all right. Went and introduced my character to Jesus with the quickness. I'll definitely be putting more hours into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I can't recommend it to anyone who wants a polished experience. There are too many aspects of this game that just make it an unpleasant and frustrating experience. In the end, I beat the game out of pure spite, not because I enjoyed it. There are enemies that will attack with nearly no wind up and hit for half your health. This includes enemies that are off screen, so that you have no idea that there is even any danger. There are pits that will just kill you without providing any warning that they will do so.There are about 2-3 enemy types per area, and the areas are usually unnecessarily massive. The map feels extremely bloated, like it was created just so the creators could say "Our game is X times bigger than theirs!"The soundtrack is decent, but is often overpowering and doesn't mesh well with the environment. The quest interface is an absolute disaster. It doesn't update properly, often is hard to notice what has been updated. And maybe most annoyingly, once your quest log gets long enough, it doesn't indicate that you can scroll down and see the other quests you have.The game is rife with basic spelling mistakes, despite it being out for over a year at this point.The story... I really wanted to like it. I love Eldritch mythology and settings. But Vigil's story is an absolute mess. I still have no idea what a Vigilant even is, much less who the main character is. All I know is that you have a magic/gifted sister that you want to save, that's it. I don't even know if we are the older or younger sister. I had assumed we were the older sister, but later dialogue confused the two. Beyond that, very little is explained, and even less is explained well. And on top of all that, they try to introduce dimension hopping or time-travel (it's never fully explained what's happening), which further obfuscates the narrative. Opening the map resets traps in certain areas. This is especially horrendous in the mine level, when I opened my map to check I was going the right way, closed it, and a mine cart spawned on top of me, killing me instantly.If you want a good Metroidvania that has Eldritch elements, go for Ender Lilies. It is superior in nearly every way, and is a much more enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this if you're looking for an action rpg platformer.Not much to say other than I really like this game. Controls were tight and responsive. Platforming was difficult to master yet very rewarding especially for a collectible hound like myself. Combat was a bit easy even on the hardest difficulty. But encounters never got tiresome given how much you can change up your combat styles. There are 5 styles to focus on. Swords, Two handed heavies, dual wielded daggers, bows, and magic. Each style has unique active skills and combos to play with. And there were a ton of enemies that was a exciting to figure out and fight against. The same could be said as well for the bosses. Really cool visual and combat design.The look of the game is very much eldritch horror. The creatures are so bizarre and almost disturbing if you look close enough. And the music all throughout was a delight to listen to. I'm glad I got the deluxe version that has the artbook and soundtrack.Lastly the story is again very much eldritch horror. It was hard for me to get the overall mystery of everything. But that's mostly because I skimmed through all the lore bits and explanations. I only ever cared about finding new gear and playing around with the skills. But that's not to say the characters were not interesting. Their stories were fun to go through. I also liked I how there's a bit of choice here in how quests can play out.Overall this game was a treat and glad that it came up in my recommendations on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely fun Metroidvania type game ruined by a bad save system. The game doesn't allow you to save anywhere except save points - unless you use consumable items (I've found two in just under 3 hours). This by itself isn't all that bad, the problem is the game screen can't be scrolled down to see the distance of a fall. Coupled together this means that players are punished for exploring in an exploration based game - the punishment for trying to explore ? restarting at the last save. After about 4 or 5 restarts in the secret cave system area, I finally got tired of re-running the same thing over and over, and not being able to explore everywhere. With the current save system I can't recommend it.  If they implement anything allows saves "anytime" or something that will let the player know if an off-screen fall is deadly, I would say buy it. I mean, lets face it - what reason is there for a character not to be able to look down and gauge depth ?Update: a dev contacted me back in November, and I just noticed it. The dev let me know there IS a way look down (you can crouch and look down), which I didn't know. This game is back on the wish list =)

Really feel this game deserves some more love, and hope to see a sequel at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: STRONGLY ADVISE YOU MAKE MULTIPLE SAVES OVER SEVERAL SLOTS - so you can go back to an earlier save if needed.If you like completing games fully, be warned: There are multiple places in this game where passing a certain point will cause current active quests to fail and for you to be locked out of some content / endings, with no warning at all. In a game that can take 20+ hours, having your run spoiled because of a random invisible checkpoint isn't fun. It's just old school fun! If you grew up with a super nintendo or ps1 this will certainly jog some nostalgia!Could use some polish and spelling checks, but if you can see past that it's a decent -vania type of game.Pros- Big map for exploration       - Cool weapon combo's       - Amazing artstyle and backgrounds       - Doesn't want to make me throw my controller across the roomCons- Not being able to see NPC names on the map, nor their location makes it a bit tedious to finish quests          - sometimes (Maybe a diary with info on characters that you meet throughout the adventure would be         - nice)        - Traveling can be a little slow sometimes

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this simple.  This is one of my very favorite games of all time.  Great story - checkExtremely fun gameplay/battle mechanics - checkVery well designed upgrade systems and weapon/item/magic variety- checkMeaningful skill system with the ability to respec a nearly limitless number of times - checkMany extremely fun boss battles with interesting and challenging ways to defeat them - checkBeautiful, unique graphic design choices for player character, enemies, and environs- checkVery well optimized at 4k/60 FPS,at least for my i7 9750 w/16 GB Ram and GeForce 2070 Super card - checkI just can't think of any negatives currently!! Even better, the devs decided to create an enhanced version that all owners get for free ("Bounty of the Night") which includes even more monsters, new/better gear, new items, and much, much more!!!Anyway, I guess I'll give this a tentative thumbs up for now..... :o)Cheers,H
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since I discovered it by pure chance browsing my Steam queue, and I can say with all the happiness in the world that this game is one of the greatest metroidvanias I've ever played. And believe me, I've played TONS of them.While it's true that now that term is highly overused by everyone, I'm kinda sad that for the most part people tend to focus on the "metroid" part of the word. However, Vigil tends to lean towards the "vania" side, and I for one really like to see this more. With heavy inspiration from titles like Salt & Sanctuary (you take a look at this game monsters and you can only think "wow this would fit perfectly on the Ska Studios title!"), Vigil offers rewarding exploration, really good level design and tons and tons of equipment and items that will make you search every nook and cranny to find them all.Not every game is perfect and obviously this one is no exception, as I believe there are some places that could be improved a little bit. The quests, while being fun and enjoyable for the most part, tend to rely too much on exhausting NPC dialogues without any prompt telling you that you can keep talking to them for more info/finish their quest. Even if you have a Notes section in your menu, these are pretty vague and don't really offer much help in certain moments. Another aspect that could be added is the ability to play the game with the dpad, as it only allows you to move the main character with the analogue stick. A minor nitpick, but it's a sin playing a 2D game without being able to use the Dpad!Overall, Vigil will be exactly what you paid for: a solid game with really good combat, tons of equipment and weapons and some of the wildest-looking bosses you've ever seen in a while. If you are interested, make sure to grab it now, as the devs announced they will be making a collab with Salt & Sanctuary and add a couple of things from that title here. What else do you need?!
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: While it shares some similarities with the souls-like genre, I would categorize this more as a Metroidvania than what I consider the newer genre of Soulsvania.  It's not difficult for the sake of being difficult.  It doesn't punish you overly harsh for missing an input by a frame here or there (no instant death spikes everywhere).  It's a perfect level of challenge that you can choose to make more challenging at your own desire.  The save pointing is well placed, the skill trees are nice and you really have to pick a path and stick to it.  I think the only con is one where you can explore for a bit and there are so many branching routes that it becomes unclear which way is the direction you want to go.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful metroidvania with a strong Bloodborne aesthetic and a surprisingly solid combat system, that's unfortunately brought down by mediocre and/or piss-easy bosses and enemies, a completely ignorable story, and poor map design. It's fine if you want a more casual experience or you adore the way it looks (and it looks  pretty, genuine props to the artists and environment designers), but it's definitely a pass if you want something with an engaging story/lore or if you want a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of metroidvanias and am absolutely flabberghasted at how this is getting so much positive praise. Everything about it from the graphics, the movement, the hitboxes, the enemy design, the equipment, weapon skills, leveling, the save system, bosses... everything is amateurish and poorly done. The moment-to-moment gameplay experience is pure frustration, and all the things I love about the metroidvania genre that games like Environmental Station Alpha, Hollow Knight, Rabi Ribi, and Salt and Sanctuary are nowhere to be found here. That last one is weird because it's clearly taking influence from Salt and Sanctuary to the point of looking like a rip-off, but it ignores everything that game does well.No idea how this game is getting such good buzz in the metroidvania community, because it's among the worst metroidvanias to ever be released.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent Metroidvania with a Soulslike flair.  It's obvious how much love was poured into this game; from the lore to the character and monster designs.  It's eldritch horror themes do not disappoint, delivering a meaningful story and ending, as long as you are willing to do some critical thinking.  Enjoyed my time with the game and will be a definite replay in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches the itch for a good metroidvania. The story is a bit convoluted and at times completely opaque, but the gameplay more than makes up for it. I had fun with it until the very end. Vigil: the Longest Night is also a pretty tame experience in terms of difficulty, so if you're expecting something challenging, you might want to start straight in the highest difficulty setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Super great little game! I'm not one for Metroidvania games, so Vigil isn't normally something I'd go out of my way to play. A friend recommended it, so I gave it a try. Fell in love in the first few minutes.The soundtrack is fantastic! Especially when you're in the forested areas or in a boss fight. Really gets the blood pumping. Even in areas where the BGM lulls, the atmosphere it creates is truly astounding. Probably my favorite aspect of the game, overall.The art! OH, THE ART! This game is beautiful! There really aren't many games like it (Salt and Sanctuary comes to mind). It's brooding and horrific most of the time, and really sells the mood the game is going for.The gameplay is great, too! While the tags are true, Vigil is probably one of the easier games in the genre. The four weapon skill trees each have tools to handle the same scenario in different ways, so you don't NEED to use any more than a single type of weapon if you don't want to. I stuck with dual blades and the bow for my first playthrough, and got pretty good with the dual blades' counter skill. With it, you can trigger a counter, making you invulnerable for the split-second duration of the ability, and do a huge burst of damage. If you continuously tap a direction after the first slash, you can keep the counter going, making you invincible until you're stamina runs out. I've used this move to kill nearly every boss in the game effortlessly.Also, throwables are absolutely busted. I've killed most of the bosses in seconds with throwables. They really aren't balanced at all, compared to the rest of the game. Hahahahah!Conversely, magic is not so great. There are a few neat things you can do with it, but the damage and flexibility just isn't there. And there aren't enough gear sets that make a sizable enough difference to justify going all-in on magic. The spells aren't great, either. Mana doesn't have a consumable to recover it, and all spells have some kind of cooldown, so you can't spam any of them, save for a few weaker ones. Compare that to thowables or just stacking the Attack stat with any of the four weapon archetypes, and magic just feels super useless.Honestly, as long as you're leveling up your character and making an effort to use your weapons and their skills to the fullest, you'll do great. So if difficulty is a concern, I can assure you it's really not so bad. This is coming from someone who doesn't handle tough games very well. It's a great game! It does have a few hiccups, though. The story isn't great. It's there, but it's not particularly well-written. There's a ton of really neat Lovecraftian Old God stuff going on, but the translations to English are so awful, it's difficult to understand what little is actually communicated to the player. So if story is your primary focus, you might want to pass on Vigil.Also, the game WILL crash on you from time-to-time, so be sure to save whenever you get to a save point! It doesn't happen a lot (maybe four times in total for me over 75 hours), but it will happen. It occurred often enough to change how I played the game and how often I saved.All in all, I highly recommend Vigil: The Longest Night! The art, soundtrack, and gameplay are all wonderful! The story leaves a lot to be desired, and the translations are ROUGH, but I don't feel they take enough away from the overall package to hurt my opinion of Vigil. Give it a try!
