_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRArt and music: 10/10Story: 6/10Combat: 10/10A near perfect hidden gem that deserves my first ever review.What makes this game great, you wonder?First of all the artstyle is absolutely beautiful and scary at the same time. You can definetly see that it is heavily inspired by the SoulsBorne series, especially Bloodborne. Do I think this is a bad thing? No. It most certainly gave its own twist to it which turned out to be awesome. Enemy and boss design is spot on, ignoring the generic bat, slime and skeleton enemies. The areas are also beautifully done. Scary and gloomy providing the player a sense of dread and loneliness. Absolutely perfect. Oh and did I mention that pretty much all of the soundtracks are absolute BANGERS? A perfect 10/10 in the artsyle department.So what about combat? The bread and butter of this game?In short, 10/10. Combat feels smooth and controls are responsive. The only thing that I could describe as bad, is the fact you cannot action queue weapon switching for a bow to melee combo for example. Besides that, perfect.The fact they limited the player to 4 weapon classes is not a bad thing in my opinion either. There are plenty of weapons to choose from all with pros and cons, except for one weapon but more on that later.Magic is fun to use, using a similar style to Bloodborne where spells are items in your hotbar for easy spell swapping, not requiring you to go back to a checkpoint to equip different spells. I do wish they gave magic a specific skill tree though.Next, enemies have clear audio and/or visual cues for most attacks, which is a major thing that often is overlooked in these type of games. Not much else to say than again, a perfect score.But I did say  perfect game. So what are some of the negative things I found?First of all, the story. This is one of the drawbacks of the game sadly. The story is not that innovative when compared to other games that use the "Soulslike" style of story telling and I'd go as far as to call it somewhat generic. But to give credit where credit is due, the way the story is told is good. Pieces of the story are not as hidden as in similar games but do require you to go out of your way to find them. There are multiple endings which I think is neat and a good choice when you have a game where new game+ is available. All in all, not bad and deserving of a 6/10 for story.Next, leveling is ridiculously fast. You'll have more skill points than you know what to do with by the time you are halfway through the game. Which is not inherently a bad thing BUT the skill trees are actually not that big. The skill trees have plenty of good skills to pick from but the fact that you level up so fast kind of trivializes the desicion making.And lastly, I mentioned a weapon earlier that has no pros and cons because of the fact it has only pros. There is a certain weapon in the game that completely breaks the game. Yeah. It is bought from a store for a ludicrous amount of gold, and I can certainly tell it is not intended to be bought on your first new game cycle. But it is 100% possible to do so. I'd rather have it appear in the store only after you completed your first playthrough.This concludes my first ever review for a game that truly deserves it. Go buy it right now!

_childDocuments_.review: Its not easy to describe this game and I am not good at writing reviews to begin with so here we go.Imagine an eldrichvania with multiple routes you can take which creates replayability for subsequent playthroughs. Its a gem that needs polishing yes, but its well worth it. Combat feels good, progression system is imo well designed and each level makes you feel stronger. The area layouts and connectivity are very well done. There's loads of secondary areas that are not necessary to progress the main story. My only concern is a few bugs here and there regarding the xbox controlls but they stated its been worked on.So yeah if you are not sure, just wait for the few minor bugs to be fixed and give it a try. I was sceptical and now I don't want to stop playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rock solid metroidvania soulslike in the vein of Salt and Sanctuary. Where it differs from S&S is that this one focuses more on the metroidvania game play while keeping the Dark Souls grim and grittiness mostly aesthetic, with the game play feeling closer to Bloodstained. While there is no shortage of great metroidvanias, this is a solid entry and well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game, the music is captivating, the gameplay is incredible and it really supports different playstyles, the trinkets might be a bit too overpowered, but I love them nonetheless. I really love the quests that encourage you to explore more areas, which you can keep track of with the implemented notes, the secret chests that challenges you to proper mind-games and the platforming, and the hunt for secret mini-bosses that are only hinted at through environmental clues. some of the quests that you do also has an effect on how the story will play out. The skill-tree makes for interesting gameplay as well. We got unique boss mechanics, optional bosses and everything looks great visually. You are also presented with comedic fashion, though it is a bit sad that you can't use the looks of one item and the stats of another, like some other games.If I had to complain about 1 thing, it would be the order in which you loot items, some early-game items you can loot are so strong that they remain equipped the entire early-game, then you change items like 1 or 2 times depending on which location you choose to go first, and when you can finally afford the shop's best weapon, you are also eligible to loot the game's strongest sword. The OP early weapon is a sword, the shop weapon is a sword, the late game boss weapon is a sword, that was a poor decision, because it discourages the use of other weapon types. The enchanting is very confusing too.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, I bought it on release when it came up, It felt a little rough around the edges but the developing team has done an amazing job fixing bugs and optimizing the game as well as adding new content.If you like gritty dark fantasy games within the metroidvania genre you will love this item. Imagine Castlevania meets Bloodborne for a somewhat accurate comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to pick a critique, it would be the difficulty; the game gets rather easy on the medium difficulty but moving over to hard can be pretty frustrating due to the save points being quite few and far between. The game does have a limited resource you can use to manually save anywhere, but since you don't know how rare they are you end up hoarding them and almost always use them only after losing a significant amount of progress due to not wanting to repeat the loss.Otherwise this is a good metroidvania with a good amount of content. Storytelling and world building are very souls-esque, where the game will drop bits and pieces of lore and it's the players job to string it all together. While the story and world are nothing revolutionary, they are solid and interesting. Exploration is rewarding. Combat is fluent and works well. Strong 8/10 in my books.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigil The Longest Night is yet another Souls (or Salts and Sanctuary in this case) inspired metroidvania styled 2D action platformer with some RPG mechanics, and for the most part the game is fine. The boss battles were easily the highlight of the game for me, and they are what kept me playing through the game. The bosses are well-designed with a good variety and honestly I didn't dislike any of them.Another thing that I really enjoyed about the game was the art style, and at times the game can look downright beautiful.  Now I do have few gripes with this game. Firstly I didn't find the game's story to be very captivating since it's mainly told via clunky dialogue spouted by uninteresting NPCs.Secondly I didn't find the RPG mechanics to be very satisfying. The game has a very basic skill tree and I had unlocked everything I wanted after just couple of hours playing .I also experienced few technical issues. I had to play the game in a windowed mode since for whatever reason the UI didn't scale properly in full screen mode. Also the automap didn't always work.I was able to reach an ending after 7 hours playing, now I'm pretty sure that wasn't the true ending but I don't think I'm motivated enough to comb through the game for things that I missed.  Overall I'd say this game is passable with few highlights and if you are interested in games like these then it isn't by any means the worst thing you can buy. However I'm not sure if I'd be willing to recommend the game at its current price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 2D platformer that is quite similar to Salt & Sanctuary, if you're familiar. It sort of a cross between a 2D Metroidvania and Dark Souls, but with only a couple of weapon types. It has a quiet and spooky atmosphere, plenty of skills to develop, and fun combat. _childDocuments_.review: Vigil: The Longest Night is a good game, which might have been great if not for several shortcomings which only reveal themselves after you're about 15% in. I'd give it 6/10.The prologue is just about perfect, the problems start afterwards.The positive:- beautiful background art- creative (but inconsistent) monster design- good music- the right "I need to discover everything"-feeling for metroidvania addicts like myself- surprisingly large and complex map- basic controls (played with controller) are very responsive and work well- okayish story- surprisingly long gameplayThe negative:- the boss fights are uninventive and most of them far too easy. I don't need exceptionally difficult fights (nor am I very skilled), but I like ones where I have to be (or at least feel) clever and creative. I beat 80% of the bosses on the first try with always the same technique: stay as far away from them as possible and spam the Flaming Magpie skill ...- the controls for advanced fighting techniques are unintuitive and not well taught by the game; consequently I used almost none of them; the game neither encourages nor teaches you to get better, you can rely on timing and buffed up standard and heavy attacks; same goes for newly acquired skills; apart from double jump and air jump the controls are terrible (ground dash is almost unusable); coming from Nioh 2 with its absolutely perfect yet complex controls that was quite a letdown; I think the developers should have taken a close look how controls work on top metroidvania games like Ori or Hollow Knight and should rather have copied than tried to do their own thing- you can block with the sword but I never learned how, when or why; the attack boxes of enemies are not clearly defined, using the buffed up heavy sword attack (swirling forwards) proofed much more effective than any blocking attempt;- there's no need to switch weapons; the maps are never really designed for bow fighting; so you use your bow mostly short range and until you level up your bow to max that's a poor fighting choice (I'm sure many other players who play differently disagree)- most acquired skills so typical for metroid games are rarely used and thus don't feel essential to the game (wind, fire, ...); if you compare it to the mastery of the Ori games or Hollow Knight or Guacamelee! you feel there's a lot of wasted potential to make character progress more rewarding- while the music is very well done a lot of the sound effects are repetitive and poorly done; especially in the mines the walking sound doesn't fit (sounds like walking on metal grates in a sewer);- you can fail quests without the game giving any hint or warning; for example fight two bosses after another without going to a special place and talking to a person first, fails a quest; that's annoying; I like to do 100% but I don't replay a rather long game just because I have to do stuff in a special order which isn't communicated to me at all; - the dialog system is terrible; you trigger it by accident all the time, you cannot cancel a conversation and you never know if a person has more to say or not; sometimes you first get dialog you already know but still have to talk to the same person again right away to get to the important new part;- you cannot use items from the inventory but have to add them to your quick items first; because of that limitation there's a lot of configuring stuff which isn't fun, also you're prone to accidentally use rare items (like custom save points) when you don't want to; so if you copy from Dark Souls do it all the way ...I actually could go on, but that would give the wrong impression, because I *did* enjoy the game nonetheless; completing the map and finding most of the secrets was fun and engaging, but I won't come back for a second run.

_childDocuments_.review: The game features a souls-like combat system with slow, deliberate movements and lethal opponents that can kill you with just a few hits. However, unlike in most souls games, dying in this game means you get a Game Over screen instead of dropping your souls/experience. This means that on death you will lose all progress since the last save point, including:To me, part of the point of souls like combat is that death is not the end, merely a setback. However, it doesn't force you to do the same things over and over again, like collecting all the items and opening all the treasures. That is a key component of what makes lethal combat work.It's true that this game also takes a lot of cues from the Metroidvania genre. It's also true that "Game Over" screens are pretty normal in Metroidvania games. However, in that genre, you typically have a larger health pool while healing between save points is hard/expensive. Death usually doesn't come by surprise. In souls like games, however, you can easily get killed by being careless which means that death is a common occurrence and often unpredictable.Other Metroidvania aspects in the game are also quite troublesome. For example, the game has very lethal fall damage. The difference in height between taking a bit of damage and dying from a fall is quite small. This is coupled with the fact that traversing is often about platforming and you will be dropping down quite often. The camera also positions the player on the lower part of the screen, so I often found myself crouching to get the camera lower to see where it's safe to drop.Maps are also another thing that is very important to me in Metroidvania games. These types of games tend to feature quite a bit of backtracking to new reach places with newly acquired movement upgrades. However, the map in this game is quite subpar. There are a lot of "inside" areas in the game, but the map only displays the outside areas. In addition to this, the map doesn't make a good distinction between different "screens", so the map is less helpful than it could be. Speaking of backtracking, that game also has an unexpected point of no return at the third boss, which makes it possible to miss secrets that can be found before it.Lastly, the first spell you obtain in this game is a very weird gameplay decision. It's a spell that holds the opponent in place for a few seconds while doing a negligible amount of damage. The cooldown of the spell is also only a bit longer than its duration so you can use it almost repeatedly. This trivializes quite a lot of enemies outside bosses at least as far as I got in the game.Essentially, it feels like the game tries to mix both souls like and Metroidvania genres without really understanding what makes those genres work, so you find all these small weird fundamental game design decisions that feel out of place. It's also worth mentioning that at the time of writing, there are quite a few errors in the English translation and even some incorrect descriptions. It wasn't a major issue for me, but some might find that jarring on top of everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit regarding developer reply: The item in question does not resolve my issue with the game, as it is rare, consumable, and simply creates a new save point. There are few scenarios where this would be preferable to a standard Souls-like death system unless the player already has foreknowledge of the game and knows the best locations to create save points. In any case, it does not stop full progress loss from that point onward, so it's a band-aid solution at best and there are certainly no game elements designed around it.I desperately wanted to give this a higher rating, because it does so much stuff right, but I can't bring myself to do it because of one enormous issue: you straight-up lose progress on death. Not "lose exp" or "lose items", but you lose every step you've taken since the last save point. That sort of thing just doesn't jive with the Souls-like game structure this game has going on. It's not enjoyable to have to try to remember to retrace your steps and pick up a certain item and retool your equipment and reallocate your skill points because you happened to have died. There's absolutely no reason why this game could not and does not use the now-standard death mechanics of Souls-likes when it has no issue using every other mechanic from the sub-genre. I can't find myself wanting to put any more time into a game in this style when you have a chance to lose every single button press if you run into a boss after 15 minutes and don't one-shot it. If this were to ever change, I would gladly switch the rating back to a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, I don't post reviews. However, I was so excited for this game's release that I had to. First and foremost there is both good and bad about this game. But there is no way for me to give it a "meh" rating. I am giving it a No at the moment due to the game breaking bugs that I found; which I have listed later. However, I am absolutely willing to change my review once some changes are made.Let's start off with the bugs that I found within the first hour of playing.1. Broken Hitbox/Controls when climbing onto second platform where rats are in first level. Must hold up at right time to actually grab ledge. Tutorial later mentions the controls as jump and pushing the control stick (toward) the ledge which does not work for this specific ledge.2. OBS doesn't recognize the game window for recording/streaming. The window is labeled as calculator; not sure if this is related... (my calculator isn't actually open.) Very confusing. Work around fix was to capture whatever window is full screen.3. **Edit** Developer has responded about this bug. Their response below has the fix.4. Menu remains open and character is able to move. After moving for a bit, the menu closes as normal. Menu actions can be performed while moving. Can get confusing if you are wanting to play and accidentally go into inventory.5. Death animation doesn't always play when health at 0.6. **Edit** Developer has responded about this bug. Their response below has the fix.7. Weapon auto un-equips when changing some settings in game.Atmosphere, music, game play, unique stamina system, rpg elements/character progression, difficulty, and artistic choice are all very good.Developer responds with suggestions and bug fixes.Very buggy upon initial release.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true old school Metroidvania with a focus on exploration. Don’t buy this game if you like incredibly hard gameplay and/or puzzles. This is the game for you if you like to explore a beautiful world, get into some nice combat and upgrade your weapons and equipment. If you like getting your teeth kicked down your throat and rage-quitting a game, look elsewhere.  The combat is fun, but not unfair - you most likely won’t have to “git gud”, although there are some tricky fights.  I dislike puzzles in Metroidvanias (if I can’t figure it out within a minute or two, I’m on YouTube), and this one has zero, so it’s a big plus in my book.  I re-played Harmony of Dissonance after this and was surprised at how similar the difficulty was between the two games. If anything, the combat is better in Vigil. It’s more challenging and more varied.

_childDocuments_.review: This game falls somewhere between Salt and Sanctuary and Ender Lillies. It's got a few more RPG elements than the later and lest customization than the former. The art is solid, the boss fights look great and the controls are slick. I'm not far enough to say if the bosses get significantly difficult but the first two weren't too bad. I'd recommend for fans who like metroidvania's that offer a variety of combat play styles. Additionally it appears the developers have addressed complaints raised by the community early on, which is always nice to see.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots to explore with beautiful graphics, not much of a challenge though.There's a lot to like about this game. It's got plenty of weapons, lots of story, plenty of items, optional and hidden things everywhere. Added to this are large skill trees and numerous ways to equip your character, as well as upgrade that equipment.Of course, several of the "lots" belong to the negatives as well. First most is the lack of challenge. The enemies are fairly dumb and one or two techniques will get you through most of the game, even after switching to hard mode. Most of the techniques I simply never needed, not even in the boss fights. Only the second last boss caused me some grief.Secondly, the upgrades are all kind of lack lustre. The skill trees are nice, but the weapon upgrades don't make much of a difference -- at least not from looking at the stats increases. Most of the items found in the game are pointless as well, rarely being better than what you have before. I liked that there is a lot of mystery, lots of story, with secret places and things to find. Unfortunately, the majority of quest items you find don't do anything, like they don't belong to a quest at all. Though I did like finding the decorations for my house, that felt like I accomplished something.The game has so much potential, and it's worthwhile playing for that potential. It's unfortunate though, because it could have been a great game, but fails in several areas. It's still worth a play, but will leave you wanting something more nuanced and challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigil: The Longest Night wears its inspiration sources on its sleeve. Developers will straight up tell you that the game was made as a deliberate homage to Salt & Sanctuary and the Castlevania series. This, of course, brings in “inspiration by proxy” into the mix with Salt & Sanctuary being a love letter to the Dark Souls series. It might be a fun exercise to dissect the game like this. Visual motif, story progression pace and tone, from Bloodborne. Tempo and choreography of the combat, from Dark Souls. Character design inspiration, from Salt & Sanctuary. And that upbeat background music piece that is played in the graveyard location sounds like an outtake from Symphony of the Night.But as entertaining as this dissection would be, I'd like to instead admire the fact, that Vigil is bigger than a sum of its parts. A small Taiwanese indie developer managed to pull off a great feat. The game is not just a wink to the fans of the inspiration sources, no: it deserves its place among and maybe someday it'll be regarded as such.It all starts inconspicuous and restrained without a hint of future depth. The Protagonist is not customizable, you're just simply dropped off at the start of the game. You play as Leila, a recent graduate of a mysterious order called The Vigil, who is returning to her hometown after being away training to become the member of the order. You are on the outskirts of a settlement in the woods. Just a few steps away are some undead enemies hungry for your blood.Two types of attack, danger evading dodge-rolls, stamina bar, enemies respawning after their death — similarities are unmistakable. But if you don't know them, these basics are easy to grasp. Overall difficulty is smoothed out by some quality-of-life improvements. You can teleport between local save points. Manual save is possible too with special items that are available in abundance. Active quests are tracked in a special UI. That doesn't mean that they point you to a specific place on a world map with a marker or any such help. The hints can be pretty obtuse, but  some memory aid, at least, is a welcome thing for sure.There's also a world map that fills automatically as you progress through the world. Not having it would be one step too far, considering that some traversal back and forth and revisiting old areas is critical, and you can't rely on landmarks being visible from afar. It won't lay all the secrets bare in front of you. It will be very stingy with revealing new portions of the world. Parts of it will seem like it is trying to play a trick on you. It doesn't help that there are separate underground and surface maps, and both are huge. It is vague supplement to your memories of traversing the game's world.It's not foolproof and that's by design: Vigil holds some of its secrets close to the chest. There's no shortage of things you might miss: bosses, quest lines, whole areas are completely optional. The journey is, of course, non-linear and the game's world will change in response to your actions. Piecing together what is really happening is a task in and of itself. The game's characters will mention centuries old historic events and phenomena that are a complete mystery to you. Picking up on subtle clues about the world and cross-referencing them between conversations with different characters makes for quite a challenging detective mini-game. The main story is a lot easier to decipher. That is not to say it is straightforward. The story would involve time travel, NPCs deliberately lying to you and a fair share of symbolism. At the end of the day, if you just press on you'll get to the end of it.The journey towards the end is not a cakewalk, but it is not riddled with insurmountable obstacles either and there's fun to be had along the way. Paradoxically the journey feels bigger than it actually is. When you zoom out all the way it looks like the map is enormous, but in practice it'll be a fairly compact experience. The path you'll make through the world is largely shaped by story bits and by unlocking traversal abilities. Those are the fairly standard double jump, slide and dash (plus an optional air dash). You unlock them as rewards for beating certain bosses and not all of them are mandatory, true to the spirit of a genre focused on exploration and uncovering secrets.And there's a lot to unravel if you're willing to go through with it, multiple endings included. A true gem. It wouldn't be a stretch for Vigil to be put on the same shelf as all the games that inspired it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game, definitely worth its full price. Music is generally atmospheric (odd to have rock music in the forest area though). Enemy variety being glaring, seeing the same type of monsters showing up in multiple areas becomes noticeable esp. if you have to trek through the massive forested areas. _childDocuments_.review: This is a very good metroidvania with a few minor issues that make it far from perfect. Overall, the map, visuals, music, and atmosphere are all there. And the combat system is also really interesting. However, this game still suffers from a lack of polish. The combat feels clunky at times, in a way similar to the old FromSoft souls games like DS1. A lot of my frustration with this game came from janky hitboxes, the platforming being pretty hit or miss, inputs not registering at times, and the game overall not feeling super responsive to me. Still, I think it's a game worth playing. I definitely had a lot of fun with it, but it's not without its frustrations.

_childDocuments_.review: We need a moratorium on developers trying to mix Dark Souls with Metroidvainia until we can figure out what is going on in their heads.Positives:-Good art direction. Seems this is the only area where they put any serious effort-Story is coherent and modestly interesting-You can look up or down by holding the appropriate direction buttonNegatives:-Stamina system is frankly bunk. Attacking should not cost nearly as much stamina as it does. Nothing like having a boss cornered but you have to sit there and rest instead of wailing away at him. All it does is extend boss battles artificially. "But that's how it is in Souls!" Hey nobody stuck a gun to the developers' head and forced them to do this.-The dash mechanic is all you need to know that the developers have never — NEVER — played a 2D game before. As soon as you get the dash your ability to fight bosses gets hampered immensely because you lose precise movement. Have fun blowing sure wins because you dashed into the boss' attack instead of inching into/out of engagement range. "But then how will you dash?" There are 10/11 buttons on the Xbox controller (which the game considers the default controller) but only 8/9 (if you count select) are used. WHY ARE YOU NOT USING THE OTHER TWO. Have a shoulder button reserved so that you can hold it down to dash. Double-tapping a direction is NOT HOW ANY VAINIA DASH WORKS.-I don't know what poise is and I've kinda accepted that the game just won't tell me what it is.-Given the expenses that go into upgrading weapons, it's pointless to use anything other than a sword and maybe a bow if you need to pick someone off. Making use of secondary/alternate weapons has always been a tough nut to crack for Vainias and this game comes no closer to figuring it out.-This game is hell-bent on forcing you to use dodge because enemy hitboxes are a mile wide and three miles tall. "But you're supposed to roll through enemies, not jump over them! This is a Dark Souls-like!" IF YOU WANT TO MAKE DARK SOULS, JUST MAKE DARK SOULS. STAY OUT OF 2D.-Monsters can be occluded by the foreground. Some of this is mitigated by having a (not really noticeable) spotlight around them, but other times a monster will be completely obscured because they're in a room you haven't entered, and then you get blitzed or stumble into a trap because ♥♥♥♥ you, that's why.-If the boss is out of vision you may be completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by some across-the-room attack they do. You'd see the telegraph if you could see them, but because they dashed to the other side of the room you have to sit there and pray they don't snipe you. "That's how it works in Dark Souls!" Dark Souls is a 3D game where you can control the camera and see the boss at all times, so you can look for telegraphs and ♥♥♥♥. You can't zoom out or get a little box that shows what the boss is doing on the other side of the screen. 2D games solved this problem a long time ago and here these devs are reinventing the wheel and then breaking it.Play Bloodstained or Hollow Knight instead. ♥♥♥♥, even Ori and (spit) Blasphemous are more competent, frankly.

_childDocuments_.review: I was into it for the first 4 hours or so, but the game has a lot of confusing design in it: -Elemental resistances for RARE elemental effects -throwing DOZENS of duplicate, worthless rings at you (Often as "secrets") -MULTIPLICATIVE STAT SCALING (stats multiplying by eachother rather than by a base) -Skills that have no apparent use. (Why "Kill nearby low health enemies" rather than just hit them once more?) -The staff/axe that shoots lasers demolishes EVERYTHING. Through walls. -A full detailed map and a quest tracker, and I still didn't know where I was going or what I was doing most of the time.The game is interesting and playable with some good visual design, but deeply flawed.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: The game is fun combat is fun, you can combo use skill which actually is fun to pull off and game  have plenty of fun ways to deal with enemy ,Agile daggers , heavy hitting axe , parry and all around good weapon Sword and range bow which has surprisingly good amount of decent skills and is a viable weapon for the game Music is nice some tracks are very catchy , background has good dark yet distinct color palette which changes according to the region , exploring these vast areas is distinct and fun to explore and find stuff Cons:The biggest con and something which actively frustrates me as player and probably the dumbest decision holding this game back is the implementation of death  . On death i go back to last saved position , so any exploration or hidden passage or items i collected are reset to that save point . and now i have to do all that tracking of my path , deal with all the same enemies remember all my path so i don't miss the items i collected . To remedy this they provide an in game item which create manual save point , its limited and can be discovered or dropped but its is not purchasable so rare item. Which highlights the issue , This mechanic has made me quit playing because there is no more fun in exploration because i will have to play the same section over and track my path and get the items again since the last save which is so stupid and makes the game cumbersome to play
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: A really beautiful game that shouldn't be missed by anyone remotely interested in Metroidvania gamesI couldn't believe what this really small team accomplished after the end game credits rolled. -gorgeous graphics-customizable character with weapons, clothing (armor types), even haircut-very satisfying and great movesets, cleaning each area of enemies never gets old.-more weapons, armor, spells, customisation option than you will ever need just to handcraft the game to your own playstyle-tons and tons of NPC-s to talk to, pursue side quests, multiple paths for different quest endings, the game is alive, not as much of a lonesome, solitary journey like many games are which take some inspiration in their art design from Souls games-multiple endings (easy to unlock all of them in one playthrough) but these games are more about the journey itself than the destination.It was an awesome journey. Buy it. It's among the better Metroidvania games out there. Even if it's technically made by an indie team, it's a high quality, nicely polished product, and an awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pleasant surprise. A great metroidvania with plenty of unique well thought out mechanics; enemy variety; fantastic music; and an interesting, compelling story. Was a bit buggy at launch but most of the problems have been fixed at the time of writing this. I love the combat and exploration. The world is strange and unique and I enjoyed searching its every nook and cranny for hidden secrets. The blend of 2D and 3d doesnt' always look great, but it manages to pull off the atmoshpere well enough that it doesn't really bother me. Only a couple of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. One is the translation, which is not terribly bad most of the time but often enough you'll see a broken sentence and such. Also, the game suffers a bit from the Symphony of the Night problem where it is a bit on the easy side, as due to the amount of freedom you can easily overlevel, get some extremely powerful items too early, and turn your playthrough into a cakewalk.

_childDocuments_.review: Another one that gets it. The gameplay of vigil will be very simmilar to anyone who has played blasphemous, but the aesthetic is far more inspired by the likes of the soulsbourne series. We are treated to another brilliant metroidvania world, full of secrets and challenges.What makes Vigil unique in the crowd, at least from titles I'm familliar with, is how richly populated it is, and how engaged it's story is, with a plethera of npc quests that intersect, and a real sense of drama (I mean tension and motivations, not melodrama).Striking a balance between overwhelming and sparse, the variety in combat is satisfyingly diverse, but you should understand the jist without much headscratching.Having played on  ormal mode (theres easy, normal, and hard) I will say it's not as challenging as it's peers (darksouls, blasphemous, hollow knight, etc.), with generous timing for dodges and parries, sizable weapon hitboxes for attacks, and a comfortable amounts of healing, I can safely say it's quite accessible for the niche it occupies, so if you can't manage the difficulty of games like blasphemous or hollow knight, this can be a nice way to still get that kind of experience, while not being barred by difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is  good for being the first game from the devs.We're looking at a solid, narrative-driven metroidvania with a tint of souls-like: exploration takes care of leveling up, unlocking character skills, acquiring items and gear and diving into the story and world setting. I already finished it and I highly doubt that I cleared all of the content.What makes it unique is that you not only explore the game map, but also a cast of characters through a plethora of obscure souls-like NPC questlines. Vigil doesn't hold your hand on that and you  miss them if you don't pay attention... BUT*This game doesn't have a punitive auto-save feature, you're free to feel safe by saving when you feel like you're going to mess up somewhere. Saving frequently utterly dissolves making mistakes in this game, its up to you if you care about it or not and if you want to use it like that or not. **Cons:- This game has some features that feel too simplistic, its like a middle ground where you can't tell if some features needed to be in the game at all or if they just need more development in order to become important. The skill trees are really fun but really short, you clear them too quickly and the enchantment system doesn't feel relevant unless its for specific things, like maxing out arcane stat or building an unarmed style gameplay (and both come from the same forge item)-it feels like there was an attempt to make a difficult combat approach, but this game isn't hard at all. I don't mind it, in fact I like it! But its like the verticality of metroidvania action counters most of the challenge in battles. You'll feel you're playing two different games if you choose to jump or avoid jumping during combat encounters.**Pros:- I'm not even going to talk about the soundtrack.- An eerie, dark and melodic story that keeps you on the edge of your seat.- The gameplay is fun! It feels indeed too simple but it gives you total freedom in it, go ahead and make your own little style the way you want to with no setbacks. 10/10 comfort points.- The devs really look like they care, the updates and patches may offset negative points. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of reviews proclaiming Vigil to be too easy. Either those players are masochists, or I'm losing my edge.Either way, I don't expect an experienced veteran of 2d Metroidvania games to die three times on the tutorial boss. Maybe I'm having a very  day, but I didn't have any particular fun in the 15 minutes of playing Vigil leading up to that.Frankly, the entire game just feels a bit... Stilted and wooden. The boss, at least, seemed unrelenting in his attacks and his timing, meanwhile I couldn't cancel out of attacks, so if I had committed to an swing and the boss decided he wanted to attack me, I just had to eat the hit. It shouldn't take a player who's played Metroidvanias and other 2d side-scrollers nine healing potions per attempt and three attempts to kill the first boss on normal mode, let alone to  to do so.If the controls were smoother, if the AI was less relentless, if their attacks were better-telegraphed in advanced or if I could cancel out of attacks to dodge, maybe things would have gone more smoothly, but as it is I'm not having any fun, and am considering refunding the game and going back to play 30XX or something.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; This game is really really addicting to play. The gameplay is super fun for me and I enjoy how the combat feels. The inputs are responsive and the fluidity give me Dragon's Dogma vibes if it were 2D. Even if you can grind levels and get strong really quickly, it's a rewarding experience and you'll have fun doing it. The only bug I've experienced so far is that my character position on the map is not accurate at all. In the map view, the positioning is about 20-30 feet ABOVE where I actually am in-game, so navigating is reallllllllly difficult because ONLY the parts that my character positioning touch ON THE MAP and NOT in-game are revealed. This can make trying to find certain areas VERY difficult unless you just try to memorize the different paths (which at this point I have because I play this game so much). It's not a game breaking bug, but still frustrating since it's a Metroidvania. ASIDE from that, the game is fantastic. The music is a great mix of what you would expect from a good Castlevania game and rock music. Walking into the Depression Forest for the first time, I didn't know i was walking into my favorite song of the game. It's a banger. The bosses were a decent challenge and the art for them is clean and creepy (Lovecraftian feels). Story is pretty good with multiple endings depending on what quests you do/don't do and who you meet. Anyway, I don't usually review games, but uhhhh play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome game. Sure, it has a few kinks in it that could be improved, but overall, it's a game you won't regret buying. I haven't played too many Metroidvania games, and am more of a Soulsborne fan, but when I saw this game it looked like it would be a nice mash up between the two genres and enticed me. No regrets.The combat is fluid, and unforgiving at times, which I appreciate a lot. You can't just go at something with a head full of steam and expect to come out on top. At first I wasn't a big fan of the skill tree system, and still not quite sure how I feel about it. It seemed like you were kind of forced into one weapon type unless you were ok with being weaker with a hybrid build, but I'm not a min-maxer either.Only real negative thing I can say about the game is the inventory management is not optimal. There's no way to sort your items, and some items you just can't get out of your inventory even if you have no further use for them (such as keys). You're not subjected to any kind of encumbrance stat, it's more just a nightmare to go find things sometimes or move around equipment even if you do want to store it. It would also be nice if the game replenished your inventory items from your stash when you use one of the checkpoints.The theme of the game is pretty dark, and somewhat bloodborne-esque, but also unique. I found myself caring about Leila's quest and the outcome of the town as a whole.Pros:CombatDifficulty (played on hard)Boss varietyStoryThemeSoundtrack (amazing imo)Art styleCons:Inventory managementSave systemTranslations aren't always as clear as they could be

_childDocuments_.review: I played only a few hours and I'll update my review later, but I want to give a positive feedback to this game in its early days. So here you can find fights in the mood of Salt and Sanctuary; you can find exploration in Metroidvania shape; you can find quests and subquests that remind an "open world" approach. Since I don't mind reading a lot of dialogues and running from a place to another bringing objects to NPCs, this last point is the only one that doesn't fit my sensibility as a player.Anyway, I really enjoyed my time spent in this game so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Tier (higher is better)GSA | Vigil ~ The Longest Night-Regarding difficulty, as no one mentions it: if you consider yourself at least somewhat experienced gamer (for example, if you can beat Souls games solo), play only Hard difficulty; if you use the systems the game offers you, you will not have a hard time at all. In such case, playing on Normal would be boring and you would be doing the game, and yourself, a disservice.The story may hook you if you can manage to make sense of what is happening (English mis-translations don't help), and it does not go by your expectation of a game in this genre (pretty intriguing and keeps you guessing).Also, the game has a lot of content if you want to 100% it; it has English weirdness because it's made by Taiwanese people (I think), but it makes up with heart, and also adds charm to the game obviously translated with Eastern perspective. In my case, more than 30 hours because I mostly explore and discover the game myself, except in (very) rare occasions.Also, the controls are a nice combo of the Souls inertia and Castlevania grace. Movement feels natural, and lends well to exploration of mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D souls-like of decent quality. The visuals are quite nice, and the gameplay works well for the most part. The ambience is lovely, with loads of rain and waterfalls. If you happen to hate rain and waterfalls, by the way, then this is not the game for you. The music is nice, too!What stood out most to me about the gameplay was that the parry window feels a bit wide (at least with the relevant skill upgraded), and this makes a lot of enemies fairly easy to overcome, assuming you're using a sword as your main weapon and have the parry skill. Later in the game, some enemies use non-parry-able attacks, which does bring back some challenge and a need for other tactical approaches. Bosses can sometimes be parried, but often not, so there is that as well. I actually had a very good time matching blades with an optional late-game boss whose attacks could sometimes be parried, and other times... not so much.Certain optional areas along the way to said boss felt like a bit of a slog. Long, repetitive, full of repeating visuals and some rather nasty obstacles and pitfalls. This can also be said of a lot of areas in the main game path, but the graphics and art style are nice enough that I didn't find myself minding all that much.The upgrade system feels pretty well balanced; it will help you manage fights against harder enemies, without ever making them entirely trivial. Some strange enchantment options too, for those looking to play around with a more exotic character build.Perhaps my main complaint is that the "dash" ability, which is needed in order to dash-jump for various traversal challenges, is by default bound to the right button on the directional button pad/D-pad, assuming you're using a controller. Movement is the left stick. L1 and L2 buttons are both used. Two fingers cradle the controller on each side. So either you have six fingers on your left hand, or you will be moving a finger UP from the L1 (shoulder) button to awkwardly curl down to the D-pad while you operate the left stick with your left thumb. This is not what you call "intuitive" or "ergonomic" in the slightest!Better control scheme? L1 for dash, instead of swap weapon. The latter can be bound to the D-pad, since you won't be doing it while moving, and can thus press the D-pad with your left thumb. These things should be obvious the second someone tries to play the game with a controller. And indeed, the button CAN be reassigned in this way... but doing that ALSO reassigns all other uses of the L1 button, including, rather egregiously, ALL the menu tab switching controls. So if you set D-pad left to weapon switch, that will also be the binding for swapping tabs to the left in, for instance, your inventory. Which is very annoying if you're trying to move around your inventory with the D-pad buttons! You can do that with the stick, too, and you'll have to if you want to use dash intuitively (there's also double-tap dashing, which barely works at all)... so, in summary, a non-ideal solution to a slightly embarrassing control scheme goof-up.There's rather a lot of quests, i.e. running around talking to people, doing stuff, talking some more and so forth. The overarching story is kind of interesting but it can be a little difficult to care about the less well-developed characters and their wishes. Not great, but not bad either.The game is, overall, enjoyable. Challenging boss fights, a decent variety of weapon types with individual skill/talent trees, overall satisfying character progression and some choice in attire. Decent number of enemy types and environments. I'd recommend picking it up if you enjoy games of this kind.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game once. I am quite confident I will replay it again sometime.So it is metroidvania, and a good one. Has some souls-like elements but nowhere near as difficult. More of Salt and Sanctuary approach: everything works, but some builds are just easy mod, others are more challenging and rewarding. So it is up to the player to set a difficulty (also, there is a difficulty level you choose on game start, though I don't really know, what it changes).Lots of equipment to find and toy around with. Story is a bit weird, but that's just me, I guess. Anyway, all in all - a very enjoyable game, that is totally worth it's price and your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigil is a beautiful and fun Metroidvania. The setting and intriguing lore setup an excellent premise. The art style and music along with an excellent combat system that supports varied styles, keep the adventure engaging throughout. The only blemish is the lack of voice acting and some inconsistent dialogues. These prevent the game characters from truly shining and keep the player from getting completely invested in this dark fantasy story. There is nothing groundbreaking here in terms of game-play, maps, combat or progression; but a well done Metroidvania is its own reward!

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh Vigil, ended up picking this game up on a whim and it ended up being a great time, albeit a couple things hold it back from being a 9/10 for me. You play as Leila, a member of a group called the Vigilants and it's up to you to save a town from what I assumed was endless night and other baddies and whatnot. You start off making your way to the town of Maye and from there you can see how dark and decrepit the world here is. Devs really did a fantastic job setting up a very oppressive atmosphere from the get go and that's sustained for the entirety of the game, especially the very last dungeon. The game uses very clean and very detailed models and looks smooth with the style of modular animation they decided to go with. Your character can use a variety of armors and weapons that actually change up her model and look very nice. Variety isn't particularly high design wise (with the exception of a certain Bondage Set you get towards the end) but is otherwise serviceable. Enemies all look very spooky and dark and there's a good amount of different enemies scattered in the game's world. Environments also look fantastic and despite most of the art being hand crafted, they certainly didn't go overboard with re-using assets, which is very impressive. Onto the gameplay itself - it's pretty basic and kinda reminded me of other Soulslike titles like Salt & Sanctuary and Blasphemous. Exploring the world is very fun, despite it feeling like a Metroidvania at times, there's not a whole lot you get that requires you to backtrack outside some wind and fire spells. I took my time exploring and saw a good bit of what the game offered and was pretty impressed by how intricate the exploration could be at times. There's a bit I do have to talk about though, and that's this game's "balance" - it's practically nonexistant if you get any ranged abilities, particularly the Magpies, which seem to just straight up delete every single boss in the game with relatively low effort and it's not hard to make it do more damage. The 4 weapons are all great and their skill trees do offer a decent variety and change their gameplay enough, but they still don't compare to just spamming Magpies or using the top end bow, which still just practically deletes everything with low effort. I think, all in all though, the game was very solid, I had a lot of fun with it. There's a ton of sidequests to do and most achievements seem to be tied to completing them. Exploring the game was a ton of fun, and despite the melee weapons being woefully underpowered compared to their ranged counterparts, the combat is still very fun and can be very intense if you do like, a melee only run. The world is dark, drab and the art is amazing, too bad for that plot though, it's just kinda there but it works. Certainly gets my recommendation, if you like games like Blasphemous and S&S, you'll definitely like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty great!I was initially put off by the art, but it's mostly in the backgrounds -- a lot of the character and enemy designs, and especially the bosses, are fantastic.I'm thinking we have Bad/Good/True endings here and I'm actually excited to go through NG+ to do the True ending and see some side content that I missed. Big plus there.--The default controls seemed horrible at first but I couldn't actually figure out how to map things across the keyboard to be more usable, and getting used to them happened pretty quickly.Combat and platforming were very serviceable especially after unlocking a bunch of skills. Some magic spells made encounters too easy, as did some specific weapons, but you could just not use them.I have to say, I wish that the map controls were a lot better. The pan speed has an inverse relation to the zoom level, so if I'm zoomed all the way out it's almost impossible to move the map anywhere. Seems backwards, since what someone would want is to zoom out > quickly move to a different position > zoom back in. Lacking the ability to pin and mark segments of the map is also a big negative since there were some spots I wanted to go back to yet forgot where they were. But I could just look up a complete map online, I guess.--altogether I would definitely recommend people play this. Great Metroidvania, great style. Depending on what you want to get out of it you can just save to a different slot at specific story-advancing plot points (they're pretty telegraphed) instead of replaying the entire thing too.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is generally pretty good and enjoyable. I don't recommend it simply because the save system combined with some genuinely terrible design choices make actually getting through the game a frustrating mess of trial and error. The game's idea of autosave is a consumable item. So, right off the bat, you have a critical save function that goes underused because it's a finite resource. Then you combine that with fall damage, which ordinarily wouldn't be such a big deal except that there are a rather large number of places where missing a small ledge is instant death. And then you lose all your progress up to that point. My own deal-breaker was dealing with a spider cave filled with giant, hyper-realistic spiders along with background spiders constantly scuttling around. I soldiered through my arachnophobia, and got through a huge chunk of the dungeon only to have a brand new giant enemy suddenly swing its way in from off-screen and one-shot me dead. Other than opening up into a room with still a bunch of normal enemies, what notice did I really have that it would a good idea to save at that point? So, now I will have to go through that entire cavern. From the beginning. Dealing with every single spider all over again. I don't even know if I'll make it to the end at this rate.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Salt and Sanctuary Lite, haven't played that?  Maybe think of a super lite version of Hollow Knight but more like a dark souls theme.  Blood, Gore, fetus' ... you know.  It's a pleasant diversion without the crazy commitment you'd expect from a similar game.  I beat it in under 30 hours and honestly a lot of that was me afk.  ( i think i let it run while i went to bed).  I didn't encounter any bugs or crashes so it seems most of what people have complained about is fixed.  The dialog and story feels off at times but it felt as if this was a language interpreter issue.  The game has an easy, normal hard difficulty option so don't feel as if you can't enjoy this because you can just crank it to easy and enjoy the ride.  Talent trees were OK but not really deep.  I found myself running out of things to put my points into pretty early.  You can also respec easily enough.  Combat is fun but weapons are extremely similar.  You can use swords, daggers, 2 handers or bows (all weapons fall into these 4 categories).  A sword feels like any other sword with modifiers making it hit harder or take less stamina for example but some weapons have a special attack that makes them stand out.  You can heal with potions, wear different armor, wear four rings and use all kinds of interesting spells.  The game is just deep enough to feel satisfying.  Finally, there are NOT a ton of resources out there to help guide you through this game but honestly you probably don't need them so long as you follow the quest log (notes in game).  Do all the quest, explore the maps fully, revisit all the places (this is a metroidvania after all), and upgrade your gear...  you'll be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork, the sounds and the mechanics of Vigil remind me of Salt & Sanctuary and I like both games a lot. Being a souls-like Metroidvania type of game, you have to explore to uncover the map and I really enjoy searching all areas for hidden rooms, for which Vigil rewards me every once in a while. Vigil also has quests, which is not typical for the genre and I find it kind of fun to run errands between exploring and boss fights. There is one skill tree for each weapon and one for Leila herself, and skilling feels helpful and pretty balanced. And you also have the option to gather materials to improve your weapons, and at one point even grind enemy loot to exchange for gold, which is a nice additional option to grind for gold and EXP.One major negative for me is how the menu closes. Vigil uses a side menu which opens on pressing the menu button. When you enter one of the side menu points you get into the "real" menu and when you leave that you get back to the side menu which I would expect to close immediately at that point. Normally this wouldn't be tragic, but since you can move Leila with an open side menu - but you can't jump or hit since the buttons are still mapped to the menu - you may or may not be tricked into thinking you can play freely again and might run off a platform just to notice mid-air that you did not jump but open the skills menu and fall to your death after really closing the menu. FML.I also really wish the devs would read the texts again and fix them, some of the dialogue feels like it's made by Bing-translating German to Chinese to French to Hindi to Protuguese to Japanese to English.Then there's the map, which can be a pain to uncover when you play in multiple sessions and it's unfortunate that there are no manual markers you can set to areas you cannot reach yet. But the game sets a few markers itself, and you can unlock something to help you find collectables, which makes it okay.Also I experienced a bug where I unlocked a path by knocking down a cage to reach the upper stages of an area and after teleporting or dying that cage was in its initial position and I had to go all the way around again.UPDATE: You can set the dash control in the settings now. Major plus!+ graphics and artwork are beautiful+ soundtrack is atmospheric and fitting+ quests+ difficulty choice and appropriately demanding boss fights (at least on normal)+ you can wear a barrel for a hat+ devs updated the dash control- side menu is aggravating- the music is way too loud in certain areas and sometimes the game does not know when to play and when to stop the music- controls are a bit rough and feel delayed at times (especially when using items or closing the menu)- some dialogue after the prologue feels rushed and is full of errors

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=====================A well done Metroidvania with strong Souls influence. Well worth the price of admission+ cleared on Hard difficulty+ Good Stuff======================- The visual style of this game, coming across like a gothic picturebook, looks fantastic during play and the player, NPCs, monsters, bosses and environments form a strong cohesive style- The game controls very well, your character is quick and responsive and once you get a hang of the dodging and attacking, you'll find yourself leagues better at going at groups of enemies then in your first few hours- The OST is very good although maybe not very fitting. Like I said earlier, this game has a souls aesthetic but uses a very castlevania sound sets of tracks. It very good if not a tiny bit of a mood killer- There's a lot of value in this game time wise. There are 3 endings of which I got one and one of these is a super secret ending that would reward going through it with a fine toothed comb. Even on a casual playthough with minimal extras hunting I got 14 hours out of it.-The map system, while not making backtracking super easy, is still very intuitive and easy to get aroundBad Stuff=======================-The quest system is, like most souls inspired games, very obtuse and ♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game includes vague notes but it doesn't make some of them much easier to complete. More annoying is that there is a VERY early 'point of no return' that you are not told about. It you fail to lay some proper groundwork in 'part 1' then the quest lines are just dead in 'part 2' which I believe locks you out of a certain ending.- Saving is a little janky, but my advice is to just save manually every time. It seems like the owl statues will sometimes autosave walking past them but I've lost some progress that way and just bit the bullet and saved constantly.- There are some weird bugs with moving platforms or doing jump attacks near corners of a map. I've found myself expelled into oblivion and having to restart but these were not often enough to be a big nuisance but enough to mention it here.

_childDocuments_.review: MY FAVORITE METROIDVANIA IN A LONG TIMEPlayed in 2022i5-11400, 16GB DDR4 RAM, RTX-3060 12gbPlayed in 1440p with all settings on High>>>>> Graphics 9/10 <<<<<The graphics chosen for this game help set the bleak tone for this world covered in eternal night. Each town, forest, and dungeon have their own unique aesthetic.  The character model is fantastic, with each change of armor granting a different appearance. You can look like a total bad-ass or a goof-ball. Your choice! The townsfolk models are simplistic, but I could tell most of them apart without having to be reminded who they are. The monster models are absolutely great, and run the gamut from regular dudes to festering horrors. There are a few odd textures here and there which stood out as odd, but that was hardly a deal-breaker.  >>>>> Characters / Setting / Story 9/10 <<<<<You play as a Vigilant. Your goal (so far as I can tell) is to uncover the cause of the eternal night and bring an end to it.  You have an attachment to the town you spend most of your time in and get to know all the people who live there.  Some folks are quite forgettable, but you do get folks with odd quirks and are perhaps odd enough that you are unsure if you can trust them...  The setting is pretty standard Eldritch Horror and it would be fair to call the setting akin to 2D Bloodborne.  But they pull it off well and create a world that I enjoyed exploring. The story was Dark Souls level of unclear for most of the story.   Heck, even after the ending I was not 100% sure of what the heck was going on and the origin of both the horrors facing me in battle and those pulling the strings from behind the scenes...     >>>>> Music / Sound 9/10 <<<<<I got a real kick out of the music tracks in this game.  There were some locations I would choose to grind for gold so that I could hear the area theme again.  Honorable mention goes to the music in the ocarina dungeons. Straight creepy.  The weapon and enemy sound effects are pretty basic and unvaried, but they get the job done.  There were a few annoying instances where a sound effect would loop and the only way to clear it out was so exit and re-load the game.  While not a deal-breaker, this did happen 5 times during my play-through and killed the pacing.    >>>>> Gameplay 9/10 <<<<<The combat is way better than it has any right to be.  You get 4 weapon classes: swords, daggers, axes, and bows.  Each class gets their own skill tree which unlocks really fun combos and abilities.  Even better yet, many weapons have a special attack much like the ashes of war in Elden Ring. However, these are always weapon-specific here and cannot be changed.  You can also upgrade your weapons and armor at the smith using upgrade materials.  If you want to be fancy, you can also enchant your weapon and gear.  Any game that lets me spin around with a fire sword is doing something right.  The traversal abilities which let you navigate the map also help you in battle.  I found the fighting system to be very fluid and enjoyable.  I played the game on normal and found it to be rather easy once I learned the system.  But got dang, look out for those bears with tree trunks. They hit like a dump truck!  Only sour point for me was the magic system which seemed a bit underwhelming.>>>>> Funfactor and Bugs 10/10 <<<<<In my 21 hours of playtime, I experienced no game crashes, broken quests, or odd glitches.  I very much enjoyed my time here and would gladly return again in the future for another playthough.  You do have multiple endings which does provide replay value.  Beware though!  You will be locked out of some endings if you progress to far in the story and miss out on any key items or actions.  I recommend going into the game blind on your first play-though.  You actions, while well-intended, may have unforeseen consequences! >>>>> Bottom Line 46/50 (92%) <<<<<There is a lot to like here.  The setting is the proper kind of moody and the variability in playstyle options will mean that you will likely find one that feels "just right."  I bought this game on a recommendation and am now passing that recommendation on to others.  Will you be able to bring an end to the eternal night?  If so, what are you willing to sacrifice?

_childDocuments_.review: A Metroidvania with a gritty dirty medieval look about it that I really like. You have for classifications of weapons but inside those you have a wide variety of move sets in them. An example being the starting sword and a sword you can get much later on that has a unique three stab move you can incorporate into your combos. This makes the combat feel varied when you could start a combo against a boss dodge roll away to whip out a bow then start using bow combos from afar waiting for their attacks to end. The map is pretty large as far as these games go but you will be able to eventually get moves that allow you to zip all over the place. The story is a bit hard to follow on the first go around unless you go after every single note that you can read. On the second run it makes it much easier knowing what you know but I'm not sure I like it. One of the endings is objectively the one you should strive for but you will need to follow a guide pretty closely to get it. The enemies are all cool and each area has at least 2-5 unique enemies that mostly drop new gear (SLIME CAP!). It took me about 25ish hours to go through a play through and a half with another 5-10 for achievement cleanup. The game is definitely worth playing and I'm hovering around $15 being fair.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright first of all, im just gonna say this game has some issues with a lot of things but seeing this game just being released couple days ago, it is forgiven.This is probably the closest thing we can get into a Bloodborne + Castlevania with Salt and Sanctuary art style. The game itself is a fair challenge which you can select between easy mode to hard mode. Any mode for me is pretty straightforward so this isnt an issues. Most enemies are slow while you move with that fast movement and a lots of you can do combos and stuff like that is pretty weird for me. The game in easy mode is very easy while in hardmode its still relatively easy for me. Checkpoint system in this game is pretty weird for a metroidvania game where you lose your progress upon death which means you have to save the game alot. But the devs balanced it with no currency droped like most of Souls-like games and a certain item for you to quicksave although its a rare one.Some of bosses name and NPC names are somewhat weird. I think its because the translation but idk. This kinda makes me feel "off" like for example that lightning beast boss. Does his name really translated like that? Most boss are just straight cheap difficulty and annoying, others have some serious challenge and fun to it.The biggest strength of this game is the artstyle and the atmosphere. Spoiler maybe: i really love the atmosphere in Flooded Area. Its by far the best looking area in the game for me. It got me the sense of creepyness of what lurks under those ships and water.One thing that annoys me more than anything is that my PC is pretty good and the fact that the recommended specification for the game for me is still a low-end, this game has serious lag in PC mostly in watery area or foggy area. Idk why but this affects the enjoyment for me. I hope the devs fix this soon.This game is still brand new and there are a lot of issues. For now im just gonna give it like that and i hope in the future updates, it would be better.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty great exploration game akin to Salt & Sanctuary. The game differs from most dark soul-esque games in that the character doesn't collect 'souls' or recollects them on death. Level up doesn't grant stats but instead talents that can give you combat skills so all gear is usable whenever it's obtained so you can care less about "is vitality more important than strength?" and go "A whirlwind axe is cooler than a bow multi-attack skill".The game has multiple difficulty levels that will allow people from multiple backgrounds to get into the game, and gives you items to save whenever you want, even moments before a boss so if you are having problems with a location you can prevent painful backtracking over and over. So while the game will force you to reload on death, it's fairly kind in almost every other way to make for a pleasant souls-like.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much a soft recommend.Pros:-Art style, if you like S&S (Salt & Sanctuary/Sacrifice).-Diverse builds.-Combat can be fun.-An array of weapons and armor.-Sound and music is good, not great, but it suffices.-Decent enemy variety.-Good size world map.Cons:-Bugs, even after years of this game being out. My character will sometimes un-equip her main weapon when adjusting armor/inventory. Sometimes status effects like poison will persist after death and upon revival.-Points of no return which are not stated or even hinted at. This forces you to read guides to ensure you don't fail.-Frustrations around when you die, you lose all progress from the last save. Forces you to use a consumable that "auto-saves" your current location all the time.-Tying this issue in of frustrations, many deaths will revolve around being unable to see your surroundings. Again, forcing you to use an arcane (magic) ability that throws an eyeball to see because you will likely fall to your death a lot otherwise.-Weird camera adjustments, hard to see a lot of times in areas where there's vertical movement. (the majority of this game is vertical movement)-Game is easy, even on hard mode. After the prologue, you will being steamrolling content. Bosses are easy and can be cheesed.-To raise another point, the game feels tedious in certain areas when you're not destroying all the content easily. Artificial difficulty rather than enemies being challenging in a way that feels like you accomplish something. You either get insta-gibbed by traps or falling, or you get 1-shot by certain enemies.-Aggravating layouts in some zones. These are nothing but traps and pit falls, and in a game that doesn't allow much visibility to your surroundings, it again just becomes tedious.-Story wasn't interesting enough to remain engaged.-You eventually just want to get the game over with.Despite the amount of cons, it is recommended to play it at least once if you like Souls likes and/or Metroidvanias, but it is unlikely one that you will want to come back to after completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, 9/10.Great graphic design (Bloodborne sends its regards) and soundtrack, satisfying fighting mechanics (4 different types of weapons with individual skill trees and movesets, plus individual moves granted by specific weapons). Level design is nice, a lot of secrets to find during playthrough. I've completed the game in about 23 hrs without doing 100% run (all weapons, armor, etc.). On "Normal" the game isn't very difficult, all bosses were beaten in less than 3 attempts (except Uptancos, ♥♥♥♥ him and ♥♥♥♥ his dungeon with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spinning blades everywhere). Overall, extremely decent game and I've got a lot of fun playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through this game twice, mainly because I forgot my first playthrough because the game isn't terribly memorable. It's a good, but flawed game. There are definitely some odd design choices, and a bit of jank or translation errors, but overall it's serviceable and enjoyable. Ultimately, the game lacks seems to lack focus and polish at times. It's got some good ideas, nice art, and music, but at the same time it can fall flat; it's inconsistent. For example, you'll go to one area and there's upbeat and intense music and you feel a bit of a rush and then you'll go to another and it's just silence, no music or anything. Instead, there should be appropriate music for each area, and then bombastic music for key moments or set pieces. The UI and quest menus could really use some work. Navigating the menu and equiping items is all a little cumbersome, and the quest notes are vague and incomplete to the point of being near useless. Most of the quests I completed simply because I'm a thorough completionist and explore everywhere, not because I knew what I should do next. Better balancing of items, weapons, and gear would also help. I mainly stuck with gear I earned in the early game because it ultimately was the best gear for my playstyle. It seemed like you never really found better gear, just different gear. Great if you're a fashion-souls player, pretty disappointing if you watch stats. But despite these minor gripes, I still think it's worth checking out, there's still a lot here to like, especially if you like games in this vein.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: I did beat the game but only because i am stubborn and not because i enjoyed it.  The game is full of weird design choices. For example the skill tree. You have to unlock basic attack options like the heavy attack for every weapon type separately. Or the ability to use spells and throwing items while jumping. I am also not a fan of the manual saving or the NPCs which change their location after giving you a quest. I did not complete some quest simply because I didn't know where the correlated NPC went.Overall this game left me frustrated and I can not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingly fun for it price.Controls and game-play are very fluid. Every weapon feels nice to use and switching between them is very comfortable. Amours/Weapons are all unique and awesome looking. The skills trees are simple to follow and let you see what your going to buy. wish more games did this.The story is intriguing, and every npc seems to have actually interesting things to say and give clues to certain side quests even though some have nothing to do with the quest giver. Love the eldritch horrors of the game.The music is excellent! The Mad Pale Raven theme is the best song in the game and goes so hard. I was pleasantly surprised by it. The only negative about this game, is that 3 bosses in the game are way too easy. While I had I think the best armour in the game, these 3 bosses never had a chance to hit me. They don't have enough attacks to be a threat. It's a shame to say, that the optional bosses are more difficult the last 3 bosses. If you are looking for a slightly more forgiving souls-like metroidvania, this is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: A good metroidvania to satisfy the itch.  Game seems to take some influence from Salt and Sanctuary but definitely comes out it's own thing.  Finished the game in just under 13 hours which felt like a good length to me.  I felt like the game packed a lot of density in it's relatively short playthrough and with all the build diversity I could see it being worth a replay.  Overall I would definitely recommend this to anyone who's into metroidvanias.  Solid game that im happy I played.
_childDocuments_.name: Vigil: The Longest Night

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty hefty 8.5/10 from me. I'm playing the game with a controller for reference.Pros:Dark and dismal art style that emphasises the importance of bright colours on interesting objects and scenes.Metroidvania style map and save/warp mechanics.Dialogue is very cool so far, picking up clues from what villagers say about certain missions and backtracking to investigate further is usually worth it.Skills trees and combat are cool.The 2D character models that remind me of an early 2000s Flash game actually work really well in this game, makes me wish that Bloodstained RotN had gone the same route as Vigil.Cons:Controls can be a little clunky at times w/ dodging and parries.
