_childDocuments_.review: This game was a really, really, REALLY fun fetch quest. The atmosphere is great, the gameplay is fun, and it's length is perfect. Not so long you get bored of gathering things, and not so short that you feel like it wasn't worth it. I wholeheartedly recommend it if you want to spend a couple of afternoons just having a chill time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially hooked with the art-style and overall idea, but the game is very much just "gather resource > craft item > use item > gather resource" ad infinitum with short breaks in between to pick up quests from NPC's. Resources constantly respawn and they're not hidden or anything.If the writing or the story was better, it'd be a more tolerable grind. As-is, it isn't very funny, or witty, or original, or emotional.  its very average.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful and adorable crafting (heavy on this) game that blends beautiful art with an engaging story. Would highly recommend to anyone looking for a relaxing and calming cozy game. Some things to consider:The gameplay can become repetitive. You are essentially gathering materials and crafting for the entire game to complete steps in quests that are very straightforward. The storyline is great, but you do not make any choices. You will craft one thing in order to craft another to complete the quest and its steps etc. etc. Each item requires 2+ materials to craft with varying amounts of each.The game can also become quite grindy. At some point I only farmed materials for a while just so I had backups. I wanted to eliminate retracing my steps all the way back to a previous area for some fur or meaty morsels lol. One huge recommendation I would give to anyone playing this game is to just collect EVERYTHING you see and more. If you think you have enough, just collect like 5+ more of that material and you'll be good. Trust me, you will save a lot of time and you won't feel as burned out when completing quests.Overall while the gameplay can become repetitive and grindy at times, I would still recommend it. The story and art is beautiful, the dialogue is funny, the music is calming, and its a very relaxing game that requires little brainpower. While not for everyone, I thoroughly enjoyed this and would recommend to anyone looking for a cozy and whimsical game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews but I have been blown away by this game and feel the need to share how amazing this game is...Ok so I am not very far in but I have just been chilling out, enjoying the scenery and happy vibes.The game has a really nice atmosphere and the artwork is something special in my opinion.The dialogue is interesting and funny..I find myself laughing out loud at times.So far no bugs but as I said, it's early days. I am so impressed with the game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked very promising in the trailer and I was excited to play it. That changed after only spending a few hours playing. its just a bunch of fetch quests that get longer and more frustrating the further into the game you get. I finished the game hoping that I could say that at least it had a good story, but it doesn't even provide that. The ending is lackluster and unsatisfying, the only good thing about it is that it was finally over. pass on this one friends it is not worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Important: If you don't like doing errands at all, it's not a game for you.I loved that game. It's short but really worth playing. It's weird, spooky and amazing in the same time. I love the art style. Would be nice to have some narrator voice there tho. For me doing errands was really relaxing, bit grinding, but still if you were collecting stuff when you just walking through zones it was not much returning to certain spots to get stuff for crafting. Story is simple, yet the plot is nicely done. Game points you in the right direction, can't be lost where to go or what to do. Good controlls, fast travel, didn't experience weird bugs. No combat, low-stress game, no motion sickness for me, perfect for the autumn's or winter's evenings :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: An ultimate cozy game if you like low stakes and collecting/crafting. Some of the top-tier craftables can get a little tedious running back and forth, but overall this game is super fun the world is beautiful and fun to explore. There are enemies you defeat with items you craft but enemies are easy to avoid (there are generous aggro tells), so there is nothing stressful in this game. Really enjoyed it, hope to see more like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly think this one might be up there in one of my favorite games of the year. The story is simple, but captivating. I love the dialogue and how the game keeps us exploring everything actively to ensure we have the properties needed to advance in the game and build new items. The art is beautiful, and every time I enter a new place I find myself pausing to admire it and look around. And don't even get me started on the soundtrack. Usually I play games muted with Spotify in the background, but this is one of the few games I play with the game's soundtrack on. It matches the spooky whimsical theme perfectly, and I love how it changes in each section.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game back in 2022, and it lay gathering dust in my backlog for 2 years before I got around to playing it. No fault of the game, really, the order in which I play things is rather arbitrary.Wytchwood tells the tale of a witch with a cauldron for a head, who must collect 12 souls for a goat in order to fulfil her contract with him. To do this, you must collect ingredients and craft a range of reagents and thingummies in order to progress the story. Some craftables are collected to give to someone or something for the story, others are made as a means of getting more ingredients.The art style is charming, and the music does a good job of setting the tone for each region. The witch herself is a snarky old bird who goes about her business with exasperation at every nitwit she comes across, and I found myself enjoying her character quite a bit. However, while this game is entertaining, it suffers from a chronic crafting grind that I was not expecting, especially towards the end. I found myself running all over the map collecting ingredients from different regions all over again to craft some of the late game items, and for that, I knock off a point from an otherwise amusing 12 hour experience - which likely would've been shorter if not for the time spent gathering. I can still recommend the game, but with the caveat that the crafting system may not be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Too much of a collect-a-thon grind for my liking, one ends up going backwards several times to previous areas gathering more materials, given that you can't know what you'll need later.Not that there is any penalty to this, but it takes time and extends game's length considerably, IMO to its' detriment.I liked the world-building but the ending itself felt quite lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, short, and cozy. The art style is super cute, It has a well-executed overarching plot, and interesting enough side plots. It's not too hard so you don't get frustrated, you can really just chill. I liked that a lot, perfect for making a cup of cocoa and reaping some souls of the local bad guys (*be the change you want to see in the world*). It rubs the spot you get as a kid, making witch potions in the garden - that long-neglected part of your brain will love running around, picking stuff, and putting them together to make spells.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a point and click adventure where instead of arbitrary item exchange chains, you instead go for arbitary item crafting and gathering chains. Though while I mostly jest, the game is not about the fine grains of it's gameplay loop. It's all about presentation and vibes. The game is cozy, but not cottagecore cozy. The leshy might come for tea, so you always keep the fire burning bright kind of cozy.The 5th 6th of this game is a bit too grindy, and there are a few moments in the story that took me out of the experience temporarily, but otherwise I have no big complaints. The deer is also really cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game so much. It was cute and cozy with a bit of dark twists. No hard puzzles, no difficult fighting. Collect, craft, and progress the story. I really liked the art style and story. Short and sweet. Exactly what I needed. Lots of running back and forth to collect things which I did not mind but if you don't like going to the same places over and over again this might not be the right game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game from start to finish. A lot of people are complaining about it being a fetch quest simulator. I mean I understand why, but this games more so for the story and its writing. I didn't mind going back and forth to places because of how cleverly the game is set up with warp points or even giving you a craftable item to teleport you back home which is the center of all portals. The places i did visit I would always grab multitudes of said items in the area that I might need so i was prepped for future requests. Visually the games beautiful, characters art design stands out from other games, the game plays pretty chill. I don't recommend playing it in one sitting however, take your time with it when you do play. I think it would come off less of a Point A to Point B game if it's not rushed and time is taken to collect items from places you're currently visiting.      RATING 4/5     ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and music are gorgeous, the game has charm and the characters are well-made. There are quests in almost every area at a time so you can gather as you make progress in the story. The mechanics are easy enough to understand, and as a whole I really enjoyed playing it and recommend it to anyone who likes fantasy/fairytale games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Super casual but a little tedious at times. The overall game design is rock solid, it's very clear what you need to be doing so you never feel lost or confused. There are some crafting ingredients that you go through a lot, making it frustrating to constantly have to collect reeds and clay but you learn to pick some up every time you walk by a node. Overall it was a great way to chill on the couch.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful artstyle with a charming story and interesting world! I loved all the characters, and my hoarding tendancies in games like this made it go quite quickly in some spots as I already had all the items to craft the next things. Overall, really nice! Definitely recommend if you want a nice magical story with a twist on common fairytales (from what I picked up on, at least) and you enjoy collecting items to craft things for story progression.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and relaxing, sometimes funny, good for everyone. That's what I thought at the beginning of my playtime (first three hours, whole first quest/day). Unfortunately second big quest looks the same like first one and the last objective (each bigger mission has four "bosses") will be probably much worser, because there's only one whole new map for last 4 bosses. Why probably? Because I won't see it, this game switched my brain off. The biggest problem with this game is that I click everything I see all the time, it's not intriguing or interesting. Click, click, click. Before every dialogue there's clicking, after every dialogue there's clicking and this game is praising you for efficient gathering, not for thinking. No riddles, no logic, no changes with progress, no difficulty, nothing extraordinary to work for. If anyone likes maxing games this one is possible to get all achievements in less than 10 hours.It might seem stupid, but there's no reason for any particular thing in this game. There's 12 bosses, but some goat tells you each day to find 4 new, so it could be 4, 8, 12, 16, 100 bosses. Probably only reason for actual number of maps (8) and bosses is dev team boredom with their own game. Or some goat businessplan. I'm sorry for this irony, there's nothing bad in this game's style or recipes, or monsters, or usables, or maps, but it's story and scheme of progression is "RPG maker default", moreover it's lacking logical problems, and UI could be more helpful.So big + for recipes, items and monsters/creatures, all the rest could be better.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! The gameplay consists almost entirely of crafting, which I've always enjoyed in games (I guess because I love making things in real life, too.) The gameplay also doesn't change that much over the course of the 10 hours I spent playing, but the storyline, humorous dialog, and the varied environments you explore keep things fresh. The graphics are done in a beautiful fairy tale storybook style, and the music is nice to listen to and appropriate for each environment (twangy banjos in the swamp area and all). And while you DO have to backtrack sometimes for items, there are portals to each area that link up to a main hub that keep things from getting tedious. Overall, I had a great time with this game, and I'd love for a sequel or something similar. I could also easily see myself replaying it someday.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game won't be for everybody but I enjoyed it quite a bit! Interesting dark storybook vibes with simple tasks. You won't like this if you hate fetch quests because that's essentially all the gameplay is, but I found it relaxing to play. Ending was surprising. Not a lot of replay value but would be worth it to pick up on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game sitting in my library for ages and had an urge to play it after scrolling through my list of games; I thoroughly enjoyed this game, offering great sound effects, story telling, fantasy and artwork, I found myself enjoying collecting resources to craft items for my quests and getting to know each of the characters introduced throughout the story. It was a fun little twist of creative yet simple puzzles with interesting outlooks to each scenario.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous artwork, beautifully enchanting stories, charming animation, and tons of fun! This really is the best adventure game I've played in a while. This was such a nice and chill experience while actually feeling accomplished every time I completed a new recipe. For all the witchy and warlocky people out there, this is also the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A "visual-novel fetch-quest" is how I would generally describe this game. It is, overall, a cozy and wonderful game. I love the soundtrack, general animation / art and aesthetic. Likewise, the fairytales are SO fun and engaging. There is, however, a lack of a cohesive and over-arching plot (it's really just: get more stuff for the goat). but, hey, the fetching itself is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't have been mad paying full price for this, and it's *absolutely* worth it on sale. Gorgeous art, lovely soundtrack, cosy crafting tasks; I loved it. Every so often the crafting can be a *bit* of a pain unless you hoard absolutely every possible item at all times, otherwise this game is just super enjoyable with its Over the Garden Wall vibes and whimsical character design.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Its a beautiful but exhausting potion run and fetch game.Adorable fairytale characters in a great world.But you have to have the will to run around a LOT to gather ingredients to create your potions. And to gather some ingredients you need a potion for which you have to have more ingredients.Its an easy in between game if you love the artstyle.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: short, cozy game with item achieving type missions. Even though it seemed to be the same type of tasks over and over it didn't feel repetitive. The game itself is short (completed it in 10 hours), it was relaxing to pick up for a few hours each day to wind down. The story line was cute and gave extra flare to the game and the color and art work is engaging and fits the entire vibe of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely and soothing story-based game that revolves around collecting resources and crafting them into solutions for problems.The game is kind of like playing through a told story about animal avatar-representations of the sins of humanity. Whom often more or less fall prey to their own particular avarices, you just also more or less happen to help them along to their "inevitable end."The game takes several inspirations from old north-western european fables, and the art style is reminiscent of a particular breed of cartoons aimed at the 5 and below crowd in say sweden and the uk.Cleanly rendered portraits contrasted against soft chalky environments and characters.There isn't much in the way of "skill challenge", although by the nature of the defining gameplay element - it can foster a gradual understanding of resource prioritization - ie check what ingredients you need for the totality of a multi-step recipe and then collect them in order by location and pathing.Or you can also wander as you please with or without the aid of the map and just enjoy the feast of scenery the game offers.Every area in the game is accessible after you're 'done' with it if you want to put together some scrapbook screenshots.Over all, a lovely experience, and I was honestly bereaved that it had to come to an end.Towards the last leg of the journey I decided to forego using shortcuts and started taking the long way around the environments to get to where I needed to be, as I didn't want to say goodbye just yet :')absolutely recommend. lovely game to play for winding down in the evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. Would 100% recommend to anyone wanting a cozy sort of game. There is really no guessing or wondering what to do next as the tasks tells you what to do. I wish it was longer so I could continue playing. There were definitely some parts that I was thinking "this is too much work" but realistically those tasks took me like 10 minutes lol. I played with music playing in the background, but at some points I would turn it off. The graphics and music in this game were brilliantly made. Each world had its own soundtrack and they were made perfectly with each world theme. Get this game immediately <3
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I have found this game to be very enjoyable, though not to be played in one sitting, as the gathering of resources for crafting can become a bit tedious. I loved exploring this world, the graphic style makes it a real pleasure to look at and the difficulty level was just right for me (pretty easy, without risk of perma-death), so it was very relaxing. The structure might feel a bit repetitive to some, though the discovery of new areas kept things interesting for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very fun. I enjoyed the fact that Wytchwood encouraged finding alternative solutions to straight combat and the fact that most spells and such had multiple uses throughout the game instead of primarily being one-off uses. The story was highly enjoyable and I only wish we could learn more about the maiden.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a delight to play. It was relaxing & the story was engaging. My biggest tip is to collect more than one of every set of ingredients because you'll need it later.There were a couple of times where I thought the game should show me more of the screen but otherwise this game was perfect. 10/10 Wholesome Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't stop playing this game.Beautiful visuals.Story that just keeps you going. So addictive. I didn't find it tedious or repetitive at all. All materials were quite easy to figure out where will you get them from and from whom. If you collect basic materials as you go, and pile them up, you will just have to return for one or two items the most. If you pay attention it becomes also obvious which materials are often repeating so you pile those up and returns to locations are minimal. Game also gives you some things you will need in chests, so just explore a lot.Love the references and humor of the game.I finished it in 11h and I would say it is the perfect length for this type of game. Got me at the ending, did not expect that.All in all was great fun.Got the game during discount but would happily pay double. Had just one bug, when an item got stuck where I could not reach it. Game could not do anything after that but exit and going back in fixed that right away. This is just one item of hundreds of them so probably just a freak accident.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Buy it on 50%, enjoy 15-20 hours of running back and forth, reading nice jokes and listening to great unintrusive music. But don't get your hopes up for the story of the year.I needed 18 hours to finish the game, but surely it can be easily done in 15.The interface andyour surroundings are very pretty and I loved the music.Though characters usually only have one picture, that does not always match the situation.The gameplay was easy to get into and does consist mostly of running around, getting ingredients, then crafting something to get more ingreients or further the plot. With your grimoure, journal and your sight the game always tells you where you are at and what you have to do.What I did not enjoy much was feeling like I sprinted sideways and barely moved up and down and having no clue how to get certain items. Only thing the game does not tell you.The story was okay. Interesting at first, but pretty straightforward in the main part. You will recognise a lot of things from fairy tales, sometimes more or less creatively spun. The ending however left me very dissatisfied. Not only could you see at least part of it coming from the beginning, it cuts you off at a point where you really think that you should be able to do SOMETHING...All in all a nice experience or 5€ or so.Play it with your child old enough to understand fairy tale tropes or for a few hours at a time to just relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty game, fun and soothing gameplay, really enjoyed it. I get the other reviews about the grind towards the end, but it wasn't terrible. There was a lot of access between worlds that made gathering easier, and gathering everything I could as I went throughout kept the grind to a minimum. Very happy I picked this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little mix of dark and sweet. You're a weird little witch who's trying to deliver the souls of several dodgy characters to an even dodgier goat. To do this you'll need to follow a series of injustices and concoct various potions, cast curses, and crate magical thingamagics, all while exploring an absurdly colourful hand-drawn world and collecting ingredients for your ever expanding craftable inventory.The game mechanics are pretty simple, explore, talk to characters, collect clues and ingredients, make items for quests --> deliver souls to nefarious goat. What really make the Wytchwood shine is the beautiful world, expertly designed for visual impact, and the deliciously twisted characters you meet along the way. A great little game for anyone who appreciates a good villain, and an even better colour palette.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements. Minor spoilers ahead. Wytchwood is a fantasy exploration game where you play as a witch that needs to collect the souls of sinners (bosses) and deliver them to the Goat (= Devil), and each of them have a specific backstory and particular sin. You have to explore several different areas, each with different materials to gather, enemies and characters to interact with, starting with 3, then 4 new ones, and another new one by the end of the game. To progress and can capture the sinners you need to solve puzzles, that almost always about crafting new materials and reagents, using the materials you can collect, in a sort of food chain, where the raw materials that can be picked off the ground need to be used to get different materials, either by crafting or by using them on enemies, and so on.The scenarios are beautiful and very well illustrated, ranging from very colorful to more grim tones, depending on the area you’re in. The characters and enemies are stylized, similar to a cartoon, but have great designs and are also very well drawn. The sinners are represented as animals, and most times that animal represents their sins and personality, and I think this is a great detail and very well thought of by the designers.Each location in the game has a fitting background music and the sound effects are good, it’s just a shame there is no narration or at least some sounds from the characters in the dialogue scenes.Regarding gameplay, this game relies heavily on crafting and gathering materials, so what you do in the first hour is what you’ll be doing for the rest of the game, only the recipes get more complex and require more complex materials. To save time, it’s a good idea to spare some extra time stocking up on materials when you’re in a specific location, to avoid having to come back later just to get materials you’re missing.  14 Achievements. Around 8,5 hours. Easy. Easy. All are story related, one for each boss. Wytchwood is a fantasy exploration game with material gathering and crafting mechanics. The several areas/worlds and their characters are stylized and beautifully illustrated, and each of the bosses have well written and interesting backstories.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Simple but entertaining game. Fulfill narrative quests by exploring and gathering items and then using them to craft objects to complete the quests.The writing isn't stellar but good enough. The annoying part of the game is there isn't much balance in the items you need. Get ready to grind for 50 bug parts while only needing a few Algae when Algae is wayyyy more common and easier to get. Causes you to constantly have to go back to old areas to collect the same items while having tons of items you don't need.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's very much a cozy game and the atmosphere suits that so well.  The art and writing are both phenomenal.  It'll have you backtracking to a lot of places and investigating various areas for ingredients, but everything ties together so well.  I've played for around six hours and gotten about halfway through the objectives which feels like a good pace.  The only trouble I've had was a visual thing where the terrain was shaky and hard to look at when I was running in the game, but I've mostly been walking around so it hasn't bothered me as much. If cozy games are your thing and you like a good story, then definitely pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful little game. There's something so refreshing about a game that almost refuses to explain anything - you're simply expected to accept all the fantastical elements of the worldbuilding; your magic, the sapient animals, the oddities among humans, almost nothing is ever explored and it feels magical as a direct result. The vibes are absolutely impeccable.Other reviewers talk about the game's grindy quality, and they're right, there's definitely a grind mostly composed of a lot of backtracking to complete whatever weird recipe you need this time, often with sub-recipes. There is no hunting for recipes, only the ingredients, and you're only told which biome each is found in, meaning you have to remember on your own where within each place each thing can be found - definitely a game well worth binging in short order. But that's also something I love about this game. It rewards you for exploring and paying attention.The story is fantastic as well. A lot of the wicked souls are clearly taking part in a classic fairy tale, but it's always with some kind of twist to better suit it to what's being presented. The best example is probably the obvious Rumplestiltskin  story, in which your target is a greedy landlord who sabotaged a local mill in order to evict the millers because "the property value went up", which sees you track down a fairy named something like Rumples who grudgingly helps you turn the millers' grain into gold so they can pay rent and keep the mill - not that they'll need to keep paying for much longer, considering the nature of the game. Clearly based on a specific classic tale, but if you'd somehow never heard of it or were fuzzy on the details, you wouldn't feel like you were missing out on too much.Overall? An utterly charming short game that I'd encourage most people to pick up. It's presently listed for $19.99 USD, so I wouldn't blame anyone for waiting for a sale, but if you watched the trailer, read this far, and still find yourself interested? Pop it on your wishlist and get it when you can. It'll prove worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The most beautiful game ever. The music, the illustrations everything is wonderful. The gameplay is not complicated, it is simply gather stuff to make more stuff, but I love walking through all the locations and feel the atmosphere. What I really love about this game is that you do not simply run around with a sword to kill all your enemies. Everything has its weakness. You have to find out what it is and use a unique spell, trap or cursed item to neutralize the enemy and get what you need from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint about this game is that it ended.If you are like me and spend hours and hours grinding for materials and going nuts over crafting systems then this is the game for you. I'm the sort of person who, in Breath of the Wild, had to stop and pick up every tree nut, every apple, every mushroom, bomb all the trees, and do all the cooking. This game was all gathering and crafting and I LOVE it. Even the 'combat' is crafting-based since it's not about hacking and slashing but about crafting the item/spell you need to defeat your opponent. And while the horder in me does balk at the idea of having to use my precious materials, when doing so is the whole premise of the game you have to forgive it and tell yourself that you are only sacirficing said precious materials in order to then gain materials that are even more precious.This is an obsessive item-horder's dream game and I only wish there was more to it. That said, there is plenty here and I definitely feel like I got my money's worth, especially given that I probably stretched this game out quite a bit thanks to my obsessive collecting. I loved the art style, I loved the stories, I loved having a cranky old witch as a protagonist, and I was pleasantly surprised by the twist ending. I honestly didn't see it coming (though someone else might have, lol). I'd love some sequal or DLC where we get to explore more of the witch's backstory too, but for now I am really satisfied with this game.That said, this isn't going to be for everyone. It's very straightforward, fairly grindy (which I don't see as a bad thing when the 'grinding' is basically GRAB ALL THE THINGS, but some do), and there aren't very many puzzles that you can't solve by just doing a bit more exploring and talking to people until the story progresses enough to tell you what you need. I might have liked if we had to sort of figure out what to use where with riddles and clues, but that might have been a bit complicated and wouldn't have worked with the way they had the recipes set up. Maybe if we get another game like this the Devs can incorporate that as the hard mode, lol.All in all, I would definitely recommend this game for all my fellow obsessive horders out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game but I can only tolerate so much at a time. I love the artwork and the story, and the best advice I could give someone starting out is to collect EVERYTHING. Don't pass up anything...chop every tree, collect every plant, everything! Cause you're going to need it all. This game is basically...I need this, but you'll have to get this from this guy first, and that guy needs this from that guy, who needs something else from somewhere else. This is not for everyone, but it is a nice little relaxing game when you have the mind for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I do not recommend this game is that I feel the description is deceitful. It says you can research spells(hover your mouse on an enemy to see what they're weak to and it automatically adds the recipe to the crafting menu), pass judgement(you do not have the ability to judge anyone, they all get the outcome that the game chooses), use your wit to solve puzzles(I've beat 4 of the "bosses" and there have not been any puzzles so far.)This game is just basically clicking ingredients on the different maps or crafting a potion or trap to get more ingredients. You need ingredients to get the ingredients that craft the thing to get the ingredients you need for a quest. And you have to run around the different maps to acquire them. All you do is run around collecting ingredients. Feels more like a visual novel than an rpg. If you like this kinda stuff then it's for you but I personally felt a little deceived by it. I do like the art and I am going to finish the game cuz I paid money.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A good crafting game whose story takes from the old tales of caution. The gameplay can be somewhat repetive, but for someone who like to gather stuff in games for no other reason than to hoard them, it can be quite satisfying. It is also fun to see a game with a hero using creativity and intelligence to reach her goals (even though she doesn't know what her exact goal is).
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fine classic adventure game, the old school adventure where you need a stick to make a trap to catch a bird because you need a feather to make a potion.  Think of it like a HOG without the mini-games; it's a pure scavenger hunt of lots and lots of fetch quests.  Ostensibly, you have an over-arching quest to vanquish a dozen villains, but it's really all just endless scavenger hunting.  To make it palpable and not tedious and grindy I broke it up and did a quest or two a day.  If you do that, then I highly recommend this.  Two thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is for people who want to live out their swamp hag fantasies, and to those looking forward to being an obnoxious old person who sticks their nose into everybody's business. The story draws a lot from folk tale tales (complete with a lucid, practical tone that dips its toe into the morally grey from time to time), which is a nostalgic treat, and ol' pot head over here is one of my favourite protagonists in anything ever.The only advice I have for new players is to grab a little bit of everything as you traverse different areas, as it cuts down on having to backtrack to places you were just in - you never know when you're going to need some frog slime or a coffin nail. You may be tempted to complete the quests one at a time or in a particular order, but each set of four will inevitably bleed into each other so I tend to just roll with whatever draws me in. The stakes are overall pretty low and while you can get hurt, there is no way to permanently mess up.The art is beautiful, the music is beautiful. The gameplay might be boring to some, but if you won't turn your nose up at a point-and-click absolutely give this a go. The story is simple yet deftly spun; and for me, it's the ending that really pulls it together. I will be coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little relaxing game with a beautiful art style, some really funny moments, and an interesting twist at the end! I loved this game! Although the gameplay itself is repetitive, the environment and questlines were quite varied and the progression through the game was well-paced. The gameplay is super easy, and I don't mean that in a bad way! It's really easy to pick up and the plot and environmental cues are more than enough to encourage curiosity and exploration.I will note that I played this on a MacBook Pro with a keyboard and mouse (and occasionally trackpad). The game is definitely more tailored to be played with a controller, but it wasn't clunky enough to make me frustrated, especially because combat situations are generous and don't require clean and quick reaction times.TLDR; Wytchwood is a great game for anyone who likes calming indie game experiences, with plenty of wit and really detailed writing and art to immerse yourself in! 9/10 from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a game with beautiful worlds and some dark humor.The story is divided into three parts of four chapters in which you have to collect a bad guy's soul each time.It's all about collecting ingredients to craft things to achieve those goals.The grind is not that bad. Just collect some more than you need as you are on it and you'll often be able to just craft what you need during new encounters. There's fast travel anyway so it's not that of a burden to go back to a place and resources respawn when reentering a scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I love this style of game. If you habitually collect every object you can and stack your inventory, you'll like this game. I read a complaint about having to go back and forth late game to various places to complete quests. Yes, you do some of that, but given my hoarder play style I didn't find this tedious. It's about 6-8 hours of playtime. I took long breaks in between quests and could easily pick back where I left off. I'll check out other games by this publisher for sure. I do think the game needed a touch more production value. Overall, if the theme and play style appeal to you, you will like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game for free, (requested a key because it looked right up my alley), and boy it did not disappoint! Wytchwood not only has an easy crafting system, but the stories throughout were so fun and well written! I would give it a 10/10, the gameplay was just incredible. Would love to see some dlc for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly charming, gorgeous and fun! The writing is witty, the characters memorable, the visuals fantastic and the mystery enticing. I particularly enjoyed the fairytale vibe that came through really well and the way the game divided itself into three acts. I think it would have been a bit overwhelming otherwise. I recommend this game to you, if you enjoy the crafting parts of stardew valley and games with storylines to discover instead of choices to make. I suppose it might be a bit "fetchquest-y" for some people, but I always enjoyed retreading old paths and listening to the different soundtracks of the areas.The gameplay is very simple. I played it partially with the keyboard and mouse, partially with the controller, and found I liked the controller a bit better. Spoilers for the next part:I was surprised how few people it took to make this amazing game when I looked through the credits, and it felt like most of them were also involved in the art. I would love love LOVE an art book if you ever decide to make one and I hope you are all very proud of yourselves for creating something so nice :) I'm looking forward to any new titles you might release!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The game is basically a fetch quest collection. You are to collect 12 souls as per your deal with the goat. That requires collecting of basic materials to craft them into items that you using to acheve your goal and that pretty much covers the entirety of the game loop. I wish there would other gameplay mechanics to spice up things, e.g. there's a cauldron in your hut in the beggining of the game but it servers no purpose, crafting is done simply in the inventory, would be nice to have some sort of minigame tied to crafting potions in said cauldron to make the gameplay more interesting. By the time I had to collect the last four souls the game started to bore me a bit but I pulled through. Still is worth it though, if you accept it for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I've only scratched the surface so far, but I sure am delightfully surprised by this one! Crafting mechanics usually make me raise an eyebrow, but I love a good point-and-click adventure and the crafting here feels more like a means to an end to get each item you need to complete the quests; it's integrated incredibly naturally. Combine that with the outstanding art direction and fun fantastical hijinks you can get up to and it's charming enough for just a quick romp, but again, this is by no means a game short on content and I still have plenty to crawl around through. Another banger at a great value from Whitethorn Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: as multiple reviews comment, this is a gathering + crafting game with a story. however it did not get repetitive or feel tiring or annoying to me in the slightest. very enjoyable stories, lovely soundtrack and adorable game art. cozy gameplay, not stressful at all. took 15 hours give or take to finish. definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Since I really love witchcraft and everything around witches, this game sparked my interest. And boy I'm so glad that I've bought it! Interesting story, witty, lovable main character with great humor, understandable controls, quests aren't tediously long, continuously revealed and logical crafting system. _childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a seriously great game. The art style and music was amazing and I laughed out loud at some points and said a lot of, "aww" at others. It's essentially a crafting puzzle game so if that's something you enjoy it's a great game for that.My only criticisms are more quality of life things. I'd like hot keys for the map and inventory, and an indication for water sources on the map. But that's all very nit picky and shouldn't dissuade anyone from trying it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a heartwarming gem that seamlessly combines cozy crafting with an engaging story. The adorable art style infuses the experience with charm, while the soothing music enhances immersion. Crafting feels purposeful and enjoyable, each creation contributing meaningfully to the gameplay. More than just a game, it's a tranquil escape that wraps you in a comforting embrace. A must-play for anyone seeking a soothing and fulfilling gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, beautiful art and fun characters, the gameplay itself is fun as well, though there's A LOT of backtracking, often I forgot what I needed and had to go to the place I was before etc etc, but honestly I didn't mind it. Don't get the game if it's not something for you, for me personally it just made me take breaks from the game and actually enjoy it a slower pace instead of speeding trough it. The story(+stories) is cool. overall it's a neat game and I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm newer to gaming, and I absolutely fell in love with this cozy game! I couldn't stop playing. I loved all of it from the art, the story, to the game play! It was really well paced and challenging enough that I felt accomplished without all the frustration. It's beautifully designed, and even some dialog made me chuckle. Wytchwood is an absolute favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The two biggest comments you will see about this game are these:1) it was too grindy and the story wasn't fulfilling enough to make up for it (on negative reviews, most commonly)2) the grind wasn't that bad, and the story was more than enough to make up for it (on positive reviews, generally)So, here's the thing. The grind in this game can be bad, and the backtracking can be even worse. On the other hand, the grind and backtracking may be almost non-existent. What determines which way your playthrough will go? Well, it mostly depends on how many of each ingredient you collect in each area the first time you are given access to them (I know that's a bit vague, but it'll make sense once you begin playing).Now, to clear some things up, I 100% would recommend this game if you are willing to play either way, like I was. But, to determine if you'll be willing to either backtrack and grind for the majority of the game for long enough to finish, here's my personal view of it. If you like playing games for the story and the story alone... you will not finish this game. While the story is clever and fun (though I wasn't a HUGE fan of the ending), it is rather sparse, and the majority of the game will not be story-progressing. You may enjoy the story, but it will take far too long to progress, and you will get bored quickly if you are only in it for the story. If you find pleasure in games BEYOND just the story, you will do just fine.THAT BEING SAID - this game is pretty heavy on the grind even if you go about collecting materials the right way, so you likely will not be able to finish it in one sitting. I think it took me about 9 hours to finish the game, which isn't that much playtime all things considered (or maybe it is, I likely play far too many video games, that's not the point though), but those hours were distributed amongst 7 different playing sessions, and even then there were times when I felt myself sitting there, wanting nothing more than to stop playing. It's quite a bit of a grind (though you'll become more efficient the longer you play).So, final remarks. Is this a good game? Yes and no. The story is good, although there's not very much of it present, almost as if it was an afterthought. The art is remarkable (at least in my opinion). It honestly is probably one of the only things that got me through the more grueling grinds in this game. The characters you meet are charming and unique, and the crafting system is honestly really well thought up and easy to use. Did I actually *enjoy* all 9 hours that I played through? No. I did not. Do I still think this charming little game is worth a playthrough? Absolutely I do.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful artwork, movement is very fluid, and it never felt much like a grind. Occasionally, while on Steam Deck, character will stop moving/responding to joystick. But it's easily fixed by quitting to the menu and you load back in immediately where you were. Short and sweet game that helped me relax.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an excellent mix of crafting and visual nobel mechanics. I recommend this game as a way to enjoy your self reading a book and being part of the story at the same time. This game is very relaxing and the stories told by it have a nostalgic touch.The only downside is that the time flies while playing it and may get you tired of reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I must be part magpie or squirrel or some other gathering and keeping type creature, because this game satisfied that part of me immensely.  As of this review I've played for 10 hours and have only completed three of the quests in this game.  Probably because I rather enjoy wandering about and I may or may not get distracted by watching the birds and the grasshoppers, instead of actually accomplishing anything. So if you like to just sort of take your time with things, this will probably fit that.  If you are more goal orientated and absolutely must accomplish things in a reasonable time, then this is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A whimsical, stylised experience in a world brimming with life. Every screen feels like a new work of art, it really takes me back to reading picture books in primary school. This entire game oozes personality, with it's dialogue and writing, down to small character moments that make this game feel so meticulously made. Gameplay is somewhat repetitive, though in my experience I found it very relaxing and therapeutic, I can easily spend hours going from one quest to another, collecting ingredients from each region. The grind doesn't feel so "grindy" when the journey takes you through such marvellous set pieces and colourful characters. Just sit back, get comfy and do witch stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: really pretty and really relaxing, i grew up on fairy tales so this scratched an itch i didn't know i had. it felt like 8-10 hours worth of Aesop's fables.gameplay is pretty lackluster though, it's all crafting (which was fun for the first hour, before becoming really tedious for the rest of the game). there's not a lot of figuring out to do since the game gives you all the recipes for whatever you need when you need it, and you spend most of the game just grinding different areas for materials.the art, music, and story kept it enjoyable, but if i was someone who wasn't a fan of any one of those aspects then the game would probably feel extremely boring. wish there were more puzzle or exploration elements to it, because i genuinely almost fell asleep a couple times while playing since the whole game was so relaxing and the gameplay was so unstimulating (save for the times i would get frustrated because i'd be missing just one material and i'd have to chain-craft a bunch of things to obtain it). i would've loved having something shorter with more interesting gameplay— or just less crafting.as a side-note: would really love it if the journal contained what had happened so far in the quest instead of just what i need to do at the current moment. usually up to four quests are happening at the same time, and sometimes i want to recall what happened in a specific quest line.overall, really good to play when you just wanna chill out! some hours i left it on while doing other things just for the vibes. hoping to see more games with this art style in the future because i was at awe with how pretty everything was the whole time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game! I 100% understand the negative reviews about the game being grindy, but the art, music,  and environments, kept it fresh enough to not feel like a chore. I also kept on top of trying to always have a at least a few of all the more common items, which meant that when I was missing something, it was only running to get one or two things instead of 15 things. The ending was great, as well as the art and music, if you have the patience to sit down and down some running around as an old swamp witch, this is absolutely worth the time!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastically beautiful game! The basis on retellings of fairytales and lore was intriguing and each of the quests intertwined well to craft an engaging, sometimes snarky story of righting wrongs. The game was beautiful--so many different color schemes for each section. The design of the world as almost like a pop-up book really fit well with the content. The music was gorgeous.This is one of my favorite games that I have played. Thank you! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games. Collecting without arduous inventory management and crafting from anywhere. Excellent writing - the overarching story relies on old tropes/fables but there are twists and the cultural shorthand allows for less exposition and more interesting dialogue. The crabby witch speaks to my cynical but generous soul. And then, great music, and gorgeous artwork, really aesthetically cohesive. And over in 13 hours of gameplay, perfect length, I love when a game ends naturally instead of waiting for me to get sick of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a wonderfully laid out experience, made for crafters and gatherers and adventurers alike! The art style is amazing, as are the character designs and personalities. The gathering and crafting did get a bit grindy here and there but overall, its expected of a game with crafting elements. I absolutely adored this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Started fun, turned very tedious very fast. This game is almost entirely made of fetch quests. No thinking is required on your part - just use your magic vision to see what item a creature needs, then check your recipes to see which ingredients you need to craft it, and then run around the map collecting the ingredients. Often to get some of those ingredients you need to defeat other creatures, some of which may need yet another item, so you get to repeat this process multiple times to eventually finish a part of a quest. If you like fetch quests the game might work for you. If you like varied gameplay then skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: very relaxing game, I really love the graphics, the crafting and story lines. I noticed you cant go ahead of the scenario because if you do it wont count and you will have to do it again (ended up feeding someone a pie ahead of time and it did not count for some reason). I don't do the quest in order so I have the tendency to do several in the same times. There is no time to do them so you are on your own schedule, there is no day or night type of thing.So far I keep going back to the game due to the relaxing gameplay and that I like this type of game where you must find items and craft them.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: So 10.5 hours in and im still not finished. But I did forget to feed myself and the dog and take the trash out. Basically, this game is AMAZING. The story is adorable and funny, and the graphics are beautiful. It's now 1am (i thought it was maybe 8pm lol) time to feed myself and the dog and try to sleep so i can finish it and play again in the morning! Absolutely amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: So delightfully cozy and fun, this game is equal parts wholesome and occult in the best way. I greatly enjoyed the quirkiness and humor of this game while following a fun but simple story line. As it is primarily a crafting game, you spend a lot of time running around collecting needed materials for various reagents, which can get tedious if you are not prepared for it. I found the setting/artwork to be so beautiful, it was the original reason I made the purchase. Visually stunning imo. Repetition is the name of the game, so if you don't want that maybe look for something else, but i would seriously recommend this to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really excellent game. I thought the storytelling was very unique, and the instructions were very clear, There were only a couple of times where it took me a little bit to figure out my next steps. I loved the checklist style quest journal. It gave me the option of pursuing one by one or multiple. I did find it a little rough in the middle where it felt like I had to go find this ingredient to go make this potion, to make this trinket, to scare this goblin, to get the ingredient, to finish this one quest bit. It could be a little tedious, but I started collecting as much stuff in an area that I would think I might need for other times so I didn't have to go back and forth constantly. I like the little transporter. acting like a fast travel port. I was happy it had a clear ending to signal me that I had completed all objectives. All in all, I like this game and I might replay it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games, wish I could find other games that I enjoy as much. The art style is whimsical yet dark, and reminds me of many of my other favorite games like fran bow, and sally face. The buildup of each quest is purely masterful, and the ability to choose which soul to track was an amazingly welcome touch pf helpfulness. While I had to travel far and often to gather what I needed throughout, I never felt that I was off track due to knowing my goals. The twist at the end was magnificent, and I truly did not expect it in the slightest. I do wish there was some small story or memory explanation after the ending, but it satisfied me nonetheless. I wish more games were able to pull me in so strongly and make me keep coming back like this one did. The music is not overly complicated or distracting, and adds just enough background to boost each part of the game. Bravo.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game but with a dark side that's fun. Fairly straightforward, but you do have to go all over the place to collect the things you need for each puzzle. I've done the first 3rd of the game, and enjoyed how at first you're just running about trying to figure out what to do, but then it all just kind of comes together at the same time even though it's separate events. Very fun and chill!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, a fun, cozy, chill, sort of time. I finished the whole thing in just under 15 hours. The graphics are beautiful and bright. And if you have an itch to be a witch in the woods, mixing cups full of mud with a stick and calling them potions, this is certainly a game for you. My only negative is that I wouldn't say it has much if any replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. The graphics are adorable and the story line was cute. It is basically a game where you collect items, but it was not boring. I found it a soothing way to relax after a long day at work. I got immersed in the cute sections of the map. It was fun and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "meh" setting, because I found this game unpleasant, yet addictive. The whole game consists of running around from place to place doing chores, occasionally dodging enemies. This is either going to be up your street or not - I didn't particularly enjoy it, but I couldn't bloody stop doing it because heeey dopamine. I'm ok with that. What I am not ok with is that most of the chores consist of killing stuff. Basically, if it's in the game and you can't talk to it, it's probably there so you can kill it. Birds? Kill. Fireflies? Kill. Pretty fairies? KILL. Kill kill kill kill. You see it, you kill it, and you learn soon enough to kill literally everything you see, because otherwise you're going to end up having to schlep back to wherever the hell you are to kill something or other to craft the latest doodah. So, yeah, I'm not hugely impressed with that side of things.There are no real puzzles to solve or mysteries to unlock. The only way in which you'll tax your brain is trying to remember what you have to collect (i.e., KILL), and where you last saw it. The mini-stories are kinda meh, often sad or gruesome. I have no idea why so many people describe it as cosy. It's a murderspree in murderland. Calling it "cosy" is like saying that "Pumped Up Kicks" is a jolly song.Other than that, it's a mix bag of good and bad stuff. I liked the graphics and music. I didn't like a lot of the storylines (grim, grim, GRIM). The symbols for the items you need to collect or craft are TINY and I found it quite hard to identify them. Having to remember that this squiggle means this potion and that squiggle means that tool is, again, more a test of memory than sense.Basically, if you want to run around slaughtering everything in sight in order to complete chores, you're probably going to like this. If you'd rather not, I'd avoid it. I'm going to finish it because of that sweet, sweet dopamine, but I honestly wish I hadn't started it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a delightful game. Pretty much like playing through an old fairy tale with wacky characters and an interesting story. The art style they went with in this game is so whimsical and colorful. Exploring the new areas was truly fun and kept me engrossed in the game while looking for the many ingredients needed to cast my witch's spells as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little crafting game with what was probably a lot of effort from the size of the studio that made it. the art is beautiful and the stories were fun. It was fairly repetitive, but the narrative made me see it through till the end. Definitely the kind of game to play when you need a book from more mentally taxing endeavors, not the kind of game to try and speed run.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: It is such a good story, and I loved the relaxing game-play. It's not super long; honestly I could go for an expansion if i wasn't a bit worried it would be too grindy. Don't get me wrong, the grind I experienced never got to the point of annoyance, and I'm not a grind fan. If your someone who likes animal crossing and wants a shorter game with stronger story telling and a bit of a witchy atmosphere then this is the game you looking for. It is a breath of earth and trees
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Music: I like it, but let me be frank after visiting the area fifth time it starts to feel very repetitive.Graphic: it's 2D, right? Everything's flat but stylized very neatly, I love the look. The only thing that irks me is character portraits getting mirrored without change — despite some characters being clearly not symmetrical.Gameplay: is 80% of picking things from ground, then some crafting and killing other things for more ingredients and crafting. There's no fighting, all hostiles are 1-hit with the right spell. You may run past everything, they won't follow you too far. You reveal spells by looking at things, and ingredients for one may be scattered all over the areas. So unless you gather A LOT and end up with way too many twigs and wasted time, or you need to go back again and again. There are shortcuts, but areas are rather small and most of them connect with each other. Plus, you get more ingredients with running around. Someone called it grindy, and, well, it is, a bit. It's generally rather short, so it's not like you have that much time to get tired. It felt weird to avoid killing some roaches, thinking, “it took time to collect these twigs, no spending them on 'ya!”Also, it's kind of immersion-breaking when dialogue lines get repeated when you are asked to bring something, then when you have the item, and then when you bring the second and third items when there are more than one. And characters repeat the list even when they already got half of it.Plot: it's a fairy tale! You play an amnesiac witch that needs to fulfill a contract with a dark spirit and collect the souls of twelve villains. The world is funny in that sense, you have humans, you have sentient animals, you have the same animals as small pets as well. And sentient Pigs in clothes, owning a pig farm with smaller naked pigs. There are some fae and goblins, as a bonus.I like a lot how the main character is kind and wise but amusingly pragmatic. She will kill small animals without hesitation if she needs that feather or paw. She will put that dryad on fire making it scream in pain, Also it disheartened me to kill crows — right when their description calls them friends of witch! There's one other thing that is probably also plot-related. The metaphor with main villains is clear, it even is said out loud. But what's up with all the closed eyes? Except villains, one boy, one plant, and one fae? What do they see that others don't?In total, it's very nice. I could use more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful stylized graphics and a good story line with a bit of mystery. I really enjoyed all the different characters whose souls you collect and the strange ways you end up capturing them.  Shorter, beat the game in about 11 hours - but I really enjoyed it. Is this for you? This game does not feature combat, instead you'll spend most of your time gathering materials for different spells and potions. The closest you'll get to 'fighting' is by creating materials that knock out or explode creatures to gather their parts. If that's fine with you, you'll like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game very much. Artwork, music. Each location is thoughtfully made, with it's own vibes, music, crafting ingredients, characters, everything. Crafting isn't boring, but sometimes I have to google how to get an ingredient, because it gives you only the location of the ingredient, but information is very easy to find. Quests are interesting. I like the main character as well and the mystery around her. Yes, sometimes I found small bugs like at the beginning I couldn't proceed with the task until went to another location and back, it didn't happen after that. So compare to all the game, how it fills and plays, it is barely noticeable and aren't big issues. I find this game better than Don't Starve, because I don't like active combat, and the mysterious spooky atmosphere is better in this game. To my taste the artwork, characters and crafting are better too. Overall, if you like atmospheric craft and quests games with beautiful artwork or you just want to be a witch for a while then I recommend this game a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a good one, I loved how it looked (and sounded, goodness the soundtrack is very fitting) and the stories of each quest line was wondrous. One thing I did not notice until the end is that you can buy stuff from the marketplace? I never ended up doing it but hey, maybe that will help with the grind!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The art is beautiful, the humor is wry and silly, and the quests are meaningful. I loved visiting all parts of the map, capturing the souls of villainous creatures. The witchy vibes were on point for fall. I was curious throughout to see how the game would end, and I especially enjoyed the fairy tale references in the last third of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: i find wytchwood to be those kind of games where completion is highly possible. where i would just play only once or twice but leaving me secretly hoping the developer to create more similar masterpieces.the graphics are beautiful and the characters are intriguing in their own ways. especially the witch, where she takes no ♥♥♥♥ from nobody. absolutely love the story line, and the way it unfolds as you progress. quests objectives are clear and easy to track.craft-able items are interesting and materials doesn't require you to grind to collect. travelling is reasonably bearable, anyway you might as well collect some materials on the way to your next destination. in fact, i only used the hearthseed just once throughout the entire run.bought the game during autumn sale and its worth my every penny. here's hoping to more games like these. will definitely recommend this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved playing this game! The storytelling was simple yet so engaging. Honestly at first glance I thought I was in for a simple cozy game about a witch, but it was so much more than that. Very reminiscent of classic folktales that tend to have darker undertones or themes while still keeping a cozy, colorful aesthetic. I also loved the character designs and overall art style of the game. Some mechanics were pretty repetitive, but constantly discovering new crafting recipes really helped to balance that out. Honestly the perfect game for a lazy Sunday inside.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game was adorable and fun, but a bit janky. I didn't encounter any serious bugs, although it seems like many people did if you check the discussions, and no response from the devs. Worth picking up if you see it on sale. Really enjoyed the music in certain areas.Other reviews mention being boring and grindy. I didn't experience  much of this, but there were some sections where I was perpetually running out of sticks or clay especially. Pick up everything you can collect for free as you run by and it should help out.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is charming, casual, and relaxing. I love it so much i'm on my second playthrough. The art is beautiful, the music is soothing, and you spend a lot of time searching for ingredients to cast spells, which is incredibly fun for me. I like that you can't die and lose all your progress--the closest thing is that you can get sent back home to your cottage if you lose all your "life." Excellent for a casual gamer who likes things that are cute but not saccharine.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game! It has an enjoyable atmosphere, amazing artwork and a simple but very engaging story. While there is a bit of back and forth to collect what you need to progress the quests, it manages to never feel tedious and kept me absorbed for hours. If I had to complain about anything, it was that it felt like it was over too quickly. It took me 10.5hrs to complete but I could have played it for much longer. Strongly recommend this if you're looking for a game to play while you relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a straightforward, relaxing, and fairly short game. The graphics are excellent and the music is fantastic! The gameplay is basically one fetch quest after another, which did get a bit monotonous, but I used this to unwind before going to sleep so I wasn't playing for long stretches of time. Worked great on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: very charming cozy game with a wonderful art style, fantastic story and dialogue, and a fun crafting aspect! if you're like me in other games with crafting aspects and ceaselessly collect materials as you traverse, then this game is perfect for you! my only gripe with it is how much backtracking there is to collect more ingredients in order to progress the story. i usually over-collect though so i didn't run into this problem as often as i could have, but it was still enough to be a little redundant. overall though a fantastic game that i could see myself replaying from time to time!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all and more than I've been looking forward to for the last year and a half. Hand-drawn cartoony graphics, relaxed atmosphere, and clear direction. I found it easy to chill with some music while playing, and while one may need grind for resources some points (such as for clay or sticks), it doesn't take very long. Overall, a relaxing rpg crafting game that will keep you entertained for the full 10-15 hours.Pros: Good soundtrack, intriguing story, nice graphics, fun gameplay.Con: The default keybindings doesn't really conform to game industry standard, but that's easy enough to change. However, the on-screen tooltips and key-press requests don't change in response to your new keybinds, so you'll have to memorize your changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great feeling for fairy tales and old children’s books. You can experience it in almost every aspect of the game, from the landscape and character/creature design, to the music and storytelling, and even the crafting-focused gameplay. You do need to be a little bit patient though. The storytelling is almost all text, and there’s a lot to read. There’s also a lot of crafting. Even though I tend to enjoy crafting in video games, I got a bit pissed off in the final hours at the number of times I had to backtrack to get one or two items. If you are regularly gathering items as you walk by them, you can eliminate a lot of backtracking but not all of it. However, the maps are small, the character moves quickly, and there are fast-travel options, so it isn’t too bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lovely fairy tale of a game. I enjoyed every moment and it was over too soon. Despite being fairly short I feel if it had been any longer it might have had more fluff to it than it needed so it was well balanced and enjoyable. Heh, I just realized that I've played for 12 hours and you collect the souls of 12 evildoers. So basically an hour for each soul.I will warn whoever might want to play this game: the thing is practically entirely fetch quest based. You find ingredients for spells, search with your witch's eye to find things that need those spells and try not to anger the wildlife enough that you faint and drop your ingredients.The story is morals based. The witch that the player takes control of is one that punishes those that take advantage of or abuse others. The art style is beautiful and exactly the kind that would be in a child's fairy tale book. I would recommend this game if you like collecting things, wandering around a world of beauty and the decay brought on by the ill actions of a few. Almost wishing the world as it is now had the witch of this story... or the goat.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Heavily focused on crafting, this colorful little title was a good time! Nothing reinvented here, simply another solid entry into the indie genre. The protagonist was written well, and had an effortless air to her. The story, though I wouldn't call it rich, was well-crafted and enjoyable. The ending felt a little jarring, but I can't think of how it could have been more satisfying, so I'm not bothered. It's a one-and-done title, so I'd recommend a sale price, but I still recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Too much grind. I'm not talking about a grind like graveyard keeper. This game has cute drawing, yes, and a pretty good story. But sadly, it is not fun enough. The game is easy, have no puzzles at all, can be used to kill time, but pretty much that's it. There is too much stuff that needs you to go back and forth, and they take so much time even with the fast travels. The game might not be too long, but I'm sure it could be shorter. Absurd amount of materials needed for each quest's each part, and every single one of them needs absurd amount of walking and meaningless grinds. For grinding each material, you also have to grind each material to collect the material you need. I will probably play more to finish because I want the achievements, but you probably shouldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first two thirds of the game, until I reached the last third and it got tedious. I became tired of crafting and how extended each chapter was. The art was beautiful, and exploring the world was nice. The going-back-and-forth from one area to another to craft a stupid item for a task in a very far place is just annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting and fun story line with a lot of just desserts served. I really enjoyed the game play, involved but relatively no stress. The music and the visuals are captivating and have a great balance of relaxing and creepy vibes. They do a really great job of building up your spells over time so they are easy to utilize. I also really appreciated that each area was set up in a way so you could work several different quest lines at once in an organized fashion. I really hope they do a part two. The ending left a lot to be desired. But maybe that was their goal? Great game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I really waited for this game for a long time.Still love the art, but was completely dissappointed with the story and the mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: A really fun point-and-click style game but with crafting. The music and art style are really charming, the crafting was fun but with the right level of challenge. I wish you learned more about your character as the game went along but it pays off in the end. There was only a few little glitches nearing the end of the play-through but nothing game breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game for everyone.  This game is for people like me who like crafting fetch quests in an immersive interesting story.  I played it all in one sitting because I enjoyed it so much.It is really low stakes, has no combat and the challenge really comes from knowing how to gather resources effectively. If that interests you, play this game.  If not,skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the game. Although, it is A LOT of running around I found the game very relaxing. I read other reviews talking about the stories of the people around you in the game. Yes, the stories start off sad and grim but through your actions you better the places you play in and overall make the people happy. The "killing" thing, yes you kill things such as birds, fireflies, rabbits, and things but I personally didn't mind it. I found this game so addicting and found the running around and "doing chores" (as one review put it) a very nice way to relax after work and it played very well for stream. It definitely is a game of you're gonna LOVE it or HATE it. I'd best compare this to an indie 3rd person minecraft without the building.
