_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Cozy, casual game with an incredible amount of busywork.After waking with no memories of who she is or how she got there, a hedge witch makes a deal with an old goat to collect twelve souls in exchange for her memories ... that is, if the goat can be trusted ... which he most assuredly cannot.The first thing that struck me about Wytchwood is the bright color palette and soothing background music. The game depicts what *should* be an upbeat cheery experience but once a player gets into it, they will find a surprisingly dark story awaiting. The souls are represented by anthropomorphic animals, such as a drunken bear, a cult-leader snake, and a doctor leech with questionable medical ethics. None of the souls needed are appealing or sympathetic characters and are all jerks to some degree. I enjoyed engineering their downfall and the overarching narrative was interesting too. The goat tasks the player with three groups of four soul quests at a time, though the four in a given cluster can be tackled in whatever order the player wishes.Gameplay is simple enough, with WASD direction control, mouse clicks to execute actions, and keys for interactions and journals. It's an easy game to immediately pick and get into. The "witch vision" key (default G) is one of the more important, as using it will give the players clues as to how solve puzzles and defeat enemies. In an overall sense, the game's flow is low-key and easy to get into, and pretty relaxing.Resources will need to be collected in order to reap each of the twelve souls, and resources and tools are found laying around the Forest (the first area encountered outside the player's home) and subsequent regions. There are a handful of hostile beasts, each with their own weaknesses uncovered by witch vision. All will show flashing skulls over their head when about to attack but are pretty simple to avoid. The player has three hearts of health (which can be easily healed with common resources); if all three are lost, the witch spawns back at her hut, having dropped some resources (which can be picked up at the scene of death). I never came close to dying and you probably won't either. I wouldn't call the game difficult by any stretch.I would say the whole thing was *too* easy if not for the tremendous amount of repetition the player will have to do. The items required to complete each soul quest start off simply enough but by the last group of four quests, the recipes have complex, layered requirements often requiring the player revisit multiple areas to gather what is needed. Sometimes, this involves having to gather resources to craft a monster trap, to get something from that monster, to get something from another monster, to built the thing you need to unlock a single component ... and all of these steps are scattered across the same regions you've been over fifteen times already. (Hint: build tons of smoke bombs and collect lots of mosquito beaks (needles) in the Swamp because fricking everything seems to require Sewing Kits as a component.) The back-and-forth grew very old, very quickly, to the point where even though it only took me 11 hours to finish the game, I could only stand to do it in 45 min increments, because I couldn't take the running back and forth any more than that.Overall, the game ran smooth, and felt polished and tested. I didn't encounter any bugs or errors. Sound design was pretty good as well.There are fourteen Steam achievements, all of which will be unlocked in the course of story play, so getting to 100% on this one is a given, if you finish.Wytchwood is a cozy, simple game with pretty dark undertones. Players may get tired of the constant back-and-forth but by breaking it up, I found it a good game to unwind with.Pros- Smooth, crisp graphics and sound, and zero bugs- Interesting narrative storylineCons- Unforgivable amount of backtracking- No real challengeFinal Score: 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a negative thumbs up review.  If you love grindy collecting/crafting games, you should pick this up cheap (20$ is a little silly, not for the duration but the lack of depth).  This is a very standard resource pyramid "lather, rinse, repeat" game with a shallow whimsical story.  It's well made, but there's no sliding grind window (i.e. collecting low level ingredients never gets easier and they continue to be required for endgame objectives), no real puzzles per se, no skill involved, and nothing to break up the fetch quest monotony beyond cute art. I accidentally mitigated the monotony by being a little obsessive with collecting everything I saw whenever I saw it for awhile, so some late objectives were trivial (given that I didn't need to backtrack to get "old" ingredients, but by the middle third of the game, I was more annoyed than excited when I got a new objective.  I just KNEW it would force me back to old content to collect random crap, presumably to pad playtime, as there was no "brain tickle" or challenge involved.I was motivated to finish it until I got to the final third... when I realized that even the core spine wasn't going to narrow towards the end and would just be "more more more".  To be honest, I'm not sure why they didn't make ten more 4 part chunks, as there was no new design or progression at any point.  Same mechanics.  Same grind.  Same lack of depth.My positive review is for the 5 hours of genuine engagement I got from the first segment.  Beyond that, I was mostly annoyed.  Five hours of charm as part of a humble bundle or 60% off sale is pretty solid.  Beyond that, it's very form over substance with lazy design.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I enjoy it. It's really beautiful, the characters are fun, it's pretty well done. I have very minor "complaints" that aren't even really complaints about the game itself, just some little things I could do without the trouble of. For example, I have to play it on the lowest graphics quality or else it lags like crazy and I get a lot of rubber banding. Not a super big deal, just a bit odd for such a simple game. If you like games where you have free reign to explore and do whatever you want, this maybe isn't for you? You have set, specific goals and that is the only focus of the game. You get a task, you do it, and it leads to another task. You find the ingredients you need, make the thing, repeat, repeat, repeat. I don't mind this so much simply because I am the kind of person who needs the dopamine hit from getting an achievement, and you will get all achievements by just playing. You also don't get much instruction for each task, you just have to figure things out yourself, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, it just made me feel a little dumb with how long it took me to figure out that I would get the recipe I needed just by using my Witch Eye on the object of my goal. I kept searching for ingredients and tried repeatedly to talk to an NPC hoping it would come to me.I think it may be easier for me to focus on the "negative" aspects just because it isn't what I was expecting (always read the reviews!), but it's actually pretty dang good, and a great way to pass the time. I'm going to continue playing, hopefully I'll finish it in a decent amount of time, as I am trying to work my way through a few games I recently purchased.I love cute, cozy indie games, and this fits into that category. I think it is worth a try for anyone who enjoys games in that genre. I got it on sale, I'm sure I would have eventually got around to buying it if it never went on sale. I give this game 8.5/10 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: + The art is stunningly beautiful and super unique. It's an absolut pleasure to just look at it. + The soundtrack is very good as well, the tracks for the different areas are all super fitting and the music overall does contribute a lot to the relaxing atmosphere this game has. + The story is entertaining and interesting. A lot of it seems to be based on fairytales, which is not something you see every day, but the story is not without some hints to modern-day, real problems. + The dialogues are well-written and pretty funny at times. I especially love that the witch is not a "blank slate" of a protagonist, but has personality and snark.~The gameplay is serviceable, but nothing groundbreaking. Collect resources, craft X. Use X to craft Y. Use Y to solve problem. If you have played the demo, you have seen all gameplay elements - use this to judge if it might bore you to spend a whole gaming doing this stuff. I didn't mind it as much, but that question is up to personal taste. ~ The game is pretty short. That alone is not necessarily a downside, but a lot of time of that is also spent backtracking and fast-travelling, meaning the actual game is even shorter. I finished the game in 13 hours, but I also left it open at times where I left my computer and I had to backtrack a lot. I imagine that with a little bit of planning and no interruptions, you could probably finish this game in a single session. - The balancing between the game's resources are a bit off in my opinion. There are resources that you will need only once in the entire game and there are ones that you will needs loads of (looking at you, Skeeter Snoots). But when you encounter a new resource for the first time, you usually can't know which it's going to be, which makes it very hard to plan ahead strategically and leads to a lot of backtracking for resources you didn't know you'd need more of. - The way quests are written doesn't mesh well with some gameplay aspects. More than once, I returned to a quest point with freshly gathered resources, only to find out that the next step of the quest would send me back right to the area that I just returned from. That leads to a lot of fast-traveling and backtracking, which gets a bit tiring. All in all, if you're looking for a "short but sweet", atmospheric story experience I definitely recommend this game. If you are looking for in-depth gameplay systems, maybe look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: The art and story crafting are impeccable, it's a really great game for those who just want to relax and enjoy going through the story at their own pace. I really had fun playing this and would definitely recommend it!However eventually the crafting starts feeling a bit like a chore. I think the developers are onto something great with the gameplay but I can't help but think about how many things they could add to make the player experience better and the gameplay slightly more interesting. For instance it would have been great to be able to bookmark recipes and have a quick crafting system without having to open the inventory. I would have liked to also have multiple quests tracked at the same time. The witch's hut was really cool, but there was no reason to go there ever. The crafting would have been more engaging if you would require making crafting tools like a furnace or a cooking pot, and having to go back to your hut from time to time to use those tools.Finally, a simple combat system would have been so fun! Like some sort of dungeon where mobs drop loot and you can find gems and rare items. It would be a perfect way to introduce an equipment system as well, finding items in the dungeon that you can wear to boost certain stats like moving slightly faster, attacks do more damage, you have a chance to craft twice the item, etc.Finally if we really want to take it a step further, you could introduce potions as well! Of course the focus would still stay on crafting but it would have been fun to diversify the way some items can be found or crafted as the story progressed.All that to say that... this game has so much potential and I can't wait to see what the devs do next. Happy crafting!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Demonic story line, Dark and creepy stories, false advertising, not safe for easily disturbed or childrenI was super excited for this game, It was advertised and discussed as a "Stardew Valley Like" game. The online page mentions the "Gothic fables and fairytales," and highlights the adventures. Such as, "Research and concoct devious spells and sorceries. Turn the greedy into frogs! Trick the wicked with cunning curses! Explore an allegorical world of tall tales, uncovering colourful personas and fantastical narratives." To put it plainly: BULLCRAP! The graphics are cutsie. That is about the only wholesome or casual part of this game. Don't get me wrong, I love Gothic fairytales and dark twists, who doesn't; this game isn't it. I DO NOT recommend this game to anyone under 18 and I feel it should come with several warnings, such as "Demonic in nature" and "Warning, Flashing Lights." For those not convinced please read below, the following will contain SPOILERS!!!!!!!!I don't understand how some people can focus on the repetitive mechanics of the game and completely miss the story line. Yes, the three "little" pigs, and red riding hood did appear in this game. But it wasn't in a fairy-tale way. First off you begin the game talking to a goat; Who wants you to find twelve souls; To then save the soul of a young maiden. Kinda weird but okay, I was sure the souls would be bad. I had no idea those souls were pure evil. Turns out the Three Pigs run a pig farm, where they force peasants to work for them, starve them until they are unable to work, then feed them ALIVE to the pigs. The Pigs then proceed to butcher their farm animals and sell them at the market. All throughout the game there are hints at a demonic tone, a witch dancing naked on blood with a man under the moon and raising the dead to scare the town, for example. What should have been a lovable, Gothic and adventurous game became us working for the devil to collect souls for him. The game starts bad and gets worse. I am ashamed to admit I finished this game out of the minuscule hope that it would redeem itself. It didn't; instead the game ends unsatisfactory, and confusing. I have bought cheaper games that lasted me twice as long. Please, if you want a fun adventurous game, look elsewhere. Do NOT let CHILDREN play this game, it gets very DARK. I will be attempting to return this game, it wasn't worth my time, money, or investment.

Crafting was more of a supplementary thing to the story for the first 8 souls, and I was happy to go to another place, collect some materials, and maybe pick up some new quests in that area at the same time. The side hustle did not subtract from the story much. But for the last 4 souls, you had to craft a big thing about every step into the story, and that really drowned out the atmosphere. Some crafting materials didn't even make that much sense and it felt like they were there just to make things more tedious. _childDocuments_.review: I have never written a review for any game, nor was I planning on it... but this game deserves at least a recommendation. I fell in love with the art style, the dialogues are intelligent, witty, whimsical and carry the story so well, the world feels so alive because of this, despite the very simple gameplay of "gather this, craft this to gather the other thing to then craft the thing you need". This might sound tedious and you will do a lot of walking but nothing feels far away, despite the world being decently sized and very versatile. The gathering and crafting is very satisfying and feels rewarding throughout the game, so does the collecting of souls of the meanies... I especially want to mention the music in this game, it is gorgeous, underlining each section perfectly without ever being unpleasantly overwhelming. Especially their rendition of "Spanish Ladies" put a smile on my face when I first heard it (and every time after that). There's only a minor thing I would've liked to see solved differently with the navigation through the Grimoire, maybe like highlighting the required recipes for the quest you are tracking and such but honestly, it didn't diminish my enjoyment of the game at all, would've just been personal preference. Very rarely would I replay a game but Wytchwood feels like a game I would love to go back to in the future."Thank you for playing Wytchwood" - No, thank you for making this game! Just lovable.

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a nice and beautiful resource gathering and crafting game. Still, I found myself wanting to come back to the world and see what else I could make and who else I might run into. I would recommend for a cute and low effort game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game with a beautifully-imagined gothic whimsy that slowly drip-feeds its darkness bit by bit as the story goes along. The abrupt ending feels a little out of sorts given the tone and story-telling leading up to it, but there remains a sense of palpable melancholy and the game earns that tone by the end.Mechanically, while the crafting is a mostly engaging twist on the adventure genre, there's not much mystery or puzzle required for the solutions. Recipes are revealed to the player as the scenario requires them, and while some of them are easily dispatched, the late game requires what feels like an unnecessary amount of farming for ingredients. This itself isn't an issue on its own, but even with fast travel there is a lot of late-game backtracking and no hint whatsoever what ingredients you'll need until the moment you need them.Ultimately, it's worth the time spent on it and I suggest going ahead and playing through it for the experience. There's some unnecessary foot-dragging on the endgame that doesn't really pay off as much as it feels it should, but the overall experience is uniquely compelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a short, quirky game that has an excellent foundation of gameplay and a fabulous art style. Some aspects can feel overly stretched out and some pieces feel less developed than others. By the end of the game, you'll feel irate at the wasted potential with this.If you're looking for a game to wile away a few hours and one that lets your magpie brain go wild whilst looking pretty, look no further. However, don't expect the game to blow your socks off.There's not many games I feel the need to review, yet Wytchwood's potential has me so irate that I felt compelled to leave some feedback. After completing the game, I would recommend it, but there are a few caveats to that below.For starters, the graphical style is wonderful to this game. I truly loved the environments throughout and I really enjoy the tiny world that has been weaved together here. Even in spaces that're underutilised, it feels like the developers took time and care to put the set pieces together. Toddling around in the world as the Witch, I felt myself smiling at all the little pieces.In terms of gameplay, I think the foundation of the game is solid. Fetch quests are some of the most tedious in games, but pottering along in the game and working along the lines created by the crafting system felt cosy almost. At its fundamental, the developers hit onto a nice sweet spot for the start, although it lets itself down as the game goes on (see below)The story elements as well are terrific. Whilst not all Twelve Souls are equally weighted, there are some shining examples in there. I truly loved the inventive pieces in the game -  . I also loved the strong characterisation that can be found throughout the game - the Souls had personalities and felt well written in this regard.If there could be a tagline for this game, it would be "Stretched out unnecessarily". Between unused spaces in the map, filler Souls who felt like they had to be brushed away quickly and a lack of progression in how you collect items past Act 1, it feels like the developers were constantly just trying to make the game longer for no reason. This is frustrating to me as there were the beginnings of great ideas in this  that then just got tossed to the wayside to make way for padding the game instead. This potential is absolutely there and I wish it had been explored more within the game. It also just felt like it held hands too much at times.  I much prefer a game to show and not tell - I want to work this out for myself! Those small areas of spoonfeeding feel disappointing, as they take away player agency and leave you feeling like you accidentally pressed a skip button.I really enjoyed this game, make no mistake about that. It took me a few sittings, but I made sure to complete it. I wanted to see the end of this and I'm keen to see the developers update further . I'm happy with the £15~ I spent on this game, but would probably recommend to pick it up for £10.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game has been a lovely experience so far and I've had such a hard time putting it down. The art style is wonderful and the writing has made me chuckle a number or times. It's an extremely cozy game but not a game for everyone. This is THE collectathon to end all collectathons. You will be running back and forth gathering spell components even if you think you should have enough. It can certainly get tedious at times. If you play the game I HIGHLY recommend you grab, cut, catch, and chop everything you can as you see it. Functionally, this is my main criticism of the game. It would be nice if the devs increased drop rates of actions. Or maybe there should be an easter egg spell that makes all resources infinite but it can only be used once. I also wish that I didn't have to manually switch between tools to perform certain actions. Don't take my frusturations as a dislike of the game. No game is perfect. I love what I've played a lot and I really do think it's worth the time spent with it.For those curious, I have been playing this on Steam Deck and while it's able to hit 60fps most of the time, a handful of ares in the game seem to drop the framerate to about 40fps. I'd recommend switching to 40hz anyways for the battery life.

_childDocuments_.review: You wake up, memories gone, recipes got eaten by this Goat. This Goat tells you that you have made a contract with them, to save a soul in exchange for 12. Sounds like a terrible deal? But what if these souls are all terrible beings? Slavery, arrogance, mischief, lies, murder, you name it. This game gives an interesting storytelling experience, with a beautiful art style and nice music to go with it. It references multiple fairy tales, but as a dummy I can only recognize two tales myself. The others give me strong fairy tale vibes but I just could not figure out the references right away. The controls are relatively easy and you can pretty much point-and-click the entire game if you wish.The major downside is the amount of back and forth's you will have to make if you do not have a habit of hoarding items. I learned that the hard way myself, but once I started farming for the basic items to craft more advanced spells and reagents, the number of times I need to go around to collect ingredients reduces.I would recommend this game to people who like point-and-click adventures with a lot of crafting and ingredient collecting. Perhaps get it when it is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is interesting, because it gets into the difference between a game that I like and a good game. And I did like it, but I can't recommend it.In Wytchwood, you're a witch, who wakes up one morning to find herself put to a mysterious task by a mysterious figure, and in the process interact with a world drawn up of fairy tale imagery and characters. The gameplay is straight forward, a sort of perpetual fetch quest of you collecting items to make up other items, with the span of what items you need expanding as the game progresses. And it's fine. The art is distinctive, the music is good but the musical loops too small, so it becomes cloying, the story is well-written and ends strongly, but is a bit confused, it's a sort of dark fairy tale mashup without the whole getting greater than the sum of the parts. The game play is solid, I see 'casual' used in a lot of reviews, and that fits, and I appreciate that there are anti-frustration measures put into the design. There's a teleport function I never used because getting back and forth across the map was never a thing. But it maybe gets too casual. Like I understand that most of the time it's about collecting whatever, but sometimes it leaves you with a puzzle and I wanted more of those moments...except in how it doesn't ever leave you with a puzzle. I like something coming along and giving me a hint, but I don't like it if it shows up on my second try. As such, the game sort of ends up being about the game that you make for yourself of playing it, and I varied between trying to optimize route and quest progression to have everything tiered up efficiently to sort of maximizing with a full load of inventory so that I could take on whatever thing right away. In short, a well-designed game, fun if it's what you're looking for, maybe a little expensive, but frustrating in how it feels like a better, more engaging game that the designers stepped back from.

_childDocuments_.review: MAC SPECIFICThe game is really glitchy on Mac. I would call it borderline unplayable. When I opened it initially, the mouse cursor was literally unusable. With some toggling of settings, I was able to get the game to run, but the controls are very difficult to use. Especially in combination with a lengthy map to run back and forth on and no way to distinguish the enemies that attack if you get too close, the game got very frustrating when I died due to control issues or lag and had to walk all the way back. I also struggled to use the tools or pick up items, because the controls completely lack precision. In a tool-heavy, material-collection-heavy game, this is a bit of an issue...The added issues with being able to use items and move around precisely (my character sort of staggers back and forth like a drunk sailor) on top of valid criticism of the repetition of the game and lack of teleportation mechanics for the map make it a lot less fun. I really hope they work further on the quality of the controls and mechanics, because it seems like reviews were generally quite positive for the Windows version. With a fairly saturated market of excellent cozy games that run well on Mac, it's hard to for this game to stand out. I love the art style and I love quest-based puzzle games, but I would not recommend this game for Mac users, especially at the price point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that understands the quiet compulsion to got out and Collect All Of The Things.All  of the resources. All of the harvestables.All of them. Every last one. And then go reload the zone so you can do it again.It will give you a *gorgeous* world to run around in while you pick All Of The Flowers and dig up All Of The Dirt and cut All Of The Logs. When you've gathered All Of The Things and made them into All Of The New Things, it will reward you with a new set of funny dialogue, and new glorious character portraits. And then give you Even More Things to find and make and refine and turn in. All while giving you a solid story to keep the cycle feeling like it's furthering something larger than your simple need to eliminate all interactable objects from the game board. At the time of this writing, the top-rated review for this game calls it a fetch-quest simulator. That's fair, to a degree. If what I've written above sound like a tiny hell, then this is probably not the game for you. However, if you're the kind of person who finds peace in gathering up a stock of supplies--and then gets a huge burst of joy from being over-prepared for the fetch quest and being able to make the complicated object right there and then--grab this. Even at full price. It scratches all of those itches, and will look *damn* good while being there to support you and love you for your self-soothing compulsive tendencies. Be the sarcastic, no-nonsense bog witch you want to see in the world. You, too, can gather three skeeter snoots with one smoke bomb.

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a simple but satisfying puzzle-adventure game, with a beautiful art style, delightful music, and entertaining writing.  The game absolutely nails its chosen aesthetic, creating a world that looks like a living pop-up picture book, a setting which is engaging and largely painless to navigate. Each of the twelve sequences that make up the story are little fairy tale fables in their own right, most with their own little twist to mix up the narrative. While the process of gathering and crafting ingredients to solve each "puzzle" involves very little actual challenge, completing a new step is still satisfying thanks to the amusing item descriptions, witch-y story logic, and interactions and animations. I found myself drawn to chase down "one more step" in each sequence every time I booted the game up; while the ending is abrupt, it's otherwise extremely well-paced.There's no replay value here, but the game doesn't really need it. I firmly recommend Wytchwood to anyone who enjoys twisty fairy tales, lovely drawn art, crotchety witch protagonists, and brewing bizarre solutions to odd obstacles. It's a very comfy way to kill eight or nine hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I preface this with: This is BARELY a negative review. It would absolutely be a positive review if my (singular) complaint were to be addressed but it really took me out of the game. You've heard it before, almost every review mentions it: this game is FILLER. the majority of the time you are backtracking through areas you've backtracked through several times before to get more ingredients. This would be fine, as a lot of the time the collecting can be fun- i've always had a fondness of "preparedness" games where you are expected to collect random bits while you are in the area "just in case". However, in this game it goes a touch beyond that. I find myself constantly stripping every area dry of all the resources i can while i'm there, and still consistently run out. I've some suspicion it is a bug of some sort making items disappear from my inventory, but i've no evidence. The problem is, some basic recipes cost TOO MANY resources. something costing 3 or 4 of an ingredient is fine if you don't do it often,  but if it's a basic recipe you do hundreds of times it gets frustrating. If you are like me, in the early portion of the game it will be a breeze, you'll have enough of everything collected as you need it because you thought to grab enough while you were there, experimented as you found new things etc... But with each act the problem grows more and more evident as this game slips from calming, funny and cute into true tedium. Many of the other reviews look past this flaw and mention all of the positives of the game, and i urge you to read those as well as the game really is charming and has a lot going for it, but it needs some serious tweaking. I like many others find myself quitting the game in frustration every time i'm given a new laundry list of things, most of which i have collected dozens and dozens of times before and still have managed to run out. TLDR: the "flow" of the game is constantly broken due to endless fetch quest misery and recipes costing too much. God, some quests you'll need to go back and forth into Forest to get enough fireflies because you suck them all dry and only get 3 tinderboxes out of it and still need more plus shiny charms.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid game. I got through it in 13 hours and enjoyed it thoroughly. The environments are vivid and varied, the mechanics are satisfying (FINALLY a crafting game where I never have to worry about inventory space), and the language is rich and enticing. I want to roll this game in my mouth and crunch down on it. The stories told remind me a lot of Grimm fairytales, with their casual violence and themes of evil-doers getting their comeuppance in a poetic way. Everything is just so filled with character, most of all the protagonist, but it never became overbearing for me. Highly recommend for playing after work/school for a couple of hours to wind down. Regarding the ending: *vague spoilers below*It was certainly upsetting and unexpected, but after sitting with it for a little bit, it made a lot of sense narratively. After spending the whole game tricking people into doing your bidding, it felt somehow appropriate to kind of feel tricked as the player. Days later, I'm still thinking of moments that were clear foreshadowing that went right over my head. It's so unfair, but I just have to appreciate the craft.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the style, the main character and the story - very well written! Prepare yourself to be asked to fetch this and fetch that, and as you progress in the story, you will quickly find that the things you need to fetch, will take A LOT of different items for you to craft. This basically means that you will have to do A LOT of backtracking through the different zones. You may want to kill this creature, sure, BUT you will need this item to do so, and in order to craft  said item, you will have to go to THAT zone AND SO ON. So be prepared to remember where you will get each kind of drop/item. I bought this game for a bargain and I honestly really enjoyed it, but the further I progressed in the story, the more backtracking I had to do.. and it became old, not gonna lie. However, take some breaks from the game, this is not one to finish in one long sitting (as the game can be completed in 10 hours time), and just take it for what it is. It is a well made game, and with a little thinking you won’t need to ask the great interwebs for help to find the different items, this I really appreciated. All in all it was pretty logical what you were supposed to do. Achievements are also very straightforward.All in all, I is a happy little wytch <3

_childDocuments_.review: A really lovely story-driven gathering/crafting game. I really enjoyed the quests and the stories they told. The art style is fun, the different regions feel unique, and the crafting is satisfying. There's a tiny bit of combat, mostly avoid the obvious enemy attack, and no real penalty for dying. There's a bit of back tracking required to gather ingredients but with everything labeled by zone and lots of map markers for quests it isn't painful.If this is your type of game, then 100% recommended.====================Minor gameplay notes (no spoilers)  1) If you find yourself unable to interact with or harvest anything, exit the game completely and start it again. Happened to me once.  2) If you are asked for something you don't have the recipe for, use your inspect tool and hover over the person/thing asking for it. Happened to me 2 or 3 times.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: First and Foremost I want to say that I really LOVE this game's Sound effects and visuals. In terms of the sound effects i'm comfortable to say that it's one of the most impressive sound effects in video games I have ever heard. For example your character travels different themed worlds and lets say you happen to pass through the forest, so you'd hear the birds chirping and the people around you whistling to themselves. Then you'd pass through the graveyard and you'd ghost eerily in the background and people crying. It really puts you in the MOOD of the game of what it's trying to develop for you emotionally. After beating the game and getting all of the achievements, I am still impressed by the sound effects. Maybe some people may play this game and not even care of that kind of stuff, but it made my experience much enjoyable. The soundtrack of this game definitely compliments the vibe of each and every world that you visit, and the compose who worked on the soundtrack really did an absolutely fantastic job. I have leaned a lot of from this game, and what I have learned is that there are deceitful people. People that unfortunately get corrupted by greed. Through greed, well people get affected by that. Some people even die because of it. You play as  Witch who is contracted to bring souls of these corrupted anthropomorphic animals (12 to be exact). Throughout each an every world and journey, you're task to craft items and potions to give and take and trade with the common people, and people of royalty to get the items you need to take down the corrupted characters and bring peace among each village and worlds. Every world has a specific problem that is being caused by the antagonist of that world, and you learn of the peoples suffering and what caused it to begin with. There was a chapter that really was relatable to me, there is a group of characters by the farm side that is dealing with a tenant that keeps raising the rent which they cannot afford only because they want to replace them with someone who could afford. That kind of stuff really puts me in the shoes of those characters. It makes me feel sad for them, but of course with the helping of the Witch. You find a way to get around this problem and outsmart the greedy tenant. Sometimes the answer is not in clear sight in our lives, and we need someone to show us what that answer may be. In this case it's the witch who does all these deeds to help people in the game, but of course at the same time this witch is doing these kind of stuff because he's looking towards the ultimate goal at hand. That goal is to bring the 12 souls to the Goat that lives near your home right next to a shrine where the Sleeping maiden rest.The story is very unique, and the visuals is remarkable. I wanted to live in this world for a moment it's that good. Basically everything checks off right with the sound effects, music, and visuals.Still the main core of the game is to craft items, and crafting is really the meat of the game. Sometimes you're gonna catch up with a character that demands separate items from you and you wont have the items ready. So you're gonna have to do a lot of tracking to get those items. The game makes it sort of easy for you to backtrack by giving you portals which allows you to get to the other worlds easier. There's also an item called the Hearthseed that Allows to transport yourself back home and I have used this item several times whenever I would get lost or was too lazy to walk to the next world. People in the review sections don't seem to mention that in the comments. Still I do agree that this game can get grind heavy with the crafting and backtracking.So I only recommend this game to a certain specific type of player. Obviously people who are into crafting games, but I'm not even crafting myself. Still this game got me hooked on the story, aesthetic, and of course the sound effects are really out of this world. I think the asking price of this game is fair, and I'd totally recommend this game. I really enjoyed it, I hope you do as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game, it really felt like playing within a storybook! The art, bgm and effects, story, and dialogues were all really pleasing. My only complaint was that the ending was in my opinion, anticlimactic and I wish there was more to the witch and maiden if that makes sense. Overall, what it says on the tin (game description) is really what you get. If you like chill, cozy, foraging and crafting, and casual gaming I recommend this :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game caught my eye thanks to the beautiful art style. As a painter, seeing the different scenes, characters, and environments had me wanting to recreate them on canvas on more than one occasion! Not only that, but the narration and character dialogue is SO well written. Clever, bumbling, funny, tragic, sassy, sweet - a wonderful assortment of personalities to discover. I also loved the story line - there's a bit of a twist that had me surprised and satisfied with the ending.Saying all that, I did have one pretty substantial problem going through this game that others have already mentioned...the game play loop.It took me 12 hours to finish Wytchwood, and a hefty chunk of that was simply running back and fourth to gather ingredients. This was fine to begin with, but around midway I found myself dreading having to go back to one area I had just returned from to gather a different item. No matter how much I tried to prepare by running around each area gathering extra resources, I still always found myself needing to go back here or there for *something*. Nearing the last few hours of playtime, I had to quit playing early on a few occasions because another list of ingredients I'd be missing would be sprung on me after I spent the last 30 minutes gathering a different list. It becomes rather monotonous after a few hours. After being through all of the areas, I grew tired of having to track back to them so frequently. Yes, there is a fast travel mechanic, but there is often a lot of space between travel locations that still must be walked through to access them.I really believe if this repetitive resource gathering had been mitigated somehow, like being able to buy more of the ingredients with the gold coins we collect, or trade in one resource for another at a trading post, that this would be in my list of favourite games. It's my one and only complaint; everything else was absolutely wonderful, and I really have enjoyed this game and what it has to offer.Definitely give Wytchwood a try - it's worth it in the end. If you're worried about the aforementioned issue, my suggestions would be to have a resource guide handy, have shorter play sessions to break up the monotony, and to take your time in each area to best avoid having to return to them as often as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed every minute of Wytchwood! It is a collectathon as others have said, but that was perfect for me. I got that nice feeling of accomplishment every time I crafted something and finished a quest. It is handy to be able to work on multiple quests at once and change which one you're tracking. The story is rich, and the graphics are beautiful. There need to be more games where you get to play a no-nonsense bird witch!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and peaceful game. I saw people saying 20 hours, but for me it was a little over 10. This probably has more to do with my in-game hoarding tendencies than anything else. If you're like a magpie and love collecting shiny things like I do, this might be a good game for you. The pros: -SUPER beautiful art. Just feel happy looking at it. -Engaging storylines with lots of interesting characters-Fabulous writing-Collecting base ingredients is fun!-Just an overall relaxing game.The cons: -There are no cons. For what this game is, for what I think it's meant to be, it's 99% perfect. And that 1% docked is just because I noticed a couple of spelling errors in the dialogue that threw me out of the game for a moment because I'm a nerd.The more I think about it, the more I liked the ending as well. I could spend more time going around and playing just for the vibes of the game, so I guess I could say I wish it was longer or had a new game +. Maybe I'll replay it anyway. Overall a very lovely and tranquil experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a beautiful and soothing indie game. The design and art is gorgeous while the story is fun and intriguing. _childDocuments_.review: 8/10The art style and OST of the game are astounding. The title screen song is so serene, easy to relax and nap to! The story was compelling, and progressed well enough to keep wanting to play a little more. The first four souls introduce you to four large places to scour for crafting ingredients. The second four souls introduce to you four more new areas to do the same while making their introduction not a tedious undertaking. The last four souls you go to collect... it felt slapped on and gated content in areas in existing opened content. The stories surrounding the final four souls also didn't carry the same complexity as the previous eight. I spent perhaps two hours rounding up for the last four souls while the previous eight were 17 hours. The crafting in the game was very creative in making use of everything you could pick up, but some of the items were crafted one or two times only for the sake of story progression. Without knowing how far you have come in the game, it's easy to waste time overstocking on materials after repeated trips back for only one of a special ingredient (I'm looking at you, dryad fruit). Having no completion percentage displayed was likely the root of this game taking so long to complete as I expected a game triple the length due to how complex the ingredients were becoming to obtain. I was massively fooled, and likely a subsequent play through could be done in an afternoon. That said, I still stand by 8/10. It's worth playing. The ending wasn't what I was expecting up until the last lines of dialog. I appreciate how close to the heart the plot was until the final breath. Bravo. There's room for a prequel/sequel with the conclusion of Wytchwood. Here's too hoping!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, fun, charming game that I thoroughly enjoyed. The story is well thought out and linear in a way that it doesn't leave you wanting for more. The villains are clear cut, the player character is fun and has a realistic personality for an old witch (absolutely adore her little crow like feet) and it didn't drag out the plot. Highly recommend this game to anyone who'd like to try out a highly stylized crafting and visual novel-esque game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really 50/50 with this game. I had a love/hate relationship with it. Love that slowly turned to hate. -Keep in mind there are 3 main parts to the game. I played it in 3 separate sittings over 3 days. And this is still my opinion even then...-I gotta say I thought the reviews were exaggerating when they complained about the grind. I felt the story was fun and cute. Not even that bad. For 2/3 of it, anyway... In the middle of the 2nd of 3 parts, I noticed it getting longer. The third half became even LONGER, tedious, dragged out. It started feeling like a huge chore and I would groan and sigh at every item requirement. I found myself becoming impatient and eager to finish the game. Loved the art. Music. Story, for the most part. It was creative and fun. But they definitely took a "we hate people and want them to suffer" approach in the last third of the game...I'm glad I played it because it definitely was fun. But it's also one of those games that you find reaaally hard to finish. Play it if you have patience. Don't if you lack it....
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a spooky cozy game. It is a relatively quick game (it only took me 14 hours to complete). This is a collecting/crafting game and heavy story-line based. The story-line is a bit predictive but still very enjoyable. You play as a witch who gives villains their comeuppance, which is satisfying. The items you can collect/craft are unique. _childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game has beautiful visuals and intriguing story. The characters are interesting and leave you itching for more answers- a very delightful spin on the fairy tale genre. Our own player character also has some great punchlines and her personality is charming.But if you're looking for innovative game mechanics, look elsewhere. I have several issues with this game. I was under the impression of having a more choice driven game as well, but whatever a player does has no impact on the actual plot. It's also incredibly tedious with its fetch quest, they can get and the lack of directions can leave players easily lost. The tutorial was bare-bones at best and I spent half my time going back and forth to get just one item from other locations I was just at one quest ago. The UI is clunky and it's hard to decipher how to meet another character's needs at times.You basically HAVE to interact with most of the characters at least once to keep the story going- adding onto the tedium. And because of the sheer amount of characters- it's hard to connect fully with any of them.I wouldn't recommend this to anyone who wants a more involved experience or gameplay loop. It has little to no replay value because it's such a heavily story-driven game. But I still would recommend it for those who don't care about any of that and just want a fun narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Too short!I don't often write reviews but Wytchwood was something straight out of a dream come true for me. For someone who adores fairytales and folklore, and has always dreamed of being a little witch woman in the woods, Wytchwood was the game I never knew I wanted. The gameplay is, as others describe, a fetch quest adventure. It's all about running around to craft A Thing that will get you Another Thing that you then use to make The Final Thing. There's a lot of doubling back and repetitive motions. The lovely artwork and fun twists on familiar tales makes the gameplay worth it. I would start and work on all the quests at once, and complete them more or less at the same time, to save myself some repeat trips to gather resources.All in all, love it - can't wait for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy is an excellent word for this game of fetch quests and crafting spells. The fairy tale influence is very present and the crotchety old witch is wonderful and grumpy in a way that felt right and fit the aesthetic. Basically this game let me live out all my witchy goblin hoarder dreams. Some of the going back and forth did start to feel tedious near the end, but the game's portals helped mitigate that, and for a ten hour game it wasn't all that bad. I will say I didn't see that ending coming, and I very much enjoyed it (even if it felt a little abrupt). If you like fairy tales or hunt and fetch games, you will adore this.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a middling score for games like this. Wytchwood suffers from a major flaw in that it's sole gameplay is "collect reagents to solve mini tasks". If you love "fetch quests" you'll like this game, because at its core mechanic, I feel that's all it is.There is no replayability once you beat it. There is little to no thought put into solving the quests as they tell you exactly what you need to resolve them. Take away that, and you spend much time 'grinding' to collect reagents and/or backtracking to zones to grind/collect more reagents. Which by the end gets exhausting more than anything. You may even want to get a guide that tells you exactly how much of each ingredient you'll need to at least cut back on backtracking.Cons out of the way, the game itself is beautiful to look at, which gorgeous music appropriate to its zones, and an intriguing enough story, about a swamp witch collecting 12 (villainous) souls for to fulfill a dark contract and being the hand of karma in the process.Combat is mostly non-existent, which is fine, this isn't designed to be a heavy combat game, but I wish it did more with it's potion craft system, or at the very least mitigated much of the grind and backtracking. At 19.99 I would hold off until this drops lower in price. It took me about 10 hours to complete, and it's a gorgeous and well-built game, but I can't ignore the cons enough to give it a thumbs up at it's current price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is set in a gloriously gorgeous setting, stylized stunningly to make one feel like they are immersed within an intricate storybook~Upon writing this review - I have just finished the first main quest of the story (which is divided into multiple parts), and adore that the gameplay is very casual - the player being able take their time to wander around, explore the world and take in all the detail - the amazing artwork, animation, sounds, soundtrack, and interface have left me in awe and anticipation for more!What I can say thus far is - if you are like me and enjoy games steeped in lore, gorgeous artwork, an astounding soundtrack and more - This game is definitely worth checking out!If you're more about the mechanics - this game is heavily crafting focused, where you will find gatherable resources abounding for crafting various tools, potions, and more to help you along on your journey~Love, love, LOVE this game so far - Well done team!

_childDocuments_.review: Collect EVERYTHING. I'm not joking. Pick up EVERYTHING. You may think, "But I already have 50 of that item in my inventory!" PICK IT UP. JUST TRUST ME. Lovely game. Cute style, easy game play, I like the lack of actual combat (you throw items that destroy the things that wanna attack you). The Witch is SO RELATABLE. _childDocuments_.review: I chose to buy this game because of it's beautiful art style, but the game itself blew away my expectations. _childDocuments_.review: The game is probably not for everyone, but it is enjoyable none the less. It boils down to a story-driven fetch quest with crafting elements. It's a lot of running back and forth to gather ingredients to make a thing to progress the story. But the art is unique, the music is very soothing in the background and adds to the different atmospheres, and the story is good enough to keep you playing. _childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bunch of fetching and crafting items.You'll need to craft items which require other craftable items and it can get tiring if you're not into it.My advice would be to hoard as much as possible, so you can avoid the need for constant backtracking.Never go through raw materials without picking them up.Overall, I think it's a good game, worth playing if you're into exploration/crafting games.There doesn't seem to be any replay value, though, because the game is very linear, and a second playthrough would probably feel very repetitive...
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I was wondering what was I going to do with my life after finishing filling up the last water bottle for the final quest of the game. Jk :)Although I see many reviews disregarding the game due to its repetitive grinding and crafting component (which reduces one’s patience to complete it in a pleasant manner — or, simply found unappealing to some), I believe there are some significant elements brought to the table by the devs, that do not receive the appreciation I believe they deserve. Most positive reviews explicit why the graphics, soundtrack and storyline have been offered in an excellent blend, colourful, engaging, inviting, and refined. So rather than insisting on why they were brilliantly executed imo, I’d like to focus more on the storyline. It’s not something never-seen, never-heard, or never-imagined before. I believe the game guides one to find some comfort in some good parables, connecting humour, bravery, morality, mortality, sacrifice, memory, kindness, justice and humanness.I believe there has been something greatly achieved through the added references of different childhood tales, tailored for the specific storyline of the game. Some Shakespeare Inspo over here, some Red Riding Hood over there, and many more, but prefer not to give unintentional spoilers for those reading the reviews first :)  If you find entertainment in a game committed to a cute storyline and don’t mind fetch quests, then most probably this one’s for you. To be honest, I believe the true value of Wytchwood resided in the details, hidden under this attractive ‘’visual’’ shell of elements. For this reason alone, Wytchwood, as a whole, should probably more likely be seen as a standard of quality for games of its kind. While impatient to open the forest well gate, standing ovation and a massive thank you for the efforts invested in this game, Alientrap

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little game for what it was. With rather simple gameplay, it's suitable for a nice evening where you just want to unwind and do something a little mindless and calming. There's lots of gathering, fetching, and crafting to be done, and this can sometimes get a little repetitive after a while. The game's story is divided into three main parts, which I think would be suitable to be played in three separate sittings to avoid burnout from running back and forth to different areas. But if you're into fetch quests, then it might not bother you that much. I'm the type to pick up everything I see as I go along, so that probably helped me some. If the game had been any longer I feel like it would've become kind of a slog, so I think game length was pretty much perfect. Gameplay aside though, I found all the characters and environments to be very enjoyable. I liked the art style a lot, and each area has a really fitting color palette for the mood it's trying to set. Each quest came with its unique set of characters, and I really enjoyed the fairy tale aspects to each story line. I kind of wish the ending had been a little more fleshed out. It did feel a bit underwhelming after all of that running around, but overall I liked it and I'm glad I picked it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I just love everything about this game. I had it on my wishlist for several years, always in my backhead and finally decided to buy it. No regrets. Mainly I kept this game in mind because of its beautiful artstyle.Sometimes it's really hard for a game to stay in my mind because I'm playing many games in a short time, but seriously, I will never forget Wytchwood. I don't know what exactly fascinates me so much, but the old witch just keeps me in her claws. This game is just 100% perfect as it is.The Storyline is a deep dive in some sad points of humanity and kept me pondering for a long time. The artstyle is just lovely and the gameplay really doesn't get boring. I have read some negative reviews that the gameplay quickly got repetitive for some. Well, yes, you are an old witch with the quest to craft different utils from resources you'll find scattered in different parts of the world. That's your only job. I don't know what an old witch would do else.For me the game neighter got boring nor repetitive. Wytchwood is a story game, so if you skip the dialogues, you wouldn't understand what exactly your doing and mainly won't catch the magic of the game.So please keep in mind that skipping the dialogues will totally ruin your experience of Wytchwood.For me, this game had some serious "indie game of the year"- potential.I'll never stop appreciating the beauty of Wytchwood.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! The story, the characters and the art were really nice. I also liked the crafting system, even though it was a bit tedious at some point when you had to craft several things just to craft the one thing you need. But I still prefer this over too much repetition and tasks that are too simple.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: It wasn't the game I was expecting, but I really enjoyed it. I had to turn motion blur off because it was making me cross eyed, but other than that the graphics are cute and the story isn't bad except it's predictable ending. It is a little grindy at times when you're collecting components, but I learned quickly just to loot everything you pass. If you need to kill something for its component, just go ahead and kill a couple. You WILL need it again!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The story is cute and clever, the crafting is varied and satisfying, and the simple characters are charming enough. As a game, Wytchwood is not difficult at all. Each quest in the main story is just a matter of finding the materials needed to craft the items that will solve a particular problem. (There is no real combat.) If you are amused by that sort of thing, you'll probably love Wytchwood. If what I've described sounds to you like a bunch of boring fetch quests, keep your distance.(By the way, for those who care ... automatic 100% achievements if you finish the game.)
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: i really like the grindy playstyle, which i've seen put some folks off. you go through and collect ingredients repeatedly, and it's fun to do. the soundtrack is beautiful, the artstyle is whimsical, and the storyline is intriguing. i'm VERY happy i got this game- it's a very good thing to just zone into and play.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: is the perfect game for the autumn season. As a witch who awakens roped into a supernatural contract and devoid of memories, you step into a beautiful, fantastical world to collect the souls of twelve local troublemakers through crafting and cunning. all 14 achievements are unmissable through story progression.The world of  is very reminiscent of children's tales such as those by the Brothers Grimm or Aesop's fables, and the game makes plenty of references to such classics while retaining its own unique approach and authenticity. The story, though only communicated through dialogue and some narration, is impressively well-written, imaginative, and overflowing with personality. You can tell that the game is a labour of love that was made by a very talented and clever team of people.You progress through exploration, collecting resources, and crafting magical items. The crafting system is fleshed out but not overly complicated, and as long as you continue to collect resources along the way, you shouldn't need to double back for missing ingredients too frequently. As you move through the story, the recipes become more complex, interconnected, and resource-intensive, but never overwhelmingly so. There is an incredible variety in ingredients, and it's very fun learning where you need to go in the world to get what you need and overcome any challenges you might face.The art and style of the game is one of its strongest points, and it is exceptional. The environments are so full and well-designed, with each location having a distinctive, cohesive theme that makes it instantly recognisable. The characters are brilliant, their portraits reflecting their personalities and motivations, and the cast is full of so many memorable figures. My personal favourite was the Leech.The music in the game is also used very well, contributing to each location's theme perfectly and completing its atmosphere. For example, I love how the track for damp, underground spaces uses sharp xylophone(?) notes to mirror the sound of dripping water. Everything in  feels purposeful and comes together to form a wonderfully unique and masterfully created world.This is a really cool and memorable little game. It's the perfect length for what it is, and every minute of it is thoroughly enjoyable. Now is a fantastic time to grab it during the autumn sale, especially as it is very fitting for this season.If you like any of the following games, this is an especially strong recommendation (or if you have played  and are looking for something similar): - very similar visual style; collecting and crafting; character-based storylines. - very similar visual style; collecting and crafting. -  very similar visual style. - similarly charming 2D style; cozy autumnal feeling. - charming 2.5D style; similar light puzzle elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games! I loved exploring each district, and they all had unique styles and music that made them stand out from each other. It was an easy game to savor, and I'm looking forward to replaying it someday! The artwork, story, music, and characters were all exceptional. Aside from a few grammatical errors and typos, the writing was really good too. Each character had a clear voice, and it was easy to fall into this world and become immersed in the Witch's journey. Brilliant!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I am honestly surprised at how much i am enjoying the game up to now! The soundtrack is really fitting and relaxing to listen to and the artwork is amazing. The controls are easy to remember and not complicated to do, which is really nice since we can actually focus on the story and solving the puzzles without always having to look up the controls of the game.The story line is well-made and thought of, not too long, not too short, just the right amount to keep the player entertained and in the plot. I absolutely love that there are multiple little stories that are connected between one another. Also, not forgetting the fact that we are not obligated to do the story in a linear way, we can go wherever we want and progress as we want while switching between the stories.All in all, for people that are looking for a cozy little game with no too much demanding tasks, Wytchwood is the perfect game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I liked Wytchwood as much as I was expecting to. Unfortunately going blindly into the game, I felt quite disappointed - regardless of how gorgeous the artstyle is and how the "bosses" (if I can call them like that in a game without combat) are wonderfully written and portrayed, I can't help but feel unsatisfied. I've played roughly around 5hrs and the game is quite repetitive. It would be surely shorter, yes, but also less mundane if not for redundant recipes you have to make few times from obscure ingredients that are also obtained in an equally obscure way. I felt like I couldn't quite enjoy it fully with that running back and forth just to get few ingredients again. I understand the game is literally recipe-oriented, but it feels way overcomplicated and takes from the experience. I honestly think adding easier ways to obtain things, like a hatchet used for hunting, would make gameplay much more enjoyable. It's not about difficulty, but, as I said, eliminating the constant repetition.Wytchwood is still, however, a relatively new game and I'd love to see more of it. I can't say I didn't enjoy it at all, just felt overwhelmed and unfortunately enough to not recommend the game to others who like me don't like grinding as much. I can see how appealing it can be to others (as it still kind of is to me!), but it just didn't end up being my cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Never judge a book by its cover. I thought I wouldn't be into this game but I actually love it! I love collecting items and solving little puzzles. The music is nice and there's something really peaceful about walking in the fields. Most of the time when I want to game I want something immersive but not stressful and this game is exactly what I need. A whimsical escape into a mysterious story!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: -game play is lightly metroid-vania like, with enjoyable backtracking to gather ingredients-art design is consistently beautiful throughout the entire ~14 hour experience-combat is mostly performed indirectly, with you crafting magical items that deal with enemies-gathering ingredients becomes a satisfying mix of exploring environments and interacting with the fascinating personalities in every new area-helping to end the conflicts of each major area brings you closer to understanding your characters unknown purpose in WytchwoodThis game was great and is definitely worth the price tag, this is one of my favorite games of 2021. It lived up to the expectations and then some. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are very nice and the characters and writing is pretty cool too. Personally I just kinda disliked the gameplay, it was fun at the start but for me personally it got stale after around halfway through the game. Small new mechanics got introduced throughout the game but most things stayed the same and crafting some of the components one had to craft a dozen times before felt more like a chore than interesting gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game! Its main story is intriguing enough to keep you playing just to know what happens in the end, gorgeous art style, very chill and great music, and a fairy tale like narrative with lots of farming here and there. This is one of those games that once you finish will leave you a bit nostalgic. As I said, there is quite a lot of farming here and there, but it is very chill to be honest, I find it quite relaxing rather than tiresome. With that said, after a while it gets very repetitive, and after collecting some "boss souls" it feels like you are the errand boy so it does become a task of bringing this, taking that and being given tasks while you are running a few already. At first you keep reading the interesting stories while you try to do your main task, but mid-game it gives this feeling that the stories do not impact that much the main one, so in the end, and for me at least, these stories started to be a chore with no meaning towards the end and it ended up being true. Each one of the chapters are its own mini stories, interesting true, but not meaningful for the main quest. I like the ending but  i think it feels underwhelming. With all that being said, I still think the game is good, I had lots of fun with it. I did enjoy farming and finding the potions while having fun with some of the dialogues and  jokes. Its story is good, loved the art and music.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a good storytelling game, crafting and farming, and not stressing about having to fight for your life to see some story progression, this is the game for you. Wytchwood was well written and thoughtful, and I would highly recommend if you're looking for low stakes entertainment to pass the time. Also, who doesn't love being an old lady with a cauldron for a head?
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The start of the game was lovely - nice art style, cool quests and the story was off to a good start. Sadly, that wouldn't last long. After collecting the first four souls (first four quests), everything gets very repetitive. All quests are basically the same with no twist to it. Meanwhile, the story doesn't reach it's full potential and leaves one feeling bored to a point where you'll just start skipping dialogues. I was still determined to keep playing, maybe I would be proven wrong after all. But then a bug appeared that seems non-fixable. I'm stuck at the Lighthouse, a place on the map and theres no way to move. My ask for help got no answer.Well, I certainly didn't feel like it was worth starting all over again and that says all that needs to be said.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet crafting extravaganza. It's literally ALL item gathering and crafting, and a bit of world exploration and some story to give it a backbone. I liked that there were quests with clear objectives, and you could see your progression as you unlock more and more of your Grimoire. The artwork is beautiful - it's a lovely world to spend a few hours in. The ending feels a little abrupt, but overall it was a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Really big comfy vibes. I typically don't play video games, but when my friend let me play it on her account I knew I had to buy it for myself. People who hate fetch quests won't like Wytchwood as this is the main dynamic, but it makes up for it in ambiance and storytelling. It's got a really fantastic atmosphere with great humor. Highly recommend it for anyone looking for a quick and cozy playthrough. It's my favorite game to date. : )
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute, quick, fairy-tale-like crafting game. This was easy to play through, and I really enjoyed the art and music. The focus is gathering crafting materials while exploring the different areas and fulfilling quests for the variety of characters. I enjoyed the enchanted setting and how segments of dialog were narrated as if you were reading an old fairy tale. It would have been nice to see some of the events happen rather than through story book dialog, and some of the quests felt repetitive, but overall this was a really cute game that I enjoyed playing through.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: For a game with roughly 10-12hrs of gameplay, it's definitely worth its price. The environments, music and overall art-style of the game had made it a perfect game for autumn (which it is over here right now). Gameplay is pretty straightforward and easy; Sometimes a little bit repetitive, as you're spending the majority of the time collecting and crafting in order to progress the story. Although it doesn't feel like you're grinding away just to get everything. You tend to pass through areas plenty of times in order to collect the majority of what you need, without having to go back over and over, which is good for the overall experience.I really enjoyed the story itself, the worlds you get to explore and the characters you meet. It's clear there's inspiration from classic fairy- and folktales, and it genuinely adds to the charm. I don't have enough hours in to judge whether multiple runs are just as entertaining. As the storyline is pretty linear, it's not that easy to play the game differently. However, I think if I would start a new game in say, a few months, I'll still be thoroughly entertained.No, the game isn't hard to play, and it doesn't pretend to be. To me, this is a perfect game to just relax with on the couch on a rainy day under a blanket and a huge cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a very cute and relaxing game (with some brutal scenes lol) very Grimm brothers storybook like. It can become a bit repetitive, but when you are just looking to relax and collect stuff and also follow a story I would definitely recommend! The music and the artwork are absolutely stunning as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute little story game. Pretty simple, mostly just crafting to progress the story. However, the story is enticing and the game itself is so beautiful that it's a pleasure to play. Pretty short game (I finished it in about 10 hours?), but I definitely think it's worth a playthrough. Don't think there's really any alternatives, just a single story, so if you're looking for alternate endings, I don't think this game is for you. Just a single, really lovely experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: - You play as a witch who wakes up one day, missing her memories, but with the obligation to fulfill a contract with a strange (demonic?) goat. In exchange for 12 souls, you have the power to revive a young maiden. This debt of souls takes you through an array of environments, collecting items, solving problems, and bringing justice to evildoers.With all the bugs, I was truly surprised that this game wasn't in early access, but maybe I just don't play enough newly-released games. I experienced all of the following bugs (NOTE: I used keyboard and mouse, not a controller):If the story weren't as charming and entertaining as it is, I'd probably lean toward not recommending this game because of how repetitive the action is. But all in all? I had fun. If you're going to play this game, know that it's a grind. But it's easy, it's relaxing, and the story is a joy to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game overall but I'll provide the Likes/Dislikes version below. If the likes are your thing and you're not deterred by the dislikes then by all means give the game a try! The formula of the game is good but I would advise the development team to look over the dislikes for improving gameplay for any future projects/games.Liked:-Crafting centered gameplay; Crafting is your everything here. Love it and cherish it!-Good story, beautiful art and lovely music that fits each area.-The personality of the witch/MC is prefect I loved it! She's witty and doesn't take crap from anyone/anything.-Not too serious! A lot of humorous character dialogue that doesn't get boring even with story progression.-Has strong potential for a sequel and would be a missed opportunity otherwise.Disliked:-The back tracking. Holy hell, SO MUCH BACKTRACKING just to get materials you're short on! The portals are godsends and so are the hearthstones but yeesh too much going backwards to make any progress going forward.-Needing materials from locations you passed AGES AGO and said materials are ONLY available in that one area nowhere else. I'm looking at you Skeeter Needles and Frog Slime <_<-So much story and work put into the game and our only reward for it is a very short (like a few seconds long) ending? There's no sense of accomplishment in that ESPECIALLY for all the time players invest!! Yeah I was incredibly salty for something so disappointing after all the collecting and crafting players do. Give us a new game+ or something, or at-least more to do.. but that ending and then just title screen? Feels like a spit in the face, do better.-The price. For that little story content (and that short disappointing ending) it shouldn't cost what it does right now. Seriously, it SHOULD NOT. Get it on sale if/when you can.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely experience with beautiful aesthetics, clever dialogue, and perfect music. As it is a crafting-driven questing game, it can certainly feel a bit "grindy" at times as you will be hopping from one location to another in constant pursuit of replenishing ingredients for new components/reagents to further the story. I personally wasn't very bothered by this too often though - it was a fun challenge to constantly do inventory management, especially if you try to work on quests simultaneously ("I need 3 of these for quest A while I'm here, and I should also pick up an extra 2 for quest C", etc). I was sad when it ended and was yearning for more! Highly recommend for a super fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its own unique charm that kept me enthralled for many hours. I absolutely adored the art style as well, reminds me a bit of Paper Mario in a way. _childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Try this game. It has wonderful graphics, game play loop, and a charming story. The Witch that you're playing is an adorable and sarcastic old lady, how you could not love it? I could play this game and just gather items and have fun.
