_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. If you like fairy tales (think Grimms and HC Andersen) and old folktales, witchy stuff, and story-based games, you'll like Wytchwood. Quirky art style, great soundtrack. If you dislike foraging in games like Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley, then I guess this game isn't for you. This game is ALL foraging.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXACTLY what it is: "As the old witch of the woods, explore a strange countryside, collect magic ingredients, brew sorcerous spells, and pass judgement upon a capricious cast of characters." <- Steam storefront description.The writing, audio ost, and visual looks is spectacular! There is a story but it's -- well it's straightforward but definitely leaves some desire However if you are expecting it to be more than what it described itself -- then you are going to be in for a disappointment. It has a Point A objective to Point B objective; no side quests, side adventures -- just different biomes, with the unique "bosses" and that's it. There's no co-op of any kind, or free roam.The only BIG negative I can say about the game is the back tracking. DEFINITELY go around and harvest and all resources at least up to maybe 30 to 50 stock maybe because you will be in a heckin time backtracking to these different biomes and hunting down what you'll need to make your judgement. Definitely worth the $20; but if you hate backtracking then definitely keep what I said above in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: You will enjoy Wytchwood if you like:- Compelling stories with a bit of mystery and ties to mythology and folklore.- Fetch quests, especially chained fetch quests.- Gathering materials.- Making stuff.- Collecting things (although you naturally fill the grimoire by progressing through the game, so there isn't much hunting around for secrets).- Witty dialog and text that does not sound archaic, but also does not make use of internet slang.- Gorgeous layered 2D graphics in the "papercut" style.- Relatively stress-free gameplay (no platforming, no battles, no timed anything)- Gathering materials (seriously - pick up EVERYTHING).Since I love all of those things, this game was right in my wheelhouse and I really enjoyed playing it. I just wish I could've gotten my hands on a physical copy while they were available.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

I thought that this would stop the animal, then you could take a feather, and then release it.  No fault to the game devs or anything, as I guess it kind of fits into the like grim woods setting, but I had to stop playing because I felt so bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the concept of this game and the characters and graphics are amazing, but it runs incredibly slowly on my laptop. Never had this problem with any other games. It's also incredibly annoying to respawn right back at the beginning, and because of the slowness and lag I can't cast the spells in time and keep dying far too often. I gave it a couple of hours. A shame, it could have been really good.UPDATE: I gave this another go and the game is really nicely put together with well-written storylines. The lag is still infuriating, but if you can get past this it's worth it. Good if you like collecting/crafting games with plenty of imagination and no combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm 5 hours in and the artwork is great and I like the quests. However, it's starting to get quite grind-y when it comes to the crafting. You need X/X/X to make Y/Y so you can make Z. It very quickly uses up resources. If your collecting ability levelled up as the game progressed (i.e. multiple instead of single resources from collection spots) it would be much better. Items do respawn quite quickly, but it's becoming quite frustrating to not have enough of a certain thing and have to revisit a location multiple times to build up your inventory.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

I also really enjoy the gameplay, the areas and music are both very nice and exploration is fun. _childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect cozy game for the Halloween season. It has witches, magic, fairy tales woven into a tightly knit package. The art style is what captivated me the most about this game. It is absolutely breath-taking. The game does get a bit repetitive with all the fetching materials for crafting, but this was the part I enjoyed the most. This game might not be for everyone but for me it was perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and beautiful game. The mechanics are fairly basic and intuitive - collecting and crafting quests - but done well and the characters are charming. The world is strange in the best way. It did end rather abruptly. I wish I got to see more, but it took me 12 hours to finish so pretty good for the price. Kind of addictive - I kept thinking about it between play sessions wondering where it was going. The graphics are a rolling storybook and the music is peaceful and serene.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, the art is gorgeous, gameplay is fun. The story is immaculate, there are so many small details. I loved every minute of it. If you get annoyed at back tracking in a game this game isnt for you, there is a lot of back tracking. It's done in a way that doesn't feel overly tedious. I'd definitely recommend this game
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed playing this game from start to finish as a sarcastic no-nonsense bog witch. You meet lots of fun characters and a lot of their stories are recognisable from old folktales. Dialogue and narration were full of quips and just silly things that had me snickering multiple times. The world feels rich, vibrant and alive thanks to the quest storylines that have you running through the different areas. The only downside to this game, in my opinion, was that you from time to time had to go collect items in other areas in order to craft something. Could be a lot of running back and forward between places now and then because of lacking sticks or so. But it's not a big deal as the portal helps cut down on the time spent running between the places.It was a great little crafting-adventure where it felt satisfying to gather the ingredients needed to craft the items needed to progress. If you enjoy gathering resources, crafting items and meeting quirky characters, then you might enjoy this game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of the day, this is $19.99 for 8-10 hours of gameplay. Might be worth it for an extremely superb game but this isn't one. Art style is fairly unique but animations are very simple. "Quests" are at best fetch-type, and crafting is simplistic to the brink of tedium. There is no real combat and it's basically impossible to game over, so difficulty and skill of any kind needed are basically zero. ASMR or children's game would be the only potential redeemers here, and at this price it's hard to justify a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

Some people said it got tedious, but as long as you get triple the materials while you're in the area your flow wont be broken, pro tip make a TON of jars, u gonna need em. The art style was up my ally, and everything was super nice to look at. The game isnt going to change your life but its definitely one i like more then others. I definitely recommend this if you like a game to turn your brain off and just relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: wytchwood is a beautiful game with an amazing story. after playing the game fully and unlocking all achievements i can say that this is a 10/10 game. the game play is similar to stardewvalley in sense that it is a crafting game about collecting materials to advance. if you do not like games like this where it is a never ending cycle of collecting materials and crafting the i would not recommend, however if you love cottage core, witchy aesthetics and beautiful graphics and stories (and a nice cry) this is the perfect game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: very much a collectathon, and a cosy one at that!perfect for a time of having no reservations, swinging opinions to the wind, and being your very own gruff grandmama.the scenery is wondrous with its level of detail, shading and lighting, and the twist on classic folktales was very much appreciated.only flaw would be the motion blur. dizziness is to be expected after extended play, and it is discomforting to get used to at first. other than that, just a bit of lag. whether that be caused by the game or the potato pc is still unknown.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of crafting items to complete quests isn't new, and the concept of items getting more complex and difficult to craft as a game progresses isn't new. However, I think that story line made the game very enjoyable even as the crafting got more complex. The load times between different areas was minimal and the travel points were well placed that even though you may have need to run around to a lot of different places to get items for crafting, it wasn't annoying to the point where I would have considered quitting the game because of it. I actually think it was very well balanced with a good story line (even if the ending was predictable). Each phase of the story, while centered around crafting, would have a slightly unique twist to it that kept it interesting!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Really really enjoyed this game. The art style is so beautiful and the music fits the vibes very well. The mix between potion crafting and storytelling was really good too. Honestly the only downside for me is that the game isn't longer, finished it in a lil over 11h and I WANT MORE!! But that's just cuz I loved it so much. Will definitely replay at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hoping I would enjoy this, but unfortunately I've got to say this was one of the most boring, tedious games I have played in a long time.The art and the music are both phenomenal. The environments are beautiful and it is clear a lot of thought went into each of them. There's so many details; each zone truly is a work of art. The music is very, very good. I enjoyed the unique music in each zone I visited and spent some time waiting for them to loop so I could appreciate them in their entirety.I did find the characters I encountered to be interesting; the overall feel/vibe of the game is very enjoyable, and I did enjoy what little story I experienced in the ~100 minutes I played. So... why the bad review? Well, the game is basically nothing but fetch quests outside of the art. You need to craft a ton of stuff in order to make any progress, and you constantly have to walk back and forth between levels you've already seen to get more of some materials to craft items. Some quests seemed like they tied into other quests, and over time I gradually got tired of just walking around to get a tiny piece of lore/story related to the NPCs I was helping.I think that, artistically, this is a fantastic game. It's very relaxed and if you enjoy crafting games and point to click, this is probably gonna be your kind of thing. But for me, it got too tedious and I just could not be bothered to progress further than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is positively enchanting! I feel so invested in all the story threads unfurling, and the crafting system is really engaging. I’ll update once I’ve finished, but I wanted to encourage people to buy this game; the art style is gorgeous and very unique, the performance is great on Steam Deck, and the music is so soothing and hypnotic! edit: have had to save and quit to menu a few times due to clipping, but this is the only recurring issue. Super infrequent! The stability is impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game was full of adventure! The art was beautiful and the story line was rich, the characters really made a leading build up to what the end would be for the dear old witch - no spoilers here! :3 Although sometimes tedious, gathering ingredients and crafting was one of the most enjoyable pieces of playing this game. I truly loved playing this and will most definitely play again because it was just that charming <3
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely game! The atmosphere, somewhat creepy cute setting and characters are really awesome! However: If you hate collecting stuff, this game is not for you. The gameplay is rather repetitive (you get a task, you collect materials, you craft the thing to solve the task). The real treasure here is the storytelling, characters and dialogues. It's amazing how cozy it is while being quite cruel.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Good but maybe not great. I'm about 2/3 of the way through the game by the look of it. It's not as grindy as some of these games can be, though it's starting to feel that way. Obviously I'm a slow, look at everything player which doesn't help.Overall the game knows what it is and does a great job of simplifying what is effectively a point and click adventure into a nice walk in the park with lovely art and occasionally funny dialogue. If you like the feel of the art and don't mind wandering a forest looking for sticks for several hours, you will probably love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A Perfect Original Fairytale game.I loved every aspect of this game from the artstyle, to the characters, to the writing, and all the little details put within the world.Even if you do not have the patience to go run and collect all the interesting little ingredients for the lovely recipes you should still buy to support this wonderful studio. I look forward to future games with a beloved whimsy.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: very minor spoilers ahead.So this game is a relaxing little quest/story game where you interact with the world by clicking. You seem to have amnesia in your old age, and you can't remember why you signed a contract with that darned goat, but you did! When the reason reveals itself, it really only begs more questions than it satiates with answers. Throughout the plot, you'll do what your contract insists of you to uncover the truth of the contract and an object of affection behind it.Or so I assume, I mean I have 1hish at the time of writing this review. It's really important that you click everything in this game to advance. There were a few times I was stuck simply because I wasn't curious *enough*. If you can't find something, revisit old places and check your map. There are areas to explore that aren't immediately obvious.In general, it seems very well-designed and not buggy. If you like story-quest-n-click games, you will love this one. It's quirky in all the right ways and has pretty music.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I ignored the reviews because I liked the art, I don't mind collecting things and thought I could handle it. No. I keep losing my mind at how much backtracking needs to be done. There's no weight limit to your inventory but you will NEVER have enough supplies, there will always be something you need one more of. I need a restorative idol to fix the sheep's spinning wheel, but I need a necromantic charm to make the idol, but I need a pumpkinjack bone to make the charm, but I need a snagvine to capture a pumpkinjack, but I need a sewing kit to make the snagvine, but I need a skeeter snoot to make the kit, but I need a smoke pellet to get the snoot, and I'm out of frog slime. Fast travel only makes it slightly less annoying. I recommend the game but be prepared to rage at realizing you ran out of sticks despite having dozens earlier.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: As a crochety old witch, you must collect the souls of the wicked (or morally corrupt) for a demonic goat, in order to save the life of a mystery maiden, who is doing her best Snow White impression in a cave in your garden. The story gets a bit dark and twisty, with the morally bankrupt selling their family for a harvest or feeding workers to the pigs when they are too old to work, so you never question if it's right to be out there reaping souls. This is the kind of "just desserts" we love to see dished up to these kinds of disreputable characters. This crafting game was the right length to avoid the necessary reagent grind becoming repetitive and annoying. Plus, the portal system between locations keeps the "hiking back and forth for that one missing item you need to progress" quick and easy.  Definitely an entertaining distraction.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It is different from everything else I normally play. The story had very good lessons and every single soul I took in this game deserved it LOL. The game has dark/morbid qualities that I liked a lot. The scariest thing was that damn Goose though haha! Violent lil bugger. The noises the gnomes make made me smile and they're cute. I love the music and sound effects this game has. Water dripping. Cauldron noises. It made the experience more immersive. 8/10 from me. Collectathon and spoopy aesthetic uwu
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this crafting game. Beautifully drawn. I found the story engaging and enjoyed exploring the world of the game. Highly recommend if you enjoy crafting and don't mind the idea going back and forth to find ingredients for your spells. All the achievements are in story so you get 100% just by completing the game - This is a plus point in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Love the aesthetic and narrative of this. It's a great little self-contained game. Small-scale, but very cleverly executed and written. I'd really struggle to think of anything to improve on. Really does need to be played with a controller, though, imo; the movement controls are just frustrating with mouse and keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game sitting on my wishlist for a while, but finally pulled the trigger thanks to a recommendation from the Indieventure podcast. Super glad I did, because I've had a great time playing this game! Great little animations and the sound effects as you hack, snip and trap all your various "ingredients" are a delight!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is a cozy crafting game with soothing music, and enough of a story to make the fetch quest aspect to hold together. The end was a little abrupt, but it could be used to pivot into a sequel if the devs wanted to, without much trouble. I loved the art style so much, and the cute additions (like dancing sheep and confetti) made this game a perfect cozy one.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable and relaxing game.You play as selfish witch (at the first sight) but you will see how selfish you really are..I love the graphics, music and little stories in big main story (my favorite area was The Mountain with story about Stag and Buck)Don't hesitate and play this game, you will be enchanted.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: the game is very friendly and easy. No fighting, no harness, just thinking and resource farming. my main rest comes from travelling this uniquely built world, with absolutely amazing art style. The story is simple, but fun. If you don't like repetitive gathering and farming games this be a miss, but still buy it ti try it and see the art style can be worthwhile :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game with beautiful artwork, great soundtrack and music design, and a fun concept! I was initially sold on the witchy crafting concept, but the game ended up having much more wit and depth to it then just crafting things for the hell of it--you craft things to meet certain objectives to advance the plot, which I appreciate because I tend to get overwhelmed if I'm just given a big book of possible crafts and told to do whatever I want with them! This game rewarded my tendency to spend extra time stocking up on all components to have them for future crafts, and I definitely recommend doing something like that if you aren't fond of the back-and-forth involved in fetch quests (though personally the areas are so lovely and the travel simple enough that that never bothered me when I did have to do it).I do agree with what others have said about the ending feeling a tad sudden--an epilogue or something of the sort would have been nice. However, that definitely does not detract from the experience of the game! Overall I loved it, and it was 14~15 hours well spent!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The art in this game is what captivated me and made me want to play. Also, getting to play as a witch with a pot on her head who has chicken legs. I could not resist. The story of the  game is intriguing, and unraveling it was fun. It got a bit repetitive, as you pick/trap, craft, and craft some more. That's the core game mechanic, so I found that taking breaks for a day or two and then coming back kept it engaging. It's a great game to wind down at the end of the day, with a soothing rhythm that's enough to engage your brain without making you too wound up to sleep.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game, I found the story compelling, the art and atmosphere is unique and beautiful. At times the gathering/crafting felt like a chore but it helps if you just alternate between questlines (allows you to get multiple resources in the same area for example) and taking breaks. For completionists: all achievements are progress-based
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I do not think it is a bad game; that said, it is not one I would recommend to my friends. All the repetitive collecting becomes redundantly tiring after a while, that you have to go back-and-forth numerous times to get the primary resources over and over to produce more items from the recipe book; there are literally no other pattern you could possibly follow in this game, and I would love it if it were more creative and flexible. The story-line is fine, and comes with some funny little twists, although not presented in a more fascinating way; at the same time the music and sound effects to be tuned a little to better fit into some scenes. I reckon that some of the details could have been fashioned differently for the game to truly deliver its ideas to the audience as well as to get the dark comedies matter, while they actually are illustrated by too many teenager-like funny lines. Great picture, though; I do believe the creators have made hard efforts on this game, but for now the presentation is a bit short to my expectation.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 4.6/5"Wytchwood" is a captivating crafting adventure game that immerses players in a world brimming with gothic fables and enchanting fairytales. As the enigmatic witch of the woods, players embark on a whimsical journey filled with magical ingredients, devious spells, and moral lessons.Art Style and Atmosphere:One of the standout features of "Wytchwood" is its lovingly rendered storybook art style. The game’s visuals are a feast for the eyes, evoking a sense of nostalgia and wonder reminiscent of classic fairytales. The expressive and detailed environments, coupled with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack, create an atmosphere that draws players into its fantastical world.Gameplay and Crafting:"Wytchwood" shines in its crafting mechanics, offering a rich and rewarding experience. Players will find themselves gathering and collecting a variety of bizarre ingredients such as toxic toadstools, eye of newt, and bottled fear. The process of brewing enchantments and concocting spells is both engaging and satisfying, providing endless opportunities for experimentation and creativity.Story and Characters:The game’s narrative is woven through a series of allegorical tales, each featuring a colorful cast of characters and creatures. As the witch, you pass judgment and teach morals through your cunning use of spells and curses. Turning the greedy into frogs and tricking the wicked with clever curses adds a layer of dark humor and charm to the gameplay. The stories are both whimsical and thought-provoking, encouraging players to reflect on the lessons imparted.Puzzles and Exploration:Exploration in "Wytchwood" is a delight, with a world filled with strange monsters and fantastical narratives. Players must use their wit and guile to solve puzzles and overcome challenges. The puzzles are cleverly designed, requiring a mix of logic and creativity to best the peculiar inhabitants of the forest.Overall Experience:"Wytchwood" offers a unique and enchanting experience that stands out in the crafting adventure genre. Its combination of a beautifully crafted world, engaging gameplay mechanics, and rich storytelling creates a game that is both immersive and memorable. The moralistic undertones add depth to the whimsical narrative, making each interaction and decision feel meaningful.Conclusion:"Wytchwood" is a must-play for fans of crafting adventures and fairytales. Its expressive art style, intricate crafting system, and charmingly dark narrative come together to create an unforgettable journey. Whether you’re brewing devious spells or uncovering the secrets of the forest, "Wytchwood" promises an enchanting adventure that will captivate players from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely for those of us that are story driven, as the game play is collecting based which is simple and repetitive. I loved the story as it unfolded, although I feel like the ending fell flat after the 18 hour build up for me; this might be because I'm used to grandiose endings that feel final, this ending is very open ended. The visuals are beautiful and the art style is incredibly unique. Wytchwood is worth it as an experience and a story for me, but if you are unsure about it you should wait for another steam sale to give it a try
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I am very much enjoying this game! The characters are very fun and the story is interesting. If you don't care for resource gathering games this might not be the game for you. But for me at least the story has has been intriguing enough, so the resource gathering hasn't gotten too monotonous. I definitely recommend playing this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a year since I've played this game, but I find myself wishing I could play it again for the first time as the leaves turn to reds and golds and crunch beneath my feet. Wytchwood is a gothic fairy tale in the form of a video game. It's a lot of grinding and repetition, but has an enchanting variety of characters and storylines, and lets you be the hero of the story at the bequest of a mysterious (and somehow weirdly powerful?) goat (not GOAT).Loved it. Want another. Will probably come back to this. Best played in the autumn chill with a dry cider in hand 🍂
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: The tags for this do it justice - if you're looking for something you don't have to think too hard about while playing, and you're just here to have a fun time exploring a gorgeously crafted world, with a lovely soundtrack, set in a storybook aesthetic that teases familiar fairytale characters and plots that you've probably heard about before. There's no stress to find any hidden achievements and there were enough areas to explore in my 9 hour total gameplay that made it still enjoyable even nearing the end, and not too many to become a headache of trying to remember which ingredients could be found where. (Slight spoiler territory, but personally I wished there had been more to explore in the Darkwood though I understand why there wasn't.)While I do recommend this game, fair warning: the main gameplay really is basically just generic fetch quest, and most of the progression for the game is just grinding for ingredients, pausing to find the ingredients on the screen, and then grinding for more ingredients (though I really, really, really do appreciate all that inventory space). The story being fairly straightforward means there's also not much replay value, though personally I feel that it is delightfully charming enough to be revisited on occasion.TL;DR - it's a simple, straightforward fetch-quest and crafting game stylized to be a fairytale within fairytales, an endearing protagonist, and fun storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! Even though the ending was a bit predictable from the beginning for me it was still a fun little magical adventure :} You are a witch in a contract with a goat to collect 12 evil/ bad souls, each with their own story. You travel around a few different places through portals to forage for a bunch of different materials to craft spells and things with that will help you throughout your journey of collecting these souls, helping others and to aid you against enemies. There's lots of dialogue in talking to a bunch of different characters. It is very fairytale-ish, which I love and the graphic art style were super colorful and neat, it looked like a popup story book! Great graphics, art, music, story, the humor and everything in between. No bugs that I've encountered and all achievements work. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I've never uninstalled a game so quickly in my life. Towards the end, I was driven by pure spite, some primal urge compelled me to complete this game for some reason beyond my own understanding. Maybe it was some ancestral curse I had to overcome in this life, some kind of initiation ritual now adapted in the form of a cutesy indie game. don't get me wrong, the artwork on display here is extremely charming and there was a lot of potential in the various folktale archetypes explored. but that's about all i can say that is remotely positive. i felt like i had something to prove to the previous players who accused this game of being too grindy. so i bit my tongue, rolled up my sleeves and got down to work. i soon found out however, that the gameplay loop was just that- an endless, unfulfilling loop with no variation whatsoever. you could sense that the devs of this game were more art-focused than anything else. everything got so repetitive that at a point i began listening to podcasts while playing. it had become a chore, no, it had become some kind of twisted mission that i promised myself i would accomplish. and to what end? to what end, i ask you? a concluding twist that falls so flat it makes the Netherlands look like its in the centre of the Alps. i don't know what species of demonic entity possessed the other 24% of the unfortunate souls who actually made it till the end (that stat says a lot already) but i can tell you one thing- we all need a discord channel that can function as a support group- Wytchwood Anonymous or something. For all its widespread appeal and cozy, welcoming aesthetics, Wytchwood's actual game design suggests that it is targeting a much more niche demographic:a) people who play games to enjoy the tactile sensation of touching keyboard keys or clicking a mouse for the sake of it cause god knows it's not for anything that actually stimulates regions of the brain necessary for conscious thought b) masochists like myself who claim in lengthy reviews that they know better but play it to the bitter end anyway xx
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky game full of interesting characters,  dialogue and interactions. Lots of areas to explore and material spawn rate is good which is good because stockpiling is always a good idea in this game. The graphics are interesting, feels like an old fairy tale or folklore. I appreciate the creator's imagination in regards to the enemies and collection style for supplies. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely lovely game.I wish I could erase my memory just to play it again.The atmosphere, the OST, the plot, the gameplay, almost everything is perfect. Yes, the fetch mecanic can be frustrating, but by playing it only a few hours at a time it was soothing to my brain.Thank you very much to all team members for creating this fantastic game !
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's like somebody made this game just for me. It's scavanging, crafting, doesn't require fighting and is quite forgiving if you can't do something on the first try. The games does also have a compelling story, though crafting really is the main goal of the game. If you don't like crafting, it is very likely not for you. I could craft forever, so this game fills me with so much happyness. It's also easy enough to play after a long day of work, but it still brings challenges. Design and music are amazing as well, they give the game an extraordinary flair. Bonus for me: the main character reminds me so very much of a good friend of mine, which really speaks for the design of said character. Can't wait to continue and hopefully not finish it too fast!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game with its gorgeous environments, unique character designs and interesting premise. But there's too much holding it back.It started with a bug that caused the character to move on her own at times and for the menu to keep scrolling through the items randomly. Some googling revealed that I shouldn't have pressed the map button when the game prompted me to. I started over, never pressed that button and everything worked fine. So, the start was bad, but I had hopes that I could still have some fun.Unfortunately, the gameplay was rather tedious. It's not very varied: you pick up stuff, craft items to get other stuff, craft more complex items from that stuff, rinse, repeat. At the end I had to run around all over the place for one specific thing I needed for a recipe. In some cases I had to craft the recipe before it, for which I had run out of materials, and even the recipe before that, for which I was also missing something. The last couple of hours were quite tiresome and the boring soundtrack didn't do the gameplay any favours.The only thing that kept me playing was wanting to see the ending and I'm still not sure if it was worth the 10 hours. If you're looking for something slow paced and don't mind grinding, maybe you'll enjoy this game. But if I could go back in time, I wouldn't buy it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game was cute and simple. I enjoyed the story a lot and I liked that it was easy to get the achievements without having to grind really hard. The crafting recipes weren't terribly hard to make, though sometimes required you to go back to other regions if you weren't farming them up as you went. The music gave a great atmosphere to each section of the game and it was honestly a really chill game for me. The art style was also super cute! Definitely recommend playing it if you're looking for a slower-paced game to just relax and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I ate this game up, for it was My Jam. I love mystical crafting witchy games and the fairy tale narrative of this was really fun. It's both humorous and somber, with beautiful art and music, awesome character designs, colorful settings, and quests that put twists on familiar tales and tropes. I loved playing as the Hag and setting things right across the land.Wytchwood is about collecting the souls of twelve wrong-doers through quests where you learn a weakness, collect the ingredients to craft what will take advantage of that weakness, and the subquests that are smaller versions of that loop. It borders on fetch-questy but there's so much to do in each zone (because you get four concurrent soul quests at a time) you can just pivot for a while while you collect and seek ingredients, and there's a hubworld between zones so when I realized I needed to cross the map, it wasn't a big deal even if I did often slump for a second. Toward the later end of the game I had to do a little more running around, but I could gather the items in pretty quick order since by that time I knew the world really well. The map and journal make it really easy to see what's waiting for you, and the crafting book is really easy to navigate and tells you what zone you can look in for what you're missing. Definitely a fun game with a satisfying story.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I feel this game is a bit overpriced. My total time is what it took me to complete the game fully and I did not look up anything and discovered everything myself. It's not a long game and while I have played many indie games that are short, I don't usually walk away feeling dissatisfied as much as I did with this one. I think people should be paid for what they made, but I would recommend getting this one only when it is on sale if you're into grindy crafting games. The art is wonderful in this and the music is very nice. However, there's very little story and the whole game can just be summarized to lots of fetch quests. From the other reviews, I expected the grind of collection, but I thought the story would at least make up for the grind especially since this is tagged as "story rich."Personally I would not consider this to be story rich, I predicted the "twist" from the beginning of the game and I kept waiting to get some story connection between the souls and your character and it didn't happen. It has some story and it is satisfying to help all the people, but it dangles this carrot that you're going to get your memories back and know the full story eventually and that never happens. Spoilers below: But really, what were those memories? How was your character connected to the souls that you collect? Sure you can get some vague idea on how your character that you play as might have been wronged by those souls, but no exact story. This game could have been so great if there were flashbacks and buildup that makes the player want to fulfill the contract to keep learning more, but nope. You've got to slog this out because hey it seems like these souls had it coming and these other people could use some help. It does feel nice to help people, but it falsely dangles this carrot that "you'll eventually know, just wait for it." Only to be left dissatisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Wytchwood is essentially one long fetch quest, casting you as a witch exploring a dark fairytale environment for ingredients in order to craft various potions which you need in order to appease the mysterious talking goat advising you. This will understandably alienate some of those who dislike this type of gameplay, but as one who isn’t typically a big fan of fetch quests I found the game to be surprisingly delightful. The artwork is beautiful, the storyline and dialogue are well-written and entertaining, the music and sounds are fantastically orchestrated, and there is enough variety to the world, ingredients, and potions to keep the gameplay engaging. I highly recommend Wytchwood to anyone looking for a soothing game with a great atmosphere (or looking to live out their fantasy of being a cottage-core crone)
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought this game because [1] I was drawn to the art style, [2] I like witchy, lore, cozy, fantasy stuff, [3] I'm also enamored by a good story/plot, and [4] I like crafting (as a witch or something similar). If you played Pentiment, you'll definitely like this one too but it has its twists. Honestly, I wasn't expecting anything but boy by the price point, this game blew my mind. It exceeded my expectations! I'm only 2 hours in right now but I already adore the game and looking forward to exploring more. It has depth which is hard to find in some games so if you're looking for a game with a good story, I would recommend this. What I also love about it is that sometimes, things that you craft would have you thinking creatively or guess where to find it. Things that don't have specific ingredients in the game will have you thinking. But if you don't like going from one place to another to find ingredients for crafting, then this game may not be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game will absolutely keep you glued once you start playing if you prefer cozy adventure games! Wytchwood is story-rich                                                                                  and filled with lore and mythical creatures. The visuals are very vibrant and stunning. If you enjoy foraging, crafting and exploring then this is the perfect cozy game for you. I will definitely replay this game. 10/10 recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Over all yes I like this game enjoyed the story immensely... However there is a ridiculous amount of back and forth. I do understand it's meant to make you work for the end means. I just want to stated a huge CAUTIONS to those who find Fetch quest and repetitive Back and Forth quest tedious. You will absolutely loath this game if this is an issue for you.If they are not a deal breaker and you enjoy ethic/ moral based story line entertain like I do then enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Visually gorgeous game, beautifully written and engaging. The gameplay is a bit repetitive and fetch-y but that is exactly what the game advertises and plays it off with immense satisfaction. The story always has you coming back and wishing for more.I recommend the game only to those with patience, and advise them to take their time when playing it to enjoy it at its fullest.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game while I was searching around Steam looking for something new to play. I read the reviews, weighed the pros and cons and decided that I would buy it and give it a try.I totally understand why some people were upset and calling it a glorified fetch quest, but I am an absolute gremlin in video games who loves a ton of items to hoard and collect (looking at you Fallout 4), so I didn't mind too much. Occasionally when I'm streaming on Twitch, I do get a little annoyed having to go back and forth all over the map to collect things, but it's not really that bad.If you like collecting things in games and don't mind a bit of a grind, this is the game for you. The graphics are unique and beautiful, the story is engaging, and the crafting system is easy to grasp, so yes, 9/10 would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Only just started playing wytchwood . . . I love it. My little cranky old woman game. I always wanted to be like this when I grew up and finally I can rpg my wildest dreams. Obsessed with how it lets you scuttle around the woods while wearing a pot and helping people with their life troubles as long as there's something in it for you. Incredible 10/10 best game of its kind. I would say "everyone should play this" if I didn't know that this is probably not universally appealing. Has the same aesthetic and sensibilities as a Discworld novel with lovely storybook-esque art and visuals. Even the quests and navigation are "witchy" somehow- or at least are intuitive (based on having read the tropes a lot) in a way that other crafting/exploration games aren't for me with my fairly limited gaming experience. Someone described this as peaceful somewhere online and I didn't really understand what they could mean, but after playing it I totally get it. Definitely calming with no real night/day sequences that I know of or "find a place to sleep to heal" mechanics. Maybe I'll change my mind later on this as I get more into the game (doubtful). I could play this game for hours but it's not so intense I get sucked into it, is basically the gist of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very hard for me to rate, because the art style and writing are fantastic, but somewhere around half-way to 2/3rds of the way through the game, you are likely to start getting very bored, as the game slowly becomes Fetch-quest: the Game. At a certain point, you have to go gather ingredients so you can make an item, then use the item to gather other ingredients, which will be used to make another item, which will be used to gather ingredients so you can make another item, which will be used to gather ingredients... you get the idea. If the item recipes hadn't become a pyramid scheme to make the game take longer, I would wholeheartedly give it a 10/10. As is, I'd probably give it a 7/10 based on the writing and art.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly charming, I adored this game from start to finish. It oozes charm from its art style to the dialogue tone to the way characters pan out. That being said, it's a crafting game meaning the majority of the game is spent picking up almost everything you come across and doing a lot of back and forth when you're missing certain ingredients. Mini-puzzles involve figuring out how to procure a certain ingredient, but the journal and grimoire will help you out with most which some people who like to figure it out themselves may not like. I personally wasn't too fussed and liked the guidance. Game is of a decent length, clocking in at about 10-11 hours and can probably be played in 3 chunks. I adored the first two thirds, but towards the end was definitely running out of ingredients and having to backtrack multiple times for one or two things. That being said, the ending pays off and it's a game I'll definitely look back on fondly.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun and relaxing game. I enjoyed the colors and the artwork and the story that was going on. Nothing was too difficult to achieve, really a game to play through in one-sitting pretty much, but enjoyable the whole time. Definitely recommend if you're in a quiet and peaceful kinda mood where you just wanna gather and craft things to nice music.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: Game crashed at the 11th soul, and corrupted the save file... The game is so repetitive that there's no way the last hour of story if worth 8h of grind. The story is fine, but somewhere past the mid point, you'll spend more time running in circle to farm basic resources and reload the same map again and again because it's faster that exploring. They definitely could have the later recipe less of a pain, so the grind don't overtake the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been on my wishlist for a couple of months. The concept sounded really interesting and the art looked beautiful. I have been moving away from the big titles and open world games recently, starting to focus on storytelling, art and innovative gameplay.This one seemed right up my alley and after playing for a bit, it really is! The story is simple, but interesting, the main character is certainly no hero, but immensely likeable, and the artwork looks like right out of an old picturebook. (Please don't give this game to children, though. It can be quite ruthless and somber at times.)The concept is simple: you collect ressources and craft things required to solve your quest. Almost every creature has a certain weakness to it, so you have to kill other creatures in order to craft your weapons, which again requires ressources won from other beasts, and so on. That way, you will soon have to build "crafting chains" ("Right, I need Goblin Snot. Goblins are vulnerable to Voodoo Dolls. So I need the Sewing Kit, for which I need a Skeeter Snoot, but I need a Smokepot in order to kill a Skeeter, so I need clay for that...") And the best thing is: the game never lets it get tedious. As far as I have come, you never need more than three of an ingredient and they are usually fairly easy to find. And if you make a habit of collecting as you go (many ingredients can just be picked up from the ground), it won't take much time at all, while still being really fun.The characters are fairly innovative and not your run-of-the-mill NPCs, the dialogues have a certain dry humour, which helps with the overall tone of the game, and, as I said the main character and her story are certainly entertaining and mysterious enough to keep you playing. Plus, I love me an older woman as a main character for a change.I can't wait for more and I'm very much looking forward to the conclusion! I might edit this after I've played some more or after I've finished it.Edit: I've finished it. It was amazing to finish it, but the drawback was, it was finished after that. I want to move into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Wytchwood very much. Played great on Deck. Colorful art and good dialogue, both with a cheeky sense of humor. The game also felt very kind. It took me a while to even notice the soundtrack; it is mostly sort of gentle and environmental. Except for the sea shanty. Gotta love a nice sea shanty.I appreciate bite sized missions. I could knock out a few steps and pick the game right up the next day. The mission tracking can be turned off if you don't want as much guidance. I play games very slowly; I'd expect most people to finish in much less time.I personally like the gameplay loop of explore, collect, craft items, use items to collect better stuff, craft better items, etc., but mileage can and should vary. I also don't mind making notes on what I need to get. The in game journal was enough on its own, but I was trying to be more efficient towards the end. I was also using fast travel more by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game. It's a lot of collecting items and going on quests, which I find very relaxing and soothing. Its great for anyone who enjoys the feeling of checking things off a list. The quests are also set against a backdrop of fairy tales and the writing of these fairy tales as you progress the story is fantastic! Also the game is just beautiful with so many settings and places to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This reminds me of those free flash games from the the 2000's, but with significantly more content and polish. It's a fun little time sink that doesn't demand much from the player. The gameplay is mainly a test of your memory, since old recipes are required for more complex, new recipes as the story progresses. The story itself is well-written, and kept me engaged.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start out by saying that overall I enjoyed the game. My biggest complaint is that the story is very linear and you don't get to make any choices, which was kind of disappointing. The puzzles are simple and most of the game involves collecting resources in order to craft/progress to the next task. If you aren't into that, this probably isn't the game for you. I enjoyed the art style, characters, and overall tone of the game. I wish the ending was more rewarding, but I liked the outcome for the characters. All in all, not a bad game. Its great if you want something uncomplicated and relaxing to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game but i definitely don't think it's for everyone. If you want a very strong fairytale/storybook atmosphere, this game will be perfect. But you need to enjoy grinding because that's a HUGE part of the game. I would recommend watching non spoilery reviews to see if you could enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game has beautiful and unique graphics, an interesting and fun story and wonderful music and sound design. As many before wrote, it is a gigantic fetch quest. So if you dont like this kind of mechanic, stay away. But as I experienced it, you'll do fine if you make it a habit to take up the respawning ressources on your way. There is no grind needed to get everything. I only had a few materials left, that I had to really go out of my way and visit an area I had no other open business in. I liked playing this game. It is fun and relaxing, the story is intriguing and the game is not to long to become tedious. The end was a little unexpected, but not at all out of topic with the story you just expirienced.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, did obviously everything that can be done. Actually, you cannot miss any parts of the story.The game works really nice as a story. Heartwarming at times, gruesome at other times. Justice is handed out in pretty rough ways. A real fairy tale. I love this aspect of the game.The game works rather bad as a game. "Jack-o-Lantern again? Really?" Everyone who has played this game knows what I mean. Some ingredients have to be collected again and again. And they are not stuff that can be gathered in one step or more than one at a time. No, there are two or three steps and then you can finally build, what you need to continue the story. And then ... you need it again ... GNAAAH!!! Recipes become more complicated, more multi-step recipes. And that slows down the story to a creep.I'd prefered if there where more things like the fountain for wyrd water at the graveyard's mansion or more market stalls where you can buy high tier ingredients. Maybe have a way to cook stuff at the cauldron in the witch's hut.But still thumbs up. The story and the artwork are just too beautiful. I don't finish a lot of games, but I finished this one, despite the annoying resource stuff. If you liked fairy tales as a kid and maybe still as an adult, this game is a gem. A gem with a fault, but still a gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a nice little game. I love the twist at the end, (should have seen it coming though). Very good game :)Positives: visuals (adorable and stunning), soundtrack (enchanting and immersive), story (creative and diverse)Neutrals: gameplay - this could be a positive if it was just slightly less grindy, but a large part of that is my own fault for being a perfectionist. A good fix would be if a resource or craftable changed somehow (maybe graying out or green 'complete' border?) once fully finished or only needed once. It is actually very good for the most part though.Negatives: There was only one thing I didn't like, which was the necessary animal death involved. If there was an alternate way to get frog slime or bird feathers (for examples) without killing them, I'd be relieved. I did see that you can buy meat at the Market, so maybe more stalls with those options and unlocking the area sooner?All in all, a very good nice game that kept me hooked and was mostly enjoyable. 8/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun and cozy game. No combat. Puzzle solving, item, and ingredient gathering is the main focus. You're compelled by the story, which is predictable, but well written enough that I wanted to finish the game to confirm what I thought was going to happen. I'd recommend this game for anyone who loves a fun and cozy game with good story telling.

_childDocuments_.review: While the theme is cute and fun, it's a very short game. I finished in under 9 hours. It's just glorified fetch quests. Go here, you need an item, go somewhere else to get it or the materials to craft it, then come back. And you do this a hundred times. Not a good deal even when it was on sale compared to many other games.Though if you want to get 100% achievements, it's an easy game to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game. It's controller friendly which is a check in my book. It's definitely a cozy game but that I did not mind. I loved the dark fairy tale theme. The ending was superb with a nice twist I thought. The animation is a delight. It takes about 14hrs to finish. I found the music to be charming in all zones. _childDocuments_.review: Such a fun and addicting game! Lately, I've had a hard time getting into games and sticking with it. This is the first game I've finished in a long time. I love it so much! _childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous art style, witty writing, interesting story & colourful characters.If you enjoy collecting & hoarding ingredients and crafting interesting items/spells/concoctions, this game will satisfy all that.There's no forced time constraints & it is very forgiving of errors & injuries (no real combat) so you can really take your time and enjoy exploring the world that's been created here. Control-wise, there's flexibility with keymapping to your preference with keyboard, controller, or you could get away with just using your mouse for the entire game.Well worth your time if you enjoy exploring, collecting, crafting, a little dark humour & uncovering the truth.Would enact witchy justice again!

_childDocuments_.review: this has been one of my favorite games i've played so far. it has charming imagery and witty dialogue, accompanied with lovely music. it has an incredibly interesting story with the perfect amount of gothic fables and fairytales, and each quest gives you the sweet relief that you were able to do something to help others through magic. the game play includes interacting with npcs, collecting materials (and you need to collect A LOT), and crafting magical items to help you defeat/subdue creatures and animals and to help you progress through the story. if you want a medium paced game, this is it. it's not too slow and not too fast. the ending was so good, instead of making me feel sad that the game was over, i felt happy and content (and it made me REALLY want to cosplay the witch with an item but no spoilers here haha). a friend recommended it to me, and i have been recommending it to my other friends, and i'm recommending it to you now :)

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game with caveats. As a game, it's pretty boring to me. Overall, though, it has merit.First off, the art REALLY carries the game and is probably it's best feature. It just perfectly captures the feeling of a pop-up fair tale book. The animations add to this. I love seeing the shuffling of the witch's feet and the various critters scurrying about.The gameplay loops is the weakest part of this game. You are a witch tasked with an objective. You achieve said objective by collecting various items in each area of the game to complete smaller objectives, which themselves have smaller goals. All of which involve collecting things. You collect and craft things that help you complete all these objectives the game. That's basically it. Some items are reused, others, not so much. It just feels like a collectathon. I was expecting more (like dialouge choices or puzzles), so I have to say I was a let down a tad. I was hoping the gameplay would change but it does not; it continues to be a "collect this specific thing, craft into something, use item to progress, repeat". However, once I accepted that is how the game is, I changed my frame of mind to treat this as something to lean back and enjoy. It is a relaxing experience. The art is so charming and cute, I couldn't help enjoying my time with this game. The music is not too busy and adds to the atmosphere.The game, to its credit, is not frustrating in the least. It gives you all the tools to find things. The key thing is to pay attention to your surroundings so you know where things were in case you need to find a specific resource. The game tells you which areas it can be found. There is no inventory limit, and no workbenches you need to go to to craft things. Sure, you might need to double back a few times, but if you just collect as much as you can, chances are you'll have what you need on you.The story is pretty weak so far since it's basically driven by collecting things (again, having more dialogue available would have made me happier). But there is a story and I won't write it off yet until I finish it. The story is (light spoilers)  . Pretty typical fairy tale stuff. However, the out-of-place humor the characters inject here and there caught me off guard. It wasn't anything to crazy, but it drew a chuckle from me.In summary, if you want a charming, relaxing, simple game about a witch collecting things in a beautifully drawn world, try it out. If nothing I said sounds appealing about this game, I would avoid it as you will likely grow bored very fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Wytchwood

_childDocuments_.review: I really Enjoyed this light-hearted, funny game. It is nice when a game has a sense of self and humour involved. It was fairly short for me and  left me wanting more. The "fairy tale" aspect was cute and the  story line was nice too. Really relaxing and enjoyable and would recommend to anyone who plays casually and just wants to relax and play an easy game where not too much thinking is involved. Reminded me a little of cult of the lamb. No swearing and (since it has been a while) I am sure was very kid friendly. It also filled my need to "collect" items, which I enjoy in games. This game checks all my boxes regarding playable, chill-out, story-line and quick game play all in one. Enjoy.

name: Raji: An Ancient Epic
detailed_description: A thousand years have passed since the last great war between the demons and the gods. Lulled into a false sense of security and having forgotten the ways of alchemy, humans find themselves at the mercy of the invading demons, who wage a new war to repay their past humiliation. Cities fall, fortresses are in ruins and young children are abducted from their homes. In this chaos, a young girl named Raji is chosen by the gods to be the sole defender of the human race. A Story of Siblings Raji and her younger brother Golu are separated as the demonic hordes attack. It is now up to Raji to save him and put an end to this reckless war. On her quest she will have to overcome the full might and cunning of the great lord of demons, Mahabalasura. Stunning Artwork Drawing inspiration from legendary tales of Hindu folklore and the medieval architecture of Rajasthan, Raji: An Ancient Epic brings a visually stunning and unique style to the action-adventure genre! Enter an immersive environment drawn in the Pahari art style and brought to life with hand-painted textures rendered in 3D. Tactical Combat Diverse weapons and powers, gifted to Raji by the gods are at your disposal. Mastering them all will be vital to your success as the demonic hordes will skillfully adapt to each and every situation; while the Trishul may be perfect for one battle, the mighty Sharanga bow may be needed for the next. A Universe Set in Ancient India For the very first time, experience a game set in ancient India and infused with Hindu and Balinese mythology. From lore full of enchanting stories and fierce battles with demons and menacing bosses to ancient puzzles and massive forts and palaces begging to be explored - you will find yourself in a sibling story unlike any other.

_childDocuments_.review: Totally worth it buy this game!!I never expected i will play a indian game like once.Playing this with hindi dialogues give it more power, boss fights are also interesting and fun to win as they are not quite easy to win every boss fight in first attempt.Give a try to demo version if you are still in doubt.My recommendation is to buy it under 500 at any cost, though i get it in 149 in sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Few hours into the game, the biggest issue I have with it is the controls. There's no auto locking to a target, it doesn't auto aim to the nearest target or lowest health target. Direction of motion also becomes direction of attack. Which means shooting at an enemy whilst staying away from them is really difficult. The responsiveness is too slow, so running away, quickly turning back and attacking enemies is difficult to pull off.Super annoying at times!!Still, gonna keep playing. I want to support indian games.The environment, concept and graphics are really great and refreshing though.EDIT:That was for playing with a controller. But when you play with a keyboard and mouse, it's a completely different story. I tried the final boss fight with a controller and lost more than 20 times. And with a keyboard-mouse? Beat it in one go. All I had to do was spam left click and spacebar!! The team should test the game a bit more thoroughly and balance things out.

_childDocuments_.review: Having followed the development of the game for about three years, I already formed something of an emotional attachment to the game - and I am enchanted that the final game exceeded my expectations in every respect. Raji is in its essence a platform hack-and-slash adventure game, not completely dissimilar from Prince of Persia. While its game mechanism is relatively simple, movement and combat has just enough depth and XP-development elements to make the gameplay engaging on the long run. All in all, the game is fun to play, the action is smooth, and never really feels repetitive. But apart from being  fun to play, what really makes this game special is the aesthetics. Everything from the plot, storytelling, music to graphic design is magnificently monumental and completely endearing at the same time. There is something epic and grand in the storytelling and the game universe, yet the bird perspective and the loving attention to detail make it seem so small and cute as well.Nodding Heads Games has used the cultural references to South Asian and Hindu folklore and arts to their maximum impact in a way that will take your breath away. Every single detail in the game is aesthetically pleasing, and often you find yourself just listening to the background music and glancing at the environment, from the grandiose backdrop to the smallest details on Raji´s saree dress. Cutscenes are rendered as animated puppet shows, levels vary from massive ruins to wilderness, and the game is packed with zany characters and villains.This game is a masterpiece in indie gaming, and surely a historic step for Indian gaming industry in general. One can only hope that Nodding Heads Games will have to chance to keep making our lives just a tad more interesting - and maybe even inspiring other indie studios to follow in their footsteps.

_childDocuments_.review: The first impression that this game gives is that it is story rich and quite atmospheric. The game has a unique camera that is so zoomed out that it almost looks like a isometric view in many places. The game is divided into several worlds each of which have very unique feel to them. The combat is not necessarily the most exciting aspect of the game, its mostly of hack and slash style. The protagonist can also use the assistance of elemental powers namely Lightning, Fire and Ice. The ice power pretty much melts all the enemies especially when powered with orbs, making the combat completely challenge-less after its obtained. There are several weapons that are unlocked throughout the game that can be instantly switched between at anytime.  The platforming is very impressive. It is very evident that there is a lot of inspiration taken from the Prince of Persia series, but the game introduces some unique tech as well. One of the biggest negative points of the game is easily the amount of bugs it has had since launch. The games seems to have framerate related issues, graphical glitches and also gameplay related bugs that make some areas of the game really frustrating to deal with. The game also does not feature many extras/secrets other than the orbs. The game's atmosphere, artstyle, theme all create this wonderful mysterious element to it that begs for having secret bonus areas and stuff but it feels like a missed opportunity by the devs.Overall a game worth trying out and is likely to be enjoyable atleast for one playthrough especially if you are into games with this kind of setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game. I expected less to be honest considering that I never encountered this game on Steam, but I was wrong. And usually when that happens you have much more enjoyment in a game. So many pros about this game:- Very nice graphics and excellent design of levels. This is like pure example of so much attention to details in big levels. I was really positively surprised when I saw ray tracing options, which add even more details and are excellent.- There is even option for several magic modifications which can add some diversity to combat- No bugs, not a single glitch or anything- Nice lore, and presented in a very new approach through paintings on a walls or other environment designs, this is like one of the best ways I saw in any game.The only con I would say is some combat chaotic encounters where you mostly just button mesh and that is it. Even if there are options for some different moves you can't do it because there is not so good interaction with the world while you fight. Also, could be a little longer, considering that team behind it is very talented.But, all things considered this is very nice game and pure recommendation from my side. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is an action-adventure game set in Ancient India centered around a young girl's journey to rescue her younger brother after an attack by demons. Raji uses a third-person isometric viewpoint to control your character and her attacks on enemies. Throughout the game, spatterings of Hinduism and its various stories will be conveyed to you, educating players on Hindu history. Raji also features multiple weapons to use to progress in the game, each one useful for certain situations. Raji features responsive, fast-paced combat where each hit feels satisfying. Anyone can pick up a certain playstyle based on what weapon they choose to main. Movement is also responsive and has no outward flaws. In terms of the action part, Raji excels. Level design is also a very big plus going from stone forests to mystical temples that keeps player in amazement at the environment. In drawbacks, Raji suffers from an underwhelming final boss and ending. Overall, Raji is an excellent game for what it is from a newbie game developer studio. Hopefully, the studio can keep going and enhancing their craft.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is a hard game to recommend, but I think it has enough merit for those seeking a certain experience.The biggest positive is its setting in Hindu mythology. I enjoyed the vantage point we have as players, almost imitating a god watching events unfold. There's tidbits of mythology that I appreciated, which went a long way to ground the action in the setting. Do yourself a favor and set the language to Hindi.Other positives include the music and cutscenes. The music is a blend of Indian traditional instruments with occasional modern flourishes. There's a few songs I'd like to add to a playlist here. I also really enjoyed the puppetry-themed cutscenes, which added another flare of an older time. The developers must have researched heavily on shadow puppetry because the care to these scenes really shows. This stage-like theme also extends to the world itself, which has a miniature feel to it. The environments themselves, at least on a conceptual level, show attention to what an "ancient epic" might look. My biggest issue was running it smoothly, which is perplexing considering this game shouldn't be so hard to run. It's not optimized well, and whether that's an engine issue or something else your first hurdle will most likely be getting rid of tearing, bizarre foliage rendering, and other things. This game isn't graphically stunning anyway, so I ultimately just played it on low settings.Story and combat make up the other big issues. Story starts out as a rescue and unfolds into something like an epic, however, the story beats are awkwardly presented and the final hour is perplexing. It seems like the written story is much longer than the game itself, because the final moments are skipped forward and abruptly halted. Honestly, I'd say the same about combat, because it doesn't really feel good, and where I think I'm hitting I'm not. It's not fun, and I'm curious as to why combat was the decision for primary gameplay when the puzzles might have been better utilized. The final boss is exemplary of both these issues.Ultimately whether you would enjoy this is based on your patience and willingness to overlook its shortcomings for moments that immerse you in a mythology not often explored in popular games.  This was part of Humble Bundles November 2022 collection.

_childDocuments_.review: For a short tl;dr, here's the last couple paragraphs:Raji: An Ancient Epic is a nice, little indie title that I wanted to enjoy, but sadly, can’t really recommend. The setting and aesthetics are great, but the gameplay leaves a lot to be desired. It just seems like everything that mechanically makes a game like this good was an afterthought for the setting. I wouldn’t say the game is strictly bad. It’s just mediocre at best once you know how to play around some of its jankiness. I’m just unsure how many players will actually want to adapt to the jankiness in the first place.The $25 asking price is also a little steep as well for what you’re ultimately getting. The game is relatively short, which is fine, but the replayability is pretty much nonexistent. A new game plus mode would help with this a lot. It wouldn’t even have to ramp the difficulty up. Just give the player the option to experiment with every weapon in the game more comfortably instead of keeping them locked to designated parts of the story. Once the game ends, it just throws you right back to the beginning again on a new save.If you’re in any way interested in the unique Indian setting, then maybe give this game a look if you have nothing else to spend $25 on. Or just watch the developers play on Steam. As for someone who’s just looking for a competent, little indie action game, I’d say give this one a pass.
