_childDocuments_.review: When I first played this game, it seemed a bit promising. From the concept being a game about Indian mythology, to the fact that the battle style seemed very acrobatic and fluid, to the art looking nice, the game looked like a top tier game for my standard.And then, I kept playing.If I were to summarize this game with two words, it would be “immersion breakage.” Every element of this game seems to be intelligently designed for the sole purpose of breaking my immersion:-Raji’s voice acting managed to be both extravagantly dramatic while simultaneously monotone. I still can’t wrap my head around that one. After every battle, she taunts the enemies in ways that fry my cringe-detecting organs to the point that I need a transplant now.-Vishnu and Durga would just, not, stop, talking. It's like I constantly am connected to a live feed of their DM's.-The picture puzzles where you get to see Raji’s memories legitimately come from a children’s game, and not even fit.-The murals where Vishnu narrates different Indian myths honestly doesn’t fit and seems to only be there cause the devs felt an obligation to share Indian culture in the game. If that was the goal, a simple system of collectible notes/scrolls would’ve been more than fine; if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.Battle review:-The battles are extremely choreographed. When I experienced the first few battles, it felt like a good design for a tutorial, where each battle teaches you a concept. But this philosophy continues to every, single, battle in the game. Battle 1: 2 enemies. Battle 2: 3 enemies. Battle 3: 3 enemies and a boss. Battle 4: 3 enemies with 2 bosses.-And don’t get me started on the “difficulty”. The game is insultingly easy, while simultaneously stretches each battle and makes it grindy, which is the perfect recipe for being bored out of my mind. Every time I see a battle arena (and I was able to predict every battle arena because the game is more predictable than the wetness of the pacific), I groan out of my mind, because I know I’ll soon be locked in grind-fest number 1 out of 4 in this singular corridor.-I still don’t get why Durga’s ability is lightning, Vishnu is fire, and Shiva is ice. Not to mention, you can switch your weapon mid combat, but never your Deva/Devi abilities, which beats the point of variety.-The boss battles are confusing. Everything else/miscellaneous: --The battle music was underwhelming. Hiranya Nagari was beautiful, including its music, but other than that, nothing much is going on in the music department.-Any puzzle, from the lotus puzzles in the water, to , to literally any parkour sequence, is just redundant. It fills play time, but theres no challenge whatsoever to it.-The story could’ve been so much more. It wouldn’t have been hard to make both the gods speaking make sense, if only the story included Raji constantly questioning why she’s doing this, while the gods speak without her hearing, so we get to see the disparity between the doubts of humans, and the plans of gods. But Raji doesn't speak or show any tendency for self doubt This, btw, is the short form of my review. There’s just so much wrong going on in the game that it’s honestly heartbreaking. I wanted this game to be good, especially as someone who loves Indian mythology above all others, but there’s only so much you can say before it turns from a Steam review into a blog post.I’ll just end it with this Tl;Dr: Never have I been spoken to by the gods, and I wanted them so badly to shut the f**k up.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to begin to genuinely enjoy this game.  On my first playthrough I didn't realize the importance of learning the attack combos and basically just went through the game button mashing when encountering enemies.  Needless to say, I died quite a few times and got frustrated thinking the game was a bit unfair in it's design of enemies who constantly attack you without much time in between their attacks to make a move of my own (especially towards the end of the game).  However, I decided to give the game another go after completing it and enjoyed the experience the second time around much more.  I really took the time to learn all the moves and combos, as well as the perks.  I found myself having a much easier time with enemies after doing so and the game became much more fluid.This game is very beautiful and the music really sets the tone.  The controls are responsive and easy to master.  I really enjoy hopping around the linear map taking in the views.  My only minor issues with this game are:1. The game does not introduce many opportunities to use some fun platforming mechanics in the game, particularly the running on the wall mechanic.  I would like to have seen this having to been used in some boss fights or just more parts of the map to make the platforming more diverse.  The same goes with the climbing mechanic, although that can be used more often.2. The game is pretty short.  Can be completed in around 4-5 hours.  It ended too soon and I was expecting just a little more game time. 3. The boss battles are fun, but I would have liked to see more, or at least some mini bosses put in.  4. The ending was underwhelming.  I won't spoil anything but it didn't feel epic after defeating the final boss, and the story kind of just ..... well....ended.  (Hard to explain unless you have played the game, but I don't want to give details about what I would have liked to see instead because that would spoil the ending.) Overall, this is a very good game and I would recommend it to anyone who is a fan of linear action/adventure games!

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is a beautiful little game. A lot of love has gone behind the game which shows while you play. _childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely gorgeous and a great introduction to Hindi culture and religion/mythology so for that I recommend it alone.However I do have one major problem with the game that I need to warn you before you buy it:The combat is AWFUL.Your movement is slow, the attacks are clunky, and the controls are terrible (it's virtually unplayable with keyboard and mouse), and some enemies are just annoying. You don't get the best powerups until the very end of the game. The fights felt more like a chore a lot of the time; I often wanted to just skip the battles so I could focus on exploring the lush environment. I don't want to be too harsh on this game because it is good and I know it had a limited production (the dev had to sell her flat to pay for the game), but the combat is really what bumps this down from an exceptional game to just a good game. I still recommend buying it to support indie/international/female devs, but keep this in mind while you play that the combat is not going to be very satisfying.Given that , I do think there will be more, so hopefully they'll be able to improve on the combat then. As it is, Raji is a flawed but ultimately worthwhile experience and definitely a labour of love that you should support.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hate this game, but I can't recommend it. The main thing anyone looking to purchase it should know is that it looks a lot better than it plays, and I don't just mean the visuals: the platforming and combat are all a spectacle to behold in trailers and gameplay footage, but actually playing it is very underwhelming. The platforming is barely even gameplay and the combat suffers from clunky controls, a too-far zoomed-out view, an overzealous auto-aim and position adjustment, and poor sound design. This game is great in a lot of ways. The environments, visuals and animations really are beautiful as is the unique art design, and while the voice acting leaves a little to be desired it's still fairly good. The game just fails in the one department which really matters—the gameplay—so I can't recommend it. If you're the kind of person who can let the gameplay take a back seat to just enjoy the scenery then I'd say it's worth it, but otherwise I wouldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is quite a good game for a brand new dev team. Quite possibly the first actually great game by an Indian team. The Indian setting and the art design are fantastic. The combat and platforming clearly take a big influence from the old Prince of Persia trilogy, and that's not a bad thing. The little Indian mythology story segments I found very interesting, and even learnt a few ones that I hadn't heard of before.However the game does have some pretty big flaws too. The first, most obvious one being the main character's voice actor. Her lines sound quite monotone and lifeless most of the time. Hindi dialog would've been nice too. And secondly, the game has 0 replay value. After the end credits roll, the game simply loops back to the first level with no changes. A chapter select feature and perhaps new game+ would be nice additions. There are some minor bugs here and there too but nothing majorly annoying.Overall I did enjoy the game and I'm looking forward to the team's future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: What a complete ♥♥♥♥ show of a game, sorry!At first I was like: Okay, charming, finally a setting that's not been done to death, India has a rich history and mythology ... and that part was pretty well done, having the Gods basically narrate the experience.Then the first combat sections started and my mood began to drop visibly. Not sure who designed this system, but ... just no.Your basic attacks are useless, since Raji will stop moving whenever you're attacking. No running attacks. That makes almost every basic attack whiff. The only option is to use dodge attacks or wall attacks. The former are wildly inconsistent, apparently also depending on which dodge animation gets used (more on that later) and the latter not always available and impossible to aim.Speaking of aiming ... the game doesn't let you aim with the bow you get later on... you have to rely on the auto aim ... why!? Most of the time the bow just shoots at thin air! We have TWO sticks for a reason, especially since there IS manual aim with the trident, etc.Now off to dodging. As mentioned above, Raji will use three different animations when dodging, all of them wildly different in speed and distance, which makes the game even less predictable ... it looks nice, yes, and she will always do the same 3 combos...it doesn't feel good though, because a player wants consistency in a game that punishes you THAT hard.Enemies bum rush and stun lock you, until you get the shield and sword, which just lets you negate damage whenever you want, basically...the fights are generally uninspired. Dozens of small arenas with 1 or 2 waves of enemies.Then we have the 3 levels, the 2nd of them is actually interesting ... the rest are just you basic ♥♥♥♥.And finally the bosses... oh my god, the bosses. Boss 1 is simple enough for a Souls veteran (And yeah, I've beaten a lot of them), but feels WILDLY out of place in this game. Nothing prepares you for this encounter, only pattern recognition from, you guessed it, Souls games. In normal fights Raji can heal almost to full once she defeats an enemy... in boss fights she can't heal at all. I have no idea what prompted this design choice.The 2nd boss is an exercise in patience, since he takes forever, but doesn't actually DO anything, but you have to repeat the same action 8 to 10 times! And use a certain weapon to actually survive the scream attacks, lol... does the game even tell you that this weapon can do that? Ofc not.And up to this point I was like: Well, it's educational, at least ... Then came the final boss. One that seriously doesn't need to hide behind some of the harder Soulsborne bosses in terms of difficulty ... only: you can't heal.And the boss has a wide repertoire of attacks that he uses in whichever combination he sees fit. Oh, and there are shades attacking you as well, and some attacks almost insta kill you (or stun lock you, yay). I have NO clue who thought it was a good idea to put this much frustration into what should have been a 3 hour narrative experience (seriously, the last 1 hour of the game was spent walking for minutes through an empty desert, then beating my head against this final boss, who requires almost pixel perfect gameplay to beat ... ON EASY).All your weapons become useless and you get a different one that is unreliable at best... why? Just why?!Who was this game made for? It's presented as a chill adventure for adults and kids alike, something you could play with your family ... then they decided: Hey, we need super brutal combat and ultra hard bosses in the game, because it's only 3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hours long. And here we are, I guess! What utter garbage. Should've stuck to making a cool narrative experience, then pitch that to actually make a cool game about India and its mythology. Instead you have this amalgamation of terror that pleases no one ... for the life of me I can't understand why this game is rated "very positive"...

_childDocuments_.review: I've put about 3 hours into Raji so far, and for even this experience alone, the price of admission was more than worthwhile.I don't write up many reviews, but I play countless games. There's been a state of ennui recently with no experience standing out from any other over the last few years. Even the inarguably biggest, best titles of the last few years have built upon tried and true formulas and story telling ethos.I stumbled across Raji's demo during Steam's recent Festival, and by the second combat encounter I was hooked. By the end of the demo (and opening chapter) I was absolutely enamored and while eager, was resigned to another 9-12 month wait for the final product, much as my experience has been with discoveries such as Haven or Exo One. I can't express my utter joy to see this would be releasing only a few days later on 10/15.Based on the Demo alone, I knew I was going to get this game one way or the other. My first two hours of the game have deepened my curiosity and with no idea of what is coming from the story (due to my purely American/Western culture), I am legitimately excited to play this again as soon as possible after the usual "adulting" required.From the stunning art style of the cutscenes (giving me a similar sensation that I experience with Okami and it's representation of Japanese heritage), to the music, completely (literally) foreign story, and the refreshing acrobatic take on combat, even if the experience ended at the 5 hour mark, the quality, passion, and experience are more than worth the asking price. With that said, even a cursory reading into the iconography and imagery presented from the outset, not to mention to mention the upgrade menu that doesn't actually become available until an hour or so in, seems to indicate there is a weighty and varied experience awaiting me.There is no reason to not try the demo. If that piques your interest to any extent, get this. Raji demonstrates the utter beauty and unique experiences that comes from a diversity of background and perspectives from our storytellers.If I HAD to make a comparison, to me, Raji is the love child of newcomer Hades (gratefully minus the rogue-lite elements) and Okami in a pre-Sands of Time Prince of Persia suit.

_childDocuments_.review: It's crazy to see how a game with themes of Hindu mythology can draw a lot of attention. You have no idea how many people would love to see something LIKE , but with Hindu mythology. I was excited for this game when it was first announced. That said, this is the closest experience we can get to that without, uhh, 'offending the masses'. (Can someone just stop caring and make a violent Hindu mythology game ? Please.)Let's first talk about what I like.I like the environment setting and the level design. The developers put in a lot of effort to set the stage for us to get into that Hindu mythology mindset. Nothing felt repetitive. I loved the part where Raji had to traverse through the bluish, watery chambers.My fondness for the levels also extends to the platforming elements; they were decently put together. Nothing that makes it particularly stand out, and it was rather linear in nature. But personally, it broke the monotony of combat, and offered the chance to explore areas.The mythology lore dumps were a nice addition to my journey. Personally, it induced a minor interest in reading up on Hindu mythology. That said, I wish the stories were presented better instead of being an audio podcast in disguise. I understand it can bring up budget costs, which is not ideal. So it's a good compromise. At least it wasn't in written form, which some games resort to.Though puzzles weren't that significantly present in the game, they were okay. But it lacked variety. Turning circles and setting tree structures right again and again became a complete bore soon.The visuals kept my eyes engaged. None of it felt as if I needed a change of scenery. Everything was naturally stitched together. Nothing popped out too hard on the screen. From the characters' names to the setting to the puppetry sequences and to the clothing of the characters, there were a fair number of tells that suggest that you're playing through a Rajasthani tale. So there is visual consistency.The music was great too. The ones in the first few levels felt way too repetitive, but it got a lot better later on. It's quite authentic, and true to the musical culture of North India.Now, the bads.Clearly, the game is  influenced by the first  game. Except one instance felt similar to the Scarecrow sequences from . Most would see this as a bad thing. I, however, don't. The fact that this game was made to play similarly to  — a game that in retrospect was 'AAA' — is an immense effort from the developers to give us something worth trying.But there's a difference between taking an influence and doing something interesting with it. Which is part of game design. And taking an influence and... well, giving it another skin. Which this game does.Let's talk a bit about combat design. As a hack-'n'-slash game, combat is EVERYTHING. Combat design is, in a manner of speaking, a puzzle itself; a moment-to-moment, time-based puzzle with a sense of rhythm to it.Light attacks, heavy attacks, strengths and weaknesses, enemy types, weapon statistics, attack and defense combos and their synergies, powerups, tech hits or fall breaks, crits, frame freezes, haptic feedback, visual impact, etc are all the toppings and cheese of your pizza.But you only get the pizza base. Literally, bread.There's not much to go with the combo system; in fact, there is no combat system. You simply beat your opponents up until they blip out of existence. While you can change your weapons, you'll likely stick with one weapon type all the way through, unless you run into enemies that ... at which point, you'll use a BOW! I was almost blown away by the variety...You also have an upgrade system in which you can power your weapons up with different elements; lightning, fire, and ice. Each of them have three types of passive attacks. The more you progress in the game, the more you discover 'wisps' that act as collectible points to augment these passives.That all sounds great. EXCEPT... there was zero incentive to use them. Pick a type. Stick with it. And Bob's your uncle.You also have an ultimate attack. I probably shouldn't have told you that. It's more fun watching people discover it only after they finish half the game... or discover it and forget about it anyway. I only used it because I never used it. Does that make sense? From a design standpoint, yes: It means it shouldn't be in the game.Execution animations desync sometimes; if you execute the enemy further than usual, you'll likely see Raji hit her Trishul on the ground, and not on the enemy itself. Sometimes, the animations don't play sounds, so the deaths don't feel impactful. The game also does a bad job protecting the player from themselves; if you execute an enemy whilst they are off-ground, the animation will play mid-air, but when it ends, you'll fall to the depths along with the enemy, dying in the process. (Slow clap.)The enemies themselves attack you but without much power behind them. Trolls smashing their clubs on the ground don't give you the sense of 'oomph' you're looking for. If you get hit, you don't 'feel' it. The only thing that stands out a bit is when you hit an enemy and the frame simply freezes for a microsecond, and even that's quite inconsistent in its 'heaviness'. Hitting an enemy sounds like thwacking a newspaper roll on something. Overall, everything feels and sounds plastic and numb.Bottom line: You can beat the  game with a single button, a single weapon, and a single tactic. Enemies have no variety. Everything feels numb to hit. Just button-mash your way through and you'll make Maa Durga proud.Now, the UI/UX. I love minimalist UI/UX. That said, readability and accessibility is crucial. This game lacked them. I couldn't tell how much health I had left, or how much health the enemies had left. Or at least, it was  to tell.I found myself tilting my head to each side to see the back of the enemies' healths to know how much more I should hit them to kill them. I didn't know when my ultimate was powered up. I couldn't skip in-engine cutscenes (argh, the worst!). The upgrade system menu was convoluted to work out.I thought 'User Profiles' was a profile system, but it's actually a simple load/save option. I used a PS4 controller, which for some reason wasn't detected. The camera did not clip through foreground elements. The cursor does not disappear when I use the controller.Overall, the UX was unsatisfying.'Gosh!' You exclaim. 'Don't get your panties in a bunch!'FINE! Let's talk about the story then.Now, I could've mentioned that this game could be for narrative-driven players like me. The thing is... ddntnjyt.'What?'I said I... didn't... njyt....'WHAT DID YOU SAY!?'I SAID I DIDN'T ENJOY IT!It was a run-of-the-mill, girl-save-boy, beat-the-baddie, this-is-bigger-than-you shindig. It's unoriginal. We've heard the story a thousand times. Just the genders are reversed here.There was SO MUCH to pluck from the Hindu mythology! The story could've taken a different direction! Characters could've been fleshed out more! It's a shame that the option to go with a 'tried and tested' story template won over creative risk.The worst offender was the voice acting. Durga sounded fine, but Vishnu sounded parched, and Raji was ... quite frankly, annoying. Her dialogues did  to further the story. Why have them in the first place? Almost every piece of dialogue must provide  of substance to the player. And her screechings of 'GOLU' could give Ethan Mars' 'SHAUN' a run for his money.When I played the demo I had concerns about how the game would turn out. Though it's not too bad, it's not worth a recommend.Unless you got some pocket change to burn.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely action platformer with wonderful graphics.The Indian mythology/culture references turns this game into a very interesting and worthy experience - if the player is into those sort of things. Thus, after the initial "this looks very pretty" impact, I mostly liked the parts where the player is granted with ancient tales.Story wise, because the game is so good looking, the devs used a 2D puppet show style for the cut scenes. This breaks the visual bling routine, and I liked it.The gameplay is allround ok.The levels are mostly linear (not much exploration). Still, some areas get locked behind you so you won't be able to go back if you missed some item because you went right and not left.There are a 4 different weapons, and 3 "elemental powers" (the last weapon is neutral).Our char is a circus performer so she's very acrobatic, and has some parkour abilities as well as a roll/dodge. Movements seems fluid but I feel sprite animations last probably too long - this sometimes made me lose track of my char movements, especially when trying to chain dodges with attacks with climbing off walls and performing some special attack in the middle of several enemies.Tutorials are present ingame and are mostly efficent.Each weapon has its own mechanic, but I usually stuck to the last one I picked, with exceptions to when I would revert to the bow (second weapon) and use a special Left Trigger ability that dealt a lot of damage. On all weapons, I felt collisions needed a better sense of impact - they felt a bit soft. Still, the mechanics are manageable and the fights are not particularly hard. I ocasionally struggled with a new enemy or boss at the first encounter, and beat it fairly easily on the second attempt.Besides the previously mentioned, these things could be improved:Some areas of the game lack proper lighting, and even if those levels could have a darker environment, at least the story murals should always be iluminated.The camera is not controlled by the player. Often I would leap in faith because distances were not clear due to the camera locked angle.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst designed action games I've ever played.The combat functions much like a Souls-like except done in ways that it shouldn't have been.• The dodge is unreliable as instead of a single animation, the game cycles between three or four types, which from what I can tell affect i-frames and dodge distance.• Every encounter is essentially enemies in groups, which wouldn't be a problem if the combat and enemy design were Action oriented instead of Souls-like - enemies attack constantly (no exaggeration) with insane tracking and they hit hard, they poise through your attacks and there's no such thing as enemy group AI, meaning you'll have 5 hyper aggressive enemies on you at all times just spamming attacks from melee/ ranged, no semblance of taking turns or giving you a breather.• The above wouldn't be as much of an issue if the game had lock-on, which it doesn't.• The platforming is super weird and doesn't mesh well with the dodge. Some of the dodge animations seemingly cut your momentum which seemingly cuts your jump distance as well, which puts you just out of grappling range for jumps. Depth perception issues are present as well.• As for technical issues, the game does tend to crash every now and then. There is some stuttering as well.While I will personally stick through the 100% as I've already started it so some achievements unlocked, I wouldn't recommend Raji even on sale. It is a frustrating experience through and through.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the art direction, and the presentation of the story. The setting inspired by Hindu mythology is unique, and I wish there were more games based upon it. However combat, which makes up the core of the game play  was unfortunately unenjoyable.  It's difficult, but not in a good way. Enemies don't get stunned by attacks, and you have no invincibility during combos so combat basically devolves into spamming dodge until there's an opening where you can land one or maybe to hits at the most before repeating. _childDocuments_.review: is an action platformer mostly with a heavy emphasis on story. The game shines in its beautifully crafted zones, it gets people to experience a bit of Hindu mythology, and it shows quite a bit of promise of things to come from Nodding Heads Games, an indie development team. As for the actual gameplay, the game is very linear, you are shuffled from area to area with a need to clear out the enemies that spawn before moving on. There are various platforming aspects of the game as you move along the game levels but never actually in combat. There are basically no puzzles in this game, so that label is a bit misleading. Likewise, it's in third-person, not first.It's notable that the game auto-saves almost constantly, so you pretty much never lose any progress if you die or are forced to quit for one reason or another. There are 4 profiles/saves to choose from.A heavy element of the game is its story, where a couple of siblings Raji (protagonist) and her brother Golu get somehow mixed up in a fight too big for them to deal with. When Golu gets kidnapped by demons from stories, Raji shows her indominable will in going to the world's end and dealing with all kinds of obstacles to save her brother--with the help of several gods along the way.During story-telling, there is minimal dialogue but a lot of narrated commentary and bemusings of a couple of these gods. Aside from that, parts of the story are revealed through back-lit flattened puppet shows. Both of these show plenty of style and reflect the culture whence the story arises. There are also murals giving a few pieces of other mythological tales that somewhat are reflected throughout the game. Even though the individual elements are all neat, they suffer a bit when all put together, giving a bit of a choppy feel. I will leave laments about the story/game's end to myself and simply say that it could have been so much better.The combat always takes place free of any platforming within a sealed zone that you can only leave after that particular fight is done. These are arranged in almost entirely strict order. You effectively use the same buttons/combinations for the first 3 weapons that you gather to their varied effects. The fourth weapon you earn the right to use at the end of the game and is too OP to be included in the earlier part of the game.The combat follows your button presses pretty reasonably well. But once you learn how to deal with the enemies, then it's just a matter of time before taking them down. There are not many different types of enemies, as the same ones keep spawning over and over. Some places it felt like you are just being overrun by different enemies in numbers, and to deal with them, you just have to bide your time. Fortunately more weapon choices and favor orbs a couple of hours in makes the combat a lot easier to handle. The regular encounters were rather satisfying for a while before they started to get a bit old.The boss fights were kind of bland and not too interesting once you figure them out, and then it's just a matter of slogging through the same motions to defeat them in order to move on. They never felt difficult, and at most, felt annoying at having to repeat the same thing a number of times while avoiding death in order to move on. The boss fights were where I really wanted a skip button, and so in that aspect, it was rather disappointing.I definitely recommend the use of a controller for this game.The most outstanding part of this game is its visuals. The short puppet shows in the story progression are really fun to sit through, and the  level designs in terms of all of the objects and 3D models look exceptional. The game's cameras are fixed though, I would have enjoyed having some freedom just to look around.The music is quite nice, and gives you that feeling of being there, synchronizing your brain with the cultural vibes of the game. The sound effects are okay, some places it felt a little lacking. The voice acting was fairly good, not the best. But once again, carried some vibes that resonated a bit with the world and gave the game an extra layer of depth.The price is a bit high, in all honesty. Even if you have a strong interest in the game, it's probably best to wait until there's a reasonable sale. I finished the game and missed collecting 1 favor orb, and thus missed out on 2 achievements, all in 6 hours. There's limited replay value, because there's going to be 0 variation between your first and subsequent playthroughs, except for maybe you would progress a bit quicker.1. Game's combat would have been made more interesting with increasing types of enemies and varied actions. Each enemy had the exact same action path and you can predict what each one will do from the time they spawn in combat.2. Boss fights involve stringing together a bunch of easy actions and just waiting for the encounter to end. These could have been so much more interesting.3. The game is entirely too linear with 0 variability, except for when you go to gather favor orbs. But it quickly falls back on the predetermined path without fail.4. Lore-building could have been stronger to really give some extra life to the world and to make the story fit better within as well.5. The game has a puzzle tag but there's realistically no puzzles. Only a few simple move-pieces-into-alignment items that offer no challenge.Overall the game is good, not great. But it's worthwhile to experience through because it dives into Indian folklore that's not too commonly explored by games and can act as a good educational experience. The level designs are just really fun to look through while you play through. I would recommend that you try out the game for what it does bring to the table, and try your best to overlook its shortcomings because it is a first project from an indie team, after all. Score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Short indian story about sister trying to save her brother from demons. Unfortunately, it is also a game with not very comfortable parkour mechanics (died a little too many times because she jumped in wrong direction) and very poor fighting mechanics. Some enemies' attacking animations are too hard to predict, dodge works only in 75% cases and sometimes doesn't protect from damage. There are 4 weapons, but really only 2 of them worth using with few exceptions. Staff - your first weapon that you will use at the beginning of the game (because you have no alternatives yet), bow - second weapon, absolute OP that allows you to annihilate enemies (sometimes even several at once) by using hovering fire - it does a lot of damage, it's quite easy to use and it's fast. Third weapon - sword and shield, almost useless, you'll have to use it in one of the boss fights and it's somewhat effective against one of the enemy types. And chakram - forth weapon that you will get almost at the end of the game - kills enemies with 1 hit, but almost uselesss against last boss, so you'll just use it in 2-3 battles and then fight with last boss using bow (probably). Probably worth it on sale, not many indian games out there. Purely for atmospheric and "cultural" purposes, but definitely not for having fun from gameplay or story.

_childDocuments_.review: wow. Worth playing, just to see how badly you can mess a game up!Visuals which would bore a nintendo switch to tears. You don't even have a shadow. The character is so small and low contrast in itself that I often could not tell whether I was on the ground or not.Unresponsive controls. She did things. Somethimes she did what i thought she should do, but usually not.Annoying 10 seconds music loop during combat. blim blim blim da da da blim blim blim - repeatYou don't have a hitbox - Its a whole shipping container. However you only notice that you get hit if you watch your health bar (instead of the enemy -who is unreadable anyways)Camera with its own mind - it pans and rotates with your position without giving you control.Unguided level design: you are standing an intersection, there is no way of telling which path goes to the powerup-pick-deadend and which one leads to the next fight/cutscene from which you can't return. Obviously you can't use the camera to look around.Nauseating dodge mechanics. You have continuously dodge everything. Only the camera jerks and wobbles with her center of gravity instead of a smooth motion. That jerky motion also makes the large bland levels even more punishing since you either jerk and wobble mildly faster by stupidly dodging emtpy or trot at very leisurely pace which takes even longer.Technical levels. You can not run up a wall because it is a wall. You can, because it was explicitly tagged for it. Quite a lot of walls aren't. 'puzzles' yeah. figuring out the controls is the hard part

_childDocuments_.review: First playthrough review time.Raji: An Ancient Epic presents a beautiful view of Indian culture and mythology. At first, it seems like a strong game from a new developer. However, as I played more, it became clear that the game lacked depth. Many players may think of the Prince of Persia series when playing, and unfortunately, Raji does not reach that same level of quality.The game takes about 5 to 6 hours to finish. The gameplay moves slowly and does not create an engaging experience, making it hard to stay interested. Many parts feel empty and drag on, which can lead to boredom. On average, I got around 115 to 120 FPS with the highest graphic settings and around 42-47 FPS while turning on all ray tracing options. I turned off global illumination and reflection settings in ray tracing to improve my FPS. The game even looks good if you turn off ray tracing completely. In conclusion, while Raji: An Ancient Epic is visually impressive and shows the developers' hard work, it falls short in gameplay and story.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is interested in mythology and cultures around the world, I was immediately drawn to the setting of Raji: An Ancient Epic, and the game did not disappoint. The Hindu cultural, mythological and artistic elements are present all throughout the game. The landscapes are beautiful, full of stunning environments to marvel at. I found myself often stopping to admire the scenery. These elements are also found in the story and its presentation, the soundtrack and even things that might be overlooked like the design of the user interface. Every single part of this game was made with care and a desire to celebrate Hindu culture, mythology and art.The story is simple but serviceable, and it matches what you would expect of a myth in the making. It also provides you with the opportunity to learn about the real-life mythology that inspired the game.Gameplay is mix of combat, platforming, and some puzzles. There is not much to say about the latter two, except that they offer variety and a decent break from combat. As for the combat; it took me a bit to get into, but once I did I found it a lot of fun, especially as I unlocked new weapons and powers. And for those who do not enjoy the combat mechanics, the game offers a story mode that allows you to fully immerse yourself in the journey.My only complaint would be that the final part of the game gave me the impression that it was either rushed or unfinished, as if time or budget run out and the developers had to cut things short. Unfortunately, this makes for a very disappointing end to a game that started quite nicely.Despite the unfortunate final moments, however, Raji: An Ancient Epic is a game I would highly recommend. It’s not very long, and while neither the story nor the gameplay are groundbreaking, the art, music, and cultural storytelling make it a unique and memorable game that is absolutely worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did. It looked great when I saw the release of it. The graphics are amazing: so much Indian lore and culture jam packed in every frame! The voice acting and music are also superb. I really liked how they had cutscenes in this puppet style, and how the narration is done by two gods chatting to each other.But the combat and controls? Oh my freaking lord. These are the game's biggest downfall.Combat is infuriating. Enemies constantly stun lock you, and it's very hard to tell if you can jump up places for areal attacks. Not to mention: certain flying enemies would randomly fly off screen, which lead me to having to shut the entire game down to respawn them and redo the fight. ONLY FOR THE SAME THING TO HAPPEN AGAIN! >:( Since combat happens every 10 steps basically, you have to deal with these issues A LOT. I'd rather do my taxes than deal with this.The bad controls didn't help either. Quite often Raji would not respond to my inputs, leading to her death and me having to redo things that really shouldn't be redone. I ain't got time for that!These two issues destroyed my interest in finishing the game. It makes me sad cause I saw it was short and I was excited to try it! _childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Raji: An Ancient Epic is a gem that transports players into the heart of ancient Indian mythology and culture, providing a mesmerizing and unique gaming experience. My 4.5 hours spent with this game left me enchanted and inspired, showcasing the potential of storytelling through the medium of video games.At the heart of Raji's excellence is its distinctive setting. The game immerses players in the rich and diverse world of Indian mythology, introducing them to gods, demons, and legends that are not often explored in the gaming industry. The stunningly detailed environments, inspired by ancient Indian architecture and folklore, evoke a sense of wonder and curiosity.Raji's narrative is a heartfelt tale of a young girl's journey to rescue her brother from the clutches of demonic forces. The story unfolds through beautifully narrated cutscenes and intricate shadow puppetry sequences that serve as a perfect storytelling medium. The narrative blends cultural elements seamlessly, inviting players to learn about and appreciate Indian myths and legends.The gameplay in Raji is an engaging mix of platforming, combat, and puzzle-solving. The game is striking in its combat mechanics, incorporating traditional Indian weaponry like the Trishul and Chakram. The fluidity of Raji's combat feels both empowering and graceful, allowing players to unleash their inner warrior as they battle grotesque demons. The platforming and puzzle elements are well-designed, providing a balanced challenge that keeps players engaged.Raji's visual style is a standout feature, and it's clear that the developers put a lot of effort into capturing the essence of Indian culture. The art direction, character designs, and the various realms you explore all combine to create a visually stunning and culturally immersive experience.The game's audio design is equally impressive. The soundtrack, featuring traditional Indian instruments and melodies, sets the mood and elevates the emotional impact of the story. The voice acting, particularly the narrator's voice in cutscenes, adds an authentic and compelling layer to the narrative.The length of the game at 4.5 hours is relatively short, but it is an experience that feels carefully crafted and does not overstay its welcome. The brevity of the game's duration, in fact, leaves players with a sense of longing for more, a testament to its captivating storytelling and unique cultural perspective.In conclusion, Raji: An Ancient Epic is a masterpiece in the world of indie gaming. With only 4.5 hours of gameplay, you've had a glimpse into the beauty of Indian mythology and culture. The game serves as a powerful example of how video games can be a medium for exploring and appreciating diverse traditions and stories. Its stunning visuals, compelling narrative, and engaging gameplay make it a must-play for those who crave unique and culturally rich gaming experiences. Raji: An Ancient Epic is not just a game; it's a journey into the heart of ancient India, and it's an experience that will stay with you long after you've completed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely wanted to support the devs in this game. I didn't play the enhanced version so my review is based off of playing prior to the update. I LOVED the lore in this game and the stories surrounding the gods and characters in the game. The story telling is fantastic! Here is where the game starts to suffer. The fights are the biggest let down. Some are good but eventually it gets repetitive. Enemies don't really respond to being hit or attacked and the sound overall is anti climactic. When you play this game you will immediately compare this to classic God of War. Which is cool! I'm down for that. However, enemy response and character movement can't be ignored. For a game like this I would have been good if more attention went into combat and response. It's bearable and actually looks cool but I would have loved to see some more cinematic sequences when using magic, finishing off an enemy or using certain parts of the environments during combat. I got the game on sale and I think if you catch it on sale and want to support the devs (which I do recommend) the give it a go. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. I love games about mythology and I can usually put up with a certain amount of wonky controls in order to enjoy the story. But I feel a lot of the time that this game could have benefited from a little more time spent on smoothing out the gameplay. I hope that they continue to make games because I think this one has a beautiful setting and some wonderful world building. But it can't only be that, the gameplay has to be a little more decent than I think this is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially Indie God of War.Not 2022 God of War, or even 2018.This is 2005.Visually, the game is as complex as one from that era. Not that it looks bad, but it's really nothing to write home about.From a game play perspective, it has all the hallmarks of the original game it is based upon, but none of the cinematic feels during the fights. The protagonist is always fighting from a distance, remaining very small on screen.The combat mechanics themselves aren't all that different from God of War, either, although the timing for the combos always somehow feel a bit off. As a result, there's never any real satisfaction in pulling off anything complex. You will button mash a lot as a result.There's an argument to be made in favour of the lore and flavor of Indian myths. This being said, You will be subjected to a lot of broken English, which isn't a deal breaker in itself, but can be annoying at times.Worth a play trough if you have nostalgia for these types of games from the Playstation 2 era. Not recommended at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji excels at presentation with a beautiful art style, excellent voice acting and stellar music. The general appeal of Raji stems from it's refreshing and underappreciated take on Indian culture and religion. This alone was enough to convince me to get the game. Unfortunately the bulk of the game play feels very boring at times. the focus of the game, the combat, feels slow and lethargic. Many of the fights having little to excite me after so many encounters. After defeating the first boss I felt the need to shelf the game because I knew that I probably already faced all of what the game had to offer. Other aspects of the game play involve intuitive platforming, and large puzzles that serve as expositional set-pieces. The brisk platforming segments are modest yet engaging enough for players to take in the atmosphere and occasional exposition, and the puzzles are also quite simplistic. Both of these serving as a nice respite in-between the slash-em-up enemy encounters. If you're looking for a straight-forward and narratively refreshing game to sink some time into, Raji is the one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad giving this a negative review, it's a beautiful game in a niche environment not popularly explored but as a game it misses on some very important pieces.The story has a strange weight to it, your hero is a hero of necessity, with no special background yet the game constantly tries to delve into it as if there's some hidden secret to tell. Your brother is apparently some special McGuffin for the enemy, but it's never explained why or where his plan is going. The climax to this game is flat and anti-climatic.The fighting is clunky, which could really use some buffering, as inputs are eaten if you aren't performing no action. Attacks cause you to go flying past enemies with no sense of smart targeting, the bow worst of all causing your dash attacks causing you to fling yourself towards the enemy while running away from them. Balancing on the weapons is fairly poor, with multiple elements but no reason to diversify. Put all your points into 1 element, spam your stagger move for the given weapon, and profit.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short (~6 hours) action-adventure game with light platforming elements. The story follows the titular protagonist, Raji, as she tries to rescue her kidnapped brother and battles demons.There are 4 weapons with 3 elemental upgrades. The weapons are diverse (a trident, a bow,  a sword, and a chakram), while the elements seem similar (+damage to a random target, stun, AoE). They can be upgraded by finding orbs. There are 3 boss battles.The game is completely linear with many points of no-return and uses auto-saves. There is 1 (one) save slot, thus the only way to replay a specific chapter is to manually copy files via Windows Explorer. The camera moves automatically and cannot be controlled with the mouse.The controls are rebindable, 5-button mice are supported. 5MB unbinds itself when the game is launched.Some achievements do not register, if the game is played offline.There is nothing that can be called a puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji: An Ancient Epic is an action adventure game where you control "Raji" a young girl,who has been chosen by the gods to stand against a demonic invasion that has occurred in the human realm and save his littile brother"Golu" from demons.   An Ancient Epic takes place in a combination of isometric and 2D side-scrolling views. One suggestion is a freeform camera would have been nice here to help line up some jumps. Even so, the lack of said feature didn’t hurt the actual gameplay.Overall this game presents story in unique style.The artwork,Music,Story Narration and Visuals are on the mark.Its impressive for the first game of the studio.The weapon upgrade and puzzles(Mandala and tree puzzles) could have been better.Also the game feels rushed at end levels.There are some minor bugs but overall it was a decent experience.The problem with the game was its short story.The entire story can be played in 4-5 hours.Also i am overwhelmed by seeing community's positive response to the game,although some people might get annoyed by seeing patriotism and positivity. I wish good luck to the studio for future projects.Grats to the devs for Game of the year awards nomination.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a beautiful game, the art direction was superb. The voice acting was apt, the music was lovely, the writing and combat however wasn't on par with the art of the game. I loved the stories of the gods, I loved the idea of a sister rushing to save her little brother, but the writing of that story line felt weak. The idea of the journey was fine, the actual meat of the story, not so much. I also thought it was terrible that they ended the game that way, Its obvious that they did that to leave a sequel on the table to possibly capitalize on if the game succeeded. I'll still recommend it though, the art [drawn, music, history] of the game is worth experiencing, even with the negatives.

_childDocuments_.user: The Last of the Star Makers
_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Is it worth $10? I guess. But be prepared to lose track of the story at the end.Would I recommend this game to people? Unfortunately, with a $25 price-point, the answer is no. I beat the whole game in less than 6 hours--feeling like I was just sort of meandering my way through and in not any particular hurry--and call me crazy, but $25 seems ridiculously high for such a short game. I got more play time out of Prince of Persia: Sands of Time back in the day and I'm pretty sure I paid less for it.The sound design is good, the music is lovely, but the mechanics aren't tight enough for me to not switch to "easy" mode about 3/4th of the way through just because I enjoyed the story/art/environments enough to want to finish the game and didn't want to have to put up with the game's poorly executed math any longer. Walking through the environments is nice and pretty well paced with the platforming for the most part, and the game's auto-save system was pretty good in regards to where it would load you when you died somewhere accidentally, but the last "level" feels super empty and nearly loses the good pacing of the rest of the game because of it.I'll admit there were some fun moments early on a la the acrobatics that gave me the same satisfying feeling PoP:SoT used to back on the GameCube--and with a couple of more weapons to choose from to boot--but overall, this game is definitely played for how gorgeous it is and not how well it plays. Big props for a female protagonist and a non-romantic/familial plot-line, not to mention the awesome mythology featured throughout the game, but unfortunately the game just...ends. And without really explaining itself. Like a bad DM who didn't mean to have their BBEG die so quickly, so instead of giving him a second phase, they forgo any illusion of choice and just escalate the ending they intended to have all along, teleport him to the end goal, and announce to everyone that the world ends because they say so. Shrug. Needed a couple of more dialogue lines or conversations to flesh it out. Or maybe something is literally lost in the translation.Also, I ran into a couple of voice line glitches where if I would die right when the VAs would start to say something, the game would cut off the dialogue and then not restart it, and in the final battle I would sometimes die twice back to back because the game wouldn't unload the previous fight properly, so I'd get killed by whatever the boss was doing before I even loaded back into the arena.

The fantastic art direction, mesmerising visuals, storytelling and a rather authentic depiction of Indian mythology are about the only reasons that make this game somewhat worthwhile.We need more games based on similar themes and legends, because right now this is something of a rare gem.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where gamers are board playing Greek, Egyptian or Roman mythology. 'Raji' ushers in a fresh take on the side-scrolling action-adventure, role playing genre. _childDocuments_.review: Help young Raji, an orphaned circus performer, rescue her brother Golu from the clutches of the evil demon Mahabalasura.  Travel through amazing and beautiful realms and face off against hordes of demons in a race to reunite Raji with her brother and save the domain of the devas.Raji – An Ancient Epic is a third-person action/adventure game with platforming in a fixed perspective world.  You play as Raji and, with the help of the gods Vishnu and Durga and their marvelous weapons, you work to defeat a myriad of different types of demons while progressing along five distinct realms to reach the conclusion of the story.  Your weapons can be powered up by finding various favor orbs scattered throughout the game allowing some interesting albeit limited playstyles.The beautiful and colorful graphics are done in the style of Pahari paintings; a popular style of miniature paintings from the Himalayan hill kingdoms of North India during the 17-19th century.  The cutscenes in this game are done in the style of traditional shadow puppets and done very well—both these aspects lend to a rich and detailed story that is enhanced by the narration by Vishnu and Durga while you play the game, the different styles of music for each area, and the stories told through murals depicting scenes from both the Mahabharata and Ramayana texts.The game is spectacular but there are things that need to be worked on.  Raji – An Ancient Epic is a rather short game with no replay value.  One playthrough is enough to complete the story and nothing changes between gameplays.  This is not necessarily an issue, just something to keep in mind.  Additionally, the combat feel sluggish or awkward.  There were many times that I tried to pull of combos but was either too slow, the controls didn’t respond fast enough, or I jumped in a different direction than intended.  I often found myself smashing buttons in hope of killing of a large group of enemies before I got killed.  Other than these two items; I had no issues with the game.There are several achievements to be had in Raji – An Ancient Epic.  Some of them are based on the story and are not missable, but there are several that are quite easy to miss which means that you will have to play the game again if you missed something during your first playthrough if you want to get all of the achievements.I enjoyed Raji – An Ancient Epic and loved how all the aspects came together to create an interesting, playable story steeped in the history and lore of ancient India.  I recommend this game for those who like to play platforming games or for those interested in learning a bit more about the mythology of ancient India.  I look forward to seeing not only more from this developer but hopefully a second part to the story of Raji and Golu in the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, since there is no "mixed" option in reviews I'll go with "recommended".The game sure is beautiful, looks great, runs great. But it has some mildly annoying issues with other things.From positives:- very nice graphics- good platforming- acceptable unique combat mechanics- interesting unique ways to tell a storyFrom negatives:The music is my big complaint, because I keep hearing like ~8 second loops constantly and they drill into my had like a TV commercial in the most negative way possible.The main character voice actress is simply... bad. I wish more time was put into her training or into finding a better voice actress. The voice lines she says after battles should just be removed and burned in the oven... the other lines are not that bad. It is like a different voice actress was performing the after battle lines.Combat is not bad. Though it starts to feel repetitive after almost 2 hours of gameplay.So far I've only noticed the cheapness of some monsters attacks and the most-of-the-time uselessness of the bow "Y" (gamepad controls) attack.If I'm using a bow it would make sense to "increase" distance from the enemy rather than jump towards enemy.So this "Y" attack should allow me to jump away from the enemy, and shoot back. Not jump even closer to the enemy.Also - does the bow's charge attack (X hold) does anything? Didn't notice a difference.And as always (not the fault of the developer), at least in my case, Unreal Engine = resolution problems.If you launch the game and notice it is stretched out or "squeezed", do a quick "Left Alt + Enter" (x2) to remedy this problem.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very pretty, and the story is quite nice. The combat feels punchy, and I do appreciate the fluidity of it all. When they glow red, they can't be staggered, which makes them even more frustrating, because your only course of action is dodge, attack, dodge, attack. _childDocuments_.review: Raji, is a great experience. I say experience because its more like a journey through a mysterious time, places and events tied up in Hindu mythology. The environments are great and the background score too. The cut-scenes have a traditional Indian shadow play style.Gameplay itself is good for the most part. The platforming and the puzzles are too simple and more like filler. The combat is where the challenge is. You fight enemies in arena like spaces with up to three weapons that you can switch anytime. The bow is my favourite. You can use the environment to pull off special attacks too. You can regain health while fighting if you stun enemies and glory kill them. The combat isn't as solid or deep as Bayonetta or something but still the game encourages playing with planning and intention for the most part instead of button mashing.My only problems with game are that it was too short and easy. If you are a casual player or you like Indian mystical themes, you will love it. If you are a serious gamer, get it while its on sale, not for the combat gameplay but for the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji: An Ancient Epic is a really beautiful but a bit flawed action adventure game, before we begin this review I like to thank my friend Snowfae for getting me this game you rock, alright then the story. A long time ago there was a young girl named Raji and her little brother Golu, two orphan children working for a circus, life was tough but they made do and had a loving family with the circus.It was an ordinary day like any other the eldest sister Raji doing her acrobatics for the crowd while her little brother put on a puppet show, until the land became darkened and demons emerged to attack the village, many people were killed and children were captured, children like Golu. But all is not lost as Raji goes after them and with the blessings of the gods like Durga and Vishnu, the young circus performer maybe able to do the impossible save her brother and stop the madman responsible for all this.Okay then let’s go into the likes, the graphics are really beautiful with an incredible use of color, environments and scenery every part of it is just incredible to look at. The levels are really good very diverse and quite detailed with just little touches that make each area stand out and feel alive, it’s just fun to just stop, stare and explore. The story is for the most part good an older sister struggle to get her brother back as well as diving into Hindu mythology it reminded me of games like Never Alone delving into culture and mythology. The gameplay for the most is good as you wield different weapons each one enhanced with elemental powers and having its own unique skill set and unique finisher. The music in the game is really good it definitely has captured the feel of being in India, the voice acting is incredibly good even in English dub, my favorite voice actor has to be the guy who plays Vishnu he just has this nice calming voice to him. The characters are pretty good even those it’s only the main character, Durga and Vishnu, but they're very well written.The enemies for the most part are pretty good each one having their own unique design and feel to them, it’s also interesting because when dealing with certain types of enemies certain Elemental enhancements works better in dispatching those enemies quicker.Now the best two aspects of this game is that one the game it tells you some things about Hindu mythology telling you in mini stories that are scattered throughout the game which are really good, another great thing in the game is the cutscenes each of them done in the style of a puppet show which I found quite unique and beautiful to look at in its simplicity.Okay then let’s go into the dislikes, the game is also a platformer but the problem is sometimes the platforming can be a bit difficult like I missed a landing and ended up dying a good bit, the game's price is a little bit too high I think $15 would have been better even though this was a gift and finally the final boss in the game is absolutely terrible it's probably one of the worst bosses in video games, the boss just to overpowered he has too many attacks, the dodging mechanic to dodge attacks can feel bit iffy sometimes and the weapon you have doesn't have a lock on system so you can miss the boss if you're not looking directly at it.It just felt absolutely terrible and the boss killed me so many times, I mean the boss is it's not hard but fair, it's absolutely hard and unfair, it doesn't take skill to beat this boss it takes a tiny bit skill and a lot of luck to beat this stupid boss. Also as I said the story is almost good, it's just at the ending is a letdown.Okay now that I told you all this Raji: An Ancient Epic is a really beautiful but a bit flawed action adventure game, it has really beautiful graphics, really good mini stories and unique and beautiful cutscenes so I definitely recommend this game but be prepared for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with the final boss, unless they get that fixed and Nerf him a bit in an update.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji: An Ancient Epic is a breathtaking journey through rich mythology and stunning visuals that captivate from the very beginning. Set against the backdrop of ancient India, this game immerses players in a world brimming with beauty and intrigue.Visually, Raji is a masterpiece. The vibrant environments are a feast for the eyes, each location meticulously crafted to evoke the essence of its mythological inspiration.  But it's not just the visuals that shine; the story of Raji is equally compelling. Rich in lore and steeped in mythology, it weaves a tale of gods, demons, and the mortal realm, offering players a narrative experience that is both immersive and engaging.The inclusion of Divine weapons adds an exciting layer to the gameplay, with each weapon boasting unique powers and executions that make combat a thrilling spectacle. The fights themselves are smooth and satisfying.One of the standout features of Raji is its music, which complements the visuals and storytelling perfectly. From soothing melodies to epic orchestrations, the soundtrack enhances the atmosphere and draws players deeper into the world of the game. Additionally, the narration between various deities adds an intriguing element to the story, offering insights into the mythological pantheon and deepening players' understanding of the game world.Overall, Raji: An Ancient Epic is a testament to the power of storytelling and visual artistry in gaming. It's a rare gem that not only entertains but also educates, offering players a glimpse into a mythology rarely explored in the gaming world. With its stunning visuals, and rich narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: "Do you recommend this game?"It's a tough question. On one hand, it is obvious that a lot of artistry and heart were poured into it. The levels are beautifully constructed and are a joy to traverse and behold. On the other, the gameplay aspects feel less polished; Raji's movements are noticeably floaty, especially during combat, where impacts don't appear to carry weight. The music is very enjoyable but in many parts it doesn't seem to match the tone of the story. The story itself is deeply immersed in hindu mythology lore, but the game barely incorporates it into the plot and simply stops altogether for long moments to teach you the tales of deities and heroes - Which I didn't personally mind, since I enjoy myths, but it breaks the flow of the game.The plot itself - which clocks in about 5 hours - is serviceable enough; save you brother who's been kidnapped by an army of invading demons, told as a tale as you act by the gods that chose you as the world's saviour. But then ends abruptly without a satisfying resolution. I also found the puppet-like imagery used by the cut-scenes a bit jarring, in contrast with the rest of the game.In the end, I would say it's still worth playing. It is an enjoyable experience, a crash course on Indian gods' lore, that contains some deep flaws. But I can understand if anyone tells me they're deal breakers.

As many others have said, the Indian culture in general has so much potential for amazing games, and Raji: An Ancient Epic is solid proof of it! Hopefully we'll see more games like this in the futureI loved the boss designs as well! Especially during the last fight (at least for myself haha) it felt challenging and a truly, climatic moment in the story There were some points where combat, which I could see may start to feel repetitive around halfway through the game for some folks, and the last chapter/act felt slightly rushed but not to the degree that it made me not like the story or the game play itself! _childDocuments_.review: Raji: An Ancient Epic is nice game from a small Indian indie studio.It feels like a mix of Prince of Persia and old God of War.Static camera can create some amazing shots for beautiful stylized environment.The story is basic but it has a lot of insights into Hindu mythology. Many story events are shown by visually attractive pupet scenes.Story narrators, Durga and Vishnu, made a great job while Raji VO was a step down.Platforming is pretty good, very PoP style. It is sometimes difficult to judge jumps with some camera angles. Gamepad is a must here !And there is a combat... It is a let down and drags down the whole experience for me. It's unbalanced, clunky and repetitive.There is no progression to it, every weapons has literally the same move set, talents are copy/pasted but with different element and there are just few enemy types that still feel very similar. Player attacks are sluggish while enemies can stun lock you to death very fast.It can be balanced by the devs in patches with tweaking attack and evade speeds, different damage values (you don't feel difference between dealing) and balancing enemy AI and damage dealt.It would be nice to have a chapter select option to have a better replay ability.It's a Nice game but with some tweaks here and there it can be a GREAT game.Still I recommend to play and support Raji: An Ancient Epic devs !

_childDocuments_.review: At first I though the game was a little meh, but playing through I started to like it more.I like that it explains a little about the Hindu mythology.The final boss I read that it was changed and was very difficult which I agree.But despite that I had fun and enjoyed the game. I'd like to see another part.7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Probably in line with what the rest of the reviews say. Beautiful and vivid world, an interesting insight into Indian culture and a story which advances nicely and builds interest well.Ultimately, the ending feels very abrupt and quite disappointing considering the pacing of the rest of the game. There are also a few parts where the game design falls short (the part with a snake just completely ruptured the pacing and made the whole thing feel like a chore). The combat is also quite simple and relatively straightforward.But as an experience, it's worth playing if only to listen, watch and immerse yourself in Indian culture and to learn about the mythology. Which is why the ending feels quite incongruous with the other 4 hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where i wish steam had a rating inbetween good and bad.Positives:The Artstyle is beautiful and the way the story is told is incredibly interresting.I have not the slightest clue of indian mythology and culture, but according to other sources it does a really good job at portraying them, so make of that what you will.The Combat is pretty neat and upgrade options offer quite a variety of gameplay options.That saidNegatives:While the Combat normally is really cool, fluent and surprisingly strategic at times, shortly befor the boss you get an incredibly overpowered weapon with only one funktion, throwing all strategy out the window, which was very disapointing.The Story itself, while beautifully told, seems really weird and confusing? Im not gonna go into details, but the ending seemed more like a midpoint or something and satisfactory at all? Tho that could just be because i dont know anything about indian mythology...It feels quite a bit overpriced, seeing as ive completed this 22€ game in about 2 hours, without speeding anywhere and dying a couple times, except if im missing something and theres actually some sort of secret ending or something, but even if there is, im not motivated to play it again sooooConclusion:wait for a sale if you really want, and maybe read up on some indian mythology

_childDocuments_.review: A fun action adventure game, a mix of classic god of war combat with prince of persia traversal I enjoyed the story, there are 4 weapon types to unlock, a spear which you start with, a bow, a sword & shield, then the 4th is a spoiler so I won't ruin it. with 3 element upgrades, each of which also have 3 different power ups within the element. upgrade points can be added and removed whenever, so you can mix and match element powerups and styles which I likedupgrade orbs are scattered throughout the levels, as well as the interactive story elements.there are puzzles to solve in the game, none of which are too difficult, but are required to further the story, which was a nice way to break up the pace of the game.there are several enemy types that you encounter, ranged, flying, close combat heavy, quick attack enemiesso you will want to make use of all your weapons to deal with different situationsyou can also run up walls and pillars to do larger scale attacks and attack enemies from above, which ads a nice level of acrobatic combat to the game.the boss fights are especially good, though I do wish there were more of them.not a long game, I beat it in about 5 hours8/10

_childDocuments_.review: • The game is well made. Lore is good. Graphics are good. Level variety is good. Level design is good but was expecting more exploration opportunities than we got. Weapon variety and upgrade system is simple but fun to play.• Controls are okay-ish, but the "unreal engine curse" continues here. I am pretty sure every game I played that is made using Unreal Engine has wonky-janky movement mechanics, not in games where devs made their own movement mechanic like AC/ACC. I think it has to do with using same code or using same asset. I like point-click to attack mechanic, its different from traditional move-click attack mechanic.• I expected a game like this to be able to run on my pc build at 200+ fps but max I got 75-ish fps @ 1080p all high settings. While I get 100+ fps in most big scale games. I guess they didn't want to optimize/compromise some of the details.• The enemies can be annoying in "mid game" sometimes, but they are not hard or too easy...just enough to keep it fun. All the boss battles are fun except the final boss battle.• This game, story of Raji, has better arc and character development than Star Wars Ep 7-9 (I guess even a indie horror movie will out beat those movies) but not necessarily a comment on the story arc of this game. The story is well written and presented! The cut-scenes are unique and beautifully animated. Voice acting and sounds are well done.• Gameplay to price value is good. Definitely worth the buy!

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is this the best Indian video game I have ever played, it's also one of the most beautifully and meticulously crafted games I have ever seen.Pro's:- The story is engaging and original. You get immersed in Raji's quest to find her brother and in the other quest that the story unfolds around her. I stopped playing Assassin's Creed Oddessy to play this game.- The combat is fast and every weapon has a different range of attack and purpose that it is suitable for. The 🔱 is a melee weapon with a large, scything range of damage. The 🏹 is a ranged weapon with destructive AOE attacks. The 🗡️🛡️ is close range, but it's the only weapon that lets you block attacks instead of dodge, and packs much more of a punch than the 🔱.- Besides weapons, you also get elemental blessings in the game, and favour shrines with which you upgrade those blessings. The three elemental blessings in the game are ⚡, 🔥 and ❄️. Each blessing has a passive attack, a basic attack overlay and a special AOE attack, each of which have three levels of unlock, for which you need to find the favour points (white light shrines). My personal favourite is the 🔥 blessing, but it's subjective for each gamer.- The lore in the game is plenty and very interesting, even for Indian gamers, who may or may not have heard various versions of this lore in their childhood.- Game mechanics have a bit of several games. The acrobatic combat is reminiscent of Prince of Persia. The isometric view with fast paced combat and mortal vs immortal themed story is reminiscent of Diablo. But none of the aspects of the game are so relatable to other games, that it feel copied. Even the code feels like inspired but original code.Cons:- No health bar. This is unsettling, specially in the first boss fight of the game. That's where you realise that while the boss has a health bar (it appears as spokes of light around the boss, and keeps reducing with every hit it takes), Raji doesn't have a health bar. After that, you hey used to it. (Maybe there's a difference between easy and hard, but there shouldn't be. Raji should be allowed to die in combat at some point, even in Easy).- Besides the white favour shrines, there are also golden shrines and purple shrines. Their crystals/lights can be collected, same as favour crystals, but I don't know what they do. Do they enhance the weapon damage? Do they refill health? Do they reset cooldowns? I did feel that the golden crystals reset cooldowns on the special elemental attack, but there is no indicator to prove it.- No side quests. The only reason that side paths other than the main path exist is to house secret location for favour shrines. There are no side quests in this game. Hence, the game finished in 5 hours, while playing in easy at a leisurely pace. A faster gamer would finish it in 2.Overall, this was one of the best short games I have ever come across. I would recommend every gamer to at least try this game, if not finish.Overall, I loved the game

_childDocuments_.review: This is a step in the right direction for Indian Game development scene. The game has a lot of flaws but it shines in a lot of areas and the next project this studio pursues, will hopefully take these feedback into consideration. Coming to the game, it is a very simple story of a girl, who had her brother kidnapped and her quest to get him.: 6.5/10 ( I wish Steam had something instead of a yes or no): 10/10. The highlight of the game imo. The classical Indian music was really good and it went very well with the themes of the game. It was soothing and made the experience great.:8/10. I enjoyed the environment they made. The temple segments felt really amazing. Although the level design felt clunky/rushed in a lot of places. Puppet based cutscenes were amazing.:6/10. From a mythological lore aspect, it was really good but the main storyline felt lacking and had a lot of unexplained elements with the ending being very anticlimactic.:5/10. I did not enjoy the combat. It was a hit or miss most of the times and Raji had a lot of unnecessary animations. The perks did not affect much and leveling them up did not affect the combat. A lot of the fights felt tedious and it was like fluff and not a part of the game.Overall, its a decent game with its highlight moments but the combat and story felt really underwhelming. I would suggest picking this up during a sale or now, if you wish to support the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I loved it. I'm mostly invested at this point in the gods and stories but playing it is literally painful at times (hand cramps from repeated actions on a controller). Combat feels super button mashy, there are times you can do combos or strategic dodges, but its hard to time since youre so zoomed out you can barely see yourself (I played on a tv). The platforming is super basic, its again just button mashing a single button, the "do cool stuff" button. So basically, you walk along a linear path, and every few meters, a combat encounter appears and you just button mash your way out of it, or die but theres really no consequence to dying, it autosaves all the time. Then maybe youll encounter a cool vista you platform in while the gods give interesting exposition, but then you have more button mashing fights and then a "puzzle" where you just spin concentric rings until it makes the picture.I think I might be done with this, maybe I'll just go pick up a book on hinduism from the library for my god mythology fix.
