_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly great, the visuals and art were fantastic! Great job by the developers on this artwork. As far as the gameplay goes there are few flaws, some being like platforming bugs (not able to jump to next platform) and the combat felt unfinished, it was okay could've been done better. Voice acting for Durga was the best I could expect, but as for Vishnu it was kind of poor, I did not get the feeling as it was voice by Vishnu, but this is a small issue afterall to be ignored.The story goes unfinished at the end I think? Like what happens to the world after the door has been opened?Raji and her brother, Golu who both are living their life off street performing seem to not have much real background in their life. It felt like Raji won the lucky lottery to wield the power of the Gods. The story was half decent. Improvement could as well be seen there.The Hindu mythology in the game is perfectly explained (not everything, but a few stories) for people who have not heard much about the Hindu culture or are new to our culutre with beautifully painted pictures in the game.Overall, I give this game a 7/10. Great work by the Indian Developers that made this game, they deserve full support for this game to be a major hit in the Indian market and also all the best for their future projects and more good upcoming games made by Indian Developers. _childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this debut entry from Nodding Heads Games. Whilst the gameplay was not groundbreaking and on occasion could be repetitive this was saved by the fantastic presentation and interesting and unique setting. I can't think of a single other game that has explored this rich mythology. The gameplay is a reminiscent of old school Prince of Persia, but with a Diablo style combat. The combat and platforming is a little clunky but still enjoyable.Visually I thought the game was stunning, the environments where excellent and the enemies pulled from the Mythology were interesting. I also thought that the "Cut Scene" storytelling through the shadow puppet displays was also really interesting.Look forward to what this team produce next.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is no doubt a great first try , but at the same time it has its fair share of flaws. Let us first go through the things that I liked about the game1.  : The game is amazing to look at from start to finish. The architecture of buildings and the design of enemies are great. Never once I saw something that felt off(water is probably one thing that seemed off but water is something thats hard to get right so I will give that a pass). I really liked boss designs(except Mahabalasura, whose design I found to be underwhelming compared to other bosses like Rangda for example). I loved the wall paintaings and also the unique puppet style cutscenes. Great job on this2. : The soundtracks were great, they always were nice to listen to while walking through the world of raji. I especially loved the soundtracks that played when I was looking at wall paintings and hearing the stories. Battle music felt a little minimalistic but for the most part did not bother me.Now I am gonna come to the aspects of the game that I am not fond of.1.  : Level design in raji did not bother me in the beginning but as I continued playing I saw a fundamental flaw in it. Its feels quite artificial and inorganic. Levels in the game dont feel like its natural or something that was built by people in the world, rather it feels like it was built specifically in order to keep combats at certain points. For example, a narrow passage, then a circular section for combat, followed by another narrow passage. This makes the world less believable and more artificial. Also the random placement of pillars in these circular section also seemed off as their only purpose was to facilitate combat. A good level design/ world building is when everything feels organic. things shouldnt feel like they were placed there for the benefit of the player but rather because it serves a purpose in the world.2.  : Probably the weakest aspect of the game. Combat has one light attack combo and one strong attack combo. Although these two can be mixed, the long and stiff animation sort of breaks the combat flow. The dodge animation is also not good when chained, the first dodge is quick whereas the second dodge has a longer animation, I dont see a purpose for that. After 2-3 fights you would experience everything combat has to offer, so from the 4th fight combat feels repititive and just a hindrance. The only time I looked forward to combat was when I got a new weapon. If the skill tree was tied to combat, and if the skills enhanced the skillset by maybe adding new combos or special attacks, combat would have remained fresh. When I recieved the last weapon, I was just happy I could quickly kill everyone so that the combat could just get over and I can move ahead. Boss fights are also nothing to write home about. The worst one being the rangda fight, which was quite boring and frustrating because it was same thing rinse and repeat and if you die, you have to do all of that again(I died a lot of times here because of the slow animation of the second dodge). The camera also feels like its fighting against the combat system. There have been a number of occations where I couldnt run up a pillar or wall because it was hard to judge the direction and distance because of the camera3.  : I think the main reason why the story didnt click for me is because Mahabalasura did not feel like a good villian . We barely know anything about Raji so its hard to gauge her personality, same with pretty much anyone else in the game. The only characters who felt like had some character building was Durga and Vishnu. Maybe if the game was longer then the story could have been written in a better more interesting way, but I understand that the length of the game is probably due to budget reasons so I wont criticize too much for the story aspect.4.  : Voice acting for the most part was a hit or miss for me. Its definitely not bad, but Its not so good either. The only voice acting that I kind of liked was of Durga. I get the feeling that the voice actors are trying hard too eliminate the "Indian Accent", especially for Vishnu and I feel like it removes the charm. For example when I heard Vishnu pronounce 'Pippalada' as 'Pipplad' I have to say that I was kind of disappointed. Big western game developers go to great lengths to localize their dialogues to local languages, so I dont see why Raji cant be voiced in Indian accent and pronounciation. Overall the voice acting was not bad by no means. But it wasnt great Either:Raji is a wonderful first try by Nodding Head Studios. Many gaming startups could only dream of making a game like Raji. But it does have a lot of flaws. As its great presentation and soundtrack tries to push the game up, the mediocre combat system, story and level design pull it down. Nevertheless, I want to congratulate the developers on their first game. You guys did an amazing job and I cant wait to see what you will be doing next. I really hope to see a bigger and much better game in the future! The game is a good buy on steam for INR 539. INR 599 is a hard buy for a game thats this small, so if you are worried, wait for a sale. Final score : 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: On the outlook this game looks like it could be something good but it comes across as something more lacking and pretentious. The gam itself has a mix of platforming, combat and puzzles in the form of rotating and moving objects, if the game stuck to platforming and puzle elements it would be a much stronger experience but the combat is just painful. You have multiple weapons that you pick up throughout the playthrough, the first and the last feel practically identical with a bow in the middle, the bow only remains useful due to its range. The momentum of the combat and the options available such as wall attacks and combo moves are kind of neat but everything feels off. There's no good sound design to go with it all, it feels like you're swining at nothing. On top of this you also get random skill points to upgrade elemental damage, the only thing to note here is that as with the weapons, you should just use the most recent one as they are direct upgrades. Honestly the upgrade system just feels like a waste of time and would have worked better as each weapon just having the attributes of the elements to make them more varied and give the enemies weaknessed to certain damage types. Moving opnto enemies. In a 5 hourish experience you run into around 6 enemy types. That's not a lot of variation and it really makes the combat even more droll. The boss fights aside from the last boss are actually ok, nothing great but visually interesting. The story is as basic as they come, gotta save your sibling, throw in some narration and a lot of cutscenes and exposition and away we go. It gets dull and boring. It all felt so unnatural and forced and could have mostly been played out in the game but instead you're lectured to and given lengthy slow cutscenes which kill the pacing of the game even more. And for the love of god the snake part is the worst thing I have experienced in my life, no tension, just boring, pretty much sums up 70% of the game. At least the visuals and music were nice but this game could have been so much better and wasn't

_childDocuments_.review: is a visually stunning journey through Indian folklore that offers a rich tapestry of culture and mythology which often goes criminally underrepresented in video games. The music is mesmerizing, and the cutscenes adorned in the style of Pahari paintings are a unique style never before seen in video games. The newly-added Hindi dub is very well done and completes the entire package.As a South Asian myself, I very much so appreciated the game's dedication to representing the diversity and richness of the region's culture and mythology. The incorporation of Hindu mythology into the game's narrative is a refreshing departure from the norm, offering players a glimpse into stories and legends that are often overlooked in mainstream media. From the stories of powerful deities to the mythical creatures, the game does an incredible job at seamlessly weaving together all of these concepts. Optional in-game murals also provide voiced background details on the main deities represented here (Durga, Vishnu, and Shiva) for those who are not as well-versed.This game is a visual marvel that does a fantastic job at immersing players in a breathtaking depiction of Indian folklore and culture. Every moment is a visual feast for the eyes. I found myself taking screenshots all too often! The intricate details of Rajasthani architecture, cutscenes that combine the styles of Pahari paintings and Kathputli; every scene is a work of art. The scenery and design elements in my opinion serve as a testament to the dedication of the developers in authentically representing South Asian culture.One of the things that I found to be a major frustration was the game's exploration mechanics. Hidden upgrades are often missed due to unclear pathways and lack of backtracking options. The decision to block off certain paths after progressing further exacerbates the issue, leading to missed opportunities for upgrading your character. It was frustrating to feel limited in my abilities, only being held back by the game itself. Luckily by the end I had found enough orbs to fully upgrade, but getting there was harder.The level design is fantastic though, and I found going through each area to be incredibly satisfying. Especially staring at those visuals! I wish there was more seamless integration between world movement and combat. Usually getting into a pre-determined area where enemies will spawn locks off the area for combat until all enemies are eliminated. This stunts the flow of the game.While  excels in its visuals and storytelling, its combat mechanics leave much to be desired and are easily the weakest part of the experience. Although the concept of utilizing the terrain adds a very interesting dimension to the gameplay, the execution feels lacking, with combat often devolving into repetitive button-mashing. Many enemies also leave little to no opening, so the combat quickly devolves into mashing the dodge button until you wait and wait and wait to find a slight opening and send out one or two attacks. Boss battles, in particular, suffer from a lack of depth, becoming tedious battles of attrition rather than engaging tests of skill. The absence of a lock-on system only serves to further the issue, making it difficult to effectively target enemies and execute strategic maneuvers.Despite its flaws,  is a remarkable achievement and huge step in Indian game development and South Asian representation, showcasing what I believe to be  highest quality video game production to come out of the region. While the combat mechanics may fall short of expectations, the game's stunning visuals, rich narrative, and authentic representation of South Asian culture make it a journey worth embarking on for anyone eager to explore the wonders of Hindu mythology and Indian folklore. Hopefully they can improve the combat in a potential sequel, which I definitely would buy!

_childDocuments_.review: Two performers, Raji and Golu, brother and sister, are alone in the world. They work at the carnival with other performers, the only family they have. During one day of festivities, while Raji is performing acrobatics high up on the rope and Golu is entertaining the crowd with his story, demons attack the city and take Golu. As Raji is unable to save her brother, she receives help from two gods that watch over her. While one has some doubts about her, the other grants her the Trishul, a legendary trident that can defeat demons. The first sign that you're about to play something memorable is the very first cutscene. All of them are wonderful and use shadow puppets to tell the story. Since most of us are not familiar with the Indian myths and terms, the game tries hard to explain so that you don't feel lost in so many unfamiliar words. The learning also comes during the quieter moments of the game, where you examine murals that tell the story of the gods or reveal snippets from Raji's life.The stages are equally impressive. Everything is so big and grand that Raji looks almost insignificant. I would've liked a few more details, as some feel a bit too empty, but the silver lining in this is that the journey takes you through various settings. Upon reaching the end of the level, you have to reconstruct a tree by rotating several layers. This is very easy because statues around the tree show when you're gone too far; they crumble and become whole as you rotate. Since Raji is a performer, she has no trouble climbing tall columns and jumping over bottomless chasms. The same can be said about her fighting abilities. She is able to perform three quick attacks with either one or the other attack move, or a combination of both. There isn't much difference between them because combat consists mostly of button mashing and dodging. Dodging can be performed at any time and as many times as you want. There is no cooldown period and you can do somersaults all day. Trident can be thrown as well, but that is mostly used for puzzles or enemies you can't reach. The other weapons you receive from gods are bow, sword and shield, and chakra, the ultimate weapon that makes others completely useless.Battles take place in special areas. Once you reach one, the area gets enclosed with a magical line that disappears only when you defeat all enemies. You never know how may there are because they keep showing up. The small demons fall quick and their attacks are easily avoidable, so they don't pose much threat. The only one you have to worry about is their special attack, marked by a glow. However, larger demons are much more dangerous. Even a single one can take you out with a few swings of his club. Other creatures, like quick goblins and flying pests, make things a little less boring, but Health is represented by a colored circle underneath Raji. It goes from blue to red the closer you are to death. Enemies have a similar circle with one little difference: once they reach the red zone, enemies can be killed instantly. Executions are also the only way to recover health during a battle. Environment plays a role in those battle areas. Raji can grab onto a pillar to swing around and hit everyone or use a wall to jump higher and come down with a powerful attack. Sometimes the enclosed area will form around a shrine that allows you to perform a special area attack. This can be recharged every time you hit an enemy and there's a loud noise when it's full. If you feel overwhelmed by enemies, you can upgrade weapons by offering orbs to one of the three gods. Durga, the first god you unlock, can add random lightning strike or longer duration of electrocution. Later you gain two more gods that grant you fire and ice. These white orbs can be quite hard to find and they're always hidden away from the main path, but they make combat trivial. While it's true that you can add power to any weapon and upgrade any power, you can easily stick to one and beat anything the game throws at you. Chain lightning is especially powerful when fully upgraded; I learned the best way is to just spam one attack button. If you don't like a certain power, you can always remove orbs and upgrade something else. Purple and yellow orbs are also present, which grant health and special attack respectively.I was a little disappointed that you couldn't revisit levels after you were done with the story. This means you're out of luck if you missed any of the orbs and wanted to collect everything. It's true the game isn't that long, but there are a few unskippable sections where you're forced to listen to the slow retelling of the story.   Rating: 7/10Reviewed by:

_childDocuments_.review: The Indian art style is the predominant factor that got me into this game and I got it for just 2$.  The unique artwork and soundtrack does stand out as a refreshing experience with a slight reminiscence to sands of time. It all falls apart when you actually get into the game loop. It was just a mediocre experience. There was nothing in the core game loop that snatched my attention. It could be a better game if it had released 10 years ago with a different character (I am mentioning this because of reasons which I will explain in post review).  The enemies, puzzles and levels are just so forgettable and does not grant any challenge. The main character was not interesting at all and she is one of the terrible video game character I have recently played as. The game holds some amazing vistas with a decent soundtrack and this is the only reason for me to recommend this game. Okay... now for some rant.I mentioned in review that she is a terrible video game character. Allow me to reason this. The game establishes that she is just a normal woman with some parkour skills holds an unknown prophecy which upon unfold gives the power to slay demons. Also the game accidently establishes the character as an innocent coward when she first encounter a dead soldier and says "wake wake. do you sleep?".  Literally it was so cringy that it squeezed my nerves. Adding to that, her constant crying out for her brother in every cutscene, with very bad voice acting which not even have the slightest attachment to the gameplay. Raji's dialouges felt like from a typical Indian TV serial and this was the most disappointing thing for me.The following issue I have is not about the game, instead its about the idiotic Indian gaming community. Some are supporting this game for exposing hindu religion and some of its mythologies to gaming world. But why?. What is the need for this. Explaining them doesn't make the boring game play better. Also some people are supporting the game as a fresh approach from an Indian developer and one of the developer needed to sell her house to keep the game development running. Here's my take on this. ♥♥♥♥ off. Yes I admit, in India developers usually don't get funding for ideas like games and it was sad that a dev had to sell her house to keep the flame alive. But the game itself feels outdated and boring. Old prince of persia games, AC chronicles, Trine, many nintendo's mario/zelda spinoffs are some better references which I can point out from my experience. There is nothing special that sold me out and wanted to recommend this to anyone and I won't recommend on the basis that this an attempt from an Indian studio. That is cheap and anti competitive.

_childDocuments_.review: I must say that I was surprised by this game; it is really well made, and while the combat is nothing to write home about, the overall story and environment are quite enjoyable. It is something that other games do to (like the Yakuza series for example, where you only have Japanese voiceover and it is amazing in that way); and I prefer it to the English+accent option, which to me is not enjoyable at all. _childDocuments_.review: I definitely don't recommend this game. Its only redeeming qualities are the somewhat breathtaking scenery and the good animations, plus the whole hindu mythology theme, which are what drew me to this game in the first place. But the negatives most certainly out-weight the positives. First of all, the combat is terribly balanced. You have so little combos to choose from, which is something that really restricts you (up to 3 chain light or heavy attacks, or some combination of light and heavy, which is not much). And you only have to 3 weapons available to use, the third of which works in a similar fashion with the first one you. On the other hand, enemies are way to aggressive and can chain attacks at the same time (which staggers you), while you can not stagger them. This forces you to either spam dodge and hit once you find an opening, which is often after 3-7 dodges just to get a hit or two in, or abuse the terrain whenever possible, spamming on repeat the climb-on-the-pole/wall attack. Otherwise, you are gonna spend a crap-tone of time in each encounter. The game also has poor level design, not indicating in the slightest which is the main path and which is the dead-end with the upgrade on the end, making it possible to reach the ending without fully upgrading a single weapon element (electricity, fire or ice). Speaking of upgrades, the game kind of forces you to fully upgrade an element, as this is significantly more powerful, that spreading your upgrade orbs towards all the elements, and thus having each weapon equipped with a different element for each situation. As for the story, it's just there, with the ending being an even bigger disappointment than I expected. And finally, the game is full of awful design choices that does not make any sense and could be avoided with a 3 hour search on YouTube about basic game design. For example, there is this classic scene where you have to move from pillar to pillar and hide behind them, because if the enemy sees you it's game over. Well in this game this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scene took over 10-15 to do (not counting the restarts), either because the animations of the enemy were too long and he wouldn't move to search elsewhere, or its A.I. was bugging or resetting on the spot. It took around 1.30 minutes of waiting behind each pillar before I could move to the next one, and there were about 10 of them. Also the final boss really sucks. To do any proper damage to its gigantic health pool, you had to use the final and fourth weapon of the game. Problem is that this weapon only uses light attack mechanics and nothing else, effectively reducing your options to just dodge and attack, and disabling the other combat mechanics, which is exactly the opposite of what a final boss should be. You should start off with little to do and acquire more ways to engage in as you progress, with the final boss requiring all of your skills and weapons you have gained during your playthrough. And speaking of dodging and attacking, you will have to do a ♥♥♥♥-ton of that during the final battle (my thumb hurt from my first attempt at this). This boss is insanely hard and unbalanced, even in the lowest difficulty, as I have read online (I made the mistake of playing on hard). The boss can down you with 5 hits and after some point he starts teleporting while having his attack animations ready to go (as soon as he tps you might take dmg). I only beat this 5 minutes tops boss fight after 2 hours, and that's because I abused the game's mechanics, as I was forced to do with every single fight after some point ( for this one I used animation cancel on my attacks while nearly hugging the boss, which took care of a huge chunk of his hp pool at a time, while partially stun-locking him). All in all, this had the potential to be a great game, but the developers didn't seem to know what they were doing, which ended making this game extremely frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: well, i played the demo and thought "i think this combat needs a lot of polishing up but i'm interested", then i played it when it came out and thought "oh they didn't really fix it" and got a refund. then i saw the Enhanced Edition came out and bought it again, and well... they still didn't fix it. :(on normal, enemies are tedious damage sponges, so i changed it to easy mode and it only helped a little. the combat is painfully unfun because hit detection is weird. even on easy, the bosses were surprisingly hard and way too long - my thumb hurt from mashing the dodge button on the final boss. annoyingly, the powerups you find to upgrade your weapons makes it harder to regain health during fights because you can't perform finisher moves. the unique finishers seem like misplaced effort when everything else is no fun. also, i havent seen anyone else mention this, but the upgrade menu UI is super unintuitive and i hated trying to assign my points. bizarre button choices there.i actually felt like the game milked its graphics a little too much, and wasn't very impressed except for a couple areas. the snake enemy looked especially bad. i dont like raji's voice acting (english), it fell pretty flat when she was trying to be threatening. i was disappointed that the indian mythology was in closely-grouped murals that you are meant to stand still and listen to. couldn't i at least be platforming while i listen? platforming and puzzles were trivial and brainless, but much appreciated because anything is better than fighting. to top it all off though, the game ended with an unresolved cliffhanger. i basically powered through because i bought it a while ago and it was time to put it to rest. but damn, i am disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful platformer from a group of small developers in India, Raji excels in storytelling and gameplay through a combination of simple but beautiful primitives that elevate the game to new heights. Based on Hindu mythology, Raji follows the quest of a daunting young girl of the same name as the title, to find her brother abducted by a demon called Mahabalasura. The quest takes her through many temples, fortresses, caverns, valleys, and lost cities fighting against any demon who stands in her way. The game in captivating and have an adequate amount of easter eggs riddled throughout the places which tells stories about some of the Hindu Gods and Goddesses.

_childDocuments_.review: 本作は古代印度を舞台に華麗な光景やら興味深い神話を聴かせてくれる一方、戦闘メカニックがややこしい。ハード以外の難易度でプレイしたらお勧めですが、挑戦を望む方にはバランスの良い戦闘体験を期待しない方が。TL;DR: + Gorgeous+ Indian mythology- Traversal mechanics- Combat system!!----------------------------------------I would have recommended this game had all the difficulties been properly balanced. At this stage, I feel that only players who have chosen Easy or Normal would appreciate it. Having played on Hard for the entirety of the game, this is what I think about this difficulty in particular: + The game can be hard indeed.+ The final boss is kind of fun.- The weapon load-out and combos limit your fighting options greatly.- Dodging doesn't always work as intended.OVERALL Positives: + An exceptionally beautiful indie game. Every frame is a pleasure to look at. Well done!+ A game taking Indian mythology and spinning a story around it? Intriguing!+ Different weapons wielded by gods that can be upgraded - even better!Neutrals:= Audio design - works, but could be much better. Even with just a few tracks, the sound feels authentic. It doesn't always work during combat engagements, though. Ambient sound is a tad on the poor side.= Story is bland and the ending is abrupt and unclear.Negatives: - Traversal can sometimes feel punishing. - Combat, combat, combat. ----------------------------------------TRAVERSAL:There are sequences where you have to jump from hanging poles. Since the camera of the game is static, you cannot change the perspective in order to perfectly aim each time... Leaving one opportunity - just push in the direction of the pole you want to jump on and press the jump button.Prince of Persia introduced this mechanic and made it simple - as long as you are facing the correct direction by holding onto the directional button, you can just press jump and the prince will jump, land, and be safe. He even moves a bit to adjust before jumping if you are not perfectly aligned and might miss the pole. In Raji, this mechanic is not utilized, so you can imagine how it goes - jump, fall, die, try again several times until at some point you manage.This made going through places with poles very unpleasant, feeling pressured that I need to be perfectly aligned each time before jumping. There are also some water lilies you jump on and wood constructions to climb that, similarly, require you to be very precise for no reason.COMBAT:I do not consider myself good at games, but I like it when I feel a sense of progression. There is hardly such a thing here. Raji's combat is simple - you hit and you dodge. There are three-hit combos that look pretty cool, and you also have aerial attacks. So, the usual, right? Hit & dodge. Well, yes, but not quite.Enemies are quick on Hard mode. They do not wait for you much. And when they are many, they attack at different intervals. That's actually the good part, which makes the game hard.The deal breaker is that you don't really know when you will be hit. The enemy attacks are telegraphed by them preparing to hit or jumping at you. This works as long as Raji is capable of dodging those attacks one after the other. For whatever reason, though, her dodge rolls (and jumps) do not chain seamlessly. They don't have to, since otherwise you can dodge all you want. After all, there is no stamina bar. Still, considering the gap between the first dodge roll and the second is large - a couple frames longer - enough to allow the 3-7 enemies on screen hit you with a melee or a projectile. Once you are hit, you are staggered for several frames. This means another incoming attack may hit you. And very often, it does. When the attacks pile up like that, you die instantly or are left nearly standing. What's more, sometimes, when you press the dodge button multiple times, Raji starts dodging by herself and moves in random directions, and enemies deal her damage again.But okay, let's say you dodge all the attacks. What then? You attack, right? Attack you do. But you don't. Because Raji's attack animation takes time and enemies do not sit still during that time. There are 4 weapons in the game. You can use only one of them while dodging. When you get out of a dodge and you press the attack button quickly enough, you perform a quick attack, which hits harder and looks cool. So, the game promotes dodging and attacking after all, eh? Alas, not quite. Combine the short gap between enemy attacks, the extra frames to perform several dodges and attacks, and you get an inconsistent combat system. I would spend 20-30 minutes per fight struggling sometimes only to find out I could have won by spamming a very easy to perform tactic. It is to look for poles to use as a jumping point. When you jump off them, you can't get hit because you are in the air and you can perform one of two aerial attacks, which both land on the ground and hit enemies in the surrounding area. This works great for the second weapon you get, which can perform several hits per jump. Saves time and kills off even harder enemies in just a couple of jumps, as long as you hit them consistently.So, then, after all, this turns from a game where you reposition yourself to a game where you position enemies around you and spam them with the same jump attack. I don't like that. I don't like feeling powerful when I am put against the wall and given a single option that dominates enemies. I would have liked being able to dodge and hit, block (with a later weapon) and hit, jump, block and hit. It's either me who sucks at this or the game is just not well-balanced, with the combat system being the central pillar.Too bad. Hopefully, the next title that decides to focus on Indian mythology also fleshes out the main challenge mechanic, be it combat, traversal, puzzles, or something else.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has beautiful visuals, art style and level design. The narration and the background music are also very nice and there's a satisfying variety in weapons, combat options and ability development system. To my opinion, the strong part of the game is it's lore. The mythological events described through the game narration are very interesting and if you have no knowledge of the indian mythology (like myself), you get the feeling that it's vast, dense and interesting, like the greek and the norse.The weak (or even disappoining) part of the game is it's length. It's too short and this affects it's combat system and the story itself. Regarding the combat, you have very little time to try your weapons and establish a combat approach in general. By the time you get a weapon and get the use of it, by adding some ability points, you find a new weapon and you put the previous aside, until you find a new one again, and so on and so forth. Each weapon seems overpowered in comparison to the previous ones, until you get the last one which is some kind of godlike super weapon that one-shots all the enemies, and sends your other weapons and their previously developed ability tree to the can. Then the game ends...As for the story, it seems cut and forced to a closure, "to be continued" style. Literaly, after defeating a boss (it turned out to be the final one), i was expecting to play the next chapter and i was really surprised to see the ending credits instead.In overall it has it's flaws but still it's interesting, fun and worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Well well well. I finished playing it today. I would give this game a 4/5 rating. There are certain reasons why I liked it and a few points where it could have been better. I'm gonna call out all the bad points first so that I can justify my reason for giving 4/5. Firstly, the story was nothing extraordinary, a tale about two siblings and one of them is a total badazz. The characters are limited to the protagonist, The Gods and The bad guys, so the focus is not shifted elsewhere, simplest story of all time. However the Ending which I'm not gonna spoil didn't leave the impact I was after. Secondly the  controls are a little clunky sometimes, really pisses me off when I try to jump on to a slab and Raji ends up landing at a bit of an angle and misses the mark only to fail in her mission to rescue her brother. When this happens during I am moving my character across a very beautiful area and suddenly Raji falls off it is mildly infuriating. I mean maybe the game needed more polishing in that area. Combat feels sluggish due to the lack of fluidity of the action sometimes, but when the combos do land it feels like a super-win, but that happens very less than expected. Getting to the better parts now:-Music:Music is definitely a very important part of the game. Background score while I was enjoying the scenery around was so soothing that sometimes all I wanted to do was to listen to the music. Rajasthani folk music was used perfectly whenever the situation arose. However some form of warrior music was missing during  normal fights, just regular music. Now I'm not a musical man but I can tell that some sort of war-like music could definitely enhance the music situation . Otherwise it was perfect.The Art:God it was awesome. All the puppet-style cutscenes reminded me of my childhood when the puppetdances used to be a thing in TV shows/movies. When accompanied with awesome music that's when magic happens. The paintings depicting the Indian Devas/Devis and their saga felt so awesome.Mythology is always appreciated much more in painting form. The buildings are obviously Fort's  style from Rajasthan which has been always been one of my dream holiday destinations. Need I say more ? (maybe I'll plan that trip sooner rather than later after we have a safe situation of course). I instantly fell in love with surroundings.Weapons: Of course many might say that the Sudarshan Chakra was the best,most badazz weapon for them but for real all the weapons are MVPs in my opinion. During combat i'd develop new skills and try them using a combinations of all the weapons. If the game had been longer we'd have more versatility with the weapons and maybe a more complexity in the combat system while maintaining fluidity but that's okay. The shield/sword thing was awesome, and wielding the Trishul literally gave me goosebumps. What else can I say. This might be a paradigm shift for gaming industry in India, so I just love it. May Raji show the light to all such future endeavours. Love ,An Indian gamer PS: Please pardon my English, not so fluent in it. f any DLCs come out for this game, imma definitely gonna pre-order.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale(~$13) expecting very little. This ended up teaching me more about just how low a game can score be. The acting is absolutely not believable, unless you believe soap operas. The combat system is straight up boring with very low enemy variance. Any powerups you get are nonsensical. For a linear track game, I can't count the number of times I couldn't figure out where to go next. character animations were really choppy and looked unrealistic and almost comical. The only positive thing to say about this game is the the worlds are beautiful within themselves. Great 3D design and art, but everything about this that is a "game" is absolutely terrible. I really have to wonder about the developers of this game were trying to do and at what point they were actually proud of this. Like... maybe this was just something they made to raise awareness about non traditional heros and mythologies... which is cool and yay and keep doing it, but seriously this game feels broken and like it was rushed out, and the message suffers for it.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 - I love mythology, be it hindu, norse, greek I love it all, the stories, the characters, everything... This game doesn't disappoint with that. They nailed the presentation aspect, but this is a videogame, not a movie. Gameplay is king and here, it unfortunately falls apart fast.The combat is not good, feels floaty. The weapons feel weak at first, there is no impact, and they made it so the upgrades are basically the secrets of the game and some of it are pretty well hidden away, thats not a good move imho... especially when those elemental stuff you get with them is the most effective way of dealing with enemies. The animations and hitboxes are jank, enemy attacks hit you when it looks like you shouldn't have been hit. A lot of the later enemy encounters feel completely unfair and just thrown together, enemies start to alternate between attacks and you don't even have time to do ♥♥♥♥ all about that if you want to engage in the combat like it was intended to do so. Most of the time I just spammed dodge and attack the same time like crazy to kill the enemies in a lot of the late game fights, the dodge attack combo straight up breaks the combat, if you smash both buttons fast enough most enemies can't hit you at all. Or just run around and shoot with the bow but even that feels bad, the arrows are not even going where you are are pointing. But if you try to not abuse stuff... god it is bad... Enemies teleport into your face, 3 at a time because there is way too many of them. Other times it is laughably easy, it's all over the place. This combat and encounter design is not fun guys...The platforming is very generic, no challenge in it whatsoever. Like it's just there for those wide shot views.Exact same thing with the puzzles, basic, no challenge. Like it's just there to show off some extra art.

_childDocuments_.review: Being an indian person, it's lovely to finally have a game that depicts my culture and some of the traditions I had growing up. I felt it was a faithful rendition of a lot of the mythology. That being said, from a game perspective, a big part of it is combat which I really do not enjoy. I haven't completed the game and honestly, i might not, because I just really dislike the combat. It is slow, the attacks don't have the tight satisfying feeling that they do for example in Hades, and the enemies are extremely irritating (especially the big dudes that shoot like 5 purple globes at a time -- they are very frustrating to fight). If there was a combat-light version of this game where I don't have to reload like 10x just to get past an annoying encounter I would for sure do that.The best parts of this game besides its authenticity are the voice acting and the scenery. The world is incredibly beautiful, as is the music and atmosphere of the game. From a game mechanics perspective, I don't actually like this game much, but from a lore and authenticity perspective, it is highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Plus Points: (1) The visuals. Quite simply, this is the one thing that makes the game really stand out. The architecture and design of the game is just stunning and the game is worth a purchase simply for the visuals. (2) The music. The music is beautiful and on-point for an story set in ancient India. Fits the theme really well and is just enjoyable on its own. (3) The world-building: The developers have done a fantastic job in building out this world and it's easy to see that there is a lot of love put into making it come alive. Neutral Points:(1) The specific aesthetics: This is me nit-picking a little bit, because I don't think it really matters for many other people but still...I could see that a lot of specific aesthetics was borrowed predominantly from traditional Rajasthani designs. For example, the fort in the game bore a really strong resemblance to the Amer fort in Jaipur. This wasn't a problem in itself (in fact, for the most part, it was quite beautiful), but I did find it very jarring when the aesthetics would once in a while shift to another set of designs. For example, after the Udaipur Jal Mahal-style Hiranyapuri level, the rocky, hilly Mystic Land felt like something out of south India (in fact, I wonder if ). However, the shrines containing the orbs continued to look like Rajasthani shrines with domes, rather than those of southern India which have small gopurams. This felt rather jarring. But I guess this is mostly a problem for someone like me who's a bit of a nerd about these things. (2) The shadow puppet cutscenes: To be clear, I really really liked this style of cutscene and I think it's a fantastic idea to use shadow puppetry as cutscenes. What I wasn't too sure about were the choices of cutscenes themselves. I don't know why  was shown as a cutscene instead of just allowing the player to experience it in the game. Minus Points:(1) The camera: Oh my god, the camera. This was one thing that very nearly spoiled the game for me. It was quite frustrating to walk through some of the most gorgeous scenery I've ever seen in a game, but not have the ability to look around, because the camera is not under my control. I haven't played any games where the camera is designed like this - floating around the character, but not under the player's control - and this made the controls really hard to master. I kept falling off ledges when i wanted to run across a wall and the  was immensely annoying because I couldn't judge distances properly.(2) The fighting: The fighting wasn't too bad, but it could do with a few tweaks. Firstly, it was quite difficult to make the slighly more sophisticated moves. For example, it was quite hard to  because it took a bit of time to . Most of the time, this meant I would just keep mashing the controls and hoping to get a good outcome rather than use a combination of moves strategically. Secondly, switching weapons wasn't easy. It would take a second for Raji to switch from the sword and shield to the bow (sometimes the switch wouldn't even happen) and this interval would give enough time for the demons to attack again. This became particularly difficult if there were multiple types of demons to fight, require rapid weapon switching. ------Overall though, great work at building a game on Hindu myth that actually looks and feels (mostly) good. I'd recommend this with the caveat that one needs to be patient with the camera and okay with control-mashing during fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, indie action adventures don't get much better. Maybe longer, but not better. Certainly not more beautiful. The story takes place in ancient India, where demons have invaded the helpless human world. You play the girl Raji, motivated by the abduction of her little brother, who is choosen by the gods to defeat the demon lord Mahabalasura. Raji is a circus performer, so climbing poles, walking on tight ropes or wallrunning is easy for her. The Prince of Persia would approve.  She soon learns to use a weapon as well and the gods teach her to invoke magic. Her abilities  can be upgraded during the game using Orbs. The shy girl soon transforms into a deadly fighting machine, chasing the demons who took her brother away.The gameplay  consists of fighting demons or solving (mandala) puzzles to continue to the next stage. Stages are small areas that open when all foes are defeated or the puzzle is solved. Raji is able to use cool moves, like running up a wall and then smashing down on her enemies or swinging around a pole. She also has finishing moves (one for each weapon/demon combination) to kill wounded demons. The gods gift to her mighty blessed weapons like a bow or a spear, which allow for diverse fighting styles. Different demons use completely different attack styles. All this helps that fighting - which is required a lot - does not get repetitive too fast. After each fight, Raji's health is fully restored. Getting killed means restarting the fight. The game saves frequently and automatically. No save slots available. The attention to visual detail is enormous, I sometimes spent a few minutes just to adore the magnificent scenarios. It is inspired by the fortresses and art in Rajasthan. As beautiful as it is, it is not very interactive. You cannot jump on tables, cannot go past a simple fence, cannot destroy anything - it is just there for the scenery. The game is not too long, so take your time exploring the levels. The gods who comment on Raji's progress and Raji herself are fully voiced. Gamepad support is fine, and I would recommend to play it with one. I used a XBox One controller. Ultrawidescreen is supported.Comparatively short and very linear action adventure in really gorgeous visuals set in mythological India.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I had anticipated for a long time. Coming from Indian developers this was the first game that had the potential to be very good. And that is where my grime is with this game, it leaves the story unfinished and that too very abruptly you feel like there would be more of it and why it just suddenly feels like the end of the game is here, but then it does and it leaves you there with questioning why the developers would just not complete the story.The gameplay is okay for the first time developers and the small team, same goes for how the game looks. _childDocuments_.review: Raji: An Ancient Epic catches you off guard with its stunning visuals and setting in ancient India. In your quest to save your brother from demons, you journey through forgotten temples and lavish gardens, every single camera angle deliberately placed to take your breath away.In terms of game mechanics: it's an top-down action game (similar to that of Hades or Realm of the Dead Gods), so it's best to use a controller. You collect weapons as you progress through the game, each with their own special attacks, as well as strengths and weaknesses. They are all _extremely_ satisfying to use and are delightful in any combat. The movement is good - the usual run and jumping - but the character models and the environments make movement a novel experience. Map exploration rewards you with beautiful views and/or skill points. The puzzles are not too difficult and satisfying to figure out.The scenery and environment is lovingly crafted. You can stare and marvel at a small, abandoned marketplace for hours and in the next few minutes, you're staring at gorgeous murals in a temple. This game is worth playing for the visuals alone - this is the true standout feature of the game.The story is good, but it does peter out towards the end. It did feel rushed, like the game just needed to get there, but unsure about the build up. In other areas, the story was quite engaging - especially with cut scenes depicted in traditional Indian shadow puppet theatre (seriously, those are gorgeous). You are also observed by two gods during your travels and you also find out about all the other Indian deities - as well as their accomplishments and relations - in an engaging way. These mythologies are often accompanied by stunning murals and excellent voice acting.TLDR; Play this game for the visuals and the satisfying combat. It's short and the ending is quite abrupt, but the unique setting is more than enough to have this game stick in your brain long after you've played it.  Here's to more games based in India!

_childDocuments_.review: Inspired by the old God of War games, with emphasis on Hindu mythology. It seemed like a game that would appeal to some of my tastes. This indie effort is in some respects really impressive but in other areas it comes a little short. From my understanding, the game was made by a small team of industry talent on a modest budget which makes sense given the strengths and weaknesses of the game. I played on normal mode, but there's also easy, hard and one hit death difficulties.To start with the most obvious, the art direction is quite impressive in this game. There's always some beautiful vista to admire in each level, and the use of colour and shadows really pop at times. The dev team makes great use of the isometric perspective to achieve a sense of grand scale in locations. The various effects and environmental details are beautifully done and makes me appreciate how far game visuals have come.We follow Raji, a girl whose brother was kidnapped by demons. We must save him and stop the demon hordes, as the Gods guide us through our adventure.The integration of Hindu mythology and Indian culture is the game's greatest strength. The stories and lore are intriguing, the way mythology and medieval architecture are weaved to the attractive visuals are memorable. Though I wish some of these stories were integrated to he main plot more. Take the legend of Garuda, that was a standout to me, I would have loved to meet this deity in actual play. It really feels like the game is barely scratching the surface of the mythos with its' short run time, but I don't think it is bad to want more.Not much to say here. Sound was pretty well done, weapons and elemental powers felt suitably punchy on attacks. Music didn't have anything that stood out too much to me but it was used appropriately based on situation, to set the mood accordingly. Appropriate instruments were used to represent Indian culture and it synced well with all aspects of the game.Play consists primarily of combat and platforming, whereas puzzle solving and exploration make up the secondary elements of gameplay. While all things are done competently, none of the elements feel particularly exceptional in execution. Combat consists of light and heavy attacks, alternating between them to land basic combos. When enemies are low on health a prompt will show up to execute them, this will restore health when performed.To mix things up there's some fun environmental interaction that is mixed into the combat. You can bounce of walls and pillars to land some explosive aerial attacks, and there are poles which you can swing around to stun groups of enemies.The game introduces three standard weapons; the Trishul trident, Sharanga Bow, and Nandaka and Srivatsa sword and shield.The trident is our first and most well rounded weapon, it has solid range, damage and can be thrown as a projectile. It is a solid weapon to get the player acquainted with the game.The bow comes next. It can be polarising at first. It is difficult to get accustomed to its' slow and demanding attacks, even more so when the ~third fight after its' introduction consists of quick enemies who gang up on you and stalk you, showcasing just how inept this weapon is at close quarters combat. Despite this, the bow seems to rack up the highest damage out of these three weapons so its' utility will depend on how capable you are of mixing it in during fights.The sword and shield is perhaps the most powerful of these. This weapon has a greater emphasis on defence, thus it doesn't tear through enemies as quickly (but is no slouch either) but the shield helps deal with those pesky quick enemies who pummel you. These three weapons offer distinct utilities and also feature an ultimate ability that can turn the tide of each battle. There are also three elements granted through play that can be equipped on the weapons; lightning, fire and ice. These can be upgraded to provide differing effects during combos and will grant additional effects to the 3 weapons' ultimate abilities. These elements seem to differ, yet are in some ways too similar mechanically.The attacks generally feel punchy but there's some issues the zoomed out isometric view causes with spatial awareness that makes landing attacks awkward, particularly if you're trying to aim with the bow, which has lock-on but this doesn't always kick in when you're trying to land split second attacks. The bow is the first instance where I realised how much I would like to have a parry ability in the game, which is sadly missing here.I think the combat would have benefited if fights were zoomed in to help with landing combos, as well as with greater combat depth e.g. more combo strings to perform and a parry to avoid the repetitive use of the dodge button. Some enemies could also be mixed differently. Some fights were annoying with how certain enemies who throw a plethora of projectiles or ones who explode on top of you are paired in groups. Swapping between weapons in the middle of fights also felt clunky.Generally well done, though it must be noted that the dodge also functions as a jump, so each leap between platforms is done in a slightly awkward 'lock on' parkour. You will also do some pole climbing which require patient timing (no rushing!) and positioning à la the Tomb Raider games. Raji will reach out her hand to signal to the player that it's safe to jump from one pole to another, a smart bit of design that's appreciated. There is infrequent issues that arise from the perspective again but it is mild.Typically used to aid story telling through the environment and character revelations.Most of them are assembling puzzles of rotating segments. They can be visually appealing (particularly the one that shows the environment reforming from rubble as it progresses) but are devoid of challenge. I appreciate how they're tied into the story but they grow dull from repetition of the same easy tasks.Very basic. It's when you take the second path that diverts from the main, you'll occasionally be met with a platforming challenge. When taking the alternate path you are rewarded with an "Orb of Favor" upgrade for your elemental magic.These weren't to my liking. The devs keep them varied but generally they seem too repetitive despite having multiple attack patterns.The final boss was my least favourite part of the game. The execution was lacking. On controller he is frustrating to deal with and not fun to fight. Switch to mouse and keyboard however and you will notice that he becomes a pushover. The ability to keep your mouse pointer aimed at specific enemies when using the chakra weapon introduced late game, as well as having movement and evade mapped to WASD and Spacebar respectively kind of breaks the fight. Your experience with it will either way be a dissapointment regardless of input devices used.I liked most of my time. I believe the developers did a decent job balancing most aspects, particularly with the scope of what it was. However I would love to see this world expanded on, with a more refined combat and puzzle solving, as well as greater variety to help keep me engaged throughout the whole run time.Some polish would also go a long way to make the experience that much more positive.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is a beautiful journey that introduces a rich culture to those of us who didn’t know the first thing about Hinduism before.Simplicity is the secret of Raji. I normally don’t mind about how long a game is, but this game made me think of it. Raji is short what is great for a game with a simple narrative and a simple gameplay. Due to simplicity Raji can make players focus on the world, Its beauties and characters’ stories.It has some problems as a game, you can notice them mainly during combats. There are three weapons in the game for now (July, 2021), and you will probably feel inclined to use more two of them, cause they offer you the possibility of long-range attacks or blocking enemy attacks. Why inclined? Cause it’s really awful trying to use rolling to avoid attacks and attacking just after, when I tried it I normally got hit in a frustrating way.I honestly feel that the Nodding Heads Games team has done a good job to reduce the impact of those problems with special effects you can get to your weapons as stunning hits. And the timing they introduce new gameplay factors is just great, but once you try playing the game again to get some achievements you may get bored during the first map (25 minutes) till you get at least one of those upgrades.I sometimes bugged while trying a jump or the character couldn’t finish climbing a wall causing an instadeath so yes this game has some weirdo bugs. But exiting the game and coming back to the last checkpoint, or changing keyboard+mouse for a joystick “worked”.

_childDocuments_.review: Likes-1. Aesthetics- simply mind-blowing2. Soundtrack- distinctly Indian, a calming, soothing yet engaging background music3. Story- crisp, engaging (albeit a bit short) story4. Shadow-puppet style for the cutscenes- many games go for photorealistic cutscenes, which feels jarring when the actual      gameplay starts. Going for a distinct artstyle for the cutscenes instead was wise decision.Dislikes-1. Fighting system-                   a. Dodge attack (space + rmb) with the trishul and sword-shield brings me closer to the enemy (instead                        of dodging), thus bringing me in harms way. Additionally, it also does different moves with varying range                        (sometimes the sword extends, sometimes she throws the shield, etc), with this attack I never know how                        close i need to be to the enemy, or whether she'll hit multiple enemies with the shield; make it uniform.                        When i press a key combo, I should know exactly what to expect.                  b. Character movement feels slow compared to her enemies in combat. Cant doge quickly.                  c. No real distinction between lightning and fire element (ice is cool tho, pun intended).                  d. Bit of a lag when switching weapons, especially during combat, where speed is key. Often found myself                        wanting to switch between bow and sword-shield mid-combat.2. No tutorial for the elemental abilities. I was confused whether they activate on all attacks or only during power attacks.3. Couldn't tell mid-combat how many power attack orbs I had left. Needs some sort of a counter.4. The fixed camera felt kinda jarring, especially given how beautiful the aesthetic is. Free camera movement would've      been great. Hope you can get that to work in the sequel.5. No quicksave, the same save slot keeps getting overridden in autosave.6. No glossary for the various demon types.7. No level map. Can't keep track of whether I've visited all locations in a level.Everything said, a fantastic game. Hope this can kickstart India's game development ecosystem. Great job Nodding Heads!

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is like Indian God of War in the gameplay and story tellingPros:- Very beautiful levels/scene setups- Steeped in Hindu myth- Voice acting/narration in Hindi- Female body representation without fear (breasts are visible - pro for accurate Hindu representation, con for streaming/monetisation)- Really cool looking, creative enemiesCons:- Gameplay can feel awkward and doesn't flow nicely- Platforming is kinda bad - fell through a floor once- Puzzles are very simple (a child could play this)- Ending was very anticlimaticIf you want a straightforward, short Hindu based game to dip your toe into Hindu mythology and like supporting indie devs, I would say buy it. It's a good example of how to build really lush environments to set the mood and atmosphere of a game. It's awkward but if you don't mind stomaching it, you can enjoy everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an isometric hack and slash that is based on Indian culture, and unfortunately I don't find the mythology to be interesting enough to prevail over clunky combat. To some people there might be an intriguing story here, or they might like the manner in which it's presented (as if it were a puppetry display), but to me it's bog-standard stuff that's not very compelling. The fighting is pretty basic and quite dubious, with poor hit detection and occasionally woolly controls making it a chore. On the odd times that it doesn't feel too bad to play, it has some really bland music that doesn't ramp up the atmosphere or tension. I actually quite like Indian musical instruments, but here they're not used in a way that appeals to my tastes, or enhancing the action.One other thing I found quite surprising was that this runs fairly poorly, considering that it doesn't have all that many enemies onscreen or particularly huge environments or set-pieces. That it was chugging along at around 40 fps in some places seems pretty ridiculous, and a sign of it not being the most optimised title, as it's not exactly pushing any boundaries in terms of design or spectacle.Overall this has been one of the most disappointing titles in this genre that I've played recently and that's a shame, as I was looking forward to it. Sadly the slightly wonky technical aspects, along with the dull presentation, and boring and janky game-play, mean its far from compelling. Whilst it isn't awful as such, I would honestly suggest that maybe some connection to the culture has aided in more favourable reviews elsewhere, because this is quite mediocre to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Mix feelings about this game. I bought it because it looks visually stunning. The world is very detailed and it feels good to walk through it exploring the landscape. But also I must say that the game is very short and easy. There's lightning, fire and ice, but I completed the game only using lightning. The combat system does not require that you use a particular set of skills, weapons or powers to overcome any difficulty and that's a lost opportunity to make the game much more interesting. Bosses are very easy too, everything is too easy and short. So, those are the reasons for my mix feelings. As the game has a low price, I'll recommend it to spend a few hours (4 hrs or less) and to appreciate the great job the developers put in the visual design. I'll give it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If there is one take-away that I have gotten from the gorgeous  is that beauty truly is only skin deep. What we have here is a fascinating depiction of Indian culture and mythology that at first glance appears to be incredibly well mounted for a first time game but as time passes is little else. It's difficult not to look at  without the long shadow cast by , and if I were to sum up my time with the game it would be to simply say that it's not that much fun to play which is disappointing. Any notions that we have a spiritual successor here are immediately dispelled as  ends up being way too pallid, and dare I say "artsy" for its own good.Despite being a relatively short game - 4-6 hours to completion depending on your playstyle -  never really takes flight, and like a bird with a clipped wing it certainly feels like it as it drags itself from one section to the next, peppered with some clunky and tiresome gameplay mechanics that don't entirely work. By the time it finally closed out, it felt like I had been stuck playing the game for 20 hours or more. does look gorgeous though for the most part and it seems this is where most of the effort and budget was centered because even the story about a young girl whose brother is kidnapped by an ancient demon and her journey to rescue him from its clutches completely peters out to a great big old nothing at the end. Featuring long sections where not much happens, the game starts to become rather listless which only ends up generating a listlessness in the player to want to continue.While I most certainly appreciate what first time developers Nodding Head Games have tried to achieve here, and as I have mentioned before the game can certainly be lustrous to look at,  falls short in the gameplay and narrative departments. While desperately trying to forge its own identity, it never quite emerges from underneath that long shadow cast by , eventually ending up being consumed by it. But by golly is it a good looking game and for that I will give it the thumbs up but Nodding Head Games are going to have to bring much more to the table because next time I won't be this generous.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: The bad first:The combat system is atrocious. I think pretty much every review has stated as much. It's true. You either spam A to 'dodge' or you get hi. Enemies attack way too often given how many you fight, your attacks don't stagger and do little damage. Near the very end of the game, you get Ice Element which freezes enemies. That's the only way to get enough time to actually execute some attack properly. it's really frustrating to play and I'm glad to be done with it.Then, what the game should have been: a platformer / puzzle mix. The puzzles are non-existent. You rotate some stuff and then a picture forms, that's it. You can't fail. Platforming? Just for traversal. Nothing is being properly utilized like the acrobatic skills of Raji to actually create some fun levels to explore with her tumbling abilities. Instead, all the flips and jumps are wasted on combat.the game really only has the visuals and atmosphere going for it and it is truly breathtaking. This is very little positive compared to a bunch of a lot of negativity here and really, the only reason this is a positive review is the fact that India isn't exactly known for creating video games. So, in light of that, this can be sondiered a good first attempt, but by god - more jumping, less fighting, more riddles, less fighting. Why would it even make sense that this tiny frail girl fights 7 ft demons? Maybe some stealth or something, Idk - something like the SNES Aladdin games perhapts where you jumped on people's heads instead of swining a sword.The ending was also super disappointing given it's basically a 'what happens now?' thing setting up a potential 2nd game. Which may or may not come. But if it does, and it does feature this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat again, I will not be going trhough that again.

_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Raji's story is based on Indian mythology which is quite rare to see in the market, and was the major reason I purchased this game. The game has amazing visuals and soundtrack as an indie title. The story itself is quite flat in my opinion, as I feel like the dev tries too hard to show you many different Indian gods on a very surface-level, but doesn't spend enough time for the protagonist's character development and her relationship with her brother. The awkward voice-acting also doesn't help. Gameplay is the weakest point of Raji -- combat feels very clunky, most puzzles can be solved within seconds, and platforming is a bit annoying as I often jump off from trees when my character is not facing the exact direction. Glad that the game is relatively short so I can finish it within 5 hours. I read some articles about the dev's financial difficulty and one of the founder selling her apartment to fund the game development, so this could be another reason if you consider to support this game.

_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are nice, the setting is unique - don't see a lot of games centred around Hindu faith, but the combat in this game is just awful. There are so many combos that you don't use because you just end up moving the character around the arenas constantly to evade attacks and spamming the main attack button. The combos that were created for the game just aren't practical to use because they either need you to be close to the enemies to work or they take a long time to charge up, and by either point the enemies have managed to attack you since they are faster in every way and once they attack you, you are momentarily stunned.Also, during combat, the camera focuses on the player character which is fine if the arena is small since you can still see all the enemies, but if the arena is bigger then you can't see all the enemies which means that you can't attack them. They can attack you however! and they do, with ranged attacks that you can't avoid because the enemies targeting system is better than yours.If the combat wasn't such a big part of the game, perhaps the faults wouldn't be too bad but you get dragged into combat in every turn (literally, you turn a corner and boom! a fight). I haven't played the game for long but the poor combat mechanics and the frequency of combat have killed any interest I had in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is a very chill, gorgeous hack and slash with a calm soundtrack to match, and an epic adventure that is within the league of the original God Of War in terms of grandeur. _childDocuments_.review: Had high hopes coming into this since it looks so similar to one of my favorite games, Dreamscaper, and it seemed to have a really beautiful map worth exploring. I refunded the game within an hour. I saw another review which already covers many of the things that disappointed me, so I'll just copy those points verbatim. This person spent over 5 hours on the game, but I could already see the same problems within the first hour."-Raji’s voice acting managed to be both extravagantly dramatic while simultaneously monotone. I still can’t wrap my head around that one. After every battle, she taunts the enemies in ways that fry my cringe-detecting organs to the point that I need a transplant now.""-Vishnu and Durga would just, not, stop, talking. It's like I constantly am connected to a live feed of their DM's.""-The murals where Vishnu narrates different Indian myths honestly doesn’t fit and seems to only be there cause the devs felt an obligation to share Indian culture in the game. If that was the goal, a simple system of collectible notes/scrolls would’ve been more than fine; if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.""-Raji’s voice acting managed to be both extravagantly dramatic while simultaneously monotone. I still can’t wrap my head around that one. After every battle, she taunts the enemies in ways that fry my cringe-detecting organs to the point that I need a transplant now.""-And don’t get me started on the 'difficulty'. The game is insultingly easy, while simultaneously stretches each battle and makes it grindy, which is the perfect recipe for being bored out of my mind. Every time I see a battle arena (and I was able to predict every battle arena because the game is more predictable than the wetness of the pacific), I groan out of my mind, because I know I’ll soon be locked in grind-fest number 1 out of 4 in this singular corridor."To those points I would also add that 1- The music is really weird. At points I wasn't sure if two different songs were playing at the same time due to some glitch, the instrumentation is just that uncoordinated and chaotic. 2- The combat didn't feel interesting at all and was extremely easy. Every time I got hit the screen also flashed, which was really annoying.3- The map isn't actually worth exploring because there don't seem to be barely any hidden secrets, and it's very linear. The fact that it's pretty is really the only thing going for it.If you're interested in this game, do yourself a favor and go try Dreamscaper first!

_childDocuments_.review: 1/5  This game used to be really good.  I originally gave it a 4/5.  I went back to play through the game again, and I got to a part where I was stuck, and getting stun locked by enemies in a manner that seemed broken.  The enemies have a dash attack, that they can use to cover a lot of ground instantly, and there is no limit on the distance they can travel.  When these enemies get out of sync (or in-sync depending on how you look at it) they can literally attack you continuously with windows between the attacks so short that you can't do any attack without taking damage.  You do have a shield, but they will break it in no time if these attacks continue, and you're back to getting hit.  I don't remember this being in the game at all, and I was confused how I could have played the game, and liked it originally if they were doing this the entire time.  It turns out the game was changed, The enemies that I'm talking about behave differently in the original game, and they appear to have much less health.  Unless I'm just mistaken.  I just finished playing the section, at the time of writing this, and I'm also re-watching the section on my older play-through.  The enemies appear to behave very differently, and go down with no problem in the original game.  In this version, they appear to be broken to me.As far as I'm concerned, this change made to the game has completely broken it, and I have no desire to continue playing the game with an enemy that annoying in it.  One of the reasons the score went from a 4 to a 1 is that if this enemy was presented to me early in the game, I would have quit, never played it again, and requested a refund for the game.  The game is completely fine up until this point, but then it becomes so un-fun, that it is essentially negative fun, and it retroactively deletes the fun that I had up until that point... essentially making it a game that's not fun at all.Change the game back to the way it was originally, please?  Perhaps un-enhance it?

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend or not to recommend, that's the question. It's a beautiful game with a simple but effective story - save your brother from some evil demons or whatever they are. You also get to learn a little about Hinduism while you are at it, and that's great. But that's where the good stuff ends for me.The game mechanics are what makes a game. At my age (40+ and have been playing video games all my life), I have grown sick of fighting and combat. That happens to be around 50% of the entire game. I'm playing it on easy just to get through the combat sequences as fast as possible.The second half of the game is something that resembles platforming. But it's not the kind of platforming that requires any skill, like Celeste, Ori and the Blind Forest, Hollow Knight or such. No, it's rather like Tomb Raider or Assassin's Creed, where you just need to know which button to press to activate the right animation. With other words, it's the casual version of platforming, which I dislike.I got this game on sale, and will play it through despite the above. But do I recommend it? Not personally, no. If you enjoy combat, then it's all right I guess. But I wouldn't bother.
