_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this game as the culture is rarely seen in games and it is an indie developer so I wanted to give them the benefit of the doubt. However despite all of this I can't recommend it. And many indie games have done much more with a lot less, so I can't let it slide. I'll start with the bad and end with the good. The Bad:The Combat is bad:- There is NOTHING rewarding about the combat even though the vast majority of the game you are fighting many, many enemies. Waves upon waves in each blocked off arena, but there is nothing to reward you for it. There is no XP system.Instead of leveling up via XP when you defeat enemies you need to find random orbs hidden in the levels that give you only one chance to level up each time you find them. This makes fighting such a huge number of enemies an enormous chore and you get nothing out of it. There is also no way to skip fights. - so is the combat itself any good/fun since you are doing so much of it? No. The Combat is really poorly designed, only 1 of your 4 weapons has a defensive option, which is the sword and shield (the least fun to play). Example of some of the flaws in the actual combat, with the bow you first need to move towards the enemy, fire to focus in that direction and then you can move back. Really bad design there. Meanwhile with the spear which is a melee weapon you hold left trigger to then throw it, why was the bow not designed the same way? baffling choice. -Combos are so very slow, you don't have time to use them, instead its all hit and dodge. - interacting with the environment is pointless, running on a wall to flip and attack is far too much effort and far too ineffective to actually be useful in combat. Its an isometric game, more thought should have been put into area of effect attacks, or fast dash attacks, etc. Instead you are slow and largely ineffective whilst your enemies are fast and hit hard. You end up fighting the same way each time, you are rolling about the arena in every fight, trying not to die and get a few hits in. Rinse and repeat. - The enemies are also tanks with lots of HP and  just absorb hit after hit. Furthermore to take away even more from the combat experience, many of them move fast and can stun lock you during combat. Its not fun. - your dodge roll doesn't have any invincibility frames which means enemies can swarm and attack you non-stop so you will die many cheap deaths. The solution is to try and take them out as fast as possible, this is not fun combat, it makes it even more of a chore to play when I want to rush all the interactions.---The final boss is the distillation of all of these negatives combined. It is incredibly frustrating and the games combat system is nowhere near good enough to warrant the final stage of the boss battle. Its not fun.  The story does very little with the culture:- While the culture and background of the game seems interesting and will no doubt bring peoples attention. They do nothing with it. Its a very generic story with only the loosest connection to the cultural subject matter. A much wasted opportunity. - The narrators are two gods, after the first couple hours its a bit tedious and you lose interest as its just yapping and no real important information is conveyed. It would be much more interesting if they gave you information about your environment, tactics to best certain enemies, etc. Instead its just nonsense for the most part.The environments are generic:- The environments are incredibly generic, given how varied and prominent much of ancient indian architecture is it feels like they did very little to actually embed much of that into this. Instead its very generic environments for the most part. - Puzzles are uninspired and more thought could have gone into making them more interesting and thought provoking. - The game gets boring after a few hours and it feels like it could have been cut in half and more focus placed on the depth of the game and its systems. Platforming is poorly done:- Other than holding onto a few wooden beams and climbing a few ledges there isn't really much to it. Is it due to the limitation of the isometric view point? why not temporarily switch to a side scroller for those sections? - Prevents you from back tracking. A couple times you are met with two paths, one contains level up orbs and the other progresses the game. You don't know which is which, so you pick the one that continues the game and you can't go back and get the level up orbs. Whats the point? The narrators are constantly yapping, they couldn't think to use them to tell you which one to take first? Its pointlessly punishing the player. Bad design. The Good:+ The voice acting is quite good though too much of it.+ The cinematics are stylized like old puppet shows.+ has a few weapons that do cool effects with different powers.Ultimately it feels like a much wasted opportunity, its another game about finding your kidnapped sibling just loosely set in a place thats supposed to look like ancient india with two yapping narrators that after a couple hours detract from the story more than they add to it. The game should have been half as long as it is, far more focus should have gone into the environments and really trying to showcase a mystical ancient india. The narrators should have been cut down significantly and when they do talk it should have provided important information or some comic relief, etc. The combat should have been overhauled, fast attacking enemies don't work when your dodge roll has no invicibility frames, their should have been an XP system so fighting so many enemies had a point and made me want to continue on. Don't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is an absolutely gorgeous game set in a wonderful mythology not often told.   It has so much lovely narration, great voice acting and mind-blowing drawings in a game.    The intricate detail in some of the artwork is simply gorgeous.The game has a nice progression as you work your way through it.   The difficulty ramps up as you'd expect, and it's up to you to allocate your "favour orb" points to create effective weapons.   It's worth looking up what the various buffs mean and how to allocate them because they have random effect, so if you don't know what to expect it can get a bit confusing.The fights are largely just brawls.  The various monsters have different ways to best fight them: stand-off range attacks, or get in and stun-lock them.  The four main weapons are granted gradually through the game,   but  none of them (except the very last) seems to be decisively more powerful. They just all support different play styles.   Saying that, there are some enemies that you simply can't defeat with one or other weapon as they rush you, so you have to be a little choosy.  But the game doesn't penalise you for dying, so you get lots of chances to try out different tactics.I'd say that the 'easy' difficulty is WAY too hard.  I'd class it more like a 'normal'.  For Easy, I'd make some of the enemies a lot less powerful, like the rushing samurai guys, and maybe spawn one or two fewer enemies in the really big brawls later on.A lovely game, that only takes 6 or 7 hours to play through.  Absolutely beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not coming from an 'Indian', but merely from someone who loves games and the things games are capable of.Raji tells a simple, yet engaging story with the best possible storytelling mediums: shadow-puppetry, artwork Hindu and characters from Hindu mythology. Add to that the beautiful landscapes and architecture from Rajasthan. The soundtrack is absolutely delightful and gives the game an authentic sense of creativity. While some of its weaker points lies in the combat system; I still believe its very much enjoyable. Character animations are great, combos perform well. .In all, a great experience. This gives me hope for the game-development-and-design scene from India. I am proud to be part of the industry and can't wait to see where gaming takes us.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat ruins this game. So many things wrong with it. Your basic attacks have a little wind up or jump and these are too easily interrupted by enemy attacks. There's no way you can pull off a combo; plus your attacks don't seem to interrupt the enemies. The range attack is befuddling. I think you are supposed to hold the attack button, wait for an auto-target line to appear between you and an enemy, and then let go of the button. I could not get it to work consistently. There are these interesting and powerful attacks that you can do by jumping off a wall or column, but they are annoying to pull off because of the fixed isometric pov and the inertia of the character movement. There are tutorials at the start of the game, but it's basically an information dump of all the attacks/abilities that you have; but then, the worst part, there isn't a reference card that you can look at to review what you learned. I believe I forgot some of the button combos.The game lets me dial the combat down to easy, but the rest of the game hadn’t hooked me enough to do this. The platforming is sluggish, but simple. The few puzzles are simple. The storytelling is just OK, with a lot of it coming from voice overs of 2 gods commenting on the action, where the player is frequently in the dark about what they gods are referring to.

_childDocuments_.review: A small gem of an indie game, combining platforming and combat in a very Prince Of Persia-ish kinda way (I find the platforming to be a bit on the simplistic side, but the combat has some diversity, due a variety of weapons to make different combat encounters feel more rewarding; we also have a small weapon skill tree where we can invest ability orbs).The visuals are also nice, very colorful, the soundtrack also fitting. Loving also the Hindu mythology, finding it original, as we don;t really have that many games in this area (or at least none that I've played). Technically, I did not encounter any major bugs, it;s pretty fluid at 144hz. Overall, I recommend playing it and I hope to see more games from the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: A breath of fresh air seeing Hindu mythology in a game. Visuals are stunning, can't say anything bad about the art. With all the good stuff aside, there's a lot of room for improvement...Story-wise, it was okay until I got to the end. Maybe the ending was done that way in the event it gets a sequel. I have no problem with cliffhangers as long as they're done well. This one was poorly executed. The game ended so abruptly, I thought I got a bad ending or something.On combat, it hurts that I agree with some of the reviews already said. I personally wasn't able to utilize all combos because some battles just got too tedious. Two bosses in particular overstayed their welcome IMO.The weapon skill tree could be better also. While I do appreciate the customization in the weapons, I think it would've been better if the weapons had fixed elemental attributes so that players can be more strategic in their utilization.Weapon switching could've been better also. Maybe assigning weapon A to button X, and weapon B to button Y. I decided not to switch weapons during boss fights because switch gave me more of a handicap than if I just stuck to 1 weapon the entire battle.I still recommend giving this game a try, but get it on sale (at least 40% discount).

_childDocuments_.review: Raji: An Ancient Epic provides a great game on the surface that could lead to something magical. You have a story that isn’t perfect but alright, some beautiful graphics, and great combat mechanics. These are severely hampered though by an anti-climactic ending, poor consistency in the combat, mediocre sound design, and various other issues. While some hardcore action-adventure fans may find something to love, Raji will likely wash away in the sands of your mind as quickly as it arrived.If you'd like to see the rest of this review and more like it, check out . _childDocuments_.review: Lots of positives with this one, but the few negatives really made me suffer through this game.Let's start with the positives:1. Great art. Played the enhanced edition and it looked great.2. Well structured story using Hindu mythology.3. Voice acting other than the title character was really good for Hindi.4. Decent enemy variety and I did like the boss designs.5. Good design and use of weapons.These negatives may not affect most of you but it did sour my taste:1. Janky combat. Combat seems like it's a decade old. No ability to lock-on targets and also the aiming was so bad.2. Hit reg and lag issues. Felt like I was playing a multiplayer game with high ping. Hits on enemies wouldn't register and enemies would hit you even though the projectile was some distance away. You could also get hit while in iframes. Sometimes jumping from the walls and poles in order to attack would get stuck mid animation.3. Sometimes you would just bounce of surfaces and fall down or into the water and die.4. Game glitched out for me a few times. Had to restart the game in order to progress.The 1st two issues really affected me a lot, as you can tell from the playtime. The game isn't that long but I really struggled here. These 2 issues are why I am not recommending this game.Hope the team improves the game for raji 2. Wish you the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Happy to finally have a game set in the context of Indian mythology. Kudos to the developers for making the game. The atmosphere of the game is very engaging and the locations fairly represent various elements of Indian architectures. Each location is also unique different from others. The game play really cool and the weapons, once again relevant to the Indian mythology, have varied combat styles.I wish the game was longer. Did not really have much time to enjoy some powers attained in the later parts of the game. The game play also seems to be more attuned for console gaming and is not the most intuitive with keyboard and mouse. The ending also felt a bit anti climactic and rushed and I hope we can explore the consequences in later games.Overall I really enjoyed the game and recommend it to anyone interested in Indian mythology.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is a really pretty game, you can tell a lot of work has gone into it. Controls are a bit awkward with a controller so I would recommend using the computer controls The scenery is beautiful and the mythology is really interesting, but pacing of the story is a bit off (the plot seems rushed after the boss fight with Rangda) which makes the confusing ending all the more disappointing. However, I recommend based on how much I loved the lore, the aesthetic, and the performance of the voice actors.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game, but with a few caveats:1.) It's short, I was able to beat it in a little under 6 hours. 2.) The game concludes on a note that feels more like the middle of a story, not an ending.3.) I enjoyed the combat, but it's not for everyone. Definitely try the free demo before buying, and if any of the above makes you iffy, wait for a sale. I bought Raji for ~$12 so I feel like I got my money's worth, but I don't know how I'd feel if I paid full price.Final thoughts: Despite the downsides, feels like a lot of love was poured into the game. The brilliant visuals, the stories, the dialogue, the little details that showed a lot of care had been put into the world. And (I'm in the minority here, I believe) the combat was ridiculously fun. Overall it's very immersive and I was sucked into the story and world the whole way through. Wish it was longer, but I'll take quality over quantity.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really interested in this game when I first played the demo at Steam games festival. The indian setting felt fresh, the visuals were good, the controls more or less fluid. The only question was combat - it was pretty lacking, but I hoped they would balance it better until release.Alas, it is still very lackluster. Your basic attacks are very slow and do minimal damage, while enemies are fast (and there are often several of them) and have tons of HP. So you have to rely on a wall attack (jump from a wall or a column and attack) which deals much more damage and has aoe effect. But this turns every fight of a repetitive excercise of running up a wall, attacking, then running again until all enemies are dead. And even when you get a new weapon this tactic doesn't change. And the fact that the game has horrible collision detection (including monsters hitting you) makes the fights even worse.You may think that exploration might make up for a bad combat, but alas. The locations are linear, and the camera is automatic (mostly picking up static positions), so you are very limited in what you can see on screen. Also, this automatic camera makes platforming much harder since it chooses really bad angles making you miss even the easiest jumps.Finally, the visuals and optimization. The game sometimes stutters and drops below 60 fps on 12900k, 32Gb RAM, 980 Pro, 3080Ti @ 1440p. When enabling RTX options, it stutters even more (GPU is around 80% load), while looking almost the same.All in all, even despite an interesting setting, I cannot recommend this game because of boring combat, bad camera and lazy optimization. The longer I played it, the more I hated it, it just progressively becomes worse.

_childDocuments_.review: The usual neutral-leaning-positive review: the game is not actually not bad enough to warrant a negative, but not good either.The visual design here is stunning - basically, the highlight of the game. The sound design is pretty decent, too.The story is meh, with the ending not even being a proper ending. The 'crash course into Hindu mythology'-style interludes seem haphazard and mostly out-of-place.The combat system (encounter design included) is clunky and not well thought out. There are things that work like charm, wall run-then-midair attack being the prime example, but aiming is generally hard, timings are unwieldy and balance is generally non-existent (are you supposed to ever switch back your weapons?). Also, getting stunlocked is simply not fun.The controls are broken as usual: on gamepad movement and aiming are combined into one stick, making bow & chakra borderline unplayable, on keyboard there is lack of freedom of movement, eight directions are not enough.The game is short, if you don't set the difficulty higher than your ability, there are approximately 6 hours of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: A copy of this game was provided by the developer.Raji: An Ancient Epic is an action adventure game about a young girl saving her brother in a tale of Indian gods and demons.The game's strongest side is the beautiful visuals. There are a lot of different rich environments to appreciate as you progress through the game. You can't adjust the camera, but I think they did a good job at forcing the camera to be in the spot where it needs to be and the zoomed out camera puts the focus on the great scenery while Raji and the enemies (except bosses) feel small.I have mixed feelings about the story. The presentation of the story is unique and interesting about the Indian gods, it's done through a shadow puppet show cinematics, two Indian gods Vishnu and Durga having a chat while you play, interacting with tapestries and rotating puzzles that tell short stories about the avatars of Indian gods. But the story about Raji and her quest is unsatisfying and feels rushed. It feels inconsistent, like Raji's character where one moment she is humbly asking the gods for help, being pure of heart and the other moment she is shouting one liners after defeating demons.The gameplay is where it falls short in my opinion. There are flashy moves with light and heavy attacks that combo off of poles and walls with three different weapons that can be empowered with three different elements, but Raji's attack animations last a longer time while the demons can attack instantly after moving, making it unfair and hard to choose when to attack. Most attacks lack precision and using the bow prefers to dash towards the enemies before shooting. There is a bow tutorial that took me 20-30 tries due to clunkiness.The puzzles and platforming are simple, but you can fall to your death easily because of imprecise controls, luckily the checkpoints are always close. There were a few bugs where platforming led me to being stuck, unable to progress, but restarting the game puts you in a nearby checkpoint. For an adventure game, the levels are designed very linear, with only a few sections where you choose to go for an upgrade point or progress the story, but these sections lack the visual hints to tell which is which. And there's no backtracking or level select available.As a pretty story book, Raji is great, but I can't recommend it as a game.For achievement hunters:Most of them are storyline, some about reading all the extra stories and collecting all favor orbs. There's no level select or backtracking.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: Raji is a very interesting game, where the main story is interconnected with the Hindu mythology. I liked much the graphics, the authentic Indian atmosphere and the traditional music. Playing this game, I felt like I'm a part of this interesting epic. The 8 directions controls were confusing at the beginning, but after some minutes I got used to them. Sometimes this controls can make the game even harder, when you need to calculate where exactly your character is going to land after a jump. I really liked the mythological weapons used in the game and the strategic options which they offer you for beating the enemies. I was quite impressed by the difficulty of some of the monsters, others were very easy to defeat. Another interesting aspect of the game is the exploration, where you need to make careful choices in which direction to go and explore, cause sometimes you cannot go back and search for Favor orbs.I definitely recommend this game, if you're looking for an authentic South Asian ambiance, vivid graphics and beautiful Indian music.
_childDocuments_.name: Raji: An Ancient Epic

_childDocuments_.review: I wish it were possible to leave a neutral review. I both can & can't recommend this.On the one hand... nice eye candy from the barefoot female protagonist, and it's nice to see this "Hindu fantasy" aesthetic as opposed to the done-to-death fantasy settings we get year-in-year-out. And the game itself is beautiful. Plays alright, though the combat could use a bit of tightening and often you don't have much sense of direction, so it feels a bit slow. It also has the LoZ issue where you end up spamming the dash-roll because it's faster than running, so Raji just goes cartwheeling all over the place.On the other hand... Look up this game on Wikipedia. $5 million grant in funding, years of development, a whole team, great ideas that should've made your game stand out, one of the main devs selling her apartment to support it, yet you turn out a game this beautiful and STILL had to scrap 3D cutscenes, some puzzles and an ending that actually... y'know, ended? Instead of a BulletStorm-level cliffhanger that'll probably never get resolved. Something doesn't add up. When you had this recipe for success handed to you and yet PHASMOPHOBIA beats you out at the Game Awards... you did something wrong. Something does not add up about the development here.It'll kill an afternoon, if you've got like 3-4 hours, but there's not much else to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Gorgeous game, both in the overworld and the puppetry animations in the cutscenes.  The ongoing storytelling between Vishnu, Durga, and the murals of Indian myths and epics throughout the game is a highlight.  Unlike Greek and Roman pantheons, the Hindu pantheon and their many avatars feel fresh in a video game format.  Once you get the hang of the controls, select a good setup, and start using walls and poles to your advantage, the combat movement feels fluid.Cons: Controls are a bit floaty, and the plot starts to come off the rails in the end, setting up a rather unsatisfying bridge to what I can only assume will be a sequel.  The weapons and powerups seem set up to have one right answer, and if you miss any achievements, it's a long way back through the entire story to collect them.  The price is rather high for the total game length. All told, it's a lovely game from an indie studio, and I'd recommend picking it up when it goes on sale.

Nothing particularly good either. It clearly serves as a support for the story.- Raji's voice acting is hilariously bad, which really sucks for a story-driven game.- A few bugs here and there.- Many fights are narrated instead of played. _childDocuments_.review: Prince of Persia + Devil May Cry style game combined with Indian Mythology and beautiful visuals. You get to play Four beautiful levels,The Ruins (8/10) - You will learn core MechanicsThe Fortress of Jaidhar (8/10)Hiranya Nagari (9/10)The Land of the Mystics (7/10)You get three Weapons - The Trishul (Trident), a Bow and Sword + Shield. The fourth weapon, The Sudarshana chakra, is over powered and you can use it only at the end.There are three elemental attack modifiers for the weapons - Lightning, Fire and Ice which are granted by three gods Durga, Vishnu and The ShivaEach of the elemental modifiers have three attributes - Chain attack, Mini Stun and Area of effect attack. These attributes can be upgraded using Favor Orbs which are Somewhat secretly hidden in the game (Imagine PoP Warrior within)Each of the weapons can have one of the three elemental attack modifiers at any given time (You cant have all three simultaneously).To fully upgrade a Elemental attack modifier, you need 9 Favor Orbs (3 for each of the three attributes). So in theory, you need 27 favor orbs to fully upgrade all three elemental modifiers. But the game has only 15 favor orbs!! (5 each in Fortress of Jaidhar, Hiranya Nagari and The land of the Mystics)But to be fair, you can add / remove the favor orbs for a elemental attack modifier and customise the attack attributes any time. Remember, you can use only one elemental attack modifier at a time. So a minimum of 9 favor Orbs is enough to fully upgrade a elemental modifier and you can always swap with other modifiers if desired.The story is narrated using Shadow Puppets, which I found interesting. The puzzles (Mandala puzzles and Statue puzzles) are simple and repetitive. There is only one elaborative Cogs and Wheels Puzzle in the Hiranya Nagari level. The enemies are repetitive, but you get a variation in enemies and the enemy waves usually mix and matches those variations. So you need to always be in your toes to chose the correct weapon for the enemy type and also switch quickly between attacks. As you upgrade your attack elemental modifiers using favor orbs, you find it easy and enjoyable to eliminate them.Overall, I enjoyed the game and played the game twice to complete all the achievements. Well worth the buy!!Cons:1. No level selector (at the time of writing this). After the game is finished, the game simply restarts and also over writes your saved profile. In a way, the game forcefully resets your progress and you have to restart from the beginning if you want to replay a level or to hunt for achievements.2. You can use only one elemental attack modifier at a time. No Lightning +Fire+Ice combined3. No difficulty level selector4. The story ending was a bit underwhelming (may be a sequel is planned?)5. I got stuck in weird places sometimes and I had to restart from the last save (Bug?)6. The game crashed on me a single time,

_childDocuments_.review: Two performers, Raji and Golu, brother and sister, are alone in the world. They work at the carnival with other performers, the only family they have. During one day of festivities, while Raji is performing acrobatics high up on the rope and Golu is entertaining the crowd with his story, demons attack the city and take Golu. As Raji is unable to save her brother, she receives help from two gods that watch over her. While one has some doubts about her, the other grants her the Trishul, a legendary trident that can defeat demons. The first sign that you're about to play something memorable is the very first cutscene. All of them are wonderful and use shadow puppets to tell the story. Since most of us are not familiar with the Indian myths and terms, the game tries hard to explain so that you don't feel lost in so many unfamiliar words. The learning also comes during the quieter moments of the game, where you examine murals that tell the story of the gods or reveal snippets from Raji's life.The stages are equally impressive. Everything is so big and grand that Raji looks almost insignificant. I would've liked a few more details, as some feel a bit too empty, but the silver lining in this is that the journey takes you through various settings. Upon reaching the end of the level, you have to reconstruct a tree by rotating several layers. This is very easy because statues around the tree show when you're gone too far; they crumble and become whole as you rotate. Since Raji is a performer, she has no trouble climbing tall columns and jumping over bottomless chasms. The same can be said about her fighting abilities. She is able to perform three quick attacks with either one or the other attack move, or a combination of both. There isn't much difference between them because combat consists mostly of button mashing and dodging. Dodging can be performed at any time and as many times as you want. There is no cooldown period and you can do somersaults all day. Trident can be thrown as well, but that is mostly used for puzzles or enemies you can't reach. The other weapons you receive from gods are bow, sword and shield, and chakra, the ultimate weapon that makes others completely useless.Battles take place in special areas. Once you reach one, the area gets enclosed with a magical line that disappears only when you defeat all enemies. You never know how may there are because they keep showing up. The small demons fall quick and their attacks are easily avoidable, so they don't pose much threat. The only one you have to worry about is their special attack, marked by a glow. However, larger demons are much more dangerous. Even a single one can take you out with a few swings of his club. Other creatures, like quick goblins and flying pests, make things a little less boring, but Health is represented by a colored circle underneath Raji. It goes from blue to red the closer you are to death. Enemies have a similar circle with one little difference: once they reach the red zone, enemies can be killed instantly. Executions are also the only way to recover health during a battle. Environment plays a role in those battle areas. Raji can grab onto a pillar to swing around and hit everyone or use a wall to jump higher and come down with a powerful attack. Sometimes the enclosed area will form around a shrine that allows you to perform a special area attack. This can be recharged every time you hit an enemy and there's a loud noise when it's full. If you feel overwhelmed by enemies, you can upgrade weapons by offering orbs to one of the three gods. Durga, the first god you unlock, can add random lightning strike or longer duration of electrocution. Later you gain two more gods that grant you fire and ice. These white orbs can be quite hard to find and they're always hidden away from the main path, but they make combat trivial. While it's true that you can add power to any weapon and upgrade any power, you can easily stick to one and beat anything the game throws at you. Chain lightning is especially powerful when fully upgraded; I learned the best way is to just spam one attack button. If you don't like a certain power, you can always remove orbs and upgrade something else. Purple and yellow orbs are also present, which grant health and special attack respectively.I was a little disappointed that you couldn't revisit levels after you were done with the story. This means you're out of luck if you missed any of the orbs and wanted to collect everything. It's true the game isn't that long, but there are a few unskippable sections where you're forced to listen to the slow retelling of the story.   Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good piece; storytelling with visuals and musics, on point. I think these games should be evaluated in a different category. Because they pay more attention to storytelling rather than gameplay compared to the overall game structure. But it promises more gameplay than a walking simulation game. Although the gameplay time is at an average level, I can say that the gameplay time is short because some sequences are too monotonous. They could have added some more gameplay elements, or they could have helped us find some items from the period the game was set in. For example, a few items that will make a small contribution to the story. I was constantly looking for a secret place and died many times because of the fixed camera angle. The thing I wanted most while playing the game was the free camera angle, at least for some parts such an addition could be made. However, when I make a total evaluation, I can say that it is definitely a game above the average. If you haven't tried it, you should give it a chance. And the way the story left off in the end we can expect a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: You can also check out my Video Review of the game  The game’s premise is set in Ancient India’s Rajasthan where a group of demons kidnap your brother and you must chase them across abandoned forts and corrupted cities to get him back.Right off the bat I want to highlight their attention to detail. In the first scene you can completely feel how her first emotion of panic for her brother slowly gives way to bewilderment about her strange surroundings.The scale of the game is designed in a way to make you feel miniscule against the backdrop of large temples and mighty cities. They have paid a lot of attention to intricate patterns and mosaics to give it an authentic Ancient Indian look.And the sound, my god, the sound, anything I say will just fall short. It successfully evokes emotions in you and makes you feel as if you are right there. I also really appreciate that they have built in these bites of knowledge to educate you about the Hindu Lore for example about Garuda or the different avatars of Vishnu, Now moving on to the combat,Basically for each weapon you have 4 attacks, left click basic attack, right click heavy attack, Shift for special attack and Q for the ultimate. There are also multiple combinations of these basic attacks with running up a pole or a wall for heavier area damage attacks. One thing worth keeping in mind is that you get health when you defeat each enemy but only if you end them with a takedown.You unlock 4 weapons while playing and you can switch freely between them1. First is Durga’s trishool which is the melee attack weapon you start off with2. Next you get Vishnu’s Bow for ranged attacks3. Then comes Vishnu’s sword and shield for blocking and attacking manuevers4. Finally, Vishnu’s Chakra which is an ultimate weapon and basically just oneshots all enemies. You get this only at the end of the gameThey also have a power orb system which allows you to enhance your attacks. The 3 Gods, Durga, Vishnu and Shiva give you different powers, electricity, fire and ice respectivelyYou should make sure that all your orbs are placed in upgrades for any one god. You can have the boons of any one god at any one point of time, they don’t stack.You meet a variety of enemies in the game ranging from the basic brute to mechanical eyes which are actually pretty easy to take down. A special mention to the Demon Ninjas. I personally felt they were the hardest adversaries to overcome. In the game you will also come across these mandalas which reveal the memories from your past. It is a sort of a mini game and they look amazing. Tip: always start with the outer most ring.So guys go ahead and get your copy of Raji. The experience of being a mere mortal yet challenging Demons with the blessings of Gods is not something you will get anywhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Overall the game is really good. I loved the way they told the story and extra lore you find in the game. The combat has so much promise. Why the negative review. In summary fixed camera when you need free movement (Like you might find yourself as I did trying to turn a camera control that is not there. I have missed so many platforms cause I couldn't gauge where the platform was.). Enemy spam in a bad way (I would never recommend putting this game above easy even on easy it is a problem.). Platforming is based on your dodge button (you jump off walls you are meant to climb (yes it's a fighting move but still)). Bow is useless in fights enemies are fast as or faster than you (exception for a few) and bow is auto aim at what you are looking at. Lastly the developers have done nothing since 2020 except release it on switch which tells me they are "done" with the game. I would recommend it still just be aware of the above and get it on discount.Story: Without any spoilers this games story is almost entirely told by flat paper puppets no joke and I love it. The story was engaging and well written. I also loved the ineradicable in the game that gave you more story behind the characters and god's that were talking.Graphics/Art Style: Paper Puppet folklore storytelling. The game itself is 3d and very well polished like I will probably be making these into backgrounds for my computer. No falling through world or flickering etc. Animations: Some animations for ledge jumping (grabbing onto a ledge and hoisting yourself to the next ledge) is stiff and not fluid (it's a small thing but obvious). The animations for combat and weapons and take-downs are well done. If you can do them before the enemy hits you.Controls: Typical controls. Nothing weird or out of place. No options for editing though. You have a small but pretty fun selection of combat moves you can do with the 2 outta the 4 weapons in the game. You have no control over the camera except zoom. The bow is auto aim only at what you look at. Combat: You have several fighting moves and finishers to each weapon you get. Only one weapon I have found needs a little help is the bow cause it had auto aim and you half to be facing the enemy you want to hit. Which is really hard to do when all the enemies are fast as or faster than you are. Can go off screen and hit you with ranged attacks. You don't know if your auto aim is locked on to them for the bow.Achievement's: You can get them all in one run highly suggest putting it on easy and enjoying the story the combat was still pretty hard even for me on easy. I found none of them to be out of the way or extremely hard to get. But if you missed one of those pesky orbs yeah good luck going and getting that thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful... and that's about all it has going for it. The story is weak . There is no chapter select - if you miss an orb (which is very easy btw, don't jump without assessing in the 3rd level - and there is no main menu. When the game ends, you restart the game again in an infinite loop. The puzzles are all very simple matching pictures/matching gears, and are very much not a big aspect of the game. This game is combat heavy, and is kind of good. The mechanics are a little weak though, as for the OP move you have to collect things instead of it being built up over time. There are no real shinies. Hearing traditional Hindu stories was a great aspect, and Raji seemed cool, but there was a lot of holes in the story. . This game is a great start and I think with some work it would be better... but as it is right now, it's just something pretty to look at as you kill enemies.

name: This Is the President
detailed_description: This Is the President is a story driven management game. In the year 2020 you are elected to be the President of the United States of America. To escape justice for your past crimes as a shady multi-millionaire businessman, you need to ratify Amendment 28 which would grant lifetime immunity to any President. Manage your official and unofficial staff like a real mafioso in order to deal with all the old problems you’ve had in the past, as well as the shiny new problems that come with the office. You’ll battle with your competitors, the establishment, the media and even foreign leaders. In this political thriller-satire mix, the player's actions will inescapably lead to situations that escalate into absurd, terrifying, tragic and even ridiculous situations. But the road to lifelong immunity is full of pitfalls, and you’ll need to remember to clean up the daily messes that arise. Some might even call these distractions “presidential duties”. Score some easy points by price capping video games and banning online advertising. But why limit yourself to ads alone? Regulate the whole Internet -- your friends in China could use some help with censorship anyway. Or how about rescuing Russia’s president who’s been overthrown by his opponent? Sending a hamster into space is one of the more “reasonable” choices, right next to helping a serial killer escape prison. Of course your team members may dislike some of your decisions, but it doesn't always hurt to remind them who’s helping cover up their dirty little secrets. Things like gambling, alcohol and domestic violence, just to name a few. Thugs, hackers, journalists, lawyers: You’ll need a variety of talents, and no matter how differently they may feel about the nature of their work, there is no moral dilemma that cannot be solved with a juicy Christmas bonus from our charity fund. Americans can put their faith in their cute little 'separation of powers' all they want, but no-one can resist your methods of persuasion. Deep down they already know: Nothing can separate power from you. There’s only one way out. Change the fabric of the Constitution of the United States by persuading, blackmailing, bribing, and bullying a large part of the political system into granting you lifelong immunity. Manage your approval rating, cash and crew unlike any US President before – stay on top of your presidency by any means necessary Hold speeches, draft executive orders, manage daily crises, hold press conferences, and tweet better than any President before Hire a team of assassins, hackers, lobbyists, and other specialists. Send them on dangerous missions that can be solved by legal means. If that doesn’t work, send them on dangerous missions that can be solved by illegal means Experience a compelling interactive narrative with a wide variety of choices and story branches. Will you end your term on your terms, or are you just a pawn in a bigger game? Rule the country as a true mobster would with a shadow cabinet that is feared and respected on a global scale

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the idea behind this game and went in expecting to enjoy it, but was ultimately disappointed.  The premise is that you're some sort of corrupt business executive who, to avoid being prosecuted for your various crimes, decided to become President of the United States and pass an amendment that would give you lifetime immunity.  It's an absurd plan, but that's clearly deliberate, and I did find the idea amusing when I started playing.  However, the humor ended up falling flat for me- it basically felt like someone shouting "Haha, politicians suck!" and stretching that one joke out for 20+ hours.  I keep hearing the game called a satire, but it's hard for me to even see it as that- satire is something that uses humor to make a point, while this game seems to be going out of its way to avoid actually saying anything.  It doesn't give any meaningful criticism of any person, institution, or ideology, and even its bashing of politicians in general starts to feel pretty toothless given just how over the top and absurd the in-game events are.  I obviously don't know the developers' thought process, but the whole time I was playing I was left with the impression that they were so focused on not offending anyone who might disagree with them that they ended up creating a really shallow and hollow parody.Then there's the gameplay.  As others have pointed out, it shares some similarities with Suzerain in that much of it plays out as a visual novel with you making choices on how to respond to various events.  Most of the correct answers feel completely random though, and there's very little true strategy- it's mostly just trial and error.  The worst part for me was the "yes/no" options that pop up between tasks.  You'll usually get 2-4 quick events after completing each task, with the choice to decided whether or not to commit to a course of action that the game presents you with, and you'll get a small reward or penalty depending on whether you pick the right one.  I absolutely HATED these- it was complete guesswork with no rhyme or reason as to which option was correct.  You decide to reward someone who helped find a group of terrorists?  Well, turns out that he IS the terrorist and framed those people!  The game probably thinks it's being funny, and maybe it would have been if this happened two or three times in the game, but you'll be dealing with dozens of these choices throughout your playthrough.  About halfway through the game, I stopped reading them and just chose "yes" every time they came up, since there was no point in me actually trying to figure out which option was right.This game had potential, but I can't recommend it.  There were some parts I enjoyed, such as finding ways to sway congressional representatives to vote for my amendment or plotting to replace supreme court justices, and it makes me feel like the game could have been great if it took itself just a little more seriously- it could still be comedic and it could still make me play a villain, but at least let me have fun being a manipulative bastard instead of mostly just clicking an option and crossing my fingers.  Ultimately, I found it to be a tedious, frustrating, shallow experience, and it gets a thumbs down from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Suzerain so the comparison was enough to catch my interest. I'd say on balance I prefer This Is the President (TITP) - there's a different economy aspect, but the game is faster, has much more content, and it's easier to read.With that inevitable comparison out of the way, I can judge the game on its own merits. I like playing political sims, but I also like playing video games - why this distinction? Because simulators often don't have much, if any, gameplay, as they're designed to simulate reality in a sterile way. A flight sim for example will treat you like a real pilot with lots of different buttons to press, rather than CJ from GTA: San Andreas who presses just one button to get into any vehicle.TITP puts you in the shoes of a newly elected president, but while simulating this political scenario it also offers you actual gameplay, such as:Gameplay mechanics are introduced at a moderate pace - usually just one per month - in order to help the player learn these mechanics. By the end of TITP, there is a lot of leverage for the player to make use of, so the choice of pace works for the game's benefit. I played the game on Challenging difficulty and was pleased with how much the game attempted to push me off balance while walking the political tightrope.Some people seem to think that TITP is simply a President Simulator where you can roleplay as your "perfect President", but unlike sims it has gameplay partly due to its pre-developed plot. Your character has indeed just been elected President, but he has a shady past and its your job to find the solution that this morally grey individual has been seeking. You can still act as the President and pursue reforms that you'd like to see in real life, but everything you do pertains to a single united goal - past Amendment 28 in order to obtain your post-presidential immunity from the law. You can improve healthcare for Americans, you can discourage abortions, you can replace bureaucracy with an efficient AI with datamining algorithms - in the end of each of these, the only actual point of doing them is to achieve a certain approval rating as part of your wider strategy to achieve an ultimate goal. All of these pertain to that one single goal your character got himself elected President for in the first place!So this is an important aspect of TITP that some people don't pick up on -  Imagine if Flight Simulator saw you play as a pilot with a drinking problem, a secret affair with his co-pilot's wife, and a sordid history of plane crashes. You wouldn't just be doing 7-hour flights from Heathrow to Dubai, you would also be dealing with all of his many personal issues in order to negotiate his way towards a single, overarching goal in life. This is how TITP introduces gameplay to a simulator-like setting. This isn't President Simulator, it's an actual video game where you must explore every possible political option - whether good, evil, or in between - to achieve your primary goal of passing Amendment 28 and obtaining that legal immunity forever.The plot therefore has to be good enough to hold your attention throughout a single term of four years (this is roughly 20 or more gameplay hours), and I believe there are enough twists and turns to keep a player interested:To use an example of the plot's strength, here's a subplot with very minor spoilers but don't read if you want to go in blind:The most surprising aspect of TITP to me is the humour-seriousness balance. There's no decades-old, tired stereotypes like in the Tropico series - the humour is current, but still willing to mock everyone on all positions of the political spectrum. At the same time, the game is perfectly serious. I'm not an American myself, but I understand the process of effecting Amendment 28 is pretty close to - if not 1:1 with - how the US political system actually works. You need to first start lobbying for a new bill to be proposed by others, you then need to achieve majorities in Congress, you need a majority on the Supreme Court, and then you need to have the entire thing ratified by US states. Reading this back, it's almost as if TTIP is indeed a President Simulator - but believe me, there is plenty of actual gameplay and humour to keep you hooked.Playing TITP I felt like I could do anything I wanted.  I could use Harry Truman's concept of Presidential power to achieve my aims both at home and abroad. Absolutely everyone was at my mercy. I actually felt like the most powerful man on the planet - after all isn't this the universally-popular opinion of what a US President actually is?

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically convoluted, tonally dissonant, and lacking a clear vision of what it wants to be. If you're looking for a gritty political simulator, you'll be irritated when the game asks you to devote your time to enhancing the reputation of a street drug bearing your Vice President's name, or when you lose reputation for not allowing a budget-driven sci fi blockbuster to shoot inside the White House.If you're looking for a tongue-in-cheek Mad World presidency, you'll be irritated when the game asks you to tackle school shootings, terrorist incidents, and drug crime. If you're looking for a competent strategy game, you'll be irritated when an option labeled "host a charity benefit for hurricane relief" actually means "host a charity benefit in the ruins of still-battered town, hindering the ongoing search and rescue efforts," or when voters disapprove of your banning gambling in apps for children. Ultimately, it's not even clear to me what game the developers *wanted* to make -- only that they've failed to make *any* of those options, and you get to experience all of those failures, all at once.

_childDocuments_.review: The only organized crime, where you don´t get punished for... politicsIn "This is the president" you have an interesting mixture of visual novel and management game, which is heavily leaning towards story telling.As the newly chosen Potus, you and your wife, as well as crazy best friend are doing everything they can.... for the people? for the country? naaah.. to protect yourself and cash in as much as you can on the way, of course.For this you have to keep the money flowing as well as your lackeys happy, who work for you (as long as you pay them and dont stress them out too much).The main goal of a politician to get his way is to manipulate the dumb mob into believing all his lies. This is mostly done by big and small activities. Depending if you set the right staff onto a problem, the result can cost or bring you voters. Realistically though, many problems you get to solve have positive and negative side effects. Some even long term .. and some are story wise, which you have to take as they come.The writing goes from fun and hilarious to some quite realistic concerns, but mostly keeps it´s tongue in cheek humor. I especially liked the many different staff options you can have, and that they effectively leave (or worse) if you don´t keep them happy. Adds some roleplay to it. Also as a non american you can even learn a bit about the basic political system.The graphics and music fit to the atmospheric story of this hopeless view into politics. Conclusio: For me, as a fan of story based visual novels i really liked this mixture.. and of course this - sometimes too realistic - view on todays politics was also fitting. Add some light management and rp parts and it makes one of my favourite games of this kind in the last years.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. As someone who played both This is the Police, I really enjoyed the narrative and writing of both games, and bought this game almost solely on the fact that it had people from TiTP involved in the writing. Unfortunately, while the game shows a lot of promise, there are some very glaring issues.1) You don’t know who you are, as a character. The introduction is particularly rough due to this, since you find suddenly “find out” that you’ve had a gay lover, killed a young girl on an accident, have a hidden son, and used to run in a gang, to name a few. All these details are mentioned with all the subtlety of your wife telling you “By the way, let’s send some money to the woman who is pretending to be the mother of our son". This makes getting into character very hard, since you get constantly surprised by these elements you should know from the get go. Even plot dumping you with all the details at the very beginning would have been better than this, I think.2) The game can’t pick a tone to save its life. Even though TiTP had moments of levity, it took itself seriously and you knew what to expect tone-wise. Here, the game is constantly pinballing from serious, to satire, to straight up ridiculousness. One minute you are deciding on whether to rescue a military submarine on Cuban waters and dealing with the potential international fallout, the next you are helping the Chinese government develop an algorithm to censor the internet because its leader doesn’t like the memes about him, and the next you’re breaking an illegal turkey fighting ring.And even though the game reached some semblance of balance from the mid game onwards, it proceeded to go full ridiculous in the final act and destroyed any kind of investment I had in the story.3) The game lies to you. It could have been just an unfortunate coincidence for my playthrough, but the Persuade/Bribe/Use evidence interface that is shown in the game’s store page (For reference, the screenshot with Senator Dickenson) is only used once in the game. Throughout the game you get a substantial amount of potential blackmail material that can be sold for money or used against someone (Or so you’d think), but save for one time, there are no instances of the latter. This is especially rough considering there are several pieces of evidence regarding the main antagonist of the game, but they never come into play.4) Money and costs are seriously unbalanced. Even though your first employees are relatively balanced in regards to salary, any other employee has a base salary at least 10 times higher than them, and they have no qualms on asking you to double, triple, or even quintuple their salary, resulting in employees easily costing you several hundreds of thousands of dollars a month each, with potential monetary gains that grow nowhere near that rhythm. And in true genius fashion, a lot of missions that can increase your monthly revenue stream are gated behind having a significant capital to begin with, so it’s very easy to get yourself in a loop of “Can’t accumulate money, so I can’t do missions to increase my monthly revenue, and my team’s salary demands increase, so I can’t accumulate money…”.5) Every month, you get a lot of minor choices that give you a Yes/No choice, with minor impacts on approval/money, but most of them are completely unpredictable when you’re playing for the first time: Do you agree to give 100k to organize a fundraiser to feed poor people on Christmas? Your reputation drops because you’re flaunting your wealth. Do you agree to shoot a bunch of civilian drones that are writing PRESIDICK in the sky? Your reputation rises because people liked the “fireworks”. Ironically, choosing the most counterintuitive options usually gives you a better chance of a good result.TL;DR version: Even if you’re an ardent TiTP fan, don’t waste your money on this game. It’s not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I review this game as someone with a bit of game-dev experience, and as someone who has actually worked in the American political system.  I had a good friend who was a mayor, I was on the staff of a Congressman, I held a post in the White House - this genre has a specific appeal to me.  Let me break this game down.Positive:So much attention to detail, it is amazing, and with great pacing to keep the player from being overwhelmed!  Kudos to the game devs on that point.The cast of characters are often believable (especially in the first half of the game), and appear to have several layers.The story is strong and gives definite direction, but the freedom in whom to use, what to choose, is generally the player-choosing.  The mechanics are clear and allows the player the freedom to use them to manipulate them in a very real kind of political way.  Player choice REALLY does seem to matter.  Often (or at least initially), the immersion in feeling the Presidential role is one of the best I've ever played.The imitation twitter is clever.The game catches the political corruption, like no other game and must always be taken into play - and unlike every other game I've played, it's not some wierd-game-mechanic corruption that simply makes things more expensive, or results less effective, but it impacts everything you do.The ability to form your own cabinet adds a great mechanic to the game, that does an amazing job at shaping the flow, feel, and opportunities in the game.Immersion value - great!UI is polished, makes sense, and allows the player to keep track of the game with great detail (I left the game about half way through, feeling repulsed, and when I came back, the UI was there to remind me, and plug me back into the game).Negative:  I understand this game is meant to portray the political world in a dark grimy satirical way, BUT WTH devs?With all the freedom the game gives in allowing the player a chance to move the direction of their Presidency, that freedom is rapidly stripped away by one of the darkest game player-characters ever created.  I am constantly having to do damage control for things that my character supposedly did, before I, the player, entered the story. It was challenging at first, and I enjoyed the challenge - until the game made me really become disgusted with my own character as I was forced to continue down the degenerate path.The imitation twitter doesn't quite hit the funny-bone I think it tried to hit, and I often found myself hating all the 'selection' choices.As the game continues the amazing plot and quasi-realism (on so many amazing levels) it is increasingly swallowed by the game developers obsession with corruption-satire.  Before the game ends, the devs have given up all attempts at realism and have given-in to full corruption satire- all brilliantly written plots components now surrender to the absurd.  Ending with a potential teaser that indicates a possible chance to redeem the repulsive, but doesn't happen.My Verdict: Brilliant game with some of the best crafted mechanics I've EVER played in a political game, ruined by an increasingly repulsive player-character.  The game eventually loses everything it amazingly built; so it can put more emphasis on the dark-satire - pushed beyond all possible boundaries of sanity and reality.  It went from fun and well built to a chore to finish the game as you wade through 'WTH' moment after moment.((MORE REVIEWS)) TO SEE OTHER INSIGHTFUL REVIEWS, HEAD TO  ((THUMBS UP AND JOIN))For my Brand New Review YT channel, check out:

_childDocuments_.review: After a promising start this game has worn rather thin, and I'm only a quarter of the way through. I'm stopping now because the gameplay systems are beginning to expand in ways that unpleasantly remind me of "We. The Revolution" which was a neat core game that tacked on so many superfluous gameplay systems that it undermined itself, which wasn't helped by the narrative ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the bed in Act 3. I do enjoy the core loop of This is the President, if only initially. Managing my subordinates, responding to crises, and all the political finagling one would expect. Unfortunately it's burned me out with the copious amount of random events that pop up during each month/turn. Interrupting my play with two to three events with yes or no answers that are entirely guesswork as to which one is the good one. Did you award the Presidential Freedom to a guy who foiled a terrorist plot with a tip? Too bad, he's the terrorist and framed his friends! It just feels vapid and needlessly punishing, and the game straight up tutorializes save scumming so you are encouraged to go back and fix it. With the catch being that the game saves at the beginning of each month, meaning that events that occurred just before you were planning to end the turn means a good few minutes sitting through unskippable textboxes (which can be sped up but not skipped) and replaying all the events you already did.As for the humor, sometimes it's great, I loved it for the first couple hours even. But it wears off as the jokes tend to be either "Lol, so random" or "Ha! Politicians suck!" the latter of which seems to be the thesis statement of the game dragged on for far more hours than I care to play. Then the game slaps you in the face with tonal dissonance as a school shooting happens or Chicago has race riots. Neither of which played for laughs but feel strange in a game where you talk the astronaut slated to be the first man on Mars back into the rocket by singing him the National Anthem. But that event ends in tragedy if you fail to pick the single correct set of dialogue options and he gets gunned down by federal agents surrounding his house, and really just encapsulates the game's problem with humor.Overall, it's a good core idea that stretches itself too thin and slowly wears you down through frustrating design, slow text, a wildly inconsistent tone.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, this game sounds great.  It's like "Scandal" where the politics play a secondary role to the damage control/spin of covering up the players' dirty little secrets.  I went into this game honestly wanting to love it, but I encountered some issues I could not overlook.First and foremost are things like spelling and grammar.  I saw at least one "United Stated" misspelling, which is a problem in a text-heavy game where you are the President.  I also saw instances where a character was referred to by both genders within the same paragraph, which can be confusing since there are so many different people to keep track of.  These are little things, yes, but all the more reason they should have been ironed out before release.The main component of this game involves assigning minions to various tasks.  Each employee has multiple ways to accomplish a task.  While this is cool in theory, you are given no indication of their odds of success or how difficult a challenge will be against their skills.  A difficulty indicator (something like "3 out of 5 difficulty" or "60% chance of success") would go a long way to informing a player's decision-making processes, especially since another key component is monitoring our staffers' stress levels to keep them from burning out.These people work for the President of the United States, so one would think they are the best of the best in their fields.  Or at least highly competent.  But failure strikes in weird places.  I'll give an example.  A journalist was suspected of obtaining classified files from my administration.  I sicced my hacker on him and chose the option of hacking the journalist's laptop remotely.  The hacker failed this task every time, even though it sounded like it would be right up his alley.  Later on, there is an option to have this same hacker pilot a drone with explosives to murder someone who is blackmailing you.  The hacker always succeeds at this, which is baffling to me since this seems like it would be a much harder task by comparison.It seems like choices are linear in the sense that there is only one ending for each option.  Only a success or failure ending has been written for each employee's option, not both.  This goes against the very nature of the "play as you want" philosophy the game offers.

_childDocuments_.review: “Dramatic, but it's way too dramatic.”The concept of the game and the graphics themselves are good. The story of this game was enough to remind me of the lesson: "It's very hard to be a moral and ideal leader." Before I started this game, obviously I was determined to reform and advance the United States as a politician with a people-conscious, progressive view of politics. But after playing the game, I assassinated 4 characters and generated budget revenue through corruption. I played dirty for my own sake. Political enemies, fake news, and distorted rumors somewhat changed my mind and made me realize how hard it was to stay in power. This experience itself is definitely the beauty and advantage of this game.BUT!! This game was a bit disappointing for me who expected a political simulation. Unlike other games of the same genre, this game focuses on stories and events. But the problem is that the story itself is not interesting. The whole story feels like watching a low-quality third-rate political drama that's not interesting, and the events are too dramatic. Of course, that is not to say that such events are unrealistic. Rather, repeating 'too dramatic' events made me lose interest in the game, and the combination of some ‘intended’ positive and negative events rather negatively affected the game.Also, there is a lack of probability. According to the storyline, the president is described as a somewhat less recognizable but inevitably elected because there are no candidates in the party, and the first lady makes a "false" plan to revise the constitution to immune their actions during his presidency."Then why on earth did he become POTUS?“"How did such a person become president?"In addition, the biggest enemies of this game are White House secretaries. They will be likely to make unfair requests randomly, and if you don't listen to them, they’ll quit their job and disappear. Even, the first lady constantly asks for embezzlement of public funds, and the weirdo vice president repeats actions that only harm the government reputation like a psychopath. Maybe the vice president needs more attention?In conclusion, I don't really want to recommend this game. Only buy it when it's more than 70% off.

_childDocuments_.review: firstly, i'd like to apologise for my grammer, i have issues but i do my best. now then on to the review. secondly this review uses the term 'player killer' which is a term i use for a segment of the game so boring or painful that i think a normal player would just quit at that point. to put this short, there was potential for a good game here, but be it by bitterness or dislike, its become a bad one for having no good options and not understanding how important balancing the selections is for a game like this. bad balancing with everything from the amount of missions and the money and overloading the player plague the game as well.speeches are a bit too realistic in that they are long, boring and without end or point, you don't get anything off them than improved or reduced voting score, which isn't that important, and honestly the speeches really are a player killer.  the game is also great for listening to youtube, in that it could just be me, but there doesn't seem to be any significant music or sounds, just papers shuffling and music snippets.  when you become president as well the game overloads you, you get a full sidebar of missions where at most you had two before, as well as overloading you with tasks to do. there doesn't feel to be enough staff as well, so stress becomes a major concern. the speeches are not even the first player killer, that would be the play, which, despite everything i tried, had no good option to compromise or bribe. the only option was to kill your former freind, which is a three point stress option and promises trouble later.                                                                                                              PRos: the game can be quite funtheres a lot of modern day like twitter and stuff in this, rather than staying historicalthe UI is designed pretty well. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, coming from suzerain and other political fiction games. There are many things to like, the game play is quick, writing is quippy, and production value is certainly high with some nice cut scenes. However my gripes mirror many reviews.Tone: The tone is inconsistent, do not expect immersion but rather a ping pong between dealing with a shooting to watching a play about gay lovers resolved by running an old man over. I quickly went from reading most lines to simply skipping to decisions, a choice exacerbated by randomness. Randomness: While amusing at first, the lack of ability to accurately gauge how to react to any given situation makes each choice feel meaningless. A diminutive cop is facing some adversity? Help him to realize he did some bad stuff netting bad press. Wear a Halloween costume to a Halloween dance? Plot twist, its formal wear so you look stupid in an outfit. Picking the most absurd option is likely the best with most outcomes netting little benefit or loss making choices feel pointless.Staff: Your staff are goofy caricatures, definitely a departure from something like suzerain or this is the police but still I can get behind it. However, besides first few all recruits are few and far between, costing from 11k to start to 200k immediately after with the staff having no qualms asking for you to quintuple that 200k to a million or quit on the spot. This compounds  certain events needing certain staff, and using staff making them burn out and quit. Get used to not being able to do what you want if you don't know what is coming in advance.Overall, these breaks to the flow of game play compound to a generally frustrating experience that quickly loses your attention. The game is too long and verbose to be a quick humorous diversion, but just in cohesive enough to lose anyone actually trying to be invested. With that I unfortunately cannot recommend.TLDR: Amusing satirical political sim that trips over its tone and randomness enough to lose serious players yet too long and convoluted mechanically to retain casual players.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I have not completed the game yet.The game is random with interesting but poorly fleshed out mechanics, barely saved by a good narrative.--I could probably use some dice to choose which actions I take and have a better time than actually trying to make the better decision. Create a pottery studio for the first lady after she asked for one? The press: "A sexless marriage filled with bickering". Display miltary strength after Chinese missiles threaten japan? The pacifists didn't like that! Most of the game is spent clicking through this never-ending stream of useless decisions. Offered to build a home for "pardoned turkeys" to survive thanksgiving? It's a coinflip between being depicted as stupid or a savior. (pro tip: build the turkey rehab)The problem (as I see it) is  If you do one thing and it upsets the pacifist crowd, you lose points--There's no recovery from the militant or pro-<country-being-threatened> crowd. It makes actually trying at the game mildly infuriating. At every click I have to wonder "Oh, will I lose popularity points because this upsets the amish?!" Who the popularity points represents changes every five seconds, too: There's no consistency you can learn to follow. You tweet like, once a year, and the content of your tweets has zero impact on the midgame. Speeches are too few, too far apart, etc. Early in the game you get options to do press releases, etc. which quickly drop off to nothing during the midgame.. Which I can understand, but it's almost ridiculous. Ollie, your techie and most valuable character, gets burned out almost every month because you can either use him or fail the task at hand. Sending your security to kill a dude costs 1 stress point, while having ollie hack into some IoT cameras takes three! He's sent to vacation almost every month because of this balancing.  Overall, I think the narrative is great, but it's just an infuriating game to try and play seriously. I believe this game would be far more enjoyable if the power to turn a bad situation good (and a good situation bad) was actually entrusted to the players. , the game has a LOT of typos, most of them are pretty obvious. I'm amazed they didn't at least run it through a spell checker given how text-heavy the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear: this game is not a "simulator game". I find it difficult to place neatly into a single genre and while I'm tempted to use the term "choice-based interactive novel" I feel like that leaves the wrong impression.I don't want to just repeat the game description: President, shady past, goal of passing amendment to escape justice. You get it. My feeling was that it mostly came across like if "House of Cards" was written less as a thriller and more as a satirical comedic tragedy, if you can imagine that. It ranges from very dark (pushing journalists in front of trains) to very outrageous (weird cult worshiping the vice president).Politically this game is kind of all over the place, and nothing feels like it's off limits. Many situations you deal with are clearly based on real world events and the game is not afraid to make a mockery of these as you manipulate the government to serve your own ends. Yes, you are intended to play as a corrupt politician and no there is not really a viable option to play it straight.Overall, I found the storytelling in this game very entertaining. Some of the stories made me laugh out loud and the characters are written in a charming way that made me sad to see them go at the end. A special mention would be the final act of the game where it really cranks the outrageous factor to 11 and delivers some truly hilarious and memorable moments.The entirety of the gameplay revolves around making political decisions as president (big suprise). These take three main forms:1. Pop-ups: A message will appear and ask you a yes or no question that you must answer to advance. Usually something along the lines of "A clothing retailer started using your likeness and campaign slogans on their t-shirts, should we press them for compensation?"2. Assignments: These are one of two cards that appear on the side of the screen with a timer that tells you how many months they will be available. They have some pretty meaty flavor text that will explain a situation and request members of your team with specific abilities. It's usually pretty obvious what team members to send but occasionally will throw in some curveballs like "We'll need a tech guy to set up the website and someone who loves nature." These resolve the next month after you've assigned them and tell you the outcome.3. Situation missions: This is the other kind of card that appears on the side of the screen. With these you choose a few of your team members to bring with you into a situation and take context specific actions to advance the story. Based on who you bring you will be able to do actions like "Launch a social media campaign accusing your opponent of harassment" , "Break into your opponent’s house and try to find incriminating evidence", or "File a lawsuit against your opponent". These are really fun and make you think carefully about what the best approach to a situation is. The rewards for successfully completing these is either money, approval rating, or items (used to increase approval rating or sold for money). They really facilitate the games writing which is the main draw of the game. There is a LOT of reading in this game so be warry of that if you are scared off by long paragraphs of text.The team managing aspect is where the strategy of the game takes place. Each month you have to pay your members a salary and manage their stress points. If they gain 5 stress points, then they burn out and you can’t use them until next month. If you do that too many times, then something… bad might happen. You can also assign them to positions in your administration that each have different effects depending on the specialist. One press secretary might increase approval rating by 3% each month while another will decrease approval by 3% but lower team member stress gain. It’s a fun system that feels rewarding when you find a really good setup.This is the President is an entertaining mostly text-based story game where you play as a corrupt politician. Thematically it blends satirical comedy and noir fiction with interesting stories and charming characters. The writing is fun, and the gameplay feels interesting even when there are a few “Gotcha!” outcomes from some of the decisions. The UI and soundtrack are nice and don’t start to offend even after a bit more than 20 hours of playtime. If you enjoyed either of the This is the Police games this is very much in the same style. Overall recommend 8.5/10
