_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 Would recommendPros:-Wonderful tough-in-cheek humor that balances out the game's seriousness well-Decent replay value; there's many different avenues to achieve your goals-Thought-provoking storyline, and honestly a sadly accurate depiction of the American political system-Actions have consequences; although they don't always feel good, they make sense with how politics and media works-The gameplay is remarkably simple, and most of the game is in your choices, as this is a "choose-your-own-adventure" style game.Cons-It gets really frustrating trying to make a good choice and realizing there are no good choices. Sometimes even the choices you think would work out end up being catastrophic for absolutely no reason.-It's a little too realistic at some points, and it's kinda scary (didn't we literally just have them find cocaine in the White House in real life?)-You have to do a ton of micromanaging to get everything accomplished. And there's no way to even try to divvy out the responsibilities like a real political official could-It gets rather repetitive at times while you're waiting for another big political option to come around-You cannot go through this trying to play purely good guy, because you're already a corrupt PoS. You will have to make evil decisions.In Summary:Every dollar you spend on a game should be at least 1 hour of entertainment. This game is definitely worth the purchase to play through, especially if you can grab it on sale. Don't expect anything life-changing, but it's overall a decent game to play between Skyrim runs.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting a new game will allow you to choose the games difficulty and there are four options to choose from. You have Easy, for players who are just here for the story, Normal is recommended for most players. Challenging is for those players wanting a challenge and Hard where any wrong action could be the end of your presidential career.  It’s November 2020, you’ve just won the presidential elections, your good friend and your vice president Antonio Estaba sings your praises as he introduces you to the American people as the new President-elect. You take centre stage and give a victory speech to your awaiting audience, it’s from here that you make your first decisions. Your first decision will be chosen from multiple two or three options depending on what you choose. This will become your speech as you address the nation, your promises to the people while you’re in the presidential seat of power. The objective of the game is to get Amendment 28 passed; this Amendment would allow any president to receive a lifelong immunity from prosecution after their term in the hot seat. The Amendment would certainly be helpful to you as you’ll be investigated for wrong doings prior to your victory in the presidential elections. No matter what else you do with your presidency, you must get Amendment 28 passed by Congress, then and only then can you be free from prosecution. To get the Amendment through you’re going to have to get some help from powerful allies from both houses, the House of Representatives and the Senate if you’re to get the Amendment passed by Congress. Your wife, Ellie and future First Lady has a four-step plan, first is to get the services of a lobbyist. Someone that has connections everywhere at the Capitol and is able to get things done. However, their services aren’t going to be cheap but they are worth every penny. Second will require you to get two thirds of Congress to push through your Amendment. Thirdly, you’re going to have to get the Amendment written into law, this will have opposition. So, you’ll have to change the ratification process, you’re going to have to get the Supreme Court involved for that. Once you have the court on your side then the voters can be swung your way easier and have them vote for the Amendment. It’s still not a guarantee that you’ll be able to get the voters to vote for the Amendment so when it’s time you’re going to have to convince each state and its voters, even those which don’t like you that it’s the right thing to do. The fourth and final objective required to get the Amendment through is that you’ll need ninety percent approval ratings across the country. This is by no means an easy task, the ninety percent is a record high, so you’re going to have to pucker up and do whatever is required of you to reach your goal. Each month will bring in New Events, some will have a time limit, others not and by completing these events may help you in getting the country on your side. The events which are available to you are on the left of the screen and those which are currently unavailable to you are on the right side of the screen. Where the events will show on the map of America as well. These events also include your promises you made to the public, what you will strive to do once you take office. Keeping your promises will keep the voters on your side and help drive up your public ratings.  Events can be anything, composing your first executive order, filling your administration or guiding a visitor around the White House but they will need your attention, although sometimes you’re not going to be able to give it your attention. Depending on the event and the choices you make will determine if your approval ratings rise or fall. What outcome you decide may be logical, politically correct or downright wrong but it’s for you to decide. However, this isn’t about doing the right thing, you need to get your approval ratings up, this might mean that you have to choose the options which you wouldn’t have normally chosen, you’re not going to keep everyone happy. As you progress, you’ll have new characters which you can hire and recruit to your staff in the White House. You can use these characters and send them out to perform objectives such as to dig some dirt on someone, kindly persuade someone to do something for you or to have them find and fix a leak within your office. There are lots of events which will require you to act upon them. Each new member which joins your staff will have their own specialised Skills and Job types.  When sending someone out on a mission event, you will be given some options as to how to proceed. Each option will be marked with a number of stars, these stars are the stress points. Upon reaching five stress points that character will stop working for you. You can help them relieve their stress levels by sending them on holidays (at 10K a pop). This can start becoming expensive rather quickly, it will also render that character unavailable for the next month. So, you’ll have to choose wisely who you send and their actions they decide upon. At times you will have fall in your lap some items or information on your opposition. You can use these to your benefit or you can sell them to your lobbyist. You can get a nice payday from some of them and you will need to have some cash coming in as it’s not cheap trying to push through your Amendment or other laws etcetera. It also costs money to hire and keep your staff paid each monthly. You begin with a kitty of two million dollars, this won’t last long so be wise on how you spent it. In the settings you will find options for Game - Cursor Size, Language (English and Russian), Text Size and Text Speed. Visuals - Display Mode (Full Screen and Windowed) and Resolution. Audio - Music, Sound and Cutscene Volume Controls. The graphics and artwork in This is the President are fantastic and it runs great except for game crashed on me the once. There are plenty of events with multiple actions to take as well as your main goal of securing your freedom after your presidency has ended. Positives  + Great looking artwork  + Easy to play + Has achievements + Has cards + Steam cloud Negatives  - Crashed once Do whatever it takes as President to get Amendment 28 passed into law, allowing you your freedom after your time in the White House comes to an end 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even very far into this game but I can't rave enough about how incredibly polished and enjoyable it is: the graphics, the UI, the writing and the voice acting are all absolutely TOP notch. I was definitely not expecting this kind of AAA quality from a $15/£12 game. The gameplay is similar to Suzerain, if you've played that: as President of your country (in this case, the USA rather than a fictional nation), you encounter largely text-based events where you must make decisions about your policies and alliances. The tone of the game is more satirical than Suzerain: it's still serious, but very much a wry commentary on the populist nature of Western politics today. What's remarkable is it largely manages to do this without picking sides, and it equally satirises both left and right.But the gameplay has several other unique features that elevate it even further: to start with, the game introduces you very early to a larger storyline/plot that only you're privy to, and which is meant to guide your decisions throughout the events/encounters. I've rarely seen this in a game of this nature: you're not just mindlessly making decisions without an endgame in sight, but rather asking yourself how every decision you make contributes to your end goal.Unlike Suzerain, you also have more control over your own Cabinet and how you use your staff, and you can even collect certain items that can be useful later on. This hybrid of RPG elements with choice-based text-heavy events feels absolutely unique and adds so much unexpected depth to the game.But perhaps the most impressive aspect is the writing: it may not matter to some, but it's written in such flawless, perfect English that is rare to find in a lot of games today, and the story and characters are fleshed out without being complex. It's a genuinely immersive experience that doesn't force you to read thousands of words of background.Have I said it contains a WHOLE FREAKIN' MUSICAL?!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep playing the game, and I recommend it for a bunch of reasons. The concept is great, there should be more political games which put you in the decision role. The length of the game is impressive, and there are enough things going on that it'll make it good to replay. Now for the criticisms...I think it is telling that it's called 'THIS IS the President'. I know its a reference to the 'This is the Police' series, but I do also find it telling, because the game never reaches a point where it feels like 'YOU ARE the President'. The game lacks atmosphere, an issue which is compounded by playing as someone who purposefully has no backstory, name, or wider details about their character. Sure, I get it, they're a blank canvas that we can interpret however we want, but it leaves the game fundamentally lacking in making it seem like you are the President. The game is also sometimes frustratingly gimmicky, which undermines the concept. It could perhaps do well to be less of a parody, and more like games like Suzerain. The political aspects of the game could also be improved - for example, a screen showing whatever Congress is doing at the time, and giving you bills to sign (which may be wild and wacky, if desired). The political side being enhanced would go some way to making the game seem more atmospheric and immersive. My two most fundamental criticisms are as follows: first, lack of character background makes the whole 'presidency' itself feel less realistic and less immersive. Second, lack of depth on the political side of the game also makes the game less immersive. I praise the game for the concept, and for the sheer length of time it seems to take to complete (I've only played a year in-game so far - 12 turns). Based on that, I would recommend the game, but it could have been a lot more compelling. 6/10?

_childDocuments_.review: I'll never forget March 2023 -- that was the month I decided to become the lead singer for my bluegrass country band, TITPOTUS. Having played supporting roles in musicals in the past (no, not the odd Broadway hit where the now suspiciously dead playwright killed a little girl in a hit and run accident with someone named "Mr. P"), we now sing our support for Amendment 28 while playing invisible instruments. Chic-Shok's gonna love it!Oh, Amendment 28? That's the amendment I'm proposing where a president can't go to prison for any crimes committed before their presidency. It'll really help the nation and is definitely a good idea, promise! That's why I had to pay 11 million dollars to get support from the House and Senate, unalive two Supreme Court Justices who didn't like my proposal, and... I guess run this country.Now I somehow gotta get my approval rating up to 90% so the people will vote for the amendment. Would adopting the hamster slowly dying in one of our space stations help? Hold that thought -- the VP is trying to propose to the woman we set him up with to keep him on a leash and he needs ideas. Can our IT guy hack all the online ads to ask for her hand in marriage? What's that, our IT guy died from overwork, and the other one was sent to a mental hospital? Okay well, send some muscle to break out the one and get that 9 year old Australian hacker on the job. So glad he only costs me $1,500 a month -- child labor, what a blessing!Now about that approval rating... how much will it cost to get that hamster back to Earth? THREE MILLION DOLLARS??? This better work...

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have ever thought being president could be so fun? After playing this game we now know why some presidents liked being president so much they tried to destroy democracy to keep their presidency going-okay, not really, but seriously this is a great game! The politics are at once deep enough and vague enough that your president could be from either party and while the characters are sometimes vaguely reminiscent of real politicians and the situations are also somewhat similiar to real life in 2021, they are also ethereal enough so that the politicians and situations are also unique to the game-which is probably for the best with the way politics are these days. There is a huge cast of characters and content, all championed by fairly simple control and game play with an interesting and often amusing, humorous story. While I do have a small wish list of things I wish the creators had done-let us customize our president more, give them choice of ethnicity and gender, maybe a chance to be non-corrupt?-but overall it is obvious that this team knew what they were doing. If your looking for a fun political game that is at once immersive and serious yet light I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is (almost) the perfect game of this archetype -- political simulations where you really do feel like you are making the choices as president. This game is very refined in its interface and storytelling. My only criticism is some of the storylines  take away from the realism of the game. Some level of exaggeration is expected for any video game, even those that are meant to be realistic, but some of it does basically go a bit too far and breaks the immersion sometimes.  But I'm sure this isn't supposed to be a completely realistic political simulator. Some of it clearly is supposed to be satirical or a hyperbolic commentary on the real world, as it has every right to be. Ultimately, if you are into this general idea of wanting to roleplay a political figure, this is the greatest game I've ever seen like that at least.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played most of the "This Is The" series of games. This Is The President successfully executes it's role of what the previous games that I had felt, had only tried to portray. A crooked and corrupt man in power who has to make decisions based off their situation, with the first two having you play as a police chief of a local town to now finally, being the big man in the Oval Office.If you're looking for a quick thrilling joyride that entails the idea of what the president does with some humor and cliches. Then look no further.  But if you're looking for something a little more in-depth and expansive, this may not fill that void.This Is The President definitely fulfills it's goal of it being a political thriller from a well put together musical about a key part of your past, to having to make non-stop decisions more for the benefit of your rating than the help of the people, all to succeed in ratifying the 28th Amendment. An amendment that grants you and any other future president full immunity for past crimes following their term in office.This story is told and accompanied by a lot and I mean A LOT of text. This game is very text heavy so be prepared to put on your reading glasses. However the game has a lot of satire to not make it that much of a chore. Eventually some plot changing events near the end of your term, which I enjoyed for the most part but can easily be disliked depending on your taste.Personally the story of This Is The President was a fun one to ride out. You could tell the writers enjoyed creating much of the scenarios both in and out of the story. Despite a few grammar and spelling hiccups that you'll run into, I enjoyed the humor and style of the game very much. Just again note that if you're not prepared to read, then this game will definitely not be your cup of tea.Along the roller coaster of emotions you'll have in order to ratify this amendment, This is a game at the end of the day, so what will you be doing while riding this crazy train of doing the impossible?The core of This Is The President's gameplay loop is predicated on making rapid fire decisions and passing bills. It can be easily tedious and even more stressful. You'll go through a president's full four year term with you having to make dozens of decisions within each month. Decisions will range from simple to obscene and you'll be tasked to find the right answer for the sake of your own gain.Make the right decision and you'll get a boost to your rating and maybe some cash on the side. Make the wrong decision and you might either get some cash or mostly a kick in the head to your ratings. But the gameplay doesn't stop there. Throughout your term you'll have to manage your staff, their stress levels, and lastly your budget. Throughout each month you'll have a list of tasks to complete on the left of your screen with on your right, a list of tasks you'll need a percentage of rating or a number of dollars to do.Your staff is needed to complete each of these tasks. Each task will require a specific type of staff member as people from states and around the world will ask for the likes of lawyers, diplomats, hackers, or some hired muscle. Read each task carefully for who you'll need and send them out on said task. If successful, you'll again get a ratings boost, money, or an item that you can use to your advantage. But after each task, your staff will begin to accumulate stress points. Max out their stress points at five in total and they'll at first, just ask for some much needed time off. But if you keep stressing them out, eventually they'll quit or decide to take matters in their own hands. Note also that if a staff member is fired, quits, or anything else, they cannot be brought back for the entirety of your save.All of this is further amplified by your constant need for money. Eventually your staff will individually want a raise and these raises can range from low and modest such as $16,000 - $26,000, to down right unfathomable as one employee I had  asked for $1,000,000 a month to suddenly $8,000,000, and even $16,000,000 a month! Thankfully I was near the end of the game so it wasn't too awful. Staff will also begin to grow grudges between one another that you'll need to settle, passports for traveling to other countries, and vacation trips in order to prevent max stress. All of this costs money, which you'll go through like water. My conclusion on the gameplay is that making rapid fire decisions with the addition of unpredictability can and be really fun. But eventually you yourself will get burnt out from this. Some months you'll go from 60% rating to a 80% then the very next month you'll go to 58% for not agreeing to put a ban on hoverboards. Add that with your budget, staff, and stress management and you'll truly comprehend how hard it is to be the president. All in all, fun for the two years of your term. To then agonizing in your final two years.This Is The President is an amusing experience that I enjoyed for the 20 hours it took for me to complete it. There is a good chunk of fun to be had here so long as you remember that it's more of an experience than it is a game. It's satire and unpredictable style of game flow makes it keep you on your toes, but can also burn you out mentally after thinking that you finally got a good grasp of the game's pace after reading an intimidating wall of text.

_childDocuments_.review:
This Is the President is a story driven management game. In the year 2020 you are elected to be the President of the United States of America. To escape justice for your past crimes as a shady multi-millionaire businessman, you need to ratify Amendment 28 which would grant lifetime immunity to any President.

Manage your official and unofficial staff like a real mafioso in order to deal with all the old problems you've had in the past, as well as the shiny new problems that come with the office. You'll battle with your competitors, the establishment, the media and even foreign leaders.

In this political thriller-satire mix, the player's actions will inescapably lead to situations that escalate into absurd, terrifying, tragic and even ridiculous situations.

name: The Invincible
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition REVIEWS About the Game You are a highly qualified, sharp-witted astrobiologist named Yasna. Being entangled in a space race, you and your crew end up on the unexplored planet Regis III. The scientific journey quickly turns into a search mission for lost crewmates. Follow its trail, but be fully aware that every decision you make can bring you closer to danger. On her journey, Yasna will face decisions that will shape the outcome of the story. Help her make difficult choices and witness one of 11 possible endings to the deeply philosophical story. Discover fragments of what’s lost and report to your Astrogator. Let his voice aid you during hard times when humanity’s greatest threat emerges. The latter will force you to rethink mankind’s ambitions and biases. Go on - make decisions, follow the mystery… but remember not to underestimate the brutal simplicity and brilliance of evolution. Robots, people… Choose whether to interact with different creatures on Regis III or how to do it. Friend, companion? Enemy? You never suspected what these words might really mean before you got here. Immerse yourself in the atompunk atmosphere by using various tools, such as a telemeter or a tracker, and drive a vehicle through a stunning landscape. Experience realistic interactions with analogue technologies in a retro futuristic timeline. The Invincible is a first-person game based on the motifs of The Invincible - an iconic novel of the world-known, hard science-fiction author and Polish futurologist Stanisław Lem. There are places like Regis III, not prepared for us and for which we are not prepared. Still, our spacecraft inevitably comes closer to the destination - for our stories and fates to cross in a dead spot.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the book The Invincible by Stanislaw Lem, when i was 8 or 9 years old (i am now 44), it was one of my first hardcore sci-fi books. I was totally overwhelmed then by the story and i used to draw scenes from the book.Now i finally had a chance to be on Regis III and i have to say - it was incredible. Yes, i know, lot of mistery was lost for me, since i knew, what is going on there, but the possibility to be in "prequel" of The Invincible was fantastic experience.The 60ies looks of technology and vehicles, the enviroment around, walking around and thinking - ah yes, this I know, correct depictions things from book.And the sight of Kondor - it was majestic.Graphics were awesome, music and atmosphere perfect. I am not the biggest fan of "walking sims", but this one is 10/10And yes, reminder to humanity - Not everything everywhere is for us.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't read the novel by S.Lem, but I can confirm that the game is essentially  in space. That's the closest comparison, because while you are looking for your crew lost in a mysterious planet, you will be constantly talking to your Commander via radio, with multiple timed dialogue options that affect the outcome. Depending on your choices and how much you decide to explore the planet, you can get different endings (from “really bad” to “really good”). There is also a recap in the form of comic book, which shows how the story has changed based on what you discovered, so every important action you make will add something to it. The story has a slow start, but gets very intriguing later on as you feel more attached to Yasna (the protagonist) and her Commander. The only thing I hate is the ending that I got, which was abruptly cut to the credits without any sort of explanation. I saw the other endings too and it’s like the developers didn’t want to give a proper ending to Yasna’s story (except for one case), but none of them feel really satisfying in terms of narrative and visuals. Too bad because I enjoyed every single moment until the last part. Other than this, the gameplay has very low interactivity, like using gadgets while walking, reading documents, interacting with few terminals, driving and of course replying to your radio. The visuals are awesome (especially if you like retro sci-fi atmospheres) and the game runs flawlessly at max setting, without bugs or glitches of any sort. In conclusion, I would recommend The Invincible if you enjoyed  and similar non-linear “walking sims”, definitely worth picking with a good discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for you as you are not likely to be a bigger fan of both sci-fi and S. Lem's work in general AND his book "The Invincible" in particular than me, still I found this video game to be excruciatingly boring, despite the efforts that went into this title! It seems they just picked the wrong format - should have not released as a video game but rather as a animation movie or series, since there is so much great graphic work and voice acting already in it! So if you are intrigued by the story save a few coins and a few hours and just go read the original book this is based on, you'll do yourself a favor.

_childDocuments_.review: Lack of a manual save option has taken the shine off this game for me.  I like to play for a relatively short time because I can get a bit dizzy.  I ended up wandering round and round in circles, desperate to stop and unable to trigger a save point.  I gave up eventually and, when I came back to the game, I didn't know which bits I'd already explored.  I have just stopped the game now, not because I was ready to stop but because, I've triggered a save point and I'm not going to risk carrying on tonight.  It's a shame because the game is fascinating and I have no prior knowledge of the storyline so it really is all discovery.  I'm also very impressed with the voice-acting.  If you don't mind the save-game issue, I would thoroughly recommend this game.  Unfortunately, I cannot give it a blue thumb's up because, although I continue to be interested enough to carry on playing,  if I'd realised how the saves work, I would not have bought the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So overall I really enjoyed this game. I have mixed feelings so i think it best to list the pros and cons:Pros:Beautiful visuals: I loved the retro futurism. It wasn't an attempt, it was proper execution. Their use of textures and colors really drove home the concept of 60/70 era scifi visuals. The robots, equipment, the old plastic, the small tv's with the exceptionally large black plastic frames. It scratched an itch I didnt know I had. By far, the best part of the game. Also the sense of scale was fantastic. There were moments where the planet felt HUGE. I have no idea what they did, but part of me thinks they just made everything to scale, and you could tell. If not, whatever they did worked.Exploration (part of visuals): Loved walking around and driving in the rover. It was a well curated experience driving around that planet, and they had an eye from the start of the project to the end. No spoilers: but the end was so fun to look at, might replay the last chapter just for that. I felt like I was constantly enjoying visual experiences that were new to me, chapter by chapter.Music / Ambience:I felt the music and the ambient noise set a great tone, and there was a good mix of both. The lofi/analog synth sound had its own style, so it did not feel like your typical 70s/80s lofi synth. It had character. Felt more like a movie soundtrack than just some lazy omage to "70s synth"Cons: Just one, but its a big one, and its everywhereControl Lock:Okay so I hate when games force me to look, slow down my walking speed, force me to do quick time events for small tasks, and this game had this absolutely everywhere. I'm not sure if this is a common pet peeve, but if its one of yours, this game is going to bother you. I will say though that its worth pushing though, but ill tell you, I paused the game a few times out of sheet frustration, and I even shut off my computer on one occassion. If th developers read this, please know that games like half-life work well because they allow the player to choose to look where ever they want, and if they miss out on a plot point, they will learn not to look away again. I feel like developers are worried people aren't going to pay attention. The problem is this caters to people that dont respect the art, and it punshies the people that do. This is hardly the only game that does this, so this is mainly a rant at the industry as a whole.Overall, this was great. I will definitely replay this game to enjoy the vibe and the visuals, great job guys!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 8 hours to beat the game. It's good. It's a walking sim, but the story is interesting, even if you read the source book. Regis III looks really nice, and the game runs smooth most of the time. I have rtx3700 and I did constant 120fps. But DLSS has no tuning options, so I don't know which preset was enabled. Ultrawide support is not there yet, but the devs are working on it. I hope they will make psychological horror out of "Solaris" next time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This has got to be one of my greatest experiences in a singleplayer story game! The controls, visuals, story and atmosphere all felt and looked amazing. It excited me to keep playing and find out about the situation. I do think some people may find the gameplay a little bland at times. However even though i haven't read the book the game was made after i understand it gives certain restrictions. That said, i truly enjoyed the experience and definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: To use a crude metric: this is much, much more of a _game_ than Firewatch. This game is gorgeous. Plain and simple, the aesthetics and environmental storytelling are very polished and on-point. They are without a doubt the best part of the game. Some of the mechanics are very clunky, and the actual gameplay doesn't do much to take the player in. It's slow to play, but not everything needs to be fast-paced and action-packed. This game is about exploration, not action. If you don't like to stop and enjoy the view every now and then, this will probably feel boring to you.To conclude; I loved it, and I do not regret paying the full retail price for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game started off well. The music, landscapes, and retro-future vibes were spot on. The building mystery was great and the cast of characters was well done. However at about the 60% mark the story began falling apart, a new character with sub-par voice acting was added, too many convenient time-skips, and the story made leaps of logic that weren't earned or justified. The endings were really letdowns and the whole experience feels like it was pointless. Art was generally well-done, minus the stiff/awkward character animations from the main character and other NPCs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Good atmosphere and visuals. It just captures the beauty and dangers of a Mars like planet. The story is really good and the choices you make do matter. There was occasional bugs with T poses, having 3 arms in a cut scene because I took auto the detector and no way to interact with a object that needs to be interacted with but nothing that a reload did not fix. All in all good game to pass the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lovely story driven game with a beautiful retro sci fi artstyle. There are a lot of the game can play out given your decisions. There are some minor annimation issues, some performance stutters and the movements system is a bit janky when navigating the environment, but I would consider them really minor flaws if all you want is to immerse yourself in a great sci fi story brought to life by some amazing art and a talented VO cast.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It was pretty good.  Real Science Fiction story from a well known author.  I think it was a good conversion into a game.  Very guided to keep you within the confines of the story but seems like an open world with limited exploration at times.  Don't expect a lot of excitement but it is an engaging story that you will want to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: As a person living in a post-communist country I really felt at home with this retro-futuristic style. If you read any book by Stanislaw Lem, or you are just a general sci-fi nerd than this game is a must-have. This game is also very relaxing and interesting to look at (although the graphics seem a bit aged at times). One of the most interesting parts of this game is that it made me scared of death, since you can't really die unless the main character really dies at the ending (as of now that is the only ending of the game that I uncovered and it was terrifiyng). But there are some negatives. Firstly the game is short. Like it took me just 8 hours to uncover the first ending. And secondly it crashed 2 times during my first playthrough and glitched out a bit. But other than that I would highly recommend this game.(I only read the very beggining of the Invincible but I read another book by Lem called Solaris and I colud just feel that this was how he imagined the looks his books)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games ever for sure. This has got to be one of the most gorgeous games I have ever played, the views of the planet, the colours, and the music are so well done. I'm a big scifi nerd, so this game ticked all the boxes for me. I really appreciated the thriller twist. No jump scares, just enough existential dread to make you really appreciate the atmosphere of the game. And oh man, did this game have an atmosphere. I can't wait to read the book and learn more about this planet and what happens next!Cons: If you want to 100% the game, you will do a lot of reloading your saves. Unfortunately, this game has checkpoints rather than typical saving, so you will do a lot of redoing conversations/ walking again. Fortunately, there are plenty of steam guides to help you out!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an amazing game (and well worth the sale price).The beginning hooked me in the ways that Edith Finch, Firewatch or the Talos Principle did, yet it subverts the expectations of these traditional one character in a dead world walking-sims.If you're looking for interactive gameplay, puzzles or anything more than a new way to experience a novel, then I can't recommend it, if however you love storytelling through games this is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I had been waiting for this game ever since it was announced. And I was not disappointed at all. The game has an amazing soundtrack, it has awesome visuals better described as beautiful. The game-play is interesting and the story is the best part of it. It starts a bit slow but I was hooked by the first hour. A very relaxing and fun break from all the fighting and competition. It's game for explorers and no one gets left behind. Play it. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: If you like story driven sci-fi games and don't mind walking through a seemingly barren but beautiful planet as the main gameplay element, this is for you.There are people that say, The Invincible is not like Firewatch or not as good, and despite I disagree with this Statement in a general way, I kind of agree that you should not compare those 2 games, because it might not match with the expectations you get from this comparison. However, for me, those two games are equally good. I did get exactly what I wished for, and I waited way too long for something like that! I hope it's the same for you!There are some smaller bugs and glitches, but nothing game breaking occurred to me.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: feels like a   in space. But it is much more than that. It is an amazing story to experience with great visuals and a comfortable playtime of about 6 hours. Some may find this short, but The Invincible never felt empty or boring.I played this on the SteamDeck and it was a great experience except for some fps drops. Like in Firewatch this is mostly a walking simulator. You play Yasna, a biologist, who is looking for her missing crew on the planet Regis III. While exploring this mysterious planet, you are in constant radio contact with your astragator Novik. The conversations between the two feel very natural and similar to Firewatch. And like in the other game, you are happy to have some company while being in a lonely and hostile environment.Loneliness, feeling lost and being in an unknown world left me playing with a feeling of discomfort (similar to the movie ). A discomfort which I quite enjoyed. Space is often pictured as a beautiful place of endless dreams. But The Invincible doesn't do this. On the contrary to Star Wars or Star Citizen, it has a much more realistic approach and shows the emptiness and loneliness someone on a far away planet would experience. This stuck with me and I have to thank the game for this. Exploring the mysterious things on Regis III and the constant fear of no way to return keeps Yasna, the player and the game going.One aspect the game never fails at is showing that the characters (mainly Yasna) are more than just created to be played, they are humans and they act like us. For example, by having doubts and not blindly following everything they are told, by having conversations and discussions about different topics or by making decisions. Specific example (spoiler!):  This just shows how this is not just a game about walking from point A to B but to be human.I will stop here now because this is one of those games where knowing less means more when playing the game. I really enjoyed this game and can recommend it to anyone who enjoys more "scientific" space stories, likes the atompunk look and is comfortable with a little bit of discomfort. Overall, a  for me. _childDocuments_.review: I bought into The Invincible on the narrative premise alone, but was pretty overwhelmed on the absolutely outstanding visuals, and consistently enticing world design which drove me into finishing the game in nearly a single nine hour sitting..The Invicible a *slow* game - so don't come into the Invincible if you're after action or even complex puzzles - this is as close to a lost-in-space-desert simulator as it is a space adventure.(Edit) 12 hours after finishing I'm.. still thinking about the game, in particular the choices I made narratively that I'd like to go back and try another way - at the time of writing my review I wasn't sure I'd wanted to wade back in, but at a relatively quick 6-8 hour game, it could be a great game to revisit in a few weeks.In the meantime - the soundtrack has been spilling out of my speakers the past hour, it alone made so much of the eerie atmosphere.. such incredible work all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a semi-interesting story to tell, I found several things that make this game more frustrating than entertaining:First is the time-limited dialog system where you have to read your options and make a choice at lightening speed. I guess the idea was to add some sort of suspense to the game. All it did for me was lead to frustration because I could not read my choices before having to chose, much less have a chance to think about them. This combined with the fact it would take which ever one you had highlighted, including "none", it often lead to a choice I didn't mean to take. It shows a real lack of understanding of Accessibility on the part of the developers.The second, again with the dialog system, is giving you dialog choices WHILE OTHER DIALOG WAS GOING ON. Choices made while other characters are speaking often are not even acknowledged, and in this breaks the flow of the story rather badly.A core mechanic of this game is interacting with things in the environment. Which you can NOT do until it gives you an icon for the intractable... which, very often, it utterly fails to do. You can search an area for the SINGLE action you can take, not find it even after looking at the obvious button or what have you, and move on... only to come back for a second pass to only then have it activate so you can use it. Given that this is the most basic interaction of the game it's rather stunning that it's so broken.And finally, there is the ending... or, I should say, the lack of one. At the point the game ends, that's it. You make a choice of some sort, and the game is over. No explaining, at all, what the results of your actions throughout the game were. Just left hanging with zero closure. Despite the frustration the game caused me with it's problems, I might have been tempted to go back to see what results you got from different choices....But, really, there are none.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game although "an experience" might be a better description as there is little about it that might be considered a game but that's totally fine because the devs have created a uniquely engaging experience.Being a fan of Chris Foss' art style (as you can see from my avatar) I instantly loved the style of The Invincible - it's very classy, retro-futuristic with a good dose of Cold War-era vibes.The barren landscapes are stunning - you really feel lost and alone out there, although you have a constant (if not disconnected) companion in the voice of Astrogator Novik. The slow pace, gently unfolding storyline, excellent voice-acting and a slight sense of constant uneasiness that the planet is out to get you, all combine to make, in my view, one of the most engaging and absorbing experiences I've ever played - I found the whole adventure remarkably gripping and realistic.The game looks and feels gorgeous and special mention must be mentioned of the soundtrack too - it adds a lot to the already highly charged sense of atmosphere and cinema.Certainly highly recommend if you like slow-paced, sci-fi cinematic experiences!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Has/Had potential but I got pissed off and uninstalled. Needs to be optimized, I can run Cyberpunk2077, Resident Evil 4, RDR2 on ultra settings all day long but i cant even run this game which literally is only a few color gradients and inanimate backgrounds on 1080p. Glitches are annoying everytime I turn the character. I also do not enjoy having to press on a joystick in order to run, there's no custom settings to move sprint off the joystick, but even if I moved the control to another button, running is a joke in the game, you can only sprint for less than 5 seconds before the protagonist gets exhausted. You cant jump which makes some of the mechanics that are only available during certain areas laughable and unrealistic which makes the fact your unable to sprint for long duration's even more frustrating. The world isn't open for exploration, its closed off and you start to dread moving forward after you get bored of looking for the right direction to move  because everything looks so similar and pulling out that stupid map to navigate is ridiculous. The chick encounters a droid that fly's around her why the #### didn't she send it to map for her and provide a real time map before she wrecked the thing?  Then there's a glitch during the part in the game where your heading back after searching for the guy who kidnapped you friends and he shoots off flares, tells you to find the high ground, then you drive the rover up where the "clue" points you to, then the rover stops working and stays stuck. You cant jump so you have to walk all the way around a giant area and I still haven't found my way to the top because of the negative experiences. Nothing realistic or cool sci-fi wise after 9 hours in, The Astrogator and main character are bots at times repeating the same things over and over like its on a timer. The game leaves nothing to make me want to continue, I wish I could get my money back.Updated March 30th 2024.....Finally decided to wrap this up so I finished the game, haven't changed my opinion about it. Garbage, the Devs clearly love Chinese people, enough said.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of the so-called "walking simulator" that want a compelling story with some stunning visuals, this is an excellent 8 hour diversion that will make you think. I wouldn't get your hopes up too much with the endings, as they all seem a little abrupt. But as with a good novel, the better endings leave you with just the slightest question of "so what exactly will happen now?"
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning views and believeable story. Stanislav Lem knows how to make a good story.I felt with the main character and even the enemies fate broke my heart.Worth it for 24€ in my opinion. Far more entertainment than a night at the movies.There are some heated parts, but this isn't an action title. The story is what this game is about.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving this game a positive review even though it really is not for me.  It does what it sets out to do.  The graphics are good.  I only ran into one glitch.  I did enjoy the retro-designs.  The story is fine.  However, all that being said, this is not a game.  It is a choose your own adventure book in video game form.  You are put on rails and cannot deviate.  There are not any puzzles.  Your communication decisions set your course.  If that is what you want and like, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I can't help but feel a bit disappointed after playing this game. Sure, the graphics are nice and the story is kind of intriguing, but there's just hardly any depth to the whole thing. Given the time to complete and the content I'd probably have been okay with spending $5-$10 on it, but having purchased this for $40, I'm not too happy with it. There was potential here, I just don't think it was properly explored. There was also a lot of walking and driving to your next destination, a lot of which is simply holding forward while Yasna climbs a ledge or squeezes through a tight gap, or just straight up running. In my opinion, this would have been better adapted into a movie than a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the game blind, and I recommend you do as well. While obstensibly a walking simulator, the environment, discovery, architecture and exploration are so unique and well created I was constantly engaged. There are several choices, some small and some large. I was pleased that these choices were often such that both courses of action are reasonable and it felt like the kind of challenging call a real adventure would require you to make.I also found the conversations to be very organic. Often with vocal protagonists, it's easy to become annoyed at their lack of awareness or critical thinking. But I often found myself agreeing with, or enjoying the spoken discovery of the main character as I explored along. The story itself, while largely derivative of the book it's based on, is fascinating and well thought out.Overall, if you want to feel like a scientist on a struggling and mysterious space exploration of a dangerous plant, I've never experienced any book or media this engaging on the subject. 10/10.TL/DR: The gameplay of Firewatch with the mystery of Outer Wilds with 1960's Soviet Bloc architecture.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This was awesome. is a great science fiction story and the game is flawless in both presentation (beautiful!), gameplay and technical aspects (I guess after a few patches, but still). It took me a bit over six hours to finish my playthrough and I already regret that I cannot experience it fresh a second time. There are some choices and some exploration (or rather: investigation) is rewarded in small branching paths in the story, just the right amount to make this feel interactive compared to a movie experience. I feel motivated to, at some point, revisit the game and get a slightly different ending, although I was overall happy with the one I achieved.Without knowing anything about the novel, I was thoroughly invested in the story from the very beginning. The science fiction has a distinct "cold war" feel to it, even if no Americans or Russians formally appear. Even the often impressive technology feels right out of the latter half of the 20s century (again, knowing nothing about the novel -- yet) and it feels perfect in many ways. The planet and the graphics in general are simply breathtakingly beautiful. The characters, their writing and their voice acting are superb and I have no complaints at all.In fact, I have literally no complaints to give at all, for me this is a 10/10 experience that in the end only increased my desire to experience more of this quality. It makes me wonder what other science fiction greatness I may have missed or could be salvaged from books and novels into great interactive experiences like this game. I hope there is more and I hope the developers find and convert them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great sci-fi adventure. Maybe it looks a little retro but it doesn't matter much. It has what many fans like myself expect: a great story, adventures on other planets, advanced tech etc. The graphics are impressive too. Unreal engine 5's Nanite shows impressive rocks :-). It is the first game where the player can find "free rocks" and rock formations. Yes, like in real life! Beautiful and highly detailed rocks and rock formations that don't hide any valuable loot. I also found it pleasing that there are no slums in the game. Sci-fi games and movies like slums, bandits and other low-life characters for some unknown reasons. Mass Effect is full of bandits, slavers, crime lords etc. This game has none of that. It is for those who prefer science, mystery, advanced equipment, other planets and so on.  Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Dirty Brown Trash Water of a game. The main reason for this is because the ending I got to was bugged and never completed. You are suppose to stare out a window and see The Invincible ship land to save the day then roll credits. NOPE. It never triggered and the character just stares out the window indefinitely. Had to look it up online to see what happened, total buzz kill of an immersive novel. So you restart the check point to hope and fix it. NOPE STILL THE SAME ♥♥♥♥. Imagine reading a mildly intriguing story, only to get to the end and find the last chapter missing. That's what this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of an adventure game is. Don't play this, Don't read the book its based on. So tired of incomplete releases of games coming out. Finish your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ work before you release jesus h christ...Now all that said...I still wouldn't recommend it. Linear walking sim, ok scenes, good voice actor for the main lady but nothing captivating or enthralling about the story. If you want a good sci fi story go play Soma, or Deliver us the Moon/Mars, or Observation. Or go read the Hyperion series.  This one misses the mark hard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a choose-your-own-adventure walking simulator. It took me about 10 hours to complete it. The story is good, and the graphics are excellent. There is some replayability in that other choices could be made, but I was pretty happy with most of my choices. I do wish there was some sort of rewind ability so that I could have tried a couple of paths, but I am satisfied with the experience that I got.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game for probably over half a year. This game has a bunch of extremely good aspects of it, but fell short in a few areas. I spent around 8 hours to beat my first play-through, and given the quality of the experience, and the clear value of a second play-through, its worth the $30. This game is 100% for the story. Its like an interactive book or movie. Noteworthy good parts of the game:1. Absolutely stunning graphics and environments. Seriously, this game gets it SO good. I played this at 4K. The textures, the lighting, the environment detail and variety was truly exceptional. There was not a single point in my 8 hour game where I felt anything at all was a lazy copy paste. There is a large variety in the visuals of the places you go. reflections from light and materials are top-notch. I have not stopped to simply take in the constant impressive environments so much in a game in years. 2. Fantastic environmental storytelling (with the exception of the last 10 minutes of the game, explained in detail with no spoilers later in review). The game really peaks your curiosity and encourages exploration to figure out and come to your own conclusion on what is going on. This game constantly had me thinking. 3. Meaningful decisions throughout the story. There were many choices I made that had significant outcomes, that really had me thinking "What if I did (option B) instead?". I spent 8 hours on my first play-through and there are enough decisions where I want to go back to explore these alternative options and see the results.4. Great performance. Played at 4K, ultra graphics (max), FSR off. 5800x3d CPU and 6900XT GPU. I know, these are good specs, but even at ultra and 4K, and no help from FSR, I saw a pretty rock solid 80-100FPS throughout the entire game. And as mentioned by point one, the visuals are simply gorgeous. 5. Hand in hand with the awesome graphics, the art style of this game is excellent. Very well done. 6. Very polished and essentially bug free. I had one time in the 8 hour play-through where I kinda got stuck on some rocks for 3-4 seconds and couldn't move. Wiggled around, proceeded normally. There were a handful of instances of textures not displaying properly on some small rocks. Some noteworthy bad parts of the game:1. The first 30-60 minutes of the game start slow, and without anything major hooking the player in. By the 2nd to 3rd hour though, I was hooked until the end as many details emerge. This will turn off many players and I already see negative reviews with very short playtime saying the game is a boring walking simulator. 2. My biggest gripe with this game is the final 10 minutes. The game was so good at letting you figure things out by the environmental storytelling, only to essentially give an intense 5 minute spoon-feeding session of information at the very end to ensure players understood what was going on. This essentially throws all the hard work masterfully explaining elements of the story of the game via the environment into the trash just to make sure some players didn't finish the game confused. I really wish they did not so aggressively explain everything at the end. 3. To build on the last point, the endings felt rushed, and some of them honestly were laughably bad. There were several endings that cut to credits where they really left me shouting "Really? Thats it? Thats where it ends?". They really missed the opportunity to have some truly bad ass and fitting endings/cutscenes. And they really set themselves up very well for them, only to not deliver. These are really only the last 10-15 minutes of the game, and the lead-up was epic, but they seriously dropped the ball by neglecting to have like 30-60 seconds of detailed closure for certain endings. To avoid spoilers, I will not elaborate. The writing was so spot on, only to fall apart in the final minutes of the game. It is really a shame the last 0.5% of the game does not match the quality of the rest of the game. I haven't written a review this long for a game in a long time, and that goes to show how much I enjoyed completing this game. It really is a shame the ending is the way it is. Regardless of these issues, I truly enjoyed the experience and do not regret the purchase, especially at $30. If you like sci-fi and space, this is a must-buy. A note after reviewing this, the developers have been releasing pretty frequent quick patches to fix game breaking bugs, improve saving system. They've also acknowledged the lack of ultrawide support and are working on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The best story-rich game I've played in a while. A space mystery that leaves you wanting to explore and learn more about the world you find yourself stuck in. The choose-your-own-adventure aspect makes me want to play it multiple times to see the consequences of certain actions and choices.Funny to say too, this game makes me want to read the book it is based on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up reading LEM books, I really enjoyed this game. It captures mood and thoughts of those books, while also creating a very pleasant gaming experience. Great visuals and you never feels alone since there is constant dialog with your in-game commander. Took me 8 hours including multiple endings. _childDocuments_.review: Wow. If Baldur's Gate 3 was definitely a great game ( I was playing it just before I started the Invincible), I now really want to call the Invincible a masterpiece! (even when compared to BG3)The atmosphere, the story, the characters - all are fantastic! Such immersive and captivating storytelling, choices that really have consequences, and amazing sound design!!! (which is sooo important both in games and movies/anime, but is so often overlooked in favour of some fancy visuals, making the worlds feel empty and dead)Thank you so much to the devs for this very rare experience nowadays - when you launch a game, and it truly feels like a work of art!!!The only thing that could have been done better are the endings. I just completed one play-through, and although the story remained logical and captivating, the ending I got (when the ship lands and you walk back to the pod to check on your friend) felt like being cut off in the middle of the last chapter of a book! And besides that last half-chapter, there is also an epilogue missing) so, kind of a let-down.It really feels like there should have been at least a couple more scenes of gameplay (e.g. what happened to Rohydra? What did the landed ship crew do after they landed?) and a cutscene with a short "epilogue" tying up the loose ends, e.g. "this and that happened, this and that was done by the Alliance/Commonwealth, Yasna left home/died/lived a long life died in peace/got a medal" or whatever.Without that, the ending felt like the credits starting was a glitch :( And then, I really thought there would be something after the credits, but no. Kind of disappointing, but remedied by the fact that I now have another 7-10 endings to explore :)Great game, would really reccomend to those, who know, enjoy and love this kind of genre. Yeah, it's not one of those alien-monster-running-shooting-looting bollocks, don't play this game if you're expecting something of that sort :Pp.s. and yes, I do also like the running-around-shooting-looting games, however this game was a really nice and welcome break from all of those. Such freedom, when you don't have to scour every single millimetre of a location until there isn't any more stupid stuff to pick up (*insert feels good meme here* XD ), just carry on and enjoy the view🔥

_childDocuments_.review: A great way to experience a story with less input than a typical rpg but more involvement than a book/ manga or a VN. Even tho all you do here are walk (u cant even jump lol), left click to perform actions, and select dialogue options, this game is still able to create suspension w/ its story telling and bgm.Story-wise there's nothing to complain since im more of the kind that prefers to turn off their brain and get carried away than being critical all the time. BUTT for the gameplay, there're some small issues here and there. The climbing/vaulting can feel clumsy at times, there're sometimes invisible walls here and there, ur car may suddenly stop moving cuz ur supposed to walk from here but the game doesn't explicitly tell u, the head movement from vaulting gives even someone that can play in VR for hours like me some motion sickness. But overall its an enjoyable experience and worth getting, but its up to u whether to get it now or wait for discount.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 - A true hard science fiction masterpiece waiting to suck you into its mysterious and encapsulating take on alien life. Will absolutely be purchasing the novel (spoiler warning) The Story:     A make your choice story game wherein you take the role of Yasna, an astrobiologist on a military mission to a long dead, desolate planet. After losing contacts with your fellow scientists and the discovery of long dead life, this leaves you with one of many choices. Adventure to find all you can in the name of science, potentially ending your life in the process? Or run, saving yourself and your crew as fast as possible. One of the few games where individual choices seem to really have a genuine impact on the game. The Gameplay:    Some are calling this a walking simulator. This is almost an insultingly simple way to label this game. The Invincible takes the job of a movie, to immerse you in its story with full visuals, sounds, and effects, and turns it into a full, personal, variable experience that ranges from person to person. Admire the scenery and take it all in, creating the most impressive and beautiful photo album to ever grace Regis III. Or don't. You can take the game at whatever pace you desire, which is exceptionally refreshing. The Scenery    Hands down one of the most visually appealing games I have ever played. Absolutely stunning horizons combined with an amazing use of colors. What could have easily been an easy/quick to design vast, ugly and dry desert was made into an expansive world with regions separating each series of anomalitic occurrences, tunnels that dig deep underground, mountains/spires that stand tall against the sky, deep bodies of mineral rich murky green water, vast oceans where the only known remaining life resides. A new world for you, the player, to observe and take in.Bugs    I encountered three bugs during the entirety of my first play through on 11/16-11/17 2023. I have heard of others encountering game breaking bugs but only one of the issues I experienced actually made an impact on how I experienced the story. The first bug I encountered made the dialog stop advancing. A simple save reload from a minute prior fixed that. The second was when my rover got suck on a piece of terrain. I was able to wiggle free after a couple minutes, and easily avoided this problem from then on out. The third and final bug I encountered was quite major, (spoiler warning)  In total, the bugs I came across only cost me a total 20-25 minutes of having to reload and replay saves. Not really that big of a deal especially when compared to some major AAA releases that are entirely unplayable. The Takeaway:    The Invincible has many themes. Faced with mortality and bitter hopelessness, how will you react? Will you face the treacherous, dry landscape to save yourself? Or will you do it to save others? Maybe just in the name of curiosity. Whatever you do on your play through of the game, you will be asking yourself one question repeatedly. "I CAN do this sure, but SHOULD I?" And the game knows this. In Conclusion:     The Invincible is an incredibly immersive hard science fiction masterpiece that pioneered the ideas of micro-technology, smart dust, and "necroevolution". The creativity in this story especially shines through it's innovativeness and unique technological designs paired with biological references that are used throughout the story. I would wait maybe a week or two after this review has been posted before purchasing it if bugs ruin your game immersion like they typically do me, however I found myself easily able to be reimmersed in the story. I would recommend this game to everyone with an interest in science fiction, atom punk, philosophically charged questions and eye pleasing scenery that will have you opening photo mode time and time again.

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly, this game is worth it just to view the exquisitely crafted planet with extraordinary attention to detail, and imaginitive geography.  Double points to giving you a FOV that includes the interior of your helmet - I really did lose myself and feel like I was viewing the canyons, dunes, and red sun of the alien world.The background and "history" of the planet was really interesting, though the current events transpiring during the mission weren't exactly a new concept - but this could very well be a product of the fact that the novel is such a staple of science fiction literature.  After decades of people ripping off the source material, any attempt to retell the original story seems cliche itself.  Still, I did enjoy discovering the lore of the planet as I traversed the landscape, and it definitely is a novel way to experiance a...well...novel.Gameplay is well done and ran smoothly except for getting trapped between the rover and an invisible barrier once, causing a reload that lost me about 20 minutes of gameplay.  Other than that, no complaints here.  Again, I lost myself in this, and really did feel like I was exploring an unknown planet for the first time, and the pace allowed my mind to wander and contemplate.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is a different type of game, not appealing to all gamer audiences. In my opinion, anyone that likes to read sci-fi books, will also like this game. It is basically a sci-fi adventure with an amazing story. The motivation for this game came actually from a book itself known as The Invincible, which was written in 1964, and the visuals and retro-designs within the game, depict how back then people imagined futuristic robots and rockets etc., would look like. Needless to say, the result is beautiful. Which Sci-Fi fan doesn't like retro rocket designs from the 1950-1960s!The game is about 8-9 hours long if you take your time to explore the surroundings a bit, but it is a somewhat linear game but the immersion is great. I got the game at a sale, so I think anywhere between 20-30$ is worth it, but only if you are really into Sci-Fi adventure books. Otherwise wait for a further drop in price.There are complaints by players that this game can cause nausea, motion sickness and dizziness, I for once experienced this only in Borderlands 3 (had to stop play it), here I did not experience it, but there are some fast movements like when you fall or get up (scripted-scenes), then I believe that's when people would feel it the most. I hope I could shed some light into this unique game, it intrigued me into reading the actual book, and as a true Heinlein fan (Starship Troopers author), I am looking forward.

_childDocuments_.review: i don't know the source material but i really enjoyed piecing together the story and exploring regis 3. the story is a bit of a slow burn though, and in some dialogues there is a lot of periods of silence (id say its realistic but might be too slow for some.) regardless, i thought the characters well written and voice acted. ive seen some people say the endings are all anticlimactic and the characters dont go through satisfying arcs. i cant say i fully disagree, but i guess it just depends on your motivation for playing the game. for me i wanted to solve the mystery, which i did to an extent. if you want to learn more about the characters, there isnt too much of that. i finished it in two sessions and dont regret it. if you like sci-fi/mystery i would recommend trying out this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a short. story driven game, based on the novel with the same name written by Stanisław Lem.The game is built on UE5 and looks stunning, the general aesthetics of the world building are of the mid century hyper-modernism.It is a linear game with a few easter eggs and multiple different endings based on the decisions you make through the playthrough.It's a fun experience and a captivating story that quickly grows on you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous but is very linear and doesn't give you any freedom in anything.Walking up to a cliff - only in this exact position, going back - sorry, you have to move forward, going further this path - sorry, you have to further explore the location you're in.Diary is useless, it doesn't give you any valuable information, but you forced to use it to complete the dialogues. Both detectors are useless too, you don't need them at all, since the environment is so linear, you just can't pass the point of interest. Additionally, there are too many scripted situations and cut-scenes. There's no danger you have to avoid, no challenges you have to face.There's no game mechanics that you have to use to complete the game, all 'toggle this' or 'use that' are just scripted animation sequences, you cannot mess up, there's no consequences for any of your decisions.I was expecting something similar to Long Dark but on an alien planet. Even Firewatch was much more fun, you could go anywhere and always find something interesting, the game allowed you to play it on your own way.I understand there is a certain type of people who would enjoy the game, but it's just not for the rest of us, if you don't mind me being a little arrogant.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's genuinely difficult to find games that aren't generic slop in terms of writing and art direction. This game achieves to do what video games as a form of media do best, and that is the ability to make you feel a story. You feel the drudgery and danger of traversing an alien planet, your actions are slow and clunky, your character is intelligent and well suited for such a serious scientific marvel that is Regis III, with very maturely written and hard science based dialogue. In short, despite the 50s future inspired aesthetic, everything feels functional and believable, the art direction is absolutely on point.This is an indie game however, so don't come in expecting high levels of smoothness and polish when it comes like things such as graphical technology or superb animations, as well as very minor bugs such as certain NPCs being in their default rigging poses. But all in all, zero crashes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Does the original book justice while keeping it interesting for anyone who might already know the story. And it's a fascinating story no doubt. The developers did a truly wonderful job of adapting it. The comic system was very interesting as well, and I enjoyed its inclusion. The graphics and the designs were beautiful as well.The game captured the wonder and terror I felt when reading The Invincible for the first time back when I was just a kid. I'm very glad Lem's story is reaching a wider audience with all the respect to the source material it deserves, and I loved the little references to his other works as well. Lem would have been proud.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, this is a "walking simulator", thought I prefer to see it more like an interactive novel. As such, if you set your expectations correctly, this game is a fantastic science fiction experience wherein you get to make decisions and shape the adventure the intrepid biologist Yasna goes on. The choices never seem forced or conspicuous either, but rather flow as natural branching points in any conversation or situation. In this way, this is in fact a better RPG than many other modern "RPGs", at least in terms of giving the player agency that is actually meaningful and natural. This makes the whole story wonderfully engaging and exciting, and you feel involved and invested in Yasna and her struggles all the way until the end. You want to keep the dialogue and discussions with your commander, Novik, going as you explore matters of philosophy, debating what is and isn't life, dealing with your fears, and getting encouragement when it's most needed.However, as much as I enjoyed the game itself, on a technical level it is almost catastrophic. Being an Unreal Engine game, the well-known traversal stutter is present, and with quite some force. On top of this, around the second and third quarters of the game, the whole game becomes a stuttering mess, sometimes locking up for entire seconds, framerate dropping from 100+ down to 30s and 40s, turning it almost unplayable. If you suffer through this, it does become better after you leave a certain base area, but doing so under those conditions can be challenging. Graphically, the game also doesn't nearly warrant such performance issues. It has excellent graphic and visual design, the "atompunk" style being beautifully realized here, but it's mostly the same, few assets strewn about in an orange desert landscape, and it boggles the mind how it couldn't be made to look even better and perform much smoother, than it does. There were also multiple places throughout the whole game where ground textures stopped blending naturally, and instead took the form of dark/light squares, seemingly fighting each other over who got to be on top.So, because I finished the game and do feel like I liked it overall, I'm recommending it... BUT, the technical performance is a huge asterisk and brings the score to a balance on a knife's edge, rather than overwhelming praise. There's no excuse why a game that doesn't look better than this can't perform more solidly. I played on a RTX 3080 10GB, Ryzen 3800X and 32GB RAM, and no other game I've played this year has had performance this shockingly bad, including Starfield, which graphically looks a lot better overall (although The Invincible is arguably the better version of that game's main story, and I wish Starfield had approached space exploration and the philosophy around it more like this game did).

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptional original book, brilliantly transformed into a game.The game adopts a nostalgic 1950s Sci-Fi genre, reminiscent of classic films like 'Forbidden Planet'. I was captivated by the book, a compelling short story. The original author, Lem, showcases a masterful storytelling style, skillfully balancing a brisk narrative pace with rich context about the mission, gradually unraveling the mystery of the land's desolation to organic life forms.The game pays a remarkable tribute to the story's central theme of Necro-evolution. The only notable alteration in the plot stems from the medium shift – a transition from book to game, akin to book-to-film adaptations. This change doesn't diminish the book's original premise; instead, it introduces an intriguing twist. The main characters, instead of being comrades from the same team on the ship 'Invincible', are depicted as members of two rival factions, adding depth and complexity to the narrative."This revised version smooths out the structure and enhances the descriptive elements, providing a clearer and more vivid picture of your thoughts on the book and the game.CuddleMonkey
