_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. Well, really I think it's more like an "interactive novel". So first - the Invincible is definitely an example of a "walking simulator", so don't expect lots of action. There's a lot of exploration (on foot and in a rover), talking, listening, and oodles of atmosphere (and it's very very pretty to look at too). The voice acting is pretty good as well (they seem to do the standard "Soviets are portrayed with a British accent" thing that the Enemy at the Gates movie did). The visual "1950s futuretech" style is amazing - all dials and clicky switches and rusty sheet metal everywhere, it's glorious :D.Second - this is a pretty specific kind of story, based on Stanislaw Lem's book "The Invincible". He also wrote Solaris as well (which was made into a Soviet film in 1972 and a US version was made in 2002). The style and language is very 'soviet' as well and I thought it was a fun touch that this came across in the phrasing even in the english translation. Lem's style can be summarised by one of his statements: "Not Everything Everywhere Is For Us". This isn't a story where you go and find the bad aliens and kick ass - it's very philosophical, very talky, and you're not necessarily going to "win" (not that it's entirely hopeless, there are "good endings" but they may not necessarily have the kind of resolution that you expect). If you know the genre and the author then you probably have a better idea what to expect. If you don't then it's still fun, but just don't have any prior expectations and be open-minded. Personally I found  it very satisfying to play and enjoyed it all the way through.There are a few (minor) quirks though. For one, the game doesn't allow you to go back after certain points (e.g. squeezing through passages in the rocks to get to the next section), which was unfortunate because I would have liked to have gone back to explore some other sections. Another thing is that there's no way to jump (my path was literally blocked by cables a few inches high in some places) and no flashlight to illuminate the dark places you often find yourself in (crank the gamma up all the way!). I think there were also few spots where some plot explanation was missed so I had to fill in the gaps a bit (I think I accidentally clicked a radio twice and missed an entire section of explanation that I would have heard on the first click) and no way to go back to hear it again. The options you have when talking to people have a timer on them which I'm not sure if I like or dislike - I guess in some situations you don't have all day to think of a response so that's good but the control method (hold space and use mousewheel to select a choice) was a little flaky and I almost didn't have time to make my choice a few times. Also there are a few situations where I thought there could have been more choices - at one point you meet a robot but having established that you can talk to them previously, this robot just does what it does and you there's no option to actually talk to it and tell it to come with you or do anything else. But these are pretty minor things. The story is really interesting and the mystery is pretty engaging. The landscape is spectacular and there's a good photo mode (be sure to change poses in the camera settings! The default one seems to be a little janky sometimes and hovers above the ground a lot). The characters are pretty neat too.Overall I think if you like walking sims and enjoy a darn good, thoughtful, philosophical scifi story with an interesting 1950s futuretech aesthetic then you'll like this one. That ticks all my boxes so I really enjoyed it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it's a walking simulator, but it's one of the most immersive ones I've played in a long time. The atmosphere pulls you in right from the start, and the graphics, though running on Unreal Engine 4, are stunning. The environment feels alive, eerie, and beautiful all at once.You play as a female scientist, embodying the perfect astronaut archetype—determined, curious, and always pushing through adversity with resilience and wit. Her journey is fascinating, and though I'm not finished with the story yet, I'm already hooked. It's clear the narrative, based on Stanisław Lem's The Invincible, has depth, and I'm excited to see where it takes me.The soundtrack is another highlight, perfectly complementing the sense of isolation and wonder. If you love sci-fi, exploration, and gripping atmosphere, this game is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with the game even before it was released ;) Glad that the final product didn't disappoint.Pros:- amazing artwork- visual novel vibes at times. Great for those who love to dive deep into the story- retro sci-fi vibe- great landscape of Regis III, sometimes I would just stare in awe- great voice actingCons:- no manual save- no jumping!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Superb game. On par with my favorite walking sim of all time, Firewatch, but in space.The only small complaint I have about it: there's about a dozen lines of "filler dialog" that are repeated way too frequently when you're aimlessly walking around and not going through the predefined path. Once I know all of them they were breaking the immersion (or should I complain about the game being too immersive?) for me, because the whole point of the world was about *not knowing what's coming next*. I'd prefer silence, or them being way more spaced out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: well, I do not like games where I am such limited in choices and paths. The story is very predictable and nothing special After 6h more and more painful to continue this nonsense. Sure a good idea, dialogs and the actors behind characters impressive, yet still the director messed up with making a captivating story out of such a good material. Graphics are awesome, the world in game too. But you can get it in many other games too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: If you love great stories, navigate your way through this one. I experienced this game more as a movie with something to do in between, rather than a full gaming experience. But the world they created, the story, the philosophy and science involved, made it a good experience. Definitely worth 5-6 hours of your time and a buck or so.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game/interactive novel - the story is good, the voice acting is well done, the music sets the mood, and they nailed the aesthetic. The comic book that is 'written' as you make choices and progress the story was also a really cool addition.My only criticism is that the movement system is mildly infuriating because you cannot jump, and can only climb/up down terrain in very specific spots).
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Story line is too shallow vs original Lem's novel. Scale is not even close enough to recognise Lem's masterpiece as a base here. Voice acting is terrible. Yasna in eng version sounds like elevator floor announcements, no life in acting in-general. Seems all conversation are AI generated. Overall game looks and sounds like another Unreal 5 engine show-off.   And not very impressive show-off both in graphical and gameplay aspects
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I did my best to like this game, but eventually I have failed.I may be not the biggest fan of hard sci-fi, but it always makes me curious. I would say, the game would've given me the satisfaction, if only I didn't knew what the original book is all about. Without the intrigue characters feel rather slow in understanding what is happening there ("slow" is a word I would use extensively while talking about this game, by the way).Story aside (I guess the downfall there is my own fault, how dare I know the synopsis of books I have never read?), what could you expect of low-budget passion "walking simulator" projects? Coherent direction, polish and attention to details, I would say. And while Th Invincible is trying, it generally lacks all three of these.Dialogues are often interrupted by further triggers you may even not expect. Sometimes you look around without a slightest idea what are you expected to do next and you should just stumble around until you find the next trigger. And sometimes you can see crossroads that hint on different paths to the goal, and most of the time the whole difference is that one of them is like three times longer than the other, without any further details and dialogues. That was really confusing.Bugs felt numerous. Instruments were becoming inaccessible from time to time, triggers fail to trigger, action points were not becoming active until i approached them three times from different angles... And twice during my walkthrough Yasna forgot to open her eyes after blinking, which was hilarious to be honest. And yeah, there are no manual saves and checkpoints are often 10-15 minutes of dialogues and walking apart. Not fun.And for the last part, attention to detail, all these things are not really game-breaking, they were just little dissapointments I have encountered while looking for better things. Like, metal detector is required twice throughout the game and is basically useless otherwise - but the output it gives is very inconsistent when you try to use it somewhere else, with half of clearly metal things being treated as "background". Tracker dots ignore a lot of people and sometimes their "pings" are way off. Some minor optional discussions ignore details that were already discovered. And well, Yasna's lines and their tone are generally all over the place.I was really hyped when I saw trailers. I was prepared to encounter everything the genre of "low budget walking simulator" should entail. The Invincible still haven't delivered. I'm not really dissapointed, I'm just... Sad.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Meh,The Gameplay is extremely linear, so much that you can't even jump. you can't fall from a cliff, you just walk and observe, basically. But you don't get beautiful graphics neither, it's inconsistent. People faces look worse that fallout4 and water looks like half-life 1. Probe flies through rocks...What a stupid idea to give you a zooming-telescope tool and not allow you to observe the planets through it! you just can't focus it and it's made on purpose. Can't recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I did not regret paying $30 for a 8 hour video game on-rail story, and here's why: If you're a fan of science fiction, I think this game is a must have in your library, as the visuals and the origin is rooted into the sci-fi of the bygone era. This game will have you see the Sci-Fi world the way our fathers / grandfathers saw it by reading novels from Stanislaw Lem*, Robert Sheckley and many more.* The story itself is inspired by the novel of Stanisław Lem with the same name "The Invincible" published in 1964 (1973 English), but for the sake of spoilers, I won't delve any further. Lastly, I note of praise to the Dev team of Starward Industries. As someone who saw a bit of that era, everything from the visuals, dialogues, and characters are on point, and honestly, it made me feel that people were kind of nicer back in the day than they are now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: As a disclaimer, I cant in good conscious recommend the game at its full current price tag of $30 USD but at $15 or below I think is reasonable. Not because it doesn't feel like the work the developers put isn't worth the price tag or even more, but because of how the game falls flat.The game is stunningly gorgeous at times, and the Atomp Punk aesthetics of the games are brain tickling cool. I really liked the narrative, the ideas it presented as well as the dialogue that the voice actors put to life 99% of the time, it kept me on my feet by being really interesting and I happily sat there 5 to 10 minutes at a time listening to dialogue before I kept going.However Im mixed on the gameplay because on one hand it is a narrative driven game with not much going on other than pushing the story forward. Sometimes you get rewarded with interesting dialogue if you explore but most of the time you just waste time and have to backtrack. I still enjoyed it enough to give it a positive review thoughif the game was more polished both gameplay and jank wise, and the game was less linear and had more going for it to encourage exploration it would be fine, But instead its a strictly linear game with the illusion of choice where as the only choices that matter are in the last 5 to 10 minutes of the game making the façade of it not being a walking simulator moot. Though I cant really decide if dumbing down the player input on the journey would make the game better or not because really what they tried to do might have been one of the better directions to go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good game.  Beautiful graphics, well-thought-out and very immersive plot.  this constant radio contact is great.  I've been looking for a game with the same atmosphere for an hour.  The game is linear, has some branches in the plot, but it's a game in the style of, I'm watching a good movie.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Yes the game is very nice, but i did expect a bit more to be honest.The visuals, feeling and gameplay are amazing! You really feel like on a hostile planet just on your own. And that feeling is the best! You really feel like in the novel by S. LemBut... as much as i loved the gameplay, it was just a bit to short. 10h was more than enough to explore everything. I hoped there will be more ways to end the game so that there will be a replay value, but simply said it is mostly a one way path just with a few endings. But all in all i did enjoy the game and the style a lot and hope to see more in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a big fan of Stanislaw Lem. I’ve read all his books, even the early ones that weren’t so great. But that didn’t stop me from enjoying the fantastic atmosphere of this game. The story is solid, and there’s even a reference to Lem’s best novel (in my opinion), The Eden! I hope there will be a game in the same style based on The Eden. The graphics are great, and the ambient music adds to the atmosphere. I recommend it to all sci-fi fans. And a shout-out for the Ukrainian localisation—it’s not too bad!👍
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game, but you have to go in eyes open with regard to the genre before you purchase.  It is a walking simulator, slow pace, sit back in your chair with a pad kinda game, underpinned by an interesting narrative that develops quite nicely.  Its does feel similar to Firewatch (but doesn't quite compare in terms of overall game) and it reminds me of Deliver us the Moon/Deliver us Mars but both of those games are better and contain much more gaming, especially when considering the latter.  Visually, its incredibly pretty and the 60s style classic Lost in Space artwork is a nice change.  There are multiple endings and I complete 4 or 5, but I hear there are 11 endings in all.  However, I'm not sure they were all necessary, some of them fall flat but there was a particular one that I enjoyed.  Definitely worth picking up if you have the right expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Astonishingly beautiful, and captivating up untill final credits. Good interpretation of the story behind "Invincible" by Lem, with lots do discover and many enough reasons to offer one more go at it.Be prepared to click f12, as you will find a lot views to put up as a wallpaper. Its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review - as I was salty it didn't support Ultra Wide when I originally bought the game...I now have a 4k monitor and OH MY GOD this game is amazing. I go this as part of the Steam Sale, thinking I'd give it another go - and the story hits hard, the graphics are brilliant and the voice acting is on point.EDIT: It says product refunded - however I rebought the game, so that shouldn't show
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A playable sci-fi film with a lot of depth in the style of how space travel was imagined in the 1960s. You really feel like a scientist exploring an unknown planet. The desire to know what would happen next was kept at the same level and kept me entertained until the end.Clear recommendation for Si-Fi fans from my side.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game in the genre, but the price makes no sense.  It would make sense at maybe 1/3 of that price tag. So I'm giving it a thumbs down, not because it's a bad experience, but because it's really highway robbery. But if you can get it a -66% rebate, then this is probably a thumbs up. I got it on special and in hindsight, I still overpaid.As for the game itself, it's sort of an interactive movie on rails. Very narrative. There are some choices, but they are opaque, you don't understand the consequences or often that you are even really making them. So if you are OK with a 6-7 hours sci-fi movie which involves lots of talking and walking, then this might be for you. The game is pretty, does the decent job at keeping things moving, and the voice-overs are good and well acted. The plot is decent, if a bit predictable nowadays. Replayability is pretty much null in my book. Once you've seen the story, getting a small detail better, or a different final cutscene doesn't justify going through all that walking again. Unlike some slightly more replayable narrative game, the second to second gameplay here is very very very plain and monotonous. It's ok once, a bit quiet and contemplative, but no way I'm going through that again for some achievements.So that's it. It might work for you, but caveat emptor.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgious looking game with a interesting story and good technical implementation. One of the few games released the past few years which look amazing and are not a technical dumpster fire. Runs really well and even has DLSS/FSR implemented, if you cant run it natively.The story is interesting, but nothing that will straight up blow you away and therefore only good for one playthrough in my opinion.That means around 6 to 8 hours of gameplay, which is fine for the price in my book.Sadly the further the game progresses the bigger the (luckily graphically only) bugs get, but no show stoppers either. Only small annoyances.It give it between a 8 and 9 out of 10."The Invincible" is a "Firewatch" with more exploration in a Sci-Fi Setting and a bit more gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a beautiful science fiction walking simulator with stunning visuals and very interesting story. I'm an absolute sucker for games like Firewatch or Suicide of Rachel Foster, so seeing this game when it was announced was a no brainer that I have to play it. And as much as I really want to praise this game for all the effort that went into it and very good optimisation (which is hard to come by these days apparently) I have encountered numerous game breaking glitches that either required a restart from checkpoint (which often means you lose 20-30 minutes of progress because you can't skip dialogues and cutscenes you've already seen) or even waiting for a whole patch to fix the problem. Which meant I kinda had to play the game with interruptions and that led to completely ruining any immersion or attachment to any of the characters in the game. Maybe that's just me, maybe you will have more luck. But because of all the problems I can't give this game more than 6/10. It's not bad, it's not amazing. Take it as you will.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Firewatch if your choices and investigation actually mattered.  Gameplay has a lot of cool toys and gimmicks to mess around with, but ultimately it's the great dialog and fantastically interesting sci-fi story to really wrap around.  It's like a 7ish-hour episode of a good Star Trek: TNG episode where the crew is trying to figure out what happened on some desolate planet, but with a Polish twist.Highly recommend to anyone who wants a good story with some great endings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly got this game for the beautiful cover art. Before that, I decided to buy and read the original novel by S. Lem. I also bought the displate with the cover art on it (as I really liked the motif). Both were well worth the money.The game itself has an interesting story that takes place before the one in the book. There are some plot holes but it mostly remains faithful to the novel. The design of the planet and technology is beautiful and has a 50s-60s vibe to it.Regarding stability, I unfortunately had to re-load multiple levels, especially the early ones, several times because the game would freeze for several seconds and not recognize me pressing the keys on my keyboard afterwards. I do recommend the game, but it would be really nice if the devs could update it a couple more times to reduce the freezes and the following inability to do the necessary interactions to continue the game without re-loading from the last save.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. If you read the book story won't be much of a surprise.There are two things I hate about this game:- Walking speed in open areas is way too slow - 120% run speed should be a walking speed, and running should not exist.- Visibility in the buggy is abysmal - I would prefer for game to drive me without my input and pause when i'm presented with story decision.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. I'm not big on retrofuturism, but this one is beautiful enough and satisfying enough in its interactions to make me enjoy it. The scenario is good, not ground-breaking, but good, and the voice acting is pleasant. Also, it was longer than expecteded. Some people would say too long, but I was just happy to keep on playing. I'd say the main problem is that exploration is very controlled, so you'll frequently run into invisible walls and will spend a lot of time trying to figure out which rock you're supposed to climb to move on. Can be a bit frustrating at times, but all in all, doesn't really impact the quality of this title. If you're into slow-paced old sci-fi and mysterious dead planets, give it a go without hesitation!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very nice walking simulator, with great atmosphere, artstyle, voice acting and a really nice story. There were a lot of times when I experienced stuttering, mostly at the camps but nothing too unbereable since the nature of the game doesn't really make you feel easily frustrated when there are small hicups in performance. All in all a really positive experience and I`m looking forward to more games inspired by literature, especially in the sci-fi genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a great Stanislav Lem's book reconstruction. The plot of the game is perfectly take a place between 'Condor' and 'Invincible' cruisers events. Attractive atmosphere and Yasna character, who take 6-7 hours of my attention.On the first glance the game has linear plot, but eventually I found at least 5 different finals. Maybe one of the negative side is the free saving is impossible. This approach diminished the intention to pass the game again, just for finding fork in the plot. My overall mark is pretty positive. Thanks to developers of the game for the great product..
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: "The Invincible" on Steam is a captivating journey that seamlessly blends gripping storytelling with stunning visuals. From the moment I embarked on this sci-fi adventure, I was enveloped in an atmosphere of suspense and intrigue. The game's narrative is a masterclass in pacing, keeping players on the edge of their seats with its well-crafted plot twists and character development.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is awesome and the world is beautiful, but it's essentially on rails and you're under no threat at any moment so even when it was trying to be mysterious or threatening I didn't feel concerned at all. The story feels very slow. I think they should implement a manual save system because I'd like to see the other endings, but I don't have the patience to sit through it all again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy story driven game. Gameplay feels almost on-rails, not a necessarily a bad thing considering what they set out to achieve with this game, and that is to tell a story with amazing visuals and music.You'll encounter multiple endings, most branch off during the final  mission, where some require you to have made specific choices during the main story.  This, along with the visuals and environmental storytelling, is the strongest aspect of the game. Gameplay and exploration is almost non-existent, you will follow a story that presents you with choices, experience some really cool scenery and moments; and get to enjoy a beautiful soundtrack along the way.For those who enjoy short, story driven games I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It had a very interesting story line.  However...  I disliked the fact there were times you might want to take a different path or choice and the  app just would not let you proceed, only to allow you to go that path after you met some specific part of the story line. The cost of the program made it worth the positive rating.  It was one of the shortest games I ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Beautiful scenery. Brilliant and captivating story. I love how it uses technical terms and doesn't treat the player like an idiot, just like a good sci-fi novel, which this game is based on. Good voice acting. The pace is slow in a good way, giving plenty of time for the player to soak in everything around them. There are lots of tiny little details that add to the world-building. Game design encourages exploration and fosters a sense of curiosity in the player. If you're into relaxing walking simulators with rich stories and lore, this is the game for you.Cons:The cons are mainly technical. There are several obvious texture bugs and occasional stutters when loading a new part of the world. The game encourages exploration but uses invisible walls to fence off places that look walkable, instead of using terrain features or other means to block the player. However, this isn't a frequent occurrence.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very good narrative game in the tier of Firewatch, Edith Finch, Gone Home, Fort Solis, The Suicide of Rachel Foster, Under The Waves and so on.I encountered just one bug that made my progression stuck. However I contacted the developers through the link in the discussion page and the day after they solved the problem! They are still working to the last patch, so maybe you would like to wait before to buy.However don't miss The Invincible if you like this kind of games. The visual style is absolutely outstanding, replying the retrofuturistic sovietic sci-fi aesthetics of the '50s, the so called atomicpunk style, oscillating between cartoons/comics and realism. The colors palette is so warm and satisfying, a balm for the eyes! Even animations are at the state-of-art; the effort to make the alien world and its inhabitants and occupants alive and realistic is fathomless. Exploring Regis is really a pleasure. This is obviously a work of passion that deserves your plause and support. Superfluous to say that story is really smart and intriguing, it's the interactive rendition of one of the best sci-fi novels ever by Stanislaw Lem. There are few variations from the original novel, but not disrespectful at all. Once I finished the game I wanted to read the book and I immediately ordered it! Voice actors do really a great job, they make the characters alive and full of humanity, they give them personality. The electronic ambient music is really atmospheric and creates a feeling of alienation and oppression, the right choice for the apparently dead surface of Regis. I like also the cute tune sung by the charming Yasna, your avatar.Lot of things to do, discover and investigate on Regis, you can never get bored, the feeling of mystery is always high. I managed also to play a vintage sovietic version of Atari Pong! :) Maybe I wanted to feel more vulnerable, more in danger, but you can never do something wrong and get hurt or feeling sick from lack of food and water and so on. Storyline is at most one way, but that's not a defect; enjoying the good story without silly biforcations and alternatives is the right choice respectful pf the good narrative source. However there are a few different endings depending on some choices in the last dialogues, so that fans of narrative branching are satisfied.Don't expect just the usual Firewatch gameplay where you just talk through radio to your companion. You can also talk and interact with NPC, that's very appreciated.More of this kind of games, thanks!For a more detailed review, please see here:
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is incredible. You can immediately tell that this was made with passion and the ambition to deliver an excellent game; and they succeeded. I can't wait to see what this Studio does next.There are two details I want the developers to know that are enormously appreciated. 1. This may be the first game I EVER played that uses chromatic aberration (CA) correctly. You are wearing a retro-space helmet, it  makes sense to use strong CA here. 2. There is a built-in Benchmark.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I accidentally found it in my library.I didn't expect anything of it, or either read any Lem(I always liked Asimov more..) and I still enjoyed it pretty much fully.Good atmosphere, good sound design, graphics was a bit.. messed up the closer I was to the end, and I experienced weird frames issues, also saw some people discussing those.. It's not making experience worse by any means.To see every ending you will probably spend more than 10 hours.I'm not sure what every decision change for sure, maybe it's just.. "fight" in the end or not to.Either way, it's good.Solid 7/10 walking sim.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Your mileage on this game may vary, depending on whether or not you read and enjoyed the book by Lem. If you did not read it, or did not enjoy it, then you should likely skip this game. However, if like me you read it and liked it, then this game is a must. The writers cleverly weave in and around Lem's work, creating a story that serves as a prequel, sequel and faithful rendition of the main story beats all at the same time. The visuals are mesmerising and the best feature of it all is the atmosphere of discovery, philosophical discussions, dread and isolation, very much in the vein of Lem's work. Gameplay wise this is a very straightforward walking simulator, where pressing forward constitutes 75% and "interact" counts for the rest. However I have never played such a great walking sim before. As an adaptation, this is a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's a walking simulator with a well told story that clearly follows a line but with a few little detours and a wonderful retro visual style that is really convincing. my first run through took me just under 8 hours and none of it was wasted for me because i just couldn't get enough of some of the details or the panoramas, this game now has a reserved spot on my hard drive and I'm looking forward to seeing a VR version of the game it will be a whole different world and experience So dev's from Starward Industries "shut up and take my money"
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A great Game that was worth the money. I really liked the artstyle. The story was nice. you can sometimes see where corners where cut but you really need to look cloesley. I had to play the game within 1-2 days becuase the story was well crafted. If you like sci-fi & space I can only recommend it! 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a story driven Sci-fi Adventure game (Walking Simulator).  You play as scientist Yasna who lands on the planet Regis III along with her crew to explore and document flora and fauna. Of course things don't go as planned and you have to find your crew and discover the secrets of this planet.Pros+ Very Interesting Sci-fi setting inspired by the book by Stanislaw Lem.+ Great visuals, some places look beautiful.+ Straight forward gameplay and runs well.Cons- Game starts off strong but I felt a bit underwhelmed later in the story.- May cause motion sickness (I felt it). Need to tweak some settings and it should be manageable.- Price is a bit on high side at launch.Overall game was interesting enough for me to finish it in 2 sessions. Took me just over 6 hours in total and I got what would be probably described as one of the Neutral endings. There are several endings possible based on your choices in the game.While the game had a strong start that hooks you I felt the later parts of the game and ending kinda got underwhelming.If you like games such as Firewatch and you enjoy space and sci-fi stories then consider picking this up when you see a good sale. Made a short review as well, if you want to get an idea of what it looks like graphically :
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and engaging narrative story where your choices determine outcomes. Beautifully done and well worth a play through if you enjoy sci-fi. Story, locations, and characters are all engaging and the story holds you till the end. Exploration is encouraged as you may miss things that affect outcomes for the characters if you don't explore the world. There are eleven endings based on your conversation choices and actions in the game. My first play through time was about 6-7 hours, and I went through a second time for things I missed the first time (and got a different ending). Enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice precursor story for events of novel, which expand a bit more on what went on with Invincible's sister ship crew + new characters on the planet before the events on what you read in novel. It was really nice to experience the world of Stanislaw Lem's The Invincible world in video game.Note that game is essentially a walking simulator but that does not take away from the experience. I presume that most that have read the novel will like the game. As it expands on events in novel and allowyou to speculate how it all comes together with what you previously read as you discover more and more info in game and progress the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is incredibly good. I don't know why, but I'm so damn tired of games that never end. This game was definitely worth the 26 euros I paid for it on sale.HOWEVER, IF I MAY COMMENT ON SOMETHING! It would be about why the interior design of the furniture and machines was the same for both CW and the Alliance? Shouldn't they have depicted a Soviet/USSR style and American style in each respective environment? To really emphasize the Cold War vibe that the game hints at?
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised more people didn't talk about  when it was new. It is a beautiful "Hard Sci-Fi" game set on a beautiful alien world with an awesome retro-futurist aesthetic and an incredibly engrossing narrative with meaningful choices. The only place it lacks a little for me is the gameplay, as it is kind of a walking simulator with a small emphasis on exploration. As a result, occasionally you might get frustrated with navigating the environment. For me, I had a couple of annoying encounters with a foot-wide cable conduit that I couldn't step over, so I had to go around. It is definitely worth fighting through that, though. I will say some people think the ending(s) are underwhelming, but the one I got fit perfectly with the theme.

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a striking and immersive sci-fi adventure, bringing to life the atmosphere of a retrofuturistic world inspired by the works of Stanisław Lem. In this first-person narrative-driven game, you play as Yasna, a biologist who arrives on the mysterious planet Regis III, only to find herself alone, with the other members of her crew unaccounted for. The game blends exploration with deep philosophical musings on humanity, technology, and the unknown, reflecting themes from Lem’s original novel.Visually, the game is stunning, with a rich color palette that makes the alien landscape feel alive and surreal. Its retro-futuristic aesthetic features clunky yet fascinating technology, like robots and manual gadgets, all embedded within a world that recalls the 1950s and 60s vision of the future. The gameplay is focused on exploration, puzzle-solving, and interaction with the environment, often relying on the use of retro-futuristic tools like a map-book hybrid, binoculars, and scanners​WORTHPLAYINGWhile the game is captivating in its world-building and thematic depth, it does have some pacing and immersion issues. The environment sometimes leads to trial-and-error navigation, and the dialogue can occasionally feel overly explanatory, undermining the subtlety of the themes. Despite these minor flaws, The Invincible is an impressive adaptation of Lem’s work, with a narrative that will appeal to fans of slow-burn sci-fi​
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: is a very special game.The developers intentionally stayed away from high-budget bombast, exaggerated character archetypes or very epic events; even Regis III, the wretched misery planet this all takes place on, lacks much exciting detail other than rocks and craters. The desolate environment complements the small cast and limited visual scope. Because, much like the novel it's based on (which was very highbrow and idea-heavy, with no female characters and only a handful of broadly sketched archetypal actors), this game wants to be about Ideas first and foremost.I'd say these are all its strengths.  has its theme - the rejection of human hubris, confronting us with our smallness in an utterly barren, dead and uncaring universe - and it's single-mindedly focused on it. It's the kind of game where, lacking a detailed UI and mission markers, you spend a lot of time checking out the limits of your environment in complete isolation.  It's usually a rock, but I still checked every time, spending longer in this fascinating world that I would have in another kind of game. I got used to the enduring isolation, unbroken save for the occasional comment over the radio to underline how you're the only living soul on the planet. It's good. It works. The sense of bleak isolation is palpable. The mundanity of the endless deserts, the sometimes-plodding pace of the narrative, they all underscore the  of the character's presence here. .That's not to say Regis III is not . The art team really did a spectacular job making a deserted, lifeless, barren world interesting and engaging. Its environments are captivating even though they are static.Those same artists did an equally amazing job creating the human side of this setting, and the humans' technological aesthetic: every vehicle and robot is all space-age wiz-bang soviet retrofuturism, all perfectly grandiose (the titular starships are the size of mountains) and all practically  for a vast and cold universe to show them their limitations. It wouldn't be nearly as impactful with a more used-future, "humbler" technological aesthetic.The voicework is excellent as well. Poor Yasna is the latest in a long line of traumatized fictional space dwellers, going through the worst day imaginable on the worst planet in the universe. Unlike protagonists like Isaac Clarke however, she's much more likely to analyze and strive to understand her circumstances. Indeed, it feels like "understanding" is like a thesis for this game - the only thing that redeems the otherwise futile effort to explore the stars. The narrative's final conflict is best resolved by presenting your findings from earlier chapters in as detailed and rational a manner as possible.Just like a Stanislaw Lem character.It's probably the best compliment I can give  to say that it fits right in with the source material, and even offers up some improvement to it - Lem couldn't have been bothered to make his characters as deep and human as Yasna or Novik or Rohytra. The game is janky at times, and rather poorly optimized - I experienced texture breaking and stuttering a lot during my playthrough - but it's so earnest and dedicated to its themes that I kept coming back despite all the bugs.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: That game has one very big problem: the game is called "The Invincible". So developers are implying that the game is based on the book of Stanislaw Lem. And well, that is definitely not true. It should be better called "The incredible adventures of Mary Sue in Space". Because there is nothing left from the original book, apart of very few names.  So, first of all, the crew of Condor made no research progress at all. The very first their expedition resulted in a terrible catastrophe. Secondly, there were no Alliance nor Confederation in the book. The book was not about political struggles at all. And yes, thirdly, Condor had landed more than a year before The Invincible, so there were *no* survivors from Condor. At all. Also, there were only one Antimat per ship, it is too expensive to have more, but here we see more Antimats than rocks. Also, in the book the robots were not transforming into different forms, but it is minor. And if we talk about other absurd things, there were no gigantic cranes on both ships, 18K-tons ships are huge for sure but still they won't fit several 1,5K-ton cranes. Ok, lets put book aside, anyway there is almost nothing common between book and game. Lets have a look at the game's scenario. We can see a typical Mary "Yasna" Sue. That girl, while being a brain damaged, pushed in less than hour the result of more than a week of work of a whole original book crew, in between of falls, jumps and run. Impressive! And she can lift an adult man; though gravity is less than 1g at Regis, but nevertheless. And yes, she is totally immune to mind-wiping. Yet at the same time she is making all possible mistakes she can do. Landed without any weapon, yet stuck her nose into every crack. And each time she was saved by one or another miracle.TL;DR: the game is just one big absurd fanfic.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I followed and wishlisted this game before it was released - I really like the aesthetic of the universe (1950's Eastern Europe in space) the game is set in and how it's been realised in the writing and graphics. The game is slow and thoughtful, less action than maybe I expected from the trailer but that's not a bad thing, just a slight surprise. It reminds me a bit of Deliver Us The Moon / Deliver Us Mars in terms of being a narrative game with some more involved mechanics for interacting with the environment. The writing is high quality (I've not read the novel the game is based on), the dialogue and voice acting help make the world and the situation more believable and the graphics are effective without necessarily having a crazily high polygon count. The music and sound design is really powerful with a lot of BBC Radiophonic Workshop type synthesis. The fact that people in space still smoke is another nod to the 1950's aesthetic! I'm about 3/4 through so I don't know how the game ends but I've really enjoyed so far. The price reflects the relative short length. My only real criticisms are technical - the framerate can be erratic even with v-sync and framerate limits and the sound can be a bit strange - voices coming out of one or the other ear when it would make more sense for them to be centred - sometimes it sounds as though it's sending 5.1 sound into my headphones but I use headphones and have my sound in stereo mode with no 5.1 or surround emulation.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, my feelings are mitigated. More into I like it than I don't. The story is nice, and there are lot of things to discover. The game is quite short and doesn't require to have 4 hours in a row to make progress. There is no difficulty, it's a story game, not nervous, not really exploration (But you can unlock success if you don't follow the path straight). The universe is quite good, Regis 3 is beautiful, and the combination is surprisingly disturbing, it's like space exploration in the 70's with weird analog devices and robots. (It's like 2001 : A space odyssey).What's annoying now : I can play  games likes RDR2 in 1440p extreme details at 120 fps without any lag, or freeze. This one at some point freeze every 5 min even in the middle of a discussion when you have to select an answer, this drives me crazy. It's too prescriptive as well without talking about open world or things like that, you "just" follow one direction, without ability to really explore. It reminds me the first very first Tomb Raider from 1996, you follow a path and can't really move out from it. (Quite paradoxical, I said upper you can explore. Well you  explore but just a bit. You have to follow a path, and  sometimes you'll have to explore a camp or equivalent).In addition some game mechanism are too cumbersome and redundant. The main character is not able to run more than 5 sec (maybe it's due the story itself, but some chapters ask to "run"). You can't jump or pass through obstacles except if they are on the path then sometime you are block for no reason. Nevertheless, I enjoyed the game, if you like storytelling and casual Sci-Fi games you would probably like it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game explores the very interesting concept of necro-evolution. The story is compelling and engrossing, it takes approximately 12 hours to do a single run-through. I really loved the story.HOWEVER, this is basically the video game version of a choose your own adventure book. You're essentially guided through the story, with very little in the way of "skill". You do need to keep an eye out to interact with certain things that'll have an effect later in the game, and there are 11 different endings. However, essentially you're just pressing buttons in a sophisticated way to move a story along. So if you're thinking it's like a survival game, or an RPG, it's basically a walking simulator. While I had fun, had I realized what this was before buying it, I would not have. I kept playing because I though that at some point it was going to change, but it never did.

_childDocuments_.review: Immersive Artistry in 'The Invisible': A Cinematic Gaming ExperienceThe world of interactive movie games just got a breathtaking addition with 'The Invisible'. It's not just a game; it's an immersive quest, a journey through beautifully crafted scenes that blur the line between gaming and art. Some decisions you make shape the narrative, while others are just part of the journey. What really sets 'The Invisible' apart are its stunning graphics and exceptional storytelling. I often found myself pausing just to soak in the beauty of the scenes, even taking pictures to capture the moment.For a glimpse into my experience, check out my playthrough on my YouTube channel . I've also shared a collection of in-game photos that highlight the game's artistic brilliance. You can find them here: [Imgur Gallery] and on my [Steam Screenshots].The game might be short, completed in under 12 hours, but it's a masterpiece. It transports you to a 60's style sci-fi era, offering a cinematic experience that's rare in games today. Your choices carry weight, influencing the storyline in subtle but meaningful ways. It's not about winning or losing, but how you choose to navigate the narrative.In summary, 'The Invisible' is a must-play for anyone who loves a slow-paced, story-driven interactive quest game. It's a vivid, immersive experience that feels like participating in a movie, set in a visually stunning universe.Highly recommended for its artistry and unique storytelling approach.There are some minor bugs I encountered, so tip to avoid them is to play on 60 FPS (set it in game options)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most gorgeous-looking, carefully told sci-fi games I have ever seen or played!It's more like an immersive tv show or film with the looks of a retrofuturistic blockbuster. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Stanisław Lem’s books, I was really excited when I first heard about this game. And after first playthrough I must say it's really good.Visuals and overall "vibe" is great. Designs are wonderful - spirit of soviet retro-futurism is strong, colors vibrant and small details help to bring Lem's vision to life. Landscapes of Regis III also have stunning moments, although upon closer inspection they sometimes lose their charm due to low resolution.I have read Invincible to refresh memory before playing, and I am suprised how well writing team have incorporated Yasna's story into original book narrative. In no point have I felt, that game contradicts it.. Moreover, I had big smile on my face each time I noticed whole quotes taken from it. Well done!As for gameplay itself - it's story driven walking simulator. There are different sections, puzzles and changes of pace, but that's it. I sometimes felt, that walking speed is to slow, but I can see how it helps to set the tone of a whole game. I once had to reverse to last checkpoint due to some bug that prevented me from progressing, but apart from that I had no technical issues.Others compared it to "Firewatch" - and watching some gameplay of it I can see it. But if you think those games are too similar to each other, go and poke some EA Sports FC/Call of Duty fans with a stick. I don't mind slow paced games and I am big Lem's fan, so I really enjoyed "Invincible". But I get that it may not be for everyone. Netherless, I can't wait for creators next project - maybe "Observation on the Spot", or "Memoirs Found in a Bathtube"?TL;DRIn the end, If you like this type of games, you will like Invincible, and if you don't, you don't. Just don’t cry that you wanted a horse, when you bought a duck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Your enjoyment of it will depend a lot on how easily you are immersed in video games, whether you like the aesthetics and logic of atom punk, and how interesting you find arid, improbable landscapes and pretty sky boxes. The plot of this single player exploration game is delivered with the steady pace of glacial movements. If you're still interested, then be excited to know that the writing is great and the voice actors do their roles very well. I am not familiar with the comics and I found the revelations somewhat underwhelming. The main premise that fails to pass scrutiny. Nevertheless, I recommend this story-driver single player game for at or under $15-20. It took me about 8 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: One line review: An astounding old skool SF experience only tarnished by persistent and niggling technical issues.Visually this game is a feast. One of those games that fills a screenshot folder before you realise you're doing it. It's like stepping into some of that old artwork, rich colours, atmospheric shading, beautiful landscape modelling - really top class (I gawped slack-jawed at rock faces (!) more than once) - and sumptuous retro-future design.The story and script are excellent. Dr Yasna makes for a very amiable and enjoyable avatar into this mysterious world and her thoughts and conversations throughout are always engaging, sharp and beautifully acted [English Version].Game-play is mostly linear (nothing wrong that with) though you do get to do a certain amount of decision making, large and small, along the way. There are no real puzzles but do please keep your wits about you when navigating; the unwary can find themselves circling.Technically, this game suffers a weird stuttering that persisted through my first playthrough, reported by players on both Linux and Windows (Linux here). It ruined the impact of some cut-scenes jerking between frames, most often with complicated weaponry effects being deployed, and can be annoying in general gameplay.Overall, though, this is a highly enjoyable tour-de-force of SF adaptation. Recommended to everyone who has ever wanted to wander alone on a starkly beautiful alien world.

_childDocuments_.review: The invincible: A Sci-Fi Adventure by Stainslaw lem--------------------------------------------------------------------------🎮 Gameplay: ( 5 / 10 )The gameplay in The Invincible is a blend of exploration, and immersive storytelling. As a walking simulator, it prioritizes atmosphere and narrative over traditional mechanics, allowing players to delve deep into the mysterious the world presents. The reason I give the game a 5 here, is even though it’s a walking simulator, there are no tedious tasks, which makes the “walking” not seem tedious. While the pacing may feel slow to some, those who appreciate a more immersive gaming experience will find themselves drawn into its intricacies, wanting to explore the deeper meaning of the mysteries that lie within the game.📘 Story: ( 9.7 / 10 )The heart of The Invincible lies in its captivating narrative, which is based on the original book by the legendary Stanisław Lem. Set in a distant future, the story unfolds with a sense of mystery and intrigue that keeps players engaged from start to finish. Players get put with dialogue choices that can lead to one of eleven different endings, which also helps with player engagement and choices actually mattering. With thought-provoking themes and unexpected twists, it's a journey that can linger long after the credits roll, giving players a feeling of wanting more of Stainslaw Lems beautiful crafted universe. 🎧 Sound: ( 9 / 10 )From the expressive echoes of deserted corridors to the eerie hum of alien machinery, the sound design in The Invincible is masterfully crafted to enhance immersion. This being said, what really makes the sound design in the invincible stand true to its craft, is the voice acting. The narrators / voice actors put heavy emphasis on different words and meanings while portraying a professional sense of realism that keeps you invested in both the story and characters. The choice of background music is also excellent, different themes of music portray different kind of emotions and feelings, which is also almost timed to perfection in regards to the different scenes and scenarios.🌆 Worldbuilding: ( 9.2 / 10 )The worldbuilding in The Invincible is both unique and breath taking. From the intricate details of futuristic technology to the enigmatic landscapes of uncharted planets, every aspect of the game's universe feels meticulously realized. Players will find themselves immersed in a world that feels both familiar and alien, with secrets waiting to be uncovered around every corner. The world is Familiar yet surreal. One trick they have used here is giving you something familiar, but then twisting it with something you wouldn’t think of. 📺 Visuals: ( 8.9 / 10 )Visually stunning, The Invincible boasts spectacular landscapes and familiar yet unique environments that helps bring its sci-fi world to life. From the desolate beauty of abandoned space stations to the awe-inspiring vistas of distant planets, the invincible offers some breathtaking views. I will say that the art style of the game is very unique and crafted in a masterful way. Even though this is true, if you’re a fan of hyper realism, this style might not suit you. Comparing it to Hellblade, Senuas sacrifice, the emotional expression in the characters is lacking, but this is not The invincibles main focus, it rather tries to win on story and worldbuilding, which it doesn’t fail to deliver on.--------------------------------------------------------------------------🏆 Overall Score: ( 8.4 / 10 )The Invincible is a testament to the power of storytelling and world building, offering a compelling narrative experience with a well-made unique art style. While its slow pace and emphasis on exploration may not be for everyone, those who appreciate rich storytelling and immersive worldbuilding will find themselves being dragged further and further inn Stainslaw lem amazingly crafted world.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, has a good style and engaging environment. The characters and their tools are well-designed and the environment is believable. Gameplay - it's a visual adventure narrative with occasional 'minigame' type interactions. Exploration is rewarded, and there are multiple endings. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really nicely done walking sim style game BUT it's not quite a walking sim. It's better described as a slow-paced very classic style sci-fi story where you explore the planet and use various machines to help you. You also make meaningful choices several times throughout the game and make an impact on where the story goes.I would mention things like great atmosphere, really nice retro scifi visuals, awesome looking tech (imagine Alien Isolation if the tech was  60s instead of 70s). The main character Yasna is a scientist and you're rewarded for collecting as much information and knowledge as possible, and then putting it to use finally.I imagine this really works for people who enjoy classic scifi literature as well, not just because of the Lem connection, but because of the way the story is told.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this game. The voice acting was first-class and the graphics were excellent. The art style blew me away though, it had that wonderful 60s/retro feel, so very atmospheric. On the whole, I loved my time on Regis III and possibly would revisit again, but maybe next time I'll bring a bigger gun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the game is very beautiful. Yes, it has a very good soundtrack. Yes, the story is quite intriguing (but not necessarily for the people who read the book or expected the game to be actually BASED on the book’s story). However, the game includes several heavily annoying features, like excessively repeatable and quite needles idle dialogues (only some four variations repeated much too often) or limited movement possibilities (the player’s character cannot jump at all). But the icing on the cake is the completely chaotic and unreliable save system. I totally can’t understand the devs who don’t implement a normal on-demand save system in a PC game in the 21st century. It is an actual dump. This system doesn't even tell you when the game was last saved. It made me play through some sequences multiple times, which was especially irritating in the case of completely unskippable dialogues. Sorry guys, but no cigar.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend the Invincible... cautiously. It certainly won't be for everyone, even if you like visual novels / walking simulators the slow pace of movement around the game world might infuriate. It's thematically consistent with the story that moving around larger spaces is slow and tiring, but it doesn't mix that well with the sort of game often completed in a couple of extended play sessions. That said, If you do have to take an extended break between sessions there's an excellent comic book entry in the menu to catch you up that gradually populates based on your choices.You have to respect the developer, the movement is a conscious choice. The game is primarily composed of exploration and discussion over comms with a mission commander, and there are voice lines that refer to the time things are taking as being mutually annoying. That isn't to say the game doesn't keep your interest with interesting or exciting scenes and no location overstays its welcome.The generally excellent quality of the overall graphic, sound and world design as well as the voice acting are the reasons to recommend. Like Control, there's a gorgeous retro-futuristic aesthetic. Buttons satisfyingly go clunk.The story, based on a novel, is good and covers a bunch of philosophical themes. I believe the ending from the book (more or less) is in here and in the final section it's fairly clear what you need to do to get "good" endings, although these may be limited by your decisions earlier in the game. I was happy with my ending, at least in the context of a game where you can't break in and say "well actually what I think is xyz". The game does in fact let you interrupt the dialogue to interject on a regular basis as a key game mechanic and while it's not always clear where the option will end up, there's normally a reasonable indication of themetic direction and they're generally more complex than paragon or renegade. The real cardinal sin is you can miss things to interact with in the environment, that are then locked off by the next story / dialogue beat, though this is somewhat excused by the fact you aren't generally expected to trudge through the (gorgeous) environments more than once. You can also miss dialogue if you interrupt it.11 endings are promised, less for replayability as much as giving your dialogue choices narrative weight. As with the M.E. trilogy it's fairly likely that if you discuss your playthrough with some friends, some of the outcomes and consequences will be fairly different. It looks like some of the arguments you can use for one type of ending are kinda proved wrong later in that ending, which is a nice touch, the character is speculating to a specific purpose (if not outright BS'ing) but doesn't actually know. Neither do you, it's all based on context of what you've seen.There are still some bugs, the game locked me in a vehicle at one point, but it does auto-save fairly regularly. If we were scoring, this would be a solid 7/10 experience. At times you'll wish you didn't have to move the character around, yet this is key to the experience, and it'll be interesting to see how the developer integrates gameplay into future titles if they make more of this type.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I recommend this for most people.  But I do want to encourage this kind of game design.Buyer, just know what you're getting into:- This is absolutely a walking simulator.  You will not "do" very much.  Expect a story, not a game.- It is SLOW.  Be in the mindset for it.  As if you were putting on a long and slow movie.  Or take it a chapter at a time, like you're reading a long book over the course of a week.If that sounds good to you, enjoy!  It's a great story.Devs, awesome work.+ Adapting a lesser-known book to a video game?  Awesome.  Thanks for taking the risk.+ Aesthetics are simply amazing.  Amazing art design.  Great graphics.  Excellent soundtrack.- It is TOO slow.  Maybe up the walk/run speed just a bit?  Run helps - but why does my character get "tired"?  That's a mechanic for action games.  Why is fast-forward only available for some dialogue?- Overall clunkiness.  Why can't I step over that little rock?  Why can I jump down that ledge, but not THAT one?  When using a controller, why does strafing sideways, even a little bit, cancel my run button?  Why can't I activate that lever?  I know it had an activation action over it...oh I was looking one degree too far to the left...- Some awkward dialogue.  Like another review said, dialogue can get cut off in weird places.  I wonder what I missed.  Then, after having learned that - I'm taken out of the game into my "meta game state" thinking things like "I better not walk too far, I don't want to trigger anew conversation until this one's done"
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Can't love it, can't hate it.There are pros and cons, overall I cannot not recommend it, but too many cons to cheerfully recommend either.Pros:- The game is beautiful: graphics are great, sound and voice actors are very good.- I love the comic mechanic: getting a custom "comic" out of the choices you make during the game is neat! Art style is also great and well used within the game as well.- Story is good, but...Cons:- Weird story delivery: a lot of story elements are delivered directly by the main character and this is both good and bad, good because a lot of narrative games use only text, bad because the character could never be aware of all the things she says, so it's very weird.- Character animations are kinda good, but often "slow" and annoying. The camera is sometimes forced to follow an unnecessarily long animation, and the player has no control over it. I've wonderful more than once if the game wasn't bugged because of lengthy anims. Also, in a game with multiple endings to improve replayability, not being able to skip very long ones (looking at you, painful cave prisoner scene).- Too simplistic charzcter controller: being set on a different planet, I would have loved to have a better character controller that makes me feel like I'm there.Probably forgetting some, but here's my take.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant homage to Lem's great novel. The plot, while only inspired by the book, incorporates everything from the original story and is set as a prequel to the Invincible, instead focusing on what happened to the Condor on Regis III as experienced by an outsider --Yasna-- on a scientific-♥♥♥-unintentional-espionage-mission.The world is exquisite and the Rocket Age aesthetic beautiful, the voice acting brilliantly directed, the writing is out of the top drawer. The gameplay is mostly linear, the mechanics are simple and limited (and limiting), but is of little consequence given the narrative-driven experience pushing the player along with great intrigue.If you like walking simulators and anything to do with Sci-Fi, space, desolation and the likes, you will not find better than Invincible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Single player Choose-Your-Own-Adventure-ish-Walking-Simulator.I'm uncertain if folks unfamiliar with Stanisław Lem or other older Sci-Fi will appreciate the story as much, but may still find it enjoyable. The Art direction is early/mid 20th Century Sci-Fi and I feel it captures that very well. Sound and music is minimal - appropriate for the setting, and done well, as is the English Voice work. Gameplay is fairly simple - as might be expected for the game genre, but there are some mechanic switch ups to keep it fresh. A couple times story summation at later stages had me question if what I thought I did a few hours ago is what I, as the player, understood what happened, but it wasn't egregious. There are also some dialog that - in English anyway - are likely lost in time or translation - for example there's a reference to something being a 'robot' that wouldn't idealize the word, but given the historical and language useage of the word orginally, makes more sense. I took about 7hr to complete a single playthrough, and there are some various decision trees you can make throughout the game giving some replay options. In summary if you like the early SciFi or Adventure games, although unless you're someone that replays to 100% a game, you may want to wait for bit of a discount sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very well optimized compared to the demos.And this is probably as immersive as a story can get.Do not go into this expecting DOOM-like gameplay or fast-paced storytelling.This is a story that's worth living through, just like the book.So far so good, I haven't seen any negatives so far, unless you don't like being limited to 90 FOV.For me personally, that's good enough. Welcome to Regis III.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Was loving the game. My rig can run it on Epic @ 1080p/60. I got out of memory errors in a few places. I have the following specs:AMD Ryzen 5 5600XRadeon 6700 XT 12GB16GB System RAMI'm well above the minimum and recommended specs. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It really did remind me a lot of Firewatch in gameplay but going in blind not knowing anything about the original story, I was very engaged the entire time. I think the narrative and aesthetics are great for what it's worth. I do wish the endings were a little more satisfying than abrupt but I like that your choices can shape the outcome, even in minor ways.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This may be a walking sim, but with it's gorgeous landscapes and fantastic retro-futuristic vibe it scratched an itch that hasn't been touched by a game in years. The story is much better written than what the industry has been churning out lately and it gives me hope that some day we might actually get a real space oriented sci fi game from a large studio. If you're a fan of old school sci fi there's no way you won't enjoy The Invincible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible, is a first-person sci-fi thriller inspired by Stanisław Lem's 1964 novel. Players assume the role of Yasna, a scientist exploring the mysterious planet Regis III, uncovering its secrets and facing unforeseen challenges.Pros:Engaging Narrative: The game offers a compelling story that delves into philosophical themes, keeping players invested throughout. Stunning Visuals: The retro-futuristic art style and detailed environments create an immersive atmosphere. Thought-Provoking Themes: The narrative explores complex topics, prompting players to reflect on human existence and technology. Cons:Limited Interactivity: The gameplay is heavily narrative-driven, with minimal player agency, which may not appeal to everyone. Pacing Issues: Some sections feel slow, potentially affecting player engagement. Technical Glitches: Occasional bugs and performance issues can disrupt the experience. In conclusion, "The Invincible" offers a visually captivating and narratively rich experience, though its limited interactivity and pacing issues may not suit all players.Score: 9 out of 10 stars—shines brightly but doesn't quite reach the cosmos.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: After 3 hours of game play I can say this is awesome. This game is completely story driven and feels like a movie , it keeps the player engaged always with emotions and actions. So far there hasnt been a moment of dullness although walking for prolonged time is involved  the engagement is very well done. This game gives the feeling of traversing a sci fi movie in a linear but with calculated excitementYou will love this game if are into mystery, sci fi and discovery. The games atmosphere matches the story and there is a dialogue with decisions hence it gives the player the feeling that I they are driving the  narrative. In short its an experience  Well done development team !
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This was a 2-3 hour game that forces players to play it in 6 hours. Walking speeds were SUPER slow, clicking on actions sometimes had issues (clicking/dragging). If they sped the walk speed up 100% this game would have been way better but shorter. The story was OK, but a little frustrated on the pace of the game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: if you liked firewatch youll love this game! Gameplay wise it isnt all that interesting, youre basically just walking from point A to B but the story and the way you interact with it is really good and immersive, reminds me of firewatch.Now unfortunately this is one of those "7 hour experience" games although it has lots of deep story choices and presumably endings to allow for multiple playthroughs.Performance wise the game runs great, i played in native 4k 120fps and it stayed locked at that framerate for the entirety of the game but my PC is quite high-end. they do support DLSS + FSR so i would imagine that even older rigs will do just fine.Imo if youre in to singleplayer storytelling then you must buy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: With great pain in my heart, I inform you that I could not complete the game...The reason for that is that the game is not optimized and buggy.First of all, the game design is nice, I genuinely enjoyed visuals etc.The story is alright, I've never read Stanisław Lem before, somehow, I missed his books, I think I will try to read it, but this is not a review on the book, but on a game. In this game the presentation of the story is weak.What I really want to say is that I cannot completely, due to the bug or a terrible game optimization. The game starts to stutter and then freezes, after which it lets you play again and then in 10 seconds it again starts freezing. Okay, in some locations, you have to tolerate this, but after 4.3 hours of gameplay, I became stuck because of the bug. While riding a rover, there is a location where is starts stuttering and freezing, after which, the game relaxes but you can't do anything, neither answer in dialogue or leave the rover. The only thing i can do is to move my head. I've tried everything, in the beginning, I was playing on maxed out settings (it was smooth for 3 hours), then I lowered to medium, then to lowest. I turned off vsync, turned it on. I removed FPS limitation, I put on back but nothing fixed the problem with stuttering and freezingI guess I will complete this game on YouTube, which is very unfortunate for the money I've spent on this game. If you want to play something like this, just try Firewatch, but "The invincible" disappointed. I was expecting a little more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful story, excellently delivered! Gorgeous to look at, enjoyable to experience and intriguing to play through (even if I haven't quite finished it myself!) Can highly recommend for sci-fi fans regardless of whether you know the novel it's based on or not, you'll want to pay attention while playing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to rate this game, because it's not a game, it's an interactive story with multiple endings.It is an interesting story. The characters are good, what they do makes sense. I didn't read the book before playing it. Some people say knowing what the book is about will ruin the experience for you. I wasn't impressed with the story anyway. Maybe back in 60s it was great. These days we got used to all kinds of depictions of alien worlds. I guess this is all I can say without spoilers.I'm not so sure I like the idea of branching with multiple endings, because it's not the kind of game I will play through multiple times. In some RPG game for example you can go through the story multiple times playing as different characters making different decisions. Here, a second run would become just too boring to go through. Hence what's the point in story branching? I watched all endings on youtube. I didn't like that I had to do it that way.So, yeah. Just be aware what you're buying, preferrably buy it with discount. It's a 5 hour interactive story, the story is interesting, the landscapes are pretty, characters are good. But there is not much else in there.P.S. Started playing games on linux. What valve did with their proton effort is amazing. The fact that you can just run freshly released games from beginning to end and enjoy it with a very high chance of success is very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: it gets a thumbs up because I have much respect for these courageous attempts. It's beautiful, great voice actors. I got goosebumps in the appropriate plot points.  High brow sci-fi territory here, regardless of what its based on. It just wasn't fun I'm afraid. It consists of trying to find the next spot where the plot wants you,  Invisowalls up the wazoo. No puzzles (maybe one?) but I just got stuck in places simply because I didn't know where the map wanted me next. So...it wasn't fun per se, but I am 100% behind the idea of using my favorite science fiction books as themes for video games! My dream would be 'The White Mountains' tripod simulator, or 'The Earth Abides' colony survival game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible by Stanislaw Lem is an amazing book, and this adaptation of it was excellent. Even though I have read the book, this game still gave me a rush of trying to navigate through the choices the plot presented. The story was quite different from the book, so it was still a novel experience in that regard. The aesthetics and world building was done with so much creativity and care, it was a spooky delight to play. If you loved the book, play this game. If you never read it, but like hard sci-fi/philosophy, and chilled out gameplay, play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Well, let me first say that this game are way too expensive, and I'm glad I've bought it on sale!!! But still 19,99 eur is in my opinion, still too much.Because only after 7 hours of gaming the credit came on and having the feeling that it's only about to get start.I've read some describing it as Firewatch in space, which describes it very well.
