_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It does what it sets out to do quite well - be a sci fi walking sim based upon a Polish authors work. It looks beautiful as well with some vistas making my way as screen captures for my desktop background. The story is interesting, but its really the amazing conversations and voice acting that is a 10/10 for me. It's not too short, not too long with minimal exploration outside the main story - but there is def some hidden.. keep a good eye out...check everything that looks odd. One issue was the  frame rate stuttering i would get with the game dropping from a smooth 4k max settings experience to under 50 45. It would in time even itself back out or i would have to restart. Only happened 3 times in my playthrough but was annoying enough to mention. Reviewed on an i9 10850k, 64MB RAM, 3080For me 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable supplementary material for the novel. Thought provoking, but not without issues.First off, it's gorgeous. The environments, atmosphere, and ambiance are superb. Human models aren't the best, but they aren't the focus. The Kondor in particular was supremely impressive. The planet itself is a visual treat.The music is perfect. No notes whatsoever. I don't think there's any room for improvement here. The voice acting is very good across the board, however the protagonist had a tendency to sigh or breathe heavily before a LOT of lines. Probably to get across how exerted the player character was at all times, but it got kinda grating after a while. I don't blame the VA for this, it was probably a direction decision.Story is compelling, but I think some players will be put off here - the pace of the game is SLOW. You walk slow, the conversations can be slow sometimes, and the narrative is a bit of a drip feed. It's not that the game is *badly* paced, it's very consistent and gives new information at a steady rate, but that rate is indeed quite slow.I liked my ending a lot, it was vague in the perfect way for my personal taste. I have only seen one of the endings so far, I am to assume there are several based on how the story went.Overall, a very good sci-fi narrative walking simulator. I think it does justice to the original fiction, and brings the concepts to a new audience in a respectable, if not perfect, way. I would recommend this to patient players who like slow burn science fiction.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple short story rather than a game. It is not open world. There is no jumping and 99.99999% of the time, no shooting is involved. It's a mystery story with a dramatic background that presents speech options that drive the story and the ending. It was satisfying and left me uneasy about some choices I made along the way -- I consider that a great result.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely amazing. I first found the demo a long time ago and played it. I was so disappointed that it wasn't out yet but they eventually did launch the full version. Getting it to run was a bit difficult because the game would crash whenever I entered a cutscene, considered refunding it, but it magically fixed itself.Now on to the actual review: Absolutely stunning graphics, story and design. I loved every second of it and the Atompunk aesthetic is spot on. Yet another example of a well made game with no greedy devs, no microtransactions. Easily one of my favorite games alongside Frostpunk and Hardspace Shipbreaker.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Staggeringly good. More like a participatory sci-fi/art house film than a game, but very, very beautiful, deeply thought-provoking, and utterly mesmerising. You have to go with it - immerse yourself in the story rather than think about gameplay. Love the futurist-soviet aesthetic, accompanied with spot-on sound track and excellent voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This prequel/slight AU is a nice addition to the novel.For newcomers, it paces itself well to reveal the mystery of the planet. Despite walking simulators being boring mechanics-wise, this one kept my attention throughout. For a barren setting it does a lot to vary it's landscape, and it surprised me with how open some areas are. It also has a bunch of side stuff you can discover if you're not following the main objective at all times.The voice acting is great, dialogue does a lot for the immersion though idle dialogue such as your supervisor checking on you is a bit too frequent.The art direction sells the setting very well, and the game looks phenomenal in a lot of places. The retrofuturistic technology fits very well with Lem's 1960s hard sci-fi vision.During my playthrough I encountered one crash and one bug where Yasna's eyes wouldn't open after a fall which forced me to reload last checkpoint, also there are occasional stutters. Still, these weren't a big issue.Overall if you don't mind a walking simulator and want to experience an immersive science fiction story, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: 7.9/10Great game. It does feel rushed for the last half of the game though which is stinky. Music and atmosphere are 10/10, the story is interesting but ultimately a lot is withheld from you. The Retro-Futuristic designs are amazing its like the 1960s just went full force into space.Game is pretty buggy, there is a lot of holes in the level design and invisible walls (I got stuck a lot because of this) and LOD issues. I feel like there was meant to be more gameplay and story but it was ultimately scrapped.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this one from the moment I saw the trailer. The classic sci-fi art style and settings are fantastic. The story was mostly enjoyable. But the pacing is too slow and the game play and exploration elements are sometimes extremely frustrating. If this game just picked up the pace a bit more and had mini games or something to keep things fun it would have been a lot more enjoyable. I think the most frustrating part was that I was locked out of completing side objectives or just wasn't able to explore an area anymore because I wanted to know what was on the other side of a rock or slope and could not go back. Also sprinting is useless as the character gets winded in about 3 seconds and has to stop. So I was forced to walk everywhere at a leisurely pace. This is a true walking simulator. Usually that's not a bad thing, but this game took it to an extreme.I would not recommend this game in it's present form to anybody. Unless you really just want to immerse yourself in 50s (or 60s?) sci-fi and don't mind and extremely slow pace. Hopefully the game is still in development and makes some changes to make the 6 hours of game play more exciting, because I really did love the atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Great storytelling game. It starts slowly as basic alien planet exploration and transform itself into filosophical adventure. The only minus I have found are short endings. There are 17 (slightly) different endings, but half of them is quite open."The biggest problem of the known universe is the human kind." 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice story prequel to Lem's "Invincible" book which is closing some of the book's plot holes pretty nicely. Atompunk setting created just great, choices matters, suspense build extremely well. Recommened to everyone who loves the old good sci-fi books and Lem's ones in particular. If you read the "Invincible" it's jsut a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, seeing the landing of the invisible! My heart beat faster xddddThat was a really good and enjoyable game. Not only could I see a vision of the world created by Stanisław Lem, but I could also participate in it! It was a great story, at times gripping. The music, visuals, and characters are really on a high level. The music, visuals and characters are of a really high standard. I can only complain about the poor optimisation at the beginning of the release, as indeed sometimes some elements of the environment loaded with a significant delay. I hope that the devs will quickly fix this and it will be great. One of the best walking sims I have played 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible. Christmas Game gifted to me. First I got hooked on the demo and wanted more of the same. It did not disappoint. You play as a Doctor, female, astronaut and you are involved in a mystery on a barren planet. The planet visuals are fantastic. The story line is good. The game plays like a walking sim and you spend a lot of time searching in a laborious but relaxing way. A few bugs, annoying save points, a bit on the short side (11 hours) but it have a nice flavor. Only got 14 of the 29 achievement so somewhere down the road I will probably read up about them and go get them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I can somewhat suffer through a Linear game but this drove me nuts. _childDocuments_.review: Very cool game! The graphics are nice and the artistic approach is refreshing - different from your usual space / sci-fi games. Story-telling is also very good IMHO. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, nice to see something a little different. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I liked playing the game; I had fun moments and moments I wanted to yell at the game. Sometimes, you have to sit and wait for the game to allow you to move on; this can be frustrating. Sometimes, you are trying to figure out what to do, but it is easy to figure it out.
