_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Strong atmospheric sci-fi walking simulator. - Art design for landscape and music is amazing. (This is the story and design Starfield should have had for their main story)- Good story and prequel to the book “The invincible” by Stanislaw Lem (Booth are a more abstract 50ies existential sci-fi. Not the shoot everything, guts, blood, and lens flare of sci-fi today.)- Starts slow, the second half of the game was much more engaging - story, landscape, and music wise.- Respect for the polish company for taking games as an engaging art form seriously! They go back to a more abstract poetic Eastern-European sci-fi. It is less about overwhelming with special effects and more about trusting in a few simple means and be more though provoking: Think "Solaris" or "Stalker" by Tarkovsky.The stylish almost monochrome locations and the technology seem inspired by European comic tradition. Maybe French or belgian, probably Easter-Europe!In Detail:Positive:•	Mood and style fit the trailers - so you get what you were promised.•	Very nice vistas and locations that provoke curiosity! I sometimes just left the story aside to roam around.•	Few bugs  on 2 day of release – (Just one in an elevator, solved through a reload) Respect to the developers, who respect their work and players!•	Mood/Ideas are close to Stanislaw Lem's Books. •	Coherent 50ies technology style: Robots have vacuum tubes instead of microchips since this was more in use in Computer in the 50ies. Good research and fitting for Lem's Books. •	Music works well. I listen to quiet a few soundtrack in this genre and ambient music. And it is good (above average) quality here!•	Since walking on another planet is interesting in itself and the design is amazing, a walking simulator as a genre choice is a good fit.•	Overall, the game is so well done, that I will read the book afterwards.•	I love the sound, feel and the vista of the binocular. I am constantly using it! 😊Neutral:•	Walking simulator – so the development of the story in the first half is a bit slow.In General, the environmental storytelling is sound. But I wish they would have more confidence in this talent and optimize it for orientation without prompts. Let me be more of a detail detective and figure it out myself. Instead, I am relegated to a prompt pushing monkey. (But maybe I am a just too curious, check everything out, player.)•	Locations provoke curious discovery, but the levels are a one-way street.- Frames in 4K, everything epic, with DLSS in okay frame rate. (Ryzen 9, 12 cores, 3080)Negative:-	Speech audio quality is sometimes too low, difficult to hear. I play with a hifi setup, so this should not be it. But since nobody else is complaining, maybe it is just me. Anyway, it can be finetuned in the settings.Who is judging?Judgement based on space Sci-Fi games for 100 hours +:Star Citizen - So I am used to beautiful vistas. But the style and the local terrain design here is better. Exploration gameplay in Star Citizen should be like this! I would even travel in real life to the valley in the second half of the game. Great, partly awe inspiring, location!Starfield:- This is the story and design Starfield should have had for their main story.Starfield and Star Citizen have different engines and goals, I know. But only as a location design, this game here does an exceptional job better than these 2.Dark Mainstream Sci-Fi Fan, mostly movies and games. Favorites: “Alien I” - the realistic mood. “Blade runner” – just the mood. “The Expanse” first season - the realism and world building.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR "Firewatch in Space" is an understatement, its so much better than thatThis is a Story telling, sci fi, adventure game through and through, dont expect some insane action. This game is a gem and not everyone enjoys Story rich Singleplayer games.My most anticipated game of 2023 and it delivers in every way imaginable. I absolutely adore this game. I've played the demos and playtests extensively and I'm just beyond excited to explore the rest of the game. The story telling, attention to detail, art style, graphics, dialogue its all perfect. I caution players that expect lengthy playthroughs from their purchase, the most you'll get out of this is likely 10 hours for one playthrough, however there are different dialogue options and choices you can choose differently. Most people dont go for a 2nd or 3rd playthrough, but you'd be surprised how much i noticed i missed even just in replaying the demosAs someone whos a massive fan of the sci-fi and space genre for film and media as a whole. My fav sci fi film of all time being the OG Alien.This game is absolutely worth every penny. There are some neat similarities tooSo far 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game Starward Industries,,,,,well done!This game is based on a book by Stanislaw Lem.  And it is a walking simulator with great graphics/music and a solid story.If U like Sci-fi, mystery,  and a fantastic atmosphere...u will like The Invincible.   I strongly recommend this game....I hope to see more games like this.....like a game based on Lem's  Eden book.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits me in the feels.The interesting aspect is, you are experiencing an adventure that feels way realer than most games because it is not really a game...more like an interactive walking simulator with decisions. There being barely any other gameplay helps the immersion tramendously though. The game is not screaming at you "I am a game!" all the time so the experience is like a movie in which you play the main part!Also very good philosophy about the nature of evolution and awesome 1960s retrofuture in the style of ray bradbury or stanislaw lem of course: Visually this game is a pleasure!Not everyones cup of tea but certainly mine :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: One play thru. Nine hours.This is just a story, not even a game.You have very limited control of your avatar.Lots of invisible walls. No return to previous maps. No quest markers. The story is forced on you, often with only one choice. I spent a lot of time searching for the next trigger item, so the story would progress. Lame premise. Lame choices.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great reference to the book, but also adds a new thread to it, with some potential for the next part. A lot of eastereggs for Stanisław Lem's fans. The landscapes are brilliant - I stopped many times to admire the views. The gameplay is not very demanding (it's definitely a walking sim), but the plot is very interesting - no matter whether someone has read the book or not (yet). It's a fantastic game to read.The only disappointment is the invisible walls, which could certainly be hidden better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game has received mixed reviews but I rather liked it. I know this a huge generalisation but I am sometimes rather disappointed with alien creatures in sci-fi, they are often humanoid with funny heads. The Invincible is very interesting in this regard, what you encounter is very clever and feels alien.I think the story is well told, interesting, is about the right length (took me ten hours - I’m slow) and has enough interaction for a walking simulator to keep you feeling that you are doing something. You can explore off the beaten track a little bit and find extra information about the events that have been occurring. I really like the transparencies you retrieve from the robots so you can see what they saw, a lot of the peripheral story is told through those.You have some important decisions to make that affect the outcome but I doubt a replay would feel very different, I was happy with the choices I made so I don’t expect I’ll run through it again. Certainly not immediately. If you are not into interactive stories, this won’t be for you but if you are and especially if you enjoy sci-fi which emphasises science rather than cowboys in space, this could be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely could not STOP playing this until I completed it. Took me 9.9 hours to do so and I loved every moment of it. As others have said, it's VERY similar to Firewatch, just in space. Im not sure if there are branching story paths, as Ive only made one playthrough, but it did seem like some choices can be made differently...whether or not that greatly impacts parts of the story, remains to be seen by me until I make a new game.This is a beautiful game! I would say its even better than Firewatch!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot. the music was amazing, making me feel like I was alone as well as making me unsettled but also making me excited and wondering about a journey that is unknown. I enjoy walking around and trying to piece together what happened to everyone and the planet. The story is good. Some parts confused me a little but a good 98% of the time it told me why so it did not get in my way of enjoying this game. In some parts of the game, you have to make a decision that changes how something turns out some of those decisions are big and some are small.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The world is scripted with invisible walls which disallow you to go where you want. You can't even climb up on small stone on the ground because it's restricted. You can't fall from canyon cliff because of...invisible barrier. So, you don't feel scared about your hero can fall or die and gameplay seems artificial. The game doesn't evoke emotions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a "walking simulator/interactive movie" where you explore a distant planet and reveal its secrets and main plot. But it is not tedious at all, and it is short enough that it doesn't overstay its welcome. The plot is fascinating and well conveyed, the gameplay is easy without any combats or difficult puzzles (beware if action in games is important to you), and your decisions affect the actions of other NPCs, some bits of the story, and eventually its conclusion. The visuals in this game are also well executed, with every element conveying a narrative point. The game has a great deal of environmental storytelling as well as visual and written clues that contribute to its lore/backstory. I took my time but still finished my first playthrough in 6-7 hours and definitely intend to revisit the game to explore alternative choices and their outcomes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't mind slow paced walking sims and you also like hard SF, philosophical themes, and atompunk (retrofuture) aesthetics then you will most probably love this game (liking The Firewatch won't hurt either).Great graphics, moody music and gripping storyline based on "The Invincible" by famous Polish writer Stanisław Lem. Note: This not an adaptation of the book's plot - it's a separate story that takes time in the same timeline and location (planet Regis III). I'd recommend playing the game first and reading the book (or comic book) later.The Invincible is around 7-10h in length and there are multiple endings based on your choices.A VR version is planned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks beautiful and the story seems like it will turn out interesting, but unfortunately this is a walking simulator where the "walking" part is clunky and annoying. The pacing is all over the place, invisible walls exist on 5cm high rocks, and you constantly get interrupted by rather lengthy climb/descend animations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art and a great setting, but there's some jarring parts that cut up the flow of the story. I think it could use a little more work, especially the ending. Gameplay is tight, it runs great on the steam deck, and looks awesome on a big TV. I like this game but I'm kinda disappointed by the ending.  It's worth playing but wait for it to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Great walking simulator (no combat, just exploring), great story, good mechanics, A+ voice acting and beautiful visuals. The main storyline will take you 10 to 15 hours, depending on your tenacity to get to the bottom of the intrigue. Some replayability due to the 10+ different story endings depending on your decisions.The story is based on a 1960's hard-science-fiction novel, hence the Atompunk aesthetic. Way ahead of it's time, liking to the works of Arthur C Clarke, and still relevant today. However, avid science-fiction fans will see the plot-twists coming by now.The combatless gameplay does not mean it's boring or even relaxing. There's some urgency to it all (lore driven, no artificial countdowns) and sometimes decisions need to be made in seconds. And yes, most of the time you'll have time to think about your next course of action, but most of it is morally gray and probably will have consequences.In short, a very high quality and polished game that's definitely recommended for fans of the genre. Personally, it was the pleasant surprise of the year (gaming wise).Main retail price is worth it for the absolute fans; otherwise make sure to get it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite recent experiences! It's exactly what I want from a story-driven adventure game. Fingers crossed, we'll get more similar games based on Lem's work.The only cons I can think of are the occasional bug (rover does not want to move) or momentary stagger during heavy visual effects, like when the antimat cannon is fired. Nothing game breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Overall GREAT GAMENormally I am not a big fan of single player games but this game sucked me into it with the stoy and graphics. Amazing story with diffrent endings depending on how YOU want to play the game. Graphics are amaing the vast scene of th planet was perfect!I played the game in 1 go didnt took a break because i wanted to know what would happen next.I really advice you to buy and try this game if you are into a good interactive story with great graphics and if you are into space exploartion story stuff. GREAT GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a hard Sci-fi game which there aren't many or any of those type of games to my knowledge. The games aesthetic's and graphics are good; Nothing to ride home about but is a quite visually pleasing to look at. The game is quite short, only being 6-7 hours long (for me anyways) majority of it is spent walking or driving the rover which only utilizes basic mechanics and nothing quite satisfying about it, but it does allow to take in the atmosphere of the game. The story is really good; quite unexpectedly good. Its strange, intriguing, sometimes quite hard to understand but it express and explains the story quite well in the end. Dialogue and voice acting is good as well. I wasn't quite sure if I would enjoy this game much before my purchase but this game reminded of Space Odyssey: 2001, which is quite literally the definition of hard Sci-Fi. So I decided why not and purchased it. It was on sale don't remember how much exactly, but even at its $30 price tag i would say its well worth it. Just give it a shot. Really! It's a quite unique and pleasant experience to enjoy.Summary: This is a hard Sci-Fi game, walking sim, great aesthetic's, and pleasing graphics. with a great unique, strange, mind-bending story for you to experience. 9/10 overall.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very rerefreshing to play a story game. JFYI:- There is no real open map, you cant go anywhere and do anything.- There is no leveling / grinding- There is no Season Pass or Paid DLC- There is no match-making or pub lobbies- There are no toxic COD fan boys making jokes about your mom.- There is no skins or item shopYou play the game, make choices, do a few hard to fail activities, and beat the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the feel of this game, it's a great ride, pretty good immersion, but a few things make it painful. There is no jump and vertical limitations in the game render it into pretty much a 2d map, with no real  reason for where the traverse points are. It's just come out so i guess it's unfair to complain because it's been pretty good stability wise, a few times the tools stop working and a restart fixed it. But I'm stuck now, cant trigger the event to get thru the gap in the wall into the city. I have tried everything and given up on it. Hopefully they fix the bug.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most convincing and best narrative games that I have ever played.You can tell that a lot of effort went into the story/dialogue development and voice acting.The graphics and the overall game setting are also a joy to watch.It took me 10h for a full play-through and another 6h for achievement hunting and checking out most of the other alternative story endings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A great classic sci-fi game.  While it is very linear there are some player choices, it's not completely on rails, and it feels quite immersive and enjoyable. It's not too long. It doesn't waste your time, and solving the mystery is engaging. If you are more action oriented or focused on mechanics, it might not be the game for you, but otherwise, I would definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A walking simulator/wallpaper generator based on Stanislav Lem's book, with gorgeous graphics, extremely well done sound acting, on-point visual style, and actually good writing? YESFor some reason, it stutters whenever there's something man-made on screen, which breaks the immersion, but otherwise - pretty polished (pun intended).P.S: I'm gonna replay that just to hear Yasna sing again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is how story- and decision-based walking simulators should be: atmospheric, engaging and above all, never frustrating or boring.The presentation stands out even above most AAA games. Sound design, art style and especially the beautiful vistas and fantastic voice acting are absolutely top notch and among the best I've ever experienced!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time classic SciFi nerd i had to play the game, especially since Eden is one of my favorite books.In general its more or less an interactive book/movie where you can choose some aspects of your journey which will impact the ending.The art style is just supreme and the atmosphere created fits my understanding of Lems aesthetic exactly.The only minor issue i had is the protagonist being a bit too immature and unprofessional in stress situations which i found a bit sad.Anyway its really worth your journey and i hope they will adopt Lems Eden next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is just a bit too serious and sometimes tryhard philosophical. Story and world are relatively linear.  Some choices on the way, most at the end, but for me not enough story and world variety to play it again for another ending.Graphics while generally very good, has some irritating object and terrain  popup issues.They added much demanded options, like more fov, third person rover camera and  sprinting. Which is nice to see.  Of course it remains a narrative  walking(driving) simulator (thankfully no pointless QTE crap). It fakes a single checkpoint save system, but it keeps all savegames!) it just hides them... stupid! (  %LOCALAPPDATA% \TheInvincible\Saved\SaveGames -rename an old one and load ingame.)  The lack of  manual saving can be annoying if you have like me a stuck UI bug after 20 minutes of (final) dialogue... ad the last checkpoint is that old.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Journey into a mystery of the planet and it's history, with a background of the cold-war like politics and what it ultimately does to people.Since it was written so long ago, all the 'technology' is incredibly retro and yet to some degree functional and perhaps similar to what one could expect.Great although a bit short story, with quite a bit 'walking/driving simulation'. While wandering, the protagonist's insight can be heard as specialist-scientist describing her point of view - good plot device (Yasna aka Jasna). Intriguing humongous MacGuffin, but still great when you think for a moment how the Alliance could be USSR and Commonwealth - well just Commonwealth or US. I could not shake the feeling that the Invincible - the name of the vessel is something to describe how much better they are vs. 'the other side' - just another part of the arms race and the rivalry and tension can be felt in relations between both sides.It would be nice to have some more puzzles instead of walking - it would make this more of a game.Some choices can be made along the way, but hard to say how much these matter.From technical standpoint the game has been significantly optimized from demo version which did not work very well on my PC to solid 30FPS at 1080 working on i7-7th gen, 16GB RAM and GeForce 1060M, only sometimes heavily lagged (to 0fps for several seconds), when it looked like it needed to load next area - once it crashed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable retro 1950’s science fiction vibe. Don’t expect too much from the robots, though, they’re kind a’ sluggish. As for the walking simulator aspect; wasn’t too bad. There’s only one short sequence – which you have to play through twice in order to get all the achieves – that is really slow. Otherwise, you can both run a bit and you’ll find a vehicle to drive around in (although no racer). Be prepared to enter into a lot of conversation. There’s no real replay value: Once you have exposed all secrets, it doesn’t have more to offer than to replay from a certain road choice – to get to all the endings. Personally, I liked it a lot, but it’s definitely not for everyone. Some lagging here and there. I’m on the constant look-out for quality games that doesn’t take to long to complete, and this certainly met that expectation. Quite linear.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a great game. It's a science fiction investigation/adventure title with a lot of content, mood and smarts. The visuals have a retro-tech look to them and there are great solid colour skies and land that give it a strong, unique look. You spend a lot of time exploring while you unravel what has happened on the planet and why. But the exploration isn't empty time. There is a constant dialogue with your fellow scientist and superior who is in orbit above the planet.  There is a fair bit of scientific investigation, but it is never tedious. I highly recommend this game. It's definitely one of the best sci fi titles I've played in the last few years.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first experience with a "walking simulator" and I must say I was quite impressed.At the time of writing this review, I've only played through the game once, and only saw one of the game's multiple endings. And even though the actions I chose didn't lead to the best outcome, the game captivated me from start to finish. I can't remember the last time I was this immersed and invested in a video game. Usually that only happens with movies for me.This was a great experience and I'm looking forward to replaying it again in a week or two to find one of the other, and hopefully better outcomes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I would really like to give this one a "meh". Art design, music and voice acting were spot on, but I never felt in danger. Actually, I had no sensations playing, unlike Firewatch (hate to compare). Story wise, it was a mixed bag.. It is a good experience although a quite long one for what it offers. At the end they explained You everything because they failed to communicate it clearly during gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game. It's a linear story with a few endings, nothing crazy in terms of how you approach it. I think some developers have lost touch with that aspect in recent years. It's perfectly fine to have just a simple, single story without too much fluff. The game looks wonderful, the colors of the landscape, the interiors of buildings and ships; all of it. The mechanics are very simple, almost entirely point and click with a similar movement and traversing system. Not much else to say. If you like slower, thoughtful games, you'll enjoy this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: There are two ways to look at this game, and both are good:1) If you're not familiar with the book it's based on, this is a superb walking sim that dares to ask the controversial question "what if Firewatch had actually good writing?". It's a slow burn sci-fi mystery with compelling characters and a main story that may feel a bit dry and low-key at first but that steadily keeps building onto a satisfying climax.2) If you're a fan of Lem's, and specially if you like The Invincible, you will be presented with an alternate retelling of the story that may seem a bit odd at first because of the amount of changes and deviations introduced, but that will keep you on your toes by playing along with the plot beats of the book, until you reach the climax an realize this REALLY is an adaptation of the novel, but from a new perspective. The best kind of adaptation, really: one that wants to complement and establish a dialog with the book, instead of wanting to act as a substitute.No matter which one you choose, if you like good storytelling and/or are a fan of good science fiction, you're in for a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly looking and immersive experience. Solid performance with very minor animation issues on a few occasions. Love the voice acting and all the actions feels like they have proper weight. Loving the experience ever since the demo was released and I'm glad they solved performance issues. Running it on linux out of the box with 120 FPS cap while maintaining only about 70% load at 1440p all maxed out FSR off with my RX 7900 XTX. Thank you for that experience so far!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: We seriously should start asking questions why small studios can make better games than so-called AAA studios.Game is very atmospheric, mysterous and nice. This is how I like space games. To discovering mystery of an alien planet, without any human enemies. Just the mystery, eerie environment and you.Only the ending, even vastly choiced, was little disappointing (short, cut).
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: After almost a year of patching it, the game now finally seems to run without crashing every hour or two for me anymore, thanks devs! Now I can finally recommend this hidden gem! This is a narrative sci-fi  adventure and basically a companion piece to the 1960s novel by Stanislav Lem. If this is enough to intrigue you, don't read further and jump in, it's great! If you're unsure, maybe look for a Youtube walkthrough to get a taste, the atmosphere in both novel & game is quite unique and the game devs strongly captured the vibe of the novel IMO. If you like old-school sci-fi with lots of philosophical musings, you might find yourself deeply loving this little, strange thing. Highly recommended now after a bunch of patches! (also read the novel afterwards, you'll be surprised)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It stutters so hard on my PC (With RTX 3080ti) that it's essentially unplayable. It was not that bad in the beginning, and the only reason I didn't refund it right away was the voice acting and and interesting story. But after reaching the Alliance base, the game became essentially unplayable even on low graphic settings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: For £25 no - for £8 -10 give it a tryCompelling Narrative - The game unfolds an engaging story that captivates the player, showcasing its strength in narrative development.Visuals - "Invincible" boasts stunning graphics, making it a visually appealing experience. Despite its linear progression, certain aspects detract from the immersion. Notably, the presence of floating textures and invisible barriers disrupts the flow. Additionally, the game occasionally resorts to 2D representations for elements that would benefit from 3D modeling, such as vines on the ground. The explorable area feels significantly limited in scale compared to other titles, diminishing the sense of freedom and exploration.Pacing and Exploration - The game deliberately adopts a slower pace, which effectively contributes to the atmosphere. However, this choice is undermined by the implementation of invisible walls in areas that visually suggest accessibility. This limitation, coupled with the precise requirements for climbing actions, feels outdated and restricts player freedom unnecessarily.Design and Physics - While the space suit design adds a visual appeal, it misses the opportunity to enhance gameplay or contribute to a more immersive experience. Furthermore, the game's physics engine appears lacking. The experience of climbing and selecting paths on slopes feels inconsistent, especially when later stages of the game introduce low-gravity conditions that dramatically alter movement dynamics, detracting from the realism and strategic elements introduced earlier (choosing how steep slope to slide or jumping down from the end of the hanging rope).
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: For those extremely rare minorities who have read the novel the game is based on, The Invincible is clearly made by people who truly loved the book. While reading the book does remove some of the mystery and suspense, the visuals and story line actually adds more color and details to the book in a faithful way. It helps the words in the book come to life especially for someone lacking vivid visual imaginations. The book and the game are a perfect pairing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Reading some comments I'd like to remind that NOT EVERY GAME SHOULD BE A SURVIVAL SOMETHING! Some of us just want to go around, and relax, and "watch a movie" with choosing our own lines, yes, imagine we don't need a complicated survival system and craft, there is plenty of that in the other games, just open no mans sky and have your way.Anyway the game is amazing. I am a huge fan of walking simulators, and simple games, which help with my anxiety. I am easily spooked so this game had enough thrilling moments for me. The environment and music are great and I was very fond of Yasna as a character. I hope the studio will make one more like this please!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: In general I am not a fan of  types of games and this one is pretty much it. You walk or drive, you interact with objects, choose dialogue options and make decisions. Not much of typical gameplay.However where this game shines is incredible mood through whole game. You feel lost, confused, under pressure and torn between options often. You get immersed in beautiful retrofuturism science-fiction universe based on work of Stanisław Lem. Here I want to point for people that do not know him, he is for Polish science-fiction what J.R.R. Tolkien is for fantasy in general.First playthrough took me a bit under 9 hours. I went in completely blind. It was nice. There is very interesting  of your decisions in form of comic that updates after story milestones.Good game to relax to.Personally I think that you should wait at least for minor sale before buying if you are not a big fan of this type of games. Otherwise you can feel that you overpaid a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The latest walk-and-talk simulator with an ominous story, interactive dialogue, gorgeous world, and an eerie, but fitting, sound track. The Invincible is a game with the exact same vibes as Firewatch, but with  cranked up a fair few notches. For those who have played Firewatch, the parallels between these two games will be quite obvious. Both games have phenomenal voice acting to go with the dialogue, and a mysterious story that will have you wondering as you play through the game. With that said, I would highly recommend you go into this game (and Firewatch if you've yet to play it) as blindly as possible.Aside from the obvious, the only real difference between these two games is where Firewatch had a few endings, The Invincible has eleven! The choices you make in The Invincible will drive the direction of your story. If you didn't feel the need to replay this game with different choices, I would certainly be surprised. Like Firewatch, there isn't much game-play within The Invincible beyond walking, talking and using a couple of different tools. This game took me twice as long to complete than Firewatch did, thus you may want to play this over a few sessions.Of course, The Invincible was not without its flaws. None of which are game breaking, but small things that needed to be polished. Some of the graphical assets, such as the ground early on, was floating with an empty void beneath completely revealed. Half way through the game, there were some textures that were obviously much lower in resolution than the rest. The biggest issue I had was with the metal scanner, which I could not adjust when the game had tasked me to. I couldn't rebind the key for that adjustment, either. I was able to progress along regardless, but it was mildly annoying to have to struggle through that one part of the game unnecessarily.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A game heavily focused on its storyline, resulting in minimal gameplay interaction. It mostly revolves around essential choices and some environmental interactions, with players spending most of their time walking and discovering new data.The game's greatest strength lies in its haunting and unpredictable storyline, depicting a world on a planet resembling Mars. The graphics just normal, but the desolate and eerie environment consistently captivates players' minds.Gameplay:
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: After playing about 7 hours I can definitely say that my opinion of the game has improved from my previous review. It's still very much a "walking simulator" but the story is fantastically interesting. I don't think you have to be a fan of "Hard" Science Fiction to enjoy this but it certainly wouldn't hurt. It isn't a game where the story takes a back seat from the action and game mechanics. In fact "action" isn't something that there is much of in The Invincible.It seems like your decisions have an effect on the story that unfolds but it's very hard to say for sure without going through the whole thing a couple of times. If you make a "wrong" choice does the Navigator do some off-screen string pulling to redirect you back into where the devs want you to go? It's certainly possible. I thought I had reached an early end a couple of times but somehow I'm still going.I haven't come across many bugs. Got caught in the landscape unable to move once and that's about it. I do recommend the game, pretty strongly in fact, but negatives that I listed in my previous review are still there. And they are still negative! To my previous comments I will add that the game mechanics are frustratingly opaque at times. You can have no clue at all what you are supposed to do and just wander about until you see a prompt for interaction which is not fun at all. Making the visual prompts larger or having them stand out more would really help there.My Original Review below:----------------------------I played a bit more than an hour and so far I haven't made up my mind completely about this game. It's actually less game and more interactive novel so it is extremely linear. So if you want an open world, alien hunting FPS you should probably pass. On the other hand it is a very interesting story. Basically a sci-fi mystery with a bit of an Atom Punk aesthetic. Walking Simulator is also a reasonable description.The game mechanics are quite clunky. Sprinting is quite useless so you are basically limited to a trot. You can't jump and traversal of the rocky terrain is done by pressing "W" when you are pointed at the right spot. If you aren't in the right spot and facing the right direction you can't go over the smallest rock or bump. Conversation control is not intuitive and I missed the chance to say something a few times because most chances to pick what you say are on a fairly short timer. Also it's yet another game that will not let you save the game manually which I absolutely hate.If I had paid a full AAA game price for this I would probably be a bit upset but it's half that cost so I'm willing to give the benefit of the doubt. Basically I recommend this game but you should adjust your expectations. Marketing and description could have been a bit better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience, indeed... BUT... why limit the game to a storyteller with basically NO WAY to do something wrong or die? Why limit the environment space and not even allow the player to pay attention to fall down somewhere? I do understand that this was probably done on purpose but, I believe this game could have been EVEN MORE BEAUTIFUL if there were many mechanics and interactions. I mean, the radiation tool was used one or two times, the radar three or four times during the entire game. In other words, why not adding ANY RISK in the gameplay? That was a very brave move.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing. The story and mystery along with the stunning visuals kept me hooked. Kind of dragged on at times but worth it in the end. Game ran well even playing in VR using UEVR. I want to try different choices and get the different endings... However I think I will take a break and come back to it later. Specs: Ryzen 9, 32gb, 3060ti, ssd, Pico 4 virtual desktop uevr
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it. No shooting or flying (so far), but the progression is more than just a walking simulator. I have been interested the whole time, except twice when I could not find the way forward. A little searching got me past that. It's somewhat linear, but each location allows freedom to go in several paths and buildings. I might play it over again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like the game.  it looks amazing and the world and story is intriguing BUT i keep running into the same damn bug where I can no longer trigger any action.  I can look around fine but my hand will be stick doing what it was doing before a bit of dialog, opening doors, turning dials, pushing buttons, etc.  Then nothing, just standing/sitting there looking at RT/Left Click prompt that doesnt work.Bought this game when it came out and only managed to get 2 hours into it out of 3 hours of gameplay and 4 attempts.  Just a dissapointingly buggy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but realtivly short game. It has a great atmosphere and engaging story. IMO for the content inside, the price should be much lower. In the end of the game, I got stuck between rocks and could not find a proper path due to a map boundary bug, and due to autosave mechanism I respawned always behind a proper path for player movement (please fix this issue or make multiple autosaves!)I had to finish the game on YouTube (last hour looking from the playthrough), but as this kind of hard sci fi setting ir rather unique I will still give it a positive.P.S. A big salute to Novik, for staying with us. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Nice relaxing walking sim with a solid story. It is on the short side though and unfortunately all possible endings don't really give the impression they matter at all as nothing happens afterwards anyway. Frequent stutters even on a more than decent PC. No puzzles whatsoever and very limited interaction with the environment. Voice acting very good with entertaining dialogues. Overall being a very decent game if you are into walking sims for which you shouldn't pay more than 10 bucks but it can't match "Firewatch" in any of the areas.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I never played a game that captured the atmosphere of this (from todays point of view) retro-futuristic sf, that is a consequence of porting novels that are this old into our present reality so perfectly. It is very immersive, the visual style absolutely fits the setting - great game and already way past the quality of comparable titles like Firewatch etc. The story is quite long for such a title - and as I know the novel I think the adaptation in a video game could not have been done better. The missing widescreen support at first annoyed me, but I could not think of a way to get the viewpoint from inside a helmet done with a widescreen picture - and the game is so immersive, after a few minutes I completely stopped noticing the bars.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! The story is so captivating! I am at a loss for words... I also really enjoyed the comic book strips and the mechanic where you take the slides out of the machines and figure out what happened. It was an amazing experience! The only small con I have is that the movement is a bit weird at times where you bump into very small obstacles but that is insignificant.Great work guys! I would love more!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Overall thoughtfully made, beautifully designed world and concepts, and interesting story (prequel to the novel if I understand correctly). There is some clunky dialogue and moments that drag on, and a few 'choices' that either don't really make sense or don't feel like choices at all, but can affect your ending. All-in-all, really enjoyed it as sort of a palette-cleanser and the shorter playthrough was refreshing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the story but make no mistake, it's HARD sci-fi. I'm talking like 20 minute conversations about hypothetical theories of robotic necroevolution, stuff like that. And the game does not hold your hand through it either. Yasna is a person who lives in this universe and knows this stuff already. it's up to you to just keep up when she starts talking technobabble.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is an amazing game on a number of levels... Beautiful art, moving sound track, perfect voice acting, and an interesting story. However, I did not find it enjoyable to play. It falls somewhere between an interactive movie and a visual novel, pulling and pushing the player through a scripted path with predefined actions. Although the world feels 'open,' it is not. I admit I have not read the book so I did not have any point of reference when I started.I found the controls to be difficult to adapt to.  Space bar for conversation, mouse wheel for dialog options. There are long segments of driving a rover which were hard for me... small windshield and (what felt like) clunky steering. I ended up restarting from a checkpoint more than a few times just to find a familiar point of reference.I am used to having more freedom in my games and I felt like I trudged through this one. Lots of dialog that cannot be skipped and must be listened to in entirety before environmental objects become active.  Climbing paths that activated only from a specific spot on the ground. The only times I could 'go my own way' was driving the rover and the game did allow me to become hopelessly lost in labyrinths of tunnels and paths.Achievement hunters will have a dilemma on this adventure. There is a decision point in the middle of the game that prevents 100%, no matter which way you turn. Since the game has only one save slot, returning to this point requires manually copying save files out for later use. After 16 hours in the game, I could go back to this junction and turn left for the remaining achievement.  However, I don't have the interest needed to play through to the end, yet again.  The game does let you experience most of the multiple endings from the last automatic save point. But, even with this benefit, looping through 3 or 4 endings took hours.Other achievements are tied to specific dialog responses and are the result of actions accumulated over long stretches of the game. You won't know if you've missed the mark until it is far too late to turn back.Achievements aside, I recommend the game to those who enjoy a highly scripted game experience.  I give the developers a lot of credit for a job beautifully done. The issue I have with The Invincible is tied to my own expectations and not to any flaw in the game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Game started off with an intriguing story but quickly fell off into a walking simulator.  I thought there would be some benefit by exploring but no there's nothing to find by walking around and exploring.  The story is all right but not enough to keep my attention for the two hours I played.  Has a cool concept but poor execution leaving me bored with nothing to do but slowly walk an empty planet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen other reviews to this game describing it as Firewatch in space, and for the most part, you would be correct.This game relies heavily on exploration, environmental narrative, and excellent voice acting that let you discover the world of Regis-III, and the events that transpired there. And it succeeds in all three.  Voice acting for Dr Yasna and her supporting cast is excellent, makes you relate and empathise with them throughout. While the story is quite short (it took me around 6-7 hours on my first run, though I still missed things), it is a far cry from other action focused sci-fi stories. Following a similar narrative course to the book, The Invincible and the way it plays allow for you to think and ponder on the questions it puts forward, in a way not many other games have made me do.The world of Regis-III, and the different structures you find there are pure eye candy, and you would be excused for spending most of your playtime staring at the environments and soaking it in. The addition of a photo mode, which is accessible at any time, also means you can admire the beauty of Regis-III permanently on your desktop. The aesthetic of retro 1960's sci-fi (think Black Ops Zombies with the ray guns) is a joyful to look at, and makes you think you've jumped into the cover of a old school sci-fi novel.This game made me buy the book, which I have read, and would happily read again. Its story, world, characters, and gameplay surprised me in the best way possible, and I do wish I could play it again with fresh eyes to experience what it has to offer for the first time once moreFor £25 in the UK, its a decent price for a game such as this. A solid 9/10. Would highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The short of it is that for the most part, the game is amazing. It has beautiful graphics, music, and the story is told pretty well. It has you constantly questioning what is happening and continuously gives hints as to what had and is happening. The game also uses the walking and buggy driving to give you time to think about any new information you learned as well as speculate and connect the dots of the games story. However most of the endings are a bit underwhelming. There are a couple or so endings that are actually pretty good and interesting as to what they imply, but the rest make you kind of go "Oh, thats it?" as all the ending scenarios are pretty short and the ambiguous fate they tried to go for just make it feel rushed and has some endings feel like the same. In more detail...Since the game is supposed to be a prequel to the book, they decided the endings are supposed to leave the characters fates ambiguous since they aren't mentioned in the book. However as I said this just makes the endings feel rushed and overall underwhelming, especially since the effort and dialogue you have to sit through makes loading a save to try a different ending feel like too much work since you have to sit through 30 minutes of dialogue and choosing the right replies for the endings. Spoilers:   I believe they should have had endings, 1 good 1 bad, that were actually mostly in line with the book that acts as a great transition between the two, and the rest could have been their own non canon ending that actually explored the implications of choosing the ending by another 15-20 minutes maximum since the game already changes quite  a bit from the book such as
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The invincible is awesome. I absolutely fell in love with the game first time I saw the trailer, and fell in love even deeper when I actually played it... This atmosphere, feelings you have, astonishing landscapes, animations, design. I loved all of it. If you are a atom punk and retro-futurism enjoyer, you should try this 100% This game gave me such a feeling, you know, this little sadness after completing it. I haven't played such a great adventure game for years. 10/10 P.S: devs pls fix saves and make part 2 :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I really hesitated to buy this game, mainly because of its small size. When I already bought it, I was a little bit disappointed. It started very slowly. However, after one hour of playing, the story just consumed me. The game became an atmospheric adventure. The story is wonderfully written. The game is aesthetic and pleasing to the eye.  I don't regret that I bought it and am looking forward to playing it again to see other endings."
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game that is more like a visual novel than a typical game. I enjoyed the story, and it sparked my interest in reading the original book by Stanislaw Lem. The developers did an excellent job with the visual design, giving it a stylish and fitting retro sci-fi look. I highly recommend this game, giving it a rating of 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding marble!Visuals, Sound, Music, Acting - All work together in harmony. They form an atmosphere that give you the "loneliness in space" vibe with a touch of "Cold War Space Race" on this rough planet called Regis III.I played it in 2h chunks and reached the end in three sessions. Because of interesting decisions on the course of yourmission, I even enjoyed a 2nd playthrough shortly after which isn't something I'm often intrigued to do so. If you enjoyed other walking sims like Firewatch or Dear Esther, you won't be disappointed with this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a journey! I was not familiar with the work of S. Lem before playing "The Invincible," but this game has truly sparked my interest in his creations. The game art brilliantly captures the retro feeling of the golden era of space exploration, with a design aesthetic that is both nostalgic and visually captivating.The voice acting and graphics exceeded my expectations, adding depth and realism to the experience. The voice actors deliver their lines with emotion and authenticity, enhancing the immersive storytelling. The graphics are stunning, with detailed environments The sense of discovery  is profound. The game encourages exploration and curiosity, rewarding players with a rich narrative and unexpected twists. The choices you make genuinely impact the story, leading to different outcomes and adding replay value. Each decision feels significant, making you ponder the consequences and driving you to think critically about your actions.I think the "walking sim" type of game play really suits this game, as I was relaxing and not feeling that I need to kill or do some crazy stuff, a genuine exploration.Overall, "The Invincible" is a masterpiece that combines excellent storytelling, stunning visuals, It's a must-play for any sci-fi enthusiast and a testament to the potential of interactive storytelling in video games. I sincerely hope the developers continue to create more games like this, as it sets a new standard for narrative-driven experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the story, it kept me wanting to know more and what happened on the planet. The atmosphere felt eerie, and the visuals are beautiful. The characters were likeable and the voice acting is great.I had some bugs and lagspikes here and there, but it didn't bother me or affect the gameplay much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very captivating, interesting story and amazing, climitic graphics make this game worth giving a try. Three and a half hours into to the game and I have not expierienced any bugs yet. Overall it is a well written and greatly illustrated retro sci-fi story and if you read the book the game is a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game in one sitting (that is how much I liked it) at first it starts slow, not much "action" but the longer you progress, the more "action" you will have. But this game shocked me with a Wonderful story, especially for someone who does not really like "space games".That game looks insanely good, the environment is breathtaking in some places, especially with everything on Ultra settings.Gameplay it felt smooth, nothing annoying to complain about, it is a slow/story telling game with a lot of exploration (if you don't want to just go rush the story) the actions are pretty clear, is a mix of open world and linear gameplay. The audio in this game, it was perfect the voice actors were on point, even better than some new triple A games.The game is not difficult at all, it does not require grinding at all (most of them are just text) to give you a wider perspective on the Story which was INSANE The ending  since the game is a choice/make your own story so if you really want to grind the achievement you will spend some hours in this game but not that many since you can select the chapters after you finish the game.Bugs I did not encounter any severe ones sometime the character got stuck in some rocks and one time  but except that nothing severe. My opinion about the game, I give it a solid 7 out of 10 the game was good, for an indie developer it did surprised me for the first game that the made under Starward Industries name I can recommend this game even on the full price if you are willing to explore everything but for the ~ 5-6 of story personally I will get it on a sale for 50%
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing that pulled me into this game was the retro styling and colour rendering. To call it a 'GAME' is a very loose term. The first few hours I enjoyed the graphics, voice acting and how the story unfolded. Then it just became something to sit back and just watch. You don't actually play! When in conversation, you do have to reply within a time set but this was not always the case. I can't really say much more about it. The ending I had was...... well...... cut short abruptly. It left me thinking, well what happened afterwards. They do have different endings but the one I had left me thinking...was that it?I've played 'watched' this game once. There's nothing there to pull me back in to do this all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Tasteful, touching voice acting.+++ Beautiful set-pieces and retro design.+++ Great player agency, and multiple endings.--- Some parts can feel a little long.--- Demanding on hardware, especially for long-distance vistas.This one sets the gold standard for walking simulators. The story is deeply interactive, and it provides several rich plot points whether explained in dialogue, notes, or simply details located in the environment. This is a beautifully rendered experience, and it deserves plenty of appreciation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Its a slow paced space novel, you will walk between the explorations, while that could be boring to some of you, it looks pretty good while doing so and also the sounddesign is REALLY impressive. I would say it feels a bit forced where you should go even tho there are multiple ways. Your desicions will matter in how the story continues. The biggest minus for me is that there seems to be no support of UWQHD Screens, and therefor the immersive feel will fall off a bit. Other than that you will pretty much get what you will expect if you see the trailers. Performance:I dont have any FPS issues. So its well optimsed. Although I dont see this as a plus, as this should be normal. But with the catastrophal releases these days its ofc worth mentioning.Specs:GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070CPU AMD Ryzen 7 3800X 8-Core ProcessorAfter completing the game my conclusion:Pro:  - Amazing Soundtrack- Amazing Atmosphere- Good Voiceacting- Solid Graphics- Solid StoryContra:- Story is way to short for that pricetag. - Gameplay is very limited: Other than walking there is pretty much nothing you can doConclusion:You buy this game not because you want to "play". You buy this game because you want to observe a cool space novel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games i played recently. Starts slow and simmers for w while but then it takes off and presents a lot of exciting opportunities to live through a very original and immersive adventure. Graphically pleasing , scale of the planet itself and object you encounter is really noteworthy ( especially towards the end of the game ). I liked most of the dialogues, even though a little big of THE MESSAGE crept  into the narrative. You can make meaningful choices and decide how your story ends. I would recommend to anyone especially for the price requested. 10/10 buy and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews have pointed out that this is a walking simulator, however you shouldn't let that deter you from buying and playing this amazing game. The story for this game is engrossing and the only complaint i have is that the game came to an end to soon. The game offers several different endings as well as numerous side objective, which you shouldn't miss any of the side objectives is you explore everything thoroughly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the very few that achieve that outstanding balance between a good psychological story and peak immersiveness, all the while delivering outstanding visuals at a rapid pace. I truly could not ask for more, and encourage you to experience the joy I did. Do no more research, do not read the spoilers.Gameplay is simple, but the story is gripping and the world design is absolutely top notch.You can also read the book either before or after you play the game, as it's an excellent companion to the game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Now, The Invincible (the Stanislaw Lem novel the game is based on) is probably my favourite piece of fiction, so I was coming into this with high expectations, and the game delivered. My only criticism is the occasional presence of visual bugs (e.g. a probe going through a piece of rock), otherwise I'm very happy with what I got.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect to enjoy a walking simulator, but I don't hate on movies for being non-interactive, so it made sense to me to evaluate this product for what it was trying to do rather than what it is not.The voice acting was incredibly high-quality. The core premise was interesting, engaging, well-paced, and well-presented. I LOVED the "bridge" set at the end, which felt like a perfect hard sci-fi adaptation of an Apollo ground control room to a starship (with a minor chair deficit). In fact, all of the retro futurist content was charming and somehow believable.If you hate walking simulators, you won't like this, true. But if you sometimes enjoy books or movies, there may be a mode of enjoyment here that works for you. I would have no problem recommending other folks to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I played ALL the walking simulators available - it's my hobby. This one is 'okay'. I guess that since 2024 seems to be game dry season, and last year wasn't great, we'll take what we can. The good: - the graphics are good, the story is relatively passable.The bad:- the 11 endings are ... oh my - underwhelming. There is no payoff on any of them - just read the novel, at least it's definitive. The branching here is barely perceivable and not something you feel you can 'control'. I would have preferred ONE good ending.And given it's so predictable, and that SF has moved on a lot since the 70s, I don't think there's anything in there you won't have seen many, many times.Overall, it feels like I should give it a thumbs up because some of the 6h it takes to finish it are decent. On the other hand, if played the forgotten city, the occupation or the painscreek killings, this is considerably inferior.  Only buy this if you have spare cash and love story-based games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice one, story is amazing, and the scene in the cave and between the mountains is awesome, well there are still some point the develop team need to pay attention to, the first is when i enter a new map in the game, it will stuck for a while, and second is sometimes when you are in the room, the game will usually stuck, especially the chapter when i first enter the base of alliance, the stuck keep happening... beside all of this, this game is perfect!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on the book and the like the comic book you that records your choices and progression.I wish to was easier and faster to replay so you could ideally try different things.An interesting story with multiple choices that can affect your game and how everything turns out.Recommended for anyone that likes adventure games
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: There's just no game and story-telling is not good enough to compensate it. In addition very clumsy controls, time-dragging and completely unnecessary interactions like moving up\down\through a small gap makes this walking simulator even worse. After finishing the game I have a very strong feeling of disappointment. I wish I had read the book instead
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I love the progressive discovery of a planet that has lived and died and is full of unexplained mysteries. Lem's heritage is alive. I loved the Kharkovchankas, these soviet vehicles developped in the fifties to live and move over the Antartica ice fields; they are used and magnified in this game to build bases on Regis III. A game that will not please every one, but certainly will interest the S.F. connaisseur and the Lem fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding walking simulator! I enjoyed the retro-futurism in the game design. Very atmospheric and gorgeous scenery. Although there could've been slightly more variety in level design. I appreciated the multiple endings. Unfortunately the game has no puzzles at all, and it doesn't really make use of its game mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's a prequel to the light novel "The Invincible". Thus, playing this game won't spoil you the novel, rather, it'll add to it.Expect about 6h of play, which for around 30$ is 5$ an hour for a nice story.You get to see a comic version of your playthrough, to remember what you did or just to get a whole view on the entire story including your choices.A downside is that the game is extremely linear, and has few endings. It's great that it has more than one ending, several goods and bad, however there will be many times where you won't feel "free" to do what you want.I wish there would be more lore, because a lot of places you get to loot don't have much but 1 or 2 things to pick up and read. Or sometimes serve just 1 function.Also, more often than not, you cannot go back to do something you wanted to. if I were to take a non-spoiler example... let's say you go in a building, and have the option to use the radio, but you leave the building, you cannot go back inside it to still use the radio and the game will consider "ok he did not use the radio" and force you to continue.Those are things to consider which in my opinion makes this game go from "amazing" to "good-very good". Where it's worth playing, however, not paying its 30$ price and watching a youtube let's play may be very tempting.Definitely read the light novel after playing the game to know what comes after.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who was reading Lem's works for years, I was anticipating this game ever since I've heard of it and I must say I love it. It shows care and respect for masterful source material and adds just enough from itself to expand the story laid out in the book (which I highly recommend too). The environments created by devs are beautiful with great music to boot and the branching story while short is quite engaging. THIS MAY NOT AFFECT EVERYONEBut for me a good part of textures were blurry for the whole game never coming to full resolution, an issue I had also with the demo of the game. It's a minor issue I'm sure will be fixed relatively soon and probably can be easily troubleshoot if needed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A Prime example on why a good story does not equal a good game.Dont get me wrong, the game looks quite good and i really like the artstyle.The Problem is the main protagonist. First of all, youre not really "playing" the game. Youre just walking from cutscene to cutscene. Thats not a problem, and theres plenty of chill games that are like this and if the story's good you can really get immersed into the world.The Problem is, that the main protagonist in this one is a whiny ♥♥♥♥♥ that does nothing else than complain and be as pessimistic as humanly possible trough what i assume would be 5-6h of total gameplay.At every slight inconvenience she just sits down and you have to listen to a 5min cutscene of her literally wanting to die. It doesnt build a character and doesnt make me relate to her in any way. Its just cringe and to be honest annoying af...
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, as a fan of Lem's writing, I am absolutely loving this game. It is a 'walking simulator', that is primairly about immersion to the story and amazing world around. It goes for 6 hours, approximately, has amazing retro style of SciFi and develops story very well. I loved it, played it with my partner watching every part of the story like a movie lasting 6 hours or more. It is not full of action, but it is full of emotions, hooks, discoveries, with very vibrant story. I loved it, and I will recommend it to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Good solid sci-fi story, pretty good gfx, but very linear gameplay which may or may not be your thing.  I don't mind that personally as long as it's a good narrative.  It didn't feel like choices mattered that much until nearer the end, and on my play through I ended up on a very underwhelming ending which was disappointing, but I believe there are others so hopefully they are better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Hello from Ukraine, dear friends from Poland! The developers have released an excellent game. I completed it in one breath. Although optimization is not the strong suit of this product, the atmosphere and style are conveyed wonderfully! It was interesting to explore various notes at stations and on ships. A fantastic storyline inspired by the science fiction of the past era. As a fan of 60s-70s science fiction, I couldn't remain indifferent to such attention to detail and ambiance. It's also intriguing to listen to the characters' conversations throughout the world exploration. It feels like you're truly witnessing a dialogue between two intellectuals who are professionals in their field. The storyline is also captivating. Another interesting detail for me was that Alliance members have an American accent. Somehow, this amused me greatly. I can confidently recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice.Good visuals (but had to turn VFX low on Arc). Sound & music is great. A bit of a walking sim / interactive novel, but gives enough variety and choice to be interesting.The walking speed the first time was okay, but I presume I'll feel it on the slow side in my subsequent playthroughs to get all achievements. Also would have liked to learn more about the universe, the Alliance and Commonwealth.

Furthermore, the game looks quite nice, especially outdoors. However,  human models in the game are somewhat lackluster, especially the faces. The game has rather low system requirements. _childDocuments_.review: I did not enjoy The Invincible.The design work is excellent, many of the visuals are gorgeous, and the voice acting is highest quality. But I felt all other elements of the game fell flat.What I expected was a narrative game with light puzzle elements, but The Invincible is not that. There are no puzzle elements. The game is essentially a visual novel, or at best a long series of audio logs stitched together. While the character is investigating, you are asked to go through very slow, extremely explicit prompts for each new action. The movement in the game is slow as well, which makes the pace feel even more glacial. Slowly walk to a location, click on a thing. Now slowly walk to the next location and click on things there.The world feels hemmed in. While it is beautifully rendered, there are fences everywhere, including some very jarring invisible walls blocking off clearly open passageways. It makes an already limited experience feel even moreso.And the narrative elements of The Invincible fail as well. The game is advertised as having 11 separate endings: that's technically true, but of course they're largely small variations on two basic endings. The choices that have an impact on those endings are limited themselves. And what endings there are felt incomplete, unfinished. I think it was a creative choice attempting to end the game on an ambiguous or melancholy note, but I found it unsatisfying.Overall: The Invincible is extremely pretty, but I found it to be a very frustrating, unsatisfying gameplay and storytelling experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand how people compare it to Firewatch or Vanishing of Ethan Carter even. Maybe some people simply don't understand the difference. _childDocuments_.review: I went into The Invincible excited to experience the story and visuals. However, the gameplay was so tedious and frustrating, I found the entire experience with The Invincible to be very disappointing.  The user interface is under-baked and very confusing and it can be extremely frustrating trying to figure out how to move to the next location on the map, so you frequently get stuck and have to tediously search how to progress, without any true sense of accomplishment once you do stumble onto the exit.  By the end I was just rushing through, trying to get to the end so I could move on from The Invincible. The story was somewhat interesting, and I'm curious about the other possible endings, but there is zero chance I will go back into this torture chamber of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: While the production of this game is very good, and surely the contemporary philosophical discussions will be interesting to some, I felt the game play tried to awkwardly straddle its clear story-driven design with faux world exploration player interactions.  It felt stifling, bothersome, and slow to have to personally traverse the world to progress the story, when there is no particular reward for spending any time in the world.  I would not recommend this game to people who aren't the type to find themselves deeply immersed in a game's story and setting.For those who are likely to be immersed, you will hopefully be able to indulge in the story, the character choices (which are somewhat unclear as to what effect they actually have on the direction the story takes, except clearly the endings), and the setting on a strange alien world.For people like me, who are not easily immersed, you will probably find some frustration in the pacing, the tedious world traversal, and the feeling that most choices only affect voice prompts.  I would rather this have been made in the story telling style of a Telltale game, than one where I'm expected to move the character from a first-person perspective.  That style would allow me to fully focus on the story, the choices I'm making, and view the world from a cinematic perspective.Scrambling over terrain obstacles is not interesting.  Quickly running out of stamina in any effort to move the character faster is not interesting.  Attempting to explore the world map to - at best, get a little extra lore - is not rewarding for the time sink that it is.  Driving through the map doesn't even let one enjoy the passing view, because between the helmet cover and tiny rover windows you can't see much of the world from the driver seat.  Most of the world is bland and barren, which while accurate to the story setting, again doesn't maintain one's interest as a player actively needing to maneuver through it.  Re-playability is very dependent on one's enjoyment and patience for the game.  I'd love to see what different choices might do in the game, but if the only way to experience the difference is to have to walk through the world again, I hesitate to consider it.  A better check-point saving system that could allow me to simply jump back to decision points as I choose would let me experience the parts I like (the story) while getting to avoid some of the things I don't (the world traversal).  Sadly, that doesn't seem implemented.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a slightly challenged (as opposed to challenging) implementation of a niche genre. It's an interactive novel / walking simulator for fans of that 1960's kinda glum alt-pop sci-fi. Not sure I can give it an enthusiastic thumbs up, but this is more enthusiastic than a "maybe." If it's your niche and you don't mind searching discussions every once in a while, give it a shot!Graphics are gorgeous. Voice talent is great, which turns out to be very important for the whole "alone on a dead planet" thing. I liked the story, but maybe some won't. It's Stanislaw Lem after all.Main annoyance: invisible walls and occasionally *very* difficult to spot interaction points.Graphics settings defaulted to "epic" on my machine, which resulted in a slideshow until I tuned it down.I may go back and see what story branches are in there.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. It's like Firewatch but (literally) set in a Stanisław Lem novel.It's not a hard game, it's mostly about making decisions and discovering the world - some people would call it a walking simulator, but I feel that doesn't do it justice.Totally recommended if you're into serious Science Fiction.It tells the story of the Invincible from a different perspective. Knowing the novel is not necessary, in fact the game may be more exciting if you don't - or like me have so bad memory that you forgot all about it.
