_childDocuments_.review: This incredible experience is more of an interactive movie than a game, much like Firewatch. And much like Firewatch, it is fantastic and absolutely worth the money.As a side note, I played the entire game on Steam deck and it runs really well. I switched to 30fps instead of 60 because it'll give you a bit more battery life and you don't need 60 for a game like this.Personally I think this is worth it at full price. I spent about 7 hours on my first playthrough, and I'm sure I'll return and give it at least one more playthrough at some point. The length and pacing of the game is perfect, giving you enough time to soak in this incredible sci-fi world and story without overstaying its welcome.The story is great, it had me intrigued all the way through. Great voice acting as well. Though it's mostly linear there are plenty of choices and at least some of those have very real consequences from what I've seen.Even after having played through the whole game, I would replay it just because it's such a nice place to be. The world is breathtaking, all the more impressive considering that as I mentioned the steam deck has no problems running this.In conclusion, worth the full price in my opinion, and an absolute must have if you can grab it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically a story playthrough, but if you want to feel like you're walking on an alien planet, it's quite immersive and the art is quite good.  The atompunk aesthetic is not overdone, but is a nice futurepast experience.  Movement is slightly annoying due to invisible fencing and limited climbing/descent options, and since it just launched there are a few minor details that need a little polish, but it doesn't crash or anything.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The towering classic by S. Lem reduced to walking and touching simulator so boring that it explains why so many characters you encounter end up in stupor or worse. Or perhaps, inexplicable absence of the option to play as a male character makes connection with the protagonist impossible. Will refund, and go re-read the book for the twentieth time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't finish it. Just googled the endings and I'm glad I didn't finish it.It's a walking simulator, or as I prefer calling it: an interactive movie. The story is great, the art direction is spot on, the voice acting is good. Yet... Its boring.  It's supposed to feel lonely and desperate, but that just stops being interesting after a while. Instead of some sort of character development you get repeating dialogs that are just obvious fillers. Sometimes poorly timed interrupting other scripts. The fact that they can repeat the same dialog alone should be immersion breaking. But it's fine because the dialog is so devoid of any context that it just works in any part of the game.  The characters don't change throughout the game. With everything that happened you'd assume they'd start to break protocol, become less professional. But who knows, maybe they hate each other. We never learn anything about the people or the factions or anything that matters. The book this came from is clearly very good, and I'm going to go read that now, hoping for a better experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a bit like "playing" a book.  The world is stark but picturesque.  The implied deep history of the world accompanied by mysterious "creatures" is the main reason this game is interesting.  The retro design style and engineering is the second best part!  I thought this was an immersive way to tell a story - by having you interact with the world and discover its secrets.  The game is very linear and you cannot step outside the narrow boundaries.  There are a limited number of choices you can make.  But you are rewarded for your curiosity, as it will unlock different endings!  Good luck exploring, astroneer!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This adaptation of its 60s original is just as hauntingly beautiful and philosophically impactful as its source. After finishing the game I immediately went to read the novel (for the first time). The visuals and soundscape along with soundtrack are done so so well, and my compliments to the VAs.I did have to reload once or twice due to bugs, but nothing too bad.I would encourage you to allow yourself to become immersed in the story, you _are_ Yasna, rather than someone playing her. Think logically, but also abandon it where appropriate. Most of all read anything you can find that might be of use.As others have said, if you're a fan of the genre and well versed, you might see some of the twists coming, I wouldn't say that made it any less enjoyable for me. Also remember it is only familiar narrative because of the work of people like Stanisław Lem (the author).Happily lost myself for a couple of days with this game. Solid pick on sale or 3rd party sellers :)

_childDocuments_.review: Love a proper SciFi story - this is very story based, little to do other than follow the story and yet there's enough opportunity to influence the flow to make this a worthy experience.Just about doesn't overstay it's welcome and several endings to enjoy.Highly recommended! _childDocuments_.review: This game may have the best art direction of any game ever. It is certainly one of the most beautiful "realistic" games ever made, and the experience of exploring an alien planet is extremely believable and frequently breathtaking. It's a completely story-based game, really just moving from one scripted scene to another with only very occasional "branch" choices. It's not a game so much as a "choose your own adventure." I like this kind of game okay, but it isn't a *riveting* experience, just interesting, and sometimes genuinely dull. The story is fairly good as a story, I'd say: good characters, good dialog, good mystery, slowly unfolding plot: it's intriguing. In the end, though, the killer is that the endings I encountered were extremely unsatisfying. Only about 8-10 hours of gameplay here, too. All in all I'd say that if you like walking-around simulators and story-based games, and you lower your expectation for any kind of satisfying or sensible ending, you'll probably enjoy this game. Most players, however, including many who like that kind of game, will not I think ultimately feel satisfied by it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the original novel, and it was a great joy for me to find out that the book was being made into a game.The guys from "Starward Industries" did a wonderful job of playing with the plot of the novel, thereby telling the same thing, roughly speaking, but from a different perspective.The beginning of the book doesn't match the ending of the game, but it was nice to . 10/10, I'm delighted and looking forward to the VR version.

_childDocuments_.review: A slow paced walking sim with cool retro sci-fi elements and a story that never wowed me. I personally like games that are fun and engaging, unfortunately this game felt flat from beginning to the end without any engaging interactions and wow moments. I never knew or read the novel and don’t know much about the original story but this story as I said was very flat, there was no moments that made me excited, after playing 3-4 hours I really wanted it to be done. But it doesn’t mean it’s a bad game, you might like it if you are really into slow walking sims without any interactions. The game is overall well designed and has good voice acting and visuals.The visuals are pretty solid, although they don’t look next gen but overall they get the job done and depict the alien world that you are exploring pretty well. I really liked the art style and overall design of objects like robots and machines in the game, they were very unique and true to this type of art style.There were some areas where textures felt very low quality, specially the metal parts of the world which I think was a very important part of the story but it felt very low quality. I played in native resolution without any super sampling on epic quality.This is an area where the game falls short, although it usually applies to most walking sim games, but here the gameplay is very basic, there is no puzzles or QTE in game, very basic button clicks, nothing more. There is no jumping or crouching in the game and you can only climb or descent on specific location of the map. I think developers could’ve easily made core gameplay mechanics more interesting and engaging.The traversal mechanic is really sluggish, so slow, there is running in game but just for 2 seconds and your character is out of breath! Because of space suit, weight and gravity? If they wanted to go for more immersive gameplay then why limit the running only why not adding oxygen meter for example? I think the game could’ve been shorter like 1-2 hours if you had the ability to traverse faster in the world.There is also a detector tool in game which I am not sure what was the purpose of it? To just show metals in the world?! Why developers keep doing this? Why not giving users the ability to save anywhere and anytime they want? What is this trend? I really don’t get it!The story is open to debate, I am sure there are many people that enjoyed it. There were parts of the game that I really enjoyed too, specifically some of the characters conversations and debates. But at the same time as I said in the beginning I was constantly looking for a wow pr surprise moment in the game and never got it. The narrative lacked significant highs and lows, maintaining a flat tone from start to finish.I really enjoyed the voice acting and sound quality in this game, it was pretty well executed overall. Although to be honest I hardly remember the music in the game.One of the issues was cutting conversations when you interact or progress in story, it happened for many times and it was little annoying. Or the time limit for conversations, you are listening to someone else and you have to act quickly before your time runs out, really didn’t like this approach. I played this game on epic settings, native resolution and no super sampling. Set FPS limit on 144 and game maintained it for most time. There were occasional stutters, lasting 2-3 seconds, particularly in open areas, but overall the game performed pretty smooth and was free from any bugs or technical issues. There is some replayability value in this game, I am sure there has been some optional areas that I missed or to get all achievements. I think there are multiple endings but because of the gameplay mechanics and lack of manual save I personally won’t get back to this game to get those missed parts. I honestly don’t understand this annoying trend.CPU: Intel Core i9-12900KMB: MSI Z690 Edge WiFi DDR4RAM: GSkill 32Gb DDR4 3600MhzGPU: Asus GeForce RTX 3090 StrixMonitor: Samsung Odyssey G7 32" 1440P 240Hz

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game with a fantastic story. Couldn't set it down until I was finished with it. _childDocuments_.review: The Invincible explicitly reveals the lust for exploration, the scientific background of the new worlds, mystery, and an unnerving atmosphere of the unexpected and exciting. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I enjoyed it so much I’ve ordered the book. I definitely recommend it but you have to know what you’re getting into. It is purely a sci-fi story based mystery; there is very little gameplay. The best way to describe it as a book game. Obviously it’s based on a book but the experience isn’t like a movie game that we see more often. This genuinely is like acting out the book. The pacing, the dialogue, and the atmosphere that a book exudes. It’s like you’re reading a book but get to impact the story. So instead of being frustrated with a character you can control them. There’s 11 different ending so you’ll be able to get the outcome you want. The decisions aren’t hidden you’ll understand and get what you’re looking for. Other than one pretty early on one. Without spoiling, I'll just say if something early on seems too good to be true go with your gut. A few options at the end are restricted if you take the wrong path. However either way there're multiple good endings still available even if you do mess up. There's just a couple more options if you don't.So if you’re a book reader I think you’ll enjoy it because it’s literally like listening to audio book but you can impact the story and see what’s being talked about. It’s a lot of fun and I can’t wait to read the book it’s based on.That all said even if you don’t like reading books I think this could work with you. It could be a way to experience a great book story that you otherwise wouldn’t have been able to. It’s more engaging than a book, for obvious reasons, so I hope it would work for you where a book wouldn’t. Who knows best case scenario it might motivate you to try reading again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game! Very atmospheric, zen experience sprinkled with moments approaching ASMR. That isn't to say it's boring. There are genuinely exhilarating moments and truly engaging discoveries paired with moments of true awe. I finished the game in about 10 hours, but there are many endings that I have yet to backtrack and uncover based on my choices. Will likely revisit soon, and recommend playing if you haven't picked it up already. It's worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for what it is - an atmospheric retro SF walking simulator. Starward Industries has done a decent enough job and has successfully conveyed a 60s SF story into an interactive experience. However, there are some things that are making the overall experience worse.Pros: - Absolutely superb music which perfectly conveys the feeling of being on a mysterious planet light years from Earth. The soundtrack is creepy and otherworldly majestic at the same time.- Great voice acting for the two main characters - Yasna and Novik. Both actors did a phenomenal job. Novik's actor, in particular, is amazing. He flawlessly captures the essence of a ship captain in an SF show from ~50 years ago.- Despite being on the same desolated planet the whole game, which is a design limitation for the visual department, the game still manages to show awesome and awe-inspiring alien scenery. Props to the studio for successfully managing to create diverse locations with such narrative limitations. I've never felt bored of my surroundings. In fact, it was the opposite. I was taking screenshots non-stop.- The story's tempo is just perfect. I've never felt like I'm losing my interest. Rather, I always wanted to push further and figure out what was going on. The game is around ~8-9 hours long, and I’ve never felt like it drags on unnecessarily.- The comic book story-telling gimmick is a nice touch.Cons:- By far, the worst thing in this game is infuriatingly outdated traversal mechanics. The game only allows you to climb or descend at very specific places, and it won't let you traverse anywhere else, despite being obvious that our character can do so. It's hard to describe just how annoying this is. It genuinely almost ruined the experience for me if it weren't for all the good things I listed above. These places where you can move forward act more like invisible interactive buttons that trigger the climbing/descent animation in that specific place rather than a traversal mechanic. I'm not talking here about going where I should not. I'm talking about reaching the designated place only from a specific spot, despite being reachable in other ways.- Movement, in general, is very clunky. There's no jumping, no crouching. Yasna will refuse to move/pass even above the slightest obstacles, such as small boulders or even big cables. Luckily, I only got stuck once into the terrain, but I was constantly in fear that could happen.- There is no strafe-running! If you run, the moment you use A/D, Yasna will stop running. And running is, btw, limited with an invisible stamina bar, which serves no purpose, and only adds to the annoyance.- If you are looking for a more complex gameplay, you will not find it here. There are no puzzles, no secrets to discover, and no actions that require mechanical skills or any thinking. These are just the most basic interactions. That's perfectly fine by me, so this is more of a warning for those who expect more gameplay here.- No manual saving. I simply don't understand why a game such as this doesn't allow you to save manually. Luckily, auto-saves were frequent enough. However, there's absolutely no reason for this game not to have a manual save. It forces you to play until the next autosave, even if you want to quit that gaming session or need to go.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a great atmosphere and story-telling. Has good graphics, allows to decide what's gonna happen just next. However, decisions are not changing the plot drastically, eventually, you will get to the needed directions. Also, it's NOT quite convenient to walk sometimes since even small rocks can be impediments. The moment with walking on metal.. it's too difficult to understand how to tune the radar, what form/status it should get to be tuned, how to go avoiding the wholes. Also, for some reason, level designers put plenty of routes/corners you might want to go to investigate, but they are just dead ends.. Then, sometimes dialogues a get interrupted by following cut scenes and it is a pity when you notice an icon to select an answer and hit a new cut scene, or crawling with no chance to get back and answer :)All being said, game has minor issues, but is still great to spend a couple of evening in. Highly-recommended! (for people, who will value atmosphere, story-telling)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Really quite excellent!  The level design is beautiful, and the game does an excellent job of making you feel like you have really high agency in determining where the story goes.  I particularly appreciate how many of the choices you make are emergent results of what actions you take/where you go, as opposed to a more canned dialog-based decision.If the aesthetics of the game look appealing to you, and the idea of a story first game is what you are looking for, this is a great one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game tells a story in the setting of Lem's novel - and does it true to the source. Having read the book before, I still find the game full of suspense and meaningful choices. The art design is consistent, of a quite peculiar raypunk style. The overall views of the planet - sometimes spectacular,As a side note, it made me realize what Starfield planet exploration could have been...
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most original sci-fi thrillers I've ever played. The game stands out for its superb artistic direction and suspense. Add to this very atmospheric "sci-fi" music and beautiful backdrops of nearby planets and stars, and we have a recipe for one of the most original & atmospheric walking simulators released in recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a walking simulator in hard sci-fi world based on work of Polish writer Stanislaw Lem. The whole story was very interesting and encouraging from start to the very end. Graphic design and visuals of the game are absolutely superb. Was getting a cinematic experience as if I was acting in the movies like Martian or Interstellar. Attention to details were quite stunning. Tend to stop for a while and absorb the beauty of the planet and sky above…First time I entered space rover I look around the cabin for 2 minutes ;) There are no puzzles as such or riddles that would challenge gamer and you have to follow a story however there are many choices through the experience that you will have to make. I suppose that you can finish the game few times to discover different scenarios. Sound and music in a sci-fi theme kinda style also added to the positive reception of the game.I played on Steam Deck Oled and it was mainy pleasant gameplay with occasional drop of fps but  considering the visuals  bravo to the creators for optimisation. Truly enjoyed last 8 hours :)Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A great story, where I have found myself holding my breath or thinking "Oh ♥♥♥♥" a number of times - and that means I am engaged in the story and feeling a connection to the character(s). This has been so far a lovely 5 hours playing, and not finished yet - and now even more interested in what is going to happen.Great to play, lovely graphics and a story which just feels amazing and fun to go through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for its visuals, well realized, period-appropriate retro-futuristic styling and setting, and excellent voice acting. Gameplay is nothing special, just another walking sim with only the most basic logic and navigation puzzles standing in your way. The story was probably a lot more mind blowing back in the 60s when the novel this game is based on was published. These days though it doesn't feel particularly special, though I did appreciate its grounded tone, hard scifi approach, and good pacing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Friend suggested this game to me since I have a love of space and scifi (more so hard scifi) and I've been enamoured with it since. And without giving spoilers, the comparisons/parallels to/nods to the book are great to encounter
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 10 hours, If I could give one thumbs up and one thumbs down, I would, the audio had issues throughout the play through, disconnected once and had to reloaded once. Interesting story but I was a bit disappointed at the ending with how it ended. Don't want to spoil it for others, so I'll leave it at that. Enjoyed the retro visuals with the 1960's Si-Fi theme, cool story that kept me wanting to see what was around the next corner, I would wait for the game to go on sale and it be a good game to play on a rainy day where you have some free time, I give it a score of 3 out of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I've read The Invincible by Stanisław Lem. It's a very intriguing book with a sci-fi story unlike anything I've ever read. It poses ideas and concepts rarely touched in fictional storytelling, and never touched in non-fiction. It's the kind of story you read and think about how outside the box it is in its portrayal of what we believe to be concrete rules for life and organisms. The game iterates on the novel and tells a very different story in a really cool way. I was left in shock when I realized this is a prequel. Quite a good one in fact.The game introduces a lot of its concepts in a similar way that the novel does yet its no less effective. I'm not sure how these moments will come across to someone who hasn't read the novel but for me, it was a great feeling and further exploration of what the novel hits on. Seeing a visualization of the metal structures, the flies, and the planet are mesmerizing imagery. This is quite well written, with good pacing as well. It ultimately amounts to a walking simulator but rarely feels like one. This is much more immersive than a walking simulator typically is. I also really enjoy the freedoms the game gives you. There's side paths to explore, dialogue choices that alter the story, and discoveries to find. You're co-writing the prequel to The Invincible - one of the most notable sci-fi novels ever. That's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: Right off the bat: If you don't like walking simulators, you should probably just skip this one. I'm also leaving a positive review here for reasons I'll explain, but while I enjoyed certain parts of this, I ultimately didn't feel that fulfilled by the narrative, though I do now want to read the book this is based on.This is a linear, narrative walking simulator that takes place in an interesting sci-fi universe where everything has a 60s aesthetic (which makes sense since the book came out then). It is absolutely gorgeous and the environments are truly a sight to behold throughout. It also runs pretty well and does have DLSS despite being an AMD sponsored title, though the lack of DLSS presets is odd. It's also fully voice acted and is largely well done.That said, there is a lot of what feels like padding in The Invincible. A lot of slow walking and climbing through environments, while listening to conversations with your superior over the radio. You do have dialogue choices you can make and it's implied your choices matter, but I found most of them made no substantial difference until the end, which sad to say, was a pretty decent letdown for me, regardless of which way I chose to go. Despite having large, open environments, this is a linear game and you'll be going down the guided path until the next story beat. There are no collectibles and only the occasional substory element to find, which has no major impact. It took me about 6 hours to finish everything, but if all the filler was removed, it probably would have been half that.I did enjoy my time with The Invincible as I got a press code for it, but if I paid full price for this, I think I would have felt a bit burned. The environments and acting are great, but the story in my opinion, doesn't justify the lack of gameplay and with walking simulators, your story has to be good enough to do that. I think for sci-fi and walking sim fans, this is worth considering, but definitely not at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is not actually a "game", it is an "interactive story telling program" ... there is no "game" to be played here, all you need to do is move forward and have the story unfold as you continuously press W.There are no puzzles to solve, no mysteries to explore, you just keep pressing W and pressing W... Awesome if you'd like to experience a sci-fi story interactively through your computer. Very bad as a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game i like it, very atmospheric and beautiful scenery. However there almost no game-play, you can just walk around and choose dialog options. But dialog choices matters.if you want to have a few nice cozy evenings, with nice game on the couch, that the game.probably this game should be a VR game, but for some reason it is not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Beautiful landscapes (yes, it's a desert planet, so it's lifeless and mostly hues of orange and brown, but beautiful nevertheless)- Absolutely amazing art design that perfectly captures the atmosphere of the 1960's original novel's analogue-tech futurism- Slow paced exploration that places immersion above action- Engaging radio dialogue between Yasna (the hero) and Astrogator Novik while she explores- Refreshing scientist hero who does NOT stumble cluelessly through the story without even getting the the most obvious hints, unlike so many other video game heroes- Good tie-in with the novel's storyCons:- If you know the novel you already know the secret behind Regis III, though it's still a good tie-in that tells more about the history of the [REDACTED BY ALLIANCE CENSORS]- The slow pace may be too slow for more action oriented players
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A retrofuturistic walking sim, based on Stanisław Lem novel from 1964.However, thanks to the setting, narration, music and the source material, I never felt bored or annoyed, that I mostly just walk and click things.There are choices to be made, 11 endings to experience and some things to explore on the side.It is funny, don't you think? We pretend that we are invincible, we name things to make them look like they are, but in reality, we are everything but invincible...
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible gave me a feeling of being trapped alone on an alien planet, searching for my teammates while discovering a hidden, unknown danger. The mysterious atmosphere is reinforced by incredible music and the song that Yasna sings when feeling lost.Retro equipment is another aspect of the game that I liked; you can see how people in the sixties envisioned the future of space exploration rather than how it is envisioned today.As other reviewers wrote, The Invincible is more like an experience than a game, something like an interactive book or a movie. Your decisions influence the narrative, but there aren't any difficult parts that require gaming skills; you also can't die (at least I didn't manage to). For me, it was a great alternative to watching yet another TV show. The fact that it can be completed in around 10 hours is a plus for me. I'm no longer able to dedicate a lot of time to playing, and such shorter games give me the satisfaction of completing the title.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

It's very unstable, really stuttering, can't figure out why since graphics performance seems good in general, even on a fairly powerful PC. I've been stuck several times, had a Unreal engine crash and I've only played a couple of hours. Such a shame as it seems like there a good game behind all the technical problems.It would require a lot more polish and bug-fixing for me to actually recommend playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played firewatch and/or love gripping plots with mystery and adventure as well as 50's serial space adventures this game is for you, it has 7-9 hours of game play but personally I binged it in one sitting because the game kept me wanting to see what happens next, I most likely even missed some things through my playthrough. The game feels,looks, and plays great. there is very fun mechanics that really subtly help sink you in the immersion of the game. There are multiple choices throughout the game that make for great re-playability as well as multiple intriguing endings. I recommend this game strongly as a very impressive,fun, and beautifully creative piece of media that should be made more. PLAY IT

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent walkingsim like I haven't played in a long time, finished it in one sitting :) . Last time I got so engrossed by one was "Everybody's Gone to the Rapture".Story, narration, voice acting, animation & style & environments are top notch, and everything is teeming with details and storytelling, it's obvious that a LOT of care and craftsmanship went into this.Rhythm is good too if you can accept that a walkingsim isn't a high-octane jump-run-shoot experience, especially given that there's so much to see and learn everywhere.Minor minuses as of version 1.0.2 (Nov. 2023): a bit of shader stutter,  fixed in 1.0.3, and the final scene is strangely barebones compared to the rest of the game; feels like it was rushed. None of them game-breaking though, go buy this and support the devs :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, it's a narrative-focused game. There are choices, and those choices do affect parts of the story, but there is no action, no stealth sequences, no chase sequences, no combat. This is a game you play to explore the environment and hear the characters discuss plot elements. It does have some interactive elements, but they are quite sparse.The art style is fantastic and the plot compelling - it is, however, very similar to the book. So if you've read the book, you might not get much out of this game, unless you were keen on seeing the robots and ships in the book illustrated faithfully. If you have not read the book, I think this is worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others I was really looking forward to this game from the previews.  I wish I could say it  was worth the wait but this game was boring, clunky and confusing. If your looking for a story rich game with jaw dropping graphics and great interactivity, find another game.  I spent most of my time trying to figure out the controls and the rest figuring out what or where I was suppose to go. How they got this from the amazing previews I just don't know.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Frostpunk this game is not even close to Frostpunk or this war of mineThe game itself is good, but I was expecting a game where I would be rewarded or punished as a result of the choices I made, like Frostpunk, or a game where I could explore the world freely, like Long Dark or eldenring.Pros:+ You really experience the feeling of encountering the unknown.+ The atmosphere of the game is very nice.+ Still better than starfieldCons:- The game has a linear flow. There is no pros or cons to the actions you take because you don't have any choice.- The game limits you, you cannot explore the world freely,  To climb rocks or go down somewhere, you have to stop at a certain point- You actually feel like you're watching a movie, not like you're playing a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's an Atompunk Firewatch in space. I dare say with even better, and more voice work. Yasna really stands out, but everyone delivers. Bleak yet vibrant alien landscapes and a handcrafted world make everywhere you look seem like a postcard. At the end of the year, I needed a game I could immerse myself in without feeling stressed to compete, or "get better at" and this was it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: People will say its Firewatch in space. It is not. It has a similar gameplay but lacks all of which made Firewatch interesting for me. The game is very railroaded and it seems like none of your choices makes any difference in the game at all. The ideia of whats going on in the planet is very interesting, but the gameplay focus so much on other things that lead to nowhere. At no time the main story actually made me interested or suprised or frightened or emotive or anything. Bland game with great visuals and fine dub, but not worth the time investment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I can see this game not being for everyone, for it's an interactive cinematic experience more so than a game.With that being said, I found it pretty outstanding. From the retro-futuristic/astropunk art style to the amazing soundtrack/audio design, I was pleasantly surprised with this random purchase.If you're a fan of slow burn, hard sci-fi media with smart dialogue (accompanied with great voice acting), I think you'll find a gem with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It was interesting enough, but in no way worth $30. There's not really a "game" here so much as a very short story that you control the camera in. One casual play-through took almost exactly 8 hours. Yes, there are a couple multiple choices to be made that I'm sure make small changes to the story, but frankly there's just not enough here to justify the price.At 5-10$ I'd say it's worth the money. Anything more than that and you're paying for way more than you get.My biggest gripe, other than the lack of content per $ spent, is why in God's name would you put an invisible sprint meter in a "game" that has no combat, no high-stakes moments, no strategic or meaningful reason whatsoever to force the player to walk for a few meters after sprinting (and sprinting is being very generous, she never really gets above a light jog) for all of 10 seconds? It was infuriatingly tedious and served no purpose other than to slow you down. Maybe they were afraid people would finish the story in under 2 hours and get their refund if they didn't artificially draw things out with this mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game with a cool atmosphere and an adventurous story. It makes you feel like the space explorer of Cold War Era. Strong narrative with logic outcome. I would like to thank all people who involved in creation of this game and applaud them for respecting a player's intellect. Good job guys.With love and respect from Ukraine.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to start with this game. The breathtaking visuals, amazing plot, and relaxing soundtrack truly make it stand out. Let's start with the visuals: every aspect of this game is picture-worthy! The landscape is so captivating that I find myself exploring every nook and cranny of the map. The story is just as intriguing as the visuals, constantly leaving little breadcrumbs for you to pick up on. You can feel the developers' love for this game in every step you take. The game involves making many decisions, so the story can differ from person to person depending on how you react in certain situations. And of course, I couldn't end this review without mentioning the soundtrack. I love it, and it truly complements the game's vibe. I highly recommend buying this game!

There are no bugs whatsoever. From the story side : It was inspired by Stanisław Lem’s novel titled the same and is refreshing - not a shiny crismas tree, but more realistic sci fi so to speak and once again, I love it. Gameplay is slow(I killed the vibe because I always play the fastest way I can and haven’t experienced it fully) and the story is quite short compared to bigger productions, however I personally perceive this as an excellent way of saving people’s time and drawing their attention. Everything in this game is a testimony to professionalism. Oh, and the soundtrack - don’t even get me started. Peace!

The most distracting were the missing ground textures, this isuue was repeating across various levels.Gameplay wise there are some decisions that change the path to finish with different outcomes. These required save scumming but after one of the patches there's now Chapter select functionality.The presentation is very cool: visual style, music, voice acting.Recommended only on deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of Lem's writing, and I think the transition of his rather lengthy, relaxed writing style to the game format works brilliantly here. The visual and sound design are entirely in keeping with Lem's aesthetic, and it reminds you how prescient and talented he was. More like this, please.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, it build up the mystery and situation until all was revealed. The environment and voice acting was awesome too. A beautiful planet to look into, with great voices to accompany the story, along with the story.One thing I would like to see, is a chapter select after finishing the story, based on what you had done on the save used. _childDocuments_.review: Perfect walking story game. If you love games like Firewatch and need to scratch that itch try this one out.Firstly I did encounter a couple of bugs. Replay value is not going to be a high as Firewatch in my opinion.However there is an engaging story with beautiful visuals.Recommended!Things I loved:-The story (it's hard sci-fi)The style and visualsAmazing voice actors (English version)Great sense of just one more scene needed to progress the storyLength is about 9-10 hours (perfect for me)Things I didn't like:-Driving sections (sometimes), the view from the rover's isn't great, part of the journey is seeing the landscape, not just the floor in front of you.The save system. Not intuitive. You have 1 save which is updated as you go. However if you notice that you may have failed at an achievement, could I work out a way to get back to the time where I failed the achievement? no... You can then replay chapters but not the save points within the chapter.Some sections are unskippable, so if you do a restart it may take a while to get back to where you where.A few bugs, only one required a restart (fell through a floor and then nothing happened)You, as far as I know, can't rebind your middle mouse button doing the conversation selection choice. Choosing one sometimes means you miss out on looking at the object or speaking certain dialog. However in both times this was an issue for me, you should have been able to do both I think.As I said, recommended if you like story based adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: Stanisław Lem is one of my favorite science fiction authors of all time. While Solaris was my favorite of his works, The Invincible was right behind it. I was certainly intrigued to say the least when I heard that there was a video game adaptation of it. I hate to be that guy, but I do think the book was better. However, I do think this is a very good adaptation of material that I thought was more or less unadaptable; at least to a video game. And to be fair to myself, there isn't much  here.The Invincible is, to put it bluntly, a walking simulator. There are no puzzles, there is no item collecting, no combat outside of a single setpiece (and even then, it’s not really combat). You are just walking, and sometimes driving across this desert planet; all the while talking to an NPC on a spaceship in orbit above you. The only real “game” element beyond walking is choosing what to say and do, which will provide some narrative branching on occasion. This probably sounds very unappealing, and normally that’s exactly how I would feel about these types of games. Plus there are some legitimate grievances I have with what little gameplay there is; movement is slow and clunky, you can’t sprint and strafe, and there are invisible walls everywhere. But this game is so gorgeous, well written, and well acted that I found myself drawn deeply into it.From an art design perspective, this game nailed the atmosphere of the book. The technology the humans use looks like props from a 1960s sci-fi movie set. The planet itself is beautiful, and the game knows it. You can disable the HUD elements (which are already minimal in their own right) to take it all in for yourself. And there is a photo mode that you can enter at almost any time, so you can take screenshots of the scenery and make it your new desktop background like I did. The ships and landscape both look and feel immense as you walk through them. And I particularly like the artstyle of the comic book that serves as a recap of events as you play the game; the same artstyle which is used in the pictures that you can pick up and inspect while playing the game. The sound design doesn’t quite match the impressive quality of the visual design, but its still pretty good and is accompanied by a phenomenal soundtrack and excellent voice acting.Being a walking simulator, the dialogue and voice acting are vital for this game’s success, and Starward knocked it out of the park. All of the characters are so captivating it’s hard to turn the game off, especially Dr. Yasna. Conversations feel so natural in this game. While you are roaming around, Yasna will hum to herself or Novik will check in from time to time, and it’s paced out in an organic way that doesn’t get annoying. If there is a pause due to the player taking their time to respond, Novik will ask if Yasna’s still there and she’ll respond on her own while you’re making a dialogue choice, or if you choose to speak at all. And all of the performances are great, especially Yasna’s.The story itself is actually a prequel to the book, but it follows the same narrative beats and adds a bit of extra lore of its own. Much like the book, Dr. Yasna comes across the same mysteries, draws the same conclusions as the scientists in the book, and will come across similar setpieces and events. I think this is one thing that the game does better actually. In the book, the theory about the phenomenon on Regis III feels like it came out of the blue. But in the game, we see more evidence in support of it before the hypothesis is drawn. Despite being a prequel, there are multiple different endings that come about based on choices you make throughout the game, but mostly the final section. It provides you the opportunity to make a similar choice that was given to the book’s protagonist, which is cool to see. Some of the endings are very obviously not canon though if you really want to treat the two as being in the  same universe, but really, neither the book nor the game are about continuity; they are about the greater theme of discovery and contact with a completely alien phenomenon, and humanity’s response to it.The Invincible encapsulates everything I love about sci-fi. It’s smart, concise, deep, and boring. I love it. A $30 price tag might be pretty steep for a game that only took me around 6 hours to complete, but it’s definitely worth picking up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fascinating and stylish experience about a world where Analog technology characterizes your ability to interact and survive within it. The story is very thought provoking and the artwork is magnificent. Come and feel what it's like to be a scientist exploring a strange other world with fairly realistic interpretations of technology.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game had some decent graphics but it was not what I expected.  For the price, even at sale price, this was not worth the money.  I know it was based on a novel but I expected a bit more challenge in the game.  It was pretty simple and even though I finished it, it was a pretty disappointing game.  This is one I should have made a quick decision and got a refund.  I kept expecting it to become more challenging but it never happened.  Boring...
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is an excellent narrative driven, walking simulator, choice making, philosophical sci-fi game. And if that's a lot to say quickly, then tough. It's a great sci-fi game! I loved the world they built. Admittedly I've never heard of Stanislaw Lem, but if this is the sci-fi world he created, then it's amazing. Can't really say much because I don't want to spoil anything, but the voice acting and writing I found to be great - easy to follow and get along with and you can get a feel for the characters in the game and the world they inhabit. As for the game itself, the graphics are great, but could do with a little tweaking here and there. They were pushing my system a bit hard at times - especially the larger open areas. And one question I have for the developers is that, seeing as there's a comic book theme to the game (you'll know what I mean when you play it), why didn't they make this game cell-shaded? I feel it would have worked really well for this game! My only negatives to this game is that the walking can feel a little slow and clunky at times, especially when climbing over objects and the subtitles don't exactly match up with the dialog. But that's nitpicking. All in all, I give this game an... antimatter ray to the face, out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoyed this title, I saw it during a promotional video on Twitter and decided to pick it up.The game took me around 7 hours to beat and there is re-play value here, as there are multiple endings depending on the choices you make during the story.Voice acting is very well done and graphically this is a gorgeous game with surprises and twists as the story unfolds.If you don't mind walking simulators, I can definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I'll leave it overnight without refunding yet... The atmosphere and the music seem excellent, so much so that I thought: "What if this is another Subnautica-like masterpiece?" However the gameplay so far... Every action is an animation that you shake your leg through waiting for it to finish... Every interaction seems like it's prolonged for the sake of it... _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The invincible captures really well the atmosphere of Lem's work, while also having an original story that captures slowly. The music also helps transmitting the eerie tonePersonally I already read the invincible before playing this game, so I was somewhat expecting the themes, but nonetheless it was good to visualise the book's content with my eyes, other than imagine it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A short but enthralling story game where you explore an interesting and well-made golden age sci-fi setting. It's slow paced and mostly exploratory, which to myself is a breath of fresh air, and allowed to me get lost and appreciate the work the artists put into making this world—I'd be lying if I said I wasn't ogling over all the fun technology. The voice acting was good, and I enjoyed the characters. It took me a little over seven hours to complete my first playthrough. From what I understand, there is some replayability with multiple endings, but it's nothing exceptional. I held few gripes, the most notable to me was that sometimes dialogue can get interrupted as you come upon an event or scenario, and you miss out on what was being said. On launch, the ending I got was bugged, but as I understand it the developers are aware of the issue and actively looking to patch it.Overall, I found this game very enjoyable. I hope we get more games in settings like this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: After receiving the exterminatus order, a fleet with the appropriate weapons is sent to the planet.A simple shooting of the planet. A huge fleet of spaceships enters the orbit of the planet and shoots it with guns.  It has an exceptional psychological effect, but it often requires an incredible number of ships so that nothing alive remains so after the procedure is completed.Nuclear purge. The most "budget" option, often feasible by the forces available on the planet. The torpedo is an atmosphere scorcher. A large plasma torpedo filled with a chemical substance, under the influence of which the entire atmosphere of the planet begins to burn.  It is useful because it allows you to burn out the atmosphere simultaneously, without the risk of burning out the resulting combustible gas in parts. Cyclone torpedoes. Later development. High-power charges used to destroy life on the surface of the planet. Alternatively, two—stage charges using the melta effect to penetrate the crust of the planet and exploding in the deep layers for tectonic destabilization and tearing of the planet.Destruction by asteroids/moon. The most radical and expensive method is used when all the others do not help, or are impossible. For this purpose, special ships equipped with particularly powerful towing devices are used.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Great for any and all fans of Stanisław Lem's works. While full of references and easter eggs for anybody who knows his books, it presents a rich story and a philosophical conundrum much in the spirit of the source material for any player.I do however have to say it's a bit of a missed opportunity: it's a walking simulator, while with all the terrifying dangers present in the game it might have been a must-play horror akin to SOMA, without losing any of it's story, if only developed that way.Still, the game has everything a story focused walking simulator should have, plus stunning visuals, and a beautiful, beloved, and spine chilling setting provided by Poland's most acclaimed sci-fi author.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: First time in a looong time, I played a game in one sit down. If you like free roam games, or games you can play without the main story, this is not one of those games. You pretty much have to play through each chapter at a time. Took me about 7 hrs total but I took my time. Multiple endings makes you want to play the last chapter more than once. Rarely ever play story mode more than once. I'm a sucker for visuals and this defiantly gives you that stylized 70's Space Odyssey vibes. In short, worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, art direction, sound design and music! Well voice acted and really engaging to follow along with everything as you explore a visually striking alien world. I had a few issues with frame drops and glitches with ground textures (not sure if that's because it's not optimized for 4k, which i played it in) but, I consider those rather minor issues, and the atmosphere they've  created along with the unfolding narrative more than made up for it in my eyes!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A solid sci-fi mystery that serves as a prequel to the novel of the same name, The Invincible is a game that captures the spirit of exploring something unknown. In terms of gameplay, it can barely be called a game; it's essentially a visual novel told from the first person point of view, where you engage in more direct dialogue and make choices. I found some aspects of the game's final act a little bit headscratching, but overall, it's recommended if you're interested in experiencing a sci-fi story first hand; it's also worth noting that it's hard sci-fi, with characters that mostly sound and behave like scientists, that discuss scientific concepts, so tonally it'll feel different to most other sci-fi games that you've played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Setting the context: I was born in the 1970s therefore I read the original Lem book The Invicible as a kid and then re-read it many times since. I really liked it and was very excited to see the story come to life as a computer game.It is clear that this game is not for everyone - especially younger generations may not like the slow pace and lot of storytelling vs. less hot shooting actions.But for me this is perfect. The visuals are stunning and Regis III came to life just like I imagined in my mind many years ago.Congratulations for the developers for not letting modern times distract them so  they kept the mood of original story.Even if I know very well the original story the game's new viewpoint into the situation creates the curiosity and tension that is needed to remain always interested Voice acting is great and adds to the feeling a lot. If there is one wish to make: I truly hope the game will get an upgrade so it can be played in VR!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is not about the systems under its hood or fast reflexes. It's an immersive, interactive Sci-Fi story adapting a work from one of the most successful authors of the genre: Stanislaw Lem. The quality of the writing, especially for a video game, is inspiring. The visuals are detailed, appropriately alien, and expressive. Numerous opportunities for player choice lets you mold the protagonist's (Dr. Yasna, Biologist) personality through the actions (and reactions) you make to the rich and constantly developing story. The devs have done an outstanding job crafting a fulfilling experience that ruminates on big ideas and pushes the player to make tough decisions. There is on-foot and vehicular travel, but prospective players ought to be made aware that this is not a fast-paced game by any stretch of the imagination. When I played the demo I thought that the pace may be too slow for my liking, but the level of immersion is just too strong for me to resist; so much so that I often found myself savoring time spent simply sitting still or sauntering around a point of interest while I listen to (and participate in) the unraveling of the mysteries on Regis III.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game, absolutely incomparable to the trash of contemporary pop culture! I mean for example illogical and incoherent 'Mass Effect: Andromeda'.I highly recommend Invincibe – the gameplay is excellent, and the story is engaging, the topic is attractive and from perfect not used angle. I really see no downsides (I was blocked by only 2 collisions).As a game designer, ladies and gentlemen, I congratulate you on a wonderful production!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: enjoyable exploring gem, visually beautiful, great dialogue and selecting the right things to say is key. The retro-futuristic feel of this, like an old 50's movie is very convincing and fun to experience. Had a hard time seeing at first so turn your gamma up. The bad part is you cant walk anywhere you like or jump, no weapons so far and would be great if had more survival items needed and or more dangerous circumstances. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: While the atmosphere and retro-futuristic look are great the novelty quickly wears off and the landscape becomes bland, especially in the playable area.The characters in the game are quite boring and lack much depth or development and I never found myself attached to any of them. Even by the end of the game I had no concern for the fate of anyone.Conversation between Novik and Yasna is often not captivating at all. If Rohytra's gun had been functional I'd have shot myself with it to avoid having to listen to Novik's annoying, ceaseless comments.Much of the gameplay was spent traversing empty and dead landscapes that you've already seen, only to reach an objective or destination that is hardly more engaging than the walk/drive that got you there.Other than discovering a few documents, the game gives no value or reward to doing any extra exploration that I found.If I could make the decision again I'd watch a playthrough and save $30.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I love the style and the story, and even we rarely meet other 'complex' npc, we'll never feel lonely because there will always be someone to talk to, and even this guy is on the radio, the way voice actor talk is very nice, it doesn't feel like a boring talkonly one thing I can comment : I expect it should be less gravity so we can jump in slow motion like people do on moon, but walking part is a bit uncomfortable to me, just a bit tho
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic story! The visuals are stunning, and the walking simulator experience keeps the tension high. There isn't a ton of action, but the engaging dialogues will keep you hooked—so be ready to listen. The walking speed is just right, none of that frustratingly slow pace that can ruin the immersion. Plus, it's short enough to keep you entertained without dragging on. You'll love it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A very good story-based game with high quality audio/visuals. Great use of material-based rendering, with a unique retro-scifi aesthetic. An enjoyable mystery for the most part.But... the ending(s) are unsettelingly abrupt. Feeling like perhaps they didn't have time to finish the game or something. Compared to "Still Wakes the Deep" which has a rich and emotional ending.  The difference is Still Wakes has almost no agency... I think but one ending (hope I'm not wrong on that) where as The Invincible has multiple.  You will likely feel, by the end, that a lot of threads were just left dangling and there was no real satisfying conclusion.Oddly you can play the whole game and never see "The Invincible".  For being the game's namesake, it can play a remarkably small part in the whole thing.But, its all about the journey, and it does this very well.  So well, in fact, that its worth a play-thru for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Oof. This is a tough one to rate. The story is captivating, the atmosphere really outstanding and the game design and cinematography is gorgeous. You gotta be aware though that this is a very, very linear walking simulator. All interactions are just "click this", "click that". There are 11 endings and it's cool that you decisions make a difference, but that doesn't change the fact that's it's just an interactive movie. That is hardly to criticize, it's just the category this game falls into, but even then some design decisions feel unnecessarily burdensome:* The walking speed: Wow. Okay, you have a heavy space suit and low stamina, so yeah it makes sense, that you walk slow and only can do slow sprints for a very short time ... but still.... ITS SO SLOW. Luckily you can use Cheat Engine to increase that, see [1] below. * The dialogue skipping: You can only fast forward through dialogues and only some of them. That means you literally hear a fast forward sound, which takes its own time and doesnt really feel like skipping. That is a point because: * The decision tree: In the last chapter you have a veeery long dialogue with decisions that weigh heavy on the ending. So if you wanna play for different endings you're going to go through this a couple of times .... and you can skip NOTHING of it. Just prepare yourself to sit throught 10-15 minutes of the same dialogue again and again, because:* Alt+Tab pauses the game. So no alternative to you watching the last dialogue over and over* Even though there are mutliple endings .... they all feel flat. You have this intriguing story arch, building up nicely and then it's just like "then there's this" and credits roll. Really? I dont know. I feel cheated.* I finished the first ending in 6 hours (without walking speed hack and not even rushing it) which is pretty short for the price tag. I don't really mind but it's worth mentioningThat just clouds the overall experience. It's still an outstanding game and if you are even the least into sci-fi novels or movies, this is a must, but it feels ... way worse then it should be. I'm giving it a thumbs down, because it made me sad to see all this potential of a fantastic game unfold to a bitter experience when the credits roll. I don't think it's really fair to the game, but the overall ratings are still so high, that I'm sure it won't make a difference. I wish steam had a "its cool, but" rating option.[1]
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is more a three dimensional graphic novel than a game. The planet is very pretty and the story is story is immersive at key points but some scenes do drag on. The slow moments combined with the limited and lethargic movement you have to traverse the planet can be boring at times and left me wanting a hard copy of the graphic novel to read at a decent pace rather than trudging through this slowly acted out 3d experience.I'd recommend The Invincible if you like a slower paced, visually pleasing experience. I can appreciate some will find this enjoyable. If you're looking for a bit more excitement and freedom from limited controls/paths, then The Invincible may not be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I like the ascetic of this game and it carries its mystique well. The set pieces of the game are part of the world rather than a spectacle in of themselves and the player choices seem to have a decent effect on the course of the game. The game was very performant and the engine seems very smooth even though I've got an old CPU on a decent video card. The pacing of the game is stable guiding you to the horizon and I was only confused where to go once when a forcefield wasn't where I was supposed to go like the others before them.  All in all the game is fairly short but I had an entertaining time all the way through because I didn't put it down until the wee hours wanting to see what happened next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A narrative experience based on a Stanislaw Lem story; I hope we can all agree this is a stamp of approval for the narrative, so I won't spoil the plot and twists. As for the game itself, it's a beautifully done walking sim. The graphics is great, the visual style of Regis III and especially its sky is great too, the controls are responsive, and everything just clicks together nicely. The game also has excellent timing: it ramps up gradually but unwaveringly, and speeds up right at the moment when you're thinking of calling it quits for today. So if you can set aside a long afternoon it makes sense to finish the game in a single sitting (about 6 hours). I really wanted this review to be longer but I'm hard pressed to find any flaws. Perhaps the only slightly underwhelming aspect of the games are the endings -- I won't spoil them but I got one of the good ones and googled the rest. On the surface they look very similar, but there is a difference that may decide the fates of galaxies (or not); this might be a great hook for a sequel but strangely, not all endings (even not all "good" ones) mention it at all! Anyway, this is a minor grip, and the game is definitely worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't hate the Invincible, but i felt it did not deliver the "Firewatch in space" experience i've seen it described as.The voice acting, visuals and story were all good but the game itself is not very well made:-Dialogue frequently gets cut off when you reach a scripted sequence.-Exploration is stiff and limited: i feel like this should've been a telltale-style game rather than a walking sim.-Some scenes have awkward "pauses" where the player character is stuck in place and nothing happens for 10 or 20 seconds. Sounds minor but it kills immersion, which is the bread and butter of games like this.-An important element of the story is the conflict between two factions, but neither of them are ever fleshed out or characterized very well.I would have preferred far fewer endings if it meant the game had a more polished and engaging campaign.If you like hard sci fi, wishlist this game and buy it once it gets some bug fixes and a sale. I've been very negative, but i still think there's a lot to like about The Invincible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is an immersive, narrative based game based on the novel by Stanislaw Lem one of the greats of 20th century science fiction.  It follows the experiences of Yasna, a research biologist who is part of a survey team awoken from cryogenic sleep for an unscheduled visit to a strange planet full of anomalies. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: games like this make me sad that there is no option for a neutral review, though i understand that such measure would cause trouble in the review system considering how important it is for the games success.from the art visual standpoint it would be a solid 4/5 with some locations and the style of ingame imersive interfaces taking a 5.music and sound design is very good. it manages it's job perfectly as for me.game pace in terms of a walking sim game is also pretty good. the tempo at which story events unfold seemed natural and captivating.story and worldbuilding. i have to make a disclamer. the scifi space travel setting is sorta okay for me, but this game draws very strong inspiration from Stasik Lem and his creative work and i am a very strong antagonist of his description of the place of humanity in the universe. basically i read some of his books and i don't like them. all of the stuff what he wrote gives off a very "humanity is just a grain of sand in the cosmos of space" and this game constantly barrages you with his philosophical interpretations of the human nature and man's uselessness and insignificance in the face of eternity. SO if this is your cup of tea and you like this existential mindf**kery - this is the game for you. unfortunately or maybe fortunately i could only get the positive vibe from the visual, sound and technical (in terms of story pacing) aesthetics, but not from the general underlying idea that the game is based on.tldr. the game is a nice walking sim with a spice of a very certain futuristic existential dread, that i personally am not a fan of, but maybe you are.

_childDocuments_.review: + Amazing scenery, beautiful graphics+ Nice voice acting+ Overall compelling and catchy story+ Satisfying visual atompunk-like and retrofuturistic aesthetics+ Some moderate choices in dialogues and actions- Small, non-gamebreaking, but annoying bugs and freezes- Sometimes junky narrative - weird cuts mid dialogue, long pauses between and sudden cuts- Very slow pace both for movement and exploration- Even though game gives you some room to explore alternative paths - it's mostly hollow and non-rewarding- The ending feels very dull as we don't really see any consequences to our actions no matter what path you chooseOverall I'd say the game is worth playing once to enjoy the beauty of Regis III and retrofuturistic aesthetics

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I can describe this is "Firewatch in space", though it's longer than Firewatch.
