_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a captivating journey through the mysteries of space and the complexities of human exploration. As a scientist stranded on the hostile planet of Regis III, I found myself immersed in a world filled with stunning visuals, intriguing characters, and a narrative that kept me guessing until the very end.Let's start with the graphics, which are undeniably impressive. The art style is semi-realistic, with bright colors and detailed landscapes that truly bring the world of Regis III to life. The skyboxes are particularly noteworthy, offering breathtaking views of shooting stars, distant planets, and a looming sun. There were moments when I found myself simply stopping to admire the beauty of my surroundings, a testament to the game's attention to detail. And for those interested in capturing these moments, there's even a photomode available, although I personally didn't use it.As someone who hasn't had the opportunity to read the book The Invincible, I can't speak to how faithfully the game adheres to its source material. However, I can say that the story presented in the game is engaging and deceptive in all the right ways. What I initially thought was a simple mission to find my lost crewmates quickly evolved into a much deeper and more compelling narrative. I particularly appreciated the game's focus on science, with Yasna's commentary on the delicate balance of planetary ecosystems serving as a thoughtful reminder of humanity's impact on the universe.The audio in The Invincible is also top-notch, with a soundtrack that perfectly complements the game's atmosphere. While the voice acting is limited in variety, the performances are excellent, and I found myself growing attached to characters like Yasna and The Astrogator (Novik). The dialogue choices are well-executed, offering plenty of opportunities for players to shape their own story. I especially appreciated the game's handling of branching choices, with the most significant decisions reserved for the end of the game and the option to change your mind based on new information.In terms of gameplay mechanics, The Invincible strikes a delicate balance between narrative-driven storytelling and player agency. While the mechanics are minimal, the game provides you with a few tools and the freedom to use them as you see fit. I appreciated the ability to explore off the beaten path, although the climbing mechanics felt somewhat restrictive at times. Additionally, the limited view of the Rover made navigation in certain sections a bit challenging, but overall, the game did a good job of guiding me where I needed to go.In conclusion, I found The Invincible to be a thoroughly enjoyable experience from start to finish. With its engaging story, stunning visuals, and immersive sound design, it's a game that I would highly recommend to any fan of narrative-driven adventures. And with a runtime of approximately 6 hours, it's the perfect length for a single playthrough.Rating: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I had i dilemma if recommend this game. In the end, I do recommend it but with some notes.The game looks very good and successfully builds an atmosphere of mystery. You feel you experiencing something alien and incomprehensible for humans. Storytelling through the environment has been done greatHowever, for a game where dialogues are very important, they are mediocre. It's clear that the Firewatch was the inspiration but they didn't manage to write equally good dialogues and build relations with Novik. The only character that I cared about was Rohytra.Voiceovers seemed to me very flat and emotionless.There are some odd design decisions that were easy to avoid. Like when you have to walk the same path a few times with not much narrative meaning.Also, a map is a physical object that needs to be lit but the surroundings are often dark and the character doesn't have a flashlight (which would be generally very useful).There are some big areas where there is not much to do and after all, exploring them is a waste of time.Despite all of that I enjoyed the game and I recommend it. It's just a shame it's not better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A great TV show in which you have to press a few buttons or drive a rover to watch the next episode.Honestly the story and visuals (when not bugging out) are incredible and fit right into the Lem sci-fi style, it's just unfortunate the actual gameplay is utterly pointless busywork (and painfully slow at that). Not to mention rather the cringeworthy Londoner accent and performance by the main character (see Melville from Talos Principle 2 for something more believable), however, Novik (a consistent secondary character) was perfectly performed and really held the story up throughout.Worth a buy, but maybe on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.  The story was very compelling.  There was a constant sense of mystery and it made me want to keep playing to see what would happen next.  The characters were well thought out and the voice acting was on target for the different people in the story.  The world that was created for the story was not just immersive it drew me in wanting to explore more of the place.   The artistic style was inspired and it really helped define this game and made it stand out.  Everything was well thought out, deliberate, and fit together nicely.  The developers really put in the time and creativity and did not cut corners or rush it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it a lot. If you like slower pace, exploration and scifi stories, this is a game for you. There are multiple choices to make, which, I assume, might change the story. Not sure about this though. My first playthrough took 14 hours. I will go back at some point and try different choices as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A must if you enjoy reading hard sci-fi novels from the 60's. For me this replicates the atmosphere of these novels to an amazing degree, from the look/operation of the technology to the slightly archaic/stilted dialog. The voice acting is good and graphically the planet landscape is out of this world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I had a hard time believing someone would encapsulate what I loved about Lem's books in a videogame, given how many franchises (adaptations or not) fell flat due to corporate greed, incompetence and overall poor state of gaming industry.Because of many personal doubts, I pirated the game and somehow found myself past a full playthrough in one sitting. This review and thus proof of purchase is my final recommendation. Looking forward to Polish voiceover.Thank you, Starward Industries, for delivering such an invigorating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely wonderful game! I'm a lifelong reader of Stanislaw Lem; he's one of the most ironic and witty scientific writers out there. The moment I saw there was a game based on his writing, I had to get it.I have not been disappointed. The game is atmospheric and immersive like few AAA titles these days end up being. It really gives you a feel for being in the circumstances the story portrays.And what a story! The writing is mature and solid, and the characters are all well-defined. Your perspective on things is quite clear, and the extent to which you are or are not informed about what's going on is always present.The interface is absolute genius; the game plays like an adventure game/visual novel in some ways, but also makes use of tools and equipment and the 3D Unreal engine adeptly, so you always feel like you're in the game, playing it, not just clicking pixels on a screen. The designers for this game have really broken new ground here, leaving titles like Fort Solis (also a good game, but far more ambiguous to handle) in the dust.I'm really looking forward to playing this all the way through! Have no idea how long it is, but I've already gotten my money's worth in the brief time I've had with the game. It is truly sui generis. I look forward to further work Starward Industries will do. They've accomplished so much with so little so far, and in many ways this game is far more gripping and tightly focused than Starfield. Open World can be fun, but this kind of directed play feels far more involving in every way. You forget about worrying about all the usual technical things while running the game, and just get into the game, and before you know it, half a day has passed. Yes, it's that kind of rare game.Stanislaw Lem would be proud!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: A great interactive story, if a bit of a slow burn (even at such a short length). Graphics and music are stunning. This is a must try for scifi, retrofuturist aesthetic and narrative-heavy games enthusiasts -- especially if you've already played your share of point-and-clicks/walking sims and don't necessarily require to shoot your way out of every situation to have fun with a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: this is just a boring convoluted mess. The challenge is making sure you press the right buttons, since the icons and button choices are horribly inconsistent then they put timers on some actions which is incredibly stressful for some learning disabilities. It's just pretty frustrating and then when you can finally move, I find very little to motivate me in the game 'mechanics'. I can't even jump down a hole and die. I don't feel any 'gameplay' here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good. I normally don't play this type of games and I'm in awe. I bought it because of a lecture on Pyrkon. I read the book and it was fenomenal. It's hard to believe that it's so old and yet still a good scifi novel. Same goes to the other ones like "Return from the stars". I wish it would get a game as well. Back to the game I stop frequently to do photos. This Eerie planet has immence beauty. Well you will have to see for yourself. The only thing that bugs me is that sometimes its difficult to interact with objects using a gaming pad. Same goes with walking. She gets stuck in places. Rarely but still. Apart from that the game is 11/10. Sooooo goood
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: We need more games like this.Very much a Sci-fi version of 'Firewatch'. It's a great chill out game to soak up some story and beautiful visuals. I'm in my 30's and sometimes I don't want to play fast-paced online multiplayer games. Sometimes, I want an interactive experience and this is just the ticket.Can't wait to continue playing this and I really do hope we get more of the same in the future as it's a space in the game market that needs filling! (no pun intended).
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Takes a little longer than a Lem book. Gets philosophical and can drag -- just like a Lem book. It has all the retro feel, multidisciplinary dive, proposals for research and inventions (particularly the book crystals hah), frustrated hypotheses, and obsession with machines and mortality. Loved it all.Great way to celebrate Polish Constitution Day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Starts ok, then down hill.The visuals are quite nice. Aside from that, this game is tedious and vague. I didn't know what was happening half the time, the story is revealed but at multiple points it made no sense to me. This is 100% a walking sim with some of the worst driving sections I have ever experienced.The big problem with walking sims, if the story isn't good, and the dialogue is bad (these are some dumbass scientists), there's no point let alone any fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for a while. Purchased it for 30€ on release day which I think is a good price for a newly released game. I wouldn't pay more than that for a single player game. The game has very nice visuals and an interesting story although I think the story potential wasn't reached. The best part of the game is that you are always in communication and interaction with a certain scientist which makes the game so much more interesting and you never get the feeling that you are alone. I wish there was more to the game once you finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game with a space extraterrestial atmosphere.Landscapes, soundtrack, presentation - I liked everything.I don't like sandboxes, so I like the linearity of the game.You should like the game if you are a fan of deep science fiction.Please, do not look for similarities with the original source - the literary work of Stanislaw Lem. A game is a game, and a novel is a novel, each of them is beautiful in its own way.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth 30€ at all. I finished the game in almost 7 hours with "Good ending" and there is no extra to do nor any sidequest to complete. If you want to play scifi space walking sims-like i can definetly recommend "Breathedge" aka "game with space chicken" - that game is almost 40 hours for 1 playthrough to complete!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's an great story and some beautiful sights (sadly with some very visible reapiting textures at times) and amazing looking objects, but despite that I just cannot recommend this as a game. Every part of this that you actually play, doesn't really feel good, everything feels unnecessarily slow and not very pleasant. I wish I could recommend this game because there is clearly some love that went into making this, but at full price there is to much missing to make this a complete game. I would say only get this game if you get a really good discount or you just want a good story and don't care about the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: First game that really made me feel like I'm playing a sci-fi novel. Visually very beautifully crafted aswell!Beware though, it is a very, very slow paced story-driven experience. The narrative will feed you bits of information and leave you wondering and puzzling together theories about how it all fits into a bigger picture on your own. Things develop rather slowly, with a good chunk of walking - as is expected on a vast, desolate planet.So far it has left me eager to play more - progressing and watching the story unfold is a blast!
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be good if it didn't crash on 3 different PC's with errors, crashes on a 3080ti, 4060 and Z1 extreme on a legion go. All with the same error codes when they crash, I am going to assume it is not my end having an issue. I wish I could finish this game, but the crashing makes this game unplayable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a serious gamer and dip into them for occasional escape. I loved Firewatch and feel that people that like that game will also like this one. The visuals are stunning, I love the Atom-Punk aesthetic, and the voice acting is great. There are no real problems/puzzles to be solved, much like Firewatch, it is an enjoyable walking simulator, like being in a movie. Sorry to compare this game to another, but as a casual gamer I spend a lot of time searching for games like this. Total escapism, great storytelling and incredible visuals. A beautiful adventure, I recomend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I tire of games that purport to feature a competent, qualified female protagonist then immediately turn them into a useless, hand-holding-required, constantly-needs-a-pep-talk, generally whiny character that constantly needs savouring by others at the first sign of conflict or distress. Give me Ripley. Give me Dana Scully. Give me Leia. Give me the borg queen. Stop giving me "highly qualified" female leads with the temerity and mental fortitude of a 13 year old child. It's more demeaning than not featuring them at all. Other than that, it's a boring walking simulator. Only the passingly-good graphics save it. You'll be far, far more amazed walking around The Talos Princple 2, and that'll give you things to do that are worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, just not ready to be played yet.Lots of graphical glitches, frame drops are immense and frequent, you can also get soft locked right now.- 𝘼𝙑𝙊𝙄𝘿 𝘼𝙇𝙇 𝙏𝙊𝙂𝙀𝙏𝙃𝙀𝙍 𝙄𝙁 𝙔𝙊𝙐 𝙂𝙀𝙏 𝙈𝙊𝙏𝙄𝙊𝙉 𝙎𝙄𝘾𝙆 𝙀𝘼𝙎𝙄𝙇𝙔 -- Voice acting is great!- The ambiance is calming, sad, and a little unnerving. Which I quite enjoyed.- The environment is really pretty- Dialog is a little too on the nose at times.- Walking speed is terribly slow and the mechanic of running out breath doesn't really seem to serve a purpose so I just found it irritating.- The game runs terribly. _childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Fasten your seatbelt! Inviciable is an awesome Sci-fi world. I love the story telling with your interactions in the world and the Comic strips. I do really enjoy the atompunk style of the game. I was a bit underwhelmed on the grand finale that they do a great job building up to. If there was a bit more at the end credits I would have given this 10/10 but because it lacks my score is 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call this a game, and there aren't really any puzzles.  It's more of an interactive story where you are occasionally given the opportunity to choose a dialog line you explore the mysteries of a planet.   Pros:* compatible with UEVR ... this game looks fantastic in VR* same setting as the book "The Invincible" by Stansislaw Lem (of Solaris fame).  It's not the book, but if you've read it you will appreciate this.* gorgeous retro sci-fi designCons:* game mechanics are not always intuitive* fairly linear ... but so was Half Life Alyx.  This just doesn't have the actionIf you want to relax, this is a buy.  If you want a puzzle or some action you might be bored.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much a serious, sci-fi linear narrative with little in the way of playful game mechanics. It executes on the narrative beats well and tells a compelling story from the eyes of the era the original story was written in. It's very heavy on dialog with beautiful art direction.Recommended if these are the kinds of games you're into. Don't go into expecting a horror game, exploration game or anything with action/mechanical gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: After this game I tried the other big walking sim -- Firewatch. Well that one left me bored and cringed, The Invincible kept me engaged and interested. That said, I'm also into hard sci fi and the themes brought up by this game are much more interesting to me than the middle aged man escapism, even if I am a middle aged man. In any case, The Invincible is a must have for sci fi fans. 60s retrofuturism is great and I've really reconnected with the Lem's work. Good game, am playing again(on steam this time)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Aby bolo jasno. Doporučujem bez akýchkoľvek pochybností. Hlavne ak máte radi pomalšie hry, milujete hard sci-fi. Skôr mi to príde naozaj ako hrateľný komiksový román. Vizuálne krásna grafika, nepoužívam foto režim, ale v tejto hre som musel. Zvuky super. Príbeh je excelentný s viacerými koncami a vetví sa aj v priebehu hry.  Neodsýpa expresne rýchlo, skôr sa lenivo vlečie. Toto môže niekomu vadiť a s pár minoritnými chybami. Ako nemožnosť preskakovať dialógy, ktoré ste už videli a  nemožnosť pohybu kým neskončí skriptovaný rozhovor  proste niekedy frustruje. Niekde textúry z blízka (pod lupou) by mohli o chlp lepšie aby sa z krásnych stali fantastické.Ale tieto slabšie  momenty nahradzujú dych berúce scény a herné momenty, ktoré  je dopredu škoda vyzrádzať.V každom prípade podporte.To be clear. I recommend it without any doubts. Especially if you like slower games, love hard sci-fi. Rather, it really feels like a playable comic novel to me. Visually beautiful graphics, I don't use photo mode but in this game I had to. Sounds great. The story is excellent with multiple endings and it branches throughout the game as well.  Doesn't go by express fast, rather drags lazily. This may bother some and with a few minor bugs. Like the inability to skip dialogue you've already seen and the inability to move until a scripted conversation ends just frustrates at times. Somewhere the close-up textures (under a magnifying glass) could be a hair better to take the beautiful ones from beautiful to fantastic.But these weaker moments are made up for by breathtaking scenes and gameplay moments that it's a shame to give away up front.By all means, support. (deepl transalted)
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I like the narrative side of the game. The graphics are nice too. I think the character could stand to not run out of breath after 2 meters event though it is stated that the gravity is lower on the planet. Also, i wanted to explore a lot, but sometimes the path i took thinking it's the wrong path, so i can explore, turned out to be the right path and i was locked out of the other path choices. I am talking about walking paths here. The game gives us a semi-open world to explore, but limits us greatly in exploration.Another thing that annoyed me is the frequency at which Novik contacted me for "Stat Update". It would be better id it was much less frequent or off until some secret trigger is activated.Other than that, the game is good. There are 11 endings including variations which is an ok amount. The gameplay is relatively simple and keeps the immersion intact.All in all, i think the game is worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the game is great: of course i suggest strongly to read the novel before playing because sometimes the text can be confusing.The artwork is good as well, the planet is fascinating.There are some tech problems with the texture of the sand.The gameplay is a walking simulator. Given that I cannot raccomand this game anyway because it's very (extremely) slow. Also the price tag is set quite high.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game in the sense that it has no intricate puzzles and you don't need to kill thousands of NPC's to go to the story. It is more like an interactive movie/tv serial. It explains to you a story but it is narrated in a way you must interact with the environment in order to know the end.Now, that said, I am greatly surprised of how well is it done and how great this way of explaining stories it. Overwelmingly possitive, in my view.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: It's an interactive walking sim with heavy weight on your decisions, which makes the game either short and somewhat disappointing or complete and quite pleasing. BUT: the decisions to take to uncover the whole mystery and to push the story forward are rather obvious.It is a pity that there are no parallel storylines, just quicker endings or very short detours; for me, there is no urge to replay the game. Get it for less than 10 {currency}, then I'm sure it's worth the time and thoughts you get out of it.WARNING: Stay on the "gameplay path", so to speak, or your fun gets diminished by long walks back, getting stuck in (metallic or rock) objects, having to reload or deal too long with the bad controls in certain situations. Don't try to push the limits to find something hidden; it isn't there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a promising game in terms of storytelling, but not worth it at all.The game perfectly captures the eeriness of exploring an unknown planet. The scenery is vast, empty and eerie. As you progress through the game, you learn more and more about the planet, possible life on the planet, and what happened to the people that were here. This is done quite nicely.The downside is that 99% of the gameplay is a very poorly made walking simulator. It is hard to know which direction to go, input is clunky and you often don't know what to do or which button to press. It can also be very slow. I have had quite a few moments where i wanted to just keep walking and characters in the game are encouraging me to do so, but i just have to wait or continue a (at times pointless and whiny) dialogue.By far the most interesting and well done part of the game is the story. I personally find extraterrestrial life and the limits of life (can machines be alive?) a very interesting topic within sci-fi, and this game tells a very nice story within that theme. Unfortunately, I found some of the hints to be much more obvious than the in-game characters. I was often a few steps ahead in understanding the mysteries that are central in the game. Some of the things I've noticed, have never been mentioned in game at all, which is pretty disappointing. Perhaps some of my questions would be answered if I replayed the game and made different choices. I'm not sure, but it did seem like at some points in the story you can make decisions that affect the rest of the game. However, since most of the gameplay is a very boring and frustrating walking simulator, I'm not going to do a second playthrough. I have played about 6 hours and it felt like 60 hours. I really want to like this game, but I honestly can't. I should also mention there are many fps drops and stutters, but those didn't bother me too much.Storytelling: 7/10 Nice story, but slow at timesGameplay 1/10 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ walking sim, clunkyArtwork: 6.5/10 Nicely captured the eeriness of a (mostly) empty planet, other artworks were fine too, but not very specialPrice: 1/10 Even on sale I paid over 20 euros for 6 hours of gameplayOverall: 3/10 The story is nice and that's about it. I haven't read the book, but it's probably better than playing this game if you are interested in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I liked it, it's a walking simulator with great visuals and cool story.There were quite a few confusing situations though.. My main complain is: everything looks like a path you can go, but you never know where you hit the invisible wall and where you not. Or which door from 2 identical looking  ones will open, when you approach it and which not. stuff like that. Or you get instruction like "Follow this road" or "follow this transport" - but there's nothing with such names on the map, so you just guessing what could that mean, periodically get out because the visibility in rover is awful to top it off.  Couple of times some events were not triggered automatically and I got stuck just running around like idiot because there was nowhere to go, just to see those events triggered immediately after reloading from the checkpoint.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: is an adaptation of the vintage sci-fi novel of the same name.  The book is pretty darn good, and you can tell the devs were fans.  The game follows the big points of the novel pretty well (namely the examination of what exactly could constitute as "alien life"), while still providing some good twists to keep anyone who has read the book on their toes.Besides obviously being based on a novel, the game also tries to capture the vibes of older sci-fi movies.  Theres a contemplative and colorful style to the game that harkens back to the fantastic and philosophical greats of the 60s and 70s.  The characters are great and I don't think there was a single one I disliked.  And despite being a walking simulator, there's still a lot to do: lots of nooks and crannies to explore, lots of dialogue choices that ripple throughout the game, and even some brief combat sequences if you play your cards right.And playing it with a fever was literally a fever dream, I highly recommend the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game. The story is amazing, enough to make me want to read the original novel. The scenery will take your breath away, at times just ignoring the story for a moment to take it all in. Having worked with the Unreal engine in the early days, they keep pushing the boundaries of this engine. Anyway, the music score is top-notch, the voice acting engaging, and the player interaction well done. This, is another hidden gem amongst all the flotsam and jetsam in gaming these days.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I usually enjoy walking sims, but I found this one to be extremely slow and with little to no interaction outside of walking and dialogue. I also think it's too long for what it offers. It's also a bit buggy and very clunky in terms of mechanics (the walking/running in a walking sim shouldn't feel like it does in this game). Also, in a game with multiple choices, endings and a chapter select feature... How is it possible there isn't a way to always skip extremely long dialogue to just test other options and endings? If you want to test different outcomes you will have to replay long portions of the game and listen to the same lines of dialogue over and over. I find this to be a huge miss.Is it a good story? Yes. Is it a good game? Well... It's not a game, it's a slow, interactive audio book with added 3D visuals... If I just wanted a story to read I could actually just read the novel it's based on.That said, I'd still give it a soft 7 because I can see the passion that went into it, the style, the mystery... and recommend it to huge fans of sci-fi and story/dialogue-centered games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic and well-crafted. The image quality varies from superb to somewhat less impressive and roughly rendered.I’ve been playing for 4 hours now and it’s enjoyable because you can make decisions that actively influence the course of the game. It gives you the feeling of having an impact. For instance, do I give my partner my oxygen bottle and risk seeking help without it, or do I give him nothing? You find out the outcome later. I think it’s brilliantly done. The style is also cool and I’d love to see more games in this style.I just wish they had made it in UE5 because of Lumen and Nanite, which would have suited the game perfectly. Unfortunately, it ended up being just UE4 and no ray tracing.Even Reshade Pathtracing doesn’t work because the depth buffer is never in sync with the actual image, but slightly offset.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This games graphics and atmosphere are gorgeous. The landscape of Regis III is incredibly versatile and varied, with amazing efforts on detail. It really feels like you are on an unknown alien planet. So far, I had a blast with the game. It reminds me a lot about the "Alien" universe, which is a good thing. I won't spoil anything, but the things that go on on Regis III are very mysterious and if you are as curious as I am, then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I say if you love atmospheric, mysterious, well-written narrative games, you will most likely love this game.It *is* slow - for those looking for action, this is not it. This is an exploration walking sim, with lots of dialogue. You're essentially playing a novel - good or bad, that's up to you, but I found the writing to be engaging, the story mysterious, and the plot moving along at a pace to always keep me interested.And choices matter! With *11* different endings, what you choose to do, can really change the outcome. And there were plenty of hard decisions and choices, sometimes I really had to stress about which was the 'best' option, because honestly, so much of the time there just isn't one.The sound and music were absolute top notch, and the environments and graphics were some of the best I've seen in a long, long time. You'll be stopping constantly to whip out photo mode for the view, or to get a shot of the amazing retro-futuristic tech broken down in the sand.So bottom line, if you're looking for a slower game heavy with mysteries and story, that looks and sounds amazing, don't sleep on this. Great job devs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: So I ordered the book "The Invincible" and I will also start to replay this gem multiple times in the future to get some of the missing endings. It really is, indeed, a cool adventure. The art style is really beautiful and will also hold up in the future and they really nailed that Atom Punk hard sci fi feeling, so the atmosphere really hits one.The conversations with the Astrogator keeps it all relatively fresh in the open environment, so that one doesn't get bored that fast.Only negatives are that climbing feels sometimes too restrictive and general movement with the vehicle could be a tad faster. The rest is to be expected with the setting (slow character with the suit and sometimes too big environments with just the landscape around one, but they are beautiful to look at).I can definitely say that it feels like a 9/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric narrative adventure game set in a retro sci-fi universe.  The game looks great. The desolate wasteland is well depicted and while it is not as diverse as for example the desert in Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak, it still has different sets of biomes. The technology is distincttly retro-futuristic and a mix of an old school robots with fairly grounded vehicles. Any interaction is disctintly tactile, with levers, knobs and switches. Music is mostly ambient and inobtrusive. Voice acting is excellent, a necessity given the limited cast of speaking characters and the amount of dialogue.  The gameplay is limited to atmospheric exploration and some fairly simple interactions. The story can branch depending on decisions made during the game.  The story serves as a sort of prequel to a cold-war era sci-fi novel The Invincible by Stanislaw Lem. Since I have read the book in the past, I already knew the big secret of planet Regis III (as much as it can be known). Even so the story worked very well for me. Just instead of gradual exploration and mystery turning into terror, I started already terrified by small clues I recognized from the book. Much like a person walking through Chernobyl exclusion zone after disaster might react after noticing a ring of dead plants. The narrative is more slow and phylosophical, tackling the spirit of exploration, the competition between nations and the nature of evolution. Some of the concepts were revolutionary in the middle 20th century, but are fairly well known and accepted today.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this playable 60s style retro sci-fi story a lot. Although it has its boring parts from time to time (especially when you got lost on this deserted planet) I liked the atmosphere and the almost meditative mood and the beautiful landscapes. To quote the main character Yasna: "I am still here. But this is all taking much longer than expected." The end was a bit rushed in my opinion and could have been elaborated more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend the game, even though I enjoyed it.  Odd right? To call this a game is a bit misleading, as it's more akin to a story you have very limited control over.  It's more like getting on an amusement ride and just seeing where it'll take you.  There's little to no combat, limited dialog options, extremely limited exploration and rewards for doing so.  It's pretty much a story on rails.  That said, I did enjoy the story it was decent enough, and now I want to read the book it's based on, but for the $27.00 I paid to "play" this I do feel it was a bit of a let down to call this a game.  There is little to no replay - and the pace is so slow and painful I will never replay it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun and interesting aesthetic absolutely ruined by navigation. The slowest walking/running speed in the history of games makes traversal a tiresome nightmare. The journal is borderline useless and also slow to navigate through. You can't go back over small ledges so you'll just have to try a different way in a whole other playthrough! And speaking of another playthrough enjoy having to do that over and over again for any minor choice because there is no chapter/checkpoint select, brilliant developers. If you're one to care about getting all the achievements you might tear your hair out with how tedious sitting through the molasses that is the traversal and dialogue (which you can't skip either another genius decision).I was well aware coming into this that it was a walking sim but that doesn't mean it needs to feel like a chore to actually play. Plenty of other games have done it better without feeling like a slog but this just felt like every hour was 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: ----------------------------read more at :The music of the game by Brunon Lubas is excellent. It manages to give the necessary feeling of space loneliness and the otherworldly. Combined with the endless deserts of the planet, the rocky formations on the horizon and the red giant looming impossibly overhead, it evokes the appropriate feeling of insignificance and comparison to these timeless and immense sizes. Finally, I feel like it should be mentioned how the game stands in relation to the book. This is because I think the case of The Invincible is very unique. It already addresses a niche audience, of narrative based games. But beyond that it also concerns the even more niche audience of hard sci-fi and I think Lem fans would be interested to know how well this adaptation was done. For the purposes of this review I read the book after finishing the game and I find that the game was written with tremendous respect and obvious love for the original text, which poses the question of the spread of humans to other worlds and on what terms this can be done.  It took me around eight hours to complete The Invincible and while playing it, I was engrossed in its world, walking its deserts, crossing electrical storms in vehicles that looked like space lada niva's, wondering what had happened to the lost crew and the planet's fauna. The game managed to keep me in a constant game of guesswork until the last few chapters when it finally became clear what was going on. I loved the atompunk aesthetic as well as all the art direction. I perhaps object somewhat to Novik and Yasna's completely British accents, however I acknowledge that their performances are amazing even though there is occasionally an annoying repetition in the idle dialogue when nothing is happening and we're just walking along. Also perhaps more time could have been spent in the introduction to make us feel that the lost crew actually meant something and also to integrate Yasna's role as an astrobiologist possibly researching and collecting specimens a little more organically. I think it's a bit steep at its current price of 30 euros, but it will fully satisfy the fans of narrative based games and science fiction. I think it achieves the demands of science fiction, the sense of exploration and asking the big questions about our place in the universe. I personally thought about it for days after finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: The Invincible is a pure walking simulator. I have played my fair share of walking sims and it’s not a category that I dislike but you are essentially watching a movie you are forced to interact with and The Invincible is one of the weaker ones I’ve played. For a game like this to succeed you have to nail 3 aspects, story, music and atmosphere. The game doesn’t do to well in any of these aspects and while it has its moments it struggles with pacing.World and atmosphere are probably the games strongest card, the atompunk theme and art style is excellent and translates well into gameplay and interactivity. Set in an uninhabited solar system on the satellite Regis III, a barren lifeless moon the game does an ok job at making a vibrant and visually striking landscape that could just have been another Starfield planet. Without talking to much about the music just yet the atmospheric tracks on display are impactful and do well to add to the immersion.The worldbuilding carries the game but can only go so far, story is the biggest letdown. The game sets itself up with a duo dynamic similar to Firewatch with your commander named Novik over the radio. Sadly this relationship between Novik and Yasna, the main protagonist never really develops and stays quite shallow throughout the story. This hurts the game quite a bit because the downtime between the narrative could have been filled with character development with this duo but never becomes anything more then just talking about the mission. Novik isn’t a bad character just not the right one for the job, this severely hurts the pacing and makes large parts of this game boring as there are no gameplay elements the game can fall back on. The narrative and mystery is exceptional and its presentation to the player is commendable. It has a dash of philosophy which helps retain some attention and get your brain going. However the narrative mostly fails due to the things mentioned above, it isn’t the sole focus and tension between plot points takes a nosedive with nothing to support it with. The music here is straight up disappointing. Not saying Brunon Lubas made a bad OST, in fact he made some satisfying sovietwave atmospheric tracks of good quality, but implementation is poor. To keep it short, during major plot points music plays a key factor in emotions. In moments where the characters are the focus music can take a backstage if done correctly. In this case the world and its changes are the plot points, good music implementation is crucial during these moments and the game just goes silent. A good soundtrack when you’re traveling and exploring is not good enough. If I were to describe this game in one word it would be; boring. The narrative is interesting and enticing but you must slog through a lot of boredom to get to it. 10/10 IGN

_childDocuments_.review: Buy on sale for sure - you would be hard pressed to get this game to last 10 hours.This game is ALL about story.  Seriously.  There is no action to speak of.  There are no puzzles to solve.  There are choices to make, but there's only one outside of the last half hour of gameplay that makes a lot of difference, and there's no hint that the particular choice will matter more than the minor choices.Luckily, the story is a pretty good one.  It rushes to some conclusions right at the end, but it sets up and solves most of the mysteries pretty well.  Note that the story is not the story told in Lem's book, it's a new story based on the setting established in his book.  It did capture the same tone I would expect from Lem, though.The atmosphere is very well done!  The music and visuals combine to make a slightly spooky, alien vibe and the technology looks very much like 50's science fiction.Saves were a bother for me.  The only saves are checkpoint saves and each one writes over the previous one.  If you want to see what would have happened with another choice, don't expect to load the game up just before the choice was made.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: TL:DR £24 for 6-10 hours of gameplay is too much for me. Game is slower than it needed to be, and I had a few bugs.EDIT2: Upon looking up all the endings I was quite excited for this game but ultimately I feel it fell quite short of what it could have been. Walking sims as a genre are fine, but I experienced some bad bugs while playing (getting stuck on tiny rocks permanently, dialogue not triggering etc) and the walking speed is genuinely painful. The fact Yasna can only run for 10 seconds before huffing and puffing so much she seems like she might pass out is infuriating. I get that you want people to slow down and look for important portions of the game but did I really need to have to walk slowly through the 4th barren desert in the game? The story is also short for the price, with all of the actually interesting story moments happening immediately before the credits roll, no joke, as soon as the main premise and most interesting inciting action occur, the game flat out ends, regardless of ending. I WANT to recommend this game, but I can't. It's too short, too slow, too basic and like many UE projects it's focus on lovely visuals leaves it lacking in every single other way.

_childDocuments_.review: The reviews that describe this as 'Firewatch in space' are spot on. It's a walking sim at the end of the day, and it's a good one. As with most walking sims, it's a slow burn, so if you're looking for action, maybe look elsewhere.The story and graphics are good, and I only experienced one bug myself where a cut-scene started while I was in the middle of an animation, and then once the cut-scene ended I couldn't move. Fortunately, the last checkpoint was less than a minute prior. There are various decisions you make in the game, but no indication that those decisions made a difference in how the game played out. Maybe it's subtle, and maybe I'd need another play through with different decisions to see how decisions matter.My only wish is that movement were more fluid. For instance, you can hold shift to 'run' (i.e. walk a bit faster), but if you try to make a diagonal movement by pressing A/D at the same time it cancels the speed increase, which is a bit annoying. Most games give you an ability to keep your speed but still look around, but here I need to make a trade-off - do i want to move a bit faster and look straight ahead, or move slowly and get to look around. (I get it, though, it's a walking sim, we're expected to stop and smell the roses.)Overall, 8/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a neutral, I would. It's not a bad game, but it's also not good enough that I would recommend it. It's very slow to start, made worse by the very slow movement of the character. Ledges that looked quite climbable or even frankly walkable just weren't an option which was frustrating. You have to climb it on the ledges they want you to and some of them are head height and not an obvious choice. Similarly some things that look like you can drop down you can't, but some really high things you can. This lack of consistency made path finding frequently tedious. I just didn't find myself enjoying the first hour or so but pushed on. Finally it started getting a bit better and I was enjoying it and then before you know it, it's over. I didn't really get the impression that my choices really made all that much difference other than the final scene and that is a frustrating 17 odd minutes of dialogue just to see a very short different ending. Needing to go to YouTube to see alternative endings feels like a failure in game design. I have no desire to go back and try making different choices anywhere else due to the pace of the game. Some sort of decision tree where you going go back to branches and, my god, the ability to skip dialogue would make all the difference. It quickly grated on me.The aesthetics are good, the plot had me curious at times. I did enjoy it enough, but as I say, not enough that I would go out of my way to recommend others play it. Sorry!

_childDocuments_.review: A very slow paced first person/POV game focused on storytelling that should take around 8-10 hours to complete. It does a great job of drawing you in and encourages you to want to know more without the need for guns or violence.Graphics are good from what I've encountered although some have mentioned graphical bugs. I did come across several bugs that locked me out at certain points but i think hot fixes may have now patched those up.My only real gripe about the game is that there are no save points to load to. The game saves automatically as you go but overwrites any previous save, so if you need to go back to a certain point in the game you cant and basically have to start the game from the beginning. _childDocuments_.review: Based off the popular novel of the same name, The Invincible is a retro-styled sci-fi game that follows the astrobiologist Yasna after waking up with amnesia on an alien planet called Regis III, apparently devoid of life. The game starts off like many other games do, with a protagonist that remembers nothing. It's a plot device that many games share, even many of my personal favorites like STALKER and The Witcher. However, the explanation for why Yasna ends up with amnesia has a very scientific basis, and the progressive discovery of learning what happened to both her and her crew is extremely engaging, especially as someone who enjoys science. Regardless, despite a rather generic starting point the game instantly grabs you with both its oddly familiar environments and Yasna's immediate response to her amnesia. Yasna, unlike a lot of other protagonists in games, doesn't just lie down and whine about her lost memories for a while, she immediately assesses the information in her logbook and triangulates her position based off previous notes she made, establishing that she is both self-sufficient and tenacious. Secondly, you learn in the starting area that Regis III has the appearance of a rather Earth-like, rocky desert and, for some odd reasons, supports standing bodies of water. Or, at least, what appears to be water. Over the course of the game you learn a lot about the history of life on Regis III, get to theorize how it progressed and went extinct, as well as the odd, metallic formations in the Earth, which defy all understood notions of what life is, or maybe what it isn't. I don't want to say too much; if you've read the book you likely already know, and if you haven't and are scientifically inclined, then you should try this game. The story is really interesting and one thing I like about it is how it handles player choice. While there isn't much in the way of exploration to be done, the choices and things you say in dialogue actively change what you do during the events of the game and these choices can be both hard to make and impactful on your experience of the game. Most games don't present very difficult choices. But here, especially near the end, my choices felt very final, very important. Like I was really Yasna, choosing how to navigate a great unknown, how to face a potential threat that humanity hitherto has never faced before. It was great.A lot of people criticize this game for being dull, just a walking simulator where you hit W and click on things sometimes. I suppose, at its most essential, that is all The Invincible is; you do a lot of walking and a lot of clicking, and there aren't any upgrade systems or combat mechanics to keep you "engaged". But the great thing about games is how flexible they are. When you read, say, War and Peace, how different is it really from a Nora Roberts book? Of course, the content they provide you with is vastly different and both books come from much different periods in time, but you are still just reading black words on a white page. Even books that sometimes feature illustration or a quirky new font are still just words on a page. Games are much different, and while Movies differ from books also in this regard, you cannot interact with and make choices in a movie like you can a video game. Of course, you could say that all games are just 1s and 0s in a software engine, but they never appear as such, while books always appear as what they really are: words on a page. Games can be as fast as Ultrakill and Sekiro, as slow as Dear Esther and Firewatch, and everything in between. This medium takes on so many different forms and shapes. All of this is to say, really, that boiling The Invincible down to a walking simulator is neither true nor fair. The Invincible is a slow-burn game, with few high octane moments and no combat system; it doesn't have a bombastic ending and doesn't come with any "OMG" plot twists. You piece together a lot of what happens yourself, and the real bombastic ending comes with the simple choice of keeping or discarding a jar of little metal robots, which is a simple act with immense implications. Don't let people keep you away from this game because it's a "walking sim". Besides, I kind of like walking simulators. They always have the best dialogue and voice acting.7/10. My only real issue with this game is the stuttering. It hitches like crazy anytime anything loads in, regardless of graphical settings. While it doesn't render the game unplayable, it is disappointing and rather annoying. Otherwise, the game runs really well outside of a few specific areas in-game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long while since I've played a "walking sim" type of game, but I found this one to have a bit more freedom compared to the last I played. I really dig the "future meets retro" theme in games. The graphics are overall very nice, but I did find the ground textures to be mediocre and I came across a handful of visual bugs and collision issues with the rover. I also found it odd at times how what was being narrated didn't match the actions of my character. Overall I found the story to have a decent plot and an enjoyable pace, and rate this a 6/10. Would recommend for anyone who enjoys sci-fi storytelling and chill mystery vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games that I completed in one breath and with great interest. The game captured me with its interest in the plot and what was happening on the screen. From the very beginning, you do not understand anything, and try to understand the whole game. Personally, I had a couple of moments when I was 100 percent sure of some theory, but then one action completely refuted this and provided a new version of what was happening. Initially, I thought that the game had an illusion of choice, as it was in many well-known games, where you are given a choice that ultimately only deceives you, because it did not affect the outcome in any way. After about the first choices in this game, it became clear that this game has several endings (as it turned out, there are 11 of them, wow), and you really decide what to do, and then you start thinking, is it right?I completed the game entirely on DualSense, so support for PlayStation gamepads is present
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this game, I had never even heard of the novel it's based on — “The Invincible” by Stanisław Lem. All I knew going in was that it was a walking sim, it's in space and had thriller and/or horror elements.So if you're like me and that's all you want to know,  as there  be minor spoilers in this review. Simply to provide a setup for what this game is actually about.The closest game, that I've played, that this game reminds me of mechanically, as well as narrative structure in how it reveals the plot is Firewatch. You'll take control of the character Dr. Yasna, whom is a scientist, or more specifically an exobiologist or astrobiologist. You'll explore a relatively linear path, interacting with objects and the environment while engaging with dialogue options — largely with Novik, the Astrogator of the Dragonfly. The ship you all flew on to arrive at Regis III. The game does have multiple endings and your choices do matter.You'll have a few tools to use to aid you in the more open areas such as a tracker and a metal detector.I  want to talk about the ideas and themes that this game brings up about the real life repercussions and the possibilities through the exploration of space and how it might affect us as a species. But I also feel like that mystery is the most compelling aspect of this story.I will surmise my thoughts with the following — minor thematic spoilers:The Invincible is a fantastic story-driven game. Though it is pretty slow-paced, and despite me being in the mood for something like that, I did find myself getting a tad anxious by the speed at which the character moves at times. Gracefully, the game is relatively strait-forward and you shouldn't have too much trouble getting to the next instance. And while some areas are very large, there are no collectibles that will make you feel like you need to walk into every corner and waste a ton of time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I love a good sci-fi story, and this definitely delivers - both in a unique way, and one which draws inspiration from other sources.  Though the visual and technological style doesn't necessarily lend itself to plausibility, it is certainly an enjoyable artistic take which fits well into storytelling akin to Fallout, Bioshock, or Metro.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invincible

_childDocuments_.review: I dont ever really lead with the fact that I've got a video on a game, but I made a video directly explaining the issues that I have with this adaptation of Stanislaw Lem's novel.The TL;DR is that they basically took his name and the name of the novel, a few major plot points, and then removed all of the rest of what Stanislaw Lem wrote to make room for all of their characters (there are no novel characters in the game) and their story (minus a few of the broader strokes the plot is new as well).The dialogue is rough, the gameplay is far too slow even for a walking sim, and frankly this was a waste of talent from a team that is OBVIOUSLY very talented. The sound design and visuals are strong, but that doesn't save sh*tty writing.Here's the video comparing the book and the game if you are interested:
