name: Breathedge
detailed_description: Wishlist new part! About the Game Breathedge is an ironic outer space survival adventure game. Take on the role of a simple guy called the Man who is just carrying his grandpa's ashes to a galactic funeral and suddenly finds himself in the middle of a universal conspiracy. Welcome to Space A massive space hearse suffers a wreck in the deep space, leaving the area filled with debris, coffins, dead passengers and yourself. Survive in this interstellar dump, uncover a global conspiracy, save the princess and don’t break your fingers while tapping the keyboard as you travel around the world (keeping your display on for full immersion is advised). Try to stay alive Space isn’t a joke (despite us trying to prove otherwise) and not dying is a challenge. Lose your progress in spectacular ways, including but not limited to suffocation, freezing, incineration, electrocution, depression, blunt trauma, and more. Litter space with garbage you created It took a long time for our ancestors to develop because they had no electrical tape. You have it and you know how to use it. With this magical artifact, you can create a vast variety of useless objects and throw them out of the airlock! There are also many useful items to be created, but be careful as this may result in completing the game. Fix and Decorate When all your neighbors just hover around in vacuum doing nothing but playing dead, various tools and gears will help you become the worst noisy neighbor ever. Create a unique space station, provide it with oxygen and electricity, install all kinds of equipment from solar panels to a hamster farm, and turn it into a real bachelor pad by stuffing it with furniture mixed with all kinds of junk. Honk! Honk! Yes, you heard that right, it’s your own private car horn! Besides that, you can assemble a small rocket, ride the dead or build a large space shuttle. Transportation helps you move faster, evade obstacles and see the death screen after a head-on collision.
about_the_game: Breathedge is an ironic outer space survival adventure game. Take on the role of a simple guy called the Man who is just carrying his grandpa's ashes to a galactic funeral and suddenly finds himself in the middle of a universal conspiracy. Welcome to Space A massive space hearse suffers a wreck in the deep space, leaving the area filled with debris, coffins, dead passengers and yourself. Survive in this interstellar dump, uncover a global conspiracy, save the princess and don’t break your fingers while tapping the keyboard as you travel around the world (keeping your display on for full immersion is advised). Try to stay alive Space isn’t a joke (despite us trying to prove otherwise) and not dying is a challenge. Lose your progress in spectacular ways, including but not limited to suffocation, freezing, incineration, electrocution, depression, blunt trauma, and more. Litter space with garbage you created It took a long time for our ancestors to develop because they had no electrical tape. You have it and you know how to use it. With this magical artifact, you can create a vast variety of useless objects and throw them out of the airlock! There are also many useful items to be created, but be careful as this may result in completing the game. Fix and Decorate When all your neighbors just hover around in vacuum doing nothing but playing dead, various tools and gears will help you become the worst noisy neighbor ever. Create a unique space station, provide it with oxygen and electricity, install all kinds of equipment from solar panels to a hamster farm, and turn it into a real bachelor pad by stuffing it with furniture mixed with all kinds of junk. Honk! Honk! Yes, you heard that right, it’s your own private car horn! Besides that, you can assemble a small rocket, ride the dead or build a large space shuttle. Transportation helps you move faster, evade obstacles and see the death screen after a head-on collision.
short_description: Survive in outer space! Together with your immortal chicken, discover the truth behind your sudden spaceship crash. Craft tools, pilot vehicles, and even control space stations to survive and explore the wreckage.

_childDocuments_.review: Well.. the game is gorgeous.. and the jokes are funny for the first 5 minutes but then fall flat. Other reviews have called this a sort of "Deadpool" style of humor and I love Deadpool. Not this.This game has VERY suspicious reviews - a lot of people have played this for maybe half an hour and more or less called it goty... weeks ago.. and have never played it again since their play time has not changed. Way too many.You get tossed into the game and there ulimately no guidance besides "go". Normally this doesn't bother me and is fantastic in a exploration type of game.. but EVERYTHING you make in this game has the smallest durability I've ever experienced in a survival game. ALL resources are finite. A lot of the resources you need for gear that you can make for upgrades are found in obscure containers that you need to beat down with your "wrench" and not just.. open. That wrench? Costs 3 metal. 35 durability. Each metal notes gives maybe 2 or 3 metal... and uses about 5 durability. You do the math. What's the point?Ultimately you're left wanting to explore the game more in a very quiet, ambient setting... and deal with contiuously dwindling resources in a world that offers no real reason to explore... while on the smallest leash you can imagine because the already limited resources you can use to explore are needed to do ANY exploring. Nothing is renewable. No farms, no solar panel, no food, no building, NOTHING to possibly make this even slightly enjoyable. You can travel out in one direction on your starting oxygen for about 20 seconds, and then 20 seconds back. Find an upgrade nearby? Great - now its about 35 seconds out and back... Apparently there's another but almost the ENTIRE MAP is either covered in a radiation zone or too cold... and the only way to upgrade your suit is to get lead from places on the map that are about 600 meters away from the starting area. That's a pretty long way from the start considering you move at a max of 12m/s without what's essentially an afterburner that boosts you to 20m/s for maybe 5 seconds. That 50 second trip? That's 100 points of oxygen, MINIMUM, more than what you can reasonably have in a tank. You can make oxygen refill stations.. that don't refill on their own.. and use a lot of resources to be able to refill. Like the metal. That's finite. See the cycle yet? No upgrades, no real "resupply stations", no bases, very little rewards for exploring and just.. a grind.Seriously disappointed. I wanted something like Subnautica (which I LOVED and beat multiple times.. supported it very early in EA) but I was really just left feeling like I have to wait for some other game to get me thrilled to explore again. Maybe this one will get updated.. but probably not since it has been months with little change and the game is looking to be "episodic" anyways.. For an exploration game. What??

_childDocuments_.review: I feel really bad to put my first negative review, but i have to warn people that it is NOT Subnautica in space AT ALL. I enjoy most of the game because I was lure to think that at some point, I will go back to my base and stock all those ressources I've accumulated and maybe continue the story, but no, the game ENDS and that feeling of being scammed appear while the credit roll.If you expect a Subnautica, prepare to be extremely disappointed.PS: INB4 some says "They never said it will be Subnautica in space", then : Why the entire marketing during the Early Access, among the Youtube/Twitch sphere, imply that it will be. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute palate-cleanser among contemporary survival-crafting games.When I first picked up Breathedge I had just finished Subnautica and was all emotionally invested in the genre. Breathedge rubbed me the wrong way. It was snarky and relentlessly self-deprecating and the recipes didn't make sense (because dropping some rocks and unadulterated rare earth minerals into a magic molecule-rearranging box to get a laser cutter totally does). I didn't want funny, I wanted real desolate first-person grimdark immersive solitude. The Forest and Stranded Deep were too low-tech and I wasn't interested in the likes of Ark.Fast forward a year. I have played every survival-crafting game that even looks remotely worth it on the surface. I sink hundreds of hours into Satisfactory and Factorio. Food tastes like ash in my mouth. There is no joy in gaming any more.Now, in my darkest hour, I am ready for you, Breathedge.* The AI dialog is hysterical.* There is a rich and diverse comedic subtext even in the placement of non-interactive props. The various ways in which your fellow engineers have perished is a prime showcase example of this.* The things you actually do to get the game to tell you the story are as ridiculous as the story itself.* Exploration and progression require putting yourself in danger.* Graphics engine performance is tip-top at ultra detail on my dinosaur video card.* Base-building is satisfying.* Every junk item is worth picking up and spending a few moments reading the caption and inspecting it visually. There is a ton of attention to detail in the environment.* There is not a plethora of information available about this game out there on the Internet. You can watch some YouTube videos, but if like me you resent modern society for forcing you to watch a video to get a piece of information instead of being able to quickly skim a text document somewhere (ok boomer), you will have to experiment with the environment and reload saves and get real close to stuff and do that old school trial-and-error approach in order to un-stuck yourself. This adds an entirely new dimension of enjoyment in a time where games are often completely data-mined and dumped for the world to see before they're even released, and you are expected to spoil yourself on how to progress before you're even required to have that knowledge.* For some reason, I really like the sound that plays when you click a recipe in the constructor that you don't have enough materials to build. It's the ultimate "NO YOU FAILED TO DO THAT" sound.* Though combat exists, it is sparse. The game is focused on survival, exploration, and story-telling.* Tool durability could stand to be tweaked over time. By the middle of chapter 2/3 I should not have to make a pile of drills to go Aluminum farming. Making tools all the time ends up becoming a bit of a chore, and occasionally results in having to revisit areas in order to acquire tech that you missed because there were more scannables than you had Scanner charges. * There are some things that are super obvious in retrospect but could use some extra context (i.e. where discharge cells come from), others that are not obvious enough (i.e. how one enables themselves to pull Breathedge energy cores or harvest Lycoplasma).* I would really enjoy an option to turn off or modify the O2 alarm klaxon in some fashion. Even with the Military O2 Tanks and over 4 minutes of available O2 buffer I end up organizing my activities to ensure that I'm back in an oxygen-rich environment before the alarm goes off. That thing is obnoxious. * It's not finished yet.Breathedge is the epitome of "labor of love" survival-crafter games and is a standard by which other games in the genre should be held. Thanks for an awesome journey RedRuins, I can't wait to see the rest of this amazing game!

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is a lengthy first-person adventure game set in space with an emphasis on crafting, exploration, and dumb jokes.In Breathedge, you control a man lost in space following the explosion of a ship transporting funeral coffins. Your companions are an immortal chicken and a fast-talking spacesuit AI providing you with non-sequiters and tasks to accomplish. The primary gameplay loop is exploring space to find blueprints, mine resources, and return to base to craft new tools to reach ever further locations. Limiting factors are your oxygen, food, and water meters and limited inventory space. Unlike Subnautica, a similar game with the same basic premise albeit set underwater, Breathedge never takes itself seriously and drastically switches focus in its later chapters from free-form space exploration to on-foot adventure tropes. Though you can shoot with a weapon or ship, combat is minimal and not a selling point.I beat the game in a little over 28 hours exploring as much as possible, netting 51 of 54 Steam Achievements. Be warned, many Achievements are missable and you are limited to a single save slot (with one more reserved for automatic saves). There is no arc to the game's difficulty, with dying usually the result of a depleted oxygen meter. Crafting is the game's dominant focus with items varying from usable tools, space components, and even the occassional one-off included as a gag or to progress the absurd plot.The consistency, depth, and enthusiastic effort put towards Breathedge's humour in all aspects of its execution makes it come across as a video game principally as a joke-delivery mechanism. Your always-present suit AI wise-cracks so rapidly, and so non-stop, that I frequently had to read the text log to keep up. A byproduct of playing titles like Skyrim and Fallout 3 is that games with a crafting element have instilled in me a compulsion to hoard every single item I come across. Do that in Breathedge and you can easily add/waste an additional 10+ hours of your gameplay time. There are a high number of items used in crafting but also an equally high number of one-off gag items included as a joke. Hundreds of these items, all lovingly modeled in full 3D, given a text description along with audio aside, all gloriously catologued within your inventory collections menu, and existing simply because. However, I still had to fight the urge to carry them back to a base like the soul-less gaming horder I seem to have become. An ongoing joke that frequently brought a smile to my face was the death pose discovery of countless other ill-fated astronauts. These are all played for laughs, with no one death repeated. Death by televsion to the face, death by honeymoon murder, death by space cow. Sure, why not? All lovingly presented and detailed solely for the sake of something to see. Breathedge is without subtlety. It litters your HUD with quest markers and with a near-constantly speaking AI suit jabbering in your ear, you never feel alone. Though long, Breathedge is unrefined, existing more for jokes than a serious contender for best crafting game on the market. An example is the need to build a research table and then invest resources towards unlocking an item. Only afterwards do you discover you then need yet more resources to actually build the item. More frustrating was that I actually bothered to collect the resources needed to supposedly research a space car. Once I had the resources I learned that the game wouldn't give it to me through research, as it was locked behind three blueprints I had to find hidden in the cosmos at random (even though it showed up at the research table).Other reviewers complained of a slow movement speed and though the developers released a patch that extended the base movement of some of your early travels, I personally found the middle chunk of the game to be the slowest. Early on, it makes sense you are slow, since you are just getting use to your limitations while gradually opening up the reach of what you can do. I felt the opening chapter was the most coherently paced of the entire game. The challenge I had was that the 2nd and 3rd chapters were overwhelming in the number of HUD markers, quests, and crafting tedium involved. Despite gaining access to a vehicle, and the ability to craft a few more, some of the most expensive (aka mining-heavy) things you can craft have near-zero reason for you to make the effort. If, like me, you attempt to earn the most Steam Achievements you can, expect to spend several hours mining resources simply for a pop-up, rather than for anything tangibly useful.While the middle section is overwhelming and with locations spread too far apart, the next section slows things to a crawl. You reach a point where you will no longer explore space of your own accord, but rather in a ship you slowly upgrade. The thing is, the ship has no speed boost whatsoever, and even with the ability to fire lasers, combat is so infrequent that you may as well be just another corpse floating in one of the coffins strewn about. At this time, the game turns into a first-person adventure game whereby you fly your ship, dock somewhere, then walk in a linear line towards an objective before backtracking to your ship. This is an example of the game's joking becoming insulting. One sequence suggests a fast-travel mechanism that turns out doesn't exist. Funny? Marginally, but it doesn't change the fact you are then forced to walk ad naseum.Despite the game's latter half shifting gameplay focus and the story explanations rushed (even for the suit AI), the whimsy, juvenile humour, and passion towards it all never wavers.There were times playing Breathedge I felt insulted, not by the humour, but by the lack of respect for my time. There are so many little things they could have done to speed things up that wouldn't have ruined the sense of exploration. The last third of the game really commits to visual spectacle in cutscenes, which by comparison makes you feel like you missed out on being able to do something far more exciting. Without spoiling anything, there is a dangling plot point regarding a potential NPC companion that goes beyond a voice in your spacesuit. Sadly, I felt this was a missed opportunity, as well as an apt metaphor for how I'm feeling over a year into the Covid-19 pandemic.I've made wonderful friendships with people through Discord and in other online voice and text tools. I've only recently gained fleeting moments of optimistic hope for the future in perhaps questing with people in-person, rather than virtually. Yet for all the talk, all the spectacle, that time has not yet arrived. Just as the story of Breathedge remains unresolved, so to does the state of things once this global event comes under control. Breathedge is a long game, a cheap game, a good looking game, and one that nobody without patience, an open sense of humour, and ample time on their hands should consider touching with a ten foot pole.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent 3 hours to beat chapter 1 but I thought it was 30 hours of entertainment. I LOL'd 3 times and smiled more than 10 times within one playthrough. This game is one hell of a cereal spitter especially when you know the reference. I even slapped the table at the end of chapter 1.As a space game, the physics is good, not the best because floating objects  should not decelerate in space. But with the self-mocking humour about the physics itself, I found that pretty funny. Besides, free float objects would cause a lot of trouble as a survival game in space. Especially when some players might found it difficult to navigate in frictionless area or chasing objects around.Difficulty is moderate to easy.  The game is story driven and survival is easy if you know what you are doing to advance. Resource is always supply > demand for all of your construction and survival, I have 4 suitcases of useless materials at the end of the game. The only resource I had difficulty to locate was aluminium. I hope there was a resource scanner so I could at least know which direction to go. What resource scanner might do (1)Select a resource to locate; (2)Scan in a narrow cone shape towards where the player was pointing; (3)Pulse to feedback if any matching was found, none if nothing; (4)Durability -1 when any matching was found per scan. Oxygen is not unlimited! As the game mentioned, some people might find it annoying to go round trip every minute, just because they haven't dig deep into game. You know, I could spend 20mins+ outside without returning to my shuttle unless my inventory is full or I am hungry.Exploration is fantastic. There is always something to investigate at obvious sites. Comedy also plays a large role here.  I would not be surprised if the DEV starts adding some other games related mocking stuff. Travel time is reasonable provided that I never felt bored for travelling.This game is potentially a great indie. I won't expect more mechanics to be added into the game soon such as the construction thing mentioned in the DEV blog. I think most players are looking forward to more story telling, plus humour of course!

_childDocuments_.review: This should be a positive recommendation.  But there's a few issues that make this a 'No' for me.  The base movement rate of the character is painfully slow, the oxygen capacity and consumption rate are bad.  Most of the crafted tools have below average durability for a survival crafting game, and there is no means to repair them.Because of these issues, it's almost as if the game actively disrespects the player's time investment.  The game demands the player go out to explore and gather but saddles the player with the onerously slow movement and low oxygen limits.  These issues seem to serve no other purpose than artificially slowing down the pacing of the game.  Really, it just make everything tedious and makes me realize other games respect my limited free time more.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game enough to play it for 36 hours, most of that time I expected to and planned on replaying it. However, upon completion, I'm over it.Breathedge is most closely related to Subnautica in terms of the crafting/survival gameplay, but with slightly less atmosphere and more immortal livestock. The humor is pretty low brow, but none of it feels out of place. In short, it was a great one-time, soft survival, story driven game. I do however have 2 complaints that prevent me from playing this until more is added.1. There is a monumental shift in gameplay at Chapter 4, which I was initially excited about because of its potential for expanding the core survival experience. But just as I was getting used to the idea of the new mechanics and how I could incorporate them with my existing experience, the game ended. Without spoiling too much, you acquire a mobile base of sorts. Sounds cool right? Like the Sub from Subnautica 1 or the Sea Truck from Below Zero. But what if, when this is introduced, the game goes from 'free-form survival/exploration' to 'linear walk/fly to task marker, walk while listening to dialogue, walk to next marker' defeating any and all purpose of the new vehicle? Well guess what, that's exactly what happens. Then the game kinda just ends, and you get the option to return to the survival/exploration portion of the game. But there's nothing new, so why would you?I felt almost baited. Because of the humor in the game, I was sort of expecting a pop-up saying "Actually, no the game didn't just end, here is your new vehicle, there's also new stuff to do". My second issue with the game is the fact that 1 of the 3 characters I interacted with never said anything the entire time. They practically harass you with written dialogue during your whole experience, with your Suit AI commenting on their accent at times. Bruh what accent? Its a never ending text wall. Maybe it was a bug, and maybe the devs plan to get a Voice for the role, but as it stands, it soured my experience.To summarise, the 2 issues I've covered make the game, particularly the second half, feel rushed and unfinished. But at the same time, I had fun for about 30 hours, and there are 2 planned FREE story-driven expansions/updates as far as I can tell that will add some more content to the game. At the end of the day, this is a very affordable game, and despite its shortcomings, I do recommend it to people who enjoy stupid jokes, references and a short and light survival experience. You'll have to decide if those three things are worth the price for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool first two chapters with great humor and a good basic "survival" concept. Very poor quality of life features such as a way to track places you've already been, or having ways to make the player do less backtracking due to them not bringing the exact right equipment or not having enough durability. Then the 3/4th chapter hits and the entirety of the first two chapters are worthless. The backtracking increases to a point where it's simply baffling. The humor is still good but the gameplay becomes tremendously boring. It's as if the complete design philosophy shifted halfway through development. Hopefully Breathedge 2 will be less disjointed and more satisfying while still maintaining its specific style.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Oh yeah....Breathedge. Totally forgot about this. What did I ever see in this game?!You know what it was? A humorous, energetic, lively, GIMMICK of an advertisement. The video tricked me into thinking I was gonna use this immortal chicken for all kinds of wacky things.Since I don't want you to waste your money on this turd, I'll just shamelessly spoil it for you.You use the chicken to depower wires. That's....................it. Yep, that's all. At least, that's all I could do with the useless thing in the 18 hours of my life I wasted.You play as a guy doing stuff. And stuff he sure does. After an inexplicable catastrophic accident involving this massive ship you were riding on, you now need to scavenge everything around your little joke of a lifepod AND everything floating around in space. Yay. Collect-o-thon.I had to keep looking through reviews and guides to see why it was taking so long to get anything accomplished. And the guides themselves must be as screwed up as this game because several times I saw allusions to being able to build your own base.This never happened.Instead, I found myself wasting beautiful days I could have been playing ball with my son just to fly my non-newtonian idiot around looking for 3 rotton shawarmas. Yes. Three. Not two, not one. Three. Why? Because I'm an even bigger idiot who impulsively buys Steam games that waste my time.I really enjoyed the first few hours for the same reason all the other idiots in the world enjoy Fortnite. They put exactly what was needed into the game to hook people. Then they just said heck with it for the rest.After a few hours it became tedious but that's ok. I don't mind a little grind, a little effort to build up momentum. Then, after going from new area to new area, mindless task after mindless task, I went to play something else and completely forgot about this. Oh, and when you DO go to a new area, you can either pack-rat everything you've collected thus far or, hey why not, start collecting everything all over again! Wheeeee! A game that never progresses!! No reason to play it! Or buy it! Go back to the lake of fire where ya came from, idiots!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted it to be like Subnautica, but the 'humor' is just soooo bad.It's not clever and simply lazy.That there is an example of the incessant 4-wall 'humor'. The designers put zero thought into any of the jokes and to mask this, they went with quantity over quality. For me at least, the appeal of games like these is the feeling of blissful isolation. There is nothing blissful about Breathedge. The constant (and I mean constant!) no-effort humor rips away any chance of establishing an atmosphere.The immortal chicken thing held my interest for a microsecond, but the rest was a crime against humanity.Unless you are a very small child, this is an epic fail.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but the experience it is not fun. You are barely given any oxygen to do anything at all and that severly impacts the exploration aspect of this game. Also the jokes the game is making start to annoy you when you have to constantly battle asfixiation. The gameplay cycle goes like this: Need resources to build an oxygen station to recharge and travel further, then you need an oxygen generator to recharge the oxygen stations you´ve built. To explore further you need more oxygen stations, so what ends up happening is that you want to explore somewhere new but you can´t because the devs were to strict with O2.To add insult to injury every so often you have to craft new tools because the one you have constantly break so then you either have two pairs of each tool as a back up taking a lot of inventory space or you will sometimes find yourself exploring but having to go back to recraft your tools. You know artificially prolonging the game, it even goes as far as to say it to your face literally during the game as a joke.In short: It had potential but it was ruined by making it a chore to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think this game has A LOT of potential. I'm gonna start with the cons first.Cons - -The breathe meter(by the way devs, should it be breath meter?) is absolutely way too short. It worked to be short in Subnautica because the movement was so fast, but even here with 75 seconds of air it's not enough time to really do anything, though I suppose that's by design for the scenario that's out so far.-The durability doesn't really make sense on something like a scanner. Why is that breaking down on use? I get it's cobbled together out of a back scratcher, but what? Also, the durability should either be scrapped completely or it should be increased for everything. It doesn't add a single good thing to the game and survival games already have built in busywork with hunger and thirst. Don't add more for artificial game length!-The scenario can also be beaten in under 3 hours, but maybe this is more of a demo of sorts than the actual finished scenario.-Why aren't containers in yet?! I may have missed them, but I didn't have them in my playthrough-My last complaint is that the humor is really not very funny for the most part. There's some things that actually land for me, but overall I think the game would have been far better off with a less goofy tone, because a lot of it is just...stupid, I think.____________Pros--The graphics and the general aesthetic are beautiful!-The zero G movement is really cool and the sense of scale is great-There is some really nice music in the game-The crafting system feels pretty streamlined in that if you've got lead, you don't need it as a raw material AND as an ingredient, you just make lead paint with it. I like knowing off the bat whether I'll need the resource raw or not-This game seems really polished so far__________That's all I've got for now. I think it's worth $12 for the scenario, and while I hope it meets its potential I can't advise a purchase unless you know you're only getting about 3 hours of a gorgeous, solid survival game, that hopefully gets better.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is a good game but i dislike it for several reasons.Humor: Even tho it made me laugh occasionly it annoyed me most of the time.Basebuilding: Deconstructing results in material loss so if you want to remodell your base you'll have to grind more mats. All you have for storage are suitcases that are stumbling around. Also there are different sizes of rooms but there's no point to build some of them. Most of stuff you can build is useless junk.Flying speed: It takes so much time going from A to B (even with vehicles) and you'll have to do it over and over again.Some might say that Breathedge is Subnautica but i strongly disagree.Breathedge is similar to subnautica regarding: Basebuilding, (downsides mentioned above) there's no Basebuilding in the 2nd and 3rd part.Exploration, but it's mostly asteroids and wreckage. Also your vertikal orientation stays the same which is nonsense in space. The world and story is absolutely silly (which isn't a bad thing per se) and for that part alone i wonder why some people say that it's subnautica in space. Survival, but there's food and water everywhere and oxygenmanagement is really annoying in this game but i'd have to spoiler some things to tell you why.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: A few hours into the game it felt like it was about to end. This feeling was very misleading. Soon after the game expanded greatly. And then when I felt like I was reaching the main goal the game switched up the gameplay and was still very far from being over. Breathedge is definitely worth playing if you're not fazed by constant displays of bloody and ridiculous deaths. Gameplay-wise it's somewhat reminiscent of Subnautica.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries really hard to be funny in a very unforgiving survival game and it just comes off as very forced. I picked this game up expecting a space themed Subnautica and instead I got a bargain bin borderlands survival game. Some of the sounds are extremely jarring and out of place while others are annoying because of how often they repeat. I found myself turning the music off pretty early in the run because it is the same track every time you leave the ship and same panic music when you start to lose oxygen, even when you're 5 feet from the ship entrance. I can see how this game might be fun if they added multiplayer but as of now it's just not what I was expecting.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica in space... but not nearly as good. I'm neutral on recommending this as I did get 65 decent hours of game play out of it. I think Bevis and Butthead wrote this game as the humor is basically on that level and not even remotely funny. Unfortunately, for me, that detracts enormously from this game. The whole thing is just ridiculous. Maybe worse, chapters 5 and 6 completely abandon the whole survival thing, but you're still gathering things as if it matters. It's almost like the first half of the game and the second half of the game are two different games and not in a good way. Of course, if you play in "Story" mode it turns all the survival aspects of the game off... which is really kind of the primary point of the first half of the game...Still, it was mildly fun overall as the original Subnautica is one of my all time favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know. Some people are going to like it just because it has the crafting element. It was pitched to me as "like subnautica but in space", which sounded appealing to me because I loved subnautica. But I found myself floating around the same space over and over again without any real sense of exploration. The game tries very hard to be funny, but it just isn't. Yet its intrusive jokes just keep right on coming, every five seconds, completely confident in themselves, but still not funny. At times I could barely concentrate on what I was doing because the unfunny comedy man would not stop talking to me. It got to a point where I was just kinda boringly floating around space looking for material that I couldn't find anywhere. I looked it up in the guide and that wasn't helping. I floated around, slowly, tediously, for like two hours trying to find one mat. I was gonna just google it but then I decided I'll probably just play something else.Aaaaalmost good game with overconfident not-funny jokes / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with fantastic humor.A "must play" for everyone who loves story-driven exploration games with tons of secret stuff and who have no problems with slight survival elements and beeing alone in space.- : it have a main story line, which is wonderful with full english voice-over and on top all the secret stuff you find and some small collectibles(which you can put in inventory, but you have them in a collectible tab too) which add stuff to the story too. side-stuff/secrets/easter eggs getting commentated with voice-over too. All of it in the right length, not short and not too long. if you want to only do story and miss most of the good side-stuff, you dont have to grind too much, but if you want to explore you can and get rewarded with secrets.- : big, diversified, tons of secrets, some of them not that easy to find, but none of them felt for me like "oh, now i flew miles to point x, here is a wrack but nothing in it.", because you get most of the times some usable stuff or collectibles with a small piece of humor.- : i would say mostly sarcasm/cynistic/morbid, not too serious, but not on the point where its only dumb- : i love the sounds of this game, they are fitting and not annoying (maybe only the drill if you use it too much).- : its okay it does what it should. free-license music. you can turn the radio off or switch by yourself in your space shuttle. music outside and for other stuff is nice and fitting- : for me like in early access, no Bugs, no glitchy stuff, no crashes, here and there maybe some slight fps drops if you look in some directions from point x, but not noticable for me if i didnt had looked at the fps counter - : in the sweet spot. you have your questmarker for the mainstory questline, every other tool-upgrade spot or everything else you have to find by yourself. Most scannable things get a marker, if you are close enough to them. some secrets didnt get anything, so dont fly blind through space.- i: if you are at the point where you really didnt know where to find stuff or if you want to have more info about x, you can look into your inventory and have all it in there, without the need of external sources- : its okay. like subnautica. it does what it should.- : you can color them and toggle them on/off, thanks.- : thanks for this, even if it is a problem for many people. but this game is so story heavy, because every piece you find will have some dialogue and if you do mainquest your suit always talk to you and commentate stuff, so you dont feel alone. if they would had make this coop there would be some nasty "stand in range to trigger x" or teleport to me stuff, which would brick the immersion or otherwise people would have miss out on stuff and would complain too. for me it will be always been like: give me a good immersive story/gameplay soloplay instead of a co-op game where my friend(s) have to fill out the part where the game lacks the content or fun.- - , but there are "landmarks" for orentiation and the stuff is varied enough to not get lost... only if you are forgetful on top :P- , because there is no checklist of what they found and what not (only some showrooms for some collectibles). so explore more, look in every corner, hover over everything and look if its interactive or you will miss stuff.- . yes you have base building and you can go pretty big and decor stuff. you can collect everything from everywhere but there is a point, if you have the story finished, where is the end, because of not infinite resources.

_childDocuments_.review: For a first chapter release, I found it to be very entertaining.  The mechanics are fantastic, stressful (ran out of air so many times because i was having too much fun finding stuff), and captivating. _childDocuments_.review: Like Subnautica... but worse in almost every way combined with forced immature jokes.I'd only recommend this game to people who have finished Subnautica and are looking for something more punishing, linear, and filled with extremely childish quips.Even putting aside the borderline homophobic, anti-PC/anti-SJW jokes, the gameplay is sadly lacking. Yes, it is Early Access, but the devs have said that the first 2 Chapters are pretty much finalized. Imagine Subnautica but you're railroaded and you can only get oxygen at bases you construct or very specific and limited locations. That's just the start of the gameplay problems. The overall gameloop is very repetitive and a slog, while Subnautica has interesting biomes and creatures with a variety of behaviors, Breathedge is devoid of almost all of that. Really wanted to like this, but the jokes put me off and the gameplay made me realize it wasn't for me in the long run.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a CONDITIONAL recommendation.  I started with "not recommended", but there's so much other truly junk games out there, and this game shows promise.   But it needs some work, so here we go:The game is promising, but needs some serious balancing and changes before I could recommend.   My thoughts so far with Chapter 1:1.  The announcer talks WAYYY too fast.  He's like the guy giving terms at the end of a car commercial.  Considering he's giving some critical hints, he doesn't need to talk that fast, since you can't absorb it while flying around trying to manage your limited air.  It's super annoying to have to go back later and read the text, and less useful out of the context of where you were, positionally in the game.  I missed the scanner for a long time, wondering how I would find a blueprint, because I was done and gone from its location before I figured out it was a hint.  TALK SLOWER.   FAST ISN'T FUNNY.2.  Reward the players when they are clever.   The hints are either blunt bludgeons (any idiot can follow a marker) or non-existent.   "Hey, a cargo hold.. probably lots of good stuff in there."  Logically, yes.  A player would feel good finding extra stuff by searching what was pointed out as the cargo hold.  Nope.  Nothing there.   So why bother telling me it's a cargo hold, jerK?3.  By the same token, next steps should be a bit more intuitive.  I'm at the bridge being told I need to find a key and a code.  I spent an hour searching the area with the limited air mechanic trying to figure out where it might be held.  Logically, maybe a captain's cabin?  Nothing in the area or on the way like that.   4.  Combining #3 with the limited air mechanic is a serious turnoff.  Either give me time to explore without constantly having to worry about the air (more air upgrades in chapter 1), or make it a more logical progression as to where to find the next item.   I don't need you to tell me where, but it's got to be someplace that makes sense if you think.  For the whole game, I've just been randomly stumbling on what I need, so I don't feel clever, I feel just lucky at times, and that's not a fun game.   5.  It seems that there's really just ONE way to solve every puzzle and ONE route to get to the next step, so it's not as much of a 'sandbox' it might appear or as similar games.   I saw a comment by one player who put oxy stations in the wrong places, now he's out of the resources to make more to get to the next stage (because they barely seed enough resources and if you don't do things in the EXACT RIGHT ORDER, you have to start the game again... that's seriously bad game design).The game has a lot of promise, but they really need to consider the psychology of games, rewarding cleverness, less fixed 'one way' solutions, a bit more of a sandbox with more solutions to get to the end result, etc  (study the structure of the first Subnautica!!!).   But right now, it's a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: In one word: Disappointing.At first glance it's like Subnautica in space. Yes, they took elements of it but turned them boring and tedious. I played chapter 1 and started with chapter 2, but can't get myself to continue. I watched some walkthroughs to see how the game goes on, then uninstalled it. Best thing the game does: Makes me want to play Subnautica.Is it funny? If you think fart based acceleration and 4x Ice => Yellow Water is funny, it might be for you. For me it isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: An inferior version of Subnautica. The pacing is slow, it was frustrating and unclear what to do at times, and getting some of the rarer resources was tedious. It doesn't have the same grand sense of exploration. I just felt like I was shuttling items around the same pathways. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoy resource-based sandbox games, and initially I found the mechanics and core loop of venturing outside into open space to frantically collect and examine before running out of air to be very promising. And still do, it's a neat twist on the genre (although I get the impression Subnautica, which I've yet to play, already kind of did this).Then, the tedium set in.Tedium describes almost every aspect of this game. Some tedium is expected in a normal game progression for this genre in my opinion. Part of the sense of accomplishment and progression comes from gradually acquiring upgrades and tools which help you progress from surviving to thriving. Thriving never happens in Breathedge - collecting resources, breaking tools, managing a constantly shrinking inventory (due to the proliferation of tools - why are there *so many*?) never stops being frustrating. No suit upgrade (besides O2) seems to address the core annoyances. Basebuilding is so useless it's bizarre they bothered to include it. Gameplay is full of backtracking and scavenger hunts for the same bits, over and over. The game seems to relish forcing you back to a crafting station so you can trudge back through the needlessly winding corridors again.But this might all be tolerable if the game's writing or plot itself felt rewarding. Ok, humor is subjective and will hit different for different people. The game leads off with a disclaimer that it doesn't intend to offend anyone, and this pretty much signals what you need to know, for better or worse. I think some of the macabre gags around bizarre crew deaths are pretty clever. But on the whole the humor, and almost any flavor text or bit of dialogue, is equally tedious. It's a rehash of '00s internet humor with a bit of #mensrights touch-up. Relatively mild, but at the same time entirely unoriginal. Women can't open jars, am I right? Oh, you've heard that one before? It's telling that a major recurring punching bag is feminism, meanwhile the only female entities in the game are a talking pair of breasts and a moaning AI. I'm not sure they're proving the point they intended.I think there are some interesting gameplay ideas here. I probably would have enjoyed it more if it had been half as long, had half the tools, half the jokes... but even then I'm not sure it would be recommended.For a bit more constructive feedback, since I really do respect the visual storytelling, attention to detail in the environment, and the promise of the core loop:- Have tools combine to form tools with higher durability and multiple uses. This gives more inventory space and less frustrating with backtracking, win-win.- Add an upgrade for the vacuum vehicle to introduce storage capacity. Reduces extensive and *slow* backtracking which currently plagues almost every quest and lets the user attempt to pack for their scenario.- Cut half the dialogue triggers. Your jokes are interrupting each other and they're not all winners. I'm sure I missed some genuinely good moments because I walked a bit too quickly.- Too late for this, but if you really want to do a running gag on "masculinism," your sexualized / infantilized characters should be men. Y'know, it just fits better in-fiction. Nobody does moaning male AIs, so the unexpected nature adds to the joke!I know real people make games, and I don't want to devalue your effort. It probable comes across that way. Technically this game is well-made and the mechanics are getting there. I recognize the humor factor is probably not for me and that's cool. Congrats on finishing something impressive, but that just doesn't change whether I found it enjoyable in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica, if Subnautica was developed by Russian 13-year-olds.It has some pretty big flaws. It has base building! But only really at the end of the game, when it doesn't provide any help with your biggest issues (junk storage and sorting), and you lose resources if you take things apart after building them, so it's just bad when compared to Subnautica's easy to do, easy to tear apart, provides-convenient-storage-and-power-and-food-growing-in-the-mid-game.It has a pretty long, cynically funny story! But the last third of the story is a terrible railroad, with no real thinking or planning but instead a lot of "go build this thing, make your way all the way back through all of the empty hallways to your ship to make it, then come back through all of those empty hallways to get back here and use it." Also, the story likes to veer into bathroom humor. A lot.Overall, it's got an okay story, awful voice acting (the narrating computer talks too fast to be understood a lot), sad base building, wonky combat you should avoid whenever possible, a terrible third act, but a generally good "explore areas to find parts and ideas so that you can open up new areas to explore for parts and ideas". But it's also under $20, so, eh. It falls on the side of "sure."
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a good game. The graphics are nice. It's funny. But WOW it's makes you just not want to play anymore after about an hour. I gave it several retries but it is such a pain to get out of the starting area. Looking for everything you need. Always almost running out of O2. The controls are to floaty. Even in the menu. It's almost like the devs were trying to make a game that sucks the fun out really quick. I really don't get what they were going for here. It's less like a game and more like torture. It's just not fun. But man, it could be a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Totally loved this. The game is incredibly polished for Early Access, I'd go so far as to say it's release worthy albeit that the content needs to be expanded on. Gameplay wise some have likened it to Subnautica in space. I can see where they are coming from, but be cautioned, this is a more narrative led experience with resource gathering and crafting built in to avoid it being a pure walking (floating) simulator. As it stands there is no base building and I'm not sure there will be. It is not a survival sim.Along with the great look and feel of the game the biggest USP is the dark and silly humour of the game. The whole premise and narrative is, well, it's silly, childish and refreshing. Never have I been seconds from asphyxiation and laughing too. Well there was that one time but I don't listen to INXS anymore.If I have to be critical I'd say it can be a little grindy, needing to collect or search out resources to make a tool or item. It's not the worst, it's not hours upon hours of grind and I think it feels worse because you're not absolutely progressing the story during these moments so it feels like a lull. Upon reflection, maybe that is a good thing, what great times feel good without bad times to compare them too? Hell, the game even pokes fun at the grind.At a £10 I'd suggest any PC gamer grab this quick. Watch a Youtube if you want to get a better feel but don't watch too much as to spoil the story laid out so far. If they never added content I'd be mad at them for depriving me of more of this, but I'd be totally satisfied with what I received so far for this Early Access game. Some EA games are a risk but this is one of those rare gems that might just be worth your time stepping in early on.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna compare this to Subnautica a lot.The good thing about Subnautica is that you can always go to the surface for more air and when you get vehicles just hop on into the vehicle to restore your air supply but in this game your can only refill your air in very few specific places, in these air balloons you can craft which hold 500 air which isn't nearly enough for when you start to explore around the area with 200 air supply on your back and finally through air candles which instantly refill your air, one is 40 the other 200. The problem is that the game seems to be kinda sparse of resources so I'm worried about spending a ton of crafting materials to craft candles only to waste them all.Either way, if you do craft some candles and explore you will reach that point where you need to return to a air supply or you will die and have to reload the game (you do not respawn back at your habitat like in Subnautica) and at this point a lot of the game is basically just holding down the W key while hitting shift every once in a while to use your boost. There's no enemies to avoid and whole lot of nothing in space, so just hold down W. I listened to a podcast while doing it so I could have some form of entertainment and even then it was so mindnumbingly boring.I also don't know what to do. In Subnautica it was simply to kind drive you forward because of the "crush depth". You want to explore further but can't, because crush depth, so you upgrade your seamoth and can reach further down, you get the uboat and prawn and upgrade theirs too and reach further and eventually you find one of many tunnels leading further and further down and you know what to do. It is a very simple formula to drive the player forwards without really telling them what to do. Just: Go deeper.But in Breathedge I have no idea what the ♥♥♥♥ I'm doing. I have no idea what the ship I was on was about with coffin's, mannequin sections, smugglers who smuggled paint and a military section with droids. What the hell is this ship? Why did it crash? What is your goal? If it is told through the radio messages or whatever then yeah I kinda tuned them out. Why? Cause every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ line is a joke. So how am I supposed to know when the game is being serious and when it isn't? How am I supposed to know when information is important or when it's just taking the piss?And once I reach the "new base" (the second cabin with air and a crafting table where I got 200 air supply) the game suddenly opens up way too wide and I have no idea where I should be going and after exploring a while and going back to my new base a couple of times I've realized how much of the game is just holding down the W key. I can craft something to increase my boost but I need crafting materials that I have no idea where to get and... Well I'm just tired of it.There is no world to explore like in Subnautica. It's space. Literally. So what do you find in an asteroid belt in space where a big ship crashed? Bits of ship, asteroids and space. Repeat. And the only things you find is these little setpieces that are always jokes. And I mean that, every single one of them is a joke. Only random corpses out in space aren't jokes but that's just it they're random corpses, no environmental storytelling to them. And the game is beautiful and has this haunting atmospheric music that completely clashes with the obnoxiously humorous tone of the "story".The constant jokes.The empty nothing.My finger aching from holding down the W key so much.It's not fun.And it's not Subnautica. It's been said time and time again but do not buy this under the pretense that "but maaaaybe it's kinda like Subnautica" cause it is not. It is not Subnautica.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is a space based comedic puzzle/explorer/collector/survival gameThe comedy is very tryhard at times but despite that it is still funny, You are stranded in a small RV style ship that can't go anywhere and you need to find resources but you have limited breath.Work on ways to improve the range you can travel through colder areas where you need to find ways to keep warm or just so far it can't be done with the oxygen you can carry. I keep returning for an hour or 2 at a time and definitely recomend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica, right at the start of the game, allows you to exist in a massive area, craft from a massive list, and access a massive upgrade set. The main appeal of Subnautica is its ability to overwhelm. You're constantly going to find more, and more, and more, and eventually conquer it all.Breathedge, on the other hand, is about being small. The main drawback of Breathedge is its ability to limit.  At any given time, you just don't have access to very much. You get oxygen at limited locations, so you're stuck at a small radius around them. You float slowly in space, and you will constantly concern yourself with building extra oxygen generators to go a bit further. You don't explore a map, you explore a radius. It's never a big one.There's not much to craft. Most of the time, you're building from a small list of fragile tools, or more oxygen generators to expand your radius just a little bit. Resource collecting becomes tedious, where it should be exciting/tense. Nothing interesting to build, travel is slow, and you're never far from your base, so there's no risk or skill involved. What's around that corner? Just three more oxygen generators to go!Did I mention that oxygen generators are finite? The simple act of exploring limits your ability to explore. I can't tell if this game even wants you to have fun. Why did they do this?There's a few upgrades, but they resemble the most boring upgrades of Subnautica. Want to go near something cold? You'll need a heat upgrade. We're picking the bottom of the barrel for interesting upgrades, and this is still the beginning of the game.That's my review. It is over now. Anything below is not really review, but thoughts.The HUMOR. I REALLY like the idea. You're in a desperate, depressing situation and everywhere you look is awful. The game subverts this by constantly making poop jokes at you. As well, this is a genre-deconstruction aiming at problems in most survival games. If the gameplay was really strong, I have a good feeling that these jokes would have landed, and would have brought something unique to the genre.But the humor twists and the game feels like it is mocking itself.- EARLY you're tasked with building some useless item "because the devs decided you should". It SHOULD be funny because you don't have time to waste. It fails because everything else you can build feels about as useless. The game is just pointing out that there's nothing great to build.- The protagonist is generally incompetent, failing to do many scripted events. It SHOULD be funny because this is a difficult situation to survive and yet you are somehow going to. It fails because the gameplay feels very limited. You actually feel incompetent. Thanks for reminding me, game!- The game is set in a Soviet space-age, really cool setting! It doesn't really do anything with this setting though.Breathedge proves that you can't both deconstruct survival games and be a mediocre survival game.

_childDocuments_.review: In the first sequence, you need to pick up a piece of gum and use it to plug a gas leak. I opened the inventory, assigned the gum to a hotkey, and then pressed B, the "No" button with the intent of closing out the menu. But wait, the B button doesn't close the inventory, it causes you to drop whatever you're holding. No big deal, I'll just close the inventory and... the gum is gone. Just gone. I managed to softlock myself in the first minute of the game. On a subsequent attempt, I managed to bug out the oxygen system, giving myself unlimited oxygen. That's pretty much my experience of Breathedge.Beyond the terrible controls and bugs, the writing of this game is god awful. It's trying to rip off the dry wit of Subnautica's PDA, but it comes off like a bumbling used car salesman trying to do stand up. Adding "probably" after a sentence doesn't make it a joke. Talking fast isn't inherently funny. Humor is all about careful timing and picking exactly the right word. That's why translating jokes is incredibly difficult. It's nearly impossible if, like the devs, you don't have a solid grasp of English grammar. Oddly, this is the second Russian survival crafting game I've played with professional level voice actors reading a script of mangled English. Please, game devs: before you invest any money in voice acting, hire a fluent English speaker to localize your script.

_childDocuments_.review: Advertises itself as Subnautica in Space, but doesn't even come close to the quality of that game.While visually this game is amazing, and controls, while floaty, are great (and the floatiness makes sense, since it's in space), the crafting interface is absolutely terible and completely unintuitive. The tutorial voice talks too fast to follow en subtitles disappear quite fast, making infodumps hard to catch. Furthermore, the objectives given are incredibly obtuse, especially if the instruction is to craft certain objects. It's never actually explained how the crafting works, the menus are hard to navigate, gathering resources or where to get what is found in an encyclopedia that I accidentally stumbled upon. I could go on.The humor is funny, but tries way too hard, opting to go for a Deadpool-movie-style opening credit sequence before even establishing the setting or initial plot of what we're looking at, *unlike* Deadpool. This extends back into the obtuse crafting where the game has you craft "Crap imposed on you by the developers", without mentioning that that is *the actual name of an item you're supposed to make*. You have to find this out by digging through the menus. The game is clearly more concerned with being funny than with being fun to play. Had the humor been the exact same, but the crafting menus and instruction/tutorials more clear and streamlined, I'd probably have loved it. As it is, though, I can't recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: How can a game be intense and boring at the same time? Breathedge is a survival resource management game in space. You and your immortal chicken ... yes I know how that sounds ... gather ice, food, metal and much, much more from the various wrecks surrounding your own crash site in order to upgrade your oxygen tanks, movement speed and tools. The constant danger of suffocation in the loneliness of murderous space is transported very well. The humor ranges from very very immature to really funny slapstick-like. Why I stopped playing is the sense of crawling, almost inconceivable progress. It's so slow, I started cheating unlimited oxyen. That made the scope of boredom and slow gameplay and tedium much more clear. Clear enough to make me not want to experience the rest of the game. I didn#t reach basebuilding, I didn't find a vehicle, so my experience is pretty surely not representative of the full game. But I just don't want to go on. It is a good game, I'm just not patient enough to grind more resources to find the next crash site that gives me one more blueprint to make one more thing to unlock one more upgrade to reach the next crash site, all with minutes of downtime floating very slowly from one site to another. etc. etc.Follow my curator at

_childDocuments_.review: The only distinguishing characteristic of this game compared to other gather and craft survival games is the fact that it is set in space. The game is extremely linear with the only real sandbox element being create your own space station. This is only really necessary in the first half of the game then you are thrown into the next part of the game and that function becomes locked out. It's a translated game and you can tell the creators wanted to make it a funny game that makes fun of space tropes and pop culture but it may be with the fact its translated but between that and the semi robotic performance of the voice actor it just really misses the mark. I didn't find anything offensive about the performance but it just wasn't engaging or funny, it was very meh! There's also a lot of overlapping and timing issues with dialogue in cut scenes so it was hard to sometimes get the full scope of the story.The craft gathering concept seems broken and unbalanced where resources you desperately need in large quantities are very hard to find and the rare components are literally everywhere. There are also time where you reach the end of an area and are told to craft an item which you now have access to so you can proceed. You are then forced to trek all the way back to the crafting area in your ship to build it just to head back, There's absolutely nothing added to this to benefit you, no alternate path, chance to gather extra loot, you just have to trek back because ..... why not?The game feels very disjointed, it really feels like the creators had created a concept at the start and changed their mind halfway through. The game at both ends feel very different. At the start of the game its very satisfying gathering the resources, there's a lot of scope to create equipment and spacesuits. Then it just dies, you create tools which end up having only enough uses in the game that you only need once and alot of what kept you engaged at the start just disappears.I only completed this game because after 10 hours I felt committed. The game is really disappointing I feel mainly because it could've been really great but the creators just went off course.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those moments where i REALLY wish i could give a mixed review. EDIT: turned into a no after finishing it, the last part is a 5 hour "walk back and forth" simulator.Overall, the game has enough going for it to make me put yes. but the lack of polish, and the sometimes extreme tediousness really prevents me from actually recommending people to get this game.i too have heard it called "Subnautica in space", but it's extremely far from it. yes, the basic mechanics are there, and there is some exploration with some cool environments. but the actual gameplay is somehow way less fun.My biggest gripe with it is the slow movement speed. you crawl at 6 m/s to places hundreds of meters away, by the time you arrive your oxygen is almost empty so you either spend only 30 seconds actually exploring a place before turning back, or you spam oxygen refills to stay there but when you do that, you'll have to go farm the materials for them back up, and guess what? even collecting materials is extremely tedious due to the slow movement and the low supply of oxygen.Yes you unlock tools later in the game to go faster, but guess what? the distances between points of interest also become way bigger, so the tediousness never goes away.aside that, the humor is fun with some REALLY funny bits and a whole lot of kind of funny things, the game is very playable but feels very clunky at times, and the story... well i guess 10 hours in there isn't really a story, just a series of gags. curious to see if the ending is worth it, because yes i haven't even finished it yet... should have probably put it on casual difficulty idk

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play  since I found out that it finally released out of early access because its combination of space exploration, survival mechanics and humour looked appealing enough. Yet, in the end, I was surprised that I enjoyed its comedic aspect the most, which hooked me up right from the beginning.As a passenger of a massive spaceship, you are delivering your grandfather’s body to a funeral, along with hundreds of other people. You are also taking care of grandpa’s chicken, as that was his dying wish. Its survival is apparently crucial, yet it is only dumbfoundingly looking at you. As if it were judging you. Nevertheless, a sudden explosion tears the ship into pieces. Luckily, you survived! Everyone else seems to be dead, though. It looks like you are all alo-🤖: .Well, it seems that our talkative AI companion, who provides both guidance and comedic relief, decide to intervene here as well. Breaking the fourth wall type of humour is its speciality, meaning that it realizes its presence in the game. And in the review, too, I guess. In any case, I actually thoroughly enjoyed the AI’s presence for the whole time, and I had several laughs. Beware that it talks a lot, as it comments on every action you do. It also occasionally insults your character, who messes up everything he touches because he is dumb as a rock.You are not going to spend your time mindlessly floating around, as you find out soon enough that a spaceship called Normandy might be your ticket home. It is pretty far from you, though. To survive this long and dangerous journey, you will need to get better equipment, as well as enough food, drinks and oxygen. Satisfying these basic needs of yours can be done via consumable items or by building small refilling stations. Thus, exploration and collecting various materials will become your routine. While common resources, such as metal or nutritions, are harvestable by your bare hands, the rarer ones, like aluminium, requires craftable tools, a drill in this case. Sometimes there might be environmental obstacles, such as dangerously cold areas or electricity. To get rid of the second one, you can use that chicke-🤖: .Even though this gameplay loop of constant collecting, crafting, and upgrading is quite simple, it is still satisfying enough to motivate you in continuing. However, what I loved the most was the exploration itself. There are tons of spaceship’s debris, asteroids and dead bodies for you to discover. Finding out about your crewmates’ last moments might be hilarious or creepy. Apart from that, there are tons of various references and easter eggs. The exploration stands out more due to the marvellous audiovisuals, which create a dense and gripping atmosphere. Sometimes you might even stumble upon pieces of art that remind me of soviet retrofuturism, and at times you can even hear Russian compositions. 🤖: .As you slowly upgrade your stuff and explore further, you suddenly get contacted by a new person. Oh, it is your Babe! Wait, who? That does not matter, as she belongs to you now! She constantly sends you messages in broken English abou-🤖: . Hush! Well, let me just say that she offers a bit different  on this whole situation.Now, you might think that the constant jabbering from these two characters might get annoying or stop you from enjoying the gameplay. The opposite is true because the number of monologues balances the gameplay loop itself, so it feels as if you were actually progressing even though you just collected some new materials. I loved their presence, as they made the world more alive. I was about fifteen hours in, and I thought that this experience would stay great.At this so-called peak of the game, you can finally start building your own base and even beautify it with furniture. You even get access to smaller vehicles, which make travelling a bit easier and faster. By now, I mostly had everything I needed, so the surviving aspect started fading away and collecting the same resources became a bit tiresome. This issue accompanies an unexpandable inventory system, which forces you to backtrack quite a lot to your base. I was willing to overlook these issues, as I still enjoyed the exploration a lot.However, once you reach a certain point in  last third, the gameplay suddenly becomes linear. There are no longer new resources or blueprints to find, and the game hands to you everything you might need on a silver platter. The exploration disappears too. You realize that everything you have done so far, including building your base, was useless and a waste of time. It turns into a walking simulator, a boring one, and it honestly felt like a slap in the face. From now on, you just galavant from one plot point to another. While the story was enjoyable as ever, the gameplay dragged it down to the point that I was forcing myself to finish it. 🤖: .The game tries to spice up this terrible linearity by focusing more on combat with robots and spaceship’s defensive systems. When I think about action in games, I imagine it should be something enjoyable. Well, it is a boring mess in here. My projectiles sometimes did not do any damage at all, and I even witnessed enemies committing suicide. As if even they realized they could not take this any longer. Well, these combat sections are just horrendous and unintuitive, and I wished for them to end every time I got into one.Honestly, if I did not enjoy its story, I would not even bother finishing . The last third, which lasts about six hours, feels like a worse undeveloped experience that devoured my initial enjoyment, like when a black hole swallows a star. However, it would not be fair to give it a negative rating. A vast majority of this title is still great, and I can recommend it to anyone who wants to explore outer space for a bit. I would just wait for a sale and keep these issues in mind. 🤖:

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:* Very pretty game - makes good use of the Unreal engine.* Interesting, well-developed environment. Presents a survival challenge that is not stressful but not easy, either.* Great UI. Well-organized, responsive, intuitive. Never gets in the way of the gameplay.Cons:* EPISODIC CONTENT. This game ends abruptly after 3-6 hours of gameplay. It's really just one big area, and when you reach a certain point, the credits roll.Now, episodic content by itself isn't the problem. Lots of "episodic" games get marketed that way - it's called "Episode 1" or "Season 1" or "Chapter 1," etc., and the sales page makes that aspect clear. The problem is that this one doesn't do that: the only indication on the game page is halfway through the Early Access write-up.I'd have felt quite differently had I known that it's episodic. (Then again, I probably wouldn't have bought it: too many epsiodic games never get finished.) The lack of marking here feels like a deliberate ripoff.* While the game *seems* open-world-ish, it's mainly a corridor in disguise. You start at point A. There are some things to do near point A, but fewer than it seems at first. The primary objetive is to figure out how to get to point B. Picture Dear Esther with a light survival / crafting element... that's Breathedge.* Weird political humor. There is a point in the game where you're suddenly subjected to some odd political commentary about "libtards." It's just weirdly and jarringly out of context. It's especially odd since the humor is particular to the U.S., and the developer is apparently Russian. I mean... well, I'll just leave it at that.* Lots of loose ends, due to the supposedly episodic content: containers that can't be opened; areas that are visible but not accessible. There's a case to store special items, but nothing in the actual game fits in it.Overall, this game was a letdown due to the length and the odd choices noted above.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially liked this game, subnautica in space, sounds golden. Then the little things started adding up. I stopped shortly after hitting chapter 4.The helper bot's weirdly paced voice juxtaposes the relaxing space music; I found it grating most times, even if the content was humorous.Every item has durability, and the durability is very small (most items have 15 uses and it breaks). This leads to a lot of back in forth. For example, you have 5 charges left on your scanner gun, decide to go check out the next objective, but there's 7 items to scan there. Your gun breaks after 5 and you gotta haul yourself all the way back to a crafting station. Then there's items like the repair tool, which also only has 15 uses, but those 15 last until chapter 4. You could just carry a backup for every item, but then you'll have no inventory. It just led me to a lot of unexpected frustration routinely. Maybe it's just me, but I made it to chapter 4 and I still had not unlocked any kind of base storage item, which led to my base's floor being littered with crafting supplies, which just seemed to decrease my fps as they all calculated collision with each other. Either the storage module is named weird, or I just never found it to scan. This grew more and more frustrating everytime i entered my base and had to dig through the clutter.Chapter 4 involves a pretty decent drive to the objective, but you get to that objective and there's a stark lack of crafting material, the game expects you to truck back and forth from chapter 2's area and that was the point I just gave up. Perhaps if the car had an inventory, but I just wasnt motivated enough to make the several trips back and forth and god forbid an item break while in chapter 4 and there's no plastic/alkali/resin/etc to fix it. Would require another trip back to chapter 2.So... subnautica in space, but more frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. Great mix of exploration and humor. Love all the references to other games, especially Alien: Isolation and Subnautica. I found it to be very fun, and had a blast playing it. However, I do have a couple nitpicks, but mostly just with the base building aspect in chapter 2/3.My main gripe is the fact that there doesn't seem to be a way to build/expand storage inside the base, or at least I could not find one. The only storage I found were the cabinets in the shuttles. Once those were full, I was forced to just dump everything on the ground near my research table. Secondly, I was confused by the ability to build a shuttle dock for the base, even though the only flyable shuttle is the Normandy, and by the time you get that flying you're off in chapter 4 in a new area, with no discernable way to get back... Overall, the base building aspect seemed a bit pointless, as it was only really useful for researching a couple of blueprints you needed in order to progress. I could not tell if the developers wanted this to be a genuine mechanic of the game, or if it was just there mostly as a joke, having to build it in order to research the suit and stuff.Luckily, the base building aspect was not a major factor, and I did still use the base to sleep and build/dock the vacuum/scooters and the space car. Another thing I'd like to suggest concerns the collectibles/random items found throughout the world. Once youve inspected them, they are "unlocked" for lack of a better term and can be viewed in the tab menu. However, once inspected, you can either pick them up or leave them where they are, and the collector I am tried to keep everything. I soon found my inventory full of useless crap lol. As long as you've inspected them, you dont need to pick them up and in fact there is no real value to pick them up as there is no way to really store/display them, and the collection shelf thing that you can build in your base will display what you have interacted with and doesn't require you to grab them. I think it would be better if either there was some dedicated object you could build in your base to store/display them.TLDR; Great game, very funny. Don't bother actually picking up the random collectibles, just "examine" them then press the mouse wheel to leave them where they are, unless you don't mind a constantly full inventory.Can't wait for the expansions!!!
