_childDocuments_.review: A game made with a tonne of love and very little care about how a player will approach the game. After following the tutorial for 10 minutes I was tasked with creating a debugging station. A look around my base and there's no station to fix up. So I go to the crafting station and under the stations tab there is nothing. So maybe I need to find a blueprint? So I go out and explore as far as my oxygen will take me. All I can find are Water, Food and Metal balls. There's containers, radios and the like, but they all require tools to open, but you can't make any tools because you need wire and batteries. After going all around and finding nothing I go to the forums. Seems the debugging station is considered a tool and it's not exactly called a debugging station (which anyone who's ever played an MMO will know that if it's not exactly called that, then it's not what you need). Now that I've found the debugging station I need wire. To get wire I'm told to disassemble radios from the forums, but you cannot take them apart without a tool that needs batteries. Since you cannot find a battery just floating around I search the forums again and find out that batteries are behind a door straight down from your starting location and you need another tool to open the door... Why is this so frustratingly difficult?? I'm sure there has to be some easy way to do all the steps I need to get past the 3rd task in the tutorial, but if this is how obtuse the start of the game is, I do not want to continue to play it. So it's a refund for me!

_childDocuments_.review: RedRuins Softworks has designed a beautiful-looking game that lacks an interesting story or any reason to enjoy its sandbox mechanics. The unsufferable humor quickly becomes unbearable after the first few minutes and only worsens as the game sluggishly progresses. If you still wish to play Breathedge despite its many shortcomings, I would recommend playing for the first half and then promptly quitting, as you’ve experienced the best part of this mediocre game.However, if you dare to stomach the unending cringe and distasteful gameplay, I would recommend playing on Story Mode to save yourself hours of restricted grinding. To conclude, playing Breathedge is the equivalent of unironically beating yourself in the head to death with a literal in-game item, “crap imposed by the developers.” RedRuins had an excellent foundation for a unique outer space survival sandbox experience but ended up a jumbled mess of half-baked ideas. Breathedge sadly turned to be nothing more than a festering heap of unending fart jokes and pointless grind fests.

_childDocuments_.review: Rarely have I played a game where it felt like I was the one being played, and not the other way around - and I loved (almost) every second of it!Breathedge is a funny, surprising, genious and at times very frustrating game. It takes you from big, beautiful sceneries in outer space, where time seems to stand still and there is so much to explore, to small, stupid (in a good way) and humouristic details that dumbfound you in the best of ways. The smaller details in the game, such as funny posters, notes, labels on mugs or even chickens, take the story to a deeper level and give you an understanding of the world in which the game takes place. The story is completed by a combination of both smaller and larger details that I never even thought of while doing the quests. So when you move along in the storyline, things start to complement each other and make sense in a brilliant and sometimes twisted way.   The creators really took a chance regarding the sense of humour in the game, and I know it might not be for everyone, but for people like me, it really hit a spot. Their ability to give hope to the players throughout a quest, just to take it away in a hilarious way is just pure genious. I've never felt more but*****ed in a game before, and I would definitely play it again!

_childDocuments_.review: Lets start simple, whatever you might *think* Breathedge is, it isn't.  I had to read a few of the positive reviews before writing this and I'm definitely going to be criticizing the game for seemingly all the things other people "liked" about it.  It's odd, there are positive reviews explaining that the game is tedious, poorly structured, and superfluous *but* it's funny.  I agree.  I found it to be tedious, poorly structured, and superfluous: that's precisely the reason I didn't like it.  It's not even hard to articulate why: everything in the game is an excuse to get to  irreverent non sequitur commentary delivered by your spacesuit.It's like, I get it.  The joke is that it's a bad game.  The developers are self-depreciating, the game frequently quips at how meaningless or stupid many of its decisions are and I'm nodding my head.  At one point the suit AI literally goes, "Does this game even have any mechanics?"  No, it doesn't.  That's the joke.  Ha ha.  Would be *nice* however, if it did.  The game this most reminded me of was that Devolverland promotional game made for E3 a few years back with crafting mechanics bolted on.  It's not that Breathedge is bad.  It's not incompetent enough to be bad.  At the same time though, it has a careless feeling rather than a carefree one.For example, there's this running chicken gag.  I mean, the game certainly says there is but it seems to have forgotten to have it *be* a running gag.  The chicken is used once at the beginning and then to short out electric currents sometimes and then at the very end.  If the chicken had been a prominent character, been involved in more cutscenes, maybe was responsible for some of the many failures you experience then it could make sense.  But nope.  The game just *says* it has a running chicken gag and I guess that's the part where I fall over laughing until I cry.  It definitely feels like no one cared or even noticed.Lest you think this is a quality only of the writing, no.  For example, the thirst and hunger mechanics.  You find food and water everywhere you go and it takes forever to run out: so why is it here?  Because survival games have these mechanics hur hur hur?  I'm not even sure that's it.  Early on you can craft a "better" helmet.  Spoiler alert: you just paint the helmet entirely red and can't see anything when wearing it.  It's funny, but here's the truth of the game: radiation is also a non-issue.  You just have to complete the quests, the actual rating doesn't do anything.  Again, hur hur so subversive.  The game is seemingly making fun of itself, and yet it's still just just about achieving the goal of being precisely what it's mocking.  In my opinion, it fails to meet its own low standards thanks to aspiring to nothing more than minimal competency.So no, I can't recommend Breathedge.  I can praise it for it's technical feats, but being basically playable and looking nice is the bar games are expected to clear.  As far as unique selling points it has a nice pulpy sci-fi aesthetic and I can at least admit a few lines made me chuckle, but as a complete package I guess the joke is that anyone like me would actually play it to the end and be disappointed.  It's hard to critique something that is knowingly bad, Breathedge is basically just Sharknado in game form: it aspired to be mediocre in pursuit of a premise but I'm not going to give it a thumbs up just because it knows it's dumb.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Answer: It's BoringLong Answer: Movement in this game is just so painfully slow. I cannot adequately express how slow the movement is. The environments, at least from a distance, are incredibly samey so unless you remember exactly what and where you've explored previously you'll likely suffer from a lot of wasted trips and time. Your oxygen depletes quickly...which admittedly is in the name, but it's to such a degree that even when you do find a location, it's highly unlikely that you'll have time or resources to explore. The item durability is ridiculously low, ensuring that you'll use up even more resources trying to maintain your capacity to function. The jokes weren't exactly anything to write home about, and everything in between is, well, dead space. Crafting exists but it doesn't exactly feel rewarding, partly because of the item durability thing, and partly because it spends so much time trying to land jokes when you accomplish things that it ruins its own moments of progression. If you want a better Space based game, I'd recommend Hardspace Shipbreaker. If you want a better survival game, Subnautica or Raft would probably be a better bet. If you want a good space survival game, well, keep looking because it isn't here.

_childDocuments_.review: Had the general gameplay been less tedious, i would probably have recommended the game.as a survival crafting game, one of the things it does do quite well is the slow progression of objectives, in the form of"in order to complete this objective, you need to do these things, and in order to do those things, you need some other things".It continues this through most of the game, which was a nice progression in the game.one of the biggest issues with the game is the slow movement, both in space, in stations and even on vehicles, everything just feels immensly slow, as all of the important areas are far from eachother, you will be stuck just slowing traveling to one area from the other with not much else going on.not to mention weird design choices in regards to crafting and researching, some things will take 10 to 20 minutes to research and you just sorta have to twiddle your thumbs until it's finished.there's an issue with the dialogue if you move too far into a new area or activate one of the generic voice lines, the first voice line will be cut off, this happening quite frequently and got annoyingwhich is a shame because the story and humor is probably the better or at least more interesting part of the gamethe gameplay also more or less changes style after chapter 3 and becomes a "space flight" game with the regular crafting mechanics whenever you enter a station, where for some reason you have to run back and forth from your spaceship to craft stuff and where ever you need to use said crafted stuff, which just feels like throughout the game and the icons.then after loading into the game another day, it was suddenly in english, so idk what happened. there is a DLC, but it was just "see how long you can survive in space"the humor in the game is hit and miss, since humor is subjective, how good it will be, is down to the individual.some of it is fun, some not so much and some is just utterly confusing.there _childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game at 70% off for $7.49. I can only recommend this game at or below that price.Overall it can be a fun distraction with a couple laughs here and there. The humor relies heavily on visual gags and references to the point where it can be detrimental. I recommend switching to the Russian dubbing w/ subtitles to go along with the soviet cosmonaut theme.On gameplay: The game starts off strong with the key elements of any survival crafting game, small starting base, crafting bench, environment full of debris and materials. However as you progress through the chapters (specifically moving into chapter 4) survival-crafting-exploration is mostly dropped. Instead you get to pilot your ship to a handful of pre-marked stations that are completely linear to explore. These stations WILL waste your time by forcing you to backtrack through their linear hallways in order to craft arbitrary key items in order to progress. I didn't enjoy this portion of the game at all and I wouldn't recommend it if I paid full price.I've seen a lot of people compare this game to Subnautica which was one of the reasons I purchased it. The game is more enjoyable if you treat it as a parody of Subnautica in my opinion. You will be disappointed if you're expecting anything near that quality of survival / crafting / exploration / story from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game right here? This IS Subnautica in space. And that's really all you need to know. Love Subnautica? Get this game. Hate Subnautica? Don't get this game.I give this game a 8/10 while I'd give Subnautica a 9,5/10. I could've given this game a 10/10. Why didn't I? Because -- and this is so incredibly subjective! -- I really really REALLY hate the fact that they went for this over the top comedic style. Just imagine a Subnautica kind of game being stranded in space -- with nobody around, with a claustrophobic sense of utter solitude and loneliness always nagging at you -- that would take itself serious. I think the majority of us gamers would be able to lose ourselves in such a game completely, wanting the breath-taking view of wide open space as we hang still in non-gravity to be the last thing we see before we draw our last breath IRL.But we didn't get that. We almost did.

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, but I feel like this game needs more people warning about the back third or so of the game.  The first half to 2/3 of the game is a sometimes overly grindy, but I found satisfying and rewarding, survival/crafting game much in the same vein as Subnautica.  When I got my first vehicle and could finally move 30m/s instead of 6 I was thrilled much like when I got my sea moth for the first time.  But after a certain point in the story the game warps you to a new map and the rest of the game is entirely different.  You never go back out into space.  No gathering, no building bases, no meaningful exploration.  You're now stuck in a ship and all you do is dock at various locations to learn some story and gather some materials.  There's a ton of backtracking through empty halls just to craft a new random part and then plug it in somewhere back through more empty halls.  Everything that made the game enjoyable is gone and replaced by some of the worst gameplay I've experienced in years.  It was enough to make me quit, and highly NOT recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Tedious.Lots of tracking around back and forth very slowly in space (even with the booster upgrade), very limited crafting/upgrades and not much to discover in the early game which just makes hovering around slowly in space even more painful, and is then hampered further by a traditional save system (save your game regularly manually, no quicksave, no save slots, if you die you have to load -- which is bad if your last autosave is a while ago and you've saved somewhere that results in you dying after you load). If you dropped belongings and respawned in your ship, that would have worked better.Resources are kind of hard to see and sometimes you'll be trying to collect them and clicking just won't do anything (this happens with all interactions in game), and then you'll accidentally bump the resource and it just rockets away never to be found again. Early game you need lots of junk but they don't even give you a way to create storage trunks or anything until some time later in the game, so the floor of my spacepod was just littered with items, trying to arrange them in piles, rolling around on the ground.The humour is occasionally alright but generally has a very repetitive tone and gets old quickly. There are jokes in the game about wasting player time with pointless filler activities, which are themselves pointless filler activities that don't even reward the player, so... is it self-aware or not? After finding the captain's cockpit which ended up being a long, meaningless quest with no new unlocks (at a point where I was flush with resources and starved of anything meaningful to make with them), I came all the way back to my base and thought... Wow, I don't think I can stomach doing another long, slow crawl out to the end of this linear piece of space (because it's kind of all in a straight line, so when you want to go somewhere new first you go past aaaaall the things you've already explored every time and back again).And the visibility issues! It's already hard enough to see little items floating around, but in some areas, you get really cold and your screen frosts over so you literally can't see anything. The solution? Alcohol! (no pun intended but I'll take it). But the game has the most realistic, nauseating "you're way too drunk" visual I've ever seen, and it actually made me dizzy and nauseous in real life. It gives you double/triple vision and wobbles your screen around, so you're trading being unable to see through frost for barely being able to see anyway and now feeling ill, and at least where I was up to, those were your only 2 options for exploring some areas.The graphics are nice, and the audio is kind of ordinary but passable, but the game just doesn't feel fun!

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop is terrible. You go out, have to get AT LEAST three metal, get other resources, go back in. Go back out, get five things, go back in. Explore for like thirty seconds at best before running back for air. Even with the oxygen stations it's hard to actually do anything, since they take rarer resources to make so you have to be careful with placing them, making long exploration trips nearly impossible. The humor is fine I guess, but it doesn't make up for the fact that you use most of your resources remaking tools that broke instead of progressing the game, just leading to a long grind with what, a good job at the end?As far as controls go, they're fine. I don't particularly like how realistic the no friction of space is since it makes resource collection that much more frustrating. Everything is floaty which makes sense, but doesn't make it any less frustrating.As far as looks, it's fun. 1960s decor is fun to look at in space. Graphics are pretty, exploring the wreckage is fun. But previous points make it hard to justify it. Mind you, this is the standard experience. There is the story mode, but it limits your ability to get achievements so if you want the completion score, you have to play the standard mode or one of the harder modes. Ultimately I don't recommend this game, the grind really isn't worth it and the story is rather predictable. This is comparing it to other resource collection games like Minecraft, Astroneer, Satisfactory, and others. I'm a HEAVY fan of these kinds of games, so even with the bias of loving resource collection gameplay loops, AND loving space themed adventures. I just cannot recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly obnoxious oxygen system, freezing system, radiation system... so many limiting systems designed to slow gameplay to a crawl and hide the lack of content (and yes, I got the first oxygen upgrade and oxygen station blueprint). Even worse, the unbelievably stupid tool durability system requiring you to rebuild every single tool after a few uses, another design intended to make you do mundane tasks over and over, gathering the same basic resources, in hopes that you won't notice that there isn't actually any game here.The slapstick humor is funny in the intro, and then quickly becomes forced and uninteresting. The funnier bits tend to happen while in space, where you are constantly in frantic search for useful objects before your ludicrous oxygen limit is hit, so you don't even pay attention to what the guy's saying. Seriously, the oxygen system here makes the basic, un-upgraded O2 tank in Subnautica look extremely generous.I gave it its less-than-2-hour shot, and ultimately refunded it. This isn't worth the price even with the -33% sale.

I have definitely had my fair share of laughs throughout my game play. Although sometimes, you may be a little lost with what tools you need or resources. Don't give up and keep going. This game is not a quick one. So enjoy the ride and happy surviving! I can't wait to see more from this game. I would love to see some kind of coop mode but I understand that this is more of a singleplayer story survival game.P.S. Those reviews of this game that say something like "half an hour was enough for me to know this game is not good", are not covering most of the game. The game is truly large and the story is amazing. This game is just what I needed.

_childDocuments_.review: There and back again: the space round trip simulator.This is a tough review, the game starts interesting, you will get flashbacks from Subnautica, but in a space setting, with a lot of humor. While some people don't like the constant jokes, I thought it was ok, the jokes are not always hitting but fine, that's the spirit of the game, I don't mind it and sometimes it's funny.The problem is that the only interesting part of the game is the beginning. The game has good mechanics, but it needs tuning. Some parts feel like an uninteresting grind, at some point you want to start building things up to improve your conditions, but you're constantly looking for oxygen, and some of the puzzles are really hard to solve without looking them up. Or like you'll spend 30 minutes looking for an airlock: get oxygen, search, go back for oxygen, repeat. After a while you'll just start saving the game and go on search missions using candles and then load and go straight. Mechanics problem. I still had fun exploring the little areas in spite of the artificial limitations on oxygen.But fine. The base building doesn't bring much, and it never becomes your safe haven like your Subnautica base. It's ok I guess.Then when you hit the second half of the game, it's a pure slog, it's just a slow corridor simulator. It's actually worse than that, because you keep having to go back to build an item, walk 5 nonsensical miles of corridors, use the item, repeat. FOR HOURS. Sure this makes the game last longer, but at what cost? I stopped having fun after the first warp, it's literally the same thing over and over, and not only that, but you spend most of the time walking or slowly navigating your ship. The two boss fights in the game are literally the same. Why not shorten the experience to wrap up the story? Why are there so many endless hallways? The level design is kind of crazy. I imagine the devs must have had a 10x walk speed hack to test it, I don't understand how nobody realized that the hallways and the constant backtracking was not adding anything to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can just barely recommend this game, it's quirky, funny, and has an absurdist comedy angle that's great. The first half of the game is a masterpiece, a 3-D graveyard space crafting survival sim with dark humor, engaging game play and is difficult enough to keep you sweating it out. But the later chapters are a slow, frustrating, too-easy, on-rails, linear, crap sack walking sim that SUUUUUUUUCKS. They clearly just slammed out the storyline with no attention to gameplay, and abandoned what made the game good to finish it. There are some funny pop culture and gamer references in the second half, though. Only buy this on deep discount, or if you are really into Vonnegut Jr./Douglas Adams/Dan Harmon style humor. I had super high hopes for the release after playing the early chapters, and I'm pretty disappointed. SAD!

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I had stopped playing before the two-hour mark and returned it.I absolutely love Subnautica and I was expecting the humor to be similar to Journey to the Savage Planet. Unfortunately, both the gameplay and humor fell flat for me.Pros:- Looks really pretty- The best joke is at the beginning when you can censor cigarettes and it turns them into carrots for the rest of the game.Cons:- A bit barren/lifeless. I know it's a space game but there wasn't much to interact with and no real threat level other than oxygen.- Grindy. Everything is spaced so far apart that it takes so long to do everything with how little oxygen you start with and tools break too often.- Pointless base-building. This game is pretty linearly designed, base building made hardly any sense seeing as I would never go back to the previous areas. They could have easily put in an extra shuttle as the next "base" as you continue the story and nothing would have changed. Also, the bases had unnecessarily segmented modules so only certain compartments could be built in each one, like why could I not build a storage module next to my crafting bench. And I hated how you'd lose building materials if you wanted to move things around. Takes the fun out of base building.- Completely different gameplay in the third part, not necessarily bad, but then it took EVEN LONGER to go to places and progress the story, it wasn't even a survival game at this point. Several times I had to go to a point, scan something, go back to my base to build the item, then run all the way back to progress the story. SO much wasted time forcing me to run back and forth.-Lastly, the humor. I enjoyed the pop culture references and a few jokes here and there, but overall the humor felt like a reddit troll trying to be edgy by making fun of marginalized people. That's not witty, it's boring and cringey. The game opens with a message about how the humor isn't intended to offend anyone, but it clearly is. That is the point of almost all the intractable display items you can pick up. I just wasn't here for it.Promptly uninstalled after forcing myself to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of this game is a flawed, but generally serviceable, survival game set in space. The last half is a brutally dull walking simulator that is almost entirely disconnected from the first half. All those things you scanned so you can build later? Useless. All those space station parts? Useless. Instead of anything building on the first half, you get filler like walking 250m to get to an obstacle, scan it to find a new item that you need to bypass it(made of common materials), walk back 250m to make that item, walk back again 250m to use it, collect the doohickey you need and finally, walk back the 250m again to complete this exercise. Wow.It's been so rare that a game has so completely disappointed me. I'm really at a loss for words.I don't know what happened that took this game off the rails after chapter 2, but it was horrible and I really hope the devs either patch it up or just learn from it for their next game, because the first two chapters were pretty good and had lots of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: The store page says the first chapter is basically finished.That said, all games have a guide, be it a dynamic tutorial that interupts the game as events happen, a pre game tutorial that forces you or shows you how to play the game or a story that guides you through gameplay goals.Now this game uses the latter, and at the beginning it does it fine, plug the hole, craft this basic tool, craft a joke to learn about gathering and refining, then after that it says hey heres an objective marker you have no way to get to good luck...The game has a useful 'encyclopedia' page where it generally tells you where to look for certain resources however... easy example, how do you craft sheers? The game doesn't tell you where you can find the scizzors you need and its obvious once you find it that youre meant to break open the crate beneath your ship but when you first start playing you have no idea what you can do and a grey box floating in space isnt the most obvious target under the preasure of suffocation. How hard is it to say "break open crates"?In general, progression isn't clear.The game feels like a very basic sandbox game with a bunch of random dioramas you can investigate and thats it, is that enough for a sandbox game? If you buy any other half finished survival game you will get much more of what you get here, which is to say theres nothing here and if there is the game doesn't give you any idea of it.The level of humour past the intro isn't anything to write home about. You come across a diaroma, you get a chuckle and then the game screams at you that you're about to start suffocating.At the current price its a reasonable gamble of getting more value at a later date for your money but if they keep increasing the price while adding more of the same content its value is going to plummet.Also I'm not quite sure what the game is trying to be. Is it just satire? Than why such a heay reliance on sandbox and survival elements and not more crafted story like at the beginning of the game? If its a sandbox/survival game wheres the plathora of craftable items you would find in any other sandbox/survival game?If the developers didn't write "At the moment, the first story chapter is implemented to the game. This is already a full-fledged part of the game, almost in the final quality..." I wouldn't be criticizing it so hard, but they did, so I am.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:Dr; A nice-looking, somewhat humorous, but EXTREMELY SHORT AND EASY GAME.This ISN'T Subnautica in space, or a beautiful-but-haunting exploration-survival game like Adr1ft. What is IS is a game with an extremely small amount of content. Without even trying, you can beat the game in an hour to an hour and a half. And thats it... no replayability due to the lack of content either.All you do is collect a few resources, make your way to a waypoint, collect a special resource, use it to make an upgraded space suit, then make your way to a second waypoint, and voila, the game is finished. Worth it for 5 bucks, not for 13.99

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this game is an attrocious timewaster.It has everything in it for a good game, EVERYTHING. But it's not. The graphics, the mechanics, the gimmicks, everything in this game could have made it good. But it can't put it all together, tries many thing, and fails at every single one of them.I could say there are three main phases of the game:1. Being lost phase. Goals are vague, oxygen is scarce, the player is working out of the starting spot and dropping oxygen balloons all over the place, trying to figure out how to progress. This part is the hardest survival portion of the game (still more frustrating than hard though).2. Base construction phase. After getting to the engineering shuttle the player can construct a base. It's entirely pointless, but the player can do it. This portion of the game revolves around vehicle-based exploration and doing laborous crafting tasks to work towards and end goal. I genuinely though this is where the game ends, but...3. The wtf spaceship story part. Well, turns out the developers forgot to progress the story in any significant manner through environmental storytelling in the survival phases, so there is a third, extremely dragged-out final portion where the normal space resource gathering part is taken away, the player drive a spaceship and docks at stations (the player can't leave the helm of the ship mid-flight). This part tries to do some story, but it's an extreme drag, and takes away most of the mechanics from the previous portions.So, it's a mess, but still salvageable. Now to the issues:a. Issues with the survival mechanics:- Never ran out of food or water. Never. It's just there to take some inventory space, it's plenty, but needs crafting so just a side bother.- The base is just pointless. There is literally NOTHING gained by building bases. By then the player can go vast distances and unlocked default unlimitted oxygen refill stations. The only partially useful tool in the base is the research table, that allows early unlocks of items, even though all recipes can be found in the world.- The base mechanics are badly though-out. Apart from being pojntless, constructing the base is a nuisance. Most modules are unlocked way too late, and the only semi-useful device, the lockers are restricted to habitation modules, so the have to be placed far from the crafting station, since that's not compatible with the habitation module. Why are lockers important? Because furniture are garbage. The two options for storage are lockers and coffers, coffers being availeable form the start. They hold the same number of items, but coffers are much smaller and can freely be placed. What's the issue then? Furniture items ARE NOT FIXED IN POSITION. They can be kicked around, and there is NO tool to move them, only disassembly (with ~50% materials refunded) and repeated placement. Coffers at least are free to replace, but to the greatest issue: the game physics system can't handle stacked items. Put one item on another, like a decor on a table, and it will inevitably go flying at a random time in the future (mostly after saves or loads). Literally a tiny decor statue flipped over my grand piano. Same is true for coffers. The player can't stack them, because they will start jumping around, can't put them on tables, because tables will throw them off, they can only be placed on the floor, and the limited flat surfaces on the crafting station. I really wanted to make a nice station, even though it's a singleplayer game, but this mess is prohibitive, making any effor literally wasted.b. Issues with the story:- There is none. Then there is something. The game wont spare time making pointless commentary on various things the player finds flying around, but up until unlocking the large spaceship, there is barely any story told. It's just: there is a signal, get to the signal. Meanwhile wondering at the odd thigns all around. This took me 20+ hours to get through.- After that it's at least "some" story, but becomes even more of a drag. In the end, it's something semi-decent, but neither goes for some intriguing story, nor for a comedic slam-dunk. It's just a resounding "meh".c. Humour:- It's not that there is bad humour in it. I expected a barrage of deadpan commie dadjokes, but nah, humour is mostly missing. There are a set of oneliners, most of those not qualify as funny. The game never tries to set up a punchline, only doing environmental commentry as jokes, but almost none lands due to the scenes not being clear or spectacular.- The chicken. Plenty potential humour, but none actually. There are about 3 or 4 uses for the chicken as a special tool, and it's not around while the player normally plays the game. It's only used frequently as a temporary disabler of electric traps.d. Pacing:- Yes, separate mention of pacing. Because it's ATTROCIOUS. The survival phases feel a bit like a drag, due to the limited things the player can do, and the vast distances that has to be covered, but still mostly fine... except for fixing the spaceship. The player needs to cover HUGE distances transporting components back and forth, the game only revealing the next required component when the previous one was placed, so it's a long flight many times back and forth...- But true attrocity follows in the last part of the game. It's a new definition of a drag. Running hundreds of meters on an empty serpentine corridor just to make reaching the destination a little (a lot) longer. Content-wise the last part of the game is 2-3 hours, but it's made MANY MORE by sheer annoyance and timewasting.  I almost smashed in my screen when I had to backtrack a 5 minute road to the ship, just because one of my tools broke that was required to fix a panel. It's consciously taking a piss on players.If not for the last part, I would have given a thumbs up to this game, saing it's a mediocre survival with lots of style and great ideas, though poorly executed. But no, after playing through the entire thing, it squarely fits in the DON'T TOUCH category. When the player starts having fun, the game takes it away, along with an unreasonable amount of time.

Just spamming voice and text lines is not going to help with that.The durability of the tools is just annoying, the crafting interface is annoying, the crafting times are annoying. Of course I explored and "grinded" in the meantime but it just stacks one tedious mechanic ontop of the next.They just seem to make you waste time so you don't realize how short and devoid of content this game is. _childDocuments_.review: This is a really phenomenal start to a game that isn't quite there just yet. Comparisons to Subnautica are in reference to the gameplay loop, rather than the world-building/exploration aspect. Wait till there's a bit more to it and I'd highly recommend this. For the price - it's a fun little package.  - Really solid atmosphere and polished graphics - decent gameplay loop but might dissappoint a little in terms of difficulty and story content. *Update* The lck of updates and clarity from the Dev team make this less appealing than it was at launch. Follow this game for a good while before investing. ----------------So Breathedge bills itself as a Subnautica-esque exploration survival game with an emphasis on dark humor. I'd say it hits most of those marks pretty well. I'll start with the comparison to Subnautica:I can see why people are saying this, the gameplay loop is super similar. (Exit base, go to new location, keep eye on oxygen, return before you die, find and craft better stuff to allow you to travel farther, etc...)Where it falls short for me, however, is that the space in Breathedge is far less interesting, and more challenging to explore than the ocean in Subnautica. The different locations are rather far apart, and you cannot move your base (yet) in order to facilitate further travel. The space inbetween locations isn't particularly interesting, although it is pretty. There are Oxygen Stations you can construct, but they're temporary and don't give you much time to think when you stop there. They're more like checkpoints. Overall - as long as the devs stick to their word - this comparison should become more apt as time goes on. So far, I find myself lacking the motivation to venture too far from the pod just due to the fat that O2 seems so scarce and difficult to build. Hopefully they balance that moving forward. As for the humor - it's actually very funny. The translations are a bit rough, and the Spacesuit Narrator speak WAY too quickly but what he has to say is usually very humorous. There are a good amount of site-gags and easter-eggs to look for if you look for them.At the time of writing this, there're a good amount of bugs (audio repeating, waypoints mixing and becoming unreadable, and some other small issues I experienced) but it's playable. The devs say they'll be adding base-building, vehicles and more in future Chapters / Updates so I look forward to those (and hope they're free), I'd recommend this game for anyone who wants to scratch that survival or space itch. It's not the best thing I've ever played but a solid experience, and hopefully there will be more to come. I got it on sale for around 12 bucks, and I think that's a perfect price for this one. If you're iffy, however, I've seen rumors that another update should be out before 2019 so keep your eyes open to see what it brings!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some potential but there are some major flawsThe autosave is unreliable and a lot of stuff is unintuitive so you have to save manually a lot, but if you save in a bad spot you're overwriting everything else.A lot of the building stuff is unclear. And when you want to undo your work deconstruction loses part of the resources. Going back to the save thing... you save before realizing you lost the resources and they're gone for good. There is no display(at least that I can find) to show how much power the base is using. And if I add up the parts I've installed there should still be power yet the base is running low on power. Same for oxygen. There's no warning something you build will go over the limit. The base building(apart from the appearance which is fine) is terrible and storage options are extremely sparse(there should be a storage module hidden away somewhere but I have yet to find it) so you put everything on the ground or in unlabaled suitcases.There's no way to customize waypoints or name bases though there is a screen from which you can turn markers on and off... but in that screen you have a dozen identically named items.The progression design is basically set up in a way that you find something, find out what it needs, then you fly back to a place with a construction table to make it, then fly back again, and hope you don't need something else too. A portable crafting bench or something would help a lot, even if it was consumable like the other stuff.Then there's the oxygen issues. There are resources in game to extend your oxygen. But ultimately they're time/resource consuming. The obvious comparison is to subnautica, but in subnautica you get oxygen each time returning to a powered vehicle.The first chapter is extremely slow, things improve a bit afterwards as you get your first vehicle, but the game is SLOW. The devs make a lot of jokes about some of the stuff they're doing, but that doesn't change the fact they're doing them.It feels like the devs put a lot of work into this, as the environments are varied and creative, so it's really disappointing to see it held back by basic quality of life issues.

_childDocuments_.review: [Original review at 3 hours, edited at 13 hours, I have now finished the story]Breathedge has not been fun to play.I wrote those words at the beginning, and I stand by them now. I bought BE purely to see who in the review sections are right: those saying it's a hilarious subnautica sidegrade, those who claim it's rough at the start but really opens up after the 12 hour mark, and those who say it's an unfunny waste of time and money.My first impressions were that BE was bad, but it might pick up at hour 12.At hour 12 I knew the game did not pick up.Now that I have finished the story, I am not happy.BE's first 20 of gameplay are bad. really bad. "I'm glad 20 minutes qualifies for Steam Returns" bad.The comedy, in the first "chapter" at least, is... non-applicable? I say this because the comedy fails in three ways at once.1. The content of the humor is little more than pop-culture references or poop jokes. If you find the Big Bang Theory funny, you'll enjoy this.2. All jokes are delivered, or reinforced, by the Suit AI voicelines. There is no passive comedy, every single joke is something a single voice says to you in remark to something you see3. Every. single. object. has a joke. opening the door is a joke. collecting water is a joke. getting to a new debris chunk is a joke. There is no downtime whatsoever, which ensures that the very few jokes that could be funny, are smothered immediately.When you progress to chapter 2/3 there is a dramatic dropoff in the amount of jokes thrown at you, to the point where I was beginning to think they threw out the "comedy" aspect when they were developing it. But there are still a few jokes, and they're just as bland as the rest. This chapter has the most interesting game mechanics, but is summed by "fly here to see a problem, fly somewhere else to find the solution, fly back and fix it". With resource gathering thrown in for "spice".But then you do it! you get to the thing and and you're rewarded with:::::: A Map.and four more locations you're going to have to go through.The first stop on that map is a truly uncomfortable experience dealing with a fully voice-acted horny female AI moaning and gasping in your ear for 20 minutes straight.From there, the last 5 hours of BE are a linear space adventure game. No open world, no resource management, no base building, no comedy. It ends on a 5 minute cutscene filled with explosions and fisticuffs and huge space battles. What in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hell?My first thought about BE was "This game needs and editor". Someone needed to tell the devs "No". This game is every thought the devs had during early access put directly into the game. every flat joke, every outdated reference, every obtuse game mechanic, every ♥♥♥♥♥♥ genre! I have never seen a game that was so obviously Early Access and so obviously had devs who got bored and wanted to make a different game halfway through.This game is bloated, underdeveloped, and lacks ANY form of cohesion. The references and comparisons to Subnautica are insulting.Do NOT buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first two chapters, where the game's mechanics and story merged perfectly in my opinion. I really could't wait to go on! I liked the story and its wacky humour as a whole, but after those chapters ended, the game-play was reduced to walking, opening doors, picking up resources in the hopes of needing them later (spoiler: you won't, probably!), crafting the odd item and looking for objects to pick up to hear what the suit has to say about them. That, and following the story. That this wasn't actively annoying but only a little boring now and then shows how good the game is, I think!

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks fantastic, the humor is pretty good at times, and there's some neat environmental pieces to take in but that's about all it has going on for it. What's even worse is that the developers seem dead set on preventing you from actually being able to appreciate it. Your suit starts off with about 75 seconds worth of oxygen so the early game consists of leaving your room, grabbing a few resources, and then rushing back to replenish your oxygen before going back out for more resources. There's some neat environmental pieces to check out but by the time you've reached them it's generally just about time to start heading back before you suffocate. On top of that, your tools have limited durability and are ridiculously fragile so that's another limiting factor when it comes to exploration seeing as you constantly need to head back to your starting location to craft replacement tools. It feels like the game outright keeps you tethered to your starting location and just punishes you for exploring. I was able to find the recipe for the upgraded oxygen tank but ultimately just refunded the game after I spent like 20 minutes going back and forth between my ship and a few different locations over and over again just trying to find rubber to craft the damn thing before finally getting fed up with the whole thing. There's basically no actual reasons I could ever recommend buying this game. I couldn't even recommend it if you're looking for a pretty game to look at because you've basically got no time to really appreciate the environmental pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge starts well but then turns into a set of boring chores as you advance. Among the things that kill the fun is the air management, it makes exploration boring because you will be going around your base of operations and back constantly to get refills. Makes it super repetitive. In other survival games you can generally build something (like a submarine in Subnautica) to supplement (not replace) your base and increase your range of exploration, but no here, it's just you and whatever tank capacity you get. While you can build some oxygen stations, managing those is problematic because it takes resources to refill them. Additionally, the tools tend to have very low durability so you'll have to constantly be re-building them. Up to the point where I played the world was quite linear so if I needed some resources I'd have to go almost all the way to the start.The controls are also frustrating for some reason, instead of clicking things to use them you have to long click. Even the quests and crafting are made in a way to make you spend too much time on them, there's no easy way to get a list of resources you need to research/build a set of items so I ended up having to create a spreadsheet to track the materials needed when I wanted to build/research more than 1 thing. In one of the quests you're supposed to create a base, but you're only told to build the different modules at a time so if you decide to build it away from your current base of operations you're gonna have to keep going back and forth in a "See requested module" -> "Go back go base" -> "Calculate materials needed" -> "Farm materials" -> "Go to advanced base" -> "Restart".Comparing this game to Subnautica is a disservice to Subnautica, if you haven't played it go  play it instead. If you have then look for another game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I'd summarise it as "Subnautica, but in Space, without much Terror and with a lot more cheezy Humour". This isn't a game without it's flaws. Unlike the superlative () Subnautica there were a couple of points where I wouldn't have progressed without , so the signposting could be improved. Unlike a lot of survival / exploration / story games there's more of an emphasis on having fun(?) expressed via the means of *lots* of "cosmetic" pickups and what amounts to a fairly basic sense of humour. I did like the shift in mechanics that occurs via the mechanism of the chapters (no spoilers here but you'll find a more detailed explanation on t'internet if you go looking), and I got  decent sense of closure from the main game (...although there's an obvious sequel hook there waiting to be picked up...). The DLC didn't do much for me as it leans heavily into the very-early-game mechanic which I found (personally) a bit frantic/rushed and not so fun as once the game and achievements develop.

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with Breathedge is how painfully repetitive and slow it is. Chapter 1 is a very dull experience, and while Chapter 2 does make things better, it doesn't last for long. You'll be grinding for materials to craft oxygen stations and alcohol over and over, wishing you could explore without so many limitations.On the bright side, the plot is creative and might succeed in encouraging you to get through these dull moments so that you discover what's going to happen next. I can't say I'm a fan of the ending, though.One way or another, if you believe you're resistant to the downsides I mentioned, you might have a good time, especially if you like searching for collectibles. In my case, it was an interesting exploration game that became a rather frustrating experience because of its burdensome survival mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing. Obviously the brunt of the survival is in the beginning of the game, which falls towards the wayside towards the end of the game in favor of story. However, the entire time the jokes remain amazingly hilarious and it took me 22 hours to complete the game. Well worth the money, especially for all the laughs it gave me. Also, the chicken is immortal, so don't worry about whatever you do to it. (No, you don't really neutralize live wires by poking them with a live chicken irl.) The jokes of the game remain consistently hilarious through the game, and I absolutely love the space suit. (It provides the jokes and humor for the most part.) The fact that an indie team made this game is incredible, though it shows as care and self-depreciating humor can be found consistently. The only small complaint I have is that the game doesn't really auto save enough, and I wish it would save after you went through an airlock into a station or ship. Just save manually though and that problem is gone, so yeah, amazing game. I repeat, this game is damn hilarious.

_childDocuments_.review: As I was playing through this game, I tried to come up with a good way to summarize the experience. The best I can say is that it's kinda like writing a term paper while your annoying roommate watches a Family Guy marathon in the background.The game tries really hard to be funny, but whether or not it succeeds largely depends on how much you like shallow juvenile humor and incessant self deprecation.  If you don't, your experience may be somewhat enhanced by going into the volume settings and turning the voice slider down to 0."Humor" aside, the game starts off as basically Subnautica IN SPACE!  You're the sole survivor of a spaceship crash, and you have to explore your (beautifully lonely) surroundings, upgrade your gear, try not to starve or suffocate, and slowly uncover the backstory while looking for a way home.  The second half of the game throws all that out the airlock and gets progressively more linear until by the end it's almost a straight FPS.  The survival elements are pretty downplayed: food and water can't be farmed (as far as I could tell) but is quite plentiful, and once you get to the point where you can build a base you really don't even need to except for one specific module that's required to proceed.  Then you jump to a whole other map, making whatever effort you put into building your base and collecting supplies all for naught.Overall, I give it a weak thumbs-up.  It's a decent game for what it is, but you have to overlook the numerous flaws to really enjoy it.

I also experienced 0 bugs, besides glitching into a wall once or twice, which honestly is to be expected with this type of game. The only complaint I would have is the crafting system feeling a little clunky; no search fields, and no ability to craft multiple items at once. Overall I'd recommend this 100% even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, I normally do not write reviews, but wow, did this game disappoint when it was completed... The first 3 chapters were very, very good! Yes, a bit subnautica in space, and a bit frustrating at times, but if you managed your resources and time well, and continued to explore, it was very doable, and also rewarding. I do not agree with some comments about the oxygen time and tools durability, because the in game upgrades sort that out as you play (bigger oxygen tanks, unbreakable handy scrapper). It was a very nice base building/craft/exploration combo, with good humour and nice graphics...Now, for the 3 new chapters and the end of the game: SPOILER ALERTBAD, BAD, BAD, from the beginning to the end, I don't even know where to start... loads of resources everywhere, but no more base building options... AT ALL... You get to fly the ship around (Normandy), shoot some robots, walk along never ending base corridors, craft some small objects, warp your ship, and shoot some more... the story looses interest and focus fast, it is poor, gameplay is boring, and at times nausea inducing... I was waiting with a lot of hope for the last 3 chapters, where I would get to build another base somewhere else, with a nice shuttle airlock, to do space exploration in style aboard the Normandy... ZERO... the shuttle airlock serves no purpose, and no where in chapters 4 -6 can you actually get out to space in your space suit, and build a base... You can only exit the Normandy when you dock in an airlock, and there are only preset airlocks in the game, no freedom, no customization of gameplay experience, nothing...So very much disappointing... So much potential wasted... I think if this is the outcome of RedRuins Softworks getting a publisher (HypeTrain Digital), they were better off taking their time, and going solo...Utter rubbish, stay away from this game!PS: The storage locker module is a joke, 3 doors, 1 storage cabinet only, and there is an annoying bug where you cannot scan a glass panel with dead hamsters that unlocks a display module (for those who like to collect and display, it is very annoying, particularly because this has been flagged several times during the early access version, and wasn't fixed for the release version... sloppy).

_childDocuments_.review: This game just isn't particularly fun. And I say that as someone who plays a lot of survival/resource/building games. The resource-gathering is tedious, the inventory management isn't good, there's no combat in the first four 1/2 hours, the exploration takes way too long, and the movement isn't very interesting.If you want resource-gathering and survival, Subnautica does it better. If you want inventory management and construction, 7 Days to Die does it better. If you want good space movement, Hardline: Shipbreaker does it better.I read a lot of reviews saying the humor is great -- and yeah, some of the jokes are pretty good. But a lot of the writing breaks the fourth wall -- just straight-up self-references itself as a video game with a developer -- for no reason other than to mock the player. It's one thing to be tongue-in-cheek or parodying, but to actively make fun of me for buying and playing the game you developed feels crappy. I just don't recommend playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alas, what could have been. The thing that made Subnautica fun was exploring breathtakingly beautiful biomes and some genuinely surprising, unexpected discoveries. That sense that literally *anything* could be lurking around the corner and you had no idea what might happen next. The resource gathering and linear story beats are just the carrot to induce the player to engage with the world. Breathedge aspires to be a spiritual successor to Subnautica, but takes all the wrong lessons from it. You spend the first half of the game foraging through same-y looking space regions, ransacking same-y looking ships, and making arduous resource gathering treks from your base to a small handful of places. There's a clunky and unrewarding base building mechanic, but it mostly exists to trap and punish the player for putting any effort into it, as you quickly leave the only region it would be relevant, never to return. That's because about halfway through, the game loses all interest in being a survival crafting sim and confusingly transforms into a linear adventure game where you travel from waypoint to waypoint pushing buttons and completing arbitrary, unfulfilling tasks. A few halfhearted boss sequences round the whole thing out. The game had a lot of potential, and while I don't doubt "outerspace subnautica" was a really great idea on paper, the execution lets down the premise here. My playthrough took about 30 hours, with the first 10-12  being pretty fun and the remainder just being the tedious slog that comes from a misguided sense of obligation to finish what I'd started. 5/10. Worth a play if you're really, really hungry to gather digital resources and craft them at a crafting station, but still a less good use of your time than rewatching Nathan For You for the 14th or 15th times.

_childDocuments_.review: First third to half of this game is decent, progression and exploration are interesting, if a little tedious due to low tool durability. Food/water for survival feels like a vestigial mechanic as it is made trivial in literally the first minute of the game. At some point you find and craft a vehicle that allows faster travel, from there the game plateaus completely - no new mechanics, just fly from one minimap marker to another and maybe make a trip back to base to craft some quest item to be used exactly once.The last third of this game is complete garbage - all of the crafting/survival/exploration mechanics are just thrown away as you are forced into a linear sequence of space stations that you explore on foot, mostly running mission marker to mission marker.It's nowhere near as janky or buggy as Subnautica and the ending isn't so awful, visually it's also a lot better, but that's all it's got going for it. The self-conscious, fouth-wall breaking referential humour was a turn-off for me, but the mechanics in the early parts of the game were interesting enough to carry my interest. Ultimately, not worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a chill survival game with slightly excessive grind, hit-or-miss humor that tends a bit more towards the scatological and mild edgelord, and that gives up being a chill survival game halfway through to be a conspiracy survival horror(?) narrative that may as well be on rails, have at it. Not my thing, but maybe it'll do it for you. I mean, it is popular enough.Okay, I gave this an honest chance and played it all the way to the end. My conclusion.Meh.The inevitable grind of a space survival sim aside, it's basically an irony-poisoned Soviet-flavored  with... well, I can't call it earthier or lower humor; Ulence Flats was a location in the original . More explicit low humor.Stupid joke spoiler: Major endgame spoiler: The irony-poisoning comes from when it  reminds you that it's a game and it rags on its own mechanics as a parody of other games' mechanics. Again,  did that now and again with "glancing at the status bar gags" but I don't recall it being so constant. That said,  does have its good gags and it's best when it leans into the absurdity of the premise and the universe: the -style gags are actually pretty funny. Unfortunately they're relatively few and far between and most of the gags are reliant on ironic expectation subversion that happens so often that the subversion stops being subversive and starts being expected... especially when you realize that the subversion supports .Major gameplay spoiler:  There's nothing intrinsically wrong with this, but it becomes really obvious when all such sequences are reliant on this limitation and therefore any time  is at risk of self-subversion you know it  happen and therefore all sense of risk and threat is lost.I mention  a lot because this really does feel like  takes a lot of inspiration from that series... and if it does, that's not a bad thing! Just look at the analogs:As I type this up, I think part of it is that Sierra third-person adventure game gags just don't really work in a first-person space survival sim, or at least, they don't with how RedRuins has implemented them. The Spacesuit comes off as annoying and chatty mostly because rather than an adventure game "examine" prompt it speaks up as a character should, when something is roughly in your field of vision... but there's no guarantee that you'll have even noticed whatever it is or are paying any attention to it, leading to a bunch of "what the hell are you talking about?" moments. There's also occasions when Spacesuit's narration will pop up when subjects are behind walls or otherwise occluded, which ends up being immersion-breaking but helpful when you're looking for some random dingus. With a traditional adventure game, it's probably easier to code in a quick action section or  tactical stealth bit rather than in a physics-based first-person engine, especially when we have so much experience with FPSes and any such first-person action sequences would have to compete against those.I guess, in my final estimation, is that with the combination of all the things it's trying to do  is trying to be  but with bits of  tacked on. Problem is,  is better on all the metrics that matter and it came out 36 years ago.And... oof, 's rushed-feeling cutscene non-ending. I don't mind spoiling that much.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is released and I played the game once when it was first released (only chapter 1) and after chapter 2&3 update. Gameplay time was moderate, the exploration was nice, however gathering resources was a quite time consuming so I spend most of my time on that. After the release, Devs told me to give one more chance and here it is.Humor is topnotch, you rarely see this type of quality. Space exploration is incredible, looks amazing and super fun, I played the game twice so I was more accustomed to the game but I can see where people getting frustrated. Game was meant to be played more relaxed so don't rush it, calm down, you will figure things out in few hours.After I played for hours, I've noticed a couple of things, first, this is not a survival game. You feel like it when you played first few hours, game promotes it self like that, but you notice that rather quickly it's nothing but hunger and thirst mechanic, I think devs wanted to create this survival mechanic first but ditched it after few chapters. You start to encounter bunch of food and water everywhere so that mechanic dies really quickly. And if you are waiting to fight something blasters, there are handful of things to fight and you rarely encounter them. So if you put those things aside, game is "gather > craft necessary item > progress"My first problem in the game was gathering part, it was indeed quite tedious but it is because of our lizard brain. When I see an item, I take it and bring it back to ship or my module. So this hoarding process goes on and on. Just like skyrim. Game doesn't require much of that resources to process actually. You don't need hundreds of wires, fabrics, plastics, etc. So storage immediately becomes a problem and if you couldn't find a suitcase early, oh boy good luck. There is also tons of collectibles and you don't know where to put them. And the how car doesn't have a trunk guys, that is a no brainer. So you create sh*t ton of suitcases to store your item. After I found storage compartment I thought "that's it no more suitcases" and guess what, storage compartment have 4 doors like you can use it 4 suitcases but no, it works like a one suitcase. WHAT?! Also suitcases are not static, they have a ragdoll, you can kick a suitcase by accident and send them to the eternal space or can be vanished. (I lost one suitcase full of refined metal, pissed me off ngl) And you spend most of your time to collect metal and after you pass chapter 3, say adios to all that you work for.There are lot's of things to get frustrated but all of this can be resolved with quality of life update. If I were them, I would make a storage module instead of compartment and put everything there and connect it with the processor. Like in Fallout 4. One storage directly to be used by a processor and compartments. So you don't carry bunch of items, ditch everything there and don't try to find aluminium from your tens of suitcases. I know weight/mass doesn't make any sense in a space game but instead you can use volume. Just add scroll to your inventory, increase slots and use volume as a weight mechanic. Which would be a really cool game detail right?Another problem is that after chapter 3 game leaves that exploration part and becomes more linear. Like you are still exploring and hoarding but on a certain path, rather then "let me check over there". It feels like I'm playing a different game, I'm not the guy who explores and try to survive anymore, I'm like running towards to the ending of story. There are lots of things to look at, but there is no interaction, you just run and gather.And shoot a couple of times. I had 4 or 5 blasters at some point because I never used them and I didn't know what to do with them. In overall game is fun enough to keep you interested and indeed funny, story is quite interesting but there are lots of gameplay mechanic half done and ditched later. First half feels like a mediocre survival game but other half feels like a (walking simulator with extra spice) different game, needs a quality of life update. Amount of detail and work looks incredible but feels short on interaction. I would recommend though, there are not many games you can play something like that and deserves it price, but don't expect something crazy and don't get angry for small things, don't hoard much, gather enough things and move on.I can understand people actually enjoy this type of humor and gameplay which I really enjoyed the time I have as well. But the content in this game is simply laughable. Like really, I played this game about 1.5 hours and finished the game. 10 minutes was looking at the settings and staying on the menu. 20 minutes was loading back an old save to check out if I missed anything.I can see that game is really promising and could be a very memorable game. But currently, you are just giving your money to support devs, not to try any new idea or gameplay mechanics. If you are going to buy this game, you should think this as an investment but actually nothing to gain besides maybe saving up some money. But if you check the frequency of updates, I guess we are here to wait. So yikes...TL;DR Game is a "hahaha but so what now and where is the new content?"

_childDocuments_.review: likes- solid work building and story- environments are gorgeous - crafting system strikes a good balance between overly simplified and complexity- exploration is generally rewarded with something new or useful- fantastic interiors, a very eerie feel to the world- some witty flavour text here and there, plays a satirical tune then follows it itself while lampooning the situation- combat is kept to a minimal and simple, focus kept on explorationdislikes- transition between chapter 1 and 2 is a bit bumpy, with certain stations you can craft in the first chapter losing relevancy very quickly. not finding the next set of upgrades can result in a lot of back tracking- o2 usage tends to end up rushing your actions in the early game/mid game. missed out on a lot of dialogue and had to read back through the messages once returned to an area with o2- some tools have expensive costs but don't last very longsmall ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥- space friction, can't set and forget- fair bit of padding in the second chapter, but gets significantly better once you unlock a vehicle, which could be right away or 8 hours in depending on how you tackle/explore the open world- dialogue can start before the previous one is finished, happens extremely often when out in space due to o2 limitswants- o2 use paused/reduced when someone is talking- more interiors to explore (the ambience in these were great), more reasons to use the torch- pitch/yaw controls, third person view- radio in the player made station- colour options for space station interior- more storage options (especially in the station), closer (and more permanent than suitcases) to the workbench and larger to boot

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to Subnautica but certainly worse. Incredibly tedious. Some unintuitive spots in progression. I never found out that there was an item to make you move faster in the beggining because it was "hidden" behind a couple of jokes. I'm sure it must get better but the whole beggining area was just a painful drag. What limits your progression in Subnautica constantly is oxygen. Here it's the same thing, except you can't just surface to get air, you have to get in your little pod or put down these re-oxygenation stations. Because of this I spent a huge amount of time just going between where I actually wanted to explore and your starting pod. There's also the fact that it takes forever for you to get your first vehicle. Another aspect that it has that makes it worse than Subnautica is that the game just gives you markers for where you have to go instead of having this constant, underlying reward for exploration.

I enjoyed the game for the most part but the plot/writing was a little simple and idk if the voice actor for the AI was the right choice. The comedy aspect wasn't that great. _childDocuments_.review: The only reason this has 5 hours of playtime is because 4 of those hours are spent moving at 6m/s trying to get back to my station for oxygen or trying to get to my next objective. I barely got through the story enough to make this an enjoyable experience. This game started well enough in the first 30 minutes, but fell flat quickly.The humor is nice and has its moments, but it becomes annoying after constantly being bombarded by a fast-talking narrator and subtitles that go away faster than you can read them. It's tough to read subtitles or pay attention to a voice actor when you are rushing to get anywhere before you run out of oxygen.I really wanted this to be a good game, but unfortunately it is not. I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually painful for me to give this a no review. There's clearly a lot of love put into the game and there's the foundation for something truly incredibly but chapters 3/4/5/6 are just absolutely abysmal. Chapters 1 and 2 are amazing, but unfortunately the game stops being "Subnautica in space" after Chapter 2 and becomes tedium incarnate. I honestly can handle quite a bit of tedium. It gets old after the first one. The humor is hit and miss. It got a laugh out of me here and there, but the game is going for a joke a minute when it is telling jokes.My recommendation? _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly cringey. Traveling across the space is magical but every time the journey is interrupted with "story" bits, I roll my eyes and ask myself why I am playing this... until the will to explore finally evaporated.The game makes it clear from the get-go that the story is just a pretext to land a joke. Okay, the problem is that jokes are very juvenile. What kind of humor? Something like this: "Someone blocked a broken leaking toilet with a hamster. The poop hamster! Hahaha." "Muslims are dumb. You get it? Dumb. Haha, look at me how edgy I am in this age of censorship." "Let's vandalise 100 coffins flying in the space. You shouldn't but sure you can. I bet you always wanted to do something like this but was too afraid to ask!"The whole time you keep getting trolled by some user on the ecomm who keeps balancing between baiting you with odd flirting and mocking you.If you are tempted like me when reading:“It's like Subnautica mixed with Prey ... I like that game a lot!”Don't. Both Subnautica and Prey are legendary games providing a completely different level of experience - storywise, atmosphere buildup, mature themes. It has 2 things in common with them - 1) you craft items like in Subnautica and 2) It happens in space.

_childDocuments_.review: I supported it in EA, and was excited. I liked the jokes, the atmosphere was great, and they were promising a storyline and not just a sandbox experience. Which is why "subnautica" and "The long dark" are my two favorite survival games. AT FIRST it was less than 10 hours worth of exploration. I loved it. Make some tools, plan oxygen stations and float around. It has this very somber, melancholy emptiness to it, when you are exploring space. And then the silly humor and silly music in your base makes the whole experience varied and entertaining.Then they went full lauch and i was excited to explore the story. While it is still funny, it is apparent that they slapped the rest of the game together really fast. Instead of the open world, you get a driving sim with complexity straight off the PS1.You drive from place to place and walk down boring tunnels and pick up mcguffin after mcguffin. They even force you to retrace your steps because resources are blocked by milestones. Meaning that if you are in a location with that resource, you cant get it before it is unlocked by your progress. Some parts were funny. But it is so different from the first stage and has too many hours of boring corridors. Shame, really. The first part of the game, with the base building and exploration in space is FUN, beautiful, mysterious and has a melancholy emptiness combined with the silly humor. If they had made 2 or just 3 levels of that, with different obstacles? 10/10. But the railroaded gameplay with endless boring corridors that you have to walk up and down and up and down make it a 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Game turned out a major disappointment after Chapter 3.Up to it, it's basically a Subnautica parody (not a clone per se, it doesn't try to hide the fact it's based on Subnautica at all, there are actually some hilarious references if you played it), so you have your middle-of-the-pack exploration/survival/crafting game, not amazing, but fun enough to keep you interested. Its comedy is actually pretty funny all along (except for an absolutely embarrassing & cringy part in Chapter 4) and the story is also well-written. I was hoping (I had played up to Chapter 3 in Early Access) for just more of the same with maybe a base-like ship to fly around, so basically just a continuation of the Subnautica formula they had already copied. Alas, the developers thought it best to turn Chapters 4 and 5 into something like Half-Life or Portal and, well, a Valve they obviously are not.Oh yes, Half-life, because did I mention they added some of the very worst action sequences in gaming history?! Yup, they did! For some inexplicable reason they thought it was a good idea to add spaceship "dog-fighting" and some of the most idiotic boss fights I've ever seen in my life (and trust me I give bad games a chance more often than not) to a game that starts out as a peaceful survival/resource gathering/crafter.The biggest letdown I've seen out of Early Access ever, bar none.
