_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica... IN SPACE! WITH CORPSES! (so many corpses!)The game is roughly broken into three or four parts. First, you start off in your shuttle, with no equipment or resources - it's basically Subnautica, if you could only restore your oxygen in your escape pod. Eventually, you'll make your way to the second chapter, where you'll upgrade your equipment to drastically increase your oxygen capacity, ability to and duration of your thruster burn, and eventually get vehicles that allow you to move at 5x and 10x your initial movement speed; drastically increasing your range. It's actually rather fun going back to the initial area - things that required multiple oxygen waypoints and additional supplies are easily accomplished in just a single air tank.Thankfully, there are multiple areas in the second section where you can recharge your oxygen, so you're not stuck constantly going back and forth from your shuttle. You'll also get oxygen candles that can entirely refill your supply, giving you the ability to stay somewhere that doesn't have a handy recharge station while you look for whatever resources / mission objectives you need.Your inventory is your constant enemy. The game is great in that, while it is _better_ to put things into containers, you can totally just dump all your crap onto the floor and it'll stay there. The biggest problem is that both food and water inexplicably take up 2 slots each in your inventory, and the game gives you _tons_ of the stuff. You'll routinely find yourself dumping bottles of water and/or packets of food to grab two more shards of titanium.Speaking of, it's worth noting that although you've got both food and water bars, the only time you might (_might_) end up starving or dehydrating is the very, very, very start of the game. There's just too much ice and water goblets (which are used to make food and water), and just straight up food packets and water bottles lying around for it to ever become an issue. It's not unrealistic - you're exploring the wreck of a luxury liner, of course there's going to be plenty of food and water around - but it does almost entirely eliminate that survival aspect of the game.After you've played the survival simulation for a goodly amount of time... it ends. You enter a working ship and blast off into the walking simulator portion of the game. It's sort of funny, because the game is still technically a survival game, so the game dutifully makes sure that there's plenty of food and water scattered throughout the maps you're walking through. They also don't assume that you've kept any of your tools, so there's _so many resources_ scattered everywhere. If you're a packrat like me, you'll probably end up with multiple suitcases full of crap in your spaceship - way, way more than you'll ever need.Finally, there's a boss battle (technically, there are several, but only one of them is actually difficult). Luckily, the game gives you about half a dozen medkits before the fight. As long as you're not like me and prioritize the medkits over the refined metal (sweet, sweet refined metal), you'll be good.The game tries to be "funny"... I'd say that it misses the mark more often than it hits it. It also tends towards the juvenile. Still, your companion AI does manage to keep up a good stream of quips and remarks that, at very least, manage to drown out the oppressive silence of deep space.Final tally: First part was good. Second part was great. Third part was underwhelming. Forth part was annoying until I went back, dropped all the crap I was carrying and traded it out for medkits. Worth a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Survival and Humor is not a natural combination (unless dying a lot is amusing to you).   Not that I don’t appreciate the attempt, but when you’re always what feels like a few minutes from dying from suffocation, starvation, thirst, or of all things, lack of sleep, well then it’s a little hard to appreciate the constant jokes.  In fact, lets face it, it just gets in the way.  How’s this tool work?  Who knows but let’s try to say something funny about it.  Toilet humor?  Check.  I still don’t know what exactly the space toilets do after completing the first chapter, but someone sure thinks they’re amusing.   Chickens?  Well that’s like the oldest prop in history.   Moving on …The other significant challenge or problem is the enemy in this game is suffocation and when you are floating around trying to discover something or grab a resource, it’s not especially helpful to have a narrative that’s trying to make you laugh. Sight gags go largely unnoticed because, you know, I’m out of air, again, so sorry, but I’m trying like, to not die right now.  This dynamic is repetitive and tedious - take a little trip from your claustrophobic ship, endure useless humorous banter (spoken too quickly to understand at times) and then scoot back before you run out of air.  Repeat.  For you Subnautica folks, imagine if you were stuck operating only out of the crashed pod, could only increase your diving depth a little and were followed around by a hyper-caffeinated dolphin making lame jokes while you were trying to not drown.   Yes, this game allows you to make what are essentially supplemental air cannisters to carry around, but they don’t grant you that much more time and obviously they require resources to make, which consumes air … etc.  Look, I get it.  I love the survival genre however this game is just not a satisfying example.  I don’t mind steep curves, frustrations, unfair surprises, running off cliffs by accident -  but this game just seems to force you to rush to survive.  Time is the enemy.  Vitals drop quickly.  Air runs out quickly.  There’s little time to do anything but get the next thing you’re running out of.   And I guess that’s probably true in space sooo ….. I’ll just stop here.That all said, roaming around outside in space is FANTASTIC.  While the physics are not especially accurate, it’s good enough to make you feel like you’re there and the scenery is simply beautiful.  So yay to the artists.  Honestly, the only reason I’m recommending this game is that it is truly gorgeous.  It has potential, but it should be better balanced to allow you to enjoy the sights and the gags.  BTW, in case you care, resources like food don’t respawn so you got about 12 hours and if you’re just exploring and trying to learn what everything does, well, you might regret it.  After 13.3 hours.  Like me.   So, yeah, mixed bag, interesting concept, pretty as hell and cheap enough I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for harvesting basic resources and building complex tools, which you then use to collect different items.. Resources are flying around in abundant quantity. Your inventory is pretty deep, but not limited, and spacesuit will require several upgrades before you can travel long distances.As you discover new stations, research crashed ships - you will learn (by scanning with a camera) more recipes for new crafts. Examine enough and eventually you get to build your very own  space station with a garage and transport!Somewhere in the mid of the game the pace goes brrr - from "no enemies and slow wondering/crafting" in areas of Chapter 1-3, Breathedge transforms into a space flying simulator, with shooting tiny targets, turrets and ice asteroids, docking to bigger shuttles and creating even more sophisticated equipment. . 4th wall breaking jokes, continuous devs' mocking and various references and memes. _childDocuments_.review: This game is simply an escape room adventure for Chapter 1. You have a very linear fashioned experience with things splayed out in what seems to be chaos, but it is all really cleverly placed. I went into the game not knowing what to do or how it is played, and it is that pure enjoyment of discovery that you get in games that makes it such a wonderful experience. The only downside is that you can't tell when something is serious or a joke. Should I save this or not? Is it junk or a joke? Etc. I've been stuck a few times. I always just go as far as I can to a new spot without returning before I quit the game. _childDocuments_.review: A funny space game in the vein of Subnautica, except, you know, in space.  Right out of the gate the game lets you know it's not trying to be serious.  The style of humour is quite silly and absurd, and the graphics are colourful.  It starts with you being interrogated by two mafia robots (think Futurama style).  They want to know what happened to you, and the ship you were on.  You then begin to tell an embellished version of events (cue cutscene) before they whack you upside the head and make you tell it properly.  You are on board a giant funeral ship, trying to bring your grandfathers(I think?) casket . . . somewhere.  Unfortunately for you, the ship explodes into many, many pieces.  Broccoli terrorists may be responsible?  The gameplay is about you trying to gather various materials from around the section of ship you were aboard, while your spacesuits (marginally) helpful AI tells you what to do. You wander around gathering supplies while you watch your oxygen, food, and water meters slowly dwindle.  Strange and silly things will happen around you.  The goals so far is to find other survivors, and wait for rescue.  The game of course, has other hilarious plans.  The game is early access, but just received a large update that seems to have added a lot of content.  Now you get to build a mini space habitat (again, like Subnautica), while continuing the story.  I've got over 10 hours into it and I haven't reached the end of the new updates.  Whether you get it now, or after it releases 1.0, if you liked Subnautica (or that style of survival), and have a silly sense of humour, then you'll like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty close to beating the game.The game baits you in with the crafting, interest in the story, some sense of progression, and the humor. As you progress you realize the gameplay is artificially extended through long travel and resource nodes that don't regenerate (requiring further and further travel). Now, all games do extend gameplay through travel, collection time, etc. This game, however, is particularly guilty of making you run around for ridiculous amounts of time to progress. They take it way too far, and overplay the "haha, that task was pointless XD" joke. It seriously ruins the game. The more you play the more it feels like a painful boring grind with little to no fun game mechanics. They should have just shortened the gameplay and allowed the game to be short and sweet.Would not recommend

_childDocuments_.review: orAlternative, terrible, but more accurate titles for this game.Breathedge is both amazing and disappointing at the same time.Which is the reason my review is so long... I honestly think these devs are cool, just read the steam page and some of their updates. Sadly that doesn't change my gameplay experience.Almost everything in there is good quality:- awesome graphics, very nice aesthetics... everything just looks great with realistic and ridiculous designs mixed together perfectly,- awesome soundtrack,- the humour is nice, but can be too much for some, I personally like it,- progression and equipment you get are nice (although the pacing of them is NOT).There are also problems, but they're not as apparent at first as its awesome graphics or cool soundtrack.In a nutshell your time outside is painfully limited, and most of it you'll spend by just pressing W.Also space is dead.While some of these problems might seem minor, or even ridiculous complaints, I'd like you to keep in mind that the devs are aware and even make fun of ridiculous game designs and mechanics.They added an objective which specifically makes fun of missions/mechanics that are only in a game to artificially extend gameplay without adding actual content, and yet for the majority of Breathedge you're just flying through empty space.At the beginning you get 50 seconds outside, but most of the important things are 15-20 seconds away. So you'll spend 30-40 seconds flying, and 10 seconds actually doing something. This ratio will only get worse, because you get bigger O2 tanks, but things will also be farther away. You'll be flying for 1-2 minutes and do stuff for 10-20 seconds at best.(there's no radio to listen to in your space suit, and you can't even set a course and a get a glass of water because there's space friction, you can't even open your inventory)Another big problem is that some of the progress you make is nullified/waste of time, because at some point in the game you can research items that you would find outside at debris. So first you spend time to grind the resources for the research, then you finally make yourself go out and fly through space for 2 mind-numbing minutes just to realise the debris you're at has the item you already researched. Not only a waste of time, but makes you think that you might've bypassed certain elements of the game, basically took the easier way to progress.This limited oxygen really discourages progression for a new player, since you have to use consumable items to complete objectives, but you also have limited resources, and absolutely no idea what's gonna happen when you actually progress.Taking risks either with your life (after which you need to load) or by exhausting your resources (might need to to restart the whole game) would be less of an issue if you didn't need to do the exact same things 5 million times throughout the game... if it needed some skill. But this combination of mindless repetition and being forced to risk your run is very bad.Basically devs shooting themselves in the foot with the limited oxygen mechanic:You can't enjoy the beautiful environment, soundtrack and the witty commentary of the AI they created, there's just not enough time at the beginning. I mean your oxygen is running out so you just have to scan, collect and progress as fast as you can, often cutting voicelines, because the alternative would be to fly another minute back and forth. When you finally do get enough oxygen the novelty is already gone.O2 recharge is unnecessarily slow, especially at manual recharge stations, where you have to press left-click for seemingly hours for a full tank. Why? It serves no purpose.It's easy to miss some of the upgrades, which really amplifies the problems I described above.Compared to Subnautica:- While the distances and travel times are similar in both games, the in Breathedge you have small bubbles of O2, instead of having the whole surface of an ocean, which severely slows down progress.- No wildlife to look at, no enemies to be afraid of. With all the ridiculous (but funny) ideas they put in the game, spacemonkeys and spacesharks in there wouldn't really stand out.- Crafting is clunky in Breathedge: you can't open your inventory while moving, you can't walk away from the Processor while crafting items, you can't build multiple processors to craft faster.- For hours there's nothing that would ease your gameplay in Breathedge. As you get better items, you'll need to go father, always stretching your O2 supply. In Subnautica the Seaglide or even a basic O2 tank felt like a gamechanger and you also get a Seamoth in just a few hours in. In Braethedge there's no cool upgrades, you just get the bare minimum.What could help:1. For starters they could increase the actual speeds to what the UI shows. Your spacesuit is supposedly capable of 12 m/s, while the actual speed is closer to 6 m/s.2. Communicate more clearly which resources are renewable. That would make certain consumables more appealing.3. Don't let us waste time on research if we gonna find the blueprint 3 minutes later. Don't make the need to explore and the need to research mutually exclusive.4. Don't draw O2 while the AI is talking. Yes, it's stupid and it's unrealistic, but unless we get more time outside, I just don't have time to pay attention to that guy. You designed the game in a way that I have to hurry.5. Let us do something while flying through space. Add a spacesuit radio, or let us open inventory, or remove space friction from the player's base movement (only for the 12m/s speed, the accelerator effect should still wear off)... anything, really.Either one of these would be a great addition, although the 1st change by itself would solve most other issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I often find that comedy, especially comedy games, can be kinda hit and miss. But in my estimation, this game lands firmly on the hit. A lot of the comedic writing is really on point, there are countless easter eggs referencing other properties if you're paying attention, and the often perfectly-paced parodies of other games and genres are genuinely great. It can wear a little every now and then, especially when you're on an attempt at the achievement for beating the game in less than 7 hours and wish you had a skip button, but overall, the writing remains charming even on multiple playthroughs.In terms of gameplay, it's a really well-paced space survival/crafting game, with some fantastic risk/reward cycles, and the occasional massive curveball that totally flips the script. Definitely a game worth picking up and thoroughly experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was on sale, looked entertaining and I thought I could use a laugh.  While I did enjoy the comedy of the plot, this game was something entirely unexpected.  The closest analogue I can think of is Dead Space 3; the part where you are flying through space collecting consumables.  If you can picture that, multiply that by a hundred and you will be close to what this is.  You play in space with limited Oxygen, so everything you do is limited by the short oxygen supply you have.  The supply is slowly extended by crafting and upgrading.  The graphics are tight and the atmosphere is excellent as are the physics in which you are operating, in my opinion the developers give such a small picture of what this game is actually about and I almost passed over this title.  The last time this happened was when I purchased Kerbal Space Program (another excellent title) and, again very pleasantly surprised.In conclusion; for a game in early release I give it top marks in story and game play.  I thoroughly enjoyed this game, I did have to go online and get a few hints, but that was due to not exploring the environment enough.Get it!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: As everyone says, it's Subnautica in space. Just not anywhere near as good.Breathedge is a game i knew nothing about and its arrival on steam came as a total surprise. The premise seemed tantalizing enough, I would get to live though another Subnautica experience, but this time in space!Instant buy on that alone.Then i got to play it, and over the course of my time there the excitement slowly and inevitably drained away.Let's make something clear right off the bat: Breathedge is not a _bad_ game. Both the graphics, sound and gameplay are good enough to hold your attention for some time. It's when you get further into it that the worst enemy of all crafting games set in: Tedium.Most games in the genre are paced in a very specific way, to make sure that you always find something new and get that tantalizing feeling that greater things are always juuust beyond the horizon. Subnautica did that very well indeed, while also part of a world that drew you in with tense moments and feelings of terror contrasted with mezmerizing vistas and cool technology. It all blended together to form a compelling world you couldn't wait to explore and build in, while simultaneously having to build up the courage to venture forth into the dark and cold foreboding depths.Breathedge, in comparison, pulls you along with only a single temptation and one urgency: to find out what gag the game will throw at you next, and to avoid running out of specific resources in your current area.The vistas are fine, there is some tension (mostly with the oxygen mechanic), and the suit AI:s humor is at least somewhat funny at times.If Subnautica wasn't a thing that existed, this might very well be enough, but since we got something to compare this game to, it all just kinda feels unpolished, flat... and repetetive.That last bit is the kicker, really. I could forgive the hit-and-miss humor, flat world and lackluster story if only the gameplay wasn't so utterly tedious.Every tool you make in the game (so far) has a durability value that is, frankly, shockingly low. Your stuff will break, and break a LOT, and you'll have to go back to your hub to craft a replacement. Material-wise, this really isn't as much of a problem as some point it out to be, it's the constant flying back and forth, back and forth, over and over again. For oxygen, for replacement tools, for inventory management... It never ends! At the start, your oxygen supply is so shockingly low you can barely go outside your hub for what feels like a few seconds before you have to go back for a refill, and even after several upgrades this feeling does NOT go away. It's by far this games greatest weakness, and no matter what you do you can only slightly alleviate it by minor upgrades and mobile oxygen stations you place in the world. Your movement will never stop feeling like you're strapped to a bungee cord to the closest oxygen source. Until your tool breaks and you have to very slowly drift your way back to the hub to build yet another replacement.Lets talk about the slow movement speed a bit more. Because it is. It's painfully slow. It feels like piloting a hovercraft with a table fan. There're boosters you can make to speed yourself up, but they run out so fast and there's no danger other than the oxygen supply, so it basically comes down to pressing the button when the bar is full to reach your destination a few seconds faster, nothing else. There's no interesting gameplay built around it at all.In summary, the  only unique aspect Breathedge uses to compete with Subnautica is the humor, and like I mentioned it's hit-and-miss. Some of the jokes I truly burst out laughing at, with others I just rolled my eyes. It really loves to 4:th wall break, joking about its developers being ♥♥♥♥ for making stuff repetetive or bad, trying to make you laugh at the boredom you're experiencing.But that only serves to further make you realize that you really aren't having as great a time as you want to believe you are having, that you just keep going because Subnautica was good so this must be too...But it really isn't. It's _alright_, nothing more and nothing less.A potentially fun game held back by endless tedium and a fair amount of forced jokes.Having played Subnautica and absolutely adored every second of it, I can't really recommend this.You might like it anyway. If you decide to buy it, just remember to curb your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: So I have dumped many hours into Subnautica. I've only played this game for about 5 now and it's already reminded me of the "discovery" and unknown feels I got during Subnautica... although with a healthy dose of humor and sarcasm that's quite enjoyable. I'm also getting very strong feelings akin to the latest Prey game. Granted, there's not the acute danger elements like in Prey, but the feeling of being out and space, exploring, drifting, not knowing if there's active danger ahead, floating through auras and slip-stream like particles. I can't put my thumb on it, but both Prey and Subnautica truly made me experience an immersion I haven't found in other games up to this point. All that to say, any game that can reignite or spark those is a win in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is a science-fiction comedy first-person exploration game from RedRuins Softworks. Chapter 1 has only just released into Early Access on Steam.The game starts with a flurry of jokes that I, at least, found pretty funny. After the short credit sequence you're left in front of some robotic thugs who demand you tell them the real story of how the hearse-liner "Unnamed" was blown up in space somewhere out on the edge of the known universe, after they've beaten you up a bit, of course. And that sets the scene for the game.Remembering back, you see a short CG sequence showing the last moments of Unnamed and then you find yourself in a small shuttle cabin, somehow still mostly whole after the massive liner's unfortunate incident, with a smarmy and sarcastic AI voice in your space suit telling you what's what. It's your job to survive for long enough to reach the evacuation zone and escape from the wreckage, together with your family's immortal chicken, of course.The introductory CG sequence is excellent, but I wasn't expecting the in-game graphics to be quite as good as they are. Breathedge uses the Unreal engine and it looks fantastic! Graphics are AAA quality, with the game world modelled on a weird sort of 1950's 'retro-Soviet' science fiction look and feel. It reminds me a lot of Bioshock, with that same sort of weird-SF feel, but it's unique, with the comedy aspect helping to carry it along.The game world in this first chapter, at least, is actually quite small, but the developers have done a fine job of making it look much bigger when you first start. The ruin and detritus from the Unnamed's demise is spread across an area of near-planetary space populated with small asteroids. The frozen liquids that have burst from various parts of the huge vessel deserve special mention, as do the frozen-in-space set pieces that you'll find scattered about the wreckage; they look amazing, if rather gruesome at times.The great graphics are accompanied by good sound effects and an excellent selection of contextual retro-style music, often complete with a sort of tinny radio effect that fits the atmosphere of the game to a tee. There's professional-sounding voice acting, too, which is mostly very well done, though in places I thought the space suit AI -- which does most of the talking in the game -- could use a little bit of tweaking.Performance is mostly excellent on my GTX1070-based gaming laptop at 1920x1080 with everything set to "epic", but it's worth mentioning that the in-game survival guide video didn't play well at all, jumping and stuttering throughout most of the video, which made it not much fun to watch.When I first started up Breathedge I thought it was another first-person survival-crafting game, but having completed the (rather small) amount of content that's here so far, I think I was wrong. It's actually more like a sort-of action puzzle game, with crafting forming the basis of the puzzle solutions.Scattered about the wreckage of Unnamed are a number of little areas. Close by are food and ice (for water), as well as some metal and a few other components. Venture further out and you'll uncover oxygen-generation and storage plans and components, aluminium, lead, etc. Progress through the story involves reaching each of these areas, learning the new recipes available and scavenging the new resources, then making your way back to your base shuttle to convert them into the means to reach the next area. Your ultimate goal is to enhance your space suit for extra speed, oxygen, and radiation protection, so you can make it across the 1.6 km or so span of the game world to the evacuation area.But, unlike most survival-crafting games, Breathedge seems to punish you for exploration. The easiest way -- perhaps the only way, given the apparent scarcity of resources -- to succeed in the game is to abuse the save system: save your game, go out on suicide runs to explore the wreckage, discovering where important components are located, and then reload, using your meta-knowledge to plan out which areas you will visit and how. This seems to me to be completely anathema to the survival-crafting genre, and I found it quite hard to get used to given my expectations of the game. There's nothing wrong with it, exactly; it just wasn't what I'd expected.The crafting itself is fairly typical, though there are no craftable crafting stations; everything is built by carrying the collected ingredients back to your base shuttle and using the single station in the kitchen area. This makes the whole game a series of relatively short, fast resource-collection runs out into the wreckage and back to your base, followed by a long final run to the end zone, all while trying to keep your food and water meters up above zero -- which tends to only be a minor distraction. There's also no combat and there are no enemies to speak of.Once I came to terms with the basic gameplay model, the only real problem I had with Breathedge was the rather weird space controls. The game maintains a sort of "up" direction, rather than letting you move with six full degrees of freedom, as I'd expected from this sort of game. It takes a bit of getting used to, but probably in the long run it will make control easier for anyone not familiar with 6-DOF games. The strange friction effects, though, just seem plain wrong. Your speed is locked to 12 m/s normally, but there's no reason given for this apparent violation of the laws of physics -- I should be able to keep increasing my speed while I continue to apply a force. Similarly with the boosted 20 m/s speed; this drops down to 12 m/s as soon as your boost stops. Why? It makes no sense!I think it's probably possible to spend too long treating the game as a typical survival-crafting game and end up using all of the useful resources within reach, effectively trapping you. I worked out what the game really wanted before I managed to do that to myself, though, so perhaps some of the resources respawn at some point, avoiding this problem. Inventory space is also a bit of an annoyance, as it's limited both within your space suit and in your shuttle base's storage. Removing the shuttle base limitation would make the game more pleasant to play, while not having a negative impact on longevity.Pros:+ AAA Presentation+ It's pretty darn funny!Cons:- trial-and-error approach to progress- zero-gravity controls aren't great- very short (so far)- inventory space is annoyingBreathedge's presentation is top notch. The graphics are strangely beautiful and the setting is graphically well realised, like a little bit of Bioshock in space. The voice work is professional and the sound effects and music are great. The game has some interesting ideas, too, and a great sense of humour. It has a lot going for it.But after completing what's available currently, I'm disappointed with the crafting and survival aspects, and I can't help feeling as though most of the game world so far is just a pointless, empty distraction; I'd expect I could speed run through what's here in an hour or so now that I know what's required.That said, the game is still in Early Access and the developers have hinted at a lot more to come. So far it's very polished and has managed to keep me amused and mostly interested for a handful of hours; I'm looking forward to seeing what happens next.

Don't believe the bad reviews from people who couldn't get past the starting area and didn't get to experience the masterpiece that is this game.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I regret paying for this. It's Soviet Subnautica in space with a plot I struggle to care about. It can be quite funny, but it feels like it's constantly trying too hard. Your little in-ear assistant talks too fast, and is never, ever not making a joke, which makes it hard for me to follow. The mental labour of trying to parse the important information from this constant barrage of nattering makes me tired.The game's sense of humour and antagonism of the player overstay their welcome. _childDocuments_.review: Breathedge has all the makings of a good survival game but is too off-the-wall for me to really recommend. If you're cool with lots of over the top, really tongue-in-cheek humor stuffed into every crack and crevice of a relatively decent survival, this game may totally be for you. But, for someone who likes survival crafting games to be immersed in a world, Breathedge's ability to have every interaction pull me out of the experience instead is a large mark against it.To be clear, the game play, when not exposing you to toilet jokes and dry humor, is pretty decent. If you like survival games, it's got all the elements that make the genre fun, I just couldn’t get into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I only have 82 minutes, but that's just because I got annoyed and bored. I might get back to it at some point.The game feels clunky. I didn't really experience satisfaction with any part of it. In fact, I felt the opposite with a lot of the game. The worst part was getting messages from Babe every five seconds, and they're horribly written with awful grammar, made it a nightmare to read. I get it though, the game even calls attention to it being the result of a poor translation device, but I'm not going to read a hundred thousand messages like that. Plus, she doesn't ever say anything useful. It's seriously all filler.The crafting is meh. Some items are more specific about what they do, some are open ended and poorly named. The storage felt limited to a point that I couldn't gather many items for later use. I read that base building is a thing, and it would open up more storage. I don't know.None of the jokes landed. They kept breaking the 4th wall, which isn't funny if you do it nonstop. The gathering is probably the best part about this game. They did a great job filling the emptiness of space with a wide range of different sized pieces in the area you're supposed to be working through. While there isn't a tier system strictly in place, many of the resources are locked behind getting certain items. The zero gravity felt decent, though entirely unrealistic. The accelerator being powered by farts was...I dunno. Like I said, the jokes weren't landing. While the type of movement was alright, the speed is absolutely terrible. It feels like a slog. I've read there are upgrades beyond the fart movement, but it's so bad I don't even want to play long enough to get them.One great thing about the game is it doesn't hold your hand. If you don't explore, you will miss things. Discovery is almost entirely up to you.Get it on a steep sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: This game is relaxing, annoying, stressful, puzzling, challenging, plentiful, lonely, crowded, tedious, hilarious, dry, very self aware, just wonderful in general... In short, it causes you to experience so many emotions in no time at all. It controls a little fast at first but when you get used to stabilizing, it handles extremely well. It makes survival items very plentiful, metal for tools not so much but it's not hard to find, and everything else is spread out and forces you to go a bit out of your comfort zone and you find that your little survival bubble doesn't have to be so small. I rarely ever leave reviews because most games speak for themselves with advertisements and hype and their price, but I had only heard of this through Jacksepticeye and I'm pretty sure I would never have heard of it otherwise. It's so low priced for how much enjoyment I got out of it and how much promise it has, don't mistake the low price for it being a crappy game, it just doesn't have anywhere near everything in it that it'll eventually have. If my leaving a review helps even one person to make up their mind, it'll be well worth writing this novella of text. Please, if you haven't already, buy it before it releases as a full game at $60+
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: 80% or more is padding. Go here, go there. Craft this, find out you need that. Lots of travel time going through empty space between wrecks. Lots of trips back and forth to a safe zone because your oxygen tank is criminally small. Lots of time before you're able to craft a (slightly) bigger tank, and of course you need to gather resources for it, which takes time collecting junk and smacking junk with other junk, all while every tool you need to gather stuff degrades very rapidly with use, forcing you to gather more to craft more tools to gather with. Needless tedium.Also, the devs know. Early on they make you craft "Crap imposed by the devlopers", literal useless object (shaped like a penis I might add), and reference padding the game, because they think it's funny.I was enticed by the premise, seemed like an interesting world. Unfortunately the story in reality is pretty much a shoestring. You're just dropped in, told nothing, and the scenery bits you come across don't help paint a picture. The trailer has more story than the actual game.The funniest thing about this game is that it took longer than the return window to find out how boring this game is. I *kind of* want to find out how it ends but at this point I don't feel like slogging through the rest of it. Why did I spend money on this...
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: So, the game is VERY early in it's life span. While most games have a few issues and a bit of content in their early life span, Breathedge actually only really needs to add more content. The game is fluid and responsive, no major hitches, and fairly well optimized. I never had loading times, or hiccups even as I explored larger portions of the map, and while the map itself isn't giant yet, it's pretty large. There's things to actually find already, and while I was more concerned with progressing, I do admit there were quite a few areas I neglected, as the current 'end' of content caught me off guard (and subsiquiently had me giggling like a school girl). The game REALLY delivers on the claims of crude humor that actually does make you laugh, which is a welcome change from some instances of games trying to force humour on you. All in all, the only thing that I would want more from the game is simply that; more of the game. I love the content that is there, and actually really look forward to new updates as they come.

_childDocuments_.review: I had very high hopes for this game, however unfortunately it has completely failed to make me want to continue playing it. The steam page and the reviews I saw for this game made it seem like it would be similar to Subnautica but in space, which I thought sounded great! However, in reality the game is more like Subnautica: Below Zero, but without the breathtaking scenery. Subnautica: Below Zero was a game I was really excited for as well, however what made that game fall short was how linear it was, it felt like I was constantly having to follow a linear plot when all I wanted was to have the freedom to explore. Breathedge falls flat in the exact same way. When you first start up the game it seems very intriguing, it sort of presents itself as an exploration-survival game, however you quickly realise that you can't really progress without following the linear plot and it just ends up feeling like being stuck in an endless tutorial. As soon as you feel like you're starting to gain some freedom and you begin settling into your base, the game suddenly throws you a curveball where you can't progress further without abandonning everything and moving to a new space because "the plot says so".On top of all this the scenery is honestly pretty boring, there wasn't really anything that made me want to explore. It's all just the same kind of wreck pieces with the same things floating around and so I ended up feeling pretty unmotivated to do anything at all in the game. I think scenery is very important for a game like this, after all it's what made Subnautica: Below Zero somewhat tolerable, so the lack of scenery in Breathedge once again just makes it feel like an endless tutorial.The humor in the game is also very hit or miss, you might like it but personally it made me cringe a lot. The humor can more or less be boiled down to "haha boobs" or jokes about the game itself which just makes the devs come off as insecure about their own game. It honestly just gets annoying since at points there's constant pop up messages that serve no point other than "being funny". The humor also feels very out of place and mostly just takes me out of the game, I get that they were trying to do something different but it honestly does not fit this game genre. Imagine playing Subnautica but the disaster you're in is just a joke, there's constant developer inserts and you have constant pop up messages on your screen every 10 minutes making boob jokes, it just doesn't work.Because of all this I can't recommend Breathedge, I wish I could but the game honestly just feels disappointing and it really does not live up to expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but it is seriously missing some more polish.The first half of the game with back and forth exploration because of missing oxygen works, but as you keep on progressing the game becomes more and more tedious to go forward :First, there's the tools. They're always going to break when you most need them. What's the point of breakable power tools anyway? I wish they would just run out of batteries (or not at all), instead you just "break" your scanner after pressing the record button 20 times. Also, as the game progresses, you will just need more and more tools which means your inventory will get smaller with time, and there are no upgrades for inventory space. Add to that the fact that on the second half of the game you just run accross corridors with lots of useless items and you get even less room. Having tools in the inventory feels like a waste of space 80% of the time, and ther'es only 4 quick slots when IMO there should be 10 quick slots that would remove tools from the inventory space. A lot of the time you end up just running back and forth 1 mile to a crafting table for no other reason than recrafting a broken tool or crafting a mandatory piece of equipment to advance the plot even though thhey could just have put a crafting table next to this spot (Yes, I'm talking about the Diagnostics Bot Dome).Then there's base building. Just a heads up : don't get attached to the base you'll never have time to finish in the first half, because you're going to completely leave this part of space in the second half of the game. I spent a lot of time building my base, even building the shuttle bay etc, just to find out I just had to leave it behind and never come back in the storyline.All the stuff you've collected and ditched on the floor or in the suitcases because you can't build drawers that open to store items in your base? Pointless.All in all, I still enjoyed the beginning of the game and if all those points were fixed I would gladly return to it, but the feeling that progression becomes more and more tedious as you get further in the game just doesn't cut it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after I saw a short part of a let's play and thought "Hey this looks like something for me",I had no expectations except that it would be a survival/exploration type game - this one with a humoristic side.All in all found the humor OK, sometimes even good, but other times slightly annoying. From what I've heard the trailers ( nothing I ever watched ) were more extreme, so it sounds like the humoristic side has been toned down a bit.Control wise, it suffers a little from consolitus in that it tries to do too much with too few buttons, but it is not all that bad. Having a quick bar of only four items is also very annoying, especially given how many "tool" items the game has.For the first 25 hours I had an OK to Good time with the game, I like the over all concept being presented in the first chapters, and the over arching story as well as the commentary from your suite.It has some issues with pacing, it is a little bit of a time grinder -  much due to the maximum traveling speed, even fully upgraded.I understand and agree with the fact that "space is big", and I LOVE with the progression of equipment, but it feels like that there is an upgrade or two missing. The crafting/base building part of the game is fairly basic ( and wth why are suitcases the only container in the game besides modules, ♥♥♥♥ just have to lie on the floor everywhere, bugging out and slowing down the game )But in the end I am heavily disappointed, because the game goes from a survival game w/ basebuilding and exploration to mostly a linear corridor runner until the story ends with an "end" sequence of a black screen and some dialog boxes, I questioned several times during this if it was a bug, but as far as I can tell, nope.After you've spent 10 minutes with a black screen the game tells you there is nothing left to do in the game and you can go play around in all the places you've already been, or better yet exit the game and wait until they've added more content. ( Essentially it drops you into a sandbox mode afterwards )I say it drops the survival part. Why?Because oxygen, food and water ceases to be issues, oxygen as a mechanic dropped and is only every used  once more in the entire story.Food and water ceases to be issues because every place you visit has bottles of water and goo packs around just about every corner.I say it drops the exploration, Why?There is still some exploration, just as there is exploration in every game - but it is not really used as a mechanic, nor is it something that rewards you.There is some indoor exploration still, but nothing compared to the first parts of the game.Tbh, this game ended when it should have opened up. It feels like after the end of the sequence above, you should still have had 50% of the game left.Do I regret the purchase? No, I had some fun along the way. Would I have purchased the game if I knew it was going to scrap the survival/exploration/basebuilding stuff after about 50% of the game? No, I would not.Tldr; About 20-30 hours in ( depending on how much exploration and resource gathering you do ) the Game throws away all time and effort you put into the survival/basebuilding part. After this it turns more into a long "get to the next objective" with little to no exploration and survival mechanics present. Base building is gone completely ( unless you count sandbox mode after story ends,  and you will most likely have explored most things explorable ).I do not regret my purchase, but would not have bought it, if I knew the above.

_childDocuments_.review: In other news. it looks great, movement is very simplified but fun. Area to explore is cool.  Crafting, Vehicles base building is interesting but rather limited.But man does the game need MASSIVE streamlining. The game has other game modes that take some of the annyoance and grind out! But also most of the mechanics. And they disable Achievements.Game was in release state for well over a year so i was sceptical. But it had major content updates and there is now quite a bit there for the price. Sadly making it bigger exposed it's problems qute badly. In the original 2 hour game they had no time to hit.Maybe then it was ok to slow the experince down and have a lot of back ond forth as "content". Now, unchanged, these mechanics (short ofxygen times, WAY too many tools, all with durability) are a  disaster!Quite some light, a lot of shadow. A very good foundation for a amazing game once it has been degrindyfied and streamlined. (EDIT:  never happened, changed it back to negative.).The light first:The humor is still amazing, although at times it tries a bit too hard. Especially the suit comments when flying around fall a bit short..That and the quite large, interesting and fun to explore area are the big highlight of the game.  The second highlight of the game. Sadly both are somewhat wasted on horrible balancing choices and grindy and tedious game mechanics. . So it  is a LONG way away from the much mentioned Space-Subnautica or even games like Empyrion. And you HAVE to go back. There is no (Subnautica)  surface while exploring. 50 (75, 150) secs out back in.    That get's VERY old VERY, VERY quickly! Apart from the oxygen supply of 50-about 200 secs - in a SPACESUIT! - not making any sense...immersion wise (yes i know... "it's a videogame") it ALSO is horrible  from a gameplay pov. That's the really bad part.  It should be raised to at least several minutes from the start. That would make progress easier. But that's not bad at all. Progress is too slow, ressources and crafting is WAY too grindy. Combined with WAY too many tools, all with durability...Than the (as usual) hopelessly exaggerated hunger and thirst....Unless you bypass it by a different game mode. Or a trainer (which i did after not many hours) , the game is no fun in the long run. Unlike in Subnautica there is no surface you can go up while exploring. You have to go back and forth between your base.  So not even Subnautica as excuse works. And unlike in Subnautica it takes quite a while until you can build bases or vehicles  to extend your reach.Both the unlocking progress and the grind levels for ressources/crafting do not go well with the other problem.1 Less tools! Use a multitool like in Empyrion to combine several of the things that have individual tools now. You also would not have to repair/replace like 10 tools all the time. It feels like No Man's Sky with it's 20 different refill mechanics.  It's just ressource collecting busywork That doesn't help gameplay in any way.2. Crafting costs down OR much longer stints outside to collect them. Faster progress in whatever way.  I find the game in normal mode, without trainer (oxgen, no tool duration)  unplayable. It's just very tedious grind in 1minute steps. Also for basebuilding you need 3 steps instead of 1 (+ressources)  like in Subnautica. That is another really unecessary Tedium added.If that makes the game somehat shorter but more fun, that's FINE! Grind was always a poor way to make games longer.3. A larger hotbar!! Why the hell are there only 4 slots if you need to juggle like 10 tools!? Yes, i know, it's for gamepads. But there are solution possible as well.----------It's basically a comedy version of Hellion. And much less realistic in terms of physics nd movement. Makes it much more accessible but i whish there would be options. movement in Breathedge is extremely simplified. It actually works just like in Subnautica, which makes no sense at all in space. Like that you slow down if you don't push a button. The game actually says so and claims "some mysterious anomaly might be at work or just lame devs" Which is a funny way of dealing with it.    has proper inertia and even orbital mechanics.  Hellion is sadly officially abandned now and won't be updated. Which is a shame because the basic that are (still) there are something very unique and special. Steeper learning courve than Breathedge but much less repetetive grind. It's worth a look but be warned. Shelter is rather similar to breathedge (-the humour) and Subnautica. Also Space based like BReathedge. But in VR. It would be quite good actually. It's is very well done control wise and has good ideas. . Sadly it has exactly the same problem as Breathedge: Idiotic levels of oxygen and very grindy crafting. Still if you're ok with that and have vr, give it a go. I had to give up on it which is a damn shame.Sadly it also has no other gamemodes, which Breathedge, Hellion and Subnautica have. No, Breathedge is apart from the fundamental gameplay concept, not really like Subnautica.  It may have taken inspiration from Subnauticas oxgen supply times. But forgot to take into account that Subnautica has a SURFACE! You don't have to go back to your base all 75/175 seconds!.  That makes Subnautica a lot less tedious, grindy and annyoing.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun in a lot of ways, and really tedious in others. There will be automatic comparisons to Subnautica, which is fair because they are so similar in some ways and yet polar opposites in other ways. Subnautica had an air tight sense of progression, while Breathedge's progression can feel extremely tedious at times due to how resources are allocated when building, how often you have to replace certain items, and how long it takes for you to achieve getting a device that expands your ability to explore. In Subnautica you always have a sense of being somewhat close to a major goal, while in Breathedge it feels so much more scattered and disorganized. Some of the building steps really needed to be streamlined or simplified to keep me going, because there are some parts where I just roll my eyes and can't believe I have to get more of this or build another thing to upgrade a certain thing. As far as the humor goes, sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't. Using condoms to breathe is kinda funny but not very clever to me if I'm being honest. I wish they had pushed the Soviet themes a bit further because some of it feels pretty half baked. For instance you can pee on anything, or use a chicken to plug a hole in a space station, but a lot of the time it feels like it's hurting the survival atmosphere. Random isn't always funny, at least to me. This part is entirely subjective so your mileage may vary. It's a gorgeous game, and runs infinitely better than Subnautica (I still can't believe they used their own custom-made, completely garbage engine for that game). Props to the design team for embracing that retro-futuristic design language that works so well. On paper, this was a game that was supposed to be my bread and butter, but the tedious nature of the building process and resource retrieval as well as some of the somewhat tone-deaf humor really hurt my enjoyment of the game. I recommend the game for anyone to try as it might really click with you, and I will definitely support the developer for being unique and interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to Steam lacking a neutral review i have a tendency to point out to readers to 'do their research'. For this game i really mean it. Got mine from a bundle so didn't do deeper research but perhaps even for that price i should have... Now as for the game some say it's like Subnautica. Forget those phony words as this is nothing like Subnautica as the focus here is on.... i don't know what the focus is on... as the standard game play loop is 'i need X and i don't know where to get X as i have already checked everywhere so off i go to see if i missed something with a 75-100 sec air tank'. Also lots of guides are in Russian. And the jokes probably work in Russian as well so if you are native speaker you might enjoy this more. I didn't warm up to the humor as you are focusing on staying alive and then a fast speaking AI voice keeps telling you stupid things and then you get messages from a chat app from some lady who also talks smack and makes equally little sense. And then there is the Save game bugs. Took me a while to encounter one but i eventually did and it cost me quite some effort. Of course it strikes when it mattered most. All in all in just some hours i found the game play exhausting. It took me 20 hours in the latest Subnautica to be exhausted, here the red line comes faster and you ask why go on. So do your homework on this. Or just skip it. This is not a substitute for Subnautica and in case you have not played the first Subnautica then please do so instead of looking at this one. I just really don't know what i am supposed to extract from this. Fun?  Jokes? Base building? Story? Seems like none of these are present. I may be wrong but my Grabber tool broke and i am unable to extract any of these from this proverbial hole of B-level game design that looks pretty and runs well but has some truly questionable game design ideas that might just not open up to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Has a Subnautica feel for the first 2/3 of the game.  Absolutely loved it.  The last 1/3 is, as others have stated, a "shooter" on rails which is okay but a big departure from the first part of the game.  It's a pity because the first part of the game is so good and interesting that it still carried me through to the end to find out the end of the story.  There are some annoyances, though.  The lack of proper storage and intuitive inventory management is an issue.  Another being the base-building that looked like it was originally going to be much deeper but ended up very shallow.  Tools that break and can't be repaired is also an issue, mainly because it's a pain to organize the resources you collect in the first place, but it would have been much better if they had included advanced versions of all the tools like they did with the scrapper.  The environment is amazing, though.  Full of mystery and tells its own story.  The mystery of the coffins was pretty interesting too.  I definitely recommend this game for anyone who liked Subnautica.  Pick it up on sale.  The ending may be a bit of a disappointment.  A bit of advice: don't worry about collecting everything in the last section of the game.  It's a waste of time.  You'll have plenty of resources to make anything you need without going back and picking up everything that's laying about.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is a mixed bag. The good:The game does a really great job at recreating the same sense of exploration and wonder Subnautica had (and this game does take A LOT of inspiration from Subnautica) but in space with a bit more of a focus on humor rather than the tension Subnautica had. And it's awfully pretty to look at when the lighting hits just right. The soundtrack is great (I can't get the chanting ladies on the radio out of my head). And the balance of reloading your breath is perfect (arguably better than Subnautica.).The bad: You're going to be backtracking A LOT. I'd argue only about 20% of your time running around is exploring and 80% of the time is spent traversing areas you've already been to as you need to resupply crafting items. I tried to make sure my inventory was absolutely filled basically every time I entered a new area to avoid this sort of thing and I still would have to go back multiple times to basically every area. This even seems purposeful as later on there will be a bunch of times where you'll be exploring a building, get to the very end only to discover a recipe that will immediately require you to head back to the beginning to your spaceship to craft and then come back to the end of the same facility immediately and use the item right next to the spot where you found the recipe.You will basically always move at a snails pace and because you're backtracking a lot this becomes very noticeable as the game goes on. There's speed upgrades but on balance they don't happen quickly enough with a couple of exceptions (EI: by the time you build a base and are ready to make the rocket bike and space car you're leaving you're getting ready to leave the first zone and enter the second zone which doesn't allow you to use either the space car or the rocket bike.).There's no real reason to build any sort of significant space base. Similar to the problem with the skycar and the rocket bike right about the time that you start having enough materials to consider building a space base that's bigger than 1 room (maybe 2 at max) you're leaving the first zone in favor of a series of zones where you can't build the space base at all and there's no reason to go back to this starting zone. I think if the zones were redesigned to everything was in 1 zone and you could build bases in all of the main areas this would be remedied but with the games zones how they are there's no incentive to do it.The humor starts to drop in quality by a significant amount after the first chapter. I laughed out loud more than a few times in the first zone but after that I think I only found one joke mildly funny (It's the jigsaw puzzle joke). And there's a few moments where the it feels like the writers wanted to write a joke about something but forgot (the best example I can think off the top of my head is that there's a device that opens jars that's designed to look like a man and your space suit mentions how people we're angry that it wasn't a womans hand. Now, you could write a pretty funny joke about that premise I imagine. But simply saying they could have avoided such a controversy it just comes off as a complaint about PC culture more than a joke about it (and this sort of thing happens a few times.).Conclusion:The games not bad by any means but I feel like these issues really bring the game down more than they should have. A bit better balancing around crafting, a map redesign to have all the zones together to favor base building, and a bit more ironing out of jokes later on and the game and this would be a solid exploration game. As it is though it's just enough for me not to recommend it unless you're REALLY itching for an exploration game and you have already played Subnautica and Subnautica: BZ

_childDocuments_.review: A tough choice to rate the game this way because it started off so strong, and may still be good if you are starting from scratch and playing through the whole thing, but the last "half" of this game is laughable. The first three chapters are great and have good survival mechanics and lots of exploration and crafting, but then it goes downhill fast. This may have hit me more after waiting a year and half for the game to be finished after playing the first three chapters, but for some reason they completely changed the game and turned it into a linear walking simulator. I don't know whose idea this was but it was incredibly disappointing. All the crafting becomes easy because resources are literally everywhere you can barely keep your inventory empty, there is barely any exploration because you are stuck in your ship the entire time going from wreckage to wreckage that have unnecessarily long halls that just seem to eat up time, and your suit AI is constantly blabbing about nothing in attempts to get some chuckles out of you. You get a few new items that don't really do anything and seems like they were just added in for you to do something, then a "boss" fight and then the game is over. Somehow the first 3 chapters were a good 20 hours of gameplay and the next three were over in 5, with one chapter literally being about 20 minutes. They make it seem like you are going to a few big areas, but nope, you get one and then you are stuck in generic spaceships the rest of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the type of game you'd want a 8/10 rating for as opposed to up/down. Price: goodGraphics: goodArt style: Subnautica, now in orangeCrafting: Straightforward, but hard to lookup ingredients in contrast with SubnauticaSurvival: Feels like a chore, not an accomplishmentExploration: mostly hindered by lack of oxygen which requires batteries (oddly) which require alkali or luckProgression: poor (needlessly, deliberately, and blatantly slowed)Tl;dr: If you *loved* Subnautica, you will *like* this. _childDocuments_.review: This is a campy, solo, story-based, space adventure.  It has so much to offer it is hard to choose the best part.  The only way to learn the Drill is to take the blue print into your backpack. Graphics = GreatStory line = Absurdly Exaggerated but GreatHumor = Pushing the limits of PG13Difficulty = Challenging at first but Balanced late game.Bugs = I could not find any. I did have difficulty launching the game after an update, but they have since resolved that issue.Tips:Starting off, holding your breath to acquire materials is tedious, but as you upgrade your oxygen tank and learn where the refill areas are it becomes significantly easier to manage.  The first air tank upgrade is directly down from the starting ship.  Even though most resources are finite, this game is not intended for hoarders.  There are ample supplies as you adventure and there is no real advantage to wasting time transferring resources between chapters.  Each chapter has more then enough resources to complete the chapter.  At most it is handy to have a box of food and water on your ship, and perhaps a second box to dump your back pack from time to time.  Do not be afraid to use candles or other resources to advance as there are tones to replace what you use.  Collectible can also take up space.  In order to get credit for finding something it only has to enter your backpack.  After that you can discard the item and view it later via the menu.  In Fact, it is a good habit to take every unique item and then discard it if you are not going to use it to decorate your ship or station.  Poster, notes, and pictures can be reattached to walls, and the trophy case displaces all the toys and underwear you find.  Be careful stacking things as they tend to wiggle a bit due to the physics engine.   In Chapter 3 the best place I found to create a base is directly behind the electrical core.  It is fairly central to most other locations and there are more then a number of advantages to placing your base there.  It is also useful to make a flat base.  A layered base might look neat but it can sometimes be annoying to navigate from the inside.  Glass can be found near the hydroponic area (Cow area) and electronics can be salvaged by capturing the scavenger bots (near the large rolls of tape).Regardless of your play style there are hours of campy fun to be had, the suit AI is hilarious, and there is so much to find that you would have to be a pro-scavenger to find it all without help.  I have no problem recommending this game to my friends.  I hope you enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 3 chapters of this game, which is what I spent most of my game time before the final part of the game came out, is worth the price of buying it because of the humor, the game play, and the exploration needed to get the tasks done to complete each mission. In these chapters, running out of oxygen is your biggest threat as you find and build equipment to make your travel faster and have the ability to go farther. The humor of the AI suit helps guide you as you explore the wreckage around you and finding "junk" to put together that makes your game play a little better. But after you complete about 3/4 of the game and get to Normandy, much of that game play is like a trilogy that has 2 great movies and the 3rd one stinks, but you watch it just to see how things end. Instead of exploring the landscape, you are piloting a ship, landing at limited places that will have you traveling down corridor after corridor, returning to your ship to make something, and then returning to corridor after corridor until you find everything the game wants you to find in that particular location. After that, you go to the next place and repeat as necessary. The last part of the game feels like the developers lost interest and just wanted to be through with it. I have played it and will likely play it again all the way through but after that, it will collect some dust before I revisit it again. I recommend it because 75% of the game play is great, with the last 25% of the game a weak wrap up containing a lot of cheesy dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did. Come on, Subnautica in space with funny jokes and Postal pissing? How can it go wrong?Well, simple. Once you get the high oxygen levels the game becomes a boring empty shell of a grind. The main "plot" is presented as a joke, which after the 15th time is jammed into your eye sockets and then further hammered in with a pipe wrench.Unlike in Subnautica where there's mystery and wonder, as well as tons of different dangerous creatures, Breathedge lacks in every department. From the easily overloaded inventory system (which to be fair was annoying in Subnautica's case too), all the way to the "combat" in the game. The game has base building, but what for? There's no need to stockpile resources any more than the shuttles you have access to that are free. Once you get a vehicle half the survival tension is gone, cuz you can just whiz around like Peter Pan stole a broomstick from Hogwarts.You do get some fun blueprints later in the game, but they are all the "win more" type of blueprints. In fact, the main drive of the game was supposed to be this mystery as to what happened to your ship, what purpose it was for and who keeps spamming you with dumb jokes all this time. The game also has a fascination with chickens. Cool story, but "just use a chicken to solve a problem" isn't an infinite resource of comedy, and sadly Breathedge leans heavily on the paltry as it's comedic backbone. Unfortunately said backbone has a herniated disc by the end of act 1, and the pipe wrench has hit you in the head so many times that it's well and truly past your colon. Any and all interest was lost for me by the end of Act 1. I had infinite resources, endless supply of oxygen, tons of water and fuel, and a space broom stick to fly around in. If you want the ultimate transportation you can even build yourself a space car. Cool, that's something to work towards, as if having TONS of oxygen wasn't easy enough, might as well make it unlimited.Well, since I got bored with this game, I might as well uninstall it.I usually don't demolish a product before it is done, but what's on offer here is irredeemable, barring an almost full rework of Chapter 1. And as we all know, it's the first 5 minutes that are important to grab the player. Well, I spent 15 hours playing this and still nothing grabbed me. Sure there's a few chuckles to be had here and there, but I can get the same and better results just by throwing eggs at a wall.In conclusion, if Chapter 1 is this bad, I can only imagine 2 and 3. It's all downhill from here, and I don't think rolling with the corpse of this game is something I want to do, and I recommend that neither should you.

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: 7/10Breathedge can be a fun game... if you are willing to suffer through it. As a veteran of games like Subnautica and The Long Dark, I enjoy slow-paced, relaxed games. However, Breathedge suffers from a couple of major issues that significantly tip the balance between work and fun toward the former:1. Poorly balanced difficulty mechanics: Sure, having but a few seconds of oxygen before you have to go back to the nearest 'breathing spot' is an incentive to explore and gather resources to get better gear that will let you venture further. However, by the time you upgrade or get stuff that mitigates this, you already need to go even further... and back again. This back and forth gets old, and a poor balance means that the time you have ALWAYS feels too short by the time you manage to upgrade your gear. The equipment that ultimately lets you get rid of all this work arrives way too late, and my guess is that all but the most dedicated players will have abandoned the game by then.2. Cool stuff arrives so late in the game and has such steep material requirements that it's not even worth using it: *MINOR SPOILER* As an indie developer, you'd expect they would have tried to maximize the fun while getting rid of assets and mechanics that will never be realistically used. Basebuilding is somewhat deep and complex, but unless you are dead set on engaging in it, you will find yourself building only the very basic you need to accomplish your goals, lest you suffer through hours and hours of back and forth gathering materials to install that one cute lamp. This is compounded by the fact that basebuilding arrives by the time your gameplay becomes highly nomadic... so what's the point of spending hours finding enough glass (super rare) to install nice windows on a place you will hardly spend time in before you need to move on?Storage space always feels extremely limited, so organizing your stuff is always HARD LABOR. Once you are finally ecstatic that you can build your first locker... you find that they have the same capacity as the pesky suitcases. That's right... after a massive effort finding blueprints, building your base and collecting materials, a whole wall of lockers has the same capacity as a suitcase, which is 1/100th the size. Why?If you can get past that, the story is fun, some gags will probably have you chuckling and the visuals are beautiful. And MASSIVE props for not only straying away from all the PC agenda, but actually making fun of its most hypocritical specimens. In this day and age, it takes guts for an indie studio to go that way.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I can't. There is so much unnecessary padding in this game, it's infuriating. The rest of the this review will be just listing things that pad your game time:-Refilling your oxygen takes an unnecessary amount of time. You will just stand around for a sold 20-30 seconds waiting for the bar to refill-Traveling between locations is slow and boring. There is so much dead space between points of interest. You just hold the w key until you get to where you need to go. You eventually get a boost, but like the oxygen, it takes forever for it to fully recharge. Even the vehicles feel like they don't travel fast enough.-The resource management is infuriating, they never give you enough storage space, and you will always have to move areas so your resources will be stuck there unless you spend half an hour going back and forth to transfer them.-The crafting log does NOT show you what resources are required to craft the item. The only way to see the requirements are if you are at the processor. Knowing what you need to craft would alleviate the resource management issues so that you can always bring things you need with you-The crafting takes several seconds before you actually receive the item. Why is this necessary? You have to be in a safe area to craft, so there is no need for this delay, which would ordinarily punish you for crafting in dangerous situations-The research. Oh god is the research infuriating. Each research costs materials to start. Then, it takes TEN MINUTES for it to finish and locks out all other research options, even if you have the resources for them. Why do I have to wait, what is this a free to play game? Absolute waste of my money, if I could refund I would.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, but the constant fight for oxygen the first 3 hours of the game, having my tools break after 5 uses, and a next to pointless base building mechanic is not fun. It's not Subnautica in space. The only similarity is the exploration and base building, and it's D tier compared to Subnautica.You go from fighting against your O2 supply for 2-3 hours in a smaller sized open area to fighting against your oxygen in a 2-3 times larger open area which is arguably the most boring part of the game. It then throws base building at you, and the more you work on your base the sooner you'll realize that it's just one big building to store junk in. And get this - you build your base and the game ushers you into a hallway/walking sim without the ability to go back and visit your base. So all that work and time you spent building a base is completely ruined. I refunded before I even got into the final acts because I had 0 motivation to play this game.Another issue I thought I'd mention, the "Grabber tool" is used to collect Alkali, a component used in the creation of batteries. This tool literally breaks in 6-8 uses. To craft the Grabber, you NEED batteries. So what do you do if you don't have a grabber to collect the resources to make more batteries? Well, you float around and break everything electronic you can find to get one singular battery. All while at the same time fighting your Scrapper's durability which breaks within 25 uses (one container takes about 5 hits to break) this game is just one big battle against your tool durability and the laughable oxygen supply.To touch on this topic, tell me if this sounds fun. You have everything you need to go explore. Scanner, scrapper, drill, the works. Too bad they break so insanely fast, so your drill breaks and you find a door that you need to use the drill on. Well time to float all the way back, make a new drill, float all the way back, drill the door. This forces the player to make MULTIPLE tools in case the equipped one breaks, so instead of your inventory being full of useful crafting materials like Subnautica, half of your inventory is full of spare tools because you never know what you're going to need or when you're going to need it.The UI is pretty terrible. The way the crafting menu is sorted is confusing, and you can't craft multiple things at once. Say you're crafting a scrapper and go to a different tab to see what else you can craft - well that actually CANCELS the scrapper being crafted. You need to sit there in the same tab as what you are crafting and wait. Every. Single. Time.Yes, the game is funny, but it's not fun. It probably has some of the driest humor I've seen in a video game, and I laughed quite a few times. But it doesn't excuse the fact that the game is just badly designed in so many ways.If this game is like Subnautica then I must've played a different game. One is a good survival game with great survival mechanics that all work in tandem to avoid tedious grinding for resources. The other is Breathedge.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't, I'm sorry. This game just isn't for me. It drags SO BAD. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. It seems to check off so many mechanics I like, offers the promise of being like Subnautica but in space. At first I was finding lots of the same enjoyment, "diving" into space to explore and gather resources before hurrying home to see what new things I could craft.But, two things happened. I lost interest in the narrative, which just didn't seem very cohesive and good, and is scattered amongst random bits of humor, trying to be edgy but often just being uncomfortable. Secondly, the awaited conclusion of the game.. sucks. The entire format of the game changes, from being an open world survival craft exploration game to being a corridor shooter. A very, very bad one. All you have to look forward to is awkwardly shooting at a few turrets, two boss fights which both are simply red-light green-light running to designated spots. No more interesting exploration, no more habitat construction, no more foraging and gathering resources necessary. I stubbornly finished out the game, and am left very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, it's very obviously inspired by Subnautica, and though it might not be as well-crafted as Subnautica, it's still worth playing if you like the genre. For some the change of pace might keep the game fresh for the 15-25 hours it takes to complete, but personally i felt like i got gadgets and stuff i hardly used and build a base i never got to use as much as expected. It doesn't feel rushed or completely disjointed as I somewhat expected, but i would have preferred a more coherent experience. Still, good first attempt from the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a good game somewhere in here, but unfortunately the game is VERY slowly paced and it commits a true crime: it doesn't just gate you in progress by having you do a lot of tedious stuff, it also punishes by having to do more tedium if you are a little bit too slow or die or anything like that - you have to go back a while, wasting consumable oxygen resources you then have to replenish by grinding.
