_childDocuments_.review: Basically, this game is what would happen if the writers of Robot Chicken decided to make a survival horror game in space.  You've got a live chicken on a stick being used as a multitool, you've got text messages from a space babe that keep you guessing as to who the space babe is even after the game is played through, you've got a horny diagnostic computer that yells at you about pushing buttons, mutant space cows, an army of undead robots (literally they made that work), space mayo, base building and crafting, and the ability to piss on anything duke nukem style.  I don't think I've ever chuckled as much at a game as this and every plot twist just is weirder and weirder.  Lots of "Come to this scene, do the detective work, WTF until you're nearly out of oxygen, go back, think about what you just saw, go back, look".  The only complaint is there's not much replay value once all the jokes are told, but it's well worth the money and 30-40hrs of play time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not Subnautica in space. The gameplay loop closely resembles the gameplay of Subnautica. However, because Breathedge is hell-bent on convincing the player that all of their actions are meaningless, the gameplay becomes tedious, and because resource gathering tools in Breathedge are essentially one-excursion-use, the game becomes TOO tedious. Too many times I had to leave at the climax of a "main quest" type mission, run through empty hallways for 10 minutes, build the tool or "Useless garbage the devs made so you could proceed" (I'm not kidding, this happens multiple times). This sort of humor happens so often that I can't help but feel like the story was seriously neglected, or as an excuse for poor level layout. There are genuine moments where this sort of humor hits, but it isn't at all balanced by the solemness of the setting, and the constant breaking of the fourth wall serves only to enhance the feeling of tediousness. Spoiler Example: You need to run through a long, empty airplane hanger, and then two long, empty hallways, and down some stairs, only to be told you need to build something to proceed. So you backtrack up the stairs, through the two long hallways and one empty plane hanger to your base, build the item, and return. Oh wait! That's only if you had the correct tool with you, when you made your first trip down, because there was a resource you needed to gather that was located at the bottom of the stairs. So, if you don't have that tool, you need to run through a long, empty airplane hanger, and then two long, empty hallways, and down some stairs, then backtrack up the stairs, through the two long hallways and one empty plane hanger to your base, build the resource gathering tool, then run through the long, empty airplane hanger, two long, empty hallways, and down the stairs, collect the resource, backtrack up the stairs, through the two long hallways and one empty plane hanger back to your base, build the item, run BACK through a long, empty airplane hanger, and then two long, empty hallways, and down some stairs, and use the item to proceed. The thing that gets me is that the developers knew this was a hassle for the player, because the game offers for the player to fast travel, runs a loading screen, and then informs the player that unfortunately there is no fast travel. This punchline is pretty funny, but I didn't really enjoy the build up of the joke, which was You'll never feel like your trying to survive in a dangerous environment, like in Subnautica. You'll just feel like your doing meaningless busywork. Which the game will literally remind you of, all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: An enjoyable game for people who like slightly challenging survival gameplay, mixed with easter eggs, an interesting storyline and some small inventory management. For those who enjoy subnautica, this is a good similar game. Do note however that the gameplay is more narrative and becomes less 'survival-ish' and more story driven by later chapters.What I liked:- Awesome graphics, great visuals and environment- Lots of exploration and funny scenes to come across, which makes the game enjoyable. - Abundant resources - you don't have to struggle to scrape stuff, which made it so much more forgiving- A gradual progression that is not frustrating - at a certain point in the game, you have adequate safe areas with oxygen so you won't find yourself chaining oxygen stations, which was a relief.- Music is goodOther comments:- An underutilized base building portion - just not much use of building a well crafted base since you move onto further areas each time- Some players complain over the low durability of tools: This was not too much of an issue, resources are abundant and is not as frustrating to me as others make it out to be.- Game lags a lot when I die, takes quite awhile to reload up my last save.- Wish that the game would allow save points at different parts of the game so I can go back and get achievements I've missed.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in this game due to the same promise of "Subnautica in space with a sense of humour" as me then prepare to be disappointed.The gameplay is very shallow in comparison, no wildlife, no base-building, and very limited yet still tedious crafting. The only thing this game would have going for it is the sense of humour, and if you're still in high-school then this game is probably right on your level. If inflating condoms and making a giant ♥♥♥♥ and balls from scrap is something you find hilarious then more power to you, but don't expect anything more thoughtful than that.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this a while ago when it was in early access with only the first chapter. After 30 minutes of trying to get past this 30 sec ox timer bored and quit the game, Then followed the news on the store page a bit to see when it was released and now on release tried it again.So, after years 1.0 is there and on the plus:1 - There is now a story choice which eliminates the tedious grind at the start as you can now examine the area without having to be back in the pod after 30 seconds. So I would guess most people can actually now play the game instead of floating near the shuttle to scramble when the timer is done.2 - style/graphics and the initial comedy approach works.--------------But after 2/3 hrs while the initial oxygen grind is gone all other irritations still remain.1 - It takes forever to get somewhere, even if you eventually install the 25% speedboost. I guess this mechanic can be found in the book "facepalm designs" iow. I almost taped the forward button down.2 - After yet another "staccato" joke delivery (nr 845) this style of humor is now also a tedious repetition.As a remote evaluation I estimate that this team was more (or only) focused in getting from joke to joke than actually creating a game.. _childDocuments_.review: Yet another Survival-Crafting-Exploration game, but this time with humour?My biggest criticism of Breathedge is that it doesn't seem to respect the player's time. In the second chapter of the game, you're given six objectives to essentially unlock progress. The map is large, your oxygen is limited (roughly 2.5 minutes at a time, plus consumables), and your transportation options take some time. There is a significant amount of travelling back and forth between base and objectives.In nearly every case, the objectives involve reaching an obstacle, scanning the obstacle, then returning to base to grind materials and build the tool necessary to progress. Every time. Adding further trips if you, for instance, ran out of durability on your scanner tool or forgot to bring it. Eventually it becomes frustrating and tedious, rather than a logistical challenge.The humour - what they bill as the real selling point of the game - is more miss than hit. For every clever subversion of the mechanics - one puzzle asks you to enable the "lower radiation" setting in the game menu - there are a dozen outdated memes, ill-considered references to "hypocrites" (in beta, "libtards"), scatological humour, and ham-fisted fourth-wall breaking.It's also not without its share of bugs - game-breaking progress-stoppers due to faulty flags, trapping the player in geometry, and soft-locking due to poor design. The autosaving is also brutal - make it a habit to manually save often, otherwise you'll find yourself repeating long stretches of the game.All in all a less peaceful experience than Subnautica and less satisfying than Valheim, with humour that's far less clever than it thinks it is. Not terrible, but disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I can't recommend this game. I wanted to enjoy it really bad, but I simply couldn't.You will read a lot in other reviews that this game is "Subnautica in Space", but this is exactly the problem with this game: It tried too hard to be Subnautica, and it failed miserably in every aspect of it.Some mistakes are just too grotesque, like the sheer quantity of useless items that you will learn to create and will serve to almost nothing, for example, there is literally one item that you create to open one single door the entire game, but as you never know when the game will ask again for that item, you end up carrying that thing around "just in case". The oxygen system is a mess as well - It's too freaking hard in the beginning, and just a nuisance later, and it's something that is basically forgotten halfway through the game.The game lacks focus, it lacks commitment, and you are left with a mess of a game that is full of awesome concepts, but never deliver it right.And again, this is really sad. You can see that they COULD HAVE been "Subnautica in Space", but it's just a project of some guys making fun of everything, all the time, without thinking exactly where this is leading. I won't even comment the story of the game... Or the writing. I feel dumber after playing this.Apart from that, the art and design team should receive a prize, it's the true highlight of this game. I loved the graphics, the soundtracks were right on point, and you can see that they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ knew how to model all those props. Everything looks good, even sometimes when people are dead - They are a frozen art of gore. But they decided to be too gore for their own sake as well. Anyway this doesn't take away their merit, they were awesome. But then again, it's kinda sad that the level design didn't exactly match the survival aspect, there is not so many places where you go "ohhh, this is a perfect place for me to build a base!", but then again, this game is not a good survival game.To sum up, I think that, if the art team had a better director and a better writer, this game would be worth it. But the game looks like a conglomerate of ideas rotting due of lack of decisions and commitment. And this sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Breathedge for the sole reason of what it begins as, and what it's sequel could be if the developers learned their lessons.Chapter 1-3 is an open world survival crafting game in space. The subnautica influences are directly in the game, so yes the influence in intended. Apart from the grind that drags on a bit, it's a solid game. Until it isnt.At one point it is no longer a survival game. It just... stops. It then becomes a puzzle FPS. Oxygen isn't even a factor anymore for the last half of the game. You follow the objectives, follow the same formula. Walk down LONG hallways, find out you need to craft something at the end of the level, walk ALLLLL the way back to your ship to craft needed item, walk all the way back then leave. Repeat several times. To reiterate the 2nd half of the game (give or take) feels like a completely different game, and it isn't a good game. I continued ONLY because the first half made me want to see the story through. It stopped becoming just playing the game and it turned into stubborn hate-playing. The ending made me interested in what the sequel could be, and if they make the game more consistent and listen to the abundant feedback on this issue. So, while I am recommending the game itself, I believe the game as a whole falls short. If Breathedge 2 is good, watch a playthrough on YouTube to find out the story without spending the time and money on the questionable first installment.

_childDocuments_.review: My interest in Breathedge was piqued by JaWoodle, who had done some gameplay videos on it, and the crafting/survival style and sense of humour looked right up my alley. And boy, was I right about that. The first few chapters in early release were absolutely fantastic,  and I couldn't wait for the next installment. The smart and sharp sense of humour in this game has me in stitches, and the gameplay was fun and engaging, and challenging as well. When the full game finally released in February, I was so pumped. And then I started playing. This new chapter was very different, and there was no further base crafting, and the exploring was limited to flying around in the Normandy and doing fetch quests inside of other broken ships, retrieving the parts to fix my ship so I could progress. It wasn't bad, but not why I had enjoyed the game. I thought, maybe in the next stage we'll get some more crafting/survival stuff. Nope. It was more run/fetch/build/progess runs through more broken ships. You can't even leave the Normandy to go out into space and explore in your suit. No more sweeping, stunning views of space as you sputter around trying to scrounge resources. And suddenly there are cutscenes where you have ZERO control over your character. And now there are "bosses" that are pretty trite, and seem like forced attempts at humour. Honestly, everything new released in the "final" version adds nothing to the game, and in fact takes away from everything I enjoyed in playing it to begin with. It feels to me like the developers just wanted to wrap this project up, so put in the minimum amount of time to get the story done and wrapped up. I still recommend the game, but once you rebuild the Normandy and are about to fly off to the next stage, everything just goes downhill. Still, I put lots of hours into the first couple of stages, and it was well worth what I paid.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game a 6/10. It's an average survival crafting game, in the vein of Subnautica, Planet Terraformer, etc. I enjoyed it the most in the first two chapters where the focus was more on exploration, crafting, and survival. Here were my main issues:1. After the first two chapters (after leaving in the Normandy), the rest of the game is very linear. There is very  little to explore other than the clearly-marked areas you must go to in order to advance the plot.2. There are collectible items all over the place, but it feels like a big joke the devs were playing on players, because 99% of that stuff is "useless junk" that you'll never really have a use for, unless for some crazy reason you go back to the start and waste your life with base-building (and there aren't nearly as many customization options as other games in this ilk, so you'd run out of inspiration very quick there). When I got to the end of the game, I really wished I hadn't spent so much time stockpiling stuff in case I might need it. 3. The one time I DIDN'T stockpile an item (a tool), I got softlocked in the game and couldn't progress (Chapter 6). I looked in every nook and cranny, but I couldn't find the parts I needed to make the thing I needed to progress. Luckily, I was able to reload from a prior checkpoint.  4. The humor mostly didn't land with me. I wasn't offended; as a female gamer I'm used to games catering to the 12-year-old boy sensibility. But I doubt even a 12 year old boy would find any of the sexist humor funny.  The writing depended a lot on tired sexist tropes (isn't it funny how dumb men are when they think a hot woman is interested in them??? ha...ha.). There seemed to be thousands of corpses around, but none of them (but one, as I recall) was female. No female characters--or corpses--have a face. And the only living female character a nameless, faceless "babe" in a pink spacesuit whose sole purpose is to draw the protagonist onwards. Really? Is this 2024 or 1980, devs?  HOWEVER, I did find some of the other jokes funny--I liked the spacesuit voice a lot, and I have to say I laughed out loud when you had the choice to swap out the robot's cigarette for something else ("Hooray for censorship!"). Also loved the Subnautica callout at the end, and the self-aware interactions with the end credits--that was great.  So, sometimes it did get a chuckle out of me. 5. The plot made no sense. Like, it was so convoluted and insane I had no idea what was going on most of the time. I think that was by design, but it would have been nice if it had been simplified just a wee bit. I didn't understand who the Green Universe were, at all, for example. I wondered at first if they were vegan terrorists (which would have been funny) but they apparently ate meat since they had cows and cans of beef and such on their ship. I also didn't understand why we needed to examine all the corpses and find out how they died. I'm sure I missed some dialogue, but it whizzed by so fast I was never able to keep up. 6. I know it's meant to be funny ("they were so dumb they all died!") but some of the scenes were pretty bleak for a game that's supposed to be funny. Smeared blood everywhere, lots of suicides, bodily organs (including brains) floating about--it was more "creepy and gross" rather than funny. I didn't really see the point of having so much gore in a game advertising itself as comedy (if I'm playing Alien: Isolation or Dead Space, no problem, if you see what I'm getting at).  7. Often very tedious (although this is expected with this kind of game). I didn't like this as much as other games like this mostly because the 360-degree space navigation was often disorientating. It was very hard to find small objects in the vastness of space, and I often had such trouble finding my vehicle, even with the white label/icon on it. I'd be spinning around constantly, trying to figure out where I was, where my vehicle was, etc. This game would not be for someone with motion sickness.  I didn't realize in the beginning that the game had a forward progression (a literal forward movement, and you wouldn't need to go back to previous points), so I wasted a lot of time building up bases and then abandoning them after they got too far away to be useful.8. This is a small quibble, but why not let us interact with the chicken? Grandpa said to feed the chicken, but we're never allowed to do so. We can't even see the chicken in our inventory. Likewise, what was the point of not giving "Babe" a face? Was it just too much trouble to animate that?

_childDocuments_.review: After four hours, I must say that this is a Very Good Game. I think I'm about halfway through the early release Act 1 Scene 1 plot (judging from others who have finished), and I haven't encountered any real bugs. The environment is beautiful and funny at the same time: wonderful artistry. Gameplay is fairly intuitive. I don't mind feeling stupid at puzzle games, and this one does challenge me in particular, but I'm not racing to finish before everyone else so I can post another boring HAY GUYZ youtube review/playthrough. As for me, I'm looking for absorbing entertainment, and this game scratches that itch. first of all, just click around and manipulate the environment, then open the inventory menu, which is huge, and click around. That gives you the roadmap for the game, the things you need to be thinking about as you fool around with all the stuff you can manipulate. Second, Well, I can't remember the second point. The immortal chicken, the running jokes, the breaking of the fourth wall, the goofy Easter eggs, random silliness, bizarre sight gags, and internet culture references--all make for a fun time. There's also a vague sense of a storyline. I mean, the spaceship crashed for some reason (no spoilers here, no sirree!), and this Act 1 Scene 1 sequence establishes the expository elements of a greater story arc. For me, this engages my interest because I have a hard time with plot narrative no matter what. There are some quirks I don't like, but, I mean, compared to anything released by Bethesda, this thing is squeaky clean. For example, everything is a fetch quest, more or less, but I dig mats gathering, as long as something cool comes from the work. In addition, I wish the plot items found and/or built had just a *tad* more explanation. I've got things I know should be installed somewhere, but in the confusion of this wide and complex game, I can't remember for the life of me where the things should go. Alas. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Breathedge, but it's a pretty frustrating experience.  It's got all the interesting systems you'd expect in a Subnautica-style survival/crafting game.  The problem is that all those systems end up fighting each other rather than complementing each other.  For example:* The game's graphics and world design are great.   the brutally-short oxygen gauge means you never have time to look at any of it.* The game puts a lot of effort into its jokes.   they're delivered so fast that you don't have a chance to actually listen to them.* You've got a variety of tools to build.   you have no way of knowing in advance what tool you'll need at a particular location, so you have to carry them all.  (And often, two of each, due to the low durability of each tool.)  This takes up the inventory space you were hoping to use for stuff you collect when you get there.* There's a good variety of resources to collect and play with.   the early game has your resource storage split into several separate locations, leading to a lot of boring ferrying between stations.  A few hours in, you get a suitcase to store things in, which cannot be moved if it has items in it (?!).* Tonally and aesthetically, the game is really strong.   it tries to be both a jokey survival farce and a dangerous-but-hauntingly-beautiful space simulator at the same time, and those two never gel together into a coherent whole.  The game is trying for a tone of "whistling past the graveyard", but the whistle and the graveyard never seem to be in the same place at the same time.You can see the kind of game Breathedge wants to be: something like Portal, a difficult game punctuated by black comedy.  It never really gets there.

It combines "old good" gaming mechanics, space environment and physics, hard survival game with very low resources, puzzles and exploring, with specific graphic style, specific "black" humor, and unusual storyline, into a really great gaming experience, which will catch you, and will not let you leave for many hours... Pros: - graphic style- specific humor- unusual storyline- soundtrack- always is there something new to discover- challenging difficulty (in survival mode)continuously growing difficulty, which let you learn new mechanics, but still keep you in an endeavorCons: - You will spend many hours in it, and keep saying yourself again and again: "I will just finish this, and I´ll turn it of..."Result: 10/10 (11/10 for this price ;-) )

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to check this out after having not played it since EA in 2018. Doesn't look like they ever made the early game any less of a slog - every trip from your one and only oxygen source (to start) means you get maybe 20 seconds of meaningful exploration time out of a ~2 minute round trip. However, unlike Subnautica, because of that single safe haven, exploration is painful and tedious rather than exciting and fun. It's like if the lifepod was your only source of oxygen for... enough hours apparently that I just quit caring.The writing is singularly terrible - this game has moments where it could be genuinely beautiful, but it relentlessly spews toilet humor at every moment where you might, possibly, have otherwise experienced a little wonder and joy. Humor relies on the element of surprise guys, 20 near identical jokes in a row isn't 20 times funnier. Either of these separately I could maybe have dealt with, but with the two combined, I just have no desire to bother.Don't buy the Subnautica in space PR. It's not even in the same ballpark.It's not the worst survival game I've ever played. I still regret paying for it.

_childDocuments_.review: As I'm sure did many others including perhaps you, gentle reader, I was very interested in this game because I loved Subnautica. You versus the environment, man versus nature, you start with nothing and slowly but surely manage to eke out some degree of control and purpose.Unfortunately, Breathedge seems absolutely determined to make sure you never forget for a second you're playing a video game via a constant barrage of fourth-wall breaks. The VERY FIRST objective is something like "craft this useless crap added by the developers" and when you do, it's essentially a scrap metal ♥♥♥♥ and balls. Then you get your first NPC contact, a female character, and her radio icon is just a pair of tits. I'm sure this is hilarious in Russia or whatever, but the entire thing just feels like it was written by a bunch of twelve year olds and kills any possibility of suspension of disbelief or immersion.I've been a Steam user for 17 years as you can see from my profile. This is the first game I've ever refunded (and I pre-ordered Colonial Marines). It's a shame, because as I said at the start I love the genre and was quite enthusiastic for this one, but the problems with it are systemic and can't be fixed with a patch.Avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say that the fact Steam's recommendation algorithms never once recommended this game to me means they are completely and utterly uselessly broken. I one day had the urge to dig through the favorably-reviewed sci-fi games for any hidden gems I might have missed, and this diamond of a game was what came up after a couple hours of digging.Next let me say this: Don't let the jokes on the store and news pages fool you. I was a bit hesitant, sometimes developers can get so absorbed in their "could care less" jokes like these that they end up treating their games the same way. The game itself is developed very seriously with lots of care, and lots of polish, not just for an early access game but for games in general. RedRuins (the developer) puts a lot of triple-A games to shame with the quality of their early access title.Now onto the actual game review itself:It's amazing. I love Subnautica, and as others are saying this game is like Subnautica. Except, everything's better balanced, better polished, better written, better exploration, etc. The black humor the game is suffused in does break the hard sci-fi of it, but at the same time they willingly explain why your suit can't even hold a minute of oxygen un-upgraded (unlike Subnautica which just avoids the topic), why your flashlight has to recharge (because it's a piece of crap but at least you don't have to swap batteries out of it.) and etc.The exploration is absolutely wonderful, and the suit's AI just makes it even better. The black humor primarily comes in as you explore and see the various ways other passengers on the crashed liner died in their final moments (because their suits only have 30 seconds of oxygen, of course.) but you also have to handle various puzzles to get into some places, which is FAR better than just using a laser cutter to make your way in.Along the way, the afformentioned suit AI makes snarky, cynnical quips regularly. You come up to a person sitting in a chair that's been reduced to just bloody goop and bone, and the suit says: "He must have been shaving with a chainsaw when the crash happened for I can imagine no other circumstance that would leads to this amount of damage." That's just one example, it would take me far too many words to properly convey how spot-on they've made the dialogue lines, and the voice actor is absolutely perfect for him too.Onto the elephant in the room: The black humor. Honestly it's difficult to imagine letting yourself find humor in the portrayal of a massive catastrophe in space, with thousands of dead passengers and your suit AI being your only company. I found the humor as palatable as the humor in BBC's Top Gear show (and Amazon's Grand Tour, I guess.) where a lot of humor is indeed drawn from its offensiveness. In other words, I really loved the humor in the game. Some of it is a bit much for me, but the little things don't detract from the whole here.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I don't have much playtime, but for a game like this I don't need it. I want to have fun in the loneliness, but then I discover a new crafting recipe by finding a hyperinflated condom on an oxygen tank, then am encourage to craft my own hyperinflated condom to breathe out of. also the comedy isn't actually brilliantly executed, except in the sense that it made me want to kill myself. There are just too many comedic ideas at once: absurdism like talking coffin robots, fourth wall breaks like having to craft 'some ♥♥♥♥ the developers made up' or whatever it was called, visual gags like when we pull out a chicken from nowhere to plug an oxygen leak, only for the chickens anus to continue the leak. None of these comedic styles fit together; it's like if The Hitchikers Guide to the Galaxy's audiobook was voiced by Goofy. Great ideas overall, organised as well as my cutlery drawer

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly uninteresting, unfun, and unfunny. I'm putting emphasis on "unfunny" because this game is trying very, VERY hard to be funny literally all the time, and it literally never works. It's a nonstop barrage of painfully drab, tired, and at worst offensive jokes, that culminate in an experience that never lets you rest to take things in. It never stops, it never shuts up, and it never gets any better.If that wasn't bad enough, the gameplay loop itself is just incredibly, mind numbingly boring. You have to clumsily navigate around space in quick intervals, as much as your oxygen will allow, to gather resources. To compare it to subnautica, imagine if to breathe, you had to go back to the life pod every single time. So you gather a few pieces of rock, head back to your ship, and repeat. There are eventually ways to get oxygen balloons out in the environment so you don't have to do that, but it takes much too long to actually get there, and as a whole, it feels like the bulk of the game is material gathering just to get your next thing to gather more materials, with little actual motivation or purpose. This could be excused if the game was nice to look at, enjoyable to be in, anything like that, but this boring gameplay combined with the neverending grating dialogue make it probably the worst game I've played in a long time. Please, do not get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Survival in outer space, w/ wacky elements.  It's obviously been heavily inspired by Subnautica, with some nice tweaks to the formula (eg: either find blueprints, or unlock the research bench and then buy the blueprints for high resource costs).  I even love the "not implemented yet!" blocker at the end, and I usually hate those.The 2nd half of the game is a combination ship-based exploring/shooter and hallway-runner w/ trivial puzzles.  It threw me at 1st, but I ended up enjoying the change of pace - this team likes to mix up the game as it goes, so it's not that unexpected in retrospect.Pros:* Solid survival-space-sim, with some wacky solutions and blueprints.* Decently large map so far, with upgrades that logically unlock more of the map just due to your increased movement capabilities as you gain more tech.Cons:* Progression doesn't appear to be on rails at first, but it very much is.  Can't get to the next section of the 1st chapter unless you happen to find the expanded airtank and its goofy ingredients. Etc.* 2nd half's bases are very on rails.Meh:* Static world.* It's not as wacky and random as the vids show - it's more a survival-space-sim with wacky elements.* After the 1st half, takes awhile before you can go back and use resources from the 1st half.  On the other hand, in the 2nd half they stash the resources you need all over each base.TL;DR - Avoid unless you like the exploring, scavenging/crafting genre.  Else, 1st half is still 8.5/10, 2nd half is a 7.5, due to how on rails it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was some sort of middle recommendation, but it's either thumbs up or down, and while this game has a lot of issues I still think there's enough good stuff here to warrant a recommend. Though with a HUGE caveat.The game starts off well. Great sense of dark humour, interesting places to explore, decent progression. But towards the end of the first chapter you will start noticing how linear it is. This is not a free-roam exploration game. Though it does hold that pretense. For that matter it's also not really a survival game. You have a hunger metre, but you will be drowning in food from just exploring the wreckage around you. To the point that it very quickly becomes a non issue. Same with oxygen and resources.  Everything is in huge abundance.The game also tries to be a building game. You can build space stations, for example. But 90% of the stuff you can build is purely cosmetic. And what's worse is that some things are sorely needed and not present. Item storage, for example, is limited to a single item. A suitcase. Which, when placed on the ground, you can accidenetly walk into an kick across the room. And then to replace it you have to manually empty all items out as you cannot pick up suitcases with items in. The whole game is littered with odd design decisions such as this.And that's chapter 2. Chapter 3 has no base building. You cannot return to the area your base is in. Everything on your base is gone for good.That is a good example of what plagues this game. Base building is included, but in a very stunted almost useless manner. And then it's just not in the game any more. More fool you for spending time making your base look cool. You're done with that now.So the game has a lot of problems. Mechanically it's a mess of badly-implemented ideas from other games. But I played it through right to the end. Why? Purely because of the writing. The game has a rather unique sense of humour. You will find many many corpses floating in space, all having died from a wide variety of silly and stupid causes. Your spacesuits AI will crack wise and mock your stupidity. You use an immortal chicken to discharge deadly electric hazards. The primary antagonists are AI space coffins that have gone rogue and are fuelled by the decomposing corpses contained within them.As I said, it's a tentative recommendation with a caveat. I'd say wait for sale, and play for a bit. See if you like the humour and setting. If you don't, then refund it. Because that's the main draw of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge follows the mold of the survival-craft genre, where you are left in the middle of an hostile environment where you can gather resources (metal, water, plastic, cable, and dozens more) and you'll craft items you'll need to survive (food, water) alongside better equipment you'll need to explore said environment.In good survival games, this keeps you always on the edge, as resources are scarce and the environment presents many dangers which make exploration both necessary and risky, all the while you have to keep in mind many long-term goals (base building, defense, exploration, equipment crafting, etc). Unfortunately, this is never the case on Breathedge, which fails to provide any engaging survival gameplay and ends up being a very tedious and boring experience. In this game's world, resources are plentiful and everywhere, so you are never in any risk, and the game features obnoxious, hand-holding hints you can't disable, so exploration is always as interesting as walking towards the next quest marker in a straight line. In addition, the environment is only dangerous because your oxygen supply amounts to just a number of seconds and you need to explore in short trips: while something like this could work in games like Subnautica, it doesn't work here, as the game level is cramped and designed by hand, which means any great distance is just an obvious equipment gate you are intended to travel later.At the end of the day, the game feels like a walking simulator with inventory management, and a terrible inventory management, too: the vast number of resources and tools needed ensure it's never going to be enough, and there are no inventory upgrades. This could work with a hostile environment where you'd want to minimize your travel time, but since in Breathedge the only danger present in the environment is the time limit, nothing prevents you from doing as many trips back and forth to the resources as you need.Another problem with the game is the humor. It's simply bad. Almost every joke misses its mark and there are thousands of them. In fact, almost every dialogue, scenery or even game item is littered with awful, cringe-worthy attempts at being funny. It just never delivers, and you *will* miss important game information because it will be presented as part of yet another non-funny joke you'll try hard not to listen to.And by the way, the game also suffers the 'MMO mount' syndrome: every time you get an improvement to your movement speed, which means you can finally progress faster with less backtracking, the level design immediately adjusts for that and distances increase accordingly. So, movement upgrades, despite being resource-expensive, never feel like an upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly another game that really needs a 'neutral' review option as overall it has a lot of good, but unfortunately also too much jank. What makes it worse is much of its problems were clearly identified by Early Access (EA) players years ago but never addressed.The first half of the game is good fun survival/crafting game ( with some issues ) the second half becomes more of a walking simulator going through the motions to get to the end of game. The humour is great assuming you enjoy its style. The exploration in the first half is great, constantly finding new things and progressing.Honestly If the first 3 chapters were one game and the last three chapters a separate game individually then both games would have been good ( with some annoyances ) and made more sense. I completed the first 3 chapters in EA and as a survival/crafting game it felt good enough and was enjoyable for 15 odd hrs I player it. The last 3 chapters are interesting from a  story line perspective and a nice ending sequence, but nothing more.For me what really tips this game into almost negative review is the lack of action by the developers are clear issues identified during EA. Its as though the dev's changed half way through development and no-one was interested in the survival/exploration/crafting aspect of the first 3 chapters!Examples include- Poor durability on tools: Though I don't agree with others that its super bad it did need a bit of tweaking.- Base Building: Is pointless other than a storage for your inventory. You can even build some items that have a specific use that you can never use.- Base Building: Suit storage does not remove the suits from your inventory.- Base Building: Deconstructing built objects LOSES resources! There is no good reason for this and it immediately restricts any creativity in designing a base as you have to fully plan it out before you start or even known what modules or compartments you can build in the future! - Base Building: Windows requires stupid amount of resources ( as glass is somewhat limited ) and limited in placement. You are in beautifully rendered SPACE environment but you can only build a few windows and only in a specific module type and not on corners! This makes it difficult to be able to bask in the glory of the games space environment.- Base Building: Storage - the storage compartment has 4 cupboards within it but you only have a single storage unit for all 4! Its not like the game can't support a storage unit per cupboard, it does so on one of the engineering shuttles. This means you have to build a stupid number of storage compartments to get any level of decent resource storage.- Quick Bar: If you use an item but have more in your inventory it does not replace the item, you have to go to inventory and re-assign it.- Base Building: Scanning for blueprints can only be done on specific single instance of an item found in the game. e.g. You want to scan a chair to add to your base, well there are dozens spread throughout the game, there is only one specific one that can be scanned.- Quality Of Life - On top of this there are a whole bunch of QOL features that would have made the game more fun to play, like having an active list of resources needed to build a specific item etc.So anyway, on the whole I do not regret buying the game in EA, the first 3 chapters were fun, and I enjoyed the last few chapters even though they felt drawn out, but overall its a bit of a missed opportunity and highly annoying that the dev's never addressed obvious issues with the game that were highlighted in EA.If you enjoy survival/crafting games then this is still worth a buy, just maybe not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I was sooo excited for this game--it integrates most of my favorite genres and gameplay elements into one package. I bought it when it was on sale some months ago, thinking I was getting a good deal for a game I was sure I would enjoy...and, at first, I did enjoy it. The intro and the first couple of hours were quirky and made me chuckle more than a few times. BUT, there were one or two...not red flags, exactly...but, things that just made me raise an eyebrow and go, "huh, that's kind of odd...oh, well, I am sure it's nothing!"I brushed those off and kept playing well past the 2-hour return limit. I was still sure I would like this game, whatever its imperfections. After around 4 hours,  though, the game started getting more and more and more tedious and repetitive till it was a sloggy, swampy, grind. Difficulty and grinding in survival games has not stopped me from loving them before. In fact, some of my favorite games are known for their near-tortuous survival mechanics. I enjoy the challenge and am driven to push through to explore the game world and experience the rest of the story or lore. But in the case of Breathedge, there was really nothing about the story or world I had an interest in continuing to play for. The game had made it clear I could pretty well guess most every secret and reveal left to discover, because, again, I had already seen it, heard it, or done it in the first few hours.Just as bad, the jokes that were, at first, pretty funny and even endearing (if usually off-color) also started getting more and more repetitive and tiresome. No ground-breaking writing or comedy in this title, unless, you count some of the memes and pop-culture references dug out from the bowels of edgy subreddits circa 2014. The humor went from making me chuckle, to inspiring a few grins, to making me roll my eyes, to eliciting an audible, "ugh" after a while. Eventually, I felt like I was playing with a little kid who thinks one particular fart joke is the most HILARIOUS thing on this earth...or in space or whatever. Sure, it might be funny if that is your type of humor, but even then, it gets old after you hear it over and over again for hours, especially when the delivery is far from masterful. I had noticed some of the stale or slightly confusing jokes and the edgy, try-hard bits earlier in the game, but I wrote those off as possible localization issues or as a side effect to the developers' attempts to wedge a joke into literally every sentence, clause, and visual detail. Statistically, some of those jokes are going to be a miss, and there had been plenty that were entertaining, so, again, I shrugged that off. But, as the game went on, it became clear that that was just it. The "funny" bits were just the the individual pieces of humor-buckshot from the shotgun blasts that are this game's joke writing. Throw every poop joke you (or the internet) can think of at the fan, and something is bound to stick--or at least get flung around the room and stick to everything else.Unfortunately, even the humor I had enjoyed was repeated into oblivion, so the weird, out-dated, and adolescent edge-lord jokes became more obvious (or maybe they just became more frequent in the game). The continuous degradation of the joke quality combined with the repetitive grind and repetitive story made this game the first I have ever tried to return. But, of course, my determination to like the game and give it another chance again and again prevented me from returning it. I guess I can hold out hope that the developers will continue working on it, maybe consult with some more skilled writers, and maybe it will grow into something I could at least recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like humor that is on-the-nose, repetitive to the point of eye rolling, and game mechanics that get replaced every few hours with different mechanics, then you may enjoy this game.  It’s got some aspects that recommend it, but to many other draw backs to really make up for the fun you might have.-= Pros =-- The intro and first couple of chapters are fun, challenging, and the decisions have actual consequences.- There are a lot of easter eggs in the form of collectable items, lines of dialogue, images, and cinematic pieces.- Space is big.  And this game gets big space down.- The music is good.- - Crafting some big space station all decorated and pretty is fun.-= Cons =-- The humor becomes stale.  There are a lot of subverted expectation gags.  To the point you are never surprised by the twist, you just wait.  They even point out that this happens in the game dialogue itself.  Of course instead of doing anything about it, they double down on it. Then triple down.- That music I said was good.  It also gets repetitive.  Then they take it away and you can’t get it back.-The game changes from a space survival game, to a space adventure game in the middle.  All the bits that made the space survival game fun stay though.  They make a space adventure game boring.  You’re on long trips through big space, sometimes minutes at a time.  You’re never sure what resources you may need.  But it turns out its not a lot and you can find them everywhere.  Still have to craft those tools and stuff at your base.  Makes for a lot of pointless walking.- The materials you need are everywhere, but space is big. It makes if hard to find what you need to progress.- Speaking of progression.  There are many times in the game where you need a specific tool they just came up with, or object to progress, or you have that one tool but you didn’t have it in your inventory.  This means getting to the way point, and being told to go back to your crafting station to craft the one thing you need.  This is actually a plot point they use, multiple times.- The inventory is small for the amount of items you need to collect and carry to be successful without frequent trips.- You will never have enough containers.  This game trains you to pick up a lot of stuff for the future.  Even without grabbing all the little flavor items you’ll run out of space.- Get ready to remember every crafting recipe.  You can’t check the recipes outside of the crafting station, and you can’t access anything other than your personal inventory from the crafting station.  So if you need to craft a part to craft an item to progress the game, you’d better have a good enough memory to remember the 12+ things you’ll need to craft, or everything you need in your inventory already.- You craft a space station for yourself.  In the beginning of the game.  Then they take it away from you.  Nothing you can do about it.  Can’t even make a new one.- The places they could put tension, high stakes and consequences, they didn’t. Sometimes they actively took out the stakes and made it an on the rails situation.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: It is technically practically flawless: you will probably not get stuck, you will likely not find any bugs, and you also shouldn't need more than 40 hours to finish it. You will have fun most of that time. Except for the times when you're busy rolling your eyes and cringing. If your English is good enough, play the main game in English, even if your main language happens to be closer to Russian. BUT: If your Russian is good enough, play the Leia DLC in Russian, it is really worth it.Details: I played this game twice: once in English, and once in Russian because I needed to figure some things out (see below).Good things first:As a space survival game, it is very good. The story is fun, and the setting is a mixture of beautiful and horrifying in equal measure. The atmosphere is a nice change from the sameness of the western aesthetic (it is mildly pseudo-Soviet-futurist, more to that later).The DLC, which is unrelated to the main story and characters, goes even more into the survival and horror aspect, and is highly recommended (but stressfull). It lacks the humoristic aspect of the main game (which you might consider fortunate, see below). The Russian voice-over of the DLC is fantastic: the experiment overseer is exactly the type of clinically detached secretary / government official that you'll meet at the Russian embassy if you have the dubious pleasure to, say, require a visa. Unfortunately, this gets lost in the English dub, so if your Russian is good enough, play the DLC (and only the DLC) in Russian.From technical perspective, this is a *really* well-made space survival game. It has practically no bugs, which is astounding for a modern game, and there is no way to get stuck that I could find. It is well-balanced, hard enough to be challenging but not so hard as to be frustrating.  It has a really nice base-building component (that is entirely optional and I managed to miss it completely on my first playthrough, but it makes your life a lot easier if you do it at the right time.) Many things can be solved in more than one way (there is only one area where you actually *need* a blaster, and I am not sure what happens there if you don't have one.)The "meh":The aesthetic and some of the setting look as an attempt at critical Soviet futurism. Unfortunately, it comes off as an odd westernized parody on Russian/Soviet aesthetic rather than the real thing. It is hard to tell if it is on purpose, as the game is intended "to be of humorous nature" (more on that later).If you play the main game in English, you get the idea that this is somebody from the west who is trying to imitate the Soviet look and feel. There is even a song running on the "radio" that is a Russian song sung by somebody who is clearly not Russian and who clearly doesn't understand what he is singing, but is simply trying to reproduce the sounds and sometimes failing. This weirdness is highlighted by the Extremely Enthusiastic American Insurance Salesman tone of your space suit and its messages.However, you'll come to miss the Insurance Salesman version if you ever switch to Russian.Because if you play it in Russian, it gets even more confusing. On one hand, it comes off a lot more genuine in many ways --  but a few of the jokes seem to be reverse-translated from English, political humor that was ubiquitous in the SU is almost entirely absent, low-brow humor (that was largely absent in the SU) is ubiquitous, and the Russian voice-overs are of a moderately low quality. My suspicion towards the end was that the devs couldn't find voice actors and did the voice-over themselves, whereas they managed to find actual voice-actors for the English version and for the DLC -- but who knows.Towards the end of my English playthrough I was wondering if the devs were kids of Russian immigrants. By the end of my Russian playthrough I was sure that they weren't (see below), but was wondering if the dev team just didn't have anyone in close proximity who is old enough to have witnessed the real thing, and are recreating the Pseudosoviet aesthetic basically as culture archaeologists - from fragments in the surroundings and from hearsay.To sum it up: the most actually Soviet/Russian thing in this game are the murals (very nicely executed!), and the copious amounts of the blue insulation tape on literally everything you build. This is what most of things in the Soviet Union were held together by. (That, and copper wire.)One other thing is that the suit talks way too much. (I am not sure if playing this in the hardcore mode would fix this, as it says "no hints", but having spent way too much time on the game already I prefer not to try.)Yes, it is a necessary setup for some jokes (you need to get used to it explaining things in order to notice that sometimes the explanations are painfully wrong), but occasionally you'd like to have some time to "decode" the scene yourself before it starts talking. And in some cases (some particularly confusing ones), it stays silent. Part of the joke?The bad and the ugly:Some of the humor (thankfully absent in the DLC as it wouldn't fit the tone) is deeply, unsettlingly cringe. The English version defuses a particularly nasty movie title, and makes the Diagnosis Station somewhat more palatable. Maybe that type of jokes flies in modern-day Russia (in which case: I am very sorry) but in the West it definitely doesn't, as witnessed by many, many, MANY western reviewers commenting on this on various websites.And that's all. Basically, the game *could* be perfect... if it wanted to.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoy my reviews? .Enjoy my reviews? .Or Breathedge is a humorous Unreal based survival game in space.The year is 2073. You arrive to attend the space funeral of your grandfather on the Interstellar Liner Unnamed. Suddenly the ship explodes.You should have a good idea of how serious this game is from the opening movie of a bunch of chickens in a movie theater. The game doesn't get any more serious than that. So, if you're looking for a serious space survival game this is not the game for you. I played in Story Mode. Story Mode is a directed survival experience.After the ship explodes you are in an airlock that is leaking oxygen. You must plug the leak. One of the things that your grandfather left you was an immortal chicken. The chicken conveniently fits into the leaking air tube. Unfortunately that's not a long term solution, so you will need to get the gum that was stuck to your helmet and plug the leak with it. You are inside a smart spacesuit that will guide you along your journey. Your spacesuit will assist you in keeping yourself alive. Like most survival games you start off will no resources and must craft items to improve your chances of survival. Oxygen is your main need followed by water and then food.You will find blueprints and scan items so that you can create them. Your tools have a limited usage, so you will have to plan for when they break. Fortunately it isn't a surprise when they break, if you're paying attention. Unfortunately the seem to break when you'd really like to use them. I took to crafting a new one before heading out if it was near the end of its useful life.There are various environmental issues you have to deal with, hot, cold, electrical, and radiation. There are spacesuits that you can craft to assist you. Since you need oxygen you will find a blueprint to create an oxygen station to allow you to create way points so that you can travel farther from your ship.Inventory is also an issue. You can only carry so many items at a time. Some items take up more room in your inventory than others. You can bring items back to your ship and dump them on the floor. Later on you can build a container to put thing in so that they are better organized.There are different phases to the game. Initially you start off having to explore by yourself. You have a very limited movement rate. You can build a series of boosters that will allow you to travel faster for a brief period of time. Later on you will be able to build two different vehicles, a vacuum rocket and a car. The vacuum rocket is exactly what you will expect when you find it, a vacuum cleaner you rider around on. The car has the advantage of supplying you with oxygen so you can use it as a mobile base.When you get to the fourth phase of the game you will be aboard a ship that you cannot exit. It gets a bit frustrating as you as stuck on the ship, after you've been tooling around wherever you want to go. As a tradeoff, the ship has guns.I had a few times where I got stuck in the environment and couldn't move. Reloading solved the issue. The game has an auto save when you enter your ship and at a few other various times. You can also manually save.A beautiful space survival game, with a sense of humor.Intel i7-8086K Coffee Lake 6-Core 4.00GHz CPUCrucial Ballistix Sport AT 2666 MHz DDR4 RAM (16GB x 2)ASUS GeForce RTX 2080 Overclocked 8G GDDR6Enjoy my reviews? .Or

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the title of this game sounds like a fetish category.Ah yes, No Man’s Subnautica.My wife’s boyfriend just calls it Spacenautica.This game is… breathtaking.A game from a Russian indie studio about putting together a bunch of resources to survive a harsh unforgiving environment. Yup. It all seems to fit doesnt it.Breathedge is, simply put, Subnautica in space with a comedic bent.  You play an astronaut who survives a space crash and you have to navigate the huge floating debris field in zero G, always keeping an eye on your oxygen, radiation, and temperature. As you unlock crafting recipes you are able to extend your excursions.  Just like Subnautica if you aren’t careful you will die and have to restart from your last save. Unlike Subnautica, however, instead of fear and dread, you are constantly amused by the environmental story telling and dialogue from your AI.  Oh and for some reason you have a chicken that doubles as a specialized tool. The game is a masterpiece, the comedy is excellent, the gameplay is fun, the story is great. The way you slowly just start from going in and out of your spaceship to how once you understand how clever and exactly calculated the routes are you start feeling more free and literally just going wherever you want. The exploration really gives you the feel of how empty and big space is... loved the vibe. Made me want to go through space more and more sometimes even forgetting what my main task was, that's how fun it was. Story was funny and the game doesn't take itself serious at all.It’s Subnautica in space, however, for most of the game, instead of base building, you're tool building (and survival, depending on what mode you play in). There is a base building component to it that is essential for progressing the story, but it's limited. You CAN build a massive base if you want, but it won't progress the story. At some point after you build the base, you will leave the area where you start the game and you can come back only after finishing the game. Afterwards you can go wherever you want and do whatever you will until there are no more resources.The crafting is great; lots of different recipes and materials and blueprints to find. The base-building is somewhat simple, but there are quite a few add-ons and decorations to fill your time with. And the progression is excellent- slowly getting access to more air equipment and speed equipment, right before the map just explodes in size.The story is in chapters and progressively changes from lone space survival by gathering and crafting things to space npc boss fighting, like a FPS from 2005. Basically goes from survival to adventure. You can't really build anything but tools and whatever plot devices are given to advance the game. It’s essentially two different games smashed into one. I can understand people not liking the very linear ending though. I personally loved playing this, and I liked how the game feels like different genres built into one game. Although there's a lot of content in the ending, you blaze through it fairly quickly. The first half is the "real" game, it's much longer, and it's great. So the ending is a bit weak, yeah. First 3 chapters are strong, but falls off after that. The humour carries it to the end though. There's a rule in entertainment that people's impression will be entirely based on how you end something, and they failed in that. But I wouldn't feel bad recommending it just for the first half. There's room for improvement even there (particular with base building utility) but I found it more than satisfying enough.People trash on the humor, but it's basically on a Borderlands level IMO, and I was more than fine with it. The Al in your suit also in my oppinion has some good jokes and I loved its voice. Lots of funny/dirty/weird "humor" at every corner. In fact, my biggest issue was not being able to pay attention to it much, as I had other things taking my attention away (oxygen timers, etc).It is for sure not the greatest game of all time. I believe you have to be open for the humor. Still, I believe the world building more than makes this game worth it. I would encourage Subnautica fans to give it a try. This game is fun, humorous, and has pointless collectibles with surprising "upgrades". I don't know what this game did to me but I just never ever got bored while playing it. 8/10 sputniks for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to like this game.  Saw a youtuber I like play it, and picked it up.  Then the problems started.The first glaring issue was the sound, if you have surround sound don't waste your time, let me stop you right here.  The sound levels will be all over the place, and you will be reliant on subtitles which often get interrupted.  Sometimes music is shaking your walls, sometimes you can't even tell there is music.The popups go away far too fast to read them, so if you want to enjoy the funny writing you will have to look to see if anyone posted it all online somewhere half the time.And, upon reading various reviews and experiences, it seems the game is poorly advertised.  Subnautica in space only applies to the beginning of the game.  After that, it's a walking simulator.  I haven't gotten far enough to see for myself because I will be refunding, but the consensus appears to be the game changes partway through.  So, if you wanted subnautica in space, don't bother with this game.Finally, the game itself.  It is painfully okay.  That is about all I can say positivewise.  It is funny, but to sum up the range of the humor; there is a pee button.  It screams of throwing everything at the wall and seeing what sticks.  They basically tried to be deadpool.  Quality of life issues are one of the biggest issues I have, the little things that make a game fun and immersive are just missing.  I don't really feel like going through a list, so here are the bigger ones.  The crafting menu is a pain to use, there is no flow to the progression, and even using the airlock is annoying because you just half phase through it.  I had to manually stop myself so I didn't feel like a ghost.This game needs a complete redo, I'm afraid.  I can tell the devs tried, but they tried way to hard to be funny and ignored making the actual game good.  I laughed, then I got bored.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I will return when my frustration subsides. Yes, this is like subnautica in a lot of ways, but much, much, much more tedious.  I haven't gotten far, admittedly, but I don't feel like I want to. Here are some reasons:1. Oxygen is much more punishing than in Subnautica. You can get a better tank, but it doesn't help much. You can craft consumable oxygen pots, but they don't last long. You can create oxygen stations that have a finite amount of oxygen that will refill you, and then you can refill those with disposable oxygen generators. Sounds ok at first, but...2. Item durability is horrendous. You can't repair for cheap, so each item breaks down completely, needing a new one. So you need to get more materials to make the most basic of tools, to then make oxygen less of a problem. Problem is, oxygen again depletes quickly. So you will find yourself running in circles more than moving forward, replacing things to get you to further areas to collect things to replace things, etc. Which brings me to the next issue...3. Many resources look the same. Ice and glass? Look the same, and you will have to be drunk to find glass, so your vision is blurry. Yea, alcohol heats you up and glass is in an icy area. While trying to get it you are also fighting oxygen as it is quite a ways away (see above again regarding the oxygen issue). 4. Knowing what to get, and where to get it is not really even hinted at for the most part. Which means you will have to explore every nook and cranny, which again causes you to fight the oxygen mechanic. The game, and maybe it is just the first couple hours, is so tedious that it made me not want to continue. And I've played some tedious games. There is humor in the game, but it really isn't enough to make you want to continue.

_childDocuments_.review: Difficulty: NormalPlaytime:17.7 hrsChapter:3Breathedge is a survival, story driven game that is beautiful on the outside and mediocre on the inside.In the beginning you start off with nothing but this funny but kinda annoying narrator that's the AI in your suit.You begin gathering random materials and start to get the flow of crafting low tier tools. You figure out with guided direction from your narrator that you need to keep going. That's the part of what Breathedge is lacking, you just keep trying to move forward and get closer and closer to your objective. I don't think the developers really thought about what would make this game so great and differentiate from other survival games. On the surface you have a well polished, atmospheric game that can't decide what it wants to be.My first 10 hours of the game was a exhausting exploration of making sure I had this to make this. It's a constant go back and fourth from one place to next just to get some little aluminum or resin you forgot. The tools in Breathedge are made just as fast as they break. For example the Drill,Scanner,Grabber are tools that use material that you have to take a good 10 minutes to find just to drive back 1000+ meters just to craft and break the durability is so low on them. I remember when i was so excited to finally craft a Laser Gun just to find out they have one use and the ammo in them is 60. 60 is not a lot of ammo for the amount of work I put in to craft the item why cant we just make ammo for the weapon instead of it breaking?Besides all the negativity I spoke about I do recommend Breathedge as a game for people to play because for $18.74 you get a lot of game play and grinding to do. The atmosphere is beautiful and the way you explore is amazing. If you enjoy survival games this is a east steal for you. If you don't enjoy grinding for hours to do the minimal then I wouldn't recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the problem with this game: I really didn't know up to the final moment which thumbs I'll click.In the chapters that were included with the early access, this is basically subnautica in space, with some zany humor. While vehicles enter the stage kinda late, and basebuilding very late, it is overall a somewhat tense, enjoyable experience. If that was the entire story I'd pop up a thumbs up and be done with it.The issue is what comes next. When you're done with the early access chapters your base - which you seemingly only just started - and you vehicle - which is challanging to get the blueprint for - immediately become obsolete. The game shifts direction on a dime and turns into this weird walking simulator in samey corridors with some crafting elements on top of it. Survival elements? Food and water litters the place. Crafting? Becomes a chore, as you need to explore a ship/station, figure out what you're missing or find a blueprint, walk aaaaall the way back, craft the thing, then walk aaaall the way again to use it. At this point all the jokes that were probably intended as self-sarcastig fall extremely flat - you're not gonna get any laughs at "I guess this game doesn't have any mechanics" when the game barely has any anymore, or non-existent fast travel joke when I really could be spared walking the same piece of boring corridor for the 5th time.I admit, the finale does kinda make up for it, a little bit, and most of the story is engaging enough to kinda power through the bad sections, so if that was to be taken at face value I'd reluctantly recommend the game. My issue is that the shift is literally at the edge of Early Access, which stinks. It stinks of doing a great job until it mattered, and then just kinda winging it, because it already sold well. It stinks of executive meddling, rushed release, loss of creative power. It's ugly.And that's why, on principle, I ended up clicking thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really mixed about this game, but in the end I can't really recommend it, simply because it's not a good open world survival crafting game.After 15-20 hours of playtime the game simply becomes a linear narrative walking simulator.SPOILER AHEAD but it's a big warning to anyone thinking about buying this.After hours of tedious grind and base building, the game forces you to repair a spaceship and warp-jump to another area. From then on, you can't leave the ship unless you dock at a station, you can't build another base or vehicle, all you can do is dock at a station, follow the marker, get back to the ship to craft the crap required to continue, and fly to another station. repeat that several times, with 2 terrible bosses and combat mechanics ( in a game with no combat 99,5% of the time ). They always give you all the resources needed, and the stations are littered with food and water. By the end of the game I had gathered 6 full suitcases of materials, thinking I'd go back to a more open area at some point, but no.The beginning of the game is extremely tedious due to low oxygen reserves ( which then doesn't matter at all and all your upgrades are for nothing, because there is oxygen on the stations ), low tool durability, small storage space, lots of back and forth, only 4 slots for tools ( and there are A LOT of tools required ), etc. I don't know if it's a real game or if the devs just wanted to troll the people who like this kind of game by making it as unfun as possible.It took me 5 hours before getting my first vehicle, 6 hours before starting my first base, and when I finally started to get all the upgrades to make the game less tedious, I had to leave everything behind to continue the story.It's basically a waste of time, and I regret buying this at launch without checking any review ( the one from SkillUp is pretty on point ). I didn't buy it in early access, I waited, and still got burned because the devs just "finished" the game by completely changing its genre halfway through.Subnautica in space this is not.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend this game and I do find moments in this game actually funny but the minute to minute gameplay just isn't fun. Further, there are some who won't like the type of comedy used in the game. I found myself chuckling at some, but not all of the jokes. Maybe the game will get better when it's completely done but in its current state with its current feel, I can't recommend. For context, I have completed the first chapter after a single restart because I had made a mistake. I'll start with the mechanic that dominates all other mechanics: breathing and oxygen. The game starts you with an abysmally low oxygen amount. You barely have enough to go somewhere immediately near your starting base, do maybe a couple seconds of something and then go back. I am going to spoil where the first oxygen expansion is to make a point. You see, I was getting annoyed with how little oxygen I had, so I was trying to figure out where to expand it. An hour in and I notice the waypoint system which specifically mentioned oxygen. I then change the waypoint color and try looking around to find it. I could not find it. I then look up where to find it and learn that the makers of this game don't understand one of the basic principles talked about constantly in dev commentary for games with verticality. In games: we do not inherently look up or down, it's not our instinct because in RL our peripheral vision is usually enough for us to catch important things. So, the first expansion for your oxygen and the oxygen stations that are required to get anywhere are directly beneath you. I had spent over an hour being frustrated with the lack of oxygen because they put in a spot people don't look.The worst part about the oxygen expansion is that it isn't even that expansive. It does not extend your range by much. What's worse are the amount of problems I had with their oxygen stations. It takes a long time to fill your oxygen tank using one and using one can be fiddly if you are moving at all. Fun fact, you drift a bit when you stop using the thrusters. There's no increasing beyond certain speeds but you still have some inertia when it comes to stopping which feels off (I learned much later when I was trying to look up a key command that apparently left Alt stabilizes you and stops this drift. Thanks, lack of good tutorial to tell me this).Another annoyance is food and water. I don't know why the game bothers with a hunger and thirst system. Right outside your starting pod is plenty of food and water to last you a long in-game time, which makes the whole thing annoying busywork that just wastes your time and, minorly, some space in your inventory. It feels like it was included just because it's a staple of the genre. Someone might argue it might be satirical in some way but satire requires some twist on the concept, it literally just plays hunger and thirst straight and immediately makes them a pointless but annoying chore you have to deal with.Another annoying aspect to the game is that you stop if you open your inventory. The game, however, does NOT stop. Which means your losing precious oxygen to look at something in your inventory and not moving to your destination, which means you won't be doing that often once you realize that fact. And that can undercut a lot of the humor. The AI is talking about a man murdered and coming up with a ridiculous explanation rather than the obvious one, well that would be nice but I'm rushing back to the ship because I'm running out of oxygen and getting the warning.That's my final problem. The gameplay gets in the way of the comedy. The ability to enjoy the jokes is dependent on the ability to relax. The game really comes across as a more relaxed experience than something like Subnautica (which I'd describe as more of a horror survival experience at times) but Subnautica is fine tuned in a lot of its gameplay to be enjoyable, even when moving about with its ecosystems while making sure to give you plenty of oxygen and easy ways to generate oxygen. Breathedge, however, has a harder oxygen mechanic with none of the fine touches, polish, or visuals Subnautica has due to setting and design choices. Maybe Breathedge will improve but I'm not hopeful. This game feels much more like a game you watch someone else play rather than a game you play.

Often times you miss a critical loot, and you get stuck in your progression because "you didn't guess that breaking this particular box would give you that particuliar material that is found no where else in the game, which is required for reaching the next stage".. ... I spend a bit more than 4hrs in this game, and probably only "played 15 minutes in those", the rest of the 3h45minutes spent moving around painfully slowly in empty space between places, with nothing to do beside looking at my oxygen reserve depleting.. I thought this would be like a space-themed subnautica (which I loved), with a twist of dark-humour. What I found instead was a "float around in empty space simulator" with a twist of dark-humour..I would have loved to love this game.. but my experience was just empty, boring and frustrating..

_childDocuments_.review: Humour is very subjective. While this game tries to be funny, is very much isn't for me. That's like half the reason to play it, because there isn't much great game play to support it.Gathering resources and building new stuff is a standard game play loop. Here it just feels like you have to rush everywhere, because you run out of oxygen. Every time you find something the narrator comments on, you'll need to concentrate on not dying - you have absolutely no time to read or take your surroundings in. The aims of the game just are in conflict with each other.The visuals are mostly fine, you can clearly make out points of interest from afar, you just don't know if going there will burn resources or yield something. There is floating useless stuff around you can't look at, because you will suffocate.First I stopped after I bashed my own head in, because I didn't notice the health drain. Now I'm in some engineering shuttle somewhere and haven't played for a month - and when I think about it, there is no reason to start it up again.It's just not fun and not funny.
