_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game with the thought that it would be like Subnautica in space and came away pretty disappointed. The environments were well lit and designed but so much of the gameplay just boils down to collecting a huge amount of the same scraps you've been collecting in the game since the first minute, with much of your resources going into just replacing your resource collecting tools over and over again (as most of them break after only 15 uses). The narration is helpful for telling you when you've entered an area of debris for the first time, (since much of the map blends together and the majority of the game is picking through zones you've already visited dozens of times) but as some of the other comments have observed the narration is poorly translated from Russian and read in such a quick and repetitive manner that there's no comedy left in it. I find myself wishing sometimes they didn't even try for comedy and would just describe things straightforward, since the environments are compelling enough to sell the game, but the devs seem pretty bent on cramming every possible fart joke they could with every description and god is it insufferable. There's even a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Chuck Norris joke, if you weren't already dragged back to middle school by the toilet humour.If you've ever been annoyed by item durability in games, this is not for you, as breaking and repairing the exact same tools every 10 minutes is most of the gameplay. Any of the punishing traversal disappears within a few hours as you upgrade your oxygen and get your speed up and after that point it's just a padded slog,Why did I spend over a day of my finite life playing this? I suppose I thought it would get better. When things seemed to be ramping up for a change of pace I reached the end of the content. The visuals were good throughout, and there are some solid landmarks to aid in navigation, but looking back on the time I spent on this game it just felt like a repetitive grind with very little novelty scattered among the chores. If there's mod support in the future that allows for you to tweak and increase item durability I would recommend it, you do not deserve to have your time wasted in this manner if you do choose to purchase this game anyways.All in all I hope this game improves. There's some very good art direction throughout that I would hate to see go to waste by being turned into just another engineered slog to inflate play time.

_childDocuments_.review: Boy, is it ever so much fun to waste a ton of playtime reloading and on traveling forth and back for just a handful of seconds of actual gameplay (literally: 20 seconds forth, 10 seconds interaction, 20 seconds back!!) just because breath is so idiotically limited for thirteen billion times until finally all components have been scavenged for some McGuffin that reduces the number of returns for the next task. (To eleven billion. Woohoo.) A true landmark of game design. Tedium. Obnoxious, endless, mind-numbingly boring, repetitive tedium. What every game needs. I'm at 15+ hours and 175 seconds of breath (Woohoo.) and the tedium generated purely from unnecessarily repetitive and drawn-out travel at brain-liquefyingly low speeds (because why would inertia and unlimited speed be a thing) is still a major disappointment from an otherwise moderately amusing game. Nevermind, found the e-shuttle. And learnt that the research desk for craftable stations contains a processor, too.The complaint stands. It may have a funny gameworld and quirky writing. But it's tedious and the jokes are ultimately flat and predictable.And again this insufferable console peasantry fluffing. Hold-to-interact and only four (4!) hotkeys? Intransparent saving with absolutely no indicator when is saved and what is saved in either Autosave or manual save, many gameworld elements simply respawning, only very few elements actually having persistence.The base building element is nothing but a tacked-on time sink with no real consequence. It would have been nice if the base was mobile so you could take all your resources with you. After all, the gameworld is rather linear anyway, and making you shuttle your so-far collected items between old and new bases as you progress is certainly not bound to quell the tedium.It may be polished to a shine. But a polished turd still remains a turd.

_childDocuments_.review: This is only "Subnautica in space" if Subnautica made you re-craft the scanner tool every 5 minutes (literally). I supported this in early access, and I'm a little bummed this is what we get. Please fix the balancing. Between the low oxygen (even after upgrades) and the low durability of every tool, I can barely get anything done and I've been playing for over 6 hours. I'm honestly about to quit, I have made at least 30 handy scrapper tools or whatever the hell they're called, and it's NOT FUN. It only has 35 "uses" before it breaks, and a simple piece of metal takes 6 hits. Other breakables take even more away. I want to progress and explore! Why the hell did you make a game, include a suggested difficulty, and then not allow the mechanics to let the player actually experience anything in the game?????Honestly I'm really liking the world and story and tone so far, apart from how I can't even get anything actually done in the damn thing cuz I'm too busy redoing crap I've already done. Let me be clear: It is so bad and so successful at ruining the experience here that I will 100% be using a cheat trainer so I can actually enjoy it, as soon as the darn thing updates from the 1.0 release. Definitely nuking tool durability entirely, and maybe then the laughable oxygen won't be such an insultingly tedious chore. Please fix the oxygen and tool usage. It's awful.EDIT: I gotta complain about my biggest irritation--the "metal" most often comes in pieces you have to break with the scrapper, like I mentioned. Occasionally, there's single pieces you can pick up, but you get those first usually and there aren't many to begin with. Also, consider that each scrapper tool costs 3 metal pieces itself to craft. So, now imagine, you're out and about scrapping containers when your scrapper breaks. ♥♥♥♥! You don't have a spare! And you only have 1 piece of metal!!! ............Yup. You're basically screwed. You get to spend the next full hour of your gameplay re-scavenging areas you already went to, PRAYING that you missed a single floating piece of metal that you can use to make a scrapper---because you need the scrapper itself to mine meta and loot containers.Honestly, who allowed this???

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to leave such a raving review for this game..It was fantastic, gorgeous, atmospheric, and both relaxing and extremely stressful at the same time. In the first part of the game. Honestly just stop playing after chapter 3 and a bit of screwing around in chapter 4. The first part of the game is just so much fun. It rewards exploration so well and is filled with jokes, discovery and satisfaction. It promises base building and quality of life upgrades. You will enjoy it.Just make sure to enjoy it while it lasts. Because once you have the final upgrades... YOU DON'T NEED THEM. WHAT?!The game completely changes into another game and shockingly becomes just a bunch of walk here through a stupid linear corridor for 5 minutes, then go back to your ship to craft something that you should have been able to craft on the spot.At some point towards the end you are not given an actual marker for what to do next and I have no idea how players are supposed to understand how to get the Microplasm on their own unless they accidentally run into it. I quit at this point.Of course there is the issue of tools being super flimsy but meh, that's not a deal-breaker.I've never had a game turn from one of the best I played to one of the worst. _childDocuments_.review: "Subnautica but in space" is a quick one-liner that sums up this game, but fails to account for a multitude of little details. It plays like someone who loved Subnautica and took heavy inspiration from it in making a new game, but it has so many little nits to pick that add up to Not As Good.For one thing, it's trying to be funny. Not like witty writing funny, but like Portal/Borderlands crossover fanfic funny. Your character had a beard as a baby and is named "Man." Ha. There is a dedicated "relieve yourself" button so you can piss wherever you want. Cute. Your suit AI constantly spews grimdark jokes in a cheerful tone, but they just never stick. The warning that you're running out of air is "Reminder: Oxygen is not unlimited" emblazoned across the top of the screen. Har dee har. There were a few good natured chuckles at first, but it got old fast. It has its moments, like when you spit at your robot interrogator at the beginning of the game only for it to splat against the inside of your helmet--the button prompt for which was something like "click rmb to show this pig what you think through an act of defiance" or w/e--but still...Oh yeah there's a robot interrogator. Because the game is framed as your character, Man, retelling the story of his survival to robocops. Not sure why, the formula works perfectly fine without the framing device. Subnautica just cold-opened with you jumping into an escape pod and watching your starship explode. More intense, straight into the action.Speaking of comparisons to Subnautica, there is also a little fabricator in your home base, and like Subnautica's fabricator, it takes a variety of materials and some time to create new equipment. However, it takes a good 2 or 3 seconds for most basic items. And you have to sit in a menu and stare at the progress bar. You can't click over and queue up another item, you can't back out of the menu. There's no reason for the construction to not be instant. In Subnautica, it took a similar short amount of time to build basic items, but even with the big ones you could still turn away to fiddle with some other equipment. I sound like a maniac, but this is just the most obvious example of numerous tiny design differences which Subnautica--i remind you, the game everyone is comparing Breathedge to--already did better. Another more concrete example is your air supply. Since you're, y'know, in space, you can't just swim to the surface while exploring, like you can in Sub. Thus, your early expeditions are incredibly short, as you have to turn back and reenter the airlock every 40 seconds or so. It felt like every time I found something interesting or started getting into a resource-collecting groove, my leash got yanked by the insipid oxygen warning.I know my playtime is short, but if I'm so unimpressed with the First Impression, the most important part of the game, then I'm not going to bother slogging through it in the hopes it gets better later. Maybe it does, but I frankly don't care anymore. I'll just hold out til Subnautica 2 releases.

_childDocuments_.review: What drew me to this game at first was the potential to be Subnautica in space. I enjoyed the first few hours; a mysterious incident, the survival elements, the dark and morbid 4th wall breaking humour and parodies, the quietness and loneliness of space. Unfortunately, that's all it had going for it and it fails to capitalise on its best ideas and gameplay going into the second half. Worse still, doubles down on the awful parts of the game while flipping its genre.In the first half of the game, the air supply mechanic becomes tedious after a while which forces you to return back to your starting point way too frequently. It becomes a  better later on, and then it becomes almost pointless. The crafting mechanics need tons of rework and rebalancing. There are way too many materials which are nearly not needed for crafting but are found in abundance. On the other hand, the few materials that are crucial for almost  crafting blueprints are not easily available. It has a decent base building mechanics but mostly useless in the service of story progression. And the second half of the game is where the ball drops. Hard. The disconnect between the first and second half is obvious. It becomes a linear walking (floating?) simulator with illogical level and corridor designs that feels rushed or lazy. The air supply mechanic? Meaningless. Base building? Zilch. The crafting? Inconsequential and infuriating. If the crafting mechanics doesn't frustrate you in the first half, it will most certainly will in this second half with the "go somewhere, get blocked, go back to craft, return to progress" process on repeat. Also, the barrage of self-deprecating gags and off-colour jokes becomes off-putting; an example of too much of a good thing becomes a bad thing.The second half feels like it was designed to pad the game as much as possible with boring back and forth craft quests without considering any interesting gameplay mechanics that was introduced in the first half. At this point, I had to really drag myself to finish it. The only tiny saving grace at the final stretch is it gave me a chuckle at the ending. But unfortunately nothing at this point can reverse all the bad impressions it left.It's a shame that it had so many good ideas, but many of them fail to take off.(Edited for clarity)

The scenario and writing should be it's forte, but are not really in the end.~25h to completeHopefully you won't feel too much the fedex aspect which is inherent to the gameplay.I recommend to not hesitate to use a guide, since it happened several times that I had no clue about what to interact with to progress, and it may also help to not forget important items here and there.Pros :- pretty decent looking, has nice spatial landscapes- the writing is quite funny, at first- like a metroidvania gated by crafting. The better your crafts, the farther you can progress. There's a sense of empowerment whenever you upgrade your gear or find/craft a vehicule, it eases the exploration by a lot.- sort of feels like a detective game since everything in the outer space is frozen, afloat, and won't move anymore. You'll have to dig through the debris to understand what happened.- exploration often leads to fun impromptu situations- gameplay feature : . Also, it's completely optional. On the other hand, since the game doesn't make it obvious, I'm warning you : Cons :- is less stressful than I expected ? once you're past the first ~2 hours of gameplay you can explore further without having to count the seconds passing by anymore. Take a handful of oxygen recharges from your stock before going out on exploration and you're set.- the inventory is severly limited, and there's no way to upgrade it. No item is stackable, and you'll want to stack a bunch of resources since crafting cost several each time. Also, some items are pretty hard to find and you will hate not having gathered enough and needing more. Outposts have their own storage, which can be upgraded by leaving suitcases on the ground. It's not super convenient to have to go through each of them when looking for something, and neither to have to move out everything you have whenever you're moving to a new outpost (which can happen up 5-6 times, depending if you find all of them). I just wish for a mod allowing infinite inventory size ...- you can only craft at fixed dedicated stations, meaning lots of back-and-forth because you need that one item to progress ...- breakable tools will hinder your progression a lot, even if it's not that noticeable- in the midgame, oxygen is manageable pretty easily but still something you constantly worry about. Later, . This challenge never feels beaten whereas I expected to end up master this constraint by crafting or finding a particular piece that would help.Should have been better :- complete change of pace once you're done with chapter 2 (which took me a particularly long time compared to the rest of the game, and felt the longest by afar). I was initially interested by the exploration/"survival" part of the game which happens at the beginning, but in the end I feel the (very) linear end is more what it should have been like since the beginning. Definitely not worth remembering- your spacesuit AI never stops with the witty comments. I like his talking rythming the progression of the game because this is very empty audio-wise, without. Unfortunatly, him being almost the only character talking is way less exciting by the end.- the free DLC gamemode (= survive for as long as possible starting with 0 gear on a new map to explore, some modified recipes, no spaceship to hide in to replenish your oxygen) sort of feels like the gamemode I expected to play since the beginning- no matter where you are in the game, food and water are not constraints important enough that you need to particularly worry about them.- global objectives feel like pretexts to elongate the gametime, since you Annoying stuff, more or less noticeable :- overrall, the story is on the "dumb and funny" side, don't expect much better- even with the boost and vehicules, moving feels pretty slow overall. It's a shame the numerous travels don't really feel interesting.- oxygen recharges quite slowly in safe areas for some reason, so you will often wait for what feels like a full minute doing nothing, until it replenishes.- when several dialogues get triggered at the same time, they cut each other. Thankfully you can read every message log later.- don't drop anything valuable in your outpost or you may lose it : everything bumps quite far when you walk against it, and stuff may move on their own because of the low gravity. Also, clipping is a thing.- markers get added automatically on your compass HUD, but you cannot place your own markers. _childDocuments_.review: I....just dont know.This game wants to be subnautica in space and funny. Humour is subjective, most jokes are obscure references. There was one joke that made me laugh out loud tho. Because it references Subnautica and made me think that it is a better game in every regard.Exploration:While subnautica uses its whole world, Breathedge uses new Areas for every chapter. While until chapter 4, you can always go back to previous chapters areas, you almost never need to. BUT: There is just an aweful lot of backtracking and grind. Subnautica solved this, by having a much more interesting world (space is empty) and the needed resources in every direction. There were enough parts of every vehicle to scan for example. Breathedge puts a ton of markers on your screen, so you just travel there, get a blueprint, return, get resources, craft, and then see that you need four instead of one, so you grind.Travel: Travel in general is way to slow. Expecially later in the game i found myself pressing W for some minutes, while scrolling reddit on my phone. No enemys, nothing to see, just empty space while you backtrack.In later chapters, you walk a lot through space station corridors, at your goal, you need to craft something and you have all the ressources, but you need to travel back to your ships crafting bench, back to your goal,. back to your ship. At one point, the game even taunts you with a quick travel that does not exist. Why?Crafting: Is okay, but grindy. What i did not understand is, why the resource needed for batteries demanded a tool that needed batteries to craft, forcing you to scavenge for batteries in some scarce resource cache, while the needed resource was right there, taunting you.Story: It works with a lot of suspense by spoken promises that most of the time dont deliver, which gets stale after the third time.So why do i still recommend it? Because in the later chapters, i had fun with the story. In the earlier chapters, there was so much potential, an many nice ideas for setpieces, But there is just so much...emptyness in between. Play in small doses.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : -Great art style, graphics, humour and story telling.            - Low travel speeds + long distances + nothing to do while travelling = slow, boring gameplay             - Fixes: severely boost travel speed, limit oxygen to compensate, incorporate collision penalties.The feeling I eventually got playing this game is like when you drive all the way to the shops only to realise you didnt bring your wallet then have to drive all the way back home...but over and over.The movement speed is too slow, I've got to a point where i need to travel over a kilometer which involves holding "W" for over a minute and a half with nothing to interact with or look at as things slowly get bigger and bigger as i approach them. Then if you cant find a clear path to progress, the oxygen limitations make you turn back and start the next two minutes of holding "W" with nothing to do except press shift every 30 seconds for a minuscule boost in speed. The scale of this game is what makes it painful, I get it, its in space and space is vast but games are also meant to be engaging. I would say this game feels like if you took Subnautica, removed all the seacreatures and put you in the deep open ocean where theres nothing to interact with for kilometers.Ive invested 6 hours into this game but the last two were just hoping that something exciting would happen. Subnautica and Green hell keep you engaged because there are threats that can appear at a moments notice and there is something of value within reach wherever you go. The only threat I felt in this game was the threat of my own laziness or unwillingness to make a second trip as my oxygen levels depleted. This is not good.Here is a potential fix, greatly boost the travel speeds, limit oxygen if you have to, make players get hurt for travelling to fast into objects. At least then there is a reason to pay attention to my immediate surroundings instead of glance at my oxygen meter then back at the objective marker repeatedly. If it shortens the play time so what, at least then I'll make it to the credits before uninstalling.This may just be my opinion, but if it isn't I hope the developers do something about it because I'd love to keep playing it, but not when it takes this long to do anything.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed certain aspects of Breathedge. But overall I'd say it was about a 10/60/30 split between fun/boring/bad. As such I can't recommend it.It isn't a game that respects your time.You'll spend a large portion of it going back and forth very slowly through the same empty areas that you have previously.And I mean that literally, there's nothing between you and your goal, nothing dangerous, nothing to interact with, just a waste of time. And a needless one at that. This is further compounded by the durability of items being very poor. The game makes you remake your tools from scratch after only a few uses. Often the game has you travel far into an area only to find you need one of the many tools available for a single interaction at the end. At which point said tool either broke on the way there or you simply didn't bring it. And then makes you walk all the way back to make a new one. Crafting stations are usually only found in "bases" and despite being loaded with the relevant materials you'll have to go all the way back and forth to make the required item. That having been said it's generally well made technically. It's not as janky as a lot of these kinds of games tend to be, if it wasn't for some of the quite frankly baffling design decisions one might think it was made by a big experienced development team. But it's weird. It has a bunch of mechanics that are either just pointlessly tedious or downright irrelevant. Base building for example is a thing the game does, but much like "The Forest" there's very little point to it, except wasting resources on something you don't need. And storage.. Oh god storage. So every container in the game has a full page(screen) of inventory slots. This includes your inventory, suitcases, and the big storage lockers that are built into and takes up an entire section of wall. The suitcases are small but also physics objects, so as a result the base storage lockers aren't only pointless to make, they're also really bad efficiency wise. As a result your storage will consist of piles of suitcases all over the floor filled with crap, or worse just the items themselves in huge piles on the floor. Like I mentioned before the suitcases are physics objects so it's very possible for them to slide, fall down or get kicked somewhere, and you can't crouch in the game, so they can slide somewhere you can't get to them.And I should mention you can only carry the suitcases them they're empty. That's right, that means when you're moving stuff you'll do it one inventory at the time. When leaving the first area of the game that means many many trips through empty space. Moving all my crap took me around 3 hours of just going back and forth. After that point the game shifted gears completely and the base I had built was left behind, and all the stuff I had previously thought was precious enough to bring with me also became irrelevant. Why? Well halfway through the game it switches gears and you'll be running through one linear space station after another just being absolutely showered in items that were previously scarce and hard to find. Did I mention the corridors are linear? Yeah that means one long pointlessly snaking area to go into, and then all the way back again, often multiple times. It's just a complete waste of the players time. There's a joke at that point about using fast travel, and when you try it quips that it isn't in the game. If you'll find that funny or not is subjective. However when you make a meta joke like that about having to do something tedious and boring, you need to then give a way of resolving it after having made it. Not just expect the player to keep tanking the tedium you deliberately put in there. It's like telling a kid at a birthday party that there's cake after they finish eating a pile of gravel. Then surprise it wasn't cake, it's more gravel. You have a laugh, then give the kid the cake. You don't just give more gravel and expect the kid to stick around. My summer car(at least it used to be) a good example of giving the player problems they needed to manage and work around. Something might happen that'd require you to respond to it, often in a costly way. Imagine that except the cost is always just your time. Everything that happens in breathedge just has you throw time at it, often with nothing happening while you run/fly back and forth between the two points you've done several times before.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I find myself coming to the store page to look at reviews, mostly for validation of my feelings of frustration, thinking, "Surely, I must be missing something? It must get better than this, right?"I have a habit of buying a lot of games and not finishing them. So I've been trying to get through a list of games, so I could finally play this without feeling guilty. It just so happens that I was working on finishing up Subnautica Below Zero, and it was great because allegedly, these games are similar. Hardly. Subnautica and its sequel are far better games. They are designed better, prettier, have better sound design, art direction, game mechanics, user interface, map/level design, etc.I'm only an hour and a half in, and I'm getting incredibly fed up. I have almost never given up on a game this early. But the amount of tedium, forced in-your-face humor, arbitrary milestones and progression points, not to mention really poor UI in both crafting and inventory, makes this game incredibly un-fun, especially coming off the heels of a very similar game that was so much better in every one of these regards.Take for example in Subnautica, the fabricator. For those who haven't played it, its your primary point of crafting for the majority of the game. When you are able to craft a new item, you see a list of icons, 4 or 5 major categories of craftables. Within those, you can open sub categories, and then finally the item you wish to craft. The icons are grey if you cannot craft something based on the items in your inventory, and blue if you have enough resources to craft something. Additionally, there is an indicator whenever you have something new to craft. In Breathedge, you have to just guess what you can craft, if you have enough materials, and constantly click through tabs that make no sense and not intuitively organized to maybe find the thing you want. Not to mention things change names based on the "Joke" of something, vs the actual usable tool you make later. It's all just nonsense, and utterly tedious, unnecessary, and poorly communicates the elements needed to effectively use.This is honestly the biggest thing I have yet to see anyone talk about. There are lots of other reviews that details things beyond this, but I haven't seen others talk about the really poor crafting UI. But keep reading the reviews to find quite a long series of complaints about this game. There's a good chance that if the review says "not recommended" I agree with the majority of the sentiments, except perhaps those about crashes. Game ran perfectly fine for me.At the end of the day, the game is so focused on being "funny" (its really not), that nothing actually makes sense or is intuitive. If the devs spent half the time that was put towards their mediocre writing and spent it on actual level, UI, and game mechanic design, this would be a significantly better game.

_childDocuments_.review: 🖥  🖥Windows 10, AMD FX-8350, 2x SLI GTX 660 TI, 16 GB RAM⭐  ⭐ 👍  👍Breathtaking visualsAmusing ComedyEnjoyable SurvivalExcellent Set Pieces👎  👎Gameplay will occasionally slow downQuite Short This is a survival game with bits of survival horror included. This is because space is scary. The graphics are astonishingly good, with rays of light perfectly falling upon celestial bodies around the player. The music is good, though repetitive. Gameplay is fun, though it includes tool durability and a water and food gauge. These don’t bother me, but they do bother some survival game players. 🎮  🎮 GatheringThe main activity in the game is collecting. The player will have to venture outside of their safe space ship if they want to be able to get home. Initially, they are only able to collect the small chunks that are scattered around space. The player is easily able to identify them by color and shape, though they are about all of the same size. The player must make sure to explore every direction as this game is fully three-dimensional. Resources also don’t regenerate. This is so the game can force players out of their comfort zone so that they continue the enjoyable story. There are plenty of supplies, so I didn’t find it difficult to stay fully stocked on materials at all. To get better materials, crafting is required.CraftingCrafting is a simple matter. The player must have the required ingredients in their inventory, and then an item can be completed. Annoyingly, items takes some time to complete and if the player moves off the menu with the item on it, the timer will reset and the item won’t be completed. There is also no queuing system in place either. This is one place I would like the game to be a bit smoother. Crafting usually allows the player to collect bigger and better resources.Advanced GatheringThere are large resource chunks that can be excavated once a player has the right tool available to them. These tools are often more specialized items to create and have a durability stat. Tools break after a certain amount of uses, though I didn’t mind this as one tool can often gather enough resources for quite a few more tools of the same type. Gamers that don’t enjoy durability systems should steer clear of this title as every single tool has a durability meter. All of the recipes for the game aren’t unlocked at the beginning. They are instead found in set pieces. Set Pieces and New RecipesSet pieces are key areas that are marked on the player’s map once they have visited the area. This is so that the key activity can take place which most often will reward the player with a new recipe. Each set piece is humorous and often has the player investigating the many items around the area. These aren’t key items are materials and can often be left behind. If the player likes the object, they can often be collected and used to decorate the player’s little space ship. Getting to each set piece can be a challenge.SurvivingOne of the biggest issues with space travel is that there isn’t any oxygen in space. It is vast and it is empty. That is why the player has to watch their oxygen gauge when they are outside of the ship. If this gauge reaches zero, the player’s health begins to drop. If it hits zero then the player is dead and they will have to start from a previous save. There are also hunger and water gauges that must be filled. This is accomplished by crafting food and water packets from materials found in space. Health can be restored by sleeping, but it costs food and water to sleep. It is a delicate balance to keep. The game’s pacing could be a bit better balanced. Quests and StagnationI quite enjoyed that there are quests in the game that advance the story and give the game meaning. I wish there were more of them though. Once one main quest is complete, it can take quite a while to get another one. This leaves the player wandering around while collecting resources while they hope to discover a new set piece. A bit more direction could be quite helpful.⚙ ⚙If you like atmospheric horror and difficult but manageable survival mechanics, then this is the game for you. This game is episodic, so the entire game isn’t finished. The game isn’t especially long at the moment, and I completed it in about 3 hours.📚  📚The story find the player playing as “The Man”. A crafty individual who finds himself trying to survive the depths of space so that he can get rescued. There are a few twists and turns that keep the player on their toes so they don’t fully understand where the story is going. I wish there were a few more of these moments as the gameplay and story sometimes stagnate until the player find a particular resource or complete a certain goal. Since this is an episodic game, I can’t wait to play the other chapters to understand what happened to our poor hero.🎧 🎧The sound is often humorous which goes along with the tone of the game. There is a lot of whacking and smashing, but there was enough variation that I didn’t mind it. The fact that there are breaks in between each gameplay moment of destruction also helps. Out in the quiet of space, the player is able to hear their breathing and the beeps that indicate that their oxygen levels are low. It increased the immersion to hear so little sound until the player is back in their comfortable and oxygen rich environment. While in the space ship there are a few soundtracks that sound like they are of the opera style. The player hears them too many times, and I would like more variety.📺  📺 The graphics are astonishingly good and use a cartoony style. Walking out of the spacecraft for the first time and seeing all of the asteroids and the sun all in one single screen just took my breath away. The lighting is used realistically, and asteroids and bits of space junk will often cast shadows on the objects behind them. The sun is blinding though as the player is placed close to it, so don’t stare at it for too long. A lot of the set pieces have unique graphics that make every single adventure out into space a treat as long as there is a goal available. Some ships are different colors, some provide more story material related to the graphics, it is quite the complete graphical package.🛠  🛠The performance for the game is nothing out of the ordinary. It will take a decent rig to play because of the graphics, but it isn’t hindered by terrible optimization. I also did not run into any bugs in the game either. This product was reviewed with a key provided by the developer for free.

_childDocuments_.review: Now talking about the game as a whole is pretty difficult considering I have upsides and downsides depending on what aspect of the game I'm talking about. So I'll split it up into 8 categories. And keep in mind, this is from the experience of someone who has all the achievements, and most of the collectables, etc.The gameplay for the first three chapters is amazing. The balance of managing oxygen, collecting resources and food/water is really good. Managing oxygen was pretty simple and I don’t ever think I died of a lack of it once. The starting oxygen is good, and the progression of getting more oxygen is a good balance as well. The resource collecting was probably one of my favourite things about the beginning of the game, it was just incredibly satisfying to collect stuff in outer space and gave me really nice Subnautica vibes (and an apology in advance for how many times i compare it to Subnautica, it felt really similar but still had its own ideas to it) I found myself not worrying about food and water as much which fits in pretty well with this game. A lot of the objectives I had fun with in the first 3 chapters and the way the humour affected the story made it fun as well (like making the “crap imposed by the developers”, more on the humour later). Now the last 3 chapters are a different story.The last three chapters of the game in short: suck. They took what made the game fun for me, which was gathering resources and doing quests in space and scrapped it. Instead you fly around in a spaceship going to different broken spaceships and doing 90% of the gameplay with gravity and running around. Well you might be thinking, “Can’t you just park the ship and go outside to get resources?” Nope. You can’t stop steering the ship until you dock, and you can only dock at the quest areas. What’s worse is sometimes the game won’t give you all of the required stuff you need to finish the quest in that area. So you have to go from area to area looking for the stuff you need. The best example I could give of this is in the final chapter you have to build three things, and one of the things is a “stabilizing unit” which takes electrical tape. In the area they give you to explore and collect materials (which is in zero grav so it was still kinda fun for me) but I searched the entire area, destroyed every crate and couldn’t find one electrical tape. Searching the entire place took about an hour, and then I had to go all the way back to chapter 4 and search until I found electrical tape which took another 30 mins. In a section, which in my second run only took about 10 mins, turned into an hour and a half. And this has happened on multiple occasions, so my first run took about 14 hours to complete. This was really frustrating, along with the awful gameplay of the last 3 chapters. The tools break way too fast, and it is really frustrating when the game makes you create a single tool for one instance and then never uses it again. The last boss fight was also, eh. I thought it was somewhat unique, but still disappointing. The last cutscene however I really enjoyed, I liked the cinematic and it felt well earned for my time playing the game.The story was not interesting for me. I didn’t feel it mattered that much and I pretty much forgot the grandpa existed until the reveal of him at the end. I don’t really have much other to say, but I’ll repeat that the final cutscene was sick.Whoever the art designer for this game is, should get an award of some sort, same with the composer. Jesus Christ, a lot of the reason I’m even making this review is how beautiful the game is. The first time I stepped outside and heard the electronic ambience music kick in while seeing a giant planet with meteors and the destroyed spaceship, I lost it. This game made me feel what I felt with Subnautica but to a 10x degree. It was awesome. This game doesn’t take itself very seriously, but in the parts it does, namely the music and design, it absolutely sets the bar for survival games and games in general. The designs of the tools, the open space, all of it looks phenomenal. And the music fits in so insanely well. The song “Ambient Music” by Jonny Easton that plays when you exit the spaceship is just way too good. From the ambient piano to the otherworldly electronic sounds. I love it so damn much. There needs to be way more attention on these aspects of the game.TLDR: Building sucks in this game. When you build something and deconstruct it, it gives you random parts back that you didn’t use to make the thing. The building is IKEA block-by-block similar to Subnautica, it’s meh. I didn’t utilize it very much because I didn’t need to except for the achievements to build the vehicles. And you never feel a need to do it because theres oxygen stations and processors pretty much all around the first map (the only place you can build a base)Since humour is a big part of this game I might as well make a section talking about it. The humour was something I didn’t expect from this game, and I was pleasantly surprised at the beginning but it started to grow old for me. Keep in mind this part is my opinion. Sometimes the humour landed really well and sometimes it got strained and tedious for me. Jokes that break the fourth wall get old very quickly. In the words of Ben Yahtzee Croshaw on “Zero Punctuation”:They sum it up pretty well. No further comment.The SFX were pretty good. Just wanted to mention how much I hate the drill sound effect :)The achievements were not that hard to get, some got tedious but they were mostly pretty engaging since they didn’t take that long (except for “The Breathtaking” which made me play through the entire game again because I saved at a poor time). Blowing up cows in the spaceship was pretty fun.Fun game, aside from some bugs where you get stuck and the bad gameplay and humour in chapters 3-6. The art design and music is incredible. After 36 hours, 3 playthroughs and all the achievements, I’m giving it a 6.5/10. It’s an okay-ish game all-in-all. I’m recommending it for the first 3 chapters and that’s it.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first bit of this game, i thought it similar to subnautica where its a slow start but gets more rewarding as you play and in a  sense that is right. _childDocuments_.review: Way too restrictive. -Oxygen keeps running out, so you have to manage to find recipes & resources before your time runs and and you have to return to your ship. Over and over again. Looking at your inventory doesn't pause the game either, so you keep burning food, water and oxygen if you try to manage your items anywhere other than places with air. At least in Subnautica you can come back to the surface wherever.-Tools have durability, to the extent that they break fully, so you have to keep scavenging from the limited resources around you to build new ones. Especially annoying, since most gathering requires some tool.-And of course. Every "survival" game needs to have them. Hunger and thirst. Adding to the already annoying chores you have to manage in this game.As lesser problems there's the movement and the UI. -Everything is so far away and you're so slow. Or everything seems to be so far because you're so slow. Hard to say.-The transition from flying to walking is a bit janky. And the floor in front of the bed is somehow broken, seemingly causing your character to bump into the small handle on the hatch below(?). That same spot managed to shunt me into being stuck in a wall, forcing me to reload a save. This might seem like a minor bug, but it's in between your container and your crafting station, so you're going to be moving a lot on that spot, making it a weird oversight.-The bigger problem I had with the UI was that there were way too many tabs in the crafting menu. At least for the beginning of the game, where there are only like 1-4 items in each category. This caused a lot of jumping back and forth between the tabs and the container, checking what materials I actually needed to craft a thing, which you have to do a lot. Since your tools keep breaking.... A lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge isn't a great game. It's two pretty good games sharing one title.Game 1 is just what it looks like on first glance: a free-roaming space survival game where you gather resources to build upgrades to increase how far you can safely travel. You can put plenty of hours into game 1 and have a grand old time, building up bases or puttering around on refurbished vacuum cleaners. It's pretty good. Game 2 kicks in kinda suddenly, though Breathedge does give you plenty of warning that you're about to pass a point of no return. In game 2, you leave behind any bases or vehicles you've built to engage in a largely linear story experience. Resources are abundant, but you don't really need them because there's no reason to actually build much of anything anymore. The gameplay takes a serious downgrade into full-on Walking Sim territory, but the writing takes a noticeable step up in quality now that it can just follow a linear ship. It's basically what you'd get if you took Portal 2 and removed all the puzzles. Not great. Pretty good. This isn't an unfinished game. It's two unfinished games glommed together into one full-length experience. I give it a thumbs up because I had a good time, but the second half still left me rather disappointed at all the unrealized potential. Overall, it consider it worth the money and time I spent on it. Calibrate your expectations appropriately and you might enjoy it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game in it's own right, but it's nowhere near 'Subnautica in space' like everyone is saying. The atmosphere isn't there because of the not-funny humour and the lack of any threats. The grind is not well balanced, and often feels overly laborious to achieve even the simplest of tasks. I'm still not clear why there's a 'pissing over things' mechanic, the crafting system is pretty rudimentary, and there's no newtonian physics for floating in null-g, like I was hoping for: You're always pretty much 'upright' in relation to doorways; you'll come to a stop after applying thrust along a vector without any counter-thrust, etc. Not bad, but I'd only buy it in the absense of anything else to play, and with a decent discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Opinion;  3 hours gameplaySo far ive got to say this game has been great. The first 2 mins had me allowing a robot to smoke, achieve the "bdsm club" achievement and die due to "pissing off a robot" before taking a single step. I would liken this to a more linear, space comedy version of subnautica. Sound and music have been exceptional so far. Graphics are good and even beautiful in sections. It has performed well and been very stable so far. Gameplay has been good with the only slight con being some instances of the interaction keybindings i am unable to change. All in all, for an early access game for about $20, i was surprised. Even early gameplay has been very enjoyable and i am really looking forward to playing more of it. *(I will be editing/updating this review upon more gameplay)Game is much more polished now, with most of the bugs or annoyances in gameplay being fixed. Gameplay is now very smooth with even more features. Base building in particular has been improved dramatically.Edit #1As of july/2020 i have finished the available chapters and the majority of the game's available content. I can now say that while there is definately room for improvement, the devs have already produced a great gaming experience. I still love this game and eagerly look forward to playing the following chapters. That being said I believe there are many things that still need work, (but be reasonable, this is still early access). The music while great, does start to get repetitive after long hours of gameplay. More tracks would be a welcome addition. The games stability also needs much work, (many crashes on my system). _childDocuments_.review: The game-play feels reasonably good, the visuals in the spacescape where you find yourself are very nice and the overall aesthetic style is pleasant. It runs very smooth, which is always nice.With all this being said, I just can't play any more.It's the humour.Injecting self-aware humour into a game world isn't a new phenomenon, nor is it an unwelcome one to me. When done right, games can uplift the experience with some well-timed, understated and wry quips. But in Breathedge, it isn't simply the lack of oxygen that can suffocate you - it is the unending, crushing, overabundance of jokes. In the first 20 minutes of gameplay I found myself sighing in exasperation when I looked at ANYTHING. Everything has a joke, either visually or delivered as a 'zany' joke by your spacesuit AI.  The quality of the jests range from inoffensively bland to nauseatingly 'Wacky' (Isn't it so random that his grandpa had a chicken, lol). And I can feel my ribs bruising from the developers elbows consistently nudging me after every joke - 'Pretty Funny, huh? hehe' they seem to say. Their presence behind every joke is palpable, an off-putting factor in any form of media. I need to feel that any humour delivered from the world, was born of that world - instead I am keenly aware of the developers involvement.The humour needs to be a dash of seasoning for the overall serene ambience that this game promises. For me, it needs to be less frequent and more subtle. Unfortunately, as it stands, the humour is a jarring note in an otherwise catchy song.While I cannot personally play the game, I will still recommend you try it as humour is subjective and what I find irritating, some may not be bothered by and others may love.If you can get past that, the game seems to be worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fresh and hilarious game!The dark and slapstick humour is so enjoyable and random XDWith gameplay not unlike Subnautica but in space, the player must harvest resources, explore and upgrade their suit and oxygen intake in order to survive and hopefully get rescue. _childDocuments_.review: Why are the majority of the reviews positive? Beats me. I am sure some people like the humour in this game (I don't). Yes, the sounds design is well done and the graphics look nice enough, but the whole gameloop conctrates about your lack of oxygen. Like other games out there using the same concept (Volcanoids for instance), it's just masquerading the lack of content by forcing you to enjoy the content in small chunks and the rest of the time spending back and forth to your oxygen source(s).Well done! This is how you make two hours worth of content last for appr. 10 times as much. Poor choice.At least you can do it like Subnautica, where it felt more natural and much more balanced. And that actually did have some sort of story and lacked this ridiculous attempt at being funny.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is fun and well written, the graphics are way better than they should be for a game that often treats itself like a joke. If you're looking to chuckle & chill Breathedge is a great choice.Getting more in depth, Breathedge is fun but a strange and largely fragmented vision, almost feels like two games in one, or that the devs couldn't decide how the game should play. Maybe part 1 was negatively reviewed I couldn't say, but the first and second halves of the game play and are paced extremely differently. Without giving too much away, the first part of the game consists of you incrementally upgrading your kit so that you may explore deeper into the depths of space. It's very survival oriented, space is very dangerous, and your focus is to craft tools that you can increase your range and robustness, and ultimately get to your goal across the map.Very late into this part 1 a base building / crafting system is introduced + vehicles which greatly expand your range, for me this was when the game-play peaked. I was well equipped, had my base slowly expanding but still overcoming risks to progress, still exploring. I was well off but space was always dangerous if I was sloppy.The second part- shamelessly and perhaps deliberately/ironically utterly throws away the entire space survival, base building etc.  Part 2 mainly consists of interior exploration, go to a,b,c, find and craft x,y,z, continue. It's no longer any survival at all, I was overflowing with resources etc. and frankly the second half is just not as fun. That said, it's not all bad in part 2 because the writing really picks up and becomes the focus of the game which was also fine because the suit is hilarious.At the time of writing this review there is more content on the way, and I look forward to it. I hope these devs refine, or make a sequel with a solid game-play direction.

_childDocuments_.review: After five hours of this game almost being good, I had to accept that it's not there yet. The mechanics and general progression are good, and the aesthetics are nice (though a bit dull), but the writing is absolutely terrible. As many have pointed out, the narrator is the worst, but in addition to talking way too quickly and with way too many words, the delivery of the information and painful 4th wall jokes really take away from the game. You'll get told about important locations by a spambot named "Babe", you have to build a model penis in order to progress the story, and just off to the right of your starting location is a dead hamster stuck in a toilet.Back to waiting for Subnautica 2 to be finished I go

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game!  The first two chapters is all about exploring and building.  Chapter 3 is more about exploring (since you have everything you need to finish the chapter).  Chapter 4 and 5 is more a linear point and click adventure with some "boss fights."  These fights felt more like puzzles to be honest.Over the entire game, the humor was present.  Sometimes it was subtle and made me chuckle. Other times it was brutally funny.  My only criticism is that the base building wasn't really needed (although forced in order to progress).  I think they should have removed a couple of engineering shuttles to force us to build our own bases.  Also the unlimited oxygen stations should not have been as plentiful in chapter 2.  We should have gotten an upgrade to our chapter 1 stations and been forced to build those (or a mini base).  Speaking of bases, storage modules in the base should have been better.  Building storage next to where you need it is a fundamental need (not in the habitat section).  But those issues are very very minor!Overall this is a great game at an amazing price.  It is pure entertainment in the guise of a survival/explore/build game!5/5

_childDocuments_.review: My quick little review is as follows (light non-story related spoilers included):Pros: Great visual and sound designVast world to exploreDefinitely has a challenge early game.Lots of resources to manage and craft Cons:Feels like 4 different sub-areas to explore do not really tie in together very well which breaks up the vastness of the world.The humor may not be for everyone, I laughed a decent amount and I cringed a decent amount.I wish there was a way to cut down on the AI chatter and keep it to important events or story moments only.The late game has a bit too much backtracking and doesn't feel as challenging as early on.Overall:I enjoyed my time in the game but it falls short on some things I wish it didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit of a mystery, as many of the pieces don't really fit together like you would expect.  It's a survival/crafting adventure with some great graphics and an immersive and tense deep-space setting.  On the surface it feels very serious, but they constantly try to inject humor in nonsensical ways that are more likely to induce head scratching than they do laughter.  One example that really sticks out for me: you inexplicably carry around a  chicken in your space suit, and use him to disable electrical hazards.  There is no additional context.  It's a short game at about 4 hours, but the crafting and exploration are pretty fun.   Despite the bizarre attempts at humour throughout, the ending was actually hilarious.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like , but much worse. And in space. It's really a space-floating and station-walking simulator with a silly/funny/stupid commentary. The game is super boring.In the first chapter, you fly 6m/s and have to constantly return to your crashed shuttle. You are super happy when you build a jetpack and can occasionally fly 10m/s. But then you have to fly further, so you have to build some rechargeable oxygen stations to refill on your way, effectively taking all your improvements away.In chapter two, you get access to a mini rocket to fly 40m/s, but everything is even further away, again reducing the impact of all the new things you researched.As you finish chapter two, you will have a mini space station built, and you will be super happy to discover a shuttle that you can fly - only to abandon the area...In chapter three, you don’t float around anymore. You fly your shuttle and dock to stations, only to walk very, very long corridors back and forth. Door you cannot open? Go back to the shuttle to build a key, then run to the door. Oh, the door has a missing piston so they can’t open? Run to the shuttle again to build a missing part. And so on...And there is no fast travel or even auto walk!Inventory management is really bad. What seemed like a big backpack at the beginning, becomes really small when you have to carry 10 different tools with you. You have to pick up all items manually, even if you destroy a bigger piece of something (by hitting it 10 times, always, no upgrades), it spawns 3 pickable items so that you have to look around and pick them up 1 by 1 again. Buildable containers? Pretty much non-existent. You can only build a suitcase that you can throw on the floor and fill with items, that you will keep accidentally kicking around whenever you walk nearby it.Even simple things like crafting or sleeping takes 3 seconds of progress bar moving. What for? It’s a single player game!Inconsistency between opening containers sometimes with LMB and sometimes with RMB was another thing that was driving me crazy.I kept playing, hoping that it will get better, but it only gets worse. At some point, while I was exploring the station (and running back and forth), I got killed at the very end, only to discover that no auto save had been made when entering the final room with a boss. And I have enough running.If you are into Open World Survival Craft games, this game has almost nothing to do with this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica in space. Comedy that you either like or hate. Separated by KM's of nothingness between. Pacing is a thing, and this game lacks it.Had the potential to be exceptional, yet falls flat in so many ways. Each "chapter" plays as almost an entirely new game, with many of the things done in the previous chapter thrown out and new mechanics introduced. Chapter 1 and 2 are the best, and the rest are forgettable -- 1KM square rooms with little to interaction with (on the order of like 5 things), separated by snake like hallways of emptiness.So many of the "missions" past chapter 2 were: find ship. go into ship. find blueprint. go back to entrance. make ♥♥♥♥. go back into to ship. Rinse and repeat. Except the ships are 1KM square rooms with bland hallways. Even travelling between places was essentially "get in ship, drive toward point for 10 minutes and twiddle thumbs".I get it. Space is huge. But that doesn't lead itself towards good pacing in a game. It could have been great comedic game if they didn't arbitrarily try to stretch it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded after 14 minutes. Jesus christ.The setting is great. 'Subnautica in Space'. Awesome, gimme gimme gimme. Technically and functionally, this game is good, the only caveats being that tool durability is incredibly low and I could already perceive the game becoming tedious beyond belief.'How could you possibly have any criticisms if you played for 14 minutes?'I understand that this game is supposed to be funny. There were jokes that made me smile or chuckle a little in the first 4 or 5 minutes maybe.But then they kept coming.And coming.And coming.The way that the jokes obnoxiously force themselves upon you in some situations, the suits computerised guide or whatever it was talking non stop after every small action you do. Jesus christ, just give me some room to breathe (ironically). By the 14 minute mark, I could see that this game was going to bombard me with jokes until I truly resented it. In fact, I already resent it.TLDR; Good game wrapped in an unbelievable layer of obnoxious writing.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not really a fan of survival games, but I do recommend Breathedge.   It's humor makes the grim survival sitiation our protagonist fins himself in really enjoyable.   I found this game to be solidly made and short, but long enough to feel I got my money's worth (much like Portal).I'm waiting wallet in hand for the next chapter to land.I like their in-world explanation for coming back from in-game deaths by having the actual game as a flashback.  I thought that was very original.Would have liked to have found more uses for my immortal chicken (yes that's an actual thing in this game).[edit]This is an update to my review to reflect the updates in chapters 2 and 3.They did find more uses for an immortal chicken in space :)More types of resources were added, more components to craft from them and more tools to craft entirely, along with modules (a camp site or home away from home).With extended play parts of the crafting system have begun to annoy me.  I have compiled a short list of things i'd like changed.:* If you don't want to keep all your resources in a big "physics mayhem" inducing pile on the floor you have to put them in a container, but the suitcase is way too expensive (16 metal for a suitcase! try 1 fabric and 1 plastic).* I thought the suitcase would be good for moving my stash between shuttles, but you're not allowed to carry it when it has contents.  This is dumb.  Making me backtrack to move my stash to a new shuttle is not fun (or funny).  The game was worth my money just for one chapter the developers don't meed to artificaly extend the playing time like this.* I'd like the crafting system to remember the blueprint I was last looking at.  It bugs me having to re-locate the blueprint after hunting down each of the 5 or 6 components required to build it.* You can't tell what's in a container without opening it.  Please can with have a textual list popup when we look at a container (like Fallout 4's looting system).* I'd like to be able to tag a blueprint in the crafting system and have the game highlight any  resources I need to craft it in my containers or nearby in the world.  This would save on much annoying popping in and out of the crafting and container menus trying to memorize blueprints.* I'd like to be able to salvage modules from the wreckage.  I can dismantle my own modules.  What can't I dismantle the wrecks?* I'd like the first module built to have everything I need to survive in it.  Building a module, then an airlock, then a generator, then an air-supply requires a lot of tedious crafting and memorizing.  I wouldn't mind if it required a larger amount of resources to build then the basic service module, but less steps would be more desirable and feel more rewarding.The robot "bodies" in this chapter were a bit of a tease.  Pity there is no way to interact with them.Looking forward to the next chapter, but I really hope for a re-work of the crafting more.[/edit][edit]This is my update to reflect the changes in Chapter 4 and the finale.OK they addressed NONE of the things I would have liked changed after playing chapters 2 and 3.Chapter four takes an odd turn from the salvage to build better tools help you explore further and survive longer of chapters 1 to 3 into flying your new ship from one linear path module to another.  Many of these modules require you to craft something to get through an obstruction at the far end making you  to backtrack to your ship through rooms you already looted, build it, then backtrack though those same rooms, to the obstruction to use the new item (and this is the only time that item gets used).  This is blatently and painfully obviously more padding out the gameplay time.There is some weak sauce space combat against infinitely respawning enemies (but that's OK you get infinite free repairs to  work out that you can just fly around the area the enemies patrol)There is a boss battle (right after one of the obstructions I ranted about earlier), just so the devs can poke fun at boss battle tropes.If feels like a lot of plot gets jammed into the final chapter after the slow burn, teasing, and clues in the previous chapters.Good comedy has good timing and this game suffers from bad timing brought about from it's chapter by chapter development.  It would really benefit from and end to end edit to redistribute the plot points and upgrade blueprints more evenly.The first three chapters had promise, but the failed to stick the landing with chapter four.Play something that won't initentionaly waste your time first.[/edit]

_childDocuments_.review: //2020_2_26Holy Cow, this is first time -in my experience- an early development has genuinely delivered on the final product! Cannot express how happy I am with the stabilization trigger addition to the flight. All the little touches, like the new awesome music and the extra help at the beginning are great. Well done, guys, you've truly won me over with the improvements and looking forward to finishing the game.I REALLY wanted to like this game: loved the concept, loved the humor, and the graphics are phenomenal. I normally appreciate steep learning curves in my games, but this one is just too much of a hindrance rather than enjoyable practice while feeling some improvement. I get that the physics are accurate in the game, but when you enforce real newtonian interactions but remove simple flight maneuverability like roll or even small controlled thrusts, then you end up playing pinball in space -wasting oxygen simply trying to pick something up or highlight an interaction. I know people in the comments complain about the poor oxygen supply, and while I somewhat agree with them, I don't think it's a game breaker, the challenge is justified. Maybe I'll come back and play a the lower difficulty settings than normal, but since achievements are disabled for those modes I'm not all that enthused.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge's humour will be personal taste. It wasn't for me. The game looks good and runs well but animations are rough to non-existent which can be a bit jarring. The space physics feel off, particularly motion. There's no sense of momentum in a vacuum.The durability system is awful. I played for an hour and crafted what felt like a dozen of the basic salvage tool. It pokes fun at bad survival game mechanics while forcing them on you. I guess that's the "ironic" part from the store description.None of these things are necessarily a deal breaker but all combined with the humour outstaying its welcome I decided Breathedge wasn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game tries very hard to be funny, but it is painfully unfunny. The game consists of venturing outside your spaceship and grabbing resources until your oxygen runs out. You use those resources to craft items that let you collect more resources, unlock new areas, and stay outside longer. It feels a bit like Subnautica, but unlike Subnautica you can't just swim up, you have to return to your base for oxygen. A lot of the resources you need are past areas you can't reach with your basic equipment. You have use extra oxygen and other consumables to get there. If you can even figure out where it is, nothing really points you in the right direction other than a casual voice line. All of this makes exploration really painful, like the game is actively discouraging you from doing it. To top all this off your tools have very limited durability and you need to continually eat and drink. This just adds to the boring time wasting of gathering more resources. Don't bother with this game unless its really on sale and you want some lessons on bad game design.

_childDocuments_.review: What attracted me to this game was the survival feeling like Subnautica but in space, with lots of humor.Short: While the start of the game (chapter 1) was showing promise, it becomes progressively worse as the game goes. Each chapter plays like a different game, giving a feeling like it doesn't even know what it wants to be. Mechanics get hold really fast and just becomes tedious. Game is overall way too long.Details:- Most of the humor is really not that funny.- Game constantly pushing for you to move making any sort of gathering in one place to be pointless.    Yet, the game gives you the ability (even forces you) to build a space station, but there's no reason to use it, and after a     certain point you cant even go back to it.- Progression in the game is very, very slow for no reason:      1) You're forced you to move long distances very slowly with nothing to do, nor any risk. During mid-game, you'll easily spend over 3 minutes doing nothing but hold W, only to stop somewhere to recover oxygen (see 3.) and do it again.     2) Tool durability just forces you to constantly go out which is not challenging, just time consuming.     3) Even resupplying your own oxygen takes time. (1s per 10s of tank capacity)- Most of the game is just Level Design and Art assets. There's hardly any mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: A couple hours in: This game deserves a whole lot more credit than "lol, look at the funny chicken and ♥♥♥♥ jokes".Firstly, I do love the writing, it translates very well and Breathedge has a great dry, dark sense of humour, and on the whole I have to agree with the general concesus of reviews when it comes to the comedic silly value of the game... however, Breathedge has some really great tactile gameplay, a wonderful Alien (1979) "old future" asthetic and a great painterly colour scheme which lends itself to fantastic looking space environments and a 70s style ship interiors.So while yes, this game is silly, and has to be appreciated on that level please dont base your purchase off that alone... it really does offer some great (sometimes tense) and thoughtful gameplay along with a beautiful asthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Main thing that did this game in for me was the humor. A lot of the jokes lean really heavy on fart and d**k jokes, which I don't find particularly funny. The visual design is fun, the crafting system, though initially a bit obtuse, is interesting and space flight isn't bad (I was kinda hoping that it'd be more like Prey, which this game's visual aesthetic seems to take a lot of cues from), but as a game that's trying to be a comedy, Breathedge naturally leans very heavily on it's gags. Unfortunately, those don't do much for me.My other big gripe is the endless alerts. You get the same large, condescending, screen-obscuring low oxygen alert every time you get down to 20 seconds left, regardless of whether it's the first or fiftieth time you've gotten it. There's also a part of the game really early on where an NPC keeps insisting you come to save her about every ten minutes, despite the fact that a) the game doesn't really tell you where she is and b) it seems like you can't get close to her until you build better equipment, which takes awhile.I'm probably going to give this another go, see if maybe the base building is quality enough to overcome the other drawbacks, but right now, I'd say your money is better spent on something like Subnautica, which does the corporate dystopia future writing a lot better.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: Breathedge is basically Subnautica, but in space. You’ll start as a lone survivor of a spaceship crash and need to find food, water, and a few resources to craft the basic survival equipment. From there you start exploring your surroundings, find new resources and start crafting better equipment. Later on you also need to build a base and find the truth behind your family and the explosion of the giant spaceship.If you’re into exploration/survival/crafting games, Breathedge is the game for you. The story starts out strong, the atmosphere is great (at the beginning at least), and it especially the sound feels like you’re stranded in space.Yes, quite a few: The first two of four chapters are really great, but once you start with base building, things get rough: There are graphical glitches, and once you’ve finished your base, it is basically useless. It feels like a lot of potential is wasted.In chapter 4, the story also gets really weird and the great humor from before is gone. You also have to walk through artificially enlarged tube systems, which are made to increase the playtime. That’s annoying and simply a bad design choice.I am not sure. I had fun for the first 25 to 30 hours, but after that the game started to annoy me. If you’ve loved Subnautica 1 and 2, and you can’t wait for the 3rd Subnautica to come out, Breathedge might give you a bit of the atmosphere you’re looking for.Maybe pick it up in a sale.Subnautica, Subnautica: Below Zero, Raft, The Forest, Green Hell, Valheim, Stranded Deep, Grounded, The Planet Crafter, No Man’s Sky

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours in. This game boasts decent graphics and a pretty detailed story. This is a very silly game and the jokes that are thrown in although obviously take away from immersion, it keeps me laughing and having a good time and reminds me to not take things so seriously when I RUN OUT OF AIR AND DIE!!!!!...... Fun game solid 7/10 for a early access. There are definitely some things that can be improved such as resources should respawn so you don't mine everything and end up needing more only to find there is no more. I really think you need to try this game and support them, this game is going to go good places and I am glad to be along for the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Reddit-level humor, this game is for you. Not my cup of tea. Also the building mechanics are only used during the first third of the game, afterwards the game becomes extremely linear. You just fly a little ship from corridor level to corridor level. Several times the game references/lampoons Subnautica. It's clear that's the game they wished they made. They didn't come close.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: This game sucks.  The core gameplay loop is 'find the missing part'. It bills itself as a crafting-survival sandbox in space, but it isn't.  You have a ton of materials and are looking for one specific material to progress.  Search through a ton of junk to find the one piece of glass on a map.  It isn't fun. This is the kind of gameplay I would expect from a $5 game, and I would still feel ripped off at $5.
_childDocuments_.name: Breathedge

_childDocuments_.review: So after my my first experience with the game in Early Access (which I thoroughly enjoyed by the way), I decided to wait for the full release to get the proper full experience.  After finishing the game, I thought I'd update my review.As a big Subnautica fan, it's definitely the first game that comes to mind when you first explore Breathedge. In truth Breathedge is it's own beast and it would be unfair to try to compare the 2 too closely.  Altough the game does start off as a proper survival game after a certain point it dramatically changes direction into a much more linear but still quite fun experience.  In retrospect this may have been a decision based on budget/timelines as there are a lot of cool survival elements that you barely scratch the surface on, and some are just plain unused.  Unfortunately base building falls into that category as well, so word of advice don't spend too many calories here unless you really love building stuff.The best part of the game for me is definitely the humor - very tongue in cheek and there are plenty of hilarious surprises along the way that had me laughing out loud.Plenty of great easter eggs / nods to other games that happen to be on my list of all time favorites - such as Mass Effect, Portal, Dead Space and a not so subtle and quite hillarious nod to Subnautica as well.After finishing the game I would rate it 8.5/10, only because I would have preferred to see more of the survival elements that were done so well in chapters 1 and 2.  That said definitely worth the purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems very repetitive and too challenging from the get go to be fun. You can't explore much either, because you are very constrained by oxygen requirements. 2 hours in and it's just back and forth. Get metal, go back to ship. Barely make it to lead paint, go back to ship. Rinse and repeat. The story/humour is nice, but not a replacement for fun gameplay. I'd be more sympathetic if this was EA, but they are content to release this the way it is now.

name: 9 Monkeys of Shaolin
detailed_description: BattleJuice Alchemist - OUT NOW IN EARLY ACCESS REMEDIUM - OUT NOW IN EARLY ACCESS Join our Discord community About the Game 'If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle'. - Sun Tzu, The Art of War 9 Monkeys of Shaolin - marks a true rebirth of the iconic beat 'em up genre in vein of old-school video games. If, as a kid you had hours of fun playing SNES or SEGA beat 'em up videogames crushing foes left and right then this new title from the creators of hardcore brawler REDEEMER is definitely for you! As a mere Chinese fisherman Wei Cheng you have to avenge the death of your friends and family slaughtered in a pirate raid at your peaceful village. Game protagonist is quite a tough nut to crack as he knows the basics of ancient martial arts only mastered by legendary Shaolin monks. Get your trusty battle staff ready for a challenging adventure in Medieval China and for merciless fights with hordes of various enemies. Action-packed battles, user friendly controls and incredible atmosphere of great kung-fu movies of 70s – all this makes 9 Monkeys of Shaolin a perfect choice for every true fan of really hardcore brawlers. 3 unique fighting styles: fight on earth, in the air or use mysterious magic seals. Combine these elements to defeat every enemy on your way. Captivating narrative: discover the fascinating story of Wei Cheng and follow him as he rises from a simple fisherman to the master of Shaolin martial arts. Stunning visual style: unlikely combination of historical and mystical elements gives you an exciting experience from every scene appears on screen. Extensive character development system: you learn a great deal of ways to victory as you discover various unlockable perks, items and fighting styles. More than 25 different levels: Chinese villages, pirate ship, Buddhist monasteries, Japanese mansions, ancient ruins and many more. 10 types of Chinese and Japanese polearms , each with its unique traits. Discover the landscapes to find new items! Co-op play: invite your friend to help you fight through growing waves of enemies and complete the game together.
