_childDocuments_.review: Hey,  developers. I have an idea for you. Give us a neutral option for reviewing games. My life would feel significantly better if I didn't have to choose between outright admonishing a relatively mediocre title over enthusiastically recommending them. I wouldn't have to mull over the decision to call out bland titles like  if you gave me the option to just post a review without recommendation.The basic premise of  is that you willingly travel into an different world called the Hollow where you have to save and support little plant creatures as you fight off red/black thorn monsters. Essentially the game is naught more than a day care simulator with a rudimentary crafting system. Throughout the campaign you're given four procedural generated maps that you can explore to find more sentient shrubs and beat trees, monsters, and cars to death for materials.The world itself is quite a pleasant visual experience, given the well-planned island mapping and general ambiance. Unfortunately the majority of the game plays the exact same song on loop, dragging the overall design into the mud of boring tedium. It's a functioning system, if anything.If it sounds incredibly simple despite minor layers of complexity, it is because the game itself is rather simple. The basic gameplay cycles around exploring and collecting materials, returning to the base camp to drop them off and craft or stop a raid of thorn monsters, and repeating the cycle. Unfortunately this is one of its biggest flaws. If there was some sort of added layer of complexity added to each of the four chapters outside of simple mechanics like worrying about making a bunch of sentient weeds comfortable in their island enclosure, it would be a completely different and immeasurably better experience. But it isn't. We're stuck with a mostly bland title that loses all luster after chapter 2.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. You mainly build your base and defend it, explore the surroundings to find the ressources to expand it. While „easy if you know how“, some functions are not intuitive, and I recommend to play the endless mode before the campain, otherwise quite some people will be caught in a death spiral and end up frustrated. Once you have worked out what is important and how it works, the camapin becomes a stroll.What I liked:- a solid set of building blocks for the base – be it defence or life support. A good mix of micromanagement in building and automation in keeping it running.- Good island design makes exploring fun, the waypoints to link up islands make it fun to travel. - base defence at regular intervals keeps you on your toes (at least until your base has become a meat grinder that takes care of attackers on it's own, which is still fun to witness) - I'm happy with the way the fighting works. It may be not challenging enough for seasoned console fighters, but for the casual gamer it's good and well.I had a lot of fun, but even in endless mode there are some misgivings:- the base island is quite small and this dictates base design somewhat - your building limitation is quite harsh, so you can't build a sprawling village/fortress with multilayer defences even if you had the space.- In the long run you don't have much to do: most islands you only clear (and loot) once, except for healing plants you don't have to go out, since the raiding monsters drop all the crystals you need and building base materials don't grow back. Once you got all the metal/stone/cloth/wood from an island, there won't be new supplies there. For longer play, outposts with mines that have to be developed and defended would be more interesting than the supply lorries. - there are no facilities for the hero or his multiplaying friends. Only the drakes need to eat, drink, sleep and be entertained. No dining or bqu'ing together with friends. The Whirlpool is only for the drakes, too.- rearranging a bigger base is a real hassle, especially if you made a few errors in early design and end up in some kind of gridlock.- Hero outfits are just cosmetics. You don't need warm clothing in winter and don't sweat in warm clothing in the summer. I'd prefer it if clothing was useful instead of just pretty. The story of the campaign works, but is very cliche (evil old male witchunters poison the environment, a wise woman fights for mother nature). The game mechanic is solid, but the story doesn't really link to it. It's no biggie, but you don't play to find out, how the story will turn out, because you already know.My conclusion: It's a lot of fun and well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a game worth playing , but it has numerous issues to be ironed out. The art direction and environment is beautiful (although I can see a couple of compression artifacts on some of the textures, and I'm not sure the crack pattern on the rocks is supposed to tile that much), and the animation is spectacularly done; the Drakes are adorable to watch and interact with. The core gameplay loop, however, gets repetitive really quickly. You start on a tiny island where you build your base, explore other islands until your inventory is full or a raid starts, come back, defend/upgrade your base, and repeat until you decide to complete the quest (go to x location on a random island and then come back to your base) and advance to the next season. In theory, you could probably beat the game in a few hours if you just beeline for the quest objective. Raids are annoying because enemies will ignore you and dash for whatever is drawing aggro. Damage-dealing defenses aren't worth it because they will draw all the aggro and get destroyed immediately, and are way too expensive to keep rebuilding. The final boss was disappointing. The pacing is quite weird; my girlfriend and I visited every island, and halfway through the second season we unlocked all of the endgame upgrades, so there wasn't any progress to be made after that other than building extra stuff to support the increasing number of Drakes.The combat is the most frustrating aspect. Movement feels stiff and unresponsive, especially right after recovering from a dash. Most terrain is at a steep angle, so you find yourself slipping off half the time, usually into the aether (Where you can't jump so if you're not fast enough to get out/use a crystal, you're dead). Parrying is useless as the stagger is momentary and you have no larger a time window to attack than you would from just dodging; it's high risk and low reward. Equally, blocking felt like it served no purpose when I could just dash past anything. Ranged weapons apart from the weed spray weren't worth it whatsoever as the ammo was ridiculously expensive for the damage they dealt (Although the weed spray had no problem instantly deleting full health Stalkers and Terminer from the game, and the ammo use reduction buff/ranged crit damage skills made it even more destructive, which was fun to watch). When I heard about the skill system update, I was glad the combat was going to get more depth, but it ended up being a disappointment. Leveling up takes a while, so every time you get a skill point is exciting. What's not exciting is getting to raise your attack speed by 1% or damage by 3%. "Skills" that amount to "raise stat by x%" while necessary, are always the least interesting in any game. Games like Borderlands, for example, made things interesting by mixing stat boost skills with skills that would add  new abilities or create new interactions (such as bullet ricochet). The Drake buffs almost serve this purpose, but they are for the most part still stat boosts, and the ones that weren't I didn't encounter in my playthrough and had to look them up. Many of the buffs were also quite useless (Why do I need to sacrifice a buff slot to last longer in the aether if I never enter it without an aether crystal anyways? Why is there a fear chance buff when most enemies die in 2-3 hits? What is the point of knockback if there isn't any hitstun and it just puts enemies out of range of my next attack?) I understand that this is a small studio and the game is intended at a casual audience, so I feel like I should still recommend this game. But I think the kinks should be sorted out to make this game feel less like it's in early access. I think the best solution would be to cut down the scope of the content and make it a really fun 10-15 hour game instead of a slogging 20-30 hour game.  6/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for August 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before September 7th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.I don’t know who this is for.  You have these ultra-cute characters called Drakes, and players have to build up their village and try to give them food, water, and entertainment.  But those Drakes are in a world filled with a dismal outlook and grimdark set of enemies.  Is this for kids or adults?  I honestly don’t know and it sits in the middle in an uncomfortable area, where adults might find it too cutesy, and young kids probably shouldn’t play with the dark visuals.Drake Hollow is about farming resources and using them to build up Drake’s home.  Players will travel to multiple islands to explore them and gather schematics, which are needed for new buildings.  At the same time, they will be clearing dangers. There is a multiplayer component as well that I didn’t get a chance to explore, but I struggled to try to find resources.  Islands have limited resources, but before long they run out and they don’t appear to respawn that quickly, that’s probably a decision to push players to explore further out, but it’s a bit frustrating as every trip takes longer and longer to reach an interesting part. There does appear to be some interesting mechanics, such as building networks to multiple islands, and leveling up of Drakes but both of those mechanics were further out than that first hour.Pick this up if you want a different type of survival, with a focus on building a town for cute characters and foraging.  This is a really interesting stylistic game, but it combines two extremes, so check the visuals on display here.   I’m probably going to pass myself, but it’s not a bad experience.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended if you just want a relaxing, sometimes challanging base building, base management, action combat and exploration experience in third person. Like their previous game, Flame in the Flood, Molasses Flood takes a few currently very popular and enjoyable gameplay mechanics and ideas and combines them well together to create something actually unique.Technically the creatures that give this game it's name are in a survival mode, they need food, water and constantly something to do or else might parish. They will help you with your base, a little Drake community basically. And if one of them dies, they are gone. But your character itself won't die forever, you will be able to respawn in your base with the penatly being your weapons losing a lot of their durability or you can ghostwalk to your last location to revive there and have no penalty other than the time it takes to get there. The base building is deep enough to not make it tedious for people who play the game for all it's offering. Your base will get raided by mobs, and the waves will scale. But when you are stuck at a certain point for whatever reason, the raids will not increase in difficulty, so the raid mechanics stay fair throughout.All in all, if you already played Flame in the Flood, this game - Drake Hollow - is a lot fairer and can be enjoyed for long hours of play with steady progress. While Flame in the Flood may be better suited for short sessions. I didn't test another huge part of this game yet - the Coop - so i can't tell you what changes as soon as you play with other people in up to 4 player sessions.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been a fun surprise. Gameplay loop is a mixture of base building, keeping your radish people alive (periodic raids on your base, which get more intense as your base grows larger), and pushing out to new islands to forage. The survival elements are more for your NPC vegetable villagers than for yourself. Graphics kind of look fortnite-ish for better or worse but it works decently for this. Combat is simple but fun so far (have run into small, large, and dog type monsters in one night playing). Also a decent number of different weapon types, although most seem to handle the same. After around three and a half hours in game we have more than half of the islands connected on our network of purple grinding poles so we can get around to the outer edges. Only concern is how long the content will hold up - I figure after another three-ish hours we should have all the islands connected/cleared, and at that point I am not sure if there is an additional level of content that will open up or if that will be all. (EDIT - Yes, there is more content. When you finish the first set of islands there is a mini boss and then you get to travel to a new set)One other note...I dont generally have a lot of patience so I may have gotten irritated in figuring out some of the mechanics related to the base building etc if I had not been playing with friends. Between the three of us we figured it out pretty quickly but the tutorial was basic and just kind of turns you loose to sink or swim. When sorting out stuff in your base it helps to press "X" to go into "inspect" mode. Of course I also quickly died of thirst/hunger the first time I tried Raft and died miserably while barfing all over the jungle the first time I played Green Hell....soooo maybe its just me. Probably.

_childDocuments_.review: Drake Hollow is a third person action adventure game with some elements of base building. It has a great sense of adventure, but at least at the time of playing, the game felt like it was much longer than it had any business being. Anyhow, you run around a magical land with remnants of your hometown strewn about a sea of gray mist and nettles, searching for places and parts to journey further through the world. To save the world, you need to work together with the drakes – small, plant-like magical creatures. It’s not perfect, but it’s a good time if you’ve got a buddy.The exploration in Drake Hollow is out there with the best if you ask me. Not to say that there’s tons to the world or that the areas are particularly special. Rather, it’s the means by which you explore. The world is covered in a dark fog that’ll tear you to shreds if you linger long, so you have to prepare for your expeditions. Your primary method of handling the fog is a small barrier charm that’ll keep you and a small space surrounding you safe for a short while, allowing you to dash from one island to the next. Waypoints are beacons that can be linked back home to make bridges between each other, allowing for quick traversal once the resources are available. You can quickly revisit old islands, but you need to work to unveil newer onesTo put it another way, you prepare expeditions and set out into the world to unravel its secrets. Honestly though, forget the secrets. For people like me, the fun’s in the preparations, with the pay off being the utility provided to you by your items. Later in the game, efficient usage of the waypoint charms will allow you to quickly traverse known areas while ferrying some resources back home. The torch helps me purify particularly infested islands, and I can use a charm to bother my friend with an eternal night. I can use a wind charm to reach distant locations, and extend my journey with a few health potions. There are a good many gadgets, and it always pays to have the right ones on hand.The combat is simple and it works well enough. You pick up weapons that come in two flavors: melee and ranged. Melee weapons are further split into one and two handed variants. That said, all melee weapons function the same, with weapon type changing attack speed and range. To fight, you’ve got a basic attack, charge attack, block, and dodge. Notably, you can cancel attacks with a block or dodge, and the combat honestly flows quite well. Supplementing your melee weapons are some ranged ones which all work a little differently, but it all works together to empower the player when attacking groups of enemies. Past that, the numbers are quite reasonable. Enemies have limited kits, and go down in a small number of hits, often falling in a one or two to a charged attack.The mist and nettles come with shades of a few shapes and sizes. While the mist is it’s own thing and the nettles don’t normally defend themselves, the shades will try to kill the player and the drakes. That said, you find every enemy in the game in the first two areas (this may have changed in recent updates).Overall though, the combat’s pretty good. It’s typically fast, and I’d never really call it unfair. While there aren’t many different types of enemies, the combat isn’t used to the point where it becomes too big an issue.The native residents of Drake Hollow are naturally Drakes. Not like dragons; similar to mandrakes. Anyhow, they’ve been having a rough go of things with the mist, nettles, and shades, and have been forced into hiding. Your job is to track them down, send them to your island, and help them grow. In return, they heal your wounds, bring you gifts, and grant you some of their powers.While exploring, you’ll find various types of resources which can be used to construct a base. At first your camp is just a handful of sleeping bags, a pot of stew, and some dolls. With the help of the drakes you can assemble your resources into some walls to stall the shades and more permanent structures to keep your drakes healthy. While you can’t really make your island a work of art, the system is very easy to utilize for making a nice compound, and has enough depth to keep things interesting. You’re always unlocking new structures, and occasionally need to save up for larger improvements.While these systems aren’t really special on their own, the home base is really one of the highlights of this game. My friend and I were always thinking about what would come next or how to better expand it to support more drakes. Past that, it was just so convenient. It was linked to newly explored areas, and could be used to store and restock supplies. All in all, I’d say it was very well done in the way that it enables other aspects of the game.The main story is typically conveyed through a few short cutscenes and comic panels. The player appears to be a troubled teen who is called by the crow to Drake Hollow’s aid. And so you meet the playful little drakes. The panels convey the passage of time in the world left behind, and the playful expressions of the drakes. The panels give the world a ton of color, despite the lack of a very coherent plot.Drake Hollow used to be a bit livelier in the past with a witch and a band of hunters, both of which leaving behind notes detailing their journeys. I never found all the notes. Maybe I’m missing something, but frankly, I wasn’t very concerned with either party. As far as I’m concerned, they’re both long gone, with any remnants of them failing to influence my journey in any meaningful way. The notes, short, far, and few between, just aren’t worth the trouble to track down and make sense of. Though there are a fair few notes, most fail to say anything meaningful without context. It didn’t seem worth the time to track them all down.The panels are a nice treat when you get them, but there aren’t many. That said, the writing is mostly an opt-in thing and keeps from holding back the rest of the game. What counts is that the parts the player is forced to sit through, the panels, are very well done.It’s not perfect, but Drake Hollow’s pretty good, especially if you’ve got a buddy to play it with. The game has a great system for exploration, even if there isn’t much special out there. The combat’s not half bad, and the base building’s honestly pretty good. The writing’s unintrusive at worst, and there’s no point where you really have to grind to progress. All in all, I liked it.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite disappointed. I expected a lot more coming from the creators of The Flame in the Flood. The game feels extremely slow, limited, empty and unpolished.First off, the number and variety of things you can build in your camp is limited by the number of drakes you have and their level. You end up having to run around forever to look for new drakes or crystals to make them level up in order to be able to build. It's extremely painful at the beginning of the game. I played for two hours, was sitting on a pile of components but was barely able to build anything durable because I could not level up my drakes.The game wants you to run from island to island to collect resources. The issue here is that there is very little to see on said islands. The resources are found in "containers" which are just the same asset (with like 3 variations) that you have to hit to make goodies pop out. Then you have to run around spamming E to collect everything. There is a few buildings to visit but there is really nothing interesting to see as the game throw resources at you in an unordered fashion. You don't even know what the things you collect are used for. The feeling of exploration dies out pretty fast.You can store your resources in a central "chest" (painfully if I may add, as it was designed for a controller and not for keyboard&mouse), but not all menu allow you to draw from this chest. For example, you will have to slowly take out each resource you want to sell. There is also no sort option. It becomes very difficult very fast to know what you have and pretty annoying to take things out.Inventory management is pretty important in open-world building game and the ball was definitely dropped on this one.Interacting with the world is also quite annoying. Everything ask you to hold the E key and is very nit-picky hitbox-wise. For example, you have to regularly collect resources from your drakes in order to build. To get them, you have to go to your drake and hold E next to it. If two drakes are overlapping, you can start praying. Then an animation plays in to zoom on your drake. If the drake is currently doing something, you have to wait for it to finish its animation (eating, playing with its leaves, etc.). Then a menu finally pops up and you can click on a button to collect the resources. And that's only for one drake. Believe me, it becomes tedious real fast.I suppose(/hope) that there are ways to simplify this process later on, but it feels like this was designed to make you waste time and create a false sense of "relationship" with your drakes.Finally the fighting is extremely stiff. I won't talk in depth about it as it wasn't what draw me to the game in the first place, but it definitely doesn't feel polished.All in all, this game doesn't feel like a finished product. It feels like an early access console game that got poorly ported on PC. It is definitely not worth its price tag. The game is going to need a lot of updates to become pleasant to play. Until then, I would just look for something else to play or for a heavy discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game. Having played for a bit with a buddy, we've already progessed through the second stage of islands (Summer).  Quite enjoyable to find better weapons as your traverse the game. Combat is a bit rugged so you have to be a bit more strategic with fighting enemies.  On the second group of islands, you'll find the short bow. It's quite possibly the best ranged weapon in the game and can one shot the Fangs (wolf like ranged enemies).  A few tips getting started.  1.  Be sure you locate the lighthouse and activate the beacon on the top of the lighthouse to display on your map where all slumbering drakes are for that group of islands.  2.  Be very selective with which drakes you level up. There are some really nice buffs you can get early on such as improved item find, fire DOT, and Sprint speed increase.  There is no autosave that I can see. When going thru the tutorial, you'll receive a notification in game when you unlock multiplayer.  BE SURE TO SAVE YOUR GAME before joining friends!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it and returned it. This game sat on my wishlist for months and looked really promising. When I got it however, it felt very early access, short and pretty buggy. For example, when I built anything it would vanish within seconds of moving away from the base. I rebuilt several times and got frustrated that I was making no progress. The combat could be fun, but is really clunky as is. I wanted to like the art style, but as I played it seemed really dated and didn't draw me in. I love the premise of this game, but it's not ready to buy yet. This could easily be worth the $30 price if things were fixed and polished and if so I will happily purchase this again. I don't want to discourage anyone from the game that has this much potential, but wait for a major update before you shell out.

_childDocuments_.review: This recommendation is a "slight dislike". The game has promise, but fails in a few ways to make it good enough for the pricetag at this moment.When you start the game, it feels as if you are progressing fast and that you have options in how you want to play and build your base. You think that exploring new islands other than your starting island is gonna be fun and you'll find new things as you do. This however, is not the case. You need to explore islands to get the exact same resources from every new island. The drakes (your "villagers" if you will) need crystals to level up.This is where the game takes a turn. Your drakes require more food/water/entertainment as they level up. You need to level up drakes to level up your camp, and you need to level up your camp to progress and get more "budget". You cannot build as many buildings as you want because of this budget. So, it becomes a balancing act to build food/water/entertainment/defense to sustain your base, while your drakes do not really do anything but harvest a random berry bush every now and then. You cannot build as you want, only as the game allows you to, making it a linear, boring prospect of gathering materials and crystals to progress into more issues.And as if the grind for materials isn't enough, the game caps your inventory at 250 items arbitrarily. So you cannot explore and grind materials freely, but have to return to base or drop loot on the ground.This game has potential, if the devs would cut the shackles they put on players and increase the difficulty of the wave defense that happens every now and then. Right now getting raided is more a matter of "ah, I am gonna need materials to repair this afterwards" because they attack from three different directions and your defenses cannot make up for that, if you don't want your drakes to starve.
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, drake hollow is a bundle game. if you get it for free, it's worth giving a shot. heck, i'm (currently very close) to beating it, but it's not finished. its FAR from finished. I would go so far as to say not a single mechanic is fully fleshed out, from the severe lack in enemy variety, the janky combat, the base building introducing mechanics only for them to be irrelevant 5 minutes later, to the fact that there is ONE SINGULAR BOSS.The game is fun, but in it's current stage it's an "early" early access game that just does not have enough content to justify paying any sort of money for it. I really wish they kept working on it, the game could have been great, but its abandoned and will never be even close to a finished game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think of this game as early game fortnite "save the world edition" with less building, less resource management and clever design inclusions. _childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Drake Hollow is a pleasant enough game to play, though it is lacking in substance.Your weapons are only found, you cannot buy or craft them, and their rarity level depends on your camp level, They also degrade like biscuits left out in the rain.Your camp is the only location where you can really find any "life" in the game, because you can take down everything without losing any resources, so you can build the town set up you want, which is good.The NPCs might aswell have been statues, for all the interaction you have with them.The cut-scenes are top notch, and perhaps the best thing about this game, which is not a good thing.The gameplay loop is very repetitive, and while there are some nice tid-bits of lore to be found around the various islands, they are (like nearly everything) randomized. So there is little rhyme or reason to them.My conclusion is that Drake Hollow feels like an early access game that got released too soon, and I suggest that you practice caution before buying it. Wait for a sale if you absolutely must have it, or wait untill there's extra content for it.The story lasts only for 10 hours, if you try to get a good bunch of the drakes and level your camp to max, and there is no free play after.TL:DR Don't buy, wait for sale, or more content.

_childDocuments_.review: I am in love with this game. From the aesthetics to the combat hands down this game will suck you in. What a world to immerse yourself in. I loved clearing realms with my friend and building up my base and drakes over the seasons. We beat the story, which truth be told is a bit weak but present nonetheless, and now Im playing endless mode where I think this game truly shines. Im just about to beat my first year and go back to a spring realm with a fully built awesome looking base and I couldnt be happier. Some minor issues from time to time glitch wise nothing game breaking just a momentary minor issue that went away like a character getting stuck between a rock or something. Plays great the music is amazing but repetitive after so much time, just put on some lofi and melt away into this world. The combat reminds me of the old zelda games and the base building is unlike anything Ive seen. Although not very deep its beautiful and amazing. The fun in the game is learning it, building to the top, of course once youve done that it becomes repetitive, but thats any game really, and with the maps being randomized each realm theres a bit of replay-ability, especially with the higher difficulties and permadeath mode, which I wanna try still.   As someone with high anxiety I can recommend this game as a release it really helped me. Please get this game while its on sale like me its ABSOLUTELY worth $15 in my opinion. Def play this with your friends! Check out The LOST Joker on twitch and youtube thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - I think the idea here was a good one, but the Devs just didn't have the technical know how to actually make a game. The game is fine if you get it on sale (i got it for half off). Otherwise, maybe avoid.If you have ever played Pikmin, you get the basic story of the game. Cute plant things in this weird world that you need to save / grow in order to prosper. Honestly Pikmin did it better because you actually USE the Pikmin whereas in this the Pikmin just give you a buff while causing chaos with their insatiable lust for Hi-C, cabbage, and balls. Each "season" is a bunch of islands that you explore and eventually after leveling your camp up you move to the next season. You don't really get any base defense buildings until the second season, which means the bulk of the early game is just... wandering. The mechanics are rough, to put it lightly. You will constantly battle with infinitely falling just by stepping on a rock wrong. The same rock you need to walk on to get that blueprint you need. These are the sorts of things that should have been fixed during the making (or even year after release) but just weren't? Honestly it just felt like the people making this game were not good at programming or design. Like, great ideas, but the jankiest implementation I have seen in a hot minute.

_childDocuments_.review: Drake Hollow is really close to being a decent game. I'm mostly putting "not recommended" because it feels like an early access game, and after "beating" the game with 3 other people, I was given an extremely anticlimactic ending. Pros:- Great art.- Interesting ideas. The game offloads the typical "hunger/water/sanity" survival game thing onto your base and the creatures that you take care of, and it's a really cool take on the genre. Instead of constantly needing to find yourself resources, you have to make sure your base produces enough and that you come back every now and then to maintain that. - Mostly-flawless coop implementationCons:- Shallow systems. Every mechanic in Drake Hollow has very little depth. Combat is a really straightforward 3-hit combo that you generally can spam over and over again. Almost all enemies can be beaten by just running up and repeating. The drakes seem cool, but they're all basically the same creature with the same needs that give various boring stat buffs. Base building is just "put more of X production up" when you are getting low. - Combat variety in general is... bad. There are like 4 (?) types of enemies, and their AI is extremely basic. There was never once in our 7 hour playthrough that I felt challenged.- Along those same lines, the "boss" monster that you fight is the same enemy with no changing attack patterns for the entire game. You fight him like 6 times. You'd think that the final battle of the game would be something interesting... but no, it's the same dude, you just wail on him like normal and he dies in less than a minute. - The game's UI feels weirdly awkward. The button that opens the "build stuff" items is the same as the "craft items", but you have to hit Tab to switch between them. Placing some important tools (like waypoints) is super awkward since you have to look down at where you want to place them, but that prevents you from seeing whether you're in range of another waypoint. The menus are weirdly organized. - Item clutter. You get SO many random crafting items, but you don't ever think "oh I need X item". There are a billion items and each one seems to be used for 1 or 2 things. Overall, the game feels unfinished. It feels like they needed another year of dev time to really turn this into a better game, but then ran out of money. They are still working on it, but it's unclear what their roadmap is.The game is... OK fun for a group to play. I didn't hate my time with it, but I wouldn't go back.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful spooky cute game, the mandrakes are endering and lovable, also really helpful sometimes giving gifts and their obtainable buffs are vital. building camp is really easy and the managment side is easy while being a nice challenge to overcome. exploring is Awesome each map is randomly put together selection of islands, the landscapes are beautiful and dashing back to camp surfing the waypoint lines is SO much more fun then fast traveling in most other games. there is a way to teleport back to camp but it's tempered by needing to craft that item which i like. the looting and pick up sounds are punchy and satisfying and though the game isn't difficult mastering the control scheme is a challenge and i hope they put together a good tutorial later on. cause i had no idea i could dash till i hit left control on accident and darted in a direction. _childDocuments_.review: I could say much more about this game here but i will name the biggest reasons i finally called it quits.Even in the first of apparently several stages the game gives the player NOWHERE NEAR enough food to keep your little sprouty plant guys sated in the least. I have had a similar problem with other games of this kind where trending to the player characters needs was just a chore, same is true here, just for the creatures you are trying to care for. Even with a fast travel network that went all over the available territory and scrounching for food constantly there were simply never enough resources to sate all the little creatures. Combat is bad and it seems more constructed along the line of "other games with combat have a dodge, so we need a dodge, other games have a block so we need a block". No element of the combat really fits together and there is no flow, only yank. Most obvious though, that the team had no idea what they were doing are the enemies themselves. Their speeds and reach simply does not fit with the movement you as the player have at hand and exceeds the players ability to react to attacks and movements. Half the players hits go into emptiness or are outright countered by most creatures attacks due to this. Some attacks enemies can wind up and hit the player while the player is still mid swing. Any horde encounter ends in the player running in circles and hoping for a moment to get some hits in without being spammed to death. As i said there are much more problems here that the pretty visuals and the neat style can't make up for.And the endpoint is that i lament the potential and wished i had not spend the money on the game that i did.Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game and I'm glad that I got it while it was on sale. It has some really cool and unique ideas such as the connecting of the waypoints as both a supply pipeline and a fast travel of sorts. The drakes are also super cute. My biggest complaint is that there is a ton of repetition. Once I completed the first area and moved on to the second I was really hoping for new enemies and a new environment but it pretty much ended up being more of the same. The raids also become tiring because it becomes a rinse and repeat of the same enemies, just higher level and more of them, defend your base, repair, every 30 minutes. It went from "Oh no! An incoming raid!" to *eyeroll* " an incoming raid" whenever I was out and about.Overall I have enjoyed the game. It has flaws and I don't think I would have paid full price for it but if you can catch it on a sale I would say it is definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hoped it was like a Grounded game, but nope. At the first look it looks great, but after a few hours its pretty boring.Combat system is really lame. You can not move while atack, dodge is also limited (like 1-2 sec cd). If you dodge 1st atack and get behind the enemy, he will charge his atack, instant turn around 180° and hits you. There is also delay for dodge while atacking (after 2nd or 3d atack combo you can not instant dodge). There are only 3 type of enemies (4 including small Bosses). A lot of weapons, but they all do the same, maybe some of them are a bit faster.Everything you do is moving from island to island, connecting trucks for resourses, killing the corrupted nodes and each island has like from 10 up to 50 (even small ones having like 30 nodes, totaly stupid), getting pretty annoying after a while. Upgrade your base and suply your dudes with food/water/entertaiment. Every 30min there will be a raid atack on your base and you have to defend it. After you visit those islands (or finish a quest), you move your base to another place with the same random islands and do the same again.There is no tutorial, how to do this or that (or maybe there was, but short and dissapeared fast, so if you didnt take attention, you have no option to see it again). For example, when I build the energy station I had no clue how to connect it to another stations. Only after trying everything out I got it, you have to press X, then press E on that station and choose options to connect.There are few more small things that are a bit annoying. Movement is slow, camera is to close to character, on every action you have to press and hold E (I really hate this mechanic in all games). Like your dude's running away and you want to talk with him, when the dialog "press E" poping up and you press, its kinda getting stucked because your dude is still running away and the dialog dissapears. So you have to hold E while runing behind him at the same time. There is no option for taking loot automaticly, that means you have to press and/or hold E every time you get something dropped.All the items are hidden in the same button, weapons in 1 and 2, and items in 3. So to chose what you need, you have to press that button many times till you get it (kinda carousel UI).At the end I was kinda disappointed of that game.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said: Get it on sale.-------------------------EDIT AFTER 100% COMPLETION:I just have two things to add after completing this game:1. Several reviews online have referred to this game as "the next Fortnite: Save the World". As a long time STW player with hundreds of hours logged in that game, I think the comparison is simply laughable and, reading these online reviews, it made me suspect these are either paid reviews, or the reviewers are affiliated with the dev. This game is NOT Save the World and it's not even close. The replayability here is almost non-existent. While the game is fun, if it's a STW experience you're looking for, just play STW. This might seem weird to point out in a review for a different game than STW, but seeing as the comparison is not only being made online, but this game is being praised as "the next STW", I feel this needs to be addressed here.2. If you're an achievement hunter, prepare to keep track of the in game collectibles, as they are bugged and can cost you hours to go back and search after finishing the game (I simply used screenshots and a checklist to mark what notes I found and on which islands). Notes ARE still bugged (you can read more about how in the numerous guides that are available for this game)-------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW: A bit grindy and there are some bugs with collectibles but other than that it's fine, enjoying the game even though it does start to feel like one of those games I'll probably never finish let alone 100%, because of the randomized and (sometimes) bugged collectibles. I wasted 2 hours trying to find the last note I needed on the first map, that honestly killed my momentum and it kinda went downhill from there.Still, the mechanics and combat are fun, so if you don't care about achievements, you'll probably really enjoy this without many downsides

_childDocuments_.review: The base of the game is fine and if you only do a zone per sessions which is about an hourish each doing all the story and grabbing all the little Drakes and other collectables it's fine. The game starts to come apart at the seams near the end with some different story elements and the base building system becoming increasingly frustrating from stuff being useless or unbalanced to flat out broken. For 6-8 hours of gameplay I would wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to give this title a positive review, LOVE to, but with the state of the game as of this moment I can't recommend it. I may edit the review for a more favorable one if the current problems are addressed, however.What was once a fun survival/base defense in the same vein as OG Fortnite (or as it's known now, Fortnite Save the World) now feels like a gamble to play with the latest content patch. It's possible to lose your character, and all their tied progress, which is an even bigger issue given that the game has a campaign mode that requires steady base development, player progression, grinding, exploration etc. I've also now encountered a problem where Options are locked, no matter what I do, and it can be well and annoying to deal with since combat does in fact require a degree of skill and awareness. Further exasperated by the fact that you can't bind your own keys. Something I was semi-okay with, even with some bizarre button layout decisions, but now with the other restrictions and risks of the newer bugs, this feels even more uncomfortable.Mainly I'd at least like a bit of a more proactive or communicative approach from Molasses Flood. I loved their previous game, I was digging this one, and I was happy, even proud to support a growing dev as we need more like them. but when there is what feels to be a limited/canned or nonexistent response to bugs and suggestions, I'd be a bit less enthusiastic about future titles or recommending this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Still busy with my first few hours, but what brilliant hours those have been so far; from the sense of the world, the story and the aesthetic, immersive and mesmerising; combat feels slick and engaging... will update was I get further into the campaign :) Well done The Molasses Flood.Edit: After a few more great hours with the game, I continue to well recommend this game. I've been playing through it with my partner (the co-op opens up after a short bit of opening narrative and gameplay) and we've been having a stellar time. It is a brilliant blend of many genres, bit of survival, bit of base building, bit of exploration, bit of third-person action adventure, and it all comes together seamlessly. The aesthetic remains sublime and the world feels very much its own place and fits the tone and conceit of the narrative remarkably well. The story itself unfolds slowly through quests and finding letters left in the world from its previous inhabitants - I'm keen to see how it unfolds.It is my great hope that Drake Hollow sells well enough for us to either see a sequel or expanded story content DLC - the foundation of this game is so strong, I would love to see it thrive for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously boring. You have to collect junk and food to keep your village drakes fed. They bumble around waiting to be attacked. You explore islands and hack at weeds to dispel the "evil" influence in the area, while being vigilant of attacks. There's literally nothing to do except collect junk around the islands and hope you have enough to build something new in your village, before it gets torn down again. My biggest complaint is the lack of a consistent Hit Box for enemies. I've hacked at enemies and plants repeatedly, up close, at different angles, and only occasionally ever hit them. It makes for very frustrating gameplay. Save your money and your time. This game is garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a great single player game, maybe fun with friends or a group.  The scarcity of resources makes this feel like a slog way too early and the drops are RNG driven... even in the starting island.   I see the mechanics there that could make it more interesting but i'm constantly struggling for resources so I can't get to them quickly enough for the game to truly grab me.  I could probably do a custom game or open multiplayer but that doesn't interest me and seems lame for a tutorial level.   I was a few hours in and i restarted to see if i could get better luck with drops my second time around.  I got better luck of course but RNG this early on really turns me off to the title.  There's also  a lot of Jenk with the controls.  Jumping is sloppy and delayed, the combat is attack or block for melee or shoot a range weapon.  There's a ground slam but not as usefull as it sounds.  THere's also no consistency in how the controls behave when interacting with NPCs or items.  Hold to activate, tap to activate,  release to activate... it feels like the game can't decide how you should control it.    Overal;: Frustrating, Grindy, Jenky, RNG and not a good play solo.

_childDocuments_.review: I brought this game to play on a whim with some friends didn't know about the game till about 20 mins before purchase and overall so far it's been a pretty solid experience.Pros:The stylised artwork suits the game and the drakes have really cute interactions around the camp.The game is fairly intuitive however if you manage to miss/forget something you can check the log.The game appears to be well optimised i haven't experienced any frame drops or lighting errorsThe menus/UI is intuitive and is easy to navigate.Cons:The Default keyboard/mouse bindings are not the best but you can rebind however I would recommend a controller. In multiplayer, the loot isn't shared meaning you may miss the chance to get new weapons if someone gets there before you. this also means when your friends load in for the first time you're going to have to drop weapons for themYou cannot return to a map once you have left it so make sure to fully explore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far the most adorable thing I've seen, but it still manages to be terrifying. Hit dodge/block and shoot with your preferred thing.The loop of exploration is what brings joy. But be warned, if you're hoping for evolving gameplay, it's unlikely to be found here.

_childDocuments_.review: A difficult thumbs up. It's s thumb sideways. The inventory system is flawed. I picked up a ton of stuff on 3 islands. Then I tried to pick up a new broom weapon and it said I had too many melee weapons. I realized I had 2 pool cues and 2 hatchets. I dropped one of each. It still refused to pick up the broom saying I had too many melee weapons even though I had 2 open slots. They need a buyback option at the store. I accidentally sold the jade jewel because I thought I was buying it. Then I realized I couldn't get it back. Once it's sold, it's EFFING GONE. The next goal was to upgrade one of the drakes. I couldn't. I had to go everywhere looking for more gems/jewels.  I am so SICK AND TIRED of having to micromanage other characters. You have to ensure you constantly bring back food and provide entertainment and food, water and sleeping/beds for the drakes. i HATE incompetent NPC's. I really do.Early on, I found a foam #1 finger and learned it was a weapon that does great damage. I somehow lost it. No idea how. It just wasn't in my inventory at one point.   Those are the primary negatives. The positives. The character design is ok. Nothing special. it appears you can find clothes to use on the islands. They do nothing for you so they're pointless. At least they don't take up your inventory space. It's essentially a tower defense game disguised as a open world RPG. Every time you leave to explore ANYWHERE, the bad guys attack your base which is a long ways away so you're SPRINTING back and wasting the jewels that allow you to walk through the mist. It appears there's a way to connect light beams from "supply trucks" but it's given me ZERO tutorial how to use them. I think it's supposed to be a fast transit function like you use the light beam to ride back to the base island faster. Haven't been able to use it yet. Again..it's a difficult thumbs up.  It plays well, has no serious graphics issues, it DID crash 2 times on me but I knew the second time to save often.
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun multiplayer game with nice graphics.  Keeping the Drakes alive early on is a bit difficult especially when they don't have the food and water needed to survive and you are constantly getting raided preventing you to go look for food on the other islands for long stretches of time.  I've lost 4 Drakes in our first play through and couldn't get past the 20/20 flashing message to build a well, but I did figure out the waypoint glide system which is pretty cool to get around the islands.  Overall a good game with some very challenging survival elements (for the Drakes not you).
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Drake Hollow is a very relaxing coop survival base-builder with great artstyle and simple gameplay loop: explore the map, collect resources and free drakes, return to your base and build to defend and care for the drakes. There's some increase in complexity as you progress but it never gets bogged down in too many mechanics. While this means that it may not be a game to sink your teeth into for hundreds of hours, if you're a fan of the survival/base-builder genre, this game is perfect for chill weeknight gaming sessions, especially playing in coop.Drake Hollow has an interesting twist on the survival genre where you need to manage hunger and thirst (and entertainment) not for yourself, but for the drakes that you take care of and defend. In return, drakes that are well taken care of give you resources to further build your base and they will also directly contribute to the upkeep and defence of your base.My main gripe with the game is that it doesn't explain the base mechanics very well, for example how much of the base item limit meter each building piece takes up, or the function of some pieces (e.g. there isn't an explanation in the build menu for what the bunker does, you need to build it to find out which can be a bit annoying early in the game when you're low on resources). The music is very soothing and the animations, especially for the drakes interacting with the environment, are top-notch. It's clear that the developers put a lot of heart into the audiovisual design. The travel system is super fun and the various weapons are charming and thematic (melee weapons are items like guitars, pizza paddles, coat racks).
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like the story and nothing felt meaningful. Game looks visually nice but doesn't really tell good story even if it seems nice and interesting at first. _childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up as something I could enjoy with my spouse and we absolutely love it. That said, it is a survival game and it does not slack on making you understand the need to be skilled in combat, thoughtful of resource use, and smart about how you set up your camp which houses your precious drakes. I really appreciate that death does not meet harsh punishment - we play this to have fun after work/school/homework so I rely on games that don't add stress to my day and this game is challenging without being brutal. It has minor glitches here and there, but thus far we have not found anything game-breaking. The areas are fun to explore, the game is beautiful, and I highly recommend it especially as a co-op experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Six hours in and I have to say this is a wonderful and charming game. You build up a central base with little Drakes that require food and water to keep going. Your base is subject to periodic attacks by monsters. There is a storyline that you get from a very nice Talking Crow and by finding notes left around the islands you explore. Exploration is both for gathering resources and finding new Drakes. You can set up a custom railway using Waypoints, which make traveling much faster and more efficient. All around this game scratched the same itch for me that Slime Rancher did, but with slightly higher stakes. I love the silly weapons and the outfit changes. I love the exploration and the surprise ambushes. Are there issues? Sure, I'd love to rebind keys and change my FoV. But a lot of the complaints I've seen have nothing to do with the very sweet gameplay loop this game has going. For those who find clearing the vines on islands tiresome: Invest in some St. Elmo's Fire. Get your life together.

_childDocuments_.review: Intended to just sit for the evening and play a mindless game but I have to say - the 4 hours current play time was all in one sitting. Nothing too hard to overcome though, not at all! Definitely give it a go if you're curious. It's worth the money for me.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A fun base building exploration game with beautifully crafted islands to explore with a unique story and an almost perfect combat system.After playing through the main campaign and a lot of endless exploration mode, I can say this is a pretty fun game with just a few flaws/annoyances that don't really take any fun away from the game.I love the base building, exploration and Drake collecting aspect of the game. Building up your bases defenses to the point that you barely need to do any work yourself during a raid is a great feeling once you get there. The Drake are adorable and there a good variety of appearance between the different kinds. The buffs they give you are cool and seeing how they change as you age them up is very nice. The combat is pretty decent for the most part. The art style is great and the Islands look amazing and are really fun to explore. I was a little bummed out when I got to the 4th biome only to find out that was the last one. I wanted to keep on going. So After finishing the main campaign I started up a new Endless Hollow game. I'm okay with the biomes being hand crafted specifically for the story, but I feel like in Endless Hollow mode they should really be randomly generated. It would give the game much more replayability. The said, the islands in the biomes are very well crafted and great to explore, and in Endless Hollow I've just made it to the 4th biome, so I'm not really quite sure what happens after that or if they start being randomly generated/just new biomes specifically made for Endless Hollow (Will update my review once I get passed the 4th biome)Now just a few annoyances about the game. The combat can be a bit wonky at times due to how the auto lock works. I some times find myself attacking something i wasn't even looking at, or hitting a tree instead of an enemy in the middle of a fight, so you really want to make sure to you "F" to lock on to specific targets at times when there is a lot around you. Most of the weapons are fine, however I find the nail gun doesn't work as well as it could. I find it feels like the nails go through enemies some times and the nails never really go where I think they are gonna go, and some times it won't fire right away after reloading. Other than that have not had any issues with the other weapons. The attack animations are annoying some times as well since while you are in an attack animation you cannot dodge to get out of it, leaving you vulnerable to attack. The one big annoyance I have with the combat is the fact that EVERY time you get you get knocked back, and can't do anything while in the knockback animation. I can deal with it most times, but it is awful when you are in an ambush with tons of Gnats, one slip and the projectiles to Gnats shoot will send you bouncing all over the place with no way for you to stop it expect for mashing your jump and dodge button in hopes that you do it just at the right time not to get hit again.Overall a really fun exploration and base building game with just some flaws in the combat mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: A lot to love about this game. Charming art style, nice music, fun combat, fun exploration. This game has a fascinating world that I feel compelled to explore. I think my only major complaint was that I found the recurring raids annoying at first. They popped up every once in a while and distracted me from what I enjoyed most, exploration. But then I found the robust gameplay modifiers menu that let me play the game how I wanted! I turned those off entirely and now I can let myself get wrapped up in this world while exploring. So I really appreciate that I'm allowed to engage with the game on my own terms. And even without the raids, I find the base building part of the game engaging. I enjoy building up a village for my little friends, and always having that goal in mind while exploring and scavenging.Also something I'm personally happy about is that this game feels similar to Fragile Dreams in some ways. An older game that's an all time favorite of mine. Ever since I completed it I've been looking for another game that can scratch that itch. Not quite the same thing Fragile Dreams was going for with the heavier emphasis on story/cutscenes in that game, but while exploring I got a similar sense of loneliness and longing that I felt was very effective. So if you're familiar with that game, take that for what you will.

Once you get Ballistas, it lightens up.With each map, theres more and more resources so the resource grind feels lighter.X (info) is your friend. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of charm and good ideas, but odd quirks and repetition really hold it back. It can be fun to play with friends and I  recommend it at $10 or less, but I beat it in less than 15 hours despite clearing out every single island. The time spent to beat it is fairly short, but the biggest kick is how anti-climactic the ending is, as well as the fact that you must start a new game in Sandbox Mode to play endlessly. If the game put you into Endless Mode after the campaign it might have some staying power just to work on the base building aspects and hunt for cosmetics, but you'll easily be at max for what you can put in the base by the end of the campaign and it just isn't worth starting over to access higher camp tiers hours later.Ultimately, everything about this game is repetitive, too. Combat is very shallow, with two melee movesets that have exactly one 3-hit combo each, a dodge and block mechanic and ranged weapons to shoot. You'll be fighting countless enemies as they respawn any time you set one toe off of an island, and your main objective is to beat weeds to death on each island with your basic combo. It can be relaxing when it isn't stressing you out with a ton of ranged enemies beating you up from all sides as the lock-on mechanic fails to target what you want it to. But even when it's relaxing it's incredibly repetitive. You also have to go back to base every once in a while to fight off a raid of enemies that attack your base, so you'll be interrupted from time to time to do that, too.I wanted very badly to like this game more than I do, but it's just a very shallow game with a beautiful art style. It feels unfinished and unpolished, with strange bugs happening like your Drakes' beds not working in Winter until you destroy them and rebuild them, or power not passing to something until you rebuild it, too. If you can find it in a bundle or get a key on the cheap it could be a fun few afternoons, though.

_childDocuments_.review: MIXED review - literally game in a nutshell:Build central baseFind drakesThe further away from base the harder things are and you have to annoyingly return to base every few hours IN THE MIDDLE OF MISSIONS to fight off bad guys from baseSUPER disruptive, I'll be clearing an island and then have to go all the way back to base to defend then spend resources and time going back to where I left off.Very annoying after awhile. After you clear and area you're reward with even more islands to clear and farther back and forth from base to defend it to last mission point.Pros - I like the character design and the story felt involved at the beginningthen it turns into a brainless weed extermination mission then going back to base, defend it then treck all the way back to far away mission island. Gets annoying fast.Waiting to see if it gets better, but right now its just weed killing and a lot of traveling back and forth nothing much else...

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot more since my initial review. Gotten used to the default key bindings and am doing much better in combat. Most of the time, I'm out exploring, clearing out the islands of resources. At first it was okay, but it got dull after a while, especially since i'm in the 3rd region now. The map gets larger as you move to a new region, but there's nothing new on the islands. Basically it's rinse and repeat on each island.Combat wise, there's not much variety on the types of enemy. Once I am used to it and got the patterns down, combat became much easier and with the current buffs I have. Vampirism is awesome.Base building wise, I haven't really explored the base defenses options. Using the waypoint circle loop tip, I've been able to handle raids alone. That is the next step I'm trying to explore. I have too much drakes now, and it's getting hard to manage them. In order to retire them, I have to hunt (grind) for crystals, which at this point in the game, I'm tempted to just rush through and finish the game.Recommended? Still a no. There's a bit of grind involved for resources, especially to level up your drakes. Grinding for resources is fine, it makes sense in a base building game. But there is no other content that takes you out of the grind, and it makes me question whether the time was worth it or not.---Initial Review:Pros- Fun if you're playing multiplayerCons- The controls and combat are a bad combination. Dodging is critical to avoiding damage, why is it binded to Left Ctrl? It makes it so awkward to control- cannot change key bindingsI feel like it's so hard to manage fights singleplayer especially when there's a group of enemies. Was trying a hit and run tactic, but the enemies move as fast as you, sometimes faster, and they have better attack range. Not recommended if you are playing single player. The game felt like a MMORPG, with leveling up, grinding resources.

_childDocuments_.review: If I'm being honest... I didn't expect this game to be as much fun as it is. The aesthetic reminded me of Fortnite, already a red flag, but it quickly turned that around with all the thorns and hedges and a general sense of mystique that screeching 10 year old zoomers simply couldn't hope to capture. The gameplay made it even better, the combat is simple but effective, exploration is tense but rewarding, and the cute little plant things are VERY adorable the more buildings you make for them to play with. One thing that might help new players is a little bit more tutorial, especially on things like waypoints and dragging materials out of caches, it took me 6 hours of gameplay to figure out that you could ride on the waypoints after you connect them to each other, I'd been walking the entire distance every time.All in all, the singleplayer experience is absolutely worth it, I don't have friends so look for someone else to tell you about the net code or whatever.

_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I was not expecting this much fun out of this game. I was looking for something to keep my Valheim addiction alive and stumbled across Drake Hollow, and how this game isn't more popular baffles me. _childDocuments_.review: At a glance this seemed like a bunch of different elements thrown together that I love. City building/mangement, open world "check off the task on your map" stuff, basic crafting, and a shockingly decent combat system, but the game just fails to commit in a few too many ways.Aside from the grindy aspects other reviews have mentioned, big problems occur with the death system. When you die, you can just "spirit walk" back to your corpse, allowing you to walk through the harmful fog and cover the entire map, then revive yourself on any island you've been to. I quickly began to use this as a fast travel system, killing myself at the starting island then carrying myself out to where I've been before to save on wards. You can end up setting up beacons which act as a more "normal" travel system, but any sense of discovery is lost when I learn I can just go ghost and look everywhere.Additionally, the game is just not challenging in the slightest, and seems in a rush to move you forward. I hadn't even gone to half of the islands before I was being told "Move to the next season, btw you can never come back to this map!" which doesn't feel good when there was such a focus on finding new stuff and places. Not only will I now have to forgo progression to satiate my curiosity or just abandon it, but I also will just have to abandon what I've already built. Granted it's not much in the first "season" but if I do even twice as much building in the next season, by the time I move to the third I'll have to leave all of that too. It doesn't feel great, and clearly is leaning on multiplayer as a crutch. Worth a play if you got this from humble or can get it cheap, otherwise meh.
_childDocuments_.name: Drake Hollow

_childDocuments_.review: Drake Hollow combines base building, exploration, and survival and colony sim mechanics to create an experience that is very unique and greater than the sum of it's parts and it has little plant creatures that are super adorable.So the game mainly consists of you taking care of these cute little Drakes by building up a base for them and going out and exploring different islands to get new crafting materials, new weapons, and even more Drakes to bring back to your camp.The combat in the game isn't groundbreaking but it is solid enough, the crafting and basebuilding aspects of the game are a little overwhelming at first but eventually they make sense, and the exploration is very fun especially with the rail systems you can create between islands that allow you to travel really fast.The game has a really satisfying gameplay loop honestly and some survival games can get really annoying with the hunger and thirst mechanic but this game isn’t too bad at all honestly with all the things you have to do to take care of your Drakes.Also playing this game co-op makes it a lot more fun as well.So if you are a fan of colony sims, base builders, or survival or exploration games, or you just find these adorable drakes adorable I would highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that looks promising, but unfortunately disappoints after a short play time.The idea and the performance itself are charming, many solutions like for example: fast traveling between waypoints, or ghost walking after death, are pretty cool, I can't say that they are not. All that idea about defending and helping veggies looks good as well.But yeah after few first quest and when the joy of exploring few nearest islands finish, true face of the game appear. Getting correct crystal according to the veggies what you got take some time, food is constantly lacking doesn't matter how much time you spend on scavenging or gathering, all ways to make food at the base finish faster then you could expect (planted 3 full garden, went 4 island more far, come back, and nothing was left.) Lack of crystals which allow you to pass through water. The worst fact is that game force you to brainless grind of materials. All islands mechanic looks pretty the same, go kill X vines, kill X enemies to get a chest, jump on the roof to get unlock scroll. All in all, the game got a lot of potential, but devs needs to discover it and use it correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game.I will say, it is far more fun to play with a friend, but it can definitely be fun alone. I have a completionist attitude, so I find it very cathartic to go from island to island, clearing out vines and enemies and looting everything there is to loot. I don't find the game difficult at all, though I will say it is best to not level up your Drakes too fast unless you have a wealth of materials and schematics to immediately improve your base with.I will say I haven't paid much attention to the story line or the notes scattered around, as I don't feel they add much to the game. To me, the fun is all in exploring, clearing islands, growing my drakes, and improving my base. Combat is easy enough that it also takes a back seat.I would say the game feels like a very relaxed, calm, and fun version of The Forest - something children might enjoy, or something an adult like myself might have a lot of fun with relaxing and playing with a close friend or more.Definitely pick it up if you can!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun! Perhaps a bit opaque in terms of direction (the first bits of tutorial are solid, but I feel it could have explained certain mechanics better), but it's an enjoyable game with friends. Some people seem to have issues with the combat system- in my opinion, I feel that while I understand their criticisms towards it, I don't feel it's nearly as bad as they make it seem. It can be frustrating to get hit by an enemy when, due to no fault of your own, the block action is too slow, but the more I played the easier it was to understand the timing of combat and find better ways to approach enemies. I wonder if a lot of people are getting stuck at what felt like the 'midway' point to me- food starts seeming scarce, and your weapons start looking a little sad. The solution for us was to just continue forging forward on the unexplored islands, and lo and behold, much better weapons and food (seeds) started to become more plentiful. A key element as well is to make sure you do not upgrade the Drakes (feeding them crystals) too fast for your camp to keep up with! Leveling up the Drakes does provide nice new bonuses for both you and your camp (such as more player health and unlocking new possible items), but if you go at it too quickly you might find yourself struggling to take care of them adequately :) the game does warn you of this, but it's easy to miss the message!All in all, I really am enjoying this game so far, have put about 4.5 hours into it :) It's definitely fun with a good friend or two, and it's really good if you are into crafting/scavenger style games with a pleasing aesthetic! Maybe not the *best* combat system around, but at least it's simple rather than overly complicated in that department! Also, the respawn features are pretty generous as well (your friends can revive you, you can revive yourself at camp with the penalty of loss of some weapon duration, or you can Spirit Walk to your own corpse to revive yourself at the spot you died. Spirit Walking is not so bad, the walking speed is quite fast compared to normal, and you cannot be hurt/there is no time limit. Only downside to it is if you had not truly 'unlocked' the island you died at, you'll have to SW to your body and then bring it to the last explored island instead. Again, not difficult or anything, just a bit of extra walking!)

_childDocuments_.review: This game was picked for me and my friends to stream on a weekend and though it was a lot of fun and showed some great promise, there. The game has a passive-collection system in the form of the adorable creatures called "Drakes" who are sadly not decended from Dragons, but that doesn't matter as these little adorable things do a lot of the building everywhere in camp, but you need to craft the amulets yourself for travel between the corruption to each island.Monsters will routinely attack the island and there's so much stuff you can smash apart, collect and such to make back home. Not to mention, if you keep the Drakes well fed, not only will they gather stuff for you, but they'll continue to work and be happy! They also have the chance of finding objects you might find useful, dumping them in the mail box for you to get later.Though we didn't get far, the story certainly had me intrigued. You play as this kid (I assume teenager?) who is on the outskirts of their city, looking back at it and their mobile, having a message from a love interest that says "I think we should see other people" which was an immediate Oof, but we ended up following a magical raven that brings us into the world of the Drake! You are given the task to not only be the guardian of the Drakes, but to also clean up and destroy the corruption that infests this whole world!Now for the technical standpoint:Graphically it has this cute cartoon look that I love and first time seeing a Drake I was just in love with the adorable thing! Oh, forgot to mention they even get you gifts too! Anyway...I found that the game didn't hamper my CPU like previous games I've played for our Saturday game and it worked well with streaming. I don't remember encountering any graphical glitches either.Controls were great, no major issues and buttons were in the appropriate places. It just feels natural to play with a controller which I only do for certain games, usually 3rd person games. I also use a 3rd party controller so if it picked up mine without any issue, it'll certainly be compatible with whatever you have!Multiplayer has one or two issues. When we played it, you weren't allowed to co-op until you completed the tutorial, which is fair enough I guess as the story is highly focused on your journey and it'd be weird if one teenager turned into multiple! We had to look up online how to join as it was never explained straight away, but apparently it's after the tutorial finishes, which is after you activate the Lighthouse. This was a pain as the three of us had to play the game singleplayer for a while before we could finally link up!That said, we were having a lot of fun, but what ended it was when the game crashed. Crashes are not a major deal breaker, especially as after the entire hour it only happened once, but we lost ALL our progress. At first we were confused, wondering why it wasn't auto-saving, but it appears that, again, at the time, it was bugged and you had to make certain that you save because the auto-save was a little tempermental. So we lost all our story progress, all our weapons, buildings and so on, but when exiting I noticed that my character and her level was still there!Stream of Part 1, hopefully more in the future:

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of potential here but they took what seemed like mobile game and stretched it out. There's a nice crafting game going on in there, but the story, going out to islands, clearing them, is quite repetitive. Its ok at first, but becomes a slog later on. You may think things change up, new enemies, new weapons.. nope. Nothing, nada. Same enemies, weapons get a bit stronger, so do the enemies so nothing ever changes. The attacking can be a bit strange, collision detection can miss sometimes, your character does sort of freeze for these really wide attack animations and when surrounded you are just left vulnerable. Also i found many bugs, stuck in some areas of the map as they make u slide off even the slightest of sloped surfaces so you can end up just physically stuck. Game crashed constantly; very annoying, and some enemies would seem to aimbot. I enjoyed the time playing it with my friend but would not go through it alone, was glad when it ended. Its a mobile game at best, very simple, they took a few assets and stretched them thin. Stop doing this with games. DO ti right, or not at all.
