_childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise is a must experience game for new players and fans of the "Tales of" series alike. From the fast paced and flashy combat, to the character moments and party chemistry, I thoroughly enjoyed every moment I spent with this game and it's DLC.  Main Game: 100% DLC: 100% -All Achievements -All Quests and Sub Quests-Max Level Characters-All Skits-Full BestiaryMy Time for 100% Main Game: Around 100 hoursDLC: 25 hours(Your time may vary, I like to make sure to talk to each NPC after big story events, etc.)The main cast of Tales of Arise was, without question, my favorite part of the game, and what I consider to be it's strongest aspect. That's not to say the other aspects are bad, I simply enjoyed the characters THAT much. Each of the games characters go through extensive character arcs and see significant developement throughout the entirety of the story. I was always happy to get new skits, whether they be for important character moments, or simply R and R between the characters. While I enjoy all of the games characters, Alphen and Shionne easily shine through as my favorites. I felt that the growth and character work between them was incredibly well done, This group of characters has easily taken center stage as one of my favorite fictional casts.Tales of Arise is an Action JRPG, that gives you quite a bit of freedom to play as you choose. There are 6 party members in total, each of which with their own completely different playstyle and abilities. Don't feel like playing the up close, hack and slash, sword fighter? Switch to the mage, Rinwell, and keep your distance with magic attacks. Want a mix of the two? Switch to the marksman, Shionne, and use guns/bombs/magic to lay waste to the baddies. The best part? Each of the characters have a wide range of abilities allowing you to alter their playstyle and strategies to suit different situations. For example, while Rinwell is a mage, you can still equip her with close combat artes to change her playstyle further based on how you want to play. Something I would highly reccommend to anyone struggling with bosses is; don't be afraid to switch up your party and try new things for different enemies. Also, be sure to pay attention to enemy weaknesses (fire vs. water, etc.).My Specs:-CPU: Ryzen 5 3600x-GPU: Nvidia RTX 2060, Nvidia RTX 4070 (Played some with each of them individually)Visually, Tales of Arise is GORGEOUS. Whether in the bustling city of Viscint, the lush green fields of Menancia, or the depths of one of the games many caves, the game is truly a joy to look at. The game uses Unreal Engine 4 to deliver a very pretty anime art style/asthetic. I would also HIGHLY reccommend using the Arise-SDK mod to increase the games draw distance further. This mod also allows for much greater visual customization as well, so it's definitely worth checking out. I was able to run the game on Ultra settings, with a solid 60+fps, at 1080p-1440p using my 2060. Meanwhile my 4070 easily stayed over 60fps while at 4K resolution. (A quick aside about the SDK mod; If you decide to use it, you may need to find your own sweet spot for the draw distance. Certain areas in the game may stutter a little simply due to the sheer amount of NPCs.)The music in Tales of Arise is FANTASTIC. Each area has its own distinct soundtrack that really helps bring the landscapes/towns to life. After a little time, you'll be able to tell what area your in simply by which orchestral piece is playing. It was always a treat to be visiting an area I hadn't been back to in a while, just to hear a particular theme I really enjoy kick in. The intro/main themes STILL give me goosebumps, and do a really good job of setting the tone for the game.Without delving into spoilers, this games story is an emotional roller coaster. You may see some of the twists coming, but for every one you expect, there is another that will blindside you. The main plot revolves around our cast trying to overthrow the unjust regime of the Renans (Humans capable of using astral arts), in order to free Dahnans (Humans used as slave labor by the Renans). Quite a lot happens over the course of the games story, and needless to say it isn't always so black and white (ESPECIALLY IN THE DLC). I've seen people complain that the game's third act is too slow, but I'm not sure it's fair to simply write it off as "slow". There's a lot of REALLY good character stuff in the third act, and while it may be slower as a result of the extra dialogue and character moments, those moments made up some of my favorite parts of the game. I'm not easily stirred to emotion by games or movies, and only a few games have every actually moved me to the point of tears, Nier: Automata and The Witcher 3, to name a couple. This game got me GOOD...several times... I don't really feel right doing a full DLC review here, as this review is meant for the main game, so I'll simply say this. If you enjoyed the character moments in the main game, and upon finishing it, wanted more time with these characters, then the DLC is for you. I went from 100 percenting the main game, immediately into the DLC and 100 percented it as well, with NO regrets. If the price seems to steep, you can always catch it on sale, it goes on sale pretty often!I ADORE this game, and it's characters. Tales of Arise is a must experience game for new players and fans of the "Tales of" series alike. From the fast paced and flashy combat, to the character moments and party chemistry, I thoroughly enjoyed every moment I spent with this game and it's DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay's good, characters are likeable.Only issue regarding gameplay so far has been that the second lord's boss fight is poorly designed. Having done all optional content by that point, I was still underleveled for it, and the fight has a DPS check that I'm certain is impossible for the point in game you get to it, unless you grind levels, at least on hard. No other boss has any issue like this, before or even far after this fight. Played through on Hard.On the technical side, the PC version is amazingly well optimized, but there is a technical that's completely by design. During fixed camera animations such as all cutscene and *all* mystic artes and finishing strikes, the game locks itself to 60fps NO MATTER YOUR FRAME LIMIT SETTING. It is janky as hell, when the game runs at 120FPS and suddenly wants to jump to 60FPS in the middle of combat, only to return back to 120FPS seconds later. It is incredibly poor design, and this is an issue that I cannot imagine being caused if not deliberately. I hope they change it.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly disappointing. I’m not going to take the “Day-1 DLC” thing into account at all in this review as I don’t really care either way and it’s been covered elsewhere thoroughly. Incidentally, I preordered the deluxe edition or whatever it was called, but didn’t get any of the other DLCs.The Good:-Game is not overly long, and that’s good because I was tired of playing it.-No technical Issues for me at all. Performance was good.-Uses the Steam controller API. Theoretically good, but I couldn’t figure it out.-Not many last-minute epiphanies and redemptions in the story.The ok:-Combat overall is not too bad, but not the best in the series. Bersaria was probably better, and Graces f was definitely better.-Music is ok.-English voice acting was fair. Not excellent, but not Baten Kaitos bad.-Overall story was typical Tales fare, but on the less original end of the spectrum. Many reused elements from previous Tales games.-Graphics were ok from a technical standpoint but world design and tilesets were too generic.-Not a hint of the old Tales dungeon-puzzles. This could be good or bad depending on if you liked them or not.The Bad:-Party was bland and unremarkable. When the most endearing member is an obnoxious collaborator, you’ve got a problem. -Dialogue was uninteresting at best and cringy at worst. -Skits were boring. (I honestly couldn’t care less about your brother teaching you to do laundry, Kisara.)-The game seems to count on you dodging all the time, but enemies don’t telegraph their moves enough.-Enemies have too many hitpoints and give too little XP and Money.-Crafting and minigames are lackluster.  -Boring evil-for-the-sake-of-evil mid-boss.-The final boss and his henchmen never talk and might not even be sentient.Final verdict: Pretty good combat dragged down mediocre world design and abysmal storytelling. Definitely the worst main-line tales I’ve yet played. Even Xillia was better. Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: what makes this game especially good and rewarding for me, a long time tales series fan is its fantastic use of its numerous sub systems to create a modern, satisfying gameplay loop where everything optional contributes to the overal experience in both plot and gameplay.titles double as skillcollection (each title is a circle with a stat boost once all skills are aquired and artes or passive traits)cooking gives cool and meaningful stat boosts. each recipe you come across widens your optionsfishing gives ingridients for cooking or fish can be sold for moneyaccessories and weapons can be crafted by materials. materials are sometimes hidden (the rare ones) or comes as reward for optional bossfights or bigger monsters in the overworldsidequests give large amount of gil and skillpointsand many more examples.in the past there have been many of those things in the tales games. but never before have all of them been integrated into the game to such ameaningful and satisfying degree.enemy design is alright. there are a bit too few enemy designs so combat can get old as you go on. but i think the enemies that are present work well and have their defining features.the combat is remakable as well, although its very apparent that AI behaviour can be tweaked in some new ways, while other traditional options are missing. this kinda sucks, because the combat relies heavily on focussing enemies down and finishing them with super moves, after their "resolve" has been broken by a big combo. but you cant tell your ai to focus what you are focussing, so you pretty much have to focus down what they go for, even if they are pretty split up themselves. theres some tedious workaround for this for example manually controlling and targeting only to return to your main and then going on with fighting. the games presentation is phenomenal, although i dont really see antialiasing do all that much and the sharpening filter (that cant be turned off) is pretty intense. but the game has a strong art direction and the main characters never have looked so good in a tales game from both a design and technical perspective.the story and characters are good, nothing amazing, but the characterdevelopment is still pulled of well and you can really empathize with most if not all characters and the dialogue taps into interesting concepts. ofc as is normal in a tales game, it sometimes gets pretty cheesy, but thats something that i personally can enjoy.all in all one of the best tales games to date. it was well worth the wait and what sets it apart from other tales games is done to great success.Edit: The last 10 Hours of my 53 Hours playthrough have kinda put me off a bit. the last portion of the game with the final plottwist are extremely tedious at times. there are multiple sections where you are forced to talk to all party members, at one point even twice in a row and the dialogue is pretty redundant. also the non skit dialogue is 50% redundancy and cheesyness. the last dungeon is a gauntlet of fights with little variation. yeah, the fist 80% of the game are much better and then it takes a dip, atleast for me.over all i give this game a totally not scientific rating of 85/100 just by instinct. the sum of its shortcomings kinda equal out to about 15 Points from perfection.

The excellent combat makes grinding welcoming need to do due to the share fun of it. The boss battles are one the best experiences I have ever experienced in a game of this genre. The cinematic shots and coupled with the artistic fight choreography is something to be hold. The game does have some short comings, like the story, it is nothing memorable - I honestly cannot remember what the characters were fighting for months after I completed the game. Nonetheless, Tales of Arise is a good game. The combat, artistic direction of the world, characters, and the share fun of leveling up will keep one coming back for more. I am hoping for the next Tales game to focus more on good story telling and then we will have series that is better than Final Fantasy. _childDocuments_.review: Now that I've finally beaten the game, I can safely say my initial criticisms are still the same. The game was just such a slog for me to finish, I could never play more than a couple of hours at a time due to how boring and uninteresting the plot and the characters were throughout the game.I started to get more into the story once I got up to the 40-hour mark, but that was very short-lived. The game then kept pulling a tug of war where I could get interested in the story and then uninterested back and forth. I didn't like how they made some of the skits feature characters outside of the main cast, occasionally having unimportant NPCs there to turn the skit into a lazy replacement for a story cutscene, instead of something that enhances the story and character development. They did this several times with skits being blatantly a replacement for a cutscene, which only made the skits lose even more of their charm.There were surprise characters from previous games that made a pleasant and unexpected appearance in the post game stuff that I was really happy to see. But it fell flat really fast and once you finish the side-quest they're a part of, Alphen even says to go back and talk to them to let them know something, but you can't even do that, you just end up fighting them again with no further dialogue, which was disappointing.I will say that the ending was actually satisfying, but I don't feel like the journey to reach it was worth it due to the terrible writing and execution of the story and interactions of the characters. The pacing was so off and the chemistry between companions not particularly strong. There just comes a certain point in the story where everyone happens to be the best of friends, despite major conflicting personalities. Usually when I play a Tales of game, you get all of that from the skits and character interactions which makes everything feel all good and proper. But this game was so far off the mark with all of that, I'm so offended it's being praised as highly as it is in comparison to previous games.If you share some of my opinions, I don't really recommend this game. If you can force yourself to push on, you'll get an okay story with a lot of inconsistencies and rushed character development, but you will be rewarded with a satisfying ending. But for me, the pain in experiencing the journey was not worth the time and effort I put into it. I don't see myself as playing this game again. I have mixed feelings about this game.On the one hand: I'm happy that it is doing so well. It appears to be selling well and the series is getting more popular as it has deserved for many years now.However, on the other hand: this is the worst Tales of game I've played.It doesn't even really feel like a Tales of game to me. The way they changed the skits, removing the beautifully drawn, interactive 2D sprites has completely killed its original charm they had. Now they use the 3D models, splice it up with very limited and static animations in a comic-style, and it somehow feels less interactive that the simple 2D skits they've used up until now.The UI is terrible, it doesn't feel like a Tales of game's UI at all, but more of a generic placeholder one. The story is so boring and badly paced. A lot of it feels so rushed and forced, I have no attachment to any of the characters so far into the story. Some of the dialogue feels awfully out of place, especially when a new skit becomes available, and they talk as if there are more than two people in the party so early on in the game, or they appear more friendly to eachother, and then when you reach the next story cutscene, they're back to being the complete opposite.The Tales of games have been slowly declining over the years and removing much of their original charm piece by piece, seemingly to appeal more to the mainstream crowd, and with this new Tales of Arise, it seems they may have finally done just that with how well it is doing.However to me, it has put the series as a whole very low on my list of games I get excited to play when the next title comes out. If their next game doesn't try to recapture the feel of their previous games, I definitely won't be playing them on release anymore. I'd much rather play the Trails series, which in my opinion, have continued to improve on what made their series unique, modernised and improved without removing any of its original charm.The complete opposite of what it feels like with the Tales of series. I want to explore a vast world, with so many story arcs that continue to impress me with how the game is still going. I want to reach a point in the adventure where the main characters gain an animal companion that they can fly, or an airship that allows us to quickly travel to areas previously visited and reach new ones. This series hasn't captured that feeling in a long time.This is the most generic JRPG I have played in a long time. The only thing that it has going for it is its combat, which is admittedly different from previous games, but feels very satisfying and a perfect evolution for the series.Everything else however, is the opposite, and I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there!I just played and finished this game for around 80 hours on moderate difficulty with almost no DLC help kits (I only used 1 arte that's from the title you get from the DLC but nothing else). As a player who plays the Tales of series for the first time, here are my thoughts about this game:1. Graphics are truly amazing! It's so pretty and detailed everywhere I go in this game.2. It has fine music. I don't think I've ever said to myself that "this is boring" or "I'm tired of hearing this". Although I don't have a very good grasp on music, all I'm trying to say is I don't have any major criticisms towards its music, and I think they all fit in pretty well in my play through.3. Combat, as well as how you acquire new skills/artes, is really interesting to me. CP management, extending combos, getting Boost Attacks ready, working around enemies' elements, and paying attention to enemies' movements (I really suck at this), these are all things I learned throughout my gameplay. The only thing that slightly bothers me is that whenever your characters get leveled up, they don't get their HP bar filled. On the other hand, I'm sure some players are up to that kind of challenges, so it's probably a fine design.4. Voice acting is great, even though the developer didn't make characters lip sync to their English voices. I'm personally not bothered by that. 5.AI-controlled characters talk way too much during combat. Don't get my wrong, I love when Rinwell says "Blah blah blah, magic!"6. Using skits for storytelling as well as adding flavors to the current situation is very fun to me. It makes feel like reading manga like the old time when I was still in school.7. Fishing is hella cool in this game and you should definitely try it out. I just wish we can use other character to fish.8. There are so many typos in English subtitles that it makes me feel embarrassed for the developer. I'm just really shocked that a series that's this big, and this specific game is supposed to be a big hit for the series, you'd think the developer would put 120% effort into it. I would be okay if there were only 1 or 2 typos, but there are so many that I feel like I have to point that out. Hopefully the developer will be more careful in the future.9. I think this game has really good character development. It's really nice to see how Rinwell grows from her past and changes her views about other members in the group throughout the story. The developer did a pretty decent job about each characters' shifts. I'm personally not a big fan of Alphen & Shionne, but I love those small interactions between Law & Rinwell, Dohalim & Kisara. I wish the developer can show us more about what happened between those 2 couples after the main story ends, and I'd love to see they hug each other or hold each other's hands!10. The story itself is okay. There are a couple plot twists that are interesting and unexpected, but other than that, it's what you would expect out of this game.Overall, 9/10, I think it's definitely worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: Short summary: There is a great game buried under microtransaction greed. The difficulty has been ramped up severely, mainly in the form of limits to healing and obscenely expensive consumables, motivated by getting people to purchase "cheat" microtransactions. If you get this game, you may want to get a cheat program as well.Long version:Well this is awkward. My original review seems to have gotten noticed, which is sad because it was an unhinged rant. I was angry due to what they did to one of my favorite franchises, even though I saw it coming given what Namco did to Tales of Phantasia on mobile. I can do better, so here's a more thorough review.I don't even know how to give ratings for certain categories under these circumstances, so some scores will be followed by [GS: X/10]. This means the reduced score due to Namco's greed.Gameplay: 9/10 [GS: 5/10]Tales games have always had great gameplay, and this one is no exception. It's the original beat-em-up RPG series and this entry adds a couple new forms of attacks to the mix. Mystic artes are easier to execute than in many other titles, jumping on the overworld is nice but underused. The Sorcerer's Ring is gone, replaced by context actions for getting past barriers. Combat in Tales games have never been completely fluid like with full-on ARPGs, but it's deliberate and careful planning will see you to victory.That said, it gets a greed score of 5 due to the inherent, psychologically manipulative design. I've played at least 10 games in this series by now, but I've never been that great. Always managed to get by and in some titles (i.e. Zestiria) even excel with honest play. Usually end up using healing as a crutch.You can't do that in this game.The major change to healing in this game is any ability that heals drains from a pool called Cure Points. On its face, it seems great: Shionne isn't solely a heal bot when I play like her counterparts in previous titles would be. Unfortunately, healing has become extremely expensive. This pool is also shared with those context actions which makes things worse. The AI drains a lot of healing just with their own mistakes. Healing items have been weakened because they are no longer a % of health. Items that restore CP (Orange Gel, Pineapple Gel) are ludicrously expensive. (3000/9000 gald!) Getting gald isn't as straightforward as it is in other games, either.It gets worse: If you aren't saving regularly and you fail a battle, you'll be spit out with any of these pricey consumables you used during said battle lost forever. Don't trust the autosave -- anything that looks like it could kill you, save save save. To be fair, it restores CP when you're spat back out, but you may need more than that for fights you'd need to save for.On top of all this, the . So even if you're not a terrible player like I am, you're not immune from this predatory system. This isn't like Violet who both harms and heals herself. You want to use the MC's abilities, you're paying a fortune in gald, which can be re-upped for "only" two bucks!Controls: 10/10They nailed it with Zestiria and two entries later, they still got it right. The keyboard/mouse controls are as strong as ever. It doesn't get overwhelming and everything you need to do can be done intuitively.Story: 10/10Tales games are best when the story is weird, and boy is this one weird. In the game's first region, I was shocked just how much was put out there -- it almost seemed like we'd have another Symphonia but without the twist. It's not, and it just gets weirder and weirder. This is easily a series top 5, and could be a top 3...but I'll need a couple years distance before I could say that.The cast is also excellent, as it is tight-knit while still having as much interaction through main story and skits as a cast of 8 might have. The cast also skews mature versus most of the games, mascot included, which means none of them are particularly annoying. The only downside is none of them are particular standouts either, like Magilou was in Berseria.Sound: 10/10Motoi Sakuraba hasn't slowed down, giving us another great soundtrack that punctuates every story beat. The Japanese voices are also strong. It's an old series, they've long since figured it out.Graphics: 10/10I don't need much to please me -- I play lots of indie games. This title marks a massive leap in terms of graphical fidelity. The maps feel more real than real at this point, and I wasn't sure where the game was going to end because there are so many detailed maps. There is repetition, but the creators got good at hiding it.Overall: 9/10 [GS: 6/10]This is gaming in 2022 -- where we have to rate games for what they could have been if tuning were a little different. The game was designed from the ground up to push predatory microtransactions, and yet all of the strengths of the series are still there. This is painful to watch, a 25th anniversary marred by greed. A beloved series, so story rich that it's akin to a 26-episode anime season, pioneering gameplay, genius composer, reduced to this for a quick sleazy buck. I still encourage everyone to cheat: You paid for a full game, not a quarter muncher.Namco can't undo what they did here. They can only make right in the next installment, or I'm out, and I don't think I'll be alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely best graphics and performance among Tales series. Probably still among the best in contemporary JRPGs (comparable even with masterpieces like Dragon Quest XI S).Quality is high. There is almost no bug in the first version (I heard there might be bug on trophy, but so far have not encountered any in my first play-through).Main theme is traditional Tales flavor, boy meets girl, unknown to them, they are going to save the world.Story is good enough to keep one care for the party and wish to explore the world more. Actions feels natural and combo is rewarding. Music is gorgeous.Each party member gets a different sets of moves and even combat concepts. If one get bored with sword and dodging, one can switch to a mage and combine multiple magic to form the Perfect Storm, bombard the enemy from afar.A few tips for normal difficulty:1. Default normal attack on controller is RB on the shoulder, one probably want to use an ABXY button for it (say B).2. In the first few chapters, avoid using consumables except for boss fights. They are expensive, and player is probably still exploring the dodge and counter system.3. Accessory can be changed during battle. It is helpful to switch to element resistance before boss lands a Mystic Artes.A few shortcoming:1. There is big secret behind main characters, but there is too little foreshadowing before the last chapter presents the truth in too short of a time.2. Last chapter reused too many enemy that already seen before. It feels very repetitive and boring in the last dungeon.3. There is only one set of Boost Strikes (for each pair) and Mystic Artes (for each member). They are fun and rewarding, but in later chapters, they again feels repetitive.4. Most Skit is about current city or dungeon or situation, and somehow too serious to my taste. They are not as fun as previous titles. Though the ones about owls is good.5. I know it is probably series tradition, but DLC on gold/item/level is meaningless. This is a single-player game. I guess these DLC are for the players that really love the game and want to contribute more to the developers so that we could see the next game earlier :-).

_childDocuments_.review: First time player of the Tales series. Been hearing about it from coworkers and decided to try it out. 17 hours in at time of writing.So.. why the hell haven't I played these before?? This is an amazing game. At first, it seems like any other just-shy-of-mainstream JRPG, but then the voice acting and character development take it to a whole other level. It always took away from the stories of other games when you had something like.. "Main character meets person who is sorta an enemy. They team up for whatever reason. They hate one another. They fight one boss fight and now they're best friends and can finish each others sentences." That sort of thing always took away from the immersion of the game, feeling like a 14 year old wrote it thinking that's how relationships are.Not this game. This game feels like a crap ton of thought and effort went into the development of the characters and the delivery of the voice lines. Really good stuff. For actual gameplay, it is pretty solid, if I were to give the gameplay and action feel a rating, I'd say like 8.5/10. I still have a lot to learn about the combat system, but from first glance it isn't super demanding or super deep, at least not yet for me. Graphics are really, really good as well. Music is top notch.Overall I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a good RPG. I'm usually the type to spend every waking moment of my time completing a game, but since I don't really have the time to at the moment, I look forward to getting home and playing this for an hour or two at a time. Really good game.

Visuals and art direction is gorgeous. Probably one of if not the best looking cell shaded game out there2. Combat is addictive and encourages lots of experimenting3. Boss encounters are very well designed and are always a high point in every chapter3. The Cure Points system is something i grew to actually like because its very simple and it programs your brain from early on to pace "Dungeons" into "runs". Chipping away a dungeon just never feel grindy4. Crafting Weapons is never a hassle because you'll find everything you need by just progressing through the story. There was never a point where you have to take a detour and grind for something (Excluding post game anyway)5. Characters follow typical archetypes but charming enough that they grow on you6. Story is well paced with very few lulls Cons1. While well paced, the writing can be very heavy handed and takes very few risks2. Dialogue is serviceable but definitely a low point as some moments come off unnatural or fall flat entirelyOverall i'm excited to see whats next for the tales series! If they can put everything in arise into a more gripping story with less hammy dialogue it can be something very special!

_childDocuments_.review: PROS - Jumping off waterfallsCombat wise, I really enjoyed tales of arise. I've tried each character and learned to use them to some extent. Some will be much easier to use than others. After experimenting, you'll be having fun in no time. Battles are very fluid and knowing how certain enemies behave helps. If you've tried switching characters quickly after calling them in for their boost arte (like an assist in arcade fighting games), it adds a different level of fluidity and combo building. It's also nice they placed a system where you can't just spam the same attack over and over or it's less effective. It was fun to challenge enemies and bosses much stronger than you as well since they can still punish you if you're careless.Story wise, I'm happy we finally have another tales where romance plays a significant part and they get together clearly in the end. I mean we've had couples in the past, Stan and Rutee, Luke and Tear, Asbel and Cheria, but it wasn't as focused. I also absolutely love all the main characters.CONS - The story was adequate, but not great. The first half was great, but it sort of fell on its face in the second half. It felt rushed. You suddenly got plot twist after plot twist after plot twist. It didn't give things time to sink in even if I played the game very slowly and tried to explore as much as I could before moving on to the next point. If there was more around each plot twist, more time, more narrative, more questing around, more locations then maybe I would say differently.Also, the game sort of does a deus ex machina at some point which wasn't really explained when I played it . Maybe it was better explained in the DLC expansion, but I didn't play it. CONS for the combat. I only have one and it's not the combat exactly. It's the DLC locked skills and skill trees. For anyone who hasn't played, skill trees are basically permanent ways to get extra stats, extra skills, faster cool downs etc. So having these permanent buffs, only available to people who paid for the dlc, doesn't sit well with me. I don't mind the free levels or items. I can choose not to use them. I don't even mind not having access to the dlc artes. But what I do mind are the extra stat boosts that I have to pay for.

_childDocuments_.review: I will try to explain the reasons why low score even when I got all achievements. I still recommend this game but with BIG caveats. I play Tales of Zestiria and Berseria before, while it’s only 2 Tales games I spent a lot of time on other J-RPGs. TLDR at the bottom. The story premise is actually good with colonialism and racism with actual adult characters in tales game, this is the first time they are doing it. I can bear the usual J-RPG dialogue about friendship, I like this genre after all, thankfully this game mentions less about it so it’s a plus. That being said Tales of Arise story best described as a ‘missed opportunity’, it should be 2 games like Tales of xillia and Tales of xillia 2 because the scope is too many and too big for one game. Here Bandai Namco made pacing of the game fast so it can be completed in one J-RPG game but it actually makes story inconsistent even though there’s repeatable story session like defeating one lord to another for 5 times (this is explained pretty early so don’t worry), dahna is a planet but the world feels small because how rushed the story is.Now onto the last 25% story part. The easiest way to describe is that 25% should be 50% of the story. Bamco really needs to delay this game 1 more year. Make it longer and got more weight each session. I can bear 75% part but the last 25% is…. just happen. All those lore dumping at once in only a short time to reveal something,  . The reveal is just for the sake of being there as an obstacle for the party to overcome and explained suddenly. Tales games always have story skits, you know like comic panels but mostly it’s just party banter like usual tales games, it should explain the lore more and interesting facts about the world for Tales of Arise case. Berseria's story is great because it stays to  problem but there are many stories to deliver to go there while Arise's story branched out too much makes the story ‘mediocre at best’. The plot hole happens few times, new things introduced to the story but never mentioned again and some of them left unanswered. The way new NPCs introduced on main story and suddenly gone gives bad feeling that he/she only there so the plot progress. I am already too far grinding story, items, and side content before realizing this so might as well complete all achievements. Honestly I don't get it how this title got best RPG on the game awards 2021.For characters, Alphen is decent but nothing special. Shionne is unbearable and not friendly, she got her reason but needs long hours of game time to explain why. Rinwell is the youngest but mature when it’s needed and goes well with Law. Law is kind of funny and stands out from other members. Kisara is the caretaker of the party and acts as a mom. While dohalim struggles to learn how a normal person should act it’s amusing and the way he talks is poetic. There are almost no memorable casts but it’s passable.Tales of Arise combat is pretty great not gonna lie, great improvements from the previous Tales game, and the game becomes more stylish with boost attacks and boost strikes. No button mashing and spamming the same artes (skill attacks). There are dodging mechanics that is actually fun. Artes are actually cool and varied. You might stay playing this game for combat more than the story. Sadly the combat hurt itself because lack of enemy type, the normal mobs' enemies maybe can be counted with all your 10 fingers because of how few it is, there is a gigant enemies type as side content that only few are different, the rest are just bigger and harder enemies of normal type, even some main story boss design at least used TWICE. You know those old J-RPG and mobile games that same enemy types but only different colors as progress goes on? Yeah, tales of arise is like that, it’s an embarrassment for a game that boasts about different places of the world to visit and different biomes only got the same enemies with different colors, All of your 4 members cast the spell and attack while screaming the name of skill, I know this is happen in all Tales games but I can see some people getting irritated about this. Too much happening on the screen in a small combat arena, making it hard to dodge and avoid damage if you use close combat characters like Alphen, Dohalim, and Law which need few hours to get used to. But if you do not use close combat characters and let AI do it, they die too fast. Bosses got too much HP make it HP / damage sponges. The AI is not good enough to play on a higher difficulty than normal on the boss stage, they like to stay in the same place when there’s an enemy projectile and attack targetting them, There is also no compensation for AI like damage reduction. A way to solve this is to change control to them and dodge, but doing it every time is pretty tiring, another one is going to artes menu to uncheck long animation arte and use arte that have short animation or use spell to attack from far away, But it’s still not good enough to justify how bad the AI is. Can change the difficulty when playing.Gald (money) to buy items is harder to earn and everything are expensive especially orange gel that only adding 30% max of CP (stamina like to casts heal spell) , to buy one the price is 1 side quest on early game. This is my first time on J-RPG struggling getting money, you will found out runs out of gald on higher difficulties. it's bothersome from start to midgame.The graphics are insanely good. The shaders they use to become more like watercolor painting are amazing and should be used for a few next tales games because it creates a new visual identity for J-RPG, really pleasant to look at. Tales finally use a time cycle that changes from morning to night. These are the strongest points of the game but again lack of enemy type really hurt this game a lot, only variants that different colors and were a bit stronger.Characters model design are great. Alphen, Shionne, Kisara armor are nice. Rinwell and Dohalim looks good too while law outfit suits with his style but it can be better. The voice acting are suitable with how you expect them to sound like, fully lipsync both in japanese and english language. English dub need more expressiveness on some part but not a problem.I don’t remember memorable OST from this game sadly except for a few like ‘Flame of Hope’ because it uses violin, the OST when fighting the third lord, and the Vocal opening and ending OST.The game just passed barely for positive review, i think Tales of Arise is good J-RPG to start if you are new to the genre, maybe as your first 5 J-RPG. Clearly better than Zestiria but far worse than Berseria in terms of story. Except graphics anything else feels need 1 more year of effort to be great but the problem might be the lack of budgets that bandai namco gives to tales team and this is almost happened on every tales game. Play Tales of Arise if you are new to the genre or run out of J-RPG titles. There is another series that can be compared to this franchise called Ys, specifically Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of Dana which is better in every way except graphics but the art direction still good to look at. Buy this game only on 60% or more sale. It suck so bad. No new playable characters + no new skill + no new mechanics + literally only final boss the new one + place (dungeon) only 3 that new + main story 7 hours, side quest so barebones to make the game longer to 25 hours + pre-fixed level on level 65 for "lazy content" + recycle map but can't visit most of them because separated title screen than main story. Play it if you want more of the characters which imho they decent nothing special except law and dohalim.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphically speaking, Tales of Arise is second to none in the JRPG Market. I had to stop myself several times to stare in awe at some of the most detailed vistas I've seen created in a videogame in 2022. I would argue its prowess is only rivaled by FF15 and FF7R. However, graphics do not make a game.Story is a joke. "Slavery bad, friendship is magic" stretched over 60000 hours. The game never ends. There are no interesting twists. Nothing of significance happens, ever.Characters are gigasimps, forgiving mass murderers and villans only to get backstabbed, repeat 1000 times.Combat gets REALLY spongey at the end. Your damage does not scale properly and fights take forever. It is not difficult nor engaging, just really drawn out. If this bothers you, feel free to buy additional levels and boosts conveniently offered in the store.Audio tracks are amazing but the mixing of them is absolute trash. If you listen to proper mixes on spotify the difference is night and day. For some reason, since Berseria, every audio file has a strong trebble pass that mutes bass??I do not recommend Tales of Arise.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: First off: I wish I could give a neutral review. Tales of Arise really is a double-edged sword (or should i say a flaming sword?).Please remember that opinions are different. Feel free to comment your opinion or questions!I played a lot of "Tales of" games and am always looking forward for new releases of this franchise. The games are always amazing with great stories, soundtrack, characters and combat, I just love them. But sadly, Tales of Arise seems to be a bit different. Let's start with the main character: He is your typical shonen do-gooder, which itself doesn't have to be bad. I usually like generic-ass hero characters (like Sorey in Tales of Zestiria). The protagonist here had such an interesting concept, but it is just so poorly executed. He never acts wrong or does a bad thing and that gets bland quickly.The Story, or rather the storytelling (minor spoilers): The Story itself is pretty good (I Only thought that way after I finished it, before that I thought it was bad) but the storytelling sucks.The first 30 hours just feel episodic, you could compare it to Pokemon. After you got every badge you can challenge the League Champion (In this case the end boss). I didn't want to know what happens next because I knew what would happen. I would just beat the next gym leader and get my badge. For the most part, the story doesn't feel connected to the whole game. There is no build-up and it doesn't feel like our actions change anything, and then suddenly in the end every interesting plot point gets shoved down your throat simultaneously. But there it was too late and I got annoyed because there were so. many. small cutscenes, conversations and forced fights. That just makes the good story feel so lazy and bad in my eyes.The Combat:At first the combat feels really good but it gets stale fast, you really have to play different characters or switch artes sometimes to keep yourself entertained. But the not so good thing is the combat in bossfights. You can't juggle bosses anymore, you can only stagger them under the right conditions, which adds to the difficulty but leads to spamming the strongest attack to get the most out of the enemy stun and that just doesn't feel good.The Soundtrack:  Sadly, even the Soundtrack is bland most of the time. They really saved the best songs for the last section of the game because there the Soundtrack really gets good.DLC: You probably read a lot about that in other reviews. Skills locked behind a paywall in a singleplayer game? Come on. This isn't a Gacha Game.And the most important thing: Were is the iconic "Tales of" save point sound effect???I had my fair share of disappointment, but the ending really saved my opinion on this game. I wanted to give it a 5/10 but now I would say like 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: wow what a ride, took about 100hrs to complete the main story. rest was mostly afk, side questing, arena, and 100% achievement hunting, i played this blind on hard difficulty. this is goty material. if u enjoy jrpgs like persona, tales, trails, YS, dragon quest, final fantasy, get this my fellow gamers. pro- decent anime story- balance character roster- alot of artes (skills) for gameplay - great voice actors- great character development- hootle cons- potions can get expensive lategame- newgame+ quite pointless- story felt rushed near the end (information overload)- maps quite linear. thank god for fast travel and campsites.- dlc buffs are scummy imo.p/s- some mentioned jp voice acting is better, - leveling artes can be bit a grindy for some people- 1 hour min lock to level each companion bonds. ugh- artifacts are for new game plus, pointless.- Accessories system could be better- imo armours should be craftable, not bought/loot drop

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the game! I'm not going to do a full scale review, but here are a few quick ratings.Story 8/10I loved the story all the way up until one of the areas near the end of the game. I think those who have already played will understand what I'm talking about. The place felt like a massive info dump and more rushed compared to other moments in the game. Because this story dense area should've been the strongest moment in the story and the mark was missed, it docked an extra point from the score. The story is great, but sometimes the game struggles to tell it.Music 9/10I enjoyed all of the music in the game. Some of the tracks felt a bit similar to each other, especially during a couple of endgame areas. That didn't mean they were bad experiences or annoying, but just not as stand out as many of the earlier tracks.Combat 9/10I enjoyed the combat a lot. It looks absolutely gorgeous, and with cut scene finishes for enemies, it's never been more satisfying to cut down an enemy, even one of the little ones. There are quite a few characters to play as with quite different play styles. Those characters also have different focuses within those play styles. Unlocking skills is also quite expansive and rewarding as well. You can build your set of skills for whatever combinations suit you best. The equipment is a lot more basic. When it comes to armor and weapons, you pretty much just forge the best set you've unlocked every once in a while and you'll be fine. Buying CP restoring items is a must. When it comes to accessories it's a little bit more complex, but I never felt a huge need to max out my damage or much else. Of course, I only played on normal mode, so I can't say I've experienced the harder difficulties.Characters 10/10Loved all the characters. I usually base this off of how hard it is for me to rank my favorite characters from the game after I've finished it, and this time it was extremely hard for me. All of them are unique and charming in their own ways, and I'm going to miss them. The skits and campfire moments have made me fall in love with each character, and I think this game did a great job at fleshing them out.Visuals 10/10The game is always gorgeous. The scenery, the character models, your skills in battle, and every cut scene including the few 2D ones all pop with their own magnificent style. I was left in awe many times throughout my journey. There are many times where I simply didn't want to leave an area because I was having such a good time looking around and exploring. I did have a few times where the frame rate would struggle, but the magical visuals were well worth it in my opinion.Overall Rating 9.2/10After averaging all the scores together, I got a 9.2/10. I'm not exactly the harshest critic on the block, but this game really spoke to me. There were very few times where I wasn't having a blast. I absolutely loved this game and it's a shame that I'm done with it. Hopefully, in the future, after a lot time has passed, I'll be able to properly revisit this masterpiece

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the entire game until NewGame+, which I decided just wasn't worth my time for whatever was available there.First of all the game has 0 respect for your time. After grinding for around 5 hours just to beat a boss on NORMAL difficulty, I decided to just turn the difficulty down to Very Easy and just slide through the game. Looking at the fact that the DLC increases the EXP rate and CP gain rate by 2x, I see the reason pretty clear what happened.I really wanted to like the game.The story is fine, the pacing is fairly slow as it takes it's time to build up. The story is mostly good, with some very predictable Deus Ex machinas scattered about, and a fairly predictable message. The dialogue between characters starts out extremely good and then just becomes the same conversation over and over again. The character pairs all have decent chemistry and it is nice that this is increasingly explored as the game progresses.The combat is mostly enjoyable aside from the fact that the game generally punishes you as much as possible. The Main DPS takes self damage in exchange for pumping up his own damage, for generally a single attack. This works fine when the attack hits, sometimes it doesn't because of very weird auto-tracking and an enemy moving at the last second. I'm okay with that conceptually just the fact that there is a healing gauge that replenishes either via resting (or throwing materials at it) just takes away from experimenting. I cleared up to the point where they start introducing the endgame+ dungeons on normal difficulty. I realized that in order to do said dungeons I would either have to grind for 12+ hours...or just stop caring and put it on Very Easy.The pacing for the RPG elements is so bad I was generally under-leveled, on normal with typical grinding, by around 5 levels. In this game even minor statistic upgrades can have large charges, so level differences make or break quite a bit. As an example, I took on a quest boss that was level 46 at level 39. Any single mistake would get me immediately one shot. Facing the same boss again at level 45 I snoozed my way through it without much problem. I didn't have the personal motivation to grind for 5+ hours prior to each "difficult" boss fight just to equalize my levels.The graphics are generally amazing and quite creative. The combat, along with the visuals, is what drew me to pull the trigger to get the game.If I compare this game to something also fairly recent, like Scarlet Nexus, I find Scarlet Nexus to be the clear winner. There are still great graphics, good characters, an interesting story (though to be honest Scarlet Nexus is just a much better put together and thought out story), rpg elements, and strong combat. Scarlet Nexus makes the grinding not a chore, makes the fights not require a loading screen each time, respects your time (I felt too strong in Scarlet Nexus with a bit of grinding on higher difficulty).I honestly wish that I could recommend this game. It has a lot of the elements that should make it good. They just don't come together at the right time, nor does it respect your time, and it also appears that the DLC is meant to be the bridge to play the game the way it would be intended.

The following ones after are a lot easier. _childDocuments_.review: I’ve always considered Tales to be a pretty character-focused series. The schlocky plots and world-ending threats secondary to exploring the lives, charms, and quirks of the ragtag bunch all trudging toward their common goal by way of serendipity and for some personal gain. So WHY they decided to make the protagonist of Arise an amnesiac is completely beyond me. The writers just aren’t skilled enough to make a character like this interesting or likeable. Whether it be making banal observations or delivering another cliche hero line, Alphen is constantly cementing himself as the most boring pillock to ever anime-sigh. Even his “arc” just consists of going from a tedious drip to a whiny ♥♥♥♥♥, I’ve never encountered a more irritating character in a JRPG before. I say “arc” in quotations because the characters in this game don’t undergo arcs. And neither does the story. Instead, the whole game is composed of moments. Scenes you’d see in a competently constructed narrative except assembled by someone who has no understanding of them whatsoever. No scene leads into the other, there’s never any set up of tone or twists. The gameplay itself is passable. Not enough to ignore the abysmal writing over but it holds its own just fine. Combat is fluid and responsive, hitting perfect evasions into combos feels great. Even if it’s a little generic it’s snappy and fun plus having BGs as situational counters adds a nice little bit of depth.

_childDocuments_.review: In an age when games are made intentionally cruel and unfair towards players, crammed with propaganda, and made to feel like a part time job, this game was a truly wonderful experience. The story and characters will stick with me forever, creative but relatable and understandable, just goodness.This is a game for people who enjoy good stories, good user experience, and good mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Not my favorite Tales story so far but its good and the gameplay is pretty good. Not bad!Edit*OK, I reviewed this too early. Now that I'm in what I am guessing is the second half of the game after the intro changes to the new one like a new season of an anime... The sadistic programmers of this game decided to give you access to ridiculously overpowered bosses too damn early. Example: Rinwell wants a flower that grows somewhere. Cool, I'm level mid-thirties so let's check this out! Oh! Did we find it guys? Wait, we're getting ambushes by a LEVEL 52 boss. Boss proceeds to one hit kill everyone. Another instance: Hey one of those lights that fell to Earth. Let's enter it! After a no break marathon of enemy fights of fairly hard enemies, again at level mid-thirties... Big boss time everyone! LEVEL 65 ****ing boss! Summons previous enemies, kill them with difficulties. Summons a death phoenix that one hit kills everyone while shooting environmental lazers that just about one hit kill you. Yeah I get it, you're no where near strong enough yet. WHY WOULD YOU GIVE ME ACCESS TO THESE MISSIONS THEN?! I am more than 20 levels away from even having a chance against the weaker one! You made me spend like 20 minutes fighting several enemies with no breaks to get to a boss that blows on me and kills me. That is just stupid! Wait till at least 5 levels away. I dragged some of these battles out for more than half an hour with pure skill just to be cheaped into a one hit tail spin kill because I was stuck in a skill animation. Don't get me wrong, I still like the game and it is great but this was a poor choice. I didn't die one time until you psychos threw a level 52 boss at me in my mid-thirties.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this game was more OPEN WORLD-ish instead of the linear progression. That is my only gripe, this game is DUMMY AMAZING. So much dialogue / with dope cut scenes and EPIC anime type animation. The combat system in really good as well, like rewarding as hell once you learn the ins-&-outs of what to do + enemy attacks. The stunning system is pretty fluid as well, however some enemy types still kinda clap my cheeks. This is a game I look forward to running back on NG+ as well, but I will be skipping the cut scenes next time LMAO, they can be LONG AF, but good on the 1st play through. The background story is pretty well incorporated into game in a way that hasn't made me wonder what the heck is happening. I would give this game a personal recommendation of a 8.9/10. They are a few other minor things that could be improved but do not overall ruin the experience, for me at least. All in all, when I run into games as good as this, I find them to be very enjoyable and tend to take my time playing them. This was a breathe of fresh air for me, so I hope anyone who reads this and decides to play it, will enjoy it just as much as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review I have written.  But I felt inclined to write this as a long-time fan of the Tales series.  I really have only enjoyed a few games in the series among the others as some of my favorite games.  But never all-time favorites.  This game changed that for me.  Not only has it become my favorite game in the franchise, which is hard because Vesperia was a slam dunk, but one of my favorite all-time games. -----Story--When compared to other Tales game, I love the approach to a more mature telling of the story, whereas other Tales games have their less mature moments.  Arise has a dark story like other games in the series, like Berseria.  But I feel like this is easier to relate to than something like Berseria of which has a story that is more entrenched in a fantasy setting.  Arise's story deals with the themes of racism, politics, and segregation.  These are real civil issues someone can see today.  And it is fascinating to see how these themes can be used in a JRPG.  While yes, there are magic elements in the game, it is not the main driver of the hardships the characters in the game face.  And with this approach to story telling, the story is more impactful than previous games in the series.  It has been an extremely long time since I have played a game in which the story has been memorable, wanting me to come back for more, but this game does that for me and I cannot wait to get on and play more when I have to step away to tend to real life.I never really noticed how hammy dialogue characters have in previous Tales games until Arise came out.  This game still has its moments, but I feel like with the more mature feeling this game gives, its dialogue and way characters interact make sense.  In previous games, you may have characters saying something really cheesy but in this game, being that characters are more relatable and build better throughout the game, they are easier to understand why they act the way they do, or say the things they say.  Playing into the story itself just wraps the entire experience of unraveling the story in this game a real treat.--Atmosphere--The graphics in the game are insane compared to previous games.  This is mainly due to a change in the engine used to make this game compared to previous entries.  This game uses Unreal Engine 4, while previous titles use an in-house engine from the development team, which had been used for many years prior.  With the switch a modernized and streamlined engine such as UE4, it allows for almost surreal graphics when playing.  I play the game on a 4K HDR10 OLED monitor with mods that also enhance visuals.  Yes, this makes the game even more breathtaking for someone like me, even with standard definition with no mods, the game still blows previous Tales games out of the water.  The definition of textures, draw distance of the horizon, and even the level design makes the world feel more immersive,  There are times I stop just to look at scenery in this game even though I really want to keep going through the story.  It is a shame you cannot completely remove the HUD to take screenshots or else I would be taking so many.The game also does a very good job of pacing through different realms within it.  The environments are varied greatly, covering many different settings you may find in other RPGs.  But it makes sure to incorporate many different inspirations of cultures from around the world and from different time periods.  I feel like this, and other small details such as how characters act, their motion, and behaviors makes the world feel alive.  There was a ton of love and dedication made by the developers to make this world feel real and living, rather than empty and hard to see yourself in, and they nailed it.--Gameplay--This game still follows standard Tales game's overworld mechanics, where you are playing as a character lead of your choosing in the overworld map with instanced battles of monsters you find along the way, but the combat has been refreshed from previous entries while still staying true to the unique battle system found in any Tales game.  And here, it excels.  Previous Tales games, while good, can be daunting at times in terms of battle mechanics with certain new features they try to add into games.  This is because they can be complex, hard to understand, or just easier to ignore than and you can faceroll through the game.  But here, each mechanic has a purpose and is understand when to use.  You do have to take time to understand the unique boost attack to each character, when and how to use them.  But there is more reward to  doing so rather than let's say learning the sigil mechanic from Zestiria.  And you could most likely still faceroll through the game beating everything while button -mashing, ignoring mechanics, but you will be punished for it more.  The game incentivizes using the unique mechanics of the combat in this game when compared to previous entries.  But you are rewarded more for it.  And the greatest thing about this is that they actually made using the mechanics in the game really fun and satisfying to use.  And do not get even get me started on how freaking amazing and flashy combo skills are.I am also going to add in here a small bit about sound design rather in its own section, because I mainly love the sound effects of combo skills in this game specifically.  Playing with a good sound system in the games makes sound effects in battles extremely satisfying.---I am not done with the game yet at the time of this review, but I am really enjoying it so far and really felt like I needed to say something.  I have not enjoyed a game as much as this in a long time, but I want to encourage others to try it too if you are looking for a great game to immerse yourself in to escape the real world for awhile, or are a fan of RPGs, new to the Tales series or not.  This may not be the best title in the series to understand how the rest of the series presents itself, as this is a massive refresh in the series to catch up to modern standards when compared to previous games.  But as a standalone game when just compared to other RPGs outside of the Tales titles, it stands tall on its own.  I am only about a 3rd to half of the way through I think, but I am looking forward to more of what the game offers as I continue to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, I guess.  Usually I get a new Tales game and can't put it down, Arise I am struggling to find a reason to keep playing.  Judging by other reviews, it appears this is an unpopular opinion since most negatives are about the in-game DLC adds or skills tied to DLC costumes that people have blown waaaaay out of proportion.Everything about Arise feels like a downgrade from previous entries.  I would recommend every other Tales game on Steam before Arise.Combat looks flashy, but covers up how boring it is.  Three artes buttons, normal attack button.  Push them any order you want, wait for special attacks to come off cool down, mash some buttons again, dodge if you want.  Difficulty is all over the place.  You can walk around in Hard, until you find a couple of mobs that you can't, and better turn the difficulty down before a boss fight.Skits suck.  I hate the new format.  The single panel presentation made it seem more intimate for the group.  The new multi-panel comic book kills that vibe.  And I just played Scarlet Nexus that presented the whole narrative in this style.  Plus there hasn't been anything funny yet.  Tales series is usually good interjecting comedy into the skits or post battle results.  Story started off promising, but quickly devolved into a standard format.  Run through some corridors, get to a town, kill the Lord, on to next set of corridors.  At one point early on, it is literally "now is the time to strike, but first lets get you a new dress!"  I guess they didn't put in enough corridors before the first Lord and had to pad it out a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the review to end all reviews. To newcomers, this will probably be one of the best JRPG games you'll ever play in your lifetime. To long time Tales fans, this game will heavily disappoint you from a developers standpoint, but will also be the best tales game you will ever play. Thats not to say the game itself deserves bad reviews even though I agree with most of what the bad reviews say.This is the first Tales game that I played. I am heavy on rpg games and I can reassure anyone that plans to purchase the game, BUY IT. The gameplay is phenomenal. I daresay perfect. There are so many elements at play and all of them are really well thought out. The progression of gameplay evolves as you go through the story too. Most reviews are complaining that the progression is too grindy. I'm playing it at the second hardest mode and I find it an acceptable amount of grindy. I've only learned how to play the game as the main character. If that style doesnt suit you, there are 5 other characters to learn with their own unique mechanics. The lifetime of this game is so long! I can easily see myself putting in over 100 hours.The story is more than decent but not good enough for me to say its great (I have not beaten it at this point though). It moves at such a good pace that it'll never get boring. I really enjoyed the adventure the characters experience too. A lot of different setting with their own twist of hardship. The characters are interesting enough by themselves and great when you foil them together. Bonus points for the voice acting too, I simp for Rimwell's english dub.To address the bad reviews - I have never played another tales game so I dont really know what essential skills ppl are referring to thats locked behind DLCs. As far as I'm concerned, I had more than what I asked for while playing through the game and being able to experience more skills through DLCs makes sense to me.The game is hard enough to require the use of items which I think is great. Yah making money to buy them is a little tough and yah you can only hold 15 but I really believe anymore than that would break the game and you'd be able to beat it in a few, dull hours. The game is perfectly hard and if you don't like that, they give you the option to spend $2 for a lot of money. Literally not worth complaining about lmaooIts annoying to see how hard the devs are advertising their DLC while you camp though. Its so in your face that I almost feel objectified. Like I'm some kind of cash cow with disposable income hah.. :(Seriously, buy the game and enjoy. :) Top 5 RPG games with FFX, God of War, Octopath Traveler, Nier Automata cuz im a 2B simp

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Definitely a really good tales game, and is one of the best animeesque/JRPG you can find on Steam. StoryThe story is not something phenomenal or mind-breaking, but it's really something solid and is well thought-out (although many things are predictable). However, while the story is only decent, the characters AND their interactions in this game is extremely enjoyable to watch. The MC is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gigachad. GameplayCombat is an easy to learn hard to master thing. Although IMO combat is a lot more fulfilling early game, where you don't have access to a lot of combat skill, so you have to truly rely on dodging and countering. Late game I find myself to mash more buttons than actually reading the enemy's movement haha. Character power progression is not entirely linear, unlike some of past tales games, so there's room for flexibility in it.GraphicsThere's really not much to say, It's hands down the most beautiful anime-style 3d graphics I've seen. The colors are vibrant, the lighting is stunning, character's faces and their expression and their body movements feel natural. Although one thing to nitpick is, the lip movements sync to the japanese dub, so if you use english dub it might be a little bit disappointing.Audio - SoundThe BGM and soundtracks are decent enough, they fit the theme of the game and nothing feels out of place. However they aren't really something that I'd play on repeat on YouTube, (except maybe the opening soundtrack. English voice acting is really good tho. Erica Lindbeck and Ray Chase pulled the MC and FMC duo really good. As for the JP voice, I can't really comment on them since I played on ENG, but JP dub is rarely bad TBH.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Tales of Arise - A Forgettable and Overblown JourneyRating: 2/5 StarsAs an avid gamer and a fan of the "Tales of" series, I approached Tales of Arise with excitement and anticipation, only to be sorely disappointed by the end of my experience. Tales of Arise is a game that doesn't dare to break any boundaries, and instead, chooses to play it safe to appease the Twitter crowd. The result is a bland, uninspired story that's not worth mentioning, let alone playing through.From the get-go, it becomes painfully obvious that the developers have taken a cautious approach when crafting the narrative, resulting in a story that feels watered-down and overly cautious. The narrative lacks depth, and it becomes clear that the game is geared towards a PG-12 audience. This wouldn't be an issue if it weren't for the fact that the "Tales of" series has a longstanding history of engaging storytelling that caters to both younger and older audiences. With Tales of Arise, the mature gamer is left feeling unfulfilled and excluded.Furthermore, the game's graphical presentation, while initially impressive, quickly becomes overwhelming. Tales of Arise is powered by the Unreal Engine, and it's evident that the developers pushed the engine to its limits. While this results in high-quality visuals, the overabundance of particle effects quickly turns the game into a visually chaotic mess. At times, it's difficult to discern what's happening on screen, detracting from the overall experience.The game's combat system, which should have been a redeeming quality, is unfortunately just as shallow and lackluster as the narrative. The mechanics are simplistic and fail to offer any depth or challenge, leading to monotonous gameplay. The flashy particle effects do little to mask the shallow nature of the combat, and ultimately, the battles feel like a missed opportunity.In conclusion, Tales of Arise is a disappointing entry in the beloved "Tales of" series. With a bland, safe narrative and an overblown visual presentation, the game lacks the charm and depth that fans have come to expect from the franchise. The shallow combat system only adds to the list of grievances, resulting in an experience that isn't worth the time or money for adult gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this one a negative review because of how aggressive they are in pushing DLCs with their fake difficulty at the beginning:-Early on in the game, the first boss will 2 shot you if you don't dodge his attack. You might think this game is hard like Dark Souls? Absolutely not, because it only happens in the first boss. They clearly design the first boss in mind to push people toward DLC like extra levels, gald, and exp.-There will be absolutely no way to make enough money to buy consumable in the early game, side quests give you very little and the items are overpriced at the beginning. They want you to feel powerless and buy that extra gald DLC because the game gets easier once you get more into the game and get more party member. Keep in mind that the fake difficulty is only at the beginning, when you're more likely to buy the DLCs to help out or just try it over and over again. Because the later bosses are just damage sponge like The Division.-They even have the ball to remove the grade shop, which is a staple in the Tales series, there is a clear evident they did it to force you toward the DLC they're selling. Normally you will get 15 item cap in the game, and 30 item cap in NG+. But they remove the item increase because why? For only $4.99 you can get 99 item cap, from the start, yeah man who needs NG+ when you can just pay to unlock it just like a mobile game?-Imaging buying a mobile EA game with extra ingame money, extra exp booster pack, item shop discount, extra SP to get skills easier. WRONG, it's not an EA game, and it's not a mobile game. It's this damn game. It has the ball to notify you that you have new costumes when you rest at a camp fire, like you've just unlocked it, but in reality you have to buy it. Yet it's an in-game ads for their costume DLCs, everytime you rest.If you're okay with playing AC or FIFA game without booster exp and extra help like a mobile game, keep reading as I will get into the game review.The game is decent, no doubt, but not great like the reviews said cause I've played Tales game from 10~15 years ago that is better than this one. It has a nicer graphic than older Tales games cause of the decision to move to Unreal engine. This is probably the best looking JRPG I've played.If you've played other Tales game before, this one will feel familiar cause it changes... nothing? If it's your first then it's a great point to start.The game suffers a FF XIII syndrome since during the story you will walk from corridor to corridor, with unskippable enemy in the way forcing you to fight them. But this game does it a little better since outside the story you can visit bigger area to fish, collect items, and fight mobs. But one good thing undone by another bad thing, the chain system is stupid, basically you have a timer after each batter with 5 level, the more you fight the better the bonus gets. This absolutely forces you to run from mobs to mobs without exploring the map, because if you stop the bonus will go away. This bonus system is designed to go along with the story because you will just run from mob to mob down a long hallway then next to another one. And it's horrible when you're out exploring the bigger section.The combat is just like other Tales game, fun to spam combo. But that's not it, they have to invent new things to mix it up, which is another negative point in this game. So you have 6 party member with 6 different ability to target enemy's weakness. During fights you will have to use their ability to target the exact same enemy, with the exact weakness. If you're fighting a ground enemy and your party member can target another enemy that is flying, you have to MANUALLY switch to that target, and the use that ability. See how dumb it is? Imagine playing a hack and slash game, you have to pause every battle to pick the character with the exact ability and then pick the exact enemy in order for it to work. Why can't the AI just know that there's an enemy that is weak to his or her ability and use it on him?But it doesn't stop there, enemy has a big health pool, for what? This game has a finishing move that require you to chain enough combo to fill up a meter on each enemy and use it to finish them. Like you have to press that button at the right time or the meter will go down and you have to do it again. You HAVE to do that move unless you want to drag the fight which will lower the reward you get. This is how every battle will look like:-Control your main character with target an enemy->Switch to another enemy in the meantime-> Use your other character ability to down them-> Switch back to the original target-> get your combo meter up-> press the finishing move. Rinse and repeat.I don't think the finishing move is bad, but the forced weakness ability is bad as ♥♥♥♥, why do I have to pause mid battle to stunt enemy? Oh yeah the camera will mess you up also, auto changing target whenever it feels like to, this is the worse camera in a Tales game that I've seen.Boss fights aren't good either, you get occasionally good monster boss that feels good to beat cause they're weak to your abilities and that's where that system shines. But the human bosses in this game is just a joke, they're damage sponge, they can't be combo, they aren't weak to ♥♥♥♥ but maybe one ability from the main character. It's just not fun to fight the bosses in this game. Just spam moves faster and be done with it.Let's get on with the story, it's generic like other Tales game, it's cringe, full of anime trope. But the last portion of the game is an absolutely mess, it is purposely designed to artificially make you the game feel longer. Cut scene after cut scene, skit after skit which repeats the same thing you just heard from the cut scene. At some point I didn't care about it cause the cut scene and skip are too long, the game turns into a visual novel at that point. And yeah the last dungeon is mini boss after mini boss, hallway after hallway also, oh yeah, best level design and story telling I've ever seen in a while.7/10This is a good JRPG which is a shame with all the flaws holding it back. Especially the early game that is designed to push DLCs. If you want to buy it I would tell you to wait for the Ultimate Edition to be on sale for a decent price then buy it, or if you don't mind the DLC also wait for the game to be on sale. At $60 you're looking at a game with cut DLCs to sell for extra profit on day one.
