_childDocuments_.review: My last tales game was Tales of the Abyss back in the PS2 era but I've played tons of jrpgs along the way. I wasn't sure why I veered off the tales series when it's supposed to be one of the spearheader of the jrpg genre. Probably because I had many other options and it became one of those things that you put away in a shelf and you're too lazy to bring it back out, but I decided to give ToA a try due to friends' recommendations and its overwhelmingly positive response. I can't say much of the story aspect in this game, it wasn't bad but it's as generic as it can be. Being an anime RPG it also hits all the common tropes that you can think of. The progression is also very predictable and the twists won't surprise you much, especially if you already watched a lot of anime or even any fictions in general.   Boy meets girl, boy gets superpower, girl is strong but can be a damsel when the story demands for it, some guy is ridden with guilt, redemption arc, some girl wants revenge but revenge bad so girl no more revenge but fights for justice, and so on. The characters can be inconsistent too, in one major scene they're all buddies and you'd think it's character development but in the very next scene they revert back to their old personality and flaws before that. All in all it'll probably be frustrating and a bit boring if you have a high standard in storytelling. I'd give the story a 6/10 On the contrary, the gameplay is what kept me hooked for that whole 50 hours. Battles in this game flows extremely smoothly and are very intuitive, it's 100% enjoyable throughout early game all the way through endgame as you discover new spells and abilities that you can choose to obliterate your enemies in thousands of different ways. All 6 characters in the game are fun to play and their playstyles can be chained together to create even more unique combos. After you finish the game there's an extra quest/post game dungeon that you can do and I certainly wouldn't mind spending another 50 hours there just from the gameplay alone. I gotta give it to Bamco for their designs in action based games. I'll give it a 9.5/10 for gameplay, the 0.5 off being that the party AI could be better. On the highest learning curve where you really want to min max you'll probably going to micromanage your party to the T anyway but I'd still think it'll be better if they can be a bit smarter so you can focus on actually doing the fight instead of keeping your party members from dying to stupid stuff.  Progression in ToA is exceedingly linear, which can be a pro or con for some. Sidequests are also mostly straightforward. It's either a fetching quests, finding NPCs, fighting mini-bosses, or doing an extra dungeon with a mini boss at the end. They all have markers on the map with fast travels available, you can definitely finish 99% of the sidequests in the game without referring to any guides. Overall I'll give Tales of Arise a solid 7.5/10, definitely worth to play but probably wait for at least a 50% discount before buying

If you loved the cast in berseria but wanted a better story, more character development and an ending that's actually satisfying, Arise is the tales you have been waiting for.Every party member actually brings something unique to the cast, doing the skits with them is fun as hell and you grow attached to all of them. Sure, there are still "anime clichés" but it doesn't really deteriorate the overall cast. Oh and, maybe i'll need to check but berseria's skits were 2d while arise's are in engine, rendered in 3d, it made the skits more immersive.The combat is FUN, i can't remember the last tales game that made me want to beat the post game content (which is what i'll do the next couple of days) as much as this one. The battle system is pure fun, and it's a bliss to experiment with it.My only problem with the game, is the music, sometimes it's WAY too over the top and it doesn't fit. For exemple, sometimes you explore plains and ruins, and LOTR style music starts to play, it's unfitting to be honest. They could have done better in that regard, i understand Arise is one of the darkest game in the tales franchise but that type of music turned me off in the context in which it was playing.Now for linux and proton:unfortunately, i couldn't get the game running quite as well as on windows with my 4GB RX580. On windows, i run it a 1080p, with AA turned down a notch and it's a solid 75hz for the most part. With Arch linux and the latest proton, it runs below 30fps with the same settings, i found i needed to set the resolution scale to 50% instead of 100 and i also had to drop the shadows to low and resolution to 720p in order to achieve 60fps. Looks to me like proton is eating too much out of my tiny 4gb of vram and because of that, i can't get an acceptable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Really loving this game. The story isn't anything really special, but at the very least it's pretty unique, and brings you to some fun and beautiful locations, despite being rather linear in nature. The characters start off pretty well, fall into a generic trope for a decent amount of time after they join you, and then are fleshed out and made a little more interesting again through late-game quests and exploration. The gameplay is where the fun is for the most part, though the default regular attack button being RB is strange, you get used to it and it doesn't feel too bad. Though I vastly prefer the arte combo system from Berseria which lets you map a myriad of arts, I get why that doesn't exactly fit in this game, because the AG/Soul system changed massively for the better. Like the dodging a lot, much better than quicksteps from the previous entry. Holding LT for your other set of mapped artes feels really strange though, it's best used for spells in most cases, effectively making it pointless for more melee-based spell-lacking characters unless trying to activate Mystic Artes. It's a pretty vast improvement over the previous entry, and a huge step in the right direction. I look forward to the future of this title and the series as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Character Design (10/10)Obviously just my opinion here, but the lead characters in the party, were my favorite out of any tales game so far. Not a single character was TOO overbearing in their own personality. Typically in other Tales games I've found they lean harder into the  "Cares about everyone but only acts irritated and coarse", "Is a literal child who just tends to be annoying by what they can't do or understand" or "The character who you never know if you can trust and seems like their always just one step away from selling everyone out". Also I understand that many of these are done with character development in mind, but to me the payoff isn't worth the wait. Everyone in Arise felt like they each had their own strong developed personality, but still had some growing up to do, or some pieces of their life to come to terms with. It's not the typical, "Look at this annoying kid you hate, but don't worry by act 2 he gets himself together. By far the characters are what made the game for me in Arise.-Story (1st Half) (7/10)A lot of people seem to take issue with the linear nature of the first act, but honestly it's a breath of fresh air, there are twists and turns, but ultimately the goal and hurdles never change overall. Compare this with other Tales games. It seems like you are flowing through 20 different shonen jump arcs, fillers included. I never liked this aspect as it felt like it just dragged the game along for no reason, under the guise of character building, but it never felt like that to me. Arise's first half feels right, I feel like I know where we are in the story progression and I enjoy that.- Combat (8/10)I never completely enjoyed the OG tales combat design, the lack of freedom of movement, and dodge based options make the game felt like combat was 80% prep and strategy, and 20% execution and mechanics. Arise turns this around in my opinion, don't get me wrong it's not perfect, and like with anything, there's only so much you can do to spice up fights after you've been doing it for 30+ hours. However compared to other games in the series I loved the feel of this combat system significantly more.- World/Atmosphere (5/10)Nothing amazing, nothing terrible. You have your snow area, your desert, your lush green lands...etc. Nothing bad, but nothing that impression to a high degree.- Graphics/Character models (7/10)Graphics were great (as to be expected), but what gives this a 7/10 vs a 5/10 is the character models. The models looked incredibly good, many of the previous games in the franchise always had a "childlike flair" to a lot of the character models, almost chibi like. Also to be clear I in no have have any issue with the previous game's art direction, I fully understand that character design evolves and games are always looking to change things up. It's just to me, I enjoyed the character models in Arise more than any other tales games, but again that potentially may just come with the enhanced graphics capabilities.Major Cons:Many of these will be obvious but just want to give my two cents. These have no ranking because even if there were it would be (0/10 - 2/10).- MonetizationThee absolute worst part of this game, 100% no questions asked, done and dusted. I'm sorry but any game that releases a single player RPG that immediately has DLC out to pay for instant levels, instant gald, and from what I hear even skills are locked behind paywalls (apparently due to certain cosmetics having skill traits). That is just silly, I was amazed that there was so much for sale, things that should have either not existed or should have been baked into an easier difficulty in the game. I mean seriously, There are packs that give you -50% CP usage, and +50% EXP gains, discounts in the in game store, and an increase in carry capacity for items. This would all be an issue on it's own. However there is another piece of this puzzle that makes this so much worse.Gald is near impossible for a new player to have going into the game, even with prior experience with Tales games. I'll refer to Vesperia, halfway through the game I had max of every consumable available, and I had a mountain of extra gald just sitting there in case I wanted to buy or upgrade gear. This was because you got Gald from just... leveling. Each fight you would get gald of some amount. However this isn't the case in Arise, The only way you can make money to keep up with how demanding some of the fights become on moderate is by selling gear, selling items, completing side quests, and finding it throughout the world in chests or hidden in certain spots. From experience I can tell you I once dumped everything I had into just getting as much gald as I could. I got up to 10k gald. Sound like alot? Nope it bought me 3 orange gels which will fill up not even half of my CP bar.EXP feels okay in the first half, but fly's off the rails in the 2nd half. There was a point wher I was properly leveled for where I needed to be, then suddenly I'm 10-15 lvls behind, and I'm locked in the story in a different area at that point.My point with Monetization is not only does it's existence feel scummy in it's own right, but as I'm playing, it feels like it was designed to make you pay for that little extra help which you shouldn't have had an issue with in the first place.- Story (2nd Half)Flew off the rails into a way overboard convoluted mess. It felt like the developers had put 90% of their energy into the first half, then just decided, we need to add some sort of crazy twist that makes no sense. Then incorporated a bunch of convenient concepts out of nowhere into the game to make the whole plan work out.Also character choices just completely stop making sense in the 2nd half. Without any spoilers, the focus on morality and hate being so bad that you cannot hold even the worst pieces of the puzzle responsible for their actions just became way to silly. It's like if I created a story where someone went around punching people, a protagonist stops him, then says, what you really need isn't punishment, it's forgiveness. The protagonist then lets him go and is surprised when he punches the protagonist in the face and runs off punching other people. Like come on man, I get that stories like to have moral themes tied to them, but there are times where usage of it just feels out of place and dumb. Even some anime's do this and it feels empty and dumb every time, in my opinion of course.TLDR: Thumbs Up, because I liked the foundation of the game, the characters, the combat and the first half of the story. However it also has some story issues towards the last half of the game and the monetization in the form of DLC is insane and needs to not become the norm, even if it's only $1 - $10.

_childDocuments_.review: My ONLY gripe with this game is the dumbed down AI. In order for Rinwell to cast Sharpness/Concentrate All, the player has to specifically swap to her, losing a good 15 seconds of combat time, allowing all the other characters to take a beating. I cannot, for the life of me, figure out why they would do this.. One simple fix to this would be putting S/C All as an option for the strategy selection. I mean, c'mon, all the predecessors have an option to fill this gap, why have you abandoned it so?? ALl the other stuff is able to be overcome by simple skill manipulation.cancelling but this, this is just atrocious.Beyond that this is probably one of the cleanest and most appealing Tales of games so far. I really loved Tales of Symphonia but this one has held me so far. I originally purchased it a while ago and it got pushed down my list, unfortunately. I am now making a conscious effort to go through my library and complete my games. This is the first one on the list, and so far it has not disappointed. I plan on buying the Pre-Order pack, if nothing else but to be able to leave a review for all the babies who are upset that they paid nothing extra for what I will have to pay $4.99 for. Lol.Ignore all the haters, I suspect most of them are lying about their play style, time, etc. There is one I can think of that says they beat it in 38 hours but wouldn't play again. On record it says they have 62 hours... Just LOL! If you found this combat too easy, you probably had it on story mode. _childDocuments_.review: Good JRPG. I was skeptical at the auto-battle functionality at first, but it made grinding a lot more palatable when I can setup my tactics and let the game run itself. Higher difficulty just made for more spongy enemies, save yourself some headache and hours of your life, just play on a lower difficulty. There's no achievement difference. I might even fire up a NG+ since I was a bit sleepy through some of the early story bits. They repeat themselves quite a bit though, so you'll catch up whether you like it or not. Certain characters have very specific motivations, and they make sure to keep hammering on those points later in the story. The love interests are all very peckish and shy, which makes sense for the kids, less for the older members of the party. The big bad guy at the end could have had more level design around them. The concept was cool, the execution felt a bit rushed. Didn't really see it coming either way, so not bad.If you're going to 100% the game, most of it comes naturally. Make sure you're camping every hour to keep up with your group members. Make sure to check your ranch animals when they're ready. Those were the only real time gated issues. You'll want to keep track of your own fish when you start that part. You don't have to cook every food item, just collect the recipes, which is nice. You DO need to craft pretty much every possible weapon, so don't throw out your old weapons, they're used for upgrades. You can sell your armor as soon as you find something better. The ultimate group battle in the arena doesn't have a pre-requisite, but it'll probably be the last thing you do all powered up. I thought I blazed through it fast, and was about 20 seconds from failing it.Combat, outside of auto-battles, isn't hard to catch on. It IS hard to get your team to use the skills you assign. Thankfully there's no achievements for getting their skills leveled up. Each member has three main skill types that level up, and they unlock additional skills. So the melee fighter has punch/kick/skill, the punch and kick level up naturally, but you'll need to set a tactic to make sure he actually uses his skills in the fights or he will ignore them. Lots of the aerial skills just don't go off naturally, I'm not sure if the AI just doesn't understand they can jump, or they explicitly need a knock-up skill first. For one of the MC's it's about half of their kit, never got that figured out, but they managed fine anyway.All in all, as long as they keep ripping Denuvo out of these games, I'll keep buying them. I've got no patience for garbage DRM in my life, so it's nice when you get a game a year later that's fully patched and tested.

_childDocuments_.review: Tales of is one of those great underrated series that no one knows about, but the ones that do love it to death. This is a great narrative JRPG with a surprisingly involving story. Playing around 3 hours at this time I was able to explore the first area and complete the first boss. I felt the pacing on this game was done well as I never found it too slow or too fast. Where this game shines the most though is the combat. The combat of these games are what keeps people coming back for more, as it is very involving and takes skill to master. I feel they have done the series well by everything they have done with this game as they brought back everything that made the games good as well as expanding upon them. Now there is some flaws in this game as it is not perfect. The main one being how some characters are introduced without any background and you are just supposed to know who they are. I am not really upset about the DLC as it is just a easy mode for extra money. And by no means is this a short game, Tales of games are very lengthy so I will expect you to get as least 50 hours of playtime before the game ends. Overall this is a very great game and as a Standalone game I give it a 9/10. But when comparing it to the rest of the series I would give it an 8/10 as I feel other games like Tales of Vesperia (my personal favorite) and Tales of Symphonia show how amazing a story and character development can be.Also a side note is you need quite a powerful pc to run everything at its full potential as this is the best looking PC game I have. I was able to get by with a GTX 1550 super and a Ryzen 3600 with 12 gigs of ram. This let me run the game at max graphics at only 60fps, so it is clear I will be needing an upgrade soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocre, the only thing going for it is it's one of the very few high budget RPG games to come out recently.Pros:+ Most of the dialogue is voice acted+ There is a crafting system+ Dodge mechanic is nice though game breaking if you get good at it, similar to early God of War in terms of invulnerability+ yay fast travel, tho sadly dissabled during some fetch/talk quests as that would fail the purpose of the quest - to waste time, no it’s not because you would miss a scene in transit there are none.Cons:- story is monotonous and generic- anime disease for anyone over 30 preventing any competence- anyone over 20 is displayed as a 16 year old- gotta love cooking- forced passive perk tree that does not add anything that wasn't previously acquired with levels in other games.- cosmetic system, yay streamers can look different to each other's content now, what about the people that bought the game for whom no effort was spared to craft appearances to match immersion?- The combat system follows in ff15 shoes, it’s a cheap hack by comparison - less than half the features and nowhere near as advanced as star ocean. For anyone that has played the games mentioned this one feels like the copy & paste of the initial formula but the person taking notes never played either game past the first combat scene.Overall its an rpg that will scratch the itch without making you want to blow your brains out while listening to the dragon quest series dialogue/voice acting but unfortunately as far as the story and character development goes its on par with a cookery anime some will love it, i certainly don’t. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Tales games since Symphonia on the Gamecube way-back-when, and have knocked out pretty much every title without exception. Over the years, the franchise has developed a very solid formula which balances interesting stories, solid gameplay, and a bunch of auxiliary systems like cooking which get "reinvented" with each new title. Some of these titles stand out (Abyss), and some just tend to flop into oblivion (Graces F).I mention the latter, specifically, because Graces F had some odd design decisions that tried to compensate for some major deficiencies in the core gameplay loop. While many Tales games forego a world map these days, Graces F was the first to depart from this somewhat historic element, narrowing down the "exploration" element of the game to focus on combat and story so that it could push the next-gen combat system of its time. Unfortunately for Graces F, the combat loop was "all enemies are huge damage sponges, and your damage potential is developed by arte usage" which worked at the time because of the novelty of the system, but got incredibly boring by the end. Most Tales games since have come up with creative ways to avoid the sponge effect while making combat interesting and challenging, but it seems someone forgot the lessons learned with Tales of Arise as this title makes a sharp return to long, belabored fights with minimal rewards that seem only to drag out content. Were it not for increasingly smart AI in the series that actually plays your party members well, I'm not sure I could have stomached the slog for this title, as by the time I got to around the 60% point I was avoided absolutely every fight possible to save myself 5 minutes per trash fight. Most non-human bosses fought get reskinned, and then fought again as normal enemies multiple times...with the same boss HP bar scaling. Sometimes you get multiple bosses together to add difficulty. But at the end of the day, each fight is very repetitious, forcing you to push toward chains in order to bypass absurd enemy health bars. Expect normal fights to be 5 minutes, with bosses taking upwards of 20 at times. It's not a good look given how smooth and fluid Berseria's combat was in the previous release. Given how much cinematic time is present in the game, it's clear this was done to just extend the gameplay time artificially, and it's rather annoying.All that said, Tales of Arise is still a solid installment to the series. The cinematic element to the series was massively overhauled, and this is by far the most aesthetic and beautiful Tales game yet. Outside some light expected social justice / power of friendship nonsense most of the characters feel solid and likeable, and the story fits the Tales formula like a glove without any major hiccups. All the secondary systems like the skill tree return with an acceptable-but-not-memorable structure that feels rewarding to fill out. Fishing and cooking make their return for some reason, and it's my hope that one day the Tales creators will get a bit more creative with these systems and either remove them or stop spending so much budget on their implementation to make room for other novel things. While combat has its flaws, the difficulty curve was still there on many fights, and the "early fights are the most difficult" trend continues on baseline Hard difficulty with some very challenging fights that feel rewarding to complete.It is my hope that Tales of Arise will form a sort of pair system with its successor title in much the same way Berseria did with Zestiria. Zestiria was a relatively mediocre title that touched on all the "necessary" elements well, but felt largely incomplete with a lot of filler...much like Arise. Zesteria was enjoyable the first time through, then felt completely forgettable until all the work Bandai-Namco put in got re-realized with Berseria for the actually good title. As is, Tales of Arise is a good game but is largely forgettable, and has minimal depth to warrant a second playthrough. Definitely on the lower end of the types of titles the franchise puts out, but still decent and not a waste of time for fans of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: It is my first review of any game and I'll try to highlight the reasons I think this game is bad.I've covered pretty much the gameloop by the end of the four hours, beating the first boss, exploring most of the features of the game (combat system, crafting, exploring, etc.)Fighting any monsters feels like trashing a sandbag and the dodging feature isn't responsive at all. So sure, it's flashy and beautiful but that's about it.Crafting is another issue... If your crafting system is about putting the player to a menu and clicking button... it's not crafting, you just changed the way you "buy" your weapon, it's not money but loot which is not relevant because you're going to grind them along the way. they, also, introduced a cooking feature which is the same as the crafting, not relevant.Now, the dialogue are awkard at best. Early in the game, the main protagnist get furious for the use of slavery and what's weird is that he get furious about the reason they used slaves instead of slavery as if slavery was, somehow, okay if put to "good use". Frankly, that was weird.The exploration is another part that can lead to frustation. Basically, you unlock a feature to explore new area. However, you have to use your mana pool to unlock those area. And that is an issue when that mana pool is used to heal your parties. Now, what would you choose if you knew you had a big badass to beat 1. expand your mana pool to explore the areas or 2. skip all the area to preserve your mana pool The game is bad. It looks good but roleplaying game is more than looks, gameplay matters, dialoue matters and so does exploration and they failed all three of them.Now, this is my opinion and anyone is free to think the game is great or bad.

_childDocuments_.review: A long awaited game for the fans in the series finally released. But did it live up to the hype? HELL YEAH! JRPG of the year? perhaps, there's Shin Megami Tensei V waiting in the shadows. Is it a good game in general? Yes, but unfortunately there are some drawbacks.Now i won't tell any part of story or synopsis in the game but all i can say is  in the terms of story and characters. So far this is the biggest weakness from the game. It all start really good then it felt rushed at the end. The villains are really weak and forgetable and there's no strong motivation from them. Even there's a MOMMY TOMBOY GF like Kisara, it didn't save the lackluster of the main story. Well atleast the characters from Arise are a little bit more mature than Berseria crew, except Rinwell and Law i guess but that's understandable considering by their age. So yeah... this is so far my biggest dissapointment it's still good, easy to follow but not as good as Berseria or even Abyss, but the very least the ending in this game is really satisfying and i can guarantee to that.Now this is the biggest strength of the game the combat is really-REALLY dope and addicting! i'll take  combat anyday. Fans of Abyss and Symphonia will be feel right at home with the combat but with additional 3D movement. Sidequest are fun and there's alot of monster hunting in the game, also there are super tanky optional boss waiting for you to test your skills and strength. The difficulty in this game is actually step-up from Berseria for instance: the Instense difficulty in Berseria is actually a normal difficulty in Arise and hard difficulty is literally hard! Those who complaining with Berseria for being too easy won't be complaining no more. There's also a chaos difficulty but you need to complete some sidequest first and then it will be unlocked. However there are some negative though with enemies and bosses for being too sponge throughout the game.Voice acting are really good both ENG and JP dub, but JP is still superior. It's weird actually for me because in Berseria i prefer with ENG dub with Magilou, Velvet and Eizen comes to mind for being the best one and then i heard Magilou's VA is now become Shionne's VA. I was exited at first but unfotunately it didn't live up as good as Magilou was, i don't think this is her fault but more like the character's fault. Shionne is just become a flat character sometimes.Now the music though... Well it is forgetable the only thing that i could remember is the battle music that's it. Both Opening songs are really great though and the theme song become my favorite track.Don't get me wrong the game is really optimized and ran flawlessly on my system but there are some technical isuues that needs to be addressed:- Low draw distance by default and you cannot change it in the game setting (because there is none). Although there are already mods that can fix it you can check in the forums.- Sometimes there's audio stuttering when entering or exiting areas but nothing to often.- Lack of center channel speaker if you're playing with surround sound setup (Mine is 6.1 audio setup with Yamaha receiver). The dialog are actually coming from both Left and Right channel. Again it's weird because Berseria dosen't have this kind of problem. i'm aware in Berseria there's also a simmilar problem but this is different, atleast in Berseria the dialog audio are actually coming through my center channel speaker, as it should be.So in my suggestion just playing it with stereo mode but with matrix decoder applied.Tales of Arise despite with weak storyline this game is definitely a must play for JRPG's fans. The combat alone will make you forget how weak the storyline was. This is become my favorite game since Tales of the Abyss and Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of DANA.  8 / 10Edit: After playing both SMTV and TOA i have to say that SMTV won GOTY for me. _childDocuments_.review: It's undoubtedly one of the best Tales of - Games in the series. The complete graphical overhaul, the animation, the story as well as the atmosphere are great. The cast of characters is well-written and their relations to each other is elevated by the, more than often, very humorous conversations at the campfire. The fighting system is mechanically at its peak, each character feels so different but also satisfying. But there are a couple of downsides as well: - While the story itself is solid, it does feel rushed at the beginning, it kind of feels like, they wanted you to unlock every character as fast as possible, before getting into the second half of the game. - The soundtrack fits each area respectively, but feels rather bland at times (not counting the fighting themes, those are pure fire)- The world design is rather linear at times, which makes some areas feel empty. - In order to get every achievement and unlock every aspect of the game, you have to beat it once. That in itself isn't too bad, but there is a lack of things to do, namely: - Last point is a spoiler regarding a certain dungeon:  To summarize: Yes, the game is great and I really recommend it to every JRPG fan out there. Those dedicated enough will have fun getting every achievement as well. But I would wait for a sale, cause 60 Euro is still a bit too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: + Decent story. Seriously the story is interesting.+ Improved gameplay compared to previous tales series+ Gorgeous visual art+ Love to see each skits, the conversation is interesting. You get know each of the character from the skits.+ Beautiful ost- The same as previous tales series, the combat is too repetitive, feels a bit boring. - There are plot holes with the story, but it's still oke.Despite of the flawless, tales of arise is the best tales series at the moment, in terms of graphics, story, and gameplay. Combat is improved, but still repetitive and you will feels boring at some point. For me, it's the story that keeps me playing the game. The story is interesting. Tales of arise and scarlet nexus easily become my favorite games this year.

_childDocuments_.review: 25 hours in, I am really enjoying it.  I have played most of the US released tales games since Tales of Destiny, and feel that this fits in the upper echelon of the series. Some of the villains to this point have been underwhelming, to the point that I can't even remember their names, but in the 3rd area I feel they introduce some complexity to the formula of the story. _childDocuments_.review: Pleasing game, played it almost every day. The extra stuff you can buy isn't necessary, but I bought some outfits just because I enjoyed the game, so it was my way of saying thank you.The story was very nice and it just so happens certain wars have been brewing and I played it during that happening next door so it made me think harder when listening to the story and what it has to say, it felt more special, like I had some wise things that it had to say to consider. The game play was fun and simple. The maps were comfortable, I picked up everything without trouble as I was running around, I'd fight every battle and do every side quest. I never needed any exp boosts or anything.  I liked the winter area lot as soon as I got there.In the end I played it purely from enjoyment, I didn't feel like I was forced to finish it, I wanted to finish it. If there was something just like it made years later, yet again, with different character, story, world, perhaps some other meaningful things to ponder about, that is welcomed by me. Just don't make the characters have the same personalities, I notice this a lot in such games, one of the main character's always moody and the other one is cheerful, you know? Perhaps you can make two moody characters that help each other open up or two cheerful ones etc. Don't stick to the same personalities.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about the Game? Well im playing Tales Games since Xillia on PS3 till now and I have to say that Arise is by far my favorite Game, finished the story yesterday and I really enjoyed the Journey of the Game. But let's go into Detail.The first thing that I noticed in Tales of Arise is the change of Topic's to a more "grown up" direction. You will notice that the Story is a lot about Death and Freedom, that could be related to modern day problems so that's a thing I like about the Storytelling in the Game. In General there are a lot more of Problems that People encounter nowadays, but not everyone will notice this references unless you are a victim of them, than you will notice right away to what it is referring to. Trust issues, Handling death of beloved People, Dealing with the past, Depression and many more Topics are part of the Story. While you play through the Story there is always a hint how you can get through these stages of life, all you need are good friends (and maybe a special someone) and that's a beautiful message, even tho it is hard to find this type of Friends in this times, but if you find them keep them near you.Well, there is nothing much to say. The music is just awesome and is spreading Dark Souls vibes at some places and I really like it. I think that this time the Combat System evolved to be almost perfect. Smooth Combos with a lot of possibilitys to fight the enemy and what I liked the most the Counter-System for certain Enemys. For every Situation there is a Counter against the Enemy -> Enemy is casting a Spell = Yoink interrupted and its mine now ; Enemy is charging at you = * Bonk * you shall not pass. There may be not that many Types of Enemy's but who cares (me not) the Combat system is fun and versatile. The only sad thing is that Alphen get's only a few Arte and only some of them are really usefull. Not that much to say, it's gorgeous with the Upgrade to the Unreal Engine.If you are playing on German Sub try not to get triggered to much, there are a LOT of Grammar mistakes in the Translation.Not every Side-Quest is completeable after you get them furthermore there is no Recommendation whitch Level you need for them (strange enough that a Recommendation is at the Challenge Arena but not at Side-Quests) so prepare to die if you want to do certain Quests because there is a Level difference of 20+

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, some of the best combat a JRPG has ever produced. I'm a big fan of the character switching (similar to FF7R) to maintain combos. While you could just as easily spam 1 or 2 attacks, the game rewards you generously for developing skill. So much care went into the characters and their sometimes stereotypical banter, you forget if you've heard it all before. This game made me smile or laugh out loud at least once, every session, no exaggeration. This game will go down as one of my favorite all time RPGs. And wow, is it gorgeous. If you like deep systems and a pretty engaging story, you should get it. And 100%, you DO NOT NEED DLC to enjoy it! If you want to make the game way too easy, go ahead, but the raw experience is stellar. I was reluctant to get this, and I am incredibly satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 Great JRPG experience packed with content.Liked:StorySide QuestsFinding secrets / hidden objects / recipesCharacter BuildingCombat with exceptionsCharacter Customization with exceptions.Dislike:DLC for outfits.  Really....WOW there even overpriced jeez.Weapons have skins but Armor you pickup does not.  BOO!My biggest complaint.  Combat Strategy for now single player only Tales game lacks targeting arguments.  (Target My Target/Target Lowest HP/ Target Highest HP/ Stay Close to Enemy/Stay Far From Enemy/ Etc...)  For a single player game I have to rely on the AI for I need more control.  This is forgivable with multiplayer but not for single player experience and makes it harder to build combo's for finishers.  Maybe I just overlooked it but I did not find this in the combat styles for AI behavior.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Overall the content felt balanced and very enjoyable.  At times there were long skits of story followed by running around to each character and having to talk to them after already listening to cut-scenes.  I started skipping this story dialog a bit because I can only handle so much story at once so maybe keep the spacing sparse throughout with story/action and only heavy during the start and ending but it was not too bad and did not detract at these times too much. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conciense recommend this game to anyone, even if the game has a lot of good stuff in it.The reason is the game is on purpose making you run out of GALD at every corner, making you thing you may have to spent real money to buy GALD. The way they do this is by simply draining you  of CP (MP if you want to call it that) and HP. As you progress through the story this becomes even more apparent, because dungeons become longer with no specific reason but to make you fight endless waves of enemies to which some of them are totally HP sponges so your characters keep using CP until you are out. They even slap you in the face by making you go through the last dungeon twice just for the sake of you spending more of your items, and making you fight enemies that literally drain around 30% of your CP every battle. HP and CP items are REALLY expensive in this game, for no apparent reason but to make you run out of GALD.Now you may think is becuase my characters are weak, well here is the other thing, the game does not allow you to be any stronger that  what you should be at any specific point. They do this by literally reducing by a great margin the amount of EXP you receive if you are only one level higher than the enemies you are facing. So basically you will be facing wave after wave of enemies with never getting the upperhand, at this point i dont know why even call it an RPG. At the end it becomes apparent that is better just to avoid the enemies instead of fighting them, until in purpose they close up the hallways so you have to forcefully face the enemies.I dont understand why most people are prasing this game, when is doing questionable practices, because if BANDAI NAMCO wanted to be fair it would at least reduce the price of the items at least by half its current price to be more fair to the player. But since they want to sell GALD for real money they hike the prices so you will run out, in hope that you will spend your money to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise is My ARPG of the year.The graphic style is top shelf and is uber crisp and stylized, I currently get a pretty solid 144 FPS on a RTX3080 so it runs very smooth. _childDocuments_.review: Out of the tales series, this is my all time favorite.The combat is refreshing while keeping it tales tradition, which is great because it's one large reason i stayed away from a few of them.The show though is the story, amazing topic choice, they weren't afraid to not steer off heavy matters of slavery and oppression giving light to a topic most aren't comfortable to depict.All the characters are well fleshed out and none i find are just their to fill the party, having their own wants, desires, fears and personalities.I will admit though for half the game i was not a fan of rinwell as i found very whiny with the matter of hating the Rana, she has the rights to, but it could of been handle better so she doesn't come off and annoying.The does get a growth after close to half way in the game that makes her very likable.Besides that gripe i am happy with the whole experience.What i found fascinating is instead of just putting post game dungeons to LVL grind they do so, but with a reason and it's own story inside with cameos from past tales games, very well done and not punching the time card till the very end.Overall, great game for both tales fans and none tales fans, a great starter game for newcomers.Happy hunting ^v^

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: The game runs great, it's visually pretty good, the plot is standard JRPG faire but that's what JRPG fans generally want, if you just want yet another JRPG game, ignore the rest of this review and go get the game because you get exactly that. If you're expecting a Tales of Game with better visuals don't even think about it.Zestiria and Symphonia had "real dungeons" where every one of them has a gimmick. Not in this one. Its the same thing over and over again until you've defeated a lord. There is no Symphonia "Mana Ring" which changes every dungeon or anything - its just a straight forward path to the Lord and you are done - no gimmick at ALL and it repeats itself on your path to the next lord. There is no "old-school Dungeon feel" at all.The combat is my biggest gripe, it's fundamentally broken due to extremely poor AI and systems that just don't work well on anything bigger than standard trash fights. Opponents need to be broken with normal attacks in order to chain combos together, however only small normal enemies can be broken, meaning your strategy devolves into spamming your strongest single arte during bosses or larger enemies. While the plot is serviceable, it has several moments that really don't make sense in the wider context, and several character interactions, particularly in the first half of the story that are just annoying. This does improve the closer you get to the end of the game though.My biggest problem though, and the reason this game is only a "7/10" is it's horrendous DLC practices that not only offer boosters and costumes, but push adverts into the game and lock abilities behind a paywall (Titles through DLC costumes). Another negative Point is the sometimes cringe writing where 8/10 Skits in the middle of the Game starts with a "sigh" and the typical: "Whats wrong (ENTER_NAME-HERE)?" with your typical deep lore answer of: "Stop caring so much about me (ENTER_PROTAGONIST HERE)". Its more annoying than anything else.The Last Dungeon was absolutely garbage (No spoilers dont worry) → Its just a dungeon with the same rooms over and over for an hour and its not taking long because its hard or anything but they throw at you Mini bosses. Nearly all of them are MINI-BOSSES... Its not hard or anything but especially on "moderate" or "hard" the enemys are not hard - just sponges where a mini-boss takes 5mins to kill even if you're overleveled.Cons:- Devs should stop forcing victims to "forgive" everything. That's just not how things work. The whole story revolves around the theme of forgiveness and coexistence and I found how they delivered the message very unsettling. If they are dealing with colonialism in stories, they should've been a lot more sensitive.- Characters are absolutely cliché of the "Sigh" type of skit vibe. Every Skit is the same blabla of "Sigh - how you feeling / doing" and your typical answer of "Its none of your business" and then your typical party members of: "Is he/she really allright? :(" yeah....- lack of monster variant. they mainly play with the colour palette change and there are like what? 10 enemys in total just with a different color?- Microtransaction seems really bad. I didn't buy any of the DLCs seperately since I bought the ultimate edition (Tales of game uknow) but I could see where BN was going at.- Character inflation in battles is seriously off. I'll mark as spoiler since you can find names here: - Field monster health was unnecessarily high and I just don't quite get why... The Devs just don't bother to add any interesting skills or patterns in higher variants of the monsters, but instead just add a tonne of health. Literally just sponge (played on moderate)- UI/UX was oddly uncomfortable. You can't access the map from the menu and you can't access the quest menu from the map. I was consistently irritated by this toward the end.Neutral:- Soundtracks were kind of "bland". The most memorable ones were actually the returning tracks, like the field boss themes. Pros:- Art Direction is gorgeous!!! The environment and the character graphics were so pretty. Honestly this is one of the most gorgeous art I've seen in a video game.- Combat is very cool. Fast-paced and engaging, and the cutscenes for the skills were also cool (Even though you kind of spam the same skills over and over later on)- Battle camera was very, very, good (Despite a handful of exception / fights). I've played Vesperia, Symphonia and Zestria and none of those had very good cameras, it seems like I made some good improvements over the years.- I wasn't too in for the chain battle system at first, but quickly got very fun. It compliments the fast-paced combats very well.- Fishing is weirdly fun...- I loved the references to the previous Tales games.- First half of the game was very engaging and interesting. Second Half interesting as well but the copy&paste Dungeons and mini-boss sponge enemys the game throws at you was just a drag period.I have more cons than pros but this game was fun enough. The first half of the game was seriously great.  The ending was somewhat "underwhelming" and I kind of felt a "relieve" after finishing the game or... atleast after the final Dungeon.All in all, it's a bog standard tales game, with worse combat than previous entries and worse DLC. Get it if you like tales or are a massive JRPG nut, otherwise there are far better tales games out there for you to enjoy.If you want a good JRPG Game with a lower price but not so "pretty" visual-wise - check out "Trails in the Sky":

_childDocuments_.review: I play Tales games since Phantasia Era (while I am sure majority of downvoters here didn't even play Eternia), and I am confident to say that I am a veteran JRPG gamer. This game is good, even great if we talk about present time. Nowadays it's hard to find a good JRPG like this title, so if you're a big JRPG fans, get this game.I don't usually write a review for games that I bought, but I just can't stand kids mentality anymore. I or lets say "We" for any veteran gamers, came from "no DLC" era, so we don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about any DLCs as long as the main experience stays the same, and it does for Tales of Arise.You can beat the game just fine without any DLCs on the highest difficulty, you just need to learn and understand the battle mechanic. I hear some people complained about CP and SP, it's not a problem I assure you guys. CP is like a shared MP, which is better because more than half of your party don't even use magic, so less micromanaging each healer to keep up with their MP. Some people here said that there's not enough SP to learn all of the titles, WRONG, you can easily max all of the titles within 1 playthrough. I stopped playing after beating the last post-game boss and still have more than 10K unused CP.The story is just fine, like any other good JRPG. It's not outstanding but it has some twist here and there, just like Kiseki minus the massive world building. But, still, I can find any other JRPG without massive world building except Suikoden and Kiseki. Mind you that JRPG is all about anime tropes, that's why we like JRPG. And I found that this game is on less-cringe side because there's no useless fanservice (no lolis etc, that's good!).Now lets talk about the difficulty. Anyone who says this game is hard or not properly balanced surely hasn't played any JRPGs post PS3 or even PS2 era. Arise doesn't require you to grind crazily like Ys 3: Wanderer From Ys, early Final Fantasy, etc. The ability to beat a boss is still on your hands, it's not like you're hopeless againts bosses' ultimate move by the next turn. You can even dodge every atacks if you're good enough. So for old JRPG gamers, this game is like a breath of fresh air after countless easy JRPGs where you can just 1-hit the final boss.TL;DRFrom a honest veteran JRPG player's perspective, buy this game, it's good.Edited for the sake of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ autumn badge.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played a few tales games, however I've loved each one. I had been hyped about this game for over a year and was checking for news constantly. Now having finished it, I can say Arise is the best tales game I've played. The story was really well done, paced, and executed. It didn't leave me with any questions at the end, and was really satisfying the whole way. The gameplay was great too. It was really addicting, and every character's play style helped keep things fresh and engaging. The visuals are huge step up from previous games, and the scenery was beautiful. Lastly, and my favorite part of the game, the characters. The cast here is one of the most well written I've seen in any game. Alphen was a really engaging protagonist and his story and growth was one of the best parts. Shionne made for an excellent heroine, and her and Alphen's relationship was handled beautifully. Rinwell's development and backstory was incredible, and was one of my personal favorites. Law was the definition of a bro, and his motivations made him a great character. Kisara's role in the group made her really likable and fun to watch. Dohalim was both a badass and hilarious at the same time, and is easily one of the best characters in the game(also he got drip). Overall, Tales of Arise is my favorite game of the year, and easily in my top 5 of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an utter disappointment. It took a lot of willpower to slog through to the credits rather than abandoning the game. Tales of Arise was supposed to be the start of a new era for Tales of games since they had been using the Xillia engine for 10 years at that point but it's not looking good.- There is basically no chemistry between the characters outside of Alphen and Shionne. The pairing of Law/Rinwell and Kisara/Dohalim felt incredibly forced, especially for the former two.- The game feels like its a relic of the past. And I don't mean the "paying homage to classic games" way. No, unfortunately not. While the game has some semi-large open areas in the start to traverse, after a few hours it reverts to exclusively throwing hallways at you. Hallways that are narrow with enemies at every corner which you can't avoid because everything is so cramped. Everything looks so lifeless, the dungeons, the cities, ... even games from 20 years ago looked more lively. You will constantly be confronted with invisible barrier when you think that it should be possible to jump down a ledge. It's like they ran out of budget because they spend everything on animations and voice acting so there was no money left to properly design the world.- The combat just flat out sucks. Enemies have way too much HP, especially bosses and mini bosses. The fights against normal enemies are basically "hit until you can strike and then strike them to execute them". The strike attacks look cool but they lose their novelty after a couple of hours and I'd wish for a regular combat system.- What even is the story. Just like the world design, it feels like they ran out of budget after the lords of the crown contest got defeated. The story after the last lord got defeated is one giant mess and I would have actually liked the game a lot more if it had ended at that point.- The pacing is atrocious. You'll constantly get slow and long cutscenes which are immediately followed up by 3+ skits which are also long and slow. This is especially bad towards the end of the game where this happens within walking 5 meters over and over again. I actually started skipping the skits towards the end because I just couldn't take it any more. Awful, simply awful.The only positives I have to say about the game are:- Hootle is pretty cool- the artstyle is great- the game ran great on the SteamDeck

Get it on sale or skip it completely.

_childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise had me infatuated in the first half of the game. Loved Alphen and Shionne and the other party members. You can tell the studio had a bigger budget for this title because the world was breathtaking and I thought the UI was slick. I was really digging the story until the second to late stages of the game where it kind of fell apart. The ending was OK, and I'm happy with the conclusion of our party member's individual stories, but the world building and story as a whole fell flat for me. The villain was absolutely underwhelming as well. There's a few big negatives that I'd like to share below, one of them being monetization that is getting a bit more insidious and affecting the game in significant ways. Overall though, I think the positives outweighed the negatives for me and I'm recommending it - I think it was worth the full price I paid minus the deluxe/ultimate edition. On a sale - definitely worth a buy. Just keep in mind the monetization used here and your comfort level supporting it.

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/5I'm never sure with these ratings if I'm supposed to rate my subjective enjoyment or the objective quality of the product.  Because asides from better graphics, Tales of Arise is objectively just more of the same, but I subjectively still love it.  Bandai Namco, the studio behind the Tales series, was and still is keenly aware that the Tales series is aging after 25 years of reiterating the same game: Action JRPG with anime aesthetic.  That's why the studio put the series on hiatus after 2016's , which itself was meant to be a sendoff after the series' 20th anniversary.  But the strong sales of  prompted the studio to take one more crack at it.Tales of Arise was supposed to revitalize and evolve the series.  However, the only major "evolution" here is the graphics, which look amazing thanks to a new engine running on Unreal 4.  A new coat of paint doesn't disguise that everything else, like gameplay and story, is the same as what we've seen from the series over the past 20 years.  So objectively the game fails at "evolving" the aging series.  But personally, I'm fine with that.  I've enjoyed previous Tales games, and Tales of Arise is more of what I like.  Perhaps I'm biased by the fact that the majority of the Tales games have only recently been released on PC and Steam, so it's still new to me.  Even if it doesn't evolve the series, it still showcases with it's enhanced graphics the best of what made past Tales games so great and memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: To put things into perspective, I've played quite a few "Tales of" and here's what I think of the ones I remember the most : Tales of Symphonia was fantastic, Tales of Vesperia was great, Tales of Zestiria was bad, Tales of Berseria was okay. With that being said, I think Tales of Arise is... Great !The graphics, the first thing you see, are better than in Berseria. I like this style a lot more and they make some regions look gorgeous. That goes for the fights too, as the special artes look really good and after playing for 50+ hours, I still haven't grown tired of them. The game runs smoothly, despite some pop-up here and there and I have had pretty much no lag with a 5 year old graphics card. That's a good thing to note considering the amount of special effects happening, often at the same time, especially during combat.Those fights, and the gameplay in general, is what makes Tales of Arise one of the best entries in my opinion. They're fluid, fast-paced, and rely on dodging instead of blocking like some of the previous games. That makes a world of difference in the heat of the moment and encourages you to learn enemy attacks to benefit from well-timed dodges. You assign artes to buttons, create your combos, see what works and what doesn't, see what you like and what you can chain together with or without party members... That's really pleasant, and you can play with the teammate you want when you feel like it ! When you don't control them, the Ai does a pretty good job, especially when it comes to healing which is the most important. And if you're still not satisfied, there's a lot of tweaking possible in the menus. This lets you focus on what you want to do, and avoid frustration.In terms of difficulty, the game opted for something a little different. Enemies that are higher level than you will give a lot of experience, but as soon as you outlevel them, they will give basically nothing. This means you will always be at a "correct" level, but never overleveled, even if you wanted to be. I liked it, as bosses were always a decent challenge this way. This also means that "grinding" for experience is pointless, and a neat little system allows to farm quickly for materials, where the more enemies you fight in a row, the more drops you get. Smart and convenient.Those drops and the materials you find on the map are used in cooking and crafting. Cooking is done while resting, outside or in an inn and confers various bonuses to your party. More Defense, health recovery, or even more drops after a fight. Crafting consists of creating new and stronger weapons for your party or accessories that you can adapt to the situation at hand. You're struggling against a boss that uses mostly wind artes ? Gather the materials and craft an accessory that reduces wind damage by 50% ! It's that simple ! I tried (I really did) to get into crafting in Berseria but I never felt comfortable with it. Here it's much simpler and really intuitive, even the most advanced "transfer" option becomes obvious and fun after a while. You won't be able to use it to its full potential before the end-game, but you also won't need it. And it makes something to look forward to ! Crafting is also a success !On to the story ! While it starts off as seemingly naive and classic, it evolves into something more interesting with enough twists and revelations to make it worth following for those who care, until a decently satisfying ending. The characters you interact with ; mainly your party members ; help a lot in this regard as they're all pretty nice. I'm usually very quick to hate a character for random reasons, yet here, and after 50+ hours, I still appreciate them all. That's not to say they're all interesting, but they never become obnoxious or annoying and that's a plus.The english voice acting is good, rarely over the top or forced, and the music doesn't feel repetitive. The banter between the characters during and after the fights adds a nice touch, and somes lines are pretty fun.Now, Tales of Arise may be a successful entry but the game is not without its flaws. I'll go over the main gripes I have with it quickly.First off, I found the main quest great, but the side quests mediocre. They're all either " Kill 6 of this type of monsters ", or " Kill this giant high level enemy ". I wouldn't call those side quests, errands maybe ? Boring.The second issue I have, although this one only occurs late game, is the amount of special effects during the fights. When many things happen at once, especially with the bosses, it can be hard to tell what's going, so you just wait for the pretty lights to dissipate.Then you have the matter of the Dlcs. When I first saw you could buy stuff like "Double Xp" I got scared the game would be designed to be grindy on purpose. Fortunately, this isn't the case and you can't really be overleveled so I may not like the concept of Dlcs, but they're not really a problem here. More of a very small bonus.Another minor thing to note is the quality of the subtitles. I know most people won't mind, but I did. Probably due to the translation, a few sentences sound weird in English, and there's quite a few mistakes in all these lines of dialogue. You have the basic spelling mistakes or inversions of two letters that are not too bad, but you also have very ugly ones, like in "This is you're destiny"...More problematic is the lack of post-game content. There's basically only one dungeon and a few extra bosses designed to take you quickly to level 100. I would have like more. Oh well.Last but not least, here's the main issue I have with the game. The enemy variety. There's about 10 (10 !) basic enemies that you will see over and over. And no, changing the color of their arms or putting a flower on their head doesn't make a new enemy, I'm sorry. They may be stronger and darker, but they're the same model I was fighting in the first region ! Not cool ! I even think double that amount would not have been enough. That's unfortunate and the one problem I really can't get over.Tales of Arise is a really good game, and a great improvement over the latest entries. The strongest point is the gameplay as the fights have never felt this fluid and fun before. The game looks beautiful, the characters are good and the story worth playing. I wanted to give the game a 9, but I can't ignore the enemy variety. Only 10 variations for a 50+ hour game ? Seriously ? That's a shame but it shouldn't stop anyone from playing it, fans of the series or simply those looking for a good Rpg. Great game, and I'm now looking forward to the next entry in the "Tales of" series ! An .

_childDocuments_.review: Let's cut to the chase, is it a good game? Yes. Is it a great game? No. Visually, I'm in awe that that the Tales series has gone from an often generic, unoriginal, and bland look to something that truly is a delight. The landscapes feel original and and makes you feel like you will get a sense of wanderlust..............if you could. There is not an open world map and each location is extremely limited. This is a shame. The towns and cities also feel limited by not being able to go inside buildings unless it's directly involved in the objectives of the story. The voice acting is great and the characters have their own charisma.  Most bosses do have plenty of personality, but the last boss feels pretty shallow with little to no motivation why he is the way he is..... other than the game requires a final boss. A lot of dialogue is rehashed to the point of annoyance. It's like the game is trying to force the messages down your throat. The battling is fun, but I don't recall a jrpg with such a limited enemy list. When you go to new areas it feels like you're fighting the same monsters with a "new coat of paint". A lot of times their moves are so similar to previous monsters that you won't really  need to adjust how you fight. There is a farming option........but it's pretty meaningless unless you're the type to what to get 100% completion on obscure things. The music is perhaps the most enjoyable and memorable that I've heard in any Tales games. I know that I've critiqued the game a lot, but it's still worth playing and the overall ending is one of the most satisfying that I've played in a long time.   I would give it a 8.25 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise did really a nice work to bring out an emotional and memorable journey. The game’s main plot is quite simple and not really complicate. It’s true that there are plot twists (good ones), but the point remains still: it’s not hard to understand. Tales of Arise didn’t try to tell a complicated story with tons of layers of meaning or philosophies. Instead, it chose a simple one, but focused on build up the soul of it: the main characters. And that is definitely the golden part of this game. Tales of Arise has 6 main characters, everyone has their own story, their own past and motive. Throughout the first part of the game, the relationship between them will be gradually formed and developed. Surely it will take time to understand all of them, but as you reach the second part of the game, you will understand them better and you’ll definitely love them. Of course, the most interesting relationship is between Alphen and Shionne - the male and female protagonist. I can only say that much, because you’ll have to figure out yourself by playing the game. The story may sometimes feel slow and probably tedious at some points, it’s not a strange thing with a JRPG, so if you haven’t played JRPG before, keep that in mind. And please, don’t skip those mini conversations between characters (the game calls it “skit”), because that is the unique thing of the Tales series, and those skits will definitely help you understand more about the characters. Perhaps the most disappointing part of the story is the antagonists. There are many of them, but in the end, maybe you’ll no longer remember who they were or even their names. Their personalities are nothing special, nothing memorable. They are “villains” simply because the story told them so. Comparing to the excellent and memorable main characters, the villains of this game is simply boring and forgettable.The gameplay mechanics are not really complicated. It’s true that there are tons of Artes to remember, but you will learn them one by one. The combat is easy to understand, but to master it and fight effectively, it will take a decent amount of time. You will need to combine different artes to form an effectively combo. The good thing is that maybe you’ll only have to do that for your main playable character in the party, the rest will fight just fine on their own. That’s the way I played, but if you’re a more strategist person, you may want to setup the artes for all the 6 characters by yourself, it’s your choice. Another thing you may want to keep in mind that this game is a RPG, and that means it’ll have lots of side quests and grinding. Doing all of the side quests is not necessary, but definitely worth your time with about 50% of them. Grinding is highly recommended, because that’s the only way you can gather the materials to craft your weapons and armors. Perhaps what I didn’t like most about the combat is that most of the time, there are so may visual effects in screen, and it’s so difficult for me to locate the whereabouts of the characters and the enemies. It’s still fine in Normal difficulty, but for the above ones, that’ll be a big problem.Last but not least, the music is still good, that is not a surprise, given the fact that Tales series always good with it, just like many other JRPGs. The composer for this game is Motoi Sakuraba, and she did a fine job with all the background musics. It’s not something extraordinary, but it’s good. The 3 theme songs - “Hibana”, “Blue Moon” and “Hello, Again” is truly ear-catching and memorable. Those animation cutscenes are good too, given the fact that they were made by Ufotable.I’m not a hardcore fan of Tales series, and I just played Vesperia and Berseria before. But to me, Arise is a really good Tales game, someone may call it the best Tales so far. Surely I will not say it, but Arise is truly an excellent game. If you’re a JRPG fan, or especially a Tales fan, then this game is highly recommended.

It is not aiming for realistic graphics but rather somewhat like a painting like texture set.Characters:The characters are well designed and very likable. The voice acting is also on point. The character dialogues and interactions are also entertaining and showcases their personalities well.Gameplay:This game gives the player plenty of stuff to do other than grinding for levels such as fishing, gathering materials for crafting items, and even growing animals in a ranch. But the best part of the game for me is of course the battle system.It is very satisfying to chain in combos and even juggle the enemies in the air, keeping the combo counter running and then unleash a devastating finisher. _childDocuments_.review: As of right now I cannot recommend this game as it has way too many problems for a AAA game at launch.  From the start you may or may not be able to use your controller if you do not have Steam setup a very specific way, (i.e., you cannot use Steam beta, must disable enhanced Xbox controller features manually if using an Xbox controller, etc.).  Once you are able to get the controller to work, that's when all the other technical issues the game has start.  For example, the game will auto detect the highest available resolution of any monitor you have connected to your PC and hard set that resolution without letting you change it to something else.  Running a multiple monitor setup with any combination of 1080p, 2k, and/or 4K (both 3840x2160 monitors and 4096x2160 TVs), the highest resolution device connected to your PC will be used.  Good luck if you're using a TV pushing 4096x2160 and have a mid-tier to low end graphics card.Next let's talk about draw distance and pop-up graphics issues the game has.  I have never seen a AAA game have such a short draw distance and pop up to the player's character.  NPCs and other in game objects will literally not spawn until they are about five feet from your character.  Now at first, I thought this was a graphics setting issue, but I quickly found that it was not.  Setting all graphics options to their max settings still produces the same results for draw distance and object pop up.  That is unacceptable for a AAA title.Next, I would like to talk about the writing in the game.  The story itself is interesting enough from what I have played, (still in progress play as of this review), but the writing itself is on the level of a high schooler writing a fanfic.  There are grammatical errors and misspellings throughout, and I am only 11 hours in.All in all, the game has some potential, but needs to finish its development cycle with patches before I will recommend purchasing.  As it stands today (09/13/2021), there have been no patches released for the game since it launched.  I honestly do not even know if patches are in the works at this point as Bandai Namco has not posted anything on Steam since the launch.

_childDocuments_.review: More of a neutral review honestlyTL;DR - terrible story even by trope filled anime standards - good combat, if you're ok with a long JRPG with a bad story/writing then go ahead and grab it.The bad: The story is a mess, it's so cliche and predictable that I can't help but cringe during most of the main story scenes. Many key plot points seem good but fail if you think about them for a few seconds or had the camera zoomed out (smokebomb allowing people to escape a half encirclement in an open area...? just one of many).Additionally there is a large disconnect between character power and perceived power - fight an easy battle against 2-3 enemies in 10 seconds just to get a cutscene where you're overwhelmed by a whole 3 more enemies... really? Initially wrote this off as "first 6 hours were a tutorial so whatever I guess" but it just keeps happening :/Large disconnect between story relationships/attitude and the skit attitudes which is jarring. You'll have characters being friendly in one interaciton set at a specific point then a story cutscene where they're behaving totally different to each other.  It's not like they're triggering out of order either, some are set to be played right outside certain story checkpoints which are then played right after.Story pacing - game rockets to a 11 in terms of scale then just kinda... deflates. Tutorial starts with beating up mech suit wearing guys when you're at your weakest and you build up to fighting some guys in ski jackets who are way more threatening for some reason? Bad guys seem to be omnipotent and know stuff they shouldn't have had any access to or even makes sense - I DID EVERYTHING TO DRAW YOU HERE *main characters walk away* OH WELL!To be clear, I'm cool with anime ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - loved Code Vein and most of the other Tales games are all good enough, this one is just exceptionally poor in terms of writing.Also all the launch DLC is expensive and largely useless, feels bad to see banners ingame about it too.WITH ALL THAT SAID, THE GOOD IS PRETTY MUCH WHAT LITTLE IS LEFTCombat feels good, better than Berseria and pretty close to Vesperia levels. I prefer TP from older games but I guess the majority of people must prefer this if they stuck to it.Kinda funny how just running around grinding or killing stuff is fun and what keeps me playing while all the story and plot is half finished unplanned garbage and makes me want to drop the game, ah well.About 14h in and honestly can't see things changing much, unless I misunderstood and this is like FF13 where the first 40 hours being trash is ok because it's the "tutorial" - ahaha. Dunno about other people but 14h of bad writing is not ok, tutorial or not.I'll come back and update if it needs it

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is huge pro fo this game much of the in-game mechanic and character specific abilitie`s feel rewarding when used properly. Playing the game on hard, enemies up until first boss or so (until you unlock major mechanics of the game and abilities) are over-scaled and feels like grind to kill but afterwards difficulty setting is fit to description. Graphic looks beautiful can tell they really worked hard on this.Major con of the game comes from its pro mentioned, normal field battles and elite encounters (random/subquest) feel so much more rewarding and fun than the actual major boss fights. Boss fights are learning their pattern once and then grind to kill the huge health bar with no real constant engagement from booster mechanic (huge missed opportunity).Story seems to be another CON as they rush some plots and try to be unique when we all know its JRPG classic cliche (DLC that comes with deluxe package is also a huge spoiler to the story line), I would've much preferred a straight up cliche story plot with clear character build up from end to end. Attempt at trying to be unique needed to be put into better telling the story cause many of the major plot outside of first boss was completely un-relatable.Overall great JRPG worth the price tag for me it would been easily top of my list if mentioned CONs were better addressed. *Note that DLC weapon they give with deluxe package is OP it matches to the level of weapon that you get after 2nd boss.7/10
