_childDocuments_.review: I've never been into the Tales games much (although I have all the ones for Steam), I think the last and only one I played before this was Tales of Destiny, and I just kind of found it okay. This game, however, has put me back onto the Tales games in a big way. The story is so in-depth, and narrative drops you right in the thick of it.As of the time I write this review, I have not finished the game yet, so maybe it'll get worse and I'll hate it later, but I can't really see that happening. I am enthralled.Edit: So now that I have completed the game, I feel my recommendation to purchase this game goes a long way.I loved everything about this game. It felt modern, yet, nostalgic all at once. It had all the elements I loved from many of my favorite old school JRPGs, but with a modern feel. I enjoyed the animated cut scenes, voice acting was top notch (in both English and Japanese), (Edit: I played this in Japanese, after hearing more of the voice acting in English, I would say stick to Japanese) and the story elements were filled with all the creativity Japan has to offer (without any of it's overboard convoluted confusion they often do these days). When you play it in Enlgish, the voice track doesn't quite match the lip sync, but even that kind of reminded me of an old school RPG. It felt like I was playing Lunar 2, which for those of you that don't know, is a good thing. The only thing that stopped it from feeling like a full-on old school JRPG was the lack of a world map, which we rarely see these days anyway, so that's okay. I also love how certain armors will change your appearance, and how weapons change appearance as well. I've always been a sucker for that. The battle system is very fun, and I love how you gradually unlock skills and battle functions that make the system feel fresh well into the game. If I had to nitpick, I could say the only thing I found a bit overbearing were all the sub scenes the game gives you. So every few seconds, it seems, your party has something to say about an event, a place, or another character. Don't get me wrong, this feature is excellent. It's enjoyable in other games, like DQ11 and Star Ocean (if I remember correctly), but in this game there are so many scenes, I couldn't help but to feel inundated by them. Of course, they are completely optional and you can skip them, but I definitely wouldn't. Those scenes give the player lots of insights on the characters and the background of the world in general. A lot of them are genuinely humorous and heartfelt, and if I'm honest, they were fun. However, with the sheer number of scenes you're presented with, it feels like too much of a good thing--especially when you're in the middle of a dungeon trying to stop a baddie from doing something evil and have to stop 3 times in one room to hear it. Again though, these are completely optional, but if you're into JRPGs like I am, it's really not. Although I griped about these scenes a little, I love the animated manga style in which they're presented. I thought that was a nice touch.All in all, I can't recommend this game enough. I kind of wish this was how the last Star Ocean game felt, but sadly, I don't think that series will come back strong any time soon..Get this game. At full price. On sale. Whatever. Just do yourself a favor, and get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that this is a well-crafted and beautiful game. It has a strong (if standard) story and great character development that helps sell the idea of your party slowly getting to know each other better. The gameplay is smooth and the combat is a satisfying system, albeit one that is a bit more strangely paced than what I'm normally used to (I'm not particularly used to using the pause menu mid-fight in a game). However, as with any game, there are a few points which needed to be looked at, namely in enemy and dungeon design.Positives:+Graphics and art style. The "3D watercolor" style that they had going produces a beautiful world design and is a unique spin on Bandai Namco's standard 3D art style.+Combat system. I honestly wasn't too enthused about previous Tales games due to their combat systems feeling excessively clunky to me, so I was happy about Arise's combat flow being smoother and more streamlined. +Story and characters. The story is a bit generic JRPG, but the character interactions and development help a lot to carry the writing. Seeing each individual character develop over the course of the journey really helps you care about their motivations and goals.+The voice acting. I played in English, and I do very much applaud the English voice cast for bringing the life that they did to the characters and world. YMMVs:=Grindiness. I noticed that I had a 20% EXP booster running, and tended to utilize food which would increase EXP gains. Even then, you were going to always be a small step behind the enemy level curve in any given area if you do not opt to grind a little bit. I have concerns that without those benefits, the game may end up hitting a point where grinding becomes a bit mandatory if you don't want it to become excessively difficult due to stat deficits.Cons:-(Story) Endgame enemy design. The enemy designs found in the later half of the game felt like they relied too heavily either tossing reskinned bosses at you as normal mobs, with mobs unique to the later zones feeling more like gigantic stat bricks than anything interesting.-The final dungeon. Building into the previous endgame enemy design issues, the final dungeon is an excessively long slog through insane amounts of forced encounters with the stat brick enemies. The dungeon VERY quickly ceases being fun and becomes exhausting, making the final dungeon a very bitter experience to end the game on.Final Word:In spite of my complaints with the game's endgame, I found the game overall to be a very satisfying experience, and I would give it my recommendation to those looking for a nice JRPG with some fun action-oriented combat and likable characters.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of things about the game that are pretty good: Combat feels satisfying by extending long combos through boost attacks and mystic artes, the semi-open world maps look beautiful, and the two dual protagonists Alphen and Shionne have some romantic chemistry that adds an extra layer.For me, the highlight is truly the characters who you bond with throughout the game. Banter during battle from Law and Rinwell, or deep, personal stories by the campfire at night, the characters all grow from solid writing and character development. It does however, suffer from the typical JRPG storytelling we've seen in past games where it starts strong and drags out the further in you get. Despite that though I found the ending had paid off and that it was a complete, satisfying conclusion to a solid game. I'd give it a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A really really good addition to the Tales series. Cloth and hair physics I found especially appealing while running around as the main female.+ Combat is fun and feels fluid. Each party member has a unique playstyle and you can switch to them on the fly in combat, which is really nice for variety in battle.+ Characters and their voices are the best part of this game!! The party dynamic really works well between them and there's character growth for each one.+ Story is good. If you're a Tales fan, or know a lot of grand story anime tropes you may know what tone to expect as it goes on, but it's still a fun ride.~Cons~- Skit rewatch menu and bestiary organization is nonexistent. It's just one long list of all ze things and you have to scroll to find the one you want (with skits this gets loooooong).- Linear levels. This is the biggest con to the game in my opinion. Even the larger maps are still pretty painfully linear.- Story, while good, feels a bit rushed in places. Especially some early game areas. I'm also really not a fan of games taking party members away for any period of time and this happens once or twice during the game. _childDocuments_.review: I beat the game after 50 hours of playing. The story is mediocre. The beginning is quite interesting. Tales of Arise jumped out of the traditional Tales world where a Savior must fight Lord of Calamity. ToA's world background is completely new. You are on a planet invaded and enslaved by aggressors from its twin planet. However, the excitement quickly falls apart as your main character has no personality other than being politically correct. The protagonist is basically Jesus Christ. He loves everyone. He forgives everything. Even if you kill his parents or rape his girlfriend, he'll forgive you and give you a loving lecture about how important political correctness is. Even Jesus Christ has more humanity and personality than him. For a RPG game, having Jesus Christ as your main character is a death sentence. You simply don't feel excited about the plot any more. The battle is interesting at the beginning. However, it becomes a chore quickly after you repeat it hundreds of times. The enemies' HP are so huge that regular attacks and techniques basically don't do damage. Your job is to keep stacking higher combos so that you can execute. There are paid skill trees in the costume pack, which means without spending $30 more on 6 costume packs your characters will not have full skills. ————————————————————Additions on Sept. 17th 2021:The NG+ is ridiculous. It is identical to the first playthrough. There is no change in level, difficulty, etc. There is no change in anything. _childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise is definitely a game worth playing, and after completing the base game at 100% together with the DLC , I wanted to share some thoughts on this experience.Let's start with the aspect you'll be facing the most throughout the game. The battle system. It may feel unspectacularly shallow in some cases. As you progress through it, though, its depth begins to reveal itself. Ultimately, the fights come down to mapping the most powerfully complex attacks - "artes" - to various buttons to pull off satisfying combos. This makes combat a matter of exploiting enemy weak points and chaining together attacks of your party members. The main character, Alphen, has a blaze sword that enables him to carry out fire-based attacks at the expense of his health. How one controls this trade-off between damage output and survival becomes mastered, especially in the harder difficulties where over-reliance on the powerful moves will leave you open in longer battles. . New mechanics are being introduced throughout at a good, steady pace, enough to give players some time to master each part of the combat before layering on additional complexity.For the most part, the combat in Tales of Arise feels smooth, and generally speaking, there's not a lot of frustration comingfrom this particular aspect. The biggest issue, however, is party AI: your AI companions make some pretty "weird" decisions during the harder battles - particularly the boss fights - such as staying in dangerous areas or failing to dodge deadly attacks. It's not game-breaking, but at times, it makes the entire experience more annoying, as you're focusing on reviving/healing your party rather than killing the boss.One of the more welcoming aspects in Tales of Arise is for sure its approach to difficulty. Sure, battles on higher difficulty can still be challenging without becoming unfairly punishing. Unlike some other titles in the series, like Berseria, which made experience gain much lower upon raising the difficulty, you can revel in the intensity of the combat without superfluous grinding in Arise. Each party member offers up a different method of fighting, really, as you find yourself switching between characters with great regularity depending on the approach taken by the player. This all does keep the combat fresh throughout the whole playthrough, and a more challenging "Chaos" difficulty unlocks toward the end for those that want a real challenge.Speaking of rewarding things, I must mention the exploration as a whole. There are various treasures, upgrades, and crafting materials waiting to be discovered around the world. The game does a really good job at encouraging players to explore every possible corner . The cooking and fishing systems add a nice layer of depth to exploration, together with buffs and bonuses that make striking off the beaten path worth it. Side quests are largely entertaining, though they do share one major misstep: there’s no indication of recommended levels. You’ll more than occasionally accept a quest only to find the enemies far more powerful than your current party.Tales of Arise’s plot is one of an underdog story whereby the oppressed citizens of Dahna rise against the ruling class from Rena. At the front of this charge is Alphen himself, a former slave now broken free, and Shionne from Rena, who has her own reasons for wanting to take down the oppressive regime. The story then unfolds into a grand conflict with deeper mysteries upon both worlds as the group travels across different regions to defeat the ruling lords. It’s a fun story at first, but some of those bigger narrative moments in an epic feel underbaked by the time you finish. That said, the journey itself stays quite pleasant thanks to shifting character dynamics and a few plot reveals here and there.Characters are sure energetic, although it does tend to lean heavily into some familiar anime archetypes. Alphen’s of the "clueless hero" archetype, while his companion and love interest Shionne is an easy fit for the "tsundere," quick to mask her feelings behind a veil of sarcasm and mock anger. The rest of the party members all fit into similarly recognizable roles, yet manage to stay interesting through unique interactions and personal growth. The real charm is found in frequent skits and side scenes the game provides for each character; they truly provide some great humor. It does not bear on the core story but does add a little more to understand the personality and dynamics of the characters. Where Tales of Arise truly comes into its own, though, is in the presentation. It feels more like the environments were handcrafted with beautiful backgrounds, adding significantly to immersion. For the most part, each area feels different. Compared to other recent games in the series, like Zestiria and even Berseria—both of which bear large marks of reused assets - Tales of Arise feels like a quite significant leap forward in terms of visual design.Overall, Tales of Arise is a nice introduction to the series: well-rounded, with an experience that mingles satisfying combat and impressive visuals with a decent story. There are certainly several flaws, AI control and the absence of co-op chief among them, but all in all, they can't detract enough from this game’s many virtues. The game will have a lot to offer either to a complete newbie or a veteran. Tales of Arise is a satisfying RPG that’s at the very least worth spending time with.Regarding Beyond the Dawn DLC - It adds another 20 hours of content, continuing the story a year after the events of the main story. It gives players an opportunity to see what happened after the conclusion of Tales of Arise, reuniting you with the familiar cast while providing a couple of new challenges for good measure. This feels more like a natural continuation of the game if you enjoyed the combat and story in general. While the DLC does manage mostly to recycle the maps from the base, it does inject some freshness into these by introducing new dungeons to blast through. It doesn’t introduce any kind of plot twists, earth-shattering or otherwise, but it does serve up meaningful character development for Alphen and his crew. Only worth buying if you enjoyed the game or on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit of history. Tales of Symphonia for the Gamecube was my first "Tales of" game. I had purchased it due to the lack of games for the Gamecube. Back then, I was not really into playing JRPG games, but playing Tales of Symphonia was still fun -- even though I was playing it more like a hack and slash game (ie. button mashing) -- and just giving Raine and her brother all the related weapons/skills that I found (with little optimization). My thinking was, enhancing the "healer" and the long distance magic user, should help out the team, and hence, help during battles. Tales of Berseria was my second "Tales of" game. It was definitely an impulse purchase, fueled with a bit of nostalgia from owning/playing Tales of Symphonia -- and with it, I decided to learn/use as many of the JRPG feature elements as possible. This was partially a success, as many times, I just loved to resort to the hack and slash elements of the game. When I saw this game (Tales of Arise) during the 2024 Fanatical Summer sale, I felt it was an easy purchase -- both to get more into the JRPG elements of the series and to enjoy the "hack and slash" playstyle too. So, with this game, how did I do? And how does it compare to Tales of Symphonia/Berseria?The story (and character development) is similar to the previous "Tales of" games. It is a very slow burn (in the beginning), and the characters do take time to become likeable. Overall, while great, these are definitely not my most favorite characters. The Tales of Berseria characters are still my favorite -- which is impressive, because they were all anti-heroes, with one being intentionally annoying. Regardless, the Tales of Arise characters do eventually become likeable -- it is just that they are less likeable (than Berseria) and takes more time to get there. Unfortunately, some of the skits (trademark of the "Tales of" series) were somewhat annoying, preachy, and felt like beating a dead horse (especially later in the game). There are a lot more of them (or certainly felt that way), and they were delivered in a slow fashion (the dialog were slower, and there were annoying pauses between the frames). At times, it felt more like I was reading an interactive novel, instead of playing a game. Also, the later stages of the story does take a few twists -- and in my opinion, it went in a weird direction. The Tales of Arise combat system is a bit similar, and yet, very different from Symphonia/Berseria. You can also get/craft new weapons, upgrade accessories, gather/cook, gather titles, etc., however, these are also different. It is probably best to simply unlearn from playing the previous "tales of" games, and learn this game from scratch. The button assignments/purpose, combo system, and even how the more powerful artes are activated are different. I don't know if comparing the combat system is fair due to the differences, however, overall, for me, I felt that (initially) Tales of Berseria had a more satisfying combat system. The Tales of Arise combat system does eventually feel more satisfying (especially once you get used to the many options) -- and there is little wrong with it. It just feels different, and a bit less intuitive, when compared to Berseria. Having said that, it is much easier to activate the team artes, and hence, the battles look much cooler (and becomes more satisfying).The graphics are definitely much better than previous games -- as this game is using the UNREAL engine. So, if you appreciate graphics, you will like this game over previous games. On the other hand, if you have grown to love the graphics of previous "Tales of" games, you will notice that it is different. Arguably, it may take some time to get use to. For me, it took a few hours to get comfortable. I don't place a high regard on graphics, so, I just consider it as a good improvement.One interesting feature that I really liked about this game was the fast travel system. Basically, once you reach an area, you can return to it via fast travel. Additionally, you can travel at anytime, and from anywhere (just choose it from the map). There were a few cases where areas were disabled due to story, but other than that, it was available as soon as you reached the location. Previous games had fast travel systems, but they were limited, and they weren't completely available until near the end of the game. In terms of annoyances, I felt that the side missions were not personal enough. With previous games, the side missions tend to focus on the characters, with each mission adding to their specific side stories. This game seems to have more side missions, but they seem to be of the "kill certain zeugles", "gather items for recipes", or "check out this thing" variety. Second, another annoyance may be the layout of the map. They seem to have sections in very tight quarters (ie. hallways). This makes it very difficult to avoid battles -- meaning you have to battle the Zeugles throughout the map (instead of running around choosing to battle or not). Third, I felt that some of the boss fights were ridiculously tedious. I understand that this can happen, if/when you are not high level enough -- but sheesh, there was one fight, where I was around the same level as the boss, and the fight just kept on going and going. Giving the area end boss a ridiculous amount of health, multiple sub-bosses, multiple forms, etc., may make the battle more exciting, or it may make the battle long and tedious. I felt that the game didn't achieve the excitement (leaning on tedious) with some of the battles. And lastly ...Regarding the annoyance with the "second half" of the game -- this is quoted, as it seems to be the main complaint (from other reviewers) regarding this game. Without giving away any spoilers, I will just say that it is easily noticed, as the title opening (animation and music) will change when you enter the "second half" of the game. Basically, I think that the issue is that it is really only the last quarter, or last third, of the game. The "second half" is really only considered a "half", because it has been heavily padded with lots of skits and a steeper level of enemy encounters (forcing you to do side quests, and grinding, to level up). In terms of relevant story, there wasn't really much left. Basically, you are simply chasing a MacGuffin. This is generally not a problem for most games, but the "Tales of" series of games are JRPG games, and with a great reputation to uphold. It really felt out of place, was unexpected, and was somewhat disappointing.Unfortunately, I also encountered a few technical issues too (right away), that needed to be resolved. First, there seems to be an issue with the audio (with the cutscenes) as it seems to stutter on low end computers, especially if it uses a low end graphics card.  To resolve, I recommend lowering (or disabling) many of the GPU related features. It does make the game look worse, but having working cutscenes is better (in my opinion). Second, there seems to be an issue with using the gamepad/controller. If you use the gamepad, along with sometimes using the keyboard or mouse, the icons (for the gamepad) will sometimes disappear. In other words, it will be difficult to determine what buttons to press, as it won't show up on any of the menus (or action icons). If you are a gamepad user, I recommend not touching the keyboard or mouse, until later in the game (when you already know what buttons does what). Overall, I liked this game. It was arguably a bit better than Tales of Symphonia, but, not as deep, complex, or as good as Tales of Berseria. Admittedly, the story and character development was slower than what I would have liked, the skits felt a bit overwhelming at times, and many parts of the game were somewhat tedious (and even annoying). Regardless, I enjoyed and do recommend this game (with all the caveats already mentioned). For me, it was worth it, especially since I had purchased this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls in Tales of Arise are very user-friendly, allowing players to jump straight into the action without a steep learning curve. The game strikes a good balance between challenge and fairness, making each encounter engaging without being overly punishing. The storyline and character interactions keep the player involved and interested throughout the adventure. While the main story is compelling, the choices made by the player do not significantly alter the course of events. Leveling up and acquiring new skills provide a satisfying sense of growth and progression.The narrative is well-crafted and keeps the player invested in the journey of the protagonists. The world of Tales of Arise is beautifully designed, drawing players into its rich environments and cultures. The game boasts impressive visuals, with detailed character models and breathtaking landscapes. The soundtrack and voice acting enhance the overall experience, adding depth to the game's atmosphere. The interface is intuitive and doesn't clutter the screen, allowing for smooth navigation and gameplay.The game's mechanics are solid, providing a good mix of strategy and action in combat. While the main story and side quests are engaging, there is a moderate amount of content that could be expanded further. The AI performs adequately, though it can sometimes feel predictable and lacking in complexity. The game offers a good range of settings to customize the experience to your liking. The game runs smoothly with no significant technical issues or bugs affecting gameplay.Overall, Tales of Arise is a satisfying game that delivers a solid RPG experience. The game does not rely on microtransactions, allowing players to enjoy the full experience without additional costs. While the game is enjoyable, its replay value is relatively low due to the linearity of the story. The game offers a good amount of content and quality for its price, making it a worthwhile purchase. Despite some areas that could use improvement, Tales of Arise is a solid RPG that fans of the genre will enjoy.Performance or gameplay meets the passing mark but remains average.There are areas that could be improved to enhance the gaming experience.Cautiously Recommended - ✔

_childDocuments_.review: It's half decent but nothing exceptional. Story is cliche, and it gets very predictable very fast, it's like a generic shounen adventure. Character development feels forced at times, although the interactions between characters are pretty cute.Progression is again very repetitive, pass through field area, kill monsters, visit town, do side quests, do the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tower dungeon  all over, kill boss, rinse and repeat.Gameplay doesn't really feel all that rewarding, it's very mechanical, spam the same beginner artes, do the character specials to negate each type of enemy attack (spells, charges etc), heal with shion and that's it. There is not much reason to learn things like combos or other more complex mechanics.Same goes for the side stuff like fish and farming, they're far from essential, maybe if the game enticed you to spend more time in open world instead of story (eg how Ys IX made you do side quests to collect enough points to progress the story) you would feel inclined to explore those mechanics more. I give it a "Recommended" rating because it doesn't do anything offensive enough to not recommend but on the other hand it doesn't bring anything new to the table either. Good time waster, it's not that long anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game. Does it have some issues? Yes, definitely. Are some of them issues that have been persistent across Tales games for a while that have yet to be fixed or worked on? Yes. But that didn't stop this from being the game I've been most invested in in a long while. TL;DR: 9/10, Great characters that make the story more than the story, good story, amazing graphics, great characters, decent soundtrack, great gameplay, great characters, bland and boring dungeons but fun levels, and most importantly... great characters.I really enjoyed the story, although it did have it's shortcomings towards the end of the game (there was a section of the game near the end where it felt like over an hour of non-stop cutscenes and skits), but overall the main story was solid and quite enjoyable. But it wasn't the main story that I was most invested in. It was the characters story arcs and how they all tied in to the main story. All of their interactions, and the characters themselves are what got me so into Tales of Arise. They took a little bit to get there, but once they did, they carried this game for me.The gameplay was easily the best it's ever been in Tales (in my opinion), with the combat being much more fluid than past titles, and the new artes being quite fun and enjoyable to use. Each character has a distinct playstyle, giving quite a bit of variety to how the game is played. The dungeons are where the game really falls flat though. I'm not a veteran to the Tales franchise, so I'm not sure if any of the past games before Vesperia had good dungeons, but none of the ones I've played were much more than increasingly long dungeons full of linear pathways and basic exploration (i.e. Side rooms and passageways) that had a few monsters spread throughout. Tales of Arise, unfortunately, was no different. By the time the last dungeon rolled around, I was done. I fought a few times here and there, but most every time I got into combat I started fleeing just so I could get through yet another of the same, bland dungeons. A that point in the game, I was a high enough level to beat the game anyways, so fleeing to get to the end didn't matter. Having said all of that, the main areas that aren't dungeons are more enjoyable to explore, and help to make up for the game's shortcomings.  Soundtrack was pretty good, though I can't say it was anything to write home about. Graphics, on the other hand, were exceptional for a JRPG. They looked stunning, and it was just so enjoyable to just to go around looking at the scenery and exploring some of the more open areas, because it looked so good.Ultimately, I'd give Tales of Arise a 9/10. Easily my favourite game of the year so far, because the characters make the story, and the story itself is quite good.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: Played this 80+ hours and by the end of the game it felt like the whole playthrough passed like a flash, the sign of a great game.Although some things in Tales of Arise felt a bit cliché, mainly some characters (the main protagonist felt a bit too "virtuous" to my taste, lacking personality or flaws), or the story, which I liked but didn't feel as much emotionally taking / heartbreaking as Tales of Berseria for instance, these little flaws didn't weigh much in regard to the rich and beautiful universe this game had to offer - many different locations, a profusion of powers to learn, a very dynamic and fun combat system, and some challenge at times, concerning some subquests - some being a bit of a pain, most being fun and rewarding, mostly necessary to gain some xp - but the whole synergy of the game, based on an evolutive friendship story, as well as the many features the game offers, make it a must-buy for any jrpg fan.One thing bothered me a bit though, concerning the difficulty gap between the main story bosses and subquest ones: I felt that there was a slight lack of balance between them, making necessary to go on playing after the first playthrough in order to fully complete the game - I would have largely preferred everything being compacted in a single playthrough, every quest and achievement being doable without having to go on after the end of the game.  As an example of this lack of balance, I lost some subquest boss fights and had to repack on items or grind a bit in order to beat them, when beating the final boss felt like a cakewalk, which felt a bit weird.But in spite of this point, it was a great experience to me, the whole game took me in and I couldn't stop playing this until reaching the end. Feeling now very impatient to discover the next Tales of, as well as any great future jrpg Bandai Namco will be preparing us.

_childDocuments_.review: (I played this game for longer than Steam is saying I did. Not sure why it's showing the wrong time, but I did actually play for hours before reviewing it.)I really wanted to like this game. The same developer made my favorite game of all time. However, this particular game is kind of a mess. I think it tried to copy elements of other popular games, and as a result it lost any of its own heart.Mechanically, it's missing a lot of basic features like a quicksave hotkey and even a menu to let me exit the game. (I'm sure there's an exit button somewhere, but it's not coming up in the normal places where I'd look for it. I have to tab out and then close the game window, and then manually shut down the game on Steam because it's actually still running in the background.) The real-time combat is also VERY poorly designed. I'm sure I could master it with time, but it is not fun or interesting enough to motivate me to grapple with such a complicated system. (This developer has often used turn-based combat in the past, and probably didn't have enough experience designing real-time.) I think they only added real-time combat in order to mimic other popular games. Similarly, the game includes a lot of bland mini-games/optional crafting features like fishing and cooking, but in a way that again feels like the developers said, "Other popular games have these features, so we should add those too." Nothing about these features improves the gameplay experience in any way.Lastly, the narrative is very generic and uninspired.

_childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise is a lot of fun, a full-blown action RPG with combo and special skill based combat with light crafting and side mission components.It's a beautiful game with impressive effects, I definitely rate it very highly but it's not without its missteps.PROS: ToA has gorgeous graphics, great sounds, interesting level and character design, fast-paced combat, and an interesting storyline about a subjugated people and their overseers that gets more complicated in its intrigue as you progress. Areas are fairly large but quick to traverse, and multiple systems, both in and out of combat, are introduced over time. AI party members are fairly competent, and you can toggle abilities on and off to suit your play style or specific encounters. Cooking buffs can affect a wide range of things, from stats to recovery to loot collection, and the game is generous towards what it DOESN'T count as time elapsed until the effects wear off. Accessory augmenting allows for min/maxing. Party members pair up in interesting ways in regards to motives and story. Skill usage is capped by recovery time, rather than an ability pool, except for healing, which I enjoy because it forces you to make tough decisions on resource usage. AI settings are a bit lacking, but sufficient (think of it like a lite version of FFXII's gambit system.) Combat is fast-paced and rewards clever skill choice for combo strings. No missables! And New Game+!CONS: Limited enemy types makes combat feel a bit repetitive and samey, and your party member's boost abilities can only target the enemy you have locked on, which can make it difficult to quickly use ones on the right enemy that have a time window in which they are useful. Fairly tight camera in combat means it's easy to get hit by off-screen attacks you might otherwise have been able to dodge, and enemies hit hard. Weapons and armor are uninspired and little more than stat sticks. The game doesn't quite shove DLC down your throat, but it's there every time you camp. Some [non-essential] skills are locked behind costume DLC. Anime and JRPG  tropes get annoying from time to time. Number of skills ("artes") is really more than necessary, and no solid feedback is given regarding their relative numeric strengths or effects of leveling them up. Regardless of input settings, accidentally using the same arte multiple times in a row is very easy. Control configuration is not intuitive, and (at least using an XBOX ONE controller) the game will only display keyboard prompts unless you plug the controller in after starting the game. Randomness in accessory crafting based on ore attributes is not really a problem, but you might need to do a lot of farming if you really do want to min/max. Difficult combat scenarios can dissolve into chaos very quickly.In short, while it may seem like I have a laundry list of complaints, they don't detract significantly from this being a solid, very fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Tales fan for 20 years, spending over 1000 accumulated hours over all the Tales games I've played thus far. The series has had its highs and its had its lows, but after the awful mess that was Zestiria, the previous main producer of the games, Hideo Baba, resigned and we were all wondering if the series was going to die in an abandoned ditch. Berseria came back with a strong success, but things were still up in the air for the future of Tales. Then, the team behind God Eater picked up the franchise and here we are with Tales of Arise.Arise has evoked a passion for Tales that I haven't felt in years, reminding me why I fell in love with the Tales series in the first place.The production value in this game is phenomenal, featuring crisp, clean graphics, incredibly optimized gameplay that I can run at 130+ FPS and top notch voice acting, music, and sound design.While I wish the story was a little deeper at times, the main cast is excellent. There is so much dialogue dedicated to the party's interactions, struggles, and even romance. The script is definitely tailored more for adults than it is for teenagers which is a nice change of pace from prior games which were aimed at a younger audience.I've heard criticisms that the final act of the game isn't strong. I've heard people complain that enemies have too much HP. I've heard voices speak about how the main cast isn't interesting.The combat is FANTASTIC. With confidence I can say that it is the best action-JRPG system I have ever played in my entire life. It's addictive, chaotic, explosive, and actively rewards the player for their skill.This game goes on sale a lot, so you can wait until its cheap (as I write this review it's only $27 CAD), but even at this moment I'm willing to preach that it's worth full price.It's so damn good to be a Tales fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish Steam had more options for reviews than just "yes" or "no". At a very minimum a third option: A "meh". Because that pretty much encompasses my feelings towards this game.There has been for long a rather cynical joke about modern video games being one long cutscene which is occasionally interrupted by short segments of gameplay. For some JRPGs this is actually quite literally true. While Tales of Arise might not be the worst example of this, it's still pretty up there. It's difficult to play the game for even five minutes without the gameplay being interrupted with yet another cutscene (unless you are eg. just engaging in repetitive level-grinding that doesn't advance towards the next goal). If I estimate there's about a thousand gameplay-interrupting cutscenes in the main quest alone I don't think I would even be exaggerating. And that's just the mandatory cutscenes. In addition there are some hundreds of optional cutscenes (triggered by a button at certain points in the story).A story-heavy game does not need this many cutscenes, especially not ones that interrupt the gameplay, the flow of the game. It might just be a personal pet peeve of mine, but it becomes quite irritating when for the hundredth time I cannot run towards the next goal for even a minute before yet another cutscene interrupts it.It would be slightly less annoying if the story was interesting. Which brings me to the next point: The story is very "meh". It's average, run-of-the-mill paint-by-the-numbers, with nothing extraordinarily unusual, interesting or engaging about it (although, to be honest, at the point of writing this review I have still not played the game through. It's possible the story will become more interesting later. However, in my experience if the story isn't interesting in the first half-hour to one hour of gameplay, it won't become interesting later. Exceptions to this are exceedingly rare.)The graphics are quite ok for the style (ie. cell-shaded more-on-the-cartoony-side), even above average compared to other games using the same graphical style.The combat mechanics are ok, I suppose (and quite varied). I personally prefer turn-based combat in JRPGs (the more classical, the better), but that's just a personal preference and I understand not all players prefer them.But now, given the binary choice of "yes" and "no", with no "meh" option, what should I vote? While I'm far from enthusiastic about the game, I don't want to be unfair. If I compare it to *all* JRPGs that exist out there (or even just on Steam) I would say this is above average, so I suppose it has to be a "yes" then. I have played much, *much* worse JRPGs than this. This is not bad by any stretch. It's just not extraordinarily good either (at least in my personal opinion; your own experience may be vastly different).

_childDocuments_.review: Tales of Arise was my first game from the "Tales of..." series so I walked in playing this game without any prior knowledge or any expectations on what a "Tales of..." game should entail. So this is purely from a newbie perspective of the game and how it was for me.Tales of Arise is one of the most colorful and beautifully crafted worlds i've ever had the pleasure of experiencing! Each region you end up visiting during your adventures are really great to look at and explore!Although, the experience does get slightly hampered due to the fact that each region is separated as a sandbox and although you technically can walk through exploring region to region you dont "organically" walk into the different regions like you would an open world game, you go through a load screen and voila you're there! The wonder and amazement of the environments around you slowly evolve from desert to forest or icy plains as you travel from region to region is not present here which does slightly affect the experience adversely.The story is pretty straightforward and quite predictable, which does not necessarily mean a bad thing as the characters and writing hold it up quite well! Some of the other themes and issues that the game tackles such as prejudice and racism are all done very well in this game!The voice acting is really good! It gave so much dimensions to the characters and the extra development you get for the characters through the skits are an absolute delight to watch! some are admittedly pretty meh, but most are very interesting and help flesh out the characters and their relationships with each other very well.The gameplay is super fun, and you can rotate between who you want to play as during fights! Each character has a TON of skills to play around with, and certain characters have their individual mechanics. There is a ton of stuff to master in this game! However i did just stuck with the few that really felt like great combos so I never explored much beyond trying to rank up each move which may unlock a new move through that as well! There are so many QoL features in this game and it really shows that the devs just want you to have fun with the game. Quick travel points are a plenty and most of them are near quest givers or quest areas so you rarely spend too much time looking for objective areas and monsters as well as completing them. Not only that, the map is also easy to navigate and an objective marker is shown as a big ass star in green on the map so you really cant miss it! Overall I enjoyed the experience and I am definitely going in once more for NG+ its an easy recommend for me for fans who enjoy JRPGs and are looking for a game to have fun with! The best time to get it for me would be if its on sale at 50%! an easy 8/10 for me!

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game. I obviously haven't finished it but I've seen enough so let's get this over with.- The good : Beautiful visuals, that cel shading is chef's kiss. So far the interactions betweens the characters is good. And thank god for that because that's kind of the stapple of the Tales Of series. - Neutral : The story is classic. There are bad guys, we are the good guys, we beat the bad guys and I guess there will be some plot twist along the way regarding events that happened 12 000 years ago. Nothing groundbreaking but it's serviceable. The sound design is okay too, a little bit too much of choir singing. - The bad : The story. Yeah no, here I mean how the story is handled rather than waht the story is. To put it simply it feels like the writers had a list of cool ideas but they did nothing to string them together so you go from one cool/emotionnal scene to another and it just doesn't feel right. A distinct lack of Show don't tell is also weighting on that crippling feeling. The gameplay : Boy oh boy now we're entering what really hurts with this game. In short it sucks, it's bad. First and foremost, and that is my conspiracy theory, this game feels balanced around that stupid boatload of DLCs. I've been playing JRPG for close to 30 years and if there's one thing that is common to every single JRPG is that the player is NEVER lacking resources. Now I know, The Tales Of series always had a 15 size limit for how many type of item you can carry but that is not the probleme here. The issue is that you are a god forsaken hobo that cannot afford a single orange gel to save your life without grinding a whole afternoon. Here I am playing like I'm in a survival horror constantly being out of items and gald. And what is not helping that situation is how awful the combat is. I'm am not good enough with words to explain correctly what is happening so I'm just going to list stuff :- You can't stagger bosses, they will tell you how you play the game and you will shut up and agree with them- Companion AI is doing its best to drain you of healing item and mana - I know, I should adjust strategies, but I don't wanna have to pause the fight every 5 second to adjust said strats. It DOES work I agree but it's absolutely awful for the flow of the game. - Same deal with switching character I'm sure they want you to switch between characters in order to string combos, to avoid attacks and whatnot, but it's the same you have to press L1, which freezes the fight, in order to do so. - 3 arte slots, in a Tales game. ♥♥♥♥ off. - A healing point before bosses... that is one-time use. So you have to save "before" using it. It is needlessly stupid, do you hate your players that much?That's just what came up on top of my head writing this. I'm sure there's more. It's really an excruciating experience. Tales of has always been a jrpg series where the player gets to pop off and have fun, and here I am having to slog through increasingly bigger hp sponges while never getting that crucial feeling of becoming stronger. I am so sorry for the people that discovered the Tales of Series through this episode.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up playing the OLDER tales games and has played every game in the series i gotta say Tales of Arise has to be one of the WORST tales games ive ever played. Story: The games story starts out solid and interesting but the further you go the worse it gets. Each zones lords has barely any story to them, the story contradicts itself in many spots, you'll have multiple skits about a topic your party just talked about and answered right after viewing a scene, and many mindnumbing party interactions.Gameplay:Battle system is so terribly boring and stripped down i eventually set the AI to just fight for me. you mash your attack button, and then press a button to do the assigned art. sounds like previous tales games right? but no.. other tales games for example you can hold up + attack to hit aerial enemies but you cant do that in this game. boost attacks are lame attacks that have special properties tied to each character and you will find yourself just spamming them over and over even if you arent using the special property. Aside from the graphics being very beautiful, the gameworld is very boring and poorly designed. Each zone has short linear pathing through each map that you just zoom through. it is a very serious downgrade from Tales of Berseria where the world actually still felt good. Quests in this game aren't very interesting either, its usually always either a gathering quest that you instant turn in, or a hunt 3 of these mobs on the screen before the town quest. The characters.... oh god... none of your party members are well written or interesting. Rinwell might be the most well done, but even she is fairly cringe at times. For me this is the first tales game where i couldn't care any less about the entire cast. Weapons are mostly reskins of the same 4 weapons over and over again. Very very lazy. Also most of these weapons look TERRIBLE themselves. You will most likely be using the weapon transmog to the 1 weapon you do like.Seriously i have no idea how this game is very positive reviews. Its VERY poorly made. Do yourself a favor and skip this one or buy it on a 80% off sale or something if you feel the need to absolutely try it. You will be full of regret if you buy it at full price or even just buying any of the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: An early take on it (6 hours played), but so far I've enjoyed the tale told and I like the two characters that make-up my party.  I've not heard of the Tales series before this game and I am not much of an anime fan (neutral, I guess) - so the game is standing on it's own merits.The combat is kinda grindy in the sense that the respawn rate is high.  Exploring places might mean that you fight the same group 2 or 3 times.  The game does have a fast travel system, but you probably should avoid it until you have any given map fully explored.  I haven't minded the grind too much - fighting the same enemies does make it a bit easier to improve your tactics and clean-up the button mashing into working towards the desired combo.I like the art style - it has a refined sort of grit that I appreciate.  The combat system involves a good amount of movement and jumping.  There is a real need to get airborne in order to avoid being struck and timing the more acrobatic moments correctly can be rewarding.  The system is forgiving enough to tolerate quite a bit of button mashing, but it does rapidly reward a more skillful approach.It's an 8 on a 10 scale from me and it will probably improve as the world expands.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: Most JRPGs rely on it as a fallback in case the gameplay or visuals fail somehow.Like Symphonia, parts of Phantasia, and Rebirth before it, Arise also follows with "racism bad" as a starter for Alphen and Shionne's quest to beat up the  five elemental based Renan Lords to free the planet of Dahna of three centuries' worth of slavery. Bonus, you also get some romance in there for extra motivational measure because it's so damn adorable to watch develop and unfold (it's well earned). Mind you, said average story does falter a bit in the second half of the game (it almost gave me Xenogears flashbacks) with quite a bit of exposition dumps as well as being slightly rushed in getting you to the final area of the game without tying up some of its loose ends. However, if you're invested enough in the characters to see how the cast fares in the end, it's worth it. Even if you do pick up on knowing where the story beats will go eventually, it shouldn't mar your experience. Side note: YMMV with the final boss, I personally didn't like how it was done, but the result was satisfactory in the end I suppose.Ngl, I was initially baffled I had a dedicated jump button or even an "evasion" button at all in a Tales game. Enemies appear on the map and in front of you (no random fights), combat is very anime flashy and bright, very fast paced with the stressed mechanics of dodging/counterattacking or "Counter Edge", even being outright required in some important battles. Beware, this has much tankier enemies than previous Tales games, especially the bosses whom you cannot stagger and later in the final area. CP or "Cure Points" acts as your healing pool and casted buffs such as Lionheart, Guardian Field, Steel, and Concentrate, so you can't attrition the enemy to death. Arise expects you to play well and do your best in evading incoming damage.As it is in Tales tradition, there's party skits, cooking, in Arise' case the obligatory hot springs cutscene, post-game EX dungeon for higher level grinding, and cameo fights from other Tales characters. Like modern Tales games such as Vesperia (fusion of old and new), Zestiria and Berseria, you can craft new weapons with enemy loot drops. Once you've acquired a new weapon, you can use that appearance as a weapon skin if you  choose too without having to change out your current one (this is new).Learning new skills/artes is either tied to completing subquests, overall artes proficiency categories (no longer tied to individual usage anymore), and character titles. Earning money is done through selling dropped enemy loot, completing subquests, or finding it in treasure bags/chests, not through simply harassing the local wildlife in battle. Items are expensive, especially for CP restorative items. Orange Gels don't normally sell for 3000 some Gald in previous games. EDIT: I forgot to mention that unlike previous Tales games, there is no internal way to play co-op with others unless it's through modding.EDIT2: in some previous Tales games, there used to be a "Grade shop" you could spend your accumulated Grade from fights or minigames into NG+ activators for the next playthrough. This one instead has collectible artifacts related to other Bandai Namco games that stand in for those carryovers, such as items, weapons/armor/accessories, titles, etc. Some of them can be toggled, such as doing 1 damage to enemies for arte exhibition purposes.Music's a bop, although I think there's some audio imbalance during cutscenes as sometimes it swells up too loud (I did this on 30/100 BGM volume and it was still loud). Could be me, could be the internal levels somehow, I'm not sure. Enjoy some Flame of Hope at least.Even on a sale, they're priced a bit high,  (which should've been unlockable somehow on your own). What's sadder is how the costume packs come with extra skills linked to titles you cannot earn on your own in the base game. There's also P2W ones that jumpstart your early beginnings in the game that make you pretty OP initially, but peter out quickly. Only get them .Yes, this game is geared towards newcomers to the series. Go play this on a discounted price, you'll like it. Personally I couldn't stop seeing Final Fantasy 4 parallels, but I'm weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game for the first 70%. Fully deserving of a 9/10.Superb story, great characterization and some of the best combat the series has to offer.Unfortunately, the last 30% is extremely rushed and some of the worst pacing i've ever seen. The final boss is also overwhelmingly boring, especially when compared to previous final bosses in the series. Post-game content is also very lackluster. Also has the worst idea when it comes to mystic artes (ultimate skills) as bosses mystic artes (except one) are not cut-scenes but in game mechanics, vastly reducing their wow factor. I was surprised there were only two mystic artes per character and even more so that they're locked behind max affinity - though I suppose boost artes make up for that.I cannot in good faith recommend this game after the dreadful final 15 hours that ruin the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: im new to the tales series so my problems with this game mostly come from not really knowing what I was getting into when I bought this. First the good. Game looks beautiful, it runs great (at least on my machine). the combat is fun for the most part, more on that later. And has some decent end game content. now the bad, or at least not so good. the story sets you down a very linear path. most of the game is very linear. the story itself was interesting at first but really drags at the mid to late game. there are soo many cuts scenes crammed together for soo much exposition it got to the point  I stopped caring and just skipped them. now the combat. as i said... it is fun and harder difficulties give you a reason to fine tune your party and give you a reason to "get gud" but later on when everyone has all these crazy moves and spells to cast it becomes a giant mess on screen. last issue. reskins! granted this is a problem most jrpgs suffer from but for 80 bucks canadian I was hoping for a little more enemies variety. hate going from zone to zone only to find a bunch of reskined enemies to fight. even though I am recommending this game I recommend you buy it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: A good game, the storyline had me curious to find out more from the get go and the gameplay  is pretty standard modern JRPG.I liked the game and would recommend it with other, HOWEVER...A big let down for me is the game's monetary system.It isn't pay to win but, about midway through the game money to buy items becomes important enough that you quickly realise you have two options, buy in-game money with real money or grind excessively. This is especially annoying if you are trying to do the sub-quests involving more difficult enemies, of course you could push on with the main game and reach the point at which money is easy to come by, but by that time you will have levelled up enough to essentially invalidate the sub-quests and their rewards that you needed the items for in the first place.As an example 1xOrange Gel, an item that is especially useful, costs 3000Gald, most items you can sell mid game aren't worth more than 200Gald. So you will need to go through around 5 or 6 battles to afford 1xOrange Gel, and it is probably better to have more than one, plus some other items, meaning you could easily grind 50 or 60 battles to get a good stock of items.Don't get me wrong, I like item scarcity as a way to increase difficulty, however the way this works makes the mid-game irritating and potentially grindy, in a way that screams "buy some Gald and enjoy the game or learn to dislike the game by grinding". This is made very clear by the 100,000Gald pack you can buy which in grinding terms would be around 120+ battles, by which time you will likely have grown bored of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: this was the first of the tales series i have played, it  was truly an amazing experience probably one of the best games in recent history. im normally a fan of final fantasy and games similar to it but this was a good experience it can take some time but i thoroughly enjoyed it. not grindy at all and the story progression is really on point.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: I greatly enjoyed Tales of Arise.In this time of game studios making women ugly and look like men, it was great to see strong female characters who acted feminine and looked amazing.The story was pretty decent, it def gets worse in the second half, mostly due to very bad pacing, but this did not dampen my enjoyment too much.The combat was really good, and I recommend 'Moderate' setting for those looking for a fun, challenging and not too grindy setting. I ended up 100%ing the game (76 hours), and enjoyed my time with it.Overall I give Tales of Arise 8.5/10 and I am looking forward to the next game in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: So this'll be my first game from the Tales series and I only played up to the second boss. After looking through some playthroughs of past Tales games, I think it's safe to say that TOA is comparable to the likes of what Persona 5 did for the Persona series. A huge QoL updates, enhanced graphics and the like. I definitely like the pacing they achieved with random encounters as you don't go into a victory screen or anything but still hear the banter between your comrades as you continue on in the field. A bit button mashing I'll admit but by getting more advance AGs, I feel like I can customize and make my own neat combo. The downside (and this is only comparing to the first vs second boss) is the difficulty spike. I remember doing fairly well vs the first boss but the second boss made me burn a lot of healing. I know my understanding of the combat system is still shallow, but the boss hits hard and doesn't stagger so I need to play safe rather than going all willy nilly like I do vs random encounters. Another downside, which is very minute, is the DLC popping up in the camp. Again, minor but really wish they didn't advertise it in-game. Definitely will recommend anyone who's new to the Tales series to give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first JRPG game I enjoy playing quite a bit in many years, last JRPG title I really enjoyed is good old FF series. Combat mechanic is interesting and engaging - I believe it will take hours and hours to test and master all skills which is good for hardcore players. If you are one of those casual gamers who just want to enjoy a game with good graphics and stories, this also suits you. The game is not perfect, there are things here and there (controls, cutscenes, loadings etc) that can annoy you but overall, this is a great game.Pros: - Astonishing graphics.- Good combat style. Lots of different things you can try out.- Not open world but there are still lots of optional exploring aspects.- Consistent 60fps at the highest graphics settings, no noticeable frame drop so far.Meh:- Some cutscenes look quite weird, much different/worse than in-game graphics.- There are small areas here and there that you just pass through in 5 seconds. This is annoying since you get that loading screen whenever you move to another area. Cons:- Default key setting for keyboard and mouse is pretty awkward imo. I figured out what works for me pretty quickly as I have experience playing games like this but if you are new to this type of combat style, it might take you a while to figure out what works for you.- I feel like this game requires you to play through multiple times before you can enjoy all the contents. I really hate when games force me to play through the entire thing multiple times to complete all contents. This might not be true but with what I see so far, I have a strong feeling this is the case here as well. Will revise in the future if not. TL;DR: Not GOTY but still a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, up until about 20 hours where I encountered a boss that was basically two-hitting my team members, while requiring us to hit him for 30mn straight. Once you understand that you can only control one character and the other 3 are AI controlled, and you see them getting knocked out in two hits without being able to do anything, thats bad.The game basically required me at that point to grind regular enemies for hours until I leveled up enough so that my team members could tank that boss and not get one or two-shotted. Worse, healing items are quite expensive and over a bloody 30mn fight (yes, actual 30 minutes because the bosses have hundreds of thousands of HP, that is an actual design choice the devs made), you use a ton, I ended up being too poor to buy enough of them to sustain the boss fight.Even so, it's not like I avoided fights earlier in the game, I fought almost every enemy group I saw in the whole game, and that still wasnt enough to be sufficiently leveled. I just don't like games that don't respect my time and expect me to mindlessly grind the same monsters for dozens of hours before a boss fight for me to be able to have a shot against him and not have the fight last half an hour.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the JRPGs and the Tales of series, I highly recommend Tales of Arise. The Story is pretty good if a little rushed at the end and the gameplay is the smoothest it has ever been. Graphically it is a huge step forward for the series, however not all the artistic choices landed for me namely the design of some weapons, levels, and bosses. The characters fill certain tropes but like most the Tales of series cast have enough nuance within them to make them memorable which is great. Over all an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't think i've ever played an anime RPG like this game but all i need to say is...- Amazing game with a really addictive story, makes you get really invested into the characters,- Wonderful soundtrack,- Combat system is really cool and i do love the special ability animations, big diversity of bosses,- Looting is pretty decent aswell,- The game doesn't force you to grind, you do it if you want to, i'm playing on the second hardest difficulty because i do want it to be a challenge but people who only want the story can go for the recommended difficulty,-  You can literally fish, if this last one doesn't convince you in buying the game then idk what will.

_childDocuments_.review: so like, I am around 25 hours into the game and I am loving it!! I'm currently on the third area of the game (I'm not far as I keep just having fun practicing combos while farming) It's amazing, the combat is insanely fluid and is a massive step up from any other tales game. I've played all of the previous games in the series and they are all amazing but from the cinematics to the hyped dramatic moments this game has Tales of Arise simply is in a class of it's own.The Issue: Paid DLC..............look I get that money is an important aspect when it comes to a business however I definitely have an issue with PAID DLC giving stat increases and perks, that imo is too far, however besides that the game is really well done.The Issue: Overpriced as heckYeah...the game is overpriced, considering the game is nearly 100 AUD it's asking for a bit much for what it is, however I personally got the game for 64 dollars through a key and I think the 60-65 mark is perfect for a game like this. I would highly recommend buying it from a cheaper, legitimate third-party.The Issue: Most Content Is Just Story Based-Okay so here me out, I love the story aspect of the game but I personally think that there should be other things to do that aren't main mission, so far the entire game has just been about rushing story and there has barely been any side-quests or sub-goals to accomplish so far, (each area has like maybe 2-10 minutes max or looking around before it's, eh, nothing to do here let's just do main mission) maybe a gathering system that levels up with use to encourage more exploration rather then just "rush story as there isn't really much more to do" The Upside: Diverse and Interesting Characters- all the characters so far have had meaning and feel alive for the most part (ignoring cleche and generic non-mc characters) they seem to have decent personalities, yes it has it's tropes like tsundere's and the whole shabang but for the most part I personally am very interested in how everyone will develop.The Upside: Absolutely Stunning Visuals and Music- the visuals alone are enough to sell me, but with how fantastic the music is during key moments is just unbelievable, each area looks alive and vibrant!! However yes the music can be a bit much at times, with over dramatization in certain fights and scenes that are meant to be more calm, however most key moments both look and sound phenomenal.The Upside: Beautiful and Precise Combat- What can I say other then the fact that the thing that brings this game from a 6/10 to a solid 8/10 maybe even 9/10 is the incredibly lucrative combat system, it has everything you could ask for. You want to switch your play-style and turn into a mage? Go ahead, wanna be a tank? Go ahead, wanna be a bloody tsundere cannon wielding women O' War? Go ahead. -Being able to slowly learn new moves through playing, by being able to experiment until you find what you like, finally finding that move-set that is perfect and feels handcrafted for your specific way of play is just *chefs kiss* exquisite.- This game shines in having limitless possibilities for combat, being able to chain skills together to make a beautiful and flashy masterpiece, I personally go for pure mid-air combo builds that can chain together nearly infinitely and it is just so much fun.TLDR;Would I buy this game again at it's high price point? Yes but most likely only from a cheaper third party, The combat and visuals are to die for and are basically the selling point of the game, if you like lucrative precise and rewarding combat, with beautiful environments, this is most likely the game for you, and you will love it! :) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Suggestions: (keep in mind I am only on the third area so these could be in the game)1. I wish the game was slightly more challenging, I'm playing through the whole game on hard and even then it really isn't much of a challenge (as of the third area) other then the second lord so far- I really wish this game had a mechanic like it's predecessors in which you have a random chance to fight much much stronger elite enemies (world boss style) (yes Ik there are the gigants but tbh they aren't exactly that strong, the only noticeable one so far is the mantis and even that dude I nearly killed (got him to 1/4 hp) at merely only level 20 yet it's a level 42 gigant) I just think that a really small chance in each area for a "legendary" or "elite" monster to spawn would be insanely cool maybe have like 1 or 2 per area that have 1% spawn rates, in which drop like a trophy or have a noticeable change to the area once dead (almost like the creature was the alpha of the area) (maybe a title for each area liberated from these insanely rare, myth-like creatures) I just think it would add a lot of end-game content (ik i'm not at end game but this is just a cool idea I'm thinking of.- random events, maybe every so often in an area you could get random events such as 'saving someone from a small pack of enemies' or 'escort ??? to the nearest town' ect, obviously some people would despise this but maybe having a small reward like 1000 gold or like 100 sp, it's just something to do when you think you've mastered an area or on the way to a new quest ect.- A much more in depth profession system, yes I know you can gather and fish, however I wish there was a way to add a grinding aspect to it that wasn't 'too' grindy that players could maybe get like even just 5 hours of something out of as a cool little profession system with gathering and mining ect.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a long time fan of the Tales Series since 2007.I have played:Tales of LegendiaTales of the AbyssTales of SymphoniaTales of GracesTales of XilliaTales of Xillia 2Tales of ZestiriaTales of BerseriaTales of the RaysTales of CrestoriaTales of Linkand Tales of VesperiaStory:I think this games' story and premise are fairly solid ideas, but could be improved or done better.  It seems to fall just behind some of its older titles like Berseria and Vesperia in this regard but still holds that air of Tales storytelling.(Many instances where the Subtitles don't match with voice lines and have spelling/grammar errors, but that can be patched.)Gameplay:I really enjoyed the gameplay and feel like it has improved and evolved over other titles in a BIG way.Each character is varied but needed, and each character has enough to them that everyone can play the game how they want. EX: "The way I play Alphen won't be the same way as you play Alphen."Having the ability to ignore damage with timing and skill is a great change all around.Enemy Mystic Artes are now tests of skill rather than forced damage.  This is a VERY much appreciated change!This does make Bosses seem a bit more like you are in an MMO Raid, but this is not a bad thing for this game.The only major issue is that there is a lot less enemy types to battle than in most Tales titles.Characters:This aspect seems to fall a bit behind in this game compared to preceding titles.  I like the ideas for each character, but I don't like how the character dynamics were implemented as much as other games like Vesperia, Berseria, and Legendia, whose characters were more flushed out and well rounded.  Solid, but again, could be better.World:Even though the story and characters are not as good as some other Tales titles in my opinion, the world building of this game is fantastic as well as beautiful.  The dynamics of each area during chapters give many ideas about what was before the story began.  I think this title is great with it's world building being up there with Vesperia's flushed out world of "Terca Lumireis" and Legendia's "Shining Blue" which leaves you theorizing about it's world well after you have finished it.Graphics:Arise definitely holds up as one of the best looking Tales titles and manages to look better than most games on the market.Each area feels like there was love and care built into it and feels very real while keeping the fantasy aspect.I think this game is a high tier Tales title that Veteran Tales players should give a chance and I believe that this game would work really well to allow newer people to the series a chance to look through what this franchise has to offer.

_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Tales has ever been, let me start there. I've been playing the series since Eternia on PS1 ages ago, and this is really next level. The story is complex and full of mystery and heart without being "JRPG-convoluted," the characters are all brought together by convenience and their own vendettas and secrets, instead of the common "my best friend and I from our village were out picking berries one day and we found a weird rock on the ground and the evil Empire killed all of our friends and now we are on a quest." It is, sure, centric on Alphen and Shionne, but the supporting cast add so much more that would be missing if they were the same 1-dimensional tropes you see in so many of these games (no shade, I absolutely love so many JRPG's and have played a plethora of franchises, but I am so happy to see Tales growing up so much!) There is not a weak personality in the entire party, and the story is serious and heavy without being obnoxious, and every villain and party member have very complex and interesting motivations, which is a nice change. Nothing is really black and white on Dahna. On to the world, though. Probably a good quarter of my playtime has just been trying to get as high up as possible to pan over these INCREDIBLE environments. Some are legitimately breathtaking; the detail is so fluid and alive and I find myself audibly being like "this is insane," when I step in to a new place sometimes. And even with all of those complex graphics and moving parts, it plays clean as warm butter on PC on the highest settings; I have yet to encounter a single bug or any drop in framerate, no matter how intense the cutscene (and there has been at least one I've actually jumped out of my chair and cheered during,) or no matter how far the view distance and rustling trees, birds flying by your face, etc. The almost watercolor-pencil graphics are so colorful and intricately detailed and, frankly, mesmerizing. As with all Tales games, the cosmetics are a huge part and they added a bunch of extra skill trees depending on what sets you're using and playstyle, but both the pacing of leveling and skill ups and unlocking new Artes is the smoothest and least grindy, well paced I've ever seen in the series. The animations for all of the outfits are great, and they are very well-designed, though I find myself disregarding things like the swimsuits because it just doesn't fit the serious flavor of the story and takes me out of the immersion in cutscenes and skits, more than any game before. That all being said, there's lots of immersion-friendly gear and I find myself spending a lot of time making outfits. I don't fast travel very much because I love exploring and naturally getting some XP and keeping my resources stocked, running across enemies, so I've always been about on par with any enemy I've met in real progression; if you play this way, you'll pretty much never need to backtrack. That's really my biggest tip for the game: don't fast travel except for Owl Forest and you'll be able to naturally keep up, keep working on skill trees, gather new Artes, craft the latest weapons without much grinding at all. That being said, the combat is incredibly crisp; it's Tales combat, but without any clunkiness. The PC keyboard mapping felt a little awkward in the beginning, but I've gotten the handle on it pretty quickly and it's well thought out, and let me say, this is the first time I've played Tales on PC and Evade on right mouse and base attack on left is such a huge qol improvement over a controller. All of the boss fights so far have been a decent challenge, but well thought out, and while they'll make you sweat, they aren't walls that make you leave the game in frustration. Also, dungeons are not too annoying to explore, which the lack of traditional Tales-like puzzles may make some fans of the franchise sad, but I'm fine with being able to keep going without too many "press this light, now go to the third floor, change this light, now go back" headaches. The story is too compelling to get caught up in all that. It's an incredibly well organized, stunning, heart-breaking story of love and endurance and loss and finding beauty in terrible things and bringing out the best in each other, regardless the horrifying circumstances and is absolutely the best game I've played recently. I'm writing this review sitting on a bench on my break at work, and it's occupying a lot of space in my head. I can't wait to go home and see what happens next. The mysteries and twists and turns in the story never feel forced, some are very unexpected and it's been such an incredible ride so far.10/10, would forget to kill monsters and instead stand on a balcony looking at an anime jungle for an hour again.UPDATE: I can't stop crying at how beautiful the environments are, how long this game is and how touching it is. Y'all, this is everything.
