_childDocuments_.review: 100%'d this game and let it sit for about a year before writing a review. I am a huge classic Tales fan and have played nearly all the localized releases. Would I recommend this game? Sure! But not as a "Tales" game. "Tales" fans have certain expectations that this game will simply not hit. However, if you come to it as a standalone title and play it as its own JRPG, it definitely hits the mark. Don't expect a mindblowing story, and don't expect to be moved to tears, but you will have some fun if you like RPGs and a little bit of challenge. (I played on the hardest available difficulty just to keep it interesting).Definitely a good game by its own merit, and I think the reviews accurately reflect that. I do hope the next entry goes back to the "roots" so to speak, but I did enjoy this one from a gameplay and aesthetic perspective. Very beautiful, albeit along the straight and narrow.

_childDocuments_.review: Having only played till the second major dungeon (and i'll try to update this upon completion), it feels better than the previous titles in nearly every way. Combat is more 3D compared to previous games, and it's easy to pick up for those new to the series. It's faster paced in combat, and the story picks up faster too which is always something the Tales of series struggles with.An interesting change from previous games is CP, which is this game's MP/mana system, only CP is exclusively for heals and buffs, and CP is a shared resource among the party. Meaning that (as far as I know) you can go wild with offensive artes and spells with little penalty. You can even call assists (called Boost Attacks) to easily extend your combos. Dodging is very forgiving as well and often give you more meter or damage opportunities. This game rewards aggression quite a bit.And another mechanic that ties into the CP thing are that certain moves spend some HP as well to do big boy damage, so it becomes an interesting balance of deciding to spend HP to quickly clear trash mobs and slowly drain your CP, or conserving HP to hopefully save CP for tougher fights or a longer dungeon run. Also on harder difficulties (with me having played on Hard), mobs can sometimes boop you for 80% of your HP so now your powerful moves can more easily get you killed if your not careful with your tactics and positioning.The only downsides that matter stem from personal preference like that 3D combat mentioned before, character design, and the camera. It might be a good idea to check out some streams or try the demo to see if those things bother you.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is one of the few RPGs in my gigantic catalogue of games across multiple platforms that I gave a go since I was hoping this would live up to the potential I saw in previous games like Tales of Vesperia and Abyss, cautiously optimistic since we have a new director, I avoided a bunch of the marketing cuz of course spoilers and just went in as fresh as I could and kept an open mind in case it was ♥♥♥♥ poopoo peepee garbage.Now I haven't 100%'d the game just yet (dear god the last couple sidequests are pretty involved and also hard), but with the main story finished and nearing 100 hours, I can safely say this is by far one of the best Tales games in the series if not nearing the best inching away towards Vesperia.You have a story that sticks to its primary theme of freedom and multiple themes lining the character arcs and subplots like redemption and forgiveness and tolerance and it really respects what I expected to be a lot of heavy-handed slavery allegories and racial tension. But what we have here is a game that treats its characters like functioning people, they will often not agree on things at first, they will have serious flaws they have to work through even after their portion of the story is finished in order to fit into the party. These characters will discuss what flaws they do have with each other in detail and communicate to each other on how they can try to improve, they will call out another character for saying something potentially insensitive because the other character has a very different perspective on a certain topic or circumstance. You have fairly standard anime archetypes that go beyond what is considered standard, and all of them are important to the story and your party and probably to you because they earn that organically and often brilliantly through the writing.Not to mention the gameplay which offers a fast paced and snappy action RPG rhythm to your standard Tales artes system and FF-esque stagger mechanic. I will say I wish the game gave you the ability to use 6 artes in Manual and Semi-Auto mode much earlier since only having access to 3 in active controlled combat feels insanely restrictive especially for characters like Shionne or Rinwell where if you control them directly you're gonna need more than even the 6 you can set later on.It still doesn't take away how fun each individual party member is to control especially considering some of their more unique mechanics like Kisara's guard counter with her shield which directly enhances certain Artes and turns her into a complete gigachad of damage reversal.The music is also a highlight with a lot of sweeping vocals and grand epic scores to highlight a great adventure to overthrow 300 years of oppression and free your people against all odds, greatly corresponding with lush colors and visuals with areas that feel much larger than they actually are due to how the game is presented in such grand style.Now I do think the enemy variety which is a common contention for this game and probably a few other entries in the series is a bit disappointing but the combat is so fluid and snappy that it doesn't detract too much from the experience, not to mention how many bosses and minibosses are genuinely challenging and intense and varied in comparison.I also noticed weird spelling errors in the subtitles at times since I was playing with the Japanese voice audio which is an easy patch it's just odd at times especially when your lead character Alphen is having a serious moment or something and you see some ♥♥♥♥ like "What are you talking aboit?!" onscreen.As well I'd like to point out that there is a point in the game where it will hand out many MANY higher level sidequests before you're even remotely ready probably under the assumption you'll save them for the postgame and several of them are around level 54-61 when you might as well be the equivalent of level 43 or so.I managed to sweep through fairly well but a level indicator for the side quests might be helpful especially if those are intended for late game.All in all with the level of mature storytelling and brilliantly written and ever-expanding characters in the cast and the crisp and fluid combat and some decently fun side content like fishing, I'd say this is a really good entry into the series and a probable mark of a new, more focused direction in the Tales franchise. Hopefully whatever the next title is has the same scope and quality while iterating on the formula and strong foundation this game has presented under the new director.And by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ god if they somehow have a better cast than this game cuz this is the most enjoyable crew to follow since Vesperia and I really do mean that.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy game to bear Tales-of name.The fight is chaotic, character customization is great(liking the accessory customization), and the scenery is pretty.The cinematography is top-notch especially during Mystic Artes(super moves for those uninitiated) and Boost Strike(new feature from Arise).One feature that actually different this time is the boss Mystic Artes.Instead of your typical cutscene, the boss MA is a full screen attack that you can dodge and prevent.This is awesome because it adds to the chaotic feel and sense of urgency.One of the bosses actually casts one trademark spell from Tales series.I play too many Tales games to recognize the incantation, even though it is altered. I literally stopped attacking and let that Mystic Artes to hit and wipe my party. WORTH IT!!The English voice acting is great. I might do second playthrough in the future with English voice.This is coming from a player who always play jRPG with original/Japanese voice acting.For completionist players, this game is also great to play.It only takes me 1 playthrough and 70+ hours to unlock all achievements, which is pretty short compared to other Tales games. For comparison, I did 2 playthrough of Tales of Berseria(120+ hours) and I still have not unlocked everything.tl;dr. A great game for jRPG players and the worth successor of Tales-of series.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and mechanics are such a huge step down from Berseria. The cool build-a-combo system is gone completely, in favor of just picking 3 ground artes and 3 aerial artes (I've heard this goes up to 3 more for each eventually, but I'm 16 hours in and the withholding of a vital, fun mechanic is torturous). The aerial artes you only ever get to use in juggles and bosses can't be juggled so they're barely relevant, especially against human-sized bosses. The ground artes can't be cancelled at all which makes the combat feel sluggish. The boost artes are an ok idea but their use is so prescriptive and their timers are so long they don't add any complexity to the game, they just add burst damage. Because the artes are so limited in what you can have out, you never want to pilot one of the spellcasters because you're either limiting your damage options or cutting off your healing. And also because they're so limited, you don't get the neat damage multiplying combo routes based on enemy type that Berseria had, it's just a basic rock-paper-scissors elemental thing.All enemies of the same type when you enter an area are at a set level, even when you're much deeper into the area, which leads to poor curves because of how often they're repeated within the same area. Because of the way CP functions as a non-replenishing resource and the frequency of enemies, mobs can't really be challenging and the difficulty spikes are entirely when you run into a boss, who are all huge damage sponges with no real variety to their attacks. All new gear is just straight up better than old gear, which means you're not making any decisions about it. The skill leveling system... lets you focus where you want to and is actually pretty good.Despite all that, this game would be great if the combat had real, meaningful complexity to it. Shame they didn't focus their effort there at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's played most of the Tales games, they made this game worthwhile. Now hear me out, for some people the story or crafting isn't as good as people say. But it's not entirely bad. You'll come across skits and scenes within their journey that makes you love or hate the character. Sometimes makes you wanna ship people together, sometimes you just want them off your team. But overall as long as you're gaining some type of emotion within the game for the characters. The devs did a pretty good job instead of it being bland and trying to skip every dialogue. Combat is amazing and they really did a few things differently but not bad at all. Once you go further into the game you can discover what attributes each character has to which you can weaken and break monsters, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ infinite combo if you wanted to when fighting. and the special move sets that each character has or combine to two people doing together is amazing and reminds me a lot of what Tales of Symphonia Dawn of the New World had. Very nostalgic for me. They have side missions that is pretty cool. Oh and you can farm up animals like cow,pig, or chickens (think those are the only three options) for materials in order for you to make food which provide stats for combat related stuff. But yeah this really depends on you to get it whether on sale or not on sale. But it's still worth playing and you should definitely try it out. Oh and you have the option of downloading it from steam unlocked so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: You play as a sword wielding badass with flaming sword to destroy people. You have a team of 6 companions you gather over the course of your adventure and have to defeat plenty of bosses and small fry to save the world. Its combat system is much better compared to Tales of Berseria, the last tales game i've played. It still feels very spammy, but there is the need to dodge and counter in this game compared to ToB. I played the game on hard up to like the final 2 bosses because everything felt kinda like a big damage sponge and the changes didn't really do much. Compared to ToB, the overworld exploration is much better and open with jumping. Overall combat in this was probably best in the series imo. There is also fishing and ranching! Story and Characters: I'm not going to spoil much, but in my opinion I think the story was decent. The characters definitely developed throughout the journey and the plot felt important to the world building. I do feel like there was a lot of unexplained lore that I wish the game would explain. As for characters I feel like the characters in this game were way cringier than ToB, but still about 75% as enjoyable with their interactions and dynamics as a team. Personally, I think most of them lack the style that ToB characters had which is why I didn't really enjoy them too much. Graphics: Its an anime style. The world feels really fleshed out when running around which I really think makes traveling awesome in the game compared to other games. There are a few monotonous zones but in general it feels pretty handcrafted and nice to look at scenery. The combat is really flashy and has tons of effects. I think you would need a good computer to run this game, but i never experienced any lag while playing so far!Pros:-Fast paced and great combat-Good story and good characters, but slightly cringey with some bad dialogue imo. -Openworld exploration with lots of features and mechanics-Fishing. This is HUGE point for any game and proves its a good game. I didn't really use this mechanic yet but i look forward to messing around with it.-Multiple difficulty settings for all player types.-no grade shop like old tales games which makes ng+ better imo-6 characters to play as with tons of unlockables-skill tree and item crafting to encourage grinding-cooking mechanic way better compared to ToB and feels impactful.-healing mechanics are also way more balanced.Cons:-REALLY slow leveling without dlc xp bonus until you get to late game-money before like 5 lord boss is hard to get without boring grind-combat feels like you hit enemies way too long compared to previous series games. Enemies feel spongy and too tanky, this could be because i'm on hard all game.-dlc is really expensive and kinda needed to speed up grind and QOT features.-i disliked the changes to skits compared to ToB, the 3d comic style didn't feel as interesting or rewarding when watching.-teammate AI is ungodly stupid sometimes, like walking into instant death attacks. lmao.Final Thoughts: If i thought tales of berseria was a 9.5/10 then this would follow in its step as a 9/10 or 8.5 only because I thought the characters/dialogue/story were kinda cringe compared to ToB. The combat and other upgrades to ToB felt really good though! I'm writing this review at level 71 and have completed the majority of quests so far. I'd say the base game of $60 is probably worth its money, I chose the expensive preorder like $110 cause why not and Id say without some of those op preorder bonuses the game would have been way more grindy. I don't think I can recommend the DLC though as its mostly just cosmetics and item boosters. I'm not a super completionist of games so I'm probably going to end up with 70 hours before NG+ wait a few months and play one more time for a total of like 140 hours.  If you think your $60-110 is worth that many hours or more you will probably think this games worth your money. If not just play monster hunter world or something, I find the combat in that more fun than this and you can play with friends. I'll be back to edit this review after I eventually one day 100% the game or do a ng+ run to revise my thoughts.Update: I've 100% the game and that was super easy to do compared to ToB and past tales games. I'd say after giving it some thought the flaws listed earlier are due to the fact the characters feel more one dimensional in this game without very unique personalities. Buy this game on sale, don't waste extra on DLC until then!

_childDocuments_.review: What i like :Artes : Initially an attack chain has three artes but extendable to six (so 12 for two types of artes) as you progress. The arte's type for each characters is unique and these artes choices are adjustable to match the enemy  weaknesses. The challenge is finding the suitable arte's chain so you can get good combo. Once you get it, you get more action.  So fighting enemies becomes much more fun. Movements : You can do movement ablilities like dodge, counter attack, jump,  double jump, jump and dodge. You will find many enemies which has fast movement so you really need to utilize these abilities to defeat it well.  This kind of fluid movement makes fighting the enemy so exciting. Character's Fighting Styles : Each characters has strikingly difference fighting style. It is very fun to get the different feel in fighting when using a certain characters. You can choose your party fighting mode too. It makes every fighting not boring.The battles : Every battle will encourage you to hone your skill in utilizing these character's artes and movement abilities for defeating different types of enemy. I always get an urge to defeat the enemy in a "beautifull/elegant" way. Once I do that,  I always get satisfaction feeling after the battle. Hard and Unknown/Hardest difficulty level : I find that Hard is the most enjoyable. Enemies : The enemies are diverse enough. They have different surprising attack, defense and dodge movement. I usually lose at the first battle just to get to know how the enemy works. I never get monoton feeling as the game progress. The enemy design and ability also different on each stage of the game story.Battle, artes Animation, environment or the graphics : Simply beautiful no complainWhat i dislike :The story (main and skit) : I think It lacks of fun or funny or surprise elements in it. Each characters brings his/her own dark past, but some conversation about the past are kinda repetitive or boring. I think the other "fun/funny" conversations fail to bring balance to the story nuance. The characters's personalities mostly  "ordinary" and many of their conversation actually feels "common".  The emotional impact of the story is low. I think it will be better if there are more intra/interpersonal conflict in the story. The relationship progress between the characters were too slow and at the end are not deep. The ending : The ending is not satisfying. It feels like there should be more piece in it. I think the story is forced to end too soon. The anticlimax is too short.  Weirdly the fight with the last boss is not long enough to give me good victorious feeling.The unknown/Hardest difficulty : Just for certain enemy or bosses. The damage dealt is unreasonably low. The battle turn into exhausting effort because it takes too long of time and resources so it is not fun anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended.Its not a bad game but I am not enjoying it.I am not enjoying the writing for the story or characters. Most of the dialogue makes me cringe because the things they say make no sense or their reactions are so over the top.The combat is okay but I am not a fan of it. It is based on a break system where you do very little damage to enemies until you combo them enough (which can fail if you cant chain enough attacks from all 4 characters) or use a boost attack (which has a timer) to break their defence at which point you one shot them with a special move.The majority of the level design is corridor based and there isnt much to see or do other than run towards the next star on the map. Some of the area's open up a bit and have optional area's but they are too few and far between.The skit scenes have been changed to a storyboard format and the majority of the cutscenes now use ingame graphics (cell shaded). I preferred the animated scenes from previous games as I found them more entertaining.29 hours into it and I am struggling to push through to the end. Hopefully the story will have an interesting twist somewhere.Edit:Played through to the end and I still wouldn't recommend it.The story picks up a bit towards the end but the characters were never enjoyable (until the final credits scene).The combat I would argue is worse in the late game due to the terrible AI. Toward the end you fight more and more boss type enemies with cone/AOE attacks, the AI isn't capable of recognising them and will continue to throw their lives away by running head first into the attacks.Its absurd that the combo system requires all your party to focus attacks and the game doesn't have an option to set them to all attack the same target automatically.I spent the whole final dungeon (hours of game play) spamming the same light spell over and over as it was the most reliable form of damage.If this is how they intend to reboot the franchise then I think its a step back from the games they released before.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game in its entirety and boy it is a ride all the way. Combat is great and while on paper, boost strikes may seem repetitive, it never got old for me once in my 44 hours playing this game. There are one or two bosses that are laughably bad (looking at you Efreet...) but as a whole the game offers a ton of visual and combat diversity from the lands you go through, the sights you'll see and the enemies (enemy variey starts to peter off once you enter the mid to late game though) you fight. Audio is a blast as well from the enemy fx, combat to ost being audible now, great improvement from Sakuraba considering past tales used to fail when it came to combat ost...it was a mess of violins and guitars but in Arise it blends smoothly. know theres alot of noise over DLC but seriously its been with Tales ever since DLC became a thing in the games industry...is it gameplay affecting? yes, but you can turn it off or choose not to buy it. why complain and pass over probably the best JRPG of 2021 (dwarfing NieR Replicant imo) just because theres optional DLC meant for either those who want 0 effort put in or to simply experience the story (just lower the difficulty...). Buy it, its worth the money in this day and age where video games either launch broken, stuffed with DLC/monetisation schemes where they dont belong (p2w mp) or with clown politics that dont belong in the entertainment industry. GJ Bandai!

_childDocuments_.review: While not the best entry of the series, I recognize it for it for it what it can and will be. This is probably the team's best forray into this generation of "Modern game". For better or for worse, the cartoon era is behind us now.I prefer the cartoon era, however the adult themes of Berseria were amazing. Berseria and Arise realocate a lot of mind space into very high RPG or what we know as the "Consequence" RPG space. While not a direct opponent to this (Tales of X2), I think it's thematically not well placed here.There is no direct gravitas on your own decisions, and the ending is not affected. While the last time a Tales game gave us this freedom was actually Xillia 2, it is definitely a step back.All of this would matter if -anything- mattered. You are not a pawn, but you aren't exactly in charge of anything either. You kind of plod your way into this sick destiny because you hate things.In the end, it's a compelling story and it is kind of well done, sort of half Anime version of "Man in the Iron Mask" and all, but it needed to be more impactful.Berseria was a far more Justified ending to Zestiria than even itself, which was itself a tear jerker once you realize how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the world was because of a single man's greed to feel nothing because of his awful sacrifice.

_childDocuments_.review: Well this will be the Last Tales game i get and i'm gonna be watching Namco/Bandai abit more closely now. This sort of Pay to win dlc ♥♥♥♥ needs to go. Not even the costumes are free of it. I didn't buy any of it.  After i got the artifacts the boosted the xp to about 100% which wasn't till like 45-50 then i felt like i was earning the normal xp i should for how annoying some of the fights are.  Which is one of the ways the game tries to get you to pay more. Basically they looked at Monster hunter games free content and thought to themselves. lets charge money for all that. Won't be surprised if there was an achievement for buying all the dlc called "Sucker" I had little to no trouble fighting once i starting using the mage character battles went from wtf to get out of my way. the semi auto movement in a word is Trash. Manual is fine you just have to manual aim like just about everything. except some spells and auto hit abilities.  Game will pause or slow down when you try to change targets manually.  What really grinds my gears about this game is stats for all your equipment feel like they do nothing. some boss mobs become normal mobs which is not so bad, but if you let the other party members try to kill it while you focus on something else it will literally live forever until you hit it even with basic attack. Then it'll prompt the combo attack which will hang around until you obey or time runs out and i lingers for about 30 seconds. The Companion AI is dumber than a bag of rocks most of the time. The pawns in Dragon's Dogma are Smarter. It's always fun to fight something your lvl and it always able to either outright kill you with jump attack or takes half your life with a simple hit. _childDocuments_.review: It took me about 50 hours to clear, start to finish, on the hardest difficulty mode, with more or less all the optional content included. With that out of the way: Pros: 1) The core gameplay is fun. If you liked the Star Ocean series, you'll like this. I did, so I did. The big monster fights especially are a treat. There's a decent amount of enemy variety too. 2) The world is gorgeous. The art team really did put a lot of effort in, and it shows. There's a huge variety in locales and they all have a distinct visual language. Top marks for art. 3) There are times when the dialogue can be funny without being deathly cringe. Cons:1) I found the character development quite shallow. Item crafting is so weak that it might not as well be there, all the gear you find are more or less straight upgrades, and once you find the "good" moves, there doesn't seem to be much sense in using anything else. Spamming Alphen's Reigning Slash cleared 90% of the content for me without any difficulty whatsoever.2) The writing can be hit or miss, and when it misses, boy does it miss. The plot is honestly interesting enough that I kept at it, but there were times I had to mute my speakers for how absolutely atrocious the dialogue was. 3) This is kind of a minor thing, but I found the controller to be quite busy. There's a lot to do in fights, and it takes a bit to get used to. 4) The soundtrack felt very bland to me. Maybe I'm spoiled, but it's no FFX. 5) The endgame and the superbosses are weak as hell. Overall, it's a good title, and I'm glad I spent the $40. It's not the best JRPG out there, or the best on steam even, but it'll do a good job of tiding you over for that Star Ocean fix.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the only games I've completed 100%. I give it a  8.5/10. TLDR: Story and graphics are enough to play this game. Combat is beautiful but repetitive. Default controls suck. I changed them to something more practical. Story: The story is amazing. I thought it was over a few times and was upset at the plot holes that they left behind. I was gravely mistaken. This games story is complete and incredible. This is one of the few games that can pull off having multiple main characters. Game play: What caught my eye immediately was the fact that you go in and out of combat so smoothly. Not like other RPGs were there is a long loading screen in and out of combat. This game drops you in combat in seconds and once the battle is over you're out just as fast. You get the after credits to the battles after you are free to roam around. The combat gets very repetitive after a while. I recommend switching characters often. Each character is fun to play and has their own strengths. You can change active characters battle, change gear, and change your skills.Crafting/cooking/Skills: These are nothing special. drop points in whatever skill you have available, unlock the whole ring, you get the title. Honestly it got to the point where I was just dropping points into stuff just because I had extra points.  Crafting/cooking is mediocre. Nothing special about it at all. cooking and eating holds true benefits only because there are skills that come active "when you are full".

_childDocuments_.review: My first game in the series and wow. Definitely worth my time. For a JRPG, it is very fulfilling with its mechanics, characters, story, and world. Also the graphics are just awesome. Lots of games now try to push the envelope with textures and details, but Tales of Arise finds a perfect balance of anime and game graphics that I hope other games try to emulate. Cell shading is used here to a level that I haven't seen before, filling in all the characters and world with textures enhancing that experience. It's flawless and runs great with minimal system requirements. The sound was good as well as the music appropriate, not standout or lackluster. Gameplay is great with multiple ways to win in battle, along with different characters and abilities. The one thing I never thought I'd say about a game as a negative, there was just too much voice over story sections of commentary that stops the game in its tracks. They aren't longer than a minute or two each time, but they stop the gameplay for a visual comic style of dialogue between characters. It's not that these optional story beats aren't good either. There's just too many of them that after a while I just wanted to continue playing and not watch characters talk for a few minutes every time I get to a new landmark area. Other than that, the game was astounding and make me want to dive into the rest of the series. Definitely a must play for ARPG fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review:Story: 8.5/10Writing: 4/10Characters: 7/10Side Quests: 8/10Post game content; 2/10Ending Credits: 10/10Gameplay:7/10Difficulty: Extremely difficult or Extremely Easy (based on your ability to dodge and mastering the games mechanics)Graphics: 7/10Buy/Wait for Sale/Rent/Pass: Buy for Standard, Buy or Wait for sale on UltimateLong Review (Spoiler Warning ahead)Story: 8.5/10The storys plot is pretty good, with only a few hiccups. Events in game flow pretty well and make for a pretty good synopsis reading. Writing and story is seperated because i feel its important to draw a difference between the two. An example of good story point is about midway in the game, a sequence happens: a party member attempts to kill the lord but is stopped by an ally. She questions them and they state "You have so much anger in your eyes, youre on a dark path... i dont want to lose you. Does our two allies deserve your hate as well just because theyre the same race as that witch over there?" (They didnt say it like that, but thats how the line i feel it SHOULD have been written.)Writing: 4/10The writing is very hit or miss. For me personally, it missed more than it hit. Using the example from story section; Law states this after Rinwell asks him why "I dont know. I just knew i had to stop you." If law had said something closer to what i wrote in story, it would have hit more harder and felt like he had grow a bit while trying to help rinwell realize she was hating all of the Renans instead of just the ones who ruined her life.  The whole time the lady is just standing there, waiting. She should have sent the monster out, had us fight it while she flees, and THEN have a heart to heart session between law and rinrin. I laughed at the scene instead of felt heart strings being tugged.Characters: 7/10The main cast is pretty good, and the character growth can be seen somewhat for the first 4 characters that join the group. The last two dont get nearly as much as they possibly could, and all of their personalities can be boiled down into one sentence: alphen is the leader that wants to make the world better, Shionne is tsundere that opens up once she realizes she is loved by her friends, Rinwell is the moody teen girl that can cast spells, Law is the likable dolt that loves meat, Dohalim is the fancy know it all type, and Kisara is the brother complex personafied (everything she does is based on what he taught her). Thats what truly holds the game back on characters is that they dont feel as real as characters from other games (like Luke from Tales of Abyss. His struggles felt real because of how he was raised and everything happening in the story)Side Quests: 8/10The side quests are pretty good, with some exceptions needing to be made because there is no lvl indicator on the mission screen (seriously, how was i to know there would be a lvl 34 mantis ready to fight at lvl 4 until i actually got into a fight with said mantis? or the fact i would have a lvl 70 boss at the end of this one mission?). Side quests usually boil down to "gather item" "defeat boss" "meet so and so", but thats 90% of side quests anyways.Post game content: 2/10This hurts. It hurts badly. There are 2 new sidequests, one about exploring a dungeon and another is a boss rush from hell. You do get new game +, but even then, there is no real reason to do it except to play on a higher difficulty from the start.Ending Credits: 10/10This is a weird thing to rate, but i do enjoy the ending credits for this game. It gives a bit more information about what happened after the story between the 2 MCs, and the final image is just perfecto. The fact it shows it was all worth it made the game really good imo.Gameplay:8/10Its pretty simple stuff: use artes to attack, dodge the enemy to be able to counter attack, and master attacking weaking spots for massive damage. Thats just in battles. You can farm ores for accessories, farm monsters for monster parts to make weapons (some even being upgraded so farming to make all weapons is nice), fishing and gathering food items for cooking. If you master fishing, you can make pretty good money from it early on. What holds gameplay back is the fact you practically have to grind if you want to make it through the next boss fight, and that Score doesnt seem to have an effect on anything.Difficulty: Extremely difficult or Extremely Easy (based on your ability to dodge and mastering the games mechanics)This game is very difficult until you master dodging and countering. Allies also have a horrible time dodging unless they are under the Strategy "Dont Do Anything", which with the easier dodge nodes in skill tree, makes them dodge almost everything. There are also 1-4 artes each character has that makes them stupidly broken, and paired with the right accessory will make them capable of being even the final secret bosses that much easier. In fact, here are the artes and accessories i use for each character (barring kisara as i dont use her nearly as much as i should)Alphen: Reigning Slash (from Sword artes usage). Warrior emblem with 4 +60 attacks, or Shionne: Magna Ray or Glacio Celestra (from bombshell title unlocked by shooting bombs with special ammo). For support: cp cost reduction and CP cost in all slots, for damage on Glacio use either magic accessory or half ag cost 50% with 2 slots of water +15% damage and 2 slots of AG half cost for maximum damage output chance.Rinwell: Celestial Hammer (Bibliophile title earned from sidequest to show books to woman in library of Menencia), Swallows Flight (unlocked upon earning title for Spell Cancellor which is from canceling enemy artes), Photon Flash (unlocked at start?) or Subzero Confinement (unlocked through water artes usage?) For Swallows Flight and photon flash, I would use Magic +15% with 4 Wind or light +15% damage, for Celestial and Subzero, i would suggest Half artes chance 50% with 2 half artes chance and 2 Light or water 15%. You could change one of the half artes into an extra element, but youre lowering the chance to lower the cost, meaning less damage per AG gauge.Law: For longest time i would use Dragon Shot into Fang Bolero, but Divine Fang Blast (unlocked through Fist usage?) deals massive damage. Warrior accessory with 4 +60 attack works on first combo, idk if it also works for DFB.Doholim: at start my combo was elusive deity into tornado dive. Using that combo enough, he can spam Crescent Flash (unlocked through Staff Usage?). For crescent flash, Magic 15% with 4 wind +15% damage or Half AG cost with 3 wind +15% and 1 half ag cost chance. (due to his ability where dodging raises his staffs damage and penetration, only 1 is needed as you should be able to dodge to recovery AG)Since i havent experimented with Kisara, there is only 3 moves i can suggest: Guardian Field, Flaming Meteor, and Igneous Discharge. As for accessory, my guess would be Earth +15% for igneous, and then whatever stat her artes mostly focus on damageGraphics: 7/10The graphics are nice to look at sometimes, but sometimes there is a gradiant that is hard to miss and kinda looks off. Maybe im just weird, but its still nice to look at none the less.Buy/Wait for Sale/Rent/Pass: Buy for Standard, Buy or Wait for sale on UltimateIf you do not care for the DLC, i would suggest getting just the standard edition. Everything I just talked about is possible in the standard edition. Some DLC are nice, like the only 1 item cost ones as it reduces the amount of grinding you will need to do. The biggest gripe i have with DLC is the fact that the DLC costumes in Ultimate are the only ones that have titles, meaning getting the middle one is purely for the bonuses they give. Also, not putting the 99 item capacity inside any of the bonus editions feels like a slap in the face. "oh, you want to carry more than 15 gels and revives? Too bad, give us more money. We dont care if you spent $100, we want $5 more"

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't done an review in a long time but lets give it a shot!!!As an avid fan of RPGs, I've played many through the years along with my fair share of Tales games.  However, I've watched as the franchise has steadily declined over the last few entries and i proceeded into this one with caution. Having said that, Tales of Arise is a significant return to form, but there are some issues that I'd like to address.Gameplay 9/10This area is an improvement in every form, and it is without a doubt my favorite combat system that Tales has ever created. The battles in this game are fast, combo-oriented, and extremely satisfying. Enemies can be a little spongy, and battles can take a long time, especially boss battles later in the game, but they are so fun and rewarding that in my 65+ hours with the game i never grew tired of them.One notable addition is a clever combo system called "Boost Strikes," which allows you to pull off what are essentially one-hit kill combo attacks with another party member, but the catch is that you must have built up quite a hefty combo on the opponent without being hit, and keeping them stun-locked throughout. As the game progresses and the player becomes more acquainted with combat, these moves become easier to execute, resulting in a very rewarding mechanic within the battles and MY GOD are they gorgeous to look at.There are a variety of other side hobbies you might pursue to add to your gaming drive, but the majority are simple and quick to complete. The level of exploration here is one significant change. Tales of Arise is still a linear game, but there are plenty of big locations to explore and hidden surprises to discover. It helps that this is the series' most beautiful game, and probably one of the best-looking games of all time. It comes down to whether you like the graphics style or not, but some of the landscapes in this game are so magnificent that I found myself revisiting particular places just to soak in the scenery.Story - 8/10This is where I have the majority of my troubles with the game. Now before I have an angry mob chase me down with pitchforks, let me explain : I enjoyed the story and had an amazing time with the characters and even ended up loving them, but there were a few issues that hindered this journey from climbing the pantheon of some of my favorite stories/characters in the franchise (Vesperia, Symphonia, Xillia). I'll break it down into two sections: one regarding the main plot, and another about the characters.This game's plot is actually extremely engaging, and it kept me interested until approximately the last quarter of the game. It felt as if the game became so engrossed in its message that it lost focus and became a little weird at the finish. One game I can compare this to is Persona 5. AND I LOVE THAT GAME! However, some RPGS tend to do this a lot by have a strong story then just letting it become a bit goofy and out of left field.It took me a long time to figure out why this cast of characters didn't exactly connect with me at first, but after many hours with them, I believe I've finally cracked the code. This game has a plot that is, to be honest, a little dark and deals with some important issues. Because of this, I believe this cast lacks the same level of "fun" as prior casts. Though I did end up loving them in the end and had a ton of laugh out loud moments. I think back at other games like Berseria, which had a serious plot as well.... but was able to generate some funny, laugh-out-loud moments that strengthened the cast's bond.There are instances like that in the game as I said, but they are mostly in optional skits and not in the main story dialogue. There are many moments of over-emotional reactions to things that felt very out of place, many characters apologizing for saying or asking something that didn't need an apology, and just some generally awkward dialogue, whether it's due to the script, over-acting, direction given to the actors, or a combination of all three.As a long-time fan of the JRPG genre, I'm used to bad dialogue, but the Tales series has done much better in the past, so it felt like a step back in that aspect. While most of the bosses were pretty badass (LOVED THE BOSS FIGHTS IN THIS GAME!) It also doesn't help that the main villain is really weak and underdeveloped, which is disappointing coming from a franchise that has previously created some excellent villains. I haven't felt that since Necron in Final Fantasy IX. On a more positive side, I liked how this game handled the themes it picked, and I think it's a very refreshing break from what they've done before; it felt fresh and intriguing (until around the last quarter), and several of the characters are standouts.Graphics & Sound - 9/10I don't have anything to add to what I've already said. The environments are wonderful, and I say that as someone who has played a lot of video games (My profile is proof and thats only 1/30th of what i have). The character models are extremely detailed, and the fighting animations are both rewarding and enjoyable to watch repeatedly.The soundtrack is excellent (Always let the intro play when i started) and enhances the experience, but the voice acting, although pretty decent, felt a bit over-acted at times,Overall - 8.6/10Tales of Arise is a fantastic new installment in the series, and it's a huge step forward after a string of duds. I believe that a few steps back were done in terms of plot, but given how many steps forward were achieved in terms of gameplay and graphics, I consider this to be one of the better entries. Should you buy it? YES!!! TOTALLY!!!

Aside from a few stutters this game is a visual treat in the overworld, in towns, and in its combat arenas. The quality of the art and animation remains consistent in battle, which overall was intuitive, engaging, and fun. While a few of the characters in the six-member main cast are forgettable, overall the protagonists were easy to relate to and succeeded in making me care about their stories and fates. The voice acting performances, as usual for the tales series, were phenomenal (I played in English) and there as not a minute of my experience I did not enjoy. This game is a must-play for any gamer who appreciates a well-crafted story and the JRPG style.Final Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Received as a gift from a friend so I guess that counts as receiving it for free.To preface, I haven't played another Tales game besides Vesperia, and that was only very briefly so I don't remember much. I went in with pretty much a blank slate with 0 expectations or predisposition on what a 'Tales' game should be. Overall, if you want a summary of my opinion, don't go in expecting an RPG that's going to blow your socks off or change your worldview, just a fun 40-50 hour romp like you had when you were a kid who just played whatever you got for Christmas.What stood out to me most in the game were the skits and mid battle character dialogue. The main story is fairly generic; if you've ever watched an anime, read a manga, or played an anime style game where there's a 'oppressor' class and an 'oppressed' class, you already know most of the story beats. If you've watched "Why Do You Always Kill Gods in JRPGs" by Moon Channel, then you also understand all of the cultural context behind the story too, so no surprises there either. The skits, bond stories and battle dialogue is where I feel a lot of effort went into the character building though. There's lots of little characterization moments that make them worth sitting through or paying attention to in the midst of battle. Unfortunately, most of the skits are optional and just lengthen the main game if you decide to view them at the first moment they're available, and to watch them again you have to rest at a campfire and Reminisce so most people will likely end up ignoring them, especially if they just want to breeze through the story. It feels as though you're kind of expected to watch them though, so you may end up with different views on a character depending on if you did/didn't watch them. Still, I wish more RPGs had the sort of optional mini side story cutscenes that you can activate at any time, rather than pushing you down a non-optional mini story in the middle of the main plot because it's character building time.The character action combat has all it needs to be good, but fails at a few key points:From what I've seen from the other reviews, some of these are related to Arise trying something new though, so I won't be as harsh about it since it's pretty much the team's first time trying something like this. Still, most of these do bring down the combat experience by a good amount.So yeah. It's a fine game. I'm not going to not recommend a game just because it isn't the Citizen Kane of RPGs, but if that's what you want constant unending blockbusters out of gaming then imo don't get this one. If you're just looking to be entertained (this is an entertainment medium, after all) then get this game whenever its price fits what you'd pay for a fairly generic but still fun anime RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I only have minor complaints about this game. Overall, this is a game that everyone shouldn't miss~TLDRReally fun game, controls are not too complicated (I used a controller to play), owls are cute, fishing is not boring, the interactions between characters throughout the entire journey and beyond is great attention to detail, making your gameplay less boring as you move from place to place. Overall, it is a fun game.ControlsMoving around the map isn't hard. As for controls during battle, there are a lot of tutorial fights throughout the game, so you won't feel like a complete idiot when looking at all the things you can do in combat.CombatYou don't really notice the different variants of enemies until you are 50% through the story, which by then you should be about 15~20 hours in already, so give the game developers a break~ It is a JRPG afterall~ Moving on the the combat, you will be getting new characters as you move to new regions, and this will go on for quite some time, so combat won't feel repetitive until after a long time. Each character represents a completely different fighting style, just try them all and pick the one you like the most.CosmeticsYou can buy the DLC if you really like the costumes. But the costumes in-game are also quite varied, so even without DLC you won't feel too bland. Each weapon looks different, you can choose to equip your strongest weapon, but wear the skin of the one you like the most, a rather nice design~OwlsThey are cute. So go around the map and find them. Plus, you do get rewards if you find a certain number of owls, so why not~Graphics and Map DesignGraphics is an improvement compared to the last Tales of game released on PC. The game does not require crazy good GPU to run smoothly and look nice at the same time, so I would have to praise the developers for the nice optimization done here. As for map design, each location/region has its own theme, and you can see the distinction quite clearly. They aren't just different colored versions of the previous map. This is also a plus~Sound and MusicThe songs are great~ The music starts and stops at the right moments during the story.Story (Spoilers ahead)I left this for the last, so if you don't want to read spoilers, you can leave now~Now overall, the story isn't bad. The message it wants to bring to the audience is clear from the very beginning. And, who doesn't like a happy ending? Especially after everything that the party had went through. However, even a good story has flaws. Let's start with the 5 countries. Each country represents a potential form of tyranny or exploitation that could exist in our world, and as we move and fight through the country, we see different arguments as to what we can do to fight against these oppression. However, given that we have a lot of story and setting to lay out, each of the countries were not given enough time. We merely touch the surface on these arguments and points before we move on to the next location. It would be much better if we can go deeper into each of these problems. But that would mean that this game will have to split into 2 parts. As a matter of fact, that is exactly what the developers did~ Well, sort of. You can tell that the first section of the story is over after you beat Vholran, and the story plays out, then a new song is played. Almost like how an anime gets a new opening in a new season~The first half of the story is great, it sets the mood, the basic settings. While it could have been better, it certainly isn't bad. It is the second half that is rather lacking. After beating Vholran, the pace begins to speed up. You find the spacechip, fly to Lenegis, close up the end of Dohalim's story arc, get a load of information, and before you can digest it, you get thrown into an unknown section in space, only to be saved and experience a lot more exposition dump. After that, gets thrown to Rena to fight the final boss. Did my description sound like it's a rush? That is because it is. While you can choose to slow down yourself and go to do some side-quests first, you don't really have much to do if you were actively clearing them as you move across the map. Also, the side-quests you unlock before the final boss are mostly of a much higher level then you would normally be during that section of the story. So you most likely have nothing much to do but to go on and fight the final boss. While there are a bunch of things you can do after you beat the final boss, they are all optional. Story wise, the pacing of the first half and the second half feels different. Considering the amount of exposition you get, it would have been nicer if they give a little more room to breathe.Now moving on to the ending. I am not complaining about the happy ending, as I have said before, they all deserved it. But it is how we got there that bothers me. After you beat the ugly but easy boss, Vholran flys in, somehow, and you have to fight him. Alright, at least we get to finish him off ourselves... At least, that was what I hoped to do. I mean, we already stabbed this guy once with the flaming sword, we left him to die in a collapsing facility the second time, killing him once and for all is nothing isn't it? Nope~ After we (Alphen) single-handedly beat Vholran, all of a sudden we choose to not kill him? We try to persuade him to become good? We choose to forgive him? What is this? 10/10 all over again? At least Vholran didn't disappoint us, he chose to take the Renas Alma and blow himself up~ Well done~ Now how is Alphen going to save Shionne? At this point, I don't really care because Alphen had the perfect chance, and he decides to be an idiot. But no~ Somehow Alphen manage to force everyone on Dahna give him power to save his girl~ This section of the story is what bothers me the most. Happy ending isn't a problem. The problem is the sudden shift in tone. Throughout the entire game we were dealing with rather serious matters, and the whole party deals with it seriously. But in the final moment, it suddenly becomes a third-rate shounen anime... This one section feels really out of place, and I am sure I am not the only one who feels that.Overall, the story is well written. It had a great start, it would've been better if it had more time to go deeper into some of its discussions and arguments. While it might seem like I am bashing its second part, it is actually not as bad as it might seem here. The development, layers after layers of truth and lies, all of it isn't bad. It just needs a little more breathing room. The only section of the story that I hate is how Alphen dealt with Vholran in the end. But after that, we get our happy ending~ Which is actually quite nice after the previous few Tales of games. After the main story, we can move on to the side-quests, one of which unlocks the Otherworld. In it, there is a pleasant surprise to players who had played Tales of Zesteria and Tales of Bersaria before~

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a JRPG title, and with that in mind you'll have to take into consideration that it is a port. Lip syncing is completely off and the story and dramatics have been tuned to a Japanese audience. Every character in the game is an emotional wreck and every little feeling gets thoroughly talked about. There's tons of voice acting, videos and action comic book style skits that you get to watch.  At times it feels overwhelming with the emotional roller coaster you are forced to endure, one moment a character is having a happy feeling and on the next video - he/she is an emotional train wreck. However, there are hidden gems that are well placed and is treat to experience when playing the game. Combat is a lot of fun, especially when you get good enough to sequence multiple chain events in a single battle. It's fast paced fighting and when grinding you can move from battle to battle with very little wasted time between battles. Exp and loot are calculated on a side window at the end of every fight - loot automatically makes it way into your inventory. Also at the end of multiple battles you end up resting at a campsite to recover HPs and buy/sell whatever you found.Tales of Arise is a fun game and if you factor in that there's going to be a lot of cheesy JRPG videos to watch with the possibility of a good story buried somewhere deep. Combat is hell of a lot of fun, and for me it's always - just one more battle before bedtime... which ends up being 50 or so and a few less hours of sleep for me the next day.

_childDocuments_.review: I am only about six hours in and there is a lot to enjoy. The combat is fantastic, the graphics are stylized and beautiful, the story is interesting. So, I was trying to find the castle gates and I would go into my map, and I looked at every map and could not find how to get to the gates. After an hour of literally running around every map in the first area, I looked it up online and you have to take an elevator...It was so frustrating. Why can't the star be where ever you are to guide you to the quest location? It isn't very helpful just showing up on the map where the gates are. It makes me not want to continue the game, but we will see after I take a break from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with every expectation that one would have for being a "Tales of" fan. _childDocuments_.review: As someone that was never able to stomach a Tales game before, I can confidently say that this is an amazing title to get into the series with. It was very obviously designed with accessibility in mind without necessarily hampering the experience for players that want to be challenged. If you decide you aren't interested in the combat or pushing the difficulty and just want to treat it like more of an exploration/story game, then you can play on Story mode and also set the battle mode to "Auto" so that the computer plays for you. I've seen people do just that and the computers can clear the whole game on their own on the easiest difficulty.I personally played on Hard and did every boss either at or severely under the recommended level except for the ultimate endgame fight which I needed to be maxed out to beat. Overall, if you're willing to experiment with all of the characters and set up their tactics, you'll likely find the game to be engaging and challenging. Perfect difficulty in story games for me is when you struggle, but also still beat things first try so as not to break immersion too much. The end game stuff can require more effort and a few attempts, but the Hard mode was damn near perfectly balanced even as I completed every side quest.The characters made me laugh and "aw" a lot. I didn't really resonate with the story a ton, but the characters kept it interesting. If you're a sucker for cheesy anime love stories with over the top stakes, I think you'll very much enjoy the whole thing.Solid 8/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A strong,  contender for my favourite Tales game ever. It  like Tales in every way that matters; all of the little bits that make these games are there. The characters and world are wonderfully vibrant (not just visually!) & incredibly nuanced — I've cried more times than I can count, at this point, and I've loved every second of it. The in-world issues the game deals with are approached with immense nuance as well, much more than I've come to expect from  rpg.The battle system is good — it, too, has all of the important Tales bits, and has streamlined them in wonderful ways —, though I definitely recommend a controller or extensive keybind remapping to avoid making your wrists and fingers absolutely hate you if you're playing mouse + keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I'm finished, I can safely say this is my favorite Tales of game yet. I say that as someone who isn't a longtime fan, nor a person who has completed many Tales games. In fact, it's the opposite. I have this weird tendency since I first beat Symphonia on GC (years ago when it first launched) to impulse buy Tales games, then after 10-15 hours end up dropping them.Whether it's the story doesn't move along fast enough or the characters just aren't interesting, something fails to grasp me & encourage me to see it through. This game never had that issue. I was hooked after an hour, played through 8 hours right away, and couldn't wait until my next weekend to put more time in.Graphics are much better than Beseria, and I had no issue running the game at 4k / 60fps on high settings with an RTX 2070 Super. I'm pretty sure if I had a higher refresh rate display, it would've ran even smoother. The game has minor issues:*90% of side quests are just "defeat X monster" (with very few variations)*last 1/3 of the game isn't as exciting as the first 2/3*story gets pretty convoluted near the end (not too hard to follow, but just overly complicated & kind of silly)*certain skill trees and abilities are locked behind paid DLC*not much variation in enemies*friendly AI just lets itself stand in hazard areas & get annihilated by certain enemies*not much post-game Those things didn't really affect my enjoyment much though. Increasing the difficulty can reward you with more XP & CP, so it rewards you for the challenge. If something's too hard or you feel it's taking too long, difficulty can be dropped on the fly (I did it twice just to move on quicker, guilty). The post-game content is sparse, but if you're a Tales fan, it's made for you. Even though I haven't really felt compelled to start a new game+ save, I'm completely satisfied with my purchase, and won't regret if it just drops on Game Pass out of the blue (like Scarlet Nexus). Highly recommend if you like non-turnbased JRPG's. Overall: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often "don't recommend" games that I play on Steam, and I probably won't be doing it to this game if there's a middle ground and not just "Yes" or "No".Tales of Arise, if you've played the Demo, feels so fun to play. But getting up to that point, i.e., the early game, is such a grueling experience. Tales of Berseria, for example, had me enjoying its combat system from the get-go; even without Velvet's OP Soul Arte and generally just fighting the weaker mobs found in the early areas. Because the combat is smooth and enjoyable.Tales of Arise feels like they tried to mix in the methodical gameplay of a souls-like to their anime JRPG combat system that you can find from prior games. What resulted from that mix is a game that tells you to build up your combo and perform crazy ability chains, but with enemy designs that scream "wait for the right timing and play it methodically". You can't give me two opposing gameplay ideas in one go.Even though I play games 60% because of their stories, and I got this game on a 60% sale, having to withstand this awful combat system for more than 40 hours just to see a mediocre storyline isn't worth my time and money. I really wanted to enjoy the game, but the combat ain't just doing it for me.If you're a fan of the Tales series, this is definitely a game you would want to pick up. It has that Tales formula that probably what made you love the franchise in the first place. If you're like me that has played only a couple of them (I've played both Tales of Destiny on the PS1 and Tales of Berseria), or are new to the franchise, it'll probably be a hit or miss, especially if you're looking for a combat system similar to Berseria.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this might be the most fun I've had battling in a Tales game, enough that I did something I almost never do, and went out of my way to cop every achievement. Arise is graphically pleasing affair, made better by a solid 60fps at 4K. It's fast, focused, and fluid. Out of battle, the environments are pleasing too, though they're not enormous maps. With practically no loading screens, transitioning to a new area isn't distracting or annoying. The sound design is notable too. Enemy design is also pretty good in the new style Unreal battle engine, and makes the most of a few uber-large creatures -- but there are few common enemy types. The writing is somewhat weak, though it's more the dialog that's terrible. The plot itself is... around par for the series? I don't know how to judge it per se. Tales of Berseria had more interesting and dynamic characters and a better plot overall, while Vesperia is worth playing for skits alone, but Arise is basically a series of battles with talking -- and some of that dialog is cringe-inducing on a significant level. Also, there are still a number of text errors in the subtitles too, which is annoying. Not as many as Berseria, but still unacceptable for a game on this level. However, I think the battle system makes up for many of the shortcomings. It's more fun than previous entries for certain, but it might get old after the first play through.  There are also few things to do when not battling or when taking a break, with fishing the primary side activity. The fishing is all right, but its not substantial enough by itself. There aren't really any optional areas or dungeons save for a sidequest which is available after the main game sequence, and that's it. I recommend this game, but its good to have realistic expectations about what  you're getting into.
_childDocuments_.name: Tales of Arise

_childDocuments_.review: Tales as a series has always had a massive emphasis on its characters, and building up their relationships with one another, and Tales of Arise is no different. Although the story begins bland and cliched, the characters draw you in, and you find yourself so invested in them that you're compelled to continue. The subtle characterization through skits, facial expressions, and minute reactions, combined with explicit characterization and development through powerful story beats and revelations makes the cast extremely likable and fleshed out, and keeps you thoroughly engaged. Tales of Arise unfortunately does have many flaws, including excessive reuse of enemies, a plethora of damage-sponges, and sometimes subpar narrative execution, but these are dramatically outweighed by its strengths, which mainly lie in its characters and word-building. It is clear that the world and narrative of Tales of Arise was very well thought out, and you can feel the love and care put into it, even as it struggles a bit in implementing those ideas. Overall, I really loved this game, and I can't remember ever getting as emotional over an ending as I did for this one, which is a testament to how strongly it built up its characters. Tales of Arise is ultimately a game that shines brightly in spite of its flaws, and I'm very excited for the next Tales game.

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10Very nice looking game, runs smoothly, effects are pretty and sounds good. Combat is nice, gets really repetitive quickly. Changing difficulty only makes you wack them more for bonus exp, eventually I just changed it to normal. Bosses feel like a chore, just a mob with more hp with an increase in attacks that you have to dodge. Would've been cool to see unique combat strats for each one.Good amount of exploration, every area is unique and sidequests for you to do. Mobs start to look bland and are just recolours of weaker versions. Also some cities just feel so empty.Characters look cool and have some interesting/funny dialogue between them. The leveling system rewards you for the more you explore (i think) so at the end game i missed out on so many artes and skill grids.The plot is really basic hero saves the world JRPG stuff, started losing interest after finding the full party. Second half of the game drags out and pours so much lore into you, could've been better paced.Overall, a decent game if you're into JRPG's, but not if you want something special or unique. I would mainly recommend it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the first Tales games I played, I have played Symphonia, Vesperia and Berseria before. I really enjoyed Berseria and I heard everyone was saying this was even better and then I saw the reviews and got hyped. What a disappointment once I started playing it.First of all the positives, which are the graphics which are better and the battle system ... at the beginning.The story is a mess. First you go around 5 different "domains" (more like cities tbh) in what feels like a NES game plot. You barely get to know the rulers of these places (except for one). On top of that there is a lot that remains a mystery. Nobody in the party asks Shionne about why she is so hell bent on destroying the lords or why she was on that train. They just go along with it.  However, once you finish with the lords the game gets even worse. The second half is rushed and there are so many plot holes that I stopped caring about the story.Characters are very one dimensional and you can barely relate to them. Their motivations are barely believable. Law, for instance, after getting his father captured because he did not like him has a sudden change of heart just before his dad is about to be executed (he dies anyway) and now he is a good boy and wants to help the team to destroy the Renans and the rest of the party is like "yeah, come along buddy even though we were fighting some minutes ago!". It is so jarring especially when compared to Berseria where you could feel why Velvet was so angry and you really wanted to put an end to the villain who also had a very good reason for the things he was doing.Gameplay is atrocious, the combat system was fun at the beginning but the enemies are massive sponges on the latter half and the dungeons (the part I hated the most of Berseria) are even worse here. Just corridors with a lot of enemies. Oh and the enemies ... The developers have palette swapped the same 10 enemies during the whole game. It's just so lazy. They even made a palette swap of one of the bosses.I am just very disappointed with this game. I thought I was in for a very nice JRPG, but this is just generic and boring. Not sure how this won RPG of the year on The Game Awards considering it was against the much better (but still a little bit flawed) Shin Megami Tensei V. If you want to play a good JRPG and have Nintendo Switch play that instead of this piece of garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: Go play Tales of Berseria instead.Tales of Arise is a JRPG with decent gameplay, even if balance between moves makes you wonder who got paid to playtest this . 2 out of 6 characters are barely playable and only used because their boost attacks cheese mechanics. In the end playing the best DPS character in the game and just dodging and spamming one button was kinda fun, so gameplay part passes.Story doesn't. Story is supposed to be good in JRPGS, but it's barely watchable. Main cast is boring and uninspiring, antagonists are so evil you feel like you are watching Saturday morning children cartoon instead of a serious story. Premise is extremely dark, but protagonists are heroic goody two-shoes. It's barely bearable in first 2 nations, but after that party's reactions are so absurd I wasn't able to take story seriously at all. Ending is absurd too, no resolution, antagonists having to suicide to progress the story anywhere, etc.This is not helped by the fact that interactions between party members aren't interesting in 90% of the cases. It's feels like they talk about same things over and over and over again, without any development. Honestly the funniest dialogue in the game happened when whole party fell from a really high place in the mountain and it wasn't even a skit.Overall not worth money spent, you are better off playing literally any other Tales game in the series if you can handle old graphics and worse gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for Tales of Arise for a long time, I bought it on launch and I finally finished it. I thought to myself "Surely this can't beat the masterpiece that was Tales of Berseria, right?".Oh, how Bandai managed to surprise me and go well beyond my high expectations.There are two planets, Dahna and Rena. Rena was always considered to be the land of the righteous and divine, even if the truth became distorted across generations of the people of Dahna. 300 years before the events of the game, Rena invaded Dahna and enslaved it, pillaging the planet of its astral energy and the people of its freedom. After that, the planet was divided and thus the Five Lords appeared, acting as representatives of Rena and competing in the Crown Contest to become the Sovereign who would rule over Renans.You start the game as a slave, known as the "Iron Mask" because of the mask he finds himself wearing for a reason he does not remember... yet. Iron Mask is tired of living as a slave, so he decides to rebel and fight back against the Renans. Ironically, his first ally is Shionne, a  prisoner with the peculiar trait of having thorns around her which prevent anyone from touching her without feeling extreme pain. Curious enough, Iron Mask also suffers from not feeling pain, see where I'm coming from?The two decide to party up along with Zephyr, the leader of the Dahnan rebellion "Crimson Crows".In terms of party, I do not think Arise surpasses Berseria. That is not to say the party is bad (quite the contrary, in fact).Here is a brief summary of each party member aside from Iron Mask and Shionne which I've already talked about before:- Rinwell: the only survivor of Dahnan magicians, she grows to hate Renans and swears to get revenge for her people's death, including her parents.- Law: a misguided young boy, he starts off at the wrong side of history but will soon learn the error of his ways and swears to make up for his mistakes by joining Iron Mask in his quest for freedom. Law is very kind, but he's also stupid. The good kind of stupid though, the kind that makes you laugh because of his sheer stupidity. - Dohalim il Qaras: a Renan and quite an important one. He arrives at Dahna and his very first act as a Renan is to stop Dahnan slavery and strive for equality between the Dahnans and the Renans. He really loves antiques, he can also be very oblivious.- Kisara: one of the strongest Dahnan soldiers, serving one of the Five Lords. Highly regarded by Renan soldiers as well, she also acts as the "mother" of the party. In fact, she takes care of everyone's needs such as cooking and laundry, she also really loves fishing. She is also an absolute tank.I personally think the party goes extremely well together, it is a joy to see them talking to each other with the well known "skits", typical of the Tales of series. I've never been bored one bit, the conversations are all very interesting and you can see the love put into the interactions between characters.And here is where everyone is suddenly divided between "game good" and "game bad".Me? I'm more of a "game good" guy, but I can't deny that there are major flaws in Tales of Arise's combat.You see, the game really encourages combo play and using different artes to keep the fight going, you are rewarded with an insta-kill attack if you manage to fight good enough. This goes for every enemy, that means you can insta-kill one and immediately attack the second one and start another combo chain for yet another insta-kill and so on. Insta-kills are basically two characters (of your choice) performing an unique attack, each combination having different attacks & animations so you are free to experiment.Sounds good on paper, right? Well, the huge problem is: you are encouraged to perform combos, yet the enemies are extremely  combos, that means they are  stunned unless you use certain party members' special attacks (which have a cooldown). So you are stuck dealing with what seems to be huge damage sponges, which can be severely exhausting halfway through the game. Me personally, I had to switch to easy mode because the amount of exp gained + the damage sponges were starting to turn me off, which is really sad considering the actual combat mechanics themselves are FUN.Now for the real question: That is entirely subjective, but if you had to ask me, I would say that this is indeed my favourite Tales of in the series, and that's saying a lot since I really loved Berseria and Xillia.I personally think Tales of Arise absolutely deserved to win the best JRPG of 2021 and most of the people crying in the Steam Discussions are mostly just extremely mad either because they don't understand basic game mechanics or because  or even worse .Look, I am a big fan of the Shin Megami Tensei series, I played through the SMT series before they came on Steam, I 100% understand the frustration.However, I also believe Tales of Arise really deserved to be the spotlight of 2021, this is the game that will finally bring the series to a bigger audience: the Final Fantasy VII of the FF series, the Persona 5 of the Persona series. And I couldn't possibly be happier for the developers who put their heart into this game, which you can clearly notice while playing.Rating is subjective and I highly recommend playing the game for yourself.With that said, I personally rate Tales of Arise:I loved this game, I am very glad I paid full price and supported the developers who put an immense amount of work to create this masterpiece. I am very glad these developers are finally getting acknowledged, I am very happy to see them thanking us, the Tales of community, for buying the game and supporting them.The Tales of series has a bright future ahead, after all this time, and I am here to witness it.Now then-

_childDocuments_.review: The Tales of franchise has really been outdoing itself with these last two games in the series.  I enjoyed Berseria a lot.  It was the game in the franchise the overcame my nostalgia for Symphonia and became one of the funnest games I've played in it's own right.  It represented massive improvements to Tales of Gameplay.  Arise managed to make fairly major improvements to Berseria.  The game actually feels modern in the ways the Tales of franchise has traditionally struggled with; like, they finally figured out how to make a world map.  What's most important, the game plays very well.  The story isn't half as terrible as it sounded when actually playing it.  Berseria made the Tales of Series one of my favorite franchises.  Arise has made it my favorite.  Take that for what you will.  The game's so much fun to play.
