_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a solid story and characters that will drag you in and hit you in the emotions then give this game a pass. If you are looking for a generic fighting game with a tales paint job then this is the game for you. The combat and the graphics is the only thing I can recommend about this gameThe story and characters are just meh at best. Felt like a chore just to slog through the game. I love Berseria and Vesperia and I even like Zestria better than Arise. Before Arise I thought Zestria was the worst Tales game I had ever played and then I played Arise. Even as much as I disliked Zestria I actually genuinely enjoyed the story and the characters (other than Mikleo of course). Arise I just couldn't find anything about the characters to like. Arise story telling is just bland as could be. There are no moments that hit you in the emotions like other Tales games. There is no Yuri having to fight against Estelle to save her moments or the betrayal and then redemption of Raven or Karol who before than had sort of been afraid defending the party alone when they were unable to defend themselves, from Tales of Vesperia. Or having to kill Eizen to free him of being a dragon, or uncovering Heldalf's backstory, or those bandit kids dying or old man Mayvin, from Zestria. Berseria had so many emotional times to list them all but Magilou actually grew on me from her back story. She was annoying but her back story redeemed her and she became one of my favorites on follow up play throughs. Vesperia Zestria and Berseria all had many many emotional and well written parts of their story lines. Much more than I could list here. Arise has none of those things and the few times they tried to throw in a twist or add emotion it just fell flat. The personalities of the characters themselves is a part of the problem. Alphen is the most bland protag in a Tales game I have ever seen. Has as much personality as a brick. While Shionne has every annoying tsundere trait you can imagine. The rest of the party is slightly better but consist of just one trait and calling it a personality. Before anyone says that the side quests help develop them I 100% the game including side quests. The side quests help but not that much. Ignore my hours I tend to go offline mode when I play games so Steam seldom tracks my hours played in games.

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on 26 hours of the game. I would say that I am about 2/3 of the way through.Visuals - 9/10A beautiful game with vibrant colours, vastly contrasting environments and unique art style. The monsters and main characters are uniquely shaped and stand out. If only the texture pop-in wasn't so obvious and distracting, the score would have been 10/10.Gameplay - fun enough/10Not much to say here. Enjoy the mob battles, but the boss battles are a kiting affair. Not much strategy goes into that. Also, it is quite hard to react to enemy moves if there is an uninterruptible input queue and you are not warned of incoming attacks from behind you.Story/writing - Ubisoft/10I went into this hoping for an intelligent and thought provoking story with deeply thought out and rational characters. Unfortunately, I did not get that. For some reason the writers keep trying to go for a melodramatic tone even though the themes (slavery, companionship, racism etc.) established in this game are complex. In instead of a mature and sombre tone, emotional moments are ruined by intensely exaggerated melodrama. You can expect a MSEL (Melodramatic Scream or Evil Laughter) rate of 1 per chapter. Instead of letting a character sorrowfully mourn their loss quietly, the writers decide a prolonged scream of "NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO" is more appropriate. It is so poorly done that I just laugh through those cut scenes, and I'm the type of guy who sheds a tear in Disney movies. Make these moments shorter, sombre, and less monologic. Poor antagonists have to sit through 5 minutes of self-reflection by the protagonists before coming to the true conflict. My second major gripe is the writers treating the audience as idiots. If I was a simpleton, I wouldn't be playing Tales, I would be playing Fortnite. But instead of letting the players make deductions on their own, the writers spell everything out for you. You will literally find a note on a bookshelf full of music literature that explains: "The types of books tells you a bit about the character of the owner of the room". Gee, thanks, I don't think I could have worked that one out by myself.The other thing that grinds my gears is poor character writing and inconsistent behaviour. Just before one of the boss battles, a party member protects the antagonist from a companion's attack because that companion is filled with hate and seeking vengeance from the boss. The party member's first explanation of this inexplicable act is "I don't know why I did it, but your angry face is wrong". Give me a break. These bunch of cretins have been murdering their way through the five realms and one attack in hate elicits a lecture on the ethics of vengeance? A classic case of rationality discarded for dramatic effect. A similar conflict could have been built up by having the hateful party member's emotional actions putting a fellow companion in danger but no, jumping in front of a fireball is always the correct course of action.Overall: 8/10Please add more depth and rationality to story and characters. Otherwise, a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, after completing the game I can wholeheartedly recommend it. I really dont like the business decisions Bandai made here and I understand that people are really angry about it. I have bought the most expensive Edition so I almost had everything included. I actually kinda forgot that I had some exclusive multipliers activated because of my edition and what I would be telling yall is that you "cheat" in this game and activate all the artifact bonus multipliers that you get with the expensive version (I also played on hard, so it really felt natural with all of them active). Other than that I love the soundtrack aswell as the characters. The developement is really good and the story unfolds really nicely with some good plot points. I can also say that the game looks really good, but the pop-ins are really weird and I dont really understand why it is there. The game also ran on my system really really well and I couldnt complain at all. I sank in almost 60 hours for a good amount of side quests plus main story, though I did not collect everything and also didnt grind anywhere. _childDocuments_.review: It's been fun so far. I wouldn't say it's a "great" game, but it's not bad, especially if you haven't previously played Tales of Symphonia.  The voice acting is very weird at times, there are typos and various English localization errors you really wouldn't expect for a title from this otherwise amazing franchise.  Characters act very familiar with each other in certain cutscenes, then the next, they are back to barely knowing each other.  It's very disjointed. Combat is much less button-mashy, and more strategic than Tales games past, but the story so far is just kind of meh, and hard to get invested in. The underlying setting so far is ripped straight out of Symphonia with almost no changes, and very rushed. I would not be surprised if the talent behind the previous Tales games was not involved with this one. Character art style notwithstanding, it really doesn't feel like a Tales game, more like an imitation, like some kind of rushed fan-fiction of Symphonia.  While it's easy to criticize and complain, ultimately this game has a little more good than bad for me so far, so I do recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Best up to date Tales game I've ever play, and probably the best JRPG so far.Everything is pretty much an upgrade from previous Tales games, the graphics, the combat, UI, and Skits.Story/main quest part its actually pretty forgiving, as you can beat the game even though you're underleveled. For general exploring playing on Moderate difficulty+ is not bad but for some bosses its pretty brutal.Love the story(probably my favorite Tales ending), the music, the graphics, and most importantly the characters development.I will give this game a solid 9.5/10, I love everything in this game, except the end game+post game enemies variety (final story area and post game dungeons), just too much reused enemies to fight when making your way to the boss(except for that 1 Giant Zeugal Boss).

You also wont get enough gold to buy consumables and craft stuff unless you grindThe spells effects and animation were cool but it's pretty much impossible to tell where your character in control is or see the bosses' attacks when your other 3 team members are also spamming the spellsStory wise, early to mid game were so repetitive. You go to a new country and then you liberate the ppl. The plots are kinda predictable. Alphen was okay but Shionne is just not likable at allIf you like the game and are intrigued by the story, i would say just play on easy difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that this was a rather exemplary addition to the Tales franchise. I'm extremely thankful that they aren't suffering from the whiney crybaby protagonist disease that ruined Star Ocean for me since Last Hope.I clearly enjoyed it considering I spent over 100 hours attaining 100% completion.I think most of the negatives being said about the game are from people that are unfamiliar with some key differences between RPG and JRPG that pertain to more than simply the country of origin.I think the biggest critic skewing towards the negative for me is just me being nitpicky. Said critic would be that there is little real variety with enemies. For the most part there is just a handful of enemy types you encounter throughout the game with the only difference to them being that they are different colors and levels in different regions with their elemental affinity changed to that of their color/region. It would also be nice if the DLC equated to something more than just getting three different color versions of a few costumes for each character, especially when said DLC costs as much as an actual expansion on other games.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you somewhat of a completionist? Do you like finishing games you started? Do you like a good pacing? Then this game is not for you. I started this game and thus I finished it while finishing as many sidequests as possible (and what my patience allowed me at the point).Things I like about the game is the graphics, visuals and environment. The battle system is a somewhat nice upgrade from previous Tales-games as well.However, the dislikes heavily outweigh the likes. In regards to story and lore there are three ways in which it is delivered to the player: event scenes, on-map dialogue, skits/optional dialogues. A fourth would be to examine points of interests.I enjoy a good story and a good lore, but it shouldn't take over the gameplay and affect the pacing of the game - which it does in Tales of Arise. In the first 30-40% or so of the game it was a little bit too much, but still manageable. The last parts of the game however is a massive lore dump - especially in the few last dungeons where you would see a 5 min cutscene, and right after that there's some on-map dialogue but there's also 2-3 skits/optional dialogues for you to watch. I lost count on how many times this happened but probably close to 10 times exactly in this sequence. Guess what? After you finish your optional dialogues and take a few steps a new cutscene begins and the process repeats itself. 10 times. At this point I literally searched the internet to see if anybody else shared the same opinion that they talk too much in this game and yes, quite a lot of others felt the same.This drawn out lore dump contributes to, in my opinion, the following:TLDR; The graphics are nice, the battle system is nice compared to previous tales games - but they talk too much and affect the pacing of the game. I lost interest in the game but wanted to finish what I had started and rushed the end (no skipping scenes though).Worth noting: The Trails series is a series known for being lore heavy as well and I played through all of them up until Cold Steel IV, and enjoyed it. Lore heavy games are normally not an issue for me but Tales of Arise had a horrible delivery of its lore, unfortunately.

The game did great at some certain aspects as you can see from my score but failed to deliver good role playing experience. it’s filled with bad executed anime tropes&cliches combined with repetitive bad dialogues unlike other JRPG, characters spouting nonsenses and lastly, the plot holes that keep breaking my immersion. But! do not hesitate buying it If you don't care about what good JRPG is or Immersion, if you're fine with immature anime-ish rpg, if you want to buy it solely because of combat or its' attractive art&design, that's fine, it's worth your money, but for me this is not a good jrpg of my taste because of some certain aspects that i couldn't let it pass. BTW Rinwell’s cuteness 10/10 Hello, community’s choice of best RPG award, people keeps saying u are well polished, i think they are blinded by all of ur beautiful graphic, so i’m here to prove that they are wrong about you being a “polished game”.-First, the game suffers from pacing issue, a fast pacing one, to the point that there is only little to no development outside the main casts. Death and lost aren't impactful because player barely spend time knowing that character, everything goes pretty fast and it made every emotional scenes pretty dull.-Introduction to each lords is not impactful, the game feels rush, in each region, you just couldn’t spend enough time in each city to feel attract to people there, words and story telling and how&when you meet each lord is not good enough to leave the impact. You walk into a city and pass through it like a wind. Past Tales of games are better at introducing villains&minor characters. Cities also are just there as a bare hollow vessel for events to occur, they barely leave any impacts or impressions behind.    To make it fair, let's just compare Artorius from berseria to every Lords in Arise, Artorius indeed a winner for doing better job as a villain, those very first Lords in Arise are even forgettable because we barely know anything about them, all we know is, they killed peopleee! bland and flat.-Characters development sucks because the story feels so rush in each chapter,Fine if you like something short and compact but this doesn’t grow on me. Another problem lies on the Skits itself, Skits, a bunch of short interactions between characters, when some of it get triggered at some point of the story, sometimes it didn't make any sense to the story or situation. Cause an inconsistency in character development. And they repeat themselves.-For the story&setting is kinda meh to me but i still give it 7    The game uses the common formula of an amnesia protagonist goes fight villians to save the world with his no life friends, i still missing games where your friends have their own life to take care and their own path to part away from you, then happen to meet and fight along again, but my experience with tales of series never be like that(ves, zes, ber and arise) your friends are always a bunch of no life following you around. But do i hate it?     No, Ys games that i love is kinda like that too but what make Ys is more interesting is Ys’ characters still have a bit of their own moment that may part away from you for a while and their own goals are more distinct from the main character. Apart from that, all minor characters are memorable, have good development and important role unlike Tales of series. In Ys most of the time the character you happen to like, might not be the one in your fighting party members, because of how well developed the supporting characters are.    My experience in Ys is the only reason of why i don’t give Arise the low score. Despite my expectation, the story is very anime-ish, it goes fast like how you watch anime, you are not supposed to take your time taking bunch of details in a scene, and you get nothing worthwhile for doing that. Like the game telling you “just go to the next scene already, so you will get another cinematic movie that will keep your dopamine level high!” all the time, and i considered that the game respect your time, your general consumer’s time(which is not me lol) that’s why i give it 7 out of 10, it’s not a bad thing just need some adjustment and rewriting to eliminate the plot holes(which i will soon talk about).-Excuse me for just one small nitpicking but the game has only one stop running animation. Not the dynamic one like other modern games, in this game, your characters' hands can teleport.-Plot holes or things that make no sense to meMost interactions are fun, but some few moments ruined the game(like :(spoiler: Mahag Saar region) (And :(spoiler: Ganath Haros region) (Minor spoiler about map layout of first region)Click to see the summary pic that i made first->  -(Spoiler, Menancia) Game tries to tell story, create a world through dialogues and environment but failed to make it a believable one. _childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game. Fun to play, beautiful graphics. The world is decently large and beautiful, making for a fun experience as you trek through your journey.But unfortunately, it feels like all these high production values are wasted on average writing. There were lots of moments that were supposed to be emotional, but they just weren't executed well. Not enough build-up, no context. Lots of scenes came out awkward rather than touching. As usual, the English voice acting is a disaster, so I ended up having to switch back to Japanese like I almost always do on JRPGs.The final boss was great in one way and horrible in another - again, beautiful graphics and F/X, totally awesome for a final battle. But the story and writing are just... ugh. Tons of plot holes everywhere, stuff that just doesn't make sense but added in for cinematic effect. By the end of the game just have so many questions, and not thought-provoking ones, but more bewildered and accusatory ("what the hell was the point of X, Y plot point?") and things like that.In addition, the side quests in this game were lacking. The huge majority of them were just fighting more monsters. For at least the first half of the game you are severely lacking in money and are either forced to grind ridiculous hours or purchase DLC money.Story and writing feel like a downgrade from Berseria, whose characters were written well, story was cohesive from start to finish, and although it also had plot holes, not nearly as big or as many. The game left me satisfied - this one... eh, lukewarm.Play it for the fun hack 'n slash like combat and beautiful graphics, not an amazing story with amazing writing. About the only things that were written well were relationships between specific pairs of people.

_childDocuments_.review: : Tales of Arise is a gorgeous game on the surface, but its beauty only goes skin deep.  The story is artificially long and padded with repeated content, and it suffers from severe pacing issues at the most important points in its plot.  : The visuals are gorgeous, the voice acting is pretty good for both English and Japanese and the level and world design is amazingly gorgeous.  Combat gets a bit slower than other Tales games, but it allows the player to use all of their party mechanics like mystic artes and combo finishers regularly, which works with how gorgeous the battle system is.  And party management between battles has been boiled down to just managing CP, which is only used for healing and buffs.  All other offensive abilities and spells are now free to use.  I have mixed feelings on this, but it works to streamline combat.So why am I giving this a thumbs down?  The story, the most important part of a JRPG, is pure frustration for me.  It's bad enough to frequently make me angry at it and good enough to make me care enough to be angry at it.  It suffers from extremely severe pacing issues, with interesting scenes suddenly being interrupted so a character can stand on their soapbox and preach to draw the scene out for another 10 minutes.  This ruins the mood so badly that it makes me not want to play Tales of Arise again whenever it happens, and it happens almost every time I start cautiously enjoying the story again.And you won't just hear that pace destroying soapbox when you were about to confront a boss who just killed a bunch of people once.  Oooooooh no.  You're going to hear about how all renans aren't evil sooooooo many freaking times in this story (as one generic, non-spoiler example among many repeated offenses).  They pad the length of the story by constantly rehashing old lines, which also ruins character development when they keep bringing up old problems to resolve again.I've given the story in this game several tries.  I've walked away from it to cooldown each time and come back to it a month or two later.  It's just an exercise in self torture at this point, as it utterly frustrates me to no end every time something cool happens only to have someone step up and start spewing their soap all over the place for 10 minutes and making me keep hitting skip scene because I just don't care anymore.  I don't care anymore.  And that's why I'm giving this a thumbs down and probably not going to torture myself with it further.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the top RPGs to make it out of 2021. A great entry point for those who never played the Tales series before, Tales of Arise is a self contained story line. One of the best thing about Tales of Arise is the combat for sure, with being able to string together different moves you learn throughout the game as your own combo and the team system works great to adding more dynamic feeling to each battle. Mystic arts also add some great visual eye candy.The cast is also very good, although each cast member retain popular anime tropes. This didn't bother me too much as they each have enough in their personality to be their own character and lovable in every right. The banters and conversations between every party member brings them to life, and you'll see each character develop not only as a party but also as individuals as they each deal with their own bias and demons. Tales of Arise also did what a lot of anime tend to avoid and actually having an adult cast which I absolutely love. Well, 4/6 including the dual protagonists are adults, where 2 party members are teenagers. Works beautifully, I wish more anime/ anime games feature adult casts instead of keeping them as teenagers.The story is nothing really to write home about. It is pretty standard in terms of Anime/ Anime games story lines but it stays engaging enough to keep you invested through most of the game. The pacing is great up until towards the end of the game, where you'll be bombarded with cutscenes after cutscenes after skits after cinematic cutscenes. It become very overbearing with an insane amount of exposition that I wish was handled better because that stretch of the game just felt tedious to go through, even if I enjoyed the cast. Probably the biggest criticism I can offer the game.The RPG mechanics shine mostly through the Arte system. If you have play a Tales game before, you'll be familiar with the system but basically the more you use a certain skill, the stronger it becomes and it can even unlock another skill for you if you use it enough. The skill tree/ set system is your standard number buff you expect to see in a lot of RPG games, nothing to exciting with the exception of the ones that let you unlock a new skill. You will be unlocking a lot of skill sets/ titles throughout the game so there is never any shortage of upgrades. Weapons and armors are your standard number buff, where you will find a small upgrade to your previous weapon and armor as you progress throughout your game. Armors offer no visual changes but weapons do. However, there is a fair amount of costumes/ alternatives in the game you can unlock via collecting owls or quests. There is also the paid-DLC costumes that you can buy. Speaking of DLC, Tales of Arise unfortunately suffers what many Japanese RPG games tend to do and that is selling you overpriced DLCs/ costumes. (Some of which contains unique skills)Visually the game is a treat. While still retaining the anime art style you'll see in a lot of anime style games, the visual effects on abilities are a whole another level, with particles flying everywhere and color bursting every possible second. Overall, I highly recommend Tales of Arise to anyone who wants to jump into the Tales series or is just looking for a good action RPG. With the great combat, lovable casts, and just overall a great experience, it easily landed as one of my favorite single games that released in 2021.

detailed_description: Saints Row EXPANSION EPISODES COSMETIC PACKS FREE COSMETIC PACKS About the Game As the future Boss, with Neenah, Kevin, and Eli by your side, you’ll form The Saints – and take on Los Panteros, The Idols, and Marshall as you build your empire across the streets of Santo Ileso and battle for control of the city. Ultimately Saints Row is the story of a start-up company, it’s just that the business The Saints are in happens to be crime. Experience the biggest and best Saints Row playground ever created; the unique sprawling world of Santo Ileso is the backdrop for a wild, larger than life sandbox of thrilling side hustles, criminal ventures and blockbuster missions, as you shoot, drive, and wingsuit your way to the top. FEATURES ● Witness the Birth of The Saints – Play through an action blockbuster original story full of criminality, extraordinary scenes and signature surprises laced with humor. ● Discover the Weird, Wild, West – Dive in to Santo Ileso, the biggest and best Saints Row playground ever, spread across nine unique districts surrounded by the vast, majestic beauty of the Southwest Desert. ● Build Your Criminal Empire – Take over the city block by block, wage war against enemy factions and tighten your grip on the streets with ingenious criminal ventures. ● Fire Guns. LOTS of Guns – Shoot revolvers from the hip, fire and forget with a rocket launcher, or obliterate up close using melee heavyweights, complete with brutal takedowns. A vast variety of familiar and exotic weapons, all customizable, and all deadly fun. ● Take to the Streets and the Skies – Blast through urban and desert environments in any one of the cars, bikes, planes, helicopters, VTOLs, hoverbikes, hoverboards, go-karts or equip your wingsuit to swoop around. ● Unprecedented Customization – Create the Boss of your dreams, with the most extensive character customization suite ever seen in the series, then complete the look with incredible options for weapons and vehicles. ● Seamless Co-Op – Experience everything on offer with a friend at any time, via fully untethered drop-in / drop out co-op, skipping the need to take either of you out of the outlandish action. Play nice together, or play all new pranks on your team mate. After all, who’s the Boss now. ● New Districts – Santo Ileso now includes 2 additional districts featuring a host of activities and diversions for you to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's a fan of Saints Row and has played every Saints Row game, including this one.....this is disappointing. Weakest game in the series, and it brought an unfortunate end to the studio that made the entire series.I am ashamed to admit that, back when the game had gotten announced, I got a little hyped for this game and actually pre-ordered the Platinum Edition on PS5 about almost two years ago (in retrospect, Saints Row: The Third Remastered, which was bundled in, was more fun than this), and experienced the glitchy madness on the day it released, all the way until I actually beat the game. While many of the glitches were eventually patched out, my disappointment still remained, and the game was still not on the same level as the other Saints Row games.Playing through the game, plus DLC, again on Steam (because I have no idea what I'm doing with my life), I've realized that, even when many of the problems I experienced had been fixed, it still wasn't fun. The notoriety system doesn't feel the same; while in the other Saints Row games, if I attack an enemy gang member or police, enemies will continue to spawn and pursue me until I either evade them or call to wipe notoriety. But in this game, as long as I prevent any enemy from calling for backup and take them out, no more enemies spawn, and the notoriety clears without anyone trying to chase me. Notoriety also goes away if I kill a miniboss of either the police or the gangs, who don't show up until max notoriety, which is easier said than done, due to the way it works in this game.Speaking of gangs, the gangs you face are either bad at fighting or absolutely annoying. The Idols aren't too bad, but some of them have glow sticks that deflect bullets. Los Panteros are pathetic, as they're either melee focused or accidentally dropping molotovs near themselves or their allies. And Marshall irritates me the most out of the three enemy gangs, as they drop proximity mines when they die, one of their specialists have these devices that can RESTRICT YOUR MOVEMENTS, and their miniboss takes longer to die than the Idols' and Panteros' minibosses, requiring you to wait until their weak spots are exposed for you to do damage to him.While the perks are a neat concept on paper, it's kinda dumb that they made the dual wielding as one of the perks that you unlock from doing challenges, which require you doing a set of tasks that are either simple, or almost impossible, and even then, you have to PAY IN-GAME CURRENCY for perk slots: two for minor perks, two for major perks, and one for elite perks. There's also collectibles, which aren't really motivating to collect, unlike in Saints Row IV, and side hustles, which, aside from the @tcha ones, aren't really exciting for me to do.What really bothers me is the criminal venture thing. So after a certain point in the story, you unlock the ability to buy different businesses by putting them on whatever spot on the map you want. Each one has their own unique set of stuff to do, like the classic Fraud and Mayhem, there's also new activities to do, like delivering a truck full of toxic waste and stealing food trucks. Why am I complaining about this? Well, why do I need to pay SO MUCH MONEY just to do Mayhem? In the other games, you didn't need to buy a random business to do them; you just go to the activity node, start it, and off you went.And in my honest opinion, the story itself isn't the worst thing I've gone through compared to some of the other games I've played with even worse story, but it's probably the weakest in the entire Saints Row series. If you mainly focus on the main story and a little bit of businesses, it's possible to beat the game in about a day or two, especially if you use the MDI-101 Multi Launcher, which you can get as early as being able to access the open world at the beginning of the game if you've made and linked a Saints Row account. (Getting an OP weapon just for linking an account is crazy.)The majority of vehicles you can drive aren't as crazy as Saints Row: The Third (I think the Marshall VTOL is similar to the STAG VTOL) and Saints Row IV. In fact, there's not a lot of the fun vehicles to drive around, and that was what had set Saints Row apart from other open world games. (Granted, OG Saints Row and Saints Row 2 didn't have goofy vehicles either as far as I can tell, but still.)So overall, this game both sucks and is boring. If you must play a Saints Row game, I'd recommend you get anything OTHER than this one, preferably the third or fourth game. If, for whatever reason, you really wish to see how bad this game is for yourself, I'd say get it on sale. Otherwise, it's best that you don't touch this particular game AT ALL.

_childDocuments_.review: Well hey there Saints Row (2022). Are you a quirky and interesting reboot of a franchise that just got crazier and more fun over time? No, you aren't? What are you? Oh, you're a modern sandbox collectathon with a thousand markers on a map to trick people into thinking they're accomplishing something while having a basically skill-less primary gameplay loop with no mechanics or challenge to speak of?Oh, that's too bad.Saints Row (2022) is a modern sandbox shooter. That means the gunplay is weak, you require zero mechanical skill to accomplish anything, there are a seemingly infinite number of identical side missions to complete, and the story and characterization suck. It does absolutely nothing better than its predecessors or any of its competitors in the market.But hey, the art team did a good job.The primary issue above all others is story. This is a reboot of the Saints Row franchise, a beginning, a place to establish characters and motivations. But there are no characters. Oh, sure, there are NPCs wandering around, but they all have precisely one attribute that is the entirety of their personality and every single interaction and piece of banter is anchored on that. They are  bland, they aren't funny - ever - and I don't care what happens to the player character or them.There is also no antagonist. You go through most of the game with really nothing standing in your way, the three other gang factions barely making an impact on your consciousness as you plow through legions of meaningless enemies. Then, maybe an hour or two from the end of the game, a character is introduced in a way that's actually decent: as a foil to the bland NPC madness of the player and friends enters the story, and some moments of fun are had with someone playing the straightman to all the crazies.Then that character goes insane, betrays you, and traps your friends on a sitcom stage making them pretend to be his friends. What? This is the final boss, the ultimate antagonist? A character we just met and interacted with that changes characterization completely after one mission?Yes.The sad part is that two pieces of DLC for this game show that the ability to tell a fun story in this world exists. There is a heist DLC that has plenty of fun character moments, and there's a LARP DLC that really leans into how ridiculous the setting of Saints Row can be, with the entire city participating in a live action roleplaying game. Too bad the main game had none of this character.Gameplay-wise there's nothing to say. You've seen everything here before. It's just shoot guy with gun, no thought required, no overcoming of a challenge desired. There is no game design on display at all. Saints Row is literally a carbon-copy of every sandbox in the last 10 years. There are also a number of bugs that have gone unpatched for several years, but that's understandable given that the studio responsible for this edifice folded. The UI just sucks, full stop. Doing every piece of menuing through a smartphone that you have to bring up on the side of the screen and navigate through is terrible. There are long loads for each selection you make and no way to track things like the challenges you have to complete to unlock the game's metaprogression, Perks. Perks are complete failure as well, as it's not just possible but a virtual certainty that you will finish the game before you have even 3 of a possible 5 unlocked, and certainly not an "ultimate" perk.And I hope you're ready to turn off the radio every single time you enter every single vehicle in the game, because you cannot default it to off and it blares over all in-game audio.All told, Saints Row 2022 is as bland a piece of modern game design as I've ever seen. It iterates in no way on gameplay, game design, or writing, either within its own franchise or the medium as a whole. There is literally no reason to play it unless you're looking to burn hours of your life away in a mindless haze.What a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Review at 100 percent of the map (most dlc is untouched)My experience going into this is with Saints Row 3, Saints Row 4 and Gat Out of Hell, and also that weird hero shooter thing that I think is a spinoff which I didn't like much. I have Saints Row 2 but in my experience it's a pain to get running. I also didn't play this one until well after all the patches and fixing.I thought this game was actually pretty good and at least belongs in the pantheon of those games. With Saints Row 3 being the best of those (I liked Saints Row 4 but it really minimizes the normal open world crime elements while jumping several sharks) I would actually rank it pretty close behind. The game is based in kind of a vague Sonoran Desert, having location analogues with Southern California, Nevada, Arizona and Mexico. They work on building a culture with a patron saint that feels like it's taking elements of real life people like El Santo and Frank Lloyd Wright. They directly address how some of the location had changed over time and its relationship to its gangs and aspects like street art. There are two Spanish radio stations, and the only country station is exclusively outlaw country. They imply Red Faction happened there but I haven't played that game so I don't know if there is a connection outside of a couple wink and nod moments. I think the setting has a vibe and is genuinely very memorable and is the standout success of this game.The story is very cute. It's very character centric and, world context aside, I think the characters are better than they were in the other games. All of your crew have at least one memorable moment, a notable function in your team, and a past that gets elaborated through sub missions. If it wants you to feel an emotion for them, it feels earned, and their dialogue isn't just a mishmash of references or trying to be funny with zero brakes. It is still a "silly gta game" but it's not as insistent as the others I played, which was something that could get irritating about them. Also, there's not too many cutscenes but I like them, the subtle character actions and how they fold out I think was interesting. There is a scene in particular where they're trying to disinfect a gunshot wound and during dialogue Kev moves to the fridge, gets out vodka, pours some on the wound and takes a swig before placing it down. I don't know how to explain but I don't think you often get that amount of relatively subtle detail in cutscenes.The gameplay, is all around fine and functions how you'd expect. Instead of grenades you get little powers that work off of a bar, and they mostly completely destroy any challenge in the combat. I don't like the way they're triggered on keyboard at all. The gunplay is probably what you'd expect from this series, being largely competent and fairly fast paced and fun. Some of the targeting decisions are a bit silly. I turned off auto aim but there was still a soft lock that would make me focus in on an enemy if I zoomed. The vehicles control fun and there is kind of an interesting Burnout style takedown system with vehicles, that you heavily rely on in missions. I think it meshes well with the series and made driving around a bit more interesting. That being said there are a handful of missions that require you to anchor a physics object to your car and it heavily influences your steering, it could glitch out and launch up, taking your car with it. There is another issue I have with cars in the mission design.Customization is overall, very nice. You have a lot of layer and colouring options, and there are tons of stores in the city. You can change your look at any time, and have access to a huge internet database of looks. I chose the prim British voice for my boss and it actually changed dialogue in scenes to account for it, as if the world then assumes you are from overseas. The weapon and vehicle customization is very fun and you can make every weapon and vehicle basically completely end game viable (as much as the latter is worth)Next is the mission structure. Overall most missions you'd expect for a Saints Row game are here. They're attached to expanding your empire so you don't have a lot right off the bat. They don't have grades and it doesn't ping you for missing sub-objectives, which I think is an okay change and made 100 percenting the game tolerable. Every sub mission has a couple lines of unique dialogue leading up to it, often with an npc specifically tied to that sub mission which I think was a choice that made them less dull to play. The single worst thing about the game is the fact almost no vehicle mission lets you bring your own vehicle. There are no races either, so upgrading your vehicle is almost completely useless outside of exploring the open world. This is a completely baffling decision and majorly bummed me out. Also, the actual "lore" of los santos, as interesting as I think it is, is contained almost entirely within a literal national park exhibit recording. It's better than nothing, which is all I remember getting from previous entries, but I feel like a handful of missions could have handled this in minor dialogue.Also, I think this game looks pleasant, I don't think they were trying to compete in the AAA space or anything, and I'd rather a game that scales well to all kinds of systems than one that barely functions on a 4080tiThe last main game related thing that's probably a reason for a lot of the pre-release hate is the tone. The main characters are millennial and they appeared to sanitize the game a bit which made people get irrationally mad. The characters don't rely too much on the stereotype of being a millenial, and I think their dialogue was largely solid. There are a couple millenialisms in their way of speaking (ex. "Don't yuck my yum") but it's generally played off as being a joke and it isn't a crutch in the writing, which is strong. Jim Robs doesn't bother me and there is actually an in lore explanation of that and it's a better joke anyways. Most of the horny content still exists in game, including Leather and Lace. You can even decensor breasts without mods which technically puts it past the spicy meter in previous entries (the nipples are hilariously bad but it's nice if you have a female frame boss and want a chest tattoo.) The only staple that I feel is missing is the dildo melee weapon. I never found one and feel it no longer exists. Sliders may be a bit nerfed but I remember having trouble making a body type I wanted in 3 and 4 as well. None of this bothers me deeply and I don't play Saints Row to jack off, but I thought it was worth mentioning. The DLC I dipped into was the Doc Ketcham one, and I'm just going to say I find the premise interesting, and I enjoyed my first playthrough of it. I don't know how I'd feel if I got it as part of a season pass or anything, but I at least enjoyed my one playthrough, and it also elaborated on the setting quite a bit. I think I'm in the outlier for that one and that's fine.I feel a bit bad getting this game late now that the studio has been shut down, but I genuinely didn't know if it would run on my system and I'd been having financial issues aside. I think the last few flops and state of release of the game also contributed to its demise, as well as that epic exclusivity thing games like to shoot themselves in the foot with.Overall, I liked this game! I would get it on sale with the season pass. I think it's worth a try if you like saints row 3 and 4 and aren't upset about changes or reboots.

_childDocuments_.review: I paid around $10 for the game and that's all I'd recommend paying for it. It's fine, there's a "decent" game here - somewhere. It is buggy as hell, and I mean buggy everywhere. Enemies and cars will bug out, the audio will sound like some cyberpunk hell sometimes. In fact, the only times I died while playing this game were because of bugs in the game. Which leads me to my next point - it's too easy. Playing the game on max difficulty provided no challenge. I was able to breeze through the game in 12 hours. The story isn't very long. I wish there was more substance to it. In the older games you'd play 10ish missions for each enemy gang before finishing them off. In this game though, it seems like the whole story is 10 missions. There is some side stuff the game wants you to do. Like starting side businesses and stuff like that but there isn't really a need to do any of it. You have no real incentive to make money because all the guns can be purchased cheaply and don't really need to be upgraded to finish the story. Additionally the clothes and overall customization is lacking as well, wish there was more. What i will say is I really enjoy the style of the game. The art style is nice and it looks good. It doesn't try to be a photo realistic city or characters and what they went with actually looks nice. The few customization opens they did have were nice. I was able to deck my character out with what they had available and I enjoyed how he looked. It makes me wish the game was longer so I could see it through longer.  Essentially the TLDR of it all is this: It's a fine game if you can get it on sale. It's a buggy mess and leaves a lot to be desired. However if you can pick it up for a good price it isn't a bad waste of 15 hours or so.

_childDocuments_.review: The pros:I don’t care that the game’s art style has changed to appeal to modern gamers. That is an expected change so it’s a nonissue for me. The voice acting, sound effects, and soundtrack are fine, they seem to be on par with what is common to the franchise. If you like the gameplay of the other installments of the franchise, then you will feel right at home here and will appreciate the gameplay improvements. The accessibility options are great and will help anyone in need of the assistance. The new business venture missions are a nice change to the business purchasing feature of the previous games.With over a year of patches the launch issues that existed at release seem to be fixed since I only experienced one minor bug that was easily fixed. The cons:The new uninspired saints consist of a dude bro with a bad tattoo, a gang banging Urkel, a female Dominic Toretto from the fast and furious franchise along with their leader your created character that is a wise cracking gun toting butt kicker. The new characters are not bad they just don’t possess the charisma, vibrant personalities, and likeability of the original saints from the previous games of the franchise. The story and dialog of the game are a mixed bag. There are plenty of good story elements and well written lines, but they are constantly being overshadowed by the bad story elements and poorly written lines. If you don’t go out of your way to do the side jobs and the business ventures this game is very short.The bitter truth:It annoys me to no end that the developers needlessly sanitized this reboot of the franchise of the irreverent and crass humor along with the sexual innuendos the franchise was well known and loved for. This idiotic decision by the developers will be a tolerable annoyance for some fans of the franchise like me. I understand that It was done to try to appeal to players that were turned off by those game elements, but in doing so they outraged their loyal fanbase and in the end this seems to have gained them nothing and lost them everything. Which is a real shame because there is more here to like than to dislike!The Verdict:If you are interested in buying the game wait for a sale or the price to go down the length of the game is not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Saints Row : By Triple FThe 2022 reboot of "Saints Row", developed by Volition, attempts to reimagine the popular open-world crime franchise with a fresh storyline, new characters, and a new setting in the fictional American Southwest city of Santo Ileso. Known for its mix of over-the-top action and humor, "Saints Row" has long embraced a “crime comedy” tone that stood out from more serious open-world games. In this reboot, Volition seeks to balance the series’ trademark zaniness with a more grounded narrative centered around a new cast of characters trying to climb their way to the top of the criminal world. The result is a game that tries to blend the wacky essence of "Saints Row" with a modernized approach, but it ultimately struggles to find its footing between the two.The setting of Santo Ileso is one of the game’s most well-executed features, capturing the ambiance of the American Southwest with an impressive level of detail. The city is expansive and varied, featuring different districts that range from bustling urban centers and scenic desert expanses to industrial zones and rundown neighborhoods. The environmental design adds depth to the world and feels lived-in, with each area exuding its own personality. Santo Ileso’s sunny desert landscapes and vibrant nightlife give the city a unique character and make exploring the environment an enjoyable experience. However, despite its aesthetic strengths, the city sometimes feels empty in terms of interactive content, and players may find that the open-world map lacks the density of activities seen in other contemporary sandbox games.The new cast of characters, led by The Boss and their friends Neenah, Eli, and Kevin, aims to bring a fresh dynamic to the series, but reactions to these characters have been mixed. Rather than hardened criminals, these characters are presented as misfit millennials who band together out of necessity, balancing between a desire for success and personal struggles. While this approach gives the story a new angle, the personalities of the characters sometimes feel inconsistent with the edgy tone that fans have come to expect from "Saints Row". The dialogue is filled with banter that aims for humor but doesn’t always land, occasionally veering into awkward or forced territory. Despite the mixed success of the writing, each character has a clear role in the gang, and players who enjoy a more grounded cast may appreciate the focus on friendship and loyalty.Combat and gameplay mechanics in "Saints Row" have been updated with a focus on action-heavy gunplay and driving sequences. The game offers a wide arsenal of customizable weapons, from standard pistols and shotguns to more creative tools like the Thrustbuster, which allows players to launch enemies into the air. The combat is responsive, with fast-paced shootouts that encourage players to move dynamically and experiment with different weapons. However, the gunplay can feel somewhat repetitive, as enemy encounters lack variation, and the AI doesn’t always provide a significant challenge. Additionally, some of the physics and combat mechanics feel loose, which can detract from the overall satisfaction of pulling off stunts and attacks. The driving mechanics, a staple of the series, are smooth and fun, allowing players to engage in high-speed chases or use vehicles as weapons with relative ease.The mission structure in "Saints Row" tries to balance story-driven missions with open-world chaos, but it occasionally suffers from pacing issues and repetitive objectives. Story missions follow the gang as they establish their empire, often combining shootouts, heist setups, and car chases. While there are moments of humor and spectacle, many of the missions follow a similar formula, which can feel repetitive over time. Side activities, a hallmark of the series, return in the form of “Criminal Ventures,” which allow players to launch businesses as fronts for illegal activities, from insurance fraud to chop shops. While these side activities are fun at first, they too can feel repetitive after multiple completions, which may impact long-term engagement.Customization options are one area where "Saints Row" truly shines, providing an extensive suite of choices for players to personalize their characters, vehicles, and weapons. The character creator is one of the most robust in the genre, with options that allow players to design everything from realistic figures to more humorous, exaggerated avatars. Vehicle customization is equally detailed, enabling players to modify everything from paint colors and decals to performance stats, which adds a personal touch to the gameplay. This focus on customization extends to the game’s gang, where players can choose colors, themes, and even the personality of the crew. This level of customization is a standout feature and may be a major draw for players who enjoy tailoring their experience to their own style.Visuals and performance are a bit inconsistent, with the game delivering bright, stylized graphics that suit the tone but occasionally suffering from technical issues. The art direction successfully captures the vibrant aesthetic of Santo Ileso, with colorful visuals that pop against the desert backdrop. However, the game is marred by occasional glitches, such as pop-in textures, frame drops, and some animation bugs that can disrupt immersion. While patches have improved performance since launch, these issues highlight a lack of polish that detracts from the experience. Still, when the game runs smoothly, the visuals are appealing and convey a playful tone that aligns with Saints Row’s established style.In closing, the "Saints Row" reboot delivers a modern take on the series that features an impressive setting, extensive customization, and action-packed gameplay, but it struggles to fully capture the charm and edge that defined previous entries. The attempt to shift toward a more relatable, character-driven story is an interesting direction, though it may not resonate with long-time fans expecting the outrageous, irreverent humor of earlier games. Santo Ileso’s design and the game’s customization depth are high points, adding layers of enjoyment, even if the core gameplay sometimes feels repetitive. Ultimately, "Saints Row" is an entertaining sandbox for players who enjoy open-world mayhem, but it stops short of reaching the iconic status of its predecessors, feeling more like a fresh start than a bold redefinition.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro'sGood character customizationLots of clothing optionsWeapon and vehicle modificationsCon'sExceptionally broken with countless unfixed bugsImpossible to play the game without running into serious bugsWeak gameplay featuresGunplay is just average at best, same with drivingUnstable and broken coopPoor controlsMinor IssuesOdd design choices especially with wingsuitLack of information given to the playerOne of the biggest disappointments of 2022 especially for SR fans, because this game is just a complete buggy mess which should have been significantly better than previous SR games in the series but for some reason just takes big steps backwards in every way possible instead of building on the success of SR3 and SR4 instead of Volition spending time to fix the game up, fix bugs they instead concentrated on DLC instead,  the very same bugs I encountered on the EPIC Store version of the SR22 which I own, I have also encountered here over a year later are still very much present and will never be fixed considering this game failed so badly, it ended the studio. Within the first 30 minutes of playing, I had the infamous HDR issue that required deleting the main primary cache bin file and then have steam repair the game, this can and will happen occasionally and make the textures, especially the sky look awful and glitch out.   This is just the start of the massive amount of bugs,  even simple things like your smartphone camera sometimes locks and requires a game restart to gain the functionality back so you can complete photo challenges,   unfortunately the bugs are so bad and prevaillant its near impossible not to run into them frequently, just now I had to restart the game because of using an ability which caused a stuttering bug which prevented me from attacking or doing anything, which is a common issue. So many bad design choices, alot of stuff even isn't explained very well like how to do barrel rolls to complete challenges for example,  some challenges are also exceptionally annoying such as "Hidden History" where you have to find small points of interest and its just very annoying, sometimes the POIs are easy to find and others hidden.   Gunplay is sluggish and not nearly as smooth and enjoyable as previous games, honestly its a huge step backwards from even SR3 which had some very good balance but SR22 just feels average at best.   Driving is pretty much the same way, its just average at best and feels like a downgrade from previous games in the series,  the cars drive sluggishly and sometimes not very responsive, drifting is fun at times and some pretty good stunts can be done once the you get used to the fiddly controls. Strange decision decisions, you can get hit by tons of bullets, run over etc - but you hit any object on a wingsuit and you insta die,  same with the train- you try to wingsuit onto the train and you'll instantly die.   Some of the same hustles from previous games make a return like playing in traffic, but feels a lot more rigid and frankly worse not better which is a shame,  couple that with a lot of information the game just doesn't really tell you. Character customization is decent and on par with previous games, you have a wealth of stuff you can unlock from clothing to interesting weapons along with typical perks and skills you can use against the various gangs as you steadily take over the city, perhaps SR22 only strong area unfortunately. Some missions are so broken that you can die literally though no fault of your own such as wingman takedowns which cause you to lose control of your character and charges you straight into walls at high speed which instantly kills you....and you basically have to restart the ENTIRE mission from scratch again. Overall, Saints Row 2022 is just a really good example of serious bugs crippling the game from the getgo, and Deep Silver forcing Volition to release way too early,  clearly needed a lot more time to fix the bugs and problems before they should have released and the developers paid the price for it,   I absolutely would not ever recommend this game unless you get it for free because it is 100% you will run into frequent issues,  that being said - the game sometimes has fun moments but unfortunately its a slog to get through when you are constantly having to check reddit pages for possible fixes to bugs you will encounter.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid gamer, I was excited to delve into the vibrant world of Saints Row (2023), set in the bustling city of Santo Ileso. However, my experience with the game left much to be desired.Let's start with the audio design, or lack thereof. I found the sound mastering to be abysmal. Guns fired with a whimper rather than a bang, resembling airsoft toys more than lethal weapons. While narration and cutscene audio were passable, explosions lacked the necessary punch, and even the footsteps of my player character were eerily silent. The only respite was the radio in cars, as the engines failed to make any audible impact.Technical issues plagued my gameplay from the start. The game crashed incessantly, with no discernible pattern to its madness. Even attempting to run it in Admin mode resulted in a broken installation, adding insult to injury. Shader compilation on startup was a tedious process, further delaying my already-frustrating attempts to play.But perhaps the most damning flaw lies in the gameplay itself. The combat mechanics felt clunky and unsatisfying, robbing the experience of any potential fun. With constant crashing hindering my progress, I found myself unable to even form a complete opinion of the game.In conclusion, Saints Row (2023) fails to deliver on its promises of an engaging open-world experience. Between its technical shortcomings and lackluster gameplay, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game, even at a discounted price.Overall Rating: 2/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially quite skeptical about this game for a significant period, and understandably so, given the plethora of bugs that plagued it during the early stages of its release. Additionally, as a former hardcore fan of the Saints Row series, I found myself somewhat disconcerted by the notion of it being a reboot. However, after finally giving it a chance and playing through it, I can confidently say that it's not as bad as many people make it out to be.While it may not stand up as strongly in comparison to its predecessors, the game still manages to deliver enjoyable moments and retains many of the elements that defined the essence of Saints Row. If there were a possibility for a company to revitalize Volition or for Volition itself to return as an indie development team and continue this franchise within its new rebooted universe, I would welcome it, provided that sufficient time and effort were dedicated to avoiding the pitfalls of its past.Overall, I must concede that it falls somewhat in the middle ground, but I do believe I could recommend this game, particularly if it were available at a discounted price and played alongside someone with an open mind.

_childDocuments_.review: It really sucks that corporate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ killed Volition off while they were still refining this game. It released in a poor state, makes some substantial departures from previous entries in the series, and doesn't tell its tale particularly evenly or well. Fan reaction to that was admittedly polarized, and very vocally negative.However, Santo Ileso is a joy to explore - absolutely packed with little labors of love, the character and car customization is top notch, and there are more than a few entertaining missions and activities to take part in. True, the new characters aren't developed enough, and the storyline should have started with them meeting up and becoming acquainted instead of already friends, but they're still interesting, have likable moments, and had real potential to develop had the game kept receiving support. There's fun to be had here, if you're willing to look past some flaws.It's still far from perfect, no denying, but with the majority of bugs having been addressed, you really could do far worse. Nostalgia glasses aside, in my opinion it makes for a far better first entry into an ongoing series than SR1 did. It's just a pity we'll never see more.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite all the hate for this game, I decided to give it a try and I ended up really liking it. I was a huge fan of the old games and they are probably my earliest Steam reviews, so I was hesitant to play the reboot as it could so easily go wrong. I'm glad I ended up trying it, it feels like a 360-era game or right after it in a lot of ways. Perhaps it's the nostalgia for that generation of games as open worlds have moved onto being too dense, but this world with fun side missions was perfect to hop back into. The desert setting was a great choice as it leads to some themeing. The world is also visually pretty interesting and their are fun hidden details throughout. I can't rightly tell you it's the best game ever or it's going to hold up, but it is a fun ride for 20-hours and that is all I wanted. It's a true powertrip in that you become way too deadly way too fast, but it at least makes for some interesting gameplay without a need to focus on realistic. I would hope they would be able to follow up on this and build on the ground work they put down, but it sounds like the studio is dead, so this is going to be the final Saints Row game. It at least is a good point to leave off on and it does work as a self contained follow-up.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ (3/5)After 38 hours in Saints Row, I can say that the reboot brings a mix of chaotic fun and some missed opportunities. While it captures the spirit of the series, it feels like it doesn’t fully embrace what made the franchise great. Here’s what I think:The gameplay is filled with over-the-top action, allowing for wild antics and mayhem. I enjoy the extensive character and vehicle customization options, which add a personal touch to my experience. However, many missions feel repetitive and a bit too familiar, lacking the creativity that defined earlier titles.The environments are vibrant and visually appealing, but they often lack the depth and interactivity that would elevate the experience. While there are plenty of opportunities for chaos, I found myself wishing for more activities and events to explore, as the world sometimes feels underutilized.The story introduces a new cast of characters, but they range from engaging to forgettable. Some characters shine with personality, while others feel underdeveloped. The humor, which is a staple of the series, is a mixed bag, with some jokes landing and others feeling flat.Saints Row would benefit from more variety in missions and side activities. Additional quests and unique challenges would keep the gameplay fresh, as some parts tend to drag on longer than necessary, leading to a sense of repetition.After 38 hours, Saints Row is an entertaining experience, but it struggles to fully define its identity within the franchise. If you enjoy open-world games with a bit of humor and customization, it’s worth a look, but it may not capture the magic of its predecessors. for fans of open-world action and customization!

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't wrap my head around this. Saints Row is dead, and their encore was so bad I actually learned to appreciate Saints Row IV and Gat out of Hell.While I can't blame the devs, I appreciate that even if the higher-ups didn't let them make a true Saints Row sequel/reboot with all the classic characters and a darker story, they still managed to make something out of it. I bought this game day one on Epic, and it was so bad I refunded it the same hour. Recently, I decided to purchase it again because one of my friends forced me to make that decision. Some things had improved since launch, but mostly the entire game is still a huge mess. I genuinely want to see the video about the development of it once the devs' NDA ends and find out what was initially planned for the reboot. The game is a huge grindfest with an uninteresting story featuring 25 story missions, of which only 2 were well-structured, and a billion more side hustles consisting of collecting ♥♥♥♥, killing a bunch of NPCs, or driving a car from A to B. Some jokes, even if most of them were pandered to death so as not to offend anyone, were genuinely funny. The general premise of some dudes going on a killstreak just because they need to pay rent and acting all casual about it—that's the kind of Saints Row humor I always cheered for. The devs still have that edge; it's just that they're operating on strict guidelines, and this is what they managed to come up with. Some positives i can say about this game is that it looks really great, the city has some great architecture and looks really unique from all generic cities we've seen in other open world games, car handling is fine and i spent hours creating new Bosses in the vast character creator. Additionally, an ability of changing your Boss at any point in the game and then being able to share it with the world is still a great addition.I'm going to miss Saints Row, and Volition, you've been a great studio always open to your fans. Thanks for the long years of service, and Rest in Peace, you sweet rockstars.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the Gold Edition of Saints Row 2023, I can safely say that I enjoyed the game a lot, and can see myself returning to enjoy more. The world of Santo Ileso is a big fun playground to rampage around in. I found myself being carried to about 100 hours before I finally decided I had enough. There's lots to unfold about what I liked, but it's certainly not a perfect game by any stretch. The campaign, while enjoyable, is basically a weird sitcom that never really accomplishes it's goal of making me fall in love with the characters. Now, Saints Row was never exactly Shakespeare. Even the first two were basically watered down versions of GTA when it came to the storyline. What it did well was going over the top, and this game does that in spades. First, I love some of the absurd vehicles in this game. You get the cars based on real life ones that sleek and cool, but also really crazy designs. My favorites included a giant boat car, a monster truck with a giant skull, and what I can only describe as a vehicle that Frakenstein would drive. You can also customize the cars to your liking. In fact the customization is quite good. Not quite on par with previous entries, but still great. I created a character with amputated legs and hands, surgical body scars, and a cactus head with flippers as shoes. It was fun to see this in cutscenes. The meat of the game, for me at least, comes from the empire building. Basically you can set up a business in any district, and you can perform missions for that place. For instance, a costume store acts as a front for costumed robbers. You scope out the place, looking for points of interest with your camera to break into, and then act as theg getaway driver once they rob the place. There are lots of business each with their own unique missions. In addition to that, there are all kind of side activities to do, like picture taking, wingsuit diving, finding collectibles, side jobes, destroying armored cash vehicles, bounty hunting, etc. If you're not as into the main quest like I was, the empire building is there to make up for any faults. There's so much more to customize too, like weapons, your houses, your gang, and even your roomates. Overall, it's a thumbs up for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Story:The story definitely has its issues. I think people went as hard as they did on it because it doesn't hold a candle to SR2 or SR3. On its own, it's not too bad and works fairly well as a gang origin story. It was about 4 people who valued each others' friendships more than their affiliations with their own gangs, who also realized that they are much better off striking out on their own, and so they formed a gang together. However, the problems arise when we compare it to its predecessors. SR2 was a gritty crime drama with interesting protagonists, antagonists, and some gripping twists and turns. SR3 was less so but it was still gripping to see the Saint's gradual rise to the top once again. In SR2022, the Saints came out of nowhere, bulldozed everything in their way, and were untouchable within a few weeks. It also doesn't help that the core members are 4 hipster millenials who look like they've never shot a gun before. Johnny Gat, Shaundi, and Playa were all hardened criminals with troubled pasts who wouldn't fit in anywhere else but a gang. What I'm trying to say is that the old Saints earned their top spot, while the new Saints got the top spot handed to them by the writers. Still, I can see what they were going for with these new Saints. They're meant to be sillier, more light-hearted counterparts to the grizzled crime lords of the previous games. If you don't take them seriously and just follow along with their antics, you'll be fine. Writing: The writing is serviceable. Watching the reviews, I came in expecting the writing and characters in this game to be a "How-Do-You-Do-Fellow-Kids" cringefest on the level of Sunset Overdrive. What I got, however, was honestly not THAT bad. Only  a select few dialogue lines made me cringe my brains out. The rest of the game, however, was tolerable - sometimes witty, but never too annoying. Gameplay:With most of the bugs fixed, this game plays and feels almost exactly like SR3 and 4 - which is to say, not bad. The driving also feels fine, but again, it's just the same driving as SR3 and 4. Everything here feels like it's been done before. The good thing about that is that it didn't fix what was not broken. The bad thing is that it's basically the exact same as the previous Saint's Row games even after half a decade in the oven. Graphics:The color palette of this game looks more vibrant and saturated than the previous games. The textures also look better, and the animations are not bad. However, the character models still look like they're from Saint's Row 4, which came out 10 years ago. TLDR: I think the people who dislike this game the most are those who have played the previous Saints Row games, which includes me, but surprisingly, I didn't hate this game. I know this game has a pretty bad reputation, and I came into it not expecting much. What I got was not too bad. I had some fun with it, despite its issues. Of course, I played this thing after it got one year's worth of patches, so maybe that's why. It's sad that this is the last game in the franchise, since Volition bit the dust. I think if you buy this thing on sale, and go into it expecting light-hearted, silly fun and nothing else, you'll enjoy yourself. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR; It's a great game. You'll have lots of fun.Also it works great on Deck. Out of the box, no tweaks needed (unless you want more battery life). I don't understand why it is Unsupported.If you don't know the previous games and haven't followed the criticism when the game was released here is a quick recap:The previous Saint's Row games were very wacky, a parody of other action games and even of themselves. When this reboot released many people were disappointed with the new toned down story and complained a lot.I was caught by this negativity as well and I approached this game almost expecting a terrible experience but I was wrong. Now I believe most of those comments are unjustified. As a fan of the series I am disappointed too that this game is toned down but the core aspects of the series are still there: the Genkibowl is there (with a different name and theme), the crazy side missions like the mayhem and insurance fraud are there, etc. Generally most of the mechanics are improved and balanced well.I haven't experience the game before the latest patch since I played it only on Steam but this is a great game now, very funny and with lots of stuff to do. There is some repetitions but some of the side missions are optional and I found most of them challenging to the right point, never frustrating and with enough variation to make it interesting.Yes, the characters are, individually, very dull and not much interesting but I believe the main goal was to capture feeling of a friendship or community of a college/university experience... in a very Saint's Row way.And in this regard I believe the studio delivered.I am very sad the studio has closed down but I'm glad they managed to release another great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Saints Row is a GTA-like game that reboots a well known parody series of the same genre. I only experienced a brief time with Saints Row 3 and the control scheme sort of turned me off. That may make me seem biased in my review, but I will try to be as neutral as possible.The game's main story surrounds your customized character and their three friends trying to make something of themselves in a California-like city. Two of the friend group are already members of some of the more prolific gangs; meanwhile, your character is trying to do right by working for the local paid mercenary group. All of their antics lead back to them being outcasts, however, and that motivates them to try and start their own infamous gang: The Saints.Gameplay revolves around doing various crimes around the city. From stealing cars to completing hit jobs, there is no crime too big or small for your ambitious character. Main and side missions will get you money and xp, but so will just going out and doing your own thing. The game rewards a lot of your actions, which gives you the freedom to get out and make your fortune your own way.It will be important to progress at least some of the story, since certain staples of the genre such as chop shops or running illegal businesses are locked behind missions. But even without those things, there are plenty of things to do on the map. It's large and will reveal points of interest as you cruise around.Speaking of cruising around, the game has a radio that is pretty decent. I wish it had more songs but it does have the privilege of having licensed music to listen to. This is one of my personal favorite features of GTA-like games, so I appreciate it even if the song list could stand to be longer.Customization is insane in this game. You can create custom colors for your clothing, cars, weapons, etc. There are so many little details for personalization, too. Some of it has to be unlocked but just the fact that it's there is crazy. And once you unlock your main base of operations, there are collectibles you find around the city that can be used to decorate it. Collectathons are nice and all, but it's even better when you can display your collection nicely.Obviously the game still has some bugs and other issues. I fell through the map once, and had a vehicle bug out to the point where I couldn't get back in it, which caused me to fail a mission. Movement can seem a bit janky at times, and traffic is pretty selfish and unforgiving. However, the bugs I have encountered have not been so game-breaking that I felt I had to stop. The ones I mentioned only happened in the first hour of me playing, and haven't happened since. Still, I recommend getting the game on sale since it has issues that need to be worked out. Personally, I find it fun for what it is and am really in love with all of the customization and collectibles.

_childDocuments_.review: In a puzzling move that defies comprehension, Volition must have jettisoned their seasoned development team in favor of a cadre of interns, and the results are nothing short of disastrous. Nothing short of that can explain it.As a former huge fan of the series, it pains me to admit that I will begrudgingly soldier on, trudging through the main storyline out of sheer obligation to Volition's once-proud legacy. However, my grim expectations leave me with no doubt that the moment the credits roll on this abysmal incarnation, I will eagerly and promptly hit the "uninstall" button, with the fervent hope that this ill-conceived chapter will be swiftly erased from my gaming memory, as if it never existed at all.
