_childDocuments_.review: One of the biggest issues with this game is the lack of direction in the story. The game's narrative is convoluted and hard to follow, with multiple factions vying for power and a vague threat lurking in the shadows. The result is a confusing mess that never fully comes together.Another problem is the character design. The game's cast of characters is forgettable and one-dimensional, with little to no personality or depth. Even the iconic characters from previous games, such as the Vice President and the various gang leaders, feel like empty shells of their former selves.The gameplay itself is also subpar. The controls feel clunky and unresponsive, and the shooting mechanics are often imprecise. The driving mechanics are slightly better, but even then, the physics engine feels wonky and unrealistic.Despite these issues, there are a few bright spots in Saints Row. The game's visuals are certainly improved, with detailed environments and smooth animations. The soundtrack is also pretty good, featuring a mix of hip-hop and electronic music that perfectly captures the game's edgy atmosphere.However, despite these positives, Saints Row ultimately feels like a missed opportunity. With a talented team behind it, the game had the potential to be a standout title in the open-world crime genre. Unfortunately, the game's poor writing, lackluster characters, and technical issues hold it back from reaching its full potential.As someone who has played every Saints Row game since the beginning, it's sad to see the series go downhill like this. Volition was known for creating unique and engaging worlds, but with their closure, it seems unlikely that we'll ever see another great Saints Row game again. I hope that the developers at Volition are able to find new jobs and continue to make games.In the meantime, I'll be playing the old Saints Row games and reflecting on what could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: The new chapter in the Saints Row saga might have transported us to the sun-soaked streets of Santo Ileso, but the heart and soul of the game remains as vibrant and audacious as ever.Santo Ileso, with its sprawling urban districts and vast desert landscapes, serves as a perfect backdrop for the fresh yet familiar antics of the Third Street Saints. As a long-time fan, exploring this new city brought a delightful juxtaposition of novelty and nostalgia. Every street corner, every mission, and every interaction evoked memories of the original series, yet felt innovative and fresh in this new context.While the setting is new, the game remains true to its roots with its trademark humor, eclectic characters, and unbridled chaos. Driving through the neon-lit boulevards or facing off against rival gangs in Santo Ileso, there's a continuous undercurrent of that classic Saints Row charm we've come to love.The new world design is a testament to the developers' dedication to the series. Santo Ileso is rich in detail, with dynamic environments that showcase both the grit and glamour one would expect from a Saints Row title. Whether you're parachuting off skyscrapers, engaging in epic gunfights, or merely taking in the scenery, the city feels alive and immersive.In conclusion, the new Saints Row, set in Santo Ileso, brilliantly marries the nostalgia of the series' past with the promise of its future. It's a refreshing take on the beloved franchise, inviting both old fans and new players to indulge in the wild escapades of the Third Street Saints.

_childDocuments_.review: I always play games a year or more late. Then they're usually patched and less buggy, and at a discount. It also means I can give a review during a time its not either being showered in praise or review bombed. However, I think they abandoned this fairly quickly. Because its still riddled with gamebreaking bugs, most noteably being the one where all your inputs stop until you restart the game. The Pro'sThere's not a lot, but when the inputs work, most of the mechanics were serviceable. Its just basically SR3 under the skin, so they probably copy-pasted the things that already worked. If it didnt have the bug where inputs would fail, it would be an OK time-killer. The Con's:*Where to start. The bugs... from hidden walls, terrain that sends your car into orbit, flickering textures, poor gamma and colorgrading, input failure, button prompts that dont respond or at huge delays, it feels very unpolished and technically inept. Like this was either worked on by incompetent people or rushed out the door. *Then there is the potemkin villlage aesthetic. The graphics aren't horrible, but the level design, asset placement and overal mood creation is off. It looks like you're driving in some potemki village/movieset. *Then there is the minimap GPS that spazzes out all the time, making you miss exits or take wrong ones. *Recycled Engine: You can tell there was a lot of copy-pasting from SR3/SR4 engine. They didn't even bother to rename the guns. And they are all present. Including the sniper, the 3burst rifle, etc. *Costume variety is very poor. SR3 and SR4 had a lot of wacky customes, but here most shops have like 8 items and its mostly facepaints, rings of accessoires. *Very small map, you can basically drive from one end to the other in <5minutes. *Male and Female animations are the same. SR3/SR4 had a specific female and male gait, especially when slowly walking. Here they both use the same animation. Very lazy, especially since it was already present in the old engine.*Understeering cars, unless you constantly use the slide mechanic, your cars dont steer for ♥♥♥♥ and will just understeer into everything. *Absence of Humor. It was always pretty campy, but it worked through the delivery of the voice actors, and the doubling down by the developers. Here, all the edge is taking off, and replaced by reddit-tier millenial writing. Which mostly consists of social ineptitude, awkwardness and toilet humor. In fact the writing is probably what killed the game the most. I didn't laugh or chuckle a single time in 7 hours of playthrough. *Voice actors: Well... the 4 ladies voicing this are definitely not Laura Bailey... Especially the brit who voiced Morgan in Starfield was a miscast. Maybe they had very little material to work with? Because some of them are pretty well acomplished, but it just wasn't landing. *Rubberbanding AI, during chases they have the Cyberpunk style of just rubberbanding and teleporting behind you, forcing you to use the extremely annoying sideslam ability that alwyas results in you spinning out. Thats about what I could stomach, and what my list of annoyances was what I wrote down in my playthrough. The reason it failed is not because of the Burger King Kids club diversity, SR3 and SR4 already did that with Pierce and he was funny in that game. The reason it failed is because incompetent people worked on it with no vision, or a funny bone in their body. And that IS probably moreso a result of ESG hiring practices.

The sandbox is locked to the main story questline; you won't unlock vehicle customization until you complete the story mission associated with your first "Venture" (replaces property acquisition mechanic in previous Saints Row), about five or six hours into first playthrough, which just so happens to be a garage.The devs seem to have cherry-picked archetypes for the game. "Santo Ileso, a vibrant fictional city in the American Southwest" has an extremely GTA V vibe to it, with sprawling butte-infested plains and desert a short drive from high-density residential areas in the city. The Idols are very reminiscent of other headache-inducing and epileptic-triggering anarchist neon ravers of the American underground dance scene; the antagonists of Far Cry: New Dawn come to mind.As for the name, the 3rd Street Saints are dead, or at least absent from any spotlight. Once you unlock the first HQ, which happens to be a derelict church slated for demolition, the main cast suddenly is dripped in pimp royal purple adorned with Fleur-De-Lis and matching tattoos.Overall, the game is good. Solid experience. Would recommend purchasing on sale. Many of the bugs present prior seem to have been patched for the Steam release. Many of the negative reviews are people who played the game for a half hour, realized it was not a $60 remake of their childhood nostalgic favorites, and left a negative review, never to touch it again. Saints Row originally cranked out their entire original tetrology from 2006-2013, and I'm confident enough game time can be had to match all of the previous entries.30 hours edit (Spoilers): Volition was literally dismantled five hours from the time of this writing due to how poorly this game was received. _childDocuments_.review: I know what you must be thinking. "That thumb is pointing the wrong way." Let me explain.Having heard about the game's extensively bad rap, I entirely skipped the game and forgot it even existed. Some time passes and I notice I have this game in my Humble Bundle monthly library (hence the "received for free"), I figured why not try it out. I went in ready to hate the entire experience and pointed out every little flaw I could find "of course they'd mess THAT up too". However, as time went by and I progressed further into the game, my opinion about it changed drastically, and I quite enjoyed my time in Santo Ileso, ended 100%:ing the achievements, too. That took me 67 hours. Could've been fewer hours, had I been more efficient. Also: There's no achievement for completing ALL challenges! So there's that.My first gripe with the game is that I don't entirely understand why it carries the Saints Row flag to begin with. Sure, it's similar in gameplay, but none of the original Saints are present, and (early SR4 spoiler) . So I'm not sure which period in time this game takes place. Is it a prequel to all the previous Saints Rows? Is this how and where the Saints originally were formed? Doubtful, too many contradictions for that to make sense. There are a few nods to the original Saints Row games, but otherwise it's just "a separate Saints Row, but elsewhere".The story is acceptable, I guess. It's nothing special, but it passes fine. The main story isn't very long, but there's still plenty to do in Santo Ileso. There are plentiful side missions, and with the two expansions The Heist And the Hazardous + A Song of Ice And Dust, that plenty becomes even more. And oh boy let me tell you, if Saints Row's whimsical humor is to your liking, the latter is a blast to play through. All the other DLC (Doc Ketchum's Murder Circus) I'd recommend only if you intend to 100% the achievements, and/or on a hefty (60%+) sale.I've heard people complain about the characters in the game. Sure, they're forgettable and fairly generic, but inherently I don't think they're too bad. I didn't really think much of anyone, in good or bad. They're kind of just there, and there's some decent comedy. Comedy that, I think, carries much of the game.Gameplay is alright, the controls function fine. The PC moves nicely and the vehicles control well. Gunplay I think is the forte in Saints Row. The guns' audio is nice and feedback from hits on enemies looks and feels good.Bugs. There are bugs. They vary widely from barely noticeable to actually game-breaking bugs. Fortunately the game auto-saves very often and if you need to load an earlier save, you're not going to lose a lot of progress. I experienced 0 crashes during my 67 hours of game. One example of a game-breaking bug I encountered (just once) was that an enemy took me into a melee "finisher" type of hold, from which I somehow managed to struggle out of, and after that I could only move but perform no other actions. I could pause the game and open the phone just fine, I could move but I couldn't attack, enter a car, jump etc. A simple reload fixed that. Once a dialogue box never left the screen and new dialogue would appear and overlap and it would quickly become an unreadable mess. Once I got a tutorial message on how to sideswipe on my vehicle, and it never left the screen, somewhat obscuring my view while driving. Reloading fixed that, too. Stuff like that. Is it a perfect/flawless game? No, not by a long shot. Heck, there are times it barely passes as acceptable. I'm convinced the game would've gotten a better reception if it hadn't been branded a Saints Row reboot. Would still need a few months in the oven, but at least the Saints Row community wouldn't have been angry. I think it's a passable game that just came out raw.Somehow I still end up recommending this game, albeit at a hefty (70%+) discount. It's a funny, buggy mess. But if you know in advance what you're getting into, maybe it won't be so bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: "Saints Row 2022: A Chaotic Mess of Identity and Tone""Saints Row 2022 attempts to infuse its gameplay with the same eclectic mix of identity markers and political affiliations found in a confusing social media biopic. Unfortunately, the result is a game that stumbles over its own attempt at satire and falls flat on its face.From the outset, the game bombards players with a mishmash of identity politics, ranging from gender identity and sexual orientation to political affiliations. The game seems more interested in ticking off a checklist of social issues than in crafting a cohesive narrative. The attempt to replicate the playful emojis and flags from the character creation in the game's visual style only adds to the overall lack of focus.Political affiliations are thrust to the forefront, with the game's writers seemingly subscribing to an 'anything goes' philosophy. Anti-White America, Anarcho-Communism, and an oddly specific stance against "establishment sympathizers" make the game feel like it's trying too hard to be edgy without substance. The inclusion of such controversial stances only serves to alienate players rather than provoke thoughtful reflection.The attempt at humor falls short, mirroring the emoji-laden real world but lacking the necessary context and wit to land successfully in its own. Whether it's the awkward inclusion of progressive elements or the forced references to a similar 'RoboCop police state', the humor often feels forced and out of touch with the game's core identity.Personal details scattered throughout the game, much like the player character's own past, add unnecessary clutter. While the attempt to create a personalized gaming experience is commendable, the constant barrage of unrelated details about the characters' lives feels more like an attempt to appeal to a checklist of demographics rather than to create meaningful connections. DAE HAVE STUDENT LOANS??In an age where smooth and immersive gameplay is expected, the constant crashes and loading screen issues are an affront to the reputation of a major gaming franchise. It's as if the developers were so focused on cramming in identity markers and political affiliations that they forgot to ensure the game was actually playable.The lack of polish is particularly disappointing given the pedigree of the Saints Row series. It's a shame to see a once-respected franchise reduced to a technical embarrassment. The attempt to make a bold statement with identity and politics becomes overshadowed by the frustration of trying to get through the game without encountering a game-breaking bug.Saints Row 2022 sacrifices a coherent narrative and engaging gameplay for a misguided attempt at social commentary. The result is a chaotic and confusing experience that lacks the necessary substance to make it anything more than a forgettable attempt at satire. In its current state it is an embarrassment not only to the franchise but to the wider AAA gaming industry. _childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend buying it? No. But the review is "positive", because I don’t think the game deserves a "negative" one.Oh boy, where do we start. It ended up longer than I expected.- Combat and character upgrades are nothing like they were in previous games. You can’t regenerate your health in combat (well, you can, but you need to hide in a trashcan and not take damage for about 3 hours). Instead, to regenerate health you need to perform a takedown on an enemy. The more enemies you kill - the more often you can perform a takedown.- Maximum character level is reduced to 20. When levelling up you will now unlock either a skill or a health/flow upgrade. Again, the more enemies you kill – the more skills you can use. ("Hey, I’m about to die - I cast invincibility", "This guy is annoying - I cast a landmine on his face")- On top of that, there are also perks, which you unlock by completing challenges. They are always active, and you can have up to 5 equipped at a time. This allows for some sort of small build-making.This is not the most original system in the modern day, but it’s definitely the most interesting one when compared to previous games in the series.- Enemy gangs now have 2 unique specialists, and when reached level 5 of notoriety - you will see a mini-boss. Defeat that, and your notoriety goes to 0.- Weapons haven’t changed much. Most of them have a special ability that you unlock by completing a weapon specific challenge. Most are generally useful, some are a gimmick, and you can turn them off if you want.- Same goes for vehicles - same old cars we all know (although they felt a bit more "arcade-like", but it can be just me). Most also have special abilities you can install. There are no planes.- The wingsuit is ok. I was skeptical about it at first, but it kind of grew on me.- The map feels slightly bigger compared to previous games, mainly because the city is now surrounded by a desert instead of an ocean. The map has plenty of good scenery and there is a decent variety to the districts. I definitely like it better than Steelport. There are, however, little to none interiors, and NPCs behavior seems not as diverse as it was back in Stilwater. If not for that, I would say that this map is the best in the series.- We can still find many activities on the map. Some we are familiar with, the others are completely new, and a lot of them you access by placing ventures on the map. They are ok. I don’t think they are better or worse compared to previous games.It’s bad. Even if I wanted to, I cannot defend the main story. The writing is just... not good. There is like one cutscene that I enjoyed. And it’s not even great or genius. It is ok, but it looks like a gem compared to the rest. The story has good ideas, yes, but it all means nothing without a proper execution. DLCs generally have better stories though.There are quite some. They are, however, mostly minor bugs, related to UI and some game settings. There are no gamebraking bugs, or the ones that will softlock you (at least I haven’t seen any in my 70-something hours). The bugs in game were annoying at worst, so I don’t think that it’s a big issue. It feels like the devs just didn’t have time to polish the game and fix all the small issues. And now that the studio is closed - nobody ever will.The game is good, if you don’t care about the story. Do I recommend buying it? No. Volition is dead, and the publisher is an ass. So the less money you give them - the better (at least wait for a discount, if you really want to spend money). I am, however, leaving a “positive” review, because I believe the game didn’t deserve the negativity it got.I tried to keep it as dry on emotions as I can. So let’s dump it all here. I like the game. I really enjoyed playing it. From the moment it was announced as a reboot, I said to myself "Ok, I don’t care about the story then". And that’s probably why I enjoyed the game as much as I did. I found it as fun as the old Saint’s Row. And I know the devs loved making it. I know they care about it. That’s why it is sad for me to see how bad it was received. Even though I fully agree that the story was bad. I don’t know where I’m going with this. I don’t even know who will read this. If you do though - I hope you will have a nice day.

_childDocuments_.review: W'sAmount of dialogues- Pretty much every mission, side mission, activity has its unique dialogue and voicelines, I was admittedly surprised by the sheer amount of them. Now are they actually good? I've heard at least four or five instances of 'Why is this <absurd nonsense> happening?' / 'Because of <some madeup reason>' / 'Why, of course!' kind of lazy writing, but they're mostly okay to listen to. In some cases I even found them... funny.Collectibles- Most collectibles are tied with the actual rewards meaning there's a valid reason to pursue them now other than to make that completion percentage number on your savegame higher. Also almost every one of them are located in a location that's accessible by foot so you don't need to worry because you forgot to bring your heli or VTOL.Number of customization options- Good ol' character creator is still here and plenty of clothes are available as an option, my only complaint is the lack of highcut tacticool helmet we can only wear on the few introductory missions. Vehicle customization, it still can't match the GTA V standard but it's quite decent, it definitely helps to make up for the lackluster vehicle roaster.Everything regarding Wasteland LARP sections- There's a LARP event ingame that's inspired by Mad-Max like post apocalyptic themed LARP events in real life and they're quite refreshing, the humor regarding the rules and limitations of such events are on point and missions themselves are very enjoyable. These parts of the game are the parts that are most reminiscent of the previous games of the franchise before this reboot. You can actually feel this game actually is made by Volition and that they didn't lose their touch completely.L'sStory- It just starts and ends, first half of the main missions are used to set the backstory and the rushed latter half is equally uninspired and boring as the first half. Needless cutscenes are aplenty especially in the early game and amount of action that's shown during an actual gameplay is greatly reduced.Characters- No more familiar faces, we got new homies in this one. Neenah, who plays somewhat of a role in the story only due to her having a generic villain of a nemesis, Eli, a pretentious Steve Urkel looking benchwarmer who only is relevant in his LARP missions, and Kevin. ♥♥♥♥ Kevin. Your phone's contact list will feel really short on this one.Health Bars on enemies- Not only they're just a cheap way to prolong combat sequences and general playtime, they're undesirable visual clutter that's annoying to look at.Vehicular Combat- They're made out of paper mache when you're not driving them. You popped a tire? Flame on! Spontaneous explosion! You killed a driver? Explosion again! You might think this is convenient and will work for you but the game spawns a ton of enemy vehicles to fill the empty space and if your objective is to hijack enemy vehicle and deliver it to somewhere else, you better pray to not destroy the target vehicle by an accident. If they did this to compensate for the lack of action I mentioned above, unfortunately it did not help much.Optimization- It just doesn't run well, occasionally game tanks fps down to 3-5 to load stuff and you can see weird graphical artifacts forming on cars and other props, I first thought my GPU was acting up again but apparently this issue is widespread, it's incredible how they decided to ship the game in this state and not patch it. What a mess.I will include the short review for its DLCs as well since no one should buy them individually. You should either: 1) Not buy this game or 2) Buy the Gold Edition.DLC1: The Heist and The HazardousAs you already noticed in the name, it makes fun of FnF all along. Hmm... I wonder what other franchise is known for its ridiculousness? 3 okay but short missions, 1 good looking player house you steal from the main villain, and useful unlocks. Not worth its individual price tag, but worth playing.DLC2: Doc Ketchum’s Murder CircusOne of laziest attempts I've ever seen to integrate roguelike elements into a game. This DLC is a huge waste of time and unless you're a completionist you shouldn't bother with this one at all.DLC3: A Song Of Ice And DustMore wasteland LARP tales. 5 missions this time, and just like the related base game missions they're fun as hell and noticably more polished. This is, worth its individual price tag.If you're a Saints Row fan, it's worth giving this game a chance as Volition got Embraced™ and there's absolutely no probability of another Saints Row coming out in the near future.To the general audience, this game definitely fits the definition of a mixed bag. Unless you ran out of GTA clones to play you shouldn't consider this game over other positively rated similar games in your backlog. Aim to get the Gold Edition for less than $12.

_childDocuments_.review: If you just do the main missions, it's like 10-12 hrs. I ended up liking it more than I expected, but it takes a lot of patience to get past the awful writing and Disney-tier dorks of a cast. It also just generally takes longer than it should to open up and "get going". The story is pretty boilerplate rags-to-riches copypasta.The gameplay is a fun enough power fantasy - nothing really challenging. AI is dumb as rocks, but performance is smooth, UI is intuitive, and there's a decent variety of action and set pieces in the main missions to help you forget that you're just lock-on aiming and shooting most of the time. Soundtrack/radio stations also have some great tracks if you're into old school hip hop, metal (whole station dedicated to Nuclear Blast recording artists), or synthwave. Character customization is also pretty great - lots of options without being overly complicated. Simple and to the point. Buy it at a steep discount and there's some fun to be had. It's not the Saints Row anybody wanted, and it definitely deserved the backlash, but there's some stuff it gets right when you're not looking at it through the lens of paying full price (I got the gold edition for $8). I didn't encounter too many bugs, other than one instance early on in the game when I first approached the church and couldn't leave my vehicle when I was supposed to (apparently had something to do with having tips turned on by default?).RIP Volition.

I've never played a Saints Row game before. It's a pretty goofy satirical parody of the genre. It's got about 40ish hours of play time in it, more if you do all the misc stuff that doesn't really matter to the story, but can give you a unique car you'll never use or something. If you'r elike me, however, and jsut do all the main story missions, any criminal ventures, and the DLCs, you'll get about 40 hours out of it.I don't want to get too into the mechanics and so forth as it pretty much does the same thing that any game like it does. Just with jokes and parodies. So if you like GTA, you'll probably like this.The thigns I didn't like:- Most cars drive like a brick, and 7/10 missions decide your vehicle for you. So a lot of the time, you'll be driving a brick- Side swiping doesn't feel good. I ended up shooting every enemy in vehicle combat cuz the mechanic is just cumbersome, often doesn't work, and felt ineffective.- While the criminal ventures can be a grind, there are two in particular that are just bad. The first is the radio venture and the second is the saints store. The radio one is just poorly made requiring you to get to level 5 notoriety, but only trickling enemies to you making it really easy to lose notoriety. I had to just let one guy live and constantly shoot at me. The Saints Store involves stealing 12 green trucks that randomly spawn around you and despawn if you're too far away. Depending on your luck, that can be a real time sink for no reason.- There isn't much for upgrading. weapons and vehicles can be upgraded thrice, and each has a signature ability. Outside of that, I had my full weapon loadout ready to go by somewhere between 3 and 5 hours in, and I used that loadout for the remaining 35ish hours. Same situation for vehicles. The game throws you a lot of unique and special vehicles, but none of them are very good. You're going to end up using the Tornado Helicopter, the Kenshin, and either the Fer de Lance or the Attrazione. You'll be given a hover motorcycle with a machine gun that you might use instead of the Kenshin, but the Kenshin is a lot faster.All in all, I had my full build completed by 10 hours in and was just playing for the story the rest of the time. _childDocuments_.review: I put in roughly 45 hours into seeing this game to its bitter end and I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gave up just 3% short of full completion. DO NOT BUY THIS. Not only are you getting one of the worst open-world games I've ever seen, you're supporting a company that no longer exists, and will not be able to make up for yet another stain on their IP and reputation.As much as I want to refrain from addressing the elephant of 'wokeness' in the room, I'm unable to. To keep it straight, I will preface this by saying that I am a normal approximation of a human being, and believe that wokeness does not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ exist. These characters are insufferable, annoying, and unfunny. Anything but 'woke'. It's what a bunch of ancient board room members believe young people are actually like. This game wants you to believe that these nigh-invincible, crime boss, super murderers are just a bunch of roommates trying to make rent. They're frequently said to stick out for the little guy, and openly hate corporations. It's the bare minimum for a human being to believe, and it only gets worse when your main character starts making millions every 2 minutes and has defaced their abandoned church into looking like a vomit-inducing frat house. There is such a colossal amount of narrative dissonance that I wonder if this team even knew what game they were writing for. Never in my years of life, my years of playing all sorts of awful games, have I seen writers be so unbelievably out of touch with the entire world. It's sometimes hard to tell if something present in the game is a joke, or is a genuine result of a person's skewed and completely incorrect belief in the world, I.E. The Idols, an enemy faction that claims to be anarchist, but is starkly monarchist in practice. Is that a joke? Is that a genuine misconception of what anarchists really are? I don't know! It didn't get so much as a pity chuckle out of me, so I simply assume the latter. The game also milks its Mexico (Or New Mexico, I don't care enough to remember or check,) setting and western aesthetic to a point of pure aggravation. By the end, you'll be so sick of cowboy riffs that seeing a cactus will either send you into a panic attack, or a blind rage.The LARPing will get no reference here other than this paragraph. It's boring, annoying, and painfully unfunny. Whoever thought of it should be blacklisted from the entire industry.The game fails at nearly every gameplay type it tries to achieve. Guns are a total joke. If you want to avoid the slog that is combat, equip the revolver. 6 shots (12 with dual wield perk,) headshots usually kill in one shot; not counting specialists. This singular gun makes the difficulty fall flat on its face, because auto-aim is so aggressive that you'll struggle to hit something that isn't a gang member's succulent grey matter. (You can't turn it off, either.) Speaking of the gang factions, the balance of difficulty between them is also a complete joke. The Idols are almost entirely a mere hindrance more than a threat. You will never not be able to kill them in a single headshot, and their specialist types require no brain power to handle. Contrarily, the Marshall group is somehow a constant threat regardless of difficulty, I assume due to their use of automatic rifles as opposed to 9mm pistols. Your health will drain fast in packs, and the constant dropping of land mines on death is one of the most annoying mechanics in the entire game. Melee combat is equally pathetic, possibly moreso, and will normally never be used by the player. It's slow, and what damage you do inflict, you'll probably take more in the process.The open world manages to be both a literal and a figurative deserted wasteland. There is not a single ounce of fun to be had collecting the 125 total drug palettes scattered across the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ map, or the ~30 discovery activities involving running around the exact same 10 foot radius circle looking for information boards so this game can throw references to the infinitely superior Saints Row 2 in an attempt to win back the tiny amount of fans that not only utterly despise this game, not only continue in spite of that, but are also idiotic enough to believe this development team is able to produce anything worth any amount of money ever again. You're actually required to do all of this monotonous side content if you want to see the various weapon types, vehicles, and customization options they have locked behind them. For the record, you aren't missing out on much, it's more ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pistols, explosives, and a beer costume.Character customization is simultaneously extremely open, yet so limited and ugly. The one positive I have is that this is the first game I've seen in the series, or really in any game with character customization, that has a half-shaven haircut. The rest is barely worth mentioning. It attempts to be a system full of customization options that cater to people who just want to make the ugliest atrocity possible, and those who want to make something that's pleasing to look at. It ends up barely accommodating for the latter, as there are little to no basic clothing options that range out of just a singular color. There is not a single shirt or jacket option with horizontal stripes in this entire game.I'm starting to get tired of writing this review. Don't be like me and waste two entire days of your life playing a game that has nothing interesting to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a cleaner version of SR3 when it comes to gameplay and content.Definitely a bit different, but it still has glorious violence and cartoonish humor. Pretty lacking in the sex humor, no gimp suit or dildo bat from my first pass. However, that being retired along with Genki bowl isn't inherently bad, but locking a murderbowl activity behind dlc is a bit scuzzy.To address this...Some of the folks giving this a negative review either fans disappointed we didn't get a follow-up to Gat out of Hell that wasn't Agents of Mayhem Related. I sympathize, and would have really liked to see an SR5, time traveling adventure, but that just wasn't in the cards as disappointing as that is.Here are the pointers that bring down the game as a SR fan:- The characters fail to break the mold of their archetypes. SR2: Gat, Shaundi, and Pierce mattered, Carlos and his sacrifice mattered.Gwen, Neena, and Kev needed a stronger connection to the gangs they represent.Also, Eli, probably needed more of a hook than, "a dude that read a self-help book."- The dialogue is very Millenial.This is not something that bothers me, I can chuckle at crappy Sitcom humor, but my tolerance for any kind of questionable writing is pretty high. It's the same issue I had with SR3 when it came out, it's very guided towards folks in their late 20's / early 30's. Which would work if the audience wasn't Saint's Row fans with very different expectations.- Minor to Major technical glitches.They have made the game way better over the last year+ since the release, but minor glitches are expected. I have yet to experience anything game breaking, but it's well documented online.Overall, it's not bad, but in the same way you can drudge through the parts you don't like of the annual assassin's creed release.The others upset are weird Gamergate dudes pedojacketing NPCs and claiming this game caused someone to die or is woke. One person I watched said the booby slider not being included was an afront to the franchise, which I hesitantly file into the changing modern sensibilities corner. I remember SR3 was hated on launch on the forums because of the wild turn towards absurdity. This is closer to SR2 in it's approach in setting the series tone, and that's fine, but it's definitely subdued in character development.So, perfect for $20 - $30.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only do I recommend it, I wholeheartedly recommend it. It's a great Saints Row entry.I'm going for all collectibles, upgrading everything, and working through the game one district at a time. I started with the OG Saints Row and kind of liked it. Saints Row 2 and 3 are probably my favorite in the original series. 4 was good, but it was constantly balls to the wall out there. And I had really low hopes for this after the absolute wreck that Agents of Mayhem was, and you know what? I was blown away, it really feels like they went back to their roots and aimed for a game that honestly plays and feels like Saints Row 2.5. In that it has some absolutely insane stuff in it, but you are building up the saints. People seem to forget in the early times of the series, the Boss was the only real badass. The rest of the cast grew into badasses through the series. These are supposed to be blurry eyed rookies that have seen some of the gang life but aren't like fully into it all yet. I've already watch 1 guy swear to never use a gun and now shows up with an AR when I call. Your crew evolves as you play, they get tougher, more badass. Anyone who says this is not a decent Saints Row entry only played 3 and 4. Or only played 4. The gun play is the exact same system as 3 and 4. The driving is the exact same arcade-y feel. Open world, tons of collectibles, gorgeous graphics.Running in 4k, maxed settings, DX12. It's beautiful. The radio stations kind of suck, but that's not a really big deal. It's all pretty mediocre in the music category. There is some vehicle pop-in/pop-out. But nothing that's like ruined playing for me, they spawn/despawn at the edges of the screen. I've never had something pop into existence right in front of me and ruin a drive. The "drifting" is not drifting, it's power sliding. That's probably my biggest gripe.I've had zero crashes and no glitches. And I'm 11 hours in, most of it spent screwing around and not playing the story past setting up businesses and maxing them out (which is admittedly unnecessary). But I've enjoyed every minute of it. This deserved so much better than the hate it got.

_childDocuments_.review: At it's heart this is a Saint's Row game through and through. Anyone saying it isn't is off their rocker. The ingredients are basically a little SR2 with a lot of SR3 in a new city with new characters. Nothing crazy and new, but also, nothing crazy and new.I'm one of the apparently few people who liked all of the SR games, from 1 to Gat out of hell. But I liked them for different reasons. I can see how people who only liked 1 and 2 would have criticisms of this one, and I can see how people who only liked 3 and 4 would have criticisms of this one. But as someone who liked them all, it's fun.There were so many people wanting SR to go back to its gritty roots, but at the same time, a lot of other people were saying that 1 and 2 were just GTA clones, and 3 and 4 is when the series really came into its own. So the writers tried to satisfy both types of people. Which is hard to do. But for those of us who enjoyed all the games, this works.I'll admit that, at first I was a little put off by how the characters are made to seem like nice normal non-gangster type people with student loans and other regular-people worries, in an attempt to make them seem more relatable to the player. But if you look at their actions and not their clothes and manner of speech, then it's obvious that they are every bit as much murderous psychopaths as the original gang. They are not the wholesome group of friends from Watch_Dogs 2, and they are not the puckish rogues of SR4.And, last but not least, the idle banter and humor is on point.

_childDocuments_.review: Saint's Row but not all the way. In this reboot, there are elements of Saints Row's spirit sprinkled throughout an unfinished world. In many ways, the game feels unfinished as you drive around the many boroughs that make up the city. Upon my first few hours of this game, it felt like nostalgic as you relive the making of the Saints. However, soon after it feels like the story takes a tank and is just filled with fetch and kill enemy quests. Now don't get me wrong, it isn't like the story of the Saints is very deep, but the history behind the game had enough to create a entirely new story line for the current gen, but instead they decided to reboot it. Now if you are going to reboot a series, all the previous stuff that was in the series should be there and built upon, not just start from bare bones again.The characeters don't feel developed. They feel like they are just a bunch of kids trying to figure things out, which would make sense, but at the same time doesn't feel like the direction is worth paying attention to. The general feel is kill and threaten people, get power.During my play through, I experienced a few crashes. Nothing to kill my progress, but just a minor annoyance when trying to play through a "lengthy"  mission. I missed the variety of cars and places that made up the city. This seemed to be really bland with a limited number of vehicles. I constantly found my self hunting for something unique only to find a "unique" variation that wasn't really unique.The physics are hilarious and when trying to out run the law or an enemy, the rubber band effect is annoying and just an excuse for bad programming. It however, doesn't get in the way too bad, but if you are playing on "BOSS" difficulty, I would expect a little more. Frequently the enemy NPCs would get stuck, allowing me to just plow down with a small hand gun. There are many more interesting things that happened but, it is what it is.If you don't think of this game as apart of the original Saint's Row series, then you might be able to over look the undeveloped story line and unfinished feel. I can at least appreciate, the tease of what it could have been, the sound track which has a decent mix of genre, but heavily Latin influenced. This series is what it is, not great, not bad but just is. You have the similar missions, wacky guns, and weird apparel. How you do not have all the previous stuff in from the other saints row is mind blowing, then the DLC bits again which trickle in. All and all I don't recommend this game at full price. This is a $9.99 budget bin buy at best. It had great potential but things happen and only so much can be delivered.I recommend this game only if you purchase knowing not to expect much from this title.Pros++ Soundtrack+ Mindless shooter+ Decent mission length+ Tons of side quests+ Character customizationCons-- Repetitive- Unfinished feel- Low variety of vehicles compared to previous series- lack luster AI

_childDocuments_.review: If you're already a Saint's fan, you'll enjoy this. If you've never played a Saints game, this is a good one to start out with (although Saint's 3 and 4 I think may take the lead when it comes to comical material). Solid mechanics, plenty of mini-games, and a decent main story. Glam customization is also abundant, but I do wish the creators would have focused a less on the Skill points system (which I didn't even need to use) and maybe on something like actual upgrades to weapons (like side-effects, higher damage, or just more random humor when using them. The Dubstep gun is a great example from 4). Characters feel kind of bland, but not terribly. Your 3 primary companions do appear to have solid character development structures, but I do wish they had given them more depth. More missions involving their personal backgrounds, a bit more weight on overcoming their former associations, or even having specific ones designated to help you when doing certain tasks or side-missions would make it more interesting (imo).Gripes aside, the graphics are nice and polished (I'm running DX12 using a Radeon RX 6800 XT when playing), the missions are varied enough in both task and execution so that they don't feel like a "Wash, Rinse, Repeat", and the humor is mostly on par for Saint's. I particularly enjoyed the ability to customize the pitch/depth of the voice for our MC. Hearing my MC in a deep-voiced southern-style come through in the dialogues never gets old lol.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a ton of fun playing in the latest Saints Row sandbox. It has all the goofy chaos I've come to enjoy from the series, but re-packaged with what feels like better mechanics to me (especially driving and shooting).  I also think the new location is beautiful (hats off to the art design team putting neat buildings/murals everywhere) and the new characters really grew on me. It plays wonderfully on the Steam Deck despite the unsupported tag.That said, I can understand how some folks will get annoyed by the short main story missions and the occasional bugs. You'll probably want to avoid this game if a lengthy main story is essential to you and you get bored by checking off collectibles. For me, I was more than happy to spend most of my time completing the side missions (even the boring ones) and challenges since I just wanted to relax and escape a bit in Santo Ileso. In fact, I will gladly play this over a number of Ubisoft open world games. It has far more variety and fun.Anyways, thanks Volition (R.I.P.) for giving me the chance to enjoy one last game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often review games, but it seems like this one might be getting review-bombed for weird culture war reasons and that it has an undeservedly low score so I figured I'd toss in my two cents.The good: This game is really fun. With only a few exceptions, I was having a blast all the way through and even after 60+ hours I didn't start getting sick of it, which is rare for me. I certainly wouldn't claim it's high art or that anything about it is terribly original, but they understand what's enjoyable about driving and combat mechanics and seem to have made fun their first priority in all things. There's solid variety in missions, you generally have a good bit of freedom to focus on what interests you most, and if you do find something boringly easy or frustratingly tricky you can fiddle with the different difficulty settings at any time to give yourself more of a challenge or breeze through a mission that isn't your cup of tea. Ramping up and expanding your organization, arsenal, fleet of vehicles and personal style is very satisfying. The customization options are some of the best out there right now. Most RPGs have nothing on the ways you can customize your look in this game. The fine: A lot of reviews call out how bad the writing is, and perhaps it's just a function of low expectations but I was actually pleasantly surprised. As I said, it's definitely not high art or a game you're going to play primarily for the writing/story but the writing does its job. It gives you enough of an emotional hook into the characters and stakes and a few chuckles and keeps the game moving along in a way that makes it satisfying to get revenge on the baddies and help/save your friends. The twist leading up to the climax was a bit wacky in how it was executed (although the core concept had potential if it was less ham-fisted), but that was my only major irritation with the writing. The game knows what sort of goofy over-the-top romp that it is and doesn't try to be something it isn't, but while story is a distant second priority to wacky hijinks it serves as a competent (if basic) scaffolding to hang the gameplay on. The I honestly have no idea: A lot of reviews focus on how this fits into the legacy of previous Saints Row games (generally unfavourably). The only other one I've played was Saints Row 3  (I think) years ago and I also had fun with that one but didn't think about it deeply which means its hazy in my memory. I don't have any emotional investment in the legacy of the franchise, and how this fits into the bigger picture of the series wasn't on my mind at all in forming my impression of this game. I'm coming at this with a mostly blank slate and treating it on its own standalone merits. If you've got strong opinions on Saints Row as a franchise, I can't personally make a meaningful comment on how that would colour your experience. The bad: While I had a lot of fun and my overall impression of the game is a recommendation, there is one part of this game that I did find genuinely frustrating and disappointing. This game undercuts its open-world concept and focus on customization constantly. This is most evident in the fact that the game mechanics allow and encourage you to build a fleet of vehicles, upgrade them in different ways, customize them to your desired style and vibe and generally have exactly the right curated selection of vehicles ideal for any given situation... and then the majority of missions don't let you use your own vehicles but instead give you a vehicle you have to use. Sometimes there's an in-story reason for this (the mission requires a deniable burner car, you're driving a client's vehicle, etc.) but sometimes there's literally no reason given. There are literally multiple missions where you drive to the mission location in your own car, talk to a person to start the mission, and then it tells you to drive someplace and for no reason at all the car you just parked is gone and there's a different car you have to drive. It's bonkers. I understand that this is done to manage difficulty and give variety but there are so many better ways this could have been achieved. Often it feels like the only job your toolbox of different specialized and personalized vehicles gets to serve is driving you between missions. The same is true to a lesser degree with your arsenal of weapons (although you use your own weapons much more often than your own cars). It's cool that sometimes they make you use certain weapons for the challenge or feel of the mission, and to let you play with toys you haven't unlocked yet but there were definitely times when I chose a mission specifically because it was a good opportunity to perform the achievement-style goal that would unlock the special ability of one of my weapons only to discover that I'm using a different weapon (and not progressing toward my unlock) for no clear reason. There was also inconsistency in when the game lets you use your own highly customizable outfits vs assigning you one that lead to me sometimes seeing myself in cutscenes wearing a weirdly context-inappropriate outfit (e.g. Wearing my motorcycle leathers and helmet in a board room scene because I had been driving a bike in the mission that cutscene was wrapping up) and other times crafting and wearing an intricate outift appropriate to an upcoming mission just to wind up dressed in something else by the game (e.g. there's a post-apocalyptic LARP quest line and multiple stores where you can buy cool post-apocalyptic clothing, but you can't wear your customized post-apocalyptic outfits in most of the missions where they'd be appropriate - you're stuck wearing the half-assed cardboard version despite the fact that other characters have more detailed costumes. Why even have all that stuff for sale if you can't wear it in the one situation where it's appropriate?). There are much better ways to handle all of this. The team who did a stellar job designing all of the wonderful customization options must be furious at whoever made the decisions that frequently undermined and ran roughshod over their hard work. It boggles the mind. You can take advantage of the customization a lot of the time and in a lot of cool ways, but there's a ton of self-sabotage and wasted potential in this regard. It wasn't enough to ruin my enjoyment of the game, but it definitely had me shaking my head in disbelief at times. The "culture war": The detailed character options include a lot of inclusive stuff. One element of this is that the gender of your character is very open-ended (it doesn't even ask your character's gender/sex, any character can use any of the body design elements and outfits, and the game is written so that nobody ever really refers to you in a third person way that requires a pronoun. Basically, whatever you have in mind for your character's gender identity and pronouns, the game won't contradict you). The ugly transphobic underbelly of the internet seems to be pretty mad about this. I've seen it mentioned (generally very inaccurately and unfairly) in a number of reviews, and it seems that there's some negative review bombing occurring based on this. To be clear, the game does not in any way stop you from playing a cisgender binary "traditional" man or woman. It's very easy to design such a character, and I'd say most of the presets look pretty cis. The only reason for a person to be mad about this is if they don't want others to have the option to design a nonbinary/trans character. Nothing is being taken away from cis folks here. I'm cis and I played a cis-binary character and there was exactly one brief line in the entire 60+ hour game where the pronoun vagueness felt slightly awkward from a writing perspective (it's honestly a triumph how much you don't notice it - I forgot completely). I've seen reviews that say you can't play a "normal" man or woman, and they're written by liars and/or idiots with a dumb culture war axe to grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Look...I know this is going to be an extremely unpopular opinion, but this game is actually alot better than the previous 3 Saints Row games (let's just say the 2nd was the last good Saints Row game)...which isn't saying much, but also, when you consider how badly out-the-wazoo the fourth and fifth games were...this was actually decent in comparison as it went back to the 3 gangs formula where everyone's at eachother's throats instead of going from a trio organization to some whacky cosmic battle crap.I will warn you; the game is an "obvious beta" situation so it may be a bit buggy, but if you can get past that, you'll actually have fun with this game. I said this elsewhere already, but the game just feels more grounded compared to the out-the-ass direction the 3rd and 4th game took, and it honestly does feel like a regular Saints Row game, gameplay wise. The characters, despite being completely new, were pretty relatable from my end (a very unpopular opinion, I know) and despite how sanitized the game was, it avoided being an obnoxious game with the constant double entendres like GTA.Unlike past games, the customization here rocks; There’s a variety of voices akin to Saints Row 2, and many other options that allow you to make your character feel the way you want it to. Very unlike Saints Row: The Third which kept shoehorning Troy and Laura's voices like every other game did (I'm sorry, but throwing out Zeus Mendoza's voice for Troy Baker's was just a total L). The weapon customization from Saints Row IV carries over, which I also applaud...not to the level the 3rd had, but still, it's better than nothing.If it hadn't been a reboot or had been its own series, or was actually given proper game development, I honesty think this game could have been a hit; taking away what made Saints Row, Saints Row, was a bad idea. It's an absolute shame Volition played their cards wrong...but whatever.I recommend you buys this game ONLY when it's on discount. Don't pay full-price, you might be disappointed. You might still have fun with it though!

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review, I completed the main story line and a decent amount of side material. I only encountered two main issues with the game itself (Bug or performance wise). First, I tried going to the helipad to spawn in my helicopter which broke the game, it had me zoomed in well over 200% while in the helicopter, so flying was impossible which made one mission unplayable until I rebooted the game. After I rebooted, I did not run into that issue again. Second, the optimization on this game is not good what so ever. I'm running an RX 6600XT and a Ryzen 7 2700 and even at medium settings, the game got EXTREMELY choppy multiple times. Choppy to the point I thought the game was going to crash, and each time it lasted for about 10-15 seconds. This definitely impacted my thoughts of the game since it did happen pretty frequently. However, after I validated my game files and launched as an admin, I didn't have this issue much at all for 8+ hours. The story was pretty good. I'm not a huge fan of how they stepped away from the original Saints Row crew or the backstory of the Saints in this game. With that said, I did enjoy the story. It was kind of nice to get a new spin on the game and I had a lot of fun playing. All of my hours in the game are from yesterday and today. There are some mechanics in the game that prevent you from just blowing through the story, which for someone who plays games like me is kind of nice. It made me go and run some side missions and actually do things to further expand the Saints Empire before I could move on. Overall, the game was fun and I absolutely recommend getting it while it is on sale. I'm not certain if I would recommend paying full price for it, I would have purchased for full price just because I love the Saints Row franchise. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, am I really going to write a massive review about Saints Row Reboot? Yes, I'm going to write a massive review for Saints Row Reboot. What a funny game to write a long review about - but honestly, Saints Row deserves it. I think Saints Row Reboot is a testament to mediocrity - the pinnacle of "mid" games, if you will. Of the many flops that have come out over the past few years, I can't think of many that have come from series as long running and unique as Saints Row. Initially scene as a sort of clone of Grand Theft Auto, Saints Row unquestionably carved its own identity through the entries of Saints Row 2, 3, and 4. Each of those games was a definitive success for Volition.Unfortunately, Saints Row: Gat out of Hell in a way permanently tarnished Volitions reputation (though, especially retrospectively, many of the core fanbase were more forgiving with Gat out of Hell's issues) with its poorer quality, and now that Volition is dead, it is quite clear that they never recovered from Gat out of Hell's impact. Their attempt to launch Agents of Mayhem as a spinoff series never landed, and after its failure, they set about attempting to reboot Saints Row. Unfortunately, this was a disaster. There are many fundamental problems with Saints Row, but here are the core ones that I would address, in order that I think they are important:1). The technical issues at launch. If Saints Row had at launch the stability it has now, I don't think Volition would definitely have died. I think they would have probably died, but at launch the game was clearly half-baked. 2). The way the game was advertised. Lots of Marvel style Whedonisms in the trailer, at a time where that sort of dialogue writing was really falling out of style. Many games got damaged from Marvel style dialogue fatigue as well, from Immortals of Aveum to Guardians of the Galaxy (though in the latter case it may have been unavoidable) to even, I'd say, titles like Forspoken.3). Severe narrative issues. It is clear that this game was rewritten multiple times, and what was finally delivered is a Frankenstein narrative made up of the corpses of a half dozen plot threads, none of which connect very well together. Its clear they were in the middle of full rewrite, realized that they didn't have time to finish it, and had to release... what it was that we got. While there are hints at some interesting ideas, very little reaches its full potential.However, even if all of these issues were fixed, I'm not sure if Saints Row could've succeeded without much better core content - a more interesting, interactive world with better activity variety. As I said before, Saints Row is a pinnacle of mediocrity. In the finished product, there is nothing really bad. The technical issues are cleaned up to not have any major issues. The characters are well written. The plot is there, and serviceable enough. There are a decent amount of activities (almost all of which involve shooting, driving, or photographing something). But we live in an era where more games are coming out now than ever, and a mediocre AAA game like the Saints Row Reboot has almost no chance of success. There are simply too many AAA games coming out for mediocre ones to succeed. To close things off, here's a funny coincidence. In 2006, the first Saints Row came out, earning a 61 Metacritic score. In 2022, the last Saints Row - the reboot - came out, also earning a 61 Metacritic score. The series really came full circle, huh?

For a criminal career in a game that is absolutely unforgivable.* Insanely spongy enemies, i don't know how to describe it but in previous SR games a simple shot to the head with ANY gun will give you a kill, now the enemies take like 5-10 shots to the face to die. _childDocuments_.review: Okay. So I want to start off and say that I sort of get why there's a bit of a divide on this game.Tonally, this game fits somewhere between Saints Row 2 and Saints Row 3. It's middle of the road, and doesn't succeed at being overwhelmingly funny, and it doesn't succeed at telling an extremely good story, which 3 and 2 respectively were pretty good at. It really needed to go further than it actually did, and I think this would have been a real classic.That being said, I don't think it's as awful as people say it is. While I encountered some minor bugs, they weren't as bad as people said. I found the gunplay alright, the driving alright, and it was fun to play overall. The only time I can think of the gameplay being bad was a forced stealth section, given the game has no stealth, and it never comes up again afterwards. Other than that? It was solid enough, and I was invested enough to get through the whole game. Well, I say "whole game", I ended with 47% completion.I think the game at least deserves more credit than people are giving it overall. I found fun with it, and it's not at a bad price atm, being only $30. Even more if you catch it on a sale. It's not perfect, it's not a classic, but I think it's worth your time. It's at least better than a lot of the more boring sandbox games that have plagued gaming for a bit.However, I'll say this: Give the game a chance. I see a lot of people give up around the 2-3 hour mark, but after you get over a hump in the beginning of the game, things REALLY open up and get more fun. I think that might be why it leaves more of a bad taste in peoples' mouths, that hump is admittedly tiresome to get through.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played all Saints Row games except the first one. And sadly a trend I see is them getting worse and worse.Saints Row 2 was a really fun game. Saints Row The Third was a nice and fresh breath of air to the franchise and really fun to play in co-op. When Saints Row IV came out, I played it together with a friend. It was buggy and much less fun with little new originality, but I ultimate still had fun.Now on the reboot. When it came out it received a lot of bad reviews, so I’ve waited for 1.5 years. Sadly, it’s still bad. It started of with a lot of disconnects & crashes. After some searching around, we found a fix, which is both limiting the game to 60FPS. It’s ridiculous this needs to be done, but it isn’t the worst fix and still playable. The bugs didn’t stop there though. We had to restart parts of the game multiple times and physics are wonky.On to the game itself. It’s a reboot to the series, but if this is a hint of what’s to come I’m afraid. It has no original characters at all. The story is boring, the missions are bad and the mechanics as well as the gameplay itself are boring and basic.I finished it, as it was doable in co-op because with the right co-op partner, every game is more fun. But during the whole game I had a bit of a sad feeling. So much wasted potential. Shooting doesn’t feel good, enemies are bullet sponges and the weapons are quite basic and boring while they proved with Saints Row 3, they can in fact think of original weapons.The only good thing I have to say about the game, is the fact that it looks pretty good at times and the city(although empty and boring) has some nice variety in it in terms of landscaping.I’m sad to make this conclusion, but this Saints Row reboot is not worth it. It’s buggy, has no creativity, and so much wasted potential. I’m afraid of a potential future Saints Row as they’ve progressively become worse and worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Haters gonna hate, but don't listen to them unless they have something more to say than it's "cringe" or "woke" - both terms that have been so badly abused that they're effectively meaningless when used as a pejorative. I see a lot of complaints about "bad writing" but these also fall flat for me - I found myself chuckling regularly at the dialogue and outright ROFLing at the LARP stuff. This game is a clear continuation of the Saints Row themes of finding freedom and personal expression in breaking away from the old institutions that hold us down and keeping loyal to your friends who truly have your back. Where once that story was told through the lense of 90's gangbangers, now it's been updated to parody the gig economy and blatant corporate corruption of the 2010's. The city of Santo Ileso is vibrant with life and full of little details that make it feel like its own place, a little of Albuquerque, a little Vegas, and a whole lot of gorgeous desert vistas that are a ton of fun to offroad through. Combat is a bit clunky sometimes but the takedowns are fun and range from John Wick brutality to Jackie Chan silly. Character customization is robust and the addition of the voice slider really lets you adjust your Boss to feel like yours. I suspect I'll be playing through this game multiple times to use different characters in cutscenes doing ridiculous things. (Someone shared a clip of the Tasty Creamy costumed boss in a cutscene and it was hilarious.)All in all, this game is great because it doesn't take itself too seriously and allows me to have fun with my game in whatever way I choose. High reccomended!

_childDocuments_.review: Saints Row 3 & 4 are two of my favorite games.  They're wild, coop-friendly, and silly as hell.This reboot is different, but definitely has its merits.  It's not as over-the-top as SR3/4/GOH, but still over-the-top.  It's not as silly, but still silly.  It has different characters, a different setting, and a different mission structure - but I like it.  I am surprised how enjoyable it is, given how many bad reviews this game has received.  It's not best in breed, but it's good enough.Pros:*Nifty mission structure with "ventures" - you basically choose what businesses you want to open, then you get a bunch of related tasks (e.g. when you purchase the clinic, it unlocks those "play in traffic" missions).  There are normal story missions too, ventures just kinda guide the random map stuff to a degree.  This replaces the "purchase all the buildings" or "hack all the places" of SR3 and 4 - doing missions to promote ventures makes you generate more revenue.*The Boss is still an idiotic badass - just a different idiot badass.*Lots of random crap to do on the map - collectibles are marked from the get-go, and provide either money, xp, decorations for your base, or all or some of the aforementioned.*You get "skills" that you can bind, which can be fun.  I like the skill where you bend somebody over your knee, toss a grenade in their pants, then throw them at their friends.  Throwing a grenade is also one of those skills.  You can have 4 active skills, and you get new ones every couple of levels.*Melee is still fun, works pretty much like in previous entries.*I like the story so far.  It's about a few amazingly skilled criminals who decide to stop working for jerks and start working for themselves.*There's a massive LARP-related plotline, and it was marvelous.  10/10 would LARP again.*Crashes less frequently than the previous saints row games, and is less buggy.  16 hours in, I've had one mission that I needed to reset to checkpoint because of a bug, and I've had one crash.  That's astounding for a saints row game.*There's a nifty kinda quick-action thing you can do in combat - if you're in a shootout and there's something near an enemy you're aiming more or less at, and that thing could explode if shot (or electrify or whatever), you can just hit E and you'll instantly shoot it without even having to aim.Cons:*Combat feels a bit wonky sometimes - takes a bit to get used to.  Probably because of the next issue...*Cant seem to be able to turn off aim assist - maybe because I play mouse/keyboard, but drive with a controller?*Speaking of which, menus get wonky to use with mouse/keyboard if you use your controller at any point.  I just pick the controller back up when I want to use my phone or browse at a store, but it's annoying.*Fire hydrants throw anything within 15ish feet of them about 30-40 feet up when broken - fire hydrants are the worst.  That might seem like a nitpick, but it isn't - they are everywhere.  Drift around a corner, or cut onto the sidewalk to get around traffic, and you'll seemingly randomly get chucked over buildings.  Absolutely my biggest gripe about the game.Other:*You can reorient the car to a weird degree while airborn - flips, rolls, just reorienting the car so it'll be pointed the right way when it lands - totally doable with enough airtime, regardless of the vehicle.  That could be good or bad.  Unrealistic for sure, but not a lot here feels like they were shooting for realistic.*There are "sideswipe" mechanics - you can basically shoot your car to the left or right to ram other vehicles as they pull up beside you.  Totally unrealistic, and I'm totally ambivalent about it - not sure if I like or not.*Drifting is..... weird.  You can drift forever.  I drifted in circles by just holding down the handbrake and right on the controller for several minutes waiting for coop partner to leave the gun store.  Never slowed down, just drifted and drifted and drifted in a great big cookie.*The early guns are really weenie - everybody is damage spongey for the first few hours (including you).  That changes eventually.*The notoriety system where you can have a wanted level with the cops and/or with the different gangs is back.  It's easier to clear than in some earlier entries.*All the characters are new - there's no Gat, Shaundi, Kenzie, etc. - it's a new set of saints.  They aren't bad, they're just different.  I enjoyed the old characters, but I enjoy the new ones too.It's not for everybody, and if you're super invested in the previous SR plot and wanting more you won't find it here, but I am very much enjoying it.  Given the tepid reviews, I am really surprised at how much fun I've had.

_childDocuments_.review: Errm... The f*ck happen with this franchise? I suppose I should start with the good. The story is kinda okay, though it's a bit underwhelming and short. So much bad in this game, I'm having a hard time trying to finish everything within the game at the moment. Now mind you, I beat this game all in co-op and I am trying to finish the rest of everything else in co-op, so all my problems have been in this mode. Some of it might be because I played/am playing in co-op, but a lot of it would more than likely happen in single player as well I'm betting. Anyway, while in quite a few of the main story missions, the mission would just fail randomly I felt like. For example, early in the game my partner and I were getting chased by a huge monster truck and we had to shoot it to keep it away. Well, it always got to one part and then we would just get ran over and had to start over. This kept happening for a bit till I guess we got lucky? That's when I knew the bad reviews may have been warranted. Other missions were bugged and we had to start over some of them and hope we get lucky. Another mission we had to look up how to get past a certain part because it kept bugging and we had to stay behind the vehicle at all times, don't dare go in front of it and that did fix the problem. Apparently capping FPS fixes it, but haven't tried the fix yet. It's a pretty long mission just for the end to crash us every time so very frustrating.The bugs, glitches, disconnects, crashes, freezing, sound cutting out warranting a restart, and hoping you get lucky is too much in this game.
