_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the thumbs down is perhaps overstating it. If I was allowed to, I would have given a neutral rating to this game. At the core of Saints Row 2022, it is technically a good, enjoyable game. There is a lot to do, and a pretty massive world in which to do it in. However, that is mostly all on the surface. When you get into the details of this game it sadly falls apart.We have all seen the complaints on the internet about how "woke" this game is, but the reality of this is - it isn't. Well, not unless your entire barometer for being woke is that there are characters that are not cool, suave white dudes. You will not find any stuff about how white people/men/etc are all evil here. The truth is there are a LOT of misconceptions about this game, and its cast. One of the main ones being that these four are just criminals to pay off student loans and that they're college students because of one throw away line they, for whatever reason, stupidly decided to use in the announcement trailer.The truth about the cast of this game is that they're just kinda ...people. And frankly not even particularly interesting people. Neenah's entire personality from start to finish in the game is "likes cars". Kevin is a guy who likes to cook, doesn't wear shirts, and knows people. The only real hint into his backstory is that as a kid he was an orphanage, and you only get this off of one throwaway side quest which is mostly a gag about limited edition fast food toys. Eli is the sole exception to this as you not only get to know him as the business mogul of the group, but also that he likes to participate in this city-wide LARP event and is essentially presented as the lovable dork archtype.You only get minuscule glimpses into the past of these characters, and for a good chunk of the game they're frankly barely there. You won't have time to hate, or grow to love them because despite the story being centred around this friends are family concept you really see only a tiny bit of them showing that. Maybe this is due to a small amount of main story missions, or what have you. Basically these characters ...exist. They're not good characters. They're not really bad characters either. And where this becomes a problem in a Saints Row game is where you're expecting these larger than life gang bangers, and what you kinda get is "what if you and your friends decided to become criminals one day". Is it a story that could work? Sure. But it's not what this particular fan base wanted.As for The Boss? Well, his/her personality is basically just "charming homicidal maniac". Same as it was in 3, and 4. It's basically the exact same character in everything but past history being acknowledged. It feels like Neenah, Eli, and Kevin are designed to attempt to be more down to Earth, and relatable versions of Shaundi, Pierce, and Gat as well ...but they lack anything that made anybody fall in love with the other three.There are more issues with the story once you get to the midway point of the game until the end, but to avoid spoilers I'll just simply state this: None of the bad guys matter, and the motive for the actual last boss bad guy is so comically bad I was just staring at the screen wondering if the game skipped like 20 quests worth of build up.Let me ask you a question. Do you like Saints Row 3? Because if you enjoy SR3's gameplay boy oh boy do I have good news for you. This is SO similar to SR3 it may as well just be DLC for it. Now there are some tweaks here and there such as the wingsuit, and the weird perk system that you'll honestly barely notice exists. But for the most part you're playing SR3 on a different map with different characters.Now the map? The map is fantastic. There is so much character put into this city ...and so little effort put into the things you can do around it. Rather than giving you a vast assortment of side hustles you do 3 to 6 times, you get a small handful you have to do 12+ times each. On top of that you have ventures, which are essentially other side hustles you do 12+ times each. On paper this sounds good, but there is a huge lack of variety. Pony Express tasks you with driving around on a time limit avoiding attention of cops. Towing tasks you with ...driving around until you can hook a wire to a car or object and drive to a marker without getting attention of cops or rival gangs along the way. Choplifting has you flying from point A to point B before connecting a wire to an object and flying it back. So on and so fort. So many different activities that boil down to the same general two or three activities slightly tweaked. It's fun, in a way - but also feels like busy work.The map is so large, but also so filled with these goes on way too long stuff that instead of coming off like Elden Ring where everywhere you go is a new adventure and you can't wait to see what you find ...it feels more like Assassins Creed Unity where it's just a vomit of dots on a map that you go to check off one by one until something better comes out and you go play that instead.That said, if you're the type of player who enjoys that kinda open world there is a lot to keep you busy here.Music is such an iconic part of Saints Row. Not only when it comes to popular radio stations like The Mix, the 80s/pop station in every game (except this one), but also when it comes to the use of music to accentuate the main story. Who doesn't get a kick out of the Boss and Pierce singing along to a song as you go to a mission. The characters are having fun, so you are too. Or when you have to save one of your homies in 3, and "I need a hero" starts playing, or diving through the alien spaceship in 4 to "The Touch". I cannot stress how important music is to this series....and then there's this. From a radio perspective alone this game doesn't even feel like its in the same franchise. There's no 80s channel. The hair band channel The Krunch is gone. No Reggae channel. Gen X is gone. Instead what the game has is very little in the realm of recognisable music. There are a few songs, and a handful of radio stations devoted to them (such as a death metal-esq kind of channel) but a good chunk of the radio songs are devoid of lyrics entirely. It gives the impression that they filled this game with music they found perusing the public domain so it could be played by streamers. Now, I don't know for sure if that is true - but if not, why else would you ditch variety in your stations?Music beats do return in a small scattering of missions, which is nice to see - but I found them to be less impact here. That being said, I'm not too into the rap genre so the songs used in these quests may simply just not be my jam.Saints Row 2022 is a conundrum in that it's technically a good game, but also a game that feels like it should have come out ten years ago rather than something that came out last year. There are textures when looking at a window that look like the kind of texture you'd see in an original X-Box or very early X-Box 360 game.The humor was toned WAY down in order to not only make the game look more modern, but also to remove some problematic aspects of the world of the game which wouldn't be as acceptable today. Unfortunately humor was kind of Saints Row's bread and butter. Be it driving through the town shooting people with a septic truck in SR2, fighting zombies in SR3, and largely the all of SR4 - this series is known for being ridiculous and over the top.This game is a game about normal people, doing a few abnormal things - but not TOO abnormal to be fantastical. It is a fine GTA clone. But in a world where GTAV exists, as well as more polished Saints Row games I'm simply just not sure who this is for. So while I enjoyed the game, and got 100% completion for it ...I'd struggle to recommend it to fans, and non-fans looking to try this genre for the first time alike.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the whole Saints Row franchise (one exception) and I've found this one especially fun. The side content goes on forever but doesn't get boring as it did in earlier games. There's cool abilities that aren't game breaking like the superpowers were but adds variety and flow to the hundreds of gunfights you'll be in. There's a plethora of challenges and upgrades to work on and I find them enjoyable as opposed to earlier game's content where it was just padding (Gat out of Hell). I think humor is good in many places such as the Atcha reviews and a few of the NPCs working with the Saints. Alot of the banter between the immediate crew is so-so, it doesn't bother me but perhaps they were trying to appeal to a younger audience (It's clearly directed towards gamer/online culture). There's many small bugs like NPC's getting stretched out to 30 ft long or the Y button infuriatingly resisting the player getting into a car or interacting with objects. I don't understand why it takes 2 or 3 presses at times just to get in a car or grab something when in GTA it would force the action like 98% of the time. Seriously if you're not lined up perfectly on something the character either takes a step forward and just gives up on the command requiring further presses or you'll get shot to pieces trying to get in a car and the stupid thing won't pull the NPC out of the vehicle. There are many scenarios you'll find this bug and why isn't it fixed by now? Why is the audio out of whack all over the place? radio will sound faded or sound effects sound tinny and there's really no place I've found decent audio balancing yet, and that's if it's not just wholly broken the other 20% of the time.The issues i've found in this game are unsurprisingly similar to ones I've seen in earlier installments - Occasional crash, ridiculous collision/physics freakouts, AI that is sometimes slow to react and getting launched out of certain heavier vehicles despite holding onto a motorcycle as if the character was firmly bolted to it in 10 different places. It's a long list but suffice it to say, I think it's worth the 20$ right now. FYI I bought most basic bundle and it actually gave me all the DLC, costumes etc,. When i logged back on next day the extra content was removed yet I was still in that disgusting gingerbread hooker costume until next logout. Some of the outfits are funny but I'm not sure why anyone would pay money for them and I don't feel the DLC's are worth original prices. Base game - def. Extra content - only if you want another 10 -15 hours of play tho I didn't find the additional content worthwhile... at all.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; dont listen to the negative reviews, its a very fun game with a lot of funny moments & matches the original 4 games in quality while doing something different. The cast isnt iconic but they are still well rounded characters with a lot of charm to them and so long as you dont take this game way too seriously, you'll have a really fun time.This game is pretty great and don't let the score dissuade you, This IS a Saints Row game, just a different gang, in a more ridiculous situation that ends up making the game more realistic while still keeping the ludicrous charm of the newer games. It toyed the line of realism & absurdity really well and its so far been a blast to play. There's been a lot of care into this game, but its so much easier to be angry so hardly anyone has noticed it. The Red Faction Easter eggs and the insanity of some of the treasure hunts quips are greatly appreciated. I can tell that the people who made this game had a lot of fun, and it shows.No one likes it when a series changes, but the story of the original gang ended 10 years ago, and people cant accept that & choose to choose to hate this game for being a different gang in a different setting. And a lot of people are mad they didn't get a remake of the first or second game, and if you read the negative reviews its almost always because they wanted a different game or a remake of a game that had its prime during a completely different era & their expectations were obviously not met.I admire Deep Silver for sticking with their guts on this one, they made a very fun game, and I think they did the reboot as well as they could have considering the fact that no one was going to be happy regardless of what they did, so they just made a good game instead.I played this at launch, and all of my gripes with the game at launch, are gone. It still has some visual bugs, but a majority of them are simply visual, they don't break anything, and a simple restart of the game fixes those if you can't stand bugs period. They even spent a lot of time improving the game since launch because a lot of the empire missions have been made to be quicker & less time consuming. Almost all of the time-wasting that was present at launch has been removed. Almost all of the problems I had with the game were fixed. And now I get to launch myself across the map with a dumbell cannon, its an absurd but down to earth game that's more fun than people are willing to give it credit for.Am I mad about the Epic Exclusivity at the start? Yes of course I am, Epic is a knobAm I mad that this is a story about a different gang than the original one? NoAm I going to complain about this game every waking moment of my life because its not a reflection of an era that ended almost. 20. years. ago.? No, I love the original 4, and I love this game too.All in all, if you're still on the fence, buy it, don't take it too seriously, and you'll have fun, and if not? It wont have killed your children like some people want to suggest. This is a great game that people want to hate because they find it easier to complain than admitting that a good game has been made here.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, then, it's time to talk about it.I've been playing Saints Row since 2006. Starting from the first title, up to this reboot that has definitively put a signature on a game studio I was fond of. I played SR 1 and SR2 endlessly, multiple times, truly appreciating them. A game that somehow aimed to emulate GTA but then developed its own characteristics, a compelling story, memorable characters, all in a more comically violent sauce compared to Rockstar Games' titles AND with a lot more customizable aspects than the counterpart, which was a win-win to me.I'll not mention SR3 and SR4, which in my honest opinion had already lost the shine and the true spirit of the Saints but were still better than...  But this game? Well, it's not Saints Row. Like many have said and will continue to say, it's the story of high schoolers who have to pay rent taxes. It has NOTHING distinctive, nothing memorable in any way. Or better, the only thing that is memorable is how much this game is useless. The lines are bland, the gameplay is uninspiring. The only thing we got is that we've taken a step back from Marvel Simulator; otherwise, we've lost all the characters we were attached to, the places and lore we were accustomed to, and in return, we got nothing. The Bosses and the Gangs are marginal, they don't even have a distinction in the missions, there's no depth even in the development of your own character or the gang, which in the end is NOT A GANG but a group of stereotypical Saints Row fans (?) who dance in the Church without any music and shout dumb things from their mouth.A huge disappointment. I hope the Saints Row IP passes to someone who is truly a fan of the world that has developed around this game series. Someone who deserves to restart it.Goodbye Volition. I might have preferred if you had closed down before releasing this steaming pot of mud.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where if it had been launched without a popular name attached, it would probably have been seen as a good alternative to AAA priced games. Lots of work went into world building (which actually works), setting up a story (which sadly falls flat), and consequently to the latter, the use of the Saints Row franchise works against this game.Instead, this should be been launched as a spiritual successor to that franchise - just 'clean'. The language has been sanitised, the humour doesn't really land (being both cleaner and cruder, somehow) but the gameplay is solidly Saints Row. Floaty cars, bullet sponges, over-the-top action moves.. Despite not enjoying this much myself, I do recommend it to people who weren't big Saints Row fans, but want something that kinda parodies GTA. Instead of being an underworld type moving to a new city, you're an eager beaver fresh out of college but stuck with no money in a town that's lost its opportunities. Go wild.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, all I can say about it is it feels cheap. I looked at the budget, and it wasn't, but most of my problems with the game were things that more money and/or time could have fixed. Insufficient characterization, because there's a whopping 2.5 missions per character with maybe 5 lines of dialogue per (slight exaggeration). The minigames/activities felt disconnected from the rest of the game, each gig/venture is run by a different npc, all of whom are given so little time that replacing them with wire-frame WIP assets would actually make them more memorable. In many cases there are skeletons of good systems, that come off shallow because there's either little content or little distinct content. Like every SMG and half the pistols feel the same, except for the pistol that functionally is an SMG. Despite all this I actually did like the game. The story, while too short and lacking in depth, was functional for what it needed to do. The crew were actually fun characters, a bit held back by the relative lack of meaningful dialogue and the fact only Neenah actually did anything, but fun nontheless. The customization was fun, punching people with a lava fist was great, but again, lacking in good/distinct options. 30000 flavors of T-shirt/Baseball cap does not deep customization make.TLDR: I enjoyed it, it's well worth picking up on a  decent sale. On the other hand, it doesn't live up to its predecessors, even when you can see the skeletons of what would have eventually exceeded them. Too bad it won't get the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... ok?I mean, it's not the Saint's Row you want it to be.  In fact, after playing for several hours there is nothing whatsoever that even says Saints row.Takedowns have a cooldownThe "gang" is basically 4 crunchy kitkat soys.  At least.. so far.  The entire game lacks testosterone so far.I just hope it gets better as I go... because, so far it's pretty boring.I'm still rating it up for the sandbox approach, the various missions and the fun of blowing NPCs up never gets old.EDIT:The further you play, the less it seems like a cheap knockoff of the original Saints and more of its own thing.It definitely is humorous in parts (the whole larping thing was hilarious) and the one-liners were entertaining.It 100% could have been just fine without them making Kevin a LGB DEI hire on the team.Towards the ending the game goes completely off the rails with a near-death sequence that is... ridiculously unrelated and immersion breaking.  I couldn't stop shaking my head.You get the best guns/tanks/helis toward the end in the spirit of most games in this genre.  Which, of course makes them pointless unless you're an achievement chaser or 100% completionist.The "hideout" which is a church (again... using the original saints script) isn't something you can upgrade or that undergoes changes along the way.  Once you wipe out the other gangs it just suddenly becomes "fixed" which is also a WTF moment.The game itself is fun, there is plenty to do.  The ability to adjust the challenge to your own liking  in the gameplay settings is a nice touch. The leveling system felt like it was just thrown in... the perks you earn feel useless and unoriginal just like the "skills" you learn at each of the whole 20 levels you'll max out before you get 1/4 of the way through the storyline.... yet still get EXP for each mission.All in all it's a thumbs-up.  I enjoyed the characters when I stopped waiting for them to be gangsters and settled on them being kitkat crunchies from Gen-Z that were surprisingly (and thankfully) anime-free.

_childDocuments_.review: New world, new characters same soul. I could just do a normal review, but this is my sixth review for this series and sadly, unavoidably, will be the last.  So let's judge it by the side activities:Not the ones the game got at launch.  Leave a troll review and thugs come to rough you up.  A quick combat bit that can be replayed to clear challenges.  Most of these activities can be.Not a mini-game you say?  Why that's nonsense, has not is always been one of the most touted parts of SR?  Regardless it's not as good as SR2, though it's a near thing.  I do miss the mall, but I'll take that loss because now I can change my appearance from anywhere.Ride sharing for assassination, what could go wrong.  Well, you'll have to progress the story to find out.Same as before, except now you can lay prone on the roof. This reduces the chance of accidentally shooting your ride.  There are more improvements, but it's fun and frantic in the way SR is.Get a car from A to B on a tight timer.  While I never lost to a glitch, as would so often happen in other SR games, I did occasionally loose to an enemy vehicle landing a profoundly lucky hit.  Game Over screens are cool though, as are all the transitional animations.Grab stuff from the air and get it back safely.  A brief series of helicopter mission that get you used to flying vehicles.The world design of Santo Ileso is wild. Hidden history tells you funny stories as you look at some of the cooler/weirder stuff the artist modeled.  That said the panels can be a bit too hidden.If trying to find panels was a little annoying, this is a .  It's not 'shoot difficult to hit/fast moving targets', it's 'FIND all the targets'.  Every gallery has at least one that is  well hidden.  The worst bit is there's a story mission that has you do some target practice and it's actually engaging. Skip.Out in the Desert there are Windmills in sets of five.  Find all of them and ya get something cool.If ya know, ya knowBla, bla, bal mandatory Superman 64 joke.  It's good fun, forgiving and these missions teach you how the wingsuit works. Couldn't, stop, laughing.Half inch cars, get cash.Rough up vendors and drive off with their food trucks.  I love the design of these mobile kitchens and getting to base meaning you don't have to fight your pursuers alone, chief's kiss.Drive trucks loaded with glowing potential disaster. Drive responsibly and guaranty a payout or fast and deal with leaking and exploding barrels.It's fun in all of them, though this one isn't as good.  Especially when cars despawn onscreen.These always begin with the boss doing something mundane (like speed dating, no really) when they get a call indicating a crime scene clean-up has gone all Pulp Fiction-y. The Boss sorts it with a plan and smooth driving.This is more of a major Quest/DLC, but it involve a venture, so I'm counting it.  The gameplay is mostly combat, but holy carp are these quests funny.  Yeah, I'm not bagging on LARPers, I am a LARPer, been one for over twenty years.  And I love this absurd parody of the hobby.  Ducktaping pillows to an SUV and calling it a monster is wacky and inventive in a way that would get any and real LARP's insurance canceled.Starts as a quest, then becomes a mini-game.  It's just a roguelike, PvE, battle royal.  Pick a character of 4 and engage.  It's fine.Get in a Tow-truck and repo stuff.  Swinging loads, wreaking stuff is a great use of the intentionally mad physics. This, like most activities, prepares you for a mission down the line.Try out impractical gadgets, usually by abusing unawares testers. Jolly good.  A whole lota fighting and bounce off towers. Great opportunity to clear several challenges at once.Taking pics of sometimes zanny materials. Snappy and I like the phone camera gimmick.  I'm quite fond of the Galaxy.Mayhem makes it's triumphant return and this time you do get some fun areas ideal for large combos.  But after three missions with the rocket launcher I must admit I missed the Dubstep gun. Obviously, most activities reduce down to ether shooting or driving as that's what SR is best at.  This is a good bit of both with some photography thrown in.  It also has a ark with a clearly defined first and last mission.  Also if, like me, you were bummed about Let's Pretend not being in this game, well, this venture will help. Wield the sledgehammer of humility, the crowbar of generosity or the crutch of self-reliance in a goofy 70s marshal arts move satire.  It's at this point I should mention I'm not a fan of Low/No Input Take-down moves, especially lengthy ones, and this quest leans on them super hard.  In summery, good but not cheesy enough. Demon slaying done wrong.  These missions have very clumsy gameplay requiring you to take careful aim with charged shots, while being smacked about the head by foes you couldn't see coming and badgered to use only charge shots.  This many targets in a mini-game about careful aiming simply ,  Ghost stories are hilarious though, two points.Do this quest last, not just because it's thematic for it to be your crowning achievement, (although, yes) rather because it's hard.  Very, very hard.  And much harder if you haven't truly mastered at least one of the traversal techniques.  Your jacking lorries that aggressively do NOT wish to be jacked.  You can try to approach on foot, via wingsuit or grab them with a helicopter.  All of these will be unlikely to succeeded and will take quite a while when they do.  I did however get great satisfaction when I finally managed to pull it off... then the game insisted I do it ten more times :(  This is a reboot of the original Saints Row, so let's address the question, is it better?  Then a 2006 GTA knock of yes, heck yes, are you kidding me?  The gameplay is fun, the physics are measured to be cartoony  and the gameplay focuses in to get as much out of the mechanics as it can.  Don't get me wrong, I do miss some of the goofier elements.  In places it feels lacking in modern improvements and it doesn't quite reach the heights of SR 2 or 4.  But do bare in mind when you think of best Saints Row has to offer, most people aren't talking about the original.  Heck all of the characters people remember and love(save one) are not in SR1.  Now I'm not saying that makes the game good.  I think what makes Saints Row Reboot good are the qualities I've covered, plus the characters(mostly) and missions(again mostly).  Especially the Main Missions.  It makes some poor choices to be sure, but those are the minority of the experience. To my mind that puts it in the middle of the pack, but hey, that's still pretty grand.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally enjoyed Saints Row 2022. Firstly I will start with the good stuff in the game I liked! I very much enjoyed the story admittedly its not the best most amazing story in a game but its still good and perfectly fine as it is. the game play and customisation is probably its two strongest traits though as Game play is basically similar to the earlier SR games and the character customisation is much more extensive along with other things able to be customised like guns, clothing and cars as well which is really what sets the SR games apart from the others. there are some decent weapons and melee weapons you can get in this SR game, the other great thing is the fact that it is set in a Fictional Nevada type setting which I Actually think is the best so far, I do love Steel port and Still water but I just love the wild west themes and the Mexican heritage and clothing also featured in the game I think this is what sets it apart from any other. now the Bad is that it has a really short story in comparison to other open world sandbox games I have played its not the shortest but not longest either, there is also a lot of problematic bugs in game which can cause issues at stages I had my clothing customisation menu freeze in the phone a few times and had to reset the game and some other issues which kind of nearly broke the game so I can understand some of the complaints which can be fixed with updates and patches but the game being woke is not what I experienced here admittedly there wasn't the same humour as previous Row games but I saw it as maybe because its different people in this one and a different setting with it being a reboot. I agree admittedly some of the bosses friends are dressed a bit lamely Like Kev and Eli. Nina is hella cool though and I was impressed with her heroics on the robbery mission and the cat has to be the coolest character :). there is nothing that I saw that was woke that I can really see in the game except for certain little things like certain humour no longer being present and toned down gang warfare. though taking over territory and killing the rival gangs and taking over is basically different this time round but still in SR style of game play.  I guess I went into this game with a fairly open mind and not expecting the after events from SR 4. I think as a reboot its good and not including it as part of the same universe as SR 1 to 4 still a lot of fun you can have with this game though and I did enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving it a thumbs up because I enjoyed my time with it. However, the overal experience of he game I would describe as "meh", it is very much mediocre.When I started the game the first things I noticed was the audio design, I wasn't sure if it was bugged or by design, it seems to be by design. All audio excluding voices and radio music is agressively muted, this for me personally disconnects me from the game experience. When I am driving a car I want to hear the car and the carnage I unleash with it, not the radio with wisper-soft environmental audio.This audio issues are presistent throughout the game in various forms, gameplay scenes are too often whisper quiet or completely dead. Imagine large shootouts with nothing but the gun sounds and barks of your enemies and player character to set the scene, put some music in to these scenes at least!The story is, as the rest of the game, mediocre. It didn't make any impact on me and the characters do not get enough screen time to properly flush out their character. I already forgot who all the bad guys are, I encountered the bad guys from each faction maybe twice.Mission structure is once again, mediocre. It lacks any long-term buildup to big showpieces. If the story reveals you are going to do a big heist, the very next mission after is said heist, no buildup, nothing. At least it had a train mission, and they never dissapoint.At least they did try to make the side missions more interesting, each one starts with a unique piece of dialogue or cutscene, for a few ventures each mission is also unique (yet still identical in structure), Still, doing the exact same "steal truck take it to dropoff" 8x I still very much consider to be braindead filler and not worth of your time.The game tries really hard to make the setting immersive, it is not. Its idea of immersive seems to be collectable audio logs spread as filler content around the gameworld.Combat is shallow, you have normal enemies with various levels of health, tough enemies with armor and minibosses with even more health. With some rare exceptions all these enemies follow the same repetoire, rushy-melee-guy or shooty-shooting-guy.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played the game on EGS, so don't mind my playtime, as I haven't started a second playthrough since but only messed around in the sandbox.Saints Row (2022) is a great game, it sits somewhere between SR2 and SRTT, with a tone that is a bit wackier than the former, but a lot more grounded than the latter.It may not feature any of the original characters (it is, after all, a reboot), but the new crew is rather charming, with Neenah probably being my favourite.It also features my second favourite setting in the series. _childDocuments_.review: Obviously, people love to ♥♥♥♥ on this game. It's not the best of the series (Saints Row 3 has that honor), but it's certainly not a bad game either. I hadn't played it before, but it seems the work on bug fixes was done well, because aside from some minor annoyances (like changing the color of some clothing and it resets by itself), I haven't had any problem so far.So, let's get this out of the way : I'm from the "Saints Row 3 is when the series got good" team. The first 2 Saints Row were GTA tryhards. The problem with trying to copy a good formula is that people have no good reason to play your version rather than the actual good one, since yours is done with less money and less talent. The only reason is refusing to join the bandwagon to be "original", and that's a piss poor reason.Many games tried to copy WoW when they realised how much money that thing was making. Guess who won. Jackie Chan realised he would never be better than Bruce Lee, so he studied what Bruce Lee did and differenciated himself by doing things very differently on purpose, hence the whacky stuff (said it himself in an interview). For Saints Row, it was clear that they would never be better than GTA at doing serious gangsta stuff, hence the whacky stuff. And that was brilliant, because as much as GTA's gameplay was good, the gangsta that takes itself way too seriously shtick was a pain in the rear. Glad someone offered a crazy, fun alternative.This new Saints Row isn't as whacky as SR3 (and far from being as over the top crazy as SR4), but it's not taking itself too seriously either. It's more tame, but it's not serious, if you see what I mean. For exemple, you have an app on your ingame phone to match killers for hire and people who want someone dead, and the app is advertised on radio and dicussed by journalist like real life ones would debate how Uber Eats is a risk for other businesses or some such. No giant dildo baseball bat, but stil some sillyness, just not cranked all the way to 11.I really don't understand why people complain about the characters either, or as I read somewhere, the fact that the story doesn't introduce them to us. I remember a TV show from long ago called "Friends" where those people had known each others for years at the start of the show, and no one was expecting the whole story to be told just so you get to know them. It was one of the most successful show of its time, by the way. So, back to this game, the characters are somewhat relatable, except, of course, the Boss, who kinda has to be a bit crazy and over the top, because if you were to relate to them, it would make slaughtering thousands of people too serious. If anything, those characters are far more beliveable than the previous crew.Don't get me wrong, I loved those characters, but they were walking clichés. Kinzy the unbelievably good hacker with social issues, Gat the absolute madman killer (in SR2 when we break him out of the tribunal, he's being judged for hundreds of crimes, FFS), Shaundi the absolute slut, and so on. The new cast is more nuanced. Generaly speaking, the whole  is more nuanced. I can see why, times have changed, it's alot more difficult to release a game as irreverent as SR3 / 4 those days. People would get offended, that's a risk for the investors, so they didn't... All the while forgetting that yes, there is a public for that, and yes, that's one of the reasons people loved those games. I, too, wish that they'd have the balls to say "♥♥♥♥ it, we're making that game anyway", but that wasn't to be. The funny thing is, people got offended that the game wasn't offensive enough. People...So yeah, basically we have Saints Row the More Tame. Still kinda silly, more so than many games, just alot less than previous installments. But it still has some "wild" aspects. It's been a long standing in the series, for what, 20 years or so now, that you can have a non binary, crossdressing, queer, whatever character. We still have it. Usually, the people who complain about that sort of stuff are also the ones to complain about "games driven by an agenda", or "leftist policies"(I've seen some poople complain that way about this game), but hey, in this Saints Row it doesn't even bothers the idiots ouf of /pol. Here, they'd rather complain that the game wasn't available on their favourite store for a year. So what ? If you really wanted it, you should have bought it, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ store we're talking about, not a marriage.The lack of consistency in complaints can be summed up with one thing : everyone had different expectations, and big ones for such a historic series, and of course all of them could never have been met, so people were disapointed, disapointment fueled their anger, and they ♥♥♥♥ on a game that doesn't deserve it. Not that much anyway. So, what do we actually get ?We have a nice open world, not the best or the biggest, but definetely better than the older ones. In comparison, it's not quite as usefully explorable as Agents of Mayhem whose open world design was damn good despite the small size, with real need for traversal to explore it and stuff hidden everywhere. We get a more convenient interface that still works alot like the old games, kinda like an hommage (fade to black everything, even though it's unneeded those days, for instance). The gunplay remains simple so as not to get in the way of the silly things we can do, so it's never a "git gud" issue. Cars to customise. Relatable characters (well, relatable to many, apparently not to the steretypical angry basement dweller). And so on.It's not as good as it could have been, so maybe buy it on sale if you have doubts. I certainly don't recommend the full price, but I do the same for evey game with that price tag. On sale, though ? Sure, go ahead. If a somewhat tame version of Saints Row is fine by you, do yourself a favor and get it. If you're not sure... Woe to you, then. Most of the reviews won't be of any help, as they are written by haters who will do everything they can to spite the game and are willfully blind to what it has to offer. Just because it's not the best game it could have been doesn't mean it's a bad game either.Now if you'll excuse me, I have a criminal empire to develop. And I'm loving it.

_childDocuments_.review: When Volition announced the reboot of Saints Row, expectations were high. The original series was known for its over-the-top antics and irreverent humor, establishing itself as a standout in the open-world genre. The 2022 remake aimed to modernize the franchise while retaining the chaotic spirit that made the original games memorable. After delving into the streets of Santo Ileso, it’s clear that the new Saints Row offers a fresh take on the series, but it doesn’t always hit the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game but felt lacking compared to Saints Row 2 and 3. Positives: Still a great source of mayhem and insanity with humor peppered in throughout. Controls are mostly solid. Characters grow on you after a bit and the overall theme works well for a reboot. I enjoy the new enemy gangs as they do stand out a bit from the older ones and fill their own niche and teh dynamics between each of them are good. I enjoyed how they aren't all allies under one roof and they do come into conflict with one another. The PMC Marshall as a faction works surprisingly well. The map and setting is also rendered beautifully for the most part, though I do think the island style of Stillwater and Steelport works best for open world sandbox games. The weapons and vehicles are still quite fun, and I like the wingsuit travel methods a lot. The goofiness of the Dustmoot plotline was done pretty well too, though I wish it would have added a certain character to your allies.Negatives: Some annoying glitches, but nothing game breaking. The leaders of two of the factions are kinda two dimensional, with only the Marshall faction getting fleshed out. The plot directions are also kinda confusing at times. Also lacks some of the elements of the older games that made them stand out, but times change, and so does humor. Gotta definitely go into the game with an open mind, and expecting some of the dirtier and darker jokes will leave you wanting. As mentioned before, while the map is gorgeous, island maps work better, as you notice where the clean rendering ends if flying around. The borders of the map come up on you quickly too. There are also a lot of plot threads hanging due to Volition getting gutted by Embracer. I also wish that the additional structures you got were a bit more fleshed out with more options to add all those decorations. Kinda sucks getting a tower with only the roof being accessible (with no customization that you could certainly spend hours finding).Overall, the game isn't the best of the series, but doesn't deserve all the hate it did get on release. There is still a lot of fun to be had with a lot of humor and lampshades all over, and it's sad that there probably won't be any more thanks to those dips at Embracer. (Personally, 2 and 3 are definitely better overall, though I would put it over 1 and 4), It's worth a shot if you find it on sale with the two expansion missions. Completed the game storyline with finding all the collectibles and secrets strewn about, and got most of the achievements. Only things left were some simple ones I forgot about, multiplayer ones, and one I really didn't want to go through the hassle to get.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe how youtubers have torn this fantastic game apart. I bought it on sale cautiously.Yes, there are bugs. But they can be worked around. The worst of all is the audio problem, but I personally managed to fix the bad balance, by setting the audio type to TV, changing the volume sliders to my liking, and restarting the game (crucial). The tutorial is an utter slog, as with plenty of games, but once it starts proper... wow. Overall it's more chill than the old Third Street Saints games, but I've played and love all of those since SR1 and still I love this one too.Sweet radio (especially the synthwave), fun arcadey driving, excellent car customization, built-in pit manouvering to get chasers off your butt, gorgeous graphics, a unique city, tonnes of destruction, awesome character creation, vibrant colours, the interactions between the new characters is great, if not quite up to the insanity of the old games, and sure, I miss those characters but these ones aren't slouches. The concept of clean cheats for fun that don't break your saves is brilliant (love the floating corpses), the explosions are huge, hydrants throw your car up into the air and the wingsuit makes it easy to get around. The Boss is stupid and funny, and the crew are all ultra-goofs, but that's just good old Saints energy. It seems like the missions have more effort put into them than SR4, as they aren't just 90% introductions to some boring side-gig.What the hell critics? Give this game a shot, enjoy the fun, imo it's been un-necessarily torn apart by the over-entitled who pick every tiny problem apart and don't look at the whole picture, and is actually, honestly, a gem. The only really bad thing about the game is that Volition won't see any of the money spent on it.RIP Volition, you actually did great on this one. I hope your staff go on to create spiritual successors.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, especially a year after release with all the patches and improvements. I bought it when it came out for a different platform and played it to 100% completion, and I enjoyed it so much I bought it again on Steam. So this is all from someone who likes this game.The star of the show is the world. Santo Ileso is incredibly detailed and populated. It feels like I'm visiting an actual city myself rather than playing through an approximation of one. The style and art direction feel right with the world design, the Southwestern United States theme was a great choice and they really nail the feeling of that area of the world. The level of detail is delightful and exploring the different neighborhoods and areas feels like it could take 30 hours itself before you got through it all. The main story is okay, but nothing to write home about. I found antagonists to be very flat and the various conflicts after the first few missions to be pointless up until the last mission. It's essentially a story about the power and bonds of friendship, which isn't new territory for the Saints Row series. But It doesn't feel believable since people as nice and friendly as the main characters aren't the typical people who are portrayed as career criminals who can murder someone without second thought, nor have the protagonists of the previous Saints Row games been this normal. The main four characters are as if you put healthy, well adjusted people from the real world into a world where it's a pretty normal thing to get a job with a deadly gang to pay your student loans and bills and rent with none of the culture shock. I don't think that was the best route to take overall from a tone level, but it isn't the worst decision anyone has ever had, it's just not what one is used to going into a Saints Row game. It's okay for characters to love each other and be friends and be generally nice to other people, and it's at least an interesting idea to put characters like that into gameplay like this.The Side Missions and Activities are the usual you'd expect from Saints Row, you've got your insurance fraud and mayhem and chop shop type things. There's a few new ideas added in for variety as well, but nothing outrageous or off color like what was in something like Saints Row 2. The brunt of the "be your own boss" build your criminal empire marketing is in this part of the game. It can feel like a grind with some of the things you have to do, but there are others that make it completely worth it, There's a large LARPing side mission that is so playful and funny, a real treat.The series has shifted its tone with this reboot. You're not sex trafficking or going to Rim Jobs anymore. This is a game that's definitely less irreverent than what came before it, which can be jarring. It's a matter of this game and previous games having completely different senses of humor. This game doesn't joke as much about sex, absurd events, or pop culture references, it's more interested in situational, every day occurrences in contrast with extreme settings types of jokes. It's a sense of humor that works with who the main characters are, and everyone's senses of humor are subjective so that isn't going to be to taste for everyone playing the game.Gameplay is good. Nothing much to report. You shoot or beat people and things, you drive around, you cause mayhem if you want. There's a wingsuit, reminiscent of the flying super power in Saints Row IV. Added car combat, both driving and shooting. There's perks, abilities, different little things to tweak your play like that. It feels good to play. This is the best character customization engine in a series with amazing character customization engines. Probably one of, if not the, best in general for video games at this time. I've been able to make my character look so much like me that it's given me chills. Voice 8 is the best one. The wealth of options for character customization is incredible, with the car and weapon customization being top notch as well. The amount of settings options is generous as well. You can really get into the difficulty settings and change it to your liking, change the volume of specific SFX down to separate volume sliders for gunfire and explosions, and so many accessibility options! It's small in the grand scheme of things, but it's all something I appreciate. The licensed music selection could've been more robust, there's a lack of a general "throwback" radio station (there's a hip-hop throwback station but nothing of the 80s/90s all genres variety) and I think the soundtrack suffers greatly from that. The score is fine, you'll find typical Saints Row the Third type music stylings as well as pieces that take from country western and Mexican music genres.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you a story.  Once there was a young criminal who had it rough growing up, and really liked to kill people and destroy things.  They found an outlet in a criminal enterprise, but they got tired of working for other criminal organizations and decided to form their own, having many adventures, and confrontations with other gangs along the way.   They started out small, doing side jobs like stealing cars, or starting fights with small groups from rival gangs, and eventually had enough money to start investing in properties (kind of weird for a gang, but whatever).  They, along with three associates, traveled all over their city, building their power base, getting newer better cribs, collecting rare weapons, filling their garages with highly customized vehicles, filling out a stylish wardrobe, and finding lots of sights and secrets most average citizens overlooked.  Eventually (after many turf fights, and a few pitched battles) they took down their rivals, including a corrupt corporation, and became very rich, powerful, and famous.Which game am I describing?  SR1+2, or SR 2022?  Because that description entirely fits both.  The people hating the game are likely those who wanted a remaster of SR2 (I'd have loved one), people who started the series with 3 or 4 and loved the absolutely over the top madness (I thought it made the games too silly and easy), die hard thugs who didn't appreciate being replaced by what I can only call disillusioned GenZ yuppies who happen to have zero issues with committing crimes to get what they want, or disgruntled playstation players who I understand got a buggy mess on general release over a year ago.  Haters gonna hate.  I even saw people complaining that the game left out things like insurance fraud and tank mayhem.  No, they didn't.  Both are in the game, so the person who said that didn't even play far enough to discover that before they started hating on the game.  I find that most of the people who hate the game never even gave it a chance for whatever reasons, as is evident by the example I gave.  Note the overall average playtime of most of the negative reviewers.  People who played for less than a day.Let's get one thing clear.  The boss (player) is entirely in keeping with the game series.  I've seen them referred to as the lost child of Playa, and that's now my head-cannon, because they are so much alike it's noticeable.  That aside, I personally did not mind the new direction of the secondary characters or missions one bit.  They don't all have to be clones of Gat or Shaundi (much as I loved those two characters) for me to accept them.  Different city, different people with different interests, different but similar story.  So what?  Not telling the story YOU want to hear with the characters YOU wanted it to be about does not equal bad writing or bad characters.  Frankly I think Playa and Gat were about done anyway.  I mean they became celebrities, president, a superhero, even went and fought in hell.  What was next?  Galactic domination?  Starting over with new characters was necessary, wanted or not.---------------------------------------------------------------------------So, on to what ACTUALLY is wrong with this game.A lot of patches and bug-fixes later, and the game runs fine on pc (can't speak for xbox or playstation players since I have neither).  However, while nothing game breaking (especially due to auto-saving) I have gotten crashes to desktop now and then, and have had to occasionally reload to fix a bug here or there (which reloading does).Multiplayer is a buggy mess.  Maybe it's the ping between my friend and I, but we gave up on even bothering with co-op.  Glitching through the world, animations not working properly, can't get in vehicles, npcs floating, can't interact with things you ought to be able to interact with.Compared to Saints Row 2 there are less customization options.  - Half the sliders from SR2 aren't even there, there is less clothing to choose from, and way less clothing customization options due to not being able to change the texture on any clothing item (unless you count the special materials you get late into game which I don't as all of them are something silly like coins, rust, cactus).  - There are a number of clothes that npcs wear that you just plain don't have any way of getting yourself.  Like something as simple as plaid cargo shorts.  Can't buy em, can't make em.  Same goes for several other normal clothing options that are lacking.  Including, again. shorts.  There is nothing resembling normal denim shorts in this game, just daisy duke shorts (for those of you who have no idea who that is, shorts that barely have legs at ll, and don't even come halfway down your thighs).- The variety of clothing is also questionable.  Good luck finding any pants that don't look unisex.  If you are playing a female or non gender conforming character, you are all set for clothes.  If you are a male player, have fun finding good looking pants that don't give you a woman's backside shape.  Having unisex options is a good thing, and the saints row series has been very inclusive, but having very few non-unisex options is not being inclusive.I'm sure there's more nitpicking I could do here, because I've seen this kind of thing with several clothing items, but the shorts/pants one is the one that stood out to me the most.Earlier for most of the game there were no artificial time limits imposed on anything.  Not missions, not side jobs, not anything.  It made for a great free roaming experience, taking my time, seeing the sights.  Towards the end game they start putting arbitrary time limits on everything.  Like less than 3 minutes to go over 2000 meters while every cop in the game tries to smash you off the roads.  Or wingsuit missions where you have to wingsuit to multiple buildings, kill enemies, blow up satellite dishes, launch yourself in the air, fly to another building, etc.  In under 7 minutes (oh and btw, if you fall you get to start over from the chopper - which is still at the first building, not the building you fell from - while the timer keeps counting down).  I get that it's the end game, and it should be more challenging, but some of the time limited mission/quests are ridiculous and frustrating.---------------------------------------------------------------------------Tldr; Ok, to sum up, everything else about this game is perfectly playable and enjoyable.  You may not like the style, story, characters, or available music, to each their own I guess.  Someone not liking some things about the game does not make it a bad game. Other than the issues I listed above I thoroughly enjoyed it, and feel like it's a better spiritual successor to SR2 than SR3 ever was.Would I buy it again so I could play it again, if for some reason I needed to?  Yep.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR 3/5Is this as bad as I expected based on what I had heard?  No, but let me give this faint praise.  I think that if this was not tied to Saints Row it would have been viewed more favorably, but as it stands it feels like a rip off of a beloved franchise I played this and SR 3 back to back and it's hard to see improvement from one to the other. 10 hours in on SR3 and I have more cars, more weapons, and more minigames.  I may not have discovered everything I could have, but if so that's part of the problem content only counts if I know where and how to access it.  All of that said, I am still having fun and graphically the game looks great, but it feels like a shadow of what could have been and a demonstration of wasted potential Bottom line. if you get it as part of a bundle, get it as a gift, or see a steep discount snatch it up to have fun for a few hours, otherwise stick to the classics.   Note I compare it to 3 not 4 because 4 quickly becomes a Superhero game, a blast in its own right but, a very different game from this and SR3.

_childDocuments_.review: Saints Row has always been the GTA we have at home. This isn't a knock against the series. The lack of expectation allowed the games to find their own voice and embrace a slapstick goofiness that the GTA couldn't really match. With no way of really topping the prior entry and no real narrative thread to pull on a reboot may have looked like the only way forward. While this game may not satisfy purists, there is a lot here to love. The characters and the banter between them finds a sweet goofiness that makes the mass-murder almost heartwarming. The mission design and set pieces rarely achieve the heights of AAA games from larger studios but finds enough excitement to last it's 20 hour runtime. Likewise, the city of Santo Illeso never matches the scale of someplace like NIght City, or Los Santos but has it's own distinct vibe. It seems we rarely see games set in the South West and the game does a good job of representing a region with a unique beauty. I played it with HDR enabled and scenes set during sunrise or sunset against the burning red orange sky were actually some of my favorite gaming vistas in years. In the end the rebooted Saints Row fits comfortably into that "perfect 7/10 rating". It's not going to please everyone but Volition made something to be proud of. It's a shame they don't have the chance to continue to build on it.

Fun but just a very weird game that kind of burned the sequel bridges. So they tried to go the "reboot" route with the new game and it just doesn't work as a Saints game. While the characters aren't terrible they're a bit too bland and "modern" to be really fun. I don't want to say the W word because that just feeds the trolls. The "modernisation" is handled pretty well and isn't too in your face or anything. I didn't enjoy the wingsuit mechanics at all and generally just avoided that as much as possible except as an occasional shortcut. The map is pretty large and  has diverse architecture styles, making the city quite interesting to play in. Much like GTA 5 it has a fairly big "rural" element but I think this map is quite a bit better. The cars and driving are very well implemented. Combat is pretty enjoyable. The writing is good and there's some genuinely funny content.Overall I give it a thumbs up as long as you don't expect to find Johnny Gat and the gang raising hell.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely not the best Saints Row game, but way better than I was led to believe. To me, it feels like Saints Row 2 in many ways, but made for an audience that values the goofy but welcoming fun of the later entries rather than the wacky but occasionally harsh grit of the first two. The comparison goes further than that. Santo Ileso feels more like Stilwater than Steelport ever did (and I loved the Southwestern aesthetic of everything, one of the best parts of the game was running around seeing all the little details that made it feel like the places I've lived, so that was a huge thing for me). Further, the story mirrors 2 much more than TT or IV did, where the focus is more on the individual saints again rather than the overall saint "empire". It is on the shorter end, but I enjoyed it for what it was, and the characters had way more charm than I expected them, too, especially the main three. Kev in particular is a character archetype I usually get annoyed by but he ended up being my bestie. Unfortunately, 2 was also a very strange, buggy game and this game honors that tradition, too, even having some audio bugs I remember having way back in 2 as well. Honestly, though, none of it actually took me out of the experience, and I was more amused than anything that they had somehow recreated retro bugs. Maybe it was intentional lol. All of that said, this game was actually pretty nice. It wasn't the showstopper I think a lot of people wanted it to be, and there are elements in the story and characters that I'm sure upset the usual reactionary goons, but if what you're looking for is a charming sandbox to run around, blow stuff up, decorate, and play dress up in, this certainly ain't a bad choice. Especially fun with a friend, too!

_childDocuments_.review: They made the main character some horrific looking humanoid in the art work and I'm EVER SO greatful that we can create insanely outrageous custom characters to play as instead. I honestly don't know what they were thinking making such horrible looking characters as presets.A very positive note is that the character customization is insanely good. The community sharing is equally as good but the only strange choice is not allowing you to download and apply a character appearance at the start of the game during character creation. Thankfully you will be able to change it whenever you please later on in the game.Another strange choice would be: Being able to change the size of your Bust or Package but not your Arse, hips, or any other individual area.Johnny Gat has been replaced with Kevin the completely one note social butterfly gymhead who hates wearing shirts.Johnny Gat was the guy you wanted around you as he would rush headlong into battle just to save you. He was a character that grew on you and was clearly the most like character of the Saints next to the likes of Julius andKevin, is the guy you want to leave at home as you'll spend most of your time trying to ignore his basic traits of I like: Cooking, Partying, Music and not wearing shirts. Kevin is also apart of the Idols gang because... uh, no reason actually. You will never actually see him do anything with the Idols besides shoot them and complain at you for doing that.Pierce Washington has been replaced with Eli the annoyingly overly nerdy businessman who has a very cringe taste in fashion. Other than being a mouthpiece for spewing reasonable dialogue sometimes, Eli serves no purpose. Because he is a nerd and the devs are checking off some sort of box, he is also annoyingly pathetic. If it wasn't for the LARP part of the game with him, I'd write off the character entirely. Shaundi has been replaced with Neenah the almost mary sue of the game. She amazing at driving, art, cars, history, lore, and planning due to her calm and cool-headed nature. She will bother you with things you didn't wish to know and there will be scenes of little importance about her CAR. She can seemingly handle just about every situation up until there needs to be a reason for the main character to do something. Oh and just like Kevin, she is part of the Panteros Gang and cares about what happens to them because... family? There really is no reason they need to be part of a rival gang.Rim Jobs has been replaced with Jim Robs and it's now based on the random character who drives you during 1 action mission. There is very little point in the change other than removing the fun little double entendre. If they were so focused on changing something that has existed in the series for ages, they should've brought back Semi Broken or just left the name alone. I frankly prefer the name Rim Jobs.The Deckers has been replaced with The Idols. These techno glowing wannabe daft punk idiots are just as annoying as the Deckers but somehow less tech savvy and more chaos, anarchy and anti-materialism. They stole the goons from Rage 2 and found all the left over Watch Dogs Legion masks they could and stuck them on the heads of Pink suit wearers. While I found the helmets interesting the overall appeal and vibe is so much less than The Deckers. Even the sex appeal is near rock bottom. I love the neon but don't care for the random blue-pink spray paint all over. It also doesn't help that ALL of the special enemy types are interesting but very annoying. 1 Shoots basically exploding stun nades everywhere, 1 spins rave sticks around blocking all your shots and not dying and the last one is the Max Alert mini boss that likes to party and summon help.The Panteros are dumb brutes of orange instead of dumb brutes of green and being called the Luchadores.The Luchadores are so much more interesting and their focus on heavy weapons & close combat melee make sense. There is only one interesting enemy type from the Panteros and that's their Max Alert mini boss. A Giant muscle women who attempts to kill you with a exploding sledgehammer. Everything else charges directly at you to die or tries to shoot you with launchers/guns.The Morningstar is possibly replaced with Marshal. Although it could also be seen as Marshal = STAG military group.Either way, Marshal is effectively another rival gang that are better at everything than anyone else. All of the units, cars, guns and tech are the cool parts of the game. Everything you get that is cool is either from them or DLC. The criminal ventures are playing it very safe. Gone are the very wacky ideas of Saints Row 2 and instead of have very basic missions that don't seem like enough time was left for them to be tested and improved on. SO many missions are shooting galleries and very little of them are different enough to be a break from the grind and slog of it all. A lot of them will change your equipment without warning or choice and other options are hidden behind a grind.The game requires very large increasing amounts of money in order to advance your Criminal Empire. Something you will have not completed before beating the game. I've beat the game and all DLC content and I still don't have enough income in order to full upgrade everything. And at a certain point your will to care about everything just falls off a cliff like the writers will to have a good story. The only thing keeping me going is the want for all achievements.The story is hardly anything that interesting and a bunch of it is copied from movies/TV shows.You spend a great deal of time dealing with 1 Big Bad only for it to be killed in a cutscene instead of a cool boss fight.The next big bad is technically multiple and are only required to be killed because they F****d around and found out.After that, you're back dealing with the same crap you did in the start of the game which are all extremely easily dealt with. _childDocuments_.review: A bit of a tonal shift from the last couple of Saints Row games - losing some of the more over the top zaniness which helped it stand apart from GTA rather than just be a "copy". This is a bit of a negative, personally, but not enough to be a lasting issue. As well, and this could be a positive or negative depending on taste, I personally like that your companions this time around are rather a lot more believable/relatable and likeable.From a technical point of view, it looks good, not amazing, but runs very smoothly. Don't think I've had any noticeable slowdowns at all and bugs have been rare, very minor, and always resolved themselves quickly.Gameplay wise, it remains GTA but actually fun/enjoyable to control, rather than focusing on realism even when it gets in the way of that. The gunplay seems solid and the cars, as always for the series, are completely unrealistic in the best way as, again, the focus appears to have been on making it really satisfying to speed and drift around in rather than blindly chasing real-world accuracy.I can definitely understand people being disappointed that this isn't exactly more of the same trajectory of the previous games but it's absolutely still a lot of fun and there is still plenty of recognisable Saints Row DNA here.

Some of the things like weapon upgrades are simplified which honestly I prefer over the modular upgrade system of accuracy, damage, rate of fire, etc. All of the activities are really good too. All SR games have that one or two activities you hate, but I like all of them here.As for the cast, I don't know what people are smoking, they're all very notable and I love them too. Especially Neenah and Kev, but I also appreciate the time we spend with Eli, even if it is mostly there to spite Gwen. I wish we actually had more personal stories with them exploring more emotional themes like Neenah's quests did.Again, I have no idea what people are on cause this has 100% topped Gat out of Hell and SRTTR and is my favorite SR title. And if you don't like it, I'm sorry that you have bad taste and I hope you have a swift recovery.

_childDocuments_.review: I am an avid Saints Row enjoyer and I don't think this game deserves all of the flak that it has been getting. Yes it is correct that it is not your typical Saints Row game if you are wanting to have that SR2 or SR3 feel again.Yes it is correct that there is some bugs including the audio and the way that all voices are so much louder than all other audio (although this can be fixed with a quick tweak of the settings)However this game still has that silly, goofy over the top feel that all SR games have had, it still has that chaotic fun that you are expecting when you jump into the world of SR, and most of all, even though it is a different feel, it still feels like it is a Saints Row game.If you have enjoyed the other Saints Row games, this still has that fun feel to it that you don't have to take it so seriously, it still has that broad range of missions and side gigs that keep you busy for hours. For the collectors, it still has all the collectables spread around the map ripe for the picking, sometimes even with a bit of thinking required to get to them. I urge you to disregard a lot of the reviews with less than an hours play time as the game doesn't really start until around the 90 minute mark. Give it a go while it's on sale, because for the $26 AUD price tag, its honestly a bit of a steal considering it is launch week for steam. Overall I would give the game an 8/10, would be an 8.5/10 with a few bug fixes and better controller support.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the Unsupported in the Steam Deck Compatibility box - unless it gets janky farther into the game it works perfectly without tweaking (although I did set the framerate cap to 45 in the Steam Deck settings to avoid any potential drops).I've spent a lot of time with this game on both the EGS release and Xbox and, while it does have some jank (I'm not a super huge fan of the physics, it seems easier to get launched into the air at any given time than in previous SR games), it's a perfectly good SR game. It's a little more grounded than what I was hoping but still wackier than the average open world game and there's missions and a whole DLC dedicated to Fantasy LARPing, which I now want a full game of. The customization is absolutely ridiculous - you can basically change the colors of anything you can equip, weapons have multiple skins, and you can adjust individual body parts and facial features if you want to make an asymmetrical character. I'm also a huge fan of the city in this game - lots of cool places to drive around and little pieces of lore and environmental storytelling to find. The new crew will grow on you too if you play more than 4 hours of the game lol.I've played all of these games, and, while this isn't my favorite one (shout out to Saints Row 4), it's still a very good video game you will probably enjoy if you like to shoot guys and drive around and do crimes. RIP Volition, wish y'all could have gotten to do another one of these.

_childDocuments_.review: Over all, a great experience. lots of great moments, and i had a blast playing it, but Man, it has it's flaws. Mainly, Netcode and bugsthis has to have some of the *worst* netcode i've ever seen. like, if there's latency between you and the host, not only will you lag, but so will the host, and the lag somehow just, keeps going in a loop and getting worse and worse.Sadly, netcode isn't the only issue, there are way too many game breaking bugs and crashes. it's un unstable game. sometimes missions won't finish, sometimes you can't get in to the car, sometimes NPC's get lost and softlock the mission (they accidentally went offroad and cannot pathfind). there's also some annoying problems with customizations (a big part of the game) not saving, when you expect them to, and sometimes they'll save options you didn't chose.that's just the tip of the iceberg of problems, and given the studio being shut down there's no hope of it ever being fixedthat being said, i really enjoyed the game. the writting's on par with what i've come to expect from the franchise, but don't hold your breath expecting to see any familiar faces. there's a few fan-service things, like the Ronin logo hidden in the church, but none of the beloved characters returned. not even Jane Valderama. so, don't come in to the game expecting a continueation of the stories from the previous games, treat it like a new start. When the customization works, there's so many options, but with how they're scattered, it feels like there's less than all the previous entries, atleast when it comes to clothes and character customisation items. but the vehicle customisation has never been stronger than this entrance, and cars feel great to drive too.If you can bear the bugs and crashes, i can warmly recommend this game, it's a fun experience

Welcome to Santo Ileso, a vibrant fictional city in the heart of the American Southwest. In a world rife with crime, where lawless factions fight for power, a group of young friends embark on their own criminal venture, as they rise to the top in their bid to become Self Made.

As the future Boss, with Neenah, Kevin, and Eli by your side, you'll form The Saints and take on Los Panteros, The Idols, and Marshall as you build your empire across the streets of Santo Ileso and battle for control of the city. Ultimately Saints Row is the story of a start-up company, it's just that the business The Saints are in happens to be crime.

Experience the biggest and best Saints Row playground ever created; the unique sprawling world of Santo Ileso is the backdrop for a wild, larger than life sandbox of thrilling side hustles, criminal ventures and blockbuster missions, as you shoot, drive, and wingsuit your way to the top.

Express yourself and unleash your inner Saint, with the most advanced suite of customization tools yet seen in an open-world game make your character, your car and your crew your own.

Dive into epic gunfights and highspeed chases, and witness outrageous only-in-Saints-Row moments in an original story that charts the Saints' remarkable rise to power. Enjoy the freedom of playing the entire campaign with a friend through seamless untethered co-op play, where you can both push the limits of your gang and create your own gameplay moments together.

name: Temtem
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game Temtem is an online multiplayer creature-collection adventure. Every kid dreams about becoming a Temtem tamer; exploring the six islands of the Airborne Archipelago , discovering new species, and making good friends along the way. Now it’s your turn to embark on an epic adventure and make those dreams come true. Catch new Temtem on Omninesia’s floating islands, battle other tamers on the sandy beaches of Deniz or trade with your friends in Tucma’s ash-covered fields. Defeat the ever-annoying Clan Belsoto and end its plot to rule over the Archipelago, beat all eight Dojo Leaders, and become the ultimate Temtem tamer! These are the floating islands where Temtem and humans coexist peacefully. Each island is a whole different world, but there is something we all have in common – our love for Temtem and Temtem battles! Intrepid tamers like yourself travel on airships to the furthest reaches of the Archipelago to find the best Temtem. Every young tamer dreams of becoming the best… Story Campaign : Journey across six vivid islands and embark on the adventure of becoming a Temtem tamer while fighting against the evil Clan Belsoto. Online World : The days of traveling solo are over. In the vibrant, always-online world of Temtem, tamers from around the world can be seen all around you, living the adventure with you, interacting with you, and fighting to become the best Temtem tamer. Co-Op Adventure : You will be able to join forces with a friend any time and work together towards your next goal. Catch new Temtem, complete a Route, or face off against a Temtem Leader; all while fighting alongside your friend in dual battles! Housing : Buy your own house at Atoll Row and decorate it your way. Buy new furniture, color your walls and you’ll be ready to invite your friends over! Customize : Customize your character to stand out from the crowd and get new cosmetics while you battle other tamers. Pick a silly hat, a comfy sweatshirt, some pants and you’re ready to go! Or maybe you prefer to wear a full-on cosplay of your favorite Temtem? Competitive : Start by choosing 8 Temtem and the pick and ban phase will begin. Take turns with your rival to pick your Temtem and ban theirs. When all the decisions are made and the turns are ended, you will end up with a squad of 5 Temtem and the battle will begin.

_childDocuments_.review: //I wrote a positive review for this game during early access, praising its fun Pokemon-like experience enhanced with co-op, quality of life changes, and some MMO features. Now with 230 hours of game-time and nearly 3 years of perspective later, here are my updated thoughts.//The declining state of Temtem is currently a contentious topic within the community, but for most players boils down to three factors: (1) ENDGAME (or lack thereof), (2) MULTIPLAYER EXPERIENCE, and (3) INTERACTION WITH THE DEVS. Here's a quick summary of the issues.(1) ENDGAME: Grindy and unrewarding (not to mention RNG-based rewards). Essentially just time sinks that honestly feel pretty disrespectful to players' time. (2) MULTIPLAYER: This game positions itself to be a Pokemon-like/creature collector MMO, but comes with a pricetag, lacks a stream of content, and only has PvP otherwise (which is hit or miss depending on player preference). (3) DEV FEEDBACK: Many have taken issue with the devs mentioning that there are currently no plans to add new tems, greedy pricing of in-game cosmetics, and a consistent feeling of ignored user feedback. As a long-time player, it's honestly really sad to see the issues I pointed out in my review 3 years ago have only gotten worse. I really enjoyed my playthrough, but after playing religiously every day, I came to a point there was nothing but a monotonous grind left to do with rewards that didn't feel worth the effort, and the release of new story wasn't enough to excite me to pick the game back up. This is a gameplay loop that I unfortunately can't recommend it to anyone else. However, if you have a friend and wish to do a co-op playthrough with no regard for endgame grinding, I think it can still be a fun experience because of some quality of life changes over a mainline Pokemon game**. Just don't foolishly expect this to be the Pokemon-like MMO of your dreams. **In addition to being able to play with your friend, I find that these additions make for a uniquely fun experience I haven't seen elsewhere:-You get a 1 time use full party-wide heal that recharges at Temporiums (pokecenters), total GAME-CHANGER as you adventure through the world.  -Moves all have 100% accuracy and critical hits are removed (for those who find RNG frustrating).-All battles are double battles and use a Stamina mechanic instead of PP that essentially adds more levels of strategy and make playing with a friend possible and fun. -Every available Tem can be obtained through catching, breeding or player trading (though given the state of the game, I wouldn't recommend sinking that kind of time)
