_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is a lot of fun with a lot of potential. Comparisons to Pokemon will be inevitable given the numerous similarities, however I think the game is strong enough to stand on its own two legs. Temtem uses a stamina system rather than the "PP" system governing creature movesets in battle. Stamina replenishes between fights meaning you will not run out of PP across numerous trainer fights, but is limited within a single given fight meaning you cannot spam a single move constantly in battle. In my opinion, this leads to a more strategic approach. All battles are based on a two v two system rather than the primary one v one system of Pokemon, and the status effects within Temtem have been modified relative to their Pokemon equivalents. All of the changes and differences are - I feel - improvements to systems in Pokemon that have become stagnant pain points.The most significiant drawback is probably the limited variety of Temtem in given areas. In Pokemon, you have a large budget behind the game allowing hundreds of Pokemon per game. In Temtem, you will go through an entire "cave" (or fort, or area, whatever) encountering the same 1 - 3 Temtem. If I see another Skail I may snap my keyboard in half. However, given that the game is still in Early access, and that expansions have begun to already bring new Temtem to the table, I expect this issue will disappear with time.

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously writing this review early on, right after release in EA, so go easy on the game.As of now, I've launched the game twice and waited 10ish minutes to play.  Guessing it'll go down a lot as the devs work on sorting it out, but for the 12,000 people it shows queueing at first it's not so bad.The first attempt, I got through customizing and some early cutscenes before it froze walking through some tall grass (assuming I ran into a Temtem.). Enjoyed the look and feel, easy to get into and well laid out.Second attempt at booting I was pleasantly surprised to see that yes, I had run into a wild Temtem, and it had saved right as the battle had started.  Small critisism is that it didn't tell me what to actually do to capture; so thinking it was like its inspiration, I knocked it out expecting an option to catch.  But no, I had just knocked it out cold and wandered on.  Small tutorial here would be nice.  Afterwards I got in several more battles, before it crashed again while interacting with a tamer.  Currently booting it up again.As of now, ignoring the crashes inherent in any early early access... It's splendid.  The character design is sweet, Temtems I've encountered so far look great, battling is fun... I'm excited for what's ahead for this startup, and wish the devs the best of luck sorting through the immediate bugs over the next few days.  Will be updating as I continue.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just isn't getting any better with updates.  The changes that they made in the latest update looked promising, but overall do nothing to change the core issues with the game's MMO design.For the positives, I genuinely enjoy battling in this game way more than in Pokémon.  Since the game is entirely double battles, each individual encounter has a greater degree of strategy than your typical Pokémon title, which ensures that every encounter isn't just a roadblock but rather an actual challenge.  The switch from PP to Stamina, changes to priority, and introduction of Holds allow for far more variety in move design which makes each decision in battle far more involved than in Pokémon.  Co-op mode is also just an absolute blast, and is absolutely worth doing if you can get a friend to join you.  If the devs focused more on these aspects of the game instead of worrying about the player economy, then this game could be incredible.As for the negatives...  It seems like every system and mechanic that is in service of the game's MMO side only serves to bring down what would otherwise be an amazing solo/co-op game.  The expensive player cosmetics, drip feeding currency, and excessively restrictive breeding system all serve to make the game far more grindy and less enjoyable, which doesn't seem to serve any purpose since there aren't even any microtransactions (yet).  With the dev's roadmap already set, it seems like they are also entirely unwilling to hear out any player feedback that isn't simple bug reporting.  It seems like they already believe that such criticism will disappear as the game becomes more complete, but no update to date has fixed the major design issues that the game launched with.  Anytime they do respond to player feedback ends up being just a token gesture, since it never goes far enough to resolve the issues that players have.  Each new update often will included some new system or feature that is clearly lacking in some critical way.  For example, the Koish hunting they added for the follow-up Kisiwa update features the exact gameplay loop as Luma hunting, since all you are doing is farming encounter after encounter until RNG gives you what you want.  This makes the feature slow, tedious, and entirely redundant since there is already a system that works in this way.  Meanwhile, actual PvE battles, like those you have throughout the bulk of the story, are almost entirely lacking from any endgame content, despite the fact that is what makes up the core gameplay loop.  The devs clearly don't understand why the bulk of thier players stop playing after exhausting the story content.The newly added raids feature a different kind of problem.  Simply put, it is a cooperative challenge that requires a group of players (each in the own separate gameplay instance without any direct interaction) to win a series of battles to get enough resources to unlock the fight with the lair boss.  Unfortunately, losing one of these fight will make a player have to spend that same resource to revive, which almost always means that the raid attempt will fail since you won't have enough to unlock the final fight.  This means that it is entirely possible for a single player to grief an entire raid by simply being bad, or even just unlucky if the get a bad team composition.  Not only did they learn nothing from Pokémon's raid problems, they made them somehow even worse.In short, while this game has elements that are a ton of fun, too many elements of the game's design feel outright hostile to casual play. _childDocuments_.review: Temtem is a pretty fantastic game, despite some of it's issues it is definitely still far more playable then some other comments might suggest. Some of my gripes include, the "MMO style" which really doesn't add to the experience and in some instances detracts from it; the world is really colorful and dynamic but it doesn't help when 10-20 players are all funneled into one area. That really shows in places like the first gym of the game and in some random areas. As well as a lack of a offline mode for players who were thinking that this game would be playable offline. Also their are several bugs that happen at random / near the end of the game which may cause concern. Specifically in a section with Trainer battles and them seemingly having trouble actually reaching you (for awhile approximately 50s more or less) or say your lead mon becoming entirely stiff seemingly reverting to it's Skylander form. But aside from those game play issues for those thinking about the main story it's great the fights can be challenging depending on the situation. Now as for the story as it is, it's serviceable. Fun, and the world around the story is interesting. The dialogue options are generally not terrible and allow you as a player to express yourself through the eyes of the MC a bit more. However though certain characters do can come off as "just annoying" when the writers intend for a more "funny / endearing" character OR said character is implied to be something more to the MC (which btw is your self insert) and it can be really jarring sometimes. But that doesn't mean you won't find several really fun characters and interactions between some hundred plus npc littered throughout the world. Overall the story of Temtem is a simple but fun and interesting tale with a few twists and epic encounters. As for End game and PVP which I will address the former first. It is "okay" for those looking for a PVE experience, however my personal hope is that Crema will add more either in Story or in Afterstory/Endgame content because as enjoyable as dungeons and raids can be... I don't see it carrying the larger player base forward into the future. But who knows for sure, apparently Crema is done adding new islands to the game and their is no roadmap as to what's to come.  But as for PVP and as of writing this, it is a beautiful and fantastic experience. With the advent of "Showdown" it's just the saving grace for an otherwise lackluster process of getting to play at a high level or at all. It's honestly quite balanced, even the "Meta" Tems feel really tame if not as good as others going on a "game to game" basis. If you want a beyond enjoyable doubles scene PLEASE give this game a go. Their are no words for how much I personally enjoy it. However I will say that their should be more PVP formats more specifically a way to play 2v2s, and maybe even singles. [Note: Their are Dojo/Clan wars, but I have not participated in them and won't talk about them respectfully]Overall this game is a 8.47/10 definitely buy it if this sounds interesting to you OR wait for a sale if you're a riding the fence about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredibly similar to Pokemon. It's a very well made game that feels pretty polished now that they've fixed the server issues. They aren't afraid to be "too similar" if Pokemon did something the right way, but they've also added their own flavor.It’s all duo matches (most high level Pokemon pros have said that’s a much better format, singles has a lot of rock paper scissors issues and duos avoids same move spam and some other silly situations as well). Instead of each ability having a number of times it can be used, Temtem have one stamina bar which drains a different amount when you use different moves, and regenerates when you wait a turn. If you over-use your stamina, you will damage yourself, and have to wait a turn afterward.There are also affinities, so certain moves do better when you have a certain type of Temtem as a partner fighter. Also there are combo moves that can only be used before/after certain other moves. It's all communicated in a very visually simple way, so it's all very intuitive, but these additions make the combat feel more dynamic than the pokemon games I used to play (It's possible these features were added in later pokemons, not too sure).Make no mistake, the launch was not smooth sailing. In the first few hours there were a lot of disconnects and lag. They were being DDOSed (par for the course sadly, for an MMO) and also struggling to cope with the sheer number of people who signed up on launch day. However, they dealt with it as good as any dev I've seen.There were multiple tweets per hour, all day long, informing us of exactly what they were up to. Exactly what the state of their internal build was, what they still had to do, when they planned to fix it, and what could possibly go wrong. It's just absolutely stellar communication. I wish we could have this from every dev.When the tweets finally stopped for the night, they did so for only 5 hours before starting up again, letting everyone know the exact state of things and their plans for the next day.They had the major issues fixed within about 5-6 hours I'd say. By then the game was very playable, just with the occasional DC. At this point it's pretty much smooth sailing.Tldr: buy Temtem. If you liked Pokemon or never played it this is the best modern incarnation of it.

_childDocuments_.review: ~Complete Guide to everything wrong with Temtem so far~I can no longer recommend this game to serious gamers because of the culmination of issues which have been piling up since the game started; all of which could've been avoided entirely. Most of these issues are not mentioned elsewhere so I find it important that you're at least aware of what you're getting yourself into. Scroll down if you're interested in the current state of the game, and please note that the in-game chat doesn't even work. As of now, the Official Discord serves as a temporary replacement for important MMO features such as the chatting and trading aspects, and should therefore be considered as part of the game atm.--- DAY 1-3: ---- Everyone playing through the story, some finishing it very fast. A breeding guide of how to breed perfect Tems was posted on Reddit and went viral, making perfect SV breeding very easy for everyone. SV = innate stats, max = 50 (Like the 31 IV of Pokemon). 7 50 SVs = perfect.-An item called Fertility Enhancer, widely asked by Alpha players to remove it from the game, still made it into EA. Early merchers bought these up from clueless players, and used them for perfect Tem breeding which allowed them to breed a bunch of perfect SV Tems.- On the Official Discord, the single #trade channel started getting spammed (300+ msgs per minute & slowmode which didn't really do anything) with mostly these perfect Tems and Fert enhancer offers, + some luma sales mixed in. The devs/mods did nothing against this during this period.- Again, merchers benefited by haggling clueless players out of these commodities and started flipping them, hoping to rip off clueless players yet again by charging premium prices. This worked because everyone gets ~100k cash by clearing the story, essentially turning every player into "single use ATMs" without game knowledge and the hype for perfect SV tems / lumas was at its peak, understandably.-Some merchers went so low that they changed their Discord display name to something feminine and avatar / profile picture to a "cute girl". They made at least 50k an hour for potentially a few days worth of time doing this, and ended up with millions of cash. The only other way to make money was catch/releasing tems, which was ~3k/h at the time (aka actually playing the game and Discord not being mandatory).-Breeding items which guarantee that SVs carry over from the parent to the child initially entered the game at 300 cash per single SV item, and 1000 cash per item to carry over 2 SVs. This was changed in a "ninja patch" on the end of this first period; the prices became 1k for each single SV item and 5k for each 2 SV item. The merchers who had all the freedom (no enforced regulations) to rip players off for a couple days likely spent those millions of cash on these breeding items before the price increase because they were spam breeding while 'merching' (ripping people off).--- DAY 4-7: ----Devs/mods split up #trade channel into several channels and enforced a 1 hour per msg slowmode. This, along with the breeding changes, killed the "3rd party app market" and made people look for the most efficient catch/release cash per hour; this became ~6k p/h rather than 3k.-With everyone now doing the same thing, and so many perfect SV Tems having been spam produced already, prices of everything rapidly declined. Fertility Enhancer was also removed in another ninja patch. Breeding is still profitable, but some gender RNG is required. The meta Tems and best catch/release spot luma Tems especially declined in price by the day.-This caused a major conflict with a quote of the Temtem store page's EA description: Breeding became too expensive for most players after the price hike, "Luma hunting" = 1/6000 chance so not really huntable, and competitive = dead because of the discrepancy between alpha players / streamers / those who took advantage of day 1-3 dev fails VS the rest.---DAY 8-NOW: ----Due to catch/releasing being the only way to make money in-game, market saturation of the lower end stuff reaches its peak. 1/2 50SV caught tems may as well be released now because they barely sell for more due to everyone offering them. They're also required for breeding so you store them in this case, which eats up very limited stash space. This makes the catch/release grind even more tedious, especially since those 1/6000 luma encounters are also devaluing by the minute.-As expected, more and more complaints start to roll in about lack of endgame content on social media and in the #competitive channel. This could take a long time, because to sum it up: -Mods/devs refuse to pin info on Discord's #competitive that's obvious to the more serious players by now, and with said lack of content, the conversations in there tend to become a loop of the same stupid questions being asked over and over along with the topic mostly being said complaints about the above mentioned issues. This adds to the frustration of the constant value declining in-game grind repetition.--- Personal opinion ---For me, experiencing this was like watching a trainwreck happening because I instantly noticed all of the issues which the devs patched out later on (too late). The game was released as EA too early, containing glaring issues and not enough content variation for serious players to test out and improve/bug fix. The total lack of a battle tower or anything like that in a monster collecting battle sim is the biggest issue. I expected that much from a game which has been playable in Alpha for 13 months already as the EA starting point at least, so that we could scout for bugs and improve its system as EA goes on.We did not get enough storage space. Many players have reached the point of all their boxes being full already, due to the amount of Tems which are required for a perfect Tem breed setup. With competitive battles requiring at least 8 Tems, there should've at least been 20 boxes instead of 10. It's a huge chore to perform microscopic sorting on your Tem storage all the time.I also find certain things making it into EA regardless of alpha player feedback a major issue regarding the understanding of the devs, like the fert enhancer:  (posted on 16 Dec 2019). I advise you to read through this entirely. It does not bode well for the future, imo. Especially when you consider things like an auction house being implemented in the future & the HUGE amount of capital which said merchers have made by exploiting the dev's silly decisions, allowing them to control the market all the way up to when that happens & then control AH as well.Lastly, the official Discord is a major issue. Most of the people in #competitive are rather obnoxious (e-peen types) and/or have that "I say this so you can't possibly be right" attitude, and all of the channels aren't moderated properly at all. By not regulating It also created the platform for bad design abusers which has already destabilized the economy before one can even be truly formed.Most of this is inexcusable, seeing as the devs said there won't be any wipes or rollbacks from the start of EA. My expectation is that this game won't be good enough for competitive people who can spend a lot of time on a game, but is rather suitable for casual players and parents who are looking to play this with their kids. I do hope that the future will prove me wrong, because I really liked the game at the start (went in skeptical, even). It just doesn't look like that'll happen based on the devs inexperience with running an MMO style game and their crucial decisions made so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Good as a standalone singleplayer experience, not worth $45. Deluxe being $20 more is insane. Bought it when it was much cheaper during early access. Playing through the campaign was a very fun experience for me, there is a really solid game here to be played. I'm a big fan of monster taming games, and this would have been one of the best indie taming games in my eyes.Drawbacks are the high upfront cost for an always online game that the developers will no longer update with new tems or maps. The development team has explicitly stated they do not feel they have the financial incentive to improve TemTem with more content, nor are they "contemplating an offline mode at this time". They are promising at this point in time that they will keep the game online for a very long time due to game design around low server costs. A reminder, though, that this game is only supported by the upfront price and no MTX / subscriptions to offset these costs.I would encourage reading their statement about the game here from a month ago:I could see the $45 pricetag being justified if they implemented a way for players to play offline alongside an "official" server to isolate cheaters and modders. With a game centered around investing all your time finding and improving your favorite mons, feeling that your progress may simply be erased when the servers shut down is a huge draw to wanting to put time and money into a game.If you have money to burn and see a $45 always-online massively multiplayer game on life support as a good use of your money and time, I say go for it. When this game was $15 cheaper and as promising for the future as it seemed during early access, I probably would have recommended it to anyone interested as well. Now I could only recommend it if you could find it somewhere cheap, at around $20 or less due to the state of the game.TLDR: Very well made and fun game, very anti-consumer state of the game and state of development. Would be worth the price with the ability to play offline.

_childDocuments_.review: Having two Temtem in battle allows for so many more strategies than if you were limited to one at a time, and having Stamina makes leveling up my team so much easier. The ability to have your Temtem rest for a turn is also really nice for when you're trying to catch a Temtem, so you don't knock it out. Speaking of catching Temtem, it doesn't have to be alone to be caught! The amount of convenience from Stamina refilling at the start of a battle and being able to catch Temtem from a group is so refreshing. Synergy, holds, and managing Stamina against surprisingly smart AI works alongside these conveniences, which makes it such a fun strategy-based game. Overwriting techniques doesn't have to be a massive decision since it's free to relearn them anywhere. No costs, no traveling to an obscure location to talk to someone that's inexplicably the only person that can re-teach Techniques... just a few buttons, and you have the moveset you'd like. Having your lead Temtem follow you outside of battle is a lot of fun. The amount of character customization at the start lets me feel unique as a player. Starting out staring at the same character model literally everyone else did (until I find a shop with few clothes and even fewer color variations) is gone. I doubt the variety would leave anyone disappointed with their starting look. Even the Temtem themselves are all unique and charming, and I'm eagerly awaiting the full release so I can start hunting for Lumas. I'll just have to find my Luma Skail again, but I don't mind!(The Lumas are so beautiful too! Their soft glow, 3 perfect stats... they're more than a few shades lighter or darker; their colors noticeably change while still looking really cool.)I've encountered a glitch where Techniques that have holds are available from the start of the battle, and my Stamina isn't refilled. The Chat section is also absent, and the box in the settings immediately un-checks itself when I try to toggle the option. There's also two very minor typos; the Aggrieved Local with orange hair and the person that stops you from entering the Arissola Dojo are both missing a space in their dialogue. The audio gets very crackly and there's some impressive lag every once in a while, but it's likely a result of my hardware being closer to the lower end. Nothing game-breaking, though!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys and is very familiar with the Pokémon franchise of games, I greatly enjoy Temtem. It scratches that creature-capturing itch that many fans of the genre have. My review will go into detail on some of the more notable comparisons that Temtem has with Pokémon.DifficultyUnlike Pokemon, this game is challenging. Not only will the main story have you face off against difficult boss fights, but most of the regular trainers will be formidable foes themselves. I think an important reason why this is the case is due to the fact that (with very few exceptions), there are no “bad” temtem. There are no Ratatas, Kricketots, Wurmples, etc. – bad creatures that stay bad even after evolution. You’ll never be facing off against a trainer that comes at you with a team of laughably easy tems.This does mean that the average Temtem player will have to do some grinding, but for fans of the creature-capturing genre, grinding easily bleeds into exploration. You’ll want to do the side-quests, you’ll want to find the rare tems, you’ll want to explore all the areas. And this necessarily means more encounters, more opportunities to level up your team.AntagonistIt caught me by surprise just how evil the “bad guys” are in this game. You too will likely be surprised if you’re used to the typical Team Rocket type of antagonists from the Pokémon games. I can’t say much more on this without getting into spoilers for the main story, but know that the adversary in Temtem is willing to go to great villainous lengths to achieve their goals. TypesMuch of the temtem types feel more simplified from Pokémon. For example, Ground and Rock are “Earth”, and Grass and Bug are “Nature.” Yet, this does not stop there being a creative diversity of tems and moves. I particularly love the ingenuity of the moves, from the stamina mechanic, to the creative synergies possible, and even to the impressive animations played out in battle. Competitive Anyone who’s dabbled in the competitive scene of Pokémon will feel right at home with competitive Temtem. Teambuilding is genuinely fun, largely due to the aforementioned fact that there are rarely any “bad” tem for you to choose; even the tem you encounter on the very first few routes in the game are competitively viable (I’m a personal fan of Kaku, which you can catch very early). In short, if you’re creative enough, you can certainly come up with a unique team that could potentially shake the meta. To conclude, I would highly recommend Temtem to fans of the creature-capturing genre of RPGs, even in early access. Whether single player or co-op, there is huge potential for fun. I’ve had tons of fun with this game over the 600+ hours I currently have with it, and I hope you do too.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being in early access, with several features with literal "WIP" signboards in front of them scattered about the world, and in spite of some rough issues with the initial launch, Temtem is already very, very promising.Temtem is gorgeous, with very bright, clean colors, and very well-balanced design. The design of the creatures is generally less iconic and memorable compared to Pokemon, but it would be a mistake to discount what they've done here. Many could probably agree that Temtem's creatures are at least on par with some of Pokemon's less iconic generations. Animation, while simple, are really effective, and the effects work is very pretty. Some of the sound effects leave a lot to be desired, with some not fitting the action, and others coming across like cheap stock clips (there's a particularly egregious duck quack that I can't get out of my head).The combat is great, both in strategy and in the smoothness of the activity itself. Pokemon SwSh was especially grating with how many button presses every single fight had for unnecessary information (please don't prompt me three separate times for each character's level-up stat increases), and Temtem mercifully streamlines this process. Fights are longer than Pokemon's, but they move along more quickly. I never felt like I wanted a skip button during the battles.I haven't played deeply enough to talk about the various mechanics at play with the elemental RPS, or the synergy stuff, but it's evident from the get-go that there's more strategy going on under the hood, and I am very eager to dive into it.I don't have much at all to say about the story at this point. It's certainly not cinematic -- the game doesn't make use of its camera or anything like that; all dialogue is exchanged via dialogue boxes and floating character models, scripted animation is very minimal, and the game never bends from its 3/4 fixed camera -- but the writing is pretty humorous and snappy. Conversations go quick and don't test your patience.It is impossible not to compare Temtem to Pokemon, Sword / Shield in particular, but it's a fair comparison to make, and one that Temtem holds its own very well in. This game does not do some things Pokemon fans have come to expect over the years, and that may come as a disappointment for some. But this $30 early access game with a development team that could probably fit in a single large van is already more engaging than the latest $60 installment(s) in literally the most lucrative franchise on the planet and it's not even finished. I look forward to spending a lot more time with this game, and I'm even more excited to see how this game evolves in the months and years ahead as its team transforms it into the Pokemon game fans have wanted for decades.

Better still, the combat elements are very good. You have a stamina bar which recovers some of its points each turn. Moves use stamina, and some moves need time to charge. Essentially, you cannot spam your nukes endlessly, as moves will damage your TemTem if you use it when you do not have stamina for it. Fight feel a bit more strategic. Also, you can unlock moves that will be empowered if you have a TemTem of a certain type fighting alongside the user. Everything hangs together well. _childDocuments_.review: Hello, TemTem community and developers,This is an open letter from me, a supporter who purchased Temtem on the very first day that it was available on Steam way back in Early Access, and has followed the development of your game from the very beginning. I hope that you take a moment to consider my feedback. I would like to explain to you why your game went from Overwhelmingly Positive to Mixed on Steam.Price and ValueWhen I purchased Temtem originally, it was half the price that it is now, for 1/10th or less of the content. Since then not only have you doubled the price of the game but you have also introduced microtransactions in the form of a battle pass. Gamers have less disposable income per capita now than they did in 2020 when I purchased Temtem. Your game is now among the most expensive games on Steam. With respect, people have trouble paying this much for AAA titles, let alone indie games with dated graphics that also have microtransactions on top.NoveltyWhen Temtem first came out, it was fairly unique in that there were not many Pokemon rip off type games that had meaningful development resources. Temtem stood out alone as the only good choice. 2 years later, there are quite a few other titles to choose from.Hostile Community ManagementAny time I have seen any kind of constructive criticism being aimed at the Temtem developers, the discord mods and community are quick to spring to the games defense, often quite rudely and dismissively. This says to me that the developers have far too much ego and believe that consumers are idiots.In Summary:Temtem was released far too early. It was a beta, sold at full price as an early access game. 2 years later it is finally releasing in something close to a completed state, and it is double the price and also has a battle pass microtransaction scheme attached.For all of what I am saying above, I am updating my original positive 2020 Steam review to a negative one and advising people not to buy this game.Cheers,Jass

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game, so much and to be honest I still really enjoy it. The Temtem are adorable (except for Bigu and Babawa), the writing is great mostly. People say it's a Pokemon clone, but honestly, that's generally because it's inspired by Pokemon and that's not a bad thing!The Story, is enjoyable. Choices, which while they don't impact the story can take on fun turns, like the twin duo you'll meet early into the 1st Island. Every item according to Crema is purely cosmetic. Almost everything you can do in Temtem can let you level up. Another thing to note, is that according to information given by Crema at this time, "completing the Premium track will grant you enough Novas to purchase the next season’s pass without any additional cost" So while you might need to buy the premium Tamerpass once, you might not need to buy it again.Honestly, this game is a ton of fun, hunting for Luma Temtem, entering Saipark during Luma Week, Fishing (mostly) for that 5/5 fish, entering 5 person lairs to battle a legendary Temtem. There's alot that can be done and more coming in September when 1.0 releases and Temtem comes out of Early Access. It's been a heck of a ride over the past 2 and a half years and I know it's gonna continue to be one!

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Pokémon fan and competitive battler, I decided to give Temtem a try. Despite the bugs and lack of content that came with the initial release (most which have been fixed), the new updates have made the game incredibly enjoyable. With any game, however, there are cons. Thankfully the pros outweigh in this case:Pros:-The art style is incredibly refreshing. I enjoy the bright colors, the character designs, and the Tem designs. I'm always excited to see what new Tems will appear in different areas and they never cease to make me go "I want it!!".-Speaking of designs, I enjoy the culture that's added. Characters have beautiful names and interesting dialogue options that change based off of what replies you pick.-Battling is smooth and visually rewarding. I very rarely run from wild combat just because I enjoy watching the encounter.-The game isn't easy. There's no steamrolling through areas or Dojos (gyms) and sometimes they'll even steamroll YOU. (♥♥♥♥ you Tihani) It's also nice to see Tems near your level when you go into new areas.-I get to watch my teammate's Tems evolve when they get there! That's exciting.-Very easy to play on Steam Link.Mixed feelings:-Co-op is smooth and enjoyable, but also a little frustrating. You can only use three of your six Tems in combat while with another person and they need to be at the front of your party to get any use. If you have a Tem with the Coward's Cloak (aka EXP Share) in your party of six but not in the top three, it won't get any experience. Which sucks, because believe me, you're going to need those three Tems when you fight and having one severely underlevelled gives you a huge disadvantage. I'd much prefer if you had access to all six while fighting, but could only choose three to send out. In addition, you're forced to follow your co-op partner (& they're forced to follow you) to different areas of the maps, buildings, etc if you're in the same party. This can be good or bad depending, so I'll leave it up to the reader.-The maps are HUGE! Which I love, but my GOD does it take forever to backtrack. You'll need to backtrack a lot if you're into breeding/Luma (shiny) hunting/Tem searching and this can become very time consuming. I'd love a fly option like in Pokémon. I know Crema has plans for mounts as the option is there but greyed out, but in it's current state, this is a bit too time consuming for my tastes.-You'll have to grind. A LOT. I know a lot of people don't like this, which is why it's in the mixed feelings section. I'm an outlier, I enjoy it. For those who have played the GBA Pokémon games, it's similar to that style of grinding. Lots of wild Tem battles to make it up to levels high enough to defeat Dojos and wild Tems in different areas.Cons:-Only one character per account. Crema themselves said you'll need to buy another copy if you want to make a second character... Which is disappointing. I play this game with my fiancée and don't want to go ahead of her on my current character. If I could make a second to progress, that would be great. I heard rumors of a second slot added for a Nuzlocke playthrough, but not a main story slot.-Speaking of characters, if you want to delete your current one, you better not have traded anything in the last 10 days. They don't tell you about that restriction. Don't expect to be able to empty your Tems and pockets for a fresh playthrough.-The evolution system frustrates me a bit, mainly due to lack of information on your Tems. In this game, you don't evolve at a set level. You have to level X amount of times from when they were caught/bred. This normally wouldn't be an issue, but I can't inspect my Tem and see what level I caught it at because that information doesn't exist, so I either have to breed a new Tem to know exactly how many levels I need to increase it to get to X evolution, or I have to just make a guess and get disappointed every level when it doesn't evolve. I failed math, guys. Pls no bulli.-Clothes are super expensive. Expect to look like a Default Danny (only with different colors) until you hit end game (which there isn't much of right now since the game isn't finished, so in this case, until you hit the end of the currently available main quest) or throw 28K at a hat. If you want your Tems to not die every fight, you're going to need the money to buy Balms and revives, so you won't have enough left for clothes. I don't think there's been a point in my Tem career where I had more than 8K. I'm sure you could manage, if you want to run back to the Tem center every battle...-Give me back my skates, I want to catch some Tems I missed in previous areas that I can no longer return to because of this. :(I'll update this as things change. I expect to be playing this for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 9/10/2022:  The full version is here and 10 hours in I could scarcely be more pleased.  The 1.0 launch feels smooth and technically sound, aside from some frame drops loading an interior/exterior.I have some minor complaints.  The version number at the bottom of the screen is permanently displayed, there is no option to hide player names, but I expect these rough spots to get polished out.I have not looked at the battle pass or the microtransaction store!  Battle passes turn games into chores!  They are not fun!  This is the state of games but the preying upon consumers is disgusting and I hope we grow out of this some day.  My understanding is that Temtem's battle pass is slow and grindy.  I can't care, they won't see a dime from me for a battle pass.Questionable business strategies aside, catching monsters is fun!  Really fun!  Every monster has random stats, making YOUR rabbit monster unique.  The art and sound and battle animations are a pleasure.  I was somewhat baffled by the UI, but I am getting the hang of it.In closing, this is the monster tamer I always wanted.  Pokemon was too simplistic, too easy, and I was just a little too old when it arrived.  I highly recommend Temtem for your monster taming needs.Launches for online games, especially in early access, are usually rough.  Its to be expected.  I would advise everyone to hold off on early access for this game.  Almost all my time in this game has been spent in the queue, with brief in-game jaunts that are quickly remedied by crashes and freezes.  Sometimes all my temtem disappear, possibly having determined that they must raise themselves since their trainer is never around.  Check back later for this game, I still have high hopes for Temtem.

_childDocuments_.review: A great monster catcher game, although it is a lot more difficult than other monster catching games such as pokémon.Also there is a time sink / grindiness element to it that is not for everyone.The various islands are pretty big with plenty of monsters (temtems) to catch and quests to do.I haven't played this in quite a while so can't speak much about the latest 2 archipelago's (islands).I do know they added teleportation and mounts, but haven't unlocked them yet (but great additions nontheless).Loved the various themes / colors and also pretty good music.There's some weekly quests you can do such as fishing and delivering items for goodies.Also re-battling gym/dojo leaders to get radars to help with catching Luna (shiny) temtems.However this is a massive time sink that so far has given me 0 Luna haha.Also the re-battles are difficult and you need to have a good counter team with elemental advantage (unless they changed it).You can also acquire a house and decorate it as you want, a bit like animal crossing.Also saw they added a battle-pass like system where doing almost everything gives XP and levels said pass.There is a free variant, so for those that play a lot or plan to play a lot it offers some nice cosmetics.There are a few time sinks though, like the earlier mentioned radars, but there's also min-maxing stats of tems and you can also breed temtems to breed a perfect one (all stats max), but it will take a while to reach that.All in all I would recommend it, but I do want to warn people that the "grindiness" can be off putting for some.

_childDocuments_.review: A very refreshing and interesting take on the monster catching genre. I backed this game when it was only a kickstarter kiddie and I’m pleased to see it in its current form. Temtem takes the flaws of Pokémon’s battle system and does it’s best to rework them (for example the PP system in Pokémon, vs the Fatigue system in Temtem). This offers new strategic possibilities and adds depth to competitive. The monster roster is relatively small compared to that of Pokemon, understandably so, however the open world MMO experience in addition to the ability to have any tem traverse the wilds along with you makes the tem count no big deal. Story is ok. It tries to throw you for a loop here and there. In some places it hits, and in others it simply doesn’t. I never quite felt the sense of urgency that it insisted upon. Conclusion is a bit abrupt and non climactic, but I was still more than satisfied with the game itself by then. The game doesn’t end, as there’s plenty to do post game. There’s a cash shop and a battle pass but everything they offer is optional and purely cosmetic. Nothing game breaking.Hope to see more monsters added in the future, more areas. Great game, hadn’t had that much fun since I played Pokémon Platinum.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:This game doesn't respect your time and requires you to grind money as a second full time job to get anything done.The entire game design feels hostile and only the most dedicated players will ever get enough cash together to do the endgame activities you can only do after completing the story.Their poorly implemented FOMO shop with skins that you cannot get via ingame activities or their extremely grindy battle pass just adds insult to injury.---I got this game when it came out in early access and it was really promising.The story itself is decent despite restricting you as much as possible in your movement by first showing you where you could go but giving the necessary item to reach that place only later and also takes it pretty much the nest island away from you and also hinders you from leaving certain places until you progress the story far enough.Either give the player mobility items later to or don't require that restriction for your environment in the first place.Evolving is also a chore because leveling takes ages and for some reason the TemTems do not evolve at level X but only after you leveled them a X amount of levels starting from the level you catched them. Which makes the low Exp grind a even bigger grind and is getting slower and slower the higher the levels get. This feels like this is only different just to be able to brag that it is differentThe battles are nice and you can play the entire story in Coop, the story is medicore but good enough for the gameplay. The most fun part are the possible responses you can give and are almost all the time ending in some sort of joke.This is now not true anymore. With the end of major updates any micro transactions have been removed and the season pass and any premium cosmetics can be acquired via ingame currency.Overall I would give this game a mixed review and say its worth buying now if on sale (considering the game is more or less finished and no major updates will be released anymore).Game is still a grind and most ways to aquire currency is in the late game and time gated.If you like that go for it, but nowadays a lot of game do this and I am tired of having a second full time job.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews, but honestly, I've been wanting a pokémon MMORPG since I finished soul silver. The fact Temtem took the risk, the challenge and the plunge, while still outdoing pokémon in a variety of things makes me very happy. The fact that it is also an indie studio makes me feel like the money spent in this game has a much higher chance to return to this game rather than leave and go into corporate decisions and/or CEO lunch money.There are better written and thought-out reviews out there, and those will probably convince any reader much more than this. However, if someone somehow stumbles upon this one, I'll say this: Temtem is a very good, polished game in Early Access (version 0.5.something, as of this.) It's not even properly half done. What is done, however, runs smoothly at above 60fps with perfect graphics on my 1050Ti even when performing intensive hits like "Fire Tornado". Glitches are few and far between, most often just a lock that makes you have to re-log. Gameplay is a streamlined, however more strategical pokémon 2v2 battle. No more "pp", but "stamina" dictates how often you can hit without taking a breather. IVs and EVs are there, breeding is there, no complexity is lost at all, It is actually gained.I'll finish this here with a simple "if you feel like you'll like it, then most probably you will." and call it a day.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the premise and game in early access and followed every update through a year after launch. put 600hrs into this game and was enjoying the promise of competitive play. However, Crema is a strange developer and soft abandoned the game shortly after launch of 1.0. they were always slow on updates, but with a live service model like they proposed, comes the promise of semi-regular content updates and response to feedback from the players. the only significant change over the first year after launch has been changing seasons, and their rotating season pass. there were still abandoned shops "coming soon" and a very grindy empty endgame that would have you fishing for hours a week, refighting the gym leaders and delivering 2 packages from location to another for little reward... Also, when the community would speak out in forums, announcements and patch-notes, they would delete negative feedback of any kind and respond aggressively. When they announced they were going to make a roguelite, the community was understandably upset that they would announce a new game before delivering on some of the basic promises they made for the first game. And surprise! another light update for temtem a month or 2 later with them announcing the essential end to temtem. Almost 2 years after release, they remove a lot of the grind and restrictive season features like non-rotating items. people would log on every day to see the new shop items, but they didnt want to include previous seasons items to increase f.o.m.o. even though the dwindling hardcore base was asking for it for YEARS, ya know, reward the few remaining people still supporting your game...A good comp is Ghostship games with Deeprock Galactic. same live-service model with rotating cosmetics in season passes. However, they were ALWAYS improving the game, adding new missions, listening to feedback. when the community suggested to rotate cosmetics from seasons into the shop. they said "why not" right away. And now, guess what? they announce and release a roguelite, while still releasing content and improving on DRG. AND taking the same mentality of listening to fan feedback as well, and its making for a better roguelite monthly.This whole experience has me basically boycotting any of Crema's games. I actually resent that i spent 600hrs and really loved and supported this game only to feel used, and theres plenty of other studios that do it right. go play Palworld made by like 2 people with just as frequent updates, or DRG where they actually care about your time and money, or nexomon which the first is free

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. There are only a few monsters I've seen that i would consider 'imbalanced'.. there is good diversity in the roles (not quite as much as there will be, I'm sure). Very interesting creatures that I feel motivated to breed, train, and evolve. The creature design is great and the monsters don't feel cheesy, played out, or downright silly *cough* gen8pokemonlookridiculous *cough*. For you comp players, the breeding system is great. It doesn't stuff you into a never ending cycle of breed/hatch/breed/hatch in hopes for decent IVs, as the odds are fairly heavily leaning towards the offspring having a higher stat roll than the parents, which allows you to breed for more options instead of forcing you to breed one creature for days for the 'best' stat roll.As for what I'm hoping for.. I would for sure like to see weather effects, maybe a little more in the way of team stat boosting and buff removal, and possibly even stat passing. Also maybe a bit more 'synergy' type things that don't necessarily require a certain element, but a certain trait or even archetype, as an example..  Trait: 'Monster will gain a boost to attack stat if its partners highest stat is Defense" so on and so forth, in conjunction with taunt/damage redirection abilities, it would help us cement roles as 'wall/tank/attacker/support/pivot' etc.  Possibly even a few forms of 'ally position swapping' that has priority and can allow us to mitigate more of the obvious predictions attacks for pvp purposes... as an example.. your opponent would want to use a super effective move for an ally on the left, one monster could swap places with priority to foil the opponents super effective attack, etc. (don't get me wrong.. 100% not complaining.. I'm completely enamored by the game, I'm just really hoping for a balanced metagame where I get smoked by an opponent because I wasn't able to predict his or her strategy until it was too late). Anyway, that's my spill. I'm really excited to see where this games future is heading. Please keep the balance in the late game! the winner should be the best strategy and who has the experience to counter the common type match-ups. Not the person whose creatures have the best overall stat values/most op monsters! Thanks for what you guys are doing :)

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow manages to shove "Haha we've all played pokemon right? Look how we're subverting expectations! Haha it's so different yet so similar, ain't that neat?!" in your face at every opportunity, while blatantly ignoring all the lessons they could've learned along the way. For every improvement they made on pokemons' tired formula, there's another two steps back somewhere else. Whether it be the typings that are *just* similar enough to feel accessible, while having very alien and strange weaknesses/strengths when compared to pokemon. The hunt for rare Tems was thrilling the first time, but all sense of accomplishment evaporates immediately when you progress through the story and hit a new inane wall of bs to get through.None of us liked how pants-on-head-retarded it was to simply bring a basic sweeper of the right typing and mop up a gym with zero effort. But, for example, the fire/grass gym just felt hollow. It felt less "Oh wow, that's neat how they switched that" and more as if the devs were like "HAHAHA!!! Best they're gonna have to grind way more than they expected to! GOTTEM!!!" The challenge varied wildly from basic typing schemes per area to abruptly run you into a team purposefully designed to beat what you just used to clear the previous zone. This doesn't feel earned, it feels forced and by design. I realize that this is its' own game, and shouldn't be held up to pokemon at every turn. However, the game does everything in its' power to emulate that series, with very little meaningful deviations from pokemon's "norm." The devs seem to revel in being aware that they're making a game that's VERY similar to pokemon, while constantly punishing you for going along with them on it.It feels like the showrunners of GoT talking about Season 8. They can talk for hours about expectations, subversions, etc. but it always rings hollow. As long as the game is a 95% carbon copy of pokemon, the bits that aren't don't feel genuine or in good faith. The last hour of my playtime was absolutely miserable, and after the fights that precede the airship crash, I think I'm done with this game. Was not at all worth the time spent, though I didn't know it until the last hour.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mostly positive on Temtem so far, with one big asterisk.It's an excellent pokemon-inspired game with a much-appreciated evolution of the combat system, polished gameplay & UX, and a super cute aesthetic.***However... it doesn't really feel like an MMO. At least not yet. So far, actually, it pretty much only has the downsides of an MMO (server issues, login queues, floods of people breaking immersion around NPCs, etc.) without any of the things that generally make those downsides worth it.There isn't a whole lot of interaction with other players, and though you can technically play co-op, there don't appear to be a lot of incentives to do so--by some accounts, it's actually even detrimental. MMOs work best when they encourage and facilitate people interacting with each other, and there just aren't many systems in place yet that do so.Nothing like dungeons, raids, public world events, difficult areas that require cooperation, big community puzzles, etc. exist in the game yet as far as I can tell. I understand that it will be hard to figure out how to translate these things into a game with turn-based combat, but without them (or at least something like them), it just doesn't feel like an MMO.In addition to that, there's very little to differentiate the journey of one player from another. MMO-like experiences can potentially thrive on that alone, if people have different journeys that lead them to information and economic value that they can share & trade with each other. But right now, it feels like a very linear experience that other people happen to be taking at the same time.So, I'm making this review positive because it's a great start and a surprisingly-polished early experience--and also, it's just exciting to see someone take the Pokemon formula and take it in a different direction--but I think I'll be putting the game down for quite some time until it actually feels like an MMO.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of potential here... but if it's not *better* than Pokemon, what's the point? The changes the devs make based on Early Access feedback will make or break this game.It does a few things very well, the art style is great, even if you don't like it initially (say, at character creation) it will grow on you.The battle system involves some subtle but very significant improvements. Stamina is much more interesting than raw PP. The vastly increased use of move priority also adds an interesting element beyond pure Speed as king. The ready-up and cooldown mechanics on some abilities is yet another interesting layer.Putting these three aspects together makes for some very interesting moveset balancing, very stamina expensive high damage moves with no ready up time, versus cheaper moves that take a turn or two to become available, or have max priority once they are unlocked.In conjunction with synergy moves and improved breeding, Competitive Temtem shows a lot of promise.I still wouldn't recommend the game just yet, there are a few frustrating elements like the odd type matchups and inflated difficulty through unfair mechanics. A lot of areas are marked as Work In Progress, it may be more enjoyable for a first playthrough once it's more complete.

_childDocuments_.review: TemTem is really good. But there are... a LOT of flaws. In this review i'm gonna address everything good as well as everything that needs to be fixed.For pretty much the entirety of the first island  which took me ~10 hours to fully complete, I had a measly 6 different temtem that I had encountered on the entire island. Yes, only 6, for around 10 hours. Seeing the same tem over and over again becomes VERY tedious and boring, and I wish they would have spread out the temtem a bit more so you can gradually find new ones as you go along your journey. I will say that the later islands do seem to have better progression, but still, overall, the lack of total temtem at the moment makes it hard to keep that excitement up.I also really enjoy the fact that some side-quests you get at the later islands require you to go back to the beginner islands and do things there. I think it's really interesting for new players to see more experienced players wandering around the beginner island, seeing what sort of temtem they have following them, giving a bit of excitement and the urge to keep going so you can find cool temtem like that one!Bugs were an issue at launch, but to be honest, I haven't seen many after the first update the dev team put out. They seemed to patch the bugs very quickly, which is very reassuring so that we know they will keep this game updated and fix bugs regularly.The game is seriously lacking in some quality-of-life elements though. The quest journal to view your quests is not available yet, so you're stuck seeing only the three or so it shows you on the side. Guilds are shown to be a feature but don't seem to actually work right now. Shop prices for cosmetics are RIDICULOUS. I am 20 hours into the game as of writing this, and I would have to spend pretty much all of my money to buy a single shirt in the game. There is no chat, which I'm pretty sure they said would be a feature... _childDocuments_.review: With the £30 price tag, I simply cannot recommend this game. The story is nothing special, the game-play gets stale rather quickly and some decisions are questionable at best in my own opinion.I will readily admit, I have not finished the main story, quest-line or whatever you wish to call it. However, I feel no inclination to care nor try to advance the plot. Your rival is annoying to deal with from the start, seeming to copy Barry from Pokémon Diamond, Pearl and Platinum in terms of his attitude but they removed the likeable parts. Whilst Barry is annoying, he's never a bad person whereas Max in this game is just a prick. The only motivation your character seems to have is to move forward because that's just part of the universe, that young Tamers must leave home and go on an adventure, unlike other games in this genre where a goal is made apparent. The Elite 4 and Champion are obviously the best examples, you want to become the best trainer and whilst this goal is very simple it's at least a goal.Game-play is a unique twist on the Pokémon formula, you still only have four moves but TemTem can relearn moves at anytime and instead of Power Points, TemTem moves use a Stamina bar that regenerates between each battle. This stamina bar has the unique feature of allowing moves above your stamina count to be used at the cost of life and a turn of rest making you think about whether it's better to rest or go all in on a move risking your TemTem's health and an extra turn. Whilst the battles are the focus on these types of games, TemTem's battles quickly become a hassle, wild TemTem will almost always exhaust their Stamina to land a powerful attack even when low on health and often KO themselves when you may wish to catch them and constantly seeing TemTem's KOing themselves to nuke one of your TemTem's just makes it feel like the games out to spite you as it strips the XP gain away from a TemTem you likely wanted to level up.Quests are a neat feature at first, you can help people in the world around you to gain unique items, medicine and money but the issue comes with how quests are done throughout the game. Say what you want about escort missions, but I'd rather a couple of them were thrown in then almost every single quest being a fetch mission. "Get specific TemTem and come back to me.", "Talk to a dozen people and then talk to me again". There is a huge section of main story game where this becomes a huge issue, but I'll get into that in a bit.The world is absolutely gorgeous to look at, the cartoon style works very well for it. Colours are vibrant and pathways are mostly clear to the player. Each Tamer you fight has a dialogue tree normally, which is both good and bad. People genuinely feel like people sometimes, but most of the time you're left questioning them or just trying to speed through your options to get to the battle. These dialogue trees become exceptionally painful when your objective is to run in a straight line fighting Tamer's. The TemTem themselves are mostly quite cute and I don't have complaints on most designs but there is an issue with how little variation there feels to be. Whilst there are 150+ TemTem species, each area only has three or four unique ones, keep in mind I said area and not routes. You can go through two or three towns and you will still only be encountering most of the same TemTem's.Now, my biggest complaint. Tucma. Tucma is a brick wall that the game forces you to beat your head against. Due to story purposes, you lose the two special tools you've obtained and don't have access to anything to change your TemTem party and from there you must find an NPC with the party you were taking to the island. Whilst tedious, I can appreciate that it works to fit and cement the story. This is no excuse though when upon finding the NPC, you must do the same thing over a slightly longer distance, fighting Tamer's, retreating because you have type weaknesses that you cannot change and thus have lost almost all your TemTem's health, healing at the NPC and then walking all the way back only to go two steps further into another fight. It doesn't end there, as when you enter the next area you are forced into doing this yet again but this time with a party of four TemTem's that were given to you by a stranger and all of your meds and items have been taken away. Once you finally finish the gauntlet of Tamer battles and running for heals, you have to do several fetch quests to advance the plot at all. Running to each corner of Tucma to fetch a single item and take it to the other corner. You'll likely start one and realise you can't even finish that fetch quest, until you fetch more items for the NPC involved in the previous fetch quest. It's tedious and nothing more.This gauntlet can take hours of time and turns into a mindless drain of repetitive actions. It prevents you from leaving the island to go and catch a TemTem you may have wanted and the game gives you no warning that you will end up trapped on Tucma until it's already happened. Not to mention, the writing of this world is very poorly written. If you care for spoilers on the story, ignore this next part.  This isn't helped as at the end of Tucma's main plot, you're still unable to travel and by this point all sense of freedom has drained away. You're on rails.I could go into more and more detail, but this is already close to an essay. There are other things to note, such as Luma's being far more of a pain to hunt then Shiny Pokémon and how poorly designed Luma Radars appear to be. I also dread to imagine how many times a Luma TemTem has nuked itself due to the Stamina bar. The fact that the second islands version of Gyms have a typing duo that essentially negates counter-play, since you don't even see TemTem type's that can counter one of the two typing's and said typing counters the counter to the other typing. There are also abundant references to other video games, but to such a degree it almost felt like this was a fan game rather then it's own thing. In fact, I think that's the perfect way to describe TemTem in its current state.TemTem is a £30 Pokémon fan-game. It's tedious, grindy and lacks the engaging story or character of the game it wants to be and lack of variance in every aspect really drags the game down. Some points I've made may be nonsensical or anger-fuelled, but after spending hours of time getting through the grind that is Tucma only to discover I couldn't go help my friend on a previous island still, I had to write this even if it was solely to vent about my frustrations. If you enjoy TemTem, by all means, play on and have fun or feel free to discuss with me why I may be blind towards a more in-depth experience.I hear Monster Hunter Stories 2 is good though if you're interested in this genre.(Edit): Monster Hunter Stories 2 is indeed a much better game of this genre, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels a lot like a mix of early Pokemon games and Dofus/Wakfu aesthetic. It's very much a Pokemon clone on the surface and in how the story is structured, but there are some major differences in combat that makes it unique (no RNG mechanics, move priority works completely different, synergy system, etc). Monster designs are hit or miss, but that's something that comes with all games of this style. I personally like a lot of the designs, but if they don't appeal to you then you may want to give the game a pass.Unfortunately, I can no longer recommend this game because just the idea of trying to catch up with it again makes me feel tired. It copies a lot of mechanics from Pokemon, obviously, but not always in a good way. There are many features where I have to stop and think "why did they include this? no one actually liked this in the game they're copying, either!" They also seem determined to balance everything around making the grind more and more tedious and difficult. Personally, I think it would be better for them to focus on balancing the battle system and making it EASIER for players to acquire "competitive" tems quickly, rather than forcing players to spend hours upon hours grinding out stats or money to properly play the game. The story is also pretty lackluster, though I will note that I only got as far as the third island or so since it's taken them awhile to add all the others. Still, there are many story elements that feel awkwardly forced in just because "that's how Pokemon does it", and I'd be incredibly surprised if the story actually gets any better later on.There's little to enjoy here for casual players who don't want to grind, and competitive players will have to suffer through said grind to reach the content they actually want to play. Unless you're absolutely in love with Temtem's creature designs, don't bother. It's just not worth the hassle or the price they're asking for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a "Yes, BUT".The game itself is plenty enjoyable, but one must be extremely cautious of extensive reliance on FOMO and Crema's apparent dislike of allowing people to earn a decent amount of Pansuns within a reasonable timeframe.Radars, Dojo Rematches, Saipark, Koish fishing, and Lairs all cycle on a Weekly basis, and all rely on  RNG. Radars especially are a "use it or lose it" style item, in that if you miss the week for whatever reason, the game will take your Radar away from you, and you do not get anything in return.As for the Pansun issue, there are a few ways to earn a decent amount of Pansuns, and (what feels like) double the amount of things that will "sink" your Pansuns, either optionally or otherwise. Lairs cost 2500 Pansuns just to get in. Dojo Parks require a MINIMUM investment of 3600 Pansuns to have access to the Park (more if you lose to any of the player phantoms you have to challenge), Saipark costs anywhere from 1000-5000 Pansuns on a given week, depending on if it's SV or Luma Week, the rarity of the Tems, etc. to name but a few.Clothing especially has been an extremely longstanding complaint among the playerbase, in that a basic shirt will run you anywhere from 10,000 Pansuns on up, same for everything else. Dyes cannot be bought individually except from players (who will usually charge a significant amount over the cost to obtain it), so your only option to avoid being pricegouged in that regard is to buy dye packs that cost 20,000+ Pansuns.This game has a lot of promise, and it definitely hits a spot for me that Pokemon hasn't in years, but if you cannot tolerate FOMO, overreliance on RNG, and in general a game that shows little respect for the player's available time, I would not recommend that you buy this game.I would suggest waiting for a sale, but Crema has stated time and again that there will be no sales anytime soon, as the Early Access price is "already discounted" (which is really just a form of 'moving the goalpost'), and I would honestly expect this to continue well past its release date in September.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a torturous chore. By the final island I was totally sapped of any enthusiasm I may have had when I first started playing back in 2020. Every battle is a drawn out slugging match, and there's no variation or creativity in the tamer encounters, many of which you can't skip. Every island has a gauntlet of a dozen or so tamers you fight consecutively, and these fights are tough and drain your resources; there's not a lot of money so healing items are precious. XP gain is useless because they make it near impossible to level up, as a way to prevent you from over-leveling and blowing through battles. Which is stupid, because the combat is so airtight that even if you over-level your party, your opponent can still overpower you; I know this because the game will sometimes drop a tamer who has one monster that's about 10 or 20 levels ahead of you, and with the right matchup you can OTK those battles. The story is barely worth mentioning; its a generic coming-of-age plot, but starts to take itself way too seriously towards the endgame. The writing is bad and downright cringey at times, with a lot of obvious bait thrown in as well. The worst part is how the game CONSTANTLY talks down to the player; you endure these tough battles and put all these hours in, and no one is even slightly grateful. The dojos are pointless and grant nothing useful to the player, and some of them have inane puzzles that are designed to simply waste even more of your time. The first battle of this game has you getting bodied by your obnoxious rival, which in retrospect, was perfect foreshadowing for what was to come. At its core, its a decent monster taming game, but whatever enjoyment you might get from it is snuffed out by the sheer tedium of literally everything else about it. Such a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game back in 2020 and I had fun just catching temtems and messing around. The art style is cute and I enjoy most temtem designs. Story is pretty plain but my main goal was to collect the temtems I likeSo, what's the problem? The game has been officially released, yet it's not really enjoyable for a casual player like me. The game puts a lot of focus on competitive fighting, but I don't mind the PvP battles, I can just ignore them. Not my wheelhouse, easily avoidable. The problem is that a lot of casual stuff is locked behind competitive level PvE battles that require a fully trained competitive teamI personally enjoy breeding high stat (all 50) tems and hunting for lumas, I don't care about combat, I'd rather sell tems to others to use, but getting such tems means you have to grind A LOT, as stats from wild battles are random, and low spawn rates for some tems makes this tediousHere's my personal experience as an example: I wanted to get a radar to help me catch higher stat tems as well as a chance for a luma. I didn't care what tem, I just wanted to hunt for the fun of it. The radars are locked behind competitive dojo rematches, and my old team is no longer viable as I've lost 3 times despite knowing the strategy behind it. The trading center has competitive tems costing 20k+, so I can't afford a full team of 8. What's the best way of getting money? Oh right, those very same dojo rematches, which makes this a money loop that is impossible to get into without another source (that doesn't take forever to do)So I threw all my WishYouWell coins into the Kisiwa well, hoping to get a small boost for one of the competitive tems. I managed to get 2 Valash pheromones (boosts spawn rate for 30 mins & guarantees minimum SVs of 20), so I looked up its spawns. It's either a 5% chance or a 50% chance.... in an area locked by, you guessed it, MORE competitive-level PvE battles. And to rub salt in the wound, you need to win three times AND pay for each attempt. When I'm trying to make a competitive team in the first place, without access to much money. You see my issue now?The game is great if you're into competitive fighting and nothing else, and are able to actually get a team going. But what happens once the competitive scene dies out? It will be too late for the casuals who will have long since given up. I enjoy a bit of a grind to get the tems I want, but this is ridiculous, as even small boosts are essentially unobtainable (and no, waiting for Saipark to change each week isn't much of an option. I want to play the game, not wait for months until it finally has something I want)The charm of games like Pokemon is that you can play in whatever way you want - battles, breeding, shiny hunting, contests, etc., but Temtem doesn't give you the choice. And honestly this is the only reason why I'm actively telling people not to play this game unless they're into competitive gaming, as it really punches you in the face for even hoping that you could have had a chill time with your favourite tems

_childDocuments_.review: I don't agree with the battle pass idea and how tedious it is to get XP on it (But it's only cosmetics, there's no pay to win in this game) but as a Pokemon fan I have to say I love this game. The story is long and challenging (Took me 60 hours personally) and post-game there's a lot to do, though if you don't familiarise yourself with competitive strategies the post-game can be quite overwhelming.Being an MMO it has an economy and you can buy and sell both items and tems. The game is server-based so there's no hackers ruining the experience. Competitive PvP scales your tem's SVs (Equivalent to Pokemon IVs) so you don't have to play the genetic lottery to get into competitive (Good considering egg breeding is a lot more complicated here to avoid crashing the tem market), but you still have to work on making your tems strategically viable such as adjusting their TVs (Equivalent to Pokemon EVs) and moveset.Strategically it's very different to Pokemon because all battles are double battles and rather than PP the game has a stamina system (Stamina refills at the end of the battle and you recover some each turn, so it's much better than Nexomon's stamina system). Some moves have synergies which boost the move if your other tem has a specific type and damage isn't RNG based, so the emphasis in this game comes from using stamina effectively, having your tems compliment each other in battle and knowing when to swap them, entirely relying on strategy with no elements of luck. If you think this is a game you can cheese with a single overpowered tem, you're wrong. Also, lumas (shinies) are amazing in this game

_childDocuments_.review: Before reviewing the actual game,im gonna talk about the ban and battlepass drama:1-The ban issues: disgusting,I don't know if it keeps happening but I hope it doesn't.2-Battlepass:-Not only is a cosmetic-only BP,but you can also get it with free currency you earn in the game itself,0$ spent.-The BP is basically a one time purchase,if you do all lvls,you get 1000 vortex (you need 750 for the next BP) which not only means you'll be able to purchase every single BP for free afterwards,but you get another free BP every 3 of them,or just extra money for the shop.-There are still more updates for the game (nuzlocke mode,for example) and they said there were going to be season and events in the future.-These people are literally saying that this game is now bad or not worth trying because THERE'S A BATTLEPASS THAT YOU CAN IGNORE AND PLAY THE GAME EXACTLY LIKE EVERYONE ELSE.-I see way too many people talking about the BP,but no one's actually talking about things like the exp boosters,which are purchasable now,last for 30 more minutes and give X3 exp instead of the old X2.Now a quick review about the actual game:-The combat is RNG-free,the stamina is an evolution of the outdated PP system and sync attacks are great.-Combat animations are way better than pokemon.-Although the story isn't a masterpiece,It works really well. It's closer to pokemon Black and White's story,a little bit more mature than your average pokemon story,with some decent twists and a good enough criminal org.-Temtem trading is great.-Housing :).-Interiors are way more detailed than pokemon.-The game is more difficult than pokemon,but in a good way. It forces you to learn how to play,making it quite the enjoyable experience and it even lets you progress through the story even if you lose,making future rematches and the feeling of being a nobody that has to improve as a tamer, way more enjoyable.-Gadgets >>>>>> MOs. (You instantly get on your surfboard the moment you touch water,no need to press a button,same goes to climbing and all that stuff)-Mounts,perma-repels with improved movement speed.-Temtem designs are great.-Characters make sounds when they speak,although this isn't voice acting,it really helps to give them personality and make them feel way more alive.Now the issues I have with this game:-Some things from pokemon that feel outdated and haven't been changed in this game,for example: trainers being static NPCs waiting for a living organism to cross their visual field,or needing to wait for each combat msg to appear one by one,making it a little bit tedious,etc.-OST is forgettable at best.-Although Temtem designs are great,characters designs are...meh,forgettable.-Some "required" items (exp share,TP,etc) are linked to side quests,and some of them may be easily skipable unless you are doing the 100% of each map or look it up in the wiki.-There's lack of legendary (mythical) tems,there are only 2 in the game at the time of this review and 1 incoming in future updates.-Although I like raids,they are way too RNG and teammates can f*** up you run pretty easily. Not only that but if you end too fast,you have to wait for all your teammates to end their run so you can fight the boss.-TP just shows a list of locations,forcing you to learn each location's name instead of just giving you a map where you can choose the place you wanna travel to.In the end,I love this game and what it's trying to achieve here. In my opinion,this is the real and logical evolution of Pokemon in many ways. Unless you are one of those crybabys that can't like a game with a BP but also like online Pokemon inspired games...this is definitely for you.
