_childDocuments_.review: Writing this as at time of game being in v0.5.10, so subject to change with later versions.TL;DR:If you played old school Pokemon games back in the day you will most likely enjoy this.  Excellent writing, with good humour and an a pretty intriguing story.  Hits all the nostalgia feels from my childhood memories, but innovates on them enough to make it feel fresh, challenging, and like you might want to call in sick for work tomorrow just so you can sneak a few more hours in.  Highly recommend, even if it is in Early Access, I most certainly do not regret the money spent.FULL:I have been a Pokemon fan since I was a small boy, and can to this day still remember the birthday my parents bought me my very own Gameboy with Pokemon FireRed.  However, I stopped playing the mainline Pokemon entries around the time that Platinum was released, because I had finished school and work and life started getting in the way.  That and the titles started getting moved to newer handhelds meaning I would have had to upgrade, which I could not justify to myself money wise at the time for the new Pokemon games alone.  I still to this day play a Pokemon Emerald and FireRed emulator on my phone when I have some free time away from home though.  So I did not play Sword and Shield, which is the obvious comparison for most people because that is what's hot at the moment, but I have heard mixed reviews with some loving it and some hating it.  When I compare it to Pokemon, I compare it to the old school Pokemon games up to Diamond/Pearl/Platinum.It follows the main structure of the old school Pokemon games, you're a young Tamer that sets out to explore the world and you end up getting involved in events which start affecting the world you inhabit.  To what end is yet unclear, as it is not finished yet, but has me intrigued enough to come back when they release more content.  The story is excellently written, with NPC's feeling interesting to talk to and some even giving you full on side quests to do for them.  Excellent world building in my opinion, can't wait to see where they take it next.The battle system is similar to Pokemon in that it is turn-based and your Temtem's have different types, with some being more effective/vulnerable against certain types than others.  It differs in many ways however, and feel more engaging and strategic to fight than what most world trainers in Pokemon did.  Key differences:- Attacks NEVER miss.- There are no critical hits which rely on RNG.- It is all type based, so if you are using a type that is strong against another you will do 2x damage.  If they are weak, you will deal 0.5x.  If you are using a type that is strong/weak against two of the opposing Temtem you will deal 4x and 0.25x respectively.- Moves cost stamina to use.  More powerful the move, more stamina it costs.  Regain small amounts of stamina at end of each turn, more if you opt to skip a turn.  Run out of stamina, you will damage your Temtem and be forced to skip next turn with them.  Stamina returns to full at start of new battles.- Status ailments such as poisoned etc. have countdown timers, meaning you know exactly how many turns until they disappear and are not until cured (looking at you Pokemon paralyse...).This means you are forced to think more strategically about your two Temtem's on the field at any time, unlike Pokemon where you use the most OP dependant on your location at the time for the entire battle, you are constantly swapping them in and out of battle.  I have literally had my backside handed to me in battles where I was 10 lvls higher than the opposing Temtem's because I wasn't paying attention to what types were on the field and was getting pummelled as a result.  The Dojo's (the equivalent of Gyms) were challenging, and actually felt rewarding when I managed to beat them.Other things worth noting:- The music is BANGING.  Played for almost 30 hours and still gets me hyped.- This runs rock solid, especially for a Early Access title.  The only bug I had was a quest not marking as complete, which was solved by logging out and back in.  Minimal frame drops, I see other Tamers on the servers ALL the time.- Your first Temtem in your party follows you around, and considering there are random players which started playing before I did in the world it lead to many moments where I said "Look at that Temtem! THAT LOOKS SICK." which is kinda cool tbh.So all in all, highly recommended.  I have most certainly gotten my money's worth and will most likely still jump on to grind for Lumas (shinies) at stages until the next content drop is released.Keep up the great work devs!PS.  If there are any developers actually reading this, your LOTR reference just before Windswept Fort had me in tears laughing.  Please, more easter eggs, keep them coming! :DEdit: Steam recognised a portion of a word as offensive, reworded to get correct context across.

_childDocuments_.review: If you play Pokemon for the battles, especially if you do VGC or doubles, you'll probably like Temtem.The battle system is very similar to Pokemon, except there's basically no RNG.  No damage ranges, no chance to para, no chance to wake from sleep (sleep only lasts for 2 turns), no crits.  Hax is gone.  Also different is that moves don't have PP, instead they cost Stamina, and Stamina is a separate stat that Temtem have.  Personally, I prefer this system to PP.The Temtem designs range in quality.  Some I really like, some I find to be a bit uninspired.  Honestly, for me personally, it's kind of analogous to 1st gen Pokemon.  Some designs were clearly done before the others, and level of detail vary, and overall the style is probably going to evolve and refine was they release more.  There's a pretty good range of content right now.  The main story takes about 20-24 hours to get caught up on (It's not complete yet).  Side quests give you Courses (TM equivalent), held items, and other goodies.  And as the servers and launch issues get sorted out (a lot of them were taken care of within hours of launch), I'm sure more content will get added and expanded upon.

Since this game isn't finished yet, i would like to offer my personal views so that the developers might take it into consideration. what i like:-only dobble-battles forces more strategic play.-the game being differcult, making battles more engaging.-The stamina-system is very clever and makes it so you have to strategise much more than in pokemon.-the lack of an accuracy stat on moves makes the game more suited for competitions.-I personally think that the breeding system is very fun and engaging. Breeding was the number one reason i didn't start competing in pokemon, since it was such a tedios task to gain pokemon with perfect IV-s. -It's also very nice to be able to se the SV-values as soon as the tems are captured, so that you easialy can choose witch ones to keep. And it also plays well with the function to release tems that you've just caught. -when creating perfect tems there is so good synergy between, training for EV-s, while catching tems for perfect SV-s and releasing tems (with no perfect SV-s) for pansuns (currensy) to buy breeding-items.what i dont like:-I feel like the conversations you have with NPC-s have to much flavor to them. For some this might be a positive, but for me, I think it's to much text. This makes it harder for me to apriciate all the work the devs have put in. I think it's a really missed opertunity that the dialog options dont affect  anything. it would be cool if you could dodge a battle by picking the right option, or get somthing extra for picking smart options. For me it is not engagning to force myself through all the dialoge without getting rewarded in any way. -pansuns are so scarce and it really ruins the experience for me at this current point. since i no longer have any battles left at this point, i can no longer earn pansuns from battles. this forces me to release tems that i catch for money. The problem with this is that you dont earn it quickly enough. breeding-items can be really expencive if you are aiming to produce perfect tems, and you gain tems with perfect SV-s faster than you gain money to breed them into perfect tems. I hope there will be easyer ways to earn money in the future, since i feel like i'm wasting so much time grinding for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to say here, if you like Pokemon you'll probably like Temtem.  Unique designs, genuinely funny dialog on some NPC's and in your response options.  Whereas Pokemon's default format is single battles, Temtem goes the double battle route and moves will sometimes have an additional effect depending on the partner currently out.  Even early game I can see how these could potentially get very powerful and as such am excited to see what other combo's can be done.  Fairly sparse on its current roster of little creatures but over time will surely grown much larger.  Additions like the Temessence vial, which acts as a one off cure all for your party, and the ability to swap between any learned moves on the fly without having to use an item or NPC are nice QoL additions that i wouldn't hate to see in a Pokemon game.  Overall its enjoyable and feels well put together as i haven't encountered any bugs so far.Currently the map feature could use some improvements, as it doesn't tell you what area you are hovering over.  During battle the game is supposed to outline in green, white, or red when you select an opponent to attack based on how effective that attack will be, but fails to light up green for some 2x and red for some 1/2x.  Overall its current form is entertaining and with a few QoL improvements, could be on of the best Pokemon "clones" there is.  For $34.99 i would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for something relaxing and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable, after the initial five minutes of game play to select your Temtem the game simply overloads.It can't process the number of requests hitting the server in a way that a standard MMO should. The result? You get stuck and have to force the client to close as it becomes unresponsive to every possible input (your controller/keyboard won't do anything). Stress tests are based off metrics that are already available and based on patreon figures, backing and general social media interest the analysts of this particular game should have prepared accordingly. Unfortunately they haven't done so and this alpha early access is perhaps one of the worst I've ever experienced. They'd be better setting it to single player, offline mode only if you spent 50 minutes in a queue (poor queue management and a lack of concurrency) and then immediately crash five minutes in because it can't handle giving you a story driven set of items.Absolutely would not recommend and will advise all of my friends to avoid it.  Waste of money and ironically, Pokemon Sword/Shield has the co-op down in a much better way than this game does. At the very least the online elements of Temtem's main inspiration actually works.

The game is not perfect, it has it's flaws and there are very well written positive and negative steam reviews and youtube videos showing the game. At the end of the day, I've put a lot of time into this game and have a lot of fun playing. Do your research and decide for yourself if you think you will have a good time. If the combat looks fun and you're worried about the battle pass and endgame grind, buy it for the main quest. it is worth it, and that's if you're a solo with no friends. Join the discord and participate in the community if that's your thing, there's plenty to do and enjoy about this game. Temtem up!

_childDocuments_.review: No spoilers, for people who want an honest (and long) review.Don't get me wrong, it's a pokemon clone.But that's not a bad thing.And it's nothing like those crappy mobile Pokemon knockoffs, you know the ones, the ones you've all played for five minutes and put down cause they were slower, dumber versions of a game that already has problems with being both slow and hand-holdy.I would venture to say this is harder than the first time you played a Pokemon game, and twice as hard if you started after gen 2.Resources are low starting off, so even a tiny HP healer is appreciated, else you make that all-too-familiar trip to the healing spot.The tamer battles starting off are incessant, but once you realize this game is more about the battling and less about useless cinematics and once you get used to that fact, it's amazing.The battling system is simple to pick up. It definitely has a chance to be more complex than Pokemon, it does not pull any punches introducing you to new game mechanics right off the bat.Unless you severely overlevel, there's no steamrolling through with one Temtem. Leave that at the door. You want a diverse team as SOON as possible, and you NEED it even before the first dojo, especially afterwards. You really get to know the type matchups if you look into it, it's not too hard to learn if you're familiar with the other series that this derives itself from.I'd say if you like pokemon, like double battles, like a good rpg, or just want a change of pace from shiny hunting on the same game then give it a try. If you don't like the newer games of Pokemon but love the older ones, then I say definitely pick this up. But if you never liked the collection aspect, never liked pokemon at all in any way, it may be hard to enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are eyeing this game you know why it  is good, so I just list here why it isn't. It is essentially a pokemon game in everything from pokedex to professor oak, you roam you battle etc. The developers didn't go far with original ideas, probably the bare minimum to be able to go home without a lawsuit from Pokemon. I absolutely hated that you literally have to fight with everyone you meet. The developers went out of their way to turn peaceful dialogue options into fights. This lead to the feeling that all dialogue options are meaning less. Why give 3 options to answer if all lead to the same outcome? I understand, that it is the "progress" of the game, but damn, they could just give some options to not fight every living soul in the game, damn it.. It is probably an alpha build thing that quests are not shown on the map, no quest log either, so good luck if you forgot the random NPC you need to find. There's no teleport between towns either. I liked the ENC-HALF potion, but the game could use an ENC-NONE one too, to avoid all encounters, if I just want to get from A->BThe other big problem I had that pokemons (I thought about correcting this, but f it, it's the same) are evolving without input and in mid-battle. Probably because it is a "new universe" (and I do say this sarcastically) but you cannot find out what evolves into what, and if your pokemon will evolve at all or at what level? For a creature game, there's suprisingly little about the creatures in the pokedex. I could completely ignore the poke stats, like str and others, it had no effect on my gameplay. The game could use a bit more INDEPENDENT world building and story, after 10hrs of play it seems I couldn't care less for the inhabitants, the only interesting thing in it is to "catch them all". The game absolutely void of original ideas, but I guess the trees look nice..

_childDocuments_.review: TemTem has surprised me in so many ways and there is true potential in this early access monster catching/battling RPG. This game adds a brand new experience to the genre which really has never been challenged. If you are a fan of turn based combat and collecting/building a team of competitive creatures, this game is for you. I was so invested in the game that I mastered google sheets in order to create an online shop which can be linked to users through the TemTem discord to trade with other players. After having put 170 hours into pokemon sword and shield, building a full shiny competitive team and catching all 400 pokemon, I can say Temtem can 100% compete with the franchise. I say this as huge pokemon fan who is starting to get disappointed in the lack of quality and polish with the more recent pokemon titles. The amount of content included in the alpha version of the game is incredibly impressive and I cannot wait for more updates. The story content can keep players busy for up to 40 hours but after that you'll have to be okay with farming and grinding as the current end game. If you are okay with that then get ready for some advanced breeding and luma hunting!ProsBeautiful Art StyleFluid Graphical PerformanceDiverse Dialog Between CharactersChallenging Main StoryEncourages ExplorationBalanced and Fulfilling Combat SystemAdvanced BreedingLumas!Economy and TradingA rival that doesn't hand hold you for half of the gameRoutine game updatesCons Clunky Side Quest Log Where are my skatesAny key <3

_childDocuments_.review: I have sunk plenty of hours in this game mainly with friends seeing who could beat it first, but it has many issues. The story starts like Pokemon you get a rival that you duel all game and you pic your Tem out of three types. After that most of the story is fetch quests that take you from one side of a massive island to the other with no quick travel until 3/4ths the way done with the game. When you get to  the end game it feels rushed and ends abruptly. Ignore it. A vocal minority of the community assumed the game would follow the typical MMORPG model and it was never advertised that way. Actual Cons:- Always online (this part does actually suck a little but the servers are solid and it has rarely affected my enjoyment. If you require your RPGs be offline then this is a legitimate reason to pass on it).- Grindy (with battles being better balanced than the big monster RPG you can't steamroll the game with 2-3 monsters. You need a balanced team and that means spending more time leveling them up. It's not Korean MMO grindy, but you will need to put some time in to get through the story which is maybe 60 hours altogether)- Economy (the pricing of non-essentials in the game is absurd. You won't be buying new clothes for a long time. The cost of getting a house mirrors the real world in how ridiculous it is. Breeding Tems is equally expensive. More time was spent designing gold sinks than gold gains)The pros:- Literally everything else. This is 100% an evolution of the Pokemon gameplay philosophy. All battles are 2v2 and many of them can be a real challenge if you don't over-level. The graphics and art design are top notch. Co-op through the entire campaign is fantastic. Post game lairs are fun. The music is catchy as hell. In conclusion:This is the monster taming game I've wanted for over a decade. Ignore the recent community drama, it's an over inflated nothing-burger. Crema stumbled a bit with some decisions (like a battlepass) and is rolling them back after listening to feedback. They fulfilled the promises they made and we got an incredible experience for it.

_childDocuments_.review: So do you want to play Pokemon but don't have Nintendo hardware? Well, us PC players finally have a decent option to do so and that option is Temtem. Let's face it, Pokemon is heavily integrated in the Nintendo circle and the odds of a release on any other platform, be it PC or otherwise, is basically zero. This has always left those of us who enjoy the concept of the game on the sidelines with very few similar games available on any other platform and almost none of those few that do exist being noteworthy or decent.I can honestly and happily say that Temtem finally manages to bring a good and well made creature collector on to other platforms. Now make no mistake, as the game that basically created the genre there is definitely a lot of inspiration from Pokemon in this game. If you're stuck on the idea that it's a "ripoff" and can't get past that then you're truly missing out on a game that really is well made and does the genre justice.I would say Temtem probably, from a comparison perspective, falls about in line in style with Pokemon X/Y. The game has a very light-hearted art style with great environments, animations, and tems in which to capture and fight with. If you're familiar with the genre already then you should have no problem getting in to Temtem as it really feels quite natural and intuitive. The handholding is also not too severe which is certainly a problem that Pokemon has had in recent releases and it also lacks a lot of the gimmicks that Pokemon has tried to implement recently with things like "mega evolution" and "dynamaxing" that, at least in my opinion, introduce little of value to the game.Now Temtem does mix it up a little bit and isn't quite a 1 for 1 clone. I mean, the inspiration is clearly there but they still do quite a bit different as well which I'll go over:- There is no PP for moves but instead there's a stamina bar. Each move requires a certain stamina and completely exhausting that bar will stun your tem for a turn and hurt them based on how overexerted they were by the move.- Not every move can be done every turn. Some moves require a charge up period of 2 or even 3 turns before they are available. This balances the high powered moves quite well as well as making you consider how you use stamina as you can easily exhaust a tems stamina before their powerful move is available forcing you to either take damage to use it or wait a turn to regain stamina.- Battles are 2v2 (or 2v1 sometimes with wild tems or some trainers that only have 1). This sometimes makes it harder to counter your opponents type if a counter for 1 is weak to the other.- The difficult definitely seems stepped up from what you generally expect from Pokemon. For instance, level differences aren't quite as meaningful and having a few levels over your opponent is nowhere near the guarantee of victory that you'd expect from Pokemon. Heck, even a 10 level advantage is not guarantee.- Moves that aren't taken can still be reapplied if you want to change it up, just as moves that are "forgotten" can be brought back in if you later change your mind. You're still limited to 4 moves and you can't change them in combat, but any move a tem has learned it can bring back in to its moveset.- You get an item called a temessence vial that is filled whenever you heal your temtem. This item allows you to full heal your temtems without returning to town, but you only get one use of it after which point you'll need to go back to town to fill it back up. This at least makes it so trips back to town aren't quite so abundant which eliminates a lot of wasted time.- The difficulty in general has been cranked up from typical Pokemon. Battles are tougher and less forgiving and dojo leaders, even early, will put up much more of a fight than you generally see in Pokemon.- RNG is less of a factor in combat numbers. This is good for those who don't want to rely on whether they get a lucky good hit and more focused on making the right choices for the right situations.- The themes aren't quite as oriented towards young kids. Let's face it, as fun of a concept as Pokemon is the games are often obsessed with catering to a very young crowd. Temtem is still certainly accessible to younger audiences but it's not afraid to throw out some attitude and explore darker plotlines and more mature themes.In the end, I feel Temtem is finally the creature capture game that people who aren't tied to Nintendo's systems have been waiting for. The game is very enjoyable, has a good mix of tems to capture, a great art style, great accessibility, and a battle system that is familiar but still manages to do things its own way. It's a good balance between drawing inspiration from a genre-defining game while still implementing its own uniqueness to stand out as more than just a "ripoff". If you're a fan of the genre and have a PC I highly recommend this option.(P.S. - The game definitely plays best on a controller so I'd recommend picking one up. It certainly plays fine with keyboard/mouse, but it certainly feels most comfortable with a controller.)

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Started off Strong, but the game isn't even finished and it's already being ruined by Cash-Traders, Real World Trading and the Player Market is controlled by specific websites. It's become extremely Pay-To-Win.Played to the end of the games current content. While it's entertaining and Fun for a time, it eventually falls flat.The game receives significant updates every month or so (New tems, tools, locations etc), so there IS that to look forward to.However a few things... heavily influenced my final decision to simply stop playing.For one, while it is "Technically" Multiplayer, it really isn't. At least not in the same fashion as most other games. You DO see other people wandering around, you CAN trade with other people but you wont really be doing much content with other players. Someone can party with you, but you're tethered to each other. Unless you're both at the exact same point in the storyline/progress of the game someone is being held back. The multiplayer battles seem... very... I dunno, clunky as well, certainly not fluid and cooperative.There are PVP matches, but it's extremely dominated by a Meta and obtaining the Tems to remain competitive in that meta requires you to purchase them from said Meta players. They decide the pricing, they decide whats valuable. Which is super... super bad for a game of this nature.These players can decide a single Tem is worth $200,000 in game cash, which will take the average player anywhere from 40-50 hours of straight grinding to obtain. Which leads to another problem with the game...TemTem is influenced and infected by a MASSIVE amount of Real-World trading. People who buy in game money with real world money, or buy rare Tems with real world money. This has lead to the player market being overly saturated with groups of players tied to specific websites that sell these in game items/currency.The same people who Sell Pansuns, are the same people who have taken over the Player Trade market. So they decide a lot of the pricing. It's not even that big of a secret, a lot of them have openly admitted to it on the Public Discord server... yet the Developers and Managers for the community/game have done basically nothing to fix this issue.While its a fun game until you hit end-game levels and have nothing more to do but fall into the toxic meta cycling of real-world influenced trading... I overall can no longer recommend this game to friends or community members. At least not until it's cleaned up.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many reviewers have said before me, "It's the Pokémon MMO you always wanted."  or "It's Pokémon, but gay."  Both of these statements are exceedingly accurate.I picked up Temtem while it was still in Early Access, played it for a few hours, and put it down.  I was satisfied with what I'd purchased at the time, but I wanted the story to develop some more, and wanted to give the developers time to do so.  I would pick it back up every few months to check out what was new, what had changed, and what had remained the same.  Each and every time I would pick it back up, I would have a renewed sense of joy and excitement to play the game.  Now that Temtem has reached it's 1.0 release, I've been playing it non-stop and have had trouble putting it down.  From exploring, to questing, to taming, breeding, just chatting with people and friends, this game has it all.  With the 1.0 release came some controversy, which is bound to happen any time a game transitions from one phase to another.  Some people are saying that there shouldn't be a paid pass in a game you already had to pay for.  I would agree with this sentiment if the Battle Pass included anything that would alter the way that you play the game, or gave someone who bought the battle pass an unfair advantage.  But the simple fact of the matter is that it does not.  The pass is a purely cosmetic feature.  The best part about the battle pass is that, if you don't want to spend more money on a game that you've already bought, you don't have to buy the pass!  And guess what?  You're not missing out on anything!Temtem is the game I've been dreaming of since I was a kid playing Pokémon.  Don't let someone else ruin your dream because they're mad that the game has a cosmetic pass in it that you don't even have to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Temtem is an adorable creature collector game that is unique from others in the genre.  Each fight is 2v2, so you can build synergistic teams, and can change the Temtems' skills anytime out of combat to set up an advantage. It requires strategic management of the Temtems' stamina and turns to achieve victory.  The story is enjoyable to play through, there are quite a few interesting twists, and the dialog with the NPCs is often humorous.  There are a variety of activities to do in the game even after completing the story, and worthwhile rewards.  You might even be lucky enough to catch a luma(shiny) Temtem!  I love the MMO aspect, and seeing players run around with unique styles and all the Tems following them around.  Most things can be traded with others as well.  You can play competitively or Co-Op with a friend.  I have to say that I disagree with those that criticize the tamer pass system, as it's completely optional and purely only for cosmetic rewards. Ample time is provided for the player to actually complete it.  It also rewards enough currency to purchase the next season.  It doesn't deserve negative reviews over such a small aspect.  I've been so excited for Temtem's official release and I would definitely recommend it to anyone!

_childDocuments_.review: It's Pokemon but if you took all of the charming monster designs and 90s aesthetics (From the early games) and replaced them with crowdfunder designed creatures and a million trainer battles. That all being said, I'll list some pros and cons.Pros:It's double battles all the time, if you like doubles battles.You get surf pretty early, which is important because large portions of the game are water based.Temtem that you find early can still be good even later on.There's an okay selection of clothing and dye to customize your character.Cons:It's doubles battles all the time, if you don't like doubles battles.You lose the ability to surf pretty early, and have to basically finish the available game (As of this review) before you re-obtain it.Temtem you find early on tend to be weak to everything you fight in the next area so you won't want to use them. This repeats itself every island.Character customization items are so expensive you'll probably only be able to afford a single piece of clothing without grinding for hours.Trainer battles are NON STOP until you've completed the game, you can barely walk for 3 seconds without encountering another trainer battle. In fact in some areas they have 3-5 trainer battles back to back with no wild encounters between them and no way to avoid them.Breeding is limited, there's a "fertility" stat that decreases by 1 every time a temtem is used to breed, the baby inherits the lowest of the two stats meaning you can only go down and an entire chain of breeding only has 8 chances to get the stats+ability you want.There are very few moves per type to pick from, most of which are "starter only", "standard", and "used once per battle" sort of deals. The synergy system doesn't really make you want to use different moves, either, since they are limited and the bonus you get isn't often worth the trade off.All in all, the game is basically Pokemon with stamina instead of PP, doubles battles only, and "synergy" moves that aren't worth using most of the time. If what you want is Pokemon with limited monster choice, limited move choice, and a pastel-ish color palette on most of the game with an absurd amount of dialogue and trainer battles that have absolutely nothing to do with anything, then by all means play and enjoy the game. However, if you were like me and were hoping to play a monster collection game that was new or unique in anyway, stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: The most painful thing about this game is the amount of potential that's on display. The underlying game mechanics are great, the graphics are pleasant to look at, and the critters are cute. But...* The controls are a mess, making movement confusing at times and switching without warning from keyboard to mouse controls.* The difficulty level of random battles is all over the board, partly because there's no visible indicator of what elemental type the critters you're facing represent; it's very common to go into battle with critters four or five levels above what you're facing and have them utterly demolished, without being able to tell why.* The difficulty level of NPCs is scrambled...you'll face off against an NPC whose critters are four levels below yours, then the next one has critters that're 8 levels above yours.* Money comes in a lot more slowly than it can be spent...be prepared to spend every cent you earn on healing potions or run back to town after every battle. And even then, you're immediately confronted with items that cost 8k, 20k, and even 80k...when you're earning at most 100 from a difficult battle.* The story is all over the map without any visible rhyme or reason. I appreciate games that expect you to double-back to areas you've been to in order to continue questing...but I picked up a mission less than an hour into the game that I had to look up after hunting for the solution for an hour, only to discover that it can't be finished until you're significantly further into the story. Why even make it available at that point, then, if it's just going to be a confusing time-waster.I understand that this is a pre-release game, but it's way too much of a mess to have been released this early, especially at the price they're charging for it. Right now, I'm having a hard time imagining it being worth this much when it's done, let alone however much more they end up charging for it.Rating right now: 2/5 stars. It's frustrating, irritating, and annoying, but the potential is obvious. I hope they clean up the mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Temtem does a great job at making a Pokemon style game. The combat is actually better than you'd expect as battles are 2v2. Some Temtem will boost other Temtem to make their attacks more powerful, some have different abilities that will also help their teammates. Instead of just have X number of attacks like in Pokemon, you get a stamina meter that refills for every fight. It's actually surprisingly challenging, you can't just spam your strongest attacks, you have to strategize.The co-op works great. The only thing that it isn't very useful for is grinding as you're only leveling one Temtem at a time vs 2 if you do it by yourself. The story is pretty good for a Pokemon style game. There's some good humor in the game like people questioning why you're exploring their houses or funny responses. There's also some side quests which is a neat little addition. Overall, it is already a great experience. It runs great. The only bug I've noticed is that there is a green/white/red circle on the Temtem you're targeting to give you an idea of how your attack will do but fairly often, it just stays white. This wouldn't be a problem if you just memorize what's strong against what but there are new types if you're used to Pokemon so you'll have to learn some new strengths/weaknesses through trial and error.There's already a good amount of content in early access. There are three islands and each one will probably take you about 8-10 hours to complete. The devs have been great in the first couple of weeks with releasing new patches pretty much daily. Hopefully the devs can keep it up. I definitely think the full asking price is worth it for the game in the current state and am looking forward to what they add over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like pokemon? If yes, play temtem...Need more? Okay.Temtem has a lot of nice quality of life features to it which pokemon refuses to do anything similar to, and never will. Such as straight up telling you the temtem's stats on the screen where it is caught. The stats that have usually been invisible or vaguely rated in pokemon games.The tools to breed perfect temtem, while costly, are readily available for you in game right at the breeding station. Naturally to prevent the massive spread of perfect stat temtem though, they can only be bred so many times, keeping some difficulty, rarity, and value to it.Move sets. In pokemon you have to use TMs or move tutors every time you want to change out a pokemon's move, not including learning by leveling up. Temtem, you can just pull up your squad list, go to the details for a tem, and drag and drop any from the list of known moves in to replace one of the currently equipped ones on the fly out in the field. No fuss, no muss.For type advantage, temtem will indicate if your attack with be more or less effective by changing the colour of the attack circle to green/red.. though it only happens if you've obtained one of the temtem you're currently targeting with the ability.In pokemon, moves are limited by PP, where you can only use them soo many times before they're unusable and you need to refill/heal them at a pokemon center. Temtem instead has a stamina system, where each move costs a set amount of stamina. You can use more stamina than you have, but the excess comes out of your tem's health, and makes you unable to take any action the next turn.All of the battles in the game are doubles battles, and you can co-op play through everything with a friend. Things can get pretty tactical, and while pokemon generally you can just casual play through even the endgame stuffs, in temtem you actually have to put a bit of effort in. They actually make things more challenging in a way that pokemon doesn't.Lastly, I enjoyed the story, and the game has a good sense of humour to it, not taking itself too seriously for the most part. There are also a lot of good references in it if you're paying attention.All in all I rate it tem/tem.

Although it's still in early release and although any and all aspects are liable to change, there are numerous issues. The developers boast customization but with such a lack of originality between options, all characters, NPC or otherwise come out looking more or less the same. Character models are charming but bland expressionless avatars and any purchasable outfits are not only unappealing but extremely over priced. Cosmetics aren’t the only overpriced things. Temtem are just as bland as the people they share a world with. Little is ever said to give more insight into what they are or why they're even called Temtem. Multiple times NPCs use not being a Temtemologist as a scapegoat for not having to explain anything. Again, this not being a full game yet can excuse a lack of story. Gameplay is grindy and more like older Pokemon games. Stamina is an annoying alternative to PP as many Tem will just K.O. themselves making a battle feel less earned. _childDocuments_.review: While there are a few aspects of Temtem that I have enjoyed, a bad taste has been left in my mouth which has prompted me to write my first ever review. Unlike many of the other reviews here, I want to emphasize that Temtem is supposed to be an MMORPG first and foremost and not a single player Pokemon game. Therefore my review will proceed with that in mind. - Art style. This is mostly up to personal preference and in my opinion looks great. It's very vibrant with a variety of colors and textures.- Music. Once again this is up to personal preference and in my opinion sounds good. There does seem to be a lack of original songs, but the ones that are in the game are both relaxing and fit the theme.- Combat system. The combat system both contains original and beaten to death mechanics. The stamina bar is an interesting addition which prevents you from simply spamming the same OP moves over and over again. Additionally, the moves themselves have time out periods and interactions with each other which increase the level of depth. People that plan on playing competitively would be sure to enjoy the combat. Now as for the reason why this is under mixed, at the end of the day this is a combat system from 20 years ago with a few revisions. I can understand the logic behind "if it ain't broke don't fix it", but come on it's 2020. At the very least add some unique ways to interact with your Temtems in battle or include an element of skill. For example, perhaps you can physically control your Temtems during certain attacks to decide weather or not they can successfully land or dodge the move. Instances like this can be player controlled to make the combat more interesting and require the player to work on things such as their reaction time to succeed.- Animations. From what i've seen, the animations can look really good at times. Moves such as the wind attack look, sound, and feel very impactful. On the other hand, there are moves where the Temtems are simply moving in place or jumping. Considering the lack of Temtems available currently, I believe the animations should be more consistant and improved. Unlike regular Pokemon, Temtem has both the power of a PC and a much smaller pool of Temtems to work on. I am not saying each Temtem needs unique animations and interactions but some of the current ones are not acceptable.- It's not an MMORPG. Temtem is simply a single player experience with a few online interactions. Currently you can battle and trade with other players much like regular Pokemon. The only difference being you can see people running around. If you want to call your game an MMORPG, at the very least it should allow for interactions between players and a game chat. There is a coop mode in the game currently but it never seems to work and all you have available for communications are a few emotes. This is completely unacceptable considering the MMORPG aspect was supposed to be the main draw of Temtem.- Story. Not much to be said for this category, it's linear and boring. They attempt to make things more interesting by adding side quests and extra dialogue options but I feel they fell short. Both are repetitive and uninteresting. Very comparable to Pokemon in this regard, but even shorter and linear.- Lack of content. The main meat of the game can be completed within 10 hours. Aside from that, everything else seems to be a WIP. I understand it's an early access game and it's par for the course, but seriously they cloned Pokemon for the most part and barely added anything original, was it really so time consuming that they couldn't add more content?- The Temtems. My issue is not the Temtems themselves, but the lack of variety. In the first 70% of the game you will encounter the same 9 Temtems. This gets old very fast and is really disappointing compared to the 160+ Temtems that are supposed to be in the game. Once you get access to surfing this number jumps to a staggering 17 Temtems. That's right, aside from a few "special" areas you have access to 17 Temtems. The "special" areas only have another 5 or so Temtems bringing the grand total to under 30. I hope you can see why I am disappointed after learning this.So would I recommend this game to other players? If you are a fan of the Pokemon series then yes, with all it's flaws it's still a decent experience. However, that's only if the game was reasonably priced. Currently the game is available for over $40 CAD which is complete non-sense. I would consider a fair valuation to be around $20 CAD. So until then, I would hold off on the game unless they add a lot of content.

_childDocuments_.review: Temtem is difficult to recommend for almost anyone. The graphics, music, characters, and monster-taming gameplay are all cheery and pleasant at their first glance. But once you begin digging into the game, it becomes nothing more than grinding and fetch quests. Quests are basic "talk to person and report" affairs which send you from one end of the map and back again several times, with little reward other than having an artificial progress gate lifted or receiving a passing "thanks" from the quest giver. Each quest consists of nothing more than text boxes playing out generic dialog with no personality. Quest markers are indistinct and hard to read on the game map. And locations, characters, and monsters have very unmemorable and overly complex names, making it difficult to keep track of what you're doing. The game does not have any of the depth that an adult player would be looking for in a Pokéclone--it's just a long slog back and forth across colorful environments that feel very copy-pasty.While I wanted to enjoy my time with the game, I felt like that time was being wasted, as I hurtled from one end of the map to the other, not caring about the quests that I was completing and dreading every tall-grass/water encounter along the way because of the further wasted time. Add in incorrect character models appearing while reporting quests, and the laziness of the whole affair became too much to ignore. The game isn't worth my time, and 30 hours was enough lost life spent on generic rubbish.When it comes to kids, however, this could be a nice game to sit them down with to while away the hours, as it is definitely intended to be a time sink. But this is also a difficult recommendation, for two reasons: 1) They could be playing something much better. And, 2) "The Agenda" is in full effect in Temtem, complete with pronoun selections and love confession quests.Temtem feels very much like a product that someone was instructed to create to meet a business goal, rather than an expression of someone's genuine creative vision. If it was the only game that you have, it's harmless enough. If you have other games to play, you're probably better off playing those other games.

_childDocuments_.review: As a player with around 150 hours ish myself, I can vouch for the game's awesomeness. Here goes:Holy Temtem, this game is a wild ride! If you're a fan of MMOs and creatures with cute faces, Temtem will knock your socks off. The game is a blend of Pokemon and World of Warcraft, but with its own unique flair. Let me break it down for you.First off, the story campaign is an absolute blast. You journey across six islands, each with its own set of challenges and quirky characters. And let's not forget the evil Clan Belsoto, who are just begging to be taken down. The graphics are stunning and the world-building is top-notch. You'll feel like you're really part of the world, especially since the game is massively multiplayer. Yes, that's right, other players are all around you, living the adventure with you, and fighting to become the best Temtem tamer.Speaking of multiplayer, the co-op adventure is where the game truly shines. You can team up with a friend and take on the world together. Catch new Temtem, complete a Route, or face off against a Temtem Leader, all while fighting alongside your friend in dual battles! And when you need a break from all the action, you can head back to your own house in Atoll Row and decorate it your way. Buy new furniture, color your walls, and invite your friends over. It's like The Sims, but with adorable creatures and epic battles.Customization is another standout feature. You can make your character stand out from the crowd and get new cosmetics while you battle other tamers. Pick a silly hat, a comfy sweatshirt, some pants, and you're ready to go! Or maybe you prefer to wear a full-on cosplay of your favorite Temtem? The choice is yours, and it's all about expressing yourself and having fun.Finally, the competitive aspect of the game is not to be missed. You choose eight Temtem, and then the pick and ban phase will begin. Take turns with your rival to pick your Temtem and ban theirs. When all the decisions are made, and the turns are ended, you will end up with a squad of five Temtem, and the battle will begin. It's an intense, strategic battle of wits and monsters, and it's addictively fun.In summary, Temtem is an exceptional MMO with all the features you could want, including a great story campaign, a massive online world, co-op adventure, housing, customization, and competitive battles. It's a game that's easy to pick up, but hard to put down. So, grab your controller, choose your Temtem, and get ready for an adventure of a lifetime. You won't regret it!- mDriveUnit

Most NPC trainers on the island will have the evolved version oft hose Temtem, spoiling you the surprise of evolving them on your own to see what they turn into.So the game has a good and fun combat system, but they really overdo with repetitive battles against the same temtem all the time. So if you are looking forward to catching them all you will get plenty of chances as you fight your 400th bird or pig.I personally don't think the game looks all that great, but that is mostly a style choice, everything is soft and squishy looking. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game, but it has many flaws that are hard to ignore. It feels like a standard pokemon game without any of the charm. You're stuck in a multiplayer setting, and while you don't have to battle other players, you will encounter some with evolved versions of the tems that you are grinding to evolve for yourself, which ruins the satisfaction of discovering the evolution for yourself. Gameplay/Combat - 4/10The combat follows a unique new stamina system instead of using PP like in Pokemon, which I actually found to be more fun. It forces you to think harder about the moves you are using, which is a much more interesting approach to the system. Unfortunately, I think this is the only good thing I can say about the combat. This game will not let you take more than 10 steps without being sucked into a fight. Typically, this would be sort of manageable if the "wild areas" were smaller, but that's not the case. If you choose to fight in every encounter, it can take you just under an hour just to reach the next town. Now, I'd have less of an issue with this if there was more variety in the monsters, but there isn't. There's been times where I face the exact same monster 5 times in a row, each time in different encounters. There is also a huge issue with the level design, where you will face other trainers more often than you would in a pokemon gym. This is so annoying, especially in the starting areas because your monsters are so weak that a small gust of wind can wipe your whole party. When you have forced encounters every 20 steps with random encounters in between, it's nearly impossible to enjoy exploring the world, because you're constantly being taken out of it. I should mention that there are items you can use in order to prevent random encounters from happening, but I can't say that they're worth the money since the currency is already so hard to come by (also the prices of cosmetics are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ high, I can't recommend buying those either.) While the combat system is cool, I think the gameplay has too many combat interruptions that take away from the joy of exploring, or even just trying to get where you need to be. It's at the point where I dread walking into new areas because of how repetitive the nature of the game is. (I understand that jrpgs are meant to follow a "random encounter" based system, but they have not balanced this game in a way that makes the system fun or interesting to deal with.)Story/Characters- 0/10I haven't gotten very far into the story, but here's what I can say about the characters. If you think pokemon NPCs are shallow, these ones are worse. Nearly every person who "knows" my character has said the same thing with different words. It feels like there are no real friendships/relationships with the characters in the story either. Each NPC is just a dull character archetype with no real personality to make their interactions more enjoyable. There are dialogue options, but they do nothing to make these conversations any more interesting. It does give you the option to be rude to people, but there is no weight to anything anyone says. The villains are your typical "team rocket" goons, which already makes me feel like I've played this game before. I guess a redeeming quality of all of this is that some interactions are more mature than others. A few characters have said some more adult words, which reminds me that this game is not entirely designed for children. However, this doesn't make any interaction with the entities in the game any more enjoyable. Monster design - 6/10If this game does anything right, I'd say it makes some cool looking monsters. I'm a big fan of the way they reinvented the typing system (though I do think keeping it more similar to pokemon would make it more accessible and less convoluted). I also think it was cool how they decided the thresholds for when monsters evolve. Instead of leveling up at a static level, they will instead level up once they have gained a certain amount of levels since the time you catch them. (if you catch one at level 5 and it needs 15 levels to evolve, then it won't evolve until it's level 20). I think the monsters are pretty unique, though some of them do look like some discount versions of existing pokemon which I'm not a big fan of. My favorite monster so far is Platypet and all of it's evolutions. This game also lets you cross breed different monsters to create new kinds, which is honestly really cool. I haven't made it to that point yet, but knowing it is an option makes me very excited to see what's next. Final thoughts - I think this game is very disappointing in its current state. I know it's early access, so I'm willing to give it another shot once it's had time to really improve itself, but I cannot recommend it to anyone right now. It's as if this game took the ideas from pokemon games, but somehow removed all the fun parts.

_childDocuments_.review: A couple weeks ago when a friend of mine picked up Temtem I was instantly skeptical. I'd never heard of it, it was probably just some mediocre Pokemon clone that'd be buggy, unplayable EA garbage. I would never play this game I said. Then, one night playing some games I had one too many and purchased Temtem, when I woke up I juggled with the idea of refunding it but heck I just got a new job so why not.I was totally blown away by my experience, hours just melted away as I explored Temtem. This game feels like a love-letter to the Pokemon fans of old with challenging battles, puzzles, and exploration. I took my sweet time completing the ~20 hours of story (Having finished just before writing this) so that I could catch rare temtem, breed some others, and explore previous zones with the new tools I earned throughout the games story.One of Temtems main selling points is its multiplayer functionality, you see other players populate the games world and can even challenge the dojo masters, do dungeons, and complete the entire story in co-op. I Played with my twin brother through pretty much all of the story and it was extremely entertaining and fun, and not nearly as buggy as I would have thought at first. Pros:1. Challenging Battles, interesting Puzzles (the 4th Dojo gave me a headache. . .)2. Gorgeous art and excellent animations.3. A surprisingly not terrible story, its not amazing but it was an enjoyable experience (so far!)4. The Stamina system is a vast improvement over Pokemons PP system.5. While only half of the available Temtem are in the game there are many really neat ones!6. 2v2 Battles and "Synergy" Moves add another layer of tactical depth that, when combined with the stamina system, makes the game feel more engaging and dynamic than Pokemon.7. Much less buggy than you would think, I haven't had a crash or frame drop as of yet but there have been a couple situations.Cons:1. The lack of variety and diversity of Temtem, at least early in the game, made battles feel monotonous sometimes.2. It's early access, have had a couple strange bugs like getting trapped in a conversation and having to restart.3. Only about 20 hours of story so far.4. Without spoiling anything, one part of the story takes away your Temtem and tools (Like the surfboard) and you have to use another team of Temtem for ~1 hour of gametime and that was really frustrating.5. While I suspect this game will eventually have a massive and explorable world it felt restrictive seeing all the "Work in Progress" signs that littered the games world.TL;DR: Whats here is incredibly promising, if Crema can keep a reasonable update schedule and continue to squash bugs Temtem will be a huge hit. It really feels like a love-letter to the genre and a callback to Pokemon games like Ruby and Sapphire. For die-hard pokemon fans I can suggest getting the game now, for more casual fans or first-timers I'd wait for an update or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access Impression:Pros:-Refreshing take on Pokemon's blueprint.-Trait and Stamina system in combat (Having no stamina will hurt your monster if you attack too much, it's a replacement for the Power Point system. And traits are just different perks a Temtem can have upon capture or evolution.)-Swappable skills instead of permanently replacing them-Customizable character (Subjective PoV since maybe some people like a certain look for a mc.)Cons:-Clearly shows you it's in Early Access (Subjective PoV...WIP signs on houses and signs on routes clearly saying more to come.-Chat Box doesn't work (Subjective...this could be a pro too...)-IVs are still implemented (Subjective PoV...This basically means they want you to grind immensely to make a perfect stat-ed Temtem, and attempting to make one of those would be a huge time and money sink.-Controversy exists over pronouns...(My PoV, but I think it's silly. It's about the character creation allowing you to choose "they/them" as your pronoun. Not exactly the biggest controversy tbh)-Server issues (The main defacto mundo Con. Some people argue over disconnects, I got one, and then reconnected with a very short queue.)Suggestions:-Add achievements-Add events for Lumas and other Temtem later on in post-launch development-Add events in general-Add aesthetics as rewards-Polish up the UI-More, better, memorable, music. (Different music in dojos, encountering your rival and other important events, etc.)

_childDocuments_.review: The initial play through is extremely fun. I don't believe the game is worth what they're asking for ($40ish), so you'd be better off waiting for a sale. After you've completed the story portion of the game, there's not much else to do besides mindlessly grind repetitive tasks like it's your job. I did that for awhile, caught some Lumas (shiny Pokemon) and amassed quite the Pansun fortune, but it's empty. This game has very low replay/post story value, imo.For example, every week there is a very specific fish you have to catch in order to claim a prize. This can take many nights worth of hours to catch. You are constantly catching and releasing fish, sitting through the encounter animation screen each time, searching for one with the very specific pattern for that week. After players complained it was too tedious, Crema's response was to guarantee the "right" fish after one thousand tries. It's still tedious, the guarantee number just used to be higher. Die hard Crema fans get really defensive and insist it ONLY took THEM a few hours, so it's not THAT big of a deal. The fact is it's RNG. It won't always take everyone only a few hours. It can and does take much longer. The only guarantee is after 1k tries. It was outrageous and blasphemous when I suggested lowering the guarantee number to 600 tries. This is just one example of a post story, busy work activity that gets old fast. Doesn't feel like you're playing a game, feels more like you're completing chores. There are other games I would rather play that are more rewarding and worthy of my time.The game has competitive potential, but the community is super limited. Crema is not making player-friendly decisions (rather financial friendly for themselves), so I wouldn't expect growth in this part of the game either.TL;DR The story is fantastic and worth the play through. The post story activities are uninspired and not worth sticking around for. Low long term competitive potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Man I really want to love this game as much as I love other creature collector titles, but unfortunately temtem just doesn't do enough to try and differentiate itself from pokemon. The plot, while admittedly being much more engaging and overall of a higher writing quality than pokemon still retains many of the conventions from said game that I personally feel bog the game down and prevent too much innovation from occurring. It feels as if the only reason we have a rival, gyms (or rather dojo's), and an evil team is just to be able to check all the boxes on the now 20 year old formula. This game does make considerable efforts to make the actual player experience better, and in some cases this is true with there being many features pokemon does not have like being able to freely swap active moves or being able to have rematches with the gym leaders, and even the difficulty of the game honestly feels pretty good as I often felt that my skills were legitamately being tested along the way. The issues crop up when you see that the game has nonsensical movesets for half of the creatures, with a majority of their moves not complimenting their stats (an example of this off the top of my head would be nessla, which specializes in special attacks but has its strongest water move as physical for some reason), and the re-introduction of the iv system (called sv's in this game). For those unfamiliar with competitive pokemon this is basically a system where upon catching a new creature each stat is randomly assigned numbers which determine how high/low that stat is, with no way to ever change that stat short of just getting a new one. The only way to circumvent this is to go through the process of breeding, which can sink dozens if not hundreds of hours just to have a creature with the stats it should just have from the start. In my 12 years of competitive pokemon experience, this is one of the communities least favorite mechanics as outside of extremely niche stat spreads you always just want them all to be maxed out, so it serves no purpose other than to add more arbitrary grinding. The last major issue of the game for me is the evolutions, god how I loathe evolution in this game. It is such a simple system, get to a certain level and your creature gets stronger, simple right? Well temtem decided they wanted to be special and change it up a bit, so instead of hitting a set level you need to gain a set amount of levels to evolve. Let me explain this more clearly using an example, the temtem bunbun evolves after gaining 20 levels, meaning that if you catch one at level 32 it will evolve at level 52. This is an issue since you can literally find its evolution on the same route, meaning you can get a bunbun and its evolution at the same level, making it pointless to even get the bunbun in the first place since you would have to be insane to want to handicap yourself by having to wait 20 levels to evolve it when you can just get the evolution right then and there. Personally, I found a this games version of a shiny version of bunbun (which also came with amazing sv's), but I am actively punished for using it since I cannot evolve it for another 20 levels, there are literally wild encounters of this tems evolution with a higher level than mine yet i cannot evolve mine, it just makes no sense to be punished for getting a higher level tem or for getting a good stat roll on a pre-evolution. All of these issues culminate into a game which tries way to hard to be different in all the wrong places while conforming in all the places it should have innovated in, granted most of these issues can be fixed with updates I doubt they will as from what it seems the developers are way more focused on adding newer content rather than looking at what's already in the game, which to their credit makes perfect sense. I can understand the appeal of this game and can clearly see all the love put into it, but unfortunately the experience is just not for me and I don't really see this game as anything more than a pokemon wannabe, which is sad since i truly hate how complacent gamefreak is and would love to see some legitimate competition to force them to make a good pokemon game for the first time in a decade.

_childDocuments_.review: As any early access game it has it's bugs and it had a really rough launch due to problems with the servers. However, the devs have shown a lot of dedication on fixing these issues and actively listen to the community. The game itself is also a really good take on the traditional Pokémon formula along with its own twists that make the game more challenging and strategic than Pokémon itself. Most veteran players that were looking for a more difficult game will very much enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Temtem

_childDocuments_.review: People keep saying that you should like this if you like Pokemon, and that's simply not true. This game forces you to grind your temtem through grass for hours on end and still gives gym NPCs unrealistic advantages (same creatures, same level, but faster and stronger). There is no "git gud" here, it's just not worth the grind due to the NPCs just having unfair advantages.On another note, the quest system is pointless. Doing things for random quest givers makes little to no difference because they give useless rewards. I just can't see this game ever competing with Pokemon for any reason other than its PC compatibility (which is just about the only thing it has going for it).

name: Cloudpunk
detailed_description: Your name is Rania. This is your first night working for Cloudpunk, the semi-legal delivery company based in the sprawling city of Nivalis. You go everywhere, from the Marrow below to the spires that pierce the grey clouds high above before scraping the edge of the troposphere. No delivery job is too dangerous, and no one is faster than a Cloudpunk driver. In this story-based exploration game, you will meet a diverse range of characters including androids, AI and unscrupulous humans at every level of society. Everyone has a story, and in the course of one night in Nivalis, everything will change. Features: Explore an immense vertical cyberpunk city with your hover car and on foot Unravel mysteries in a world of corporate conspiracy, hackers and rogue AI through the eyes of Rania Meet a diverse range of characters and immerse yourself in their everyday lives Your decisions will have a lasting impact on the inhabitants of Nivalis Discover hidden places and items unlocking additional stories

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Why it's 8/10: I only say that because some of the achievements are more difficult to get and I wish it was easier to tell where you are on the map, where you have been and where you've yet to go. Without this, you have to play the guessing game unless you know for sure. REVIEW: Cloudpunk is a very unique game with an interesting story. The characters range from humans, to automata to androids and every character has a unique way of speaking. The little things that you can find in this game are amazing. I found myself caring a lot for the reoccurring characters than I had expected myself to. The message in this game tells about a broken and corrupt city, much like most people live in. It gives you a choice between right and wrong, a choice of whether or not freedom is deserved, a choice that isn't yours to make--but you do because the game needs you to, because the people in the game need you to. The story all spans across one night and I know if I had a night quite like the one that Rania had, I would've quit before the second package was delivered. The main thing in this game is morals, and your actions from your decisions. It makes you think about your choices, it shows you what can become of that. It shows you that sometimes things aren't worth forgetting and sometimes it's worth it to be patient. I definitely recommend this game because it's a very relaxing game about driving around a broken city and delivering packages to broken people. The story, though can be slow, is worth diving into and reaching into every last inch of the map to see everyone and everything. Maybe Nivalis isn't the perfect place, but maybe you can help make it at least a little bit better than what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game for an hour so far, but I think there are some things that can be improved in this game, so I write this:Advantages:1. The main character of the game is female, and the outlook design of the characters is in line with cyberpunk future style.2. The scenery is beautiful, with lots of Japanese and Hong Kong elements to match the cyberpunk style.3. It's amazing to drive the car up and down.4. The minimap has a variety of landmarks to explore, just like Cyberpunk 2077.5.I love the difference between driving from the first-person perspective and driving from the third-person perspective, where you can hear raindrops pounding on the window from the first person perspective.6.The UI is unique when the characters talk.Disadvantages:1. When entering the game for the first time, the voice of the characters and the noise made by the flying vehicles were slightly loud.2. The protagonist can eat food and buy supplies, but it doesn't show whether the protagonist has eaten enough. I think there should be a progress bar showing the satiety of the protagonist.3. After that, some food is eaten immediately and some food is left in the backpack, which makes me a little confused. Would it be better to make them the same?4. When the protagonist walks on the ground, she can switch to the wider third-person perspective, but in the wider third-person perspective, when the protagonist walks around some corners, the perspective changes stiffly.5. The beginner's guide doesn't seem to say that the M button can open the big map. (or I missed it?)6. It would be nice to have an interface that showed the main character's outfit, as well as the car's gear, instead of just showing it all in the backpack.7.Would it be better to add a full novice tutorial to the beginning of the game?  It's a little too sudden to start the game with a delivery.  Maybe you could set up a scenario where the protagonist gets familiar with the structure of the car and tries driving it.In general, I think Cloudpunk is a good game for immersive relaxation. Rushing to complete the game process may lose the fun of playing.By the way, driving from the first-person perspective is much better for me. But when it comes to parking, it's better to switch to the third-person perspective.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic Cyberpunk game. I'm mostly someone who plays multiplayer games and find it harder for myself to get sucked into singleplayer games but I saw the beautiful city planning and gorgeous lighting and had to try the game out. At first I thought I would get bored of the simple gameplay of pickup package > deliver package > pickup new package. But the dialogue of the characters as you go through really set the tone and the atmosphere to the game. By the end of the game I was invested in every character and simply enthralled.I'd find myself parking somewhere and just admiring the views and bustling city around me before heading to the next job. Only real issue I had was sometimes when trying to make a fast delivery the car wouldn't really slip between traffic like I'd like but that's just me being picky to be honest.Anyone wanting a skip dialogue button is missing the entire point of the game. Without dialogue this game is simply aesthetically pleasing but damn the story is what truly make Cloud Punk  my favorite game of 2020Overall 9/10 Absolutely must play for the story and beautiful sights.

I understand that this is an art & design decision and that it wouldn't change the gameplay - it would have opened it up to a much wider audience though.Silky smooth on my GTX1080 on 4KVoices and sound are goodBuy it and surprise yourself at how much a less frenetic game can be enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to tell: this game is a hundred times better experience than Cyberpunk 2077.Sci-fi setting of a decadent future, worthy of the name. Intriguing, engaging.The choices that the player makes are not so incisive on the narrative apart from some feedback through dialogues. But it is a game that ends in about 20 hours only if you get lost by exploring every corner of the map. However I expect to see some real consequences with the upcoming "City of Ghosts" DLC. Or at least I hope so.A masterpiece from an aesthetic point of view: an accurate level design (sometimes the elevators are really annoying though), immersive and original.Few indie games are so well done like Cloudpunk. And what else I can say except that I cried a lot for the finale?It's worth to spend your time playing it. Bye Ben, bye Huxley.
