_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed this 'game', but it wasn't without flaws, as others have said, gameplay is not the focal point, it's more of an interactive story in the same vein as To The Moon and Firewatch, if you go into this game thinking of it like that then you'll know what to expect. Overall it dragged a little, the whole story wasn't exactly to my liking, I feel like it dragged a bit.The good parts are the visuals and atmosphere, it's a very pretty game and I love the style, the music is really fitting too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have thought driving a taxi could be so much fun?THIS is how you make a cyberpunk game. The setting, story, characters, visuals, everything about this game is gorgeous. The driving is just a delivery system for the story, but it's still a lot of fun. It takes a while to get the hang of it, but after a while zipping in and out of traffic and between buildings like a hummingbird becomes (almost) as engaging as the ongoing exposition.This game is relaxing and simple and easy to play, without becoming boring or monotonous. If you want a game to chill out with, this is the game for you. Or if you don't, play it anyway. It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: What initially attracted me to this game was the aesthetics and atmospheric style of gameplay. At first, the game seemed like a generic walking simulator (or rather, "flying" simulator) and the story didn't grab me until a couple of hours into the game. However, after this, the story seemed to pick up the pace and I began to actually be interested in the story and reappearing characters who would appear, in some cases, multiple times throughout the game for certain side quests and as part of the main story. Overall, was this game worth full price? Ehh, I enjoyed it but I'd definitely wait for a sale. Though I can definitely see why people were put off within a short time after starting the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. The script writing is sublime. Not only telling a compelling story but filling it with humor and pathos. Cloudpunk's world feels full and alive, with the streets filled with strange and wonderful characters. Do be warned that this is not Cyberpunk 2077, and the missions are mostly delivery missions. But they rarely feel that way. The writing and characters combine to make what is usually an achievement drudgery in other games feel fresh and exciting. Backed up with a synthwave soundtrack and the evergreen joy of flying a hover car around a megalopolis Cloudpunk is well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the 'wokest' game I ever played, and it shows poorly not just the drivel dialog, but in the game design too.Credit to all the many artists and sound designers who made something very impressive and immersive of this voxel engine, but the story itself was very boring, quite aimless and I'm afraid it falls short on so many levels for a game that it leaves me wondering why I gave it as much of a chance as I did. I think I finished it in a couple of hours, seems like it was made for people who've never gamed before.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed. I'm 5 hours in and I love everything about this game. I am essentially delivering and driving, but also talking to people and learning their stories. I don't know if choices matter, but you make some moral choices and they sometimes wrench my heart. I also love exploring the city. Even though everything is blocky, I find myself stopping on pedestrian crossings to enjoy the view of buildings in some areas. I love the dystopian feel too, and the occasional observations by some characters of toxic capitalism and gentrification. There are some deep thoughts for sure. I recommend this game if you're looking for something chill, beautiful to look at, and like to explore and meet different people. There are also items you can pick up that are marked on the map if you like to collect/find things (I do!).
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it more than I expected to and at the same time also less. The story and themes are not at all subtle, the blocky art style is fun, I can't drive for ♥♥♥♥, if anything happened to my dog I'd kill everyone in the room and then myself. All in all a mixed bag and not something I feel the need to revisit anytime soon, but still worth playing. And definitely grab City of Ghosts, the story feels satisfying enough without it but it's a sequel-length add-on that lets you see the outcome of some of your choices in the core game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Not a definitive "no" here, but enough cons to restrain me from a definitive "yes." So I beat this thing pretty much through pure willpower (and am in a pretty extreme minority based on achievement stats). It overstays its welcome pretty significantly as the hours go by and you realize that you're not really impacting the world or in possession of much agency over it. That would all be well and good if there was a really solidly written story (I literally have a shelf in my Steam library called "Walking Simulators are My Jam:" I am the perfect audience for an experience without much "game" to it), but what you're getting here is very episodic story beats that don't have much connection to one another and are very hit or miss. To give credit where credit is due I have certainly played games with far poorer writing and Cloudpunk undeniably has its moments, but take heed that you're very rarely going to want to play just because you can't WAIT to find out what happens next. If you're cool vibing on this thing for a few hours until its gameplay loop (fly to location, park, walk to location, press button, repeat) starts boring you, with the understanding that you will probably lose interest before the end credits, then I would recommend picking up Cloudpunk. These developers clearly put love into this experience, and the art design can be gorgeous. But unless you push yourself or are a completionist for the sake of it, you probably are not going to be given incentive to see this thing through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a real treat. Excellent visuals, really nailed the aesthetic of a cyberpunk world. Some of the characters are really excellent as well, which is ideal because it is a character driven narrative. I enjoyed every minute of it. I will admit, though, that the steering of the vehicle is a bit clunky and hard to control, which as the primary action you do in this game is a bit too bad. The idea behind the control scheme was probably to try to make it easier but with both keyboard and controller I found it could be hard. That being said, nothing should take away from enjoying a well laid out set of cyberpunk tales woven together by a kind but sassy delivery driver.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: It's an art game, not a game game. Has some cool artistic/visual stuff going on but that gets old after about 10 minutes and what you're left with is a very boring, stereotypical, dime-a-dozen, super generic Cyberpunk story and gameplay that is quite literally 100% a walking/driving simulator. All you ever do is go from point A to point B with almost no variation whatsoever. If the story was actually something better than your average Reddit post then that might be something worth putting up with but it isn't. In the previews, the game looks pretty cool, but once you play it you will quickly realize the world has absolutely no depth to it whatsoever. It's not fun and it's not interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Very weak game design: useless items, copy and paste shops and vendors without meaning, everything feels pointless, because does nothing or almost nothing. Pointless dialogues and useless npcs. Rain under roofs, generic soundtrack, mediocre voice, uninteresting main character, too much uninspired jokes that ruin atmosphere and tone. Only good atmospheric things are cockpit view from car and appartments.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most underrated games in my opinion and is very unique in how different it is to other games out there. Pros:-Ambient music is on point, some of the characters are brilliant and memorable, the flying car you have (HOVA) and apartment, and how you upgrade them, helps to immerse you better, and the story/narrative experience is well worth sitting through. The actual map to explore is very nice too, the artwork may take some getting used to but actually works very well. Cons:-Game can feel a bit "preachy" at times, some one-off NPCs will, for example, lecture you from a non-progressive viewpoint and your character feels like a moral crusader in response. Areas to explore don't feel so memorable/different to each other even though exploring and travelling are still enjoyable. Game is a total steal on a sale price, but at full price £16.99 it's still well-spent in my opinion if you're looking for a futuristic "delivery driver trying to survive in a new, eccentric city environment" game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: There doesn't seem to be much of a game here. However, it's almost completely stress free and that's the good part of it in these isolated times. There are some time trials but it doesn't seem to matter if you pass them or not.Visually this is block graphics. I'm not a fan. Areas seem small and load times long.The most fitting adjective I can think of for this game is dull. You fly around in your little flying car. It's slow and handles like a flying brick. There's other traffic which flies into you without a care. Your car gets damaged but I didn't try to find out what happens if you don't fix it. Likewise there's a gas gauge but again I don't know what happens if you run dry. There are upgrades but they don't seem to do much.Game play consists of flying to nav points, picking up packages and dropping them off. Sometimes passengers too. Dialog and characters were uninteresting. I pushed through the short duration, the last third in the Christmas break.Then there's the story. I don't know what to make of it. There's a choice in the end but the game doesn't seemto bother explaining what the choices mean and doesn't say much about what happened afterwards.I guess I'm flagging this as not recommending it but I don't really care enough one way or the other. Steam really needs a third option for this. Recommends/doesn't recommend/unimpressed?
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Dev team you worked wonders!This game is by far worth more than £16.99 or whatever price it is on sale.First time i looked at the game i thought meh but i was mistaken because the game is story and the graphic style is a bonus but not the main attraction.The story is just phenomenal, I hope we get a sequel or even DLC I'd be happy enough to buy that.I can't explain the game apart from your a delivery driver on your night shift and your life changes from then on.Strongly urge you all to buy it!Stop Reading Buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game so far. If you like the cyberpunk vibe than this game is definitely for you. The world is really interesting and I usually get side tracked doing the side missions and trying to get the achievements, which usually never happens with me, so that shows how interesting this game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: After 5 hours of playing, I can honestly recommend this game. It's fun, The Good: BEAUTIFUL world. When I say "beautiful world," I mean it. The art direction is so phenomenal. I love the mixture of voxel and cyberpunk. The colors really pop and the locations are mostly well-designed. The BUILDINGS... I have spent way too much time just studying the buildings in the background.The soundtrack is PHENOMENAL. I could listen to it all day.Also Camus is best boi.The Decent: Voice-over work. There are a few really decent voice actors in this, while also having some voice actors that could have been better. Namely the main character - she does a decent job but it didn't seem like she had much voice direction? I don't know, but she could have been better. Her deliveries are kind of flat. BUT Control seriously makes up for it; his voice acting is the best in the game.The flight controls. While generally it's pretty okay to move around in the HOVA, ascending and descending is clunky, even after upgrading your HOVA. Turning isn't as tight as it could be.The Not Good: Camera controls. Most of the time you can't control them, which would be fine if they didn't go wonky when turning a corner. I absolutely LOVE when you reach specific scenes and the camera moves to show you the beauty in the background, but then it will do a 180 when you turn a corner around one specific building.The map. Not only is it difficult to understand, but you can't zoom in/out or pan, let alone set markers for navigating. I want to go back to this one NPC who will take old games - no, I have to remember exactly where she was, exactly in which section of the map, while also remembering the sections of the city I have to fly through to get to her.Overall, a genuinely fun game that I would definitely recommend. Flying around the city is relaxing and beautiful and I just... well done job, overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever take time to write reviews but this is a really nice, chill, beautiful game. I love the art style, the music is on point, and the story is way more than I expected going in. I got invested into the characters and the world is very interesting, even the little side NPC people you can talk to. Don't pass up an opportunity to talk to NPC's. I liked going around and trying to find the collectibles in the game, it really gave a way to explore the world and find the random NPC's and sometimes you'd return things you found to them. I really enjoyed watching on of my friends stream this game and I bought it myself to play. I love the ideas of the city and the world and I hope that maybe in the future there is another game that evolves on the world and we can see more of what is happening around in different cities. Overall my personal score for the game is a 9/10 only because I don't know if there is any replay value here but it is a good experience to have and to say you've played. I hope to see more story/explore games set in this world in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The story and voice acting is a little heavy handed, and even sometimes corny, but it has its poignant moments. The graphics are good (as long as you don't look too hard at the holes).Gameplay wise, there isn't an awful lot to do. There is a main story, and a few sidequests, but there isn't a big post-game or anything. Even the main game doesn't do much to spin on the main gameplay loop. Despite the fact that the main character is poor and trying to work their way up the city, there isn't really anything in the way of resource management. Despite the fact that the main character works for a legally grey company, there isn't really much in the way of evading the authorities that isn't directly scripted. There's no natural or emergent gameplay, only what is scripted.Also the main character is dumb as rocks and asks what's in every package. Every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly captivating game which oozes atmosphere and mixes both nostalgia (I first started gaming in the 70's) and charm, slowly pulling you into its beautifully realised world.AAA games - with their realistic graphics and generic, repeated tropes - should look at this and bow their heads in shame.Was not sure about buying it (despite being utterly compelled to do so, after watching trailers and reviews) and decided to take the plunge: so glad I did!Sincerely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: One question: Would you like to drive a hover car across a future cyberpunk city? Fly all over, see the sights, deliver cargo, maybe walk around a bit, grab some sushi, and meet interesting people that may need your help? Then this is the experience for you!PS. You may become a terrorist in the process OKAY HAVE FUN!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and well worth the money. The game has been developed with a lot of care and is solid, no glitches that I have found so far. The premis of the game is unusual, a delivery driver having adventures and damn good fun, the game play is smooth and fluid. The atmosphere is well done and even pixel worlds can give a great atmosphere, complete with the Vangelis style soundtrack. So whats not to like, just get it. A good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is an interesting game, and concept, that relies ENTIRELY on it's story. However in order for this game to rely on that, the story itself has to be somewhat good, and guess what, it isn't.The gameplay of this game is total hogwash. It doesn't exist, instead you just control a flying car, that has horrible controls, and are delivering packages and what not to people. This game is basically USPS simulator 2021. And don't even get me started on the money system, its god awful, especially the quest of getting all the punch cards and giving them to this one lady for her to only say give me more.The story is decent I'll give it that, the voice acting is marvelous, however in my playthrough, I was never really connected to the characters at all, that includes Rania and Camus, why you ask? Well simply put Rania is to arrogant to even like, and then Camus is an annoying companion. I truly wish there was a way to skip main story dialogue like how you can skip useless characters dialogue.That brings me to my next point, the useless characters, why do the exist? Who knows only the people that made this game know, for in my opinion they are an easy achievement and you move on without even thinking about them.I must commend the creators of this game however, for they tried making a game that was unique and a bit interesting to play, but failed to add any substantial gameplay or at least make the story somewhat enjoyable. For playing this game it's like controlling the main character in a movie, and having no control what so ever on what they say, and or their responses to other NPCS in the game.In the end I do not recommend this game for people who expect to play a game that is based in a Cyberpunk world with possible good gameplay and a good story, for this game only does good on 1 of those 3 things, and that is it makes a decent cyberpunk world. That's it, and if you want to try this game out, buy it on sale, that's what I did, because frankly it is an insult to pay $20 for this hogwash of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a beautiful voxel-based game that takes place in a large Cyberpunk styled world. The story is highly compelling and often gets emotional as your decisions can impact the way the game ends whether it is in a good, bad, or neutral way. The gameplay itself is very relaxing and enjoyable, especially while exploring the multiple places where you can park and explore the city. Overall I highly recommend Cloudpunk to anyone looking for a visually stunning and relaxing game with a compelling story.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: If, like me, you're such a fanboy of Blade Runner that you would do almost anything to spend some time in that dystopian universe, then I recommend you buy this game!Seriously, Cloudpunk seems to be a slightly minecraft-ish take on the Blade Runner universe, with a noir story and fantastic soundtrack thats more than a little Vangelis.Me likey.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: Stylistic, but it works for atmosphere. 6/10Story: Blatant at times about real-life parallels, but manages not to get stale and predictable. 7/10Gameplay: heheh floaty car... 7/10NPCs: Endearing and silly,but believable, like the first time you reached that first settlement in Fallout 3 and had a giggle. 8/10It's oddly relaxing for a game that relies on just a couple of mechanics. It's a manner of telling story that worked in Red Dead Redemption 2, and just as well here: perfected dialogue over gameplay that's just stimulating enough to keep you busy while you're engaged in the story. It hits you with a couple of rather blatant moral decisions, which could have been less on-the-nose, but nonetheless, I've played this game for two days straight riding around in my HOVA, giggling at NPCs and genuinely concerning over the people I've met in-game. A fun, down-to-earth, atmospheric delivery game that occasionally reminds you of its opinions on ethics and society. 7/10 Overall. There's plenty to do and I see myself dumping many more hours into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Good and bad, so I'm overall positive here - this is a series of fetch quests where the joy is just riding around this bizarre voxel crafted city, and is generally a comfy time. You are a member of a delivery service. I loved much of this aspect, but what was really strange and terrible, was interjecting modern day political issues in a far-flung future where everything should be alien. It's strange and ruins the immersion. Thankfully enough that cringe only happens on occasion but I had a good time... the short stories were largely fantastic.There were just a few strange bizarre continuity oddities that I noticed.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk, in my opinion is a missed opportunity.The idea is so cool, story is engaging visual is amazingbut the idea of having many store and an apartment but does not affect the story in any way shape of form isextremely disappointing.But all and all would recommend this to who ever is interested in the cyberpunk genre. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Not a long game, but a good quality story, unique graphics, and a real sense of heart.  I thought it was excellent value for the money, and it feels great to be able to support this kind of product - and a group of people who clearly put a lot of effort into building something with vision and style.  If you love the original Blade Runner and can do without nonstop shooting and the gritty Hobbesian future of Deus Ex or Cyberpunk 2077, the "other punk" is a fun little game that you'll probably enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The ambient in this game is great!It's a slow paced linear adventure where you'll enjoy a great story told through a lot of dialog.Not a game for the itchy trigger gamers, but one of the cerebral and aventure game lovers amongst you.If you enjoy CyberPunk, a good story and are not in a rush to get through a game, you'll have a blast with CloudPunk.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface by saying, I am someone who is VERY poor financially. I cannot work full time due to disabilities, have had to live on foodstamps twice in my life, and currently live in a trailer. I know what it is like to live at the bottom of the food chain in a capitalistic society.The approach this game takes, and that many games/tv shows with strong stance on political injustice and that want to change the world (which is not an inherently bad thing) is that it fails to actually connect with the struggles and the pains that people who suffer from illness, poverty, and loss of loved ones, and instead uses them as a platform to make a point.I liked this game a lot at first. But after a while, it just became an insanely bleak, pessimistic take on the world we live in. It felt very black and white and very childish, when it could have taken the time to explore in depth what it means to BE these people. To feel what it feels to have been hurt and lost, and help us understand and grow and become stronger.The quest that really ended it for me was when Bill, who previously lost his brother Gill to suicide, is played up as a complete idiot who has  This is so cartoonishly villany that it broke any suspension of disbelief I had. The main character (who I did like for most the game) proceeds to just yell at him for being to stupid to realize what was happening. I closed the game, and uninstalled it. I really vibed with the first 6-7 hours with this game. But the themes never go deeper than "Rich bad, poor people good."Everyone in this game is either terrible or in a terrible situation. And the creators just blame the city. Everybody wants someone to blame. They want there to be clear right and wrong, for there to be sides, and they want to be on winning side. It is OKAY to be angry about these things. It just feels like the devs never moved through that anger, and still need to express that through this game and perhaps the new one coming out. I imagine if thats the realm you live in, you will enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry a few times. Literally. It have awesome plot simple gameplay, great voice acting and UNREAL cyberpunk atmosphere. I think after my little adventure night in Nivalis i don't want play C2077 anymore, Cloudpunk showed me the real sadness of buisy neon nights in megacity. I think i played games too long, and now i just want to rest. 10 suicide elevators of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, very atmospheric and well put together. The flows nicely and there is always something to do, but you never feel rushed or pulled in different directions. Having story choices is nice too, makes it feel more involved.Relaxing and enjoyable. Would probably turn the sound fx down a bit, the other cars driving hum a little loudly.Otherwise fantastic game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic atmosphere, but with a forgettable story and abysmally boring gameplay. Drive around from point A to point B collecting stuff and delivering stuff. You can also walk around from point A to point B collecting stuff and delivering stuff.Full price is laughable for such an incredibly shallow gameplay loop masked over with hours of mediocre dialogue and afterthought systems like collectibles, apartment/vehicle customization, and a story that drags on forever to nowhere interesting. Wait for sale, or just watch someone else play through. You won't be missing much.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an ambitious fusion of visual novel and open world RPG in which the former excels and the latter lacks. That being said, the clever writing and unique voice acting alone makes this worth a play-through, especially the main character who is one of those rare believable female protagonists.I enjoyed driving in the city through multiple ways to get to your destinations including taking highways for speed or swerving between buildings to generate shortcuts all while skillfully dodging traffic. In contrast, being on foot was sorely boring as it boils down to holding your joystick toward your destination while hoping you don't take a wrong turn. This is partly due Cloudpunk's RPG mechanics of the game lacking in any meaning, such as buying from food stalls that don't affect your character, buying things for your apartment, and picking up stuff off the ground (I was never compelled to open my inventory), so there felt little to do while on foot other than admiring the views.While these unpolished side-activities can distract from the main strength of the game (the story), they can be ignored. But my main criticism is the loading screens between city areas that interrupt the flow of dialogue and detract from the experience. This happens too often since Cloudpunk revolves flying through while you're accompanied by continuous conversation. If possible, if would've been well worth it to have long empty tunnels between city areas where you could discretely load.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is primarily about the vibes, the atmosphere, the soundtrack. If you've ever wanted to just sort of live in that scene near the beginning of Blade Runner for a while, this is the game for you. Mechanically the game is fairly simple and largely based around fetch quests, but there's some good audio narration going on. Play with headphones.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Experience the night shift of a delivery girl on a cyberpunk city by driving around on your hover-car. The concept of this game is simply brilliant, but the execution is sadly not up to par. This is a game that could've used more polish to reach cult classic status, but as is, will remain an enjoyable, but average experience.The game uses voxels to represent the world, and although at moments the city can look stunning, the same can not be said of the characters, whose models and animations are downright bad. The level design of the city is also poor, with a very utilitarian layout that never tries to make you believe the city is alive.The story, while having a couple interesting concepts, feels unpolished, forcing its beats to reach an epic ending that it didn't need and doesn't feel related to the protagonist' story at any moment. While the game is filled with choices, none will have any impact on the story, apart from off-hand remarks here and there, again, unrelated to the main story.As long as you are a person that can overlook mediocrity to enjoy concept, I recommend this game. You will have a handful of fun hours flying around the city of Nivalis.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game was just what I needed right now and everything I wanted in a Cyberpunk game, flying cars, pixel art, and a great story. I found myself stopping a lot and taking in the city. I took my time with the game and finished in in 14 hours. I'm thinking about doing another play though to see how different choices add up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely review games but this one is a pearl.If you like Blade Runner and cyberpunk ambience then this is for you.I can talk all the great things about this game, the atmosphere, the music, the storyline, the city, the storyline again,I don't like games that look like minecraft but this one i can get past it.It has 32:9 aspect ratio support and now 5.1 surround sound as well to make you feel the world around.The game mechanics are good and they work well as a filler but they are there to be that. No easy no hard mode, It's just relaxed gameplay and full of intrigue.Going on 5 hours play time of this review and i want it to last forever and want to know more of this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: They ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NAILED the Bladerunner feel. The city just drips with distopia and the soundtrack is fantastic! Using VorpX I played the game a little in VR and it was AMAZING. _childDocuments_.review: A fun little game with a lot of navigating through an amusing, bright, futuristic world that is reminiscent of Tron or a Daft Punk video. The graphics and experience of seeing the world are fun in and of themselves. The gameplay, an intriguing and involving story, only enhances the experience. _childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not polished enough to justify a  $20 price tag. If the game were $10, I would be giving a more positive review. There a few bugs in the game that are frustrating enough to make you quit out. Most importantly--one of the bugs FORCES YOU TO QUIT OUT. After 2 or 3 updates already, the devs have still not fixed an issue where the character gets stuck in the most random areas. Sometimes you will be walking up stairs and get stuck, even when nothing is around you to block you in. What is more frustrating is that other characters will block you into small areas and there is nothing that can be done to free yourself other than to quit the game. Additionally, the game stutters on even the highest of specs with your PC as I have seen in other reviews/posts, and when the character is running horizontally across the screen (which is about 30% of the time) it feels like you are playing at 30fps because of how rough the running animation is. There are positives to the game as well. It has a very pleasing aesthetic and and a great soundtrack. It is relaxing when you are not stuck in a corner, and does not really have any consequences that I have come across at this point which allows for a very stress free experience.A good game--but not a not a good $20 game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely game. Don't be fooled : it is more like an interactive movie than a game. The only gameplay is delivering packages or people all over the city. Everything is in the level design and the story.The city is gorgeous, eerie. The cyberpunk vibe is definitely there. It's best enjoyed in first person though (press X and scroll up).Apart from the city, it's the dialogues that makes the game enjoyable. They're not too present and you don't have a lot of choices, but when you do have choices the game doesn't really tell you if it was a good or a bad choice. You're left with your choice in utter silence while you continue to drive. It makes you think.It's a good game to play in short sessions to relax.Finished it in 12 hours while trying to catch collectibles for a while. It can probably be rushed in 8 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: So in six hours, I've beat the game. Now, if I could recommend this game, and also NOT recommend this game I would. Here's why:Pros:1. The theme, aesthetic, and overall feel is SUPERB. Whoever did the world building nailed it, there's a few discrepancies where it falls short, but its very well done. 2. The plot is pretty good! The entire story arc is well done, and would have been even better if not for the terrible voice acting. 3. Controls are nice and simple, and easy to learn. 4. The music is awesome, and fits the theme perfectly. If only it would consistently play throughout the game, and not through scripted start flags only. Cons: 1. Voice acting. Its terrible. There are a few characters that shine, but the majority of voice acting in the game is either non-interesting or just plain bad. In one case, a little girl's voice actor sound like a full grown adult with the pitch shifted too high. I found myself skipping most of the voice lines to read the subtitles instead. 2. Waiting around. One of the first things cloudpunk tells you, is to never be late delivering a package. But more often then not you find yourself waiting around in your HOVA for a navpoint, while either a bad voice actor fills your ears or for the voice lines to even start at all. This may be a cause of my tendency to rush through missions, some other players who like to take their time may not experience this. That's all I have. Overall, the game is good, but good have been great if a few of the cons were addressed. I'd recommend this game, but only if you're willing to look past bad voice acting and the other issues listed above. If you have the spare cash and about ten hours of time, give Cloudpunk a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of those old dystopian sci-fi films then you owe it to yourself to give this game a go! Check.You just can't experience this anywhere else!To top it off, the developers are so in touch with the players... With may features being released (and upcoming) that were inspired by community feedback (Just check out the amazing first-person gameplay!)In short, this is an amazing experience that you'll keep coming back to. It looks beautiful. It sounds stunning. You'll find something new every time you play....Go ahead, just give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 this game is what I needed to scratch that Sci-Fi itch. I loved everything they did, to the story to the world, to the sounds of the city and the music, all of it is perfect. I wish this was multiplayer, I want to roam the city with a friend. _childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I wish that I could return Cloudpunk. The basic premise -- a discrete courier in a cyberpunk dystopia -- is fairly solid. The execution leaves a lot to be desired. Overall, there's the  of a good game here. However, there's no challenge to the gameplay itself, and nothing interesting to see while you're playing. I would have wanted to see some challenge while driving, some hidden side to the world while walking, and something to emphasize the illicit nature of what you do  rather than a disconnected info-dump from talking head. Oh, interesting characters would be nice, too.I'm a sucker for cyberpunk, so admittedly I have high standards. That said, I'm also willing to forgive a game that nails the basics and feels right, even if it has some flaws. While I wanted Cloudpunk to be good, I quickly found myself wondering why I was bothering. Again, good idea, poor execution. Hopefully, next time they'll do better.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- amazing city atmosphere and design- great soundtrack- very nice story- phenomenal voice actors! (Rania <3)- eye-candy voxel graphicsCons:- flying's a bit wobbly and funky but you get used to it- could use some more upgrades to the HovaIt's a very good and thought out game. Firstly, the city is amazing - I kept flying around just looking into small "streets", buildings tucked together next to each other, small, warm-lit windows and the general look of a crowded city. The bloomy and colorful lighting gives it a mesmerising feel and you can really feel Nivalis breathe.The storyline is also good, not that long (I finished it in ~10h) but you can still fly around after completing it and do side quests (79 achievements!). Characters are interesting, the voice actors are pleasant to listen to and all in all the game was an experience I'll definitely come back to.Graphics - 9/10Sound: 10/10Story: 9/10Controls: 7/10Difficulty: lowReplayability: yes!Overall: 8+/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Dame with the Dog.I wasn't expecting anything when I decided to play it. I didn't know anything about the game, I didn't read any reviews either. I just saw "punk" in the title, and it was on sale, so I thought it would be a good deal. And it was! Surprisingly, I liked the game. This is unlike any game I've played. For me, the gameplay is relaxing. No violence, no rush. The graphic style is fun and pleasant to look at. It was interesting to explore the game world. The narrative is also engaging. And due to the excellent soundtrack, the game world has become even more atmospheric. I really like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Dropped the game after playing it for 7 hours. I must confess I'm not a fan of visual novels, which is what this game is at its core. You just go from point A to point B to hear people tell endless uninteresting stories that go nowhere, with poor characterization and jokes. After a while I used the space bar to speed up "dialogs" (you never chose your replies), and even with this it took ages to the point the exploration/driving part was no longer fun enough to endure those phases. Add to this a map that shows highways where there aren't and no indication about levels, ie whether you are above or below your goal and how to access it. Call it bugs, or tricks to increase game lifetime, anyway this quickly gets very tedious.Cloudpunk gives the feeling the game designer, writer and art director didn't work on the same game which ended up being as pretty as it is dreadfully boring. Wish they made or will make another game with this art direction and music. A missed opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy how casual the game is even though it's quite immersive in sound, visual aesthetics as well as the story that I'm inserted into during the entire experience.  I really love wandering the walkways and driving the streets of Nivalis exploring and even just picking up items.  I would have liked to have a little more freedom of choice during some of the NPC dialogues as well as some branching story arcs depending on my decisions.  Overall, I really love the game experience and it's just the kind of casual encounter I'm looking for at the end of the night to wind down and kick back to!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Its fun to drive around a super futuristic city in a hovercar, just living the life... but jfc the writing is so cringey and preachy. I love hearing all the colourful characters and their stories... but I don't want to hear what is obviously the writer(s) pushing their dumbass politics down my throat. I don't mind politics in games but there's this thing called subtlety...Anyway, great if you just want a drive through a cool blade runner ass scifi setting. Not so great if you don't like having agenda pushed on you with the grace of an obese, lost panda on MDMA trying to gently caress a stick of bamboo from a koala, or whatever the ♥♥♥♥ they eat.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, my review is "tainted" and informed by other reviews I read of the game on Steam but they are true. Visually, the game is beautiful most of the times and even breathtaking at times. Unfortunately, it took me 8 hours to realize that there is not much more to this game than the visual splendour.PLEASE DON'T COMPARE THIS GAME WITH THE BLADE RUNNER FILM. While it has a variety of neo-noir and cyberpunk visual elements like neon lights, rain etc. and while they have done a good job of it, the game severely lacks in an interesting story, characters or any sense of purpose or direction. I don't mind a direction-less or purpose-less game per say but I don't like a game that pretends to have one, without any substance to back it up. Like some other reviewers have already noted, the game can be VERY PRETENTIOUS AND PREACHY at times. I am fine with a character or some characters in the game being pretentious but playing the role of a preachy protagonist is a big turn off, especially since you have so little real choice or agency in the narrative. All of this becomes especially annoying since you cannot skip the dialogues. Also something which other reviewers have mentioned and apparently even got blocked by the developer for a suggestion to have skippable dialogues. That too, left a really bad taste in my mouth. If you are alright with or even enjoy the things that I don't like, you might love the game. Visually, its amazing how they could have constructed such a vast and detailed landscape. Driving through it is fun but I did not find anything else worthwhile to do in the game. Unfortunately, I realized all of this after 8 hours of gameplay so I am not sure if I will get a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Love it, the story is actually keeping me invested and playing the world is huge and so colorful and feels so life like of course I have my problems but that's with every game The camera is my biggest one i want to see all of this beautiful world but when I'm in the apartment an i go on the balcony i can only barely see the world cause I cant move my camera But the story is beautiful in its own way
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: While the main story is pretty cheesy and predictable, the atmosphere of the game was surprisingly good. The music managed to suck me into the whole "dystopian but with a faint glimmer of hope" mood of the game and the game did a good job of making me feel like my choices made a meaningful difference. I've played many AAA titles with far worse voice acting.The only thing that really felt off was that while the story had me scratching a living off the bottom, I was pretty much rolling in cash almost from the beginning. So, when I was given several opportunities to keep things rather than turn them in, there was really no reason for me to stray from the high road. I also think I got to meet the "main character" a little too early, as in... why would they even notice or care about me at that point. And perhaps more importantly, why did the player character seem so uninterested, seeing as only minutes earlier she seemed really curious. Both issues could probably have been solved by having to do a little more "grunt work" and struggle a little before opening things up. But then, ofcourse, players might have been put off and refunded the game before even discovering what it was about. There's just no pleasing everyone I guess.Finally, I did encounter a couple of bugs with the mission scripts not progressing properly, both were solved by quitting and restarting the game and I didn't lose any progress or items.TL;DR: Lovely atmosphere, will play again to see if I can find some more side missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks really good. Tons of atmosphere and they flying car is neat. I love the music and the aesthetic. But it's basically a cyberpunk themed walking simulator. If you're into relaxing walking sims and love Blade Runner you will probably enjoy this game. After three missions I thought I was missing something. I was so bored. So I looked up some reviews and game play because I thought I had to be missing something. I wasn't. There's just not a lot of game play here. You just deliver packages and listen to people's stories. This game is not for me but if you like walking sims it's a beautiful one.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to drive one of those Blade Runner hover cars around that city? Well, now you can! In Cloudpunk you're a delivery driver, Rania who was pushed out of her home town by debt collectors and came to the city of Nivalis to survive. You drive around a huge cyberpunk city, meet people, learn their stories and make a few choices along the way. It's kinda like Coffee Talk, VA-11 Hall-A and other "perform a job and chat to clients" narrative games. It's pretty good! The devs are also making a life-sim/restaurant simulator in the same universe called "Nivalis." Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially this is interactive storytelling.. AWESOME!At first I didn't even know how the hell I ended up in delivering packages for strange and subversive individuals and what's the point of all that. The main story pushes you forward through the city while you're able to delay it in order to explore, collect punch cards or meet crazy and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up people living in the city and struggling to do so. There are several surprising turning points that makes this whole setting just more weird hence intresting.But please don't expect too much from the gameplay concerning freedom and possible activities. Although it's pretty amusing to follow the partly entangled stories, there's not pretty much to do when you're done.In the end I really enjoyed the story and would also pay full price if I hadn't bought it already on sale ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game! I know I'm comparing apples to oranges here, but I enjoyed this game about as much as I enjoyed CP2077. It has a very unique concept, not your standard typical "kill the bad guys" style gameplay, which was very refreshing to me. Looking forward to future content and hopefully progressing the storyline!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you drive around from point A to point B, while listening to the story unfolding by means of discussions between the protagonist, her annoying dog AI sidekick, and various other characters. The main focus of the game is the story, and the atmosphere of the city. Could have been good if the story was actually decent, but it's not. It's full of clichéd characters, it has no depth, dialogues tend to be long and tedious. On top of that, it exposes super simplistic views (bad evil corporations vs good willing and nice lower class people) which doesn't help the world building. All of these issues killed off any interest I had in the story, and I didn't finish it.The atmopshere is good, but second point that I didn't like in this game (and this is more a matter of taste), is the voxel graphics. I thought I would get over it, but I couldn't. The super low 'poly' design of the characters gives off a cartoony vibe, which completely cashes with the cyberpunk settings.Be aware the gameplay is quite simplistic and not the focus of the game, this is a story-driven game.Maybe if you like the voxel style you could give it a try, but don't buy it for the story.I digress a bit, but I see this trope a lot in video games: The main character, although evolving in an immoral/criminal environment, exibits extremely naive world views, is overly empathetic and kind, while still stealing/killing/committing bad deads either through gameplay or storytelling. This is the case here on a smaller level, but still. When you evolve in an evil corporate steampunk world, and knowingly choose to engage in illegal activities, the cheesy, overly kind character doesn't fit.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a cyberpunk game where you can just chill, drive and walk around, soak in the atmosphere and experience somewhat of a story, you can go ahead and buy this game - maybe wait for a sale. I got this game in a Humble Bundle, which was around 14€ for 8 games. 1,75€ for this game is a good deal.If you're looking for a gripping story with good writing, any sort of engaging gameplay, any resemblance of a challenge or any features that would give a game the label "immersive sim", then this game probably isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10I would rate this as the best game ever to describe a cyberpunk world before the launch of 2077.(I did not played through a single game like this continuously 7 hours of thrilled experience.)However the English sounds a bit weird at some points, but you can skip the dialogues anyway. Good luck delivering! Make through your first night!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Ever saw the Fifth Element movie and wanted to fly around in a futuristic city between the skyscrapers without seeing the ground? Get this masterpiece.A perfect game to play in the evening. I am not a fan of such (as many will say: pixel-looking) voxel models, but it looks amazing (and, I guess, voxels are the reason (among others) that the game can run so well); neon lights are perfect. And with a cockpit update this game becomes really atmospheric. Honestly, this game is so good you will be wondering how come no one has thought of this concept before. Future, rain, night, neon and vehicles between the skyscrapers.Cloudpunk is a story, told with very good voice acting. Your task is just flying (and sometimes walking which might be a bit tiresome as a path to your goal is not always clear) from one location to another and listening (also sometimes seeing) the story unfold. And that is it; no action, no shooting and no racing with NPC's. Therefore, if your would prefer that, you won't find it here. But the game is far from boring for those who love to enjoy the lore and sightseeing big digital world (or a city, in this case).What this game might be missing is, perhaps, more stories and activities. Future DLC's will be a welcome sight. And a few minor things like various dialog choices being absent, but, since Cloudpunk is a story, it is not really an issue, more like a thing that is usually implemented and something that everyone is used to... Also, there are people writing about searching for a parking in the game... Well, yes, you can't just park anywhere, but it is just one lane with a few slots being occupied. Not like all is taken and you have to circle around, hoping someone will take off :) And that parking lane, if not visible, is somewhere around your navigation point or drawn on your map :). Well, thank you for making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I am 10 hours into the game after 2 sessions on stream and havent completed it as yet. However I have seen enough to know that I really love it. The story is compelling so far, the atmosphere of the city is really fantastic with a great soundtrack to go along with it. The voice acting quality varies however the games many quirky characters are fully voiced and overall it works very well. The game is a very chilled experience which is right up my street.You are open to go anywhere you want in the vast city yet the story itself is pretty linear. I have had a few occasions where I have been given two ways to complete a mission but I cant say how much changes depending on these choices. Some may say this more of an interactive story than a game and for some that is the case. The definition of what a "Game" is has changed a lot for many of us over the years and we are definitely better for that.If you are a fan of the cyberpunk genre and like heavy narrative titles this could well be for you. It has definitely surprised me a whole lot and I look forward to completing the story..
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a game. Don't even ask me why because it is such a simple idea. You fly around a dazzling city and deliver stuff. Doesn't sound like much does it? But somehow it is.The game has a unique atmosphere surrounding it that is so powerful that you'll wake up the following day and think that you are still there. It just grabs you. And the devs must have read my mind because the only critisism I ever has was the lack of an internal cockpit. Hey presto it arrived today and I can't wait. Cheap at the price too. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for extremely intricate gameplay that tests your skills and challenges you as a gamer, then look elsewhere. The mean streets of Nivalis have nothing for you. However, if you enjoy a great story with interesting characters, moral quandaries, a well developed world, and an amazing atmosphere, then this is your game. I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: If I was to review this in terms of it being a passion project I would give it a full thumbs up. However, I'm looking at this as a game not a portfolio piece...So with that out of the way let's list off some things about this project.The bad: - Graphics options or should I say a lack thereof to be more precise. There's none, simple as. No options to change the settings (as I've been pointed out to, you can change the screen resolution...YAY). Just forget about antialiasing, texture quality, shadow quality, depth of field etc. Or any other graphical option. But hey! you can change screen resolution...right guys? - When looking at games that have released about 5 years ago such as The Witcher 3 you'd expect them to be quite demanding yet this game somehow proves to be more demanding on your GPU then The Witcher 3. The developers response: "Tweak your cooling settings". On a 2080TI really? I think a better response to this would have been to actually work more on optimising your game. - Pausing the game, doesn't actually pause the game. - The game is tagged as an RPG yet I don't see how it can be classified as this. You have no option to roleplay (just a minor thing that people tend to look for in a ROLEPLAYING Game)- There's no dialogue options as you just listen to your character spout off their own opinions and you're expected to feel compelled to care as a result of this. - There's practically no gameplay, it just revolves around you driving from A to B with some minor puzzles here and there to get to your destination and by puzzles I mean find an elevator. - I also can't see how this game takes 16GB of ram it just shouldn't. The good: - It looks really good, it's definitely a good take on Cyberpunk albeit a bit stereotypical (Blade Runner Clone) nothing really that you haven't seen before if Cyberpunk is your thing. - Voice acting is not bad but not amazing either. - Minor apartment customisation (again if that's your thing, go for it). Unfortunately, that's about it in terms of the good things this project has going for it. I really wish I could give it a thumbs up and as I said at the beginning, I would if I was judging this as a portfolio piece. However, it's not it's apparently a video game just minus the gameplay. Which looking at the oversaturated market that is the modern video game industry I'm sure it'll find its small cult following, after all who needs gameplay in video games? TLDR: -If you're looking for a cool portfolio piece you've found it if you're looking for gameplay keep moving.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews for games on Steam but I think Cloudpunk is great and is definitely a title worth supporting. I re-wrote this a few times because each time I'd go on and on about everything I love about this game. The game is beautiful (seriously. Look at the screenshots for this).The music is awesome (ties in well with the cyberpunk world).Story is really interesting (i tend to skip stories in games but this one is good and told in a non-invasive way).Game play is very simple (which isn't bad - it's fun to fly around and explore and listen to the soundtrack).So far, I'm loving this game. The sense of scale of this game is incredible. There's so much depth in the world ION LANDS created that the actual story has taken a back seat to my exploring. The world feels very lived in. There's people wandering around, vendors (of various flavors) selling this and that, guards posted up, and random people to meet and talk to which further reveals more about the world. The sound design in this game is fantastic by the way.If I have any criticism, it would be that the world is SO deep and feels so lived in that I don't feel as if the player can really feel immersed in it. I feel like I'm more of a visitor. I'd love to have further control of the camera and maybe drop it into a first person perspective just to get a closer look at the details that are hidden within the sheer scale of the world. tl;dr Cloudpunk is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with a few flaws:- Amazing atmosphere and graphics, the lighting looks so good- interesting story- flying around the giant city is very nice- a lot of dialogue, so much that I muted it halfway through the game and just played music instead. I had missions where I got soft-locked until a full 5 minute dialogue completed- a lot of commentary about current social/political topics. Sometimes felt like I accidentally opened twitter- The CEO in the pizza delivery mission is very based, most relatable character
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't so much a game as an audio drama that you listen to while driving through a beautiful pixel cyberpunk city. The story and voice acting is great and I thoroughly enjoyed my 8-ish hours of play time, but it is definitely not for the zoomer-brained dopamine-starved cutscene skippers out there, the gameplay is very shallow and very much serves as just a conveyor for the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible voice acting and fantastic presentation lift this game above the clouds. The gameplay loop is very simple - driving is a little jank and the on-foot exploration feels pretty limited. But the game nails that sense of immersion in a cyberpunk setting. Give it a go if you like visual novels, story-rich original settings, or talking dogs.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been exactly as I expected a visually impressive, relaxing gaming experience. With enough options and linear story to keep you hooked while playing. I highly recommend this game for anyone who wants a tamer more relaxed game play. A game made for after you have gotten home from work or school and just want to enjoy your gaming instead of tryharding a multiplayer game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: What a treat. Fantastic story. Incredible visuals. An absolute blast flying around this futuristic cuberpunk city. I dont leave reviews often, but had to on this. Wonderful game. Cant wait to see what these devs have in store next. This is a MUST play! The DLC might as well be a second game. Highly recommend both to everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a busy parent who plays games to relax when you have the time? Look no further. Amazing game and the city really feels alive. You will spend half the game listening to the characters and driving your flying car around the city. Great game to unwind too after a busy day instead of stressing out trying to keep up with the sweats on an FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: If delivering illegal packages (including humans and droids) in a dystopian city full of neon lights (where unlicensed jazz is punishable by death) sounds appealing to you, then this is the game for you. It's not a challenging game. Story is linear with minimal choices to make. There are lots of achievements, hunting them was one of the most entertaining part of the game for me. Graphics looks pretty for block environment. It's got a chill mood to it, with rain in the background most of the time. It's pretty relaxing running errands for people and AI in the world. If you liked roleplaying taxi in GTA, you'll probably enjoy playing this one. PS. Don't stand too close to the lift when it arrives. I got stuck there a couple of times and had to restart the game from previous save point. Otherwise, I didn't encounter any bugs. It runs smoothly overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! Very immersive, especially with music turned off. Driving around town inside the car is a truly  relaxing experience. The rain effects on the windshield are slick! I love to explore all the nooks and crannies, and seeing all the variety that the environment artists created. The game is also incredibly well optimized.Spending time with Cloudpunk is like spending time with a good lover: It won't demand commitment, and no matter if you meet it for 20 minutes or 2 hours, you will have an amazing time together~
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Visually this game is very interesting. There is a lot to look at. The story line was somewhat interesting but not overly exciting. Most of the time you are going from point A to B which can get tire some but i ended up beating this game in about 5-6 hours. IF ON SALE BUY THIS GAME. I got it for $16 cnd and it was origanally $22. If you are looking to scratch that cyberpunk 2077 itch, this is the perfect game to play. A Huge tip I can give to people is that you can play almost the entire game while in first person. They dont really show you that on the steam store but it made playing the game 10x more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't really feel quite like anything I've ever played before. I liked it a lot. I play games for the stories, and this game's got a good one. There's great balance between personal and political conflict. The world feels well-developed, and it's easy to get sucked in for the stories attached to all the characters, even the small ones that at first feel insignificant. Absolutely great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game very well could have been a bog-standard visual novel, because all of the characters are so flat they look 2D anyway. 1D, even: it's "we're goooood people. and those people over there? they're baaaaaaad people" all the way through, although at times the game tries to make it look like there are some shades of grey in play. There aren't. All of the choices are pretty much inconsequential, and the gameplay boils down to drudging along from point A to point B while listening to the dialogue that gets progressively more cringeworthy by the hour. But at least the music's nice! And the city itself looks great, the voxel look is kinda weird, but it works (not for the NPCs though). But overall - can't recommend it. It started off not strong, but cute, it had some charm to it. But by the end I just wanted it to be over. Oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Rania is insufferable. I thought there'd be a twist ending revealing she's an android or something, which would explain her robotic text-to-speech voice acting and bouts of sociopathic empathy loss, but no... She's just a terrible human being. *Especially* when compared to the character she interacts with the most, "Control", who is a fantastically written/acted character. And, interestingly enough, The visuals are neat. The world-building is cool. The driving is... Okay. The walking parts are often long or repetitive. The missions are mostly bland fetch quests, but you knew that going into a courier game.I don't exactly regret buying it, but I can't give it a thumbs-up either. Wish there was something in between.You might like it if you enjoy cruising around, exploring and learning about this world more than anything else, there's a fair bit of cool backstory to discover. Just don't get it if you're looking for riveting gameplay or a compelling main character.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty but tedious and boring. Story has no focus or tension, filled with pretentious dialogue and pointless characters with terrible voice acting. Gameplay is non-existend, exclusively drive von point A to B. Would have worked as a form of walking simulator with a good story, which it hasnt. On Foot sequences are absolutely terrible, slow, wonky and with camera issues. Don't bother playing this just for the atmosphere, you will be bored pretty fast
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: if you're like me and have always wanted to experience a little slice of a cyberpunk world such as bladerunner then this is it.although the graphics are made up of blocks similar to minecraft, it still evokes the feeling of being in a futuristic city and the games lighting and effects really help with that.the game mainly consists of doing deliveries in various locations, talking to interesting characters and having to make difficult choices, most of the voice cast are great and give real uniqueness to each character although i cant say as much for the main character that you play, rania, the voice actress is very wooden and lifeless, there's very rarely a time when she shows any emotion but thankfully it doesn't disrupt the story and you just get used to it.something i definitely have to compliment is the soundtrack, its superb, it makes driving around the city so immersive, if you like synthwave music then i think you'll really enjoy it.if you're wondering whether or not to buy it at its current price of £15 then id say yes, the game isn't tremendously long, my play time after completion is 10 hours but there's more other little quests around the cities, but the main focus is the experience, i really enjoyed this game if for nothing more than just the feeling of driving around a cyberpunk city with cool synthwave music accompanying me. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like flying around in Blade Runner or The Fifth Element.  Great soundtrack, amazing city and environment.  Everything really feels like a living breathing world with the people wandering around and all the small encounters.I'm extremely impressed by all the detail in this game, everything feels great.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible in its atmosphere. Even with the voxel building block people it is so easy to be walking around Nivalis and just become totally enamored by it, so much so that I walked on every rooftop I could just to see the city in all of its neon-grime splendor. The rain, the dark brooding monolithic skyscrapers paired with bright neon advertisements and the constant threats of death to illegal jazz players over the loudspeaker really make this game feel cozy. Especially if you are playing during a rainy dark evening irl and can hear the autumn rain falling on your roof. The story is ok, and the voice acting is pretty wild. At first I absolutely hated it, but after a while it grew on me. Really what was a persistent issue for me was that dialogue goes on for so long, that you will drive to your destination and just sit there and wait for the characters to stop talking so you can proceed. An early game problem I had was there are random citizens of Nivalis that you can talk to, but my handler would be talking my ear off about whatever, so I'm sitting in front of this npc for literal minutes while someone talks in circles. However for its many faults, Cloudpunk is an awesome pick up set down sort of game. I never felt like I truly had to bury myself in it like Cyberpunk, the Ascent, or Citizen Sleeper, but it is really something special. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's not a bad game per se - but don't expect anything revolutionary. You fly from A to B, do some silly talks with npcs, make largely meaningless decisions occasionally and that's basically the whole game. And optionally some irritating collectible stuff on the side (be sure to check - in that case - if your steam achievements didn't break at some point).The story is barely there, but there is some ... sort of it I guess ?First 20 minutes are best - as the game is indeed visually very nice, with decent ambient-ish sound setting. But that gets very old very quickly.If neutral ratings existed, I'd probably rate it as such.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wonderful aesthetic... Cruising through the city in my HOVA in cockpit view, seeing the endless rows of skyscrapers parallax in and out of view, it gives this amazing feeling of megalophobia that I haven't felt in any other game before.The voice acting is a bit hit-or-miss, but the hyperfuturistic dystopian world itself is incredibly interesting. And the soundtrack! Oh my god, just... *chefs kiss*
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Very boring. Very linear. The only thing more boring than flying a HOVA is walking around. The resource management (i.e. money) is trivial and inconsequential. Also, I really disliked the protagonist. $4.99 is probably the correct price point for this game, in terms of value. If you've got a decent rig, Cybperpunk 2077 is an awesome experience by comparison, even with the $60 tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Driving and platformer RPG with a good and thought-provoking story, good characters, and an absolutely gorgeous 16bit-esque Cyberpunk voxel world. I mean it, it's super cool-looking. Took me about 12 hours to complete the main story while taking time to gawk. You can go back and finish side quests after you complete the game, I had a few more hours in doing that. I liked everything about it and will def pick up the DLC sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Great indie with great ideas behind it. The gameplay is VERY simple and the graphics are a acquired taste but the atmosphere and the sound design are excellent. The story is very interesting and the dialogues are extremely well written and feel natural. Very happy with playing the main story and the expansion. I want to see more from these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The story got me hooked. The noir vibe was palpable and a joy to be drawn into. Your first night in the city is unforgettable. Cloudpunk really nailed the feeling of a major city, I think alot better than many other cyberpunk being made. Overall this story is worth living through and the gameplay itself is great for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: A game about driving from A to B listening to people stories in the dystopic city of Nivalis. There is a fair amount of social commentary beyond the regular big corporation = bad messaging and the shining neon lights atypical of the cyberpunk genre. The game has some flaws in terms of pacing shifting back and forth between relaxing deliveries and a world-ending urgency. However, you do encounter a large number of interesting characters along the journey with a lot of voluntary exchanges lurking in the street corners of the suspended cityscapes.Also, if you love collectathons, this is a game for you. The game does not ask you to look for each available pick up on your own. Instead, they are always highlighted on your map, which I found to be rather nice. However, to get to each pick-up, you have to look for elevators and passages that lead you to the items you are looking to collect. Which is one of the less enjoyable parts of the game. All and all, it is well worth the money you spend on it. Just don´t expect any combat or deep RPG systems. This is a delivery simulator with voiced dialogue thrown in that tries to tell you a few entertaining stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this small Review, I haven't played City of Ghosts yet (will Review this one after playing, even though I heard some people say the maingame and DLC should be viewed as one).There is not a ton to say about this Game.If you like Cyberpunk Stuff and don't mind a fully voiced story driven walking/drive-flying simulator without much else gameplaywise going on, then you will probably love it.As someone else already wrote in the reviews, the main draw for this Game is it's atmosphere.It all comes together with the voices, the music, the story and of course the graphics/environment.This is just a chill Game with only a handful of "urgency" moments, otherwise you can explore at your own leisure and just get lost for a bit.I also like that it basically tasks you to do "mundane jobs" in an extraordinary crafted world.Yes, many places will feel samey after a while and there is also one specific (Collectathon-)Quest that is rather annoying, but overall it's very good and kept me interested the whole Game through.Sure, the story isn't perfect, but as I said, it keeps you invested 'til the end.The Rest is just the right framework to get lost: Synth Music which is not the best you ever heard but still very good, the neon-light environments, the bleak outlook, the very good voice acting and all presented in a voxel world which still looks pretty good.So yeah, would recommend! Now on to the DLC...
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: It's literally a long night.7.5/10Pros:Cons:There are many cons that can be improved, yet I still recommend this game.Hope there would be DLCs to continue the story and/or put a new zone in the map and/or get into the spire and see what people in the spire look like because the current story doesn't describe too much about the spire.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. Light on gameplay, but the stuff that was here is done well. You'll either be flying your car or running around on foot talking to people and collecting items, and frankly I enjoyed both. I felt the addition of timed sections to the driving was enough to keep it interesting and test the skills you've naturally gained from flying around the city. I did however find myself getting a bit frustrated that there wasn't a "fast travel back to my parked car" ability, but it wasn't much issue.This game is absolutely DRIPPING with atmosphere. I very much enjoyed wandering around the different districts and enjoying the different craftsmanship and living conditions, soaking up all the experience. There's tons of strangers walking past you and plenty of cars flying over/under you that the city never feels underpopulated, you feel like you truly are just a tiny cog in the vast, spawling machine of Nivalis. The juxtaposition of the impoverished areas like the Marrow and the Ventz with the shiny towers and signs of the Mochi district or Avalon Heights really sold a truly thought out cyberpunk city to me.I enjoyed the voice acting. Control's voice in particular was very homey and comforting, with Camus being an amusing and good contrasting element to Rania. (Some of the NPCs pronouncing ramen like ray-mun is a sin tho)I didn't really feel like there was a "right" answer - at least not totally - for most of the choices that come up later in the game, which honestly was very refreshing and got me invested in the characters quite a lot.Overall, this game is for you if you enjoy atmosphere-rich experiences with a small amount of gameplay depth. I felt some of the walking sections to grab items were a bit tedious at times, but not enough that I didn't go out of my way to collect every item I could find. (Stock up on move speed increasing consumables like energy drinks)9/10 - Very solid.

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitate to call this a game, because I've completed it but yet to find a fail-state, but I will refer to it as such for lack of a better word.The negatives first: It's NOT an RPG, as it's tagged as on Steam as of the time of writing this. That's not inherently negative, but it was the tag that made me purchase the game. As far as I can tell there's no way to fail this game? I'm not sure if it's possible, there were some moments where I can see that it's possible to fail, but I can't see anyone actually doing it. The controls are a bit finnicky, but once you get used to them it's actually a lot of fun to zip your HOVA around and through buildings. There could be some more options in the settings screen though. Strafing is done with Q and F for some reason, which took me a while to realize, because strafing isn't covered in the control settings.The positives: This is a GREAT, atmospheric story experience. I love cyberpunk, and this is as cyberpunk as it gets without the violence. The story touches on some very deep philosophical topics, and has a few moral dilemmas where I expect the story can diverge. The graphics are awesome, and the constant rain gives it great atmosphere.Conclusion: I loved this, even though it's not a traditional game as such.
