_childDocuments_.review: I love Cyberpunk/Synthwave stuff, the neon lights, the dystopian setting, the Weeknd; it's my favourite type of world.  tl;dr for the below - I spent about as much time writing this review as I did playing the game.  I recommend it if you're into this type of world and don't mind about 8-10 hours of gameplay.  For a longer read though...So I liked this game, but I think it was mostly because I love the atmosphere of it, which is done really, really well.  The soundtrack is good, the main voice actors are good, the story is ok, the graphics work well, I didn't really get bored of doing missions, I found the main character and her sidekick compelling enough to root for.  With all of that said, I feel like these good or great parts aren't built on well enough to truly be a "must play" game.The story's short (<10 hours), but that's not a deal breaker... usually.  In this case though, I had no motivation to explore when it was done.  Okay, I can wander around, pick up items, earn some more cash - for what, though?  During the course of the story I had already bought all of the apartment upgrades, I've upgraded my vehicle, bought new clothes... cash really doesn't feel important.  If cash had more purpose, then I'd be far more inclined to explore the world, complete all of the hidden Easter eggs, and earn more of it to spend the cash.For example, I wish that I could spend on better cars - faster, sturdier, or more fuel efficient.  Or, provide us with a wider range of upgrades for the cars - super damage resistant shell, auto-vehicle avoidance (maybe with some kind of limitation or huge expense) etc.  Let me buy/rent a fancier apartment, maybe lease them out to get some more money on the side.  This one is maybe a bit ambitious, but; let me move up in the business and hire drivers to run routes for me, let those drivers have advantages/disadvantages dependent on how much they cost to hire (how much of a percentage you take of the delivery fee).I also feel like for the story missions, the ones that resonated the most were when there were time limits.  I understand that part of the point is to do some exploring while missions are ongoing, so maybe that prevented a lot more timed missions being added, but the most fun I had was zooming through as fast as I could, trying to find the best route while avoiding traffic and buildings to deliver the package in the time limit.  In the blurb for the game it says "Two rules:  and don’t ask what’s in the package." - play up to that.  Make it possible to miss a delivery, because it doesn't really seem like this can be done.  If a "moral" choice on whether or not we deliver a package needs to be made, then let us choose whether or not to look inside the box, and have consequences for doing so if we end up delivering it afterwards (lower money earned).On the "moral" choices bit - when the game has you decide between Option A, or Option B, there doesn't appear to be any tangible consequence for going either way, or if there is it was so subtle that I didn't notice.  I would've loved to have seen this be a lot more impactful to the way the story plays out.When the game finishes, a steady stream of randomly-generated missions to keep me busy would've been great.  Yeah, it's pretty much always gonna be "point A > point B", but with the world open and no missions coming in, I felt a bit lost.  If you pair that with the upgrades above, you could keep money flowing in while you explore and check off the side missions scattered around.  Maybe spawn some races?Let us do more with the map, set waypoints, plot us the most efficient legal way to get there from our current location.  Upgrade-able In-car GPS?Another small gripe I had, was the inventory management.  After upgrading my HOVA the first time, I didn't realise that the items you equip on it are in your inventory, so I ended up selling them just thinking I must have picked them up somewhere.  I wish that there were 4 sections in the inventory - 1 for junk items that you can sell, another for items that pertain to quests that you can't sell or otherwise do anything with, and a couple of side areas to equip/unequip clothes and upgrades for your vehicle.I wish I could give this a thumbs sideways because I enjoyed the ~9 hours I spent playing the game, but for the reasons above I'm hesitant to recommend it.  I think on the balance of things, if you enjoy Cyberpunk kinda stuff, don't mind the short story, and exploring a beautiful, futuristic, bleak, neon-tinged, bladerunner-esque city appeals to you - then buy it.  The bones of a really,  good game are here, they're just not used as well as I think they could be.I hope that further content gets released for this game because I would be keen to re-visit this world.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything else, I want to point out that the currently displayed promotional videos don't yet show the recently introduced absolute GAMECHANGER third-person on-foot camera (in beta). This makes a MASSIVE difference, and I hope people visiting the store page will see this. I will detail why below.This is a recommendation, with some caveats. This game is one of the purest, most jaw-dropping audiovisual representations of the cyberpunk aesthetic to date. If you ever wanted to step through the screen while watching Blade Runner, then ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this game for you. From the dark, rainy, smog-ridden cityscapes with their neon-lit spires, billboards and hover-car traffic, down to the abandoned, broken, poor districts, the game is DRENCHED in atmosphere. Driving or walking through these environments just has an amazing sense of space and scale, made so much better by the recently implemented third person camera. Having the ability to look up and around at these towering skyscrapers (instead of whichever apartment wall the previously fixed-camera made you look at) makes you feel small and insignificant, turning the previously very arduous backtracking into spectacles of worldbuilding. Add to this the top-notch ambient sound design and the beautiful Vangelis-style soundtrack, and you've got a 10/10 for presentation.Having said that, what you must know is that the gameplay itself consists of going from A to B, walking to someone, having a chat, and going back. Repeat until the story is over after about 8-9 hours. There are also plenty of optional NPCs to talk with. These chats do a very good job of providing insight to the inner workings of this world, and the main plot has some intrigue to it, but the delivery is very uneven. Some of the voice acting is either over- or underacted, poorly written, stilted, or all of the above, threatening to derail the immersion. .Overall, you must decide if experiencing and spending time in this world is a strong enough attraction to carry you through the game for its runtime. If you expect intricate gameplay mechanics however, you might want to wait until Cyberpunk 2077 comes out. For me, the wait for that game has just become a lot easier. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk bills itself as tough gritty cyberpunk adventure, and it's not.  It's a beautiful and relaxing walking simulator that you happen to drive a spiffy flying car threw.  I loved this game to pieces, I played all the way threw and then came back to finished the side quests, it's just not what I expected.  That said, what the game gets right is the atmosphere, this is a gorgeous world that I loved every second I was in it.  In general I do not like voxel graphics, but the wold and the lighting are so well done that I wouldn't want anything else here.  As I said before this is more of a walking simulator than a adventure game in that there does not seem to be any death or way to loose.  There are only a few times in the story that you are on the clock, and even there, there is no real time crunch.  I love that they took frustration out of the game, it adds to the tranquil beauty of the experience.  The characters are wonderfully acted, but the stories they tell are a bit clipped off and all too often underdeveloped.  There is a lot of philosophy crammed into a game that is already short on interaction with NPC's, and although the dev's were trying to say some great things with it, it did feel a bit forced.  Also, as much as the voxle graphics succeed for the world, they fail for the characters.  The stark difference between visual quality in place and character often took me out immersion.   The game focuses more on flying than walking, so on ballance it still works overall.Another negative is how big the world is, and how hard it is to find quests and collectibles.  Both are easy to miss in the expansive world of the game, and often require MASSIVE amounts of back tracking to get too.  The world is great, I love how it captures a rainy night in a big city.  It just felt like the actual content didnt come close to matching that same massive scale.   I truly loved this game, I played and explored until there was nothing left for me to do.  It clearly has more than a few flaws, but the good easily outweighs the bad.  If you want a beautiful pworld to explore and a game to lovingly unwind in I highly recommend Cloudpunk.  Just know what your getting yourself into before you chose to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished my first play-through of this game. Controls: Controls in this game were slightly awkward initially *you might expect so, seeing as I was slightly out of practice Driving HOVAs of recently. but in the end they came together well, I would strongly advise playing this game on controller, and try to play it in first person. It will be disorienting at first, but by my first hour, I felt comfortable flying from point to point in first person. Progression: The game-play is highly repetitive, with very little actual progression, beyond that of a couple vehicle upgrades, that do make a noticeable difference, and nick-knacks for your apartment but I would have liked less binary upgrades - Instead of just Has upgrade or Doesn't have upgrade, the vehicle's performance in the various aspect could be improved in multiple tiers, and potentially could be built to sacrifice one aspect to improve another - like a HOVA that can strafe left and right very fast at the expense of slower elevation. Vehicle customization seems very lacking. Gameplay: The game is highly repetitive, in its nature, with curveballs throwing every other mission. I almost feel as though the lack of normal events makes the fore-said curveballs more of an anticipated annoyance, than a fun encounter, I can remember thinking to myself "What will go wrong this mission?"  Flying from A to B is pleasant, relaxing, and the amazing city design keeps the player engaged. Running around the various platforms on foot often feels tedious, and slow. Story: I played a more or less straight and narrow play-through and enjoyed the story, the voice acting brings this games' story up a notch. I love the dialog that i'm given durring flight from A to B, and I was very irritated any time I was stuck in a lengthy dialog on platforms on foot. I know it was neccesary to make conversations take place on foot, I just wish they'd worked out ways to keep dialog outside of the car, as short as possible. Overall: I recommend this game for anybody looking for a time sink, in an awesome city with a pleasant story. I am very interested in the speedrun-ability of this game just because of the unique movement  but I fear the lengthy dialog makes that unlikely, half the run would just me clicking through dialog as fast as you can.

_childDocuments_.review: Erghhh the twitter gifs looked so promising. It's still fun to recreate those gifs, just puttering around and looking at the legitimately gorgeous environments. _childDocuments_.review: I loved each moment I spent playing Cloudpunk. Pros:-The narrative was compelling; although you could say that it had its lows, overall it was intriguing and interesting, and leaving room to interpretation about ethics of AI, and the problems it could bring if we let it do all the logistical work of a mega-city. A fine cyber-punk, sci-fi, noir tale that will take hold of you. - The gameplay was ok, somehow basic for a taxi simulator.  I think the atmosphere was the main point of the game and to get lost in the city. -The graphics were enthralling, a Minecraft aesthetic fussed with your run-of-the-mill cyber-punk city. -The sound track was awesome that helped with the immersion.  Cons: -Endless and tedious to-get series of collectibles that for the most part were useless.-The controls were a little bit off. -I know that Rania was its own person and we, as players, were along for the ride but I would have loved to have more options when talking to NPC, some of them were interesting.  Conclusion: -I highly recommend this adventure. Hope to see more of Cloudpunk in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy Cloudpunk if you will enjoy the following:---CLOUDPUNK is an immersive and extremely well-acted story set amidst a dark, neon-lit city. Nivalis is so enthralled with consumerism and hacking biology that the only hope comes in the form of a lowly delivery driver, Rania. I came into this game with modest expectations - a quaint delivery game set in a neon-punk aesthetic.What I experienced, though, quickly and completely enthralled me into a sardonic take on a world quite like our own - beautiful and ugly. Cloudpunk often goes on sale for $7 but it's well worth the $20 release price.Cloudpunk touched my heart and brought tears by the end. Thank you Ion Lands

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game.I came across it from a passing mention from Hello, Future Me's video on Cyberpunk 2077, and decided to give it a go.in fairness, it does many things right. The graphics are cute, the soundtrack isn't original by any means, but it's clearly reaching for a Vangelis synthwave vibe, which is at least appropriate for the setting, and the gameplay is cozy in an inoffensive, Law and Order on a weeknight kinda way, but.Man, the writing.The story puts you in a number of "moral quandaries" ala saving or harvesting little sisters in bioshock, with a few important differences:1. They are never handled well, even by that standard, and that is NOT a high bar to clear2. There's always a very clearly telegraphed "correct solution" to the predicaments you're put in, rather than letting you sit in the uncertainty and find your own way through3. That correct solution is, invariably, what is correct according to the cultural norms of an upper middle class Liberal American in the early 21st century.4. If you aren't part of the afore-mentioned smart set, you are not welcome or well thought of, period.I regret buying this game, and I regret the time I spent playing it. There are piles of better games out there, I encourage you to find one of them. This game does not reward your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A number of the other reviews I've read complained of boredom, so I'll preface this review by saying that Cloudpunk is not an action game. It's a narrative game. It's for those of us who like the combination of driving and listening to something that we can immerse ourselves in. As for those complaining about the voice direction; they're just objectively wrong, and that's okay.I picked Cloudpunk up as a sceptic, but a sceptic that really just wanted to fly deliveries in a sci-fi setting. What I got was a really engaging story, great voice acting, compelling characters, a fantastic synthwave soundtrack, and ultimately, fulfilment. I couldn't put it down.It's pretty linear, story-wise, and the choices you're asked to make definitely had me second guessing myself, but ultimately I don't think they have a huge impact on the events that take place in the story. With that said, it's so nice to just fly around in the rain and let the dialogue wash over you. It's equal parts relaxing and exciting, with story beats that kept me playing just to find out what was going to happen next. It turns out it's exactly what I was looking for at the time of purchase.I've just finished the story, which took me about 10 hours, but for this game, I'm going to wait some time, and play it again, with a focus on finishing off the achievements, rather than grind it out now. This game deserves another full playthrough.I really hope many others get to enjoy this gem as much as I did. There's something kind of special about Cloudpunk, that I've struggled to find in other games. It's like being a passenger on a really good road trip. If you like that idea, try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this title up despite seeing some negative remarks regarding the gameplay and voice acting. I have to say that I have no regrets, especially at the price point. The voice acting certainly isn't superb, but having been a gamer for over three decades now, I am prone to cut a game some slack in this regard. I remember just how bad voice acting used to be in games, if they had it at all.The gameplay is as advertised, you're a delivery driver so you do a bunch of point A to point B driving, as the story gradually unfolds. The story while not the greatest was something I really enjoyed. Furthermore my play through was bug free.My only critique worth mentioning is that upon story completion you are able to free roam and wrap up side missions/explore. This aspect of the game would have greatly benefited from a random delivery generation system to keep you busy after the story line was complete.All in all, I really enjoyed the time I have invested in Cloudpunk, and recommend it to anyone interested in cyberpunk themes and narratives.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll give it to the devs, this game is pretty comfy thanks to the amazing work in the game’s atmosphere. Music and visuals blend together nicely to the point that just walking around by foot or with the flying car and do some sightseeing becomes quite an interesting activity. In regards to the gameplay i have one minor thing to complain: there's a fair amount of padding here. You can recognize the padding as the parking spots for your car being too far away from your objectives, items that are scattered too far between each other and the lack of a jump button for your on-foot sections.The weakest point of the game, in my opinion, is the writing. I can’t understand how people say that this game’s writing is incredible. The pacing is so slow and the outcomes of the game's conversations are almost always predictable. In a fair number of missions i was just thinking “Ugh. Get on with it.” as the characters talked. The main character is also someone i didnt like. She's so abrasive that it hurts. She makes it pretty clear that she hates the city while being a sassy prick with almost everyone that she meets and i truly mean everyone. From the random guy on the street to the “Kingpin” of that city's section. Also, her very brief remark about cultural appropriation as she swindles a guy to buy a flower she found in the sewers made me cringe. Social Commentary is pretty meh as well. Eveyone that is rich is a bad person, the game has some obnoxious caricatures of streamers, hackers act like cartoon supervillains and every single poor person in the city is a good person that was unjustly thrown into misery so we shoud sympathize with them all.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Cloudpunk for the past few days and am really getting into it.  When I bought it, I expected it to be a simple shooter and racer, but it's much more than that.  I love the RPG and adventure elements!  So far, it has a deep and complex story-line that is slowly unfolding.  Turns out your employer is into some shady business, and the cops are none too happy with you even though you're just a driver on your first day driving a cab (that's not a spoiler as you find that out nearly right away).  For me, the game is actually relaxing.  There's no boss fights or fast-paced action sequences or time limits that test my not-so-youthful-any-more reflexes.  The game makes you believe your time is limited while delivering packages and passengers, but you can take your sweet time exploring without penalty whenever you want (except for a few scripted events).  There's some puzzle solving elements, but that's really just finding your way to your destination on foot through the streets and back alleys after finding a parking spot.  Once you make a few deliveries, finding your way around the city on foot becomes second nature.  Though many times it's easier just to hop into your cab and then park down the street or on the other side rather than find your way through the maze of walkways and alleys on foot.  It's a fun challenge, not a hair-ripping one.  One detail that I'm really, REALLY happy for is that you're not on one long linear path between any two points -- the streets and roads are laid out in a sensible open-world grid pattern, just like a real city would be.  It does lack in a few ways though.First, there's no tutorial.  You're dropped into the world and sent on your way to do your job.  Maybe that's okay because the premise is that this is your very first day on your new job as a courier/taxi-driver after moving to a new city.  At first, the city seems huge and you can get hopelessly lost if not for the green symbols on your mini-map.  But once I accidentally figured out how to call up the big map, you discover the city isn't really all that big after all, and I became more comfortable driving around exploring without being afraid of getting hopelessly lost and unable to find my way back home again.  Being "the future" your car flies, and so you're not stuck driving on the designated streets.  You can freely fly between and over buildings to get to your destination if you so choose, completely ignoring the city streets.  Though there are some invisible walls that prevent you from flying too high or leaving the perimeter of the city, but it's far less egregious than most games.Second, the controls aren't customizable.  The controls are geared toward the keyboard.  It does support a game controller, even though there's no game controller options.  The button combos needed to switch between 1st person and 3rd person are a tad confusing.  At first, I found myself switching randomly between various weird camera modes until I stumbled upon being in 1st person on foot, and 3rd person while driving the taxi (you really need to be in 3rd person while driving in order to avoid crashing into other cars and street lights and buildings and everything, especially when you're flying).  That seems to be the optimum, at least for me.  I'm afraid to experiment because I fear I may not be able to get back to this mode again.  At least it was easy to invert the Y axis (too many other games don't allow you to invert the Y axis -- and those other games are literally unplayable for me).  My main recommendation to the devs is to allow for customization of controller buttons.  The right thumb-stick controls up and down movement of your car when you're flying.  I would think the left thumb-stick would be the better control for this, and use the right thumb-stick to look around.  Just my opinion -- yours may be different.  Most games I've played use the left thumb-stick for translation (linear movement of the character) while the right thumb-stick is for rotation (rotating the camera in place) -- used together these axis allow one to move in any direction freely and looking in any direction freely.Here's a suggestion.  The city is divided into 11 "districts" connected together by tunnels which serve as loading screens to each district.  Each district contains multiple blocks and neighborhoods.  If you draw the districts with pen and paper positioned relative to the labels of all the tunnels to each other, you'll find they mesh together like a jigsaw puzzle.  Doing this greatly helped me learn my way around the city.  I wish the game had included a "supermap" that shows all the districts and tunnel connections at once. Overall, I highly recommend this game if you like open-world RPG/adventure games that aren't super challenging, and the cyberpunk atmosphere appeals to you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game but not a great one. 11 hours to finish the whole thing - and I spent quite a bit of that simply flying around - is a bit short. The story was interesting but by the end I felt there were a lot of loose ends. We don't discover anything about Rania's history, and that's the biggest gap. The main quest was engaging but again, leaves a few things hanging.The only proper side-quest is collecting the punch cards for Evelin, and that brought back too many bad memories of gathering Nirnroot for Sinderion in Oblivion.The graphics start out feeling quite fresh but after a couple of hours playing the constant neon brightness is pretty trying, and the blocky shapes get old fast too.The music is excellent. Most of the voice acting is good, although one or two characters are excessively hammy.I'm giving it a recommendation because I played to the end, and that definitely doesn't always happen. But wait until its on sale because it's not worth the full asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that I put off playing for a long time after getting it from a humble bundle, thinking that it would be a crazy taxi like game, but it turned out to be a relaxing story-driven game.You'll know if it's for you pretty early on but I found the story engaging though the voice acting is hit or miss with no outstanding performances and progress can be gated off for stretches because they never give you a waypoint and conversations can't be interrupted so you just have to sit and wait while the conversation goes on.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: That was a really good and fun 12-hour adventure with only a few hiccups.The cyberpunk atmosphere was spot and the blocky graphics did not hinder the experience, as they were overall quite charming and everything else about the presentation (music, voice acting, story) was excellent. The gameplay is like a walking simulator, just that you are also driving a hovercraft two thirds of the time while listening to music, engaging in conversations about the world, experiencing the story and also trying to avoid the homicidal maniacs that drive the other hovercrafts.I played with a controller and while I did not really mind the controls too much, even at the end of the game there were situations where I hated them. Even more tedious was hunting for punch cards for one particular long quest that turned out to be a fetch quest with only a minorly interesting story and some really, really annoying long jogs around the least architecturally logical parts of the the city. I finished the quest, but I did not like it. I also did not like that the game's UI basically forced me to turn my attention either to the lower left part (during conversations, which happen often) or to the lower right part (whenever driving to a destination or hunting for items to pick up). I feel that half of the time I spent glancing to the corners of the screen, which hurt the overall presentation a bit and undermined the atmosphere the game was trying really hard to establish. Instead of interacting with and through the game world, I interacted with the GUI and at times this was really quite frustrating.On the bright side, these more annoying aspects of the game's design were not able to deter me from finishing the game. The main characters are likable and relatable, many of its side characters are interesting, funny, thought-provoking and even sad. Huxley was the best of them and the way the character worked on every level. Rania as the main character was great. So were Control, Camus and many, many others. The game's underlying mystery was interesting, even though the conclusion felt a bit rushed and underwhelming.In the end this is a game without combat and without serious attempts at stopping you from completing it or experiencing its story. If you enjoy sci-fi, especially of the cyberpunk variety, and want to experience a great story and atmosphere in such a universe, then I can highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: meh, very much a walking simulator, some interesting characters, but the main character is not one of them.  the flying is very boring as well, doesn't feel like fast passed racing or some cool spaceship flying, more like driving down the highway in a slightly faster car most the time. getting loot is tedious and every quest is a variation of a fetch quest.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking for a novelty, in search of a creative and atypical universe, Cloudpunk will transport you to its pixelated world with an heavy atmospher, dark, noisy, perfect transcription of a futuristic and dystopian megalopolis full of androids, automatas, and twisted mind human beings. Due to its strong and mature themes, this game has a fantastic Cyberpunk vision through social questioning and technology dependance problems.Talking about problems, the slightest NPC has its own, its own personality (great voice actors), and side quests are really interesting, while moral or immoral is always a question above your head, just like in the main scenario of the adventure, a full of multiple choices adventure.The characters are endearing, you really want to keep knowing more about them and about their past, the city is alive, and the beauty of it is fabulous, oppressing, with diverse neighborhoods and a great level design. What a pleasure to walk in, or drive all night long, Korben Dallas Style. <3A highly recommended game, an independant pearl, pure joy, and one of my favorites games of the year.What a fantastic work for this small team in charge of the project. Cudos to Marko Dieckmann for his creative vision.So finally, does Androids dreams of electric sheeps ?I don't know, but personally i dream about going back to Nivalis, and i'll be there for a part II, in the future, or to infinity and beyond... ...the clouds.+ Level design+ Graphism, pixel style in a huge futuristic open world (not everybody will like it)+ Voice actors+ Multiple choices Scenario+ A lot of UPDATES from the devs, including the FPS view, perfect for immersion+ Low price- a few bugs, but really minors (like desappearing PNC)

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. The city is well designed and together with ambient sounds and the music, it creates a nice atmosphere. But if you are looking for action, look elsewhere.It is a nice walking/flying simulator with a good story. Kind of Blade Runner mixed with Hard War fetch quest marathon. Some dialogues are a bit lengthy (annoying), but nothing game breaking. The first person view is a really nice touch and makes the walking/running in the living city a more enjoyable experience.Some characters are inspired by movies ().Played on Kubuntu 22.04, Ryzen 5 2600, 32 GB RAM, RX 6600 XT - not a single crash or any issues what so ever during the 11 hour playtime.Well done, ION LANDS.

_childDocuments_.review: This consumer’s interest was piqued. Maybe they stumbled across this page on accident, like a discarded newspaper tossed open by the wind. Maybe they were just passing by a conversation on the street, and heard the name ‘Cloudpunk’ thrown around a few times through light clouds of cigarette smoke. Either way, they’re here... A decision had to be made. Purchases weighed, and doubts had to fade. The roar of the neon city called them, veiled by damp atmospheres of heavy sound and smog. Why was the reviewer so vague in their description of this item’s creation? Was this cryptic writing style going to offer them anything? You look past this poor schmuck’s spectacle of paragraphs, pick up your package, and head off toward your next destination. _childDocuments_.review: Plenty of other reviewers have hit on all the major points, both positive and negative, but I will say that this game left a lasting impression on me.  The atmosphere is great--a dark, rainy, future cityscape with  flying cars soaring around towering skyscrapers.  That alone made the game fun for me, and with the new update to drive the cars first-person, I'll be putting a few more hours into the game.Quick points:1) The game is shorter than I would have liked, with only about 10 hours of content.2) The talking does get annoying--I would have liked more quiet time just to enjoy the driving instead of so much dialogue between the main character and the car, passengers, etc.3) Most of the quests are fetch quests.  More of the timed deliveries or racing would have added variety.4) I liked the voxel graphics style.  It feels like playing in a world built of Legos.

_childDocuments_.review: i dunno, i wanted to like this game since i'm a huge cyberpunk/blade runner fan, but this game isn't it.first off, the city and sound design are amazing. absolutely nails the them, almost makes the game a recommend on its own.however, the game is BORING. the entire game is a fetch quest to drive through the city. there is a little exploration and some side quests, but they are also simple fetch quests. while driving through the city is mesmerizing, it wears off after 2-4 hours and the game is about 10 hours without the side content.this could be saved if the story is good, but it isn't. super cliche and you can see the twists coming from a mile away. the voice acting is decent, but it's definitely on a cheap budget and can't save the poor script.if you just want to drive through a 3d pixel cyber city, then get this game. but otherwise, there are much better cyberpunk/futuristic games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted this game. I loved Space taxi on the Commodore 64. I thought this was going to be it.Alas, It is minecraft with vehicles. If you like blocky minecraft worlds, then this is right up your alley. If you are over 10 years old and are waiting for Cyberpunk 2077, don't bother. What meeting would have possessed you to do this?Been gaming for 35 years and rarely have I seen a game that had so much potential frittered away on game breaking features. Perfect Dark and Space Taxi this is not.Refunded a game that had so much potential.Oh, and the despatch manager reminds me of the useless old jedi who gets cuts down in order 66. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly reading the bad reviews one might second guess this... i dont know what the bad reviewers were expecting or coming in thinking but seriously i dont understand the bad reviews. This game is a masterpiece.Writing 10//10 : some of the conversations really convey dystopian ... some of the convos will make you saddened, laugh , feel for the people you are talking too, and angry at the world you are in. The underlying story is compleling and interesting and grabs you once it starts unfolding, Big shoutout to the writer Thomas Welsh!!Graphics 9/10: I dont normally like voxel graphics , but its done so damn well that often i forget im looking at voxels. also the choice in style actually lend to the world not take away from it. Amazing scapes and beautiful scenery.Voice 9/10: Well done all the way around. The people who are supposed to be monotone do it well ( there are only a couple) and every char. has personality often feeling like hopeful yet downtrodden denizens. My hats off to the actors.Gameplay 9/10: This seems to be the biggest contention in the reviews. I dont understand why. Its a linear semi open world experience. not a free flow open world ... it guides you through the story to unveil what the game is trying to show you, the lessons and human faults we all have. Sometimes thats best done with a guiding hand.. a Control if you will.  All & All worth full price if you like games that make you think, give you intrigue, hide the main underlying message within a main story that you dont get too till you start to unravel the inner workings of the world you are in. I highly recommend and hope to see more from this universe!!

_childDocuments_.review: []This game is... AWESOME. I bought this game prior to actually having a PC because the reviews were overwhelming positive. I thought it would be a great game to start off with so i could get the controls of a keyboard down. I was not mistaken. Honestly, I was distracted by how colorful and beautiful the world was. It seems simple: Pick up a package and deliver it. But the more you do your job as carrier, the more in depth and immersive the story becomes. _childDocuments_.review: I was drawn in by the aesthethics but the game itself turned out disappointing. Why? I think the main reason is the control. The vehicle is jerky, the screen turns at strange moments while exploring out of the car and it remaps your controls - I played on a keyboard so maybe a gamepad would be better. However as someone who drives a lot in real life I can't understand why there is no GPS route tracking in this future - not to mention an indicator whether your goal is above or below you.The City is rather dead. In the two hours of play I supposedly visited a number of districts yet I couldn't tell you which is which - they are all samey. Secondly this game does a number on my GPU. I have a new and quite powerful laptop and it got really hot. Won't comment on the story as it looks like I've only gotten through 1/4th of the game.Cloudpunk really fell short of my expectations and didn't engross me in it's world.

_childDocuments_.review: Ham-fisted political "commentary," entirely unlikeable characters, and gameplay that would be great if you could GET ON WITH IT. The poorly-written story and obnoxious voice acting bring gameplay to a screeching halt as you wait for them to finish before you can resume what you're doing. Particularly in City of Ghosts, you spend more time aimlessly walking/flying in circles (or doing nothing at all) than you do actually playing the game. It's very obvious which characters you're supposed to despise based on the exceptionally cringy over-the-top voice acting, and yet the protagonists and their allies are equally annoying and objectionable.This feels like a bad high school creative writing project somehow shoehorned into a well-made engine and environment. If the game were just an open-ended "delivery simulator" with story-developing missions interdispered, it would be fun. Instead, once you get thru the story, you are dumped into the world with basically nothing to do... oh, and you have to spend in-game money for fuel and repairs, so forget about just indefinitely flying around appreciating the aesthetics, since after the completion of the story you have no real way to EARN that money.THE GOOD:The visuals are stunning, especially for a voxel game, and the cyberpunk gritty-yet-beautiful aesthetic is well represented. This game would be a delight as a more open-ended, less story-focused game. The controls are pretty good, and I would love to play it more.

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a delivery service game set in an interesting and dark world.The game is set during your first night on the job. You are given two rules to follow. Don't miss a delivery, and don't ask what's in the package. The second rule obviously sets an underlying tone to the game, and how shady your job is.The game is heavily story driven, and there is very little actual gameplay. Most of your time will be spent driving around the beautiful cyberpunk city. You can fly around freely, including changing your altitude. You can speed up on highways, and have to occasionally buy fuel for your car. The other half of the gameplay happens once you've arrived to your delivery destination. You'll have to disembark at the closest available parking, and walk on foot. During these moments you can talk to select optional NPCs. And then hand-deliver the package to your client. Everything is voice acted, and you will be hearing conversations for most of your time playing.Unfortunately, for a game that has such an emphasis on conversation, I didn't think the voice acting was the best I've heard. It was quite hit or miss. It was never awful, but there were times where I felt like emotional delivery wasn't quite right, and the pacing of the writing was off. It could have been better, but didn't ruin the game for me.That's because the overall world and story is really intriguing. Some of the stuff people say can paint the city in quite a grim light, and there are some disturbing concepts in this dystopian city. You also quickly see the grey area that your delivery service operates in. You will occasionally have to make moral decisions, without a direct consequence being visible to you. The game kept me interested for that reason.Overall, I think it's a lot of fun. There is very little actual gameplay, and it's quite a chill game, despite some of the topics I discussed. If you're interested in being part of a world like that, I recommend it!As I play through more, I will update the review accordingly if needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk might be an "acquired taste" kind of game, but for the right audience, it is an absolutely perfect one.It's really a large collection of short stories tied together by an overarching narrative that slowly crops up basically without you noticing, all in an exploration-based package. That package being flying in a satisfyingly floaty car, and getting out of the car to deliver and explore a myriad of districts. If you like getting lost in a winding, large place that you can only access small bites at a time, you'll have a lot to look forward to. The beauty of the dark voxel environment is wonderfully atmospheric, and it makes the maze-like levels feel less grueling for people with a good amount of patience.Whether they are in the main line of quests or side-quest/interactions, they are all great works of micro fiction. They are often funny and heartwarming, though the game doesn't pull punches when it comes to depressing grit of Cyberpunk. Yet, it never stops celebrating the goodness of humanity (androids unambiguously included). As such, it feels like the purportedly horrendous city is much more a collection of good people trapped in an awful place, where a few villains manage to ruin it all.The writing is truly odd. Part of it might be the odd style of acting, or the limits of writing so succinctly. But with a moderate suspension of disbelief, it can be easily appreciated as a charmingly eccentric tone.Fe sahatek, .

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I am not a fan of voxel graphics, I must say Cloudpunk gets the atmosphere of a night cyberpunk city exactly right. The atmosphere and the story are the main reasons for playing. And the flying car which is difficult to control, but satisfying to fly. Because, despite a great freedom of movement and exploration (and various collection and trading mechanics), the game is at its core a walking simulator. Or a running simulator in this case.At key moments the player feels a distinct loss of agency, which is in contrast with the general freedom and can be irritating. But you do make choices. Moral choices between messy alternatives that may be both bad (or good) just for different reasons. The game then refers to the outcome later, although the mechanical impact is minimal. The real impact is that you had to think about them and decide what you consider better (or less terrible). And that is the third main reason for playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, ok music, non-existant gameplay and mediocre plot and writing.The game has the RPG tag for some reason, but that is false, there aren't any RPG elements whatsoever, Cloudpunk is a walking simulator and has even less gameplay that your typical walking sim. All you do is drive from point a to point b listening to people talking. You might think that this game should have some driving or taxi mechanics, but it actually doesn't. You basically fly straight to a point you are told in a linear story, with zero obstacles or challenges on the way, ignoring roads due to clunky controls and that's it. Well, you can collect junk lying aroud to get money to buy decoration items and hear a bit more random dialogs. But ok, no gameplay is not always bad, many games are about story and narration, right? Yeah.Problem is, the plot and gameworld are generic, stories you are presented vary and some are ok (most are not, consisting of overused and superficial cyberpunk fluff presented in a preaching manner), but the way they are expressed is extremely bland, since all you do is listen to people talking. There are maybe 5 choices in the whole game you can make, and they are nothing special.The worst though is the main heroine, one of the most boring and annoying protagonists I've seen. She looks totally out of place in the gameworld and talks like your typical modern female studies college student right out of the memes, with exaggerated and childish opinions on everything, and about as interesting as a tree stump.tl;dr Don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, you start your delivery driving and the world starts to suck you in and eat you alive. The cyberpunk theme and atmosphere is strong here. You get warned left and right, to be carefull, that nothing is as it seems, and you only get hints of what is about to unfold onto you. The mystery of the city. The secrecy of the locals about what CORA is refering to. Its all so wonderfully craftet and set up.My critical points are probably the fact that there are things to discover that have a great setup, but lead nowhere. There is a bionic arm to buy for example, its very expensive and you can only find it at very specific dealers, but all you can do with it is travel to another district and sell it for profit. You cant equip it, you can't give it to someone, its just there and you can pretend you are a streets dealer.I spent a lot of empty time in this game, thropy hunting, trying to find every corner of the map, and you can probably finish it in one sitting if you keep picking up quests and finish them. You should kind of wait with exploring tho since there are some areas which are locked until you get your quest for that part. All in all I highly recommend this game if you have an itch for cyberpunk-esque settings. I dont know how much impact your choices have in this game, but you definetly feel the consequences of your choices. People talk about things happening, and you know your decision caused them. The game regularly gives you very heavy binary decisions to make. There are kind of "choose the lesser evil choices" and "if this is this and I dont prevent it its bad, but if it isn't and I still prevent it its even worse" situations. And you feel the outcome. Maybe not in an instant, but you will.It's great.Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: While everyone's waiting for the big Cyberpunk2077 release, Cloudpunk has been around for quite a while now. It's basically a story driven delivery-game with exploration elements, beefed up by a huge amount of Blade Runner atmosphere, presented in minecraft-style graphics of massive proportions. While you should not expect any challenge from the game at all I recommend you hop in and enjoy the vistas along the ride, paired with an incredible soundtrack. Sure, one might argue about the dialogue quality here and there but overall I kind of enjoyed the quirky, sometimes flat out absurd characters, which remind you you're walking around in a fictional world. The city however is huge. After a while you really learn to make out the subtle differences between the parts of Nivalis.Cloudpunk, as it stands at the moment, takes a very lean approach. It does not stray far from pushing you through the main story although it might as well have served as a backdrop for an indepth pixel-art GTA if it wanted to. But it does not want to. So you are down to driving around, collecting items, transferring people from a to b without (and that's a great thing for a change) violence. A couple of times the game will ask you to make moral choices. Even though they do not return to you in any fatal way, they are worthwhile enough to keep you guessing whether your choice was correct.If you just like to immerse yourself in a dense Cyberpunk atmosphere, Cloudpunk will absolutely do that for you. In particular the optional ego-pespective and cockpit modes enhance the game by a lot and almost scream for VR support (which hopefully might follow one day).Despite some missed opportunities Cloudpunk is already great as it stands right now. If there would be a sequel one day it could not hurt to build on the subtle RPG-elements and add perhaps HOWA racing. Also I'd like to have side-thrusters on the HOWA for more efficient controls.

_childDocuments_.review: I did my due diligence before purchasing this and looked up some reviews. I was well aware that this game involved nothing more than driving about delivering parcels while listening to dialogue. But nothing alerted me to the fact that the driving, the core and only gameplay element of this game, handles poorly.My main gripe is that you cannot tilt your vehicle up and down.Listen, a car, that you drive on the ground, navigates on a two-dimensional plane. It can accelerate or decelerate, and it can turn left or right. Mathematically this gives it two degrees of freedom in a two-dimensional space.A flying vehicle moves in three-dimensional space. A properly designed flying vehicle should allow you to accelerate or decelerate, turn left or right, and in addition to that, tilt up and down. This gives it three degrees of freedom in a three dimensional space. That's how flying any flying vehicle in any video game works, and also in real life.Unfortunately in this game, where driving is what you do most of the time, and is the very core gameplay mechanic, they decided to disallow tilting up and down and replace it with a very slow and unsatisfying mechanic where you just slowly float or sink your flying vehicle up or down. Sure, this allows you to adjust your height, but as a result you never really are able to have a satisfying way to move through the world vertically. This is akin to having a car on the ground not be able to turn left or right, but instead only able to slide left or right slowly while always facing the same direction.For a world that has such verticality to it, not being able to quickly move yourself along the vertical axis feels stifling. I want to go high, go low, weave through between the buildings among the traffic, go to high places, and down to low places. Unfortunately you can't do that with any kind of dexterity. Just look at how Mile High Taxi handles driving for instance and the contrast is night and day.I didn't even care that this game would be only driving and listening to dialogue. Sure, I don't mind doing just that and driving through a pretty cyberpunk world. In fact, I was looking forward to exploring a pretty world without having to fight or kill people for once. But the driving just does not cut it, and I can't bring myself to continue no matter how pretty the world may be.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game, very cool aesthetic and world.  You mainly drive and walk around certain parts of the city, giving delivery's or driving around people. The mystery of the company, what you deliver and the city itself was captivating but at times, obvious. The VA work was either good or bad, which is very important in a game where you rely heavily on dialogue and voice acting. I had seen people complain against the protagonist but I understood why she acted the way she did, she did come from a population where they are farmers and more rural so being in a city makes her both ignorant and unable to hide her true feelings. I did not like her companion, Camus, I found this character overly irritating and his dialogue was unbearable at times. I also had a big problem with the choices you make in this game, most do not matter or are entirely ignored (with me completing a delivery and Control saying that they would forgive my past choice if i did something for them when I followed their orders). I do not like when games do this and the ending choice made no sense to me. If you like the cyberpunk feel and music then this game is good but know that choices do not matter and you mainly just drive and follow a set storyline with characters that sometimes are interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The Good - The city looks great while driving around and you're not focusing on anything too closely/staying away from the roads.The soundtrack is great, really fits the aesthetic.The interactions with one off NPCs are generally pretty interesting.The Bad - Your HOVA handles horribly, even with upgrades for turning and ascending/descending.When you're on the street level completing deliveries the character models are so jarring it blows away your immersion. The portraits of who you're talking to almost never come close to the model also.Rania is a pretty boring character, she acts stand-offish with everyone even when it's against her interests. Camus, who is with you almost from the very start, is plain annoying. Using him for exposition and as a sounding board for Rania could be done well but the never ending silly questions ruin it. The story really slows down after a couple hours. They even showed off the big plot point really early but then Rania completely ignores it.Choices don't matter and some choices the game doesn't even recognise. One very early choice sees you delivering or disposing of a package. I delivered the package as Cloudpunk wanted but was then told my next delivery would wipe away any infractions I had made against them even though I had done as they wanted.I really wanted to like this game but it just turns into a slog of going back and forth with not much between point A and B. The story does get interesting at times but really drags on when it's not. If it's on sale and you only do a delivery or two at a time it might be worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk contains a nice story and well executed.  Only a handful of timed missions that I get the feeling don't really matter if you do not beat the clock.  So really a relaxing game to enjoy.You have a few moral choices to make, which lets you feel somewhat in control of the plot but only just.Aesthetically this game really stands out, with the bright neon glows and colours.  Contrasting the grim and dirty feel of the cloud level streets and walkways.The main protagonist has a great voice and very pleasant to listen to.  Which is a bonus, due to the amount of dialogue in the game.  I had no issue listening to Rania voice her opinions of the new city she finds herself in and certain situations.  I never found myself screaming for a skip button and Huxley is also a stroke of genius.  However there are quite a few others that just seemed plain odd choices with their accents.  You'll know what I mean when you hear them.I feel more could of been done with some elements in the city, just to make it feel more, 'alive.'  The highways are full of traffic, but there's no real logic behind the traffic movement.  Car parks have HOVAs but you never ever see another HOVA setting down or taking off!!  You hear sirens but never see a police HOVA or witness a car chase.  Would of been cool to see NPC's getting pulled over.You see futuristic trains hurtling through the sky-ways but they never seem to stop, nobody gets on or off.This game is full of beautiful garnish, for lack of a better expression to give it the look and feel needed.  If only the world you spend so much time chasing around was a little more interactive.  ATM's, Drop boxes and lifts are the only objects you can interface with, that's NOT an NPC to talk to.I only point this stuff out because I thoroughly enjoyed the game, it's refreshingly original compared to so much other stuff on Steam.  I hope there is a sequel with MORE... Just MORE everything, especially MORE interaction with the environment.  A city that feels a bit more alive and natural in the beautifully crafted pixel world.  The feel of moving around is great, the first person camera mode when driving a HOVA is without a doubt EXCELLENT! and shows what Ion Lands are capable of when it comes to adding content and updates.Bring us the DLC and then Cloudpunk 2 please!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: i've been playing this game again now that they've added first person mode and a really impressive hovercar cockpit - even more than before, just sitting around and taking in the view is a great way to spend your time. the streaking water on your side windows changes angles depending on your car's speed, which doesnt sound like much, but it's such a wonderful touch. cloudpunk is easily one of my favorite games this yearthis game might be something really speciali'd been following this game since seeing it on steam, and was expecting a little 1-2 hour game where you fly around some linear areas. on the contrary, the game is Massive and open. it has an incredible art style (along the lines of else heart.break() which i also love), aggressively corny old school adventure game dialogue and voice acting (with none of the frustrating hunt-the-pixel or guess-what-the-dev-was-thinking puzzles), and a very satisfying hover car to fly around.i am enthralled! i didnt realize that four and a half hours had passed since i opened it

_childDocuments_.review: Less a game, more a delivery device for pure neon drenched half remembered cyperpunk atmosphere. The voxel aesthetic really works at creating a sense of scale and sprawl and the soundtrack sounds like a half remembered version of every other synthwave thing that makes some connection in your brain.  Narratively and mechanically, making you an insignificant delivery driver makes the monolithic size and scale of the megacity Nivalis - the real antagonist of the game - really work. You have little you can do to interact with, much less change, the immutable city. It's not for everyone but it's a great way to spend some time, flying about, picking up snippets of backstory from the various characters and street vignettes, chill in your cab using the (essential) in car first person mode. Take in the view.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, Cloudpunk is just... un-rewarding.Game play is repetitive: fly, walk, fly, walk etc... which would be fine except for the incessant dialog performed by monotonous voice actors (except perhaps for the lead character, Rania).To add insult to injury, the missions are terribly timed to the script, forcing the player to sit through pages of conversation before receiving, say, the next nav point or even simply completing a mission. Some dialog can be skipped, but many of them, painfully, cannot.More so, there's a lot of fabricated names and places in the Cloudpunk world, but characters would often pronounce words differently even while having a conversation with each other! The lead character's name, Rania, for example, was pronounced at least three different ways and often within the same dialog exchange! I'd usually give voice acting -- or more specifically voice direction -- a pass, but not in a game that is constantly bombarding the player with dialog.Even if the dialog were edited for some MUCH needed brevity, the game play mechanics also fall flat. Things like repairing your HOVA (your flying car), getting fuel, and even adding upgrades do practically nothing to add to the initial game experience and instead only serve as yet one more mundane distraction to the main story line.Finally, although Cloudpunk is billed as a flying car game, you'll also be spending a lot of time walking around. This experience also needs improvement, and at times can be downright frustrating. There's multiple levels and things like elevators and transporters to deal with, but the mapping system is not sophisticated enough to guide me along the way. And of course the parking spot is always going to be in the opposite corner from where I need to go. Argh!I played through the whole game hoping that the ending would transcend the shortcomings, but that too was a disappointing and ultimately forgettable experience. Pass on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So full disclosure, i play so many games i cant even keep count. My backlog is filled to the brim. I play everything from 2$ indie games to fully priced triple A games. I stopped playing almost everything else when i got into this game. Cloudpunk is officially now one of my favourite indie games of all time.Warning: This is mainly a driving game which is 95% fetch quests and a collect-a-thon. You play as a delivery driver in a cyberpunk dystopian city. You can get out of your vehicle only at designated parking spots to explore but theres not much to do besides talk to NPCs a pick up items or deliver your packages. If this sounds boring to you then do yourself a favor and skip this game. Don't force yourself to play a game you know you wont like just to leave a bad review.The soundtrack is amazing and all the screenshots of the game fooled me. I thought the graphics were realstic until i jumped in and everything resembled minecraft. To me, that just added to the charm of everything. I've seen a lot of folks complain about the voice acting, but remember , depending what country you live in, this game is between 10-30$. Its an indie game. And i think for that price, the voice actors did a fantastic job. Objectively speaking, i can't say that the voice acting was amazing but i did start caring about the characters, especially after a few hours playing the game.So a great soundtrack, open city with beautiful colours and landscapes, places to explore, a great story, fun driving mechanics and for a great price.To anyone who likes a good indie game with a great story but little to moderate action, this will be for you. However if you're a triple A gamer mostly, and you have high expectations for gameplay variety and voice acting, do all of us a favor and pass.To me, this game was a gem and i believe to the right people , its a game worth cherishing a dumping a ton of hours in. That being said, the game is only 10-20 hours long depending if you skip talking to npcs and you just follow the main quest.TLDR: experienced and seasoned INDIE game lovers, dont sleep on this game, however if you only play Triple A games usually and you're looking for a cheaper game/ want to branch out into indie gaming, approach with an open mind, if you should even approach it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely and relaxed game.  An absolute gem of entertainment, if you're a fan of relaxed story telling. This game is busy work made enjoyable. It's not like its full of exciting gameplay or really hard fights or something like that. This game is basically a fancy, kinda-open-world walking simulator and that's a good thing. The story is absolutely lovely. The characters are all voiced accordingly, if sometimes a little predictable. Still, everything is full of atmosphere and written lovingly. Sidequests, if you can call'em that are also quite lovely if not a little short at times.The music, or rather the lack of music at times is my personal high light. Very reminding of the Blade Runner films, simply a perfect match and very soothing. In general the sound in this game is an absolute master piece. Rich, full of life (and robots) and somewhat overwhelming at times. The constant noise of a big city never sounded this inviting. Make sure to use headphones for this one though, it really, really helps pulling you in.Graphicly you're in for a treat if you like the clunky Voxel-aesthetics. There is lots of things moving, blinking, crashing and falling apart everywhere, this giant city world truly invites to explore, if not for the many, but short loading screens and artificial boundries. A little blemish in an otherwise amazing feast for the eyes.None the less, this game is for you if:- you don't mind running around from A to B, back to A, then to C and back to B again just to get send to A once more (youre a courier  after all)- if you like futuristic sounding, well,... "sounds" and music- you just wanna explore a new world, with an atmosphere so palpable, you'd wanna just be there, experience it for real, but also never wanna see it come true due to it's scary vision of the future- you love neon, techy blinky lights and hover cars that swoof around with amazing sounds- you like a well written story that takes it's time- if you've made it this far in the "review"

_childDocuments_.review: To lead off, you need to understand that there are few things I love as much as cyberpunk and making deliveries.  This should have been a slam dunk for ION LANDS, and they effed it up.To be clear, it was not due to a lack of effort or love.  They clearly poured themselves into this game, and that's fantastic.  It makes me feel terrible for leaving this review, and it kept me playing for a long time out of a sense of duty, but it does not make the game good.The main problems are threefold:First, the setting.  Cyberpunk is dystopian by nature.  It's a social hellscape, everyone knows this.  In order to make it worth spending time in a cyberpunk setting, you have to give a player something to make up for the unrelenting inhumanity.  Usually this is a violent power fantasy, but there are other options.  Cloudpunk didn't pick any of them.  Cloudpunk is a game set in a crapsack world about scraping by in a crapsack world.  In its best moments, it is a guilt simulator.The protagonist isn't even particularly punk.  There's no resistance here.  She's presented as an outsider: she "hates the city," and plays a few pranks.  Ultimately, however, she fits right in.  The city constantly confronts her with its ugly crap and she routinely decides (without any input from the player) that her best response is piling on her own ugly crap.  This is framed as resistance, I guess, but it comes across as collaboration.  Not so much with the individuals she hurts, perhaps, but certainly with the ethical void of the city.  It's hard to stomach, not because she's not a hero, or because she's just another petty villain, but because she's not anything.Second, the gameplay.  There are a ton of driving games with terrible controls but few have the sheer audacity to punish you when their terrible controls cause you to gently collide with objects.  I'm not talking about head-on collisions, here, or even fender benders, I'm talking about clipping curbs.  I get it, it's a game about paying the bills (as riveting as that is), but the repair costs rack up awful fast even for a careful driver.My biggest gameplay complaint, though, is the length of time you spend waiting for elevators.  It's not a small quantity.  Cloudpunk is a single player game; why do the elevators move when I'm not on them?  Why isn't there a call button for when the elevator is in its other position?  Why is the city full of "escalators" or "ascenders" that immediately teleport me from place to place, often within the same small area, but all over the city they've chosen to install elevators that I have to wait for, then manually activate, then wait again as they travel to their destination?  For that matter, I HAVE A FLYING CAR WHY AM I WAITING FOR ELEVA-- ...It's maddening.  Cloudpunk really wants to waste your time, and that is something I always struggle with forgiving.Third and least importantly, the graphics.  The game has an aesthetic, I will grant.  Rendering '80s adventure game characters in 3D without a resolution increase is an interesting choice.  People are monstrous, vehicles are blobby, and the buildings... I have to say, it works okay on the larger structures.  I don't have a problem with the buildings.  But I do play a lot of Minecraft.Additionally, the aesthetic is abandoned all the time.  The chat boxes are high res.  The character portraits are high res.  The billboards are high res.  The sky is high res.  The particle and glow effects are high res.  Even the sea at the base of the city is rendered as a somewhat more modern polygonal surface.  So it is inconsistent as well as highly questionable.Aside from these three major issues, I'm also broadly unimpressed with the direction of the voice acting and the marriage between the visuals and the script.  There are so many jarring repeat mispronunciations and graphical misrepresentations that there is clearly a need for greater internal communication at the studio.  I mean, maybe the dog's name really is intended to be 'CAM-us,' and not 'ca-MOO,' but that's just the tip of the iceberg.As there often is in works of fiction, there's a good internal metaphor for Cloudpunk: at one point in the game you meet a collector of ancient video games.  She espouses the view that ancient video games were all philosophical lessons, and suggests that the lesson of a 'Streets of Rage' stand in is that violence cannot solve urban decay, because when the game ends, it just starts over again at the beginning.  This premise is obviously presented for a laugh, but playing Cloudpunk feels like its developers truly believe this on some level, and that their armchair philosophy is as least as bad as the collector's.Someone loves this game.  Certainly, almost 7000 people have given it a thumbs up.  But I just cannot get behind it.  ION LANDS wants to make a slice-of-life cyberpunk RPG in this setting, and the thought is like nails on a chalkboard.  What a opportunity that is, and what a disappointment it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: well... fantastic! it is like several year long dreams in gaming and fantasy coming true. may sound silly, but when you love open worlds, love vehicles (even with dashboards and inner atmoshpere, yikes!), love doing jobs with vehicles (like micro missions in gta or mafia e.g., too few games out there with this gaming style), love blade runner, love pixel-style games and love cyberpunk stuff and scifi in general - than this is a game you buy after the first trailer without thinking a lot. visuals, design, variety: intense. amazing. just stunning. this is feeling more cyberpunk than cyberpunk 2077. graphics are not everything...world: great.controls and movement: great.story: i don't know. very sampathic, but also a bit... naive? drool? strangers who tell you everything about their illegal activities? but it fits and i see a positive message behind this and can live with it so far.i missed the sale and i don't regret. this game is well desigend, worth every buck and hopefully gets the proper attention and more content or sequels or whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is/looks charming. Even though the whole world is build pretty minimalistic (everything is made out of blocks ....) the game manages to look beautifull no matter where you look. It feels like they just added the right details and left everything else out of the equation. I stopped counting how often I looked up the skyscrapers and just thought "damn i need to take a screenshot for my desktop background". So if you want to evaluate the looks of this game, they are straight up a 10/10. When it comes to Gameplay there is not much I would want to add. The traffic is as annoying how you'd expect it in a crouded city full of scum lol.  The HOVER drives super smooth and well there wasnt a moment where I got bored of driving this HOVER through the corners of this city. Well otherwise the Game would be gargabe since you spend most of your time driving the HOVER and it is your main gameplay. Other than that you just walk around the city, explore, collect stuff here and there and talk to people. Well yes that is about it. It doesn't sound like much at first, but if I am being honest. This game does not need any more than that. The gameplay manages to make you feel like a citisen of this Cyberpunk city. The only  things that I missed where a few mission ideas, where i thought to myself "well that would have been a great mission. Sad they didnt add one like yadayadayada". But well that are just the types of mission that I would have liked to see. Also I highly recommend playing the whole Game in Ego-perspective since the cockpit looks gorgeous and it just feels so damn cosy and satifiyng to drive through the city, while the rain patters on your front window. The Story ..... Well the story is not too bad. In fact I really love the story, but it lacks a few things here and there and sometimes it was hard to comprehend some of the actions of some characters. Over all it was pretty good. You really started to feel somewhat emotional to some of the characters even though I did not get as emotional as the protaginist herself. I dont want to spoil to much so yeah that is all I am going to say. Let me just add, it is one hell of a ride.Something I wanna mention is also, I had not even one perfomance or bug related issue with the game. Nothing gamebreaking. I know Games should always be like this but at the moment it is unusual for games to work that well. TLDR;This Game was awesome and if you'd like to play a backseat-type of game, wich feels and looks awesome with a great story and a really interesting world I can highly recommend this game. You won't be disappointed. Over all I give this Game a 9/10. A great game standing out in the pile of garbage that is called "Gaming-Market".P.s. Only CORA knows if our hunt for Punch cards will ever stop.
