Why couldn’t it be possible for the player to get out of the car anywhere, on any building (with the search for collectibles and objects, the description of which would be interesting to read)?!After the first two hours, I found a quest where I was asked to find 20 cards. The next 1.5-2 hours were the dullest even in comparison with the "walking simulation games." At the end of the quest, the NPC told me several phrases and offered to find another 20 cards. At that moment, I wanted to have a katana in my hands (as in "Tokyo 42") to chop into pieces of this NPC.I will not say that this is a bad game, but this is a game with a beautiful cyberpunk city, in which I hope there will be a good story (I really hope because I like the main character and his android), but the "walking simulator" spoils this game, because it’re practically nothing interesting. It would be better if the whole gameplay was on wheels.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: In this story-driven 'cyberpunk' game, you will encounter a diverse range of characters, including androids, AI and mindless humans in all strata of society. The Cloudpunk environment is very immersive and the whole city is amazing. From the atmosphere, to the lighting, to the sound, to the story of the characters. But at the same time, we can only imagine what could have been if the game had taken a different direction. Throughout the city, there are hundreds of buildings, if not thousands. Lots of NPCs that unfortunately most of them don't interact at all. The possibility of exploring the city either by HOVA, train or bus could be an attractive option. While the game could be so much more, the feeling is that they did a good job in creating a game that would hook anyone who likes to enjoy stories and a cyberpunk atmosphere.Something to improve on is definitely the rather confusing driving and the orientation leaves a little to be desired.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I can not praise this game's atmosphere enough. It is stunningly gorgeous, from the visuals and the world design to the soundtrack. This is what made me play it to 100% completion and I enjoyed every minute of being in this virtual city, despite the somewhat repetitive gameplay.The writing, on the other hand, was atrocious. What irked me the most, by far, was the constant shoving of SJW agenda down my throat. Cringe-worthy attempts at lecturing that stuck out like a sore thumb, something I could've gotten on YouTube for free. If we had neutral dialogue, this game would've been a true gem. Instead, despite actually agreeing with some of their views, I found the playable character alienating and obnoxious.Because of this, I am giving this game a negative review. A damn shame, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: It's an interesting concept and the visuals are unique and pleasing. However, the mechanics of driving the car are not very smooth and just slowly irritate you constantly, but the real reason I eventually stopped playing is because the woke/feminist political commentary. Sometimes it was subtle/funny and sort of enjoyed it since it at least added some unique character to the protagonist. However, it was more often just too much on the nose/bashing you over the head with bizarre caricatures of real life people (i.e. a character in game named Glen Bo is an absurdly exaggerated and grossly mischaracterized version of Stephen Crowder doing a 'Change my Mind' segment).It's unfortunate I won't be finishing the game because it felt like there was a lot of potential for more interesting stories and development, but I have far too many games in my library to play to spend more time on something mediocre. If you are bored and don't have anything else to do, then this might be a good time waster for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Look this is not an action game, Think of this like the walking dead, but with less exitment.  You will make choises, your choises will come back to haunt you in the open world.  So what I am trying to say is that this game looks good, and it has a great story.  If you want action or game play, this is not the game for you,  if you only want a good story this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: GET THIS GAME!! It's amazing, for the price this cost I'm shocked at how fantastic it is! The game runs smoothly, with hardly a hiccup I can even remember! The story is really well done and I found myself drawn deeply into it! You can also find a lot of side fluff and get drawn even deeper into the city! The voice acting is also amazing! Could have done with a bit more of a music feel over the somewhat high screech of nearby HOVA's! If you are still reading this and not already playing this game then check out my video here for an idea on the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely cannot recommend this game if you have something important that you should actually be doing. I'm afraid to say that it's either too long to be this devouringly atmospheric, or too addictive to offer so much playtime when I should be finishing term papers. It's basically pure atmosphere and world-building dialogues, based around driving (flying?) deliveries in a hover car. I'm not even really into cyberpunk, or cars of any kind, but... I need to go back in. (1)0/10 it's a trap! * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator  and/or join the !
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this... and not, at the same time.The story itself sometimes glitters and is very well written, well-paced and thoughtful. Other times, it's poorly written, has awful grammar, and the sometimes wooden VAs really ruin the mood.I also hate how I'm forced to sit in my car or stand still and listen to long-winded dialogue that I can't skip. I can read faster than they can speak!I like the art style. The story isn't fast paced or violent, which works in its favour. Unfortunately, the gameplay is repetitive. Still, when the story and the world and the characters shine, they really shine. If you want a narrative-based cyberpunk game with trains and robots and neon lights, this is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: beautiful game with an amazing athmosphere!The story a few hours in is intriguing, i like the voice acting as well as the humor. Its pobably my favorite game this year! edit:The game does slow down a bit eventually (pickup x items) but i still consider it to be one of my favorites this year - still can't get enought of the beautifull vistas
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Just an absolutely beautiful game. The sound design and voice acting really brought it to life for me. I tend to gravitate towards more "cozy" games, and while this absolutely hit all the marks for moody and atmospheric, I was pleasantly surprised to find it also quite engaging. There is just enough excitement and variation to keep it outside of monotonous without becoming stressful, with choices that feel like they have weight, a main character that was pleasant but flawed (character flaws are way more interesting than a perfect hero), and an environment that felt alive. Sure, the story was at times predictable, and some of the characters and dialogue a bit on the nose, but you know what? I didn't care one bit. Would absolutely look for future games like this from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I would higly recommend this game because the developers have a dedicated Discord page for bug reports and support and that are really great about adding new features and are really good about taking suggestions into consideration. The gameplay is very smooth and the storyline keeps you engaged throughout your journey as a Cloudpunk Driver in Nivalis. The game has a very unique and intriguing aesthetic with the wonderfully implemented voxel graphics making it a very cool art style for a video game. Of course this is an early review and I have experienced some bugs with my game, however it was very easy to report them to their Discord server and they'd usually be fixed within a couple of days. So great support, great gameplay, and a wonderful Cyberpunk style game. 👍
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Great story. Great voice acting. I can't recall a prettier game.  The blending of pixel art graphics with modern effects in a futuristic world is stunning.How can a game that costs around 20 bucks include hours and hours of great voice acting while $60+ games include no voice acting?  Looking at you "Animal Crossing."  Highly recommend this game.  Just know that it is quite short but definitely worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an action packed game. The game is go from point A to B. That is it in terms of what you do. Yes you pick some items up to unlock areas. But the game is all about the story, the dialog you have with the other characters. I enjoyed the story this game told and how it told it. I would recommend this fully, just understand it is not a flashy, fast or action packed game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a visually very pretty game with an engaging story.  It may be worth buying when deeply discounted.  I went back and forth between a thumbs up and a thumbs down.  The good:  Visually awesome, with a good story and interesting characters.The bad:  -The story is 85% of the experience.  This game can easily be finished in a weekend, and after that it (to me anyway) there is not really much of a point in doing multiple play throughs.  Things may change a little based on some of your choices, but if you want hours and hours out of a game I think this is not the one. -Over the top with the pro-socialist "woke" content and themes.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this game if you just looking for something cool and relaxing. I love the short stories, discover some character stories and find hidden places. While I enjoy the game, the performances can be terrible without changing the setting. I needed some time to find an almost clean solution : enable the v-sync and change the culling settings / prediction.Maybe a default configuration for some of the recent graphic cards (the problematic ones) could help ?
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that is best played at night or with closed curtains. For a game made by a few people. it manages to get that  cyberpunk feeling better than that OTHER studio that tried and failed. The story is actually interesting and to my shock. the game showcases some moments when  your choices actually matter. worth paying for on a sale or not. get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting premise marred by some shortcomings in implementation. First, though, the good:- Flying cars feels really good. Probably better than you'd expect. The flightpaths are clear, and for the most part, there isn't too much chaos with regard to other cars.- The voice acting ranges from good to great.- There's some good worldbuilding, and the city of Nivalis has been thought through from a lore standpoint to a great degree.Now the not-so-good:- Some dialogue drags on for way too long. If it wasn't linear, this might not be a problem.- Very few things that should have colliders "do" have colliders. You can walk through tons of props like barrels, security scanners, other people, etc.- Animation smoothing on foot isn't at the level of the rest of the game's animations.- Some holograms and effects are play by the voxel rules, while others don't. It sorta breaks the immersion and makes certain things just feel like "assets in a game world" instead of "being a part of Nivalis"
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly love this game. I've always wanted a cyberpunk game with a floating city and 'flying' cars. It looks amazing and has a lot to offer. I do find myself wishing for a little bit more action though, the AI and characters seem more like background pieces than actual characters. I wish there was more events like races or us being chased. Also, I'd love to see outside of the city in the future, but I understand that won't be for a long time.Overall, I still love this game, I've been waiting for it to release for a long time, and it did not disappoint me. It's easy to lose track of time while you fly around and deliver packages.Edit: Finished the game, some of the characters do grow on you. I generally really loved this game to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun game with an interesting story. The driving, the world, and the soundtrack was absolutely amazing and fit together perfectly. I played mostly in first person when roaming on foot and came to be one of the most unique games ive ever played. The first person perspective makes getting immersed into the game so much easier and was a great decision by the developers.Even with the world being a pixelated art style, the city and other areas are designed with so much detail and from a distance you could forget that the pixels are actually pixels.My only complaint is that some of the character voice lines were pretty clunky when interacting with other characters, but it didnt take me out of the game too much.Im definitely looking forward to the next game by Ion Lands.P.S. Cloudpunk and Hyper Light Drifter are the first two games to get me into the indie gaming scene and may be two of my favorite games ive ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it so far, gameplay is a little lacking but the atmosphere is outstanding. If you ever just wanted to drive around in the Blade Runner or Fifth Element universe, this is the game for you. Very chill game, fun to drive and just walk around the areas and seeing all the shops and buying ramen. Also, the music is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I dislike driving and avoid it at all costs in real life - but the story and ambiance of this game still pulled me in. Ironically, one of the best games I ever played, although you spend a lot of the time driving and parking. The characters are complex and there is always a sense of mystery lingering about ...
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this game is absolutely brilliant, and I for one loved every second of my 14 hour playthrough. Of course I still have some achievements left to hunt for, and I will, but as I finished the game I was left feeling somewhat unfulfilled. This is not exactly because of the game itself, but rather because I felt the end was somewhat too abrupt. There should be more, and I would actually be happy if there was some mechanism that would keep providing delivery missions after completion. There is so much more to explore in this amazing city, and I definitely hope there will be more content to come in the future. This city has so many stories and secrets to uncover, and I definitely hope the devs and the writers provide them.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a while, and seeing it in action with the first-person camera got me to take the plunge.Since I knew what I was in for after doing some research on this game, I wasn't disappointed. It's a very relaxed game with an atmosphere I could lose myself in. While I originally thought the entire game would be making deliveries, there were some parts of the story that surprised me. The other characters you can interact with around the city also add some flavor to the world of the story. During and after the story, there are some collectibles to fetch if you want to get more familiar with the city.A couple bugs I ran into that were minor inconveniences were:1. After a certain point in the story, I was seeing two car icons on my on-foot mini map until I reloaded my save. Trying to avoid spoilers, but if you played through it, you know the part I'm talking about.2. After beating the story, I was unable to leave my apartment until after I reloaded my save.I would recommend this game to anyone that wants to relax, take in some atmosphere, and cruise around in a HOVA listening to some decent ambient synthwave background music. A few missions had timers on them, but for the most part I was just getting from point A to point A, and listening to dialog.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: All style, no substance. The city design is great, yes, but thats the only redeeming quality of this game. The characters are cheesy and boring, extremely boring dialogues, no real story or background, no meaningful presentation or introduction to the main character or game world, no meaningful interaction with the game world. Literally just driving from point A to point B, with an occasional irrelevant choice. Fine to fly around for a while to enjoy the beautiful city design (which on the other hand ticks all the boxes of cyberpunk clichés, bringing nothing new to the table), but gets old and repetitive really fast. Also lots of backtracking to the car in sections where you have to walk by foot. I wanted to like it, I really did, but the total lack of an compelling story, interesting characters or fun gameplay just couldn't motivate me to continue. Nice environmental design is not everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I love the atmosphere, the gameplay, everything! However...even with the installed drivers for my game controller it doesnt seem stable in registration of it; one minute it works, next minute it cuts off, then it works. Its frustrating to continue flipping in between controller and keyboard when the controller makes my hand feel less cramp.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a pretty cool game where you play as a delivery driver in a futuristic cyberpunk city with towering buildings and flying cars.The game mostly sees you taking deliveries or parcels from point A to B in your flying car. It's pretty cool flying around the city in the car just weaving in and out of traffic or just deciding to fly out of the highways duck between buildings for a shortcut. It reminded me a lot of the flying cars in Back to the Future 2 to when they travel to the future.There are also small areas which you can park and explore on foot though this part of the game is a little less enjoyable as theres not much to do in these areas, other than picking up mostly useless items and maybe a person or two to talk to. One complaint I had here is that these on foot areas can be a bit hard to navigate as the map can be a bit confusing in these areas.The city itself looks great, even though the characters and city have a kind of low res 3d pixel style, it gives Cloudpunk a unique look that I really liked. The city  is really atmospheric with a Cyberpunk feel and is almost a character in the game itself.The story in the game is pretty good. You're  playing a woman called Rania who has moved to the big city of Nivalis from her rural homeland and is working her first night as a driver for the delivery company Cloudpunk. The game takes place over the course of that first night and while Rania herself isnt that interesting or charismatic as a leading character, the supporting characters like her AI dog and delivery Control operator make up for that. Not to mention the variety of characters you meet through the course of the game who include a variety of oddballs and interesting characters. While the game is made up of a load of these small character centric stories theres also an overarching plot about a mysterious AI which becomes more prominent as the game progresses. There are some points where you are offered a couple of choices in how you want to resolve a particular delivery or story moment though most of these choices never really felt that impactful on the game.So overall I enjoyed this game. It's chilled out and atmospheric and while it's a bit limited in terms of gameplay everything else about the game sort of makes up for that shortcoming.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: One of my top 5 games. I've played it twice through and through, got it for myself on ps4 first, loved it so much and talked about it so many times that my gf got me the signature edition for xmas... and a pc version so I could experience driving the hova in 1st person. (to carry around the little Camus pin's on my bagpack irl everywhere is dope) Can't say how much playing this game meant to me, sometimes I'd just start it and drive around Nivalis. My most impactful & immersive feeling in game since firewatch or abzû. I can't wait to play the dlc when it comes out, and see what cool things the game has in store for us again!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Are all the positive reviews bots or shills?The "game complete" achievement is under 15% earned, I walked past a building and got a ~10% achievement. None of you liars played this. This "game" if you can even call it that, has no gameplay. The promotional material above? THATS IT. You drive and walk around a procedurally generated city as an insufferable tumblrina (the developers linked page is Tumblr LMAO) as she makes snarky remarks to everyone and everything you do. It's the worst cringe imaginable as you can tell the writers thought they were being slick and "feisty". The other voice actors are horrendous, the writing is like ChatGPT wrote it and there's TONS of mindless sewage dialogue about NOTHING. the Raina/Camus/Huxley triplet of slop can give you an aneurysm. This game is HUGE and it simultaneously has no content.I finished it to see what passes for "very positive" in current year. It was like I was locked in a bathroom and could only get out by being forced to eat a bathtub of mayo with a spoon. I feel sick and disgusted. This game has convinced me of the dead internet theory, am I the only human here? and if the reviews aren't bots, they're shills and I demand compensation for the torture this fake game put me through. This may very well be the worst game I ever played in my life and I've played alot. The word cloudpunk will forever trigger me. Stay away if you value your sanity
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a game developed by ION LANDS. It is a cyberpunk adventure (almost slice of life) game where you deliver packages, deal with characters and sometimes face the consequences of your choices. It has a 3D pixel art that I wasn't very happy with it at the start. But the game is quite immersive with solid characters, good music and excellent voice acting. The pixel art was forgiven due that. There are some timed missions I hated but that's personal, not the game's fault.Good:+Immersive enviroment. You can use this for a Shadowrun or Cyberpunk game. You can see Blade Runner in this.+Very cool voices. Everyone had the right voice. +Unique and different characters. Huxley is my favorite.+The city feels alive with all the commercials, sound effects and crashes. Sure, they repeat sometimes but there's not much that can be done about it. Bad:-There's a point in the story where you upgrade your vehicle. I wasn't informed or educated on the differences between the choices. -I saw no colorblind mode. I made a bad decision or two due it: I couldn't distinguish properly the quest points.-There's a sidequest where you need to find 80 pieces of something. While it makes sense in the game, 80 is too much. 30 or 40 pieces would've been better. This is a very nice game. Be it at full price or discount it's a very nice game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed it. It's a walking simulator style kind of game. Not a whole lot of action, you're just there for the story. The game looks gorgeous and I did get the feeling a lot of effort went into the game. After the first few deliveries, you kind of get this feeling of "Is this it?" But the story picks up after that and I thought it got real interesting. I guess what I enjoyed about this game the most is that it just feels different from all the other games out there. And once in a while, that ain't so bad. A solid 7.5/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Full Disclosure: The developers were kind enough to send me a key for streaming Cloudpunk.With that out of the way - overall the experience was very enjoyable. I had a couple of minor quibbles though. Not being able to freely move the camera when walking around is one. I am given to understand this may be patched at some point but the more I played the more I realized the camera angles are set to provide you with a very atmospheric viewpoint for each area. This includes then a couple of spots where some CorpSec cars fly over you chasing someone, showing buildings collapsing in the backgrounds, etc. So having now finished the game the fixed camera grew on me!The controls on camera switch however probably needed a bit more tweaking so that you don't start running back and forth between camera switch areas by holding down the controller in one direction. Again this is a minor issue to me but I'm sure it bothered some people.The voice acting, in general, was very solid. There were a couple of lines right towards the end that felt a bit flat to me but I'm not sure if it was the delivery or the writing itself. It was very near to the end of the game though in a conversation between Rania and Control. There were a few other times I felt Rania came across as rude or "smarmy" just for the sake of sounding that way - not due to the actual situation at hand. Again these are minor issues.The atmosphere of the game is SPOT ON. It just feels great, the large skyscrapers, neon lights, the rain (the puddle reflections threw some people off since I don't think they reflect exactly what is around - I didn't notice it either way), the sense of scale both driving and running around, the characters, the story lines and how several of them ended, and so many more things I could name. Just really great work with all of that!My favorite character though by far is Huxley - but then I'm a big Film Noir fan and I found that whole part of the game just really enjoyable. I'm not going to "rate" anything here just reiterate I very much enjoyed the game overall and so did several people who watched it on the live streams.Edit: Still a solid title that has been updated with even more things since launch! Still highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a masterpiece for me. Even if I'm not a big fan of pixelart, this absolutely got me. But it may be because I've always dreamed of flying over a big cyberpunky city like this. (In my dreams I was flying bigger ships and the city was Coruscant from Star Wars but I also thought about taxi-flying in the city of the beginning of the fifth element, and this is a mix of both!)Most important for me was the story of this game. Something unique, I think back to after finishing. And you have the first person perspective, open world, and it's playable with controller. What more can I wish?Thumbs up ION LANDS, you did a great job, and even if the upcoming game would normally not make me interested, I'm hyped for it because of Cloudpunk! Keep it up guys and thank you for this great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played in a long time. Phenomenal atmosphere and OST, and the writing and little bits of lore and character development are nothing short of genius. The way the world changes based off of the choices you make it feel that much more alive and I love that about it; some good immersion. Emptying my pockets for the DLC and I'd definitely pay for a sequel. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a beautiful cyberpunk adventure when it comes to exploring the city and knowing every little story among its neighborhoods and sky roads. It is a shame that some of its gameplay mechanics are not funny or coherent. Ultimately, the game is worth it for the lore, the characters and the story that will motivate players to play until the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I generally lean towards games that you can put hundreds of hours into, but the premise here justifies the short plot: one brutal first night on the job.  It's also kind of cool that the play isn't hardcore difficulty, because god knows that the morally ambiguous choices you need to make are.  As far as cyberpunk goes, this hits the mark dead centre; most of it is very believable in the least pleasant way (lightened with some great satire), and all of it is tinged with the manifest grime of cynicism, injustice, and dying aspiration.   Sounds like a blast, eh?  But the weird thing is that it   Mostly very well written (if a little contrived here and there), mostly very well voiced, and 100% engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is an incredibly impressive looking game with not a lot to it.First and foremost - this game looks amazing. The game takes place in a dark cyberpunk city that looks like a cross between Blade Runner and a fever dream version of Shinjuku. It basically crosses off every cyberpunk cliche, but does it in a very engrossing way, despite the low-poly graphics.You play as a delivery driver with a robot dog companion who has just come to the city to escape her past. Through your job you meet all kinds of strange people, androids and AIs. The encounters are sometimes funny, sometimes touching, but some attempts at satire kind of fall flat. As for what you do in this game, it's extremely simple. You pick up a package at point A, drive with your hover-car to point B and deliver it to the customer. The city consists of a huge area in which you drive around, and many small "islands", where you can land with your car and move around on foot. So essentially you go to one "island", drop off your package, pick up some items and talk to NPCs, and then you're off to your next job. Sometimes you get a choice of what to do with a package or need to reach somewhere in a certain time, but that's it. This game is basically a pure exploration/"walking sim" type of game.Overall Cloudpunk is a cool-looking and charming cyberpunk experience and I would recommend it if you like the aesthetic.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game to just chill out and experience beautiful cyberpunk atmosphere. Gameplay is repetitive and simple - deliver packages, loot items in small areas, talk to NPCs, listen to dialogues. Sometimes game allows you to make some simple choices like to whom you will deliver your package or give you simple quests like - find me object A than you will be allowed to enter zone B. Nothing more (at least, during first 3 hours of gameplay).Sound design and music are beautiful, game supports surround mode, so if you have quadro or 5.1. acoustics you will experience in-game immersion better. Voxel cyberpunk style city is just gorgeous, it really triggers emotions that I experienced when first saw movies like Blade Runner, Running man, Total Recall, Fifth Element and Judge Dredd.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been biased towards Voxel graphic games but this game...So I bought it thinking it to be just some casual driving simulator with cyberpunk themed assets. But to my surprise -(casually put you can walk and roam and talk npcs and all)  this game is a very story driven RPG with choice and consequence...damn this game scratches on itches I didn't think I had! Primarily the itch Cyberpunk 2077 left unscratched this game somewhat does it way better, aside from how easily It had me immersed from a casual "test run" to going objective after objective! The music and sound design is awesome, with very colorful and intersting sounding NPCs that don't feel generic. The story/mission design is great too! The ability to walk, in first person, or third, and view the world around, buy food from vendors. variety of environments to move in! I can't begin to phrase a proper essay/statement for how awesome this game is! Tl;dr - Very Immersive and atmospheric Voxle based Cyberpunk RPG and a MUST for those with a cyberpunk/bladerunner itch!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Game is about deliver driver, reminds me of The Transporter by Jason Statham - Ask nothing and just do the delivery. But I cannot like this game.The player's character, Rania, is so indifferent and unlikeable. I played for an hour, the story is painfully hollow and broken. You are Rania, a new cloud driver and receive delivery commands from the Control. What is annoying is the destination is only given after the talk, no way to skip or make it go faster. Those talks should happen when player drives and has nothing else to do, rather than wait to hear chit chat for minutes just to know where to drive.Everywhere looks alike regardless which part of the city you are in, pick and deliver, there are short stories but uninteresting, I'd hear a better story if I drive Uber and talk to passengers in real life. I experienced few cyberpunk elements, might count a bit doing the  mission, but the rest are just pixels style and 3D cubes. Traders and drug dealers wandering around the street freely offering food and drugs, I do not see anything changes after take in any. NPC to talk to are marked with a face, they offer awkward conversation I feel so embracing, the plots are poorly written. And it is ridiculous when Rania starts the question then ask: What do you want? And the Control is so out of character, too.I am more sorry for the 1.5 hours I wasted than the money I paid for this game.I unlocked every achievements from 81.9% to 30.8% of all players, really do not feel for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 4.25 stars out of 5!------------------PROS: 1) The aesthetic! My god the aesthetic! Taking all the best of Blade Runner, the 5th Element, Cyberpunk 2077, Minecraft, atmospheric city sounds, and moody synthwave (or adjacent) music, and putting it all in this gigantic city, which, though much less detailed and with much less to do in it would nevertheless geographically dwarf Night City (from Cyberpunk). It's simply incredible what kind of atmosphere they were able to achieve with voxels (especially when you play the game in 1st person - which I was over halfway through the game before I even realized you could)2) The controls - especially while flying!3) Likeable main character (certain supporting characters are likeable as well)4) Interesting take on a cyberpunk genre game. You're basically an underground, legal gray area Fed Ex / Grub Hub / Uber person asked once or twice to potentially abett in a splash of terrorism.5) I'm gonna list the story in both the pros and the cons sections because it is both a story full of plot holes and quirks, and yet also a story that somehow still manages to be moving and enjoyable - a story you will enjoy the most at the beginning when you're just starting out and it's fresh and the clunk hasn't become apparent yet, and again towards the end when you begin to find out what happens with the characters you come to care about.5) Scales INCREDIBLY WELL on the Steam Deck (SteamOS)! 800p 16:10 undocked / 1080p 16:9 docked, all visual settings maxed out. I found Cyberpunk to be a perfectly enjoyable experience on Steam Deck as well, both tactilely and visially, but this one was a much more no-compromise experience! The Deck was more "made for this kinda game".-------------------------CONS:1) IMO, the chief sin of this game is that it frequently presents you with seemingly high stakes, stress-invoking decision points....only to have none of those decision points ever seem to have any real consequences. Like for example: at one point in the 3rd quarter of the game, it gives you a choice to either deliver or dispose of a virus, builds the moment up like fates of nations hang in the balance, and then moves on afterwards like nothing happened, regardless of which choice you make. This kinda thing happen multiple times in the game. And in retrospect, it's baffling and infuriating.2) Very inconsistent voice acting. The main character, most of the major supporting characters, and even an incidental character or two are well acted, but others are....well.....PC Gamer described them as "distractingly bad", and that's very apt. It's as if they hired a few professional actors, and then just put up a Craigslist ad for the rest.3) The story has a bunch of holes and quirks in it. In the middle third you really begin to experience tedium, though it does rise again towards the end. Nevertheless, even the end is flawed for a handful of reasons, two of which being a) another seemingly consequence-less "major" choice, and b) it seems to be a pretty abrupt switch from status quo doldrums to bam, all the sudden we're in the closing arc.-------------------MISC: 1) having played this right on the heels of Cyberpunk 2077, I am so struck by how dramatically different a take on the cyberpunk genre it is. It's a much simpler, much more basic treatment that mostly just sees you making deliveries. There is no combat, and I think it might even only be one or two places where you might possibly even be able to die. Ultimately this is a story game hiding inside a delivery game, hiding inside a gorgeous cyberpunk dystopia. However, in the simplicity is also beauty, and a 13hr game is almost the sweet spot for a guy like me with a toddler in the house and a podcast to work on. It's not at all a game you can beat in 10 minutes, but it's also not a game that will demand 12yrs of your life and your firstborn child! And for as vastly different as it is from Cyberpunk, it also, in a strange way, feels kinda like a "kid sister" to it. There may be nothing more to this feeling of connectivity but the "cheerfully gloomy" neon atmosphere of cyberpunk dystopia that they both deftly invoke, but the family resemblance is still very much there, and it feels, in retrospect, like the perfect cool-down game to play after coming off the major time investment that was Cyberpunk!

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a philosophical adventure/walking sim with cyberpunk vibes set in a blocky voxel world for those who don't mind wonky physics and a clunky interface. There are many interesting characters scattered across the city, though most NPCs are either non-interactive or limited to mission props.The driving bits in your HOVA (flying taxi) are awkward and imprecise, but this is only a major issue when combined with the brain-dead AI traffic that will ram you as it remains blissfully unaware of your presence. Still...it's a vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is great if you're not looking for anything too involved. It's easy, fun and stylish. If you're on the hunt for more sophisticated game dynamics, however, you'll probably be disappointed. The only thing you do is pick up and drop off packages, essentially clumps of pixels, over and over. But Cloudpunk isn't about its gameplay; it's about taking in the cyberpunk city while listening to the (mostly) good interplay of characters. You won't lose yourself for hours on end because of that simplistic gameplay, but the game shines in bite-sized 30-60-minute chunks. The best is when you set out on a new mission and the theme song drops. Pump up the bass and bask in the neon pixelated world.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence about this one for a long time, but glad that I finally played it. This is a very atmospheric game - the bleak futuristic city is really captivating.  The story pulls you in with themes of inequality, corruption, and artificial intelligence. The entire extent of the game is performing fetch quests  with the story being told through interactions with your dispatcher, various clients, and a few other characters. I found it relaxing, and enjoyed it, although it did start to feel a bit tedious after a while - I can see how some might not enjoy this type of gameplay. Fans of the walking simulator genre (such as myself) should definitely check this one out.+Beatifully-designed bleak, futuristic city+Immersive exploration of ever-relevant themes+Wonderful chillstep soundtrack and sound design-Some of the choices posed to the player felt rather superficial and contrived-The entirety of the game is fetch quests, the story and setting are great, but it did get a bit tedious

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:The game is about walking, driving, talking, and picking up objects. I think there's enjoyment to be had in the act of traveling and looking at things along the way, but that's all there is to do in this game when you're not talking. If you can appreciate a walking simulator, this may appeal to you.There are long stretches where you're just driving in one direction with nothing to do. You can land on some of the buildings (there aren't any interiors, just exteriors) at any time and explore them to split up the monotony. There are characters to meet, some of whom have side missions, but you'll run out of places to explore before the halfway point of the game. The latter half is drag where you're just doing main missions to finally end it.I encountered a few bugs. I fell through the map twice. Some quest markers wouldn't trigger when I got near them. Some NPCs would appear on the mini-map but wouldn't actually spawn. These were all fixed by restarting the game.Graphics:The game uses a voxel art style. The city is really nice, and the voxels suit it well. The people looked more questionable; I think they look ugly. There's a falcon and a dog in the game that look like N64 models; not voxel-based at all. They look out of place.The world itself is interesting to explore with cool buildings and environments. There are a lot of reused assets. This is reasonable, considering it's an indie game and the world is so large, but it does mean that exploration gets less interesting as you get into the game and start noticing you're seeing the same models over and over again.The city collapses around you as you play. You can't interact with this; it's just an animation that happens in the distance to some of the buildings, but it was cool nonetheless and reinforces the overall plot of the game.Despite my gripes, I have a positive opinion of the world as a whole and enjoy exploring it. It's quite different than other open worlds in terms of design and is quite well-made.Writing:The main character is a Middle Eastern farmer named Rania from a small rural town who has only been in the city for a week. This is a great opportunity; if they represented someone with that background accurately, it could make for an interesting dynamic through a fish-out-of-water story with a rarely portrayed perspective. Instead, Rania has the mentality of a Californian college student. She has no cultural signifiers of her background. She hates guns, disdains religion, never mentions any details about farming (even when meeting other characters who are farmers), and her dialogue is filled with trite progressive talking points. She also seems to know the city better than its residents.There's a music video maker you can meet interested in the pattern on your cloak. At first, Rania assumes he's hitting on her, but it quickly becomes clear he's not actually interested. Despite this, she calls him a sexual predator anyway and complains about "cultural appropriation". The writers are clearly on her side, but she sounds insane.There's a street preacher you can meet, shouting about nonsense. The dialogue is amusing, but at the very end, Rania mentions that he's not approaching any men, only her (note: he didn't approach her, we, the player, have to approach him), and there's follow-up dialogue about how religion doesn't respect "women or minorities". This is unprompted and unrelated to anything the preacher says.There's a side mission where you have to deliver memories from a husband to his widow. Even though Rania's been here for a week, she explains to the woman, whose been living in the city for years, why people in the city make copies of their memories. Rania shouldn't know this; this is a deep cultural fact that most people in the city wouldn't have experience with.There's a theme of "corporations bad" that the game beats the player over the head with. The government is made up of corporations that are part of a council that controls the city from "The Spire". They pass laws and regulations, collect taxes, and pass acts (something like "The Android Equality Act" is mentioned). At one point, a character (a 1-dimensional stereotype of a WASP designed to be hated) remarks that anyone who doesn't like the standards of living in the city just doesn't like the free market. Her husband remarks that the people should "seize the means of production". However, all the problems are caused by government incompetence, negligence, and malice. Licensing is too expensive and excessive (a license is required to play or listen to jazz and to play Chess), taxes are too high and aren't spent on improving the lives of the people, and there are discriminatory regulations on purchases (you buy artificial skin for an android because the law allows humans to buy it but not androids). "Seizing the means of production" would not help any of these issues. These are libertarian criticisms of left-wing economic policy. Corporations don't and can't, enforce licensing, intellectual property, make purchases illegal, collect taxes, etc. Governments do that. These things generally make it harder, not easier, for companies to make a profit. The game explicitly shows that regulations on the free market are bad, but then we are told that, actually, free markets are bad. They literally present a corrupt left-wing government, call it "the corporations", rename the police to "CorpSec", rephrase "maximizing tax revenue" to "maximizing profit", change none of the details, and think they've made a point. If it weren't for the overt progressive messaging elsewhere, I'd think this was actually a crypto-libertarian game.It's explained that there's always parking available and never traffic because corporations want to keep everything running efficiently because that maximizes profits. But then it's explained that the city isn't well looked after (there are disasters throughout the game), and that "The Spire doesn't care" about it. But these are contradictions; obviously, a city that's falling apart is less profitable than one that's stable. The game gestures at corporate powers being incompetent and/or powerless (the game implies both at different times), but they *can* competently keep the roads and parking running well. It just doesn't make sense.At one point you find a credit card. If you return it, you get $1,000, but if you steal with it, you only get $750. This is consistent throughout the game; the good choices are usually rewarded more. This undermines the messaging in the game as we are literally shown that morality is aligned with profits, but are told the opposite. Money is also plentiful. Without selling anything or doing bad, you can easily afford every luxury available for purchase, undermining the game's poverty theme.The game gives you a handful of choices throughout the game that, at most, change dialog. Most have obvious right answers. One of the most ridiculous was a segment where you had to choose to save 3 out of 6 people from a toxic gas leak. Your choices are a black woman doctor, a black android who just wants to help people, an android (with no skin at all) who is a veteran, the WASP stereotype from earlier, the white evil scientist who caused the leak, and the white CEO who talks about bailing his brother out when he "ran over that colored woman" (remember, this is like 1,000 years in the future).The main plot is about an old AI called CORA. The details are built up as a big mystery, but it's a small thing in comparison to everything else. CORA's dialog is some of the most obnoxious, masturbatory dialogue I've ever listened to. It's like someone heard the Sovereign dialog from Mass Effect 1 and tried copying it with no understanding of why it was cool in the first place. There's a consistent theme about people being "programmed by their environment", which is both not really true and isn't examined in a meaningful way in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: A neat Sci-Fi delivery game of which you can explore this Cyberpunk-esque city which can look stunning at times. You can tell the developer has put a lot of time into making the city and the people in it feel real, it has a very dark and depressing vibe to it I find. I play this game with very little interest in the story, I really only play it to listen to music and chill out exploring the city, and it works really well for that.The games biggest weakspot for me is the amount of dialog, I wouldn't mind if a bunch of dialog was presented when I interact with someone on the street but after every delivery there's so much dialog it gets annoying. I have the voice's muted as I found the voice acting to be weak, but it means that I mostly ignore the text since it drags on for so long when i'm trying to drive. Both the dialog and the overall story have been the weakest part of this game for me. Not all of the characters are bad though, I actually do enjoy interacting with people on the street and sometimes the people I deliver to, I just don't like that how much forced dialog there is. If however, you can get past this what you have is a really neat game, and maybe you're the type of person who's into the story in which case you'll have a blast, but even if you're not there is still fun to be had here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning. It's refreshing to be in a cyberpunk environment as just a regular person instead of the usual detectives and hackers and gangsters. Art, story, environmental effects, and soundtrack are all great. I've stopped several times just to watch the clouds and listen to the music for a while, or driven off the highways into the various neighborhoods. Such a chill mood.

_childDocuments_.review: You know this feeling you get when you know a dev team was very ambitious, and was able to deliver on everything they set out their ambition for? This game is basically that.BUT, to be ambitious is not only about setting a high goalpost, but also about boldly making calculated sacrifices for its sake.Needless to say, the city and environment design is breathtakingly gorgeous. Not only did the blocky design not interfere with the environment, it added to it. The sacrifice of that is the character sprites which look like a Roblox character got dropped as a baby.The atmosphere, including music and traffic is something that makes you produce a substantial amount of cream in your nether zones. The sacrifice of that is crashing into anything that moves or doesn't move, and driving physics that feel like your car has some vendetta against you from back in the day when you were both working under the highly-esteemed Gambino family.The character development, design, and storylines feel like reading an ethnography. You get involved with everyone. You love, hate, sympathize, get sad for, get happy for, almost everyone. The sacrifice is the fact this entire story happens in one night; god I wish I had Rania's out-of-time existence while im studying for a final. Also the mission from hell: the infamous punchcards.The way this game manages tension and the lack-thereof is absolutely ingenious. I swear, as Rania was experiencing moral and decision fatigue from how many choices she had to make that affected people, I started experiencing it too, dropping my nice face and just making tyrannically "moral" decisions, in a way that says "By lord Jesus in heaven, if this city wont make sense, then I will just do what I think is right at the moment, and let anyone behind me, good or bad, burn." The sacrifice is the rushed ending that didn't have any buildup, including for the characters involved. We got the equivalent of someone pulling you off stage with a pole mid performance.Every little interaction is meant to focus first and foremost on world-building. Not every interaction is consequential and intense, but sometimes its just about knowing more about the culture. A decision I absolutely love. The sacrifice is the fact that consumable items have absolutely no purpose. Well, at least I managed to learn that Rania's favorite meal is the traditional sushi platter ig.There is one instance where I feel the devs made an anti-sacrifice (i.e. sacrificing something good for something bad). It's when we got  in exchange for Tl;Dr: I like this game the way I like my one-night-stands; knows what they want, knows how to get it, and knows what to give away in order to get it.

_childDocuments_.review: My Playtime at the time of writing the review is representative of the whole game story finished with vast majority of sidequests. The best cyberpunk experience you can get right now. The graphics can be a bit inconsistent (some shaders or the game logo are not voxel stylized, the rest of the game mostly is), but overall very immersive. The voxel graphics can take an hour or so to get used to.  Driving controls are better soon after you get a better car and some upgrades, and this game has also that amazing feeling from old school GTA and NFS games, when you're just driving around the city, enjoying the soundtrack and your surroundings and you let everything in your life go. Story is amazing, there aren't any plottwists you wouldn't get after playing it for a while, foreshadowing is a bit obvious, but not every story has to have surprising twists. Characters are well-defined, their stories make sense, and it is really easy to empathize with them. Some storylines were really moving, I have to admit some ninjas cutting onions were definitely there.All in all I would take this game more as a visual novel, with game elements, a very refreshing take on the cyberpunk genre that doesn't try anything very bold with it at the same time. Just a note, that after they included an option for first-person movement of your character, I never switched back to the side view,m which was originally the only option.I would definitely like to return to this universe, and I am wishing the game studio good luck with their next titles.PS: Soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lit.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I just got this game on a whim so I wasn't expecting much. But I ended up enjoying the commentary and the look. There's not a lot of gameplay though. It was more like an interactive story with a lot of walking and a few false decision. The gameplay loop gets a little repetitive pretty quickly. It reminds me a bit of old fetch quest games from Lucas Arts and I think that's all it's supposed to be. Overall a low stress experience with a competent story and neat aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Crime Cities, but with less shooting and a better city.Quite good for an indie game. I was sucked in immediately, missions flow one into another smoothly. Great ambience, fitting the relaxed-style gameplay.The story was okay, if you are a fan of cyberpunk in general, you will see the plot twists a mile away, but some characters grew on me nonetheless.Despite voxel graphics, the city looks really nice. Made lots of screenshots.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is better than the sum of its parts.If you were to take every aspect of it apart, you'd probably think Cloudpunk is a very mediocre game. The voice acting is hit or miss, the music is always fitting but forgettable, the story had me invested enough to see it through to the end but not enough for me to really care about the fate of my characters...The gameplay itself is decent, even though your Hovercar's hitbox always felt a bit bigger than it should be, and the (fixed) camera while travelling on foot can get janky.But strangely enough, when you put all of those things together and serve them as a single package, it works pretty well. It's easy to lose yourself in the game's world, with the occasional interesting character or quest.It's like eating a bag of chips. If you start looking too close at the ingredients, you probably won't like what you see. But if you accept it for what it is and get lost in it, it's a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Cyberpunk meets Quarantine, meets Minecraft. You get Cloudpunk.The voxel art game is a very interesting concept and quite enjoyable as you fly around the city completing, mainly delivery missions to begin with. However the more you play the more you begin to get involved in more meaningful missions that involve the citizens of the city you are in. There are several characters you interact with along the way, however the city itself is quite vast and some people you speak to, have no bearing on anything you do.The game itself is very playable and has no bugs from what I experienced, smooth gameplay and a large city to drive around in, which is even larger if you take into consideration all the connected maps. The maps are connected by tunnels which you warp in and out of.You can also park your vehicle and walk around the city which is always floating above the clouds. Interact with some characters and do side missions as well as collect various things for powerups along the way.There are some issues though. One criticism is that the game is far too short. Steam is showing that I played the game for a total of 8 hours, which from start to finish, isnt a lot. Although the game does have some sort of "main plot", its very thin and doesnt offer much in the way of game play as its very disjointed. There isnt much scope for any major characters apart from you yourself, although you do have one main character who you grow fond of. But an abrupt and unexpected ending was a bit disappointing for me especially since it felt like such an anticlimax.That said however, you can always go back and finish off side missions. But I can help but feel the game could have been so much more. The side missions afterwards just become repetitive and somewhat pointless since there is no main plot to follow.Overall a good game, nice cyberpunk style graphics and easy enough game play but could have been so much more. I would only recommend buying it if its on a sale with a decent chunk off as the gameplay doesnt last very long.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: For the full story, you need to buy the base game and the DLC, then play through the base game to completion and the DLC will continue, including your choices (so it says).The game is casual enough that you can 'ignore' the main storyline quests and continue with the sidequests and fully complete them, the game is forgiving and satisfying.The controls get a bit janky in the DLC with racing, but it's still decent. The graphics are nicely polished, and you really should experience the 'in hova' view (first person), and at least first person camera while walking around, at least once. The music is very good, the whole experience is 'bladerunner cinematic' while also mixing in drama, humour and a reasonably good cyberpunk dystopian storyline.It's a pretty well polished game, the only major bug I experienced was a member of the public phasing through the floor.I've played this mainly on another platform, the game's worth the price at half price for the main and DLC.The writing had me gripped for the story, and as far as 'delivery person with a storyline' games go (like Lake, Death Stranding, etc.) this's a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a while ago and I really enjoyed it. It's not the most gameplay heavy game, but it does what it advertises really well. It's about exploration, talking to different people, and seeing different things. It's about making decisions and not knowing if they'll have a good or bad outcome. And if you've ever just wanted to fly around a cyberpunk city, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a meh... option instead of positive/negative.  Which really is a shame because it could have been better in a lot of aspects if it was just not voice acted or the story was better written.Good atmosphere, love the music, controls, interesting side characters (more interesting and unfortunately more likable than the main character that's voiced by a monotone, moody written, dull dull person) and world building is interesting.Main characters make me wish I could go full rogue, i find them really unlikable and jaded (for reasons I know).  Pashta I really dislike, 3/4 the story I really dislike as well.  No surprises in the story, very telegraphed.  Ultimately the only characters I liked was Control, the dogs voice actor (character and writing is obnoxious), Huxley (he talks a lot though)... yeah that's about it.Really get the game for the atmosphere and the time killing fetch quests, so get it on sale.  I paid $7 on sale and I feel that's about right.  Don't get it if you need a good story line (seriously gets cringe and had me eye rolling, took a break a couple of times it was that bad), good voice acting, or need different styles of quests, you will be disappointed.   So I really feel this is a 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda bummed out how it turned out to be. My background, I tend to play pretty polished games and as my library suggest AAA is most of them.I hoped this game would be kind of a cyberpunk replacement, with less of a forced story, where you can do missions and then still find side quests.Anyways, reasons why I didn't like it: - Cars flying through buildings- Never saw a cop car, thought Corpsec is more omnipresence, but this is also a part of the issue that there is a mediocre ambience in the game.- 3 Different styles in the game, characters look completely different in 3D and in Pictures and the map looks like it is voxel minimap from minecraft- The Soundscape is mediocre at best- The voxel count is usually very varying- Why are there so many super buff but short people?- What is that ticking noise I always hear when walking?- Why loading screens- This would be more of a console game- There could be more people walking outside- More missions- Have you thought about mod support to fix those issues or are going to make this game better?If you got free time on your hands and almost no money then maybe, just maybe I could recommend a mediocre game with mediocre atmosphere.
