_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well thought out and overall fun experience. The open voxel world of flying cars and grungy cyberpunk towers and platforms offers a lovely mix of Blade Runner and Fifth Element aesthetics. Worth every penny!You can also customize your HOVA (your car), home, and the player character, which was a great touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  I like the game, but it isn't for everybody.I made it through cloudpunk in a couple of long sessions and I enjoyed the experience.  It's a narrative forward game whose value is largely in the story.  The vast majority of actual gameplay is pretty much drive your HOVA from point A to point B.  Or wander around on platforms looking for stuff to pick up.  There is no real difficulty, at least until they introduce the timed deliveries.In my mind this game functions best as a work of interactive fiction.  You explore the largest city in the world and as a delivery driver interact with it's inhabitants.  The writing is above average for a video game and it hits all of the notes you expect a "high cyberpunk" story to hit.  It frequently gives you choices, which I know at least affects the dialog, dunno if it affects the missions.  If you liked Neuromancer (the book) you'll probably like the story in this game.  If you don't know about Neuromancer, your time is probably better spent reading Neuromancer.    Parental guidance; this game spends some time talking about future kinky sex.  It isn't absurdly graphic, and I think you can actually miss all the conversations, but it is in there.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, original, sad, hopeful. Cloudpunk is a work of love. If you like Bladerunner or cyberpunk as a genre and look for a mostly stress free game, then Cloudpunk might be what you are looking for.Cloudpunk's strongest part is its city ("Nivalis") as a place to drive your flying car through, or explore different locations and characters on foot. The architecture is fantastic. Sometimes I just stop for a while to enjoy it. While the main story and the side quests may appear not as sophisticated as in big budget titles like Cyberpunk 2077, one gets emotionally invested. Using many known elements, Cloudpunk's setting and subtle worldbuilding is still an original take on the cyberpunk genre. You don't want to live for real in this setting and many fates are sad or even grim. The setting is rich enough to make a full RPG out of it.Cloudpunk is mostly a peaceful game - sky traffic is not without danger, though. XD There are no traditional fights in it, but there are some timed missions. Five from five stars. Would deliver for Cloudpunk again.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a little jaunt through a gorgeous pixel / voxel art game in a Cyberpunk city with some amazing characters, quests and A or B decisions on how to finish said quests give Cloudpunk a look. You play as Rania, a girl from the Eastern Peninsula who has to move to Nevalis, a giant mega-city, to work as a Delivery Driver to the titular Cloudpunk. There's so many interesting people to run into, like the Android who's paid to be a literal Sex Doll, laying still and everything to the Android Detective who speaks in old black-and-white "cold slap of rain" style similes.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk emulates the Blade Runner aesthetic fairly accurately with its downtrodden, claustrophobic atmosphere, down to the minute details like the commercials echoing around you from the blimps and brightly lit ads in beautiful neon. It's just a shame that the cyberpunk visuals are wrapped up in such mediocre gameplay. I wanted to love Cloudpunk but the dreadful dialogue got me off to a bad start, and the game never really recovered. Characters never shut up and the so-called humour is more miss than hit. The on-foot sections are hampered by performance issues, and while the city looks fantastic I can't say the same for the hideous NPCs.Flying through the city without distraction is the best Cloudpunk gets, but it's short-lived.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is an excellent little adventure. It's a glorified walking sim, which isn't a bad thing at all when you nail presentation. Great writing and an absolute triumph of an atmosphere make driving and walking around Nivalis a very pleasant experience. Worth the asking price and I look forward to the rumored sequel
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving the game so far, it feels pretty alive, I like the story. While most of it is basically going from point A to point B they found a way to keep it interesting. Driving the HOVA is challenging at times and I'm trying to get better at it. Playing it and looking around makes me wish for more in the universe from what I've gleaned talking to npcs. I wish we could be street racers like those you see, or corpsec chasing after whoever broke some corporate law, etc. Great Cyberpunk experience. I just wish I remembered where my apartment was haha.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: It's games like these that make me wish Steam had a "neutral" option for reviews. For the sake of this review, I feel more compelled to recommend it than to not recommend it.This game's visuals, atmosphere, and environment are amazing. Without a doubt, the setting is the best thing about this game. The music, SFX, and background audio (of certain intercoms heard throughout the city) definitely make this game feel like the Cyberpunk story teller it claims to be.The story is rather meh. At the time of writing this, at 6.4 hours in, I have not finished the story. I'll finish it eventually, but It definitely feels like it drags on too long, and certain story events are simply in the way. The voice acting doesn't help with this. I'm certain that the story would be more engaging if the character's . For the sake of comparison, most of the characters in this game sound like high school students sight-reading the script to a play....like it took effort to get the line. Some characters sound very good and help mitigate this, but even the protagonist sounds like she's reading a script instead of talking. Definitely a killer. Otherwise the game is chill and probably worth the $20 it's listed for. As advertised, you drive around a dystopian future city, delivering packages for an illicit delivery service. I give it a 6/10. I recommend watching gameplay of it before deciding to buy it yourself though.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Do not let the graphics deter you from this game. This is an extremely atmospheric game, that envelops you in that gloomy, cyberpunk atmosphere and delivers a story that makes you attached to the people you meet.The gameplay is simple, you only walk, talk and drive your car. The meat of the game is in it's story and world presentation.The voice acting is surprisingly AAA quality and very varied. The stories of the people you encounter, as a driver for an elicit delivery company, are all unique and very often even provide you with a simple A or B choice that leaves you to wonder what became of the person in the end.This place has a story and it is out there for you to engage with.I went into this game not expecting anything but the atmosphere. In the end, I got much more, and this game WILL stick in my memory as something unique I played, in a world of "Ctrl+C Ctrl+V" games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Death Stranding and Cyberpunk 2077 had a love child. The game is relatively short if you did what I did and just blast through the missions. Mu suggestion is take your time, explore, talk to everyone. Unless a mission has a timer it isn't timed.Take your time, explore enjoy the ambience. This game is 9.5/10 for me.Warning: This game is a slow paced game, not a lot of action. That's my style, but it may not be yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Great base of a game. Beautiful, interesting, rich and immersive, however it feels like its missing a mechanic or two, maybe a tweak here and there. For example, I would like to see vehicle meters to track damage, to go along with the fuel consumption. Meters for the character to go along with the food and other purchasing options. A zoom function on the map would be nice too. Overall, a nice game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning game, mesmerizing atmosphere, well-thought NPC interactions and a beautiful cyberpunk metropolis...You should buy it if you are a cyberpunk fan.Yet, there is this frustrating thing that I must tell you about.I am already invested in the story but the dialogues are endless. They just don't end and they don't actually say anything about the story. Almost every character is a bit sarcastic and they never SHUT UP. Stop speaking if you are not going to say something that matters. Long dialogues do not weave anything into the texture of the game. Every time someone starts speaking including Rania, they just go on and on and never stop. I don't know why you went with this but please, it is sucking my life energy. shuuut uuuup.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm 8 hours in and I felt like leaving a little review.First of all, don't go in expecting a choice-rich rpg where the story can branch into many different directions.I feel like it's easy to get that impression from the promo material.PROS:- A large and beautiful open world to wander about.- The presentation of the cyberpunk setting is top-notch. If you're a fan of that specific kind of ambience, this game has it in spades.- The story feels fluid and dynamic, tackling many different subjects you can expect from a cyberpunk'esque world, from starting an android uprising to questioning how a cherrypie salesman gets his cherries.CONS:- I can't help but feel that, even though the developers conciously chose to go this narrative and passive route of storytelling, they could've gone the extra mile and added in some fun interactive choices during dialogues, even if this wouldn't mechanically change the outcome of the story.- The ingame camera is fixed most of the time, framing the world in such a way that really brings out the beauty of a neon lit dystopian. However... the camera does tend to go a bit nuts when you're navigating through narrow alleys, which is kind of annoying.- There are also several moments in the game where the main character (or another character) mention something happening, even though this is not visible for the player, which can be somewhat confusing at times.Overall, I think this game really caters to a very specific audience.If you enjoy the cyberpunk setting and you generally prefer a rich story over diverse gameplay, then this is definitely worth picking up!------------------------------------UPDATE [12 hours played, finished the game]:------------------------------------Okay, so I finished the game after 12 hours of play.Here are some small footnotes I wanted to convey in order to fill out my review.So now that I've finished the story, I cannot fully confirm whether the choices you make in the game actually affect the ending, but I do really like the ending I personally got, with the choices I made.There are most likely plenty of side-quests/characters I've missed, as some locations are harder to reach than others, but that did not deminish the overall experience for me.I do want to add one more Con to my little list above however.I find it somewhat a shame that a lot of buyable items in the game have little to no use whatsoever. It would've been nice if eating food gave you perhaps a little speedboost (on foot) or that buying decoration for your home did something besides adding it cosmetically.I even bought a cybernetic arm off a merchant at one point, which cost a lot, but as far as I know you can't do anything with it. Bit of a shame in my opinion.Anyway, I still do think this game is definitely worth a buy if you're a fan of the cyberpunk aesthetic and repetitive, but chill gameplay supported with a fleshed out story.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes going into this, maybe that's mostly why I was left disappointed. But I also feel I have some genuine criticisms. I did finish the game, I guess that counts for something.The soundtrack is absolutely incredible, easily the best part of the game. Everything else however, was simply underwhelming. As for the actual gameplay, I'd say it's one step above a walking simulator. Maybe comparable to something like Death Stranding except you're driving. So the gameplay definitely isn't anything to write home about. Heck, there aren't even any races, aside from timed missions where you try to reach a destination in time.The second best part of the game would have to be the story. But that's where most of my criticism lies. I was primarily interested in the main AI storyline, but that only comprises about 30 minutes of the game, maybe an hour max. Everything else just felt like, to me, random distractions and side stories. And this is if you only focus on the main quests. But I did everything.None of the decisions are meaningful. Just slightly different responses and it's mostly how you feel about a situation. It seems there are no truly wrong decisions. Just a reflavoring of the same outcome. Even the final decision in the game, almost harkens back to the original Mass Effect 3 endings... not literally a "different colors" situation, but... close.The only reason this is middling for me is because I love AI, and that part of the storyline was alright. And the soundtrack definitely elevated the experience for me. But if you're not particularly interested in a story involving an AI, and some nice cyberpunk/synthwave music, I'd give this a pass. Definitely listen to the soundtrack, though!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is packed with content. I spent 6 hours playing this game and wasn't bored a single time. The only thing I wish was included in the game was a sandbox like mode. Idk what it would be called if sandbox is the right word, but I wish there were just deliveries you can make that aren't story related and you continue doing different shifts and just flying around in this awesome city. Overall though, wonderful game, I can 100% recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a dope game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: My mind blown. I didn't know that there is a lot of people working on this game. Thanks to the latest updates "FPS Unlocked", it's very mesmerizing to see the city walking around in first-person with great lighting. Each character have a story, voice and accent even if they slight blocky appearance. I hope there will be a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game for the concept and visuals and it delivered more than I expected. Full thumbs up. All the cyberpunk city landscapes from movies that I've always wanted to see more but couldn't. It is not an action game and should not be reviewed as one in my opinion. It is about following a story, which you can do while exploring the stunning world the developers created. There are other popular games where you only need to follow a story and people like me buy them for that reason.One of the best things of this game is that you only need one hand to play. The other hand is for holding your drink while you explore the city and enjoy all the details in the buildings. You can set the voice volume to zero and relax with the music and sounds.I really believe (hope) that there will be updates for this game to include more content, there certainly is room for it, but I will continue to enjoy the game and explore the entire map after completing the main story.  Only two points I would give as feedback:-If I miss a dialogue there's no way to repeat it. If something distracts you you better pause (Esc) the game-No option to change the hotkeys for the lateral movement upgrade, which ends up being the same as my Action key
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 100x better than the Store page here makes it look. How the HELL did I miss out on this for so long?At the ending credits I was waiting to see the name of the Marketing people so I could talk ♥♥♥♥ about them  here specifically, and of course there weren't any.  Your publishers did you all dirty on the marketing.This game is what happens when you put all of your talent everything except Marketing.  If this game were a Dungeons & Dragons character, it rolled a 15 for every stat except Marketing, which rolled a 2.The world building and environment art are outstanding. The voice acting is great. The narrative is decent. The core game loop is great, My only feedback are a few things:- Fire your publisher and get a better one if you haven't already because their marketing team failed _miserably_ on this- The character art improvements of the new game you announced recently is perfect, so I won't talk ♥♥♥♥ about the character art in this game because you all obviously already know- If I make it to the destination before the dialogue finishes, you guys should have some voice lines to interrupt and say "alright we're here" so that we can skip the conversation and continue.  That speed boost upgrade (which I loved) made me have to spin in circles for a few minutes sometimes, which is not fun from a game design perspective- Many of the choices I made during the story ended up having no pay off or consequences at the end, and so some of those minor story arcs seemed like a waste of time in hindsightLittle things that I especially liked:- The video game console was great, one of the timed missions started while I was in the middle of a high score run and so I failed it- The surprise ending gift was great... I just need a button to interact with my friend!- Letting me free roam around the city and explore after the story is finished is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I love the atmosphere of this game, but it's basically a walking sim with awful voice acting and obvious good or evil choices that crop up occasionally. There's a talking dog character that was particularly grating to me, although mileage will obviously vary there. i'd recommend giving it a go if the visuals look appealing and being prepared to refund if you start to get bored. It looks like this dev's next game will be set in a more interactive version of the city, which is closer to what I was looking for here. Cloundpunk's city feels lived in, but I didn't feel like I was living in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game purely for the Synthwave, and I was well-rewarded for it. You start out as a basic-level courier delivering boxes from place to place. Nothing special. As it turns out, you find yourself involved in an actual story and a character arc; a real one, and it's a lot of fun. Also, if you buy the "City of Ghosts" DLC, the characters you meet actually make references to the decisions you made in the base game, and the choices available to you adjust accordingly. The controls are pretty straightforward. Driving and flying your hovercar doesn't take long to learn, and the in-game art is beautiful, and I mean just beautiful. There were times when I held off on progressing the game story simply because it was so unbelievably relaxing to get lost in the environment. And the soundtrack, my God, the OST is incredible. I bought the OST just so that I could have the soundtrack on my phone and listen to it while I'm away from the computer going on leisurely walks through the city where I live. So, interesting story, interesting character development, gloriously beautiful music. Yes, I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a visually beautiful game the audio+music is fantastic. I sat down one night and played for a few hours before I decided I needed to get off for work. I love the little interactions between the characters and there's plenty of times where it can be really wholesome. This game is an absolute vibe and is a must play! I recommend you to get this game and play it but whatever you do, don't ask what's in the package and always deliver on time. Control out.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Good pair of headphones on, listening to the rain running down the windshield, music punctuating the mood as we weave in between tall buildings, over cities, a deep rumble ever present, under bridges, we are close now. Our nav point is in view, navigation has parking off to the left, spin around and descend, using the view from the camera below to make adjustments as we hone in on a parking bay. On foot, wind blowing, we have a job to do, we scoped the walkways as we flew in, the elevator up ahead will get us where we need to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I played this game a year and a half ago but I thoroughly enjoyed it. Its a game i keep coming back to and makes me excited for their upcoming game 'Nivalis'. The characters, the stories, the conversations, the city itself and the lore. I was hooked and mesmerized the entire time by how beautiful the city looked and how you could tell the richer places apart from the poorer ones. I liked the fact that you drive around most of the time because i just wanted to chill. However i did want to enter buildings a bit and interact more with the environment. Overall, I absolutely loved it so...9.5/10worth my money. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a keeper and well worth the price. _childDocuments_.review: Its a nice game. i liked neon look, music etc. You will like the game for sure, so its recommended. my only grumble is that there are few controls  (A big plus), BUT  the keys used are W,S,A,D and space bar =  up, left shift down = down .I am a totally lazy player and could not remap the space or left shift keys, to the side buttons on my mouse.I could remap to other keys say up = G.. _childDocuments_.review: By cora this game is preachy...The hero cant help but judge everyone around her, telling them how they should live when she is the one who just moved into the city. She has no problem spouting out things like "cultural appropriation" when someone wanted to use a pattern on her jacket but, in the same conversation lying about value of items she has just to make profit. Belittle random people about religion or actions to her AI Dog as she drives highly likely illegal cargo and buy drugs to get in to clubs to work with criminals. She will moan and make comments every time she gets an affluent client, saying things like she will laugh when the higher parts of the city come crashing down and they live among them (Poor?) but still somehow makes enough money in one night to fully furnish an apartment and get food for a kid she ... adopts? _childDocuments_.review: This game has a great soundtrack with a simple yet fulfilling game play experience.  I recommend this based on two things that I can't simply ignore. One, the price for the content and regular support is fantastic. You will easily get the time for cost back and then some. Two, The dev is active in making changes, adding things, wanting to do more. It's a smaller dev but what is here is great and I love the style and feel of everything. I look forward to patch notes to see what new things are coming and changing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The game drips of Blade Runner Style, even has Vangelisesque atmospheric music...and as there hasn't been a lot of good titles in that vein since the old Westwood Studios’ 'Blade Runner' [on GOG now!] that's not a bad thing. The environment is immaculate and must have taken ages to create. It’s a lot to look at, though it's hard to really feel each area is different from each other visually. Besides the vehicles buzzing through the skyways, and generic npc's walking everywhere, its mostly a static world, save for the random mission giver or food cart or merchant.  I wish there were a few unique buildings to walk into, a club, a restaurant, a disco, anything would be nice.The game plays out in character driven story missions. Nothing complicated [fetch this, talk to this dude, deliver this etc.], they exist to move the story along.  I'm only about 5 hours in and taking my time. The interactions are sometimes funny, sometimes poignant, sometimes sad. Often a cautionary tale of our future.  As amazing as it is, it does tend to all look the same after a while. This game feels like modders could really take it and run with it if the devs allowed this someday. It would be great to add more content, add multiplayer, add social bars and clubs to meet and chat in.Don't expect a lot and you'll be happy. I recommend purchasing and experiencing it for all its merits. It's a game to sit back and relax with on a rainy Saturday night, sipping your whiskey and coke and soaking in the atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've now finished this. My feelings haven't changed from the below.I'll be honest... I've not finished this, but I will review and finish it just because I put my money into it and at this point I can't refund... But for everyone else who may be thinking about it?This is a glorified walking simulator. The walking speed when out of your vehicle is too slow (yes you can buy boosts) but oh my god a lot of it just feels so unnecessarily and arbitrarily long if you're trying to collect everything. That part of it is just very dull and very boring - but it's the developer's decision... e.g. elevators that take an age to move from place to place or really non-intuitive maps that require you to move around (albeit quite slowly) to discover where a certain elevator or tunnel may be so you can get to a place where they may have placed items.Now you may say... That's not so bad... Except 90% of the items marked on the map for you to collect have no bearing on the plot at all and are used very minimally in side quests. The items are there for you to fetch to give 'hidden depth' of which truly this game has none. Zero. If items are not important they just shouldn't be on your map to collect at all. It inflates the gameplay time artificially.Only purchase this if you're into "the feeling of cyberpunk."Don't buy this if you expect anything more other than great visuals. The developer's care and attention began and ended there. I would love to say they put effort into the story but when there are a vast amount of collectables... Well, if you're someone like me that wants to collect everything then it becomes a distraction. At that point I couldn't really tell you what the main story is because I'm too busy doing everything else and going through arbitrary (but good looking) crap to get it.Please, don't believe the hype. Buy this if you want great visuals and aesthetics (and providing you can also stop the collectathon that I'm on)... Otherwise, avoid. Your £17 could be spent better elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this game up on the steam sale because I like the cyberpunky, futuristic idea and theme. I usually never finish games or actually do any type of achievement hunting,  but this game was able to suck me in and keep my interest long enough to want to do those things. _childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: +Atmospheric and chill game+Great cyberpunk style city.+Great soundtrack+Rather interesting plot (at the time of writing this review I haven't gotten through it yet, probably somewhere in the middle)+A sufficient number of side characters and quests (not a few, but not too many either)- The architecture of some locations is too confusing, to collect all the items in them you have to run quite a few laps (e.g. the Stacks area).- Lack of ability to view the map of the whole city at once.  At the beginning of the game accidentally stumbled upon an NPC who buys antique game tapes / disks, and forgot in which area of the city it was. To find it again, had to fly around almost the entire city.- As an extension of the previous point, the lack of the ability to manually put a marker on the map to not lose the location- Lack of health indicator on the car. It is not clear when to repair it- Quite weak optimization. On PC it works without problems on highests settings,  but on Steam Deck I had to limit FPS to 30 for the game to be comfortable to play. At the same time, increasing the graphics settings from medium to high does not affect the picture much, but the power consumption increases from 10 to 25w. Overall I'd give it 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: A true and pretty awesome cyberpunk game with a rich story, well-rounded characters, awareness of socioeconomic and political issues and some really emotional and humorous moments. Rania is a debt orphan from "the East" who had to sell everything including her dog's mainframe in order to escape the debt corps and now she's an immigrant in Nivalis working minim wage semi-legal deliveries. She meets lots of interesting, quirky and often tragic characters in her jobs, suffers racist and sexist micro-aggressions as to be expected and stumbles upon an actual Goddess. The DLC is really a standalone sequel, having the same gameplay time as the original. There is lots of dialogue during driving and themes touch on family, friends, history, philosophy, capitalism, automation, slavery and mental health. Since it's not an open RPG you don't have as many opportunities to choose what you can do, but the story is so gripping and Rania & Camus are such solid characters that I don't mind following their own decisions most of the time. When I do get a decision, it kind of tears me up inside knowing I can't just reload and see what happens. The only negative about the game which I consider maybe a missed opportunity is to have an array of radio stations to listen to like in GTA. At least the reason why we don't get to have that is kinda part of the story, whereby you basically have to pay a premium on everything as basic as the generic automata to respect your gender identity if you are anything other than a "Mr.". I hope that in the next game Nivalis there's some radio though. It would give us more opportunities to tune in to what's happening in Nivalis, from corpsec stuff, pop culture to revolutionary media. Plus, there is SO much driving, you gotta have a little something!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful atmosphere, fantastic soundtrack, relaxed gameplay. I love the world of Cloudpunk - there's plenty to spark the imagination! As much as I love lore-heavy games, I appreciate that the player isn't constantly being bombarded by exposition.The voice-acting is somewhat uneven, but good overall. There is some swearing and, given the overall vibe of the game, it often seems misplaced. Some of the references to 21st century culture crack the sense of immersion, but they do encourage the player to think on our present from a different perspective.As this is a more casual game, don't expect your decisions or morality to drastically impact the story. The narrative raises questions, or thought experiments, that encourage (at very least) a second playthrough.Annnnd, that's my review. Yep.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: How can you not love this game? 10/10From the sky high buildings, the exciting "Blade Runner style" music to every single character, related or non-related to the main story, comes a great adventure that sets off a newly amazing character named Rania and her AI Camus. While at first glance this looks like a another Indie game showing up on your Steam front page, IT IS NOT. It is a completely new adventure, filled with things to see, hear and experience. The story starts off as normal delivery game, but sets off to a crazy deep story, filled with plot twists and stories you'd never know could exist. This game is by far one of the best experiences i've had in video games, and I just played TLOU2, one of my favourite games. Congratulations to everyone working on the game and I hope that many updates will come, cause you rock and you've made an amazing game for the world. You should be damn proud!Ps: First person view? You guys are just simply the best. Keep up the good work and I hope Rania's story might continue in some DLC or future game, cause she's a badass! Camus too ;)

_childDocuments_.review: It was not what I expected. It was much more.The theme is very Neuromancer/Bladerunner-esque. The setting and music match it perfectly - I'm considering adding the soundtrack permanently to my favorite playlist. The visual style is... interesting. 🙂You play as the protagonist Rania, a strong-minded, young woman with a no-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attitude who moves to the city Nivalis and starts a job as a delivery driver to get rid of her debts. Most of the gameplay loop consists of hovering through the city with your vehicle and having conversations. The game doesn't put any tough skill barriers in your way, so that you can focus on exploring the city and listening to the oftentimes snarky dialogues.Definitely would love a sequel to that!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk plays its strengths right from the start, it is a game all about . From the moment you drive off into the night sky,  . Taking off on foot to deliver your first package, .When you.....well you don't do much of anything else in this game actually. For a 26 CAD price tag, Cloudpunk has very little to it mechanic-wise. You drive -> walk -> talk in a gameplay loop that's serviceable only on the best days. Crazy Taxi, this is not; the most your car can hope for is to not bump into traffic on the speedy blue highway-tunnel as you drive in a straight line holding W down for two consecutive minutes. Running on land is more of the same, except you might have to take some detours to find an elevator because you parked on the wrong floor. I'm not sure if there's a way to "lose", the game has a few timed events but I cleared them all on my first try. The game also has a lack of some (imo) obvious QOL features including:- No indicator when your "speed up" buff from eating/drinking runs out- Disposable pick-up items being individually highlighted on the map, just as important as your side or main quests- Elevators that you have to wait painfully long to use because they are on a different floor- The inability to change anything about your vehicle except its trail (aside from a single decision you make early on, which locks you into a single car model for the whole game)- No indication what the other overworld buff (the eye) does, still no clue about this one- No minimap- Your car automatically slowing down to a standstill when you go through a transition, despite entering the new map at full speedIt's a game really held together by it's incredible voxel graphics, which depict the in-game city of Nirvalis as a sprawling mess. Towers stacked upon skyscrapers, piercing the sky with unnatural neon lights and speeding cars; that mix of "technological marvel" and "human folly" the game hopes, and manages, to achieve. Every screenshot of the driving segments could be someone's pretentious desktop background. However when you take off on foot, the style makes the human models look a little silly and out of place with the brooding tone, like Pixar characters in a film noir. Outside this neon-city setting, the diversity is disappointing. Cyperpunk frequently carries themes of income-inequality, and the game has a clear hierarchy correlated to the altitude of buildings, but this is in no way reflected by the visuals. Every island in the sky is virtually indistinguishable from any other. There are 2 areas in the game which are solidly very different, but both appear later on and are used disappointingly sparingly.Cloudpunk's story is good! It's a "stuff happens" type narrative as opposed to a more traditional structure, but it fits a premise like this; it's like you're viewing some of the more exciting snapshots of what it means to deliver packages in Nirvalis. There are some more major plotlines that pop in and out between side stories, and they're also good! Some characters can seem simple or tropey at first, but more often than not they're fleshed out to become, if not round, than at least interesting towards their end. I also really like that intractable characters and important items are highlighted on the map at all times, so you can't really miss any narrative beats so long as you put in the time.  The narration reminds me a lot of VA-11 Hall-A in this aspect (funnily enough another cyperpunk game). Both games feature this snapshot style and the writing is enjoyable and relatable with some poignant points about the nature of being human vs machine. Cloudpunk's improvement is that it's more philosophical moments are told through much more natural language for the most part. The wanna-be philosophy major speech is left to a pretentious wanna-be philosophy professor (as opposed to a 13 year old sex worker).The voice acting is the thing that tips Cloudpunk into the "recommended" range. You don't have the option to click through most of the voice lines in this game, which is usually really frustrating for me, but I didn't mind here because of the great performances! Especially of note are the "android" performances, which strike a really nice in-between of human and not, with strange inflections and staggered deliveries. This makes every new characters' humanity (in the biological sense) a guessing-game, which is thematically relevant... I think.
