_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews but this is a Fantastic game! the story was very in-depth and it really sucked me into the world. The atmosphere was absolutely beautiful and stunning. The only thing i would have to dislike were the camera angles. I had to exclusively play in first person since the two other camera angles were very clunky.one recommendation would be adding weapons and police to hide from since cloudpunk is supposed to be against the law.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is a pixellated sci-fi story about a delivery driver that flies through the skies of the city of Nivalis.The game has great musical composition and interesting and eccentric characters, that all compliment the overall atmosphere of the game, I recommend this game for anyone who wants to follow Rania's story as she makes her way through the city. I found the game to be fun to play, the story to be very interesting, and the dialogue to be witty and well written. For those who like good cyberpunk style sci-fi this may be worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Really love this game, the soundtrack, the neon lights and the city design really amazing. The cons for me were the sudden annoying change of camera when in foot and the lack of change of view while in the vehicle. Leaving that aside, I really enjoyed playing it. As a Blade Runner fan, this is a must!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. The gameplay is somewhere between GTA, Crazy Taxi and pick a Bethesda / Obsidian game. But set in a believable cyberpunk world. Good time-waster and really interesting stories from the people you interact with. The worst part of the game for me is the voice acting. The writing is good but the voice actors are very monotone with little emotion in what they are saying. You can tell they just read what they had on a script with some inflections here and there. It just doesn't seem natural at all. There is a part (this not spoilers) where Camus says he likes a song that goes "BAH BAH BUH BAAAAHHHH!" but he almost whispers it like when the voice actor was saying it they were afraid the person in the cubicle next to them would hear them talking loudly about something not work-related. There are many more parts like that with many other characters. They just don't seem like they even believe in what they are saying. Outside of that everything about the game is a joy to experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game tags itself as "Cyberpunk", "Atmospheric", and "Open World" for a reason. Its not a game that tries to challenge you or place you in difficult situations. Its strictly a voxel game that does everything it can to achieve a vibe and own it. When I first loaded it up I couldn't help but be blown away by the sheer scale and how virtually everything other than the fictional ads, water, and overhead clouds were made in voxel. Absolutely every single asset from the buildings to the people to the vehicles is a voxel asset. And to be totally honest, there are some really well crafted assets throughout this game. To create the illusion of shape, design, and function with cubes is no small feat and I applaud the graphic design. If you've played voxel games in the past you may be familiar with the drawbacks of this medium. What Cloudpunk does quite cleverly is surround you in perpetual rain, capturing the cyberpunk vibe as well as giving them a more manageable draw distance to work within. This in turn gives them the option to create more detailed spaces that don't require re-loading detail levels and giving you a much more fluid experience as you travel. Additionally they master the glow and bloom effects of every light in the city, nailing down the sense that this is a rainy, neon city that never sleeps. This game shows just how much potential can be packed into a voxel style of graphics and most importantly how to do it right.Another aspect of the game that deserves praise is the world building. Every limitation has a plot based reason; be it the limited flight ceiling, traffic system mechanics, fetch quest relevance, or what have you; everything has a reason and purpose. This further rounds out this game's immersion despite the voxel medium being used to create the game's environment.Where this game leaves MUCH to be desired is its story and mechanics. Choices are sparse and EXTREMELY limited. The side quests only tell the writer's own morality tale rather than letting you explore and come to conclusions on your own. Nivalis (the city you work in) is cast as a miserable place where people with nowhere else to turn. What this game needs is balance; where city can be seen as equally positive and negative and allows you to decide whether you like or hate it.  Instead, you exist in the cynical perspective of Rania who's assumptions are always right to some degree or another, and good and bad exist as opposite poles. The "evil" misogyny is over the top and eye-rolling, and the "good" social justice commentary revolves around how being poor gives you the only chance to not be a horrible person. This game struggles with being polar and only appealing to a single political audience. Then there is the game's driving, which is problematic considering driving is the game's core mechanic. It feels fluid when you're going straight or veering slightly left or right. But the moment you need to execute a more controlled maneuver like tight turning, ascending, descending, or parking, things can get ugly. Parking is a struggle at first and binding the "gotta-go-fast" speed boost key with the "gotta-park-now" key was a poor choice in my opinion. Additionally, making it nearly impossible to refuel without smacking the gas station was a poor design choice that could easily have been fixed by either changing the design of the refueling station or changing how much the HOVA wobbles around in tight maneuvers. This wouldn't be as much of an issue if refueling your HOVA weren't such a vital part of the game. I spent more money on repairs than I did on gas and opted to just ride around a smashed up HOVA repairing only when I absolutely NEEDED to rather than getting the repairs I needed.For the price of $19.99, this is game is wonderfully atmospheric, cyberpunk, and open world enough to be worth the price tag. The lighting, soundtrack, and clever use of existing voxel mechanics to achieve its atmosphere are what make this game worth playing. If they charged anymore than this, they would require a better story, better driving mechanics, and a better flushed out open world navigation system.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: You're a delivery driver in a cyberpunk world. The game is basically nothing but driving and dialog. The driving is good, but basic and sometimes clunky (mainly with ascending and descending), and the dialog and story is great. The visuals are beautiful but exploration is rough as everything looks the exact same. Overall a relaxing and fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best stories I've experienced in recent memory. It's been a very long time since I've played a game with this much atmosphere, or experienced any story period with a world that feels so real, and detailed. I cannot recommend this game highly enough, and You would be doing yourself a favor to give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome writing. Awesome level design. Voice acting can be really good but sometimes it's a little flat. Not a lot of gameplay other than driving and walking around collecting stuff. If you can be satisfied just with good dialog than you'll like it. If you can't or if you get easily annoyed by games wasting your time, it's not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is an atmospheric story in the purest Cyberpunk setting.Made by an indie dev studio, the choice of a 3D pixel art style was polarizing for many, but what made it work was the lighting and atmosphere."Cyberpunk 2077" has given us the gorgeous Night City and promised us flying cars, but did not deliver on that promise!But here in Cloudpunk, that is the main selling point !Driving/Flying through the upper levels of Nivalis City feels like you are on Star Wars' planet Coruscant,while the lower levels feel like "Blade Runner" dirty underbelly.The writing is super. We get many stories that tackle Sci-Fi subjects and then are asked to make a choice, which make us deeply contemplate the issues. Immerse yourself.The voice acting is great and greatly supports the story. While the pixel art visuals may get tiring for some, the voice acting keeps it fresh.The only issues I had with the game, was the slow movement outside your car.I get it, they wanted us to, no they demanded from us to take in the city as we travel, to feel what it would be like living in such a sinking ship of a Megapolis. But even with stimulants, the running speed was way too slow..I am glad they made the gameplay more dynamic in the "City of Ghosts" DLC with much more activities for players.And can't wait for the newest "Nivalis (2024)" game that promises to add other genre elements like management,but most importantly will show us the city in daylight and not pixelated anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Let's hire to Cloudpunk they said.Nivalis would be fun, they said.It would be fun, they said.Well, if you would know what happened.Cloudpank, a game developed and published by Ion Lands, is a kind of special one.You slip into the role of a female person. Her name is Rania but Control mostly calls her 14FC. Control is the superviser of Cloudpunk and has a 'grand-father' voice. Rania and you now work for Cloudpunk, your tasks are always the same: Pick up a package from point A and deliver it to another place B. Should be easy, right? Your vehicle is called a 'HOVA', inwhich you have to try sneaking a way through the heavy and chaotic traffic of Nivalis, the complex city where you will have to live now.Inbetween the flights, the assistant gets a new KI - the best friend of Rania - her dog Ramus. He, together with Control, helps Rania to survive the first night and looks for her not getting lost.The deliveries begin with normal packages, you should'nt know the content. Unfortunately, some packages won't be silence, they'll drive you crazy. The deliveries are getting more complex, at the same time the story becomes more deep.The gameplay of the game is simple as possible. When you're in your HOVA, you can drive like a normal car - espacially you can move up and down. While walking through the town, you can find and collect interesting stuff, talk to serious dealers and drink a cup of coffee.The voice called Control leads you through the game, explains what to do and talk something a bit scary.The game's terrain is a sacrified town called Nivalis, which will be collapse by some day. Everything is build with neon, dark buildings with flashing advertisements, puddles on the walksides reflect them. A big steampunk town with its own problems made with a lot of tiny blocks and more heart of the team.Everything in the town has several faces - even the atmosphere and the town itself.At the beginning, I felt lost, chaotic. While playing and getting the town well-known, I felt worried and being in danger. The game cathes your soul, watch out.I am playing the game a second time. There is so much to explore and the team is so glad of all suggestions, they're nonstop working on it to implement new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The game: Not so great. Go from point A to B and listen to/watch dialogue. Repeat. The story is okay, some characters are funny, some are not, there is a great dog (which is also your car), all of it is at a extremely plodding pace.The city: Absolutely INCREDIBLE... cruise through the neo-punk city with a great soundtrack flaming away, and you wont want to leave this voxelly world.It is rare that I would put the graphics above the gameplay, but this is a definite thumbs up for me anyway. It's not just graphics, it's a wonderful vibe, unmatched by anything I've played in a long time. You will spend most of your time wondering why you can't DO more in this lovely place, but heck, I enjoyed it anyway. And the story was nice, the mechanics of it just don't hold even the smallest candle to this world they've created. The fact that most of it is just eye-candy just makes it more eye-boggling.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Simply beautiful to look at, but the gameplay is pretty limited, and game world is marred by relentless mediocre voice-acted dialogue. Its stilted and annoying, and with absolutely no gameplay effect. The experience reminds me of trying to play though a hollow FMV adventure game from the 90's : after an hour or so you come to realize the gameplay is just a wet paper wrapper for a half-a$$ed performance art piece.What a waste.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice Game. The city is beautiful, and the OST would totally fit in the Blade Runner Movie.Of course, the gameplay is a bit limited... but it is very enjoyable to travel across the city.Two weeks after release, the Dev are still upgrading the game nearly every day (Fix and Quality of Life improvements). They are very responsive and dedicated to their release. The main problem with this game is that you will want it to be AAA game... you can feel some technical limitations (not a real openworld city for example) I hope this game will be successful enough to fund a more ambitious sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game!Now after ~6 months after finishing it and settling down my impressions, I still remember it as one of the most amazing games I played in the last year or two.I've fallen in love with the game aesthetics, its retrowave music (though I wasn't a huge fan of the genre before) and immersive cyberpunk atmosphere. The world full of beautiful, funny and cyberpunky-scary stories, crafted with love and devotion. Great voice acting. Believable characters.This game will always have a place in my heart!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at bottom. I used to drive deliveries, so my interest got peaked when I discovered this mostly story game with driving elements. You play as Rania, a new face looking for a fresh start, with her optimistic AI dog companion, Camus. Traveling to the only city of its kind, if not only city on the planet, she gets a job for the “illegal” delivery service known as Cloudpunk. Illegal in quotations only because the company itself is technically legal but the operations of its business aren’t(?). Spend the night with Rania to experience 3rd shift in the mega city of Nivalis and the discover the secrets that it holds![RANT ABOUT MY ISSUES WITH THE GAME]Now onto what I think are the two biggest issues with the game. The writing gets confusing because the whole city needs to be explained and it never gets explained well. Which would be resolved through more of the protagonist asking more questions or having more meaningful interactions with the NPCs of the game, if Rania wasn’t so frustratingly apathetic. Which leads into my next gripe and primary one with the game. Rania (in the base game) is our only perspective to gain information about the city and she just doesn’t care. Only giving her opinion on subjects at inappropriate times like casual conversations with strangers and not the big story choices of the game (which very rarely if at all matter). I think this is done just to contrast the absurdity of the city with her humbler origins, I don’t think it’s ever presented well. I only began thinking about this theory when I kept asking “Why is she written like this?”.[END OF RANT]Angry ramblings aside, I think the rest of the game’s cast are either funny, compelling, or comically obnoxious. I got a couple laughs out of some of the dialogue. Shout outs to my boy Huxley, love that guy. Quick note about the driving, piloting the HOVA (car) is most commonly compared to driving a conventional boat combined with a plane. It takes time to figure out how much you need to steer to clear corners safely and how to weave up, down, and around traffic, but you get used to it and I really enjoyed the driving.The voxel art of the whole city is well done and pleasant to look at and helps to reinforce the vibe of the mega city between the upper and lower sections of it. While navigating through the city you can hear announcements in the background spouting paradoxical dystopian messages to further sell you on the grim state of Nivalis. Music is appropriate too. All very neon, future, ambiance kind of thing. Good filler for the ears.Only reason I’m giving this a negative review is because I bought this for two reasons. Primarily, to experience a new story, and secondly for fun HOVA delivery driving.  It fails on the first part so I can’t really recommend without a sale just to play. TL;DR: Respectable game, good music, some good characters, bad writing, the main character is insufferably indifferent. Try and nab it on any kind of sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are not high def, but the art style and feel of the play space is amazing - sort of a futuristic noir. It was a joy to play through the story and when I realized they had released DLC that I had missed, I didn't hesitate to buy it and reinstall. Can't wait to go through the second half of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Music is a weak place in the game. I was impressed by the first trailer, but when I bought and launched the game I didn't find any similar compositions. It was disappointing.Of course, the game has bright pros. It is an atmosphere of cyberpunk and freedom. I like how the game is designed. It is fascinating and forces you to come back to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: A chill game which examines our relationship to work, community and the cities we live in. I really enjoyed playing it. It's repetitive in nature but in a way that allows you to enjoy it. The Hova (your hovercraft) handles in a satisfyingly floaty way, and it's upgrades produce a noticeable difference in its handling over the course of the game.  Stellar voice cast really sells the world of Novallis. An ancient and decrepit city  where both technology and society stopped developing long ago. Now most people from CEOs to delivery drivers are just trying to make it through another night.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. You're a delivery driver set in a Cyberpunk BladeRunner cityscape. The gorgeous graphics are very immersive and you really feel like you're in this huge city. There seems to be no distant clipping of objects, and there is no transition / separation between walking around and flying in your car/HOVA vehicle - the people and buildings are always there. The dialogue / story is interesting and I was quite hooked into it. The game offers you choices to make and I found myself really thinking through about the implications of each choice, before deciding what to do. I cared. I didn't know how it may affect me later on in the game.Just a few small gripes that I would have hoped were not present in the game at launch date:- A common one, is once the main story arc is completed there is nothing to do. You can collect the  but really there's nothing more to do, which is a shame. I'd like for a 2.0 version where I can keep delivering things and keep the game fresh.- Also some of the dialogues can be quite wordy with no way to skip or speed through the talk. Just stuck listening for minutes while I'm waiting for the NPC to stop talking- Transitioning between districts can be a bit messy as you fly high/low to avoid other traffic yet after going through a tunnel you are placed midheight, at a standstill, and loads of other HOVAs crash into you. Would be nice to keep the speed and same height as you entered- When walking around, switching between First Person and Third Person is always incredibly disorientating with the camera spinning around slowly. Just do a quick half second zoom in / zoom out- The money situation in the game didn't really make sense. You can buy food and drinks but never really needed . Also when speaking with Vendors I didn't know if buying anything would help.  I think a lot of these are purely cosmetic and with the event of a future expansion, this economy can really be put to good use.- The choices you make in the game (main story arc) don't really amount to much. I'd like to have seen more consequences that showed the effort I made in thinking out the consequences and making a decision.I really love the old ancient game SimCopter, and there has never been anything like it since. This seems like a perfect game to incorporate some of its features.Some ideas:- Add more collectables around the city. All sorts of different types of things. Or perhaps visit and log famous locations. Hidden objects in obscure places. - Random Deliveries through the city- Some deliveries are time sensitive- Some deliveries are fragile and require minimal bumps/damage to the HOVA- Extended HOVA upgrade system upgrading parts or even vehicle, which offer various "abilities" or defences- Upgrade your HOVA AI to different voices/personalities?- Perhaps some jobs require different types of HOVA (sport racer, taxi hova, large coach hova, cargo hova, tanker hova, armoured carrier hova, fighter hova - missles/lasers)- One garage could be your home garage where you buy/upgrade/store all your HOVAs- Some random events happen that you can assist with, like accidents (call police), fire (call fire service), perhaps police can sometimes chase you if they scan and see who is onboard.- Some missions may require VIP transport - a large group of people, a single person, a thief/fugitive who needs a quick escape and police may pursue you and try to catch/stop/damage your hova.- Perhaps some missions can be rescue (mass evacuation of a fire scene, or a medical evacuation from a scene), or stopping (helping police) in other runaway criminals in their hova.Those would change the dynamic of the gameplay quite a bit, but just ideas to see where you could possibly take the game after the main story arc is complete. Either way, you'd need to offer quite a few avenues to , which then means you can  on upgrades/expansions/etcLoved playing the game, and look forward to seeing future updates.Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Been happily running and fly/driving around this low poly (large right angled pixels) for nearly 9 hours now and I am loving it.The story line is engaging and sometimes quite funny. The gameplay keeps you occupied while you deliver your goods (mostly unknown goods but sometimes people) and you have to make some tough decisions (the outcome of which is not often apparent straight away).Not sure how much of the storyline is left but I am really enjoying this Blade Runner-ish environment so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a work of art. The city of Nivalis is 1000 times more immersive than a certain other Cyberpunk city from a long delayed and gijjillion budget game. The mood, the vibe and the little details are spot on. I know there will be those thinking how can a low count polygon game be good looking. Well, Cloudpunk is it.  I highly recommend this game to all those who love futuristic city settings and good storytelling. I'm looking to spend more time in Nivalis, so keep the games coming Ion Lands!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: cute game, I like the atmosphere. Get it on sale. Pros - driving around, storylines are nice, the world is pretty cool and immersive. Cons - social justice-y, unnecessary gender stuff, the odd place where you'll fall through the map, pretty linear despite the cons, I'll probably get City of Ghosts on sale at some point. I wish you could go into stores and buildings and stuff and do more with money.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. and i've got to say, I LOVED IT. the music is amazing and the art style is incredibly fitting. driving was a bit difficult to get a grasp of (looks simple but i keep forgetting the right joystick was lift leading to many MANY collisions. too lazy to see if i could re-keybind it.)  the story was very good. it kept me hooked to the point where as soon as i started playing i played it all the way through. There are many decisions to make in this game. I don't know if i made the best choices. But if you buy and play this game through, do me a favor and ask YOURSELF these questions:"Did I make the right choices? Is this the way I wanted everything to go? Did I do it RIGHT."9/10 would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and it was exactly my cup of tea. It is pretty relaxing (except for the very rare timed mission) and it has some story to it. You explore every part of the city and you meet some people are gonna annoy the crap out of you and others that you'll like. This game is definitely one of the best games I have played and it's the perfect game for someone who wants an open-world with a bit of story sprinkled into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a magnificent experience, and a great but flawed game. The world is breath-taking, and it's a joy to just drift around and explore, taking in the sights and sounds. There's so much potential here, and the developers said they are exploring their options and where to go from here, which is definitely something to be excited about.It's a walking/driving simulator with heavy dialogue, all voiced over. The voice-overs are generally OK, sometimes quite good, and in a few cases quite bad. You play a delivery driver in a cyber-punk city where things are falling apart, and end up entangled in some schemes as the story goes along, reaching up to a satisfying if a bit rushed conclusion.From a mechanical perspective, the game suffers from issues with camera and driving controls. The camera angle is fixed in the current build, which makes it harder than necessary to take in the beauty of the city. The devs are working on a fix for that.The driving controls are rather unresponsive, especially the ascenders (going up/down vertically). Your vehicle moves horizontally, and you hover upward/downward like a helicopter with a couple of keys (or the right stick), but it never felt good. The default xbox configuration is confusing since my brain is hardwired to treat the right stick as the camera control, so I spent a lot of time accidentally going up or down and ramming things.Most missions are OK, and are mainly an excuse to explore the city and build the atmosphere through dialogue with the mission NPCs. A few were exceptionally fun (e.g. the whole Huxley arc).The game felt the right length overall, if a bit stretched toward the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The world quickly becomes addictive and convincing. The visuals are beautiful and detailed, the voice acting for the main characters is top tier, the city design is well thought out.  Flying around the city is amazing - you really do get a feel for the vehicle and there is no feeling like swooping high above a large shopping district, looking for parking and then walking along gangways you previously viewed from the air. The atmosphere in this game is perfect
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest star of the game is 100% the city itself. It is dense with atmosphere, the art is fantastic, and flying around sightseeing is the most enjoyable aspect of the game. Full disclosure, I haven't beaten the game yet. Controls make your junker vehicle have heft, and you are giving a pretty good degree of control. The art of the game though is just so gorgeous. Voxelish graphics have been overdone in the indie scene, but not like this. Even using voxel assets, the level of detail and variation in assets in to be applauded. The districts all have their own feel, but still feel like they belong in this world. The developers could make a whole new game using this exact world and assets, just different gameplay, and I would buy it in an instant.I see there has been some negativity about the lack of any really challenging gameplay. I think to enjoy this, you NEED to understand this game, at least so far for me, is a super low stakes affair. No combat, no high skill racing, no tactical decisions to be made. Don't come into the game expecting that. There are some narrative decisions to be made, but the story isn't the reason to play this game. It is all about getting your cyberpunk atmosphere fix.I do have a few qualms to mention though. I am glad the onfoot parts exist, but there really needs to be a zoom in option. Even if it is a button hold and not a toggle. It is super easy to get stuck on something and not even be able to really see it. There are some rough areas for camera movement as well, a few times I have gotten in a loop of camera transitions, constantly moving between to angles. It wasn't a big deal, just had to not move for a moment and let the game catch up. If a developer read this review though, the lack of zoom is my only real complaint (besides, it would be cool to see some of the art up closer).I have read some negatives on the voice acting as well. This is a budget affair folks. I actually think the voice actors themselves can put up good performances, I just think the direction they were given may have been slightly off, probably because it was coming from the developers themselves. I really didn't have a problem with any of the voice overs, it kind of actually fit for me with how unusual the world is in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a truncated version based on the upper character limit for Steam reviews. For the full version, watch the video.It’s hard to define what exactly a story-driven game is. Isn’t every game that tells a story in some sense story-driven? After all, the story determines what you have to do next to progress, it puts what happens into context and, you know, tells you the story the game is intending to tell. In less abstract, more practical terms, story-driven usually means that it’s light on gameplay with more of a focus on dialogue. And I feel Cloudpunk fits this description.You get to experience the city of Nivalis through the eyes of Rania. She comes to Nivalis after the typical dystopian cyberpunk debt police threaten to arrest her to find work and earn some money, so it’s a classic setup where the protagonist serves as the audience surrogate to learn about the world they inhabit. She takes up a job with the eponymous Cloudpunk, a delivery company focused on discretion. They never ask what’s in the package and they deliver everything. The game takes place over her first night on the job as a delivery driver.And that’s mostly what you end up doing in the game, driving around town in your hovercar, picking up packages and sometimes even people and delivering them somewhere. The gameplay interactions are fairly minimal. Flying around the city isn’t that much of a challenge and most of the deliveries aren’t timed or anything. At best it’s the same thing you’re doing in every open world game where you’re taking a commute between triggers that advance the story in some way. It’s not a bad experience, there’s a nice sense of exploration when driving around. And if you treat it like the RPG it wants to be, you’re incentivized to not just head from objective to objective but instead also take the time to have a look around.You can also get out of your hovercar and explore quite a few sections of the city on foot. There are many landing spots with these little self-contained island in the city. Seeing the city from this perspective was great, I loved walking around these little neighborhoods. The mood the game paints with its visual aesthetic certainly manages to create a feeling that made me want to spend time in this place, at least after I turned off the rather excessive bloom.Unfortunately, that’s also the only thing that did. For one, even though I like the game’s aesthetic, the voxel graphics mean that there’s not a lot of detail to be found. It’s all just general hints at what a cyberpunk city is supposed to be. And the non-trivial amount of copypasted content means that a lot of the time your surroundings don’t seem to have that strong of a visual theme that would make them contrast with each other. I never managed to generate a strong mental map of the city. The game suffers from the same problem a lot of open world games are afflicted with and that’s that the minimap is just too damn convenient and pretty much a necessity to ever take your eyes from it. As such, I was never really soaking in my surroundings while doing missions, I was looking at my objective markers all the time. So the game ultimately doesn’t manage to make use of a lot of environmental storytelling. This lack of environmental storytelling also extends to the on-foot portion as well. The spaces you can walk around in are littered with the typical markers found in most other open world games. And what’s there to find seems half-hearted at best. Now what I will say is that I generally liked the little interactions with the characters you can talk to. Quite a few of them serve as fairly obvious parables for real-life topics and this is where the writing shines the most. During your exploration of the city, you can also find a bunch of items, though most of those serve no purpose whatsoever. There are a few quests surrounding items you can find and bring to specific NPCs, like the vintage game collector or the lengthy collectathon where you have to scour the city for punch cards to restore an android’s memories. I’ll be honest here, I hate these collectathon missions. In general I tend to avoid them like the plague, because they’re patently busywork intended to drag out the runtime of your game. While I personally didn’t much care for the gameplay, the writing is generally mostly enjoyable. It does have a tendency to drag on sometimes by outstaying its welcome during certain conversations, but it also has quite humanizing touches for some of the characters you get to talk to. The one exception here and probably the worst one this could’ve happened to though is our protagonist Rania. Some of her lines and behavior are almost schizophrenic with how contradictory they are and quite a few turns of the narrative made me wish for a possibility to just reach through the screen and slap her i.e., for this to be more of an RPG where I get to play a character the way I intend to.For a game centered around an illicit delivery company, you also seem to never get into any trouble with the debt collectors Rania is ostensibly trying to hide from, or the ever-present private police forces, whose only method of investigation seems to be directly asking suspects if they work for Cloudpunk and taking said suspects at their word with no further inquiry. I think the game stumbles a bit with this aspect, where the horrible state of the world is more communicated by characters telling us about their suffering instead of the player experiencing the hardships themselves, i.e., telling instead of showing.One feature a lot of story-driven games have is that they like to give players choices to make. And Cloudpunk too has a few missions that present you with a choice, such as disposing of certain packages or delivering them to their intended destination or bringing certain characters to one place or another that somehow informs their later fate. Most of these choices don’t really seem to have that much of a consequence after you made them. Even the big finale of the game hands you a choice to make that doesn’t seem to change much about the status quo. And the fact that they don’t seems to be deliberate. I can’t fathom a story-focused game presenting you with these choices and actively downplaying any significance they might have could happen by accident. And I get the impetus behind this. After all, why would a lowly down on their luck delivery driver be in a position to change the world? That would be entirely antithetical to the theme that this is a cyberpunk dystopia shaped by millennia of unresolved problems. Now I reiterate, the game is pretty to look at and in general has an absorbing atmosphere and I like a lot of the little narrative touches. But unfortunately, the barebones and not particularly challenging gameplay coupled with the generally unlikable protagonist doesn’t fill me with confidence in recommending the game. To me, Cloudpunk represents a lot of unfulfilled potential. The gameplay could’ve used a shot of adrenaline by implementing an actual challenge. There are a few later missions where you’re given a generous timer that you have to actively try to fail, but that’s about it. And on foot there’s nothing to do but run from A to B, turning the whole game into a walking simulator. It’s a game that’s to be liked more in terms of what it’s gesturing towards with its narrative ambitions rather than what its interactivity has to offer. And that’s a shame, because like I said, I enjoyed the vignettes that gave me glimpses into a variety of different lives, even though admittedly, the narrative is clearly written with an intended message and a corresponding bias. But I’m not sure if that can outweigh the downside of generally lackluster back and forth on foot or in your hovercar.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: So I love this game.  I grew up with blade runner and 5th element as some of my favorite movies.  The music is perfect, the atmosphere is perfect.  There is a real joy just flying around delivering packages.  There are a few basic upgrades for your car, No shooting, no building.  You have really fun, smooth flying mechanics, an extremely interesting world lore and incredible atmosphere.The walking parts are great for pacing of the game and to give you that ground perspective.  They are about 1/4 as fun as flying but its still ok.  You wont have access to an entire megacity, you are limited with a floor and ceiling for each section of the map.  Really though, I had so much fun experiencing this world that the limitations of the game are pretty easily overlooked.  Many of its limitations or small shortcomings are kind of charming.  The voxel graphics work flawlessly with a megacity full of 90 degree angles.  It's kind of a beautiful idea.  The voice acting may take some getting used to but its good overall.  The dialogue is always pretty upbeat.  Even when things are going bad you have Rania who wants to do the right thing.  It was honestly the best game to smoke up  with and enjoy a few quarantined afternoons.  You don't have to kill anyone, you barely have to race a clock. Enjoy the atmosphere and the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: For a relatively small production, it is praiseworthy. While it wasn't to be expected that such a small team could fill this huge world, one will still feel a certain lack of content.However the biggest problem lies in the primitive moral choices the game offers. They feel forced and unnatural - with little if any nuance.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The game loop is literally just get package, drive to location, give package, wait for dialogue to end and repeat. The main issue I have with this game is that its hyped up to be a very atmospheric game but it just feels so dead, like you go from point A to point B where the appeal should be that you get immersed into this cyberpunk-esque world filled with life but the NPC's feel like NPC's, and the first person view doesn't allow you to look around in the cockpit. Don't buy this game if you wanted it for its immersive aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk cuts right to the very heart of Cyberpunk, not just in aesthetic but in knowing what it means to be cyber*punk*. The gameplay isn't particularly involved; mostly just drive from A to B with the odd decision thrown in. But it doesn't try to be much more than it is, and instead focuses on giving a concise, immersive and moody experience. The main characters are highly likeable (Rania takes no nonsense), with wonderful and distinct side characters and plots thrown into the mix. The main story is moving - if somewhat shallow at times.It's a driving simulator with flying cars in a cyberpunk setting. What's not to love?
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I held off for a while but I bit the bullet when they added the fpv to the driving. It's got plenty of dialogue and some quirky/funny conversations (tick tock tick tock). Great synthy ambient chill choonz. The clouds though, are something else, especially after pulling a lung full. Definitely the guys that made this game have put their heart into it, and I will look forward to seeing what else they put into it. Good value game for whats on offer. Yes, you're delivering packages mainly, but they've done it in a way that is entertaining with some great ear and eye candy to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really beautiful and immersive game. Some reviews will say that this is a ~walking simulator with no meaningful gameplay~, and well.. that is actually true. But it's a very atmospheric and engaging walking simulator. The artwork is excellent, the music is great, plot and voice acting are pretty decent but not stellar. It might not be everyone's piece of cake, but people who enjoy this kind of stuff will really like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting plot, is graphically beautiful and has an immersive soundtrack. There are also a decent amount of places to visit on the map. The dialogue can be a little long at times, as I sometimes got to the destination before the dialogue had finished. However, this doesn't detract from the gameplay too much, as it provides you with important background information, clues and a sense of the atmosphere within city.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk is an adenture game, very similar to point-and-click genre, but in 3D and with flying car. It has fantastic atmosphere, pretty voxel graphics and excellent music. The main story line is interesting, but not very original. Side quests are very simple, some of them require the player to make a decision that will have consequences later on. All decisions, however, are pretty meaningless and have very low impact. Content-wise, Cloudpunk is quite small. Most of the time is spent on flying and running, especially if you want to collect all pickups, talk to every NPC and complete all side missions. Voice acting is mostly great, but some actors are on the "passable" side. For an indie game it's still very good.The worst thing is the camera while on foot. It follows a predefined path and some angles could be better. In couple of places, it snaps 180 degrees in an instant, which is very disorienting and makes controlling the character difficult. Also, during transisions, it seems like the controls are locked and that can be very annoying when your character runs into a wall and gets obscured by something. There are other, minor problems, but devs are patching them.Cloudpunk is very fun and relaxing. A must have for any Cyberpunk fan who loved Blade Runner. Just don't expect a grand game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell a lot of love went into creating this game. The flying is truly so much fun, it takes me back to the FFVIII Ragnarok.This is a moody look at a very possible, very wet, not-so-distant future. It's your first night in a new city, with new rules, lingo, customs and trends. You as the player are experiencing the same learning curve your main character, Rania, is, and this manifests in every way, as you become more familiar with traversing the gorgeous Nivalis skyscrapers, you also begin to gain mastery over your driving, becoming better at your job just as you would in real life. It's a really well-crafted story and you get to know the city like you live there by the time you're through.If you've ever wanted to relax by flying a car through a futuristic mixture of New York City, London and Tokyo, delivering elicit materials from client to client, and making decisions that impact the whole of the human race, grab this.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: In cloudpunk you drive around delivering stuff while exploring an interesting city with just as interesting characters and dialog.Great atmosphere, good music and graphics.Didn't have any boring moments during playthrough so very recommended.I only wish the mouse could be of more use when controlling the vehicle.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Captivating storyline, fun and memorable main characters, interesting NPC interactions, amazing environments, and a banging soundtrack. Overall fun.The gameplay is fun to me, but I could see how somebody who doesn't care for storyline at all could get bored.My recommendation is that if you enjoy books/audiobooks and/or pretty sights, you'll enjoy Cloudpunk. It's almost like a book with great voice actors, beautiful environments, and mildly entertaining gameplay.The soundtrack alone is worth a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Bladerunner and Cyberpunk, this is a must play.  I'm only a couple hours in, but they absolutely nailed the atmosphere.  Do yourself a favor, and play it at night, turn up the sound and enjoy the world they built for you.  There is a lot more here than just delivering packages, but I wouldn't want to ruin it for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.  If you've ever wanted to play the mood that Blade Runner has, this is a way to do it.  Story line is good, and engaging, graphics are a unique blend of 3D and 8-bit for a really cool effect that I've not seen before.  Voice actors are pretty good, and the plot line is fun.  Over all one of my favorites this year.  It's well worth the 8 hour play-through it will take.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I basically bought the game to just drive around a bit on my laptop. I didn't know there would ne a complete story in this game so I was pleasantly surprised! The atmosphere of this game is simplistic but very cyberpunk at the same time together with the soundtrack. If you like driving around for fun and go from A to B to unlock a bit more of an interesting story then this is your thing!Only critisisimn I would have is that the game didn't really run well on my laptop. The graphics look simplistic but it's still heavy for some older GPU's. Also ir feels like this game has more potential then it's using. For example you can find crafting items but the only thing you can do with it is selling them. There are also a lot of NPC's where you can talk with but they only give an achievement but no assignment. Or the tons of foodstalls where you can buy food that you don't really need. And the last example is that buying another car or upgrading the car is there. But the things you can buy are very limited. Also I would have liked some freeroaming to where you could deliver packages that are outside the story mode and upgrade. But this all is more of a wishlist.In general I really liked playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy: If you are looking for complex gameplay.Buy: If all you ever wanted is to fly and walk through a city as depicted in the Blade Runner movies while listening to 80s inspired synth music.Concerning the gameplay:You fly from A to B, collect items, talk to people, upgrade your vehicle etc.But as i mentioned before the city is absolutely gorgeous!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The game is undeniably well crafted to the dystopian blade-runner-esque style, however apart from it's style, Cloudpunk doesn't really have much else to offer. A gorgeous world that perhaps would've worked in a shorter lengthed delivery.Story - The main story itself is fairly slow and feels like it's always just about to pick up and start getting interesting but never quite gets there. The game uses the odd decision here and there to pad out it's story with more depth, "do I deliver this package that I suspect is a bomb, or do I throw it down the garbage disposal" kinds of decisions, which would've been interesting if they were in any way integrated into the games story or carried any kinds of consequences, spoiler: . By the end of the night, you are forced to make a final decision that feels rushed upon you seeing as the character has about as much connection with the city as the player does the games world. Again the final decision has seemingly little effect on the world around you.Character Design - Much of the gameplay other than driving from cutscene to cutscene is centred around the player interactions with the weird and unique characters that you come across during your deliveries on Nivalis. This is why the character design in this game was so disappointing to me. The character models in the game were underwhelming at best, and looked like they were play-testing models that were accidentally left in the final cut of the game, they're extremely out of place considering the games polish in terms of its world design. The NPCs are given unique marks and features that are visible in their character portrait, but are completely absent from their models that look nothing like them. This means that you spend most of the game listening to these characters talk while you're staring at an unrecognisable and unresponsive face (still better than the good 40 minutes you'll spend sitting still in your car waiting for dialogues to finish).In short, the game had promise in its setup and setting, but under-delivered in its narrative depth and delivery, as well as its character design. I'd give it a 'meh' if I could, miss this unless you have a burning desire to see the world for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: this game is good , its not perfect but its good . To start if your looking for some game with combat in some cyber punk feeling city this isn't the game for you and dont expect it to be its a simple game where you deliver packages and in your car around beautiful pixel city. all i say is dont but it tho there are flaws like the car being quite unresponsive and lots of the jobs becoming tedious time wasters to increase the game length , the city isnt all beautiful either lots if it is black and grey walls hidden behind the neon signs so it feels incomplete and rough around the edges. in conclusion i believe the game is good if you can get it on sale but not for full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudpunk absolutely nails the aesthetic of a dystopian cyberpunk future, from the vast and varied city full of interesting inhabitants to the excellent soundtrack and voxel visual style.  It sucks you in, even with such a simple premise.Essentially, you are a delivery drive who takes jobs dispatched to you via a central dispatcher called Control, who must simply complete the given tasks.  However, it has a rich story that grows deeper as you play, and with so many people to interact with and things to do (as well as some true choices to make) the tasks do not feel stale.  You can upgrade and maintain your HOVA (vehicle) with new visuals and handling, as well as purchase items for your apartment, and some aesthetic choices on your character itself.I've put about 5 hours into the game at this point, and I don't think I'm close to the end.  I am a pretty casual player and pick it up for a delivery or two every few days, but I am always looking forward to the next bit of story advancement.  If the aesthetic appeals to you, you should absolutely pick it up just to drive around through all the beautifully rendered districts of the city.  And if you want more than that, Cloudpunk seems to have a good bit to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game. It's a story-driven walking simulator where you go from character to character delivering parcels around Navalis. I can't say much about the story without spoiling anything but, I found the world deeply engrossing. And found the story pretty damn great with very little fat. It did take an hour or two to get into it but it was well worth it. Any fat that is there, is just the game introducing you to more characters to give you a feel for the city of Navalis. For what it's worth, this is 10/10. I will be buying the DLC now that it is on sale and will purchase Navalis when it comes out. Just a side note: I could have done this game in perhaps half the time but ended up taking my time, not rushing from mission to mission. I even spent time just looking around the city and also collected as much as I could.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: all you do is fly around and deliver packages or passengers + explore some locations by foot to get those packages. from a to b, from b to c, its simple, dont expect anything else. if you are fine with this, you get an amazing atmosphere driving through a large city while listening to the dialogue like an audio book. dont expect too much, you are a delivery driver, most dialogues are mundane, its not action thrilled with twist after twist, you are just another driver doing its job.that being said, if you want a relaxing game with an awesome atmosphere, the game is freaking amazing and i loved every second of it. you fly around in a blade-runner-esque city and what more do you want?a true gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like kinda RTX-Minecraft in Adventure Mode. The reflections are beautiful, the only unrealistic thing is the rain, it just feels like a cheap layer stuck on the camera when beeing on first cam. The dialogues are quite average to funny. Why is my review negative?Well my internet once went down and I tried to launch the game and it only said,"This game can't be launchned in offline mode" or something like that.WHY?Why does a Singleplayer require internet connection to run?!What are the benefits?Even Denuvo isn't as worse as that!Edit: It turned out that this game uses some costum DRM, whichs locks you out after few days.It may also lock you out if you start your PC while having no internet.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: It's raining...I'm glad that I picked up this game again after a couple of years. The (new?) first-person-view adds to the immersion and it did it for me this time! The atmosphere is wonderful in this dystopic city and the dark story unfolds nicely between the deliveries and little side quests.It's raining...
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game when you can get it on sale. The game features amazing immersive cyberpunk graphics in the voxel style and a great engaging story that suffers from a lack of focus. The game leaves you wanting to know more of the world, for example the vents or the hollows. I found that there was many opportunities in the story where they could have gone into a lot more detail about the locations that are "outside" Nirvalis or they could have added some side quests for after the game to further explore the lore of the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. Package deliveries wandering, in a cyberpunk city, with great stories, great voice acting (Camus, Huxley, ...), great music.It took me around 17 hours to finish it, and now, I'm just waiting for more (DLCs and expansions ? :))One comment though : camera angles & controls are pretty weird sometimes
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I picked it up because of how it looked and I like the delivery aspect. I was however happily surprised with how much story and world building this game put in :), the devs really cared to nail the cyberpunk theme with interesting npc and funny jokes.I did not finish the game yet, so I do not know how long the game will be but so far I am very satisfied with this simple yet very well polished game. If you like exploring, soaking up a games atmosfeer, Don't mind that there is no action or combat and like interacting with npc. I think you might enjoy this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I'll describe this game in terms of its best two qualities: Atmosphere and storytelling.The world of Cloudpunk is not only beautiful but does an amazing job of feeling real. Everything from the sound of the never-ending rain and its droplets on the windshield of your HOVA to the PSA announcements that fit in with a city that no longer cares and yet is tongue and cheek make the setting seem very engaging.Now for story telling. Admittedly the gameplay focuses on fetch quests and doesn't really deviate from it. However, each little quest and mission involves fun characters that are well voiced and well written. You know that whenever you meet a new character it will be interesting. The stories presented are also well done in terms of dilemma and choice. Not choice in terms of gameplay mechanics, but in terms of morality. You will constantly get to make a choice, often not between good and evil but between good and good or evil and evil.If you're looking for a game that is really a great experience and doesn't require high energy, Cloudpunk is a great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cozy but not boring. I played through the main game (I still need to try the DLC) the week my dog died, and it lifted my spirits perfectly. A great pick in general, but especially if you tire of the dark and misanthropic aspects most sci-fi games have (even though I do love me some techno-bodyhorror-corpo nightmares). An abundance of immersive features are a delightful treat, although I do wish the rain wasn't a weird screen filter as it can break my immersion when playing in first person. Grab it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric visual novel with excellent graphics and a good soundtrack, which takes place in an open world AI dominated city of the future. The game takes place over the course of the first night for a new driver (the protagonist) working for Cloudpunk, a shady delivery company. In between the driving and delivering there are plenty of side stories to follow up with various quirky lego-like characters that are encountered, each with their own strange history. There is no combat and few puzzles, other than occasionally having to find a way to travel between different levels of the city when on foot. The choices to be made involve interesting moral issues, but don't seem to affect the main plot. My main criticism is that there is no manual save, which for me makes the game less re-playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Did I buy this to compensate for Cyberpunk 2077? Yes. Was I diappointed? Yes. Don't get me wrong, there's nothing wrong with the game itself per se. It's nice to look at. The soundtrack is okayish. But it just lacked emotions, interesting characters & a good story for me. You play as a young woman working in a delievery service in a cyberpunkish world above the clouds. The pixellook is cute, even though the people walking on the streets look a bit creepy if you get close to them. It is always raining and nobody has an umbrella. There is little to see after a few delieveries because the whole world/city seems to look the same.Actually, I'd rather sell this as an parking simulator than a atmospheric sci-fi game, because I was constantly looking for places to park my car and THEN had to navigate through an enervating city with a confusing map. Flying with the car is okay, but also not a very great feeling because I am generally bad at driving so this applies to flying too, of course. My car was broken 24/7. The protagonist.. well, voice acting is bad here, her personality pretty annoying, too. "Don't ask what's in the package?" ALWAYS asks whats in the package. Really, girl? You don't have choices like in an rpg so I way always stuck with being angry at her. The dialogues are just not very well written and the courier services repeat themselves very quickly and are the same. I would have preferred to just do my job, but the protagonist thought otherwise.I wouldn't recommend it, There are better courier games on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic of this game is nice, and it's very impressive that it has full voice acting, but at the end of the day it just isn't engaging. Never-ending fetch quests combined with a narrative that doesn't reflect the gameplay in any meaningful way. Your character constantly talks about money being tight, but you never have to make any difficult decisions surrounding that - you can afford nearly everything after 30 minutes of play.  The graphics also get terrible the closer you look at them - the voxel aesthetic looks great from a distance, but on NPCs it looks goofy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: A well told, patient, and confident story about a cyberpunk noir dystopia in which youre a humble delivery driver. A linear story but freedom to roam around, with various quest decisions that affect characters lives as you go on.This should be obvious, and what I say next is also obvious from the games images, but I feel it cant be sold enough - The pixel art, atmosphere, and aesthetic are GORGEOUS. It positively radiates cyberpunk appeal in the best of ways for fans of the genre, perhaps the best decriptor that comes to mind is how Ridley Scott spoke about his visionary goal for Blade Runner, in that he "Wanted the future to feel old". This its that nail on the head.To get the most of the aesthetic, you can use F3 to toggle the HUD on and off and pressing V in your HOVA will switch to first person mode, which comes with a shift in dynamic sounds and how the HUD works to incorporate the HOVA systems, which is a wonderful little touch.Has been a delight to play through. My small irks being just that, small - *Controls in first person for the HOVA can be... fiddly. This was with me on keyboard though, and we all know keyboards and vehicle driving often dont marry well.*The main characters personal beliefs at one particular point struck me as hypocritcal regarding a choice you get presented, BUT thats entirely subjective. So take it of leave it.All in all, mucho recommend!Jolly good show Devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: April game review;So like many I can't wait for Cyberpunk 2077 to come, but in the mean time i've started playing Cloudpunk. Cloudpunk is set in a neon-noir story in a rain-drenched cyberpunk metropolis. It’s your first night on the job working for the Cloudpunk delivery service. Two rules: Don’t miss a delivery and don’t ask what’s in the package. This vivid, intricate metropolis is genuinely stunning to look at. It's a bustling sprawl of neon signs, roaming spotlights, colossal billboards, and hover cars scurrying back and forth between monolithic skyscrapers. Lower your car to street level and you'll see pedestrians milling around, noodle stands, and seedy nightclubs. In the air, advertising blimps, trains streaking along suspended rails, and the glow of thousands of apartment windows. The sheer density of the place is remarkable. It ticks off every cyberpunk aesthetic cliche, but it does it with style. So if your wanting to past some time before Cyberpunk definitely consider picking this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: Another interactive story trying to disguise itself as a game. If a Blade Runner, Crazy Taxi, GTA and Mindcraft mashup sounds good to you, sorry to say this game is not that. While it takes heavy influence from the rain soaked future-punk dystopia tropes, fusing it with the aesthetics of voxel art, the Devs forgot the videogame in the process. Literally fetch quest after fetch quest with no actual challenge. Tiresome/boring gameplay after an hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I havent completed this game yet but I'm loving it, it looks and sounds stunning, the models are not what you'd think they'd look like, imagine Minecraft and Cyberpunk were fused together to make a flying/driving game, this is it.This game isn't like the vast majority of other games, its one of those rare gems that you see once or twice every few years that truly breaks the mould in games.Take it with a pinch of salt the story telling, just play the game and imagine your playing in the Blade Runner world.Have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game! If you like narrative driven games and the cyberpunk aesthetics, I'm sure you will do! Spoiler free tips for more fluent gameplay:- Try both the first and the third person views. For walking I preferred the first person but for driving I used both. - I recommend playing the in short intervals, like 30-60 minutes per day, this way it doesn't get repetitive or boring. Try to also play it in like two weeks, this way you don't loose the narrative. - I recommend collecting loot (the blue square thingies on the map) ONLY if they're on your way. You only need a few loot items for fixing elevators and such. Also no reason to collect them for money, you'll get enough dough from the missions and discovering new areas. - I recommend collecting the items (the white square thingies on the map) since they're all quest related. - Once you find water, sodas, energy drinks or energy bars that are cheap (under 10$), buy like 40 of them. They give you a temporary walking speed bonus. Use them every time you walk longer distances around the areas to collect the items more quickly. - If you like the game, buy the DLC. It's kinda better than the original game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: I was pulled into this game by a the graphics and music, but I was really let down by the gameplay and the story. Nothing ever felt consequential, and the delivery quests got really old. I had to stop because of the writing; I am a big fan of social commentary, but this was so on the nose that it quickly became unbearable and very predictable to the point that I just had to tune out. I don't have a huge issue with the voice acting, but again the writing was just so over the top that I felt like I was just reading twitter. If you just want to cruise around in a cool cyberpunk world and listen to good music, I absolutely recommend this game and you will not be disappointed. But if you're looking for something deeper in commentary or gameplay, you're better off looking somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as i saw this game I knew I wanted to play it!So many things about this game I love, such a vast and busy open world that feels like it goes on forever, great use of colour and sound. The environment draws you in so much, the art style is has a a very charming retro feel to it yet so much detail.When it comes to the sound, I played with headphones and the soundscape makes you feel so immersed in the world.The voice acting is superb with many different accents making it feel like people and cultures from all over have come to live in this city and really brings the great character writing to life.There is much humour to be found in this game, be it either via the people you talk to, the announcements you hear in the background or even the things you read, to break up the many little stories you unveil as you go around delivering packages.I found the 3 hours I've played so far flew by with so much of this world yet discovered, I feel i have barely scratched the surface and looking forward to playing more of Cloudpunk.

_childDocuments_.review: An eerie future is depicted, the sounds and visuals give you an immersive experience. You work a shift as Rania on the Cloudpunk team and although you speak to many people on the way, you still feel very much alone in the world at first. The blocky closed-in railings prevent you from taking a leap to your death, but will you want to, or does the controlled existence of the future feel comforting in the end.It is a mostly relaxing game with simple mechanics. i really enjoyed exploring and pondering the question of how we ended up in this dark cyberpunk future. I was left wanting more...
_childDocuments_.name: Cloudpunk

_childDocuments_.review: The driving took me a little bit to get used to. I expected something much faster. Instead, the car is pretty slow and the turning radius is wide if you don't slow down. You end up veering into oncoming traffic which can be frustrating when you're trying to go fast and not crash. If you crash too much you will need to repair the car. But I got used it and if you are going slower your turn is so much tighter. I ended up enjoying the driving and once you have a feeling for it you can get around the city quickly.Now, you will be getting out of the car a lot. So much of your job is to chat with someone about the package. That means trying to find the closest parking spot, setting it down, then running to the spot. Cloudpunk doesn't make it easy because most of the time the meeting place is not close to the parking. The locked camera can get a little weird too because it moves a lot.Anyway, the city is the best part of Cloudpunk. It looks fantastic from all directions and I can tell a ton of work went into laying everything out. There's always something interesting to see. Especially when you're running around on the ground, it's probably why the developers chose to lock the camera. The angles they set provide some beautiful shots. The city feels alive with all the traffic and lots of random people walking around.Overall, Cloudpunk is a well-made game with a beautiful city. If the idea of completing jobs for a delivery service sounds interesting then you should strongly consider it. I wish the writing was more to my preference and that I could look past some of that voice acting. For the more visual, a video review,

_childDocuments_.review: Making a game thats more focused on story than gameplay is fine (I've enjoyed walking sims like Firewatch and Edith Finch) but you're kind of riding on that story being compelling. The main flaw in this is that  the dialogue is overwritten, every exchange feels like it goes on longer than it needed to, there have been some interesting plot points dealing with the cyberpunk themes of class inequality, transhumanism, ecology etc but unfortunately its viewed through the lens of an unlikeable, bland, protagonist who interacts mostly with 2 dimensional rich ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ so she can be judgy about it. She also has a pet dog and Jesus Christ who thought it was a good idea to have a dog character who speaks (as in a human imitating what presumably a dog would speak like) for most of the game!? Its maybe cute for 5 minutes then its just annoying. The MC also is either a bad actress or was given bad direction cause I really dislike her performance (admittedly it might also be due to her annoying generic american accent). The other main character control however does a quite endearing performance, it gives a lot of character with not that much exposition. Anyways the gameplay is bad and the story is bad so what's left? Well the artsyle is cool, mostly. Its voxels so you kinda love or you hate it really. The character models look quite Lego-y but the environments are quite well realized if slightly derivative of other Cyberpunk works. The Music is ok I guess

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly pretty good. Expected a taxi driver in flying cars/cyberpunk style of game and actually got a pretty competent story with it. A lot more than just flying around making deliveries. Controls are good although sometimes the camera can be a bit annoying, mostly when dropping altitude as the car seems to bounce upward a little. Characters are introduced nicely and sometimes during dialogue sequences things will be subtly let slip about their true intentions or who they really are, and often in a way that makes you question if you are understanding them correctly. Don't think I was ever able to work any character out until at least half way through their storyline.There's also a lot of hinting at social commentary but again more in a 'it's a cyberpunk game, don't read too much into it' theme.There's about 10-15 hours of gameplay here in the main story so for the asking price can definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:DrThe story, and conversations with side characters are usually fantastic, with only a few exceptions. It's just unfortunate, that the art becomes boring after a time, and that the gameplay, from the get go, lacks much interest. Making the game feel like a slog to get through.Wait for it to go on sale for 5$, AND just watch a playthrough or film edit on YouTube.  The artistic expression, and the story, deserve your money- the lack of depth in that art, and the painfully boring gameplay, do not.--Long Review--The art style is interesting as a small art display, something you would spend 2$ on, just to do a bit of exploring before you become bored. Unfortunately, as a full game, it quickly loses it's charm, before becoming scarcely bearable. When you spend 10-20 minutes on foot to pick up a single item, you want more fidelity in the game, than it's voxels can offer.The 3d characters are bland & boring, frequently using models that don't match their 2d portraits at all. Again, they also lack any fidelity, given to the simple texture work (read as solid colors), and lack of physical polygons(read as low #s of voxels) that form them. This said- their 2d portraits are usually fairly beautiful, given that they are not voxel/pixel art, and are well rendered. You frequently see interesting cyberpunk characters, or androids. Some side quest characters appear to even have their own renders done for them.The gameplay is atrocious with a Keyboard, and for me, a gamepad refused to work (Thank you Metal desk, messing up BluTooth signals!). This said, even had a gamepad worked, the game design while on foot is painfully boring. Literally minutes of walking, in a straight line, to pick up a single item, then walk all the way back to your vehicle. This would have been acceptable had the environments art been more engaging, had there been more small pickups to distract one from the feeling of emptiness, or had the design involved extremely simple jumping puzzles. Even having to avoid simple obstacles without jumping, might have added some interest, particularly if you had control over your camera while on foot. The Story, is GOOD! While the main character comes across as a bit agro(hostile) for my tastes, and leaves me worried she will rub someone the wrong way, and end up in hot water- when it comes to choices in the game, you actually get to choose. You frequently run into side characters, with small stories, and missions- while the gameplay of these missions is the same drag, it's interesting in this dialog, to see the world fleshed out. These side quests also give you a better feel of the magnitude of the main story, and how you may or may not fit into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it became pretty unbearable by the end.The first two hours are amazing. You are flying through a rainy cyberpunk city, making deliveries, meeting people, and collecting random things. But then... that's about it. There is nothing more to it to make you want to complete the game. The ending was exciting, but it (1) felt like only part one of the story and (2) the dialogues are still awful.The gameplay pretty much ends with the driving/flying. You can get used to the controls, I recommend upgrading your car as soon as possible, so that you can fly above the highways - this allows you to appreciate the city. Moreover, the city has multiple districts, but they all feel the same. The dialogues also fell the same! Because there is nothing to them, just random facts about random characters you meet.I noticed a new game about Nivalis is going to be released in 2024. It looks promising. I hope the developers are going to learn from their mistakes and create somethings special. The setting is there, everything else is missing.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the cyberpunk artstyle and would like to just walk/fly around a world in that very style, this is your game.The story is servicable, some characters can be a bit annoying, but the atmosphere it pretty decent. Its not the kinda game you are gonne play for a long time, but it will absolutely be good for a few hours of sight seeing.I would like to see them add support for Workshop content in the game. While visually stunning, the world isn't particularly deep. Eating food at street vendors doesn't have any animation beyond a "what do you want?" and "thank you" voiceline. You might walk past a small night club, but cant enter since its just a fassade playing music. I'd love it if the community was able to add interiors you can enter and things like that.Id also like to see a bit more variety in NPC behaviour. Appart from the few ones that have some dialog, they all just walk along from one point to another. Its totally fine if you are just following along for your mission, but when you stop to take in the world around you, its kinda sad not to see anyone else do the same :/All that being said, it was certainly worth the 6-7€ I payed for it.
