_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Fix the gun controls!  This game is a complete disappointment.This game has a lot of potential but it falls on its face every time it takes a step.  I have enjoyed the Sniper Elite series and looked forward to this game being fun.  I had read reviews that the game was difficult and didn't control well.  I chalked that up to the reviewers having not spent much time in other VR games.  There are times when I will read about a game and realize that the review has spent all of two hours in VR and are not accustomed to how the games handle.This game handles bad, really bad.  It feels like the people making the game had only seen Half Life Alyx.  The Devs idiotically tried to implement a "Gravity Glove" style pickup mechanic which I bet they thought was "cool" and "added something to the game play".  What would have helped is making it so the player could actually pick up something in the game.  The pickup mechanic just doesn't work well and half the time I end up trying to pick up something on the floor and then I have a grenade in my hand that the game thought I was trying to pick up.  What works in games is letting players simply bend down a pick something up with a grip button on the controller.  It's simple and lets the players enjoy the game and not get frustrated at it.The game is amazingly strict about the play boundaries.  You would think I mean the guardian system but no.  The game freaks the ♥♥♥♥ out every time you get too close to a wall or crate.  You get too close, the game goes black in the headset and says return to the play area.  The odd thing is, I'm in my play area just trying to crouch behind a crate for cover but no the game says I'm not playing it correctly and has to punish the player for it.  It was really annoying when I was not moving at all but the game kept telling me I was not in the play space.  Or when your trying to get to cover but your shoulder clips though an invisible wall and now you can't see anything.  If your going to do this to your players, allow an option for that to be removed, it breaks immersion and makes the game just about unplayable.  The menu is one of the dumbest things I've seen in a VR game.  The main menu comes in the form of a notebook or journal that's grafted to your left hand.  Someone in a conference room must have been like, "You know what's overdone?  Simple, easy to read, and concise menus.  We need to think outside the box and give our users something new and amazingly dumb to use to interact with the game."  Thank little baby Jesus, yes the christmas one, that the only time you have to use that crappy menu is only on the main screen and you can hit pause to use a real menu.What this game needs is to improve its crap controls.  Hey Rebellion, have someone show you a real VR game like Onward or Pavlov and just copy how those guns handle.  Rebellion, also you need to sit down and think about realism vs play-ability.  What is in the game is neither and the game suffers greatly for that.  Onward and Pavlov have bolt action sniper rifles that don't drift out of your hands for no reason.  Too many times I've grabbed the rifle off my shoulder in game and it's sideways in my hand.  This is just so surprising that a well known PC game's entry into VR is done so poorly.  It's so disappointing to find the core of the game doesn't work.

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to recommend for now because there are a few issues with the game that ruin the experience. The first thing I noticed was that my vr hands were about four centimetres higher than my actual hands in real life (im using a rift s), which obviously was very distracting especially when trying to aim a sniper... this is Sniper Elite yanow.... Also there is a constant weapon smoothing to help while aiming but it is way too much there needs to be an option that allows you to lower it or disable it when you are not aiming because when I shifted my aim with a pistol or any other weapon it took the game like half a second to keep up because of the smoothing, this make it very hard to shoot things. When using the weapons it was very challenging because it didn't even feel like I was holding them because of the hand offset and the smoothing, it was like they were floating above my hands, i would have to constantly let go and regrip the weapon to get comfy and then it would just start shifting again floating out of my hands really weird. Weapon scopes are very dark and its very hard to see through them, i have to have my hands jammed in my face to be able to make the scope bigger because of the hand offset and the weapon floatyness. Also reloading and bolting the weapons is a bit jank and needs to be smoothed out. Im sure there will be a path but i just cant recommend when my weapons are floating around the place.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's where I stand on this.  Devs please listen.  The system feels clunky just as others have said.  One of the features, holding the book to choose your level is not a bad idea, I quite like that but the way in which the book is being presented is painful on the wrists.  Now I use an Index controller so I have to point my fingers at me to use that book meaning I have twist my wrist. You put it on the front of the controller instead of it's side somehow.  It's bad, very bad on the wrist. It's not natural at all and does affect game play as it affects that wrist before each mission.  Test and correct this please.The scope mechanic isn't bad actually, I adjusted to it quite quickly and didn't need a stock to assist though using my stock improved my accuracy and stability before using the focus system so the game does translate if you want to use a stock instead.My next big gripe comes from loading pistols.  The griping function is horrible when you need to grab mags out of weapons.  It's just horrendous.    Half the time you can't get it to register your hand near the mag of a pistol because of how close it is to the pickup indicator for grabbing the pistol.  The other problem I find is that I end up accidently gripping the mag and yanking it out because of how the Index controllers operate.  This could easily be fixed my making that grip a little further out from the gun and giving us a release button to prevent these issues(old pistols had heal releases on the bottom of the grips).  In all honesty all these pistols have a release on them IRL so that should have been a dead give away.  This issue alone makes playing the game more difficult than it needs to be.  My fight should be with the enemy and NOT the controls.  All in all, it's not half bad when your actually able to shoot but that's the problem, sometimes you accidently draw a mag from a gun and then drop it without realizing it and end up in a rough spot trying to either recover the mag to shove back into the weapon or your struggling to get it out.  SMGs don't really suffer from this but in areas where you use Welrods it is just painful.  It's sad that games like Onward have had this right since day 1 and somehow you didn't learn from it or it feels like you never handled these weapons IRL and didn't translate them in appropriately.  Anyone buying this, you cannot use 2 hands on pistols.  They are 1 handed only. If you try to 2 hand grip you will rip out the mag. I really want to put a thumbs up on this, I like the game. I seriously like the game but these controls need corrected horribly before I'll recommend this and allow my friends to break their wrists just trying to select a mission.

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game on sale and hopefully after all the issues I'm about to mention get updated. I'm giving this game a thumbs down cause Rebellion has committed VR sins that games 2~3 years old have already figured out and VR devs need to learn these lessons now if we want VR to grow. The bad:-Motion smoothing: Dear god you put it on everything, EVEN MY EMPTY HANDS! Why?! I thought my tracking was lagging till I figured it out. I understand a lot of people are shaky when free handing a VR weapon, but at least give us the option to turn it off/tone it down/select which type of weapon has it. As someone who has 1K hours of VR shooter experience with zero motion smoothing or virtual stock I felt like I was moving through Jello (TM) the entire time. It dulled all my movements and made me feel handicapped. The only time it helped was when sniping but even then I wanted it to only kick in while in focus mode. And don't get me started on the rocket launcher! Y'all added so much smoothing to that thing that trying to move your arm to aim the thing is a suggestion at best.-Controls: Its simple guys, Grip button for grabbing the weapon, nades, and environmental items, and trigger to grab the weapons mag, bolt, and nade pins. I was constantly grabbing my pistol while going for mags or re-gripping my weapon while trying to charge the bolt. Pavlov, contractors, and other VR shooters have already figured this out YEARS ago. Its a good system, use it!-Weapon handling: While trying to swim in jello I was also constantly having to re-adjust my grip on my gun cause y'all were stupid enough to let the weapon stay in the position you un-griped it in instead of resetting it to line up with your hand like every other shooter does. This lead to the gun being shuffled around till it was 5 inches forward and 3 inches up making me punch myself in the chest just to use the scope. And I had to shuffle it back or just re-holster the gun to reset it. Wtf is that?!-Graphics/Environment: Now graphics don't make a game. But they sure as hell help. Especially when you have a WWII game as generic as this story wise. This game looks like it was made in 2006 by an indie team. And I know y'all wanted to have it viable as a Quest port, I understand that, but why did you use the quest assets on PC?! No PBR mats, minimal normal's, every NPC was a mannequin with lego hands, and the poly count was laughable. I'm pretty sure there have been other Sniper Elite game that look a decade better than this game. Oh and the levels were so dreary with the exact same color palette of brown, grey, and sometimes some green. All that while every environment was tiny as hell. I know you wanted to save GPU memory for the quest, but y'all should have designed around that and had in level loading or streaming for the quest so as not to neuter the other versions.-Level design: Boy when I saw that the first real level was a wave shooter I almost lost it. Luckily They got better from there, but not by much. I was excited to see that the level started getting bigger, but every time I got into the groove of a level it just ended. And the lack of level objective variety got boring after awhile. Just shoot, plant explosive, and shoot some more. And that wouldn't be so bad if that loop actually felt good to play (see below).-Gunplay: Man the only fun guns to shoot in this game are the scoped snipers and the silenced pistol. Everything that's full auto bounces around with the jankiest animation that has no ramp ups or downs and just feels like babys first full auto animation. -NPC Movement/Animations: While wrestling with the horrendous motion smoothing and janky full auto guns I had to battle one more hassle, the NPC's animations. None of the animations in this game are procedural or blended in any way. They turn on a dime with no ramp up (A pain while trying to take long range shoots) and jerk and drop like a sack when shoot then snap into a ground pose waiting to be shot again. It seriously feels like then went back and used the first sniper elite games animations from 2005.-"Realism": I originally wanted to go into this game with no assist at all on the sniping. But quickly realized that the bullet in this game are made of Quaker oats and fly a foot to the side every 25 feet life a nerf dart. As someone who does long range shooting IRL I felt like it was just luck based without the assist. I know ya'll want people to use hold overs, but jesus make them reasonable.-Collision: On more than one occasion I would be standing still near a wall or opening and the "You are out of bounds" Black screen would suddenly come up and not go away for 20 secs no matter where I moved. That combined with getting stuck on every little piece of environment geo really annoyed me.-Interaction (Or lack of): This is a VR game guys! Let us pick up things, let us slap things against other things, even basic physics would be ok. The environments felt so empty and lifeless. Lets us turn the valve and actually plant/arm the bombs, not just press a button. That's VR 101.The Good:-Sniping: The sniping in this game (with a scope) is the best in any VR game right now. Using the left trigger to increase the scope size and zoom in more is a great idea, and I would love to see it in other VR shooters (Plus apply a lil motion smoothing to steady the shot).-Kill cam: It's a sniper elite main stay and it's just as good in VR. Looks great (Which makes me think that's where most of their graphics budget went).We need to do better so VR can gain the reputation it deserves as a medium.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected more. To have a VR game in 2021 with hands ghosting through surfaces, enemies clipping through walls and shooting you despite them not being visibly in front of you, items not having real time physics around you, just aint it. On top of that, the game isn't really set up for room scale, which is weird. If you try to peak left or right physically around corners in the game, the tracking gets all weird and your hands don't really follow you so it gets awkward. I'm sure the game will improve over some time, and i'm rooting for it to succeed because we need more AAA titles being released on any VR platform.I guess I expected VR games to follow in HL:Alyx/Boneworks/TWD SS footsteps and up their game (pun intended). These games are the benchmark of what the users expect moving forward.That being said, I'm going to continue to play though the game because shooting stuff in VR is still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite is a WWII franchise about marksmanship, stealth, and cunning. The levels are often large and open ended, allowing for different approaches when choosing how to deal with your tasks, whether that be assassination, sabotage, or something else. It's no surprise that this is a franchise ideally suited to VR, and we now finally have an installment exclusive to virtual reality users. Is it any good, though?The graphics of Sniper Elite VR are okay, but it comes across as a game in which some compromises were made in order to make it work on standalone HMDs like the Quest 2. As such, you're nowhere close to the visual fidelity of games like Half Life Alyx, but the graphics get the job done, I suppose. The first thing you might want to do is disable the lens flare option, as it looks hideous in its current implementation. Another low point in the visual department are the character animations, which feel stilted and jerky.The sound design is fine, from what I could tell. Weapons sound good, and the iconic slowed-down clang of the rifle's firing pin hitting the primer from previous Sniper Elite games is also present here. I don't really have much more to say on the matter, since good sound is something to be taken for granted.The most important element to get right in a Sniper Elite game is the gameplay. For context, previous Sniper Elite games have difficulty options that lets players choose how authentic they want the experience to be. On the easiest settings, players don't have to worry about bullet drop or compensating for the wind. These options are present in Sniper Elite VR too, which is good. The X-Ray kill-cam feature is also here, and it feels about the same as any of the other Sniper Elite games (which isn't a bad thing at all!). If the sniping feels good and authentic and you have the same X-Ray kill feature as before, then this is already shaping up to be a pretty good game! Well.. except for the fact that this game has a glaring flaw.Actually manipulating your weapons in this game is comically uncomfortable. On the Index, the fuse pin on the German stick grenade is extremely fiddly to reach, forcing you to bump your controllers together to pull it out (which can only be done with the grip pad, and not with the trigger, which is a trend you'll see with a lot of things in the game.). The Beretta pistol has a similar problem since it has no mag release button, in fact, none of the weapons have any functions bound to any of the buttons. Break-action shotgun? You have to reach down the barrels and pull it down, instead of using the latch that's SUPPOSED to be able to be operated with your thumb, or in the case of a VR shooter, your face button. You also can't grip the pistols with both hands like you can in many other VR shooters. SMGs like the Sten gun have comically high recoil for some reason, likely a remnant from the previous Sniper Elite games.This isn't even touching on the worst aspect of the controls, which is that your guns kind of just do whatever they feel like. If you try shouldering a sniper rifle and aiming down the sights, you'll quickly find that the gun's fighting you at every moment to throw off your aim. This is almost certainly a result of the game's virtual stock being poorly implemented, and yet it feels like there was no difference, regardless of which stock option I selected. What this means is that you have no chance of firing off quick snapshots, which a skilled VR shooter would be able to do in a game with better implementation, like Pavlov, or H3VR (Especially with the latters' newest implementation of rifle smoothing, which allows for accurate standing shooting at extreme ranges.). You're also gonna miss many deliberate shots because your gun jerked itself slightly to the side just before you pulled the trigger. In a game called Sniper Elite VR, having the rifles be this abysmal to handle is unacceptable.Without going into more detail, because I couldn't bear to play this game for more than 30 minutes or so, I'd say that the controls feel so bad that nothing else in this game can compensate for them. I haven't even mentioned things like the jankiness of the telekinesis grab in this game, or that the levels so far seem extremely small and limited (in a franchise that has had some really large levels in previous games.). That's why I can't recommend Sniper Elite VR.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: It took me about 13 hours to complete this game (which only 2% of users have this achievement). Unfortunately, I did have to repeat several missions in order to get enough stars to be able to unlock the last few missions. So my playtime includes doing certain missions more than once. At the end of this ordeal, I felt relief and disappointment. While the sniping is fun in this game, everything else is really subpar. None of the other weapons feel fun to use. The mission and story structure is also odd in this game. You're basically an old man recalling his war glory days. Unfortunately, this makes the story feel disjointed, along with the broken mission structure. You pick missions from a book, this UI structure is unruly to navigate. It may be harder than the actual sniping. You have to get enough stars to unlock later missions. Getting enough stars is no easy task. Some star sub-missions include stuff like finishing a mission under a certain time limit or getting a score high enough. I never got any of these stars on my first attempt. It also takes away from the game because when you're going for these star sub-mission goals, you have to focus solely on them, to the detriment of your normal play style. It makes the game feel even more linear and rigidly structured. You're told exactly how to play this game. There's also several janky things about this game. For example, when you're looking down scope on your sniper rifle, it will suddenly move left or right and away from your target. No, I'm not talking about the normal scope sway. That's another thing, you can focus to aim better down scope when using a focus ability, but a red square reticle will appear which is unrealistic. I would have preferred just for the focus ability to steady your scope. Enemy AI is also inconsistent & they will seldom try to even flank you (even when alerted). Game is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 90 frames per second for the most part, although I did experience a few frame drops (on high graphical settings). The game does have full locomotion, smooth & snap turning, and teleportation options, as well as some comfort mode options. Unfortunately, there are some vignettes that you cannot turn off (when you button push crouch down, you will have a vertical one and when there is an explosion near you). You have magnet hands by default. Unfortunately, I was often grabbing the wrong thing. Locomotion felt janky as well. The graphics and sounds were okay, but not particularly good. While I did not experience any game-breaking issues or serious bugs, I did experience several annoying bugs, like weapons floating in the air for no reason. I also accidentally clicked on restart instead of load checkpoint twice ... which is very easy to do and very annoying when it happens. Overall, I would say wait for a sale before getting this. Currently, there are just too many issues holding this experience back.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite VR is a thrilling and at times truly tense stealth-action game. Physically keeping your aim steady while ghost sniping a base full of guards or leaning to hear an officer's footsteps while you clutch a suppressed pistol are why a game like this should be played in VR. It could be more polished and the beginning maps feel cramped but the sneaking and shooting in the later stealth missions provide an impressive experience.After a few exciting but constraining opening missions the game starts giving the player some leeway in calmer environments. Subtle play styles become viable and encouraged so the action is often more player-initiated than forced. Shadowy hiding spots to crouch in can be found during night missions and patient scouting frequently pays off. One of the larger missions is essentially a 'Hitman' contract with a target that can be approached from several different directions in a rural area. How you ultimately take him out and from where is your choice.'Seeking Vengeance', one of my favorite missions, has you moving over and under enemies, ducking into tunnels, blowing up vehicles, and quietly eliminating high ranking officers as you infiltrate a beach fortress. The best maps are sniping playgrounds that you'll return to so you can try different loadouts and strategies.The soldiers you're fighting generally react consistently and convincingly even though they're sometimes less concerned about dead bodies and explosions than they ought to be. They will hunt you down or at least start investigating if they hear something or if you stay in their view field too long. You can distract soldiers and even knock them out with thrown bottles or helmets and they'll try to set off alarms when they see their friends drop.Enemy snipers see farther and are more accurate, soldiers with radios fire flares that bring down explosive strikes, and armored enemies will test your grenade throwing and head shot aiming. Enemies also move toward your last known location once you've been spotted. You can attempt to flank them as they approach or set explosives first and then intentionally let them see you.Weapon variety is what you'd expect with a semi-realistic sniping-focused WW2 game. The emphasis is on rifles but there are SMGs, shotguns, and pistols as well with capacity, damage output, and noise level varying between them. The suppressed Welrod pistol is good for quiet short-range work although its slow firing rate can make things awkward if you botch sneaking up on someone.Semi-automatic handguns can be swung at guards for low-decibel knockouts and let you more easily shoot your way out of trouble if you get spotted. The trenchgun is rarely useful outside though it's very effective for point-blank room clearing. Later in the game you come across a suppressed carbine that makes sound masking unnecessary but until you find it you'll be listening for noises in the environment to cover the sound of your very loud sniper rifles. RPGs, mines, TNT, grenades, and trip wires can also be found during missions.Once you get used to those tools and the enemy behavior I recommend trying to play on Sniper Elite difficulty without the HUD. For me the game is best when I have to plan routes, carefully observe patrol patterns, listen for environmental masking sounds, and look for chances to dart between concealment with minimal assistance. Having a sniper's location revealed to me when I see his suspicion meter pop up is far less exciting than spotting him on my own. Simplified ballistics and excessive HUD information can make it too tempting to tune out and start playing the game like a shallow run-and-gun shooter.The physical aspect of VR sniping comes through in this game and there is real tension when you're about to go for a hard shot. Actually crouching and literally holding your aim steady while waiting for a plane to mask sound before the guard in your crosshairs slips away is quite nice. As with other Sniper Elite games you'll be hitting high-scoring trick shots at enemy vitals and equipment which the game rewards with mission stars, achievements, and now delightfully stereoscopic kill-cam views. Note: The game did get a big update that provides plenty of options for improved rifle handling (I was able to get it working well with my gun stock) but there are still some issues remaining. There are a few too many 'out of bounds' warnings when the player is just looking down with their back near a wall or other object. The game also seems to change the player's height when they move 1:1 on slanted ground. I hope those issues are fixed soon but they certainly don't ruin the experience.Even with the remaining issues Sniper Elite VR is one of the better VR stealth games available and quite fun when played with a physical gun stock (I used a ProTube from start to finish and enjoyed it). If you played the game at launch and were bothered by the weapon handling or other problems I'd recommend giving it another try. The September update introduced many detailed options for controls, comfort, and performance/graphics which addressed most of the community requests.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR. Its clunky, unintuitive, lack-luster and feels like a 2017 VR game that was put on the back-burner until some CEO needed some extra cash.The kill-cam is amazing, it never gets old. And that's to be expected seeing as Sniper Elite is and always will be about that sweet sweet visceral kill-cam. That's about where the really good stuff stops.The guns, the levels, the movement, everything feels just... okay. And there are some super annoying things about it too like the bounds of play where you will often go to take cover, only to be met with a black screen and red letters saying you're out of bounds and then teleport you straight into the enemy fire. I've died multiple times because I've gone to take cover only to be teleported straight into the line of fire. Like guys... it's a VR game, LET ME GO WHERE I WANNA GO.Then there's the gripping of the weapons, it's SO floaty. And this is written after the patch that supposedly fixed hand positioning, it didn't. Not to mention every time you come out of a kill-cam, your grip will be rotated 45 degrees and is only fixed when you let go and re-grab. Every. Single. Kill-cam. And the load mechanics are so vague. Because the interaction points are so large and vague, you'll either end up grabbing the bolt when trying to grip or vice versa. I've frequently unloaded my rifle because I've grabbed the bolt while trying to grab the grip. lmao Like indie studios of one to two-person dev teams get gun handling SO right, there's no excuse anymore. Step up your game.Then there's the fact that Non scoped rifles' bullets travel at visibly slow speeds. Now I realize this is how the other Sniper Elite games were but guys, this is VR, our senses are so much more attuned to it now and it sucks.The story? WHAT STORY? You get a narrator that constantly drones over the action. Like dude, shut up. Nothing takes me out of it more than hearing the constant voice of my future self in my ear for 60% of the mission. Also showing me this guy's family playing in between missions and him constantly telling me that he fought so his kids could have this peace is not the way to create emotion and attachment. I don't know this character and I don't know his family. Show me the horrors of war and its toll on his mind, show me the bond with his brothers in arms, show me why their suffering mattered, I mean make a friggin statement on war! Don't pelt me with this bogus John Wayne glorious purpose crap.The levels are painfully linear with zero wiggle room for creativity in play style. I was hopeful after playing Sniper Elite 4 that we would get that sort of semi-open world but not. This is rigid, you go where they want you to go and do what they want. Honestly, I think these bigger devs trying to get into the VR space think we're all stupid, that we constantly need our hands held. Give me some freedom, which is ironic in a game where you're fighting fascists.All in all, if like me, you were expecting Sniper Elite 4 VR, you'll be disappointed. Now while I'm sure a lot of talented people worked on this and its state can only be blamed by overpaid CEOs and board directors undercutting innovation in favor of a quick buck, that doesn't change what it is NOW. And it's just another cookie-cutter, poor handling, on-rails shooting gallery to join the seemingly never-ending list of disappointing VR titles. *sigh*

_childDocuments_.review: Please note: The bones of a good (if simple) VR FPS are there, but in it's current format I can't quite recommend. The Devs have kept in contact with players via the forums however as the game has been out for 6 weeks, and the fixes seem quite simple to implement, it's time to leave a negative review.The biggest issue at the moment is the lack of customisation options; with all the wide array of control options in the world of VR, the best thing to do is just let players customise they're own button mapping completely - no matter how absurd the layout may seem to the developer. On my system, for example, you use the side-grips to pull the bolt on rifles, rather than the trigger (do the motion in real life and see how weird that feels...!). Meanwhile, as a player that prefers (fair) teleporting, it feels a little condescending that they insist on practically stopping the flow of time whenever picking your teleport point - there's no need for that, so where's the option to turn it off? Likewise the usually wide variety of difficulty options in the series is not really there - some players like challenging enemies with simple sniping, others like the opposite - both should be catered to, especially when the series usually does.Meanwhile there's a lot of small issues all over the place - the 'out of bounds' registry is all over the show, sometimes blacking the screen out in an intense fight for no apparent reason. The placement of weapons on shoulders/belts etc is a little fiddly too - the main reason I've died so far is because of fumbling around for weapons and having them fall through my torso (although this seems a little better than at launch).From a design standpoint, the levels are a little simplistic - I'm not sure if this was done to support the feeble PS and Oculus Quest hardware, but it definitely holds this back from being a fully-fledged Sniper Elite game. SE3 and SE4 had excellent huge levels that required a lot of planning and strategy to complete cleanly - these are PS2 FPS levels by comparison, with some areas that open up a little, but mostly it's generally a very linear slog.I would say most galling thing with this type of game - and we've seen it with other releases like Fallout VR - is that it reeks of a developer who hasn't actually played much (if any) VR themselves. Go load up something like H3 and learn how to make really solid believable weaponry in VR! Go see how other games handle 'out of bounds' issues! Go see how many options some of these games pack in to cater to a wider range of gamers! And then cry when you realise that most of these are made by very small development teams. And of course, absolutely go play Half Life Alyx to see what the current gold standard is, and maybe dissect why it works so well  (hint - 'russels' didn't exist in the 1940s).

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the sniper elite and was excited when I saw a vr version of the games existed. And so I bought this game on sale and was excited to see how it translated to VR. IT'S FINE. While I did enjoy the time I put into it this game made me realize something about sniper elite. I prefer the series for it's stealth gameplay with sniping sprinkled in-between. From the first couple of missions it feels like you are mostly defending a point from being taken over. I did enjoy this but it got stale really quick and I never thought I'd say this but the kill cams were very annoying. I don't know if it's just me but when playing the vr version cutting to the kill cam and back to first person is disorientating and makes me confused for a second or two as to where I'm aiming. Plus the sudden change of light made me feel a little sick after a while. Both of these things make the missions feel a bit long and boring. I also had problems with the hands that hold the guns. This was probably my computer but I noticed that sometimes my hand movements wouldn't be picked up by the game making it a bit frustrating to aim sometimes. However I did noticed this happened a lot when I'm near an in game open window so maybe I was just hitting the in game environment. Picking up weapons and storing them also didn't work well for me. Not only do I have to make sure that I have a grip on what I'm grabbing but I also have to pull back pretty hard to equip a gun. And no matter what the game tells me I can never pocket the weapons for later it worked in the tutorial but nowhere else. Now yes I'm being quite negative for a recommended review but I think all that is needed to show what you need to expect going into this game. Sniper elite is a mostly stealth focused video game that has some fun sniping physics to make it's self different from the crowd. So I think it's best to let sniper elite fans that enjoy the stealth know that this is more combat and sniping focused. Because I did enjoy the sniping mechanics they are very satisfying to get down and not only that there's a lot of content for how average price the game is. It is an overall good game but just not a game for me I'll just stick to the non-vr games they feel a lot more satisfying to me for the added stealth elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Can, maybe, be a little bit more fun after a few Major updates, otherwise will not be worth the full price.Feels very clunky, guns drift ever so slightly while holding them with two hands, weapon-belt drifts and rotates on you, grips things you aren't close to(try to grip stock on rifle after reload, but grips bolt again, which imo should be progammed to be impossible immediately after a reload), no running(afaik), says I'm "outside play area" when I step inside objects like tables... just NO! That's not what the term 'play area' is used for in VR, was super confused at first, since I knew I was nowhere near being outside my actual 'play area' I have setup in my headsetGraphics are very dated, screenshots looks juiced up from what I saw in-game with highest settings, can't interact with much, textures are rather bland and uninspired, polygon count feels like it's not even up to 2012 standards, particle effects/explosions look like they would run on a Celeron just fine, the 'splash effect' from throwing a wine bottle on the ground would be put to shame by the 'blood effect' from Quake 2Story feels a bit uninspired, but is okay'ish I guess, havn't gotten very far, so it could get better. _childDocuments_.review: It's fun. I don't quite get all the hate other reviews are giving it. This is also quite a meaty game compared to many other VR games for the same price that can be completed in 2-3 hours.The shooting mechanics are what you'd expect from a Sniper Elite game, but in VR. Yes, some sniper rifles, specifically the DeLisle Carbine, which is only unlocked by the end of the game, has the magazine, the bolt and the grip very close to each other, but even then, it's perfectly playable.The "X-Ray" kills mechanic is kinda poor in this game, it completely breaks the flow of the combat and you always have to readjust your aim after the killcam ends because your physical hands would've drifted away by then. I feel like they could've done this better, perhaps some sort of in-world zoom that is not visible in-scope or something. Thankfully there's an option to turn the killcam off completely.I have completed the entire game on the hardest difficult with no assists. While it's definitely doable, I would not recommend it even if there's an achievement for it. It kinda saps some of the fun out of the game, mostly because there's so little feedback as to where your bullets are firing, that you can't really adjust.It has full Valve Index support, but am not sure it's the best device to play this, solely because of the subpar image quality of the headset. There's just too much blur to be able to aim well without a scope, and even with a scope it's blurry, even if you look directly forward in the headset. The height calibration was also off, I was basically always floating above the ground, without an obvious way to fix it.There's a lot of difficulty and comfort settings, so if you don't want the balls to the wall realism experience, you can adjust the game for yourself and still have fun. In fact, after beating the game on the hard difficult, I switched to the easy one and still had loads of fun doing the extra challenges. Actually seeing where my bullet would go also opened my eyes to not rapidly pressing the trigger button, as that does slightly move the aim, just enough to miss. Slowly squeezing as you focus in felt more 'authentic'. This also made me realize holding focus for longer usually nets you a lot more points.It's by no means a perfect game. The AI is a mixed bag, sometimes they will flank you and kill you in 3 shots, sometimes you can facetank dozens of bullets without issue. Just like in the non VR Sniper Elite games, there's a small amount of "enemies see you through walls and shoot you through corners" issues.There's a bug where if you load a save, your stowed grenades will become unusable.There's no weapon customization at all. (Unless you consider unlocking non scoped variants of the sniper riles as such) There's a per-weapon challenge system, but all it gives you is extra points if doing special kills (i.e. eye shots give 20 extra points), which is kinda useless. The final challenge on a gun also unlocks a golden variant for that weapon, but only for the scoped rifles.The game also never really explains what the difference is between all the sniper riles. There is no stats for each one anywhere, so you just have to try them and maybe feel the difference, somehow.The achievements are kinda grindy, notably the collectibles and ESPECIALLY the "master every weapon" one.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: The Game defiantly holds your hand for the first 30 minutes, as you get a bunch of game play right away. , then it slows down to a base/headquarters section of the game where you can choose your load out and select missions from your home. As you progress, you will learn how to select a load out, learn the SMG, pistol, and rifle. Your book shows your load out, your current and last missions, as well as any discoverable items that you may have found.Sniper Elite VR Also gives you multiple ways to play though a mission, which are welcomed on the harder difficulties, as you easily get swarmed by automatic fire and sniper rounds. The realistic bullet model feels very tuned and its extremely hard to land a head shot on a man in cover. Holding your rifle at an angle will result in your bullet drop being off and your shot missed. The Belt system can use some tasty tips from Onward; a more clean cut way of holstering your weapons compared to Sniper Elite VR’s current implementation.The Story Is fast paced and the flow of the game is kept to a steady beat. Each Mission has you in a different part of Italy, all the while bring your some majestic views of some very beautiful mountains peaks. Game elements (such as tower defense or waves) which, to those that enjoy Wave mechanics and tower defense, this game is gonna feel right at home for you. The Waves are not endless by any means, and you find yourself finishing missions mid fight, which can be a bit of a turn off after living in your Lee Enfields Scope for Thirty plus minutes.An Authentic Difficulty HeadshotLevel DesignLevel Design is right where it should be for a studio like this. It is easy to place explosives around the map and use them in the right time to make a very strategic play. There is one level where I placed a mine to drop a Jager, who was armored and armed with a sniper… and he doesn’t go down in one shot. This is where place-able/ equipable items such as the proximity mine come in handy Other missions do feel like they are implemented back in a different and more difficult way, which makes you use what you learned in very reinforcing way. Rocket launchers are placed about the levels as well, and the collectables are placed in positions that reward you for checking and looking. Even some of the ammunition given to you will greatly reduce the amount of shooting you will have to do.Using Munitions Around The Level Is A Great BoonComfort And ControlsControls and Comfort As for the controls, they feel like they have been optimized for the Quest 2 in mind. Nothing about handing any rifle with the Valve Index (Knuckle) Controllers feels remotely similar to Onward in anyway. Now I know these are two different beasts, but I am hoping to see a feature to select your controller for the most optimized VR experience. This does not pair well with a clunky feeling belt. However this is by no means game breaking. They have recently updated the game with better working AI and improvements to the belt and equipment holster.Toggle switch for holding a rifle is really nice because I do find myself tensing up on the rifle, distorting my point of aim. With toggle you are able to let go of your grips and relax. Its a really nice feature they added, and it saves you energy and strain on the hands and wrists.Snipe Elite VR can easily become a sweaty game as you are always ducking and reloading from incoming fire. Its not as accurate as some players might be in multiplayer games like Onward, but this can be a good thing, even on Authentic Difficulty.Sometimes You Just Get Lucky (Authentic Difficulty)Final ThoughtsI Think Sniper Elite VR offers something in a space that VR is not too well developed yet. The Story line feels very much like the old PS2 Call of Duty Games, And that’s not bad at all! Rebellion Studios nails the feel and look of the last Great War, and its done so without being so taxing and demanding.The Gun play feels good enough although I wish they polished the look and feel of the automatic rifles a little more, as I really enjoy running though like the map with an automatic and clearing the map of Nazis like the good old PlayStation 2 days. The narration and story are very immersive and the situations you are put in are very challenging and very fun and worth the full price of the game.If you would like to See more content on Sniper Elite VR, Check out Our Content At GamesWithGreg Youtube And Twitter! And share if you think this will help someone!

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Index + 2080ti with smooth locomotion:This is a very soft recommendation contingent upon a sale that's $10 or less.I had no issues with aiming and shooting virtual fascists, maneuvering around the environment, nor interacting with the inventory system. It's also a very straight forward experience: load into a linear small form mission, shoot everyone you see, and ex-filtrate. The novelty of loading and firing WW2 era weapons against Nazis has a certain charm, one that almost feels like a VR version of the Medal of Honor and CoDs of the early 2000's.Additionally, keep your expectations low, and you'll be pleasantly surprised at the level of polish. Everything does work, and well enough that I never felt like I was inhibited by the game's inherent mechanics, just the short comings of the overall game design, i.e. small levels and minimal depth.I don't regret my purchase, but I certainly don't think I'll play through it again. The mixed number of reviews are pretty apt, so your mileage will definitely vary.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't want to believe many of the reviews before I bought this game.  I thought, most of these people are probably just casual players who can't handle VR like I can.  I have been a VR enthusiast for years.  I currently have a Rift S and an RTX 4090.  I have never really ever experienced any discomfort from VR games.  I haven't experienced any from this game yet either, I just wanted to make that clear because I think it's relevant.  I realize at the time of this review I don't have a lot of time in the game, but there are some games where you know early on it's not going to be a good game.  I'm currently running 1.5x Super Sampling from the Oculus debug tool with max settings but 2xMSAA.  That's already a much lower resolution that I typically run.  I usually run a minimum of 2.0x super sampling, but this games frame rate was basically crippled by 2.0x.  The game runs fine once you get some settings that your system can handle, so that's at least one good thing that's important.To me, this is not a Sniper Elite game.  I have played most of them, 1 through 4, I have not yet played 5.  This game doesn't seem like a AAA title.  It seems to me like a game an indie developer that has never played VR thinks how a sniping simulator ought to play, but wasn't totally dedicated to the sim aspect of the game.  The game could be decent enough if you just had the option to fire the guns single handed.  I really don't like firing the weapons with two hands because the hand you're holding out in front of you gets tired from holding it out there for so long.  I did play Farpoint on PSVR with the gun that came with, that was actually really cool.  Holding an akward imaginary gun out in front of you is not even remotely similar to that at all.  There's that, and the fact that they expect you to manually reload your weapons.  To be fair, there is at least an option to turn off manually reloading, but if you are running manual reloading, it's extremely difficult to do when sitting.  Not everybody wants to play VR games standing 100% of the time.  At least they added an option to adjust for height, that is another positive.  I mean, this game has potential if they'd fix all the little issues.  The way you snipe is by holding the gun up near your face like you would with a real gun, but you zoom in and go into a sort of bullet time or slow motion.  This didn't bother me, but I can see this really being a major game breaking issue for some people who are sensitive to motion sickness.  I prefer firing scoped weapons in VR games by switching to a dedicated scope screen like Fallout 4 or Borderlands 2.  I can do it, but with that, and having to manually reload, on top having to hold the your arms out in front of you, it's just a bit much.  It makes it very difficult to relax and enjoy it.  But the main problem is level design.  The levels are tiny and you're basically on rails.  Shooters on rails were an acceptable design in the very early days of VR, but now, that's just lazy.  There's no reason they couldn't have just ported one of the existing Sniper Elites over to VR, THAT would have great, and a heck of a lot better than this mess.There are some cool things like being able to fire Panzerfoust rockets.  Throwing grenades is just awful.  They do try to make it easy, but the range is pathetic.  You're throwing a stick grenade, something designed to be able to be thrown a fair distance, and you're limited to 25 feet max.  I feel like I could chuck a stick grenade a solid 30 yards without too much effort irl.  Firing pistols is actually great, except the manual reloading.  Ditch the requirement for two handed weapon handling, speed up the guys sprint, make swapping weapons easier.  You swap weapons in the same manner as Bone Works if you've ever played that, where you have them "stored" around your body.  Give us some alternatives for viewing through a scope.  You know what really bugs me is when you're looking through a scope, when you're viewing something in the distance, it's all blurry and pixelated like the game is actually zooming in on a distant object rather than rendering it at a closer distance through the scope.  It's very bizarre.I realize this review was mainly just me rambling, I didn't really think too much about it beforehand, and I don't want to spend a ton of time writing this.  But my point stands, I didn't want to believe that a Sniper Elite VR game was actually bad, and I guess it's not completely awful, but it should have been much, much better than this.  I do not recommend this game, unless it's dirt cheap, and since it's from a AAA studio, they think they can sell it for top dollar.  Even if you're a VR enthusiast like me, you may be thinking, it can't be that bad, well, it's pretty bad.  If I had to rate it, I'd give it a 4 or 5 out of 10, call it a 4.5 out of 10 to be fair I guess.  I just want to roll my eyes when I think about it, and dream of the day when VR games might actually be something good, and not just quickly slapped together cash grabs.  After this debacle, I'm very seriously concerned about Medal of Honor VR, which I have not yet played.  Mainly due to the negative reviews and the price never dropping to a reasonable level.

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving a positive review so this game doesn't get buried and forgotten about by the developer but just wanted to share some thoughts on why I'm refunding and why I will re-purchase upon patch fixes implemented (if they happen to be implemented).Starting off, a lot of people are slandering the game for what they perceive to be a very poor visual experience and essentially a Quest 2 port-based experience. I don't think the main problems with the game are visual and, in fact, quite enjoyed the visuals. I don't think the realistic aesthetic should be attempted for VR games without the expectation that the game will be either minimally interactive, short or woefully underwhelming in terms of gameplay as is the case for most big VR game launches. I'd rather interaction be the basis for a good core gameplay loop.I think this is where Sniper Elite VR fails to some degree - the basics are all there. There's manual reloading, free locomotion, etc. You have holsters on your back for your rifles and the grabbing function is Alyx-esque. The problem with Sniper Elite VR's interactions lie solely with the way your hands interact with the rifle right now. They feel heavy. Your hands feel floaty and heavy and smoothing for the rifle is heavy-handed as well and takes away from the interaction significantly in the opening moments of the game (as far as I got before deciding I want to wait for patches and not get burned like I did with MOHVR before purchasing again). The bolt on the rifle feels stiff and the haptic feedback using a Q2 through VD is over-pronounced instead of subtle for weapon interactions. If I were to give notes to the devs, I would implore them to allow options to change weapon and hand smoothing and give an option to turn off the virtual stock (without using a stock to compliment the virtual stock using just controllers and your hands, the virtual stock feels like you're glued to the weapon). I'd also implore them to give an option to turn off the volume-dampening surrounding the narration as it feels jarring, give an option to remove the red-screen on the kill-cam, make the haptic feedback during rifle interactions shorter and less over-pronounced and allow the player to manipulate the bolt using the trigger instead of the grip so awkward wrong-grip interactions don't happen. I'd also like to see quicker interaction mechanics overall - I should be able to reload a weapon quickly without it feeling awkward or too hand-fed and slide a bolt quickly with subtle hand-movements a'la H3VR/Pavlov/Onward, etc. Also I've heard you can only one-hand pistols. All VR weapons should be two-handed to some degree allowing for off-hand stabilization or it feels awkward. Also also - allow me to fail! If I pull the bolt back and I forget to reload it, let me push the bolt back in and make the gun make an empty click sound. I don't want to have my hand grab the bolt at any time and have it be locked in place. The chaotic nature of having to do things manually is what makes VR great. Let me fail. Hats off to the devs for their foray into VR. I really hope you take all these notes on board because your sales will come over time with a good product, not all at once like with flatscreen gaming, and I think it's important for Rebellion to show that they're dedicated to their consumer-base, as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: after the last update by the devs on this game the room scale is broke. I emailed the devs about it shortly after the update about a yr ago but it was never addressed.. the game keeps making the player way to tall or floating above the ground. and the calibration from the menu doesn't  fix it.. I can no longer recommend this game.  :(  walking dead onslaught also got worse after a game update.. :( Please devs , at least allow us to download an older version of the game. under the beta selection.... Thanks.. old review: I play in my 2 car garage with my wireless vive pro and use my play space to the fullest. I prefer to walk in my play space corner to corner and use Manual Redirected walking with space turn via OVR Advanced Settings. Sniper Elite VR lets me play this way and I am very thankful for that. A lot of the maps are huge so I will walk in my play space and use joystick locomotion at the same time when I have to cross a lot of ground.         My biggest complaint about Sniper Elite VR is I am always getting black screen saying out of bounds, return to center of playspace If I barely go somewhere I am not suppose to, like over in game furniture, big rocks, tree trunks, some dead bodies, and even certain slants in the terrain. I also get this black screen sometimes when I'm not near any geometry but just on a flat open space. It also goes black a lot when I'm just trying to duck in real life, probably because the fat collision box is colliding with near by cover.          Second complaint about the game is the non sniper guns panning movement is  laggy/smoothed when moving them around in space. All the guns seem to have same smoothing which is needed for sniping with a sniper rifle but the short range weapons don't need the same smoothing and feel slow and not as responsive as they should when in close quarters combat. It's hard to pull empty magazines out of the pistols, they need an eject button on the controller. Don't wait for a pull out retical to appear just try to pull it out and it'll be easier i think.. A release slide button for appropriate guns would also be nice.        It's   hard to aim down and see the iron sights of most guns, all the iron sights need glow in the dark paint as they blend into the background often. Not all the iron sights are accurate either. You're expected to just aim via the tracer bullets when you're not using a scope but the bullets feel like they drop too fast in Normal and Elite difficulty so it doesn't feel great. There is no bullet drop in Easy mode , and these bullets feel much better, but the enemies can't damage you very fast so it's too easy. The sniper rifles have bullet drop and wind to calculate in the Hard/Elite difficulty. Bullet drop and wind also effects your aim on every non-scoped gun differently in Normal and Elite difficulty, but there isn't really a way to tell which way the wind is blowing besides shooting a shot and looking at the tracer trail. You cant see the trail in the scope for some reason so you have to open your other eye quick to see it in Elite.  I perfer how the guns feel in easy but I have beaten the game in Normal and Elite..      My last complaint is the grabbing is janky. It is difficult to grab ammo/guns right in front of you by realistically putting your hand on it, it is way easier to Force-grab from a distance and I learned like 10 hours into the game that you can force grab without the magnetic icon even appearing on the objects, so knowing this made it really easy to force grab but sometimes you just want to really bend down and pick something up for immersions sake. It is a good game over all , Maybe even a top 10  VR game. The more I played the more I learned to enjoy it. I turned off the kill cams early on as it seemed like it was taking me out of the action to much. I also learned to keep looking down the scope after pulling the trigger to see the effect of my shots. I played most of it with a Protube gun stock and this feels way better . It's cool that you can dual wield and swap a weapon hands on the fly. I liked picking up the dead enemy's Nazi's guns and grabbing the mags from them so I could use the bullets later. The graphics seemed a little dated but it ran Great. It's a Great game for the Price. I would of liked more close quarters combat but it is a sniper game after all.  I beat it in 12 hours on Normal difficulty then I had  fun going back to get all the stars. Then I was going for all achievements which I have never done. Now I only need one more!

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, not great. The good: It's a Sniper Elite game so the sniping is amazing. The X-ray killcams are still here and work surprisingly well in VR. The performance was great, I didn't notice a single stutter or dip in fps. The ability to holster an extra pistol is a nice touch. The story is somewhat interesting, though it does become a bit repetitive. The narrations are well done.The bad: The game feels like it was built for the Oculus Quest, not PCVR. The visuals are muddy and low poly, even on the highest settings. Being day one there are a lot of bugs, like the rifle not wanting to holster over the right shoulder and the hands being a few inches above the actual controllers, making aiming with anything other than the rifles pretty difficult. Overall, Sniper Elite VR looks and feels unfinished. The game is very fun but it is impossible to ignore the bugs. Wait until some future patches or a sale to pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Review: Love it !!The game looks great it has a great detail in the environments, a narrated story that gives a progress to the player throug different levels, you have also an initial target practicing part to test different weapon types besides the Sniper Rifle, and of course you have additional models of Snipers to use. Some players are reporting that they have slow or heavy hands when reloading but I didn't have that issue at all I even recorded a video that I will upload to my channel once I finish other things but so far I love the game. UPDATE: Devs released a fix that solved the miss aligned hands for the users that had the issue. Several bad reviews were for this sadly.The Aiming in Virtual Reality is main core gameplay and it feels so amazing to see the results with the kill cams; showing the entry points of the bullets. It is a Mortal Kombat fatality on each well placed shots.Besides you controlling your pulse to make a perfect shot the game brings realistic ballistic physics on advanced difficulty that you have learn to master the correct trajectory of the shots. Besides that, this the game brings you a focus action that will give you a slowed time and controlled pulse/breath from the character as it is on these series and it rocks. The entire shooting mechanic is so much fun to play and is exacerbated in VR.My only complain so far is that I agree with other players, grenades should be allowed to be thrown naturally. Also the bullets entering the weapons feel out of place as you grab them correctly to the slot position and "blink"... they magically appear inside. After all the amazing shooting action these 2 details lower the amazing immersion achieved already, but I do not care to much to be honest.Using an I7+16gb+EVGA 1080 ftw (factory oced)+ Vive Pro the game works perfectly on maximum quality .I disable Vsync on Nvidia drivers, set the max frame rate to 90 fps, Maximum performance and AA completely disabled as it makes things blurry.  -- The game works PERFECTLY without any bugs and without any performance issue so far -- I will update my review as I keep playing forward and will upload some gameplay videos.Kudos to Rebellion/Just add water Devs, great work, you have my support :)Update with 1st video. _childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: I've got it almost maxed out on gfx settings, running on a mid range machine (Quest 2 + link, RX 580 8gb, R5 3600(only running 4 of 6 cores), 1tb NVMe SSD, and 16gb of the slowest ram you can get), having a phenomenal frame rate, with 120% RS. Not sure what that one dude is chirping about... Must be running on a potato salad, or something.The guns do feel weird, and your off hand when gripping the rifle, does not line up with your real hand. That, somehow doesn't ruin it for me, though. It's a bit sloppy if you wanna run and gun, but this game is meant to be played, using a stealthy approach. That said, if you take your time and plan your routes, you should manage to enjoy the game a bit more. What sells it for me, aside from the fact that I got it on sale for $13 CAD, is that it has a full campaign (like the old shooters), with some decent replay value. Also, has a detailed and engaging story, and top notch voice acting. I love to get swept away into a game's story. This does that, fairly well.Buy it on sale, for sure, but if you wanna just chill and play a solo campaign, this is worth it. It's a breath of fresh air, honestly. When I reached the 2 hr window, I was like, "this is fine."
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, because as much as I anticipated this game, I can't recommend it. Having only played an hour, I can't speak much for the story, but as for the weapons, it just doesn't feel like it should. My largest issue is with the controls and tracking. After shooting a few rounds with the rifle, it seems like I need to let go and grab again. The scope is sometimes very small, and sometimes it takes up my entire view, even though its in the same spot. As for the controls, I really don't get why the grip button is used for everything. The trigger should be used for pulling the bolt and reloading so that you make sure you perform the right action. Accidentally grabbing the weapon has become a slight annoyance for me when trying to reload. Other than that, the game seems solid and just needs some tweaking. -Played on Quest 2 via Airlink and Index
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: Going from HL Alyx to Sniper Elite VR feels like going from Doom Eternal back to Wolfenstein (the one from the 80s).... but without the nostalgia factor.Good things first:- The sniping part is quite fun (however, the bullet slow-motion effects don't work well in VR) and worked quite well for my Steam VR setup.Things that annoyed me the most:- Selecting the mission from a mission book for which you need to break your wrist to read it (@JAW: Have you even tried playing this game yourself? I cannot imagine any testers that would give that a thumbs up).- When putting my left hand down to rest it I constantly picked up either my left-hand gun  or some ammo from the bag. It feels like getting your hand in one of those stick fly traps which you cannot easily rip of when the other hand is trapped in one too. Especially fun when enemies are attacking you.- Overall the whole grabbing system feels quite unnatural and you often end up picking up something you didn't want to or having your gun in a strange angle.- Enemies are dumb and annoying. You can shoot a door to which they stand next to without them noticing. But they might spy you from 5 km distance at a checkpoint.- When reloading a checkpoint you often end up blacked-out because the game detects that you collided with an object (which is the checkpoint itself).- Almost no interaction or physics fun with any objects in the world (you cannot even throw grenades by a hand movement)....

_childDocuments_.review: In all the VR games I have played, I believe this game has the worst controls ever. Playing with the Index controllers, I was constantly dropping every gun I touched. In order to pick up weapons, you must grab and magically flip the weapon towards you. You cannot remap the grab function and trying to do this with the Index controllers made the game almost unplayable for me. I spent the majority of this game standing around trying to flip guns into my hands and then trying to place both hands on the guns, only to keep dropping them over and over. The reloading process is also very awkward. The rifle scope also drifts a lot and holding it steady is pretty difficult. Enemies inside the scope are also blurry and hard to see. There are also constant black screen warnings if you step outside the play area. Overall, this is a very poor VR experience. I'll just stick to playing the non-VR Sniper Elite games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a great time, but still has problems. Most are minor but involve comfort. First off, I don't love how the 2 handed gunplay feels. The off hand's wrist movement (angle/rotation) doesn't affect anything. This makes zeroing in shots outside of sniping (fairly common) pretty wonky. Second, there NEEDS to be an option to turn off screen shake from explosions. I don't know who left that in and didn't expect shaking the whole world in VR might be an issue. Third, I find "ratchet" ladder climbing systems to be very unpleasant. If I can't have direct climbing control, please include an option to bypass the ladders and teleport up?That said, the game is a lot of fun. Little moments of controls doing things you don't want them to is disappointing, but acceptable for the experience. Close quarters is frenetic and hard to excel at, but is intense in a very gratifying way. Stealth is surprisingly compelling, giving me better peak-around-the-corner thrills than even the excellent Espire.1. And that option to put a reticle at the center of the screen for comfortable smooth screen turning is still genius.Overall, I'm really happy with this game and hoping to continue having a good time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: I personally am hooked on this game and would call it the best stealth title you'll find for VR. Its got the great bullet cam feature, you get a great mix of Sniping and Sneaking, interesting, well laid out levels and nice rewards system for certain weapon use and kill types and collectibles to keep an eye out for. The graphics are nice and i've had a great looking, smooth experience playing on a gaming laptop with an i9 and a 2070 graphics card. Other reviewers have given this a thumbs down though I think thats too harsh for a title of this quality. Yes, its not perfect. The mechanic for grabbing items takes some getting used to and can be frustrating at times (so was Half Life Alex) , the story is forgettable, you have to use the control to crouch and cant IRL, and, the only REAL irritant for me, there is no melee kill weapons! Still, all that was rapidly forgotten as i got to sneak into Nazi territory and wait for the perfect moment to take my shot so the sound was masked. I also found a lot of replay value. I went through first on "Story" mode to get a feel for the game and not be frustrated with overly difficult challenges. once through that it was fun to go back and play at higher levels. Wanting to improve your score for certain levels or complete a level without being detected are all fun challenges for me.Now if they would only give us a Nazi zombie level!
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions are everything for most people, when I tried Metal of Honor: Above and Beyond on release day there were many issues. The lack of many, I would call 'standard features' like smooth turning, were absent from the game. I refunded and have not tried it again, Sniper Elite VR may end up the same way. Visually the games look quite similar, although the character models don't look as uncanny. There are many options for changing your movement type/locomotion, off to a good start. The first mission I noticed my VR hands were about 5 centimeters above my real hands which was disorienting. Next I had some major issues using the Valve Index controllers, it almost seems to sensitive or not responsive at all. I had continuous issues trying to put guns on my back, they always fall to the ground instead. This mechanic works great in Pavlov but almost never does here. Next you have to use the 'grab' button to bolt the rifle, grabbing ammo from your belt, and holding the gun; what I notice is after I take my hand off the trigger to bolt for the next shot, instead of grabbing the gun I grab the bolt again and lose a bullet. There are also little circles indicators on the gun guiding where to hold the gun, where to reload. When I see my hand hovering over this circle indicator, it grabs the wrong thing. I just can't see this being user error when I play Pavlov regularly and problems like this rarely occur. This is an issue with all the weapons in the game, not just sniper rifles, and other index users have reported similar buggy controls. I was hoping for a somewhat open level design like previous Sniper Elite entries, taking on the mission sorta how you want to and play into the 'stealth mechanics' but so far the levels seem to be structured in a very similar way to Metal of Honor: Above and Beyond. The world is connected by selecting the mission you want to start, load into the world and play for about 10 minutes or less before congratulations you did it on to the next one. Loading screen. Mission select. Loading screen. main character narrates everything that is happening before your eyes. congratulations! Loading screen. Loading screen. do you see where I'm going with this?It's kind of funny, the folks at Just Add Water have made a very similar game to Respawn's MoH. Respawn's game released first with many complaints like price, optimization, missing options, etc. Just Add Water fixed the major flaws like pricing the game reasonably, runs better, compatible for all players, but it doesn't change the fact that it feels like your playing a interactive movie. Not to mention all these "games" are made with Facebook money so anyone with a Oculus Quest 2 is strangely playing the superior port of the game. Makes me feel good about investing in this Valve Index am I right fellas.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's mostly about interacting and aiming with guns, this game makes it very frustrating to interact and aim with guns.  Having played H3 and Arizona Sunshine, I figured these were all solved problems and was looking forward to some sniper focused story and game play.   I was incorrect.  Your hands are horribly "floaty" and seem to lose position often.  Have to reload in the heat of battle or during session at the shooting range?  Forget about it.  You'll routinely do anything but what you are TRYING to do with your gun.  Again, these are things that already exist in other games and are done VERY WELL in those games.  How did the game even get into production without someone being able to first say "Yes, we have a really excellent weapons handling model figured out!"?Also:* So-so graphics, even on highest settings* physics objects often freak out and fly all over the place, including bodies
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: There's a reason the reviews are mixed. I'm generally a pretty open person when it comes to my enjoyment in a video game. I was left disappointed and got a refund. Here's why.Rift S/2080S/5800xPros: Great scenery and character models, especially on high graphics settingsKillfeed is another level of awesome, especially in VR.Guns look and sound great.The focus mode is perfect for VR, definitely the best sniping I've done; no unrealistic sway or wobble.Movement control is where I wanted it to be, comparable to pavlov/contractors/onward.Cons: WHY ARE MY HANDS 3 INCHES ABOVE WHERE THEY'RE SUPPOSED TO BE? WAS THIS NOT PLAYTESTED?Seriously that ruined the entire experience. I'm punching myself in the face trying to look down the sights, and reloading with a physical gunstock is impossible. When you reload, you can't grab the grip of the gun because it's the same button as chambering a round, leading you to grab the wrong thing multiple times. I'm all for immersion, but why do I need to stop mid combat to fiddle with grabbing my gun?I really REALLY dislike the tunnel vision effect. It pops up seemingly whenever it wants to and it's super easy to forget where you are. You do feel like you're in danger, but it's difficult to rely on instinct in these scenarios. It feels artificial.If there was a hand recalibration setting and a way to disable the tunnel vision, it would be up there as one of the best VR shooters I've played. I read through every review on this game and thought "Maybe that won't happen to me." But literally every negative comment left, I had experienced. I'm very disappointed. I was also hyped for MoH and I'm left feeling the exact same way.5/10 Cannot recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of VR best new shooters.  It definitely doesn't compete with games like Half-Life Alyx but VR is lacking when it comes to single player campaigns.  Sniper Elite VR is amazingly well paced, action packed, has fun stealth mechanics and that X-ray kill cam never gets old. The campaign is lengthy and knows how to deliver a compelling story-line in VR. There is no standing around watching people talk.  I feel the controls can still use some tweaking but overall I really enjoyed this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: This feels and looks like another Quest port, even if devs may have based the PCVR version on the PS4 version. Or maybe they made a really low poly PS4 version that easily could be used for the Quest version. No matter the excuse, this game looks Questified, and looks as if the devs have been trying to hide the low-poly models by making nicer textures and adding grass etc. But take a look at objects that should be round - like a plate. It's not round, but maybe octagonal or so. In the very first level check out the armchair, it's really ugly with extremely few polygons. Also you can pick up very few objects, because the Quest processors can't handle real physics. So you get none of that in this game. Shadows are just blob shadows, you got no dynamic light and shadows in this game, because the Quest processors can't handle that. Also check out the npcs, if you look closely, can you see how few polygons they are made of? Does not look like a game from 2021, maybe more like a game from 2005. And check out the pieces of bricks when something explodes - big low-poly chunks flying at you. The game has been somewhat optimized for the Index, meaning there is finger tracking, and some textures are great. But devs only made some surfaces nicer, and forgot many surfaces where you can see the ugly low-res textures. This show that some high-res textures were added, but this probably was never a PCVR game from the beginning. Thus this is no PCVR game and will be an easy refund to me - but still a sad one. I was hoping that we'd at least get the poly count making this game look just slightly like real PCVR, but unfortunately that did not happen. Btw, I'm using an i9 10900K cpu, oc'ed RTX 3090, 32GB and the game is on my Samsung 860 EVO 4TB SSD. I got solid 90 fps with res 200% and graphics on high in 90 Hz (didn't bother checking 144 Hz, because very low-poly games are dead to me no matter the performance). Congrats to standalone Quest users - this game is probably one of the best you got. But PCVR enthusiasts might want to use 14GB drive space for anything but this garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite VR

_childDocuments_.review: Beside the positive reviews, Sniper Elite VR is not a good game. Weapon handling is more then inaccurate, sometimes it isn't even possible to properly aim on the target, because it is impossible to hold the weapon steady. Sometimes the gameplay is more like a flag in the wind, constantly swinging from left to right. It's almost impossible to hold the gun still or see properly through the scope. The x-ray view doesn't make shooting any better either. If you feel like playing an unfinished game that doesn't even have really good graphics, you can/should buy the game, but if someone values getting a graphically appealing game that also offers good gameplay and realizes decent weapon handling, they shouldn't buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Would be great if it wasn't for the very poor weapon interactions.Key issues I saw:* Every gun feels very floaty, like there is half a second of delay when moving it around* No second hand grip on pistols that I can find* Interaction areas are generally too small and hard to grab even with the annoying popup* Some of the grip areas are in unintuitive places, specifically forward grips for smaller weapons* No magazine releases or other controls. This is especially frustrating on pistols.* Magazine grab areas appear physically inside the index controllers, making them impossible to grab* Bolt handle and trigger area use the same interaction and are right on top of each other, making it very easy to grab the bolt again after cycling instead of the trigger.* ...and many moreThese are solved ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ problems people, just look at pavlov. They aren't a result of limited budget, just poor decisions. Hopefully they fix these issues, the game seems like it could be interesting

The balance of the missions feel a little inconsistent.  Some of them are simple and easy to get through, others are a little more challenging.The story itself is not engaging, I find the gameplay with each mission is what keeps you there, not necessarily the story itself as to why you are going through the missions.
