_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like reading a book or watching a really wonderful sci fi movie.Music is engaging and some times the imagery is breathtaking.I am not going to comment the gamepley etc, apart from the fact that really deep exploration is needed in order to finish the game...At some points i got stuck not knowing where to look for the next clue. My advice: don't get spoiled, just keep looking and pay attention to the details, it all makes sense in the end. All the answers are in the ship log.Also your tool (scout) is mandatory :pThis game is an exploration masterpiece. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: You can lift-off a planet in your spaceship in search of unsolved mysteries, fill out your oxygen tank with trees on the moon, follow the sounds to strange places, search for dead civilizations... it has the eerie feeling of subnautica with no crafting and so far not too much stress. This game captivates you and keeps you engaged in the story and its mystery. I strongly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Completion Status: 100% achievements (At the time of writing this there is some achievements that are unobtainable due to the DLC not being released yet.)Outer Wilds is a space exploration game that will have you as the pilot of spacecraft exploring your galaxy learning the history of ancient race known as the Nomai. Their mark can be seen throughout the solar system and now, for the first time, one of your kind is setting to the skies equipped with a translation tool. With this in your arsenal the story begins. The Good: - An amazing story- Exploration is rewarding - World is lively and changes as you play- Puzzles are challengingThe Bad:- Possible to shortcut leaving to confusion- Some puzzles require waiting- Character can end up spinning against your will as you fumble in zero gravity  The music heard within Outer Wilds is lovely as it is functional. On most planets will reside another traveler and they are each equipped with their own instrument, which can be handing in figuring out where in the galaxy a certain planet is. There is also an achievement for listening to all the travelers at once. Besides the music your audio will vary depending on where you find yourself situated which only further allows you to get immersed in this galaxy, but this only lasts for so long as a game defining piece will cue and after hearing this the first time you will know..When exploring the galaxy I was happy to say that i never got bored seeing what each planet had to offer. No two where alike as the world design area brought something new to the table. The world will dynamically change around you and sometimes you may be too late to even experience something! The game offers top tier world building while looking well polished as everything looked like it belonged. Get ready to read! This game's lore is centered around you exploring with the newly created translation tool. This is a tool that allows you to translate any of the found Nomai writing text (which there is a lot). Despite the game having zero spoken dialogue I was genuinely captivating to read their story as none of the text found was ever completely useless and all served a greater purpose. As a new explorer of the Galaxy you'll need a way to traverse from planet to planet. With this need your given your very own spaceship which will serve as your home base for all explorations. The ship itself took a bit to get it down on flying properly but once you got it down you'll be zooming from planet to planet with ease. The ship serves a vital part to your explorations as it housed your space suit and accompanying gear. The ship is also outfitted with an auto pilot, but just be warned it may not be the smartest. While exploring the Outer Wilds you'll come across some problems collecting certain important information and it's up to you on figuring out how you'll obtain said information. The puzzles always felt rewarding after completion as you'll receive a large lore dump, and the have a new place to start searching for more clues.  All 'quests' can be found in the terminal on your ship through the Rumor tab as it will display where you may wanna keep exploring or offer new locations to check out. This game is all about exploration and finding things out yourself so there really isn't a main quest that the game is pointing you towards. Once you start to explore then you'll know where to go or at least have an idea. The game's difficult resides within your problem solving skills and how well you can piece information together. There is never any real input heavy moments as everything is pretty lenient. The challenges all come from the puzzles and most of them just require patience. There is a good amount of achievements in Outer Wilds and they all game me a reason to try things I normally wouldn't think of trying, A perfect example is the (non-hidden) achievement to fly the model rocket you find in the stat or the game into your home planets moon which is a fun achievement that has you do something out of the ordinary. None of them are to hard to get either! As of writing this review there is a good amount of unachievable achievements as they seem to have been released early ahead of the rumored upcoming DLC.  After you have finished the main game there isn't that much to keep playing for. I did find myself spending an extra couple of hours in the game after completion grinding for achievement which provided me with a fair amount of replay value. Outside of completing the achievements the game doesn't offer really anything else once finished. Outer Wilds has struck a very soft spot in my heart. This space exploration game is more than it looks as there's a lot at work here and all you gotta do is start uncovering the truths. And these truths are best left for personal discovery so hopefully your able to hop into the Outer Wilds and make your own findings.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game revolving around space, heck, the sci-fi genre as a whole, if I can exaggerate.But I have been incredibly passionate about this game since I got it on sale a few weeks back, and honestly, I wish I could've paid full price for this game, because it truly is worth every penny.Outer Wilds tackles a genre that I love, and takes most of the time place in a setting that I love; this game basically feels like a love letter to games revolving around space and the vast universe out there. _childDocuments_.review: This is my first true review of anything so please forgive any imperfections. I honestly do not know if this is my favorite game ever. I finished it about an hour ago and was not sure how to accurately convey my feelings into words. I have a great understanding of the science that the game utilizes to play its story, and Mobius does as well. This is one of the first games that I have played completely blind and being able to discover all that i did was so rewarding. The best part about all of the exploration and discovery is the fact that the game does not give either to you. Once you reach a certain point, (about 10-20 minutes into the game) you are completely on your own. I have played and completed every FromSoft games so I am no stranger to no direction. The difference here is that where dark souls Does not tell you where to go, The Outer Wilds gives you EVERYWHERE to go. You are able to go to many places in Dark Souls, but there is usually only between 1-3 "correct" paths. The player is able to go anywhere they like in the solar system and they will progress. Also, Do not assume me to be a Souls hater (I only say this because the souls community can be brutal). DS 1 2 and 3 as well as BB are in my top ten games of all time. They just need to find out how to share the space with The outer Wilds. I even began with the fact that I am not sure how much I like it. However, the more I speak about the game the more I like it. My favorite part is that although I just recently beat the story and have explored what I think to be ALMOST everything else, in the game, I want to go back to explore all that I have started and anything else i have not seen. I personally believe that although there MAY be imperfections to this game, every single game developer out there needs to spend time to 100% complete this game so they can see what the standard should be no matter what.Please respond with any constructive comments so that I may improve my review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games of all time. But it's not for everyone.Some people enjoy games for the story/lore and how it affects them on an emotional level.Other people simply want fun gameplay mechanics and things to do.And there's mixtures of both. This is primarily a story/lore game that functions like an 'escape room'. If you've ever done an escape room before, you know that there's no point in doing the same room again. You already know the solution. That's why people say you must play this game blind. The core of this game is essentially solving a giant escape room puzzle while piecing together the story. So if you know any parts of it beforehand, it will take away from the feeling of discovery and problem solving.Don't play this expecting extremely in depth survival mechanics.DO play this if you like space flight, physics, science, exploring abandoned places, etc.Music is also pretty great.

_childDocuments_.review: So this review would be a side thumb, however since Steam is forcing an up or down on me I'll go for the down. If you like atrocious riddles with almost no hints and to find out literally EVERYTHING for yourself you can skip my review and buy the game, this is for you.The game looks really good, the planets are unique and it's filled with good ideas, mechanics and "wow" moments. The story itself is not that bad either, what IS bad however are the "riddles". Nobody tells you what exactly your goal is in this game. There are no quest markers, nothing. Just hints after hints which are so small that you can easily miss them and it's not very engaging. You'll read most of the stuff that you can find in this game and after some time it dawns on you what you have to do. But how to do it? Nobody will tell you. So you walk around the planets, find some stuff and think to yourself "cool, I gathered everything and I finally know what to do! But how do I do it?" Nobody tells you! There's people out there that will tell you that this game is finishable without a guide but it's really not. NO SPOILER AHEAD. To finish this game you need to step on X during the right timing of Y but nobody tells you where X is and when Y happens. (And that's only the first thing of other things that you have to do in a fixed timespan. You died? Guess what, start over!) That's why I cannot recommend this game, which is sad because overall the game is very unique and cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds isn't just a game; it's a breathtaking odyssey that transcends the boundaries of the gaming world. From the very first moment I strapped on my space suit and took my first shaky steps on Timber Hearth, I knew I was in for something truly extraordinary.Unforgettable Exploration: One of the most captivating aspects of Outer Wilds is its vast, beautifully crafted solar system. As a curious Hearthian astronaut, you'll have the chance to explore every nook and cranny of this intricately designed cosmos. Each celestial body holds its own mysteries, puzzles, and stories waiting to be unraveled. From the eerie interstellar graveyard of Hollow's Lantern to the serene beauty of Giant's Deep, every location is a work of art.Time-Loop Mastery: The game's ingenious time-loop mechanic is its crowning achievement. With a 22-minute time limit before the sun goes supernova, every cycle is a race against time. The urgency adds a layer of tension that keeps you engaged, but it also encourages experimentation. Each failed attempt unveils a little more of the intricate web of secrets, pushing you further down the rabbit hole.Narrative Brilliance: The storytelling in Outer Wilds is nothing short of masterful. Through notes, dialogues, and environmental storytelling, you gradually piece together the history of your civilization, the Nomai, and the impending cosmic catastrophe. It's an emotional rollercoaster that will leave you in awe and contemplation.Soundtrack and Atmosphere: The hauntingly beautiful soundtrack by Andrew Prahlow perfectly complements the game's atmosphere, immersing you in the sense of wonder and isolation that space exploration entails. The sound design, too, is impeccable, from the hum of your spaceship's engines to the eerie sounds of alien technology.Philosophical Depth: Outer Wilds is more than just a game; it's a philosophical journey that ponders the mysteries of existence, the impermanence of time, and our place in the universe. It leaves you with profound questions and a newfound appreciation for the cosmos.In conclusion, Outer Wilds is not just my favorite game; it's a transcendent experience that has left an indelible mark on my gaming journey. Its blend of exploration, storytelling, and philosophical depth makes it a true masterpiece. If you haven't embarked on this cosmic adventure yet, I implore you to do so. It's a game that will stay with you long after the credits roll, and it's a journey you won't want to end.

_childDocuments_.review: "The best game nobody can tell you anything about. If you like sci-fi, you'll love this game. No more information needed - which is good, given that this is the most spoiler-influenced game in existence. Just ... buy and play this game. Now. Stop reading this. Just go buy it!My only complaint with this game is that it is rather short for its price (18.2 hours as you can see). But there is more fun and love packed into this little game than any AAA game out there to date."This was the review I wrote after first finishing Outer Wilds - before the DLC came out, before covid, and before I had become the person I am today. And as I reminisce about that fact, I often realise that I only am - the person that I am - because of Outer Wilds. Without exaggeration, in three years, not a day has gone by where I haven't thought about this game and the message it left me with..I won't hide it - this is largely a personal experience (it always is, just look at the other reviews), and Outer Wilds came at the absolute perfect time, for it's absolute perfect target audience. Still, I say without exaggeration that this game changed the way I look at the universe and the way I interact with the world present around me. This is, in large part, because Outer Wilds is a game about the passage of time - the store page says that much - and despite being a game about a time loop, the message this game leaves you with is that you can never go back to the past - and that's to be embraced. Some things will only ever live on in our memory, and even those we forget are still felt - in the rustling of leaves, in trees they once planted, whose shade they knew they would never be rewarded with themselves. When a game like this ends, you know inevitably that the characters are "dead" - no more dialogue to explore, no more replayability to enjoy. They, too, only live in your memory, and deep in files you'll already be over-familiar with if you come home to visit. As such, I felt a small part of my soul die with them, and I think back on it every day.But I can never return to the Wilds. None of us can, and that's okay. Such are the wishes of innocence, and I oft think of my childhood as having ended with this game's finale. I was raised as a woman of science, and a stout atheist, but this game changed that for me - and gave me purpose where I'd never found any before. I could say far, far more, but I'll spare you. Play this game. Don't look anything up. You ... won't, in all likelihood, have the same experience as me, but we'll both be there after it ends. Maybe then, you and me can toast marshmellows over a campfire on some wild and unexplored planet of our own, stranger :;)
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Hello and welcome to my Outer Wilds review!Firstly, this game is absolutely brilliant. I have to admit that I don't lean towards 'exploration' when thinking of my favourite games, and admittedly I was frustrated at times, but seeing the praise this got, and all the 2019 award nods, I knew I had to try it - and boy am I glad that I did. I literally smashed this out in 2 days - my weekend flew by.So, to scratch it off, I'm not huge on exploration games without guidance (I like to think my in-game time is optimised and not dilly-dallying in the wrong direction). So to be up-front; I did use a walk-through for a significant part of my game-time (evident by the small amount of game time I spent to complete it). For me personally, it didn't take much away - if anything I got to experience the wonders of Outer Wilds when I otherwise wouldn't have. If exploration is your thing, and you have the time to trial-and-error your way across this solar system, then you're in for a real treat and will likely get even more than I did out of it (and I'm already telling you this game is the business).Outer Wilds (in-game) is a humble wee space program operated by your charming, and musically gifted, alien race living in a small solar system (planets give off a real King Kai planet vibe (DBZ reference lol)). From very early on you are given free reign of this system to explore as you see fit. For all those wondering where to go there are serious hints you can pick up while exploring the planet you start on (Timber Hearth) which ultimately acts as a tutorial level giving you information on all the different equipment, and the very purpose of Outer Wilds.This is essentially the basis for the story telling - as you discover more things, the game will nudge you in the desired direction by dropping names of other planets, etc, in text logs you find. Again, you can literally go where you please at any given time, but you might not know enough about where you are, or about what you're doing, to make the most out of your time there - and it's this approach to game progression which is honestly something to praise. Whereas any other game might give you an item after defeating boss, which would unlock a door you've encountered previously but couldn't get past, the hypothetical door in Outer Wilds is always able to be opened - you just might not know how to open it yet. Effectively this means you could complete the game in 22 minutes (how specific, wink wink) if you immediately went to the locations required to access the end-game - but the whole point is you're discovering information which leads to your progression. They've absolutely crushed incorporating the narrative as the driving force of this game. Truly next level - a real benchmark in the realm of narrative-driven gaming.I won't spoil anything for anyone looking through reviews wondering whether to pick this up. Very little can be said about the planets, and the mystery, that wouldn't ultimately belittle the impact unless you experienced it first-hand. But it's good. Real good.

_childDocuments_.review: You may fly into the sun a couple times, blow your ship up, and you'll definitely get incinerated in a violent and beautiful stellar explosion more than a few times. Outer Wilds is a hand-crafted exploration experience that marries your intuition and sense of wonder in such a unique way, and I can't recommend it enough. Visually amazing, the art style lends itself superbly to the colorful and varied worlds that the game has you search across. The soundtrack and musical motif is understated and phenomenal, punctuating feelings of curiosity and finality. The gameplay is simple, but the game teaches you to use these simple mechanics in new ways that send you deeper into the mystery. The only negative I can think of is that it had to end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special.Every part of it is something incredible. The tiny solar system is beautiful, and each planet is more unique than I could have imagined. The feeling of wonder and discovery you get exploring the solar system time and time again never gets old. The ship is a blast to fly, and the music is phenomenal. I still listen to the soundtrack on spotify from time to time. The "time loop" feature, while not a new idea, is executed perfectly and gives just enough time to do a few things per loop.This game is the best mystery story I have ever played, watched, read, or experienced. I (obviously) won't go into details, but you NEED to play this game to completion. It is absolutely incredible. I could not recommend this game more.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game after 26 hours and I think it truly is a fantastic game.I really wanted to beat the game without using any sort of guide or walkthrough (basically because I didn't want any spoilers)... but I ended up having to look for some hints at some points. The world (I mean, the solar system) is so open that you can get the information in so many different ways that it may be really difficult to connect all the dots to finally reach the end of the game. Even with the rumor map (which I loved) I was not able to do it.I think my only complaints have to do with the translation. I played the game in Spanish, but it switched to English in some dialogues, and some of the Nomai scripts sounded weird.Regarding other aspects of the game, the 22-minute cycle might be annoying at some points (specially when you are about to discover something crucial and you start hearing ).  I read some people complaining about the controls, but I played with a controller and it was really easy to get used to it.The ending was incredible. I was so much into it that I didn't notice that I played through it with my mouth open. Really weird ending, but somewhat satisfying...Can't wait to play the DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having extremely mixed feelings about this one. It's super original. It's full of mystery, great soundtrack, cute world... But I couldn't finish it, because the frustration simply overhelmed me.It's essentially a walking simulator. Explore ruins of an advanced civilization and try to find out what happened and more importantly, why are you stuck in a timeloop (and why most others aren't aware of it). Decyphered texts and events you run into are recorded in a ship's log, slowly building up a complete picture of the mystery. There's a lot of really cool ideas, some light puzzle elements, the mystery is really captivating. So why negative verdict?You run to your ship, you lift off, you fly to a planet, rummage around, find something interesting and accidentally die. So you run to your ship, lift off, fly to the planet, try to find out how you've got to that interesting place again and eventually die. The idea of repeatedly dying, restarting where you left and going on is deeply ingrained into the game and I'm just sick of it, because half of the time, instead of exploring the interesting stuff, I'm running to the ship, lifting off, enganging autopilot, putting on spacesuit.It was barely bearable till about maybe 80% into the game, where every trip meant another mystery. The game -is- rich and really fascinating. But by the the end, a lot of expeditions were "run to ship, lift off, engange autopilot, put on suit, rummage around, die, learn nothing" (is it starting to irk you when I repeat the process over and over? now imagine having to play it over and over)In many cases I ended up reaching to walkthrough, because the game is fairly harsh and doesn't exactly tell you what to do. So you try approaching an electric jellyfish and it fries you ship. You try approach a jellyfish without your ship and it kills you. You check walkthrough and learn that you were pretty much doing it right, but you need a bit of luck to slip between tentacles. Run to your ship, lift off, engange autopilot, put on suit, die and then go through the same process again, trying basically the same thing, just in case that this time you don't die. No, thanks.Eventually I just found the story online. It's a great story (even though I admit I was hoping its various aspects are intervined more tightly than they were). I admit that just reading it without the immersion wouldn't have nearly the effect playing it does. But at some point I decided that endlessly running to your ship, taking off, enganging autopilot, putting on a suit and dying isn't worth it for me anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: This review will do nothing to hinder the game as it has great reviews so I'm sorry to have an unpopular opinion.  First of all, if you get dizzy easily or are doing any kind of substance (smoking or drinking) playing this -- speaking from experiance -- it is not the best combination for this type of game.  That being said, I do have some legitimate gripes...The first being the learning curve.  Now I know I only have about 2 hours in this game but you would think that would be enough time to learn the controls right?  No...2 hours into this game and I still spiral out of control anytime I even so much as try to turn at faster than anything 5 mph.  I do like how you have other people to talk to (NPCs) on different planets and its cool running into them but I don't really see much of a direction of story in talking to them. Im giving this game a thumbs down just because its kind of boring.  If you're not really good at flying around/maneuverability type of games.  Now I know people are probably like (well did you even research the game) I saw what steam had, they made it look more fun then it actually was...I can see why some would like this, but for me outside of not knowing how to fly, I just found it pretty redative and painfully boring...If you don't have patience....this game is not for you **raises hand**
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: (There might be a few spoilers in this review: hopefully not too many)I first learned about this game through some of my friends. I thought I might get bored fast due to Outer Wilds being a more lore-focused game, but after playing it was able to have a much bigger impact on me than if I was not fully paying attention. The idea that everything and anything can be important to help you understand what exactly to do next in the game helped me fully focus on the game and understand the story that was taking place in the outer wilds of Timber Hearth. Each planet has its own life to it, that being both lore-wise and the flora and fauna. Every planet also has its own feeling while exploring and while waiting for the right time to properly explore different parts of different planets. One example is the hourglass twins The Ash Twin and The Ember Twin, as for The Ember Twin you have to be quick to explore everything before the sand fills the planet, and for The Ash Twin you have to start waiting for all the sand to become sucked up by The Ember Twin. One of the best parts of Outer Wilds is how you can learn by actually paying attention to the game (Lore Spoiler)   Another amazing thing is the soundtrack. (Small Spoiler)  Overall, the game and its story was a wonderful experience that I wish I could do again without knowing what happens in the game and I'm so happy I was able to experience this game with such little spoilers towards the story and lore. You should buy this game and experience the whole game without looking anything up or being taught how to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely intriguing story hampered by stupid platforming. Would have LOVED this game without the arcade platforming. I know exactly what I need to do, and youtube confirms it, but I simply can't do the jump right and each try takes 5 minutes. Don't buy unless you like platforming and are good at it. (Make no mistake, the little bit of the story I've seen so far is actually very good)
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: It is incredibly hard to write positive reviews for this game, because it is entirely possible for a positive review to ruin aspects of the game for someone. If at any point during this review you go "Ok, I'm sold!" stop reading.Outer Wilds is a game about discovery, creativity, and gathering information. Progression is not achieved through powerups or permanent upgrades. Progression is achieved by learning. Therefor, the more you learn from outside sources, the less game you have to play. Please, just jump into this game. If you are looking at the reviews for this game, then you are most likely the kind of person who wants to play a game like this. You've probably been yearning for a game like this without knowing it. This is a game with heart, a game that makes you think and feel and laugh. This is a game that is so incredibly distanced from the horrendous trends of recent games. This isn't an online shooter that will make you feel bad within 5 minutes of playing it. This isn't a game specifically designed the same way casinos are. This isn't a mindless and more expensive port of a game that had already stood the test of time. This is Outer Wilds. This game will put you through an emotional journey, it will make you a part of its story, and despite all of us having the same world to explore, your path through the world will be different from everyone else's.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games I've ever played. This game is so interesting because you do not progress through getting power ups or new abilities but through obtaining knowledge about the universe. From the beginning of the the game you can immediately beat it. You just have to explore the world collecting clues in order to do so. For this reason, if you are planning on playing the game, you should try and avoid spoilers like the plague.Aside from the unique concept, this game has a wonderful art style, soundtrack, and characters. The environments are legitimately interesting to explore. This game tests your understanding of space, time, and the nature of the universe. I don't remember the last time I was so engrossed by a video game. Would one hundred percent recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A topic most reviews don't touch on.  The incredible sense of accomplishment and pride you feel when overcoming an obstacle and reaping the rewards of a discovery you made with no guidance, just you, is enough reason to buy this incredible work of art.Truly a profound, heartfelt, and thoughtful experience.  If this game even slightly peaks your interest, buy it.  No need to read anymore, just buy it and avoid any information on it like the plague.  As everyone else says, the best possible experience you can get out of this game, and trust me you want that, is to go in as blind as possible.  If you're still reading allow me to present more to you.  Everyone talks about the amazing and captivating story of this game.  But I don't see many talk about the primary detail that makes this game so special.  This is in essence an exploration / mystery game, but unlike others in 1 key way.  The mystery in others such as the Sherlock Holmes games or questions in other game genres that invoke in us a desperate desire to know the answer, tend to guide you.  Whether a lot or just nudging you in the right direction they help you in some way.  Not this game.  If you've ever played a puzzle game, Portal for instance, and been stuck on a puzzle for a while, when you get that "AHA" moment and you finally figure it out is a great feeling of accomplishment.  You figured it out on your own.  You didn't have help.  You didn't look it up.  You solved the problem yourself.  There are many opportunities for that in this game, and man they are sweet.  Whether its how to solve a problem, or a piece of the puzzle you haven't found yet, or a piece you have and just haven't thought of, when it suddenly comes to you and it works.  It feels as if you're a researcher whose finally discovered the answer to a problem they've been struggling with for years.  Maybe not a great comparison, but you get the idea.  The sense of accomplishment alone is enough to warrant buying this incredible game.  And at the end, you'll just sit back for a quiet moment and take a deep breath, as the game has just taken it away.

_childDocuments_.review: Cherish with caution, it is one of these games where the experience can only be had once and then it's in your head forever, ironically it can't be replayed. But please don't wait or shy away, you would miss out, it will be 70 hours of f***ing around and finding stuff out and it is such an awesome joyride. Laugh at me all you want but the OST DLC is a must buy, so is Echoes of the Eye which adds perspective to why stuff happened the way it did.You are a little Hearthian, from the microplanet Amber Hearth. Today is you first day as an astronaut, your ship is ready, time to become an explorer. There is a moon, a sun, and a bunch of other microplanets in your small solar system which aren't fully explored, be the first, observe history. You get the launch codes, hop in your humble spaceship, engines thrust, lift-off, full throttle, you misjudged it, you are going to fly full speed into the sun. This is it, a split second of fear and everything turns white. You see a strange face, you feel something weird, you wake up near the launch pad, screaming. Today is your first day as an astronaut, your ship is ready, time to become an explorer. What the f***ing ♥♥♥♥, I just died, what happpened?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly the best - if not one of the best - game(s) I've ever played.The mechanics & game world are fantastic, the music is sweet to your ears, and the storyline is fun to follow all the way through, with unexpected twists & a beautiful conclusion.It's a game that makes you rethink your thoughts on death, and I think it can easily change your perception on the 'everyday' so to speak.I absolutely positively could not recommend this enough, it was not entirely what I thought it was before I bought it, and it turned out to be more that I could have possibly guessed.Also: Please, do yourself a favour - play this one without watching/reading gameplay first. The less you know about this game the better it will be.This game is about exploration, companionship, life & death, and puzzling, and I would play it again from a fresh start if possible in a heartbeat.

_childDocuments_.review: I can say without hyperbole that this is one of the best games every made.  This is the kind of game that inspires others to create their own.Going into this game not knowing what to expect is truly a unique experience.  Finding all the hidden information, following the clues littered across the solar system, finally figuring out what is causing the loops and what it all means.  Discovering the Nomai's history, getting to know them via their recorded conversations, learning about their hopes, fears, triumphs, disasters and tragic end.  Meeting the other travelers, figuring out what makes them tick, and why they, like you, headed to the stars.  The awe inspiring sights of the sand pouring from one planet to another, planetary cyclones, a crumbling planet with a black hole at the center, and the feelings of dread inspired by the Dark Bramble and it's the denizens who lurk there.And on top of all that amazingness of fantastic design and excellent writing, you have a towering technical achievement.  Things happen regardless of where you are in the solar system.  Traveling from one planet to another, or one area to another is always seamless.  You can go from tearing around space in your ship to crawling through caves deep within a planet to warping to an entirely different planet all within a few minutes and never have that feeling of immersion broken.You will not regret getting this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Superb art direction alongside an amazing OST. I can't say much about the story without spoiling it, if you enjoy exploration and some mystery solving — chances are you are going to like it. However, it's not for everyone, and if you're the sort that gets frustrated easily over failure  and has a hard time figuring things out without much guidance, and gets annoyed by it, make your purchase carefully. Even so, I think the probability of regret is low.  There were a few moments I had to look away from the screen due to how bright they were and the vehicle is going to spin if you hit things violently.Get the DLC too and I recommend that you only play it after finishing the base game. Very important.I don't really consume much space-related media since usually I find it too bland , and thanks to that I have a limited repertoire to compare it to, but I really like their approach to the technology of an alien civilization. It's advanced, yet it doesn't feel too exaggerated or intangible, its rules are clear and followed and they aren't some sort of god. The existence of a solid culture is clearly visible and it never felt flat for me. The way the Hearthians are rustic is nice and once you hear the soundtrack during your gameplay you'll understand how much thought was put into everything. It's something simple, perhaps not even difficult to achieve, but seeing this much care put into a game is extremely refreshing.Again, there's not much that can be said without spoiling things, but if you like works with absolutely no humans and great creature design  — with some anatomical details easily available to see and think of how they work on your own, if you are interested in it just like me — I recommend it. I found the friends really nice. They're great. I like their outfits and the small variations within the same species.The exploration aspect is really fun and there's a lot to see. When it comes to driving, at first you might find it a little complicated but all you have to do is have patience. Don't rush things. Each planet was carefully designed and all have a nice sense of novelty, so don't be afraid to take things at your own pace — You'll probably find yourself stopping to simply appreciate the scenery and certain moments. The graphics are impressive. The usage of colors is amazing, they're not too saturated, but not too dead either. That combined with the music and the story is something that'll stick with you for a while.Outer Wilds has a lot to offer, and it's something you can only truly experience once, so make the best out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is difficult to not have spoiled. _childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: The closest game I can think of to this game is Breath of The Wild, in the sense that exploration feels rewarding for the sake of exploration. Once the training wheels are off, you have an entire small (but dense!) solar system to explore and figure out, in a gameplay loop so addictive this game has practically kidnapped me. One of my favorite games this year, maybe even the best. If you're interested in exploration and don't mind reading (mostly chat logs, no essays or anything), I would recommend this game in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: 10 / 10 amazing.I haven't played a game that really made me look forward to the next session like this in a long time. Everything comes together perfectly. Great music, solid gameplay and physics, very satisfying exploration of the world and learning new things, and no load times. Some things are a bit obtuse to figure out, but really the game gives you a whole lot of clues for pretty much every major thing you have to find. One thing I really wish I had known before I started was this isn't the type of game where you unlock new equipment or power ups. I initially thought if I couldn't get to a certain area I would unlock it later or something, like in a Metroidvania.Really the only negative was performance, it performed very poorly at a comparable resolution  / detail to other games. I had to reduce the resolution / detail a lot.

_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm listening to the soundtrack for this game for the umpteenth time while studying and decided, you know, high time to write a review.This game is magnificent. You already knew that, all the other Overwhelmingly Positive reviews already know that, honestly you're probably reading this review as like a post-game validation since you've already beaten it and just want to gush about it with other people. Trying to explain this game to my friends is hilarious because it's always just--bro I can't. The universe explodes every 22 minutes and you're a little dude flying around in a spaceship doing whatever you want. It's whimsical, it's tragic, it's tense, it's slow, it's smart, it's beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: The core mystery is kind of interesting, and I credit that the game has value.  But it's just not interesting enough to deal with the "walking around" simulator.  There are a few puzzles, but nothing that feels really rewarding to solve.  There are some ancient texts to decide, but nothing profound. I've played 13 hours now and I've explored several locations, but I still don't know what I'm actually trying to accomplish.  Mostly it seems like a "point and click" type story game, but with the added difficulty of running from place to place.  And if you miss a jump (all to easy to do since the walking controls are pretty poor) you have to start all over again.The idea of a roguelike with no enemies is interesting, but I want to unlock something - open a door that stays open, purchase some perks for my character or... something.  As it is, I start every loop no farther along than the last time.  In Dark Souls at least you're building muscle memory and combat skills.  In Outer Wilds there is no combat.  There are no unlockables.  There is no progress.  You just... start again.It's not terrible.  There's intrigue here, and I've enjoyed discovering more about the central mystery of the game.  Maybe I'll come back to it.But the game play itself just isn't very engaging.  There are no enemies and no puzzles to speak of.  The controls are frustratingly amateurish, and there's no way to improve your starting conditions.  No shortcuts, no perks, no save points, no fast travel.Navigate to a location, explore it, check it off the list. Recommended instead:     The Signal From Tolva     The Talos Principle     The Turing Test

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds is a game that's definitely worth checking out.Here's some of my thoughts on the game:Good Things:- Amazing feeling of exploration | Mini Solar System gives you the whole world to explore; you'll never be disappointed in how vast the reachable world is- Plot | Honestly one of the best stories I've experienced recently. It's fascinating and very well written; no details are missing.- The idea | Though loop mechanics are not new to gaming, here it just feels different. There's something about the world that's always alive without you.- Music | OST is well spread through the game; it's only there to emphasize the important moments, and the music is great.- Visuals | Though there's no edge-cutting graphics overall, the game looks beautiful, and everything fits the style of it- Navigation | Ship HUD, map, ship logs, and the tools make the gameplay very smooth and improve the walkthrough a lot- Puzzles | Most of the puzzles are very well made; they require thinking outside the box and using every tool you can find and the environment itself to solve themBad Things (spoilers!):- Ending | To me it felt somewhat flat with too much supernatural force involved; it felt the opposite of the highly detailed and technical plot that the game introduces before the end- Puzzles | While most of the puzzles are good, some of them felt awkward and misleading, like the forge on Brittle Hollow that makes you feel like you are doing something wrong trying to reach it while the entrance is not related to the elevator at all or the part of the same planet that you can access only by waiting for it to crash into a black hole, and the place with cacti on Hour Glass felt more like the hover pack challenge than the puzzle. Another example of misleading things for me was a very important part of the game: Nomai Ship. I explored Dark Brumble a lot, but looking at the ship using a scout didn't make me feel that it's something that can be reached and felt more like a reference than the core game location- Level Design | Some of the planets have a huge amount of underground systems that might be confusing at times, especially when playing a game with pauses between the play sessions. Going there repeatedly and trying to explore everything might be discouraging sometimes. Also, it felt like there were the fewest clues as to how to get to the hardest-to-reach locations.- Some Game Mechanics | Meditation and the map for the suite were surprise mechanics that I found only by the end of the game by chance; they are quite important, and it's a pity that developers didn't make them more obvious by putting them somewhere between some random lines of dialoguePersonally I love the game, but some of the details that I described made me love it less. That said, I think the DLC feels more mature and fixes most of the problems I had with the base game.I'm done with the game and DLC, but I will miss this tiny world waiting to be explored.

_childDocuments_.review: We had a good year for games in 2019, and I feel like this one may have flown under the radar for many. It is first and foremost a puzzle game. If you arent into the Mysts, Witness, Antechamber, Portal, etc., type games - this may not be for you. If you ARE into puzzlers this one has a lot of heart and soul that goes beyond the generic "you are stuck in someplace and need to figure your way out." You have no antagonistic agent or "villain" or "entity" pursuing you in this little solar system. The system you are locked into is on a timer, and you are mostly trying to beat said clock in an effort to stop the system from exploding every 30 min with no one really understanding why they are in this infinite loop.As you delve deeper you discover more and more about the lore of each planet, and of those who came before you, in an effort to understand why this is all happening and perhaps how to stop it.There is plenty here that is common in the puzzle game genre. But there is also a lot more that they bring to the table fresh.Story/Lore: 10Music/Atmosphere: 10Controls: 9 (getting used to the orbital mechanic of some planets and flying the spaceship has a bit of a curve)Gameplay: 8*Visuals/Graphic: Unique - 8Overall: 9/10*Caveat: The game can more and more tedious as it drags on. The looming supernovae which constantly resets your progress becomes less of an interesting mechanic - and more of an added challenge to try and remember what you havent done, or where you havent been before and trying to get there quickly. With some puzzles being a trial and error it can be a real drain on your interest in the late game. Dont be discourage, the game can in fact be beaten well within the time they've provided you. However, near the very end of the game I found one "puzzle" which had me totally hosed. I looked it up and had no idea where I would have learned how to access this area. It may have been in the 100s of notes/logs you pick up that I probably didnt internalize properly. This is the reason for the other -1 point in gameplay (in addition to the repetition). I dont think there was enough visual cues, or hints, for me to ever have found this area on my own.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do we even begin? The player character that controls like a ragdoll in a hurricane? The physics system that genuinely just doesn't work? The ship that bounces around the planets like a pinball? Or maybe that "ancient alien texts" to uncover that read like your thirteen year old nephew's creative writing project. I've spent a few hours with the game now, and I have to say that I don't understand what the joke is. Am I playing a different game than everyone else? Or is this like people ironically posting positive reviews on metacritic? The music that cycles through the same three banjo songs quickly becomes incredibly grating, the 22 minute time loop does little more than make you feel like you've wasted your last half hour of gameplay, and the designers seem to have forgotten about the concept of an atmosphere or momentum conservation, because half the time you jump, the planet just... keeps moving without you. That's right, if you jump directly upwards, you're probably going to come down somewhere else. Is this some component of a symbolic experience? Or is it just poor game design? Either way, I've played day one Bethesda games less broken than this.

_childDocuments_.review: (It says I haven't played for very long, but that's because I originally bought and played it on the Epic store. I bought it again on Steam just to support the devs.)I'm not a professional game critic by any means, but I play a lot of videogames, and Outer Wilds is a . I do not use that term lightly, but this game deserves it. Outer Wilds displays an excellence in game design that puts most AAA blockbuster games to shame. Striking environmental design, impeccable writing and storytelling, simple but effective game mechanics, and a phenomenal soundtrack that will send chills down your spine.Unfortunately, by it's very nature as an exploration-driven, story-focused puzzle game, it is difficult to actually talk about this game in any detail without spoiling it. Have you ever played a story-driven game where you wish you could wipe your memory and play it for the first time again? Outer Wilds is that kind of game. However, Outer Wilds is not a game for the impatient, and it's not going to work for everyone. The story and exploration of this little slice of cosmos has to engage you enough to want to continue, because the story and exploration is the only reward. If you want combat and action, this isn't that kind of game.  If you want a game with endless hours of replay value, this isn't that game. If you want a hand-holding linear story experience, this isn't really that kind of game either, because the story is told through exploration of an open world, and you can piece it together in any order (although it does give clues to nudge you towards important locations). It's a game that rewards taking it at your own pace and letting yourself get invested in the world.If what you've seen of this game through the screenshots and Steam description looks cool, and you're on the fence about getting it...let me push you onto the greener side of that fence, because Outer Wilds is a one-of-a-kind experience, and it's a top-three contender for my favorite game of the past decade.

_childDocuments_.review: This is now my favourite game ever, I think. I cannot praise it enough, and I cannot insist enough that everyone who reads this must play the game. The less you can know about this game before you play it, the better. Just strap in for 20 - 30 hours of adventure and mystery. I promise it's worth the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds is a fascinating journey into the unknown, accompanied by striking visuals and a memorable soundtrack. Once you get the hang of the spaceship's controls, hopping from planet to planet in search of knowledge is incredibly engaging. The game does not force you to solve one puzzle after the other - curiosity naturally guides you to the right places, making you feel like an explorer piecing together the secret of the universe. While I love the boldness of the time loop concept, it was also source of many frustrations for me. Hard resetting a puzzle game after 22 minutes can feel unnecessarily punishing, especially when certain events only happen at certain times, which meant a lot of waiting and repetitive gameplay for me. Nevertheless, I deeply appreciate the game as a whole; it tells a story of the desire to understand what's out there, the unsettling realisation of the vastness of the universe, and the confrontation of forces we can barely reach, and even less understand
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: In all my years of gaming, I have never played a game quite like The Outer Wilds and I doubt that I'll ever play another game that impacted me as much as this game did.I played this for the very first time at the beginning of this year/end of last year and completed it a few weeks after starting. Despite technically completing this game, I have thought about it almost every day since and I even jump back in it sometimes for space shenanigans or to just vibe and roast marshmallows in front of the campfires throughout the planets while listening to the incredible soundtrack.Not only is this an open world game, it is an open solar system game! Any planet or celestial body you see can be landed on and explored completely. If the idea of exploring an entire solar system with no loading screens, piloting your own spaceship, learning what happened to the sentient alien species that came before you, and uncovering the secrets of your solar system sounds good to you then you'll be in for a good time with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: I was bored the first hour. Amazed the next 5 - 7 hours. A little confused / bored again after that.As long as you're exploring these amazing worlds it's super engaging. But solving the puzzle in the end was a bit underwhelming as I don't feel  had clear clues.Think I had a better time reflecting / thinking about the game than playing it sometimes.Will not be for everyone. Don't be fooled by this being a 'must play', it does require you to take your time, and it might not click with you.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most fulfilling exploration games that I have ever played in my life. I started loving it when I had my first "Aha!" moment, and wanted to find out more and more and more. I could not recommend this game more to anybody who is even slightly interested in the exploration genre.Be prepared to think, and enjoy your time in the Outer Wilds.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: What is to say about Outer Wilds that hasn't been said before?I consider this game to be a masterpiece and a milestone in video game history, and I do not say that lightly. It's rare that a game tell you a story in a way that ONLY video game can ; without cut scene, without a narrator, without extensive dialogue giving you the tour of the land or explaining to you the stakes in grand details. It's only through its game play and masterclass level and world design that Outer Wilds will tell you its story, and the only narrator is your own curiosity. You'll be amazed, you'll laugh, you'll be afraid, you may cry ; you surely will smile and experience the awe of discovery and in the end, as the credit rolls, you'll be there damning the world you won't ever have the privilege to experience it again for the first time.It's more than a game. It's an experience. It's art for sure, but we're past the old debate of "Are video game art?", right? Well, if you have a doubt, play Outer Wilds. Even if you don't, play Outer Wilds. Just play Outer Wilds.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: A space discovery game in its purest form, Outer Wilds offers a galaxy worth constantly trekking through to link its several mysteries in what is all a serene odyssey with moments ranging from marshmallow roasting and campfire banjo comfort, to the ever terrifying fear of the unknown and instant dread of one little mishap. A game whose core themes strike me to my very bone, I hope you play it and I hope it speaks to you in a similar way it did to me, as this game helped me feel heard in a dark time that nothing else has really come close to since. That may sound dumb, but you'd have to play it to know.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Really phenomenal game, there's not much like it. Community's very hush-hush about this game's whole shtick, but it's an open-world (open-galaxy?) space puzzle exploration game. There's an overarching mystery to solve, but you'll figure that out over time. The playtime's around 20 hours, give or take. Go in as blind as you can, take your time and read everything closely. It's a very special kind of game that has a lot of heart and talent poured into it, and it leaves you with a lot to think about by the ending. Seriously recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: The best exploration focused game I have ever played and second best game of all time right behind Celeste. The themes are rustic yet fantastically otherworldly, the mechanisms of control and structure familiar yet unique, and the story expertly guided yet not handholded in the slightest. It doesn’t need artificial rails to get you where you are supposed to be since personal intrigue more than fills that role. Just a simple “I wonder that is” can lead to hours on a trail of informational breadcrumbs to wrap up a single line of questioning while opening a web of knowledge along the way. When all of the puzzle pieces are put in place and that solar system of unknowns becomes known, it will all fit together so beautifully that you will wish you could wipe your memory to do it all over again.Few other games have as emotional a soundtrack. It could have been so easy to have a synth for every track in the game since space always seems to be the setting for atmospheric drones in media, but no. The score is filled almost exclusively with acoustic instruments to really drive home that space exploration is never about the space itself, it's the beings that explore it: a theme that carries over into the story as well. Same goes for the best song. You know,  one.Echos of the Eye needs immense recognition as well. Fear was given occasional attention in the base game within certain places and events, but only as a quick scare as an explorational pallet cleanser. In the DLC, the horror of the unknown is incredibly pervasive: being the component that ultimately ties the entire experience together. The story is expanded upon not in the conventional way of DLCs that are tangentially related to the main story or straight up retconning, but in a way that resolves major lingering questions that many wouldn’t have even asked in the first place. Entwined, defining even, but not completely derivative.Hopefully I have highlighted the strengths of Outer Wilds while still being vague enough that you have no idea what you are in for. The less you know, the better.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: I usually refrain from choosing any game as a favourite. However, since playing Outer Wilds, it has become the standard to which all other games will be compared.Not so much a Puzzle game, as a Mystery game. With a wonderful universe to explore, and a story to discover.I recommend not reading anything about the game, do not look at any guides or watch any videos.Just play, explore, and enjoy.It is one of those games that is best on a blind first play through. I wish I could forget everything about it, so that I could play it for the first time again.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: This review is gonna be short and sweet to avoid spoilers!This is a game completely worth your time if you're interested in video games as a storytelling medium, exploring an cool sci-fi fantasy or just want a game you can take at your own pace. If it sounds like I'm being vague it's because this is a game truly worth going in blind. _childDocuments_.review: If you are buying the bundled versions that include the "Echoes of the Eye" expansion DLC there's a few important things to keep in mind.First, the base game and Echoes are basically two different but loosely related adventures.Second, the game doesn't distinguish in an obvious way which locations relate to the base game and which relate to the expansion.  In the game you are free to travel to any locations in the solar system.  As such, I highly recommend that you ignore anything to do with the radio tower on Timber Hearth and ignore the deep space satellite orbiting the solar system until you have completed the base game.  Those two locations are the first steps into the Echoes DLC.  Otherwise you will be pursuing two different stories simultaneously which might make things a bit confusing.  By ignoring those two locations you're pretty much guaranteed to not accidentally blend the two separate adventures together.This game is a piece of art.  What I see in Outer Wilds is a lot of love and passion put into a game.  There's nuance that you won't even notice that's there, but it's there because a design team wanted a full, complete and immersive game.  It's pretty deep in that sense.  After you play through the game, I recommend looking up some of the Easter Eggs.  They aren't so much Easter Eggs as they are intricate design details that will make you appreciate the game more.Some people say this is one of the best games of all time.  I understand the sentiment, but I don't know if I'd go that far.  It's a good game and a clever game for sure.  And it is a great execution of a difficult concept.  I definitely recommend it.There were parts in the game that did feel a little grindy.  When you get stuck and just try every possible variation of a clue until you find something that works.  But I feel I appreciate the game more now looking back on it.  The parts that were grindy was because of me.  I hadn't figured out something as much as I thought I had.  If you're grinding, you're probably not doing it right.As an extra bonus, I loved the soundtrack as well.  I've listened to it quite a bit outside of playing the game.As the description of the game clearly states, you are looping through the same 22 minutes of time over and over.  However it doesn't sound as painful as you might think.  You don't have to repeat a bunch of mundane tasks at the beginning of each loop.  You pretty much just jump in your ship and go whichever direction you want from the beginning(except for the very first loop which sets the backstory).Space travel doesn't take much time.  Everything is extremely scaled down into a little mini solar system.  The planets are comically small, but not in a bad way.  It gives the game it's own unique feel.  The planets are big enough to need some exploring, but not so big it becomes a major chore to explore nor that you get hopelessly lost, and it doesn't take long to get back to where you were if you get interrupted by a loop reset.  It can be fun just hopping from place to place in your little spacecraft.Ship controls are precise and about as intuitive as can be given the nature of travelling through space.  However, that doesn't mean everything is easy.  e.g. landing on the sun station is, while optional, probably the most difficult piloting in the game which there is aptly an achievement for.  However, when on foot, things are pretty straight forward.  There's only a couple tools at your disposal and you won't be collecting a big giant inventory.  You can carry only one extra item at a time.  I like what they achieved with the simplicity of this approach.On one hand it's easy to operate.  In the beginning, you'll discover lots of things no matter which way you go, but on the other hand if you're not paying attention, you will eventually get stuck mid to late game as you start trying to figure out some of the harder pieces of the puzzle.  Getting through this game is not only about piecing together a story, but also learning how the universe works and using the knowledge to aid you in progressing through the story.  The game doesn't force you along a certain path, nor spoon feed you solutions.  The game is an intricate web, and very few things exist in isolation from everything else.  So the game can be pretty difficult in that way.  As an extra dimension, you quickly realize that in the short time loop you exist in, things are changing, and so WHEN you do things matters as well.  It's really beautifully done.To make things more difficult, you are most often learning information out of order(since you can travel in any direction each loop).  Luckily the game provides a "ship's log" to keep all your facts straight and help you determine how they relate to each other and what may be significant.  Without it, the game would be way too difficult.  An essential design feature and well thought out.Towards late game(don't worry, no spoilers), I kind of got stuck and progress was slow.  I was lucky to get one new log entry during each cycle.  Even after sitting down and going through the log in detail, I had some trouble determining what my next step was supposed to be, what I should try next.  Eventually, after careful consideration I was able to figure the less obvious parts out. In terms of difficulty the game really is incredible and I found a great sense of accomplishment upon getting through it.Don't make the wrong assumption about difficulty of this game.  The mysteries and puzzles you have to figure out aren't odd mixes of steps and items that are unintuitive like many adventure games do.  The mysteries are hard, not because the solutions are convoluted.  It's hard because you have to use the information you have to really think about the way things in this universe work.  You sometimes figure things out when you're not playing, and race back to the game knowing you found the answer.  Everything makes sense, maybe just not immediately.The game took about 40 hours to complete, without using any walkthroughs or hints.  Although there is some overlap in those hours as I unknowingly explored some Echoes of the Eye expansion stuff in the main game.  I have a separate review for the expansion: Echoes of the Eye"Many people loved the ending but it didn't have me as emotionally invested in it as much as I think it expected me to.  Not a bad ending, it just kind of felt like it tried too hard to be fantastical.  I didn't really feel any attachments to any other characters as they are mostly static throughout the game.  That's static in a literal sense, no one ever moves anywhere but you.  They just stand in one place the whole time.Even though I was kind of medium on the ending, the game still gets a recommendation from me because getting through the game was really the most fun.  As another reviewer put it best: "it's about the journey, not the destination."  Maybe a tiny bit, if you just like the story so much you want to go through it all again, but there won't be any variation in the game.  It'll be the same game.  Once you get through the storyline thats pretty much it.I only got 6 or 7 achievements on my own.  I don't know why they are all hidden, they are mostly things you would never ever figure out on your own or accidentally.  Many aren't related to the normal path of the story, which I found to be kind of annoying.  Too many pointless side tasks.  I ended up doing a search online to find out what the achievements actually were.  I had to seek an online guide for the "deep impact" achievement as it was so darn specific, you would never guess the exact procedure for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: By far the most unique game I've ever played. It can be beaten in 20 minutes, but that requires having explored the entire solar system, which requires upwards of 36 hours. Thus, avoid spoilers at all costs. The exploration, puzzles, physics, and mechanics all add to this incredible experience. It's sad to see how few of my friends actually own this game.I still haven't played the DLC because I don't want to exhaust my time playing this game all at once.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, here we go...Are you ready for to lose your social life making theories and searching for answers? Even if you said "No", just buy this game and warn yout friends and family that you'll be out for a while.Outer Wilds... Is an incredible experience. It's one of those games that just works BECAUSE it's a game. When I started playing, I was a bit lost. I was almost totally blind (I saw my gf playing like, 10 minutes) and didn't know what the game was about exactly. But then I started discovering things, and connecting the dots and when I realized... I was obsessed.Now, a bit about the game: basically, you're an Astronaut that is taksed with exploring your solar system just for the sake of exploring. But something weird happens and you find yourself stuck in a time loop! And thus you need to explore to try to understand why is this happening to you!Okay, I don't know if you payed attention, but I said your task is to explore a SOLAR SYSTEM. That in itself should sound interesting, right? Not only that, but every planet you'll visit is as misterious and interesting as the next one! You can see in the trailer that one of the planets has tornados all around, and just to give you a bit more, another planet has a freaking BLACK HOLE at its core! Don't tell me that you don't wanna know how this works!Also, it might surprise you, but the game has a really interesting and mysterious story! You'll find lots of mysterious things and wonder how is that thing connected to everything else (oh, and trust me, everything IS connected somehow). But I think what makes it most interesting is how the story is told: by the world itself. You won't get NPCs (well, some) or Cutscenes telling you whats happening. You'll get texts on walls and enviroments that tells a story, and you'll need to connect the dots to understand what happened in each and every place you'll go.Ah, the soundtrack is amazing too! I keep caughting myself singing the theme every now and then :vI just think... More people should give this game a shot. I'm amazed by how I didn't really hear about this game until my girlfrind told me recently. This game deservers more, and I think Mobius Digital continue to make games like this one.(Also, pro tip: if you can play it with a friend or your partner watching you, the experience is greatly improved! Me and my girlfriend kept making theories and laughing and getting scared everytime we discovered a new thing. And having a second brain to help you connect some dots really helped!)
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful.Never thought I'd be attached to this game so much. Was a little iffy in the beginning but it's a good thing that I stuck with it and kept going. Every planet is different yet all beautiful and interesting in their own ways.Go play it. Experience it for yourself. Don't look up guides. You only get to experience it once. Trust me it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: As usual, I will be writing my review in two parts, one after a few hours of play, and one when I've finished. So far I've been really enjoying myself playing this game. The visuals are nice, the controls of the ship are a pain but easier as you get used to them. The story is intriguing, and there seems to be a lot to discover. I would love if there was voice acting for the characters, but I enjoy the personalities and the culture of this world.
