_childDocuments_.review: probably the single greatest adventure I have had in a video game in my 15+ years of playing games, and one of the most memorable experiences I have had not just in this medium, but in ANY medium. have played the game to 100% completion three times now (although your first experience is undoubtedly unique and impossible to replicate) - EGS version, steam version, and PS4.outer wilds is a cosmic puzzle that you solve through pure exploration, but it is also an incredibly touching story about commitment, sacrifice, and finding meaning in your own life despite its inevitable end.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds is amazing. It carries you through a beautiful adventure of mystery and discovery. You'll go from a naive, bright-eyed explorer to a grizzled veteran of the solar system in 20 hours. You'll see wondrous vistas and technological marvels while finding solace in the music of your companions. You'll probably also learn some things about yourself as you wrestle with understanding the cosmos you find yourself in.It is, however, one of those games you can never truly play a second time. Once you are done, I must recommend sitting down with a friend who has never played it before and convincing them to play so that you can relive those moments of wonder and discovery and wild speculation through their eyes. You may need to put duct tape over your own mouth to avoid giving away the secrets they still have yet to learn. They'll walk past the secrets you know are right there, eyes a fraction of an inch from the thing that would unravel the whole story like a single thread pulled from a sweater. And you'll have to sit there, quietly smug, letting them think there was nothing left to discover in this one ruined building.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2020 Spotify recommended part of the soundtrack "Travelers" to me, and I really enjoyed it. Eventually I figured out it was from a video game so I looked it up on steam. It seemed like an alright game, but I didn't want to pay $25 for it so I wish-listed it and went on with my day. 2 years later, I had a gift card from a friend and saw that it was on sale. "Why not" I thought, "could be interesting." I had never seen or heard anything about this game, and I had no idea what gameplay was going to be like. I assumed it was some sort of space survival game.This has now my favorite game of all time. What seems on the outside as a fun campy space exploration game is so much deeper than I could have imagined. Incredibly compelling story, beautiful graphics, and a soundtrack that would make Mozart feel self conscious, this game has it all. Don't let the roughly 50 hours (as of writing this) fool you, I adore this game to pieces.My recommendation? Don't look up anything. Just buy the game and go into it blind. If you watch any gameplay it'll ruin the whole experience, and you really should just see it for yourselfWhile the knowledge based puzzle game isn't for everybody, you'll have a feel for whether or not you'll like it within 2 hours of gameplay.This is a game that I recommend every single person at least tries out, as it is a masterpiece.(P.S. It's DLC is equally amazing, and big enough to be a sequel. Play the base game first, then go do the DLC stuff)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever had the privilege to play. Outer Wilds legitimately has it all: the ability to explore a myriad of unique planets and structures, one of the most beautiful soundtracks I've ever heard, puzzle-solving that requires you to actually use your brain and experiment, a brilliant adherence to the fundamental laws and principles of physics, an outstandingly intriguing and captivating story, and one of the best endings I've seen in all media with an incredibly moving message. The feeling of exploration when investigating a brand-new location, the immense satisfaction when piecing together the intricately woven story, and the profound emotion that comes forth when you beat the game are completely unparalleled experiences I've rarely found in gaming (and never have I found all of these in a single game, aside from Outer Wilds).Outer Wilds is also a truly open-world experience. Even a game like BoTW, lauded for its open-world gameplay, at least nudges you in a certain direction with its story. But the sole motivator for exploration in Outer Wilds is your curiosity: the story is designed so you can visit any planet you want in any order, so each person will have a completely unique experience with the game. Whether you choose to visit a planet to follow up on a previous discovery or because you think it looks cool is entirely up to you, and I absolutely love (and miss) this level of freedom in game design.The DLC is also a perfect companion piece to the story, taking a small gap in the story and beautifully expanding on it in a meaningful and congruent way. While I did not enjoy it quite as much as the original, it was a phenomenal addition to the series and completely worth the money.The only complaint I have about Outer Wilds is that I can never play it again, because once you finish the game you can never repeat the exploration and discovery that makes this game so incredible. But even so, I will never forget this truly one-of-a-kind experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible mystery game. I absolutely loved it, and am very grateful for people recommending I play it blind.However, it does make it difficult to review the plot, so I guess you'll have to trust me when I say it's interesting, intellectually stimulating, and exciting. If you like sci-fi, if you like mystery, if you like exploring new and wondrous places, this is the game for you. I especially appreciated the fact that most plot threads had multiple avenues through which they could be discovered, and that plot relevant locations had a lot of threads you could follow on from there. Also, that oftentimes answers to trickier puzzles usually just needed more exploration in another (sometimes far-off) direction.Mechanics-wise, I have no complaints either, really, barring that navigating tight and particularly dark spaces could, very rarely, be a little bit of a bother. I suppose I might have wished for the ship's headlights to be a little brighter than the personal torch, but it only came up once. Otherwise, steering was fun, and the autopilot covereth a multitude of navigational sins.The game's artstyle is very distinctive, I think, and I particularly liked the... uh... linguistic direction that the game took. That is to say the older writing. Attempting to avoid spoilers, I thought it was very novel; I've never seen anything like that before, and thought whoever came up with it performed a masterstroke in terms of mystery game design. It's a very small thing, but I thought it was nevertheless one of the more well-designed aspects of the game's mechanics and story. The environments were also well thought out and beautiful.The soundscape was quite well put together, and the way that the music was indicative of changing events was very helpful. Not that many tracks, but each fun to listen to and evocative of what it represented.Overall, I heartily recommend this game!EDIT:After playing the DLC, I'd just like to add that it essentially adds more of everything I described above, with some minor horror elements, which honestly seem more like blind mazes than horror experiences at times.A new location (which is amazing, but I'm not going to spoil why exactly), new mysteries, and new puzzles.The music in the DLC is phenomenal as well, and it feels like there's more of it than in the base game - or perhaps I just noticed it more. In any case, the soundtrack and sound effects are superb. The ending also changes based on if you complete the DLC, and I think it enhances the experience.Despite all the praise I have for the DLC though, I think they could have provided a few more clues - there's essentially one of every clue, so there's slightly more need for thorough exploration. Now, you don't need to find everything to beat the DLC or anything, but I think it would have been nice to have more clues scattered around - even if they were just suggestions of places to look which you might have missed; the base game has full of those kinds of nuggets, but the DLC not so much.Still, I had a very good time with the DLC, and I think it ultimately reaffirmed by decision to recommend Outer Wilds. Be curious on your journey! =)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing, and unfortunately I can't go into too much detail without spoiling the game. I'll avoid as many spoilers as I can, and I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND that you don't look up walkthroughs, or any kind of solutions or puzzle hints while you play. This game will give you all of the information required to do everything in the game, and the game will also keep track of all of the important information for you in a player log. I would go so far as to say to not look up any gameplay videos beyond what is on the store page since they might contain spoilers. This game is best experienced as blind as possible, and for you to chart your own course through this fantastic game.With that disclaimer out of the way, I'll point out some details that might be helpful to people who are considering buying this game. As noted in the description of the game, this is a time loop game, but this doesn't work like how a game like Deathloop work. There are no upgrades and you can't carry over items into the next loop. There is technically one thing that might be considered an upgrade, but it is not required to do anything in the game, nor does it make completing anything in the game any easier. Also, do be aware that there are some scary elements in the game; especially the DLC. On that note, there is only one DLC for this game, and I would also highly recommend that as well, but I would say that it is best played after completing the main game. The DLC should be titled as an expansion for how big it is, as well as for how it ties into the story and themes of the main game. It is not required for it to be played after the main game, but it gives you the most impact, and you'll have the greatest understanding of it if you play it after the main game.Aside from this game being amazing, it is also the best example of a time loop puzzle/mystery game in my opinion. This game was so good the I 100% both the main game and the DLC. A lot of care was put into the design and details in the game, and the team had a strong understanding of the real life physics that play a role in both the puzzles and exploration. This game is nearly perfect with only minor complaints that are trivial in comparison to what this game achieves. I can't wait to see what Mobius Digital does for their next game, and I have high expectations for them.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game, it's good.  Didn't quite live up to the hype for me, as a lot of the "puzzles" felt obvious; only two or three really felt satisfying, and they were "oh, that was fun" not "Wow, I finally figured that out!"  Mostly it was exploring and realizing that I missed some little key thing, having to go back to find that, and getting a clue to put it together.  And some of the "fit together multiple pieces" were a major letdown; honestly, one major chain that I thought would be the start of the final sequence turned out to be, AFAICT, just a bit of backstory.  Neat, but quite the letdown for the buildup.I definitely would have been much happier if there were some sort of save-state or rewind functionality; of the 27 hours steam says I played, probably 6-8 were just leaving it paused when life interfered; probably 2-3 were wasted when I failed at random things and had to retry, 1-2 were trying to solve things correctly but subtly wrong in ways that meant the correct solution didn't work, 2-3 were things that I *thought* I failed to execute correctly, but were actually wrong, and most of the rest were fun exploration and putting the pieces together.  Not a terrible ratio, but if I could have saved those ~6-10 hours that felt wasted, I would have been much happioer with the game.Original rage-review:This seems pretty good, I'm intrigued and intend to continue.  But while it feels like it's not intended to be a punishing game, I just utterly wasted 20 minutes due to various stupidity.  Some was my fault, some felt like a "haha, don't do that", but it's frustrating that the game has taught me that 20 minutes is enough time to make some real progress, but this time all it was was stupid mistakes getting in the way and preventing me from getting anywhere.  I normally like the way the game works, but sometimes a "please rewind the last thirty seconds so I can do the thing I've done three times before without issue and not be an idiot this time" button would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems to have been developed on the fundamental misunderstanding that making the player 'slow down and look at the world' may be reasonably accomplished by wasting the player's time.There is nothing remotely interesting or valuable in or about this title. No new character interactions are unlocked as the world is explored and information is learned, the world and its objects are extremely rarely interactive - on a scale which makes release-day No Man's Sky look like it was bleeding-edge tech, the designs are noticeably rough and amateurish, and the music is remarkably(!!!) uninspired.The majority of active gameplay is this set of actions, repeated ad nauseam: walk to your rocket ship (15 seconds), fly your rocket ship to a planet (45-90 seconds), walk in circles around the barren planet until you find an object with which you can interact (120-360 seconds). If you are lucky, the interactable will be a 1-paragraph flavor text! Considerations for fuel and oxygen mean that you must now return to your ship, though (120 seconds). Having departed again, the player may make it about two-thirds of the way to a second flavor text paragraph when the time loop ends. Shucks! Oh, well. Return to the "walk to your rocket ship" step.There are no 'characters' in the traditional sense. There are cardboard cutouts who will speak at you for anywhere from 1-8 lines. Their lines do not ever change depending on circumstance, and the cutouts provide you with neither supplies nor information. They are found at fixed locations in the world and exist exclusively to convince the dimmer players that the game's 'solar system' is not lifeless.The critical deception of Outer Wilds comes in its effort to contradict this unassailable truth: there is nothing to discover in its world. Outer Wilds is a small, unremarkable place with exceptionally few features located at unacceptably great distance from one another. Those who play this game will spend significant time staring at a near-black screen waiting for a planet to draw nearer. If that compels you to consider a purchase, then I advise you seek psychiatric assistance before following through on the purchase. Do not waste your time with decidedly less-than-middling games like this which lash themselves to, in discomforting zealotry, the "less is more" dogma.A note as to the pricing: I would not complete this game if it were free. Its base $25 price tag is nothing less than insulting.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game. The music, the story, the ideas and puzzles are pretty good. I think most people would enjoy this game. I found the game too frustrating. The puzzles aren't that difficult but the repetition of lengthy tasks with a timer is stressful. Especially because many of the tasks involve waiting. The fact that you need to collect knowledge to progress is fantastic, love that mechanic. The fact that these tasks, even when you have the knowledge, are difficult because it is difficult to control your movements is punishing.I understand why the controls are the way they are, and you get a feel for using accelerations which is neat. But I would give all that up not to have to redo the same tasks over and over.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Almost exactly a year ago, I gave this game a negative review, citing my personal struggles directing myself through the solar system, my two left hands (which made solar travel especially perilous), and my poor memory (which invalidated much of my loose play style generally).This time, it happened. It snapped together. Once you get one thing (in my case, the quantum ♥♥♥♥), the rest flows together. I suddenly understood how to pilot my ship (and even found the eject button!), how to keep the fundamentals without getting swamped with memorizing names and individual plots between text blocks.I'm still not smart. I don't think I would have managed to complete this game without exactly two Google searches (and a couple lore dumps from some wiki pages). Still, I can say that I did experience at least some of the same catharsis many other far more clever players managed without any help.It's incredibly strange and then incredibly special, in that order. If you (like me one year ago) tried this and found it incomprehensible, let it rest. Let it simmer. If you get the urge to try again, to find whatever you were missing, you will almost certainly find it the second (or third) time around. Take it from an idiot like me: You have the curiosity to get it done, even if unlocking its threads feels like traveling against the current of a Category V Hurricane at the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this might be the best game I've ever played.It's cliche to begin saying this is not a game, but indeed a experience. As I'm a huge fan of puzzle games and walking simulators (both of which this game is, just in the manner where the puzzle is understanding how this 'solar system' works and is connected, and you are definitely walking through space... time (sometimes just floating around)) this game just hits the nail on the head with my favorite genres. More than that, it evokes so much... this game gave me the creeps, anxiety, fear of being insignificant and subject to the most random events (specially deaths), awe of the grandiosity of the universe, and I think it has probably the top 3 stories I've ever read in my life (from someone who played a whole lot of visual novels).If I could choose just one piece of media with the following 'try to go into this not knowing about anything of this at all' this would definitely be it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more art than entertainment. Much like Kerbal Space Program, Outer Wilds is all about providing a simulation demonstrating all the many and easily achievable ways to die in outer space. Unfortunately, all the charming events and feelings of wonder are easily outnumbered by all the frustrations and confusion experienced throughout. No one can accuse this game of being unambitious, but ambition doesn't always result in an enjoyable or entertaining experience.I knew going into this that there was a pretty stringent time/death-loop which of course means there will be a lot of repetition, trial & error, etc. to the game. However, the experience is one that felt more punishing and harsh than one that pushed me to seek out more answers to the mysteries of the Outer Wilds. Though losing only five to twenty minutes of progress (due to accident or the time loop) may not seem like much, a continual compounding of such time thanks to mistakes (most of which don't feel like my fault) wears down your patience. In fairness, my tolerance for this kind of repetition and cycles is limited. We all have things to do and lives to live, and I have a hard time allowing a game to put me into a position where I have to constantly redo, backtrack, or recycle content just to progress. While the time loop is novel as a concept, it doesn't make up for being a frustrating gaming experience. Only through continual death do you have the opportunity to piece together the world and story/narrative which are peppered here and there throughout the solar system. There is no obvious direction to follow nor narrative provided to guide you through a storyline. You're just there. You find out about the world and the solar system by interacting with them. This is fine for some, but for me, it felt like trying to find the bottom side of a formless blob. It's confusing and unclear for a large portion of the game until you explore and try enough things out to better make out what the heck is going on. The game strongly depends on your willingness to either burn enough time into it to figure things out through the loops or will require you to be willing to find guidance outside of the game. If you don't like either, then I think you will find Outer Wilds to be a frustrating and largely unsatisfying experience.The lack of voice acting and the planets/moons all being tiny are also disappointments but overshadowed by other issues. And while a completely objective stance, I feel I must mention that I truly found this game to be a bore AND a chore to play. In my second bout of playing, I actually fell asleep at my desk while waiting for the timing for an action to be just right (way too much waiting around for a game on a time loop). I *never* fall asleep while gaming. It's also why I've had a hard time picking this game back up to complete.While it made a great first impression, it was one that waned more and more as time went on due to all of the annoying deaths, obtuse puzzles, glitches, and honestly - the time loop. I'm glad to have played the Outer Wilds, but I'm more glad to be done with it. I truly don't understand or agree with all the rave reviews and hype surrounding it. Unfortunately, I didn't find enough positives from Outer Wilds to be able to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Great game in fact.Sadly isn´t a game for me.I would love the story as a book.The time loop is an intersting setup and I quite enjoyed exploring. In both I felt lost in a way I don´t like. I have nothing against difficulty, I played Hollow Knight and Celeste. But in these two games, I always had a goal. _childDocuments_.review: Eventually somewhat satisfying. Some frustrating mechanics, and the solar system comes to feel kind of empty and meaningless. Seems to rely heavily on wild goose chases and doesn't provide enough context. It seems like most of the "discovery" is discovering how the devs want you to play the game. Given its emphasis on "physics", a lot of interactions seem to be lacking. For instance, the on-foot interactions are not very good. Try stepping (actually requires a jump) over a 3 inch obstacle in front of you, and you get stuck; or moving perpendicular to a surface causes you to either slide along it, bounce off or up. No character development, but I guess that plays into the whole existential feel.---Edit---The game was good, but not a sublime experience, and that's disappointing given the possibilities.After thinking about the concepts a bit, I just have to say the ideas proposed by the game require you to suspend reason quite a bit, and the entire game feels like a contrived story atop an interesting game mechanic that misconstrues certain terms to fit particular puzzles. For instance "observing a quantum [thing]" is misrepresented as "a consciousness actively, visually, perceiving a thing". This is not the meaning of observation. If you think about observation of quantum states as measurement, then it is more accurate. If we assume "observation" to be sensory experience of phenomena, this still begs the question: what about non visual observations such as the other senses? For instance, if I am standing on a surface, not looking at it, I am still touching the surface, which means that it is being observed. Other measurements also effect the measurement. So, all this is to say that it's frustrating that you have to turn off your flashlight and all of a sudden you're no longer observing a thing even when you're not looking at it to begin with, and despite the fact that you're presumably "observing" it through other senses (and with four eyes, these beings probably have 10 primary senses). It just leaves a lot to be desired.Also, "The Eye of the Universe" begs the question. Is all of existence a form of consciousness resolved from probability to a momentary state by observation of itself? Another question is whether this Eye is the universal resolver of quantum states to necessary states. But these questions don't matter to this game.And white holes are a stupid, Instagram worthy idea, especially concerning a person entering a black hole and exiting a white hole. Does their consciousness remain intact despite the fact that they will necessarily die? Or is the individual consciousness something outside of the self (such as The Player or the protaganist's soul)? Don't ask interesting questions, just do the puzzles you were given and don't expect much.--- mild spoiler to follow ---The big bang could have been interesting. Why did they decide to make it boring? How do you represent a faster-than-light expansion of nothing and the transition of possibility into probability into necessity? "Uh... idk let's just make it look like a ball of light. Maybe an underwater explosion. Those are cool."

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of all time in my book, no hyperbole. I love it dearly and would recommend this to nearly everyone. It's a one-in-a-million type of game for me.Be aware that this is an exploration-focused game. The world IS the game. It's one of the very best gaming worlds ever created, and *actually* unique in some aspects.Also be aware that you will want to read stuff in this game. This is about a mystery, and it unravels in written text you discover and you will want to read more of it as you go, else you miss out on the whole point of it all - the mystery is very interesting in my opinion. There is no voice acting, and the game is front-loaded with some of the slightly less interesting (and to the grand scheme of things, almost irrelevant) dialogue. Read it, but don't let it slow you down. The mystery is ahead, up above, down below, all around. Go explore.Knowledge is progression here. They embraced this and had the game track your progress in useful ways, there's a good notebook / journal that lets you sort progression by location. Good stuff!If you are the type to shy away from reading and find yourself skipping through any and all text to get moar action, this game is not for you. I'd argue it's 100% worth it to break with that habit and play this. I wish I could neuralize myself and experience it for the first time again. Basically:🎵 Let's do the timewarp agaaaaain 🎵

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews on games, but this one absolutely deserves a positive rating. This game was unforgettable.Spoiler-free overview for those who want a bit more detail before committing: this game is about knowledge. As you gain information, you progress through the game. Clues will point you to other clues as you explore a miniature solar system.This took me over 20 hours to complete. It's not exactly a 15-minute adventure. But this game is worth every minute you put into it. If you're on the fence, consider this an invitation to experience one of the most phenomenal stories of your life.

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds was one of the most enthralling and mesmerising mysteries I've ever had the pleasure of following the crumbs to solve. It lays out a mystery both complex and surprisingly simple once you see the whole picutre. Solving each clue and slotting it correctly into the wider picture makes you feel Giga Brain, while also being clearly enough laid out that anyone can figure it out by reviewing their notes and revisiting key locations.And you're rewarding with a trip unlike any other, from start to finish.This game is about the journey, with the final mystery being a cherry on top of the beautiful time you've had until then, leaving you with a feeling of completion and....pace.Will definitely play the next thing these guys put out

_childDocuments_.review: Being sent back to the camping site every measly 22 minutes got REAL OLD, REAL FAST.There's no fun or challenge in doing the same space travel and cave exploration several times.UPDATE after finishing the game:- Great story (for the most part).- It's great exploring new places (keyword being *new*, sadly).- Gameplay is still a mixed bag...the big problem is that I'm not sure if playing it yourself is better than just watching someone you like play the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing.  Part exploration, part platforming, part puzzle solving.  It is very finely crafted to give you lots of things to do, consistently feel like you are making progress, and give you other things to do if you get stuck on one path.  It also excellently balances difficulty and encourages you to take risks. _childDocuments_.review: Death comes for us all. Can you discover the terrible secret of space before time runs out? Or will you just fart around trying to get enough speed to dive under the currents of Ocean Moon and squander what precious moments you have left. Outer Wilds challenges us to ask ourselves "Why not both?". But in the end, none of it really matters anyway. We can't save ourselves and we certainly cant save anyone else in this video game of life. Thinly veiled propaganda for the church of nihilism. As a senior citizen, it's been a long time since I sat down to play a game and then looked at the clock and was shocked by the time - just like in that comic. And you never even get to fight Kratos, just explore and figure stuff out! 8.5/10 (The last 2.5 points being deducted because of the quantum moon car talk puzzlers)

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T watch a trailer for this game. DON'T look at the game's store page videos and screenshots. DON'T even read game reviews including this one!! _childDocuments_.review: When i play open world games, i tend to open up the map and create a path to the main quest spot that includes the most locations and markers. _childDocuments_.review: This game is the only reason I now sort ratings by negative before I buy.This game is SO overrated. I chose to give him a chance willingly, in good faith. I was EXTREMELY disappointed.This "game" actually is a waiting/walking simulator, where the game doesn't give you ANY hint about what you have to do, but the plot twist is that there's a hidden countdown.The main mechanics of the loop put you in a constant state of frustration: if you miss something, you go back to the beginning of the loop! But beware: to get back in, you have to wait! And believe me, you'll miss. A LOT. ALL THE TIME. The game gives NO indication.You walk slowly, you move through space slowly, everything is slow, but the game is made in such a way that you have to be fast enough to move through the story. Prepare yourself for a looping speedrun until you reach a room where you'll read a few lines that leave you with NO further information.The controls are AWFUL : the game wants to make them realistic, so you have to accelerate, counter gravity, counter your own movement, ... because "you have to understand, games are realistic nowadays!". This makes the overall experience all the worse, as this is the eighteenth time you've passed through a planet, and you know you're going to die a dozen more times. You'll also have to manage your oxygen, as well as the fuel in your jetpack. Resource management in a puzzle game! This has NOTHING to do here, and further degrades the experience by artificially extending the game's lifespan through player's repeated deaths. Especially as these two resources are necessary to the game: your oxygen is naturally emptied as you play, and the jetpack is naturally emptied as you move around the world. So you're limited in both time and movement.The story itself, the core of the game, is empty, uninteresting and poorly presented. In concrete terms, the game arranges elements randomly on the map, and it's up to you to link them together to form an increasingly incoherent whole.I finished the game by accident, without even realizing it, and I only noticed it because I got the credits rolling. No cutscene, no explanation.I fail to understand how a game like this can be voted GOTY when it's only intended for a small percentage of gamers. The developers obviously forgot that it's the game's job to hook the player, not the player to force himself to like a game.NB : I wrote this whole review during the UNSKIPPABLE waiting moments where you juste have to AFK and wait because the universe is not yet in the good alignment.

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds, this breathtaking experience made me feel both incredibly small yet so vast... Playing it properly this time (lol), I explored everything from top to bottom, and the DLC brought back powerful personal memories, further strengthening my love for the game as a whole. the mysteries uncovered in the DLC were so amazing and touching... _childDocuments_.review: This is hands down one of my favourite games! Open world(s, exploration based gameplay, puzzling all the pieces of information you get together, it's all right up my alley. The solar system is unique, creative and spectacular. And the feeling I got when I figured out something new was amazing, and rewarding. There were some scary parts, as you expect from a game where you go into space, but I would not call it a horror game. To friends I call this game an information-based roguelite. _childDocuments_.review: My oh my.... what an experience..... jeez, i'll collect my thoughts now...First off... lets get the disclaimer out of the way... this game ain't everybody's cup of tea. _childDocuments_.review: The problem with recommending the Outer Wilds is that it's best to go in blind, but to share what made it such a great experience for many people is to kind of spoil that. I was lucky enough to stumble upon in on Steam and bought it on a whim, so I went in as blind as you possibly can with a modern game. I didn't even know about the time loop mechanic (despite the fact that it says it on the Store page, RIGHT THERE!)What I'll say is that if the screenshots and trailers pique your interest, if the vibe or music works for you, consider giving the Outer Wilds a try. The gameplay revolves around flying between planets trying to unravel the game's mystery with progression being based solely on your own understanding the game's solar system and its story. No ship or tool upgrades or whatnot. Just reading and solving environmental puzzles. The central mechanic of the solar system is a bit arcane, but I think the game does a well enough job in helping players wrap their heads around it.On a slightly spoilery note, I'll share one of the biggest impressions the game left on me. The story and its themes strike an emotional note somewhere between I love it. I'll listen to the soundtrack every once in a while and certain songs can make the entire game just come flooding back to me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is so special to me. It's my favorite game of all time, even beating Monster Hunter (which is kinda insane). The pure love and passion this game radiates is infectious. The chill vibes of your friends on timber hearth. To the dread you experience in dark bramble. I just can't help but smile whenever i boot it back up just to be in that universe again. _childDocuments_.review: DO NOT LOOK ANYTHING UP ABOUT THE GAME BEFORE PLAYINGThis is a warning to anyone and everyone who EVER plays this game: DO NOT LOOK ANYTHING UP WHILE PLAYING OR PRIOR TO PLAYING. This is the singular best game for "Aha!" moments that make your entire brain click. If you're looking for a KILLER story game; one that will make you take another look at your existence, and the meaning of how that existence affects others. You take the role of the most chaotic aquatic-species astronaut ever to explore a solar system and discover the story of the Nomai, an ancient race that lived in your solar system. You're the first person with a translator device that can instantly translate Nomai text; so you're the first person that can understand everything they did and said.Personally, I wasn't sold on the DLC until the moment I discovered how to beat the game; play it AFTER you play the Basegame. This game is a game locked behind knowledge, so any further information about anything would give stuff away. Unlock the knowledge. Unlock the game. Play Outer Wilds. Personally? It's my favorite game I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful. There's a lot at play, and it's full of surprises. It's nearly impossible to explain what makes this such a vivid experience without spoiling anything, as every discovery is intended to draw you deeper. The graphics are lovely, and the atmosphere adds to the sense of exploration. Every planet is hand crafted, their trajectories are pre-ordained and you are simply a tiny spec in the midst of it all.At first, it seems rather standard and slow paced. At first. It only takes about 20 minutes for you to realize just how deep this all goes, and just how frantic of an experience you will inevitably have. Take your time with this one, as games this vibrant and interesting only come along every decade or so.TL:DR = Zelda - Majora's Mask meets Subnautica in space.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Wilds is by no means a bad game. I understand why people think it’s a masterpiece but it’s definitely not for everyone. I cleared it to the end, but it just didn’t suit me.The good:What I loved about this game a lot was the premise. Once you get access to your ship the game doesn’t really tell you much. You do whatever you want to do. Eventually you'll find things that capture your attention and you’ll want to know more about them. The whole game is about piecing together the story through exploration which means that most of the time you’re examining planets while coming across all sorts of mysteries and puzzles. The universe is simply amazing and I had a lot of fun exploring the planets and the story behind the Nomais. The OST and the overall atmosphere also makes the exploration a very fun experience. I’ve heard a lot of people complain about the movement controls but I personally really enjoyed that aspect of this game. I also liked a lot of the game’s ideas. The quantum object thing is one of the coolest things I’ve ever come across in any game (I literally had a dream about going to the restroom and whenever I looked away the toilet would disappear lmao).The bad:The game has zero tolerance for your time. You’re in a loop and every 22 minutes you die and go back to the start. It became more and more annoying every time I died just before getting enough information from a place. This forced me to not begin any new adventures if there’s just 4 minutes left to the explosion. Sure the time loop is needed for the story but there’s more time limits. On top of the loop there’s gas tank, fuel gauge, crumbling environment, rising sand… almost every planet has its own additional time limit. There are cases where you have to go to a specific location at a specific time to solve a puzzle. This means you’ll find yourself either rushing to a destination or waiting few minutes before you can take action. If you miss your chance you have to start over. It’s just very frustrating. Naturally there is one more way to start over - death. You will die a lot in this game because there’s many things that can easily kill you. Plus you have to watch the same unskippable cutscene at the end of each loop and I'd be really glad if I could jump right back into the game when I die.The changing environment made me think I have explored everything just to find out that it changes during the loop. The ship log will only tell you “there’s more to explore” but that doesn’t really help since the planets aren't small and the environment keeps changing. It’s great that the game doesn’t hold your hand although at the same time it doesn’t give you much indication that you’ve done things right either. This can lead to a lot of frustration and a feeling of bumbling around blind depending on how much patience you have. Sometimes instead of a feeling of reward for figuring something out you can just feel relief that you translated some new writings before the 22 minutes are up. It can easily feel overwhelming at times.The puzzles are partly amazing and partly bad at the same time. You’ll have to figure them out through trial, error, death and observation. The reward is a sense of personal achievement for figuring the puzzles out. Reading guides will only rob you of the game’s reward but sometimes I just had no idea how I was meant to figure them out. You must be a genius to find out the solution to every single puzzle in this game.In conclusion there is a lot to like here but it’s very frustrating if you aren’t sure what to do next, run out of time or just slightly mess up and you have to do it all over again. It became an extremely frustrating survival time-management game that keeps sending you to the beginning over and over again. Overall it gave me an impression of eating a fish: “It tastes delicious, but the bones are really annoying.”

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game basically is true exploration at its core, it makes you wonder, it makes you theorize. You will get your money's worth, even at full price, especially since this game does things that isn't done very often in other games.I've bought this game, thinking it was just some sort of exploration game, with not much meat to it. It was fun to explore for a while, especially the home planet, but then it began: unexplainable things happened. I didn't pay much attention to it, thinking it was just some sort of oddity the devs put in for fun.Then I explored further and further, finding texts from the ancient civilisation that you get introduced to at the start of the game. As I read, I was basically getting deeper and deeper into a web of stories, questioning a lot of things what they meant or what it resulted it to. It evolved into things I didn't even imagine, and it had me theorizing until the very end. Furthermore, it has that Antichamber-esque feeling of progression, where you are initially lost and a bit scared to progress, you will learn and understand things more and more as you go on, become more and more fearless, try out new things, and get further and further, reaching places you wondered how to even get there, or never guessing that these would be possible.And while there are some very frustrating moments, such as the game/game world being a bit confusing at times with its mechanics, it's never at a point where you ragequit. (Though at later stages I kinda had to cheat and look some things up, but that could be because I was kind of getting a bit too impatient.)Though there were 2 main gripes I have about the game. For one, there is one thing that kind of seems a bit out of place as to how it would fit into the timeline. I won't spoil anything, don't worry, and it's nothing that basically ruins everything story-wise. The second thing is that certain environments are a bit complex to navigate around at first, making walking around a chore, until you discover shortcuts.Overall however, it's a great game, and one that won't be able to be replicated that easily.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: Very innovative game!  Kind of reminds me of Myst meets Majora's Mask, but in space. The puzzles are interesting and challenging and makes you think outside the box in ways that other puzzle games I've played haven't. Flying the spacecraft is pretty cool as well: a little touch of realism piloting a small craft in a zero G vacuum environment.  The physics can be frustrating at times, and it never feels like you have enough time per cycle, but I suppose that just adds to the mystique.The Echoes of the Eye DLC is also a lot of fun, with a few (albeit simplistic) elements reminiscent of survival horror stealth (like Penumbra or Amnesia, though not even close to as scary).  It's a worthy sequel with fresh mechanics and a good story.Highly recommend this game for anyone who enjoys challenging puzzles!

_childDocuments_.review: You have not played a game like this before. The mechanics for this game can be really trippy which leads to the one of a kind gameplay experience. It reminds me of Subnautica but instead of water its space and instead of survival its adventure rpg. My favorite planet *well planets* were the Hourglass twins although Id suggest exploring Giant's Deep first. The map changes over time so if something is inaccessable just be patient and you will get your chance. Also if you find yourself stuck use the scout or signalscope as they often hold the key to your next clue. Most of all dont spoil the game as its really only meant to be played once(20-30 hour playthrough) and uncovering the story yourself is the most rewarding part of the game. Good luck and happy exploring!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by my IGT, I've finished the game outside of the Steam version. I bought it here because I felt the devs deserved it.Games are better at creating certain emotions and sensations over others. Anger, frustration and accomplishment are common in competitive games or challenging games with high skill-ceilings, sadness and bittersweet joy can be teased out through a touching story. Fear and dread can be evoked by a game with an oppressive atmosphere or tense situations where the player is defenseless.This game inspired awe. This game made me feel small in the face of a vast universe. That's a unique accomplishment.I won't go into further detail. _childDocuments_.review: Others have already sung the praises of this game in ways I can't even articulate. Instead, let me offer some advice for future space-travelers:-Note all of the game's tags. This is a fun space exploration game, but it's also a puzzle game, with a deep, story-rich mystery at the center. Remember to READ; the writing isn't just there for lore purposes like you'll find in other open-world games.-Again, it's a puzzle game. You gotta put your brain to the test. If you hit a dead-end or don't know how to progress further, try using something else in your tool-belt, or go check out another path, or heck even just look back and review what you already know. It might not always seem obvious, but you might run into something that, with a bit of context or some extrapolating, can help you progress.-If you ever get frustrated, feel free to take a break. Sit back, watch the planets go by, tune in to some music. Heck, cook some marshmallows if you've got a campfire nearby. Take a load off, you can always try again later.-You can do it. No really, you can. You don't have to be a legend, or a genius, or a hero, but you do have to be willing to try.This doesn't have to end up being your favorite game of all time, but hopefully you'll still find something to enjoy out of the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am primarily writing this due to the Mystery Fest going on right now in hopes that some of the people on my friends list will see this and consider giving it a try. First off, ignore my playtime here. I initially purchased this game on the Epic Launcher as it was an exclusive when it launched (a choice made by the publisher, not the developers). I bought it here again to support the developers, as well as to get my wife to play it on our Steam Link. :)This is my favorite game of all time. Nothing else is even close and that's a big statement considering how many games I have played and how many games I have loved. This game is special, but it's hard to express why without ruining the experience for others. If you are considering playing this, do not look anything up. Do not watch someone else play it. It can only be truly experienced once.Here is what I can say:This game is a love letter to curiosity. You are put into a solar system absolutely full of unknowns and it is up to you to decide how you want to proceed. There are no quest markers, there is no linear path to take. The game respects your intelligence and every individual's journey will be unique as a result. The gameplay loop is also unlike anything else I've ever experienced, as the ONLY thing that gates you is your own lack of knowledge. The more you play the more you learn, which pushes you into other mysteries to try to figure out.There is a very heavy theme being explored throughout the game which will come together beautifully in the end. They really stick the landing. It will likely cause you to go through a broad spectrum of emotions if you have any sense of wonder or empathy in your bones. The person who wrote this story and the way that the story is conveyed has a great understanding of how to create individuals that you can bond strongly with.The music is simple, but stirring and expertly enters and leaves the game as the moment demands.There is a massive community of people who watch people play this game even if they don't consume any other content in this way, just because they want to relive it through someone else. Because, like I said, everything in the game is about discovery and learning and once you have gone through it all, you cannot truly relive it yourself.It will not be for everybody, no game is. But, for so many people, this game is an unparalleled anomaly.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ever made, by far. Incredible storytelling, innovative gameplay, excellent puzzles, perfect pacing, and masterful music. It expertly balances vast space exploration storytelling with intimate emotional moments. It is harrowing, inspiring, groundbreaking, and ingeniously designed.Outer Wilds isn't just a wonderful game, it's a testament to how games can provide experiences that no other medium can offer. And it does it all flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Outer Wilds

_childDocuments_.review: If I could sum up this game in one sentence, it would be "Don't be sad that it's over, be happy that it happened."Outer Wilds made me feel things I never thought I would.I now understand that art is supposed to not just show you sights and sounds you've never experienced before and that you didn't even imagine could exist, but also emotions that you never knew existed too.If you wanted an example of how video games could be real art in that regard, I don't think you could find a better one here. I don't think you'll find a more bittersweet ending.Because nearly all the progress in the game is your knowledge of it's mysteries and mechanics as a player, once you experience it once, you can never experience it again. Thus, the game has no replay value. My hope is that the game will make you feel at peace with that once you are done.If you decide to try it, here's my pieces of advice:-Play for more than 22 minutes, no matter what. If you still don't like it after that, fair enough, but you owe it to yourself to play at least 22 minutes.-Don't look up spoilers or puzzle solutions if you can at all help it. You will be robbing yourself of an experience that you can never get back if you do. I'm not bullshitting you. If you had to pick one game that you genuinely stuck by not spoiling for yourself, make it this one. Don't even look up the game on Wikipedia. I'm not aware of any piece of media you will benefit more from going in as absolutely cold as you can.I used to think the fact that we die robs our life of meaning. This game taught me that doesn't have to be true.

_childDocuments_.review: Just play it. This game is a straight-up masterpiece in my books and I've never played anything like it. It encompasses the exploration, mystery, action-adventure genre absolutely gorgeously. The best part of this game is that there aren't any objectives that needs to be followed despite there being an overall story. It's purely driven at our own pace and by our own curiosity. The more you discover, the more invested you get into the whole story-line of the past civilization that once lived in the solar system and the reasons behind the existing remnants.The game feels absolutely satisfying to play and it's engine feels really good. The world building is just amazing with different gorgeous and unique planets all tied to one another. You can feel the different gravity from different planets and such. The low-poly visual style also looks really nice and clean. The sound track is also really good since it's very atmospheric and ethereal. Makes the experience even more authentic. There's just everything to love about this game. Looking forward to the DLC !!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I never happened to suggest a game that in my opinion is a must play regardless of the person I'm talking to, but I found myself bringing so many friends into Outer Wilds without ever giving in to the temptation of describing it in details. Outer Wilds is to me not just a game, but a journey of self exploration, you venture in a world that's in a way not too far from the one we know so well, inhabited by otherworldly creatures called Hearthians that were driven by curiosity to leave their nest and see what's beyond. But you're not presented with a story that intertwines between these folks, as you soon will be following the route that many before you set for your people, From the cozy planet of Timber Hearth, you will be joining the Outer Wilds Ventures, with the sole purpose of raising your head to the sky and navigate the solar system that for generations fascinated your kin... as you're gathering the admiration of many for doing so. This is as far as you need to know, because everything that will happen after you set foot on your vessel will be entirely up to you. Every single person approaching the game will have a completely unique journey and will experience a spectrum of emotions that entirely relies on their choices, and the beauty and horror of it is that you can only play this game for the first time once. So let me beg you to trust your guts and get into this unreplicable experience, or if you're lucky enough to be approached by a desperate soul like mine, let them live this journey through your eyes, as we survivors can only live it once again through others.Outer Wilds deeply changed the way I face my everyday life, please let it change yours.

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable game, with no other really alike to it - one of pure exploration and discovery, The jetpack-ing and lunar lander-ing movement would make for a fun game by themselves, but the thoughtful design of these strange little 'worlds' instilled wonder in me each time I visited a new one. Atmospherically the game's tone somehow captures a therapeutic soothing but with oppressive dreadfulness at the same time, with the latter throwing the former into starker relief and making the player appreciate it the more. Despite the high reputation of Outer Wilds, I didn't get started with it until years after buying, in what I now realise was a fear of being disappointed, of not getting the same delight out of it so many others had done. But there was no disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but Outer Wilds was something really special.  One of the most immersive stories, and some of the most exciting exploration I've ever played.  Unfortunately, you can only play it once.  The entire game is tied to the story and the story is one giant puzzle, pieced together from fragments of conversations you get as rewards for finding hidden corners of the universe.  You'll be playing for hours, get to a section you cannot for the life of you figure out, and be forced to walk away.  Later, a single piece of information you find can entirely rewrite how you look at the game's mechanics and suddenly a puzzle will click, and you'll fly as fast as you can to go try out what you think will work, and it will, and it's one of the best feelings.  But once you beat the game once, it's trivial to beat again.  Everyone is right when they say go into it as blind as possible.  Discovery is the best part.  And you can only discover this game once.

_childDocuments_.review: In order to understand my rating, I will need to spoiler a few things, just to prepare any reader for it. Outer Wilds could be described as a first-person mystery Sci-Fi exploration game set in a small solar system with a few planets, satellites, comets and moons with a peculiar characteristic: the sun will become a supernova every 22 minutes and all life in the system will be reset, thus the player will restart at the same spot again after that time. You’ll be playing an alien humanoid lifeform born on one of the planets, Timber Hearth, ready to explore the galaxy with a somewhat makeshift spacecraft. The game will totally leave it up to the player how to approach each cycle in the solar system, but generally speaking the aim is to discover as much as possible about the peculiar situation and some ancient civilisation. After about 20 hours on a completionist approach, here is my pros/cons list:Pros:+ exploration game+ cute galaxy setting+ colourful and diverse planets+ free to choose your play style+ progression of the sun into a supernova+ knowledge base Cons-- super repetitive, and quickly boring for me, up to the point of becoming extremely tedious-- annoying to start all over again at the same spot at each cycle-- 22 minutes reset and time-dependent access to some information or locations leads to lots of time wasted on waiting for the right moment and replaying again if it failed, in my opinion an artificial extension of the play time- Pretty static environment on the planets and other celestial bodies- Static NPCs and dialogues written on a rather mediocre level with lots of irrelevant babble- NPC characters shallow- Very hard to learn and navigate the spacecraft- Console controller based, with little effort and adjustment towards PC setups- Super fast planet movement making it hard to land and stay on them- Strange gravity on some planets surfaces due to fast movement, you can easily be jettisoned off the surface- The game will keep it a secret that progress is somewhat saved after each cycle, you’ll need to find that out yourself- Hard to find out hints and many locations deeply hidden- Lots of ancient texts with inconsistent, irrelevant content without contribution either to the atmosphere or riddles- Very hard to find out how to get to the ending- Some serious frame rate drops at some locations and transitionsConclusion: Outer Wilds is probably most interesting to people who like exploring in a mystery / Sci-Fi setting with some tough riddles and have a good amount of patience as well as resilience to be reset every 22 minutes to try again. Personally, I didn’t enjoy the game although I do like some other titles of the publisher. Rating: 3/10 points

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Frustrating controls. If you can overcome the awful controls - you'll be in for a phenomenal experience. I couldn't. I only experienced tedium.EDIT: Played it till the end and still found it to be lacking for me. The game is a 6DOF Puzzle Platformer with a timeloop mechanic. If any of those things aren't your thing then steer clear. If you like Puzzle Platformers then you'll likely enjoy this. The 6DOF controls are wanting and games two and a half decades older pulled off the controls better such as Descent, Fury3, etc. Even more recently you have Prey but that's AAA so I suppose it isn't a fair comparison.I didn't enjoy the music much and found it tremendously cookie cutter. I suppose it fits diagetically but you can easily have somewhat interesting music while still being barebones and simple. I think I wouldn't have been so irked but the music here is made to be a very core aspect of the game.The game has three elements narratively - your civilization, the Nomai civilization you learn about at the start, and the ending sequences. Unfortunately, of these only the Nomai narrative was compelling which is rather sad since the game spends a fair bit of time attempting to invest you into individuals from your civilization. The sequence of events to finish the game are also narratively unsatisfying. It felt like an attempt to quickly paste together a shaky narrative with no emotional through-line via a sequence of evocative, if hollow, events. Honestly, for all of the game's desire to throw light upon the fragility of existence it has almost no answers for it. I wouldn't hve been irked by it had the game not brought the topic up on the first place.Regardless, I think that much of my lack of enjoyment in this title stemmed from me not realizing that this was basically a puzzle platformer, a genre I dislike, and that the narrative relied on themes of existential dread with zero discussion beyond a flimsy conclusion. If you're into puzzles and platforming, if you're into fun simple music, and if you don't mind philosophical discussions being iffy then get this game. It's good. If none of those check your boxes then save your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I do already have 15 hours in Epic Launcher, if that means anything to you.This is the best video game I have ever played.  Sure there are good games out there, but they always fall short of the full extent of the medium.  RDR2 won't let you wander off during mission, Uncharted needs to you follow the action setpiece one particular way.  But Outer Wilds.  ♥♥♥♥ dude.  Outer Wilds lets you go where ever the ♥♥♥♥ you want, when ever you want, it's just a matter of you knowing how. And sure, Call of Duty looks more realistic every year, and who even pays attention to the music?  But Outer Wilds.  The music is part of the game, it's part of the narrative, it's part of the characters, it's part of the way you interact and traverse the world. The narrative weaves itself with the gameplay and gameplay stems from narrative so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ well.  It's the perfect intersection of music, art, design, gameplay, tech, and story, where each bit has to do with everything else.  When your character closes their eyes, there's two lids, because your character has two rows of eyes.  They paid attention to everything.  I don't know if this is the ultimate coincidence of game development where everything slotted perfectly into place, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, they did it.  It's the best game I've ever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ played.  Like I need you to believe me.  Sure I have more hours in No Man's Sky and Shadow of War.  But Outer Wilds.  It was the most fulfilling game that actually embraced what it means to be a game to as much of an extent as I can imagine.  It's the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ best game I've ever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ played.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why this is overwhelmingly positive. If you like a story based exploration game just buy this, don't read anything up about it, don't watch anything, just play it, it's 100% worth the money.This is a game that's all about discovering the story yourself, nothing is there to tell you "go to X and do Y", there's no right or wrong way to play it, you simply start out with a bit of an introduction in how to get out into space then you just decide where to go. As you venture out you discover things, read the information you find (it's really quite concise and to the point) and put those bits of information together to work out what you can do next. The universe is scaled in a way that nothing feels like a drag to get to, there's a few challenging bits sure but I never felt like it took too long to get places or that I couldn't find some new piece of the puzzle.My only negative really is the ending, but that's more of a personal thing since it's one of those 'open to interpretation' things but I won't go into details since it'd be a major spoiler.The long and short is I completed it in 17 hours in 2 days, the way you learn the story as you go by your own discoveries is an incredibly fresh way to tell a story in a game that kept me wanting to learn more and to go explore other places to know the how, what and why's. Well worth the money, I just wish I could wipe my memory to play this again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a really unique experience for me. Exploring the tiny solar system as a funny, four-eyed alien, looking for answers and finding out about the history of an extinct high-technology alien race whose legacy is artifacts all around the planets and an endless time loop in which the protagonist is trapped was heaps of fun, wonder, surprise, and sometimes also frustration because of some of the puzzles. If you want to try something out of the ordinary "go there and shoot that" stuff, I highly recommend this game. The world, the design of different planets, the music, the ideas that are often light and funny but go also surprisingly deep, work together as a whole. It is an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game, of all time. So obviously it's going to be hard to talk about it fairly. Also you're not supposed to talk about Outer Wilds, everything is a spoiler and I will not wish anybody to get spoilered on this particular game, it is too special. So what to say?I think you need to be a space nerd to love this game. The amazing things about Outer Wilds is that it takes all the cool space concepts, the things you can hardly picture when NASA tells you there's a planet that is doing that in a distant part of the milky way, and it amp them up to 11. Living through some of those things is just so incredibly cool and unnerving. Every planet you visit has a different concept that is every time just... So cool. They fit so much soul and so much nerdiness in such a teeny tiny solar system. The first twist is amazing. You're immediately like "what the ♥♥♥♥ just happened" and then you're hooked. You need to understand. You're following an ancient civilization, you're armed with the first translator for all the writings they've put everywhere in the solar system. And they are themselves just so personable. Following their fate is incredible. The music score associated with that alien race is beautiful.Next the humor is lovely. Not too heavy handed, just a darling. The ambiance, the music... The graphics are simple but I find them quite beautiful. Everything has been thought through. There's so many moments you are like "oh my god, this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game". Don't spoil yourself. Don't watch any big idiot youtuber play it while not giving a ♥♥♥♥ about the story. Just try it for yourself....And then try again once you get a better hang of your ship.

_childDocuments_.review: You know how early films look a lot like plays?Wide shots, exaggerated movements, and not a lot of action happening on the z-axis: films made with the mindset that the screen is just a stage curtain? Eventually they evolved into something that could never be captured on stage. Montage editing, shot variety, etc. And you know how some films are considered a giant leap forward in that progression?Outer Wilds is one of those for video games.It is very hard to find narrative, immersive  games that I feel are truly built for the medium. I get it; games are relatively young as a medium -- especially high-fidelity games not insanely limited by technical limitations.But Outer Wilds is it -- maybe the most built-for-the-medium video game I have ever played.Games like Myst, Portal, Firewatch, & Superliminal are my some of my favorites. I love puzzles, "walking simulators", & immersive worldbuilding. Outer Wilds wonderfully combines all the best elements of these in a way that's so original and polished that it feels like a real step or three forward -- "If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants" and all that.The real standout thing in Outer Wilds is how tailor-made it is for the gaming medium without ever just giving game-y things a pass -- and doing so in a way that feels obvious & effortless. Bullet sponginess is just a thing in shooters, for example. Adventure games are full of waist-high walls and ledges that can only be grabbed if they're a certain color. Walking simulators limit their gameplay to cardinal movement and QTEs. Repetition, reloading, & respawning are are both core to the medium while also existing in a sort of logical blind spot. Occasionally these things are given a thematic, in-universe justification or are part of some meta-textual higher layer. But usually not. And even when they are, it's sort of on the periphery.Outer Wilds is quite literally built around the game-y things that we're all accustomed to. Heavy elements of puzzle games, walking simulators, physics sandboxes, platformers, and more; it combines and reworks them into something that is neither a self-aware deconstruction nor a loose sandbox. Absolutely nothing is chocked up to "well, it's a game".It is a cohesive, immersive, consistent world that is entirely it's own and inextricably a video game in the very best way.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply beautiful. This game made me shed a tear, or two... or dozens. But I beg you, don't mistake it with Outer Worlds, those are absolutely different games. You get nothing but clues and story that'll lead you to the new places, solve new secrets and finally discover what really happened with the previous inhabitants of this system and why does the sun keeps on exploding, just as all the others stars you can see at the sky. In this game everything makes sense and is connected. OST also is one of the greatest ones. Game also has some secret endings. If you're going to feel "too free" with everything avaible from the start, just use your ship logs to see what do you have to discover and where should you go next. I personaly advise not to bruteforce anything, since there's solution for everything, but feel free to test whatever you want, maybe you'll discover something interesting ;). Good luck hatchling

_childDocuments_.review: A space exploration game that challenges you to learn the rules of physics, which are considered to be highly accurate, and the rules of the game. you explore different planets, meet other explorers and uncover a large mystery as every 22 minutes time loops and the game begins again from the beginning. Much like a rogue-like game where you die and come back to beginning but keep some items, in this game you don't get new items but you learn new things which give you these galaxy-brain moments that makes you want to continue exploring.The story is unraveled piece-by-piece as you delve deep into the darkest and most dangerous corners of the system. It's an incredibly beautiful story with a message that will stick with you long after you've completed the game as each moment is something you worked hard to find.The music is heartfelt and beautiful. and manages to fit into the world of the story in a magnificent way that has made a permanent home in my head. This is a masterpiece. A perfection of exploration. If you're like me you will almost be afraid of venturing further into the most hidden areas of the game but that's the beauty of the exploration, the fear of the unknown reaches of space and this executes that feeling of adventure wonderfully as it is YOU who decides what to do and where to go next.The DLC; Echoes of the Eye, is with out a doubt in my mind one of the greatest DLCs/expansions. It takes that feeling of both fear and wonder of the vanilla game and amplifies it. If the vanilla game had you awe in wonder this will stop you dead in your tracks. It's actually amazing what they've been able to accomplish with this DLC, let alone the original game. It's added to the game in a way where it feels like a natural part of the world but a major part of it feels separated as it's own game almost (it will make sense if you play it) You can technically do this whenever you want but I would suggest you finish the vanilla game first then go back and play this DLC. it doesn't exactly spoil anything BUT it is a wonderful addition to the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot possibly undersell how amazing this game has been. I previously beat the game on an Xbox. I re-bought it to experience the DLC in VR (Using the NomaiVR program (Support them separately, they are doing great work)). I have been a gamer my whole life, starting with an Atari and Nintendo as a child and progressing through to now and I can tell you with no doubt that this is my favorite game ever. The joy of exploration and satisfaction of discovery are incredible in the game. Please, give this game a try.If you have a VR headset, I even more emphatically recommend this game. The only reason to skip out on that is if VR can make you queasy, as it is a wild ride.If this developer manages to capture the magic they put into this game into any future games, I will be floored. This has the feel of a real magnum opus, and I cannot possibly expect any combination of talent, creativity, and time out of this team to trap lighting in a bottle like this again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly one of, if not, THE best game I have ever played. The story is extremely immersive and complex, the exploration is exciting, and the dialogue is hilarious. You can easily delve deep into the clues all around the system and try to piece everything together because the information is so well presented within the game. Not only are the puzzles challenging, they're also tons of fun to do and most can be solved in a variety of ways. If you ever need to go back to something, there's no tedious backtracking since the map is so easy to traverse, and also loads of fun to fly around in. Every time you go someplace, you'll probably find something that you missed last time you were there, or have a breakthrough in your investigation.This game is truly a masterpiece and I look forward to discovering more and more secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T READ REVIEWS IF YOU HAVEN'T PLAYED IT ALREADY!Wow, just wow. This game is a once in a lifetime experience. You can only play it for the first time once and that's the only downside this game has. But it's an awesome experience, that will stay with you.This game feeds of your curiosity, the developers and writers are masters of feeding you crumbs, so you follow clues from one planet to another. You have always something new to explore, while it never holds your hand. After starting the game, after a brief tutorial it's just you and the several planets of your solar system. You can go wherever you want to and nothing will stop you. I also like to describe this game as a metroidvania, where instead of items or skill to progress to the next part, you acquire knowledge. Nothing ever changes in the game, the only thing changing is your perspective and i think that's an awesome concept i've never seen before. And while some people will feel negative about there not being any quests, any action nor combat, if you are a naturally curious person that wants to experience a great story, this one is for you. Also great atmospheric music, thanks Andrew Prahlow!Highly recommended, 10/10.PS: Currently playing the DLC and so far it didn't disappoint. Hoping for the best.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games I've ever played.  Best to go in knowing as little about it as possible.  If you think games absolutely need quest markers, you probably won't like it.  You will need to put the pieces together yourself, in fact every system in the game supports a sense of discovery.  Artstyle, soundtrack and gameplay all resoundingly propel the experience forward.  Hats off to the developers, I can't imagine anything that could have been improved upon, except having more of it.  Very few bugs, a well polished experience unless you set out to try and clip through walls or something.  The game is not annoyingly difficult, nor is it boringly easy.  Not too short, not too long, although I wish there was more.  Absolutely worth the price, not a single major negative thing I can think about it, and a load of positives.  If it interests you, try not to spoil yourself on anything.  It's the sort of game you can only truly experience once.
