_childDocuments_.review: Testament is a competent adventure game, but it falls short of Cyan's classics. It's like baby's first Cyan game. The puzzles are all contained to one small area, and most only involve a couple moving parts. I find myself missing the deeper lore and esoteric puzzles with alternate writing systems etc., but for someone who gets overwhelmed by a more intellectually demanding puzzle game, this could be exactly the right level.I do think that the design of the game suffered a bit from the conscious centering of VR play. The adjunct just flattens the design space of every interactable in the game, and even when you couldn't do more than one or two actions with that object anyway, having the extra layer between you and the thing you're using is not a positive for immersion or fun. And it's not like it's massively better in VR -- having to pick up the adjunct and then fire it at things feels just as unnecessary. The adjunct does try to justify itself by eventually gaining the ability to "chain" between interaction points, possibly also carrying an electric charge... but I have yet to see that really pay off.Also, everything feels very slow. There's a lot of filler padding out the distance you have to walk, and even with that this does not seem like a long game. I have yet to beat it, but excluding the time I lost realizing that I was hopelessly stuck in a bugged state, I'd be surprised if this takes me over 8 hours. (Note: I had previously had this review as Not Recommended due to this bug, but Cyan helped me fix my save file, and I believe they are fixing the original bug)This is worth playing if you're looking for an atmospheric, immersive and cozy puzzle and exploration game. But if you like Cyan-style games for the cleverness of their puzzles and the depth of their worldbuilding, you will likely be disappointed by this relatively sparse and straightforward offering.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I was a kickstarter backer for this game.I want to start this review with a short story. Many years ago, when I was a young kid, I found a copy of Myst at a thrift store. I wasn't sure what it was, but it looked pretty so I got it. After figuring out what I was supposed to do, I was hooked. Then I found Riven, and voraciously devoured it. Ever since, I've been a huge fan of Adventure games, and Cyan especially. I didn't back Obduction on Kickstarter, but picked it up during a sale. I was curious what Cyan had been up to since the Myst series ended, and I was pleasantly surprised by it. It was a nice blend of the beautiful art style Cyan was known for, a very interesting world, and some interesting puzzles.Firmament is a game that after I completed, I had to sit and think about for a while. I can't simply recommend it like I can Obduction, but while I see and understand a lot of the criticism expressed in other reviews here, I can't recommend against it either. There are things that I think really, really work about this game, like the very interesting art style that absolutely fits with the late Edwardian era. There are some great moments where things click into place, and I got really invested in everything the game was doing. But then there were some puzzles where I got extremely frustrated, because of either weird controls/limitations, or just opaque design decisions. And some where I felt just as frustrated as I did during Myst 4's infamous frequency puzzle at the beginning. Yet...despite all the negative, I can't help but say that I came away from the experience charmed. There are some moments and set pieces that genuinely awed me. And even the annoyance of some puzzles couldn't detract from the sense of wonder that exploring the world gave me.So while I've recommended this, I think you should know that my recommendation is based on a preference of mine: I will put up with bad puzzles if the world and story are there. I played Ring: Legend of the Nibelungen for god's sake. If you prefer a well-balanced adventure game with equal care given to narrative and puzzle design, then I'm afraid Firmament may not be for you. It's a flawed game, but I am still glad I spent the time with it that I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a typical Cyan game. Unfortunately I don't mean that as praise, specifically. This game was developed with such a single-minded focus on the restraints of VR that it pared back significantly on every aspect of game design that are the hallmarks of Cyan's work: rich and deep worldbuilding, interesting characters, a complex story that unfolds organically as you play, and puzzles that are integrated into the world in a plausible way. All of these elements are severely lacking compared to Cyan's previous games. Even the graphics are not especially good; presumably if they were better, the game wouldn't be able to run in VR for most computers. If you're looking for anything other than a VR-focused puzzle experience, you're likely to be disappointed.So why am I still recommending it? Because it's still a solid video game with difficult but mostly fair puzzles, and evocative architectural and environmental design, and worth the cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Technical and polish issues aside, Firmament was a wonderful experience, and one of the most substantial VR games I've ever played. The worlds here, while not necessarily graphically impressive, are beautiful thanks to great art direction, and they're easily the most wonderful places I've ever had the pleasure of exploring in VR. Huge landscapes, dilapidated facilities, and jaw dropping set pieces kept me engaged the entire playthrough. Some nice ambient sound and a solid soundtrack are the icing on the cake.The game design itself is also great, though not perfect. Cyan made a lot of very smart decisions here to ensure the game was well suited to VR. The adjunct is a clever way to ensure all interactions are hard to miss and easy to understand, and it completely circumvents an issue I had with Myst where many of the switches and levers in that game just didn't feel good to interact with. I would  to be able to push buttons and throw switches, but if Cyan doesn't have the resources to ensure they all feel good then the adjunct is a solid solution.The puzzle design here is also suited very well to VR, as they mostly focus on figuring out how to use self-contained mechanisms to your advantage. This means there's no need to take notes and no need to travel back and forth over long distances. I will say the puzzles are largely on the easy side, and a handful of them feel like they could be solved just by trying everything until it works, but there are also several good "aha!" moments and even then, just being able to waltz into a factory and mess with the equipment in it is something that we've all wanted to and it's fun doing that in this game! Unfortunately there are a couple that feel more like busywork than fun, but they don't bring the experience down too much.The game's OST is solid, but not amazing by any means. It's got some cool sounds that set the mood well, but it lacks memorable moments and melodies.One of the weaker aspects of the game IMHO is the story. The story itself is cool enough, but (Very general spoiler regarding how the game handles the story) With all that said... Bugs. There's a lot of 'em right now. Lots of missing polish too. Thankfully I only managed to encounter ONE softlock (Yay?) on my playthrough! When you play, save often, alternate between save slots, and ALWAYS save before interacting with a complex moving object, there's a chance it'll get permanently stuck. Major bugs aside, there's also stuff like missing sound effects, janky elevators (I'm sorry Cyan but there's literally no excuse to not at least throw a smooth step function on all those elevators), the nauseating Camelus (Again, literally no excuse for that thing to not have acceleration/deceleration and for it to not respond according to the degree of rotation being applied to the socket. Linear movement like that is a huge no-no in VR), some lackluster sound design and animation moments (Better than Myst, but still not great. I wish the sound and animations of these old mechanisms actually suggested they were old and worn down. There are also a handful of moments where sounds pass through walls or when expected effects, like a lowpass filter when underwater, aren't applied), graphical issues in VR (I'm using a 4090 and made sure my drivers are up to date), I could probably go on with more individual issues, but yeah, there's a lot of stuff I hope Cyan fixes and improves upon here. The game probably should have spent some more time in the oven, but I don't want to spend too much time harping on these issues as when you get past them there's a really cool game here.I definitely recommend Firmament, especially if you have the hardware to play it in VR. VR is definitely lacking in experiences as substantial as this, so I think it should be on any VR enthusiasts radar, even if it might be best to wait a little bit for more bugs to get ironed out. Of course, VR aside this is still a great game and an amazing world worth exploring!
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great game! Loved the environments and aha moments! generally the puzzles were not as hard as other cyan games but they were not easy either and provided me with leisure challenges where i did have to really observe and think instead of force my way though. there were a couple of glitching moments but nothing a reload of my save file didn't fix easily.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Sharing some quick thoughts as I'm just about 4 hours in: you'll like this if you're a fan of Cyan-type games. Cyan is taking a different approach with this game, while older MYST games usually have you approach individual puzzles with their own unique mechanics to learn in the area they exist in, Firmament takes one mechanic (The Adjunct) and uses it across world-spanning scenarios. Since the world building deals with fantastical art-deco-inspired machinery, the puzzle mechanics feel supportive of who you're supposed to be and how you're supposed to be doing it. As someone who played Obduction previously, I'll say I'm finding Firmament to be a more accessible and enjoyable journey so far by comparison. CYAN's artists have really given it their all this time, the amount of fully bespoke assets they had to create for this game is crazy and I'm finding myself pausing just to look at the environments from some of the overlooks the devs lovingly build around the realms. The DNA of CYAN as a developer is on full display in this game, they've always had their own ways of doing things, and it's a real treat to not see such an old developer simply rest on the laurels of one smash-hit game -- as a still-independent studio, I'm actually not sure how Cyan made this in the time frame they did. I'll update this review as I get further along, but for my $35 I'd say it's worth checking out for the genuine Cyan formula.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok, but i was expecting something along the lines of riven or myst, but this is very surface level in comparison. Most of the puzzles are just logic. No notes or deeper thought is required to solve them. The only puzzles that took time was because one was figuring out math and routing of a circuit (that gets reset and you have to do again) and one was searching for switches. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently I've backed "Crane Simulator 2023".Lackluster performance aside and bugs, what is presented here isn't something I expect from Cyan. The context based remote thingy already made me suspicious but what you actually do with it is so unbelievably boring I don't even want to play any further. Where are the machines, levers and buttons that I've no idea what they are doing? There's no mystery here. Plug your blue electric beam in the same sockets and read what the command prompt says. Press Q and E for fun. Nobody gave any thought that you actually SEE what you're doing. Even the very first puzzle is a total stinker from visual design because you can't see what you're doing half of the time.If this was any other company I'd probably don't give a thumbs down but I'd also have never bought this game because the premise alone stinks.I haven't read a single thing about Firmament before. Just the track record of Cyan and also backing Obduction very early on, made Firmament an instant-back, no questions asked kind of deal. I also haven't followed Obduction and oh boy, was that a trip, such a fantastic game from start to finish.Eventually I'll play this further but the first hour was SO BAD, I had to make this rant. Hopefully it will get better and I can enjoy it for what it is. In that case, I'll update the review. If it stays like that, wait for a deep sale or better yet, don't bother because there are way better puzzles games out there.edit: I've finished the game and I won't change this review. Not a single puzzle was fun. The good thing about it, there's only a handful. I've played 7 hours and left the game running for at least 1-2. The story is okay but after a terrible game, who cares about the beautiful graphics and music? I don't even want to get into the story, mostly because of spoilers but also because the execution of the idea is so underwhelming and barely makes any sense even if you suspend your disbelief. The idea though is very interesting and in more capable hands this could have been something great to talk about.So, I really don't know what happened to this game. It's apparent that something went wrong because nobody can tell me 5 years of work went into it. Maybe for a new studio and their first game but not for an industry veteran like Cyan which are quite used to make these kind of games. I think, what we got is merely the corpse of what Firmament should have been.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Firmament is a great game. The visuals are stunning and the story is very good as I would expect from a Cyan game. However I do have mixed feelings about the puzzles being easier than I would expect from a Cyan game. While on the other hand I think it helps players, from my personal preference I really enjoyed the harder Cyan puzzles such as the ones that were in Obduction and the Myst series. Sometimes stuff gets stuck in the geometry but you can use Teleport to Safe Spot in the options to fix that. Overall though this was a great game and a really enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this! If you're expecting a game that's exactly like Riven, say, you'll be disappointed - I think Cyan did a great job of optimizing the game for VR users and other folks who don't want to have to stop to take down a lot of notes, and I think that threw a lot of die-hard Cyan fans from the old days for a loop. What you'll get in this game is a lot of accessible, well-designed puzzles with a reasonable (not impossible) level of difficulty, and (in my opinion) the most consistency stunning visuals of any game that Cyan has ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, not great.  The puzzles were, for the most part, a bit too easy.  None were too hard, either, although there were one or two "hunt a pixel" type moments.  I generally enjoyed myself and got exactly what I was expecting from a Cyan game.  The only thing that really annoyed me was the info dump from a narrator.  It was mostly fine, but went on for too long in a few cases.So I give it a 3.5 out of 5.  I deducted a half point for the narrator not spreading out the dialogue more, and one point because too many of the puzzles were a bit too easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome! We've been waiting for this game for a long time, my son and I played the first one together. The puzzles are great so far, and I'm really happy with the graphics as well. I really hope there's another game in the is style after this one, I don't mind waiting! It's a lot of fun for us to solve the puzzles together too. Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: This game is somewhere in the middle, which is why there is such a split on positive and negative reviews. Let's start with the good things. The background music is nice, the visuals are stunning, the realms and initial information you learn makes you curious, and the novel idea of the adjunct is an interesting add. The options you can change (like scroll speed) are nice, and being able to set yourself to run is a necessity.Now the bad. The puzzles are a letdown, especially considering what you expect from Cyan based on past games. Most puzzles are self contained, mechanical, require precise positioning and ordering, annoying to solve, and not as difficult as previous Cyan games. Some very frustrating. There is very little 'aha' and satisfaction, rather than feeling like "finally, I'm done with that really obnoxious puzzle". The exception to that might be the mixer puzzle. The story was not great. I was curious to know what happened, but let down by the ending. Everything is revealed right in the last 10 minutes of the game, with not much other discovery along the way. It wasn't really a very flushed out story. I found myself running around a lot to get from one place to another...sometimes things seemed so far away...you know where to go but the trek there was annoying at best. There is only one autosave, which is terrible because it updates every 10 seconds or so it seems and if you get locked in a bug your autosave does you no good since it saves so quickly. It would have been nice to have a lot of manual save slots, but you only have two. Then there are the bugs. I had a few along the way and if you didn't have a recent back up save you might have had to restart. I know these may get worked out but some of them were just insane - not being able to move or reach something at all and then being stuck there forever. The asking price, in my opinion, is too high. The game should only be about $20-$25 based on game length (for me, roughly 12-13 hours).So, why a positive rating? While the storyline is lackluster and the puzzles were often annoying, it was still fun to play overall and I liked the new ideas Cyan had. Plus the game is beautiful. I wish they would have upped the difficulty and variety in the puzzle department to match older games. Cyan fans of the older games will likely be somewhat disappointed like me, but people new to Cyan might find this just the right difficultly. It's a recommend, but only slightly.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Firmament, Cyan Worlds' next adventure game outside of the MYST universe, is an interesting foray into something new.  The game is not super long, and seems a bit empty, but overall is a good experience that highlights new stories and tales that Cyan wants to bring to the world.A few of the puzzles make you scratch your head.  I do think there could be more use of some of the puzzle solving methods earlier in the game so that you more intuitively know that it's something you can do.The whole story wraps up in a way I think does the game justice.  I just wish there was more at the end--perhaps a sequel or some written stores in the world?  I yearn to learn more!Overall, a game worth it for any MYST or adventure puzzle game fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Using AI to generate critical plot and narrative elements is completely unacceptable for a developer of Cyan's pedigree.EDIT: Assuming the devs' statement is accurate, then the game just is so poorly conceived and written that it reads like it was written by AI. Whether that actually makes it better or not is entirely up to your discretion, but given what's there and the way the use of AI was softballed in to begin with... nah.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game without any hints and without getting stuck. That means I liked it! So I'll recommend it... especially if you love first person puzzle games and Cyan. It's not without faults. There are some bugs that needed resets to fix. They leaned a bit heavy on the AI when making the game. The world building wasn't as deep as Riven or Obduction, and the narrative is kept pretty simple.The adjunct system is different from anything else Cyan has made, directing your attention and eliminating any guesswork as to what's interactive and what's not. If you're a fan of games like The Talos Principal and aren't into classic point and clicks, the spatial reasoning puzzles might be a welcome change. Cyan doubled, tripled and quadrupled down on platforms that move while you're standing on them; those were some of the most memorable puzzles in Riven and Myst and they're everywhere in this game from start to finish.It's not Cyan at it's most inspired. But it is a worthy addition to their body of work, and makes me excited for the upcoming Riven remake.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing Firmament - it has great environments and sounds and easy to moderate puzzles. Actually I like it better then Obduction which has in some parts more gorgeous graphics and more difficult puzzles.Firmament reminded me a lot of INFRA, the puzzle game where you try to operate/fix all sorts of engines.There were some bugs and glitches but they should be fixed with every new patch.I wish they had given us unlimited save slots but just two. I always like to save each new location to visit when i finally finished the game. Its fun to "stroll around" the worlds when all puzzles are completed.I hope Cyan makes enough profit of Firmament to invest in a new game, probably again with the help of Kickstarter, I would definitely invest again.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished.  This includes some time sitting at the menu.  I had been waiting a long time for this one.  I was a Kickstarter backer on this.  I played the VR proof of concept they released back in 2019.  I h ave played every Cyan game since the original Myst.  But after tearing through this game in two sittings, I am sad to say I can't recommend it.  The Good:The worlds are pretty, like always.  There were some interesting puzzles. (The conservatory puzzle was fun)The narrative went in some surprising directions, which I appreciatedThe Bad:Well, a lot.  :/The puzzles:They are all pretty intuitive, for the most part.  But so many of them were so tedious!  If you recall the rocket puzzle from Myst, or the teleport puzzle from Obduction, and you'll know what I'm talking about.  Several of the major puzzles require you to do a lot of walking just to try a solution out, and then, sometimes, you have to do more walking to see if the solution worked.  It doesn't sound bad, but it gets old.The puzzles also felt so small.  In Riven, there was a puzzle which required knowledge from each island.  In Obduction, you had to learn a number system and, if I recall, had to write down license plates for some puzzles to use as a code elsewhere in the world.  In this one, every puzzle is self-contained.  And most of them are just "move this thing over there"-style moving block puzzles.  They weren't interesting.  Bugs!  There were several times were major set pieces bugged out.  Or there were other times were I would stand on the edge of some moving object and then get stuck.  If you have to have a "Teleport to a safe place" feature in your game (Which they do, and which I had to use many times) then maybe your QA needs some work!Additionally, sometimes I would encounter some mechanism that I couldn't use for some indiscernible reason.  I would later discover that it had stopped working to "help" me move to the correct part of the game.  But when this would happen it always made me wonder if the game had broken.  Later, I am pretty sure the game DID break because a mechanism didn't present me the options I was expecting.  A "Teleport to safe space" did the trick in that instance.At one point I fell through the world into an empty void.The UXThe core mechanic of the game (using switches or ports to control mechanisms) really didn't work in every place that they tried to get it to work.  There is a spider-related usage of this mechanic that didn't work for me at all.  NarrativeThis was a big miss for me.  From the very beginning, I was underwhelmed (the opening of the game is less exciting than even the VR proof of concept's opening).  There is a voice in your ear for the entire game, and from a story perspective, I could never understand how this person knew what I was doing the entire time.  They are constantly commenting, and from a story perspective, it made no sense to me.It also felt like they took a major story inspiration from a well-known game series and did a Cyan riff on it.  That's not necessarily bad, but the Cyan riff didn't add anything, IMO.The ending comes quick, and dumps a lot on the player all at once.  And none of it feels earned.  Conclusion:If you are new to Cyan games, get Obduction, or the new Myst remake.  Wait on this one.  If you're a Cyan fanatic, get this one on discount.This isn't an issue about the bugs.  The game's design is the problem here.  As a longtime Cyan fan, I am really sad about this.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: This ain't it, mate. I Kickstarted it, and while I don't regret supporting Cyan after all the wonderful work they've done in the past, I can't in good conscience recommend this game. It has so very little going for it. Visually, it looks pretty good. Not quite as nice as Obduction could be, but also not system destroying, so I'll take that. The aesthetic is pretty decent too. That's about all the positives of note.Now for the negatives. The game may look good, but it also looks empty. The realms you visit are massive. Massive, sprawling, and dead. Prepare to run for ages between puzzles. The game looks good, but not good enough to make the travel anything but tedious. And slow, plodding tedium is the name of the game.The puzzles? Boring, uninspirired, and so very, very slow to solve. Everything that moves in this game take forever to do so. Loading between realms? Slow. Loading between subareas of realms? Slow. The progression of the story? I would say slow, but what story? Apparently there's supposed to be a narrator dropping tidbits, but her not saying a word beyond the intro seems to be a known bug, and it certainly hit me. Maybe the story is good, but I didn't get to experience any of it beyond the intro narration, all of about a half dozen lines, plus two whole lore books (of about 5 pages each).Honestly, I can't even call this mediocre. It wishes it could reach mediocrity. There's just nothing here worth seeing. All that's here is a broken mess, that stumbles along at a snail's pace. Even if the bugs were fixed, I'm not sure this would be worth playing. As it stands, I would only buy this if you want to support Cyan in hopefully making something worth your time in the future, or as a thank you for their past games. Your time, though? Your time is precious, don't spend it on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Review without spoilersFirmament is an exploration game with logical puzzles, which have to be solved to get access to all areas and finally to uncover the story behind the mysterious sceneries. It resembles to the games “Riven” (Myst part 2) and “Obduction”, also developed by Cyan, but the main differences to the former two games are the lack of story elements to be found while exploring the scenery and the usage of a new technique to interact with machines.The game seams quiet short depending on how you play the game: if you are in a hurry, it is possible to complete it in less than five hours; but if you explore the scenery and love to investigate the machines piece-by-piece, it will over a relaxing time with nice puzzles.Here are the positive and negative aspects of the game in short.Positive:* impressive scenery with a lot of details; * puzzles, which fit into the task of the explorer (find your way around obstacles), and which are not so hard to solve;* game with the fifth patch was played on a win10 system without any crashes;* the background music fits with the atmosphere of abandoned areas;* the technique to interact with machines is easy to learn, but also offers some interesting possibilities of combination.Negative: * only two slots for saving the game;* while exploring the areas a person is telling you some pieces of the story, but theses remarks are not stored anywhere (no journal available);* no exact task list is given to the explorer, and the overall target is not clear. This loses a lot of tension (be patient until the end);* almost no story is told while exploring the areas. You have to wait until the last chapter, which presents a big surprise;* the story told at the end of the game, does not perfectly fit into the explored areas; more artifacts about the story would have increased the tension to go on.Résumé:Firmament is a nice exploration game with a surprising end, but unfortunately it cannot reach the degree of tension as in the Myst series or in the game Obduction. Nevertheless, it is fun to explore the areas and solve the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Never played any of the Myst games or other Cyan games but lots of walking simulators and puzzle heavy survival horror games.Firmament starts out great. Epic environments, mechanical puzzles, subtle storytelling.But sooner or later the puzzles start to get tedious and you realize that they are not engaging or creative.Most of the time you need to do a specific sets of actions in a specific order, pen and paper are never required.You never need to search for clues or find them in the environment with few exceptions.Also some aspects of the puzzles clearly lack feedback. There are parts were you need to lock/unlock a device but there is simply no feedback...so is it currently locked or unlocked?Often you will be running around looking for sockets and the only way to reach them are some very specific angles and locations that can easily be missed.Compared to other puzzle heavy walking simulators (like INFRA) this game falls short of its potential. A bit more creativity in puzzle design and a bit less tedious mechanics and I would have given a positive rating.The deserted environments and the soundtrack are the highlights of the game. The story is rather confusing and does not make much sense in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Firmament has a beautiful design and artwork, a pleasure for the eye when you play the game. Surprising and original at times. The puzzles do not require much brainpower, however a few require very much patience and perseverance (good excercise for me, but I did not like it in the game).People who expect a sequence of Obduction might be a bit disappointed: the story is limited and it is not complex, you do not need to make maps to keep track where you are. On the other hand, people who do not like real mind binding puzzles and complexity can give Firmament a try and enjoy this game.So, I can recommend Firmament, but it does not get a A+.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game. The environments and puzzles are all well thought out and designed the way that Cyan is well known for. The environments are gorgeous and the story is captivating. Some elements feel they needed more development time or testing, but none of it is a deal breaker. Cyan is the OG of the first person puzzle genre and this creation is absolutely worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the worst games I've played because there's nothing redeeming or interesting about it. The world is lifeless and boring, the story/twist is dumb and honestly predictable (and even if you don't see it coming it's stupid) and the few puzzles are more frustrating than rewarding (especially in the stupid ice world). Save your money and don't buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful puzzle game from Cyan Worlds, in the Myst/Obduction style. About 14 hours game play from start to finish.I ran through it twice to make sure I'd seen everything, it's got a brilliant story line, and it's worth taking it all in and not rushing through it. Some of the set piece puzzles are tricky, and one lacks a bit of logic to the solve, but it's still a 5/5 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

_childDocuments_.review: Firmament looks like a Cyan game (in fact, it's gorgeous), but it does not quack like one. I'm shocked that this is what they put out as a final product. Game-breaking bugs and crashes aside, the actual gameplay and story are both lacking. Unlike the Myst series and Obduction, Firmament has gameplay and story that are both quite shallow, and at times, unimaginative or uninspired.I can't even say that the puzzles are decent - they're mostly poor. I'm used to seeing Cyan produce some of the very best puzzles in games, but the puzzles in Firmament are simply frustrating...for all the wrong reasons. They're almost all simple positional traversal puzzles. After a while, I found myself wondering when the puzzles were going to vary more or become interesting, but this is Firmament's schtick. A handful of the puzzles also lack sense. You'll solve them, but without a firm understanding of how or why something worked the way it did. That's terrible design and goes against Cyan tradition. Furthermore, many of the puzzles are very finicky. You'll find yourself understanding what needs to be done but getting frustrated because you're trying to fine-tune your control/movement to do so. You'll finally get the thing to move the way you want and then the game may randomly reposition it (or you) or just crash altogether, forcing you to re-do a bunch of frustrating gameplay. I had to do one of the more tedious puzzles 3 times...Cyan is great at creating those endlessly satisfying "aha!" moments and making the player feel accomplished for figuring things out. Firmament disappointingly misses on this front, lacking the thing I most enjoy about Cyan's other titles.I'll end with some positives. The developers clearly had a strong focus on the visuals. The game not only looks stunning, but the art and visual design are very interesting, and reminiscent particularly of Myst and Riven in some ways. I loved the environments...While the visual aspects of the game are amazing, I would hope that Cyan return more to their roots and shift the focus more toward story and gameplay for their future games, even if that means giving up some visual quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Firmament

name: Contraband Police
detailed_description: The year is 1981, and as a young officer trainee, you are assigned to work at a border post in the mountainous region of Karikatka. Entry into the Acarist People's Republic is strictly regulated by the party and your every move is monitored! The situation at the border escalates when your comrade is killed during one of the interventions... Document control Every visitor must have a set of valid documents. Even the slightest discrepancy means refusal of entry. Over time, the number of documents will increase and errors will be more difficult to detect. Smuggling detection Our intelligence regularly provides information about suspicious drivers. Search their vehicles using a UV flashlight and then use the appropriate tools to extract the smuggled goods. No amount of contraband should cross the border! Shootouts In some situations you will be forced to use firearms. Your station is a constant target for Oberankov's gang attacks, and every away mission carries the risk of a clash with the enemy. Police chases Desperate smugglers may attempt to escape from the control zone. It is your duty to stop and arrest them! Buy and upgrade police cars to improve the effectiveness of your pursuit. Post management Upgrade your police station to increase its defenses and improve subsequent inspections. However, keep in mind the rising cost of maintaining your station. Successful inspections, foiled smuggling and successful interventions are a few ways to earn cash. Special assignments Always be ready to intervene in an emergency. Solve crime puzzles, support your comrades and thwart the Blood Fist rebels. Make decisions that will determine the future of Acaristan.

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police was a very pleasant surprise. I think most of us expected a quaint "euro-jank" sim along the lines of Hobo Simulator or My Summer Car, but this game surprised me in many ways. First of all, the production quality is really good for such a small indie game. The looks, the graphics, the sound/music - while obviously not triple-A quality - are all quite good. The gameplay is interesting and engaging, both the "Papers, Please" style document and vehicle inspection part, the gunplay and even the story and side missions. While it's not Witcher 3, but everything is well written and the voice acting is great.However, what totally sold me about the game was the style. The 80's Eastern Bloc feel brought back vivid memories of my own childhood, growing up in barely-post-soviet Hungary, I've seen these cars and trucks (even driven/owned some of them), the architecture, the government propaganda, I drove through such border checkpoints, handing over your passport with mandatory bribe money folded inside (even if you didn't have anything illegal) so they don't take your car apart just for fun. Heard all the stories back in the day about the weird ways people were trying to smuggle stuff back home from "The West", cigarettes, booze, cassettes, VHS tapes, kitchen appliances, jeans and clothes, etc. The border guards, the police, everyone knew people were doing it, yet also everyone coveted the shiny new western stuff, so blind eyes were turned in return for a few "gifts" left at the crossing, the cost of doing business. It was a "live and let live" type of deal.Contraband Police captures this era of Eastern Bloc weirdness very well, just like "Papers, Please" did, albeit not as depressing. While "Papers, Please" showed the bleak, hopeless, harsh realities of trying to survive under such oppressive regime, Contraband Police is a lot less heavy-handed and brings some much needed levity and fun into the mix, not to mention a complete story with actual characters and multiple endings based on your choices.While the game is obviously not without faults, some bugs, glitches, imbalance and missing features, the devs seem to be actively working on fixes and additions (like the Endless Mode a lot of people have been requesting) so there seems to be some mileage in this game yet.In closing, Contraband Police is a very nice surprise. Instead of the run of the mill "eurojank" we got a very well made, fun and engaging sim that brings a huge load of nostalgia for those who lived these times and quaint enough to entertain those who didn't. Well done!Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: An [Okay] inspection game, similar to "Papers, please", but different with more things to do and a 3d spin to it.It has a great vibe and gameplay for the first couple of hours, but then, nothing really changes, and the game is more than twice as long as "Papers, please" and becomes repetitive and meaningless once money is not an issue.Lost interest once money was not an issue at all, easy to come by, and when realized that upgrades are somewhat meaningless, you get an extra space so you don't have to hassle that often to deliver prisoners/goods.There is no real complexity to the game nor real conflict with corruption or a choice of how to spend money, consequences, whom to trade the contraband, take risks, etc.Combat and side activities like interventions or main missions are very easy and give quite a lot of money in return which further simplifies the game. Since combat is also quite simple, the starting pistol is enough from start to finish, selling everything else provides a ton of money, but money doesn't buy anything useful.Since you get more money than you need, the game becomes quite shallow, simple inspection, and at that point, perfect inspections are simply not worth the time, as they give extra money that you don't need. Some variations would be great, more focus on inspection, maybe different tools/machines, different things to look out for, some form of management for other places, some kind of corruption scheme, something.Overall, it simply lacks complexity throughout the game and has a lot of shallow places that offer little to nothing in return.

_childDocuments_.review: I have had this game on my wish list since it was first announced. My opinion is that overall it is an ok game with the potential to be a really good game but there are some incredibly frustrating mechanisms getting in the way, namely combat, AI, and tools. Combat is not so bad but most of the weapons feel under powered. Next is tools and oh good God are they something, the tools are so weak it really takes away from the fun of the game. You will constantly have to go to a tool shop that is very far away in order to buy more or call to have them delivered, however if you have the police truck at your checkpoint then the tool delivery can not come. Also some tools allow for alternatives but others do not which makes no sense. For example you can cut with either an axe or a knife but you can dig ONLY with the shovel: not the knife, not the pitchfork, not the axe, not even your own hands. Have a mission where you have to dig three holes? better bring like 2 or 3 shovels, and ONLY shovels. Also your fellow AI customs officers are pretty useless, you can upgrade them all you want but they don't contribute anything to the actual searches of vehicles, delivery of prisoners or contraband, or to stop fleeing suspects. Its really frustrating to watch a suspect announce "I'm gonna run away!" then slowly get in his car and start driving away just to watch all 8 of your fellow customs officers do nothing to stop him at all, just stand there like cows while you have to do all the work. the only good thing the AI is good for is during raids on the base but the thing with the raids is that they can just be disabled from the menu, thus making the AI officers EVEN MORE useless.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so bare bones for being a fully-released title, I thought for sure it was an early access game. However, what I found was so incredibly addicting through its routine gameplay. I love the basic framework, but there are many things that still need improvement. I think this game would improve immeasurably if the devs focused more on the base building aspect of upgrading your own border control post and less on the repetitive driving around. Why are we the one to drive every prisoner and piece of contraband when you play as the commander of the post? I sincerely hope they add some kind of mechanic to control what your guards do, like making deliveries for you or posting up at a specific spot to better stop rogue smugglers. Having more than one vehicle makes this seem like a no-brainer, but I guess only you get to use the cars. Speaking of which, what is the point of arming your guards if none of them can stop any old person in a hatchback that decides to drive straight through? The guards seriously need to do SOMETHING in camp other than repel invaders. Being a one-man army just nullifies the point of having any other guards with you.That leads me to another gripe of mine: the random road ambushes. I actually ended up turning this setting off (thankfully that is an option), but the random ambushes add very little flavor to the gameplay. These events actively turn me off to engaging with them because they reward almost nothing and just take up your time. The random events need to be reworked significantly, but thankfully you can turn them all off for now. I am excited to see the addition of the endless mode, as I think it is just what this game needs to take a step in the right direction. I think this game needs an overall clearer vision for what it wants to be. Hopefully, he devs can take this solid framework and polish it into a true gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, my comrades, gather 'round for a tale of Contraband Police, a game that takes us on a wild ride to the gritty, vodka-soaked streets of a country in the '80s that's, well, let's just say it's got a certain Eastern European charm. Now, let me tell ya, this game is like a shot of pure adrenaline mixed with the finest local spirits – it's a rollercoaster of smugglin', corruption, and choices that'll make your head spin. hicFirst off, the setting, my friends – it's as Slavic as a hearty bowl of borscht. The developers have nailed that grim, era-appropriate atmosphere with rusty cars, drab buildings, and a soundtrack that'll make you wanna dance the night away. You're a border guard, tasked with stopping the flow of contraband and fighting corruption, but here's the kicker – you can choose to be as clean as freshly fallen snow or as dirty as a muddy puddle. hicThe gameplay, oh, the gameplay, it's like a babushka's stew – a mix of ingredients that somehow just works. You inspect vehicles, scan cargo, and interrogate suspicious characters. The attention to detail is impressive, my friends, from examining documents to searching for hidden compartments, it'll make you feel like a true detective of the borderlands. And don't even get me started on the car chases – they're more thrilling than a drunken bar brawl. hicNow, about that corruption, you can choose to take bribes and bend the rules. It's a slippery slope, my comrades, but it adds a layer of realism and moral ambiguity that'll leave you pondering your choices like a philosopher with a bottle. Will you uphold the law or succumb to the temptation of, well, let's just call it local currency? The choice is yours, my friend. hicThe story, well, it's like a novel filled with twists, turns, and morally gray characters. You'll meet shady smugglers, corrupt officials, and folks just trying to survive in this harsh world. The writing may not be Nobel Prize material, but it's engaging enough to keep you hooked. hicNow, let's talk about the graphics, they won't knock your socks off, but they do the job. The world is gritty and authentic, and the characters have that certain Eastern European charm, even if they look a bit rough around the edges. hicIn conclusion, Contraband Police is a game that'll take you on a journey to a bygone era of intrigue and corruption in an unnamed Eastern European country. It's as Slavic as a bear wrestling with a bottle, and the choices you make will have you questioning your very soul. So, my friends, pour yourself a shot of the finest local spirits, grab your headwear of choice, and dive into this adventure – just remember to keep your morals intact or get lost in the depths of corruption. hic Na zdraví, comrades!Wodka.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Enhanced dyslexia and colorblind tester. An example of how a good indy game should be. Addictive gameplay loop, that progressively challenges you, various side activities and on top of that a small campaign based on your actions. It recreates the atmosphere of the cold war era and while visually definitely not next-gen, it does give off that old skool games look of the early 2000's with a modern filter on top. Love that look of drivers humorously rolling down their windows. And many other quirks in the game. I have not experienced any bugs but beside that one time my cars drivewheels got air while my tail was dug in a small hill, due to my own fault. I had a prisoner inside and couldn't get anywhere. Luckily this game has fast travel and this reset my vehicle and I could continue my mission without restarting. I would not recommend fast travel for anything else than fixing a stuck position, the campaign only last about 16ish hours without fast travel for me. Completing all side-objectives and occasional equipment/contraband/prisoner-runs in the campaign. Do note, I got quite productive with checking cars, there are aids but I would not recommend this game if you have dyslexia or colorblindness. It will turn into a point and clickgame if you use the aids too much and the game's charm is in finding the faults in the details you personally find. The only time I use the aid was to pinpoint the tints of colors. The game is not difficult per-se, but you will find yourself struggling if you try to rush things, prioritize your tasks and then take your time. The game luckily won't hold your hand too much but with a bit of logical thinking, structuring and utilizing the game's many manuals and tools you always have a grip on any situation. Practice makes perfect. You can always reload your day.Some things that are a bit too rough around the edges like combat, can suck out the otherwise fluid gameplay loop. It's still nice to have combat as a break from checking and expanding on the campaign, but it doesn't work smoothly enough to be thrilling. Driving is barebones but the chases are a nice distraction anyway. One thing that was a bit too much were the color tints during checks. Im not colorblind but I would like it if i could compare tints of colors right next to each other. Now my manual opens on the right and the document is on the left. The only time I was able to distinguish colors were when it was a totally different color, but most of the time you have to identify small changes in tint from one end of the screen to the other.    I recommend not upgrading too much too early, your income is based on your level and while you have the freedom to do anything you want, making things expensive early on will put a lot of pressure on you for not making any faults to survive another day. Slowly upgrade the things that you need the most. You will eventually level up and make more cash.On a sale this is a ton of fun for the money. I prefer to have a short solid indie experience that delivers a specific niche/mood than an expensive politically safe triple A time sinker with too much fetchquests any time of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is seriously lacking polish. I don't know if it wasn't proofread or just poorly translated, but some of the written instructions contradict what the game actually wants you to do. Some of the time when you fail for "entry regulations" it's not at all obvious what the problem was. It's a cool idea that actually doesn't resemble Papers Please as much as I thought it would, being more about the inspections than the paperwork, but still needs a bit more work before I'd recommend it. Also a minor gripe, but where Papers Please had numerous factions you could choose to side with and you were incentivised to move quickly, this game has pretty much two sides: government or rebel, and it doesn't really focus on speed. Now granted, the fact that it differs from Papers Please is still a good thing, but I think the speed pressure of Paper's Please was one of its best features, turning time into a resource you had to choose where to spend.

_childDocuments_.review: Minor edit as I don't feel like rewriting the whole review at this time, much of it is still somewhat relevant, but at least the biggest issues can be somewhat alleviated (disabling ambushes, increasing times-cale, etc). section no longer really applies, as the devs have added the possibility to change the timescale (default is 1 day = 20min, you can 'tripple' this to 75 minutes = 1 day, which is ample time to do stuff). This no longer function as an infinite ammo-glitch as enemies drop more than just ammo, however it is still far too frequent and feels tacked on and not balanced around. This is still the case\issue. Time limits upon time limits existing to do nothing but make you drop whatever you're doing to do it all 'now, now, now'. Very annoying.--For the most part the game is enjoyable\fun, but I can't really recommend it in it's current state.So why I don't recommend it;While this isn't\wouldn't be an issue in and off itself, plenty of games have time management as an important gameplay mechanic, this game however does not. Time Management feels like it was put into the game, because Papers please had it. Currently, it serves to limit you from doing "too much" in a single day, while simultaniously expecting you to do "everything" in a single day.Every few days you get further restrictions and complexity to the inspections (this is good, not a bad thing), that serves to take away your time more and more (inherently not necessarily a bad thing). Then, once you've finished the (increasingly complex) inspections, you have to transfer prisoners (with little\no time left), give contraband away, purchase new tools to find contrabands with, and\or get ammo.It is far too frequent. It devalues the experience, ontop of serving as an infinite ammo-glitch (as you get more pistol ammo than you know what to do with). There's essentially 3 types. Story missions (unskippable), Side-phone missions (5 minutes to answer, then 5 minutes to do it), Side-mission events (F2 to answer, have about 1-2 minutes to press F2 or you lose it, so better not be doing anything else after an inspection! Like a prisoner transfer, or you'll lose out on cash!).Time-limits, and\or the missions\events themselves are fine. The issue comes in how everything relies on "do it within this time-limit, within this time-limit!", while constantly drowning you in increasing amount of stuff.A standard (later\mid-game) day:  You do a couple of inspections, double and tripple checking the paperwork (3+ different ones that has to be cross-checked, + the cargo lists). Maybe you even arrest a smuggler. Then you get a phone-call (5 min to answer, 5 min to do the mission, have to drop everything else), so you run up and do this. On the way you get an ambush that destroys all 4 wheels of your car (which bugs out the physics a bit and you now barely can drive forward). You do the mission, then try to get back. By the time you're back, it's late afternoon with another couple cars or so to go through. By the time you've gone through, your prison is full, your inventory is full of contraband, so you then starts to unload.On the way to the prison camp, you get an ambush, totalling the car all over again (as you repaired it when you got back), wether you drive through or kill them make no difference to car totalling (except you'll recoup the repair cost if you kill them).You get to the camp, unload prisoners, then drive towards the base. It's now the next day, and you also get another ambush. Then after this ambush, you unload the contraband, decide you need more tools (as you're out of tools for searches), drive over to vlad, get the tools, and on your way back, another ambush.It's not difficult, it's not hard. It's just unenjoyable and serves no real purpose other than to drag out your time keeping you from the core loop of the game (inspections).  Doubly so as Ambushes give you the money to repair the car (once you get back), and recoup more than the ammo you spend (I use about 2-3 pistol magazines an ambush, and get about 6 back).Overall, I really enjoy the game. The core gameplay loop is great, and I definitely suggest getting the game, when\if these things gets addressed. As currently, these things just soils the experience (increasingly so).The changes introduced by Week 2 patch is welcomed and can be used as a band-aid, but I don't feel it addresses the real issues pointed out in my review, and so I still can't recommend it in it's current state. Hopefully the 3rd or 4th week patch (assuming we get that) addresses this, and I can change this from a not recommended, to a recommended review, as I think it's a great game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Comrade, you have been lucky enough to be assigned to a border crossing post. Serve and defend the motherland!Comparison with "Papers Please":  It does need to be said, this game and PP does share a very similar setting and job. Inspecting paperwork, looking for contraband, and allowing in those that pass the requirements. I will try not to state how I feel about each difference as opinionated answers may not reflect each individuals wants.Time: In PP, each day lasted a specific amount of time which forced the player to accurately and quickly determine the validity of each entry. In CBP, I do not believe that there is a time limit, with more focus upon smaller details. As the world is 3D, and having to document errors with each vehicle a time limit may or may not frustrate players. Game Play Loop: In PP, the game play loop was go to work, perform duties, start the next day with small cut scenes that would occur at set times. In CBP there are additional activities that will spring up such as story missions, immediate alternate missions, base invasions, and free roam to explore the area under the government's control. Money also feels different in both games. In PP, money was generally a hard consumable to obtain on first play through and that is the lifeline between your families life or not. In CBP, as long as you are adequate at your job money will not be an object, with additional ways to earn money. Due to having money not being a true driving force, I just bought everything relatively quickly.   Story: Although the story is certainly serviceable, and allows the player a branching system to stay true to the government or work with a rebel force to overthrow it, PP does it in a much more streamlined fashion. The rebels in CBP seem just rather inept, potentially because every couple of nights as you defend the base your team will kill dozens of them without a casualty. Music: Music was nice. Some of the music cues while working were rather relaxing. Graphics: I had no issues running above 60 fps. The bad: The main complaint I have is near the end of the game. The idea of this style of game is to start rather simple, and expand the demands of the player. At the beginning, you are asked to verify names, passport numbers, and expiration dates are valid. The end is demands much more, but without a time limit this really did not bother me. What did bother me was when forgeries become a possibility, and I could not get a good example of comparing the paper that was forged vs an authentic one. The only solution is to use the games compare system, where you click the item in question and compare it to what is in the book. No other time was this a requirement for any other system.Side complaint is interaction with the other characters. You will not find a Jorji here, you will not get a compelling story of reuniting lovers and trying to save the guards life so his wife does not immediately become a widow. You get put in some situations where people will plead about there circumstances, but the writing does not make me care about pointing out their documentation flaws and sending them back into the wild. Side complaint two. At times your base will be attacked by a waves and waves of rebels. After the first one, this becomes a chore to content with as no matter how quickly and efficiently you kill enemies, it is timed for up to four minutes. There are multiple ways to exploit this mechanic, and as much as I think the developers wanted to capture the players attention it really just got boring. It is weird to say the game where you make sure Bob is in fact Bob and he can enter your country offers a massive shooting section, but it is just boring to me. Final: A play through with one path was around 11 hours. Is it good? Yeah, I think it is. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a game. This game gets you immersed VERY easily. The story line for a SIM is Decent. The tasks you're required to do is not busy work nor fetch quests but rather you play the role of a detective, a defender and an auditor all at the same time. The detail involved for you to inspect areas of vehicles was really good, however, could be improved but considering this was released 12 days from this review, i can't complain. No complaints on the gun play honestly I enjoyed it. The driving can be a bit tedious at times since most times the places you need to go to are far from each other but the starter vehicle isn't half bad. However, I found that trading with the newcomers of the border to be pretty useless and quite unrealistic? (idk if IRL border officers trade items whilst on active duty with new comers only to arrest them for smuggling 5 seconds later xD). I managed to unlock and max out all weapons, vehicles, commodities and personnel without ever having to trade with any newcomer nor personally deliver the prisoners to the labor camp or contraband to the station. I always called vlad and prison transport to the border. Another thing that bothered me was the incoming Main quest calls and give you a timer to answer the phone calls forcing you to interrupt inspection, I think they should wait till all the cars are done clearance and then a phone call can happen cuz even then, I doubt a border control stops operating out of no where because an officer got a phone call about a murder that happened at a restaurant LOL. Also, the money you get to stop driving and eliminate the gang members shooting you isn't worth it AT All as you only get  $70 across all stages of the game. you can only buy 1 AK Mag with that. But I do very much believe the pros outweigh the cons by a mile. I think the price is somewhat justified if it continues to get updates and bug fixes and hopefully maybe a DLC expansion? Overall rating 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's just fun. (8/10)Pro -- Whilst simple, it is easy to become complacent which in turn forces you to focus to get it right; and for me that's a great thing. So many games become to easier and than boring, whilst this will penalise you when you forget or overlook something in the inspections.- I enjoy the ability to customise the base and than balance that against your income. You need to think, will this improvement be worth the cost of purchase and on-going costs to run. - I find comedy in the general interactions between my character and all the entrants or smugglers. - Their are good elements for morals/ethics decisions at play; do you accept a bribe to allow a man entry to save his family or enforce the law(s). The letters you receive later in the game give indications to how that worked out for those individuals.- I like managing/deciding on whether I take the arrested to the camp, go buy supplies or hand in my contraband after full-filling my duties at the post.Neg -- There is much interaction between you and your hired help, additional dialogue or purpose to them would be good; other than that they help you repel attacks.- Driving can be a bit clunky and whilst using your sirens whilst driving can occasionally cause accidents that hinder you, where you might fail in your task. Although it has made me laugh each time it has happened.  Possible growth - - It would be interesting to see if in the future that their is a barracks for the guards, not just separate upgrades for them; but something that required both. Eg, Barracks level 1 allows for the additional recruitment, whilst level 2 would allow promotion of the guards themselves. The barracks might improve their health and give a fortified position to repel attacks, whilst the individual promotions gives the better gear.  - Same as above, but improved cosmetics, better upgrades to the yard, no on-going costs, just up-front costs for fencing look, inspection areas etc.- The upgrades are dependent on your promotion/rank.Overall, its just fun and I look forward to how far I make it in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite on the level of papers please sadly...Now don't get me wrong this is a pretty good game, and if you liked the bureaucratic gameplay of that game then this will scratch that itch... To an extent. However its completely bogged down by superflous and completely mediocre gameplay elements that just have no real reason to be in the game. I'm a border control officer so why would I be driving around doing bloody tailing missions? I mean it doesn't make sense from a gameplay or logical standpoint. The constant phonecalls to go do some other random thing that has nothing to do with the border control is honestly annoying although mostly ignorable. I haven't completed the game so I've no idea if ignoring them has an effect though.It's just not necessary. In fact none of the "open world" elements are necessary or even fun at all. It just detracts from the main gameplay and lets face facts this isn't a triple AAA game, the shooting and driving mechanics are severely lacklustre at best. So why they decided to force you to drive around (being ambushed constantly) and do these really out of place missions and busy work is beyond me.It also detracts from the relatively rare moments that made papers please special. Like a dude begging to be let in to help his family but with a minor problem in his paperwork. This game does have that but so far I've had a lot more "chase this guy" "go follow that guy" "go here and do this" missions which, as I said, just feel out of place here.I'm also REALLY not a fan of the vehicle inspection elements. For some reason I just can't seem to ever get them right. Finding broken parts of vehicles sounds easy but almost all the vehicles are rusted piles of crap anyway and its super annoying to have a perfect score ruined by a missing bumper that you had no idea was supposed to be there in the first place.Now you're probably wondering why I'm recommending this game when I have quite a lot of problems with it? Well the fact is it is a pretty good game and doesnt deserve a negative review. It was released in better state than most AAA games and the devs seem active in the forums and are addressing at least the most egregious issues people have with the game. Namely the bad ambush system. So while I'm giving it a postive review I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. Basically i recommend it but don't expect it to become your most favourite game of all time.It's like the opposite feeling I had from papers please. Where I expected to hate that game and ended up absolutely adoring it. I expected to love this game and found myself thinking it was "just okay"
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Quick run down of my rants and praises. 9/10Pros- Shoot rebels and steal their contraband.- Make money from arrested and dead rebels.- Fun game for the price, I got more than I expected.- Defiantly worth a second play through, more than one ending.- Can become pretty challenging with the border checks, especially at the end with everything tied together and if you're trying to get perfect inspections. - Pretty interesting story and how fate is determined/events.- AI has ammo... not just 3-7 rounds when looted.- A studio that finally releases a finished product instead of a beta type release. - ProfitCons(Minuscule)-  AK has like zero recoil. Like a little tiny bit more would be welcoming... At least it's not ridiculously unusable in a sense where I can't hit a barn door 10m away. But I don't feel like I should be full auto hitting a watermelon sized target from 100m away.- AI bodies disappearing during or after gunfights really quickly, I want that ammo >:)- How tf does the commissar know who the smugglers are? If you already know just point them out homie, who's side are you on? Are you omnipresent? If I missed him I don't think it should fine you... just keep the chapter going until he tries to pass again.- Siren on loop. A very obvious start and stop. Idk if that's how it's suppose to be but it's annoying after about 2 minutes. - 5 minute time goals to be at an objective no matter where at on the map or what condition your in. Cons- Ambush mechanic. I feel like I'm constantly being attacked by rebels while on the roads.... And I mean like 2-4 times when I'm just driving a half loop around the small map. Also pretty much occurs after every incident. Main reason I didn't enjoy going out or exploring. I did notice it dropped a little towards the late game although I was making less frequent trips out. - THE FREAKING WHEELS ON THE SD2 whatever Geo Metro looking thing. If there's smuggled contraband in the tires goodluck trying to get to it. The wheel is so small you're practically never going to hit... you'll either hit the fender, the rim, or the ground. I've gone through so many types of tools trying to crack them open and nothing works. Also I've let so many go by with flat tires it's insane. Geo Metro OP. - Game is finished when storyline is finished. It would be nice to at least to get a warning that your gameplay is going to entirely be done for. - Shotguns have zero range. Pretty much useless unless right on top of someone. Save your money for a SMG or AK. I'd highly recommend this game. My biggest complaint is the ambush mechanic and how many there are. Like isn't this a totalitarian regime... where are all these rebels getting these weapons? Am I not doing my job at the border by catching all these vigilantes smuggling in weapons? Is Vlad behind this? Where is the Commissar and his all seeing eye watching me search these vehicles?I enjoyed the storyline and being able to pick a side to support although I wish the gameplay didn't end so abruptly. I had one more baddie on my list to catch but I suddenly got a call and took it and finished the game without even realizing it. Idk if I can sleep knowing there is still one smuggler out there that I didn't catch... Another annoying con was the siren on a loop... like it was obviously a loop and had a blatant start and stop. Also AK is extremely OP due to the recoil... like don't make it Tarkov level recoil where it's ridiculous but I feel like it's peashooter recoil level. Like just a smidge higher wouldn't hurt. Shotgun has no range also so, it's a no from me. Also I found the dead disappearing really quickly during a gun fight, kinda annoying when I'm low on ammo and I need those sweet sweet rounds (really nice on how the AI carries a decent amount of ammo though!).  Overall I'd highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a nice change of pace... One minute you're checking paperwork and letting cars through the toll, the next you're in a high speed chase or shootout with multiple baddies. Then right back to border checking papers and cargo. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me. I was expecting to patrol the boarder, stop contraband from entering, turning away people that don't meet the requirements and maybe get into a firefight if a traveller didn't like the outcome of their attempt at crossing the boarder. But I was heavily mistaken; There is so much more to this game than meets the eye. Open world, Resource manager, being a detective of sorts, a story with choice & good conflict, and the list continues.    My only gripes is that sometimes there will be contraband in the engine bay, however there isn't actually an there. Just a bug i'm sure. Another is the abundance of ambushes; Its very obnoxious repairing your vehicle only for it to be shot up about 30 seconds after leaving the boarder camp. If they were tuned down a little to be more rare, but made a little more difficult with more risk/reward. Would make them feel exhilarating & refreshing.    Overall I REALLY enjoy this game, I 100% recommend giving it a try.  [UPDATE] I have now finished the game, and would like to update this review;  My previous feelings and thoughts still stands however, upon finishing the game I was sadden to see the lack of any continuation or endless mode for the game. After you finish the final mission your whole save gets nuked. No way to continue playing on the save, no new mode unlocked, etc. I hope this is a feature coming in the future just because how great this game plays even without the story missions. You could still work the boarder, encounter ambushes of fellow gang members trying to break their comrades out of prison, do intervention missions, etc.  Still a great game, and I look forward to doing more playthroughs to chose the other choices.

Please note that my information is based on knowledge available up to September 2021, so there may have been updates or changes to the game since then.Title: "Contraband Police: A Gritty Dive into Border Enforcement"Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)"Contraband Police" offers a unique and gritty simulation experience, taking players into the challenging and morally complex world of border enforcement. While it has its strong points, the game does come with some notable drawbacks that affect the overall gameplay.Immersion in Law Enforcement: The game excels in immersing players in the role of a border police officer. The attention to detail in recreating the everyday tasks and responsibilities of a border patrol agent is commendable. The developer's dedication to realism is evident in the game's mechanics, such as inspecting vehicles, interrogating travelers, and searching for contraband.Moral Dilemmas: "Contraband Police" effectively explores the moral dilemmas faced by border officers. You'll be forced to make decisions that can have significant consequences, and the game doesn't shy away from presenting complex choices. This adds a layer of depth and authenticity to the gameplay.Challenging Gameplay: The game can be quite challenging, especially for players who enjoy a realistic and demanding experience. Keeping a close eye on details, managing your resources, and making judgment calls can be intense and rewarding.Limited Scope: Unfortunately, "Contraband Police" suffers from a somewhat limited scope. The gameplay can become repetitive as you repeat similar tasks over and over. There's also a lack of variety in the types of vehicles, travelers, and contraband you encounter, which can make the experience feel monotonous after a while.Technical Issues: As of my last update in September 2021, "Contraband Police" had its share of technical issues, including occasional bugs and performance problems. It's worth checking if these issues have been addressed through updates.Niche Appeal: The game's focus on realism and its niche theme might limit its appeal to a specific audience. If you're looking for a fast-paced action game, "Contraband Police" may not be your cup of tea.In conclusion, "Contraband Police" is a simulation game that successfully immerses players in the world of border enforcement and poses intriguing moral dilemmas. If you're a fan of simulation games and enjoy a challenging, realistic experience, "Contraband Police" is worth considering, but it may not be for everyone.

The game have a unique style and act almost as more investigative papers please. It does not have the philosophical and criticism that papers please often provide with its emotional impact, but it does have a small storyline which is also very interesting and very fun to play through as an introduction to the much beloved "endless mode". I really recommend the game for people who enjoy a full on 70's / 80's Soviet aesthetic doing the work of a police border patrol inspector and commander whose action and dedcisions sometimes impact the country more than people realise.
