_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting 4 years for this game to come out! It has been worth the wait! Im going to go over a list of PROS and a very short list of CONS. I want to do the CONS first because there isnt a lot wrong with the game (and the devs have done their best since its early March release to fix bugs that affect story progress, achievement progress and minor tweaks, such as, Car Health, bullet damage and other balancing tweaks related to inspections.)The tutorial is helpful but I still feel like it doesnt explain some of the core mechanics and can be difficult to understand for new players who havent played Simulator games. My concern is mostly for new players just blindly figuring things out or resorting to Steam Guides for help. My friend has never played a Simulator game and I had to explain a few things about the searches and how to bring up their menu up to check things. I do think the tutorial was helpful but it left a couple things out or it was a little too confusing resulting in educated guesses.Some contraband is hard to find in the engine compartment and also under, behind or around seats. It can be super easy to miss these, mostly due to the camera orientation. When you finish searching a car and move on to the next one you learn you missed a couple pieces of contraband in these tough to search spots. I think its mostly the camera view and how you cant see something unless you are away from it or at a weird angle. It only costs you about $20-60 for an inspection, when $200 is max you get for perfect search. In the beginning, that little of money can impact your finances a lot and could spell disaster for a newer player.  The searching of cars get progressively harder with each chapter. You are given parameters that could deny entry for those trying to get across the border. At one point you're checking to see if they are asylum seekers, whether or not they have a vaccination card and even restricting how much food or chemicals one can bring over the border. Whether its a mistake in name spelling, wrong Passport number or even too many flat tires and broken windows, you can deny entry for many reasons.The gun play feels really good and that's a plus because you will have to defend your checkpoint from rebels and you will also get story missions (one per chapter, a total of 8.) From time to time you will be asked to do an Intervention and this can usually end up as a car chase or a shootout. There are a handful of guns and a grenade, including guns being given to you for some story missions or Interventions. Guns dont cost you anything extra, except ammo. You can buy these guns or wait to get some of them in different chapters that offer up a gun and lots of ammo. But you make a decent amount of money and you can put the Makarov to work for 3-4 chapters before you decide to get an SMG or AK-47 (both of which can be picked up through story missions.)Speaking of car chases, you can upgrade up to three vehicles and these vehicles will help you chase down people running through your checkpoint, drop off people you've arrested at the labor camp and to drop off contraband at the local police warehouse. The rebels will also set up ambushes and shoot at you in random places of the map when you head out to do missions, interventions and to deliver criminals and contraband to their proper places.You can work for the government or the Rebels and each have 8 chapters. My first play through was for the Government and took me a casual 18 hours. I wasnt rushing the game at all and really enjoyed the pace and the variety of missions I went on. There are easily 40-50 hours of achievement hunting for those who like to chase achievements. The achievements are super easy and just require you to play the game over time and youll get every achievement with ease. The devs are now working on ENDLESS MODE, which is just as it sounds. Right now you can only do the story as a Rebel or G-Man but the Devs have made it clear ENDLESS MODE will offer a lot of variety.There is a ton of options to make the game how you want. Sick of being ambushed or your checkpoint being attacked, you can turn that off. Are the days too short or too long? Well you can set the day length at 25, 35 & 45 minutes. There are also a slew of graphics settings to allow you to get high FPS or to make the game look damn good! Running on the UNITY Game Engine, the devs build a beautiful locale that surrounds Karikatka. I dont really count this as a pro or con, but think it adds a nifty touch to the game. No one speaks English and you have to read subtitles the entire game. They created a whole new language that sounds a lot like Central Europe or Southeastern Europe, also known as the Balkans or the Baltic States, respectively. At first it was annoying having to read all of this but you get plenty of time to read it all and it kind of makes you focus more on the real point of the game, stopping contraband from entering your nation.This game will be a sleeper hit and it will also go unnoticed for most of 2023. I highly highly highly recommend this game to Simulator fans and think its a great game for all ages to enjoy. These devs put a lot of work into this game and it shows! Normally when you wait so long for a video game to release, its typically a AAA game from a major studio and usually its lackluster and devoid of anything they put out to hype us up. CRAZY ROCK has poured their hearts and souls into this game and I hope more people find this little gem and enjoy it as much as I have. Its been years since I waited for a game to come out and actually still enjoy it after the Honeymoon period is over. $20 isnt a lot for this game and I hope they make enough money to continue on with titles like this one. Hands down my favorite new game in 2023!

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police - A Fresh Take on a Familiar ConceptContraband Police is a new entrant in the gaming scene that puts an intriguing twist on the well-known concept of border control gaming, taking inspiration from "Papers, Please." While it carries some echoes of the cult classic, Contraband Police attempts to break new ground by transitioning from the 2D world of paperwork and stamps to a fully immersive 3D environment with a story-driven narrative. The game also introduces some novel features, such as daily quests in its endless mode, that add variety and challenge to the gameplay.The transition to a 3D world is undoubtedly one of the game's highlights. Contraband Police immerses you in a detailed border crossing, where you must scrutinize vehicles, inspect cargo, and interact with people, making the experience much more interactive and immersive. The move from a flat 2D world to a 3D environment is a natural progression, allowing players to feel like they're genuinely at a border checkpoint.However, where Contraband Police falls a bit short is in its storytelling and the emotional connection between the player and the characters. In "Papers, Please," there was a constant moral dilemma as you faced desperate people trying to enter the country. The game would only penalize you if you made too many mistakes, which allowed for more empathy towards the characters. In contrast, Contraband Police's approach of deducting money right away lacks the same emotional impact. Perhaps implementing a similar system to "Papers, Please," with warnings or citations before financial penalties, would enhance the emotional depth of the game.Additionally, one aspect where "Papers, Please" outshines Contraband Police is in its reintroduction of memorable characters. "Papers, Please" featured characters like Gorgi, whose humorous and memorable interactions with the player provided levity in an otherwise tense atmosphere. Contraband Police could benefit from incorporating more character-driven moments to create a stronger bond between players and the individuals seeking entry into the country.Another area that needs improvement in Contraband Police is the behavior of NPCs. Currently, they seem to serve little purpose as they merely stand around until a border attack occurs. Enhancing the role and interactivity of NPCs could make the game world feel more dynamic and lively.I love this game, I really do, but I don't think it's quite there yet. You should definitely still give it a try but I feel like this game needs a touch more time to roast in the oven that is game development.8/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's a great game if you ever played and enjoyed Papers Please. I like the fact that it has lore, some possible choices to make, mini-management of your base and decent shooting mechanics for its price. The only couple of issues I have is that 1. The game is pretty short. I've finished the whole game in around 1-2 hours, siding with the goverment. However there are achivements like finish 100 days on the border or arrest 50 smugglers, which is not possible if you want to complete the game once. I will be replaying it in the future, just to check the gang side of the story and how it plays out. Fortunately, devs already announced "Endless Mode" in the future, so I will be definitely looking for that!The game was very stable for me, I never had any crashes or visual glitches. The only minor glitch I've encountered was the contraband hidden in the tire of Micrus, which was impossible to get, but I've already reported it and I believe other players did as well, so hopefully they will patch it soon too. To sum up, I believe it's a great game, with enjoyable gameplay, cool small lore, nice mechanics and decent graphics. For it's price, especially if you get it in a bundle (or have a game from a bundle which gives you additional discount on top of the current release one), I think it's worth to buy and try.

_childDocuments_.review: There is just something so satisfying to deny entries, especially in this day and age.The inspection and busting people part is very enjoyable, the rest are very poorly made and dull af.Wait for at least 50% sales if you are on the fence about it, no puns intended.After finishing the campaign, I decided to give another thought to this game. It pains me to say this but  this game has/had a huge potential to go close to GoY level. The gameplay at the border is amazing, but the forced story, driving mechanics, shooting mechanics are just horror shows. I remember hearing a game designer advice somewhere that when you are creating a game, you should concentrate on the part that makes the game fun. I thought on that regard, this game is a bit stretched on other parts that do not matter so much. Instead of forcing a "story" in campaign mode that forces you to drive somewhere or have a crappy ps1 level shootout, it could've just had the story developed around the border. Should've scrapped the whole thing outside of the border, and concentrate on it instead.Here are some nice examples, devs used real life events like pandemic and drive different restriction at the border which is super cool. So there could've been people coughing and adding some mechanics or measurement to handle that would've been fantastic. Pedestrians crossing with contraband is another line to develop too if one desired.  Instead, we get some sht driving and sht shooting. If it's once or twice then whatever, but if done multiple times, i can't stop but to wonder why are you making me play the sht parts of the game. Because to be completely fair and honest, if you take out the border part of the gameplay, I wouldn't play it even if I've been paid to play, it's an absolute horror show. Ultimately, the border part is doing the massive lifting hence the positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: Eurojank Papers Please with open world FPS elements. You play a border security officer at a road checkpoint in a fictional Socialist country. Pretty similar to Papers Please so far. But it's not just about checking Papers, you also have to look at their vehicle, check for smuggled illegal goods, and fight against rebel gangs. There are some story elements, where you can choose to be a straight laced officer, a corrupt cop or side with the rebels.I think the game is pretty great, with a couple caveats. 1. Glitches, performance issues and general Eurojank qualities. 2. A pretty unforgiving autosave system with no obvious way to manually save. 3. Random gang ambushes can be annoying at the best of times, and you don't get much loot from bodies.

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police, developed by Crazy Rocks, is a first-person simulation game that puts players in the role of a border patrol officer in a fictional Eastern European country during the 1980s. Your job is to inspect vehicles entering the country, search for contraband, and make decisions that impact the flow of smuggling and the political tensions at play. The game is a unique blend of simulation, action, and puzzle-solving elements, offering an intense and sometimes morally complex experience.The game’s atmosphere is gritty, with a strong sense of tension as you carefully inspect documents, search vehicles, and uncover hidden contraband. The mechanics of document inspection and vehicle searching are detailed, requiring players to pay close attention to discrepancies and suspicious behavior. Over time, more complex challenges are introduced, such as handling bribes, confronting smugglers, and deciding whether to follow the law or engage in corruption. However, the repetitive nature of the core mechanics might wear thin after extended play sessions.Pros:-Immersive and tense border patrol simulation.-Detailed mechanics for document inspection and contraband searching.-Moral decision-making adds depth to gameplay.Cons:-Repetitive gameplay loops can become monotonous.-Limited narrative depth outside of core tasks.-Some mechanics feel underdeveloped, particularly action sequences.Overall, Contraband Police offers a unique and immersive simulation experience with a strong focus on inspection and moral dilemmas. While its gameplay can become repetitive, it’s a compelling choice for players who enjoy detailed simulations and decision-based gameplay. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police starts off really well. It has an interesting premise and it changes the formula enough so it is not a 100% copy of Papers, Please. Gameplay is not perfect but it is solid enough to do its job and the game design keeps it fresh by making it harder as you progress. Besides checking papers, you'll be driving around a small-ish map doing errands, buying ammo and tools, and working your way through procedural side quests every now and then. Most of the items on my checklist when I review a game are alright here, so I wouldn't say that there's anything particularly bad with this game. But also, there isn't anything particularly amazing.For the first few hours, I was really liking Contraband Police, but the more I played, the more I started to get annoyed by it. I'm sure I don't have much until I finish it, but I've had enough. I literally have no interest in even watching a youtube video to see how it ends. This game falls in the category of "chill time passers", so if that's what you're looking for, this is your game. I personally don't like games to chill but rather than to immerse myself in experiences that will add value to me. And this game did it until it didn't. That's why I'm not finishing it and the reason I'm giving it a negative review.3.5/5 - Not a ripoff of Papers, Please.

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband police is literally papers please but in a 3d first person setting. Check for hidden contraband, refuse them entry just because they shaved their moustache off.....bit extreme but ok lol. Upgrade your checkpoint, hire staff, prevent prison escapes, take part in car chases, shoot outs, buy guns and tools, find hidden cash around the map, transport prisoners to new locations. Everything you could want is here.That said, here are my gripes with the game so far. The notice board gives added tasks to abide by. In the tutorial I had to refuse cargo that did not match the itinerary provided. So if the civilian put 3 fridges as cargo but they only have 2, then you should refuse them entry. I did but I was penalised for doing so. So! I had a guy state he's moving 3 cows, but there was only 1. Going by the previous experience I thought ok well both instances they had the item mentioned and both times their passport etc have been correct, just not the correct amount of cargo stated. So I'll let this one through then as I was wrong to deny last time.....I was penalised for letting him through.So basically you are damned if you do and damned if you dont. Unsure about the main game yet so it might just be in the tutorial this happens.The shootout was also confusing because I, as a player, didn't know you wanted me to fight back. The NPC next to me shouted "We've got to get out of here! Drive!" before being shot. So naturally I tried to drive away but the car wouldn't move and the ignition wouldn't work. So I climbed out and fought back. But I was practically dead by then lol. Lastly I feel refusing someone entrance based on if they have shaved or not seems a bit extreme but thats just me lolThose are the only gripes I have so far ^_^ loving the game and wanted to play throught the night but couldn't because of work in the morning haha.I feel the NPCs need a load more differences about them. Currently its just the same two guys with or without a beard. Add more ethnicities and female drivers to mix it up a bit. Make some skinny, overweight, have different faces etc. Different clothes too. I think they only cycle between 3 outfits at the mo.Little details I know but I feel it would add a bit more something something to the game

_childDocuments_.review: It's awesome, I've expected this game to be released for a while and doesn't disappoint.One improvement that I see is about the save game feature: - we need to have manual saving or auto save to be more often than it is right now, including for when you die or game lost occurs (like when you kill a prisoner by accident wink-wink).
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the price I'd give it a neutral review, but since this isn't an option I will rate it positive because I actually had a good time playing it (and might consider replying with different decisions in story & getting all achievements).I picked the game up on a key site for around €16 and I feel kinda okay with it. Full price is a bit far-fetched in my opinion.TL;DR: The game needs more variety in NPCs and animations. Accuracy on checklist and visuals should match and not punish you for missing stuff you couldn't actually see, or it wasn't there.Funny & dumb moments:- Chasing a guy fleeing inspection - I don't hit him, he runs his car into a barricade and dies → no way to inspect the car nor that I can ask my crew to "clean up" ?- I deny one guy to get into the country - turns around and drives off - while driving off he just runs over my crew mate (without any consequence). No loot on my crew too :<What I like about the game:- Music (radio is lackluster though)- Storyline with 2 different routes (good cop / bad cop (corruption, bribing)- 3 Different modes (story, endless mode, challenge mode with leaderboard)- New game plus (keep base upgrades and inventory)- Driving is always fun, although I only use the Zavod because it's the best no matter what.- Punishment for slacking in inspection- The option to see what you might've missed if you don't get perfect rating (learning curve)- Collectibles, yet I lost interest going for them quite fast because payout was so little and money is useless past mid-game. The only reason to go for it is the achievements.What I dislike about the game:- Corpses disappearing randomly? Sometimes they stick around, sometimes they vanish. Picture this: You get attacked in your outpost and kill like 50 guys (by yourself) and not even half of it will remain on the ground nor for a longer period if you drop off your stuff to get space in your inventory. Loot is trash most of the time, too.- No way to pick up guns from enemies and turn them in for money - they're contraband/illegal too, no?- Getting forced getting back at your base in time (makes no sense when I chase a guy across the map and try to get all smuggled goods out of the car)- Limited time (no timer) to accept missions (the ones during the day that require you to hit F2)- Limited radius on missions / street fights- Quite a small world to play in / most places you either only visit once or never (unless going for collectibles)- Animation bugs in a full released game shouldn't be a regular issue (NPCs in sitting animation outside the car for example)- Gunshots not registering, although you're clearly on them or your bullets getting stuck in invisible walls- Enemy always aimbot and hit you even when running/strafing and jumping to dodge, your crew is trash compared to the enemies- Your own crew sometimes hits your car with gunshots (stationary at the garage) when people flee from inspection- Car inspection not accurate with checklist - for example, I didn't get perfect score at times when I check no bumper, but that was wrong because they were there but not visible?- Variety/love in detail on NPCs (clothes, looks, gender, etc…)- Cars always occupied by only one person - doesn't make sense. Not what I expect from a fully released game.- Smuggler stashes in cars not accurate with the checklist - I had multiple occasions where I searched everything, but apparently I missed stuff? Probably same issue with the car inspection mentioned above.- Multiple tools per category, but they're pretty much useless aside from the most expensive?- Gotta be prepared for every possibility, so stack your car with ammo/guns and all tools at least once.- Early game (sometimes) - struggle with money. Endgame - money is useless- Low resolution textures in cars (motor region and such)- Prices for delivery/pickups- No way to later on automate car inspection- Base camp could really need more way to expand it
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game is very interesting and the devs have done a decent implementation. It is another gem like KCD but nowhere near as lengthy as KCD is. It would take around 10-12 hours to complete a playthrough and you could possibly extend it by exploring the other decision paths of the game which leads to a different ending. The map of this game is a bit stale to be honest but since it was not meant to be a completely open world game it does not matter. Graphics are somewhat dated and there could be object loading delays when moving from one area to another but that's not really an issue since everything else works pretty well. I think the devs have stumbled upon something good here and I hope they'll take the effort to add more content to this game because I feel the story mode could be just a little bit longer than a 10-12 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Less stressful and more tongue in cheek than Papers, Please, it shares a similar inspiration with a bit more realism and slightly less dystopia. Join the revolution to overthrow the Communist dictatorship or become the soulless tool of the bureaucracy you always knew you could be, the choice is yours and someone's going to try and kill you for it. What's not to like? Come for the enjoyable game play, stay for the subtle (and not so subtle) anti Communist humor!
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game. It's Papers, Please but in 3D with more stuff to do, and that's amazing. The police activities are fun, from checking border entrees to chasing fugitives and investigating local crimes. Of course, as with it's pixel predecessor, Contraband Police allows you to side with a rebellion or the government, and the choices are certainly difficult to make, which makes the replayability and story that much more interesting. The driving system is also noteworthy for it's surprising immersion. Everything about this game is clearly a labor of love. Great stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game with maxing everything out in 15 hours.  I think it is a good game for the money.  It is a lot like Papers Please, except a bit deeper in the amount of things to check and immersive 3D world.  The pacing is good.  The build up of information and complicated nature of the game is well done.  The environment looks good.  I never came across any bugs really during my playthrough.  I think I did have to "unstick" my vehicle a single time, but a button popped up to allow me to do so at the one point I needed it, so that was a big win in my book.  The story is sort of shallow but can be interesting if you can mentally separate everyone and everything in your head.  It should be known that the names of everything in this game has a strong Russian (?) influence with a lot of -rov's and -kov's.  So it can be sort of difficult for my plebian American brain to keep people and groups straight.  I did really enjoy it, though.  I ventured into YouTube to make a series on it.  Same name as here.  So anyone that wanted to see some unfiltered gameplay can check that out.  I do recommend it, through and through.

There is a handy book that you can cross-reference by clicking to verify its correctness.

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers a thrilling experience for its price point. It provides a range of exciting challenges that keep players engaged throughout. The game is easily accessible to players and offers plenty of content to keep them coming back for more.One of the game's features is the car damage recording mechanic. While it is an interesting concept, it can be quite boring, and some types of damage may not be immediately obvious to players, such as broken windows. This can be frustrating for players who want to fully immerse themselves in the game.The game has five types of weapons, but players may find that only the SMG is necessary to complete the game. This can make the other weapons feel unnecessary and underutilized.The property and employee upgrade mechanics in the game offer a way for players to customize their experience, but they are not necessary to finish the game. Some players may choose to focus solely on the core gameplay and ignore these upgrade mechanics entirely.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Like Papers Please, but built on a first person shooter engine. Check papers, check the cars, follow new rules and guidelines, earn enough money to upgrade your security checkpoint, sometimes have shootouts with people and car chases.Overall, it gets a bit fiddly at times. Wanted posters may look like two people due to engine limitations and you have to check who is wearing the right shirt. Enemies despawn after a shootout so you can't collect their guns and ammo and you might be left with barely anything of your own. Cars handle a bit stiffly. Your tools have durability for really no reason. Checking details of specific governments, like what colour paper they use is just tedium.So it's kind of a mixed bag leaning on the positive side of a recommendation. Didn't wow me, but some people might enjoy it despite its jank.

_childDocuments_.review: pretty fun game, just wish you were able to engage with your comrades at the base a little more. i don't like the ending only because if you finish the last mission the game ends and you have to start over from scratch. i had $10,000 saved up so i can upgrade everything, only to finish the game and lose all my progress. im definitely doing another play-through to get all the achievements. i recommend this game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: A Fantastic Experience for Fans of Papers, PleaseAfter spending around 25 hours with Contraband Police, I can confidently say I thoroughly enjoyed the experience. From the start, it reminded me a lot of Papers, Please, and I was instantly hooked. The game offers a more open-world feel, allowing for various missions to tackle while still maintaining that satisfying inspection mechanic. I also loved that beyond the main campaign, there's an Inspection Mode, where you're challenged to stay alive as long as possible, adding even more replay value.While I did encounter a few minor issues along the way, they didn’t detract from the overall enjoyment. If you loved Papers, Please, this game is absolutely worth checking out. A solid and engaging experience that I would definitely recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished Contraband Police. It's... a *very* Playway game. They tend to be... weird. Like, this is extremely influenced by Papers Please. But it's 3D. And you're also dealing with a vehicle and cargo.And bandit raids. And revolutionaries. And smugglers. So there's some first-person shooting.And there's an open world aspect. Sort of. It's not much of a world, but it is there. There's some hidden collectibles by the points of interest, which just give you $ and a sense of completion. And missions to go to these places for a variety of things. It's not always combat. One was a murder mystery.None of it's done terribly *well*, of course. The enemies do take cover and pop up to shoot... but can also be seen reloading away from cover while standing upright. Your allies do lay down a lot of fire in a fight, but not all of them aim. NPCs get different looks, but it's like, 5 beards, a couple hats, and a couple glasses. All white guys. Though, at least they remembered women exist, as one voice on the phone is not a guy.This is why Playway titles are always kind of fascinating. Not just for what goes in, but what corners get cut. Most are worthwhile, many certainly manage to be something Different.So I do somewhat recommend this game. It runs, it's a bit janky, but rather bug-free. (The only thing I noticed was 1 vehicle on 1 day that consistently ding'd me on import restrictions, despite being under the limit.) It's not great, but it does get a (minimally) passing grade in the many areas it tries to provide you with an interesting experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because it looked like 3D Papers, Please and other reviews basically said as much.Pros:- The inspection part of the game is really fleshed out and a lot of fun. It seems like it would get repetitive but hasn’t for me at all.- There’s surprisingly a lot of story in the game, with missions outside of just inspection that change up the gameplay.- I have been playing this solely on Steam Deck and other than a little bit of lag when driving, it runs great! (You’ll probably have to change up the controls, though)Cons:- I’m not a huge fan of the driving or shooting. Both feel unsatisfying and floaty to me, but I think they could be great with work.- This seems to be common of a lot of simulator games, but why are there no women at all? I can understand maybe not in the actual police force, but it’s hard to believe women would never need to cross the border.Other than the small cons, I am really enjoying the game so far and already know I will be doing more than one play through to see the other options.

Highly recommend giving it a try !

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a solid 9.3/10. It is an infinitely better version of Papers, Please except this has actual engaging gameplay. The story is interesting and fun to watch develop, the inspection of cars is fun and didn't get boring or repetitive (to me at least.)The only thing I wish that was a little different was less of a focus on the shooting parts of the game and a little more depth on the vehicle inspections. Possibly adding ways to have your border guards be able to pre-inspect some of the vehicles to verify issues with cosmetics or notice anything weird going on with the driver. Or possibly adding a second inspection lane, maybe even automate some of the process via your employees.The game is fine as is, I just felt those would be nice additions.By the end of the campaign I think I'd killed liked 400 people or something which I felt detracted a bit from the realism of the game but like I said it wasn't a big issue. _childDocuments_.review: Insanely well-made game for an indie project. If you enjoyed Papers please it is simply a must-play. Gameplay is good in all aspects. Inspections are very similar to Papers please, but adding "physical" interaction with people their cars, and goods really pushed it to another level. But what surprised me the most, are mechanics completely unrelated to the inspection process. When I saw gameplay screenshots I expected clunky shooting and car driving. But the truth is, they are both really well made. Shooting is quite fun and has a nice feel to it. When driving the car you really feel its "weight". Hell, you even feel the difference between RWD and AWD cars. On top of all previously said, the game also offers a good enough story with some degree of player choices that impact how the whole thing plays out. Of course, this game is not without issues. Typical performance issues, and some minor bugs but nothing game-breaking really. Yes, some animations are very simple and feel unrealistic, and the graphics also are not top-notch. But in this time and age when 90% of all games are some AAA nonsense, this is the real diamond in the rough. Straight 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is surprising me, as an avid Simulator fan, it's a breath of fresh air to pick up a game like this, and have it feel like it's a finished product. I am enjoying the feeling of playing another game like Papers, Please again with the mechanics this title has introduced. It is way more enjoyable to look for contraband in the vehicles and cargo, rather than the naked x-ray photos from Artstoska. This team also took the route of Rebels vs. Communist Regime with their Storyline, allowing you to make decisions that affect the ending. The gun play they've advertised heavily on is as janky as you would expect a game like this to be. I was surprised to find enemies not dying to one bullet to the head in the first fight, but it seemed that you are scripted to lose, as enemies have died to one hit in the head since then. The only issue I have run into is the abundant amount of enemies that are spawning along the roads when you are taking prisoners/contraband to their designated POI on the map. I have resorted to getting out of my van before driving by certain POI's (Motel, Ruins) and walking past them on foot, in order to spawn the enemies that would have attacked my van on the road. The health of the vehicle is very low, and the tutorial says you could either Drive by or Fight them. Driving by is basically asking for your progress to go away. It kind of takes the fun out of the game when I need to constantly park and check what's in front of me while I utilize the free roam feature. I hope the development team can look into that, otherwise, this is near perfect what you'd expect from this title.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. I spent almost 40 hours completing the campaign and inspector modes (unlocked everything). Good value for money. The game is primarily about inspection so don't expect a premier shooter experience. The graphics are not flashy but there is enough detail that I didn't really care. I had the odd crash but it did not affect my experience.Positives:- Lots of hiding spaces for contraband - check everywhere!- Car chases where you have to P.I.T. cars off the road to stop them.- Shootouts (no scopes which can be a little painful)- Lots to upgrade in Inspector mode.- There is a large variety of checks to conduct with enough variables on the daily intel board to keep you on your toes.Rather than talk about any negatives, I'll mention some suggestions that I think will improve the experience:- During car chases have an option for AI to deploy a stinger/roadblock up ahead for a cost.- Add a basic 2x scope to the long rifle and red dot to the automatic rifle.- Reduce handling on evading vehicles if a tyre has been shot out/is flat.- Increase the speed (vary the handling) of the other vehicles (I found that I just bought the fastest vehicle early on as there was no use for the slow ones).- Either have a second page of inventory (purchasable upgrade) or add a separate inventory space for weapons and tools.- Save game option - at this time the game only saves once each morning when you wake up.- The daily mission to sell contraband needs a bigger reward or less contraband requirements. As it stands it isn't worth the hassle to wait until you have the right amount. Its more convenient just to hand over to the guard.- Some clarity on when accepting a bribe will be detected or not detected. Sometimes I could get away with it, sometimes not. Is this a random risk?- The final upgrade to your sleeping quarters should max out your perception most times. I find with the final upgrade to roads, i was spending longer on the line and my perception would barely touch the final bar after sleep.Overall, a great game for the price. I look forward to seeing what updates are implemented and where the game can go.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Fun to play, challenging and always full of unexpected twists. The game takes the best bits of "Papers, Please" and mixes it with shootouts, some detective work and town building to make an entertaining and addictive game to play. Every time I feel that the game has become repetitive, there will be a sudden unexpected twist which will throw whatever vehicle search you were conducting out the window for a shootout.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Very similiar to Papers Please setting/story wise. I haven't finished it yet, but so far I can say that it has a story in addition to the outpost management and border control routine. The shooting, driving and such is acceptable, not really much more to say about it.There are some random events that involve lots of shooting that break up the monotony, they never last longer than a minute or two though.You have to manage your funds and you get punished if you let a car through that shouldn't, you can upgrade your base and the crew of the base. You can buy and upgrade your cars, but don't expect anything more than old eastern european ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There's a shop where you buy tools that degrade, guns and ammo. Games like this, similiar would be games like Station Simulator really do have a place I think. Do you ever feel like playing a game but you don't want the intensity of Cod, CS or the intense management of an RTS, or the eternal grind of an MMO,- if you want to play a game, but not THAT game? Then I would dare say that this is for you, its a really nice break from everything else, and it has wonderful pacing.I'm 5 hours in now, I estimate around 10-15 hours total before it goes on the shelf, probably forever and I'm going to be happy I played it. Buy if you need a temporary break from your other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable game for 15€. The game progressed smoothly and it was fun to upgrade the border station and to thwart smugglers. The game eventually start to offer you story mission that ultimately offers you to choose between supporting the goverment or the rebel group that is planning a revolution in your country, there is also plenty of shootouts in these missions and while roaming the world delivering contraband and prisoners. Even though the shooting sections were mediocre it never overstayed its welcome to the point it felt repetetive.  Still i somehow felt that if the game would have had a little bit more things to upgrade and maybe more different types of contraband it would be truly exellent. These types of games have a great potential to be truly fun and addictive games and i would love to see more of these. Great game overall and i would definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: If you're wanting to play this game, it's for the border checking sections.  Which are very fun if you enjoy things like Papers, Please.  Sometimes it doesn't give you the best details on what counts against regulations, either that or it can be buggy with it's own checkings.  I'm still not sure if soap is counted as a chemical or not.  The shooting sections that are sprinkled in are as generic as can be.  I think they are at their best when a raid happens on your checkpoint and you have to fight alongside the guards you've upgraded.  I would probably enjoy most of the shootings ections more if I could have a guard or three tag along with me to help in fights.  It'd at least make me slightly more satisfied.  TLDR: Border checking is really fun, maybe slightly buggy or not clear sometimes.  Shooting sections are boring, but a necessary evil.  Oh and the story isn't too much to write home about either, about as generic as the shooting.

_childDocuments_.review: Good evening comrades!First of all I can say directly that the wait was really worth it.Besides the usual activity of checking documents and ensuring daily regulations, there are extremely well implemented management elements, such as managing the border post or transporting contraband and detainees through the wondrous forests of Acaristan (the world is surprisingly accessible and "big" for not being an official open-world game).Another plus is the great (but I'm afraid a bit shorter) story. It is exciting and offers "Papers, Please!"-like decisions. There are also so-called "intervention missions", through which you can earn a small bonus.I really hope that there will be an endless mode or something similar in the future, so that we can serve our government even after the story is  the end, it is simply a great game with cool implemented mechanics and management elements!

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to give a very constructive criticism; First of all, the reason why I recommend the game is that the first few hours of the game are quite enjoyable and you really have fun in the process. In my opinion, it can be tried on a discounts just for this sudden enjoyment.But the game is starting to get extremely boring with little interaction and activities and repetitive days.They tried to create a small world, and  it's a nice idea to take prisoners to camp or go somewhere to sell contraband, but it was a terrible way they implemented this. Vehicle mechanics are absolutely terrible, such a mechanic like this should'nt exist in 2023. The roads are always the same and curvy becomes boring to drive after 2 minutes since you watch literally the same environment.Our main duty, the border guard, starts to repeat strangely after a point because we always do the same things and we don't have a proper target to improve. I really liked the details such as trying to interspersed with a story, murder solving, etc. It breaks the chain of being a border guard and feels like a change of atmosphere, but the story missions are too slow.Random events that will fill every day can enrich the game. The only random event is getting ambushed by 4 raiders.  New interaction events that can be added will enrich the game. Increasing the typology of vehicle mechanics and roads/landscape and environment will positively affect the atmosphere.At this point, you see that I played the game for 6 hours, and I played the last 1-2 hours by forcing myself. The final decision is up to you, I wrote down all the troubles I encountered here :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game. I only wish that they would add a sort of 'endless' mode outside of the base story mode where you play strictly as a border agent and not have to deal with the other side quests. The base story mode is fine but can get annoying if you just want to actually as a border patrol officer and not have to worry about all of the other side quests and what not. _childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasant surprise !I was skeptical, but bought it anyway. Gosh what a great game. Really refreshing and new approach. It's "Papers, please" taken to next level.I really like the "puzzle" this games offers. When you have to control many details before you can Approve or Deny entrance. Even then for maximal reward, you have to make sure to note all faulty details in inspection. More details you note, the bigger reward is.  Every time I make a decision, there is uncertainty if i missed something. After chapter II, the amount of things you have to watch out increases a lot. It becomes a mystery game, with a burning question "Did i get all the clues or not?".Extra part is, you have to arrest correct people, take them to labor camp. Take contrabands to police warehouse, fight gangs who always ambush you when you're driving these two things. Aaaand this is the part where games fails. Gosh this is annoying as heck. The game has gunfights, either on the road or when border crossing is attacked. This part, although a welcomed mix, is really annoying due to how, too simple it is and anti-climatic. There is also some detective work, which was done pretty well. But not too hard. The map design is also one of it's biggest minuses. It's a bland corridor. You gonna spend a lot of time driving to camp and police station plus to other parts. This drive through canyon looks like a long, identical corridor. Nothing to see except tress and canyon rocks, plus those annoying ambushes.  While I presume this was done to make game less system demanding. The two most used routes to camp and police should still be somewhat more interesting visually. More nature, wide roads, something to make that drive feeling lees like identical corridor. However this games shines at you looking at papers and inspecting vehicles. A truly well made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the campaign and I think its a great game. People say it's repetitive, but that's literally what it's supposed to be, It's supposed to be mundane, until it isn't. I think the biggest thing they could improve though is the performance, it's a little slow and choppy sometimes. But I cant wait to see how they develop this game in the future. There is one thing that pissed me off about gameplay. For instance the prisoner transport mission, why didn't they just block the road in the first place, with a tree or a car (like it shows in credits). Also why damage or destroy the car if they're boss is in it, when you eventually get stopped, there's basically no one there, two guys and one gun that's not even pointed at you, when I first got there I popped them both immediately because I didn't think it was part of the cut-scene. I'd also like to see a more interactive map, more locations even if they aren't directly for the campaign (like a grocery store or something). Being able to talk to citizens out side of the checkpoint (have you seen suspicions activity and what-not) or be able to have a drink with your officers. To take consumables, smoking to replenish alertness, or drink to lose it (drink to much and you black out and lose money). All in all great game, had fun, needs work wish it was more like trailer. Keep up work!
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: I played a fair bit of this game before endless mode came out. I had a fun time with it. Now that endless mode has come out and its fleshed out a bit, its gotten REALLY good. The only issue is that the pursuits are a bit of a chore, You just drive out and pit maneuver the enemies of the state. I wish that there was a mechanic to shoot while driving, but I can understand that its a bit to implement. Haven't stumbled upon any glitches, gun play feels fairly serviceable. Has a neat cover mechanic that will peek you out when you aim. And if you don't feel like shooting enemies, the game does let you turn off raids, although that may only be in Endless mode. The story mode isn't Casablanca, but it tells *a* story in the world that kinda sets the mood if that's your thing. If you want to jump right into it and play endless mode, you can also do that without any downside. TL;DR If you liked Papers Please, want a chill game to play after a long day,  or are looking for something a little different, I think this game is well worth the 20 dollars. Glory to Acaristan.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is great, But in recent times I have seen bugs. For example: car getting stuck at border or killing every enemy on road ambush and game continues to tell me to escape or kill attackers. Because of this, I had to disable road ambushes.In career mode, there should be option to search the smugglers for any possible illegal items. By adding this feature, you can automatically find the illegal item and arrest the suspected smuggler. Without this, you have to search through the whole car and waste your time.For the criminals that drive away from inspection, there should be option search their bags or packages for any possible illegal item.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Things you should know: There are 8 vehicles that may come through. A lot of the smuggle/contraband hiding spots are in the same locations no matter the car/truck. Each model has its own variation but 8 is just not enough. It becomes quite repetitive after just 6 hours. Arrests, chases, smugglers - they don't really vary. It's pretty much the same each time. Also, don't expect much in the way of upgrading the border station. Options are there, and they are helpful, but the place will forever look like a pile of garbage.Now that said - I did have a good time. I beat the game, and while the story was seemingly an afterthought, the focus truly is on the gameplay, not the writing.You're provided with a team of police who walk patrol around the property. They serve little to no purpose. The only time they do anything is during raids and they don't seem to aim well enough to ever hit their target. Expect to do ALL of the work when this happens and make sure you have the ammo and weapons to pull it off. Days/nights can run really short - this means if you are still inspecting cars/drivers late into the night, you may either get little or no sleep and the next work day will start. This leaves you with no energy to be able to use the assist functions during inspections. While not a huge deal - it does slow things down and makes it easier to miss things like age limits (where math is required) or making sure the color and style of paper match what that particular originating country uses.It's a fun game and the inspections/review work isn't particularly hard. It has enough variety to keep you entertained for a while but it really needs more content. Even outside the main campaign - it's just more of the same. I do think this game is ripe for DLC expansions/content and I think that would go a long way in helping. That said, with the lack of content - it feels like whatever may come in DLC form should have been baked into the main game.I wouldn't spend $20 on the game, but $15 is fair. It's a good time if you're into this kind of auditing/inspection simulation genre. I found it more entertaining than "Papers, Please". Having drivers decide to suddenly "f*** off" and run while you are inspecting their cargo off to the side can be fun to have to dizzily spin around and sprint to your police car to start the chase. Just don't kill the driver/smuggler - it will likely cost you a decent amount of cash as a penalty. The game does let you choose to side with the government, party, or the "good" of the people, and the ending will vary a bit depending on what path you choose.I recommend it, just realize it's base price is $20 and that is mostly for good reason. There just isn't enough content to justify much more. Maybe wait until a DLC package? Rare to find a game like this. Worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: It's just too janky to be enjoyable, it's always a gamble with play way games, this game is akin to papers please but without any polish. The performance was all over the place and I wasn't a fan of how little challenge the game provides, the UV light makes finding contraband way too easy and the gameplay loop itself is pretty brainless.If you watched a youtuber play this, or you played papers please, there is nothing new or exciting this game can offer you.Like thief sim, it feels more like a garrysmod map than a fully fledged game. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: Contraband PoliceTHINGS I LIKED:- Realistic and historical nature- Fact that the dev team is small (Games with small dev teams are usually very good in my experience)- The NPCs speak actual foreign languages (People who haven't bought the game, there are subtitles!)- Time-appropriate vehicle, building, radio, and weapon style.- The game's immersive gameplay.- Heard abt this game from CaseOh.THINGS I DIDN'T LIKE:- Lack of NPC voice line variation- Lack of female characters (or at the very least, gender variation)- Lack of character customization- Small map (Since dev team is small, I won't count this one, but I would enjoy a map expansion in the future)OVERALL:Honestly a really good game. It provides a somewhat accurate depiction into what a Russian-esque country in that time frame. It is also really entertaining, time consuming, and almost even addictive. Only con is it does have some bugs, there's a lack of variation in voice lines, and some other minor things.FINAL RATING:All in all, I'm gonna give this game a 8.5/10. Would recommend.                                         - MelodiousOwl, Amateur Steam Critic

_childDocuments_.review: While being a border guard, you are confronted with choices and a story between rebelling against the system or joining them. You will be given choices and therefore need to gain more money to upgrade your border crossing with more staff, cars, housing, tools and weapons.You do this by obviously not making mistakes by the wrong denial of entry or accepting the wrong people. Searching cars and comparing them to daily or story objectives. You can also trade with the people that come across.Finding contraband is fun and a little challenging - and rewarding. You must arrest smugglers or wanted criminals and transport them to jail. While driving in the open world you may encounter rebels and you have more choices to make there as well. Overall, I am really enjoying this long awaited game and it's holding up to exactly what I was hoping for. It's fun and quick to learn. For under $20 it's a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, around 12-15 hours campaign, 2 options story wise, so there is some replay value, excited to see the challenge mode update. _childDocuments_.review: Really fun with just enough frustration to make you restart the day over and over. The game does well to make you suspicious of everyone that tries to come through the border and keeps you on your toes with a lot of curve balls. Only issue is that the amount of smugglers and regular border crossers are scripted meaning if you stuff a day up you can restart and the same number will appear that day, it would be a lot better if this was randomised so it would keep you guessing. Also some damaged parts on the vehicles are vague for example the missing mirrors, it's unclear if the centre mirror inside the car is included or not.Optimisation could be better as well. Frame rate changes significantly in certain areas despite the graphics not being the greatest, though the graphic quality itself is not an issue.Still a really good game despite the few gripes mentioned

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police is a Simulator game. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this one. It's kind of like a first-person Papers, Please, with more added to it. I personally didn't mind the side missions, because it broke up the monotony of checking passports/restrictions/vehicle damage. It can get a bit repetitive, especially playing for many hours, but breaking up play sessions helps. I did find myself getting a bit frustrated with the ever-expanding list of things to check sometimes, but once I found my groove, it wasn't as much of an annoyance.I would like to see the world expanded some more - not necessarily a larger world, but making the current world a bit more interactive, in a way that gives players more things to do outside of checking passports all day. That being said, I do look forward to the upcoming Endless Mode and will give that a shot once it drops. Overall, I recommend picking this one up if you're looking for something to scratch that Papers, Please itch, especially on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: I waited to finish the game before I made a review and this game is one of the most fun games I've played in a couple years. Some points for why the game is worth it:The story is interesting and fun like a 3D game of Papers Please and some choices you make can lead to death.The game mechanics are controllable but a little wonky making for some fun car driving.The economy of the game can be really felt from start to mid but in late game money is not a problem.The combat is not hard but you can die from getting cocky or not finding cover. (I killed around 400 Terrorists in whole play through and died about 10 times)The border checkpoint gets more complicated overtime and is consistent with new paper requirements like Papers Please. The contraband scenarios are like a car mechanic mode where you use many tools to hit and bang everything.I rate the game a 9/10, the developers of the game are active in the community and they are improving the game at a steady pace. _childDocuments_.review: Great game but since you can't play the game when you don't have internet access because launching the game directly is not possible due to developer hostility, I have to give a thumbs down. If there is an update available but you can't load it due to lack of steady internet connection when in the countryside, you can't play. If you change the game from for example C:// to D:// then you can't even set up a shortcut to the game manually due to developer hostility. Steam can also bug out (tested it) when changing the disks so you would have to completely reinstall the game. If you were working on a mountain travel hut before going hunting and then wanting to play in the evening, you can't if following cases arise:- No internet- Update needed- Steam update needed- copying the game from an external hard drive (with steam access (4TB in my case)) to your Laptop hard drive due to storage space complications doesn't work. In other words: You install it and any normal actions cause the game to be unplayable due to developer hostilityWhat is this developer hostility? A security measure so that you can't pirate the game but the steam key is in the game folder and there is an offline mode so the game would only have to check back with a few steam files and give the ok. Simplified example: Game gets launched manually --> game checks offline steam library --> game checks its own key --> match found --> game launchesNow what happens with this game? Game gets launched manually --> Error message and force closing of the game whilst in main menueSo the game can in fact be launched but the development team decided deliberately to screw with the playerbaseNow for the good and bad parts of the game itself:- Great tutorial- Not overwhelmingly many smugglers or runners- political tasks that effect who can cross the border implemented with only one day too soon (misalignment)-unrealistic gun front recoil ( wrong weapon pivot point) pivot point for the AK shouldn't be the pistol grip like for the pistol- unrealistic NPC reactions and overly aggressive driving NPC behavior to the point where they suicide into your own car until it explodes (tested it). Btw. you get the penalty.-Upgradable buildings (ladders can't be accessed)- fun little side missions- unfinished map and invisible walls rather than actual obstacle barriers (takes less than an hour to fix the meshes in a way that there aren't any invisible parts)- bodies despawn immediately after ending a mission fight which is unrealistic and encourages taking fire in order to get the loot- unrealistic steering- shortcuts for when in car- when a smuggler runs the border, the car can get pinched in a certain way where parts of the car are inaccessible and thus ruining the possiblility for a perfect inspectionThose were a few points that I think are good to know. I may have only played 7 hours of this game but in that time I have been testing the game for bugs and glitches and there are some that I won't list up here because they are turly game breaking but I also won't inform the devs about them as they from what I have seen son't care about the quality so it would be futile. If the devs however somehow read this and want to know the bugs and glitches, I will tell them as long as they would actually fix them.

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police - A Challenging and Intense Border Control Simulator!Contraband Police is a unique and challenging game that puts you in the shoes of a young officer trainee working at a border post in the politically strict Acarist People's Republic in 1981. As you work to regulate entry into the country, you quickly realize that every move you make is closely monitored by the party, and the situation at the border becomes increasingly tense, especially after the tragic death of one of your comrades during an intervention.One of the standout features of Contraband Police is its focus on document control. As an officer, you are responsible for checking the validity of every visitor's documents, and even the slightest discrepancy can result in refusal of entry. The game starts off relatively straightforward, but as time goes on, the number of documents to check increases, and the errors become more difficult to detect. This adds a layer of challenge to the gameplay, requiring keen attention to detail and careful decision-making.The game's setting in the mountainous region of Karikatka is beautifully rendered, with detailed graphics that capture the atmosphere of the time period. The sense of tension and suspicion in the air is palpable, and the game does an excellent job of immersing you in the world of a border officer during a politically sensitive era.The gameplay itself is intense and engaging. You'll need to carefully examine documents, cross-reference information, and make tough decisions on who to allow entry and who to turn away. The consequences of your choices can be far-reaching, affecting the story and the outcome of the game. The sense of responsibility and the weight of your decisions add to the game's overall immersion and replay value.The story is intriguing, with the death of your comrade adding a layer of mystery and intrigue to the game. As you uncover more about the events at the border and the political situation in the Acarist People's Republic, the plot thickens, keeping you invested in the outcome.One potential downside to the game is its level of difficulty. As the number of documents and errors increases, it can become quite challenging to keep up with the pace, and mistakes can have consequences. However, for players who enjoy a challenge and the thrill of high-stakes decision-making, this can be seen as a positive aspect of the game.In conclusion, Contraband Police is a unique and immersive border control simulator that offers a challenging and intense gameplay experience. With its focus on document control, intriguing story, and immersive setting, it's a game that will keep you on your toes and test your skills as an officer. If you're up for the challenge, put on your uniform and get ready to uphold the party's regulations in this politically charged game!

_childDocuments_.review: The year is 1981, and as a young officer trainee, you are assigned to work at a border post in the mountainous region of Karikatka. Entry into the Acarist People's Republic is strictly regulated by the party and your every move is monitored! The situation at the border escalates when your comrade is killed during one of the interventions... Document controlEvery visitor must have a set of valid documents. Even the slightest discrepancy means refusal of entry. Over time, the number of documents will increase and errors will be more difficult to detect. Smuggling detectionOur intelligence regularly provides information about suspicious drivers. Search their vehicles using a UV flashlight and then use the appropriate tools to extract the smuggled goods. No amount of contraband should cross the border! ShootoutsIn some situations you will be forced to use firearms. Your station is a constant target for Oberankov's gang attacks, and every away mission carries the risk of a clash with the enemy. Police chasesDesperate smugglers may attempt to escape from the control zone. It is your duty to stop and arrest them! Buy and upgrade police cars to improve the effectiveness of your pursuit. Post managementUpgrade your police station to increase its defenses and improve subsequent inspections. However, keep in mind the rising cost of maintaining your station. Successful inspections, foiled smuggling and successful interventions are a few ways to earn cash. Special assignmentsAlways be ready to intervene in an emergency. Solve crime puzzles, support your comrades and thwart the Blood Fist rebels. Make decisions that will determine the future of Acaristan. The developers describe the content like this:This game may contain content that is not appropriate for all ages: Occasional violence or brutality, vulgar and explicit language

_childDocuments_.review: It would be hard for me not to recommend.  There have been a few games that have tried to replicate what Papers, Please did but I think they missed the point.  The point shouldn't be to *replicate* what Lucas Pope did, instead be inspired by it.  And here we have "Contraband Police," one of the worst titles I've seen in a long time.  But don't let that particular aspect fool you, this is a very competent and thoroughly well-designed game.  It's not quite an immersive sim, and it has a story to tell.  Gameplay consists of checking paperwork, yes, but also a lot of investigation.  What condition is the car in?  Does it's tonnage match?  Is it registered to the right person?  The game makes full use of it's 3d nature having you comb inside and out, checking cargo, opening suitcases.  There's just as much to visually inspect as there is paperwork to compare.  And then you realize all of it is interactive because smugglers can and will hide contraband literally anywhere and everywhere.  That's the baseline, ph neutral.  And if the game had *just* been that I'd still be giving it a big fat thumbs up for just how well it executes on this premise.Yet, in swoops a larger game.  Getting into gunfights, investigating crime scenes, delivering prisoners and contraband, purchasing tools and supplies, upgrading your people and station.  And all of this, while not *quite* as detailed or involved as the core loop, are still delightful.  You might get ambushed while delivering a prisoner.  Someone might try to buy illegal contraband.  You can even do some light trading with the drivers before you deny their entry.  This is where the game shows it's thoughtfulness: none of this stuff is just there to fill out time.  It all works together to build this world of chores you inhabit .  Will you side with the government for the paycheck?  Or the rebels?  It's not a terribly deep game, but it puts details into all the places that really matter and it shines for it.There's an endless mode on the horizon and we'll see how that plays.  Personally I think the story mode is very well done, it can be planned and give the player a specific experience, but I can see how a more procedural endless mode to play with the mechanics is desired.  I bring this up simply because I think the game is worth it *now*, and frankly I'd be just as happy seeing a sequel announced.  This game was an unexpected treat and I'm looking forward to spending more time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: My work day started like any other, dull and monotonous with me questioning my life choices. A cargo truck pulled up at the checkpoint disrupting my musing, I hate cargo trucks they take more time to inspect properly. The driver was a foreigner, which wasn't a problem as long as he was willing to respect the rules and laws our glorious party had outline for this great country of mine. As he handed me his papers I noticed he seemed tense, I wondered if I was coming off a bit hostile which would be bad since i pride myself as being a friendly welcoming person. So after I had got him to verify that everything on the cargo manifest was indeed what was in the back I decided to crack a joke the lighten the mood. So I did, the driver chuckled, a crate laughed, I arrested the driver, his smuggler buddy hiding inside and the contraband they were trying to sneak across the boarder. It was productive day.Okay actual review time.My sad attempt at wit aside (thanks for indulging me if you got this far), this is nice game, thats well crafted and really knows how to let you get into the swing of things. Especially its core mechanics by gradually introducing them at steady pace so you don't get overwhelmed by them. The plot isn't anything profound or ground breaking but its serviceable for the time and setting but you really should be playing this more for the inspection process which does get broken up sporadically with a little action and gunplay. Visually the game is surprisingly good for something that didn't have a triple A budget (can't say that about a lot of triple A games these days ironically). Anyway if you like analyzing things for inconsistencies and don't need to constantly be in high octane situation this game might just end up being your jam. While the asking price for it is with in reason in my opinion, if you're still on the fence add it to your list and wait for sale then try it.

(Seargent Maksimox should move the prisoners to the labor camp every other day for example)Overall, i would give this game a sold 7.9 out of 10. _childDocuments_.review: Welcome to what i hope will at least be a semi helpful review to you my friend which i will break up into individual segments, starting with price, story, game play, and additional content. So my friends let us begin.Price/ValueContraband police is a fairly priced game especially considering today's economy for games and for what your getting you really can't complain, the game is priced around $30 in my region or something similar where ever your from. I got the game on when it came out, so i got a 12% discount, which was nice but i would still have happily paid full price. I usually like to wait for a sale before i purchase a game but whatever sale I've seen for this game has been really small, so in my opinion it's not worth waiting and i do believe $30 is a reasonable price for what your getting.Game playThe core of any game especially CP is how does the game run. In simple terms great, i've never had any really issues regarding it's performance the worst that's happened to me is the AI drivers acting stupid but that's really it. The mechanics of checking papers are very nicely done and are slowly introduced to you as you progress through the game, ranging from simple name checks, vehicle weights, forgeries, and additional sub documents to name a few. The checking system overall works well although it can be tedious as you progress through the game 6 different documents all covering your screen but it does make sense. There's a simple ranking system you get papers right your promoted you unlock new stuff and increased rewards. If you get papers wrong your fined depending on your rank and point in the story, but it does not affect your rank. . Only real gripe with it is sometimes there's no direct cross-reference so you'll have to pick it up and manually check it but it happens rarely (assuming you don't get fatigued). The key mechanic to make sure you can't perfectly check everything from day 1 is the fatigue meter which can be improved as you upgrade your residence, this does feel a bit inconsistent in how it upgrades, as i feel the jump in the last upgrade is quite big, but only my personal thoughts. You can upgrade some elements of the outpost, being the prison, storage, residence, your collection of vehicles and the vehicles themselves, bit pricey but it's so you have something to work towards. The random missions you get are fun enough but are somewhat infrequent at least for me so don't expect call-outs to frequently. Attacks on out-posts have varying frequency, but add a nice element of surprise. Moving on to the contraband checking it works well, although some areas such as the engine can be a pain to check with elements being hidden extremely well. You'll get the odd runner which you have to chase, which is a nice change of pace but again at least for me infrequent. The shooting is really solid for  the game. The biggest compliant i would have is how expensive everything is especially the weapons, with the sniper (last weapon) costing you up to 5 days of work depending on how well you check although by the point you unlock it you should have some cash lying around. Finally for gameplay the bribes are the worse as they are completely RNG based so there's no way to increase your chances of getting away or getting caught and the punishment for it $800 dollars of your cash, which depending where you at in the game can cost around 1 day to 4 days of your pay. Overall the game play is great just some minor issues, and a lot of it is being addressed in the endless mode update.StoryLook this part going to short, the story is about your average communist government trying to control every aspect of life and the rebels trying to fight back with you caught in the middle, there are a few story missions which are done well enough but are far between as they're spread over the 30 days, each gives you a choice whether to side for the government or rebels leading to different endings, so that's up to the player. The story missions are done well and are varied to provide a good experience, but as said before are far between. There are different chapters which change regulations for the outpost which again add nice variety and work well with "beggars" which are appear here and their basically begging you to let them in despite their faulty paperwork, regardless of entering or rejecting them there's a unique letter for each. No real consequences other than not seeing said letter, if you let them in you get the standard penalty for screwing up, but you may get a reward from said "beggar". The story is not the vocal point of the game it's there just to add another layer, it's not particularly complex, but it is fun and enjoyable. Overall thoughtsIf you enjoy sim's you'll love this one with a nice unique twist rarely seen, and if you loved papers please you'll also love this more complex and open version of it, if you hate either of these than you'll hate this game as it can get repetitive like any simulator . The game is updated frequently (as of writing) and we are looking forward to our next big update the endless mode, which rids of the limit days in the story and goes on well forever with more features. If you're still hesitant to pay $30 for just story then wait until endless comes out. Overall if i had to give the game a rating it'd be a solid 8/10. I hope this review helped and i thank you for reading it my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police is its own worst enemy. Screening people entering the boarder, and checking for contraband is great fun. I wish I could do it all day. Then the game interrupts my daily checks because "the border station is under attack" so now I get to play a shooter. Is the shooting BAD? No. Is it as good as an actual dedicated shooter game? No. It's mediocre.And this repeats over and over. Start actually playing the most polished and fun part of the game (the border screenings) and get interrupted to do a half-baked stealth mission. Then a half-baked investigation mission. Then a half-baked tail sequence.  Every single one I begrudgingly complete to get back to the border screenings.I don't need this game to be CoD, LA Noire, and GTA. Some people with bad tastes or low budget might appreciate this "a bit of everything" approach.  But as an avid gamer I wish the game would've stuck to what its good at, and the part that is the most fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Some red flags to consider when shopping for "simulator" titles like this: 1. When you click on the developer's name it redirects to the entire PlayWay S.A. catalog. It's common practice with PlayWay to obfuscate what games a developer worked on before their current one, especially when the current one is likely to gain traction with content creators (like this one, which is going to sell itself on "a 3D Papers, Please.")2. Gunplay. Sim titles like this are a hodgepodge of mechanics and ideas, usually thrown together to pad for time. First-person shooter segments are never the strong point of a simulator title and this one leans into them quite frequently. Having spent a little time with it: the guns *could* be worse but they're in no way fluid or fun. Just bog-standard, and the only real UI to facilitate shooting is a weird red dot hovering over enemies, which feels like the result of a developer realizing all the earth tones in the map and character designs means you can't actually SEE the enemies that well. The solution: a cartoon dot that you just have to aim under to get headshots every time. 3. Too many concepts. Contraband Police could be a solid game with just the border crossing and the idea of upgrading your outpost to be more effective. Gas Station Simulator showed you can have a really jankily-built game still have a sense of progression just by hiring AI and assigning them to do your least-favorite tasks. Frankly, I'd much rather not have to leave the outpost and partake of the lackluster driving sequences to travel to locations I don't particularly care for. Even the shootouts where the border post gets attacked could be interesting IF the whole point was I can upgrade my post to the point it's self-reliant. Sure, I can give my guys better guns and armor but at the end of the day, I still have to throw contraband and prisoners in a van and go run chores early-game. From reviews I'm seeing here, I know my dream of having a Gas Station Simulator-esque border crossing where I level up my NPCs to do menial tasks automatically (perhaps even add multiple inspection lanes and let an NPC do inspections for me with the understanding they have to flag me if any real inspection is needed) are not to be. The upgrades are purely to make things stronger when random attacks happen. It's aggressively okay, but I worry I'll be back to this review in a few hours of gameplay with the same story most popular simulator titles have: after the first few hours they KNOW a streamer will broadcast, it drops off. Maybe it won't. For now: buy with caution.
