_childDocuments_.review: While I do absolutely love the game, there are a few things I'd like to point out: 1. It is very difficult to see broken windows (sometimes its impossible, even during daytime) ...maybe make a blue outline for all the windows so they are easier to see? Or perhaps maybe just make them shattered/"spider-webbed" so its easier to identify it.2. Sometimes it can be confusing to determine exactly what the entry regulations are. For example, one of the regulations is when someone has more than 3 problems with their car they should be denied entry. Well... what if someone has *exactly* 3 problems with their vehicle? Can they be approved, or not? (I'm pretty sure I've declined them *and* listed it as an entry regulation- which passed me on the inspection, other times it fails me... I need to go back and play again to make 100% sure).3. Trying to get a perfect score on the inspections during later stages of the game is very time consuming/ tedious... I wouldn't mind if we had another 5-10 minutes for each in game day.4. Getting attacked during an inspection... God, I hate that part of the game so much. Its not because "Ah! Oh my god, we're getting shot at! leave us alone!" No...I hate it because of all the times I have a good inspection (I admit, they're not perfect), but the times where I spend what feels like an eternity trying to catch all the mistakes, and right as I'm about to approve or deny entry to someone, an attack happens, either that or I'll spend more than a few minutes inspecting a car only to realize just as I'm about to approve or deny them- it actually turns out they're a smuggler. Before I can approve/ deny/ find contraband and arrest someone... We get attacked. Next thing I know the driver gets scared and drives off. Yeah... So much for getting my moneys worth after inspecting someone. It is realistic, I admit... but its super annoying.5. Having a time limit to return to the border. Again, yes, it's realistic... but annoying when I just chased down a smuggler. (For those who don't know, you can still search the car for contraband), I recommend looking for all of it first *before* arresting the driver so you don't have to worry about the time limit.6. Contraband in animals... yes, really. I think the game was intended to have it be so that if there is contraband in an "animal," its actually supposed to be fake/not move at all. this only happens if the animal is unloaded. If you unload an animal and its moving, its real. If you unload an animal, but its not moving, it's fake.I do love the story! I wont spoil anything, but I love details like if you deny entry to someone because... legally speaking, you have to, it turns out people are actually being deadly serious when they beg you about letting them in because if you don't, they will lose their job/ house/ family/ friends/ etc. not only do the send you threatening letters in the mail next to the newspaper, they likely are the ones who cause you to be attacked. (This would make my complaint about attacks invalid to those who weren't paying attention) However, for those of you who weren't paying attention, what I'm saying is how I actually *like* being attacked at random, because its realistic for you to receive retaliation/ karma for ruining someones live(s), plus if you're fast enough, you can loot bodies, but it does suck to lose a car you were inspecting.Overall, I give 4.5 out of 5 because of the imperfections/ bugs/ glitches I mentioned earlier, but its still very close to being perfect, maybe give yourselves a few months or a year to improve, and this game will be a perfect 5 stars!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a magnificent game. It's stimulating, challenging, and requires the most thorough of thinking. The comparisons to Paper Please are warranted, and I loved that game also. But as someone who loved that game, I was also a bit worried about what direction Contraband Police would go. It didn't make it any better that it was yet another Unity game, which is ironic considering Papers Please was updated in the Unity engine. But I think you know what I mean. There's no shortage of janky simulations made in Unity that simply borrow the same assets from every other game. But my expectations of a jank broken game with half assed mechanics was completely unfounded, and honestly, kind of jerky on my part. Okay, not just kind of jerky.. Very jerky. Crazy Rock and PlayWay hit out of the park with this niche investigative simulator, and I commend them for it. This game is exhilarating! I love it. I absolutely love it. Criminals can be clever in the way they hide contraband, but it's not even just the contraband you need to watch out. Just like in Papers Please, you need to check their papers for forgeries, incorrect passport numbers, expiration dates, compare vehicle weight, keep an eye out for wanted criminals, and much more, *including* investigations and missions that take place in the game itself away from your border patrol! And many of these missions also lead into what is also my favorite part about this game.. The combat. Combat should not be as fun as it is for a game like this. You'd think it'd be an afterthought, but it's not. It won't be something along the levels of Escape From Tarkov, but it doesn't have to be. It's fun.Now my absolute favorite inclusion is somewhat of a recent feature, and that is the endless mode! Which is something that the development team didn't even need to add, but they did! They added it, and it's addictive. In the campaign, you're allowed to upgrade your facilities like office, jail, and vehicles, but in endless mode, there's so much more to upgrade!When I saw my favorite Youtuber Drae play this on his channel, I knew immediately that it was worth at least worth a gander. But the game just kept getting so much better, and the developers kept doubling down on improving the game.. And I absolutely love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game! I absolutely loved the gameplay loop, got 17 hours out of it which was what I expected for the story mode. There's no endless mode yet, but I've read it's planned.I hope the game will eventually get more content such as : more faces (women?), new vehicles, new rules, new weapons, new outpost upgrades (especially this one since it gives you a feeling of progression and there's not much to do once you're rich and bought everything, one of those upgrades could be a NPC to assist you in your car when going outside), etc. The loop is working well, so more content to expand on it would be awesome! When I first played the prologue, I thought the open world wasn't working well with the "papers, please" aspect of the game.. but upon actually playing the full game it's actually very good! It's a nice break to give you other things to do. My favorite main story quest in the game has to be the murder investigation one! I love thrillers so it's no surprise that I enjoyed it, but I was really surprised that those quests weren't redundant which I was expecting at first. Not at all, they're varied and don't ever feel the same. Music is also really good.Here's a small section on what I didn't like:- Gang attacks in the open world: apparently it's going to get fixed soon, which is good, because there's too many of them for very little reward so it was a bit annoying to me.- Sniper rifle was such a let down, doesn't seem strong at all and no scope either to facilitate head shots- I wish smugglers' snake symbol were harder to detectI'm really nitpicking because I loved the game, would definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game play and borderline addictive. I LOVED Papers Please and this game tops that 100%. While in Papers Please you sit in your post all day and just check papers of course. This game you actually get to be first person outpost military. The way they implement the first person element just makes the game that much better. On top of that you have to worry about rebels attacking your outpost as well as people smuggling contraband through tires,bodywork and etc. Not too mention you can actually leave your post in your car similar to an open world type style game to get new equipment drop off prisoners to the labor camps as well as some side mission that act as if you are just border patrol. They did a good job making the game fun and interesting and on top of that you can upgrade your whole outpost there is a campaign which is cliche but not terrible by any means. I love the game play this game has to offer and played it 13 hours straight just grinding out campaign missions and the addictive endless mode it offers.     Very good game I recommend to anybody who played Papers Please I highly recommend the game for the same reason I would recommend the other they just did it better. 7/10 100% looking forward to any improvement the game might come out due to positive reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Inspector mode is out and it's even worse than the story mode. Oh well.I can't recommend this at the moment. It's got way too many problems that stand in the way of enjoying it.Initially there is a good amount of checks that need to be made, but quickly you get completely overwhelmed with all manner of nonsense checks and it's far too easy to overlook something. It wouldn't be so bad if I could save the game whenever I wanted, but I can't. The game has no save function, only autosaving once per day.Spending 10 minutes carefully checking off a bunch of stuff only for the person to drive off and then you get docked ~100 money for missing that they had a broken side mirror doesn't make me want to be more careful next time it makes me want to reload, and that means restarting the whole day as you can't save.There are side quests, but I've not done any of them because the opportunity to take them seems to be literal seconds, and they occur right in the middle of a workday, sometimes right in the middle of when you're performing a check. Why? As a result I've rejected all of them.Driving is buggy, my van has ended up hitting *something* and coming to a dead stop on multiple occasions. Plus any car chases or anything you do can lead you to the far side of the map, and then you've got a damn timer to get back to the border before you fail the day for some reason. TIMERS SUCK.The checks themselves are often buggy. There's a game mechanic where you can click the name/date/whatever and have the game match it. Often when I've done that and the inspection report is clean I've marked the documents and approved, the person has driven off, then it's come up saying the name and date were invalid and I'm docked money. wtf? Again, this would cause me to reload an earlier save, but I can't.Checking for illegal goods is buggy. There's supposed to be a marker on locations that indicate contraband, but often there isn't. So you'll do all the myriad of checks, find everything's all good, and wave the person off. Whoops you've just lost more money because there was contraband here there and everywhere, in all those places you checked and found nothing. AGAIN - this would make me reload an earlier save, WHICH I CAN'T.There are a bunch of issues like this, most of which could be worked around by being able to save the game whenever I damn well please. I have no idea why these developers continue to make games with no ability to save the game. It's a basic function that should be in your game, and if it's a design choice, it's a stupid choice.Finally, people are saying that the game is way too short. A game like this should provide 60+ hours gameplay at least, and apparently people are completing it in 11-15 hours. I wouldn't know though as I've not been able to force myself past 5 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I replayed papers please right before buying this, to see if it would hold a candle to it, and I have to say, it's a near perfect spiritual sequel. It does have some annoying problems, but the pros outweigh the cons ten times over.You run a checkpoint, much like in papers please, but you get a ton more interactivity. Finding contraband in PP is a pretty quick and easy process, but figuring out someone is smuggling alcohol inside their seats and then getting to tear them out with your knife is SO satisfying. I absolutely love the core gameplay.I'll talk about the few cons I have, because the developers seem pretty receptive to feedback, and because I think they're worth mentioning, but keep in mind that although I might sound harsh, my list of pros is "pretty much everything else"The cons:There are collectibles, which give a decent amount of money, so they're great to find, especially early on. There are some that are common sense to find, funny ones, like the one hidden in the bathroom right next to your house, and then ones that are absolutely impossible to find without a guide. Driving can be really slow, especially in the beginning (when you'd be looking for the collectibles), and these files and buried chest can be in absolutely random spots that the game will never take you near without you exploring there for yourself. If you'd like to randomly scour across an almost completely empty open world, be my guest, but otherwise I'd ignore them or use a guide. Some off these hiding spots are actually f*cked and I NEVER would have found them in a million years.The clunky driving from Thief Simulator is back, and it is in rare form. This can be annoying in its own way while you get used to it, (or re-get used to it if you love Thief Simulator like I do), but there are two major problems1. There are car chases. The way the trees and roads are designed, it is absolutely impossible to offroad and try to cut someone off, so you're stuck driving behind them and slowly gaining on them unless you invest thousands of dollars into buying and upgrading the fast car.2. You can put a siren on, which is great and convenient because most people will get out of your way, except for the walking people in the police station who have absolutely no issue with walking right in front of your car. You really never drive without the siren on, it's just so useful. Except some drivers bug out and seem magnetically attracted to your car. I swear, some of these drivers are paid off by the rebels, they seem legitimately out for your blood. If you get caught in a random encounter, bullets do a ton of damage to your car, so any car crash can be fatal. I remember one time, I was very far from the checkpoint, and some guy tboned me, kept going, and pushed me directly into a tree. My car exploded, killing him and stranding me all the way across the map. I'm now out $250 for the car, $500 for a "fatal accident" and have to either spend the next 5-10 minutes holding shift and w, or reload a save and start the WHOLE day over. It really sucked.However, if you can deal with that and minor bugs, like things phasing into each other, and the car radio audio doubling and turning into a very unpleasant listening experience, this is a wonderful game with a lot to love in it. I can definitely see myself putting 100 hours into it. It's genuinely so much fun.Surprisingly, the gun fights, although pretty simplistic, is pretty satisfying! (Hot tip, upgrade your house early on, it upgrades your max health, which is a must have). In Papers Please, there was a beauty in its simplicity, but in Contraband Police, there is so much more depth that I found really rewarding and enjoyable.In my opinion, a must buy for anyone who enjoyed Papers Please. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police is a game where you role-play as a border post commander in the early 80's communist era. You have been assigned as the new police inspector at the checkpoint. There are smugglers trying to fool you and the vehicles are packed with illegal goods.Watch a snippet of gameplay here: You start by checking the driver and his papers, just like a real checkpoint officer.You should also identify inconsistencies between the driver's passport and vehicle registration papers.Are they the legal owner of the vehicle? Is the car safe to drive? After completing this task, you will proceed to the final vehicle inspection.Anything can happen, so it's important to make sure no stone is left unturned at the end of your inspection. In communist Russia, collecting contraband is considered a service to your country, from secret compartments under the hood to the underside of the vehicle and tires. Your duties in the smuggling police will range from visually inspecting the vehicle to dismantling car parts.Receive and confiscate illegal food, beverages and illegal drugs. After deciding whether to let them in or deny entry, the game prompts you and rewards you with extra cash if your decision was correct.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10: Rather than recycle that stupid Russian Reversal joke written in the review for the prologue, the most important thing to know is that  is the greatest law enforcement simulation ever made. The FPS element was a bigger part of this game than originally anticipated.Nominated for  for 2023.Enough has changed since the prologue that ol' Il Pallino had to write a whole new review. Despite the full release of  still taking place in the early-1980's and featuring border control, what has changed is that the game becomes progressively more difficult. First the player only needs to check the travel documents of people coming into the fictional nation of Acaristan. (Which is in the likeness of the former Soviet Union.) On the second day, the player will be made to inspect vehicles suspected of smuggling contraband into Acaristan. On the fourth day, the player will need to account for the sort of cargo that freight trucks bring into Acaristan. Sometime afterwards, the player will then need to check vehicle registrations, check vehicle weights, and make note of damage to vehicles. Once the player has finished making note of everything, a decision needs to be made to either allow the traveler into Acaristan or turn them away. Anyone caught with contraband should be arrested and eventually sent off to a good old fashioned work camp. Contraband will eventually clog up the storeroom (where the player may need space for other crap) so the player will need to make a trip every so often to the  to unload their contraband for cash. The player will likely also want to visit Vlad's Tools so they can buy replacement tools to locate contraband with. Vlad also sells weapons for which the player will need in the event that bad guys attack the border crossing. (And even ambush the player in the small area beyond the border crossing that's within Acaristan.)See the review for . Although I suppose a screenshot for the lazy would be sufficient!Everything about  is positive, duh! Well, it was nice that  features the ultimate plot twist about communist countries: They're more capitalist than what capitalist country propaganda had people believing back during the Cold War. Rather than the government just throwing money at the border crossing, the player is expected to sustain the border crossing out of their own pocket by making the correct call in either allowing or denying people from nearby inferior nations into Acaristan. The player can even make money taking bribes from smugglers who occasionally offer them. If that's not enough, trade with incoming aliens (along with Acaristani citizens) in which the player can try to buy low and sell high as a side hustle. (For better or worse, the player cannot make use of the coffee, toilet paper, and pure vodka that can be bought and sold.) Sometimes smugglers will crash the gate, in which case the player will need to run to their police vehicle (one of three possibilities exists) and drive after the gate crasher which will lead in either the arrest or death of the gate crasher and a time limit to return to the border crossing to discourage players from thoroughly examining the contents of the vehicle that just crashed the border. (And perhaps make a quick run to either the work camp to deposit the gate crasher or Vlad's Tools.) Fortunately, if the player gets into a firefight with terrorists, the clock stops so the player can either take evasive action or shoot up all of the bad guys.The addition of a UV light to see where contraband is hidden is a nice addition and saves wear and tear on the tools the player can purchase. (Ol' Il Pallino once encountered two red vehicles in a row when a red vehicle was suspected of smuggling, and without the UV light, ol' Il Pallino would have torn up the seats, upholstery, tires, and fuel tank of the first vehicle when it wasn't a smuggler.) For better or worse, there's quite a FPS element to . While the mechanics may be too simplistic for a FPS lover, at least headshots count for something, and it isn't anywhere near as bad as the shootouts in . The player is punished for attacking any animals in the game. (That includes those dumb animals that are born and bred for slaughter that belong on a plate. Hooray for eople ating asty nimals!)There's something wrong with people who don't already own . Those poor souls are likely literally poor and cannot afford this amazing game about law and order! Oh, and glory to our beloved General Secretary Igor Acarov!

_childDocuments_.review: what can i say, a game that on the surface seems to have a simple premise of checking documentation at a border, deciding who crosses and who doesnt. however its more than that. as time shifts by, newer restrictions are imposed, which forces you outside of what you had learnt previously thinking you mastered the ability, and then a new curve ball comes full force, making you check newer documents for Novid 78 xD, amongst many other additional layers that end up teaching you a new mechanic in a non intrusive way, but also adds unique world events that effect the traditional and simple mechanics of a document checking game as this. it keeps it refreshing, and interesting. then ontop of that, you have an actually interesting narrative.. an active rebellion taking place, which over the course of the game and dependant on your decisions can directly affect how your day to day job plays, and what events unfold throughout the narrative. a dude coming across the border has contraband, but has told you his family is being held captive and is being forced to do this in order to free them.. do you ignore your compassionate side and lock him up under full force of the law, or do you take a temporary financial sacrifice to help him out.? or someones documents are clearly a fake, but theyre trying to cross the border as his children are orphaned and alone, or another guy is trying to cross to get to his sister thats on her deathbed. etc etc, you get the point. this game gives the player a chance to choose what kind of guard you wish to be. do you wanna be compassionate and feel joy when their kids send you a little drawing, and the guy thanks you. or do you wanna lock him up and hear his kids ended up dying? theres also key narrative moments that allow you to choose which side of the fight you wish to lean on.. feeling like you want to free your beloved country and allow its people to live in peace? join the blood fist, or do you wanna be a die hard cop that forced the law? then stick with them. each distinct choice has an important play in its branching narrative and its actually fun. i completed it in about ten hours or so. but it was truly different and fun. i sided with the rebellion, and allowed some people to pass in special instances. and in other times for criminals and rude folk i was brutal. the story in this game is fun, and the writing is amazing too that kept me interested and engaged. i wish it continued, but hey ho. id rather feel i enjoyed it and wished for more, than to have more and wish for it to end. ahem AC VALHALLA. the gun play is decent enough. wall leaning, leaning out of cover, but not in the sense of pressing e and q, but pre decided locations, which i found out way too late xD.. i did notice some issues with shots being registered when aiming down the sights, specifically more so with the pistol. but it was enjoyable enough. overall this game was a pleasant surprise, and i thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. theres so much they could do to expand on the story and its worlds narrative, continuing after the main story, with your choices playing a big part in it. id love that.wishlists: more story content continuing on from where it left off, with all player custom choices reflecting how it starts and what happens. or alternatively you could put us as a different character thats going after the character we play in the main. or even a origin story of how the rebellion started, and in the perspective of one of the fighters as the war rages on. or continuing it as a rebel in rebel controlled checkpoints, having to keep an eye for government loyalists trying to get through the border, or ex government officials and so on. more map to drive around, with more dynamic random world events. more guns, more incentive to continue playing after finishing the story. but overall, this is a great game. BRING MOD SUPPORT. WOULD LOVE THIS TO HAVE FULL VR SUPPORT WITH MOTION CONTROLS AND SUCH.

_childDocuments_.review: Papers Please started this interest with border patrol, and Contraband Police took it a step further. For an Early Access game it has a decent amount of content for the player to enjoy. I'm optimistic about this game and hope the devs continue with this great start. I would certainly recommend trying the demo at the very least. The premise of Contraband Police is the player takes the role of a border guard in a communist / soviet-esque setting. The players success (and ability to continue playing the game) will depend on their ability and efficiency as a border guard. The better you are - the more money. The worse you are, the chances you might go broke due to upkeep. The  is very basic and straightforward. The player interacts regularly with items and people to check for any discrepancies. It starts simple with passport pictures, expired documents, and potentially some smuggling but as the game progresses the checks become a lot more difficult. In a way, it makes you think how much has to go through someones head when doing security. As situations in Karikatka unfold and new developments happen, the demands around the checks will change. Fortunately, the game does have some manual click-to-check functions for players to do checks quicker. It will cost the player a little focus each time it is used (which will enforce the need to rest). There are tools the player can buy in the world to improve their border guard ability. Sometimes this may be weapons, it may be tools, or upgrade to the player's border stop. (be it personnel or buildings). It is an open world map where players can interact with a few places, drop contraband or prisoners off. A van is given to the player to start, but if player's don't feel like contraband and prisoners all the time they may call for a transport (which will cost a pretty penny)! The premise is the player allows cars or trucks to go through and can ask the driver for documents or to step out of the car. If necessary, the player can make arrests and find contraband around and in the vehicle. Players may account for cargo and take it out of the vehicle to further inspect if anything else is hidden. While this is happening, random events will occur that will demand the player's attention. My suggestion is to do these missions as they pay a pretty penny. Don't worry about the border though, it doesn't seem like the drivers have any choice but to wait :). I don't know if this was on purpose, but it is appreciated when things go haywire and gangsters start raiding the border and the player needs to defend (hopefully with more than just a pipe). There are other missions that help  with the development of the story and it feels like the missions are decently well rounded. The  are pretty good. They aren't extremely detailed, however the game does a good job immersing the player into the environment. The level design seems pretty well organised to me and well laid out. There are cut-scenes in the game in addition to small animations that NPCs will engage in. Visual upgrades to the border base are also noticeable as well as the personnel. The  are well done. I think more needs to be added to this domain, but again, for an Early Access game I think a decent amount was included. The player can play music while driving around in the police truck. Overall, I would highly recommend this game on sale. If it seems interesting to you even if its not on sale, I'd say go for it. I really enjoyed my play through and can only hope the devs continue to add to the game as much as possible. Fingers crossed down the line there is some sort of endless mode and hopefully workshop items/missions. TO THE DEVS:-Endless mode would be highly recommended and I think appreciated-Any plans for workshop items / missions down the road? I'm sure the community would love to help out-The steering is a little weird and stiff... not sure if it was meant like that. The animation for the turning also isn't the most accurate... small detail :)-Perhaps a sort of flash/easy mode for those new to the game. I played Papers Please so picking this up wasn't an issue, but noticed some other gamers were overwhelmed - even with a solid tutorial. Maybe an option in the gameplay menu?-Well done with the environment, actually impressed with how much there is even in Early Access. Continue working on the world and adding events, items, things, NPCs whatever to it.-Give player an ability to see future ambushes maybe with a radar down the road? -AI partners do not feel useless and actually provide cover / do something during gunfights. Enemy AI also feels well balanced. -What about stopping regular traffic? Why not add more to the game in terms of exploring by allowing the player to do random stops INSIDE the country? Perhaps on endless mode, may be too much for campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, and this is my opinion, which might help the dev team and other players who are undecided about buying it.Firstly, I must say that I really enjoyed it, so I'll give it a positive review. I played through the whole game without getting bored or anything like that.Although it's quite repetitive, and you mostly do the same tasks, it managed to hold my interest. The fact that the torch doesn't reveal everything, and you need to keep an eye out for hidden stuff, is a plus that prevents the game from feeling too mechanical.There's a significant variety among all the newcomers. As far as I can recall, I didn't see the same face twice. However, I have to mention that there are no women in the entire game. Everybody is male, which made it a bit monotonous for me (I'm not getting into issues of sexism or inclusivity; I'm simply saying that seeing only guys all the time got a bit boring).Overall, I quite enjoyed playing it.On the downside, I would like to point out that I didn't find anything in the story that made me go against the government. In games like Papers, Please or The Beholder, the dark side of the government is more obvious. However, in this game, I couldn't see a reason to be against it.Similarly, there are a few moments where you can choose to help people and let them pass. I did it, and apart from a thank-you letter, there wasn't much difference if I hadn't let them go. I suppose it's just the personal satisfaction of helping people.To be honest, I had the feeling that there's no real story. Things happen, but that's it. They ask you to go here and there, fix a situation, but I didn't feel like there's a proper underlying story.Sometimes, when I caught someone with contraband, they offered me a bribe. I accepted it once, but the money wasn't even the same as the penalty I received for letting them pass, so I didn't do it anymore. I earned more money by following the rules (the bonus for catching a criminal, sending them to prison, confiscating the contraband and promotion is greater than what they offer you).Another thing is that the guards in the zone are a bit useless. I mean, they help when you get attacked in the control point, but they do nothing when a newcomer tries to escape. Also, you can't take one or two guards with you as cover when you go out and get ambushed, which happens constantly. I think they could be more useful.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Good little game! Fun gameplay, decent story (including an unexpected murder mystery) with multiple endings, very nice difficulty adjustment settings, and an endless non-story mode that I was glad to see.In the whole game I only encountered a single gameplay bug, any mistakes you make in your inspections are your own fault. The one bug I found was when I got penalized twice for wrongly arresting a single person (once when I arrested him, the second one when I had Maximov clear away his car and cargo.)Things the game could have done better:-Graphics. The game's graphics are just fine, but even on max settings there are some quite blurry textures for the some surfaces, and people's faces can look like they have strong sunburn.-Too many smugglers and not enough people who try to persuade you with stories to let them in.-No women in the game whatsoever.-There are only like 5 voice actors who worked on the game, so you routinely hear the same voice lines delivered in the same way by the same voices.-I fully expected to encounter the man Novikov spoke of who he wanted revenge on, but I never saw him (though it is possible I simply didn't recognize him, if anyone can confirm he is an encounter, please let me know)-I wish the FOV could go a little higher.Other than those small criticisms, the game is very good and I highly recommend it for anyone who remembers Papers Please and always thought a 3D first-person version would be cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: This game comes in with a unique-ish concept and spends most of it's time as a low quality shooter.Not enough border guarding. There is no real pressure to churn through new arrivals. It's very simple to do a thorough inspection on all 4-5 men in single passenger vehicles. Pay is based on perfect reviews, not numbers of processed. So very easy to shine your UV light on everything and just tick all the boxes.I do like the idea of the game, and it has really good potential. Taking a break from the border to drive prisoners to the labour camp and have a gun fight on the way is really cool. But..The story is a very weak, I have no motivation to care about the rebellion or side with the smugglers. Even the people pleading to get through to visit their dying mother. It all lacks a bit of heart and narrative. NPC guards are just shells waiting around for a raid. Raids go on for too long, I found myself later in the game just crouching behind a box, waiting for my guards to shoot the generic bad guy raid, (from the same direction as every other raid) for another 3 mins and afkd to get a drink. Again, low quality shooty bang bang. I'd love it if guards could react to border events. So when I'm running to the police car, shooting my AK at a fleeing subject, heart thumping in my chest. And my guard says "Hello commander" in a flat neutral tone as I rush past. And I die a little inside.

Would recommend this game to everyone liked papers please, likes 80s USSR vibes and simply wants a great game about border police in 1980s. Definitely was worth the wait. Thanks for this amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now, I can't recommend this game due to just how much work is still needed to get rid of gamebreaking bugs and glitches.Restarting from checkpoint after failing or dying leads to an infinite loading screen and the only way to move on is to alt+f4 and then restart the day. Ambushes are bugged because enemies glitch through the map and are nowhere to be seen. This is more of a severe annoyance due to constantly being hounded by the combat music everywhere I go. Because there is an active ambush that is impossible to end, I'm unable to see any other objectives or move on to do anything else in peace.  Also, I'm unable to melee attackers because my character gets into some kind of bugged state where my melee weapon never reaches the enemy despite the weapon being in their faces. (I've had this happen with the knife and the pitchfork already and I'm positive it'll happen with any other melee weapon.) I'm unable to switch weapons. I'm unable to interact with vehicles and the only way to deal with this is to alt+f4 and start the day over because reloading checkpoints is broken due to the infinite loading screen bug. I found out that the game loves to corrupt your save files and/or delete them automatically and there's nothing the player can do to prevent this from happening. Because of this, the only way to progress is by constantly restarting the day over and over and pray you don't get hit in the face by another game-breaking issue and you play absolutely flawless every day.This is just a few of many game-breaking and severe issues this game has and it's mind-boggling how the devs never bothered fixing these problems and it's even more egregious how this game has so many positive reviews with so many game-breaking bugs. Apparently, people think games that are barely functional are masterpieces. I'm more convinced that content creators blow this game up so much and give the wrong impressions. Is the game good? No. I can't get through the first day because, I keep encountering countless game-breaking bugs one after another with no end in sight. Can it be good? Yes, if the devs actually get off their rear-ends and fix their game instead of riding the high of "success" and exposure it's been getting lately like every other studio that gets a spot of exposure and cares more about that than their own game does. I don't care what others say. The game is broken beyond belief and it's a miracle it even functions. These issues should have been dealt with a very long time ago.

Being the good cop that I am, I unloaded an entire magazine into his testicles and got paid for it. 10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of this game is great. It has the potential to be a lot of fun. I think the devs did a great job so far in terms of gameplay, however it's clearly still in the works.I was going through the five day training, read all documents precisely on the first day and still got it incorrect when there was either one discrepancy or nothing wrong at all. Alternatively, when I denied someone for one discrepancy, I was told they were cleared for entry. I sat there utterly confused, scratching my head wondering what I could possibly be doing wrong. I was both penalised for letting someone with a false expiration date through and penalised for denying someone with a false expiration date also. The only thing I could think of was their age but there isn't really a way to check whether their age is correct. It just tells it to you.Ultimately, I checked forums and it turns out that I am not alone in this. It is a bug. While this can and most likely will be patched, it feels like something that should have been checked prior to the game's release. As a result, I, as well as others in the playerbase are losing money for no reason whatsoever. That really puts a damper on things and can hinder someone from progressing the way they're supposed to.Please look into this because this game genuinely feels fun otherwise and it's a shame that something like that can ruin the experience.Otherwise, I have high praises here and will change my review once this is fixed. Usually, it feels kind of silly to give a poor review on a game for one bug (so far, there may be more), but this is something that affects the main gameplay and if someone doesn't bring this up or criticise the game's flaws, the devs are going to assume everything is honky dory.

_childDocuments_.review: Really struggling to see whether or not I should recommend this. My reasons are below.First off, if you know and like "Papers, Please" , you'll like this. You play as a border guard, also checking documents, but also you check vehicles. Rules and laws keep changing so you have to keep being focused as the gameplay changes. I love this, and as a person who has always (strangely) been really interested in playing a game where you are a border / checkpoint guard, I really enjoyed every aspect of this.There are some things that I liked less and stuff I think should be / have been improved on, like for example:- you get like 5 cars daily to check, and they all come simultaneously at the start, it's not like you get a car in the morning, wait a bit and two more show up. You know, a little randomness of when the cars arrive, I think this would be more dynamic and realistic.- random events should be added. There are tons of scenarios that I can think of straight away that can really peak gameplay in a game like this; attacks from newcomers (shoot out from the vehicle as you ask for their documents), terrorist attacks (VBIED), more ethical decisions (family of your character come as newcomers) etc- Checkpoint management, as for now, we can only upgrade our house, prison and warehouse. But what about all of the trash scattered around the checkpoint? That weird cabin you cannot enter? Gun emplacements? Watch towers? Search lights? Etc Etc.- Assign tasks to other guards. I was kind of hoping you would do checks on vehicles together. Instead, you have 7 guards wandering around, doing nothing. It would be cool if you could assign a guy to check the vehicle cargo for example, as you go over personal documents.Other stuff I truly hated:- Roadside ambushes. This happened WAY too often, not just way too often, I happened literally everytime I went out. Not just once, most of the time I got ambushed two to three times, which is genuinely annoying. They always kill the prisoners in the back instead of me, they ruin the vehicle, and just give me the idea that I am in no mood to go outside the checkpoint anymore. But, I can hear you say; "you can turn it off", well, I have a point about that too:- Optional random events. I find this really weird, to be able to turn off stuff like roadside ambushes. I feel like this is part of the game, and part of the experience. It feels like a really weird choice to have it on either off or on. I feel like the game should rather focus on tweaking it, and making it less toxic than having the option to turn it off completely.- Lastly, the ending. What an ending... I was enjoying the game, doing checks at the border. I had fun plans to upgrade everything to the max soon, but then I got the final mission, did it, and the game gave me the credits and deleted my save file. What..? I know there is an endless mode coming (I think, I hope), but why deny me from at least spawning back, allowing me to spend all the money I had tried hard to save, and buying everything? Also basically denying me to unlock other achievements? I literally have to start the campaign all over again to do this. That is a genuine weird thing. And something I want to turn this review into a not recommended game.But, while I enjoyed the rest, I wont let the ending ruin the rest of what I enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun sim-work game. It does what it says on the tin and adds a little story that is cohesive and adds meaning to the game. Endless mode is fun as well and allows you to focus on whatever you want to do. Check the papers, clear them or reject them, anlyze each car in minute detail to try for a perfect inspection, go on missions, get ambushed, fight back, arrest criminals and collect contraband. It's all up to you.There's still  a couple of bugs, but nothing that destroys the game (you might have to restart a day here and there if it locks up). The biggest issue is returning to the base when an road-ambush was still ongoing. This locked my game every time. So make sure you kill or escape it completely and lose the notification before heading in for the night.The action side of the game itself is not too challenging and most of time you won't have to worry about dying or failing often, but that's OK.In typical simulator-game fashion, the achievements are a GRIND to 100%, but they are all obtainable through natural play. They can be a bit janky in a couple of places. --Get all the roadblocks done on your first time through a save file --On the  contraband drop (endless mode) get all the crates BEFORE the bandits show up for Pacifist, if they spawn the achievement won't pop even if you don't attack them--Patient zero is an RNG event inside an RNG event, it will show up but it might take longer than you think it would, Easily the most tedious achievement. --David vs. Goliath is probably the most fun to try and get. It was nice to be able to just reload the day and go back to the mission start to retry it--if you had to wait for a natural occurrence to get this one, the success rate would be even lower than it already is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my review only playing 1 play through of the campaign (I did a government play-through) and a bit of the inspector mode.Pros:- The inspection system, it felt satisfying to spot mistakes in peoples paperwork and finding the symbols on their transport/cargo to signify they were a smuggler etc.- They gave u more to look out for in the inspection system progressively rather than having to look out for every little thing from the get go, it made it a lot less intimidating to learn and more friendly towards small attention span people like myself.- The upgrading system felt straight forward and gave you something to grind towards, so I see that as a great incentive to do inspections correctly and earn extra cash when you can.- The story itself was alright, it was obviously very political and aimed to make you choose a side very early on (at least with the campaign mode) I only chose the government as my first and probably only play through cause I didn't like disrespecting the inspection system, which was my favourite aspect of the game so yea.- Items felt nice to use, the shovel and pitchfork i felt like i used probably like 4 times during the whole time i played. ( knife MVP just saying)- I found the smuggler info on the board somewhat useful but honestly i would usually just blacklight the vehicle anyway and you can usually find out pretty quick if they are a smuggler.Cons:- The driving in the game felt kinda janky, which made having to drive after criminals if they drive through the outpost kinda tedious. I also didn't like how if the person decided to make you chase them, you couldn't properly search their cargo for contraband cause you couldn't unpack it outside of the outpost (unless they had a particular type of car that let u access the cargo easily). Just to specify you can still cut tires and other stuff fine when you finish the chase, its more just if cargo items in the back are stacked ontop of each other you cannot search the items under the top of the stack.- Half the map felt useless to venture to, i pretty much only went to drop off prisoners, buy stuff then sell contraband and go back to base, then repeat. (unless a campaign mission required a different location.)- The random rebels camping around the map that would start shooting at you, felt not worth it to stop and actually deal with them. Usually because in campaign mode you were usually either on a time limit or you wanted to save as much time as possible to go back and sleep to recover perception points etc. Not to mention those encounters did not pay off money wise pretty much at all.- I wish you could place markers on the map, kinda like the campaign mission exclamation marks that turned up on screen, just so if you wanted to go somewhere it was easier to mark it out and just drive rather than checking map constantly.- I found it kinda annoying that most of the people who had sad stories (like telling me they were trying to reach their kid etc) majority of the time they had something up with their paperwork so you would be punishing yourself to let them through. Then you would get an angry letter the next day, idk I guess that was my fault I was siding with the government so.- Defected Bodywork.... I have no clue what this vehicle damage looked like half the time and mostly just guessed. (this ones probs my fault, I think there was a section in the book that would of explained it but yea)- Perception system (i dont remember the actual name but the thing you used to compare details to tell if something was wrong) I felt like this system was kinda useless? I barely used it at all during the inspection system itself, Usually I found you could just compare and tell on your own rather than needing your perception tokens.- Late game invades on your outpost, felt way too cluttered and just tedious to clear out all of the rebels. I understand why its like this but you would end up having to kill like 80 plus people, then after all that most of the bodies would despawn so you would only be able to loot like barely a quarter of the people left.OVERALL/TLDR:I like the game, even tho I have some cons that I did not like, I feel like the flow of the game and the objectives were fine. I think I'm going to enjoy inspector mode a lot more than the campaign since the outside outpost quests appear to be optional? So I can just do my silly inspections on Vehicles all day and vibe. I would give it like a 7.5 out of 10, I recommend at least 1 playthrough :D

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, this is my review of Contraband Police. I have recorded over 37 hours in this game so far, but with the arrival of endless mode I will start playing it again fully.  The contraband police is probably not for everyone.  Not everyone will enjoy this, but if someone gets the hang of it, they will have a lot of fun.  I was personally interested in the work of a border guard, so for me this was a simulator that I couldn't help but buy.  The game only has a main career so far.  A career as such is somehow not long enough.  even if you really enjoy the game and do everything in as much detail as possible, you will finish the campaign within a few days. But as I wrote above, the authors are working on endless mode and that should solve this problem.  A little about the campaign.  You play as the main border guard who checks passing cars and trucks.  At the beginning of the control, they are quite simple and the player is introduced to what his job will be.  These first days I really recommend reading everything and trying to understand everything otherwise you will have a problem in the later parts.  As your days at the border go by, you will constantly complain about your work.  You'll have to check more and more and watch out for more things with each check.  You will have to be more careful about contraband.  Sometimes faced with a difficult decision.  You will have to fend off border attacks from time to time.  Sometimes in the middle of the working day they may call you with a voluntary mission that I recommend doing.  They are interesting and above all they will give you quite a lot of money that will come in handy.  Speaking of money, you won't have much money in this game.  It can be said that you will have more money towards the end of the game.  Until then, you will still have something to put them into (better cells, better equipment for workers, better cars...).  The whole game is in the Eastern style.  There is nothing better than riding a Zhiguli and listening to fast Eastern style music while you go to stop at a small house by the road where Comrade will sell you a Kalashnikov.  Overall, players from slav countries will definitely enjoy it more.  The campaign has its own story.  The story is written quite well, I would say, but I won't describe it more because I don't want to give any big spoilers.  I tried to write this entire review as spoiler-free as possible.  I definitely recommend giving this game a try!  A very good addition to the simulators.  I apologize for any mistakes.  I'm writing this through a translator.

No save function the game auto saves only at the end of the day when you go to sleep or you can            restart the dayGames worth the money, if i had to make a suggestion it would be allowing to save so if you need to quit the game you don't lose progress if you haven't finished the day yet. _childDocuments_.review: Thee entire prologue available at the moment is a conditional training of the player in all the basic mechanics of the game. First, they explain to us how to check the documents, then they show us where to rest, how to cut tires and seats in search of contraband, where to put criminals, and so on. After completing the training, all this seems very obvious and understandable, but the player would definitely not be able to guess the many gameplay features on his own, so the training deserves special praise. Moreover, you need to understand that the checkpoint post is not everything that is implemented in this simulator. We’ll also have to travel by car, catch villains, and even shoot from a pistol.The most important thing, of course, is to find the smugglers who want to trick you and smuggle something across the border that cannot be smuggled. To prevent this, the player needs to inspect the documents of the citizen and his transport. These are two completely different processes, which are connected with each other. First, the player must take the person’s passport and other documents, starting to verify the data with each other. It is necessary to verify the name and surname in all provided documents, compare the expiry date of the passport with today, compare the stamp and background of the passport with the official data for a specific country.All the necessary data for comparison is available in the border guard’s notebook – there are indicated all the parameters that need to be paid attention to when evaluating the documents, there is a list of all currently available countries and all the data we need are indicated – what stamps can be, what passport colors are used in this country.Accordingly, if a person has one country indicated, and builds a seal from another, then it is worth taking a closer look at it and, of course, not letting it cross the border.There are actually many such subtleties, but in an hour you will understand them at a glance.It is important to clarify that our border guard has a stamina parameter, which is spent every time you compare parameters in documents using mouse clicks. However if you recheck everything several times or miss the mark, then by the end of the working day your endurance will end, and you will have to compare names, document numbers and seals by yourself, by eye.However, this is even more interesting – there is no sense of casualness.Moreover, it makes no sense, for example, to spend stamina comparing names or passport numbers – they can be compared by eye in a couple of seconds, it is better to spend energy on something important or not spend it at all.Don’t forget about transportAfter checking the documents, it is worth opening the form and putting crosses in those points that did not agree, and then proceed to inspect the car.Open all the doors and trunk, look under the hood, run through the cabin looking for suspicious things.Here you can even unload everything from the trunk, inspect and compare with the import invoice, banning the entry of the truck if it contains prohibited items or goods.Of course, you can not only inspect the interior for contraband, but also open seats, upholstery or tires in search of something prohibited.Everyone shouldn’t cut tires in a row – they will be fined if you just spoil a person’s property.To find a smuggler, you need to study the latest news reports, plus examine the list of suspects at a special stand. If, for example, there is a suspicion that contraband will be brought in today on such and such a car, then such a car should be inspected especially carefully.By cutting the seats and tires of the car, I was able to find contraband in the form of cigarettes, alcohol, packs of money and even drugs.For this, a citizen who tried to bring all this good to the country was sent to a temporary detention facility, and everything confiscated was thrown into a warehouse.Oh yes, you can still close your eyes to the violations of the citizen and take a bribe, letting him into the country, or you can put an innocent person in prison.That is, the developers thought of the possibility of a bad guard, who in a bad mood puts everyone in a row.Life outside the checkpointSurprisingly, the gameplay of the simulator during the inspection of documents and cars at the checkpoint does not end – the game has already implemented a fairly large map.The player has the function of delivering prisoners from a temporary detention facility to a prison, plus we ourselves deliver all the seized illegal to the state warehouse, receiving good monetary rewards for both these actions.For example, after the surrender of all the contraband and two prisoners, more than a thousand dollars fell into my account, which I then went and safely spent on tools.Yes, in a communist country, the guard buys himself tools for opening the cabin, tires and other containers in search of contraband, so the gamer will have to periodically go to the merchant and buy everything he needs.This is a very interesting process, since you need to look at the map constantly, while turning on the flashing lights and not crashing into everyone.In addition, there are situations when attackers simply hit the gases, breaking through the barrier – in such situations we can sit in a “loaf” and overtake the criminal, crashing into him at full speed.It’s an insanely fun process, in fact.ConclusionAt the moment, I can confidently say that I liked comparing documents at the checkpoint, looking for inconsistencies and putting a red stamp in a passport, and the process of assessing a car, inspecting it and opening it are quite exciting activities.

_childDocuments_.review: The game tries to be 3d "papers please" with extra content but falls flat at the attempts.Pointless tiny open world with no real reason to explore it. Money stashes are just radom piles scattered around with no clues given how to find them. Every day you know you gonna get ambushed by the same 4 bandits in the same locations. The checkpoint work never feels overwhelming, just 4 - 6 cars every day. The contraband could be easily spotted by using uv light, no variety in this. _childDocuments_.review: There's no women (except for the dispatcher)But that's fine because this game lets me beat up cars like a Street Fighter mini-game...In all seriousness this game is an example of a fine indie game, it might even look fun to play in VR. What with the driving, shooting, and slashing of tires, the day job of being a border guard isn't the only thing in store for players.Some complaints is that most of your fellow police are basically furniture except during a base assault, which is the main reason why you would even hire them (only other reason is the prison guard), they don't transport things for you (it would be interesting if they do and sometimes they might even steal the contraband for themselves if they are crooked cops) nor do they accompany you on missions, so as the new commander of the post you seem to be forced to do EVERYTHING except being a leader, nothing will ever get done without you...the entire station AND it's newcomers will wait for your return.Though you COULD gain the luxury of having stuff done for you down the line, the cops will charge you 500 dollars to have prisoners and contraband transported, you lose out on your gains by doing this and that's kinda dumb considering your position...so more busy work driving it is.  Vlad I can understand though, since he is an independent shopkeeper so having him come over at a cost makes sense.Additionally, while the game has some replayability (in choosing to play for another faction in the story) I don't really like the way it is handled, for example when you finish your final mission your game is just finished so if you have stuff you needed to do for achievements you are stuck playing a new game for that...except well, the game is mostly a bunch of busy work, they are fun for the first times but once you get done learning all the routine and game mechanics near the end of the first game it all feels very bland.  The story provided for both factions are not enough to get past another full game of busy work in my opinion, though they share different outcomes (in a singular picture with some descriptions) all the missions are the same except for the final mission, which is a quite a bit lazy.  The whole rebel path feels like a waste of opportunity because there is a lot of potential for being a double agent there, but instead both paths plays the same and that is most unfortunate, you will mainly be doing it for the achievements.Enclosed are my experience playing this game and beating this game for 15 hours, I took my time looking at all the gameplay and messed around quite a bit, so I hope it will be enough for a full experience for those who wants to look at the actual gameplay
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game, but that's purely because of my tastes and not necessarily because it's a bad game. At first glance the game seems pretty fun and relaxing. You start with a 5 day training to get the hang of it and during this time it's very doable. You slowly build up your knowledge and what you have to do each day.I was quite surprised on the last day of training when they wanted me to catch the runaway. Like... What... All of a sudden I had to respond fast en drive fast and they only way I figured out to stop him was to drive him off the road which results in a vehicle maintenance fee. Not to mention first time I was too slow and it was game over immediately. So driving back with the criminal in the car I was very much hoping this would not be a daily occurrence.Then the next day came and it became apparent instantly that the training doesn't cover even half of what the game entails. All of a sudden you need to check stamps, vehicle registration, weight, vehicle type, occupation... So much more than you did in the training. And I personally don't feel like they explain it that well.I need to check stamps now. But what do I compare them to? I can open the duty handbook but can't do a 'match'. Does this mean it's just something I need to visually check? And what about the occupations? When are they wrong or right? Also, do I only check for contraband when I can see on the board the driver matches a description of possible smugglers? Or do I always check for contraband?The more I read reviews and look at pictures, the more I get the feeling the game is more pointed to those who enjoy guns, violence and arresting/shooting people just for the sake of it. And don't get me wrong, that's okay, it just isn't what I personally was looking for in this game. I was more hoping for a relaxing 'be an officer of the law and do everything perfectly' kind of thing. I also read that later in game you have to fight rebels on the road and defeat raiders who come to the base.Not sure what that's about, but it doesn't sound like the relaxing gaming experience I wanted it to be. I don't see a way to change the game to being more easy so for me personally, this just isn't my kind of game.I do have to compliment the graphics and the making of the game. They really did a great job in how it all looks and feels. The game is in Russian? I think? I don't speak it so can only guess. But with subtitles it's very doable and I do like that there's voice acting for everything, makes the game feel more fleshed out.

Would love to see a Co-Op add on or mod, or something - just to be able to enjoy the game with a friend - that's my only complaint.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a puzzle game where you get feedback when you're done with the checks and how well you do them affects how much money you earn/lose. You can upgrade the station for better cars, better staff, more capacity, but I like that it never gets to a point in the game where you've upgraded everything and now there's nothing else to do because your staff is doing all the work for you; each staff member has their own role and your character is specifically the one for doing the checks. The FPS aspect is really easy (and this is coming from someone who is normally not very great at easier FPS games), so I wish there was an option to up the difficulty, but they do have different game modes. There is a story mode with all of the game features plus story events with different choices and endings, an endless mode which doesn't have the story events but you can play endlessly, and a challenge mode which is an endless mode where you just do the border checks and can compete globally. It's addicting and it's surprisingly fun to check documents. You can even choose to let people go for no reason, and sometimes the people you put in jail will break out and you'll have to fight them. Driving is annoying, but you can always fast travel.

_childDocuments_.review: Contraband Police is a game that offers a distinctive and intense immersion into the world of border security and law enforcement. With its focus on realism and the challenges of inspecting vehicles and identifying contraband, this title provides a unique experience that's both thrilling and educational.The core premise of Contraband Police revolves around your role as a border control officer, inspecting vehicles, identifying illicit items, and making decisions that can impact the safety and security of your fictional nation. The game's realism is evident from the get-go, with a vast array of vehicles to inspect and a variety of tools at your disposal to assist in your work.The tension and excitement that come with each inspection cannot be understated. The sense of urgency when identifying potential contraband and making quick decisions keeps you engaged, even if you're facing the same task repeatedly. The feeling of discovery when you uncover hidden items or catch a suspect in a lie is immensely satisfying.The game's graphics and audio add to the overall immersion. The environment is suitably gritty and realistic, creating a convincing portrayal of a border checkpoint. The sound design, from the engine hum of vehicles to the detailed inspection sounds, adds to the atmosphere.However, it's important to note that Contraband Police's realism can also be a double-edged sword. The game's complexity and the need to follow correct procedures might overwhelm some players, especially those new to the genre or looking for more casual gameplay.Additionally, the pacing can be slow, and the gameplay loop may feel repetitive to some players. If you're not captivated by the detailed inspection process and the constant scrutiny of documents and cargo, you may find the game less enjoyable.In conclusion, Contraband Police is a game that stands out for its dedication to realism and its focus on the intricacies of border control and law enforcement. It offers a thrilling and educational experience, immersing players in the daily tasks and challenges faced by those in this profession. While it may not cater to everyone's gaming preferences due to its complexity and potentially repetitive gameplay, it's a fascinating opportunity to explore the world of border security and contraband detection. If you're interested in the subject matter and are looking for a unique and immersive simulation, Contraband Police is well worth a closer look. It's an engaging experience that may just leave you feeling like a real officer on the thin blue line.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's fun, what can I say? Graphics could be better, but the lighting covers it up and gives the game a distinct feel. The only  downside(?) is that the game is quite easy, as soon as you get a gun most interactions become trivial. Spotting discrepancies in the actual border part isn't much of a challenge, with the only exclusion being the fake passports, but by that point you've upgraded your post enough to be able to scan every passport with the scanner. Despite that, the game does provide a nice challenge closer to the end, with you having to remember all the smuggler hints and remembering to check all 13 possible reasons to reject someone. Everything outside of the border post part is mindless and pointless. You have to drive across the entire map to first drop off criminals at the labor camp, and then drop off the contraband at the police station. It's good worldbuilding, but the only gameplay during those parts is the ambushes, which are somehow both really annoying and extremely easy. Closer to the end of the game, you even get the ability to get a house call from the cops, so you don't even have to drive anywhere.The gunplay is... well.. 4/10 at best. The AK sounds like a 9mm.Story is nice, but it's not developed to the point that I actually care about characters.After beating the game, you don't unlock any NG+ features or an Endless mode, which would always be nice, as playing through the same thing again except for 6 diffirent choices in story missions gets really repetitive.Overall, this game is great and an easy pickup if you loved Papers Please, but it's got some issues that prevent it from being my favorite game.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game, but note that it is quite buggy. It still feels like an early access. There have been quite a few times that I've gotten into a state where I cannot continue in the game, whether it be a driver refuses to enter the checkpoint, or my character gets stuck on a prop, I haven't had this level of interruptions in any other game I can remember playing. The save checkpoints you have to reload to are sometimes okay, sometimes unforgiving. The mechanics of the game are generally good, it is truly enjoyable. I however dislike having to fill out the inspection report with things that are broken on the car (windows, mirrors, lights, tires, bumpers, body). You have to do it for both vehicles that will go through the checkpoint and ones that will be denied. It adds a lot of time and is quite an annoying mechanic, but you cannot make the full amount of pay per vehicle unless you do it.I really enjoy the game balance between the actual checkpoint work and open world work and missions. When your prison fills up with prisoners, you have to make a run to drop them off at a labor camp. Same goes for when you need to buy more weapons/utilities or drop off contraband at the police station. That is a mechanic I wasn't expecting and it's really enjoyable. The endless type game mode has you start from a dilapidated border checkpoint and really work to build it up in several different ways. I'm doing this after having done the story mode and it is even better than the story mode. Really nice game type.

_childDocuments_.review: Announced back in 2018,  has been one of the most anticipated titles amongst the  catalogue. Considering their large and wide deck of high quality games, that is saying a lot.After a couple of delays, and fans questioned if the game was ever coming out,  absolutely shutters any doubt, releasing it with an absolutely outstanding qualityThe game is good, so good, it's a straight up Double-A title, elevating any expectation you could ever have. If you think this is just another simulation game, you have no idea where you're getting in!  will surprise you, as it surprised me throughout its campaign.Welcome to Acaristan, a fictional Communist country in an equally fictional world surrounded by different cultures and values. You're the fresh appointed rookie to the border post. Your job? Control everyone that comes in, as you have to look out for criminals, contraband and even deal with humanitarian dilemmas.All of this looks great on paper, but perhaps a bit simple. That's why  went all in, delivering an elaborate and engaging game, fusing management and action in an exciting campaign, surrounding players with a plot, choices and events that further extends the overall experience.After the conclusion of the well elaborated tutorial, which does a great job teaching the basic mechanics, a considerable amount of new features will unlock progressively. It's a great way to avoid players being overwhelmed, since there are quite a few of them. Checking ID Cards, Passport Numbers, or possible hidden contraband is just the beginning.As days progress, new factors will unlock, such as the need to check the licence plate, vehicle type and its weight, and many more. The principles go much deeper, as players start to notice changes amongst the regime rules. Political conflicts may end up in harsh decisions, such as denying entry based on country of origin, or even profession. You, as the border officer, can inevitably accept or refuse whoever you see fit, but each time the intended decision is taken, money is earned. Having a negative flow will result in the post bankrupt. However, decisions truly become dilemmas when morality is questioned. Some of the people you either accept or refuse will eventually reach out to you, detailing the impact of your decision. I found this to be a nice little touch.With your daily obligations completed, you are free to roam the town as you wish. Take prisoners to the Labor Camp for an extra profit, trade or buy new items and weapons, search collectables or treasures, and engage in shoot-outs. I found the time after the working hours to be really satisfying, but also very short. is far more than a 3D , in fact, it's a straight-up Police Sim game with no compromises in its arrangement. Random events will trigger which require you to defend an area, support officers of the law or just chase down criminals on the runaway. Other events, however, are story related and progress hand in hand with your rank. These missions are unique and present a special overview regarding the country's regime. Spy on the opposition, tail suspects, or help to solve a murder by collecting evidence and hearing the witness.As you earn money, experience and new ranks, it's almost obligatory to improve your outpost. Upgrade or hire new guards, expand the jail, storage and your own house. Buy new police vehicles and upgrade them to become an unstoppable force. These updates will save you time and help you further manage the confiscated goods.Let me tell you, for such a small town, there are terrorists trying to overtake the regime, criminals who want to put their hands on the confiscated goods, or just a bunch of misfits who want to free the prisoners. The roads are not safe, and while driving around you have a new third person camera, in case driving in first person isn't your cup of tea. The overall driving feels substantially solid and satisfying, with welcoming realistic touches included.You wouldn't be a police officer ready to change the regime without some shooting involved, right? In , the intense shoot-outs feel good, not over the top as you'd expect in a , but instead allowing you to decide the best approach.  Either escape or face the threat. The last option will reward you, especially because you can loot the enemies. Even though they tend to disappear rather quickly after you kill them.With 30 different days,  is quite lengthy, offering quite the replayability. During scripted moments, the game will save at every major spot. Otherwise, it will save in the beginning of the day, and at the end of your duty. I'd still prefer a quick-save function, but I understand the idea of having players dealing with their choices. You can even consider this to be perhaps the first Police Survival game, if you will. Difficulty wise, it's a slow start, where escaping with life may very well be your biggest reward. But as money starts to flow, and with better gear, those criminals have their days numbered. The progression is highly gratifying, and playing it without restarting the day will most likely result in peculiar moments. Not to mention you can in fact lead your border post to bankruptcy, so the whole dynamic value of choices is important.Visually, Contraband Police looks good, has some nice design touches and textures. I particularly enjoyed the lightning, perhaps out of everything else. However, a lot of work went to create a handful of different vehicle sets, plus a distinguishable deck of NPC's. These two aspects are, after all, obligatory considering the game we're dealing with. If you like how the aesthetics look here on the Steam Store, you'll overall enjoy its visuals through and out.I have been playing since February 27th, which by then Contraband Police was already very stable. I believe it was already in its stable version, and although updates having been released, the overall performance was always quite decent.Settings offer some optional changes, but I found the optimization to be quite good for a game developed in Unity. Only lost a few frames when driving in the third person mode. I did, however, had Anti-Aliasing maxed out. Shadows and other details can also be lowered, but with an RX 6700 XT, the game ran flawless at maximum settings. The frame drops were most likely due to my CPU.Aside from all the possible configurations, I found Field of View to be the most limited one, maxes out at just 70. The language package is very diverse and will most likely satisfy players worldwide.  Considering the active development cycle, you can expect new features being implanted in the future, either by further re-arranging the performance, or by adding new gameplay content.Which side will you choose? Free the country, or play by the rules of the regime? It's your call. Different outcomes surprised me, as I was expecting a much more linear setting. Still, with an amazing setting, captivating gameplay and a strong sense of freedom,  is incredible for its price tag, especially with a discount on launch day.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, the only issue I have is during Inspector Mode. While playing Inspector Mode there are criteria for who to deny access, these criteria change every few days. The issue I've come across is sometimes I'd mark them down for Entry Regulations, ex. Someone is under the age of 36 and that means they are denied access, yet the game tells me they shouldn't have been denied. It is very frustrating when the point of the game is to pay attention to all these details, whilst attempting to catch smugglers, then you get punished for doing a good job.
