_childDocuments_.review: Edit 19/10/2023: Endless mode is here and sadly you cannot continue from the career into the endless mode. Nevertheless it adds the gameplay I felt was lacking from the original release and makes this game worth its 20 euro price tag!I had fun with this game, but I have to say that for 20 euro I was expecting more content. I played all the side missions and finished the game in around 10 hours.The world building falls flat when compared to Papers Please and there is way too much time spent on shooting bad guys that just stand in one spot and shoot in your general direction. Of these 10 hours, probably less than 5 were spent doing the core gameplay of checking papers and vehicles.There should be an endless mode where checks are procedurally generated to allow the strongest part of the game to last more than 5 hours. I cannot recommend this game if it costs more than 10 euros and does not have more than 5 hours of fun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: In contraband police you take the role of a Border Patrol officer. The game takes place in a made-up country with some real life inspiration. On the surface you're going to be a Border Patrol agent allowing or denying visitors into your country.It is not as simple as saying yes or no though, you will be searching their vehicles, checking their paperwork and even chasing them down at times. With all this labor you will be making a paycheck every day. The money that you make is yours to choose with how you spend it in the world, I won't go into too much detail but there are a few choices on how you spend your money. Throughout your journey you will also be asked to participate in quest that will shape your country. How you decide to handle these quest will have a butterfly effect.The gameplay feels solid and there is a nice feel of progression throughout the story. Even though the gameplay from the surface level seems repetitive it is not what because of the elements are used to mix it up. Because of the political instability you never know what is gonna happen on any given day.Overall for $20 this is a very unique game that I would definitely recommend if you are on the fence about getting it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is that classic spot the inconsistencies type of game but wrapped up in a fun little story. There is a surprising amount of gun play as well though you are pretty invincible if you use cover and flanking tactics. Finding the stashes of goods people are trying to smuggle is a little cathartic as well. I finished my initial playthrough in around 12 hours playing for the government. I was surprised to find the game does not let you continue where you left off but instead dumps you back at the main menu. I hope they later make a freeplay mode or something so you can explore the map at your leisure with maybe daily rotating rules. I will make it a point on my next play through to upgrade everything and see if I can ignore the story calls.But all in all I enjoyed it and the price point is reasonable too.
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It knew what it wanted to do, didn't overstay its welcome, and it never felt like the inspections were punishing you. A QoL feature that I really appreciated was that your inspection timer paused if you left on a mission. This didn't happen with supply runs (as expected), but when you accept a quest it pauses the time of day. By the end of the game I was so flush with cash that I never did my own transports. It was delivery for Vlad's Tools and my comrades would pick up my prisoners with a phone call. I would give it a solid 7/10, above average and worth the $20 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: it was legitimately fun for a little bit but the map reminds me of far cry 2 in a really bad way. sorry but we learned not to make maps that are only corridors and have nothing remotely interesting to explore in them about 15-20 years ago. thankfully you can fast travel without really any penalty, though i am being thankful to a system that lets me play this game less, so take that how you will. i also ran into several bugs that softlocked the game, requiring me to restart from checkpoint or even the whole day. the save system sucks badly, there's no way to manually save, so if you do run into a bug you often lose a lot of progress.the way this game plays reminds me of a beta product, but this game has supposedly been out for a year and half so there's really no excuse for the major issues in the game still. there's fun to be extracted from this product but it may just cost too much of your time and sanity.ps while this game has some really nice models some of them have only english text for whatever reason, including the stop sign on the traffic arm at the border post, really breaks the immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: Surpassed my expectations, I would liken it to Papers Please but with more bells and whistles.  While the main fun and focus is inspecting vehicles and documents (which is done very well, I would suggest not using the in-game auto-inspection mechanic as this makes game play too simple imo); You are not confined solely to the border post as you transfer contraband/prisoners, have shootouts, go out for tools and weapons etc.  You might also have to chase a smuggler or defend your outpost from attacks, all the while upgrading the outpost with more/better guards and facilities.  There is also a story and in game you are given freedom to accept bribes or allow people to cross even if the paperwork isn't in order for whatever reason.Overall, while some aspects such as the gunplay and upgrades feel a bit tacked on, it breaks up the loop of checking papers/inspecting vehicles rather nicely.  The game is also jank but not in an endearing way (Brigand Oaxaca, Xenus 2 etc) but in a cheap way, however for the sheer effort put into it and for the price ( I got it for 15 on sale) it is well worth it.  It is a simulator that actually tries and it easily could have been so much less in terms of content and certain aspects of detail.  If you like puzzles, simulators or games that try to break the mold a bit, give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite fun, and addictive. Heavily inspired by Papers, please, but not a boring clone. It's a nice take to it where you do more than just be a border control guard.There are a few improvements that could be made for sure (contains spoilers):* Days feel a bit short, even after 8 hours into the game. Sometimes I am done with the drivers and there is plenty of light left * The world feels a bit empty. Just hotspot areas have things in it. There is no much life in it other than the drivers driving around and the ambushes.** Adding some houses, wildlife would make this better* Some more hotkey options would be nice as well, changing the way you approve or deny an entry (instead of having to talk with the person to do the final decision would be cool to have a hotkey for it and changing the flow where you deliver the documents after, while allowing you to still edit the inspection report after making the decision - similar to what Papers Please does), hotkey to pull up the inspection report for car damage* A bit more interaction with the guards with fleeing cars: feels odd that they just do nothing to a fleeing car when you have heavy armed guards at your post and paying big bucks for them* The ambush mechanic should be revamped. It's nice on the first and second encounter, and then just become an annoying thing that can kill your precious cargo (prisoners) when taking them to the quarry (use the downed tree as an ambush instead of randomly popping up dudes shooting at you; add ways to slow you down, maybe lower the firepower but make it more challenging to flee)* Sometimes it's really hard to spot broken windows in the cars: not sure if I am just blind or if bugged.* Some drugs are said to be hidden behind the car seat, but in some car layouts it's super hard to spot thoseOverall, I'm happy with this game and I hope they keep improving on it and make it even more challenging, just like late game papers please gets. We definitely need more games like Papers please and this game is in a good direction!
_childDocuments_.name: Contraband Police

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who's ever played and enjoyed Papers please wanted a game likes this. It's basically that, just in first person and with a shooting/driving component. It's so much fun...and like probably most people...I don't know why LOL. You're literally doing a job and being hated for it. But yeah, it's a great concept and it took me about 23h to finish the main campaign. The games only has one major problem. The performance is absolute garbage. The game looks like it was made 10 years ago (except maybe the lighting), but you will not be able to keep it over 60 without a 30 series card. It's not a fast paced game that requires super high fps, but it's still no excuse, so just be aware of that. Overall it was great fun and I hope to see a performance patch and maybe more game-modes...possibly a CP 2 one day as well. Great job devs.

name: Sable
detailed_description: Embark on a unique and unforgettable journey and guide Sable through her Gliding; a rite of passage that will take her across vast deserts and mesmerizing landscapes, capped by the remains of spaceships and ancient wonders. Explore the dunes on your hoverbike, scale monumental ruins and encounter other nomads as you unearth mysteries long forgotten and discover who she really is behind her mask. With its unique art style and original soundtrack by Japanese Breakfast, envelop yourself in Sable’s world and explore everything at your own pace. There is a lot in this world just waiting to be discovered. Do not be afraid. Take the leap. • Explore a rich world, full of remnants of past civilisations. • Climb, leap, hover, glide – use everything at your disposal to discover every inch of the world in front of you • Customise your hover bike as you find, or earn, new parts • Help other clans and nomads that you meet along the way • Lose yourself in an adventure and find yourself through masks, outfits and other collectables, to represent who you are to those around you… • Complete puzzles to earn rewards and forge your path in an unforgiving terrain • Try your hand at fishing in the desert, and showcase your collection of bugs and fish in the Vivarium.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a really special game. It is easy to just get lost gliding around the beautiful landscapes, finding cool things to do over every horizon.The art style is amazing, the gameplay feels fun and fluid, and it's refreshing to have an open-world adventure that evokes Zelda Breath of the Wild vibes while having no combat at all.I'm really enjoying it and looking forward to continuing playing

_childDocuments_.review: Artful indies generally fall into two categories: sad ones about grief, and joyful ones about growing up. This is one of the latter. Sable is a nice chill game. Roam around the desert, do little quests, solve small puzzles, sit and watch the sunset. Sable is pretty short. In my time with the game (15 hours) I completed all of the quests, found all of the masks, and found enough chums to be able to get max stamina. Speaking of stamina: do not pass by chums at any time. You will be doing a lot of climbing and running, so getting more stamina is paramount. I played most of the game with 2-4 upgrades, but getting the final 2 towards the end just released a bit of pressure.The writing often contains little self-aware passages that lighten the mood. Not that it gets dark at any stage, but it is a game about growing up and part of that is realising that you can still enjoy things. My only issues with the writing is that is never addresses the core mystery of the world (), and even throws completely untouched story threads out there ().. I had audio glitches and frame drops basically all the time, and my PC is good. Other Steam reviews say the same thing, so be warned: it will happen to you too. It definitely does bring you out of the game and detracts from the experience, so I hope the devs get to the bottom of it. In the meantime, you kinda just have to bear with it. I was able to, but I know that it's not easy for everyone.My final bike configuration:

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. I don't think most people would, but, I do.+ Engaging, detailed, expansive world, full of varied and inspiring landscapes and environments+ Relatable and endearing character dialogue+ Well executed cell-shaded art style+ Climb-anywhere truly open world, only limited by your stats and traversal abilities, with few to no invisible walls or truly inaccessible areas+ Wide variety of cosmetic upgrades* Effectively a walking simulator: this game has no combat, no risk of player injury, and no real fail state* Somewhat anticlimactic, open-ended ending* Limited reward for player accomplishments- Limited amount of mechanical customizeability: the only mechanical upgrades you can attain are climbing stamina and sandbike upgrades, the latter of which leave much to be desired in terms of attainable raw speed- Not the most stable gameplay experience, with an above-average quantity of bugs that tend to permeate the experienceSable is a very unique game. It occupies the space somewhere between a traditional walking simulator, like What Remains of Edith Finch, and a true open-world exploration based game, like Breath of the Wild. The experience leans heavily into the player's sense of discovery and exploration, as finding and exploring new areas, engaging in dialogue, and solving light environmental puzzles is the breadth of experiences that the game has to offer. Overall, it's a very chill and relaxing experience, from start to finish. For some, like me, that's just alright. But other players might just be pushing through, wondering when they'll get to the "good part" with real challenge or stakes. For those players, I'm sorry to say, you'll probably just be disappointed by what lies ahead.Sable is a game for people who like Breath of the Wild for the exploration, and think the combat is unnecessary or doesn't need to be there to maintain it's core appeal. Just don't get too far into it expecting it to be something it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a great game for explorers at heart. I continuously have moments of surprise and wonder as I take to the open sands, increasingly impressed by the volume of experiences this indie title has to offer. This is a world that you immediately want to know more about, full of characters that you want to know even moreso. While it can sometimes be a bit wordy, the characters and interactions are all genuine, and often emphatically kind with themes of helping others, self-discovery, righting wrongs, etc. If you like reading, this will be a bonus. But if you don't you may have to look past this. Overall, I love this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So if you like quiet strolls in quite vast desert landscapes with nice mountain views - this is for you. If you also require a lot of things to do - not as much. The game elements are, like the desert, quite sparse. You travel between areas, jump and climb and collect items do deliver to various locations. Like quite a few other games, so there's nothing new there. It kinda works but isn't that exciting or challenging. But as mentioned, if you like having just something beautiful to look at and immerse yourself in - it's fine. And fits with the overall style of the experience. Obviously for fans of Moebius/Jean Giraud.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Saw "Sable" on release day, just couldn't pass by.From the get-go: aquired some questionable funds, seem to have eradicated the local insect colony, stole from a child (accidentally?). A day well spent.But actually though, techical stuff aside (on that in a minute), "Sable" feels really good to play. It makes me feel welcome to both relax and not really think about anything, and also reminisce on my own travels. Every encounter and place visited feels somewhat rewarding. The visuals are great.Now, the technical stuff we set aside.Ability to see through walls: 10/10. A blessing or a curse depending on how you look at it.Ability to get into surfaces: Fazed through a rock I was trying to climb. Fell out the opposite side. Saw god. She told me I was doing well. I cried.The camera is kind of wobbly, but maybe it's just me being unable to sort out my mouse sensitivity. Perhaps we'll never know.At one point, my mouse disappeared while in the item menu. Disorienting, soul-crushing. Sort of like waiting for your mother at checkout, but with lower stakes.The sky sometimes changing colours instantaneously catches me off-guard every time i see it. Just like the bike when it bumps into actual nothing. What's going on.I'm playing on a bit of a worn-out setup, so I'd suggest looking at other reviews for more technical comments, as I might have brushed off a lot of things as "just another day in the office".All in all, will definitely spend many more hours in the world of "Sable". Some updates with fixes wouldn't hurt, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I was watching someone on YouTube play this game and thought I would try it out myself on my computer. The art style and open world appealed to me at first. After spending a few minutes in an attempt to be able to play the game in some state of entertainment( adjusting the graphics to the lowest they can possibly get), I realised I won't be able to experience this game at all or to the fullest. Pretty disappointed but there isn't much I can do.  I only recommend this game to those who have the newest and high end pc towers because it runs poorly on mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This must be the most relaxing game I have ever played. No stress, frustration or combat of egos to be found. Just the tale of a young girls rite of passage as a globe trotting explorer. The graphics appear to be an hommage to the late, great illustrator Jean Giraud, or Moebius when drawing as his Science Fiction/Fantasy alter ego. Extremely enjoyable and a world to lose yourself in.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: An initial warning:  Sable lacks a main plotline (sort of).  It's all side-quests, but wandering the world and doing those quests *is* the main plot.  Travel and discovery are the whole point of the game.  If that's a major turnoff, Sable might not be for you.Anyway, this is what you get when someone other than a "AAA" studio makes an open-world game.  It's cozy and relaxing.  The writing is great.  The art is fresh and gorgeous (play around with the line weight setting...it totally changes the look of the game!).  There's warm humor and a beautifully melancholic ending.The bad(ish):  There's a little movement jank (with the game almost always being forgiving enough to offset this), and the game can stutter a little when moving at high speed through/into a new area.  None of the puzzles are exactly mindbending, but they're satisfying enough.Excited to see more from these devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable had so much potential. Could have been this decade's Ico or Journey. But it desperately, desperately needed another coat of polish. So many potentially great or emotional moments were undermined by performance issues, graphical issues, control issues, UI issues, physics issues... They really needed another few months to fix these minor but highly distracting problems. I'd rather they cut the amount content by half or a third, if it meant they could really perfect the remainder. As it stands, it's merely a decent meditative exploration game, instead of the work of art it could have been.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: with only 5 hours put in so far i can say very easily that sable is an outright classic right out the gate, i havent experienced such a personal and heartwarming story in years from video games. to nit pick a little though i can say that there are extremely light performance issues but over time i doubt that will still be the case. buy this game. play this game. you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: It's no masterpiece - it's aesthetics are certainly it's strong point, and it has it's fair share of flaws (bugs, unclear quest directions at times, poor questlog) - but it is a solid and enjoyable experience. Outer Wilds does the whole "future society living in the technological shadow of a far more advanced past society" thing better, Mutiazone does the whole "fantastical coming of Age story about helping others and finding a place in society" thing better, and Shadow of the Collosus perhaps did the whole "mysterious ancient open world" thing better way back in the day, but if you're looking for a solid combination of that and don't mind that it essentially boils down to a mix of fetch quests, fairly easy puzzles (usually, some of the time-based ones were a bit annoying) and compelling but usually short platforming sections, I recommend it. You'll pretty much get back what you put in exploration-wise, and there are certain parts of the game that are very beautiful. It certainly stands out in the open world genre due to it's laid back nature, feeling almost more like something akin to Journey at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: this game is everything I wanted in breath of the wild: a vast world that's still concentrated enough that it doesn't feel entirely empty, cool worldbuilding, and an actual story. plus, there's a button dedicated to sitting down so you can take screenshots. the game, for me, was extremely buggy, however. lots of pop-in, held items disappearing, and my bike vanishing entirely. the positives of the game compensate considerably for the deficits in gameplay though. this is a very sweet story that's fun to play in a unique world i want to know more about.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S ABANDONWARE AT THIS POINT.BUGS GALORE.SHADY AND INEPT DEVELOPERS / COMMUNITY MANAGER.STAY FAR AWAY.The "Breath Of The Wild at home"...I hate to give this game a negative review, because there's really an awesome gem of a game beneath all this pile of trash.Shedworks should be ASHAMED of releasing a game in this ludicrously unfinished state. It's clearly maliciousness to release this dumpster fire without at least an "Early Access" tag on it. Stay away until the developers have at least some semblance of ethics and morals.The game starts in a closed hub environment and it's just around the 2 hour mark that you're free to experience the "real game" along with all the glitches, bugs, technical problems and performance issues. Perfectly timed to bait you into buying an unfinished and completely unpolished product.There was literally ZERO QA done for this product. Every time I open the game there's a new bug to be found.- Performance is utter and complete trash.- Had to MANUALLY enable AA in Nvidia Control Panel or else the game is visually disgusting.- Fast traveling makes every trader item dissappear.- The camera is horrible and clips though everything.- Menus and UI stop working randomly.- textures and shadow flickering constantly, sometimes the whole screen.- Not even the audio works properly, constantly stopping, stuttering and crackling. _childDocuments_.review: Perfect chill exploration game with stunning visuals. Great fit for curious players that spot something in the distance and want to find out what it is and want to know more about its lore.Also has a good amount of cosmetics and bike upgrades for those wanting to be rewarded for exploring.A very healthy dose of "I can't put this game down".
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a thumbs up because I actually really love the atmosphere and being able to cruise around on my hoverbike like Nausicaä - but I have to admit that there are lots of technical issues and a few bugs that make the gameplay annyoing sometimes. Others have already complained about the framerate, I find it very annyoing as well. While the game runs mostly well at 60 fps, the video-like sequences when someone's talking to you are not fluid and look horribly chunky and out of synch. I did not have these problems with the demo version.I can call my bike to me, but I often don't dare after it got stuck with its nose in the sand and I needed several minutes of maneuvering head down to finally right it again...so not an option I suggest if you have an uneven plane between you and your bike and it's far away...which makes this feature kind of unusable. To summarize: It's a beautiful game build with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ engine, I guess? (i know nothing about game-development.) The unique graphics and beautiful setting and theme still make this game my current go-to to unwind and simply climb ALL the things.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing experience. Very relaxed game with no fighting or deaths - you go out exploring the world and it's very unusual inhabitants. There's some interesting background history about the planet that you find out as you go along and interact with some crashed spaceships.It's almost like a meditative experience and parts of the game just stay with you, despite there being quite a few bugs (both literal and the software type).
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: For the asking price I would say sure. I have a love for these kinds of games so it makes it difficult to be critical. Like other reviews, the ultimate problem I had with it were the bugs but this is the only time I will mention it. So many good parts are cut off by the bugs that it makes it hard to justify what is offered. But I will ignore this and instead talk about other things I think it could have done.Gameplay is the story - The goal is to explore and discover yourself (protagonist)There would be a lot to enjoy with this game if there was more depth. Everything seems just enough of a mystery to be called one, but ultimately there is rarely a pay off for things you do. None of the lore and characters are bad per se, but when the goal is to find yourself, it can be kind of a let down when most of the things to do are treated like chores. The story is lovely on it's surface and sometimes it can be deep if you think about it, but a lot of people might not already have the tools to extract that meaning. It shouldn't hold your hand and tell you what to feel, but there is never a resolution to things. It's always just what it is at face value regardless of how much some of the journey filled me with wonder that I kinda had to make up myself.The art is great when it works and the soundtrack is always good.The art style would be lovely, if it was also consistent with itself. It goes from having a comic book style to trying to be a full 60FPS beautiful painting type deal. In the show Kino's Journey they actually use various art styles when telling different types of stories and that can work. But here it just feels like a stark contrast with itself. The songs also really set the mood but they don't make me feel like I can feel what the characters or the world is about. The songs are desolate and hit certain beats but they also don't convey a sense of meaning other than whimsy, desolation, and isolation. It doesn't have to be dynamic visual to audio to be good, but I don't feel much after awhile. To end on a good note and why I still think it is worth getting.Games like this feel more rare now than ever. Every game feels like it must have a set amount of goals and things to do. But this game does try to be itself rather than something else. It borrows mechanics and templates, but it does try to be it's own world you can relax to. It needs polish and I hope if the devs continue to update it that Sable will be that game someday. Or even better that more games will try to be themselves instead of making a bunch of checklists. Interesting that a game about having a bunch of chores to do doesn't feel that generic to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I've recommended this game in my review however that is with a big asterisk, if I could give a neutral vote I would, which sucks because I did enjoy the game a lot. I completed it in just under 20 hours, I have all the achievements, did all the side quests, etc. and I wouldn't have one that if I wasn't enjoying myself at least most of the time, but there are a few things that I did have a tough time overlooking; - The first and most immediately noticeable problem is that sound effects and sounds in general can stutter quite a bit or just flat out not play, this one didn't really affect me and after a while I didn't notice it at all, but it was the first big problem I encountered.  - There are a few mechanics in the game which could have done with a lot more polish, the worst of which being the hoverbike, which will flip and roll everywhere if it even thinks there might be a bump on the ground. Even when you're riding smoothly it feels clunky and heavy, even with the faster later game versions. - Interactions with NPCs (especially shopkeepers) can be a big buggy, and I've noticed a few spelling mistakes throughout the dialogue as well. Shopkeepers will sometimes soft lock requiring a restart, and on at least one occasion I accidentally found a bug which allowed me to sell items at another items price. - Lastly, this game absolutely chugs performance wise, I've got a 2080 and r5 3600 and I still run around 50-60 fps with dips in the 20s in some of the more busy areas. Even with all of those points this game really does seems like a labour of love, and for all of it's faults I did enjoy it enough to push through and 100% it. The story is a refreshing break from the usual "chosen one" archetype, the world building fits seamlessly with the setting and I found that I quite enjoyed collecting all the little snippets of info explaining everything, the environmental puzzles (while simple) were still enjoyable and a nice break from the quests and exploration and lastly the game is just calming, I enjoyed sitting and looking over the world.It's for those reasons that I'll still be giving this game a positive review, despite it's issues, because as I said earlier; I did still enjoy playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about 8 hours into the game, but I'm loving it so far. The artstyle is simple but fits the theme perfectly, the story and lore has me intrigued, and the gameplay is very fun. The controls aren't hard to pick up, and there isn't a steep learning curve to play. I do have a few issues though, the camera sometimes bugs out and I can't see where I'm going. The climbing controls are a bit janky sometimes, especially on sloped surfaces, and while I'm not playing on the most powerful computer, the framerate is somewhat inconsistent. The biggest gripe I have is the menu & map. Trying to navigate it using the mouse is shocking. Buttons inputs are off centre, or sometimes non-existent. Trying to click through to different sections from the map can place a marker off the screen, which requires some time to find them and delete them. That being said, these issues didn't detract very much from the game itself, and I would still highly recommend playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game has such a great concept and I wanted it to feel a little like Journey did back on PS3 but it kinda fell short for a few reasons. One is definitely the music which was only really noticeable once in the first 2-3 hours and other than that was pretty insignificant. I also noticed a lot of stuttering audio issues when in a city in the game, especially affecting the music while having conversations. It became really annoying after a while. Another reason it fell short is the art to be honest. The art style IS unique and you could call it quite pretty but some character animations are very... choppy? I think it's meant to be stylistic that the characters animations are drawn or something but it gives this weird feeling that your movement is losing frames almost. The camera could be janky at times. For some reason they put sprint on circle so you have to claw hold your controller just to run about while looking around. There are all these little things that constantly irritated me and prevented me from actually enjoying the game. I like the idea a lot but it didn't feel worth the other stuff. I might come back to it and try again but for now I'm negative about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A calm and beautiful indie-game. There is a lot of Moebius in this game - I like Moebius, so that's nice for me. And I also enjoy, that I don't have to kill anything all the time (not that I don't like games I have to kill everything - I played Doom and God of War and Borderlands and I liked them all   ;)  It's just very relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Money very well spent. A wonderfully good surprise. The game's aestetic can be unsettling, but soon enough I came to love it. The gameplay is close to breath of the wild, but without combat. Exploration, climbing, collecting and sidequests. I'll go as far as to say I liked the universe better than BoTW, in terms of world building and architecture. If like me, you grew up fascinated by movies like The Castle in the Sky, you will like this game.The few complains I have will be about some visual bugs I've experienced, Sable's very stiff animations and a main quest-line that could have been flesh out a little. But it's an indie game and I already got way more that what I was expecting.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable just came out from the workshop and is full of dust and bugs, but oh what a marvel under all that grime.Let’s be honest here. The game is far from finished but when they work out the kinks it will be one of my personal favourites. If you like slower atmospheric games like Shadow of the colossus this is for you.What I like the most is how you interact with the environment. You are living in a desert, but the environment and the people are benevolent, which is a rare thing in a game. Even if you can’t really hurt yourself, you are still spurred to explore for the sheer joy of it. It’s all part of your coming-of -age ritual age. You are SUPPOSED to fall from great hight or get lost in the dungeons. I’m also a big fan of the artist Moebius whose art and comics are the inspiration for the game. This game makes me feel stuff. Also, it’s ridden with bugs and corrupted my savefile 8h in. After many attempts to restore it I gave up and restarted the game and it was still fun. That’s how good I think it is. (This is a tip. Find where your system is saving the game and make a copy of it occasionally.)If I’m forgiving wandering glider, lost cartographer dialogue in Badlands, weird artifacts from fruits I can’t pick or where able to in some earlier stage of production, stacked towers of insects, music themes that doesn’t stop and layers upon other music so I must restart (this is one of the reasons I think the game tends to break), stuttering graphics, freezes AND save corruption it must be good, right?If the production team get their sh*t together this is hands down my Game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy this game, but it's simply marred with too many technical problems. The list of problems is lengthy:- Inconsistent frame rate-massive stuttering while assets are streaming in-loads of pop in for distant objects-audio glitches-climbing mechanics are spotty at best.. a problem when so much of the gameplay revolves around exploration-piloting the jet bike feels mushy with very poor handling-the game (at least on PC) doesn't seem to remember menu settings correctly. For example, setting a specific costume doesn't save when loading the game up the next time.The art style is interesting and it's a nice game for casual players in theory... but I can't recommend it due to all of the tech problems. :(
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely little game.It's not an amazingly perfect game. It's got its flaws. If the hoverbike riding had a bit more finesse to it, a few more inputs to let you control how your hoverbike slews across the frozen waves of sand, some way to drop a fin into the sand and carve up bright, shimmering arcs of sand as you did donuts across the desert, it would be astounding. Instead you just point your hoverbike in a direction and hold 'go', and try to keep it from wallowing too badly. Which is a bit of a shame since there is so much desert to drive through. Once you get a few bike part upgrades it's pretty much okay, but it's never *great*.The rest of the game is pretty damn good though. It's a small open world with a main quest that's really just "wander around and do whatever side quests make you happy". And it's a very pretty world that really nails its clear intent of being an interactive Moebius drawing. It was a really nice little vacation to a world of no responsibilities and no real danger, just roaming across the imaginary desert and thinking about what I'd like to be doing with my imaginary life. As of now, I've done all but about the last few quests in this game and it was constantly delightful.It gets a little stuttery on my Steam Deck at times. Just all these little gaps in the motor noise. Starts to turn into a slideshow sometimes when I'm biking around some of the more cluttered areas, especially if the Deck's not plugged in. But it's a super pretty slideshow. Maybe if the biking was more complicated then this would make it more frustrating, I dunno. Ultimately it's a really good little novella of a game about a girl going off for a very safe wander around the world to figure out who she wants to be. It's not great but it's pretty damn good, and I sure like I got twenty or thirty bucks worth of fun out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the art style of the game, it's really unique and beautiful, sometimes I can just leave the game AFK and enjoy the environment around me.The story is good, the music and gameplay are great too.For anyone that like beautiful environment, exploring, going around doing NPC's quests while enjoying the relaxing lofi-like music, Sable may be the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is a thumbs up but with pretty big caveats.The game has a lot going for it, first and foremost the very unique moebius inspired artstyle and world. And I'll say this now if this doesn't attract you odds are the game is not for you.The gameplay has a lot of influence from breath of the wild but it's almost purely exploration and traversal with some puzzle thrown in and no combat at all (or failure state for that matter, you can't even take damage by falling), that makes it a very chill and contemplative experience.It's also somewhat small scale for an open world and yes that's still in the positives, there isn't a whole lot of filler content (with an asterisk for later) and while there is a good amount of repetition in the type of activity you'll be doing it's short enough with enough variation that I didn't get bored (but it was good there wasn't more it was starting to get stale by the point I finished everything I wanted to do so a bit more would have been too much).So TL;DR : a short and sweet open world adventure with a really cool artstyle and interesting world.Now onto the negatives and oh boy, the game is not well polished. It doesn't ruin the experience but it's something you can't brush off. I've basically had one major glitch per play session. None are gamebreaking but some need to restart the game to fix. I'm not going to list all the glitches I've found cause it would take too long but it's clear the game doesn't have the QA of higher budget games.Now it's something I'm usually willing to ignore especially with indie games but in this case what I find problematic is some of the glitches or poorly implemented features that negatively affect the core experience. It's clear that some sections of the game just haven't really been playtested as you can see some immediate issue with the route that you are expected to take.There are things like unreliable climbing surface in a game based on stamina management, janky camera, no ability to skip time despite some events being time based, and a big one, really bad LoD that makes spotting some things at a distance impossible when that's explicitly something you are supposed to do (what's the point of climbing to a high point trying to spot point of interest or collectibles when those don't load properly?) and generally a lot of minor annoyances that don't ruin the experience but they are noticeable and they add up. And they make other things that are clearly choices (like not having region names on the map to force you to pay attention to what characters are saying) feel harder to accept.So it's not so much the lack of polish but the fact it really takes away from the experience and erodes the good will of the player to want to engage with this world. If you don't have the patience to deal with that the game is again not for you.And one last thing : don't try to get all the chum eggs. They're collectibles and getting those you find on the way is important as they are how you get extra stamina (and at least getting one or two stamina upgrade makes some specific section a lot easier although you don't really need more than that), but please don't try to get all of them, there are a lot.  Like, way too much considering the scope of the game, and you don't really have a way to track them down unless you're pulling out a map online (at least those you already have appear on your map so there is that). It's not unusually tedious for open world games, but in this game in particular there is just not enough content to justify having so many of them, you're basically going to double your playtime if you decide to look for all of them and with something really tedious. It's ok to go to the end of the game once you run out of things you want to do and it'll make your experience better. I guess it's not really a negative for the game cause it's optional but if you're as obsessive as me and it's hard for you to let go of optional stuff just know it's really not worth your time to do that one and if you can't let it go it might be better to skip the game entirely.There you go, I still think the game is enjoyable overall, and it's got some soul to it, but know what you're getting into.Have a nice day~
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Chill yet very interesting game. Like Zelda: Breath of the Wild but you're exploring the world riding on a Star Wars hoverbike. The world is interesting, and discovery the culture your character is a part of is very fun. Like I'm inside a Moebius comic. The world is alien yet familiar. Recommend for anyone who has time for a chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like a lot of nothing? Because that's what exploring feels like in this game.Also when you find a chest it's 95% going to be 20 credits.Urn chest - 20 credits.Normal chest - 20 credits.Metal egg chest - 20 credits.Fancy looking chest, believe it or not - 20 ♥♥♥♥♥ credits.The amount of times exploring or small puzzle is rewarded with 20 credits is just stupid, but even still money is too hard to make. There's a lot to buy and it costs quite a lot.And to make matters worse there's a beggar who asks for infinite amount of money but gives nothing in return. Talk about wasting your few hard earned credits, geez. Had to use memory editing to give me my money back.Swimming is too slow.Climbing ladders is too slow.Skipping chum egg animation is not possible.Environment has quite a lot of places where you can fall into places you're not supposed to. Even fall through the whole world and keep falling forever.Riding your bike and collision is buggy. You can use your bike to clip through walls.Audio is weird sometimes. Inconsistencies in the volume.It's a shame. I like the game overall. The vibe is nice and the world is cool and love riding the bike and climbing&exploring but there are a lot of minor problems and bugs that together diminish the experience greatly.That's why I give a thumbs down. _childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill exploration game. To me, this is like Horizon Zero Dawn without a battle system. I loved that game for the story and I like this one for similar reason but with the benefit of not having to grind levels, or battle, or farming stuff to make enough money to buy the items you want. Puzzles, if they can be called that, are fun and require just enough thinking to make it engaging without being frustrating. The story confused me a little at the beginning but as the game goes on things started to make more sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A good open world game that got better after the patches fixed framerate drops that would sometimes cut in the sound/music, plus allowed tweaking the visuals to make it more comfortable to play for longer periods of time.A very chill coming of age story and a peaceful experience overall. Perfect to zone out and relax after a stressful day.5 stars, would dissociate again
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: So it's a bit buggy at launch, but this game is AMAZING!  I didn't even think it looked that good in trailers, and the idea of a Zelda-like game without combat seemed a bit too watered down.  But boy was I wrong!  You can pick this game up and enjoy the simple comic/manga beauty for 20 minutes or hours.  Which is great for adults with busy lives.  The low pressure exploration and non-linear narrative are rewarding without being frustrating.  It's got so much heart and class, it outshines any technical hiccups.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but with major caveats. The game has heart, and I love what they were trying to go for with it. Unfortunately, my time with it was mired by technical issues. The game was constantly undermining itself, right up to the very last second where the credits ended before the credits song did and cut it off. If you can look past technical shortcomings and just immerse yourself in the vision that is on display, then you will enjoy this game. I just wish it was like 20% better.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I like Sable and I recommend it, BUT: (and I understand the it's a tiny dev team)-there are still optimisation issues, 2 years after release. Weird stuttering and audio glitches in certain parts of the map, I don't have a potato pc-the "glider" is just not fun to ride, it doesn't feel smooth. Also not fast enough, even with upgraded pieces. Will sometimes get caught on invisible pieces of geometry-the menu's, map, inventory etc doesn't work well with mouse input, feels very janky, really un-enjoyableOk, on to the things I liked:+amazing art style, feels like you are in Jean Giraud's (aka Moebius) art+100% peaceful, just exploring and climbing and sitting down and meditating+dialogue is top notch, well written. No voice acting, but I think that would've ruined it.+music fits perfectly, doesn't intrude*You don't really need it to complete the game, but there is a way to increase your climbing stamina. Just have to find the right place, so get exploring ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is fun. A nice little open world exploration game with some very nice views (and I like the soundtrack and the cel-shaded visuals). The quests are enjoyable and range from collection tasks to logic puzzles to jumping and climbing puzzles (I found the latter a bit frustrating though, but you can skip those ones). I thought it felt a little *too* empty in places and that there could have been more POIs, but there's fast travel options. A little more about the background of the setting would have been fun too (who were the Hicarics? How did the forest get Petrified? etc). But still, it's a fun exploration game, would definitely recommend if you like that sort of thing!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful game, one could spend hours just taking in the scenery. You play as the character Sable who is on her 'gliding', a rite of passage where she can learn about her world and what she may want to do as an adult. The quests in the game are aligned around the theme of discovery, some are challenging, some are easy. Many involve climbing to great heights and gliding from one point to another. Although there is no possibility of 'dying' within this game, some of the challenges involving climbing had my heart racing and my palms sweating. Overall a beautifully conceived game with great attention to detail. It reminds me of Riven, another exploration game that I loved.

_childDocuments_.review: It was the art style alone that caught my eye for this game. If you're looking for a chill game with no combat, mostly fetch quests, and the most vibe filled ambiance/music, then this is the game for you!There are some "dungeons" in this game, but overall they aren't difficult and they aren't even necessary for the main "plot" of this game. The story line follows a young girl who is sent out on her pilgrimage to find out what she wants to be when she grows up. It's a rather endearing story that I believe everyone can relate to. This is a slow game with a fairly large map area to explore. I found myself often stopping and just letting the game "do its thing" for a minute or two because the ambiance, the music, and the ever changing lighting of this game is so peaceful and relaxing. Overall - 8/10. I truly enjoyed the unique art style. I enjoyed the ambiance and overall vibe. I really enjoyed the story line. But sometimes the control got a little janky and it was difficult to do the "dungeons" when controls weren't so refined. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game; it's right up my wheelhouse. Unfortunately, while it starts with some interesting ideas, all those ideas ultimately fall flat. - The game is beautiful... But character animation is jarring and capped at 30 fps. - You can climb, glide, ride, and explore just like the Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild... But all those abilities feel stunted and climbing is particularly frustrating. - You can go on quests... But they're almost all fetch quests  with unsatisfying endings- You can unlock special ancient clothing.... But the clothing confers no benefit. It's just cosmetic.- The music is beautiful... But is too quiet, starts and stops abruptly, and is frequently punctuated by a loud jarring "jingle" every time you find a specific collectible item in the world. ... and so on. _childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. However I only recommend it for people with a lot of patience and great appreciation for art. Don't expect much challenge or depth.The Good:Like everyone has said, the art style is unlike anything I've seen in a game before and that alone kept me motivated enough to spend 24 hours playing. The music was a nice touch that made me feel relaxed and eager to hear more. The story was well written and charming. The writers clearly had a fun time with their adjectives and gave a lot of personality to faceless characters. Expect to do a lot of reading if you really want to understand the game's world and message. The climbing mechanics were very satisfying. I found myself going out of my way to climb weird things just to see if I could. The climbing and floating are forgiving, and I never experienced any particularly glitchy moments like others reported.The Bad:I never experienced anything 'game breaking', so I consider these criticisms minor, and didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game. You can effortlessly clip the camera through walls and the player, especially when in tight interior spaces. Doing strategic jumps in doors was rough because the player model kept obscuring my view. The inventory seemed needlessly complicated with how many button presses were needed to switch sections and scroll to read things. Keyboard menu navigation had some odd choices such as pressing 'backspace' to navigate back. The user map markers were way too easy to accidentally place. I found myself spending more time deleting accidental ones than using them. The dialog choice menu would sometimes freak out if you needed to scroll while using a gamepad, so I had to use my mouse instead. The map also had several fast travel markers incorrectly placed. All of these complaints are easily something that could be patched later, so I hope the devs stick with it!One last thing...devs...please write the names of the regions on the map! I had the hardest time remembering what any of them were even after 24 hours of play time!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one. We really need a mixed review option, because Sable deserves it (for now).Sable is just a wonderful unpolished gem. It has everything for a relaxing experience. Wonderful ambient music, interesting and funny quests, amazing locations and views (especially the ones you get in search of chum eggs), nice npc's. It really has that adventure game feeling where you just explore and do quests. No one is harmed, everybody is happy.Unfortunately, that relaxing experience is interrupted by the massive amount of bugs. Major frame drops, visual glitches, map and inventory bugs, hoverbike bugs (you can call for it all you want, it ain't gonna come), all sorts of stutters, gliding and climbing bugs, walls that aren't even there, random pop-ins and don't get me started on the camera controls. Getting past Thieving Magpie Well was a real challenge. Basically, you can encounter all the possible bugs in this game. Now, take all these problems and your gaming experience won't be that pleasant. I actually struggled to finish Sable mostly because I got immersed in the story, but oh boy, I wanted to quit it numerous times.I'm sure that if the devs try to fix all the issues, this game will be highly appreciated (not that now isn't). It just need a little polishing here and there and it'll be great.I really adore Sable, with all it's flaws. It's been a while since I played such a calming game, BUT at times it was really frustrating and annoying. The cuteness got me going. I really hope that the performance problems will be resolved so I can replay it and REALLY appreciate it at it's full value.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable, by developer Shedworks and publisher Raw Fury, is an amazing open world style game that heavily focuses on exploration and story. You play as Sable, who is a young child that is in a very remote part of the desert with their clan. As Sable, you must undergo a rite of passage by exploring the world to discover who you are. The world is full of sights to see and people to meet, all of which are wearing a mask of some sort. But there is still much to do before you are able to embark on that journey.When you first start the game, you are in a ruined temple of some sort with a giant face on the wall. Sable then says they should go back to the Ibex camp to get ready for the ceremony. You then make your way to camp and talk to Jadi who is a really nice almost grandmotherly person who talks to you about your coming of age journey that you are about to embark on. From there you have to complete a few missions including building your hoverbike that you will use to travel the vast desert and obtaining your gliding mask from the temple.This game, from the beginning, draws you into the story and the world you play in. It has a way of establishing meaningful connections to characters that you only see briefly with its dialogue and narrative. The art style, while simplistic, is very well done and beautiful. There are a lot of little details in the particles and lighting, from dust in caves to the blowing desert wind. Sable focuses on the idea of finding your own path in the world around you by seeing it all and discovering it for yourself, while telling a significant and meaningful story along the way. The world seems desolate at first but as you explore there are many things to find, from items to collect to ruined buildings and crashed ships. As well as many camps and other people to talk to along the way. Even though there is little guidance on what to do and where to go, that is a part of the experience of the game, putting you in the shoes of this child becoming an adult in a massive world trying to find your place.I honestly have very little issues with this game. It's very well made and you can tell a lot of care and effort went into the making of this game. That being said, there are some problems with the collision and the camera movements. The controls themselves are fine and the game has full controller support as well as the standard keyboard controls. The issue with the camera movement is that it's really touchy and hard to control at times; sometimes the camera will just pull up for no reason and stare at the sky or you won't be able to turn in it time to see where you are going and you’ll fall off. Another issue is with some of the collisions while climbing, you can climb up pretty much anything but some of the surfaces are a little broken. You can fall through some edges at times to climb on top of a ledge that isn't  actually there and fall back down again, that only seems to be an issue when climbing irregular shaped objects though. Sable is a well made indie game centered around exploring the vast world around you. The story is well written with the characters and narrative drawing you into the world thus making the experience more meaningful. There are a few issues with climbing and camera movement that may need some polishing. I am giving this game a 9 out of 10 rating because it has some polishing to do but is still a really good game as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: *Yes, after many fixes.I'll start with the issues, in no particular order. -The camera is problematic as it clips and awkwardly shifts on the environment. For example: It has often lodged itself in the ground when I am climbing.-The glider is unpredictable as to whether or not it will respond to your calls. It also controls pretty poorly and will flip, stop, and impact invisible obstacles often.-The mask you choose won't stay on when you save and exit the game. Every time I reload the game the mask changes back to the default.-The visuals can be at times, nauseating. This can be compounded by stuttering, jittering, graphical pop-in, and weird camera movements.-The FPS will always kick off at 30, even if it is set at 60, and it will drop often and rather randomly. Even if you're playing on a system that manages 120fps easily on games like Death Stranding.-The game seems awfully confused by the concept that keyboards and mouses typically work in conjunction. It struggles to accept the placement, movement, and clicks of the mouse at random.I do hope these issues are resolved.Now to some positives:If you like games like Journey, or Death Stranding than this might fit your interests. A great deal of exploration in a desolate landscape with some wonderful ambient type music to accompany you. Interesting story with intriguing, though simple, puzzle solving. Depending on your views, you might consider the game to be rather pretty at times. There are some basic RPG elements like resource collection, quests, and item trading as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into Sable expecting some crazy parkour abilities. Although I was very wrong, I enjoy how Sable turned out nontheless. Dont expect any combat, this game is pretty much a walking sim with puzzles, although sometimes these puzzles can be bugged. For the most part the game is fun, however performance tends to lack and I have no idea why, the graphics are not intensive. Speaking of, the graphics in this are incredibly unique, it mixed hand drawn with 3D in the way borderlands did, but in my opinion this game is definitely more of a treat for the eyes. Everywhere you go exploring this open world, youll find something interesting to go to. My favourite part of this game is definitely how many options you have of getting around. You have your basic movement, plus the ability to glide infinitely, plus your speeder, plus climbing. Overall the game is great to play late at night chilling in a VC with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The open world, slow paced, and narrative based gameplay of Sable made this game a genuinely therapeutic experience.Sable doesn't rely or present you with any necessarily stressful moments, enemies you need to overcome, or any sort of fighting whatsoever. Instead, you simply travel from place to place, taking in wonderful scenery along the way, and spending time investing and learning about the story of each character and location. The unique but simplistic cell-shaded art style of Sable only improves the beauty of every visual. Not to mention, the calm soundtrack by Japanese Breakfast makes each location even more immersive and stunning.Unfortunately Sable is plagued with bugs that somewhat distracted me from the experience, and you're bound to come across something game-breaking and having to restart your game. So remember to save often if you plan on playing Sable. Regardless, this game has so many wonderful qualities that absolutely make it worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: ‎‏‏‎ ‎‏‏‎ ‎‏‏‎ ‎‏‏‎ ‎ ‎ Ever since I first saw this demo in the Steam Next Fest, I knew this was something special so being able to play this game is an absolute treat. The story being so well contained in the demo, expands tenfold as you continue your journey and growth as Sable, discovering facettes of a new, strange world which help you find the characters identity throughout the game. All too often I would find myself just riding along the landscape and trying to see a new place that I had not explored or climbed yet, being its own challenge throughout the early game. The task of trying to find a shear wall and a way to get up it, while after many,  attempts being able to look out over the vast horizon and just feeling that accomplishment. The use of sound and lack thereof, was what truly blew me away as multiple times during my playthrough I would discover a long lost treasure and be taken aback by the swelling music that frames the achievement of a new mask or artefact into something special. On the opposite end of that, travelling the dunes with only my thoughts and the sound of my hoverbike, opened the way for a constant sense of adventure and discovery as new terrain appeared on the horizon.  Although simple in its own way, this game knows perfectly what it is aiming for and uses every aspect of the design to convey a beautiful experience of exploration and awe.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, what really draws me to this game is the setting. A pre-industrial people living amonst the ruins of a spacefaring civilization, using what they can scavenge for themselves. I love this concept, it's what I loved about Horizon Zero Dawn as well.Sable is all about exploration. There's no pressure, no enemies to fight, you are on a journey and that journey is what it's about. Nice and relaxing, but far from boring. The entire project feels like it has taken inspiration from a comic and turned that into a game. I mean that in a positive sense.The minimalist cellshading furthers the appearance of an animated comic adventure, in fact I've seen comics with exactly that style. I'm not totally a fan of it, as it is kind of unimmersive to me, but that's subjective.The sound design tends to be rather minimalist as well. While that fits the aesthetics of the game, I'm not a big fan of i t either. Really hate the sound of the chum eggs, for example. But again, subjective.The one problem with this game is the controls. They are janky at best, you can make it work, but it can be annoying. When selecting dialogue options, you have to click exactly the right position, otherwise you'll just use the currently selected option. When in the map screen, don't click anywhere, not even the icons to switch to another screen, or you'll plant a marker outside the map area. When moving around, the camera likes to get behind stuff in tight areas and sometimes when falling while climbing, Sable can't really decide wether to fall, stumble in mid-air, hold on or just fly away.In summary, controls and handling really need some work. Other than that, fans of casual atmospheric exploration games will certainly enjoy it. Fans of games like Journey or Abzu might as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "We need something between Yes and No" kinda recommendations. You'll see that most of this review is me going over the cons, but the pros simply require less words and take up more of the experience time-wise.The direction and (most of) the pieces are there for a very charming game. The art style is appealing in an interesting and fairly unique sorta way, and the landscapes coupled with the great soundtrack make exploring very enjoyable.But the game definitely needs work. It's not too buggy but there are still bugs nonetheless, and some aspects of the game feel like there isn't enough polish put into them.Pros:>>Exploring feels chill and unrushed. There's a lot of space between locations to enjoy using the bike, and the locations are good at bringing an initial sense of mystery and curiosity to the table.>>You go out into the world with the sole purpose of finding what you wanna do with your life, and (while the game doesn't put a ton of effort into fleshing out each of the many options) in the end you'll likely feel some sort of investment in your choice.>>The world isn't terribly varied, but it doesn't need to be. While the map largely consists of desert-esque or wasteland biomes, there's still some slight variety (one biome is a vast sandfield, another is scattered with towering buttes/mesas, etc.) so the view doesn't wear itself out.>>The soundtrack vaguely reminds me of Road 96 or Outer Wilds, a sort of chill road trip vibe. >>Riding around on the bike is generally pretty fun. Even when lower-end bike parts leave you with low handling stats, flopping around over dunes is still kinda fun in a humorous sorta way (probably because, unlike if you were to flip a car, the game is merciful with your momentum and righting yourself).Cons:>>As I mentioned, the game is decently buggy. I made a separate section below for some specifics.>>The map uses black icons for points of interest, which (considering how the map is designed and colored) very often makes it a pain to spot them. White would be MASSIVELY easier to spot throughout the overall map.>>At the beginning an idea is built up that the bike will be a fairly personal companion on this journey, they even give it a name. But outside of being told this at the start nothing is really done to reinforce this idea. I just think that's a missed opportunity.>>The bike parts' balancing needs some work. Nothing is broken or exceptionally useless, but the amount of work that goes into getting certain parts does not reflect in their performance. The absolute best bike parts in the game can be *bought* pretty early on for a sum of money that is honestly fairly easy to obtain. You'd think that would be awesome, but suddenly you find yourself spending the rest of the game getting all these new bike parts that look cool but are just worse in every way in terms of performance. I think it would be better if they put in a system to upgrade your bike regardless of parts, and the parts themselves functioned the same as your clothes: just appearance.>>As for the writing... (This'll be long, so feel free to stop here or skip to the bugs if you don't care) The writing isn't all THAT bad but I still gotta rant here cuz I have lots of problems with it. Not as in the overall narrative, as it's a game where your journey and exploration are the narrative. My problem is with how the game handles dialogue and interactions with NPCs:>>>>The game tries too hard to inject an excess of emotional impact into every interaction, as if Sable has a profound relationship with (or profound caring for and interest in) every character, after only a few words or even before then. >>>>There's an overeagerness to be descriptive (which makes even simple observations very wordy) and flowery (which often leads to thoughts that just don't translate). Some mild examples include, "Around the sun, celestial bodies move in a rhythmic dance," and "...humming a tune that seems at once new and familiar." It could be tolerable if it was occasional but this is present throughout almost the entire game. >>>>My biggest peeve in writing: one half of a dialogue is in speech format ("Oh! You surprised me!") and the other half is in narrative format (I apologized for startling him.). This is how dialogue plays out between NPCs and Sable, respectively. It comes across as janky and completely ruins the flow of reading through a conversation.>>>>The irony is that, while Sable's text boxes leave her exact spoken words up to the imagination, the rest of her text boxes leave NOTHING to the imagination. In her narrating thoughts, she spells out how people speak or behave, how you should be perceiving the world, etc. A written story would obviously be more tell than show, but a game should be more show than tell and they didn't do that here. It's the far opposite of minimalism, which is a shame because it contrasts sharply with what makes the rest of the game good.>>>>Instead of leaving certain pieces of information to be read in a codex (like detailing the Machinists' culture or some such) you're forced to mentally put the dialogue on hold to read through constant spatterings of exposition, courtesy of Sable's thoughts. Personally, the game would be wayyy more enjoyable if 90% of Sable's thoughts were moved to some sort of lore codex and if Sable's text boxes were converted to actual speech instead of narration. Leave some stuff up to my imagination; the magic honestly diminishes when it's spelled out for me.Bugs:>>The game requires a full restart A LOT. Why? Because certain things in the game don't properly update until you do so. Moved to a specific spot to catch a certain fish? That fish won't pop up, you'll just keep catching something from a random previous area you were in until you reboot. Can't talk to that one NPC who only shows up at night? Wait til you see them, save, reboot the game and ta-da! you can talk to them now.>>Hitting Esc to open inventory/etc. very often leads to the cursor disappearing and becoming unusable, while hitting the Map hotkey (which opens access to the same submenus) doesn't.>>Textures on certain objects will randomly blip out of existence when taking certain camera angles. It doesn't happen too often, but certain object types consistently vanish if you're climbing them and move the camera below an overhead view.>>Hitboxes are occasionally poorly aligned (climbing two feet away from the edge of a cliff) or missing (instead of crawling through a certain vent or two, just walk up to it and hit jump and you'll vault on top of the vent and through the wall it's leading through).>>Speaking of hitboxes, just remove hitboxes for the chum eggs entirely. There's a lot of issues (character randomly leaning over at 45 degree angles, leg glitching up inside body, etc.) that would be solved by taking away the hitboxes for those things entirely.>>NPCs that wander around certain areas very often either get stuck on tiny bumps in the ground or straight-up walk into walls or other large objects.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the exploration of Breath of the Wild but wished that there was actually something to explore and that the focus would solely be on traversing a vast world without things like combat being a distraction, then Sable is pretty much what you're looking for.Sable is fully focused on finding places in the desert world that the titular character inhabits, as she embarks on her rite of passage. It's very compelling: there's always another landmark, always a potential quest around the corner, and collectibles are visible enough that each one becomes a tangible goal. It's a game of simple mechanics, but the focused take on those few select mechanics makes it a tight journey. The presentation does help: the comic book like visuals are charming and atmospheric even when they sometimes glitch out, and the score from Japanese Breakfast is beautiful and a keeper even outside the game.There's a few downsides - some glitches and other jank, everything's made accessible and "casual" enough that the game rarely expects players to really showcase their grown knowledge of the game (there's almost always an easier path around the corner if you can't climb high enough at first) and the writing flicks between "serious" and jovial like it's choosing the tone for each conversation at random, which then leads to the game as a whole feeling a bit disjointed in its mood. But they're minor issues, I found myself captivated more than I expected and went out of my way to collect and explore more after the game gave me the option to finish it, simply because I found the world so enjoyable to explore.Sable isn't an indie icon, but it's definitely a cult classic in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant. Must-play for anyone who likes games that effect your irl life and/or collectathons. There are a number of games that make it to my favorited tab, but this is one of the few i'd be sharing with just about everyone, whether they're used to games or not. It hits the perfect balance so it's fun regardless of experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A game seemingly made specifically for me. One of the most relaxing and chill games I've ever played. No combat, and the traversal of the world was clearly paramount to the developers. The bike handles pretty smoothly and the glide and climb features make every climbing puzzle easy enough to handle, especially when you increase Sable's stamina. Multiple outfits can be found or bought throughout the world, multiple bike parts and colors, several unique and interesting masks can be obtained throughout different missions in the world.The world itself is immensely gorgeous and the art style lends itself extremely well for the "desolation" of the sand planet we're on with many interesting sub-biomes included. My jaw actually dropped a few times cresting a hill to see an ancient monument off in the distance. The history of the world is even more delicately handled, with little exposition through character interaction, but by reading about the world and deducing from what's shown you can determine where we are, who we are, and how we might have gotten here in the first place.The sound design is extremely well done. Every bike engine has its own unique gurgle and thrum, the world feels and sounds like you're interacting with it. And above all, the music by Japanese Breakfast is beautiful and ethereal, with day/night versions of many of the songs. You begin identifying the areas of the world with the backing songs. It's somewhat short, I milked most everything out of it (minus some chum collecting) and it was a solid 15 hours, easily shaved by fast traveling everywhere (I wouldn't suggest it, the driving is part of the fun). It's a game to put on for a relaxing time, for those looking to explore a new, exciting world in a natural way, or for those looking for a bit of a hint of Star Wars to their game. The developers noted they were inspired by the opening Rey segment of Episode VII, and you feel Star Wars in other ways: driving a speeder bike through tall-trunked forests or weaving through and around tall, rocky buttes and canyons. Can't recommend it enough to anyone who plays video games.
