_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, yes it does have its bugs 100% but none of them were game breaking for me. Most could be fixed by fast traveling somewhere. Some of the scrolling bugs were honestly hilarious, but fine. A bit laggy in places but not sure if its due to the new update it ran pretty decently at 60fps on my huge 4k monitor lol.The game itself is beautiful, the narrative relatively simple but no less engaging for it. Loved some of the hidden gems in there, worth spending time driving around the desert for :D. Also the bike upgrades <3, loved them. Oh and clothes! So many clothes! Very much recommend this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really great, amazing atmosphere, very fun non-linear gameplay and it's a beautiful homage to Moebius' art style. The game is almost entirely about exploration and puzzles with no combat, so consider if that's your thing before buying.The main problem plaguing this title is that the game has horrible framerate issues at the moment. Even with every setting at minimum, the FPS still dips HORRENDOUSLY in some parts of the map. Even at its smoothest moments the framerate is still rough. I've never been one to complain about framerates but it sometimes gets almost unbearable in this game.All in all I still love this title, it's clearly made with lots of love, just wish it was optimized properly.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Played and got 100% achievements on Steamdeck with no major issues, just sporadic sound stuttering.I loved this game from start to finish, you play as Sable, a young girl loved by her tribe, getting ready to go through the "gliding", a kind of rite of passage to adulthood where you have to explore the world and at the same time get to know yourself and discover how you fit in that world. The gameplay is based on exploration, the climbing mechanic reminded me of Shadow of Colossus, where you can improve your stamina not by killing lizards but by finding the cute pink chums. That's another point I find important to notice in this game, there are no deaths or killings, it brings a kind of peace and relaxation to exploration while you're traveling on your hoverbike. It's an exploration game with some easy puzzles, not an action game, and it's fine as it is.The design and aesthetic looked like it was ripped straight from a comic book, every screenshot I took looked like it was from a Moebius strip, absolutely loved it.Soundtrack is fitting, not grandiose but simple and intimate, sometimes reminded me of Vangelis, r.i.p.The world building is simple, but I found myself really engaged on discovering the world and all its secrets, and it was good enough for me, reminded me of playing the very first Tomb Raider in '96.I understand that the game might not be for everyone, it is straightforward and simple, but the way the game made me feel is something I will thank the developers, because they made this 40-year-old empathize with this teenager called Sable and her will to discover the world but more importantly discovering herself.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Camera is a bit janky, and the game runs slow on my bad laptop. Which is usually fine but freezing in the middle of a jump and having to climb all the way back up sucks. game looks cool tho, will play it eventually but from my short experince its buggy and even the menus are laggy on slow computers. so dont buy it if you have a potato like i do
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this one, and it made me feel like I was living in a  world. It specifically made me think of the Monk and Robot series, I'm not entirely sure why, it just had those chilled, relaxing vibes. The world is , it's large and expansive, dotted with small settlements, and you take your character to various location that you find. The music is low-key and really lends itself well to the relaxing wholesome dystopia. That's about it though. I went into the game assuming it was story rich due to the assigned tag. It is . This is "story rich" if the only thing you've ever played in your life is Solitaire. It has some , but it has barely any story, they are two different things. There isn't that much going on, there's a bit of an intro and after that you're pretty much told "Welp, off you go then". And that's it. The lore is uncovered through some quests, but it doesn't help that there are moments of bugginess where  and so the 'quest' did not progress for me. And most of the other quests are to the tune of "I got an X, I should go find more X". Some quests seem to hint at an interesting story thread, but end abruptly and without resolution. The game is actually full of similar tiny little papercuts, involving suddenly bad camera angles, awkward pod controls, uninspiring travel, laggy transitions. Worst of all though is the weird : the on screen character runs in a weird , while the background is smoother; this combination made me nauseous. It's the first time I've ever gotten a headache from a third person game. If you are prone to nausea in some games, do have a look at more videos to see if this could affect you. Looking at the trailer video, I feel it's been sped up slightly to make it appear smoother than it actually is. I actually feel bad giving this a not recommended, it's quite obvious the amount of care and effort that has gone into the game which I did appreciate, and which made me want to keep pushing on.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Edited Review!!!I changed to recommended, but with a warning.  This game is NOT FOR EVERYONE!Sable is as much a piece of art as it is a game.  There is much that is lovely here, but some of the game play elements are 'not amazing.'  See Cons below for details.It IS lovely, though.Pros:1.  The game is pretty.  The comic book art render is really cool.2.  The music is great! Like, amazingly well fit to the environment and gameplay.3.  A world with truly no misogyny.  Odd but REALLY REALLY nice.  Also, no combat, no violence.4.  The world is visually beautiful.  Seriously.5.  Puzzles are like a cross between Super Mario Bros and Portal.6.  Did I mention how great it looks?Cons:1. Super frustrating to play.  There are quests that are almost impossible until after you have built up your Stamina.  This is not made clear.2. UI is broken.  Sometimes I can't access the Settings menu while playing, it goes directly to Controls.  Sometimes  I can't save.  Sometimes I also can't exit the game directly, I have to Alt-Tab out and kill it using the Steam menu.3. Apparently can't remap keybinds.  Really?  It's 2022.  It SAYS they're remapped, but they aren't.  I got used to this, but, come on.If you decide to give Sable a try I recommend that when you leave the clan, follow the directions to Burnt Oak Station first.  Concentrate on finding Chum eggs and trading them in.  This is how you build your Stamina.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics, soundtrack, and story line are all exceptional, but the dialog is also written as beautiful prose. While at first I wasn't sure if the game would hold my attention without enemies, the quests are riveting, the game encourages curiosity, and the puzzles are really fun. There are a few places where there are glitches in the game, but not enough to cause any major problems. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing game thatSable takes all the fun exploration mechanics made popular in "Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild" and applies them without any combat or high-concentration moments. Makes for a great "podcast" game if you want to throw something up on another monitor.This game really tickles the itch of "Hey, I think I see something over there, i'm gonna check it out" and getting rewarded for it. Zooming around on the hoverbike is satisfying and while there are some physics bugs, there's nothing game breaking.The world is well designed and laid out. I was hooked on every conversation, trying to learn more about this world from every word. Uncovering the history and culture of Sable was just as fun as exploring the maps.Admittedly, the game is not well optimized and it may cause computers to go full throttle every so often. Soundtrack is relaxing with just the right amount of melancholy. The music as you leave home for the first time really hits hard.Overall, a great game that I'd recommend to anyone who loves exploring
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't for me. Compared to games like East Shade or Rime that I thoroughly enjoyed because the environments were so gorgeous and interesting to look at,  the graphics and art work in Sable did not inspire me or make me want to explore as they were too basic and too repetitive, and for a great deal or walking, there isn't much to pick up or discover along the way. There are also visible black seams in larger objects / scenery showing through which isn't pleasant. The music is also uninspiring, very basic synth loops, nothing like the opening vocal track on the trailer video. The character movement is clunky and somewhat illogical - if Sable can jump and grab a wall from a platform, I'd expect her to be able to jump off a wall to another one and grab it - but that doesn't work, she just falls. The dialogue is badly written and not displayed in a clear way - the script feels like it's been poorly translated from another language, and it's hard to tell what's a description, what is Sable pondering to herself, and what is dialogue from a character she's trying to speak to. To reload a game save you have to exit the whole game and then reload after you have effectively restarted the game up (which takes a long time compared to a direct "load saved game" option from within the current game). The save game option is also awkward to get to - for some reason it's the last menu option in the list... All these aspects mean that unfortunately for me I didn't enjoy playing this game and decided to request a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, and quickly becoming one of my favourites. There is so much to discover and explore. Climbing the tallest monuments, slowly making your way to the top, taking in the view just to see in the distance. Something taller, larger, or so much more unique in design or silhouette.Moreover, I really enjoyed the integration of bugs into the story, finding the many butter/ dragonfly's. The insects that have different ways of capture hidden with in each biome.Whats interesting to note, is that you can collect more that the necessary amount of badges to claim a mask. At first I thought that once I had claimed the masks, that the tasks associated with them would end. But this is incorrect, you can continue to decide and refine your path.Would greatly recommend to people who want to play a game, with little to no frustration, and a focus on exploration of the world and self.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Aimless and relaxing.This game is like a warm hug. Sable's premise is simple, its gameplay is straightforward, and every part of it gives you a sense of wonder and adventure like you're a kid on a trip to somewhere new.This isn't a coming-of-age story, but certainly an interactive rite of passage. There's no long series of events that mature your character, no decisive moment that forces you to act above your age. It's what a four-year-old might think "" should look like. You're given a chance to leave your clan, explore the world, and find your calling. Once you've had your fill and decided what you enjoy, you find your way back to your nomadic relatives, enjoy a quick ceremony, and thus completes the game. It's a very spiritual header and footer to an otherwise mundane plotline.But you shouldn't be here for the plot. At it's core, Sable is an exploration game. The plot is merely a loose thread that connects two pins on a corkboard. There's no direction, no quest order, and nigh on zero guidance. By simply floating around on your hoverbike and investigating every nook and cranny, you'll find interesting people, unique collectibles, and no shortage of fetch quests. Many of these collectibles and quests are tied to a side story, setpiece, or puzzle that really makes this desolate wasteland feel alive. Accompanied by serene music and soothing sound design, Sable is a fantastic game to relax with.For as simple as it is, Sable is a great game. It's a slow-paced, tranquil, surprisingly pretty, and incredibly charming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A coming of age for a young girl, tasked with exploring and learning about her world. Little fetch quests, puzzles in long abandoned and torn apart space shuttles. soaring through the sand dunes! I've been mesmerized with the art style for days, the opening sequence and the music, I almost cried at how beautiful it was.Bite sized exploration with lite Breath of the Wild mechanics and no combat or threat of "losing". You wont regret the purchase, please give this game a chance.And too the dev's, thank you and I can't wait to see what you do next and I hope you expand on Sable's story and world!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, that was both an incredible journey of exploration, and a very emotional coming of age story. Gorgeous and awe-inspiring locations, the artstyle is creative and just fuels my screenshot addiction, there are some beautiful moments with characters, and now I feel like a part of me is gone.The game is a pretty buggy, not game breaking bugs but certainly annoying, along with a far few stutters. The games progression system in terms of upgrading your hoverbike is also a joke cause you can buy anything you want in 2 or 3 hours. The biggest flaw of the game is that you hoverbike is never really a particularly smooth ride, which is a shame because it looks beautiful and when it works it feels amazing. But ultimately, these flaws don't really matter to me much, because this was an amazing experience.for me personally this was a 9/10, but in reality it's probably more like an 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Should be an Indie Gem but is somewhat let down by bugs.The art style in this game is great, evocative of Moebius. The music is pleasant and moody. The hover bike mechanics are pretty poor, and need a lot more polish. Most of the bikes nosedive when crossing a small hill, or they get caught too easily on geometry. There is little reason to collect the various hover bikes, and the most difficult one to get isn't as good as one you can simply buy in early game.There are quite a few bugs in the game, but nothing game breaking. A few I had to quit and restart the game to resolve. Some of the climbing can be frustrating because of random loss of grip that causes Sable to slide downward.I would like to see more done with the quests. Quite a few of them are fetch quests (collect 3 things).Quitting the game is very annoying. Settings -> Navigate to Save/Quit dialog -> Return to Main Menu -> Have to watch developer logo splash screens -> Game title screen -> Press any key to start -> Quit game from Main Menu. Have the devs never quit out of a game before? The whole process felt weird and console-y.Overall it was a pleasant enough game. Chill exploration vibes.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is really similar to Breath of the Wild, where you are given a huge, beautiful landscape to explore and make your own journey through.  I think it's better than BotW in one major way: there aren't any enemies to worry about.  This game is so nice in that it allows the player to explore without interruption, providing a truly relaxing, beautiful world to enjoy without the threat of suddenly being attacked and/or dying and resetting to a far previous save point.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: So pretty and relaxing! But . . . Some improvements are necessary. I bought the game last night and played for 5 hours straight!I got to the 3rd town and it felt like things started to fall apart. I immediately tried to hover over the water, because that's how hovering works, and I was disappointed when I ended up just driving around the bottom of a lake. I explored the area around Eccria and got separated from my hover bike. When I called, it never came to me... I went looking for it and couldn't find it. Seems to be glitched through the map, tried upgrading it, but that didn't make it appear either. It was around this time that I discovered THIS GAME DOESN'T HAVE AUTOSAVING!?I just played for five hours (without saving apparently) to encounter a game breaking glitch... 1) You should hover bike over/on water, and it should have a nifty waterwing animation. 2) Calling the hover bike Is prone to error and needs some more safeguards (I think mine fell into the thieving magpie well?)3) Autosaving should be on by default and able to be turned off in settings.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for 12 hours. That is by far the longest I've ever played on a demo. But now the full game is out, so let's talk about a few things I like and don't. I like the exploration aspect and the game isn't a locked in type of quests. You can explore, solve, and find new puzzles and items that will help you on your path. The color when you are in certain buildings or areas is sort of boring, but they may fix that at some point. I recommend this game 100% if you like exploration puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A charming indie game with incredible art style. I really enjoyed the calming nature of exploring a new planet with a unique history and discovering bits along the way. The game takes a ton of influence from Zelda: BotW, in particular the climbing/gliding mechanics, finding the koroks (chums in sable), and obtaining masks. Unfortunately the game has some glaring drawbacks: it's buggy, has camera issues, lots of places where clipping can get you stuck, the climbing/hopping jittering is incredibly annoying. As for game play, they could significantly improve the climbing and running mechanics, as they feels slow and inorganic. The bike riding could be so much more fun if they improved the jumping/gliding mechanic. It didn't feel freeing when hitting a small bump as the vehicle would spin you like crazy. Overall fun game but could be significantly improved.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really sorry if this "review" is rumbly or doesn't really give you an understanding of what its like to play the game, this is my first review, and i had such an incredible experience i had to write it downSable is a game about choice. Its about growing up and finding your place in the world. Its about discovering who you are and choosing your path. Its in some way, a personalized game just for me.I don't know what i thought about this game before i played it, probably that's its a cool sci-fi action game with a unique art style, and that's it. Instead i got a deeply personal experience that ill remember for a long time.This was my first open world game, and I'm so glad that it was. From playing linear games where the direction for me to go is set by the creator to going to a game where you are free to do as you please was, to be honest, quite scary. I usually like having things in control and understand what I'm suppose to do, and starting this game i was a bit anxious somehow about what would i do in such a game. But when i stepped into Sables world these worries faded away. in sable you are playing as a young girl named sable as she goes on her Gliding, a rite of passage ritual where she is suppose to figure out what will shell do in the world. The Gliding is, technically, about career, but i believe the game is more than that, its choosing who you'll be in world. When the Gliding started, and i was left alone with this open world with only some hints and advice on what should i do, i started wondering if this game will fit my path. In the village where you start i saw some professions, but none of them fit me. I didn't want to end up choosing a path that doesn't feel like me, and i thought this game might be just that, a list of some jobs i can choose, and that in the end ill come out wondering why the game exists except from to give the player some superficial choice. I continued with the game, i discovered different paths that i could go to, different masks i could choose for myself to put on. None of them fit me. then i met someone. She was a knight, but unlike the others that were guarding some places as they should, she was traveling the world. She told me she was on a second Gliding, this one isn't the one you are suppose to do when you reach the right age, but one she decided herself to go on. Eventually i found a mask that fit me, a mask that doesn't fit to conventional ways, and one that filed me with comfort. Finding this mask meant so much to me, but in some way, it was completely meaningless. no matter what i chose this game thought me that i don't have to wear it as others do. I could continue searching for eternity, having joy in the sense of not being confined to a single mask. I could always change, always keep searching, and even if i find my way, i don't have to stick with it or follow it to where it leads me. My path goes my own way, and i can always change it. I could talk for hours about the fetch quest in this game, the incredible music and art direction, the calming atmosphere, the unique world, or maybe the climbing mechanics, incredible dialog and even the bugs, but i feel like talking about them takes somehow from my experience with the game. The game is about growing up to the world and finding your own path, your own mask to put on. Some of the world isn't perfect, nor everything fits you. But the game, as the world, is about the path that you carve for yourself. When i had all the options before me and finally chose my mask and closed the game, i did it with a smile knowing that even though i found the mask for me, it will never constrain me to any road. If Sable taught me something, is that i don't have to be constrained to to a path that people, or society carved for me. I don't have to fit into a path of an artist, a path of a leader or even a path of an outcast that does what they desire and love. I can choose my own path, and ill remember this game, and that knight that continued on her Gliding whenever I'm carving it to myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: After the patches and bug fixed the game is now playable, though while riding the hover bike i still have some bad frames drops while im running on a 3080. Aswell the climbing has frustrated me beyond belief sometimes because it has one of those "you can climb anything and anywhere" mechanics that every developer takes from BOTW but yet again they failed to realize what made it so good there, the fact that all the landscape was actually climbed by some game testers and seen what levels of stamina (you can upgrade stamina just like in BOTW aswell) is needed to get up to where, but in sable, half the stuff i try to climb i clip through, and especially towards the end of the game it became almost unbareable. In a game where theres climbing involved and used as the main aspect, maybe make sure YOU DONT CLIP THROUGH WALLS THAT LOOK CLIMBABLE, i feel like thats pretty elementary, and im not referring to the areas where there are walls that are MEANT to be clipped through, as there are a couple, im referring to poles and walls leading upwards, typically towards a cartographer balloon. All in all the game is quite nice and calming, can be a very fun little adventure, but for the price point honestly youre better of wating for some sort of sale, i dont think this game is worth its price point due to there being such a current lack of content in general compared to other games at the price point not to mention the polish, if we compare this to something like hellblade senuas sacrifice which is only a few dollars more, the polish and story in that game is above and beyond compared to sable. I highly reccomend watching some gameplay and really finding out if sable is for you before buying because i feel it is a very niche title seeing it has no combat to speak of and the puzzles are beyond simple, though exploration and roleplaying can be very fun. TL;DR, Games pretty asf and fun to roleplay, but the gameplay doesnt have much to offer and climbing can become VERY frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game. It has a very unique peaceful feeling to it and makes me relaxed after a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ work day. It feel somewhat like Zelda Breath of Wild but also very different and stands out on its own. I don't know however why I get only 40 FPS with my RTX 2080Ti and an I7-8700K CPU at 1080p in some regions like the forest like region at the beginning after I left the tutorial. This doesn't make any sense since I can play Cyberpunk at higher resolution with constant 80 FPS and high to ultra details. I hope a future patch will solve that problem. Besides that I really like the game and recommend it to any adventurer who can live without shooting everything in sight.

_childDocuments_.review: Guiding Sable through her journey of self discovery was a truly unique experience.Every settlement reached or obstacle climbed came with new and interesting ways to occupy your time along the quest to find your calling.It's just you and your bike, with a whole world to explore.While the experience of the world and its story is outstanding, unfortunately, there are quite a few technical problems with the game. The game is very buggy, with some of the traversal mechanics getting the player and camera into unexpected positions. Game performance was all over the place, with no apparent reason and regardless of any in-game settings.Menus often stopped responding correctly (or stopped altogether at times), and objects/NPCs in the world sometimes stopped being able to be interacted with; these were resolved by reloading the game.Even with some technical issues that have stopped me from continuing other games, I was completely taken in by Sable. Definitely pick this game up.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind, this is basically an open world walking sim.Clocking in just under 12 hours before I finished the game, I really enjoyed it.I enjoyed the art, the music, the exploration.It was a perfect game for me to wind down during the evening.Unfortunately, this game is not without its technical issues:1. Menu navigation issues. Keyboard and Mouse inputs seem to conflict.2. Map markers can be added outside the map, and multiple for some reason are added per mouseclick.3. Audio bugs where ambient sounds from certain areas persist during playtime.'4. Frame drops in denser areas, sometimes stutters too.This is just 3 I know from the top of my head because they were rather annoying to deal with.Even though I didn't experience anything gamebreaking, this game unfortunately isn't polished. In this current state, I would not recommend this game at the current price of 24.99 USD.Especially given the technical problems the game still has.If it was 15.00 USD or below, I would recommend this game 100%.PROVIDED the dev team polishes it.

_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you play as Sable, a young girl who goes on a journey of self-discovery in a beautifully designed and interesting open world. While the adventure is not particularly long compared to other games and the world at times can feel a little bit empty and lonely, the game succeeds in invoking a serene atmosphere and presenting a unique colorful planet and culture. The game centers around the main objective of following the ritual of the gliding (a journey on which you decide what your future role in society will be) and the side objectives that go along with it, but it let's you decide how much of the world you want to experience before making your final decision. While this means that Sable is a game with almost zero pressure and makes it more of a meditative experience than a game in a classical sence, it never overstayed it's welcome in my opinion. Worth it if you enjoy games that provide you with chill vibes and an interesting world to explore as the main focus.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with my one major gripe: the camera felt awkward with the mouse, most likely designed for controller and without proper adjustments. Once using a controller, however, did not have problems with it anymore. Do not recommend playing without a controller.It reminds me of BoTW in some ways, all of them good - wonderful capability to climb on almost anything, vast open world to explore, highly exploration based. However, it's not just a BoTW clone - it takes its own stance, and does it well. I recommend turning quest markers off for the majority of the game, and just exploring - go seek out everything that looks remotely interesting, there's probably something worth your time over there.Bike and character customization is also quite good; there is a wide variety of options; character changes are purely vanity, but the bike changes are not - which is somewhat bad (changing how your bike looks changes how it works) but also very nice, being able to fine-tune how you want it. I often went with odd mixups of various pieces, somewhat ignoring stats and focusing on appearance.On the topic of the bike - absolutely love it. Oftentimes open world games leave wide open spaces between the various points of interest, leading to lots of boring treking. Sable twists this with a constant companion in the form of your hoverbike, making the distances actually interesting to traverse.I especially love the varied looks of the different areas - they look similar enough to feel like one overall place, but different enough to be distinct. The wide open spaces that dominate much of the landscape allow for navigation via landmarks, rather than the map. One minor gripe here: high reliance on map markers for finding quests. I ended up mostly ignoring them and just exploring, knowing I'd eventually find it and have fun on the way, but I'd love it if place descriptions were more verbose, allowing more organic pathfinding.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: The game can be buggy at times which is a true sadness because this is a really great game. I was looking for a game to chill out with and Sable managed to do that and let me enter an interesting world that I didn't want to leave. The open nature of the game and how it let you play it your way was perfect for the theme of searching and allowed me to immerse myself into the game and character of Sable.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start by saying I absolutely loved this game. The graphic design, the story behind it, the music was all simply amazing. It had so much potential to be a wonderful experience of calm exploration. But unfortunately, what should have been calming - I found enraging. There are some really bad optimisation issues, often making riding your hoverbike (a part of the game that should also be really fun) frustrating and unenjoyable. I love this game obviously as I 100% completed it but near the end, I was frustrated and didn't even enjoy the ending. I can't in good conscience recommend the game with the current bugs. However when I hear that these are gone I'll change my review - this really has the potential to be a wonderful little story about discovering yourself and your freedom. I enjoyed it - bugs aside.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game a 7/10.Lovely art style and very relaxing to play thanks to the wonderful music. Puzzles are at a easy level but still manages to get your brain working. Lots of quests to keep you occupied and lovely world to explore.However it receives a 7/10 because there were defiantly bugs in the game. Also the climbing, the camera, and the map were incredibly sensitive. Which at times could be very frustrating.Overall it will keep you occupied for a good while and i'd say you get your moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: No aspect of this game works:Exploration: World is empty. Apart from what biome you're in there is no variation in environment, and the biomes are basically recolors. You also can't just move around the world and enjoy it because of how buggy the camera and bike are.Story: The whole finding yourself aspect makes no sense as you earn badges for doing chores for people with jobs, not learning how to do their job or what they actually do, just doing things for them. The worst example of this is Mechanists, who have a spiritual connection to machines, Sable doesn't, but it's fine you collected some crystals so you're basically one of them. The only job you can do is being a Glider, so it feels like you should just stay as a glider.Gameplay: Extremely unvaried, your moveset doesn't change after you leave the tutorial area. Outfits don't even provide bonuses even when item descriptions act like they do. Climbing is a watered down version of BotW's where they didn't bother adding the strategic element of leading. Controls: I played on PC with a mouse and keyboard which was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare, highly suggest using a controller. Menus are the worst offenders being near impossible to navigate without one.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience that's actually hard to recommend due to how poorly the game runs.Even if you have a computer powerful enough to run it smoothly (which means little as you'll still encounter problems that shouldn't exist), Sable is riddled with bugs, glitches, and inconsitencies that'll make you scoff no matter how well you manage to put up with it. Though there's no combat, you will have enemies. Here are just a few of them:- The hoverbike, which doesn't know whether it wants to be that, a beach ball (it bounces off of everything), or an ostrich (it often tries to bury its head in the sand, making controlling it quite challenging).- The camera, which has a mind of its own. It *loves* to point upwards when you're done climbing a surface, among other annoyances.- The climbing... Lord, the climbing. It looks like BOTW, but it's far from being as well realized as that (which is saying a lot cuz even BOTW's climbing has its moments).- Platforming! Yes, this game has platforming. There aren't too many spots that'll make you ragequit, but the few there are really highlight how floaty and unresponsive Sable is. You thought Pitioss in FFXV was infuriating? You better get ready...- The sound design, which is probably the most glitched aspect in the entire game. From constant sounds that play when they shouldn't (but they do because the game is put together very poorly) to audio suttering across the board, this game has it all.And that's just the tip of the iceberg...The art direction is stunning, the soundtrack is cozy, the writing is charming, the world building is intriguing, and the puzzles are fun. If you think you can put up with a faulty game full of performance issues and glitches, Sable is one of the best gaming experiences 2021 had to offer. I love it, but I can't deny that all its issues annoy me to the point where I put off finishing it cuz I just bought other games (writing this towards the end of the 2021 winter sale) that run so much better even though they look like they shouldn't, so playing those is all the more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! It's a short relaxing open world story with easy to understand controls and mechanics. The story itself finishes at about five or six hours but there's a lot more content if you wish to unlock all of the achievements and masks. The art style in this game is one of the most unique directions I've ever seen and kept me amazed in the world of Sable.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely fun, with different types of puzzles to solve, quests to complete, and secrets to uncover. I played many hours of this game and would definitely recommend it to others. However, it can be frustrating at times when the game glitches, which was a barrier for completing certain puzzles/obstacle courses. The game is mostly sound, the glitches are few and far between. But when they happen, they can be quite detrimental (ex: climbing and jumping up rocks and then suddenly being unable to grip the wall for no reason - falling allllll the way back down.... multiple times). Nothing that can't eventually be patched/updated by the developers though! And again, there are so so so many good things about this game; it's quite exceptional IMO that the game has as few glitches as it does, as an indie game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great mechanics and combines platforming in a 3D world with puzzle-solving, hoverbike-gliding! and a focus on exploring. Gliding on the bike is a tad clunky or maybe just needs more practice to get fluid. Some bugs with massive frame rate drops(enough to stall the gameplay, below 10fps) when traveling close to the edge of a map's range. Hopefully the bugs get patched up since it's only day two since release. The soundtrack from Japanese Breakfast is enough to have me hooked; you go from hearing only the sounds of your bike's engine to being pulled in by trance-like, synth and pad lushness. I was fantasizing about the possibility of seeing cell shading in games again and Sable does it in a pastel dreamworld- simple and ethereal shapes and soft, muted colors expand the feeling of solitude and exploration. If you need me I'll be in the desert gliding on my custom bike for several days.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: open world game without hamfisted survival mechanics or weapon durability. better than breath of the wild because of the aforementioned reasons. it makea me happy. i only play like half an hour every 6 months but its just a game that i turn on and then ride around on my bike for 30 minutes and it makes me feel an immense peace. i have no idea what the story is about besides going on a fun little pilgrimage im such a #slay #girlboss. beautiful graphics no matter what settings you use. the settings, especially the stuff related to the cel shading intensity, are more about what style you personally like most than what makes it run the best or look the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little game :)The world and atmosphere are interesting and fun to explore, I had a blast with itArt is really nice and unique, cool music tooI bought it and couldn't put it down until I was 100% done with itIt has few graphical bugs on occasion and isn't very well optimized but would definitely still give it a go!

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing game. Just you and your bike to explore the world. If you like this art style, you should check out french artist Moebius. He is the main inspiration for the visuals in this game. Gameplay wise, It is pretty simple. Basically a collect-a-thon and fetch quests. _childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I want to live in this world for longer.  The art style is great, the feel involves just enough action and mystery, and you don't need to have dangerous enemies or too many hazards to make it challenging.  You have to use time, make connections, and occasionally check out unexpected places in order for things to click but it's so nice when they do.  The music and ambience just amp it further.  Some of the areas feel too 'clean' and new for their supposed age and condition, but that's a really minor gripe.Shedworks, please find some way to extend this or expand it.  What's that thing in the system map we never find out more about?  What are in the places we can't reach?  I hope for more of this place you've made.  (And now the camera isn't annoying, bonus.)
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A great meditative open-world experience about a coming-of-age girl, trying to determine her place in life, offering a small but densely filled handcrafted desert for you to explore, creative writing, magnificent artstyle and relaxing music. The game is narratively built around exploration and finding stuff yourself, which creates a feeling of freedom i haven't felt in any openworld game in a while. It also philosophically resonated with me greatly, diving into the topics of youth, figuring out your own path, destiny and other old-as-time ever-relevant questions. My Sable playthrough definately became something personal and I hope it will become such for you, since that is what it's created to do. The only drawback are several technical issues and bugs which might sometimes cause subtle frustration, but generally aren't deal-breaking.Overall: A unique and easily personal experience, which might've used a little polish, but is still easily the best game I've played in the last two years. A definate buy for every indie-game appreciator, teenager confused with the adult world or just anyone who loves a good open world.9/10

So I guess I am going with not recommended because it's a pretty small world with not a whole lot to accomplish. Give me an update with a new region and a dozen new puzzles and quests and I will be happy to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a work of art and plays like one!a coming of age story with free and open choices witch simplistic themes yet so engaging and fun to play. There are a number of bugs and framerate issues that can be a hindrance sometimes but considering this is the first game from the minds of just two english guys who had no prior experience with game development on this scale it's amezing what they pulled off, definitely recommend it's a unique game and experience just know it doesn't always run smoothly 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: i absolutely enjoyed playing this game. it is truly a unique and one of a kind experience.the game is very fascinating and i found myself a little sad at then end...simply because i was at the end of my gliding. a wonderful journey it was  full of memories not soon forgotten. the game is a bit rough around the edges at times but it is more than made up for. you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when an indie team makes a Breath of the Wild inspired game that has no monsters in it? Well, you get something like Sable, of course! Equal parts exploration, chill, quest solving, and platforming, this game is a truly remarkable experience and a must play for any exploration enthusiasts such as myself, which was always my favorite part of games like Botw. There is no way to die in this game, but the game does not hold your hand and alot of the joy of the game is figuring out how the game works. There are a few things in the game that are rather obtuse for specific quests and may need a look online, but overall this game is a fantastic experience. When I was finished with my playthrough, I just sat on top of a pillar and watched the moon set and the sun rise...you could do that for hours in this game the scenery, ambient noise, and the music are such a perfect mix of relaxation and beauty! Do yourself a favor and get this great game, if you haven't already!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game but it's very janky. It definitely needed more time to be polished because bugs are abound. Graphical bugs, sound bugs, occasionally the core climbing mechanics bug out. However, at it's core it's a genuinely fun low stakes exploration game with some great writing. _childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: While Sable isn't perfect and would really benefit from more QA and bug fixes, this game is greater than the sum of its wonky parts. Really enjoyable open world exploration game that's obviously inspired by Breath Of The Wild. I'm quite surprised that a game of this magnitude was made by a small indie team.While Sable is quite average in the puzzle department, exploring this world was definitely the highlight.I really loved the OST made by Japanese Breakfast, and the sound design was great!Sadly, this game feels unpolished and I encountered a lot of bugs and glitches:Huge framerate problem especially while using the bike, a lot of audio stuttering, loud audio spike out of nowhere while exploring, musical themes stacking on top of each others, big environnements loading late, not being able to interact with a specific NPC without restarting.If you can bear the technical hiccups of this indie game, I would recommend it if you are looking for a chill game to explore, especially at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is this a visually stunning game with charming characters and landscapes, but there is so much to say about the calming joy that can be found exploring the little camps and towns of Sable or riding the dunes in your junky little bike. It is a pleasure to simply explore the game's world in search of new quests, clothing items and pieces to modify your bike, chum eggs and quirky desert-dwellers each with a story to tell. While there is no combat or health system I did not feel this detracted from the experience and instead heightened my enjoyment of adventuring without the stress of health preservation. I would highly recommend this game especially if you enjoy Zelda - Breath of the Wild or similar, as you can definitely tell the developers took some leaves out of those pages ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I finished  last month. What I expected to finish in six pleasant hours back in December turned into an unexpected 15-hour journey that I had to turn into chunks of playtime on the weekends. I seriously underestimated this game with regards to the content it can offer me, and now, at the time of writing this, I’m starting to sort of miss it.Now, I never played  (or any  game for that matter), so it might seem odd when I say  reminds me of it. I, however, don’t mean that as a bad thing. In fact, for an indie game, I think that’s a bit impressive.As a game that places emphasis on exploration,  offers you various methods of traversal. You can run, jump, sprint, climb, and as a Glider, you can… well, glide.You also have a super cool hoverbike that initially runs a bit crappy, unless you’re willing to find or buy good parts. What’s cool is the bike is at your beck and call, similar to the steeds in . The interesting catch is if you stray too far away from it, your bike will never show up; you’d have to trek back to its location. Although I’m not a fan of this particular constraint, I understand it’s to encourage players to think about how they travel, the game being exploration-oriented and all.So where  you travel? All around Midden, a place separated into five distinct, sizable regions – all filled with  simple yet fun platforming elements.As you roam the open world, you’ll come across characters that offer you side-quests, most of which are nonlinear. Finishing quests can either earn you badges which you need to craft masks, or reward you with some form of permanent resource boost. The primary goal is the mask collection, which I’ll talk about in a bit.These quests don’t push any annoying time-based challenges of events towards you, showcasing the game’s peaceful nature. However, finding them all can take a while as they’re spread out around Midden. In fact, some of these quests are tucked away specially for players who have an itch for exploration, so finding them in particular is almost as if they were exploratory rewards themselves. So there’s a high chance you might bump into a point of interest or two when and where you’d least expect it.Of course, getting to this point is slow in the beginning, that’s why letting your curiosity take the wheel so you can go places is pertinent. As you progress and explore, the game unveils itself more and more to you.The purpose behind doing any of this has to do with the narrative themes  conveys: Exploration and self-discovery. As a Glider, you set out to work with those you meet, learn about the world, and find the ideals you most connect with. This is where the masks come into play in the narrative.Masks are the final goal of the game. It represents what you want to become by the end of the game. The more masks you collect, the more ‘roles’ you can have as options.When I first started, I felt sceptical, believing I’d make the same decision I was expecting myself to. I was wrong. I changed gears when I reached the end, proving the game’s message right all along.The messaging is sewn right into the game’s experience – from the characters you meet, the backstories you learn about, the intent you carry when doing your quests, and the general experience of exploring the game’s world.In essence, the game is very consistent in showing how it’s more about enjoying the journey and letting the choices simmer in your mind a fair bit rather than simply reaching the destination, picking what you expected to pick, and calling it a day.Now, the game doesn’t come with its set of issues. And boy, there are so many of them.The most obvious ones are the technical issues. Occasionally, weird sounds popped in and out, framerates spiked and dropped, and I came across a gameplay glitch or two that forced me to restart the game. At one point, my hoverbike clipped through some wall. There was no way to recall it, and I was forced to trek back to it, and collide with the part that was sticking out of the wall to dig it out, as if I were Mario nudging a Question Block to get a mushroom. Thankfully, I never ran into any game-breaking issues.Outside of the technical issues, the quest design was fine if you can look past the fact that most of them are fetch quests. It isn’t as bad as the quest design in Rockstar’s games, though, so I won’t complain as much about it.The game’s artistic as well as animation styles are indeed unique, and it has become a favourite of mine. In fact, it’s the main reason why I first wishlisted the game. The animations skip a few frames to resemble the comic art-style we first saw in .However, the visuals themselves do have minor readability issues. I had to tone down the shader outline’s thickness to the absolute minimum, after which the game looked better and ran faster. Go any higher than that setting and the game will look as if you slapped an ‘Extra Bold’ font format on it, which is unappealing on so many levels.Speaking of font formats, the user interface was readable and pleasant to look at. Its minimalist tone matches the game’s ambience. Some elements within the game — such as the GPS system — are extradiegetic, which adds to the immersive experience.The UX is a slightly different story, and the world design is where I highlight the most criticism. When you roam around in the world, you should ideally be able to tell where you are based on certain points of interest around you.Part of what makes  such a wonderful game to roam in is how intuitive it is to understand the world. As the game’s largest structures, the blazing refineries in Gastown act as the player’s ‘north star’ in their travels; always visible, always guiding. The decals play a vital role too. Tire tracks that go in various directions on the road indicate those are paths frequently taken by either Scrotus’ men or other parties. Paths that don’t have these tracks could potentially lead you to rewarding points of interest. All of this helps players absorb the game world’s topography such that they never feel lost in their travels.That was not the same experience I had in ; exploring the world was made difficult because of the lack of good world design.As much as the hoverbike was meant to be the game’s highlight, the one you start out with is quite crappy because you don’t  as much as you do  on the ground. As riding the bike is part of the game’s core loop, you NEED to find some parts if you want to ride fast, save time, and enjoy the experience.The main menu’s UX was rough too. Any form of tactility is rarely present, if not entirely absent. Instead, it feels rigid and unresponsive. It doesn’t match the UI’s smooth vibe. Navigation is a bit confusing to work with when you first begin to explore options to edit Sable’s outfit.Initially, I was going to point out the worst offender: the lack of keybinding options. However, the developers addressed the issue with an update released literally a day after I finished writing this review. So I had to re-edit the review a fair bit during the weekend to reflect that.Look past the technical issues and it's a simple, decent game with a narrative that’s got heart. Got an itch for a small adventure? Give  a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been describing it as a Zelda game without the combat to folks without context. I hope to see DLC content or just more games like it in the future. Sometimes the bikes can tweak out a little while jumping, but overall I haven't encountered many bugs (cept them icky beetles). _childDocuments_.review: Breathtakingly good sound design and fun to play through when you need to relax. The game feels similar to Journey and Gris, it's just you exploring an open world on a bike. Customize your bike, your aesthetic, and enjoy going on different little questlines. There is no combat; the game is really just about exploration, puzzles, and completion so it can feel tedious at times if you're not a completionist.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought Sable, I wasn't really expecting a whole lot. I booted up the game, and immediately I was in love with the visual style. Then I fell in love with everything else about the game.The story is surprisingly deep, and the world genuinely feels ripe with personality. Journeying out into nothing only to stumble upon  was really satisfying. Arriving somewhere new, meeting people, doing tasks really made me feel at home with the places I visited and I even began to miss certain areas and certain NPCs from said areas on my journey.Some of the dialogue in Sable, especially in the ending sequence of the game, hits especially deep. Getting all the masks and listening to Sable's thoughts on each mask the community behind them was really touching, and definitely worth the time spent.The game is a little buggy sometimes, climbing isn't always perfect, it isn't brilliantly optimized (quite a bit of stuttering), and the fishing is rather annoying.The gameplay itself is essentially just glorified fetch quests, but that's not to say it's a bad thing. Each of them felt unique, and I didn't really get tired of running around and doing them either. Sable strikes a fantastic balance of cutting things off at the perfect point before they become annoying.The sense of scale is brilliant, and hovering around the map feels fun and intuitive. Finding something new was always really fun, and it was fantastic to explore structures and unlock secrets.The cosmetics are really fun and offer a decent bit of personalization to Sable. It's a little difficult to find some items of clothing, and I think there could still be a bit more variety.The Bike building aspect is really fun, Simoon evolves with you on your journey, even if finding enough cuts can sometimes be a bit annoying. It really feels like you have to work to upgrade Simoon, and it feels great. I do wish the stats for each bike part weren't a mystery before you bought them, I ended up getting the Nomadic set before any others, and bought the full thing. No other bike parts I found were better until very late game which was a little unlucky I think.Sable is an excellently paced game involving exploration, unique-feeling tasks and quests, awesome personalization, and an absolute ton of personality. Topped off with a beautiful art style, well designed world, and gripping story, Sable really makes you feel like you're part of the world. I would recommend Sable to anyone who enjoys those things.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea how to rate this in it's current state. The game isn't buggy or anything but there's one design choice that really baffels me and can ruin the experience when it happens.I know you were going for immersion here but please make it so that your glider re-spawns in a location near you instead of trying to auto drive to your location when you call it. I'm in a situation I'm miles away from  and my glider is stuck in a rock and when your game map is huge and exploration is the main goal, walking to your destination will become tidious really quickly. No immersion is worth this.I like the look of the game and other things in it, well.. some parts of the art style.. I'm not a big fan of but those aren't deal breakers.Reloading the game won't fix this either. My glider remains where it is.This is a completely fresh experience for me. I can feel the sence of wounder and the game looks gorgous but walking all the way to the things you want to explore kills the joy, you are more like "Finally! I'm here" rather than "Oh! look at this!". So until this is fixed, I can't recommend this. If you don't have your glider stuck.. well... great! this is an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is an atmospheric, engaging game with interesting worldbuilding, puzzles that are just the right level of challenging, and a stunning coming of age narrative set in a unique landscape. Though its charmingly-low-res appearance can occasionally lag and require you to teleport to another point in the landscape to unstick yourself from a glitch, I never encountered any insurmountable setbacks, even as a pretty novice gamer.Sable's ultimate message is that we are not alone as we find our way through the world if we have the courage to take the leap and reach our hands out to friends and strangers alike. There are cool people to talk to and learn from everywhere, and it does you good to go out and meet them. As a person who is eternally distracted by sidequests, a game that was pretty much entirely sidequests was exactly up my alley :)
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that can really transport you somewhere else. Getting lost and exploring the the world was a great experience and I find myself wishing there was more content as I felt I wasn't ready to leave it quite yet.Some framerate and lag issues in some instances but I could overlook it due to the awesome artstyle and overall vibe of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Games a little buggy in areas, but honestly i think the atmosphere, the story, etc can out weigh the buggy-ness of it. and im sure these bugs are easily ironed out by the team soon enough :)been waiting for sable to come out for a few years, and was absolutely outstanded by the result, so much better than what i expected. the graphics of the game are a true masterpiece, the music is beautiful
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is wonderful. But one of the core parts of the game is gliding around the desert and that mechanic is just ridiculously janky. My bike is constantly flipping out as I go over big dunes, one side will dive into the sand at random moments and I'll flop around for fifty feet, or the camera will go haywire for no apparent reason and I'll be looking at the sky all of a sudden. It just breaks all the immersion of the rest of this awesome exploration game. Still, bad optimization, weird audio issues, and jank aside, it's a good experience that could have been amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I do like this game, but there were a lot of bugs for me. For example, sometimes I am stuck on the first text option and can't choose any of the others. Another time the game wouldn't let me switch clothes. Nothing wrong with the visuals, it's a beautiful game. I just wish that it was smoother to play because it's really annoying to have to exit the game and boot it up again so things are temporarily fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable, low-key but very involving game of exploration, puzzle solving, A LOT of climbing on things, and quests. The visual interface and the colors of the environment are spare rather than lush, and there's not a lot of surface detail on most things, but it is all thematically consistent with a desert world. There are a few minor engine glitches, but nothing worth being bothered about unless you insist on climbing on giant statues.Definitely a game worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: decent game, held back from greatness by performance issues and a fairly disappointing story. When I finished it I was like "That felt like a waste of 20 hours" (artificially inflated playtime leaving it on overnight). in hindsight I'd pay about 15 dollars for this gameGreat: world design is cool, Climbing is cool (if not a little anemic), vibe is excellent. Not Great:Story: My main issue, is that this game has identity issues, it's not sure if it wants to be a coming of age journey or a sci-fi archaeology game. The main character is your typical self-doubting hero. I would have loved to see a story where they grow over the course of the journey, using the inner monologue to show how she's growing over time.In reality, there's very little different between her leaving, and returning. She does, however, manage to: Uncover the lore of the world by linking 7 untouched mechanical wrecks, discover ancient artifacts, become genetically superior to other humans by way of worm tears, and learn to harvest the most expensive commodity in the world.why is sable so special? we are never told, it's never justified, and she *barely* grows as a character. Right up to the "ending" she's basically the exact same person, and the only thing that's changed is that she's chosen a job. I think that the archaeology aspects should have been shifted to a "pilgrimage" style so that they could serve the coming of age story better. performance issues: fine most places (rocky/desert) terrible in all others. Google: "Sable performance" for more info
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: You know how sometimes you try to jump over a fence in a game and start climbing it instead? That's how it feels to play . to see if you can tolerate unskippable splash screens, graphical issues, a tiny stamina bar, wonky movement controls, broken starter quests, and re-reading the same unskippable conversations over and over again. I waited too long to try it so now I'm stuck with it, but you've still got a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game really is a product of the time it came out. Copying Breath of the Wild and other games of the sort without the consistency and the quality, just the quantity. Empty open world with climbing that is tied to a stamina meter where it does not belong and truly spoiled the experience. The whole world is empty and, yes that is the point (kinda), it could be 1/4 of it and you would find all the appealing landmarks immediately. I personally love open world games, but do I find them a slog to go through when there is nothing to do.The stamina bar is what makes me hate the game the most. There are areas that you can't climb on. There are angles that you will fall off immediately. So tell me why in the name of all that is holy there is a stamina bar in this game? The story is like Dark Soul's storytelling without the lore or the potential of theory crafting. It is bare bone and at the end of the game, you feel like you accomplished nothing, except finding jigsaw pieces for 16 different puzzles. Don't get me wrong, I like the idea behind it, but the game feels like it is sacrificing it's own ideas to just awkwardly stack what is popular. You can buy it and try it, but I feel like you can just watch a playthrough of it on Youtube and skip the travelling parts and you will get the same enjoyment I had, but with extra time to spare.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a game about exploration. It's a game about finding new and exciting places, history, culture and ultimately yourself. You are a part of the Ibexi clan, a group of masked nomads who travel across a mostly desert world, who have a coming of age ritual called the gliding. When you are of age, you get access to a stone which allows you to glide in mid-air and your own hover-bike and are sent off into the world in a journey of discovery called "the gliding". As you make your journey into the world, you will find out about the world itself, it's mysteries and culture and learn about the different people and roles that they play. But as your journey has a beginning, it also has an end. When the time is right you will return to the Ibexi and choose your final mask, and your role in this world...The story of Sable is told both directly and indirectly through your interactions with the inhabitants of the world, ancient data logs and through the architecture of the world. While I was hoping for a bit more in terms of content the amount of storytelling is fairly solid for a game of this length. There is typically at least one major settlement per region where you can interact with people and learn more about the world, but really this is a game where you ride solo. Think of it as a Team ICO / Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild fusion with the art style of French artist Moebius.After solving most of the game's mysteries it felt right to return to the Ibexi and finish the gliding.This is the most fun I've had in an exploration game for a while. There are two major mechanics in sable which are the gliding stone, which allows you to glide for an indefinite distance, and climbing.The exploration of ruins using climbing and gliding takes up most of the game, with each location, or ruin, having a number of puzzles you'll need to solve in order to get unlock the mysteries of the world, along with some material benefit such as currency, cosmetics, or a collectable. Climbing is fairly intuitive, and most surfaces can be climbed. This is dependent on your stamina bar which can only be increased by visiting a certain location...The hover-bike is used mostly for exploration, and finding new locations. It's very fun to used, but can be a bit fiddly to handle if you're not paying attention to the dunes. This also changes if you're using certain bike parts, as the faster bike parts are useful for travelling long distances, but were far less stable.Customization is a nice part of the game, but not essential. New clothes and bike parts can be found in ruins, or bought from traders. The bike parts offer different stats for your bike but your clothing choices are purely aesthetic. Ultimately neither matter too much, but having a faster bike allows you to get around a bit faster.It took around 12 hours to finish the game, and would probably take a few hours more to collect one of the main collectable items in the game (ie. the chums). For the price point I would definitely say that it's worth it. I binged this in a 2 day period, but it would be easy to break this up and explore the game more slowly over a week.This game definitely has bugs. The main three I encountered were: - Occasional audio stuttering which occurred very sporadically. - Menu glitches, which sometimes made it impossible to navigate the menu using the mouse (though you can use keyboard) and didn't allow you to remove way-points from your map. - Glider calling breaking: Essentially you can whistle to call your hover-bike to you. I had this break once during gameplay and it required a complete restart to fix. The whistle isn't essential, but it's definitely a pain having to walk back to the hover-bike when you're used to it being at your beck and call.This game is absolutely stunning. I'm a huge fan of French artists Shuiten & Peeters as well as Moebius, and this game really captured this art style absolutely perfectly. There were some instances where the draw distance meant that large landmarks suddenly popped up out of nowhere, but that was fairly rare.Playing Sable for the first time felt like I was 10 years old again. I felt a real sense of excitement and adventure going out into the world and exploring with no bounds. While the bugs were noticeable at times, it didn't significantly detract from the experience. After finding all the secrets I could it was cathartic to finally decide to return home and finish the gliding.I would highly recommend this game, and hope that the developers do manage to fix some of the more persistent bugs. Without the bugs, and with even more content (please give me more!), this would easily be a 9/10 or 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to do this, but I just can't recommend a game that's this unfinished, this full of bugs, this much of a polished turd. Before I tear this hunk of unfinished garbage apart, I will say that, when it ran right, it was stunningly pretty, the story was interesting and compelling, and overall, it was an enjoyable game, so long as you can overlook how unfinished and broken it is.Firstly, let's talk performance. I have a decent PC: Ryzen 5 3600x, 32 GB G. Skill Trident-Z Neo RAM running at 3600 MHz, Sapphire Nitro + 57000 XT, and the game runs off an m.2 NVME drive, Samsung Pro 890 or whatever. Nothing of the current gen, but an absolutely rock-solid rig, and one that should be more than capable of playing this low-poly, graphically-not-at-all-intense indy game, smoothly and without any issues, at the "default" settings. And yet, the audio is garbage, sounding like a VoIP phone line suffering extreme packet loss, where the bike's engine sputters and coughs and hiccups, not because something is wrong with the bike, but because the game can't play the engine sound, the environmental sounds, and the music all at the same time without sounding broken. Sable constantly 'disappears' from atop the bike, to where I'm just driving an empty bike - until I dismount, whereupon she re-appears. And if I'm somewhere with more than just a few polygons, like the Dead Forest? I regularly get a huge reminder splayed across the bottom of the screen saying DON'T LOSE YOUR BIKE! You fool, I'm literally riding MY BIKE RIGHT NOW! I could go on. And while these issues are mitigated by turning the quality ALL THE WAY DOWN, they are not resolved, not by a long shot.Let's talk about climbing, a core mechanic of the game, and one that's absolutely necessary to have any hope of completing even just the tutorial level. Sure, most of the time, it's fine. If a wall is vertical, Sable will latch right on and start climbing away (even if the animation is a bit borked; look at that left foot from underneath and compare it to the right while you're climbing up... smh). But if the wall is slightly beyond vertical? Good luck getting started! Of course, no problems if you're already climbing and the wall starts to arch out above you, you'll grip to it like a little gecko no worries. Or how about if the wall is less than vertical? Where you could maybe stand, if you were so inclined? Better get used to constantly trying to both stand and climb, and maybe also trying to jump and fall! It's a lovely animation to get stuck watching while Sable struggles to figure out how to do life. Or what about the random high-up places, like the roof of The Watch, where some of the things that are there actaully aren't there? There are plenty of these seemingly-climbable/interactable set pieces all over the world that just don't actually exist, and Sable just phases right through them. Climbing is a MAIN MECHANIC, and it's so broken it's laughable. I could go on, but I have other broken crap I want to talk about.How about the overall "polished turd" aspect of it all? Do you want to keep a selected quest as the active quest, until you choose otherwise or you complete it? Makes sense, seems reasonable. And in this game, often that's a non-issue. But I had an entire play session, several hours long, where if I interacted with the menu at all, including just pausing the game, it would de-select my active quest, and I would have to make sure to go in and re-select it every time before exiting the menu. Restarting the game fixed it, but WHY WAS THAT A THING THAT WAS HAPPENING IN THE FIRST PLACE?! Or how about this: one of my first indicators as to how little of a crap this developer gave about putting out a finished product was when I first fired the game up and had to select a different screen resolution; every time I would choose a new one, as in I would scroll to the next resolution, not actually choose it and say "I wand to use this one", it would immediately switch to that resolution, and reset the selected menu item to a different one from the resolution, whether it was field of view, antialiasing on or off, etc.. I would have to move the selection back up to the resolution picker and move one more, whereupon the cycle would start all over again. This is indicative of SO MANY other things, so many other little issues that smack of the whole "ehhhh I don't wanna deal with making that behave better, it's good enough, f*ckin' SEND IT!" mentality that this dev seemed to take towards this game.Keep in mind, everything I'm mentioning here is just what I could think of off the top of my head; there is PLENTY I did not touch on, so many broken things I didn't mention here. If you look for other not-recommended reviews out there, you will see many of the other glaring issues this game has, and even with everyone's listed issues, I doubt we've managed to touch on them all. There are a LOT of them. I don't write reviews often, maybe a half dozen in all the years I've been on here, and you have to be extraordinarily excellent, or supremely broken, for me to bother. You can guess where Sable lies. Which...It's a crying shame. This game is, like I said at the beginning, gorgeous, the characters and story are compelling, zipping around on the jetbike (when it's working right) is wonderfully fun, and the exploration aspect of the game is satisfying and largely well-done. But it's such a broken mess... I can't imagine being the dev, spending so much effort, such a large chunk of your life, making a game that one would presume you would care deeply about, only to release it so broken that it made Cyberpunk 2077's release look like a finished product, and leave it foundering still, 16 months later. It's shameful. I'm glad I bought it on sale. I wish I'd pirated it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a slow burn of a game.  There’s really no specific storyline or campaign.  It’s basically a lot of little campaigns in a huge open world.  The game is all about chill relaxing and exploration.  No combat, and there isn’t any voice dialogue, just bubble texts, but they are entertaining and informative.  I would only get this on sale, because of one big drawback.  The performance.  The lack of optimization of this game is very bad.  I tried it out on the Xbox Series S, my own gaming PC, and the Steam Deck.  And all of them confirmed that the game needs serious patches, which I doubt we’ll ever come.  However, if you can ignore that, the game can be quite fun.  I highly recommend visiting this website on the 7 things you should know before starting the game:  Helpful tips, like how and where to increase your stamina, and make sure to buy maps, and use markers on the maps, or you’re going to get lost.  And don’t forget about the Fast Travel mechanic on the maps.  It’s a time saver for this huge world.  I also recommend collecting all the rings and finding the mysterious shrine in the Badlands, if you do you will eventually receive what I consider the best reward of the game.  I do hope the developers do a sequel, and fix all the problems the first game has.  The artstyle, and the music were very cool and relaxing, the rest of the game just needs more polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen a number of negative reviews about this game, which in my opinion are slightly missing the point... TL;DR - get over it, this is a different kind of game!This is a game of exploration, finding your character's purpose and style, interacting with other characters and doing "quests" for them. No combat, no death, no health bar... just chillin' in some gorgeous visuals in an intriguing world. I love this game as a total change of pace - no "twitch shooting" (indeed, no shooting :D ), still some challenging (but not too taxing) platforming, some light RPG (outfits and the vehicle can be modified cosmetically and upgraded a little).Some criticism centres around the bugs. There are some, certainly, but some of the comments about stuttering animation may again have missed the point - the style is reminiscent of anime and the animation gives that feeling that you are part of an interactive animated movie, not a game - it's part of the style.Yes, the bike does get stuck in the scenery sometimes (particularly if you ride it up high and then save/reload, it's under the surface). Seems a bit of a downer, but here's a workaround: go to your nearest Machinist and ask to customise your bike. It will miraculously reappear in the workshop area. This may involve quite a bit of running to get to the right character, but it saves having to reload an earlier save or starting again.Love it, embrace it, accept that it's two guys developing this. and enjoy the ride.
