_childDocuments_.review: A journey it was. And oh boy, what a journey. I rarely write reviews for games. But for Sable... I had to write one. And I really, by heart, wanted to write one. Talking about "playing" Sable would not do the game justice. Even labeling it as "a game" would not do it justice. Sable is a piece of art. An experience. And a magnificent one as well. From the brilliantly written dialogue to the heartwarming characters up to its vast world. A world such artfully crafted, that even its emptiness is detailed, enriching the atmosphere rather than feeling like something is missing. Everything feels like a significant part of this whole journey.Sable resembles a puzzle in which every piece is crafted in such a detailed and lovely way that putting all of them together creates a beautiful image filled with passion. And I do know that it has its imperfections, but they were not able to keep me from experiencing this game. There are plenty of games in which even smaller flaws would have kept me from further progressing and playing the game. But something about Sable, its world, and its characters, was of such magical nature that I just could not stop playing. Progressing through this adventure, I took my time as I really did not want this journey to end. Even after reaching a point where I could have just ended my odyssey, I still took my time to either complete and enjoy the few quests that were left, or roam around the world one last time.This is especially noteworthy as I began this journey at a time when I lacked the motivation to engage in games that were meant to keep me occupied for a long period. So, I mostly relied on playing through a few indie games that had playtimes of three to four hours, which seemed perfect for my situation. But in Sable, I lost myself.This project is a beautifully crafted piece of art, which is not only gorgeous to look at, but also magnificent to witness. And it really accompanied me through a time where the overall stress in private life seemed so overwhelming that I lacked the motivation to engage in one of my hobbies for a longer period of time. The real beauty of the game lies in its individuality of experience. What for me was Sable will for you be something entirely different. My journey through its world, seen through the light of my eyes, will differ from what you perceive with yours. Elements I felt a deep connection to may not resonate with you in the same way, and vice versa. What intensified my immersion in this experience might differ from what captures your imagination and draws you in. My Sable is not your Sable, and your Sable is not my Sable. You may perceive a completely different game, as it is not about traversing a linear path but about embarking on a broad and personal journey that I am happy to have experienced. In Sable, I lost myself and in Sable, I found myself.Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/13/22 EDIT: I changed my recommendation to no. I personally still like it and I'm going to finish the game, but the lag and glitching definitely gets worse the further in you go (Hakoa in particular runs *horribly* and looks half-baked at best). The game has been out for 6 months at the time of writing this. The grace period for that kind of leniency has passed.---Sable is an amazing game with a few minor (though admittedly glaring) issues.If I had to describe Sable in a sentence, it would be: "Breath of the Wild for pacifists." While a lot of the gameplay is similar to BotW in terms of gamplay loops, world design, questing, etc., combat, one of the main aspects of BotW, is completely absent from Sable. There is no health bar and you cannot die. Without spoiling too much, there's also no great evil you're working towards defeating- it is purely a game about exploration and self discovery. That lack of conflict may make it seem like a boring game at first glance, but on the contrary, Sable manages to take this as an opportunity to refine its gameplay and make the elements it does focus on deeper than BotW. In short, it is a more focused game of smaller scope.First, the good:- Atmospheric soundtrack. The game includes multiple fully voiced songs as well as amazing ambiance for all the locations you visit. Said ambiance may not be comprised of "bangers" or be entirely memorable, but it definitely helps set the mood and immerse yourself in the game world- Speaking of, Sable is one of the most immersive open world experiences I think I've had in quite a while. A lot of the navigation is skeuomorphic in nature, contextualizing the tools you have with the tools the character has at their disposal: You cannot view the map until you buy said map from the mapmaker of the region you're in, and there is no minimap- instead, you mark waypoints in-game instead of on the map screen based on what you can see in the distance and then head there with a handy tool that shows you a compass and the general direction waypoints are located relative to you. This keeps the player from staring at their minimap while also providing user-friendly navigation if needed. There is still fast travel, but considering how big the game world is and the need to return to old locations occasionally, I consider this a necessary evil. The UI is also hidden by default (you need to hold a button to display it) and even then it's extremely minimalistic, meaning most of your time will be spent actually looking at and interacting with the game instead of at menu screens- Tons of customization options. You can trick your hoverbike out with a variety of different parts that you purchase from shops, and you can even dye it different colors using color dye sets found scattered in chests around the world. Clothes, too, can be purchased from various shops or found hidden across the world, and they are designed to be mixable to a certain degree, allowing you to express yourself more freely (I do think it would be nice if you could dye clothes as well though!)- True freedom. The game has a linear tutorial section, but once that's done, the guard rails are off. The game of course does have a recommended course you can follow- one questline leads to a new town and one of the questlines in that town leads to another, etc.- however you are never railroaded onto a "main story" questline and you absolutely have the freedom to visit all the areas in whichever order you want. The game's narrative is one of self discovery, and they put their money where their mouth is by letting you tackle things in any order you please.- Fun writing. This one is more subjective, but I find a lot of the characters, especially the main character, to be very witty and charming in a wholesome way. The game makes some quips but they're never truly mean and there is always a positive message at the bottom of it all.- A variety of options. You can freely change the contrast of the colors to your liking as well as the thickness of the lines until the game looks how you like.Alas, even with a game is great as Sable, there are a few issues which detract from the experience sometimes:- Performance issues. While it has been improved vastly from the demo, performance leaves something to be desired. Zineth (another game I'd recommend if you like this artstyle) was made in 2012 with comparable environment sizes and a similar artstyle to Sable and it ran much smoother all the way back then. My computer is getting to be on the older side but still has a respectable graphics card and Sable still manages to tank the framerate momentarily in bigger areas.- Barren environments. While there is a lot to do, sometimes you can really feel that this was made by a small team. There are a lot of stretches of empty desert that are quite frankly copy and paste or randomly generated with absolutely nothing to do or see in them. It makes sense, seeing as it's a desert, but I feel like they could have done something a bit more to not make these stretches of the game so mind-numbing, especially considering the game is 20+ hours long by my current estimations.- Minor bugs. These are bugs that on their own don't ruin the experience, but can add up to detract from your immersion. Cameras sometimes not panning properly during cutscenes, your bike's recall pathing messing up, some dialogue boxes not being formatted properly, plant leaves glitching out due to buggy wind, some treasure chests not opening, etc.- Sound clipping. This is a big one. When entering areas that take lots of processing power, the sound has a tendency to clip in and out. It doesn't happen all the time, but when it does it's seriously annoying.All in all, Sable is a great experience and you should get a decent amount of time out of it, but I'd recommend keeping in mind that it is, at the end of the day, a game made by a smaller team, and that shows through in places. It's also a very zen style game, and if you go into it playing it like a regular game then you might be disappointed. For those undeterred by these warnings, however, it is a truly unique experience that shows sometimes all the motivation you need is a little curiosity.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, and wish I could generally recommend it. The vibe, the music, the art, and the writing are all so delightful. It just pains me that there are so many parts of the game that seem unfinished or don't work. It manages to create such awe inspiring moments of wonder, scale, and loneliness. Flying the glider is kind of terrible. As soon as you catch a jump/air it just goes bonkers and rolls terribly, clipping through geometry. It ruins any mood, sense of calm or vibe that you have going. For something so critical to the game it is surprising that the vehicle controls and acts so erratically.Also, your glider is constantly getting stuck and can't reach you. Sometimes it actually just embeds itself and gets stuck in a rock or the ground. Also, even though I'm riding my bike I keep getting warnings not to lose my bike.The stamina meter is super hard to read against so many surfaces in the game.Also it stutters no matter what resolution I put it at. I have a Ryzen 5000 and RTX 3070. There's zero reason why it should perform so poorly.The camera is always passing through walls which breaks the immersionIf these things weren't issues I would give it an unqualified recommendation, but as it stands I feel the game is working against itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the vibe of this game, encouraged me to take it slow and chill. I got to see some really interesting environments and solve some great climbing puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: i want this game to be good but there are a lot of bugs and terrible qualities of life. i love the art style of this game, it is great. there could be improvements but overall i like what it's going for. other than that literally everything else has bugs, and even the graphics have it's downsides at times.cons and bugs:frequently bumping into random rocks/weird generated land sending me flying and spinning. why? i get that the first hoverbike is junk so i get why on that one, but why all of them? make a separate floor for the hover bike or create a condition to ignore the little pebbles and rocksweirdly restrained shop mechanics. i ventured out after the main story kinda gets vague and visited every cartographer only for them to sell nothing. only after i completed the mystery of who stole the core at eccetric city did every cartographer start selling their maps. and that quest is super ambiguous, im pretty sure you could accuse any one of the suspects and still get the same result.after like 4 hours my hover bike bugged when trying to call it and after that through out the session the hoverbike would just do nothing when i would call it, even if i was 10 feet away.calling the hover bike when it works, doesnt have a great pathing so it ends up just flying further away from you if there's an obstacle it can't climb up in the way. which is often cause the terrain is pretty extremethe graphics are great but when it is "dark" there are literally no colors. i would prefer if the colors were just slightly less saturated, or if there was better lighting like putting torches or other light sources like the crystals in the dungeons so i can see the color of the objects instead of majority of my play time in caves or dungeons or temples with no torches i have no color. LET ME ENJOY THE ART YOU CREATED.Pros:i love the art. when there is light or when you are inside the spaceships the color and the style and the weird mix of animation on 2's and 60 fps simulated capes is very interesting and im enjoying looking at it (probably because i liked spiderman into the spiderverse)the gameplay is very similar to zelda, including large blocks pushing and retracting in a regular pattern to launch character and puzzle object inorder to solve puzzles.i do like the landscape visually. its a damn shame the vehicle can't roam across it fluidly. i love seeing the horizons and the general landscape and how it is artistically built. exploring it is a big pain in the ass. i constantly find myself flipping and barrel rolling with out intention, and i find myself using the fast travel system more than i want to because traveling is just a pain.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's totally overrated.The camera is super wonky and jumps randomly, climbing is janky, the performance is a joke, the world is too big and empty, there are very little rewards for exploration, your vehicles pathfinding ist really bad (if it even trys) and it handles horrible; driving, running and especially (!) swimming are too slow; most quests are boring fetch quests, my cursor sometimes disappears in the menu, the map menu is pure terror, the dialogues are strangely written, clothing has no impact on the gameplay, new vehicle parts have far too little impact on the gameplay (to be fair: the last and most expensive vehicle parts feel really good to play with). _childDocuments_.review: Despite some of the minor bugs I've encountered, Sable is a wonderful game and I'm happy I got it as a Christmas present.I took my time, completed every achievement, and found over 110 chum eggs before the end just by exploring the world and completing its quests. This game rewards you for being curious, and the way it directs you towards things feels intuitive. If you think there's something around the corner when you're being directed the other way, there just might be.I love the connections Sable makes with people and the secrets she uncovers about the past. Puzzles to uncover this lore were not difficult or too simple.Returning to the Ibex camp, I was almost sad since the journey was over, but everything in Sable feels like it has a purpose and Sable found hers.The bugs I encountered were not game-breaking, but some more annoying than others:- Audio issues: Cutting in and out. Random machine noises after teleporting or just driving in the desert- The bike does not move sometimes when called even though it responds- Sable getting stuck in a loop climbing an edge (jumping or pushing forward fixes it)- When starting the game, the framerate is capped to 30 unless changed to another option- When starting the game, my mask gets set to the first one in my inventory- I found a single floating cache I could not interact with in the WhaleIf you love exploring, discovering secrets, or following a story at your own pace then you should give Sable a shot. _childDocuments_.review: Sable is one of the best games I've played in the last five years, and an experience I think many people will enjoy. An immersive world, calm and relaxing gameplay, plenty of mysteries to discover, and a satisfying narrative arc all make up a wonderful debut game from Shedworks.That being said, I understand where some of the negative reviews are coming from. Sable is so good that the few flaws it does have -- mostly in the menus, text-box prompts, and occasional sound design flaws -- stand out very much. These are discussed below.That being said, I am impressed by how few glitches there were in a game this size made with this small of a team.I am only leaving these comments because I hope Shedworks takes them into consideration and can repair them for future releases.Still: the sound design, soundtrack, dialogue, and exploration are all so satisfying that I think most people will love this game, as long as they don't expect triple-A polish. There were so many impressive narrative moments and stunning sights, and the gameplay felt very fresh almost throughout the entire 20 hours. All in all, 9/10. I look forward to Shedworks' next release.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a really lovely, interesting game. The art, music, and writing all work excellently together to create an incredible (and incredibly unique) atmosphere. While the game can be cleaned up in a few places, I still highly recommend it.Sable has incredible aesthetics. Each area has a unique aesthetic, each including its own color palette and central elements. You have the ability to customize your hoverbike and your own outfit. The hovebike's customization is more in-depth, allowing both the swapping of pieces as well as colors. Each hoverbike piece has its own stats for moving, and these are locked to the aesthetic pieces, which means that, should you want certain stats, you have to stick with certain sets. However, there are lots of high-level bike sets with minimal stat differences (I didn't notice much difference) and you can pick between many nice aesthetics at this higher level. Your clothing is more "locked": as far as I can tell, you can't change the color of any piece, but it also doesn't provide any mechanical function to you, despite some implications in the writing elsewhere.The gameplay is, by and large, really lovely. I dedicate a lot of time, money, and attention into gaming, but I've never been good at almost any aspect of gaming—I found that the level of difficulty was right for me. Sable is more about an experience than a challenge, and the puzzles are never mind-wracking. I haven't seen any complaints about this, so I'm assuming that, even for more "hardcore" gamers, this hasn't felt bothersome. In my case, it felt right for the comfortable, exploration-based goals Sable seems to have. Hyper-challenging puzzles wouldn't be right for this game.Characters are nice to talk to. No one character has a special focus. The characters also have a nice level of depth, and many have smaller stories, but the focus is on communities or larger stories. I really liked this and felt it was well-balanced: again, Sable doesn't feel like the kind of game that would benefit by creating really complex characters. It's more about the journey.Many of the critiques of this game in the other reviews focus on potential glitchiness or mouse deceleration. While these are issues, I found them both to be minor; they largely didn't detract from my experience (I honestly though the deceleration was intentional, and I never really was bothered by it). There were a few other things I did care about. I'd agree with some other reviewers that parts of the landscape felt too empty. This was especially true of the Sodic Wastes and parts of the Badlands, which, despite the latter being very small, both felt unrewarding to explore, especially when compared to Eccria and Burnt Oak Station, which were early-mid game for me.Related to that, there were also some things that felt un- or underdeveloped or poorly explained. Some of the collectibles and economic elements felt odd. I only realized in mid-late game that you could sell things back to the merchants. As a result of this, I only got many of the bike parts mid-late game, and never really got the chance to use them at all. However, I'm not sure if it would have helped if I had discovered the ability to sell items earlier, as it's really unclear what and when you'll need things for. I spent much of the game wondering if there was a hidden cooking mechanic I was missing, as there's a massive amount of food items you can collect in your inventory, only one of which I can really think of a use for in the game, and it's only used once (with an alternate solution possible). That food item, too, is , not found. As it turns out, it seems most of the food items are intended to just be sold, but that's never really made clear. I can imagine many players hoarding them for no good reason.Once you do find out that items can be sold and find even one or two good, renewable sources of sellable items, money quickly becomes a non-issue. This ended up with me being in two weird stages of the game: early to the middle of mid game where I felt weirdly un-monied, and then the second half of mid game to late game where things felt like they were progressing too-fast because I was finding the solution to all of the puzzles and able to buy anything I wanted (which, to be fair, money doesn't really buy you solutions to puzzles or quests in this game very much at all—just convenience and style). I don't know the exact solutions because I'm not a game dev, but I do feel even a few small fixes could help this problem, even if they wouldn't solve it: some sort of early pointer to the ability to sell items would be great, as well as some way of better being able to track which items are useful or not useful (or at least a way to log where you found specific items so you don't have to fear accidentally losing something that you don't remember where you got) would both be useful. I'd also love something more to do with food you get, but that'd be an entire new game mechanic.I'm also a little disappointed with the fast-travel. It works fine, but there's no clear hint towards it existing by anyone or anything at all until you hover over a landmark and discover it on accident. This is thankfully quite easy, but it's significant enough that it feels it should be explained. It also feels like it should be more earned, or at least more consistent in how it's earned. Right now, you unlock fast-travel by simply going to a location, but not all locations you expect to have fast travel do (this is one thing that made the badlands feel miserable), some that probably don't need fast travel have it (a few ships and such), and sometimes you have to go to a weirdly specific place to get the fast travel unlocked (there's a few ships where you have to get pretty deep to unlock fast travel despite having no real reason to go there after unlocking it, and a few vertical movement centric locations that make you go high up to unlock fast travel despite, again, rarely having a reason to return). While I'm also generally not too upset with fast travel being so easy to unlock, it did feel a bit odd: this game is so exploration centered that being able to teleport anywhere feels a bit like I'm skipping some of the best parts of the game, although it is currently a necessity to some degree with how big the map is. I think the solution is making it a more intentional part of the game to unlock fast travel: maybe you have to do a small quest, visit the cartographer and/or buy the map for a region, or find a special NPC. None of this is a neccessity, but I think it would help round out the game more.Alright, that's all—although this critique section is long, I really, really enjoy the game. My main points were a few areas that could be improved, but I still think it's highly worth playing and deserves far more attention, as it's lovely and broadly very well designed. Would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: ...you will love it or you'll hate it. For me, it's easily one of the best games I've ever played. Where else do you have truly open-world exploration—go where you want, when you want—non-linear quests, zero combat and zero harm, yet a believable and relevant backstory, with great writing in an immersive environment, all with captivating graphics and amazing sounds? Your female protagonist can run, walk, climb, scramble, crawl, sit, swim, jump, glide—oh, and fall!—and she can ride a customizable hover bike. Sable's setting is in an alien world, but it's not pure fantasy as the most important problems that she has to solve, and the decisions she has to make, are the same ordinary but life-shaping ones most of us have to face in the real world.  Some people have technical problems with the game. There are bugs, true, though far less now than there were on initial release. With a truly open-world game it's hard for developers to anticipate everything. And I have no real performance issues, I suppose because I have a reasonable system, albeit one that's now 6 years old. Plus I spent many years heavily involved in the virtual world of Second Life, so some of the graphical glitches I encounter in Sable I just shrug off by comparison. This game is very relaxing, and you can always take it at your own pace. BUT I found that it sometimes triggered my acrophobia. If you are climbing to great heights and clinging precariously to sheer, windswept surfaces, the graphics and the sounds are so good you really feel you are there and in peril—this despite that no harm can come to Sable and that she can always glide to safety. I just took breaks before coming back for more! I strongly recommend Sable. I think it's good value for money. But if you are in any doubt, wait for an offer, and explore any potential technical issues quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: - The game looks fantastic. You can screenshot practically any moment and it'll look great- I'm legitimately impressed with how diverse they made a desert wasteland feel. Gliding into the blinding Sodic Wastes for the first time wowed me, as did the petrified forest of The Wash and the black sands of Hakoa. The best location is probably The Whale, though.- Unfortunately, it doesn't look so good in motion on Steam Deck. It was a bit framey regardless of settings- The music is fairly nice. I enjoyed the vocal tracks, but the environmental music was forgettable- The plot is a very simple coming-of-age tale. The backstory is 3/4 Children of Time and 1/4 Horizon Zero Dawn- It's hard to highlight individual quirks in characters when everyone wears occupational masks and there's no voice acting. Because of this, none of the side characters really resonated- Like any open world game, there's also side quests. Some of them are pretty entertaining (most of the Eccria quests), but others felt like chores (anything involving beetles)- The best parts of the game are the vibes you get from exploring, not the story- The gameplay is bog-standard open-world fare- The high points of the gameplay are your traversal options. The main one is your hoverbike. Unfortunately, even the best parts in the game don't allow it to handle much better than the Scooty Puff Jr. from the tutorial- The bouldering and hovering mechanics are much more fun. Each cliffside and sheer wall has you scanning the environment for clues on how to top it. These mechanics make exploration a blast- Unfortunately, your stamina (used for running and climbing) is tied to a collectathon quest for upgrades- I feel like this game sacrificed a bit of substance for style. I imagine that balancing these things is difficult for indie devs, but feel like better writing or a more inspired plot could have taken the game to another level- As mentioned before, it was very choppy on the Steam Deck. It played much better on PC- I'm used to bugs in my open world games, but there were a lot of issues. Summoning my bike would often leave it stuck on the environment, you can cheat climbing sometimes by running diagonally, and so many NPCs in every location were running into geometry- The camera is also a struggle in any place with low ceilings- . Without the bugs and camera struggles, this would be one of my favorite games. However, because of those flaws, it's hard to overlook the bland story and bog-standard gameplay. It's still a fun world to explore as-is, though

_childDocuments_.review: The developers have released a second patch, but have yet to release any patch notes. Framerates seem to be a bit more stable, but visual and audio stutter issues persist. After testing with keyboard and mouse, it seems that the player can't even call their hoverbike as there is no keybind for it. This is a nice game, but still needs a bit of work to get into a playable state. The developers have responded to the numerous bug reports and discussion threads here on Steam and have stated that they are actively working to push a patch that will focus on some of the more severe issues.Unfortunately, I cannot recommend Sable. Here's why:This game makes me motion sick. That's probably due to the tearing, stutter and shimmering. If I take a break and do something else, my motion sickness goes away after about ten minutes.While the visuals are neat and the world is interesting, I cannot recommend this game due to the numerous bugs I've encountered. Some of these bugs weren't even an issue in the demo, yet somehow they are now present. Sable should not have released in its current state.Hopefully these issues will be fixed, but hold off on buying for now and be wary of any glowing reviews, especially those from individuals who have received the game for free, that don't state these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Following many of the negative reviews I have read before posting, I played most of Sable with strange audio clipping in the music, glitchy menu interfaces, clunky climbing mechanics, and the game auto-equipping the ugly Cartographer Mask every time I loaded my save.But 16 hours later, none of those issues came close to eclipsing the fun I had playing through this game. Sable does an incredible job of inviting you to explore. Instead of viewing the strange, buggy-feeling climbing system as a mistake to be patched, I believe it should be embraced as a core feature of the fun of the game. Only then can one recognize how well Sable has captured the illegal joy of feeling like you've glitched your way to the top of a seemingly unreachable peak only to be met with a considered collectible once you're up there. Without fear, Sable welcomes awkward, oblique approaches to verticality.Admittedly, though I loved the writing it mostly went in one ear and out the other. The joy for me was in the spaces in between quests. I personally like the hoverbike controls and the violent (but inconsequential) effects a small pebble has on your ride. If you choose to hate on the driving without having ramped off of a dune then ejecting to launch yourself up a cliff, I think you have passed a wonderful opportunity by.I was very impressed with Sable and of course I hope patches fix obvious audio and interface issues, but they could never be enough to stop me from weaselling my way forever up, up, up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I took a vacation in the real world, but Sable feels like a lot of the things I look for when I go traveling. The beauty of each unique environment (from color palette to geological features to flora and fauna) is a sight to behold, and the breezy flow of traveling on your hoverbike as the music gently sets the scene. The relaxed, go-anywhere pacing of the open world lets you set the agenda without fear of missing out or running out of time, and be as focused or haphazard in exploring and interacting with the world as you choose to be. The lack of combat informs the tone of your character's interactions with the people of the land, and you feel more like a part of the community when you're solving problems other than "kill # monsters." The protagonist's arc is a classic coming-of-age story, and the final choice you make determines what sort of person you've decided to become in a satisfying way. But more than anything, the game is beautiful. Screenshots don't do it justice, you need to see the way it moves for yourself.

Usually I can't even see any of the buy/sell items, which after a 15-20 minute climb around some monolith to get to a shopkeeper, just kills any desire to play.-Calling of the hover bike usually results in the bike getting stuck on something and unable to make it to you, even if you're in the middle of open sand.I want to like this game, and I suspect with a lot of bugs being fixed I will come back to it, but it just ends up being a battle against multiple problems to attempt to enjoy the game. _childDocuments_.review: There is so much that I thought to say about this game while playing, so many moments of complete joy and fun while being completely surrounded by its alien world. There are so many amazing things to say, but in the end, I will put it more simply...Despite 'Sable' being imperfect, it is beautifully imperfect, just as we all are. It is now among one of the greatest video games, even art of any sort, that I have experienced in my life. This game grabbed me, held me, and has left me in a position where I feel that I will be thinking about it for years to come, and perhaps the rest of my life. The impact it had on me was fascinating. As a somewhat fussy gamer who often doesn't stick with games or feel driven to continue unless it has Dark Souls combat, this one cradled me and absorbed me until it filled me completely. I had a feeling I would like it, but I had no idea just how much.I will say nothing more, and will leave the experience up to the player who reads this. But if you want my advice, play this game. It is one of few 10/10 games on this Earth.

_childDocuments_.review: I de-wishlisted this game after reading about the framerate issues and bugs, but a friend encouraged me to play it regardless and I am so glad they did.Sable is immersive, beautiful, and has taught me that I actually really dig exploration games. There is a magic to Sable, in both what it omits and details, but at it's core it is about discovering who you are and that span of time in our youth where we try to piece together possibilities - or don't. This is the type of game where you turn it on and you sincerely don't know what you're going to end up doing that session, and that's part of the fun.I played it on SteamDeck. I experienced framerate issues, especially after extensive play. I also experienced quest items that were unselectable and had to eventually learn that some NPCs randomly don't have a talk marker over their heads, but you can still talk to them nonetheless. For me these issues were fixed by exiting to the title screen and reloading.

_childDocuments_.review: To start with, this game is very glitchy in its current state. If you can't deal with unstable framerate and texture pop-in, consider this a negative. But if you can, this is a beautiful and interesting open world to explore, with a lot of the same gameplay themes as Breath of the Wild but without the combat (which was frankly often a chore for me after a point). If you played BOTW and your favorite part was climbing up tall things, seeing something cool on the horizon, and heading off to explore, this is 100% for you.Special mention to the gorgeous art style, which looks like a living comic book. The way the color palette changes through the day cycle is incredible. If the game gets a technical spruce up to match its art and world building, it'll have my strongest recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A touch on the buggy side, but beautiful and heartfelt.Commence vague blathering.There is no looming disaster, no gaudy villain, not even a time limit, and that's sort of the point in-game and out. The world is beautiful and mysterious, there is so much that at once makes total sense with all you have seen before and yet still begs a million questions. A history broken but not altogether lost, and I wish I could dig deeper, get the answers, understand more deeply, but... I think one of the lessons is that you won't always get that. Or even CAN get that, you need to let go.The ending, losing "that", I think I actually cried. Blathering over.

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game since i saw a gif on twitter, and the art style immediately piqued my interest.The game features a one-of-a-kind Moebius inspired artstyle and it looks great.The music is mysterious, ambient and soothing.Its mechanics and gameplay are fairly simple, don't expect any depth here. It's all about exploration and "how do i get over there" and it serves the game well enough. Some issues with the climbing mechanics exist, but they are not particularly egregious, in my opinion.Here come the bad stuff:  •  Stuttering. Constant stuttering, low fps, low GPU utilization. It just plagues this game.When i played the demo, it ran just fine. But the final product will leave you dizzy. (The recent patch seemed to have alleviated these issues, but in certain areas, and when traversing on the hoverbike, the issues persist)  •  Audio issues. There are numerous issues with the audio of this game. Constant stuttering of the audio, whether it's the sound of your hoverbike, your footsteps, or everything else. Random, high volume mechanical noises happening out of nowhere for no reason.  •  The UI and Menu are very buggy, as if the mouse and keyboard are constantly fighting. Sometimes you might select an option you din't intend to. Other times you will try to mark something on the map and you will place like 5 markers in the same spot(because you clicked instead of pressing E). Random compass markers that are invisible on the map and have stayed there during my entire playthrough. The currency counter refusing to fade, and having to restart the game.  •  Not being able to change keybinds at all. Overall, i don't think the game should have been released in this state. They should have at least waited to iron out a few of these issues before they went with a full release. Or at the very least, release as Early Access, so that people know what they are getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Sable Devs,As a hardcore Moebius fan I'd say you did the man proud. Did you ever see a documentary where Moebius met Miyazaki? Their admiration for each other was unmissable. I reckon that had Moebius been alive and visited your shop we'd have seen something similar. Seriously - you've done very, very well.Small points: any chance the smoke could be made transparent? That solid black is, for mine, the only weak point in the visuals; further, if you could smooth out the glider dynamics I'd appreciate it - I find it a bit bumpy / crashy at the moment; finally, Mobius drew beautiful faces. I understand your use of masks did away with a entire swathe of trouble and angst but one does like to see a person's face (it's the nature of being human) so fingers crossed you have the resources to make that happen next time. As for bugs, with the new release I didn't have any.Speaking of next time, I'd happily pay for a Sable 2. Beauty, serenity, joy - more please. But if you're over it and want to do something else I look forward to it.Sable - 9.5 out of 10. Sublime.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed relaxing with this game. You glide across the sand dunes on a spiritual coming-of-age adventure, solving little missions to help others out along the way.At its core, it's a platformer driven by a bunch of side quests with pretty simple puzzles. But the music, atmosphere, art style, and story all come together to make this a pretty feel-good, chill game.I'd launch it up, explore, chill to the music by Japanese Breakfast, and eventually stumble upon a quest or just a puzzle segment to work through. No pressure, no failures, no restarts. And when I decided I was done with the game, I just went back to my start village and told them I was ready to end my Gliding, and performed the ending ritual.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game runs like silk post patch and is an easy 10/10. Turn up high visibility or whatever they call it, crank the field of view out and everything opens up. The world building is expansive and engaging. The dialog is superb, the atmosphere is very relaxing, and the music is simply put perfect. The puzzles are fun, feel pretty fresh, and has so far never felt tedious. The bike somewhat fun and customizing it has you looking for cuts everywhere. There is a lot of foreshadowing for stuff to come that never materializes, and I hope that it gets added in DLC. The game is also very evocative and emotional. The presentation works and the dialog options usually feel like they make a difference, even if they probably do not. This whole game is a mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game has scratched a particular itch I was unaware I had. A very relaxing setting, where the simple act of exploring is the experience and the reward. Its actually made me retook at a lot of games wishing it was possible to just.......... wander.Personally have not experienced any of the bugs and issues that many have documented in their own reviews, however that does not mean said bugs are not a thing and I would recommend looking into the bugs to see if you would personally find it worth it.If your fine with that however, then I cannot recommend this game any higher, especially if you are looking for a nice chill time
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice experience unfortunately undercut by rushed and unpolished development, lots & lots of bugs and glitches appear in every place you could possibly think of (bad performance; misspellings; broken menus, entity interactions, music, climbing, and more).Very much an indicator that the size of the project was much bigger than they could really handle; writing, character development and story suffer because of this too. Even if the world is truly a beauty to look at and explore you get the feeling that every story and npc interaction could have been written to have a much stronger impact on you as the player and your character.Still I have to recommend it, yeah absolutely the game would have benefited from an extra year of polishing and it is simply a crime that it remains as broken as it is, but what you get out of it is still great, dancing through the wasteland and seeing incredible sights is the one thing the game got really right, and makes it worth it for that reason alone.Avoiding quests and just running around for the first couple hours conveyed a feeling I hadn't felt in a long time, that feeling of being lost inside a world and discovering parts of it little by little, which is very hard to capture in a game and even more in today's games which cannot stop holding your hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't get very far into the game, and in my 23 minutes of playing I experienced weird technical issues with movement. Character would get stuck or rigid in certain area's when climbing or running, and npcs would spaz out in the background. After completing the first fetch quest, I was than told to fetch 3 more items so I could complete my bike. I proceeded to fetch the Refund page and uninstall the game so I could complete my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a cozy adventure game that's basically a smaller scale Zelda Breath of the Wild minus the combat and set entirely on a Dune-like world. The game is about exploring and trying to figure out where you belong in the world, and overall I think the game does what it sets out to do really well and I really enjoyed it.8/10*I will note that the 1.0 version is FULL of bugs, and I had to restart the game basically every time I sat down to play. A lot of them are UI/UX based (like all the menus randomly ceasing to work, or adding a map marker actually adds 5), but there are also plenty of audio bugs like screeching sounds randomly happening or gameplay bugs like falling through solid ground. Basically, I think they launched the game a bit too early, and I would suggest waiting till the team patches the current problems
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt my favorite game. I wish there were more combat-free exploration games like this out there!The art is gorgeous, colorful and lush night or day and never visually overwhelming. I love wandering the Midden on my hoverbike and taking in the scenery. The open-world is fun to explore and truly open: aside from the opening in the Ewer, nothing has to be done in a specific, linear order. You can explore as much or as little as you like and you don't have to complete everything to enjoy the game.This is a game about taking time to explore and reflect without combat or violence. It is a story of growing up and finding your way. The soundtrack is beautiful and immersive, and sometimes as quirky as the game itself.This is my go-to chill game and I recommend it to anyone who likes the freedom of exploring open worlds without fighting or dying and and very little hand-holding from the game. As someone who doesn't excel at, or enjoy, platforming, the climbing and jumping were (for the most prat) all fun and accessible with sufficient stamina upgrades.Highlights of the game are:- climbing and floating- exploring 7 different desert regions- desert fishing in the sand!- collecting butterflies, plants, and bugs- riding and customizing your hoverbike, earning new bike parts- earning/collecting/buying new clothes- quests of varying lengths/layers to earn badges which upgrade to masks- a varied cast of characters to meet- puzzles in abandoned space ships to explore and complete- hoverbike speed/racing challenges- adorable chums!Occasional glitches are there and easy to overlook in the pure joy of the game. I saved early and often and fast traveled out of the spots where I got stuck and was just fine!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Give it a solid 8 soft 9. Beautiful score done by Japanese Breakfast. Art style is fantastic and I found my jaw dropping at times due to the sheer majesty of some of the set pieces. Writing is also great. I found myself running around trying to find more people to talk to, not only for new things to do but just to hear what funny, weird or even heartwarming things they had to say. Gameplay is serviceable but then again who is coming into this game expecting the most amazing gameplay. There are some no clipping issues, framerate issues and this might just been me but controller issues. Overall an excellent experience one that was worth every dollar. If you are looking for a good new game and have a few dollars to spare I recommend Sable.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but the bugs just rip you right out of the experience. It's frustrating riding along when you suddenly hit a random bump that is completely invisible, and sends you flying and bouncing. There's also camera glitches when you're climbing around. Ugh. Maybe in a few years it will be fixed, but it's not worth it at the moment
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Pros* Good Music* Good Exploration* Cozy Vibe* Good writing, gets you immersed in the world.Cons* Performance issues out the wahzoo. Ran choppy sometimes no matter what I tried.* Moving objects sometimes vanish. Makes some climbing difficult, and puzzle items disappear. (But are still interactable.)* Audio issues, sometimes. Cutting out? Stuttering? Not sure how to explain it.Overall, the game is incredibly charming, and it was fun to just boot up and burn away a chunk of hours mindlessly exploring shipwrecks, ruins and caves. Collecting eggs. Some weird polish issues diminish the experience, but not so much as to detract from the game as a whole.Map Expansion DLC? Sable 2? ???
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: What a gorgeous experience! This was a game that came to me at the perfect time, but I think anyone who plays it will get as much out of it, the physical, emotional, and artistic formation of Midden is such an achievement and I will not stop thinking about it, wanting to be a part of it, for a long time. I've also maybe never played a buggier game lol
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game 13 out of 10 points. I can't do that, sadly, simply because it is not my job to rate spectacular works of art. I started playing this on a resolution so low and shadow generation so low that I could comprehend what was going and so that my pc wouldn't croak. I was already having a good time. Comes the time I change my pc and badabing badaboom the game is even more than stellar. I got to burnt oak station at night with the glider in the background and that was already all of things I could've wanted from the game. I'm currently lookking for worms, fish, butterfly and the llast mask. Here's the issue: I have no idea what happens if I chose a mask and I don't know if I can go back. Thank you Sable and thanks you dear devs. Would strongly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game. One of the best indie titles I've picked up in years. I was hooked from the start, and was left feeling so fulfilled. The graphical style was SO great, and with the recent inclusion of a photo mode, I've been able to snag some great wallpapers.If you're debating on whether or not to pick up this game, and you made it this far into the reviews, this is your sign: get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet and smooth ride. For a while I couldn't decide, whether I liked the concept of not being able to fail in a 3d exploration game. Also the fact, that you only meet nice people put me off for some time. But time and again I was surprised by the joy of exploration as well as by the really warm and humane writing. The implementation of Moebius' ligne claire in a 3D world is really well done (and the game is evidently heavily influenced by the art of Jean Giraud - Moebius). The colour aesthetic is (also in terms of lighting) of very high quality (check out the colouring of the city before turning the power on, or how the colour shading changes when looking through a blue window in one of the shipwrecks)
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I expected much more to be honest. The game isn't bad, but isn't good either. It's mid.It lacks some polish here and there, especially on the optimisation side of things.The exploration isn't anything special, while it should be the whole point of it.The puzzles aren't too fun either, same goes for the locations you visit.I hoped better, but I was kinda disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: this game is EXACTLY my thing. immersing yourself in a sci-fi culture, exploring wherever you want, and all with a BEAUTIFUL soundtrack and a gorgeous art style inspired by fantasy comics? a story about coming of age, deciding on your identity, and the joy of discovery? combat-free, puzzle-solving, and queer representation? i'm only sad i didn't play this sooner!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's really cool. Very chill and relaxing to play. The world building is amazing, a lot of lore to be discovered. You have missions, but more often than not you are just propelled forward by your own curiosity. All the landscapes are huge and fascinating. Things to collect, but not loads to remember. Never feels grindy, not even once. Climbing mechanic is fab and well thought out. Lots of reward for climbs in just stunning views. If I had the time I'd play this for days.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I really, *really* enjoyed the demo before the full game was released and was DYING for it to come out.I love Sable's art style, and the plot I expect was even better. Unique concept too.Took a while for them to finish sorting out the bugs but I can safely recommend this now, lovely exploration game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I tried this game for an hour. And I definitely dislike this game's world. You know, those worlds, which are endless pointless desert with a few interest point which are used only for YOUR quests. Empty, barren worlds without internal logic, centered around you. I dislike those a lot.Also, it seems that I dislike the game's main selling point - graphics. And certainly I dislike gameplay, which seems to be mostly environmental puzzles. Environtal puzzles and clunky, unresponsive controls are absolute disaster.I think, I'll just refund this game before it really annoys me.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is an interesting and very unique game. However, it is troubled with small annoying little bugs... that needs to be fixed. Once those are done, i'm sure the experience can be more smooth and relaxing. The unique design and graphics makes you desire to see more of the vast and lonely desert, however... it feels sometimes lacking of "life". I hoped it would be more alive rather this cold and barely animated world. The music isn't ongoing, which is a shame... It would have been more enjoyable if the game had more to listen to... I'm going to wait for optimisations and bug fixes... then i'll revisit this game. But if you're looking for a peaceful adventure, and now and then solve "puzzles", this might be worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I don't mind buggy games, but it is odd that they are now a norm. Still found some odd buggy graphical instances with the sky suddenly changing color from night to day and vice versa instead of the gradual shift initially seen. A few shadows still flicker. The game, right after I got the bike and rode out into the open larger world began to lag in an odd way, especially considering such lag and stutter never happens in more graphically intense games. Oh well. Will still play through and hope it turns our alright. If you don't mind bugs still existing then go for it, if not, don't. As there is a don't still advised then overall... nope on recommending.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Overwhelmingly bland. The art style doesn't save it. It's clear that it had no QA. There are movement bugs present in the first minute of the game: Just jump and grab any ledge and you'll see it. You're given a speeder bike to traverse the desert, but the bike apparently wasn't made to go over the gentle curves of the landscape, and leaps around all over.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing atmospheric game. This game is all visuals and exploration. I love the style, the world and the bike! Reminds me a lot of watching Dragonball back in the day. Some weird glitches once in a while and can feel a little slow, but the world is so interesting and varied that even errand running is a pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially attracted by the art style of this game but the game itself is really perfect for me.  It's relaxing but still quite challenging and has an interesting open world that is not too big or too busy.  It definitely gives a good sense of place and is great for escapism.A big thumbs up to the developers too.  I had an issue where i got stuck in a cut scene after a quest and when I contacted the developers they responded really quickly asking for more details (saved game file). In a couple of days they'd fixed it and released a patch over Steam that solved the problem.  They were really polite and helpful and seemed to really care about their game and the people playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A laid back game with no combat or risk of death.Best parts of this game are the music and art work.You are a Glider named Sable.  You are given a bike and sent off to explore the surrounding desert to find the path you will follow in life.  Along the way you perform tasks, collect badges for mask crafting, climb mountains, and explore what the region has to offer.Good, relaxing game that you can run through the story in 10 hours or so depending on how much messing around you do. I would wait til this goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: It takes some effort to get through this if you're looking to get all the collectibles. Frankly, if that's your goal, you should find some guides online to help you out. If you want to play this casually though--or are okay with getting most (but not all) of the collectible items, then this game can be quite fun. It has a very unique art style and some really fun puzzles to figure out using unique mechanics. This game is NOT for everyone, but it can be quite fun and entertaining for those who do like it. Chasing collectibles isn't the only thing the game is about though, and it can be enjoyed leisurely as a unique ambient sort of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: If you search through 90% of the negative reviews, you'll find something to the effect of "I really wanted to like it". My concerns mirror this, and I'm not sure I can add too much more to be substantive beyond this:The moment to moment gameplay isn't a jam. I don't mean the puzzles, although they could use some polish too. I want to stand on top of statues and take in the splendor of this world. I want to look around at beautiful landscapes while I cruise. I want a vibey soundtrack that sucks my soul in and makes every moment a main character moment.Unfortunately, Sable is a miss on almost all of these counts. The bike is buggy, even over smooth terrain. Vast swaths of land are empty, and upon further inspection of landmarks there is a chance there's nothing more to find; your curiousity is stifled instead of inspired as in most collectathons. The music shown in the trailer knocks it outta the park, but the normal soundtrack is meh.TLDR: This game is on sale for 10 bucks rn, I'd wait for that price.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Given the small development team it's understandable that the camera and movement systems lack polish, but the technical issues really are widespread and ever-present. Still, the centerpiece of this game is its gorgeous landmarks and views, which bring about some really special organic moments of wondrous scale and beauty.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really cool, visually gorgeous, fun game, although I do have to say there more than a few bugs, such as the character clipping through the levels, maps inaccurately showing where characters/locations are . It is definitely a game I would recommend, with good design, amazing game mechanics, just has a few issues with buggy gameplay, but given how new the game is, and how the game works, this is alright but I hope it gets patched soon. Otherwise, really good art style, interesting story that makes sense (well, up until now), and really good puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I'm not usually one who cares about aesthetics and customization in games, but this one really made me. What made it so meaningful is that I didn't care too much about how Sable or the bike, Simoon, looked, but what it meant to be wearing what I wore. Each option has a history and meaning behind it, and the game gives a fantastic sense of you carrying on that history or representing that idea when you choose your clothes and bike parts. Since nothing in this game is dangerous, I felt completely free to explore wherever and whatever I wanted. The fluidity of the movement, the beauty of the landscapes, and the gentle music pushed me always to explore further, even though almost all of it is optional. There isn't a ton of dialogue with the characters, but I still felt connected to so many of them. If you want a peaceful game about exploration and self-reflection to play during late nights, I can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me nostalgic for the feeling of growing up. It makes me miss the days where I had the whole world ahead of me and countless options to choose from on where I wanted to direct my life. This game is playable emotion. I bet it was no accident that the scenery is reminiscent of "Oh the Places You Will Go." Play this game and recommend it to your younger family members who have endless possibilities ahead of them. This game makes me want to rewind time and grow up all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a great game for open world exploration enthusiasts who have no issues with the absence of combat and hectic gameplay. Fantastic atmosphere and visually pleasing with it's non-typical graphics, truely relaxing and the soundscape is also pleasing. The game has a few bugs that, while not gamebreaking, takes away some of the feeling of flow as you progress. At least one bug encountered required me to exploit another bug-like "feature" to be able to complete a task, but all issues were solved quickly with a few google searches.Personally I think the game could have been substantially longer, but it was nevertheless worth the price. Will probably play it more than once even if I unlocked it 100% already.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Great open world adventure game that doesn't overstay its welcome unlike many other contemporary open world games. It has a beautiful art style that was inspired by the art of Moebius. Its gameplay, on the other hand, seems to be inspired by The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. All well done. I found both the world-building and the soundtrack to be equally good. The only fault that I can mention are some annoying bugs that perplexingly haven't been fixed even years after release.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game in which you are solving climbing puzzles without stress as there are no enemies to fight except your skills on choosing the right path.I really liked the gameplay mechanics, the climbing was intuitive and fun to do. Never was I stressed or bored out.The visuals are stunning and often invites you to just stand still and marvel at it. The art style is perfectly balanced.The sound design is also very well done and the score is repetitive but never boring.Overall, get it on a sale and play it.PS: Most of the performance troubles I had, were solved by using VSYNC/2 (reducing it to stable 60 fps). I think there is some kind of bug if there are more than 60 fps possible. I am using 4k 120Hz Gsync Monitor with Nvidia 2080TI and enabled Gsync.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I loved my time with this game, the art style and sense of adventure were both fantastic, the world wanted me to explore and learn more. I always dig games where you can participate in a world instead of being the chosen saviour. Only bad thing I can say was the more I explored the more I encountered some janky geometry at some parts of the map but its to be expected with the ambitious size of the game and never caused anything gamebreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much, it's literally one of my comfort ones to go to. It gives the same feel as driving in the middle of the night, except you're in the middle of the desert on your hoverbike. The world of Sable is about her coming-of-age, and it asks nothing from the player except to explore the vast world and to try and find out who you want to become. Which is an awfully nice theme for a game, and one that is rarely seen nowadays.There are some minor issues with the game such as slight movement glitches or like faulty, weird camera angles (which I'm sure is fixed already, because I played the game a year ago) but other than that the game is wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic art style with a very strong Moebius vibe. Decent gameplay with a compelling list of things to do and to explore which doesn't overstay its welcome. The background lore was quite interesting to dig through as well even though it had little to no impact on the rest of the story and world. My one complain is that the game does feel a little janky and unpolished at times but nothing that killed my enjoyment of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Charming game focused on the joy of exploration. The lack of pressure in the environment gives it such a wonderful feeling of possibility. Oh, to live in a world where the youths grow into adulthood by traveling around in a safe yet fulfilling manner, unpressured by the demands of education or capitalism. If it were me, I'd keep riding that bike forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A great game about a girl in a journey.This is a game of exploration, take your time and enjoy. The graphics aren't the realistic type that people are used to these days, but are great in an artistic point of view, I just love gliding around and exploring.Having won (on a giveaway) this game about a journey in the same day my dog died made it even more meaningful.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Calling this a vertigo inducing adventure puzzler, which it is!, doesn't do credit to the ambient free spirited nature of this game. Has been on my wish list for a long time and I am happy to have almost completed my journey.Will likely return to the game occasionally to simply enjoy the scenery from a great height.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Too many bugs and poor performance.This was my most anticipated game of 2021 but, unfortunately, I can't recommend it due to the state the game is in.  Way too many bugs that hindered my enjoyment and immersion.  Tons of audio bugs, countless menu bugs, floppy physics for the gliders that have you spinning and doing nose dives all the time.  There's a bug on the map menu that causes there to be a constant slew of markers on your mini map that never go away.  Trying to set a marker to follow is pointless because you don't know which marker is the one you set versus the other 4-5 markers that won't go away.Often the glider gets stuck under hills or rocks and won't come back to you when you call it, leaving you stranded, forcing you to have to fast travel to another location to respawn the glider.  This killed the desire to explore for me.Wait for updates.  I don't know how long it will take to fix this game and get it running properly, but when it is finished, I think it'll be a good game.  Right now it's not a good game.  It's unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: shameful waste of amazing talent,in the first moments I though I was discovering a hiden gem like Journey or even Ori (because of the amazing music). But after meeting an entire village populated by women (main character refer to them as "she"), I though that was weird as most of them actual look like men but ok, a female tribe, why not.. then onto the next village main character meets a npc that looks again like a dude and refer to him as "them", scrached my head for a few seconds then I understood.. this game is confused about its gender... and the magic is gone.what a stupid waste, after a few bug fixes this game could be in the top 5 indie open world of all times.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Really wholesome game. Beautifully drawn art style, like travelling through a world by Hergé  or Mœbius, and the music and audio just adds to that. If you're a bit burnt out on open world games, this is a lovely antidote. Just chill and explore as you please. Look forward to seeing what Shedworks do next. Really impressive debut.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: The premise and art style of the game is cool. Your character is a teenager (maybe 15?) and is sent out on her own into the world to see what she wants to be. For the rest of her life! A literal child being expected to figure out what she wants to be for the rest of her life, wild.You can gain badges associated with different guilds (for lack of a better word) like merchants, guard or mechanic but at no point did I feel compelled to be a part of any of these guilds. All the guild members are effectively identical because you can't get to know the characters because everyone wears a mask. The reason for this may be explained but after ~5 hours I was rapidly becoming apathetic.You know how in Skyrim or the Fallout games the quest marker knows exactly where you should go and you don't need to think? There's none of that in this game which is good and bad. Good because you have to pay attention to what people say and to your surroundings but bad because you're not even given a waypoint to the quest giver that's completely forgettable.Climbing is pretty good. You have a stamina bar that you can upgrade by collecting these weird "chum eggs". As far as I know you're never told what to do with these, I had to look up guides. Apparently to get all the stamina upgrades you need to deliver 100 eggs! And there's an unskippable cutscene every damn time you pick up one of these crimes against nature.Puzzle difficulty is all over the place. One involves standing on a pedestal and waiting for sunrise, I arrived at midday and had to wait 15-ish minutes; yawn. The astrolab puzzle is pretty cool. There's crashed spaceships with puzzles in them that I could not be bothered to finish due to the insane bizarrchitecture.There's fishing. On a desert planet. Somehow. It's awful even with the easy fishing enabled.The hoverbike physics is awful. The bike is supposedly sentient although it never acts like it. Before your character chooses what faction to join Sable says goodbye to her bike but the moment falls flat due to a lack of character building of this bike.The locations are all forgettable. The only ones I remember are Errica (because it's an actual town with water) and The Watch (giant astrolab).The main character is pretty forgettable too. I'd forget her name too if the game wasn't named after her.Performance is pretty terrible, lots of screentearing and stuttering despite having a 3060ti. Plays alright on the Steam Deck, it has some stuttering. For some reason the game doesn't have a quit button so I have to Alt+F4 every time I want to close the game.If you can get the game for $10 go for it, otherwise don't bother.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most relaxing and fun single player game that i have played in a while. Sable doesn't have any enemies, fall damage or any way to take damage. It does have an amazing soundtrack, a beautiful (and reletable) story, memorable characters and area's. If you're looking for a relaxing, open world game with a great setting, Sable is the game for you
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I so desperately want to be able to recommend this beautiful little game, but ultimately, I can't.  It's an exploration game where the core mechanics are jetting around the desert on a floating bike, climbing on anything and everything you encounter - and neither of these mechanics really work.  Driving the bike around is at best tolerable, but it never really clicks.  The bike doesn't handle that well, never really gives a feeling freedom, and most irritatingly, the best one is not earned, but bought at a random merchant.  The climbing mechanics are unpredictable at best, and broken at their worse.  Sable often loses her grip, snaps back and forth between walking and climbing animations, or just gets jetted away from a corner or bump way to frequently.  The most infuriating parts are the segments where you must climb on rotating elements.  The engine flat out cannot handle these.  Sable falls of constantly, sometimes retaining a movement vector until you restart.  Even worse, the most difficult climb in the game features floating rocks that vanish and reappear constantly, I imagine do to a culling issue from the large objects moving.  This should have never made it through QA.Finally, the performance is very bad, particularly for such a graphically simple game.  Pop-in distance is way to close, yet the game bogs down to the point of interrupting the sound and beautiful soundtrack continuously.  On a 10th generation i7 and a 2070.That being said, the story and world-building are exquisite.  I will look out for another game from this developer and I hope they are able to address these shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable's unique art style and calm environment look like great selling points, but this is ruined by almost every other aspect of the game. Other games like Journey and Abzu with a focus on exploration don't overbear you with lots of exposition or text, you just *do* what you need to do and learn through the world. Sable starts you with tedious fetch quests on a loud bike, trying to explain why you should care instead of just making you care. I would be able to look past some of these more annoying details, but along with this the game is very buggy. There is constant frame dips, the animations sometimes bug out, the camera fights you every step of the way during exploration, and there is random bugs that stop you from completing quests.Overall I would not recommend this game to anyone, unless you are very patient in dealing with the bugs and issues. I'm sure there is something to be discovered here, but I just don't think that the effort is worth it in this case.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you want something interesting with quests and puzzles not too hard. Seems like the target market was young adults with the focus on exploring personal identity with 'masks'. I thought the graphics level was perfect for the story. Some thoughts on things you need to know up front: (1) Searching for Chum eggs along the way should be a priority. Cashing them in with the Chum Queen will increase your stamina. Stamina is quite essential for all the climbing you will be doing. (2) Search for money caches and scrap metal. Money is needed to buy maps of the 6 regions and scrap metal is for the scrapper's mask. (3) Interact with NPCs to acquire quests for outfit and bike upgrades and especially for masks. (4) You can save the game at any time but you only have one save game slot.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Storyline is pretty good. Exploration is (literally) next-world. Artwork is simplistic and cozy (kind of a Studio Ghibli vibe - I dig it), and the music is simply phenomenal. _childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands, Sable is a great adventure game to pass the time or chill out in and I half recommend you check it out. However there are a few glaring issues with it that need to be ironed out before I can fully recommend it.I have to address this before anything, currently I seem to be softlocked in The Atomic Heart, if you enter through the top without using the keycard that you presumably need to open the front door, it seems that you can leave back out of that hole in the roof because the surfaces are unclimbable and because the door is locked, you can not escape the room.Technically also this game suffers from severe hitching and frame drops, even though my PC can run RDR2 and other resource intensive games just fine, so I'm not sure whats going on there.When those issues get fixed, then I'll recommend it fully.Aesthetically, in all departments this game is stunning. Visually the art style is great, the UI is easy to understand, readable and clean, the sound design is pretty good, maybe lacking in ambient audio and motorbike/glider ambient engine noise but it's still pretty good. So really no major complaints there. This is the only bit of praise I'm giving and it might seem like I'm being overly negative, but keep in mind that this makes up a majority of the game itself.I'm 25/100 on the gameplay though, the platforming feels fluid and plays pretty well. I think everyone can tell that the devs are going for a BOTW type of game, but the problem is that Sable misses the mark on what made BOTW such a good game. The only way you seem to interact with the world of Sable and the things set out for you are through platforming with very light puzzles ONLY. There is no sandbox to mess around in and so far, 3 hours in and there seems to be no metroidvania/zelda style tools to use that helps with puzzles, helps traverse the world, ect. Other than the gliding mechanic. It feels like this wont change and I don't see any tools/gadget/magic or any-way-to-influence-the-non-existant-sandbox catagory in the UI so it doesn't look promising.Because of the setting being post apocalyptic, the only interaction with the world being platforming with no possibility of dying due to no fall damage and no enemies from what I can see, there is a strange feeling of a lack of threat. I'm just exploring with no rhyme, reason or challenge and it feels like there is no purpose to it all, like there are no stakes at play in both story and gameplay and while that's ok for some games, it's a lot more jarring knowing the setting of the world and seeing no enemies or monsters to avoid on your journey? I think I should elaborate on that and explain this feeling further:Sable seems to be inspired by 3 pieces of media, the game "Journey", the game "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild", and the movie "Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind", although the game captures the visual feel and the overall tone of those medias very well, it does little to compare the hardships all protagonists go through in their journey. In Nausicaa, a movie about humanity interferring with nature and Nausicaa herself doing her absolute most to avoid disrupting the cycle of nature, she still faces great danger and challenges from said nature that she has to solve through peace, understanding and non-violent measures. In Journey, a game about a middle eastern view on life, death and rebirth, the hardships of life are represented through it's enemies and damaging weathers, that you must trek through, avoid and overcome on your journey. In Breath of the Wild, there is an overarching plot told from the get go that raises the stakes and sets a clear end goal in mind, but when just exploring and navigating to a distant unmarked location, the question will always eventually turn into 'HOW will I get there', there are threats, environmental barriers and changes in the landscape that keeps you on your feet and constantly using the environment the tools you have to your advantage, it could just as easily screw you over as a sudden change in the wind direction could land you right in the middle of enemy territory.Sable appears to not have anything like this and even 3 hours in and starting to explore the full map, I'm starting to question whether it will ever change.If it doesn't, then I think some combat update is needed at least, maybe add just a common enemy that occupies abandoned structures and monsters roaming the open world, give us a sword for close range attacks and maybe a rickety single shot gun for long range attacks. Doesn't have to be anything special but SOMETHING to make us alert in this world would be appreciated.
