This game is worth it!)~A wonderful, peaceful journey through a desolate yet fascinating world, unfortunately full of bugs and glitches.+Lovely open world adventure+Fun glider vehicle+Unique graphics+Nice music+Great characters+Fascinating world+Lots of costumes and bike-parts to collectBut on the negative side...-Stutter in places-Lots of audio glitches-You can clip through some surfaces that should be solid-Some quests are buggy-One puzzle in particular is almost completely brokenIf you overlook all these issues, I would rate this as one of my favourite games in recent years. _childDocuments_.review: I would recommend Sable. The glorious visuals, that feeling of freedom to explore and the pure wonderment of what's around this corner. However, For all its wonderous Incal-esque discovery, I would not recommend you purchase it just yet. it comes with a pile of caveats...I understand that game development is a very thankless job, you do your best and then everyone piles on the moment a bug is found.However...bugs so far:- The glider handles terribly even when going straight forward. It seems like there is some issue with the ground collision on either side of the bike. If a wing so much as observes the sand, it will immediately shoot up triggering the other wing to dip down, repeating the cycle. Just have it hover higher up?- Climbing can be quite the tall order when geometry meets. This can cause Sable to jitter uncontrollably and make breaking free of this a challenge. Not to mention when you climb up moving platforms and reach the top and Sable does her best wiley coyote impression.- A good amount of the foliage has decided that verticality isn't for them. Instead, deciding to give this whole stretch across the horizon lark a go.- Sounds, a lot of the sound effects don't seem to have been mixed down well enough. compare picking up a single piece of scrap metal, to a box of it. One is a satisfying *clink* the other is a deafening roar.- Music can often get stuck. When unravelling mysteries hidden across the land, you will encounter certain areas that play a very ominous track. These ominous tracks can sometime get stuck and play underneath other music (moody, but I'm fairly sure that's not what they were going for). This happens even when you quit out to the main menu where the title card piano tune will being rudely interrupted by a single detuned string being plucked at odd rhythms.- The game can never remember which mask I last wore so I have to change it each time I boot up the game to maintain my A E S T E T I C.Maybe wait a month before you dive in.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game a lot. The visuals are probably the first thing that catches the eye. Aside from the beautiful illustration-like style, all the characters, objects and environments are well designed. Music and sound manage to elevate visuals even higher.Exploration is rewarding. You constantly see something interesting on the horizon, and while making your way towards it, find a few more spots to check. Once you reach your destination, there is free-form climbing to do and light puzzles to solve. Both of these mechanics are not super challenging but engaging. While doing it, you may find characters to talk to, gear to collect and bits of the world's history to unfold. Riding a bike between destinations felt a bit underwhelming to me, but you get to admire the environment while doing so.Most quests you can do are not very intense or dramatic. Often they exist to point you towards cool new places. It fits the game quite well in my opinion, though I wish they went deeper into what each mask entails. Currently, the game has quite a few technical issues. The developers are working on it and already improved some things. I hope they continue: Sable is great and deserves to shine.

_childDocuments_.review: I anxiously waited for this game after the E3 2018 presentation, and I was not disappointed in the slightest. The game is so beautiful in every way. The story of Sable's gliding is simple but heartfelt, the environments are stunning, and the music is incredible. It was so wonderful to get lost in the game for hours, gliding across the dunes, climbing to the top of The Seven Sisters, jamming to the Eccria theme, and hunting down every last chum. There are some extensive technical issues--Sable and the camera clipping through the environment, disappearing hoverbike, random pop-ins, etc.--but it didn't break the experience of the game for me. Amazing game! I can't wait to see what Shedworks does next!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a part of me that wants to start this review with a list of some of the bugs and problems I encountered during the 33 casual hours it took me to get 100% of the achievements, but I'm not going to. Having to restart the game every now and then because of a crash or shop items not showing up is unimportant to me if the game is good enough and Sable, for me, is far more than good enough.Playing Sable made me feel like an explorer, discovering lost histories and incredible vistas, meeting and helping people along the way. The art style may seem simple but the world is rich in detail, beauty and secrets to find. The writing adds further details and beauty, fleshing out the past and present of the planet Midden and it's people, giving far more depth to the game than I expected and - perfectly - never quite answering all of my questions. I spent at least 20% of my time in the camera mode documenting my Gliding, taking in the environment and admiring the variety of customisation options for Sable & Simoon the hoverbike I picked up on my travels. But some of my favourite moments were those I spent sitting down for a few minutes, to reflect on whatever was on my mind after climbing so high and travelling so far. It was a beautiful journey from start to finish, both visually and emotionally, and by the end I felt actual heartache for the world I was leaving behind - a world I hope I forget about, so I can relive the joy of discovering it all again in the future (a sign of an enjoyed experience if ever there was one). If you want something peaceful, mysterious, atmospheric and full of wonder, I can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A marvelous game!"Sable" is all about exploration and discovery, a journey through vast areas full of interesting things and people. How you progress through the game is up to you, quests will guide you along the way. Puzzles always remain fairly simple, and several mysteries as well as collectables can be found along the way. The visuals are quite unique, reminding me a lot of SketchUp (a 3D modeling software I often used as a kid to build houses and rooms for fun). Sound design and soundtrack are very relaxing, calming even.The only thing that needs improving is the technical quality at times; there is some stuttering while gliding (presumably because the world is loading in the background?) - which can be somewhat reduced by setting the FPS limit to 60 -, and the occasional audio crackling in very few areas (seemingly when many sounds are mixed?).Overall, an easy recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is, before anything else, an exploration game. Why, oh why, is exploration made so bloody difficult???I ran into a slew of problems, both intended and glitches. Among them:. I am disabled, but I swear I have better stamina than Sable. Sable will regularly not grab onto climbable surfaces for some reason. Even outside of glitches, if I tried to grab onto a climbable surface after jumping or gliding, Sable would slide down the surface a little. This would be a cute little touch did she have normal stamina, but she doesn’t, so it meant I would fail to climb up . No really, I can’t stress how bad climbing was, which led me to never attempt a single climbing/platforming challenge past the first 2 hours of the game (cartographer's balloon excluded). It also caused me to give up on deeply exploring certain landmarks, especially vertical ones, because it happened way too often that I would fall back to the ground because of something out of my control, and have to do it all over again. The bike's navigation AI is really bad. It would regularly get stuck on the most random obstacles, even ones that were laughingly easy to just circle around. I’ve encountered quite a lot of visual glitches, the most annoying of which were camera glitches. For example, it would get stuck filming the ceiling or inside Sable during certain convos with NPCs. Even when it’s working, the camera is quite bad- especially when using the bike and climbing, it would lock in certain directions. Please stop, I want to enjoy the scenery. While not the biggest deal, the game and animations are pretty stuttery. You can’t repeat certain conversations with NPCs. Because some quests don’t have objective markers (which is something I usually like!), it led to me completely missing out on them because I forgot about the clue the NPC would have given meThat’s a shame, it really is, because the game is so gorgeous! Beautifully designed, full of artistry, the cities are bustling with life, the environments are surprisingly varied for a biome that remains essentially ‘desert’, it had detailed set-pieces, lovely color palettes that would change with the time of day… What I have seen of the lore so far is also pretty good. I love the mask thing, the different professions and the whole advanced technology/ancient civilization dichotomy. Ultimately though, what many describe as a chill experience only brought me frustration- and after 5 hours, I gave up on playing it further. Sable is by no means a game to run away from, but it isn't one I can recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable's a beautiful mess.The soundtrack is great, the visual style is obviously gorgeous. Loved the feel and lore of the world, and how it all conspired to create some magic moments: the first time gliding across the dunes on your sandbike, climbing up a really high mountain, or when you finally learn a bit about the culture and history of the people.On the other hand, Sable can be quite unpolished. People walking into posts, audio stutters, getting caught on weird invisible edgees while climbing or driving, and other frustrating bugs just happen with a certain regularity. Once I was swimming through the air like water and a few times I got locked in dialogue without a way to fix it except a forced restart of the game. What's worse, these bugs seem to have been around since launch and the devs either don't have the resources or the will to fix them.All in all, Sable's far from a perfect game and even feels rushed and unfinished at times. Still, I enjoyed it for the mood it conveyed, and I will keep a couple fond memories from it. The bugs I've encountered were a bit of a downer at times (especially when I had to worry about getting softlocked), but they usually resolved themselves after fast-travelling or restarting the game. So nothing that ruined my experience.I'm a fairly efficient player, but I took my time with it - never fast-travelled anywhere except to fix a bug (and even then, just going to the nearest POI). Took me 24 hours to finish the game, which imho makes it a bit overpriced. At 16 bucks or below I recommend it, but for 25€ you can do much better.

_childDocuments_.review: After much thought I've decided to leave a review.This game does not deserve the Sweet Baby Stamp of Shista. Its a good game made by good devs that had so little for SBI to touch that its not noticable. Indie devs and good games such as this do not deserve to be ♥♥♥♥-upon because they fell victim to a company that admittedly practices predatory tactics.Exploration: 9/10 Vast and nearly no invisible wallsVisuals: 8/10 a wonderfully unique art styleGame design: 6/10 simply because I wanted more stuff to go and find, more story, more SABLE.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much in this game to love, but with a caveat. It's not for everyone. Lets get the issues out of the way first. The camera doesn't always work. It'll get stuck in the scenery or refuse to focus on what you're trying to look at, especially during the platforming sections. With that we move onto my second complaint, the climbing. It works well when its not the central focus of the game and just another exploration mechanic. But the game will sometimes give you platforming sections and the game falls apart. The climbing isn't responsive and tight enough as a mechanic to sustain those sections and so they just end up being a nuisance.Now that's out of the way, lets talk about the positives. Exploration is the name of the game here folks and it is fantastic. The world is big enough that you feel like there is a lot to see but it's not so filled with arbitrary crap that you feel stifled by it. There are a handful of collectibles around the map but finding them feels like an organic by-product of exploring the world rather than something you have to go out of your way for.The main plot is simple and intimate. You play as a young explorer looking for her place in the world through a ritual called Gliding that sees you trying to acquire as many masks as you can before settling on one that will define your role in society for most of your life. The side-quests are all quite fun and often tied directly into the main quest of gathering masks so nothing you do feels redundant. There's a massive quest that sees you investigating a crime, another which sees you donning the identity of a vigilante, one that has you searching for a poet, and these are just some among many such unique quests with interesting plots. There are some standard fetch quests as well but the characters were fun enough that I didn't mind doing them.The worldbuilding and lore in Sable is exceptional and probably my favourite part of the entire game. There are ruins of ancient civilisations dotted all around, parts of a crashed spaceship, a myriad of bizarre and interesting creatures, one of which gives you a quest. I loved getting on my glider and just setting of towards an interesting looking structure on the horizon and that curiosity is almost always rewarded.Honestly, I could go on and on about why I loved this game but I can't say much more without spoiling things that I really think you need to experience for yourself. So, if you're a fan of open-world exploration games with a relaxed vibe and no combat, Sable is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm one of the two people in the world, who didn't enjoy Zelda BotW. I'm only mentioning this here because i saw the comparison so often. Sable is different, and i enjoy that a ton. I didn't know anything about it going in.Sable immediately spoke to me. The lore and world are really intriguing, i just love the idea of young people venturing out gaining powerful abilities and eventually coming back, settling down and *losing* all that. You don't have a village of unbeatable lvl 99 characters. Just like in real life, the senior citizens are not the most powerful ones. They are past their point of greatest ability, but have a wealth of experience and wisdom to offer, and the time to give it.The characters here feel like people. I'm male and only playing male characters if offered. I love the fact that i play a female here, and that there is no fuss made about it. The depiction is very realistic in some way - i'm not weak and soft and need the help, i'm not a big boob scantily clad nymphe, i'm not an abrasive and rude "strong woman". Just a normal person on the brink of adulthood, which many of us might still feel like even in their 20s and 30s. That's rare, it doesn't feel like a political statement, but like a story.There are still some rough edges and a little jank, which can be expected and fogiven at release. _childDocuments_.review: Let us not mince words: This is a visually stunning game. Whatever magic they worked with this engine to make it feel as if you are playing a detailed fine pencil drawing, works beautifully. The style reminds me of the drawing style of Ricardo Delgado, and to see it move in 3D space fluidly without aliasing issues is amazing.Beyond the visuals, the game is an exploration focused open world experience. You won't be doing any combat, no extra mechanics, no fat. This is very much about the journey, and not the destination. The chill music, relaxing sounds, and inviting color pallets all lend to the overall vibe of the game. The adventure and pleasure you take from this game is up to you and your patience for stopping to take the time to appreciate it.I went nice and slow, and got a bit over 20 hours out of Sable completing 100% of the achievements. And chances are you'll want to complete them all just to see everything this world has to offer.Yes, it has framerate issues and stuttering audio that can detract from the game's vibe, but that is not a reason to avoid this game at all. Ignore the negative reviews, they are all sucking at the rotten ignorant teet of 'baby wanna stable framerate'. Go back to your COD and let everyone else enjoy this beautiful and relaxing experience on their own volition.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a game about a girl, of the same name, discovering who she is, who she wants to be, all within a beautiful and amazingly well-realized open world. This game has a lot going for it, and it's not often that I find myself just getting into a zen state as soon as I just ride the sands, discovering what lay in the ruins around me. I have yet to finish the game, but I've experienced so many bugs and issues with the game that I want to warn those who desire to purchase that there might be some terrible hiccups to ruin your experience. On Xbox Game Pass for PC, the same is barely functional, so I purchased the game on Steam because I really did want to enjoy this experience, and for a two-person team, I can't wholly blame them. However, even on Steam, the cracks start to show. Despite having such a gorgeous open world, framerates are atrocious. Running on a GTX 1080, some areas absolutely crash and burn, hitting as low as 20fps in spots. Frame hitches are everywhere. Pop-in is drastic, constant, and unavoidable (I played on an SSD for the record). Climbing is bizarrely broken in places, and puzzles seem to rely more on glitches to be solved than solutions. I also had one completely game-breaking bug that required me to quit the game, breaking any immersion I might've had up until that point.I want to love this game. There's so much vibrant joy to behold here, and the game is truly fun to play. Yet, every time I would begin to enjoy myself, I'm ripped out of my immersion by some sort of hitch in the game. I am recommending it because I see the value in this game, and there is so much to love here, but be warned - it may not be the desert you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for what has turned out to be an incredibly tedious game. I was lured by its artwork and music, but it turns out that is really all that the developers seem to have put much effort into in creating Sable. This is a game that really wants you to explore the world and take in the surroundings, but the truth is those become really uninteresting after about an hour. The game is buggy (significantly less so than when it first came out) so the experience of just flying around the world can feel unsatisfying and pointless. Why go through the effort of creating an immersive, Moebius inspired world if the colors constantly blink and frames constantly drop?Regarding gameplay, this is a game with neither violence, nor a health bar, which is fine, but also a game that seems to lack both stakes and consequences. The puzzles are easy and there does not seem to be a way to experience setbacks. Once again, another aspect in which Sable feels more like test content than a finished product. This is not to mention the irritation experienced when trying to navigate, for example, the correct angle at which to approach a wall so Sable can climb it. This is not the game challenging you to get creative with the controls; this is just inconsistent game design.I'm seven hours into the game. Sources on the internet say I'm about 50% through. Normally I reserve judgment until hour twenty, but I don't think this game offers twenty hours of content. For that matter, to the extent that one can play this game for 14 hours, I wonder how much of that is spent just flying around looking for something to do or reading menus/dialogue/text that the game has already had you read once before. I really really want to like this game. The characters are quirky and unique, the color palette equally so, and the world itself feels like someone's very good, well thought out unfinished idea. Yet every time I pick up the controller I feel let down by something else.

_childDocuments_.review: These 9 hours have been in one sitting so I can tell you with confidence as someone who both loves this genre of games and this game itself: **Sable is not only buggy as Hell, it is straight up Unfinished**There is area you go to later in the game, behind the starting area where their are many crashed ships. Here there are many FULL PILLARS and PARTS of buildings you can just walk thru. I found a line of orange bugs just floating in the sky. The audio cuts out constantly and plays the wrong sound cues. I felt more like I was beta testing a game then playing a finished product.That Said: I am having an amazing time. If you liked how messed up running around Skyrim was you love this game. **THE WRITING IS GREAT** I do really care about Sable and getting her what she wants, most people don't have a lot to say, but Sable has a really nice inner monologue that makes up for it. **This game is BEAUTIFUL** Style over substance for sure, but omg its a good style. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I wanted to LOVE it, because it has such a cool premise and it's full of potential. And it's enjoyable sometimes, but has a big problem that's the reason why I'm giving it a negative review: This game is extremely broken.I have never in my life played a game that's so full of bugs in a way that affected my whole experience. The amount of fun I had with it doesn't compare to the amount of annoyances and frustration I suffered from every time I stumbled upon a bug. And there were so many of them, that I decided to make a list of those I remember, or I wrote in my notes with the purpose of putting them here:● A lot of "Don't lose your hoverbike!!" Warnings when I'm using the hoverbike in question.● Your hoverbike call doesn't work most of the time, meaning you have to run to find your own bike that doesn't even bother to move a little bit.● And when it does, it can get irreparably stuck in various decorations, meaning you don't have a proper way to get it out unless is using fast travel.● The map not loading at the speed my hoverbike goes, a lot of times ending with the bike glitching out while the map is loading until it repair itself or Sable gets off and get on the bike again.● Sable disappearing from driving the bike (the UI glitching too)● A lot of problems with the places loading, making the bike stuck in the textures and refusing to go past them.● In one of the airship missions, there was a BIG hole in the middle of the room, basically below you, and in one moment I fell into that hole. I couldn't get out. Sable didn't make a single effort to climb the surface, and there wasn't a walkable way out. I had to use fast travel, and it reset my whole puzzle progress.● There's a common sound glitch that loads every time you get close to it anywhere on the map, and boy it's LOUD. It's like a mini sudden jumpscare every time it activates, and it never stops re-loading while you're playing, so you'll hear it multiple times if you trigger that zone.● The climbing mechanics are just unbearable. Since you can climb everything, it can glitch like crazy. Sometimes sable doesn't know what to do against a surface, and it climbs it funny, sometimes you DON'T want to climb and she does anyway. Sometimes she free-falls and glitches against the various surfaces beneath her, making her float or jump super high. And for a game that has A LOT of climbing, it made it SO unenjoyable.● There was one fishing bug in particular that made me SO mad because I was having an awful time completing the achievement and then.... Sable froze in her place with the rod out. And she could move, but she couldn't do ANYTHING else. She just stood there and moved around, and I couldn't fish, and I couldn't get out of the minigame, she did NOTHING and I had to reset the whole game, and then it randomly froze AGAIN in like three different times. If you can tolerate a broken experience, you may enjoy the game. I did in some parts, and it's gorgeous to look at, but I can't ignore all of these reasons. If the devs had any interest in fixing most of the game, then I would change my review. But seeing that it has been years since the game launched, and it's in this state, I doubt they have any interest in spending more time with it. A shame, honestly! I repeat that I think it has a cool idea going on, but what left me with was disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, there are bugs. Quite a few, at launch, and rather egregious ones. If you're reading reviews around this time you'll be aware of that.Here's a recommendation on who should buy it anyway: if just looking at the screenshots and videos gives you a sense of joy or wonder, it's you.One aspect of this game I appreciate the most is how positive it is. There are no evil antagonists, no edgy antiheroes, no mindless ghouls for cannon fodder, no real sense of danger whatsoever. Sable proves you don't need those things to be compelling, narratively and in gameplay. It's full of basically good people doing their best, it centers around a choice by a young woman with no external threat or righteous crusade to pursue - an internal conflict alone, one which becomes your conflict. That, plus a sense of curiosity and wonder, is enough to get you to the end of this lovely story.I won't lie, I put the game down a few times after yet again being unable to buy at the shop*, or a button wasn't pressing down under me**, or the hydraulic catapult refused to actually launch me into the air***. But it was probably a good idea to break up the time I spent playing anyway - I found coming to the game fresh gave me a new sense of appreciation just for being in the beautifully rendered world.Can't emphasize it enough - they nail the visuals. It's incredibly impressive. Every detail is there, even line outlines on the shadow maps - not a trivial thing to do I believe, since so few other games would ever see the need to try.Unfortunately there's always a balance, and I think the incredible attention to detail here is also the source of major graphical struggles. The game looks simple, but in my experience outline shaders imply post-processing, and ones which look this good may involve a lot of 'extra' rendering behind the scenes. Perhaps they can followup with serious performance gains, but perhaps it'll always be heavier on the hardware than it looks.Anyway, my technical theories aside, it's a delightful game. You might decide to wait to see if the bugs are patched out. But if you're as fascinated by the beauty of it as I was, it's worth the frustration, just take your time.(* restart the game, ** try walking on it from different directions, no jumping, *** jump right before it extends so you're in the air)

_childDocuments_.review: I really really really wanted to like this game, mainly because as a huge Japanese Breakfast fan, she does a stellar job on the soundtrack here, but I wish that could be said for the developers and testers. They do her work a disservice by not producing work as polished as her delightful, spacy, airy and magical minimalist soundtrack. The game is basically Breath of the Wild without combat, and just puzzles and exploration. So in that sense, if you hated BotW because the world felt empty and there was nothing to do, you will hate this the same. But if you loved it due to the world feeling alive, but empty at the same time, with the occasional landmark, dotted with some lovable NPCs, you’ll enjoy this in a similar vein. The writing in this game is quite beautiful, the NPC dialogue and when describing Sable’s inner thoughts is a nice touch. Artistically, the game hits its objectives as it feels like a coming-of-age film but in game format. The whole storyline is about a young girl growing up, going through this post-apocalyptic journey of self-discovery and exploration of the barren desert which captures mystery in every corner. Through exploration and quests you can find lore to discover what happened in this world, but you can care as little and as much as you want about it. Played this game on my Steam Deck mostly, and initially, performance was pretty horrible. Unable to hit a stable 30fps. In the high polygon count areas it would dip to average 23, 24fps. Stuttering and almost constant frame drops made this game an absolute mess to experience. After some time, I came back to the game to discover performance had been improved (partly due to the SteamOS updates to the Steam Deck, but performance was reported as improved generally) and I was able to hit around a good average of 40fps, but stuttering still occurred, albeit less so.You may say, oh, well that’s cos you were playing on a SD you fool. Well, lo and behold, when I downloaded and played the game via PS Plus on my PS5, a much more capable piece of hardware, it still stuttered. Performance was better, a bit better than my later experience on the SD, but there was still stuttering. The game can be very frustrating at times due to this, and the camera can go crazy at times when in tight spaces or you crash into certain geometry while on your glider. Further, less serious nitpicks follow: - The lack of maps for larger locations??? Where tf is this merchant in the Vivarium?? Can make some quests in Eccria pretty annoying.- Climbing trousers seem to do nothing??- Glider sometimes just doesn’t react to you at all, especially when calling it, you have to call it multiple times, or just walking over to it is faster…..- Getting stuck on random stuff, as sable or on your glider.- Climbing can be glitchy- This didn’t happen to me, but check this glitch - “If you want to get the new bike parts, you will have to start a new game”, see comment at 14 Jan, 2023 @ 6:40am   - Unfortunately there’s lots of discourse online asking about is the game performance better now/fixed. The last update to the game was 2022. Following on from the cons, the devs have expressed themselves that they have no desire to patch these bugs and glitches or address the performance in form of any fix. This is pretty awful post-game support and just pure negligence towards a game that deserves better, but as I said at the beginning, it’s less a game, and more an art-piece, and that seems what the creators want this to be. If you fancy an extremely cosy BOTW experience without the combat, and all of the climbing, exploration and collecting (and fishing!), with a mysterious desert world represented by a really nice art style and a stellar, stellar soundtrack, you will probably like this game. Or at least the idea of this game. If stuttering, glitches and less-than-optimal performance will absolutely frustrate you to the point of never returning to this game, I wouldn’t blame you either.   It really is pretty awful for me to have to recommend you play the game for under 2hrs to see if you like it and then see if you can try get a refund if you don’t. But that’s the state this game is in, and for that, there’s no way can I recommend this game, and unfortunately it won’t get anymore love in the future.They have done Japanese Breakfast here a huge disservice here and I will never forgive the devs for that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may not be what you're looking for, if you are expecting a typical open world adventure game with a unique art style. This is a game about exploration and discovery, both of the world and of oneself (as the plot is basically you are sent on a coming-of-age journey to decide what your calling is). There is not any significant conflict driving the game forward, and no battle system. There are some really cool areas that help paint a picture of the world's lore, and some of them do provide some interesting challenges in figuring out how to reach the top via climbing and/or other means. Unfortunately, this game is really buggy. From visual glitches to gaining weird momentum randomly, I'm a bit concerned that the game has received new content updates without some of these things being addressed. That being said, I still recommend this game for being the chillest game I've every played, with a great setting and art style. Its an absolutely unique take on the open world experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start. Chum Queen. Find the Chum Queen early on or you will have a hard time playing.Welp, I'm just sitting here waiting for some machinist to decipher some alien races tablets or something, and then I'll hit the perfect game achievement after I finish my Gliding by choosing a mask so it's a good time to hit up a quick review whilst I wait.Sable is a great game only hindered by performance slowdown, a glitchy and sad add-on fishing update, kinda sparse city center, and other minor bugs that may require a reboot.Having said that, I thoroughly enjoyed the sense of adventure and emptiness of the landscapes. The music is often ambient and perfect for atmosphere building. Climbing here and there, gliding from ledge to ledge, has got me hiking outside in the real world in the middle of winter. And per usual asking myself, "What's just over that hill?" Spoiler: More hills. It's always been more hills. And it is never going to change lol. I'm basically stuck in a 90s loop hooping Jack doesn't die in The Titanic. But he always does. Anyways... my same logic sneaks it's way into this game. Always climbing new heights.For the most part, the climbing seems to be fair w/the player having the ability to complete a fair share of the game without needing to upgrade stamina, and I find that important b/c some may not discover stamina upgrades until much later than myself. Climbing high, looking over the barren landscapes, or into valleys, or city centers, or whatnot.... and scanning for new landmarks, more chum eggs, more anything is really right up my alley.The game gives me a slight sense of adventure found in an older RPG called, Grandia. Tho supporting characters' character building and depth is not uber strong in Sable, I felt like your personal journey is what is alive, and it manages to carry the story.The game is mostly fetch quest, and the beginning 3 quests actually annoyed me, and I almost turned it off, but the landscape and intrigue pushed me beyond those first several quests, and I soon found I enjoyed the freedom beyond that dam wall in the beginning.So bottom line: Let discovery and the unknown carry the game, and keep your expectations for innovation moderate.

_childDocuments_.review: I had avoided this game near launch due to some of the framerate and performance complaints and... well they're still evident to me at this point. outside of the visual style, the most distracting thing about this game is the inconsistent framerate. But that certainly didn't make it unplayable for me. I just have a hard time gauging the review for anyone who isn't used to lower Framerate and/or graphic fidelity.Anyway, outside of the frame and flicker issues from my lower end system, it's a nice game. Big open map with a bunch of locations and various objectives.No final objective really presented other than "get badges and obtain masks" without much additional detail.A game fully about exploring with some sidequests on the menu(Edit) So fishing was added as a later mechanic to the game a few month after it came out (Nov '22) and I had earlier complained how it had a dedicated button in the control scheme but literally no NPC i came across mentioned fishing, like, at all.There is exactly 3 NPC's that care about fishing and they exist at points that just aren't indicated on the map at all (one of them being of significant size)They really could have updated the map but they never did... and in a game with so much empty space, you really have to stumble upon one of them to get it started. An updated map might clue folks in at least.Anyway, i was initially shocked that the achievement of collecting a single fish being as low as %6, but i guess it makes more sense as it was a later addition to the gameStill, for a mechanic that spreads across the entire map and has significant monetary implications as well as additional completion goals, there should be at least a few more NPC's in the main hubs that mention those locations instead of, well, ZeroThe fishing is decent enough and having a sort of zoo to collect stuff in is a neat addition.The reason for this edit is that it's basically entirely missable (again 6% of players have ever experienced reeling in one fish when there's a dedicated button for it)I still really like this game, but after spotting the "Fish" button right near the start and not ever figuring out the one hidden NPC i need to spot in the middle of the desert to actually do that is worth mentioninguhh 7/10 if you like exploring, climbing, riding bikes, collectibles, etcBasically BotW/Genshin without the combat.... literally

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend the game in it's current state. Even after it's first "performance" update, the framerate is all over the place.I played the game half on Steam Deck and half on my Desktop PC. Both have horrible audio stutters the moment the frame rate fluctuates (going from 120 to 15 to 1). Audio stutter is also present when on a stable one (eg Steam Deck locked 30fps). In a game where taking in the sights and the atmosphere are a main draw, this completely rips you out of it.If you do play on Steam Deck, by god make sure it's on the SSD. The main issue seems to be with streaming assets in, so the moment you hit a point where it needs to load in a new zone, you're gonna get hit by the massive framedrops. (It's also funny since the problem gets worse the more you upgrade your hoverbike since going faster means it needs to load more)The art and story are nice. However, I do still have gripes even taking performance out of it.An example are unskipable cutscenes. If it's something new being shown? Okay I get that you can't skip it. When you are collecting the 80th Chum Egg I'm sorry but I got sick and tired of it real quick. Same goes for getting your masks. The cutscene for collecting some of the main story masks is the same. It lasts a while. AND YOU CAN'T SKIP IT. I was waiting on cashing those in when I felt I was near the end of the game. I spent my metro commute not playing the game, but just cashing in mask, after mask with the same long cutscene over and over.Also regarding the BOTW style stamina system. By itself I have no issues with it. The problem is if you hit exhaustion. You can walk while it recovers but the moment you don't they enter this panting animation for the full recovery time. And the issue worsens as you upgrade your stamina because it means that the wait time to get out of that "exhausted" state takes even LONGER.I really wanted to like this game. You can tell that there is passion behind it but. It's flaws just made it a worse and worse experience the more time I spent with it.I have done all the prerequisites to finish the game. Even close to getting all achievements by the looks of it (only missing 2 I think?) but I'm done.I really wanted to love this game but I can't. I still look forward to whatever projects the developers does next because it is clear that there is a vision behind it.

_childDocuments_.review: With 0 combat, the Breathe of the Wild and classic Tomb Raider style puzzles and traversing environment sucks you in massively, going so far as saying this is the perfect zen game. Nothing to worry or stress about, just simply enjoy your time with it's gorgeous soundtrack playing in the background. The highlight is the breathtaking environment to find yourself in. If I've not been playing the game, I've been stuck in photo mode. The cel-shaded aesthetic and colour palettes really highlight how mesmerising this game is to play.With the exception of one bug where the bike doesn't always come to you when you call, there's not really many negatives I've picked up. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale after seeing it appear in my recommended a few times, and I honestly didn't think too much of it at the time - and yet I really came to enjoy the game. It is open world, which I find to be off-putting in some cases as my attention span can be a little short and too much choice is a bit scary to me, and yet this game strikes a really wonderful balance of being big enough to get lost in and not so complex that the task seemed overwhelming. The premise of the game follows the main character through legitimately taking as much or as little time exploring as she wants until she can return to her clan, and so you as the player have a lot of freedom in how you want to tackle the amount of time and energy you put into it. There are some korok-like quests reminiscent of breath of the wild, but they're not compulsory to the game at all so don't be spooked by finding them.All in all the style is unique and fresh feeling, and the premise is sweet and very relaxing. I enjoyed the subtle customisation with bike parts and colours and outfit changes, but again these are not necessary mechanics if that's not your thing There is absolutely no combat or damage mechanic, so I really recommend this game to people who like to have a little amble around with low stakes.Finally onto my only real criticism which I think a few others also mentioned - bugs. If you're nervous to buy the game because of this, I cannot emphasise enough how minor they tend to be. I played through on PC and have had zero problems other than a few movement glitches, and frankly that's not a game breaker from a more indie game for me. I didn't have to close and reopen the game at any point for any bugs, but from what I heard from others this fixes issues immediately. The save mechanic is free at any time so if you're very worried about progressing and bugs, you can save at any time as many times as you need. Only downside for saving is there's no clear indication it saved like a symbol in the corner, but I found it still saved my progress perfectly everytime.All in all a very cozy game with a very sweet and relaxing vibe to it, I really recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a complete pleasure to play despite its many glitches. It quite clearly is heavily derived from Zelda Breath of the Wild, but still has a unique visual style, interesting lore, and vast environments that are significantly different from each other. There are a few very specific locations that did an amazing job at creating a pretty thorough sense of wonder. The climbing challenges it presents are fun, and the puzzles are ok.I wish so much that it could have fewer bugs, because there are MANY. Framerate issues, choppy sound, getting stuck on geometry, the hoverbike pretty consistently twirling in absurd ways, environment lighting shifting unnaturally, and there are more. I also wish the hoverbikes were more exciting to handle and that the bike with the best stats (which still didnt feel fast enough tbh) wasn't available for purchase so early.It's a real testament to the core gameplay of Sable that these bugs, which definitely made the experience less immersive, are still absolutely worth tolerating if you like open world exploration and platforming. I like this game quite a lot for the experience it gave me, and it could be polished up to be much more pleasurable.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is one of my favourite discoveries of 2023. I have always enjoyed games that reward exploration, even more so game that focuses solely on exploration. It's rare to find such games, without combat or pressure of any kind. Sable is just that.Before diving into what makes this game mechanically good, let me just say that the art is amazing. Every places you visit: old monuments, ancient ships, villages, desert landscape, everything is just so beautifully crafted. The color of the world and the night/day cycle, coupled with a superb soundtrack, makes every ride accross the desert a magical experience.The overall vibe of the game is super chill. All the characters you encounter are happy to see you and chat with you. Most of the game quests are fetch quests which mixes well with the exploration part. Most stuff you are requested to find will lineup with the places you want to explore.On the topic of exploration : Sable does exploration perfectly. You have all the freedom to go at your own pace. There is always something in the distance that will peek your interest. I can count on my fingers the number of time I wasn't sidetracked while going somewhere. There really is a feeling of wonder and amazement with every new discoveries.Also you are given the proper tools to orient yourself. Everything is thought out to make your journey as easy as possible. The map, compass, markers, fast travel, etc. Sable understands what so many games fail to do in order to let the player explore without frustration. The UI has been refined to not break the immersion and the flow of the games feels natural.Beside that the endurance mechanic is pretty forgiving and is more used as a way to prevent you to access an area early rather than punish the lack of pathing in you climb. At some point you can pretty much just go straight up without thinking and reach your goal. There are some minor annoyances (like fps drop is some areas, or the climbing behaving wonky at time) but I overlooked it completely given how perfect the journey and immersion was.

_childDocuments_.review: A game about the joys of exploration, and finding fun and meaning in freedom. A gorgeous game in many regards. the writing is wistful, charismatic, developed, and gorgeous in it's prose. It carries a lot of weight and can sometimes be the difference between a quest ending up as mundane or being genuinely fulfilling, emotional, and worth while, which it does more often than not in my opinion. The music sells this games quiet yet quirky atmosphere, perfectly reflecting the inhabitants you will be able to interact with on your journey. Japanese Breakfast have done an amazing job here. Visually this is absolutely stunning with some wonderful colour theory, designs, and vistas to drink in. Some quests are better than others, some of which are a joy to engage with while others are more simple in their design. The map is a satisfying size with enough structures and secrets to find to keep moment to moment game play fun and interesting for a very decent amount of time, as well as being consistently visually interesting through varying environments and structures. This game excels in it's atmosphere and gives off a wonderful impression of everything in that world having purpose and presence which is difficult to achieve in a post apocalyptic open world setting. some issues with the game revolve around glitches, as well as some unfinished smoothing out of the movement system. Certain inclines will have you climbing them as if they're stairs making the climb very difficult and cumbersome. A few audio glitches. I kept getting a particular audio cue that I realised was an events audio cue playing out randomly when it wasn't supposed to, as well as some issues with the music and sound effects cutting in and out inexplicably. Menu usage also had some problems. There were a few moments where I would be unable to scroll through my items or through dialogue options which was annoying. There were also some strange pop in and outs with certain assets which made for some weird moments and frustrating game play. though these were few and far between. If I could change anything about the game the only thing I'd do is add some extra bike controls that would allow for more stable riding. As it stands, movement on the bike can be awkward and requires far too much effort to not suddenly go twisting and turning like a boulder crashing down a hill. I would perhaps add some  controls for the elevation of the bike to allow for more planning and better moment to moment engagement. perhaps this could be a boost so players could cushion their fall or get a bit of extra air time when they go over a large jump. But that's just my personal view on it. Overall I really loved this game. So much so that I hardly played anything else while I played it. If you're someone who loves open world games and wants the satisfaction of being able to explore every inch of a beautifully crafted world accompanied by some stellar music and writing, then this game is very much for you! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overview: Sable a great game but I would not recommend it to everyone. It is a great exploration/puzzle game in a unique world but It can start very slow and there is no action or tension in the game at all. There are also a lot of tedious tasks and some things that could be cool that fall flat. The game is very short which is honestly great as I think the length makes the theme and experience make a better impact. Tips that I feel like would have improved my experience: (Barely Spoilers)1.Find bike parts that make your bike faster and buy them. 2. There are little collectible worms. The place to turn them in is pretty close to the exit to the tutorial zone but I don't think anything leads you there. Turning in the Worms can help make things less tedious. 3. You can sell things to merchants. This ones on me as I just didn't notice the Sell Menu until later. ____The Good:Sable has a wonderful world, characters and story and the mechanics for traversing this world can be entertaining. There is a fun vehicle, climbing, puzzles and an interesting glide mechanic that are interesting and can still feel great after hours of playing.I believe the developers crafted something really beautiful and unique with this game. When this game is at its peak I feel like I can be immersed in this majestic alien world and culture that the developers envisioned.The Bad:There are a lot of interesting plot or world developments that I feel like do not get explored to their full potential or just end without a satisfying payoff. Cool quest lines that just sort of end. Most characters or plots only have one quest and then have no impact on the rest of the experience. Some of this may be intentional due to the themes of the game but I just wish some of the concepts, quests and locations got better conclusions.The Stamina and Bike are terrible at the start of the game and make travelling and climbing a chore when they should be exciting. Even with upgrades, the bike doesn't go very fast and I feel like faster speeds would have made it more satisfying to ride around and travel. I also felt like most of the fun or interesting bike parts were kind of overshadowed by the buy-able upgrades for speed which made getting unique upgrades less satisfying. I don't know if I missed something obvious or got unlucky but I did not figure out how to upgrade stamina until I was almost done with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Sable. I came to it after an intense couple of FromSoft games and it was the perfect antidote; an ambient adventure game with zero combat set in a reasonably small open world map. The beautiful cel shaded art style speaks for itself, seemingly heavily inspired by the late French comix genius Mœbius and Hayao Miyazaki's Nausicaä (itself inspired by Mœbius' work.) The desert world it conjures is immersive and full of enough mysteries to encourage thorough exploration without overwhelming the player and the wonderfully soothing Japanese Breakfast soundtrack gently washes in and out as day and night cycles pass and new areas are charted on the back of Simoon, your trusty sentient hover bike. It's a meditative experience for sure. This effect is only marred by the frequent performance problems and audio glitches, but to the tiny dev team's credit there are regular patches rolling out to address these issues and even add new features such as a camera mode. The gameplay itself is fairly simplistic, amounting to little more than easter egg hunts and fetch quests, but the stories of its characters and the lore of the world are quietly fascinating. It comes off like Zelda BOTW or Fumito Ueda's more platform-y efforts without the combat to interrupt the relaxed vibe and while there are annoyances such as camera glitches and collision weirdness, if you're familiar with Ueda's work then you can probably forgive Sable these flaws. Other titles brought to mind as I journeyed through the Midden were Panzer Dragoon Saga for its exotic mysterious atmosphere, Fez for its amazing soundtrack and puzzling and in its joy of platforming and exploration, even the 3D Mario games. I don't summon such names lightly and though I don't think Sable comes close to matching those games at their best, if enough of the rough edges can be smoothed off then I can see myself returning to this magical game many, many times in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish that I could recommend this game. It's beautiful, the story is nice and simple, there's a wonderful soundtrack by Japanese Breakfast and you meet some interesting characters and encounter some wonderful environments along the way. BUTthis game is super buggy mess.I've tried this on multiple systems and:1. the frame rate has huge dips2. the bike is really unsatisfying to ride it feel like it's always crashing and swerving and not smooth at all. 3. the audio feels like it goes out of sync and sometimes will get stuck repeating a sound from earlier. 4. the map and location marker system is horrid and deleting markers doesn't always work and sometimes the active quest marker gets stuck and you end up just riding into nowhere. 5. The bike auto return pathfinding stinks and often gets stuck causing you to lose your bike.6. and many other small things like the audio just stacking ontop of each other and clipping and massive framedrops that don't recover.tldr: it's a lovely game with a beautiful atmosphere but it's just way too buggy to be enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable has an interesting setting and neat aesthetics, but ultimately the game falls flat for me. While it's good for indie developers to be ambitious, it's equally important they understand their potential limits.Sable is an open world game where you can climb anything, a coming age story, places to explore! Except all of it is shallow. Sure you can climb stuff, but there's never a point outside of a handful of fixed locations. The story and character interactions are very simple. Humankind is probably on the brink of collapse here with it's 20 total people in the world. There's little challenge to anything that you explore, no sharp edges to get hurt on. My interpretation of the story was also that childhood/teenage is full of mystery and fun and exploration, but once you step into adulthood, you have to give it all up and do one thing for the rest of your life and never travel or do anything interesting in your life again which I hated.There's also lots of performance problems and an aggravating camera to contend with.
