_childDocuments_.review: For people who love exploring games & having a chill experience, 100% recommend this game. You can play at your own pace & there's no rushing your journey. Without spoiling too much, I really feel like this is what I, as the player, am experiencing the journey, not just the character Sable. I have fun interacting with the characters in the game & love how mysterious this game can be. Even when coming back to the game, after not having played for a while, I can still pick it back up. The music is great & I absolutely love the art design they chose for this game.This game made me feel nostalgic & emotional. And it felt like coming back home <310/10 Would play again if I could play it for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a chill and relaxing game to play with no stress whatsoever. It's game where you can immerse yourself after a long day after work and mindlessly explore the beautiful world around you. The only gripe I have with this game is it's weird performance issues. I'm not sure if this happens to everybody but sometimes the fps dips so low that it stutters the game very often. I usually restart the game when this happens and it fixes itself. I see that this game is heavily inspired by BOTW and that is very much a good thing. I enjoyed both games thoroughly.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get past the glitchiness of this game then it is awesome, however I can't recommend this game to anyone based off of the performance of it. Minus performance issues, this game is incredible, like many others have said: Sable is BOTW with a sweeter story. The side quests are meaningful and feel as though you are making true connections with every character you meet along your journey of self discovery.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem! The exploratory element of this game is exactly what a curious player wishes for: an openworld, a humming companion > customable glider and logical puzzles, that are sometimes tricky but never too hard to solve - patience is recommended.From time to time it is a bit wonky, there are some stutters while climbing or interacting with objects. And while fishing there seems to be an issue, that causes freezing. But all in all this game is beautiful too be in, to look at and to listen to. Please create some merch for it, I would like to have a nice tote or mug or shirt.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanics-light zen experience in a really beautiful world. There's so much joy in just seeing the day turn to night, shadows slowly swallow the cell-shaded landscapes.Despite lack of complexity, the world really tempts you to explore it.Wasn't expecting the writing in a game like this to be good, but it really is! Nuance portrayed in very few words.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I had too many bugs issues along with controller issues. This game is amazingly stunning and really beautiful, but it does not run smoothly. It hurts to know they were so close to something utterly great, and supremely missed the mark in all other areas. I'm sorry I'll never know the end of this story, it wasn't compelling enough to compel me through all the bugs I endured.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: this game was everything to me. if you're into big emotions Oh Boy is this the game for you. i'm never going to forget the feeling of running around eccria for the first time and the sensation of complete joy that shook me because oh my god, there's a city out here. i agonised over the decision you have to make in the end and even when i did settle all of me was wishing for more. this core sort of conflict of the game really appealed to me, of having to choose who you're going to be for the rest of your life. the journey of trying to figure that out was so worth it, though. even though the ending of the game left me feeling sort of empty inside (in a good way?) i've still be rewarded by all the people i've met and the things i've done. all of that was far more substantial that whatever mask i chose. also simoon made me cry. a hover bike made me cry. man.all that being said, this game is incredibly buggy. sometimes simoon would be driving and sable would just like fall off the seat and stand several metres back while simoon keeps going. sometimes npcs or animals wouldn't appear or wouldn't be doing the actions that they were supposed to be doing for you to complete a task. etc etc etc i'm probably missing some. i would like to stress that none of the bugs i ever experienced were game-breaking, as i was able to remedy all of them by just saving, going back to the menu, and loading back in. however, these bugs can be confusing, frustrating, and cause a huge loss of immersion for the player. i understand anyone who found themselves upset with the game for these reasons.overall though i would really really really recommend sable to anyone. yeah the bugs suck but the overall experience i got playing the game was worth it regardless. huge emotions from this wonderful game. p.s. i 100%'d this bad boy and got every single chum and mask so i'd say i know my stuff. godspeed gamers i love you
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable adventure! Lots of puzzles, collections, and hover bikes! Large map with really cool themes. There were a couple of bugs in a few of the puzzle dungeons, but it just added to the complexity of figuring out how to solve it with the bug. I was still able to complete the game and find/collect all the items/pieces. The art style(Moebius) is why I wanted to play this game and not knowing what kind of game this was going to be, I was pleasantly surprised.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some serious flaws. Most of the quests seem unfinished, there are so many rendering issues that they had to put a weird outline filter on everything.... but most of all I encountered a horrible bug where the vehicles all move extremely slowly. The vehicle you start with moves slower than walking, and I found myself running from place to place just trying to find a faster vehicle. When I finally found one it was only 50% faster than walking. It's absurd because about 1/10th of the quests require moving faster than the fastest vehicle in the game.The other bugs (like what happens when you drive your scooter into a lake and then get back on it) are more amusing than game breaking since this is a casual game.... but the slow moving scooters fill the entire game with frusturation.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, buggy game. The atmosphere of the world in sable is amazing. Spent hours just enjoying the world as I traveled through it. The quests and puzzles aren't very hard to figure out and accomplish, but enough of a challenge to keep you engaged. I loved all the characters I met and some of the conversations I had with them actually made me introspective. Unfortunately, it is not a stable game. I personally didn't run into major game crashing bugs, but things like the bike not loading, character interaction option not showing up, can't select items in a menu, etc did happen. The fix was always easy though, just save the game, exit to title screen, then load the save file. Game doesn't take long to load back up, so it was usually less than 30 sec to get back to what I was doing. These bugs weren't a constant issue, but enough to make note of. I would say I had to restart a save file about 15-18 times over the course of my 20 hour play through. The game is a relaxing experience and I do recommend diving into this world just for the experience of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: If you like:-slower paced games-exploration without any rush-the aesthetics of Moebius, Nausicaa, and/or Kino's Journey-insects and other crawliesThen you will probably enjoy this game! There is a little clunkiness at times, but nothing so far that breaks the game. There's plenty to explore as well, so any slight issues can be forgiven easily by the expanse of the game and fact it is a small team release.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's a very relaxing experience without any expectations. Just go out and explore the world with all it's wonders, the characters and quests are quirky and fun to follow. It's one of the only games where I felt compelled to complete all the achievements just to have an incentive to explore more.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Been looking forward to this game since Greg was posting clips of bikes and sand. Everything from the music, art style, controls and writing, this game is a joy to play. Minor graphical issues sometimes but plagued with some pretty glaring audio bugs like tracks endlessly playing and what I could only describe as start-and-stop on the metal scrap pickups. Not terribly jarring but can be quite the inconvenience with how often a restart is needed to fix it.Other than that, this game is wonderful and more than worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I could describe this game is if you took Breath of the Wild, Death Stranding, and Outer Wilds and meshed it all into one game. That is what Sable is, but with its own peaceful twist.This game is all about exploring what the world has to offer and finding yourself along the process. A very interesting coming of age story that is almost told like a novel.It is a great experience to have and I am glad I played it.HOWEVER- beware of one flaw I found in this game:Do not expect there to be a grand hidden story that unfolds the more you discover.Yes, there are storylines you can follow. Some are interesting, some are not. But I have never completed one and was starstruck amazed by it....so unless you are just head over heels in love with this game, don't drag out your playthrough longer than you feel like it needs to be.(Once you are satisfied with what you've done and explored, go do the final quest.)The experience is a calm adventure about exploring and growing with a message about finding your path in life. That is all there is to it, and it is a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever felt like becoming a teenage member of the sandpeople from Tatooine in a touching coming of age story illustrated by Mobius while listening to chill-hop? Nor have I, but you want to now, don't you? It's a hell of a ride and it cured my ADHD. Actually no, it didn't, but it certainly felt like it should! It's a monumentally creative, fascinating journey that is surprisingly deep, extremely fulfilling, oddly calming and incredibly visually impressive. 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very qualified "yes", mostly because the game is still unpolished. I had so many UI glitches and audio bugs, saving and restarting the game was a matter of course. At the end, a background soundtrack just would not stop playing at the top of everything else, no matter what I did. So ... I'd wait.But the graphics are very interesting, and there are the seeds of a truly great game here. It just didn't come to fruition, this time around I think. It's an okay game. But nothing too special, unfortunatly.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of my favorite games of all time. Maybe not for everyone, but I've never felt more present and connected to a game's world, and a central character. The game so effortlessly puts you into the mind of sable, and the way the world is constructed, I never once felt like I was doing something that sable *wouldn't*. The gap between gameplay and roleplay just disappeared, and I've never  had something quite like that happen before.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, the game is full of tiny bugs, but none of them were red flags for me. The nice atmosphere, the unusual art, and the feeling of freedom were all deeply appreciated. You can teleport on any of the location you visit, so even if you get stuck, you can always teleport to a place that is less than 2 minutes away. The game is like a Zelda (for switch) game, but very zen because there is no fighting, just poetic moments. A few infos gathered here and there let you know a bit more about the planet you live on ("Midden") and how  which is nice: it builds the story and the environment. A few puzzle here and there but nothing hard, it is really a game to explore a world, marvel at some of the nice monuments, and pick up (sometimes interesting) quests along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with an amazing art-style. That said it is filled to the brim with bugs and glitches, stuff will fall through walls if you're not careful and with no way of resetting it, this causes you to be locked out of some puzzles. Audio can be very glitchy especially when you have frame drops. Also for some godforsaken reason the camera is tied to your frame rate.other then some minor annoyances this game is very relaxing and a great pick up at a discounted price.P.S. I'm excited to 100% it because they have added achievements for a fishing mini game that isn't in the game yet and that is stopping me from 100% it right now,.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest selling point is the extremely unique Artstyle, I haven't seen before, but that's where my praise sadly ends.The game feels pointless, I'm not exploring a world and just begin to stumble upon mysteries and civilizations, I'm following quest markers in an empty world.The Storyline feels alright, but fails to engage me into the rest of the game. The NPCs were forgotten the moment i existed the conversation.My biggest issue is sadly the animations and the artstyle funnily enough. Lots of stuff keeps clipping together, the bike keeps touching the floor for the smallest of bumps, every animation of every NPCs is in this weird frame by frame thingy, while everything around it is as fast as the framerate allows and the artstyle sometimes makes certain unimportant models and areas way to cluttered and drawing 100% of the attention, from the thing i should be looking forward to exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like lore? Do you like exploration and adventure in a lovely open-world? Do you not hate sand despite it being coarse, rough, irritating, and getting everywhere? Then hop on your Jetbike because Sable is the game for you.Jokes aside, this is a really nice adventure game with some great stories and memorable characters. It does have its bugs, but they're not game-breaking or too numerous, and for a new studio I couldn't be more impressed. I was drawn in by the world of Sable and hope I'll get to see more of its universe and lore as a whole in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It's pretty, it's engaging, and it is the perfect length for what it is trying to be. However, it is buggy and my game in particular stuttered every time it auto saved, which was highly unpleasant. Despite these flaws, the game holds up as highly entertaining. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game. At first the world feels really big but by the end it's pretty small. The graphics are nice but performance is not that great at times. Movement can be buggy in places which is not the best considering that most of the mechanics are based on movement. In some ways it resembles the movement in breath of the wild but with less polish. I found the game nice and relaxing with an unobtrusive story.  It took me about 20 hours to 100% the game but it can probably be done quicker.Also - the UI is really buggy with mouse/keyboard.The game does not benefit from having a fishing minigame.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly think Sable might be designed for toddlers. It has amazing visuals, a killer soundtrack, and virtually no gameplay at all. I'm fine with an indie game being broken and buggy, but I've seen zero challenges or creativity in any of the puzzles or fetch quests in the 8 hours I played. You can hardly call these "puzzles" when they all consist of "climb wall, pick up battery, put battery in hole." Platforming and racing are so bare-bones easy, you could beat this entire game in an induced coma. I knew there would be no enemies or combat, but I expected at least SOME creativity or difficulty, some reason to go out and explore this big, beautiful open world.I finally quit and uninstalled it because no matter where I went or what amazing new vistas I saw, there was nothing worthwhile to discover there, just some stupid collectible worms and scrap metal. What an absolute waste of money.Buy Outer Wilds instead. It's a million times more creative than this vapid, brainless garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best video game experiences I've ever had. The open world and soundtrack are phenomenal. I got to the end of the story but didn't get all of the achievements because it felt like my character's journey had come to a good and natural end. I love the choice I made and don't regret it.I have genuinely good memories from playing this game and reflect on it a lot. I don't think there will be anything like it again
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I'm most likely going to add this to my list of top 3 favourite games. Its like if someone mixed the game journey, star wars and exploration together, absolutely loving it (i'm reaching the end of the game). The game design style is unique and beautiful and there are many fascinating things to find. The only negative thing i have to say is that some of the small quests confused me and i resorted to google to help (there were some great tips and tricks to be found) - i do generally find quest based games confusing so its also possibly down to human error.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely EPIC!Really loved this game, from start to finish. To say that it's heavily inspired by TLoZ: Breath of the Wild is an understatement. The devs have stated as much themselves. But, it so much more than a copy of the exploration and climbing mechanics of Zelda. It has heart for days. It gave me strong vibes of Ray Bradbury's "The Martian Chronicles", or something out of Asimov's Foundation Series, with how science has devolved into something of a religion, but not quite. Worldbuilding is great, art direction is great, gameplay is relaxed and laid back. There's a really charming story in the middle of this. I really loved the game. A very well made piece of entertainment art. Would love a sequel, possibly with a bit more open world and slightly larger scale. Until then, I'll probably have to go for a new playthrough of Breath of the Wild to get my fix. It's been awesome being you, Sable. It was an honor to accompany you on your gliding.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Even with all of the bugs in this game, I've had one of the most immersive experiences in this game that I have had in a while. I mainly credit this to the wonderful soundtrack with performances from Japanese Breakfast (a new favorite band of mine) that allowed me to be fully enveloped by the neat little world this two man dev team has developed. Perhaps as more patches arrive, this game will become a polished masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Like other reviews have said, it's essentially the Legend of Zelda: The Breath of the Wild without combat. I enjoy exploring and solving puzzles as well as learning about the mysterious world built around the nomadic traditional life that the main character, Sable, lives through. It is a very relaxing game to play as well.I dislike the few bugs that I've experienced while playing. To name a few, there are audio glitches, menu bugs, and a the hoverbike's silly navigation system when you call for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Breath of the Wild + Trigun + Animal Crossing.  Once the game gets going I was really immersed in scouring maps for hidden structures, working my way through the 20 simultaneous fetch quests, and finding new species of butterflies.  It's definitely rough around some edges and a couple of the puzzles were a touch obtuse which required checking a guide to make sure I wasn't doing them wrong, but overall it's a real gem.  I highly recommend it for something so detailed and crafted without relying on fighting and battle mechanics - in a way, the pacifism immersed me the most as exploring the world and helping others with quests felt very grounded.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10 needs some general fixeshow can people say so much and at the same time still say nothing?clicks to talk to a persongreetings child.farewell child!hop on the bike and the camera gets stuck well i drive off, only fix is exiting out of the game. reloading the game without closing it didnt fix the problemaudio cracklinggot my bike stuck, reload timegot stuck on a rock and had to reloadgot stuck walking strait, had this happen twice. had to reset the gamevisual stuttering
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: this game is just horribly unoptimized. Broken geometry, laggy framerate, z-fighting, broken textures, everything you can think of is in here. Not to mention janky movement and climbing. Just play Outer Wilds, it executes the themes and gameplay of exploration 10 times better, its far more polished, and is objectively better. This game has maybe one interesting quest in it, while Outer Wilds is entirely interesting from start to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Typically these platforming/puzzle games don't interest me for very long but this game's mystery and exploration really drew me in.  I first started playing it on pc game pass during a covid leave and then when it left game pass I got it on sale later on.  The game does have bugs: audio tears, stuttering video and the airbike likes to flip out over small bumps but nothing that makes the game unplayable.  The game has been out a while and the creators of the game don't seem interested in fixing those as of yet.  It's a game full of mystery, wonder and soul searching.  There is no dying, killing, or fall damage in this game just a calm play through.  Though the game could provide better hints/info on quests as I had to look up on the internet help for some quests where the game info was lacking.The most recent addon is rather underwhelming, some fishing for a mask and catching butterflies for.....well no reward really just the "fun" of getting them for a scientist.  Too bad they couldn't have added another land to the map with a few more interesting quests.Its worth getting unless you really must have nonstop combat/death in your games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Surreal and beautiful. If you're looking for an immersive open world to wander around and get lost in, this is it. A bit underwhelming compared to some bigger titles in the open-world genre. But for a less exciting title, this world has beauty, depth, and a scale that leaves you breathless and wondering for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a piece of art, it will drag you in visually and then keep you interested through the large open world that allows for a lot of exploration. Although the perspective can get a bit awkward and the story is a bit boring at times, I would overall recommend the game if you are looking for a relaxing experience that leans into a unique art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I liked it when I started. But when I booted the game again, I now had broken sound. Seems there is very little to do to fix it. Lots of mentions of bugs in the game, stutter, etc. And that it gets worst as you go on.For a game with quite the sound ambiance, having said sound stutter completely break this for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: It's a no pressure relaxing game.  If the best thing about open world games for you is exploring than this is perfect.  I wish the world was a bit bigger, but that’s my only real complaint.  The art style reminds me of Moebius’s work which is what drew me to the game in the first place. The only thing I wish I had done differently was explore the first area more and find the queen early in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Others have described this game of having strong elements of being 'like Breath of the Wild but without combat' and it feels like an apt description. I have absolutely loved playing it. It's a very chill and easygoing experience with a bit of platforming and puzzle-solving, but otherwise just relaxing exploration of a varied desert landscape, just you and your hoverbike. There's fun heart to the encounters and characters you meet along the way, interesting ancient mysteries to slowly uncover, and it's just all in all been a really pleasant, fun, and relaxing experience. For me personally it's been more or less the perfect sort of game, very much the kind of game I want to find and play more of, and I would eagerly play more games like this. It felt long and content-rich enough to satisfy, yet I would jump at any DLC or a sequel in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored every minute of this game. From the killer art style to the chill atmosphere of just exploring this magical world I cannot recommend this game enough. I understand it's not going to be for everyone. You have to get invested in the world because all you are going to be doing is gliding from one location to another, solving some quests, doing some platforming or solving some puzzles. And that's it, that's the game but if the world gets its hooks into you then it will be more than enough
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this so much. What a captivating experience - the freedom to go anywhere, the total lack of conflict, the poetry and depth of interactions, the soundtrack, the incredible locations, the whole thing was magical and I can't stop thinking about it. I was sad to get to the end, and I wish I could experience it all again for the first time, but it's the kind of thing I know I'll keep dipping into - just to spend a while driving around, visiting places old and new, seeing a few old friends, climbing up high and watching the sun go down (and then come up again).
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: There are definitely some lingering bugs in this game, though I never experienced a game breaking bug. Mostly menu's not working as intended, music persisting when its not meant to etc. Having said that the art style and quality of the world to explore with just you and your glider make for a phenomenal game. Highly recommend to anyone interested in exploration for the sake of exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you for that wholesome story, that was lovely :)While it was a bit short for my taste, I think it was well worth the $25 in worldbuilding aloneThe most fulfilling parts of this game is piece by piece uncovering the history of the cultures you encounter, it's really captivating in a way I haven't seen in an RPG in a very long time
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really good, the only downside is that there are frequent audio glitches and the frame rate is unstable at best.  There were also occasional glitches like not being able to navigate a merchant menu or pick up an object or things like that.  All that said, it was a really great story and game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!Something very nice about simply exploring the world at your own pace without the violence.I initially fell in love the game due to the art style that reminded me of Jean Giraud (The Incal, Arzach)Add on to that with the score by Japanese Breakfast and you get a beautiful atmosphere.Well done!!
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful. I haven't gotten too far into it, I just finished the windmill task at Burnt Oak, but I am already so excited for what I will find.The music is perfection, and really adds to the experience. The visual work is phenomenal, and I find myself in awe at points, looking over a vast horizon on top of a giant boulder. As a freshman in college, this game spoke to me on a personal level. Sable is scared to leave, and misses her home, but knows she must find herself in the real world, and she will find happiness and fulfillment in her journey. Overall, amazing game 100000000000000000/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Love open world setting and its lore. The story of you going out to explore and eventually choose a calling, though simple, was very effective. I loved the bike customization, and the puzzles and quests were pretty good, though I felt there wasn't really anything to do in the open world between the major locations, so exploration didn't feel as rewarding. Still, that first time I came out of the tutorial area and discovered the wind tower in the distance, music playing as I made my way to it, is something I won't forget.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: no hate to the devs, plenty of hate to sweet baby.but putting that hate aside i can't in good conscience recommend this game as it is just an open world game with no combat and thus falls to the same tired tropes and the usual open world gimmicks without anything to help it stand out in anyway game play wise, and thus it feels like bad busy work.the art style is fabulous, and is what drew me in, but it was as vast as an ocean, deep as a puddle.there is a story to it, but i must warn that there is SOOOOOO many text boxes to read i stopped after i got my first speeder, the only way i could stomach this much talking is if there were actual voice acting, because i would have liked to pay attention to the story being told but you cant expect anyone nowadays to read a book with their video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played an MMO but all you did was stuff around with the level design trying to get where you're not supposed to go?This is like that but you're supposed to try and get where you're not supposed to go. No combat, just pure exploration and abusing the hell out of the games climbing/jumping mechanics to reach new heights so you can ... uhh .. find a new T-shirt or something.Its a lot of fun actually. Vast open areas, gorgeous visuals with a unique art style. A little glitchy sometimes, especially with UI stuff. If you have a solid enough PC/GFX card it should run fairly decent.All up, I'm loving it so far after 4 hours of play.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: it's a "loose" game in that you don't *have* to do anything, you can just wander around. it's also pretty flat achievement-wise, with only basic quests. that's all ok as the world is beautifully realized with stunning art direction. the feel of riding your bike over the desert dunes is amazing.i also appreciated the space they give you to inhabit conversations. a lot of game writing can feel very deterministic, but your character often equivocates and hedges in conversation with others. it's a compelling twist that rang true for me.it can be a bit glitchy, with some issues in collision detection and menu navigation. but those are dwarfed by what it does well. it's a beautiful experience and i'd highly recommend it, especially to fans of the artist Moebius, by whom it was clearly inspired.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed Sable and highly recommend it. I think the story and open world aspect work together wonderfully, and i think the game is a great adventure to go through. Pros: Fantastic fun riding around and just simply exploring. Moments of, "I wonder if I can climb that? I need to find out."Just looking out at the scenic views and watching the sun move across the sky. Cons:The textures and graphics can be a little choppy.The puzzles don't take much thought to figure out. It's uh kinda of a lot of empty environment to travel through.Final Opinion: Worth the buy, and the joy is in the journey, not the destination.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The graphics are vibrant and the overall game experience was very immersive, I was hooked. If you’re into exploring and discovering new places while completing quests and collecting interesting items, this is for you. It’s a peaceful game with puzzles and riddles involved. I recommend building stamina by collecting chum eggs to make climbing easier. Bike and clothing customization was cool but I wished they showed the specs of the items prior to purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Greatest game of all time. I am connected with the characters, I am in love with the world. Although my hours are low, I've spent a mental eternity in this game. I love Sable, and you will too. This game gets so much hate and although you might get turned away by that, those reviews are left by the type of people who want action. I've seen bad reviews and harsh comments, clicked on their profiles, and what do you see? Thousands of hours in FPS, twelve minutes in Sable. Not only have they got a bad basis for you opinion, they probably haven't built Simoon yet. Please buy the game, you'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the early game is fun and adventurous with an eye-catching art style I found myself often bored as the world feelt barren, not that it's a desert but the content being spread way too thin with most places being onestop spots. The quests are decent and the puzzles feel underutilized but the writing is above average albeit wordy.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is a wonderful game.It's relaxed, interesting, compelling, and with an art style that will stick with you. The BoTW-inspired gameplay feels right at home in the world, which feels built for the overarching plot rather than the other way around. I've enjoyed this game immensely and will likely continue playing it to the 100% point, but not without annoyance.Technically, this game is a trainwreck.I never got above 60% and 50% GPU and CPU utilization respectively, and yet I've rarely struggled to maintain a steady 60fps. Even with settings turned way down and the framerate capped to 30, this game rarely holds a steady framerate. I wouldn't mind it running poorly, but the constant dipping in open areas is remarkably irritating. Combine that with the occasional visual glitches and misaligned geometry (which by themselves would hardly be worth mentioning for an indie game like this) and it's clear this game needed a few more weeks, if not months, if not a year to iron out the backend.Fortunately, we live in a world where updates exist! Where developers can seamlessly keep working on a game after it's release, and the improvements they create can be seamlessly integrated into every existing copy. So what have the devs done with the nearly two years they've had since release to make this game playable? From what I can tell, not much. Granted, I've only started playing this game now, so I can't exactly do a side by side. But from what I've been able to find the developers have done little to nothing to make this game not just playable, but enjoyable. And that's a huge disservice to the game they've created. I can't in good conscience add to the pile of (well deserved!) good reviews without letting prospective buyers know there are problems with this game, and problems with any team that would deem this an acceptable product to sell.That having been said...I do hope a sequel is on the horizon. One that not only expands upon the wonderful world the dev team have built, but the technology that allowed it to be presented in slideshow form.

_childDocuments_.review: After just finishing the game, I can say I highly recommend it. It's relaxing and fun, with reasonably challenging puzzles. The story is quite nice, giving us interesting lore that we piece together along the way.I think the biggest selling point is the atmosphere, most notably the graphics, which many here have pointed out seem largely inspired by French comics artist Moebius. As a fan of many decades, I can easily imagine his characters like Arzach or Major Grubert traversing this environment. In fact, I ended up spending a lot of game time wishing there was a Moebius game, or wishing this was a Moebius game instead. In any case, the game looks great. I've heard many people complain about the lack of shading, and I can understand how that might be a problem, but I found it was something I could get used to quickly and was essential for immersing myself in the old style comic book coloring.But the atmosphere doesn't rely on visuals alone. The background music is great too. It gives everything a vast, lonely, and sometimes light feeling. It's distinct, and not too generic. Actually, parts of it does, in fact, sound very similar to Moebius' Arzach TV show from 2003.That said, the game is a bit buggy. Some puzzles I was sure I was solving correctly would not finish. Restarting the game would suddenly fix the problem. Though the pop-up commands were useful, many of the keyboard commands were not shown in the options, making you guess, or search around by process of elimination. The backspace command was a particularly odd choice of leaving a menu instead of esc. Calling my bike usually didn't work.Others have also complained about the night time look. I didn't mind it too much, but it is quite washed out. In that way, it is rather faithful to the comics, but can be dreary game play, as everything is almost one tone. I would strongly suggest keeping it, but having a sleep option. In fact, it would be fun to have your character take out a bed roll, start a campfire, and sleep through the night.Pros:- Light, poignant, sci-fi story- Beautiful, atmospheric visuals- Unique and immersive soundtrack- Relaxing, but challenging game playCons:- A bit buggy- Needs more complete Options menuOverall, this game was a memorable experience. The story likes to often point out why we enjoy adventure, and that doing things for the first time is a big part of that. I guess that's why they give you the choice to finish the game, or continue roaming the world. There isn't a particularly heavy message here, but it is thought provoking at times and ultimately enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: At the date of writing, I cannot recommend this to anyone who wants what this game is clearly trying to deliver. It's not because "the game is bad lol", there is much more nuance to this sentiment that really needs to be considered here. To elucidate, the world that Shedworks has built for this experience is in many ways perfect. There is rich lore delivered to the player in ways that would feel like second nature to anyone who's experienced free-form open world games in the past.  (BoTW) is an often-drawn comparison, and that's fair in only the most high level, broad strokes fashion.The world of  is truly rich, but one could also make the argument that the physical world itself is so vast and bereft of life that you'd really have to turn over every rock to find it. There's truth to that in . You can often find yourself in moments where you have essentially 'cleared' a city or camp of activities with almost no indication of where to go (and more importantly - why to go anywhere). This is a problem solved by a few separate but cooperative elements. Firstly, the characters you encounter along your journey will clue you in often enough as to what other regions or points of interest surround that particular area, there are dedicated cartographers that will pretty bluntly guide you - and for the players who like to look at and touch everything, there are some arbitrarily placed signposts with  cardinal directions (not sure how or why that is).Something else that will likely pop into a players mind is that there is not exactly much to do in the world except go somewhere else. Typically this time would be dedicated to some kind of combat, but it is well understood that  intentionally has removed all forms of violent solutions from the design of the game and there's nothing wrong with that - it's rather refreshing. But this space could be dedicated to a slew of activities that would have truly raised the engagement floor and expanded game play loops in a way that wouldn't have altered the ethos or core design of the world.The first hour or so, you are frequently interacting with characters that are obviously designed to tutorialize the very few core functions and features that Sable can use during her Gliding. It is this experience followed by the sharp lack thereof that will drive you to seek out more people in the world. Without getting into spoiled specifics, the characters you encounter all have unique personalities that don't always fall into super basic stereotypes. There is true reward for players who take the time to invest some emotion into each character's scenario.This is where the experience of  starts to garner a bit of a bruise. The bike that Sable constructs for herself is a really awesome and fundamentally a fun bit to imagine having outside of the game! However, the honeymoon phase was unceremoniously cut short due to some very odd behaviors that seem to be attributed to a really lackluster physics implementation. The bike will wobble around when landing from even really small jumps, which is not ideal since the entire world is comprised of terrain that should lend itself to really fun traversal.If you find yourself far from your bike, you can call it. But, it is a genuine gamble if your bike makes its way back to you in a manner that makes it useful. I've found my bike happy to return to me inside walls, under terrain, willingly drowning itself, or just simply not complying at all - stopping itself visibly hundreds of yards away from me.Running and climbing share a common stamina pool, which makes plenty of sense. However, the actual movement of that stamina indicator is not linear, rather cubic or quadratic. This makes estimating how much stamina you actually have left more of a guess. Now granted, in my eight hours of play, there are few climbing scenarios in which I wasn't able to actually get to the next ledge and recoup stamina to continue my exploration, but its an odd design choice for a UI element that is purely meant to inform.Oh goodness, the bugs. In no particular order: Physics, UI/UX, Audio, Shaders - all have bugs that start to infest the experience.This are not many elements of the game that specifically depend on physical models to operate. But the ones that do, notably the incoherent behavior of Simoon, break the polish that  really deserves.For a PC release, the navigation of menus to include inventory, maps and quests carries almost none of the nearly ubiquitous staples of how menus should work in a game. There have been countless instances of the mouse no longer working at all in menus that require the entire PC to restart in order to resolve. If/when a player pauses or moves between certain menu screens, I'm greeted with my desktop for a few frames before returning quickly back to the game, something I've yet to experience in any game compiled in any engine - particularly Unity.As an audio designer myself, this is just painful. But none of the issues here require a background in the field to identify as broken. The seemingly random but frequent instances of really poor polling of sounds effects is truly an experience that causes genuine unease. The main menu sounds clash with the (very nice) theme. Random sound effects from instances that have not been cued will play. The sound of scrap chests are entirely too loud. Some environmental sounds (like that of a ship interior) will linger for hours before another triggered track (such as a machinist shop) crushes the entire mix into inaudible garbage. Without seeing exactly what logic is driving these issues in Wwise or the native Audio Engine, I don't have a single clue how to remedy this, but with a game that needs to deliver serenity, this needs to be a top priority.Yes, the stylized shaders are pretty and really innovative. Crushing an entire vista scene into a handful of colors sounds easy on paper, but really difficult to execute, and I appreciate that. However, what I interpret as an attempt to salvage performance due to excessive draw calls, things like shadow elements and surface details often get drawn far too close to the camera. A URP game with such sparse geometry with this level of technical art direction should be the gleaming star of this generation.Yeah, idiot. It's awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very atmospheric game, or better said, 'interactive experience'. The audiovisuals are gorgeous. Jean Giraud / Moebius comics brought to life. Very easy to pick up and play, even after a while of not playing it. Simple controls. No need to button mash for boss battles. No need for twitchy 'frame specific button presses to make that jump onto the next platform'. While there are some relatively straightforward environmental puzzles, the focus is mostly on exploration and talking to characters to get more quests. This is a great game to sit down and unwind with.

_childDocuments_.review: Sable is an enchanting experience. The developers took the aesthetic of a comic by the late and great Moebius and brought it alive in 3D. They also seized upon the general vibe of a lot of those comics in Sable's worldbuilding. Unlike modern sci-fi, Sable cares a lot less about the technical ins and outs of its world, and more about the feeling of living in that mysterious and colourful alien world.Having made an exquisitly engaging setting, the developers then provide the player with robust tools to explore that world. With stamina-based free climbing, slow falling, and a customizable high-speed "mount", Sable's large map beckons in a way that I have only felt before in Breath of the Wild.However, unlike Breath of the Wild, Sable completely eschews combat. This creative choice makes for a much more atmospheric experience. Without the pressure of resource management or timed threats, you are free to discover the many secrets, puzzles, and platforming challenges the world offers.While a chill exploration game might not be for everyone, it's perfect for me, and if the idea speaks to you, dk yourself a favor and discover Sable's world for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I see a mustard yellow sky with stars like snowdrops as I climb. Scaling the peek, I sprint across terracotta sand to the next rise. Ascending towards an angry cloud lashed with gold lightning. Dust or ash or both tumble from the cloud. I don’t know what’s up there, but there’s lots of transparent, crystal-like forms in the area, each one percolating with gold particles. Presumably the cloud and the crystals are bonded. A sense of foreboding builds the closer I get. A similar feeling hit me half an hour earlier, as I stood beneath a set of interlocking stone platforms rotating far above the ground. Ashen ground that spewed endless plumes of smoke, dashed here and there with red.But there’s nothing to fear. This is . No evil needs vanquishing nor villain confronting in this gorgeous, cel-shaded land. Even the giant beetles don’t bite.Just poo.Shedworks’ debut title is all about the discovery of self-actualisation by its eponymous hero, Sable. After a long tutorial in the confines of her clan’s valley, she embarks on a rite of passage, known as the ‘Gliding’, by leaving her home and journeying into the wilderness. Who she chooses to become is your decision to make – if and when such a time comes.The beauty of  – or rather one of its many beauties – is that time and freedom are essentially yours to do with as you will. Sable’s journey doesn’t involve pain or hardship. It’s a spirited journey that emphasises joy and leisure over adversity. Your only companion is a hoverbike, which can be kitted out according to your specifications. It’s more than just metal, though; a whistle will call the bike to your side if you find yourself separated, suggesting its engine thrums with a living energy.The Gliding, then, is for both of you.Across a sublime wilderness, clans await your coming, some more eager to help than others, but almost all with quests to offer. Masked clans. Whether plantweavers or cartographers, the people of Sable’s world all wear masks. Symbols of belonging and purpose, but not of allegiance; these clans coexist in harmony.When I shot off into Sable’s world of Midden, initially all sand dunes with scattered pockets of civilization and metal husks, I thought of Rosie Huntington-Whiteley’s character of Splendid in . Seizing a sick acolyte of a mad warlord, she screamed, “[Who] killed the world?!” A rhetorical question, speaker and viewer alike knowing exactly the sorts of people who had ferried humanity to the brink. But I was quickly disabused of any notion that something  had happened on Midden. I wasn’t flying across a post-apocalyptic wilderness, tough though it could be. It was just a beautiful, vibrant, living land. And inhabiting it is a joy you won’t soon forget.The map is divided into several areas, each with their own aesthetic and vibe, adding diversity to an otherwise sandy expanse. There are forests of particoloured flora, salt flats, and plains decorated with the bones of colossal creatures from another age. The scope of the world is consistently breath-taking. Best seen from a great height, climbing is a key facet of  gameplay, and it’ll reward you with extraordinary views for your dexterity.Directly inspired by the art of the late French cartoonist Jean Giraud (Moebius),  linework is much like a comic, and its use of colour some of the best I have ever seen in a game. Taken together with a marvellous soundtrack by indie band Japanese Breakfast,  aura is pretty hypnotic.That lovely spell is occasionally broken by a few faltering steps, one of which is its obtuse UI. Clicking the option you want on a menu should be straightforward, but whether navigating by mouse or keyboard it’s bewildering how quickly you can break it. Combining inputs frustrates the UI, especially during conversations. Sometimes I had to repeat dialogue trees because I wasn’t able to select the option I needed to leave. Slow and clunky, I groaned whenever I had to use the menus.It’s a cumbersomeness that can translate to the game world, too. Sable is not always a deft character to control, with the camera frustrating your passage through narrow tunnels, or every so often bouncing her off rock faces. And whilst I’m having a moan, I’d point out that audio bugs still persist, months after release.But none of these problems overwhelm . The cumulative power of its aesthetics, the funny, insightful writing, and simple but fulfilling gameplay keep the experience intact. Even now, having fully concluded the game, I miss it. I miss the pleasant drone of my hoverbike, the dust trails at midday and the magenta glow of dusk.And the sunsets. That enormous white sun enriching the sand and rock, excavating Midden’s many layers of history. A curious history, scattered across the desert and carried on the wind.Wrecked ships from beyond the stars are the only incursion on this otherwise ancient and peaceful land. Their digitised and mechanical croaks, almost like the remnants are angry to have come so far for so little, suggest something utterly alien to Sable’s way of life, to her home. But given the inscription on some of their storage crates, it is not so alien to you and me. Splendid’s furious demand to know who killed the world booms again in my mind, followed by the static-laced words of the ships’ logs. Words of unmistakable danger from a world whose population likely demanded more than it could ever give.Though the loss of life a tragedy, there’s a strange, melancholy relief their mission capsized, as the sun rises on a land treated with equality and respect by those who dwell there – however they came to inhabit it.

_childDocuments_.review: full review whenever i finish this game but *SHAKES YOU BY THE SHOULDERS* I LOVE JAPANESE BREAKFASTanyways this game is so beautiful - i am absolutely obsessed with the moebius comic inspired artstyle + the soundtrack - and the dialogue is well written. a gorgeous atmospheric world, and i like the message of self-discovery (at least AFAIK in the 5 hours i've played)the criticism about how the game is poorly optimized/buggy are all true though. it really takes me out of the immersion when my glider is once again stuck in the middle of a wall or the character AI's are making them run into walls/somehow exist with the same dialogue both inside or outside buildings. the technical mishaps and some poor game design choices really get in the way of the artistry -- which is such a shame! there's a lot to love in this game, but the fetch quests can be a bit tiring in order to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I have loved playing Sable. One thing I have truly enjoyed is that there is no main quest that you have to follow. After the brief introduction and tutorial, you get to choose everything you do and don't do, and are pretty much only limited by the borders of the map. There is an end "goal" of sorts, but this goal can only be achieved through hours of exploration and mini-quests. It's important to note that you will have a much easier time completing tasks for the fisherman and collector if you visit them soon after you start so you can work on their tasks over the course of your travels.The only real issue I've had is that I've experienced a few glitches where I won't be able to call my glider, pick up any insects, and once where the beetles weren't behaving normally. All of these were easily fixed by saving my game and exiting. And the only recurring glitch I've had is with the glider not showing up after calling it. I've also had some graphics issues where the sands will start glitching as it approaches nighttime.Edit: After the most recent update I opened up the game again to check out what was added. Although I liked the addition of the fisherman and collector, I find the fishing mechanic to be somewhat difficult. I haven't had much experience with fishing in games so I don't have much to compare it to, but once you get to the rarer types of fish I've found that it's almost impossible for me to catch any. I do realize there are better fishing rods that you can purchase, but I would think that you should be able to catch more than two types of fish with the basic rod that you start off with.

_childDocuments_.review: SABLE is a really cool open-world exploration game where you can go anywhere on the map at any time you want (tutorial part excluded). The story feels awkward during the tutorial, maybe a bit too forced for my taste, and the way your character talks in their heads makes you cringe at times but you quickly forget about it. It becomes natural after a few more dialogs. You begin your journey with a simple quest "get to that person over there !" but you're not forced to do it. Quests are simple enough, the world in itself is simple enough. Same stuff on different locations. Sand everywhere but different color and yet, it feels refreshing every time. It's a chill game. The ambiance is on point, the music is great, visually, it's extraordinary. I recommand playing on the "thin lines" btwThe game just feels good. Your character movements are sometimes a bit wobbly I admit (I'm talking about you, climbing over a small edge animation !) but you forgive it massively. The stop-motion like animations are so great. I have no negative point towards this game. Or maybe only one. The game is said to have a few devastating bugs. My experience was that my game crashed after I collected an item and decided never to load again. I lost everything. My IT bf played with the files and it worked for a while, but nothing would save and after I launched the game again after playing 3 more hours, losing everything again because the game wouldn't let me save felt utterly disappointing. I played 20h+, collected many items and over a hundred of eggs. I didn't get to the end of the main story. Too bad. But I still recommand playing this. It felt really good to just travel throught the desert with my cute customized bike. Really nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: **Thank you to @duhnuhnuh_duhnuhnuh for the game code.**Overview:            A very pleasant experience that is certainly worth your time. My experience can be fairly well summer up by the three B's: Breathtaking, Buggy, and Boring. The game is jaw-droppingly BEAUTIFUL at times, and some of the quests and environments are incredibly well-made. However, there seems to be a little bit of an issue of 'style over substance' here. The game is pretty BORING for a regrettably large portion of the experience and basic gameplay with incredibly mundane quests (most of the time) did not lend itself to anything particularly unique. The unique nature of the game comes in with obviously, the artstyle, and the beautifully crafted world and environments within the open world that just bring you to your knees. I found myself sitting and looking over jaw-dropping vistas in basically every major area, as each area had their own unique, enticing vibes that just made you want to stare. I did have to kinda look past all the texture and lighting glitches that were happening in my FOV at basically all times to enjoy these views, but it's not as big a deal as it may seem. The game is BUGGY as heeellll though... I encountered constant, and I do mean constant, audio, visual, or gameplay bugs. Just be prepared to be torn out of your immersion every other minute, because I know I was. The game would be significantly better without the bugs, but is still certainly playable even with the missing frames, constant lighting issues, annoying camera, and countless other frustrating bugs that I encountered throughout my playthrough. Still definitely a good game that I can personally recommend overall. More details on my time with the game below----Sights and Sounds-The artstyle is incredibly beautiful and unique (very screenshot-able)        - Looks good up close (as long as the camera isn't clipping through the entire structure you are in) and is breathtaking far away-Camera issues and TONS of graphical pop-in took me out of my immersion quite frequently-Usually very weighty and satisfying         -But there was a pretty consistent trend of audio bugs like where music suddenly cuts in or out, chimes banging together loudly, or random loud sounds that are very clearly unintentional for the given moment          -Specifically my engine sound on my bike actually hurt my ears-Very beautiful and fitting score, thoughGameplay- Movement on the bike is super unpredictable and feels pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible, honestly        - Movement on foot is much better, and you have a lot more control when NOT climbing (diff story)- The BOTW influence was very apparent, and having played it just earlier this year, was a nice refresher        - Still much less fleshed out and the gameplay was much more boring overall- Introduction of new mechanics and the whole 'gliding ceremony' thing felt a little bit tonally conflicting but important to the continuation of the mechanical improvement overall- *ALMOST* all quests are laced with tedium and are painfully predictable         - A bunch of fetch quests or quests where you go solve an annoying, basic puzzle for a reward you didn't really care about- My time with the game was shorter than most, but I still thought the borderline-hour-long intro in the introductory area was way too long. Let me go explore the world please- Speaking of exploring the world, that was by far the best part          - Exploring caves, ruins, and ships weren't particularly fun nor did they yield enticing results         - But just finding the new, incredibly distinct areas within the world was soooo cool                           - All the different areas were super unique and breathtaking in their own ways-Specific moments like climbing the bones, going to the lightning plateau, and leaving the Ewer were what made the game as special as it ended up being-Dialogue with other characters was repetitive, but still usually quite interesting because of each character's own, special characteristics and personalitiesNarrative/Story/Goal-Despite the annoying length, the intro was a good way to set up the overall narrative and goal         -Concept of collecting a bunch of different masks was very enticing and interesting at first, but became much less interesting when I learned HOW you go about collecting the majority of the masks (boring)-The characters all felt very real, very similar to BOTW in that way-A sentimental story overall with leudo-narrative dissonant elements, but a mainly conjoined story + gameplay-Rare unique quests were hidden among a sea of boring, monotonous, and repetitive ones         - These unique quests do make the game worth it, however.-In general, the open nature of it all overwhelmed me a little bit, and kind of pushed me to want to just get the story over with, which I do regret a little bit now, looking back         - Most quests being boring also turned me away from doing as many quests as I could've Performance- Good at best	- Mid-High range PC (3060 ti) struggled to run 1440p at 144 hz on high settings, ended up capping at 60	- LOTS of frame stutters/drops throughout but worst in the open world	- A BUNCH of pop-in- Nothing game-breaking, but the camera, gameplay, visual, and audio glitches highly degraded the experience- I would've been less critical overall if the game was less buggy	- The bugs were constantly taking me out of my immersion, alerting me to the problems of the game that would've been negligible if I was fully immersed
