_childDocuments_.review: This game changed my standards for RPGs and open world games.Sable was made by a 2 person dev team and now sits as one of my favourite games of all time. It's a beautiful mix of visuals/design inspired by Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind and an open world that is as good if not rivals some of the AAA classics in the open world genre.I followed this games development and prior to it's release the idea of no damage or combat in a expansive world caught me off guard, but Sable doesn't need combat. There is so much to explore, it's so seamless and there is so much content PLUS more being added via updates. For me this gave me the same feeling as playing Breath of the Wild for the first time. Each new zone comes with it's own unique colour pallet and atmospherics, it's own puzzles, it's own tribes and unique characters to match. Travelling across the vast desert on a hover bike that you can customise with unique parts from each zone is a blast.It even has it's own koroks to collects known as chums! Praise the Chum queen.This is a genuine experience I think you should enjoy for yourself, especially if you enjoy cosy open world titles.Note: they added fishing so I'm going back in.10/10 definitely worth the buy ESPECIALLY if you're buying while it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: This had the makings of a beautiful game, if it just weren't for all the bugs. I could have easily played this another 20hrs if the bugs just didn't ruin every 2 minutes of my playtime. I would definitely not recommend buying Sable at full price or even the discounted price I hate to say, but this game still needs a LOT of patches to fix its many many problems.Update: It's been two years since release and the game is definitely operating smoother, performance has improved and there are a lot less bugs. Unfortunately I did come across some glitches now and again but nothing to take away the immersion. Frame rates still an issue, mostly in one particular area but otherwise like I said everything went smooth. Finally feel I can appreciate the game and recommend it, either at full price or on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous, clunky, expansive, opaque, endearing, annoying, and ultimately worth checking out.Despite some frustrating design choices (calling the hover bike is hit-and-miss, non-climbable surfaces aren't clearly defined, navigating menus with a mouse is sure-fire way to ruin your in-game compass...) and a bevy of bugs,  triumphs in the joys of exploration, both of its world and the nature of personal identity. It rewards patience, problem solving, and adventurousness with a firm sense of style I very much enjoy: heartily rec'd.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely charming game. If you've ever wanted to play a game directly inspired by the works of Moebius, this is your game. It's got it's fair share of bugs having just been released, of course. But being a small indie dev team, it's absolutely fantastic otherwise right out of the gate. The story, scope, and breadth of the game are just phenomenal. Nice and chill without being dreadfully slow. If you're looking for action and fighting, look elsewhere - this is a passion project about character development wrapped around an open world begging to be explored. The controls are simple enough, though my one UI gripe is that (as of this review), some of the interface in the hoverbike customization menu is a bit wonky. I'm sure it'll get sorted out with a hot fix at some point. Other than that, I'm having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Sable was an absolute joy to play through. The quiet, contemplative adventure I had riding through the desert as Sable was one of the most relaxing, borderline therapeutic experiences I’ve had the pleasure of playing in a long time. It has some technical bugs here or there and no small amount of jank, but the sheer amount of charm and atmosphere made it melt away for me more times than not. One of my favorite indie titles in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game. Can't really describe it. It's an experience worth experiencing. The one and ONLY con about this game I can think of, is the frame rate issues, even on more high end devices, occasional terrain un-loading or not loading at all. But if you just don't pay attention to that, it's an amazing game. The way the song "Glider" plays the moment you enter the wide world of The Midden made chills go down my spine. Beautiful vocals for both "Glider" and "Better the Mask". After 43 hours of playing this game, the final song wanted to make me tear up but it got kiiiinda ruined a little by the song cutting off before it had the chance to even get to the middle of it- Listened to it in full right after and still got the full message. Definitely recommend playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Its damn impressive considering it was made buy 2 ppl. The game is purely exploration and discovery, there is little to no challenge in most quests. Its a good game to wind down, exploring while listening to chill music. There are some bugs with the camera and framerates. Hoping devs will iron them out.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast with this game.The unique atmospehere, the awesome music and the art style are outstanding. If you want a relaxing and captivating expirience without violence (no fights, no dying of any sort), then I can recommend this fantastic game without any doubt.I enjoyed Sable from the first to the last hour of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all of the games that Ive ever played, I don't think that any one has ever given me the sense of wonder and awe that this game has given. The landscapes are beautiful and make it look like every moment of gameplay was made by a master landscape/ cityscape painter. This and the climbing mechanic, make it so that this game, while not challenging, an amazing way to relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Sadly the audio issues are too bad to ignore.If you cancel your sprint before the stamina runs out and sprint again then the audio freezes and the game stutters... I glitched the story by going to the spaceship before the village and lost my bike. Once I found my bike and finally strode over the open dessert with the dust behind me..... There was endless audio pop in of the wind trying to murder me and drowning out the music. Then the wind stops and the cycle repeats making my ears bleed all while driving in a straight line. I could mute the game but that's not what I paid for. Praying they fix some bugs so I will hold off on my refund until they do.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: When you get old enough, it is time to see the world and decide what you want to do with your live. The gliding is a ritual travel to do tasks for all kinds of people to find out what you like and what you are good at. It starts by powering an ancient gliding stone that prevents you from falling to your death - a magic parachute if you will. Say your good byes to your clan, get on your hoverbike, and find your luck.The desert is vast, but there are always some points of interest on the horizon. Climbing to the balloons of the cartographers is always a good first step in a region. Raid an old human ship for scrap and find out a bit more of the history. And always there are Chum eggs to gather. Combat isn't part of the course - there are few humans as it is and only impossibly big skeletons around - climbing (and gliding back down) is really at the core of the experience.There are many different parts for your hoverbike to upgrade, it's really a shame there isn't a real race track around... You can whistle for your bike to come to you when you did a bit of climbing - but instead of appearing behind you, the thing is actually trying to travel to you. That takes some time... when it can actually path to you at all. At last you can fast travel to the nearest point on your map and your hoverbike will be by your side again.When you have seen some of the world, won a few medals and masks, you get the message you could end your gliding. No rush though.Sable was more fun than I thought it would be. Mostly because there is a real sense of exploring the world and discovering ancient structures. You get compass directions to find your way which is enough to have to search a little bit without being lost. It's really encouraged to look around instead of staring on a maker in the corner.Upgrading your stamina with Chum eggs and upgrading your hoverbike with money made from scrap is a great feedback loop - the more you explore, the better you get at it.The flat textures make it hard at times to judge an incline, some more details at short range would help. Running at 60 fps (even with default details) the game was dropping often frames - hover biking at high speeds felt really shaky. The performance isn't great.If you like exploring and climbing or like a game that can be played while listing to a podcast, Sable is a great title.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours into this game and i love it. The art style and lore with the likability of the personalities in the game make it a relaxing and enjoyable time. There's much to do in the large open world and though it may seem empty at first the longer you play the more you begin to learn about everything this game has hidden inside. The dialogue is simple and often short which is nice in the sense that you're not just reading filler forever. For me the game gives a nice vibe of actually having freedom in what you do and where you want to go, see something cool in the distance? Just go there whenever you please. Don't like an area? Just leave. There is lots to do and tons of quests, the more people you chat with the more you find yourself doing. There is a lot of go here and collect said item and bring it back but beyond those the quests are honestly fun. The puzzles in my opinion are calm and not annoying giving some lore to keep you wanting to play for hours on end. It starts to seem like the story just keeps unfolding and there's rarely a dry moment. Those are the pros of the game. Now the cons.Cons:  The game has serious optimization issues. Consistent frame drops, the game is still playable but makes things feel real clunky at times. The farther you proceed in the game the worse it falls apart, i have a well built computer and running this game on medium graphics and uncapped frames it tends to feel like it starts crashing on itself the longer you keep playing. (I did lower settings and tried all options and the same issues would happen.) Falls apart as in merchants shop pages won't load items or if you close the page on the "sell" tab when you go back to said merchant it gets stuck on the "sell" page and i have had to restart the game to fix it. Sounds will just flat out break the glider makes a choppy noise and when you hit a hill that would typically launch you into a long jump, you just kinda flip around in weird positions until the bike straightens out and continues on. When you reach the southern end of the map the frame drop is significant and at times everything is almost movin in slow motion. It's a bit disappointing because in the start of the game it runs fantastic but as i said the more you progress the more it seems the game just kills itself. Overall i rate this 7/10 fix the performance issues and this could easily be a 10/10. A game i could see myself coming back to play multiple times.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, but had to play it on PC over steam deck. The deck settings had to be weirdly low for it to run without dropping frames really hard. Perhaps I'm just bad at optimizing, but be at least a bit cautious if you were planning for this to be a deck game. Would like to play more as the game is excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a beautiful game and experience.I had seen some gameplay trailers and screenshots of the game before release, but not until I sat down and played it did I realize, “Oh, it’s like I’m in a Moebius painting.” I am an artist, and Moebius is one of my top artistic inspirations!I loved the story and gameplay but honestly the game could have been terrible and I’d have still played it just to exist in the beautiful world. Seeing a vibrant dawn or dusk sky over the just-barely-not-grey landscape was breathtaking every time.The story and setting were lovely as well. There was no health; despite being a desert it wasn’t harsh or dangerous. It felt as welcoming as my first steps into Journey years ago. It was almost a relief to explore a place that I knew had already been explored by thousands of people before me. There was no pressure to be the chosen one, or to do great deeds no one had done before. I just had to figure out my place in a world that was new only to me. I have been under a lot of stress trying to find a job lately, and it was soothing to not only have the freedom to explore, but know I had a safe place to return to.10/10 would find inner peace again.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game. Very atmospheric, cartoon-like graphics. An amazing work on colours especially the lights and shadows. The day/night ambiance is a plus. Truely a beautiful game.There are some bugs where you go into walls, or can't climb on things but you can get around those bugs quite easily. In my opinion, it doesn't really get in the way for completing missions or enjoying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: + the exploration is a joy and always "rewarding". you'll naturally and smoothly progress from one location to another, because there is always a point of interest on the horizon. there are tons of interesting spots to find and explore, often providing a unique and spectacular view or a special atmosphere. of course there are some treasures to be found as well, but don't expect to find some huge riches out there.+ gorgeous graphics and one of the most unique artstyles i've ever seen. artistic appealing from start to finish. there are spectacular views and atmospheric moments all over the place, it's a pleasure.+ the story is vague and let's be real, kinda non existent, but sable is one of those rare games, where you don't actually need a complex plot and an intriguing story telling to keep you hooked. it's more of a build your own adventure kind of game since there isn't such thing like an evil threat to fend off, no huge quest to save to world and no miraculous wonder to achieve. it's a meditative and philosophical ride, all about what you're doing with your time while being out there on your gliding, exploring the vast and mysterious world full of interesting people and abandoned temples, crashed space ships and other fancy or odd locations. what did you learn from all those impressions and what's your final decision to shape your future?+ calm and abstract soundtrack, just like the games atmosphere. quite impressive stuff from japanese breakfast.+ decent amount of collectibles and stuff to find. pretty much nothing is marked on your map, except the chum eggs, when you found it. i kinda liked this concept, since it kept the exploration fresh, but made backtracking for 100% bearable. the chum eggs are placed very well, so it is quite easy to find enough for the achievement. keep in mind there are a lot more out there and those are hidden a lot better.+ which brings us directly to the next positive, i quite liked the map progression. its pretty much all empty at first. you have travel the dessert without any clue and have to obtain the map parts from cartographers in the different regions. if you've found a place of interest, it will be marked on your map and those spots will turn into quick travel locations as well. + there is a decent amount of quests to be found and they're pretty diverse as well. the game got some interesting characters, so i've enjoyed most of the quest related dialogues as well. there were quite some gems, like elissabets quest line, the philosophical llhor quest and the hilarious shade quest, to name some.+ i'm usually a huge fan of movement abilities and climbing and of course sable isn't an exception to this. i've quite enjoyed the gliding ability and the ability to climb on almost any surface, except some of the metal ones to secure some puzzles and platforming, only being limited by the stamina "bar" for climbing and gliding won't consume any stamina at all. expanding the amount of stamina over the course of the game improves the enjoyment of the climbing part even further since you'll be able to reach higher locations providing spectacular views and of course some secrets.+ despite all of the zones being desserts, they are still looking quite different and unique. all zones definitely got their own flavor and atmosphere going, loved it.+ the game has some fun and laid back puzzle and platforming.+ different outfits for sable and customization options for simoon (the bike).+ moebius style and dune flair (watch out for worms!)~ there is no combat or any threat at all, so keep that in mind before buying this game. if you're expecting combat and/or survival aspects, you might be disappointed with this one.~ the cutscene when obtaining a mask should being able to skip since it's always the same for all of the masks and takes like forever. this "issue" isn't annoying enough to make it to the con section, but yea, could be much better.- the flavor text of the collectibles (chum eggs and scrap metal for example) is always the same. instead of some plain item description, it could be used for lore and world building. definitely lost some potential there.- unfortunately the games optimization is a bummer. frames ranging from around 30 to 120+ on certain occasions. frames droping like wild for no reason and a couple of other fps issues. at least my average frames were decent enough to keep playing.- some smaller bugs and glitches here and there. npcs stuck on obstacles, obstacles floating in the air or glitching with other ones, sable switching the mask after restarting the game and many more. nothing major game breaking tho, but if you're bothered easily by smaller issues, probably waiting for some fixes and updates would be better.10/10 despite having some technical issues which hopefully will be fixed in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game! it's basically breath of the wild with no combat, and with a pace and mood closer to a short hike. lots of climbing or looking in nooks and crannies to find hidden rewards. very much a cute coming of age story about exercising freedom and discovering yourself, and i am a sucker for that ♥♥♥♥. the quests are pretty basic for the most part, lots of "go talk to so and so" or "go find X of Y", but the way they fold into the broader theme of exploring the world and discovering yourself makes them far more compelling than in your average RPG.before going into this know that it is still very buggy. i didn't encounter any game breaking bugs, but there were several instances where i'd be climbing on terrain and it'd disappear entirely. a couple of times dialogue boxes stopped responding and i had to restart the game. until they fix the remaining bugs (hopefully they do) you'll need to go into this with some patience.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: a really cool little world filled with unique characters and interesting quests and wonderful story; the art style and graphics throughout are very pretty (though there are some lag issues i noticed while playing) and make this game one of my favorites. sable herself is adorable and i am positively in love with her.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

_childDocuments_.review: Embark on a unique and unforgettable journey and guide Sable through her Gliding; a rite of passage that will take her across vast deserts and mesmerizing landscapes, capped by the remains of spaceships and ancient wonders.
_childDocuments_.name: Sable

name: Atomicrops
detailed_description: Mow-down at the hoedown! Pack your bags and move to the idyllic countryside. Pay no heed to the nuclear fallout – it adds a lovely glow to your complexion! Upsides – everyone wants a piece of you! Downsides – everyone wants a piece of you... Grab your blunderbuss and get ready for twin-stick, bullet-hell, roguelite, corn-chuckin' action game that will last until the cows come home! As any self-respecting farmer would: Farm. Marry. Kill. Sow and harvest as many fast-growing crops as you can before the day is done to earn a huge profit. Purchase weapons and items in town at the end of each day. Celebrate the end of each season with special shops and rewards. Permanently Upgrade your farming and fighting abilities. Earn a payout each run that can be used on permanent improvements and unlocks. Progress through the years with ramping difficulty and even greater rewards! Befriend an entourage of pig pals, chicken chums, and cow colleagues to automate farming tasks. Woo and marry a kindred spirit from the local town to fight and farm alongside you. Unlock new characters, spouses, difficulties, and permanent upgrades. Most importantly, you can unlock many cats to permanently roam your homestead (yes, you can pet them). Defend your crops from unforgiving nightly attackers looking to rampage your hard-earned harvest. Fight challenging bosses each season until you reach the final season - the Nuclear Winter. Explore the far reaches of the biomes to find useful relics of farms long past. Powerful loot increases your farming abilities and helps you fight enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I am genuinely in love with this game. I have lived with 2 different woman for about 3 years (separate). That wouldn't matter, if it weren't for the fact that the love I feel for this game feels more powerful, and different than that with said women. I hate punishing games, and I thought this would be one. It, is, but it's not soulslike unfair, you can farm “souls” AND have fun. Visuals are very pleasing, music gets stuck in my head for weeks. I have had dreams about this game, and the music. Lit yo. I read about 30 negative reviews before I buy any game, and all of them were outdated.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of bullet heaven / action-roguelites, and a pretty dang good chunk of Harvest Moon / Stardew Valley type games. This? Eh. Interestingly, the game is priced ABOVE that of most bullet-heaven / VN-likes, but lower than most farm sims, so I was expecting it to be either a great action-roguelite, or a trash farm sim.Atomicrops, I don't know, it's definitely got an identity crisis. I don't hate it, but I just feel like it should be something else. Farming while doing the combat feels silly, and fighting while tending to your crops feels silly too, not in a bad way, but not in a good way either.I think if it was up to me, it WOULD be a full-blown Rune Factory type of game, full town, recurring villagers and so on, but the second you step out of town, bullet heaven / action-roguelite mode, harder over time, temporary upgrades, waves to survive, going out there to collect materials, find new things to unlock stuff with, etc. Maybe a marriage candidate needs their family crest from their old destroyed village out so far into the wilderness that there's NO chance of getting back before the difficulty is in total apocalypse mode? Imagine the struggle on the way back, swarms to dodge through, only to get chased by something faster than you that you're sure will one-shot you, you barely dodge it as you reach town so you can finally get married to your chosen spouse, equip them with the finest stuff you've got, then go right back out and beat the heck out of that guy that just chased you together.This game, everything relies on everything else to work, and that makes the reliance on RNG worse.Get bad rolls on farming stat drops? No money. No money? No guns. Run ends.Get hit by a boss's terrible collision detection? (I'm looking at YOU worm.) Better farm a heart, which takes time and money away, which means less profits, possible run end.Go on a run and have a day where you find no/few seeds? Run wasted.Shop only rolls the high-value weapons that you can't afford? Can't defend farm, farm eaten, run wasted.Run gives no combat skill points? Move too slow, can't get seeds in time, run wasted.Run gives no farm skill points? Farm too slow, can't afford new guns, run wasted.The constant running back and forth between the outer zones and the farm is already getting grating, and I've only been playing for an hour, I can't imagine how bad it is for players who've been at this for days.I wish we could decline the helicopter ride and get an extended day or a bonus for playing "risky", it's maddening to get pulled out of your farming work just to get right back on the helicopter again because you can't afford anything.I wish the weapon shop had a "bargain bin" for people who can't afford the price jump between seasons.I wish the character select screen told us hints about how to unlock other characters (one's DLC though, IIRC.)I wish the game had a few early-game achievements and meta-progression bits just for pity and to make it not feel like your first few runs are just wastes of time. Seriously, AFAIK, all the meta-progression stuff is at the END of the game, not the beginning. Imagine playing a roguelite where you get nothing until you've beaten the game, THEN they start unlocking things so you can... beat the game faster...?Anyway, I'll give the classic mode a go, I've still got about 40 minutes left in the return window. I heard classic was better, time to find out.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, very much like stardew valley mixed with enter the gungeon.Recently there was a really nice update which really helped the game by adding mods to guns and allowed you to keep your guns.They also made quite a lot of quality of life changes.Each run normally takes between 30mins to 1hour 30mins.The game can be a bit hard to start with at first however the more you play the more you learn how to manage your time between farming and exploring.Hope the devs continue to work on the game and look forward to what else they come up with in the future :)
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be played quickly.  My review will be just as quick:Imagine the usual collect-o-farming game, the "Turnip rancher" game my wife's fond of.  Now make it a bullet-hell roguelike in a post-apocalyptic, the plants-may-be-sentient game, where the usual farm tropes (chickens, scarecrows, cows, etc.) are all various buffs that can help you. The art is very pixelly in a way that will look just as artistic ten years from now as it does now.You can also flirt with the locals.  Presuming you've managed to find the time to grow roses to bribe them with.I haven't "won" yet.  I wind up getting overwhelmed after awhile.  But I'm getting better.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Took me 52 hours to 100% the achievements. If you don't want to do the achievements this game will last you about half that time, but I really recommend the achievements. I legitimately had fun getting them, even if I had to look up a guide every now and then cuz I was like "ok but how DO I kill the moon?"The thing about it that I really hated was the ear cancer tier music, but I like playing roguelites with the audio muted while listening to podcasts so it just made me glad that I wasn't missing out on anything. As soon as I turned off the sound I got over my urge to refund Atomicrops. Very much worth your money, especially if you get it on sale like I did!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, because the games that are so bad or so good to actually push me to do it are very few.This game is a hidden gem. Everything has charm, from the music, to the intricate details in the art, the animation and the mechanics.It is at its core a twin stick rouguelite that centers on fast-paced action, keeping the rhythm of of the two gameplay elements (farming and shooting) always spot-on and never boring.The difficulty curve, the permanent and run-specific buffs are well balanced.The only speck on an otherwise spotless experience is that it could use a larger variety of biomes, enemies and items to ensure it doesn't get repetitive at the 100 hours mark. But maybe The Binding of Isaac spoiled me on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game! I haven't played a whole lot yet, but I love its pixel art style and the animated opening/prologue was pretty well done. The controls are a bit tough though - for instance, on my first day I forgot I was supposed to harvest the crops - and it didn't seem like I was able to get my DS4 controller operational, but hopefully I'll get used to that in due time.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and cute game. late game, the whole thing becomes a bit of a bullet hell like enter the gungeon. the weapons and the mods are pretty cool. the days are pretty short so you do need to be pretty quick on getting items and seeds, especially when you're playing alone. Drawbacks : - the music, while not bad, becomes extremely repetitive very quickly- the fact that i have to keep buying and switching to another weapon all the time to increase my farming and fighting skills means i can't just stick with a weapon i like and go for a certain playstyle which brings me to the next point.- Each run feels exactly like the previous one. the enemies you encounter feel very samy, the music is once again very repetitive and you can't switch to a different playstyle since you need switch weapons all the time to increase your skills and you need a very good balance of allies in order to make enough money to afford anything mid and late game. So you end always looking for the things every run.I feel like it's missing something to make each run a bit more different than the previous ones like hades where you can just stick with one weapon for a whole run and choose different combinations of boons to make your powers different.The game is still very much worth buying in my opinion and i had lots of fun playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game! The first few runs were really overwhelming, and I made a lot of dumb mistakes. But once I got a handle on the mechanics and started seeing all the little things I could do to get further, I had a lot of fun. Really fun aesthetic and style, along with some punchy shooting mechanics and fun little synergies. For this price, it's a steal!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I've always found myself strangely drawn to farming games like Harvest Moon and Rune Factory, but also always felt dissatisfied playing them. Atomicrops seems to have filled that void nicely. The crop management and shooting are active, exploration is rewarding, and enemies and items are bizarre and fun.The game has character out the wazoo. Your crops are some of the cutest giggly, cheerful, bouncing mutants ever. Your farm animals are very helpful when they haven't been abducted by aliens (don't worry, they'll return to you). The characters and love interests are... special. But hey, they give you stuff if you work for it. So, totally fitting with the interactions of games in this genre.I'll warn you, it has some of the weirdest sound design I've ever heard in a game. I was put off by it at first, but it's kind of grown on me. I still have it turned down a fair bit, though, because it's a lot. Also, you lose your gun every day. There are some things which kind of mitigate that, but it's still iffy whether you'll get to keep your fancy upgraded weapon each day. Not keen on that part.For the amount of content in the game, it's a steal on sale. Highly recommended to those who want to work on their multitasking skills.Edit: The Doom and Bloom and Feline Good updates added a bunch of stuff which make it much less enjoyable for me. DaB added a lot of strong, uninteresting upgrades which dominate play. They're very rewarding, but make play very automatic. FG (amongst other things) upped the moles who inhabit your farm during the day, so they're more of a hassle. You're constantly harassed while farming, which was already a frantic tapdance.I still recommend the game, since I think you can revert to previous updates. If you're in its niche, you'll probably get a lot of hours out of it regardless, but it's a lot less satisfying to play.Edit 2: With two more DLC updates, guns no longer break (although they are prohibitively expensive), and the farming has changed in interesting ways. Still very random, but it's more challenging again, and I've been enjoying hunting down the last several achievements (which I do not recommend, as they are extremely random and difficult). Surprised to still be seeing new things in the game at this point, so there's certainly been a lot of content added.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a public beta patch in the works that I feel like answered enough of my problems to change my review, so I'm doing my due diligence and updating my review.- poor palate choices  that makes enemies hard to see and differentiate between enemies, your crops or your drones. - still a problem - needing to manage your inventory without gameplay pausing. This is frustrating because merging your crops becomes pretty important to earning enough points. - while being perfect at the game is an option to combat this, i dont think- there was a complaint here about the enemies being bullet spungy, but this update has a patch that lets you upgrade your main gun so this isnt as big of a problem.-weapons break every day, you cant fix it, you just buy a new one, and have to upgrade it. upgrades/items are  really expensive and you pretty much have to be getting multiple merged plants daily after the first season. - fixed by not feeling like you have to buy an upgraded gun all the time because your main gun can be upgraded.-there is now a decent amount of variety in bosses and eventsSomething I think can be both a plus and a minus: the game doesn't really tell you much. I played the tutorial, and even though it mentioned the merging it didnt say that it was so much better. its a better idea to save seeds to be able to merge than to plant them by themselves. its frustrating at the beginning but once you know the basics its fun to stumble around and learn something new in the game. like finding a new upgrade or getting a different love interest on the farm.There's a lot for you to uncover, a bunch of mechanics to master, and item combos to experiment with.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting take on the Roguelike genre. Combining an arcade shooter with some light farming elements makes for unique experience where you have to carefully manage your time all the while enemies are constantly trying to kill you.I originally went into this game for the art style and stayed for the gameplay, which left me wanting to improve so I can get better and more efficient with each run. The soundtrack is also really good and I would recommend looking into the composer, Joonas Turner, as he is very talented.The learning curve for this game is a little steep at first, but once you get the hang of it, you can get some really fun runs with some of the upgrades and weapons you can get. However, the later difficulties of the game do turn into bullet hell which can be a turn off for some people, but there are certain upgrades you can grab to help mitigate this.Overall this game is definitely worth the $15 price tag and I would recommend it to anyone who likes a good rougelike.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine! It's fun, I definitely got my money's worth, and it's easy enough to pick up and play. However, as you get to the later levels the hitboxes (wider than you'd think) and the bright colours / environments combine to make half of the deaths feel unfair. Upgrades, and especially synergy between upgrades, are crucial, but they're so niche that again, you feel like you only get a really viable combination about half the time. The difficulty of the bosses is all over the place as well: The final boss is SO easy that I've never taken more than about 40 seconds to beat it, wheras the worm on level 1 or the random aliens that show up will kick my ass even with a decent loadout. There's a lot to like here, so try it out if you're on the fence at all. There's just something quietly unsatisfying about it. Even when you win you don't feel like you really accomplished anything, given how meagre the permanent upgrade rewards are.EDIT: I Came back after a free update and a paid DLC. Some of my issues (like the over-saturation and the swingy bosses) are still there, while others (hitboxes) have been fixed or changed to mitigate some of the issues and give you more incremental progress faster. I'd change my score to recommended, but Steam doesn't like you changing your mind and will wipe the reviews. I was on the fence before anyways, and feel mostly the same way as before, but I came back for the DLC and remembered there's a lot to like about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start with the good, since it's mostly good:This games concept is very original, the way the genres have been merged here is far more interesting than anything I've seen in a while. The game manages to genuinely give me some of the same joy as an actual farming sim while 100% not being one. The game is mostly a bullet hell roguelite at it's core, and while that's not exactly the unique part, even that is done in a way far different than most of it's peers. The map for example is not laid out in your typical fashion of a bunch of rooms stitched together, it is a farm and 4 areas (and sub-areas) you may go to and from as you please. The farming aspect obviously is the main gimmick here and it is done wonderfully, it's simple to execute, hard to get good at, and is complicated enough that it feels rewarding to learn, managing what you farm, and how you farm is important! The Simplicity of the game overall is a big accomplishment, simplifying doing so many things at once so that it isn't completely overwhelming is hard, and (for the most part) the game has achieved that. The games art is gorgeous, the colors and concepts in every sprite are wonderful (save for maybe the character portraits but that's kinda normal for farm games for some reason) I can't believe just how good they all looked, it can be a VERY cluttered mess at times, but even then, it's pretty. The music is really fun, the whimsical vocals add a really nice sense of fun to everything, or even occasionally drama, the only issue is a lack of a whole lot of variety either from dynamic music, or different tracks, but I touch on that in the negatives...which are as follows:It is a little too dependent on luck, I think a good roguelite should allow you to be carried by skill, but things like unclear hitboxes, terrible weapons, and enemies that can just be better than you, really makes this iffy sometimes, it's not hugely luck dependent, but I've had occasional runs where I just get nothing (or get a bad thing) and I end up destined to lose, but because of how most of the progression works, I still had to drag it out to bring bonuses into the next run (not fun).The town, the place where you buy things, is a cool idea but (I'm hoping I just missed something and I'm wrong) there is seemingly NO way to choose not to go, after every day, it drags you there, even when there is a nigh 100% chance you won't be able to get anything, or don't want anything, I found myself questioning why I couldn't just decline and stay, at some points it yanking me away even lost me some of my resources or turrets! I mentioned earlier the visuals could be a little cluttered, and I must say, in gameplay it's really an issue, being able to track a million bullets of the same color while weaving through an environment that straight up hides enemies can be impossible, 90% I've gotten hit, I've had no clue what even did it, sometimes just to realize it was something hidden behind a sign or bush, so that could be touched up a tad, maybe add some bullet colors to help remedy that first part, lets me know what shot them, and what speed they'll be going, while making them easier to track individually in the heat of the moment. The music is really repetitive, it made me realize just how hard it must be to make the music in a roguelite stay interesting, as you will hear it OVER and OVER again, it isn't very dynamic, every event, season, and area has it's own theme, but only one, and they do not from what I can tell change with the context, having something like more instruments when there's more enemies could've REALLY helped here, or alternate tracks, it can get grating.all in all though, my compliments were:good idea, good gameplay, good art, good music,and my complaints were:tad too much luck dependence, being forced to go to town, occasionally hard to read visuals, and music repeating too much.With my compliments being so broad I hope it's easy to tell I really like this, and highly recommend it, it's price is a steal in all honesty, I hope you try it, and if you don't like it, you can always refund it, but I doubt you will.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god, in short, I cannot possibly recommend this game more.It's a perfect cross between Stardew Valley and Binding of Isaac with it's own fantastic, quirky art style and humour on top.It's brutally hard and will absolutely have you frustrated at times, but it's perfect for soulsborne players as it rewards practice and skill, never feeling unfair.There's also an absolutely insane amount of content- as of writing I have 78 hours play time and I've BARELY gotten a quarter of the way in?I honestly think this is one of my favourite games ever. _childDocuments_.review: Roguelike farming.  Fun to play and addictive.  I didn't like it at first, but once I understood all the concepts I started loving it.  So give it a chance.During the day, you explore to gather as many seeds and upgrades as possible.  When night comes, you sow, reap and defend your farm.Some people complain that runs are repetitive.  This is because the environment is always the same.  But this is actually a good thing, since time to gather upgrades is limited, it's good to have a general idea of where to go. _childDocuments_.review: Quite the fun game! There's so much to do, and so many ways to optimise your time. It's pretty challenging, and with a way to scale the difficulty to your liking. HOWEVER; This is genuinely one of the most stressful and overwhelming games I've ever played. You know how it bills itself as a combination farming game/bullet hell? Instead of merging them into a flow, you literally do both at the same time. It can get incredibly hectic, as in any given moment during the night; you might be 1)Shooting, 2)Dodging, 3)Hovering between whatever you're tilling and whatever you're watering, and 3)Flicking your mouse over to the farm-plots every 0.5 seconds to start the next farming action (Planting, tilling, weeding, ect), all at the same time. You also have to keep track of your watering can's fullness, and if it runs out, weave over to the well and refill it. Of course, that's BEFORE the most recent update. Now, planning your farm's layout is far more important than before, and that just adds another background process to do. The actual bullet hell is not too bad, it's just the fact that it's put together with the farming. If you cannot multitask, I cannot in good faith recommend the game to you: If you can, though, this will likely be a  fun test of your ability.

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a game I've been hyped for since it was announced. The art style looks fantastic and the idea of mixing bullet hell with something like Stardew/Don't Starve sounded awesome. I purchased the game and after playing, here is my opinion...It lives up to its name as something unique and interesting, combining more than just bullet hell, but some dating as well? Don't get me wrong, there's tons of benefits to these characters but I feel like the amount of effort put into the dating part was either not enough, or in the wrong direction. Perhaps the dating part could be changed into something like an alliance/friendship? Otherwise, there's not enough depth to give any personality to them since they function more like a vendor without a chat box.Combat is simple, but still interesting thanks to the selection of weapons. Anyone new to bullet-hell type games should definitely give this a shot... but that's my only complaint. Sometimes, I play feeling like things should feel faster, more hectic, and chaotic. Throw in a roll/dodge and this game is Grade A in my books.Farming is great in this game and I couldn't tell you how many times I crossed my fingers for those nights that would let me make MASSIVE mutant crops until sunrise. _childDocuments_.review: I'm unfortunately feeling more frustrated rather than enjoying Atomicrops, I wish that Steam fixed the third option of being in the middle ground over a game because I don't hate it, I just can't give it a thumbs up as it is right now. Now at first glance I thought that I was getting into a long engaging game that fuses shooting with crop harvest, and I did get just that, what I didn't expect from this game however is how unforgiving it is, even as a rogue-like, I'll list up my praises and issues with the game so that you can get a better idea of what awaits.PROS: + Stylish and unique game with vibrant colors.+ Weirdly calming and engaging music.+ A lot of replay value.+ Good balance between farming crops and shooting stuff (It feels like Enter the Gungeon + Stardew Valley in a way)CONS:- Way too fast day and night cycles, making it hard to multi-task between exploration, farming and defending.- Insane difficulty spike (No, I'm not exaggerating) I have played a lot of Rogue-likes, but this game is borderline sadistic.- Linear story progression and perma death, so it feels like you're repeating the same campaign over and over.I'm willing to spend more time with this game as there's a lot to like here, but as it is now, I hope there will be some updates to make it less of a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly surprised to find a shooter roguelite I actually like, the only other one I put a solid amount of hours into was NT (about 150 or so). I can see myself putting a similar amount of time into this.Tight and well considered combination of shooting and farming mechanics and a host of different items and utilities allow you to make different "builds" with particular strengths. You could focus on massing a lot of farming land and high seed income and making lots of less valuable crops that require less management on your part. Or go all in on gaining fertiliser and focus on making megacrops (requiring 2x2 grid of the same crop fully fertilised).I'd say the shooter side itself would be pretty weak without the farming component, but the overall result more than makes up for that. It would be nice to see a little more attention paid to the guns and player agency surrounding them. Some are pretty bad and aside from (as far as I can tell) one character who has a chance of them not breaking each day there's no other way to keep a hold of better weapons and avoid bad ones (god help you if your choice is Butcher's Knife or Squirrel Launcher).What's there is already pretty damn solid, really hope this gets more content and tweaking as it has a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: is a weird hybrid between being a farming simulator, bullet hell and a rogue-like all in one game. Your goal is to defend the last standing farm in a post-apocalyptic world filled with mutilated enemies wanting to destroy the last farm in existence and murder you. Despite the concept being interesting for the first few hours, it shoots itself in the foot with little variety and random factors in the game that really hurt the replay value of this title, which is extremely important for any rogue-like game.• An interesting concept for the first couple of hours, but becomes repetitive quickly• Art style looks decent, the plants you grow especially stand out• The game really tries to rush you with the limited amount fo time for each day• Gets overly repetitive as the game doesn’t offer enough varied content or random factors to make each run feel different• Some enemies charge at you from off-screen that can result in a cheap damage• The difficulty when you progress through the years doesn’t add many new enemies, only overwhelms you with more of the same enemies with slightly different attack patterns• Some weapons are clearly superior than others and, needs balancing• No drastic overhaul to the seasons in terms of visuals is disappointingThe basic premise behind  is an interesting one, during the limited day time your crops are safe from enemies and you’re free to explore the surrounding lands that are split into different biomes. These areas are filled with small camps that will reward you with seeds and item upgrades for killing marked enemies that are guarding them, as well as general enemies roaming about. Once night falls however, your farm will be attacked by waves of enemies that you’ll have to fend off till the morning if you want your crops to survive the night.Only giving the player 2 minutes everyday to do everything seems extremely limiting considering you have to travel to different biomes, kill enemies for seeds, go back to your farm, sow your seeds, water the seeds, wait for them to grow and then harvest them. Sure you can do all this during the night as well, but just to put into perspective, it takes roughly an entire day and night to clear out a single biome. This mechanic makes you play faster but not better, taking unnecessary damage from enemies that you could’ve easily avoided if the time limit wasn’t so strict.You’ll encounter different types in the biomes that you explore and whilst most enemies are fair with their attacks giving you a chance to avoid them, one enemy in particular is rather cheap at lowering your health. In each biome there’s an enemy that charges at you, however the problem is that they can charge at you off-screen giving you little to no time to react and move out of the way before taking damage. If I was able to see the enemy whilst it was preparing to charge it wouldn’t be a problem, but countless times I’ve been hit by a charging enemy that came onto the screen from nowhere with no prior warning. The game’s meant to be hard, but this is just cheap damage rather than a difficult enemy to avoid.In order to properly defend your farm at night, you’ll need to purchase various farm animals, weapons, collect passive items and various defensive units to help defend the farm and make it more efficient to grow and harvest crops that reward you with money. There is however, an odd design choice when purchasing a weapon from the shop which happens to break said weapon on the next day (unless you have a specific character or upgrade the has a chance to prevent the weapon breaking). In the earlier years, you can get away with using your standard weapon that does fairly low damage, but as you progress through the years and they get increasingly more difficult, your standard weapon won’t hold up.Each season is broken down into 3 days, on which, the final day you’ll be put up against a boss who doesn’t reward you with anything that interesting whether you defeat it or wait the night out. Unfortunately these bosses are either fairly easy or downright unfair to defeat depending on what weapon you have at the time. Rogue-likes have always been repetitive but often offer a different and unique experience by changing and randomising different factors, however this is not the case for . There’s not nearly enough content, variety or random factors to keep the game interesting for very long, to the point that each run feels practically the same. The bosses are the same every season, the biomes you explore always feel the same, no new enemies are introduced as you progress through the years and the weapons that become available in the shop are very limited. For a rogue-like,  definitely misses the mark by a long shot in terms of replay value.As you explore the biomes you’ll find NPCs to save that are held hostage in some camps, they will provide you with bonuses and extra stats for the foreseeable runs when you purchase them. Some upgrades seem rather pointless, with such a small upgrade that it’s practically useless (example: an additional 1% chance for your gun not to break the day after you purchase it) whilst others are more noticeably practical to help you progress through the years.Progression is made when you complete 4 seasons and finish the run, you’ll be awarded with the next year that ‘ramps’ up the difficulty the higher you go in the years. Even though the difficulty does get noticeably more challenging the more that you progress, I couldn’t help but notice how instead of creating new enemies with harder attack patterns to dodge, they just decide to cram more enemies on the screen to satisfy the bullet hell genre of this title. This was a major disappointment, and only further discouraged me to keep making progress in this title. With such little variety in practically everything, what’s the point in trying to get to the final year?Nothing really stood out all that much with the soundtrack, it was all fine with the small amount of variety when you enter a new biome but apart from that it didn’t stand out that much. The sound of the plants happily yelling in a high pitched tone was rather distinctive, and helped with realising which plants had fully grown to harvest.The overall art style is very clean and detailed, I especially liked the way that each plant that you crop has some kinda face that really adds a sense of charm to the game. I was slightly disappointed by the lack of change in the environment when you progressed through the seasons, for example, I couldn’t see any snow in winter, . There seems to be a clear lack of detail to the environments since they just look bland and boring compared to the enemies that you encounter. At best,  is a bare-bones rogue-like that doesn’t offer enough content or random factors to make each run feel unique or different from the last. After completing the first year of the game, you’ll be playing through the same bosses again and the same enemies only in larger numbers and being more aggressive. For the cost of the game, you’d be better of getting any of the other countless rogue-likes that have much more content and replay value than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a balancing act by design, and it's wonderful. When you first start a simple tutorial runs you through the premise of the game, then throws ya in! It's up to you to figure out the mechanics from there, just experiment with what works for you. I promise the game gets way easier the more you win, every year you win you can set the difficulty higher, with the scale being 1 to 10 but I haven't really noticed there being that much of a difference (Year 7 at time of writing). Incremental difficulty adjustments let you get used to the changes so it doesn't seem like huge jumps in difficulty, and the game does have upgrades that you can buy to keep in between runs so if you find it difficult there are ways to give yourself a little boost. All in all, it's a good game that continues getting pretty neat updates consistently (thank you for the hitbox and roach change Bird Bath Games). Buy it if you like roguelike bullet hells like enter the gungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Despite my hours I have seen quite a bit of this game already. This is because I played a lot of the Limited Thyme Preview, so I would say that I have to say here is just. Atomicrops: Stardew Meets Gungeon But Falls a Bit ShortSoundtrack…………………………………………………………………………..⭐⭐⭐⭐/☆ (4/5)- This game has an awesome soundtrack that fits into its theme quite nicely. It’s quirky, lively, and a bit silly, which suits the game well. Only complaint is that there’s few songs. Graphics………………......……………………………………...........................⭐⭐⭐/☆☆ (3.5/5)- Good graphics for sure, but not as good as EtGs or Stardews. Boss sprites and character portraits look quite detailed though.  Atmosphere/Mood…………………………………………………………………⭐⭐⭐⭐/☆ (4/5)- A cultative combination of the music, bosses, crop animations, and more, the game accomplishes it’s mood quite well. Gameplay……………………………………………………………………………..⭐⭐⭐/☆☆ (3/5)- The game is a bit repetitive, and doesn’t have all the best permanent content. More on that later. Potential Time Investment…………………………………………………………..⭐⭐⭐/☆☆ (3/5)- Due to the lack of permanent content, and an issue with keeping players completely engaged, time invested will likely be a bit shorter than other roguelites. Price……………………………………………………………………………….⭐⭐⭐/☆☆ (3.5/5)- The price is probably a bit too high for this game. It is best to buy it on sale. Lacking of Bugs…………………………………………………………………⭐⭐⭐⭐/☆ (4.5/5)- I have found only one bug playing this game, though it’s hard to say if it’s a bug or an intentional feature. Overall Star Verdict*...………………………………………………………….🌟🌟🌟/☆☆ (25.5/35)- At its core, the game is a lot about management, where two interesting concepts have been combined in a way that is a bit short of being perfect. *Overall Star Verdict is calculated by finding the mean of the seven different categories; that is, adding them all up and dividing them by the amount (7) to calculate the Verdict. Generally, the initial Verdict will be rounded up for the final one.A lot of people want to say that this game is “Stardew meets Gungeon.” In part that is true, but definitely not completely. And not necessarily for the better. This game is a bit short of being a perfect combination of those games. Farming is definitely a major portion of this game, and for the most part it’s not bad. The player has to till the ground, plant the seeds, and water them, simple stuff. But the game takes it a bit further than that. Plants can be fertilized to increase their value. Fertilizer is dropped from enemies, tying in the farming with the combat a bit. In addition, if crops are  This is a fitting mechanic because it encourages players to think about how they arrange their crops, instead of just mindlessly planting them everywhere.  The action is a bit short of being up there with the greats. Lots of the time it’s somewhat repetitive, and unfortunately this doesn’t just apply to the farming aspect. There is little enemy variety, and several of the enemies are just enhanced versions of weaker ones. However, some of the enemies that there are have interesting attack patterns, which spice things up a bit. This issue also applies to the seasons as well. There’s four main seasons, and one final season. Each main season lasts three days, and features one boss at the very end. Every night the player will face a siege of mutant animals trying to eat the player’s crops. The difficulty of this siege ramps up nicely as the game progresses, and rarely feels unfair. In fact, at the beginning, it is actually quite easy. Very few enemies appear, and those that do have very little health. In addition, during the first year enemy bullets move insanely slow. But more on that later. Unfortunately, there is only one boss per season, which makes the fights feel a bit less unique. Once the player actually manages through the first four seasons they will go into the  This season is different from any other. It is entirely at night, and features only a single day. During this the player will be fighting off against the  This boss fight is actually very unique, because unlike most enemies it cannot be damaged through usual means. Instead, the player must . This boss fight is executed in a way that perfectly combines both the fighting and farming aspects of the game, and is definitely one of the highlights.  I mentioned how easy the first year of the game is. While that is still true, that does change later on. After beating the game once in the current year the player will be able to access the next year. There is not much difference between years, other than difficulty. As the years increase so do enemy bullet speeds, enemy attack speeds, enemy health, etc. Think of it as the Summoning Stones from UnderMine. There are some rewards for completing higher years, though they may not be enough to keep players engaged. The only rewards are  The marriage portion of this game isn’t exactly what it might seem like at first. It centers around roses, a rare crop that have a few, valuable uses, including dating. Dating one of the characters really just comes down to what they are offering at the time for the player’s roses. This makes it feel less like a relationship and more like a bartering system. In addition, besides from character portraits, none of the characters are interesting in the slightest. They have very little personality or story of any kind. This game has a beast of a soundtrack. The songs capture the feeling very well in the majority of the scenarios. My personal favorite is the boss theme of Summer. The graphics in this game are good too. Some sprites look a bit flat, especially with character and enemy sprites. This is heavily contradicted by the greatly detailed nature of the crops and boss sprites. There are some features that the game is missing and feels a bit unfinished because of it. Keep in mind these are from what I know and have experienced. First of all, there seems to be no almanac of any sort to keep track of the different crops. This makes it difficult to know which crops are more valuable than others, and as such makes it hard to prioritize which ones to grow. In addition, there’s no way to keep track of all the different items either, unless the player actively sees them or has them on them. Second, the game does not have an on-screen map. There is one in the inventory menu, but it’s quite small and not that helpful. Because of this, it’s easy to get lost at the start of the game. There’s also some areas that are just empty, with nothing in them at all. This is very apparent towards the ends of each biome. There’s also very few achievements in this game, and I don’t really see why that is. Hopefully more will be added in the future. So, for the most part, I do enjoy this game a fair bit. However, if you want to play a true roguelite, go play Enter the Gungeon or UnderMine. If you’re coming here purely for the farming, go play Stardew Valley instead. This game is not the best example of either of those two genres.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool and unique take on a roguelite that mixes a top down bullet hell with some basic farming sim elements in the vein of Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon into the mix. In general I really do just find this to be a rather unique experience though, not just for any one element, whether it's the structure, the artstyle, the premise, everything feels like a rather fresh take on this style of game and as such it had me hooked for quite a while. This is definitely worth a shot if you're at all interested in this genre and it in fact is probably an easy enough place to start for the most part if you're looking to get into roguelites on the whole for a few different reasons.One of the most interesting aspects of this game for me is the way that the scale feels extremely small, with the core gameplay loop revolving around leaving your farmland for stretches of 2 - 3 minutes at a time to collect resources and return to your farm to both grow crops and defend them from waves of enemies. Due to this limited time you are given with each day and night cycle, the world itself ends up being rather small and self-contained. This is further reinforced by the relatively small amount of items and upgrades actually present here, With 5 or 6 big runs likely being enough to have seen the vast majority of these rewards. While this limits variance, Atomicrops makes up for it by making almost every item a good choice instead, allowing for most runs to be viable to win in one way or another as long as the player properly sorts out their priorities on where to go from their current position. Any time you find an item, you're likely to be excited due to this as well, as you know that it is very likely to be getting a great upgrade that's worth the time investment to earn it.The lower quantity of variable content like this also makes the game rather accessible as well thanks to not having to keep tabs on so many moving parts at one time. I also love the way the items are framed in this, as the only way to consistently get them is to devote time to scavenging through the various biomes that surround you, which not only makes each encounter feed into a strong risk-reward dynamic, sacrificing time and potentially taking damage for an item, but it does wonders for the atmosphere as well. The game is able to so potently establish the setting of a nuclear wasteland through this gameplay loop, forcing the player to go out of their way and brave their harsh surroundings time and time again just to have enough resources to generate basic income. Having everything tie into each other so nicely creates a strong feeling of cohesion to the point where I'd say that nothing is particularly out of place or frivolous, it all feels very thoughtfully put together.While the lowered variance might help with this, I do think that the game has some issues with feeling almost as if you need certain upgrades to have any real chance of winning however. It feels like a run in this game is rarely able to get off the ground until the player has a few farm animals to help with the farming process, especially cows and pigs, but thanks to the random nature of this game, there are runs where the player will not get them early enough even if they spend their time aggressively exploring the landscape and doing nothing else until they're at a big disadvantage. While I understand that this can help craft a more dynamic experience and further contribute to the atmosphere, I feel like the borderline necessity of these animals is still frustrating nonetheless due to the fact that they're being put at such a steep disadvantage regardless, as I feel that in these sorts of games, the other items should feel more like things to improve your chances of winning or at least do something interesting, rather than being practically a requirement. Some of the enemy encounters also feel a bit rough, whether it's the worm boss with its strange hitboxes and absurd speed that can make certain situations undodgeable, or the mushroom boss that equates to running around your farm all night trying to meticulously track down every individual spore and wasting a lot of time without really acting as a threat, being far closer to a nuisance.Overall, while this game is a bit rough in certain regards, I still really like it and think it's quite a unique take on this genre. The developers also seem to be in a constant state of updating and improving this experience as well, as can be seen with their most recent update completely overhauling the weapon system to be less RNG dependant and more strategic, which is always something I adore seeing in games. I love how every element of this feels tied back into the central concept of farming, all the way down to your HP drops being seeds that you need to plant and have grow, rather than just generic hearts on the ground, really goes a long way to making things feel focused, and it also usually contributes to its own brand of challenge in the process. A must have for fans of roguelites, and probably one of the better starting points for those looking to get into those games as well.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best bullet hells on the market. What makes Atomicrops so good is the constantly changing pace. You're always in control of how intense you want things to be, and there's a lot of tools & upgrades to make each difficulty level enjoyable even for experienced players. Each of the guns is very unique and the way upgrades are modular means that it's unusual for the same set of guns to be the best option in a given run. Very tightly balanced with almost all upgrades valuable, although there are definitely some stand outs powerwise.I would highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm no stranger to roguelikes, some of my favorite games are in fact. I'm sure you see the red thumb and see where this is going: BUT. In Atomicrops, a game with a fantastic concept, the fact that it's a roguelike makes it fall flat on it's face, or maybe that's what makes it playable, I can't tell.Since this is a negative review I'm going to be dead serious and quickly go over the problems with Atomicrops:First of all, it's similar to bullet hell games, a genre I'm DEEPLY familiar with.  Hitboxes. You'll often find your limited health fleeting for all the wrong reasons. A bullet hell will feel most rewarding with a when you're punished only justly. Touhou Project accomplishes this with a minuscule hitbox in a very clear position, a small circle at the waist. In Atomicrops it's unclear where the hitbox is on not only the player but also on the projectiles, and it almost feels like the enemies don't play by the same rules you do. This amplifies attacks by making it impossible to go through with the intended dodging route for boss attacks.Second, it's a roguelike, another genre which I hold dear. I've been around the block, I have! I've played games like NetHack and Dwarf Fortress, and I've spent my share of hours on contemporary roguelikes like FTL.  In NetHack you fight to retrieve the Amulet and save the day! In Dwarf Fortress you wage wars, establish yourself through trade and diplomacy, and watch it crumble to ruin once you ー the player ー are enveloped in greed. In FTL you're being closely pursued by rebels while on a secret mission to destroy the flagship and stop the intergalactic coup! Certainly no small feat. You might think you know what I'm about to say, but I promise I'm not gonna say farming is pointless (lol). Roguelike is often more than an element to a game, it's a style. You find yourself getting invested in a sand castle and feel your heart break when the tide comes in, or overjoyed to have your picture taken with it before such. In Dwarf Fortress you can create a near-invincible fortress before entropy inevitably destroys it. In FTL you manage your ship's upgrades, and tweak it until it's ready for the next encounter. In Atomicrops I find myself starved of resources in one way or another. First you have too little seeds, then too little fertilizer, or maybe without an upgrade, and for what? Not only does it feel like you're not working towards some kind of end goal, it feels repetitive and futile because of the permadeath. Permadeath is a great mechanic, but in my experience with Atomicrops it feels suffocating, because I found myself dying far too often, almost like it was a game mechanic and not  In a roguelike you die or you lose or something, that's just a fact, but when it feels like you die and only die it gets frustrating. In FTL one game would be about two play sessions, 2:1. In Atomicrops I found myself playing two games in one session. The fact that the game itself points to a strategy guide stares this fact down in a way I can only describe as upsetting. It never feels like you're learning, it feels like you're losing.Finally, the concept. Fantastic. Farming and fighting twin stick style, two tried and true core mechanics that people love!  You're given very little time to focus on farming, and it's supposed to be what gets you through the game. For a game called Atomicrops, you can quite far with very little farming, not that you're allowed to do much to begin with. More than half the game is fighting, which is a bad thing if you subscribe to the ideas in the first section. If days and nights were twice as long the problems would be staved a bit but that fixes a symptom, not the system. So whats the point of farming? It's supposed to provide money, but it often provides so little for such substantial work during the day time. What does the money get you? You can buy seeds to plant more crops, and buy weapons (and tools every couple days). So you buy a weapon, and it is a fantastic upgrade!   So on top of not feeling like you're growing as a player, your character grows equally little.This cocktail of problems results in a mediocre experience that only languishes the further you play. That's all that progresses; playtime. You only play more of the same beginning without much of any further content that isn't about the same. You see people with absurd bank accounts in the game and think that it's difficult but accomplishable, but it seems it's some sort of positive feedback loop that the game doesn't allow players to enter easily.Atomicrops needs a massive rework. It feels like it's half of a game. Like a display of it's best mechanics in the worst way it possibly could. THERE! I didn't just say it's bad, I gave a few reasons, and even a solution for one! If my review says it was for a previous version then by all means take the game for a spin, but as it stands, this game feels like a prototype.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an unexpected treat. I received this game from a friend and didn't pick it up for a while because I just normally do not like bullet hell style games. But I was talked around into trying it and found the gameplay loop to be surprisingly fresh. Yes, expect to die. If you suck as badly at bullet hell games as I do, expect to die a LOT. I was worried the fact that dying ends your run would cause me to get frustrated and/or rage quit. But the farming aspect of it combined with the colorful graphics and jaunty music keeps me coming back for more. When you die, it doesn't feel unfair like so many games in this style feel. It feels like your fault and if you just worked at it a little bit more, you can do better next time. I see this game compared sometimes to Stardew Valley. I don't play games like this enough to make a good comparison, but I can definitely tell you it is NOTHING like Stardew Valley, so don't walk into it expecting that. It is not relaxing or peaceful, it is a mad dash to the finish line, with so many effects running across the screen at times you'll feel your eyes start to go crossed.  And yet there is something so satisfying about even death, when you see the new high score blip across your screen...Definitely not a 10/10 smash hit, but it's a solid 7/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a weird review to make. I've gotten to the last 'level' of this game, and unfortunately that's where I'm going to leave off.Atomicrops is a game about a man moving into an old farm after a nuclear bomb goes off nearby, creating mutant plants, residents and enemies that you have to mow through in order to get to the end. Throughout it all, you'll be getting upgrades that make the game not as difficult, and be growing crops to get money to expand outwards and continue playing the game.I'll start by saying this; Atomicrops is not a BAD game. It's fun, for sure, running about, planting crops, shooting and looting. It's also certainly unique- a cross between Stardew Valley and I suppose the Binding of Issac, with eight different areas that you can explore with 3 minutes in between each little pause to do so. The game revolves on a clock system- you have three days in a season, and four seasons in a year. Each day takes about 3 minutes to finish, where it'll go into night where you'll have to defend your crops in waves, usually taking another 3 minutes. 6 times 3 is 18, times 4 is 72, each round on average in Atomicrops takes about an hour and a half to complete.Of course, that's where the dullness starts to begin. Even after Year 3, I was feeling the tediousness of sorting out the game for the better. The bosses are repetitive, having only two of them per season, and have dodgy hitboxes that don't feel fair. Enemy variation is alright, but it feels like the enemies are placed at random.This is where my biggest gripe comes in. The game, of course, runs on an RNG system. It randomises literally everything that isn't the main character and the starting weapon, which can become hair-pulling when you're trying to keep alive and the game won't drop what you need to stay that way. This also adds into my least favourite aspect of the game- the fact that Achievements are directly linked INTO the game and its progression, asking you to earn (At most) 90% of the achievements to claim 100% completion in the hub area of the game.This would be okay if the achievements in this game weren't mind-numbingly difficult to obtain, especially with the RNG of it. One achievement in this game (One that, for the first time, I refuse to even try and obtain) is called 'Extra Fries'- it requires to you to grow and harvest 114 potatoes in 10 seconds. For reference, Potatoes are the starting plant, and do not drop from anywhere in the game except weeds in the main area of the battlefield. This means you need something called the Sprinkler Tractor, that drops seeds upon landing on them after you plant them, but tractors have a charge that needs to be refreshed after each use- UNLESS you have an item called Hotwire, which randomly appears from crates or purchases from the townsfolk, who only have a small chance to have it, which you also need roses to trade to get, and that's not taking into account that you need 114 spaces of tilled soil to even PLANT that many potatoes, so you need to get lucky with pickaxes, or earthquake scrolls, or pigs... And you can see why it's such a difficult achievement to obtain.And that's not even taking into account the fact that you also have to battle the Year System. Sure, for most of the achievements it is easily obtainable to get them on Year 1, the starting year, but that year is dull and boring and takes too long to be fun. But then there's the Year 10, and specifically, the 'Robusta's Hoodie' achievement, which requires you to not only beat Year 10 but beat it with the character that doubles the game's speed. Everything moving twice as quickly when it's already impossible not to take damage in a year that has too much to even dodge.I also have to point out that I REALLY don't like the artstyle. It's pixel-art but in an uncanny valley type way. The characters make facial expressions when firing their weapon that just looks wrong, and the only two human NPCs in the game have this malformed look to them that I just don't enjoy.Overall, I won't recommend Atomicrops, but I also won't outright tell you that it's a no-go. Atomicrops is a grey line on a white painting- you're not sure if its meant to be a design choice or a mistake, but it looks too weird to be ignored, and it makes you feel bad for hating it if others are enjoying it.
