_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I've ever played. Pleasing art style, awesome soundtrack, fun (and chaotic) game loop, and very replayable. Each time you win, you can increase the difficulty (up to 10) and buy permanent upgrades. It's not on Gungeon level with loot variation, but still has enough to make each run different and focused on different aspects of the game. Only flaw is that RNG really messes with you some runs. Sometimes I just restart when the first and second days' loot is awful, no matter how well you play. That and the image layering issue I've seen in-game and in other reviews, but other than that the game is really solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a lot of fun, despite a few big issues.The game alternates between running around the overworld, run'n'gunning enemies and collecting upgrades / seeds, and then returning to your farm to plan and harvest whilst defending against waves of intruders.The core gameplay-loop is satisfying, and everything you do feeds into  other parts. The controls are responsive, and the game has a charmingly creepy visual flair to it. Combining, defending and then harvesting your crops is satisfying, and so is the thus earned spending of cash in town for new things to play around with. The Upgrades are varied, and quite a few of them can make otherwise mundane parts of the game a core component of your earning strategy.So the baseline of the game is fairly solid, and I do recommend it on that basis. But there are a few issues, some of them quite major:- The game does not have a strong visual fidelity, or to put it in a less pretentious manner: It is soemtimes VERY hard to tell what the fu*k is going on. Enemies, your character and even your crops constantly wiggle and animate, all while increasingly large amounts of bullets cover most of the screen. I often take damage in the game from sources I couldn't even identify.-Some of the weapons suck. A lot. And in town, you get to pick 1 out of 2, meaning you'll often be stuck with a piece you don't really like. Since statupgrades are, largely luckily not entirely, tied to buying a new gun, this can be really annoying. Foregoing a purchase not for any strategic reason, but because you dislike the weapon, shouldn't really happen.- The game has a very harsh "Do bad, keep doing bad" curve going on, which can be frustrating. A lucky, or unlucky, set of first drops can majorly influence how your run will be going. And the stranglehold RNG has on the difficulty curve often annoys me. How much of a pro shooter you have to be often entirely depends on whether the game feels like throwing you a bone or not. Certain seed drops (Sunflowers and Heart Beets) can secure a season by themselves.Again, the game is fun. I just feel like it is very much "Okay" rather than "Good". Some balancing, or the option to turn down RNG a bit would def. help.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't gotten to experience many bullet-hell (Enter the Gungeon) type games but I absolutely fell in love with this game. It has SO much potential for additional content, the farming element is great with its currency/point system, crop combining, and somewhat tower defense night-time gameplay. Pros: - Cute apocalyptic plants that grow into overgrown "mutant" plants with enough fertilizer - Multiple playable characters with different attributes that affect your experience.- Meta currency (cornucopias) that improve your game and help you tackle each level of difficulty and subsequently improves the look of your “overworld” staging area that’s decrepit when you first start the game. - Decent difficulty scaling for casual/beginner players - Controller optimization is better than other games I’ve played, specifically comparing to Stardew Valley (though keyboard/mouse is easier in my experience)- Playtime is decent for the price (I’m on year 4 after 20 hours played, with a max of year 10 year difficulty)- The rose/relationships mechanic is a nice addition. Neutral-Music is quirky, you’ll either love it or hate it (I enjoy it)Cons-Gets somewhat repetitive with item builds and top tier items (and tractors), needs a bit more itemization or some sort of enhancements. For example, I feel like getting the weed wacker tractor is nearly required for later years to manage the weeds that grow into monsters if left unchecked. It would be nice to be able to buy “modifications” to tractors or even level up one plain tractor to have various abilities.-The gun mechanic (gun breaks after every day) is a little frustrating when paired with the fact that you get random guns every day and some are NOT very good at all. I’ve lost runs because I’ve been forced to take the squirrel or cleaver gun. All in all, I love this game, it’s unique with some flaws but not deal breakers, and I’d love to see more additions to the game in the future! How about a zombie DLC? Literal plants vs zombies opportunity!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute banger of a roguelite with a twist!Picked this title randomly from a retailer for 0.80 cents just by being amused of the game trailer (props to the advertiser, give him/her a raise!).Atomicrops tries to shake things up and bring a breath of fresh air, by combining the beloved action roguelite formula ( isometric action shooter in this case ) with farming! The game cycle is really interesting, having you charging in 4 different biomes and killing enemies by day, and grabbing seeds/upgrades and farm animals,while on the opposite hand during the night time you defend your farm.This whole system works like a charm encouraging micro managing your seeds,watering,tilling,planting etc while at the same time giving you insane adrenaline rush when you get raided at night (Some great Bosses appear too).On top of that your Farm/Main Hub Area is filled with tiny but permanent upgrades that very soon transform your whole experience and play style .Graphics are cute and different animations for upgrades/equipment and even cats are very cute,There are also Years,which serve as higher difficulty settings offering higher risk to reward ratio, as usual in modern roguelike games.The replayability here is insane and the game encourages you to complete the steam achievements (which I really recommend giving a try to complete) which reward you in game too,which is something really pleasant to stumble upon,i think for the first time.To sum up,Atomicrops is one of those silly games that you pick up cheap but fill you schedule for days without  a pleasant way.My only negative opinion about the game is that runs sometime take too long (more than an hour) so many people use Robusta (a character that speeds up everything real time) but I find playing with him very nauseating and not enjoyable.But this is understandable, because of the whole game system and mechanics. Keys sell insanely cheap online, so you have no excuse to not give this little roguelite a try :))

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelite fans wanting something a bit different, and want something to put a lot of time in.  Atomicrops is one of those games that's the definition of a solid purchase. You're not going to feel bad about the 15 dollars spent here as you will get a fun return on investment here, something that you'll play for hours at a time (hell even with leaving the game on, notice the hours played here). Will the game be something that will revolutionize the genre or will stick with you 10-15 years down the road? Not right now no, I do believe that is possible with tweaks here and there it could be, but it's a game that has a couple of “yeah, but”s about it that won't put it in the elite. That definitely doesn't mean it's not worth the money.It's the combination of mechanics here that really shine, as the basic but not too complicated shooting turning into resource gathering turning into a chaotic version of Harvest Moon/Rune Factory all combines into a roguelite game that succeeds in each phase of its gameplay.  Guns are fun to use and do have reasonable strategies, and little additions like the combination of crops for 2x2 mega crops add a layer of skill for those looking to maximize their runs. Chaos is the name of the game here, as some additions of the time mechanic and limited space to build your plots can punish bad choices but also puts you under pressure to actually do things. The difficulty scales in years reasonably without feeling like just adding bullet sponges.A lot of my complaints about the game are little ones, things that can irk me, but don't drag the overall experience down. I would like to see a couple of more weapons added, and more items that make watering less reliant on getting watering cow on your side. I do think more can be done on the procedural generation on the biomes, and I think that “gun breaks less” character does need a balance change.Overall, a solid game that can help you being stuck at home and take hours and hours of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Developers if you're reading this, I'm sorry but this game is very boring and poorly thought out. I tried to like it, but I can't.A bullet-hell and farming sim crossover? _childDocuments_.review: I try to avoid roguelikes/lites unless there's an upgrade system of some kind.  Yeah, you can practice and learn from each run, but given my limited time to game, I like games that give a sense of progression outside of simply learning the game.  Games like Rogue Legacy and Heroes of Hammerwatch come to mind as games that implement these systems well.Hence, Atomicrops, advertising that you can "permanently upgrade" things with a special currency each run, made this a possibly viable game.  That, coupled with the farming concept & art style, seemed like it'd be a pretty fun time.Alas, the permanent upgrades are extremely limited.  Even within the game, stats are very simplistic.  Enemies are bullet-spongey from the start, and there doesn't appear to be any way to raise your base damage.  After putting in 4 hours and multiple attempts with the first 2 characters, I've gotten to the end of year 1 a few times.  However, grinding to that point over and over, with the extraordinarily minuscule gains earned each run, wears thin quickly.  This is the type of roguelite I don't like, wherein the luck of the draw on which relics and weapons you get access to can be a bigger determinant of your success than your strategy or skill.As so many reviewers share, Steam really needs to have a 'meh' option or a numerical rating system.  I wouldn't outright give this a 'no', but would caution anybody looking for an in-depth upgrade and progression system to look elsewhere.  This is much more Binding of Isaac than Rogue Legacy.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 5/5 Bullet-hell rouge-lite with multitasking farming components and a psychedelic post-nuclear war setting.Atomicrops is about speed and opportunity cost. Days last only a few minutes and planning ahead can be vital.The game is structured into three phases: Day, night, town-time. During the day you traverse 4 different biomes located north, east, south and west of your farm. The goal is to defeat as many enemy camps as possible ideally during day time. They will reward you with upgrades and usable items including seeds. You'll get to choose between upgrades often.During night time your crops will be attacked and you have the opportunity to defend and plant seeds. After the night is over you get to spend cashews and roses the two main currencies in town. The game will always teleport you there with a high chance of breaking your weapon and equipping you with your standard pee shooter. But no worry, you can buy weapons in town and progress with the relationship of NPC. There are 4 seasons, with each 3 days and a bonus one with only a final boss fight. The third day of each season consists of a boss fight at night so planning ahead is crucial. Once the boss is defeated, you get to access the upper part of the town where your harvesting performance gets rated and potentially a lot of upgrades and currency awaits. This includes cornucopias, the currency that can permanently upgrade your character. To do so you'll have to rescue ant builders, which will randomly spawn in one of the four games biomes(either in tier 1 or tier 2).  To progress into new game areas you'll need bridge parts or a certain item. Variety in the game is only achieved through unlocking new years. you do this by beating a whole year. The game will end then, teleport you to the starting area and you unlock the next year. There are 10 years, each making the game more difficult. Featuring faster enemies, numerous new enemies, new attack patterns, less starting health and higher item prices. You can select which year to start before each run. I've been enjoying the game a lot and the music and theme is super catchy, colorful and psychedelic

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly my favourite game of all time and something I find myself picking up for a few hours frequently. My hours in this game may not be as massive as some other games I've played, but the sheer joy this game brings me more than makes up for it. The game is pretty hard. It's a rogue-lite twin stick shooter bullet hell farming game, and I've never seen anything like it. I main Dandelion or Oregacrow primarily. I've gotten to year 7 difficulty and I still find myself dying on year 3 sometimes with the latest DLC boss fight. This game makes you get good, and I ended up getting better rather quickly. Year 1 was originally hard to beat and took me many failed attempts, but through trial and error you learn what's going on. I never touched a guide for this game, and only recently started looking at what other people do in the game. I definitely recommend going in blind, rather than confusing yourself with strategy videos on the internet. The game will teach you what you need to know, and any cracks can then be filled with seeing how other people play.

_childDocuments_.review: (Full Disclosure: I got this as part of the September 2021 Humble Bundle, so while it wasn't free I didn't pay $15 for it)Nope. That's an overall nope, not a nope on everything. The graphics are cutesy and the music is good, so it's the gameplay alone that takes this one down. In its attempt to be a hybrid farming/action shooter game, it does both poorly. The farming is simply holding down the RMB on a space to till and again to plant. To water your crops, stand near them after visiting your well. It feels like a bad mobile game where I'm just tapping the screen. Alternately, instead of farming (or while farming at night) you can go kill mobs surrounding your farm. Gameplay here is a meh bullet hell, but with only a few slow-motion balls on the screen at a time.I'm not saying it is impossible to have a mash-up of Stardew Valley with Enter the Gungeon, but am saying this ain't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: this is gonna be one of those reviews that makes me hate the thumbs up/down system steam hasthis game feels like it could easily be 5 stars, the first couple years of the game are fantastic and had me hooked, but as you unlock more years, the difficulty spikes and HARD as youre at the mercy of RNG. until you get a cow to help with watering and a pig to help with expanding your land, you're pretty much useless, the years start off harder than they end as you're forced to fend off relentless enemies with your pea shooter for the first couple days. you get less hearts and spend the first 2 days dodging countless bullets from dozens of basic rabbit enemies as they begin to take 4-6 shots to take down. what started as some of the easiest enemies to take down and avoid and kill, quickly became some of the most bothersome. once you can buy guns, and earn some decent perks, the combat becomes more bearable. but all it takes a small amount of bad luck, or a ballsy decisions gone wrong and you're dead. then the last hour or so is just down the drain, all the perks and weapons you've grown accustomed to are now gone as you've reset back to day 1 with nothing but a pea shooter, 5 hearts, some potatoes and 9 squares of soil.sure, there are some permanent changes you can earn throughout your various playthroughs, but its all meaningless stuff like "increase rain cloud duration by 20%" or "blood rain drops additional fertilizer". (you get fertilizer like candy btw). maybe the permanent upgrades improve once you give the ant 100 cornucopias for a workshop, but i only have 50 of them and frankly i dont know if i have the strength to even go on. i'm on year 4 and going through that first day again and heading to the easiest area only for dozens of enemies to see the screen covered in bullets and enemies all coming towards me, and knowing that this isnt even CLOSE to the hardest year is simply demotivating. i can't even fathom what year 10 must be like. i'm sure by the time most reach year 10, they'd have most things unlocked and who knows, maybe there are perks that let you start with a cow and a pig, and a character that has a faster and/or more powerful pea shooter or has 10 hearts no matter the year. it wouldnt fix all my problems, but just starting the year with those would mean so much to me.among other things, i feel like the game should be a tad more merciful. im fine with starting over from year one, but i feel like you should be given a bit of an extra chance when you die. i know theres a chance to find a respawn pod, and thats good, but maybe when you die, you have one extra life that puts you back at the start of the season with half your max hearts but you keep everything else and only let it happen once per playthrough. maybe there can be a new character that starts with additional lives but reduced hearts. i understand that most of my issues seem to be common traits of the rogue-like genre, reasons why i could never get into games like isaac or spelunky or gungeon, but unlike those, atomicrops actually managed to captivate me until i hit that wall where the game just became unforgiving. i'd like to make it clear that i dont mind the difficulty, but there does need to be a little bit of mercy. maybe i'll keep grinding the first couple years, maybe i'll unlock something that will alleviate most my stress and i wont just be forced to bullet hell while praying to the RNG gods for something that isnt crap, but if not, i think my playthrough ends here, and i'm legitimately sad to say that considering how much i did enjoy the first couple years.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - It comes down to: it's a rogue-like where you can't do anything to avoid getting hit due to sprite layering (or lack thereof). And I can not, will not, should not, recommend that to anyone.It's a shame, because the game is pretty fun.The trailer is pretty great.The music is pretty bangin'.And yet, they don't know how to layer sprites. So enemies will spawn/stand behind your farm animals, totally invisible to you, and then shoot you. You'll likely never even see the bullet that hits you.There's a ton of depth to this game, the mechanics are well thought out IMO, the bosses are fun, but it's literally impossible to recommend this game if the dev can't figure out how to show you the bullets that are coming to hit you. I sincerely could write multiple additional paragraphs on what I love about this game, but it doesn't matter, because I still won't recommend it, because it's still broken on a core level.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a good idea in there somewhere but the pacing is all wrong.It's too slow in terms of progress, upgrades take too long to earn for what are either barely noticeable permanent improvements or very temporary ones.Simultaneously the day/night cycle is too short to allow any real amount of exploration and farming, to do one properly means neglecting the other almost entirely.  The result of this is that you put no thought into what you are planting or when.This game would be so much better with a couple of tweaks.  Increase the benefit of upgrades a little, split the day up into farming and exploration sections, stop the timer during the farming part of the cycle to allow people to farm properly (use action points instead of time perhaps) and you could have a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Do you know what makes a good game become a great game? When you can't stop playing! That's exactly what happened to me with Atomicrops, planted and harvested by Bird Bath Games studios and published by the hand of Raw Fury, it's a roguelike title with immense action to the mix.Atomicrops are the mutant offspring of Stardew Valley and a top dow view roguelike such as The Binding of Isaac. A country life simulator, where planting is the soul of the business, but with a twist of walking with a gun in hand to annihilate everything that tries to destroy our plantation.Like most roguelikes, the story only serves as a backdrop to set the player in his universe. Well, in an area where practically nothing happens, a young man arrives with the promise of his uncle to have left him a farm. As soon as he arrives a large atomic explosion emerges from the horizon, leaving the entire area destroyed and with remnants of nuclear dust. Hence the name Atomicrops, since all the seeds we plant become super animated mutant vegetables.The main objective is to plant and harvest the vegetables to sell when the city sends rain. Hence the money to buy new weapons, evolve passive skills, and acquire small parts to build a bridge to find new areas. Within this spectrum of weapons and passive skills, there is still a skill that needs time before it is available, and that helps and in what way the player, the tractor. So there are some types of tractors other than the “Wrecker” that destroys all the weeds in its path and that drops seeds and fertilizer. The “Wood Chipper” that reduces enemies in the vicinity of the tractor in fertilizer, or the “Sprinkler” that helps to water the plantation.Returning to passive skills, as previously indicated, all purchases are made in the city where it will be possible to talk to the different NPC’s who sell these products. The currency of exchange in Atomicrops is the Cashew. However, there is still the possibility of exchanging roses for said passive skills that somehow help the player in his demand as a farmer. This is where the possibility of marrying one of the two characters for this purpose comes in. But how do you get married? What do you gain from that? Rue will join the player in the exploration of new areas, where he helps to attack enemies and leaves some seeds along the way. Borage will take care of the farm and will occasionally leave fertilizer.This title mixes three important elements, the fact of having to plant to get money, time management, and the way of combat. Regarding time management, during the day it is possible to take care of the plantations, explore the different areas that contain different types of seeds and enemies. When night comes, it is important to return to the farm and protect the plantations, since that is when all enemies decide to attack. Although the most important thing is to stay alive …There are also different seasons that are separated by three days of play. At the end of each season, there will be a confrontation against that season’s Boss. For example, in the summer it is necessary to defeat a sun, which, however friendly it seems in the first version, the second version of the confrontation will be much more complicated. The confrontation against the Bosses is in fact where the game goes from a simple situation of running and shooting to action and adrenaline high to its maximum exponent! Since it mixes attacks of all types and shapes where it is really necessary to have good reflexes. All enemies have different attack patterns, from huge bullet curtains to onslaught attacks.The design of everything is just wonderful, the enemies present themselves with a mixture of docile animals, but with attacks and fierce expressions. From rabbits that dominate different firearms to crabs with barrels of toxic waste on their backs.Atomicrops is a charming title, suitable for those looking for action and many hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is an addicting, fast-paced, farm sim/bullet hell/rogue-inspired game that is full of charm and passion. This game can be stressful at times but as a good friend of mine told me after buying the game "This game is excellent at rewarding the player" which couldn't be more accurate. If you want to play it safe you can do just that, but the game will reward you for taking extra risks. You could alternatively tend to your farm more since you have enough seeds to plant. The option is up to you. The more you harvest, the more money you receive which is how you get guns, animals, seeds, and other helpful things like that. Without a successful harvest, you won't reap nearly as many rewards, but a max season nets you multiple goodies that further aid you in your quest for the next season and combat purposes. The replay value comes from you upgrading your base with cats, permanent stat upgrades, obtaining collectibles in the wild, new characters, and best part of all, achievement hunting. I consider myself a big achievement hunter by nature. so when I first bought the game to see that the game gives you more permanent stat boosts from obtaining achievements, I was more than happy. That being said, there isn't much of a stat boost, but it's a little something extra. I just want to extend a big thank you to the devs for this masterpiece, and I would love to see and support future ideas behind the bright minds that brought us this game. If you were on the fence about buying this game, you should just buy it. It's super fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very addictive, with quite the learning curve at the beginning.  Only oddity is that in the opening area where you can select your character and more which has no fighting, it causes my GTX1070 to nearly max out at 4K 60fps max settings with 8x supersample in NVIDIA control panel everything set to quality, but everywhere else it stays below 50%.Playing the DLC now, and it is either a cash grab or a way to play the game with increased difficulty due to the fact you lose heart beats and have to grow oregano that goes into a cauldron by your farm where you can choose from a buff or heal.  But the more you grow the more it takes to fill the cauldron and the heal is inconsistent.  Might be +1 health or +3 health at the max.  This is offset by the fact you get cauldrons in town that add some buffs, but primarily adding day time to certain areas. Games like Binding of Isaac and Gunfire Reborn really spoil you with their item variety. One major issue is the power creep of the different guns they each serve their own specialization but stuff like the squirrel gun needs to go. I say its even worse than the pea shooter since the speed of the projectiles miss 80% of the time, especially against year 10 enemies since they usually move around so much. Finally my last small gripe would be the rotation of items from characters (where you use roses) where they would sell a heartbeat seed, just remove it please I am not paying 4-5-6 roses for 1 seed.I love the art style and the music is very poppy!Overall a very fun and enjoyable experience!

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits the spot for fans of many different game genres at the same time. I'm a fan of rogue-likes, farming and competitive games (RTS/MOBA). I could never enjoy top-down shooters or pixel art games, yet atomicrops struck gold for me. What's so good about this game for me is you play one run, the equivalent of one MOBA match, and have to find a way to best manage your resources within the time limit. Every day that passes the game gets harder, and if your strategy didn't allow you to scale high enough to beat the end game monsters, you lose the match.It's day 1. Do you spend your time planting your low-quality seeds to buy a weapon on day 2 and kickstart your early game, or do you ignore farming and explore for better tiered seeds for a better mid-game economy?Do you skip monster camps that won't give you an early game advantage, or do you full clear the biome?There's plenty of optimizations strategies like this to play around in atomicrops, and the matches/runs format really helps this. "Someone posted a new strategy, let me try it out in a match". "Let me just play a match before work". And then you do and see if it reflects in your high score.Like any other game that people speedrun these days, it's not originally a speedrunning game. I had to download a save file with all the things unlocked finished before I could start doing the highscore runs. The game has an excellent campaign, I had a lot of fun buying upgrades for my farm or character, but as a MOBA/RTS player, I found more fun doing the high score runs than finishing the campaign. Which again is why this game is so good: it hits the spot for many different types of people.

_childDocuments_.review: An EXCELLENT roguelike that impresses me every time I play.Combat feels so CLEAN! It's really satisfying to dodge bullets, get fun upgradable guns, and destroy everything in my path. The enemy types are interesting and provide a proper yet fair challenge. There have been very few times where i felt the damage I took was because of the game giving me something unfair.Farming is fun too! The micromanagement kinda feels like pikmin, in a sense, which is a game series i have thoroughly enjoyed. It can be stressful to farm at night while enemies are attacking you, but as long as you dodge while farming you really don't need to deal with the enemies until later years (which act as difficulty levels).The items and guns are really well designed, and each one can have a run built around it, which is a great aspect in any roguelike. You could go for walking on weeds cuts them up + cutting weeds damages nearby enemies + cutting weeds increases day length. You could go for increased rose drop rate + roses grow instantly + polygamy so you have an army of hunsbands and wives to decimate your enemies. Really anything goes in this game.Really not much to say here. Mostly I wish this game had a wider variety of items and guns. I wish the maps were a bit more random instead of the same one for every run. I wish the metaprogression had a bit less impact so you don't get a bit of a power creep halfway through the game.Other than my minor gripes with it though, the game does a really good job of making itself fun, fair, and all-in-all just a really good game. Even difficulty isn't a problem because less experienced players can stick to early years, and players looking for a real challenge can go into the later years or even use a turbo mode character. Heck, even I beat the first year after only like 5 tries, so that's gotta say something towards the accessibility of it.

_childDocuments_.review: And here I am all the sudden have over 30 hours on this farming sim x bullet hell roguelike. Only have made past half of the difficulties but I feel qualified and obligated to write a review.Starting with the aesthetics, I think they nailed it with the cartoony pixel art and silly sound effects. I'm no art major but I really like the style overall, works well with the gameplay.The best thing about the gameplay IMO is the pacing. During the ~10 minutes of day-night cycle I always feel engaged no matter what my choices are, and then I get the break while in town in between days with a chance to suspend progress. Other than that it's a less crazy version of Binding of Isaac; you get powerful upgrades throughout the run, some of them can combo but never break the game.  The final boss fight is also brilliant in that all your work matters, if you haven't gotten there I'll let you figure it out.The only negative in my experience is: some of the more powerful permanent upgrades depends on the previous run, encouraging me to do an easy run before trying out challenging difficulties.  So far I've chosen to ignore it and I still live.  It also wouldn't hurt to shrink the player hitbox just a tiny bit on the head, like 2 pixels.Overall I think this is an excellent, and one of the better roguelike games. Actually surprised it didn't become popular.  Would love to see more playable characters.  If you read this far, pick it up! It's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE this game. The roguelike elements and art style remind me of Nuclear Throne, but there is a really cool farming mechanic which is unique to these kinds of games. Each run is one year long, split into four seasons (each consisting of three days) with a boss at the end of each season  You need to split your time each day into farming and exploring/fighting enemies to find upgrades, seeds, fertiliser and items. At the end of each day you will be taken to a market where you can buy randomised weapons or equipment using money (cashews) earned from farming. This is not an easy game. It is fast paced and you have to make quick decisions on what to focus on and this can sometimes seem a little overwhelming (especially when you're new to the game) but the game doesn't punish you too badly and as long as you're spending the time doing SOMETHING, it'll usually all work out. The good news is that the more you play, the more unlocks (some permanent) you will find which will make the game easier. The "bad" news is that there are many different difficulty settings to make things even harder... After about 9 hours I'm still grinding the first difficulty to try and get more upgrades! All in all I really cannot recommend this game enough. It's straight forward enough that anyone should be able to jump in and give it a go, but challenging enough that even seasoned gamers will struggle with later difficulties. Whilst I don't think that there is such a thing as a "perfect" game, this is probably as close to a perfect roguelike for me as you can get so I'd give it a 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The last patch improved this game by leaps and bounds, and now it feels very fair and balanced.1st - they buffed watering significantly so it's no longer the only choke point of play. This is a huge + in my book.2nd - they buffed farming by adding an in-game upgrade system that gives you plots. These get bonuses and automatically sow seeds for you, helping with inventory management immensely. This gives you a lot more reason to farm while making it a viable lategame path. This increases variation in gameplay immensely since you must balance between those two playstyles throughout the game.It makes it a lot more fun, imo.3rd - They fixed several of the most annoying bugs that could really hamper the overall fun of game to game play. For example, these bomber guys could hit you from across the map for no reason, and it ruined visual clarity because they'd throw dozens of bombs on your screen. This is gone, and it helps the game immensely. Several big bug fixes like that happened, and it makes the game more polished.4th - They increased cornucopia gain, though this can still be quite a grind even if you win year 10 over and over again.This combined with more enemy types and options of play make this game a lot of fun. I do think there's still issues, but I consider this game to be excellent now, though visual clarity is still a problem at times. That's not a gamebreaker by any means, however.

So I will place here a recipe for huckleberry pancakes instead.Huckleberry pancakes.1 3/4 cups all purpose white flour4 tablespoons sugar1 tablespoon baking powder1/4 teaspoon salt1 1/2 cups of buttermilk5 tablespoon butter, melted2 large eggs1/2 cup HuckleberriesIn medium bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, set aside. In small bowl combine buttermilk, butter and eggs. Add buttermilk mixture to the flour mixture, combine until mixed do not over mix (I prefer to use a whisk it does the best job). Fry at 400 degrees. _childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly so addicting and fun. After I saw Skooch bring it up I thought it looked cool then Humble Bundle decided to drop this bombshell of a game onto my lap. It's very well designed and doesn't feel repetitive (aside maybe the first 30 seconds which is you just tilling your farm) and at first i was apalled that the game didn't rotate from Nuclear Winter ->Nuclear Spring/Spring and be year2 or such. BUT! Year 2 as a starting point is already so fun and challenging as a roguelike fan. I can't even imagine what year 3 on is gonna be like!!!There are unlockables just like a roguelike should have of course. You get cornacopeia or however it's spelt. And you gather these along your year to use in the hub to upgrade things like the scrolls you use, the tractors you get, your starter gun etc.I think my only real complaint is the gun breaking, after i invest so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ money in them. But to be honest if you're playing the game right you DON'T NEED the new guns you bought really. It makes the game easier (most of the time... I'm lookin at you butcher knife and squirrel gun) but it really sucks to invest a lotta money into the guns only for them to break. But hell. later in the year if again you're playing right. You should be making so much money it won't MATTER if your gun breaks.I'd say my favorite way to play is to just get a lotta barn animals. Cows will help water your plants, Chickens eat weeds (that grow on your tilled land irritatingly enough), and Bees pollinate your plants to grow faster. Turrets and scarecrows are also a thing (though tbh i only really care about the turrets) and there are upgrades to these things as well! Like to use a million turrets? BAM you can get upgrades that allow your turrets to water plants around it. Like having a LOT of cows that water your plants? BAM The cows can take bullets and ♥♥♥♥ them out for you. DO YOU LOVE CHICKENS EDDY?! They turn weeds into ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flowers that you can harvest and honestly the money adds up!Normally I always recommend to buy a game when it's on sale, but I'd honestly say I woulda paid $20 if I knew this game was this fun! If you like Binding of Isaac THIS is the game for you. No question

_childDocuments_.review: I've never cared too much for Rogue-likes or even "Rogue-lites", the lack of progress (due to its mechanics) and the grinding nature (due to its mechanics) of the gameplay usually puts me off and makes me go look for more satisfying mechanics. All things considered it's still and interesting game that plays pretty well, with an interesting spin on what is a very common style of mechanics. On top of that it combines it with the bullet hell style and adds another element of stress for the player to manage.Getting started seems to be very important and will determine the rest of the game, as a lack of exploration and swift sowing will result in lagging behind and a slow but eventual defeat. The sessions are not that long between deaths but at least for me it gets a bit tedious after a while, but I might perform a lot better if I looked up some guides and learned a few strategies for metaplay.While it's not my cup of tea it's a nice implementation and a really nice independent production that I would recommend if pixel graphics, Rogue-likes, and bullet hell is what you enjoy.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is interesting with how it's handled the gameplay loop and is a bit deceptive with the whole farm, marry, kill tag line. If you go into the game thinking there's going to be more dating elements and farming is done separately sort of like stardew valley but with guns and action packed content then you're going to be disappointed. In reality Atomicrops is a rougelite top down shooter with an emphasis on time attack. You go through the four seasons split into three days each and your goal is to simply survive while making as many cashews (currency) as you can. Every day is split into a day and night cycle where you go out and explore doing the day (usually 2 minutes long), collect upgrades and seeds, and overall just kill everything in sight. When night falls you've generally got to go back to the farm to protect it from bundits and pests trying to destroys your crops (usually 30 to 40 second waves). Although if you don't plant anything you can strategically ignore this part of the cycle and continue to explore and gather upgrades but be warned that your farm is the key to making money. At the end of every day a chopper comes in a takes you into town where you spend your currencies. Roses are given to specific npcs that in turn give you specific upgrades they have that day with upgrades randomly changing every day and eventually ending in their wedding ring once you've gone through the friendship cycle with them. Marriage comes with bonuses such as having an extra friend to fight with you or someone who will stick around and take care of the farm while you're gone. Cashews are used to buy guns in which stats are attached to so generally speaking you want to buy a gun every day but not all guns are worth it and sometimes you might not need certain stats. Other than that you spend your cashews on seeds, pickaxes, fruit trees, farm animals, etc, and when all is said and done you repeat the cycle by going back to the chopper and doing it all again. As you get stronger you can explore the other areas from the desert, plains, jungle, tundra, and to each respective biome's second area. Overall the game is fun and once you get a feel for how it works you can kind of enter a sort of flow state where you know what you're looking for and what you're lacking but also ultimately as usual with these types of games you're at the mercy of rng a lot of the time. Lacking in seeds, not getting enough fertilizer, having a problem keeping all the crops watered, etc. There's definitely a bit of a problem when it comes to replayability once you hit year 10 which is essentially the hardest difficulty. Most big unlocks are dictated by which year you clear and otherwise at the main menu you spend cornucopias you earned from beating bosses and games on permanent upgrades to help with the cycle. Atomicrops can also be frustrating at times with how much visual clutter there is on the screen at times from enemy bullets, your own projectiles, flashy effects, aoe indicators, enemies randomly spawning behind you, etc. Often times, especially near fall and winter, I find myself going "what the actual ♥♥♥♥ is going on right now???"

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting rouge lite that blends bullet hell, survival, and farming. The game is nuanced and rewards more time with the game, allowing payers to discover elements of the game that are not explicitly explained as well as a realm of potential strategy. Smart farming is also rewarded, with higher crop yields and potential for even more if you build your plot well and plant strategically. Starting out in the game is somewhat slow and you will probably wander through the game without a clear aim besides survive and grow as many seeds as possible. Discovering that growing 4 of the same seed in a square and feeding them compost will allow you to make mega seeds. This is a game changer and will make the farming much more strategic, and increase your success in the game by a wide margin.At 15 hours I'm enjoying the game more and more as I come to understand the strategy, and understand how to beat the game on the basic difficulty. Don't expect to grow into a pro over night but stick with it and you'll become a dedicated nuclear farmer in no time.

_childDocuments_.review: A great top-dopwn action rogue-like mixed with farming sim, but I have to give a downvote due to whatever the hell they did with the recent updates, because holy hell they cranked the difficulty level to twenty. The final boss is just a bullet hell nightmare, caking the screen in everything, which wouldn't be a problem in of itself were it not for the fact that you have to farm in order to damage it, which is nigh impossible with all the crap on the screen. It fells almost as if they took something difficult but balanced, then someone sat on the control panel and accidentally upped everything without knowing.EDIT: Okay, I came back to see if any updates may have fixed the issue, and, starting over, It feels fairly balanced so far, though I have yet to get to the later difficulties where I experienced the BS. However, I will retain my negative review for one reason. There is a glitch that I have found twice in a single day of playing that cripples the player, stopping me from firing my gun. It affects controller and M&K alike, and cannot be fixed with rebinding. It stops if you transition levels, but good luck when it happens, especially during a boss fight without the ability to defend yourself. This is a potentially run ruining kind of glitch that cannot be toleratedEDIT EDIT: Okay, after playing a lot more, it seems that all of the issues I've had have been fixed, so I can give this the thumbs up i originally wanted to give this game. some of the bosses are still less fun to fight than they could be (the spider comes to mind), and the game loop is ridged due stark disparity in efficiency between low and high water demanding crops, but overall, this game is a good blend of action and farming sim. the randomness is solid enough to make no two runs completely alike, and the amount of content and progession metrics are enough to give that sense of consistent achievement. Don't know what as with the difficulty spike in the past, but it's all good now.

_childDocuments_.review: is the best game I've played all year, hands down. It's so good in fact, that I had to buy it for four other friends, just to give them the excuse to play it too.It's a fast-paced, run-and-gun bullet hell game with a bunch of strategy and unlockables. The permadeath and randomised nature of it means every run is different, from the placements of enemies to the items you get to power your farms, to the people you can marry to fight alongside you to the bosses you fight. The range of characters and the 1-10 difficulty system (called 'Years' in the game) give you a steady but measured increase in difficulty which eventually builds up to the hardest year, Year 10.There has been no greater moment playing a game that I can remember in recent times than completing the (very difficult)  achievement with about 0.5 seconds on the clock. The largest portion of the run was spent strategising how I was going to kill that many elite enemies in one day, preparing the area, preparing items and practicing the route I was going to take - having it work first time was also a blessing!The game is endlessly addictive, and the majority of my 81 hours within the game come from just playing for fun, not for any particular mission. The wide range of achievements, playable characters, items, animals, bosses, locations, enemies - the list goes on - make it one of the best games I've played in recent memory. Every friend that's played it has also said it's a great game, and it makes for a pretty entertaining one to watch too.Games with underlying metas and strategies are also a fun highlight to me - sharing tips with friends about the best items, the best synergies etc. reminded me of childhood rumours about Pokemon moves and the best teams you could achieve in those. The art style is also a huge plus, not too insane on the eyes and quite charming.In short; you should play this game if you like dungeon crawlers or bullet hell. Instead of a dungeon to crawl you have 8 areas to explore every game, and the difficulty curve is generated per-run - so every run usually has some kind of on-the-edge "I'm about to die" moment which only ever goes one of two ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is pure chaos. But it's the good kind of chaos. It is your typical farming sim except that a nuclear bomb dropped on the farm and destroyed everything while also mutating plant and wildlife. Now your only goal is to survive the next years.Atomicrops is mainly one thing, a roguelite. Each year in the game is an independant run. You need to grow food on the remains of your farm to supply the local mutant folks with fresh food, which they reward you with money in return. The game features a day and night cycle like you would expect from a farming sim. Daytime is usally calmer and you are mostly save onj your farm except the occasional mole. Around your farm are four biomes, each one having their own distinct enemies. Enemies either roam around or protect camps. These camps give rewards if you kill their guards. This way you get seeds, items and animals for your farm. It is necessary to scavenge the biomes for anything useful, mostly seeds and items so you are prepared for the night.The night is when things start to get hectic. Bundits (bunny bandits) attack your farm in multiple waves and try to destroy your crops or kill you. These waves get stronger as you progress through the seasons. At the last day of the season you will also fight a boss. It should be worth noting, you don't have to kill all the enemies, you just have to survive until the night ends. But killing enemies will drop fertilizer and sometimes seeds.Between scavenging biomes and defending your farm at the night you also have to find the time to take care of your farm work. You need to plant seeds, water the seeds, fertilize them for extra value and eventually harvest them. You also need to cut down weeds, which will block seed placement and till the soil between harvests. Each crop you harvest gives you instant money which you can spend after each night in the town to buy a new weapon, seeds or other stuff. Buying guns is incredibly important because that's the main way to improve your stats. Every time you buy a gun, you increase one of two stats, farming or fighting. Farming improves the speed of all farming actions while fighting increases damage and movement speed. You need a good balance between both of those stats, no matter what kind of build you aim for.Weapons will also come with random mods which have all kinds of passive effects that are unique for each weapon.At the end of each season you also get a festival which acts as a scoring system. Depending on how many crops you sold, you get rewards from the town mayor, more crops means more rewards. These rewards are helpful in the long run since they include stats items and animals. Speaking of animals, animals work differently here compared to other farming sims. Instead of taking care of them, they take care of your farm. Each animal does something different to help with your farm work. Cows water crops, pigs till soil, chickens eat weeds and bees will speed up growth. Animals are needed to save time on farm work and reach huge profit numbers. There are also useful items that synergize with your animals.Beating four seasons and returning to your farm one last time will also start the final boss fight. This boss works completely different to the other bosses. Instead of taking damage from your weapon, he takes damage from harvested crops. So if you didn't invest in a good farming strategy you will have a bad time.Beating seasons will also give you a currency for metaprogression. You can buy upgrades between runs but I don't like this part to be honest. The upgrades are not very good and are too expensive but you need them to have a chance at the higher difficulties. It also doesn't help that if you browse through the upgrades, they are all listed individually instead of summing up the ones that are identical. Makes it hard to read through the list to understand what benefits you currently have.The visual art style is very bright and colorful and emulates a cartoon style. This also fits the music, which is loud and chaotic. It is the perfect style for a chaotic game like Atomicrops.And for people that want even more chaos, there is the challenge character Robusta which speeds up the entire game (you, enemies, bullets and the timer). Beating the highest difficulty with him even unlocks a special achievement and cosmetic award.Overall, if you like hectic bullet hell roguelites and want to try something very unique with its gameplay, buy Atomicrops. I didn't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate giving this game a thumbs down because I really like it, but there's some issues that I think really needs to be addressed. The game is just way too greedy when it comes to rewarding players. Dodge roll games made the same mistake with Enter the Gungeon, and they listened to the feedback and made it better.Guns cost way too much money early on in a run. You can try growing as much crops as you want, combined crops, grow sunflowers that give you extra money, have chickens lay eggs for money, but you never seem to make enough money to buy a weapon, and even if you see a weapon that you can afford, it so happens to be lower tier weapons, the type of weapons that have waaaay too slow reload speeds that are absolutely ABYSMAL going into YEAR 2 and over. Ill be into my 3rd day, at the store ready to go into the 4th day, not able to afford useful weapons leaving me no choice but to continue on with the pea shooter which is just a very terrible weapon mid/late into the run, IN HOPES that I can finally get a weapon that I can actually rely on. Even other roguelikes like enter the gungeon start you off with weapons that you can use for an entire run.Sometimes growing crops just feels absolutely pointless when the money return is so little, you cant afford anything, your efforts have no rewards. Sometime's I skip growing crops for a 1-2 days and just go explore to see if I can find anything useful like seeds, or pets to help me efficiently grow crops to gain more money, but it just feels like it's hopeless. There's almost no motivation to continue playing.I hope that you devs look into this, because I've been researching and it seems like many players feel the same way about the game.As for what I like about this game, I love bullet hell games so thats why I bothered to check it out. The animations and character designs are fantastic, I love the soundtrack.Also I come from playing the nintendo switch version, that version weapons are easier to buy but the weapons break after a day, so I was use to playing the outdated version that you guys apparently haven't updated yet. I bought it on steam because the performance on switch is unplayable when things get very hectic.

But once I get familiar with the garden, fix the bridge, know the routing to dodge bullets, planting a whole screen of the planet is fun. Game also tests strategy and time management. _childDocuments_.review: Frickin love this game, absolutely delightful surprise. I got this game from Humble Bundle and didn't expect anything original or mind-blowing, I ended up with 42 hours and still not even halfway done with it and that's coming from someone who hates rogue-likes.A brilliant bullet-hell, farming sim, rogue-like and while that may sound like some other indie games you probably forget the names of this is different. The game is split into exploring and gathering during the day and fortress defence and farming during the night, each day is about 4 minutes making its feedback loop quite addictive. Farming and shooting are equally satisfying to do and getting good at them doesn't take too much effort. Once you survive a year it doesn't turn into the next year but instead brings you back to the hub and acts as a new run more difficult than the last. The bosses each season are incredibly well designed and well animated, each one is completely unique and they are perfectly challenging. Hell all the characters have amazing designs and animations. The art and aesthetic is so well done and very pleasing to look at.I really hope this game gets more attention and more praise because it is genuinely one of the best rogue-likes I've ever played. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in the midst of an identity crisis and doesn't excel in any genre it is trying to be in. In terms of farming simulator, you are limited in what you can plant due to the amount of space and adding more space is random. I've had runs where I've only gotten one expansion on farming ground and a couple pickaxes that provide one-off soil expansions. There are frustrations with the farming part that I guess is supposed to be the challenge of the game but in the end it's more annoying than fun. You need to combine your seeds into a 2 x 2 section instead of planting them in 1 x 1 bits in your garden to maximize your cashew profit (game currency) but this is difficult because of the controls plus the time constraints plus the enemies trying to kill you. It is a bullethell game, so you will most likely want to use a controller but, doing so provides an awkward farming experience. The only time when the clock is not ticking down to the next enemy wave or boss is at the end of a day or season and unless you have stocked cashews (the games currency) visiting the city is pointless. There really, really needs to be a point where you can manage your garden without the hassle of time constraints or constant enemies attacking. The permanent upgrades also are meaningless and do not give any sense of progression (i.e spending a whole run to get enough permanent upgrade points for a 1% chance of guns not breaking is not worth it imo). I truly believe the game is designed the way it is to mask the fact it has little content to offer. There are maybe 7 guns total and you do not get to keep them after purchasing them (they break at the end of a day) and there are a couple npc's that you can marry to offer you additional benefits like fighting with you or tending to your garden. While I think the mix of farming simulator and roguelite can work, I think the developers have missed the mark completely. I've completed year one and I feel like I have seen everything the game has to offer in 4 hours. I would HIGHLY suggest to the developers that the clock not start until you leave your garden at the start of the season or day. This simple change would do wonders and give players the opportunity to layout their garden. The game also needs more content in terms of items, weapons, enemies and just general overall variety. Year 2 felt exactly the same as year 1. The weapons breaking also feels like an afterthought. Like I said in the beginning, the game is trying to do so much , that it is missing that polish from both genres of roguelite and farming simulator that can just make the game fun. I will keep an eye on it to see how it develops as it seems to be getting updates regularly but I would not recommend it in it's current state as once you figure out the formula for progression, there are more frustrations than fun once the veil is lifted.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Takes too long to get to the good part of the game each time. The repetitive startup section wears very thin after a few runs. Visual clarity could be much better, which is something important for a bullet dodging game like this. It would probably be more fun if more of the mundane tasks like picking weeds/tilling soil were done automatically by standing in close proximity, the same way that watering works, holding the button down is very tiresome after a while. Base gun isn't much fun, and depending on how your run is going you might be stuck with it longer than you want. The farming aspect feels very secondary to the roguelike shooter aspect, but exploring the same weak environments every game isn't interesting enough. While there is some fun here, everything feels too slow, and it's never good when the game reminds you of other games that do what it does better.  It was entertaining for a bit but I got so bored with the early startup portion of the game that seems to take so long, the slow walking, the slow shooting, the slow planting. An action game shouldn't require this much waiting, and I can find better options.-extremely repetitive-environments offer very little variety-planting stuff is a chore-farming is an afterthought to shooting-often stuck with the boring starter weapon for long stretches-game is too slow to get going.-game years seem to just make the game harder, not introduce new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Combining a farming simulator in a post-apocalyptic world with an action-packed roguelite is a very daring idea. The setting of the world reviving after a nuclear disaster is revealed in the game with dark humor and no less dark overtones. We sow the beds with completely ugly plants, raid the camps of mutant bunnies to get precious seeds and artifacts, and then save up money and marry a mutated rabbit. Well, or at the local analogue of Doctor Manhattan. Or not marry anyone, but eat your cucumbers in splendid isolation. The cultivation of gardens takes place in very close contact with the protection from the raids of mutant bunnies, and you also need to find time for raids on hostile territories. Every three days, a huge boss runs into our garden with a bunch of henchmen, who will be very difficult to cope with. It sounds cool, and it is played very cool, even if it was not without its drawbacks. And the designation of these shortcomings is extremely constructive, because I really want an already good game to become even better.The gameplay immediately captivates you with the speed of what is happening and the requirements for your ability to make quick decisions. Most often, the player has to solve a large number of tasks in an extremely limited time, which leads to a constant flow of adrenaline into the body. And it's a lot of fun, but gradually you start wanting more. And here comes a collision with reality, namely, with the fact that the game desperately needs a greater variety of content. Difficulty levels are displayed here in years, and the maximum is Year 10. So how is Year 10 different from Year 1? Insane number and high health of enemies, more advanced artifacts, several new playable characters and that's it. That is, there are no questions, the complexity grows insanely, but what changes besides this. All enemies are the same. All bosses (there are 5 of them here) are still the same and go in the same order. All locations are the same, and they are all available to you even in Year 1, even in Year 10. You can make at least 2 different bosses in each season, so that the player has this expectation of the unexpected constantly inside. Some secret locations with powerful enemies, but also corresponding rewards, available only at the highest difficulty levels. More weapons than there are now, and more possible characters with whom you can start a relationship, with unique abilities that they give you as a reward. The forums show that the creators continue to develop their game, so I am confident in its bright future.This game is already very good at the moment. Gorgeous visual design, its own indescribable style, hurricane action, a very natural mixture of genres, which seemed so easy for the creators. To build up more meat for these muscles and the game will definitely become one of the pillars of the genre, I have no doubt about it.

The increasing difficulty system is pretty good and the curve isn't TOO horrible. They're still providing free updates which is neat. It's definitely worth it to play.

_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 5-10 hours in and still haven't gotten past winter year 1, yet I can play Issac on hardmode... Pros:It's a rougelike I guess? Props for trying to make a new "genre" of farming. too bad it requires rng to unlock any permanent upgrades.Artwork is okin-game upgrades are a short walk away, and diversified. For some reason the game is still compelling enough that I keep wanting to go back to it, but TBH I think it's just me wanting to at least finish a fully year and unlock permanent upgrades before throwing in the towel on the game. This game has nothing on the difficulty when compared with demon souls lol.Cons:gameplay is sloppy. It's actively encouraged to "hold" down both mouse buttons...There's no time to "farm" if you even want to call it that.Most "runs" in this game are less than 10 minutes in length.Enemy difficulty scales with time, so too does shop costs etc. If you're broke once you'll be broke forever till you die. Have fun at the mandatory shops!The game just drops you into it, with a 2min tutorial that doesn't even explain some of the finer mechanics like mega crops, what roses are for, how to heal, etc.Like custom controls? Well certain buttons are out. Can't map to num pad or even use it (in general)Want to use a controller. I hope you love Xbox scheme...The whole game runs on a timer. You've got maybe 2 mins plus before returning to town. Upgrades are 100% not balanced (which is fine for the most part IMO)Permanent unlocks are mysterious. There's no "hand-holding" or goals for that matter. Hell I don't even know "how" I unlocked some of the characters...Update: I googled it & being able to "unlock" the permanent upgrades relies heavily on RNG.The game lack of a real inventory. Every thing is coded as a scroll wheel to a single button. You have 1 active item, 1 active tractor, 1 active seed. See where I'm going here. No hotbar, no number row, 1 button per category each.The hitboxes are slightly off sometimes you'll dodge a bullet by a hair & still get hit.Little to no story or the lack thereof. How can you even compare this game to Issac when the only store is at the start of the game? At least Issac has lore, open endings, and imagination. I got married during 1 run, you get a partner. That's it. no story, no achievements, no glam.If you want run & gun arcade-like style gameplay this may be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral rating, The game has five characters but honestly none of them are really different. One character has flight and automatically tills soil/Kills weeds, In exchange for worse mobility. Another makes the game twice as fast as it would normally be, And one simply gives you a lot of time. This sounds nice on paper but ultimately runs follow the same formula, Which makes these upgrades relatively meaningless:- Day 1: Pick desert or forest, Clear through it for supplies.- Day 2: Pick other area, Clear though it for supplies.- Day 3: Farm crops.New season: Rinse and repeat with two other areas.The only thing abilities like Flight permit you is the option to explore later areas sooner. But I find you always fall back to this formula, To the point where I'd rather just pick someone without the mobility restriction. All your characters have identical stats and the same starting weapon.You get used to the pacing, But starting off in this game I thought days went by way too quickly. Extending the duration of the day doesn't really fix things either. One character has a passive that extends the duration of day by 50%, But you'll get to a point where it's mid-fall and there's legitimately nothing left to do in the game. I wish instead there was a small buffer period between days/nights which gave you the option to farm crops, Which would give you the option to immediately skip to night. (With abilities increasing day length adding to this buffer period)

_childDocuments_.review: First the cons:The farming is only maybe 2 minutes in each day, you farm tops 10 minutes a year. NEEDS MOAR FARMING!Additional runs get boringBonus places don't unlock until the 4th run and onenemies on additional years get more spongey and there isn't variants with additional yearsrng on amulets/collectibles [whatever they are called] can lead to either a bad or good run, luck of the drawthe last boss is a ♥♥♥♥♥ on how you kill himFor a game thats plot is based around farming you do very little farming, the days are incredibly short and are also the only time you can explore so you have to choose if you want to farm and get money or explore and get power-ups and seeds. When night comes often bosses will teleport you to them NO MATTER WHAT YOU ARE DOING. Same as the morning helicopter, your ass is going whether you like it or not. The game moves to quickly and makes you focus on fighting over farming. If there was more farming this would be a cool game, but currently its 2 minutes farming until its fight time. Not as good as Gungeon or Undermine but its ok. 10 hours to get to halfway point of the game, year 5. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game that seems simple but has plenty to discover and learn. Combat is fast paced with a good mix of weapons that all feel unique and stronger than your starting weapon. Farming is surprisingly complex with a lot to consider if you want the best results. The tutorial does not take long and single day in a play through only lasts a few minutes so even if you try several runs you should have time before the 2 hour refund limit to know whether this game is for you or not.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR ABSOLUTELY Flawless gameplay loop but lacking in weapons and interaction between shooting and farming 7,5/10So, i've been playing this game for a while now, and i absolutely love everything it is doing, the way the gameplay works is just flawless, however, it is severely lacking in variety.I would say the game revolves around 4 main variables, crops, guns, animals and upgrades (yeah there are spouses but for they dont really change gameplay that much).Lets talk about crops first.There are 4 biomes with 4 different types of seeds (depending on the tier), 3 special crops, 4 trees, 3 defensive crops, roses and heart beets.Thats a good amount of crops for the game, while i'd like more, and some variety in how you acquire them, maybe if the deeper you go into a biome, the better your seeds will get, or something, that would make for some interesting strategies, the amount is acceptable.Lets talk animals.There are only 8 animals in the game, 4 of them being direct upgrades, so essentially, there are only 4 animals, and i feel like there are a few missed opportunities here with fun mechanics.Every animal does basically one task, and they only serve as an "automation" of some task you already do, like cutting weeds or watering crops.I feel like there could have been a lot more creativity at play with how they are handled.So lets talk upgrades.there are a bit under 120 upgrades on the game, (counting boss upgrades and normal upgrades), and here is where things get underwhelming for me.If we compare this game to Enter The Gungeon for example, wich is another roguelike with top down view and bullet hell gameplay, minus the farming, there are 271 items in it currently, being 210 on launch, and they only affect combat mechanics.This makes me a bit sad, because there is so much that could be done with items in this game, and variety in that  department would make things even more replayable and enjoyable.And now, lets talk about the worst offender in this list.The Weapons...Oh boy, The weapons...There are currently only 12 weapons in the base game, and 2 weapons on the reap what you crow dlc, amounting to 14 weapons, and this is just sad.if we draw the comparison to enter the gungeon once again, there are 243 weapons in the base game currently, and it may be wishful thinking to hope for this game to have that many weapons, considering guns is enter the gungeon's whole game.But come on man, 14 guns is not enough!!!It feels weird to have so little options in what is essentially one of the 2 key aspects of the game. (shooting and farming), there is so little creativity in it too.Most of the guns are just basic concepts with some farm skin tied to it, like, "sniper, but its a parsnip" Assault rifle but it fires potatoes" "shotgun but different name".none of them interact directly with your crops in any way meaningful way other than MAYBE watering them if you have a mod, and this is extremely disappointing.I really hope this gets addressed in the future, or maybe if there is an atomicrops 2, (wich i really really really really REALLY want, please, id pay anything, i would offer my fistborn as tribute just make it, i'm begging you), they could put more time and effort in making some fun guns and a more interactive weapon system in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever thought to yourself: "Isaac and Gungeon are cool and all, but I also like Stardew Valley and I can't decide which one to play." _childDocuments_.review: Rouge likes such as Enter The Gungeon usually turn out to be an exercise in frustration due to RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ being the primary make/break factor in whether or not the player is victorious.Atomicrops is significantly less of that and places more control in the hands of the player. Sure, drops are still random to a certain degree as is the placement of enemies in the main areas. However all of that is predictable based on what zone of the map you enter. With this semi-consistency players are free to choose when and how certain zones of the game are tackled and in what order they should be.Something super important  that made this game for me was how you could heal and increase your maximum health AT ANY TIME so long as you had the resources! In Gungeon the only garunteed source of health is the chamber rounds earned from performing a no-hit kill on the floor boss, in atomicrops you are GARUNTEED a growable health drop for killing a season end boss that if hoarded and maximized could restore 8 hearts instead of 1 if you maximize your investment of resources, and the extra increased your max HP!After a few teeth-clenching losses at the start I admittedly almost wrote this game off as yet another rougelike to languish in my library, but as soon as I hit the pattern of explore, defend, farm, profit I just kept going! Currently I have unlocked all characters and am on year 7/10(the difficulty) and I am having a ball!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too sure why this game is labeled as a farming sim.... cause it honestly isn't one. Neither of the things I would actually consider this game to be are even listed in the popular tags... shooter and bullet hell (though light bullet hell). The overwhelming majority of the game is shooting things. Not farming.I got it in a Humble Bundle so no skin off my back... but I probably won't pick this up again. I play farming sims to relax and when I redeemed this it was because I thought I was getting a farming sim with a twist... it's post apocalyptic. Very different from most farming sims.Instead I got a game where the days last less than 2 minutes and during the day I have to shoot things to get seeds... followed by night... which is all shooting. Maybe 20 seconds of a day/night cycle is actually spent farming or tending plants. I wouldn't mind if the game was SOME shooting, but it is overwhelmingly majority... shooting.So that's why I just can't click the recommended button because the game calls it's self a farming sim.... the tags call it a farming sim... and it just isn't. It's a top down shooter with a tiny side of farming and if you were looking for a farming sim like I was... you will probably be disappointed.THAT BEING SAID! It is NOT a bad game. It IS a well made game. The sound track is pretty good. The graphics are good. The controls are good. The gameplay is good. The keybindings left a little to be desired but that is an easy fix. The art is pretty good. I'd also say the pacing on difficulty is pretty good as well. The days and nights get harder but it's not rapidly by any means. The tutorial isn't as informative as I would want. The sound effect for digging is annoying on a scale that is only beat by the dripping water sound in Hydroneer, otherwise the sound effects are nice.So if you are looking for a top down shooter where you also do a tiny bit of farming... this is for you! I recommend it in that case.If you are looking for a farming sim though... this is not the game you are looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic realization of a wacky concept. Essentially you manage a post-apocalyptic farm by venturing out to collect materials during the day, then tend to your farm, then at night you fend off waves of rabbits and slugs or a boss, then visit a shop and take a breather. Repeat for 4 seasons.It is very, VERY overwhelming at first because you often have to tend to your crops while blasting enemies simultaneously, but after some playthroughs you get a feel for the unique strategies involved and you sort of segment in your mind what has priority at each moment, eventually entering a sort of zen state within the chaos.The art and animations and sound are just so full of character - it's a very cute game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Highly addictive, rewarding, innovative game. The core gameplay loop is really clever, taking some tropes you know about farming sims and transforming them completely for the twinstick rougelike genre. That does mean that the game is mostly a top-down shooter, and is not really for anyone trying to create a home and life for themselves like in Stardew or Animal Crossing. That being said, if you like fast-paced action and liked those games too, you will probably enjoy the way this game parodies and flips the life sim tropes on their heads.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I played 167 different games in 2022. This is easily in my top 10, and quite possibly in my top 5 favorites I played all year. In fact, I am still enjoying it in 2023.Atomicrops offers progressively more challenging gameplay as you get more experienced with the game mechanics. The learning curve is - dare I say - near perfection. You will be pushed to your absolute limits with multi-tasking as you dive further and further down the bullet hell rabbit hole.The core game loop is tightly packed, there is hardly ever a dull moment in a run. There is just enough randomness to keep each playthrough engaging even after you master the gameplay. The music is delightful, and I find myself humming along as I play. The characters and the farm pixel art are adorable. I find myself just wandering the "menu" after runs, admiring all the cute little Easter eggs and attention to detail. The DLC mixes the game up in interesting ways, and they have even recently launched "classic mode" to restore your ability to play with the older mechanics. The collectible system is charming and brings the world alive. Finished runs end with the oh-so-satisfying surplus mode and scratch that special itch. The amount of polish this title has is astounding.At full price, this game is well worth the money. On sale, you would be foolish not to pick this up. Honestly, just buy this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The way I'd describe it is 'stressful in the good way'.It's an aesthetically charming time management game, think Stardew Valley, but with a focus entirely on combat.The sense of power you get as you progress through a run is addicting, the game does a good job of pacing itself by drip feeding you upgrades.You're constantly doing something at any given point in a run, which makes it appealing if you've got the attention span of a 2 year old.Only complaint is that at times, the screen can get a bit busy, which is really bad for a bullet hell. Especially when there's lots of lobbed projectiles on screen, which are visible, but can't actually damage you until they land.
