_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game a while ago, but only yesterday as of writing this decided to play it. I'm a huge fan of Nuclear Throne, so this game appeals to me in the same way, with it's pleasing designs and it's interesting post-apocalyptic environments, and of course the brutal roguelike gameplay. It's addicting, it's fun, the world feels lively and enjoyable to explore, and I love discovering everything about this game. No run feels like a waste, even when you die, as you're constantly progressing through the cornucopias, character unlocks, etc. If you're a fan of roguelikes, definitely pick this game up. It's full of surprises and keeps you hooked pretty damn easily. I just hope it continues to receive updates and DLC as it has been, because I'd hate to see an underrated gem like this fade out.EDIT: Having played an additional ~10 hours of this game, I feel like I need to update this review to include my newer sentiments on it. While I agree with everything I said above, I am also beginning to see this game's one major flaw, that being it's lack of unlocks. Contrary to other roguelikes, like for example The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, there are simply not enough unlocks to make it feel like it's worth going through the gameplay loop repeatedly, and not enough variation to have it feel interesting every time. Isaac does this better by giving each character their own unlocks, which gives not only motivation to keep playing runs, but also gives an incentive to play the other characters. Currently, there's no real reason to play any of the more challenging characters in this game, so I feel like this approach could help. Permanent cosmetic like skins for players and crops, or permanent gameplay changes like unlockable guns/pigeons/upgrades, would generally make the game feel more rewarding to play.I would still recommend this game, as I feel as though it's pretty early into it's development cycle, but I do hope for more content in future, that just makes the game feel more rewarding.Edit: I am very pleased to say this game is NOT dead! New updates and DLC have been coming out since I last played, and the game is more fun than ever. I still definitely recommend this game and its DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I might be in the minority here but I wanted to share my thoughts because I feel quite strongly that the game was balanced much better before the most recent update. It got straight to the point, no tediousness or artificial scarcity. Now there's an unavoidable window that takes up  your screen after you purchase a gun, and blank slots in the harvest winnings. I'm not sure why they opted to remove items from the main reward pool and place them on the guns instead, when the overall goal is to have a good harvest.  Purchasable gun stack-upgrades have been taken out and replaced with random mods. Before it had a great amount of RNG without being excessive, but with the mod system they just took more control out of the players hands. Plus it was a hit of bliss when you could afford to spam-buy all the upgrades in one go. I just find the overall anticipation once you've completed a day to be lessened because of these changes. It's just such an odd attempt to balance the game. The guns are now much more expensive due to the potential mods, but once you start affording them the bosses are now so much easier to kill, the battles taking mere seconds, it doesn't feel earned somehow. It's silly because so much obvious effort and care was put into designing the characteristics and different behaviours of these bosses, but now they're spending less time on my screen due to the weapon changes. I know it sounds like I'm saying "I'm mad that I can buy a powerful gun that gets the job done" but what I'm actually trying to say is, bosses should stay relatively challenging,. If you're going to breeze through it, it should be partly hard-earned through skill since the creators went out of their way to design each boss uniquely for you to need a different strategy to defeat it. I know a chunk of the player base was complaining about the gun-breaking system, I had found it frustrating as well. But overtime I had actually grown to love it- . It's a nuclear wasteland. These are supposed to be guns that were slapped together in a shed with some scrap and rotting vegetables, crafted by some grimy alky donned with an eyepatch and pitchfork for an arm;  It's just unfortunate that for the sake of a game's success and longevity, developers often need to cater to a type of player that wants games to all follow some homogeneous outline of what it  look like and how it function. Some people genuinely enjoy the challenge of being thrown into the deep-end, having to adapt and push through frustration, but then the game is pushed to be more inclusive to casual players and it loses some of the things that made it so unique and charming to begin with. Atomicrops is still a solid game. It just feels like a significant amount of the life has been stripped away in favour of appealing to a wider audience, and I can't help but feel a little heartbroken.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: They've made guns persist, the crow is a streamlined and interesting way to play, they added Surplus mode at the end of a successful run to make the grind feel less demoralising, and there is a lot to pursue if you like the main game loop. Overall, these devs deserve to be recognized. Just be aware that this is not a chill farming game or a precise bullet shooter (screen clutter can still be very overwhelming)EDIT: I have many more hours than this on the Switch version.I want to like this game so badly. It's just so hard. No really. If you like tight bullet hell shooters, you'll feel disappointed over the lack of real progression (your guns break, dying resets everything all over, and hitboxes are a little wider than you'd think)If you like farming, you'll have no time whatsoever to lay out your crops nicely or get a good rhythm going. For reasons beyond me the developers made it so that if you elect to spend the 'day' component farming you will still be attacked by enemies. Even then, you are so constrained for farming land that you're pushed back into combat anyways. I'd love to learn the game better and get better but man it's so hard and that difficulty really makes it less fun, so I just...don't want to at the end of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was a labour of love, but it really just... doesn't feel meshed at all. The bullet hell and the farming sim are largely unrelated. It's honestly quite confusing. It doesn't feel like one game with multiple elements, but two games that are largely separate, but where if you do well at one, you get bonuses in the other, but not vice versa. If it's a bullet hell, why am I trying to farm to gain experience? Shouldn't the experience gain be related to the core gameplay mechanic? If it's a farming sim, why can't I reliably get crops going, I have to constantly leave my farm to get seeds.It just feels really confused. I'm going to give it another couple hours. I'll try. Art is beautiful though.EDIT 1.5 more hours: I have played more of it, and while there is certainly something to enjoy there, I still can't recommend it to others. I stream, and I basically only play games on stream, and I just can't see this being something I play more of. Unfortunate, but I hope they designers push on and make more, because there's definitely good stuff in here, it's just buried beneath an unfortunate A vs. B gameplay mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: Until few days ago, I would have recommended this game to anyone asking.After all, I was streaming it every week end for most of the last year, and I played it even more than that beforehand. It was a good mix of if Binding of Isaac and Stardew Valley had a baby, which is pretty crazy when you think about it, with a roguelite progression that overall wasn't too grindy. Oh it had flaws, for sure, the layering is terrible and you will get hit by bullets and enemies hiding under others elements and the weapons and characters are so unbalanced it's almost criminal. But despite that, the game remained fun to play, and there was hope those issues would eventually maybe be addressed. And then all hell broke loose...Cue the Deervil DLC, coming up with an update patch which hide in its first line a terrible truth that you will only figure out when you start playing again. The core loop of the game, the main planting system, was completely remade into some of the most asinine, bland and dumbed down system possible for such a game. Every grain of personality and decision making that made the game good and pleasant to play is gone. Everything is now standardised with the better crops types locked behind a level progression system which needs you to plant and harvest lower tier seeds to unlock the better ones. There is no longer variation in how much water/fertiliser/growth time a seed has. There are only tiers, and leveling to upgrade to better tiers. It's like they took the worst DLC character that everyone hated because of how unfun he's to play, and copy pasted it to the whole game.Why would they change what worked and leave what didn't? Don't ask me, I don't know. Probably yet an other developer stuck in "vision mode" persuaded they have this great plan and idea for the game as a whole and failing to consult the player base to ask them what they really want or need. Vision will never make a game good, you need to keep your feet solidly on the ground to be able to look objectively as what could be better. This my friend, is how you alienate the people who supported your work and spreaded word about it, be it with mouth to ear, or broadcasting.So stay away from this game, at least until the changes are reverted, or until a new change arrives and completely remove this stupid system.EDIT: After the developer most recent addition, out of honesty I'm putting that review on hold the time for me to check the changes are effective, which make take a while as I have others things lined up at the moment. I want to also mention that this will not change the fact of what happened, that will remain forever. But I appreciate a step in the right direction, even it it took around HALF A YEAR to come, especially as it's something I initially suggested in the forums.

_childDocuments_.review: Bro, what are some of the other reviews on about? 'The days are too short!' My guy you last a quarter of an in-game day so you really shouldn't say things like that. Besides, there are plenty of way to extend the day, my personal favorite being the heart beat related time extender with heart beat keikis from Deervil giving me like 10 minutes and letting me finish exploring before the end of fall. Game isn't that hard, beat Robusta year 10 (which is the hardest difficulty I'm pretty sure) with like 45 hours. One thing of note is that the seed beds don't replant infinitely. If they have to repeatedly replant within a short window of time, they slow down and only plant one at a time, preventing ultra-high scores with certain nitro or megaton tractor builds. I'm wondering if this is an issue with the upgrade that makes the seed beds create their own seeds, working like the propogator upgrade that slowly generates seeds, and if I could possible build it to work without the free seeds. Anyways, if you can multitask or know what you're doing and can handle light bullet hells, it's definitely a fun roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: For once, a rouge like game that doesn't annoy me with constant death. I got this game a couple days ago, and that same day, I stayed awake until 5 AM playing it. That's how much fun I was having trying to figure out the game. It goes by quick, and personally I like that. It makes it feel like when you die, you don't truly lose anything. There are a couple personal nitpicks I have though, like how to upgrade yourself permanently you need to find specific characters, then you can upgrade after you die. Which is cool, however I do wish the RNG on them was a bit more they show in one specific spot on one of the maps, and that they'll spawn there every day until found (unless you die, then they move to the other map). As I've only found one, and I cannot find the others no matter where I look and how many times the game resets. So it makes permanently upgrading kind of annoying. Another I have is sort of with the weapons and how you have to upgrade the weapon every single time you pick it up, which I find a bit annoying. Kinda wish you had an ability that you pick only one of the guns to keep upgrades on permanently, but you move slower holding it. Just like a little thing to help save a little bit of money while not making it too difficult. The last one I have is with the marriage part of the game. I don't know if it's just RNG, but I have yet to even become friends with any of the merchants because the lack of roses I get. But like I said, it's possible it's just RNG kicking my butt.Overall, I always have fun with this game. _childDocuments_.review: Awesome "Stardew Valley meets Twinstick shooter".So, what you can see from the trailer - Planting and harvesting crops Harvest-Moon/Star-Dew Valley style while gunning down enemies - is pretty accurate. However, there's more to it than initially meets the eye. Every day is only a few minutes long, at daylight, your crops are safe, during night they get attacked. So you plant them at day and defend at night? Well... first you need to get the seeds! So now you need to factor in exploring. However, exploring is better with better guns. Which you can buy, but they only last for a day...So, this game is descision making, descision making, descision making. When do you do what? Upgrades always let you choose mutually exclusive options. And you need to make decide quick most of the time. Bring to that that over the time, your farm gets more and more chaotic and you're incentivised to keep it orderly.This is not a relaxing shooter, it's stressful, but oh so enjoyable. And when you get hit, don't worry you will find heart seeds occasionally, like one every day or two. Wait! Seeds? Well yeah, of course you need to plant it, grow it, nurture it, defend it to get a heart back, what did you expect? A forgiving rogue-lite?There's some between-game progression, but it's like feeding teardrops to dehydrated people.Us rogue-lite players must seem to many of the audience like some masochistic kinky gamer bunch anyway. And this game  demonstrates that perfectly. I totally recommend you join us!

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty weird hybrid of farming sim and bullet hell, but one that, while leaning heavily in the direction of bullet hell, manages to maintain that addictive loop of making sure you keep your crops healthy and your garden growing. The exploration aspect of searching for resources during the day and defending your crops at night ties the cycle together, making the plan for each day clear and concise but also hectic as hell, as you try to clear mobs, watch the clock, decide on what to search for, and oh, yeah, not get shot and die. _childDocuments_.review: I have to say I am completely amazed by this game and this will be a very long review. For years the game sphere has shifted from games without meta progression to ones where the lack of such a system meant that the game was lacking crucial element. Such games reward very frequent play with rewards that add up to much more when compared to players that play less often. I am one such player, there aren't many games that can keep me playing for long and I often switch games. Atomicrops was the creme of the crop (pun intended) for me. Finally I found a one shot wonder that sratches every gaming itch for me. Be it the active combat that is not that overwhelming (this might be controversial), it has mechanics that aid gameplay and you don't have the constant pressure that you must make erything of each run or your time is wasted, unlike rougelikes with meta progression. In Atomicrops you can jump in play for a day and call it quits, save the run for another time and jump right into the action, you don't need to remember what you did that last time, you can just look at your stats the lineup of seeds that you have and in a moment can assertain the state of your farm when day breaks. I have to say I still haven't defeated the first year and I have the Reap what you crow DLC. I would like to say that having bought the Crow DLC it is much easier to pick up the game because (I share the Crow mechanics) . Now I would like to look more in-depth into the game mechanic-wise. Firstly combat, I have to say that I feel the comabt is very smooth, as a whole you have an immediate intuitive feeling for how a gun would play by just looking at its model the shooting is smooth and to me the gun effects are not obtrusive, they even complement the gun and its bullets really nicely. Now the enemies are diverse but not I a way that all are completely different. I find that the zones are very well segmented and you can tell visually how enemies become sronger, every zone has its own challenges and they feel very different.Secondly farming, I am very happy with the way it plays out, you have a quick and easy step by step process to growing your farm (again I will explain and use the spoiler box) . The crops are diverse and you can easily tell them apart which improves readability considerably. They are not too much so that you get mucked up in they diversity. You can also boost your farm with friends that you pick up in the wilderness. I also love the setting that allows you to both shoot and manage the farm at the same time, this takes a lot of the pressure off of you.Lastly the bosses, I like that they are clearly spaced out and you can feel the difference in complexity and difficulty, I have not fought agains all bosses but I am happy with how they work.Now from a graphical stand point, the models are really cute in all aspects, I like how the enemies look and the way the game has a slightly goofy side, it adds a lot of charm. The colours are vibrant and I like how the models for enemies and the player juxtapose with the background meaning the crops and soil. The bosses pop out the most which help you a lot. The bullets do not get lost in the heat of battle as even though the game has some flashy effect you don't get distracted. Now lastly I would like to talk about the music and sound effects. The music took me a moment to get used to but know I have it constantly running in the back of my mind, it is catchy and captures the atmosphere of hectic movements that at the same time have the rythm of a bee that flutters in the wind trying to share to its compatriots the location of the sweetest nectar while at the same time raindrops try to swat her from the air and you have rolling thunder in the distance signalling they impending doom of the increasing difficulty of each incoming day. I love how the small crops cheer and jump when they have matured enough to be gathered. The gun sound effect are subtle and they give you the feeling of power when you shoot, the feedback is rapid.All in all I am very pleased with how the game turned out and I especially recommend this game to people that like an action packed game that does not give an unfair advantage to players that constantly play given the lack of meta progression and it is completely different each run. I adore the music and sound design even with its added goofiness. With the new DLC it makes it easier for new players to become acommodated to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a great rogue-like that mixes many different genres. At its core, the game is an entertaining top-down shooter that pits you against hordes of enemies rushing for you and shooting their own bullets, turning the game into something of a bullet hell. Combined with this is the need to find the tools to expand your farm, earning you precious income for important upgrades to survive the increasing difficulty. Completing one game unlocks harder difficulties and new characters that have their own gimmicks, turning your next playthrough into something new and exciting. There are added collection and achievement systems that add extra incentives to play on harder difficulties. However, the game does become repetitive as the core map doesn’t have a huge amount of variety. For example, the map layout is more or less the same with the same enemies in their specific areas. But don’t let this deter you from trying Atomicrops. If you’re into rogue-like games, you’ll most likely enjoy this game. But those looking for a more casual and relaxing experience might want to look elsewhere as Atomicrops always keeps you on your toes.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkably good roguelike shooty game with a little bit of farming mixed in. That should be pointed out - combat is the focus, and while you will plant a lot of crops, it's not at all like say, Stardew Valley. That said, it is a lot of fun, although it takes a little bit of getting used to the gameplay loop. The art style is certainly a thing, and it should say something that while I do not enjoy that particular kind of art style, I still keep playing because the game is just that much fun. My only small complaint would be that it's not obvious at first how do you acquire upgrades that carry from playthrough to playthrough, you have to find characters out in the biomes, but it doesn't substract that much from the fun. Definitely reccomend this for anyone who is into roguelikes.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots going on at all times. Hectic style of play. Like a farming sim, mixed with a bullet hell. Explore, grow crops for cash, turn in cash for upgrades. Lots of mechanics to learn, master and enjoy. Day and night, relationships, killing, farming, rogue like elements, upgrades, wacky power-ups and weapons. Yah, good fun. Sink some time into this one for sure, addictive exploration. Graphics are pixel like, but cutesy? Reminds me of old SNES RPG game graphics. Sound and music decent. Fun and playable mash-up of styles. Controller works, probably better on mouse/keyboard? Subjective. Give this a some love.

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique roguelike where you farm by night and battle for your seeds by day. The gameplay alternates between base defence and dungeon crawler, and you have to manage them both, usually both at the same time. A unique roguelike twist that it pulls off well, maintaing classic elements like massive bossfights, powerful weapons, 3 or 4 item combos that turn you into a living god of death, and of course, that REPLAY VALUE. The OST and characters add a lot to the game, and when you master this game you will feel like a living legend in a way that other roguelikes cannot. If I had to make one complaint, the game is rather hard to start with, but you pick it up fast, and the update where you auto-shoot while farming helped a LOOOOOT.Hard game, but addicting. Very fun. 9.5/10. Needs a "Year 2" mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.  The art style, the music, the game-play, it's adorable, but in the way that the show  is adorable.  There's some ever-so-slightly darker / mature undertones that make it enjoyable for everyone regardless of your age, but on the surface it's just such a cute little game.  The soundtrack specifically reminds me of a lighthearted version of  mixed with some of the  soundtrack.  I don't think I could think of a more fitting OST than this, it's very clever and well-made. It's not like your typical roguelite where RNG is the ultimate controlling factor over your play-style.  You have a ton of control over each run and you won't ever be shafted by RNG in my experience so far.  Upgrades are nicely balanced and all have a place in the game, and it feels like you have control over what upgrades / build path that you choose.  Not only is it fair, but there's a lot of skill-expression too.  From mastering tending to your crops while being attacked to managing your time perfectly to optimize the amount of upgrades you get in the day, there's a lot that  the player can do to impact the outcome. Regardless of how you play, it's a bullet-hell.  As long as you can dodge everything , then you can scrape by 100% of the time, albeit not as exciting as if you were to play properly.  Progressing through the rounds is dictated by just lasting until nighttime is over, so you technically don't have to kill a single thing except for the final boss.  However, if you manage your time well, you can breeze through the early difficulties all while feeling heavily gratified for playing efficiently.  The higher your score, the more currency you earn to purchase permanent upgrades outside of a run so there's a heavy incentive on playing the best you possibly can.This game is a rogue, not , which typically means that there's going to be some sense of permanent progression between your runs, and boy does this game have a lot of it.  You can unlock characters, several different categories of permanent positive modifiers to your runs, and even new characters to ROMANCE in the town to gain items or seeds that affect your game-play.  The replayability factor from what I can tell right off the bat is similar to that of  or .  You generally know what you're going to be up against, but with enough random events, upgrades, and permanent progression to keep you coming back and enjoying it just the same as your first run but better, since you actually know what you're doing.  There's also benefits for achievement hunters if that's your thing.  Unlocking enough achievements will give you permanent slight increases to your stats and these bonuses appear in your in-game home area in the shape of vegetable / fruit-shaped hedges which is such a cool idea.There's a little bit of something for everyone even if you're not a roguelite fanatic.  There's 10 whole difficulties for you to mess around with depending on if you're a casual player or a hardcore player, there's loads of rewarding progression that comes in many forms to keep you coming back for hours and hours, there's the ability to romance an interesting cast of characters, and for only $15 , .  It's very well polished and I'm looking forward into dumping so much more of my time into it.  The only thing that would make this game perfect in my opinion is if there was multiplayer.

I often have this listed as my favorite steam game for a reason, thoughtful design, and an endlessly fun gameplay loop.  10000% worth getting

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game during the holiday sale and to be honest, expected very little from it. I had bought and returned three other games that same day because the gameplay was uninteresting or the game was just too buggy or, well, hideous. Then I boot up Atomicrops and am greeted by the beautifully-animated opening cut scene. This game is great. At this point, I have only managed to claw my way to Day 2, but I plan on seeing how far I can go and what secrets Atomicrops has to unlock. The music is shockingly great. Seriously, the tundra theme? It absolutely slaps. EVERY song is good to fantastic. The pixel art is adorable, expressive and funny. The derpy faces the slugs make after you knock them around a bit gets me every time. The sound design is tight and hard-hitting, especially for the different types of gunfire, and while there is eventually a LOT of visual noise on screen, Atomicrops does a good job of distinguishing different bullet types so that you know if it's something thrown out by an ally or an enemy. It can be a little much once there are more enemies on screen, but it's kind of a hazard of tower defense gameplay when things get tougher. As stated, I bought this game yesterday on sale. Was it worth it? Well, I have over 15 hours on record. I had the day off due to bad weather, and I couldn't put this game down. The simulation aspects are extremely hollow, so I wouldn't recommend engaging with it based on that alone, but beyond that? It has more than I could have ever asked for, especially for such a low price tag. It also helped me realize that I REALLY enjoy tower defense gameplay, and will be probing the genre for more gems like this in the future.Do yourself a favor and pick this up! You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst games I've played in a while. Why does it have positive reviews? Who knows. I learned never to trust steam user reviews a long time ago so I got this for like $1.75 outside of steam just to try it. The best way that I can describe it is that it was a potentially great game that's a roguelike and should be a roguelite. If there was ever a game that needed some kind of progression system, this is it. Having literally less than a minute per round to actually go outside of your base and have fun with the shooting part is very depressing because the parts at your base are just boring crop maintenance. You will never have time between days to do enough between everything you are required to do: till, plant, water, harvest, explore, fight, defend, all in a two minute window each day. To say that you feel constantly rushed is an understatement and it just isn't fun whatsoever. You can't spend long out having fun because in under 2 minutes night falls and you have to defend your crops. When you are done a helicopter comes and forces you to go back to town and start a new 2 minute day. F-cking great. Items in town are comically expensive to the point that there was no reason to even have a part where you come back to town because even after two hours on one save slot I still can't afford any of the weapons in town, especially when after those 2 hours I have under 200 seeds and a gun costs 3200.... The game has zero freedom of choice, like some of those terrible linear tower defense games. Either play how they want you to play or fail quickly, and nothing is ever explained to maybe possibly help the player understand how the developers wanted them to exactly and perfectly play their game according to how they specifically and perplexingly designed it.The only other game I can think of that was so heavily destroyed by being roguelike (no progression) instead of roguelite (some progression) is Genesis Alpha One.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's not for everyone, but you should definitely give it a chance. The audio and visuals might put you off, but the gameplay was quite entertaining.Comparable to, I couldn't say much. I haven't played any games exactly like it, so it feels a unique. Yes there's the bullet hell genre going for it, but there's also farming and time management. I really liked that I had to choose between making more money with farming to get better guns, or finding upgrades in the outer world.My favorite gun was the leech, and I loved playing with the DLC character Oregacrow. Oregacrow was difficult to win with though, so most of my wins are with the dandelion.Controller is definitely do-able, although crop placement can get annoying if you're trying to build large crops.Audio is obnoxious, can be hard to get past, but it grew on me.Visuals, not a game i'd normally go for, but once again grew on me. It's a fun concept, don't give up based solely on the graphics.Difficulty, not too much if you find the right build. I like playing different characters though, so it took me a while to beat it. I'd say I'm an average gamer, so it's definitely possible to win with some effort. As for seasoned players, there are plenty of challenges, and even personal ones you can give yourself.Base upgrades, barely noticeable, but a nice addition. They don't make or break the game, and if you're the collector type, you'll like this.

The DLC "Reap what you Crow" is an odd change from the "base game" however, with the way it functions most of the content is located on the DLC character so by not choosing the character you can still interact with a lot of the new content but not the odd restriction or different game type. This game, for the price, is an EASY 10/10 and that's not a score I give out lightly. Definitely worth a play and multiple completions. I really hope we get more content out of Bird Bath Games in the future and hopefully a sequel or more DLC's.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing through each year getting harder and harder while I was slowly getting better at the game, then going back to an earlier year with the daily run and finding it so much easier than the first time. Now that I've played through all the years I hop on most days just to do the daily run, slowly getting all the cats and statues, I would definitely recommend this game and I hope they continue to update it and bring us more DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, Brotato meets Stardew, flying pigs with turrets - One of the best games I have ever found at giving value worth your time. Each run is maximum 1.5 hours, but each run takes so much focus, and injects so much dopamine, that you feel you've spent the whole day powering up and making bank. I picked this game up on $10 sale and was blown away. It ticks all my boxes: farming and econ management, upgrades and relics, meta-upgrades, deep "skill-trees" (haha), the perfect mix of frustration and earned progress, precise and responsive controls and combat, cohesively wacky and lovingly detailed graphics, wonderfully vivid soundtrack, and replayability. Many reviewers seem surprised about the WASD pseudo-bullet hell, but combat is still very straightforward and a clip easier than truly "difficult" action games like Crypt of the NecroDancer. I really enjoyed that combat wasn't just "melee hit and run with crappy ranged attacks" that a lot of 2D farming sims are addicted to: in Atomicrops you farm to buy guns to bulldozer enemies to farm more crops to buy more guns. It's tied intimately to the farming system, and it's glorious. One note: the meta-progression does take a while (about 5 hours) to discover, but the game makes up well for it before then.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the updates for about 2 years and have nothing but praise for the devs.It's not perfect (what is), but it's constantly moving uphill, every update's a banger adding so much content and creativity to the table, I've never been so impressed by both the quality and consistency. Not afraid to do overhauls when it's needed, all of the major DLC's were free (apart from one) and the last boss added was done so well...I just can't wait for what's to come next
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda in a bucket here. The game has really fun moments, but also has really down sides.    Overall, it's a cool indie roguelite, but i don't think it's my type. I would recommend for y'all to take this when it's cheaper, 'cuz i don't think it's worth the full cost.It has some parts where you need to learn without any directions of "what to do" or "where to go" or "what's the point" or "what's the objective".... but again, it also has impactfull moments of frenzy fire and chaos. Hope y'all enjoy it more than i did. 5/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Humorous and challenging, the developers definitely found the fun in this otherwise strange dichotomy of gameplay systems. This game rewards you for quick thinking, quick reflexes, time investment, and strategy. There is plenty of content to keep you busy, with a healthy variety of enemies, weapons, plants, and unlockables. Despite requiring you to juggle multiple resources and gameplay systems, the game manages to pace itself and not feel too overwhelming. Nothing so far feels unnecessary or out of place.As someone who's really into real-time resource management and challenging PvE games, this feels right up my alley and I'm excited to continue discovering what this game has to offer and see how far I can go.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic roguelike with a unique enough twist. A few things that should be mentioned right off the bat is the lack of nuance between zones and enemies, bosses become repetitive and easy much more quickly than games like isaac (especially the final boss), and the farming system is not very fleshed out (it feels a little bit tacked on but it is still fun). Those three negatives are fairly minor in my opinion. The variety in guns and mods make up for the games short comings. I feel that I could get many more hours out of it. P.S. the Crow is probably the most interesting character but he probably simplifies the game a little too much
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I got this in the Humble Choice, but I had it on my Wishlist for... a long time. At first I couldn't remember why I was interested in this game. I told myself I would play a single run and then move on. The tutorial was fine. The first run was pretty neutral. Then the next morning I woke up and thought... "I could do better than that. One more time."So here I am 4 hours later, and telling myself to *MOVE ON TO ANOTHER GAME FOR A WHILE*.Yeah, I recommend it.Update: There's a few things I wish this game did differently. I wish it had a sandbox mode. I wish I could keep my farm past one year. Honestly I'm kinda sad I have to start over each year. However, I guess for people that enjoy doing quick runs this is a good format.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a solid 8 hours my first sitting. This game is INCREDIBLY fast paced, which is deceptive because it seems like a farm simulator at first. It's basically an arcade game roguelike which uses farming, exploration and combat as the progression mechanisms. All your choices have huge consequences and there's so much replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most original and fun bullet hell roguelikes out there. I absolutely adore this game, and the devs have done an amazing job! :) The game itself is presented in such a fun and vibrant pixel style, and the gameplay is so hectic and crazy in a way that really leans into the wacky setting. Cannot overstate how much i love this gem. The devs have even released 3 major content updates for absolutely free post-release, the game was amazing from day 1 of early access, but it has come so far and the updates have been an absolute blast!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Y'all really should put 'permadeath' in the title, I know it says roguelike but that is not what I would've expected. (I would've thought you could die during your adventures but would keep your farm)That being said, wow it works great! I was initially mad that I couldn't build up a giant farm and go back to it later but the thing is, I can always do that in Stardew. This is more of a challenge, being very careful and strategic to make the biggest farm. Love it. Lots of fun. And as a pixel artist myself I really enjoy the graphics, possibly the lowest resolution I have seen display this kind of personality.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's essentially Binding of isaac + Stardew valley/Harvest moon.An initially complex-seeming set of mechanics and relentlessly short timers, hides a suprisingly replayable challenge and long persistent progression system10/10, would reccomend to anyone who wants a challenging way to burn the hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: The game balance and difficulty feels like it is missing something. The biggest and most obvious flaw with the game would be the hit boxes. They feel too large and ill-defined. I think my other big issue is the difficulty doesn't feel progressive. If I'm progressing through a game like enter the gungeon I feel like I know roughly where I am going to die in a run and try to get past that point each run. In Atomicrops it feels quite random. I can be doing fine on a run until one night were a large amount of enemies spawn and I'm not even able to deal enough damage to kill all of them.Another smaller negative is probably half of the guns don't feel that fun to me. This is probably more of a personal thing so your mileage may vary. I wanted to like this game but overall found it a bit lacking. I like the theme, I like the core gameplay loop but overall there are enough downsides to the game I might have gotten my fill after beating year one.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I do not write reviews for video games, but this one is quite special. I have replayed this game a dozen times, and each time I revisit the cold depths of Atomicrops's oceans, I feel a sense of revamped adventure that I can't describe, and no other game can pull out of me. Experience this game in its entirety, every nook a cranny has something beautiful within it.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Bullet hell rogue like with farming elements. It's pretty fun but definitely one of the more gruelling ascension mode grind outs with a faster difficulty ramp up. Overall it leads to some pretty good memes, stick with it and you'll get a nice kitty collection.//Year 10 gets pretty stale, advice is to farm the highest difficulty you can manage. Regular content updates and patches for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Rather good game.It has the late game roguelite/roguelike issue that doing well usually means you need to get lucky with the drops in the first stage to secure the win. Else you end up in scenarios where you need to be AI trained robot levels of good to pull of the win. That said, unlocking the late game stuff is a fun ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical going into Atomicrops based on the concept, but it's actually become one of my favorite Roguelikes. The devs nailed the gameplay loop between the combat and crop planting, and there's plenty to explore mechanically for folks that like a challenge. You're never really overwhelmed with what to do, and the free DLC adds lots of late game content to give the game more play as you continue. The only thing I wish is that there was a little more variety to the different landscapes, but overall it's a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Flamboyantly Psychedelic, Easy to understand but difficult to master. A masterpiece in it's own lane.Pros:-Roguelite elements aren't ride or die. In fact you can 'win' your first try.-Amazing art.-High Skill Ceiling. If you're willing to grind for it the ultra difficult content is there (Year 10 Robusta, Cat Shrines similar to a heat system, about 10 frustrating achievements in the lot).-Great damage scaling. Not too broken unless it's on bosses or with DLC Scythe. Check *Con-Classic and regular mode.Daily runs are fun and rewarding.-If you're an RNG runner and you live off that high this is a great game. Luck matters. 80% of the items have impact on decision making. Camp spawns and routing feel comprehendable after a few runs.-Waterchris <3Cons:-This game even on year 1 can be overwhelming to new players.-Layering can be frustrating. Sometimes bullets or enemies can hide behind helicopter or other elements.-No story.*-DLC introduced some broken elements. I played 40+ hours without the DLC and I promise you it's better to play without it till you find yourself craving something new. If I had the +++Scythe in my first 10 hours of the game I wouldn't have played much longer.Observations:-There are lots of Gungeon elements and seldom few elements of Stardew. Don't go into this reclined.-There are a lot of small consequences to missteps that might steer away more casual gamers.-Learning curve is pretty tough. Just roll with the punches especially when you dug your own grave.-Very few weapons. Not a bad thing. Just an expectation setter.Overall:8/10. Unique, frustrating, atomic.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Its weird, Its fun but its so much. Not only do you need to simultaneously manage your farm and raid different areas the runs are long and you need to manage a lot of resources. They also released a dlc which changed many core elements of the game which might be better but I cant get used to them. It is not something i can play for a long time but its worth to check out.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: It takes some time to learn, but its an amazing game. It's a mix of stardew valley and enter the gungeon where you'll be doing an insane amount of multitasking (dodging, shooting and farming). The soundtrack is very hit or miss, with some songs that seem composed by a 4 year old and some you'll be humming even after the game ends. Game could use some polish in a few areas and at times you can't even see the enemy that hit you. Other than that, it's a must-play for any rogue-like enthusiast. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of things I like in it. I hate it.It's a game that divides your attention. You need to cultivate crops by tilling, planting, fertilizing, watering and harvesting crops. You can get seeds by fighting monsters in nearby areas. At night you must protect your crops from invading monsters.There's tons of pickups to help you on your way. Often you need to pick between two options. There's never any pause to let you read what your options are. There's never any opportunity to plan out how best to plant your crops. There's never any chance to work out why what you're attempting is working so poorly.The game explains itself very poorly, and I suspect if there was a good explanation, it wouldn't help that much. The very basics of the game are easy to grasp, but in order to do well you'd need to optimise your approach and maximise earnings each day. There's some aspect of intelligence lacking from this game's design. I suspect that this imagined aspect could elevate it into something excellent. But the way this game is just a relentless onslaught of unpleasant challenges seems intentional. I feel like the things that made me hate this game were probably intentional.One aspect that may explain why I disliked my time with this game as much as I did concerns buyable weapons. Your default weapon is pretty bad. You can buy better weapons in between days. I almost never had enough currency to buy a weapon. You can just save your currency, but that means you won't spend it on things that'd help you earn more currency. And the following day, different weapons will be offered, which cost many times more than what you were trying to save up for. I feel like I was missing some aspect of how progression was meant to work. I can't tell if it's just ineptitude of design, or trying to cater to an audience that isn't me.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adore this game. First played it on Xbox game pass and fell in love with it there. Loved it so much I had to get it for desktop. I've sunk way more hours into then I thought I would but it gets you into its clutches and holds on.The game play is similar to a lot of different upgrade/shoot em ups out there with the difference of the farming for money and the entire feel. Things don't pause to upgrade, things don't just give you an upgrade and a level up. You have to fight and avoid and survive to gain those. It definitely makes you work, but for fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that keeps you thinking with each new Year (level).When you start, you'll spend the first couple of Years discovering the mechanics, the areas you can explore, how the currencies work, the different guns, etc.The first few Years, you might run through every square foot of every battle area, as you meticulously wipe out every foe and gather every resource. You'll quickly realize that this strategy carried you through the first few years, but you're going to need to make some serious decisions on what to focus on and what to avoid. This keeps you active in all the different mechanics, and you can't "decide" to play one way and stick with it - the randomness and variety keep it fresh every run.One run you might find yourself overloaded with seeds right away... so you learn to skip fighting enemies where the rewards are seeds. Or you may get a tractor that cuts weeds for you, so you build AWAY from that and you avoid anything that helps you boost your weed cutting, while you focus on powering up in other ways. But of course the next run this might change... you might find scrolls that till, water and fertilize crops FOR you... so now you can stay out fighting more and spend less time tending your crop.There's a lot of good mechanics hiding right under the surface, and they're all discoverable. You'll not need to refer to a Wiki unless you want to.I made it through Year 10 which is the "end" of the game unless you want to chase achievements. Steam is showing about 70 hours of play time - I got Year 10 done in about 55 hours of play with about 15 hours of the game idling.My one criticism is that as you get to Year 8, 9, 10 you will start to see that a bad start can subvert your entire run. You have to run off in a compass direction right at the start to begin gathering resources, but RNG can be cruel. There are many conditions and patterns of RNG drops that make it such that you can't get enough money to buy a gun upgrade after Day 1 or 2. For example you may get an abundance of seeds and fertilizer, but nowhere is a water upgrade found... So you get to the end of the first couple days and you didn't manage to cultivate and harvest enough to buy a gun upgrade. And if you can't get a good gun in these later Years you can kiss your run goodbye. I'm not sure how this could be improved, because the RNG is stable and really fair for the most part.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: A great game despite having to learn the mechanics on the goWhen  i first started Atomicrops i was overwhelmed pretty fast, despite beating year 1 on my second try (i did get very lucky tho). The tutorial does tell you about the basic game cycle and how to tend your crops, however it did leave out tractors and how valuable they are, how to create megacrops and that fight stat is more important then having a fancy gun. Also i only learned about ants by discovering the builder ant later and for the main upgrade mechanic the game should at least give you clues where to find them without having to look it up since alien and sage ant are absolute gamechangers.This is propably why so many players dropped the game without having even beaten year one wich is disappointing since with the upgrades and knowledge it is a very enjoyable game with a addicting gameplay loop. If you liked Enter the Gungeon but thought the bullet hell aspect got too tough on later floors this game is definitely for you and if you are really dedicated the Atomicats farming gives you a reason to keep playing even after unlocking all improvements, characters and difficulties
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on Epic first and got a Steam key later from a Humble Bundle, hence the low playtime. Probably around 15 hours total, made it to the end of Year 3 several times but never quite to Year 4.A worthy experience (esp on sale) if you like the idea of chaotic bullet hell mixed with farming sim, but it feels like a B- execution of an A+ hybrid idea. Props to the devs for fleshing out many details since release with free updates, but the lack of co-op, the insane unrelenting difficulty curve, and the uninspired map design keeps this from true greatness. I do think my biggest hurdle in the game though was the RNG shop, which will stick you with the worst guns in the game sometimes, destroying your entire run. But hey, RNGesus comes for all of us.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the bundle with the base game and DLC during a sale a few weeks ago but didn't have a chance to really get into it until this past week. I am addictied to the gameplay loop, explore, farm, wave defense, profit, repeat. I put in about 10 hours in a few days as of the time of this review.Apparently they reworked the crop system and veteran players don't seem to like it as you can see from their whining. As a new player I like that it is easier to manage farming during wave defense. I guess if you are hardcore min/max gamer this will anger you. But as someone who just plays games for fun and not as a streaming job while restarting your runs unless you get the perfect RNG meta build, it's a good system. Highly recommend Atomicrops as an original and unique take on the roguelite formula.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Later levels provide huge challenge but can get repetitive and boring quick with the same stratergies applied most of the time. That being said, it's one of the few skill-based roguelites out there where upgrades do improve your gameplay but are not entirely needed to get good.6/10Graphics cause eyesore after a while especially with all the stuff happening on your screen.Simple repetitive mechanics without unique build crafting or synergies between items.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like roguelikes? You should get this. Do you hate roguelikes? You'll prolly like this one, you should get it. I honestly have major issues with roguelikes because the constant reset makes me feel like Sisyphus. I also am not very good at video games and I get frustrated easily. This game has managed to hold my attention for 114 hours. I think this is because the between year section where you buy upgrades means a: something is always progressing and not being reset and b: I am driven to collect cats.  It's  super addictive and is pretty welcoming even to filthy casuals like myself who just want to farm.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think a farming roguelike shooter would be so damn fun, but my god does this odd mix-up of genres work so well together. The art style is beautiful, the gameplay is properly challenging, the mechanics of the farming are deep yet intuitive. As soon as I picked this game up, I wasted the rest of the day playing it. One of the best rogue-lites I've ever played!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I understand that I'm the problem here but I'm putting this game in the too hard basket. I love Roguelikes and like farm sims but this just didn't add up to the experience I was hoping for.Upgrade paths happen at a glacial speed and it feels unsatisfying.You can never afford a weapon upgrade because they are always more than whatever I earn that round. Doesn't matter how much I earn. Out of the 10 or so play throughs, I've been able to afford a gun upgrade once. It was good when it happened but with such infrequency, I gave up trying.The camera becomes jarring when there's a lot of action on screen and I am trying to move around. It has no problems following me in one direction but as soon as I move in any other direction, it has this dramatic turn (like it's trying to show more of what's ahead of me when it's not necessary) and since you're being attacked all time, it becomes tiring to look at.Too much happens in-game in the expected amount of time given: you have to both tender for a garden to earn peanuts during the day while being attacked (your crops are safe but you're not), and defend the garden at night. And explore. And you're give 3 minutes to do it all in. There's not enough time to grow plants that are worth the effort, fend off enemies and explore. So you're pulled out of the action only to go straight back in because I have not enough peanuts or hearts for anything (except maybe seeds and a pick axe if I'm lucky) and I'm always in constant need of seeds. I buy seeds but it's not enough. I uncover plots of land to plant more seeds and explore and get more seeds that way, but it's never enough seeds. Exploring is a chore because you're constantly being told to go back and defend your crops. In one play through, I tried to grow my crops in the day and just explore at night. But I kept getting seeds that would take longer to grow than the day, so I would have to stay with the crops and defend them giving me no time to explore. And unless you abandon your hard work, you get stuck in this loop of fending and growing the few seeds you do find.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Bugged out and wouldn't let me progress in the tutorial.  Dumb farmer kept telling me it was getting to be dark and I should go to defend my land.  He said this message nonstop for a full game day/night cycle, preventing me from interacting with anything or progressing in any way.  The controls were also just awful.  Refunded this garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic roguelite where you can get ahead early and hard if you're smart. Keep on top of stuff and you'll rip it apart. The only con is that the unfriendly worm is really fast and trains too closely to your movements sometimes so it's unavoidable to die in some cases.I'M NOT OWNED I'M NOT
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this game, its like the lovechild of 'Binding of Issac' and 'Stardew Valley' due to the bullet hell and item based aspects and the farming and stat based aspects. The metaprogression is slightly subtle at first but is also very noticeable once you get further into it, and even then it can be fairly noticeable at the base levels of some of the progression stats. Some characters are better than others based on your playstyle (my fav's Thyme and least fav's dandelion) but all seem to be fairly balanced and will further be balanced from what i can see in the upcoming patch notes. If you like bullet hells, roguelites, or farming games, then this is right up your alley, if you said yes to all three then this is just the type of thing you would absolutely LOVE. 9/10 would 100% reccommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to spend more than hour in this game and 18 hours later on both my steamdeck and pc I love this game it easy to pick up refreshing to play and re-playable it with a great farming and bullet hell gathering aspects woven together better than i'd have imagined possible one of my favorite chill and action orient rogue likes ive ever played its worth it full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: (have also played 10+ hours on Switch at the time of review)Has a very addictive game loop and this could be one of the best roguelites out there, up with Hades and Binding of Isaac, if it weren't for some fatal flaws that seriously holds it back. Firstly, it is extremely cluttered. There are a lot of distracting elements going on on the screen and it is very difficult to see most of the time you're playing. This is compounded by the fact that enemies and enemy bullets can be hidden behind your crops leading you, through no fault of your own, to walk into them. The palette choice for enemies and bullets can be frustrating as well because they often blend into the background, making them difficult to see.Secondly, and this is related to my first point - the hitbox on your character is enormous. It covers their entire body and this is a problem because when it looks like you can simply walk around a bullet, you get hit instead, because even your character's head counts as part of the hit box - making distances frustratingly hard to judge. Thirdly there are just too many particle effects and moving objects on the screen at any one time. If the crops didn't bounce up and down and move so much, getting hit on the farm because I can't see wouldn't be such a problem. But the entire game is like stimulation overload which can make it quite frustrating.Lastly, the metaprogression.... it kind of sucks that the ant is so hard to find before you can start giving it currency to upgrade your metaprogression. It took me 9 hours on my Switch's save and 3 hours on PC before I finally found it which kind of sucks because it feels like you are just ramming yourself into a wall repeatedly for no reason up until that point. I also really wish they had expanded the metaprogression a bit more than what it currently is.I still recommend this game because frankly it is extremely fun and addictive regardless, and still worth playing if you get the chance to pick it up cheaply. Hectic, arcade-y fun for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast. The concept is brilliant and incredibly fun to play, and has great replay value. The upgrades and cats are satisfying to obtain. The characters are unique enough, some of them feels too similar. (other than oregacrow but he's DLC.) The "years" are a rewarding way of altering difficulty, and I enjoy doing daily runs to gain extra cornucopias. The achievements are great fun to achieve, a unique twist that can alter your runs and rewarding to get by giving you bonuses in your runs and adding a little decoration to your hub. Sometimes I wish that either you got more cornucopias or upgrades where cheaper, but that might just be me. (Who doesn't want upgrades.)Definitely a great game for someone who wants a good challenge, and likes achievement hunting.8.5/10 -some rando on the internet
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game through the humble monthly and I've been pleasantly surprised because I personally mostly lost interest in the top down shooter roguelite subgenre and haven't really enjoyed a game that falls into this category in a good while, but this feels fresh and it scratches that "just one more run" itch just right for me. It's difficult, but not brutally so, and every run you learn a little on what you could've done better. It is pretty overwhelming at first, but discovering everything and figuring things out is half the fun. Good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'll mention that it works perfectly on Linux with Proton — the experience was so seamless, I never would've guessed it's not native.This isn't a farming simulator in a conventional sense, as the agriculture portion of the game becomes less important on higher difficulties, and you're reducing it to a bare minimum (at least that's my play style) in favor of roaming and attacking enemy camps. So, don't expect this to be "Stardew Valley but with guns". Nonetheless, crop farming is the essential and central theme of the game.The core genre of this game is a roguelite, similar to Rogue Legacy and Undermine in a sense that there is a meta-currency to spend to improve the skills of the character, and has that item collection system like in The Binding of Isaac and Undermine, which can, similarly as in those games, lead to some really wacky and fun combinations which makes you excited and curious about which of the items you'll encounter in the current run. You can choose the difficulty level before starting a run, so you can avoid being overwhelmed by difficulty, but you can also choose to always play on the hardest difficulty if that's your thing. The soundtrack is original and awesome, makes the feel of the game unique. It can get repetitive, as the runs are pretty much the same, except that the enemies move faster and have more health (etc.) on higher difficulties, however, it doesn't feel repetitive while you're mastering the game, discovering new areas that you couldn't before, trying out different guns and so much more.Overall, I recommend this game, it's a really complete and cohesive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: #Beat (Year 1 / 10) on SwitchA fun rogue light twin stick shooter about post apocalypse farming.Loop:- There are 4 main "fields" in this "farming" shooter you can go to. Each is a biome. They all have one biome beyond that (as far as i know) as well. Think of a + symbol where the middle is you farm. You go to these areas and clear out point of interest. These POIs can result in: Pets for your farm, which help you farm better, seeds for farm, game mods, which help overall abilities, and a few others.  You have a limited time to do this before nightfall. At night you defend your farm. There are 4 seasons in a year, as there are. You do each season 3 times, the 3rd being a boss. After each night you can go back to town to use money on upgrades or items, including guns. After each boss, you will gets some additional stuff including currency for permananet upgrades.  Survive the year to win the game and unlock the next year, which is a harder difficulty. My only major complains with this game:- You need a new gun. Trouble is, depending on luck, you may get this earlier or later. Once you spend money on a new gun, you just wont have money later for another. So you are stuck with the new gun for the run. With rare exception. Buying new guns grants mods as well. So ideally you would do this several times. Its just really hard to do that and i wish there was a seperate currency for the guns.- (Minor) - There is a time limit to the day giving you limited time to explore or farm. I just wish this were longer. You CAN make it longer with upgrades and other items. But you will have to go back home or risk your crps/currency.- Towards the end of a run, farming seems less important, as your money at that point is largely spent and you cant afford new guns or upgrades. So late game tends to focus on just exploring for mods if possible.A fun rogue- light that isnt without its flaws, but is worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like brussel sprouts. You'll either eat them with a smile of satisfaction on your face, or you'll try them once, spit them out, never touch them again, and give them the evil eye when they are placed on the table every thanksgiving and Christmas. I love brussel sprouts, but I can't say the same for this game.The good - I'm trying hard to find some good. The concept of the game is interesting. You get your own farm in a nuclear wasteland, and have to try to grow crops to make money. It is a blend of a traditional farming game and a very old style arcade shooting game. I want to add more here, but I'm coming up empty handed.The bad - The music is like nails on a chalk board and definitely missing the professional touch. Even the really, really old arcade games had better music than this. By far, this left that nasty taste in my mouth that I just couldn't swallow and had to spit out. The graphics are old style but felt sloppy and unfinished. The game play (the very little I experienced) feels like an old shooting arcade game where someone had the afterthought of "Hey, you know what would make our shooter better?  Farming!"I like farming games and don't mind arcade shooting games, but this game missed the mark on combining the two styles into a quality game. Perhaps over time I could acquire a taste for it, but in short, these brussel sprouts just weren't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun bullet-hell roguelite. The game is definitely not an easy one,and your first few runs will almost certainly end in disaster unless you have other bullet-hell experience. This is par for the course of the genre, however.My biggest criticism comes from the fact that some of the bosses are not equal. Namely, the worm boss in the Spring is an absolute pain to deal with unless you have an AOE weapon, and the Spider boss during the Winter is just plain awful to fight and seems to be more of a test of health than anything. _childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is an amazing mix of twin-stick shooter, roguelike, and farming gameplay that I highly recommend to all gamers. At first glance, I was not impressed by the art style and, having received it in a Humble Bundle, I was wary of this being another throw-away title. After only one play through I was hooked.The gameplay loop of daytime exploration and nighttime farm defense felt great. There are benefits for each aspect of the game whether you prefer fighting or farming and I always felt like my current run had some advantage that I could focus on to win the round. And when I died, I was always eager to start over and try again. A full run would take me about an hour and you can take breaks about every 5 minutes to continue later.The difficulty of the game is somewhat hard while starting out. You may die a few times as you learn the mechanics and the huge selection of upgrades, but each death still provides you some progress to your next farm upgrade. Even if you were just grinding points to upgrade your farm, there are plenty of fun and challenging achievements with in-game rewards to chase after.After having achieved 100% completion, I am eager for a sequel. Fingers crossed for Atomicrops 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addictive. I don't play too many roguelikes/lites on account of my poor concentration and skill ending many runs, but even though this game is challenging, it's really enjoyable. The premise is that you'll be running a farm in a nuclear wasteland and you'll have to defend your crops from the mutated creatures surrounding it. In the day you go off and explore the biomes and get into danmaku battles with progressively mutated wildlife to get more seeds to sow and pick up delicious rng-dictated loot, upgrades and farm animals. When night falls you return back to defend your crops whilst frantically multitasking and trying to plant and harvest the seeds you harvested in the day. Also, more danmaku. A 'run' of this game is a whole year, made up of progressively more difficult seasons, but since the year is broken up into seasons and days, it's really easy to just play a day or two, return to the town, and then hop out if you've got stuff to do. The game has a bunch of different mechanics that aren't difficult to understand but require some strategy to exploit to your full advantage.It's kinda like a perfect marriage of Enter the Gungeon and Stardew Valley. If you like roguelites, pick it up! It's really quickly becoming my favourite roguelite from my limited experience. Also, the crops and enemies are weirdly adorable...
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: After I put so many hours into the Switch version of this game, I just had to play it on Steam, too, because I like it so much. Now, if you're wondering why...Well, first off, the replay value of this game is INSANELY high, if not endless. There is so much variety in every run that it never gets tiring for me. The gameplay itself is also a lot of fun, so that certainly helps. It's very fast-paced due to how focused it is on time management in addition to mixing bullet hell and farming sim gameplay. It lacks the life sim elements that most other farming sims have, though, so look elsewhere if that's what you want from the game. But if you want action-packed, fast-paced gameplay, you've come to the right place.One flaw I will mention is that unlocking all the permanent upgrades and other stuff takes way too long, but again, the variety makes it so that it's not a boring grind.The game is definitely challenging but not impossible to master -- another reason why I like it so much. The learning curve is pretty steep, but the payoff of mastering the game is incredibly satisfying and worth it. Plus, the developer adds appropriate balance changes when necessary.The music is quirky yet kinda strange at first, but it grew on me after a while. However, i've played the game so many times, to the point where the soundtrack can get tiring. I sometimes wish there were more songs as a result. I'll never get tired of that sweet, sweet Tranquil Moon theme, though -- best song in the game, in my opinion!Overall, this is easily the best farming sim i've ever played. It also counts as my favorite roguelike, and perhaps even one of my favorite games of all time. If you enjoy bullet hell action games and you'd like a unique addition to the genre's usual formula, (in this case, having it fused with farming sim gameplay) then absolutely BUY THIS. You will not believe how good this game is! Sure, you'll have to understand the somewhat daunting mechanics first, but it is oh, so worth it! Trust me on that one.I can't see myself ever getting tired of this game. That's how good Atomicrops is!

_childDocuments_.review: Just like it says on the tin, it's a roguelite bullet hell farming sim (I hate to be reductive, but Gungeon + Stardew is an accurate enough simplification), and it's fun as hell. A lot of people have been complaining that the game doesn't do the best job explaining itself, which I would agree with at least partially. The tutorial does a good enough job of explaining basic concepts and controls, but leaves a lot for you to figure out yourself (exploration flow, pigeon scrolls, merging crops, quirks of the L2 button which does at least four different things, etc), and it'll take a few failed runs of you messing around, exploring, and failing to put the rest of the pieces together. But when you do, oh boy. One thing in particular I think this roguelite gets right is that the items you collect that change/modify aspects of each run are given VERY FREQUENTLY, and are generally limited to items that effect how you farm and defensive/support passive effects rather than completely changing/limiting your offensive capabilities, which, for me, makes for less runs where you're two stages in and are doing badly because the game gives you a series of "bad guns," which was often the case with me and Gungeon. It also seems as if these items are all available from the outset, not requiring you to "unlock" their presence in the game from a merchant or a random draw between runs. Instead, those unlocks involve permanently upgrading your starting stats, or increasing the length of the day to give you more time before your crops are in danger at night. Things that spin the game slightly in your favor rather than introducing more random chance into a genre built around RNG. TL;DR, it's Gungeon + Stardew. Complicated controls and a slightly-too-vague tutorial, but it's fun as hell and the randomized aspects are always interesting and helpful and affect the gameplay in such a way that you'll rarely have a run that failed from the outset because of bad luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Super-Fun Bullethell-Farming-Mashup.Why is it Fun?Because its increasingly Challenging (by Choice), there are lots of Upgrades to Unlock, good Design (imo), , great Humor, while everything is underlined by fantastic Music.Game is structured in Runs, each Run is over one Year (ingame of course) which is seperated into 4 Seasons with 3 Days each.Every Day in Dawn you are dropped into your Farm to explore the surrounding Biomes for Seeds, Powerups and the like while growing what u found for Cash(ews), Life or Roses. At Night, your Farm gets Attacked by Waves of Enemies trying to rid themselfes of you and eat your Crops. Every third Night of each Month, their is a Bossfight (which is no Spoiler imo). As soon as a Night is over you get transferred to the Town where you can Buy Weapons and Seeds for you Cash(ews) or Romance a Bachelor(rette) for certain Powerups and their assistence.The Difficulty of the Game progresses with each cleared Year, there are 10 Years in Total. The Player is still able to choose though which (of the unlocked) Year(s) he/she wants to play for the next Run.There are numerous Upgrades to be obtained, like slighty increasing your Movementspeed, reducing certain Cooldowns or a slight chance to block Damage. These Upgrades are bought for Points you are able to earn each Run, usualy in a Choice of 2.Different Characters can also be unlocked, each brings a specific Perk to a Run and brings some Sort of Item or "Assistent" (like a Drone, or a Bee).The Game Supports Achievments both in Steam and Ingame.Very enyoable Game, each Run is different, Boss fights are interresting and the Music might bring Joy to your Heart.I'd say its worth the full Price.Side Note: Feel fry to Comment on both my Grammar as well as well as my spelling, trying to improve my language here.

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a fantastic game. It is certainly not as deep as other roguelite shooters nor is it as full-featured as farming sims. Despite this the game has become my chill, happy place game when I just need to not feel stressed out and have some fun. The gameplay loop is extremely satisfying and while each complete playthrough is fairly short that also means that if you die and have to start from scratch it doesn't feel like the huge crushing setback that other games in the genre can feel like.It also greatly helps that Atomicrops is incredibly charming. The artwork is just so much fun, the attention to detail in the character designs really communicates that a lot of love went into making this game. The music is also fun and cartoon-ish and the sound effects are wonderful with all sorts of moist splat and fart noises that are a wacky delight. It has a warm and silly sense of humor that never gets in the way or becomes annoying, it's just such a fun game!Free content has been added since launch and the game has enough of a difficulty curve that even after 29 hours I'm still unlocking new things that definitely make interesting changes to gameplay. Probably one of my favorite games of 2020 and a welcome relief from isometric rogueltes that beat the crap out of me.

_childDocuments_.review: Well thought out twin stick shooter that achieves everything it attempts. Frantic gunplay (and fantastic Joonas Turner soundtrack) of Nuclear Throne combined with what may be the most fresh twist on the farming simulation genre seen to date. There's enough going on here that I'm forced to mention the charming and inspired pixel art as an afterthought.The amount of multitasking demanded creates a near limitless skill ceiling. The difficulty progression - framed as a march through the years in line with runs being organized into seasons - means the content will most likely outlast your interest (in a good way!). Like Nuclear Throne before it, I see myself returning to this game on and off for years to come.A perfect 10.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful fusion of farming and roguelike.
