_childDocuments_.review: First, a word of note: If you're looking for a laid-back farming sim, this is that. Atomicrops is closer to Enter The Gungeon than Harvest Moon. But if that tickles your fancy, keep reading.Atomicrops is weird.  weird. Whether it's the premise, the visuals, enemies, and bosses,  off-kilter enough to catch the eye, or the downright surreal genre blending, this game is an absolute chimera.The core loop is pretty simple. You go into the eight major zones outside the farm, clear camps to get upgrades, animals and seeds, then grow the seeds like usual. At night, enemies appear on the farm and attempt to eat existing crops. Once dawn comes, you get a Base Phase to buy new weapons or things like Bridge parts and chat up a group of potential Spouses at the cost of Roses. At the end of every 3 Days, the season changes and your yield is tallied for score and rewards.As for meta-progression, you gain Cornucopias based on your haul that can be used on permanent upgrades (or cats). Personally, I found the progression only really gets good after clearing Year 3(the core Higher Difficulty system) due to the cornucopia rate just being too . A little bumping up of the bottom end would be more than welcome.Once it gets going, and you start to understand the balance between farming and gunplay (which are more intertwined than you'd think at first), it's an absolute blast.This is a game that's more in tune with a twin-stick shooter than farming, but Atomicrops manages to strike a stellar balance that has very little downtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, it's like a single player top-down pixel version of Risk of Rain 2, item decisions and player movement make a big difference in how well a run goes. It's got some unlockable upgrades, but it feels pretty well balanced to keep progression fun and interesting. The unlocks are in a persistent "base," but  you don't interact with your "base" during a run, each run starts out more or less identical except you progress through 10 difficulties called "years". Each year is slightly harder than the last and has the potential to unlock another small upgrade.It can get repetitive, but if you like rogue-likes it is pretty fun. The combat has an old Raiden Arcade (that plane game where you dodge all the enemy bullets) vibe and I used to love that game, so this was right in my lane. This kind of repetition doesn't bother me also some times if it's poorly balanced or too many upgrades are locked up it can feel tedious, like you're just playing for your next run, but you feel invested in each run for itself and your tactics and movements can make a bigger difference than an upgrade.Very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not what i expected at all. Had i paid full price i would have refunded it.  From the reviews i was expecting stardew valley with a farm defense type deal at night, well thats not really it. Its more of a timer shooter, you have around 2 min to either plant your farm while getting shot by moles and stuff or leave the farm to fight enemies and try and get seeds and power ups without buying them at the traders, once that timer is up its night time where you have to defend your farm from crop eating monsters, once night cycle is up which is another 2 min give or take you are taken to town to buy powerups and weapons if you got any money that day. after an hr of play i still have no idea how you get cashews which is the money in the game which you really need to progress as the difficulty spikes fast. Maybe its from harvested crops im not sure.  i seem to be just short of affording anything decent every time despite killing multiple things. your health needs to be grown but the seeds cost roses which are not easy to come by. all in all the short timers and confusing progression really kill the game for me.  i do not like the game but the art style is cool, movement feels good and alot of effort went into making it despite it not being what i expected. _childDocuments_.review: I like the game. While you don't have any pressure the start of the game is probably still the hardest but not only will you understand it better in no time there are also a ton of permanent upgrades (cross run progression) that will help you out a lot without it getting too easy too quickly.There are important decisions to make regarding how you spend your time, which upgrades you choose or how risky you want to go giving you freedom and challenging you at the same time.The playable characters feel different enough to encourage different playstyles or at least focus on different strengths and even one character to make the game faster if it wasn't fast enough or difficult enough for you already.The enemies are varied and are fitting to their biome and scale up well throughout the years (difficulty). There is a variety of bosses but they could have been a bit more difficult in my opinion. I feel like most of the difficulty in this game comes from normal enemies.The game got a lot of (free) updates over the years and if you don't like them you can turn off the DLCs or play classic mode.My least favourite point in the game would be if you are too fast and have already cleared every combat area in the game and you can only farm but that rarely happens and even if it's not for long. The leaderbords give you some competition and it can take a long time to finish all of the upgrades, collect every plushy, statue and cat.I really like the game and defintely recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Plays similar to Nuclear Throne with the farming of Stardew Valley sprinkled on but works better than that sounds. You spend the game planting and growing mutated crops while exploring a post apocalyptic hellscape teaming with machine gun totting rabbit, an evil sun, and of course giant mutant bumble bees. It's a game that doesn't take itself too seriously while still being engaging. Music is catchy and sound effects are simple but effective which add to the experience.I used an Xbox controller and it controls well as a twin stick shooter type. Some of the controls and concepts aren't explained in the brief tutorial. For instance, you can make "mega crops" by planting four of the same seeds in a square next to each other and fertilizing them. They are worth more than the individual crops. There is a little down time between each short day where you are forcibly airlifted to town where you can buy seeds and guns or romance one of the lovely, horribly mutated, bachelors or bachelorettes (I seem to always end up with the rabbit). Guns break after one day of use (except with one character who only has a chance to break the gun) and you only have a couple choices for guns each day. This encourages experimentation and gives you a reason to keep the crops safe. Unfortunately some of the guns are far superior to others. This may be a deliberate choice but I would prefer a buff to some of the weaker guns. It's a pretty challenging game and having a crappy gun vs a boss can end a run.I wish there was a bit more content. There are different "years" which are more like starting a run at a higher ascension level in Slay the Spire as opposed to a continuation of an existing run. The higher years make the game a bit harder and more bullet helly but don't introduce any new concepts, abilities, guns etc. The other rogue-lite aspect randomizes the various killing fields with different enemy placements and upgrade pickups. It doesn't really change how your approach each area, but I appreciate the variety.I got a decent amount of fun out of the game but probably won't play again unless/until there's a major update/dlc. I would recommend to anyone who is into modern rouge-lites.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: The comparisons to Stardew Valley are very misleading, because the games are fundamentally very different. I would hesitate to even label Atomicrops a farming simulator game, when compared with other games in that genere. It's definitely a bullet hell game, and its definitely a roguelike game. For me personally, I find that to be fun, but the playing experience is very dissimilar to stardew valley. (specifically, the fact that in Atomicrops you start over from the beginning every time you die)edit: After 80 hours, I would classify this as a roguelike with a strong emphasis on meta progression, and bullet hell, and a farming mini-game to make money. One interesting aspect about this game - if you beat your previous run, you start out the new run with a significant advantage. It makes it fun to chain runs together.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Such an unique idea, personally I haven't seen a game with similar mechanics to its. The concept is great and the realization as well is. I'm amazed, actually the game is quite monotonous: try not to die from moles, survive night and sow the fields; but a gaining hardness with each year, various characters and to explore more of the map are still making me keen. Imo it needs more attention, already have recommended to all my friends
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Don't bother. Game is poorly balanced.Guns are FAR too expensive. You're gonna get maybe 70 on the first day, and they sell for 60 if you're lucky. After that, you'll have maybe 800 while they're selling for 1600 or 3300. Take a hit? Good luck getting enough roses to buy the heart beets to get the health back.Spend your days trying to plant crops (only real way to make money) but have to till ground, then fight the damned weeds all the while getting shot at during the daytime because moles are everywhere.It's such a giant mental strain.Guns should not be this expensive. Someone make a mod where all guns are 60 at the start and you upgrade them, and moles have 1/2 spawn rates or lower.Seriously, game would be a solid 8/10 if you could actually afford ways to defend yourself and didn't have so much f***ing busywork just trying to keep up with the absurd prices.4/10.

Feels like bar mitzvah music on acid or something.Long and short: I regret my purchase, but I'll play the game with disdain - I've played early accesses with more polish than this pile of semi fun eclectic garbageEdit: after posting this...I can`t play it to get my moneys worth.... it`s garbage, I hate it, I wish I could get a refund - I hate this game

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game with some major downsides that rip a lot of the fun out of it like a sudden suckerpunch.The spider boss is awful. If you happen to coin flip it as your boss and you have a short range gun, of which there are a lot, then you just can't fight it. On top of that it runs around spamming bullets that you have to dodge all the while other ranged enemies are spawning and it spawns melee enemies that rush you down. Frequently just ends runs unless you're popping off.The moon event with the witch is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it makes me wonder how you're supposed to deal with it at all. It seems to spawn way too early into a run and you just lose so many crops because the witch sets fire to everything. The only counter seems to be hitting a weapon that waters but even then the event just sucks all fun out of a run before it even starts.Elite enemies are an interesting idea but the fact elites protect entirely vanilla rewards is so dumb. You have no incentive to fight them and most of the elites take way too long to kill. The immortal aura on the desert crab enemy in particular just runs away and spams waves of bullets at you all so you can get 3 seeds and maybe 1 rose. What is the point? You are better off just moving to a different camp/biome and farming weaker enemies.The character balance seems lopsided at best. The 2 earliest characters giving faster crop growth and +1 weapon mod are such huge upsides, meanwhile the Lion feels like you're playing with your hands tied behind your back and god forbid you play coffeeman. The gameplay loop is so fun and captivating but suddenly being hit by immortal crab elite or witch blood moon just pulls all that joy away and replaces it with bitter frustration of how you were supposed to play around it. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: A bullet hell with an annoying gimmick, a mediocre mess propped up with excellent graphic and sound design. The game's fun to look at, there's no doubt about that but the game play is incredibly flat. The entirety of Atomicrops can be described as either holding down L2 to farm or R2 to shoot with little thought and next to no planning. The only instance I can recall trying to plan any of the planting is when I really wanted to make sure I had roses for the next day or found a rare buff to planting the same item side by side. Surviving one year grants you the ability to play at a higher difficulty the next run. Unfortunately, playing the next run means you've lost everything from the previous year. Worked really hard to earn enough roses to marry one of the paramours in town? Well, they're gone. Upgraded a worthwhile, random weapon (which you can only find in town, by the way)? Oh well, it broke the next day and/or it's gone too. The ultimate failing of Atomicrops is the want we have for continuing the progress we've made on our farms from year to year vs the loss of progress in roguelikes. The bridge between the two is typically some permanent buff to our characters but in this game they're just not very good: Tractor's start with full energy, a few percentage point buff to one thing or another. There's simply no means to change how you approach the problems in Atomicrops, every run feels identical to the last with a slight difference in difficulty depending on the random drops.Other roguelikes such as Rogue's Legacy offer a fundamentally different play through with each run by mixing up the dynamics of the classes and providing permanent buffs between runs. The sense of progression offsets the frustration of restarting while the varied means of tackling the castle, as well as the procedural generated nature of the setting, make each run feel somewhat different and interesting. Atomicrops offers very little of this. The only means to permanently buffing your character comes from the cornucopia currency which you can only receive at the end of each season and only if you've done well enough to earn it. The buffs themselves are just way too lackluster to ever do much of anything. The tractors being ready to use instantly means next to nothing when I'll be spending the rest of the day moving between camps in the wastes trying to find additional buffs. A few percentage changes here and there are very difficult to plan around and add very little to the diversity of play between runs. Atomicrops isn't a bad game but it isn't worth $15, more like $5. It feels like an expanded browser game from the 90s, not a full release worth putting cash into. I can only hope this game is eventually opened to the Steam Workshop and we can add the few touches it needs such as 'weapons no longer break' and 'marriages last between years.'
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is an extremely addicting roguelike that wears its chaos as a badge of honor, Everything's frantic and stressed. You'll be running around like a chicken with its head cut off trying to scramble up any upgrade you can find, trying to see through the visual noise to survive. Extremely fun but due to the frantic nature I feel like most runs play out the same. The year loop is only fun because of the increased difficulty. Another thing I'd love to see as a quality of life feature is some way to see the description of items without having to sit for so long in one spot.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Ever dreamt of a twin-stick shooter / farming simulator / time management / action-roguelike game in a colorful and quirky dystopian setting, where you shoot anthropomorphic bunny bandits for loot, summon badass tractor-nukes and marry mutants? Well, "Atomicrops" got you covered.Never believed that this oddball broth of a game can manage to create a coherent gameplay loop, but it does!The controls are quite a handful to get used to, but once they do, you will be rewarded with a challenging and fruitful endeavour. Managed to defeat the final season boss once or twice, but there are still a lot of unlockables and challenges to go for.Rad!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: it's fast paced and zaney, and ur expected to die a lot until u get better. it's also kind of about time management & thinking about what you want to prioritize each day. i feel like some people look at the cute graphics and get the wrong expectation from this game. it requires time & skill to learn to dodge & strategize with different item synergies, adding tons of value imo, and the chaos is also very entertainingi think if u like challenge and dying in games and u like getting flustered & excited & getting better, esp if u enjoy rebuilding with different playstyles and strategies each run & mastering them, u'll probs also love atomicrops
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of the hardest games i've ever played. i am yet to beat year five. the amount of heart beets they give is down right garbage. just when i feel i could beat year five, a hundred things go wrong all at once, as if the game is not meant to be beat on year five or higher. bullets spawn out of nowhere. monsters sudden gain more speed than they should have. its as if the game is cheating... i can beat year 3 easy, but 4 gets harder. but five seems unbeatable. every video i found on youtube of someone beating year five or greater seems to be exploiting the game in some way which i do not care for. thank you for making a rage fueled game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nice, but do not expect it to be a chill farming game with some combat, this game is super intense with an overwhelming amount of things going on visually, it is super hard to keep up. The first few runs are calm and a little stressful, but once you beat the first level it is just hell. There is no slowing down or else you fall behind. If that is your speed, you will like this game, if you want something chill, this is not it.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: God this game is so fun and addicting. All these people claiming it's too hard even though they're "pros at touhou" or some other garbage bullet hell are straight up lying. I can't beat level 2 on enter the gungeon and yet I've nearly perfected this game on steam achievements. IT IS HARD IN THE BEGINNING. Stick through it, try to learn it and it becomes so much more fun and easier later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible, I received in a humble bundle but damn, I wouldn't complain about the price given the experience. A lovely farm you seem to have taken over has become overrun with swarms of mutant creatures and you must survive waves of freakishly colourful creatures, while making sure you water, grow and harvest your crops.The sound track is strange yet it compliments the environments surrounding you as well as the Nickelodeon meets Magic Mushrooms style artwork. Expect to meet some wacky creatures and freaky bosses all while your plants and friends laugh with joy amongst the chaos that unfolds. Fortunately there is a bit of breathing space between waves but don't waste your time, Players can explore outside their farm to try find better items which there is a lot to collect, These will help you in each run and you'll have lots of fun juggling various tractor upgrades, weapon upgrades and farm upgrades to ensure you have enough money to evolve to the next challenge by the next season.The challenge is great. The more you harvest during a wave, the more money you have to spend in town to buy upgrades. Make sure you work hard!  I find bullet hells to be therapeutic but you know, that could be the ADHD in me and at the end of the first year, I was excited about knowing that the next year game can be more difficult and brutal. Bring it on.Only let down I feel is the game begs for a 2 player co-op campaign. I could see 2 players on a couch grinding towards unlocks and achievements which would work well with some pizza and energy drinks, sharing the madness together would be heaps fun.Overall, It's a ridiculously wild bullethell that brings a fresh twist to the slow and relaxing farming sims out there. Get on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Farming sim on steroids (and nukes?). Its basic harvest moon with a bullet hell - murder animals to fertilize your plants. Get help from bees, cows and pigs to grow your crops. The game has 10 difficulty levels and takes time to master. Nice art that's complemented by the music.Not too much of a plot (pun).
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Atomicrops is a interesting concept, a blend of farming, a Roguelike, and a Bullet Hell. But, as it is right now, IT is fundementally flawed. One of my main gripes with this game is the RNG. Ok, I understand that a roguelike can have RNG and sometimes you'll have bad runs, or good runs. HOWEVER, if you don't get the good items in the first few days, you're practically ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Especially the Blood Moon Events. Oooooo, I hate these events. If you don't have the turrets or scarecrows for this event, get ready to be showered by constant enemies shooting at you and eating all of your crops, meanwhile a witch with high health will be constantly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on your crops.    Now, I WOULD BE FINE with most of the projectiles in this game if it weren't for the fact that YOUR HITBOX IS BLOCKY. Now, in any Bullet Hell game, it is vital that your character has a small hitbox to compensate for the loads of bullets coming their way, in order to dodge them skillfully. But with Atomicrops, most of the time you are hit by a stray bullet/enemy that you SWORE that you wouldn't get hit by.   Another gripe I have with Atomicrops is that the weapons break too fast, and most of them are just terrible when it comes to the hordes of enemies coming your way. For example, what the hell am I going to do with a sniper rifle when a swarm of mosquitoes are eating away at my crops? Or with a double barrel shotgun that reloads slow and does subpar damage compared to a shotgun that has more ammo?   I really hope the dev of this game recognizes these issues and fix this game, because it'd be a shame to let the potential of this game to waste.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing gem that I feel like most roguelite that was mostly under bigger content creators radars. A good bullet hell in creative setting. Defending your land from radioactive vermin, witches, and the elements come to life themselves.  Beaten it a few times and I still pick it up and mess around. My first impressions here
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun games I've ever played. One of those strange combos of genres that just works so well. Amazing soundtrack, satisfying game play, and insanely hard to master. This game and Hades are the only two games that I can spend literally an entire day playing. The new DLC took a little getting used to, and at times some aspects of it can seem a little unfair. However, this game is supposed to be hard, and it reflects that very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: **Edit**: I've changed my mind about the chain gun. Sometimes you really do just need to kill every mf'er in the room. Also after an ungodly amount of tries I got the Robusta Year 10 achievement. How? Light cheating. I played over and over and over again until I was good enough that I was getting to the end of winter 3/5 times (I hate you spider and rabbit) and to the end boss about 1/5 times. I finally had a game where I had great upgrades and a really good garden. Then while in town, I exited out to desktop. Navigate to "C:\Users\*username*\AppData\LocalLow\Bird Bath Games" and copy the entire Atomicrops folder onto your desktop. Then play against the last level. Hopefully you succeed. If not, exit the game. Copy the folder from your desktop and paste it into the same location overwriting the other folder. Bingo bango you can try again from the final stage with all your stuff. "bUt ThAtS nOt ReAlLy GeTtInG tHe AcHiEvEmEnT!!!" I'm an adult with a full time job. I paid for the game. If your mom had purchased me this game after a nice sea food dinner and pleasant company and she had a real problem with manipulating save files I might care. hot tips: The crop upgrade that fires missiles when you plant crops takes down bosses faster than anything else. Squirrel gun with splash damage can do surprising amounts of damage. Playing Robusta and then going to any other character will make you better at the game. This game is absolutely fantastic. I seriously thought it was only okay and then I noticed I had almost 80 hours in. Its super simple. Plant crops, kill monsters, defend crops. Repeat. In between rounds go to town and buy stuff. Pro tip. I personally found the loss of mobility with the chain gun not worth it at higher difficulties. Do no underestimate the cleaver. Dual wield and rapid reload will have you mowing through enemies. The only weapon I couldn't get the hang of was the scythe because it can drop without the ability to deflect bullets making it incredibly high risk while having similar damage to the cleaver which despite appearances is a ranged weapon. Anyways. Buy it. Totally worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that made one gameplay loop, and polished it to perfection. Each run is on the same farm, with the same areas to explore, and the same enemies to fight, but the random items, guns, is enough to keep it fresh. The drive to keep improving at the simple gameplay loop is addicting and will have me thinking about what I could have done better hours later. In terms of difficulty, this ♥♥♥♥ is tough as nails. The first few runs will kick your ass to the dirt, but once you get that first win, its difficult to stop, and the ramp up in difficulty is done perfectly, as the second stage will feel impossible, even though you still have 8 other stages to beat.If you have any interest in difficult rouge-like shooters, give this a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: with my 123 hours on this game (yes really) it is a very fun game, like a fighting and framing game but you know that, i know some people will be mad at the start bc its to hard, and i get it but keep on playing year 1 and you can beat it, it takes some time but, i have done it so you can to! all and all its a good game and you should play it 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a bonkers idea. I mean really now it's been done, you wonder how no one had thought of it before TBH, but really it's a crazy idea. Farming games have always been really popular. I used to play Harvest Moon when I was younger a lot. Then Stardew Valley reignited the love for this sort of game, and the new Animal Crossing on Switch got a wider audience into this kind of game.Then you have the rogue/bullet hell side of it. Bullet hell roguelites have became incredibly popular in recent years,  so the need to come up with new takes on the genre is always present. Marrying these 2 kinds of game together is something that I would not have personally thought of, but I'm glad someone did think of it, as it's amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I knew it was part farming simulator, but based on the footage I thought that the combat would be more fun. The runs end just as they are starting to get good; it's super annoying.If you're looking for something that looks like this but with a more creative artistic style and more engaging gameplay, I recommend Voidigo.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game enough, i legit recommend this to everyone i know. This game is a perfect mix of resource management and a bullet hell. Enemy patterns are pretty easy to learn making you feel like you can progress after each run. The farming and combat mix very well, making it so you have to risk getting hit while farming, but not making money if you only fight at night although they give you enough time to do both. The sound track is amazing, making this game feel lively and upbeat even with the dark undertone. Again couldn't recommend it more, love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: very fun game, i bought it back when retromation won his bet against the devs and it has been massively updated and changed since, but you don't have to worry if you want the old style of play as they have added a classic mode, in general all these dlc and updates streamlined and added more content to the game and the general style is beautiful and has had a lot of work put into it, it can be a bit challenging but even if your not good at top-down shooters i would actually recommend playing this game to get gud, as the differing levels of difficulty allows for easing into higher levels of difficulty, overall a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I guarantee you've never played a game quite like this.  If it's your jam, it's going to scratch an itch you didn't know you had.  It's definitely a niche title, and quite difficult.  The multitasking and situational awareness required to play successfully takes time and practice to develop.  But man.  What a unique experience, and the aesthetics and music are on point as well.  I nearly 100%ed it on Switch, and had to rebuy it on PC just so I could like, have it again. Have more of it.  It's good.  It's very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this arcade style game. It is so much fun to beat each level and work towards beating level 10. Even after achieving level 10 there is still so much to do. Trying to get all the achievements, and the the daily challenge keeps the game re-playable. Also, I have purchased Reap What You Crow DLC. I think it is a fun new way to play and the two new weapons that come with the new character are amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Combine Roguelites, Bullet Hells, and Stardew Valley, and you've got yourself one hell of a ride.The game starts off relatively chill, but don't be fooled - it ramps *hard*, especially on the later "Ascension" levels.You'll die, then keep coming back for more. It's an endless cycle, just like trying to farm that very last crop before the day ends, only to find you're 1 cashew away from a minigun and have to settle for weaponized squirrels.Try it. I think the developers deserve more credit for the love they've put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: For new players please please look up videos on people who have spent a lot of time playing and see how they play, it is absolutely a huge change and makes the game much more manageable and a lot less crazy to start with. That being said, having a blast playing and don't plan on stopping anytime soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Since I got it on sale for only a few bucks so I got my money worth but not on sale I would not recommend.While it's fun for awhile but then it gets very repetitive. There is not enough of a difference between runs, they all feel very samey pretty quickly. If there was more variety in how runs played out it would be much more replayable. I also didn't care for how timed it was not giving you almost any time to just tend to your farm. There are good bits and it is fun at first. The runs are just too similar after a handful.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, So simple yet so complex at the same time, in the later years getting used to, Planting, Fertilizing, and shooting at the same time takes me more brainpower than i'd like to admit, but it's a hell of a good time, a great game from top to bottom, 100% recommend, Be aware, This isn't a roguelite game that you just "beat" the first time
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

_childDocuments_.review: Modern city life got you down? Well you’ve just inherited your late uncle’s farm, time to pack your bags and start fresh in the peaceful countryside. What could possibly go wrong? A nuclear apocalypse, that’s what. Now you’re in a hellscape wasteland defending the last surviving source of sustenance – your crops. And every mutant wants a piece.
_childDocuments_.name: Atomicrops

name: Kynseed
detailed_description: A huge new update is now live! The Big Build Update adds farm and farmhouse customisation, building projects including bridges and Hob damaged houses, brand new gameplay gating, a beautiful feature-packed progress screen, a new challenge system with over 450 new objectives with rewards, story cut-scenes, combat totems around the world, loads of new and improved dialogue and many more changes. Embark on a lifetime of adventure in a beautiful world of creativity and intrigue. Raise a family, customise your farm, run a business, craft items, and battle some marvellously malevolent monsters. Your actions and decisions matter in our adventurous story filled with purpose and promise. Lend a helping hand to villagers in need and discover the unique blend of creativity and choice that sets Kynseed apart. Come and join us - your legacy awaits! Story based RPG set in beautiful regions with battles against dark faery tale creatures. Customise your farm and farmhouse using Kynseed's new customisation mode with hundreds of items and limitless design possibilities. Run a business such as a blacksmith, apothecary, or goods store. Develop relationships with villagers who will remember your deeds, actions, and pranks! Combat the evil Hob army as they construct powerful totems and cause the destruction of crops and buildings. Rebuild broken houses and buildings for your neighbours and new NPCs. Gather materials to create items, forge weapons or mix cures for bizarre maladies. Buy strange artifacts from the mysterious Mr. Fairweather - items that can aid your chores, help you in combat, or just let you mess with the world. But be warned of his life tax; each item must be paid with years of your life! A world where everyone ages - raise a family then step into your children's shoes and continue your legacy. In Kynseed, live your life the way you choose in a lovingly handcrafted 2D open world. It’s a beautiful RPG adventure from a couple of tea-making veterans of the Fable series. ABOUT PIXELCOUNT STUDIOS PixelCount Studios is a small team of independent developers who have come together to build the game of their dreams. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: First reviewed in 2022 and revisiting in 2024. An excellent game that's clearly influenced by Stardew Valley but introduces a host of interesting new mechanics. Combat, in particular, surpasses that in Stardew. That said, Kynseed is also one of the few games of this genre that provides as much interest to the pacifist players out there. At launch it was not without flaws, but the devs were actively engaging with the community and releasing updates pretty much twice weekly since launch (we'll forgive an xmas hiatus). --> After the Big Build update, a lot of the irritations are ironed out.Quest rewards and prerequisites now make a lot more sense.You get a unique friendship quest once you maximum the friendship meter with each NPC. However, one of the notable rewards for completing these ultimate quests is more friendship points which are entirely obsolete as the friendship points have already hit their max. These quests should trigger when the 2nd (not final) friendship heart is reached. It used to be tricky to get shops to be profitable but has been improved. All the shops feel like an asset now. I said that I was confident that the dev team would iron out the issues and I'm delighted to say they have been.  I'm now over 300 hours in. I've thoroughly enjoyed the experience. One of my favourite games of 2022 and in my top 10 most played (amongst illustrious company like Civ 6 and Total War).

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: This review has been redone twice since Lionbaum responded)Here is a comparison of Stardew Valley vs Kynseed, highlighting all the great features! I'm perhaps not the best comparer since I played maybe a week of SV before getting bored, but I'll try comparing anyways. At the end of each part I have who "wins" that part in my opinion (SV or KS)Farming: Stardew is very focused on this, while it is more of a side-project in Kynseed. [SV]Exploration: Kynseed has a HUGE map - way way way wayyyy more places to go, sights to see, and people to meet. There's also lots of items to search for, not just plants but "proverbs" that teach you where to find certain items or how to use them. [KS]Activities: Many of the same activities in Stardew are present in Kynseed. Fishing is less of a minigame; cooking has lots more to do, with several minigames and many effects for the dish. You can also buy a shop (Goods store, apocathary or blacksmith) to run and try and make a profit from. [KS]Animals: Animals have much more of a role in Kynseed; you can ride your pig and eat it too, as well as sheep! There's also chickens and cows. Cows are stationary (at the moment) while the others wander and you can have them follow you. There are also pets, including a standard dog, pugs, cats and some sort of creature you'll have to find yourself (plus more to come!) that each have their own ability (some abilities are yet to come) [KS]Battle: Now I haven't done any battling in Kynseed, but this is base off of what I know. In Stardew, it's more of a dungeon crawler; you just have your weapon, your health and your stamina. In Kynseed, there are more stats used. It's also almost turn based (but not quite?) so you can make certain moves or maneuvers. So yeah it's more fleshed out, but this is more of a matter on what type of battling you like. [Tie]Characters: Stardew has more fleshed out characters with more dialogue, but Kynseed has way more characters to meet and marry. [Tie]Family: As said before, Stardew has more fleshed out characters to marry. However, there are many more options in Kynseed. Plus, you can have your spouse do stuff for you (like cook!), and in the next big update you'll be able to have kids which will certainly be more fleshed out than in Stardew. [KS]Score, SV-KS: 3-6. Though like I said, I'm biased ;)There's still more to see and more to come in Kynseed! Personally, I'd buy it at the next sale (Steam Christmas sale I believe) to support the devs but wait until at least the kids update. That way you can start playing with a real goal :)

_childDocuments_.review: I actually enjoy the game a lot and played all of these 40 hours in the span of 2 weeks but then completely stopped. I do have some issues with the game as well as some things i like about it, starting with the positives.Positive:* generation systemIn all fairness it is very creative and it creates for some really interesting character designs and choices. Being able to cultivate your own playable character from childhood is a cool idea.* shopsRunning stores is a great deal of fun, especially since it is a great excuse to use the very creative crafting system. While it isnt perfect, they pulled it off better than most developers of single player games do.* Crafting systemNever have i seen such a cool and unique crafting system, especially when it comes to making potions and cures. With each ingredient having its own unique effects the crafting system becomes very elaborate and fun. You have to explore the cures and make your own by discovering when to use an ingredient to cure a specific disease.There are obviously more positives but those were the most notable ones.Negatives.* pvp systemI liked it at first but i was expecting something more open world, with monsters spawning on dangerous areas of the map, when i first left the farm i was almost expecting to be ambushed by a monster but i never was, which was dissapointing...Instead the pvp system we were left with is predictable and very easy to beat...* ShopsWhile i mentioned shops as a positive they are also a negative because as you start to scale your businesses and create more of them they become very hard to manage and consume ALL of your time. Since you cant buy stock from the ledger you have to go to each shop and individually stock them each time they run low on suppleis. What would be great is to enable restock from the ledgers so you can do it all from one place to save game time.* Farming systemHonestly it feels like it was completely overlooked by the developers, it doesnt feel useful and it doesnt generate a profit at all, i barely use the farming system either because it feels so redundant, especially when i could just by all the vegetables i want from one of the stores that i own.Again there are more negatives but these are the most notable ones.As it stands i cannot recommend this game to anyone. It isnt finished and its one hell of a grind to get anywhere in the game. It needs some serious polishing and even with the new builder update i doubt its gonna reel me in for another go at the game. What we need is a complete pvp overhaul, store owner quality of life changes and a farm rework and maybe then i would be able to confidently give this game a yes, but for now it has to be a no.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a very mixed reaction to this game, but I will say the positives are outweighing the negatives at this point. Overall I'd definitely recommend this game as it is full of charm and there's lots of fun to be had. Pros: * Art style is beyond beautiful, and the world feels very lovingly crafted. It's bursting with cozy, whimsical charm. Exploring is a joy* Music is magical and adds a beautiful, fantastical mood to the game . I especially love the theme playing when you enter the North Gate. In fact, all the different areas seem to have there own theme and vibe which is lovely. *Mini games are so well done and make crafting so much more fun and engaging. I really love smithing and cooking* The story is engaging, and the writing is really funny. The game isn't afraid to be quite dark at times which I adore. Not everyone will like this, but I find it really refreshing. *You can buy a dog and a cat, and you can ride your adorable pig whose name is Truffles. Super cute and fun. *Selling produce is really fun. Rather than chucking everything in a shipping bin, you buy a stall and customers will haggle you ( which is another mini game ). I love it. * Lots to do, including running your own tavern. I'm not there yet, but I'm excited to try it out. *Works gorgeously with controller. Lovely UI*Heaps of bag roomCons: ( and suggestions )* I appreciate the game doesn't want to hold your hand, but I think the game could use a bit more direction, especially as you're starting out. Perhaps the game could implement a more streamlined set of tutorial quests to ease you into the game because it is a surprisingly big game with lots of mechanics and a lot of things to do. I found myself feeling quite scattered and aimless at times. I think the game would really benefit from opening up a bit slower as you learn the different workings. *The goddess offerings are a confusing system, and I'm not sure I'm getting it. I'd love to see a more interactive tutorial there. *I often feel I'm googling too much to find out how to do things. How to sell things? How to mine? How to obtain a sword? How to marry? etc. Overall, I'm enjoying my time in Kynseed, I just think it needs to find a balance for those who like to be thrown in without a map, and those who enjoy a bit more direction. I certainly feel I could use a bit more guidance to get into it a bit easier. I'm excited to see how it fares when the full release goes live in December. Definitely give it a go because it really does have something for everyone, and it's so lovingly made. You can feel the passion leaping off the screen.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Harvest Moon, Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, and Story of Seasons. All of that and you would think I'd be sick of the genre but this has a fresh take on farming sims that I've not personally seen yet. There are of course many overlapping elements but even the farming system is completely different compared to other popular farming sims. Dare I say simpler?Aside from the massive map and the aging mechanic I appreciate the Goddess mechanic and the influence these offerings to the Goddesses can have on the PC's week. The fairytale and wivestale influences incorporated into the world building is a cherry on top for me.This is also a SUPER small thing for me but... you don't have to name anything. You're just the farmer and your animals don't need names either. I personally like that. I hate coming up with names for each animal without a random button like in Stardew. If naming helps you get into a game this might not be the easiest game for you to get into.Bottomline: If you're a fan of the genre you'll probably enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, much like Minecraft and Terraria, plonks you into the world without so much as a "how do you do?". Like Minecraft, one of the first things you will see is a pig. You will then come to the logical conclusion that the point of the game is to dedicate your life to your porcine friend, devote your time to growing and harvesting various fruits and vegetables to offer to the pig, and humbly request its transportation services in times of need. (Psst! Give the pig gassy apples. Just trust me on this.)The second thing you see will be a young vegan/vegetarian man who will make up a poem on the spot about how your lovely complexion brings to mind amphibians. You will proceed to marry him when you are both old enough. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules.If a lack of hand-holding is distressing to you, then you may find yourself relying on walkthroughs and the discussions for a while, until you get the lay of the land. And should the aging and death mechanic feel equally distressing, know that a single lifetime can last hundreds of real life hours, and you will probably tire of the game before your "founder" dies.Time does pass rather quickly in the game, but as I have said, your character will have many more sunrises ahead of them, and the mapstones, proverbs, and quests are hardly going to vanish like the morning fog.Want to be a shopkeep? Go right ahead! Brew potions, forge weapons, haggle with customers and lament the fact that, no, you cannot use your newfound wealth to raise an army of cats, dogs, and pigs to conquer the world. Ah well, maybe one day . . .(I would recommend using guides for cooking and forging and so on. Wasted some high quality ingredients only to let the jam boil over. My poor jam-less toast.)I do think the way your twin reacts to the new sacrifice ritual is overly dramatic. Perhaps add an option for players to choose between the old ritual and the new one, so all the people whose complaints presumably led to this change won't have to be subjected to it, and the ones who enjoyed the morbid nature of the game can do so.I'm looking forward to playing more of this game, and am excited to see what updates the new year brings. Congratulations, Devs. I hope you enjoy the Yuletide season and take a well-earned rest.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a late backer for this game over the summer, and I have to say that my expectations were not only met but exceeded. The pixel art in this game is some of the best and most detailed I've ever seen. The soundtrack is charming and gives off a very relaxing aura. The ambient sounds never get repetitive or annoying (huge plus for me) and everything about this game just spells out potential. I do love that it shows off pagan influences and mythologies too, not something you often see in these types of games. Just keep in mind when/if you purchase this game, it's not by any means complete.. there are a lot of features that are hinted at by NPCs (in a charmingly humorous fashion) but are not featured yet. This game is going to be huge someday, with a ton of content.. and for right now, for what it is, it still has a ton of content. All in all this game is very relaxing and I think anyone with even a passing interest in simulations, farming, adventure or pixel art games should check it out. For the price, it's more than worth it!Apologies for any mistakes made in this review. It's my first ever review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is NOT at all what it seems. If you're looking for a farming type game like Stardew Valley, My Time at Portia/Sandrock, Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Rune Factory, etc. this is NOT the game for you. Honestly I don't think there's a single person I'd recommend this game to, not because it's necessarily bad but because it isn't good at anything and every mechanic in the game is implemented much better in other games. It feels more like a point & click game combined with a mobile idle game.I'm honestly quite upset and could probably write a whole essay on every thing this game does wrong, but no one has the sanity to sit through an essay of me ranting.Instead I will give a very strong warning that no matter what you expect out of this game, whether it's the combat, farming, romance, characters, dynasty, cooking, fishing, exploring, running business, character & building customization, etc. you will be sorely disappointed because none of them are good. They range from horrible to okay at best.Highlight of issues:Want to live life how you like? Sorry, your only option to make money is owning a bunch of businesses, every thing else doesn't get you nearly enough money and rep. There is no specialization. I wanted to be an adventurer.Want to run a business? Sorry, all you do is stock it and hire some people and watch money and rep slowly come in. Brainless. And they are completely unbalanced.Want to farm? Sorry, super basic. No modifying farm plots, not many crops, super basic farming system in terms of growing, harvesting, watering, etc. Also no machines for turning food into other stuff (besides grain but have to go to a windmill on another map).Want to craft? Sorry, all you get to do is play boring time consuming mini games that you brainlessly click. Also there are no conversion/crafting machines for your farm.Want to customize your farm & house? Sorry, doesn't exist.Want to focus on your family? Sorry, I can't imagine playing the game long enough to get to that point. 30 hours in and my character has gone from 18 to 19 and I own all the businesses and am super rich.Want to level up like an RPG? Sorry, you can't level up your stats, only use eugenics to make better kids. Which you will probably never get to anyways.Want to customize your character? Sorry, doesn't exist besides changing colors.Want to automate anything? Nope, not doing that.Want to know what an ingredient does? Sorry, good luck finding all the notes.Want to enjoy a compelling story? Nah, pretty boring.Want to meet interesting characters? Nope, everything has to be comedic. It gets stale real fast and characters have little depth. They also don't react to things, such as disappearing for 5 years and no one bats an eye.Want to romance characters? Boring and doesn't feel like much. Plus if you want someone around your age you have few options and their stats will likely suck anyways.Want to enjoy combat? It's fun at first but quickly becomes spending an eternity dodging to get enough hits in on the enemies.Want to enjoy a full non-EA release with few bugs? Nope, lots of stuff was broken on release. Even now there's still a ton of bugs and things not working properly.Want lots of content? Not much here and they had to push out some content that was supposed to be part of the full release.Want an interesting economy? Have fun with a completely broken static economy that makes no sense.Want a balanced game? Nope, so many balancing issues and decisions that don't make sense and cause the flow of the game to feel off.The only good thing I can say about the game is that it does look beautiful. Everything else is mediocre at best.I spent 30 hours hoping I would get to the fun part. It never happened. Save your money. I'm sorry to say but with the core mechanics in this game I don't think it will ever be good game, let alone fun. I wish I could get a refund.Buy one of the many other farming life sim games out there that do all of this but much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start off with a part of development in this game I didn't like changed.At the start when you play Kynseed you play through a prologue that acts as the base tutorial and sets up the story of the land that kynseed takes place in, Quill. The prologue introduces you into the belief system of the people you meet and teaches you the mechanics that it offers. It's rather well done if not lengthy for a tutorial of its caliber. It spans 14 in game days and only afterwards can you really start playing it as the sandbox it is supposed to be. Now all of this about the prologue being long isn't the focus of my main issue but it is one that exists. My issue is in a censorship of the main prologue, most notably the last day, the festival. Some people would spoiler it but it is literally for the prologue which if you intend to play this game you would play beyond for the most of the story.Now, how is the festival censored and why does it matter? In the current iteration of the game the festival starts with everyone from the town gathered around a wooden effigy like construction with a priest and two volunteers to be chosen from. you are given the choice on which of the two. After you make your choice the person appears inside of the effigy and its face lowers obscuring the person to be spit out as flower petals. Real child friendly, but life isn't always like a fairy tale and the previous version had so much more shock factor that made the prologue amazing. The original version has the same setup, but when you chose the person they would be taken into the hole inside of the effigy and be trapped inside with metal bars, the effigy would be set alight and the effigy and the person inside would be burned. The older variation really has a more impactful "What have I done?!" and painting the shadows onto this happy-go-lucky fairytale, like before Disney got to their fairytales.Other than the messing with the original good prologue, the game is solid. Nice gameplay loop like Stardew with more mechanics and minigames placed inside. Great idea with the aging of everyone including yourself, and the use of life expectancy as currency for 'legendary' items.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr Kynseed is a unique take on the Stardew Valley-like genre that I’d call ‘expanded farm sims.’ Its first in-game month of gameplay is a long tutorial / story prologue that, if approached incorrectly, can feel rushed and overwhelming. If you are willing to look past the pacing issues at that stage of the game and get through to when the game really starts (after a brief fast forward to young adulthood from childhood) you will find deep, thoughtful and often silly Fae-heavy world rich in activities, diversity and complexity that certainly rivals Stardew’s equivalent 1.1 or 1.2 versions, if not more. If you want to ride a pig, make a deal with a Fae demi-god, be shocked by dark undertones beneath a superficially silly world, shoot apples off of trees somehow making them better quality, and much, much more, then you should try Kynseed despite the qualms of other reviewers. I think that after 57 hours of playtime, I am finally ready to review this game. Let me be clear about two things right out of the gate. Firstly, I am not done the storyline; and I am *definitely* not done the game. There is a lot here to chew on, and enough variety therein that I think it would be unfair to call any of it filler (though some portions can start to feel that way at a certain level of repetition). Secondly, the most common complaint I have seen in other reviews is that the game doesn’t give you enough time. That is -and I don’t use this language lightly - objectively untrue. Let me explain: During the prologue of the game, your character is an early teen (13 years old), and you play at that age and stage of development for one in game month: fourteen in-game days. During that time, your character always wakes up at 6am, and cannot stay awake past 11pm. This effectively strips some time out of each day, limits when you are awake, and does make things feel a bit more timing sensitive. This isn’t helped by the fact that your time-keeping method to start is the leaves (flaps?) of dandelions that you pick up – no joke. Maybe I’m dumb, but that didn’t help me stay on schedule. The game isn’t shy during this first month about throwing lots of opportunities at you. You are quite limited, relative to the full scope of the world, in terms of where you can go and what you can do, but even within those limitations, there is a *lot* you can still stay busy with. The people who feel there isn’t enough time in the game, I suspect, fell victim recurringly to what happened to me just a couple times: they got distracted by the many activities you can do, and missed ‘Story Tasks.’ The prologue functions as a kind of tutorial, and each day you are given a different task by your adoptive uncle. If you miss the task for that day, its gone. Sometimes the game kind of shames you a bit for it, letting you know that you missed it one way or another. For people who come to Kynseed from Stardew, it probably feels hectic and a bit frustrating. But here’s the thing: that’s just the prologue. Without being too spoilery, not too long after that first month you have the impediments and limitations of childhood lifted, arrive abruptly at young adulthood and, even more wild, you don’t need to sleep *at all*. Yep, that’s right: zero sleep. As an adult, all 24 hours of the day are your’s if you want them, every single day, forever. Your character will live until 50 years of age, so let’s just say, hypothetically, that you fall through some kind of time warp and end up 20 years old instead of 13. Each year has 4 seasons; each season has 14 days. Let’s say you happen to incur some kind of magical penalties and you lose 5 years of age further, and are playing from age 25 to age 50. That’s 1400 days of gameplay. One thousand four hundred in-game days, of which you could choose to milk all 24 hours if you are just that much of a madlad. Oh, and then, by the way, you can actually declare an heir (any offspring of your’s - stork-delivered or shoe-adopted - of your family is eligible)  *and keep going.* So that crazy number of 1400 days? That’s just your first kick at the can. Your heir gains a huge portion of the benefits and progress of your first character, and can pick up where you left off, more or less. Depending on how you raised them, they could just be objectively better than your first character! So, when I said that the complaint of ‘not having enough time’ was objectively untrue, that’s what I meant; you have *as much time as you want* to play the game, to pick away at things. Sometimes the way they pitch tasks at you left, right and center (especially during the prologue) makes it *feel* hectic, but if people could just get past the prologue they’d see: ah, so I really do have *all the time in the world.* Alright, so that’s my two big points out of the way. To summarize: Kynseed is big, it has *lots* to do, and gives you an abundance of time to do it. If you like games like Stardew, please don’t be discouraged by other reviews about the game giving you too much to do; Kynseed has flaws, but it has had a ton of love poured into it and is absolutely worth completing the prologue *at least*. My current playtime as of writing this is 57 hours, and that is from the prologue plus not quite one and a half years more (I’m in mid of the summer of my second year as an adult), so the game has a lot to offer as a fresh spin on the wide genre that games like Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon occupy.Now, if you are, by some miracle, still here, let’s get into the meat, shall we? I want to start my fuller review by saying that I have another word doc with two and half pages of notes of my suggestions and ideas that I plan to post in the game’s discussion forum. I’ve been playing this game with a fine tooth comb, and there is a lot there, with clear signs of more coming. With such broad scope and unique execution come opportunities for fine tuning and improvement, so if you are looking for the kind of totally polished product that Stardew has become over the years, maybe hold off a bit. That’s not to say it is bug-ridden or anything: I never once had the game crash or soft-lock on me, and if I did they literally have a built-in “Unstuck” button, so it probably wouldn’t have been an issue. It’s just that it still needs a bit of time in the oven to truly find itself and knock out the rough edges that have come from its ambitions. [[Continued in Comments]]

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game in Early Access in 2018. I think I played it for about 10 minutes at the time but was excited about it's potential. The promise of the game was just fantastic and I was excited.It's now released and 'done'. Except it doesn't feel done. I enjoy games that need wiki's and can put hours and hours into games that give you an open ended window. I love farming slow burn life sim games, but this one I just cannot seem to get into.The prologue builds this world and this interesting story. I was excited to play the game. It's art style eventually grew on me and I liked the goofy town people. The fat and poop jokes were funny and added character (at first). After the prologue the story just dies and it becomes this kind of boring rep grind. The villagers began to annoy me, the crude jokes eventually just became annoying. I felt no desire to complete the tasks for people, no desire to level up skills. Mini games become repetitive and dull very quickly.  It felt like EVERYTHING was a grind just to be a grind and the rewards didn't feel like they were worth it.It has a lot of potential. There is this interesting story and world but feels like nothing happens with it. It felt like the story kept trying to tease me. Something would happen and I'd go "oh, great it's kicking off!" only to suddenly have nothing to do again but the 'daily' grind.  This 1000% feels like a game that was a crowdfunded thing that got way way to ambitious and wanted to tick way to many boxes, not a game that came from some developers that have done other games before.In the end, I wanted to love this game but I find myself opening it up and pausing it and then getting distracted by other things.

_childDocuments_.review: Below has been spoilered as it's old, but I don't feel any need to delete it. My edit at the bottom's where my garbage take lives.  <======>2024 Edit: Lemme preface by saying this:  and not every game that has farming in it is Stardew Valley. Thanks for being patient, I'm done yelling baseless speculation at hypothetical people now.Anyway, this game's a hard one to recommend, if only because I find it somewhat difficult to describe. I wish Steam had a "middle" review for something like this. I really like it, myself; it's kind of a cute little chores game for me. Like something to pop in on when I just want to check a few boxes for my brain's sake - or enjoy some of the admittedly great ambiance - and I feel like it'd easily find the same niche for many others. It's a pretty game with a lighthearted sense of humor that has no shortage of things to do in it, provided you're not half bad at making your own fun with some of it.Speaking more historically, though, Kynseed was very much a victim of its own hype, an unfortunate situation I see a lot of indie games with ambitious premises end up in. It promised a lot and while what it delivered is very much a nice relaxing time, it doesn't quite measure up to the vision of it you see in your head while you're chiseling through the early access builds. Perhaps I'm just still reeling a bit from when the tone suddenly changed from a dark fae story with jokes in it to being 100% jokey, not to mention the whole deal with that one composer they had to fire (yet another talented person turned out to be terrible, c'est la vie), but the game seemed like it was aiming for more intrigue initially, which I think is why it was reviewed so poorly when it released.Well, besides the fact that it obviously wasn't done, and kind of still isn't in a few ways, but I'm trying to be nice.In short, y'know, since this is supposed to be a review and not the script for a YouTube essay, this game's kind of a charming mess. If you're willing to look past its rocky development , you've got a great little fae-themed sandbox to run around in and flex the imagination muscle a little.If you lack that natural inclination to flavor everything you play with your brain spices, you should probably steer clear or get it on sale, because it'll most likely end up boring you after the first 10 hours or so.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this game is very enchanting and delightful. It's not exactly like anything else in the genre but will remind you of plenty of other games that inspired it. Of course everyone compares it to Stardew Valley but it's really not much like that. The writing in particular is excellent. The devs are hardworking and responding quickly to player feedback. It's not totally bug-free yet, but they're squashing them. Definitely recommend if you're interested.

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR: If you wish Stardew Valley was more difficult/complex or you enjoy old Celtic folklore and aesthetic, you're probably gonna enjoy this.---The game is still in the works, and I bought after the Big Build update. That said the level of quality and amount of content surpasses a lot of finished games in the genre.It is a bit overwhelming at first because it is chuck full of all kinds of things to do, but if you stick with it you'll find this is one of the most addictive and entertaining games I've played. In terms of difficulty, it's really malleable depending on how you want to play. However it's absolutely not the kind of game you turn your brain off to. The game does save notes on just about everything for you so you don't need to fret if you did miss something the first time it came up. I've seen a few reviews complain about the style of writing for the books and notes being confusing to understand, but after you initially read the information, if it was something important, the game will save it for you in layman's terms, and more often than not it's stated multiple times in different ways anyway. Personally I love the style of writing, it creates immersion in the setting.Keep in mind I this isn't a "cozy game". The world has darkness and grittiness to it without being edgy. There's always a lot to do so you will probably feel stressed and overwhelmed if you're that kind of person. And some parts are definitely more difficult and, if you're like me, will make you rage. All in all though, knowing what the devs have planned and what I've seen so far, I have no complaints whatsoever. This is probably the best game I've ever played and I really hope they continue to work towards the goals they had set for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews here are so sour but I don't have the same complaints. Honestly the negativity of posters brought a terrible sense of preemptive disappointment to starting the game, and when I started playing I was always waiting for the other shoe to drop. Well, I'm 34 hours into this game and I'm nowhere near bored nor have I experienced anything gamebreaking or terrible. I know I'm going to sink hundreds of hours into this. It's got dry humour, it's beautiful, the minigames are inspired, the combat is new to me and really fun for someone like me who usually hates combat mechanics, and I am really loving the worldbuilding and character design. I'm hoping that as I progress more and more of this dark world is peeled back. It's not stardew, as much as I loved stardew, but that's a good thing, it's it's own game.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, and it's gotten even better since release with the "Big Build" update. There's so many things to do - the combat is fun, I enjoy most of the mini-games (although I'm sick of the smithing one), and the art style and music is lovely. _childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, as well as games with generational mechanics like Crusader Kings, or Mount and Blade 2, I can't recommend this game enough. I waited for full release for the last 3-4 years and my expectations and hype have been exceeded. This game feels like a love letter to people who love this genre and at 70 hours in I feel I have barely scratched the surface of this game yet am engrossed in the depth I have found so far.In addition to that, I did have a pretty bad bug in the game although there has been very few issues I was experiencing a bad crash to desktop, I have been an active member of their discord and noted how I was bummed their recent patch didn't fix my problem... to which the developers DMed me, asked for a copy of my save, fixed it and sent it back to me! Like holy crap! These guys are incredible! This is a game that is clearly a work of passion by people who are showing they give a crap about the thing they made. Thanks again Pixelcount!

_childDocuments_.review: As many others have noted, ehat was supposed to be the primary goal of the game - passing on a legacy through generations - is useless and pointless.  Not only is the entire game easily finished in your first character's lifetime, but most of the legacy mechanics don't even work. It's fun at first to explore and find everything for the first time, but everything beyond that devolves into "randomly" generated fetch/craft quests from the abysmally bland NPCs.  Crafting minigames are cute the first couple of times, but they have to be repeated EVERY SINGLE TIME for EVERY SINGLE ITEM.In the end, it quite literally fails to love up to its own description due to incomplete, broken and un-implemented features.

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game HOWEVER...If you constantly need new things to do in the game and would prefer a stricter storyline and side quests and main quests and so on, I would wait for the game to be fully finished instead of starting early access.  It is frequently updated and I foresee the main storyline being added to in the future as it kind of just drops off and leaves the player to just go about their life with little direction.  If you enjoy total freedom, though, like I do, this is not a problem at all.  There is plenty to do for players who enjoy deciding for themselves how to spend their virtual days, months, and years.  I recommend playing during early access for players who can create their own storyline and virtual goals thus needing no preexisting one to guide them.  For example,I personally have been pushing off the combat area of the game for (virtually) a couple of years because I am content in intensely focusing on growing my shop which I have formed into a bakery.  Because the storyline is pretty nonexistent in direction and goals, ignoring an entire aspect of the game doesn't really "hold me back" in the long run of the game.  I'm getting rich enough to be able to hire people to run my shop later on and then will have so much free time to then explore aspects previously ignored on my own time whenever I feel like I want to pursue this.  In comparison to stardew valley, it is more of a "choose your own adventure."  The scenery is far more beautiful and intricate, along with an infinitely larger world map, more villages, more people, and more difficult.  The realistic ageing system is neat as well. I only ask for more character customization like clothing in the future and then it would make my top 3 games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy 2D pixel graphics like in Starbound ? Do you enjoy socializing, farming and a bit of fighting like in Stardew Valley ? Do you enjoy cooking and enjoying the benefits of your food like in Don't Starve ? Do you enjoy gorgeous soundtracks like in Hollow Knight ? Then you'll enjoy Kynseed.This is an excellent game and i have enjoyed most of it. Thank you to the developers.However ! My good gaming friends, don't be fooled : the whole "pass your seed over generations" is NOT in this game. I think 80 to 90% of the players out there will end the main story with their first character. The shops rep system is just too broken if you run your stores well. I had 4 shops doing good and i've reached level 8 rep very fast and remember thinking  : "Is that gonna end so soon" ? Level 10 arrived super fast as well and with it, the end of the game. Summary : a great piece of gaming which paradoxally fails at its core mechanic. It's good, you're in for a nice journey, but you'll never play your kids ! You've been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having fun with the game, but I definitely feel what some other folks are saying who don't recommend it. I was originally just giving it a cursory glance as another farming/life sim in the same vein as Stardew, Harvest Moon, etc., but then I caught on to the generational game play. Well that's new! And I won't be in a situation where nobody ever grows old and none of the kids ever grow up! :D But then I smacked into the wall. I unlocked the vast majority of the map (minus only 2-3 zones) in just the first year. I think those other zones are locked behind later story beats. I figured out that the most profitable and easy-to-run shops were the blacksmiths, and the worst was the general stores. I ticked off 4 of the 6 goals from the Kynseed, one of which I won't be doing because it's literally just be a 'bad lover' so.. And I unlocked 2 of the 4 magic areas. Again, all of that in just the first year of game play (after the prologue). So.. while I would love a game similar to Stardew that has a generational mechanic like this, it ultimately feels unneeded since you can do it all in the first gen, which is the worst feeling. D: I still go with a recommend because it isn't a *bad* game (and there's no neutral option), it's just too short to need multiple generations. I probably wouldn't have explored as fast as I did if it wasn't for the letters I got about Chicken Auctions, Sheep Auctions, Masters, and a bunch of other stuff that you can only partake in if you keep pushing further north in the map. I'm not sure how much more the devs plan to add, but I'm a bit perplexed that they claim this as a finished product when the balancing is in dire need of attention. Go ahead and grab it on sale, but I would not pay $25 USD for something that promises multiple generations when it just doesn't need it at all.
