_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is a generational game.A genre I am... obsessed with.For context a generational game is just "A game where through some mechanism, time will pass and the game will continue even when characters you use die of age or other causes"Still working on that definition.Otherwise I wouldn't really have given it much attention.Honestly the game has a bit of a jank to it like most games in this genre. But nothing game breaking or experience ruining. Its Jankiness can be somewhat fun at timesIts combat system is very fun and unique which surprised me cause it took 5+ hours to get to it since the game is harvest moon esc for the most part. I would play a game thats just the combat expanded into a roguelike.The generational aspects are... hit and miss, some very very smart choices, but other choices that hurt it.It has one big issue in this regard, a single generation is too long, even with its smart life tax system. You can do everything in a single generation if you wanted. Which makes the whole having kids thing seem kinda pointless.The system works fantastic when you die. But it took 25+ hours for me to speed to my death.Also people just don't have kids fast enough. The world's population goes down faster then it grows so you'll get batches of random added into the mix over time. It works but is a bit sad to see a family line you liked die off. Contrasted too Crusader Kings where in a generation or 2 down and you will be warring with the ancestor of your founders best friend, moments like that are really fun! As far as generational games goes here is my Pros and Cons:Pros: Combat is great and training your heir to be good at fighting is satisfying. Stats matter, so making sure your heir is set up to play how you want is important.The life tax system is genius. It's a system in which dying in combat, or buying specific upgrades accrue a life tax. At the end of a single year, time jumps x years in the future equal to that tax. It's mixed in with the narrative, adds weight to your choices and speeds up time without just fast forwarding time like games like Massive Chalice or CK have to do. This system reminds me of “years of peace” in Wyldermyth but is a lot more direct, controllable, and impactful. This system is complemented by having a hard set death age. 50. At 50, you die, all left over life tax applies to your heir. Makes you really consider actions that affect life tax. Plus 50 is kinda a nice year to die, makes a reasonable "then he retired" age.It Utilizes Life goals really really well. You get random life time goals, a few of them. If you fulfill one you get to add a stat to your heir in any stat you choose. 3 of these are the same every generation it seems: make x money, make x rep, make x friends. With 3 random ones. This felt like a really good amount. A few of these I would be fulfilling during regular gameplay, while others made me do things I might otherwise skip or ignore. Plus the reward is good! But not too good, I felt like I had the wiggle room to ignore annoying ones, like the make 40 friends one.Cons:25+ hours to get to generation 2... when I was rushing. The Life tax system helps a lot, taking 10+ years after every single year, resulting in you hitting the next generation in 3 years time… but 3 years in a stardew like game? Star dew has your grandpa judge you at the end of year 2, thats end game for some. This is further pushed into the limelight by the fact that you can beat the whole game in generation 1 no problem. The Years are long, I feel this only really helps with farming. But honestly the farming is so shallow and just plain that I would prefer a version of this game without farming.The town ecosystem is just super dry. People don't really do... anything for you and so people aging, dying and being swapped out feels engaging as a whole. In Most Generational games, most characters can be used by you. Sometimes as units or enemies. In this game they can be used as shopkeepers, but I found the only stat that matters in running shows is “hourly rate”. your shops will be quite lucrative with the worst employees if they don't cost much. An alternative would be to have a town event like a tournament, the combat in this game is unique and deserves a lot more content and attention anyways. This way, you might grow a personal rivalry with a family via combat. Basically I have no reason to care for anyone, and my wife was chosen based on A) looks and B) traits. This kinda leads into another Con, their is minimum NPC on NPC interactions outside of the occasional marriage that just change where people live it feels. To continuesly mentioned Crusader Kings (CK), this type of game always benifits from people having their own relationships with eachother. I dont think this is nessasary tbh, and is more just one way to help NPCs feel less static. NPCs right now are just a list of stats, traits, likes and dislikes, and relationship points. Traits + likes and dislikes, are a good start to building a NPC that feels interesting, but unless those NPCs interact somehow, they just feel like systems designed for me to have to exploit. A simple way to put "likes and dislikes" into NPC interactions would be to just have that NPC grow liked plants in their home. Changes that I would suggest from a "generational game first" view.Shorten every season by half. 14 days a season Is too much, 7 would make generations come fast. You can get a lot done in 7 days.Remove farming/Focus less on farming, the farming aspects are already really shallow. The game feels more like monster hunter but you own shop's on the side(ie Gathering + Fighting for monster parts). So double down and add more content to gathering and combat. Farming feels so lackluster cause your seeds are non renewable and you kinda have to jump all around to get the seeds you want. Plus your farm is set, you can't customise or organise it, it's just very shallow for a game about farming.Have weekly events involving townsfolk. That way they feel less static. Things like, coming to your house to sell/give you a rare item, maybe dates, rumours, the aforementioned tournaments. Things like CK 2 events add alot. Simple character building moments, maybe your just given a choice and it gives you a weekly buff/debuff. Maybe gives you items or other things. Lots of variety could help, and so could having traits determine what kind of events pop.I think heavily cutting back on the farming and crafting mini game count would make time and space for these changes.Just some less structured nitpicks:Im 40 hours in so maybe the plot just admits this, but is this some body snatching stuff? Cause if not a few things that bug me:Why when generations pass does your wife and siblings get nuked? That just seems like your missing out on alot of those fun family bond situations generational games offer. My angry brother would have run the shop if not for this, which would have made it funny to run in and say hi to me.Why does your friendship not reset on death? its weird to me that I would be best friends with my dads friends.TLDR:As a generational game case study: 10/10As a harvestmoon like farming game: eh, the farming is meh compared to owning businesses and huntingAs a RPG: the combat is good, but feels like it got less attention in development then other systems. Would love to see more of it!.Overall I really enjoy this game and it was an excellent case study on generational games!I just keep feeling like its being held back by small things, always a "but":Generational stuff is fun! BUT season are too long.Combat is fun! BUT their is only 3 areas and only 1 weapon type.The Town ecosystem is cool! BUT NPCs dont... do anything.Anyways, yeah, I do like this game.If you like me, are into the Generational game genre, give it a try if you can and are willing to sit through 20+ hours per generation.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried playing some farming/life sims (like My Time at Portia and Stardew Valley) but got bored of them after a few hours. This was a gamble in that sense and i was very happy i took it. For me every day in this game seems to have something new happening and i feel there is always some goal to play towards (other than "make the best farm ever"). That has kept my motivation up and i still have time to do all the other farming/fishing crafting.The crafting minigames seem to divide the opinions of players but i really enjoy them. I haven't done any crafting in other games that feel as satisfying, especially cooking.I've played this for 18 hrs at the time of review and i'm still on my first character so maybe there should be some mechanic to move faster in time if i get bored at some point and want to continue playing with the offspring of my character and see how the townspeople change with time. Another minus for me is when owning a general store and putting stuff up for sale it would be nice if the game remembered what price i used previously. Now i have to check the ledger and then put it on sale if i find it there.Anyways, i still recommend this as it feels really satisfying to play and i really like the minigames for crafting!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Kynseed at many stages - early access, full release, and now the big build update. And I can confidently say that the devs keep innovating and improving the game. It gets better every time - optimized UI, tying the story together, huge new content updates. The game is beautiful and has TONS of content. One thing I especially love about Kynseed is that is has a work around to a common problem with farming/survival games - always needing the wiki pulled up. Kynseed fixes this by building a wiki in game - you get information about items and people by exploration, building relationships, and gaining items. It's very innovative and makes testing and learning fun, not just a chore you have to look up out of game. I highly recommend Kynseed!

_childDocuments_.review: As it now stands, I can't recommend the game even out in Early Access. There are a good amount of things that are missing, most of which are my pet peeves. Most important is the save slots. For people who are going to try this, be warned you only have ONE and only one. It'll autosave after each time you sleep. The story is ok so far, I kind of stumbled a bit playing this, a first for me since I've played a lot of rpgs and farming games. The controls are a little confusing if not clunky. Telling time is rather confusing as well.With the bad out of the way, here are the goods. Yes, story is pretty good, pixel graphics are ok, the color scheme, pretty bright. The concept of the game, I like it. It's new and I've always wanted to play as my children after my main kicked the bucket. Soundtrack is nice as well.Overall Summary: Too early for early access.PROS:- Good story - Soundtrack is quite nice so far- Pixel are, different but not bad- Writing, entertaining CONS:- 1 save slot, I know this early access, but I've played a good amount of really early access games and support them like on Patreon. I had 12 or more save slots for those games. This killed me good.- Not a lot of content out yet, again early access thing. Which I can't keep throwing out, the reason I wanted to try it out was the game summary where we can play as our kids. I thought it'll be implemented by then.. - Controls are a bit confusing to say is an understatement.- Boring, I fell asleep because most of the days I had nothing much to do but the same old house hold chores. I don't even have the chore of caring for the crops because I could only buy a certain amount of seeds on a certain special day... It felt like a slog to go through each day. That's how empty the game play is as of now.Suggestions to Devs:- Please consider adding numbers on your clock system. I kind of need to know how you measure time in that game.- I get the auto save after sleeping thing. A popular choice among old retro pixel farming games, but may you please up the save slots? This was a gripe for me on SDV, but I let it slide because we can have more than one character save.I'm just going to wait for this game to have more content before playing it again. I'll change my stance until then. But devs, don't let this one review ruin your game dev cycle. Just please continue doing what you can.It pains me to even give a "no" on STEAM. Because I only give positive reviews on the games I've bought, and I know I would love them.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with tons of activities and choices! While there are obvious comparisons to other games, Kynseed offers a great number of opportunities to define your character and identity within the world rather than getting caught up in level progression. The game relies heavily on a sliding reputation-based social interaction system which acts as the starting point for quests, platonic/romantic relationships (non-gender restricted) in addition to intel and lore gathering. Kynseed offers a lot of content to be absorbed while catering to many play styles in this life sim where the world evolves and experiences time, with a mesmerizing story. The UI is packed to the brim but well organized. The game plays smooth. Both keyboard and controller defaults are near perfect. The fresh take on 'crafting mini games' will keep you hooked and exploration will keep you prying and wondering for new experiences and obtainables. Pushing past the 'on-the-rails' tutorial and time-tasks is well worth it. The tutorial may feel rushed or funneled but it prepares you for the real meat of the game that follows. Reading the lore matters again! Overall, Kynseed delivers the often forgotten core of RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a little leniency since it is in early access... that is until I noticed that its been in early access since 2018, which for this game to still be like this is unacceptable.I'll start with what I like about this game.  The graphics are nice and pleasing looking (except for one issue but i'll get to that later).  The combat this game is fun to do and makes the fights interesting to go threw.  The event that happens at the end of the tutorial month was a real surprise to me and that made me a little more interested in the game (not spoiling and also aware that this might upset people that know about it).Unfortunately that's all the good things I can say about this game as there are too many problems this game has.  The biggest issue is the tutorial itself.  It took me 4 hours of playing the game to get threw the tutorial and that was me being patient with it,   I can understand up to an hour in the tutorial but I'm sure a lot of people will turn their nose away from the game if you make it last 2 hours let alone 4.  The economy system in this game is pretty bad as well, why bother doing blacksmithing, farming, or fighting monsters for money when the easiest way would be fishing (especially since almost everything you get can be sold for only 1 coin, which is ridiculous).  There has also been a few instances where the game just crashes with no reason (I went afk to make a sandwich and left it paused and it crashed for an example).it is sad to see that this game has a lot of potential and can be very fun to play, but right now it suffers mostly from an identity crisis.  It does not know what it wants to be, does it want to be a farming game? Well you barely have any farmland to work with and the seeds you can buy to grow are worth so minimal its pointless to even do.  Does it want you to work at the blacksmith's area all day?  Again, reward is so minimal for doing that plus it takes time out of your day.  And while I enjoy the combat, there is only one little area that allows you to actually fight anything, which is upsetting.  The story is pretty stupid too, why on earth wold I willingly sign a contract with a strange creature to give my life and my future family's lives away for a seed and the ability to see a gnome that threatens me if I don't feed it daily?In the end, after all the ups and downs I honestly could not enjoy this game and personally, I think pixelcount studios is asking for too much money for this game.  It's not worth 12$, its worth 5 at best with how it is at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game for its art, humour and incredible music. Not to mention the fun, addictive mini-games for alchemy, smithing and cooking. Where this game really shines though is in the depth of characters and world. It has been a really long time since I have just enjoyed exploring every corner of a map and interacting with every NPC. It really takes me back to that sense of wonder I had playing Fable for the first time as a kid and for that I am very surprised.However I see why it might not suit some people especially if the humour isn't to your taste. It isn't Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon but something else entirely different and that is what I love about it. In saying that I could see how people could come into this game expecting a farming sim but really Kynseed is a lot more freedom than that, which could frustrate people who like clear goals.Can't wait to see what comes next in Kynseed and from PixelCount Studios

_childDocuments_.review: You should buy this game if:- You enjoy a fairy-tale theme.- You like the shown pixel art.- Beautiful soundtrack that strengthens the fairy tale vibe.- You appreciate a game that is clearly a labor of love that is making its way to completion.- You like story plots with an interesting concept.- You enjoy life sim as that's the main focus of the game rather than the story - there is one but you advance through them in due time while most of the playtime would likely be spent making choices in how to live your character's life in the game, will you farm, manage a store, hunt, etc...You shouldn't get this game if:- You don't like the pixel art (environmental or npc as some people strongly hate the latter while they dont mind the former)- You don't want an "in development" game, check the game's roadmap.- You don't like to read "much/fairy tale stories or lore".

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just finished the Prologue and I already know it's going to be one of my favourite games of all time. As far as cosy games go, this is top tier, one of the best. It deserves to do at least half as well as Stardew Valley, if not the same or more. It's particularly recommended if you are at all a fan of fantasy and folklore of a mostly British origin, there's so many cool references and darker undertones without ever quite getting as far as folk horror - there's more than a few influences there yet it keeps things cute and kid friendly, although on the maturer side. I didn't realise til now that this is from the creators of Black and White, and Fable, and there are strong nods to those too. If I'd realised sooner I would have got this ages ago, it's been on my list for a while. It's just a really beautiful cosy game that will put a smile on your face if any of this appeals to you. Also, it's huge with as much potential for role-playing as you like, so many options for playstyles. My only minor criticisms is you are subjected to a lot early on, Stardew does it slightly better in gradually pulling you in, but I feel this has more scope and more to explore and discover. Also the music is fine but could do with I dunno, more epic variety? I'm being picky but maybe I will discover more as I'm still early game. But those are not reasons to avoid this. Did I mention it was beautiful? Seriously one of the best looking pixel graphics games I've come across, the colour palettes, detail, design and world-building is phenomenal. I almost feel guilty buying this game in a sale, absolutely worth full price.If you are looking for a cosy adventure RPG with many options for which path to take, and you want some escapism from the world outside, this is it, don't hesitate!

I puttered around with it, 10 minutes here and there, and then plot twist and I got hooked.  I love cozy games with a dark twist, and this one hits all the sweet spots on that. _childDocuments_.review: I am sad to say that I do not recommend this game. Farming and life sims are my favorite type of game and I'm always anticipating a new one. Kynseed has a beautiful art style and a really interesting concept, but unfortunately lacks in a lot of ways. I didn't play much, some might say that six hours is not enough for me to judge one way or the other, but it just didn't hook me. I waited for a long time for this game to come out of early access and was excited to finally delve into it, but when I did... I just found myself running around not understanding what the point of anything was. I was supposed to bring milk to an old man and that was about the most purpose my life had. How to make money was unclear, and even if I could make money, I wasn't aware of anything I would actually want to spend it on. How to progress was not really well explained and the ways in which I knew I could progress didn't really seem all that interesting. This game probably has been compared to stardew valley to death, but well it should be. It's a similar game and a similar concept but misses on a lot of marks where stardew valley succeeds. Stardew valley has a way of explaining systems as you go along, keeping you hooked, giving you obvious progression and upgrades, having a well written but easy to follow plot line, and compelling characters. All things this game lacked, which is the reason I bounced right off that thing. I bounced off it so hard, I felt guilty. But it's honestly just not worth my time. It feels so empty and hollow. And it hurts me to say because I wanted it to be good so badly and I feel like it has a lot of potential. Maybe if the devs continue to add things and edit things, eventually it will be the game I was hoping for, and I'd definitely be willing to try it out again in the future, but as of right now, it's just not there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a recommend because it's a fascinating game with a lot of fantastic ideas and I would love to see it be further iterated upon. However, as of writing I feel that it needs some fine tuning and balancing. In addition, I think a few systems can use a bit of an overhaul or refinement. Some systems are unnecessarily complex that makes playing this game feel overwhelming at times and some systems need more refinement to feel less repetitive/stale. This game is absolutely massive and not always in a good way.Just based on the prologue (which is several hours long but only introduces only a tiny fraction of what the game has to offer), this game on the outside this looks like a typical Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons/Stardew Valley-like game. However, if you think this is a Stardew Valley-like experience then looks can be deceiving. If you're looking for a relaxing farming/grinding/min-maxing type of game, this probably isn't it. If you're looking for a visual-novel like relationship sim where you can learn about the world and get to know the local townsfolk then this isn't it either. This game kind of has a jack-of-all-trades, master of none kind of situation going on. There's so much variety in what you can do. You can befriend the townsfolk, farm resources, fight monsters, craft/cook/smith items and so much more. However, each of these things in a vacuum is ultimately fairly shallow and simple.For example, lets get into that list:In regards to befriending the townsfolk, there are a ton of NPCs (with great names!) spread across this massive world that you can build friendships with and learn about. However, it's likely that eventually you'll come to the realization how shallow and lifeless the NPCs are. They have some unique dialogue and backstories but I found it difficult to really care about them because the bulk of your interaction with them are just fetch quests. It feels like they're mostly there to make the worlds feel lived in rather than be unique personalities that you want be friends with.In regards to farming and gathering resources, there's an interesting system where basically every item has unique methods to increase their quality that you slowly discover as you play. However, there's not really a "farming" aspect to it. You can't customize your home/farm to optimize crops or anything. Almost every resource in the game has predetermined, set spawning locations that you can learn and that's the extent of resource gathering.In regards to adventuring/combat, there's a whole combat system that mixes stamina management, positioning, timing, and real time strategy that's pretty interesting. However, the combat gets repetitive since the ultimate result of this system is basically back to back to back singular combat encounters with some variety of monsters and attacks.This game is a massive world where you have to make the choice in what you're focusing your time on in any given moment. This game has so many different mechanics that it's actually dizzying. I don't think it's humanly possible to play this game at 100% efficiency and do everything at once, but I also don't think it's the developer's intent to make that the goal though. There's just so much you can do at any given moment and too many things to keep track of.That may not sounds too awful because hey, more game to experience. But it makes it very hard to understand what you should be focusing on. There's so many mechanics that are poorly explained so it's hard to make a call on what is worthwhile to do or not. As a result, it feels like there's a lot of trial and error to try and figure out what works and what doesn't. But also this doesn't feel like a game where you can just do everything at the same time. You have to focus your attention on specific parts of the game at any given moment which highlights the shallowness of a lot of its systems and mechanics.Ultimately, I find this game fascinating. The world/lore is interesting and I love the *idea* of what this game is trying to accomplish. However, I find that I'm struggling to get into the groove of this game. That said, I'm willing to and going to continue playing and maybe I'll stumble upon the "right" way to approach this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics of the game are awesome, and there's a ton of stuff in this game. However, it is definitely unfinished. I really hate that this is not in early access. I bought this game thinking that since it was fully released, it would be finished. If you don't usually play early access games, don't buy this one yet. This is a different kind of game. Don't go into this expecting Stardew just because of how it looks.The crafting is really, really fun (though I still don't know how to make higher quality medicine at the apothecary?). This game has a huge scope. It's got so much stuff to figure out and play around with. Even just the amount of NPCs to befriend/marry is crazy. I absolutely love it. The use of the different stats you have for so many different things is pretty neat. The NPCs even have stats that affect their quality of work if you hire them. There are many routes you can take and you don't have to do everything at once. There's a lot of waiting/time wasting as your progression is dependent on having children and basically taking over their bodies when you die. You build up their stats through their lives to have better stats in you next generation. Buying items from Mr. Fairweather speeds things up a bit, but I'm 68 hours in and still on my original character. I think this is something the devs should work on in the future.So, in conclusion: Yes, I recommend this game. The caveat to that is that you need to be okay with the game not being complete and still needing tweaking. The devs have not abandoned it and seem to be updating it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited when I heard that some of the Fable makers were developing a new game. I had to test the new game immediately and decided to support the makers by buying the early access version - and I was not disappointed.The game has a lovingly and fantastically designed world with an atmospheric soundtrack and the turn of the year. In addition, there is also an implemented annual cycle (daily routine of the NPC, festivals depending on the season, etc.).The NPCs are all individually designed and have unique character traits.The world is full of things that you can already discover now and offer you many game experiences and opportunities: buying your own business, side quest, building relationships.And all of this already in the early access version!Of course, there are still a few bugs here and there. ;) The developers are very lousy and keep bringing out updates with incredibly long changelogs. _childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is charming and deserves a lot of love for the years of effort that went into it. Sadly, I feel like a lot of it is still unbalanced, and a lot of development time has gone into sometimes relaxing and sometimes truly annoying minigames. The story feels empty; it takes a long time to build rep to get to the next stage, and your reward is a short line of dialogue and an item you might not use. Characters around the world have dialogue that very quickly loops over on itself. There are tons and tons of books laying around with paragraphs of sometimes-helpful sometimes-nonsensical content--content which I feel should have been put into dialogue, not walls of text that are easily ignored. Parts of Kynseed really make me laugh. Others make me groan and want to close the game. Example: "Finally ready to try your hand at marriage? Well, you have to start at the beginning of the week...which just passed! Oops! Looks like you'll have to wait 6 days. Try to remember come next week!" Many moments like this one that feel more like they're trying to stretch out content to last your character long enough to get to your next of kin. I'm trying really hard to be invested in this game I've been eagerly watching for years, but something is still...not quite right.If you're looking for another Stardew Valley, I don't think this is it. It feels closer to Moonlighter, or some other shop management sims. But man, if you like wearisome minigames, this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed sets out to do what Fable couldn't: a world where time actually does pass, people age, and you can make your mark on the world. Typically of Peter Molyneux's grandiose promises post-Bullfrog, Fable was unable to pull it off, with Fable 2 especially notable for forcing a nonsensical plot development through to cause the necessary years to pass so your character's family (if they had one) would have noticeably aged as promised in the previews.It's brilliant concept to have as part of a game, and one Kickstarter and a protracted Early Access period later, Kynseed's full release is finally here. It doesn't feel ready for the big time quite yet, unfortunately. As one of two newly adopted twin orphans, you start the game at the age of 13 on the farm of your adoptive "uncle". He gives you some tasks or errands every day as a tutorial to the game's many subsystems and functions. Perceptive players will immediately note that their twin sibling is literally named "Sibling", and speaks to you like a coworker rather than with any kind of familial warmth. Head into the nearby village to perform your first tasks, and you find that villagers may give an introductory spiel when you first meet them, only to lapse into canned and often inconsistent comments shared among them all. A villager who dislikes you may be openly unpleasant in greeting, but still accepts a gift (and really enjoys it) only to then bid you farewell with a surly "goodbye, I suppose". You come away feeling almost like they're animatronics, rather than the actual people their detailed profiles imply.This lack of punch to the writing extends to the seemingly endless quantity of books and proverbs that absolutely litter the landscape like the local bookmobile violently overturned on the highway. The writers are trying in vain to capture the same sub-Python humour and whimsy of Lionhead's games, except subtlety and clever wordplay are nowhere to be found: it's all teeth-gnashing rhymes, bland puns, and painfully obvious double entendres, with dollop of fourth-wall breaking comments and contemporary references ladled on top. It's clear what's meant to be funny, but you see it coming a mile away and it fails to surprise and delight you. Unpleasant to read, and with so much of it; yet read you must, as crucial hints and game functions are often explained within. Once you've done your tasks for the day, you're basically at a loose end. You can explore the corner of the world that's accessible during the prologue, and enjoy the increasingly tedious hunt for "World Stones" within each area, all of which must be found in order to remove the fog of war from the map. Most of your time is spent actually travelling between quest markers. Your run speed is quite slow given both the distances to be covered and how fast time passes, so you are well advised to ride the pig from your farm. You can do pretty much everything while mounted on the pig, including working the blacksmith's forge or watching the till in the shop, which makes me wonder why the devs didn't just increase the on-foot speed further.Work tasks like the forge or shop all involve their own minigame, which is a neat idea, e.g. chop ingredients and scrape them into a bowl when cooking. While this is fun, it is also completely unforgiving until you get to grips with the controls, and the game doesn't care that ingredients are hard for a new player to come by: screwed up? Too bad, they're gone, no do-overs. This especially hurts since some of the crafting stations are owned by NPCs who charge a fee *per item crafted* to use it. There is a help screen but it's literally just text, no guided tutorial, so it's down to trial and error off your own back, which again would be fair if not for the costs involved. The timers and fact you only get one item out of them, no matter what, push it out of the realm of Fantasy Life which didn't time you, and would start giving you the ability to build multiples as well as bonus items per minigame.If you try to engage with the NPCs, many will offer you mini-quests, and it soon becomes clear there are only three of them: "I lost item X at location Y", "Cook me a meal that includes ingredient X", and "I need you to bring me X number of item A and Y number of item B". I soon had a long list of people expecting meal and grocery deliveries, sometimes specifying items or recipes I didn't have access to yet. As a result, you get bored and restless for actual things to do. Apart from uncompletable errands and unprofitable crafting, all there is to do is bop around uncovering maps, finding yet more literature, and seeing which trees and bushes you're allowed to pick the fruit from so as to accumulate the 30 apples and 6 pears on some ungrateful NPC's shopping list. Oh, and fishing, every cozy game needs a fishing game. You are not allowed to know about, or work toward, any other goals during the prologue.For me, the prologue took just over five hours, or two and a half of my evenings where I have time to sit down and game (you can't save anywhere you like, by the way, so nuts to you, people with families or limited time). I was playing more out of a sense of obligation to see it through than due to any enjoyment of the gameplay or investment in the storyline. I finally reached the major story point which sees you transition to adulthood, and now the world was completely open to me to explore and do what I wished. The main quest wanted me to do yet more running around fetching things, and quite honestly, I had long since stopped caring. I've seen comments saying the game really opens up and the wait is worth it, etc etc... I couldn't muster the enthusiasm any more, the journey to get this far had poisoned the well and spoiled its own great first impression. As I tromped along piggyback to yet another quest marker, I was thinking about Stardew Valley, with its plethora of activities, charming and memorable characters, and fact you can get started on stuff and see tangible results pretty much immediately.All those books that are essentially instruction manuals for game functions, why aren't these also interactive in-game tasks to give us more to do during the very thin prologue? I had no idea about the whistle that lets you summon and give orders to animals, for instance, because my eyes had glazed over after the innumerable preceding books that only served to tell a few dopey jokes or meaningless lore, and so had ended up ignoring it until spotting it by chance being mentioned in the forum. The whole Goddess Day offering/buff thing is also supremely detailed and overwrought for something you're expected to just sit and read even though it has no effect yet (most of them affect systems you haven't heard of yet since they don't come into play until later). I had quests which were literally impossible: either the NPC would not accept the item, or they did, but were back in the same spot the next day, acting like it had never happened and giving me the same instructions to do it all again.I realize this is a review of the prologue more than anything, but feel it's fair warning that it is a substantial hurdle that must be overcome to access to whatever actual game awaits beyond. I respect the developers for their bravery in making it lengthy: too many games expect us to care about a character's past that we either didn't experience or were rushed though (Fallout 3 had complaints about the Vault 101 opener's length). That doesn't excuse how tedious and off-putting it's proving to be, nor the fact that the game has been a long time coming and yet this was not apparent from pre-release playtesting. It has driven me back to Stardew Valley. I'll probably revisit Kynseed once some post-release updates are done, but for now, I can't recommend it.The best farming/marriage game remains Stardew Valley. The gold standard for a genuinely funny action RPG with many jobs and crafting is Fantasy Life on 3DS.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  As other reviews also already stated, there are many problems with the game sadly. There are many – many - many things to do, sadly most of them generic and boring. With this many things progression is too slow, and I was curious how I would feel with the whole ‘having an heir’ mechanic, but I was unable to progress that far. I really did want to like it, as I am a huge fan of farming games, starting from the 1st farming game I played which was the Harvest Moon: Back to Nature on PS1. I dont think the core game can actually be fixed, it is as it is now, but I hope this review will help decide if this game is for you or not.   Without further delay, here are the parts that build up the game and my personal problems with them:   Farm, farming and materials: in this game farming is so basic, I wouldn’t even call it farming, especially after you have the talent that auto-waters the crops after the 1st time. The plots are predetermined and you can’t change the layout, and don’t have any way to upgrade or customize your farm. There are plenty of materials, but a lot of them have no reliable way to get them (like mint, which you need for the cooking skill upgrade).  Animals: there is not much you can do with animals either, if you buy chickens, they don’t even have a designated building, they just stay in the middle of your farm and lay eggs. Pigs and sheep make fertilizer which could be a nice addition to farming, if farming was actually a thing. Riding them is another option, but at the start of the game you can choose the key that opens a fast travel option which is way better, unless you prefer to walk (or ride a pig/sheep). After you unlock certain areas, you can buy seeds that lets you grow chicken- and piggy- meat, that I found a way better and easier source of protein. There is also the cow with infinite milk. So animal handling is also pretty basic.  Crafting: all the crafting mechanics in the game have the same issue. They are pretty well thought out, and really fun at 1st. But as you make 10, then 50, then a 100 swords/ soups/ whatever else, it loses the interesting factor and just becomes a chore. This I feel could actually be fixed if at a certain point crafting things would become easier, as in life when you do something constantly you get better, and you dont need a few generations for it, sometimes a few days of constant repetition is enough. Yes you can order items, but at the start it takes too long for the items to arrive, and as these shops work, you could have infinite stock and it still wouldnt be enough. It is not a good feeling, nor a good design decision, if people keep coming one after another, demanding buckets for example and you have none and you keep turning them away. An easy fix would be, if people only come and order the items they need, and leave the ‘need for having a stock of items’ mechanic for the general store.  Shops: you can buy them and run them yourself (and basically do nothing else), or hire staff to do it for you, but the only way you are going to make real profit is if you run them yourself. I have seen people turn away from my blacksmithing shop, because the person I hired, who was actually running it before me didn’t handle customers quick enough. Also hired staff dont get skill levels quick enough either, they where working for almost a year with no increase in talent. Not to mention the guy who was the blacksmith before, had 0 talent to begin with and his name is even Jeremie SMITH, I mean...  NPCs, relationships and marriage: I personally was unable to care for any of the NPCs. They seem too generic, with no interesting conversations. Stardew Walley and Harvest Moon had portraits for the characters which made them more relatable, but they also had more fleshed out characters to begin with. I do understand where they tried to go with this, but it also became bland instead of something good. For marriage all you need is to get to 3 hearths, then you need to present a white rose (this is not writen anywhere btw, I was still going on dates waiting for a prompt or anything that I can now propose), then starts a quest. Make sure there is a map where charmweed is available to harvest before you propose, because having several in your inventory doesnt count, the quest fails and you have to start over the whole process, and you can only propose on Monday.  Fishing: compared to all the other tasks and crafting minigames, this one is the least imaginative, and also very boring. The better fish are nearly impossible to catch because they don’t bite, just swim around. It is not fun at all, just a time waste. I like fishing in a lot of other games, but this one is not good at all.  Combat: this I liked, you can benefit from having better gear and getting ready with food and potions, but also depends on how skilled you are. You can choose from 3 forests, which is basically the general difficulty and you can increase it by going deeper into the respective forests.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit for developer response:Appreciate the response, and may change my review (original below) when there is a road map accessible from the store page. Happy to give more specific feedback on items somewhere else, if there is such a mechanism in place beyond Steam reviews. I do want to note however that I had wishlisted this game for years waiting for a polished release, and this is technically no longer in early access. I didn't want to play through a game like this in an Early Access state (and is one of the reasons I have not yet purchased "My Time in Sandrock") because they can be quite time consuming, and often the story is spoiled on a second or third play through when the game is "done".I understand you are doing something different, but I think your difference maker is the generational aspect of the game. It's like the persistence mechanic in many rogue likes (or should be, as I have read the bonuses are not great, and I can see that reflected in the gifts you get from the rabbit fae, as many of them I simply don't see the need for or think warrant spending years of my life on) and I think that is a brilliant idea. However player expectation is important, and if you are deviating from it you need to make the systems clear either by outright telling you or by clearly guiding them down it as a central theme. In example...If you give me a farm house, a base of operations if you will, then I sort of expect to use that resource to do my farming and crafting. I am fine with us running around efficiently teleporting from spot to spot to harvest a region, but that devalues your actual farm to just another set of plots (and probably the least useful of them), and kind of sets the player up for an "Oh man have I been playing this wrong". I do more work at "The Twanging Gardens" (A great, non-innuendo joke which probably makes me appreciate it all the more) than I do at my farm. It's unfortunate that this character was introduced as a "Fruity" fellow that was going to grope me in his house or if I didn't stay on my toes. I think you need to watch yourself with this, you do paint everyone as pretty gropey, but it's a problematic trope for gay men in media and I know I am out of my element talking as a CIS white man but I think it's well documented and discussed online. If the commentary is some of the people in your town are homophobic and wrongly accusing this man it really doesn't play out enough to make the commentary... commentary. One of the first characters you meet is gay, and openly talks about grabbing people in front of a 13 year old. I get "kids these days" are introduced to sexual themes very early but I am still not sure it is appropriate for them to be talked too so unfiltered as the norm WITHIN the game world. I am going to guess this is because there isn't special dialogue for you when you are young, but this is a problem with the "aggressive horniness" of the writing.Original Review:The best thing I can say about this game is it's a unique experience. It feels like the vision of the developers, unfortunately the developers do not seem to understand what makes a game fun and when perhaps their own preferences and desires aren't either marketable or enjoyable.Pros:- The music is phenomenal, whether delivering subtle nods to past great video game music or just comfortable country tones. A+ experience.- The art is stylized consistently and interesting. The character faces are about the only area that falls short. Some of the important characters are great, but so many of the other ones are a pretty ugly and messy.- I actually enjoy the limited farming plots and spices. This game plays like a time management game more than a farming sim. Watering crops is almost removed entirely by a single perk that is quite easy to get. The movement perks are by far some of the most important, while I find many of the others completely lackluster. Using the rootways and goddess statues correctly really starts to open up some possibilities of efficiently getting the simple stuff out of the way for the more complex undertakings. The game doesn't communicate this though, it let's you stumble into it by finding out you can just sow crops wherever you want, which makes very little sense from a player expectation point of view. This is a big problem with the game in ignoring your expectations or convention for a uniqueness with little payoff. It's often different for difference's sakeCons:- It doesn't care about your expectations of a farming sim, and tries aggressively to be different without communicating such. Your actual farm is probably the least important spot, where I spend the least time.- The game is very slow other than farming and gathering. Marriage alone is an elaborate week long ritual. Increasing rep with people is important and can be quite slow early on.- There are very few interesting well written characters, which makes the choice of partners seem fairly arbitrary and lack punch.- The writing is aggressively horny and tiresome. One review said it was "british" and "like monty python" and this is rubbish. I am tired of people labeling tiresome humor as dry humor. The game even has a book in it about someone complaining about the "dirty" humor but then slides in with "but keep up the innuendo!". It's like they understand they are bad at this but instead of working on it they just said screw the criticism lets stick with it.- I get that the game is about kids but... give it a rest guys. Honestly some of this story gives me "Uncle touchies puzzle basement" vibes.- The mini games are brutally tiresome and unrewarding. I'd like to fill my store with pies or jams or what not but there is no way I am going to do the puzzle 30 times to stock up. I am decent at twitch stuff so I can do most of the stuff, but for the general audience of a farming sim I think it's way too difficult. This criticism is also wide spread and it is clear the developers are ignoring it as well. They have a vision and they'll be damned if you like it or not.- Tons of stuff seems pointless or arbitrary. I don't know why I would spend any time on some of the aspects of this game like animals for instance. Many aspects are just tedious and shallow with little reward.- The whole story is interesting, but in a strange way. I don't like the goddesses and the game seems to both say you should and you shouldn't. Your sister and the rabbit fae make good points but the game just sort of drops them and has you forge on with the goddesses, your sister even has an about face right when I am inclined to agree with her. l haven't experienced the whole thing, so perhaps there will be some player agency here, but I somehow doubt it.I'm going to keep playing, but in no way would I recommend someone to purchase this game. If you are bored and want to witness some strangeness with a delightful paint-job, dive in, but be forewarned it's tedious and confusing and unnecessarily complex to get into the unique aspects of the game. Perhaps if the devs seem to be more interested in addressing some of the criticism out there I'll be inclined to change my review but they seem to be intent on delivering their vision.I also find a reliance on Discord for community is a huge red flag. These communities are often very cliquish sound chambers rather than meaningful player engagement.

_childDocuments_.review: You have scrolled down here because... well... you're not sure whether or not it's worth it, right?So you look at the screenshots, watch the trailers, reviews here, on youtube, maybe check out a let's play video or two just to get a feel for what the game offers, correct?What those things are unable to convey, however, is the actual 'feel' for the game, my review included.So essentially any point I try to make is pretty much moot......BUT.......what I CAN tell you is that, after only 46 minutes my verdict is 'yes! Buy it!'. It's charming, nostalgic, beautiful, relaxing, and fun. Now, in my advanced age of thirty-two years, I can't relate to what is hip these days, with your Fortnite's and your Apex Legends-es, or trendy new-fangled AR Pokemon games on hip phones. But I have played a fair few games in my life, and dabble in indie development as a 3D environment artist, so I might just know enough to realize when developers are passionate about what they're creating......and it absolutely shows. It was a toss up between Stardew Valley and Kynseed around the same price for me. But somehow the more water-colour type art style, multi-generational aspect, and potential for a more well-rounded game spanning several genres spoke to me more when it came to Kynseed. It's absolutely fantastic so far, and I can't wait to see what direction the devs take with it!Well worth it in my opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;Hard pass, regret buying.Maybe some day I'll revisit.I didn't have fun once in an hour of playing.There are better games in this genre.I played for an hour and did not experience anything reminiscent of fun. The beginning of the game is very sloppily strung together and they just have you run what feel like VERY long distances to do fetch quests that don't really feel satisfying or teach you how to play the game. You have to find stones to activate your map but it feels very tedious and frustrating that even the beginning areas don't have maps. It's a farming sim but you have to wait until the third day to even have any mention of seeds. The tutorial both feels exhausting and uninformative.One of my hardest criticisms of the game design is they attempt a tutorial but it is so poorly organized and honestly just not fun, that it dissuades me from investing time into it when I could just play a more solid title in the genre like Stardew or Graveyard Keeper.In an hour of the game I managed to harvest a bunch of random plants with little concept of what to do with them, run around on a pig that steers like a car on ice, did not see combat ONCE (Which was a huge selling point of the game), and honestly I was just left waiting to have fun the entire time I played it, without enjoying anything but the art style itself.I could not recommend this game less. It's an example of a really pretty game with really bad game design and too ambitious of a project for a novice studio. They should have really simplified the concept and play-tested it more thoroughly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gorgeous, well-written, atmospheric and original. It is also, unfortunately, unfinished. I've waited two years and it is bizarre to me that the core feature of this game--the cycling through generations in both your dynasty and the world--remains barely functional. Your character just vanishes when you move to the next generation, and no-one reacts. Not even your own family. Your spouse just pops out of existence too. This is extremely jarring, yet is largely unacknowledged as an issue. Instead work is being done on a DLC that expands world features. Great, of course, but the core gameplay is not finished! I really wanted to love this game. I do, largely, love it. But I cannot recommend. Just play Wildermyth.

_childDocuments_.review: --- Disclaimer --- This is obviously early access AND freshly early access. Thigns can change and my vote of up or down may change with it.Kynseed is an interesting game so far, you take on the role of either an adopted son or an adopted daughter and run around doing stuff around a settlement. It has a great deal of Harvest Moon/Rune Factory/Stardew Valley feel right off the bat. However, it seems to have a depth underneath the surface as you explore. Crafting is rather interesting, and the quest and chore system is pretty interesting too. Not everything is in yet (The Devs place signs to tell you some of their plans in game while you explore) so some systems will yet to be experienced.Overall I think this is a very powerful addition to the genre of day-in-the-life games and will probably surpass the ones I mentioned previously when it's done. I see quite a lot of potential for a good game in this wrapper, but it's rather early in development so who knows what we will get.I'll give it a thumbs up because nothing about the game made me shudder, except the appearances of some of the characters in game. Also, the music was excellent! Shouts out to the musician.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that this game is not without it's faults. It's not until long after the tutorial when you begin to fully grasp the mechanics of the game that it truly begins to shine. The story is also a huge selling point for this game and once you reach the end of the tutorial it really hooks you so if you do pick it up and think it's not for you try to make it past the tutorial which lasts 14 in game days.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very difficult to describe this game without it sounding just like a Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon clone, but as someone who's spent hundreds of hours on those games I can confidently tell you that Kynseed is a very unique experience.  In Kynseed you won't grow into an agricultural powerhouse making millions per month off of your factory farm.  Instead you'll spend time learning how to bake pies well, figuring out how to help your modest businesses stand on their own two legs, exploring a fairy-enchanted world full of innuendos, dark secrets, and heart-wrenching surprises, and ultimately choosing for yourself exactly how you want to fit into the world's little ecosystem.It's not perfectly polished and in some areas it's lacking, but if you're looking for a fresh perspective on Farming Sims or Life Sims then you could happily sink a few long weekends into this title.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who recently bought and played through Fable 3 (wish I snagged 2 while I had the chance!) and acquired a copy of Black & White 2, I can say quite happily that this is good ole Lion's Gate humor in a nice Indie package.  Do I wish it was a little more complete before Early Access?  Sure, but I don't mind picking up what will hopefully be an amazing game for ten bucks.  The beginning feels a little rushed, days are short, tasks are many, and there isn't much time to idle-chat with NPCs, but I'm sure that's one of the things that will be ironed out soon.  But it's charming, with the same exaggerated uncanny character design the Fables had, and nice little details to help you along.I have high hopes for this.  Let's just hope that over-promised features were a symptom of the corporation.  (And knowing EA, it was.)

_childDocuments_.review: The only real gripe i have with Kynseed is that there is no definitive ending, Granted thats a personal gripe and why i decided to stop playing when i did but that doesns't mean that theirs no point when you'll think that you've done everything there is to do. From the start of the game to the "ending", or the point in which you've decided you've done everything there is to do is gonna take time to reach that stage, mostly because of how winded the intro is. You'll either feel overwhelmed or over joyed, like i was, when you realize how much content there is to actually do. From the mix of the western style RPG mechanics and the farming and management systems all the way to the dungeon delving aspects.The world and setting you find yourself in is kenned from old folk and fairy tales or from some of the classic fantasy stories like Willow or Never Ending Story. In the land of Quill you'll start your adventure with either your brother or your sister as two siblings living with an old women living in a shoe until one day your uncle, Uncle bill, takes you back home to his farm where you'll be given different tasks each day, feeding the pigs, filling the troth, milking the cows and so on and so forth. Eventually, while at your new home you start having dark and ominous dreams in which lies the theme of your story.Through the prolog, which is quite a long prolog, You'll be taught the different mechanics and the lay outs of what Kynseed has in store. You'll be sent on different tasks from your Uncle, Uncle Bill while you go out and meet the residence of Quill where you can obtain different friendships, relationships and eventually marriage and children once you grow up and yes, Growing up and starting your own family or a shop is just a few of the things you can do once you move past the prolog. The the amount of interesting characters you can develop relationships with is where this game really shines. Every character ive run into has had their own unique personality that are all, typically, very witty and funny.One of my favorite things about Kynseed is the amount of details there are in the environment, The Pixel art is absolutely stellar and really helps keeps the player wanting to explore more. Not to mention how soothing the soundtrack is. Theirs a lot of fun to be had in Kynseed, My only real gripe i have is how long the prolog takes but to be fair their is alot of different mechanics to learn so its fair that the prolong is so long. If you're someone who looks to have a definitive ending for your games, It doesn't seem that Kynseed has that.The combat is where Kynseed really surprised me. A turn based style that easy to learn but takes time and planning to master. Combat is only introduced while in one of the three dungeons where you start off by choosing your loadout, Which you can craft yourself, like your weapon for example that camp be smelted and made by blacksmithing yourself and your campfire meal which can also all be crafted. I was quite surprised to see how in-depth that combat is but to be fair, all the system in Kynseed act as intricate and involved as the combat doesKynseed can feel overwhelming at times so my best advice is to not skip the tutorials, even if you think you know how to play cause you've played Stardew Valley. Think of the two games as apples and oranges, Yes they're both fruit but they're drastically different. Kynseed stayed in Early Access for 5 or so years and from what ive played, they spent every second of those years making Kynseed one of the best Life Sims on the market. My personal favorite thing isn't the intricate systems or the amazing pixel art but instead its all the charming characters. I get major Fable vibes when trying to swoon over a blonde pixel lady or when running my own shop. An absolute gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an early access backer for Kynseed; and I can say without a doubt it is a special gem of a game. Kynseed is a wonderful welcome into the Lifesim/RPG & Adventure game genre, with a wonderful and talented team behind it. Their experience and passion show quite clearly and is reflected throughout every inch of the game, down to the little things. The art direction is beautiful and rich with colors showcased well in varying environments in the pixel art style. Pixelcount studios had a vision coming in, and have delivered on it so far with every update to the game, all leading up to the release of the 1.0 official launch soon. They've engaged with us as a community all throughout the process and have been very open with listening to their players and communicating.Kynseed puts it's own wonderful touches on the multiple genres it entails to create a rather unique experience in a similar space we're quite familiar with. Start a family, have a farm, run some shops, explore the world and even make your way through dungeons, something we've all seen before but not in the Kynseed way. From it's art and color palette, to it's music and game design Kynseed is a refreshing breath of fresh air in this space. Most interesting of all to me was the combat system, which has you in a sort of familiar turn based style with a twist that keeps it very engaging and most of all fun!I'd certainly buy this game now if you're on the fence as the full release is right around the corner, less than a month away at the time of this review, with more and more updates planned well into the future as support won't cease at launch. Even with the increased price tag I'd encourage anyone curious to dive in, and tell a friend too. I don't usually leave reviews and I'm not that skilled at them but felt compelled to say something about this fantastic game!

_childDocuments_.review: Having read the reviews and the developers (humorous) intro note, I expected the game to be much more unplayable than it is. It does take a while to explore the map and I hope that in future updates we might get a little key to where the characters live as there are so many of them.  I came to this game looking for a game to get addicted (in a similar way to Stardew Valley) and I'm not disappointed. Can't wait to play the final product!

Also the feeling that time, rather than any arbitrary "energy" as the limiting resource is a great, albeit stressful, mechanic. Also be prepared for more puns than I have ever seen stuffed into an alpha.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Game. Basically a mix of what the Fable games originally wanted to be, before hardware limitations reigned them in, and Stardew Valley. It then proceeds to get a fun kind of weird while maintaining the original farm-sim aesthetic by introducing some eastern European occultism.Great game for the price range, and definitely worth sinking a few hours into.When looking at this game, one should be thinking Pixel-art Fable with an emphasis on business empire management, rather than Stardew Valley-esque Farm sim.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is on the cusp of greatness but it comes with two very big caveats for it:1: You have to be someone that's good at setting your own goals within the broad objectives given and work towards them because there is a TON of breadth and progression, but not a lot of narrative drive for those wanting a more storied experience.2: while it is out of early access, it is very much not still finished as the story currently in the game is called chapter 1, with chapter 2 work progressing once some quality improvement is done.You can really feel the evolution of some concepts from the classic Fable games all throughout this.  The art direction is fantastic, there's a lot to learn and explore, there's lore to find hidden all over, and it carries some of that lowbrow humor the old franchise is known for.  The key thing though that may disappoint some if not made aware of upon entry though is this is NOT Stardew Valley (nor is it really trying to be), this is NOT wholly a spiritual successor to Fable, (and for good measure) this is NOT The Sims.  You will see strands of DNA pulled from the direction of all of these, but with it all it's really trying to blaze some innovative trails with it.  In the end it is doing some really cool design concepts that are about 80% there, but could use some more polish passes and development which the devs seem to be very active in working in as well as taking any and all feedback to consideration on further direction.  If you're like me and like your game worlds to let you loose and carve your own adventures and direction to end goals, then there's already an amazing time here with a TON of gameplay time.  If you're looking for a more linear and narrative-heavy experience though, this likely won't be a thumbs up for you at least in its current state.  At the $25USD price point though, it's pretty hard to go wrong if at least to try and support a team doing something incredibly ambitious in gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game! I'm so shocked it has negative reviews, but I understand that everyone has different likes and dislikes. I found the characters to be pretty interesting! I read another review where someone said the characters were lacking depth, but I honestly can't see how anyone can say that. I got excited increasing friend lvls to learn more about them. The concept of this game is just so unique, but you need to invest some time in it. I recommend this game to almost everyone! I even bought it for a few people so they can try it. I think I saw another review about the concept of time being too fast, but that's kind of what the whole game is about? I don't want to give anything away, but time/death/old age, it's a part of the game. Time management is part of the game. I think the creator did a great job of mixing the morbid and adorable. I love all the little lore and things you can find. It's really immersive. I couldn't put it down when I first started playing. I think I have 85ish hours on record and there is still SO much to do!!Don't let the negative reviews dissuade you, this is an amazing game, with adorable graphics, creepy lore, interesting characters, fun mini games, mining, farming, fishing, romancing, festivals, shopkeeping. _childDocuments_.review: is a sandbox simulation game that is very relaxing in nature. Please keep in mind that the game is nowhere close to completion yet. There are many more features that the developers are looking to add. Even still, there is plenty to do in the current version of Early Access.The most important thing for you to do is going around and collecting things. You have to also talk to people, run errands, feed animals, catch fish, farm, etc. You will have daily tasks as well but it's okay not to finish them.The map is quite large and you will reveal extra portions of the map by finding map stones.According to the store page as well as the initial launch screen, the future plans include aging with time, for yourself, for the people and pets around you. So look for that in future updates. After living a whole life and dying, you will be return as a newborn child. I think you will have to play a long time to see that, but a very cool feature indeed. I look forward to seeing this being implemented in the future.The game runs in day-night cycles, and you will need to sleep when it gets dark. Even if you don't want to go to sleep, the game will force you to do that. I have seen this in other similar games, so no surprise there.The game saves automatically, so you don't have to worry about losing progress.There are no achievements yet, and I do hope that they will be added.The graphics are so beautiful, everything looks so cute. It's a nice way to use pixel artwork, for sure.Everything is very relaxing, I enjoy it.Controller is fully functional here in this game. You can also play with a keyboard and mouse.It's definitely fairly priced for the things you can do currently in this very cute game. I look forward to the additional content as well. is a sandbox simulation game that is very much in Early Access and the developers acknowledge that from the beginning when you start playing. There is a lot of things to do already and more to come. The game is currently missing a nice tutorial, only a few simple button-oriented function in the beginning. So I was struggling a bit in terms of knowing what to do for a little while and just walking around aimlessly. I hope there is a regimented tutorial put in place soon to get the player more comfortable with the gameplay.The controls on the controller takes some time to get used to, for now, I find that the keyboard controls are a bit easier to grasp.For people who really enjoy games like  and , you will definitely want to get in this game early, especially if you want to help out the developers, to contribute thoughts and ideas, and to be a part of its growth and development.It's very promising indeed, and the planned features do seem like it will be a game that stands not only among its peers, but be outstanding as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bought the game during early access about 4 or 5 years ago and had been following the development like a hawk because I was so excited to be able to play it one day. After putting over 35 hours into this game after full release, I can honestly say that it feels really shallow as a whole.On the surface it seems like a really well thought-out game with plenty to do all of the time, but just because it touches on lots of different types of gameplay doesn't mean that there's any depth to those areas. Farming consists of planting things over and over again with no way to expand or improve your farm, cooking is really unbalanced with the same few mindless mini-games producing widely different star ratings depending on what type of food you're making, fishing is just casting a rod and waiting endlessly for something to bite...I was truly so excited for this game and although I don't have a bad time playing it, I'm not exactly having a great time either. It really sucks to say, especially as somebody who is largely known to enjoy 'boring' games, but there just isn't much here to keep my attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Last play this in 2022? did't recommend it at that time, ton's of bugs and missing feature. The world is pretty big, you won't have enough time to manage your animals / crops.- Cannot hire helper to manage your farm. Which is weird since you can hire staff for your shops.- Have a few towns or village, but most of them are pretty much the same set up (Tavern, Smithy, Clinic and general stores). The only different is the some village have pig auction/race and some for Chicken and other animal probably, yet to unlock every map so far.- Only 10 hot keys, no rotating of hot keys set up (Press shift or Tab in other games to rotate another set of hotkeys) or maybe i haven figure it out? With your axe, shovel and whatnot personal equipment, you would have left with only 1 or 2 for other stuff and this game have quite a lot of things to use.Kynseed has a pretty unique world to explore which you probably won't see in other games, even thought there's still feature that i wish to see but not yet implemented. _childDocuments_.review: This little project I decided to back a few years ago has grown into a massively charming world that has blown me away with its unique character and overall love that the developers have put into this game. If you want a farming sim that has an unique charm to it, a deep European-based folktale lore that isn't afraid to become eerie and a tad scary, and the ability to play through the different generations of your family; I would recommend playing this game. It is still in Early Access at the time of this review, but even then I have fallen in love with the project I have watched grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. It's fun and interesting. It's based on some really cool folklore. They keep adding great new features in updates which keeps things fun. _childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is a very charming, fun, relaxing game with a lot of depth. You can tell that a lot of love went into this game. I set it aside during EA and picked it back up upon release to find that it had come a long way. It's been in great shape since then and seems only to be getting better with new content and major systems incoming.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not finished, but I'm still having a lot of fun. The notes you find around the world are both helpful and hilarious. _childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: The story and the town are interesting, and I find the fae/folklore backdrop to be the right balance of fun and slightly creepy! Most of all I really like the ageing concept of this game, with having your character grow older and eventually carry on as the next generation. This particular aspect was something I was looking for in a farming/life sim, and as a Harvest Moon Friends of Mineral Town veteran, it sure does get boring playing the same life with the same villagers for 50 in game years without anything ever changing! I'm looking forward to more content as the game gets finished and polished, but even as it is currently, it is still loads of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I waited until it was fully released before getting too far in and it's an amazing premise so far! I'm excited to see where else this takes me and what other updates the team comes out with. There are a lot of notes but I quite enjoy them as they're cute and very fae-like with their little riddles and fourth wall-breaking. The link to the wiki is very helpful, I've used it a few times already and the F3 help function is pretty useful as well. The pacing is a lot better than what it used to be,  I used to feel simultaneously bored and overwhelmed all at once as the pacing was a little too quick but there was also not a lot of original quests happening at once so it got a bit much and a bit stale too quickly. Now, I think it's great! The amount of side quests the NPCs give you can be hard to keep track of though so perhaps if you could limit it to one or two types of quests per NPC or maybe make an easier way to manage all the quests.I also find that there doesn't feel like a lot of time in the day to get much done and I'm always passing out mid-quest. I'm looking forward to the community growing and where else the devs take this game, it's such a fun twist on the farming/dating sim type and it's such a fantastic original idea!
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Still in development so take that in mind when judging it, but even in this rough state the visuals are gorgeous and the gameplay features and mechanics feel refined.
