Expect for an experience similar to games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, but still unique and new, with a much more mature sense of humor and enviroment.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game that immerses you so quickly into the story line that you don't even realize the amount of hours that have passed. Love it! Love the music! Love the colors and art! Love the animations! I even love all the small glitches.I would love it even more if the quest list page was easier to follow, it seems a bit rough around the edges and i can't really keep track of all of them even if the NPCs tell you that you have to give them something.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: An unfinished, more fantastical version of Stardew Valley, with some strange design choices.Cons- Fishing is confusing and somehow both too complicated and too simple. If you cast directly onto a fish, they get caught and can be reeled in quickly. If you cast near them, they run away. Some fish swim deeper than others, but it is unclear how this mechanic works, other than you cannot affect them when they are deep, unless you cast near them, then they can swim away or disappear entirely by going even deeper. Thus, all you want to do is cast directly onto them to get them immediately. However, plenty of the locations for casting are way too far away from the fish. Also, some of the times you cast onto the water, it bounces off of nearby land because whoever designed the water areas didn't correctly draw the lines so while the fish might be swimming, your rod can't cast there. - The game is designed to be extremely grindy. For example, all of your tools have a mastery level connected with them, with each level requiring more usage before you can get to the next. I must have caught damn near 1000 fish and I am only about midway through the craftsman tier of the fishing rod, with another 6 tiers to go. For swords, you probably have to kill even more creatures. There is no indication of what experience each thing you do with these items gets you towards your progress, or whether higher value items get you more experience.- The game just doesn't feel alive. The characters walking around are not interesting, with no obvious personality. This is likely because there are too many of them and they don't actually say much of anything. Also, you can buy every shop in the game, so it makes it less like you are part of a community and more like the people are your employees. A number of them in one town all hate you, and I haven't progressed enough in the story to figure out why.- Ranged attacks seem pointless.- There is no viable way to make lots of money outside of owning shops. Farming is out because you have very few plots and it is extremely tedious. If you just fish a lot or craft a lot, you will be spending hours for very little gain. And most shops run out of money before you have a chance to sell all of the loot you've obtained.Pros- The combat system is fun, honestly. I like that it is easy to grasp but difficult to master. I died a few times, but I don't know what the consequences of using up all of your "chances" in a combat area actually are. Despite the above point about ranged attacks, I liked the combat system. The only concern I have is that it won't be any good after you have fought all of the monster types.- The game is very pretty.- The music is great as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I can see that the developers put some thought into mechanics, but what makes or breaks farmings sims a-la Harvest Moon for me is characters and atmosphere. Characters here are one-dimensional at best, and the story, well, got the same tonal backlash as most horror films about rural cults, Wicker Man, Midsommar and such. You've got creepy Paleotlitic Venera Goddeses which curse you if you don't offer them sacrifices, . All and all — this is  something I want from my relaxing farm sims. Uninstalled, but, sadly, can't refund, was an EA buyer. Oh well, that'll teach me not to buy anything from devs again.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, I REALLY want to. But it's frustrating and both underwhelming / overwhelming imo. There's "so much to do" but nothing to do at the same time other than stardew-style fetch quests. The cooking / crafting aspects specifically, when seeing them on the trailer, looks amazing. I thought It added a very unique and nice little touch to the game, a lil bit of cooking mama throw back + moonlighter w the combat and shopkeeping; BUT it is hard for no reason. You don't get a "practice" round, no tutorial, nada when crafting anything in the game other than the bucket. Whether it's a bucket, food, medicine (it's all set up cooking-mama-esque). So you go in blind, inevitably fail within seconds (like when making a sandwich and baking the bread), then lose ALL the ingredients and are stuck confused as to what happened. I HATE this. Why is there no tutorial ?? No way to practice? No quick little video guide? Just very confusing, WRITTEN instructions if you go into the settings and LOOK for them outside of the crafting station you're at.This really sucks because the game is beautiful, has so much detail, and has such an amazing *idea* of a game but executed it soooo poorly. So so poorly.--Edit: "But there is a tutorial. HoPe ThiS HeLpS" and there's just one singular tutorial for making the bucket. No, that does not help when there are so many different types of crafting / mini-games other than pouring metal into the mold and whacking the blade. And no, written instructions aren't the best imo and shouldn't be the only form of "tutorial" you get when crafting a unique item / playing a different "mini-game" for the first time. Like at LEAST include some pictures in the written instructions lol.

_childDocuments_.review: The prologue absolutely blew me off my feet and out the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ window, but after that... _childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: What an excellent game. I've struggled with how RPG mechanics get implemented in most video games - there are ultimately very few that make what you're choosing to do mean anything but they still get the RPG tag b/c you chose a shotgun as your weapon, or you chose blue magic instead of red magic, or planted rhubarb instead of went fishing. Kynseed does make your decisions matter and it does it in a world that feels alive.It's made it pretty clear to me how difficult it can be to make a game that reflects the stats your character has. I've had it since alpha and have seen all the tweaking that goes into making all the different mechanics of the game be more or less difficult depending on how high a corresponding stat is.It did take a bit for me to wrap my head around the game, that might have also been all the alpha years, but here's the gist: play as your generational line (most of your stat improvement will come from going to the next generation) and accomplish feats to unlock better tools and skills and... no spoilers and I haven't finished the main story myself but you might be ultimately out to get a bunch of mystical beings who are causing a lot of mischief.I think the people who struggle to like the game are just going at it from the casual, farming sim view and want things that aren't really here. You shouldn't get attached to the iteration of your character, you shouldn't be looking to feel close to the villagers, or to your pets - everybody and everything dies and new ones come. You shouldn't be hoping to spend all your time cultivating a farm - you can do it, it just wouldn't be much fun. You also do not, at least not with any ease, become an all-powerful oligarch / god made flesh who has all the resources and is exceptional at everything. Keep your eyes on how things will impact you down the road and you'll be having a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is a really beautiful game with lovely music. Currently in early assess as I type this Kynseed shows a lot of promise of what it can become if the Dev's keep on the track they're on. There is a small learning curve as not everything is explained so you can discover how some things work on your own, I personally don't mind this. There is a huge list of interactive NPCs and I can only imagine this list of interesting somewhat insane characters will grow in time as new areas and villages are completed and added.Currently I have 12 -13 hours playtime and even though the game is far from complete there are still many things left for me to do. I have a personal rule of getting a £1:1 hr of game play ratio for my games and Kynseed has exceeded this so far with a reasonable price point of just over £7 it's well worth it if you like these types of games. Grinding / Farming games do tend to give you more gameplay for your money overall so that is to be kept in mind to if like me you wanted to kill some lockdown time like I did with a new game.Whilst it has a long way to go to complete with the likes of Stardew Valley I hope that the Dev's continue to make something spectacular as it's a lovely game to play and a fab stress buster if you want to loose yourself in something meaningless for awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game.A lot of things working pretty well. I think it's insane the amount of beauty and love that went into this game. It seems a bit overkill though. A bit sad that more people won't end up playing it. _childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has the potential to be one of the best of its genre the combat is really fun, the world is incredibly charming, it has a great sense of humor, and the visuals are great. The main problem I have is that it has left early access despite only having the first chapter of the game being available that is not to say the game is lacking in content hell I have been playing it for around 86 hours and am still not done with the first chapter however after learning that the game still doesn't have all the content I have decided to wait till everything is out before I continue the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and relaxing game. Like most the reviews it is tempting to compare it to other farm-sims like Stardew Valley. But it isn't Stardew, it isn't Harvest Moon, this is its own game within the same genre. The visuals are absolutely stunning and atmospheric, the music is pleasant, the gameplay loop is its own version of fetch/carry/gather/craft that absolutely satisfies. The minigames surprised me but instantly reminded me of Fantasy Life. I like them, but if you don't like minigames then this might not be the game for you. The NPCs are bland, which is my only gripe so far. However as a veteran of 'There is a festival tomorrow!' from Rune Factory games, the repeated dialog is nothing new either. I absolutely recommend this game in its current state and hope it gets a few updates to expand on what is already an amazing experience. The only caveat is if you don't like minigames and sandbox open ended play, don't get a game based on minigames and sandbox play.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in early access the date it was released. I played the prologue as it once was, and I was immediately intrigued. And now, all this time later, I've returned to the game in it's fully finished (though still receiving amazing updates) state. Just having experienced both its earlier days and what it is now, I can say the developers of Kynseed have worked so hard to make this an amazing game. The improvements to the UI, the changes to the story, the implementation of some of the important elements like the aging systems and romance systems, it's all be incredible to witness the growth of. The most recent update as of this review (the big build update) has added so many features that are so fun for those of us who like customization options. I think Kynseed is also a massive success in terms of the atmosphere it creates. It knows exactly what it is, what it wants to be, and delivers on that. The creepiness of the fae, the whimsy of this weird little world, they nail it completely with beautiful pixel art and music to complement it. I love this game and I can't wait to see what else it accomplishes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but there are just too many aspects that are unfinished. Or the shop management system where you can own 3 types of stores, 2 of them barely survives while 1 is just free money like no other. _childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is genuinely one of the sweetest, most charming games I've ever played in my life.I love the story, I love the game play, I love the goofy character designs... The beautiful realms you travel to, the spooky mobs you fight, the skills to master!Like all open-world games, it can feel a bit daunting at first, since you're thrusted into a world with new mechanics to learn and master, but the prologue to the game feels less like a tutorial and more like the beginning of a new life.Please, if you're on the fence about Kynseed, take the leap. _childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but I absolutely love this game, have been obsessed with it for a week or two now, I love everything ranging from the art style, the mini games, the NPCS and the events!I am so excited for the next update and future add-ons, I can tell the developers have worked really hard and have put a lot of effort into this project.Mad respect and love to the developers for making me addicted to this game, I haven't been so attached to a game in ages!Would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the potential to be as big a more-ish timesink as Stardew Valley. I already find myself thinking "one more day and then I'll go to bed" type thoughts. That said, as a veteran of games like Story of Seasons, My Time at Portia, etc (you know, a regular enjoyer of this genre), I have some constructive criticism,1. Sometimes when doing a task I legit can not find the target NPC. The map won't even hint about their location. So I run to the wiki for a hint of where they might be. Could this immersion-breaker be solved?2. The villagers all seem very... same-y. How can I choose which one to marry when the only difference seems to be name, age and sprite? Some more variety to personality would be awesome.3. It would have been nice to be able to name my twin. Calling her Robyn is fine, but I'd like to have chosen her name myself. Makes her more personal, and the game more immersive4. I tend to ignore my brounie, and have yet to be jinxed...It's still early access, and a WIP, so I can't provide feedback on much else. I haven't seen it yet, after all. Game seems to be going in a nice direction and is pretty. I look forward to future content :)

_childDocuments_.review: What makes this game addictive and great?You can own shopsYou can do farming You have a nice combat system, very funny and intuitiveThere are great mini games I love the tasks I love the lore and that you collect proverbsThe difference to e.g. stardew valley is the generation- and offering thing; characters are not that deep since you do time skips etc (don’t want to spoiler) and can have a lot of children and play more than one generation; there are no events with villagers, but there is a huge world to explore with a lot of secrets and lore. I played the demo in 2018 i guess and loved it, and I’m glad the developers took their time to create this gem of a game.Let me put it this way… you get something like potion permit with more diversity and less repetitive tasks, you get something like stardew valley with less depths in characters but more puns and quirkiness and combat, you get villagers that are as mean as the old animal crossings villagers (world world like) that open their heart very slowly but rewardingly. I think you have to be a certain age to fully understand that game and the tutorial isn’t that great; you’re somehow thrown into the world. But if you know the mechanics of farming and low key lifesim games, you will enjoy the possibilities that game gives you. And for me, as a bookseller IRL, I LOVE the shop systems! I mean it’s Christmas time and busy as hell at work but I still chose to own shops in that game. That’s how much FUN it is. And the music. Oh the music.  And the details in the maps. Damn I love that game.

_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Before I give my initial brief impression, for now, I want to point out one thing. I promised myself, I won't be purchasing titles in EA anymore, a good few months back, no matter how appealing or promising they appear to be.And then, Kynseed convinced me otherwise. The game at this point is a little more than in the middle of the alpha stage. And as someone with some background of putting ideas and concepts from the paper, into actual functional reality - a.k.a turning mockup into a functional prototype; I understand why this game took a good amount of time to pick up the pace.The game on paper, very well laid out and intriguingly put, should already give an indication of a huge undertaking. And that's not even thinking about the technical side of the game, simulation is one of the most difficult implementations in the IT world - if not the most difficult. And the devs of this game tackle with it head-on, pretty hardcore.And, I wouldn't even go for it, if they:a) Don't have extremely well and open communication with playersb) The transparent cycle of the development and responsiveness c) Though they have increased the difficulty of putting this project together with the decision to build up with players, rather than obstructing development in a more encapsulated process, it definitely is the big selling point.d) Last and probably most important reason that influenced my final decision, they know what they want with the game; they have a clear vision in which direction it is headed and they stay away from giving shady promises - they are very realistic.The conclusion is, I dig the concept of the game. And it may be influenced, or similar games are on the market, but it is a gem among them and distinctively unique - meaning it has mechanics and features in place, that makes it stand out on its own. However, the biggest reason I bought is that developers won my trust and ensured me they will deliver the promised product. How many promising games, have fallen the victim to plentiful empty promises and ambition? Exactly!.P.S At the end of the day, it comes down to you. The game as it is in the moment is far from being ready for a full-pledged playthrough. And if any conclusion is to be drawn from my review, it's that you are buying it now to support the product and devs. If that is not what you are looking for, my advice to you is to wait for more content to be released and then come back, by then many of us will revise our reviews to address the changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Now I have played for a good amount of time and I really love the art style and feel of the game thus far, but given the time I put into it I felt curious on what other people may have thought or think of the game. Now at the time I am writing this the game has mixed reviews and understandably too. So here are my thoughts on this game and things I've read so far (Spoilers or game mechanics talked about for those who want to keep themselves new to what is in the game)1. (Prologue) In the beginning of the game you're subjected to the idea of the game being continuous and that it goes on forever as you expand your family generations, As a person who loves character customization I felt a little off put by how little there was to design or personalize my character, but understood as that was not the point of the game but rather to carry on with whatever character you become in the future. And in my excitement I was thinking of all the possibilities that would come from the passage of time in a video game as fable was one of the only games to really touch on that subject in a fantasy video game world, but some curious points really came to mind when I really thought about it. How many sprites are there for the game to have a seeming loop with new people being born and people passing it would be a huge undertaking to make each character both personable and unique, so with that in mind I wanted to see where it would end up, and for the record I have been taking this game very slow and have been enjoying each and every moment I can to enjoy the new feeling of a fable like game again. But top close this long section off I am very intrigued and curious how the devs plan to tackle such a large idea and if they plan to expand the map further than what is already accessible ( I have read a sign that suggests that they will expand the map but do not know for sure whether or not it is planned to be a larger expansion or a single area expansion) But there are definite huge promises being made with the idea and prospect of the game alone. Good luck developers!2.(Mechanics) Some mechanics seem rather pointless at the moment or lack any real motivations to pursue doing them, for example it is quite commonly asked what the point of catching insects is, and I have found a book in game detailing that it may be used for a dye mechanic later on, which dyes to the best of my knowledge are just used to change hair color and can only be currently obtained by buying them from vendors or winning them in the in-game game show. And there isn't much customization or personalizing of your home to the best of my knowledge it is strictly unchangeable in any way. so making dyes would essentially just be to change the color of your hair which once you've found the color you'd like to stay with there would be no reason to seek out the mechanic, and with how little you need to change hair unless you are indecisive it is not costly to buy dyes from vendors or play the game show previously mentioned. With that being the biggest question for mechanics I will leave it there while I still am playing the game and experiencing the extent to which the other mechanics reach. 3. (The Mixed reviews) Now I got this game on a whim which actually worked out for me as I do love the game and all it has to present thus far, But I do not recommend doing that, take the time to read the reviews and see if it is something you would like to invest your time and money into. because commonly I see people have played the game a lot but lack a desired late game or continued story line with meaningful development which I do not know where my current standpoint in the story is at as I do not know how far I am into to story or really any indication of what in particular is happening and that may be due to my way of playing but I do find it a little off putting to not have some semblance of direction or idea of what I am to do. Now I am all for an experience of trial and error but after finally getting my feet on the ground I realized I essentially missed certain key points to get certain things done and felt as though I had failed in some way to accomplish what I had set out to do which some reviews I have read also relate to a degree. but take your time and choose what may be best for you.4. (My current thoughts) While I do love the idea and promise the game has, it is just that in its current state, a promise. and whether or not that promise is fulfilled is completely up to the developers, to which I would like to trust in that they make a final product I can enjoy and come back to time and time again, but to buy a game that has quite a few placeholder items, books, dialogue, can be a bit off putting no matter how many witty and clever jokes they may make with them. And a worrying point I have not reached myself yet but to have read about is that when you do move onto your heir to start the next life, you may lose your spouse and siblings if any were born along side your heir, whether they disappear completely or are written off as they passed away is concerning to the life you lived before that to build them up and create a new experience into the next life.But those are my thoughts and opinions thus far into the game and I hope that if you have purchased this game that you are enjoying it and if you haven't then I hope you consider taking the time to see if you should and I hope this wordy and lengthy review helped somewhat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another game where I wish I had a neutral option. On the one hand, this game had some unique aspects that were pleasantly surprising and lead me into sinking a good amount of time into it. But on the other hand, there was A LOT about it that was super shallow and left me thoroughly unsatisfied. Essentially in this game you own a farm where you can grow crops, raise animals, get married and start a family, own & run a shop (or multiple), fight in dungeons, participate in festivals, collect items, help out the townspeople by completing notice board tasks, and more. BUT the details within that were either really fun or really disappointing. I'll start with the disappointments - The townspeople all feel super shallow, which was a total bummer considering how many there are. Usually I have a hard time deciding who to marry in game because I like too many options but this one was the polar opposite for me because they were all just so 'meh'. Also, it doesn't really feel like there's a main story line. It feels like there's just a bunch of little side quests to keep you busy and to make money, but there's no main plot. You could look at it in the sense that you can do whatever you want in the game and forge your own path but for me, it was just unfulfilling. I just made a bunch of money and then got bored. The combat and mini games kept me busy for a while since I owned my own blacksmith shop but if I hadn't done that, I would have gotten bored with the game and stopped playing WAY sooner. One of the main points to this game is living long enough to live through your heir but I didn't get anywhere near the point of that happening and I probably would have ended up hating the game if I forced myself to do that.BUT there were also some aspects that I liked and some pleasant surprises that kept me going for as long as I did. The first thing that really slapped me in the face was how dark some of the story line is, especially the Summertide festival. That one hit me real hard. The rest of the game is upbeat and cheery but just with a little darkness sprinkled in which was a nice change of pace compared to the always bubbly farming sims that I've played. The other pleasant surprise for me was the crafting mini games. Each time you want to craft a weapon, cook a recipe, put together a medicine/cream, etc. you have to play a unique mini game. I personally enjoyed doing all of these, especially the blacksmith one (something about it was just so challenging but soothing, idk). BUT if you don't like mini games like that, you might find that to be tedious since you have to do it every single time you want to craft something and you can't craft in bulk. I also really enjoyed the combat. Usually with cozy games like this, you can just slash your way through everything but this was almost turn-by-turn combat which forced me to slow down and be more strategic, which I liked. I also thoroughly enjoyed the music in this game. It changes based on which area you're in (and sometimes even depending on which shop you're in) and it was all really beautiful. Overall, I had fun with it and I'd recommend it if you like a lot of mini games and that combat style, especially if it's on sale. But if you're looking for something with depth and a meaningful story line, I would look elsewhere unless they do some major updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is a wonderful game that's full of charm, humor, whimsy and even some dark and creepy things! First off, the game is beautiful to look at and to listen to. My favorite artwork so far has been the intense weather that the game has. When a storm is happening, its really happening! Pouring rain and the sound of the drops crashing onto the ground and against rocks and buildings... if I didn't have so much to do in game I'd be very tempted to just sit there and take it in.The prologue does take a bit of time and I can see how some people might not be able to get through it. It takes its time immersing the player into the world, its customs, lore and game mechanics. Its very much akin to how Fable was. Personally, I found the starting bit of the game to be relaxing and enjoyable. Once the prologue is over the game really opens up and its main story becomes evident. The player is free to go almost anywhere they wish right off the bat, to befriend or becomes enemies of anyone they wish, to choose what they want to spend their time doing. For example, I decided to seek a potential spouse among the populations of the towns outside of the starting town. The generational gameplay (animals and people, including you, age and die eventually but the player can continue as an heir) is one of the things that first drew me to this title, and I wanted to have a family (though you can adopt orphans if you would rather do that). Meanwhile, I saved every brass I had so I could buy the Goods Store and use that as my main job (something different from farming). Other players might buy the Blacksmith or the Alchemist or become a monster hunter. Having this freedom is a deep breath of fresh air - most games in this genre tend to have no options other than farming. Kynseed deserves more praise and much more attention than its getting.

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is an excellent early access game with an incredibly satisfying gameplay loop! I really enjoy a lot of the game so far, but there are some significant problems too, because it's such an early-access game, and I hope some of these issues will be tweaked in upcoming updates!Pros- Gorgeous backgrounds and intricate maps. I love the Mapstones and the exploration required to fill out the map, it's very satisfying and fun!-Incredible music assigned to every zone on the map, just phenomenal stuff I never get bored of. Very moody and fun. A couple of Kynseed tracks are up on YouTube and I'm constantly looping them!  Can't wait to buy that full OST. - The farming system is really fun! I love the market days, and the selling mechanic you have on your market days with bartering. - The proverbs/notes/recipe system is really neat! I love finding random scraps of paper while exploring, and having them contribute to my overall knowledge of the world! It makes exploration incredibly rewarding and it makes the world denser with stuff! The lore sheets, especially, are really intriguing! - I like the idea of all the shop ownership stuff, that's really exciting promise for the future. -I like all the character designs a whole bunch! Very fun and varied. I can't wait for the town festivals and events to be implemented too, I love how unique each little area is. -Love the overlay with the additional information like whether crops need to be watered/animals need to be fed. Very useful and cool!-All the controls feel pretty intuitive, and the game overall has a great UI. Cons/Improvements Needed- The pacing of the game, as is, feels really off. Despite having reached max cooking and max farming skills, I've not even become an adult yet! For a game that's supposed to be about multiple generations, the years almost seem too long? I think it might be more apt to have each season only be 7 days long, instead of 14. - Also re: pacing, despite farming being very easy to complete with minimal effort, the shopkeeping system is incredibly long! You see almost no improvement to the store, and even when I hired the most competent people in town, with the highest stats, they didn't seem capable of breaking even, let alone making a profit. I'd love for future iterations to either have you man the store yourself so you can do better than your employees, or have some sort of training system that you can throw money into, so your quality/rep increases better? The shopkeeping stuff seems paced out for a multiple-generations game, even though the rest of the gameplay doesn't quite aim for that.-NPCs are still pretty flat, they don't have much personality yet beyond liking and disliking certain foods. I really LOVED when you get unique quests from NPCs, even one makes them memorable. Lucy Arrows and Ash Brown ask for you to do something unique (investigating the ruins/searching for a mythical bug) and because of these events, I actually remember their names! More of those would be incredible. -Despite the animals being adorable, trying to select them and feed them all on your farm is SO difficult. Trying to select the correct chicken or pig when you have multiple animals is INFURIATING. I also had to turn to the internet to figure out that you had to inflate them and slingshot them to harvest meats! It would be nice for an NPC to tell you that as a secret or for the tutorial to mention it. - Not sure if this was a bug or an unfinished thing, but in your second year after the timeskip, your sibling sends you a letter and asks to meet you in North Wood. Despite hanging out at North Wood for the next three days after receiving that letter, the event never triggered for me, which was a bummer. These moments where there are hints at being a story are excellent, so I was sad to not see that!  -As other people have mentioned in better depth, combat does suck as of now. I avoid it wherever possible. -As other people have also mentioned, the tool system is pretty confusing. Is Zinc or Luminium better for certain things? It feels weird too, because whenever you level up, the level-up seems tied to the tool, and not to your character, so you'd never want to change your tool, for fear of losing the progression with the level-ups? I'd love clearer markers of why the different tool materials matter, aside from how we sell them in the blacksmith. - I wish you could become friends with the Masters of the Trades before you finish their quests. I love Old Mother Hubbard and Marshthwt and Twig, and even if I can't marry them, I wish I could up their friendship level/give them gifts while also completing their Mastery quests. -The offerings system is super cool in theory, but weird in practise. It feels strange that when I'm trying to optimize the blessings and curses I receive, I often end up not giving 3/6 Goddesses offerings? That feels like the sort of thing that should have consequences in-world, especially with all the Lore. -Similarly, the brownie thing is really cool, but I would love more development as a system?Maybe he helps more around the farm if you feed him? Maybe you get to learn more about him? Cool, but underdeveloped. - I would also love a clearer picture of how you can improve your own character stats! Are there certain things you have to do, or are they entirely random? Anyway, I love Kynseed so far, and I can't wait to see what the developers have up their sleeve. It's worth playing now, and once it's fully a funished game, it'll be even more worth it, I'm sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed, even in Early Access, is a game full of activity. From adventuring in the woods and fighting monsters, to fighting with jams and pies in the kitchen. Spouses. Shops. Crops. This game has it all. Even exploration is an enjoyable feature. It has a unique setting, unique gameplay, a unique way of teaching you about the world and the game, and I have no doubt it will have a unique story full of twists and turns, light and dark. The game itself, even without all the activities available, is stunning. The pixel art is genuinely out of this world, the environment, the unique characters with their own bizarre physical quirks. Big noses. Buck teeth. Angry eyebrows. I remember the first time I saw the season of Spring and the colours genuinely took my breath away.Kynseed has recently faced some backlash for what is quintessentially a public relations nightmare. Are they deserving of that backlash? Certainly the man that committed the crimes is. Many are even willing to go as far as to say that the men that reacted slowly to his crime are, that I will not comment on. I do not know what was at stake for those men, they did not hold the rights to a powerful part of Kynseed and were likely extremely afraid to see the game's development damaged.There are many people on the Development Team for Kynseed, many people putting their passion into this game that were not involved in the current controversy. Many people whose passion shines extremely brightly in this game. We currently have no idea what is going on behind the scenes in the Kynseed team, but I for one do know this - I do not want *these* people to fail. I do not want to see these people fail because of one horrible man and some incompetent management.This game, even in it's current state, helped me through an immensely dark time - I think the Covid Pandemic triggered something in all of us, but loading up this game made the dark world a lot brighter for me and many other people. I, for one, do not want to see that brightness destroyed by the acts of a few small, weak, and simple men.So please, judge the game for what it is and, even if you want the people responsible to fail, don't ask for the entire team to fail. They are not all responsible.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Take this recommended review with a very large grain of salt. This game has so much potential and it's sad it can be so frustrating. I want the developers to know that they have something good here just needs some tweaking. There is at least 1 mini-game mechanic that has ground one part of my character to a halt because I am unable to get the right quality of item. There is no joy in that I cannot complete the cooking master quest line because of it.I was unable to run the apothecary because the mini-games were impossible to figure out. I made nothing but stink bombs no matter what I tried to make or ingredients used. No matter how many times I tried to decipher the instructions the stink bomb was all that resulted.  If you fail you lose all your items and gain nothing from the experience, This is not fun or relaxing it's  anger inducing. The art style is very pretty but at times can be very hard to navigate on certain maps when dark or raining. The music over all is pretty good. Tasty acres has my favorite sound-track while Poppyhill's polka must be set on fire. The interactive menu with NPC's and items is not pleasant. I play on a PC with an x-box controller and it took me too long to figure out how to equip items and interact with NPC's. There is a lack of information given to the player about items. I.E. the glass lens, when you start your character you're given one and no explanation of what it does. Later on in the game you find the traveling vendor sells another glass lens but you have no idea why you should buy it. This glass lens is a pretty important mechanic to get to other realms and something players should be aware of but there is nothing to teach of this inside the game. There seems be a lot behind the friendships of NPC's in the game but my god is it hard to get there. It's helpful that you can get info from NPC's about other NPC's but then it's not. Feels like playing roulette when gift giving. I'm just not a fan of the game mechanic ' buying people's love'  in any game but that's just me and not a bash against the game.I've done a little bit of the fighting in the forest. There are a lot of items you can take with you and use on your run but again little information on what they do or how they help is given. It's pretty easy for the most part being turned base combat but I don't like turn based combat, so that's on me. I've changed my review from negative to positive so many times Steam must be getting whiplash. I promise this is my last one. I recommend this with the hopes the developers improve what they have otherwise they have a cute, grindy, heavy handed with poor mini-game game.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on Kickstarter 3.5 years ago and tried its early alpha shortly after. Decided it was too barebones and lacked any direction, so I cooled off and forgot about it. Sadly, it doesn't seem to have any more direction in late 2020. They still don't have a solid core game loop down beyond fulfilling random tasks for villagers until the clock ticks down. Watering crops is trivial due to lack of a stamina system or even a limit on how much water is in the watering can (direct comparison to Harvest Moon here). There's not really much incentive to get coins, either.I ended my playthrough tonight after the first timeskip, if that matters. Maybe the economy actually shapes up afterwards, but I really don't want to sit bored twiddling my thumbs until that transformative moment occurs. The game quite simply needs a better, more meaningful and more engaging game loop in its first ~10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, after being part of this mess since 2021, I can not really recommend this game.This is just a really chaotic studio. There is so much love to details, but bugs that have been in the game for at least 2 years(that was when they told me on Discord, that they will fix it)They constantly change their vision and take forever to bring out a new update.There should have been a Tavern Update(not really something, I was much interested in, but widely requested) somewhere in mid-2023, instead we got a "Big Build Update" at the beginning of 2024, which sure is nice, but did anybody ask for it? After restarting my play through a 3rd time(since you often have to restart, after big updates), it is again evident, that the whole generation thing gets relevant too late. I finished the main story in my second year, when my kids where still kids.The whole game loop just doesn't seem to work and like with the mentioned bugs, it just seems to me, the developers never really played the game from start to finish, otherwise, they should have seen a lot of the problems this game has=== Old review ===I still like this game, but it seems badly balanced. There is a lot to do, farming, having a business, fighting, becoming the best friend of everybody, etc.There are a lot of really nice details, like lore, minigames, easter eggs, etc.The main selling point, the generation stuff, takes too long to get relevant. You can easily finish the main story before you have kids. Taking over your kid, doesn't really change much.There are a few bugs, that needs fixing, while they are not game breaking, they get pretty annoying like star rating not working, but you need them to finish a Masters Quest and have to use the work around of sending out your kin to find them.Maybe some more time will fix some of this problems, but I am not sure, if they whole concept can really work well. Days often seem too short, a year too long and not a good way to make major time skips.

_childDocuments_.review: Now first and foremost i'd like to point out that this review stands for version v0.1.19.2626 of the early access. Now i have no intention of picking apart incomplete features or anything that is obviously or statedly incomplete, as that would be unfair. I will also say that the music and art are beautiful.The reason i don't like this game as much as i thought i would is that it just throws you into the deep end - while it may have a few tutorials, the world is massive and it wants you to explore, but doesn't give you the time to do that in a day. Unless you ride the pig, which the game never tells you is a thing. You also have to go around finding "proverbs" clues about how to find certain natural resources, and so you have no real idea of what you're doing for a long time. While you can review the proverbs, there doesn't seem to be any way to review the tutorials. I have a problem with the way the smithing minigame is setup because you have to hold and then let go at the right time for most of it (which i don't like, because i tend to panic and release early, meaning im consistently failing)I suppose most of my dislike of the game comes from the feeling i get almost instantly of being in over my head with absolutely no assistance - a feeling that is not helped by the fragmented and incomplete guides scattered across the internet. If you have issues of anxiety dealing with unknowns and a time constraint, this game is not for you.EDIT: The game has since gone for a full release. I still can't in good faith recommend it. The devs need to focus their efforts on something. As it stands, the game is trying to do way too much, and kind of sucks at all of it. The core mechanics feel clunky, the day rolls by way too quickly (which, considering the game makes a point of giving timely offerings, kinda screws you over) the minigames range from frustrating to infuriatingAnd the problem is instead they spend their time tweaking minor story elements and details of the prologue (which also takes way too damn long, and doesn't give you a good vibe for the game) The wiki is also laughably incomplete.This game has the potential to be great - but it seems like it's very, very far off from achieving that potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Potential to be really good but it feels unfinished.What is here is good but the pacing is out of the window and some features are implemented really weirldy and relatively bad.You have the option to skip time a couple of years and/or play as your kid but there isn't much of a point in doing so. You can easily finish everything worth finishing with one character. And that playthrough is fun and good. If you skip the time all the npcs that you've come to like will get old or die. New seemingly auto-generated ones will take their place. But they are boring, ugly with seemingly no quests attached to them. And when all the major quests or tasks are done, what reason is it to play further? To conclude, I like and somewhat recoomend the game but they could have cut several badly implemented features and focused on other parts and this game would have been a classic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brilliant. The developers took their time, reimagined every aspect of what a game in this genre could be. There is so much depth to this game. I love that every craft has it's own minigame- and that each one tries to mimic the craft itself. Cooking looks and feels like cooking. The same for smithing and so on. So many other games that I play, crafting is for things I need. In Kynseed, it's part of the game itself. It's fun to try to outdo myself in quality scoring, or realize it's time to call it quits for the night when I start missing hammer blows. Sometimes, I do feel a little lost for direction. It's been so long since I've played a game that didn't lead me by the nose. I just have to stop, think about all I can do, where I'm at, my overall goal at this time, and so on. This is a game meant to be played over generations in the games, not completed in two or three seasons. There are so many things to do and only you decide how you want to play your game. You can't place your farm plots. As far as I've played, you can't decorate your house or land. If that is one of the main reasons you play these games, THIS IS NOT THE GAME FOR YOU. Farming is an aspect of the game. It is not a farming simulator. I've seen negative reviews because of this. Feels like dinging a lingerie store for not selling tires. I bought this very early on, played 30 minutes, and didn't touch it again until full release. I'm so glad I waited- and that version is what my review is based on.It runs smoothly. I have not had any crashes. I had one quest bug out, and I saw this was common so I'm sure it will be fixed soon. It didn't affect my game.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I really like it. I've almost finished my first in game year and there's lots of things to do. It's a bit more limited than Stardew Valley in terms of what you can do on your farm, but other areas, such as owning a business (apothecary, blacksmith or general shop) expand upon the life sim genre. Making things such as weapons, potions and dishes each have their own mini game, which I also really like.You can do all of the other things you'd expect, such as fish, own animals, cook and grow crops. The combat mini game is fun and better than Stardew.However there are some short comings and it would be great to see these expanded on:- Limited amount of potions, powders, creams to make in the apothecary. I've owned and apothecary for two in-game seasons and I've made all of the medicine now. Would be great if they added in more recipes. It's also frustrating you can't make combat items such as medicine, even though you can buy them from other apothecaries.- Limited interaction with family. Other than set chores and ask them to follow you, you can't really do much else. Would be great if you could do more with them.- Customise your home and shops, such as placing furniture and being able to interact with them. Expand and design your buildings, change flooring and wallpaper. You can customise anything at the moment, except specialising your shop to 3 different types.- Easier access on how to harvest plants, crops and fruits with better star ratings. At the moment you need to find proverbs (which is fine). But then you either have to remember how to harvest them or look through a clunky book. Would be good if you could select the item in your inventory to display the tips.- More businesses! We have 3 at the moment, plus the devs mentioned owning a tavern in the future. Would be good if they added a couple more. Mortician and gravedigger? Hunter? Restaurant?- No snowing animation in the winter. This one is purely a personal gripe. There's snow on the floor but it rains instead of snows...But overall, I really recommend this game. It's great. Looking forward to seeing what comes in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Video version: Kynseed is perhaps the most early Early Access title I have ever played. Although the game’s art style, music, and general atmosphere may be great, the amount of content in the game is so limited that I am honestly surprised that the game is being sold in its current state.Before I get into that though, I will start with what the game DOES have going for it, namely its aesthetic. I quite enjoyed the way the art style and music blended with each other, it provided for a rather calming experience. Given the genre, this will likely work in the game’s favor later down the line. It’s definitely going for that Stardew Valley feel, but with a more complex art style, and that is perfectly fine by me.However, just about everything else to the game is simply not up to par. The gameplay boils down to repeating the same couple tasks over and over, the map is full of large empty spaces, the mechanics present are extremely simple, and the game lacks content in just about every department. I could not go five minutes without running into some placeholder text for a gameplay mechanic or map area that has simply not been implemented yet. On top of that, the game is also quite buggy. There was one bug in particular that had me stuck riding a pig around, teleporting me back onto it whenever I tried to get off. I get that this is an Early Access title, but Kynseed feels more like a very early demo, one that really should not be sold in its current state.As such, I cannot recommend Kynseed. The aesthetic may be nice and the ideas there are definitely fine, but the game simply lacks in content and is far too buggy to be worth your time. Honestly, the only ones picking up this game should be those dedicated to helping better it through constant feedback to the devs, but at that point it is really just the devs dumping the testing onto its consumers. It is quite the disappointment, as I can see this shaping up to be a nice, finished game, but in its current state, it is simply not worth it.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the makings of a masterpiece.The prologue is an entire season of comfort juxtoposed with the feeling something isn't quite right here. As you go about your day as an adoptive child to a kind old man, nursery rhymes and folklore bring a nostalgic comfort most games in this genre don't have the creative freedom to achieve. The whimsical play on words is clever, and has only gotten better. I love the prologue, but since its last update it's lost some of its mystery. Right now the direction of the sinister aspect is quite clear but with the care that's being taken with this game I can tell it'll continue to get a few more polishes.After the prologue, the pacing changes and the game opens up as you'd expect. I've been thoroghly enjoying it, and I'm glad to see one of the next focusses for update as I write this will be combat.The lighting and colour palette deserves a special mention because from day 1, when I downloaded a demo of this game, where just the farm, "father" as he was called then, "sibling" and Twig Nook existed. I knew someone had conceived a beautiful and in depth world. The weather effects have added such atmosphere. There are even very well lit golden hours. The game is a stunning example of 2D gaming having more artistic potential than most 3D styles of games. The world is querky and really beautiful to look at. I was not surprised to see people who had worked on the Fable series were behind this game, it actually makes a lot of sense.Stardew Valley was very well done, it showed there IS a market for Harvest Moon style of games aimed at adults too, outside of children with nintendo consoles. For me Kynseed has the potential to be greater.I would say Kynseed is to Rune Factory what Stardew Valley is to Harvest Moon. A complete reconception of a fantasy style of Harvest Moon, that has the soul only indie developers can achieve at this point.So many games nowadays have the creativity on the backfoot, beholden to statistics, making them feel empty and soulless. Many games in this genre prioritise the daily grind for financial gain, whilst selling that slower paced alternative country life, but the farm in Kynseed is just one aspect of a potentially very full game (although still being built upon). I thought at first that would be a bad thing, but this game is so full of life and other things, that really all it took was a better balanced game so that you don't spend all day grinding with crops and milking the way I did with every Harvest Moon game. The fact that all the animals you can interact with don't necessarily live on your farm, the fact that the extra space for crop planting is not necessarily on your farm, forces you to stop and smell the roses of this game.The balance this game has means I can really get into the rpg side as well as the tycoon side, and now I make sure to fish enough fish to feed my five cats and dog (about to be two dogs), and have fish left over to sell at my stall. That steadier pace of life is why I'm attracted to these games in the first place. I'm trying to play out my ideal. That's the very heart of this niche genre, and this game prioritises that.I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development of this game for a long time, and before I judge the game, I want to judge the developer's approach to the marketing and crowdfunding, which has been excellent. Always sharing new things here and making jokes there, replying personally to messages and creating a good sense of community, at least over Twitter. it's really a good mark of a team that wants to make something other people enjoy, because they care about making an experience for those people. And that's highly commendable.As for the game, well where do I begin? I haven't poured nearly as many hours into it as I would have liked yet, but it seems bursting with life and you're left to your own devices to the point where it's hard to know where to go when you start, but in a good way; a large portion of the world is open for you to figure out on your own. It's your oyster, as you might say, and it doesn't feel overly intimidating, nor does it feel like it holds your hand.Artwork's beautiful and they clearly spent a long time on it - same with the music, and I'm so glad they really kept the same musical style from the Fable games. It's very unique and lovingly composed. I'm really glad they went with this art style as they managed to create some very charming and colourful sprites that are just pleasing and invigorating to look at. Similarly, I always loved the naming schemes and the writing style of these guys all the way back to Fable, and that whimsical wit and childish humour shines through here. Playing this game is like sinking into a billowy armchair with a cup of cocoa on hand - you can't help but be lulled into comfort.The game is filled with many secrets and collectables which all at the very least add up to build the world and make it feel more immersive, or sometimes show off the style and humour of the devs. As a downside, it's hard to know what some of these do sometimes, outside of an interaction telling you you found them.Negatives? Oh boy, it's honestly hard to find any. In the prototype, I had an issue with the placeholder UI, but it's been cleaned up immensely. That being said, despite being more thematically organised, the abundance of available tools, consumables, items, actions and overall prompts means figuring out how to interact with things or use objects still takes a practice spell to get use to. But once you've got it, you're away. There are bugs, being early access. That being said, I haven't found anything game-breaking, the devs acknowledge their existence within the game, and with the most prominent one I found - characters clipping into objects like desks and stoves - I find equally as often in apparently fully-released triple A titles as well. If that's the worst that the Early Access gets, it's still a pretty damn good build.I wish for nothing but a great future for this project and Pixel Count. I was sad to hear when Lionhead closed because aside from anything else, it always had clearly talented and hard working artists and creatives. This game does seem to be very ambitious, as a lot of the Fable games were, and it's only fair to be cautious about whether they can pull it all off. But, I've seen more love and enthusiasm poured into this project than almost any other i can think of - they clearly love doing what they're doing and care about the game they're making. I look forward to watching this game grow with future updates. For now, it's a stable if slightly rough and occasionally scarce game, but above all a beautiful world that is a joy to explore, and I highly recommend picking it up at its current price, as it may be worth a lot more as it gets larger and larger. Also, the devs really deserve the support.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon its exit from early access, the game was evidently underdeveloped. Many of its systems were poorly explained, often buried within walls of text riddled with puns or left completely unexplained. The game's susceptibility to exploitation through shops and the lack of compelling reasons to explore the world further diminished the overall experience, despite its captivating beauty and intriguing lore.However, with the recent introduction of the big build build update (currently in open beta at the time of this review), a significant portion of these issues has been addressed. The game's tutorial has been revamped for better comprehension, and an achievement system now guides players more effectively. The game world has undergone a notable transformation, featuring expanded NPC dialogues and the introduction of several new key story characters. The addition of various random events, both story-driven and incidental, contributes to a more dynamic and immersive world. This not only lends a natural, vibrant quality to the environment but also imbues a sense of significance to the narrative – a stark improvement from the previous version where the story progression felt somewhat purposeless.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and I do recommend it but a few things stop me from enjoying it half as much as I would like to, keep in mind while you read this that the game is still in early access so a lot of stuff here is understandable and will likely change. I currently have 20 smth hours in the game, I will also change my review as I get more experience and as the updates come and go. General positivesThe graphics are absolutely breathtaking, the lore and writing are full of charm and are nothing short of addicting, I love the dialogue and the descriptions of pretty much anything, the mounts, most of the mini games, the weekly events, I like the pace of the game, how long the days and seasons are. I love that when we are adults the game doesn't force us to sleep like a lot of sims do. I looove the combat system, honestly for me it's one of the best in any sim games I've played so far. I love that it's much less boring than Stardew Valley in both the battling and foraging aspects, and farming is also less demanding, fishing is pretty chill as well. It makes the game less grindy to the player and more relaxing, whether you are casual about it or want to be the very best that no one ever was. I also appreciate the amount of freedom you have to farm and sell crops for revenue or run shops or complete assignments or focus on the adventure part of it though having main or side storylines that also honor that sense of freedom would be nice. Specific negatives so far- One of the downsides of Kynseed is that it lacks in storytelling past the prologue as of now. There is also no interesting background or depth to the characters, despite their sheer numbers and the witty writing they seem to have no relationships with each other and no life stories, secrets or ambitions. - One of my biggest issues with this game is it's giant scale. There's too many maps, and they're way too big, and there's waaaay too many npcs. This is a big problem for me specifically because they don't introduce these things to the player in any moderate or cumulative way in which you're able to take in the information and appreciate it as you progress. Instead of blocking certain content off as you play through, they just keep most things open from the get go so that if you want to get to know the characters and most of the world, you can, but it will not be enjoyable because it is not digestible and it just becomes overwhelming. In short it's very hard to get any kind of sense of who is who or where is where or forge any minimal connection to anything (besides the animals uwu) So you find yourself making questions like "do I know everyone?" "oh god where was her house?? " "what map was that on, again?" "where did I get this?" It also happens with collectible items like food and resources. There is no nice encyclopedia type mechanic that tracks generally where you found the things you have picked up. I would just love to actually know where items i have already found are without going to the wiki or relying on my poor memory lmao. Though I do appreciate the game´s goal of making you rely on habit, you might be lost and wandering around chaotically at the begginning but as you play more you start to become familiarized with who lives where and what grows where I just think it is inconvenient at times and a little intimidating for new players or people who are not that used to these kinds of games.But generally speaking this is a really fun game, i just feel like it needs a lil editing, which makes sense since it´s still early access.

Content and mechanics referred in-game are not actually implemented on numerous occasion (ie: the game literally tell you about pig breeding... but it's not in-game) and even story-wise the end-game doesn't exist yet.It's sad to say, this game is still unfinished and I don't think it will ever be. _childDocuments_.review: It's frustrating that this game lacks a clear objective. While there are plenty of activities to do like farming, owning a shop, or fishing, but none of them seem to serve a purpose. The coins you earn from these activities have no real use, since there is nothing to buy, rendering the grinding you do feel pointless.You can improve your fishing, cooking, and combat skills, but the progress feels meaningless as well. For instance, to level up your combat skill, you need to collect resources from mobs, but once you reach the endgame, there is no incentive to engage in combat. Furthermore, the high-tier skills you can unlock are typically only accessible after completing the story, so there's little motivation to unlock them beyond the sake of unlocking them.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Stardew Valley? Well this is SV on steroids.There is sooo much to do and so much to learn. And it's funny, and the mythology is quirky and sometimes dark.I would argue that the NPCs are not as developed as in SV, but, I'm not as far into the game to really tell, and there are many (many) more in Kynseed.Crafting  and gardening are... unique and you do need some getting used to it, but that's not necessarily bad.Fighting is a lot of fun and nicely implemented (it's hard!).The ONE thing that needs work is the map and travelling. It takes a hundred clicks to get the info you need, there is no zooming, there is no real fast travel (there is... but really really clunky, though I like the idea of requiring a consumable) and there is no way to set way-points, so be ready to have a notepad with you.It already is a great game, and if the developers keep adding some content and refining some mechanics, you could easily sink hundreds of hours into it. Go for it!.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge _spoiler free_ essay ahead, sorry everyone.... This game is an absolute BANGER. ive been binging it for days now, 100 hours in, and theres still SO much to do, ive skipped work to play this im obsessed. I recommend it, ill give pros and cons. Its a wonderful magic rpg that can be cozy and scary at the same time, theres a lot of crazy twists that will totally change the tone of the narrative, and I love it! I never know what to expect next, all I know is that i can just take my time without major consequences, which is perfect for my style of gameplay, I get distracted a lot with side quests and can spend days on them without feeling anxious abt it. You can buy a shop, an apothecary, a restaurant and even a smith store if you want! All of them have their own minigames that are so cute and fun.  Theres so many mysteries to solve and so much lore to learn. If you are not sure about buying this game, you can disregard any bad reviews left until February of 2024, the game has completely changed since The Big Build Update released in the same month and most of the old complaints were fixed or changed. The new tutorial/prologue is way better now covering all chore mechanics. A lot of life quality upgrades were made, making the game more enjoyable and less of a chore. Each NPC has its own storyline that gets revealed as you progress them, and building relationships are actually vital for the gameplay now. This games feels like a child between Graveyard Keeper and Stardew Valley, i love both of these games and couldnt be hapier with kynseed, its current state feels very polished. Decorating your farm is very easy atm and theres so many cute options and colors. Oh and you can get your animals to follow you all around the world and have your own children take your legacy <3 Having control on what your family is doing during the day is honestly SOOOOOO GOOD!!! i love this mechanic Now the cons: I dont personally think most of these is bad, but since i saw a lot of people criticizing the game for what im abt to discuss, i think its worth mentioning in a recommendation, but its up to personal taste. This game is way more complex than the avarage farm rpg and it has a very slow gameplay that requires time, so beware if thats not your cup of tea before you buy it. In this regard this games reminds me a lot of Graveyard keeper. I.e.: The game will leave you in the dark for a while, and i mean a while like ingame months, maybe even years. Each item (food, herbs, swords, potions, everything) has different traits you have to find out by yourself, theres like more than 40 dif traits, its a ton. You can also learn the best condition to find the item. Theres more than 5 unique maps with different fauna and fish, some itens only show up at specific times. All of this information can be gathered sloooowly by exploring the map and gifting npcs, and as you learn, the info you get will be automatically added to your player menu so you can check it later, its like an in game encyclopedia you can check anytime. So that means that at the beginning of the game you are gonna have zero info on everything, that will force you to play with the wiki open most of the time until you have learnt enough about other NPCs and itens to just check your player menu instead. I personally find it all overwhelming at first but now Im super enjoying this complexity. I dont mind having the wiki open on my phone while i play, but some people hate that, and that is 100% ok, this game is probably not for you if thats the case. Also this is the type of game that will give you a task, and to complete this task you gotta talk to a npc, and that npc will ask for pretty rare item, and you dont even have access to the city that has the rare item they need, and sometimes that will take you YEARS in game to complete. So again, if tahts not your cup of tea, stay away of this game. One more thing: Besides Kynseed not having a time limit penalities by taking your time to play, NPCs sometimes WILL die in this game when you pay your life taxes at the end of every year. They die by old age or other reasons i dont want to spoil, so you can accidentally be unable to finish an NPC quest line after the time skip, this wont stop you from finishing the game, but if you are a completionist, it can be pretty annoying to have that happen to you, so be careful, or just check the wiki for spoilers on whos programmed to die and when.BEWARE: Since there was a MASSIVE update to this game recently, the >fandom< wiki is mostly outdated, most of the gameplay info there has completely changed and is now inaccurate and will confuse the hell out of you (it confused me lol), so use the oficial wiki for gameplay info. The fandom wiki is still usable for Fish spawn times and other small specific stuff, but thats it. Theres a lot of useful guides in the kynseed steam community tab, I 100% recommend checking them for updated game info, if you have any game mechanics questions, search them first here on steam for an answer, thats what ive been doing

_childDocuments_.review: While writing this, I understand this game is in development and I'm sure it will be more polished when completed. Some of the things I'm pointing out may be improved or fixed by the final release. Despite my criticism, I do think it will be fun for the right people.Good:The art is charming and a pleasure to look at during gameplay. The music, when playing, is a delight. The songs are cute and add to the mood of the art. The cooking system is really cute and fun, albeit a little awkward. I actually liked cooking the most out of everything. Other crafting systems also were fun, the little I did them.Collecting proverbs scattered around the map while exploring was pretty fun, and actually anything involving exporting felt pretty rewarding and fun. Finding map stones, finding new houses/farms, and curiously looking at all the strange trees or points of interest was really fun. Not so good:The music doesn't loop well. I found it eerie and strange, when midday the music would just stop for several minutes. This could be ok, if they're were sufficient ambient sounds to make up for the deafening silence in these moments. I don't notice the lack of footstep sounds, ambient sounds, or whatever when the music is at least on. The first few days of tutorial felt confusing, but manageable. The main thing was I felt confused about what I could actually do. There are A LOT of instructional books scattered around that are helpful, but sometimes irrelevant to your current abilities. You can reference them any time though.The NPCs dialoge was strange a lot of the time. Many of them are openly hostile towards you, despite your uncle's insistence they are good, kind people. It is a bit funny how mean they are, but I wasn't a fan. On the subject of dialogue, there were a lot not adult themes jokes and innuendos than I expected. This isn't exactly a bad thing, but unexpected. I would not recommend this for anyone under 14, or anyone who minds raunchy humour, despite its cute aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved kynseed in early access, and I still love it after the full release. There a few bugs, but I haven't encountered anything game-breaking so far. While there are some elements of the game that feel a bit incomplete, I'm still having a great deal of fun and I'm excited to see what the developers bring in the future. (The developers are also pretty active in the game's official discord and have been responsive to feedback and bug reports.)The setting feels unique and immersive. I absolutely love the magical and fae elements. The NPC dialogue is hilarious and the NPCs themselves are varied and interesting. I find the minigames to be fun and engaging, there's also a good variety of them. The combat system is very well-done; it's fast-paced, pretty intuitive, and challenging without being frustrating.Please do be aware that this game is not much like Stardew Valley despite what some websites say. Personally I find it more relaxing that Stardew (less time constraints), but the main difference is that Kynseed is not a farming game at all. It's much more about exploration, gathering resources from the land, and running shops, and farming is only a small component.To anyone considering buying this game, I absolutely recommend it! I'm obsessed with it and I think it's only going to get better. There's a lot to do but it never feels overwhelming or confusing. I'm having a great time with this game and I can see myself playing it for a long time to discover all its secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Harvest Moon fan since A Wonderful Life came out in America. I've been obsessed, though since Wada left the series has been steadily losing its charm as it focuses more on farming and romance than the overall immersion of being a rancher/farmer. Stardew Valley was a good love letter to the series in terms of gameplay, and should be praised for its focus on customization. However, it did not scratch that itch either. Its writing and world felt rather forced to me.This game has a vibe similar to Moonlighter, HM:A Wonderful Life, or Graveyard Keeper-- The village atmosphere is very immersive. But where Moonlighter failed in being very simplistic and more like an app in terms of gameplay, and Graveyard Keeper failed by insulting its fanbase with a hastily written story that makes you feel wanting more, and a skilltree that feels largely unwarranted, this series feels much more alive. I'm a few hours in and still only in the beginning stages as my farmer is still a kid, and I'm already in love. I saw the kickstarter for this a long time ago, and have been thinking about it since because the trailer alone had showed me that this was made by people who felt the same way I did in terms of Story of Seasons and Stardew Valley. I'm so glad that I found it again, and was able to buy the game. I'm looking forward to how it'll develop.For criticisms, my only complain is that sometimes the controls are a bit confusing, and the map system is really terrible for a world that seems so large. It's hard to keep track of where everything is when I have to search through each area of the map for stones like Assassin's Creed vantage points. Most of the time I wander around the village hoping to stumble across one of the villagers I need rather than trying to figure out where they live.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game with a nice folklore and magic premise. I've been following it's development since the earlier stages and I'm proud to see what it's become. The visuals are beautiful in a pixelated way with lovely music as you run through the land of Quill, in Y'stor. The story is satisfying and interesting without ever rushing you to complete it. The game can be hard at times with finding items and the minigames for certain things but you get the hang out it. There are so many characters to meet and date, but if you don't want to, then don't. It's really up to you. Wanna be a farmer? Go for it! Fishing? Okay! Fighter? Train for the occasion! You have complete control over what you do and can be satisfied in many small or big ways. Sometimes, you find yourself sucked into one task at a time, fixating on one thing you want to do, and there's no punishment for doing so. Others time you find yourself relaxed, just exploring and running around to see what you can find. It's worth at least a try, it's not for everybody but I can confidently say if you like games (Stardew, Harvest Moon, Sun Haven, etc.) focused with magic, farming, life-sims, etc. then this could be for you.
