_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game! From the world, to the concept, to the execution, the art, the music, everything else -- this game is a joy and I always look forward to playing it. A huge part of what makes this game wonderful is that the developers are very attentive and responsive. They try things out, listen to feedback, and adjust as needed. Right now, the game is trying out some new things with the Big Build Update and, for the most part, it's a great experience! But you can se the devs responding to feedback about other features, where things are going, how people are responding, etc. That is a big deal -- to have such engaged devs. It's clear they love this game and it goes a long way in building a community that loves it right back.This game allows you to go at your own pace. You can be as intense about it as you want or take it easy. One newer feature that kinda upsets that vibe is the enemy totems that appear and destroy houses. I wish that had more of an optional feel or some other way to engage the player around rebuilding homes that didn't feel like a "game tax." I scrapped my first play through and started a fresh one with this update. I didn't feel like I was repeating things needlessly or losing out on anything. That being said, I've yet to move on from my initial character to the next generation, so I'm curious what that will be like. A few other things on my wishlist that I'm sure the devs will consider:- some type of basic auto-restocking for shops- something more meaningful with the destruction of houses. I don't know what that is, but right now I'm more inclined to just let the houses remain destroyed and take my time gathering resources.- maybe NPCs to befriend or get-to-know in the other realms? Right now they're places you just hop into every now and then and the inhabitants are, well, indifferent to you.- This might just be me, but...that clown with the hook hands in Mellowfields HAS GOTTA GO. Okay maybe not. I can get over it. I promise. But knowing that clown could be there waiting for me has meant my apothecary shop suffers severe neglect ;) There's a lot of good this game has going for it. It's charming, relaxing, fun, unique, weird, and I'm really looking forward to where it goes next. The roadmap for development is out there and it looks like we're in for some interesting stuff! All in all, get this game, support a small but passionate dev team, and enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, do I recommend the game in it's current state for the price? It's a big MAYBE. That isn't a negative, this review will be complicated and layered I apologize in advance. To address the elephant in the room, this game gets a lot of the obvious comparisons to Stardew Valley and it's not entirely unwarranted, but I think it also will lead a lot of people astray. This is NOT a farming sim game, pure and simple. If you're only interested in farming, this game probably isn't for you. Farming is a feature and it's useful, but if all you want to do is farm, odds are you won't get much out of this game. It's a cog in a much bigger wheel. This is a Fantasy life simulation game with a dark fantasy story and a wide variety of gameplay options, all with a fair bit of depth to them. You can run 3 different types of shop (currently, with plans to expand in the next few months to a fourth) and each shop is actually well thought out and different, rather than just being a different skin over the same base mechanics. Running the shop requires you to have good time and money management, and even then you'll end up using them often as a way to grow your reputation more than your money in the early game. In addition to the shop running, there are also mechanics for cooking, Dating, friendships, pets and their functions, and tons of little things hidden throughout the game to find. The combat is actually pretty interesting and also offers a good bit of depth and challenge to it. The map is pretty big, and you aren't forced to go to sleep every night (or at all, after the prologue). In fact there are some things you can only do/find at night. That said, the game is not without it's issues. So far I've found two instances of NPCs not being where they were supposed to be (based on all the in-game information available to me) which have prevented me from taking place in events. Now it's possible I was doing something wrong and I imagine visiting the discord server that they have linked in the in-game pause menu would help me to some extent, but I think it's important to note for someone who just wants to play the game without having to visit external resources, you may find yourself coming up against a wall from time to time. Overall I recommend the game, but I think it's very important to note that this isn't really a universal recommendation. Do you own Stardew Valley? If not, I think that's a better purchase for less money at the moment. Unless you really DON'T want a farming sim and you specifically want more variety, a better story, and don't mind some rough patches, Stardew is the better purchase. Similarly, if you're specifically looking for a farming sim, and that's all you want, I wouldn't necessarily recommend this game. If you are against using external resources, or if you're against bad things happening, don't get this game. If you DO get the game, I hope you have a blast with it. The music, art, world, story, everything I've encountered so far are beautiful. I just know that in the current state, at the current price, and with the current "It's like stardew valley" buzz around it, there will be some people who aren't happy and I want to try to mitigate it

_childDocuments_.review: This game keeps getting compared to Stardew Valley, but IMHO that comparison is flawed. In this game you CANNOT improve nor your house nor your farm, you can only plant in the existing provided slots. That alone means that the farming aspect only takes a miniscule amount of your time. The rest of your time in this game is spent between exploring, talking with NPCs, doing tasks, and fighting. There is a day/night cycle, but you never have to rest. You also are not limited to a single character, as the premise of the game is to build a legacy, with future generations inheriting the farm and continuing on the adventure.- Stunning pixel art graphics- Great soundtrack- Combat is innovating, engaging and well done- Crafting mini games are cool, when done once in a while- Exploring the world early on is amazing- There is no limit on the actions that you can do each day, which, for some, can be a boon (if one doesn't like Stardew stamina system)- LGBT+ spouses are allowed- Crafting mini games gets old and boring, VERY quickly. Especially because it needs to be done for each and every item. A quantity selector would have improved the situation.- Each area of the world feels same-y, and traveling between each to reach your destination gets tedious. You can spend resources to fast travel, but otherwise expect lots of walking between each area (with associated (fast) loading screen). Bigger areas would have improved the feel of coherent and sprawling villages, instead of the mini zones with 1-2 houses we have right now.- NPC interactions are generic and limited to a dozen or so lines. They don't feel unique, they don't feel personal, they get recycled way too much. They feel like robots, breaking the immersion of a world populated by different characters.- The star rating system is abysmal. It does not depend on your skills, but to a list of factors specific to that item. It could be considered a great thing, until you realize the complexity of the system, which basically asks you to search the external wiki for help. As an example, a 5-star cabbage requires: to be in week 2 of Autumn; being adept with the sickle; windy weather; sheep poop fertilization; worship bonus by donating to the Freyl goddess. - The Kynseed mechanic should be the core mechanic of the game (given its name) and is what enables the legacy system to kick in, ensuring that your legacy inherits bonuses thanks to the accomplishments of your ancestors. It fails hard in this regard, because the first character you create is able to finish the game alone without any problems whatsoever.In a nut shell, this game is stunningly beautiful and charming for the first few hours, but the overall hollow world and the grindy gameplay turns this into a chore later on.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is initially fun and gives the impression that you'll have a lot to do, then gradually peters out.The NPCs are shallow, designed to get replaced by generic NPCs that are born as the game goes on. Everyone spits out the same lines of dialogue, with some slight variants between 'personality types.' The starting NPCs have some extra dialogue each time you rank-up your friendship then immediately go back to the same lines as everyone else. The lack of variety would be less blatant if the game didn't present an option to ask every NPC how they're doing and what they're up to.It feels like the multi-generational aspect is supposed to be a large selling point for the game, but in it's current state it feels tacked on. It's briefly interesting to see an NPC you like marry someone else and have a kid, but the NPCs are all so lifeless that it's hard to care.You can have up to three kids, but you best not become invested in more than one. The multi-generational game doesn't feel like dealing with multiple generations so once you start playing as the next generation it marks all the kids you didn't choose to be your heir as dead in your save file. The lore explanation being that they 'moved away.'I could forgive the lack of NPC depth and the lask-luster multi-generational mechanics if the rest of the game was good. The minigames are fun when you start, but quickly get repetitive. Running a shop is initially fun, but after a while the shops almost runs themselves. Besides the shops and shop upgrades, there isn't much to spend money on so at a point you end up with a bunch of stores printing money for you with not much to do but wait for them to earn you enough reputation to rank up. One of the fastest ways to rank up in this game does indeed appear to be owning a bunch of shops and repeatedly sleeping in your bed to make days pass. It doesn't feel rewarding to earn things in-game because of how simplistic and effective the shops are; you can even order 4-star items from them, largely undermining the game systems for earning these things yourself.If this was an early-access title, I'd say it looked great. I can't recommend it in its current state, but I will keep an eye on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed is a game that at it's core could rival games like Stardew Valley. But sadly it is holding itself back in several major areas.The progression in this game is extremely tedious:1. Each tool gets better by using it, so far so good. BUT the amount of grinding is insane. You have to use a single tool over ten thousand times to progress to the highest level.2. This game has skill trainers and to learn the skills you have to give them a way too large amount of items that have a certain star requirement. Which in itself is not bad but it mixes with point 3.3. To aquire a higher quality item you have to fulfill VERY specific conditions like pick it up at dawn, ride a pig, during a storm, while being followed by a dog or while you eaten something that gave you flatulence (this is not a joke).These conditions are everywhere and every time you pick up an item you have to look in a wiki to see if you can fulfill these conditions or not. If you don`t do this you cannot progress.After 40 hours of gameplay i feel like running on the same spot with hardly any progression. Only buy this if you are prepared to spend over hundreds of hours doing a lot of busy work.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand how there are so many positive reviews about this "game" everywhere. Feels like a complete chore rather than enjoyment and freedom. You start with a lazy twin that does absolutely nothing to help you with on your endless wave of tasks. Haven't finished doing a task because you had to deliver milk to the other side of the map ? Well here are more tasks and more milk delivery tasks just to spice things up. NPCs treat you bad, the goddess treats you bad despite you worshiping the damn thing, the twin is impatient and forces you to do everything just because she thinks that would improve their relationship with their new father and nobody gives any sense of direction. After a while you actually get sick of the chosen pixel art style because everything blends together and every piece of sprite screams for attention and your eyes can't focus on where your player can pass or the things you can interact with. Don't go in thinking if you enjoyed Stardew Valley that you would enjoy this. The game won't let you breathe for a second and wasting any time on exploration feels negative as you would be given even more tasks to do or your father could die because the twin forces you to go somewhere you have never been before and gives you absolutely no idea of how to get there while all she does is water the extremely limited amount of available crops. This game does look beautiful at first but don't let it fool you as you will be doing absolutely nothing you want to be doing.

Meaning this "Full Release" game only has appoximately 30% of its story content included, with the tavern not even purchasable until Q1 2023.If you don't mind playing what is still essentially an Early Access game or can get it on sale and temper your expectations, I would strongly suggest getting the game, it has great potential, but I don't make recommendations on potential, and I can't recommend this game in its current state.It's a beautiful world and has some wonderful writing, but past that there's just a foundation of a game, it really needs fleshing out.Note: A lot of my hours logged for this game are sitting on the menu and testing mods since I'm building and testing them repeatedly, so don't take my hours played as any real indication of how long I've actually played this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a slow paced, farm life sim/RPG. It's a bit of a mental shift if you, like me, play a lot of "optimize everything" sims. You can't seem to do that in this game; which is okay, it forces you to slow down, read, and actually kind of meet everyone in town. There are a LOT of people! Trying to fit every task into every day is impossible, which, again, is kind of the point; you have to pick and choose...and there is a lot to pick and choose from! I'm still pretty early in the game, but it definitely seems like a long story arc and a lot of content.However, all those positive things said, my biggest issue with the game is the clunky and AWFUL interface. It is SO bad. Inventory management (so many unnecessary tabs!!!!), getting around town (the quest tracker should be able to be re-mapped), figuring out what time it is (the dandelion thing is cute, but really annoying), and interacting with people (an exercise in waaaay to many clicks and having to exit and enter the interaction multiple times). The interface requires more of your attention than the game itself! It totally breaks the soft, laid-back vibe of the game.I'm going to keep playing, but it barely squeaks out a thumbs up because of the UI.Note to the developers: I know the whole "save every night" thing is a thing in this type of game, but for players who might have to drop in and out of the game (kids, lives, jobs, etc.) it's a really frustrating and dated mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Game is adorable, and has that Lionhead/British humor I have longed for since I was a child and played the first Dungeon Keeper on PC.The devs do have a weird obsession with family tragedy though.. I certainly wouldnt let them near my own family..**EDIT**So, people are review bombing the game, due to the composer of the game forced himself on a community member. The composer was fired when it was found out, however the company has kept quiet around the entire ordeal, which is pissing some people off.. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying that I don't recommend this game at its current stages, but I do recommend people to support the development and follow this game. Minor problems: The early part of the game is polished enough for players. Once the introduction section is over, the game starts to show cracks and issues. There are plenty of bugs (and I mean PLENTY), but that's expected of an early access game. There isn't a lot of things that are clearly laid out for players, so to fully understand and utilize all the possibilities of the game the player needs to seek outside sources (guides, the community, or the development blogs) to learn what should be done. I also find a problem with the holes in the plot so far. I constantly encounter the "who cares" question when interacting with NPCs. The only person I cared was the sibling and the father, but that's abruptly ripped away from the player after the introduction section and I'm suddenly left with no motivation or reason to interact with NPCs. I also find the whole fae issue confusing and irritable at its current stage, with no explanation for a real reason to ever deal with them again. But I must say that I do notice an effort to create unique characteristics and cultures among the different villages, but it's not clearly demonstrated or fleshed out yet. I expect these issues with plot and bugs to be fixed in the near future. I know once they get to it the plot will be extremely rich, perhaps richer than games like Stardew and Harvest Moon. The way that they've coded the father and sibling so far has shown to me that they have the capabilities of fixing this plot dilemma once they get to it.The good: Despite all my gripes, the project is really ambitious and I'm extremely excited and happy to see how much development and effort is being poured into the game. I love how responsive the dev team is with the player base, and they constantly aim to update and grow the game. I love how beautiful the game is and how much is being fleshed out in the environment. I also love how beautiful the music is. The little events in the town square are also very interesting and I love the mini game for metalworking. The community is extremely supportive for new players and even if you don't pick up the game now, feel free to join the discord or participate in discussions. At the very least, read the development blogs that the dev team releases every month! They're extremely informative and fun to read which works to definitely keep the hype of the game alive!On the issue of price and durability: For the current price it is pretty good with how much content there is so far! 10 bucks for 6ish hours of content is a good price. Again, there's just so much to do in the game but isn't clearly demonstrated, so that means that dedicated players will clearly play beyond my measly 6 hours on the game. If you really get into the game and community you'll quickly discover that there's always something new to discover and explore as development continues. Keep this game on your radar and support the creators. It's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth backing, if you want to encourage this sort of thing.As the devs make very clear, this game is far from finished. It is playable though - in my three hours play time I encountered no crucial bugs, and the whole experience was very much like the first hours of a game like Stardew.Which brings up another point - this is a game like stardew - in the same genre, but  has it's own character.Where the art in Stardew is more cartoony, this is more Impressionist - but both are gorgeous pixel art.Stardew is about building a farm, and exploring, in that order, and So far Kynseed seems to be more about exploring, with a little farming.The humour is very british, and corny, with lots of references to pop culture, plays on words etc.Don't buy it now if you want a full game, but if you want to back a promising pixel art farming/adventure game that would be great if/when the devs deliver on all their promised features, have at it.PS: You can ride Truffles the pig - that little feller can really book it.

It just adds to the immersion of the game and the lore.I did play this when it was in early access and the game looks and runs way better. I did not pour in the same amount of  hours and im glad i didnt since the early access save files were apparently not accessible after general release. _childDocuments_.review: 15/02/2024The Big Build update has made pacing a lot better, NPC's seem a lot more fleshed out. The time seems to go quicker than before but that could just be me enjoying the game. I'm still only in the tutorial section but the improvements are there and I can tell the dev's are trying their hardest to build upon the foundation they have.I am curious to see how the Kynseed will be paced better, the main selling point for me was the generational development and passing the Kynseed to the offspring. Everything else feels like it should be secondary however it previously felt like the opposite. I completed the majority of the game with my starting character on initial release and bought all the stores that were available at the time. After this, it just became a chore managing it all.I am genuinely hoping this game succeeds and the concept improves. If I wanted to build things and crop crops I would play Stardew. If I wanted to run a business I would play Moonlighter or many of the other games like that.Kynseed needs to play into its unique mechanic as it is its greatest strength.Thumbs up for the update however I will thumbs down if I am unhappy once playing the main content.Past review:Edit: i love the game but it needs more fleshed out features.    Original EA review:Before I write my review, I need to inform you that I am rubbish at sticking to one game at a time and quickly lose interest then come back at a later date and try again. Read on with this in mind:Kynseed is a very ambitious game and that is what initially peaked my interest in the game. It has a lot of features and player choice which is a big bonus for me. I like that you're free to wander off and do as you please, accept quests if you like, explore the many areas in the game, go fishing, mining, farming, socialising etc.That said, as someone who lacks imagination, I struggle to engross myself in the game as others would. I often just find myself wandering around not quite sure what to do next.Once complete, I suspect this will be one of my favourite games as I love being able to choose the life of my character.If you're unsure, just take the leap of faith and buy it, it's only £9.99.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: Kynseed is spread too thin. The biggest selling point of this game over other farming / life sim games is the multigenerational gameplay but I find the core gameplay loop too dull to actually reach the point of requiring an heir.Farming:There's nothing to upgrade or customise.The garden plots are preplaced and cannot be modified (Using the greenhouses on other maps are better because you can grow out of season veg).There's a few herb boxes you have no control over and cannot add more.There's a few trees and bushes for fruit. You cannot add more as far as I can tell.Animals:Unless I missed something there's no animal breeding.You start the game with one cow. One cow provides unlimited milk every day.You can buy chickens but you get more than enough eggs from chickens owned by others.You can buy up to three pigs. They provide fertiliser. You can ride them (why bother? The fast travel system is far better). Finally you can kill a pig for three pork chops but don't bother killing your own pigs when you can kill respawnable pigs owned by others.You can buy up to three sheep. They provide fertiliser. You can ride them. They provide no wool or meat.You can have a cat or dog follow you around.Maps:There's a fair number of maps to explore and they all look good. Unfortunately there's little compelling reason to revisit most maps after exploring them the first time. Only a few maps have worthwhile plants to gather. The fast travel system is quite useful.Fishing: I find fishing tedious. Cast the line and then wait ages for a fish to bite. Right click to hook it / reel it in. Repeat. Only the most basic pond fish seem keen to actually bite so be prepared to wait around. On the plus side if you enjoy fishing there's more than enough fish around the various maps and you will never run out.Tools:You can slowly improve certain tools through use. Crafting higher quality tools doesn't appear to make a difference. I won't cover all the tools just ones that seem lacklustre.Bucket - Collect liquids. You can craft them out of different metals but why bother? They all do the same thing. Buckets are pointless, see below.Glass Jar - Does the same thing as a bucket + lets you catch bugs. (There's literally no point to catching bugs but you can...)Watering Can - It holds unlimited water from day one. After getting a rank 2 gardening skill you only have to water plants one time.Shovel - Does nothing unless you have a dog following you.Mining:It takes multiple days for ore to respawn in the mines. It's not something you can do daily if you wanted to.Combat:The combat system is fine. I have no problem with it but I don't really enjoy it either. If you do enjoy the combat there's good news. You can fight all day and night. There's multiple areas to fight in and you can increase the danger level  after each battle or continue at the current level in an attempt to reach the end of the zone.Shops:There's three different types of shops you can own.A goods store (sell everything at any price).A blacksmith (take orders and sell smithed items for a set price).An apothecary (take orders and sell powders / potions for a set price).The main reason I see to own a blacksmith or apothecary is that you don't have to pay the 5 brass per item crafting fee as the owner. Despite what you might think gaining money is not the real purpose of owning a shop. The REP you gain is far more important and gaining money is very simple. You can hire npcs to run your shop for you which is a nice feature if you want to set it and forget it (or just have them cover certain times so you can do other tasks).Goddess Offerings:A bit limited in scope but the blessing / curse system is an interesting concept and allows you to slightly tweak things in favour of tasks you enjoy.NPCs:Kynseed has a large number of npcs who can age, reproduce, and die. Although this sounds exciting this type of system leads to very shallow interactions. The main way to make friends is to buy people's affection. Every npc has 3 liked items and 3 disliked items, any other gifted item will result in a small amount of friendship points. Gifting items will sometimes result in the npc giving you a tip about a liked / disliked item, a bit of lore, or some pointless (I suppose it's meant to be funny) non unique text.When you make a friend they will give you a very basic "story task". Examples: The vegan lady doesn't want her husband to enjoy meat so take his pork chop that's on the floor. The blacksmith gets headaches from being in the forge, get him some pep powder. That's it. There's nothing else to the npc.You can date / marry anyone but don't expect anything more complex than what has already been described (other than the wedding prep which is tedious).Misc:After becoming an adult you never have to sleep. You don't need to eat. You have unlimited stamina. This might sound good in theory and maybe it would be if there were many things you wanted to do, but after a certain point I just wanted to skip days to see something new.The crafting mini games are interesting the first few times but grow old quickly. They are also very inconsistent. Some of the mini games are quite easy and some are needlessly difficult to complete. In game time pauses while cooking but for some reason continues to run while smithing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting and charming game. Articles always compare it to Stardew Valley (and I admit, that's exactly what got my attention, too), however that's not really fair. Kynseed is VERY different. Sure you farm, you fish, you get married. But the mechanics are very different, Kynseed's cooking and crafting is a lot more varied and complicated. The story is different, the setting very much so, etc.I would suggest waiting two weeks for the EA to end, however. Devs are hinting that to people on the forums and Discord as well. It looks like the content may double or triple in that release, and existing saves will no longer work. But if you are interested in the game, by all means get it and play in a couple weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: Super awesome so far! I started playing because I was told it was similar to Stardew Valley, and it IS somewhat similar, but it really is an awesome game in it's own right and doesn't need the comparison. _childDocuments_.review: Get ready for a relaxing time sink. Think of this game as a collector game, and you might not dislike it as much. As for me, I've had a fantastic time playing as Greywyn the orphan tycoon.A pair of orphan siblings are whisked away by their long lost uncle, to a fey filled land of dark secrets and mysteries to reveal. Childhood was a long, but relaxing grind, of learning how to farm, craft, fish, and get to know my fellow villagers. I want to make friends with everybody, but I fear that may take many lifetimes. At the end of the year I was surprised by the dark decision the village forced upon me, but after that I was made a fey offer I couldn't refuse, and now my legacy will go on forever. As an adult I have become a pretty terrible dungeoneer, but fortunately my deal keeps me alive... in some form or another. I fear there is a lot more to combat I have yet to know, or maybe I'm just bad.I now own 8 shops, and occasionally spend days personally managing them, or delegating to my employees. I order stock nearly every other day, learn to set prices, and get richer by the second. I find my apothecary to be the most profitable, although I prefer delegating there, as making medicine and learning traits is rather time consuming. Next being the blacksmith, and then my goods shop. I fear I don't manage my goods shop very well, and on top of it I am a terrible employer, paying only the lowest possible wages. I still manage to make money, and reputation, so who cares about the little guy. These villagers don't have the option to quit as long as I pay them, so I can be content with my riches.I enjoy the task of crafting, although it can be time consuming, and is not required. I could always increase my reputation, and buy stock if I wanted. Cooking, medicine making, and blacksmithing, all can be a nice distraction from the daily grind of friend making, farming, and dungeoneering. The land is vast, and exploration plenty. So many secrets to discover, skills to learn, and fish to find. I just wish finding love wasn't so difficult, I have yet to find love and make a family. I also wish increasing my stats wasn't so long.59 hours in, still a ton of things left to do, I fear I will be lost in the grind of Kynseed forever. I feel it is not a bad thing though, plenty of enjoyment to be had still.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable toybox of a game. Even after Big Build Update, I'm not finding a ton of narrative (a little more, though! Like an extra treat for making friends), but the systems and minigames are pretty fun and there are a lot of them. The additional gating of areas after Big Build frustrates my explorer impulses a little bit, but it does force you to get to know the villagers instead of, er, ignoring them. As I had been. How Big Build works with friend-making is so: you run into a broken bridge, you need to fix it. To fix it, you require friends (often with a certain stat level). To make friends, you need to give them gifts or do chores for them from the bulletin board. You do also need friends for the overall grind game (which expects you to be accumulating friendship and reputation) and if people like you enough, they'll let you use their trees and farms, and, at max friendship, give you a gift or a minor plotline.This is just a lengthy example of how Kynseed sandboxes. It's mostly about numbers going up and the progress rewards recently introduced with Big Build both accentuate that and make it a bit more satisfying (you are no longer waiting for hundreds of reputation points before you get a little ding). The systems that make numbers go up are all pretty decent - cooking is tactile and colorful, if still a little more confusing than it has to be (when it doubt, check help and then uh check it again). Combat feels crunchy. Exploration is dense. Getting high starred fruit and veg is still ... complex, but seems better signed. Etc. The narrative is sparse but has sparks of menace and interest. The quests are mere fetch quests, but can be done in a popcorned group and do give little bits of direction to your fishing and foraging endeavors, etc. It's a colorful numbers-go-up game, and I quite enjoy it on that level.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, even after several years Kynseed is not the next big Adventure/farm Sim you were hoping for.Pros:-Fun and witty writing (Excludes NPC dialog)-Fishing is enjoyable esp. after a couple of upgrades, no tedious minigame-Option to pay a wage or run your shops yourself-Fun art style, good looking weather effects-Different towns/regions have a lot of artistic character-Lore-Devs added character creation when asked to (should have been there to begin with but, I digress)-Story starts out strong, a cool sudden twist that is a lot of fun to experience, but fizzles out very quickly after that.-Combat systemCons:-Farming itself is almost wholly unnecessary and dull-There's a tedious freeloader NPC that curses your farm if you don't feed it everyday-No customization past your initial character + dye. No Home decoration, no layout design, no haircuts, no clothing changes, no pet colouring, No building fences or farming plots, no shop or town remodel, nothing.-NPC dialog pulls from a very small pool of lines-Shops become a chore to manage because NPCs wont order stock. There's a lack of balance, either you have so many stores you spend all your time going to them to order stock for them or mining so the blacksmiths have ore OR you have just a couple and reputation will take you in game years to earn-There doesn't seem to be any kind of satisfying pay off. Even after I defeated all the dungeons on harder settings, it didn't matter.-The grind. For everything. ''Masters'' need you to grind items to progress, but you have to rely on luck to get the drops needed eg. Monster parts at a specific rating. You can guarantee the rating by upping the difficulty but you can only hope the mobs spawn AND drop your items and not other items. Also you need 20 of them.-NPC 'final' friendship quests are very hit or miss-NPC romance dialog is lukewarm, they are just the same small pool of comments NPC reardless. A 'date' is just a small list of demands from the NPC then they go home.-Marriage quest list of tasks is tedious-Deep mines should have been an achievement but just became another annoyance thats solved by bottles of water or milk. -No maps for mines.Overall, I patiently waited years for development and Kynseed is just so unfulfilling that I need to drop it instead of hoping it'll get good after 1 more reputation level up or another 10 hours of play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty as hell and a little creepy (in a GOOD way)! I’m super excited about the progress this game is making and adore the level of detail put into every part of it. It’s beautiful and whimsical, but has a simmering undercurrent of “this feels like a brothers Grimm story when do I get eaten”. It’s really unique and doesn’t hold your hand too long, just long enough to give you a rough sense of the world and not spoil anything. The devs communicate really well with the community and are incredibly organized. They really deserve all the praise and respect they get for how well they keep us up to date on what’s going on behind the scenes. Definitely the best 10$ I’ve spent in a while!

_childDocuments_.review: Boring, minigame-ridden and shallow. Rather than elaborating or deepening the game mechanics, the developer decided that repetitive mini-games and mindless grinding would do the job just as well. Reskinned regions emulate content while essentially being the same. The various fast travel mechanics, for example, are repeatative copy pastes with minor differences. The developer masked useless redundancy as effort. Pretty packaging, boring content. Save your money, buy something more decent.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't Stardew Valley. It's something else that I find more fun. Basically every aspect is designed to reduce my irritation with it, the gameplay loop feels satisfying and there are no consequences for taking your time with the story. If you approach Kynseed rushing yourself, you'll feel very overwhelmed. But slowing down doesn't mean you miss out at all, which I prefer.A lack of depth in the NPC department kind of works in its favour. Each one is thought out with a small story and the abundance of them (plus the 'marry anyone') feature means it's easy and rewarding to make a lot of friends (something I never do in other farming sims). Time actually progresses, yes, but it settles into a good pace that doesn't necessitate the use of the generations mechanic, I'm looking forward to it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: This review is during early access. I have had so much fun with this game! I am absolutely gobsmacked by the size of the map and the number of NPCs I can interact with. Every area of the map has it's own unique character to explore. I've made it through the prologue and about a year of my first life at the time of this review. I've done a lot of farming, exploring, and playing with NPCs' emotions. I have not bought a shop, so I do not know anything about that mechanic yet. It's going to take so long to live my life and move on to the next one! I am worried that it will get too humdrum, but I am hopeful that they'll discover the perfect pace for the game. It seems that they are actively adding more interactive themes in the world, so I bet I won't run out of new things to do per generation by the time the game releases. The story is so whimsical and extremely quirky. I am in love with premise and I plan on actively playing the game as it develops. Even in early access I consider the game playable and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this game was getting some kind of update every now and then, I understand that some things take time but perhaps adding different mini games to pass the time and keep people engaged? I still think this game is incredibly charming yet it sadly cuts off in terms of the story aspect in a really unsatisfying way. This would be fine for a demo but for people who buy this game early it would be nice to know what kind of direction it's going.I would not recommend for people who want a story or character driven game as the story only lasts for about one hour of game play and characters are so interchangeable and forgettable.=======================================================================This game is somewhat reminiscent of rune factory or stardew in that relation building, combat, and crafting are all tied together with some very distinct differences. Whereas the two other games somewhat rely on a smaller cast of characters to make the world feel lived in kynseed has much more npcs to interact with, the problem however is that the npcs don't really feel alive. Sure they all have distinct personalities but unlike the other games where you can see how they interact with their families or even spend their free time kynseed has a lack of this and it makes interacting with people up to you finding their favorite item and gifting it over and over. You'll get recipes and kind letters in the mail sure but the only one you really focus on is your spouse.The offering day is probably one of the smartest features in this game that really makes you plan how you will spend your precious time. Want good ore for your smithy? At the detriment to other aspects you can get it for a week. Better quality or simply more fruits or crops? You can offer for that. Better mob drops? Yes. You just really need to pay attention to what curse you get based on your offerings. Curses such as stronger monsters and weaker weapons can really effect you when you try to kill a mob.Combat is a bit janky for me at least. Out of all the things you can do in the game i try to avoid it when i can. The monsters have certain moving patterns but it's sometimes hard to hit them and many have projectiles that can get annoying. (this aspect could be better if the items you got were rarer to gather by finding in the wild IE:sapplings)The shops are interesting and my favorite is the blacksmith as I get to make the tools i want. The system of favor within a town that can allow you to order higher tier ore is a bit of a grind but since the game encourages you to live many lives and spend a long time it can be somewhat forgiven. Hiring workers isn't something i was interested in as i just do the work and take the orders myself but ti does seem like a nice mechanic that can allow your store to become somewhat self sufficient, even being able to hire your family to work there.Having animals is somewhat interesting as there are individual stats for sheep or pigs that allow them to run faster, chickens produce eggs, and pigs can create manure for crops, dogs show dig spots where you get treasure, but you do have to take care of them. Every now and then chickens may not produce eggs, pigs or sheep won't let you ride them, or your animal may change color. These are signs you aren't taking care of your animals. Keep in mind they all eat different things. Overall the manure mechanic is the only really interesting aspect. The dig spot is actually kind of boring and gives you mostly small beans of money. Dig spots require better shovels to get deeper and while you can get items it's mostly bones.Right now the mentor mechanic is getting specific items and turning them in. You get more knowledge of the specific aspects your mentor teaches but it's not really that interesting either.The farming is the usual, you grow things in certain seasons and take care of them, the foraging being similar that certain things show up in specific seasons/weather/time of day and can be affected by blessings. Certain items are much more annoying to get because they spawn in certain locations in a specific time frame and are generally far from each other. One of my least favorite things to do is get wistle root for quests only slightly first before saplings.The quest boards are very good as you can find events as well as quests for certain towns. The world is broken up so far into three different towns where they each have their own quest boards that highlight events in the specific town as well as give quests for certain npcs in that town.FISHING! I absolutely adore the fishing in this game! You can train your cast to hit items or fish to just real them in, in my opinion much better than stardew fishing and much more fun.Hints in the game are interesting, you'll randomly find different pieces of paper that tell you about certain items that could describe them or help tell you in what condition you can find them and what areas they are found.Stats are leveled up by preforming specific tasks and make your performance in those tasks much better. They can level up depending on the blessing you get or slower depending on the curse.The story is very interesting but obviously not completely implemented in the game yet. You trade away years of your life in order to see the fairy realm. The being that took those years also wants your body after a certain amount of time has passed and will revive you from death in exchange for years of your life. Also acting as something of a shop keeper that will sell you boons for more of your life. After you first exchange your life you come back to see your adopted farther has died and your sister has now left the house. It is uncertain if the goal of the game is to eventually defeat the being that wants your life or to reunite with your sister, however as time passes in game your sister very well may be long dead before you reach her. Part of the game is also marrying and having children that you will eventually take over the body of.......

_childDocuments_.review: Having reached the 100+ hours mark, I felt it only right I leave a review!I waited 4 years for this game to purchase once launched, and boy have I enjoyed it. While there are bugs and a few improvements to be had, for a majority of my time I have thoroughly enjoyed it! One of my biggest frustration with the farm sim community is the constant comparison to titles like Stardew Valley. No where has this game claimed to BE that, and I think it unfair to do so. The story was that perfect blend of dark and light, and had me INVESTED at the end of the tutorial. There were so many moments I found myself moved by the world and lore, and I found myself sad when it was time to say goodbye to some characters. Although I WISH they could have more emphasis on each death, I DO understand it's not reasonable as generations pass. I LOVE the generation system. I honestly thought I wouldn't like it, but found myself rubbing my hands together, waiting to take over the next generation to see the changes that pass. The lore behind it is executed perfectly, and i am obsessed with our fae patron.I personally enjoy the dramatic art style, i know a lot of people want "pretty" characters, but I thought it very realistic and charming that people aren't same-faced at all. The job system is wonderful, and take my word for it to TRUST YOUR STAFF. I felt the need to stay in control, and the moment I assigned the npcs to it, I realized how silly I had been. I really enjoy building a familial empire. The only REAL complaints I have is that sometimes you go a little stir crazy wanting time to pass faster because you want to be able to progress with better stats. The animals could be a little more useful, but I am sure that can be improved on. I personally love the game giving tips through proverbs, but I wish some of them had more impact. I ALMOST wish you couldn't get the boons the tips give until you find it. It would add a certain challenge to unlock outside of reading a wiki...If you've made it this far, what I'd impart to you is that this company has taken their dreams of a new type of farm game, and DROWNED it with lore and love. I think it's definitely worth the support, and I am really really happy for the studio, and wish them lots more success. Let my hours played tell the story!

_childDocuments_.review: A very tough one to review. So much to do that it's a very exhausting game since everything is so cumbersome and convoluted, with as much intent to punish players as reward them.Gives off a lot of Graveyard Keeper and Gleaner Heights vibes with its hidden dark undertones, and Rune Factory with its "toss in everything, including the kitchen sink" volume of gameplay choices...just not nearly as player-friendly as any of  them.Usually I like to play a LOT more before reviewing, and I will, but honestly, the time I did spend in the game to get through the trainer prologue has just exhausted me, and I hate fighting against game mechanics just to try to enjoy a game.So as much as I was eagerly waiting for this title to release in its full form, I feel that the game mechanics are so far below the bar set by other similar games, that I just have to put it aside and hope and pray for quality of life improvements to make it a much less boggy, tiresome struggle just to play, much less enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, if you're old like me you might remember that on ABC in the late 90s/early 00s they had a limited series about Merlin and there was a general obsession with Camelot/fantasy that felt super magical.This *feels* like that. The depth of lore, the humor, the ART STYLE. This game has heart, it has a vibrant identity that sets it apart from other "cozy farm sims". The roots run deep and can be dark, but it's such a compelling world that has been built here.8.5/10. It's definitely a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: Kynseed have really pulled me in with it's dreamy pixelart, witty and actually funny dialogues and great world to explore. You age in this game, and everyone else too. Babies turn to kids, old people die etc.This is not Stardew Valley, the world is bigger, it's heavier on the story, dialogue and quest side of things, and less farming and tending to animals even if that stuff is also here. Along with crafting mini-games that you have to master to get good items to either use or sell.Get the game if you want a cozy and atmospheric experience in a magical world full of small secrets, wacky people and loads of stuff to do that don't feel tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the concept for this game, and it really kills me to not be able to recommend it at this point in development.The atmosphere, music and areas are all so beautiful and the first 8 or so hours you'll be having fun exploring and collecting. However, after you've discovered everything in all areas the game gets pretty bland. There isn't much guidance for what you need to accomplish in the game, no meaningful overarching plot that I can determine by interacting with any characters.The characters are all very milk toast as well. You give them gifts to make them like you or do little fetch quests on the notice board to gain friendship, but there isn't a lot of dialogue that makes befriending anybody really all that worth it. The dating system is very boring, as you just walk around the map and the character just says "This is romantic" or something of the like... nothing is developed. This seems like a bit of an oversight, because the game seems to really be pushing for players to date and marry and have kids with the characters... so why can't we get characters with actual personalities? In Stardew Valley each character has distinct personalities, plots, etc to make dating and marrying enticing and fun, and give the game replay ability... none of that is involved here yet which is such a shame.There are things i do really like about the game. Being able to own a business rather than just farm is a fun change from other farming sims, and the combat system is pretty fun and very different than hack and slash combat in other farm sims. Something I always hated about other farming sims is that your kids never age, and having kids seems really pointless. So the concept of your kids aging up and taking over for you and your original character dying is very interesting. I just wish NPCs had more personality and back story. It's a big world filled with a lot of... nothing. I sincerely hope that with the next few updates the DEVs will be adding better dialogue, backstories and dating/marriage dialogues.
_childDocuments_.name: Kynseed

_childDocuments_.review: A weird one, for sure.Weird characters, weird + confused atmosphere, weird mechanics, weird story.But don't let that discourage you if you're into a farming sim that comes with a kick; Kynseed is certainly still an enjoyable time with what's there, despite its flaws.The last big update was Feb 12 2024 & hotfix on April 3 2024 as of this review.TLDR; Solid 7/10 that finds itself unfortunately heavily hindered by serious money scaling issues & too fast of a progression speed. If that alone was fixed, EASILY bumped to a 8.5/10.+ extensive tutorial that makes sure you've got your balance before kicking you out the gate+ more than enough to do in a day (and a lifetime ;D) that you'll find yourself becoming part of the insomniac club to keep the enterprise going+ no set bed times; no passing out at a set time at night, no forced sleeping schedule (except for children), and no rifled through pockets upon waking+ camp fires and inns you can use to sleep/pass time are all over the place, removing the need to go back home+ more than 1 method to teleport around map+ skill trees & shop perks! (๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧+ decent selection of customization options & furniture+ long live the glory of the pig-steed+ game does not force you to do (almost) anything you don't want to; just throw some employees at it and get that passive income while you do stuff you're interested in+ don't want to get married? No problem! Adopt some kids and boom, problem solved.+ multiple mini-games for crafting (that come with bulk crafting options, and can also be skipped by having employees do it)+ slightly more simplistic Megaman Battle Network-style combat that ends up being an enjoyable challenge (or a difficult one, if you're feeling spicy)+ feels feature complete and not in need of mods outside of personal QOL choices+ builders rejoice, there's fine tune placement of objects+ pun-tastic humour & plenty of personality+ monster design is on point+ Fae (albeit less dark than lore accurate)+/- while there IS a "golden path" mechanic called thatterways, they only show you the map you need to be on (or what mailbox you're looking for, rather than leading you to the person).+/- generally more demanding than something cozy like Stardew Valley; how much goes on, from festivals to auctions to sales to events to requests from multiple cities to goddess blessings to weather to multiple store management and etc, can get quickly overwhelming+/- dark undertones that very clearly existed have been removed, despite it making parts of the story incoherent and underwhelming :c+/- lot of the stuff villagers say is unhinged and/or out of nowhere (i.e: once I brought a dead rabbit to my mom and she threw it back outside. That's it, that's the story xD) +/- animals have the whole colored butthole constantly visible thing going on-/+ generic responses from NPCs that everyone uses flood both dialogue and mail; children have very few pieces of unique dialogue, subsequently turning every 5 year old into extremely articulate and respectful mini-adults that barely acknowledge your familial ties- the family/generational mechanic is presented as a core part of gameplay that heavily defines it, but uh...you don't actually have to use it. At all. Whatsoever. - The end game material meant for the final boss is obtainable at the start of the game without any special tricks or glitches, completely destroying the need to upgrade your tools in tiers.- the last boss is a joke in general. Added insult to injury:- skills level extremely fast, and it doesn't take much effort to fill out the required materials/crafts to fill out the skill trees - penalties for not sleeping are practically nonexistent, regardless of how long you keep the insomnia streak up- anyone who can get a grip on the systems and has moderate RPG/sim experience will finish 90-100% of the game within the 1st year, nevermind going 10+ years or a generation. I fully understand that life/farming sims are meant to be taken with a casual stride, but this is EXTREMELY fast progression to a bare bones ceiling. Doubly so for a game that presented itself as needing a whole family lineage to complete.- : Money and Renown are generated far too quickly through shops, and the cost you pay for every shop you purchase is pennies in comparison to the profit you'll gain in just a few days of having them. Said cost to buy them barely increases with each town, despite their profit margins being massively higher. With the challenges you'll complete up to unlocking the ability to buy said shops within the first 2 to 4 weeks of gameplay, you'll have more than enough money to buy 2 out of 3 shops in the first town. The mats you picked up along the way will be more than enough to stock them before you get the perks to increase order inventory and enough money to order. Perks that you gain passively.These 2 shops alone can allow you to immediately commence ignoring both Money and Renown for the remainder of the game. It does not take a lot of time for them to generate enough money to buy the next towns shops, and from there the remaining shops on the map. Even if you don't supply any of your own materials to them and solely restock through purchasing while having employees do the crafting, you will not run out of money. In fact, you'll be turned into Scrooge McDuck diving through gold piles.Click spoiler for exact numbers: - while you CAN order 50x of 1 item now, you cannot bulk order 50x of every item you want at once nor re-order everything you did last time without manually doing it every single time for every single store- the marriage system is as bare bones as it gets; any of their relatives do not become yours or acknowledge you as family (including if they're supposed to be your spouses kid pre-marriage) + it only takes 1 pie and 1 turn in before you start getting harassed daily for not making enough money on the shops even when you're making crazy amounts of gold x_x- time skip mechanic is irrelevant, nobody cares you were gone & shops pick up as if it's tomorrow instead of 10 years later XD- pixel art on humans is a hit or miss (with the majority being a miss, imo)- the lack of an "Order All" button for shop inventory is sorely missed with just 1 shop and is an absolute nightmare with 4+; makes the entire shop management system a tedious chore that gets abandoned once enough money is made because of how much time it takes just to order everything- unlike everything else, cooking cannot be done by employees and there are absolutely no options available to order anything already cooked for shop inventory- unlike everything else, fish cannot be ordered for shop inventory even after you make the store a Fishmonger

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game unlike Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons, in my opinion, and is more than just running a farm and forming relationships with locals. While you can still do all that if you wish, in my experience, all that kind of went on the back-burner the moment I got out of the prologue and was allowed to leave the town. This is like the Fable series, with a bit more life sim thrown in it. Which makes absolute sense, as the devs are ex-Lionhead.Relationships themselves are much more simpler than those in other farm sims. You can learn more about an npc as you raise hearts with them, and some even have simple cutscenes recounting something that happened to them in the past. The things you learn are basic; one guy doesn't want to be a vegetarian, but is because of his wife. Another is a child of a Fae. You kind of just learn one "big" thing about them and that's the extent. However, it's very easy to make friends with the npcs, which is something I really like. It's less stressful, in my opinion, and easy to gain "FP" by running errands, or giving them items they like. I don't think there's "decay" either, that or it's very unnoticeable.Marriage (while I've only just gotten married in game) seems to take the Fable approach of "just come and see them every once and awhile". There's not much to marriage outside of raising heirs and having farm automation. Again, something I like. I don't want to be stressed about my marriage while adventuring, nor do I care about romance in a game that doesn't offer that sort of thing. You marry someone to help make you money, and I'm down with it.There's a lot in here that seems like a nod to the Fable series, which is comfy and nostalgic to me, as someone that's played the series since I was a kid. It's got that humour, along with game mechanics that are similar in ways. You even have the dog constantly barking at you because there's a dig spot nearby.From my understanding, this game is a "delivery" on a few of the promises Peter Molyneux made for the first Fable game, such as planting a tree and watching it grow, slowly growing old, and your children picking up the adventure where you left off once you kick the bucket.If you're looking for a game EXACTLY like SDV or HM/SoS, I would maybe look elsewhere, or watch people play this (past the prologue, as the game feels different playing as an adult vs being a kid) to form your own opinion on if you'd like it or not. If you don't like Fable, I have doubts that you'd like this game. But for those that do, this game could be right up your alley, ESPECIALLY if you liked the "life" activities in those games.Sorry to talk so much about Fable but it seems like this is not common knowledge!! Fable!!!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinking of buying this game, take it with a grain of salt. -- This is not a finished game.However, that doesn't mean it isn't fully worth it. Once you get into it (with patience), it's a really enjoyable experience.Let's start with a Pro's & Cons list, Pro's:The art is stunning and has been so wonderful to play in. The environment art is gorgeous, the minigames are really well polished, and personally though I've seen a few people complain about the "ugliness" of the characters, I think they're brilliant and really show each villager's personality. The devs have successfully done something other recent pixel art games seemed to have failed in recently - this is NOT a Stardew Valley game with slightly different graphics. If you loved SV, you've probably been looking for a game similar to it like I have and been disappointed by the amount of games that have basically just ripped off its entire story and gameplay. This game doesn't do that at all, and while it has some similar feelings to SV at times, it's completely unique in its gameplay and story.The minigames are really fun (for the most part). Baking pies is relaxing, the blacksmith minigame is profitable, and the whole apothecary gameplay with ingredients having traits you need to discover by finding proverbs throughout the map, it really adds to the game. Some of the minigame processes do need to be tweaked (please don't make me make another hellish jam)  but overall I've very much enjoyed the minigames.ENJOYABLE combat system. I'm not usually one for combat (you can imagine how much I hated mining in SV), but the combat system is really fun. You encounter combat by going into the three "Arenas" - Simplewood, Midwood and Toughwood. Each wood has a "depth" system and the further you go into the forest per round, the more difficult the bosses get. You can combat the increasing difficulty by developing your skills in Melee and Archery, crafting (or buying) potions and wards, cooking recipes that increase toughness, strength, etc and levelling up your weapons. So far, it's been a really rewarding experience, and it's also an excellent way to build reputation.USEFUL SPOUSES AND CHILDREN !!One of the bigger annoyances in other games like this have been the uselessness of spouses and children once you've married, however in this game you can get your spouse to go gathering for needed items in various locations, they can do chores with a rota you set, etc. EXCELLENT COMMUNITY.If you experience a bug or crashing, or if you have feedback or suggestions .. or if you just want to show that you named your baby "Ugly" and you find it hilarious, there is an official Kynseed discord you can join. You'll find the developers of Kynseed are really lovely and appreciate the feedback you have, and are working actively to make the game even better. CONS:As I said in the beginning, this is not a finished game. From what I can see from other reviews, at around 9-14 hours in, there's a massive lull in gameplay and a feeling of frustration you get where the game can become a slow grind and most of the tasks feel less like a quest, and more like a chore. HOLLOW NPCs.There's 83 NPCs you can talk to, and you can marry any NPC except for fae. The only issue is you're not very pushed to marry the NPCs, because while most of them have a good storyline when you're talking to them their daily interactions are very empty. At some points it really does feel like you're talking to the same character in a different skin .. 83 times. It's a pity, because a lot of them have very good concepts (Kane Hines and his dog obsession, Hazel Nutt and her cat obsession, Edna Teapott and her old messy relationship) but when it comes to day-to-day interactions, it's like talking to a placeholder you'd expect to find in an Early Access game because the character isn't fully implemented yet.Same goes for the main storyline involving your "sibling", who spends most of the time in the prologue being a dislikable ass you don't really talk to, so the whole betrayal arc feels forgettable and you don't feel the sense of guilt you're sort of supposed to. If the twin aspect was stronger, for example if you were to actually do tasks with your sibling, and if the NPCs around the village remarked the fact you were a twin it would feel more full.The other realms (Tír na nÓg & E'ergreen) are very obviously unfinished gameplay wise, and it really feels like a waste of time going there. The specific cleansing watter, special milk, eldersberry, shops etc seem to be the only reason either realms exist with the fae who occupy it feeling more like -- once again -- placeholders than NPCs you should be interested in, which makes for an empty world you quickly do an item collection round for rather than an otherworldly realm you're excited to step into. There's also a good few parts of Tír na nÓg where you see the whole game map ending when you go fishing (in the fishing spots closer to the edges of the map).A lot of the gameplay isn't intuitive, and you have to spend a lot of time going and looking up things in the Wiki and on the Discord if you don't want to be completely stumped. For a two week long tutorial prologue, there really aren't enough guides that explain quite a good amount of the core features. There's quite a bit of a slump you experience while playing initially after the prologue until the second time you return to the Circle, because rep is awkward to build up if you don't know where to go for it (combat), and if you're relying on the small amounts of rep from villagers you get while doing very repetitive tasks. Due to it being only recently fully released, there's quite a few bugs that build up in your mind and break your immersion a little - there's been times during the "I've Dropped One!" quests where the item I found just disappears from my inventory and the task list still asks me to return the item, and just small things like that which negate the fun experience little by little.TL:DR;Pros:- V nice art- Unique gameplay (unlike the other SV ripoffs that have come out this year)- (Mostly) fun minigames- Useful spouses and children- Responsive lovely developers who take feedback given wellCons:- NPCs can feel quite hollow- Storyline feels a bit weak in the beginning due to empty supportive characters (dislikable sibling)- Lull in enjoyable gameplay in the beginning after prologue - Gameplay not intuitive (spend a lot of time looking up guides)- Other realms unfinished, feel emptyOverall it is an enjoyable game if you have good patience and it has brilliant potential, but if you find you'd get too frustrated over the cons keep the game on your wishlist and observe the feedback over the next few updates the game devs are planning. I'm looking forward to seeing the future of this game ^^

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very beautiful game that was clearly made with a lot of love and care, but ultimately I cannot recommend it because it fails in its main purpose which is to entertain. Many times while playing Stardew Valley I wondered what it would be like to play with a larger map to forage, more NPCs to meet, more land to develop and more things to do; the answer is, not something very fun.The game has many different mechanics and things to do as well as an expansive map, which initially sparked my interest and kept me hooked for many hours straight while I finished the prologue, however by the time the world opens up I found myself wondering what was the point to all of them. You can craft potions to cure ailments and give status effects, but these don't ever seem to come into play, some NPCs mention needing this or that because they're feeling this or that way, and you can give them what you might think will help them, but there's no reaction to it, or none that is communicated to the player, each NPCs has three likes and three dislikes, which affect the relationship gain when you gift them, but you can similarly just gift them whatever you have an excess of and the relationship will grow anyway, slower, sure, but the days pass so fast and you have so many excess items just from foraging and farming that you can max relations in short time, you also don't need the items to make money, and the game discourages you from doing this because you can only sell a handful of items at each shop each day as they have a limited budget, and you don't even need to anyway since you get much more money from NPC quests, which are all fecth quests essentially.There's many different mini-games for each crafting kind, for example I got two see two different vesions of smithing, one for a bucket and one for a sword, two different ones for potion-making, and many for cooking, this is neat... in the beginning then it just kinda becomes a chore, luckily you can craft in bulk as well and you can have a little fun maxing out ingredient quality and doing well in the crafting to get higher level items, but we come back to the thing I mentioned in the last paragraph: for what? A single high-level item is all you can sell at any store and you wont need the money, you basically need to craft to fulfill more fetch quests, and to level up your skills, which give you the ability to... get more items every time you craft something. It's an endless loop of fetching, crafting, delivering, for no other reason that to see some previously destroyed buildings not be destroyed anymore, and more NPCs moving in, which you can then complete more fetching quests for.There's supposed to be a mechanic where you pass from generation to generation, but I didn't get to see it since apparently to marry someone you first have to cook a pie and then get some item, and then do a bunch of other things I didn't pay attention to since I was already running around completing other five fetch quests at the same time, and my character is only 20 years old at this point while she'll die at 50, minus a dozen years I can give up in exchange of some bonuses that I never saw mattered for anything.In all this game gives you too many things to do with very little reward for each of them, so you end up foregoing doing any of them and wondering what's next, do you continue the main story and possibly end the game with your first character and never seeing the heir mechanic? Do you spend hours maxing out everything for no apparent reason? Do you spend the time decorating your farm? (there's a handful of utility buildings but you'll have no reason to use them really for all I said before). And it's a ll shame because the writing is very good and the story seems quite interesting, particularly after it takes a dark turn during the prologue. I think this game should have focused on just two or at most three things, whether it was fleshing out the NPCs and relationship mechanics, crafting, exploration and combat, developing the farm, developing the town or the story, and while it is true that all of these are connected in gameplay mechanics, instead of complementing each other, they suffer for it.

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who bought the game in early access and have seen the roadmap slowly but surely being realised I want to first mention that this is a very special game. With that said, it should be mentioned that there is more (free) content planned in the near future, which will expand the game even further. And for those who likes to compare and might be wondering; no, this is not a new Stardew Valley. There are similarities, but the two games are also very different from each other. I feel Kynseed has everything you need for a fun pixelated life sim sandbox rpg, with a big focus on adventure and family. You live, you die and the new generation (your kids) takes over. The npcs (and there are MANY of them) also ages and eventually dies, leaving a new generation behind to take over. There are also fun (and a bit challenging) mini games associated with creating. For example, you want to cook? Be prepared to literally chop everything up and actually cook it yourself. The better you perform, the better results you get and I like this very much - that you actually have to invest time and effort into it to get good results!The same could be said for combat, which I find both fun and quite balanced in this game. It is not too hard, but not too easy either. Combat in Kynseed uses active time battle mechanics where the player can strategically dodge and defend against incoming attacks. Each action in battle costs stamina which regenerates and before diving into the different battle areas there is plenty of opportunity to both plan and prepare. An opportunity you should definitely take!There are of course other fun things to put time and effort into as well like farming, mining, fishing, helping npcs or why not owning and running a store! Kynseed also has a great sense of humour with a lot of fun and interesting dialogue and lore. The soundtrack is really beautiful and atmospheric and the different seasons in game looks very pretty. So is it worth the price tag? I honestly think so. A great addition to the collection for sure ^.^

_childDocuments_.review: Not only it is riddled with bugs, ranging from minor visual glitches to game-breaking bugs, but there also seems to be a lack of certainty surrounding the development and release. I've seen more than once a dev reply on the forum wishing that "" and saying that "". Look, there is nothing wrong with wanting to keep developing the game after launch; in fact, it's commendable, but updates following 1.0 release should focus on fixing and adding new stuff to the game, not in changing things that are already established because you didn't have the courage to commit to a vision while the game was in early access.But my biggest problem so far is with the devs lack of commitment in fixing the so constantly bugs.I've encountered a bug that has been reported multiple times for almost a week now, and there's still no satisfactory development on part of the devs. It feels that no one at the studio played the game before hitting the 1.0 button.I can't play anymore until this bug gets fixed, and from the looks of it, is going to take a long time for me to be able to play the game again. I fully understand that fixing bugs is not an easy task, but it took 5 days of constantly reporting for the devs to start asking for more information on the situation.TL;DR - game is bugged AF, 1.0 felt rushed, take devs too long to fix game breaking bugs

_childDocuments_.review: Was honestly surprised by the amount of negative reviews. The game is definitely unpolished, but the current product is almost a dream game for me. It's less of a structured "game" and more like a sandbox fantasy life sim. Like I said the game can seem disjointed, buggy, and unguided sometimes, but you can get lost so easily in several different aspects of the game. I bought a blacksmith pretty early in the game, and then hired the previous owners to work for me while i rake in the profits. The perk system and skill tree for just owning that one shop blew me away. You can raise your employee's skill level, use your store's reputation to order better stock or unlock other cool perks. It's such a time drainer and I love it. If you're like me and you get lost in sandboxy games, then I'd strongly recommend. If you have no patience for a game that doesnt have a clear sense of direction or purpose, then I wouldn't recommend.

Also if you love exploring, this may be the best farming game, as you are not that attached to the farm and you don´t need to come back to sleep everyday once you are old.I would prefer that the legacy system is more "needed", as you can honestly beat the game (the main story at least) with your first character, and there is no need for your legacy to grow to beat it.
