_childDocuments_.review: I kinda liked this game, but not enough to recommend it, it kinda felt slow, clunky and frustrating to just traverse normally at times. I can definitely see what they're going for, and I think this puzzle game is executed great, I just wish the movement didn't feel so sluggish.the story is interesting, I wish it were longer though, maybe had a different perspective or a followup?
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to like this game: its core mechanic is brilliant and well-executed, and the puzzles are generally challenging without being frustrating (with the exception of ), and the graphics are gorgeous. There are some frustrating crash-to-desktop bugs, though, and some weird POV-locking and stuttering that occurs when manipulating in-game objects.Unfortunately, I hated the music. The first song was fun, the second one was awful, and then the third one was so jarringly loud I turned the volume all the way down and didn't turn it back up again until the next cut-scene. And since I'm the kind of person who collects video game soundtracks, this is a major, major turn-off for me. But the worst is the storyline threading the whole thing together. So... yeah. This same mechanic employed in a game with a less obnoxious soundtrack and a less hackneyed, overwrought plot? Yes, please.DO buy this game if you like challenging, mind-bending puzzles, never get tired of Hallmark movies no matter how awful the scripting is, and enjoy the audio aesthetic of Sara Bareilles.DON'T buy this game if you can't stand warble-sprite-hipster-coffee-bar music or if you prefer plotlines that aren't lazy clichés.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I would cautiously recommend this game to lovers of puzzles out of interest if nothing else. The central mechanic is genuinely clever and the best of the puzzles are satisfying and fun, unfortunately others... could have stood a little more play-testing. Also certain puzzle ideas could have been expanded on to make the game both longer and better.On the negative side the controls are janktastic, not so much an issue with the majority of puzzles because they mostly rely on figuring out the trick and are then pretty generous with how accurate your actions have to be but definitely a problem when the solution is suddenly platforming or that one time there's a time limit.And finally there's the story, it's well told and well voice acted and basically the most polished part of the game, but.... it's the wrong story for this game, or perhaps this is the wrong game for that story or both. This game needed a story about worlds within worlds or repeating patterns or scale or something, that story needed game-play that tied into the repeating motif of a shared sketchbook.In conclusion, interesting game, but far from perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: BEAR IN MIND: There is apparently a game-breaking bug towards the end of this game.  I and others were able to get around it by restarting the level, but some weren't so lucky, so keep this in mind when buying and for this reason (as well as in general) I'd recommend getting this at a steep sale.  Unless you somehow get really, really emotionally invested, then the last few minutes aren't so special that you'll feel really cheated out of the experience, though.  (Imho the really cool ♥♥♥♥ is a couple levels before that.)So that said: I really enjoyed the gameplay and the physics.  I managed to escape the Maquette to game-breaking levels, repeatedly, and had a great time with that.  There's an eeriness to being in the larger versions that the game really leans into, and I found most of the physics-based puzzles clever, but arranging things in the smallest Maquette (and even in the larger one) can be really finicky (especially if you're engineering a plan to escape to places the game emphatically doesn't want you to go).  I had some nice little "aha!" moments and some times I had to check a walkthrough (I kept forgetting you can technically achieve goals in any size of Maquette) and the later levels actually get incredibly spectacular.  There's a specific image that will absolutely haunt me (in a good way) and no doubt be a source of inspiration in the future.That said, there's like...a story to this?  With some kind of a romance?  Idk, it seems to have absolutely nothing to do with the Maquette except as a physical representation of the world created by the characters' relationship, but it's honestly so loosely connected that it feels like the story got slapped on top of the gimmick in a hurry.  I like the sketching motif, and how the drawings change to reflect the characters' emotional perspectives, and maybe if it had gone a little deeper with the story or created a way to more clearly tie the relationship to the level design then I would like it more.  As it stands though, it's a really good idea for a game that could definitely be more fleshed out in its execution, and a really boring story that seems to be trying to Dear Esther a game that doesn't need it.  I'm reminded of Mind: Path to Thalamus, which had the same entrancing visuals paired with a story that I absolutely could not have cared less about.Tl;dr: Play it for the visuals and the gimmick, it's not for people who need a well-rounded story with their game, and be mindful of the game-breaking bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: At the start of the game, I was worried the plot could turn out to be about yet another depressed teenager. Fortunately, it isn't. Maquette feels like a mix of  and  but features its own creative mechanics too. It's rather interesting how the sketchbook pages take form in the maquette, and the puzzles are very intuitive, although not too easy either. You'd expect a game like this to be easy to softlock or glitch, but they've done a great job checking whether there are invisible walls where needed, and sometimes going out of bounds is even part of the puzzle. Oh, and the soundtrack is fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: Maquette's beautiful aesthetics and a fascinating central mechanic is ultimately let down by lack of depth in either direction. The product results in an unpolished, linear walking adventure where the author shares a personal love tale that fails to transcend to a universal theme.Traversing the world and exploring begins exciting and full of potential, but the player is rarely rewarded for this exploration. More often than not, the player is punished with flat, expansive areas that have no visual design to indicate accessible paths. Invisible barriers and transparent, unfinished textures are common. Twice I was forced to reload an area: once after exploring some ruins and finding myself stuck in geometry and once after accidentally hitting a trigger through a wall and soft-locking.Accompanying this is a folk score that plays upon hitting key checkpoints. Despite being a fan of this genre, the lyric-heavy music feels entirely unfamiliar and out of place in this sort of game.All told, this is a pass. Look instead at the much better and highly polished inspirations for this game: The Witness, Outer Wilds, Antichamber, and Portal all surpass Maquette.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Maquette. The puzzles are absolutely brilliant, it's a really cool concept, and the game is short enough that it doesn't outstay its welcome. I love these kind of cheap, short, interesting games that explore a novel concept like this. To be honest the story was kind of bland, but it didn't really get in the way of the puzzles so 🤷‍♀️. It may not be up there with like, Portal or Talos Principle or the Witness, but it's still a cool, well-made puzzle game that's worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: Maquette didn't lose me right away. I was drawn in by the promise of an interesting story, really good music, and puzzle mechanics with lots of potential. The first thing that took me out of it was how poorly the game runs. My computer can run much more graphically high-end games than this, but Maquette had a choppy framerate and multiple crash bugs for me, and the game stutters when it transitions to cutscene. As I played through the rest of the game, the rest of the promising elements lost their luster. The music only lasts for a couple of minutes on every level before being replaced by ambience. The story is relatable, but relatability doesn't immediately make a story interesting, and the story of Maquette is not interesting at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed Maquette a lot. The environments and visual effects are quite interesting. The puzzles were a good mix of ideas. I couldn't figure out a couple of them, but the ones I did figure out left me feeling all kinds of proud of myself. I'm glad you can mute the music. If there was a story-free game mode, it would have been twice as good. It seemed like every time I was really starting to enjoy myself, there would be a snippet of someone's failing relationship that I would have to suffer through before I could continue. Why would you build a game around a failing relationship?!?! It's such a downer and I don't know or care about the random people having the trouble anyway. Totally weird and annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and beautiful puzzle game, with a unique recursive mechanic that feels like a fresh new challenge, just like the best puzzle games have. In order to solve any puzzle, you'll need to think outside the box in terms of scale and well, recursion. It also has a gorgeous mind-bending setting that fits the gameplay perfectly. And, it's all tied by a touching and relatable story about a relationship. Don't miss out on this one, it's one of the most unique puzzlers you'll find on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: First, the primary reason I would not recommend this game: It's clearly labeled for full controller support. While it could've worked for some people, I and others had a bug where it would not accept button input. Rebinding doesn't work either since the developer used incorrect input settings. From Discussions posts, it sounds like the cause was identified by users but this wasn't addressed by the dev in the year+ since release. The game's charming enough, with a couple of clever puzzles, but not much that hasn't been done before and, arguably, better. Maquette seems to be, itself, a model or toy meant to contain the story they wanted to tell. Honestly, a couple of story segments felt on point and packed a punch, but on the whole started to feel trite and forced.A puzzle game shouldn't force a middling story on a player and a story/experience game shouldn't have puzzles this finicky. While it's mostly good at guiding objects to correct orientations, the times when it's not make me somewhat relieved I couldn't play with a controller. Overall, I can't recommend this to people at full price, but at a deep discount playing through the first few levels might be worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I had to sit on writing this review for a few weeks before finally deciding to do it because it feels bad to write a negative review for a game which is so close to being excellent. Firstly, there is so much to praise about Maquette. The visuals, the music, the voice acting, the general story, the creativity - there are a lot of things it does exceptionally well. The art direction in particular is fantastic, and there are a lot of moments which are genuinely stunning - especially near the beginning, as well as towards the end. The way it incorporates full-band music as well as emotive, believable voice acting truly brings the story it wants to tell to life. Honestly, if i was watching someone play this game, I would have no issue 1000% recommending it without issue.However, I played it. And it had a ton of issues. There were multiple times where I got completely soft-locked - key objects clipping through the ground, getting trapped in rooms, etc. Though, when it comes to getting trapped, near the end of the game they tell you to hold Triangle (on a PS4 controller) to reset to the center of the level - this would have been great to know during the tutorial, because I had to reset multiple times and lost tons of progress along the way. I'd tried every button on the controller to try and reset, but wasn't aware of the hold. Though, ultimately that's my fault, again if it had been present during the tutorial rather than only showing up during the last 20 minutes, it would have made a huge difference.Beyond that, the controls were supremely bad in certain spots - especially in the latter half of the game. Some puzzles demanded far more precision than the systems allowed for, and beyond that, doing simple actions like rotation of objects started having effects on the player character. Things like doing a few rotations making the character randomly teleport, and also when moving the object in question, sometimes it would flip the camera around so that you constantly had to re-orient yourself. There were many more issues I encountered of this nature, but the point is that finishing the game was actively unpleasant in the last few hours - which is really unfortunate for a relatively short game. Now, to be noted, I played the game on launch day and have not replayed it since patches were issued, so I cannot offer any insight as to whether these problems have since been ironed out. If they have, then I would recommend it; but I can only express my experience with the game, and while I greatly enjoyed parts of it, there was just too much struggle to truly enjoy it. In short, it's a really great game which is unfortunately encased within a fairly bad game. I do hope that patches can improve the encountered issues; but as it stands from my personal experience, I cannot recommend Maquette.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: Love the story, voice acting, music, and game mechanics. The controls can get frustrating in parts and it can lead you to miss solutions to the puzzles. The game is beautiful and the recursive puzzle design is great. The ability to switch between different levels is brilliant and leads to some fantastic eureka moments.The only complaint I have is with the controls. When placing items, they will get stuck on geometry and land slightly off. The jumping is very restrictive; making it feel like you can't make jumps. It seems to have a large horizontal length, but a small height and in some places jumping just doesn't work. Missed a solution because of that weird jump arc. Finally, it would be helpful if there was a run button. Sometimes my walk speed would accelerate and then slow to a crawl for seemingly no reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: This kinda sucks to write, because I was really pulling for this game to live up to what I was wanting it to be, but it just kinda didn't. First off, the game doesn't really feel nice to play. I get that it's a bit hard to get player movement down, especially when things are changing size constantly, but this game just generally feels clunky to play. Ultimately, it really focuses straight in on the story, which would be fine, aside from the fact that I knew almost exactly what was going to happen pretty much from the start. I kept waiting for it to subvert my expectations, but it just didn't. Because of the ways that the environment reflects the story, I really could've seen this game being a really good one if they just straight up removed the voices and writing from the game. There are a ton of symbols that could've made the story satisfying to figure out and piece together, instead of one that disappoints with its simplicity. The puzzles are unfortunately pretty one-note. There are also many points where the game has solutions that are unbelievably easy, but incredibly frustrating to figure out, which I would attribute to the many distractions within the area you're in at any given point. It's absolutely a really pretty game, but it just feels like it doesn't fit the game that was created around it. It's definitely hard not to focus on the negatives, especially because I generally would say that I had an alright time with this game. In terms of things it does well, I'd say that the voice acting is pretty alright, as well as the music. Obviously the visuals are pretty nice, and the basic idea behind all the puzzles is solid. The problems arise when the game tries to force its strengths into the rest of the game, which just ends up feeling really awkward. Overall, I would honestly probably say it's an alright game. But I would say with pretty solid certainty that this game doesn't live up to the marketing or the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: There were a lot of things I did not like in the first chapters of the game - there was a lot of guessing about what to do and where to go which I think needed a bit more consideration. Later, when I figured out how the maquette works that was not an issue. I enjoyed the puzzles but I would like if there was more of them.I did not care for the story, it was uninteresting. Voice acting was good but the script was a bit generic. I get the relation of the environment to the story but it was all on the nose. The music choice was unusual for a video game but much like other things in this game. The last level - the exchange - was probably the best but it also crashed a bunch in that one.If you were let down by Superliminal or Manifold Garden like I was, this is how it should've been done.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game. From the visuals to the music (Love the choice of songs from you guys at Graceful Decay, it plants the game firmly in a time, location and atmosphere. So many artists that I never heard of before as well!) to the gameplay, to the story. I was gripped the entire way through. I wish there were more of these types of smaller, intimate games that want to tell a story. Great game guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It's a cool concept, the potential is huge, and for about  20% of the game, they nailed it. For the other 80% of the game, they totally missed the mark. To put it bluntly, this should really be an early access release. There are tons of invisible walls, many places where you can see through gaps between models and terrain. Speaking of which, the terrain is janky with tons of places where you can walk where you shouldn't, and others where you can't walk where you really should be able to. This game starts off really strong, super atmospheric. I'm not normally into these kind of emotional story games, but the mechanics were enough to draw me in. But once you get through the first level or so, the polish drops off and the cracks begin to show up. Most of the puzzles require noticing a tiny detail (for example, the shape of a fence so you can pass a crystal through it, or that there is a dim light on an inaccessable ledge).  Beyond that, I can't help but feel a bit railroaded. All the levels tend to have one item at a time, which you use on one puzzle, which has one answer. There are few real puzzles in this game, the rest are either incredibly easy, or like mentioned above, aren't actually puzzles. Basically, the game railroads you the entire time. I expected to have lots of cool adventures using the size changing, but it's mostly reserved for items and when you do change size, it's just to walk from point A to point B. I thought I'd be walking through lots of nooks in houses, along rafters and other similar things like in games such as Chibi Robo, Minish Cap and really any RPG where you have size changing and puzzles. Nah, almost none of that, and where there is some, it's just, 'Enter crack in wall, collect item, walk out and get big again.' The  is huge for all sorts of cool things, but sadly, the game just doesn't do any of them somehow. Being tiny should be cool, in this game, it's just a chore. Not to mention the controls are god awful. Trying to put down items is a nightmare. The game has a mechanic where you can't put down an item if it doesn't fit, but like all other elements of the game, it's totally inaccurate and often won't let you place things. In addition, you can't place items down near places they activate (there is a level centered around using crystals to pass forcefields, if your crystal is less than a mile from the forcefield, good luck putting it down). At this point, I've written more than most people would read and haven't even scratched the surface. If you've read this far, I suggest you just watch a lets play, you'll get waaaaay more out of it than actually playing through the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumb very slightly down -- definitely a title where I wish Steam's review system had more granularity than just thumbs up or thumbs down.The good:* very pretty* nifty concept for a 3d puzzler* nice music (dunno if it's original for the game?)The meh:* very short game* the framing story was *eyeroll* -- game would've been better without it* walk speed at higher, uh, zoom levels was painfully slow -- holding shift should've doubled your speed instead of halving it (never needed to go slower)The bad:* positioning controls for objects were frustratingly titchy for a couple puzzles* BUGS -- ran into three (objects getting stuck in "place" mode, except it wouldn't let me drop them or pull them back, necessitating a reload; on the final level, hitting F sometimes put me under the dome instead of inside it, requiring a restart; and, worst of all, a lever on the final lever failed to work properly, and I wasted a bunch of time before looking it up and learning it was a bug, necessitating a reastart)All told, some cool ideas in it, but not enough real meat to it. Probably spent three "real" hours finishing it (discounting the time wasted on bugs or AFK), which would've been two if I'd been able to run faster.Once the fix some of the bugs, it'll be worth a look, but IMHO it's a stretch at $20. Would be a good $10 game, assuming you're into funky puzzlers and/or overly mopey walking simulators.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a unique game. I went into it thinking it was like superliminal due to the trailer, but it is honestly its own thing. While solving puzzles you are hearing snippets of a relationship between two individuals, and it tells their story while you play the game.I personally enjoyed the puzzles far more than their story, but you may like it more for the latter.Nice for what it was, don't regret my time spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: This could've been great, but it wasn't.This is a walking simulator with a dull story (I was yawning the whole time, and holding W didn't help with that).The gimmick is not utilised in any challenging manner (it's mainly for placing objects at 3 different scales), and objects can easily get stuck on other objects, which makes interactions awkward and annoying.The exploration is unrewarding since the world is empty bar the floating text. I've tried to find something interesting to look at, but have gotten only extra minutes of walking, at times in complete silence.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Maquette has wonderful world design and neat puzzles, but the story falls flat and the sparse content may not live up to the price point. If you like puzzle games and walking simulators, you’ll probably have a good time! If you’re looking for anything other than those exact two things, you’re unlikely to find good value in this.Maquette is a puzzle/walking game that attempts to take the player on a physical journey through the emotional lifespan of a shattered relationship. You are guided by the words of the man remembering it, Michael, and solve puzzles to make your way through worlds that he and his partner, Kenzie, once imagined together.These worlds are easily the best aspect of Maquette. They’re colorful, imaginative, varied and cinematic, and even though it requires a great deal of walking back and forth through them, I rarely tired of the many unique vistas on offer.In these levels the world is recursive, meaning that there is a smaller copy of the world inside the one you’re in, as well as a larger one outside of it. They do some neat things with this concept, and the puzzles, though somewhat sparse, do have cool moments. There is a notable lack of guidance which can be frustrating, but I didn’t run across anything I couldn’t puzzle out within a few minutes of experimenting.I ran into a few bugs, mostly harmless visual issues, but there were some terrain clipping issues, and a puzzle in the second to last level that was very glitchy when placing objects. Remember that you can press and hold F to teleport back to the center of the level! The game would also stutter for a few frames whenever I triggered a story event, and my computer is no slouch (i7-8700K, RX 5700XT, 32GB RAM) so it seems to still need some optimizations.I am an avid puzzle fan, and no stranger to walking-simulator type games, but I will say I felt a bit lukewarm on this one. First off, it is short. It took me 4 hours to complete the story, and I took my time. Somehow though, it still felt empty. The puzzles and story bits often act more as breadcrumbs leading you on long walks through levels than as the real meat of the game.Maquette starts out story-heavy and puzzle-light at the start and slowly shifts that balance the other direction as you progress. Some earlier puzzles can be simple to the point of tedious, but there were satisfying challenges in later sections. Nothing on par with a Portal or a Talos Principle, but a solid showing, nonetheless. The story on the other hand, is the same level of lukewarm the entire way through. The voice acting is great, but the writing is trite and predictable, and by the end I was largely indifferent to the narrator’s emotional journey. Turns out that immaturity and poor communication skills destroy relationships. Who knew?The real tragedy of this story is in how this stale narrative causes the game to sabotage itself. The conceit is that the world reflects the events and emotional arcs of the story, but these environments end up telling a far more compelling tale than the story they are meant to reflect. The breathtaking worlds of infinite scale are undermined by the banal writing, and the story’s blandness is in turn dwarfed by the emotion of the world built to convey it.I did enjoy my time with Maquette! I think it has fantastic visual design and innovative puzzle concepts that keep the game afloat despite the dead weight of the narrative. If it sounds up your alley, wait for a sale and give it a shot! Either way, thanks for reading!
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful mind-bendy puzzles, which were actually challenging at times. The way the background would repeat out into infinity and create booming sounds when you placed items was quite satisfying.I gotta be honest, I turned the music off pretty early on. This is why people generally use atmospheric music in games, and not potentially-polarising bands.Would recommend as long as you can deal with the quite personal relationship narrative stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: A totally fine little game. Its very pretty and has some interesting puzzles, but its kind of half puzzle game half walking simulator. It has a cute little story about a relationship, but is more focused on the feelings and experiences of relationship beginning and troubles than having much to say about that experience, so depending on your taste that may be cool gel well with the atmosphere or may seem thin and make it seem to drag between puzzles. Also its very linear, it doesn't necessarily introduce some mechanics well (like crystals removing colored fences, y'know like they do), and can swing without warning from conceptual puzzle to just a jumping puzzle, so a wiki can be handy for not getting frustrated.But a nice little game for 3-4 hours. Neat, but not spectacular.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautifully designed short game; in terms of story, style and music.Very reminiscent of Superliminal, but does not expand on the gameplay elements to the same extent.Expect a more watered-down, walking experience in terms of gameplay. Overall still very fun with decent replay-ability.Maquette is definitely more story-centric than similar games in its class.The story being the main focus it starts of cringy but ends up being quite beautiful not only in story but also in artstyle and its absolutely fantastic music. It also offers speedrunning opportunities similar to other games in its class which is quite fun.Overall would definitely recommend if you enjoy short stories with an added element of unique gameplay that focuses on challenging the way you approach obstacles.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: overall I recommend. the gameplay is great and the puzzles, while short were alright and presented enough of a challenge to be a puzzle but not enough to be obscure. the game was very short (whole game completed in 2.4 hours with me being distracted and alt+tabbing often) but the quality is there and I don't think I regret spending the full price on it. the story was very cliche and I didn't really understand how it interacted with the environments of some of the puzzles, I would have been skipping the forced cutscenes but... they're forced... and don't include any kind of skip function and remove your ability to bring up the pause menu while playing which is just honestly very annoying as I really just wanted to play the puzzles because the concept was cool. other than that the story is passable, dialogue is written well enough and the voice acting was very well done IMO.there were a few times where I was able to softlock myself just due to how I was exploring the game as well as getting stuck in between some geometry of a puzzle element and a wall. the game only tells you about the reset key in the final level so I had to restart from checkpoint and lost a couple minutes of progress, definitely a minus but the game autosaved enough to where it wasn't an issue to restart from the last "checkpoint" for me. (I also found a way to escape the map completely and found that there's only three layers you can actually walk on before falling out of the world)
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: When purchasing Maquette I expected new types of puzzles because of the recursion effect - which I got: Most of the riddles weren't two hard once you understand the concept but a few of them took a bit longer to figure out. All of them were interesting and different compared to other games I played.But what I didn't expect was the deep emotional story of a relationship whose mood is reflected in the color and structures of each chapter. The soundtrack adds a lot to that.I would have loved if the game was a bit longer though (took me 4,5 hours for the first playthrough and 2,5 hours to get the missing achievments) but I defintely recommend it to everyone who likes storytelling and puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I was  excited for this game, and immediately purchased and downloaded it as soon as it was possible on Steam. I grew up with games that used to be called "adventure games" but today are generally labelled "walking simulators". 'Myst' was the first computer game I played and ended up being hugely influential on my gaming tastes along with its sequel 'Riven' and then the forgotten classic 'Obsidian'.So obviously a game like 'Maquette' immediately piqued my interest and I waited and watched for any updates on it that I could find, especially after finishing 'The Witness', I  something to fill that adventure/walking/puzzle game void that was left.'Maquette' starts out wonderfully and bursting full of character and promise. The visuals are stellar and never get repetitive, and the puzzles ramp up in difficulty very nicely. The thinking behind the mechanics are well thought out and solutions were many times surprising and unexpected. Also the music selections were distinctive matching well to the DIY/sketchbook-style visuals and sound design were a nice surprise and high quality. The only criticism I have of the gameplay is some out of left-field 'platforming' type sections (using jumping to get to different platforms) that come out of nowhere and seemed so different to the rest of the puzzles that they stood out poorly and what made it worse was the controls are not well suited to platforming. But other than some weird platforming sections, the recursive nature of the puzzles is truly magnificent and the visuals are surreal, painterly and add such incredible depth to the puzzles themselves.Unfortunately the gorgeous visuals and fascinating puzzle mechanics are tied to a story that is cloyingly maudlin and predictable. I played this game with my husband and we were both able to predict the exact story beats the script hits. I don't mind a romance story at all, but this was  rote. The story starts out fine, and is a nice meet-cute story that is injected with personality and vibrancy via Bryce Dallas-Howard and Seth Gabel's natural chemistry in the voice acting. But, by around the halfway point the story flat-lines hard to painful predictability and not even their considerable acting talent can defibrillate it back to life.Which was just  a damn shame. Had this game employed a writer that didn't rely on simplistic sappy cliches, or banal romcom characterization and could meet the creativity of the puzzles and visuals this game would have been truly something special. As it stands, I will still recommend it to people due to the ingenious idea of the central puzzle mechanic and creative beautiful visuals but it will come with a huge asterisk disclaimer to ignore the story and come up with your own because it will be infinitely better than what you're presented with in the game.:  /
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience marred only slightly by some obscure puzzle solutions and a few opportunities to accidentally softlock the game. Fortunately the levels are short enough and the autosaves (and regular saves) alleviate the issues of having to redo any puzzles. I imagine a couple of patches and this game will be among some of the greats.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I am so deeply disappointed in this game. Absolutely gorgeous art direction with buggy, jerky controls, extremely simple puzzles (except when you miss a hint or the mechanics aren't functioning correctly), an under-utilized recursion mechanic blended with an extremely bland relationship story that's overly drawn out with long, simply-animated cutscenes with voiceover. Feels like the game is 15% basic puzzles and 85% generic relationship story. I've been following this game for almost a year now and it's such a letdown.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: I was cautiously excited about this game.Ultimately, it tried to present itself as something that would push the boundaries of this nesting-doll world design - something which has been done well in other proof-of-concept projects.What I ended up paying over 20 CAD for is really just a simplification of those ideas; immensely limited, and employed only to solve mildly frustrating puzzles which unlock incredibly unpleasant, unskippable narrative scenes.All of this I forgive; it's reasonably fun to play, albeit quite overpriced and complete with some fairly serious bugs and oversights.It's smaller details that really put me off. Untextured polygons are visible in many places, which for a game of such limited scope and design complexity is quite disappointing. It was trivial for me to break the apparent boundaries of the game world and fall off the map, while proving that the Maquette itself was not nearly as interesting or expansive as it tried to seem; that's fine, there have to be limits, but they did such a bad job of hiding it that I broke my immersion effortlessly. This whole thing feels like it was rushed out the door, where just a bit of extra care could have covered up the shortcomings of this product.It's fine, but I would not pay more than 10 CAD for the experience. I feel like I bought a demo, and it didn't even have the usual "early access" assurance which keeps me away from projects like this.Sorry Annapurna, you folks usually make good calls.
_childDocuments_.name: Maquette

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all about the story. There are varying levels of puzzles to solve, but they are used to progress the story, not the other way around.If you're expecting purely a puzzle game, you will be disappointed. But if you're looking for an emotional story with some puzzles along the way, you came to the right place.

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to choose thumbs down and mention some of the good things and bad but I decided for thumbs up and you already read the positives.  This was an OK game, but it could be really good, not great, if they fixed the controls.  Half the time you feel like you are fighting with the controls.  The puzzles; instead of feeling  like you are figuring out the puzzle and trying to find a way to solve it, you wrack your brain for hours and then give up only to find out that the solution is a trick. The game leads you to the clues on how to solve the puzzle and then you find out that the solution is in a completely different direction. Half of the puzzles just felt like dirty rotten tricks.  I still had some fun.  It was fun feeling like a giant and also feeling like a Lilliputian.  So in spite of all  of the problems, I still say get it on sale and have some fun, maybe. _childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this.  Some of the puzzles are very clever and the storytelling and aesthetic are great.However, this game is so frustrating in so many ways I cannot possibly recommend it.  The seemingly simple controls are totally non-intuitive and really janky. There are frequently solutions that look like they should work that just don't because the janky physics arbitrarily block them from working.  At certain points it feels like movement is PAINFULLY slow which means making mistakes takes forever and is extremely frustrating.  The game does a really poor job of telling you what your actual objective is, since the game progresses by you just being in the right place at the right time. I have a couple times already solved the puzzle and not realized it because I didn't do the exact thing needed to trigger the cutscene. The environment frequently gets in the way of the puzzles, particularly when there is platforming involved, because it isn't clear what you will or will not be able to jump on or how far or close you need to be to interact with various elements.Worst of all though: most of the puzzles are not fun. It is a lot of find the one place to put the object you have that makes it so you can go somewhere you haven't gone before.  These kinds of puzzles are either trivially easy or basically impossible without looking up the answer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game bridges a story and puzzles in a 50/50 balance. It took me around 4 hours to complete. _childDocuments_.review: + Purdy+ Great soundtrack+ Great voice acting+ Good puzzles+ Story coupled with art and sound direction is emotionally compelling= Story is otherwise pretty run-of-the-mill if you look at the genre of the text itself, but is not heavily represented in games= Short, but not too short (took me about 4 hours)= Keybinding, but not all keys- Some of the "a ha!" moments in this game are just a bit too elusive, mainly due to cues that are a bit too subtle*- Some of the puzzles are more "half-life 2-esque"; a little too finicky with a little too much emphasis on the physics engine to really make you feel smart**- Near the end of the game, one of the puzzles wrestles with your controls, likely because of the aforementioned slightly jank physics coupled with indie controlsVerdict: Grab on sale* I'm actually pretty sure I solved a puzzle or two wrong, but I have no idea from the feedback the game gave me whether or not it actually was, and I saw no hint system or a gradual emphasis on particular cues like a slow color flash, or a word becoming bold.** One of the puzzles I figured out in like 30 seconds, but the controls were so finicky that I thought I was doing it wrong, and made the puzzle take like 10 minutes. _childDocuments_.review: it just feels pretty raw and amateurish on many levels.first, the story is completely forgettable and has nothing to do with the game. it seems that now "solve some puzzles - get fed some cheap unrelated story dialog" is almost a de facto standard in "indy puzzlers", and i hate it. manifold garden worked just fine without a story, or if you feel the game absolutely must have one, make it fit the game.but i would totally forgive any story missteps of the gameplay was great. unfortunately, it's not quite there. it's often hard to tell an intended solution from an unintended one. one can see how they tried to twist the consistency of the rules to enforce their "correct" solutions, often failing and only encouraging the player to seek a way to break them (well, at least in my case). for instance, an object you hold won't push other objects - unless those objects are still moving. so you want to push one crystal with another? just make one crystal move and push it before it falls asleep. there's the usual staff like invisible walls, things you can or can't jump on, etc. overall, control feels very imprecise and janky. i think i only liked one puzzle (the one with 3 keys), and it was in the final chapter, which deviates from the general "maquette" formula. like the others said, the world-within-a-word mechanic does feel underexplored, but i'm actually not sure if there are ways to make more of it than they did, at least when the world it static. possibly it's just shallow past the initial wow.generally, i feel that superliminal explored similar concepts better.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a hard time with enjoying this game, especially knowing that it could take players anywhere between 2-4 hours on a $20 base price. I'm sorry that I'd have to mention that up front, but there are a few more reasons why this game kinda left me disappointed:- The narrative (in a sort of predictable fashion to me) is about how a romantic relationship begins optimistically, but then slowly starts to deteriorate. I don't feel like critiquing the contents of the narrative itself too much, but I didn't feel engaged with it. Maybe the narrative is only meant for people who've had a messy romantic relationship before.- The gameplay can be tricky and convoluted (mostly cuz you're left to figure things out for yourself) but it also doesn't seem to mesh well with the narrative for me. How is a game in a paradoxical universe supposed to make sense with a love story? Either there's no connection that justifies it, or I just don't get it.- There's no advanced graphics settings, which is an absolute shame. Fortunately, there are essential options like fullscreen toggle and an FOV slider, but not advanced settings to adjust individual graphic effects. So I guess my only options are to fiddle with the Low, Medium, and High graphics settings and I'll still get fluctuating framerates no matter what I choose?Other than that, the game looks amazing! I do appreciate the visuals, environment art, and the music, but I guess it all didn't leave me feeling amazed by the end of the game.If you really want to try Maquette, I'd get it on sale. If you're on the fence about buying this game, then take the reviews into consideration first.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun puzzle game. Honestly, it was a bit shorter than I would have liked, with it only taking 5 and a half hours, but I don't mind that too much. I'll definitely play it at least one more time. (I'm writing this after my first play though.) There was only one place where I got so stumped I ended up trying something that I knew wouldn't work and got softlocked. (Come on, like you never tried to break a puzzle game at least once) Other than that, the puzzles were simple enough, but still enjoyable to solve.I'm usually more into strategy games, but this was a nice change of pace.You know that thing where a game has a cool mechanic that is only used, like, twice? Maquette is nothing like that. The way you can make objects change size by interacting with a mini model of the room you're in is a great mechanic that is heavily explored and utilized throughout the entire game. Each new puzzle is a different use of this mechanic, but it never seems to get old.I'd say the game was worth it, although I did get it for 50% off during the summer sale.Also, you've seen the trailers: The art style rocks.

What's here is good, but if there was just a bit more packed in there, it would have been phenomenal.Lots of other reviews I've seen have complained about the story. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Maquette. Like the trailers show, this is a puzzle game where you place objects around a dollhouse-sized area, then you can explore that dollhouse area as the size of the doll. So you drop a small bridge down over a gap, then you can walk across it yourself.I was able to get through all the puzzles fairly easily, although I can understand why other people might struggle with them. You've got so much room to move about in, and the important details of the puzzles aren't always easy to see. I think I've just played so many puzzles games like this that I was able to intuit most of the answers right away.The story about a break-up was also very good. It's very easy for a story like this to feel overwrought, but I think the writers struck a good balance with it. Overall, this was a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: A short, story-laden perspective-based puzzle game in 7 chapters and the course of one beautiful, tragic relationship.Pros:* Beautiful, apt music at many of the major starting points.* Levels are gorgeous.* Puzzles are of varying difficulty - usually tough only if you haven't twigged to a new mechanic.* Great voice-acting.* Story is heart-breakingly relatable ()Cons:* Took me.. what, 4 hrs?* About half the achievements are for speed-running the levels - hard pass, thanks.Meh:* No hand-holding - use the Options to find the controls, but even then it's guesswork.TL;DR: If you like puzzles and love a good story, 7/10 (9/10, if on a decent sale); else, avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a pretty interesting mechanic and very pretty artstyle but its hard to recommend.For its current price I personally can't recommend it even though i did enjoy the puzzle aspect of this game.If you enjoy puzzle games and the artstyle then i would say it is worth picking up on sale. Otherwise i would look elsewhere.The gameplay can be clunky at times due to objects getting stuck and occasionally phasing through the level causing the need for loading from autosave, usually a little while back.The puzzles are actually quite good and do make you think, its just a shame there wasn't more of them.The story itself is underwhelming, the relationship goes on as you would expect and isn't particularly engaging, Get together happy, Things aren't going as well as hoped, Breaking up and then Moving on with your life. This all goes on in the background with text during gameplay sections and voiced cutscenes between scenes. I was expecting it to amount to more, affecting the game world itself more and actually tie into the internal world and shrinking/enlarging objects.The final 2 puzzle areas were a nice touch in this regard by playing more into the characters motivations but I felt like there wasn't the same climax when it came to the game systems we learned to use up to that point. These final chapters are also both over before you know it.Which is probably one of the bigger drawbacks about this game overall, its length. A lot of the gametime in the first half of the game is spent backtracking and for a game as short as this it is really noticeable.My playtime is probably longer than some due to leaving the game on while seeing to other tasks or having to replay sections but you are likely to get 2-3 hours playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Locked in a church, with no way out, I contemplated again why I kept playing this game. I had made my way there in a way other than the creators intended and I was stuck. Now, you might argue that it's not the creators' fault that I got myself stuck in their game and you would be wrong. But let's assume you're right - what do I do next? My first impulse was to just stop playing - it's not that I was really enjoying the game anyway. But the story had just taken an interesting twist - and I wanted to see how it would pan out. So I reluctantly got myself to load the last auto-save and continue.That was no good, the last auto-save happened after I got inside the church, so I was still stuck. My only other option was to restart the level, and go through all the trivial puzzles and tedious walking (a portal gun or translocator would have been handy) to reach the point before entering the church again. And that's not the only time I found myself where I wasn't supposed to be. The next level is a maze and, trying to find my way out, I got outside the map not once, but twice, by different means, my newly acquired ability to walk through rocks being a telltale sign that it's time to load a save game, manual this time (I've learned my lesson!) Speaking about manually managing save games, I'd like to mention an issue I had with the settings UI: I've been playing first-person games for two or three decades but this was the first time I couldn't set the mouse sensitivity to the level I'm used to - an instance of Apple-grade oversimplification.So, why did I even start playing the game? I excitedly grabbed it immediately after watching the trailer, which showcases a recursive world, kind of like a fractal, where when you change something in one level of the recursion it also automatically changes in all levels - a mind-blowing idea really, just imagine the possibilities! But, if the developers had a creativity quota, it seems they spent it entirely on that idea. The rest of the puzzles (except maybe one) are trivial and uninspired, they are fillers really to what is essentially more of a cinematic experience rather than a game - so that you do something different every once in a while other than walking along, reading the writings on walls, and watching cut scenes. As Bilbo Baggins might put it, puzzles are so scarce that they feel like a small amount of Nutella scraped over too much bread.As a cinematic experience, it's a nice one. Given the main concept of the game one might expect the story to be mathematically or philosophically inspired but it is instead the chronicle of a romantic relationship, a bold and welcome choice! Although simple, it is engaging, with good voice acting and interesting dialogue. The story is presented through cut scenes and excerpts written on walls, which have some literary value, although a few spelling mistakes detract from that somewhat. Also adding to the experience is the impressive architecture and the breathtaking effects of the world changing around you as you progress through it.It is a shame that puzzle design didn't get the same attention - this is supposed to be a game after all, not a movie. I dream that one day the people behind the puzzles of a game such as The Witness are made aware of the Maquette concept and use it to create another puzzle game - to show the world how it should really be done.

_childDocuments_.review: Dreadful.The selling point is the size changing mechanic. It's interesting at first, but underdeveloped. You've quickly seen it all, and the next puzzles are basic, uninspired.The meat of the game has you walking around in large lifeless spaces in search of an interactive object, then walking around plenty more in said large lifeless spaces in search of a spot to use it on.Visuals are not that great. Motion sickness is easy to catch. The music is awful but can be piped down. Object manipulation is awful as well, but controls cannot be improved.On top of that, you are subjected to a draining 3rd-rate narrative, a mundane relationship/breakup between two uninteresting lovebirds who keep whining through their nose.Platitudes and gooeyness.It left me incapable of playing more than 1 chapter per session.Later on, the game turns into a mere walking simulator.In maze-like environments.The kind of cheap crap no puzzler wants to suffer, so I uninstalled.Poor design effort, poor implementation.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Buy this game if you want a few hours of stylish puzzles that you'll never play again.The game is pretty.  The puzzles are fun and challenging.   The music is good.   However, the narrative feels contrived and out of place.  The "story" doesn't have any relation to the puzzles, and only a vague relation to the world's aesthetic and mood.  The constant cut-scenes are distracting and feel like they exist only to pad the game out.  In addition, I don't think there's much replay value.  I feel like I'd easily remember the "trick" to solving all the challenging parts.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game, just an overpriced one. I beat the entire thing in under 5 hours (including all achievements), and I wasn't rushing (except to earn the speedrun achievements, but I only went for those after doing a normal playthrough). And this includes the multiple points where I deliberately went out of my way to go places which (I knew beforehand) were dead ends, just to see what was there. You can buy all three "The Room" games for the price of this one game, and each individual "The Room" game has more content than this one.Also, I got softlocked a few times. Be wary of that. And the game frontloads its difficult puzzles in the first two chapters (not including the prologue), in addition to some of the answers not being intuitive (a certain "jump on rock to escape" solution comes to mind, since it's hard to get ON said rock in the first place, so I thought it must not be a solution). And there aren't all that many ACTUAL puzzles to solve, in the end. So it's not the best of puzzle games in that regard. "Better than passable" would say it best, with a decent story and visuals (though not the BEST visuals on closer examination, and since you often have to make yourself tiny compared to the world around you, you will be closely examining many parts of the world whether you want to or not).If I'm being generous to the story elements and atmosphere, I'd say the price of this game should be around $10. As a pure puzzle game, however, it should be priced $5 or less. And I imagine that's what most people will buy it for. Regardless, $20 is too high from a consumer standpoint. Perhaps it needs to be that high to make up for the money spent in production, from the developer's point of view. People who were going to buy it anyway can probably afford $20. But I imagine better recursion games will come out in the future, for cheaper, and when that happens, the price of this game is going to need to go down if you want anyone to buy it.To your average puzzle game player, I'd recommend waiting until this game goes on sale before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Flawed but ultimately worth a play.Pros:The diarama mechanic is neat and used in some interesting ways. The art is gorgeous. There were several sequences, like the long neighborhood walk towards the end, that I found particularly impressive. I found the story touching - I don't play "story rich" games so I wasn't expecting anything like that. Parts of the story hit close to home. The voice actors are excellent - way better than most games I've played. The sountrack has some nice indie rock/pop tracks.Cons:Somewhat buggy, especially at the end. As others have noted, restart the final chapter a couple times and you can get through it. Frequent manual saves can be helpful. Some of the puzzles near the end are especially obtuse. _childDocuments_.review: The recursion based puzzling gameplay on offer here is pretty interesting overall. _childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game with a simple story to accompany it. There isn't much to say about this - if you enjoy puzzle games which focus on perspective and scale you'll probably enjoy this. As with all puzzle games, looking up to much about the game itself runs the risk of spoiling the game itself. I would recommend this though.As for technical issues, in the concluding arc, I ran into 3 crashes, all of which occured while interacting with the primary interactive itself. Little in the way of progress was ever lost, due to the generous autosave, however. If I had one complaint, it was that I wish there were more puzzles in the concluding arcs - it almost feels like they were a victory lap with little in the way of additional challenges in perspective and scale.

_childDocuments_.review: The artistic direction is magnificent, and the core mechanics are really fun. The gameplay is really cool, and the object resizing encourages the player to navigate through the environments. The first few hours of gameplay truly impressed me.However, the rest is more mixed. I found myself soft-locked a few times, unable to solve a puzzle without reloading my save. The first time it happened, I was stuck for over half an hour before realizing it was just impossible without reloading. And that's the problem. In a puzzle game, the game should typically always be right, and I should be questioning myself and trying new approaches. Here, the "trust" was broken, and I found myself several times wondering if I didn't understand a puzzle, or if the game had soft-locked me. It breaks immersion, makes the player wary, and eventually discouraged me.However, I still recommend it if you're a fan of puzzle games, don't mind occasionally consulting a solution, and want to enjoy unique environments and gameplay.

Only sometimes the key would disappear after use. There was also a puzzle where it made you believe you had to change the size of one key but really there was a seperate key all together. It was justified by the story but idk maybe could have been a more elegant way to clue you in.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see how this game isn't for everyone, but I enjoyed the heck out of it. Puzzles were just the right amount of challenging and mind-bending. I never experienced any of the show-stopping bugs that some users reported (maybe they've all been fixed in later updates?). Some of the puzzles were hard to get the piece in the correct spot, but I got the hang of it. The story was... fine. But completely unnecessary. As far as I can tell, the story that unfolded during the game had absolutely nothing to do with the gameplay... like zero correlation. It was sort of like the game was already made and someone was like "this needs a story." And it was slapped on just to have a story. The voice acting was good though.Bottom line, if you like first-person puzzles with a physics-bending element, give this a try! If you get into the story, great. _childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept of bending reality by interacting with the maquette itself. Overall, I feel the learning curve could have been a bit better, partly making some more use of skills gained earlier. As it is, there's quite a few puzzle solutions that can be tough to figure out but that don't have a good enough payoff. Though there is the potential for soft-locks if you're not careful, given how complex the main mechanic is, a modicum of common sense will prevent those.At the same time as the puzzle, there's a love story going on. In my opinion, it is well-written and well-acted and got me emotionally invested. Personally, I would have loved to see a different resolution to the story, but that's just down to personal preference.

_childDocuments_.review: The art design and puzzles are fantastic. Get the game for those alone but then switch the audio off. Play some music you like instead. The "story" is laughable. It feels like it harks back to a San Francisco that existed in the 1970s where the lifestyle was bohemian and carefree. While, according to the story, the two characters Michael and Kenzie could very well have painted together while sipping wine in the park back in the 1970s, the fact that they live in the 2000s (they send texts with their phones) makes the aforementioned scene a complete anachronism. And maybe Michael and Kenzie's relationship is a problem only to people over the age of 40 for whom a modern relationship where the man is neutered and the woman sounds like a mewling teenager is cringe-inducing. If you're 22 and this couple describes the kind of relationship that you find healthy and balanced then you'll enjoy this story.Finally, the couple breaks up for the most stereotypical of bust-ups: "you never *listen* to me". Wow. That was deep.
