_childDocuments_.review: I do not get the hype this game receives. The combats lack any tactical depth, at least at the recommended difficulty level. It is also not a role-playing game in the narrow sense but rather a tactical combat game, with characters having some attributes that pretend to have an influence on story events. However, these events are poorly "written" or entirely trivial, as well as the decisions you can make. ("Choose: Will character A and B be 1) rivals, 2) friends or 3) lovers?" "I choose 3." "Congrats, now they are lovers!") it is also not obvious why exactly this character behaves in a certain way. The micromanagement on the world map is extremely repetitive, so also no tactical depth.The worst element, yet, are the "legacy characters". These are characters you played during a previous campaign. You can either encounter or recruit them in other campaigns. However, while they have their names and abilities in common with the characters you played previously, they are not actually the *same* characters. Instead, the game asks you to imagine that they are their descendants (which makes no sense at all, since characters can have *real* children) or that they are the stuff of legends that can appear in different stories at the same time (or some similar weird mental balancing act).So, no, I cannot recommend this game. If you like tactical combat games with "individual" (note the scare quotes) characters instead of armies or civilizations, you might give it a shot. But please do not expect any role playing of a reasonable degree.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enjoying the game so far! Combat is fairly simple and linear, as seen in other titles such as XCOM. The strongest selling point is the story-telling part of the game. Characters develop bonds between each other, be it love, friendship, rivalry or hate. They can also change appearance based on outcomes during their adventures such as losing a limb in battle or replacing your arm with one made of fire.The only cons I will mention is that during their conversations sometimes the dialogue seems a bit off. Kind of like in a somewhat badly translated game. And the only way to upgrade your gear is by the end of the chapters and resources are very scarce.This is my first review I think, hopefully it helps. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game!! Gives you enough intriguing story to have fun imagining what happens in between. The magic mechanics are unique and I adore the world's feel - told like a half-remembered fable or legend. I got really attached to my party and have since repurposed them into characters of my own to write about - highly recommend if you flock to games with party relationships in them!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I was somewhat torn on this review. Wildermyth has an ambitious concept, and there are brief moments when it truly sparkles. Unfortunately the game just doesn’t come together due to problems with lack of content, unclear mechanics and poor user interface.The idea of an emergent narrative in which random and scripted events combine with character personalities and relationships is really quite brilliant. Early on in my play, I had some really entertaining moments when the comic cutscenes still felt fresh. However, you don’t play long before you start seeing repetition. While it’s possible for the dialog to change up a bit based on your party makeup, you will have to wade through a lot of stuff you’ve already seen for this, and it generally doesn’t seem worth it.The game also lacks variety in its mechanics. There are three classes, roughly translating into the familiar archetypes of fighter, ranger and mage (who interacts with scenery to create effects.) They each have a limited selection of abilities that do not do much to break up the routine of fights. Random events can cause characters to undergo transformations, such as having limbs take on animal or elemental characteristics, which might give you an extra attack or change your stats for better or worse. Monster mechanics don’t vary much, with just a couple of tactics it uses. The AI can be wildly unpredictable and/or nonsensical; monsters might spread out their attacks, focus on a single target, or dance around and do nothing even with several targets in range.The balance in character development feels off. Some interactions between transformations and abilities are incredibly strong, while others are lacklustre or downright detrimental. Some abilities are effectively useless, or worse be very unpredictable in value. For example, a mystic ability can allow you to use books for a stunning effect, which can be very powerful, but in one game I took this ability and I don’t think I saw a suitable piece of scenery even once.Fights can vary dramatically in difficulty depending on random events, density of monsters, and plain luck. In one of my earliest encounters, one character was sidelined by the event and the others were quickly overwhelmed by huge numbers, nearly prompting me to give it up and refund the game. I decided to try again, and was then met with much easier encounters (at the same difficulty setting) with perhaps 2 or 3 monsters to deal with. With the exception of this unfortunate early experience, base difficulty felt very easy to me, but turning it up means that characters can easily get 1- or 2-shot by lucky hits or enemies which weren’t even visible when you ended your turn. This doesn’t feel like a greater challenge so much as it just feels arbitrary and unfair. You can mitigate this to some extent by being very cautious, but doing so reduces the game to a crawl. I do not find the game communicates information well. While you can preview which enemies you’ll be able to use basic attacks against when moving, it isn’t always clear which special abilities might work. The game gives you a percentage chance of success on attacks, but it’s not clear where these numbers are coming from. Cover has vague descriptions like “good.” Characters have two avoidance stats, block and dodge, which are compared against accuracy to determine chances of success, but I have no clue how. I don’t even know why these are two separate stats to begin with. Consequently, I don’t know how much value there is in a particular modifier such as +5 dodge. Similarly, some cutscene choices have a chance of success, but the game doesn’t tell you which stats affect these or how you might improve your chances in the future. Similarly, the UI is unnecessarily complicated. For example, during combat, you can right click on your hero portrait to view your character sheet. Simple enough right? Except you can’t do that in several other places. If you want to see your character sheet while levelling up, you click on a picture of the character in the window banner. While selecting items, you click on a small coin-shaped portrait. During cutscenes, a text link. The game requires the player to learn four different ways of seeing your character sheet in different situations, some of which are not at all obvious. Sometimes it just doesn’t seem possible to access information at the time you want it.Putting all this together, you will have choices to make while playing, but often you have no way to actually determine the value or potential consequences of those choices.I gave this game as much time as I did because it really seemed it might be great if it started to click for me, but this just never happened. It’s a shame, because I’m sure this could be a real gem if there was more content, the mechanics were clearer and the UI was improved. I’d have more hope for it and be more forgiving of its issues if it was still considered early access. As it is, I don’t think the game was ready for full release. I get that it has a very positive rating on Steam, so it must be working for a lot of people, and maybe there’s a reason I’m just not connecting to it. But I noticed that achievements list only 29% as completing the introductory campaign, which takes a few hours, so it appears there are many people who never get more than an afternoon out of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game, not my usual thing but I picked it up because of everything I've heard about it. Was not disappointed at all. The turn based combat is fairly simple, but can have a reasonable amount of depth and I find it great.The story's are brilliant and fresh, it's like reading a comic book but you also get to fight the battles. I've not played a game like this before and it deserves all the praise it gets.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Genius level devs, felt like reading a book where all pieces fall just exactly in the right places and everything gets better the more you play, to boot you get to have a nice xcom style gameplay on the map and in the combat itself.Made 3 characters, randomized them till I got suitable personalities, Compassionate Leader Warrior (with my kinda looks), 2nd Gal Hotheaded Romantic Hunter (red/orange hair ebony), 3rd Romantic something Mystic (teal hair white), 4th was from story recruit, a random black chick, tweaked little bit hair and outfit color to be more darker, made her a warrior and and she also was a Compassionate Leader. First transformation: The hot headed chick becomes infused with fire, the entire story seems to take into account the personality of the character in terms how to powerup, that is if your open minded for change, there are so many choice moments and story telling besides the xcom style combat.Second power up: The dark chick meets her inner dark raven like being, when infused fully, her head turns into ravens head lolz, was like wth is this fate or coincidence. Then my male character at the end gets captured and his face gets infected slightly and crystallized, looses 25 charisma and gains 35 loneliness. Guess compassionate leaders get the short end of the stick in terms of human looks in the end.Was nicely surprised how my characters developed and transformed their inner personality outside basically. My mystic hasn't yet transformed or she was already from the beginning. At the moment after beating the first boss you get a summary of years of peace how well you performed overall, then the story evolves even further with new challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional game. I class games in the following way.Low quality > blehlow to mid   > it beats worrying about the rainmid              > ah screw it, ill play another half hourmid to high  > im enjoying this, itss really stopped me worrying about the council tax billhigh              > youve played for 316 hoursBest              > Hello work, this is Anthony, I wont be in for the rest of the week! i have foot and mouth!This game has the potential to cost me my job!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful for idly passing time in an immersive roleplay experience. I loved how attached you could become to the characters, how customizable and unique they are, and really the art form of the story telling. There's nothing else quite like Wildermyth. Fantastical, mythical, romantic, action-packed -- can't go wrong!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: For me, Wildermyth scratches the itch I get when I want to play D&D, even just the crunchy goblin smushin kind, but my friends are busy. The procedurally generated stories feel rich, you grow attached to these emergent stories, and it's a lot of fun to sit with a group of friends and stream it and voice your own characters? lol, it actually works as a dnd substitute when everyone is too tired, haha.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Xcom tactical combat (that's deeper than it first appears, crank the difficulty a bit and you'll figure it out whether you want to or not) with a procedurally generated story telling system Bioware must absolutely envy and a beautiful art style that proves you don't need fancy 3D polygons to have great graphics, Wildermyth is a good turn based strategy game wrapped around a Fantastic (with a capital F) story engine that I can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd feel nostalgia while playing a game. To see a hero rise and take on the world, and eventually pass it on to their children is something I've never seen in a game like this. Then after barely beating the last boss, the ability to save your favorite and starting up the next campaign only to see that same champion as a young person again filled me with emotion. Absolutely stellar game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: If you like having open world where what you do changes things- this is it.Not only can you explore as you see fit, this strategy rpg allows for choices made with your party, gives a distinct D&D feel through options on both how to level and how to approach battles, and your group grows and ages out of play over the course of the story. Who you start out as, will not be who you end up with. After over 12 hours of play my first group is about to start retiring. Now every recruit I have trained beneath will move up and take over.Choices on rivalries as well as romance and friendship make the PCs feel more alive- and the ability to sidequest and interact with varying NPCs make the world feel organic. Sure, it isn't your stereotypical 3D play as a single character- but the way this feels is just as addicting and fun as Fable started out- and its still getting attention from its Devs!This already serves as a great option if you are a streamer as well! Get your chat involved! Let them help in the decision making so the world isn't yours alone!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game! Its crazy at some times and events don't always happen the way you expect it much like a dnd game, in the best way possible. If you get a couple friends and dedicate characters to them you get attached to the story you create while doing the campaign. Decent combat and strategy and the customization for the characters can often times lead to many unique styles of play.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: The heart of the game-play of Wildermyth is XCOM-style tactical combat in a fantasy setting, and on that front it is a success. Combat is challenging and tactical, and the special skills you select for your characters has a meaningful impact on your choices.Also like XCOM, outside of combat, you will guide your heroes throughout the world map trying to manage the crises affecting the land. You will recruit more heroes as the story moves forward and likely have several parties in different locations exploring, building, fighting. As chapters close, years will pass and some heroes will retire while new ones will come of age. Retired heroes may sometimes be saved as legacy characters that you may use in future campaigns, which is a nice touch.The story is told through comic-strip style cut scenes using procedurally-generated dialog between the characters. Your heroes' individual personality traits may also modify this dialog. While these scenes are sometimes moving or interesting, I found the writing to be largely prose-y and pretentious, with too much focus on being poetic and not enough on being readable. The personalities of your heroes doesn't often seem to come through here in a memorable way either, which is disappointing and makes it harder to feel invested in the characters.These issues aside, Wildermyth is a very strong tactical RPG, and I recommend it to anyone who has been looking for a fantasy-themed XCOM-style experience. However, I wouldn't count on becoming enchanted with the setting, writing, or characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough. If you love whimsical and melancholy fantasy this is already perfect. But the real winner for me is how you take a group of fairly generic starting heroes and watch them genuinely evolve, age and take on scars and changes from the decisions you make. Many of the adventures even end up being multi-generational, with the offspring of your surviving heroes from each act sometimes joining the adventuring party later on.If you like story-led RPGs with a strong tactical component, you owe it to yourself to get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: The only game in my memory, where your decisions and consequences thereof, ACTUALLY mattered! There doesn't always seem to be clear cut choices in most scenarios. And I never felt once that the game punished me for whatever path I decided to take my merry band of heroes down. Great story telling in random events throughout each campaign, gives this game a high degree of replayability.The combat I found to be fun and interesting. Not overly complex but rewarding enough to try experimentation. The graphics and sound (including the music) I found to be exceptional for an indie game. Really evokes that story book feeling that I think the developers intended when creating this superb game.Over the course of multiple chapters in each story, I could not help but get attached to the characters I created. I felt genuine concern over each one, and got thorough enjoyment watching as they grew, developed and some even reaching the ripe old age of retirement. It really gave me a sense of achievement that few games seem to provide me these days.Overall a very enjoyable experience that exceeded my expectations. As one of the few games I would merit picking up at full price, these developers deserve it. A game I would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game full of short stories and all sorts of adventures, The art style is straight out of a children's book, but the stories themselves are very deep at times, invoking emotional responses beyond the story lines in a lot of more widely known games.  It's almost impossible not to form attachments to certain characters you find along the way, made all the stronger by the fact that not every story has a happy ending and there isn't a clear right or wrong choice to hardly any of the options you are provided with.  The game itself is enjoyably replayable and no two playthroughs will ever be exactly the same, every decision matters.  If you've not played it, I definitely recommend, you wont regret giving your time to this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I can't believe I never left a review for this diamond in the rough! I LOVE this game. Have played it many times over the years, gone through various campaigns, found love, and sometimes lost it. Not even the strongest of my adventures survived the Summer Dragon, but their legacies carried on the fight after their brave sacrifice. I wish more games really captured that epic feeling of fantasy and adventure. Try it out! You're gonna love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This was my personal game of the year for 2021. Overall this was a very unique and enjoyable experience as a fan of D&D and strategy RPGs.I love the art style, music, and storytelling! There's enough flexibility in combat and character builds to keep things interesting. The overworld pressure to press on combined with limited healing and permadeath can make for a challenging experience.Much to my excitement the devs also continue to add new content in the form of pre-generated campaigns and new character building options.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I maybe have written 1 or 2 reviews in my 30 years of life. However, this game is deserving. I have loved every second of it. From the depth to the warmth. The bonds of the characters and so much more. This is quite truly an amazing and breath taking game. Thank you Worldwalker games. You've given me some joy, adventure and emotion back to video games for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I played this long bevore it got to EA. A great game so far, all about building your own Story. Luckyly the developers add new storys all the time (which are the meat of the game.) You will fight, you will cry for your fallen ones, and you will see your heros go through numerus evolutions. A Charakter where all limps are replaced by fire? Check, Cristall eyes or becomming a half wolf Check. Needing to reevauate your weapon choice because of a severed arm? Check!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Xcom, fantasy edition, featuring a bucketload of lore, a more forgiving character death system, and some truly decent writing.Play this if you:-Love isometric strategy-Enjoy story heavy rpg's featuring custom characters-Are interested in a storybook like aesthetic with beautiful artRough spots:-Underdeveloped overworld map (including features that are more or less meaningless, like building defenses)-Slightly frustrating character aging mechanic that feels inconsistentI have already got my money's worth, I didn't know I needed a procedurally generated Xcom like fantasy game with more replayability, but here it is!  Give it a shot
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! If you like tactical games this is for you. If you like semi casual games that are easy to pick up and put down (not that you are going to want to) this is for you. It may not have the depth of some of the heavy hitters but the art and the concept more than make up for any short comings.Note to publisher: Please put out more content, I do not usually go for or like dlcs but I would readily open my wallet to continue to support the great work you have done. Do not abandon this gem too soon refine it and build it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever positive review you saw for this game is a drastic understatement. So much heart and so much love is in this game, it is definitely worth your time. The game play is enough to hook any player happy with turn based combat, but the real sticking point is the stories you can make. The interactions with the characters you create are fun and great, the relationships that you can have and influence are wonderful. I always come back to this game from time to time, it is wonderful
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game back in alpha, and I gotta say I've really had my fun with it. If you enjoy TTRPG's and the like, it could serve as a way to scratch that gaming itch (I certainly know it did for me). The base game stories aren't bad, and the game also offers a good variety of difficulties, with the last one (Walking Lunch) being brutal if you don't play your cards right. If you run out of things to do or want a changeup, mod support through the Workshop is available. The character buildup in this game is really nice - even after you finish a campaign with a set of characters, you can recruit them as Legacy heroes in future storylines. Of course, this can snowball into some of your initial characters becoming complete combat monsters from the get-go, and it feels really satisfying. I ended up bringing in my original warrior from the first campaign into almost every succeeding campaign, and between then and now, it really felt like she went through thick and thin to become the terror she is.The multiplayer in this game is... just ok. It really felt like Worldwalker Games added it simply because of popular demand, and it shows. I didn't encounter any bugs, but between the people I played it with, we all agreed that the game was better built as a singleplayer game.In my personal experience, I'd recommend playing either of the middle difficulties to start, and escalating from there as you see fit.  Overall, I'd say give Wildermyth a go, especially if you like TTRPG's and tactics games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is just behind Baldur's Gate 3 for me in terms of replicating the feeling of a TTRPG, but while Baldur's Gate does it with a high budget and intricate combat and interactions between a well-designed party, Wildermyth recreates the feeling of watching a table of PCs change as they move between sessions. It's really cool.There are a lot of campaigns to play through and they're pretty okay as stories, but the highlight of the game is the way you'll grow attached to your collection of randomly generated heroes and watch as they go through randomly designed arcs of their own and with each other. Long campaigns will have your starting characters grow old and sometimes retire while leaving behind children to continue as new characters or having trained the next generation. My favorite feature is that at the end of a campaign you can turn your characters into 'legacy characters' allowing them to keep appearing in future campaigns. Eventually you'll have built a full cast of mythological heroes who all cross over between eachother's (sometimes incompatible) stories like a proper myth. It's really cool!The new Rougelite mode is pretty neat although i'm maybe having the most trouble with it's story mode. The writing in this game is generally good but occasionally falls into unfunny memes or long tangents into unreasonably self serious complicated lore that makes me want to turn off the game and nap.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: We need more fun co-op games!  Wildermyth is a fun-vibe co-op DnD adventure.  It has cute graphics, funny dialog.  We role play and read the lines aloud for our characters.  While RPG greats like Divinity Original Sin 2 are also co-op, they are huge campaigns.  Wildermyth is shorter stories that the group can complete in a reasonable time.  Because it is turn-based, there is time to talk together about what to do, without needing to rush.  Wildermyth is a cartoony graphics type of game, and though there is combat, it is cartoony and there is no blood or gore so younger kids can play and enjoy too.   We need more social games, and Wildermyth is a game the whole family can play together.  Plus, as a Steam Remote Play Together game, we don't have to buy a separate copy for every member of the family--nice!  Not only can the whole family play together from one copy, but family members can 'try it out co-op' for free without having to buy it, which encourages them to give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes to show that having developers that care about their product, not just their total profit (take note please Bioware, EA, Activision, etc) can produce something truly magical.  The stories that develop in this game are what draws you in, no matter the difficulty level and ease or difficulty of the combat itself.I would easily pay for DLC for this game that had more narrative stories and further expanded choices and such.An incredible game, great artistry, fantastic experience.  I can see playing this for far more hours than some of the more extravagently priced games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good in early access, with at least 20 hours of main campaign content. It seems like a good structure for mods; players can tell their own stories in D&D style and provide much more content. I'd hope that the developers expose the battle mechanics as much as they do the story framework, because 3 classes and ~10 abilities per class will probably get stale after a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical based on the game's cartoony visuals. I love RPGs but I wasn't sure if this one would do it for me. But I read all the positive reviews here and watched a few reviews on YouTube and decided to give it a try. I was pleasantly surprised. The game is both deep / immersive and incredibly replayable--far more than I expected given its rogue-like elements. This one is well worth a buy. 5/5, two thumbs up, all that jazz.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game with a few exceptions.  It is a fun tactical RPG with a smattering of grander strategy in clearing territories, building defenses and gathering resources that can be spent between chapters.  It is really well done in terms of art and graphics and has interesting combat mechanics and skill trees. The only thing I do not like is the story.  Well, the story is actually interesting, but the catch is that there is SO MUCH OF IT.  It is like I have to read a whole graphic novel between each battle.  I found myself just clicking through most of it.  I know it is lazy and lame of me, but I am the consumer, right.  Bottom line - if you like graphic novellas and reading a lot between the action, this is a really cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Buy now.  Play until 3 a.m.  Grow your legacy of heroes with their own (very well-written) stories.  Then they can be Legends Reborn when you start a new campaign.  Five campaigns offline, so this is based on lots more playing than the counter shows.Wow, this game is amazing!  Build a team of unique individuals who grow and learn and mess up and change.  For example, Julie thought it would be a good idea to stick her arm in the fire shrine that didn't feel hot to her, and now she can shoot fire.  But not carry a shield anymore.  She may transform more, or die, but even if she does, she can return in a later campaign.  Quick turn-based tactics + mild management + RPG character progression.  Less fiddly inventory b/c items are permanently assigned but replaceable.   Also it's great not to have to put up with gory messes in order to play something fun.  Great skill progression with perks, improvable gear without it being tedious, and every aspect is fun.  Most strategic decisions are on a timer, so it's weighing the tradeoffs.  For example, I could build defences in a province, which helps defend against incursions, but building takes time... which runs up the incursion timer.  Patrol to reduce the challenge of the upcoming attack, or save time by attacking now instead of letting the enemy have more time to improve?  Good strategy is rewarded.  Every change to a character shows in all their pictures and paper sprite.  For example, Grant added a cape, Vivian got gray hair because 20 years passed, Ella lost a leg and replaced it with a peg leg, and Julie got a fire arm... it all shows.  Downside?  Still early access, and it crashes sometimes.  But lots of autosaves mean I haven't lost much at all.  It already has several playable campaigns (with great stories) and 2 generic ones and a lot of random encounters.  I'm looking forward to more writing and bug fixing.  Also looking forward to multiplayer (beyond experimental)... co-op missions with a group of 3-4 friends would be stellar.I thought the paper-cut-out art style was going to bug me, but it didn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable indie game that captures so many awesome aspects of fantasy storytelling that RPG fans will love. The community makes mods to enhance the game, and it remains in active development. Buy it to support this awesome duo of indie creators putting so many AAA studios to shame. Hope they drop some kind of DLC eventually so I can give them more money. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: A very passionate and fresh Party-Based RPGAlmost like having your own D&D Dungeon master crafting and tailoring a very fun story as impacted by your choicesmaking replayability factor very highCombat is very intuitive and fun and allows a lot of interesting and meaningful tactics to get you through the game10/10 Exactly how a person would imagine an ideal traditional RPG
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: For an indie game, this game is a ton of fun and is thoroughly exciting to play! It has a ton of customization for your created heroes which is boosted even further with mods and the dlc. Choosing where to put your heroes and how you optimize your time and them is great. There are lots of events in the game that are influenced by how many party members are brought, their relationships with one another, and the actual area itself. I'd recommend this game to anyone who is a fun of rpgs or enjoys some good old fashioned storytelling in a game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I can say its a pretty fun turn based strategy game with some story telling aspects. It did not have the amount of 'permancence' that I really thought it would, I was kind of expecting a somewhat more proceedual story where choices mattered... but honestly it doesn't feel like they do, or if a hero die they aren't permanently gone either as they can play in different campaigns. As the maps are seeded I doubt I see burial sites any time soon, and my characters haven't really so far come back as npc's or anything in other stories so idk... Its fun rather 'simple' fighting with a cool magic system, the pop up book style feels pretty nice with the comic strip style cutscenes. After a while events start repeating enough that you know the outcome of different choices. I kinda like the transformations options, they give you cool new abilities to spice up your playthrough Such as flame hands that can set stuff on fire.....It might not be a 10/10, but its not terrible. I enjoyed it and by thus can recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the game-play seems fun and potentially deeper than it appears on the surface. However, the dialogue and/or translation into English is so catastrophically poor, that its almost completely unplayable. The dialogue honestly feels like it's written by a 15 year old AI (Artificial Intelligence). I cannot express how disappointed I am because the game really seemed like it could be fun. However, the writing is just beyond unacceptably poor.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely legendary game. Got it on sale, but would've been worth it full price. The art is wonderful and whimsical and has an aesthetic that feels really unique in the gaming world, the writing ranges from hilarious to beautiful, and both the narrative  gameplay aspects are incredibly fun. I thoroughly enjoy playing through the campaigns and seeing what comes next (Eluna & The Moth is my favorite so far,) but I also really have fun with optimizing the characters in my Legacy to have a deck full of overpowered heroes on standby. Generally, I just 100% recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 10/10!!! OMG WHAT A HIDDEN GEM!!! If you are looking for a virtual D&D to play with up to 4 other friends then get this game!!!Wildermyth is easily the greatest hidden gem of 2021! It is the closest I have ever felt a game get to Dungeons and Dragons without being insanely complicated. The humor in this game is out of this world and being able to get a group of 5 together and play through procedurally generated campaigns with customized or randomly generated characters is so much fun. The first day getting it my friends and I played for 7 hours straight!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, amazing devs. It is absolutely an experience worth the 20 dollars. If you like D&D, XCOM, And a dash of mythological/storybook vibe then this is more than worth 20 dollars just for the 4 completed campaigns. Then even more replayable with the random generated ones and eventually custom made community ones. Infinite potential for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.I'm a big DnD and roleplaying nerd and while sometimes I wish the game offered more customisation and options for dialogue/skill based choices apart from that it's perfect. There's so much replyability in the different campaigns and the option to bring back characters from previous games is dope. Ya like DnD? Ya like RPGs? Get this game
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: A great procedural RPG that sees your heroes grow and develop over decades, forming relationships and even raising children to become heroes in their stead. The combat is fun, and there are a variety of character builds to explore with interesting feats that can be made to synergise in clever ways for tremendous fun and power.The style of writing, however, is over-sophisticated to the point of being incomprehensible at times. Certainly the writers are trying to avoid cliches, but the phrases and onomatopoeia used are so experimental and esoteric that I am exhausted from trying to work out what is actually being said.Just dial it back a bit guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a wonderful gift to storytelling. I found myself absolutely tied to the characters and their silly stories. Watching them change and fall in love and their children join adventuring and worlds be saved; and some doomed. It was a beautiful heartwarming experience that was improved by simple and fun combat, an easy to understand map system, and creative storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is made up of encounters, simple time management, quick "make a choice" things, and rarer cutscenes about the campaign/backstory. Encounters (a la DnD) are where you move characters around a grid and perform actions based off their class. There are three player classes at this time: warrior, hunter, and mystic. The warrior & hunter are fairly standard, but the mystic is very unique and lets you use pieces of the game board to attack others. The time management aspect confused me a bit at first, but it's really important to doing well. The cutscenes & choice dialogues are really well written and tailored to your characters. They repeat sometimes though, which hurts replay value. The art is really nice. I like the look of the game a lot. I really enjoyed this game so far. I think I'll wind up getting 50-100 hours of gameplay in before running dry or needing to install mods. If you've ever played DnD, it has a very similar feel to prewritten campaigns from a book. I think it is a little sparse for now, after only two stories played though (~12 hours), I had around 5 duplicate make-a-choice dialogues. The relationships between characters are also fairly shallow. However, the creators did a good job working personality into the dialogue in a natural way. For instance, I have two "snarky" characters who became rivals, and they occasionally trash-talk. Overall, I would most strongly recommend this game if you 1) want to play DnD and haven't before, and want to know sort of what it's like or 2) miss playing DnD and can't get a group together or make time. I think the game feels a little unfinished still, so if you're tight on cash, you may want to wait a little longer to see the improvements. I look forward to seeing how the makers expand the game, and especially exploring mod packs once more are published.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think it is adequate to call this a dungeon crawler. While the battles have a bit of a dungeon crawler type feel to them, in that their tactical like Gloomhaven and X-Com, giving you this explore as you go to the point where you're trying to unravel the map, locate the enemies but doing so cautiously and with hopefully a strategy, the core of Wildermyth is in the story. No I don't mean the Bioware kind of stories, which, by the way I did like their older RPGs. It's more likely a story weaver on top of a tactical battle with some stategic map thrown in. A closer, but imperfect comparison would be Massive Chalice.Now I will say that there is a lot of reading to this game which will probably turn off a few and challenge young children, but even with a few repeats I didn't mind the stories that are often based on character traits, because the characters felt a lot more like mine than Massive Chalice ever did. Sure, I cared about my characters in that game, and especially getting great children and therefore future characters to play with, but this one hits a little closer to the heart/emotional core. I let my characters make questionable choices to fit their traits and it felt... good to do that. The problem with a number of RPGs, the older ones and the mixed genres like this one is they say you have choices, they claim you can get into the character set and then... promptly, and sometimes harshly punish you for doing exactly that with hidden mathematical schemes for end game content or providing you with clear this is the right choice and this was the bad choice... based on outcomes.  I am only two campaigns in now, and will do the rest, but I have yet to feel that disappointment with this game. When given a choice, I feel I got something... either way. I don't HAVE to try and have my weird character do the logical thing in order to not have her completely under-powered for later battles. I can enjoy the relationships or the rivalries in the story without shackling myself in the battles. And this does NOT mean these relationships and choices don't have an affect... they actually do. Romance, children, rivals can all get bonuses in the battles, and they're worthwhile too, if you use them properly... and if you don't you still might be okay.So where I am going with this if you don't mind reading events and character interactions as some light reading, and you like the tactical battles that you see in games like X-Com, Gloomhaven and Massive Chalice, and you enjoy some nice instrumental music (love that too), and like to feel like the characters you are playing with are yours... this might be for you.  Difficulty can be scaled; the overhead map has a bit more right and wrong to it but it's not too complicated and the world/theme is just neat. So if you are on the fence, wait for a sale and give it a go. It's a wonderfully delightful game to play, that you can also do in one hour sittings or just marathon your day off and love it equally that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth really draws you in and makes you think it's THE DREAM: a semi-bespoke but also randomized engine for telling RPG stories with emergently interesting characters AND interesting turn-based combat!Unfortunately Wildermyth draws you in with the fake novelty in a very deceptive way.My first 3-chapter campaign? It was amazing. It felt like I was following a number of well-developed characters through a surprisingly-well-developed story with interesting tactical turn-based battles as the mechanical crux. My original hunter and warrior fell in love! Their son became a new recruit after chapter 2! Every tile unlocked on the world map was a new story! Character upgrades between chapters felt meaty and important. Managing Legacy Points to prevent my enemies' progress kept me on my toes. At the conclusion of the campaign I felt like this was one of the best games I'd played in years.Then I started the next campaign. And I realized I would be replaying A LOT of the same stories, just with different characters. I stole the giant eagle's eggs twice. Then I realized bumping up the difficulty was a bit too much and I needed to restart. Then I realized that the story I was playing was only *barely* customized between runs--in many cases, just character names/portraits were changed. I wanted it to be overall a new experience. I wanted to see that Wildermyth had HUNDREDS of stories to experience. That's what you expect from an emergent storytelling RPG right? Wrong. The stories repeat surprisingly quickly. The feeling of hollowness starts creeping in at maybe the 8 hour mark and then sets in very hard very quick. The game's bones show very quickly.And then the illusion broke and I wasn't interested anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I love Wildermyth. The dialogue and character development is unlike anything I've seen; I just finished a campaign with a few friends and we can all agree that we've never been more attached to a group of 2.5D characters. The gameplay and combat is simple, but deceptively hard, as one wrong move could swiftly result in lethal consequences. Even the smallest adventures and escapades your characters embark on have never felt so engaging. Nothing feels tedious and nothing drags on too long. This game provides a unique feeling of comfort and investment that in the end will leave you with, for lack of a better word, fulfillment. Never felt more strongly about recommending a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: For its first ten hours, Wildermyth is charming and great. But, like the Wizard of Oz, once you've played enough to "see behind the curtains" into the game's narrative and gameplay systems, the magic and charm swiftly atrophy. Wildermyth is, ultimately, wildly overrated.I have a piece of advice I often tell my creative writing students: "If a detail is important enough to put in once, it's good enough to bring up again." If, when introducing a character, you spend several paragraphs describing the tattoos covering her body, then those tattoos should be a pivotal aspect of her character. They should be brought up again later by the character herself or others. You do this because it trains the reader to pay attention; it imbues even mundane observations with intrigue.This is, in fact, a form of Chekhov's Gun, from the famous playwright Anton Chekhov who said: "If in the first act you have hung a pistol on the wall, then in the following act it should be fired. Otherwise don't put it there."Wildermyth, however, repeatedly hangs pistols on walls, only to completely ignore them later. For example, one of my primary characters that I've used across all my campaigns is a warrior with a WOLF HEAD. You would think, perhaps, that this might constitute a rather conspicuous detail. You might think other characters that she recruits would ask, "Uh why in the world do you have a wolf head?"But you would be wrong. My character having a wolf head didn't change anything in the story whatsoever. Because Wildermyth's individual story hooks and vignettes are largely self-contained. So a given story arc might have multiple parts that span several chapters, but story arcs never (that I saw) interact with each other.So actual character and world development feels random and disconnected, and as a result I found Wildermyth's story-telling to be uninteresting and emotionless. Sure your characters can "fall in love" but all that really means is some tag in the UI, with minor gameplay and story effects. A sad definition of love, if you ask me.Which leaves us with the game itself, the mechanics. And what's there is decent... but there isn't much there.I have this term - "indie threadbare effect" - that I find myself using all the time, to describe indie games which push replayability far beyond the game's mechanical depth and breadth. That also describes Wildermyth quite well.There's 8 or so scripted campaigns, as well as the choice to pursue a procedural campaign. Your characters within these campaigns can become legacy heroes that can be re-used in other campaigns and even advanced to higher tiers. So it looks like there's a lot of replayability.But the game's mechanical content lasts about 2 campaigns. There are THREE classes, each with 10-15 abilities (passive and active) as well as a small pool of general abilities. There's also 10-15 spells total for the mage class. By the time you've completed your second, maybe third, campaign, you'll have seen and done it all.Of course every person's sense of novelty is different... but I was shocked at how quickly the gameplay grew stale. By the third campaign, it's fair to say that 99% of the battles were mechanically identical to ones I'd already fought before. And even the procedurally chosen mini-vignettes started frequently repeating.The game has an undeniable charm but at this stage, I'd say it's more of a platform than anything. It desperately needs more content. More classes, more abilities, more vignettes. But while all of that will improve the GAME part of Wildermyth, I'm not sure anything will fix its fundamentally flawed story-telling. In a good story, details need to matter. If my main character's head gets replaced with a WOLF SNOUT, that should matter. It should inform every future interaction that character has.But in Wildermyth details don't matter.In short, Wildermyth is just a very light game. Story-lite, gameplay-lite. It's quite breezy. Which may be just what some people want. But anyone interested in depth in their gameplay and story will want to look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: If you like spending hours fighting your way through a campaign only to have your entire party annihilated by forces beyond your control due to random dice rolls, this is the game for you!I've cleared 3 of the campaigns and was working on the 4th, and either you steamroll a given fight or get completely destroyed, and not due to your decisions as a player.The game is gorgeous and the writing is superb, but losing all my progress to chance is not fun. Ever. Under any circumstances.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you just want a weekend's worth of storytelling, this game is worth the price. Good pacing between the story segments and action segments. The heartfelt writing comprising the semi-randomly created story arcs will bring to mind the staple themes of camaraderie, danger, sacrifice, and homecoming that lovers of high adventure remember from the works they enjoyed as kids. Those who don't count themselves a member of this happy demographic will most certainly be amused, and possibly converted.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Very good turn based strategy game with nice RNG events that make the game fun.The "legacy" hero system is also very interesting and fun, as it allows you to build up heroes the way you like to play, with reasonable limitations that still allow you to feel powerful yet challenged by the events!Overall this is very well done and I hope the devs release more content. I'd be happy to pay for an expansion or DLC for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I play 'hardcore' with one single save file and no reload. When the game over screen appears, the overwhelming sadness lingers. Not because I am frustrated with defeat. But because I miss the characters I have seen developed during the campaign and now, it's the end. Some become legends. Most not. The story can be heartwarming and heartbreaking at the same time. A really good RPG with high replayability.Highly recommended. A game-play video as follows.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to be the one dissenting voice here...But... I didn't like it.  This game is very "Meme" oriented, and feels like it was designed so that folks can have their own customized choices that fill out every possible character.Except... all the characters have a distinct slant to their actions and opinions.   Ran it through a few times with various characters, and no matter who you choose, or what personalities you go with... the story never changes.And that, in my opinion, is one of the worst storytelling mistakes.   It feels like playing D&D with a railroading GM, who has a personal message he WANTS you to learn, and he has thought out all possibilities, but ONLY for his own solution.  It feels like all the "Roads Not Taken" have not only had the "KEEP OUT" sign put up, but also have had the doorway bricked up, painted over, and everyone agrees that we'll never talk about the door again.So... yeah, Seems everybody else really enjoys this, and I accept that I'm probably the only person who feels off while playing it.   But something about this game feels off, and I trust my gut more than reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful, fun game. The randomness of events and level-up options forces you to learn new tactics and form new strategies every time you play, which is something not achieved by most games.In virtually every other game in a similar genre (I say similar because this game defies several genre stereotypes), the player develops a certain build and style that is effective and then sticks with it, hamstringing the replayability of the game. Wildermyth rather ingeniously circumvents this, while at the same time creating enduring stories and characters.The writing is funny and smart, the art is lovely, there are custom difficulty levels, and there is a Steam workshop--this is an absolute gem. Buy it. Thank me later.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I am utterly shocked by how excellent this game is. It captures many facets of DnD that most games fail to, even some of the GOATs like Divinity and Baldur's Gate. I opened this game with a friend and immediately played through an 8 hour campaign, only breaking for food. I can't describe to you how extremely rare that is for me. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: The writing has heart. The turn-based combat seems simple but has depth. There are many more interesting character builds and party combos than you might realize after the first few campaigns. There are tons of tiny QoL enhancements that make the game a joy to play. The difficulty is highly adjustable and varies from a breeze to a tsunami. The developers continue to push out free content updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for something like this since Double Fine let me down on Massive Chalice. Wildermyth is XCOM combined with the D&D campaign you were DMing that got canceled due to COVID with just a dash of the aforementioned Massive Chalice thrown in thanks to the actual functional generational play.You take control of a small party of adventurers on whatever mission (the three campaigns in the game so far are rather good and do buck some of the stereotypes of high fantasy that we see games ingrained in), guiding them in battle, while they figure out their own lives. You'll see them fall in battle or grow old and retire and see some of their kids pick up the torch and continue on. And at the end, once the BBEG has fallen, you can make them folk heroes and have them show up for other adventures.I didn't expect to get attached to randomly generated roguelike characters, but I really did. When the lovers Fazad and Glen each lost a limb, only by a twist of fate for them to be restored I was overjoyed. When Laivm lost her son on his first mission protecting his mother and her dearest friend, I nearly cried. These little people really came to life for me.I'm not usually into early access games and I NEVER leave reviews for them unless they blow me out of the water. Wildermyth did. I'm so excited to see what else is in store.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing through the first campaign and found it enjoyable.  Combat provides for strategy without getting bogged down in too much complexity.  Over world map provides a basic strategy game as well where you weigh the reward of gathering resources against the risk of your enemies growing stronger over time.Credits sequence after completion of the campaign provided quick flashbacks to memorable events.  It also provided a brief epilogue of how all the characters lives played out afterwards.  I found this to be a really nice touch as it gave me that feeling of finishing a book I enjoyed where you feel a little sadness to part ways with characters you had gotten to know.If you're on the fence, go check out a video (as I did) to get a sense of what the game is.  I was happy with my choice to purchase it :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This special game is a tactical wonder with impeccable graphics and music. The randomization of the story line include the characters in battle modified state. Your character gets a spear, it will be displayed on the story scenes with a spear. It's the brilliant ever changing character states displayed in the scene of the story which immerses me into the game play. Very clever. I do recommend adding this game to your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I could never finish X-COM or Darkest Dungeon because I'd always delay the final mission ad infinitum, trying to max out my roster until I'd eventually grow tired of it. In that regard, Wildermyth soothes my battered soul; this game has that exact same appeal, but is actually made in a way which allows or maybe even encourages you to approach it this way.But, yeah, even aside from that, great game. I really like the art and the soundtrack, emergent storytelling is super cool, and the game is really fun to 100%. It's also very replayable (there are many different builds you can go for, much more than it seems at the beginning, and so, so many ways to make each class shine) and can be really challenging (but still fun) if you play on higher difficulty levels. Hard recommend, one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, some of the mechanics seemed really fun and innovative in interesting ways, but the overworld gameplay is just so awkward and half-baked, I just couldn't deal with it. How does it make sense that almost ALL actions in the overworld take weeks or a month to complete? It doesn't! "Hey, our friend is across the hill, let's walk over to check on him." How does this take TWO WEEKS? It's the worst case of ludonarrative dissonance I've encountered in a long time. I understand it has little impact on actual gameplay, but just watching a counter tick down on the map screen over and over and over again, waiting for no reason and for almost no reward (or an actual punishment) just annoyed the hell out of me. When the game told me that I had to clear out all monster to proceed, but there were no monster spawns left on the map, I just couldn't bring myself to explore the whole map to make sure the game didn't mean undiscovered spawns, with every move from area to area taking weeks, and scouting them taking even more time. Narratively, my party just started hanging out and had been in a few fights, but the game told me that I'm in already my second year of adventuring, I just snapped and refunded the thing. I understand that this might be a dumb reason, but the overworld is full of some of the dumbest design decisions that I've seen in an otherwise really pleasant and thoughtful game:(
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I must confess to "sleeping on" Wildermyth for much of 2021. I've historically had two main gripes against "procedural" games. One, I've found that procedural storytelling has never been as compelling to me as "crafted" content, and two, I find it harder to talk to friends about our experiences with games that have procedural elements. I've long been skeptical of whether a procedural game could produce truly mind-blowing moments, like Bioshock's "would you kindly" or Half-Life 2's "pick up that can." Only recently did I begin playing Wildermyth with a friend. We've played now for eight hours or so (across three sessions), but I've yet to complete any of the game's campaigns. And although I'm not sure that Wildermyth will be the game to truly make me change my mind about procedural games, I love the consistent nods to the choices you've made and the way your characters have developed. I've found that the rivalries, romances, transformations, and pets add so much texture to my experience. Not to mention that I love the Mystic class, and I don't think I've seen anything quite like the interfusion mechanic in any previous game I've played. The Mystic can "interfuse" with environmental objects, and then gains specific spells that can be cast from the object depending on the Mystic's interfusion ability and the object in question.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun but definitely use mods. The base game is unforgiving. The game's default balance makes it so anything above the absolute lowest difficulty requires high level legacy heroes, save scumming, or incredible luck. It's slightly more fun in multiplayer but most steam users won't be able to use that, since you have to already have friends for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game, played through all the campaigns in about 18 hours.  It got pretty repetitive toward the end; however, if you're into this genre that probably won't turn you off.  Eluna and the Moth was pretty challenging, and I really felt like I was pushed along by the game.  This was something I felt was missing in the other campaigns.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure what I should praise about Wildermyth most: The great storytelling system? The wonderful set of mechanics below it that are enlightening to look at? The interesting tactical game included? The great use of time and timers as resources for the overland map? Or the excellent modding opportunities?Maybe I should look at the less good parts instead, because there are so little? Okay, it takes some time to figure out the story mechanics, because you might lose track of what is relevant to the characters, what to the story and what is just about items or transformation (thought those rarely come without story relevance) or tactical advantages for the next fight - but that is mostly forgotten once you get comfortable with the system. Admittedly, the quality of the stories is not consistent (as of 85 hours Eluna and the Moth was the highlight, while I cannot even remember the Ultrix-story), but it seems the devs have their priorities straight and will add more stories with a DLC. And the world, characters and even interface are pretty often a bit to fourth-wall-breaking about the whole "this is a story. Like in a book."  gimmick.Still: Awesome stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun and interesting experience. I'm playing through the stories with a buddy, and it's really feels incredible how the stories unfold. The characters, though randomly generated, feel extremely real, and the story lines I've played so far are incredibly well written. The combat is passable, but very simple. The game really thrives on the story's that play out and the drama that forms within, and narratives that form between the stories as "legacy" characters exist in different events.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good strategy game, more challenging than I'd initially expected. The real charm comes from the writing and events that alter your characters. The writing may not please everyone, it tends to take ramblingly vague word clusters of adjectives over a clear description. That was a clear choice though designed to work with a procedural game, you're invited to just fill in the story and assign meaning. Procedural events though reoccur often, expect to see the more common ones five or six times if you play through all the campaigns. That said, there's still plenty of events/encounters I know I haven't seen because there are suppose to be at least 10 themes. The story campaigns are actually quite good, worth paying attention to them and they have a nostalgic feel to them that works well with the art. Many of the character stats don't seem to matter or affect much, maybe they do, but there's no clues. Customizing characters and seeing the transformations adds a fun element to things.There is a lack of abilities though, as often as you play and have to create new characters, you'll wind up using the same few builds over and over. Because getting abilities is slightly randomized, its also hard to do much experimentation if you're inclined. With lucky roles, you can get pretty over-powered characters or wind up with unfocused blobs that aren't useful until they die.The death feature is great though, letting characters sacrifice themselves or escape with wounds is an interesting feature - the story/lore person may wonder how "legacy characters" is explained in game. That can get odd.The family/offspring feature lets your heroes children have adventures, But the game only tracks parents and immediate siblings (I'm a bit nervous this means a grandkid could hook up with their grandparent).
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy Wildermyth, but it's important to know what sort of game it is. This is a storytelling game. Everything is based around your choices, the astounding quality of the written plots, and the procedurally generated heroes which you build. This is where the depth and fun lies. But Wildermyth does not have a particularly deep battle system. It's like a stripped back, less polished Xcom - which is totally fine, so long as what you are looking for is a game to dip into for its story, rather than master its tactical elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I normally post goofy comments for LoLs, but this game deserves a review from me. This is, by far, one of the most well-developed and immersive games I've ever played, period! I picked this up originally because the screen-shots reminded me of a Paper-Model Baldur's Gate, with turn-based strategy and stuff like that. But it is so much more than that. This is what you'd get if you mixed Darkest Dungeon style art (paper models), with DnD lore and character development, with Baldur's gate gameplay. I freaking love it!! You get to create a campaign, either solo, or with friends online, and immerse yourself in hours upon hours of character development. The story-telling is done through a comic-book style of reading and artwork. The characters that you randomly generate, or recruit throughout the campaign, actually get pulled into the comics and have dialogue (THAT ACTUALLY BUILDS ON THE STORY!!!) and interactions with each other. This game reminds me so much of Dungeons and Dragons where you can devote hours and energy into fleshing a character out, developing them through gameplay, and with one miscalculation lose them through the raw battles that get thrown at you. I legit got tears in my eyes when my character that had been with me from the start, and had received a blessing from a wolf god and was undergoing a transformation, finally met his downfall in a dungeon encounter. The cutscene, along with the story-telling part of how he fell, couldn't have been more theatrical and amazing if I wanted it to be. And I have had dozens of these and I'm not even 10 hours into it yet. I hope this comment gets seen by the developers to keep, and I hop they keey doing what they are doing. Add to this game in every way you can, add more stories, just keep building it, because I can guarantee you (with almost 100 percent confidence), that this game is going to be HUGE if you keep it up! Great job developers and I hope everyone enjoys this as much as I do!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I love this truly unique game.  The artwork and music is beautiful, and the game involves compelling fighting and character progression mechanics.  Where the game really stands out however is in the stories it tells around the characters.  If you spend hours with a party of adventurers and heroes, each will experience unique individual stories and you will begin to feel like you are the ONLY person with that specific character.  Once you introduce a hero from an old campaign into a new campaign, it feels a little like an old friend has returned.I wholeheartedly recommend this wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is both easy to get into, and easy to continue playing. The game's mechanics lend itself well to both multiplayer campaigns, and solo play, with the added benefit of having legacy characters, and campaigns to further their growth to provide continued play beyond the initial campaigns involving them. If you're looking for a fun, close to tabletop rpg experience for you and your friends, this game won't let you down.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: While a little rough around the edges, Wildermyth is a gem. Combining the fun of turn-based combat with the possibilities of a rogue-like adventure, it is well worth the buy. The only problem I have with it so far is that there is currently a limited amount of stories and events which happen to your characters - meaning that you know which choices to pick for your preferred result. That will be solved with more content, which presumably will come at full launch.The amount of customization is awesome, the fact that your characters' changes (both in personality, circumstances and equipment) are all visible and present in their presentation as you adventure along is magnificent. A great game so far! Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Bought 48hrs ago.I did not like the trailers/gameplay videos, seemed pretty bad.  But I read the reviews and decided to take a leap of faith.Gotta say this is one of the best discovered games since Slay the spire and Hades for me.Started the adventure with Kanye West, Will Smith and Kevin Hart, later on formed Capitalism party with Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg. Villages made discounts, Capitalism has changed the world (for the better, i think).Not too long into the game I was forced to google the names of celebrity children (possibly put me on some list). Unknown to me before, now Willow Smith and Chicago West is the best side map exploring duo.I've just completed two campaigns, but Kanye West insta made it and is the only tier 4 and tier 5 hero. He is truly godlike. The rivalry between Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Bezos was unforgetabble.Local politicians, old classmates, current friends, favorite celebrities, or completely custom chars. Adjust their personality traits to match what'd you expect and you'll have an amazing experience.I dislike head transformations. They ruin the immersion for me. (in my run Oprah Winfrey has been turned into a crow-head against her will.)And there was lack of faces and hairs selection at start, but I've found mods to solve that.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully written and complex, and has really grown into itself with the 1.0 release especially.  For as straightforward as the character builds are, I didn't expect the combat of this game to be as challenging as it is and it's part of what got me hooked.  Create a bunch of your own characters, watch them grow and return for future stories, and mostly watch them lose limbs.  It's great.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I've only finished two campaigns, but wanted to write a review.  This game is great, the stories and choices are awesome, and you really don't know what's going to happen as a consequence. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves TTRPGs this one is a blast. I started out carefully making adjustments to my characters but have ended up letting the game make these decisions in true dice rolling fashion. The stories are wild and usually funny, then you get surprised with a deeper thought-provoking story. Based on your choices, some of these stories have tugged at the heartstrings a bit. Other than the first campaign, I haven't seen a lot of choices regarding friendship/romantic options between characters, but that doesn't make this gem any less enjoyable to play. The art is simple and perfectly fits the mood depicted by the creators. You can even create your own adventures and share them!It may be worth pointing out that on occasion, I have inadvertently clicked on the wrong thing and ended my turn instead of attacking because the monster card swayed out of the way and I missed, but other than being slightly annoying, it's never caused a team member to die, just click carefully.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the closest I have ever seen a CRPG approach the tabletop RPG experience. I just finished the intro campaign, and it was amazing. The crunchy mechanical bits of the turn-based combat and advancement systems are fun and engaging, but the real star of the show is their procedural story generation, which is the best I've seen - the combination of RNG and well-written and -illustrated comic-book interludes works beautifully. It's the classic and mostly-tired zeroes-to-heroes story, you start with three farmers forced into adventure, but it's executed so well I can't complain. They gain new companions, develop rivalries and friendships and fall in love (all of which have minor mechanical impacts), randomly pair up for character-building side adventures, have children, and occasionally fall in battle and have to be replaced with fresh young faces. There's a big overland map to scout, delve into dungeons, fight off monster intrusions, defend settlements, and gather resources. Between each chapter about a decade passes, so your favorites will grow old and eventually retire - certain events will extend the retirement age. And when a campaign is done, those heroes become legends and feature in later stories (though I haven't started a second one yet). Highly recommended, a steal at $25. My 2021 CRPG GOTY so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is a unique and entertaining game concept, from the 'paper-doll' combat boards to the story comics to the character customization (both appearance and abilities).  I love that you can have nonbinary characters in the game (being enby myself) and even installed the mod that lets the game generate nonbinary characters with equal probability to binary male and female. One of my favorite things to do is see who ends up paired as friends, rivals, or lovers, since I'm always generating those randomly. The fact that personality traits alter the dialogue makes replays fun, too, though eventually (if you've played as long as I have) you'll definitely notice repeats of random generated events. That's just to be expected, though!At this writing, I have played all the 5-chapter campaigns. They are all very well-written and challenging (I played the second-to-toughest rank in combat difficulty, I believe, but kept the number of invasions average). The Deepist campaign is particularly tough because for many of the key encounters you are being chased or infiltrating into massive numbers of enemies. I must have tried 5 or 6 times to complete that campaign before I finally reached the end, and even then only by the skin of my teeth.I'm now working on playing to build up my legacy characters, as I don't yet have any that rank higher than tier 2. My favorite ones so far  are a mystic with Celestial build and a hunter with Elmsoul--both are quite formidable. Aesthetically, I love the crow wings, and so a few of my characters have'em.I believe I could be playing this game for a very long time, especially if new campaigns / events are released! I'm already excited for the weapon/armor DLC that I think is coming out in May 2023. :) Keep it up devs!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is great. There is a beautiful combination of comic book narrative with tactics-based combat. The magic system is interesting too. It's all about taking control of scenery and using its natural properties. At first I was freaked out about getting my characters hurt or killed, but eventually you learn that it's not about any individual character, but rather seeing generations of characters grow, evolve, die, retire, etc. If you want a game where you can sit, relax, and spend an hour or a day playing, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is a labour of love that feels truly new and unlike any other game I've played before, despite many familiar RPG elements. It's not perfect but the developers have managed to meld the randomness of procedural generation with the fixed plot points crucial to telling any story with emotional impact (as anyone who has tried to write something before will know, true randomness rarely leads to a coherent story, let alone a story that has real heft) to a higher degree than anything I've seen previously, and that I hadn't thought possible at this indie scale. Very happy to see a non-AAA, non-visual novel game that puts story at its core and works too. Highly recommended for everyone who enjoys games under Steam's 'Story-Rich' tag.
