_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I was definitely enjoying the early access, kind of forgot about the game for a bit and was pleasantly surprised to see the full release. I haven't had too much time with it, but it's been an absolute delight thus far. The art style grabbed my attention but the game play kept it, and the full release has only improved the experience. Check this game out, I can't imagine any RPG fan who won't find something to enjoy here!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my radar for quite a bit, and I'm so glad I finally gave this a chance! It really reminds me of D&D with a different take on the magic and battle system that I quite enjoy, giving more lenient yet distinct resource management to magic users while allowing more simplistic yet genius battle mechanics. The story development and character-building aspects of this game are so wonderful, allowing you to simply have fun or make intricate OC's to tell a story with, and a lot of campaigns to play through. The developers are currently making a unique gamemode dlc that sounds absolutely perfect, as well as currently have a simplistic yet nice skins and armor dlc which allows even further character customization and storytelling. I plan on buying the dlc once I've finished all of the basegame, as I want a "completed legacy" of all the current campaigns from basegame, but afterwards I plan on making extended universes and using pre-existing oc's of mine for fun. I cannot recommend this game enough, the price may appear a bit steep but honestly just watch some let's plays of the game to see if you'd like it then take the dive if so. I recommend "Seri Pixel Biologist" for a really nice story-based lets play of it, but there are obviously many others you may find better intrigue from. For further pitch, I have a three-centuries-old woman named Linda who's just literally walking around the world while completely on fire, and she's a badass in battle but an absolute dork on the team. When the world isn't trying to end, she's off in the mountains with monks and painters. Her name is Linda, she's watched several of my favorite heroes die tragically or herorically :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: The character building and development are excellent.  All of the little stories give connection and depth to your characters.  And being able to see your characters become legends and come back in future games allows for really strong attachments to form.  It's as close to an open ended story as you can get, without sitting at a table playing with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of tactical RPGs and emergent storytelling games. Get it now and thank me later.

I hope some of the concepts in this game are reprieved by more game developers because there is potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: You need this game.  If you like D&D, Swords, Spells, Rampaging ugly monsters, myth, intrigue, and a good fantasy saga -- then you simply MUST get this game.  While some may look at Wildermyth and see not much more than a simple "Choose Your Own Adventure" game or visual novel, doing so would be a disservice to both yourself and the game.  There is an awful lot going on here 'behind the pages', and this game is amazingly well-done and the artwork/style is astoundingly beautiful and done just as well.  The main focus of game play is reading panels as in a comic book, with the characters shown/drawn in various poses (i.e., not 'static' 2D images) with highly illustrative facial expressions appropriate to the situation.  The story/situation will change based on the attributes of each character, their interplay and their developed history within this play-through.  (!!!)  The characters' dialog and expressions change as the game/story progresses, based on the interplay of the aspects/attributes of the characters and party, heavily influenced by your choices within the story.  Within each story or subsection, you may be required to make one or more choices as to how a particular character will respond to a situation, or to decide which avenue of approach or tact the party will use in the given situation.  Another very nice aspect of the game is that when you finish a mission and get an item, that item is clearly displayed on your character in every panel/scene thereafter.  Not stupendous, I know, but another nice little touch that shows the attention to detail paid to the game by the devs.  One thing to be aware of beforehand is that all equipment assignments are permanent, BoE (Bind on Equip), you can also craft new equipment {weapons, armor} for each specific hero, however.  As the story moves along, you will have to scout new areas, clear monsters from certain locations, and then "research"the area to secure it for the townsfolk, and then you can claim the resources generated there at the end of every month.  There is time pressure in the game in that as the story progresses, at the end of every month, as you generate resources and upgrade your locations defenses, and craft new equipment, the monster factions gain upgrades, too, in the form of new monster types as well as health and armor upgrades and new powers.  Everything is done so very well and meshes together in such interesting ways, that whilst playing the game, it easily becomes one of those, "How can it be 5AM already?!?" games!!  You need this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, far better than I was expecting. Was originally iffy because of the visual style, but the game is good. Easily the most authentic TTRPG experience I've encountered. _childDocuments_.review: I rarely write Steam reviews, because someone's usually already written a much more coherent opinion before me.  I had to make an exception for this game.  It's a really impressive merging of emergent storytelling, character-based relationships, and DND-like strategy game.I've played dozens of RPGs.  This one feels the most alive.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a story generator where you're in command of a company of random adventurers facing down a large threat. Though you directly control them in combat, they each have their own personalities and their interactions outside of combat are surprisingly interesting and dynamic.It hooked me more than I would expect a game of this type to do, mostly due to interesting writing for the encounters and interactions.I can think of 2 things that might be hold-ups for some people1) There is a lot of reading. Nothing is voiced and most of the story plays in slides that have art and talking bubbles like a comic book. If you like comic book storytelling, then you'll love it.2) If you start playing it a lot, you will run into some of the same random events eventually in other campaigns, and it spoils it a bit when you already know how they will end. This may be less of an issue in the future, as the devs have created a modding system where anyone can create their own dynamic and story events to tie into any campaign. _childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is a good game that proves not all review scores should be treated equally. There are those movies on Rotten Tomatoes like Pulp Fiction, Star Wars or Raiders of the Lost Ark that share the same exact Rotten Tomatoes score as Best in Show, Three Kings or the Star Trek reboot. All are good movies but some are classics and some aren't despite having the same RT rating. This Overwhelmingly Positive game isn't a classic, it's just a good enough game that's difficult to not recommend but isn't one that I'd rave about.At it's core, Wildermyth is a pretty simple game of party-based procedural combat with paper doll cutouts on a battlefield. The game starts on a world map (well, kind of a region map) and you go uncover new areas. Usually there will be a fight to take over the region from whatever menace you're fighting. When you engage in combat, you face off with foes on small maps with you team of up to 5. The combat is broken down in a I-Go/You-Go format, with each character usually getting a move then a strike. You proceed through the tactical map with the usual objective to wipe out the opposing force. The opposing force might be strange looking robot-type creatures or monsters, each with different abilities. If you win, you take over the area and that will get you a couple of extra resources at the end of the chapter (see the itemization paragraph below). If that was it then Wildermyth would be like most any other game out there. When you start a game, you choose an adventure from the list of 5 (plus some legacy generic campaigns). It will have 3-5 chapters and the campaign just kind of sets up the foozle you're trying to beat. These aren't particularly entertaining. They exist only to set up the main adventure.Within the campaign there will be some smaller stories that kind of randomly pop up that give the game a bit more flavor. It's a bit like something you might see a novice tabletop GM do, with the adventurers coming across a sword in a stone, or a monolith in the middle of the woods or a friend who might need help.  They're told in a comic-book kind of format and choices can matter but only in somewhat of a minor way. It might look weird that a poor choice made the head of my fighter look like a pigeon but it didn't really impact game play. If these stories grab you then you'll probably love the game. I wasn't quite as impressed. As someone who has played with good GMs over many years, I found these stories fine but they didn't particularly thrill me. I heard more inventive stuff in my weekly games of D&D or Battletech. The writing is okay but not superlative and the stories seemed a bit generic. I really appreciate the attempt but I'd say the execution was only fair and therefore Wildermyth doesn't "grab" me the way I had hoped it would.As you progress through the chapters, your characters will age and eventually retire. Some may die and can either be remembered as a legacy or forgotten. Sometimes one will retire and pass on knowledge, helping your newer characters to level very quickly. It's a good mechanic and provides continuity to the game, which helps with engagement in the game world itself (because the wilder world offers really nothing to get engaged about).Graphically this game has a pretty unique style. The characters are paper-doll cutouts on the tactical maps and surprisingly this works. They're not incredibly detailed but the art is good enough to get a feel for each character, their armor/weapons are appropriately displayed and it lends itself to duplicating that table-top experience that the game is trying to replace.There are 3 classes (though they aren't created equally) and each class has a handful of skills you can choose between as you level up. You'll notice a substantial difference with higher level characters and the difference between a newbie and a seasoned veteran is stark. Those skills you choose will help determine how your character will fight and there's a list but you're only presented 4 to choose from (you can "spin the wheel" again to get different skills for a cost). This prevents you from creating characters sporting the same overpowered builds, which means that when you do have that one perfect build it's again really obvious and fun.Itemization is also pretty basic. You uncover and secure regions to get some raw goods. At the end of the chapters you can spend those raw goods to buy some new armor (out of about 5 types) or weapons (3 levels of the typical weapons you'd see in a RPG). These might only do 1 point more of damage but when you combine that with the skills, small itemization changes can make a big differences. You might as well spend it since you can't take it with you anyway at the end of the campaign.This game has 5 difficulty settings, from pitifully easy to insanely hard. When you start a campaign you'll choose what level you want. Well, there are really two difficulties - combat and the overland map. The normal difficulty will be a challenge to many. Ramp it up and fights become a tense chess match with the usual screaming when the RNG Gods decide to hose you at the most inopportune time. I encountered no bugs at all in the game. My sincere thanks to the devs for this.So are there any problems? Not really. I think the game is fine. But like some of those highly rated movies on RT, I've watched this movie and while it was entertaining I'm not sure I need to see it again. It's a nice little blend of RPG and tactical party based combat but neither side goes deep enough to really grab me. I appreciate the attempt at story telling but these stories aren't grabbing me. I appreciate the aging of my heroes but I've had ones retire that I couldn't even remember their names. I appreciate the tactical combat but I've played better in a number of games (Fell Seal, FF Tactics, Battle Bros, the original X-COM). Wildermyth does a lot of things well enough that I think it belongs in a lot of folks' Steam libraries. But after playing Wildermyth for 10 hours, I don't have much of a longing to return to the game. Instead, I'd like to find a really good tactical combat game. Or a fun RPG with a long, overarching story. Or just to find another well-run tabletop game. Because while Wildermyth attempts to bridge all of these areas - and does so to some extent - it just doesn't go far enough to satisfy me in any of them. Your mileage may vary but this is still a game you should strongly consider buying. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of RPG's over the years, and this one has its own unique charm to it.It feels a little bit like a board game with tile-based combat. The classes are simple and unique. The way magic is done in this game is really interesting - your mage possesses objects on the board which are then used to launch a variety of attacks.The subplots have a lot of charm to them and your heroes visibly age over the course of the game. Choices you make also affect the way they look. Definitely pick this up if you like tactical RPG's.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: In the three odd hours it took me to play through the introductory three chapter campaign, I felt more attached and invested in my characters than I have in 99% of 20+ hour videogame sagas. It's a delightful little experiment in storytelling where the focus is on the semi-random outcomes for -characters-, with the "big bad" just there to deliver a hook for the heroes to take action.If I had to layer any constructive criticism, it does suffer from none of its elements being *outstandingly* good - as is often the case when a game tries to be so many things at once. You will find better tactical battle games. You will play more engaging and indepth world level strategy games. But what's there is perfectly serviceable to the game's main task, pleasant to play, and gets the job done.It's a fascinating experiment and I'd love to see more games take risks like these.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely magical.The writing is beautiful, full of wit, sweetness, humour and sadness in just the right dose. Well made campaigns and mechanics and really no one playthrough is the same.The art is simple and wonderful, and the tabletop lite feel just makes you want to try anything without minmaxing, and just enjoying the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal. This is going to sound dramatic, but this game perfectly executes (already and only in early access, no less!) that concept of "perfect game for me." You know what I'm talking about. Everyone has a concept of *THE* game that scratches every itch you could want from a game. For me, this is that. There is so much content already. I will support these devs in any way I can. This being a labor of love is evident in every aspect of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a seriously good game. And I don't say that lightly.I don't know how to describe this. It's challenging, yet not too challenging that you can't enjoy the stories. It's replayable, not on the surface of things. It's kind of a roguelike, but not a roguelike either. Your characters change physically, mentally, socially. I always discover something new in each run. The devs also post new content quite regularly, even though I'd say - having played at the very first days of the launch - that even as it was, it was already very complete.The artstyle is beautiful and there are a couple of nice mods in the workshop for those who'd like more choice in appearance, stories and events.A seriously good find.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun turn based DnD simulator game. You will enjoy this game more if you're into the role-playing aspects like with Crusader Kings. Character sheets are really well done with constant callbacks to previous encounters through permanent gear, visual skins. history and even mistakes made in battles that result in wounds / perma debuffs at least feel interesting in a story way. The strength of this game is definitely the ability to tie each progressive upgrade to a point in the campaign where you reached it. Combat overall is pretty fun, interfuse magic is definitely the most interesting combat which looks like it took 10x the dev time of ranged/melee. Melee/ranged are very simple but still pretty fun to play with some really fun stuff like defensive gameplay and traps. All in all, upgrades in general feel really fun and there is a lot of potential for DLC to expand there for more replayability.I will say that combat doesn't translate as well into higher difficulty levels as most of the combat mechanics isn't really strategy and moreso ties into character relationships with rivals/love interests having buffs for each other on the battlefield.Monsters are cool designs, boss fights are generally pretty fun and difficulty is pretty much perfect. Complaints are the lack of depth in the game, in some ways there needs to be story based procedural generation for this type of game as comics/events repeat after the 2nd campaign already causing there to be a massive drop-off in replayability at least story wise. There is also a lack of attention paid to legacy characters (finished campaign heros that you can replay) as certain characteristics like what they looked like before a transformation, or their romantic relationships in other campaigns, are not stored or interacted with. The comics themselves are sort of whatever, most of them I barely understand tbh but the game is a really great indie gem that has a lot of potential as a genre if someday better art and better story writing is there.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really wonderful game. The difficulty may not be what you're hoping for if you're a veteran of games like X-COM looking for a challenge but the complexity is enough to keep it consistently interesting, the story telling is beautiful and the art is surprisingly stunning for a game that isn't graphically demanding. I'd suggest it to anyone with a passing interest in the genre without hesitation.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Short, Short Version: Wildermyth is cutting edge, innovative, and fun. While it may suffer a little bit on extensive replay it combines procedural storytelling and gameplay very well and is definitely worth checking out.Short Version: Wildermyth is something special. Every part of the game is well done, and while I wish there were more events this lack of quantity does not prevent it being a great game. If you like tactical turn based RPGs and want to play something unique and interesting you definitely owe it to yourself to explore Wildermyth. I expect there are going to be some people out there who dislike it for some reason or another, but even then it is worth playing simply to see what Worldwaker Games has pulled off. YOU MAY LIKE THIS GAME IF:You like innovative takes on the tactical turn based RPG genreYou are tired of games that use D&D-style or point driven magic systemsYou like developing your character over the course of multiple campaigns and seeing how they permutateYOU MAY NOT LIKE THIS GAME IF:You don’t like having repetitive events over multiple playthroughsYou dislike not having not having complete control over how your characters are developedThe papercraft art turns you offFull Version:

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Wildermyth. It has some very unique ideas, it's a solid tactical RPG and while neither the animations nor artwork are top notch they do the job of conveying what information they need. If you like tactical RPG's you'll almost certainly enjoy this one.However, there are a few glaring issues. One of the big selling points is that you can play a campaign coop with your friends, but the game really does not support control for multiple players. If one person has a window open in the campaign map, it pops up for everyone, and if someone else closes it, it closes it for everyone. The campaign also has a bad tendency to pass time unprompted or while players are still in the process of making decisions, and will skip cutscenes if one person reaches the end of the cutscene. I found a way around this by just designating one person as the "decision maker" but even then there would still be friction between the actions of different players making the game confused, which does take away some of the enjoyment I had in the game. There were also other glitches and bugs that were too small to point out here, but my point is that the game suffers from quality of life issues and needs more polish to iron out the bugs.Mechanically, the game plays just fine on normal difficulties, but as you crank up the difficulty you will quickly realize that the game is extremely unforgiving. A character hitting zero HP, something which can easily happen in one hit after your first few missions, permanently cripples that character. If it happens again, the character is straight up dead, and most of the time you'll be stuck with level 1 recruits that will, again, die instantly when hit. Especially in campaigns that have more than 3 chapters you'll also see your strongest characters retiring, and you'll be forced to fill the vacancy they left with new recruits that are simply not ready for what awaits them. The game tries to lessen the impact of this by letting you craft gear without time investments between chapters & by removing some of the powerups from the monster decks when a chapter ends, but the amount of power they lose is laughably little when compared to the power of the characters that retire on your end.As an extra note, the game also does not do a good job of explaining certain things, forcing you to learn how stuff works by trail & error. For instance, you can sometimes unlock mutations for your characters, but the game doesn't really tell you what you get when you unlock an option to mutate, nor does it tell you how your character will mutate further. And for example, if you're a Mystic, you can get the Humanist ability, which lets you perform special interfusion effects, but then doesn't tell you what those effects do. This is made worse by the the fact that every time your character levels up you get like 3 choices of abilities to pick, and chances are high 2/3 are garbage choices. Oftentimes, you won't realize you made a bad choice for one of your characters until it's too late.So, in short, I really enjoyed Wildermyth. It's a good game that I definitely enjoyed playing, but it has some issues that I felt were important to mention to anyone planning on buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool TTRPG-y video game! So far I've done the first chapter of the three-chapter *tutorial* campaign with a friend - the gameplay and plot / writing are very engaging, and the mechanics are generally fleshed out well. We played 4 hours in one shot and had to make ourselves stop since we found ourselves 'one more turn'ing it for like 30 minutes after we said we'd be done for the night.There's loads of campaigns that are available, but you *have* to do the tutorial campaign first before you can do any of them, so I cannot speak to them. That being said, the tutorial campaign has thus far wildly exceeded my expectations, so I have faith in them to be as good - there's currently two single player (or multiplayer) campaigns (the 3-chapter tutorial one, and a 5-chapter main one), as well as 3 strictly multiplayer campaigns. You can also do 3 or 5 chapter campaigns with no overarching story, and only random events (random romances, random plot events like a party member becoming a werewolf or background story events, etc). There's also steam workshop support for custom campaigns/mods, which is also nice, as well as a wiki that is reasonably fleshed out.On the flip side, the game could use some polish - in multiplayer there was occasional jank with text dialogues disappearing for me or my friend (oddly, usually me, the host, more than them). This isn't a softlock or anything but it was definitely a bit weird. Some mechanics aren't explained well (e.g. it's hard to determine enemy movement speed/range, from what I can tell?), but the game has lets you save pretty much whenever dialogue isn't going on, so you can xcom-savescum a bit if you want to while learning, or fall back on autosaves, or potentially just wipe, take penalties for that chapter, and keep going.Overall it's a very fun game and definitely the best TTRPG-y experience I've had in a video game/on a computer, with friends remotely.

_childDocuments_.review: If your favourite part of XCOM was that it created a completely new story every time you played, then don't hesitate. This is the epitome of that. It's part XCOM, part Massive Chalice, part King of Dragon Pass with just a dash of classic tabletop RPG mixed in and a good helping of a narrative style and aesthetic reminiscent of webcomics like Order of the Stick. Even better, it's moddable and new scenes that can happen over the course of a story are easy to add. There's hardly anything not to like here. Note, however, that the game is currently fairly easy - so if you're looking for a really tough challenge, you might find yourself disappointed. Play it to experience a dynamic story with characters that are unique to your iteration and that you'll nevertheless grow to love.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on sale and it's proven more than worth it.  If you like roguelites and tabletop RPGs, buy it.  You won't regret it.Pros: * closest you'll come to playing a tabletop RPG without awful BO and/or children screaming on discord* familiar grid-based combat system with unique mechanics (the mystic, a magic user equivalent, is particularly neat)* incredible depth of character development leading to some unique and often hilarious conversations amongst your party; they will fall in love, have kids, turn into living fire and other such typical developments.  They'll also develop new skills and acquire gear, pets, etc, and all of these things can impact both combat and their interaction with the world.  Choices matter!* lovely artwork and several campaigns out of the box. I've finished the first and am partway through the second on the list and so far they're really engrossing stories and have been a blast to play through.  * It's always the newbie warrior who joins up being all "MY MAMA SO GREAT I'M THE BEST" who runs in and dies first, amiright? Every friggin' time.Cons: * the graphics won't be for everyone. the sprite-based thing works out well overall, though; don't let it dissuade you.  what you end up with is lovely artwork that adapts to your characters' appearance and gear.  You'll watch them transform, age, etc., to a more satisfying degree than you'd find in a more mainstream game trying to look like a AAA title.* the camera can be a bit fiddly at times. It's a quite minor gripe; things go a bit off-center when the camera jumps to the next character if you've been panning the view around (or something). Overall, really fantastic game that'll keep you laughing and feeling the feels and occasionally cackling maniacally for a good long time. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: My GOTY for 2021. The plus : - 5 campaigns with a story, ranging from 3 to 5 chapters.- Create your own heroes and forge them to be legends. - Simple but efficient tactical-RPG gameplay, with a twist on magic. - Heroes have personnalities and it shows. Even if you encounter an event you already seen, heroes will react differently to it based on their traits. - Unique visual style. - The storytelling in general.- Gotta love them MODSThe minuses : - Default difficulty is sometimes too easy, at least for me. With good understanding of classes building it's easy rolling on the game. - Music ( which is really nice BTW ) can get a little repetitive. - The game is in english, while it's ok for dialogues between characters it can get difficult for non-english speaker to understand outside of dialogues. _childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth's strength lies in its customization and clever procedural generation to weave stories centered on characters you create. I've never seen another game quite like it. Personality stats either bring life and variation to randomly generated heroes or allow you to re-create your own beloved characters. It's so much fun to get a story event and have your own characters participate in a consistent way according to their personality- but still have every campaign be different/fresh every time. They feel alive and I love them :-)-Turn-based combat is fun and satisfying with significant challenge at higher difficulty settings-Excellent writing-Enormous replayability-Fantastic multiplayer capability, local or online-Narrative strengths: characters with customizable appearance and personality, fun character relationship system, procedurally-generated events in between combat that change depending on hero personalities, poetic and poignant prewritten campaigns, interesting themes, transformations system-Those who are into modding/writing will find significant support for adding their own content into the game (this was one of the devs' original goals)-Devs continue to add content and updates to the story and mechanicsI highly recommend the armors and skins DLC as well especially if you love character customization!

_childDocuments_.review: [edited[Initially I gave this game a good review, because the base game is really fun. I completed it fully = had 100% achievements. Later, a paid DLC is added to the game, adding new achievements, so now my platinum 100% CHANGED into a 59% achievements. Affecting my AGCR. And almost half of the game's achievements are paywalled behind a paid DLC. Not a fan of this policy, broke my heart. [initial positive review below. Game is still fun if you don't care about achievements]I fell in love with this game. It's cute, it's emotional - a slightly more colourful and bright version of the Darkest Dungeon - here also your heroes can get hurt and die in a fight, so you need to be careful. There is a lot of possibility to customize your characters - you can make them the way you want, customize each character's looks, clothing colours and name. There is the mechanics of progress for your characters - their skills and gear - but also for your enemies, who get gradually stronger during each campaign! Then there is the legacy aspect in which your characters can have children and former heroes can be used again in a new campaign - I haven't explored this aspect fully yet, as I have just completed one campaign and started the second one. The game is extremely pleasant visually, making funny references to tabletop games and with stunningly beautiful drawings. The music is nice and the gameplay is quite intuitive. I haven't encountered any bugs and everything worked smoothly for me. The combat (turn-based strategy on a small board) is satisfying and easy to learn, even though it contains some new, original elements - for example the way magic works is something I haven't seen before. Wizard class characters can interact with objects during combat and the effect of the spell depends on whether you enchant a stone, a piece of furniture, a plant or a campfire. I can't wait to play again today after work :D It feels that the game has a potential for tens or even hundreds of hours of satisfying gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really fun, and the developers were really responsive in helping me solve some issues I had regarding multiplayer.The gameplay itself is a simple turn-based combat style. The art-style is wonderful, and the story generation is a really fun way to get attached to your characters. All of the mechanics are fairly intuitive, though I do wish there was more explanation as to what some of the stats are and how they affect your characters. That being said, i've been able to bring in people who've never really played any video games at all and have them figure out the game easily. For more experienced players, theres still plenty of challenge and risk with a no-save mode, more careful gear selection, and higher difficulty settings.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really struggling to like this game. The art is good, but there are no animations. Characters and monsters are represented by static paper standees that "hop" around in a very annoying way. I'm struggling to understand the story, if there is one, because the dialogue seems to be either randomly generated, or translated very poorly from some other language. The game also doesn't seem to have any kind of help system. Nothing pops up when I hover my mouse over buttons or icons, so I have no idea what doing anything does. There are no descriptions of abilities.I was told this was "fantasy XCOM" but it's no-where near the quality of XCOM. It has no narrative, no descriptions, and the graphical decisions are from a primitive era. I don't understand why it's so wildly popular.Edit: With a bit more play time, and a bit more introspection, I think I've hit upon why I don't like this game. It is listed as an "RPG" and "Choices Matter" and yet neither of these claims are even remotely true. It's very rare you even get to make a choice (most things in the game are decided for you randomly), and even when you do it has no impact on the gameplay at all. And the almost total lack of choice and control of character actions and behavior means there is no role to play. It's a storybook game, sure, but not an RPG. So this is a great game for people not looking for those elements, but definitely not a match for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is a delightful game, with gorgeous art and fun yet rewarding gameplay.Though I feel all of that pales in comparison to the living story that evolves as you play through the game. Throughout the game, your characters (heroes) will get stronger, level up and generally be better at 'hero-ing'. Yet through frequent (but not annoyingly so) random events, your characters will tell their stories and gain new abilities, new items or in unfortunate circumstances, lose limbs or get other physical disfigurements. The list in the base game is already massive, but add on top modding support and you have a plethora of events, stories and side content for your characters to go through!I could go on for hours about how fun this game is, or how unique it approaches its genre but... just pick it up and give it a try! And what's better is that you can play with friends via Steam's couch co-op feature, so you don't even have to experience the game alone if you don't want to!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing 'adventure, turn based rpg' game. It's clever, it's rewarding. The campaigns are as short or long as you want them to be. _childDocuments_.review: Ok first and foremost I simply love this game! I am amazed at how many different bases it covers and still keeps itself held together. Some games try to cover too many bases and add too many different mechanics or idea's but this game just somehow adds all these different types of game play, themes and stories but doesn't feel cluttered or clunky. think it's a safe bet to say that if you like any of the following you will have a blast with it too. Dungeons and Dragons or PathfinderWritingReadingComicsBoard gamesCartoonsAnd Fantasy set stories in generalThe random encounters and generated characters make each play through of the same story different than the last with new consequences or benefits dangers and side plots. Every decision matters with either a gain or a disasters and each one of the story settings are unique. Further they are still adding more content and It has a Steam Workshop which I think will add endless content and new missions enemies adventurers and characters. If I knew how to mod I would mod the crap out of this game! It has so much more growth and possibilities and as it is, is a ton of fun already! I would pay whatever price they asked for this game I think even in early access it's enough fun to buy already even if they were done with content. Get this game! Support this team they have something truly special here and I want to see more!

_childDocuments_.review: The best RPG I've ever played, with stories that evolves around you and your actions - and not a story you simply follow or discover. Every playthrough is unique. Lovely graphics, and a charming sense of humour. There is a lot to do, and even choices you make that you think might ruin your game can be in your favour, which shows how clever the game engine is. It's a MUST BUY in my opinion, if you like RPGs or even real life table-top RPG sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Never been compelled to write a review until I played this amazing game. Wildermyth really makes the experience your own as you play, from customising characters freely, to guiding their own progression, it really does feel as if the story was made for you and you're not simply a bystander. Gameplay-wise this game is also very strong, there are many strategies and abilities at your disposal, and with the scaling difficulty of enemies the dynamic events that occur around your characters makes for an enjoyable, and fluid campaign with both triumphs and losses along the way. Again, another example of how this game has perfected personalised stories around great game-play. Wildermyth is already a great purchase at it's current price, I've only completed the Gorgon campaign, and it already feels like I've got my money's worth. I can't wait to see where the modding community and the Developer Team add to this game, it has a lot of potential to be very special. (If it isn't already)
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! Wildermyth does so many things ... * gives you beautiful, timeless art with characters that change from your choices and equipment, * characters you can root for, fall for* choices and stories that stay with you like the best role playing games, table or virtual* a unique musical score that gets in your head* tactical gameplay that's quick to learn, hard to master, with all the extra difficulty you want* a world full of creatures, relationships, people, and stories unlike any other. * Just FUNIf you like tabletop games, games that make stories, turn-based tactics, rougelikes likeXCOM, DnD, FTL, Final Fantasy, you'll love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun turn based adventure game. The art style is beautiful and the 2-d paper doll aspects really give this game a unique spin. It's been a joy to create new characters or level up legacy ones. The workshop for this game has been a wonderful addition to adding extras to the already great story-lines and giving the much needed addition of better relationship changes or advances. I do wish the multiplayer aspect of the game was a bit more polished as there are a couple of bugs with the choices being reset or continual refreshing of the page specially when choosing which character related to who the most. I also wish the game had a system for two people playing at once so that characters stop going at the same time when they're not intending to (ie. something like initiative would be cool). I'd also love a chance to setup a formation for your characters during most/some known battles so that the squishes aren't sometimes in the front or warriors stuck behind a ranger who may not want to move.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is one of my favourite games out there. So what is it?You play heroes. Build a party. Go through a story. It has high replay value, as the story elements can (and do change). You can adjust the difficulty as you like. You earn legacy points through play. These can be used to recruit new characters or to make up the shortfall when crafting gear.Also Legacy points can be used to "Promote your Heroes" at the end of a story. Heroes can be added to your Legacy collection. This allows them to be recruited in later games. When promoted at the end of the story, the character is more powerful when brought 'out of retirement' It is fun looking back over old characters, seeing how much characters can change - both personally and physically.  A fun aspect of the game is the Transformation events. You come across something that alters your character - sometimes removing their ability to wield weapons - but replacing them with potent abilities. Sometimes too potent. I managed to kill one of my party when they got caught in a rain of meteors that my star-touched character dropped.   Stupid Critters and their grapple/drag abilities. Anyway. Lots of fun. Has Multiplayer that I never played. And apparently Omenroad is fun as well - but I haven't touched the DLC yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

I know I only have a few hours logged but it was a few hours straight and prevented me from getting to bed on time for work.  Been a long time since that has happened to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't recommend this game enough, Wildermyth is a game where the journey is more important than the destination and that journey is different and impactful as it is personal every time you play it. If you like games where you get to see your hero take shape before your eyes, seeing their adventures build upon them then you will love this game.A character I had started as a snarky rouge but after bonding with a fire spirit suddenly he was a fire bender! I can't wait to see what else the game has in store for future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Wildermyth is an experience. After 5 chapters of growing with some pretty dope, transformed characters with tons of artifacts at my disposal, all around levels 4-7, I accidentally ran my B team (levels 1-3) into the final map. A gruesome gauntlet of Deepists in front of them, powered up over the years, they managed to beat the odds. 3 of the 5 that entered died in battle for the cause. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start with a detail I love about this game - magic system. It is absolutly wonderful. Finally something fresh in this area (at least finally in an overall good game :) ). This game offer more folklor magic, where mystics drain power from enviroment, destroying it in the process and it is done wonderfully.Now for the more general review: strong, good game. Great narrative, art style, nice combat system. But most important is overall feeling of the game. It really does good job to make you feel myth atmosphere.Few bad things:- Combat could have been more complex. Not more difficult, sliders are ok in that regard, but offer more complexity to it. Its not bad how it is now, but could been better.- Overall gameplay loop is a little too repetetive, even "random character events" are all in the same loop. Some variety would be nice. For now Im 100% sure I will finish whole game, but Im also sure I have to do it one campaign aty the time with few weeks in between. Binging would kill fun for me.- English is weird in some dialogues. I'm clearly not native speaker, but I saw more people struggling with it. I get it might be flavoure thing and I appreciate it, but I would also very much appreciate non-flavoure version as an option for people struggling with the language.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. This game is great. It's amazing. I love the story telling and I was addicted for days after getting it. But I have to admit that it lacks replayability. Eventually you're playing through the stories for the story to progress rather than the combat actually being interesting or the characters having their own personal stuff. Especially once you've seen a lot of the side quests it becomes less mysterious and more "Let's pick this option cause it's better". Although I think that's the end result of any game like this. There will never be infinite options and so it will always be eventually predictable.My only real gripe about the game is that combat is either ludicrously easy or super hard most of the game. Either my guys are strolling around with like 10 armor dealing 10 damage a hit and I can just rush to complete the level or I'm limping along at 1-2 hp on all of my characters at the end. Nothing ever feels like an even fight most of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you enjoy a story that evolves as you play.  As characters come and go, you develop somewhat of a player-ai relationship that encourages careful choices and hero development.  Combat is a little basic compared to a game like D:OS2, but don't let that dissuade you from looking further into purchasing Wildermyth
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a 'Eh, it's alright' vote for Steam reviews. Starts off fun, engaging, and creative, but after a dozen hours or so, the weaknesses start to glare through. Honestly if it wasn't CO-OP I probably would have stopped there after playing the first couple of scenarios. Once the random story elements start repeating, the immersion breaks start to reveal the lackluster difficulty scaling (once you've got a fighter or a scout with a couple key abilities, most combats are over in two or three turns. Without trying, I've gotten achievements for killing End of Campaign bosses in the first turn.) The 'crafting' system is laughably simple and boring. The good abilities are too few, and the monster AI is like playing against a slightly slow child. This is not X-COM meets DnD. I liked this game, and I want to like it more, but what I imagined as an endlessly replayable fantasy RPG turn based game is in reality only about as deep as it's paper doll aesthetic. If you have a friend or two willing to make the journey with you, it's a bit more value for the money, otherwise, wait for a good sale and spend a weekend with it, then move on.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a tactical rpgs like fft or fire emblem, but the game turns out to be more of a DnD game with tactical gameplay. The game allows you to mold the story the way you want and I dislike this kind of game since there is no tension, stake, or shock throughout the story. Even you can choose your characters' love interest 1 minute into the game without any detailed relationship between the characters. I just don't get why the dev puts relationship options at the beginning of the game where the player still doesn't understand the characters very well. This breaks the game immersion for me immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Great replayability, which increase the fact, that it was made for modding - so if you want to create your own little story to spin in another tale, you can! The Legacy system make you be able to keep your favorite characters, and you can go with them on another adventures too. You can rank up one of your heroes at the end of all campaign (depending on the campaign, sometimes two), and if you rank up a Legacy heroe, it can keep the changes, what he or she had at the last campaign (sadly you cannot keep your Large Pets {battle pets}, if you get one). Also, if two of your characters fall in love, or begin a rivalry, you can save that too, so when another campaign you are able to get both of them, they can continue their relationships from the saved point! If your characters are love each other, they can have childrens too, so you can build up really long lines of heroic families too - really a legend worth to be told! (Well sometimes happens with legacy heroes, that a child will be older, than the parents, as you could recruit the children it earlier, than the parent, but that doesn't change the way, how they act towards each other.. Also possible for 'lone' heroes to have kids with random NPC's, so their childrens can also join in the adventuring businness.)You can also customize your heroes with some imitation, like colors, height and weight, and personality (it depends on both your "hooks" and "personality stats" - you can change them when recruit, but not afterwards), and if you doesn't like their given background, you can rewrite it for yourself - just be sure it fits to the hooks, you choose to your hero. (For some heroes you cannot choose those, mostly for the childrens of other heroes.) And i didn't talked about how you can gave your heroes different weapons, armors and learn different skills... Your heroes travel with minimal "backpack", so they have max two set of weapons and one set of armor with them, but the possible amount of items to choose from is quite large.Overall i can recommend it to anyone, who like a tactical battle system with evolving characters, and love a fantasy themed setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: So disappointed by this game.  It has excellent writing, but I can't stand games where damage is so punishing your heroes get 1-2 hit and die; I'm not here for horror elements.  "Normal" difficult shouldn't be tuned to maim / kill your party in the second battle.*Edit after developer response*I think it's great that you're looking at reviews of your game.  Responding to my legitimate complaint about the design around hero maiming/death with what amounts to "lol git gud or play on easy mode nub" is exactly the kind of toxic response I expect from a forum goer - not a developer.  It's not me, it's you. Of course I know there are difficulty level choices - you force players to pick one when they start, where they are clearly labeled.I'm good at strategy games, I've been playing them for most of my life - what I don't like is being emotionally invested in a character that gets maimed or killed because of punishing damage and RNG mechanics.  I understand that some people like that kind of thing, and that's fine, but my review (and personal opinion) isn't "Damn I wish I could could suffer the indignity of playing on easy", it's "Games where normal difficulty is designed to be punishing and harsh are not fun for me."Responses like yours are exactly what chills and prevents meaningful conversation around difficulty choice in games - it's impossible to have the opinion that a game is too difficult or punishing because the automatic response from people trying to tear others down to put themselves up is "well that's your fault, not the game's".  Censoring and gate keeping that kind of feedback is what leads to blind spots in game design, while at the same time othering and ostracizing the person who was brave enough to post their feelings about it.Thanks for perpetuating the awful stereotype - no response would have been better than what you wrote.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Game mechanics - good.  Graphics - tabletop/board game style, effective.  Gameplay reward loop - Nice dynamic between the overland strategy and the tactical fights. Story telling/narrative style- pretty good.  Gives a convincing illusion of being open and player driven rather than linear.  Some people might not like the teenage heroic comic fantasy style, I like it.  Replayability/repetitiveness - events start to repeat around the 10 hour mark...for the price I think there's enough content though.Conclusion- An impressive attempt to conjure up a tabletop/boardgame aesthetic.  Well worth it.Edit...The teenage story telling style got to me.  Trying too hard to be deep and meaningful in a new age 21st century way.  Not for me...
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Quite  fun to play and discover, though I highly recommend getting some mods, they add a lot more diversity of events. Overall you do get drops of a storyline, it's fun to build a hero or a family of them through several campaigns. The graphics are also distinct and give a paperdoll feel, which works better than it should
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I'll let a story tell you my thoughts on the gameThe story begins with two warrior friends, as they wander their way up to an old cottage on a hill belonging to a former adventurer and lady witch of the woods. She had gathered the two friends, along with her apprentice. A female Hunter who would aid the two friends in their journey to defeat a strange cult which kidnapped people to sacrifice to their Bull-Deity.  She informed them of their nearest location and sent the trio on their way. Fighting through the woods, the trio made it to the cults hideout. There, they would be successful but one of the two warrior friends would be forever changed by a ritual performed there.The trio returned to the Lady of the woods who informed them that they must stop this Cult, as she has seen in long ago in her time. She promised to aid the adventurers when the time came but sadly died that Spring. Following the notes, and wisdom from the lady of the woods, they travelled across the land in search of a library which could contain the information they needed. During their journey they met an old mystic who would join in their travels. She wished wished to avenge her husband, as the Bull-Deity cult had taken his life, and thus she joined the party. The Mystic was quite helpful with guidance, leading the party to this ancient library. It was there that they would do battle with this cult once again. Thus, again claiming another victory, the group would take tomes and maps from the library, temporarily retreating home for a couple years to track the cult.It was not until their later years that the group, now bigger with the addition of a new warrior. A daughter of the original two friends. This mighty group of five would learn that the Cult has taken a mystical fire stone in hopes of using it in their sadistic plan. The group of mighty five would traverse across the land, to the underground fortress of the Cult, and it was outside there they prepared for battle. In the night before they talked about their adventures they had along the way, like;When they traversed through the lands and came across the ancient Stormwell. The group used their strength to repair and empowered one of their own with the mighty electrical powers of the storm! Or!When the group got stuck underground during an expedition, and deep under the mountain, they stumbled upon an ancient temple to A Thnarric god, The god of rivers, words, and rhyme. The groups mystic who'd always held a secret passion for the study of ancient Thnarrland, thought it was a life highlight, and a subtle sign that all she'd learned and lived through had prepared her for this journey. Or!When they met the Dreamchanter, A singer and storyteller known throughout the land for her glorious songs and stories before she was wounded in an accident. Although wounded, the Dreamchanter and her singing apprentices sat at their fire and sang songs and told stories. The voices that the group heard would be as beautiful as sirens, and they would never hear anything as beautiful again. Or...the injuries along the way, the loss of eyes and hands...The dead companions who did not last long enough to hear the laughter of the group around the fire.It was these stories, tails and legends that the party laughed, discussed and drank too the night before the final fight. For in the morning they would descend into the caverns to meet their fate......For one story ends....TL:DR Just buy the game dude

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. Having generational characters, watching them grow old and eventually die actually means something. The stories are well written and interesting. The art style is charming and unique, resembling a tabletop game where the pieces are like popups instead of being 3D. You will find some duplication of events if you play long enough, but each campaign seems to have a lot of unique events which don't pop up in other campaigns which keeps the events fresh and engaging. It reminds me of XCom with the combat, just fantasy based. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: My boi Barnak got so good with a spear he could lock down entire rooms if he stood in the middle of it, and he was definitely the hero of our group. He lasted until the final battle where he jumped in to take a killing blow meant for his daughter. She proceeded to beat, and I need you to stay with me here, the everliving hell out of the BBEG and I realized Barnak had a worth successor. 15/10 would zone out playing and stay up until the middle of the night again
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Half choose your own story book, half fantasy X-Com clone, Wildermyth is a game that feels small, and plays big. It's definitely a case of being much more of the sum of all its parts: the tactical combat is quite easy and straightforward, the characters, mages aside, are not really that "special" to manage, the story is quite simple and the choices are few, and not that deep. And still, in the end the game manages to capture your attention much more than you expected, and it manages to make you care about your characters and their fate. A perfect game to share with your kids too, to introduce them to the joy of turn based combat and "classical" RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This is an almost wholly unique experience. As someone who plays a ton of D&D and treasures the collaborative storytelling aspect of the hobby, I must say that this is the closest I've seen to a game capturing that feeling of ludonarrative and procedural story generation. Extremely well done.I think that the art direction of the player characters could use some work and expanded options, but other than that, a lovely game that I absolutely did not expect to play til 5 am. Can't wait to pick it back up for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much. So far I've played all the way up to and through Elena and the Moth, and that campaign was so incredibly amazing that I stayed up till 4 am and have to write this review to calm down. I've searched long and hard for games that speak to me, and this is the closest to perfection I've ever come. Here are the attributes I love in a game that shine in Wildermyth: An open world with a strong plot but plenty of things to do and interesting choices and consequences. Multiple characters that interact and grow together (wildermyth's way of doing this through procedural generation is at least equal to if not better than any other games' prewritten characters). Intense combats full of tactical decisions and multiple options for each character, with various means of adjustment pregame to get the difficulty you want, and just enough randomness to keep you on your toes. Fleshed out skill gain and equipment growth. Maybe best of all the opportunity to take characters from past games and start fresh with them. I'm just barely starting my journey with Wildermyth, but if you are looking for any or all of the things above, I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging tactics game and a beautifully written meditation on the power of stories. The pre-packaged adventures are great in their own right, but the true promise of this game is the platform it provides. It's better than the hype led me to believe. I'm very happy I was able to experience this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to write a good review. At first the game is interesting and playful. Well written. Great art. Some interesting interactions between the characters. And I loved the ability to customize your party. Having your characters age, experience relationships with each other, and bring their children in the party are all pretty unique experiences. Alas -- they are also shallow ones. Family relationships are so superficial it's just not very interesting. Not much unique dialog. No real challenges for family members. I also got bored with the same grind over and over. Not enough variation in the different chapters or stories. Details differed, some of the items and monsters differed, but nothing substantive. I'd wait until a really good sale for Wildermyth unless the producers do a lot more to add variation, spice, and relationship depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: They really pulled it off. There are pre-written events occurring in random order, where you can make decisions that may affect a character for the rest of the game, and yet it feels like natural progression. Haven't seen this even attempted anywhere else.Aside from that it's a well put together turn-based tactical party game with its own sets of monsters. Your characters develop an actual personality of sorts, if you roleplay them. It's what comes closest to a DM-less pen and paper I have ever seen. Also great with friends in coop. Using steam remote, they don't even have to buy it necessarily.

_childDocuments_.review: Creating custom story campaigns is exceedingly complicated and a steep learning curve; so bear that in mind if your friends have gushed about the customization for creating your own stories to play through.That said, the premade content in the game is AWESOME! There's a thriving modding community to add new content, and the DLC is nice and affordable to add some fun extra perks.I've been deeply entertained by watching my characters grow up and make choices. The graphics are charming and nostalgic; I love the paper-doll style of everything (this also makes adding new graphics a bit easier than some games, as you don't have to learn more complicated 3D modelling just to be able to add a new element in).Combat can get a bit repetitive, if you're not a major fan of battle strategy, this game might not be for you. I prefer the story cut-scenes to the actual fights, but the fights have been easy enough on Storytelling Mode that I don't feel like I'm getting bogged down by them, and can, as the game mode implies, focus more on the story itself rather than the combat gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best RPG I have ever played. This game is how interactive storytelling should be. I whole heartedly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access, yes, but an incredible engine for building significant and emotionally-engaging stories around procedurally-generated characters.  A real impressive trick.  Imagine Order of the Stick with King of Dragon Pass DNA and XCOM-ish battles and overworld.  Fun, engaging, surprisingly affecting, and only getting better as time goes on.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game.  It is a cross between Around the World in 80 Days and XCOM.  Stay with me here.  Around the World in 80 Days is a interactive novel, on the high end of the complexity spectrum compared to a Choose Your Own Adventure book.  If you go slightly down the complexity scale, that's what Wildermyth does; there are a number of long, slightly branching encounters which are very well written and interesting.  Then at many of the story points, there is a tactical battle to resolve.The tactical combat is pretty good.  Check out a letsplay to see the graphics; it is "aggressively" 2D although it takes place on a 3D map.  I can see some people looking for photorealism could be put off.  It's not as complex as XCOM or Battle Brothers but it does have some interesting ideas.  I like the way magic works with "interfusing" power into objects, then blowing them up or using them some other way.  For example, if you interfuse a bookshelf near an enemy, then you can execute "Lore Dump: overloads the monster with too much information, causing damage and probably a stun".  It needs a little balancing, first level characters can get easily one-shotted, but that will be improved during the early access period.The existing story encounters are nice, and show a good variety.  There is good worldbuilding.  The key idea is to put unique details onto a small number of characters (maybe, 6 total, unless you got some people killed).  Each story encounter focuses on one or two characters and you can remember details about them this way.  There are also nice mechanics for relationships between the characters, both romantic and rivals.  For example, if one rival gets a showy critical hit, the other one gets a plus to their own critical hit chance called "Did you see that?"  Some people may be unhappy that weapon/armor upgrades are permanent, but  this plays into the uniqueness of the characters.  One character gets that fancy sword, period, you can't pass it around to whoever wants it this time.I think this game will really take off if the promise of modding works out.  The developers have said that modding is a key goal and it is already supported, with a wiki and instructional posts.  If the community jumps in and contributes encounters, this will be a huge benefit to replayability.I'm definitely looking forward to see how this develops.  It's fun now, with interesting ideas about story telling and character uniqueness.  I'm confident the balancing issues will be worked out, but if you like the idea of "Around the World in 80 Days" plus XCOM, you should definitely jump in.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, creative, one of a kind game. Each campaign has so many possibilities and all events are extremely well written. The combat and metagame is complex and satisfying but is very easy to understand and pick up. This game really nails the sense that you are going on an epic quest. The combat encounters are also just long enough to be engaging but short enough to not grow stale. If you enjoy tactical gameplay, character building, or reactive storytelling this should be on the top of your list.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not played much, but this game has me excited (which is rare these days!). It offers a fantastic D&D style adventure with legacy board game style elements. The basic game play elements are very good but it's the story elements and how these have a lasting effect on your heroes that makes the game what it is. Upgrades/ changes to characters make sense because they're embedded into the story and relationships affect stats on the battlefield. Really like the pacing and comic book style story and it has choices. There's so much potential here. Side note; I've played the physical and PC versions of Gloomhaven and liked the idea behind it (RPG with legacy elements) but I'm finding it hard to work out why it's the number one rated board game of all time on BGG. This game for me surpasses Gloomhaven (in it's current release state) because I find it more fun. There's a lot of depth in Gloomhaven's combat - if this game could show the same kind of depth as that during combat encounters it'd be great. Time will tell if the combat in this game keeps people playing in the long term.Great ideas and great execution, good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever found a game that just...felt right? Correct? As if it was made for you and just you, as if someone had looked into your soul and said, "Hey. What is it you want most in a game? What if we give to you?"For me, Wildermyth is that game. An incredibly charming blend of XCOM, Paper Mario, Darkest Dungeon, Old-School D&D, and procedural event chains from dozens of other games, Wildermyth is a game that drinks you in. Its aesthetic is delightfully timeless, pop-up book and papercraft that sometimes looks silly but always feels wonderful. Simple paper-doll characters come alive with well-placed expressions, matched with the random stories that Wildermyth pulls from the deck. The stories become a chain of events as your brain does what it always does - finds patterns and meanings in randomness. The combat is simplistic, but deeply engaging. It needs more options for sure - more classes, more abilities, more variety - but for an early-access game it is deliciously option-packed. You have environmental control options, tactical movement options, sneak attacks, archery, abilities that stack in fascinating ways, synergistic combinations emerging out of random rolls in the deck....And the stories!The random events are also drawn from a deck. As I said earlier, they string together, replies changing based on character personalities, aspects, and (I believe) past events and Hooks. Doing the same event with two parties may only superficially change the dialogue, but sometimes, it really does feel like a new event. But more importantly, your brain makes them a story. Your brain takes the little moments - the romances, rivalries, injuries, friendships - and chains them into one long chronicle. If I have any critiques of this game, they're very light. It needs more of everything - more monster factions, more campaigns, more personality aspects, more Hooks, more gear, more random events for the deck to pull from (I've seen quite a few repeats), more classes, more abilities, more choices, more deeply-fleshed-out relationship systems. It needs more ways to interact with the world without violence. It needs more options for building things, more options for leaving behind elements on the world. It needs an endless mode. It especially needs more music soon - the looping overworld theme is...repetitive, to say the very very least.  The very, very least. The music is probably my biggest critique of the game; it's beautiful for about five minutes and then it becomes extremely white-noise. Overall, though, what an incredibly small price to pay for a game that feels as if it was designed for me personally. If you're the sort of player who plays Crusader Kings 2 or The Sims and makes up stories in your head as you go, this is the kind of game that will appeal to you. The strategy elements are very light and very intuitive, and the stories are already spinning into wild and wonderful things to experience. It can only get better from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, narrative forward game that is oddly addictive. You get attached to your characters in a way that I've never experienced in other RPG games. My only problem with this game is that so far is that I've played tactical RPG's with better mechanics but once I cranked up the difficulty everything clicked a bit more.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of sandbox story-generator games as well as tactical strategy like Xcom.  This is one of my new favorite games.  It has interesting generated story, characters, relationships, and choices.  The writing is genuinely charming.  The difficulty scales well and is anywhere from super easy to very challenging and unforgiving.  Tactically the game is very interesting and different monsters fight with refreshingly different tactics.I hope the devs are able to keep content coming.  The game seems pretty well polished for 1.0, but as is always the case with procedural storytelling games, more is better and the variety keeps the game fresh.  76 hours in I feel like there are still a lot of events I have not seen and there are still enemy types that I have not seen much of yet and am learning to fight well.  However I am also seeing a lot of repeats of the more common events.  Granted I didn't start noticing a lot of repeats until probably 50 hours in, but still.  Conclusion: love the game and it feels like a breakthrough for the genre.  Can't wait to see what the future holds for it because I already know I will keep coming back.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: "The magic of Wildermyth is that it loves stories so much that it builds its entire structure, from graphical style to prose to combat to campaign structure, around its characters becoming legends. It then cements those ideas in place with a Legacy system that turns those legendary characters into stories again, weaving design and storytelling together throughout. Wildermyth gives the impression of being charmingly ramshackle, but surprisingly flexible and tight under the hood, which all adds up to a truly special experience." IGN"If you're interested in narrative, there's a theoretical game you've already dreamed about. It's an impossible fusion of deliberately crafted stories and pure systems-driven anecdotes, all lending themselves to stories of your own like procedurally generated bricks." PCGamer
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Fun story and roleplay driven tactical RPG with great replayability.  This was a random find, I wanted a game I can play while traveling on my MacBook. I came across this game and I was glad I did. Overall a solid 8.5  out of 10.0What it is:- You play through a campaign, and most of it can be done in a single longer sit down ~ 3 hours.- Replaying the same or new campaigns you can pick past (legacy) characters to retell or continue their story- Random encounters, events, and campaign related decisions inject choices into your gameplay that have drastic effects on the overall story and your characters- At a high level there are three classes (Hunter, Warrior, Mystic) with a fair amount of variability in what you focus on. As an example a Hunter can focus on ranged, melee, or even swap weaopns mid combat and do a bit of both.- The strength of your characters comes from level up ability choices (pick one of three random presented), character specific events where the plot decisions impact your character, and itemization found from exploring, defeating combat events, or crafting- Art style is top down view and has a table top feel to it- Combat is XCOM lite with some interesting unique twists- Magic system (with the Mystic class) has a unique core mechanic where you draw on environment objects and the spell casting options are strongly influenced by what that item on the combat map does. This introduces tactics complexity, where do you set up choke points is dependent on what the Mystic can influence via these placed objectsPros:- Great story art, roleplay decisions and story development are done via gorgeous art panels- You can definite the personality of your characters (do you want two party characters to get along, argue a lot, or even romantically get involved)- When a rp event triggers, which character(s) are used, the choices you make, and consequences of those decisions have a huge impact on the growth of a character. - The details of the story are fun, engaging, and varied. - Lots of replay- The escalation of investment in your characters sneaks up on you, at the start of the game I had no attachment to any of my characters - they were randomly generated down to the names - as I progressed in the campaign all the roleplay events helped create an attachment and appreciate for your characters, what their drives were, etc. - Replaying even the same campaign adds a new experience and value in further growing your legacy teamCons:- No voice acting at all, I think this is a missed opportunity. AI driven voice acting could add so much more to an already amazing story experience- The invasion events depending on where they spawn and the direction they head to can be incredibly annoying to catch up to- RNG of combat can be very quirky. You can have a long streak of misses (blocks, dodges, etc) that feels very awkward and unreal- the random spirits that run away if you catch them can provide some added enchants and augments to a character and their equipment. Having 3-4 rounds to catch up to it seem like a poor implementation of what could be a lot more interesting if done differently. I would have preferred if these were optional quests that appeared on the world map's conquered areas. You can double  back to that zone and do a dedicated exploration to  uncovered the reward
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been burned by EA, I’m hugely skeptical of ANY EA title. To illustrate, when I buy EA, I set a timer for an hour. If I’m not 100% convinced, I refund. This game passed the one hour test.On that note, it passed ALL my expectations. I’m not far in, but I am amazed at what is there. I like the art style and the presentation; it seems they have a rather large sandbox to play with here, and I’m looking forward to it.  I’m not a Dungeons and Dragons player, never have played, although I like RPGs and strategy games. This beauty fits nicely for anyone who is into either genre. I could tell an intricate story of my heroes and how they went from farmer to hero, lost arms, forged rivalries, etc. but it’s far easier for you to play and see for yourself.That said, there’s a bit more that would take this game from great to absolutely amazing. I’m thinking along the lines of more nuanced relationships (for example, parent-child), but I’m sure those will be added in due time. For now, hard buy; get it to support this great project.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Ridiculously beautiful art and music.-It's fun to start with young heroes and play through their life stories. The emergent storytelling really works.-Combat is tense and exciting, but not punishing.Cons:-There are only three character classes.-The overworld campaign part of the game lacks depth. It's mostly just moving to the next location and fighting. The world doesn't really react to my choices.-I'm starting to see the same random story elements multiple times after two campaigns.This game could start to get old if played too often, but it's great for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Wildermyth

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished one of my first playthroughs of the campaign and I must say I am blown away by what I've just experienced. Despite being generated by random in some ways, I've fallen in love with some of my characters and I can't wait to bring them into other storylines or to replay some.
